I got my bowl to go and it came out super fast. Like amazingly fast. Like I ordered and paid. And then I looked at the menu again while I waited. I got half way through the tacos and BAM my bowl was hot, ready and packed up nicely to go. And it stayed hot all the way back to the office. 

Interested in coming back at some point and exploring the rest of the menu - especially if I don't have time to kill!

Subway is a Subway- the sammiches do in a pinch but in a city known for hoagies there's always a lot to be desired. I enjoyed my lunch, the kids liked their apples and milk that came with theirs. 

It's a tight squeeze but there is ample seating upstairs. They had one high chair but I had two babies with me. 

I can imagine with the location they get a lot of riffraff so they locked bathroom door nearly wasn't opened in time for my 3 year old potty trainer. 

It was good- I'd stop by again if we were on foot and hungry like we were that day.

Damn good slice of pizza! Crust is thin & chewy, sauce is delicious. Love how the cheese is slightly browned & the stripes of sauce on top. Nice touch! 

Special includes 2 slices and a can of soda for $3.50. Can't beat that.

Great lunch spot if you work in Center City. Tacos are a little over a buck and usually 3 or 4 will do the trick. The BLT burrito is amazing.

Caution: Burrito's are small, that's why most are around $3... My recommendation: get 2 or 3 tacos and a burrito to make for a great lunch. And don't forget the amazing hot sauce to add on top. Avoid nachos as it's not melted cheese, more of a cheese fry sauce.

Always friendly service and very quick... Even has a outdoor seating on a nice day

The best sandwich place in Philadelphia. Anything and everything here is tremendous. People talk about Geno's, or Pats or Tony Luke's but this place puts them all to shame. So if you're a slob like me you'll love this place, but there are also some veggie options, so you don't have to feel like a slob if you make the hard choice to steer clear from the 50/50, the BBQ brisket, the turbacon, or literally anything else on this long consistent menu.
I ordered a chicken cheesesteak from here and it was the worst. they didn't put what I asked for on it when I ordered it. It tasted like it I was eating sand, that's how dry it was. Then

Popeyes lacks the notoriety of its competitor KFC but is just as good and maybe better.  Have been hitting this place up more lately strictly for their chicken fingers and fries.  For sides other than red beans and rice, fries are my go to.  The tenders actually come in mild or spicy which is a theme for this place in general more spice.  They even sell solo jalapeños. The diet cherry coke I get usually tastes like Dr Pepper but this place is good for my fast food fix.  Mac and cheese and mash potatoes I would shy away from as they are not that good.

had an all-out glutton fest with my SIL. We shared the "classic", "turbacon", and "mensch". all of the sandwiches were great!  My personal fav is the classic...a close second would be the turbacon.  I will be back!
Worst customer service ever. These girls will have someone catch a case. Very unprofessional and so rude.

Double fried wings aren't bad. Not the best korean style fried chicken I've had, however. Good for a quick pick up at lunch or dinner.

Would recommend soy garlic flavor.
Ordered out a make your own bowl, everything came as ordered and extremely quick. The bowl itself was ridiculously good and I can't wait to order again!

Couple weeks until my diet starts so I was looking to wreak havoc on this place... Average at best. I got an order of 20 crispy wings with buffalo, soy garlic and wasabi aioli. The sauces were mediocre and the chicken was moist but bland. It needs more seasoning in the breading. They also do not deliver as apposed to what this and their website says.

Wow, I'm surprised at the mixed reviews. I was kind of sad because I thought that this Potbelly had closed but realized it's the other one on Walnut Street, and this one is still here. 

About the service: Never had I had any trouble with service. Actually... I feel that service was superb each time I came with the BF.

The BF and I would come to this Potbelly on occasion for lunch. One day the BF wasn't feeling so good so I got him lunch here (and he was at home). One of the staff recognized me and asked me where my BF was (lol). We had a nice conversation and I told him the BF was sick. Another day, we came back together and coincidentally, the same staff member was in and he started joking around with us about the day I got food for my BF when he was sick. I've never had any trouble with the other staff members either.

On to the food: My fave is the A Wreck. So so good! The BF likes the Meatball sub that has marinara sauce and provolone cheese. He also likes adding mushrooms for an additional cost.

We also like to have some potato salad as a side.
The sandwiches are so good and I like how they are just so warm and yummy!!

By the way, the place could get really packed around lunch time because of the people who work nearby.

Anyways, enjoy!!

First time in Philly since the 4th grade, looking for a good sandwich for lunch. Did not disappoint. I went with the Barnyard. I felt like taking the whole sandwich back to my hotel and getting weird, but instead I just went back the next day and got the mensch. Would definitely recommend.
Amazing sandwiches!! The farm fries are to die for!!! My lad was overwhelmed with orgasm eating his 50/50 sandwich!! Two thumbs up!!

During my year of school, I must have visited this spot a dozen times or more. I have tried their rice bowls, theirs salads and of course their double fried wings!! They have over ten different sauces for their wings... And their green cilantro based sauce is great as a salad dressings or for dipping fries. Honestly I use it on everything!! 

They are pretty economical and definitely give you a bang for your buck. Big portions of satisfying and savory food for your money. I have noticed you get more food when you eat in than take to go. 

Lastly the wings are indeed freshly made so expect to wait at least 15 minutes... Or call ahead for pick up.

the food here is awesome. you can use restaurant.com certificates every 30 days. ive had their salads, bruschetta, soup, hoagies and pasta. no complaints. your order is always ready on time. im addicted!!!!!!!!!

We had a meeting that was catered by Jake's. The sandwiches tasted good but were a little messy for a work meeting. I decided to check out the place for lunch and it was a much better experience. Piping hot, filling, and yum. I got the megillah in a haystack fries bowl. Sent a pic to my hubbie and he was instantly jealous. Brisket, cheese, bacon on fries, who wouldn't be jealous?
I love this place. I've been coming here for years. Make sure you bring cash tho- they don't accept cards.

Once again, "why don't we have this in DC?"

Ok.  Admittedly, I'm on a pre-Thanksgiving binge thanks to Thrillist.  But who would have ever thought of a Turducken Sammie?!  It's brilliant.  If you thought that Thanksgiving Balls (see Blind Pig) were the end of all Thanksgiving Comfort Food then you have a strong contender in the Turducken Sandwich.  Because let's face it, the only thing better than turkey is turkey+duck+chicken.  Throw in cranberry spread with apple sausage stuffing and you got the basic foundation.  The creme-a-la-creme, however, is the fried hash browns to add a crispy texture and warm childlike feeling.

Why are these chimera creations so brilliant?  Because that's who you'll end up eating a Thanksgiving Feast anyway.  Nobody just eats the turkey by itself and then the mash potatoes separately.  You mix it all together and stuff it in your mouth.  It's just that Jake's Sandwich Board and Blind Pig figured out a more efficient delivery mechanism.  It all ends up the same anyway.

Brilliant.  Just brilliant.

Overall, skip Thanksgiving dinner.  You've got everything you need with the Turducken Sammie.

[Original Visit: November 2014]

I am not a fan of poke but this place may have turned me into a fan. I ordered a specialty ahi bowl and my gf ordered a custom bowl which was infinitely better than mine. 

My only gripe with this place is the water situation. You have to ask for it and it is lemon flavored. 

The staff is friendly and competent

I would come back for takeout or delivery via postmates

This place is the real deal! High quality, delicious sandwiches, all cooked and hand-carved in house. Every Saturday, I buy lunch for my employees and when I ask them where they want to order from, "Jake's" is usually the consensus. Make sure to always ask if they have any specials and be sure to order sides of crunchy onions and fried pickles - the best!
Oh yes my pork with black bean burritos was the best today ... they are fast and good ... also take along for chips and salsa ... not much more to say but OH YEA..!!!
If your looking for a place that brings you back to your mom and dads cooking this is the place. Great homemade food and great coffee.
Great sandwiches. Ordered the Daves Brisket and the sandwich was very tender, love the siracha tingle.
Unbelievably good. One of the best sandwiches I've ever had.

One of the best poke restaurants that I've been to in the United States. The owners, who are almost always there, Amanda and Ed, are so pleasant and such a nice couple. They really love what they're doing and they have experience in owning previous sushi restaurants In New Jersey. The Fish distributor that they work with is excellent, and on the 5 times that I was there, the quality of the fish, salmon, tuna, and others, was always excellent. their system to build up your poke, requires ( if you do it manually like I do )  that you fill in a piece of paper, and you basically build up your poke based on rice or greens, the fish, and then many different options for toppings / extras/ sauces! This is something unique that I've only seen in red poke. Every single time that I came there, together with different guests,  the Poke that we had was fresh, delicious, and made with love. For the price of about $10-$12 you get a big bowl of poke, which is filling, delicious and fun! Highly recommended.

Jake's Sandwich Board, which occupies a rather non-descript block in Midtown Village, can be easily missed from passing by.  However, I have passed by this place no less than a thousand times, and since this is my last week in town, I figured I would give this place a go.  Jake's has received both local and national accolades, and after tasting the food, there's a reason: monstrous sandwiches that are full of flavor and worth your money.

The menu is a little overwhelming, but relies on four meats: pork, brisket, turkey, and chicken.  The styles range from traditional to the unusual (including a brisket sandwich with crunchy peanut butter).  Not wanting to stray too far from familiar territory, I opted for a 50/50: a shredded pork sandwich with bacon, sriracha mayo, and sharp provolone cheese.  The sandwich was huge, but oh so tasty.  Really enjoyed the mashup of flavors; the sharpness of the cheese against the heat of the mayo and the saltiness of the meat.  The whole roasted cloves of garlic on top were also a delight.  My only complaints? The pork was a bit dry and the mayo wasn't nearly spicy enough for my liking, but otherwise, this was a great and unique sandwich.  It definitely gives DiNic's a run for it's money.

While the atmosphere isn't much, people are clearly here for the food and unique sandwich combinations.  Competitively priced, big on flavor, and with so many choices to choose from, Jake's is definitely worth at least one visit, especially for those looking to branch outside of Reading Terminal fare.

Unfortunately,  this Chipotle gave me cold rice... Cold chicken.. Not popping hot to balance out the salsa or guacamole!   The Chipotle n Ardmore is the best!  City Ave.. Horrible and 39th walnut ..waste of 9.57
Try the double fried wings - finally some good wings! Sides are pretty good as well. Delivery was fast.

I am so thrilled to have a restaurant nearby that makes homemade flour tortillas, great guacamole and authentic dishes that use fresh ingredients.  My veggie burrito had a wonderful mix of grilled peppers, mushrooms, and onions with the right balance of rice and beans.  My husband's al pastor burrito was equally tasty.  The tortilla chips had just been fried and were not overly salted. To make the meal even better, they included two different kinds of homemade salsa and pickled jalapeños and carrots.  The owners could not have been nicer.  Long live Cafe Canela!

Place: it was a bit weird having a stack of potatoes and stuff as a line guide and then walls of awards that were dated back over 6 years ago. Tacky and awkward. The atmosphere was nice though. 
Food: a bit pricey for some meats between buns but my brother and mother (bought food for them not me) enjoyed it. They were amazed at the amount of bacon in the BLT. Loved the fact that there were free toppings for the burgers :)
Service: fast and easy. Didn't wait long and food was fresh.

I have tried Crisp Kitchen twice now (same location) and had a decently good experience. It is the same concept as Honeygrow in that their main items for you to order are salads or stir fry. Both times, I have had salad. 

My first experience in-store was better than my take out experience that I ordered online. The salad portion looked bigger when you ate at the restaurant rather than left with it. The first time, I did the Cobb salad and changed up a few items and the second time, I did a build your own. 

With the take away salad, I felt like it was mainly lettuce and just a little bit of the toppings I requested. It also was not stirred around very well which would not normally be annoying but the container was pretty stuffed with lettuce (a good thing) so when I went to shake in my dressing, it stayed on top of my salad and everything at the bottom was dry. 

My dressing of choice at all these types of fast-casual salad restaurants is White Balsamic. If you are used to the Honeygrow White Balsamic and like its tartness, you probably won't like this one as much. The white balsamic here was good, but was very sweet and almost tasted like it had a decent amount of sugar added to it. 

All in all, not a bad experience and would recommend giving it a try! The girl who checked me out was very friendly and my take out order was ready on time. I would probably recommend eating in-store to get your money's worth but avoid the 12-1 time slot. It is really crowded!

I could just write "Banana Tahini Shake" and leave it there. It's amazing - topped with crumbled animal crackers and served through a pipe-like straw. Amazing. I wish they came in extra-extra large. The falafel sandwiches are terrific, especially with the spicy sauce. And the staff is so nice! They're always busy and on the run, yet take the time to make sure you have all you need.

dude dude dude dude dude bro! you wanna get some bad-ass fried chicken?? This chicken is totally sweet, pimpin. I'm not talking about some bogus-ass Wendys or KFC chicken. This place is sooooo sweet!! I seriously mean it. Get the 10 piece boneless wings for $8.00. May be not too filling but it's legit crispy. like crispy crispy.

Pretty standard Chipotle set up/service. The line can get a little sloppy and rushed, but overall my recent visits have been pretty good.

I've been doing the Whole30 program, and Chipotle is one of the few chains where it is pretty easy to dine out and be Whole30 compliant.

My go-to Whole30 order is: lettuce bowl with Carnitas (only protein that is W30 compliant, double if need be), mild & medium salsas, and guacamole. It's actually delicious AND you don't end up feeling bloated and weighed down (like you might with a burrito).
I was in the mood for some honey BBQ wings and it hit the spot. The extra crispy wings were really good!

Really nice staff and tasty salad! Clean restaurant and easy, customizable ordering makes this a perfect spot for a quick lunch/dinner. Preparation was efficient. 

You chose from a variety of salads and stir-frys. I would love to see a larger variety of options.

Best cheesesteaks I've eaten in awhile, since Im a Jersey girl. haha. 
Had the Charlie Brown..a simple but DELICIOUS. Deff will go back again if im in the area

Got a chicken cutlet sandwich and honey bbq wings. Chicken cutlet sammie was legit, like one of the better sandwiches I've had in quite sometime. Wings would have been great naked with sauce on the side, but it was gooped on there and was a real pain in the dick to eat, it also took away all the crispiness from the breading, which to me is the whole point of korean wings. I'll try em again though...naked.

Before you go in to Five Guys you need to ask yourself, "Am I going to feel up a burger or am I going to get laid?"  If it's the latter, Five Guys will not disappoint.  If you think eating a down and dirty burger and fries is going to ruin your diet and throw you into a depression for the rest of the summer, you might try Subway next door.

My first experience at Jakes was amazing. I had no expectations because I just needed a sandwich for lunch at work. It arrived promptly and the sandwhich was out of this world. I got the Village Turkey and chocolate covered bacon- because how could I not? The Sammy was great and the chocolate covered bacon was to diiie for. 

I have gotten jakes 4 times since the. The second time and third I did pick up and got the same order as the first. It was to be expected, great. 

The past two times have been increasingly difficult. Last night my order arrived 50 minutes after they said it would and I knew my order was at my door, not because someone called me but because there was a car outside with music blaring that my sandwhich came from...

Today it took about two hours to get my food and I changed it up and got the turbacon- not as good as the village turkey. I got a cookie too that was good but very small for $1. I called three times to see where my order was and they just kept saying it would be there any second... 2 hrs later....

I will eat at jakes again but I will being doing pick up or ordering my lunch very early. Luckily they have two locations so maybe 40ths street delivery etiquette will be better ...
Brisket sandwich: best thing I've ever put in my mouth. I promise you will go back for seconds.

Consistent at being the most disappointing at everything, this chipotle is in desperate need of new management and team members. Definitely the worst experience of any chipotle I've ever been to. From low quality food prep to unbelievably poor customer service, this chipotle wins the award of most disappointing on every level. Unfortunately, it is the only location on campus.
Fresh bread and toppings, great tasting meat, and friendly service.  I'm glad I stopped in today.

Can't beat the price at this place.  Get there about 10-15 minutes before noon and you'll easily get a table.  Hot sauce bottles are shared, so you'll get a lot of other customers asking if you are done with your bottle yet so apply early.  Food is average.  It's not the greatest but certainly not the worst but again, can't beat the price and what you get.  I've been going here about 15 years and it's been consistent since Day 1.
This Poke was incredible. I got the Volcano Signature Bowl. The woman was so friendly and recommended it to me and it was extremely tasty. I definitely recommend.

I'm normally pro Chipotle but this one was pretty chaotic. I hoofed it over the other weekend for dinner and was informed upon approaching the line that they'd run out of black beans. Um, what? You're Chipotle, you should have beans coming out of your ears. Not to mention the kid working the line should've informed his cook that he needed more. 

I waited it out about 10 minutes for more beans to be cooked, but didn't get even a fake apology for being made to wait. When first informed that I had to wait, I told the fella I'd want a new tortilla heated up (he'd heated one anyway and already put the rice on it knowing the beans were out) and then tried to pass me back the cold one. To have this be my problem is not the end of the world of course, but dude this kid is not doing this Chipotle any service by working there.

I did eventually get the completed burrito I wanted and mostly enjoyed it. I live in Fairmount and am rarely in University City. I can definitely say I won't go out of my way for this place again.
Whats up with the dead rat in dining room for customers Chipotle?Never going to eat here again .Second time it was shut down by health department.Bye bye Chipolte.
Mobile ordered. Fast service and ready on time!! Always fast and friendly staff. Definitely good place for a Mexican fix

Went here for the first time in May '09 and am in love with it. The fries are bangin as is all the other food. Never had a problem with the service.  I always make it a point to do so when I'm in the area which will be more often since I'm moving.

This turkey sandwich was excellent. This isn't Dietz and Who? processed meat, it's hot carved thick cut thick taste fowl fit for kings. The bacon is also delicious and broccoli raab is steamed to perfection delicious.

If you like sandwiches, go here. And if you don't like sandwiches, I want no part of you.

I got the turkey with onions and avocado topping, overall pretty big, and good but not sure worth $10. The place is cute and fun, and lots of unique hoagie choices. Everything looked fresh, and was made ready to order. I'm glad I finally tried this place after walking past it all the tine, curiosity has been satisfied!

These people know their sandwiches, but be warned, there's only one option for vegetarians.  

I am a convert to the "haystack" style sandwich, which is your chosen fillings served on top of a pile of delicious crispy fries.  No bread.  If you, like me, are a carb addict looking to cut down, this is a terrific way to get the carbs you love the most while skipping the ones you love a little less than most.  I got the Schmeer (roasted turkey, roasted red peppers, baby spinach, provolone, onion) haystack and a birch beer.  One day I will try the Sloppy Dog with two hot dogs, mushrooms, roasted peppers, cheddar and mustard.

First time here but I've had poke before. The only thing holding this place back from being 5 stars is that I wish i could have added more than one sauce to my bowl. However, all the ingredients tasted really fresh and my order was made quickly with no mistakes!

I tried going to the Food Truck Festival on Locust Street yesterday, but it was way too crowded. I've walked past Jake's before but had never been in, so I decided to come here instead. I ordered a Farmer's Market sandwich. It came out quickly and was really delicious! It was a huge hoagie type sandwich - I ended up eating half and saving the other half for lunch for today. As a leftover, the bread lost a little texture (not Jake's fault by any means since I refrigerated it), but the veggies had more time to marinate in that amazing sauce and it was still delicious overall the second time around. I would definitely come back and eat here again. 

Not sure if it was an option (I was in a rush after wasting so much time walking through the mob at the Festival, so I didn't peruse the menu fully), but I'd love the ability to buy half of a sandwich with a tiny side of something instead of the whole giant sandwich.

The worst! Cheap but awful. There is no difference between a burrito and a taco. If you want beans and/or rice with your burrito, you have to pay more! People in third world countries eat beans because they are cheap. This place puts a price premium on this staple.

21/2 stars... JUST OK!  Should have had a sandwich at reading Terminal tho

Pulled Pork sandwich without coleslaw????

Wasn't stacked, it was just a tad dry, and they were stingy with the sauce!

Staff are like Zombies, not a warm atmosphere... Smile every once in a while for crying out loud!  Especially the girl at the register...

Place was clean as a whistle tho!

My man would give it a 2 stars. I upped it to three because of the good fries and fried pickles. The man says "lacking flavor". And I agree. Even the garlic bomb would have been more dynamic with some BBQ sauce or fried pickles on top. Brisket was tender but again missing flavor. The sriracha sauce was almost invisible.

There are two types of summer eaters, those that can only manage to make it through cool, light, refreshing fare, and those, like me, who have fond memories of eating greasy food poolside and have carried on the tradition.  Yesterday, in the sweltering heat, I decided to venture to Jake's for dinner.  It has been on my list forever, and for some reason, I just had never made it over there.  

What I was most pleasantly surprised about was the frenchfries! For I think maybe 1.00 more, you get a bag of perfectly delicious, perfectly salted french fries, that I will go out on a limb and say are in my top five in Philadelphia (or at least top 8).  I opted for the midtown chicken.  It was very good.  When I was ordering, I was disappointed that I couldn't get my sandwich in a wrap, but after trying the bread, I was very happy with my fully carb loaded sammy.  My only complaint was that I wish my sandwich had a bit more kick, I added hot sauce at home.  But reading Bill M's review, apparently I was just unaware of the many toppingg options.

Even if this were the most amazing breakfast sandwich, I could never give it above 2 stars. Why? For the egg white portion of my sandwich, dude pulled a solid, white pancake-like object from behind the counter (that was the egg white) and cut it into quarters. 

Then he nuked it in the bizarro half microwave-half monster. When it was all said and done, he forgot to add the Black Forest Ham to my sandwich. The only thing that was probably made out of anything real was the bread. I'll probably get these every morning though.

Yeah, they're still pretty awesome. Tried a wrap and it was delicious. Chicken and bacon were cooked perfectly. Double cheeseburger platter was also ordered at this same time and was just as good as the other times ordered. This place is more consistent than their "sister" join, Big Daddy's pizza. Also, their pizza with extra cheese is really good.

The pulled pork is probably the best thing on this menu. I came here for some cheesesteak and their meat to bread ratio was a little off. The pork is succulent and juicy and well worth coming here. Sadly I won't be back to this place because there's far more other places in the neighborhood and in Philly that are worth going to. But if I had a last-minute choice this would definitely be it.

Such a sad beginning to lead to a sad ending! I visited Crisp Kitchen hoping to check out their froyo. The choices in flavor were nonexistent. Vanilla or chocolate, throwback to the days before frozen yogurt was hip. So okay, I said let's see what they have for toppings. Again I was disappointed to find out that there were limited toppings. Although supposedly free there was actually a 69 cent surcharge for pineapple! I went with craisins and mangoes, served with a swirl of "both flavors". The total with tax was $3.99. I was handed a yogurt cup that was filled with quickly melting yogurt. With a few steps outside the store, the melt turned into a sloppy mess. I had sticky icky pants yogurt on my hands in no time. It was not an enjoyable feeling at all.

Honestly the sandwich tasted great my only issue is the lack of meat! My god for 10$ there was barely any meat just filler...onions, mushrooms, and that big ole hot pepper in the Fire Steak. I'm not the least bit happy.

Real good ingredients, filling and varied sandwiches, good promotions, and always friendly.  Also, nothing over $10 (unless you're doing the challenge and then you're asking for trouble).  Definitely go there before noon as it's not as crowded.  I'd say it's much better than the sandwich chains but not as consistently good as some places in South Philly.

I can always get a seat at this Chipotle. It's conveniently located, and if I order ahead, there's really no wait! staff are always nice. 

I'm a fan of their burritos.

Jake's Sandwich Board often gets the short end of the stick when the Philly roast pork greats are considered. Sandwich aficionados often refer their advisees (rightfully, I may add) to Paesano's or Dinic's for their fix of this staple Philly food. Frankly, I do not understand why Jake's gets ignored; their product is on par, if not superior to, the ones offered at those aforementioned joints. To be clear, my allegiance for best pork sandwich lies with Paesano's Arista, but Jake's is a close second. 

This mainly stems from Jake's roast meat, as it offers a tender, unparalleled distillation of porcine flavor. Pork sandwiches here are customizable, and toppings range from the requisite long hots to the uncommon cracklings. The rolls are standard Philly fare, not quite as deliciously crusty as Liscio's or Sarcone's product but better than whatever mush Dinic's employs. The brisket is tasty too, check out the brisket cheesesteak for a superlative rendition of the Philly tourist classic. Do skip their standard cheesesteaks though, these fall flat in comparison to more dedicated shops. 

Jake's also slightly edges out their competition in two other regards: $5 pork sandwiches on Mondays (eat your heart out, Subway), and having a deep fryer. $2 nets you a nice taste of delicious fried pickles, and the other, slightly more expensive deep fried offerings make for pleasant munching. You can even get sandwich toppings on fries instead of bread just in case you want to shave a couple extra years off of your life. Head to Jake's and get a pork sandwich, some fried pickles, and a few extra napkins for the juices that'll inevitably drip down your chin. You likely won't miss the more popular options.

I'm impressed.
My coworker and I ordered the Famous Double Fried Wings.  I got Sweet Chili and she got Soy Garlic.  Both were good.  Mine was spicy which I like.  I did think mind wasn't as crispy as you might find with normal Korean Fried Chicken but I tried one of the soy garlic and that was nice and crispy.  maybe it was the sauce that took away some of the crispiness in mine. 

the only gripe is that delivery doesn't start til 2pm so we had to wait awhile before we could order.

I like this place a bunch. It's low budget, decent food and just half-block from work.  I only go after 1:30/2p, too crowded otherwise.

My favorites are the Macho Nachos (loaded w/jalapenos) and the Blazin' Buffalo Chicken burrito.  Not a meal to bring a date, but definitely for an good, quick, inexpensive meal.

I love Spanish cuisine, authentic or fast food. I stopped at Hot Tamales one day for lunch because I always walked past it when going to the 7-11 and thought I would give it a try. First off, my gf and I waited in a long line to give our orders. When we finally reached the register I realized I only had my debit card with me and they only accepted cash (no signs on the doors or anywhere else except for a small sign on the register which you can't see until you're right on top of it). I went safe and ordered two tacos, thinking that would pretty hard to screw up. Boy was I wrong. Not only did the food take awhile to come out but it was the blandest taco I have ever tasted in my life! It was as if they didnt season the beef at all. It was just a bad experience overall. The only plus side to this place is that they are cheap. But if you want cheap you could just walk over to Taco Bell @ 30th Street and your guaranteed good fast-food.

Finally tried this place after walking by many times. Wish I hadn't. It is very inexpensive and you definitely get what you pay for. The food wasn't horrible, but it was bland and just tasted cheap. The best way I can describe it is that it tasted like someone described to them what a burrito was and they winged it without ever trying a real one. The only way I would recommend this place is if you were very hard up on money and just looking to put inexpensive food in your belly. I will not be coming here again.

I work across the street, so when I'm hungry and short on time and have waited long enough for the lunch carts to have all gone home, I will occasionally think to myself, "Oh, cheap tacos. That place was ok, right?"

And then, 20 minutes later, I'm holding my belly and thinking, "Why did I do that again? Why don't I ever learn?"

Yes, they are cheap. The basic burrito is under $3. So of course, you set your standards kinda low, and go for it.

Except I guarantee you, Taco Bell uses better ingredients. The "turkey" is this horrific mass of spongey brown chunks that are supposed to imitate ground meat, although why there was a shriveled up piece of what appeared to be celery that had been freeze-dried and reconstituted, I don't know. The chicken is shredded and unrecognizable. I've never been stupid enough to try the beef.

It's simply nauseating. The reviewer who said they use fresh ingredients because the lettuce is crisp has a different definition of "fresh ingredients" than I do. These guys obviously buy hyper-processed generic materials in bulk, or possibly they take leftovers from other area restaurants. Maybe the "turkey" had celery because it was originally destined for meatloaf. Or dog food.

More likely dog food.

$3 will get you a few pounds of fresh fruit from the fruit carts. It'll also get you a fresh egg/cheese sandwich with lettuce, tomato, onions from any lunch cart. 

And if you splurge and go to $4.50, you can get fresh marinated chicken breast pulled from its marinade and grilled right in front of you, and then turned into the most delicious sandwich ever, from Khalid's cart outside the Starbucks on 18th and Market, a block away.

Seriously. There are better things to do to your intestines for under $5, that don't involve a food experience this shameful.

I used to come here religiously because I was fooled by the "creative" options, and I kept trying to give them chance after chance when I had bad experiences (which, come to think of it, was every single time I ate here).

The meat is always dry and cold because they sit it under heat lamps all day instead of letting it soak in the juices and seasonings (like literally any other pork/brisket place). The rolls are always soft, but not in a good way. The rolls taste like they buy last week's rolls for half price.

The only reason anyone should come here is if they work nearby, have no time, and get pork on a Monday ($5 build your own). If you have the time, go to DiNic's in Reading Terminal for the brisket or Italian pulled pork (though they usually run out after the lunch rush, so you should get there before 12pm. It makes this place look like Arby's), South Philly for roast pork, or Cleavers on 18th Street if you want onion rings or sriracha on your sandwich THAT badly.

The only thing this place is good for is the $5 BYO pork Mondays (because that's all it's worth...), and the raspberry green tea is good.
Got "the hypocrite"... A bunch of vegetables with bacon and provolone on fresh bread. Nice. Super fresh ingredients, and they make your sandwich to order. Will be back

While it is a hefty portion, it is a bit expensive for a grab and go food. I also felt like they didn't have as many options as their competitors (honeygrow, sweetgreen, etc). All in all, pretty good!

The food here is very good.  I've had nearly everything on the menu and they're all decent.  I highly recommend the firesteak, barnyard, and the turduckin.  The rolls here are always nice and soft in the middle and has a little bite on the outside, which I love.  

I don't come here for the service, which is ok but not particularly friendly.  The blonde girl at the counter is usually surly, but I still come here for the food.

Red Poke Express is an incredible experience! Their seafood is high quality and the flavors are incredible. I made my own bowl with yellowtail, tuna, brown rice, seaweed salad, kani salad, mango, ginger wasabi shoyu sauce and lots of other fun add-ins.

I strongly recommend trying this place out if you're looking for a healthy bite of fresh seafood at am affordable cost!

My only suggestion would be to provide reusable dishes while you dine-in and plastic ware only to-go. We did not see recycling options anywhere for all that plastic, which was sad.

I have tried this place about 4 times since it's been open (don't judge me ;) )and haven't had anything I didn't thoroughly enjoy.  They are quick and friendly at the counter and the ingredients are fresh! Extra kudos for labeling the gluten free sauces.  I'm really glad this place is here.

We had a pork sandwich and a brisket sandwich.  Both were really good.  Had good bread - which is key.

I was able to witness two people finishing up the challenge.  Looked really intriguing ... they came no where close.
So so good! Definitely try it, the ingredients are so fresh and the service is friendly. I can see this place being a new favorite of mine

Over hyped burgers!!  Went here with a friend to try it.  He's eaten here before and I havent so I wasnt sure how or what to order.  Went up to cashier and she said to me "this will be the best burger you've had in your life" I said great cant wait.......

Quite disappointed!  The burger was good, but not the best.  My bread fell apart and the veggies I asked for were non exsistant.  All I asked for was onions and green pepper and pickles.  I got a piece of each one of them.  Not a slice but a cut piece.  The fries were good, greasy but good and they do give you alot of them.  The regular size could probably feed 2.  There is the peanuts also.  You can eat as much as you want, but they are salty.

Place is ok, but overly hyped.  

Happy Eatings!!

Consistently delicious sandwiches. Of particular note: the 50/50, the Mensch, the brisket cheesesteak. The roast pork and brisket are superb. Fries aren't anything particularly special, but they're certainly not bad. If you're trying to be healthy, you can get a sandwich over lettuce, but come on. Healthy. Like that's a thing.

I've been going to Jake's for a while, since my office is right around the corner. I always get one of their amazing sandwiches, usually the fresh pork. Today I opted for the pork cheek chili. It may have been the best chili I've ever had. It was amazing. Perfectly seasoned and spicy. The meat was tender and delicious. And the serving size was what you would expect from Jake's. Another huge thumbs up for my favorite lunch spot.

Delicious. The BBQ brisket sandwich is flavorful and the fried pickle is over the top. It's ~$9-10 for a sandwich and they're filling. They also offer their sandwiches over lettuce which looked appetizing also. Cool vibe with something for everyone.

To be honest, after having a tony luke's pork sandwich not many places can get positive reviews for a provolone rabe pork sandwich.  This place was good, but not great. The broccoli rabe was way over cooked - tasted like they got canned broccoli rabe and then steamed it to death. The pork was great but could've used a little sauce, and the provolone was added on the top instead of within the sandwich so when I bit into it the cheese would pop out and barely be with the bite of pork. My sisters both loved their sandwiches, the farmers market and the meatball sub. Overall B+, I probably won't be coming back since its 10$ a sandwich.

I always order pizza and wings from here. I must say every time it is delicious! I have tried different salads especially baby arugula salad was the best. I highly recommend to order from this place! They have a sitting area as well however most of the time I am ordering pick up due to time constraints.

best in the food court :)
the service is awesome, love the people there....

I must say as a vegetarian they had many options.  Calaloo was good, lil oily but yum.  Yams, dumpling, etc fresh n full of taste.  Veg pattie very yummy.  Loved the scotch bonnet hot sauce.  Returning

They could use some more seasoning on their beef sandwiches I felt like they were a little bland and I had the wasabi cheesestake & the garlic bomb I put the Chile sauce on both of them which made them better and the role on my wasabi was not fresh,like the chocolate covered bacon tho.

My go-to pizza delivery place. The pinwheel pizza is seriously huge and they use the perfect amount of sauce to cheese ratio.  The bread used for the hot sandwiches is fresh and I would recommend the mozzarella sticks and zucchini sticks - both are very tasty. I've also had the shakes which were delivered cold while the rest of the food is always hot. Very quick delivery.

Husband and I were craving some fried chicken wing, my friend recommended soho cafe. But since soho was closed due to holiday, we yelped to see who else have bon chon like wings. We concluded to the following ..

Pro

- the wings were still crispy after 1 hr car ride (Traffic was bad today )

Con 
- they did not valid their 10% off and said it was for drinks only. 
- each order came with French fries. (Wish they indicated that somewhere on the menu). I ordered extra French fries not knowing .. I assume they come with pickled radish like bon chon

All in all. The place was pretty good if you're looking for bonchon like wings
A couple days ago I came here with my mother and I must say that my food was very tasty. However I've been on the toilet for days now.

Pretty good sandwich. The food was great and so was the service, but it wasn't really what I wanted. The sriraccha spread was a little bit too much for me and the pork was a tad but dry. 

I may not have been in the mood for the type of food that Jake's had to offer. I'll have to give them another try and see if the taste suits my craving better.
Went back again and got the crispy sandwich double with onion rings. So good and tasty. That chicken is huge and so tasty. Love the crunch and freshness of the vegetable.

I used to love Jake's, but the last two times I've been in, I've gotten the fattiest brisket ever.  I'm fine with a little fat, but these were SLICES of fat with no meat attached to them whatsoever.  Take a little bit more time to prep your meat, guys.

the gringo sandwich is effing delicious. very nice folks here. love when someone recognizes my pokemon tattoo lol that's probably why I'm leaving this review. but seriously, the pulled pork is on point, and the menu is very big so I will be returning when i'm hungry and when my pokemon evolves
The 50/50 was decent, but the pork was dry. Kept having to irrigate with water.  But good taste.  Fries were fantastic.

We don't have these in Boston, but I know Potbelly from trips to Chicago. It's good for a quick inexpensive lunch when you're on the go. Here, they even have a few tables outside so you can people watch and catch some rays while you eat. I usually get the meatball, it's warm and melty and yummy in my tummy.

Sandwich was one of the best I've had in a while. Got the Mensch that had the perfect amount of horseradish and everything came together so well. The price is higher than most lunch spots, but the quality makes it definitely worth it as every part of the sandwich was amazing! I definitely  will be coming back for a long time.

Went here for the first time and I tried the garlic bomb, now something called the garlic bomb should have a ton of flavor, which it did.  The roll was perfect and the fried garlic cloves made this sandwich extremely tasty.  Next time I go, I plan on getting the Charlie Brown.  

I also went with a few people from work who tried the ghost pepper sandwich.  It always a little strange when they make you sign a waiver before eating anything but they did for that sandwich.  For anyone who loves heat, then this sandwich would be good for them.

First Cheesesteak in Philly. Kept it simple with just a Cheesesteak. Woah! Brisket was nicely seasoned, cooked and splashed with its own gravy. Carmelized onions. Mild provolone and ... Amazing bread! They don't have bread like that in my 'hood. Next time I'll take two ... One for the road.

Even though my sandwich was a 3-star sandwich I'll have to chalk that up to ordering wrong, because my boyfriend's sandwich was a serious 5. 

I got the create-my-own pork with sharp provolone and roasted garlic. I didn't specify my bread and they gave me seeded instead of plain, which isn't a deal breaker but I would have rather had plain. So make sure you specify! The pork was juicy (oily) but without some kind of prevailing condiment it just didn't have a whole lot of "oomph" if you know what I mean. 

The boyfriend got the Mensch: beef brisket, horseradish, melted provolone and carmelized onions on a plain roll. This thing was killer. The bite of the horseradish mixed with the sweet onions really made it awesome, and the brisket just had great flavor. This was the moment I officially decided that I'll take brisket over pork any day (unless of course it's on a pulled pork sandwich slathered in BBQ sauce). 

Obviously they're doing things right here with fresh ingredients and large portions. There is ample seating at tables and at the window overlooking the street, and their Kodiak soda actually tastes just like a Coke (plus, free refills!). I'll definitely be back to try their other sandwiches.

It took me about 20 mins to walk to this place from my work. I spent  a total of 40 mins walking to get food. It was well worth it, even if it was just for the chocolate cover bacon!! Yes chocolate cover bacon. YUM!
I had the roast pork sandwich with sharp provolone, pepers, broccoli rabe, onions and GARLIC. It was DELISH. I will be going back for more!

Gave this place a second chance I guess it's ok way better than any other fast food that serves burgers. It gives that food truck vibe only I know that other  food trucks burgers taste better lol. Anyways yes it's decent still overpriced but worth it once in awhile.
I have had this pizza twice and I have to say the veggie pie is absolutely delicious, I never had a complaint, maybe turn it down on the greasy part, but other then that it's fantastic.
Yeah, its great. Go here get anything be sure to get fries cause they are good. Then find a cozy bench because your gonna need a nice nap after this meal!

We walked by here on our way to Primo's and after a quick look at he menu changes our plans and went in. 

The sandwiches are amazing! Huge portions and around $8 - totally worth it.  I had the midtown chicken - chicken breast, cheddar, mozz, avocado puree - unreal. Plus FREE peanut chews!!!!!

This will def be our new go to lunch spot. 

Highly recommended.

The execution of my midtown turkey was mediocre, despite what I thought was a great idea.  The bread was like 80% of the sandwich, and because of its thickness, all of the fixings (pickled onions and red pepper) on top promptly fell off when I tried to eat it.  The guacamole portion was kind of skimpy as well.  Not sure if I chose the best sandwich.....Some of the pork and brisket options looked pretty appetizing.  Maybe I'll come back for one of those.

Worst chipotle I've ever been to. Unbelievably bad. Not only is the customer service horrendous but they give you the smallest servings at the standard chipotle over priced food. Cold food. Never have enough of anything. Not worth your time. Every employee should quit because they clearly hate their lives

The PokeSpot is a welcome new addition to Philly's assortment of poke restaurants, and is definitely a stand out. Similar to most poke places, you can choose a base, proteins, and toppings. What sets The PokeSpot apart from what you'll find elsewhere in the city? PokeSpot has some bases you can't find elsewhere, like zucchini noodles, if you're into that. They've also got an array of proteins marinated for additional flavor and variety (the chili salmon is AMAZING, spicy tuna was meh, not very spicy), in addition to the standard proteins. And then, of course, you get unlimited toppings (with the exception of the avocado, which is extra. Unless you really love avocado, not sure the upcharge is worth it, with the 1/8th of an avocado tiny portion you get), which is always great. They've got quite a few more toppings that you wouldn't find elsewhere, and some you would find elsewhere but definitely stand out, like the onions that are marinated for extra tastiness. If you want variety and quality, The PokeSpot is definitely worth trying!

habanero chicken and a side of mac n cheese that tastes like kraft
a surprisingly satisfying combo, especially after drinking...

Food quality and service - 4 stars, dining room (sooooo hot in here) 2 stars.

Get it to go!

Jake's has been open 2 days. I have gone to Jake's both days. I'll probably go tomorrow.

Day 1, I went for the free roasted pig sub, apparently just missed it. However they were offering a free combo upgrade (fries and drink). I decided to try the "Jake". I mean the place is called Jake's, it has to be good. It wasn't good, it was fucking amazing. Rib-eye, provolone, fried onions and a roasted pepper laid on top. When you read it you don't really realize you just bought a cheesesteak. The cheese was nicely melted in with the rib-eye, not just laid on top. The roasted pepper was delicious, wish it was even spicier. The fries were awesome, they seem to be double fried or coated in something. Then again, free fries always taste better.

Day 2, I went with the Village Turkey. Fryer roasted turkey, bacon, arugula and cherry spread. They were out of the arugula, so I subbed spinach. Tasted like Thanksgiving, actually it tasted like what I wish Thanksgiving tasted like since my Mom can't cook. 

The only negatives so far are, the sandwich makers are just starting to learn how to make the sandwiches, so it takes a little longer and the cherry spread guy needs to ease up his grip, I don't need a 1/2" layer of spread on my sub.

Finally there is a good sandwich shop in Center City that isn't some shitty chain. Looking at you Subway, Quiznos, Jimmy John's and Potbelly.

This location just opened about a month or so ago. I was surprised and happy to see it go into this shopping center ! I stopped in the other nite to order food to go. The restaurant itself is quite small - about 5 tables max. There were quite a few people that were standing there waiting for their food. (They appeared a bit disgruntled) I could tell they were having some trouble getting things together in the kitchen. It took some time before someone noticed I was patiently still waiting to order. My order was placed and I accepted I was probably going to be waiting some time too with the other folks. To my surprise (and probably to everyone else's frustration - my food came up immediately !) However when I got to the car realized they gave me chicken on the bone and not tenders. Oh well ! It was still good. Everything was hot too. They just seem to be getting settled in to having this new location. . That usually takes some time. It is worth coming back again.

If you find yourself crossing Passyunk where it meets Broad, gettin cranky and in need of a quick, inexpensive little snack for yourself, why don't you stop and get a soft pretzel? I'll point you in the right direction: Look, Philly Pretzel Factory is right there. 

Their pretzels are very good- consistently hot and freshy, soft and dense inside, crispy outside. This location is always sparklin' clean and the employees are friendly. And another thing- Philly Pretzel Factory has this extra hot Dusseldorf mustard that's nice n spicy in that horseradish way that goes zzzziiinnnggg up ya nose, just how I likes it.

We've become regulars who come whenever we get a hankering for Korean fried chicken and the yummy garlic soy wings.  But when we ordered delivery at around 6P during the superbowl, we were told it would take "at least an hour and a half."  We were actually fine with that, figuring we'd have the wings in hand by halftime.  At 7:45P I called to make sure they didn't forget our order and was told "the delivery guy left and is on  his way."  We waited and waited and ... nothing.  Not even a call to apologize.  Unfortunately, you've lost our business Chix and Wings.

I live just a few blocks from this place and I am so happy to have this as an easy option for food. The ingredients are fresh and I just can't get enough of it. The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable about the ingredients. The soy sauce they use is gluten free and they label which sauces are GF and the sweeteners they use in certain sauces are honey. You can get salad greens as the base and I tried that at my most recent trip and I will definitely do it again. For some reason it seemed like a small bowl to me when I first got one but once I was done I realized it was plenty. I think the prices are reasonable when you take into account how much you would be spending on a similar roll of sushi that had similar ingredients and would be a lot less food in volume. Anyway, I highly recommend this place. It's a fabulous, quick, healthy food option for the area and I'm sooo happy it's here!

I almost never review established chain restaurants like Chipotle because I don't think they or other people care, but maybe they do care these days since their image is going down. Unfortunately, this location is not doing much to improve it. Chipotle is awesome because its supposed to consistently deliver a delicious, nutritious, and filling meal at a reasonable price. Twice in a row now, they've ran out of my two favorite toppings (fajita veggies and corn) around 9:30 PM. I realize that's late and ingredients run out, but for a chain like Chipotle that has its daily inventory needs down to a science, this should not happen twice in a row. I go to a chain like Chipotle and not the local burrito place because consistency and quality is expected based on its brand name. In them trying to save a few dollars on potentially not wasting that extra batch of corn and veggies, they will lose many customers that will just stop coming past 9 PM. Just make the extra batch, guys. 

Also, their rice here was wack. Barely warm, many kernals seemed either uncooked or overcooked - basically dry and inedible. 

Going to Qdoba next time.

Currently battling sleep at my office desk...that's right I am in an official food coma!

I stopped by Jake's to pick up lunch today. Got the turbacon and a side of fried pickles. Do you miss thanksgiving? Well today I did but my craving was fully satisfied. The turbacon has turkey, stuffing, gravey, hashbrowns, and cranberry sauce all on a roll. It's a dream come true. 

The fried pickles were also delicious! They came in slices the size of silver dollars with a sriracha mayo dipping sauce. Yum yum!

This never was my preferred place for repeat pizza order but I was told that the person buying wanted to try something new.

An order was placed for a pepperoni pizza and an appetizer.  The food was delivered in a reasonable amount of time but found out seconds after I closed the door, they never delivered the appetizer.

we immediately called and advised we are missing an item from the order and requested if we could just cancel. We were told there are no cash refunds. So, this appears to be a regular thing for them because it is posted on their online menu.

I am guessing they have a quality control issue as I've seen other reviews indicated food being bad to terrible With no cash refunds being the reply. 

The pizza itself wasn't terrible but it wasn't something I would actually intentionally order again.   The appetizer that was something unique and definitely something I enjoyed so I don't want to completely bash the place.  

When the appetizer arrived, it took about 30 mins for it to show up.  It was absolutely made fresh and it was very hot, which is never a bad thing.  Unfortunately, it has confirmed my theory that they never made it to begin with so the driver could've never turned around and just dropped it off.

There are tons of pizza places in Mayfair, most of them are not very good to downright terrible.  This establishment just joined the rest of the trend for the area.
Best milkshake I've ever had. Literally amazing and would recommend to anyone, they are simply the best!!

I really like five guys. This particular location is very clean and the staff is extremely friendly. Today I went for the bacon cheeseburger and it did not disappoint! For a fat food joint I think the burgers are spot on. I do not care for their fries though so I skip those. The wait can be a bit long at times. I will be back! Solid 4 stars.

I think Potbelly is a great place to get a sub.  The subs are fresh and priced about the same as either Subway or Quiznos, but I think they are far better than either of those two competitors.  I highly recommend the ham and swiss which is delicious toasted.  A lot of people just get the subs here, but you should also try the milkshakes and some of their cookies.  Both are almost equally as good as the subs.
You guys suck ..went to eat 8pm n it was closed ...suppossed to be open till 10 pm ....

Reasons why my coworker thinks I am a weirdo:

I get my (roast) pork sandwich from Jake's with au jus, garlic spread, raw onions, broccoli rabe, and sharp provolone... come into the office, and make her hold it to marvel in its weight.

I then take a picture of the sandwich, to post to my twitter feed of course, with the caption "Now that's a fucking sandwich".

Once I start eating said sandwich, I start moaning things like "Ohhhh my goddd, I never want this sandwich to end." Please take note: I'm not even half way through it at this point.

She leaves to run an errand and here I am, sitting at my desk staring at the other half of this monster sandwich half in defeat, half trying to find the willpower to make it through the whole thing because yes, it's really that fucking good.

As of right now I have about a quarter of it left, and I took a break to write a yelp review. This sandwich is taxing. I'm definitely going to be suffering from some itis after I finish it but god damn, I can't let this thing go to waste. Plus it's so moist from the jus, that I wouldn't be able to save it for later because it will totally fall apart.

But yeah, get it. Because it's seriously probably one of the best roast pork sandwiches I've had in the city.

From the time that I worked around the corner from a Potbelly in 2004, I have adored their tasty sandwiches with a particular weakness for the Italian on wheat.  A few years have passed and since that time, they have added variety in offerings (salads) and sizes (skinny, original, or large for sandwiches), as well as a calorie count.  Well, after seeing the comparative calories on the chalkboard, I skipped the Italian and opted for the Turkey Sandwich and was pleased with my slightly healthier, toasted delight.  Potbelly continues to offer a solid sandwich option in my book.

Tip: you can ask for light mayo (even though it's not listed) and you should not miss the hot peppers which add a delicious kick of spice and vinegar.

Good and fresh poke bowls! I made my own bowl with 3 scoops of protein. The fish was fresh and all ingredients had a great taste! I could only wish more toppings and maybe a bit larger bowls with bigger scoops or more rice. Overall this was a good experience but not significantly better than other poke bowl places in Chinatown!

Still love Jake's.  Just got back from the free levelup lunch.  Wanted to update my review to let all those bread-phobic members of the yelp community that you can get a naked bowl.  I had pork, sharp provolone, crushed chili, broccoli rabe, and horseradish in a bowl.  It was delicious and I could only eat half.  "No one eats carbs anymore."

Been to lots of events in and around Philly for my whole life.  I have eaten a lot of roast beef sandwiches and this place, hands down, has THE BEST ROAST BEEF I have ever had.  It wasn't too wet, but the roll held the moisture well.  The taste of the beef was fresh and seasoned perfectly.  It's all you need - just the sandwich.

The menu is limited, but stick to the roast beef.

You will experience SOUTH PHILLY ettiquite... not overly friendly, even if you DO speak Italian, which the owner does.  Probably came off the boat 50 years ago, but he is a staple in the community to which he belongs.   

It is a tiny, quaint place - don't bring a crowd or you will have to walk Broad Street with you food.  

ONE NOTE - it is hard to find!!  We walked up and down the block and my boyfriend had been there before.  There is purple neon on the window and a the name is a decal on the window.  There is NO SIGN, other than the menu on a chalkboard on the sidewalk., at the bottom of the steps.

I did say quaint....

ENJOY!!!!!

Excellent bowls and the wings are great too.  The only Negative is their not-so-fresh veggies that come with the wings.  If they are brown, they might be better off not including them with the meal.  

Will still come back.  I hope they do a visual check in the future.

I was wrong about chipotle, I've been a fan of qdoba for so long and vowed to NEVER give chipotle a chance lol. My first experience at this location was terrible. I ordered a burrito bowl and they were out of cheese!!! I thought my corn was entirely way too sweet. I hated my meal. I gave them another chance this time at the city av location. I had a chicken burrito bowl with plenty of cheese and guac with an amazing side of chips. I used to think qdoba had the best chips, now on a good day their chips can give chipotle a run for their money. But if the chips aren't fresh you can get a stale batch. Chipotle chips have this wonderful crunch qdoba can only dream of having. I would prefer a little less salt but still very good. Now this guacamole, my goodness I'm in love with the overall quality. My only complaint is the long lines. But I'm an official fan now

Ive been wanting to try this place for some time but everytime I've been in the area the line has been too long. So today I had a enough time to stop in and the line seemed long at first but moved quickly and after I ordered my Jake Cheesesteak it arrived moments later. The soda selection consisted of Birch Beer, Cherry Soda, Cream and other classics. 
The sandwich looked great with long Jalepeno Peppers laid across the meat. The bread was terrific with a great soft center and crusty outside. However, after the bread and neatly placed pepper, the sandwich took a turn towards blandsville. The quality of the meat was good but it had no real flavor and should of been drained a little better. The provelone had no real bite to it and I think to pair with the peppers it should of been a sharp provelone. 
I had high expectations for jake's and I am sure ill give it one more chance but will trying one of the pork sandwichs next.

The only reason I was able to give 2 stars is because the fries were good. I'm not sure what Checkers did but the burgers aren't good anymore. Not sure what kind of hybrid meat they're using but tastes off. To place an order felt uncomfortable as the girl working the window had an attitude. Trash overflowing in parking lot and bird bodily fluids on tables and chairs. I used to have good memories of Checkers.

This is one of favorite spots for lunch or a quick dinner. I love the menu, their wings and Mac n cheese are delicious and mouth watering. I also love their rice bowls, they give you the option to choose between white and brown rice, and what kind of meat you'd like in your bowl. My favorite is the sesame chicken salad, I never order salads from fast food places because they're always very bland, and not well put together, but the salads at Chix & Wings are very good. I love this place, and service is not that bad either.
If you've never tried a Tahina Milkshake, do it! When I saw this menu item, I did not hesitate. The Turkish Coffee was recommended so that's the one I tried and it was absolutely incredible.

Delicious! Very fresh tasting, good rice, lots of toppings options.

I went here with my boyfriend for dinner, but it would make a perfect lunch. I got the smaller poke bowl, which was the perfect amount of food for me. My bf got the bigger one and was still a little hungry afterwards. We both did build your own brown rice bowls with fish. I got the wasabi yuzu sauce which was yummy but maybe a little too much (I usually think salads have too much dressing), and bf got his without dressing. The dried mushroom was very delicious, I guess it was rehydrated because it wasn't really dry but it had an intense mushroom flavor I really liked.

Planning to go back soon!

So good! Came to philly for work and had to try this place out. Staff is friendly, food is off the charts!! I've been twice already. The ingredients taste fresh and to die for! I also got the soup, which was perfect for the cold rainy weather. The broccoli cheeses was rich in taste. The was a beautiful bite of cheddar cheese as well as a warm broccoli aroma. It was the perfect temperature and each spoon full was a burst of yummy again and again.

3.5 stars
First, I didn't know this was a chain until I saw one in D.C. a little disappointed. I only came here for breakfast and it seems it's not a popular choice. There was plenty of room and it took ages to get my oatmeal with bananas and nuts. In fact, the bananas looked like they'd seen better days. I think I skipped some ingredients because of the delay.

I'd probably try this place for a lunch time sandwich and forgive the slow service on my first visit.

This 5 Guys location is massive! The food was mostly up to par, but I have to agree with a previous commenter that the fries were a bit undercooked (not as crisp). They had Mr. Pibb (Pibb Xtra) in the fountain... I can't remember the last time I've had Mr. Pibb... pre-millenium?

What I like most about this place is that the floor isn't slippery! @15th I can be standing still and I just slowly start heading off in a direction. I especially hate it when I'm sitting down and I keep sliding. Overall, this is a better area. There are almost no bums and very few obnoxious kids.

Other than that, I've been getting the same exact thing since 5 Guys opened on 15th and in this 4-5 year period the price has gone up about $1.50. For a regular drink, fries, and a cheeseburger it's $10.99. Where do you draw the line 5 Guys? If it weren't for this latest price hike, I'd give 4 stars. I repeat, WHERE DO YOU DRAW THE LINE!? For $11 there are much better options around.

Lastly, dining on walnut 11th-broad is better than dining on chestnut 15th-18th (liberty place included).

All things chicken in one place.  Wings, bowls--which are a choice of rice, topped with chicken.  One of the rice choices was soy lime, so I have to go back for that one.  I ordered the fried chicken sandwich.  The bun was fresh, it had a good amount of chicken strips, the batter reminded me of teriyaki.  Wasn't a lot of flavor to the chicken, I'd describe the flavor as "deep fried".  Fries had a nice crisp texture and were hot.  No complaints but not a wow experience.  It's on my list of places to stop when I want fried, or want chicken.  The bowls intrigue me so I'll be back for one of those.   Lots of flavor choices with the wings but I'm not a wing guy.

I walk by this place all the time but actually made my way in for the first time today...and it was an awesome decision! 
The staff is super friendly and the food was delicious. I had the chicken tenders, which were HUGE (I couldn't even finish 4), with Mac n cheese and fries. They also have a variety of sauces. Everything was great...and the pricing isn't bad at all. I'll definitely be going back!

I ordered the Fire Bowl, easy on the Fire, and let me tell you it was delicious! The fresh salmon. The shrimp. A touch of spicy mayo. All over white rice. You can't beat a light healthy lunch like the ones at Red Poke Express.

I ordered thru Yelp and it was ready in a jiffy!

Not my first time there and it won't be my last.

One of the better options on Walnut b/w 39th and 40th. It's a standby for a decent sit down burrito place. I usually get the naked vege burrito bowl (guac comes free -- YAY for being vegetarian!). It's relatively clean, though the dim lighting makes this place a sad establishment to eat at.
The roast beef with horseradish mayo and jalapeño did not disappoint.

i went back for the new year. everyone or business deserve a second chance, well the food was hot, the service was excellent and friendly. looks like a new staff :) do  recommend .... wow Popeyes in Roxborough!! AND THEY HAVE DINNER SPECIALS

I found this place on a Sky magazine or something and heard there was a roast pork sandwich with sharp provolone. I'm a HUGE fan of Dinic's in the Reading Terminal but the line is always ridiculous so my boyfriend and I tried this out as an alternative. 

It's a great substitute! Definitely different but equally tasty in it's own way. My faves are the barnyard and the 50/50 sooooo goooooood. And plentiful. And get some fries while you're at it!

A word of advice though: Don't come here to get a cheesesteak. It is not that place.  There are a million places in Philly you can get a good cheesesteak from and this is not one of them. They also have some sandwich that has a whole long deep fried pepper on it (can't remember the name) but that one is average.

If I was grading the restaurant a year ago before I had tried the cheese steak (a friend got it) or the pepper one, I would have given it a 5star hands down.
Avoid lunchtime at all costs unless giant crowds of babbling Penn kids are your thing. Avoid move-in week all together.
Good quality Philly cheese steak with creative options. Had to have one during our short stay. Jakes is an all around pleaser for kids and adults.

Everytime I come back to Philadelphia, I have to stop by Jake's.  The sandwiches are among my favorite in the city, and that's not easy - there's some pretty stiff competition.  I'd say the Barnyard and the Mensch are among my favorites, but I've tried nearly all the menu items, and so far not a single thing has been disappointing.  Keep up the great work - I will continue spreading the word as much as I can.
If chicken wings with the fine hairs left on and Mac and cheese soup (perhaps it was from a can) sound appealing eat here. Idk the chicken sandwiches  looked good should have gotten that.

We had Jake's Sandwich Board on our radar for weeks and finally made it out there for lunch on Saturday out in the city...

Food: 4.0 stars
The bread the delicious (the perfect combo of soft and toastiness).  My fiance and I shared the ITALIAN (Grilled) and the 50/50.  These sandwiches are delicious and different than your run of the mill sandwiches.

-- 50/50- The sandwich has bacon on top of the some of the best pulled pork I've had with a tasty sriraccha sauce.
-- Italian- Your classic italian sandwich with a good balance of onions and red peppers

Service: 3.5 stars
Service is prompt.  They made sandwiches fast and properly.

Location: 3.5 stars
12th and Sansom

Price:
Two sandwiches, fries, and two drinks will run just above $20.  Expect ~$10 per person.

Ambiance: 4.0 stars
They have a flat screen TV to enjoy sports and the restaurant is large with a classic feel.


Overall: 4.0 stars
Great sandwiches with a great vibe.  Definitely give it a shot if you're in the area.  You wont regret it... and you'll probably be back for more.

Went here with my boyfriend and we both got the spicy fried chicken sandwich. We both liked the fried chicken itself, and the spicy sauce added a nice kick. The food came out quickly, and the employee was friendly. However, we found the portion size to be pretty small. We were also confused by the beverage selection. My boyfriend wanted a diet coke, but the only beverages they had were water and plain seltzer water. As a fan of seltzer, I was okay with this, but it seems like a poor business decision since I know a lot of restaurants make a lot of money from soda. Overall, definitely better than Wishbone down the street. I would go to Hatch & Coop again, but a few things could be improved.
They had no meat to make cheesesteaks!!! How does that happen on a Saturday night??? You go through craziness trying to park and get in there to discover they were not prepared. Shame.

I have no clue how this place has positive reviews.  Hadn't ordered from here in a while, and now I remember why. The fried food is NASTY. Almost seems like it would take effort to make it this bad. 

Mozzarella sticks were so dry and the fries were the worst I've ever had. I'll stick to Pizza Roma, George's Burgers, and Renzi's. I drank a half a gallon of Iced tea to wash down this horrible food LOL

I. Love. Five Guys. Their burgers are so good I don't need a bun and I never get a gluten reaction from their fries. I also love the peanuts and free refills. This is definitely my favorite Philly location. Get yourself a double cheeseburger, damnnnn.

We like to order out once/twice a week bc our family is very busy. I was super excited when I came in to the area because the advertise and offer gluten free pies. I ordered it every week the past few weeks, and it is the best pie hands down without having to downtown. My only gripe is that I'm gluten free because I have celiac disease and although I have been calling and requesting I can't reach anyone directly to find out if they are going to continue to accommodate our demographic. Any foresight is appreciated.
My favorite lunch place in Philly with amazing cheesesteaks for some reason took cheesesteaks off the menu. That decision deserves one star.

There isn't really much to say about this place accept for inexpensive food. I've tried some of their more unique offerings, the potato pierogie burrito and the chicken carbie burrito and each one was really bland. After seeing a co-worker come to lunch a few times with a bag full of food from there, I went again and got the original chicken burrito and some chips with cheese and salsa. Its ok, I feel like this is food that a random snack bar would serve. Its cash only and only open for lunch during the week so those are other possible downsides for customers.
I had a volcano bowl with yellow tail and tuna. It was pretty good and they were so nice to put a chair outside for me as I was with my puppy.

We poke everywhere and this is quite possibly the best Poké I have had in Philly.  And second only to Poké in Toronto.  The price and quality beat any place I've ever been to and the service is fantastic here. Don't be daunted by parking in the city! There is plenty here.  Love this place!

We ordered delivery from Jakes about 45 min before closing. We weren't sure if they'd still deliver so close to closing but they did. They closed at 9 but the delivery showed up at 9:25 (estimated delivery 9:10 so a little over). But this was forgivable since it was the last delivery of the night so I'm sure the delivery guy had a bunch of places to get to.

Now to the food. By the time we got the food, it was cold. BUT that didn't take away from the deliciousness!! We made our own brisket sandwich which was AMAZING. The brisket was phenomenally flavored. The crispies we got on the sandwich wasn't crispy anymore.... but still a great sandwich. 

The fries and onions were cold as well. BUT they were still shockingly yummy! I don't like cold onion rings bc they taste greasy, but I devoured those fried onions like nobody's business. The fries were also perfectly salted. I recommend the mixed bag of fries/onions because it's the best value. 

I can't wait to try the food when it's hot!

Stop by on a Monday around 3ish, were the only customers in there. Split a 50/50 and a Charlie Brown with an order of fries and some birch beer to wash it down. 50/50 was perfect combo of pork and bacon with a delish siracha spread. Charlie Brown cheesesteak was meh, nothing great but not terrible. I enjoyed the fries, perfect crunch and some good sauces to dip in. Would check this place out again if I'm in the area to try some of the other sammies on the menu.

I've visited the original Goldie location a couple of times and I am a big fan! However, I am not a big fan of parking in center city. Luckily, there is a Goldie (AND a dizengoff!)  in the WF food court. 

I was there around 1:30pm but there was still a big line. Unfortunately, the food court is very tightly spaced and there are baby strollers everywhere waiting to take you down, but that's not their fault. 

Today I got the harissa falafel sandwich and shawarma fries. I thought the food was pretty much on point with what you get at the original location (i.e., very good.) The falafel is wonderfully light and the pita is very soft and thick. The harissa sauce was on the saltier side.. it probably would have tasted more balanced if it had a little bit more vegetables. 

It came out at a reasonable speed despite how busy it was. They give you buzzers to know when your order is up. The woman at the register seemed stressed and seemed a bit annoyed with her job. The two cooks appeared a bit frazzled too. 

I don't think I would recommend taking the sandwich to go, as the crispy falafel is best eaten ASAP and the sauce would probably make the pita soggy.
The Turbacon is an excellent sandwich.  Every Monday the pork sandwiches are $5 all day.

Don't particularly enjoy this food court, because it is stuffy with kitchen heat, and not special. But I keep coming back because of its central location. It is quicker and cheaper than the other nearby upenn facilities. I liked quiznos brand at one point and this one could bring me back into the fold. Everyone notices how extremely nice and conscientious the employees are. And they make a darn good sandwich. I don't want for much else. I would give 4 stars if only the cookies and chips/ combos didn't cost well over a buck but at these prices I had to take a pass on dessert. They are asking too much for ordinary items which are elsewhere for considerably less. I understand this is more a fault of the chain than this particular proprietor.

I was really looking forward to a whole roasted pig sandwich with roasted peppers and good provolone cheese.  What a major disappointment.  I do have to say that the staff was exceptionally friendly, but the food fell sadly short.  Why bother to go to the trouble of actually roasting a pig when you're not going to season it, and you're going to cook it until it's dry?  Even with the au jus that they put on it, the meat was still bone dry.  All the jus just made the bread soggy.  Not to mention, they were out of cracklings, served me seeded bread when I ordered plain (in writing), and the roasted peppers were *green* and still had a significant amount of skin attached...not at all the flavorful red roasted peppers you can expect in a place that really knows about food.  Even the provolone didn't have much flavor, although maybe I'm spoiled by places that actually serve good sharp provolone on their sandwiches...and for less $.

I've been to Jake's many times and always had a great roast pork sandwich, but this time I went with Alie A's recommendation and got the skinny chicken sandwich.  I wasn't disappointed.

The chicken itself was tender and juicy and the roasted peppers and onions added a lot of flavor to the sandwich.
