The bread, while soft and fresh, has too many seeds on it for me, but you can order your sandwich on a non-seeded roll.  One of these times I'll remember to do that.  They also have really good, salty french fries.

My only real complaint is that I wish they had more spreads that were non-mayo based.  I even said something to the girl behind the counter last time I was there and she told me a lot of people were saying that, so hopefully that will change in the near future.

I was very cautious about going to this place at first. I heard a lot of mixed reviews before I decided to try it out. I don't know why everyone was giving this place grief. Jake's is unbelievable! Its Garlic Bomb is out of this world. Don't listen to all these self proclaim critics. They're to busy having their nose so far up in the air that they can't see how amazing the food is right in front of them. If you're looking for an authentic go-to brisket place, Jake's is definitely it. I go their 12th street location at least twice a week. Definitely go try it out and find out for yourself. I promise you that you will not be disappointed!

Have had both the smooth and creamy rice bowl and the spicy sayce rice bowl - I liked the smooth and creamy option a little better but both are very good, especially for the price ~ $7. The bowl comes with white or brown rice and a little salad, shredded carrots and broccoli are also in the bowl. It is a good amount of food for just one person and may last you two meals if you're not a big eater. It's a great lunch or dinner option and it is prepared very fast, less than 10 minutes.

Great spot if you want quality, Americanized Mexican food at a fantastic price (i.e., $1.19 for a taco). I would recommend anything there but would have to vouch for the classics: original burrito, hard shell corn taco, nachos. The Crunch & Munch is a Hot Tamales original that is another great recommendation. Atmosphere is on point as well with hits from the 80s on repeat. Also, wait time for your food is almost nothing. Lastly, don't forget it's cash only.

Omg!!!! Haven't experienced outstanding customer service in a long time. Josh and Manny are beyond a great example of customer service. Keep up the good work guys. They were nice to every customer who walked through that door. Good job best pretzel factory ever!!!

Ive been to several Five guys locations and they never disappoint. This one is no different. 

Staff is friendly, Food us tasty (ordered the little cheeseburger with onions mushrooms lettuce tomato) and fries. Lots of places to sit and eat. 

Will be coming back here next time I'm craving a burger!

This place is awesome!  The Mensch is my favorite with a close second going to the 50/50.  I usually go with the Mensch because my coworker and I usually split an order of Farm Fries as well. We're big eaters and we walk out of their stuffed.

Careful around lunch time because it will most likely be packed but they still sling their sandwiches quickly.  You can call ahead but you may still get stuck in line since they don't have a seperate pick up spot.  The food is so good that doesn't bother me though.

My wife dragged me into this poke place and told me that I "must try it". I'm a smart man to listen to my wife! I ordered a crazy mixture of all sorts of poke, stuff, toppings and sauces. On top there were three different kinds of sushi chunks.  All of it was on a bed of brown rice. I wolfed the whole thing down in three minutes it was so tasty. Do not hesitate to try this place - it was absolutely fabulous.

Good not great food and overpriced, check somewhere else to eat. The employees are on the doochey side too if you know what I'm sayin. I told the delivery driver next time my food comes cold I'm gonna slap the balls off you and he just smiled and said thank you have a good night.

Okay so I stopped in here strictly on impulse as I'm making a greater effort to try new places. I love that the place is dimly lit. I'm not a fan of bright lights especially when I'm dining. The 2 tiered layout is interesting. They even have a wheelchair lift inside. The staff was surprisingly friendly. Could they be taking a cue from Jimmy John's?

So I ordered a pizza sandwich (pepperoni and cheese) and it suffers the same fate as subway's BLT. If I don't get vegetables the sandwich is flimsy as hell. If I do get vegetables, I don't even taste the meat because they were so stingy with it. Potbelly has some kind of special pepper concoction they use, and it really has some bite too it. The peppers and onions were some of the best I've had, but uh... it's no substitute for meat.

Since it was my first time there they let me get a free cookie (it was good). Another plus is that there were free refills AND they had raspberry Nestea in the fountain. YES! If it weren't for that, those peppers would've burned the hell outta my mouth and I'd be giving 2 stars. They have milkshakes too, but I had business to take care of I didn't want business to take care of me 30 minutes later.

Overall, the term "potbelly" doesn't have anything to do with the meat on the sandwich... at least not the pizza sandwich. It's really named after a potbelly stove. I'm gonna try this place at least 1 more time and I'm gonna get a sandwich with meat on it and see if I can't give this place 4 stars. If not, then the search for new food continues.

Read about this place online before we came to visit Philly and decided to try it out since my son was demanding cheesesteaks for lunch.  We ordered the Cheesesteak (it was brisket, which I don't think is traditional), a BBQ (which is also brisket with BBQ, sautéed onions, and fried pickles), and an order of fries.  The sandwiches were pretty good, though my oldest son said he should've ordered the non-seeded roll and liked the Philly Cheesesteaks at school better, and my youngest wouldn't even eat it :/ Whatever, I'm not sure they have great taste in food anyway...they'd eat Kraft Mac&Cheese for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  Their sandwich was a little bland for my tastebuds, but the BBQ was much better...just added some sriracha for some kick!  If I was to go again I would leave my kids at home and order the 50/50...OH, and the fries were LOVED by everyone...yay!!

Jakes=Form without substance. I like meat. I am from TX so grilled animal is a staple next to milk. This place has has all the right signage but doesn't follow through.  I took a cheat day off my diet for this place and should have walked out after the first bite. Why?

1. Bland bread. Tons of great local bakeries in Phila and they must buy from Acme. No taste and immediately went soggy.
2. Dry overdone ribeye. Teach the cooks to tell doneness by sight and make them pass a test or something,
3. Decent but unimpressive  brisket. After the ribeye sandwich debacle, a decent brisket was welcome. But ANYONE can slow cook a brisket to taste great.  All of  their trappings had me expecting a smoked marinated masterpiece not something I threw into my own slow cooker  on the way to work. 

Come on guys, raise your game! The now defunct Smoked Joint restaurant had tons better food  by far and THEY WENT OUT OF BUSINESS.

If you want a real ribeye sandwich fix try john's pulled pork by the south Philly ikea.

For all you Soho - Bonchon chicken fans: Compared to Soho the sauce is not "completely" on point. However, I must say, for center city, this is not bad at all. Also, the price is "slightly" cheaper that soho, and the wings are definitely bigger. 

Cons: All the unnecessary side choices. They are a bit cheap on the portion of the sides (radish, rice). They charge an extra $2.00 for sides, and the sides don't really seem that fresh. The false advertisement of being "Korean." I'm sorry but I didn't see a single Korean person working there, nor do I think it is even Korean owned. 

Pros: Convenience, local, worth the price. 
I recommended this place to my eye doctor who is a huge fan of soho, he said he liked it too. This place was pretty empty when I went here. I was here twice for take-out. 

Recommendation: go with double fried spicy or soy garlic!

As with all Chipotles, the food here is quite good. Personally, I am partial to the steak burrito with double meat. However, a few things hold this location back. For one, the lines can become astoundlingly long during peak hours. Like, there are people out the door at noon waiting for their burritos. Another complaint is that several members of the staff are just over the top in their efforts to make conversation and seem cheery. I would much prefer they simply take my order and allow me to proceed to the next station rather than demand to know what I'm up to, if I'm particularly hungry today, whether I've been to the bar represented on the t-shirt I'm wearing, etc.

Again, good food, but there are better Chipotles out there.

Not Cafe Soho's Korean style double fried wings at all!

Although they mention it in the flyers in the restaurant, this place unfortunately can't compare to the Cafe Soho franchise wings.

Overall, the wings were crispy and well cooked, the size for the wings were average, altougth the drumsticks were on the larger side.  The wings weren't too fatty overall, but it would have been nice if my wings were tossed in some kind of sauce rather than just served plain.

The included sauce was sweet, and it seemed like it came straight from a giant jug somewhere in the back of the kitchen.

My included side of mash potatoes was warm and soft, about on par with Boston Market quality.


3/5 stars for food, 4/5 stars for service.

Maybe, I will come back for the chicken bowl combo, but will probably avoid the expensive average chicken wings until they make a "real" Double Fried Chicken.

Why did I bother the time to put in my order 3 hours ahead of time and pay in advance so that I can show up and find that the order  isn't ready yet? Instead of a serious apology she tells me to sit down and wait while they get my order ready.

We tried Jakes because we were starving and it was close. Also, when we looked it up we saw that they had "cheese steaks."  Well they did but not the traditional Philly cheese steak subs. Jake's was brisket on a hoagy with caramelized onions and provolone. Don't get me wrong, it was tasty. The brisket was tender and juicy. The crunchy onions and fries were also good. The place it self is classic sandwich shop deco. 

Overall, we liked it and if in the area again we will come back.

After the potbelly in my town closed a long time ago, I was excited to find out that there was one in center city just a short walk from my office. 

My experience was decent, the employees were all friendly, the resturant was clean and I had a pretty good sandwich, but it just wasn't what I remembered. For starters, adding mushroom to your sandwich is 60 cents extra. And I recall them selling pickles on the side which I didn't see on the menu. 

I would probably go back to Potbelly, make try their "pick two" option, but it won't be at the top of my list.

They changed their name to Chix and Wings! I walked passed it twice before coming inside. The owners are really nice. I ordered soy garlic and French fries. I tried to get dice radish, but they didn't have any. 

Having high expectations of korean BBQ wings, these wings didn't even come close. The texture of the fried wing was literally fried chicken. The sauce itself was thick, almost a bbq texture. Then it was sprinkled with actual sesame seeds! As for the fries, it came in a whole basket!  After a few minutes, the lady gave me diced radish for free. They were delicious. Fresh and cool. It was really kind of her to give me diced radish! 

Disappointing for the wings.. Maybe it was just the soy garlic! I'd come back for the radish though for sure.

Have been on a poke kick over the last six months and tried the 5-6 spots in the area. Would have to say this is the best of them all. First and foremost, the ingredients are extremely fresh and the place is immaculate. The Salmon and Yellowtail is as good as any expensive sushi restaurant. The Eel is awesome. Ten sauce selections. All ingredients are light and not at all greasy. The staff is very friendly and helpful.  This is the best combination of healthy, delicious and affordable I can think of in the entire city!!

I was just visiting Philly for a month when I stumbled upon this place, and I'm so glad I did! This is some of the best chicken ever. I had the rotisserie chicken salad and it was so fresh and tasty! Then I tried the boneless wings and they were perfectly crispy and delicious. I absolutely love this place! It can take a while to make the food, but that's because they make it fresh, so it is worth the wait (and i doesn't take that long, it's just not like a drive through). However, you can call in your order or order through Yelp if you don't want to wait when you get there. The kitchen is open behind the order counter so you can see them making your food which is cool. There's not a whole lot of seating because the place is somewhat small.

I've been to Jake;s and love the sandwiches.  Recently placed an order for home delivery.
Very impressed!  Sandwich was excellent, well packaged and even the milk shake came with an extra glass.  Today, when most services are slapdash, Jake;s packaging and thoughtful inclusion of condiments, a wet wipe, and even a free mini chocolate, shows a concerted effort toward quality,  You've got to try this place.

I came here with ultra high expectations considering it was voted best roast pork in Philly. I have to say it was OK but definitely didn't meet my expectations. I ordered the classic roast pork and broccoli raab and the 50/50. The roast pork was good however it was a little dry. The broccoli raab didn't complement the provolone cheese like other roast pork sandwiches I've had (Dinics and Paesanos). As for the 50/50 which was much better only because of the sriracha mayo suffered the same short comings as the classic. I was expecting a sandwich that was dripping after every bite. This place is good but doesn't measure up to Paesanos in the Italian Market.

Came here as some food blog said it had one of the best and most unique sandwiches. This place was so gross I felt sick just from the smell of my sandwich. I had the one with pork and rinds on it (totally something I'd LOVE + it was recommended) and I took one bite and gave it to my boyfriend- something I never do! It was sooooo salty and pork was so saucy it hid the texture and flavor of the pork. The sauce had a horrible taste too. There were other mismatched flavors in there that made me want to spit it out! Perhaps I had bad meat? My BF had the fried buffalo cauliflower and it was a tiny portion on a large bun. Bread tasted like gluten free bread (gross!) so we just ate the little pieces... not worth the money either! Hash browns we're good and that served as my lunch 

So, so many good places to get an amazing sandwich in philly and this is not it. Treat yourselves to a great bite elsewhere!

If you are looking for crappy, cheap iceberg lettuce style Tex-Mex that is one step above from Taco Bell, this is the place for you. And I say this as someone who occasionally craves exactly that. 

Tacos are around $1.  I usually get the ground turkey.  The hot sauce is vinegary style and good. 

Today, for some reason I opted for the spicy "beef" chili salad. Unfortunately, it was like 99.9% beans and if it had 1/2 oz of beef on it, I'd be surprised. But besides that, and the fact that they wouldn't sell me an extra side of tortilla chips (it would have been the same price as their nachos) this place is not half bad.  

I can't lie. I will definitely go back.
Jake's was a decent eatery. It's offerings were a unique take on sandwiches in a city known for the Philly Cheesesteak this place does its heritage just fine.
Fast, efficient, friendly, and very patient when I came in to make a 6-sandwich order.

Ordered the mild buffalo and honey BBQ wings with mac and cheese. The wings here are regular size - not the jumbo ones you usually get at wing places. The wings here are not as juicy or tender as the jumbo wings at other wing places (like BWW or at sports bars). At other places it's enough to last two meals but finished it in one here. The mild buffalo wings are good and the right amount of spice. The honey BBQ wings were covered in a little too much sauce. The wings here still have the wing tips included. The mac and cheese was just okay. It was a little too much cheese sauce and wasn't the baked style. There were two small carrot and celery sticks included, but the carrots were brown on the outside. It would probably be better to leave off the celery/carrots if they don't have fresh ones available.
I love Chipotle. This location has super nice people, and they are always friendly and generous with their servings of food. These guys do an awesome job. Keep up the great work!

My boyfriend has been here a few times and loves it. He usually gets the 50/50 sandwich. It was my first time here, I got the Barnyard sandwich, he got the Megillah and we got fries to share. Everything was delicious but for some reason 2 people after us got their orders before ours. Also, there was an employee just standing there, doing nothing, while it was busy. I would've given this place 4 stars but the service sucked. The food was good, very filling too.
Nice, clean, fast lunch. More a takeaway place than eat in but totally acceptable to do so. No table service. No prob. Ingredients fresh and nice. Tastes yummy.
Loved it bc we could make our own cheesesteak bowl! It's such a little gem in center city! It gets packed real fast so don't forget to make a reservation!

Not an encouraging lunch spot for Philly vegetarians.  Well, if you're down with $6 PB&J sandwiches, then you're all set, but otherwise.... meh.  I'm shocked at the brevity of veggie options available here, especially since so many other local chains do a fair job of incorporating healthy and meat-free options into their menus.  I've done the PB salad thing a couple times, but they're honestly just not that good nor worth the price (Corner Bakery's salads, right across the street, are far superior).  

It's too bad, cause Potbelly is right downstairs from my office and I would happily buy an eggplant/tomato mozzarella/veggie anything from them, but no such options exist.  For what it's worth, I've actually noticed that a bunch of people in my office tend to go meat-free for lunch (it's just a lighter way to get through the day....).  Oh well.  I don't eat at these places much anyway, but when given the choice, I'd take a Cosi sandwich over Potbelly any day.

My favorite thing about Philadelphia is all the good sandwich (Hero) shops. I refuse to say Hoagie. In all seriousness you people make a good Hero, but unfortunately this place is not among them. 

I tried this place because the menu looked so enticing. My mouth was literally watering while I waited on line reading the menu. I truly couldn't decide there was so much that looked good. Well thank god my mouth was watering or I wouldn't have been able to swallow the dry tasteless sandwiches I received.  I ordered the Mensch and the 50/50 and couldn't have been more disappointed. 

I ate half of each sandwich and had the other halves wrapped up. I gave them to the homeless guy outside. I thought I was doing a good deed but in retrospect maybe I didn't.

New place to the down town phill went there for first time with my friends today and I ordered the crispy chicken drum stick with sweet chili sauce. I am very surprised to found out that there fried chickens are comparable with Bon Chon Chicken but in a much cheaper price. The service was great and fast. Definitely going to be one of our new place for quick bites now.
My goal is to try every sandwich on the menu. I've had about 10 so far and have not been disappointed yet. The charlie brown (a cheesesteak with bacon and peanut butter) might be my current favorite.

A group of us from work ordered lunch from here. Two of the guys in the group drove to pick it up, so I cannot comment on the shop nor the customer service. I can, however, comment on the disappointment I experienced. After 17 years of eating a veg*n diet, I recently started eating meat again. Prior to eating at Jakes, I had not eaten BBQ pulled pork since I was a kid. So I was really looking forward to it. I ordered the BBQ Pork which, according to the menu, comes with fried pickles and coleslaw - even better! I also ordered chocolate covered bacon. When the guys came back to work with only sandwiches, we were all a bit confused as all of the pickles and coleslaw which should have come with our orders were not included. Our office is in SJ so obviously they weren't going back to get them. Oh well. Then I opened my BBQ pulled pork sandwich to find that the coleslaw and fried pickles were ON the sandwich. Who the hell puts those items on a sandwich without at least disclosing that on the menu?! The way the menu reads, one would typically not assume these items come on the sandwich. Had the menu not been worded so poorly, I (and at least one of my coworkers who ordered the same as me) would have asked for the pickles and coleslaw on the side. The other disappointment was the major lack of BBQ sauce. There was barely any sauce on the bread and none whatsoever on the meat. If I order BBQ pulled pork, I expect it to be heavy on the BBQ sauce. The amount I received on my sandwich barely registered on my tastebuds. That being said, the meat itself was quite tender and delicious. The chocolate covered bacon was great. I would consider going back again now that I know exactly how to order. The potential for a great sandwich is there, but the execution was poor. It would really help this place to rewrite the menu to be more specific as to what actually comes on the sandwich vs what comes on the side.

After so many disgusting cheese steaks in Philly, my expectations were pretty low for Jake's.  
My garlic bomb cheese steak however, was actually edible. The meat was not tough or fatty and there was a lot of it. The battered and fried garlic didn't really add anything to my sandwich but was good by itself. The fries were by far the best part of my meal. Perfectly cooked and perfectly seasoned. 
I wouldn't go out of my way to get here but if you happen to be in Philly this is a solid choice.

not impressed with this place; quality and price do not add here.

i got 2 proteins with brown rice, their 2 proteins amount to 1 protein compared to the other spots in chinatown and northern libs. they ran out of seaweed salad at 12pm on a weekday... so i settled for cilantro, cucumber and masago as my toppings. all in all, for $12.90 i wasn't impressed with the quality of my bowl. 

2.5/5 
either bring the price down or hike up the amount of protein and quality of ingredients

I've been meaning to try Potbelly's. Today was the day. I had lunch with my friend. We walk in and there is a line. The woman behind the counter is trying her best to keep the line moving. I order the Farmhouse salad with the Potbelly vinegarette. At some point the line is supposed to shift into sandwiches and salads. As it shifts I lose my place. So some kind of order would be nice on busy days. Taking names, roping off 2  different sections. Onto the food. The salad was good. I love Blue cheese so it was a good touch. I would have loved to have croutons but because the woman in front of me ordered hers with out I think I got mine without also. Not a big problem but if there was more structure to the line it may not have happened. I will go back hopefully not on a busy day and have a sandwich.

Chose this place for lunch while in the area based on Yelp reviews.  Ordered the Midtown Turkey. The veggies were fresh and good.  The turkey was only dark meat, which I don't like, and tasted reheated not fresh.  I'm disappointed with my choice and had much higher hopes.

"We proudly prepare and serve ridiculously creative sandwiches, made with house-roasted meats and veggies all hand carved to order." So says the sign  at Jakes.  For most places, a declaration like that might just be paint on the wall, but I get the feeling that it is more like a religion for those that work at Jakes.  

Located a little off the well worn tourist track in Center City, a Jakes is still a convenient short walk from the Avenue of the Arts or the Convention Center - and a walk well worth it.

You step in off the street and your nose is immediately greeted with a nice bouquet of roasted meat combined with a BBQ sauce finish.  The dining room is comfortably modern with USB charging outlets at each table just under the big roll of paper towels.  The table also features a bottle of sriracha and a bottle of heat called Jakes hot sauce that is not for the timid.

We ordered three sandwiches to share among 5 of us and we were satisfied.  We got the Skinny Turkey - I thought the veggies were a little over roasted, by the dw thought they were awesome.  We also got a BBQ - plenty of brisket although they included a huge hunk of fat that I thought would not have made it through the trim.  We ended up requesting an extra side of bbq sauce but I am sometimes known as an over-condimenter.  Our third sandwich was the 50/50, which was the star of the group and a 2012 Best of Philly winner.  The sharp provolone set off the sandwich and the blend of chopped pork and bacon was poetry.  I am not usually a fan of seeded buns, but the extra toughness of the roll was a complement here.

We also grabbed a farm fries with beef gravy which was a little extra dose of decadence that can easily take the place e of dessert.  

I really wanted to try the turbacon too, but not ordering it makes me want to get to Jakes for my next visit sooner rather than later.

I've had a few meals here with friends. Overall, the burgers have always been good but the quality of the fries ranges from soggy and cold to crispy and hot. The restrooms have always been clean as has the dining room - save for the table area where a gentleman and his three young (under 6) children ate during one visit. 

The wait at times can be a bit much especially if you are in during a non-peak time. One issue I had with this location as opposed to some of the others I have visited is they never ask you if/what toppings would you like. They expect you to know and tell them - not a good thing for the first time visitor.

If you are in a rush and want a quick, greasy burger go to Wendy's. If you have some time and extra cash give Five Guys a try.
Great fresh pita, tasty felafel! The Israeli Salad, cabbage and tahini make a delicious mix. A fair priced delicious lunch.

The debate goes on. As a native Californian, I have to say that it didn't quite measure up to In 'N Out, but Five Guys does a solid job. Their burgers are juicy and flavorful, the buns are hot, the fries are crispy and the shakes are delicious. The produce wasn't as fresh as I expected, but I was still very pleased with my satisfying burger. It's big, bright, and great for groups. If you've never had one, give it a shot!

Crisp Kitchen is the latest addition to Philadelphia's fresh salad scene, with stir fry and frozen yogurt options as well. The space is large with a number of ordering stations on both sides of the kitchen. It's easy to pick a pre-set option, customize it, and pay - I was able to easily make changes to my salad and appreciated how clearly the system indicated how each removal or addition impacted my total price.

The Crisp Cobb was good with fresh, ripe ingredients. My added focaccia bread was a little dry for my taste, but that might have been due to a visit on a slower weekend. Overall, Crisp Kitchen is a nice healthy option to check out!
Amazing (duh, its a chipotle) but honest toms is hands down better
Seriously, this is just a kind of fancier subway.  I thought it would be hard core sandwiches and things.  They were yummy and all, but not what i thought it would be.

Chipotle in University City is only getting 4 stars from me because of the chips and salsa...  The burritos would only get 2.5 stars.  The staff would get maybe 3 stars.  There is no consistency with the way the food gets prepared, wrapped, or served.  Isn't there a class for that?!  It's great because it is close to work, but not good if multiple people are going in on an order.  And let's not get started on the price...  $12 for a burrito, guacamole, chips and salsa!!  Huh?!
Greasy but tasty. :) would definitely try it again! They also carve the meet right in front you, which is pretty neat.

I eat lunch here at least three times per week. They are tacos llike mom used to make with the help of Old El Paso. That isn't a bad thing! The tastes are clean, the tacos are simple, the burritos and chillitos none to spicy. Nothing is greasy. I get a simple inexpensive lunch with this unusual hot sauce that is more Carolina pulled pork baste than Tabasco. I crave that sauce.

Try it of you don't need beaucoup salt and cayenne to enjoy your lunch.

I am a huge fan of sushi so decided to give a try to a poke bowl and wow!!

I picked the rainbow bowl and everything was fresh from the avocado, rice and meats ! I did ask for extra tuna cuz raw fish is life. I have difficult finding fresh tuna and this place nailed it!

You can also build your own show in the picture below...

As someone famous once said "I WILL BE BACK"

stopped by everyone's racquet with mr. h to get a racquet restrung.  while we waited, we stopped into jake's for lunch.  it's clean and the staff is friendly.  the sandwhich board is easy to read.  the thing i don't get is that the pig is featured prominently on the windows, yet the menu is extremely cow-heavy.  not a complaint, just a disconnect i noticed.

i can't remember the name, but i ordered one of the lighter sandwich offerings -- chicken, cheddar, avocado, and red onion.  it was good.  i could only finish half, though.  all of the onions are on top, so they kind of fall off.  

overall, jake's is a decent establishment and a nice place to grab lunch if you are doing some shopping on 13th.
Excellent choice for lunch or dinner. Everything looks so delicious and you know it is one of the best in town if the establishment is always busy.

Delish. Got the Garlic Bomb and the 50/50 and both were great. The Garlic Bomb was better, but you better LOVE garlic. You will leave FULL-- I ate one sandwich 3 hours ago and I am still reeling. A go-to Philly spot.
I ride & die for Red Poke Express.  It is fresh and fast and great for sushi addicts.

Tasteless food with and expensive tag
They didn't even have salt n their dishes. I would not recommend this place until they can fix it. One star for the food and loud ambience

I love Chipotle. Great food for a decent price. The one thing I don't like is that they are often out of various ingredients, like chicken or beans. On top of that, this seems to happen at peak hours, as well. Overall, it's a great place to go when you've got about $8 and are hungry.

Trying to eat a little healthier in the summer heat, we stopped by the PokeSpot for custom bowls. I loved the variety of options, including zuchini noodles for a carb-free base, and the fact that a custom bowl is only $11.50 regardless of how many toppings you pile on (as long as you steer clear of a couple upcharge items like avocado). The staff was helpful and friendly for any questions we had on our options. 

The only issue I had was I asked if the corn was fresh and was told yes, but it had the mush-factor of canned corn. Other than that, the bowls were tasty and we have already been back!

I would have given them 4 stars because I really like their pizza. It's the best pizza I have had in the area, and I have lived here for over 16 years. My daughter turned me on to it. The pizza is thin crust, not too saucy with just the right amount of cheese. And their ground sausage and pepperoni is absolutely delicious. The crust has a nice chew to it. But the customer service is AWFUL! The girls that answer the phone need a crash course on telephone etiquette and customer service skills.

Amazing.  First off, I love sandwiches.  I would rather eat a good sandwich than a piece of cake.  I've been wanting to try Jake's for months now, but just never found myself in the neighborhood.  After spending some time in the pro shop down the street, I decided to use my Quizzo winnings from the night before for a delicious sandwich.  I entered with every intention of getting the pork sandwich with provolone, broccoli rabe, and garlic, but when I went to the counter, I notice the sign for today's special.

It was fried local eggplant, spicy marinara, arugula, cheese, mushrooms, garlic spread and balsamic vinaigrette.  I guess I said something aloud about that sounding good, because the girl who was going to take my order said the special is really good, we'll only have it for a few weeks.  I was sold.

When I got back to the office, I couldn't wait to eat that sandwich, and it did not disappoint.  The eggplant was perfect, not too heavy or soggy, the cheese tasted really fresh, and the sauce was good, with just a hint of spice.  The bread was also perfect, which is where I think a lot of sandwiches fail.  I probably could have eaten half, but it was so good I ate the whole thing, but didn't feel stuffed afterwards.  

So glad I finally went here, although I'm going to have to engage in some self-control to keep from going back all the time.
Good flavor. Average portions. I agree with PA S. they COULD use a softer bread. Central location is a plus. Definitely has the Philly flavor.
Great food, fast delivery. The wraps and salads are both delicious and the fish is fresh.

Very tasty food. Amazingly fresh soft pretzels! 
I love that you can buy other items such as philly cheese steak pretzels.

Nice location with outdoor seating.

Just tried this new place tonight and I have to say I think I may be hooked.  I did the create your own bowl and everything was perfect. I got to choose my own base, my own protein, my own toppings and my own sauces. I'll be back, probably sooner than later.

We went for dinner, and the place was pretty empty...guess most folks like their sandwiches at lunch.  Hubby ordered the Barnyard, and I had the Village Turkey.  We would've ordered the sandwiches on multi-grain bread, but we saw that option too late.  We also ordered a side of their fries.  The sandwiches were filled with a good amount of tender meat, and the sauces were flavorful, but their standard white bread was kinda thick with a chewy crust.  We both thought the bread overwhelmed our sandwich innards, and I actually wished that they had a Potbelly's "skinny" option where some of the bread could be scooped out.  Aside from that, the sandwiches were tasty and the fries...the fries were delicious!  Perfectly fried and crispy.  I'd give them three and a half stars, but three is too low so I'm giving Jake's the benefit of the doubt with four stars.  Fun ambiance and friendly service.

Came to Philly looking for a Cheese Steak sandwich and was disappointed in what I received at Jake's.  The quality of the steak seemed really low.

I was up in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles about 6 months ago and had a Cheese Steak sandwich that was far better.  
Sam's Philly Steak   
 Tarzana, CA 

It seems crazy to go to Philly and not get something better

Best wings I've ever had! The double fried soy garlic are my favorite. they're a bit sticky though so they don't make good leftovers. Also their chicken fingers.... bangin! get the honey mustard sauce. their sides are subpar but the fries are decent. you go for the chicken not the sides.

Tried it a few times and always feel that the food is unnecessarily greasy (they even have paper towels at the tables).  This in turn leads to a lack of flavor (other than oil). Really not my cup o' tea.

Wow - tucked in on 12th street, this bbq packs a punch of flavor.

We went out for lunch and made a game time decision to stop into Jake's.  None of us had been there, and we were glad we stopped in.

They have some creative sandwich ideas, from roasted pork, brisket, roast turkey and others.  I had the mensch (12 hr roasted brisket, caramelized onions, horseradish sauce).  Fantastic.

Fries were decent, sodas are no-name brand but they have good flavors (birch beer!).

Moderately priced - $6-8 depending on what you get.  Looking forward to trying some of their other sandwiches, and breakfast.

I usually hate writing reviews about "fast food" places because everyone knows already what a Big Mac tastes like and have pretty much formed a solid opinion on experience already, but Five Guys is under the radar, and shouldn't be.

The first time I ever had Five Guys, it was when I was living in Virginia and ate at the inaugural spot. It changed my life as far as fast food burgers go. Listen, Five Guys is GOOD. Like, REALLY good. They make every burger fresh. There are a dozen topping choices at least. The potatoes are delivered fresh every day and they even tell you from where. You can nosh on peanuts as you wait to make your order. I've NEVER; not once, had a bad burger at ANY Five Guys I've ever eaten at, from Philly to Norfolk. If you order a large fry, I hope you brought 3 friends with you, as they give you a LITERAL LUNCH BAG of fries. A regular fry can be split 2-3 ways EASY. The workers are ALWAYS nice. They let you add artwork to the walls. I LOVE Five Guys. I will go out of my way for Five Guys.

Why not 5 stars? Five Guys ain't cheap. You are getting a damn good burger and PERFECT french fries (assuming you like your fries like I like mine, which are done, but still a little limp. No crispy fries here.) But, for a burger (2 small patties, a "little" is 1), regular fries and a drink, you're easily about $20. That same amount of food is $7 at Burger King. You're spending three times the money for Five Guys. Which, in my eyes, they are more than occassionally worth it, but it IS a consideration. Also, they only cook the burgers well, but it somehow doesn't ruin the burger.

Five Guys is totally recommended and the best "fast food" burger you can get anywhere; hell, one of the better burgers PERIOD you're gonna find.

Huge sandwich.  You don't need that side of friend onions or fried pickles unless you're super hungry or there with a friend.  I had the 50/50 based on reviews I'd read and "it's all right"  is the best way to describe what I tasted.  Friendly folks, but I had better sandwiches from a street vendor.

Convenience - A (It's right across the street from work!)
Food - B- (Not the worst burrito I've ever had)
Value - A (Gigantic and cheap)
Decor - who cares? Take it out

The double fried wings are delicious!!  It's nice to know that I don't have to drive all the way up to North Philly to get my beloved korean fried wings.  I got the spicy wings and wish they were a bit spicier but the flavor was spot on.  It even had that wonderful crunch in the skin that I adore.  Looks like my family will be getting more takeout from here on my way back home from work....mmmmm!!  I need to try some of their other menu items.  It's a little place and was really busy around lunch time.  Good thing we ordered ahead of time.

There's a good deal of nuance in the way I appreciate Hot Tamales. The whole is more than the sum of its parts so I think a deconstructed view helps. Furthermore, I should also state my underlying beliefe that consistently mediocre is in my view better than occasionally great. 

Pros
-No surprises - there's such a thing as really bad food, but the fare at HT is not. The food is consistent, tastes fresh but is bland and completely unimaginative. That said, you're not going to be biting down on bone or tendon and pulling stuff from your chipped teeth wondering WTF is that?!?

-Cheap - the prices are literally just inflated over early '90s taco bell with tacos starting at $1.19.

-Crafty - I think they're onto something in their art of upselling. With low margins on the food, HT milks the peripherals like $0.19 to-go hot sauce (which I suspect is sysco generic hot sauce liberally cut with water) cups and an extra charge for the living large upgrade of 'fiesta rice.' I don't mind. I study it and think of ways I can apply this kind of scrap to my life.

Cons
-Otherwise underwhelming. 
-Decor - somehow reminds me of Saved By the Bell

I have worked near Jake's for about 4 years now and last week was my first time at Jake's. Craziness, right? It's about time and I will certainly return regularly. Last week I wanted to try somewhere different for takeout during my lunch hour - I always end up at the same 3-4 places. I decided to try out Jake's and went with a 50/50 for takeout and omg, it was fabulous! A huge, filling sandwich full of pork and bacon and the Siracha mayo added a great topping. It was so good I spent the rest of the afternoon at work in a mini food coma.

Today I went for a sit down lunch with a friend and on the recommendations of people on Yelp, I tried the Firesteak and again, omg. I have a very, very high tolerance for spice and this firesteak definitely tested my tolerance. It was so damn hot, plus I got the fried hot peppers so they added more spice. After the first half of my sandwich, my mouth was burning. Luckily I got some of their birch beer (fabulous too, btw). I was determined to finish the sandwich, though, so after a short break and drinks of soda, I finished it all up. I will probably not order the Firesteak again because it was good and spicy, but too spicy for my generally very tolerant taste. 

I'll definitely get to working my way through the menu at this place. The prices are a little high for me to go too often, but maybe a few times a month would do me good and leave me in a happy food coma. :)

Yummy!! Fresh turkey spinach salad! They gave me tons of turkey ham and a lot of spinach. All ingredients were fresh and I enjoyed my salad. Was huge so I could have left over but I am a girl with big appetite! Other friends had sandwiches and said very good also. Solid local sandwich shop for sure. 

Now actually it became my regular sandwich spot. I always get mensch. It's soooo good. Potato cake and mixed fries are must.

Two stars for never having to wait in a long line (typical of most Chipotles that I've been to, both in Philly and DC) and to being conveniently located. 
But other than that, I'm disappointed in this location. 
I am a HUGE fan of chipotle but this location is rather stingy with their portions. I think I got like 5 pieces of chicken with my burrito bowl and they never give you enough rice or lettuce! I always have to ask for "a little more". Other locations usually add a decent amount so that all of the items are balanced. Who wants a bowl of salsa and sour cream with like a half scoop of rice and 3 shreds of lettuce? pfffffffft. gross. 
Head to the center city location, waaay better. But if you live in university city, you will probably have to actually ask them for more rice, corn, salsa, beans, lettuce, guac, whatever. because they don't give you enough for your money ((this is all in comparison to like... every other chipotle)).

This place is so over hyped im not sure why. The burgers are good but not what people hyped them up to be. Its better than average but not to die for. I think the people hyping it up are comparing the burgers to Fast Food burgers (McD, Wendys) in that case yes its better. I have got into debates about how over hyped this place is. Maybe you went on a off day or try a different place. Its just a regular burger the main difference is that theirs is more fresh than what you get at your standard run of the mill Fast Food place. Is it worth the price i say yes but dont go expecting to have your socks blown off. Its more hype than meat here...Lol...

I have been to Jake's a couple of times and have yet to be disappointed.  I really like how all their sandwiches have a unique spin on them, you can't find a sandwich like theirs any where else.

I really like the Village Turkey which is turkey breast, cherry spread, bits of bacon, and arugula on a sesame roll. The taste all together is phenomenal and I really love the cherry spread the put on the sandwich.  I think I could put that spread on anything and it would taste awesome.

I also like their spin on the cheesesteak which is called a Jake, everything is the same except they top it off with a roasted long hot, which can spicy, but it was nice addition to the sandwich.

I have yet to try the turducken sandwich is there for only a limited time so I have to go back before they get rid of it, it sounds real good. Overall I don't think you can be disappointed here and I recommend if you are looking for a different spin on sandwiches

Be prepared to feel bloated. Their pork is super succulent and well seasoned. Good portioning with the sandwiches. If you're not feeling a sandwich, try the 'build your own haystack' which is fries + meat + three toppings + sauce. Again, you're gonna feel like crap when you leave, but so very satisfied.

Great great food! Mac and cheese was okay, spicy chicken wings was amazing!!! The delivery was fast and everything came in hot! We ordered the fried Oreos and Reese just to try them and it was worth the try but it wasn't good at all, too much dough and very grease.

Reached out and said they contacted me and never did. I reached back out to them... said they need the exact day and and time of my purchase... lmao months later you want me to recall a the exact day of crap experience. Then they say they need my card number and or name I provide.. no response terrible customer service. Smelly and crappy establishment. Run piss poor.

like the cheesesteak joints
qdoba's always nearby
but a little worse

I use to enjoy this place but then realized the sandwiches were just ok. The bread is hard, dry and makes up a good portion of the sandwich. Prices also have gone up after the renovations and they changed their menu and took away some sandwiches that I use to enjoy like the garlic bomb. I do like the fries here though but again, the prices have gone up even for these. Also when I asked about the platter, the counter girl had no idea what it was even though it was on their menu. She said they weren't trained to serve the platter. I figured how hard can it be?

I'm not impressed. I ordered the chips and salsa and two beef tacos, one hard and one soft. The chips and salsa were okay although the spice level was nearly non-existent. The tacos weren't great. The hard taco shell was stale and unappetizing. The taco comes with cheese, lettuce, meat, and salsa. It was dry and didn't have much flavor. The soft taco was the same story except it wasn't a stale taco shell. 

The one thing this place has going for it is the prices. It was $7 for chips and salsa, two beef tacos, and a fountain soda. Not bad. 

The people working there were polite enough. Beyond the food, the drawback for me was their music is terrible. No thank you.

I tried the 50/50 and it's easily one of the most amazing sandwiches I've had in Philly! The sriracha/ mayo on the bread definitely was a key ingredient! I love how creative all of the spreads are and how fresh all the meat is! Definitely one of the best sandwich shops around and the employees are all very helpful and know what they're talking about. It was very easy to get a recommendation from them on what to try and they're very reliable. My belly was happy and yours will be too!

I come here to praise Jake and his Sandwich Board, specifically for three options that I can't seem to live without anymore:

The Mensch- beef brisket and horseradish, a combo from the gods. No matter what else is available, I always, ALWAYS need to get the Mensch. It is reliable in a way that nothing else in life is. Satisfying to the last bite, and nothing if not filling.

Crunchy Onions- an excellent alternative to onion rings, decadent and delicious.

French Fries- The oldest standby in the book, but I'll be damned if they aren't some of the best around.

The rest of the menu has been hit and miss. The Village Turkey? Very good. The Schmeer? Will make your breath stink so much that no one will like you. The Classic? I always love a good meatball, and this is certainly one.

A man's sandwich spot.  Everything is heavy with meats and sauces and bread.  I had the brisket picante.  It was amazing.  Brisket, hot sauce, guac, and fried breaded onions that I could've eaten a bucket of alone.  That sandwich sparked a wave of fans in my office and we went back when I came again for my second week in training in Phl and everyone wanted to go back.  This time I got the veggie since I was trying to behave and it wasn't quite so life-changing.  I regret not trying the one with peanut butter.  Coulda, woulda, shoulda.
I was recently in Philly for business and ate here three times.  Tried a different sandwich every time and they all were absolutely delicious.  A must go if you are in Philly

Since my initial sandwich taint waxing here quite some time ago, I've been back periodically.  I must say, they've got some killer ideas.  I dig their predilection for putting deep fried toppings on sandwiches.  The turducken sandwich with the cranberry sauce and fried hash brown on top was genius.  Although seasonal, one of the best sandwiches in the sandwich capital of the world.

Also, them panko-ed fried onion husks - boom - i need a statin.  The best peice of deep fried onion I ever put in my mouth.

So so falafel- overpriced too. It's just dry, not that flavorful and they are stingy with the already small balls. Too bad - I was looking forward to this place opening in Whole Foods/Amazon. I really like the sister restaurant there- although also overpriced...

Also, the hours really suck! Why do they close at 7pm?
Large menu, better than average sandwiches, fast delivery, great salads and soup. Good Value!

My cousin's friend made a huge announcement on social media recommending this place. This is the newest and closest poke spot to my work so I was so excited. While the food was pretty good, I would say my overall disappointment was with the operations and services experienced at my visit.

They were out of zucchini noodles and cauliflower rice. Didn't they just open? How is that already an oversight?

Every review mentioned building your own poke bowl. Was there any other option? I picked the Spicy Salmon bowl but still had to pick everything I wanted in the bowl, aside from the rice/salad options (which yes, I know I had to pick). I saw under the Spicy Salmon that there were ingredients that go on that typical bowl. I never said I wanted to build my own sh**, and now I'm being told I have to. If I requested the Spicy Salmon, can't the employees just figure out I wanted everything in the description after I said so? At this point, I'm already down the line and can't really see the description anymore.

What if I never had a poke bowl before? I would not have had a clue about what to put in the poke bowl. I felt like I was being rushed and stupid for not knowing what some of the ingredients were.

Employee: "What sauce do you want?"
Me: "What sauces do you have?"
Employee pointed at the bottles with labels I can't see from where I am standing and still didn't know after they provided the names.

Jesus! I know it was lunch and busy, but customer service wasn't their thing. Out of the four or five people working, one was nice enough and friendly to me. My poke bowl probably could have been better with some guidance. The staff gave this place 3 stars. Sorry.

I went to Jake's Sandwich Board for lunch while visiting Philadelphia. We ordered a garlic bomb cheesesteak (cheesesteak with garlic spread & fried garlic cloves) and a 50/50 sandwich (1/2pork,  1/2bacon, sriracha spread & sharp provolone). I sampled a piece of the garlic bomb cheesesteak. The garlic bomb cheesesteak was not on Jake's menu (you must request it). I saw it on the Travel Channel. If you like garlic, Jake's garlic cheesesteak is perfect for you. It's a GARLIC explosion!!! The sandwich was good but it was too garlicy for me. 50/50 was the sandwich I ordered. All of the meats blended well together. Jake's 50/50 was tasty. I added more sriracha spread to my sandwich. The potato cakes are delicious. Service was fast and friendly. The shop has a few tables and bar window seats (clean inside). I give Jake's Sandwich Board a 3.5 rating.

This place is pretty awesome. It's become a go-to take out spot for me on days when I forget my lunch at work or when I just want something different. I always go with a build-your-own, two chicken proteins (i'm not super into raw fish) with a bunch of toppings. They have a ton of options and their sauces are awesome. My co-worker always gets a seafood bowl and swears by it. Would definitely recommend as take-out if you're in the area!

I read all the good reviews which led me to this place.  I was in Philadelphia and decided that I should try a sandwich shop.  Going in I didn't see any traditional "philly cheesesteak" on the menu, which I was OK with as the offerings did seem to be unique.  

As a Texan my eyes were immediately drawn to the smoked brisket sandwich.  Going into this I knew there was no way it would compare to Texas brisket, but I had to try it.  I was very disappointed in the sandwich.  It just didn't have any flavor.  Next someone had ordered the fries with meat and gravy goodness all over it.  I tried them, but really did not like the gravy.  Perhaps I am use to southern gravy and just didn't understand this type of gravy.

The other people in our group seemed to like their sandwiches, but my experience was just a bit lackluster.  I would say as a foreigner coming into Philadelphia you may want to try something else.

Love their crispy chicken salad. Other salads are good too, including fish fillet salad, mango habanero salad, and sesame chicken salad, but the crispy chicken salad is our favorite, with fresh mix of veggies topped with plenty of warm, made to order slices of crispy, yet moist chicken. Tried their rice bowls too (teriyaki and sesame chicken), but prefer the more balanced mixture of the salads.

MEGA CURLY FRIES!!!!  this is definitely the go to!  I've never had anything bad here.  Pizza is awesome, steaks are awesome, fries are awesome, hot wrappers (even though I didn't even know what that was until now) is awesome.  They also have those really big pizzas that barely fit through the door of your average NE Philly Row home-- worth it! oh yeah and... MEGA CURLY FRIES

I have been a frequent customer of Jake's since it opened more than five years, and I have never left disappointed.  My favorite sandwich is the brisket cheesesteak, which I would put up there with any cheesesteak in the city (and that's saying a lot).  The other meats are good too, but I've always loved the brisket the most.

The staff has always been friendly and provided quick service.  If you need a place to grab a quick meal or snack and want to enjoy a unique menu of combinations that seem to always work, Jake's is your place!

Ordered delivery on Caviar bc i had credit there so I can't speak for the service but the poke itself was good!! Some places will give you a lot of rice and skimp on other ingredients but that doesn't seem to be the case here. They offer a ton of toppings and protein options and it was hard to choose! (We built our own with raw salmon + ahi tuna and shrimp ceviche + raw tuna) the only complaint I would have is the rice tasted a little old but I'm sure it'd because it was the end of the night when we ordered and you can't really tell after mixing it all in. I would definitely come back in person next time though, since delivery is pricey. 

We both loved our bowls!

I love Chipolte but this location is the worst!! Slowest service ever, the counter they make the food on disgustingly sloppy, and I don't think anyone there can actually wrap a burrito.

If your in the area, just go to Qdoba and don't let this Chipolte ruin your opinion of all other Chipolte locations.

Came in after 4 hrs of social drinking watching my kids mini soccer tournament on a Friday night. The kids were starving as was I & my wife. My kids love Five Guys & I prefer them over any other fast food burger. Got a small cheese burger with jalapeño & mushrooms. Wife & kids got small cheeseburgers with bacon. Everything was good never really have a problem when I come here. Our order was up reasonably quick & tasted good. Filled us up & did the job. I'll definitely be back & will review again.

Gross.  Would give zero stars if I could. Had a pizza roll  and a  "hot wrapper". They were both bland and really soggy. Even the sauce for the pizza roll tasted funny. It's one thing if only one piece of your order sucks, but BOTH items? Ugh.

I visited Philly for a weekend and wanted to try the poke. It is set up similar to others, a bar with all the ingredients and you build your bowl as you go. I ordered white rice with tuna and salmon. I added onions, kani salad (imitation krab), fish eggs and onions crisps. I added some ponzu sauce in place of my usual soy sauce. I like to shake my bowl up to really mix it all together. It was really great! I may not get the onion crisps next time since I got sweet onions, but I really enjoyed the meal. The employees were so nice even though we came close to closing time!

As previous reviewers said, the cauliflower rice was not too crunchy or too soft. And it didn't feel like they skimped on the fish.

I definitely will go back and recommend to friends.

Jake's Sandwich Board is pleasurable a sandwich venue as one could hope to experience.  

Firstly, one must acknowledge the staff.  Attentive, energetic, and consistent, you can see them working and assembling or prepping food throughout the day with vigor in a well kept cook area.  They are personable and prompt and in my many visits, have a fairly high degree of consistency even under heavy load.

The environment is well adorned with photos and a 5lb Challenge Wall of Fame/Shame.  Not going to touch on that because the proportions deserve a look in person, as well as the overwhelming number of failed attempts.  Quite amusing.  However, a personal highlight are the well crafted chalk boards which offer seasonal flair, clean lines and a very consistent style, which lends a nice air.

The food selection consists of a standard board offering variations of pork (until the recent porchetta experiment my favorite), brisket, steak, and a couple of chicken options.  For the grain/wheat averse, Jake's also offers the option of going breadless and having the meat over a bed of greens or on fries.  I typically opt for the former as the greens offer up the drippings of the absolutely fantastic flesh and accompaniments.

Speaking of, while the bacon and sriracha permeate all things Jake's, I highly recommend either the Picante or Gringo, which utilize Jake's Fire Sauce.  

I really cannot sing the praises of Jake's adequately, other than to say that their naked bowls really show off the meat they prepare.  As I mentioned, I favor the pork and mentioned their porchetta.  This is another aspect of Jake's that I like.  There is usually something special in the works, and it has never failed to please.

TLDR:  Eat at Jake's.  Now.

After coming to Philly for the past 5 months, I've finally had m y first Philly pretzel! This place is great because there is plenty of parking AND there is also a walk-up window (drive thru on feet!!). Pretzel prices are pretty cheap, 5 for $2!!! I dont think you can get any cheaper than that!!

The pretzel itself is super plump, very bready, which I like!! I always get a side a of spicy mustard w/ my pretzels :]

This was my first time trying Poke and I must say I was impressed. I ordered through the ritual app and by the time I went to pick up the food it was ready and waiting for me. I got the bowl with a rice base and for my protein I did  snow crab and the shrimp Ceviche. For toppings I went with wasabi, cilantro, corn, Kani Salad, green onions, and sweet onions with some onion crisp topping. For sauces I had Chili Garlic Aioli, Chili Ponzu, Pokespot Sauce and Sesame Ginger Sauce. I love that we can pick any toppings and sauces we want at no additional charge. The food was fresh and reminded me of sushi without the wrap. I'll definitely be back again!

Long line. Thought the place would be fabulous! Nothing could be farther from the truth! Ordered seeded roll with turkey, bacon and prov. That's it...nothing more. Sandwich was $10.00!!!! Got home opened the sandwich to find barely anyhting in the roll. Shredded turkey that could feed a mouse, looked like 2 strips of bacon and one slice of prov. $10.00!!!! Not even delicious...just meh. Will never go  back. Stick to WAWA folks!

We were in Philly for a short period of time and went into Whole Foods just to grab a snack. To our surprise, we found an incredible food hall. I had six falafel balls with a sauce - I can't recall which sauce it was now. They were the best falafel I've ever had. My friend had a tehina milkshake. We're still talking about the falafel and shake two months later!

Goldie - please find your way to NYC like Dizengoff did! :)

The people were very nice but the food was...well... less than I expected. First I ordered the turbacon because I saw the video of like a Diners Drive ins and Dives type of show. The sandwich I got was nothing like the one on there. Foe starters there was like one strip of bacon on there. Nothing that you should even put bacon in the name. The turkey near the bread was dry and the top of the sandwich was soupy and the fried potato cakes were not crispy and actually got stuck to the wrapper and, well I was just disappointed. 
I returned it and since I knew I wouldn't get my money back I got the 50/50 which is supposed to be half pulled pork and half bacon. Again they did not live up to the hype of the bacon. The sandwich I got was really a 80/20 and the 20 is being generous. It was piled with the pork and maybe 2 slices of bacon. You can't really taste the bacon because of all the meat drowning it out. The only thing that saved the sandwich was that I got the roasted garlic spread instead of the sriracha spread. 
I'm not sure that I would go back or maybe I will try a different location but I was not happy.
The roasted chicken is ridiculously good. Like homemade. The fried chicken is burned beyond edibility and they are no longer on eat24.
Probably the worst cheese steak I ever ate. Also ordered the farm fries which weren't very good.

Worst service ever. I went to the drive through and placed an order. After getting to the window to pay, I had ask the gentleman for hot sauce on the side and he handed me 1 packet of hot sauce and 1 packet of honey (which I didn't ask for). I proceeded with asking him for extra hot sauce and he turned around and grabbed me a another single packet of hot sauce for a total of 2 packets of hot sauce. This defeats the purpose of asking for sauce so I just drove off and left. I don't understand how someone comprehends hot sauce as as an individual packet. If I could I would rate this place with no stars. Terribly disappointed at this location.

I don't like Subway. I live in Phila. where the hoagie was invented. I would never go to Subway when I have some of the best hoagie bread, meats and hoagie making workers throughout our region - yes, I am a total food snob. 

With all that said, when you need to feed some men working in your home and there's a Subway nearby - well, this Subway location/franchise is very good. The employees are nice and pleasant - and they make a decent sandwich at a good price. And the place is very clean.

Goldie is the best! 

I've had their falafel salad at their Franklin's Table location. It has delicious falafels, fresh mint, sunflower seeds and beets. The falafel here is super fresh and flavorful! I cannot wait to try their pita sandwiches. 

At this location I tried their tahini shakes! We had the original shake. It was so good! At first, it was very sesame seed forward and then the sweetness hit me. Seriously 10/10. Super delicious and original.

In the cold winter months, I enjoy a meal indoors and this is my favorite place to eat at in the food court. I've only had the chicken pesto sandwich and it was pretty good! The vegetables are fresh, the chicken is flavorful and the bread is nice and toasty. 
This is certainly one of the better Quiznos I've eaten, but then again I recently moved here! :D
And it helps that the husband/wife duo that run the place are extremely friendly! Give it a try!

Staying in downtown Philly for a few nights, and thought I'd look for a good sandwich.  I tried the TurBacon, and it was not too shabby.  The meat was moist and tasty, the bread was fresh, and the meat/bread/topping ratios were very good.  I also ordered a cherry soda (yum) and a Farm Fries (not so much).  The farm fries tasted like a sour salt lick... The cheese was overpowering, and it was just not a well conceived dish.  I couldn't eat more than two bites.  

The service was pretty good.  The young lady who took my order was not very friendly, all business, but not terrible.  The guy who bagged up my order was very friendly and offered a refill on the drink that I downed while waiting the few minutes for my food.  

Overall, it's a good place, and I'll probably stop back before I leave town.  Their shake special is Apple Cider, which sounds awesome, and I also want to try the Garlic Bomb.

Salty. Falafel is real small, over cooked and no flavor. They gave us a tiny side of falafel for 3 salads. When I asked for another one, she made the biggest deal and gave me a tiny amount that barely did anything. Really!!??  The salad was wet..mushy..not fresh

Had about 80% of the menu and everything is always on point. The steak and egg with siracha ketchup is bangin, midtown chicken and the village turkey homeruns. Fries are always hot and crisp, and a good root beer float goes a long way in my book. Service is fast and friendly, they don't even give me dirty looks when I grab about 400 peanut chews from the bowl.

Holy stuffed belly!  Went here for lunch with a colleague as it is in walking distance from my office.  

I browsed the menu online before I went, and to be honest, was having trouble deciding what to get.  I knew right away I would be getting the Peanut Chew shake (my sweet tooth said Thank You!), so I had to decide which sandwich would go best with chocolate and peanuts.  I was still undecided when I got to the counter, but went with the Raging Bull, a combo of steak, corned beef, russian dressing and swiss cheese.  Totally delish!  The meat was really juicy and I loved the menage a trios of russian dressing, cheese and meat.  Between the thickness of the shake and the sandwich itself, I'll be enjoying Raging Bull The Sequel soon.

My friend and I totally gorged ourselves and I know I will be going into food coma shortly.  I found it a little on the pricey side for lunch, but will be sure to go back if I am jonesing for a milk shake.
Spicy double battered Wings is all I have to Say! AMAZING Wings.

I only ordered take out, but was pleased with my experience. I'd give Jake's 3 1/2 stars. I ordered the 50-50 in a salad bowl - greens topped with pulled pork, lots of bacon, cheese, and sriracha mayo. Definitely indulgent, but I had just run the Philly half marathon, so it was exactly what I wanted.

They also have chocolate covered bacon!! A meat lover's paradise.

When you say "Sam, this sandwich is $9" I have expectations. Said expectations were not met. I went with the 50/50 because bacon and roast pork sounds like a good thing. It wasn't. The roast pork was dry, and although the flavor was great, the dryness just killed it (in a bad way, not a good way. [I know the kids have made 'killed it into something good]). There was plenty of bacon but it couldn't redeem it. Also, the portion was on the skimpy side. I'm not one for a belly busting sandwich, but come on. Let me think that I'm getting a little value for my hard earned Washingtons.  This place falls into the hipster trap of offering 'peasant, working man's, blue collar offerings' at SoHo (sorry, I don't know the Philly equivalent of SoHo yet) prices. This line of thinking is what ruined Brooklyn. This is what ruins a lot of things. Why can't things be the way they used to....ohmygoodnessI'mold! That is all.

I normally love all chipotles and I never have issues with the food here, but I noticed that this time when I went the brown rice wasnt cooked well. I asked for another bowl of it and I noticed the same thing... seems a bit off to me. I dont know if ill be going back to this specific chipotle!

Loved the food at Jake's Sandwich Board on my first visit. I kept it simple and went with the classic pork sandwich. Barbecued pork with broccoli rabe and provolone. Topped with some sriracha and piled on a sesame seed bun, it was delish and just what I was looking for. The only reason that I gave 4 stars was that I think the meat could have used a bit more sauce. It felt a little bit dry, and for the price of each sandwich ($10+), it should be perfection!

I gave this place 3 chances!
I will not be returning. There was always persons hanging out and trying to pick up every female customer that walked in, shenanigans and idle chat. More importantly, last time I went in I had to wait a whole 20 mins to get asked what I wanted to order because there was one employee sitting just looking at the line, another employee came from out the back  then stopped to chat with a customer, who by the way, didn't put her order in yet because they were both busy flirting with some pickup artist guy. When all that was over they had to serve her because she was next in line! All this time the employee  that was sitting down albeit with this customer could have been serving her food! There was just ONE male employee serving TWO customers with multiple orders! Employees have zero customer service skills and they do not seem to care either!

My fiancée and I consider ourselves a kind of Chipotle aficionados. This place, does not make the cut.

Unfriendly service, often waiting for ingredients, mistakes, and the atmosphere is often very loud (students but also the music is usually blaring).

We have now gone here four times since moving to the area this past summer. Tonight is likely the last try. There just hasn't yet been a good experience to convince us that we can expect anything good from this location.

luv their chicken, but just called for delivery. 

'sorry, we don't deliver'
 saw on yelp that you do
'no delivery'

I usually go to the drive thru. Today I decided to walk to the window. Must be sloths staff night or something.,,,,,,slow isn't even the word because it wasn't even busy. Checking the menu, maybe something for my kid and hubster..... sigh maybe I'll just wish another 5-10 minute while they take their sweet aushhhh time. Oh it's my turn yay!!!!! Got to the window, I did a UTurn like going down on a dirty vagina "nevermind" dirty and disgusting it was! Looking at all the trash they have on the floor, the corners, the papers, the wrappers, the fries, the food, wtf  I'm not getting my family sick if they can't keep where they store food clean. I should've took a picture and send it to corporate. There are sloth morons that work here, not only slow but dirty too, never mind. I'm good.

Very good pizza and nice people. I mostly get the meal via delivery and I never had a issue. Was always fast, hit and correct. When I ask for condiments on the side or extra of something they always made conscious effort to satisfy my request. A great place...

Sorry, I don't eat fried chicken altho I almost bought a biscuit but got out in time before ingesting the 270ish calories for 1.  
But I had to write that when I went in to use the restroom, the restaurant smelled wonderful and I was tempted.  What got me tho was the bathroom!  It was spotless!  And on the way out, I noticed the whole place was spotless.  
If I ate this type of food, I would eat it there.

A lot of the Yelp reviews of this place mention that the reviewers were poke virgins. Although this place is good, it doesn't hold a candle to better poke places I've been to. I wouldn't exactly call myself a poke master, but certainly a poke addict that has made it a point to try and find the best poke spots in New York City, Washington DC, and beyond. I have yet to find an amazing poke place in Philadelphia, and I was hoping that this would be it - but it certainly is not (the best in the area I've found thus far is in Ardmore, if you're curious).

With that being said, Red Poke tries hard, but the piece size (very small) and portion (also small) of the fish you get is sort of disappointing. For the most part, the good flavor is there, but it is completely ruined by the fact that it appears that not all of the ingredients are fresh here (can't say I've ever experienced that at any of the poke places I've ever visited). I love to get something spicy (jalapenos) which is evened out by something sweet (fruit), and Red Poke has two common fruits that you'll find in bowls on the menu - mango and pineapple. Unfortunately, neither tasted fresh and were probably the canned variety. When I finished my bowl, there was a whole lot of fruit that I just left in there uneaten, because the fruit portions were excessive (more fish, less fruit!), and they just didn't taste great.

Also unlike other Poke joints, you fill out a menu card when you order a custom bowl - checking off the ingredients that you want added. This I did think was a good addition, and it ensures that you know everything that you could add to your bowl, and that you get what you want.

All in all, the food was okay, but I probably won't be back to Red Poke. My search will continue for a great Philly poke stop.

The original owners sold the place. A serious shame because that food was amazing. New food is standard fare, not terrible but not particularly good. Same menu for the most part, but tortillas were no longer hand made, everything was a little heavier, and the flavors just weren't there. 

I wonder where the old owner went!

Great food, but slow service. It also appears that their credit card machine is NEVER working. Of the 5+ times I have been there, it worked only once. Sometimes I pay cash, but mostly I walk out and go elsewhere

So, I think this is the place on JFK and 18th. If Its not, sorry.

Long lines, snotty staff, and shitty mexican. The staff acts like they are doing you a favor. My favorite is the dude who types as fast as humanly possible onto the register. He'll take your order in 2 seconds only to have you wait 10 minutes for a quesadilla that looks more like a tiny soft taco folded over and microwaved. Also, this place uses cheese whiz type queso in their signature chilito. The prices aren't half bad, but the ingredients rival the quality of the ingredients you'd find at an Aldi grocery store.
Decent, love the Philly sports collections around the resturant

DO NOT EAT HERE! Everytime I come here there is some type of problem. You wanna talk about horrible service. I've never felt so disgusting eating fast food in my life because of not knowing if my food was contaminated by the workers purposely. Most of these employees have no manners or professionalism at all. I'm embarrassed that the low level employees share the same race as me. I think they amuse themselves by seeing how rude the can be too the customer. I didn't even mention how long it took for my order the last time I paid them a visit. I swear it took over 20 minutes. If you're starving for some fast food do yourself a favor and don't go to checkers.

I had not gone back to pot belly as I did not like it - but we had a corporate luncheon catered from there today and a few things seem to have improved:

1.  The chopped salad with cranberries and walnuts was not too bad (I'd get it without onions in future).

2.  The meatball sandwiches arrived hot and the sandwich boxes (Box 'o sammies) were cute and well organized with a variety of sandwiches.  If I ever go to potbelly again I'm getting the meatball sub.

3.  The dark chocolate chip cookies seemed to be freshly-baked - albeit a bit greasy (butter or margaine?) - they were DELISH.

Much improved.

I tried Jake's Sandwich Board for the first time yesterday, compliments of Level Up App and why have I not rushed here before??

I ordered the 50/50 sandwich (l/2 pork, l/2 smoky grilled bacon with house sriracha spread and sharp provolone) and it was delectable.  I took a couple of bites of it while it was fresh (I had to go to the gym in an hour).  It was super tasty.  The sriracha spread makes the sandwich!  The roasted pork was surprisingly juicy.

I agree though, it really wasn't 50% bacon but there was enough to notice the contrast of flavors.  Also, a bit of a turnoff was that I wrapped up the sandwich for later and put it in my bag.  When I took it out of my bag, the brown paper bag the sandwich was in, was completely soaked with grease.

I heated the sandwich up for lunch today.  It's a shame the sriracha spread soaked into the bread.  But the sandwich was still the envy of my department.  I definitely have to go back again!

I've been to Jakes plenty of times before. I love how they make their meats and carve it. It's my first time back after their renovations and they did a great job. The place looks awesome! I love the USB charging station. Ive been telling my bf we need to come eat here for our day in Philly. Wasn't too thrilled about our meal yesterday. Here's why: 

1. They need a kids menu. Even if they rarely get kids that come in. Having a kids menu would be nice. If they have one...it's not displayed. Grilled cheese. Turkey sandwiches. Something. My 6 yr old can't eat a whole sub to himself. No sides. Nothing. 

2. They charge for everything. When did they charge for wheat bread? $2 for bacon? Sheesh. $43.50 for 3 sandwiches and fries. Way too much. 

3. The counter girl (slim asian maybe Hispanic with glasses) just stands there. Looks you in the face. It would've been nice if she asked us what we're in the mood for. Suggest some of the items. Ask if we have any questions. She was very blah. "We don't do lettuce. No milkshakes today". Even my bf said she was very blah and not what you would expect from a counter girl. What happened to the other one? (White girl, glasses?) she was so friendly. 

4. They need to add more dressings on their sandwiches. My village turkey had a black cherry sauce which tasted AMAZING. I just wished they were more generous with it. The meats were dry and could've used some extra sauce to disguise that. The rolls were super tough. Almost stale and than toasted for the sandwich which made eating it impossible. My bf did not like his cheesesteak at all. Flavor was there in the sauces though. 

5. They should add meals. It's really pricey.  A bag of chips and a drink would've been nice for a $10.50 sandwich. Instead it's 8.50-10.00 for a sandwich PLUS $1.50 for a drink PLUS $3-$5 for fries/onions rings. Hence our $44 bill. 

Good things:
1. They have Birch beer. Say no more. 
2. USB charging stations. 
3. The fellas were friendly. Always busy. 
4. The farmers market fries were amazing. That's the only thing worth the price ($5). It reminded me of Montreal Canada poutine but upgraded with cheese..bacon and pulled pork.
