5. You can see everything the guys are doing. You can even see them carving the meats for your sandwiches. 
6. Lots of local support for farmers there. Awesome.

A decent burrito, but getting in can be tricky if you're not paying attention.  Whoever designed this site must have thought that Ivy League students are more attentive than the average Joe (the Plumber).  Follow along so you don't look stupid like me and my friends.

When you walk in, you'll probably think that you should go through the door directly in front of you.  Wrong.  That's where you exit.  The entrance is actually directly to the left.  Yes, you smartasses will say, there IS signage.  You probably won't see until after it's too late, but it's there.

We ordered three burritos and the dude who was charged with rolling them up was incapable of rolling two of the three.  This was the first time ever that I've ever been asked whether I would like to have my burrito rewrapped or if I just wanted to eat it in a bowl.  WTF?
My experience here was awesome. The service was possibly the best casual fast food dine in experience I've ever had. Awesome staff.

Despite the number of times I've been by this place, I somehow just noticed it the first time a few weeks ago. I thought it was still Maccabean something? I was going to try another new spot, but this one just "called me." It was empty, which usually isn't a good sign, but I can be really low key and times so I was all for it.

I dig the set up with the paper towels, the layout, and the menu. I got a Jake (steak) and it was cool. The roll wasn't as soft as I would've liked. Maybe I should get one to go some time and let it marinate. I liked that they had Sriracha. Tried some on my fries and they were poppin (good amount of fries at that). I'm somewhat pleased that drinks and fries are only a dollar. It keeps things simple. It otherwise evens out the price of the sandwiches. Had a great iced tea. They have microbrewed sodas... never tried one of these.

I'm definitely coming back to try some kind of custom mash up sandwich. AU JUS! Aw shucks! The vibe is what you could expect from a steak place. "Eh, it's my job whaddya want from me?"

Do yourself a favor and eat here!
Pulled pork, broccoli rabe, Caramelized onions, mild provolone and pork sauce. Do NOT forget to add the crunchy long hots!!!

Got the Megillah and fried pickles. The Megillah was one of the best, if not the best sandwich I've had in Philly. The brisket melts in your mouth. The fried pickles were flavorful crunchy and a little spicy. Best I've had. I'm going to go back tomorrow to try a different sandwich. Sad I didn't find this place sooner.

Bbq Brisket Sandwich was BANGIN! Brisket was so delicious and juicy. The onions were saucy, the BBQ sauce wasn't overbearing. The cheese held it together and the fried pickle was the icing on the cake

My favorite chicken fingers in Philly. Long list of sauce options helps sweeten the deal. Good sandwiches too. 

Not crazy about the sides though, but I guess you can't have it all, still come here for the fingers and sandwiches!
Amazing vegetarian foods! Very quick and friendly service. I highly recommend the falafel sandwich.

I came here twice within a week. I am here traveling on business. This is the typical small business sandwich shop with its own spin. As far as the food goes, I had the jake the first night w/ fries. I must say the sandwich was delicious it was good portion size as I couldn't even finish it, the fries were pretty good too. In fact I was so satisfied I went back about 3 days later and tried the 50/50 e eryone had been raving about. This sandwich was like the the jake as far a portions go, but it wasn't really flavorful like the jake was. I was a little disappointed but I would definitely go back there given the chance. It was pretty reasonably priced too.

I was in philly for the weekend & obviously had to get a cheese steak for the drive home.  I looked up places walking distance from my hotel & stumbled upon this gem.  The reviews sounded good, and the other sandwiches on the menu sounded awesome.  

I got the garlic bomb cheese steak & i added mushrooms & onions.  it was EH.  It was lacking flavor.  Even with all that garlic & other yummy goodness on it.  Maybe it needed more cheese?  I don't know.  Something was off.  I had only one other cheese steak experience & it was on Long island @ this specialty ribeye place & it was amazing, so maybe I'm just comparing.  
The fries were delish though.  

I would suggest you come in & check this place out, just don't get a cheese steak.   

People were friendly & place was clean.

It's a great place for a quick poke bowl. Tucked into Queen Village, this place is kind of an oddity - that area is full of eclectic/upper end restaurants, and here you have a relatively cheap poke place. I'm not complaining - we went there for an afternoon snack. The unagi was fresh and warm and one bowl filled both us up really well. It might not be the most inviting place to sit and eat, but it's definitely fantastic food.

when done well sino-korean chicken is amazing.

this place is good but not mind-blowing

go spicy

Jake's Sandwich Board.  Best of Philly 2012.  
Best Pork Sandwiches.... Slow Roasted Pulled Pig Sandwiches (to be more specific).

We shared the 50/50 and Italian Pork sandwiches.
- 50/50 (described as 1/2 pork, 1/2 smoky grilled bacon with house sriracha spread and sharp provolone)
- Italian (described as pork, broccoli rabe, and sharp provolone cheese)

Good ingredients.  My heart and tastebuds were set in for a great time.
However, I think the execution (making of the sandwiches) failed.  
Both sandwiches we ordered - the meat was a little dry - it could use some au jus.
Also the balance between the meats and the sharp provolone cheese was off.  Boo.
The actual meats had good flavors but were a tad bit too salty and completely overpowered the cheese.  I'm a big fan of sharp provolone cheese.

We also ordered Birch Beer to share.  YUM!

I'll stick with Paesano's or Tommy DiNic's for pig sandwiches.
Paesano's - http://www.yelp.com/biz/paesanos-philadelphia#hrid:zzsHIKowcwtx361qiRoeSw
Tommy DiNic's - http://www.yelp.com/biz/tommy-dinics-philadelphia#hrid:nJuEVZ525YseV4eOyFUM2g

WHAT EVER YOU DO ,  DO NOT EAT AT THIS PLACE!
... Late night walking from target, tummy starts growing , usually wouldn't eat anything fast like this but not eaten since lunch and starving, I decided to grab something, which turned out to be a huge mistake!
I got a chicken meal , and next day all hell broke loose literally!  
The entire week I have hot / cold swats , can't keep anything besides clear liquids down , pounding headaches , and that's just scratching the surface ! After going to the dox , I find out I have food poisoning ! 
Please save yourself the doctor bill and the pain just don't eat there ! 
I can't say that each of the chains are like this but Ive eaten from there 2x and now and each time Ive gotten sick !

After giving the GF's brother and cousin a cold, blistering tour of Philadelphia's historical sites, we had to stop for a cheese steak. Would we go to Jim's? Pat's? Geno's? No thanks. I knew if there was any place that could redeem Philadelphia by providing a decent Philly's Best type cheese steak - it would be Jake's Sandwich Board.

When you enter - be prepared for the gauntlet of different types of sandwiches. Jake's doesn't pigeon-hole itself as a cheese steak only type of joint - in fact the 50/50 (half bacon, half pork) is one of the monster creations that this place houses. While the three of us all got cheese steaks, we were drooling over the other options as well. To make up for our lack of sandwich diversity, we ordered fries, potato pancakes, and chocolate-covered bacon as well.

Jake ($8.50)
Fried onions, provolone cheese

Jake's cheese steak is a solid iteration of Philadelphia's iconic sandwich, but alas - it is still no Philly's Best. The meat is plentiful however, which is appreciated. I prefer grilled onions that aren't diced up. The sesame seeded hoagie roll does add an unexpected toasty element, but apparently you can order them unseeded as well if that's your pleasure. Overall though, the sandwich was a bit dry. Jake's does carry Siracha hot sauce table-side though if you need that extra kick.

French Fries ($1.50)

Jake's fries were nicely fried and crisp - perfectly done. The innards were deliciously creamy. A bonus? They were not overly salted! It's also sold at a great price point as well for what I considered a healthy amount of fries.

Potato Pancakes ($4)

While the fries were great - the clear star of this show were the potato pancakes. As you can see - they were seasoned very well - some chives even? In any case - they were amazing!!! These potato pancakes were actually flattened, mini hash browns - I was thinking that they would be like latkes. I'm glad I was wrong. I would seriously come back just for these bad boys. True story: I talked these potato pancakes up the rest of the day - I must have brought them up at least five times. They came with a spicy chipotle mayo-type sauce that was a simply perfect complement to these perfectly fried potatoes.

Chocolate-covered bacon ($2)

At first I thought they had mistakingly left out this part of our order. Apparently though, these are made ahead of time and are put in the fridge/freezer. When we were done with our meal, we received these nicely wrapped packages. Which opened up to reveal ...

Two thick-cut slabs of bacon - covered in chocolate. This 'treat' was more unique than tasty. In fact, only the GF's cousin finished these. In my estimation, the bacon was too chewy - I was hoping and expecting more of a crisp crunch. I definitely got the whole salty-sweet dessert thing (which I love), however texturally, this was not a hit. It's not a good thing when you need to unclench your jaw after trying to eat this dessert. 

Cherry Soda ($1.50)

They have a variety of sodas here - including unique ones such as cherry. Bonus? They offer free refills! The cherry soda was definitely a hit.

And if you haven't heard about the Jake's Sandwich Board challenge on the Food Network, you may want to check it out yourself!

If you can down 3 pounds of sandwich, an entire box of Tasty Cakes, 4 Philly soft pretzels, 24 peanut chews, and a cherry champ soda in under 45 minutes - you can earn your place on the wall.In fact, if you fail - you still earn a spot on the wall - as a failure!

Last tidbit - apparently you can order all the sandwiches in a bowl without the bread, in a salad, or on a haystack of fries. Genius. 

Overall, Jake's hits the spot on so many levels (did I mention the potato pancakes?). While the cheese steak still isn't the best I've ever had, it gets the job done for the most part. I can't wait to come back for the Mensch, which contains slow-roasted brisket. And yes - for some more potato pancakes!
Teriyaki and spicy chicken bowls were bombbbbbbb! Also had the double fried sweet chili wings and im must say they top bonchon in chinatown. Def a must try for all chicken lovers in philly

Not all chains are created equal, and Chipotle does a solid job of offering more healthful options than its competition.  

Our fave is the vegetarian fajita bowl, ordered with extra black beans, extra rice, corn salsa, hot salsa and guacamole.  Squeeze some fresh lime (near the soda fountain)  over all and you are good to go.  If we are feeling particularly decadent, we may ask for the cheese and sour cream.  A bowl is more than enough for two meals.   

Both the black beans and guacamole could be better spiced and the salsas should be zippier.   When your repertoire is as limited as Chipotle, every item should be exceptional.

I've eaten here before but after today probably not. got the brisket n provolone and basically paid for a roll with a meat spread. in the past when I've ordered the sandwhich justified the price, now I just feel duped. i hardly had any brisket! service is always good but as someone who works in the city and is always buying lunch in the city if i splurge it had better be well worth it, and this just doesn't make the cut anymore.

The most disgusting buffalo sauce I've ever had. It was a huge disappointment. 

The chicken was okay at least, but the buffalo wing sauce was awful. Nothing like traditional buffalo sauce. They must have mixed it with mayo and bleu cheese or something. 

Stay away if you're a purist.

This place is in a great location, surrounding a lot of other stores, restaurants, and hotels. So if you're craving a poke bowl while staying around the hotels then this is place to go. 

As for the food, there are so many options to choose from. You can pretty much pick whatever you want for your protein, toppings, and sauce. You get a lot of food for the price that you pay; so that is a good thing! I got the spicy tuna and salmon, which tastes pretty consistent with all other sushi and poke restaurants. 

The restaurant seating is limited and a bit small; so be ready to sit elsewhere.

You can also order ahead online so you have to wait!

I am a poke addict so first priority since moving here is to find my go-to-hands-down-fave poke place.

It's never too busy here so you don't have to worry about a long wait even during the lunch rush. I like building my own bowl but there are pre-made bowls available for you to choose from if you don't want to make all the choices (and there are so many!). The poke portion is two scoops of your choice of fish. I found the portion a little small but was impressed by the freshness of my choices. I'm a salmon fan so I got the spicy salmon and chilli ponzu salmon. I love that you get your choice of unlimited side options, you get exactly what you want without having to worry about substitutions. Overall, the PokeSpot is a good go-to place right in Center City. I'm still on my hunt for my favorite place but this is a dependable choice.

DON'T BELIEVE THE HYPE!!

My wife, my son & I went there after hearing how great these burgers were. I can make a better burger @ home. Five Guys would help make this a better burger if they do a few things: put their product on a solid bun, maybe a kaiser roll(the one they use falls apart, & in my opinion, it should hold the meat), stop burning the burger( I like mine done, but not charcoaled), because this kills the flavor, & when a customer asks for condiments on his burger, make sure that they get them( I asked for hot peppers, onions, & bacon, & got a plain burger !!) They also give you a lot of fries, but, again, I've had better. If you want a better burger, go across the street to Nifty Fiftys. Cooked to order, & way better flavor.

LOVE THIS PLACE. Can't even describe how tasty this was. I have been here twice and eaten a sandwich from the Midtown Fall Festival once, so I've tried three total sandwiches here. 

Here's the low down:

50/50: Perfection on a roll. It's pulled pork, bacon, and their famed sriracha spread. The bacon isn't too crispy, just crispy enough. The spread is not too spicy, but is spicy enough. I know this is a bold statement, but...this is probably my favorite sandwich in Philadelphia.

Garlic Bomb: This is no longer on the menu, to my knowledge, but you can make it on your own based on their DIY sandwich menu. It's essentially pulled pork with garlic spread. MMM. I added provolone to mine, and let me tell you, I had the BEST breath. 

Haystack DIY: So instead of a sandwich on the DIY board, you can make your creation into a "haystack," which means you can put your sandwich stuff on top of bed of fries. What is better than replacing your bread carbs with fried carbs? Answer: nothing. On mine, I literally piled pulled pork (seeing a pattern with my food choices yet?), garlic spread, sharp provolone, and their house BBQ. Perfect, though you WILL need a fork. 

All in all, this place is a great spot. Quick service, consistently awesome food, good location, never too crowded. 5/5, baby!

Incredibly fresh Poke bowls with a lot of variety! Truly one of the best I've had in the area. Ordered off a delivery app at work and did not know what to expect. All of the ingredients were very fresh and blended well together. Planning on stopping into their physical location soon and ordering again at work.
It's good.  It's fresh.  It wasn't magical but maybe I ordered wrong.  Very clean.  Nice folks.  Worth a visit.

Ordered a pizza, well done, for delivery. It arrived so greasy, and cooked just enough to be considered done. I usually enjoy their food, but this was awful. Ate one slice, and felt sick from the grease.

Food is usually pretty good I must say and I've ordered for about 6 years now. I've had no issues with orders until this past year. They've been messing up orders and sometimes the food is spilled or missing when delivered. For example today we ordered online.. They delivered a spilled Alfredo dinner and added a Pepsi to an order we didn't ask for. Little things like that brought my 4 star experience down to 2 stars.

I used to love this place but since there's a rude teenage girl working there I won't go there again. The past three time I've  ordered this girl is so rude I wanted to cancel my order. The first time I thought maybe I was reading it wrong but the past two times its been absolutely unacceptable. It's like she's having a weird power war with the customer. She's been rude and unprofessional on the phone and in person. I love the food here and they're very fast but I'm not going to be treated disrespectfully by a tween. I won't order from here again and they'll continue to lose business as long as she's at the front register and answering phones. It's a shame because the other two teenage girls working there are very nice.
Your gonna love this! If your seeking for that "great sandwich" this is the place! Chocolate covered bacon!!

Delicious poke! Wonderful service!

I found out about this place through the ritual app and was impressed by their prices and options. The food did not disappoint. The spicy tuna was divine and their sauce selection was superb. 

I just wish they had easier access to water cups. I felt bad continuously pestering the terrific staff.
Alright, I finaly got my philly steak sandwich! I had the classic and a new type of frys they had, all was damn good!

I went here before they had their official grand opening and I was not impressed. It may have just been because they had recently opened, but I ordered the regular chicken sandwich and instead of a bun, I received four of the Original Kings Hawaiian rolls sliced horizontally. This threw the chicken-to-bun ratio off significantly, so my first few bites were all bread and no chicken. I also ordered a side of fries and I kid you not, there were twelve fries in my bag...TWELVE! I would've gone back but I was already at home by then and it wouldn't have been worth it. The house spread was tasty and the chicken was hot and fresh, so I may give them another chance in the future.

I'm always on a quest for  a $5 lunch in Center City. The shear number of suits than can afford $8 to $10 every day makes this task all the more challenging. You bet your britches I was stoked to find out that Jake's offers a $5 roast pig sandwich on Mondays!

It was good. Definitely not the best roast pork in the city, but solid. I really can't slam such a cheap sandwich, let alone one made with the most heavenly of meats. 4-Stars for being cheap, but 3-stars overall because at full price, I know DiNic's is just a couple blocks over in the terminal.
Pretty decent poke spot! They give you a lot of food for the price you pay. They pretty much have everything you can ask for in a poke bowl!
Great sandwiches, wonderful service and hospitality. Split our sandwich in two, two boats for us. Details count!

I came here for the first time for lunch. It was AMAZING. The four of us came at around noon and there was no line. For someone who is used to at least 30 min wait outside of Pokéworks in Manhattan, this is a huge plus for me. 

I built my own bowl and ordered a salad with two proteins (Garlic Ahi and Spicy Tuna) along with Sriracha Aioli. I also had seaweed salad, Edamame and Kani Salad as toppings. It was delicious. Note to myself, next time I will mix it up a bit. The sauce was a little too rich. I will either swap Sriacha Aioli with Ponzu or Shoyu sauce, or swap a fish to raw tuna or salmon. 

Highly recommend. This will be my new go-to lunch spot. :)
Seems dirty. Staff is unprofessional, and rough around the edges. Owner is aloof, and doesn't seem to care about customer service. Music is loud and inappropriate.

Come here if you want your sheeeeeeezzzse fudge up! ‍ it's so simple! Shoot me. There's too many morons that work in here, so ghetto, Rachet, this place is gross indeed. It shouldn't take 20 mins for some burgers, wings and fries. (Sigh) I'm surprise they still in business.

Just opened yesterday.  Sort of a Paesano-type operation.  Nice menu.  I like that the sandwiches appear to be slightly simpler than Paesano's.  I do love me some Paesano's, but there is a lot going on.  There's like 1-2 less ingredients in these sandwiches and it lets the ingredients shine.  I thoroughly destroyed & enjoyed a brisket sandwich with horseradish sauce, fried onions & provolone.
And here's the thing.  The onion rings were the best I've ever had, hands down no question, and I'm a ring lover.  Crispy hunks of onion (not rings really).  I think they are double-breaded, with panko being the outer layer.  Awesome, incredible.

I plan to be back there often, will update as I eat my way through the menu.

Like any girl lucky enough to get married in Philly, I wanted soft pretzels for the reception.  I am so glad I called South Philly Pretzels!  Josh is a fantastic person to work with.  For a wedding, you really want to work with someone who thinks that your wedding day is as special as you think you think it is.  Josh was one of the most responsive vendors I worked with during the whole process.  I don't think he ever took longer than 10 minutes to respond to my many questions via email.  

From the moment I spoke with Josh, he made it abundantly clear that our wedding was a top priority.  He arranged a tasting/trial for my now husband and I.  He didn't miss any details - our initials in different sizes, various salt colors, etc.  The delivery was flawless and we couldn't have been happier (pictures are posted).

Thank you South Philly Pretzel Factory!!!!
I ordered the steak Stromboli my first time ordering it arrive quick and hot. Really great will be ordering again from here
Incredible roast beef sandwich. It's seems family owned, very friendly staff. Highly recommend

Good beef ,if its fresh ! Depends how long it's sitting it can sit there a week if its slow !
More money then nicks roast beef ! Bad thing u oreder food u have to sit there for 1hr 20 min every time beef should be in and out !

Okay, these wings are definitely 5 star wings, but the rest of the choices are somewhat lacking. BUT MORE IMPORTANTLY, WHY THE HECK ARE THEY NOT OPEN ON SATURDAYS?????

Just thinking about the wings from here is making my mouth water. They are delicious! Every order is made to order, so they post the approximate wait time right at the counter. If you go right at lunch time, be prepared for a wait, but that wait is completely justified by the food. 

The wings are double fried, that's right, I said DOUBLE fried! You can't get wings any crispier than these. Oh My God, and once they put the sauce on them, it's over! As the wings start to cool a little, the sauce sticks to the breading and makes a candy shell-like texture to the wings. It's definitely a pleasant experience eating the wings. I have only had the Honey BBQ sauce on my wings, because I do not want to mess with a good thing. Others have had the sweet Chili sauce and say that they are also to die for. 

Between the wings and the rice bowls (gotta get the crispy chicken in the rice bowl), I don't really know which is my favorite. The wings are always amazing and actually really filling. My only gripe is the lack of side choices. They only offer a few sides to choose from: fries, rice, corn, broccoli, and I believe coleslaw. I may have missed a couple, but nothing real special on the sides. Like I said, the wings make up for it. 

The rice bowls are huge!! They are at least 2 meals worth and it is a perfect match of cripsy, boneless chick with rice and veggies. Just like I have not tried any other wing sauce other than the Honey BBQ, I have not tried any rice bowl other than the Teriyaki bowl. If you're feeling a slightly more healthy lunch, you can get grilled chicken on the bowl, but seriously, if you're offering me double fried chicken or grilled, I'm taking the fried. 

They also offer sandwiches and wraps, that have gotten two thumbs up from others that have been with me. But I will still be sticking to the wings and rice bowls.
This place has the best sandwiches period. The staff is fun and on point. The prices are quite reasonable for what they give you. I will go back.........

Gave it two tries and both times were bad. When chicken is your thing, make sure it's good chicken. Unfortunately, the chicken was rubbery, fatty and nasty. Tried both the fried chicken sandwich and the RCT (chicken thigh). The fried chicken tasted rubbery and of poor quality. The RCT was inedible with a thick layer of fat throughout the entire sandwich. Won't be back again.

Please open more of these.  This falafel sandwich is great. Crunchy veggies, perfectly fried falafel, and interesting sauce.  Goldie also makes fantastic fries and you can get them with shwarma spice (why you would choose not to is beyond me).  They come with ketchup, but its not crappy Heinz.  This ketchup isn't overly sweet and has a very nice tang to it.  To complete your Goldie trifecta, get a tahina shake, preferably the Turkish coffee.  This is what I want milkshakes to taste like.  Sweet, but not too much and with some interesting texture.

I'm really not quite sure why this place receives so many 1-star ratings (come on. that's harsh). I have been a big fan of Hot Tamales since some coworkers told me about it just over a year ago.  First of all, if you're going here and expect cheap Mexican food to be either A) The best Mexican food you can possibly find in the city or B) Authentic, NOT Tex-Mex style, you will be disappointed. No one goes to Taco Bell for a high-class feast, either.  That said, I do believe Hot Tamales to be excellent for what it is.  I know I'm not the only one because any time I bring up the idea of going there, any coworker within earshot rushes over with money in hand begging me to pick up something for them, as well. Their menu items may be hit-and-miss according to your tastebuds but gems can be found if you know what to order and what extras to add to them.  The addition of jalapenos or guacamole or some of their other extras can really dissolve the "blandness" people describe here.  The hot sauce IS a joke and is to be avoided though, as others have pointed out.

As for the issue with the food taking a long time.. yes, that can be a concern but it usually happens because, (not surprisingly) it's a small place and most of their customers show up around the same time of day.  For instance, I showed up at noon today just behind a group of 12 businessmen who ordered before me and sat down to wait for their food. I had to wait for their small kitchen to complete 12 full orders before getting to mine.  It happens. It's just exactly the same as if you arrive at a popular place with a drive up window and have to wait in line behind a bunch of other cars.  I would not fault the restaurant for not serving you as quickly as you deem appropriate when they are simply trying to keep up with demand for their food.

My main complaint? They are not open on weekends when I could ride bike down to eat there more often!  In summary: When I want cheap, decent tex-mex style food and am in the area, this is my first thought every time.  If I want authentic Mexican or something special, I can go to any number of other places.  Hot Tamales is great for what they are, in my opinion.
I just discovered this spot - sooo good! It seems to be family run and they are so nice. The service is great and the food is reasonably priced. I'm trying to get the word out to my neighbors :)

I have only eaten at a chipotle twice. This was my second time. I came here a week ago and I noticed there weren't any lettuce being offered. I'm not sure if they were out or if they just don't serve lettuce anymore after those outbreaks. This is the first time I've eaten at a chipotle since people have gotten sick. I had had a bowel with white rice, steak, black beans, guac, sour cream and salsa. I also order the chips with cheese dip. I had about 2 of the chips. They had a lime flavor to them. I wasn't a big fan of it. My bowel was good though and it filled me up. The service was fast. Most importantly I didn't get sick.

I love, love, love Jake's. My personal favorite is the 50/50, but the turkey and brisket options are also great. I'm pretty obsessed with the roasted vegetables too. Okay, I really have nothing bad to say about this place - even their soda options are the best. Seriously.

I love this place! Their food is fantastic and unlike other Poke places (like Hai Street Kitchen), you get unlimited toppings. The quality of the fish is great and although it's on the more expensive side for a quick lunch, the portions are huge. My favorite thing about this place is that they offer cauliflower rice - it's an extra $1 but so worth it if you are attempting to eat healthy!
Delicious poke bowls with all the toppings!! Friendly and fast service too! Definitely better to go with a bowl as the burritos are on the smaller side.

Omggg the falafel is so good here. And they're so patient when you're trying to decide what tahini sauce you'd like. The only thing i didn't like was the ketchup with the fries. It takes like curry but if you like curry you'll love it

WORST McDonalds location ever!  They consistently mix up the order, went in there one time and they were out of smoothies, another time the play place was closed for NO reason, and now they give me a salad with no croutons, no tomatoes, fatty chicken.  Once again I have wasted my money.  I eat there sparingly (wouldn't at all if it wasn't next to my job).

Sure, the fries are good.  But aren't they supposed to be?  I would never give a 5 star rating somewhere because they serve what they are supposed to and other locations do just as good if not better.
Best pizza I've had in a long time. Great crust, perfect amount of cheese. Just yummy!

This is now my favorite place to get wings and fries. Their wings are great sizes and the sauces are amazing. The fries are nice in color, shape and size plus taste. A nice crunch to them it's a great side order. This a nice little place to get a great meal.

I tried the Pokéspot yesterday with two friends. We all built our own poké bowls. I got unmarinated salmon and tuna with too many toppings to remember (unlimited!). 

Pros: The ingredients tastes fresh, lots of carb choices (white or brown rice/zucchini noodles/cauliflower rice), very filling portions, kind and courteous staff, closer than all the other poké places!

Cons: Not a ton of seating and some wasted space, it can get a little loud in there. Not much in the way of cons!


Will definitely be back!

Had a Buffalo chicken steak! It wasn't good at all the meat taste old. It was filled with meat and the fries were a lot. But the food wasn't good at all. New to the neighborhood so I'm trying a few spots. Probably wouldn't eat here again. Total was $11.02 reasonable

My wife and enjoyed the meal. The crispy onions are very good. Also, the classic pulled pork is good. The pork is roasted in house and shredded.  Ample helpings and reasonable price. Worth stopping in. However, note, it was 32F outside and the store was a little chilly.

My first experience at Jakes was amazing. I had no expectations because I just needed a sandwich for lunch at work. It arrived promptly and the sandwhich was out of this world. I got the Village Turkey and chocolate covered bacon- because how could I not? The Sammy was great and the chocolate covered bacon was to diiie for. 

I have gotten jakes 4 times since the. The second time and third I did pick up and got the same order as the first. It was to be expected, great. 

The past two times have been increasingly difficult. Last night my order arrived 50 minutes after they said it would and I knew my order was at my door, not because someone called me but because there was a car outside with music blaring that my sandwhich came from...

Today it took about two hours to get my food and I changed it up and got the turbacon- not as good as the village turkey. I got a cookie too that was good but very small for $1. I called three times to see where my order was and they just kept saying it would be there any second... 2 hrs later....

I will eat at jakes again but I will being doing pick up or ordering my lunch very early. Luckily they have two locations so maybe 40ths street delivery etiquette will be better ...



Ok I'm editing my review because I just got a call from jakes and they're refunding my order for the inconvenience this week. I truly appreciate when a business takes time to correct its mistake. I truly do believe this place has great sandwiches and I was truly agitated with the delivery process. However I'm extremely impressed with the business in making it up to me. 
Jake's- you're off my shit list and back on my recommendation list

bunch of whiners on here. It is very good for the price. I came back and told my co-workers to try this place. the place is clean, the people where nice and the food is not bad. Can't ask for much more in this ratty city!

Worst cheesesteak I've ever had. The meat was all fat, not edible!!!

Ps the onion strips are ok
The wings here are fire. The fries not so much. I got the spicy garlic wings and loved them. I can't say anymore and this place because I got the food using Uber eats.

Finally got around to trying my first sushi burrito and it did not disappoint! The rainbow burrito was so good and fresh. The staff was really friendly and got my order together really quickly. I'll definitely be back!
I ordered a bowl of teriyaki chicken with brown rice, tastes great~ I am satisfied with the price and service. I definitely will be going back again.
This place is so great! The staff is so friendly and well knowledged on the type of food they served. I never had a poke bowl and they gave good recommendations.

I don't understand how this place stays in business. They have very limited hours and their food is terrible. I have never had worse Mexican food. Nothing is authentic to the point I even asked for hot sauce and was given buffalo sauce and was told that is all they have right now. Chipotle has better Mexican food than this place. I would recommending going anywhere else but here for food. Well at least it was a cheap mistake.

LOVE Five Guys!!! I was happily surprised when I discovered this recently opened location. I just had to stop in and get a burger. I always have a blast mixing and matching the stuff that I put on there. Currently my favorite is tomatoes, lettuce, pickles, grilled onions, jalapenos, hot sauce, and ketchup. A definite plus for having real jalapanos instead of the pickled kind. And as always, the over abundant amount of fries gives the Five Guys' signature greasy brown bag look top it off. If you have never tried their burger before, you definitely need to go and SOON.

i agree the hype is over the type.  we finally went to see what the big deal is.  the hamburger most order is two fresh patties grilled to order.  i had mine "animal style"(i wish In N Out would go national) -- 5 guys calls it the everything burger with grilled mushrooms, pickles mayo and fried onion with lettuce and tomatoes.  the fries are fresh cut and fried to order.  cannot go wrong.  the salted peanuts are free to scoop in a small dish, but i think people see them as a decoration as they are not so fresh.  overall not bad and if you love burgers, go here instead of other burger fast food joints.   the place is run by a bunch a kids who laugh too much and it adds to the wait, but i dont mind.  my homemade burgers are bigger and cheaper.

Basically like any standard Chipotle, but with frequent issues. 

The staff is always rude. Every single burrito I've ever ordered here has fallen apart. They just try to hide their mistake by adding foil to the destroyed burrito. 

Is it that hard to wrap them correctly?
Terrible customer service.  girl who waited on me was so rude and mumbled. There was a puddle of water at the bottom of my bowl.

I previously wrote a very negative review, but my last visit was excellent. The new staff were very friendly and the food was delicious! Hopefully this trend continues, because in the past this chipotle has been awful.

We ordered the 10 piece double fried wings with a side of fries. I liked how were able to choose two different sauces for our wings, so we went for soy garlic and honey bbq. I'm always interested in everyone's take on KFC so I was excited to try the soy garlic wings out. I was pretty disappointed. The soy garlic wings were completely drenched in sauce that it overpowered all the other parts of the chicken. The honey bbq ones were okay - nothing to rave about. They also the lacked kind of crispiness I like when it comes to KFC. Although I was not impressed with the wings, I will say that $10 for 10 wings and a side is a good deal.

I'd never had Poke before, didnt even know what it was, but it was GREAT here and we definitely will go again. The quality of the fish and everything else was very high, and the service was fast and friendly. Good view of Headhouse Sq. too.

I WENT TO FIVE GUYS BURGERS THE OTHER DAY!  DID YOU HEAR ME???  I SAID, I WENT TO FIVE GUYS BURGERS!  WHAT?  YES.  FIVE GUYS.

This is no place to go for a nice quiet fifteen minutes away from work!  Five Guys is a large open space with a concrete floor so it echoes as much as the Grand Canyon and there's no shortage of noise!  

Each and every time a patron walks in the doorway of Five Guys, as many staff members as possible all yell at the top of their lungs, "Two in the door!" or "One in the door!"  Then everyone else responds by yelling, "Two in the door!  Got it!"  The same goes for the number of patties ordered; "Two patties!"  "Two patties, got it!"  

I am absolutely convinced of a two things:
a) The same people who yell "Two in the door!" are the exact same people who yell, "Two in the door!  Got it!"
b) Some of the staff took the job at Five Guys simply so they could yell all day!

One particular staff member's speaking voice was at the same annoyingly high pitch and volume as her two-in-the-door squeal so there was no relief to the insanity of yelling.  

WTF, Five Guys?  Is this seriously necessary?  While I was there, never once was there an occasion that more than two people ever walked in!  I mean, seriously, if you need that much advance warning that you have a stampede of three customers, perhaps you should reexamine your business model.  

OK, I get it that you're trying to re-create the old short-order restaurants where the 55 year old waitress who's been working at the same place for the past 32 years yells out her order to the line cook who's worked there for the same amount of time.  I get it.  Now, stop.  It's unnecessary chatter that adds nothing to fare you offer.

The fries?  Well, if you take them out of the paper cup they're served in as I did, and dump them into the paper bag that the burger came in, you end up with one greasy bag.  No surprise there (and no reflection on my review because of it).

The burgers?  Mediocre at best.  Whoopdie-doo, you put two small grilled burgers on a bun and call it a "large burger".  Well, no, it's not actually a "large burger" as a paying customer would assume; it's actually two small burgers on one bun.  Perhaps someone needs to yell that out too.

For the price, Wendy's offers a burger that is hands-down in the same ballpark as Five Guys.  

And I know a LOT better ways to enjoy "five guys"!  I'm jus' sayin', is all...

Wooo Hoo!! Potbelly's!! It just can't get better than this place!!!

Excellent subs, it doesn't matter which one you get, they're all tremendous! They're very very reasonably priced and the shakes are seriously to die for. I usually get either the Wreck or the Italian Sub with everything. I get the macaroni salad and an oreo or vanilla shake and my week is totally made! 

Seriously, if you want incredible lunchtime food at a great price, you really gotta get it HOT!

Chipotle is the best thing that has ever happened to Penn. :) My burrito is perfect ever time. They also have a line at 9 am, which is hilarious. And I love that they're overtaking Qdoba which is a terrible establishment with disgusting food.

You can't really give Chipotle less than 2 stars because you know what you're getting yourself into before you go. The food is average at any location but good for a quick mex fix. The reason I'm reviewing this location in particular is that despite the employees being pleasant, everything I wanted was out. Asked for veggies, wait was 8 minutes, I passed. Asked for guac, wait was 30 minutes!!! Obviously I passed. Asked for chips and guac (before I knew guac was out) and she charged me for it and said just a minute then after told me about the guac and also said they were out of chips completely! So now she had to go back and refund me. Again, the staff was very nice but the system was clearly very broken. And mind you, this was at 7pm, wasn't like 9:55 closing time. 

I would return to a Chipotle in general but I would not make any effort at all to return to this location.

Consistently fresh, delicious and generously portioned poke. Many options for base, protein, toppings and sauces with no up charge for premium ingredients such as kani and seaweed salad. Great spot to grab lunch if you're shopping around in the Rittenhouse area. They also have a rewards program where you collect a star at every purchase and get your 11th poke bowl for free. I also sometimes receive coupons. Good value and hands down the best poke spot in the city of Philadelphia.

In terms of fast food, this is as good as it gets. Burgers are cooked fresh in front of you with your choice of many toppings, fries are great, and the whole atmosphere is straight to the point and done well. They only do one thing, but they do it very well.
This maybe my favorite 5Guys it's. Clean the cheese melted nicely and We loved the fries
Very good BBQ Pork but huge portions, too big for me for lunch on a weekday.
Very clean location and one of the best Poke bowls I've had. The ingredients seemed fresh and the spicy mayo sauce was delicious!
The employees are very rude, there is always a missing ingredient, and the food is often way over-seasoned or completely bland. The worst chipotle I have experienced.

Jake's impresses me a little more each and every trip. In my personal opinion it is clawing for best sandwich shop in Philly. Think about any classic Philadelphia sandwich and just add a frill. In no means is it over the top though. They celebrate Sriraccha Sauce here, they even have "I Love Sriraccha " T-shirts for sale.  

They have a great cheesesteak here called the 'Firesteak.' It is a traditional cheesesteak with a deep fried long hot on a Carangi roll and for a small up charge you can get ghost pepper on it. If you choose the ghost pepper, you must sign a waiver. Pork is their speciality though. The 50/50 sandwich is the crown jewel of Jake's, at least in my opinion. It's half bacon, half roast pork, Sriraccha spread and sharp provolone. 

They must buy a fresh cooked pig everyday because there is a full pig on display everyday that they get the pork from.

To all the people that told me they were better than qdoba, Get a life lol. Nothing spectacular, taste okay. Portion size not bad. Corn was wayy to sweet threw my entire meal off. I will admit the guacamole was awesome other than that I could've spent ten bucks elsewhere

It feels like there are so many new poké places opening in Philly, but this is one of my favorites! Great variety of protein choices (not just tuna, salmon, but chili ponzu salmon, spicy tuna, ahi tuna.etc). I appreciate that they have salad options instead of rice as well.
 
Atmosphere: Clean, with seating for around 10-15. Generally pretty quiet before 12, with available seating. They also make it easy to order beforehand, so it's really convenient and quick for grabbing takeout!
 
Food: Main benefit is that there is a lot of variety (gluten-free options for sauces, and the protein options taste quite fresh). I thought the amount of sauce they put was just right, whereas some other poké places put a bit too much in.
 
Recommended Must-Try: Not usually everyone's favorite, but I love masago (fish eggs) as a topping! Would recommend trying it at least once with poké!
 
Overall: 4.5/5 - very quick, easy, and tasty lunch option! Only small complaint is the price, but you're also getting a good amount of fresh tuna, salmon.etc, so the price also makes sense to me.
I had no idea what exactly I wanted just chicken and biscuits and the manager helped me order without ending up with a million sides. Great customer service!
I have a bad experience with this place, "the Worst Buffalo Wing" My Life, has a service that should improve their quality and Customer Service

This is quite the SPOT! Large portions, friendly staff, clean restaurant and great food. Can't get any better than that. You select 2 or 3 proteins and your base (rice or salad), then you get unlimited toppings of seaweed salad, Kani salad, roe, mango, mushrooms, etc. will try my best not to come here every day.

The Good:
In my experiences, you tend to get more food for your money here than the Chipotles in Center City.
There's a considerable amount of seating, and if that somehow fills up, you're right next to Penn's quad, which is good for Taco picnics.
Compared to Qdoba, Chipotle's ingredients are fantastic. It's not necessarily authentic Mexican food, but it's tasty.

The Bad:
LONG LINES. At peak times especially, expect to wait a bit. This isn't a reflection on the staff, who are actually pretty efficient, but more a consequence of serving a college neighborhood.
The other patrons are genuine college students. Sometimes, it can get a little bro-ey. For someone like me who lives in Spruce Hill but isn't a student, that's a huge turn off.

The name of the restaurant is "Hot Tamales" and they don't serve tamales. When I asked the Betty-Page wannabe about it, she was a little rude. Needless to say, never stepping foot in a Hot Tamales again.

A damn good sandwich but their attitude kept it from being 4-stars. My wife and I both had Groupons which we decided to cash in before they ran out of the Turducken special. When we ordered, then remembered we had two Groupons ($10 each) we told her we wanted to order separately. She was kind enough just to take them together instead of ringing us up again. Afterwards she was berated by either the owner or manager in front of us. Obviously he wanted to get the point across to us (and to her). 

I mean seriously, if you're on Groupon you are trying to get new business and the least you can do is try to make everyone that visits feel welcome so they return. The service for others wasn't really with a smile either, there seemed to be a lot of tension between a couple workers (and most noticeably the aforementioned jerk). 

Either way, when it came down to the food it was really great. I had the Turducken sandwich which was turkey, duck, & chicken with a cranberry sauce, apple-sausage stuffing, gravy & three hash brown cakes on a sesame seed foot long. I saw a lot of turkey & a little duck but not too much chicken or stuffing. Either way the sandwich was very tasty and came with a free soda. Hey, its or a limited time only (like the McRib) so you best get on it... 

My wife had the classic which is meatballs with roasted garlic spread, marinara, spinach, mozzarella, & fried onions. Again, a very tasty sandwich with even distribution throughout. 

So a very positive food experience and a sub-par personality experience. They were very slow and the sandwiches came out pretty fast. We will probably return if in the area and need a quick bite at a good price, but the sandwich wars are pretty strong in Philly so it might be awhile.

Really good affordable sandwich. But when I asked for a cup of tap water they refused. Pretty sure that's illegal and violation of health codes. 

This place clearly has no clue what it's doing.
The best fries!! Day or night! Open late night too! Good for the soul man!

This is a preliminary review of sorts.  I'd passed by Jake's many times but never gone in.  This weekend I ordered a sandwich at the Midtown Fall Festival.   I got the 50-50, which is half pulled roast pork, half bacon with sriracha mayo and sharp provolone.  I inhaled it.  While I could have done without the Lord-of-The-Flies-esque pig heads on the table (seriously.  there were two.  ew.), the sandwich was out of this world.

My interest is now piqued and I will definitely be exploring what else Jake's has to offer.

This place was the highlight of my trip to Philly this summer. It has the most original and diverse menu, and honestly leaves nothing to be desired unlike Pats or Geno's. Can't go wrong with the Jake, but I reallly wanted to try the 50/50 and their Siracha mayo, Nom! It's draws a crowd without being rediculous (ahem Pat's, Geno's, and Jim's). The place is clean, and the service is quick. Worth the 3 hour drive for sure.

run from this dirty nasty food store! they have an app if you order your food will never come! then they have the nerve to be mad you ordered from the app they advertise like wtf to make it worst they never made my food and made me drive all the way to the store for a refund i will never ever go to this store again

I had a coupon and had not been to a Popeyes in years so I decided to try out this location. Admittedly we were not noticed right away and there were no other customers but I see below comments bashing the service while I experienced friendly and courteous people behind the counter. I always go for the Mac and cheese but I am always disappointed in the lack of flavor in ALL fast food restaurants. The biscuits are high in calories and high in salt but not terrible. We ordered spicy chicken tenders and spicy bonafide. Both were delicious and great when reheated the next day. I was nervous how I would feel the next day being that I don't eat fast food/greasy food very often and I felt fine. I would differently go back and try different options from the menu as well.
Suppose to close at 8- walked in at 7:45 and they said they were closed!! Don't post your hours til 8 and close earlier than that time
Very delicious tacos! I love the soft tacos with Barbacoa and guacamole so much~ Reasonable price with three tacos that satisfies belly!

The posing says open until 10pm, at 840 on monday July 8, 2019, they were closed.
I had been here a few times during the week when they were open, food was as expected

I'd normally switch around from pizza shop to pizza shop until I found this little Gem that's almost at the corner of Cottman & Franford. If a place can put out that much stuff on one menu (actually it reads like a little book) it's gotta be good. And they don't hire fat & ugly girls either. I think it's a require ment that if if you're gonna work there, you gotta be smokin' hot. Druggies is just like the women that he employs~smokin' hot !!!
    So folks, If you wanna pretty-descent hot pizza, stronboli, really good wings, & a lot of other high-in-chlosterol (but it's sooo-sooo good) food. Go to Druggie's.It's a mark above all the other 5,955 pizza shops on Frankford & Cottman Avenue area pizza joints, this place won't let you down. You won't regret it  folks ! The only thing that they could do a little better in is to hire their delivery drivers' from the U.S.A. & learn how to speak the English language, but just as long as I get my Druggie's !!!
    Druggie's out beats Pizza City & all them other guys that are nearby. I'm surprised that their still in buisness. Hey Drougie's~ You got myself as a customer for life !!! God Bless You All & God Bless The Good Ol' U.S. of A.

It's chipotle, if you like it you like it. There is plenty of seating which is convenient, food is just what you would expect from a chipotle- build your own burrito bowl is the best. Tip: if you do a bowl you can ask for a tortilla wrap on the side at no extra charge

With the increasing competition (Mexican Post, Qdoba and now Joe's), I would like to give a shout out to my favorite place down town. It's not the best Mexican food in the world, but it is quick and provides definite value-for-money. I think that you are better off going here than one of the large fast food chains, plus they are local and different, which is nice when you can get it.

Hot Tamales is really only open for lunch. You can get a good, freshly made burrito here for less than $4. For this area, that is an unbeatable lunchtime deal. Get in line before 11:45 am or you may be in for a long wait. 

There is a seating area, which quickly fills at lunch time. The interior is simple but well-maintained, so I would not call it a dive. It is probably not the best place for a romantic date, unless you are into Formica table tops and offbeat eighties music. (There is no TV, but they do play B-sides and such from eighties-era bands and that is kind of fun for people who are of a certain age.)

It might be true that the pricing on the take-away hot sauce and rice is a little stiff. There can't be much margin on the actual burritos, so I can't find it in me to hold an extra dime or two against them. If you are eating in, there are large squeeze bottles of hot sauce for no extra charge.

Solid choice for poke but you need to know what you want when you walk in the door as the staff doesn't seem to be trained beyond knowing the names of stuff.

They have salmon and tuna - each are available 3 different ways.  They have other proteins that didn't register with me because they weren't raw fish.  I'm not looking for the "accessible" options when I go out for Poke but maybe some people are - not my thing.  The fish seemed fresh and was portioned out with little scoops so I'm guessing it weighed out as promised.

They have a pretty wide variety of the assorted toppings and sauces.  Again, not much help from the staff but I can point with the best of them and managed to build a more than decent bowl.  All of the usual stuff.

Of note: have you ever had a King Cake and tried to find the baby?  Same experience with the wasabi.  That didn't make much sense to me.

BOGO! 
$1.00 to park for 20 minutes
fat bowls full of delicious food
a staff fully equipped to answer all my questions
clean bathroom 
comfortable seating
points program too! 
what more could you ask for?....more sauce. that's it. That is probably my fault for just not asking. lol. 
I'll be back!
Great wings! They are a bit pricey but worth cause the wings are huge.  One of the best in Philly for sure.

I am giving this restaurant four stars, only because of a minor detail, otherwise, it would have received five stars. 

I have heard of this restaurant before, but never knew where it was located, and I usually bring my own Lunch into work, so I never try new places.

I decided to give this place a try (using Ritual) and realized that their restaurant is directly across the street from where I work! (Convenient!)

I ordered a Create-Your-Own Stir Fry. I got chicken, pineapple, roasted cashews, brown rice, roasted broccoli, sweet potatoes, and asked for the sesame garlic sauce. I also requested the garlic herb focaccia bread on the side. 

When I walked into the store, it was a LOT larger than I imagined it to be. There were plenty of tables to eat, as well as the stations where the workers create your meals were very large! It was also very convenient that they had a rack in the middle of the store where the pick up orders were located. I saw my name, grabbed a fork located in the back, and went on my way. 

As for the meal itself, it was delicious! It was warm, I loved the sauce (it had a hint of spice which is perfect cuz I hate anything spicy). The portions are very large, I only ate half of the bowl and I'm already full and put it away at work. 

The only reason I am giving this location four stars instead of five is because I never received the bread I requested on the side. Unless it's supposed to be chopped into my stir fry and I didn't realize?? But there was no bread in my bowl. Perhaps there was a small bag on the side of my bowl I needed to pick up which contained my bread? I don't know, it's annoying because I paid an extra $0.89 for that, and while that's not a lot of money, I don't want to be paying something for nothing.

It's not as good as I'd hoped nor as bad as I'd feared.
Potbelly is a fast-food sandwichs chain with decent prices and an EXTREMELY limited menu.

I had a Chicken Salad salad that was passable.  I had them add artichoke hearts and remove the dried cranberries.
Though I am not thrilled I prefer it to Quizno's and Subway.

Line moved quickly and servers were well trained and fairly friendly.  (But THAT's because they are new.) I am certain that quality will diminish over time, as most fast food places (and manicure joints) do.

Wow, now I don't know whether Luhv or Goldie is my favorite moderate/fast food vegan place.  As impressive as Luhv is, I think Goldie is even better.  I simply have never had falafel this good.  In fact, I went a few years not being sure I even liked falafel, because at other restaurants, it is so heavy and bland.  Goldie's falafel is crisp, light, and delicious.  I loved it served atop Goldie's salad, which featured mint leaves, beets, chopped cucumber, delicate salad greens, and a drizzle of tahini.
This place is the best poke I've had in my life. I just introduced my boyfriend to them and he is equally obsessed.

Love this place. I've read complains about the price but I think you get plenty for what you pay.  I'm most impressed at how clean this place is and how fast the workers are.  Even the manager helps out which is a plus.

Chipotle is the best restaurant ever known to humankind.  Stephen Starr and all his iron chefs cant touch it.  Seriously.  Just give up at being a restauranteur because Chipotle has arrived in Philly.  Honestly, would you rather have some overpriced sushi and tempura that you can get at any two-bit Japanese place while listening to some God-awful techno or would you rather eat Chipotle?  Don't answer because that's a rhetorical question.  I don't know why I am comparing Pod to Chipotle but either way, Chipotle is awesome.  It's a ton of fresh, hot, well-seasoned, delicious food at a very low price.  It fills you up, sometimes even enough for two meals.

Okay so the food was good burger and fries can't go wrong (you can but they didn't) 
 Everything was fresh including fries (still warm) not to mention they give you a shucks load of them 

Free refills on soda was a plus 
Clean inviting atmosphere and staff 
Great music 
I notice several small complaints hence the 3 not 4 stars 
I notice that there was constant glove changing by staff members was was awesome 
How one particular staff member seems to have a lot of nervous energy he kept rubbing every surface with his gloves on as if massaging it then he touch the cheese on someone's burger before changing his gloves. I don't think he realized it or did it purposely like I said it seemed more anxiety than anything. 
All other staff members where great with cross contamination measures (probably should give 4 stars ) wish I could rate the food and cleanliness separate. 

Outcome I was satisfied but wasn't wowed by my food 
I will return I recommend this location 
Great for families 

Cleanliness of employees and establishment deserves 4 stars

I work in the NorthEast area, so I'm always on the lookout for a nice, quick spot to grab lunch. So, I was in the area and stopped here to see what they had. (Sidenot, its of no consequence, but its funny how ALL of the pizza joints in the Northeast are run by Russians or Brazilians, and never Italians.) I saw a few lunch specials that sounded pretty scrumptious, so I decided to go with a "Kenny Special," which was like chopped chicken fingers, with bacon and whiz, topped with some special sauce/seasonings. First, it was HUGE, and it was only like $6, so that was pretty cool too. The only issue was that it wasn't very good. It was just "okay," and the combination of bacon, whiz and seasonings just made the whole thing overly salty as well. Because of the selection and price, I'll probably stop by at some point in the future, but I'm not going out of my way.

I just went to your location in Philadelphia at 19th and Market, for the first time, and ordered the Stir Fry Plum Hoisin.  Imagine my surprise when, finally sitting down at my desk delighted to eat my stir fry, I notice that the beef which is supposed to be included in the dish is nowhere to be found.  I note that a prior reviewer who had the same dish had noted that the beef was minimal.  It seems you seem to be taking minimal to levels not yet seen before.  

While I could understand how a minor ingredient such a sesame seeds may have been forgotten, it's hard to imagine how a major component such as the sole protein source could be completed left out.  

I would like to be able to say that I would be a repeat customer, but I'm not sure my protein-less body could stomach a walk over to get another incorrect meal.  I hope corrections could be made so that future patrons would not be deprived in the way that I have been today.  In the absence of that, I would advise folks who like to receive what they order to stay away.

Not much to look at but delicious food and great service.  Here I'd the place to have a Philly cheese steak. Full of roasted beef onions and provolone cheese on a toasted bun. Yum.   The ginseng lemon honey tea was delicious. Not crowded on a Sunday but I imagine packed during the week.

Came here for the food challenge and it was outstanding.

Great bread and cheesesteak. Pretzels were great and the cherry side is the perfect "wine" for the meal. Nice service.

Small place and lots of unique sandwhiches to still try.

The sign by the digital register says debit and credit cards only. Next to it is a tip jar with cash in it. John Belushi as Falafel Chef would make a perfect skit of this place. I might come back after July 1st when they have to take cash.

The food is great when it's made correctly but you NEED better front end employees. They are the reason my order is wrong 90% of the time and it's become increasingly more frustrating having to call back and wait for my food to be made correctly. And the new girl knows absolutely nothing that is available on the menu which makes ordering with her basically impossible.
Everytime my family eats over there we end up getting sick. But at other Popeye's we're perfectly fine. Something isn't right with this picture.
Pizza here is delicious! We ordered supreme pizza and wings and they really good. The order was made fast and delivered quickly.

Ordered their signature sandwich, fries and fried pickles. First impression was the sandwich size.. very small. At a price of $7-$8 it is far too small. It was about the size of a value sandwich from a fast food restaurant. I have had Wishbone's fried chicken sandwich and it is at least twice the size and MUCH better. The good news is the sandwich had decent flavor, although nothing special. 

To add to the disappointment, the fries were really awful. No crisp, no seasoning, just pale basic fries. Once again, reminiscent of a value meal fry. "Fried" pickles were soggy and wet. Finally, the sauce with the fries and pickles tasted like sweetened thousand island. I did order this for delivery so perhaps that contributed to the overall poor meal. I may give Hatch and Coop one more chance in person. It's a shame because the concept and menu looked great. Oh well

Great quick sandwich place that is an order-at-the-counter but still has lots of tables and counter seats to enjoy your meal without feeling rushed. The bread is phenomenal and I find myself craving the sandwich already from time to time (I got the chicken with the roasted red peppers, cheese, and avocado mash). Now that I'm writing my review... I want to go back even more.

This place does it right!  They slow cook all of their meets and it shows in the quality.  I usually go for a Brisket or Pork sandwich and I am never let down.  I am there at least once a month to check out their monthly special; usually a seasonally inspired sandwich with some creative ingredients that cannot be found in a standard sandwich shop.  Lately, they have been service a corned beef on rye on Wednesdays; I only got there once but plan on going back.  The meat was extremely high quality and the rye was thick cut, soft and moist, just like it should be.  

I have also used Jake's to cater a party at my home.  I ordered a Brisket and Pork make your own set up, and my guests loved it.  The Brisket was completely devoured but I did have some Pork left over, which I enjoyed the following week.  

If you ever find yourself in Midtown and need a bite, definitely check this place out.  If you are not in Midtown, make it a point to get there; this is a unique place serving creative sandwiches with quality ingredients that are usually only found in expensive restaurants!
I was at five guys yesterday i ordered my food.  But wen i got my food.  The burger was pink i asked to speak to a manger. They said he s not in.
Loved the food, salad was great, fries were better, and the tehina milkshake was the best. Will return here again.

If you ever told me that I'd be going to a grocery store just to eat, I'd think you're crazy. But alas, this is what I've been known to do these days at this amazing Whole Foods location. And with the addition of Goldie recently, I finally get to try Michael Solomonov's more recent food expansions in Philly. I've bookmarked the original Goldie location since it's opened, but I just never got around to trying it--thank you Whole Foods for solving my problem! 

Now, to the food...holy falafel! Goldie is all sorts of yum and then some! I ordered the falafel with the schug tahini and an order of plain fries. My fresh pita was loaded with ample fried balls of goodness and perfectly balanced with a cucumber and tomato (Israeli?) salad. It was so freaking good! The schug flavored tahini was explained to me as a Serrano chili sauce I believe, and it added the perfect amount of heat. As for the fries, even plain, they were sooooo good! The fries were nice and crispy and very fresh. I can't wait to try more items off their menu.
One of best poke places I've tried. Food is very fresh and service is great. They give you a decent amount of seafood or chicken with you food.

Used to go here often when I lived nearby, stopped in recently and was surprised how neglected the place was, very dirty. Only 1 other table was being used but they were all filthy and this was shortly after opening, so the dining area was obviously not cleaned the night before, nor did they take the time to clean before they opened up.

Seems like both the night mgr and the day mgr don't care. I didn't get anything when I saw the state of the dining area.

If they're filthy when they open up imagine what else is being neglected that we can't see.
I really like this place. Great options for vegetarians and the portions are very generous. Also a good location for when you are gallivanting around rittenhouse.
Service is terrible. I've been twice now and had a terrible experience with rude and nasty staff. The food is mediocre and they nickel and dime you for everything. I'll never go back.

Extremely disappointed, I ordered a large plain pizza it was cold had to warm it up in my oven, Don't Think I will be returning , Feel Like they gave me a pizza that was already sitting there , not satisfied smh ‍

I don't normally write reviews but this time I had too. I ordered some food from them and found pieces of plastic in the food. It was late so I had to call to speak to someone the next day. The owner told me he couldn't do anything because I didn't call right then when I got the food. Mind you , I did but it was closed by the time I called. I told him I wanted my money back. He asked if I still had the players. This guy sent someone to my house to put up a player to give me some off the money back . I'm never ordering from them. My kids could have choked on the plastic.That's disgusting.

I'm happy I've found yet another good, new lunch spot!  The concept here is like many other Poke places.  You select your protein(s), a base, toppings, and sauce.  To get you started, they also have standard recipes (their signature options).  You pay based on the amount of protein (and maybe an extra dollar on certain toppings like avocado).  You'll most likely land within the $10-$15 range for a bowl.

For my first bowl with PokeSpot, I ordered one of their signature options.  However, I was still able to customize it a bit with a few extra ingredients.  I got two scoops of protein, Garlic Ahi Tuna, on their zucchini string base.    Toppings included two types of seaweed (black and green), cucumbers, soy beans, and ginger.  Sorry, I can't remember which one or two I added (on top of the signature recipe), but am glad I did as I recall the signature bowl looked a bit light.

Taste was on point, but I did feel a bit more of the protein was in order to get the value proposition right.  And while I am hopeful for a bit more protein in my next bowl, but I wasn't hurting of hungry once I finished. 

Service was friendly and quick, however, I came in around 1pm so missed the lunch rush I'm sure.  The place is clean and has some limited seated for those not looking to head back to the office to quickly. I settled for a working lunch back at my desk =(.

Asked for easy on cheese pizza. And I got this one! Disappointed!! 
Delivered on time by Grubhub, thank you !

I'm definitely a Bonchon snob and can't wait for them to open in Philly, but "Chix" is a pretty damn good alternative. For $7 you get six wing pieces and a choice of side (go for the daikon radish or cole slaw). I ordered online and got my order within 20 minutes! The wings were still crispy with the sticky sauce fried on, and I can't help but say this is on par with my Bonchon (Annandale, VA). "Chix" has gained VIP exclusive access to my "chillin at home in ma sweat pants .. can't get off the couch .. let's just order" rotation.

Came here for lunch with my husband. The name give a feel of a unique and one of a kind spot. 
I had high expectations of this place. I mean, who doesn't like good fried chicken.

Pros:
The french fries were actually really good. They are served with a tangy sweet tasting sauce. 

Cons:
The chicken was a big disappointment. We ordered the special of the day...Honey Fried Chicken Sandwich. The slightly sweet flavor of the chicken was good, as well as the crispy breading. But that's it. The actual chicken was overcooked and very dry. Part of the chicken sandwich I actually had to bite with my side teeth because it was that tough. The sandwich was served on an King's Hawaiian bun. The bottom of the sandwich bread was greasy and falling apart, as if the chicken hadn't been drained of the grease.

Drink wise, they only offer water and seltzer.

Overall:
The idea of this place is great. But the end resulting food leaves a lot to be desired. Not sure I would come back. Maybe after some time, and some improvements I would try again.

I grabbed Poke on my lunch break yesterday for the first time and did the build your own bowl. You can choose two different types of protein (they have chicken and tofu for those who don't like fish!) and unlimited toppings. They did run out of their supply of the kani topping I wanted but it was still delicious without it. 

They offer more than just rice as a base as you can choose zucchini noodles or cauliflower rice (for extra). The staff is very friendly and helpful with offering suggestions of sauces / toppings. I definitely plan on coming back!

The veggie bowl is great and they also have sofritas to add to the vegetarian options. Overall it's a typical chipotle. It gets really full around lunch and dinner, but the line moves pretty quick. 

This location runs out of things (like guacamole) sometimes, but I haven't had this problem often. However they do seem to have unexpected closings a lot more than often than any other location I have encountered. They often close here for bad weather or random unknown reasons (while the surrounding restaurants stay open).
The best poke spot in Philly!! Good ambiance, great staff, and fresh poke. Had the one in NY and had to get it in Philly as well. Bomb!

I've been to this place couple of times. I would definitely recommend their sushi poke bowl. The sushi were fresh and the portions were right on. The services were fast and they also have sittings. Definitely is my to go sushi poke bowl store.

The staff at this location simply can not read the orders.  I customized a noodle dish and they left off half of the freaking ingredients.  Sadly, I had walked all the way to my office and could not return to get my money back.  The taste of the food was good would have been better if they actually read my order when it was being made.
Horrible service. Was the only one in there, and waited 5-10 minutes before I walked out because no one helped me.

I am still waiting for Bonchon to open, so as of right now, this is still the best chicken place around center city, so I was surprised they did not have many good reviews. The service here might be slow but since its double fried chicken, and coated by order, it cant be fast. I think that the place look more like a fast food chain, so pp was expecting the speed of those. The chicken here are good, and it comes with a free side with your order, the best sauce are soy garlic, spicy bbq, and sweet chili, and they are comparable to SoHo, much cheaper too! Come try out, you wont be disappointed!

I used to love this place before they re-modeled (which was essentially paint the walls and add a lighted cow in the background). My biggest complaint is that they got rid of the steak sandwiches!!! WTH? Now they only have brisket, pork, turkey and veggie. There is also no option for adding an egg, which was an ingredient in my previous favorite sandwich - the steak and egg! To top things off, they added about 2 bucks to the cost per sandwich, so now walking out of there paying under $10 for lunch is out of the question. The sandwiches seem slightly smaller too, but don't quote me on that. Very disappointed. 

Today I had the Meganillah. It was okay. I think there is a good chance that this place goes under in the future, whereas I wouldn't have said that before.

Stopped in today and got the 'new and improved' classic. Although I never tried the earlier classic. Now it is meatballs, marinara (I refuse to call it gravy or red sauce), spinach, mozz and caramelized onions. Holy shit! It now beats out the Village Turkey as best sandwich. Also I think their fries seem to be getting better, if that's possible.

A Checkers is a Checkers is a Checkers.

Not the best location, but they've got a drive-thru, so who cares? Fries are delicious.

Great falafel sandwich. The balls are nice and crispy outside, soft and flavorful inside, with a surprising green color on the interior. Cucumber, tomato, and cabbage salad with tzatziki all wrapped in a tasty pita...yum. And a good value with the combo...plenty of food for $12. The optional seasoning on the fries is tasty but in my opinion could use more salt. Easy to fix. The dip for the fries is tasty too. The turmeric lime soda tasted mostly of turmeric to me, but that was interesting too. Worth the try if you crave falafel! Good service as well.

Greasy, Nasty, Crap. 

I got the crispy chicken Bahn Mi and it was an insult to Viet. Regular roll, coleslaw with a ton of mayo, pickles, jalapeño, and that crispy chicken. The chicken was Ok but the sandwich was inedible despite being large. 

Colleagues got wings and fried Oreos. The wings were about 2.5 stars but overshadowed by the Oreos, fries, coleslaw and onion rings that were disgusting. Even with the Seamless $10 discount, this place was extremely disappointing. 

I grabbed my phone ASAP and my stomach is already hurting. Avoid at all costs. 

*puke*

Village Turkey: had crispy bits of skin clinging to them. The turkey flavor was brightened by the smokiness and fat from the bacon. I loved the added twist of the cherry spread; it established the savory, salty, sweet trifecta. The arugula provides the bitter element if you like that sort of thing, or you could sub in spinach.

 Philly Wasabi:  I absolutely love wasabi and how it adds not only spice but flavor; the nose tingling, allergy clearing creamy wasabi spread was amazing over the steak. The American cheese blended in completely and added to the creamy, salty bliss. And those crisped fried onions on top are just an added present.

Now on Mondays, you can get one of Jake's Whole Roasted Pork Sandwiches for $5 dollars. I don't even have to tell you that this is the same price as a sandwich from Subway. While the meat wasn't the thick, hand carved slices of pork that I expected, the chunks of pulled pork mixed with the crisp skin cracklings and spicy chili relish served me well. They pack a ton of juicy meat into that sandwich.

This is the healthiest tastiest bowl I've had! If you like sushi you must try this spot. My daughter brought me there and I had the Spicy salmon; it's a must try! And trust me you'll be stuffed I was so hungry when I got there and I only ate half. I took my leftover half so that my husband could try some, but of course I ended up eating half of that too. So good so good so good!

After taking the drive from NYC after seeing this place on a food show, it's well worth the trip.

The Garlic Bomb delivered! Though not overwhelming with Garlic, this sandwich was delicious. 

The place is clean, the service was awesome, even the bathroom was clean. 

If you're driving parking on the street is the way to go. One hour ran me $3.00 in a street meter, pay parking lots were $7.00 and up.

I'll definitely be back.

They have great ideas for their sandwiches.  For example, they made Turducken sandwiches during the Thanksgiving time. My all time favorite is the steak and egg sandwich. 

They have specials all the time. Monday is $5 sandwiches, Tuesday is a bbq meat plate.  

They have ice cream cone with candied bacon bits for $1.

They are featured in Food Network's Outrageous Food.

They are awesome.


The End.

Reached out and said they contacted me and never did. I reached back out to them... said they need the exact day and and time of my purchase... lmao months later you want me to recall a the exact day of crap experience. Then they say they need my card number and or name I provide.. no response terrible customer service. 

Still no resolve. Place won't last.
