  The burgers are the same fantastic quality Five Guys is known for.  They have a plethora of toppings available, and the meat is fresh and quality, and the rolls are really what bring it together.  Too many burger places skimp on the rolls, going all out on everything else and putting it on a cheap supermarket roll.  Five Guys goes a step up, it doesn't overwhelm the burger, but doesn't disintegrate after 2 bites either.  The topping run the gamut of everything you might expect to put on a sandwich.  Ordering "everything" gives you all of the expected toppings for a burger, along with mushrooms.

  The fries were a bit undercooked, but still very good.  They aren't shy about the portion either.  One regular fries is enough for at least two people.  I suspect the large would be enough for a family of five. They also cook them in peanut oil, and have warnings posted in case of allergy.  However, the warnings weren't as obvious as at the Chestnut street location, or others I've been to.  They also have complimentary peanuts available while you wait.  They also have Gold Peak iced tea, and a better soda fountain than most fast food, including Cherry Coke, which is always a positive for me.
Do not go to this place! They serve you badly the staff is not friendly the manager is rude the food is super expensive, this place has already closed several times due to unhealthiness ..
stupid is being polite they do not even speak English so how can they get the order correct a half hour for 2 hamburgers to be made right stay away

I never ordered from them before but I tried them out. They have some amazing Salads and their crab salad is off the charts. But they do have a problem with ordering turkey burgers and gyros. In the written menu is states the gyros come with a salad or rice. The person that I spoke with on the phone insisted the gyros only come with french fries. So, he sent me a full new salad and added the cost to my bill and the french fries. Their fries are not that good and I preferred not to have the french fries. Their Italian dishes are good too. Oh, I forgot the Margherita pizza it's like I was in Italy, Naples: wonderful. All I can say about the margarita pizza is bravo.

Horrible experience, unprofessional staff, rude drive thru service and the girl was on her phone the entire time as I payed. I literally can not believe the horrible service I received here! They got my order wrong and don't bother to apologize. I will never return to this ghetto dump!

These guys get it. There are a ton of places where you can get a $14 salad or stir fry. The food quality here is good and consistent. I put their salad up against Sweet Green or Just Salad any day. The difference is the service . The women and men behind the counter hustle and get it done right and fast. And if there is a mistake they are quick to fix it and make it right.

I don't usually eat at places inside grocery stores but my friends could not stop gushing about this place and their tehina milkshakes. They know i'm obsessed with milkshakes and couldn't wait for me to try it. All I can say is that my fear of ever becoming lactose intolerant was eased a lil by the creamy dreamy taste of their chocolate tehina shake. I wouldn't have believed it was dairy free had they not said something. The milkshake alone deserves 5 stars but then we had the falafel and shawarma spiced fries w/tehina ketchup and it just solidified this spots platinum status in my books. Every time I go back to Philly, I will most definitely be hitting this spot up.

The manager is not wearing a mask. 
Three people have already asked for their money back on drive thru, but since but since she and the other employer in the back room, nobody is able to get their refund,
 I was inside the store calling for someone to take my order for over two minutes, before the manager without a mask came out of the back room with the only other employee.....

I don't know who gave them two stars but they must have been high drunk or stupid this is one of the very best Popeyes in the city of Philadelphia I must say and I am a harsh critic I'm not easily won over but I have to give credit when credit is due these people really take time to cook their chicken through at hot the skin is clear it's fresh the mashed potatoes are always piping hot the coleslaw is not greasy or mayonnaise too much it's just right who's ever in charge of this restaurant needs an accommodation these people really put their heart and soul in the cooking this food and it's very delicious and it's very savory I never had a bad combination or piece of chicken from this location that's why I drive out of my way to come here excellent place to order original down south fried Louisiana chicken thank you Popeyes keep up the good work

I can't say I wanted to write this review, but at this point it's so ridiculous it would be a crime not to. I love Chipotle, and just about everywhere I've been in the world where there is one, I eat at it, so I'd like to think I have a very large sample size from which to draw from. I'll just cut to the chase here. This Chipotle location is THE WORST at wrapping burritos I have ever been to. By far. Nothing comes close. It's honestly unacceptable and sad for a restaurant whose crown jewel is their burrito to fail so spectacularly at this relatively simple task. The first couple times I went I gave them the benefit of the doubt and assumed it was a fluke. As I go to school nearby, this is the only location within walking distance, so I've come here easily over 30 times in the last couple months, and I am not exaggerating this... literally every single time I have EVER ordered a burrito, it falls apart the second I open them. The staff here seem like nice people, but they do not care whatsoever about taking the time to make a good wrap, either that or they don't know how. I have a normal order with no extra ingredients, and it's just unacceptable at this point. No other location I have ever visited has trouble with this. It's ridiculous how little effort the staff here puts in when attempting to wrap a burrito. Boohoo, woe is me you might say, just eat it with a fork. But if I go to a burrito place to get a burrito, I think it's pretty reasonable to expect even a half-assed attempt at getting an actual burrito, not a glorified tortilla bowl. It's ridiculous and without fail they disappoint me with their burritos every time. Moral of the story is, if you come to this location, avoid the burritos at all costs. Maybe I will update my star rating if they address this issue in the future, but until then, it's absolutely deserved. Everyone I know who has come here agrees with me on this issue. Chipotle, please bring out your head chefs to teach these guys how to wrap a damn burrito! 

Signed, 
An upset burrito enthusiast

We ordered poke bowls for delivery from Red Poke last night for the first time. The ordering platform we used (Uber Eats) required a selection of two proteins. I would have preferred to stick with just one but went with the big eye tuna and yellowtail. 

The bowl was large and the ingredients were fresh, but every so often something in the bowl had a mild chemically taste. I couldn't tell if it was the cucumbers or the onion crisps but I narrowed it down to those two things, which I'd probably avoid in the future. The cucumbers were sliced a little too thick for my liking, anyway. I'd just try other toppings next time. 

This wasn't my favorite poke spot but I'd be open to trying again in the future.

Stopped in to pick up a healthy meal. So I had the salmon tuna on a top zucchini noodle base. Also had edamame beans and seaweed topped with a pinch of mango pieces  some yuzu ponzu dressing drizzled on top. Fresh n sassy.

It was so flavorful and delicious and I felt so healthy. I really gave me a boost of energy for the rest of the day.

Instagramable foods. So it's a cute little restaurant café. You can send a little table right inside the window. So that's kind of cute. Not too many tables but hopefully you'll visit when there's not a big crowd.

I'd love it if they had A variety of freshly brewed iced tea available. 

Food was good and fresh. 
------

Want lazy, ignorant, uneducated women with disgusting fingernails and hair taking your orders and bagging your food? Look no further!! The workers at this location have all gone downhill along with the place itself. I made my order and waited at the counter for it. SEVERAL of their horrible female employees with nasty "I'm too busy for you to care as I work my $5/hr job" attitude walked by me MULTIPLE times. My food was placed where they put all food that is ready - literally 5 feet in front of me but behind the counter so they HAVE to hand it to you - yet no one handed it to me. About 3-5 of them passed my food and myself several times and ignored it. Finally I made a fuss after waiting for about 10 MINUTES!!!! It was at that point the African American day shift manager (long fake black hair) admitted it was ready the entire time just sitting there. Really??? This is how y'all MANAGERS act? Fire fire and then fire some more and hire people who actually care about both the food and the customer.

We ordered from somewhere else using one of those food ordering apps and the driver had a canceled order for Five Guys and they gave it to us. It was fries and a double patty everything burger and it was pretty good although I'm not a fan of everything on a burger. So, we decided to order specifically from here to give them an honest shot. I got two bacon cheeseburgers and large fries via Door Dash. The food was amazing. Bun is large and soft, burger was cooked perfectly with a good bite to it, bacon was crispy and had a great smokey flavor to it. Five Guys doesn't charge for extra toppings (which I assume is why the previous order had everything on it) so I got extra bacon for free, extra cheese for free, as well as ketchup, mustard, lettuce, pickles, and onions (fried onions is free but I eat them raw). But the fries is where they shine. Fresh cut, perfect golden brown, and plenty of salt. The quantity of fries was massive. I suspect they filled a cup with fries and then dumped about 150% more fries into the bag afterword (I almost got filled up on the fries alone). Now, the order was a bit pricey but between the quality and quantity, I think it's more than worth paying a little extra.
Really bad taste original chicken.  It arrived on time I'll give credits for it. But the chicken was overcooked -- Even the thigh was not juicy at all.
What a nice build your own poke bowl - a generous serving of 2 proteins, along with some nice yummy toppings on the warm brown rice... so good and filling, totally satisfied, and all for 10.75.

Fresh ingredients and friendly service! I would have liked a little less rice and a little more ingredients for the price but overall it was delicious and a tummyful The rainbow burrito was off the hook. See what I did there? :)

Their online ordering service is horrible. Every time I order online they mess up my order and forget a one or two toppings. They also give like half of the amount of food when ordered online. Definitely go in store

You could call this a deconstructed sushi roll. Delicious raw fish, fresh vegetables, and delicious sauce resting on a bed of rice.  The bowl as a whole is very light but very filling! The staff was extremely nice, allowing me to taste the sauce and being considers of food allergies. I will be back!
Ordered a bowl of steak with rice for takeout today and the rice was uncooked! There wasnt even that many customers in your store to rationalize the slacking off.
Double fried wings are out of this world! Not a whole lot of seating so when its busy you'll be hard pressed to find a seat. Good selection of different foods and fountain drinks.

Staff were super nice. But, food quality seems to have gone down a lot. Hummus is just ok. Falafel's seem to have both shrunk in size and lost flavor. Isn't the same as it was. 

(Also, the shop adds an additional 10% supplemental charge before tips.  If prices are too low, raise prices... supplemental charge just feels sneaky.)

I have a new favorite poke spot! I was mourning the loss of my local poke spot due to Covid when UberEATS ran a $0 delivery special for Red Poke. I gave it a shot and I am so glad I did! This easily beats out both of the other places I've gotten poke in Philly. Portions are huge and generous. I ate two thirds of mine for dinner and was stuffed, and just returned to finish it off as a late night snack. Ingredients are fresh and tasty! No brownish avocado here, nor did they skimp on it... well worth the extra $1. The fish was diced into perfect cubes and couldn't have been fresher. Options to customize were limitless. I made my own bowl because I like a combo of salmon and tuna and specific toppings. I'm sure the house bowls are tasty too if you're less picky. Price was extremely reasonable. Delivery through UberEATS was seamless and right on time. I'll definitely order again and try it out in person when that's an option.

I ordered food from here today and the food was completely wrong. The cheese steak I order was made wrong all together. I took a hr to get to me when they are 5 minutes away from my house. I called back to have them fix it and still have not gotten back to me or delivered the food. I would not complain if I was not allergic to onions but I am.

Worst pizza I have ever had in my life.  I ordered a supreme pizza which is supposed to come with mushrooms, italian sausage, green peppers, onions and pepperoni.  It would be a shock if you could recognize any ingredient on the pizza as they were minuscule in nature.   not sure what it is about Philadelphia and not knowing what REAL italian sausage is supposed to look like but they are obsessed with this crumbled sausage.  Being from Chicago I wish someone would show them what it's supposed to look like on the pizza,.  But anyway to add further insult they had the audacity to deliver me a cold pizza.  I paid $28 through Ubereats fit a disgusting pizza.  i will never order from here again.

Good chicken when they don't overcook it.. past several orders have been overcooked and dried out. When called to ask about the order, was told they only would do something about it if I would drive the order back.
I've lived in NE Philadelphia for the last 6 years and Bellissima continues to impress. The absolute best restaurant to order take out hands down!! Their App is awesome as well.

I used to order from here and the food was awesome. Now, I'll never order from here unless they get rid of the nasty girl taking the orders over the phone. The menu reads, "Dinners/Meat Platters, served with side salad and garlic bread, choice of side: pasta, french fries, steamed broccoli,  baked potatoe.  The first entry under this heading is NEW GRILLED VEGGIEMANIA. It was delicious the first 2 times i ordered it, over pasta, once over past with grilled chicken.  The last time i ordered it, Ms. Nasty employee told me it doesn't come with a side and proceeded to argue with me when i asked her to look at their menu. I said fine I'll still order it. When it arrived at my house it didn't even come with a side salad or garlic bread. When I called to ask about it, Ms. Nasty proceeded to yell at me that my order doesn't come with anything.  NEVER ORDERING FROM HERE AGAIN.

First time, walked up to a locked door and was told they only have beef w/wo cheese, no menu, no niceties, nothing outside to eat on.
Drove to a park four blocks south and found a bench,
Worst Sarcones roll ever, meat was mushy, dry, asked to be very, very wet, and that was not honored. Gravy was flavorless. No pepper flakes,
Ate 2 bites and tossed. Went to Nicks for a perfectly wonderful sandwich.

Staff didnt allow us to enter and manager refused to let us order on the spot because "they had 37 online orders to do first" and couldn't spend 10 seconds making a small burrito.. Beware, order online and expect long waits.
I'm going to stop ordering from this location.  Literally every time I have - including for delivery - the order has been incorrect.  Every single time.

I order from Bellissima quite often because their food is always amazing. Not once have I had a bad experience. 

My order was placed directly on Yelp tonight. A small cheese pizza and fries was about $16. That's including a delivery fee and 15% tip for the driver. Estimated wait time was 35-45 mins. 

The wait time was accurate -- it took approximately 45 mins for my food to arrive. When the driver got to the door, he called to confirm that he was at the correct address. I actually appreciate it when drivers take the time to do that. It gives it a more sense of urgency in my opinion. 

My cheese pizza, ugh... I was left speechless after the first bite. I wanted to eat the entire pie, it was THAT good! The cheese was the perfect consistency and didn't slide off the bread. The slices were cut nicely, they came apart very easily with little effort. My fries were a little cold, but I still enjoyed them. 

You can't go wrong with Bellissima; everything on their menu is scrumptious!!

Been ordering from this place for years and just about everything is good. Service is friendly, if there is a mistake they work to fix it asap or give you a credit and delivery is always quick. My one issue is the turkey that comes on the hoagies. It's dry and has a bland, old fashion kinda flavor. It doesn't taste very good. Hoping they awit h that soon. None the less I will continue  ordering from this place and continue hoping that one day the turkey is different.

Please be mindful of hand washing and cleanliness. People get sick if food gets contaminated. Avoid touching different surfaces and then touching the pretzels, with or without gloves. We prefer to see employees more aware of infection control practices. Otherwise, best pretzels ever. Thank you.
the pizzas are very good!  They are juicy fresh, there is good service, the bad thing is the prices that are a little high
Fantastic sandwich all around. Owners are wonderful. Customer service was superb. I would recommend this to anyone.

Bit of a double whammy in terms of derivations from my normal reviews since I try not to a) review chains and b) give reviews fewer than 3 stars but I think that this chipotle definitely warrants both. 

I come here somewhat regularly and as a chipotle lover, I've been to most of them in the city and they're all good. However, this one in particular wanes in comparison to the others for one reason and one reason alone - inconsistency. It's really just super off. 

I feel like I'm playing a bit of a Russian roulette whenever I go to this chipotle because the experience seems to vary vastly depending on the time of day or day of the week with no real predictable pattern. The service is fine (sometimes good, sometimes not but nothing to complain about) and the quality is also fine (nothing to write home about, good or bad) BUT the portion size just absolutely throws me off. 

I swear sometimes I get double chicken and it's like two little half scoops of meat and other times it's a size able portion even though I only get 1X meat. It really depends on the person who's serving you and though it's a somewhat small detail it is so egregious I had to make a comment on it. 

On the most recent visit, I was very hungry and ordered double chicken. The person ordering next to me (who got a different server) ordered a single portion of chicken and actually got visible amount of meat more than me. The business might be able to make improvements if it does some quality control and standardizes their portions otherwise customers are going to leave 50% of the time feeling like they didn't get their money's worth. Until then, however, I will be making much fewer stops to this location if I can help it - there's another one nearby in powelton that seems to be more consistent.

Ordered via GrubHub two make-your-own bowls with tuna and salmon. The food was very good and I'd happily eat it again. If you're not starving, it's enough for two meals and it holds up well as leftovers. Took off one star because delivery was 40 minutes late :/
This place is the best!! Roast beef sandwich is out of this world and the small boutique style atmosphere is perfection.. We will def stop in there again soon!
Worst chipotle I have ever been to. Completely mismanaged. No one in the restaurant cares about their job at all.

I arrived to the drive-through and ordered three black and tenders, he told me they only had five pieces when I open my meal it was regular chicken tenders I drove back around to the window and he told me they didn't have black and tenders I asked him why he didn't tell me that When I placed my order and his only response was sorry we don't have that and offered no solution or to remake my order.
I don't expect much from Philly at this point... no juice, no shakes... par for the course.

Chocolate covered Bacon!: Let that roll around in your mind and I'll get back to it later on in my review. 
I was walking to Holt's Cigars after leaving the Reading Terminal's Beer Garden where I was sitting and crying in my Yeungling about the closing of Harry Ochs, my favorite butcher that had just closed. Sad, sad day. On my way to Holt's I passed a small sandwich spot that caught my eye because they had a big roll of paper towels on each table. Right away my Spidey senses were tingling! If they have a huge roll of towels on every table then they must have great big sloppy sammiches! 
I looked around, grabbed a menu and went on my merry way to Cigar Heaven where a couple of friends, Frank and Dean met me in the smoking lounge. A Cigar and a Espresso later, we decided we were hungry and we went to Jake's for a Sandwich. 
We all ordered the Pulled Pork, mine was The 50/50 which was half Bacon along with Sharp Provolone and a nice sauce, Frank had one with a load of hot peppers and crushed peppers so he was assured he wouldn't taste anything and I don't know what Dean had because it was gone in a couple of minutes. 
My sandwich was fantastic, the Pork was tender and flavorful and the Bacon added a smoky touch to it. The roll was perfect, it held up fine, trapping all the juices in. Frank raved about his sandwich and Dean want's to try the 2 foot sandwich challenge and get his picture on the Wall of Fame! 
Now the Chocolate covered Bacon. One of the staff offered us a sample-Dare we try something so wrong and so weird? Hell yes! And it was great! Salty, crisp, thick cut Bacon dipped in smooth Dark Chocolate....where have you been all my life!

Too many young teens with lack of social skills & customer service. Order is usually wrong i.e. ask for no pickles, always end up with them or no ice, always get ice. It's the lil things but when I pay for a service I expect it to be correct. But when the order is right it's good at least.

Great spot to grab a quick bite for lunch.
I love the customizable menu. The options are ample but not overwhelming.
Fish is fresh and very tasty!
Portions are generous and they'll keep you happy for the entire day!

Excellent food but the worst customer service - EVERYTIME!!!!!
I think its the culture there as people working downstairs at the coffee shop have the same worst attitude towards their customer. I ordered a Falafel Sandwich and Falafel Salad and the lady taking order said she will call my name and to that i said dont you guys have that vibrating fob that shows red color and vibrates once your order is ready ? She bluntly said ohh its for the restaurant other side - other side meaning they share same space with another restaurant DIZENGOFF - I said why is that and to that she didn't had any answer. I also pointed where i was seating as its very crowded every-time - and she said we will call your name. After 30 mins of wait I walk down at pickup area and there it was my hot (cold as ice) falafel sandwich and salad - to which the stupidest people on the earth (people working in there) said to
Me "Ohh we called your name" - yeah right!!!
****WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE****

The Manger at this Subway is extremely rude. I go to this subway all the time. He always has a attitude but has never been flat out rude until today. I asked him if he wanted to ring someone up for a bottle of water before he finished my so she didnt have to wait and he totally flipped out and told me not to tell him how to run his business. The other customer told him that she wished she didnt open the bottle because she would have left due to his rudeness. I would have told him to keep the the sandwich if I wasnt so hungry. Needless to say I will not be returning. I also plan to file a complaint.

I have been here a few times and tried different varieties. It's good food but not the best to my taste buds. The quantity is good enough to eat for 2 meals (atleast for me). I have tried their coconut curry chicken as well as tofu. I also tried chicken curry with brown rice which was just okaish. I have also tried their hot sauce curry with rice which is decent. Overall it is decent food and good quantity.

Went to get some breakfast this morning. Drive thru was wrapped around the building, so I went in. Nobody at the counter, but a bunch of employees standing around in the back just chatting away. I said, "excuse me, can someone take my order?" Was ignored. Said, louder, "hello? Anybody home?" Still no response. Employee walks RIGHT PAST ME and says/does absolutely nothing.

So I walked out. Won't ever be back, either. Why waste time with people who'd rather stand around chatting than working?

Delicious cheesesteak! Made with real mushrooms, not the canned ones. The big Stromboli is humongous. Enough for at least 2 people. They brush it with garlic Parmesan butter. It's delicious. The only downside is the bread to cheese ratio is off. There is not enough cheese for my taste.

Im boycotting checkers drive in restraunts!!! I went there 2 weeks ago for lunch. Ok so I went there today. When I called my bank there were 2 charges for today and 1 for the 9th when I wasn't even there on the 9th!!! I called the bank and explained this to them. They said the charge on the 9th was done around at lunch time. I know for a fact that I was waiting for my ride to come pick me up and take me to the hip orthopedic. And my ride came around 12:15. The food I had was really good. But I WILL NEVER GO THERE AGAIN

There's 2 things to be said

1. The greatest Roast Beef on the planet.

2. I've never had better tasting coffee in my life.

They delivered all the way to Port Richmond and it took less than an hour, so I'm happy about that! We ordered the South Street Bowl, Dragon Bowl, Salmon Love Burrito, and Rainbow Burrito. I will say even though they all were marked as 'spicy', I wouldn't have called any of them particularly spicy. The sauces we were given were all creamy/sweet like. There's a siracha mayo type sauce as well as a hoisin one and plum type sauce. The ingredients definitely all tasted very fresh, and the servings are large. I'm not too sure how big Poke is in Philly, and my only comparison is to one other establishment which is now closed. I would say if you're craving raw fish/sushi then you should just get sushi since the bowls have a lot going on and are covered in sauce - it's hard to taste the fish on its own. I do think all the fish and eel were very fresh tasting though! If I could give 4.5 stars, I would.

This is basically the only poke spot (see what I did there..) I go to now because it consistently lives up to my poke expectations. There are so many choices and the bowls are filling and flavorful. 

For a base, you can pick white or brown rice or even mix it up and be healthy with salad, zucchini noodles, or cauli rice. I love that the protein can be either plain raw fish or already pre-marinated. I like mixing one plain and one marinade so that it's not overly saucy but has some flavor mixed in. There's also cooked proteins, but not sure why anyone wants poke with cooked chicken.. gross. For the toppings, there are a lot to choose from and generally you can ask for some extra of whatever you like best (all the seaweed salad for me please) and the employee will add more. There's a bunch of different sauces that I've tried and some dry toppings as well. I've never had a bowl here and the ingredients seem fresh. 

My only complaints are that I wish they would put the water where it is more accessible to customers so you don't have to ask for a refill.. it's just water after all. The avocado is way too expensive.. 1.50 for 1/4 of an avocado is outrageous (though I've seen that upcharge at similar places). Also some of the employees seem grouchy sometimes. Those minor things I can look past to get some solid poke!

We came here last night before an appointment at Hand & Stone around the corner. We gave ourselves half an hour to eat in the fast-causal environment, which we've done before and it worked out swell. I was so excited to try Goldie since I can never get to the Center City location in time before it closes. I immediately knew what I wanted and ordered the falafel salad and fries. 

It was a disheartening experience, though, because the food took forever. My boyfriend ate his Dizengoff while I picked at it and waited. We became officially late for our appointment, and the food was still not done. When it finally arrived, I asked for it to-go, and the girl apologized profusely. She offered a refund, which I appreciated, but that just meant more waiting and we were already 10 minutes late (which means a 30 minute wait for a small salad and fries!). 

I can't really comment on the food because everything was cold and soggy by the time I (hangrily) ate it at 9 p.m. I'm really bummed about this experience. The previous tenants, Wiz Kid and Cheu, left Whole Foods because it wasn't a good operational fit. Honestly, I'm not sure that Goldie is either. Maybe they are just struggling to handle the demand. Next time, I'll stick to Dizengoff or try the new FedNuts stand here.
Loved the food, came here for lunch 2 days in a row! Highly recommended fresh in house sauces, chicken etc

Best Poke in Philly. Fast, fresh, tasty, and well portioned. Miso soup and Seaweed Salad were yummy. I usually order from Uber EATs but recently picked up in person when no couriers were nearby.

Once again, I took a chance and went here and once again, they screwed up my order. Is there a hiring policy that states only stupid people are allowed to work here?

Also, the guy working the window had neither gloves nor a mask. I should expect no less from this place. I will be reporting them for failure to follow basic COVID-19 precautions.

I like their brown rice and vegetables.  I live in the NE, and drive into center city about once a month to go there.  I'd go more often if they were closer.  Have you considered opening a place in the NE?  You'd probably do well up here.
They don't know how to make their breakfast stuff. I ordered a sausage McGriddle; sausage and the bread. Somehow I got egg and cheese on that. Don't answer the phone. Run by incompetent teens.
Best hot roast beef sandwhich in Philly! If you are local, they deliver to.your house for free! Now, I need to.try the meatballs!
I've been going here since it opened and the food has been consistently fresh and tasty. I recommend the Crazy Burrito.

don't let the old school yellow sign fool you! It looks modern inside. don't forget to use your yelp check-in for 10% off. 

Chicken is fresh and made to order. Variety of sauces.  The owner is extremely friendly and even gives us free samples to try different chicken/sauce combinations.  Can't beat the value of price and taste!

Ordered delivery tonight after walking by this place so many times and never stopping in, and I was pleasantly surprised. I ordered the chicken sandwich with cheese and a side of onion rings as well as the crispy chicken bowl with chix rice and a side of mild creamy sauce. 

Yes, I, one person, ordered all that. I couldn't decide what I wanted. It's been a long week, okay?!

The sandwich was delicious. The chicken was still pretty crispy even for delivery and the pickle, cheese, lettuce, and onion game added some class, texture, and flavor. I had ordered the onion rings because why not and those could have been crispier but they were still good. I dipped a few in the mild creamy sauce.

The bowl was also pretty fantastic once I added that mild and creamy sauce in. I don't know what magic that sauce is made out of but I thought it was a great mix of heat and flavor. I'm not too sure about the partitioned takeout container because it made it difficult to mix it all together, but I got a couple solid bites of chicken, rice, vegetables, and sauce together before I fell into a food coma. I like the crisp on the chicken. The vegetables were more than just broccoli and carrots, which was fine by me. I love me some squash. Overall, not my favorite chicken bowl in the city (could use some more crunchy texture like some lettuce on the bottom maybe?) BUT still a solid contender.

The sandwich was definitely my favorite and I would totally order that again with some of that saaaaauce. I'm interested to try their wings sometime too and maybe some other sauces. Solid chicken spot!
Best roast beef available in philly and that's all I have to say. I promise this is a place you want to check out!
Nobody in the kitchen was wearing masks and those at the counters were not pulling the mask up over their nose.

I apparently interrupted the woman behind the counter in the middle of a FaceTime video call.  She stopped talking, but didn't end the call, so the person on the other end was just hanging out listening to me order my sandwich.  It was weird.

We have been coming to this location about once a week for the last four years. We always get three happy meals; two with a soda and one with an apple juice (box). Tonight after finishing his apple juice box, my 4 year old began coughing uncontrollably while running around and playing in the Playplace. I went to the counter to ask for some water. Because at this location, for some reason,  there is no water available at the self serve soda fountain.  I was told I would have to buy bottled water. I explained that my child was choking and we are paying customers (with other paid beverages) and we just needed some water. I again was told I would have to pay. My 4 year old refused to drink the soda that his older siblings had. And unfortunately, even if I dumped the soda out of the cups that I had paid for, I would not be able to fill it with water myself for my 4 year old.
The most upsetting part was the lack of concern on the part of the "manager," who positioned herself between me and the employee I was talking to. After this brief exchange I politely told her that she lost us as regular customers and we would not be coming back; to which she replied "that's fine."
All I wanted was some tap water for my coughing child.

My husband and I have tried so many poke places in Philly and this is hands down our favorite. The freshness of ingredients and generous portions are standouts--I especially love the edamame and pickled ginger. The sauces are all fantastic as well; I have a hard time picking just one! And the Crazy Burrito is consistently "wow" good. We'll never go to another poke place again!
Good food at an excellence price.  Place is basic inside but very clean.  Considering the quality of the food and the price I would recommend it to everyone.

Fking ladies managers we order by mobile phone and when I pick up my order she said some one already pick up your order she didn't check order numbers and then said it is your fault, I have to make another one free order. So arrogant people.when I get my order is 20mins to wait.

We've been to the PokéSpot a few times and really enjoyed our poké bowls both times! The flavor combinations range from what you'd expect to some more interesting options, too.

My husband and I have really loved the bowls we've gotten - probably our favorites of the ones we have tried elsewhere in the city!

They have a number of signature bowls listed on their in-store menu board, but no explanation as to what is actually in the bowls. 

Also, the heating seems to be working too-well. Both times we've been in (in the middle of the summer and then this past weekend in the cold), it's been noticeably warm inside. Something about an over-warm environment + raw, fresh fish concerns me.

Popped in here for a quick takeaway bite the other weekend and was happy with how quick the order came out.  I'm not very familiar with poke bowls but love sushi, so figured a deconstructed one could be tasty.  And it definitely was!

I opted for the one with shrimp, tuna, crab, mango, crunchies and spicy mayo and was pleasantly surprised at how large the portion was....a HEAPING pile of deliciously sticky white rice, topped with the fresh seafood, tons of "crunchy" bits and cucumber.  The only thing I didn't like was the random addition of whole grape tomatoes - they just didn't fit at all with the dish so I ate around them.  Since I got it to go, they put the spicy mayo on the side for me which was a nice touch, but it's highly recommended you really mix the whole thing up together for the full effect.

Everything tasted great and I felt full, so I'd say it's worth the price,  but at the end of the day I think I'd still much prefer actual sushi to a bowl.

I had one of their rice bowls a while ago that did not leave me wanting to return. However, I had a few recent recommendations for their salads and wings that made me give them another try. I got the 6 piece soy garlic wings with fries. The fries were crispy and tasty. The flavor of the wings was very good, although they were not evenly sauced, so some parts were just dry. I also didn't want to continue eating them when I came upon a feather in one of the wings. I may go back to try the salads.

The soy garlic and honey bbq sauces were good. The mango habanero didn't have much flavor. The actual wings themselves were neither crunchy nor very tender. The fries and onion rings were decent. The meal as a whole was underwhelming and overpriced for what was received.

Great burger. Always fresh and cooked perfectly. Bun slightly thin but not huge deal. 

Fries great, I always get Cajun for the extra burn. Coke freestyle machine with free refills cools the tongue. 

Service great, usually done in 5 minutes. Eat the free peanuts whIle you wait! I never had my order wrong. Very friendly and clean. 

The price is high so I usually spread out my visits which makes it more of a special treat.

My favorite poke place in Philly. I'm not in love with the tuna, though I like the chili ponzu salmon. But what makes this place great is the toppings - interesting, tasty, and unlimited toppings on the poke bowl, and they go beyond the standard 8-10. Maybe 20+ options for toppings and something like 6-8 sauces.

I am super lucky in the fact that the Sofitel hotel is nestled next to a couple of different Poké joints but I choose this one because they had more carb-less base options other than just a spring mix. 

You can start your bowl with your typical rice options OR opt for Zucchini noodles OR Cauliflower rice. I went for the Cauliflower rice because I wanted to try something outside the norm. It was so good and exactly the texture I was looking for. 

I also do appreciate that all the toppings are unlimited! With the exception of Avocado. 

Ladies working there were super nice and patient with me as I tried to figure out my perfect combo. Definitely recommend this place and I have a feeling I will be back for a quick lunch before my Philly trip is over

Chicken and mash were NASSSSTY! 
Chicken taste bad and it taste like it was fried while frozen sooooo nasty. No flavor 
And the mash potatoes taste like box HORRIBLE! I wasted $10 for sure. My first and last time going to this Popeyes!! 
Manager also didn't have on a mask!!!!

This is between 3-4 stars. They have a huge menu, some are hits and some not. I love the cheesesteak hot wrapper- like can't get enough of it. I think there's one phone girl that is a lot better and friendlier then the other though. Parking is a pain and ppa is already to ticket even if you are just running in for pick up. The kids think the pizza is ok and my boyfriend likes the wraps.

I love their burgers. They are delicious. Their fries are whatever to me; however, their burgers are so tasty. I always leave full and even if the line is long they get you your food pretty quick. Way better than going to a fast food place and not that much more expensive. I don't recommend going to often though cause you going to get big.

Placed an order online for 2 16 pieces meals and extra sides. While the web page states that the order will be worked and your number called out, they did not begin to make my order until I arrived. To make matters worse I tried calling the store and they did not answer. It went to voice mail and the mail back was full. Not to mention the breasts were dry!

Didn't know philly had its own kind of fast food joints. Not bad either little better than McDonald's. I'm from the south and one thing I love and and miss the most from this place is the coolaid slushy! Man it was the best.
Two words: tehina shakes! Life changing delicious and seemingly nutritious. Sesame milkshakes are where it's at!
Employees respond to the customer with dis respectful smart ass comments. First and last visit.

It's in white bread not toasted. I've never even seen a club sandwich not in toast like wth. So of course it's falling apart even more than usual. This place sucks!!!
I had the falafel with harissa sauce and the shawarma fries. The Israel cabbage with the falafel was extremely well balanced. I highly recommend it.

Ordered my food on Grubhub at 3:40pm, it is now 5:35pm and my order just showed up. After calling twice to see where my food was, I was told that they forgot to put the order in when I first placed it. No apology, no refund, just excuses. 

Never will order from here again, no matter how good the food actually is when I get around to eating it. 

Edit: Ate my luke warm sausage parmesan sandwich...it wasn't worth the wait.

My husband n I order 12 pieces family meal chicken we ask for "Spicy" then we came home open the chicken box. Chicken look so old so dry it look few days or couples days old chicken. It didn't taste spicy at all it taste bland. Use guys need to make fresh chicken  everyday not left over n refried them over to serve customers. Definitely a huge fan of The PokéSpot! I've ordered for delivery and stopped in for takeout for the first time yesterday. I'm fairly certain I ordered the same thing each time; a rice base with one scoop of ahi tuna and one scoop of spicy tuna. I topped with seaweed salad, avocado and cucumber, though it's kind of hard to narrow down because there are so many delicious fresh options! Crispy onions add some texture and wasabi shoyu sauce on the side is perfect for an extra flavor kick. 

There was a line when I visited in-person but it moved quickly and the employees were friendly. The bowls make for a hearty lunch and tide me over until dinner. Nothing but praise from this girl!

Pro:  Great food in a great neighborhood! I stumbled on this restaurant after a visit to the Farmers Market. Having visited Hawaii before, I was curious to see if this Society Hill establishment could capture some "Aloha spirit" in their creations... News Flash: They did! The Volcano Bowl is my favorite menu item thus far. As the jalapenos stood poised to kick-start your taste buds, the cucumber balanced out the spice in cool and refreshing fashion. Meanwhile, the Rainbow Bowl's use of pineapple the contrast the fish and ginger made the bowl light and fulfilling. 

Con:  It's a slightly small dining area, not the best for big groups.

Bottom Line: My new favorite for raw fish in Philly! I want more!
Damn, they cheap on the food. The prices was way high compare to the other pizza places on the street.

I can't praise this place ENOUGH. The poke bowl portion is perfect and filling, and the ingredients are always fresh. This is my go to for quick and healthy delivery or to go when I'm in the neighborhood.
This location is a joke. Rude staff. Wrong orders. The most stereotypically bad McDonalds you could imagine.

Ive always been really picky with my food. 
Most of the time unimpressed.
BAM!! BUT THIS TIME, IT REALLY HIT ME! 
CAFE CANELA, on the corner of 7th and Jackson.
Mouth watering, jaw dropping, eye popping, neck cracking food/ service/ atmosphere. 
I've eaten at several (if not most) Mexican Restaurants and this one is hands down the best!
Blows the competition out of the water.
I really liked the friendliness too.
I had one of their burritos with fresh vegetables and home made flour tortilla.
Steaming steak seasoned to perfection!
With the number one salsa in my book.
The burrito was more than enough to feed a family of three! And the price WAS RIGHT.
I received a free cup of cinnamon coffee as well which was the icing on the cake.. 
Ill definitely be recommending this place to anyone!

Always coming into Whole Foods like whoa with all the options. I usually go for the hot bar because of the good value, but I was intrigued seeing a Goldie and Dizengoff. Went ahead and decided I wanted a falafel and was not disappointed. Service was great and friendly. The employee suggested a medium spice tehina sauce and I ordered the hessinah (sp) and it perfectly complemented with the pita bread and falafel. The meal itself was perfect for lunch. I am very excited I tried this and would love to try their tehina shakes next time around!

I love poke and have been faithful to another wonderful poke place for a long time. However they are closed on Sundays, hence the discovery of The Poke Spot. 

But I am SO glad I did discover it.  They have a wonderful assortment of "signature bowls" but also the offering of "create your own". My favorite thing is that you can add multiple proteins to the CYO.

Still..the garlic ahi bowl is my favorite with its wide variety of ingredients, textures, and delicious marinated tuna. 

I always get a seaweed salad on the side which is also delicious. 

All in all, go here.

Pro tip: They only accept pick-up orders through Grubhub and Caviar.

I decided to try this place for the first time today and I was mildly disappointed. I will say the wings are good, but with the service I received I would much rather go to Crunchik'n right down the street.

I got the soy garlic wings, which are sprinkled with sesame seeds. The were crunchy but oddly were getting soggy as I ate them. The wings it self were juicy, but for the flavor, not my favorite rendition of soy garlic.

With my wings, I also got a side. For my side, I had gotten brown rice, which I couldn't even eat because part of it was undercooked. 

As for the service mentioned, I had to call three times overall to order. First time, no response. Second time, they hung up. Third time, I was able to order but I was rushed and couldn't even asked for them to repeat my order before the hung up. When I got there, I also didn't get one smile, hello, or thank you. I only tipped for the kitchen staff.

I go to this location often with my friend for lunch. I love it bc this location isn't as busy as the other locations are. Which means the lovely ladies can take their time with making my burrito to perfection

Great breakfast sandwiches and good customer service. Those are the two things I look for when visiting a restaurant. A place can have good food, but if the service sucks. I'm not coming back!  I have seen a lot of businesses come and go. Many are good at first but they lose their customers and ultimately their business because they do not stay consistent. They do catering too!

It's unfortunate, but I have to give Bellissma Pizza an updated two star review due to my experience with them tonight. I placed an order through Yelp for a buffalo chicken wrap, a veggie quesadilla and an order of French fries. The delivery man was pleasant and handed us our order in person instead of dropping it off at the doorstep. 

Opened up my bag and I did NOT get a veggie quesadilla, I got a veggie wrap. I called Bellissima and a woman answered the phone. I explain what happened and she asks me (in a super condescending manner) for a receipt with a ticket number from the bag. There was no receipt on my bag. There was a menu stapled to the bag and she kept going back and forth about how that's how they know which orders were placed. She said, "Did you order through DoorDash?" And I said, "No, I ordered through Yelp." She asked for my phone number because I don't think she understood GrubHub works in conjunction with Yelp. 

She put me on a brief hold after she found my order in the system and said, "Would you like me to give you credit because we're really busy right now and I can't have someone come out to deliver your item." I asked how I would know if I was credited and she said they look it up by caller ID and the next time I call they'll have my credit on file. Yeah... I highly doubt that's going to happen. I can say goodbye to $10 that I spent on food that I didn't want. She wasn't even apologetic and seemed like she was rushing to get off the phone with me. I hate writing negative reviews, but I did not get the service I deserve. I was a customer with Bellissima long before I created a Yelp account and I've never been as disappointed as I am tonight.

Whenever the grandkids want McDonald's this is the one we go to. The restaurant looks a lot better since the renovations, but the service remains the same. The other night I stopped there after work and ordered three different meals. I get home and some items are missing. This wasn't the first time either. A few times before I had paid for items that were not in my order. Because there were so many missing things I went back to retrieve the rest of my order. They were nice about it but it was the inconvenience that bothered me. Plus eating cold food wasn't my idea of a good experience.

That McDonald's is an absolute dump. I went in with my wife, mother & grandpa for a quick bite after a day out. We got the food from the new computer menu. Which isn't a bad idea. Works great. The people on the other hand, not so much. The server that bought our food to the table just threw the food down in front of us. The employees that aren't working (which is 75% of them) were sitting on the tables, screaming and cursing all over the store. F this and F that. Two of them messing around and playing around and one almost fell into my grandfathers food. Not a single table was wiped down. We had to do that ourselves. Basically the place is a total dump. Employees and atmosphere both. Always has been. I promise I will never go back.

I've been ordering from Drougie's for years and they just completely disappointed me. I've spent over $100 this week alone at their store because of a death in the family. Very disappointing since I've spent a lot of $ in there. Also their excuse was they have a new girl on the phone.
I've been here twice. Every Checkers restaurant is different from the others. The service is ok. I like how the restaurant is close to other grocery stores in the area.
The drive through 17 minutes! Absolutely ridiculous!! That's a gallon of gas wasted. The inside is closed and no bathroom access. The worst.

quite a unique philly tasty treat.  This place was recommended to me by a local.  he said it was the only pizza he would eat.

I didn't find the pizza special, but the atmosphere was philly cool.  Small, lively, always moving, pizza & a drink for $4 if you pay by credit card...cheaper if by cash.

delightful

December 27, 2014  I frequent five guys periodically and have always enjoyed the fries. Today, I purchased 3 burgers and 3 fries for almost $35.00. It was pure garbage! The fries were wilted, soaked in grease so much so the bag was dripping with grease. The oil had to be old and the fries were absolutely not edible. The burger was bland and even though I put salt and ketchup after 2 bites, I tossed it along with the wilted grease soaked potatoes into the garbage. The lettuce was yellow and left a rancid taste in my mouth. If not for a 30 minute drive (to and from Clifton Heights on Baltimore Pike) I would have returned the garbage. If 5 guys continues to serve this kind of garbage it will be closed by spring. I tossed $35 of my hard earned money into the garbage can. I will never go to another five guys. Ever!

Goldie offers Mediterranean food at reasonable prices.  They are located in the downtown Philadelphia Whole Foods Market.  I get the falafel sandwich and a sour cherry iced tea.  All for about $10.  It's a must stop if your hungry while shopping at WF!
News story that investigation into a criminal organization operating out of this restaurant netted drugs and guns and 5 arrests.

Bad management no one is in charge everyone run around with chickens without heads and I'm messing with everyone's orders it shouldn't be a terrible expensive mistake so I need to do something better management
My delivery order arrived in 11 minutes and that is some magical wizardry. Delicious food too!

Very fast and healthy option, and although it seems pricey, you do get a lot of food. 

As someone who doesnt like spicy food, my only issue was the selection of sauces. There were 6 to choose from, and 5 of them were spicy/firey which left me with hoisin sauce, which wasnt too good. I wish they had more mild flavors to choose from.

I wasn't too impressed, but if my friends wanted to come again I would probably come along.

I'm surprised by all the negative reviews. I've been to this location multiple times and despite the fact that it's always packed, the staff is always plentiful and they keep the line moving quickly (and generally with a smile too).

Charging 2.05 for guacamole is lame but certainly not this locations decision. 

Also, whenever they break a burrito (I'm bad at limiting my ingredients) they always offer to rewrap it.

Great restaurant.  I am now addicted to poke and could possibly eat it everyday.  I have this place to thank.  I've been here I think every time I have a gig or when I am working in Philly.  I think I have tried about 10 different thing on their menu.  I will try to remember all of my favorites.  Protein bowl is magnificent.  I recommend the Garic Ahi.  The Spicey salmon is real good if you like spicey food.  I could go on and on but you cant really go wrong because you can customize the ingredients, ask for more or less sauces and even add those fishy flakes.  The tuna here is really good.  If you haven't tried poke drop what your doing and and go get some.  You don't know what your missing.  This place satisfies my poke desires.

I cannot say enough good things about this place. I order from here like twice a week and I'm never disappointed. The roast beef is amazing. $13 for a roast beef sandwich, a drink and chips. I get mine soaked, with banana peppers on the side and a raspberry tea to drink. I constantly crave the roast beef sandwich from here. I've never gotten the chance to go in here but I have to- to tell these people how good their food is! Keep it up!

I have to add their roast beef sandwich is the best one I've ever had in Philly. Forget all the other overhyped places and try this place. You'll be totally hooked.

This is my favorite poke spot in the city.  I find the quality of the ingredients, the selection of toppings, and the price to be highly favorable compared to other poke spots I have encountered in the city.  

My favorite is the spicy salmon.  In the 3 times I have been here I have received a decent quantity of fish where I am satisfied that I am not being jipped.  There are a few dozen additional toppings and ingredients you can add and, with exception of a few items, are all free to add to whatever quantity you desire.  Cups of water are also free and there are individual bathrooms available

I was on the hunt for fried chicken in center city and found my way to Chix and Wings. $19 later, I left with 20 double battered wings - half soy garlic, half sweet BBQ. Crispy, crunchy, savory, sinfully delicious. I feel like - and boyfriend confirmed - these are some of the best fried chicken wings we have every had in our lives. 

There's a lot more to try at Chix and Wings - sandwiches, platters - things I would try, definitely, but I will not be able to return without getting more double fried wings.

The staff was kind and helpful, the spot was low key and laid back - not a ton of space to eat, but very clean and simple.

Honestly, for a quick meal - or a pile of hot wings for the football game - or a fried chicken dinner for a small army - this is the place to go!

PokéSpot offered Philadelphia BoGo, and Philadelphia jumped on the opportunity. We all lined up for a hour to just get some air conditioning, and then most of us waited a little longer. I would say, the wait was worthwhile. At $12 you can sink into two choices of protein with unlimited toppings.
What makes PokéSpot unique is that the actually offer pre-marinated protein, which certainly adds to the flavor. They offer spicy, pozu, and garlic style Salmon/Tuna/Shrimp. I went with Spicy Salmon and Spicy Tuna, but they offer much more than this (including a vegetarian option of organic tofu).
If you're a first timer they'll definitely help you out too. They have the standard mayo based Sriacha sauces and the standard vinegar/oil based ponzu style sauces to finish your dish off with. I definitely recommend adding in some traditional seaweed salad; it may be neon green but it still tastes good!
Pokespot has comfortable seating and a clean bathroom available (please fellow Yelpers, help it stay this way)! No need to buy a cup of coffee to use a restaurant in Center City, enjoy some poke!
I'm definitely going to have to come back to check out the zucchini noodles; the rice was delicious but I'm sure I packed on the calories after consumption.

A friend and I stopped by Whole Foods to grab a snack from Goldie after visiting a nearby museum. We tried the classic hummus, which comes with a seasonal salad and one pita, and the Turkish coffee tehina shake. The hummus was great - smooth and very heavy on tahini (my favorite), and the tehina shake was delicious (the hazelnut halva was a great touch on top). It was a great snack. I'd return if I was near another location in the future.

Crisp Kitchen has a pretty good thing going, but they really messed up when it came down to their new(er) General Crisp's Rice bowl. On top of the grossly overcooked brown rice, you will find crappy fried processed chicken nuggets. That really surprised me, because their stir-fry meats are fresh and sliced--and are made with obviously real meat; not this processed chicken crap! I actually enjoyed the grilled pineapple most, in this rice bowl.
I feel insulted by this dish and I felt offended to have been asked $10 for it.
C'mon Crisp Kitchen, you're better than this; at least, I would think that you would want to be.
Otherwise, still a pretty solid place, even though I'm very tempted to deduct a star.
28" Meat-Lover's...SOOOO good! Forgot to check in yesterday as it was a quick in & out!

Assembly line sandwich making at it's not so finest. follow the line of breads, meats + cheese, condiments, and soup. Pay towards the end and maybe you'll get a cookie if your feeling extra adventurous. Potbelly is a more fanciful version of Subway, but only really in the meat and bread. Grant it the soup is there, but it's some of the worst I've had! If you ask me I'd rather sink my teeth into a $5 foot long.

And now that jingles stuck in your head. Huzzah!

Worst service first off there is a line of cars pulled over waiting for food 
The girl bringing out the food took my recipe and is asking me what my order was  I have been sitting waiting for my food almost a 1/2 hour worst part is the girl bringing out the food is scratching her head and handling food also swinging the bag with our food 
Never again

Quarantining, we ordered 2 Lg Chicken Soups, received a call moments later explaining that they only had Goat Soup. I asked to cancel the order the lady stated I'd have to contact Uber to cancel, I know from experience that Uber will still pay the restaurant and return your delivery fees if cancelled on your end. I didn't want to go through the hassle so I said we will take a 1 Curry and 1 Brown Stew, to which she replied that will be a small, I agreed assuming that was somewhat reasonable. Imagine my surprise when we received the smallest of smalls pics below. I called back to ask if they thought this was a reasonable substitute for their mistake, she replied what mistake I called you back and told you, the mistake is you shouldn't have soup listed that's unavailable and she should also learn how to cancel orders via Uber. I couldn't go back and forth so I told her they wouldn't get any money bc I will dispute it through Uber and get a full refund. Poor customer service, the right thing to do is send an appropriate size meal or larger to compensate your mistake. We were tryna work with them by taking the platters, but what an insult, we didn't just want soup we needed it as we are quarantining. I shouldn't have ordered from them anyway as the last time prior to this we ordered salt fish and it was bland, stop boiling all the damn salt out of the fish.

It's a pretty dinky sandwich for the price.  I do like how they use an analytical scale to measure the meat.  The angus beef sub was decent - it was just really soggy.   I added banana peppers to it and it was pretty tasty.  They are also generous with the cheese, so I could go back again.  It's just kinda expensive for what it's worth.

This is a ghost kitchen located in a trailer behind Saladworks. They do not list a phone number and there are no directions anywhere so it was pretty hard to find...

They have a lot of interesting menu items that sound amazing on paper but the execution just isn't there. The meat is dry, the queso tastes really funky, the burritos fall apart and you just expect a lot more overall. Even with things like Flamin Hot Cheetos and Doritos added, the dishes still taste so bland... The only main dish I liked was the Flamin Cali Crunch which is their take on a crunchwrap supreme. Honestly their best items are the deserts like the deep fried Oreos and cookie dough, but that's hard to mess up...

The management must really be mistreating its employees for them to be so rude to customers. I just ordered 2 tacos and as I went down the line, every single employee snapped at me. I have never had such an unpleasant experience at a dining establishment. I understand that the line is long and it must be stressful but it can never be justified for 5 employees in a row to snap at a paying customer.

Extremely unprofessional. Very rude. HORRIBLE STAFF with terrible attitudes. If you are an independent contractor (Ubereats, Doordash etc) they will refuse to give you the customer's order. They will require you to confirm your order without actually seeing the order or giving you the order.

I'm not a *huge* raw fish / seafood person but my fiance is so I agreed to try their Phoenix 
( chicken) poke bowl, and am so glad I did! It tasted SO fresh. All of the ingredients complimented one another so well - (chicken,Cucumber,Red Onion,Edamame, mushroom,cilantro, classic shoyu sauce, green onion,sesame seeds on top of rice) Plus it was less than $10 and enough for 2 meals! I did ask for the spicy sauce and think I received the regular sauce, but am not positive on that since this was my first poke experience. My fiance built his own bowl with salmon, tuna, and various veggies and was equally impressed with his meal.
We ordered delivery and it came on time with no issues! Can't wait to try more bowls from here!

Yes! This is how you get me to eat a salad!

Disclaimer: Review coming from an Israeli-food noob. Not familiar with the cuisine enough to really critique, but will share what I'm liking thus far.

If going vegan means I'll just eat this kind of food all day everyday, then I say: hell yes!

I got the falafel salad, shawarma fries, and Turkish coffee Tehina shake.

Salad ($9): Copy & paste from their website, the salad is..."Built on a base of baby kale and napa cabbage, our salad includes six falafel balls, carrot, beet, marinated green cabbage, cucumber, fresh herbs, za'atar sunflower seeds, a lemon date vinaigrette, and tehina." Never thought I'd voluntarily eat beets and dill, but it turns out I will happily do so when it's dressed with tehina sauce and mixed with all sorts of other healthy goodies.

Only critique is the falafels seem a bit small compared to ones I've had in the past and slightly overcooked. You get a slightly bitter exterior, but the inside is full of soft warm deliciousness. Don't think the falafels alone are worth it (which is a menu option - a bag of 6 for $5), but yummy addition to the salad.

Fries ($3): I'm supposed to be on a diet and totally shouldn't have gotten this, but I am so glad I did! The portion is very reasonable and dare I say generous for $3. They could have been crispier, so not sure that I got a fresh batch, but they're warm fluffy fries seasoned with shawarma spice (including turmeric, cinnamon, and fenugreek). They come with a side of tehina ketchup, but my noob side thought it was sauce for the salad so I mixed it in that.....

Tehina shake ($5): As soon as I took a sip, it was an uh-oh moment because I knew there was no turning back. Bow down to the hazelnut halva! Know Ross's face when he sips Rachel's green drink that Joey offered him in Friends? That same face right here every time I took a sip. Chef's kiss~ I should not go for a second but I want it so bad!

Combo of all 3 saves $1. I think there's a 10% additional service charge. Total after tax was $19.01. 

Definitely a pricey lunch to eat everyday but for once -in-a-while meal, it was delightful! Secretly hoping this is considered "mediocre" Israeli food because as a newbie to the cuisine, this was quite heavenly and I can't wait to explore more into what Israeli cuisine has to offer.

First impressions: Nice cozy spot and very homelike. 

FYI - If you see other Hispanics patronizing the spot, you know this spot is legit. 

Food was great as I ordered the al pastor tortas as that is one of my favorite Mexican dishes. Everything was fresh. Avocados were fresh (first thing I judged), pineapples were fresh, and the lettuce and tomatoes were fresh. Now the grilled pork itself was slightly gamey but the fresh juices from the pineapples toned down the gaminess and gave the pork this nice marinaded taste. Very authentic. 

Definitely a spot I would come back to.

Finally poke has come to Center City. This is my favorite spot in town, the ingredients are all fresh and they allow you to taste the offerings in case you are trying something you are not familiar with.  I like that they have staple dishes you can order for your first time. I like the make your own option, you get two free proteins and all the toppings and sauces you want. I haven't had anything that I didn't like. The line moves quickly and the staff is always super bubbly and nice. I highly recommend stopping in for a quick bite, you will not be disappointed, try the spicy tuna and salmon too.

Hot tamales always has a lunch time rush! It's quick convenient but it really nothing out of the ordinary. There are about 20 tables to dine in- very sterile and corporate but the people are always nice and the service is quick!

We tried Jake's sandwich board during last years' midtown fall festival and decided that we wanted to stop in and try other items on the menu.    I like the Gringo, red onions, avocado and pulled pork and my husband favors the 50/50,  the sandwiches are huge and jammed packed with meat, which would be why they are a tad bit pricier then your average sandwich.  However, on a couple occasions the pork has been dry and a little hard to enjoy. The French fries have always been good and I love the cherry soda. 
The décor is really none to speak of, but there is always an open table if you want to sit and enjoy your meal. The service isn't the quickest and the woman at the register isn't the friendliest person but she is efficient so I don't mind some much.
But it will do when you need to grab a quick lunch or dinner.

This is the worst McDonald's I have ever been to in my life. From the start just ordering the person had an attitude. Then I drove up to pay the person had not idea what I ordered, then when I went to pick up they food they gave my food to the person in front of me. Honestly the most incompetent and rude staff ever.

I've always preferred Subway over Quiznos, but I recently had the Chicken Carbonara sandwich.  It had very strange proportions, but plenty of cheese.  
Foursquare reviews labeled it the worst Quizno's around, but I definitely had a worse sandwich from the Quizno's in Center City.
I probably wouldn't return unless I had a coupon.

The line here doesn't go by as quickly as the one at One Liberty, and this place is in the middle of Penn so there are tons of loud college kids, but I have enjoyed nearly everything I've bought here.
I love the ease and healthiness Chipotle provides, so if I'm coming home past 8 when Walnut  Streets parking is free, I would probably come here over Sweet Green next door.
Had the ciabatta steak sandwich and it was excellent! Looking forward to trying what else they have to offer.

I love all Chipotle's, except this one. 

My coworkers and I work a couple blocks from this Chipotle location and we order 3 times a week. (We have a serious addiction) I always order the salad but Chipotle always forgets the salad dressing! So I called the manager, Theo (I think that's what he said his name was) to understand how to order a salad since I am so obviously doing something wrong.  I'd like to share his response to my inquiry.


Theo's way to order a salad from Chipotle's website:
1. Order the salad
2. Order the dressing. (You'd think this is all that needs to be done, but Theo taught me this new secret way to order salad dressing, keep reading)
3. Please include dressing in special instruction notes.
4. Call the store and let them know that you've submitted an order online and that you'd like salad dressing included in the order.
5. Get in line to pick up your salad. Request salad dressing for the 4th time. 
6. Collect your salad. (Don't forget to check the bag, because you will not find your salad dressing in it)
7. Ask for your salad dressing.

Theo, thank you so much for the kind response.  I really appreciated your guidance in this troublesome journey that I had to embark upon.  I now know the correct way to order a salad from Chipotle at University City.

Sincerely,
Kara

So I stopped in to the new Crisp Kitchen location, a couple months after it opened - in order to let them work out the kinks in their system, which appear to have resulted in a number of negative reviews here. It was towards the end of the night and not busy at all, so there shouldn't be any problem with my order, right? That's what I wondered, as I nervously placed my first order.

Ordering is much like any other place with a touchscreen, you make your choices and customize and pay for everything. Even though it's similar to most places, Crisps' ordering system is still a positive experience. 

Of course I'd find a big hiccup with it - I couldn't customize the Spicy Shrimp Noodles dish - as I wanted rice noodles instead of egg white noodles. The lady came around and helped me, but pointed out that 'apparently' everything can be customized except for 'that dish'; but, the sweetheart said it would be no problem for her to make it with my choice of rice noodles. 

I hereby ask management to address this: why can't I customize the Spicy Shrimp Noodles dish? I probably would have walked out, had I not been able to get rice noodles with that dish. Customers are suppose to be able to customize all their dishes, right? 

Anyways, I'm happy to report that I really enjoyed my Spicy Shrimp Noodles dish (with rice noodles). It was perfectly cooked and served. The rice noodles were delicious, the veggies were fresh and plentiful, the sauce was a perfect accompaniment, and the shrimp were done to perfection. Though my second problem, which I find problematic with most of these stir-fry restaurants, is that the meat (protein) is lacking - or even MIA (according to some reviews) - there should be more of it. $10 for a bowl of cheap noodles and veggies, with a little side item of meat, is pretty pricey and doesn't entice me to come back here often. 

I also got a drink, so I could try the beverage fountain. Luckily I could get soda water (I love seltzer without the syrups), the tea was nice, the fountain was a 'New Hope' company so it's supporting local business, and just let me say that the 'red birch beer' was deeeeeeeelish! I've pretty much quit syrupy sodas, but it's hard to imagine not getting at least a cup of this red birch beer during any visit. Soo good!

Also I'll point out that the Crisp Kitchen restaurant is gorgeous to enjoy your meals in. It's a spacious, charming modern place with a very cool golden-glazed concrete floor. This is all brand new construction, created specifically for Crisp Kitchen, and they did a great job of making it an appealing place to visit for a meal. 

Crisp Kitchen (much like Honeygrow or Sweetgreen) is not for you, if you're looking for a meaty meal. But it's a very nice addition to the neighborhood if you want some stir-fry (or salad), and want a cool place to enjoy a meal with friends.

So excited to see the Poke Spot is finally open! Went inside for a quick lunch to go. I've always liked DYI everything, so naturally created my own bowl. To start, you can choose your bases among white and brown rice, mixed spring, and Zucchini noodles (or you can mix some of them together!); then you can choose two or three proteins (three is $1 more expensive), among the goodies of raw tuna, raw salmon, snow crab (extra $1.95), chicken, tofu, Marinated tuna or salmon, spicy tuna or salmon, or shrimp ceviche; then, top it with unlimited toppings from edamame, black seaweed, green seaweed, mango, fish flakes, and more!! To finish it off, marry it with any of the sauces from sweet to firey (Some of the choices looking very interesting, sesame ginger, anyone?)

Overall, I liked the options they have, though it will really keep me a loyal if they were to have eel too... 

Service was friendly and tentative. The price is in the acceptable range in Center City Phila...

I almost rated a 4 for the $, but I received a good amount of food for the price paid.  The service was fast and the employees were courteous.  They were open during a snowstorm when everything else was closed.  I'm glad I chose this establishment instead.  The fries are to die for, and are fresh cooked, juicy, and the best I've had in a while.  The burger was a great size, and the mushrooms were juicy, and the cheese was melted perfectly on the burger.  Better than ANY faster-food establishment out there.  The only drawback was that there were bulk bags of fries sitting on the other side of the restaurant.  But perhaps they just received a shipment.  I asked for extra mayonnaise, and they gave me it free of charge with a smile.  I am not one to eat out often, but I definitely will choose this place over anything else the next time I venture out for fast food.

Sometimes, all it takes is hearing a word before I abandon all other thoughts and lust after said item. For example, bubble baths, shoes, wine, eyelash extensions and, most recently, hoagies. 

My mom said the word to me on Saturday morning and for the remainder of the weekend, all I could think about was sinking my teeth into turkey, cheese and fresh veggies on a delicious roll. I've been trying to watch what I eat so I came up with a game plan and allowed myself to indulge - but only if I saved half of whatever sandwich awaited for dinner. 

I wanted to try a place that was new-to-me, and with a variety of factors to take into consideration, I eventually landed at Jake's. The menu was filled with mostly hot and very pork-heavy offerings, and there were only two choices for cold sandwiches, but both had turkey. I opted for the schmeer: roasted turkey, sharp provolone, baby spinach, red onion, roasted peppers and garlic spread (i.e. mayo) on a long roll. I say I hate mayo but at this point I think I'm just kidding myself. If a mayo-based sauce is called spread or aioli, I'm all in.

I got that bad boy home and, true to my word, wrapped up half and tossed it in the fridge for later. The next ten or so minutes were spent in heaven, if heaven were a sandwich. It was soclose to my favorite turkey sandwich from Paesano's. More field testing is in order.  

A note to the owners: the menu on the website is impossible to read! I thought it was just on the iPhone but looking at the site from my laptop yields the same straining, unless you click on the pdf. 

Also, for those with extremely large appetites, Jake's has this crazy challenge where if you eat a dump truck's worth of food in less than 45 minutes, you get your food for free (and the indigestion I can only assume comes with) and your picture on the website. If that's your kind of thing.

I came here for lunch and ordered a custom stir fry with beef, brocolli, scallions, mushrooms and peppers. There are 6 total ordering stations (3 on each side of the room) where you can choose and place your order on a screen, similar to Wawa and Honeygro. You are able to pick a premade option, or customize your own. Your stir fry has a choice of protein at different price points and your choice of 3 vegetables. I was slightly disappointed when I paid extra for my 4th vegetable (scallions), and there was none in my stir fry. I got the fried garlic toppings and had light plum hoison. The stir fry was quite oily but overall tasted good. It took about 10 minutes and my customized order cost $10. The portion size is pretty filling and I am able to eat half of it for lunch and the other half for dinner. The interior is very spacious, with more standing room than chairs and tables. This seems like a good alternative for a quick lunch, but would probably try other items on the menu.

FINALLY, IT IS HERE.

As a Colorado native, I was ecstatic to see that Chipotle arrived at Penn.  No more disgusting Qdoba.  Chipotle is the premier fast food burrito, with a freshness and quality (a SPIRIT) that just does not compare to anything else (except maybe Don Memo, but they take too long).

The one complaint I have about this place is that they sometimes are inconsistent.  Sometimes they give you too little rice, and then everything else, which is done in proportion to the rice, is lacking.  They you have this little fist-sized thing when what you really want is a burrito the size of a baby.  On the other hand, sometimes they overfill and the tortilla breaks.  Then you spill beans and rice all over yourself while the entire campus watches you through the Walnut Street window.  

Still, fantastic place.
