Just what I needed. Some oxtails, rice and peas and cabbage. The food was flavorful and came out hot! They accept cash and card and the prices were extremely reasonable. Based on the price and quality of food, I would 100% go back again!

I rarely review anything.  But, THIS place is insanely GOOD!  Never a disappointment. 

Pizza is great, sandwiches are awesome. Rolls are fresh. Fries, in any shape and topping you could dream of. Salads galore. Tuna salad is delish. Breaded Chicken hoagie never disappoints. My husband loves the sweet chile hot wings and the 3 cheese cheeseburger. It's like 5 restaurants in one. If they served sushi, I'd use Drougie's exclusively.  

Every pizza place has a bad day, but not Drougie's. The food comes, it's hot, packaged perfectly, never missing a sauce or item, and tastes delicious!!! 

The menu is ridiculous. So, many choices!  Sometimes it takes me 15 minutes to figure out what I want because there are so many options.  

They also are on Grub Hub. Super easy to use and you can pay with Paypal too. Bonus!  

I only ask them to change one little thing... The coconut shrimp appetizer, it needs a passion fruit dipping sauce. :)

My hat goes off to the staff. You are efficient and the fabulous food you make perfectly shows how much you care. You guys rock! Thank you!

After watching an episode from one of the food network channels, I took the drive from NYC to try the Garlic Bomb sandwich.

My bf ordered the 50/50, and no disappointment here. The only thing I didn't like was that the sandwiches were not hot or warm in temperature considering meat it's in them. Aside from that, great tasting and different sandwiches.

Place is small, and parking outside can be challenging but take your time to find a street spot. 
The parking next to restaurant charges you $7 for one hour, but street parking was $3 for one.

The average sandwich prices were between $9-$10.

Ok, customer service.

The mensch is a pretty huge and pretty great sandwich that is worth the price!

The wasabi ribeye looks like it is probably awesome and I'm going to get that next time.

Quick service, plenty of tables,and  good sandwiches can be found at this establishment.  The roll has a great texture and isn't ridiculously tough to the point of absurdity(like some other Philly sandwich places).  The sandwiches are pretty damn large so prepare to take half home for another time.  

Bonus points for having sriracha available to tack some kick onto the sandwiches.

On the action-movie-parallel-satisfaction scale, this place is Blade Runner.

One of my absolute FAVORITE poké spots in Philadelphia! I had the opportunity to come here with some friends to try some of the different poké bowls. What I love about The Poké Spot is that there are a few signature bowls but you also have the option to build your own bowl. 

The three of us decided to build our own bowls and I was very happy with the decision of creating it myself. The Poké Spot has so many delicious toppings to choose from. In my personal bowl, I put in Ahi Tuna, Spicy Salmon, and Spicy Tuna. Side note: You can pick three proteins for only $13.99! On top of my proteins, I added mango, seaweed salad, corn, and kani salad, with a sriracha aioli sauce on top and onion crips. It was so delicious and extremely filling. I ended up turning it into two meals. The proteins were incredibly fresh which can sometimes be difficult to come across. The staff was also very engaging and helpful with building your personalized bowl. They were able to recommend which toppings pair well together. I will be in here often!

I had just gone on a run and was craving something refreshing and filling. I had never had poké before, so decided this was the perfect time to try PokéSpot. It was great! I had the spicy salmon bowl, and it was the perfect combination of flavors and textures. I loved all the crunchy topping choices, and the salmon was so fresh. Their tables were a little dirty/sticky but besides that, I had a great experience here.

Disappointed.

I was walking all over philly looking for somewhere to eat and this place caught my eye. 
With the positive reviews on yelp I figured I found a profound philly spot.... NOPE. 

So, I went with the midtown... turkey, avocado, roasted veggies and picked onions on a whole wheat sub. Everything was fine except the bread. The bread was old. There was nothing fresh about it. I still devoured my sandwich because I was starving but if your a sandwich place, I need you to have fresh bread. It goes hand in hand, Sandwich=Bread. 

I doubt I would come back, maybe on a random whim but doubtful. I'd rather deal with the crowds at reading terminal.

FYI: Do the build-your-own option to get more bang for your buck!

WHAT I GOT: white rice, salmon, tuna, kani salad, seaweed salad, edamame, masago, roasted seaweed, and spicy mayo

PROS: Finally a build-your-own poke bowl spot in the Rittenhouse area! First thing's first, the interior decoration is super cute! It gave off a really clean and modern looking vibe. The poke bowl itself was also one of the best I've had in Philly so far! The fish tasted pretty fresh (especially the salmon. too good.) and the toppings were all prepared nicely. They also give you a decent sized portion too. I absolutely LOVED the seaweed and kani salad. The kani adds a bit more protein to your meal (with no extra charge) and the seaweed adds a bit more flavor depth and balances out the bowl. They're also super vegetarian friendly and offer a lot of healthy topping choices. I also wanna give a shout out to their spicy mayo for actually being spicy! At most poke spots, the spicy mayo is way too dense and doesn't have that kick I'm looking for. The spicy mayo at PokeSpot was perfect. The spice wasn't too overpowering but it still gave that creaminess of the mayo. Bravo.

CONS: Music was a touch on the loud side. It was a bit hard to hear the people over the glass food barrier but aside from that, nothing bad to say about the food.

HUSBAND'S CORNER: Good food, not a bad price point for poke, especially in the Rittenhouse area. For my proteins I got the garlic ahi, chili ponzu salmon and tuna. To be honest, their non marinated fish is better than their premarinades. Other then that, the food was good. As the wife stated above, music was a little loud and as we went when it just opened, the employees were probably a little tentative so it was hard to hear them when I had questions.

I have a new favorite poke spot and it is convenient called The PokéSpot. 

The place is brand new, cute, bright, and has a few tables set up. Definitely set up more with the intent of a grab and go, but you definitely have the option to sit. 

The staff were super friendly and accommodating. They're happy to suggest bowl ideas or let you make your own. 

There are so many ingredients to choose from that you could probably eat there for a year and not repeat an order. Everything is super fresh and pairs together wonderfully. My boyfriend had the spicy salmon bowl with crab which was to die for, full of creamy spicy goodness, and I created my own bowl with a mix of spicy and ahi tuna, veggies and mango and sweet and spicy sauces. The prices are fair, the portions are generous, and we both left so satisfied. Loved it!

So happy to find a great poke place within walking distance! 

This is one of the better poke I've had. We built our own bowl with Scottish Salmon, white rice, edamame, seaweed salad, masago, mangoes (amazingly sweet), pickled ginger, radish, cucumber, red onions, and spicy mayo. Delicious, fresh and really filling. Also, the owner and her 10 year old daughter were super sweet. 

I'm going to be getting a lot of poke delivered home:)

Overhyped & below average
I was just diagnosed with celiac disease so I cannot eat breads, oats, rye, etc.   My boyfriend had a craving  for Five guys.  I checked their website and it said they had a gluten free alternative to the hamburger bun.  Surprised, we went on our way.  We got there and of course, no gluten free option.  So i had to eat mine out of tin foil.  
I may be part of the minority, but i didnt think this burger and fry joint was anything special.  The cashier was dumb, its extremely overpriced, they lied on their website, and it didnt taste any different from any other place.  
Nothing about this place was special.  Go to Nifty Fiftys instead!

In three words - Nom Nom Nom!

Much like Paesano's, Jake's is a place that takes all preconceived notions of Philly sandwich shops, and tosses them straight out the window! why add on some heat to your steak sandwich with basic hot peppers, when you can go with homemade fire sauce and GHOST PEPPERS? Why limit yourself with regular toppings when there are things like peanut butter, wasabi, sunny side eggs, and homemade roasted garlic spread to utilize. Jake's is a place that really likes to kick things up a notch and it does it well!

If you're looking for a pig out sandwich you can go with one of their many pulled pork sandwiches that utilize whole roasted pig; one of seven varieties of game changing cheesesteaks, specialty sandwiches like the TURBACON, and then some! but they also have plenty of leaner sandwiches and even feature a solid veggie option in the Farmer's Market. 

Toss in some enticing fountain sodas, delicious shakes, and sides that range from your typical fries to mini potato pancakes; and Jake's is a place that gives you more to love. Especially if you're adventurous enough to go for the Five Pound Philly Challenge - http://www.jakessandwichboard.com/Jakes_Sandwich_Board/The_Challenge.html!

This place has the worst customer service! The lady on the phone would not apologize for getting my order wrong and demanded that i send the food they delivered back in order to get my new order. I was given the wrong food an hour late and an attitude when i called about it. When I asked to speak to a manager I was told that one wasn't present and that I would have to make an appointment to talk to him. I will never recommend this place to anyone.

Every time I bite into their sandwich it reminds me of my grandmothers roast beef growing up. No offense to Nick's but this is the best beef in the city. If you are expecting a steakhouse setting with a a bunch of tables this isn't that... this is a small cafe with a huge cut of the best roast beef piled high on a fresh Kaiser roll. The staff here makes you feel at home and I love coming here. I suggest a long hot to accompany this little piece of art ! Extremely addictive.

Its sunday 11/21/21 and ive literally been waiting in the drive thru for 35 minutes, this will be the last time i come to this mcdonald. 
Need better management and more employees.
This is the mcdonald in ne phila of castor ave..

I came to Philly for a conference in pre-COVID times and was really craving poke. All the reviews led me to this place, and all the reviews did not disappoint. 

I asked the staff what the most popular bowl was, and they made it for me super quickly. I got back to my hotel room, and was so happy that I had decided on poke - and poke from Red Poke! It was fresh, flavorful, and filling. 

I had enough to last me for dinner the next night too!

This was my first time ordering from Bellissima Pizza using ezCater for a Drs. office in NE Philly that specifically requested several different types of pizza - Pepperoni, All the Meats, Veggie, BBQ Chicken, Cheese (They DID ask for Eggplant Pizza, but I don't know any place on Earth that makes that...LOL).

ALL of the pizzas were incredibly good and cooked to perfection!  The staff at the office keep coming back for seconds and thirds and raved about how GREAT the pizza was!  

Of course, I sampled several different kinds...The toppings were fresh and the crust awesome.  The perfect pizza for folding and chomping away at!

Move on to something else.  
This place really looked promising when I came in.  Looks like an old-style eatery in the decor.  When I got up to the counter,  i could barely hear the person because there is so much mechanical noise.  There was one woman working the counter and when a guy opened the door from the back looked at the one woman trying to help six customers, he just shut the door ignored us and went back to believing that customers aren't important.

I ordered the chicken salad. When it is done right, it is fantastic.  Too much to hope for at this place. The chicken salad was disappointingly uninspired and almost flavorless.  I added salt and pepper and choked it down.

The place wasn't clean, tables wrecked, the floor dirty, even the trays up at the register were filthy and at 3 in the afternoon, there isn't an excuse other than they just don't give a F.

They make some pretty great sandwiches at Jake's Sandwich Board. It's right in Center City and makes for a great place to pick up lunch. I like walking in and seeing a whole roast pig lying on the board... it looks so delicious.

Here are my favorites:

- Fire steak - a spicy one. The sharp provolone and fried onions go well with the steak, but my favorite part is the fried long-hot chili they throw on top of the sandwich. Paired with the house-made fire sauce, it's excellent.

- Philly Wasabi - I love wasabi, and the crunchy onions really go well with the steak.

I've always wanted to try the Charlie Brown although I've never gotten it... but peanut butter, bacon, and cheddar on your steak? Sounds unique... and maybe it would work?

Ordered a Sicilian pizza with 4 slices missing in the middle. You could see grease spots where they were . I called, girl says we're too busy and only have one driver. She asked cook and he said thats how we make them. After I hung up, I looked closer, the slices were flipped over onto outer slices.  If it was a driver issue, id understand,   but, they lied about it.

I'm no Poke expert but this place is great! To me this is a no frills poke bowl that's filling and inexpensive. They serve bowls and sushi burritos. They have many bowls to choose from or you can build your own. I opted to build my own with two meets. The tuna and salmon were fresh and tasty. It's not the most delicious cut of tuna or salmon but it gets the job done! You then can choose from a vast assortment of toppings. Some are crunchy, saucy, etc. Each adding another layer or flavor, texture and balance to the bowl. I did the classic shoyu sauce. It was super good and basically a soy sauce based sauce. They are more than happy to describe any items to you and to let you try a sauce before you commit. The place itself is cozy but super comfortable. Give it a try!

At what point are they going to be embarrassed that they are essentially charging 25 cents a fry? The fries are delicious. Yet they cheap out on them constantly. It's not a one time thing. It's all the time the fry bag is half empty.

There have been a lot of new Poke bowl places opening up in Philly and I decided to give this one a try. I used the Ritual app to order and pick up and my bowl and it was a very simple process. You can choose from a variety of premade bowls or customize and create your own. There are plenty of options for toppings, sauces, meats, rice, etc. to choose from. I definitely recommend building your own bowl to try out all the toppings! 

The inside is pretty small, there are only about 3 small tables so if you're planning on going with a group just be aware of that. Overall, they serve a pretty solid Pokebowl. Everything tasted very fresh and the size of the bowl was decent and also very filling. Definitely something I will be trying again!

Was so happy to go back to Goldie at Whole Foods.. was I in for a disappointment! Area around Goldie was not clean, plates, cups, food on tables. The humus was ok but a small portion, the dry, undercooked, cold, non crispy, cold falafel was a great disappointment.
The falafel sandwich was dry and also filled with dry and cold falafel. No tahini to be found to make this dish less dry.
This place has gotten really bad over the last few months. The employees are rude and careless. They take forever to make food. And I've gotten sick from eating here, twice in the past couple weeks.

I have been ordering from here for a long time I ordered through Uber eats. Pizza fries chicken nuggets and a cheesesteak. While serving my son his food I noticed a fry looked weird upon further inspection it was a piece of fried shrimp. Which i am highly allergic to. I called to let the shop know that they need to be careful with what they are mixing together and the girl on the phone unbothered by the potential deadly health risk said ooooh sorry.  

Definitely won't be ordering from their again

I was very excited when I saw that Chipotle was coming to University City.  The burritos are yummy, enormous and incredibly filling, and (imo) a good value.  The side of chips and guac is worth adding to your order if you are either incredibly hungry or have someone to share it with.  To me, Chipotle is far and away the best of any of the Mexican fast food chains.

Uhhh yes please! Long wait but worth it. We were looking for some new stuff around the area and found this hidden gem. Best Mexican-infused food I've ever had in Philly. I hope this pop up never goes away! That fried cheesecake was super bomb! Or should I say hella bomb ;)

I know I'll be in the minority here but while Five Guys is better than average, the hype is a bit much.  

This new addition is close to home and thus I've visited on several occasions.  Each time the service has been worse and the wait time lengthened even though the crowds are smaller.  

While obviously the ingredients are good, insisting on cooking all the burgers to well done wrecks the meat.  It's a real shame because it could be the difference of a star on my rating alone.  Little burgers are one patty.  Standard burgers are 2.  

Fries are very good and plentiful.  A small can easily feed 2 and 3-4 can split a large.

Menu is limited but that's actually a good thing.  Five Guys focuses on what they do well and doesn't try to be everything to everyone.  

Overall a definite step up from the typical fast food options in the area but not even close to a In-and-Out or some of the other regional burger spots like Basically Burgers in Doylestown or even Sabrina's Cafe downtown.

Online ordering is a big plus and orders for multiple sandwiches are number coded for easy identification without have to unwrap them which makes a group order really easy.
No use beating around the bush:  Chicco has the best roast beaf sandwich i have ever had.  Get it on a round roll with horseradish and sharp provolone.
Convenient, delicious. Been here many times to eat in or take out. The salmon burrito type item is so delicious. Lately, I've been restricting myself to the vegetarian bowl.

Your standard chipotle restaurant. It isn't the best but if you go during the right time and staff you can get a pretty well made meal. During peak hours it's insanely busy though with some of the more basic of students waiting on a line out the door.

Chick-a-licious is new fast food joint in Center City near Jefferson Hospital.  It is an inexpensive spot that boasts a healthier fried chicken. 
 I don't know how healthy it was but it sure was very tasty! I tried the special which was four Chicken fingers and french fries for 7 dollars. It came with 9 or 10 dipping sauces and I choose the spicy BBQ sauce. The chicken fingers were large long pieces of breast meat with a very thin but crispy layer of breading. The flavor was amazing and the fries were also very tasty.
 I came back for a Caesar salad topped with the same chicken fingers, and as a added bonus they have a lot of salad dressings available including Wasabi. Great cheap eats destination.

Came here on opening day, and honestly didn't get the best impression. Right as we walk in they tell us they may be out of some fish. I appreciate them being upfront, but how do you run out of fish at a poke place. We ended up waiting in line for almost an hour which was crazy. The line was long, which was fine, but they moved soooo slow. I was so uncomfortable in line, the place was hot, and everyone was fanning themselves with menus. It was pretty gross. I blame most of these issues on it being opening day and I have hopes that they will work through these mishaps. 

Food: meh. Not the best poke or even close. Maybe closer to the worst. I got the shrimp and crab. The crab was tasty but I did not enjoy the shrimp at all. A bunch of them still had tails on them and I kept crunching on it. I couldn't even taste the dressing. Not sure if they didn't put enough or it was just bland, but I didn't taste anything. Also this place is super expensive. It came out to $15 for one poke bowl. Rip off!!!!!

I've walked by this place a 100 times or so on my way someplace else, always loved the smell of the pork cooking that you envelops you as you walk by. So finally went today. Good pork!

Had the 50/50 sandwich, pork and bacon. Ok if there was any truth in advertising, it should be named the 80/20.  There was bacon there, but not anywhere near 50%, my 20% number is a very generous estimate. may I suggest a more accurate name, pork with some bacon. Having said that, after I was over my bacon disappointment, I realized the sandwich was really good. The spicy thousand islandish dressing was fantastic and complemented the meat really well. I'll definitely be back, and who knows maybe I'll get the 80/20 again.
Closes earliest Tran 10 on Sunday's when it says 11. So pissed. Acknowledge your time

I have been loving this Chipotle for healthy, fast lunches. Yep, I said healthy. Because if you forgo the wrap, cheese and heavy meats, you really can have your Chipotle and eat it too. Ask for a burrito bowl, and then use a lettuce base with just a little bit of brown rice and black beans, plus onions and peppers. I've noticed that Chipotle workers across the board are super generous with toppings, which is awesome, but also dangerous if you are trying to watch what you're eating. 

I finish off my burrito bowl with pico and both of the tomato-based salsas, plus some guacamole for some rich flavor and healthy fat. Their guac is super fresh and tasty. No dressing needed! 

The employees are always fast and friendly. Once their diet coke dispenser shot out clear liquid which was a bummer, but besides that, this location rocks.
I know it's just McDonalds but this is the second time I've been in there, got a large fry and they gave me like 10 fries. At least fill the container

WOW! I popped into Red Poke Express for a quick protein-heavy pre-concert dinner and could not have been more impressed!

I did a Build Your Bowl with a mix 2 and decided on white rice, yellowtail, shrimp, mango, pineapple, cucumber, edamame, tomatoes, avocado, pickled ginger, seaweed salad, lemon, and tempura crisps topped with ponzu shoyu sauce. 
I clearly should be designing these bowls behind the scenes - because it was absolutely incredible. 
Everything was very fresh, the portion size was huge, and the price could not be beat for $9.75 ($1 extra for the avocado, because I'm worth it.)
I was absolutely ravenous and I didn't even finish the thing. 

For a quick in and out place to have a decent amount of seating, and a customers-only bathroom available, I can't recommend it enough. I don't get into that corner of town so frequently these days, but look forward to going back again!

I'm writing this message in hopes that this meets management. I stopped by the 19th and Market Street store today for lunch (9/22/2017). I have never been made to feel so uncomfortable by strangers, let alone employees who are supposed to be in the hospitality industry. As soon as I walked in I could see a few woman behind the counter whispering and when I was about to order my food one of the woman said "How many babies are in there?", pointing to my stomach. I am currently 8 months through a tough pregnancy. I answered with "one", and there started the conversation between the three employees about how "big" I am. And they wanted to know "if I'm sure there's only one" because of how "large" I am. Visibly annoyed, I did not engage in their conversation, but they continued to talk about me until I left the store. I'm not sure what store policy's are set in place but I think it it absolutely disrespectful for someone to talk about me they way they were. When I returned to work, I was visible upset and told my colleagues about the situation. They were also appalled by the behavior of your staff. This interaction has not only lost me and my family as a customer but my colleagues as well.

My experience here was horrid. I've had bad experiences before but my burrito barely tasted like a burrito. I spent $13 on something that had no queso twice as much tomato as usual and stale rice that was crunchy when I bit into it. I honestly don't even blame the workers for it because I'm sure Chipotle severely underpays them. So Chipotle sucks. Don't come here or come here and just tip the workers because I'm sure they aren't paid fairly.

In a city filled with so many food bowl options (there are at least five within two blocks away), The Poké Spot is a refreshing change. Who else gives such huge portions of high quality protein (spicy ahi tuna, chili ponzu salmon, shrimp ceviche, snow crab, chicken, tofu, and more) with so many good toppings?

Do not "settle" for a Signature Bowl (prebuilt bowls for the undecided)... just build your own! It's actually a greater value if you build your own because you get not one but two choices of protein for the same price as a Signature Bowl. There are 24 toppings in all and you can get as many as you want, within reason, of course, because the bowl is only so big.

Speaking of big, the bowls here are much larger than the poké bowls at the popular Poi Dog nearby. I filled mine with chili ponzu salmon and shrimp ceviche (the shrimp are jumbo sized and you get six of them!), cucumber, mango, masago (fish eggs), mushrooms, dried seaweed, and bonito flakes over white rice (you can substitute brown rice, zucchini noodles, salad, or cauliflower rice, too).

Did I mention there are 9 different sauces you can top everything with? Wow! The Poké Spot gets a super thumbs up from me.

So my 1-star review was conveniently removed by Yelp HQ because of my lack of "first hand experience" when I in fact came here, ordered, and ate ON MY OWN. So....seems awfully shady.

I had the worst Mexican food of my life, if I can even call it food. When I asked for spicy, rather than putting salsa or jalapenos or something, my burrito was douced in vinegar-y Tabasco. C'mon everyone knows Tabasco isn't spicy its just salty. The burrito wasn't warm and it was small. I thought they were really cheap but she said I had to eat two to get full. Like is this burrito tapas or something? 

I would seriously recommend going anyyywhere else to get Mexican food. Just walk 10min and go to Chipotle on walnut.

Super fast, super yum enough said. The falafel sandwiches made with Dizengoff pitas is a must. Staff is super helpful in case you are unsure of what to choose. This place is a must at any of their locations, hands down best falafel I have ever had.

This review is only for the pierogies. I know, how did I not get a hot dog at a place called Franks? But, the homemade pierogie sign won me over. They are nicely salted and stuff with potato goodness. Get it with the sour cream. Yummy and quick!

Sussshi Burrritoooos , is the excited sound that keeps playing in my head as in some japanese game show , whenever i am about to order at Hai street. 

Don't be fooled by the ho hum production line setup , the ingredients and the idea are really fresh and exciting. Couple that with a staff that genuinely gives a damn about the customer's order, it is pretty hard to go wrong with this place. 

The salmon and tuna was delicious and so were mushrooms, and having the choice to order it in a bowl can help channel one's inner Gojira as you devour through the meal. Equally good for lunch and dinner !

I laughed at first, but was dragged there by my teens who decidedly love the place. And you know what? For less than $10, it is a really great and yummy alternative to a sandwich or burger for lunch. Very fresh and incredibly quick service.

A great spot for when I'm craving falafel at my desk! For less than $9 I get a couscous bowl with falafel and all the fixings plus a piece of pita! It's is a great amount of food, and just like the bag says, the pita is like a cloud... this is a prime location in center city with outdoor seating next door! The main complaint is that lines can get crazy during the lunch rush. Even the online ordering can get backed up, but that doesn't keep me from coming back!
Services was ok but the perogies were homemade and very delicious. It is also 2 for $2, so it is a no brainer to stop here amd have some. I will definitely be returning for more.

Finally tried this place for the first time and had the Gochu-mango spicy tuna bowl. Listen, this isn't authentic Hawaiian poke, but I wouldn't expect that here. If the goal is to offer sushi burritos and poke bowls modified for American tastes and suitable for serving high volume, I think Hai Street meets that goal. There's more rice and mayo than I need and than you'd find in an authentic dish, but really enjoyed my lunch and service was fast. Tuna seems high quality and the toppings are pretty authentic. The essence of poke for me is freshness and contrasting flavors and textures and that was nailed. Spicy, sweet, and tangy and crunchy & soft in one bowl wakes up the palate. Nice alternative to my other work lunch options in this are!

It's in the stadium so OF COURSE the line is long, but thankfully they have a cafeteria style system that makes the wait short. One trick is to grab a cup they just put out to make sure your fries are as fresh as they can be. Both beats crab fries during a Phillies game...takes a bit of the sting off of a loss that's for sure.

Got the flank steak wrap and it tasted really good but unfortunately the portion size is more like a snack than a meal.
I had to get a sandwich somewhere else afterwards.
So basically their $10 wrap is more like an appetizer.

Wandered by and stuck my head in because it looked interesting. The young lady working there asked me if I wanted to come in and see what they had. I really loved their huge selection of craft beer. Had a stout from the cooler, a piece or chicken and a pot pie. All was really good. The staff is especially friendly and helpful.

This place should have more than 3 stars. Why? Because it is tasty, healthy, no frills lunch food made with quality meat (Boar's Head) and white meat tuna at a reasonable price. I've had the tuna wrap a bunch of times and can't wait to try the brisket and South Philly pork sandwiches. 

It is clean, friendly, quick (no long lines) and well-priced for the area. If you're looking for an experience (Naf Naf, Sweetgreen, etc.,) this is not it. But if you're looking for a good sandwich or wrap for under $8, you will be glad you came. Cards accepted with at least $5 purchase is a plus. So glad I never have to set foot into Devon & Blakely again with its pre-made sandwiches and low-quality food.

Interesting concept. It's actually quite delicious. I'm a huge fan of sushi, so I thought I would give this place a try on a friend's suggestion. I like that they have a "create your own" in which you pick the protein, up to 4 toppings, sauce, and crunchy topping for the price of the protein. I had the katsu chicken wrap with spicy mayo, carrots, cucumber, pickled onions, and tempura flakes. It was delicious, and very filling. I didn't expect the katsu chicken to be cold, but it still was very tasty and had a crunch to it. I also tried their wasabi guacamole with chips. The guacamole was very good...just a hint of wasabi to give it that unique taste. The chips were amazing!!! Thick but light, salted to perfection, and not overly oily.  My only complaint is that for a "sushi burrito place" they didn't have a spicy tuna option....maybe my sushi tastes are way to Americanized, but whenever I have sushi that's a roll I always get. Overall, this is a great place, and I will definitely come back. The food is fresh and you feel good eating it. The staff are friendly.

Just a heads up that It's more of a take out place since the place is kinda small...there are maybe 6 bar stools along the wall and you could probably eat here if it was 2-3 people, but it's not meant for groups.

Inconsistent - Ordered the taco salad which seems to be featured this month and when I arrived home the salsa was missing from the order. Additionally, there was no cheese on the salad. So basically, the taco salad consisted of lettuce, tomatoes and a cup of chili. Very disappointing.
This isn't the first time that items were left out of an order at this Wendy's location.

I visited Wishbone at 12:30 on a Monday and there were only two other customers, which is slow considering the location. I ordered a pound of wings ($8.95/LB) and a biscuit ($2.25). The wings are not seasoned well and not that tasty, therefore, I urge you to purchase one of the variety of dipping sauces they offer for an additional 50 cent. I was disappointed, at least one dipping sauce should have been included with my order. I hate when companies squeeze money out of customers by charging for condiments. I understand paying for additional condiments, but at least include some condiments with a customer's order. What's next, paying extra for napkins? But I digress. Butter is also not included with the biscuit. Specialty butter can be purchased for an additional cost. LOL. Again, what's next, charging for napkins? I ordered the Honey Butter which was pretty good considering that I had to pay for it! The biscuit is made from scratch and as for taste, it was 'ok.' It probably would have tasted better if it was served warm.  The menu is pretty diverse, they sell fried chicken (white, dark, and wings), sandwiches, salads, desert, and sides. They also have an impressive vintage soda collection. Now to the good part, they serve beer, prices range from $2.50 and up! They sell everything from Blue Moon to local craft beers! The atmosphere changes on Friday and Saturday nights from calm to wild! Thanks to party goers the line is usually long! Centered in the heart of Gayborhood, Wishbone is the perfect place to people watch on the weekend while sipping on a cheap cold beer! Wishbone's staff is friendly and the main reason why I am not giving it 4 stars is because I was not satisfied with the food and paying extra for condiments. If I could rate it based on the weekend vibe and beer alone I would give it 10 stars! By the way, they also deliver.

It scratches the same general itch as Dizen Goff when I don't have the time to make it over there. Slightly less expensive as well. 

Their pita and hummus are fine, but not as good as Dizen Goff. The steak shawarma had a slight gamey taste, which was unexpected, but didn't put me off. The chicken shawarma is significantly better. I was excited about the baklava, but it didn't ultimately taste of anything.

I wouldn't wait in line for this stuff, and the lines do get long. If there's no wait, it's not bad.

The food is exquisite.  I had one of the best meals of my life.  Everything was excellent.  As we were debating what to order the girls making their exit at the table next to us said "everything is amazing!" and we're effusive with praise for everything they had on the menu including the lavender gin and tonics (only $5.50) which it appeared they had several of!  Well they were right.  The Chicken Marsala is divine.  The squid is cooked to perfection.  Everything is perfect for sharing.   The ambiance is loud...it IS a pub...perhaps some noise dampeners could be added.   But the music choices were excellent and I couldn't help but feel elated that there was so much positive energy coming from this location that was once an abandoned eyesore only a year ago!

Went here for lunch yesterday, spent approx $9 for a 2 entree, 1 side meal and a drink.  I ended up tossing it and getting a Smoothie from Smoothie King.  I wasn't thrilled with the food at all.  Everything was bland.  No flavor in the steamed veggies, the beef and broccoli or the salt and pepper chicken.  I veered away from the breaded items, so maybe that's where all the flavor resides.  

Won't be going back. :(
Hands down the most amazing Mac and cheese ever. I would choose this Mac and cheese over sex. No exaggerations. It's that good.

Sushi burrito. Nuf said. All I need with any of these wraps is a side of spicy mayo and my day can't get any better. I love how you can customize every part of it and they make it super quickly right in front of you. An Asian version of chipotle and the packaging is adorable!

This is a decent place to hit if you are going to play it safe at the Reading Termial Market.  But with all the choices, I'm not sure why anyone would! Or why I did, for that matter. 
The produce is local which is pretty cool.  People helping people, I like it. They have an above average salad bar...I made a rockin little creation with seafood salad.  They have a decent selection if hoot food too served buffet style, but I cannot attest to this as I stuck to the lettuce. My main gripe is the price though. I think I spent $14 on a salad and bottle of water? That's too damn high!

There are so many good places at the terminal market... pass on this place unless you like corn bread.  If you do, just buy the corn bread and run.  There is nothing else here that is worth your time.  The food is not bad.  The chicken was moist, but it had no flavor.  The mac and cheese... way over cooked... the noodles were soggy.  The green beans were over cooked as well.  The lemonade... not good.  Corn bread... very good.   I would only buy corn bread from this place in the future.
Entrees are great, orange chicken, honey walnut shrimp, beef and broccoli. The fried rice, chow mein and white rice and flavorless and gross.
Buckminsters is a fabulous addition to the neighborhood. The cauliflower au gratin is like cauliflower Mac and Cheese. It's so great we orders it twice. Service was excellent!! We will be back often.
I love the mac and cheese and corn bread here! But, like the other reviewers, the service is awful. The staff is incredibly rude and not helpful.

They have a tasty vegetarian hoagie.. Not eating neat usually limits your options in conventional chains but I'm okay with ordering that here because it's tasty goodness .. And you get 5 stars from me when on multiple times you've delivered food at 2am to me and friends at the bar!! Gotta love that!!

I walked by this place on the way to a meeting, and knew I'd be having lunch here later on. I love all things sushi, and DIY sushi Chipotle style was something I needed to try. 

I built my own roll, with salmon, mango, and a few other ingredients. I found the mango to be way over powering, and all in all the roll was nothing special. 

I had the experience, but don't need to go back. I'm just as happy with a 3 roll combo from a cheapy sushi place near by.

Normally, I love Qdoba. They have a lot of options and their gumbo is one of my favorite foods.. however, the U City Qdoba has definitely gone downhill in the past few years.

Before the Chipotle opened on 39th and Walnut, Qdoba was a very reliable, affordable and delicious place to go. However, lately their food has been lacking in freshness, their portion sizes have significantly decreased and some of the staff really don't know how to make a neat burrito! I hate when burritos are not wrapped properly and become a disaster to eat. Also...everyone knows if you order a veggie burrito, they are not supposed to skimp out on the vegetables!

There are only thing that keeps me coming back to this particular Qdoba
1. Double Point Tuesdays (hey free food is always a win!)
2. The gumbo (which you cannot get at Chipotle)

But if you are looking for a good burrito (naked or otherwise) I would recommend walking the extra block and a half to Chipotle!

I should have taken the hint of how bad the food was as soon as i stood in the empty line and watched 4 women argue on whose turn it was to handle the only customer in line. They used very little words. Just pointed and grunted. 
Their food was disgusting. The meatball sub tasted as if it was sitting for weeks. The meat was pale. When we returned the $7 meatball sub (2 meatballs on a long stale roll) and asked for something different. The lady rolled her eyes and said "It good. Fine, what you want?"  We picked mac and cheese. They practically tossed the container at us so we can leave. Then she shoved the meatball sub at us and said "Eww take it. We no want it". If you won't eat your own food, why the hell are you selling it to people who can potentially get sick from it. 
I tossed the mac and cheese in the trash can. Never ever will I eat or even look in the direction of that so called "food" spot. And I've lived in Philadelphia all my life. The worst food. The worst customer service.

Working another show means eating another fast meal.  The show itself was at the famous Trocadero Theater for Jersey Shows Battle of the bands.  I really just came along for the ride this time.  And just helped out a little when it came to load in.  After half way through the show, we decided to get food.  So my friend Kevin suggested that we go a few blocks down to the Reading Terminal Market. 

The Market is huge and has a lot of vendors and little restaurant stands.  It is a amazing place for a person like me.  So many choices to pick from and all of them smelled delicious.  Unfortunately we were on a time limit.  So we had to pick the place with the smallest line.  Which left us with Franks Alot. 

Frank's alot is a basic American BBQ spot. It seems to blend different items from different areas of the BBQ world.  From your basic Hot dogs to BBQ chicken.  It does seem that Frank is just a name sake.  There was no one who could be frank in site, unless he is a little Asian woman.  But the service was good and fast.  I got a Texas Tommy, which is basically a hot dog with cheese and bacon wrapped around it.  Apparently their version was a little different.  It has the same basic elements.  The difference is in how it is made.  Usually the cheese is wrap around the dog.  Then the bacon is wrapped around the cheese and the hot dog and it is cooked that way.  They just threw the cheese on bacon on.  It still tasted the same. So in the long run it really wasn't to much of a problem.

All in all the meal was nice and satifying.  So I would say that Franks Alot is  Fat Kid tested Fat Kid approved. 

As always stay peckish my friends.

Had a great drop in lunch here today.
Chicken tenders with two dipping sauces - a buffalo blue (which I normally don't like but was excellent here) and a very smokey chipotle.
Came with a very tasty mac and cheese. Full of veggies and other tasty morsels.
For a few extra bucks it came with a PBR which was a perfect easy drinking accompaniment.
Place is clean and stylish.
There's a big selection of other beer too which is nice.
Lots of baked treats that I didn't try.
Rice pudding too.

It's Japanese Chipotle!  Love it! We had the slammin salmon and the screamin tuna. Both were good but the screamin tuna had more flavor.  We substituted the spicy gochujang sauce with the spicy mayo instead.  I think I would have loved the slammin tuna if I didn't get to try the screamin tuna.  My only complaint is that I wish the rolls were slightly bigger.
Such a unique blend of Asian and Mexican. I want to try e earthing they have. I also like that you can pick your own ingredients and custom make your food.

Ok so here's my 6th review... and I'm writing reviews so people like me (who enjoy good food, good atmosphere, good times, and a good bargain- on occasion) can find reliable reviews for the hot and not so hot places around Philadelphia.  All that said lets start the review.
Ok this may be a cheap shot at a franchise but there are so many good neighborhood restaurants out there and I'll take the risk of eating at one or two bad restaurants knowing that I can find others that are good.
Only  in dire straights when Im with a friend and I want food that is fairly quick, reasonably priced, somewhat healthy, fresh, and served by friendly people in a clean and ordinary atmosphere will I return.
Until then I can do without it.

Disappointed of my Double Cheeseburger!!! My husband order Double Cheeseburger for me, for my supper, the tomato and vegetables are missing!!! He asked for ketchup, the lady told him they don't have ketchup. I feel so sad and the burger now taste so dry!!!

The food is great here.  I love the #5 (Vito) with hot peppers or the #13.  The service is quick and reasonably friendly.  The music is a touch loud for those who enjoy conversation, though.  Overall, though, it's a positive experience.

Also, they sell day-old rolls for $0.50.  These rolls are integral part of my cheese steak sandwich recipe, so... thanks, Jimmy John's.

I had refrained from writing a review from this place to see if they improved but it seems it's not going to happen. The staff is SUPER rude at this location. I have tried coming here on different times, different days and it's always the same thing. The items displayed on the menu are not available half the time and the staff tells you as if you should expect this to happen in every restaurant. The food at Hai St is good but I will stop going to this location until they decide to hire decent people for the job.
This place is disgusting!!!!!!!!!!! Went here the other night and my fries literally tasted like bleach. The staff is always rude. I will never go to this particular Wendy's ever again.

I love this place!  I started going to Hai Street when it first opened and I am fortunate enough to live nearby.  However, I work on the East side of town and wish there was one there for lunch!!  I love the menu and that they constantly add new items.  It's healthy, satisfying, consistent and great customer service.  Please open more locations!!
Excellent service! Much better than the e Coli competitor down the street! Less traffic, better food, and better service! What more could you ask for? Highly highly recommend!!

I really enjoy the sandwiches from JJ and they generally live up to their reputation for being freaky fast. On one occasion, however, it did take over an hour for my food to come so I had to cancel my order. Other than that though, it's not a bad choice  for quick good food.

I was very excited trying this place out and want to know what's the hype about. Ehh...it's okay, nothing special i had the slamming salmon and sweet green tea. 
The slamming salmon is a good size burrito stuffed with a lot of white rice, veg and couple pieces of raw salmon. The roll didn't have much flavor in it. And it wasn't spicy what so ever .  
The sweet green tea taste straight up like water to me with green color dye. 
Overall experience was okay. And  It is pretty pricey for an Okay burrito
 I would give this place another try, but somewhere else  not at this location.

This place had a nice relaxing atmosphere. The food selection was a standard fast food Mexican place. I was really hungry so I ordered the smothered burrito and it did not fail to disappoint! It was loaded with queso on the inside AND the outside, and seriously smothered with sour cream, cheese, guacamole. This was so good and so fast.

Way too overpriced for what it is, but tasty and convenient nonetheless. 9 bucks for an 8 inch, anemic sub, chips and drink? Gross. "Thinny Chips" will fool you into thinking they are healthy. 1 bag = 2 servings or 260 calories. "Low fat" Turkey Tom has 515 cals and a ton of fat from the mayo. Eek! Steer clear if you're looking for a healthy, tasty sub. Go to Subway for better choices and prices!

The food is delicious it seems like most of it is made to order, the place looks clean. Everything was perfect except for the young lady seems more occupied with her cell phone doesn't say thank you or your welcome, but nevertheless, great experience good food clean place.

Two friends and I tried out Buckminster's on a Thursday right after 5pm. As we walked in, we were the first in the restaurant and seated ourselves at a table. We shared several small plates such as the potato chips (don't waste your time), sunchokes (i never heard of a sunchoke before, but it was good), squid (yummy), crispy chicken, sweet potato curry, beet soup (very earthy taste), and the bologna and cheese. My favorite dish was the bologna and cheese. My two friends and I had 2 drinks each and shared the plates above and the total came to 125 bucks. When we finished all of the plates, I was still hungry. More substantial dishes would enhance the appeal for me in the future.

It was better than another sushi burrito place I've had, but still not fully hitting the spot (or maybe I'm just not a sushi burrito person?). I recommend getting one of the menu options instead of making your own, unless you already very familiar with sushi burritos simply because some combinations will not go well together.

I finally got to check this place out! The workers are super friendly and they have lots of funk! It's definitely a place to try especially for the younger crowd. I think I liked the green tea matcha drink for 99 cents better than the actual sushi burrito! The sushi burrito is basically a kimbap and like Kelly C, i totally agree I could make some better kimbap at home! I got the donkatsu sushi burrito and they put way too much sauce in it. It was so salty I really just couldn't finish it. However, the slammin' salmon was alright! Nothing amazing but it was edible ;) If you're into a cool atmosphere for A-ok food, you should check this place out!

Good portion size. I got the salmon roll. The rice wasn't totally cooked and the hot sauce used overpowered the flavor of pretty much all the other ingredients used. 

The iced matcha was good, pretty sweet and LOTS of matcha in it.

Food is good but they have some serious customer service issues. They are rude and you can tell they are unhappy. There is a new person every time I go, which is at least twice a week. Service is very inconsistent. I will try it one more time but that would be it. I always have to wait for falafels to be cooked too. Isn't this a fast food place?

Can't get over the rudeness I experienced today. As I was washing my hands in the restroom the manager, Peter (tall white guy with blondish hair) says rude things about me and my appearance, and teases me with his employees. I had just had a positive experience with the promoter outside of the store and I had a complete opposite experience inside the establishment. He is supposed to be a leader as the manager, but he makes rude jokes about a patron to his employees. Extremely unprofessional. I will not be returning to this location and I will advise others not to as well.

Neon Lobster is out of this world, we ordered the mussels and linguine and shrimp and linguine and it was fantastic. The portion of linguine could have been a little more, but all in all it was very very good! My husband could not get enough. We are excited to go back and order again and try their other dishes! My husband said the staff are all very nice and welcoming. We are very glad to have this new seafood restaurant in the area.  We highly recommend Neon Lobster!

Wishbone is an excellent choice for any hunger need. Maddi is by far the best customer service associate on premises. Her personality and presence truly made my experience remarkable and I will most definitely be back again. Thanks, Maddi!

This review is actually for the location at Lincoln Financial Field and not Citizens Bank park. (I noticed there is no listing for the one in Lincoln Financial Field.  

I was at the Eagles Home Opener on Sunday, September 11th.  At the half, I waited in line for some Chickie's and Pete's Crab Fries.  I waited about 25 minutes (Yes, I chose to wait in line) and when I got to the front, they stated that they were out of cheese.  

As you know, the cheese is pretty much what makes the fries so delicious.  There were on discounts or other future offers provided for being out of cheese that day.  It was a very disappointing experience to wait in line for 25 minutes and then leave empty handed.
This Mac and cheese is EVERYTHING. And the chicken. SUPER crunchy. The girl behind the counter was really nice and this is now a spot I have to make it to before I leave Philly!!!!
The made my sandwich before telling me the price. He and the price of the town can you get me Waymore than I expected.
Food was OK but a little to vinegary for me. DIdn't have a long wait on a Saturday at 7pm-ish. Would try again.

Found this space on uwishunu who were highlighting the 'The Top New Restaurants' in Philadelphia.

First entering the space we were greeted by lovely host/cashier. She told us the specials and gave us time to choose our selection. After deciding on a warm lobster sandwich and fried oysters wrapped in bacon, our hostess told us of a fabulous special. 

The overall ambiance was adorable and very chic. I enjoyed the seating arrangement and overall feel of the restaurant. The chef brought out our food and made sure we had everything we needed.

The food... To die for! Seriously. The moment I took a bite I knew this was a great fit. How amazing!

This place is affordable and awesome. Love it! Good service and good food!

Every time I've been here the wait has been outrageous. One time I ordered take out online and my food wasn't supposed to be ready for an hour, decided to get It anyway and when I went to pick It up I waited another half hour for them to make my food. They hadn't even started It yet. Food is good but the service is very slow

They take the fast out of fast food. Still 5 people away from ordering after 20 minutes. It's 9pm on a Tuesday, get it together! No sense of urgency by staff and this place is gross! You say raise minimum wage, I say bring on the machines!

This was my first sushi burrito ever and to be frank, it was pretty average. I'm unsure if it's the concept that doesn't work for me or if this place was just rather average. I went with the suggested spicy tuna and I really feel as if it was lacking in both flavor and size. For $10, I don't feel as if it is good value. The dude who was serving me was really light handed with the tuna so perhaps it was just a fluke. I'll give it another shot next time I'm in the city.

Great food, got the rice bowl with portobello mushrooms. They have some seating inside. Their pricing is reasonable too, starting from $6.99 for a rice bowl or nori wrap. If your looking for something tasty and healthy,  then check this place out.

Apparently the computers are down and lots of product is missing but the store is still open for some reason. They are only taking cash. Employees are struggling to add prices with a calculator and they are writing some orders down and telling others to the food handlers. It took me 16 min to be waited on when there were only 3 people in front of me. I ordered a coffee (they were out of all lids) and waited 12 minutes for it while people who ordered after me got food and drinks before me. I finally asked about my order and received no apology but instead had my coffee slammed on the counter while the employee muttered that people should be able to see that they were having issues. I still don't see what that has to do with food orders going out before my one little coffee.  I hate that this is the closest McDonald's to me but I'll go out of my way to avoid this poor service 
Update: I should have stayed away. On my next trip I ordered a meal with an orange juice and was told they didn't have any because the water has been shut off. She offered me something else instead and stated that I could get a coffee or frappe. I requested a frappe I also asked if it was possible to substitute for me on my McMuffin for an extra eggs. She said yes. When I got to the register she charge me for the egg (why tell me I could substitute it then) and for the frappe (not my fault you were out of OJ-it should be complimentary in that case). There was some nasty brown water all over the floor where food was kept that two employees were trying to clean. Never again. 
Update: Came to 24 hour drive thru at 3:30 am starving. No one answers the drive thru microphone. After 5 min I come to the first window. No one is there. Car in front of me honks for 2 min straight until someone comes to the window. I honk also then someone comes to the 1st window and removes the cash drawer but ignores me (this is the manager per another employee). Another person comes and tells me the system is down so they are closed despite The fact that it is a 24 hour McDonald's and there are no signs posted stating that there is an issue. The WORST!!

This place sucks. I've been in the drive thru line since 9:10.. it's 9:30.. I still didn't get my food.. what a disgrace.. the worst McDonald's I've ever been to in my life! Then the guy taking my order had attitude and was extremely ignorant.. talking about.. "hmmmm huh" when I said thank you.. wow shut this sh** hole down..

They left an item off my order, no biggie I'll just call and get it fixed. Well I call the number listed here, it's the other location. So when I find the correct number, I call and they have a voicemail system set up so you have to leave a message to speak with someone. This is insane for restaurant! What if I got the wrong order? I have to wait for a callback...? 

Chicken was decent. Mac was not good.
Service is awful and very slow and they have no air conditioning in the summer I would not recommend this Popeyes waist of money

I got a bacon ranch salad today and it was horrible. The greens weren't fresh and it looked like it was made days ago. I noticed when I got home so I didn't have time to go back. This why I really don't like McDonald's.
Fresh.  Filling.  Healthy.  Tasty! Signature roll is just enough for lunch without risk of a food coma.

Lured in here by helpings of Mac and cheese- it looks so good. However, prudence has always been a finer point of my personality, and when asked if the MAC was vegetarian and was deeply disappointed that it wasn't. 

The cornbreads are vegetarian, but slightly too dry, i've gotten them twice- at least- because they look so damn cute and tasty. Brownies are such a hit or mess out of the four times I've gotten a brownie two of those times that brownie was spectacular, the other times it was stale. 

The beer fridge is a nice touch and well priced too.

I love sushi. I love burritos. Sushi burritos?! YES, SIGN ME UP. I've never heard of sushi burritos until I visited Hai Street Kitchen. The concept is just like Chipotle, Subway, Salata, etc. You pick a base then choose your fillings and sauces. They also have choices you can choose from if you don't feel like getting crafty. If you hate sushi, no problem! They have other choices on the menu as well! My boyfriend ordered the Chicken Katsu roll and he loved it! One sushi burrito is enough to fill you up. I'll definitely stop by here again if I get a chance!

I'd like to give Hai St. Kitchen a higher rating, but the attitude we got from the two roll makers yesterday was really unprofessional. You could taste it in the food. I know it's the 4th of July and you're working, but at the same time, you're closing at 3pm. Don't give us attitude because WE, the customers, pay the bills. 

The food was ok. Drinks and chips were mediocre.

I was so so so excited to come here and I was let down so so so hard. This place has such a great vibe with coolers lined up with craft beer along with original and modern decor. Unfortunately, none of that can help the fact that the chicken's flavor was god awful. They highly brag about their pretzel crusted chicken, but they forgot to leave out that doesn't compensate for the potent flavor that instantly hits you when you take a bite. Even the 75 cent honey mustard couldn't save it. I'll give it an extra star because the fries were somewhat decent. Such a shame for such a beautifully decorated place. Give it a try for yourself and let me know if you felt the same. See you all at Popeyes down the street.

I've visited Philadelphia on two separate occasions, and both times, I made a stop for sushi burritos here. Their burritos are huge, and I found myself taking half of it home for later on both trips. Everything is good, but you might want to ask the employees to go a little lighter on the gochujang sauce (if your sushi burrito contains it) since it can get a little too salty and spicy.

I used to come here all the time. Now, however, they have removed all vegetarian proteins from the menu. A vegetarian can get a roll with cabbage, carrots and various other vegetables, but no source of protein. This makes no sense. Why can't they offer hearty and filling mushrooms like they used too?  Or tofu?  Or beans? Or even cheese (which was on the menu for a brief period of time).  I won't be able to eat here again until they can provide a balanced meal for a non-meat/fish eater. Instead, I will just go to Hip City Veg, a block and a half away.
Cheaper than all the other chicken chains. Taste pretty good for what it is and the spicy was actually spicy unlike Popeyes.

Love Qdoba. If you haven't tried their Mexican gumbo, do yourself a favor and TRY it. I would have never ordered it until my sister talked me into trying it. It is by far my favorite thing on the menu. Id pick Qdoba over chipotle and moes anyway specifically because of the Mexican gumbo.

Saw this from afar and noticed there was no line so I was ready for this fast service.

I walked into the line and there were about 5+ more workers and some were just walking around talking to each other. I waited from 3-5minutes before someone came to serve me. 

I would not recommend spending your time at this Chipotle especially if you're in a lunch run. There are two other locations in Center City that are much faster than this one that I will be going to from now on.

3star because cashier was nice and food was good. The wait brought it down 2stars and employees looking at me while I wait made it worse.

Subway is a guilty pleasure.  There have been ups and downs, but yep, usually ups.  The service is always quick despite the lines this location can draw.  The seating area is always tidy.  My fave?  Turkey and bacon on wheat.  That is all.

This McDonalds is average. There is room for improvements. The parking lot can get a little congested at times. There are 2 drive thru lines however that doesn't always mean faster service at this location.

I've been a Hai Street Kitchen fan for a VERY long time, so when the 40th Street location closed, I was bummed because that one was the closest to home and work.  However, while I was running some errands in Center City one Saturday afternoon and decided to break for lunch, I figured I would check out the 18th and Chestnut location and treat myself to a sushi burrito.  While Hai Street has preset menu options, I always prefer to customize my own sushi burritos, and the staff is always very accommodating to my requests.  I usually gravitate towards grilled chicken, chicken katsu, or shrimp tempura with ginger miso dressing, and carrots, garnished with fried garlic and tempura crunch.  Sometimes they offer seasonal toppings such as pineapple so I often add that in if it is available.  Hai Street better not leave Center City, because if they do, I won't know where else to get my sushi burrito fix!
They gave me a regular coke instead of a Diet Coke. And they forgot the chocolate milk for the happy meal...let's just say, I wasn't happy.

When I've had a bad day and feel like shit, I come to Popeye's (hey some people have pints of ice cream, I got my fried chicken).  I really love Popeyes and this one is probably one of the cleanest and tastiest I've been too.

I've never heard of a concept like this, but I must say, I'm hooked!  This place specializes in sushi-ritos (burrito sized sushi rolls).

The first thing that struck me about this place was how incredibly friendly ALL of the staff members were when I walked in.  I came in around 6:15 on a Friday night, and surprisingly, no one else was in the store at that time (though that didn't last long, don't worry!)  When I walked in, every single crew member looked at me and said 'hi' and welcomed me/asked if I had any questions, which really impressed me! It's not always that the staff at these sort of fast casual places continue to have warm customer service after opening weekend.

I got the slammin' salmon roll, and it was DELICIOUS.  Nori paper + brown (or white, if you like) rice + medium rare salmon +  lettuce + cucumber + red onions + pickled mango + spicy gojuchang sauce.  I got the regular size, but there was an option to make it a deluxe size for $1.99, which I probably would have done if I had wanted to be stuffed afterwards (I was full but not necessarily stuffed).  

Not a lot of seating, so definitely don't plan on sitting inside unless you're lucky and happened to snag one of the tables.

Loved this joint! Great Mediterranean food and plenty of options for vegetarians. This is an excellent lunch spot in center city especially to grab a quick lunch to bring back to work. Every time I've gotten a very fresh meal and its been super tasty. Pita was also great too. Would definitely recommend.
Been here 4 times since they opened and will continue to return. Consistently good food, exactly how you like it and fantastic service as well.
They always have a long line during lunch hour,  but it moves very quickly.  It's not gourmet by any stretch,  but it gets the job done. The bowls are one of my go to lunches.

I love Qdoba. The staff is always super nice and talkative. Unlike Chipotle, they don't give me weird looks when I say "no beans please". The burritos are stuffed to the max - I always get a fork and eat out some of its innards.

The Chipotle of Sushi Burritos! It was cool to see them make a burrito with the toppings I wanted. Overall cool hip place with very little seating and no restroom. It was just ok for me. Not impressed nor excited to go back.

Waaaaaaaaaaaaay better then Subway.

Freshly baked rolls are awesome. The only thing is this is a take on the classic Philadelphia Hoagie, not a classic Philadelphia hoagie...i.e. Primo's, but good none the less.

Stumbled upon this joint looking for something filling and healthy. The poke bowls are delicious and offer a nice variety to the sandwich shops and other similar spots. The stadd was really pleasant too. Definitely will be coming back to try a sushi burrito.

We did not go to the actual restaurant but visited their booth at the July 4th festival on the Benjamin Franklin parkway. My boyfriend and I both tried the sushi burrito. I tried the shrimp tempura one and it was AWESOME! My boyfriend had the chicken one and didn't really like it but I didn't think sushi and chicken really went together anyways. If you visit their store definitely get the shrimp one! You will not be disappointed.

Tacos was wet and soggy when we told the drive though lady she got an attitude and we waited for fresh hard tacos that we never got cause she spit at our car after we asked how much longer I tried calling corporate but no answer just voicemail horrible place stay away I'd they can spit at you what do they do to the food when no one is looking

I love all things middle eastern so I was super excited when I saw that they were opening so close to home and work. I will say that your experience is HIGHLY dependent on the staff at the moment that you are ordering. Literally the key to having a good experience at this location i'd say. I have been here 7-8 times and sometimes they have no meat, sometimes there is no cucumber salad, one time there wasn't even any pita. One time I think they gave me something older and I did get sick.

That being said, the few times that I did have the ideal naf naf experience it was awesome. I really like the shwarma and all the sauces. They are flavorful but not overpowering. I also enjoy all the fixings they are (usually) so good! The pita is always light and fluffy and perfectly baked. I tried the garlic sauce for the first time and it was on par with some fancier restaurants I have been to. I will go back for my shwarma fix but I do just wish they tried a little harder!

I have had the pierogies here and they are pretty good but what I really love are the BBQ chicken wings.  They are so tasty. They taste like they have a sweet glaze on them, which is really good. Today I tryed the mac and cheese and it was ok.  Nothing special but kinda good if that makes sense...lol

I've seen and heard from my friends that have had a sushirito and I wanted to give it a try because it looked good. I ordered the salmon burrito. I thought it was okay. There is a good amount of lettuce and cabbage which there were a good amount of bites where I just ate rice and salad. When I got to the salmon part, it was okay because I felt that the gochujang sauce overpowered it. It also would have helped with the salmon was more in the center so I can get a bite of salmon in every bite instead of just eating rice and veg and then salmon and veg.

Our sushi chefs were pretty cool, spunky, friendly. Ambiance is kind of cool, semi hipsterish?? I feel like there was a nose ring, boho glasses, a bandana, a tattoo of a woman on a woman (maybe Idk I'm just a regular hungry 9-5 drone)- I digress....Good location downtown.

That's where the pleasantries end, sadly.

I had the "Soft Shell Crab", and my friend had the "Holee Shrimp". Both had wayyyyyyy too much sauce! One bite and you'll be feeling like you've done something you shouldn't tell your mom about(wipes corner of mouth). The veggies looked fresh. The meat was pre-cooked/ sliced, soooo....yea, that's that. The ingredients were were disproportionate(4-5x more veggies than meat). It feels like you're eating an obese American sushi. 

In all fairness, we wanted to try the big sushi burrito looking thing, and that, my friend....is what was delivered!

Sum-
The Big sushi burrito is the evil love child of someone's love for sushi and the American demand for Supersized & YUGE!!!! everything. Way too expensive for what you get, IMO. The veggie ingredients seem fresh.The ambiance and staff are cool, but not cool enough for me to go back.

Pros- cool friendly staff/ambience, location, fresh veggies. You get the product as advertised.

Cons- taste of food, cost

WHAT I ORDERED: Make your own roll with brown rice + salmon tataki + carrots + grilled zucchini + romaine lettuce + ginger miso dressing + roasted peanuts + tempura flakes

PROS: Salmon roll delicious + price

CONS: Small + other proteins looked like they had been sitting out/not delicious

-----MORE DETAIL----

FOOD: DELICIOUS. Salmon is seared on the outside very very slightly and raw on the inside. Tastes like just raw salmon. Veggies were fresh and ginger miso dressing (I asked for light) added a slight sweetness, tanginess, and depth that was delicious. They do not make the sauces I don't think - they had to go check the label for ingredients.The other proteins though had been sitting out and didn't look quite so good - I probably wouldn't try those.

SERVICE: GREAT. I had some weird dietary restrictions today and they were super patient and willing to go check on the ingredients.

AMBIANCE: Asian style Chipotle. Small, bar seating. 

GOOD FOR: Grab and go, quick bite, eating alone, catching up with a friend, healthy eating.

So excited to have a new hummus/falafel place near the office. I'm always a little skeptical of quick serve/fast food concept places. Worry the quality will suffer. But this place is fantastic! Hummus and Baba are on point. And the falafel was great! I tried the veggie bowl and it was delish! The pita tastes fresh and the sauces were really good as well. They were quick to serve and I will definitely be back soon!

Place is great, there is a pizzeria right in front of the restaurant and I choose wishbone every time.  Only issue is there is a strange after taste with the fried chicken.  It could be MSG in the seasoning or a weird salt that I can t put my finger on, but I can t stand that after taste.  Other than that it is a great restaurant, and a decent value.  Chick-fil-la needs to take notes, from wishbone.

I was excited to see a sushi burrito for which I've never tried. I ordered a create your own with brown rice, grilled chicken , Asian slaw, avocado, cucumber, jalapeno aioli, and fried shallots "for crunch". They said they did not have brown rice, grilled chicken or jalapeno aioli. So I got white rice, chicken katsu, and spicy mayo instead.  The flavors were good but I did not taste the spicy mayo nor the fried shallots. It felt a bit dry needing some kind of sauce to bond all the ingredients together. I will try again and hopefully they will have everything listed on their menu.
Good food, terrible customer service. I asked a question, only to be ignored. It was absolutely not professional from their side. I hope that they will change the waiters.

I went there today and had pizza fries and beer battered onion rings. They both were the worst thing I tasted and had to grow them away.
The onion rings had no taste in batter and also it didn't have any salt or pepper or any other seasoning. It was so oily it was like eating oil.
Pizza fries had fries with tasteless cheese and a marinade sauce. Normal French fries from McDonald's are 100 times better than this pizza fries.
People seemed to order grilled chicken and I think it should be good
I didn't try as fries and onion rings killed my mood

I was so surprised to hear that something similar to Sushirrito in SF was on the east coast! Once I found out about this place, I definitely had to try it for myself.

What's so special? It's sushi in burrito form. What's not to love. Choose your own rolls or to avoid the "mess" you could get it in a bowl. You could either choose one of their signature rolls or build your own. 

Got the Slammin Salmon with spicy mayo and fried garlic for almost $8. It was delicious and DEFINITELY met my expectations! The burrito was huge!!

Came here with a group of about 15 people and was surprised at how quick we were served despite the long line! 

On the downside - the restaurant is pretty small. They only have bar seating and stools by the window. I also didn't see a bathroom. 

Overall their rolls were on point! I will definitely come back when I'm in Philly!
the food is pretty good but the service is bad and the employees are very rude AND it is very dirty, that's why I never use there restrooms.

This is by far one of THEE WORST McDonalds in the city I've gotten into two different arguments with these young immature kids they call employees. When you go in instead of them being attentive and waiting to take your order they stand in a circle with their backs to the counter discussing everything but the right thing. One female employee who was waiting for her order to bag up started playing in the hair of a male employee then goes and touches the food no gloves on at all. Then as I waited for my food which took 20 mins for hot cakes and sausage the employee calls me to get it and drops it on the counter well when I asked to speak to the manager I told her your employee is ignorant they need to be trained. I don't know who the owner is but he needs to check the cameras when he's not there cuz this place absolutely sucks when it comes to customer service.

I love the Reading Terminal!  With a number of great food options, the toughest thing to do is saving room for all the good food!

Tootsie's is one of those places I absolutely have to take my family or friends visiting from out of town.  They have a rotating hot foods menu which is always good for trying different foods, whatever I'm in the mood for that day.  I typically share some ribs, mac n cheese, roasted potatoes and pork sausage with whoever is lucky enough to be visiting me :)  

Service is always very quick and friendly, and it's a good place to go during the lunch rush (when all of the other lines are backed up a mile long!)
I got a slammin salmon.  Checked out the place in University City because so many people were talking about it.  It's hype.  The sushirito is essentially a huge kimbap. It's too bland.
A absolutely wonderful fried chicken sandwich with all the fixin's. Left my mouth watering for more. Maybe not the healthiest meal in Philly, but.... Delicious!

Today we stopped by here and when we placed our order all seemed well besides them telling us that the milkshake machine was down.  Went to pay and the drive thru lady asked us if we could drive to the other window on the opposite side of the building to pick up our for (the passenger drive thru window). O_o.   So we did despite the price of gas nowadays.  When we got our food I checked our bags everything was there except my daughter's toy in her kids meal. When I said something to the employer she said "we ran out".   The whole point of us getting a kids meal was for the toy other than that we would have just ordered something else for her.  Either way we made our way back home.  Took a bite of the burger , it was by far the salty-est crap I've ever tasted. Didn't even bother going back.  Won't ever again spend another dime there again.

The food is really good but they nickel and dime you for everything. Extra scoop of rice, that will be two dollars. You want lettuce, that will be extra. Really  - it's just lettuce and rice! These are cheap ingredients. You are better off leaving the customer happy. Lastly, there is no price transparency. There are step by step instructions on how to build a bowl but I have no idea how much each thing costs. I will go back when I am craving it but ordering is painful.

I love Poke Bowls, I've had some really good ones. This place had only one worker for 5 people waiting in line, meaning one person taking care of making food and work at the register.  I ordered a Poke Bowl with tuna fish, and the places I went to buy Poke bowls, I also would choose the ingredients that I want in the bowl, that didn't happen. My bowl was 1/3 empty, while my friend's was full. So i asked why that is, and the worker told me that, it's because they are out of something, so I said, I'm paying $14 for this, add some rice then.  Absolute disregard of customer's comments, she added the rice. The bowl had more green salad than anything else.  I didn't like this place at all, would not recommend.

This was my first time here and first sushi burrito.  I had the HoLee Shrimp. It had great flavors. I got it with brown rice. I would have liked a little more sauce, but over the burrito was great. The store was clean. Service was fast. Not much room to eat there, so plan on getting it to go.

Overpriced chicken tenders in my opinion.  The concept is a good one, but I expected more than chicken fingers and biscuits that have clearly been sitting under the heat lamp most the day. They do have a best soda collection which is why I rated 3 stars instead of 2. Not sure I would come back here
Won't be my favorite in the city, but it's convenient, lines aren't too long, and pretty good. not a huge fan of the Naf Naf fries though.
