Great spot to grab a quick meal. Portions are large, but do not leave you feeling heavy.    I highly recommend this place if you are on the go and looking for something healthy.

I've been there a couple of times and the food was good but the ambiance is a little cold to me. It lacks some warmth and I think that they accomplish that by changing the lights by the liquor area. 

Service was good but I didn't feel like staying there any longer than a drink or two. Please make it more cozy...candles are great but what's the point of having them if the dimmers are not on point. I'm all about supporting my neighborhood so I'd recommend checking it out. Cheers!

Chicken and biscuit was sooooo dry. The girl at the counter clearly lacked customer service skills and sense of self awareness and party music threw me off so early in the morning. The cola was good though!

I love this place.  The menu seems a little strange, but literally everything we tried, we LOVED (and we ordered 90% of the menu).  The bar is growing, but already the wines on tap are a reason to stop in: the barbera is delicious.  The staff is friendly.  The bar is open late.  The place is so comfortable and inviting, yet funky (in a good way!).  What a wonderful addition to the neighborhood!  Welcome to Point Breeze Buckminster's, I'll probably see you again tonight.  ;)

A wonderful, magical place where sushi and Chipotle lovers can join together and hold hands in peaceful rejoice.

I can always eat sushi, but I can't always afford sushi. I have a tragic issue of ordering sushi rolls when I am very hungry, which leads to WAY too many rolls eaten, and way too much money spent. (It's worth it, but my wallet often whispers, "What can we afford for the rest of the week, though?") 

ENTER MY LIFE SAVER. Hai Street Kitchen's sushi rolls are what I have always envisioned- amazing, glorious sushi THAT ISN'T BITE SIZE. After finishing a burrito, I can feel full, satisfied, and skip the part where I separate myself from the group and cry about how many calories in rice I had just consumed.

Imagine you are Alice in Wonderland, and you eat that cake that shrinks you down to tiny size, and then you come across a sushi roll that hasn't been sliced yet. That's basically what happens. Without the rabbit hole.

With a local, we were able to go for a late lunch on a Sunday, where there was NO line, and the happy, helpful employees were eager to help. I would have liked if they had asked "if you've ever been here" so that I would have a better idea of how things worked. If they ask that I usually get the worker to make me THEIR favorite combination, but instead I ordered the Slammin' Salmon off of the menu (Around $10. See other Yelp reviews for this, you already know I loved it). Boyfriend and "tour guide" ordered "The Crunch," which got 5/5 from both of them.  "Tour guide" was upset that the Mango something or other wasn't there anymore, but it doesn't matter:

There is something important that I need to talk to you about. The Wasabi Guacamole. If you're an avocado fan, and you're okay with a LITTLE bit of sinus clearing wasabi, I promise you that this $0.99 add-on is ABSOLUTELY WORTH IT. It's not overpowering since the Wasabi is calmed down by the cooling avocado, but the flavors are powerful enough to really compliment everything in the roll. DO IT. DO IT.

DRINKS: The drinks are a bit pricy (Hibiscus Tea was $2.19), but I would recommend getting one in case you are overwhelmed by the kick of the flavors.

SEATING: There is a window facing seating area, but it only has 4 chairs, so make arrangements to eat somewhere else. 

MESSY: The rolls are VERY MESSY. They do tend to fall apart. If you opt for Burrito style, grab a fork/spoon anyway so that you can scoop up what fell out. Honestly, next time I think I would go for a bowl so that I can taste everything individually as well as together, and not worry about looking messy in front of a date!

Wow, I'm not really sure why this Qdoba has such bad review.  I really like their chicken quesadillas and the service here is pretty standard for a semi fast food joint.  Their quesadillas have the pefect cheese to meat ratio.  I am not a fan of too much meat on a quesadilla. I like the preportions to be almost equal, and qdoba gets it just right.  Also they have the best chocolate chip cookies ever... yummy! The only issue I have with this Qdoba is that if you pay with a debit or credit card they don't give you a receipt, you have to ask for it.  This baffles me, why wouldn't I want my receipt? Anyway other than that, everything else is good.

Their chicken strips are by FAR the best in Philly! Their sauces are out of this world, but be careful with the Triple XXX hot sauce, YIKES! The mini pot pies are fantastic and I could slap my mama over their macNcheese! I love this place

Second visit and really enjoyed the sushi burrito. The burrito is loaded with veggies but a little skimpy on the meat. The homemade iced green tea was delicious! Price is a bit higher than some other lunch options in the area at roughly $9-11 depending on what you get.

OKAY SO THIS WAS MY FIRST TIME EATING HERE IN A WHILE, SO I WAS EXPECTING EVERYTHING TO TASTE GREAT... THINK AGAIN! THE WORST SERVICE A CUSTOMER COULD ASK FOR ALONG WITH THE QUALITY OF THE FOOD.. my boneless wings were barely wings more like bread and the fries were barely cooked... Oh wait there's more! My rolls were so stale that when I bit into one it fell apart bread crumbs everywhere smh I refuse to eat here .. wingstop you'll never get my hard earned money again  btw I didn't take it back because I was already home when I noticed everything smh. 
Good luck future customers of wingstop at cottman anyways lol

Is it wrong that I think this place intentionally made a marijuana themed sushi-rito business? This venue is on HAI street after all, their slogan is "rolled your way" and when they wrap your sushi-rito up, they twist the ends of the wrapping paper, making it look like a fat blunt. Lol Jk. 

All jokes aside, this place is comparable to Chipotle Mexican Grill. Out have your option of the main meat/seafood, rice, toppings and sauces. I split a salmon roll with my friend and it was delish! It consisted of salmon pieces, avocados, red lettuce and rice all wrapped in a big piece of seaweed. I thought it was a delicious combination. I just wish that they have more of these kinds of places in New York City. 

Would I come back? Sure.

Great little salad bar in the Reading Terminal Market. Fresh ingredients, both hot and cold selections. I really like their cole slaw. Make you own salad. What could be better or simpler. Delicious food, lots of choices. Highly recommend.

Was lured in by the concept and positive reviews. But I have to say i did not care for what I ordered AT ALL, however perhaps I need to try again because I will say it was fresh and is a great great great concept. .. and I see other reviewers rave about this place and concoction, in particular, but I THREW IT AWAY. That says a lot for me, ha, not much food waste in these parts :( ... Hmmmmm....

I had one of their posted creations, the salmon one, and added the wasabi guac to it because well wasabi and guac go together with salmon brilliantly. This creation however did NOT work.

I just didn't like the flavor, it was too sweet for one--I dont think I cared for the mango on it and would have left off the sriracha type sauce that was one of the standards on this "rollito"... blah ...

perhaps will try again and crunch it out instead and no sriracha sauce (it's not called this but i don't remember what they call it but sriracha is the base)....I dunno though if I will, am kinda turned off and $10 in the trash isn't a lot but it could have gotten me a delish sandwich at Hip City Veg....lol

A couple of stars for great, friendly service and a great concept but *think* about what you order or get the sauces on the side at first. I did not pick well...

So I got the slammin salmon signature roll, I think the ratio of vegetables to meat is way too high. When I bit into the roll I could only taste all the vegetables in it. I think the concept of a sushi burrito is innovative, but I feel like there could have been more meat in it. I've only been here once and I picked the signature roll. You can also make your own roll so I think if I had done that it would have been better (perhaps substitute or pay extra for more meat). The roll was around $9 and some change so a bit on the pricier side. I think everyone should try this at least once. I went on a Sat afternoon around 3ish, but I heard there's usually a line during lunchtime.

Attended my first Phillies game (though actually was there to see the Red Sox, who lost in spectacular fashion). I felt compelled to try the fries -- local, specialized, and somewhat mythical as they are. I showed up during the Phillies half of the first inning and the line about half the length of the maze that you have to go through to get to the fries, and it moved quickly -- was probably in and out in about 5 minutes. 

Anthony N does a good job of characterizing the fries: thin, crinkle-cut, hot, crispy, salty. I tried to eat all of the ones that were less seasoning-heavy, leaving those for the boyfriend. Having some ketchup to cut the spice/salt was helpful. The portion is huge -- I didn't have to snarl at bf for eating more than his share for a change -- I got good and full on less than half of the giant cup o' fries. I probably won't go out of my way for these in the future, but they were quite good, and seemed a reasonable value for the portion size.
They should reconsider there hiring process. The people working here are ignorant and lazy. The food is good but they need to fire everybody working here!!!!!!!
Really great! I always get the Hai Street chicken burrito!! Lots of flavors and good quality ingredients.

I was stuck in Center City during an awful rainstorm, and in this weather, your most inner cravings come out. My stomach wanted: pierogies. I thought.. where in the city can I grab a to-go, tasty, reliable batch. SO naturally I did a Google search my phone and it pointed me in the direction of this place. "Menu highlights include Charbroiled Hamburgers, Italian, Polish and German specialties.... Polish kielbasa and pierogies." And the fact that it was located in Reading Terminal, I thought without a doubt, these would be delicious. Boy was I wrong.

Confused when I spotted the place, it seemed more like a sports bar & grill rather than a diverse food spot. Graphics of flames over-took the menu boards and 5 Asian ladies working behind the counter. I was expecting a grumpy Polish man, in fact I was really looking forward to that. I ordered the $6.25 platter which comes with 5 pierogies and two sides (I chose mac n cheese + green beans). The piergoies tasted stale-crunchy, not good-crunchy and barely had an filling in them. The taste was OK but I was severely disappointed that I ended up with 5 sad, flat looking piergoies. :(

Probably won't come back here again for this, but I will be sure to check out their hot-dog/wings selection.

This is actually a super efficient and great way to eat a sushi roll with less rice.  It's literally a sushi burrito wrapped with your choice of fish, veggies, sauce, and as much or little rice in a seaweed wrap.  My salmon roll with spicy sauce, brown rice, and veggies was very good and came with a very generous portion of salmon.  It's more filling than a typical sushi roll and definitely has more than 3x's the amount of fish.  It's about $10 for a roll, and you have the option of customizing the wrap or converting it into a rice bowl or even salad.  Definitely worth a visit!  Will be back to try the tuna very soon!
I finally had the food, and it was delicious!!! I ordered the drunken crab, gg burger, matts, and truffle fries. Everything was good! I will definitely order again.
Pita is the best thing in there. The service is excellent. The food lacks flavor. Very colorful, that draws you in until you taste it. Mamma's have nothing to worry about.

sushi burrito, done time and again in all the more popping cities before finally being adopted by some industrious business man in Philadelphia... I was willing to give Hai Street a try but I've confirmed to myself yet again the over-ratedness of the sushi burrito phenomenon.  Essentially a novelty item running on the current tide of "organic, lots of veggie, colorful food" hype.  Accordingly, the place looks hip and clean so props to them.  Don't get me wrong, the food tastes fine, I just don't foresee myself paying the extra bucks again for such a gimmicky food choice.  To put it succinctly, Hai Street brings something new to Philadelphia, but in the culinary world is just one of many dull rocks in a river.

Terrible service! I actually didn't take the time to check the review of this particular McD before arriving. I know better next time. 
The Drive thru Line was ridiculously long for over 20 minutes. I couldn't escape because of the barrier between the line and parking lot otherwise I would have left after 6 minutes. 
I got out of my car  and walked inside... only 2 people were working (this was 2pm) ...isn't that prime lunch time where people were waiting inside as well. 
I asked what the hold up was and they said they were short on staff. I just returned to my vehicle and waited for the line to move and left.  Check the McD's reviews!

I came here for lunch today and got the slamming salmon. it was delicious, a little spicy, but good! I had pretty high expectations and I wouldn't say I was disappointed, but this is something I can live without. oh, and the green tea is great! there was no wait and the staff was friendly enough.

I am a very big fan on places like Reading Market, and Philadelphians should be proud  of this market and all the things it offers. 

It was a beautiful day in Philly and I waited all day to have my stomach ready for some good Southern food and it wasn't easy choosing one. I opted for Tootsie's because I love all the greens that they have and the line of people ordering food it seemed like it was the place to be. 

The ordering process was simple: you take a "to go" box, fill it up with all the  yummys you want and weigh them, $7.99/lb; which mine came up to $11. I know, I love variety! 
I had brown rice, lots of collard greens, whiting fish, chicken breasts, kale & quinoa salad, even had a little bit of their macaroni & cheese. 

I loved all the greens. The whiting fish was a little tough and the chicken breasts were dry and bland (not very happy about that); the rest were just ok. The place was clean and the employees were very efficient and had great attitudes. 

Overall, you can try it if there are no other choices; but it's Reading Market, there's plenty to choose from.

What an unique concept. I'm not sure that a sushi burrito is any healthier for you than a normal burrito, but what a taste explosion! The salmon is unbelievable, quick, easy, delicious, and "maybe" good for you. I'll definitely be back!

Don't believe the hype. 

I was super excited to try this place because of their cool sushi-burrito combination. My boyfriend and I ordered off the menu instead of "make your own roll". I got The Crunch and my boyfriend got the Slammin Salmon. He said his salmon roll was pretty good. The Crunch was not bad. 2 tempura shrimps and lots and lots of veggies. It was a little more spicier than I can usually handle (but I'm not a spicy food eater). Both our rolls kind of fell apart even before we bite into them. I wish they use bigger seaweed wraps or something to hold everything together. 

The down side of this is I felt really sick afterward and thinking about them makes me feel sick now =\ it's really not what the hype makes it to be. It's good to try if you never had it, but you won't miss out on anything. I prefer my sushi the traditional way. 

This place is meant to be for to-go. They have space you can eat inside but super limited. Tables against the wall but only 4 stools. Parking on the street or garages. The garages are super expensive.

If I could give zero stars I would. Normally great service but Friday night the "night shift"  got my order completely  wrong. I got home and called to inform them of their mistake. A number 9 no mayo no cheese no onions and the "manager" starts in on me as if it was my fault.  He went on a profanity laced tirade.  Never in my life have I experienced  anything like that.  I returned the sandwich  and got nothing but here you go. It was pretty bad.

I did take out.  It was ok to me. I have had better.  I think the wings were too big.  My only hang up was how the fries were packed for take out. Not covered and I didn't get all the seasoning. They were bland.  I may try again at another location.
Great for the drunk and impatient. Just the right amount of carbs and extremely fast service.  My favorite thing is the 6 inch BLT!

First off, I have eaten at several different Qdoba locations throughout the country.  Every Qdoba I have eaten would be 5 stars, except this one.  The person preparing our food gave me extremely small portions of everything and I would have to always ask for more and paid very little attention to customers.

I'm not a foodie or food snob by any stretch of the imagination, but this place is purgatory of food. Got the buffet so I can't speak for the salad bar. The fried white fish was decent, and that's about where the positives end. Chicken tenders are moist on the outside by dry inside. The most bland Mac n cheese I've ever eaten, and the baked ziti is just not good in any way. Stewed beef might be dog food. On top of that there are flies.

We were hungry and it was just ok. Yup  chicken is like shake n bake but it's decent cause it's tender. Mac n cheese is a standout as is the sauces. Also beer to go? They have fin du monde from Quebec. That's awesome. Wasn't expecting much so but  it was good or we were hungry I can't decide..

It is redecorated and looks like a better environment, but the food gets worse, french fries are too much, and the bad thing is that the cashier will secretly join the topping fee so that you pay more money and the drink is no longer available for free Of the cup, in short, this shop is getting worse.

I would recommend this restaurant. The service was very good. The manager, is a kind , very personable and very efficient. My son was being careless putting the straw in his juice box. He ended up knocking his plate to the floor. The manager brings us another meal for free! We love this restaurant, we enjoy the vegan dinner! Beans, rice, vegetables, avocado , etc. Price was fair. I recommend it.

My slammin salmon wrap was fine but a bit overpowered in the vinegar/sugar flavor. My main issue is that, eleven dollars later, I was still hungry ,,, figuring that 22 dollars would be needed to fill me up, I could probably do better at any of a number of real sushi places without the fast-food ambience.

After the first snow storm in Philadelphia this year a buddy of mine and myself went to this location. I had never had anything from Checkers in my life.  There are two words to describe this location..... "Ghetto & Cheap".  Now that I have that out of the way, the food was merely a stomach filler.  I was so hungry at the time I didn't care.  We ordered 4 Bacon Burgers and fries.  They weren't horrible, just really greasy. The staff was friendly; no complaints there.  I'm just not a huge fan of ordering through a bullet proof glass window.  It kind of takes away the ambiance of any storefront. There's plenty of parking and yea....that's about it.  Would I go here again?  Only if I was starving and it was down the street.
Incredibly friendly staff and they had the best Salmon Burgers I've ever taste!  Corn bread was also delicious, but I think they gave me too many french fries (felt wasteful)

I got the Flamin' tuna at the new Liberty Place location. I want to love this but by the time I got back to my desk, less than 5 mins after I bought it, it was soggy and falling apart. Took one bite of the roll and the whole thing starts to fall apart. The Nori was wet.  I ate the inside and threw out the rest.

I come to this Subway often, especially when I have an appointment at Jefferson.  The staff here are very friendly and they smile.  The sandwiches are tasty, fresh and flavorful.  They always have cookies, chips, juices, etc in stock.  Auntie Anne's just opened in the same building as Subway.  I would like to give them a try too!

Amazing concept, great flavors - possibly the coolest thing I have ever eaten. I love sushi, and was not disappointed by this new method. It's kind of similar to building your perfect futomaki roll? And then eating it hand-roll style. I had the Slamin' Salmon loaded with yummy pickled veggies, papaya, and cabbage. Will for sure be returning to this spot!!

I was in town for work and this was down the street. I saw sushi burrito and I yelped (no pun intended) a little since the sushi burrito restaurant in Boston closed before I even had the chance to try it. 

The place is really small and sits about 2 people lol. The place is def meant for take out. When you order it's chipotle style. 
I went with the salmon burrito special. They pack it in this really cute brown hexagon box. I also got the sweetened ice green tea. This was really messy to eat. You take one bite and everything else just spills out. The taste combo was okay it was missing something to marry it altogether.  The tea was a bit sweet but it's refreshing to have. 

My thought on this sushi burrito is that Id stick to sushi rolls. It's too filling for lunch and if there's a next time I would rather go with the rice plates than the burrito style.

Sushi Burritos, whaaaat? I've been to Hai Street twice now and it hasn't disappointed either time. The first time I got the bowl with brown rice and tempura shrimp, it's one of their suggestions. So good! Nice Asian Flavors without the heavy, greasy feeling. There was mango and cucumber with a nice sweet and spicy taste. I also had their iced green tea, delish, just as the guy at the counter insisted it would be. I was so happy with my dinner choice! I've heard lunch there is super busy but since I don't work in the city I can only check out places for dinner usually. There was no wait and the employees were nice and informative of what they were offering. I went back a few weeks later and got the burrito with chicken.  This time I tried the hibiscus tea, it could have been a little sweeter but was still a nice drink to have on a hot summer evening. 

I will definately be going back soon!

I went here yesterday and bought some chicken wings, mac and cheese & cornbread, everything was superb, finger lickin good, so good that I may have to stop down there again today for some more. So if you want to give yourself a treat. This is the place to go.

Vicinity: Not clean inside
Bathroom: "Oh heck no"!
Staff: Friendly
Customers: Ratchet 
Food Delivery: neatly packed


Given that this "restaurant" is directly across from a horrible high school, it's explainable why this particular McDonald's seems like the slumps. The food is either hot our cold when handed to customers. The back of the counter (front floor) is always unorganized and filthy. I don't care eat there....but im addicted to their chocolate chip cookies; that's all i eat from them.

Stopped by for lunch, and wow, what a delicious meal! A very unique combination of quick on the go food, quality ingredients, and mouth watering flavor. My partner and I both got the sushi rolls and the different teas they offered, and we had zero complaints about everything! Customer service could use some works, but I'll give the gals a break since busy during the lunch hour. Would recommend!

Small self serving restaurant with your typical buffet food, chicken, meatloaf, fried fish, etc along with a decent salad bar.  I was pleasantly surprised by the price.  It's by the ounce but isn't as expensive as other places I've experienced.  The food was ok, but most of it was not seasoned.  I understand that being it's a self serve for a variety of tastes.  Be warned, it's in a place called Readings Market that is a framers market on acid.  People everywhere during lunch time going to the diverse number of restaurants at this location.  I would recommend.

Bossy cashier tell me to go stand over there and she is pointing.. tell me not to put my phone on the counter.. so many things I must not doinstead of asking me politely. Not the first time.

The new manager scares me every timeat least the food is gd.. better than the service

It's a train wreck of a meal that you just can't keep yourself from hankering from time to time. Give in, get that Triple Whopper, and remind yourself why you don't go there. 

It gets three stars because the only thing sadder than eating at Burger King is complaining about eating at Burger King.

There's always a huge line but it moves fast.  That being said is it worth it?  Ehhhh.  We made the mistake of grabbing fries in the front.  Rookie error.  Grab the ones in back as they are hotter and fresher.  Ours were cold so we didn't love them.

As people here have said make sure you get the cheese.

349/365

Chicken tenders and biscuit were slammin. Love all the dipping sauce options- biiiiiiig dipper over here. 

Mac n cheese wasn't my thing, and the baby pot pie was kinda gross.

The staff were very friendly, and extra points for being open late!

Charging $1.19 for guacamole in a vegetarian burrito is nothing short of robbery. For that reason alone, I would never eat here. The "hot" salsa is really just medium. 

The staff doesn't understand the concept of "everything", and only most reluctantly put what I ask for in the burrito. Also, the guy who was making my burrito insisted on scraping the bottom of the lettuce and zuchini containers when he could very well see that there was almost nothing in it. I am not saying, throw the food away. But bring a fresh box in, and add the last bits to that and then give me a full serving you stingy person!

The tortillas here are seriously weak. They start tearing as soon as the staff remove it from the grill. 

In sum, Chipotle, a 2-minute walk from here, is much much better. I don't understand why anybody would still go to Qdoba when Chipotle is a stone's throw away. I did, just for old times' sake, and I regret it. Very very disappointing.

I have been to this Qdoba many times. I hadn't been here in awhile and it was good to be back! I prefer this Mexican "fast food" grill over Chipotle any day. I had a Naked Burrito - Vegetarian. You have a choice of Brown rice or white rice (I chose the Brown rice). I also love the Mexican gumbo, quesadillas here. For soda drinkers, it's cool to note they have one of those new machines where you can have lie or raspberry or cherry flavored added to soda. They even have Sparkling water. And free refills is nice when you are thirsty, as I was. I think prices are reasonable, and food is tasty.

Been here twice after my interest was piqued from seeing it every day on my commute. You get a lot of food and it's tasty and filling. I've had the steak and the chicken with rice, but the meat itself doesn't knock my socks off; however I think next time I may get just the yellow rice with the cucumber/tomato salad, onions, and tzatziki sauce. The pita bread is nice and fluffy, and the fries are really good; both time they've been made on the spot for my order.
I've visited toward the evening hours and it hasn't been busy at those times. Staff was friendly and patient.

Ventured into Wishbone not really knowing what to expect. My two friends and I were pleasantly surprised at how good (and juicy) the chicken was. I was sold on the Mac and cheese after the employees let us try some before buying - their mac and cheese is awesome. The two employees were so nice and very helpful when it came to making up our minds on what to buy. The buffalo bleu sauce was so good - if they sold it by the bottle I'd buy it. The only suggestion I'd make is to somehow make sure the food is served at a higher temperature. (It wasn't cold but could have been much hotter)

Overall it was a fun place to eat with decent food and down to earth employees. We got a few pounds of chicken, some biscuits, some sauces, a pound of Mac, and a 6 pack of beer for around 50 bucks.

I haven't even taken a bite of my sandwich yet, but wanted to take a minute to speak on the amazing service I just received.

I placed an order around 12:45ish this afternoon, was prompted that my order would be ready at 1:20, I completed my purchase and meandered around the Rittenhouse Square area waiting to pick up my meal. I arrived and for whatever reason, my order wasn't showing up on their end. They took a couple minutes looking and the gentleman working told me to not worry and they whipped my order up right there on the spot. 

They've created a return customer out of me based on this instance alone.

Very surprised how this " sushi burrito " turned out, couldn't ask for anything more, my fiancé grabbed me a screaming tuna burrito, it was phenomenal fresh and everything I hoped it would be will definitely be going back for more

Whenever I go to Reading Terminal, if I'm not making a bee line to The Dutch Eating Place I'm usually on my way to hit up Tootsies. Because, people, it's finger lickin' good! And I'm talking fried chicken all the way. It's simple, it's crispy, and it's my go-to for some southern comfort food. And at $7/pound for their food bar, your wallet won't be moaning too much either. Almost all of the people that you see crowding the little diner type of seating are primarily locals as most tourists make their way to Dinics or they've already been previously snagged by some other sandwich establishment. They just did some small renovation to the dining counter so it looks clean, updated, and ready for your regular blue collared worker to get a good meal. The employees are always pretty friendly when I go as well, polite, and expedient! In general, it's a pretty good place for the price.

Interesting concept, got the slamming salmon roll.  Basically a burrito sized sushi roll.  Aside from when I arrived back to the office and finding out I had a completely different roll than what I ordered it was pretty good.  A little weird to eat to eat but I was satisfied.  Not sure I'd rush back there again, i'll probably just stick to a good sushi spot instead since there are a number of good spots downtown.

I've prepared plenty of sushi burritos at home over the years and this was my first time eating one from an establishment. Hai Street Kitchen makes very good ones.  Fresh ingredients, impressive wrapping/packaging.  I will be back for more.  Oh, and I ordered one of the salmon rolls with mixed greens, cucumber and miso sauce.  I also love that they employ bicycle delivery people.  Personally I think they should consider scooter delivery, but that's just me.

Had to ask for things several times.  The cashier seemed to have his own ideas for service, or who to serve.

The food was good, but on the high side price wise.

A pleasant option. We had an early dinner here. Everyone ordered something different and each choice was tasty.   The bowls seemed to be the better option.  The room was clean and the staff was efficient.

So the service was quick as expected and the cashier was pleasant.

I ordered a big Mac fries and a mcchicken.
The big Mac was good as well as the mcxhicken. The fries were disappointingly cold and under salted. This really ruined the experience for me.

Ok to begin; the food is amazingly great!!Chicken fingers awesome and the red bliss potato salad so damn good!! That being said, the reason I gave 2 stars was because of my experience when buy my food. I don't even let rude restaurant workers bother me anymore but what really bothered me was the fact that as the worker was weighing my food she dropped it on the counter and instead of getting another piece of chicken she picked it off the counter and just wrapped it up. Seriously!? Just severely bad customer service and more than likely against food/health code.

Got the slamming salmon loaded with everything on there.  It was definitely a bomb choice!  Take note that this is my first time trying a sushi burrito kind of food and this mix of concoction is absolutely on point!  I'm a big salmon guy and the salmon here do not disappoint!  Not the most freshest I've tasted but in no means it's not good!

The lines moved rather quick and the food was prepared a la subway mix and match style of your choosing so you know what exactly is in the mix.

Only thing that I find trouble with is finding parking near here.  Since this is right in the city finding parking here will be difficult.  If I had to plan it out I would definitely plan to find parking elsewhere and make this a destination when I'm visiting the area.

Honestly with all the hype I wanted this sushi burrito to be the best thing ever but overall I would rather have sushi. It's a lot of extras and not much actual real fish. It lacked in flavor and falls apart when you try and dip it in soy sauce so wasn't easy to eat either.

I came here to see what all the hype was about.  I have to admit - it is worth all the hype!  I was torn between the Slamming Salmon or The Crunch and went with The Crunch. Fresh veggies, a good amount of heat (with the spicy mayo) and a little crunch with the yummy tasting tempura shrimp.

The one drawback - I think I got a little bit of a shell on the last bite .  

Overall though, I would definitely return!  A little pricey, but to be expected in the neighborhood.  Staffers friendly and helpful when trying to decide between the two.

A yummy hidden gem on 18th street!

Holy wasabi guacamole! This place is the bomb dot com!!!!! If I lived in Philadelphia, I would come here every day for every meal. No joke! The staff is amazing and answered my 800 questions and did it with a smile. The concept is so freaking clever, I wish it was mine! The ingredients are super fresh and mmhhmm tasty!!! 

I had the slammin' salmon with wasabi guacamole. So much food for the price. Gosh, I need to get to Philly right now to have this wonderful piece of food art.

Such a disappointment! Seriously, any of the near by halal trucks have better stuff than this place. I got a chicken and rice bowl with salad and pickles. The rice was so dry and everything else was just mediocre. I also got a baklava, which was soggy. Just never again, save your money.

This is NOT susharitto-so don't expect it. My mistake was to think that it would be like the original. Hai street is ok but it is very expensive and does not even try to be "sushi" influenced except that they use raw fish in some rolls. Otherwise there was lots of pickled vegetables, lettuce and bland items. Will not be back. 2 rolls 1 drink = 30$ and seriously it was not yummy or memorable.

This place didn't set my world on fire. "The Shroom" is good and certainly flavorful, but I'm not the biggest fan of tempura; it was the only veggie option available. The salad was good and the vegetables were fresh - spring mix, beets, pickled onions, cuke, ginger miso dressing. I would love to see them add a tempeh or tofu option.
I really like this place. I had a craving for sushi but I didn't want to sit and eat. This was a good substitute.

so i'm a huge hai fan. i go through 777 deals fast and frequently. i left a review here when they first became popular...but this location has fallen short on quality and it sucks. i go back every time cause i think the time before that was just a random bad day for them but it gets worse everytime. the rolls just aren't as fresh as they used to be and it looks kinda dingy in there now. my seaweed today was awful -- so rubbery and hard to chew. two stars only because it seems like someone does quality control at the hai in liberty place. go there for your rolls. now...i'd say totally overpriced
The worst drive through! The girl at the drive thru 9/13 at 1 Am was rude and was cursing!! Worst service ever! Will never go there!!

It tasted good but the people who work there did not really know how to make it very well. It fell apart after the first bite. They werent friendly either, i would go again but with lower expectations.
Love the idea of large sushi rolls that are as filling as a burrito! Veggie option is delicious, however I with there was a tofu or other veggie option too! Maybe soon ;)

I grabbed a sandwich at JJ's the other day. It was decent, but nothing spectacular.

I had the 8" Italian on wheat bread. The ingredients were very fresh. I wish I would have known they didn't but mayo on it because I would have asked for some. Also, the dressing was on the light side. As good as the meat and bread tasted, I would have liked a little something to moisten it up some. Also, I wish instead of bread that they had a wheat hero option.

My other gripe is that chips are their only side item. In this day and age to not have a healthy option just doesn't make sense.

On the good side the service was good, the prices were chip, and it was a good sandwich, just lacking a few things that can easily be addressed.

Home of the Sushiritto, Hai Street Kitchen has got to be one of my favorite go to foods when I'm in the city. There are many choices to choose from which is awesome! I would say the Sushiritto is quite filling so you can always save it for later! The only thing I wish there was at the shop is more seating.
If you don't like sushi, you won't like this place. The seaweed wrap is xtra-stinky.  Definitely wished i had the 20 minutes back that i stood in line :-/

Normally Qdoba would get all the stars from me, but, well, this time, there was some ridiculousness involved...

I always go for the nachos - either shredded beef or chicken - and have my chips on the side. This may sound strange to people unfamiliar with Qdoba nachos, but trust me. They pile on SO much stuff, that it is impossible for you to eat it all before the chips go completely soggy.

Well, poor child at the register told me I could not have my chips on the side... EXCUSE THE EFF OUTTA ME... I've been getting them that way since the first Qdoba opened in Philadelphia, thankyouverymuch. So, she tells me the general manager said no. After a few seconds of mumbling about "what kinda nonsense..." the GM comes out from the back with another employee, and explains that some idiot was trying to eat them while they were driving, dropped them in their lap, and the queso was SOOOOO hot, that they had a car accident. So, for legal reasons, they have to put the cheese in a separate container. 

OK, put the cheese wherever you want, but I want my chips DRY. How hard is that to understand?

The damn things are delicious, though, so I have to rate it as A-OK... cuz as we all know, good food makes everything better.
No Surprise...As Advertised

Two words: CUSTOMER SERVICE! 

I love walking into a restaurant where the staff immediately greets you and offers menu suggestions when you seem a little lost. It was my first time here and I decided to go with a bowl over a burrito upon learning that there was more food in the bowls than the burrito! The bowl I got was called the shrimp avocado and it was super delicious. Very fresh ingredients and an equal protein to filler (rice, lettuce, veggies) ratio!
Great sandwiches/sliders for lunch. Great quality. Service was excellent. Huge order of fries with each sandwich. Definitely will stop by when I need lunch in University City again.

Here's the thing: a sushi burrito is a novel idea, the packaging is cute, the boxed water is trendy, but I just don't like it that much! The burrito is just too big... I think part of the appeal of sushi is that you're getting the whole taste of the roll in a single bite, and you just cannot do that with the sushi'ritto, unless you have a giant mouth and can manage to smoosh the roll somehow. I might have myself to blame for this, but every time I've been there, my burrito is kinda bland, and I can never, ever finish it - it's too much food for me. 

It's definitely something to say you've tried, and it's a novel idea, but the execution just doesn't live up for me,

love this place. I've been coming at least once every two weeks for a few months. the food is pretty incredible. the chef is a great guy, and every single thing I've ever ordered was amazing. every time I come, i'm stuck with the same quandry: get something i've had that I know is amazing, or try something new that will probably be amazing. 

and the bartender, kait, is awesome. she's so nice. she works really hard too, as a bartender and a waitress. but she just takes care of you and is genuine.

i like this place cause it's not crowded, the people are really nice, and i love the atmosphere. it's a very "homey," comfortable atmosphere.

this is my new spot, and i'll keep coming around.

I really enjoy jimmy johns. My favorite is the Beach Club. Their sandwiches are always fresh, service is fast, and the employees that work that have always been really cool. And I love that they are open until 3am since I always like late night snacks.
The most instagramworthy in all the city ! Go at least once and make your own sushi burrito. These things are surprisingly filling and are pretty well priced for sushi grade fish.

Went to the one in Sharon Hill today, ordered the food, but told them we'd be RIGHT back as we had a cheesteak to pick up at "Leos" (just 1/4 of a block down the road) & it was a very hot day outside so we didn't wanna have to wait in the car.( My husband has cancer & can't take the heat) We returned only to find that they hadn't even STARTED to make our sandwiches! They didn't even APOLOGISE! Hope that dead rat I saw by the dumptster didn't die from the food! NO lie!! This is what happens when white people go to a black establishment! Believe me! I've seen it MORE than once! Look up Sharon Hill,Pa.One of WORST towns in the U.S! 40 yrs ago was a beautiful little town!
The Mac and cheese rolls around in my mouth. The chicken is the most juiciest chicken I have ever tasted. Can't wait for seconds

This place was surprisingly good.  I was swinging by Philly and I decided to stop by and im glad I did.  It's basically an chipotle with an Asian twist.  I ordered the tuna while my friend ordered the salmon.  I prefer the salmon because it wasn't cut up as much as opposed to the tuna that was cut extremely fine.  The only negative may have been that there was a lot of vegetables but that's really nitpicking.  I would swing by again if I was in the area.
The food is good. the service is ok not great. But the big thing is that their bathrooms are nasty and dirty.

The dinning room is a disgrace, food and trash are everywhere and what's sad is I'm sure it sits like this all day and no one takes the intuitive to grab a broom and dustpan and clean up. Even where the condiment stand is where you get straws and napkins is dirty, this place is always out of condiments for to go orders and the lines are always long. I'm sure if the cashier would cut the gossiping to the food expediter in half the wait will also be cut in half. This Wendy's is disgraceful, I'd be ashamed to work here or even be caught eating in here. This place needs new effective management who takes pride it their place of business not some carefree bum who shows up for a paycheck. Just saying...

Whoever invented this sushi burrito is a genius. I ordered the chicken katsu, one of the popular items on the menu, and it was delicious. One of the girls who made the burrito was really friendly, which was good. Planning to get the tempura shrimp next time!

UPDATE: since my initial review, I have actually tried this place. I ordered and paid online to hasten the process, and I'm glad that I did because when I went to pick up my food, the line circled the dining room. I ordered the chicken shawarma basmati rice bowl with marinated onions and garlic sauce. Eh...the chicken lacked flavor, and was a little dry to me, and the rice was also missing something. I thought that the marinated onions would add flavor...not really. I ordered two falafel just to try and they were good, not better than Mama's Vegetarian, but good. The BEST thing that I had (from a $12 lunch) was the pita. The pita was GREAT! It was warm soft and fluffy and the reason I upgraded my review from 1 star to 3. Would I eat here again...probably not. I can get the same food better and cheaper elsewhere.

If you are looking for uncooked food, look no further than Qdoba across the street from Temple's campus. I was out of commission for nearly a week after eating one of their burritos. It was really tasty, but was not worth the pain and uncomfortably that I felt afterwards.

I visited Hai Street for the first time for lunch today, and was very pleased with the experience. A friend an I arrived at about 11:45 to find only one person in line in front of us (by the time we left at 12:30 or so, there was quite a line). We decided to split two sushi burritos (Slammin Salmon and Hai Street Chicken) and got the larger sizes (yay protein). The sushi burritos were made promptly, within a couple of minutes, and we were sent on our way. Luckily, because we had beat the lunch rush, there were several seats available at the bar by the window (only about 10 seats in the whole establishment), so we enjoyed our meal on site. 

All of the ingredients for the sushi were incredibly fresh and delicious. Additionally, except for the last couple of bites, the burritos held their structure very very well. The chicken on the Hai Street roll was crispy and flavorful, and the salmon was fresh and salmony tasting. A very good price bargain for the quantity of food and quality of ingredients. However, my complaint for the burrito roll (and a common complaint about burritos in general) is that it was hard to get a bit of each flavor in every bite. This is definitely not the fault of Hai Street... just the nature of a burrito. So some bites were sauce and salmon laden, and some were all rice. I think that I will definitely come back in the future to try more flavors and to use the "build your own" option, but I will stick with bowls or salads. The novelty of the sushi burrito was great, but I feel like a bowl would allow each bite to be more balanced, the way single bites of sushi are typically composed.

I come here twice a week. I love the salads! I wish they would get ranch dressing (only have peppercorn ranch.) I'm a fan of the tuna, quinoa & crab salad 

The hot buffet is yummy . Mac & cheese, fried chicken, beans & rice!
A good standby place, a lot of fresh vegetables, but also a lot of canned stuff. But, a great selection and variety.

I was pleasantly surprised by the sushi burrito.  I don't quite know what i was expecting but I think what I got was better then expected. 

I made my own burrito with white rice, salmon, guacamole/wasabe, red cabbage, cucumbers, and papaya salad topped with some spicy mayo and crunchy garlic.  This made for one very large sushi roll.  I have to say I feel like this was a perfect combo and if I were to go there again, I'd get this exact same thing. 

The total came out to $10 which at first I thought was a bit pricey but then again, it was filling and specialty rolls would run about that much or more so I'm thinking it might be a reasonable price.

(very little seating. maybe about 4 bar stools)

Wow this was unexpectedly delicious. Very clean. EXTREMELY nice, helpful staff. Decent amount of food. Ordered the chicken shawarma pita sandwich with garlic sauce, onions, pickles, and some other white sauce too. Amazingly fresh. Yellow rice was only so-so. Had naflava in sea salt and caramel (think sticky, crispy pastry with finely ground nuts) for dessert. Definitely getting that every time I go there. Highly recommend.
Good place for a quick fix on "munchie" type food. I've had breakfast there twice in the past month, great value!
The service is terrible. The food looks really unappetizing. The people who work there also seem to hate being there. I walk in starving and walk out craving Chipotle instead.

Pretty funny how I found out about this place. I was at QT vietnamese sandwich place and someone there was eating a sushi burrito from Hai Street. Thinking it was something on QT's menu, we asked him about it and he told us it was from Hai. I then added it to my list of eatries to try out. Recently went and I got the Crispy Shroom roll, and it was pretty good, however I want to try it with one of the spicier sauces next time though. I did add on the avocado for $2, which seems pretty pricey. I don't really like the practice of advertising one price and having so many add ons tacked on. But it was good, fast, convenient and I'll definitely try it again.

I loved the baked chicken and mac and cheese, so the food was good. The people here aren't the best. They're impersonal, even rude, and aren't helpful. If you decide to order here, don't expect great service. I would really need to be in the mood for he baked chicken to go back.

The city lacks in these types of places.  I gotta throw it 5 stars for what it is.. A takeout seafood joint that executes it niche perfectly.  If your coming here, your probably getting a lobster roll.. as you should be.  I prefer the warm one, but thats me.. crab cake was decent.. everything else was pretty good.. fresh..  The people who work there are really friendly and seem to go the extra mile.  It's priced right.. your not going to get lobster at McD's prices.  I dig.

Sushirittos are amazing. I got the salmon with extra salmon. It's pricey at $14, but hey so is sushi anywhere you go right?

The salmon was very fresh and buttery!

3.5 stars

My first sushi burrito! I went around 6:30pm on a Saturday and there was basically no line, which was nice. I had the Slammin Salmon roll. Decent size but I think it's kind of expensive for what it is. However, it was good quality and the pickled jicama added an interesting texture. I'll probably try out a few other sushi places in Philly before returning.
The security guy Joey is super helpful. He made sure my phone didn't get stolen while it was charging.

I'm a big fan of this place. It is much less crowded than the Chipotle around the corner on Walnut. I normally order a steak or chicken quesadilla. Both are excellent. And on the rare occasion I indulge in a dessert, the chocolate chip cookies are also quite good.

What's more, I often order double meat on my entree, and I would say at least half the time the staff does not bother to charge me for the second portion of meat, which is a great deal.

Really pleased with this place. Went looking for a quick place to get some asian food and was really pleased when I found Hai Street. Having Steak/Pork/Chicken on the menu is really nice for those who can't stomach uncooked fish. Super happy with this place, service is great and the menu is unique and delicious. Only thing is that it can get a bit pricey. (avg. $10+)

Last night at around 1am a small group of friends and I visited on our way home. My friend wanted pizza so crossed the street while we waited in line. As I was ordering about $50 worth of chicken for our group my friend returned with his slice of pizza. He was simply holding it while we were in line. Between ordering and paying I playfully nibbled at the tip of his slice of pizza hanging off of the plate. A stuffy looking dude barked at us that now he had to kick us out because we couldnt consume outside food or drink. At first I thought he was joking but soon realized that no, he was actually just a dick with the inability to discern policy from practice. Look, I could see if we were a roudy after hours crew or if we were being loud, rude or disrespectful. We never had the intent to consume any outside food, and I had literally just ordered $50+ worth of food. The employee was simply cranky and rude. There are just too many options in this area for anyone to put up with snarky or poor service. Do better. Until then, we wont be back.

At Hai Street Kitchen & Co, sushi and burritos have put  aside their differences and joined together to together to create a super force set for food domination. City of Brotherly Love indeed.

I had seen the concept executed well in San Francisco, but never have seen anything like this on the East Coast so I was very intrigued. 

When I arrived I had no idea what to order, there were plenty of choices and I had just one stomach. Le sigh! The friendly counter person said that the salmon was the most popular on the menu but his personal favorite was the chicken katsu. I was sold. It was topped with a teriyaki sauce, romaine lettuce, red onion, red cabbage and green papaya salad. And because I'm fat like that, I added some wasabi guacomole and fried shallots on top as well...as well as a side of freshly made tempura corn.

I was happy with the size of my sushirrito, it was not too big and not too small. However, I found it a bit dry and lacking of flavor I ate all the chicken inside before giving up. Perhaps I should have gotten the salmon instead.

The tempura corn on the other hand completely satiated my hunger for all things salty and fried. Those little buggers are addictive and before I knew it my little paper box was just a small puddle of oil.

An interesting concept that works! It's designed like a Chipotle/Qdoba where you see all the ingredients and you watch them make it. It's clean and the roll I ordered was really tasty! I got their Mexican porkbelly with brown rice, lettuce, cabbage, carrots, spicy mayo and yucca chips for a nice crunch. I'm definitely getting this combination again. You have a choice between making your own or picking from a menu. I don't think this location has a lot of exposure, but I will be coming back for more.

I tend not to expect much more than the standard quality from Qdoba, and that keeps my expectations at a manageable level so I am not disappointed. I would say this  location lives up to those standards. Nothing has blown me out of the water about them, but every burrito and bowl I've gotten has been just that- standard, tasty and undisappointing. If that's a word.

The servers at this Qdoba aren't very enthusiastic. I haven't come across one who gave excellent customer service, asked us how we were or seemed like he or she wanted to be there. I guess that's fine, but to keep me thrilled to keep coming back to a fast food Mexican chain, I'd like a little flair to my experience.

Qdoba does have a nice rewards program that my boyfriend signed up for. And Tuesday is double points day. So we come most Tuesdays, and that's that. Enough Qdoba for anyone, I'd say. But they're keeping it consistent, so Tuesdays it is!

I really like the concept of this place. This is a good spot to hit up for a quick and easy but tasty meal (also good for a quick beer). I was loving their ginormous selection of bottle craft beers, especially since you don't see a lot of those beers sold in other restaurants. I had the Southern chicken sandwich and was really impressed. The chicken was moist and tender and I really liked the slaw on the sandwich. The jam added a little bit of sweetness that balanced out the salty from the fried chicken and the slaw. I was not as impressed by the mac and cheese.. it appeared a little dry and burnt. Other than that, everything else is fantastic!
Chicken is always good but the cashiers and attendants need a better training at customer service.

In England, naff is not a compliment. You don't want to hear 'That was naff.' about your food or service. My visit to Naf Naf Grill yesterday was ironic in that all I could think afterward was 'They should rename themselves, Naff Naff Grill.'

Where was the manager? The assembly of bowls, Chipotle-style, looked like they had four new staff on the line who had all just started. More backups than the Schuylkill heading west out of Philly on a Friday afternoon.

Four people, shoulder to shoulder, getting frustrated with each other.

No pita bread. Yes, no pita bread. For a middle eastern restaurant, that's McDonald's without buns, an English fish and chip shop without potatoes. As SNL asks; Really?

No falafel. Stand to the side please, it's cooking. We can serve those who want steak or chicken with their hummus, but we ran out of falafel. Really?2

Bowl assembly person 1 "Sorry, because we have no pita, we'll give you some fries, instead." 
Bowl assembly persons 2, 3, and 4, and the cashier - no one added fries to the half-empty bowl of hummus and salad (No falafel or pita, now no fries either.) Really?3

The hummus was good. Not $7.95 good, though. 
Amateur hour at the Naff Naff Grill.

First time here, I like the idea a lot but I'm not sure if it's just me or if I just prefer bites of sushi better. Would recommend for a try to see yourself. The service was friendly and the food was good but not craving worthy in my book.

So the good news first: they no longer charge extra for guacamole.

Bad news: they charge extra to wrap the burrito in an extra tortilla if the first one breaks or doesn't get rolled properly by them the first time. Incredible. It is not as if I had asked for more than my fair share of fillings - it was a normal burrito and the lady rolling it didn't roll it properly and it started to burst its sides. I have no issues with this, rolling a burrito can be a tricky task. But when I said you could just put it inside another tortilla and I'll take it, I was told that I would have to pay extra for it!! @#$@!@#$

Anyway, I maintain that with Chipotle a hop skip and jump away, why anyone would eat at Qdoba is beyond me. I went here because I was at the post office next door and because the line at the post office ate up most of my break, I ended up with only 5 minutes to pick up food.
Greeted with a smile. Served with gusto. the only thing is, they got my order wrong. I wanted salmon and they gave me shrimp.. so one star less.

the food is still delicious! no denying about that! but the price took me by surprise today.  i ordered 3 wings and a scoop of mac and cheese (heard it was phenomenal) and it came to a total of $9.10!  tbh, i almost wanted to say "take it back!".  

while i think the wings are maybe worth it. the mac and cheese, on the other hand, is no doubt a little too much for me.  again, it is very tasty! but the price needs to come down a little bit... the chicken is $8.95 /lb and the mac n cheese is also $8.95/lb...? basically i would choose chicken every time if i only got $9 to spare.  forget about half and half.  also, smaller containers would help manage the weight of the mac & cheese.. it's so dense! i don't need more than 1/3 of a lb of mac and cheese.

it's gonna be a while before i return back to wishbone :(

This is probably the slowest McDonalds I have ever been to. The people who work here dont care at all about anything. They love to give stank looks ESPECIALLY if you try to pull out the app to use a damn coupon. They are lazy and slow and management should be ashamed. They need some undercover boss up in this establishment, such an inconvenience to go here. Go to Wendys across the street, or better yet Chick fila!

So glad sushirittos have come to Philly!  The concept is identical to Chipotle but think Japanese. I ordered the chicken katsu and it was delicious. Lots of flavor and everything just worked. Definitely add wasabi guac,  makes it 10 times better.

I was so excited to try this place.  Love sushi and love burritos. Every bite of my crunch burrito ( shrimp tempura, spicy mayo, pickled mango, cucumber, and lettuce) was delicious. I was sad to see the meal end. I shared corn tempura side and chips and wasabi guacamole. The food was super fresh and fabulous. Dreaming about when I can go back already.

Loved this place! Very different, but being a big burrito and sushi fan figured I would check it out. Me and my friend each ordered one and split it. My favorite was the screaming tuna (i believe it was called aka a spicy tuna variation). It was soo good! I also tried the slammin' salmon, but preferred the tuna for some reason. Both were good though! I also went for the chips with the wasabi guacamole. The chips were ok, but the wasabi guacamole was awesome! Will definitely be returning.

I don't know how many locations they have, but damn.....their stuff is delicious! My friend brought me here after a night out drinking. Their fried chicken is good, but you definitely need some of that dipping sauce they charge you for. Their Mac & Cheese is incredible. The line was very long, but it move quickly. I'm curious to see what this place is like during the day, and when there aren't a whole lot of drunks there. I'm totally bummed that I didn't get to try their corn bread. Next time i guess. Chicken is crispy. Mac & Cheese i full of flavor.

I would have totally given his place 4 stars, but as someone who cares about the environment...they've failed. They don't care whether you take it to go or eat there. They rush you through the line and bag every single order into a large plastic bag. I noticed that most people ate there, and tossed all of the containers and bags into the trash. They could be more environmentally conscious and not give out bags, especially when it goes into the trash minutes later. It's the Californian in me.

If you like sushi, this is basically burrito sized sushi, but messier. It's definitely a meal that calls for napkins: unlike a traditional burrito, this is just an open ended roll, so ingredients tend to fall out. Depending on what combo you get, it can also be a little mushy. Very tasty though.
My main issue is that they sometimes get the order wrong or sub ingredients without asking. They put breaded chicken in my order unexpectedly (breading = gluten). My coworker who got an order at the same time had a completely different order than what she'd paid for. Definitely double check what you get.

This place is the most horrendous sandwich in the world. Literally heaps of mayonnaise on top of low grade deli cuts. To top it all of, the worst bread ever.  They even have the nerve to sell day old bread. You couldn't pay me to eat this garbage. It doesn't get much worse than Jimmy Johns. Anyone who tells you otherwise is delirious.

Awesome place, Very friendly Staff.

At first, I saw the assembly line style food set up and I was skeptical, but:

The Prices are very inexpensive, and you get SOOO much food.  The food tastes very good too.  The Nachos, Quesadillas , Burritos are HUGE! 

My favorite is the Chicken Three Cheese Nachos, it is like 2 meals worth and its only like $6.25!

Sushi meets a burrito ...  yesssss :-) Absolutely love this place.Eat here every week - great place for lunch on the go. First time I went generic and got the Slammin Salmon (it was terrific). Now I switch it up and create my own. Everything is delicious, but I highly recommend getting the spicy gochujang, black pepper teriyaki, wasabi guac, and pickled mango as ingredients. Get creative - you won't regret it ... and get a bowl sometime - they are equally delicious.

Yay Buckminsters! Welcome to Point Breeze! I tried to stop in Buckmister's on their opening day, but it looked way too busy. However, I was able to make it about a week later. 

Drinks: I had both the Passyunk Zeke and the McQueen cocktails. Both were delicious and would totally be willing to drink either of them again (and multiple of them). My only complaint was the bartender who made my Passyunk Zeke left a solid inch and a half at the top of my glass and I thought it should be filled more. Given that it's a new place and they probably haven't made the cocktails a bunch yet, I'm willing to forgive and try it again soon. 

Food: seems like the menu changes pretty frequently, which I enjoy. I had the parsnip fries, which were delicious. They're not small-cut like your typical fries, but larger pieces of 'tater that are excellently seasoned. For the main meal, I had the pork and apples. Perhaps a bit of a small portion, but the meat was very tender and I had great flavor!

Absolutely delicious! Such a simple concept, perfectly executed. It's Sushi chipotle style! :)
Will definitely come back. Ordered the salmon and chicken, loved them both.

My boyfriend knows how much I love sushi, thought I'd love this too, and he was totally right! He had told the staff that he was about to get on a flight from Philly to Nashville to bring me two sushi burritos and they were extremely friendly and helpful in packaging them for me so they stayed fresh. He bought a hai street chicken burrito and a ho-lee shrimp burrito, both deep fried. I don't typically like meat in my sushi, but the hai street chicken burrito was amazing. And the holee shrimp burrito was as good as a shrimp tempura roll, but actually better. Best part? Even after a 2.5 hour flight, they were both still so good! I have him bring this to me every time he flies in from Philly now, I love this place!

Nice for the novelty factor, but probably wouldn't eat on a regular basis. There was a surprisingly generous amount of filling (I had the Ho-Lee Shrimp) and it was very satisfying. Ingredients were fresh too.

"How do you do this to food?"

"It's magic."

How do you make it taste so extraordinarily good? 

Genius. 

Like its namesake Buckminster Fuller (do yourself a favor and Google him before you go), pure genius. Like all genius, somewhat idiosyncratic and delightfully unique. 

I'm going to name check the squid, the broccoli, the cauliflower (get both cruciforms at their apotheosis), the Masaman curry, the muthaf*ckin chicken Marsala--ask about the sauce--ingenious. Washed down with house lavender gin & tonics. Get the hay-infused flan because, hey, when's the last time you had something with hay? It was my first time and it made me feel like I was grass feed and free range. 

Genius + Love = Buckminster 

Clearly, there is love in that kitchen and it goes into the food. I feel like I've been ravished by a new lover.

No, no and no..... perhaps they should ship their crew to California to retrain on how to make a proper 'sushi burrito'. I've tasted much better ones on the West Coast. The concept is neat, as is the packaging but the overall execution is poorly done by Hai Street. 

The sushi rice was dry, undercooked and not up to the standards of sushi rice. When you can't get the rice right, it's a downhill battle to redeem the rest of the food. 

As for the tuna in the tuna roll, there was the equivalent of a teaspoon of tuna in the entire roll.  (seriously...?!).  

No thanks.  I prefer Chipotle anytime over this.

Qdoba, I really want to like you more than Chipotle. You have more options, plus my favorite thing ever: queso sauce.  The thing is, you're just not as tasty as Chipotle.  Qdoba's rice and chicken just simply don't have as much flavor as Chipotle.  No matter how much delicious queso sauce I put on my chicken burrito, it just isn't as flavorful as it should be considering all the stuff I put into my burrito.  Now, this obviously doesn't stop me from enjoying a chicken queso burrito from Qdoba because, despite the fact that it's not as flavorful as it should be, it's still pretty good.  However, with a Chipotle opening up a mere block away (kinda weird right?), I'm not sure how often I'll be going to Qdoba anymore.

Interesting concept, hard to eat though. The burritos are huge and are packed full with the protein and veggies. I got the Ho-Lee Shrimp and it was good but could have used more sauce- I should have asked for more on the side. The shredded beets were an interesting addition to the usual fillings within a sushi roll. It's similar to eating a Chipotle burrito, you can never get a bite of all the fillings because the burrito is too big to eat in one bite. The location is small and there is limited seating but I appreciate how there is an abundance of outlets.

Why does anyone like this stuff?  It always makes me feel sick, and it's overpriced for an inferior product (like any major fast food chain).  If you need to stick to the neighborhood, you're much better off going to one of the food carts around Penn for a filling burrito at half the price.

While I've had Jimmy John's on several occasions by now, I've never actually stopped in until last night. The place is branded in a really fun in-your-face kind of way that I think adds to the appeal.

As for the sandwiches, I've only had good experiences so far. Everything is fresh, service is fast, they're open late, prices are reasonable-- nothing mind-blowing here, but they don't get anything wrong which puts them ahead of most.

Amazing quality and great prices! Lots of great options to choose from for proteins, toppings and sauces. The Matcha Green Tea is also perfect, and lightly sweetened. Staff was very nice, restaurant clean.

It's hard to rate salad, but this salad, lettuce, tomatoes, olives and all was very fresh and tasty.  That being said, I especially like the Quinoa Salad that I added to my plate. It was very tasty. I would definitely go back there if I am ever back in Philly.

I've been coming here for years just for the bbq wings. They are so addictive. I'll usually get about 2lbs to bring home and share with the family. Nothing else here looks appetizing enough for me though.

My go-to place in western Center City for omelettes, breakfast sandwiches, cheeseburgers, cheesesteaks, etc. Nothing fussy, just standard diner restaurant food. And not too greasy. Dining-in is a no frills experience, which I actually prefer; just give me my food and let me eat in peace. Places like this are a dying breed in Center City. I'm glad Tony's is still around.

I wish I could give minus stars.  The chicken sandwich was horrible.  Month old lettuce in my fridge is less wilted.  The roll was chewy and chicken hard from the microwave,  The fries were under cooked.  This happened once before.  Obviously not a fluke.
i cant speak for the franks.  but, those bbq glazed baked chicken wings are outta this world.  try it...  pretty damn amazing.

First off it is obvious that they can not handle the traffic that comes with this location. I faced over my order for 2 salads on their own form but they didn't have my order ready upon arrival (and they had almost an hour to do so). Next when I get there they have to make the order and she makes one salad and wants to argue me down about the second one that was on the fax... Fed up I just took the one. I will not be going to this location anymore. Not worth the time or aggravation.

I literally stumbled across this place during pride and was so amazed! The atmosphere is so great. Jamin Music at like 11 pm. A whole wall of different beers and ciders a la The foodery. The chicken is what people come for. It's good. Is it the best? Nah. But the whole experience is so great that you can kinda overlook it. They have different dipping sauces and sides that work really well with the chicken. I have been to another location on Penns campus. Super cute location without the beer wall.

I've never written a yelp review before, but this was by far the worst tasting food I have ever had and I didn't want anyone else's money and time to be wasted like our's was. I went to this restaurant hungry and excited on Friday night because the reviews were so good but I was severely disappointed. The restaurant was clean, the food looked good aesthetically, which is why I'll generously give two stars but the food tasted so bland and horrible. We got about $30 worth of food and left after eating a few bites because it was so bad. The mac & cheese, the wings, and the chicken strips were atrocious. The only bearable item was the potato salad that still had too much horse radish. If you go here, I really think you will be disappointed as well.

I have been going to Mama's for falafel sandwiches and when this place opened up I was hesitant first but I finally made it there n loved the idea of having rice or couscous bowl with all sorts of fresh toppings and sauces. I thought the food was good and falafel was cooked properly. BUT as any other franchise food goes, the quality tends to deter as time goes on. Last 2 times I went Falafel looked cooked but when you bite into it, it's actually RAW which isn't really appetizing and not good for your stomach. I think they are cooking at a high temp to fast track the process and not letting it cook on right temperature all the way as its suppose to. I don't think I will be going back there even for their rice and couscous. I will walk another block and go to Mama's.

If there's anything that RTM is lacking, in my opinion, is good, fresh to-go salad options (I do realize there are some pre-made options out there). Tootsie's is just what it states - hot & cold buffet, quickly.

I stopped by a little after 3pm on a weekday and got myself a nice container full of salad. There was nothing fancy, no crazy cheese options, just enough to make a solid garden salad. The place was clean, the food was plentiful and the line was short. Signage states the produce is from Iovine Brothers, which is a plus.

I did scope out the hot food options (I guess you can mix and match) but nothing that looked too appealing to me - lots of starch and fried foods.

One thing to note is that the picture for this place is out of date, I believe they are up to $6.69/lb.

Who doesn't love this place?!

I think this particular location is priced a little higher. but when your drunk, and hungry, who caressss! I will pay 10 bucks for crab fries EASY.

There is virtually never a line, and when you do order your food you never have to wait long. I say if you come into Xfinity, eat here!

Went in here more than an hour before closing just to be told they didn't have chicken or steak at the time. On top of it, workers are so rude, they act like they're doing you a favor. But the customer service department is on top of it and replied quickly to my email. I'll give them another shot at a different location.

Came here for the first time last night, from Reading. Totally worth the long drive. Easy to park because it's in the Northeast. The place wasn't too busy, so were able to order right away. Ample seating with several large TVs. I got the classic wings combo, half lemon pepper (figured I'd have to give Rick Ross' favorite a try) and half mild along with the seasoned fries. There is a hotness scale on the menu with the approximately 10 flavors to choose from. I don't have a preference, but I saw from looking at the online ordering that you can specify all flats or all drumsticks. You can see the food being made through the window along the side area seating. They don't use heat lamps and everything is cooked to order. So it did take just about 20 minutes to get our food, but it was well worth the wait. They brought our order to the table. Wings tasted amazing, they weren't huge but I wouldn't call them small either. They were nice and crispy, not soggy or rubbery. The fries were like nothing I've ever had. They weren't made from sweet potatoes, but they had this slightly sweet flavor. The seasoning is optional, but I would definitely recommend getting it. I don't usually crave fries or even eat all of them, but I couldn't get enough of these. And fortunately, they give you a *lot* of them. I'm not a dip person, but there was like four dips to choose from as well. Soda fountain was in the seating area so no worries if you go for the "atomic" flavored wings. The price of the combo with a drink was $10, very reasonable imo. Staff was very friendly too, she chatted with us before we left. Felt like a safe area, saw a PPD van slowly cruise past the storefronts in this shopping center and across the street. Wish this place was closer to home but they are about to open a location in Allentown as well. This location has only been open for a month or so. All in all, very good but skip it if you are in a rush or only like jumbo sized wings.

Came here with a small group after a Yelp event. Plenty of room on a Sunday evening. They offered small , interesting food options that met all of our different needs, from Vegan to Bacon. 

I ordered the little pork on an English muffin sandwich , which I was told was all house made. It was delicious and the price was right. I should have ordered 3. Ha!

I was impressed at their beer selection, specifically they had a beer from my favorite local brewery St Benjamin's. 

Overall, between the food , drink and company, we had a fantastic time and the one who suggested coming here was feeling pretty good about her choice.

Special props to our bartender Jalissa , who was  really friendly, knowledgable and attentive. You couldn't have asked more from her.

We came in with 12 people at 10am. Our waitress had no other tables. We waited with menus for 15 minutes with no water or coffee. We asked for coffee and she was like "So... you're ready to order?" and got all huffy when we said that we were still waiting for two people and we would like drinks. Apparently, you only get two cups of coffee? I must have missed that on their gigantic menu. I love diners but our server obviously hated her job.
please make another location somewhere in north philly, preferably nor libs or fishtown. i would order delivery every night.

Good food at a great price!  Got the chicken Bahn Mi and the smores tart.  Both were delicious!!  

Menu was diverse with a great selection of homemade baked goodies too!

Maybe I had really high expectations or I've been spoiled by good sushi or I just got a bad batch but I'm pretty disappointed. 

My friend and I saw the menu and we're amazed by the idea of a giant sushi roll/burrito and how it incorporated some Korean elements too. I got the slamming salmon with brown rice and my friend made her own.  The rice ended up being so sour (too much rice vinegar?) and all the gochujang sauce was unevenly distributed that I couldn't finish it.

Another downside is there's not enough seating. I understand it's a small place though. There were also twoo tables outside but no seats...so everyone was just standing around it.

The plus side is that the fish IS really fresh and the portions are extremely filling. I like the interior decoration as well.

Sushi buuuurrrrrittttoooo. I love the concept. Just like chipotle, subway and all the other build it how you want it chains- you start with rice and a protein and pile on all the veggies, sauces, crunchy fried toppings and whatever else your heart desires. My husband and I shared a Ho-lee shrimp with shrimp tempura, spicy mayo, asian slaw, beets and garlic fried crunchy bits. I subbed carrots for the beets because I feel like beets overpower everything. We also got a Flamin Tuna with yellowfin tuna tartar, gochugang, romaine, carrot, beets, avocado salsa and crunchy green onion. We subbed the beets for cucumbers. The idea was to get 2 different kinds and split them. I didn't realize they would be so huge! I ate my half of the Ho-lee shrimp and I was stuffed. I tried a bite of the tuna and it was really good- I was just too full. If we hadn't put the fried green onions in it, I feel like the integrity of the burrito would have held up just fine. My hubby ended up eating it later in the evening, but of course the onions weren't crunchy anymore.  I felt like there was a good ratio of meat to veggies but my hubby felt like he should have asked for double protein. It's a solid spot to grab a quicj bite to eat. Come hungry!
