t never fails. every other time we go something is wrong or missing...you go there takes 3 people to place 1 order..including the supervisor.. you place and order and something is wrong or left out..asked for mixed reg and spicy got all regular asked for side of small mashed potatoes..get home ..ta da no potatoes!! i mean this is not rocket science people..and fast food workers want $15 and hr?!??! The chicken is ok..but they need to drink some wake up or energy drink they are all half asleep!!

I made and error and may have posted this to the wrong location..the location for the bad service is 800 Broad near ave of the arts..not the one at broad and snyder..

They need a Hai Street Kitchen & Co. (or an equivalent) in New Jersey/New York.

Atmosphere: Chipotle, but for sushi-like foods. 

Food: Slammin' Salmon, at the regular size. It's already pretty damn large, so I can't imagine what the gozilla looks like. Anyway, fish was fresh, not too much rice, and an amazing amount of crunch with the cucumbers/romaine/jicama/cabbage. Also, that gochujang sauce is tangy with just the right amount of spice, and it really made the flavor of the roll. I finished it and felt perfectly content. Got the hibiscus ice tea, which was just okay. But the sweet green tea is great if you're a fan of matcha. You'll be paying about 10-12 for your roll, which is pretty decent.
The drive-thru workers are rude and incompetent. There was a hair in my sandwich. Enough said.

This place is awesome.  My fandom in wings has never been huge.  Of course I shared the occasional wings with friends during Eagles games, split wings as an appetizer with my girlfriend, even ordered wings from local pizza places from time to time.  But this is different.

I find sometimes ordering wings from places you never know what you're going to get.  Dried, lackluster meatless wings with no originality are usually what I come across, not here.  Juicy, meaty wings every single time.  I have been here three times since it's opened and I've enjoyed it each time.  I like to try different wing sauces each time I go.  Also the fries are amazing.  Unbelievably  good.

I really really like Jimmy John's sandwiches!! The ingredients are sooo fresh and they use real hellman's mayonaisse! I always get the Turkey Tom but I have also sampled the Vegetarian which surprisingly... I liked!  The staff is really upbeat and your sandwich is made in less than three minutes...lol  JJ's is also pretty cheap, a sandwich is just about $5 which is hard to beat!

I was skeptical about a sushi burrito but I'm now a fan. The sushi was fresh and the staff on Wednesday night were great. Informative and helpful in making my selection. I deleted a few items from the standard burrito that I chose and they offered to substitute something else. I added extra tuna for $2.50 which was a good choice. Two sushi burritos and 2 sodas cane to $27.00. Definitely give this place a try.

No, no, do not go! Food tastes bad. We both tossed salad bowls after just a few bites. Steak has a funky seasoned coating on it... chicken bland and not fresh. The only edible item was the warm pitas that accompanied the salad. With so many great center city options, this was such a disappointing meal.

This is heaven. A burrito with sushi in it... brilliant. I had the spicy sushi grade tuna with carrots, cucumber, and white rice topped w soy sauce. It was divine. Perfect portion and I had very little leftover. Very reasonably priced and super fresh. Next time I'm in Philly, I will be eating here for sure!

I really appreciate the extra mile they went for me here I normally don't like the Wendy's bun taste a little fishy to me probably nothing wrong with it because it's just the way the bun is but I mentioned it and they offered me the bun from the number 9 item on the menu the chicken sandwich with the burger and there was much appreciated and while it's not a normal thing still I recommend eating here.

So I get what they are trying to do here but the problem is unless the cuisine is a novelty for you then it is really nothing great. The food is just ok. They are applying a subway style fast food approach to middle eastern food. That is what you are getting fast food. The problem lies in the fact that there are numerous carts on the surrounding streets doing similar food much better. I opted to try their steak shawarma. The meat was not very flavorful but the hummus they rimmed the bowl with was pretty solid. The rest of the pick what you want topics are pretty mild in flavor. Not the best but not terrible, middle of the road which is what I expect from a fast food place. Also being asked if I would like it "Naf it up!" is a lame phrase for combo adding sides like fries. I feel sorry for ever staff member that has to repeat that line all day.

Super obsessed with the rice bowls! I get the katsu chicken with wasabi guacamole, veggies, and spicy mayo. I work right up the street and since learning about this place I come here at least twice a week! Everything is so fresh and delish! Get the lemonade and hibiscus juice mixed, you won't be disappointed. So happy Rittenhouse has so many different food options,and this is one of the best if you're looking so something different!

I lover this place, I come here all the time to stuff my face after I leave the bar. It is great, you can drink here as well. Just read the other reviews you will see that it is perfectly acceptable to drink till the elephants fly.... I want to personally apologize to the families I may bother but hey it's gonna happen..... I'm an old man and I can't remember where I parked my car half the time so give me a break already. EH.... MMMMM Fried Chicken in my belly-yeah it eat.

I liked it. I went on a cold, dark, winter's night and it was very nice. I had a few good beers with my friends and the shared plates were good. I loved my dish, the curry, the most. While the food was satisfying, I didn't feel physically comfortable to be honest. It felt cold and hard to me. Maybe in the warmer months it will soften a little. I also would love an after-work happy hour rather than the late night version, but I realize we can't have everything. It's just nice to have a new place in the neighborhood.

First time having a sushi burrito. Did not disappoint! I built my own burrito with salmon, mixed greens, papaya, carrots, cucumber, onions, and tempura bits. Staff were really friendly. They also serve pokè now.
You want to see what is wrong with America?   Come here anytime of the week.  Inbreeding gone bad...

Good but nothing really special. The biscuits were my favorite part of the meal, and the only thing I can say is unique and worth going back for. The chicken was good, but once again no better than other chicken based restaurants I've been to in NY & Philly. I'm more keen on foghorn, andys, or Popeyes (if you don't care about putting on airs).

I was very unimpressed with the food at Buckminsters. If you're going here for dinner, don't. Unless  you've had gastric bypass and have the stomach of a goldfish. If you're looking for a nice cocktail and small plates that look like modern art.....by all means. I however will never return to this place for the simple fact that I could have spent the same money in a Stephen Starr restaurant and been satisfied. Sorry Buckminsters, good cocktails won't get me back in the door.

I found nothing wrong with Jimmy John's, but I don't understand the love.  It was a very ordinary sandwich.  I got the sandwich because Hummus nearby was closed for labor day.  If I come back, it will be for a similar reason.  I would not go out of my way to avoid returning here, but nor would I go out of my way to get another sandwich.

My experience at the Locust Street location was similar.

Plusses: Cost was under $5, sandwich was delivered instantaneously.
Minuses: None.

Had the chili dog.  If you're a fan of a true Coney Dog their chili will be too thick and meaty for you.  However, if you don't have any idea what a Coney Dog is then you'll be fine.  The Pierogies on the other hand were very original and tasty.  Could go back for those as a snack by itself.  Be sure to ask for sour cream or some other condiment because unless you ask you ain't getting it.
The only thing I enjoyed was the biscuit. My fries were burnt, and the chicken tenders had a very odd taste. Never again.
Definitely my favorite center city hoagie shop! They always have good service, prices, and quality of ingredients for hoagies and soup.
Got their chicken caprese sandwich. SOOOO delicious!!! Friendly staff too. Hope to be back again
Great place!!!! I left my debit card there and the staff was super nice and helpful!!!!!

I actually work at the Radian (the building in which this Jimmy John's is located), so I've had my fair share of JJ sangwiches for lunch this year.  My fave is the #9 - the Italian Night Club.  

Being from Philly, there's this whole Hoagie vs. Sub debate going on, and I'd call the sandwiches at JJ's "Subs," not Hoagies.  There is nothing authentic about them in the true Hoagie sense of the word, but that doesn't stop them from being delicious.  They definitely hit the spot.  The bread is particularly delish, and makes our lobby smell nice in the mornings  :)

This is a chain, but these guys score big on presentation... very attractive shop for being such a tiny space, with cute signage and fun, gimicky logos everywhere.   And service is good... the people working in there are very nice and service is at lightning speed - Like I said, I go for lunch all the time, and it's basically never crowded, so I've never waited longer than 60 seconds for a sammy.  Don't know what it's like at night time, tho.

I'm actually going to miss having them so close, as Wednesday will be my last day working at the Radian.  They are what your standard lunch spot should be - clean, friendly, fast, cheap, and yummy.
Had the Shrimp tempura roll.  Fantastic flavor - well seasoned, great portion.  Love this place - really original take on old ideas.

I can't even believe that I'm coming clean with this.  I've been shamefully sneaking off to this place in the middle of the Reading Terminal Market the same way your man creeps out of my place at 6 AM.  Head down, shades, throwing some side eye...but secretly feeling pretty damn good.

What's making me feel so good, you ask?  Well, it's not the creepy ass lima beans, or old man ham and cabbage.  The salad bar?  Eh, I could take or leave.  No, there's only one thing for me here.  One nasty, nasty thing.  Fried whiting.  Ohmygod.  Such fried deliciousness.  I never ever liked fried seafood, so I have no idea what possessed me to swing that way one day.  Just to make it extra gross, I like to add a nice mixture of "tartar" and cocktail sauce.  Oh, it makes me feel like so dirty inside...but at the same time...so satisfied.  And cheap.  I mean, the food, not me.  Ok, maybe me.  But I can regularly get a full fix of the good stuff here for under $3.50.

I know Reading Terminal has a plethora of yummy. wholesome, good for the world vendors.  I'm not saying you shouldn't go to them most of the time.  But every once in a while, don't be scared to unleash your inner freak and make some sinful mouth love here.

***Disclaimer:  Your man is not actually creeping out of my house at any hour.  If he were, I probably wouldn't have to drown my sorrows in fried fish.***

I tried this place out of curiosity and was pleasantly surprised. I had the philly steak wrap with the teriyaki pepper sauce and it was very good. My only objection is that the staff could have been more friendly.

Me and my hubby were here 2 days ago trying their wings. We found their menu a little on the expensive side for wings. My hubby got the 6 wings combo with 2 flavors and fries. He ordered Teriyaki and BBQ flavored wings. He loved the whole combo and swear he will return for more wings next time. Well, I only want a snack so I ordered the smallest amount of wings possible, which is 8 pieces with 2 flavors. I try the Hawaiian and the Buffalo flavors. The Hawaiian wings are very tangy and the buffalo wings are not spicy enough compare to the domoinos wings. Our bill was $17.00 and we waited nearly half an hour in an empty restaurant. I wasn't satisfied with my snack but my hubby was. I guess I will try WS again to give another try.

This place it amazing! If you're like me and use urban spoon to find the best places to eat, I can tell you that this is the greatest place to go. I got salmon, black pepper teriyaki sauce, carrots, cucumbers, grilled zucchini, papaya salad, and avocado salsa in a brown rice wrap. It was absolutely delicious!! Warning: Hai Kitchen is expensive, like $8-$10 a burrito (not including chips or drinks). Very clean, fast service, and extremely filling. Well worth going AT LEAST once for the experience, worth going back again and again for everything else :)

Greatly disappointed.  I was really excited about the concept and had been waiting to try Hai St. since it opened.  However, it fell really flat.  To start, the space is really cramped and there is only seating for four so unless you are comfortable awkwardly standing while eating close to someone, this is basically a carry out place.  The music choice was a little edgy for an eatery too.  Nothing against rap, but hearing Rick Ross and Kendrick Lamar made me feel like I was in Foot Locker, not a dining establishment.   The food was mediocre and really overpriced.  I ordered the sumo steak and expected at least the meat to be hot, which it wasn't.  I couldn't taste the onion, and the asparagus really didn't go that well with all of the other ingredients.  The portion size was minute and only really worth half of what I payed.  I've had worse, but I've also had much better.

I stop by Tootsie's usually when I forget to pack a lunch and need to grab something healthy-ish. Disclaimer is that I rarely have eaten from the hot food bar and mostly stick to salads. 

This place can be very busy at lunch time, but I appreciate that they are always properly staffed and usually have one or two staff members cleaning up messes at the buffet and refilling items. I'm disappointed that in the last few years since I've been working near by, the prices have increase to what I feel like now is almost unreasonable for salad. Another thing that bothers me is that they cut the veggies HUGE so that your salad weighs more. Like, for example, the tomatoes are cut in fourths. 

Overall, it's a decent place for a quick lunch.
Pretty good for this new burrito sushi concept, a bit pricy at 8 dollars and above but def enough for a meal. The Katsu pork did better than salmon in the burrito interestingly

A fun lunch option!  I got the crunchy shrimp roll.  It ended up being much larger than anticipated.  It tasted great, but it was a little difficult to eat (I also have trouble eating normal wraps &hoagies).  Be sure to eat your sushi roll with a napkin and fork near by.  I felt full after eating the sushi burrito.  I would absolutely go back and try a customized burrito.

I was surprised--I came in on a Saturday afternoon for lunch only to see that the place wasn't very busy.  Regardless, I settled on a whole wheat chicken quesadilla, which really hit the spot, as they only recently started using whole wheat tortillas.  As mentioned in Ni K.'s review, the staff was very friendly and eager to serve, which put me at ease right away.  Also, given that there was hardly anyone there, it didn't take me long to find somewhere to sit.  When the weather is favorable, there is outdoor seating available as well.  While it's a tough choice having both Qdoba and Chipotle in the neighborhood, Qdoba is a definite go-to when I don't mind walking a bit further from my usual spot.
Pricey but there is something addictive about the salmon. Poached just right to keep the middle soft. The papaya salad is also a must!

i absolutely love their steak shawarma in a pita and fries that were made fresh for us! i felt however the pita portions are a little small for that price. Also the service was good and friendly, but a little slow

HUGE line at the Phillies' game, but it was surprisingly efficient!  Crab fries were pretty good (pretty standard, crinkle fries).  The cheese sauce was the best part (consider getting two containers).  Wish the fries were bigger / wider to scoop more of the cheese sauce into my mouth. 

Make sure to grab the fries they are just putting out or you'll get cold fries like I did.  

185/365

Outrageous selection of craft beers! The biscuits are delicious and made from scratch. The mac and cheese will definitely go in my top 5. It has a little kick and the flavor is amazing. Staff is excellent, and they stay open until 3 or 4 am. I will absolutely be returning to try the rest of the menu.

Went here for the lunch the other day and forgot about how amazing this place is! I got the tempura shrimp bowl and it was DELICIOUS and so filling! I saved half for dinner that night. Also the chips + guac are fantastic. Despite the fact that they was a pretty big line in front of me (6 people) I probably only spent 15 min there.
My daughters and I went to Hai Street recently for the first time.  We had quick service and our lunch was absolutely delicious. Cannot wait to go back!

So i decided to try wingstop this evening for the first time however I dont think id be returning after the cashier took my money and forgot about my order. The best part of the service was that i was able to get my money back because I cancelled the order. Get it together

Wow, the food here was really good.  Surprisingly really good!  It's an excellent lesson to never judge a book by it's cover.  Sure, it's in no way fancy but the price is cheap and the quality is excellent!  I had coleslaw and fruit and salad from the cold bar and then fried chicken, greens and mac and cheese from the hot bar and oh my god, it was some of the best I've ever had in my life.  From what I hear, the quality of food is also consistent which is a plus.  Consistency is detrimental to any place whether they make it or not and quality wise, Tootsies will be here to stay!  Very friendly employees as well.  

PS, I came here with two VERY finicky and VERY picky old ladies.  And they had no complaints.

I love this Jimmy Johns. It's right by my work and they deliver! Their delivery should have a rating on its own! It's always so fast and they never mess up my order!

Their sandwiches, chips, and cookies are always amazing. I usually get the Vito or the Club Lulu. It's a great and easy way to get a quick lunch delivered to you on your busiest days! 

Overall, I would definitely recommend!

Omg, so friggin good. Just go...You'll be happy you did. Been trying to get here for a year. 
The chicken Bahn Mi is without hesitation the best in phila - the bread is extremely special. 
Wings are big, plump and delicious. 
Neat homemade hot sauce. 
The chicken Caesar salad is perfect. 
And finally, the chef or owner has extraordinary baking skills. There's a slew of desserts that are as darn good as anything you'd get at metropolitan- and that's big. The cookies and custard pie are exceptional.
Their food is mediocre at best and service terrible. I am very disappointed that my first experience at Jimmy John's is undoubtedly my last.

Everything we had was fantastic! The pirogies are probably the best I've ever had and the pork was unbelievable. The wait staff was very knowledgable as well. And they have some fun mixed drinks too! We will definitely go again.

Don't order from here if you want a hot sandwich, crispy chicken and a crispy roll. 1 hour for delivery and the chicken was very small... only fit half the roll.  Sandwich was just ok. May have been better if it was hot and crispy.  Won't order from here again.
Very good! I was pleasantly surprised by the flavor and freshness. I would go back again and order the chicken shwarma!

This place beats Chipotle in the "fast casual" department.  I'm amazed by how great and high-quality the food is, especially given how fast and affordable it is.  The only qualm is that it could have better ambience for those dining in, as it feels somewhat unwelcoming.  I highly recommend the salmon and chicken varieties.

I really enjoy this place for lunch when I am picking it up and going right home.

They have very limited seating, a long table against the wall and window with about 4 stools.

This is not great when you want to stop and eat while shopping in the area or want to eat in the restaurant.  The University city location has a few tables, but there isn't much seating there either.

Both locations are pretty small, so I get that there is limited seating, but at least have some outdoor tables in the summer?

I really like to make my own creation, I usually get the salmon with various veggies such as the papaya, jicama, carrots, etc.

I also like either the spicy mayo or the peanut sauce as my sauce.  The only reason I have not trued the other sauces, is because there is no description of them to be found and the restaurant is usually pretty busy when I am there, so I feel like I am holding people up if I ask. The staff usually wants to get you order quickly and get to the next customer.

I also enjoy either the fried shallots or garlic as my crunch.

I do which there were more meat/fish options.  I would love to have more sushi quality fish in my sushirtto.  It is kind of disappointing when there is only one non-fried fish option and there are no real sushi fish options either since everything is cooked. However, even though I wish there were more options as stated above, I do always enjoy the salmon.

The wasabi guacamole and chips are also delicious and I do not usually like wasabi, I only like it on my own terms.  It gives the guacamole a really good flavor.

Hai Street Kitchen & Co is what happens when you cross Chipotle with your favorite sushi place; furthermore, the results are quite tasty.

You choose between a sushi burrito or sushi bowl, then choose what type of rice you want, what type of meat you want, and what type of veggies you want. There are plenty of options so choose wisley.

They also have predetermined recipies called "Signature Sushi Burritos", which is what I opted to get; "The Hai Street Kitchen" with chicken Katsu, black pepper teriyaki sauce, romain, pickled red onion, red cabbage, and green papaya salad.  It was very tasty. 

It should also be noted that they have delicious housemade lemonade and hisbiscus iced tea. If you're in the Philly area, this place is worth a quick pop in for lunch.

4.5 stars. Actually to my surprise this place is fantastic... not the worlds biggest fried chicken type of guy but this spot was yum, wishbone was a hit! 

First off the people working were really nice! The restaurant is clean and it was open late! 

I ordered a 3 piece of breast with fries And cornbread. It's was wonderful, chicken was perfectly fried ( I liked the triple XXX sauce more than the pesto and tamarind sweet) also I was not a huge fan of the ketchup at all... but I like fries without ketchup too so that was not too bad for me. 

They have a great selection of bottled brews and drinks for much more adequate prices than the bars and clubs around so I think it's a worthy stop at any part of the night especially if you get a little hangry.

Till next time.
Hai Street is basically the Japanese version of Chipotle, just a little pricer. It's great for a quick bit and at least appears healthy.

It's a regular qdoba...no big deal.

While the ppl are usually very nice, there is one female manager who I am not a fan of.  They are also usually stingy w/ the portions compared to other Qdobas.

We ordered the chicken cutlet sandwich. It took 30 seconds for our order to be ready but it smelled as if the oil in the fryer hadn't been changed in a month and looked like it , too... A roll with gross chicken fingers on it... that's it! We were informed that although the sandwich "looked weird", this is what it was supposed to be. Will not order anything from this location again. 1 star only because the crab fries were ok, otherwise it's a big fat 0

How is this place totally empty on a Sunday night? $8 cocktails.  $5-6 glasses of choice wines.  $15 for Sunday night curry + beer night.  carefully curated beer and wine list, with real gems on bottle list.  Bread that is on par with High Street's. $5 appetizers, every bit as good as FDR or P&K. That's not a knock on either of them - a composed radish dish this good SHOULD be twice the price. This place gets 5 stars just for the quality-price-ratio.

They earn a 6th star for the curries. They're seriously the best Thai curries i've had in this country. Possible the best I've had anywhere. Generously portioned, intensely fragrant, rich, complex, made with high quality ingredients, and punctuated with fresh herbs. Just be warned that they don't mess around when they say something is a bit spicy.

(They get -1 star because the flatware sure is ugly.  conveniently saves me from having to find a way to give them 6 stars anyway)

There's a reason that G. came here 4 times last week. It's crazy good!

I have had my eye on this place since it's grand inception due to the clever concept of a sushi burrito that's new to Philly. However, I just never had the opportunity to try it until now.  The concept is very "chipotle" or "subway" offering a choice of protein and 4 sides and choosing either a roll or a bowl, I can see how some would argue that this place is pricey if you look at it simply as takeout food but if you look at it from a sushi perspective where you easily pay $8-15 for one roll and in many sushi cases you order 2-3 rolls, a filling sushi burrito roll with fresh and pure ingredients for $10 is very reasonable.  Looking at their selections, I wish they had more sushi-like fish concoctions.  But I guess they had to feature meat choices for the carnivores out there.  Being this my first time, I had to go for the slammin' salmon signature roll with fried shallots to stay true to my sushi roots. What a great light and fresh choice, even better than sushi in a health perspective since I'm not drenching each bite into soy sauce.  Fresh fish, greens, ginger - I wish they would feature a plain wasabi sauce that's not guacamole based as I don't eat avocados. Sad I know, allergies damnit.  Other gripes include a lack of seating and a lack of a bathroom. But overall, great and healthy alternative than a burrito or burger but more filling than a salad when you wanna go for a "take-out" choice.

There is so much hype about this place that a lot of my friends that tried this before I did didn't really have great things to say about it because of their high expectations. I didn't lower mine, but I was still generally satisfied. This isn't a life changing meal, but it is a 'fresh' take that is great to perk up your lunch rotation.

It's a pretty place, and it's a little reminiscent of a chipotle/qdoba set up. Clean colors and lines, and aesthetically pleasing.

I got a hand roll filled with white rice, tataki salmon, spicy mayo, pickled mango, carrots, spring mix, cucumber, and crispy shallots. I did not taste or feel the crispy shallots at all, so I guess it didn't matter or not if I got them. I am a huge fiend for spicy mayo, so I'm glad I got the spicy mayo, rather than the gochu jang spread - which would make your roll taste more like hwedup bap than a sushi roll. I didn't really care for the pickled mango, but everything else was great. I'm glad the tataki salmon was just ever so lightly seared, so that I still got that raw texture and taste.

I also got the mexican grilled pork - their signature version - and it was awesome. I'd get it again, most definitely.

I laughed a bit when I saw how they got the rice onto the seaweed wrap - they use a machine! Having worked at a sushi restaurant as a server, it's just a little embarrassing to watch that happen. It's not too difficult to just spread rice on a a sheet of seaweed, but I guess the machine is part of the gimmick? Or to standardize the amount of rice being put on? I think that's the part that slowed down the process the most.

The size was a little disappointing, but I was sufficiently filled and there's always the 'jumbo' option. I'll be back hopefully. I like this place.

I'm not sure I truly understood the meaning of soul food until I tried their mac n' cheese. Just writing that out is making me salivate - and it's located next to all of the hip clubs on 13th. This is the best kind of late night food (or dinner / lunch I guess, too) and will wrap you in warm feelings of delicious goodness.

I was dying to try this place, but I still have yet to visit the store. I ran into their tent at the PIFA event in the city. I got the salmon roll and the green tea. I had just come from dim sum with my mom, but just HAD to try a sushi burrito roll. I was not disappointed. I was so full but still couldn't stop eating. I can't wait to actually order something from the store.

I honestly have walked pass this place multiple times, and one night I decided to go in. For starters they sell beer and they deliver it!! After you walk pass their selection of beer, you see all the different choices of food that they have. They sell fried chicken, Mac and cheese, fries, and etc. Their fried chicken is by the pound and I ordered a 1/2 pound of their white meat chicken which was two pieces. After you finish ordering, you get to pick a sauce to dip your food in. They have a wide variety of sauces but I decided to go with their barbecue sauce. 
After I payed, I was able to find a seat and enjoy my food. For starters their fried chicken was not greasy compared to other places. The chicken was nice and juicy, and it was cooked to perfection! The chicken had a nice crunch to it, and it melted in your mouth. The barbecue sauce paired nicely with the chicken, and it was a little sweet but not too sweet. 
The best thing about this place is that they are open till 4 in the morning on Saturdays! I went to this place at 12 in the morning and it was amazing! If you haven't check this place out you need to, especially if you like fried chicken. You will not be disappointed!

They are fast, I cannot take that away from them.  With that said I'd rather they be good then fast.  Blandness and turkey loaf are the orders of the day.  I don't care if i have my sandwich in 90 seconds, I'm willing to wait up to 100 (maybe more!) for even a modicum more in quality.

Summary: Okay food, terrible service

I was looking for a place to grab a bite to eat with one of my friends who works in Center City, and hadn't been to Reading Terminal (RTM) in a while, so I figured that it was a great chance to head back to this veritable food Mecca.

After getting totally lost somewhere in the lunch rush, we finally came by Franks-A-Lot, which he had been wanting to try for a while. This place is mostly classic American, serving BBQ, chicken, hot dogs, along with a few Polish items.

The line wasn't too bad (~3-4 minutes), and when we got to the front, the fellow taking orders helped us make our selections quickly. I got the pierogi platter, which includes 5-6 freshly made pierogis, 2 side items (I got the mac & cheese and the potato salad), and a drink. My friend got the turkey burger. Everything was priced reasonably, and I paid 7 dollars and change for my platter while the burger was around 5 dollars.

However, our experience went sharply downhill the moment we got to the checkout counter. I don't mean to stereotype, but the Asian lady handling the register was probably the meanest and worst person that I have ever had to deal with at a restaurant. She was constantly yelling at customers (including us), she snatched money/credit cards from people's hands, handed bags to the wrong people and then literally ripped them out of their hands when she realized her error, and even made a young 5-6 year old boy ready to cry. She accidentally gave him my friend's burger, and then just made a very horrible looking face and yelled something in another language, as if it was his fault that she messed up, and ripped the bag away from him. It was truly... shocking, for a lack of a better word to describe it.

Once we got past that horrible check-out line, we (miraculously) found a table in the seating area and got to the food. My friend said that the burger was decent, albeit nothing too special. As for my platter, the pierogis were over seasoned and very tough, while the potato salad was passable. The only redeeming element in the tray was the mac and cheese, which was above average. I understand that I'm not paying for a gourmet pierogi, but still, there have to be some standards. Unfortunately, I found none.

All in all, I just hope that this was a bad day for them, and hope to try them again in a few weeks to see if it was just a one-off thing.

Tip: At RTM, try to avoid the afternoon lunch rush if at all possible - it's really bad between 12-2 PM.

Sushi burritos are off the hook! I got the Shrimp Tempura roll. The rice is definitely cooked correctly for sushi. Prices are totally reasonable too! It's a little messy so keep it in the paper while you eat it (just like a burrito)

For the past few years, every time I mentioned that I wanted to try out Hai Street Kitchen, I would get pretty lackluster responses. At the time, I did not understand why - a sushi burrito sounded like the harmonious marriage of two of my favorite foods. 

I stopped in right when they opened and luckily did not have to deal with a line. I'm a huge chicken katsu fan and it was nearing 100 degrees outside, so I opted for a cooked option - otherwise, the slamming salmon and yellowfin tuna both sounded like awesome choices. The ordering process was quick and painless - I emerged about five minutes later with a neatly packaged, decently sized chicken katsu sushirrito in what felt like a sturdy cardboard tube, and a cold matcha drink.

My favorite part of the meal was the matcha drink - it was refreshing, had strong matcha flavor, and I'm not sure if it was the sugar content or the caffeine, but it woke me right up. Unfortunately, the chicken katsu sushiritto is not particularly amenable to takeout - 20 minutes later, the tonkatsu sauce had seeped out of the burrito, through the cardboard, and smeared around my bag and all of its contents. The chicken was also quite soggy, having been encased in the burrito with wet shredded vegetables. The flavors were good though, the chicken portion was quite generous, and in general, the burrito had a good ingredients-to-rice ratio. 

Overall, I did think that Hai Street was worth checking out for the novelty, and there were other options on the menu that caught my eye. Unfortunately, the combination of sushi and burrito was not more than the sum of its parts, and actually sacrificed one of the best traits of both - their portability and convenience as takeout food. That matcha drink was awesome though - I'd stop in again just for that.

I braved the line here for lunch today and got the slammin' salmon roll. Ahhh! It was SLAMMIN'! 

For $8.99, they put a ton of beautiful cured salmon, brown rice, lettuce, mango, fried shallots, papaya salad, gochujang, and red onions inside a lovely nori wrapper. This is filling, has healthy ingredients, and is totally worth the money, in my opinion. 

They have a wide variety of options and combinations to choose from, or to make your own roll or bowl. I was really impressed with their salmon roll, and I don't think I would have changed a thing. I liked the assembly line that they had going - although the line is out the door everyday (they just opened last week), I was impressed with how quickly they took my order, prepared my roll, and swiped my credit card.

I think Hai Street Kitchen is here to stay!

Love their crabfries.  They moved to a new, permanent location near where their standalone stand used to be, near the northeast corner of the stadium.  The lines are long as ever, however.  They've set up a labyrinthine, waiting lanes (similar to those found at Disney World).  Still worth the wait....

After a night of partying I smelled the chicken on the way to my car, so I had to stop. I had two chicken biscuits(I made them) and their Mac and cheese.the biscuit was sweet and savory, and the Mac and cheese had pieces of biscuit in it. Both were delicious and I paired it with a Fat tire for extra goodness. This place is a must stop.

Great ingredients, endless combinations and an amazing fusion of flavors- pickled mango, pork belly, gochujang sauce, - and all relative healthy (or not) depending on your combo. I'm relieved to have an affordable and casual food option in center city.
Cool idea, really good execution. Go with Go Zilla for some extra meat, it's worth it.

Best sliders in town! Great customer service, very welcoming environment and definitely recommend the illadelphia. There's always weekly specials that go on. Also dip your fries in the boomboom sauce, recommend to me by Tom which was an overall nice guy. Will be back again

The wraps are actually Sushi burritos . And it's pretty delicious. I had the mushroom fried sushi wrap. They have other options like chicken and other meats. The idea is great. The veggies were fresh and they had a good variety to choose from. Very healthy menu and caters to a vegetation diet. It's like a chipotle that' serves Sushi. They even serve the salad bowls if you don't like the sushi rolls.

I'm lovin' the food truck rotation this year at the Porch!  M.A.T.T.'S Gourmet Sliders definitely delivers.  (I asked what the acronym stood for and they said "Matt and Tom and Tim" or something like that.  I said Matt is definitely the one benefiting, but they didn't seem to mind...super friendly staff here!)

Overall, I'm glad it's not just plain old burgers (not that there's anything wrong with that) but it is nice to have a variety.  The regular burgers are actually very good and spiced well and the quality of the meat is good.  The little slider buns are perfectly buttery and grilled so they don't fall apart.  

I've also tried the crab cake sandwich with beer slaw which wasn't a slider but was on a full sized burger bun.  It was delicious and full of crabmeat and seasoned well.  My only complaint would be that the crabcake itself was very soft, as was the bun and so combined with the beer drenched slaw (though delicious), it kind of fell apart and needed some sort of crunch element to counteract it.  The regular fries are pretty basic, but this time I upgraded to the truffle parmesan fries, which were really tasty.  A coworker got the turkey/avocado California sliders and said they were delicious, too.

I will definitely come back to try some of their other varieties of burgers.

We were excited to try Buckminster's, the newest addition to the very up and coming Point Breeze section of the city. My husband had been talking about it for awhile now. We always love supporting new spots in these less obvious places in hopes they will stay & help in the revitalization of these types of neighborhoods, especially this one so close to home & my brother's new house. 

The tiny corner place has cute details making it industrial chic trendy. West Elm-ish if you will. Sleek black tables with a simple gold metal stripe, hanging geometric pendants over the bar which matched the tonal wallpaper and a nice pop of turquoise on one wall. I dug it. Candles on each table adding to the ambiance. It was however freezing inside. Uncomfortably so. Now, it was the first real humid night of the season and I think everyone freaked a bit because this was the case with everywhere we went that night. 

We were really just headed there for pre-dinner drinks on a rainy Friday night, but were keeping the option of staying for dinner open. We let the waiter know this. 

We were seated immediately in the back on the long bench against the wall and I really should've spoken up when they walked us past the more private single tables towards the front because we were on a date after all and I think this could've in part made the difference in our experience. I get that the place is small and they did what they could  with the layout, but I now know that the girl next to us is getting an elf tattoo on her upper left shoulder and the guy she was with is having a hard time getting some orchestra tickets for his upcoming birthday. Ugh. I don't know if it's the fact that my youngest daughter literally talks non stop from 7am to 7pm and mommy just needed a break from constant chatter or that the music was way too loud and people needed to speak VERY loudly for all to hear every word, but I really wanted to just hear how my husbands day was. We made the best of it. We still laughed and enjoyed ourselves but, it just wasn't the vibe I was going for this night. If coming on a date, ask for a table up front. We both agreed perhaps it's better as a drinks with friends type of place. 

Our waiter, John C. was absolutely fantastic! Very attentive and knew the menu, both drink and food, backwards and forwards. He refilled our water constantly, even bringing a fresh carafe when ours sat a tad. He checked back on us often. He helped us select our drinks. They were innovative and I really like the single pour or group pour options. I will note however, unless I chose beer or wine which I wasn't in the mood for, there was really only one choice for cocktails for me as I don't normally choose to drink rum, scotch or brandy as a first option. No vodka choices, but the tequila drink did me just fine! I loved it in fact! 'Thyme' Killer (Tequila, Green Tea, Wheat Beer, Lemon, Thyme $7!) Hubs ordered the Funky Diabetic (Copper & Kings Brandy, Rum, Banana, Vanilla, Smoked Chili, shaken with ice $10) and then the Fizz Lemon (Mezcal, Lemon Cordial, Amaro with Egg White shaken frothy $9). He very much loved them both, the first better. Drinks were strong, very tasty and fairly priced. 

We did nosh on the popcorn which our neighbors had and smelled so amazing it was hard to resist (like when you walk into a movie theater). I just had to try the parsnip fries. Sounded so interesting. They were delicious! They subbed out the buttermilk dressing and I ate them plain. Ooey and gooey. Carmalized and crispy at the ends! A definitely must try!! 

We looked over the menu and while it had some truly interesting components, it really wasn't doing too much for us that night. I heard it's heavily Polish influenced which is neat. If we stayed, the hubby was going to get the Bologna Sammy which we heard is the thing to try here. The Toasted Spelt gnocchi with Roasted Mushrooms sounded really interesting. I would've had the Massaman Curry which unfortunately seemed like it was lacking something. I'm not sure if it contained veggies which just weren't listed or the dish didn't have any, but it was heavy on the carbs with just rice and sweet potatoes. The pear pickles sounded neat though and I'm sure it was flavorful. The curry was the only vegan option on the menu besides salad. I did find it odd nowadays to not see specifically listed dairy and/or gluten free options, especially in a place that seems a tad "hipster". I guess that's not really a top priority from the owners of Kensington Quarters. I will note that I loved seeing all of the locally sourced ingredients on the menu such as cheeses from Farm at Doe Run, Kensington Quarter meats. Neshaminy Creek Croyden Ale and Rose' from Mullica Hill, NJ. Big props for that! 

We would come back again and give it another go as the menu is seasonal. Great for drinks with friends. After work oysters & apps. Brunch if they put some tables outside on a nice day (?) The curry and beer Sunday special sounded intriguing too

I don't get the less than amazing rating here.  Food was delicious, fast, and just what it said it was on the menu.  Perfect.  Could there have been more shrimp?  Sure, but that would raise the cost, so no arguments.

Naf Naf Grill has decent options for a fast-casual middle eastern place. I probably shouldn't have tried the chicken shawarma rice bowl, because overall it didn't taste any better than the "chicken over rice" I typically get from food trucks nearby, but cost me twice as much. (The flavors, of course were a bit different - less spicy, greasier, and pretty salty.) I would probably come back to try another bowl - maybe the baba ganoush, as I've heard good things about it. The pita bread that came with the dish tasted fresh and was very fluffy and soft. 

The portion was decent, but I noticed that I was given a smaller portion than other customers who ordered the exact same thing, but who were larger people. I know I'm petite, but it's kind of uncool for me to pay the same amount as everyone else if I'm getting less food! Perhaps I should point this out next time and ask for a discount, lol... Other than that, the service was good. Still... tough for me to feel compelled to eat here often with so many similar options nearby.

I heart Jimmy Johns and I like to think they heart me. 
I also heart a good value and efficient service so Jimmy Johns gets high marks. 

Their tuna salad sandwich (5/5 stars) helped me get through lent. The tuna itself is made with real mayo, fresh onions, and yummy stuff, and they put alfalfa sprouts in with it! I usually had a few slices of provolone to it. 
I also enjoy their Club Lulu (4/5 stars), and it isn't as stellar as their tuna, but has bacon in it... yum! I also ask to add cheese to this sandwich too since it doesn't regularly include it. 
Their bread is fresh, and the rolls are pretty soft and tasty. 
Oh, and their chips are nice and crispy too. 
They also have a customer appreciation card you can ask for- buy 10 sandwiches, get 1 free.

Wishbone Philly apparently just opened. I picked up a mini chivken  pot pie and I have to say it was absolutely delicious. Washed it down with a chocolate Nutella  cupcake that was also delicious. Give it a try.

My rating would probably be between 4 and 5, but the smoked prime rib special they offered recently really solidified the 5 star rating. I love the adorable little rolls and the 2-bite sized cheese steaks and pork sandwiches. I think those and the crab cake sandwich are my favorites.

Stopped here for the first time today on the way to sunbathe by the river. We ordered the Shrimp Tempura and Salmon house burritos. The burritos were amazing! I'm not a fan of spicy and I don't eat a lot of chicken or pork so it would have been nice to see some more house rolls with fish that aren't spicy. The process for ordering was a lot like Chipotle or Subway and I always get overwhelmed with all of the options! I like when places have a lot of house options that you can choose to tweak to make spicy or sub out a veggie you may not like. The menus with the sauces and veggies were really small and right up on the window instead of overhead so it might be difficult to decide what you want before it's your turn. I am most likely in the minority here. :) We ordered the regular size and it was definitely big enough for lunch. I'd have to be super famished to need a zilla roll.

Overall - delicious and totally happy that we stopped in today!

Went their for the first time the food is really fresh and not that badly priced. I made my own sushi burrito it was done fast and fresh I also got the hibiscus tea which wasn't that bad. Would definitely go back again.

For a fast food chain, it's really worth the visit. Order online to avoid the lines. You get a free pita and all the ingredients taste fresh in this branch. I had to try the chicken shawarma after watching the Avengers extra scene. This is just my personal preference, but ask for a bowl. You get so much more than the pita, and it's easier to eat.
Everyone here is so nice. No idea why it was rated one star. Rush hour lunch and everyone was pleasant and very professional. Thanks guys.
Great experience! Loved the sushi burrito and the packaging for it was adorable and easy on the go! Great place!

I can not believe how clean, new, slick, friendly and pleasant my experience was at the new (actually 5 mos. old) Panda Express, fast-food Chinese in the Comcast Center.

Normally I can not stand sloppy, gloppy, steam-table, mall Chinese - so boy was I shocked when the food not only looked great (albeit lots of the choices and all of the shrimp choices are fried) but tasted good, too.

Trepidatious bynature I ordered only a small a la carte (1/2 pint) box of Honey Walnut Shrimp (Fried + Mayonnaise + Sugar = health BOMB) and instantly recalled the bygone era of late 1980's Chinese-American fare.

The Manager, Jay,  was very accomodating and said that now - for large orders (and within a few blocks) they will deliver and the offer party trays and catering.  The even have a deal they will do with schools for fundraising.

The wheels are turning...  Perhaps a Panda Feast (for $30 you get 3 large entress and 2 large sides - enough for 4 (easily) to 7 (tiny eaters) people.  A big pan entree $36 - $48 if you pick shrimp feeds about 8 people.

They also have a small catering package for $96 that easily feeds 16.

I am planning a prty soon and will update my review with the results - but so far I am shockingly pleased with Panda Express.
Just no, from the banh mi chicken burger which simply doesn't work to the mac n cheese that disappointed I was thoroughly unsatisfied with my meal.

Hip place, but the fried chicken failed badly with that crumbly breading, wasn't crunchy and lacked memorable flavor.  Jalepeno corn bread was ok. Mediocre food....didn't impress me enough to come back a second time.

We just ordered from here. We were so excited to try this place! Unfortunately, they messed up our online order so badly that I didn't even want to eat what was delivered. First of all, the "Yellowfin Tuna" option on the online menu is REALLY SPICY, and nowhere on their online menu does it indicate that. It was so awful that it took over all of the other flavors. Second of all, neither of the sauces my friend and I ordered wound up on the burritos, and they seemed to mix and match pieces of our orders. Finally, I asked for a little of my sauce on the burrito and some on the side...I did not get my sauce on the side.

If I ever go back here, I'll be ordering in person and watching them make it. I love the concept, but I do not love throwing money away on food I don't want.

While shopping with my husband, we felt like having a small snack and decided to give this place a shot. We split their shrimp tempera roll and it was enough for a snack for the both of us, but we each could easily could have been devoured our own roll. The nori was great - nicely roasted with lots of flavor, the shrimp tempura was also great.  They were nice enough to let me swap out the asparagus for pickled papaya. 

The price is really what deters me, it cost us ~$10 for this sushi burrito which was ~80% vegetables. We probably won't be going back, we'll bring our $10 and get some really good handrolls down the street.

I miss the Screaming' tuna! (please bring it back).  But still opt for the Slammin' Salmon.  A spicy option with fresh salmon and veggies.  I haven't had a bad roll yet. A great lunch option for a mix of sushi and burrito.
They went above and beyond to take care of my allergic requirements. And it tastes delicious ! Thank you,team!

I walked by one day on lunch hour and decided I had to try it soon since I love sushi and burritos. They have signature roll combinations already selected or have it rolled your way...I did the latter. STEP 1: Select your style - roll or bowl STEP 2: Choose your main ingredient  STEP 3: Sauce it Up, STEP 4: Pick up to 4 toppings STEP 5:Crunch it up. So here's what I had, Nori roll with White rice, Salmon, I wasn't going to get a sauce but decided to get Black Pepper Teriyaki, Romaine, Cucumber, Carrot and Asparagus. For .99 cents you can add Wasabi Guacamole and Yucca chips as my crunch. I thought the roll was delicious. I also brought fruit from home, so, if roll is not satisfying you could GO ZILLA or add a side: Chips with Wasabi Guacamole, Sweet corn tempura or Miso Vegetable soup. Yes, I will be back. I think this is a great concept merging sushi/japanese with Mexican/Burritos. Cool concept.

If you are a fan of Mexican food, this is the place for you. They have a great assortment of nachos, quesadillas, tacos and burritos. Think of it as slightly classier Taco Bell. 

Each item is made fresh to order and you get to watch them make it too! I am in love with the Chicken Quesadillas and their chocolate chip cookies which are huge. I also love how clean the place is. The atmosphere and wall murals also add a nice touch. It's a great place to go when that taco craving hits!

Food & Drinks: 4
     I chose the sushi burrito, the process is pretty neat. I was basically a chipotle but for sushi burritos. I went for the fried portobello as my protein, because I'm vegetarian and a ginger sauce. For my four veggies, I got the spring mix, shredded cucumbers, avocado (which cost extra like always), and the pickled onions. Then she rolled it up and I ate it. It was so much better than I thought, I was a bit skeptical about the ideas of Japanese and Mexican cuisine coming together, but I worked out. One thing was the it was a bit expensive, I got a burrito which was $11 and a water which ended up costing $2. 

Environment: 3.5
     The seating area was really small only about six chairs and two then which looked out the window. But this is not supposed to be a place where you sit down and can spend hours with your friends talking. This is either a take on the train or while your walking kind of thing. But there wasn't much decoration, it was mainly just a small place for functional purposes.
My sushiritto ended up being about 80% carrot and 5% actual salmon. A waste of money for something that doesn't taste very fresh to begin with.

BBQ Bacon Whopper gives me a baseline price on the Livingsocial PYT punch card special. For the sandwich only, same price before tip and no wait. Burger King wins. Now about the deferred maintenance, the place is falling apart. Think trailer trash decor.
Every time I go here they give me what they want or leave food out that I've paid for... three

He says: The burritos are ok.  They are filling and appear nutritive.  Perhaps in a futuristic world all people will be forced to live off of these relatively unremarkable entrees.  However, that is not today.  First, the pluses.  The meats are relatively tasty and the salsas are not bad.  The big minus is the cheese which appears to be a bland variant of American.  Why someone would put American cheese on a burrito escapes me.  Secondly, because they don't heat up the burritos sufficiently after assembly, the cheese is not melted and the burrito is sometimes of uneven temperature (i.e., the meat warm, lettuce & cheese cold).  

She says:  Why go to this establishment?  So unremarkable, I paid one over-priced visit and never went back.  It wouldn't seem so bad if there weren't other (better, IMHO) Mexican options and if I had more money.

So good! I only got chicken tenders (I know, lame) not only were they good, but I got a side of mac and cheese and the apricot corn bread. It was amazing. The corn bread was moist and warm. The mac and cheese was also very tasty. Reading Terminal Market is a bit overwhelming but I'd definitely give this place another shot!

I've been wanting to try this but was wary of going in (for no good reason). A co-worker was telling me about this great place in Philly when I realized this was the place she was talking about!  The staff was very helpful as I had no idea how to order. I ended up getting a bowl with double protein. Spicy and yummy. Also, I felt like I got a lot for the money. Next time I'm getting a roll!  Can't wait.

People were very professional. Place was very clean. Food was terrible. Some pieces of chicken weren't cooked all the way. I get the concept, but the food is bad. Mostly fat on the chicken. Wouldn't recommend, but I'll let other ppl make a decision for themselves.

First time getting a sushi burrito and it was delicious. My only complaint with Hai Street is the variety of options for toppings. I've been to a lot of poke restaurants before and have never seen so few options of things to put in my burrito/bowl. That said, it was delicious, I just wish I saw seaweed salad, plain edamame, crab salad, etc.
Worst service for walk ins because corporate prioritizes the cars.  Someone could he 5th in line behind you but get food first because they are in a car. I LIVE NEAR HERE you jackasses!
Slammin Salmon is good too.
Cold cheese on my burger. Highly disappointed with the quality that is normally upheld as other Wendy's establishments. They got our order wrong.
Worst fast food service in area, expect to wait ten+ mins for any 2 items of food . In 3/5 visits the employees either gave my order away to someone else or gave me the incorrect order.  Unbelievable

My 2nd time here yesterday really good!!! I has the salmon roll the first time and the crunch roll the 2nd time!!! It's so good so filling and I always get a great tea. Really nice place always clean. Although no parking I always find a spot that I can run in order and leave. See you again.

Not a fan of the craft chicken, unfortunately. I like very crispy chicken skin so think Korean fried chicken (Bonchon) or the typical Popeyes. This breading just didn't do it for me. However, I will be back for the chicken pot pie and the mac and cheese. The mac and cheese is absolutely out of this world!! Must try!!

I am not a food critic, just like food. I got the Ho-Lee Shrimp, highly recommend it if you want something light for a meal. How do you stuff your face in sushi? Make it on big roll, burrito!! Great hospitality on their food truck! Just wished they had the dynamite roll available on their food trucks. Great work you guys! Keep up the good work!

The food was actually pretty good.  It was delivered earlier than expected.  An extra A plus for having the most attractive delivery girl ever.  Makes me want to order there more often.  Thank you for making my first experience a good one!

A pretty interesting concept. Think a gigantic sushi roll that isn't cut into 6 - 8 pieces. Sort of like a Japanese burrito.  We ordered the salmon one and the shrimp tempura one. I thought the salmon was better, I liked the Chinese veggies and wasabi guac that was on it. I went at 2pm, I was in and out in 5 mins. (I've heard the line can get long)  definitely something to try once and I would go back if I was in the mood.  Also, the lemonade was horrible, jus sayin

WHOA! I've been dreaming of sushi burritos for years (seriously, ask my wife) and it was totally worth the wait. This place is awesome - friendly and prompt staff, great location, and delicious, fresh, and healthy food. The Slammin Salmon was fantastic and the sweet green tea excellent too.

If you're reading this, stop and go to Hai Street. So good!

Great beer selection. Typical bar food. My friend and I both had bacon blue cheese burgers and fries. The burgers were very good and one order of fries is enough for two people.  They sell beer to go which I found very interesting.

Bland yet greasy chicken that is really honestly not like any fried chicken I've had before. More like shake n bake. Weirdest Mac n cheese I've ever tasted. Limited drink selection which sucks, and what they do have is expensive.
The food was delicious, but fell apart in my hands. It was difficult to eat. I would just order a bowl. That defeats the whole idea of a sushi wrap.

The only reason I gave it 3 stars was for the blondie brownie.  That was one of the best ones I've had.  The chicken is nothing to be impressed about.  Didn't expect to receive burnt fries either. I don't recommend the tamarind sauce at all.

Best ,best , best  sushi  burrito  ever  I literally wished they had one closer to me I'd eat here everyday that's how good the food is . The quality and freshness is everything. Me and my sisters go here all the time we love it.

I really want to love this place but I just can't.  The chicken has no flavor, no  salt , just nothing . I had to dip the chicken in the sauce I bought just for some kind of salt . The mac and cheese is good, but that's about it. This is my second time eating here. I mean no flavor at all. The employees are really nice!

Went in on a whim..wow loved this place..owner so friendly n helpful.
Its like a bakery with so many many homemade goodies to chose from ..all looked so yummy ..
Tons of stuff to chose from..
I had chicken tenders and mac n cheese with chicken pot pie . home made succotash.
This place is a MUST TRY...u will not regret it ..no way 
Wholesome comfort food at a reasonable price..

The food was ok but man the service was horrendous!!!!!!! I had two separate orders and a question about the size of the different things on the menu so that I could order something appropriate as it was my first time there. The girl behind the counter acted completely aggravated and very rude with my TWO questions. I ordered them stepped over to pay. There were two girls standing at the cash register, I had two separate orders and for whatever reason each of them decided to take one but ask me questions at the same exact time. I told them to please talk to me *one* at a time as they were both asking me the same thing about each order "if I wanted to naf it up with French fries". Really!?? I go to answer and the girl who was making my second order starts yelling at me from 5 feet away if I want veggies and pickles on the second order. Since I'm at the register trying to answer these two robots talking over each other, I don't hear her and she gets annoyed and yells "hey lady I talkin' to you!" Stunned, I look up and I'm like "um, what?!" I tell her to just add the veggies and I am humiliated in front of everyone else in line. Awful. Then I turn back to the cashiers to pay for my orders and again they ask (AT THE SAME TIME) if I want to "naf it up". I COUDN'T WAIT TO GET THE HECK OUT OF THERE!! Where do they find these people????!!!!!

Horrible crab fries.  $8.  Milky cheese whiz for $2.  
Be ashamed Chickie and Pete's

I went here for the first time during the summer but it wasn't as good as the second time. The first time I got it, it was too dry and not enough sauce on it. It was okay and not something I would travel into the city for. 
Today I was in the area and thought why not give it a second try. Glad I did! Super delicious this time! Very quick service. 
I got the chicken katsu with white rice, spicy mayo, romaine, red onions, carrots with crunchy shallots.
Fun place, good food. I mean, who doesn't love a sushi burrito... but the space is cramped so be prepared to take your food to go. Definitely worth it.

Get to the Chase:

Pros:
1) SO AMAZING! Perfect service (quick, courteous, and very friendly...especially if you go there 2 times every day)...never messed up an order and always fresh ingredients
2) Make the bread themselves, which is never crunchy, stale or soggy like Subway's
3) Delicious combos! I can't suggest which one to get, cuz they're all amazing but definitely go 1 ft not half size 

Cons:
1) NONE

Don't know if they still do it, but they had a punch card as well where after the 7th sub you get 1 free

First time ordering lets just say it will be my last! 
Wings are size for a baby. There barely any meat on it for a wing place the options of flavors are small. It was gross and i was still hungry after. Never again! 

Cant really write much considering there is nothing to go off of. If you really want good wings dont bother coming or ordering here.

Cute little hispter-y place with very friendly staff. The sushi burritos are huge but delicious and I love how all the ingredients are procured responsibly and eco-friendly. Great option for vegans! Hope to see tofu as a protein option in the future.

I just ordered from Matt's through Grubhub. I was looking for a juicy burger and a new place to try. I ordered the "Matts" sliders. They do not specify that the burger is beef, but I guess I assumed that it would be. However, what I ate did not taste like beef. It was gamier and the texture seemed different. I know some places use ostrich instead of beef because it is cheaper and supposedly tastes similar so maybe it was ostrich or a mix of both. I shouldn't speculate because I really don't know, but what I do know is that it didn't taste like beef. I ordered it with lettuce/greens, which were slimy and starting to turn that dark green/black that greens do when they go bad. I feel bad saying all this about a relatively new place, I do want them to do well, but I have to be honest. Those sliders were not good and I question what I ate.

Read about Naf Naf Grill in Philadelphia magazine. They offer somewhat different food options than the usual Philly fare. I became a fan of shawarma after seeing the Avengers and visiting Dubai. The shawarma was good and filling. The pita bread was different than what was offered in Dubai, but it was good nonetheless. There were more sauce options than I was use to. Unfortunately , I couldn't try them all on my first visit but that gives me a reason to return.

Wings are great! Prices not so much. 

We normally go on Monday and Tuesday where's it's wing night. 

Pros: tons of different flavors, you can eat in and normally empty, staff is friendly and helpful, clean and wings cooked fresh while you wait

Cons: you have to pay for dips (ranch blue cheese etc), no cups for water ( sounds cheap but judge your mother) and no thrash cans

Still worth the it, my one recommendation is to order ahead of time because it takes awhile to prepare. Enjoy

$15.07 for a brisket sandwich!!  This does not include chips or a drink.  It was $11 a month ago. I questioned the price increase when paying and was told it was due to the  cost of meat increasing.  I work around the corner and have been coming here with coworkers for 2+ years.  Good food overall and nice people, but I cannot justify the 36% increase and can lo longer eat here.  Just told other coworkers who usually join me and they were in awe.  Unfortunately, Fresco just lost some regular paying customers.  Almost forgot... DON'T order the cheesesteak panini.  Made that mistake once and it shouldn't be on the menu.  Trust me, just don't.

This place looks like a good idea but the sandwich I just had there was pretty disgusting. I got the fried chicken BLT sandwich. Thin, flavorless bacon on a gigantic roll with a thin fried piece of dark meat chicken. It had a big rubbery chunk in the middle of the sandwich. I'm OK with paying nine dollars for a sandwich if it's terrific. This was not.
Man, they gave me lots of food for about $9. I usually eat a lot, but this time I barely finished the whole meal. The meat is really good. Better than I expecred.

I realize when I type this that this is Checkers I am talking about, what do I expect. However, this is the worst Checkers (Rallys when I lived in the midwest) I have ever been to. I will never be back. There is so much wrong with this place I don't know where to begin. Food is typical of Checkers, however, their service is the pits. They take forever, you have to order from behind bullet proof glass, they don't even understand their menu and have overcharged me. They have forgotten items, and they are rude. I once stood there for about three minutes before they even acknowledged my existence. Terrible. I will never go back. Avoid this place.

I don't know why we keep coming back to this Checkers.  My husband loves the fries, so I think why we keep giving it just one more shot.  Well today I went and not only was the food not hot, they messed up the order.  Also...the mic in the drive through is horrible.  There is a lot of interference or something, but it is just bad.  I hope this will be our last time here.....

Customer service non-existent.  I was the only customer there and ordered a sandwich, which they gave to someone who came in and ordered after me. One of the men behind the counter noticed me standing there for a long time but said nothing, until I said to him "did they forget my order?".  He then said, "Oh, we must have given it to that other guy....do you want to wait?" No apology - okay, no thanks, I won't wait.

Pretty dope place for an afternoon drink. A friend and I went here instead of happy hour and we couldn't be more pleasantly surprised. Their beers are around $3 (which is happy hour prices), but what had me sold it for me were their wings, they were flavorful, made fairly fresh (as they only make small batches) and with just the right amount of crunch. It had a bar vibe with the drinks and hip hop music, but a chill lounge feel.

Must try for the wings alone!
Food was fine. Make sure to ask for a receipt. The cashier clicked through and tipped himself then had me just sign. Incredibly dishonest.
The service took FOREVER. It literally took 20 mins from us ordering to get out food. The chicken was disgusting and tasted fake. Yuck!

Jimmy John's has freaky fast subs. How freaky fast? I made a mistake in a catering order. I needed 60 sandwitches. My caterer had the wrong day (which was my bad). I called Jimmy Johns, and they actually had all 60 delivered within 30 minutes of the order. That's freaky fast, and my event was saved.

This place has chicken white and dark on the spot. Ready to order! 

We're from out of town and just left a local club. Perfect pace to comes

Garlic wings were great.  It comes with 2 sides and a drink for $11.95Next time I'll skip the cole slaw...........it really didn't have much of a taste except for sugary.  Very weird.

The onion rings were okay, you get 5 of them.

I really liked the corn peach corn bread which runs about $2 and something.

I'd go back again.

There's no place to sit down here...........you have to be lucky to find an empty table in the middle of the market, or an empty booth and eat standing up.

I love this concept of making something, in this case sushi, more accessible, more affordable, and more friendlier to the masses. It's a Chipotle-esque menu and where the customer can pick and choose what they want in their sushi burrito baby. Very fresh toppings. Definitely opt for the green papaya salad as one of your toppings. 

In many ways, this is a glorified bigger sized sushi roll that isn't cut up into 6 or 8 pieces. Or a really big hand roll. Or a really big rice ball concoction. But, I like it. I wish we had something like this in the Northern VA area. 

This is a highly portable meal, but it will get soggy over time. The fried corn consists of individually fried corn kernels, so it can be hard to eat. Do not wait to get home to eat these, these will get soggy really fast!

Friendly staff and two great rolls: the Chili Citrus Pork and the Slammin' Salmon. The seaweed did a terrific job of holding a good amount of ingredients in one wrap.

Shockingly, I think I preferred the salmon! The crunchy jicama plus the grapefruit citrus was just so refreshing and pleasing to the palate. The Chili Citrus Pork was no slouch with a great low heat that built as it was devoured.

The location is pretty tiny with a standing bar across the front window and one wall. The trash cans, while a good size and nicely color coded, took up perfectly good seating potential. Additionally a couple two tops could likely fit in the center of the room. Thankfully it wasn't too crowded when we were there. I could definitely see getting the rolls for takeout.

Looking forward to trying some more roll types!

The sushi burrito signature roll was very delicious and very filling. It came with a good amount of meat, but what threw me off was that the spicy tuna for the screaming tuna looked a bit patted. I would've thought it came with tuna pieces as opposed to a paste consistency. This might be because the tuna is suppose to be spicy so it's already mixed in with tuna. Anyways, I still thought it was very good to eat. Also the drinks were only a $1! Which definitely helps on a hot summer day

This is one on the best Taco Bells in the area!! I stop here from time to time when I'm in the city because every time I go, it's on point.

My only gripe is that one time I went and ordered a burrito supreme and its was literally most beans and a lot of them. There was like a small sprinkle of everything else. Otherwise, everything else I've ordered has been properly portioned, hot, and delicious.

Hands down one of the best Taco Bells.

Hai Street Kitchen not only looks, but makes food just like Chipotle as you can choose between either a roll or a bowl, and with various meat/fish/veggie entrees.

My boyfriend and I opted for the "zilla" option, which lets you choose two different meat options for an extra charge. We recommend shrimp tempura and tataki salmon for the ultimate sushi experience and if you're willing to shell out get the wasabi guacamole for an extra charge as well.

My only complaints about this place are one, there's not many seating options seeing as how the place itself is very small, and two, the prices are so pricey. For two Zilla rolls with guacamole we spent $25!

Regardless, it was worth both the drive and the money especially if you're craving for a different sushi experience.

I really hate coming here, but I can't stop eating their fries, so I'm doomed. The service here is iffy. Most of the time it's painfully slow. Once I came during lunch and was told they're weren't open yet because the managers had come in late. Who does that?!? I was even short changed a whole dollar once. I tried to tell the girl at the window she owed me $1, but she was convinced that her math was correct. To make sure, I even did the calculation on my phone and still no dollar. The manager came and sided with the young lady, so there was no chance of ever seeing that dollar ever again. They're lucky there's no other Checker's in the area. I just know to never use cash at this location.

Moving from San Francisco, I used to go to Sushiritto and loved it. Didn't think a sushi-burrito could get any better until I tried Hai Street Kitchen & Co! I wish the name was a little more catchy and described the sushi-burrito, but this was hands down better than Sushiritto! I am definitely going to become a regular at the downtown location!

Pierogies were tasty. didn't have a hot dog but would totally eat a ton more of the pierogies. Wish they had a little sauce out to put on them. Also couldn't find any silverware to eat them with either.

The best quick eats that I've found in the Gayborhood. Thick pieces of chicken in a batter that's light and not at all greasy. The sweet tamarind sauce is a favorite; when I opt for the pesto sauce, I save the leftovers for a sandwich spread. I'd also highly recommend their honey biscuits.

The WORST!!!!!! McDonald's I've everrrrrrr visited!!!! The worst! 

Waited 20minutes, 20 minutes!!! Till someone spoke to me, just to ask "oh, what did you order?"  just to get cold fries, and over an cooked chicken sandwich and the wrong drink. 

This location deserves NO stars, but it wouldn't let me post my review

I rarely go to fast food chains, but the heat and the thought of a frosty made me cave.  I don't like drive thru's, so I opted to hop in real quick, then take my food home.  Well, real quick turned into 20 minutes of a stalled line.  I'm not exactly sure what the holdup was, but the employee's didn't seem to care.  No one even pretended to hurry or look apologetic.  When I finally made it up to the counter (After I watched at least two people in line behind me walk out in a tizzy) the cashier took time to continue joking and talking with her co-worker before even looking at me.  No apology for the wait even after I was finally recognized.  I got my food in a fair amount of time, then stopped over to get some ketchup and the pump was completely empty.  Oh well, my frosty was still delicious.

I worked at this store for a while, but I've been back many times to eat since. The food is consistently good, and inexpensive. If I want a good sandwich, this is my place to go. I can vouch for the freshness of the food, the bread is baked multiple times daily, the meat is sliced in store, and the veggies are fresh as well. The best part about this, and all JJ stores, is that they're super quick. You won't be waiting around for them to make your sandwich, it will be done VERY quickly.

I went here for take-out and boy was it good! I ordered a fried chicken salad, 5 chicken wings, and a biscuit. The total was about $19 but there was so much food. The wings were large and the crust was amazing. Super crunchy and well-seasoned. The salad was great because it had large chunks of chicken, croutons, pickled onions, and a yummy dressing. The biscuit was soft and fluffy with a hint of sweetness. Really good take-out fried chicken and reasonably priced. I wish they had one in CA!

I am loving this place! Who wouldn't want a sushi burrito? I stopped in today and I was a first timer. They people behind the counter were very helpful, they explained everything. I ordered a shrimp tempura burrito with wasabi. Wow it was delicious! Everything was very fresh and reasonably priced. It's very  similar to a Chipotle but with sushi. 

Come to find they have a few locations in the area.We will defiantly be back. Solid 5 stars

The chicken strips were really good but the mac and cheese is definitely in the running for worst I've ever had. I'm not sure if it has jalapeños in it but there's something green and spicy, the cheese is bland, and I'm not really a fan of the breadcrumbs on baked Mac and cheese. The jalapeño cornbread was cold and dry but surprisingly sweet which was kinda odd. I will say that the sauces are amazing, especially the tamarind one. It's worth it if you just wanna grab some chicken to go but I wouldn't make a meal out of it.

Rude rude rude. Was served by a reddish haired middle aged woman. I smiled, greeted her (I was in a fab mood before I stepped in) and all I got was a loud "what do you want". Not a single smile the whole time. And in the end, when I asked for a bag with handles for my take out, she barks "you need to spend more to get that bag!". Wow. First of all, that's crap policy - I bought two meals shy of $20 and the flimsy little brown bag was bursting at the bottom - and second, what's with the attitude? This location used to be a lot better when it was newly open. Now the food is inconsistent - meat was dry and flavorless, portions were tiny - and the service is completely lacking. The King of Prussia branch has much friendlier staff and the food there is usually more consistent. I'm just gonna stick to getting my Naf Naf over there.

This place labels themselves as having these famous crab fries but there is NO CRAB in the fries or sauce (which you have to purchase separate).  I've had crab fries before, from other places, and crab fries should have crab in/on it, it's what actually makes it "crab fries". The fries here are crinkled and seasoned with a cajun type seasoning, that's it. Needless to say, I was pretty disappointed.

Interesting concept! I am always up for Asian fusion food ideas!

It is a small restaurant with only standing tables (one bench outside of its restaurant). The menu is limited and clear. Alternatively, you can have customized sushi burritos.

I had the steak option and my burrito was super yummy! It was juicy and flavorful. I definitely liked the seaweed wrap! So unique!
