Not 5 stars because if you are starving, you are NOT going to be full for $8/$9 here. 

If you are into healthy portion and eatery, definitely go here! 

If you are huangry, go to Chipotle instead and order extra everything just like this buzzfeed, then you will be stuffed!

http://www.buzzfeed.com/jessicamisener/ways-to-make-the-chipotle-burrito-person-hate-you

Food was average, nothing special. 

My one star review comes from the service. The guy we dealt with (assuming the owner based of what he was saying) was incredibly rude. My friend and I were the only ones in the place at the time and we had a few simple questions about the menu and asked for suggestions. The guy we were dealing with was very short with us, didn't want to hear or answer any of our questions, and was no help at all when he gave the most minimal effort to answer these questions. 

I would not go here again, nor ever recommend this place, simply because I would not want to support a business that does not care for their customers and treats them with such disrespect.

Apparently "craft fried chicken" is limited to wings and tenders that aren't even made fresh-to-order. They sit under heat lamps for who knows how long. I wanted to love it here because it's right around the corner from my apartment, but...

I've had the white meat tenders twice now, and they were average at best. They weren't dry or anything, but they weren't special. For $9 a pound, they weren't filling at all. 

The mac and cheese was dry (probably from sitting under that heat lamp all day). 

I chose the four dipping sauces (on two separate occasions) that sounded the least spicy, and they were all spicy (who puts wasabi in honey mustard?).

Fantastic service
Hoagies are so-so, but boy --
they sure bring 'em quick!

I needed to order lunch for a dozen people on short notice -- Jimmy Johns totally handled it, no problemo.

The food and cocktail selections here never disappoint.   The menu is consistently fresh with new options all the time.  I definitely think that Buckminster's is a fantastic choice for dinner, happy hour, or brunch.   We live right next door and we can't get enough!

This place was extremely disappointing. My friend "won" a happy hour that was basically an hour of open bar. This open bar was to include all draft beer and well drinks. However, when we got there at 7pm, they informed us that the draft beer system was down because someone had messed with the gas. We all ordered well drinks instead. Then they let us know that the tonic water was messed up, followed by letting us know that there would be no carbonation in any of the drinks. All drinks were served in small plastic cups and we were told to bring our cups up anytime we wanted another drink. All in all, first impression was that this place is pretty terrible and unprepared for a scheduled happy hour. Giving two stars for assuming management didn't prepare the staff for the whole situation and the bartender being somewhat accommodating.

Sliders were a little dry this time, otherwise A+(they were not dry the first time I ate here). The toppings were very good and the sweet potato fries were what sweet potato fries are born to be. Sold me the wrong soda by mistake (may have misheard me).

I live around the corner so I was excited when I heard this place was opening. I love FDR and P&K, so I was expecting big things from Rob especially after his travels, needless to say I was let down. I mean why the hell are bagged Good's chips a menu item? I will say I started with the Squid which was awesome and something I'd expect from Rob then I ordered salted radish. Now, I have been going out to beer/wine eatablishments for years and worked in the restuarant industry for 11 years. In that time I have never seen a block of cheese served with no accouplements til I got the cheese at Bickminsters. Seriously, was I expected to eat s block of cheese with a fork? Other menu complaints, having bologna and ham on the menu as an appetizer is way to similar. You can do better and I hope you realize that and make the adjustments.

Had lunch at Hai street today and I wasn't super impressed. The decor is contemporary and cute (although the space is small with only bar seating), but the food was just average. I had a custom shrimp tempura roll with cucumber, romaine, sautéed onions, shallots and spicy mayo but overall the taste was pretty bland. The food was fresh and the green tea was delicious, however I doubt if I'd return just for that.
I really like the food at Hai street and have been several times. I would normally have given it a 5 star review but today the staff were so rude I am not sure I will ever go back.

I'd love to say this place is great, but they don't deliver where I live.  


Let me rephrase.... They said they delivered and when we called back with an order, they then told us they don't deliver.  


I'll bump this up a few stars if they ever manage to get a sandwich to my door.  Wouldn't be a big deal if it wasn't 1 am in the morning.

I was really excited to try the sushi burrito since it had so many good reviews but the taste was average. I ordered the slammin' salmon and the crunch. The crunch burrito, I can barely taste the shrimp tempura since the shrimp was so tiny and one of the workers went overboard with the spicy mayo. The slammin salmon tasted better than the crunch. It was not worth $10 per burrito.  I cannot deny that the service was great though.

Steam table buffet inside the Reading Terminal. The food was all general American food, but tasted good and fresh. Some of the stuff offered is fried chicken, ribs, mac and cheese, fried fish, yams, mashed potatoes, collard greens, and cole slaw. There is also a large salad bar area. Overall, the food was okay and got the job done.

I had the slammin' salmon burrito. Quick service, great combos of sauces and veggies to bring out the flavor of the salmon. Very filling--you could definitely make two meals out of one burrito. Its the japanese version of chipotle in a sense. A bit pricey, but you'd expect as much for a sushi burrito.

Ok I had 0 expectations about those fried chicken. Probably another of those gas station quality stuff that looks way better than they taste. But I was so wrong. Crispiest crust ever with the juiciest dark meat. And the donfire sauce was so spicy but complements the fried chicken perfectly.

About 20 minutes ago, I wrote a less than flattering review. The review wasn't for the food, but for customer service. I ordered and paid for food through Eat24 and my food never came. I called the restaurant so many times but no one answered. I just got off the phone with the owner who was so apologetic and very nice. There was a mix up with Eat24, which allowed orders to be placed even though he was closed today. The owner offered to pick up the tab for my first order, which I appreciate. That is TRUE customer service! I am looking forward to trying the food. Thank you Matt for calling me, I appreciate it!

I like Popeyes but the staff here are rude and they need to get a grip. 

I refuse to eat here ever again!  Well unless someone picks the food up for me on lunchbreak..

I do love this chain! Since I'm from the Midwest, I've been enjoying JJ's subs for many years, but Philadelphia seems to have just recently warmed up to this crazy company. 
The service is always speedy, the restaurant is clean enough, and the subs are delicious. 
One tip: If you want a more filling sandwich, tell the sandwich pros that you want them to "Leave the bread in", otherwise they will rip out the insides so that you taste more of the fillings.
I've found that the prices vary, ie, the one here near campus is a little more expensive than the ones in Center City! Basically, the franchise is able to charge what they individually want. 
I definitely eat here frequently and don't intend to change.

I could eat here for every meal (and sometimes do)! This place is like the Japanese version of Chipotle, but soooo much better! (No offense, Chipotle.) Their ingredients are fresh, you can customize any roll or bowl, and their sides, like the Sweet Corn Tempura, are amazing!

Around the lunch hour, there is always a line out the door. But don't worry, it moves rather quickly. After the business day is over, you can get in and out very quickly. 

The staff is always beyond pleasant.

Work in University City and order from here pretty often.  The subs are good....not great but good. They are super fast with delivery. I mean, super fast. From the time I place my order, I start down the steps from my office and they are usually out front in minutes.  Here are my issues. The other day it took me longer than 3 minutes to get downstairs to retrieve my order. They called my office mates phone and she told them I was on the way. The delivery guy gave attitude because I wasn't there waiting for him. I have to point out, the delivery peeps aren't very happy or friendly. I'm sorry you have to ride your bike in freezing temps. Another issue...they regularly  forget something on my order . Over the last two weeks we ordered from them about 5 times ( I know, a little excessive). All 5 times something was left off the order. I love that they are that quick, but not at the expense of my order.  They need to work on that. One other issue....more meat in the sandwiches wound be a plus. Sometimes they are a little sparse. Overall, it's a quick, easy and descent lunch...but there is certainly room for improvement.

Food:5/10
Service:4/10
Atmosphere:4/10

OVERALL:4.3/10

The food tasted ok I guess. It's what you'd expect for a fast food restaurant. The service was pretty slow. When I ordered something they forgot it. Also it's dirty. It should be cleaned. Especially the play area.

Japanese sushi? No! Japanese burrito is what they call it. Went here after a company meeting and was amazed with the size and taste.

I had the chicken cutlet roll which you can choose the inside ingredients from many varieties. If you are hungry, you can choose the GODZILLA size which is double the size of normal.

They also do rice bowl's which looked very good as well.
Great place to eat from. Always excellent customer service and the food is made with patience and care. And the food tastes excellent. I would recommend any of the many burgers:)

After walking around the whole, I picked franks because the bbq chicken looked silly good. 

I ordered a couple things and I'll give them individual rating: 
1. Chili hot dog: 1/5, I think dc hot dog trucks are better
2. The potato-filled-dumpling-looking-thing: 3/5, it was average. I ate it without sour cream. Tasted like Mash potatoes in a dumpling.
3. BBQ chicken: 4/5, this is legit. The skins got a ton of flavor. Would eat again

I wanted to try sushiritto for awhile so when I saw this place I had to go in. It reminds me of chipotle but with Asian flair. You can choose what type of meat you want and variety of toppings and sauce. It reminded me of a huge sushi roll. For about $10, I think it's not a bad deal. The sauce in the roll ended up runny and kind of messy to eat. I will definitely go back when I have the chance!

If you're looking for something different and out of the ordinary definitely come here. The staff was super friendly and the burrito was pretty good!!! Make sure you come early though because they run out of things fast!!!

This was a new experience for me, and coming from Chicago that's saying a lot.  They have sushi burritos, filled with your choice of meat, fresh vegetables, picked vegetables and toppings, all rolled with rice and seaweed.  My friends and I shared the chilli pork and chicken rolls and found them fresh, and delicious.  The combination of textures, coupled with the flavors of the meat were fantastic.  I wish I could have brought some home with me.  The restaurant itself is more of a takeout style, but for a quick meal, it was comfortable enough.
Not anything amazing.... can get a better burger elsewhere. Bun bigger than the meat, Parmesan cheese on the fries smelled off. Sauces werent good. Just average if that in my opinion!

This place was a bit overhyped. Yes, the flavors are good but they could use some improvements.

I went about a week or 2 after this place had opened and I had the shrimp tempura sushi burrito. I was a bit disappointed in the simplicity of the prep. The seaweed came straight out of a packet but I was hoping that they would toast it real quick for a bit of the aromatic roasted seaweed smell. 

The rice was already prepped and loaded into a machine which was pretty cool and unique. 

I've heard the sumo steak sushi burrito is amazing so I'll have to go by and try that sometime but I wouldn't go out of my way to this place.

What Philly "hoagie" place charges you for cheese?
What Philly "hoagie" place has no small cups for side condiments?
What Philly "hoagie" insists that THEY must place all your condiments ON the sandwich--that they can't even put them on the side in the wrapper--and the condiments must be put on the whole sandwich not on half.
Welcome to Jimmy John's University City !!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Glorified Subway--no better.

Music is blasting so loud the order-taker couldn't even hear what we wanted-didn't matter anyway-cause they were gonna do what they wanted to do on my hoagie!

ONLY thing keeping them in business is they have a captive audience from the hospitals.

Japanese Burrito? Definitely interesting place.  The Hubbie and I tried the slammin salmon roll and hai street chicken roll.  Both were delicious.  If you like sushi rice and seaweed, then you have to try it.  The salmon was so fresh and yummy.... One suggestion would be to have avocado with it. They don't have that as an option but would be perfect.  We would def. come back for more!

I love sushi and I love the invention of the sushi burrito don't get me wrong. BUT the customer service really ruined my experience. First I had to over hear the fact that they didn't have any chicken at all then that they had no avacado salad. That takes away most of the options on the menu. Then to top it all of the girl making my burrito had the worst attitude. She worked like the place was super crowded, hastily and pushy. I asked if the mayo was super spicy, she said yes, then I said I don't want it then so what does she do, offer me the next spicyest sauce doesn't ask if I really want it then slathers a ton in the middle. Then she just started putting all the ingredients on it to make a roll on the board. They could have a great business if the people working there at least acted like they liked their job. Instead the great food gets overshadowed by bad customer service.

I came here before they did a few changes to the prices which I wasn't really happy about. I love the food, especially the mango habanero wings. Ugh amazing, and the seasoned fries are oh so good but you have to pay for dips and prices are just not worth it now. Although I might come back when I make a bit more money.

Dave's double cheeseburger is very tasty. I think they improved their recipe. On top of that I also ordered large Chili which I have been eating for years. It didn't disappoint as usual. There is absolutley nothing fast about their drive-thru. From the moment I drove into the line to the moment I got my food took about 15 min if not longer. My order also was missing a spoon (essential item for my Chili and hot sauce). Chili was cold and had to be reheated in a microwave. That slogan in my pic is bunch of BS. Service is lacking.

I'm definitely a fan of the size of these wonderful sushi burritos. If you haven't had one before, a sushi burrito does not typically include a tortilla or the traditional Mexican fare you might be used to. A sushi burrito is simply sushi ingredients in a hand roll, super sized. This place was delicious, and it's not hard to see why both food truck and stand alone locations are a success. 

These tight space doesn't encourage a lot of people of toddle, and the lunch hour in Center City is packed, so I anticipate taking your lunch to go. Enjoy the weather! Get outside! 

I ordered the Slammin' Salmon comprised of the tataki slamon, gochujang sauce, romaine, cucumber, pickled jicama, and red cabbage ($10.18) PLUS additional Avocado Salsa (additional $1.99). Boom right up to the Go Zilla price, but worth it. It's a bit of a pricey lunch, but hey, great fresh ingredients will do that to you. Also, you have the choice of brown vs. white rice, and I went brown without a regret. I particularly enjoyed the pickled jicama, the perfect blend of sour to the spicy sauce. 

Overall, it's a filling meal, not too bad for you, and oh so scrumptious. Can't wait for Friday when I go again!

Cheers, 
D

This Fine dining Mexican establishment has my heart. A tighter grip than the strongest bench vice of which any craftsman could dream. The cleanliness and friendliness of the staff and the establishment itself is both mesmerizing and captivating. Like a child's first day in Disney land, my eyes widen with excitement, each and every time I step foot through the front gates. My breath is shallow and short, and my heart palpitates as though I were making love for the first time, every time. Every bite of food I take within these hallowed walls, is like an orgasm in my mouth. Bursting with flavor and deliciousness in every bite. 

Aramingo Taco Bell, and staff - you are my first and true love. 

Love

Kirby

Ordered for takeout on caviar. We got a rice bowl and sushi roll. The rice bowl has salmon, which was a little shocking when it was sashimi. I got the sushi roll with chicken katsu with the miso dressing. Everything tasted really good; my only complaint was that the sushi burrito didn't stay it place. It fell apart after three bites and rice got everywhere.

This is a fantastic option for a lunch under $10. "Asian Chipotle"/ "sushi burrito" pretty much nails the description on its head, though I usually think "raw" when I hear "sushi" and my favorite options here are cooked. It is totally customizable, so you can switch up your order to match your cravings.  The recommended combinations are also fine choices with the best IMO being the Hai Street Chicken. Their sweet green tea is DELICIOUS and a perfect balance to your meal if you're like me and enjoy generous pours of spicy gochujang. It is worth noting that their staff is extremely friendly. There's always a positive energy in the place!

If you're torn between roll or bowl, I would go bowl because the nori tears easily and you run the risk of spilt saucy rice, which is never a fun clean-up. My favorite combo is bowl, chicken katsu, cucumber, red onion, red cabbage, papaya salad, yucca chips, and spicy gochujang. Yum!

Popped in here with the wife and daughter on a Sunday night. We were looking to try something fast and different. My daughter, who is living in the city while at med school suggested Hai Street Kitchen, describing it as as an Asian Chipolte.

I was a bit surprised, it is very small space. Most of the their business is take out. They had a standing counter but only 4 stools if you wanted to sit. The restaurant was very clean and bright.

We had 3 dishes, all bowls  THE HAI SATAY- grilled chicken, spicy peanut sauce, romaine,cucumber, carrot, pickled jicama, cilantro. This was OK, not really what I expected but not bad. I was anticipating a Thai or Indonesian style satay sauce. It had a little kick to it and the grilled chicken was good. You can chose either a bowl or wrap. 

SLAMMIN' SALMON -tataki salmon, gochujang sauce, romaine,cucumber, pickled jicama, red cabbage -My wife was pretty surprised as the salmon was sushi grade and not cooked. It is not that she doesn't't like Sushi,  just the menu didn't really make it clear it wasn't cooked if your not familiar with the definition of Tataki. Which we were not.

My daugter had the THE CRUNCH -shrimp tempura, spicy mayo, romaine, cucumber, pickled Jicama, grilled zucchini. This was an OK dish.

We also had the spicy Miso soup which was very good. My sweet iced green tea was pretty good also.

All of the food was fresh, light and seemed healthy. The staff was very nice. However none of the dishes really stood out as something special. It is a tad pricey for what you get also.I don't think we would go back unless I was in the are and looking for something fast.

Tried the Sumo Steak! A perfect combination of flan steak, sautéed onions, black pepper teriyaki sauce, read cabbage and asparagus- oh and crunchy onions in a fresh roll of white rice and seaweed! Spectacular food and service! Totally worth the hype.

Panda Express is one of my go to lunch options. They have by far the best Chinese food in Center City. It's always fresh and not too greasy. They serve alot of customers and do so very fast while always maintaining excellent customer service. Every time I go all of the workers are pleasant and courteous which leaves me walking away with a smile, a giant soda to power me through the afternoon, and some great tasting Chinese food.

3925 walnut  st location has yummy bean sprouts 
 .i'm spreading the word  sandwich was delicious!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

And they say people from fast food restaurants should get paid $15 an hour. HA! If you give me attitude when I'm giving you business, then you deserve that minimum wage. They ALWAYS forget to give you utensils and sauce and when you order something extra on your burger, SURPRISE, they take it all out. I asked for extra pickles not extra attitude. Stay classy BK.

Updated space on 40th street! The seating area is comfortable and aesthetically pleasing. Had a BOGO coupon to use and figured it was a good day for an inexpensive lunch date. 

The line was empty so took a minute to choose, but we got two burritos, one brisket and and pulled pork. Different toppings on both so we could see what was the tastiest. The worker behind the counter was quick and generous with the portions, which I appreciated. Compared to other point and eat restaurants, I think Qdoba is the most cheaply versatile to eat at, because you can stack your burrito or bowl for a flat price. 

Brisket was tasty, pulled pork was tastier, and the toppings were all fresh, but needed some salt and extra sauce for flavor. The chips and salsa were alright as a side, maybe a little stale. I'd go for lunch here again, for quickness and how filling it is for the price.

This is definitely my Chipotle, Japanese style. I made my own burrito with salmon, roasted beets, pickled mango, spring mix, asparagus, yucca chips and gochujang sauce. It was amazing. All ingredients we fresh and can't wait to go back.

Stumbled into this fast mediterranean eatery and was so surprised by the quality and flavor! I got the chicken shawarma rice bowl with onions, pickles and yogurt sauce. It was a great mix of flavours and the meat was well spiced with cumin and other things I couldn't identify. I also had a side of fries that were more like slices of fried potatoes, but we're actually very good!

cute little place with dozens of craft beer to choose from, along with a few other bottled drinks. we only had the chicken pot pie for food. so-so. but will go back and try the salad and perhaps the mac n cheese. the desserts looked great. cool atmosphere, great staff. check it out!

UPDATE.  It gets more disappointing each time I visit, the breaded skin of wish bone wings gets thicker and thicker, until the skin is about the same weight of the chicken, this is fraud.

Personally believe that the fried chicken tastes better than the university city one. Had chickens by weight the night they open up and it's so good. Having the southern sandwich today and this stuff is MASSIVE! It's very heavy so the buns are a bit thin to hold it, the sauce is sweet, the chicken can get a little bit less crispy in the sandwich. But still, I like the taste of it and ppl are very nice and welcoming :)

There is hardly a place to sit down, even during a late evening hour.  It's not a testament of a busy kitchen--there simply aren't any chairs or tables and you're forced to chow down outside on the curb.  Lack of dining room aside, the fresh, zesty ingredients are healthy and pair well with one another (pickled mango and salmon), but the absurd price (about 10 bucks for a salmon roll) doesn't warrant the casual effort of wrapping some rice and a bunch of topping into a single nori sheet.

Cool, cool, could be better. It's all hype, really. The workers didn't really seem to care about what they were doing. They throw the toppings on, and it was very inconsistent throughout. Our sauce was plopped on and poured on one side.

I got a salmon roll with brown rice, spicy mayo, romaine, carrots, zucchini, and cucumbers. The protein to vegetable ratio was terribly off. I didn't know how to feel about their salmon; it lacked that firmness that raw salmon usually has, and it looked like it had been left out for a while. I also wasn't sure whether or not they had attempted to cook the salmon. Every bite had either too many veggies or too much sauce--also kind of overpriced for the overall quality.

It was worth a try, but definitely not going to come back for it again.

I've been here a few times and even though I am giving three stars because the food tastes good, I am going to have to boycott because Hai Street is way too expensive.

I got the shrimp tempura and ordered to "go zilla" size because I remember feeling like the regular size didn't fill me up. They take out the same size rice wrap that everyone gets, and put two pieces of shrimp on it. I ask if that is really the amount they put on for a larger size, and I get a look, and one more piece of shrimp goes on. Nothing else is different about the size at all, just one extra piece of meat, for something like $1.50 extra.

I was pissed about it the entire walk back to my office. I paid $12.86 (including tax) for a burrito that is smaller than Chipotle, and I got attitude for asking them to actually give me the size I asked for. 

The thing is.......the burrito tasted really, really good. So what would be two stars gets bumped to three, because their ingredients are really fresh and delicious. But don't go there unless you feel like paying double for the amount of food you would normally get for that price.

Creative and delicious food, reasonable prices and a perfect array of choices. A fun and quick lunch for being on the go. We had the tuna tataki and the crunch pre made options. Next time we might be bold enough to make our own, but it'll be hard to choose!

I had high expectations of hai street having read reviews online.  It's a really cool concept, sort of the japanese spin on chipotle.  I had the shrimp tempura and chicken (go zilla).  Ingredients were fresh but i expected more i think.  there aren't too many options on the menu (you can probably check it out online) and i think ill opt for the bowl next time to mix it up.  

Pros:  healthy options, brown rice
Cons:  slightly overpriced, still hungry afterwards

Wonderful experience. It's basically an Asian chipotle. Definitely a great idea for Asian food lovers. I got the tuna/kimchi roll with the chips and wasabi guac. Gotta try the chicken katsu next time.

I visited the Hai Street food truck at 2016's first Night Market in Roxborough.  I tried the Slammin' Salmon sushi burrito which contains 
Tataki salmon, gochujang sauce, romaine, cucumber, pickled jicama, and red cabbage which was $11.  It came packaged in a cute hexagonal shaped box which was very convenient since I had to walk down busy Ridge Avenue with my food.  The burrito itself was a bit too large for me.  I ended up eating one half completely and then just picked out the salmon and rice in the second half.  I absolutely loved the gochujang sauce as it added a nice spicy kick.  I think I'll just stick to sushi rolls rather than sushi burritos since roll portion size is more manageable, but the flavors and salmon in the burrito were tasty!

The BBQ wings here are perfection! The have right balance of crispness on outside and tenderness inside.  They taste like they are cooked on an authentic coal BBQ grill. The sauce is also the right balance of tangy/sweet/spicy but not overpowering. You can also order sauce on the side. 

My other favorite is the cornbread.  It is very moist on inside and cooked just right (golden brown) on outside. 

We ordered Mac and cheese as well.  I will say it was average.  Not bad at all, but nothing to rave about. 

Overall, great fast takeout service.  We drive 30 minutes to Reading Terminal just to get these wings!

Not an incredibly extensive menu, but still a great experience! The concept is great and the burritos are yummy! I got the salmon and would totally recommend it. 
It's a fast food kinda place...so definitely don't expect your traditional sushi fine dining. 

Wish this place stayed open later though!

I must be upfront, I am a serious fan of this chain. So, there won't be much in negatives from me. I was just excited to learn that this place was nearby. I use the term nearby loosely, because it's 10 miles away. Oh yeah, the food. Love the lemon pepper wings. Honestly, there's several flavor options and all are pretty good, but lemon pepper is something special. One aspect that sets this place apart from other wing places is the great dipping sauce. Without a doubt, the best blue cheese dressing on the planet.
Burrito was really fun, but they did not put a lot of tuna in at all. Definitely a cool experience. But the meal was sub par.
Tasty meal for about $9. Essentially a Chipotle/Qdoba type of spot, but for shwarma and falafel.

This is a real time review! I am sitting in Neon Lobster right now- they didn't have water and offered us free sodas :) I am eavesdropping on the staff who is super friendly to every customer that comes in or calls . As the smell grows stronger - my appetite grows bigger (I'm waiting on bacon wrapped Scallops and two warm lobster rolls).  (10 minutes in) I can smell the lobster and hear my bacon squealing!! My mouth is now watering and my girlfriend is growing more hangry! As I wrote this they came out and said sorry for the wait your scallops are cooking!  Hold on here comes the food- it is simply amazing !!! I can't say enough !!!now let finish eating damnit !!!

This is definitely a gem of a restaurant. We have gotten take out multiple times and had them cater the rehearsal dinner for our wedding - both I highly recommend! Matt's has the best sweet potato fries I've ever had, hands down. The cheesesteak slider is amazing and was a big hit during catering. The crab cakes are dope. I love that they switch up their veggie burger seasonally. They have a really spacious indoor seating area as well that would be great for groups. The customer service is awesome too - we always feel welcome!

Wishbone is a pretty chill place to grab some chicken and sides.
It doesn't wow me and it's a bit pricey for what it is, but the food is solid. The chicken tenders are good quality and I like the Mac &a cheese.
The jalepano cornbread is decent as well.
The Baum mi chicken sandwich is surprisingly great.
Overall, this place is solid especially if you're trying to grab something fast and casual.

Not my cup of tea. As a die hard asian food fanatic I was really excited when I heard about hai street kitchens.  The idea of a susho burrito sounded genius. So afterwork,  me and my sister decided to try, and it definitely was not what we expected.  We got the slamin salmon and the crunch. The salmon was fresh-yes, but the tangy sort-off, gochujang sauce was masking the salmon taste. On top of that,  the lettice and pickled sliced cucumber threw me off a little. I think the rice would have been better if it was flavored with vinegar.  All in all, I think it was way too much going on to be considered sushi. If I had to eat there again I probably will only get rice and salmon. Maybe im more of a traditional asian food than asian fusion.

Jimmy John's always sounds good in theory but is fairly boring in practice.  I wish they had more vegetable options for the hoagies.  Service was quick.  Just nothing too exceptional to say beyond that.

My wife and I visited Buckminsters for the first time and had the perogie, cauliflower, and stuffed cabbage dish's well prepared and delightfully seasoned. The waitresses and waiters (sorry I am so bad at remembering names) were very helpful and welcoming. We look forward to another visit.

Amazing sushi burritos! Totally unique and super tasty. I wasn't sure how the quality of the sushi would be since it is a take out style place, but it was absolutely phenomenal. My friend and I ordered the slammin salmon, the sauce was spicy but insanely delicious. I recommend adding avocado to your burrito. 
It was a little pricey, I added avocado to mine and it was $12, but it's a lot of food and was well worth it. Service was fast and everyone was very nice!

This place is TERRIBLE! Do yourself a favor and avoid at all costs.

Just kidding! One of those places you want to Yelp, but would rather not, because you want it all to yourself, but then you end up reviewing anyway out of obligation. I'm probably gonna delete this review after I post it. Just saying.

Lines can be long, but service is extremely fast with that sushi robot. Really fresh ingredients and amazing flavors. We shared the Slammin' Salmon, the Hai Street Chicken, and the Sumo Steak rolls, and each one was different and delish. Slammin' Salmon made my heart smile. Definitely my new go-to. Not the cheapest lunch option for its portion size, but a fresh one. #worthit

-----

UPDATE: Been back a few times, and although always satisfying, it can get a bit inconsistent with flavors since there's always a different person assembling your roll.

Tried to go on their soft opening and the line was around the block. I am a sushi lover so sushi burrito was like....a thing for me. 

Finally had it for the first time today. Pick-up time was longer than I expected (30 mins) and I did have to wait in a line that almost went outside the doors along with every white business suit 20 something year old in center city but I must say, it was worth it. 

Great lunch portion. Raw salmon, veggies, and rice. I will certainly be back.

They really need to get a separate window for cashier and person giving food or something.  Took over 15 min to get something at 2:30 on a Saturday.  I literally watched over 7 cars (customers) leave due to the wait for the drive through.

**3.5 Stars**

My cousin recommended this place because it is infamous for the West Coast concept of a sushi + burrito.
Came here for lunch and there was not much of a crowd. Very clean inside. They have counter-top seating tables and small menus to take a closer look at. They offer recommended signature combinations as well as a DIY burrito/bowl. Since it was my first time, I decided to try a signature roll and ordered the Slammin' Salmon with brown rice; my BF ordered the Hai Satay.
My sushirrito was exactly like a spicy salmon hand roll but 10x bigger! It was good but honestly nothing exceedingly special. My BF's tasted exactly like the Thai chicken satay skewers but wrapped up in a sushi roll, again not bad but nothing special. At about the 3rd bite, our rolls were falling apart due to the flimsy nature of the seaweed so we ended up eating the rest of it by fork. The regular portion was just right for me (you can order bigger).
It was a good first-time experience and worth a try, but probably not something I would crave for the next time I come back to Philly.

Hai Street Kitchen

Taste: 8.125/10
Price: 8/10

$10 for a Slammin' Salmon (norwegian seared salmon, pickled jicama, red cabbage, lettuce, tempura crunch, gojuchang sauce). I got double protein in this

This made me happy. I thought I'd give it a try because this is across the street from my office, and I was surprised. The RATIOS were on point they didnt do me dirty w the too much rice in sushi trap I know all too well. I never have a clue what goes into sushi or any of these things but I know salmon so I said sure why not LOL. It was tasty it had a really nice flavor. I added sriracha and every bite was some boom boom pow. Id pay $10 for more of these im satisfied with the portion size and their menu is decently big. My only complaint is that the thing was open ended so every bite i took kinda pushed it out of the other side so it was a little messy towards the end but its all good

There are so many reasons to love this place. Their menu is full of options for people who love traditional sushi as well as the Philly cheesesteak lovers. I have one pet peeve with eating sushi and it's that the pieces are sometimes too large for my mouth and you can't quite cut sushi. Now there's the sushi burrito which allows you to take as big or small of a bite as you want. 

They have like 3 chairs to eat in the place. I wish they had a little more indoor seating. At least it's close to rittenhouse which allows for some great people watching.

Once I heard that a sushi burrito existed, I had to get my hands on one. It's delicious, everything about it. The staff is very nice as well. I got the raw salmon with zucchini, cucumber, spring mix, carrots, and wasabi guacamole. Their guacamole is great and everything tasted very fresh. I wish I could have this every day!

I would advise one not to go here. First of all, I walked in and the place felt like a sauna. I then checked the temperature and it said that it was 76 degrees in the restaurant. I instantly started sweating especially after waiting in line for such a long time. I had to press my body up against the counter to keep myself up because the heat in the place was overwhelming me. Also, Immediately after I ate my sushi burrito I started feeling nauseous, followed by a headache. The next two days I was constantly throwing up with severe stomach pain. Everyone I talked to said I must have been given bad sushi, which is the only reasonable explanation I can think of being that the sushi burrito was the last thing I consumed before my sickness started. I have had a good experience here once before months ago but needless to say I am scarred from this past one and will stay away from now on.

Was just here the people taking my order were rushing me and being super impatient. Basically got yelled at by the guy taking my order. Meanwhile some Junkie comes hobbling over to my car begging for change and drugs. (Not their fault). Got our order wrong but appeared to be correct when we checked in the car. Blasting hip hop super loud not giving a f**k about their customers. I will return but honestly I'm super pissed and want someone to pay.

Decided to finally try this place after walking by it several times. I ordered The Crunch, which is a shrimp tempura with brown rice and veggies.  I was very pleased with my choice. It was simple, delicious, and tasted fresh. I will definitely be back to try another meal of their menu.

It's a cool concept, but that's doesn't mean eating a sushi burrito is the best experience. 

The sauce for the slammin salmon was good. Eating the burrito was difficult because the seaweed would tear and the whole thing would fall apart. 

Not ideal on the go food, but it was ok. 

It can be summed up with: cool idea, but I'd rather have sushi or a burrito. Not them together.

This is my first Yelp review and it is only fitting. I visit this location at least once a week. I'd say I use the online services at least 90% of the time. The two young ladies that typically take care of the pick up orders are wonderful. The one girl knows me by first and last name, and is always super excited to see me. The regular line may appear to be lengthy, but this stellar staff always handles the rush.

Overall, the food is always consistent and delicious. Keep up the amazing work!!

Tried it out during my day trip to Philly to compare it to a similar sushi burrito vendor that I have tried in DC.  The flavor of this food is definitely meant to accommodate American taste buds.  If you are looking for an affordable, but filling lunch that you can take on the go with you around the city, then Hai Street Kitchen & Co is a good place that is worth checking out.  

The business model is very similar to the "Chipotle" or "Cava" concept with the customer holding the ability to choose whatever toppings (up to 4) he or she would like with their burrito.  One can also opt for a "salad" or a rice bowl.  

Everything tastes very fresh and the staff were very friendly and knowledgeable about their ingredients and helped me with my order.  I had the "create your own" roll with spicy tuna as my protein.

Great place for vegans and vegetarians! The food was fresh and delicious. I actually liked it better than Mama's vegetarian which is like right around the corner from this place. I'll definitely be back again.

What a great little bar - an updated corner bar for sure. After a yelp event down the street at Cafe Ynez I decided to join a small after party and get a bite to eat. The bar and the tenders were great and they have a fairly impressive wine and cocktail offering as well as a good draught beer list. I tasted the Mojo IPA from boulder Beer, Weequasher from Coppertail and Foul Weather Jack from Saint Benjamin.

I decided upon the Pork Curry with rice which was filling and delicious. The rest of the items on the menu (from an upscale bologna and cheese to a "Bacon Buddy" English Muffin with cured pork) looked terrific. Prices are reasonable and the service is very good so I will definitely try to stop in sometime in the future with my wife.

Good food and good company with about 6 or 7 other yelp elites.

Awesome! I've never heard of a sushi burrito before I was recommended to this place, but I'm super glad I now know what they are! The two ladies working when I arrived were extremely kind and helpful and got straight to recommending and making us two delicious burritos. They were extremely flavorful and delicious - and not too bad in price. 

I would definitely recommend this place.

I set my expectations too high for this place because I loved the concept of a "chipotle" style fast casual for ordering sushi. You pick bowl or roll, a protein, and then vegetables. I am amazed by the machine that spits out sheets of sticky rice (if you have ever made sushi by hand, you will understand why this machine is so amazing). I am awed at the sight of my sushi being rolled into a giant burrito sized monstrosity. I am drooling at the thought of shoving the massive roll into my mouth.

Like any good fast casual during the rush of lunch, there is no seating available. But that's also because this place is smaller than a bedroom. We scurry outside to find the nearest bench across the street. The sushi burrito comes wrapped in parchment paper in a sturdy cardboard box. Everything looks so good so far.

My expectations are for "chipotle style fast casual with great flavors" but In reality, this place is more akin to a "subway with average flavors." The flavor is a little better than the sushi you might get from a common sushi restaurant or one of those pre-packaged boxes of sushi from a grocery store.

Therefore, if you are craving sushi and want a quick bite, go for it. But I would go elsewhere for sushi, and I would go elsewhere if I needed a quick bite.

Also, it's a mess to eat. Your typical burrito has a sturdy tortilla skin, but your sushi burrito has delicate frail seaweed that isn't closed on the ends, so things easily fall out. Also, wait too long and the dry seaweed is now soggy.

I sent $18 on the worst food I have ever tasted! The wings wasn't done, why have the extra well done option and done even cook the wings. I mean I couldn't even chew the meat. To much salt on the fries soda was flat, just disgusting I will never order from here again!

I feel like I'm committing college student blasphemy when I say this...but sometimes I just get really tired of eating Chipotle.

Whenever that happens, I'm just really happy that this Qdoba can offer me Mexican food options that Chipotle doesn't.

If you're not sure what to get here, my go-to dish is the Mexican Gumbo with Pulled Pork and all of the toppings. It's hearty, filling, and it has the perfect amount of spiciness to add a little kick to the soup.

This Qdoba is pretty clean, and the decor provides a very warm and inviting atmosphere to dine in. The staff here are competent and efficient, and when there is a line, you rarely have to wait long to get your food. Luckily, because everyone seems to be obsessed with Chipotle on this campus, long lines don't really happen here.

If you ever get tired of eating Chipotle all day, give Qdoba a try. I definitely think it's underrated by Penn students.
Not a Restraunt its fast food. Always mess up your order. Terrible.

Really enjoyed this adventure my daughter found this on a foodie site can't wait to share with my sushi loving friends would come again price is reasonable for a sandwich and drink in the city .  I had the shrimp tempura roll with Asian slaw beets brown rice avocado salsa and ginger miso dressing and the  iced sweet green tea was good also limited choices of drinks but all looked and sounded interesting and were made in site -- seating is very limited a few bar stools and 2 standing tables outside looks like it does a killer take out business can't wait to go again

Delicious food, very reasonable prices. Very friendly owner who doubled as waiter.  The grilled mac and cheese appetizer was really good.  The grilled chicken skewer we ate was a substantial portion with skewered, grilled veggies and even pineapple, and a lot of tasty potato wedges, mixed with sweet potato.
Popeyes is Popeyes and chicken is chicken. Nothing special to see here except the side options are not listed on the drive-thru menu. The chicken was freshly cooked and hot!
Yummy fried chicken. Loved the southern style sandwich as well. They have a wide range of beers and it goes well with the chicken. I will come back again for sure.

I've gone to this popeyes maybe 5-6 times, always via the drive-through. The last time I went, the cashier "accidentally" held my credit card. I forgot that she had it until I got home, and immediately drove back within 20 minutes to get the card. I did not use the credit card anywhere else that day. The next day, over a thousand dollars of online shopping was charged to my card. I contacted Popeyes headquarters, filed a formal report, and ultimately got ignored. I haven't been to this Popeyes or any Popeyes since then and probably never will.

Edit: The chicken was great. But not great enough to cost my bank over a thousand dollars.

Checked out Naf Naf Grill last week (conveniently it is located right near my work which is a big plus!). I like how you choose your base, then meat, toppings, and sauce. I went with the pita with falafel with the tomato/cucumber mixture, red cabbage and added hummus to the inside of the pita. They also have various sauces to choose from - I went with Tahini which they drizzled on top. The pita itself was soo soft and warm (I believe they bake it fresh) and I would definitely order it again. I also got a side of chips which were okay. Next time I would like to try the hummus base with chicken schwarma!

My burrito was customized, I had the steak in it which was not cut right; the meat was so chewy... I couldn't even eat it properly without biting it all out. The amount of wasabi guacamole they put in there was a joke, especially when they charge $.99 extra for it. They also put the wasabi guacamole in my boyfriends burrito, which he didn't even asked for... And they still charged him $.99. The only good thing about this place is the fresh veggies they put in the burritos. This place is definitely not worth the hype, it's not even filling; I rather go to chipotle for more food and it's less expensive too. Overall two burritos at Hai's Kitchen costed us almost $24, ridiculous... I was so disappointed! If I was going to spend that much money, that better be the best sushi burrito I've ever had in my life, instead.. It left me feeling bitter, frustrated, and still hungry. I'm never coming back, they've lost my business.

Sushi Burrito where have you been all my life?  I love this concept, not only is it fun, but is also tasty and delicious.  I'm glad that they had options so you did not need to complete from scratch (I'm not creative enough to create something so tasty as the slammin  salmon).   MMM pumpkin miso soup- really?  why has no one else thought of this?  And the take out containers- so cute!

If you like old bay-style seasoning and French fries, then this is the place for you! Served with a cup of cheese on the side, grab yourself a little bucket of crab fries and catch a game while you're at it.
I had the warm Lobster Roll, and it was very chewy and tasted too fishy.  The roll and the fries were good though, and they were very nice!  Overall, not worth $20.

Not bad. A tinge overpriced, but I like the ingenuity! I mean in theory, it's pretty much an oversized handroll so nothing really imaginative about it, but they made it easier to eat (the seaweed is more brittle so it usually breaks away when you take a bite) and added some fusion elements to it. That being said, if you are looking for authentic japanese cuisine then you are in the wrong place. However, it's a great alternative to the hoagies/sandwiches that are traditional lunch staples. It also makes me feel a little less guilty because the ingredients are on the lighter side: rice, seaweed, veggies, choice of protein. Although, it's a bit easier to eat, it usually ends up falling apart near the ends. Different from a burrito or wrap, you can't really tuck the ends in for this "burrito". Be prepared with napkins and a fork.

It gets pretty packed here during lunch and there is very limited seating. I would recommend going outside of lunch hours or grabbing an early dinner. Not really worth it to stand in a line out the door for this.

I'm a fan. The first time I got the Slammin Salmon with brown rice rolled up. They give you a lot of salmon. The roll was a lot messier than I thought it would be. I don't really like messy so next time I went with a bowl with all the toppings of the Steak roll except substituted mushrooms. Those are some really good mushrooms. I'll definitely be ordering more of those with some different toppings. I find that the rice has a little too much soy in it for my taste so may switch to salad but overall I really like the concept. The chips and wasabi guacamole are also really good.

Suggestions to make it a little healthier: Add grilled chicken and/or shrimp, there's too much fried protein, and also back off on the sauce a little.

It's like a sushi burrito. Though at first glance it doesn't seem like a lot of food, it leaves you feeling quite satisfied without all the grease. It's definitely a healthy lunch choice! The line does get long during lunch peak hours. I'd say the best thing is the wasabi guac (extra cost but worth it!). I tried the tempura shrimp and it was awesome. I love the crunchiness with the rice. They also have different types of crunchy things in your roll. I couldn't hear them very well, so I chose a random one. I'd definitely come back again to try their salmon! I also want to commend them on the hexagon shaped box! It's super cute!!

Now that the colder months are behind us, time to think about spring and summer. Thank goodness Neon Lobster can help us do that in Pennsport! I went yesterday and had the Maine Lobster sandwich combo. The lobster was on a nice grilled piece of bread and the portion was definitely worth the price. Also, the fries are DELICIOUS!! I don't think that happens very often with take out places, but these are worth it. I can't wait to go back to Neon Lobster for the Warm Lobster roll.

I live around the corner and feel really awkward getting chicken fingers from real restaurants, so this was my last resort. 

The chicken is decent, but definitely not worth the price per pound (especially when there's more breading and less chicken). The mac and cheese is dry and burnt, but a step up from Wawa. 

All of the sauces are spicy (not like "my mouth is on fire" hot, but not even the honey mustard is sweet). And I'm gonna go ahead and be that guy to say 75¢ is too expensive for the size of the containers. Should be 50¢ (it adds up, dude). 

The beer selection is pretty decent, but the prices for a place like this are pushing it at 50¢ to $1 more than anywhere else.

Basically only come here if you're drunk.
Interesting combination of ingredients that taste great. Unfortunately mostly suitable for take-out, few seats.

Franks is my default when I go to redding terminal.  Their honey glazed wings are off the chain!  I usually get a combo platter with 5 wings, Mac and Cheese and Corn.  These are the best full wings I have had!
Thought I'd give this new neighborhood place a try but very disappointed. Tried the chicken shawarma with couscous. Chicken was cold, slimy and didn't taste like real chicken...

Sloppy, lousy, senile.
It takes a lot out of me to go out of my way to make a Yelp review.
They're so slow and sloppy. They're so miserable that they want to spread it. I have seriously contemplated whether to work here or not just so I can show these guys how they should work.

Located in the back of the food court at the liberty place mall. Definitely among the top 3 most generous chipotles I've been to. Don't be scared of the line! They're really efficient and it moves FAST. 

Minus 1 star because it's a little bit rushed, I got tacos once and the toppings were all over the place.
The best chicken, hotdogs, cornbread EVER!!!! The food  is sooo fresh & the place is always super clean. The staff is courteous and very helpful. Robert

Oh hai! I had heard great things about hai street, none of which I can repeat. I was completely underwhelmed by their food and don't think I'll ever go back. 

I thought almost $10 for a rice bowl was a bit much. $7-8 is definitely more reasonable. The presentation was disgusting, with everything slopped together into a cardboard container. The worst part was the 5-6 tablespoons of their house sriracha poured over my meal. I ended up throwing half of it out because it was drenched in a weird red sauce. 

The concept is good and inventive, however the execution was poor.

Phenomenal!! I got the classic dark tenders and they were the perfect amount of crunchy on the outside and moist and juicy in the inside. Never had such great tenders in my life! I also got the orzo salad and half baked cookie- both delicious. So many options that I didn't get to try... Will need to come back! This place is very friendly and has unique yummy options. My only complaint is that it is a little expensive.

I happened to pass by this place on my walk from the train station to my hotel. It's great for a quick fix of classic Middle Eastern food (falafel, shwarma) that is well-made and tasty. The price is right too!

I figured I'll give it a 2nd try ,yet again I was let down . I ordered a ten piece combo meal although the chicken wings and sauce were really good the fry were burnt and extremely greasy. The lack of cleansing in this store is simply downright awful. From dirty tables,dirty greasy floors, dirty  bathroom sink ,nasty greasy food trays and dirty main entrance door glass with handprints all over it. That let's me wonder how prep their food. I'm guessing that was the reason why the place was empty at lunchtime hour. One star for the chicken wings.

I'm so glad that Point Breeze is getting more restaurants! Restaurateur Michael Pasquarello (Cafe Lift, Prohibition Taproom, Bufad, Kensington Quarters) has expanded into South Philly with chef Rob Marzinsky (Pub & Kitchen, Fitler Dining Room).

My husband and I ventured here on a weekday around 6:30PM. The restaurant was semi-packed and we were seated in the front. To start with we ordered cocktails. My husband had an Old Fashion and I ordered a Dirty Martini (I was a little disappointed that there were no cocktails with vodka - just a personal preference). We then ordered our starters which were the Fried Parsnip and Mushrooms (I think this is a seasonal dish). Both were excellent! The mushrooms had such complex flavors and very bite was memorable! For our main course we went with the Bologna and Cheese and the Crispy Chicken with buttermilk, watercress, and fried onion.  My personal favorite out of the two was the Bologna and Cheese. For dessert we went with the maple toast with maple toffee and ice cream which was melt-in-your-mouth good.  

I would say by 8:00PM this restaurant was packed which is great for our neighborhood!  Our waitress was so nice and was very knowledgeable about the menu. All in all we had a great time and will be coming back!
I cane into the restaurant to buy a dessert.  The staff decided to ignore me for about five minutes straight as I stood there waiting to pay.  I turned around and walked out.

The only thing keeping this from being a 5-star review is the high price. (Or should I say, "hai" price??)

However, to help get rid of the price guilt, I recommend taking advantage of their deal on sweet green tea, which is 99 cents when you buy it with a sushi burrito. 

Food-wise, this is an awesome alternative to the plethora of greasy and carby offerings in the Rittenhouse area. If you're going to be spending $10+ anyway on lunch in this neighborhood, it might as well be fresh and nutritious. 

I got a Slammin' Salmon roll to go, and it was fresh, flavorful, and delicious! It was a perfect balance of protein and veggies, and the pickled jicama added great texture and flavor. 

The very first bites are always neat, but when you get to the ends of the roll, they loosen up and get all over your hands. Since this is the second time I've eaten here, I was prepared and got a utensil set from the counter before checking out. This completely saved my fingers from being coated with spicy Gochujang sauce. 

Overall, great lunch option to take "to go" and enjoy in nearby park.
The apricot corn bread is yummy!! The chicken is delicious!! It has a different taste than what we are use to when getting BQ chicken.
This place is hella delicious. Omg. I have no words to describe my joy. It can get packed but that's how you know it's delicious.

Stopped here on two occasions over the course of Outfest. It's a great place to people watch if you sit at the window. They also have an EXTENSIVE selection of beers from which to choose. Checking out is a bit laborious as the staff don't seem to have a handle on the process or even opening the beer for you. 

The second visit was the the problem. We stopped by after a concert (around 11:30pm) for food given the limited options downtown. Just say no folks. We had the most interestingly disgusting chicken tenders and mac/cheese we've ever had. We couldn't even finish them. I mean the aftertaste alone was enough to make you sick to your stomach.

Come for the beer, run away from the tenders!

I was just visiting the Philadelphia area for a day and this place was definitely on my list. I've heard so many great things about it I just had to go! I got their slammin' salmon signature roll. It was great. Only down side was that the salmon wasn't trimmed correctly and was left with some chewy bits. Other than that, everything was fantastic. They also have a brown rice option!

I've been going here for breakfast and lunch for about a year now I love their food!! There customer service is great too I love talking to the girls!!! I went here today and sad to say they must have changed owners again I didn't see the usual girl cook it was a man. He didn't make my breakfast platter right!  maybe next time around I'll order again.
The food presented to you looks unappetizing. The food is ok, but I wouldn't recommend going here. Make the extra effort and go down a few blocks to the WaWa.

MATT's is such a great deal with amazing sliders. The classic sliders are my favorite, but the mac and cheese is also delicious. The $5 mac and cheese comes with fries, which is way too much food but quite the steal! The workers are always very friendly.

How I heard of this place: My first memory of Wendy's might date me: commercials from the 1980s of a cute, old woman yelling out, "Where's the beef?" This, however, was my first taste of a full Wendy's meal.

Type of cuisine: Burgers. Fries. Frostys. "When Dave Thomas opened our first Wendy's restaurant in 1969, he opened the door to a new gold standard in quality food. His words "We don't cut corners on quality," affected everything from our hamburgers to our customer service. When other restaurants were using frozen beef and mass-producing food, Dave developed an innovative method to prepare fresh, made-to-order hamburgers, allowing us to quickly serve high quality and variety to millions of customers daily. He coined the phrase, "Quality is our recipe." Every day, we honor his legacy and continue to live through his values and fresh philosophy by using select, premium ingredients and serving food that's made fresh with every order. That's the way it's always been and that's the way it will stay."

Ambiance: Being in a rush to make it to our Thanksgiving weekend destination in the beautiful village of Warwick, New York, there was no time to go indoors. I imagine that it resembles the likes of other fast food chains: plastic chairs and laminate tables, a walk up counter with registers and the kitchen beyond. The drive-thru, similar to others, gave us pictures to enjoy while placing our orders through the two-way speaker, as we drove around the manicured grassy mound hosting the displays.

What I ordered: I ordered the Bacon Deluxe Single (but ended up with a double), as did one of my dining companions: "Three strips of Applewood Smoked Bacon piled high atop a hot 'n juicy beef patty, made to order every time. Add American cheese, cool and crisp veggies with a little condiment love and you've got a hamburger to satisfy your senses." He also ordered the Double Stack: "Two junior hamburger patties topped off with American cheese, ketchup, mustard, pickle and onion. Made fresh when you order it. Big on taste and small on price!" My second dining companion chose the Triple Cheeseburger Deluxe (minus tomatoes): "Our delicious hot 'n juicy beef patty topped with all the essentials: American cheese, pickles, onions, tomatoes and lettuce." We each also enjoyed a 5-piece Chicken Nuggets: "Eat with your fingers. Crispy outside, juicy inside, Wendy's® Chicken Nuggets are all-white meat. You choose the sauce: barbecue, honey mustard, sweet and sour, ranch or honey." And our meals were each accompanied by fries: "Let's face it--everybody's got fries. Wendy's has got something special. Naturally-cut from whole Russet potatoes, cooked skin-on, and served hot and crispy with a sprinkle of sea salt for a taste as real as it gets. You've had fries. Now try some Real fries." My meal came with a small soda, Sprite; Samyar enjoyed a large Coke and Chris substituted the soda with a vanilla Frosty, made with fresh Grade A milk and rich cream, thick enough that a straw and strong slurping muscles could hardly handle it.

What I loved: My favorite part was the fries, as it nearly always is with fast food. I enjoyed the somewhat less salty, soft, doughy natural cut strips of delicious potato. The chicken nuggets were also juicy, tender, with a crisp outside. The bacon, abundant, crisped to perfection. The Frosty a thick, vanilla cup of delicious.

Why I loved it: Quick. Easy. First time at Wendy's, celebrated with two of my favorite people. I am also sort of excited about my next trip to Wendy's (though not any time soon), when I can sample one of the baked potato options. Yum!

Cost: Low to average ($5.49-$7.99 per burger combination meal)

Excellent food - tasty and fresh.

My favourite option is to build your own with Chicken Katsu, Spicy Mayo and veggies.

Ordered 1/2 lb of wings, got 4 pieces. The menu says 1/2 lb yields 6-8 pieces of wings - a complete lie. Sauce is good (pesto Parmesan). The star of the show, wings, are ironically dry. Mac and cheese is good, very salty, if you're into hypertensive diet.

Really delicious and fresh ingredients, but definitely take a few minutes and order online rather than waiting in line! 
The pita is super soft and fluffy, and pairs well with a side of hummus (which is delicious all by itself). Great ability to personalize your meal and make it exactly how you'd like it.
I might consider requesting "extra sauce" next time I order a bowl, as there wasn't enough to incorporate fully into the bowl.
The "fries" are actually more of a chip, and while it only had a little crunch, it had good flavor and helped with the burn of the harissa sauce.
Cute dining space, just really small! Judging by the line, not all of the patrons would be able to eat in the dining room if they wanted to. For the time being, there is outdoor seating available, but that window is quickly closing.
Will definitely be coming back. A weekend visit might be better, where it will hopefully be less crowded!

AHHH even more amazing than I'd ever imagine... Half a roll satisfied me (even though I was starving!) and the other half made a great lunch the following day. I got the chicken katsu, spicy mayo (yum!), brown rice, romaine, carrots, and cucumber! AHHH so yummy you have to try it out. The drink and custom roll was about $10

The utter stupidity at this location is astounding! They messed up my order not once, not twice, but 3 times! This location should win a national award in "Not giving a shit!" How can you fuck up a plain cheeseburger 3 times! The people behind this counter looks like it causes them physical pain to do their job! They just keep Fucking up your order until you just give up! It was so ridiculous that I couldnt wait to "Yelp" about it!
Great place to grab some sushi burritos! Lots of toppings to choose from. The staff are polite and very welcoming. Great environment! Music and places to sit.

Think of this as eating a giant unsliced sushi roll or like a burrito, but instead of a fajita as the skin, you have Nori (seaweed) and rice. 

I tried the shrimp tempura sans the spicey mayo and I tried the yucca and shallot as crunchy options.  It had a really nice flavor overall except you only get two pieces of shrimp tempura and the Nori (seaweed) was surprisingly oily.  Regular seaweed that you have for sushi isn't oily at all, so I wasn't sure why there was an abundance of oil soaking through the paper.  All in all, $6.99 (if you get the vegetarian option which is portobello mushroom) to $8.99 is a pretty good price range and I'd come back to try the flank steak wrap or the shrimp tempura again (yeah, despite only getting two pieces of shrimp).   

There's a counter with some stools but otherwise, not much seating area so this isn't the place to bring a giant group but otherwise, nice place to grab a bite or something to go.

Oh QDoba.  You are always there for me when I need that 1000 calorie burrito.  Your food prep people are always so quick and efficient.  QDoba - you have caused the schism between my belly and my rational mind to expand considerably.   Seriously though, good size burritos for pretty cheap, and the beans/rice is totally edible.  You're not going to get the inner-Oaxaca eating experience here, but they'll do the job of satiating your craving for down and dirty mexican.

I much prefer the quality of food from this location of Hai Street over that of the one that just opened in University City. The sushirittos are craftily rolled too, so that mine didn't fall apart even when I was walking around center city hastily eating the whole thing in less than 5 minutes. The atmosphere is very much a grab-and-go type restaurant instead of a sit-down-and-hang-out type, so if you want to get a roll or a bowl and have a picnic or bring to your next meeting, this is the perfect place to stop by! 
I got a sushirrito "rolled your own way", and was happy to report that the rice was not weirdly pickled this time, the salmon was fresh, and the vegetables I stuffed into it nice and crunchy. I also added peanut sauce, which had a great consistency and crunch to it. 

If you're looking for better quality food (for a somewhat higher price, but for healthfulness!), come to this location. If you want to socialize and hang out with friends and talk about your sushirittos in the restaurant, stop by the University City location instead.

Ugh, this place. I am unfortunate enough to live across the street from this place. If I didn't live here, this is one of those fast food locations I'd visit once and never go to again. 
But of course, it's just too convenient sometimes. 

The food sucks though. It really does. Every chicken sandwich is dried out. Almost every burger is burnt. All the fries and mushy and cold. The only thing that doesn't taste awful are the pie thingies they have, but there's no possible way they could screw those up, right?I mean, they're sent to the place pre-made. The occasional stacker is okay too.  

If you like/love/have a weird hankering for Burger King, you should find another location. You never know when you may walk into this place only to be told there's no burgers. 

I'm not joking. It's happened. Twice.

My friends and I tried this place because we were in the mood to try the Pierogis! For a platter of either Pierogis or BBQ chicken, you can choose 2 side items and a drink for about $12. A decent price for the reasonable amount of food you get. The BBQ chicken was good and flavorful. The mac and cheese and fries were standard, nothing amazing. One of my friends had a hot dog and she thought it was really good! My Polish friend said the Pierogis were pretty good too! 

The food was just average. I feel as if there are better vendors to try in Reading Terminal. Yet, Franks A Lot is still a good choice to try some Polish food! I would come here again for the Pierogis.
It tastes like a normal sushi, except it's bigger. The prices are quite expensive... Awesome places for teenagers. I tried the tempura shrimp, I liked it!
Pretty quality chicken for a great price. The wings and tenders are bigger than your average. Crispy outside with a super moist inside.

I became obsessed with the burritos here - called them gerbils since that's about the amount of mass you're putting in your stomach. Favorite thing to do was to load up the burrito with verde tabasco sauce. Also a tip: if you get the vegetarian burrito, you get guacamole for free. That's the cheap/poor college student in me that's talking.

Great subs, but they don't have consistency in their "policies". I ordered delivery from JJ twice and there has never been a problem. Now they said that they can't go past 44th Street when I live on the corner! So I said fine can you meet me at 44th and Chestnut and he goes yea sure! Asks me my name and number and then out of nowhere he said sorry we can't deliver there. Come on don't get my hopes up and then bring it back down. Very disappointed

If you work in the area, like I do, it's a great spot for a quick lunch.  They have a kale citrus salad that is always on point.  The hot food items are hit or miss.  I raved about the fried chicken tenders to a friend, and then on my next visit they were stringy, dry and old tasting.  I vacillated between 3 and 4 stars quite a bit but had to settle at 3.  I've been here several times and the quality, variety and friendliness of cashier has been inconsistent.

Good food. It may have been because we can 30 min before close but the meat was a little on the dry side.  The menu is also very limited. 

Spotlight: the falafel was made fresh for us and it is the best I've had in a while. I'd go back for it

Its expensive and its simple.  But somehow its also amazing.  The line was long, but their setup was insanely efficient and went quickly.  My husband and split and big one with cheese and they went down fast.  We are from Texas and never had crab fries before, what a genius thought.  If I am back in the Philadelphia area, I will definitely seek out a Chickie's and Pete's for some of those crab fries!

Great place to hang out, watch sports game, and drink beer. 

Must order sweet potato fried, mussels, and blue crab!

Blue claw is very meaty near the core and no meat in the legs, but sweet and delicious. 
King crab legs were not fresh and relatively difficult to crack open. They were more of a plasticky twistable texture. 
Snow crab was good for their legs.

Not really sure how I am supposed to eat these tacos. Seriously? For a restaurant constantly plagued with controversy regarding food safety, you'd think they would be on their A game. This is pathetic.

I can't quite figure this place out.  I love the neighborhood, the vibe is sort of a quirky science bar?  The food is pretty exotic and I think it delivered.  I just couldn't quite figure out what I was experiencing....great bar food or quirky restaurant?  The wine list was just ok and quite expensive for what I got.  I'm going to check this place out again because it does appear to have potential.  I have just found that when I leave a restaurant and I can't quite figure it out, it doesn't bode well for the place.

it is what it is.
i come here for naked burritos. It's pretty bland, I have them throw each and every salsa on it and it still needs something.

I always hate coming to this location. The guys here never wrap the burritos well, so the burritos up falling apart even before I bite into them. The ingredients are also not as fresh. Last time I ordered the Hai Street chicken here, I could tell that the chicken was dry, overfried and way too salty.

My advice? Either save your money for a better tasting lunch, or go to the University City location instead, where they actually know how to make these right.

Tootsies has been consistently good over the years, and a best bet if you want to grab a quick meal at the RTM and not fight the crowds. You can usually find a seat around the perimeter. Priced reasonable as it's a help yourself deal and food is weighed by the pound. Pretty good if you like soul food, and the salad bars have always been fresh and stocked well. I'm a big fan of their tuna and chicken salads, fresh and none of the annoying celery. Hot foods like the meatballs, chicken wings, roast beef, pasta, and veggies, I find to be pretty good as well. you will assuredly find something you like here! I think a lot of times, this place gets over looked and is under rated since there are so many great and popular choices at RTM. But I'll tell you, Tootsie's has its loyal following for the locals and working crowd in the know.

Believe the hype! This newly opened spot is cranking out some seriously good eats. I was fortunate enough to have someone order a few rolls to go for me.

I had the opportunity to try the Sumo Steak, Hai Street Chicken, and the Slammin' Salmon. The salmon stood out as the best of the 3, with raw fish in a gochujang sauce and pickled mango. The steak was almost as satisfying in a teriyaki sauce. The chicken katsu ended up being the least favorite because the appeal of katsu is the crisp breading, and that was lost in the roll.

I was expecting the rolls to be loaded with rice Chipotle-style, but was pleasantly surprised to see only a thin layer. I was also worried about the roll being held together with the nori, but had no issues with the rolls falling apart. Although each of the rolls had a crunch element due to julienned vegetables, definitely add yucca chips into any of the rolls to elevate them to the next level.

One downside is that I hear the lines might be crazy. I think I'm willing to brave the lines to see what else the menu has to offer!

Absolutely horrible. Normally I give places a second chance, but clearly they don't deserve even 1. They have given me the wrong wings on multiple occasions. This is the only wing stop location that is close by. On this visit, the cashier did not greet me. In fact, she had her back turned and had me standing there while she finished her personal conversation. There were 4-5 workers talking, cussing, and laughing while I waited over a half hour for my order. When I received it, the wings were the wrong type yet again. I requested fresh fries and one worker in the background said "no." I am appalled that this place hasn't been shut down from subpar customer service. Better off making wings from home. Unbelievably bad experience and it will be my last.
Fairly quick, reasonably priced Chinese food. It's not going to rock your world, but you'll get a decent lunch with plenty of seating.

Hoorah for the Wendy's triple baconator! My wife tells me I'm going to be found dead at Wendy's for getting this "heart-attack" burger! I love the fact that they have the calorie & fat counters listed with all of the items they serve, pretty cool & useful (not that I need to worry about calories with my skinny behind self:)!

It's hard for me to find anything wrong with this Wendy's because this is a laid back crew. I tell them not to "f- my" order up ant hey repeat exactly what I say to the staff in the back (late night, no-other-customers-to-hear-the-cursing-joke type of thing!!!)

Jimmy John's is a solid choice if you want a good sub. Definitely a hospital favorite, at least from what I see in the the ED. 

The sandwiches won't leave you stuffed, but they are good size, the ingredients are all fresh, and it is relatively cheap compared to other places. Staff is friendly and very efficient too. 

Pepe: Nothing too crazy here...this one is like a better-than-average ham and cheese, which is made better x2 with the addition of bacon.
Totally tuna: I'm not usually a fan of tuna, but it was fresh, tasty, and I enjoyed the "tasty sauce." The slices of cucumber switch things up a bit and also added a nice touch and crunch. Unless you have your toothbrush, a bottle of Listerine to gargle with, and three packs of gum, tell them to hold the onions because they go all out on this one. 
TURKEY TOM: More like turkey nom. Quality turkey, lettuce, tomato, mayo. Great option.

So good, filling and pretty fast. Wanted to try the sushi burrito deep fried but it was obviously place had just been slammed and there was only one server. Will try it next time. Overall great idea and tasty dish!

Had the salmon and tuna specials. The quality seemed good and service was fine. Two issues:

1) The sauce is overwhelmingly sweet so that the fish is completely drowned out. It was like a sushi burrito with sugar. 

You can order your own way so probably next time I would stay away from sauces. 

2) We ate at the counter. The a/c comes out blowing through vents at you feet so that the four of us were freezing. Maybe there's a way to divert them away from diners?

No surprises here, but then there aren't usually surprises with a blowjob but you're always glad you got it.  Splendid, spicy fried chicken, quickly and reliably served at an impossibly great price.  Sides and biscuits are imperfect so I'm not giving it 5 stars, but the rice and beans is probably your best choice...especially if you hit it with a little hot sauce.  Really love this place.

Worth pointing out that this place probably has the most helpful and cheerful staff on any fast food joint in Philly, so bravo to them.
The Buns can be unfresh and stake tasting sometimes. You can tell that's the Fries were unthawed. They frequently mess up my orders as well.
