The staff is friendly and the food was decent. The restaurant is clean also. Especially compared to the McDonald's that's across the street, which is the grossest McDonald's I have ever been in.

I haven't been to this location in quite some time. I walked up to the counter to find chicken wings, chicken tenders, fries and biscuits. Everything looked like it was made in house which is always good. 
I ordered chicken tenders with a side of fries. The tenders were white meat (which I loved) and it appeared to be marinated in a blend of spices before being covered in bread crumbs and fried! The lady at the counter weighed my food and gave me a price after asking what dipping sauce I desired. She then told me the fries would be just a minute and she would bring them to my table.

Since I was waiting on my fries, I decided to begin eating my chicken. Once my fries came, there was a basket of shoe string fries with a dipping sauce that did not appear to be ketchup. It would have been a five star rating, but the fries were cold. Since I had to wait for my fries, I was expecting them to be hot.

My suggestion is to go the this place earlier in the day to get everything nice and fresh. Otherwise, it's a nice alternative to Chil-fil-A or Popeyes in the area.

So, so delicious. I have been waiting to try the sushirrito concept for SO long now, and Hai Street does it so well. 

Love that you have the option of the wrap, a bowl, or a salad. More options, the better. The ingredients are fresh and tasty, and the size of the wrap is also pretty decent for the price (which does seem pricey at first glance-- however, you really will be the perfect amount of stuffed/full after the meal!)

Definitely opt for the wasabi guacamole (that will be an extra 99 cent charge) because it is super tasty and adds some great creaminess to your filling. 

There really is no seating in the restaurant-- which is kind of a bummer-- but besides that, loved my experience here. Would definitely go again!

I could eat their Spicy Tuna burrito for lunch every day. It's that good! I still have dreams about it...

Checked out this place for the first time last week and picked up the Spicy tuna and Salmon specialty burritos and a sweet green tea to go for lunch before the lunch rush. 

The staff were super friendly and really knew how to make a sushi burrito. Everything was fresh and delicious, and surprisingly cheap. Can't wait to go back!

I got their crab fries. They were decent fries with crab seasoning. I tend to like crispier fries but their's were a bit chewy, which confused me. However, I like fries in whatever form so I finished them off. Will order their other items next time!

This place is the tits. Best fast-casual concept in a long time. Sushi Burrito aka sushi-rito. I think the only places that have them are NY, SF, and Philly. So definitely enjoy this place while the concept is still novel. Pretty soon this will be common across the US - and feel good knowing you were in at the beginning.

I know it's Super Bowl Sunday morning and I know a place that does breakfast all day and delivers gets busy but taking 90+ minutes to deliver to me a cold egg sandwich, cold hash browns and cold French toast is unacceptable. Thanks for the refund and coming back to pick up the food but I won't be ordering from here again.

Came here for the first time, the service is awesome, the staff are very friendly it's not loud and obnoxious inside, music is very up to date and relaxing. The food is amazing!!!! My god man, perfect chicken, crisp fries! *dies*

Well priced, lighter lunch option in the area that's a good choice if you're working in the area. I typically enjoy the hummus bowl option, and you really can't go wrong with any of the proteins they have available. Everything here tastes fresh and the staff is friendly and accommodating if you have any questions, or are looking for recommendations for your meal customizations.

Service is quick which also makes this a great place to grab something when you're on the run, but there's also pretty good seating that turns over pretty quickly in the space which makes it a good spot to dine in as well.
The foods always great. I love almost all their sliders and the staff is always nice and helpful. The only reason it's not 5 is it's just a bit pricy. But quality nonetheless.

My friend is obsessed with this place so I was excited to try it since she is also vegetarian. I got the bowl, which personally seemed like a way better option and it was delicious and fresh and spicy! The chipotle style restaurants are always are a great way to try a bunch of different combinations, so I'm excited to go back again. Everyone I've recommended it to has really enjoyed it. Great lunch spot and the line moves super fast!

The concept of the Sushiritto was too intriguing to pass up when I first learned about Hai Street.  The system is much like a Chipotle where you pick the protein, sauce, veggies, and crunch topping.  I picked the spicy tuna with spicy mayo, carrots, red cabbage, cucumber, and wasabi guac.  It truly is sushi wrapped like a burrito.  Hai Street offers a really nice healthy option.  My sushiritto cost about $10.  
I really think this is a restaurant that could expand around the country.  The biggest downside over my two visits has been the speed and preparedness of the employees.  They seem to always be out or right on the verge of being out of various toppings and sauces.  They are also painfully slow.  If I were coming in for a quick bite on my lunch hour, I would be annoyed.  Once they get these bugs worked out, it should be a great casual spot for a healthy meal.
The worst.   It should be shut down.   McDonalds should be embarrassed.  Customer service is terrible.  Food...   not up to standards.  Just the worst.
Onside temp 95 degree and this  place no AC .. it felt like eat in the sauna room. The food was good and restroom seem clean.

Worse customer service I've ever experienced from a wingstop location. I ordered my food and was told that there would be a 15min wait. Multiple customer who had ordered after me at the register received their meals before I did. I noticed that my order had sat in the kitchen when they called my name after 30mins wait from the time I ordered, my order sat cold in the kitchen for over 15mins. Long story short I will never return to this establishment and refuse to recommend it to anyone else.
Great lunch spot. Surprisingly filling but you won't be stuffed. Nothing will knock your socks off but the chicken one and tempura were both very tasty.
This place is so bomb it's like a Chipotle for sushi. All the ingredients are fresh and everything is made quickly. Highly recommend!
Hard to order through the bullet proof glass. Super unclean. And employees are rude. If you crave Taco Bell, go anywhere else please.

It's your average burrito restaurant. I prefer Chipotle better, but this place serves up decent tex-mex fare. I usually get the chicken burrito for lunch -- it's a fine place to sit down and enjoy yourself in the winter, but I would not come here in the spring/summer when there are so many food truck on Penn campus that serve better, cheaper versions of the same food.
Affordable, tasty, great sauce selection. 1 pound of dark meat strips, 2 sauces and a fountain soda was under $10. New go to in a pinch!
They always manage to screw up my orders. Horrible service.
Great menu items!! Lite but yet flavorful dishes had the charred squid and parsnips fries Welcome to the neighborhood

While visiting Philly for a weekend trip, I finally got to try the sushi burrito!! I ordered the spicy tuna tartare with additional gochujang and a bunch of the veggies and all the crunches. It was so good! I expected more fish, but this concept is so well done that it doesn't really matter to me. I had some difficulties unwrapping the paper to get to the burrito, probably because I was overexcited.

I really enjoy this stand! I've had the chili dog, barbecue wings, and baked garlic wings. I wish I could replicate the crispiness on the garlic wings. They're simple delicious. The chili on the chili dog also has a unique flavor.

They charge for ketchup. First time in my lifetime seeing a place charge for condiments. 

Chicken tenders were tasty. Mac and cheese was kind of sloppy and burnt. 

And you can't just get a cup of water. 

Interesting place....

Delicious! We ordered a make your own with salmon and a hai street chicken, both were excellent. The chicken one was outstanding! We read reviews that mentioned skimpy portions of protein, so I ordered the larger size for the Salmon burrito and it was the same size and had the same amount of meat as the chicken which was ordered as a regular size.  We would order again, but would probably skip the size upgrade since it did not make any discernible difference.

After a long, long wait! I finally got to have the only thing i never imagined i would fall in love with. Sushi burrito. It is basically a big sushi roll but it has all the flavors and sauces inside that soy sauce is not even needed. Probably one of the best food i've ever had.
The chicken strips here seriously rock. Seriously. The place is a bit shoddy, but wtf. Chicken. mashed.

We ate here a little after lunch time.  Ordered the corn bread, perogies, potato salad, and macaroni and cheese.  The corn bread and macaroni were really good.  The corn bread was sweet and moist.  I could have eaten another two pieces and been great!  The macaroni was baked and pretty tasty.  The potato salad was very bland and had way too much dill in it.  The perogies were cold and stale.  Very disappointing considering this was the main part of the meal.  I'm sure if they would have been hot, they might have been good.

WOW!  A japanese buritto bar?  How come I didn't think of this genious idea!?  I finally visited HSK yesterday around 2pm.  I was told the line runs out the door and down the sidewalk, so don't go during prime lunch hour.  Hence, I waited until 2pm and was pleased there was no line so I could take my time and read the glorious menu.  Basically, its like a giant sushi roll.  OR, is basically like a buritto rolled in a seaweed wrap instead of a flour tortilla!  

You can choose a roll or a bowl.  You can choose one of their signature rolls with items already decided, or you can make-your-own!  I went al out and desigined my own roll.  I got the the tataki salmon (similar to sushi salmon), rolled up with spring mix, sliced cucumber, asparagus, roasted beets, and crispy garlic.  I also added the wasabi guacamole, which was freakin delicious.  The entire roll was like one huge salmon sushi roll to me, but better!  The beets and asparagus inside were so delicous.  I can't wait to go back and try the green papaya salad and pickled mango fillings next.  Also, you can choose a sauce, I got the chimichurri sauce which is like a green pesto basil spread, it was so tasty. 

I'm thrilled this place is booming with business, becuase I plan to come here often for a healthy, delicious, and different lunch!   They really need to do a frequent buyer card, or something like that.

I had a party for 11 people and had Panda Express cater it.
We ordered 2 Panda Feasts and a tray of 12 Veggie spring rolls.

The food arrived hot, fresh and on time.

Jay - the manager and Rob - who delivered the food - were great to work with and even gave us additional side orders of Fried Rice and Noodles - so we had ample food.

The Honey Walnut Shrimp was a big hit.
We also got Chicken & Broccoli and Beef & Broccoli for "safe" choices.

Everyone enjoyed the food - and the price was withing my budget.

I will definitely use them again.
I am so amazed at how good this "fast food" Chinese is - especially when they cook it fresh to order.
Great and modern fast food chain store that makes up for the overstaying-it's-welcome McDonald's down the street. Guac isn't extra either like ecoli-infested Chipotle.

now this is a concept. sushi paired with burrito. what a genius idea. i built my own "sushirrito" with brown rice, salmon, all the veggies, and teriyaki sauce. my creation was pretty good but by the time i got home the teriyaki sauce had made it very soggy.  one thing i wish had been an option was PLAIN avocado- they have a wasabi avocado option but for someone who despises wasabi this was a bit disappointing. the concept is cute and i would definitely try again.
Good sushi burrito, and great location! I had no clue this food court existed at the station! Love the different options ie brown versus white rice, avocado, and the option to make your own.

Personally believe that the fried chicken tastes better than the university city one. Had chickens by weight the night they open up and it's so good. Having the southern sandwich today and this stuff is MASSIVE! It's very heavy so the buns are a bit thin to hold it, the sauce is sweet, the chicken can get a little bit less crispy in the sandwich. But still, I like the taste of it and ppl are very nice and welcoming :)

A lot more expensive and not really worth the money. Mams falafels near by to them has good cost effective options. Naf naf does not have whole wheat options. Even for a small teas spoon extra hummus they want 1.5$ extra. And guys here make sandwich too messy. They really need to learn from Mama's on how to make a sandwich.

I brought my friends from out of town to Hai Kitchen because of the multiple positive reviews. Not only was the staff rude but the food was over priced and the food was horrible. It was just Americanized sushi in  burrito form. I would have paid 5$ max

Went here for a quick bite to eat before heading to the DMV. I was surprised at how cheery and nice the woman in the drive-thru was. Props to her.

Delicious hash browns!!

First time going and it was so good! I was walking visiting the area and decided to stop in because it smelled so good. They have different fixing which you can put on a bowl or in a pita. I got the chicken shawarma salad bowl. It came with a side a pita and reasonably priced. The atmosphere was chill, environment clean, and service was good. Definitely will hit this place up again when I'm in the area.

Not even deserving of ONE star service sucks here; long drive thru time 1/2 hour minimum. Walk up wait time still long, and you could be the only one in line. Always horse playing around inside. If there was a place closer I would never patronize this location.

Sushi burrito = delicious! Yes, it is the novelty of a sushi burrito that is now trending, but the quality of the fresh ingredients makes Hai Street amazing.

We ordered the California Roll and the Slamming Salmon. We wanted to try their creations first, but you can create your own roll or bowl (starting to sound like we're about to smoke...). You can get brown or white rice and they have a cool machine that flattens the rice to the seaweed. The California roll was better than the slamming salmon, but in both, the ingredients were fresh and crisp. The salmon was thinly sliced and very fresh. I wish they used real crabmeat instead of the stick. Don't get the hibiscus iced tea - it tastes like nothing. The regular size was a good amount of food for me, which I didn't even finish, without feeling stuffed. Get the Go Zilla if you typically need more to fill up. There is less rice than sushi rolls so less carbs and more yumminess! 

For everyone who is complaining about the cost, it's really not that bad for what you're getting. Also, a burrito and drink at Chipotle is also $10 so quit complaining. Warning: there is limited seating and kind of smelled weird inside when we went so don't expect to sit down at a nice restaurant after a long day of walking. Perfect for a quick lunch or bite.

Whenever I dont pack food for lunch, I always go to Franks A Lot. It's right across the street from my work place so it's really convenient. The line is extremely long during lunch rush hour but I think it's all worth it. If you want to avoid the rush hour, try going after one. My personal favorites are the bbq chicken wings, cornbread, and hot dog. You can't go wrong with these selections!!! 

Happy Eating!

Worst Taco Bell in the city, very rude and slow. Food sub par at the best. Need people who like their job and treat customers with respect. Don't do full menu, waited ten minutes for someone to wait on us to find out they don't do breakfast (and there was no other customers there). Never again.

This place was already trending and I had to get my hands on their "sushi burrito". So I went here with 3 of my friends and were already amazed about the fresh ingredients they use. The meat/seafood was readily prepared and rice was on point. On the menu they already have a couple of set sushi burritos for customers to choose from, also they give you the choice to customize it from rice to meat to toppings and veggies. If you've been to Chipotle you already have the idea of what this place is like. 
 I got the shrimp tempura with their set toppings along with sweet green tea. As soon as I took my first bite, I was hooked. With the slight cultural taste of Japan, comes with an American urban twist. It was pretty difficult to eat this without making a mess because things sort of fell out ( the only thing holding the sushi together is the thin wrap of seaweed and sticky rice, can't blame them though - it is what it is.).
 Overall this place was awesome. Id definitely come here again! Best lucks to this business, excited to see new things on the menu soon.

Never again. The driver spent 20 minutes on and off the phone with me just to find me when I'm at a major intersection by Johnny Brendas. When she arrived the food was cold and smashed. She then says "I left your drink in the car do you want it?" Uhhhh-gee, sure since I paid for it! She gets it and it's Mountain Dew?! They don't even have Mountain Dew on their grubhub menu! When I pointed that out she argued with me and said to call her boss. Stuck with a crappy soda and cold food. The fries were plastered into the wrapper and worthless. I reheated the sandwich and it was ok, but if I wanted to cook for myself I would have saved a few dollars by not ordering from them.

I like the concept of a sushi burrito, but I think Hai Street Kitchen does not successfully execute it. I ordered the crunch and it turned out to be ok, but not worth the hype. I also got the sweet green tea, which was light and refreshing. 

Firstly, the value you're getting isn't too great. The pricing is kind of high compared with the portion of the burrito. Secondly, taste wise, the burrito was okay. There isn't anything too special about the rolls that would make me go back and order another one-- especially with the price. I would rather order a 3 rolls for $11 sushi lunch, or get a burrito at Chipotle that's bigger and cheaper.

I was lucky enough to come here on Tuesday. They offer 60 cent boneless wings on Mondays and Tuesdays. We ordered 20 boneless wings and our flavors were original hot, garlic parmesan , and honey barbecue (they have more flavors that satisfy all taste buds). We also grabbed some fries. 

Overall, the wings were good and meaty; battered and then dipped. The honey barbecue were my favorite. The sauce was thick and somewhat sweet with a little tang. The original hot was so so. Nothing special since this place specializes in wings. They weren't saucy at all, but the presentation made it clear that the wings had soaked up the sauce. The parmesan wings were tasty as well. Each flavor definitely had its own distinctive taste. 

The texture of the blue cheese we used for dipping was very runny and it barely tasted like blue cheese. This was an issue for me because each dipping sauce costs .69. The ranch dip was as to be expected. The french fries were average. They're supposed to be a popular item on the menu and appear to be fresh cut (based on looks). I will admit that I ate them after I ate the wings, so they cooled down a bit. My understanding of fries is that they taste better while they're hot. 

I'll be going back soon (most likely during the Monday and Tuesday special). After spending that, I can't imagine spending $17 + for 20.

Definitely a splurge lunch place, I don't wanna say overpriced because you get what you pay for -- fresh ingredients, uniqueness and great flavor! Wait can be long sometimes but everything  is worth trying, you just can't go wrong

The space is very cool and hip yet with genuine comfortable atmosphere. Im a huge fan of the chef and was floored that his magic continues.  This guy got a 3 bells rating at Fitler Dining Room, when he opened it and Buckminster's has the same inventive creativity that made every bite perfect.  My friends and I enjoyed every single part of the meal, and wish we had more time before we had to be somewhere because the vibe was the type you'd want to just soak up.  FYI: definitely get the stuffed cabbage!

Was craving a good sharwarma when I stumbled upon this place.  Really good portions. And the servers are very friendly. 
Chicken sharwarma in a pita or a bowl is too good! Tons of sauces to choose from!
I've been back there at least 5x since.

My now wife and I contacted Hai street about catering our wedding.  We were able to hire them to come out with their food truck (we had one other truck as well) and they handled all the appetizers and half of the dinner (splitting with the other truck).  They were a big hit.  There were basically no lines as they had everything prepped ahead of time.  Leading up to the wedding everyone at Hai Street was super accommodating working with us to make a menu, and making it fit our budget without any real concessions to how good the food ended up being.  On top of all of that their prices were great, especially when compared to the usual wedding caterer rates (which are just outrageous).  

We would HIGHLY recommend Hai Street for catering an event, let alone if you're just hungry and happen to be walking by a location!

Definitely a freaky fast Jimmy John's.

I walked in, ordered a Bootlegger Club, and walked out the door with it in less than a minute.

Granted, I was the only customer there, but still...that's fast.

Convenient location for Penn students as well.

Double the awesome.

Wow! I was looking forward to a posh dinner in Philadelphia, but First I stumbled upon Naf Naf for a snack. The concept is like chipotle where you pick your protein and your style and you go down the line. But really it is extremely delicious Middle Eastern food. My son does not usually like falafel and Shwarma But he thought they were extremely delicious here. The fresh fries that are like warm potato chips are delicious. The falafel is super fresh. And they have great baba ghanouj and very fluffy pita. Also the people who work here are extremely nice. Big ups to Dreamane and Anaya and the young man who was working on Wednesday at 3:30 PM. Five enthusiastic stars for naff naff!

I do not get the entire wave with this place. I mean yeah I get the hype--white girls love sushi and love burritos so the two in one is a Instagram foodies wet dream...(I kid- sort of). 

The sushi isn't authentic. It's not bad. It isn't amazing though. It's made chipotle line style. It's a unique experience, don't get me wrong. I just don't see the hype since the food isn't that good. 

Also, there is almost ZERO parking by the restaurant--AND the restaurant is small as hell. So prepare to pay $12 for a decent tasting, okay sized sushi burrito, that you will probably have to eat on the sidewalk next to the restaurant, as you watch groups of people walk in that wouldn't look out of place at a Taylor Swift concert...or a place like this. 

Mostly hype, won't be back.

Five stars because the chicken fingers are among the best I've had. I wish the sauces were free (they have several unusual flavors, and getting a small array would be enjoyable, but each costs an extra $.50.) But when a place has near-perfect chicken, you don't nitpick.

First off, I'm so glad the east coast also has sushi burritos. I first experienced a sushi burrito in SF at Sushiritto! This one was great to be able to customize and they were very accommodating for the orders. I made a custom roll similar to their salmon one but wanted to change a few things up. The teriyaki pepper sauce is spot on with the salmon. They also had a sample of one of their rolls, which I thought was awesome! This place is perfect for a picnic in the park or for on the go. I'll definitely be back here to get my sushi roll to go next time I'm in Philly.

I was given a business card by one of the owners. I decided to try the place out the following day. Been there twice in one week. 

Food: Chicken tenders are really good, chicken pot pie was good, biscuits are good. Mac and cheese was good on my first visit, second visit mac & cheese was okay. Wings are okay (stick with the tenders).

Dessert: Brownie was okay, cookie tarte was hard, tasteless and old.

Plus: The beer selection here is better than some of the bars in Center City.

I stopped by Franks on a recent trip to Philly and enjoyed a pretty darn good lunch.  I ordered a plate of pierogies with homemade sour cream, mac-n-cheese and green beans for sides, and threw in a piece of banana cornbread for a sweet final addition.  All of it was really good.

Passed this place a couple of times and noticed the line snaking out the door. Something in there has got to be good, right? Decided to stop by today to investigate. They sell "sushi burritos" which is essentially a whole sushi roll, wrapped up and cut in two like a burrito.  The place has very few seats so plan to take you food to go. They wrap it up in a cute little box for you.  I took mine to a shady park bench in Rittenhouse Square.

I ordered the "Crunch" was a delicious combo of tempura shrimp, lettuce, cucumber, pickled mango, topped with some spicy mayo. It was just the right amount of crunch, freshness and spice! My only complaint is that the filling is a bit "wet" which made for a bit of a messy eating experience. The wrapping paper soaked through a bit and disintegrated at the edges.

For a drink, I tried the hibiscus iced tea and liked it very much.

Overall, a nice addition to take out lunch choices, especially for the health conscious!

Don't frequent this establishment too often but the times I have it's been mediocre.  Very few true fast food franchises in the area which to a certain extent is a good thing. But this is a faster/cheaper option than most take out in the area.
No the greatest clientele dining inside lots of loud cursing and vulgar language on the times I've been inside.  Prefer drive through.  Food is typical Wendy's fare when in a pinch might be the place to go to.
The crunch burrito was very good! The soup special today was pumpkin miso. That was good as well. I loved that the calories were posted on the menu.

This is not sushi. If you come in looking for sushi, go to Crazy Sushi around the corner. 

However as an Asian fusion restaurant it's okay. Since it's a burrito technically, the rice wrap is just too thick, and it's overstuffed with ingredients that just drown out the fish. 

Eat there for the novelty but not really for the food.

Naf Naf Grill is less than a block away from where I now work.  Add to that its fast-causal approach, and it should be in line to becoming my one of my regular go to spots.  Based on my visits thus far, it has not earned this kind of 'tier 1' status just yet.

Their menu offers pita sandwiches, rice, couscous, or salad bowls, and also a hummus bowl.  All can be made with chicken, steak, or falafel.  They also offer some extensive veggie options, but I haven't had a chance to try any of them just yet.

I found my chicken pita sandwich to be A-Ok.  It was made to order and quick to deliver.  My steak couscous bowl wasn't quite what I had hoped for.  The portion just didn't seem to add up and the steak didn't have much flavor.  However, it too was made to order.

Net - I'm not writing Naf Naf off just yet, but I am looking at other options instead of just making it my regular spot.  It has location potential at least...

Such a creative way to do sushi! I love the concept of it. The lines do get long here, but don't worry, they move pretty fast. I ordered the new Tuna roll (Screamin Tuna) and tempura corn. Both were amazing. I did try my husbands tempura shrimp roll and I liked his more than mine, but mine was still good too.

The reason for 4 stars and not 5 is because my roll completely fell apart while trying to eat it. The nori wrap got really sticky and soft from the tons of sauce. I practically used my hands as a spoon to eat it. :-( As for the tempura corn, it was great! It had that nice sweet and salty taste to it and a nice crisp. But make sure you eat it first. If you wait till later to eat it, it gets really chewy and beyond greasy!

They were the only place not swamped during the lunch hour.  Man, those other guys were missing out!  Quick and easy lunch.  Food was pretty spectacular.  I got a random assortment of dishes and all made my mouth happy.  Mac and cheese was my favorite though.  I have a new regular stop in the market!

Great place!  Good food, had a sample on the house ( fried chips, aioli, pico de gallo and gazpacho). OMG! I also had the teriyaki pineapple burger and it was amazing. 
The bartender Lindsay was really nice and attentive.. Definitely a good time.

Not going to lie, I thought the place be bigger. But it sure does pack a punch! My mom and I arrived maybe about 30 minutes prior to closing and not only was the staff still friendly and pleasant. The food was still super fresh ! You can't beat that at all. All options was still available and still crisp. I definitely recommend for everyone !

I went there today and had pizza fries and beer battered onion rings. They both were the worst thing I tasted and had to grow them away.
The onion rings had no taste in batter and also it didn't have any salt or pepper or any other seasoning. It was so oily it was like eating oil.
Pizza fries had fries with tasteless cheese and a marinade sauce. Normal French fries from McDonald's are 100 times better than this pizza fries.
People seemed to order grilled chicken and I think it should be good
I didn't try as fries and onion rings killed my mood

I go in that was my  first mistake.. I normally go to one location when I do eat their chicken and it is not often, but being lazy, didn't want to drive across town but since I was already in the area!  I wanted a 11 piece 2 breast 2 legs 7 wings.. WELL,  sorry was told We can't do that.. (Even with upcharge) NO we can't!  OK...

Ok, what can you do? We can do 2 breasts 4 thighs 2 legs 3 wings. Well, I don't eat thighs! The girl behind the counters tells me  I can give you 2 breasts, 5 wings, 4 legs,  I get home,  I have 2 breasts, 3 wings and 6 legs and  highly disappointed because the coating on the chicken taste as if it was cooked over and over again in old grease almost like a burnt taste. NEVER going back here again!  lesson learned  When you get a hard time.. and you are willing to pay extra and you still get a hard time LEAVE!

Wonderful staff and amazing eats for late night! Stumbled in here late night and was graciously taken care of by both Takina and Tay. ALSO, stellar craft beers that are amazingly cheap! Solid date or hang out spot 8-)

Naf Naf is like the Mediterranean version of Chipotle, except it's faster and tastier than Chipotle (yeah, that's right, I said it). I really appreciate all the vegetarian options and that they label them on the menu. The Veggie Delight is definitely a great value and very tasty. The falafel is crispy, and the pita is warm and fresh. I also really dig the sumac onions and purple cabbage. Some of the sauces are a bit odd, but the garlic and tahini sauces are yummy. I will say the "fries" are really more like homemade potato chips, which is disappointing. Overall it's a great lunch spot!

This is your typical Burger King, nothing special or out of the ordinary. Service is always slow as are the employees, they seem to rather talk to coworkers or play with their hair than take your order. The bathroom was a disgrace and didn't seem to be cleaned in some time. The tables in the play area looked to be wiped down with the towel they use to clean the fryers.  I will never return here unless I'm starving and all of the other food places in the area are burnt to the ground.

I've decided that Checkers is my fave fast food burger. I got hooked when I lived in the midwest and ate at Rallys (same thing). This is why I like Checkers burgers best: they have an equal ration of ketchup, mustard, and mayo on the burgers and they use RED onions. IDK, it's just a good burger. Also their loaded fries are delicious, messy and probably 1300 calories but that's OK they're so good. 

Also the counter and drive thru move fast. A++

I decided to try this okay again to give it another try.  Got the create your own zilla roll with spicy tuna and shrimp tempura.  Got red cabbage on it with roasted garlic and tempera flakes. The whole thing was deep fried. All around the taste was alright. I would have liked a bigger selection of toppings, maybe kimchi? Or edamame? I feel like those would be a better alternative for people like me who don't really like uncooked vegetables (carrots, pickled cabbage) on my roll.

Can there be a six stars option? This place is delicious, cheap, service is speedy and friendly...seriously no complaints. One wrap was enough for two small meals for me. When I finished the first half, I was so satisfied but also really excited to know I still had half a wrap of tastiness in my near future. This place is the best - can they please open another branch near Penn?! I think college kids would literally eat this place up

Bad. Just bad.   We tried the tuna.  The tuna is sub-par. and there wasn't much of it.  It's just mashed and tastes just okay.  There is no avocado.  There's a lot of rice and the overall taste is barely average. It's just low end food for mid-price.  I would never eat here again, nor would I recommend it.  Neither would my dining companions. We eat a LOT of sushi at far better places, every week. We tried this thinking it was something unique.  It might actually work with better ingredients, but I guess to stay at that price point, they need to skimp.

The woman who waited on me was wonderful..  No complaints about the service.  The food was mediocre at best.  Breading was way too salty.  Chicken wings had tough meat.  Food sits under heat lamps, and is over-priced.  And they charge for tiny potions of dipping sauce.

Love love love this concept. Finally got to try this today after begging multiple friends to go. Line was out the door, but I can definitely understand why. The food was delicious, the workers were really nice, and the place is pretty cute. 

I got a shrimp tempura roll with pickled mango, cabbage, pepper teriyaki, onions and lettuce. I believe i said hell yeah with a smile multiple times while I was eating it. Hadn't had sushi in a while, so that was fantastic for satisfying that craving. As most seemed to do, we took it to rittenhouse and had our burritos in the grass on a nice sunny day. Made for a lovely afternoon. We also got wasabi guac and chips which were pretty good. Could taste the wasabi but it wasn't overwhelmingly spicy and had a generous amount of acidity with the lime. even had some nice fresh different toned chips that showed a little extra care than just typical tortillas. 

Drinks were also nice and appropriate. We got lemonade and sweet green tea, which paired deliciously. I'll have to give the hibiscus tea a shot next. I want to go back here and try everything. slammin salmon, I'm comin back for you sir.

Since this subway is a block from the hospital, I tend to frequent it a lot.  Why?  Because it's cheap, quick, and I can watch my sandwich being made so I know it's getting exactly what I want on it.  The restaurant itself is fairly clean and I've never had an issue with the employees here.  They take my Jefferson FastPass which is nice, because I tend to run out to lunch and forget to grab my wallet for some reason.  

My main issue with this location is that occasionally their lettuce is, well, not green.  There might be a subtle hint of green freshness, but mostly it's the leftover white portion of the lettuce which doesn't look appealing.  Also, they go extremely light on the onions, I always have to ask for more.  But maybe I just like onions more than most people... who knows.

I just ordered from this place for the first time and I must
say that I am impressed! The sliders are AWESOME and
cooked to perfection.

The customer service was supreme; thanks to Tony and
his excellent customer service!

It's about time Point Breeze gets a place like Buckminsters! The space is small, but cozy and the bookshelves above the bar give the space a rustic feel. They offer a decent selection of beers and cocktails and have a few wines on tap. 

The food is more of a tapas style, so plates are generally smaller. The chicken leg is seriously one of the best pieces of meat I've ever eaten. I wish they would make that into a larger plate or a meal with some sides because that would be heaven!

Overall, great addition to the neighborhood and we'll certainly be back, especially since we can (finally) walk to a decent bar in the area. Now, if only Point Breeze Ave. would follow suit!

After waiting many months for Neon Lobster to open, I finally had the chance to get my hands on some lobster rolls in South Philly. Well the wait was worth it!

I ordered the Cold Maine Lobster roll with fries. The sandwich was decently sizeable for a lobster roll and the meat was nice and tender. The bread was grilled and held the lobster in well. Great flavor and the fries were really good too. I'm excited to come back and try the Warm Lobster roll!

For those who do not know (CC reviews below) crab fries are crinkled fries in old bay seasoning - no crab included. Chickie's and Pete's is famous for it here, and I have to admit as a Philadelphian I love them. 

However, they really abuse the ballpark prices here - $9 for crab fries (only one size offered) and an additional $2 for cheese. Their fries are always pricey, but $11?! I like C&P but they're truly not THAT good, and they clearly found a high-margin system here and have no interest in sharing the wealth with fans. 

The lines at this concession stand are ridiculous, managed a little bit by the cafeteria style check out. It's also a very messy stand with fries all over the counters and floor - not a great look. Overall, just another careless food vendor ready to lynch you for your money...didn't stop me from buying fries though. I crave what I crave.

Delicious! I ordered the warm lobster roll, which came with big chunks of lobster with butter on a grilled roll. There was a mix-up with delivery, which was grubhub's fault, and the owner remade the order free of charge and delivered it himself. Oh, and he added free shrimp cocktail, which was also delicious and a nice surprise! I was very impressed with the service. Now I can't wait to try the cold lobster roll!

So this da McDonalds dey be using up here, man, and it less ghetto as the one down south round MLK. The drive through real nice, the food be coming real fast and everything. The inside of the establishment is more on the yucky side and the people at the counter will ALWAYS get your order wrong. The bathroom is atrocious, and the tables are sticky. Although it is McDonals.

The pictures look really good, but the sushi burrito is not as good as we had in mind, we had the shrimp tempura, we didnt taste any shrimp. But the whole thing taste healthy though. It is not good enough to make me crave and go on purpose. Maybe when i pass by. Taste more like a salad with lettuce and rice

After hearing about this place, I was really excited to try it one day. I woke up on Saturday morning to a Snapchat from my friend of her roll and immediately walked over to get one myself. 

I opted for the build your own option. You get a choice of brown/white rice in a hand roll or bowl, 1 choice of protein (I got portabello mushroom which is the veggie option), a sauce (spicy mayo), 4 toppings (cucumber, asparagus, onions, carrots), and a crunch (fried garlic). This was $6.99

I also got the hibiscus tea for $2. 

Initially I wasn't sure if I'd be full or not, but I was definitely the right about of full, not stuffed. A good amount of lunch! 

My roll was very tasty bursting with flavors from the fresh veggies they put in, and the fresh seaweed. My tea wasn't overly sweet and they often are and very refreshing. I love spicy mayo in my sushi so this was an added bonus. 

I definitely will make this place more regular. I want to try some of the other toppings and I think next time I would go for the shallots and not the garlic since there wasn't much garlic taste. And I want to try the wasabi guac too! 

Go try this place for a fun experience! All the people were so funny and kind.

This place really disrespected my BBQ chicken sandwich.  I was expecting an extra delicious experience and wound up with two stale pieces of bread, two small pieces of chicken breast, and BBQ sauce on the side.  Immensely disappointing, wish I hadn't paid for this garbage.  I'm still hungry... 

Oh, and the Mac & Cheese isn't great either but I had to eat something

Chicken and mac and cheese, the mac and  cheese was unique with a lot of different flavors in it. was very good! But the best part was Annie, the girl at the counter! She was upbeat and fun! Excellent customer service skills

I was starving and I went to the first place that dd not have a funky smell and I'm glad I did! I saw perogies and instantly ordered that. I got homeade mac and cheese and fries as my side, although I wish cornbread was a side (and thats why its 4 stars) cause thats what I really wanted. The fries were fresh off the frier. Brought half my meal home with me. When I return back to RTM I will be sure to go to this location again!

Great food. The hummus was creamy and delicious and the shwarma was very good too. The baba ganoush was slightly lighter than expected but none the less the quality of the bread made it taste great. It was my first time eating at naf naf and I will defintely go there again when im in philly.

Love this place for serving a salmon burrito wrapped in nori! I love that you can get brown or white rice as well as plentiful veggie options! My fav is: Tataki salmon, white rice, ginger miso dressing, lettuce, cucumber, carrot, and finished with fried garlic mmmm!

I've gotten delivery via caviar and besides the order being slightly incorrect, it was a good experience. My go-to $10 dinner!

This is my place, was in Philly for a week and went twice, the first time it was late after a couple of beers and the best drag show I have ever seen, the second time I decided to come sober just to make sure the chicken was as good as I remembered it being. It was. I love chicken tenders and dipping sauces, and this place is definitely the best at that- but even better because their soda on tap and beer selection. 
Oh, and I forgot to mention the Mac n cheese-it's to die for. Oh -and the biscuit with their homemade honey butter. Everything was amazing honestly....down to the service, the nice folks there gave us a cookie because they forgot something on our order, and the cookie was amazing as well. Really great food, open late, with exceptional service and cleanliness, really don't know what's not to like.

This was a truly delicious meal. Ingredients are so fresh and they have some unique flavor profiles like warm carrot salad rubbed in coffee and dates, as well as fried parsnips paired with a horseradish sauce mmm. 

My friend and I shared the gnocchi and pierogis (fully aware of our tasty starch party). The gnocchi was so so amazing with pickled cabbage, a whole egg yolk in the center to break over all of it (yeah that image just made you shiver in delight), and local ham chunks mixed in. It was perfect. The pierogis with a thick amount of caramelized onions were probably the best I've ever had. 

Cocktails were also something to remember here. They charmed me with an egg white drink (can't resist em) that had gin, coconut milk, cherry and spearmint. holy hell was it a winner. I tried the house gin and tonic with lavender and citrus as well which as A OK. They have some great bartenders. Place was cute and well decorated with a relaxed atmosphere. People that worked here were all a bit awkward and quiet in trying to remember what was in everything, but new place, so all good stumbling sirs.

had you guys at the Folk Fest last year and I PRAY you will be there again.
I went another time and still just as delicious! I love this place.

Hai street is hot stuff!

On an evening visit we had fortunate timing.  There was no line when we ordered, but by the time we were halfway through our rolls the line was backed up to the door. My beau and I each ordered a roll, he opted to "go zilla" for additional protein leaving us both satisfied with our meals.  

Like Christine B. mentioned, the hand rolls are messy. Just picture trying to eat a burrito that wasn't tucked in at the ends and you'll get an idea of how messy it can get. Regardless, it was a delicious mess! My portobello mushrooms with spicy gochujan sauce, asparagus, carrots, cucumbers, and cabbage brown rice roll hit the spot. Everything was fresh and well seasoned.

This healthy no-msg meal cost us $20, including a box o' water & chips with wasabi guac. Will be back to try both rice and salad bowls. For those who haven't been, it's definitely more of a takeout place, with some counters but no chairs.

Special thanks to the friendly guy behind the counter who complimented my Peter Pilotto dress & hooked us up with a delicious dinner.
Had the B.L.T. Very flavorful. Biscuits to die for. Arnold Palmer was not strong an I loved it. Good for big groups bar table seating. Staff very pleasant.

I like it. Friendly staff. It's pretty good. I gave it a four simply because I just had the slamming salmon for the first time yesterday and It made me sick to my stomach. Everything is good but I would steer clear from the salmon.

Holy shit!!!! Best food I've tasted in a long time. From beginning to end. The cheesy cauliflower, the broccoli, the squid, the pork shoulder, chicken Marsala, pierogis!            
      The flavors were like an orgasm in my mouth! The lavender citrus gin and tonic! Damn damn damn! Best new jaunt around!   The waitress jolisa was great ! Attentive and very helpful with all the menu items!
Wanted something quick on the way to the movies. They gave me a wrong order and when they fixed it it was very very cold. Also slow as molasses.

Stopped in for a quick lunch between business calls in the neighborhood.  Never again.  The place has ballistic Plexiglas along the counter, but the other fast-food chain restaurants across the street do not.  Service was not quick.  I had the cheese burger combo, and the cheese was like wax.  They got the condiments right when I asked for no lettuce and no mayonnaise, so that's good.  The fries were well cooked and crispy.  Even so, the atmosphere is a huge turnoff.  Next time I and my coworkers are in the neighborhood at lunch time (which will likely be next week), we will definitely avoid this place.

Went with the family and had a good time at this location.  The employees were great, energetic and VERY helpful.  The food was scrumptious, and the veggies were fresh.  I loved the quesidillas.  I would visit again.

A hidden gem. Food is fantastic. Good for lunch, dinner and a quick snack. The Drunken Crab cake may be the city's best crab cake sandwich, the illadelphia is a highlight and you will absolutely enjoy their standard "M.A.T.T.'s Slider". Follow their Instagram for some delicious special offerings.

I first had Popeyes when it was the only restaurant and closest location in Boston . Back from where I lived , it was about 30-45 mins away from home depending on traffic . I used to have to drive out there when I crave for It . In my opinion at the time , it was better than kfc . Moving to Philly , I seen it everywhere so I don't really go unless I really really crave for it . 

What happened to Popeyes chickens and their mash potatoes and gravy now ? I ordered the 12 pcs chicken tenders family meal because I don't really like the bone in and ended up getting the regular 12 pieces of chicken . I didn't have time to go back and exchange because I have to get to work . The chicken was dry like it's been sitting there for hours and the mash potatoes and gravy lack flavors . It doesn't taste the same like it used to be . First time back in a long time and everything was horrible .

Stumbled upon this place and don't regret it. This place is similar to a chipotle but for Middle Eastern food. I opted for the Beef Shawarma bowel with rice, hummus, veggies, onions, and a jalapeño sauce. The dish was accompanied by pita bread. 
I loved it all!! The hummus was great and well seasoned. The beef was freshly cooked and tasty, the rice was average, the veggies and onions were a good add on and balanced out the flavors. My jalapeño dressing was an added bonus, it gave the food the added kick that in love.
Staff was average, it was pretty empty when I went so they looked more bored. 
Overall good choice and yes I would go back!

Truly excellent falafel. Also very good hummus. The harissa hot sauce was delicious and very savory. I prefer flat pitas, these were the puffy kind, but fresh, warm and tasty. Surprisingly great meal for a medi chain. Will definitely eat here again.

The food is mediocre but what seals the deal in giving this location a one star review is the service. The restaurant is beyond stingy and berates customers when they ask for toppings. I had an employee demonstrate in front of me he thought I was given the proper portion by trying to spread the topping out to give it a fuller appearance. When I asked for more, they decided to toss the extra topping in front of my face rather than to add it to my bowl. 

The manager is the driving force with treating customers as money making machines rather than patrons trying to enjoy their food. Her toxic personality has filtered down on the employees there.
Falafel is fried fresh when you order, pita was soft and fresh, and big portion sizes! Be careful, the green sauce is pretty hot, Red is even hotter!

I found out about this place a while ago. I regularly browse through restaurants in my preferred cuisines for new places. I had bookmarked here and wanted to try it but then I cooled down. I get tired of "build your own bowl" places sometimes. They seem overly expensive for what I end up getting and I prefer places with lots of seating so I can people watch. They do have a row of stools for about 5-8 people but that's my idea seating arrangement. Anyway, this is all leading up to me saying how wrong I was! See I wen here with a group of friends and they wanted to eat outside (this location is about 5 min walk from Rittenhouse Square) and I'm so happy I suggested this place! I built my own wrap with white rice, (freshly made) katsu chicken (a type of Japanese fried chicken), onions, lettuce, carrots and cucumber with the ginger miso sauce. Now I must say that I was leery about the sauce because I don't really like miso, but I really REALLY love ginger so I went with it. This is also my first time eating a wrap (I dislike too many textures in my mouth), but it was great. The chicken was nice and warm and everything mixed so well together without becoming muddled or lost. I also got a sweetened green iced tea and I was pleasantly surprised to find that they used matcha tea, rather than regular tea. It was great. I normally dislike straight matcha tea because it's too bitter for me but the sweetness mixed with the bitterness was refreshing and delicious. I definitely recommend this place and I'm actually really sad that I can't go to it again because I'm home from college (I would've gone during finals but I broke my ankle so no yummy wrap for me). But come fall I'm definitely going here again and again.

When I'm hungry, I take food risks. Some work out well and some are just, well....
While waiting on line trying to figure out the perfect "design your own roll" (nope, I haven't done the rice bowl yet), I saw an ad for the Featured Item which was the Slammin Salmon Dynamite roll, which is the slammin salmon roll, coated in tempura crispies and deep fried. 
As the line moved, I deliberated between yes and no. I ultimately decided to "Dynamite" my roll (not sure if Dynamiting is a thing, I could have totally appropriated the term and used it for my own needs. I didn't ask but the guy seemed to know what I wanted).  Dynamiting, BTW, adds about 3 minutes to the wait time. Your finished roll is coated in an egg wash and then covered in 2 extra nori sheets,in order to keep it all contained, then rolled in the tempura and ultimately fried. All the while, my anticipation was building.
All the way back to my office, I had a warm roll in my hand, and I'm not going to lie y'all, it felt good.
I began to regret my adventurous choice because deep fried tempura crispies apparently become razor sharp bite punishers. 
Also, the roll just feels heavier in my stomach as I type about 30 minutes, post consumption.  The blame lies with me, however, I wanted to pass along that information to any other curious folk out there.

Went to Philly to bury both my grandmother and my uncle. Had an opportunity to catch a ride with my father to the airport. We both stayed in Rittenhouse square, though at different hotels, but that's a whole other review. Anyway we decided to meet up for lunch and decided to go for a walk to find something around in the area. For those unfamiliar with Rittenhouse square it's like a poor man's Union Square in San Francisco. We start chatting and next thing i know we walk for an hour and got no food. It was getting close to time to go to the airport and I wanted so famous crab fries for chickie and petes in the terminal I've passed so many time before.  Obviously pops was still hungry so we decided to go to the real thing. The one by the ballpark was on our way so off we go.

Arrive around 3 on Sunday and it's pretty empty. Host seats us right next to two full tables while the rest of the place is empty. I guess I'm California bougie for wanted to sit farther away from the only other people in the spot. Hostess was not pleased. We found new seats and waited. And waited . And waited. Guess it's my fault for being a brat but pops got up and talked to another lady who we assumed was leadership. She walked away and said she would get our waitress. She arrived a short time later. This lady was all south Philly. She looked like she could throws those hands. 

Time to order and got the buffalo chicken Philly cheesesteak with some crab fries. Now here's the thing. I know the best cheesesteaks don't come form Gino's or Pat's so I wasn't going to buy into all the hype of the crab fries. When they came out I have out a little chuckle. I really don't know what I was expecting. Defiantly not real crab neat or anything like that but it was underwhelming to say the least. Bro. It was crinkle cut fries with Old Bay seasoning. For anyone that's had seasoning salt on fries, same concept. The star is the white cheese sauce that it comes with. Like with most cheese sauces, as time went by as me and pa-dukes chopped it up, the cheese started to congeal making it un-dippable. I'm going to recreate these at home soon.
The buffalo chicken cheesesteak was forgettable. It feel apart on first pick up and came with a cloying sweet blue cheese sauce. 
Pops had a crab cake sandwich that came cold? Is that a thing? He didn't love it. 
He also asked for the most top shelf tequila they had and it was patron. Okay then. I'll leave that for his review. 

Took most of the sandwich to go for the plane but of course I left it in the car when I got dropped off. Guess the subconscious mind wasn't happy with the experience and decided to leave it in Philly.

Literally the worst fast food experience you will ever have. I've come here many times as it was a guilty pleasure. As it has spiraled downhill I've finally given up. The food is dried out and burned and the cheese is never melted however, the service at this location is what makes it the worst. These people do not care enough to ever get an order right. Honestly, it's pure laziness. I ordered two sandwiches and handed over a $20 and the cashier gave me a $1 back. One night the cashier rushed us through the drive thru then proceeded to make us pull around to wait 15 minutes for our food. The employees have the most miserable attitudes and you might want to say "can you blame them?" Yes. If you can't do your job efficiently then don't work there. How hard is it to assemble chicken, lettuce, and mayo on a bun? From stale buns to disgusting heaping globs of mayo. From soggy greasy fries to blackened buns. By the way if you actually park and walk inside to order, they will ignore you and only serve the drive thru until all the cars are gone. When the bars close and there's nowhere left to eat around here, please, save yourself and choose WaWa instead.

came here from san Francisco have been a big fan of popeye's for many years. but the ones in the city have been going down hill. so we decided to give this one a try . it was great ! the Cajun rice was very good like how it was in the city long ago and the chicken was very crispy and not old at all . they made a lot here. I think they do a good job that's why they make so many at once. I really was thinking about taking some back home . it was really good ! haven't had good popeye's chicken for a long time.

My friend lives at the apartment complex where Jimmy John's is located because She is at Penn.  I tried their Turkey Tom with their vinegar chips. First, they were prepared very fast.  Second, the cold hoagie was actually pretty good. In my opinion, they were definitely better than Subway or Wawa's hoagies. It seems the dough feels more firm and chewy than other typical hogies. Hoagie is pretty thick with enough meats and veggies. Lastly, the prices were very reasonable.  If I have to eat lunch very fast, I would definitely try here one more time.

Definitely will not return. Food was expensive. Mexican sandwich was sweet? Biscuit is very not how a biscuit should be. Chicken tender is very dry and bland. Charged for sauce. I guess only my bottled beer was great, but even that could not save my $30 experience for a little bit of food.

After reading about this place I had a lot of hope in these sushi wraps. For around the same price as two sushi rolls at most place you get these burrito like wraps how ever you would like. Definitely pricey for what it is, messy soaked in sauce and not tightly wrapped like an actual sushi roll. I have to say we were happy with it but definitely glad we didn't go out of our way for it. I don't think I will be going back anytime soon just simply because you get a less sloppy and better presentation if you were to just go get sushi somewhere.

I am sort of disappointed with this place after hearing all the hype about it.  I have been on two occasions.  The first occasion I had the Mexican.  The second occasion I has the crunch.  I thought the Mexican was actually really good, but not worth the 10 dollar cost as well as the shady extra up charge for wasabi guac sauce.  The second time I went I wanted to eat the same thing but nope, the Mexican had been taken off the menu.  Then I asked for the crunch which was two little shrimp in a roll.  I asked for the yucca chips since it was good last time, but nope they changed the menu and that was gone too.  Just disappointed for the decrease in quality but sky high prices.
I was in Philadelphia visiting and this is the best QDOBA I've been to. The employees were so nice and everything was very clean. I didn't feel rushed ordering.

This place is alright. The service was really slow when I went. My BF ordered a burger that I can't recall the name of which help explains how lackluster it was. Definitely a pass. I ordered a crispy spicy chicken sandwich which was pretty good but not something I would come back specifically for. It more like it's nice to have but I won't miss it when it's gone.

I tried their new Paleo bowl as I try and eat grain free dairy free when I can when I travel and I was timid but it was so good! So happy I found a great and easy option as I travel for food! Definitely going to go back and get this again.

The bathrooms were pretty dirty and I went from a 9 to a 6 instantly after eating their nachos. Plus my mom called me and asked me to meet her at the flower show but I was too intoxicated for that. Overall I had fun and there was great music.

Not sure why the reviews are not more generous for this place. This place was a lifesaver for me when I was in Philly for an already expensive weekend. I love a fresh salad! for me that is greens and lot's of them. They also had a variety of protein sources so you could make it a complete meal (hardcooked eggs, tuna salad, chicken, etc). A good variety of dressing but you don't even need that with all the variety of other goodies. If you stay away from the heavy stuff you can get away cheap!!!
No seating that I am aware of but I was not really looking, maybe there is somewhere in the market you can sit after you pay, I don't know.

Meh.

I was SO super excited to try this because of Instagram (sigh, what a huge hype social media creates) but I was disappointed. Also, I think I was expecting too much because of Cali's Sushirrito, but this doesn't compare.

I ordered the Slammin' Salmon which consists of raw salmon, gochu jang, lettuce, cucumber and yellow radish. However, it just didn't work. It really just tasted like slobs of gochu jang and the salmon didn't taste quality like what raw salmon tastes like in regular sushi. I LOVE salmon, whether it's cooked or raw, but I was not feeling this salmon at all. The seaweed was also quite soggy because they have the rice on beforehand, which in actual sushi places they don't put the rice on until a customer orders making it seem not fresh. I don't know, in conclusion I don't recommend this place and would not come again.

I had my first sushi burrito here. I've gone here 3 times. The first time I didn't like it much - probably because I ordered something I didn't like much. I gave it another try and ordered their Hai Street Kitchen with the addition of mango, and it was delicious. Staff is friendly and service was quick. Food was delicious and pretty healthy I think.

Simply put -- POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE. 

Just rude and dry and you can tell none of the employees want to be there. I asked questions and the guy literally was irritated to answer. Sucks... I mean, granted, it's Taco Bell, not the place known for the best customer service or food but come on, let's have friendly service and at least some type of excitement to 1. Have a job 2. Providing food to folks. Lol. Food makes me happy. It sucks when people ruin that experience. 

And when the heck did these taco boxes get so expensive? Two of these cost me $40?! 

My rant is done.
The hype is real, I loved the place! I had the signature chicken Katsu burrito and I liked it. It was a subtle flavor but the dressing was a pop in the mouth!

I adore Chipotle. I really do. Always fresh, and the guacamole tastes good. But on my visit yesterday, I got a chicken bowl with hair in it!! I took the closed bowl outside to the park to eat it, opened it, and there was hair in with all the ingredients :( 
I have never had that happen. And I don't have black hair either. Please fix this, Chipotle.
I've been here twice and both times the customer service was good. They were very friendly! I got a burrito both times and they packed it full which was most definitely worth the money.
Pretty awesome. Best thing I've had in a while. I'm usually a white meat only person. The dark meat tender were so good!

It was drizzly and grey last night, but Neon Lobster staff charmed & warmed me up with a delicious sample of their seafood stew...but I had already ordered my lobster roll and fries...but now I can't wait to go back and get a bowl-delicious! The fries didn't disappoint after reading other reviews-I took my roll home and the fries were still crispy and hot when I got home. I should have just stayed and eaten my hot lobster roll since they dont transport as well as the fries. Staff is great and I am so happy they have added something so friendly and yummy to this area of the city!

This store is absolutely horrible it's not only dirty the employees lack professionalism and cleanliness that being said this is why I give this location 1 Star! Also the floor was so slippery that i wouldn't be surprised if someone gets really injured in this location!

Build your own nachos- whoever invented this concept is a genius! I loaded mine with chicken, cheese and two types of salsa. They also have spicy queso and habanero.

The food is delicious and decently priced (cheaper than chipotle). 

The service here is really good; the employees are cordial and the very quick.

I was really excited to finally try the sushi-burrito, but was quite disappointed. First, I was confused that typical sushi was not on the main menu- like tuna, salmon, white fish, etc. Veggies and chicken were the main ingredients, while tuna was only available as it was on special.

Pros
-novelty
-you can say you've had a sushi burrito

Cons
-fairly expensive
-on the small size in portion
-wasn't entirely impressed with the flavor
-extremely limited seating

Best drunk food around.
Chicken? yes. Mac n'cheese? yes.
Eat all your feelings.

My go to place for when I am feeling like Chinese. It's more of American-Chinese, and the orange chicken is what pulls me in. I have been eating Panda for years and never have I been disappointed, however, I do wish the didn't change to brown rice in their Fried Rice. Love this place and if you have never tried it you are missing out.

So the food here is pretty effing good. Evrey thing from the chicken to the mack and cheese  is amazing. It's not an extensive menu so I've had everything. The dark meet probably their best. It's a solid go to. Their sandwiches are pretty good too. The reason that I'm giving it 3 stars is because of their service. When you go to wishbone you either A. live around the area, or more likely B. Are wasted in the gayborhood and need some food ASAP. B is the more likely scenario. And unfortunately you're going to be in for a bit of a wait. The issue is that the staff is pretty slow. Like brutally slow. And they get slammed with customers and online orders to the point where you want to strangle someone you're so hungry. But the food is amazing. Truly amazing.
Worst drive-thru EVER!!! The wait is so long it's ridiculous! And this is every time!

I had the infamous sushiritto. The salmon had a strange taste to it, but I wasn't so scared of getting sick that I stopped eating. It was strange having lettuce in my roll -- I can't say that it added much or that I would get it again. Same goes for the onions. 

Overall the experience was good, the location is cool, but the food wasn't so great. I'll definitely go back again, but but now I'll know better how to customize my order.

Well not ordering from here again. Paid $2.00 for avocado...got no avocado. Paid $.75 for a side of dressing..got no side of dressing. Paid $4.25 for about 15 chips and a brown guacamole that's about ¼ full...actually looks like someone else had gotten to it before me. 

Seriously who is checking these orders?? Why even include the option for extras if you just ignore them?

Edit: ALSO didn't realize that they didn't even bother to put any dressing on the burrito. So no side dressing and no original dressing. Great.

Holy Jeff Goldblum! Not since The Fly has there been such an interesting crossover.  
Lunch time in center city can be a tricky thing.  You have to start with a plan and make sure you don't overstuff yourself or else you will fall victim to the 2 PM sleepies.  You also have to make sure you don't understuff either or you will find yourself making a 2 PM trip to Brown Betty's....or so my friend tells me.

A few trips in and I can now declare I am a fan.  I started slow, with the shrimp tempura, but now I am a mixing and matching master, making my own creations.  I love all of their ingredients and the 2 folks I brought there as well became quick fans too.  

Maybe Philly will stop being known for their cheesesteaks and start being known as their sushi burritos.

Imagine the type of guys who serve you at a South philly deli. They have a slight accent of some sort.  They recognize you when you come in and remember your preferences. They jump over the counter to hug some of their regular customers.  They ask you a bunch of questions about your order, many of which you never considered ("do you want onions? peppers - is that hot or sweet? how do you want the bagel cut?).  They want you to get what you want.  They are the kind of servers you consider family.  

That's what you get at Fresco. The staff is awesome.  But, you get all of that in a larger style restaurant in Center City. 

The food is A-ok.  I have tried a few salads, some desserts, a wonderful vegetable pannini, a bagel to eat in and a bagel to go.  All good.  The price is right. The location can't be beat. Try Fresco.  I think you will be pleased.

I do appreciate the innovation that is the "sushi burrito" but I think I may like my sushi to be just sushi and my burritos to be burritos. Although the chicken katsu was flavorful and delicious, I felt strange biting into such an ample portion of sushi flavor. The line was very long but it moved quickly and it was nice eating my sushi burrito in Rittenhouse sq park nearby. I tried it once and do not avidly plan on getting it again but I do recommend it for anyone who still means to check it out!

Apparently finding a salad bar in center city is rather difficult - i've tried to find one that has a good variety that isn't $7.99/lb (I'm looking at you Whole Foods!)

Good variety, fresh ingredients (minus a few canned goods...but what do you expect when you get Chick Peas?) and reasonably priced! Also- i have a slight addiction ot their croutons.... Their Chicken is fresh - not the typical chewy/sometimes slimy salad bar chicken you can get.

In addition to the salads, they have a good selection of hot foods as well as a few desserts, tuna salad and chicken salad. 

Friendly cashiers and workers are constantly refilling the produce! Definitely a nice change to visit when in Reading Terminal Market if you don't want to be in a food coma past lunch time

Qdoba is sort Chipotle. Honestly, besides some slight variation, I cannot tell the difference. It's a chain. They make burritos on an assembly line. You can get tacos or quesadillas. It's like someone said, hmmm, Chipotle, I can do that, made some minor tweaks, and bam.

Anyway, if you like one, you'll likely like the other. It's all the same.

Their idea of a sushi burrito is cute and it is fun to eat! I ordered the crunch (shrimp tempura) and slammin salmon. The burritos were falling apart as I bit into them though since seaweed and rice don't really hold everything together. The mango strips in the slammin salmon adds a nice fruity touch. The shrimp in the shrimp tempura crunch wasn't the freshest. They are about $8-9 each. I was disappointed that they were so small for that price (definitely not burrito sized). It is more like a gimbap or uncut sushi roll than a burrito.

There is a bar with a few high stools inside, but I would recommend taking your sushi "burritos" to rittenhouse square and enjoying it the park.

WOW!! It was delicious. All their signature rolls sounded good. I chose the slammin salmon roll and it was SLAMMING. Each bite made me love it even more. 

I washed it down with sweet green tea which was also delicious - just right amount of sweetness. 

I'm definitely coming back to try everything on the menu.

The item here is the mac n' cheese. It's really a cross between mac n cheese and hamburger helper with that being said it is delicious. The jalapeno cheddar cornbread is tasty and it's a nice portion. I recommend having it with the honey butter that they have. 
Super cool after the party spot.

Every now and then I try to fool myself into thinking I like sushi. When my friends and I needed something quick and light on a hot day, we decided to try out the sushi burrito at Hai Street. Dining Partner and I split The Crunch with brown rice. Three bites in I knew I still didn't like sushi and this was not the burrito taste I was hoping for. Dining Partner being a sushi liker, had no problem eating the remainder of the burrito. If you like sushi you should try this. But if you don't like sushi this isn't going to sway you to the other side.
The workers here are the dumbest bunch of idiots I have ever laid eyes on. Every time I come here it's always a clusterfuck with these idiots.

I think the weather brings out odd cravings. First hamburgers, now hot dogs. 

After a horrible bout with internship, I hurried out of that building for a hot dog, plus tea -- reviewing tea spot right after this. 

I got to Frank's early so I witnesses the ladies prepping the meals of the deal. Everything was steaming hot and looking very tasty. Too bad I  wasn't in the mood to eat anything heavier. The hot dogs were not ready so I told them to take their time with it. Didn't take long at all. 

I took the two hot dogs, kosher, with the side of fries to the tea spot. It was a bit chilly a couple of weeks ago but the dogs were piping hot by the time I got around to them. They were very tasty and the fries were more than enough. In fact, I had to waste the fries because I couldn't eat them all. If you have children or just a child this would be a good lunch to chow on because it was plenty for me. 

Now, about a few days ago I went back again and guess what I got. Two hot dogs minus the fries. I caught them when they closing but I wanted something quick anyways. I WILL try their other dishes. Trust.
Delicious shawarma in a casual to-go or sit-in establishment similar to Halal Guys or Chipotle style. We especially enjoyed the falafel - made fresh for us !  Also the  tzatziki sauce is legitttt

I thought to myself how can a place mess up boneless wings? They're so easy.... I should have listened to all the reviews. I ordered boneless BBQ wings; they were overcooked to the point where it became difficult to chew after a while. Also they were dry, and they were very stingy with the BBQ sauce. Charged at extra 85 cents for a side of ranch. I didn't even finish my food, thats how gross it was. Definitely won't be back. There's really nothing good I have to say about this place. No wonder why they're always empty.

I have been seeing a bunch of people on here as well as Instagram posting about this place and have been trying to get it into my schedule ever since. I was  over in Center City one weekday on my way to UPenn and decided to drop in and give this place a try. It is truly a wonderful place and is the Japanese version of Chipotle. 

The only negative with this place, which is why it is receiving 4 stars is that there is absolutely no real seating there are 4 stools against the wall and that's it. That's fine and all I guess and luckily the wraps/rolls whatever you want to call them transport well. I went with the Mexicana which is the pork belly roll and it was phenomenal, screw the seating at this point. It was also pretty substantial and I was full after eating it but I did try the chips and guacamole anyways and it was really good as well. This is a solid spot in Center City and I hope that at some point they expand, move to another location that bigger, or just open another one. In the meantime though I will deal with this place not having seating. Go, get there now.

Wayyyyyyy better than the chipotle down the street and I'm a huge chipotle fan. The employees are much nicer and they aren't skimp with the portions. Everyone is friendly. Queso and guac are Fuego. I've been going her way more Diego how atrocious the chipotle is around the corner.

Fist time trying a "SushiRRito", I'm extremely pleased with the flavors and the size. Soooo good that makes me wanna go eat there again, but I'm just a traveler passing by. 
I ordered the Flamin' Tuna, but instead of the guacamole wasabi I ordered just avocado and added spicy mayo to it and made it extremallt delicious and extra spicy :)

Well. A Sushi Burrito is a fun little concept, and a tasty one at that! Not as many vegan options as I'd like (ONE base, & it looks like they changed it from mushrooms to zucchini, which, for this vegan, is a total bummer, and none of their signature rolls are vegan). Give us another base option--it'd be fun for me to get a little more creative here. Also, maybe clearly mark which of your sauces are vegan.

Still, it IS vegan friendly, and I really did enjoy my meal here...of course that was before they lost the mushrooms from the menu...so I'm torn between 3 and 4 stars. Let's call it a 3.5.

Sushi burritos are the gods gift to the planet. You order chipotle style and more down the line adding or subtracting items into your wrap. I split and tuna and salmon and both were amazing. I could have left out the asparagus in the tub wraps though... 

The place is little and set up for take out but does offer a few stool seats to sit. 

All in all I will furrr sure be frequenting here.

much like all of their stores I do adore their cafeteria style seating.. it really lets you know the kind of place you're in... the food is ok. It's not GOOD.. but its definitely not BAD.. I like the fact that they put cilantro in their rice.. however the amount of rice to EVERYTHING else is way to much. A vegetarian burrito is not well thought out and it seems you end up with a pile of carbs ( rice, beans, tortilla) and a little cheese salsa etc for good measure.. The actual vegetable choice is only like onions and peppers.. Now I'm a fan of onions and peppers but I don't want an onion and pepper burrito... You'd think a chain like this would have created some better vegg friendly options.. The quesadillas ( cheese) are ok.. all in all I'd always choose mexi-cali over this place.. but mexi cali has weird hours.. so this is when we end up in here...every worker I've come across has been nice and helpful.. All in all it's just OK

My free custom roll was achieved in solid 2 hours on the opening day in the line thanks to my sister...

I ordered the salmon w/ brown rice, spicy gochujang, asparagus, cucumber, red cabbage, fried shallots and yuca chips. Although the salmon gets a little lost texturally in the mushy rice, the flavors were there.! This hybrid of mexican and japanese always danced around in my head and i'm happy theres a place in the city where I can execute it. Personally hating the idea of rice inside a tortilla, the nori wrap is perfect, light and crip.  Tad too sweet & lacking in acidity, the Hibiscus Iced Tea was still very refreshing. 

It is no one cuisine, eat it, savor it & enjoy it because it taste pretty good. I'm returning soon for the steak and shrimp tempura. 

P.S: Staff is young and full of enthusiasm, its pretty cute.
