Ordered take out, super fresh and delicious chicken salad! Very friendly and nice staff. The pastries looks amazing, everything is house made.

I have ordered multiple times from this McDonald's and not once has my full order been correct. I paid $50 the other day for multiple meals and I received about $10 worth of food. I have not even received a refund. Ridiculous.

The first time I went there I ordered a meatball sandwich and an order of french fries. The amount of fries was more than I would have expected and would have been a sufficient meal by itself. I also like the sausage and peppers. As with anything you get at Reading Terminal Market, get the food "to go" as you will have to walk with the food and search out a spot in the seating area.

I've been here plenty of times but never wrote a review. I know they advertise themselves as sushi burritos but it tastes nothing like sushi. It's more like a Japanese bento box in a wrap. Overall it's still good if you know how to order and what you like in your wrap/bowl. Again, do not expect this to taste like a sushi roll. The closest it'll taste like is a giant California roll if you want to compare it to sushi. Sushi is not simply rice, vegetables, and a protein.
The staff is very friendly and helpful since they know the menu is different. For a fast casual restaurant I think it's good. I'd definitely recommend dynamiting your roll (deep frying it) and wasabi guac.
My only complaint is that for a "sushi" burrito place they do not have regular wasabi (only wasabi guac which is $1 extra) and I wish they had seawood as a topping option. At least make it a bit more authentic/Asian.

I'm a huge fan of Wendy's, even after working there throughout high school and college. They have high standards of cleanliness and customer service, except not here. The wait inside the restaurant is longer then I have ever experienced, 1 very rude cashier, who was taking her time socializing. 1 person left behind me while waiting for my order to be taken. When I got to the register I was not greeted, strike one. She took my order, and when I went to hand her payment, walked away. When she finally came back I handed her my card and she gave it back to me so flippantly. Got my food and they forgot the sauce for the nuggets, I know they specifically ask for a reason. Back in line for another 10 minutes for that. Finally sat down to eat in a dining room that was very dirty, only to be solicited by someone selling bootleg movies. They are getting 2 stars for my food being tasty and hot, the fries especially have to be hot to be enjoyed. Otherwise, this Wendy's needs some customer service training.

Running errands today and needed a quick bite to eat- and I just moved to Philly from AZ so I knew Jimmy Johns would be fast. Ordered the #1 Pepe and had it handed to me before I finished paying. In my opinion, the bread is what makes a sandwich, and the French bread was amazing at this location. So soft and perfectly baked! After talking with the employees, found out they were under new management since about a week ago and seems like they are really out to make a great impression. Big plus, they'll deliver right to my house!  I recommend calling to see if you're in their delivery zone though.

toooooo much rice it was so thick with rice and the citrus pork was cold there was just not enough flavor going on in my bites .. I been dying to try this place and I was disappointed but looks like other ppl love it but I won't be getting it again

I don't think I ever stepped foot into this Burger King, although I live nearby for over 15 years. The reason being is that I only venture here late night and used the drive through for my fix on fries. Late night service was good. But drive thru are always weird and creepy for me. Especially when the speakers are messed up, or people working talk over the mic and I hear everything. Fun tales of late night cravings.

This place is absolutely adorable! I went with my sister around 5pm. We were able to get a seat by the window overlooking the street, but there is not much seating otherwise. 
I ordered the tempura crunch but added carrots and fried shallots. My sister customized her own pork belly sushi. This place isn't "proper" sushi by any means but I give this place 4 stars for friendliness, creativity, and deliciousness! It's a creative twist and though it doesn't taste like traditional sushi, it doesn't make it bad by any means. The sushi seemed small but ended up being more than either of us could finish. My only negative comment is that the green tea was watery and too sugary

I love this place. I live about two blocks away and Jimmy John's makes for a great snack (or meal) for under five dollars.

I've gotten the #2 Big John (roast beef) and the J.J. BLT. The roast beef sandwich was fantastic! It could've used some black pepper, but otherwise it was spot on. I love the bread here and the general freshness of the ingredients. The BLT was also great - they're pretty generous with the bacon, which is, of course, the best part.

The space is also fun; I love the funny signs up on the walls. It gives you something to look at when you're trying to avoid awkward silences with the person you're with...not speaking from experience. The staff was funny. It's a pretty good location to put a sandwich/hoagie/sub store - within a student apartment-type complex, next to a Capogiro's, on a college campus.

Next up on the list to try: #4 Turkey Tom and #6 Vegetarian (my friend swears by it).

This was my last meal before heading back to the DMV a year and some months ago. I was dying to try this place out since it opened in the summer of 2014. I went here on a Sunday morning so the restaurant wasn't busy at all and got the Slammin' Salmon and the Hai Satay. My eyes glistened with happiness as I saw my sushi burritos being made but as soon as I got the chance to take a couple of bites, I immediately succumbed to dissapointment. 

In all honesty,  both were OK. Not what I expected but it wasn't bad. The sushi burritos lacked flavor and the rice just didn't seem to match the toppings very well. People tend to forget that the rice is as important as any other ingredients involved. Maybe it was just a bad day but it definitely wasn't a memorable experience for me. Would I go here again? Maybe but I wouldn't sweat it if I was on the way to this place and my car broke down.

Good soul food. Nice variety.  Taste yummy too.. Fried chicken a little dry but everything else was good. Yama, black eye peas, ribs, greens, fried chicken, smothered turkey, Mac and cheese and more.  The food cost $6.99 per pound plus tax.. yes it's weighed..

They also have a salad bar option if you're not interested in soul food

Cons... needs a little more seasoning in their food.. but I'm sure not everyone can tolerate really down home spice..
This jimmy johns took 40 minutes to deliver. I also found a hair in my sandwich and they forgot my chips. Soooo....

I went to Hai Street Kitchen on opening day for an early dinner around 5:30 (only waited about 3 minutes, not very crowded.)

The space is tiny.  I would imagine on a busy day that it looks packed and intimidating.

I ordered "The Crunch" - shrimp tempura, mango, asparagus, with brown rice (brown rice added a nice hint of flavor.) I really enjoyed my roll. 

My only gripe was the size of the roll.  I was expecting Chipotle-sized sushi burrito, and got a much slimmer, slightly shorter burrito that was full, but not packed to the seams like Chipotle.  Granted, maybe if I had ordered the larger size "go zilla."  I left satisfied and full, but was just expecting a little bigger.

The staff was friendly, helpful, and attentive. And seemed to be working reasonably efficiently for a busy opening day. 

I will definitely be returning to try some other combinations!

great subs. better prices. 

alot of people dont understand that JJ's isnt subway or wawa.  they have a fairly set menu.  you can take some things off or add some things to your sandwiches but its not a build your own sandwich place.  this however, isnt a bad thing since they've done a good job of building an extensive list of hoagies for you to order.  

the bread is always awesome.  i can understand that some people might complain about the amount of meat on the sandwich, but i think most people would agree that a smaller amount of good quality lunch meat is better than a pound of crap lunch meat.  i mean seriously, if anyone is comparing the quality of JJ's to wawa or subway they are kidding themselves.  

the prices are awesome and the speed in which you get the sandwich is oddly fast.

4.5 stars for the food and 3.5 stars for the price. It really isn't a great bang for your buck, but I'd say it's a nice occasional lunch treat if you're craving sushi and don't have time to hit up a sushi restaurant. I've only had the salmon which was quite delicious.

A staple for chicken lovers everywhere. Great homemade sauces. Great bottled beer selection. The mac and cheese was good but not the greatest. Citrus honey biscuit was good as well. Friendly staff. Try to mix the don sauce with the sweet chili sauce for a clutch savory taste.

Only 4 stars because I hope they can make the floor and tables less sticky.

All hype. Little protein given, too much rice and veggies (and you have to pay extra for the "better" veggie sides). They were out of the spicy tuna tartare, so got the salmon tataki which made me feel sick. Only thing I liked was the pickled jicama. 

But most importantly, one of the employees was extremely rude. Blonde girl with glasses called customers "f***ing idiots" for accidentally throwing out trash in a garbage disposal that was "out of order". Apparently there was a sign, but it was nowhere to be seen, and either way, customers should not be treated like that. Would give 0 stars because this place does not know sushi or service, so will not be returning.

I would say the place is okay. Really hyped up. Maybe I had really high expectations. I got the slammin salmon and my sister got the flaming tuna. Bland when it came to taste... If you try it, think of a big ol handroll.
Small plates. Good food and drinks but portion sizes are very small for a neighborhood bar in Point Breeze.

A great find when I visited Reading Market and had a flight later that afternoon.  Made myself a nice salad for the flight, and it was like $5.  Much bigger and better than airport food.  Chicken on the salad was really, really good.  Wasn't expecting that.

A good choice for salad, and the vegetables are fresh.  Located right in the center city, and  a good alternative to pizza, hoagies or other typical fast food.  The only thing to watch out for is the $6.69 per pound price which can add up, especially when dressings and condiments are priced just like any other item.

Sushi burrito is a good idea. I mean, who doesn't like a giant sushi roll with lots of toppings and ingredients? So I was excited when Hai St opened shop. I first tried their sushi burrito in one of the Walnut Street street fairs, they had a table out selling their burritos. My friends and I got some and it didn't turn out that good. The burritos were mass produced and stored in a cooler/refrigerator before, the roll was cold and the rice has hardened. Not a big issue, there should be a different standard for what you can get on the street, you really can't expect that much.  It's definitely not a great first impression but I would give them a second chance.

So for a business meeting today we thought of going outside the norm and order sushi burritos from Hai St. I thought since we're going for custom orders, we will get freshly made burritos. Using UberEATS we placed an order for 7 people, paid $80 and waited 45 mins to receive... 1 burrito. 

I called them back and at first they couldn't find the order, and then proceed to tell me that they only wrote down the first item on the list and since they were so busy that they ignored the other items on the list. If I want my food, they will issue a refund and I'll have to reorder, pay the handling fees that UberEATS charges and wait for another god know how long.

The staff over there seems to think that issuing a refund would make everything alright. "Well, we're issuing you a refund" Meanwhile, I'm panicking about what to say to our clients and my colleagues since it's already past 1. The lack of training and the nonchalant attitude of the staff speaks to what kind of a place this is. Needless to say, I don't think this place is for me and I urge you to not consider them as your catering option.
Went around 4:30 so no big line. definitely in the top 3 most generous bowls I've ever had

PROS: Fresh ingredients, interesting concept, tasty
CONS: Pricey for lunch

Spending close to $10 for a tasty but small salmon sushi-rito (or a large salmon sushi roll, depending on how you look at it) is not a bad deal. At a normal sushi restaurant, you'd likely order a much smaller sushi roll for around the same price. 

But burrito-fying the concept of sushi leads consumers (me) to associate lower quality to the roll on a subconscious level, I think. You get a higher quality and higher-priced NORI-wrapped Asian burrito, in contrast to the cheaper, larger, carb-intense Chipotle burrito.

If you have some extra money to burn and a small appetite, definitely hit this place up!
Food is good and fresh, but the floor and counters need a bit cleaning. It would make a much better place if my shoes don't stick to the floor when I walk
Service was quick, slammin salmon was amazingly delicious, and staff were very nice.  There isn't much sitting space, just some stools against the wall and window.

Jimmy John's is so bad that if one of my friends mentioned to me that it was "pretty awesome", I'd assume they were being sarcastic. The sandwich bread is bad, and the cold cuts all taste the same. It does earn the honor of being "cheap" and "open late at night", but it's confusing to me why people go here when decent restaurants are so close! 

On the plus side, they are always very quick with sandwiches and the people behind the counter at this location are extremely nice.

My visit to the University City Wishbone 3 years ago left me wanting more, but oh how things have changed! I went to the new Gayborhood location and first noticed the large selection of specialty sodas. They've got some innnnnteresting flavors! I opted for two pieces of dark and one piece of white chicken, a root beer, and a honey buttermilk biscuit that ran me around $12 bucks. They have wings, sauces, salads, sandwiches, mac and cheese, and really ridiculously good looking desserts. One of my gripes before was that it gets expensive, and it still does. But it is really good too. I love the options of dark or white meat and will be making this a more frequent meal. The decor has a rustic feel which is identical to the UC location and the restaurant and eating area were super clean.

Food is decent and filling but the place is so dirty it's enough to make me not go back with fear of how things are actually prepped. There's food spilled all over the counter where the staff put together your food. The floors are also dirty and you can see their work stations behind the counter are not kept clean or organized either. The staff is also under whelming, and robotic. No greeting, no emotion, let alone any type of eye contact. Might as well automate it with robots for cheaper production.

Really incredible.  If you can find this place it is sooo worth it.  Best $10 you'll spend any day. The basic burger slider is insanely delicious. And the "illadelphia" cheesesteaks are out of this world. 

This is a serious no-frills establishment.  Just a counter and a shared eating area (shared with the bagel place, Schmear). But what else do you need when the food is this good?  Please go, you'll thank me later.

Ingenious!!! Sushi burritos?!!! Yaasss please! So I have yet to officially dine in, but my husband's work had a food truck luncheon. My thoughtful hubby brought home the spicy shrimp burrito.

It's pretty much a shrimp tempura roll in burrito form with additional veggies- cabbage, radish, and carrots. Just be careful of the tail, unless you like the extra crunch. Ha! 

If you're a sushi fan, then this is simple and healthy lunch (right?). Hope to try out the other options soon!!

Love this place so much! So delicious and a great alternative to regular sushi. I went to Japan a year ago and since I got back was unable to eat American sushi (sounds bad, but it's just not like the real thing). The point is, this stuff makes me really happy based off of the taste and freshness. I am a sucker for the slammin salmon roll with the gochujang sauce. The servers are as friendly as you'd like someone to be who spends most of their day on their feet. No complaints here, except the price it could be lower, but it is rittenhouse after all!

This place has improved so much since it opened. They hired new staff and boy has it made the biggest difference in the food and service.

A+ to service. I was amazed to be asked if I wanted a sample of a drink I was considering...  and even made the drink custom to my liking. Big shout out to staff member Chantel - keep it up!

*I advise to skip going at night because it's clear that quality does not match during the day (unless you want luke warm burgers/overly salty fries)

Fun!! As a vegan, I do agree with the other veggie Yelper who stated that it would have been helpful for them to label if their sauces were veggie friendly.. Not mandatory but helpful. I always research places before I dine and wrote the Hai Street before dining and the General Manager was very quick to respond with this list of veggie friendly options. In case anyone else out there is interested, here is the list.. Obiously, for your main ingredient you would choose the zucchini.. For your sauces you have the option of the following: Black pepper teriyaki, salsa verde, gochujang, ginger miso, and the spicy peanut dressing. Sadly the wasabi guac is NOT vegan, womp womp! But my boyfriend said it is delicious for all of you non vegans! All of the veggie toppings are vegan friendly except the papaya salad, as well as the crunchy toppings. I opted for the zucchini with brown rice and various veggie toppings with the ginger miso sauce. It was very tasty! I left feeling fulfilled. I saw that a lot of people were saying they felt that the portion sizes were small.. We were satisfied but we didn't come on empty. We both also had teas which were delicious as well. We will return to sample different sauces and combos. The staff was friendly and efficient. We came on a Saturday shortly after they opened so we didn't have a problem getting a seat but I could see how this would be an issue if you went during a busy time..

I really like the taste and the entrees that qdoba offers.  Always had a good portion, fast service (once I had only 3 minutes on the meter, no joke), and respectful servers. I hope they keep it up at this location, some are falling off. 

Qdoba is missing a star because of the limited parking at times when local traffic is heavy. A turn off when you're really hungry.

Good, solid menu with reasonable flexibility. Cheap but fast, courteous service. Even their sides are pretty well done as well (chips, cookies, etc)

Four stars for being open late, but three because I never feel full after eating the sandwiches...

This hot and cold salad bar has a lot of variety and would probably be a haven for someone who is extremely indecisive. The hot bar rotates daily with different items, which is generally nice in terms of variety. The cold bar appears to have the same daily choices. I've tried some of their chicken dishes such as the chicken marsala and their chicken wings. I enjoyed them, but didn't care for the chicken fingers as I found them to be overly fried and looked a bit dry. The mac and cheese was just "ok". I really did enjoy their fried whiting fish. By far, my favorite thing I've tried there is the sweet potatoes. SO good! The actual salad bar has a ton of different vegetable varieties, which makes the idea of having a healthy meal super easy.
I haven't tried their breakfast offerings, but I've peeked at the hot bar during breakfast time and it looks tasty. 

A downside is the price, which is currently weighed at $6.99 per pound. It's very easy to go overboard and next thing you know, you're paying $13 for lunch. Yikes! I've also noticed that this place seems to be a favorite amongst the 60 and over crowd. The cashiers are also friendly as well.
#5 Vito - really good clean italian sandwich.

Walked in and was surprised by the cool geometric decor! The staff was very friendly and patient with any questions about the menu. The mixed drinks were delightful but the food stole the show. We had the charred broccoli dish, the cauliflower dish, the pierogies, and the massaman sweet potato curry dish. We shared everything and were blown away by each one! Will definitely be coming back and have been relentlessly suggesting it to my clients :)

Yikes. Given the rave reviews, I had built up so much positive anticipation for months before coming here, only to walk away impressed with how unimpressed I was by the food I had here. Perhaps this not really the place to go for dinner, though given how some of the dishes tasted (or didn't... as things tended to be on the less flavored side), I'm not sure I would consume them at other times of the day either.

Out of the 4 food items we ordered, the chicken liver mousse appetizer (now $6) was the only satisfying one. Although it consists of two (somewhat sweet) finger-sized slices of cake (listed as "paw paw" bread, or papaya bread) topped with dollops of chicken liver cream (it had the texture of soft cream cheese, rather than mousse), it tasted good and had a good combination of flavors and textures. 

We also tried the pierogies (~$10ish). Although this was my second-favorite dish of the night, the pierogies were still not memorable, as I don't recall the filling (other than puréed potatoes). The lightly caramelized onions added a nice touch, but the sour cream on the side did not seem like a very thoughtful choice of "sauce" to complement the pierogies. 

Upon hearing that the server liked the toasted spelt gnocchi best out of the more entrée-like items, I decided to give this dish a try. The mushroom broth was the highlight, and taste-wise, there was nothing too problematic about the overall dish. However, texture-wise, this dish was very incoherent, and even unpleasant. Unlike typical gnocchi, which is fluffy and tends to have a slight chew or bounce to it, this gnocchi crumbled upon contact, did not absorb much of the mushroom broth, and got stuck to the crevices of my teeth as I was chewing it. I found myself twirling my tongue against my teeth like a windshield wiper to get all of the potato out. The mixture of cooked and raw white mushrooms that came with it was also not particularly pleasant. For $16, this turned out to quite an expensive dish, given its small size, the ordeal I went through to eat it, and how I felt like I hadn't eaten after eating it. I've had tastier and more filling gnocchi for cheaper at "fancier" restaurants in Philly. 

And while $11 is not a wallet-breaking amount, the squid dish was probably one of the most expensive versions of squid I've ever had in Philly per cubic centimeter of tiny chewy white pieces of squid, embellished with a lot of nasturtium leaves. (This dish could be called "Nasturtium Leaves" instead of "Atlantic Squid" given that you see more leaves than squid.) Surely, I was not at Per Se, so I was confused as to why such a tiny amount of food was placed in such a large plate.

I was still hungry after we left (I had to eat a Trader Joe's frozen meal). The menu is small and consists of mostly small-sized, carb heavy items. I also didn't see a lot of menu items other reviewers described. There was nothing truly substantial to choose from, so definitely don't come here hungry! It was also pretty dark and cold in the restaurant. I had trouble seeing my hunny across the table. The bar area is brighter than the tables along the wall. 

On a positive note, the restaurant looks pretty and the service was good. I would definitely come back to look at the restaurant and maybe grab a beer (from their small-ish beer list) at the bar. (I didn't find the Basque cider to be appealing either, but maybe it's because I didn't expect it would taste like kombucha, since it was listed under wines along with a cabernet, rosé, etc...) I think a lot of creativity went into creating this restaurant and its menu, but I'm not sure the fine dining prices are warranted based on the food quality and size.

The meat is marinated and flavorful. Every piece of meat has the outside crisp edge it gets on the spit, every single piece. The hummus is near perfect, not whipped consistency or too thin.  All of their salads are very tasty and fresh. I got the steak shwarma with a couple falafel on the side. The falafel are 75 cents a piece for a large ball of perfectly done falafel. The bread is baked onsite and is the perfect thickness to retain all of the juices from the salads and tahini. Finally, cheap good Arabic food in CC.

.2 miles from my house makes me happy, warm and fuzzy. Welcome to Point Breeze and thank goodness you are here. We watched with anticipation as you were being born on our weekly walks home from Breezy's (also stellar) breakfast and lunch. 

Tonight we finally got here and fell in love with the cozy funky decor and warm and happy service. The parsnip fries were a religious experience. I'll be dreaming about them all week. The Brussels  sprouts were incredible. Such a unique addicting flavor. My husband enjoyed the Passyunk Zeke cocktail and I loved my holiday wheat beer on tap. We can't wait to come back. So happy for more upscale choice in our Point Breeze neighborhood. 

Four stars only because it's nice to have a funky menu but a few old standards or mainstream choices would be nice for our picky eater friends too.

Wishbone participated in the Philly restaurant festival that we attended at the Academy of Natural Sciences.  Their mac and cheese was one of the best dishes at the event and the chocolate chip cookie was really good too!  The only reason I am not opting to give them five stars is that by the time our friends arrived to the event they were already out of the mac and cheese.

After I ordered my food I asked if they had any boxes of baba ghanoush left, the guy looked at me in a very unhappy and sort of upset manner and said I would have to make one for you. So I said no thanks that's fine. Then the woman who rang me up I asked her if I can get a bag she said bags are only for big orders and she asked me if I wanted a receipt and I said yes but she never gave me one. Really not the greatest customer service. I'll definitely look for other places near by as this is not worth it at all
We missed a reservation on a Saturday night. Wandering the streets , in the rain, we stumbled upon Wishbone. Food was great... coleslaw.. omg.. and we loved the beer selection. So happy we found it.

I have no complaints about their wings (been here twice & they were ALWAYS delicious & cooked to perfection), however, their online ordering system needs some work. I placed an order (6/10/2017) for my son to pick up while in the area, only to find out their computers were down so they NEVER received it. After sending screenshots of the order & confirmation number to my son, who in turn showed the ladies at the front counter (whom he said was very polite), then the order was placed. This is bad business (the reason for 4 stars). If an online order is placed & a pickup time is given, when arriving to the establishment the customer expects their order to be ready, NOT wait an additional 30 or more mins. That's the reason WHY I order in advance to save time waiting while there. The online system should be configured/adjusted/"tweaked" to know when  the restaurant's computers are down to keep from accepting pickup orders. For now, i'll just call beforehand to confirm if the computers are functioning properly before placing an online order...because I WILL be back!! :-)

Not only does this guy steal from his staff, he robbed the shit out of me. We ordered a chicken cutlet sandwich and were given a stale roll with 3 burnt chicken tenders on it and nothing else. It was just a roll with burnt shitty chicken tenders. I went back to the guy and asked if this was right and he said yes it was.  He even acknowledged that it was weird and nasty. Look closely at the picture that they call a "chicken cutlet sandwich". This guy makes a fortune selling cups of melted American cheese. People need to leave this place alone.

I got the platter for $12.20. The platter had a thigh, wing and two legs(BBQ chicken) w/ two sides(french fries&mac and cheese) as well as cornbread which costed me an addition of $1.55. The total cost took me by surprised because I thought it would be like $11.50 total, however, no. And on the menu, it said you would get a roll with butter. However I didn't get that which was weird. The food was okay. The BBQ chicken was the best, but their mac and cheese was typical and fries were like any normal fries. Their corn bread was good though. In all, it was okay. I don't think I would get it again.

Simple food.  Quick delivery.  Cheap.  No frills.  Nothing outstanding.  Somewhat under seasoned.  And really cheap, overly salty scrapple.  But everything was exactly A-OK.  Wouldn't hesitate to order again, if no other option with equal or greater star rating was available.

I came here during the Eagles parade to dine with my friends. Upon arrival, the server had the worst attitude. She didn't greet us or anything and her negative energy was annoying me very much.

Anyways my friends and I ordered our food. The server didn't bother checking on us or anything. About 15 minutes after we got our food, she dropped a check when we didn't ask for one. We ended up ordering more food, which I guess annoyed her. 

The food was okay. I guess this place is just convenient if you need a quick cheap take out when you're running late but definitely not a brunch place to sit and dine with family. 2 stars for the food.

Coming from SF, I was totally surprised to find a restaurant similar to Sushiritto. It's great that this place is a piece of home away from home!

The concept behind the sushiritto is so ingenius. It's basically a sushi roll in the form of a burrito, but the flavors mend together so seamlessly. (Well, ALMOST seamlessly, because personally rice and lettuce do not pair well together.) The employees hand-roll the sushirritos for you on the spot, so every time I order something here, the food tastes so fresh.

My favorite is the Slammin' salmon, but the pork belly is a solid option as well. For the health-conscious, Hai also offers a brown rice option! 

Overall, this is a really good lunch takeout spot!

This place was perfect for a quick lunch. It has a NYC cafeteria vibe on a smaller scale specific for chicken. Food is hot and ready and costs per pound so keep your hungry eyes in check. They serve beer and have plenty of space for individuals or groups. Weekends they stay open until 4am for those late night cravings.

The fried chicken has pretzel in the bread which sounds strange, but is a small flavor compared to the reset of the chicken and spices. They serve chicken tenders in both white and dark meat which is unheard of in this area. If you like onions and peppers in your mac and cheese it's worth getting a full container of the pretzel breading topped goodness. I finished up with a piece of jalapeño and cheddar cornbread that has a good kick and finishes sweet. 

This is my new philly comfort food spot for sure.
Friendly customer service and easy to order. Poke bowl wasn't as good as Hawaii but it certainly satisfied my craving. Will definitely go back to try something else!

I love this place. Nice guick spot to have lunch. People are friendly and food taste great. Now the extras aren't extras, which mran u csn get all on your burrito for the same low price. One thing I did notice it that tge burritos are a little bit smaller than they were.  But they're still good and filling.

The food when cooked right and your order is right is really good. I love the chili cheese fries. The service however is REALLY bad. The employees are rude and almost always get your order wrong. Sometimes I think they do that on purpose. I don't use cash anymore unless I give the exact amount because I just don't trust them. I recommend using a debit or credit card and checking your order before you pull away.

Let's start with the fact the whole restaurant was completely smoked out and smelled like old grease. Second the wait for your food is just outrageous. And last but not least the service was not professional at all. They were joking and being unprofessional the whole time I was there. Smh.

A few days ago, my coworkers were talking about this "sushi burrito" concept, and I was fascinated.  I didn't catch the name of it though, and then thought to myself that I'd have to ask them again on monday--when, on my way to UPS on Saturday, I saw Hai Street kitchen!!!  I was on my own for lunch, so I decided to try it out.

This is basically chipotle, except your pick of steak, pork belly, chicken katsu, shrimp tempura, tataki salmon, or grilled portobello, and toppings that are asian/mexican-ish.  what can I say?!?!  it was delicious.  I got the hai street chicken, and had to keep myself from chewing off the little bit of rice that was stuck to the paper.  The "burritos" aren't as crazy big as the ones at chipotle, but I think they're far tastier (probably just sick of Chipotle).  

One thing that wasn't quite clear to me--how do prices work for the "custom" rolls?

Anyhow, the place was clean, staff was friendly, service was fast, and it's great value--what's not to love?!  We'll be back soon :)  Keep it up!

If you're looking for sushi, hit up a sushi joint. If you're looking for a burrito, go to a Mexican restaurant. Unfortunately, this place reaffirms that you can't get the best of both worlds. 

In short, friend and I had high hopes for what we thought would be an enlarged, satisfying roll of sushi for each but instead left hungry and mildly disappointed. 

Friend got the classic burrito roll while I opted for the Slammin Salmon bowl. To be fair, the salmon (and sauce) was good, but for about $10 a bowl/roll, the protein portion was quite measly. It looked inviting at first glance when sliced in half, but the ends of the roll were mostly rice. Moreover when compared to the bowl, the burrito roll was noticeably smaller if you are to deconstruct it, with the only difference being the amount of rice (that was subsequently left over due to lack of sufficient protein) they pack. 

The concept of a sushiritto is novel and exciting and its execution even instagram-worthy, but unfortunately the actual thing is neither fun nor filling. People seem to have varying experiences here so I wouldn't recommend against it. As for me, I hope one day its quality & quantity will measure up to that of which at its Mexican counterpart i.e. Chipotle (yes, one can hope).

Just another place to grab a sandwich or wrap in the city - nothing too special.  Stopped here with two of my coworkers for lunch.  Unlike, Old Nellie's across the street, there was no one in here and there was not a long line to wait, so if you are hungry and in a rush, come here!  The staff is also very nice and friendly.

I got the buffalo chick wrap, pressed into a panini, a Snapple, and chips which totals right around $12.  It was pretty good.  There is outside seating, so we were able to sit outside on a beautiful day which was also a plus.  

The menu is versatile and you can customize it as you please.  Convenient if you are in the area, but nothing to write home about.
Wings to go who? Best wings I've had in awhile. The baked beans so sweet and perfect. The cashier's where amazing and on point. My new spot.

Bad experience.  The people working seemed wholly uninterested in providing good service.  Honestly, it doesn't seem that hard to read what's on a paper and then put that in a sandwich.  3 of the 4 subs we ordered came wrong, including one not having cheese that we paid extra for.  I was trying to tell the person making the sub to include certain items that she was just ignoring, but she was not interested.  They seem more concerned with getting things done fast (and wrong) than providing any kind of customer service.  And on top of all that, the food is bland.

If only I worked near by! Seriously, if I worked close by I would be there every day for lunch. It's just the perfect lunch spot. Think Chipotle but japenese more friendly and accommodating but not a chain. That's sort of how I would describe Hai Street.

My guy had the crunch in a roll and I had the screaming tuna in a bowl. Both were fantastic. I really loved the screaming tuna. The pickled mango really added to it and the tuna was fresh with an awesome kick. If I ordered it again, I would totally get the roll as all of ingredients in their take out bowl were hard to cut and put together. Not a big complaint, just an thought. 

Definitely try this place if you're nearby! I can only hope they plan to open another location closer to either where I work and/or near home!

I'm a sushi lover and was excited to try the sushi burrito, but I was unimpressed. I ordered the Slammin Salmon. The fish was fresh, but something in the execution just didn't go. The concept is great, so I would still go back and try something else.

Apparently they CAN screw up a simple sandwich order even with not a single person besides you in the store, lunchtime on a Tuesday. I guess that should have been my tip off to go elsewhere as well. Staff too busy discussing PlayStation to also be expected to follow protocol.

My order arrived with 4 items missing. I was told I'd be called back for a refund in 20 minutes, but never heard from them. In the online ordering system, I was forced to select a cheese in order to complete my order, but left a note saying I could not have cheese or it may kill me. Of course, when my order arrived, 2 out of 3 sliders wers covered in melted cheese. No picking through it possible. 

The delivery was quick, but I had to throw most of it out because it was inedible and I didn't get the main thing I wanted anyway because they forgot it. I rarely if ever give bad reviews because I don't like to take money out of anyone's pocket, but they literally took it right out of mine.

One of the busiest taco bells that I've ever been too. Needs to run more efficient given the fact that I see a staff of at least 10. 

All of the sauces needed to be replenished. 

If there is a partnership of Taco Bell and KFC there should be 2 managers.

My friend and I ordered food from here at 1:45am via Uber Eats. It was recommended because it was only .7 miles from our apartment and it said delivery in 30 mins or less! He ordered me a Big Mac, small fry w/ ranch dipping sauce and a chocolate milk shake. Our order was 40 mins LATE and when it finally arrived at our place, there was no ranch and instead of a chocolate milkshake,we received a soda. I called the Uber Eats Corp and they said they could only accommodate me for a 50% refund. It should have been a 100% refund simply because of the fact that it was not 30 minutes or less, which is false advertising and on top of that our order was wrong.

Quick stop pre ice skating for a healthy dinner.
Started with a mix of spinach and spring mix, perfectly grilled juicy chicken for my protein then added literally every topping except for feta ( sumac onions, olives, radish salad, beet slaw, julienned carrots, chickpeas) just to name a few, topped with a heaping scoop of hummus... all for $10!
Everything is fresh and the portions are huge. 
The falafel and pita looked good too but we weren't trying to carry anything around so something to look forward to next time.
A must go for center city dwellers looking for a quick healthy and filling meal.

Love the idea, I'm all in for Fried Chicken and Beers. Great takeout comfort food.

The execution is BAD. Cold and unappetizing fried chicken. The sandwiches attempt to mask this with exotic slaw's that swing and miss.

Chicken lovers move along...

Have always had good experiences with Jimmy John's in the past. Went to this location tonight at 9:03pm and walked in with my Fiancée. As we were looking at the menu, the register employee was counting his drawer and rudely snapped, "don't bother looking, we closed at 9:00 since students are out of town." WTF! 1) your door was not locked. 2) you are not a university cafeteria, you are a restaurant and franchised business with set hours of operation. 3) if you are going to change your hours, a simple note on the door would be a good first step to preventing customers from expecting you to be open. 4) when a customer comes in three minutes after your arbitrary closing time as a result of no posted sign and the doors being unlocked, I suggest being polite and professional.

You may be near my home, and I may enjoy your sandwiches, but you just lost the business of two non-students who would buy from you on a regular basis, year round.

Ordered a Nashville chicken sandwich and Mac to go. The chicken was juicy, the bread was fresh, the toppings were fresh. But it just didn't taste great. The Mac tasted a bit too much like stuffing - not enough cheese flavor.

I think this place has a ton of potential with some recipe tweaks. The staff I interacted with were fantastic too.

Not really worth the hype or the price. I'm a college student on a budget, and if I wanted a $10+ burrito I'd go to chipotle where at least I get more food. The concept of the sushi burrito is certainly interesting, but I'd try it once and probably not again. 

There's one option for vegetarians, and actually it was pretty tasty.

I really did not like the food here. My boyfriend and I went and he got a sushi burrito and I got a bowl. The proportions and ingredients and sauces are just not quite hitting the mark for what one would expect when eating Japanese inspired cuisine. I am not a picky eater and always finish my food but I did not care to finish my bowl at all.

Went during lunch time and they had the line moving like a well oiled machine. Was able to get in and get out and it was packed. The staff was friendly and fast and the food was what you would expect from Chipotle. No complaints here but get there before the rush if you're looking to dine in.

Judging from the reviews, people seem to have enjoyed this place significantly more than I did. I decided to try their hot food buffet. Everything about it was horrible. The food was hard, stale, and disgusting. I had the fried whiting, roasted potatoes, green beans, and chicken fingers. The chicken fingers were not terrible, but everything else was an utter waste of money. I was so disturbed when my platter rang up for $11 (it's weighed by the pound). I'm even more distraught that I spent that much on now that I have eaten it. This is the first review I've ever written, but the food was so bad that I feel it's warranted. Please do not put yourself through it. Choose to eat somewhere, anywhere else in RTM... or go with the salad.

Nice atmosphere. Nice service for the most part. Wine prices seemed low until I saw the light pours and tasted the mediocre quality. Beer selection was not my favorite. The dishes I tried were all fine (the pierogi, the fried chicken, and the sweet potato) but were all overpriced tiny portions.  I expected better value at 21st & Federal and would not go out of my way to return. That being said, they have a captive audience in that desolate neighborhood and seem to be doing just fine without me.

I guess I can't be a true Philadelphian because I am not impressed by these crabby fries. I recently went to my first Phillies game (gasp!). My friends were raving about how we must go to C&P and get the amazing crab fries. I didn't think these were anything special. They are just crinkle fries sprinkled with some old bay. The portion is large. You can tell they aim for quantity over quality. Overall, they are okay if you want fries, but I wouldn't make a special trip for them.

The price is high, but what do you expect at the stadium?

Overall a pretty good experience! I ordered the shrimp tempura and the new tuna sushi burrito. Comes in a cute little brown box. 

Hai street kind of reminds me of places like currito or subways where they make it in front of you. There isn't much place to sit. Maybe at most 10 seats.

I did eat them an hour later so it was definitely soggy. But I thought the shrimp tempura was much tastier than the tuna one. The tuna one was a tad too salty for me. The ingredients all go well together and it feels like you are eating one big sushi roll. Flavors are not that of typical sushi, so keep that in mind.

Naf Naf is a great fast casual addition to the area. It's like Chipotle in that you decide on pita vs. bowl, select a protein, and then go crazy with salad and garnishes. I've tried a few combos and my favorite is pita + hummus + chicken shawarma + chopped salad + purple cabbage + extra garlic sauce (which makes me self-conscious about my breath, but it's totally worth it).

I had always been good and never had ordered the fries, but then the nice cashier offered me free ones to sample...AND THEY WERE FREAKING DELICIOUS. Now I'm afraid to go back since I won't have any self control around those fries, but I know I'll be happily lured back soon enough.

This location has been the rage ever since it opened. Honestly, the roll is small and for its size, it's not enough to fill you up. It's great for a snack though. The crunch roll was good and I enjoyed the mango and the crispiness of the shrimp tempera. 

Be warned!! Eat the roll ASAP, bc it gets extremely soggy if you let it sit.
The last time was much different than the first time. Something happened with quality... because they don't make sushi burritos like they used to.

I never thought I'd love a chain sandwich restaurant, but hands down this place is better than any sandwich chain! How can you not love a place that boldly states: "We'd love to see you NAKED, but state regulations require shoes and shirts!" Ginchy and great! This place is close to work and I have a feeling my coworkers and I will be O.D.ing on the sandwiches!! 

The food is pretty tasty, too. I got the Beach Club (#12) on their 7-grain bread. It was fantastic! The avocado spread was perfect. The bread was thick and full of grainy goodness. The staff is pretty kick ass too - funny, witty, and very friendly. Go for the sandwiches, stay for the cookies!!
Typical chipotle but 5 stars for the girls working the online ordering section. They know me by name since I order too much and are always friendly.

OK, I know it's KFC, but in the spirit of Yelping everything, here goes...

This was a horrible fast food experience.

It's a crappy neighborhood, so I didn't expect a "pleasant" experience, but jeez... it's a national chain... aren't they held to standards?

My mom and I stopped after a doctor's appointment, and what the hell was I thinking.

We were told upon ordering that the crispy chicken was cooking and would be about a 10-minute wait. After about 30 minutes, they called our order. I get to the window, and he informs me that they don't have enough crispy chicken to fulfill my order. Um, dude, didn't you just say y'all were cooking some when we ordered??? Oh, right... it's all gone now cuz the next 10 orders that came in after we arrived had already been filled while we sat patiently and waited.

So, I say fine, I will eat original chicken... well, my side orders were wrong, even though they were printed correctly on the receipt... how do you get mashed potatoes and gravy out of COLE SLAW. It doesn't sound the same or even look the same, right?

Then I get home, cuz I'm not hanging around that joint, lol... they got bulletproof glass for a reason, and it's getting dark. I see no reason to learn why they need the bulletproof gas in a fkn KFC. So, anyway, one chicken wing tasted like it was left over from the day before, and the others were kind of hard, like they had been sitting under the heat lamp all day.

Yes, I called the 800 number on the back of the receipt, but I wasn't allowed to complete the survey. The automated system informed me that calls from store locations, employees and their families weren't allowed and I would have to call back from another phone.

Um... I have never worked for KFC, nor has anyone in my family, and I called from my CELL PHONE. UGH.
I just had there "SLAMMIN SALMON" that MotherF"kr is good and to take home I order the "HO-LEE-SHRIMP" @ the FESTIVAL FOOD TRUCK @Claridge ac nj. I must try the SO-CAL next time.

Tootsies is tucked into a huge food market in downtown Philly, way in the back, and is definitely a great addition to the culinary collection that makes up its surroundings.

Price-wise, a little steep, but understandable given the urban locale and that there's not a lot of competition for salad bars in the market. Fresh ingredients, decent amount of options (could use more SALAD options, seems like they spread themselves a bit too thin trying to do a dinner buffet AND a salad bar), a little seating area... this place has everything you need for a quick, healthy lunch!

Horribly salty and drowning in sauce.  I called Wingstop and told them my kids and I did not enjoy the wings, we tried 4 different flavors and its highly processed, cheaply made and even the blue cheese was salty.  I requested my money back and told them I would return the wings, they said no.

The food is fantastic and they have a good selection of beer. The bartenders and waiters are really friendly, knowledgable and attentive, and the vibe of the place is hip without being too trendy. 

I highly recommend the squid and the curry, but really everything I've tried has been superb (with the exception of the tasteless grape jelly that came with a cheddar cheese plate).  Prices are fair given the high quality of food and decent "small plate" portion sizes.

In words of Laura G., "this is the coolest thing I have ever put in my mouth." I am definitely a fan of this place, I mean I came here twice in one week! Hai street is a brilliant concept. With the sushi scene in Philly being so popular, Hai Street is definitely stealing some customers. It is similar to sushi, but differen in the sense that you have portion control of what goes in you mouth per bite. The seaweed wrapped Japanese burritos were amazing. My first visit I ordered the Hai Street Chicken which consisted of crispy chicken and some veggies. The seecond time I ordered The Crunch. This burrito was filled with shrimp tempura, spicy mayo, lettuce cucumber, pickled mango, and asparagus. Both of my orders were delicious. Side note: the tools the staff uses to create these burrito are pretty interesting! The machine that puts rice on the seaweed and the mat that helps roll up the burrito look awesome - I want some for my apartment (well one of each). Anyway, the homemade lemonade was a nice touch to my meal. I am interested in trying the boxed water next time! 

Heads up, there is barely any inside seating so be prepared to either pick a spot in Rittenhouse or head to a different indoor location i.e. office, apartment, friend's place...

Employees here are usually relatively friendly, which is rare in Philadelphia.  Usually all the businesses, especially in Ucity, have employees who are pretty miserable and are sick of the college kids.  Only reason I can't give 5 stars to this place is because I definitely got food poisoning from eating here once, and I rarely get sick from eating food.  I still go here to eat even after that, though!
Tried The Crunch - sooo good!! Hai Street was a recommendation after expressing my craving for sushi. So convenient for on the go. Can't wait to go back and try another one!!

I wish I could give this place 0 star. So my husband was so excited and called me telling me how cool this place is and he ordered food from here for our dinner. And this is how our food look like (24 dollars worth of food) with burned mac & cheese, burned biscuits & 2 wings & 1 leg. We came back the next day (the place closed when he got home) & asked them for the remaining chicken that was missing. After showing picture of the food, There was this one super nice lady that works there told us that her manager over charge us. She said the meal supposed to be 11 dollars because it's a combo but manager purposely charging us 24 because she charged everything individually. So the manager (her name is SHAY) called us back with an attitude and said reason why the bill is so high with a small amount of food is because it is 2.50 per biscuit which she never told us since the beginning that's why we are charged for 24 bucks (only 2 wings and 1 leg) with 2 burned side you guys. This is insane. I never leave people bad review but the restaurant doesn't even deserved all these stars. Btw if you guys come to this location the food is not even fresh because they don't make it there. If you guys want better wings go to bonchon in Chinatown or soho in northeast philly it is 100 percent better. To the owner of this place: I hope you will find a better manager because with this type of workers, you will end up losing many customer. There is much more I would like to write but for now this is it. Hope you will deal with customer better next time SHAY. Thanks and I'll never come back.
I WAS STARVING!!!! This was good food. Get the crunch with pickled onions instead of jicama!!!!! Omg!!!

I had the worst experience ever here. I ordered four sausage biscuits in the drive through. There was one car in front of me and maybe four or five guests inside. The worker at the window came to the window three times to confirm that I ordered four sausage biscuits as if this was a difficult order. He had us pull up past the window and said he would bring the food out. After waiting about 25 minutes I headed inside to cancel the order when the guy began walking around the counter to hand me the bag. After all of that, I asked to speak to a manager that refused to come out from the back to speak with me. So much for fast food and customer service. I usually stay away from McDonalds for several reasons. This experience confirmed that I need to stick with Chick fila for fast, good food paired with excellent service.

The food tastes fine - and the cafeteria style of "design your own" burritos, tacos and quesadillas is catching on fast -but don't be fooled.  It's still fast food - and it is super-duper HIGH in calories.  A typical burrito has 1100 - 1600 calories.  (Naked will reduce it by 330 - as the PLAIN TORTILLA is 330 whopping calories alone.)

That said - I do enjoy the Naked Chicked Burrito, no cheese, small (70 cal) taco-sized torilla on the side.

It's just too hard for me to "hold the guac" and save 220 calories.  That guac - for fast food guac tastes muy bien to me.

By the way - I think Jack-in-the-box owns Qdoba - I know Chipotle is owned by McDonalds.

FAST FOOD - people.
Eat under a health advisory.

Best salad in Philadelphia.  They rotate their salads every season, and it's always a magnificent blend of greens with fruit, nuts, and grains.  I tend to swap out the grilled chicken for the fried chicken, which they let you do at no additional cost.  The portion is gigantic, especially for the $10 that it costs.  I never get tired of it.

They've only been open for 4 days so I'll hold off on being super critical.  The atmosphere is soothing, the layout is tight but they're making it work in a small space.  Currently they don't take AMEX, so hopefully that'll change once they get all of the kinks worked out.  I'm not a fan of the food menu but the McQueen is a great cocktail! Delicious!  This spot is very much needed in this neighborhood.  Glad to have them!
I got violent food poisoning after I ate here last Friday, just wanted to give others a heads up.

Had a terrible sandwich from another shop...called up Jimmy Johns and they delivered in 7 minuets!
Love this place...Jimmy Johns is always there when I need them.  They deliver to my office (which is not easy to find).  I've tried most of the sandwiches and they are all delicious.  Friendly and super fast they are a terrific staple in University City.

After seeing a bunch of Sushirito restaurants during my trip to San Francisco, I was happy to see a place like Hai Street open up in Philly! I ordered a Salmon, mango, fresh greens with wasabi guacamole roll and it was amazing. So fun to eat. This place is more like a novelty place to me, so I haven't been back since, but it is definitely worth a try!

I ventured over to Panda in the Comcast building yesterday for lunch.  I gotta tell you, I WAS IN THE BATHROOM ALL DAY.  I may have gotten a bad batch of beijing or orange chicken because I was sick for the rest of the day.  I couldn't even finish an email without running to the bathroom.  Although I typically like their food, that was my last visit to Panda Express.

Neon Lobster is a new corner store takeout in deep South Philly.  While it offers several fish & seafood choices, its signature menu item is the Lobster Roll.  You can order this sandwich in the traditional Maine style (cold lobster chunks w/ mayonnaise) or in the newer Connecticut style (warm lobster chunks with melted butter.)  I opted for the traditional preparation and it was indeed very delicious....as good if not better than any lobster roll I've ever eaten in Philly.  Unfortunately lobster rolls are never cheap in comparison to their size and here they are priced at $15 each or two for $25.  One thing I would recommend to the owners is installing a couple of tables and chairs inside in case someone wants the convenience of eating his/her sandwich on the spot rather than taking it out.  It's def big enough to fit in a couple of tables.  The service at Neon Lobster is very friendly and there is limited street parking on Snyder Avenue and side streets.

Pretty solid place.  Braved the crazy out-the-door line for its 2nd day open; definitely worth it.  Best I can describe it is "Asian Chipotle" (they even have corn chips and "wasabi guac").  They have a few set menu options, but you can build your own salad/rice bowl/nori roll with various meats and toppings.  

They have a wide variety of meat options: salmon, shrimp tempura, breaded chicken, grilled pork, steak.  Toppings include tons of shredded veggies and interesting additions, particularly the "pickled mango," which was a delicious counterpoint to my steak with gochujang sauce...the steak.  Gotta give a special shout out to the steak.  Tender, actually PINK inside, no gristle (are you listening, Chipotle?  Might wanna ask for the recipe).  

I went with a rice bowl (not a huge fan of seaweed), and it was really good.  Minor complaint was rice almost too glutinous, but definitely didn't make the dish taste poorly.  I also had a side of miso eggplant soup (two options: pumpkin or eggplant), which was delicious.   

A great addition to the grab and go (they have no seating by the way) lunch options in Center City.  Will definitely be back.

I don't understand the rave about this place. The salmon sushi roll I had was terrible. They oversauced the roll with this extremely sweet, disgusting concoction. I guess the appeal is that it's cool to eat a burrito sized roll. Definitely not going here again.

This place is amazing, an example of what happens when diversity meets innovation and the results are spectacular.  I'm one of those who loves a good sushi and Hai Street offers up a gigantic one. You can customize you order from their plentiful options of yummy veggies or choose one that is already perfected from their menu. Overall is this a plus. My only draw back was the service. It wasn't inviting and when you tried to questions, the workers do not make an environment where you would feel safe to ask, especially Samantha. My final verdict is a good place for lunch with the co-workers.

This place is literally so good no review could do it justice! Just do yourself a favor and go check it out, treat yourself. Very fresh and flavorful . I love the spicy tuna burrito. Me and my sisters love it here we try to go on a sisters date every now and again and this is our spot.

I was craving burgers and was on a budget. The closest place to me is Burger King on Castor and they are having a 2 for 10 deal, which is a great. The only catch is that this place has a one star rating on Yelp. I gave in to my hunger and budget and went here anyways. 

So first off, my server Rashauna was excellent. She was soft spoken and polite. I also hear her take orders from the drive through and she was courteous with other customers as well. For 10 dollars got 2 whoppers, 2 fries and 2 drinks. I didn't opt for cheese but I can't imagine it'll be too expensive to add.

My burgers were terrific, Burger King promised their burgers to be made-to-order and they delivered. My beef patty was spanking hot and had a great crust to it. The veggies were crisp and fresh. Note that I came in 30 min before the dining room closed.

My fries however, were warm only and soggy. I came back to the counter and asked if I could get some fresh ones. Again, great service from Rashauna, she smiled and got me fresh fries immediately, no hassle. She even suggested I can come back later for my second batch of my 2 meals deal so they could be crunchy.

I never gave tips at a fast food before but I did tonight. I understand that service like this is not guaranteed every time, this visit however, was really great. Shout out to my server. 

Note to the manager though, please clean up the dining room, there's spilled drinks everywhere.

We'd been hesitant to try this place as it looks like you're average corner store. We woke up one weekend and were feeling like breakfast sandwiches so we called and ordered. So good! Much better and more reasonably priced than most of the breakfast places around here. We've ordered breakfast a few times since then and its been consistent. My husband recently tried their donut and is still raving about it.

So much hype/talk for nothing too special. Boyfriend and i decided to check this place out since everyone was talking about it and there was so many articles out about Hai Street opening! We went a few months after it opened so it wouldn't be overly crowded. We each got a sushi burrito and shared a lemonade. The sushi burrito was well made, but everything was expensive. It wasn't even that filling. I think i would've needed two sushi burritos if I depended on this place for dinner! I think there was too much rice in the burrito too, but I guess that's the whole point of a sushi burrito. I suggest going elsewhere if you pass this place.

If you are in to flavor and customization Wishbone delivers! White or dark meat chicken? Wings or tenders? You choose your favorites. I had the white meat tenders and found them to be delicious. For me the coating was not too thick, but I do wish it had more seasoning. The pretzel flavor is nice. They are not super crispy because of the reheating process, but I like the set-up and having the chicken prepared makes for a fast meal. 

The sauce selection is fantastic, it is sure to satisfy almost anyone. There are many to pick from, it was hard to choose! The mustard sauce has heat from wasabi and sweetness from honey. The buffalo blue sauce is also good with a lot of blue cheese flavor and mild heat. They make everything in house. The fries are really good and crispy, but mine were a little too salty. The ketchup they serve it with is also homemade, it is more savory than sweet but I thought it was a nice change. The quality of the ingredients and careful attention to flavor combinations really shines through the sauces. This really makes the meal five stars worthy. 

I also had the famed mac and cheese and it was amazing! There is a lot of flavor going on, and it is all cheesy, creamy, with crispy parts from the breaded top. They also have a pretty large selection of homemade desserts. The thai coconut tapioca pudding was a few steps up from the tapioca pudding I would have as a kid as far as flavor and quality goes and brings a sense of nostalgia. Not to mention they have a large selection of drinks, try a snap tea with your fried chicken and mac. 

I will definitely return to Wishbone, and you can even have it delivered right to your door with Uber Eats!

Hai Street was everything I wanted it to be! The quality of ingredients was outstanding and the freshness just blew me away. I got the Slammin Salmon Nori wrap and it will take a lot, I feel, for me to venture and try anything else because I love sushi-grade salmon so stinkin much. 

I would disagree with the people that complain about the high price. I think you get a lot of amazing fish (if that's what you choose to order) and a filling entree for under $10 and that, in a city, is a steal! I'd rather pay this price for the quality you receive. 

My only recommendation would be to add avocado as an option! That seems like a no-brainer to me!

This Jimmy Johns is the same as all the others, but I give it five stars on account of its being open super late. There's nothing like grabbing a great sandwich when it's late and you're feeling effervescent from a fun night out. And it's super convenient to most of Penn's campus, so that's a plus as well.

Oh I almost forgot about this place. I was in there confusing drive thru and finally got my ordered place , and I asked for lettuce and tomato on my sandwich . They charged me like 9 dollars for a 7 dollar sandwich with like 30 tomatoes on it. My fries were cold so I had to go inside . It was raining so that sucked. Went inside and the manager was frustrated and high strung with guest, so when I finally approached her and asked for fresh fries ,( I didn't know about the tomato sandwich yet), the manager resisted to honor my request mentioning she , [I] " just put those fries in that bag, they fresh" aggressively might I add. I told her I just want fresh fries...The manager threw a hot batch of fries in my bag and I left.  Hers what I got when I got home and it was cold
Fantastic service, super friendly guy. Pet friendly too (I called ahead to make sure) Crab cake sandwich, beef sliders, and truffle parm fries were awesome. We'll definitely be back!
Great Mediterranean place in Center City. The staff is friendly and quick and the place is very clean. Excellent chicken shawarma with tasty toppings. They have pitas and bowls...everything is great.

So, I placed my order online, and it stated that my order will be ready at 1:30 (a lil after lunch rush), but when I got there, my order wasn't ready yet. I don't even think I was next for them to do since I saw the cashier grab from the middle and asked the girl if she could do this one next. I take my meal back to my office (across the street) and then dug in. OMG, it was ice cold! Was the heat warmer on? My rice was hard and cold, my meat was cold, the beans were freezing, fajita veggies were, you guessed it...cold, and my lettuce was too (oh wait, that's supposed to be cold...lol!) I couldn't believe it. I rather walk an extra 2 blocks an head over to Walnut. Ugh. So angry!

*This is an update about 10 minute after writing the above - I just bit into BAD meat. I finished about half my meal and everything tasted fine (except cold), but then I bit into a piece that was so bad, I threw it up. I couldn't even swallow it. The taste was so foul. Did you guys mix old meat with new?!?!? Yuck!

Finally found a location that makes a good meal. Others put slob out usually i throw 1/2 away but not here. Dual drive ins get your order quickly and made to order. While it maybe a bit pricey i guess quality food costs more $$. It is close to Temple hospital and Roosevelt Boulevard so it's as best as easy off, easy on. Give them a try...

best invention ever! sushi burrito's are my new favorite food. even the regular size is perfect to have half for lunch and save the rest for dinner. it can be busy so don't go if your pressed for time during your lunch break but it is so worth it. friendly service and very willing to make changes if you need to trade out ingredients.

These chicken strips are like heaven on earth. I love the fact that they are all priced based on weight. The sauce choices are out of this world good. Donfire: holy crap, wheewww that's hot, so food but so hot. I made the mistake of ordering strips and donfire before going to Woodys for a night of dancing. Holy hell, heartburn. Omg. If you like hell spice, go with Donfire. If you like spice but also flavor (donfire has great flavor but it's hottt) go with chipotle lime mayo. My husband loves their beer selection, I can't drink beer because of the carbonation... but if I did, this is the place I would go.

Yes, it's overpriced, $2 just for cheese sauce, I get it. But this is a Philly classic and no trip to CBP or any Philly sports venue is complete without some crab fries, in my opinion. The line can get long, but it moves fast.

Horrible!! We came into this spot to get a bite because right next to it is the DMV, where we were waiting for road testing. The service here is horrible and runned by kids! The only good thing I can say about this place is , at least the bathroom was clean. Other then that,  go find another fast food  or anothe BK spot to eat at. This is the last resort.
I went there for lunch and had a great sandwich for lunch, but then I noticed the amazing beer selection. So I came back a few days later for dinner and had chicken tenders and a sampled a few brews.

I love the Naf. I live the Naf. I am the Naf.

This is a pretty good falafel/shawarma place if you're looking for something quick and painless. It's in the style of a Chipotle or Subway in that you build your own sandwich or bowl down a line while viewing it through a glass window. It's a good concept that works for the type of food served. I got a falafel sandwich with a variety of fixings. The pita is pretty big, and the employees are generous with servings. My only complaint about this location (it's the sole Naf Naf I've been to) is that it was pretty understaffed when I stopped in. But I doubt that's typical.

FILTHIEST men's room in the history of restaurants!! There is a bucket under the urinal to catch dripping urine instead of fixing the plumbing! Are you serious? Also a used bloody bandage left on sink! Are you serious? 120413 2:31pm

Dream come true!! I have longed for a fast food type service with good mediterranean cuisine. Naf Naf has made their mark. It was not like what I had in Dubia but it will do!!! This was a great find. This was my husbands first time trying mediterranean and Naf Naf helped me give him a taste of why I rave of about shawarmas, hummus, and falafels!!! We are hooked!!!!

Cool concept. Japanese/Tex-Mex fusion, Hai Street Kitchen & Co feeds the American obsession with the sandwich. Burrito-like nori wraps stuffed with the protein, vegetables, and condiment of your choice, they have the potential to satisfy multiple cravings in one bite.

I ordered a salmon wrap with carrots, cucumber, pickled onion, and pickled jicama, topped with ginger miso dressing. A flavor burst, it hit the spot!

With limited seating and standing room though, it is best to grab-and go!

Been here twice now, and both times have been great. Fresh, quick, and tasty. Wendy's 4 for 4s are my life, and they should be yours too! Pick and choose between so many amazing options, I highly recommend it! As for the restaurant, it's one of those fancy new and modern fast food places so there's a fire place and nice tables to sit at. There's even outdoor seating! Highly recommend if you want a cheap quick bite.

This Taco Bell rocks!
The staff are SO polite and friendly even when you go in the middle of the night. The staff is super courteous. The food is always quick and fresh and well. I've never had an issue with an order being incorrect.

Got to the drive thru around 5pm. It was not busy at all and there was only one person in front of me.  It took 5 minutes for me to finally get to the speaker to order. Then they said 'they will be right with me'.  Another ten minutes goes by and nothing. They said 'they will be with me soon'.  

I then gave up, put my vehicle in reverse and left and I will never be coming to this location ever again.

Food was low quality, staff was rude. Food is very overpriced $10-$15 if you choose one or two "customized" ingredients that should be included. Rice was not fully cooked. You will get better quality food from a food truck for $5 or take your $15 and get a decent meal at dozens of places within a 2 block radius.

I love sushi and burritos, and combining them was a fantastic idea! Way to go Hai street! 
I have to admit the idea of a sushi burrito sounds weird and unhealthy at first but they have lot of healthy options. You have the option to build your own roll or bowl or select from some of favorites they have. I got the slammin salmon special and it was super delicious. It came with pickled mango with some spicy sauce, lettuce, onion, and raw salmon. I substituted the spicy sauce for chimichurri sauce and the flavors went really well together. My friend got the mushroom special roll which came with grilled portobello mushroom, tomatillo salsa, spring mix, carrot, roasted beet, asparagus. That roll was super yummy as well. We ended up splitting the rolls in half and sharing each roll. I cant wait to come back and try the rest of the specials!!

THIS place...the line is a JOKE! For falafel and shawarma??? First of all, they set up around the corner from Mama's...selling falafel. I can ONLY assume that the people who are willing to wait in the line that wraps around the tiny dining room (and pay the price) at this place for falafel either have never tried Mama's OR they just don't have cash (which Mama requires). Every time I try to come here, the line fills the dining room! Which...wouldn't be a problem if it actually moves quickly...it doesn't. Which is ridiculous considering that based upon the location, I can only assume that the idea is to cater to the center city lunch crowd. Well...many people don't want to spend their full lunch time standing in line WAITING to order their food. I did read a review though that says you can order online to avoid the line. So...maybe I'll do that, or...maybe I'll just get cash and go to Mama's...

This is a nice fast-casual lunch spot in center city. The line gets long during lunch but it moves fast. The place seats about 25 people inside. There is some outdoor seating in a common area near the restaurant. The steak shawarma salad was very tasty. The portion was a good size too. The salad was prepared in front of me. I also got a few falafel balls on the side and found them to be pretty tasty as well. The shawarma meat was better than the falafel though. My co-worker got the chicken shawarma on pita, and loved it. This spot has become a top choice for my co-workers for center city lunch.
Awesome food me and my family went opening day and enjoyed ourselfs boss and managers is wonderful it will be my favorite place to eat at

This Taco Bell used to be excellent but they just fucked me in the ass. 

I made my standard order of good and tasty Mexican foods and decided I'd live mas and ordered a "mtn dew spiked frozen lemonade." I returned to work to enjoy my lunch in my truck under a highway over-pass when I realized they hadn't given me a straw. I finished my excellent tacos and threw my drink directly into the trash. I refuse to be cuckolded by this franchise.
An amazing introduction to sushi burritos! Every place Ive tried after this has not been half as good.

Yea, I'd like a full sushi roll...but I want to be able to eat it on the go.  Maybe you could wrap it up like a burrito?  Yea and while you're at it, pack it full of top notch ingredients.  Hai Street may not have originated the "sushi burrito" concept, however, they did bring it to Philly and introduce me to this easy yet awesome idea.  

I went with the Slammin Salmon on recommendation from Brad P and was not disappointed.  Between the fresh fish and the pickled mango, ever bite was full of delicious tastes.  I'm really glad I went Go Zilla (large) since it went down quickly.  Since they have a few prearranged menu items and a nice selection of "make-your-own", there is no doubts Hai Street will have plenty of chances to earn that fifth star from me!

I've wanted to try Taco Bell's breakfast menu since it was introduced but no locations in our area served it. Lo and behold I come across this new location on GrubHub serving breakfast so I gave them a shot. I order a breakfast crunchwrap, grande scrambler burrito, grilled breakfast burrito with potatoes, hashbrown patties, and Cinnabon cinnamon balls. The food arrived earlier than estimated and was absolutely delicious. My only complaints are that they did not grill my grilled breakfast burrito (but since it only cost a $1, I didn't bother complaining) and they did not provide any flatware (my friend ordered a breakfast bowl and needed a fork). Since they did not grill the one burrito, it was virtually indistinguishable from the scrambler for me save the addition of the potatoes in the wasn't-grilled offering so with a difference of $2+, the grilled burrito is a superior option. The hashbrowns were comparable to McDonald's but were larger in size (and I believe the prices are the same). The crunchwrap is the real MVP here: hashbrowns, eggs, bacon, and nacho cheese in a grilled tortilla. Fast, affordable, and delicious, highly recommend.

Apparently the computers are down and lots of product is missing but the store is still open for some reason. They are only taking cash. Employees are struggling to add prices with a calculator and they are writing some orders down and telling others to the food handlers. It took me 16 min to be waited on when there were only 3 people in front of me. I ordered a coffee (they were out of all lids) and waited 12 minutes for it while people who ordered after me got food and drinks before me. I finally asked about my order and received no apology but instead had my coffee slammed on the counter while the employee muttered that people should be able to see that they were having issues. I still don't see what that has to do with food orders going out before my one little coffee.  I hate that this is the closest McDonald's to me but I'll go out of my way to avoid this poor service
Fantastic food and friendly staff! Their Mac and cheese and nashville hot sandwich are both great!
I love these tiny burgers. The food is fresh. They just don't pay attention to customers request. Then they started cooking the burgers medium rare instead of asking for preference.
Seriously jimmy johns? Literally 1 slice of salami, cappicola is non existent and 1 slide of provolone? Service was quick and the bread was good. There you go, a star for each.

Best breakfast sandwich in fishtown. It is seriously prime hangover food. Also they will deliver groceries to you.The prices are so cheap you are stupid if you don't give this neighborhood place a shot.
