The only downside I found here is that it is a little overwhelming if you aren't very familiar with the cuisine.  I didn't quite feel rushed, but I didn't give myself enough time to really decide what I wanted as the lines were so long I didn't want to keep letting people ahead of me, and the descriptions aren't behind the servers on the line, that would have helped me a little bit.  Regardless, my salad here was down right awesome. You move down the queue line and add what you want to your choice of basis (bowl, salad, pita, etc).  Its similar in style to the other options out there (I'm looking at you chipolte) but the food is oh so different.  Everything was very fresh, and very flavorful.  The portions are huge and come with complimentary pita bread which is out of this world.  I got the chicken swarma salad bowl and added a bunch of toppings, I am embarrassed to say I ate it all, and was very full.  The flavors were different, bold and so tasty! My friend's falafel salad bowl was exactly the same, very filling, flavorful and different! This is definitely at the top of quick lunch places for me, and a great way to try something a little different than the norm!

We stumbled upon wishbone by accident. I normally don't take much time to write reviews.  This place a god-sent for the Southern foodies. The all white chicken tenders are juicy and flavorful. The mac and cheese is off the charts. The last time I had Mac and cheese like that was in Italy. 

They have healthy drinks, juices such as Orange-mango and watermelon cream.  

The service kind and be sure to ask for samples.  I will definitely make a trip back to this place.

I've been to Wingstop several times when they first opened up and was always satisfied and happy with the food. I went today and will not be returning to this location! I placed my order over the phone, the lady over the phone had an attitude! I asked for a side of beans with my order and she told me with an attitude they don't have beans (I haven't been here in a while apparently they discontinued that side). I said ok, then I just want the wings, not the combo, she told me then it will have to be 8 boneless wings since it's just an individual order, I said that was fine. I also ordered 3 piece Hawaiian strips combo. When my boyfriend got home with the order, my "boneless wings" almost looked like popcorn chicken! I asked for half lemon pepper half hickory bbq, the lemon pepper were dry and hard. The bbq  look like they threw the "wings" in the box and just poured the bbq sauce over top, they weren't even tossed!!! And it was suppose to be 8 wings and there was only 7, and this wouldn't be a big deal if the wings weren't so damn small! This is my first disappointment with this place and I won't entirely give up on Wingstop because I've had good experiences in the past, but I will not be returning to the cottman location and judging by the reviews and ratings here, they just fell off completely!

Finding out about Jimmy John's delivery was a HUGE game changer. Since learning about it two weeks ago, I've already ordered delivery 3 times. I'm always stunned by how quickly it comes (often in less than 10 minutes)!!

The subs are delicious, but the pickles are the main reason I keep coming back. I truly have yet to find anywhere with better and bigger pickles. They also sell buckets of them, which is wonderful but dangerous. They're so good I can't trust myself not to eat them all in one sitting!

The staff is exceptionally friendly. I've never had such great conversations with servers at other fast food joints!

Not to imply this is a one in a million fast food establishment that is unlike any other fast food establishments you have been to. I just think that this is a good spot to get fast food before you see a movie at Riverview. I'm always here chowing down on the BK Double Stacker. I've tried other sandwiches but they were pretty lame (fish sandwich and one of the steak sandwiches).

I've never been to Philadelphia and when I looked for places to eat this was one of the places that showed up. I LOVE sushi and the concept of a sushi burrito really caught my attention. I was really looking forward to try this... I arrived at the restaurant at 8:34pm, they closed at 9pm so I still have time to order my food and enjoy it. You could see in the employees faces that they were not happy that we went in there. I told them it was me and my
Boyfriends first time, they didn't even cared
About explaining how to order or what to get. As we started to order they just had a bad attitude and we really
Felt like we were not welcomed at all. I felt rushed during the whole process. One of the last step is to ADD YOUR CRUNCH... they skipped that whole step with my boyfriend's burrito and when he asked they were like "oh we already put that away and I closed your burrito, I can give it to you on the side" when he asked for it she just gave it to him with a bad attitude. When I was going to pay for our food she asked if I wanted a receipt and I said no, the girl walked always without saying anything not even a thank you for coming, or you're all set so I was standing there waiting and the other girl
Came up with a really bad attitude and told
Us "are you guys waiting for something else?" And we were like well I don't know cause she walked away... anyway my friend asked her if he could
Grab the chopstick for free and she rolled her eyes and said yes... after they were done with the customers they just walked off to the back and started using their cellphones... when we left they didn't even said good night or anything.

I give them two start for the bad customer service, for me that's more important than the food. I liked the burrito but the service was awful, they treated us like they were giving us the food for free, I paid the same money as a customer that maybe went there during the day. I wouldn't recommend this location maybe if you go to another one the service would be better and you might get a better experience but for me as a tourist I would not recommend this, those two girls really killed my experience.

I didn't want to let the secret get out about Buckminster's. The folks behind Buckminster's really hit it out of the park with this place. Came here on opening night with the Mrs. and a friend. 

We tried practically everything on the menu and all of the dishes were delicious.  I especially liked the Thai beef curry. Great vibe and friendly service.

I go to this McDonalds all the time. Although Ive never experienced bad customer service they are a horrible McDonalds. They ALWAYS forget something in your order or run out of food. If they weren't so close I would never go there again. I feel like they hire people who don't know what their doing. They need to be shut down.

Wings are small but aren't too bad, but it blows my mind that you can order three orders of 6-pieces (18 wings total) and literally only receive 2 tiny sticks of celery.  So three people are supposed to share two tiny 3.5" sticks of celery? Such a bad look. This is the norm here unfortunately, it just took until now for me to finally be fed up enough to post this.

In Philly on a work trip so I was looking for places to go get good takeout and this was the jam.  Best chicken sandwich (Nashville Hot) that I've had in a long time.   Will definitely come back next time I'm here!

Finally got around to stopping by at Wishbone, thanks to a strong craving for chicken tenders and fries. To be honest, part of the reason I had not tried it yet was because I didn't think it would be anything special. Boy, was I wrong!!

When you first walk in, it really doesn't look like anything special - I was actually a little disappointed. The chicken and sides are all prepare snd sitting on heating racks to stay warm, which didn't look too appetizing. Luckily, they make the fries fresh when you order them - that stopped me from walking out. They have 3 types of fried chicken - white meat, dark meat, and wings. All are priced per pound. I opted for the white meat boneless fried chicken. My hungry belly convinced me to order 3 tenders instead of just 2. For reference, each single tender is HUGE!

I was a bit surprised by how much I ended up paying. Thoughts while checking out: "$15 for 3 tenders, hand-cut fries, and ketchup?! They charge extra for ketchup?! Is it too late to walk out now?" Unfortunately, yes to all. But my worries were assuaged as soon as I began to eat. The hand-cut fries were just what I was looking for - not too thick but not too thin, a light crisp on the outside, and an overall rustic feel. My ketchup concerns were put to rest immediately - it's no ordinary ketchup! It has a blend of spices reminiscent of the curry ketchup at Frankford hall. While the chicken tenders don't look like much, I was so amazed when I took a bite!! The crunch from the pretzel crust on the outside contrasts with the moist, tender white meat on the inside, providing excellent texture with each bite. The quality of the meat must be commended - Wishbone delivers on is promise to serve only the best chicken.

Since I went for lunch, I did not get a chance to try out their beers, which they also pride themselves on. They've got an extensive draft list that does not appear overpriced.

Given the pricing, I most likely will not be visiting here often, but I'll definitely be back when I feel like treating myself to some quality fried chicken and hand-cut fries!

Like many of the other reviewers, I am beyond thrilled that Buckminster's opened up in Point Breeze. The neighborhood was in need of a restaurant and bar of this caliber.  The cocktails are simple and delicious, and very reasonable priced, as is the entire menu. Love the "neo-bistro" concept, which uses a lot of fresh seasonal ingredients in an unassuming way for some unique dishes.  They just started serving brunch and the Carolina rice congee with pork is seriously one of the best things I've ever had.

Very Good!
A very inventive way to eat sushi !
The place is simple, but atmospheric, and the food is very easy to customize. A tad bit on the pricey side, which is to be expected for sushi

I always feel ridiculous paying $10 for a lunch that won't fill me up. I'm disappointed that one of their vegetarian burritos has no protein, I think it would taste great with some tofu! I've tried it twice and I don't think I'm going to go back. The addition of beets in it feels off to me.
Inexpensive, creative and filling! This is a great place to pick up lunch if you want to eat outside. Service is very quick and helpful.

came here slightly intoxicated with some girlfriends and really enjoyed our fried chicken. it was fresh and the breading and flavors were great. i wish the sauces here weren't so expensive, i always need hot sauce with my chicken! the fries took forever to come out and weren't that good so definitely just stick with the fried chicken!

I ordered from here over the weekend, having had positive memories of the time or two I'd eaten there a year or two previous. This latest experience hurt that standing for me some. Admittedly, most of the negative aspect of this latest order was derived from the service/delivery side of things, but hey - they offer ordering from their official website, so that should be something they can handle competently. 

I ordered through their site and promptly received a text telling me to expect it delivered surprisingly quickly - within twenty minutes. That sounded unrealistic, and I was more than fine with the actual delivery taking longer than that. But time went by and we moved from the early promise to an increasingly late reality. I called and the employee I spoke to seemed baffled by the concept that I had ordered through their site and not a 3rd party service, as though ordering through the site weren't an option. I finally pulled up the email confirmation I'd received, told her the exact email address it came from and that I had a confirmation number to provide, and she suddenly gave me an "oh yeah, we got that, it's right here; I'm just waiting for a driver". Fast forward another 15 minutes with no new update. I called again and was told the driver had just left, and true to that, shortly after I got my order. 

By that time everything was lukewarm, and the macaroni and cheese had shriveled and deflated so much it looked insulting to be in its container (because of how little it now filled). My bacon-avocado chicken sandwich wasn't bad, but it would have been much better hot and at least somewhat approaching fresh. Everything else in the order - wings, biscuits, coleslaw, the seeded honey mustard - tasted fine, but again somewhat diminished. The exception would be the mac and cheese, which I think would have been disappointing even if it had been fresh. 

I know that most restaurants exist to be best experienced by eating in, and I have sympathy to how the demands of the recent explosion of delivery services and apps has stacked new challenges for many of them. But there was something fishily incompetent about the whole ordering process, and the food wasn't transcendent enough to overcome the negative effects of that. I'd try the place again if I was stopping in, but that's about it.

This was...pretty good! If you're expecting the same as Sushirrito in San Francisco then you're setting yourself up for disappointment because Sushirrito is life. However, as its own sushi burrito joint, its not bad at all. I thoroughly enjoyed my custom made roll that included 3 main ingredients haha. The salmon was surprisingly fresh...not that I was expecting not fresh salmon, but I was surprised at how fresh. There's not a lot of available seating but there weren't many people there when I went. There's even outlets on the walls by every seat, which is nice. The price isn't bad either, for a little over 10$ one roll lasted me 2 meals. These are the kind of places that I'm really happy to see succeed. It's food that's fast (I don't want to call it fast food though), and its not incredibly unhealthy. Yay for more healthier options! Will definitely be returning if I'm ever in the area again.

Is it sushi?  Is it a burrito?  Is it sushi?  Is it a burrito?  It's a sushirito!!!  Or a burrushi... whatever it is... its delicious!!!  I met a friend at Hai Street Kitchen for lunch yesterday.  She did the tuna one... I went Slammin Salmon... and it was so so so good.  The price point is affordable, the food is wrapped with care, and overall, it can't be THAT bad for you.  I happen to not be so much of a sweet and savory fan... so I wasn't crazy about the sauce on mine... but that was my own dumb fault.  I can't WAIT to go back and get another one with a different kind of sauce... maybe the spicy peanut sauce?  yum!

Wash it down with a hibiscus tea... day = made.

Everything was delicious, but the mac and cheese blew me away. A creamy four cheese affair with spicy chipotle to cut the richness.  If you get the half lb chicken/half lb m&c for lunch, it is entirely worth the nap you will need afterwards!

So there I was 7:40pm in my truck craving wings. I was just crossing the Tacony bridge back to jersey. Suddenly 10 mins later I found myself turning back around to head back to philly. Why? Because there was a wingstop there! They have some awesome wings if you never been.

They have different flavors to choose from on a whole scale between mild, hot, and then there is HELLA HOT.

Personally, if you are like myself and can't stand saucy wings and the mess involved with them, they do have some that are light on sauce and some that are dry rub based.
I am a sucker for their Garlic Parmesan wings as well as the Louisiana hot wings. DO NOT get their Cajun version confused with the Louisiana wings. Big difference. Some say the Cajun is better but I beg to differ on that.

The menu prices are so low that when I went for the first time my expectations were relatively low.

Oh boy was I wrong, the food was absolutely incredible, and beyond exceeded my expectations!

I would easily pay almost double the price for any of their food options.

Quality food, great service, a true 40-years-running-strong family restaurant. Would give 6 stars if I could!
I ordered through eat 24 and order was never confirmed. Tried calling myself and got no answer? :/

So I think the key is to get a made to order roll. I got the salmon roll and added wasabi guac with fried garlic and I loved it. It was about 11 bucks but def better than the signature ones. I recommend making your own!

Meh. Impatient service. Impersonal. Guy cleaning counter over food. Server touched rolls with her hands. Cashier handled money and then touched food. Chicken tenders: nothing special. Italian sausage: bland. Over priced. Try another place.

Pretty good food. No complaints just good. Not spectacular... good, solid food. For under $11 bucks, I was able to leave full. Plenty of fries, nicely topped sliders, nice people... combination for a return visit with friends. I had the California Burger and reg fries. I wasn't underwhelmed... just... whelmed. But the combination of good service, clean atmosphere and solid food warranted my 4 stars. It's hard to find good service with people who actually seem like they enjoy their job these days.

First time for me, I bought large wonton soup. I don't know how people enjoy the wonton with very thick skin and no fillings at all ? I'm ended up drink the broth and the fries stick which comes with it. This is the first and last time for me.

I prefer to eat Panda Express when I'm craving Chinese food. Although there are many Chinese restaurants near my work, they all seem to be hit or miss. Panda Express always tastes the same so there are no surprises. 

The restaurant is set up so that when you arrive you enter a line and order from a list of menu items presented behind glass. Depending on the size that you order, you can mix and match different entrees. The lines moves fairly quick with the exception of indecisive customers. For around $10 you can get 2 entrees, a side and a drink. (+fortune cookie)

Once you pay for your order, you have the option to dine in or take out. The place is kept clean for the most part.

They put very little meat whether it be lunch meat or tuna on their sandwiches and it's not worth the price they will be shutting down soon I'm sure and the food isn't even that good the only thing that's somewhat good is the roll and the stupid delivery guy act like he couldn't come an extra block I even tipped his ass pretty good.if you made better sandwiches and I wouldn't mind giving out a good tip each time oh well university needs to open up old Nelson's and close them down

If this place is not a front for a drug operation I'll be real surprised. If you go inside it's so depressing you'll need a xanax, the drive though always seems to have a long line even though the menu has not changed in 1000 years. 

The store attached too it has old products and there alway seems to be someone just standing around outside. 

I went there today and there were teenaged boys just standing in the street like that's what you do.

This is the worst McDonald's i have been too, i will go out of my way to go to the one on Broad and Hunting Park. 

And to top it off it has the highest gas prices around. Why would anyone go here? 

The only saving grace is malyika if she is working the drive though it seems to go smooth.
Craft fried chix. Sooooo good and the sauces are bosses! Mac and cheese is off the chez. Best late night snack. Impress a date here!
Friendly service, and good quick food. A great variety of beer. Good for a late night bite

The food is OK, but doesn't seem to be worth the price. Every time I've gotten the Mac and cheese it's been crusty and almost cold. Also, the chicken tastes decent at first, but without fail every time I buy from here, by the time I finish the second chicken tender I'm pretty much ready to stop eating, and the thought of another piece makes me feel sick. Not sure why.

I love Wishbone. The location and the hours are so convenient. Before or after the bar, whenever you're hungry, whether for a snack or something bigger, go here! I personally get the pieces of classic white. I normally prefer dark meat, but the white is so juicy and still salty, and the breading is very thick and flavorful, so I like the balance. I personally like the BBQ sauce the most and almost always get it. I don't know that I would recommend the other items here as I am just here for the fried chicken. 

I love that you can also drink a variety of beer for cheap very casually here.
Great fries. havent had burgers but some look verrryyy nasty... i had #2 chicken strips, and it was good...

Ordered a lot of food only thing we enjoyed was the Beijing beef (went back and paid for a second helping each good)

The cashew chicken was bland and slimy not sure if that's the normal texture but it was way to soft than the cashews where just raw tasting really weird they should have been crushed and cooked prior but weren't just thrown into the dish (again first time having this dish so nothing to compare it to just didn't care for it at all) 

I got white rice because the "fried rice" was not fried it was brown rice with vegetables in it. ‍ not fried rice at all 

The lo mein was reportedly dry and under seasoned (per my guest) 

The Beijing beef though wow 
Texture was great sauce and flavor was prefect had a slight after kick which I enjoyed much 
  
The total for 2 of us was roughly 30$ we tried the 
Cashew chicken bowl 
And a plate (2 entrees and side) 
Plus the 2 pints of Beijing beef (seconds ) 


Probably will skip this place when craving Chinese but would mind grabbing a pint of the Beijing beef if I'm walking through

Probably one of the better places for sushi burritos. I ordered the mushroom poke bowl and it was super delicious, even my boyfriend was impressed. If you're vegetarian or vegan, definitely try the fried mushroom burrito or bowl. 

The interior of the store was cute & bright. I liked how each seating area had it's own utensils and organic sriracha sauce (which I also recommend trying out). If you like Japanese/Mexican food, try this place out. It's kinda like an Asian chipotle.

Horrible customer service. The drive through attendant got on the mic laughing super loud before saying welcome to Wendys. When she finally did take our order she was extremely rude. In and out on the speaker because she was stopping to laugh and joke with co workers. Then we get the sandwich and its red inside...had to throw it out!
Provides great chicken and great service. Yelp lost my order but the manager was willing to help me.

Great food and very welcoming, vibrant and modern decor. Went for brunch. Loved everything! Griddle cakes with their jam, fried potatoes, the omelette, fried eggs over beans and the pear dessert were fantastic. 
And don't be intimidated by the menu, if you're unsure, just ask the server- but you can't go wrong with just about everything.

The food here is delicious. I had the chicken bites and the mac and cheese. Both were interesting, effective takes on what are normally pretty traditional dishes that people don't mess with too much. Also, Erica, the GM, is very nice. I recommend checking it out!

Good variety, however the hot food is really bland. Maybe it's to accommodate the palates of the diverse crowd that flows through RTM. But hot food that's available calls for more seasonings...
Price wise they hit the mark at $7.49/lb.. But again, value is pointless if the food is missing some ummpfh. When comes to food, quality and taste are key.
The area itself is well kept. So if you tongue doesn't mind the lack of flavor...go for it. I however will pass going forward.

We stopped here after finding nothing in center city to suit our completely reasonable desire for a tasty, quick, and reasonably priced meal. 

When we walked in, the environment is automatically welcoming, it feels like a snapshot of Philly. They have a great selection of beers, hard sodas, and unique soft drinks to choose from. 

The employee upon hearing that we had never eaten here, gave us a complete rundown of the options and ways to consume this delicious food. 

Before I could place my order, he heard what we had been considering, and anticipated our needs. 

The prices are not cheap, but neither is the experience. We paid 25 for 2 sandwiches, fries, a soda and a beer. 

I don't even like Philly, but I would come back to Wishbone.
Pretty good look and design! Taste good for salmon! Love the boxed water! But it is a little bit expensive.

Was going to order chicken and French fries especially because I was craving fries and the reviews and pictures look so good. However I was disappointed because fries aren't listed on any of their menus.

The staff here is so rude. I've only been here because it is the closest McDonalds and I get cravings. I've never met more miserable McDonalds staff. They don't even greet you or tell you to have a nice day. Makes me skeptical of what goes on in the kitchen. Plus, it should not be called fast food. People have waited over twenty minutes for their order.

Hai Street Kitchen has been open for awhile now, offering fresh sushi burrito options to the downtown business crowd. Perhaps it was the thousands of Korean kimbap rolls I ate during my childhood, but I opted to stay away at first.

Ultimately though, the GF kept begging for a bite. So before we went to the Rittenhouse Farmers Market one weekend, we finally stopped by. I was sad to see that the Mexican pork belly combo was no longer available, so we decided to split the Hai Street Chicken, Go Zilla sized of course.

With our sushi roll intact, we decided to lay out in Rittenhouse Square to enjoy our treat.

Hai Street Chicken [$10.86]
Gozilla size, chicken katsu, black pepper teriyaki sauce, romaine, pickled red onion, red cabbage, green papaya salad

A wide swath of nori housed crunchy, crisp, moist chicken katsu, along with fresh romaine, red cabbage, and green papaya. The black pepper teriyaki and pickled red onion provided some acidity, with the brown rice lending some substantive starch to each bite (you get a choice of brown or white). Fulfilling indeed - this definitely satiated our afternoon craving. Gozilla size gives you extra meat - so for an extra dollar or two, I'd go down that route for sure.

This is the worst fast food restaurant on the planet. The employees are rude, the food is poorly made, and they do not care about serving what you want.

The first time I went here, they were rude over the loudspeaker and impatient with my questions. I ordered about 8 items, and several of the items they told me that I couldn't have it because "it would take too long." In other words, if it's not already made, they don't want to get it out of the freezer.

When I finally ordered all the items they did have, I pulled forward and gave them my credit card. They told me to go park and they'd bring me my credit card. I told them no, I'd wait for my card since it only takes a second to swipe. The woman proceeded to argue with me and told me that I would mess up their timer if I didn't pull forward. I reasserted that I would not leave my card. She ran my card, which took less time than than it took her to argue with me. Then she told me to go park because my food wasn't ready. It took another 7 minutes (I timed it) before my food came out. (By the way, there was nobody in the drive-through behind me.)

As I drove away, I noticed two items missing, and two items I did not order. I went back to the store to swap them out for what I actually ordered. They told me that they were out of those two items, so they substituted....without telling me.

For some reason, I decided to go back today and order a grilled stuft burrito and a water. It took the lady about a minute to understand that I just wanted a cup of ice water and not a bottle, but she proceeded to charge me the price of a soda. So I told her I didn't want any water. She was very rude and short with me. When I got my burrito, it was neither grilled nor stuffed. It looked scrawny, the rice was hard, and it was barely warm.

I generally avoid fast food, but for some reason decided to try this place. Don't bother.

The taste: Great

The Size? Not so great. For a $10.78 the Go Zilla (the large one!) Chicken Katsu roll is probably about 10 bites. It's a really expensive lunch.

This restaurant is like an Asian fusion Chiptole. It's an interesting concept that mixes an Asian styled food into a Mexican styled package. Each burrito covering is sushi-seaweed with rice lining the interior, just like sushi. You can choose from a variety of meats and veggies to customize your roll or choose from the standard ones. But at Chiptole, you will leave full... here, you might need to buy two burritos. 

Also, there was a limited amount of seating inside in a bar type style along the walls. The interior looked nice, and the staff was pretty friendly. Because they opened yesterday, there was a line yesterday and today out the door. 

Verdict: try it once, and hope they increase the size of the burrito later. If it wasn't such an expensive lunch, I would probably eat here a couple of times a week.

Credit cards are accepted here.

Everytime I go to this location its an experience. First of all, its hard to order because of the bulletproof glass. Its not always a bad experience, but half the time you get a rude cashier. The last time I went there, there was a fight that went down over someone standing in the wrong place...yeah. 

I went there about a half an hour after they opened and the chicken was not very good.

Long story short, if you go here get taco bell and not kfc.

I, like many a foobooz reader and  self diagnosed "foodie" awaited this opening with anticipation, then decided against going on free sushirito day, tried and failed to go the next day (12:30- line was down the block, ain't nobody got time for that) and finally succeeded last week. And man. Was. It. Awesome.

Pro tips: 
-No line at 11:45. Yes line at 12:30.
-byo water bottle and save a few bucks on their weird carton water, you're not eating there anyway.

I was very happy (ecstatic and full) with my:

Tried that nasty chicken sandwich I took 3 bites the remainder was dumped into the trash need I say more

Food is good and their couscous bowl is delicious! I always get the bowl with falafel and it's super filling that you can save it for the next day

Terrible service, people who are working there never wash hands and their nail is inside the food all day. I found a hair in my food. So disgusting. on top of everything they have very rude and bad attitude.

My wife loves fried chicken. I love fried chicken. After her showing me some
very sexy slutty pictures of food from this chicken joint we ventured a journey
for ourselves to try. 
The reviews were glowing, as did the pictures. We could not

Man the Philly food truck scene is exploding. There's almost a new truck here every other week. M.A.T.T.'s is one of the newst on the block, and its a solid place for some sliders. Just passing by the truck, the paint job, menu, and the word "Gourmet" in its name gives it a sense of being on the higher end of things in price and, hopefully, quality. I'm typically not a fan of expensive food trucks cause I think it defeats the purpose, and I had no intention of trying this place out, until one day when I was really craving a burger. Having the option of just getting one of the original sliders ($3.50), and being next to Dos Hermanos, I was able to combine it with a couple delicious and cheap tacos next door. 

The slider itself was good, not anything particularly special, but good. As far as beef burgers go, it doesn't compare to Spot Burger. However, the next week, I saw on their Twitter feed they had a chicken sliders special (2 chicken burger sliders + fries for $7), which sounded moderately healthy and cheap enough to convince me to try it. I don't think I've ever had a chicken burger before, but these were amazing. The ground chicken (which sounds weird, but wasn't) was perfectly seasoned with spices and fresh herb (cliantro?) and topped with garlic aioli sauce, lettuce, and tomato. It was seared nicely and really juicy on the inside. Two sliders sounded like it wouldn't have been enough, but it was served with a generous portion of fries with sea salt and were fried really well. It probably sounds silly to say the fries are fried well, but its actually hard to find well-seasoned, not overfried fries around here. This is where Matt's has a leg up on Spot Burger. 

In summary, I was really pleasantly surprised by the chicken sliders and hope they have them as a special more often. For the original sliders, you can get 3 for $10, but you also get fries with it, so its actually not a bad deal at all.
The customer service is good, they listen to what you want. The only problem is that the food is cold sometimes, and they just throw the food together, so that they can move on to the next customer.

Their sliders are extremely small, but prepared with great ingredients and flavor. The sliders looked very well prepared, almost as if I was eating in a restaurant. If you're a big eater, however, one meal (3 sliders) won't be enough.

My main problem with this place is that it's extremely slow. Given it's a food truck on a college campus, I expect to get my food at least within 10 to 15 minutes. When I ate here, a few days after they'd first launched on Drexel, it took me nearly 10 minutes to even put in my order, because the guy was chatting with the person at the front of the line. I get that the people here are new and less experienced with the food truck business, and I appreciate their attention to details in their sliders, but it shouldn't take 20 to 30 minutes to get a quick meal.

Only giving this one star because I can't give it negative 10.   It's a Burger King - I had low expectations.  I ordered a whopper meal and stood at the counter for a full 6 minutes.   A woman came through the drive through and ordered a whopper without meat.  

They screwed up and gave her my whopper.   While standing and waiting at the counter, the customer walked in  and returned the whopper (mine) because it had meat.  They quickly made her a new sandwich.  

MEANWHILE... two employees opened the sandwich and peeled back the bun to check for meat, realized it was my order, and proceeded to put it on a tray and tried to serve it to me.  

I told the girl I wasn't going to eat it and she legit grabbed the tray out of my hand and threw it on the floor and yelled "this guy won't eat that one so will someone PLEASE accommodate him?" with such a snotty attitude.  

Again, low expectations cause fast food, but it was still ten bucks!!

One of the standard, Mexican "fast food" places in University City. Most people say that it's not as good as Chipotle, but I find the two to be pretty similar in taste and price. I absolutely love the quesadillas here, which I don't think other similar Mexican places have. Definitely worth going to if you want a quick, Mexican meal!

We went here with friends from out of town who have never been to Naf Naf before. The staff were exTREMELY unfriendly and barely spoke to us. It seemed like we were causing them a disservice by ordering our food. The staff was also incredible stingy when it came to the toppings they gave us. If we asked for cabbage, they would put a couple little things of cabbage ontop. 

That being said, the food was very good and was your typical Naf Naf experience which is why I gave it a 2 star.

Super busy during lunch time, long line...yet not long waiting hours. The service is fast and efficient.
Coming to food, as I'm a sea food person, I loved the shrimp entree, and shrimp appetizer. It's sad they have only one option for sea food in entree, honey walnut shrimps and fried shrimp in appetizer, but it was delicious. The only issue I had with honey walnut shrimp was that it was way too sweet, but maybe the recipe is that way. I got noodles as a side, but I regretted it. The noodles are dry and hard to chew and extremely oily. The fried rice were good and the next time I go, I would always order rice as a side instead. 
The ambience is okay, crowded, well, that is something expected in center city. I would recommend this place if.you want to grab some affordable good food on a busy work day!

THE FRIES are THE BEST!!!!! 
Parmesan wings are so SALTY. BUT the fries make up for it. I can see myself taking a trip just for the fries.
Excellent food!! Great service!! The line was super long and they were packed but they went through everyone's order like no tomorrow!!

I went with a customized sushi burrito and got brown rice, salmon, chimichurri sauce, carrots, cucumber and onions. I didnt want to overload on toppings because I wanted to taste the salmon. I also got a cold hibiscus tea. I forgot to ask if it was sweetened so I was slightly surprised. I liked it because it doesn't taste watered down but would definitely prefer it sweetened. 

The sushi burrito was really good especially the salmon. I highly recommend the salmon. I do think the portion and the price don't really match up but I do remind myself that sushi isn't usually cheap so I guess it balances out. But the fact that I wasn't full after this meal even with the drink deducts a point for me. Also the chimichurri sauce was really oily. It was more oil than herbs so it coated the outside of the sushi burrito and I ended up with really oily fingers so ask for extra napkins if you're getting the chimichurri sauce !

Sushi? Check. Burrito? Check. SUSHI BURRITO? Holy crap, marry me!

Like others stated, it's seriously innovative and the fact that I can have sushi on the go, wrapped up makes my day so much better. 

Hai Street Kitchen, you have my heart.

Outstanding Restaurant.   The workers are very friendly. Today,  I was greeted by one of friendly  chefs  named Sophie. Its an upscale fried chicken restaurant  with the Best Wings in the City. They have Tasty Salads,   Delicious Biscuits and a fine dessert selection  with good Coffee.  The Food is prepared fresh everyday by the  Culinary chefs.  Also, They have a unique fountain soda selection.

This is seriously innovative! First of all, who doesn't love sushi?  The amount of sushi restaurants in philadelphia are countless.  So to turn sushi into a fast food type of thing is genius, really.  This is basically like a chipotle.  They have a number of things on the menu, but you can pretty much choose what you want in it.  Make your own sushi roll is what it really is.  Their sides are pretty good too, I tried the tempura corn.

There are bar tables against the window and the wall inside for you to dine in.  The inside looks very clean and contemporary.

It's clean. Service is fairly quick. 
Only problem is lines get LONG here. 

I'm just happy they got rid of that nasty Grundy Chodey McDonalds that used to be here. It was a Homeless shelter!  Bums would come in and stink up they place. Beg for your money or food. It was sickening. 

This Panda Express is doing well. They have a security guard to combat the homeless.

Ordered the chicken shawarma bowl with rice, tomato cucumber salad, covered in the garlic mayo sauce plus a side of their naf fries. Everything was delicious and very filling, I barely finished the fries! And the pita that came with the meal was soft and fluffy, giving it a homemade feeling. Will definitely be back again in the near future.

To recap my experience with the Rhawn St Philadelphia Checkers location, I'm choosing to recount my visit(s) in a way that's a bit long winded.

I've always enjoyed the food. The fries that Checkers has are, in my opinion, out of this world. Loading it up with cheese, ranch, and bacon? Pure genius. This isn't a knock on the product at all, even if I found the decision to stop serving chicken strips nothing short of mystifying.

As much as I've always enjoyed the food, however, the service is absolutely atrocious. 

I almost always order the same thing when I choose to eat your restaurant's food. Chicken fingers (now nuggets), loaded fries (as described above), a large soda, and buffalo sauce. As God as my witness, even though my order is exactly the same, I've NEVER been charged the same price twice. The median cost of my meal is usually somewhere around $7.50. Sometimes, it's a little more, sometimes a little less, but it's never the same. To be fair, it's usually at least close, but never the same. I always thought this was more comical than anything.

The drive-thru is BRUTAL. The wait is completely unacceptable and it has been for YEARS. It's very common, during high traffic times, to potentially wait over 20 minutes to order and receive your food. It's food retail, I understand that occasionally call-outs can happen, or an unexpected rush of business can catch a staff flat-footed. This happens ROUTINELY at the Rhawn Street Checkers however.

Given that this has been a problem for several years, I have to assume that the location is staffed properly and NOT operating short-handed. Combine the issue the location already has in charging me correctly and it leads me to only one logical conclusion:

The existing staff is terribly trained and can't keep up with customer demand.

For me, this all came to a head last night. I bartend, and after finishing work I decided I could really go for my usual "grease pile" instead of going to my local WaWa for a sandwich. I saw the line of cars and sighed a little to myself knowing the the wait was going to be a lengthy one. I have a go at it anyway, and after about 5 minutes I'm able to give my order (again ... Different price)

When I pull up to the window after waiting the usual 20-25 minutes, I noticed my bag was unusually light. No loaded fries. The gentleman at the window admitted he made a mistake. I'm now assuming "mistakes" are a big part of the reason I wait in line so long. He the hands me back what was a half-empty box of the saddest looking fries I've ever seen. Seeing as that he's already screwed up, I would have thought the LEAST he could do was stack the box a bit. 

I notice now that they also didn't include the buffalo sauce I asked for either. It sounds a little silly to say the sauce and the fries are a big reason for my patronage, but it is. Given that I've already been in line for over a half hour, for a half-assed box of fries, hearing that they don't have what I consider to be part of my order, sends me into the red.

I'm tired, I'm hungry, and I've waited FOREVER to be told news that I COULD have been informed of when I put my order in ... A half hour prior.

I'm mad, and I complain only to be met with shrugs and 'move along' dismissive comments. I expected someone to apologize and offer to comp my food. Instead I felt like I was completely blown off by someone that's supposed to be managing a business. NOW I'm furious and really lay into the staff.

After receiving a refund (another whole process since the window attendant didn't know how to issue one) and giving back my food, I'm finally able to drive off. Still hungry and mad as hell over the just short of 45 minutes I wasted.

Granted, again, I was really upset. I probably was over-reacting and took out years of frustration over issues that all seemed to converge. However, that doesn't mean that any of the problems I was angry about aren't very real and completely valid. 

You have a serious customer service issue that I now believe is stemming from a poorly trained.

As it stands now, however, I don't think they'll be seeing my business again

UPDATE: The company did reach out to try and fix things

ANOTHER UPDATE: I received calls from the district manager and the NEW general manager of the location. Both encouraged me to give the restaurant another chance. To their credit, I'm been there 3 times (on the company) and NEVER had an experience even close to my previous visits.

Against all odds, maybe things are legitimately moving in the right direction?

Oh my gosh!!! I  Popeye's chicken and this establishment is the closest to my house. I feel like I'm a glutton for punishment because my order is always wrong. My order is the same always. Two of the specials, 11 pieces for $9.99, mild with no breasts and 2 large fries.  I'm convinced that the workers don't know chicken parts!! Maybe management doesn't teach the parts of the chicken to employees!  They definitely should!!! Order #22 at 4:21pm on 2/1/19.
The chicken is good. But the jalepeno bread - kill for it. It's amazing. Get it, get it, GET IT!

Hahahaah..the reviews at my local BK are hilarious!! I wanna add another one.Yes. Lots of teenagers running this business. Kudos to them! BK managers do not care because people will still purchase their burgers on the rush. It is convenient. I go with Whopper Jr..which shrunk. Helps with my diet...so no problem and I get my 4 piece tenders. Oh and Im terrible using the new machine for getting water. Restroom when Im using this place to u know....and then off to go vacuum the car next door at the gas station. Convenience. Yipeeeeee! No working Wifi.   ;( If they had Internet this would be my hangout because it is close to all the highways entrances. Whoosh! Take a drive.
Great wings! Lemon Pepper is my favorite or the mango habanero if Im in the mood for something with a lil kick.

I have been to two locations for wishbone. One is in West Philly and one is in Center City. I think the center city location is better. 

Wishbone mainly sells chicken tenders and they are pretty good. The breading is quite crunchy while the chicken itself remains moist. You can choose between light and dark chicken. 

What I like a lot about this location is the craft beers. There are a lot to choose from and they go well with the chicken tenders. They also have more obscure and specialty sodas.

My one qualm is that with expensive chicken tenders, they also charge for sauces. I think that if you spend above $5 for chicken, you probably should get a free sauce. The sauces are good, but can they really cost that much to make? I also wish that the sauce containers had wider mouths so that it was easier to dip the large tender into.

New, clean, and very friendly staff. 

It's the same chain Panda Express that I hate that I love, and so far this location is pretty nice. However, they were out of a lot of their dishes on a Wednesday at 1:30 pm, which isn't cool. The chow mein was almost gone and I didn't want to get stuck with the last bits, no cream cheese rangoon, no shrimp, and a few other items were out or almost as well.

I stopped here on the last leg of my last Rittenhouse shopping trip as I realized I hadn't eaten all day. At first I thought maybe there'd be a lot of filler (rice) and little good stuff (salmon), when I saw the friendly guy prepping my sushi burrito, I was quickly proven wrong. He assured me it wouldn't fall apart, further assuaging my sushi burrito fears. He rolled it up nice and tight and put it in a little cardboard tube, which I promptly popped into my bag and was on my way.

I opened up my tube of yum right when I got home and the flavor was outstanding. I loved the pickled veggies and the slightly tangy and spicy sauce. It did get a little messy at the end of each burrito half, but no one was around to judge my drippy fingers. Similar to regular sushi, I quickly got full and took a little rest before finishing off the second half when I got hungry again 20 minutes later. Why does that always happen? Someone ought to research that!

All in all, I really liked it. If this were closer to my apartment, I could see it becoming a problem!
Food was not seasoned. Chicken was bland and Luke warm. I paid $9 for 6 drumsticks and it was not worth it. I see why the employees push the sauces, you need them for any type of enjoyment.

Is their a - rating for this place worst place to eat.. waited for my food for about half hour it's ridiculous. Soda didn't taste right at all.  I'm not around this area but this not how you run a fast food restaurant. Worst experience ever...

It's the cheapest place to eat in the Reading Terminal. I usually get the Kale. The meatballs are nice. A bit salty though. 

The Employees are nice. It's clean.

Only thing is sometimes the flies come out and circle the food....but this can be said for any of the stores in the Terminal.

As far as fast casual goes (restaurants in the Chipotle, Shake Shack price point and quality), this place is great! 

The chicken shawarma pita was delicious and filling, and not too expensive. I will also say that this was some THE BEST falafel I've ever had. Yeah, that's right!

The best pita ever was how I remember Naf Naf Grill when I first had it in Chicago. Unfortunately, I don't think I can say that anymore. I stopped bowl for lunch and grabbed a steak hummus bowl that comes with a pita. The steak was pretty dry, but bearable to eat once mixed with the hummus. I was super excited for that fluffy pita I had remembered, but this time, it was flat and doughy. So much disappointment.

The new owner and his buddy are fantastic. They made a very college town corner feel like a neighborhood.  Just real good people. I get that their sandwiches are simple, and still I loved their veggie sandwich. When I want no fuss food I'm going to come here. I wish them all the success in this new endeavor of theirs!
Rude employees, extremely slow service. Do not recommend to go there unless you starving

I would like to know why ? Just why? Okay so here's my horror story. Sometimes I crave for a burger so I have to get this one particular one from Mcdonalds. The one near me is so bad it's Broad and Onely #2. The people are rude and have poor work ethic and have poor appearance. The establishment looks shakey. Like you keep second guessing everything in there ... any way I was despaerate and was gonna press my luck and the line is always long and slow. It take 30 minutes at they drive thru. One time, I forgot what I order so was in line so long. You will burn a quarter of gas in this drive thru. I feel like they owe me when I grab my mystery food because o forgot what I ordered for sure. Any way it's just all bad here.. forget the main story. The question is why? Can we please have professionalism? A MAKE OVER IT ALSO STINK ON THERE SOMETIME

Apparently the computers are down and lots of product is missing but the store is still open for some reason. They are only taking cash. Employees are struggling to add prices with a calculator and they are writing some orders down and telling others to the food handlers. It took me 16 min to be waited on when there were only 3 people in front of me. I ordered a coffee (they were out of all lids) and waited 12 minutes for it while people who ordered after me got food and drinks before me. I finally asked about my order and received no apology but instead had my coffee slammed on the counter while the employee muttered that people should be able to see that they were having issues. I still don't see what that has to do with food orders going out before my one little coffee.  I hate that this is the closest McDonald's to me but I'll go out of my way to avoid this poor service 
Update: I should have stayed away. On my next trip I ordered a meal with an orange juice and was told they didn't have any because the water has been shut off. She offered me something else instead and stated that I could get a coffee or frappe. I requested a frappe I also asked if it was possible to substitute for me on my McMuffin for an extra eggs. She said yes. When I got to the register she charge me for the egg (why tell me I could substitute it then) and for the frappe (not my fault you were out of OJ-it should be complimentary in that case). There was some nasty brown water all over the floor where food was kept that two employees were trying to clean. Never again.

It's a bit expensive for a fast food sushi burrito, but it does taste yummy.
Surprised that I hadn't been to hai street yet.  Both the screaming tuna and slammin salmon were great. Fresh fish. Great ingredients. I like the bit of spicy kick.
I got the giant rolls and they were a be hard to eat because they were too big and not rolled right enough.
Can be a messy burrito experience, but worth it and very filling.

I've become a regular here.  It really does feel like a neighborhood place.  The guys who work here are super friendly and remember my usual order.

While they are friendly and talkative, they are just a little slow.  I think it's because they are doing such a good job & taking so much care with the food, but if I'm in a hurry I just make my order and come back to pick it up, or even call it in ahead.

Their bagels are good & I've enjoyed the Fresco veggie panini and tuna hoagie.  The quality of their food seems really fresh and good - i know they make a lot of stuff from scratch, including their soups that I keep meaning to try.

Delicious chicken! A staple of Center City. Every time I come to town I have to make this place a part of my trip. Just around the corner from all the bars in Philly my friends and I always feel welcome and enjoy the quick pit stop in a fun night out. The manager is a jewel. Be sure to ask for Chevy because her heart and smile when you walk in are just as welcoming as the mouth watering food. P.S. definitely try the cheesy ranch dipping sauce.
They have lots of options in comparison to Chipotle  and it's honestly super delicious. Price wise it's pretty good too. Would recommend coming here alone for a burrito bowl.
Ordered take-out before the night rush. The chicken was absolutely amazing, and so was the mac and cheese, and the staff were super nice.

The food is tasty and definitely fresh, but it seems like they're nickle and diming you. You don't get a ton of food anyway, and they're very careful to weigh the meat and give you measured out portions of everything else. It's not particularly cheap (more than Chipotle for example) and doesn't leave you full.

The lines are always crazy long during lunch but for good reason! And don't worry they move fast. The falafel hummus bowl is my favorite and usually lasts me for two meals as I get all the veggies on top. There's a bunch of varying sauces to put on top which are great and vary in spice level. I pile them all on!!

We ordered two crunch wrap supremes and some Doritos Locos tacos. When we got home I commented that everything looked "thin". So we unwrapped the crunch wraps and there was no meat! One had mostly tomatoes and the other was just over loaded with sour cream and cheese. The tacos all had a very very sparse amount of the correct ingredients so that when the taco was closed both sides touched each other! Worst food. Get it together, it's really not that difficult!

Ordered the Wisherbone sandwich. The chicken was a tiny piece of fried nugget that was about 5 bites on a huge big bun. The sandwich would have been great had the chicken actually been a full fillet that covered the bread. So disappointing. 

The red potato salad is quite sweet. I didn't see relish in it. It's a dill potato salad so not sure where the sweetness is coming from unless it's made with miracle whip or sugar is added. $3.75 for a small cup. 

Corn bread is on the small side for $2.75. I'd expect a full square for that price. Overall, not impressed with the food or portions of this fast food type place.
this is actuallly what i received after ordering oatmeal on ubereats from this mcdonalds. who does this? i also ordered a vanilla shake and they gave me a cook. so pissed off this place sucks

Looks like someone in Philly finally caught onto the sushirrito trend! 

I was happy to see that Hai Street was pretty cheap, but that's only because the portion is pretty small. You can build your own sushirrito or choose from their signature items. I got the sumo steak, and it was pretty good, but I prefer real Japanese ingredients (and why do they put asparagus in everything? ick)... We also tried the $2 hibiscus tea, which tasted like barely-flavored water. Thanks for that.

Definitely wish there were more seating here. There are only a few high top seats facing the window, and everyone else goes back to work or eats outside. Would be a pain come wintertime.

Once the novelty wears off, hopefully Hai Street will give us a little more value for what we're paying!

It was late in the evening, around midnight or so. I had been working hard, representing Yelp at an event at the Rotunda, and once again forgot to eat. Seeing as how it was past my bedtime, I was just going to wait till I got home and then scarf down a bowl of cereal, but my tummy wasn't on board with that decision. Luckily, I saw the welcoming beacon of Jimmy John's, and eagerly went inside to place my order.

I'm a traditionalist when it comes to my sammies, so I went with my standard ham & cheese with lettuce, tomato, vinegar and mayo. It's pretty hard to mess this combo up, which is probably one of the reasons I love it so. I ordered it up with the friendly counterpeople and moved to the side to wait for it. During this time, another customer walked up and asked what the alfalfa sprouts were. The staff tried to explain it to her, but in my sleepy state, I decided to take it upon myself to give her the scoop. "Sprouts look like hair," I told her. "And they taste like grass." Have you ever said something you didn't mean to say and at the same time, see the words coming out of your mouth, unable to grab them back? That's exactly what this was like. Everyone in a five foot radius stared at me. Amazingly, that was also the exact moment my sandwich was ready, so I took it and slunk out of the shop.

Driving home, still pink-cheeked from my sprouts lesson, I ate the hell out of one half of the sandwich. The bread was kinda stale and the taste was very meh. By this time, though, I could barely hold my eyes open and my hunger had almost passed. Not the best culinary experience, but I did embarrass myself in public again, and as we all know, that's priceless.

Disappointed. I have had Hai Street Kitchen before from this location, however today I found it inedible. I had a tuna poke bowl and the tuna not only looked very gray but it also tasted like it was not fresh. I gave it two tries before I tossed it in the trash. I will have to think twice before having it again.

This review is for the men's room only.

First off the bathrooms have a key pad to get into and the five digit code the counter person gave me was so overly complicated to remember I had to say it over and over in my head as I crossed the dinning area. (Side note when I left the bathroom there was someone at the other door trying to type in the code unsuccessfully.  So it wasn't just me.)
Then inside the spacious bathroom, I gave the toilet the customary pre-flush, and water spouted out the back of the bowl from the intake pipe.  It was clean water, but still there was a small puddle forming on the floor behind the toilet. (After doing by business I flushed again and more water came out)
I did my business and went to wash my hands and water was spraying out the side of the faucet.  Seriously this place needs to get a plumber in there or the whole place is going to be flooded.
Other then that the bathrooms were clean and well stocked and the baby changing table seemed well taking care of.

Really?  Isn't a croissandwich egg meat and cheese on a croissant?  So if I order a bacon croissandwich no cheese shouldn't I expect Egg and bacon?  Instead I got a cold croissant with maybe 3 thirds of a strip of bacon broken in pieces.  Do I have to open everything I get before I leave the drive thru?  So frustrating
  Always far away by the time I open my food to find its not what I ordered.  The young ladies at the drive thru are very nice and friendly but that doesn't help me now.

WOULD NOT RECOMMEND
This place is okay to go if you want a light lunch.
I feel that the choices for toppings  are limited but the option to get the sushi-burrito deep fried was good. 
Food wise I would have given the place a higher rating but the customer service was pretty disappointing. Both times I've gone there they have messed up my order, the second time I was with friends who were out of state and wanted to try out sushi-burrito for the first time, and they too experienced negative customer service. The employee helping us even made false accusations to the whole kitchen about us when she messed up our order and that was the last straw for me. The food is good but not good enough for me to deal with the service.

I recently visited the 19th & Market Street location. It was lunch rush hour but the line moved fast.  The food was great! I had chicken kebab and rice with hummus and pita. I will definitely be back.  Only thing negative I have to say is one of the servers was less than enthusiastic about working that day. I will excuse her because she was pregnant and I know the feeling.

Got takeout tonight for the first time. Long line but moved fairly quickly/m. Ordered two rolls - one of the premade options and one of the create your owns. Both were very delicious and filling! I could only finish half of mine. We also got the chips and wasabi guacamole which were very good as well! 

Def go there if you're hungry. Huge portions. Can't wait to try it again!

Great fast food option. If I lived/worked closer I would be here on a weekly basis. Fast service, even when there's a line out the door you won't wait more than 10 minutes. The salmon is my favorite. I add a little soy sauce to mine when I get home.

OH GOD WHERE DO I STARTTTTTTTT?!

My two favorite things, sushi and burritos, molded into one heavenly culinary creation. 
I tried the slammin salmon, and it was tasttttttttty. It was like one big sushi roll for a 650 pound quarterback. They have different meat options that you can put in a rice bowl, a salad bowl or a nori wrap: chicken, steak, salmon, pork, shrimp and Portobello. I wanted something that resembled something close to sushi, I opted for the salmon and didn't look back. They have signature wraps and build your own; this restaurant is a hidden gem nestled in center city. 
The only qualm: limited seating and no soft drinks. I had to buy boxed water- steep.

Probably the worst McDonald's in Philadelphia.  Slow service, COLD FOOD and ignorant employees. If your fries are hot you're in luck. If you get an extra burger or fries in your bag (from the ignorant employees) you're even luckier. More than three times I've drove off GLADLY with extra goodies. Not that its a bad thing on my part but they clearly don't pay attention. I'd hate to be the one who has to wait for food because they passed it off.

I had the pierogi platter. First of all the food was cold. The pierogis were way over seasoned. They forgot the sour cream even though they said it was in the bag. Sigh. Had high hopes but really awful. The salad was okay though. Wouldn't return.

stopped in today for a big bufford and a shake, they used to be a value added chain now they are as expensive as arby's or fudruckers, they totally screwed up the burger order and could only eat 1/2 of it because the mayo & bbq sauce were fighting eachother so much it just tasted horrid, thank god I got a milkshake to make sure no heartburn set in, called into corporate and let them know, I doubt i'll stop here again

I like coming during my lunch break. I go back & forth between online ordering and waiting in line.  I order the same thing every time, however the size of my bowl varies by a lot depending on who's working. Y'all need to be more consistent with those scoops. Then y'all keep putting Delani on register. He always has an attitude. Always.

Went for dinner tonight with a friend and used a Groupon. I had the chicken skewers and my friend had the surf and turf. Both meals were very good. The food was fresh with great potato wedges and asparagus. The server/ bartender was extremely nice. I'm going back for their small plates which are reduced for happy hour. Give them a try!

Skip this place! The only reason why there's always a line is because they are so slow to serve! We waited an hour in line thinking this place must be good because of the number of people waiting and the somewhat positive reviews on Yelp (although few). Big mistake. The food here is just edible. I don't think I would ever come back.

After waiting an hour and another 15-20 mins for the mac & cheese to finish cooking, we sat down and expected to enjoy some good BBQ wings. Nope. We bit into some DRY, BURNT wings and felt sooo ripped off of not just money, but precious time that we will never get back. *sigh* 

- BBQ Wings: dry, burnt, no flavor inside
- Mac & Cheese: undercooked and nothing special
- Sting Beans: steamed and a little salt sprinkled, meh
- Pierogies: they boast it like it's their specialty but it's just fried dough. bland and I don't see what's so good about them?

Me and my family came here really hungry, the outside door happened to be locked so we tried to get in, but one of the workers said "only drive through we are short staff" When we clearly see costumers in the store. We didn't have a car for drive through, so we called my Aunt to come pick us up to order drive through. When we was making our order during the drive through the worker was already being rude to us, but we didn't mind. We went to our window my Aunt gave them the money for our order and we only got our Drinks nothing else, not even the receipt. The worker asked us to move up so we did but we never got our food, even the car behind us got their food. My sister came into the store questioning the workers about our order but everyone was ignoring her and being very negative. They did not want to help us but just laugh because we looked stupid. Took over an hour to get our order, and when we got home. My personal order, order number 11 was not in the bag. The completely forgot my order and now I'm hungry and get upset. These workers are very inefficient and very rude, I highly recommend this place to get rid of these workers and actually hire someone who can give respect to costumers. My whole family is very upset thank you very much.

The only reason I'm giving this 1 star cause I live so close but this place is horrible everyone is rude never get what you order if you do you should play the lottery better chance of winning the mega million

I am obsessed with this place.  Discovered it right before I moved from Philly to NY and now my soul craves it all the time. 
 
The sushi burrito hybrid solves the problems that the components face as individuals.
Sushi:  Yummy, fresh and healthful ingredients, but leaves you feeling like you didn't quite eat a meal, and often expensive.
Burritos:  Yummy, good bang for you buck, but your stomach will probably hate you later.
Sushi burrito: Yummy^2, lots of fresh vegetables (and fish, if you're into that), satisfying but not too heavy.  Rejoice!

Also, the sauces are all delicious!  My favorite is the gochujang.

One final thought:  some other vegetarian/vegan reviewers have complained about the switch from portabello mushroom to grilled zucchini as a base.  As a vegetarian who isn't the fondest of mushrooms, I'm actually very happy about this!  I'll restrain myself from going into it here, but it drives me crazy that portabella mushrooms are the go-to vegetarian alternative at every restaurant.  "Hmm.. they're brown and round.  That definitely makes them burgers, right?"

YUM! Originally I was going to order through UberEats from the University City location, but I figured since I already work downtown that I'd give their Center City location a try. I immediately saw that the wings looked extra crispy, so I decided I'd give them a try. 

They price them by the pound (about $8/lb), so mine came out to a little over $5 for 5 wings, which I didn't think was that bad for Center City eating. I got the fries for $2.99 and I thought they were substantial for the price. Not to mention they were the crispiest hand-cut fries I've tasted. These kind of fries can either be too chewy or taste burnt, but these particular ones were just right. The wings were great and stayed crispy when I had my leftovers later. Surprisingly the fries kept their crisp as well.

I will be back. It was about $10 for everything I had (no drink), so I will know next time to bring extra cash for something to quench my thirst.

I used to come here a lot and get the hummus bowls, which I loved. Sadly the last two I've gotten on two different days have been disgraceful. I ordered one for myself and one for a friend, and my friend remarked that it looked like I'd given her my half eaten bowl because the bowl looked like someone had literally scraped the hummus off the sides of the bowls. There was a little stuck to the sides which did appear as though someone had used a spoon to remove the hummus rather than put it in.

I was very upset when I noticed my bowl was the same way. It felt like we were paying for a bowl with hardly anything in it. I don't know if the person did this on purpose or if was an oversight, but I was truly disgusted. This needs to be corrected asap as I am a Naf Naf Rewards member and have eaten so many lunches here, but I can't see how they can justify serving someone this bowl let alone eating it.

Try to stop here every once in a while because I like the boneless wings and they're open late.  This location is super slow, and almost never have a majority of the menu.  I could understand running out of something occasionally, but we're talking more than 50% of the time they're telling me they have the three most basic burgers but are missing the toppings that make the 2nd and 3rd burger different.  It's actually a comical level of incompetence in management.  Whoever runs this location should be ashamed.
They gave me the wrong eggs wrong toast and no onions in the home fries which I paid extra for. Avoid like the plague
Horrible ..... the worst chicken McNuggests I ever saw or tasted.  They looked like hockey pucks!!!!

So it's a Burger King, if you've been to one, you've been to them all! But not really because this one has a soda machine that you can combine ANY flavors of soda and it is amazing. I seriously go there for that reason. It's so awesome hah

Came here on a quiet Saturday afternoon and was a bit disappointed since my hubs had hyped this place up. It's okay, I forgive you. The hummus is way better than the baba ghanoush but it could also be the consistency of it is not as creamy as the hummus. The hummus is divine. The pita is also soft and fabulous as well. The chicken was dry and it could've been because we arrived at the tail end of the afternoon. We didn't experience the same generous helpings if ingredients as some others but the meal was filling and adequate for the price they serve. I'd likely try another quick eat dining establishment in this area (there are so many) next time.

Typical Chinese food. People get Orange Chicken the most. Orange Chicken tastes sweet and sour, no taste of orange despite its name. Beijing Beef has a little kick to it. This was really good, and it reminded me of Korean Bulgogi's spicy marinade. SweetFire Chicken is basically sweet chilli sauce poured over it.
First order, fast delivery, friendly delivery person and the food is delicious, highly recommended.

I traveled all the way from New York to come to this place I stopped at multiple locations, all which had sushi restaurants. However, I didn't go into any of them because I wanted to try out this place. Aftertwo hours of traveling and finally getting there, they had closed down early without any notice by half an hour. I'm very disappointed, there were so many good reviews on this place and I wanted to try it out. I guess I'll never get to try Hai Street kitchen. :(

5 pierogies, 2 sides and a drink for $8.99. I got double Mac and cheese as a side it it was well worth it. Not dry, baked with that good crust, what more can you ask for?! Pierogies were small but good! Seared on both sides with a side of sour cream and you can call it a day.
Girl that made my poke bowl was rude and although I paid for extra sushi was not given a portion even 50% greater than what was ordered. Wouldn't go back

I usually avoid buffets, but when Reading Terminal is packed and u need to get food quick Tootsies is a good option. They don't just have a salad bar, but a variety of other foods as well. I've been here a handful of times over the years. On my most recent visit I bought enough food for lunch and dinner. I had ribs, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, rice, string beans, greens and cornbread. Everything was good. Nothing memorable that I would crave or come back for specifically. Individually, you can get each item done better elsewhere. But in a pinch it's more faster and convenient to get everything here.

I'm giving this establishment three stars, only due to the nice woman who made my meal. Otherwise, 100% I would be giving two stars.

Ordering online was super easy, and I was pleasantly surprised to see the nutrition information (as I am on a Keto diet, so I need to be mindful of carbs and sugar). 

I arrived at the store a little early (12:11 PM when my food was supposed to be ready at 12:15 PM). The line is sooo long, and I cannot find the pick up station anywhere. I walked around two times before I saw the pick up rack, completely hidden by the fountain drinks station. I saw two other orders were ready, and it was 12:16 PM and mine still was not done. 

The woman making the food asked me my name and when I told her, she said that her printer was broken and that my order never printed out. She made my meal and was very apologetic. She was very sweet. 

As for the food itself: I ordered a chicken shawarma salad bowl with tahini sauce. I did not like the texture of the lettuce. The chicken seemed a little dry. But the sauce was not bad. It also was a lot of food for me, I ate about 3/4 of the bowl and then had to throw the rest out.

I do not eat pop-eyes, but my boyfriend does.
I'm giving it plenty of stars for the delicious food and the sweet staff at the front counter.

I'm giving it -2 stars for the most uncomfortable environment possible. I felt like I was getting the death stare from 80% of the customers eating at the tables. My boyfriend felt it, too... It was creepy.

Like, really creepy.

I absolutely love Naf Naf and I often find myself going 3 times a week! Food is always delicious. Unfortunately, the employees at this location are SO unfriendly. When I ask a question or i ask for an extra scoop of sauce they seem annoyed and aggressively do so without making eye contact or acknowledging my request. In addition, the employees blatantly don't treat each other with respect, making unnecessary comments to each other about their work. I have worked in the restaurant industry for years, and I never leave comments on places unless positive; however, I have experienced unwelcomeness and disappointment too many times by the staff here to not leave a review.

Even before Covid, this place has been a disaster! I don't go here that often; usually like once a month or so. BUT, EVERY time that I do get food from here, they get it wrong!!
     The place is close to me, so it's more convenient, and that's why I go back. Plus, before I order, I say to myself, "they have to get it right this time."
     But anyways, whether I order in person, or delivery, or through mobile pickup, they always manage to get my order wrong! Most times, they don't give me half my order, sometimes they'll miscount something, sometimes they'll make something wrong, or sometimes they'll give me something totally different than what I ordered.
     I mean, all they have to do is READ their screen!! This place has the poorest of poor management! Don't even bother doing mobile delivery with this place, because you'll be upset with your order when you get it, and there will be nothing that you can do about it.
     Oh, lastly, when I do go back into the restaurant and tell them that they forgot half my order, they look at me like "I" did something wrong or something. They're looking at me like I got 2 heads. SMH
     So, when they go and make the rest of my order, they still make me wait over 10 minutes!! Unbelievable.

I never have confrontations with people, especially people working. I'm very nice when I approach a worker when there is something wrong with my order, no matter where I go.
     I'm just glad they have this app so I can vent. It's just ridiculous how some places continue to have p*ss-poor management, and I'm not the only one who said that they have p*ss-poor management. Just take a look at the other reviews. Ugh.

Food:1/10 Everything is soggy and overall cheap and awful.

Service:7/10 Pretty fast service. I guess that's why they call it "Fast Food."

Atmosphere:6/10 The interior is pretty nice. So is the exterior. It's also connected to KFC. Go there instead.

OVERALL:4.6/10

This was the favorite of my friends when we'd see a movie at the Bridge, er, Rave. I always balked going there because I want my Mexican food cooked with more love and care. The food had the elements of Mexican food, but it never seemed worth the calories. What I can say is that it's fast, which is important to make a movie showing. The food is also filling, but not in a soul satisfying way. 

I think Qdoba is successful because it fits a certain need - food for people who don't have the money or time to invest in a full restaurant experience. And it is a better alternative to the McDonalds that is a block away.

The place is honestly a lifesaver. I've come in here many times at 1 am desperate and in search of food. There's salads, sandwiches, desserts, and the chicken tenders. Don't get the pot pie, it isn't anything worth bragging out. The fries are great as well, hand cut and always piping hot. 

The chicken tenders are delicious and super juicy unless you come around closing time. The chicken tenders are charged by the pound so 3 huge tenders are roughly like $4. I recommended everyone to get the white meat tenders because those are the best, simply put. 

There's also a huge selection of sodas and beers which is pretty cool too. Another plus was their variety of sauces. You have to get a couple so you can figure out which one is your favorite but they're only 50 cents each. So If you're looking for a cheap quick bite go to Wishbone!

I tried to go to this location in Philadelphia on Market street and i was refused service because i have a ESA service animal and they wouldnt sevice me unless i brought my dog outside and tied him up. The lady was very  rude about it and made fun of my service animal saying ESA isnt a service animal. Please Dont go to this restaurant  they have no manners and the people  are very Rude to people with disabilities. I will not be spending my money here again. I recommend the WaWa accross the street.

My daughter is obsessed with this place. I think it is good, and it is great concept. Basically like a Chipolte with sushi rolls on steroids. Very fresh ingredients and the rolls are tasty. There is limited counter seating, so for me personally there are other places in the neighborhood with some service/seating so I can enjoy my food more.
This is a clean, efficient operation with great service, and a refreshing concept with solid execution!
