Hummus is decent but the service is spotty. Sometimes the people behind the counter are pleasant and sometimes, like today (5-19-17 at 3pm), they are rude and act like you are bothering them by daring to ask for food. 

With so many other Hummus spots opening up nearby with comparable pricing and better quality food, I don't see any point in going here if the service is lousy.

I've seen Qdobas in so many cities across the US for the last several years, and for some reason, I've never visited one, until recently.  ...really?  this place is EXACTLY like Chipotle, except they're stingier, and their meats/veggies/salsas aren't cooked/seasoned as well (at this location anyways), their lettuce was a little more wilted, and they sucked at wrapping.  Also, their quesadillas are ridiculously greasy.

Anyways, I made it sound bad, but it's not all that bad.  It really is just like a Chipotle.  I'd favor Chipotle, but this could do in a pinch.
Chicken is excellent. Front counter girls often have unnecessary attitudes. Hopefully owners will read how great food can easily turn into a meh experience once wait staff drops the ball.

Tender delicious chicken in the tastiest, crunchy, pretzel-based breading...yum! The tenders, which you can get with either white or dark meat, aren't loaded with a lot of crazy flavours, You taste the meat! The breading is not too salty, and has the perfect crunch. The chicken pot pie was also a hit! In addition to all that goodness, they have a great bottle selection. What can be better than a cold malt beverage with your fried chicken?! We will be back!

So many of my co-workers are obsessed with Hai Street Kitchen since they opened, and I kept seeing those long boxes being walked around Rittenhouse that I finally convinced my husband to try them out with me for an easy dinner one night. We went over on the early side to get our food to go, and around 5:30ish during the week it was still quite populated. 

Thankfully the wait was short (once we decided what to get). My husband got the roll with tempura shrimp (can't remember the name), while I created my own dish opting for a salad bowl with their salmon, asparagus, beets, sauteed onions, and the gochugang sauce. The food was good (the salmon is deliciously raw and well marinated), but there need to be a few tweaks done to the service. First of all, smile please. Some staff were great, some looked miserable. Secondly, for a salad bowl there should be WAY MORE mixed greens. Not one handful. Finally, the amount of sauce added was RIDICULOUS. Everything was DRENCHED in it, and it's a spicy sauce so you don't want that much of it anyway. The quality of the veggies at least was good. My husband really enjoyed his wrap, but it wasn't enough food for him for a meal. Given the prices and portions currently, we won't be going back. If they improved just those few things slightly, maybe. It's cheaper than sushi rolls at least.

I love checkers French fries, every time I think of fries I though of checkers they have the best seasoned fries it's so delicious. I like the customer service the staff are nice and friendly. I would recommend checkers to everyone!
Great Food! Great Prices! Don't feel gross after eating but healthy enough to walk the other 15 blocks that I need to.

I went to this Panda Express location near the Market street! I remember I stop by this location because I had a jury duty that day! The food was delicious I had ordered a shrimp lo mein and some vegetable egg roll! The service was fast considering it was lunch time! The price was very economical too! I definitely recommend anyone to stop by and try it for themselves!

Quite possibly the GREASIEST fast food I've ever eaten!!!! I don't go here a lot, but I'm ashamed to say I HAVE gone here about 3 times this month. Mainly because it's close to the school where I'm working this summer. 

Some things I've had here are the champ burger (too salty), spicy chicken sandwich (edible), the fries, (WAY too salty also), the hot dogs (which I actually think are good!), apple pie, (also good) and the chicken nuggets. (I can only eat 2, and I trash the rest because the salt and spices start to burn my tongue.)

This particular location is super slow at lunchtime.

I'm so excited this place is here! Everything is under $10 and the vegetable selection is on point and super fresh. Wasabi guac is excellent. Sushirito wasn't huge, but the upsize for an extra $2 is totally worth it for those hungry days. Will be back alllll the time.
I got the fried rice/veggie/orange chicken meal and it was so bland and didn't even have flavor. I would recommend Master Wok in Liberty Place or the Chinese cart on the corner of 18th and Market.

This place is awesome!! They have hot and cold foods and a place that makes fresh Boardwalk Fries all season long is a place that I will be going to from now on. The prices are phenomenal and the service is outstanding. Thank you for opening a the best corner store around. I will be back. Thank you!!

Wow I thought I liked Wishbone but recently had the CRAZIEST EXPERIENCE at the S. 13th street location. I came to the restaurant late night on Saturday (1/11/20). I ordered fries. Moments later I noticed my husband had just waked in, so I waved him down and asked him to join me in line. I asked the server behind the counter to please add an order of chicken strips to my order to which he very loudly and abruptly asked "for who, him!?" I said "yes this is my husband, I was waiting for him and I'd like to add to my order." He looks at us perplexed (insert your assumptions here on race, sexual orientation, etc) and pointed to the front door and said "back of the line." Flabbergasted, we just went to the register to pay and I was asked my name. When I told the cashier that no one ever asked for my name and that I ordered fries and chicken strips, he was confused. As this person got increasingly frustrated I asked for the manager. When the Manager asked the original, rude server what our order was, he replied "they did not place an order," with as much vitriol as he displayed earlier. When my husband raised his voice slightly to ask why the server was literally lying, the server asked security to escort us out. Needless to say, I'm utterly SHOCKED and DO NOT RECOMMEND ANYONE GO HERE.

Went to this place the first time. A standard cafe for a quick snack. I took a Brisket Sandwich which was really amazing but also pricy. 13 Dollar was a little bit too much for a lunch break (only for the sandwich).
I will definitely come but try one of the standard sandwiches which are around 7-10 $.

The restaurant was hard to reach and required some slick parallel parking skills but overall pretty solid to get a sushi fix. The sushi burrito seems to be a new fad that is just starting to hit Chicago, but is pretty prevalent in Philly.

The restaurant operates like a Chipotle, as many fast casual places do these days. Although the workers didn't seem the most enthusiastic, all I care about is the food. I ordered a sushi burrito with brown rice, salmon sashimi pieces, and a variety of vegetables. They allow customization though we could only have 4 choices of vegetable fillings. I quickly learned while trying to eat the monstrosity that any more fillings would not have been possible to wrap.

The burrito suffered from the same problems as Chipotle - unevenly distributed ingredients. I had to unhinge my mouth to get an even bite of everything. However, the flavors were good though a bit salty.

Overall, the restaurant is a little gimmicky but definitely worth a revisit.
Came in here just to grab a vegan baklava to go- most excellent. Love that they had the option and i was craving it. I'll come back for a proper meal soon!

I recently took a few friends who are new to Philly to try out sushi burritos. This sushi burrito experience was also new for me. As we walked into the restaurant on a cold day, there was ample heat. The workers behind the counter patiently waited for us to look through the menu of various sushi burritos, poké bowls, and create-your-own options.

After deliberating, my friends and I decided to go for a variety of rolls and try them all out. We tried the Chicken Katsu burrito, The Crunch burrito, and The Slammin' Salmon burrito. Overall the Chicken Katsu tasted pretty good and included some tempura style chicken, cabbage slaw, sweet teriyaki sauce and other flavors. It was a pretty well-rounded flavor, and it wasn't too overwhelming for anyone who tried it. The Crunch Burrito was similar to a tempura style shrimp sushi roll. However, the wasabi guacamole that came on it was EXTREMELY overwhelming and strong. If you aren't a wasabi fan, the flavor really did overpower the roll. The Slammin' Salmon burrito was pretty tasty, balanced, and everyone who tried it liked it. 

Overall, I think the sushi burrito concept is neat for a try, but it's not something I would order regularly. The filling put in it is similar to the amount in a standard sushi roll, but I find that it's just a ton of rice. What I can say is that they are very filling and kept everyone full for many hours afterwards. Additionally, after paying around 10-12 dollars per roll, it does keep you satisfied. I would say it's worth going for a first-time try, but it isn't something I would get on a regular basis. 

As for the restaurant, it was a casual fast-dining setup with barstools. My friends and I were in a group of seven, and I would say we took up almost all of the seats. Service was fast and efficient, however, there are no restrooms for customers to use. There is a useful hand-washing sink which is useful after your burrito can fall apart in your hands and make them dirty. There was a guest Wi-Fi network, however, the employee I asked the password for couldn't seem to give me the right one. 

Conclusion: It's a cool stop for a one-time try in my opinion. I would definitely like to try the poké in the future though. This is also a pretty good restaurant with healthy options that aren't too overpriced.

Tonight was my first experience with Wishbone. Delivery was reasonably on time and the food was great. The Wishboner and classic chicken tenders were great! Warning - the Donfire sauce is HOT but delicious! Nice to see good food and service. I will be a repeat patron.

Perfectly average Burger King, notable mainly for its hilariously unpunctuated sign out front (from September: "9/11 Never Forget Try Our BK Double Stacker Now Serving Breakfast"). Convenient when you're going to the movies or the DMV. Parking lot is very small, but abundant free parking across the street.

IN SUMMARY
Food freshness: average for BK
Order accuracy: 90%, good
Overall staff attitude: typical Philly apathy and disdain, but not actually hostile
Cleanliness of dining area: good, slightly worse on weekends because of the movie crowd
Cleanliness of bathrooms: don't know
Refills on drinks: yes 
Condiments, napkins, utensils: grab 'em yourself
Kid's play area: no
Drive-through: yes

Welcoming and friendly staff!
Dining room even has a high top table for a game of checkers while you enjoy your lunch!
Great, polite, speedy service! The food is warm and tastes great. I would travel to come to this particular Taco Bell.

I obtained the Vito and asked for Hot peppers (Extra charge). Once I paid the ten big ones for it, I filled up my own drink and had a seat at a high table with bar stools. 

Once I unwrapped the sandwich, I was looking for the other half, could it be that the person behind the counter didn't wrap half of my sandwich in the wrap? No, I was mistaken, the sandwich was just that small. 
If it wasn't for all the wonderfully places signs throughout the place, I don't think I would ever step foot in this place again. 

I understand that given the location, across the street from University of Penn, any type of food place would do good, but come-on! Were is the quality & quantity people! 

I would not touch this place with a 10 foot pole! 

~The 10 rules of Warren Buffet was the best!
Good chicken, excellent slaw, desserts looked really good.  A very welcome option for upscale take-out. 3.5 Stars.

I mean it's fine. It's right by my office, so it works well as a quick spot to run out and grab lunch. The pickles are probably my favorite topping. The chicken and hummus could use some more spice in my opinion, but I guess that is what the sauces are for. The place itself definitely gets quite crowded during typical lunch hours.

I like the Japanese-Mexican fusion concept. I had slammin salmon with brown rice and chips & wasabi guacamole and they were all delicious. The salmon was actually raw (I think the only raw fish option). The ingredients tasted fresh and the rice was the right seasoning. I hate it when sushi rice is bland and not sweet or sour enough. 

I took off one star because the restaurant was very small and did not have enough seating. I think it's more of a take out place. We don't live ok the city so we ate there. There were only 4 stools. I would visit this restaurant more often if there were more seatings.
Great food noting like your neighborhood Chinese store everything is real meat an taste delicious it's worth every penny

Ordered from here today for lunch on UberEATS. Saw the reviews and thought I would give it a go to get a different taste from typical lunch.  Well it came hot so that was a plus but I am not really too impressed. I ordered the red bliss potato salad, a biscuit and white meat tenders. The biscuit was the best tasting thing with the citrus honey butter. The chicken was um okay I guess and the potato salad had way to much mustard seed or whatever they put in there. Too overpowering for me. That's all I tasted and the potatoes weren't cooked to the same consistency. Would I eat her again? For the prices probably not.

Totally remodeled location. Clean. New soda machines, new furniture, redesigned bathroom, free wifi, the works. Stopped in for a quick lunch break and had the apple pecan chicken salad. Fresh and tasty. Created my own coke zero flavor.

I don't like sushi because I don't like seafood or nori. But I'm writing this in hopes someone out there is awkwardly picky like me. Hai Street Kitchen has a lot of options for us, too.

They give you the option to skip the nori and have anything in a rice or salad bowl, which is of course what I chose to do. They have plenty of protein options that aren't seafood (again, this pleases me) like pork, chicken, and steak. I do think they need a grilled chicken option, though. I love that you can create your own combinations. The Hai Street Chicken (chicken katsu, red onions, red cabbage, green papaya salad, teriyaki sauce) was SO fresh and flavorful. It comes with two big pieces of chicken, so the serving size is decent. I finished the chicken first though and was left with the veggies, but they alone were super tasty.

I went a few minutes before closing, but the veggies were still crisp and fresh. Also, everything just seemed so clean and neat behind the counter. I will definitely be back! The pickled mango & wasabi guac are on my list of toppings to try.

My apologies for bothering to disturb you with my business.  I was the only one there and four people were behind the counter.  When I asked to put in an order at the cash register I was bruskly told to go talk to one of the other workers.  When one finally did take my order she made it seem like I was a total inconvenience to her.  With all of the other options in the Reading Terminal Market I would steer clear of this one.

OHH EM GEE. This place. IS DELICIOUS. Best chicken- moist and juicy. Unique sandwiches with different types of toppings that pair so well together. The soda fountain has so many different types of flavored sodas. I love it! The restaurant itself is super cute, and it's never too crowded. I love coming here!

I want to like Wishbone, I really do.  The restaurant itself is beautiful, really well done. I have had it probably five times at this point, and have been disappointed every time.

I have held back on a review but the latest sandwich I got is pushing me over the edge.  The chicken itself is minuscule, covering less than 50% of the bun.  It is also soggy, not crispy. I had Chick-Fil-A last night and am wishing I had just done that again.  The chicken sandwhich from Shake Shack is also much better.  I'd expect more from a dedicated chicken spot.  This is the 3rd time I have been disappointed in a sandwich from here, I am done.  The potato salad has way too strong of a dill/mustard flavor, not edible.

The tenders are hit/miss. Sometimes good, but cannot eat more then a few of them.  Again IMO chick-fil-a is better

I gave them a shot on my last trip to Reading Terminal. 

Simply put, the fried chicken is phenomenal. I would gorge on that as my last meal if I could. 

The ribs... shoe leather. Seriously, it was like eating rib jerky. Maybe I got the bad batch. 

One out of two ain't bad.

This place was amazing. People were friendly, the food was delicious and the beer selection is HUGE! I got the Nashville chicken sandwich and my boyfriend got white meat chicken... it was a tough call about whose meal was better. We will definitely be back when we come to Philly!
This the worst McDonald's ever I found a roach in my soda! I'm going to call and have this place shut down!

I had Wing Stop on Cottman Avenue today for the first time and the wings were not good at all! The wings had no flavor. Very bland taste-and they were small. Order chicken parmesan -didn't know they would throw a big clump of dry Parmesan on the wings which made it worst! Yuck! The mild wings had no flavor and over cooked ...maybe I caught an off day. I will  not return.

I thought turning sushi into a burrito roll was blasphemy. But then I tried the slammin' salmon roll and it was BANGIN. Also get their matcha green tea drink. I thought it would be bitter like the red fruity tea drink ( the name escapes me) but it was sweet and delicious- well, if you like matcha green tea.

I've been wanting to write a review for this Taco Bell for some time. 

I have to start out by saying this might be the best Taco Bell I've ever been to. I may even go as far as to say, it's the best fast food establishment I have ever been in. That is due in part to management. Every time I have patronized, I have always had someone very friendly. I usually have a custom order due to dietary needs, and my order has always been correct. 

I have brought a handful of coworkers/friends to this spot and they've looked at me all crazy when I boast, "this is the BEST Taco Bell" and sure enough we leave with them agreeing. 

One particular visit, my coworker and I went for a late lunch and dined in. One of the workers came up to our table to see how our food was. Keep up the  great work!

I always get a rice bowl...no hummus no baba just rice chicken, sumac onions, chopped salad, garlic sauce, sometimes I want the other sauces but it's rare (I hate the mango stuff), the pita comes with it... so you might as well get the bowl instead of the sandwich... I worked here for 2 weeks at the KOP location a few years back and I must say I loved how clean they are, how serious they are about fresh food, the growth of the company, Hiaro (I think that's his name) being a great GM? RM? For opening the Malvern location...  and over all the background of the company. 

This location specifically though is quick, clean, clean bathrooms(dramatically long bathroom code... but I understand why lol) and has amazing eye candy .
There was a FEATHER in my chicken fingers!!!!!! Absolutely disgusting and requested a full refund.

I've been here numerous times and I'm never disappointed. After work I like to grab several burritos to bring to my friend's for pre-gaming. Lol. The burritos are always a hit and the staff is always cool.

This Mc Donalds is to me one of the worse ever ,the customer service is not good at all,The milk shake machine is down almost 3 days of every week ,the employees were cursing and playing while the line was to the door.My order was incomplete no napkins ,straws or even a have a nice day was said to any customer in the lines.It was just poor service all around

This place has been on my list for long time and finally tried Friday lunch! At noon surprisingly it wasn't very crowded (considering the office crowd around). I ordered Chicken Katsu roll and the server was super quick in making it. Less than 5 mins and it was ready and I was out of the place. I really enjoyed the flavor of sauce with chicken pieces. A little hot sauce makes it more flavorful. Very filling and good for the price.

Very simple food. Good variety. Different things each time I go. I have had a problem with swallowing anything other than very soft food, for a couple months now. Most of their food is very soft. Tastes good. Best part is, you can take how much you want, depending on your appetite, and a great price!
If you want Chinese fast food, this is the place to go.

I never saw a McDonald's that closes whenever they want in-spite of having business hours. This location is by far the worst I ever visited since I was born. I really never seen a McDonald's so unprofessional. The teenagers working have attitudes when taking orders and at the window. This location even ran out of burgers at one point, like how??? This location just need to shut down or hire a better manager.

JUST GO TO CHIPOTLE!
Terrible customer service bad attitude. Half assed, asked for manager and was told I was speaking to her.  Alexis. Yeah right!  April 3rd 7:30 Pm. 2020. Crappy attitude not answering phone, not faking orders face to face not taking orders online. I will never walk into that store again. I am a Chipotle guy now. Chipotle is 1/2 block away (3925 Walnut) I buy for myself and my family of six most times. I can not take this place any more I used to be a real fan of theirs. The management has gone into the toilet. 

Update: Complaint on the qdoba website yielded no response whatsoever. The app is too time
Consuming to set up. I spent 20 minutes entering my email address at least ten times. Why does it not remember the info once entered??? Then my order was rejected anyway. Unhelpful staff stated that it was too close to closing time. "Online stops 1/2 hour before closing. Even though I had wasted twenty minutes setting up the app, it was more than 30 minutes before closing. They somehow rigged the phones to hive a busy signal or route my call to their super-annoying fax machine. I wish I had taken pictures of the indifferent/rude staff. They really seemed to be entertained by my frustration. Don't bother with this company. If you're holding their stock SELL IT. I am excellent at predicting the demise of poorly managed companies. I can see it from the customer's perspective. Qdoba, there are lots of places to buy tacos, burritos and other fast food/casual dining options. ?Why would anyone tolerate abuse and neglect as a customer while there are so many better alternatives?

We get take out from Wishbone once a week. The coating on the chicken is perfect, it's light and the chicken is perfectly cooked every time we order it. Get the drumsticks because you pay by the pound. The mac and cheese is okay not really my taste. It is odd they don't have mashed potatoes. But the sauces!!!! They are 50 cents each and all amazing. I use them for other foods I make at home. The Don XX sauce... is so so good!!!!

I'm a regular at this place, and what brings me back is the kale, quinoa, and black bean salads. I wish they had even more vegetarian salads, but have several that would be excellent, but they mix in chicken or seafood. I have never tried the cooked, hot food items, so I can't speak to that. They also dropped their LevelUp, which was a disappointment, but they do take credit cards, including Amex. But who needs it when you can get lunch for $4.50?

We were planning a family reunion to be held in New Jersey but my brother and I live in California. Tootsie's team made it so easy. They answered all our questions and even anticipated some things that we didn't think of. They contacted our venue and made sure everything was perfect. Now,the best part was the food. We were able to serve a variety of food. Everything was delicious and there was plenty for everyone to have. They even provided us with Philly's famous soft pretzels. The cost was very reasonable in my opinion.We would definitely recommend Tootsie's for anyone's catering needs. Thank you for helping make the reunion dinner a big success.

I come to this Naf Naf location for lunch ALL THE TIME. It is absolutely delicious and the workers are very friendly. My biggest tip is that you should order head. They have an app that allows you to place an order and a pick up time to avoid the long lines in the restaurant. You can also mobile pay so when you come to the restaurant, you just need to grab your lunch bag (with your name on it) and you can be on your way. 

Note: They do have seating although it can be hard to find a table if you come during peak business lunch hours.

Worst customer services they basically make you come in because no one answers the drive thru but the food is ok other than that they need to improve on the customer satisfaction the old checkers when I was younger is much better than the new one but this is just my opinion

Only ever ordered this off of Caviar so I am solely basing this review off of the food.  Was not expecting the chicken to be as good as it was.  It was less of fried chicken and more of a chicken strip which I really appreciated.

We also ordered the Mac & Cheese, potato salad, corn bread, and biscuit.  I'm a biscuit person, so personally I thought the biscuit was better than the corn bread.  The corn bread had jalapenos in it, which I wasn't the biggest fan of.  Mac & Cheese was OK - but I'm pretty picky with Mac & Cheese.  Not usually a potato salad person, but LOVED the potato salad!
One of my favorite places to eat, I'm literally there every weekend for my now favorite flavor spicy Korean. I also love the staff Ayanna your team is great!!!
The food is hot and service is relatively quick, even late at night or during off hours.  No complaints!
Nashville Chicken Sandwich is AMAZING! Just tried this place for the first time after reading reviews raving about this sandwich and I was not disappointed

This has to be the worst experience I've ever had at a Burger King. Went through the drive-thru to get breakfast for my son. These people didn't put any utensils in the bag. Then to add insult to injury the woman working the drive-thru took orders and handed them out while sitting down. I literally had to stand while in my car to reach over and get my bag. Not once did she even attempt to stand up or assist. Just utterly ridiculous. I will not be returning. I wish I had my receipt. I definitely would have taken the survey.

very good and inexpensive! nice restaurant-quality wings.

can def taste the pretzel crust which is very fresh for me~  a nice alternative to KFC or popeyes~

love the variety of sauces. i went with a classic and picked buffalo bleu.  solid choice!

can't wait to try the mac and cheese next time!
Sushi borito here is so overrated. I've had better. For someone like me that doesn't eat raw fish, menu is very limited. Price is okay.

The Nori Wrap with brown rice and shrimp tempura - the perfect amount of food, blend of flavors and great veggie combo.  A Chipotle style "roll your way" option was fun to customize. Highly recommend.

The workers here are awful, they act like they have no common sense. It was 9:50 PM and I'm waiting in line for over 10 minutes with only three other cars in line, once it hits 10:02 they only served one car and told everyone else that they're closed.

I love hand rolls. They're my favourite form of sushi. This is like a hand roll on steroids and is about the best thing I could ask for after a brutal weekend gym class.

I went with a build-your-own and got the chicken katsu on white rice and seaweed wrap with spicy gochujang, spring mix, carrots, cucumber, asparagus, and crunchy shallots. I died and went to hand roll fusion heaven. It was really, really delicious.

I am docking 1 star for lack of low-fat protein options. There is chicken and shrimp - both fried, plus flank steak and salmon. I would have liked a grilled chicken option. I will say that the chicken katsu was a good choice in terms of the amount of protein you get. Two large chicken pieces was more than enough to make this a filling meal.

I will be back on many a sunny Saturday in the future! This is also a great option for dining in the parks nearby - very portable and easy to eat. Service was friendly and fast!

Reason to go to Burger King?  Their Whopper Jr. ,no cheese with fries.  I treat myself once or twice a year.  Its a good sandwich, the right size,  maybe 3 ounces, with that Burger King back yard charcoal taste that is damn good.
The choices are good. I had the bbq chicken with green beans. The chicken was dry but the green beans were great. They were not the friendliest behind the counter.

Matt's is great, very nice guy! He serves some decent sliders. Yes, they may be small but the flavor is huge! I always upgrade the fries to the truffle parm fries. Definitely worth it! I like the original slider and the crab slider. Though anything here is pretty good. Just FYI they don't have a sign outside and they share a space with a bagel place. There is a sign on the door though.
I would crawl on my knees through shards of glass just to bask in the aroma of those sweet potato fries.

I visited the new location in Liberty Place today.  I ordered the salad bowl, which was nothing more than a bowl of shredded cabbage, a little scoop of guacamole and two small tempura battered shrimp.  You live and you learn.  The worst part was the customer service I experienced.  The young man who made my salad was great, but Ebony, the employee at the register should not be in the front of the house.  I waited almost a whole minute for her to come back to the register after I signed for the food.  Then she hands me my receipt and goes on about her business.  I had to ask for a bag, which she handed to me.  So I paid $11.00 for a bowl of cabbage and I have to pack the bag myself.  Not to mention that she seemed to have attitude and never said hello.  The one thing I have no tolerance for is poor customer service!  They have Chic fil a and Chipotle just a few steps away; both have great customer service.

After I removed the chicken from the cup of oil it was sitting in it was semi-salvageable. I love their wings butI noticed when I get food from them through Uber eats or to go the quality of food is horrible- almost as if they know you aren't going to bring it back. Disappointed.

I ordered the baconzilla meals. It was fantastic the fries were hot and crunchy and seasoned so well. The workers were humorous and helpful. The service was a little slow but the great food made up for it.

I love Naf Naf. I usually order the same thing each time - chicken bowl and rice with cucumbers, cabbage, pickles, onions, w/ tzatziki. Their pitas are also soo soo good. Lunchtime can get a little crazy but otherwise service is quick. Falafel and Naf Naf fries are also made super fresh and super tasty. Plenty of self service tables to eat at after ordering. Prices are reasonable and within the standard $9-$12 range for lunch in center city.

UBER EATS REVIEW:

food was hot, fresh but the only thing i'd complain is that i asked for chopsticks and hot sauce and never received but other than that it fulfilled my panda express craving!

I've been here multiple times for sushi burritos, and it doesn't get old. I love sushi in general, and will take it in any available form. While it doesn't come with a whole lot of meat/fish/protein option, there is an option to upgrade and pay a little more to get a little more. Honestly, the rice makes it pretty filling either way, so if you're trying to save your pennies, just forego the upgrade. They have pre-set options for burritos, or you can build your own.

I do recommend getting the Iced Matcha Green Tea, its lightly sweetened, and sooo good - even if you're not a huge fan of matcha.

There is some seating, but space is limited at this location, and I don't believe they have a bathroom.

A decent fast food option, but nothing to write home about. Rice to protein is way off--sometimes feels like I'm just paying for rice but the other ingredients, although sparse, are SO delicious it's almost worth it. The spicy aioli and shrimp tempura and pineapple create your own is unbeatable. Kind of like a fish taco

My husband and I used to eat at Popeyes a lot growing up but haven't in the last few years...until the chicken sandwich. My husbands a huge chik-fil-a chicken sandwich fan but I'm 100% Popeyes! We get the spicy chicken sandwich with extra spicy sauce - so. good. Crispy, big piece of chicken, saucy and spicy. Chik fil a is too bland to me. Obviously not the highest quality meat but it's fast food, what did you expect? It's great for what it is in my opinion!

Super unimpressed with the manager here. She was incredibly rude when we came with a coupon. She was curt and said that she wouldn't apply it, even though this location isn't marked as an exception. No apologies, and refused to make eye contact while raising her voice. Customer service here is just awful and left our group with a sick feeling. Won't be returning to Panda again.

My son really wanted Mac and Cheese. They had it prominently displayed in the counter cases. The problem was that it had a crusty top. He likes soft mac and cheese without the crust.

He nicely asked them to scoop from under the crust and they obliged. They even let him taste it first. They also gave him a free chicken wing when he expressed interest in them. He ate both up, and went back for seconds on the mac and cheese. 

As a dad who often has his kid order something only to change his mind and toss a perfectly good sandwich out I really appreciated how accommodating they were to a fussy young man.

Came for dinner on a Thursday evening.  They had a decent selection of beer for a chicken place.  We ordered 1lb of chicken wings ($9.58) and a half cup of mac n cheese ($5.20). I was disappointed by the chicken; very dry outside, yet greasy.  The chicken is only bearable with some kind of sauce that they charge extra for.  The Mac n cheese was ok, but nothing extraordinary.  Honestly, would've preferred Popeyes or KFC even at the same price.
My chicken sandwich literally tasted rotten. Slow service and the cashier had a terrible attitude.

Not sure how I feel about this place. I think I had different expectations going in but didn't let that sway my review. Love the concept and locally sourced natural ingredients... I Agree with everyone... Japanese chipotle. 

The set burritos had some unique options but I opted for the crunch (shrimp tempura). I was a little disappointed with the amount they gave considering the price point(2 pieces). It's set up like chipotle so each station is worked on by a new person... Here is the issue I had... The first guy took my order for the meat... Then the next guy did the greens.. But he didn't know what was suppose to go on it. It seemed like he just looked at the bins and threw stuff on... Then the next garnish station was the guy that put my meat on... He noticed it was messed up and took the "wrong" stuff off. I'm cool with that no big deal... But he ended up putting too much spicy mayo when I told him "very little mayo please". I let all that slide BC it's opening week.

The place is stand up bar only... The staff were friendly but I felt they were either the B team or just didn't study the menu well enough or just tired from a long day... I went on a Saturday night... So was that their 2nd or 3rd day opening??? 

I would definitely recommend checking this place out if you like sushi rolls. I love seaweed so having so much of it all at once was pretty good. But the overload of spicy mayo messed up my taste buds (not that it was spicy... It was heavy and overwhelmed other flavors).

Good luck and hope the place works some of the kinks out to have a successful summer!!
Don't order on line at this location. They prioritize people in line and my friends waited over 15 minutes after the pickup time stated. Poor management!
Love this place!!!! Large portions and great bottles beer selections . The chicken is HUGE

Gave me hospital strength food poisoning. Must be some cross contamination or food being kept below healthy temperature going on here; because 5 hours after my burrito my stomach was a bloody mess. Would never think about eating here again

Walked in this office thinking I would get a $ 1.00 sandwich for customer appreciation day and was told off by the manager and kicked out the store. The cops were called and report sent to Corp Offices. I'm home and still upset and hungry. The owner/ manager was rude even pulled his phone out to record me. I hope this location is fine or taken out of business before someone gets hurt! Waiting for corporate to call back.
I love this place I go here almost everyday , the manager is kind and even the cooks interact with your order to make sure everything is right . Would definitely recommend it
The pierogis were cold and hard, the mac and cheese was oily and the coleslaw was flavorless. Do not recommend. Although service was quick

I just ordered from here and spent about 40 bucks. They forgot all the sauces, the fries are salty as hell and the wings are full of oil. Literally had to throw the entire bag away. When I called and spoke to the manager Brianna and requested some kind of refund she refused. She even claimed not to know the corporate telephone number and proceeded to hang up on me. (After picking up the phone on the 16 ring). This is unbelievable! Horrible customer service skills. I have them a one because I couldn't give them anything less. We do not need a business like this in our community.

This is like the Chipotle of Japanese food - fast, fresh, and totally customizable. The veggies are finely cut and crispy, the meat/protein is satisfying, and the sauces add the final Asian touch. Their eggplant miso soup is perfect for the cooling weather, and actually has a decent amount of veggies - I wish all miso soups were like theirs. 

The only downside is the limited seating, so expect take-out if you go during peak hours.

Great place for quick lunch. Sit down or take out. 
Vegetable feast is amazing includes salads, hummus, falafel and fresh pita (so soft). The hit and very hot sauce goes very well with it. I have also tried at their Chicago location Lentil soup which I just love it.

My best friend and I stopped in yesterday as we were looking for a non alcoholic happy hour lol what better than food! This place is a hidden gem! The owner has excellent customer service and was very charming and welcoming to us. The food was really great, we both had the crab cake sliders which were so good & the sweet potato fries! I'm definitely coming back as I actually want some more today!

Delicious. Delicious. Delicious. Working near this place is the my worst and best nightmare, really. The balance in taste is fantastic, and the fresh, yummy ingredients are staples in this place.

I'm sad that they've switched the picked mango out for the pickled jicama, so I skip that particular topping now. Slammin' salmon is still my favorite, though.

This food is so nasty the chicken taste dry the mac& cheese tast fake sometime the food look like it been sitting out for days they have the worst salads i don't know who make them  they taste like nothing this food so over price and it taste like shit i will never eat at this place ever again it's not worth the money u pay.

As expected the line was long and the service was slow.  The sandwich came hot and the chicken portion was large.  The chicken was stringy but the sandwich was still pretty tasty.  The bun was like a Hawaiian roll and was delicious, so I added one start.

I'm in love.  There's not much more to say about this place that hasn't already been said.  A really cool, niche concept and great execution.  The staff is warm and welcoming, the ingredients are fresh and healthy, and the price is reasonable for a high quality meal.

I opted for The Crunch this time around, and stole Brad P's idea to add wasabi guacamole.  Welp, now that I've tasted it I'm pretty sure I need to have that on every roll for the rest of eternity.  Thanks a lot, Brad.

I also had the sweet green tea and wasn't expecting it to be so..... green.  But the juice-colored tea ended up being really refreshing and delicious!

So happy that this place is so close to work for me.  I will be back, and soon!
Definitely the worst McDonalds in the area. No one knows what's going on, no one knows what to do, know one knows what you ordered and no one has any manners. Avoid unless you are STARVING!

Best way to describe this is meh. It's nothing special. The fries are good. The chicken is crispy and juicy but rather ordinary. The spicy tenders lack any actual heat. They could definitely offer more sides and sauces. The price is nice though.

I order Taco Bell from uber eat . 
I'm sorry if you hate your job and you can't offer customer fresh food then YOUR NASTY . 
If you work in this Taco Bell your NASTY. I didn't even bother I throw out all that IN THE GARBAGES never again . People don't order from here it's gross.
Went through drive-thru. Order tsker and the person we received the order from were GREAT! Very courteous - a lost art!

A good place to get massive custom burritos and Mexican salads, as well as nachos smothered in queso.

Standard layout with an assembly line. The steak is a bit chewy, but spiced adequately with the salsa, it's not bad in a quesadilla or burrito. The servers are generous with their portions, too. Only gripe is that guacamole costs extra every time.

Satisfies the burrito craving, at least.

The food is ok but the service is terrible. They put in the wrong sauce on my food and instead of fixing it or apologizing they lie to me. They also charged me $1.50 extra for the hummus and didn't put it in my bag.

You know how in general it's not a great idea to get McDonald's because of the food and service? Turns out, it's especially not a great idea to order McDonald's using Uber Eats. I've tried giving them a chance on multiple occasions but they seem to ALWAYS mess it up. So, if you see McDonald's on Uber Eats, pick something else. You'll be glad you did.

Quality of food is not a problem. On every one of my past three visits (2 at the drive through, 1 to go inside), my order was wrong. I didn't complain to anyone, because I didn't notice until I got home - my fault for not checking.

The pretzel crusted chicken is so good! It is weird though that the wings cost the same amount per pound as the tenders, so your basically paying for a bunch of bones... 
All of the meals are priced by weight and it is kind of expensive but I enjoyed the meal. The tenders are pretty big so two were enough for my lunch and I enjoyed the s'mores bar as well. 
The half baked cookie was not good. I'm not sure what makes it half baked because it seemed fully cooked to me...the person who I got lunch with had half of it and gave the other half to me, then after one bite I threw the rest away.  I would not get it again.

This place is a dump. Tried going through drive thru before 1am on a Friday night. They close at 2am. Lights all on, place all lit up, menu screen lit up, nobody answering, hello? Beeping horn! Nothing. No answer. Drive up to pickup window and see a person inside walking around. Beep horn again. Nope. Person sees me and walks away. Guess the employees make up their own hours in this place. Which is it? Bad employees or piss poor management. I say both. Go elsewhere.

I was the very first person in line on free lunch day and I'm sitting at my desk now having Hai Street for a second time.

I absolutely love this whole idea - it's completely different from anything else you would find, and that makes me think Hai Street will be here to stay. First time, I had the Crunch roll which was amazing and fresh! I've got the Sumo Steak now (added the spicy mayo because I loved it on the last roll) and also some tempura corn. Ummm whose idea was tempura corn?? High five for that! The Sumo Steak is super yummy as well, with the spicy mayo giving it that extra kick I wanted.

It is definitely more on the expensive side for just a roll, but I think the quality of ingredients speak to that. My roll and corn was around $12. Definitely not an amount of money I'd spend on lunch every day, but it's a nice treat from time to time.

Best of luck to Hai Street, hope you guys continue to do well!
Good idea, liked the taste, wait time was quite long. Would go again, price seemed a little steep, but center city is like that.

They have a a dish there that is just delicious, the honey walnut shrimp is amazing

Everyone I go there they are either out of them and have to remake a batch or they are just down to the last serving and person in front of me orders them.

I wait for them so it's a fresh batch 

I come here and also get the veggie Lo mein I prefer more veggies than the noddles and I always ask them to add the Teriyaki sauce on my noodles.

Over all if you don't go during lunch hours you're doing great but I've seen the line to the door at times.

Every time I stop in here the staff is welcoming and ready to go. I am in and out very quickly and ingredients are always fresh. They also helped me with a last minute catering order for 50 people! It was fresh and right on time. I will for sure be back! Make sure to sign up for jimmy rewards for free stuff! I will be back.  Also, the GM is extremely good looking and a breath of fresh air. Come for the speedy delivery / freshness , stay for the hotties that work there.

Terrible waste of time. Came in around 8pm and they literally had nothing cooked and ready to eat. The only saving grace was the polite waiter/cashier. This place was understaffed and underwhelming. I think its ridiculous running this location with only 1 person up front because the people in the back were doing absolutely nothing. She needed and couldn't get it asking repeatedly for Orange Chicken to be cooked along with fried rice!

***This ballpark stand primarily offers crabfries from a popular Pennsylvania restaurant Chickie's & Pete's (several locations throughout the city); the fries were crispier and hotter than a lot of ballpark fries out there, but I found the Cajun-like seasoning to be too strong and salty; maybe this would go better with the cheese dip that is available at an extra charge***

I remember seeing a Chickie's & Pete's stand at the Pittsburgh Pirates' stadium PNC Park, but I did not get around to trying it though the stand seemed popular.  This French fries stand seems even more popular at the Philadelphia Phillies' stadium Citizens Bank Park.  Chickie's & Pete's is a local restaurant (with a few locations) that features all kinds of dishes, but their signature crabfries are very loved and make for the kind of easily prepared finger food that can work at a ballpark.

The line gets quite long, but the pick-up process seems fairly efficient (at least the first part).  They do one size of fries and the staff quickly puts them up on the counter for people to grab.  You then go to one of the registers to pay.  I think they could probably use a few more registers to keep up with the fast kitchen.

The fries are crinkle cut fries though they are skinnier than the frozen crinkle cut fries so the fries here are very crispy.  I am not a big fan of crinkle cut fries, but I did like these ones over the way-too-close-to-Ore-Ida-fries at Nationals Park (from Shake Shack).  The Chickie's & Pete's crabfries were hot too and ballpark fries are often cold and soggy.

The fries were heavily seasoned with a Cajun-like seasoning.  While I liked the hotness, freshness and crispiness of the fries, the seasoning was too strong and too salty.  I did not opt for the optional cheese dip (available at an extra charge), but this may help cover the saltiness of the fries.

The fries did not feel that expensive since they were a large portion and more than enough for two or even three people to share.

Service was fairly quick (at least before the game), but I am not sure how quick service is when the lines get really long.

Chickie's & Pete's definitely serves fries that you will not find at most ballparks.  That being said, I did not really enjoy them because they were too salty.  They are definitely worth trying since they are a local food item, but I would opt for the cheese dip if you are going to have them.

Chickie's & Pete's is located within the stadium so it is only available to game day attendees; general parking is close to the stadium and is $15 per vehicle.

Rarely do I heap such ire on a place where food is cheap and plentiful.  You are in the Reading Terminal Market for cripes sake!  Fresh food and produce are abundant!  So what do you do with it?  Mix over cooked, rock hard, chicken with wilted lettuce for a salad.  Throw in mystery seafood with a chemical taste to it with macaroni for seafood salad?  I almost lost it.  Tossed it into the trash.  My mistake was thinking it would be fresh because of the fast turnover, NO, NO, NO!
i ordered 3 pcs wing meals. and one of the wing the inside is pink color n smell bad.

THE ABSOLUTE WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER! AND IT'S CONSISTENT!!!The managers/owner of this location should make an anonymous call or visit so that they can experience the grief and sincere unprofessional behavior you are guaranteed to experience at this location! The workers are cursing at each other, throwing things at each other, talking on their cell phones checking their cell phones while mixing your food it's constantly happening. And if you call they laugh while picking up the phone talk in the background to the others while taking your order it's like your being pranked. It's DISRESPECT on another level! I have finally convinced my husband to go to the other location near where we live! I will drive an extra 5 minutes to be treated with respect when I'm spending my money . We went to the other location where we encountered VERY NORMAL PROFESSIONAL BEHAVIOR AND ATTITUDES from the staff. The owner at the COTTMAN LOCATION should be ashamed I can only imagine how the care for the food at this location!
This place lacked energy I wasn't greeted nor was the employee helpful at all it took about 20 minutes to get my meal and I was the only one in there on a Sunday...
It's a buffet the food is just ok. Definitely should try it because they have different options daily. I just wish the food had a bit more flavor.

Out of curiosity, I had to try this Japanese burrito sushi thingy. I got the crunch: shrimp tempura with spicy mayo which cost almost $10!!! It was good but huge. Well, it's a burrito without the beans! I liked the taste not the price. I went for a second time to try the Chicken and black pepper teriyaki sauce. And it was as good as the first time. Still not happy about the price hahahh. So if u have an extra $10 to spend on a strange combination of two cuisines( Mexican and Japanese) not taste wise but idea, go there you will enjoy it for sure. I know I will go again.
Three and half Yelps!
Consistently good food. The place is usually pretty busy, and it's nice to have good food so close to where I live.

I get it its  a Taco Bell were the employees are sub-par anyway....but this was the most ignorant low grade set of employees I have ever seen in my 40 years of eating alleged fast food....they just built and it should already be condemned......stay away I'm telling ya....heard it here

The Asian girl working literally got an attitude with me when I told her the ketchup had sticky gross stuff on it. All I did was ask for ketchup packets because it was sticky and she rolled her eyes and handed some to me with the biggest stank look . There's mad flies all over the dining room and the tables are dirty but there's a bunch of girls in uniforms on their phones doing nothing. It's really weird . This place definitely needs bettering management because the service made me so upset that I had to make this review .

A pleasant surprise to find a sushi burrito here! The employees were helpful in making suggestions of what their favorites were. It was delicious. 

The lack of seating is a let down, but maybe this is just a grab and run to the office stop. I'm not from the area so I'm not sure. Therefore not taking off any stars for lack of seating, just making a point so others are aware :) 

Stop by! Their to go packaging is convenient little box.

We found this place accidentally when the restaurant we were going to was full. I'm so glad we walked in. Excellent chicken and service! My niece and I split the Tasting Menu and that was so much good food. The ladies working there are awesome! Thanks for the great meal!
All that I tried is the buffalo wings and cornbread. The wings were so good I went there 3 days in a row. The place is small but they have a lot of stuff. Check it out if you're in Reading terminal.

Very bad customer service. Employees seem like they don't care about their job, place was filthy. They forgot ALL of my sides as if I didn't even order them. Worst Popeyes I've ever stepped foot in. Won't see me here again.

The drive-thru is very very long I'm getting ready to get out of line to go to another restaurant but why I'm sitting in this line at Wendy's I'm looking at Kentucky is not that crowded Burger King is not that crowded Taco Bell has a long line just like Wendy's. The food is not that great I don't even know why everyone is in this long behind line they must have a mix-up in the restaurant they must don't have enough fries cooking or any Burgers done this is absolutely crazy but it's starting to move now and I also looked down the street and McDonald's is crowded nobody don't want to cook a nice Sunday dinner I just got off of work and I'm tired so I just want to grab something and go home. I still have four or five cars in front of me I can't see all the way around didn't even get to the window to place my order yet hopefully my food is fresh and my fries are hot.

After being ignored for 10 mins at 3:30am then finally being told they were closed due to system issues, I left the McDonald's on Ogontz and drove to the one on Stenton. They were closed also. Why are they always having issues??? Why can't they post signs to make customers aware of problems??

I had a great experience going there for the first time today.  The place is bright and airy.  Service was very good.  I had a chicken shwarma which I liked.  I loved the big, fluffy pita, it had a good amount of filling, and the sauces were flavorful.  My friend was not as keen on his bowl, which was half empty and looked dry.  He said it was bland, and had very little salad, which had asked for.  We'll be going again and he'll try something different.

Naf Naf Grill popped up the "Hot and New" list so I had to give this place a try during my lunch hour. As expected, the line was nearly out the door during lunch but it moved rather quickly (it took me about 15 minutes from the time I arrived to get my order) because its 'Chiptole' for Mediterranean food. Second, it's rather on the pricey side because of location. 

I ordered a chicken schwarma bowl with all the toppings and a warm, fresh and fluffy pita is included in the order. The chicken was seasoned okay, the toppings were a nice touch but nothing about Naf Naf Grill jumped out at me as a reason to return. There are other places in the area that serve better Mediterranean food at the same or lesser price. 

However, I guess Naf Naf serves its purpose as being a quick bite but do not expect a unique taste you have not experienced anywhere else.

Staff was friendly but very slow moving. Bathroom sink was scalding hot to the touch and the sandwich was missing bacon and cheese. They did fix the sandwiches right away but it was one of their signature sandwiches.
Otherwise the restaurant was clean.
We went here but in Wells Fargo honestly 10/10 would eat crab fries as my last meal if I was on death row. Only downside is they don't provide u with any good way to carry ur food????? Questionable.

I am vegetarian so I only ever get the one with guac and cheese, but it's fantastic. Fast too.

Best secret that isn't a secret: you can buy an entire loaf of day-old bread for 50 cents or a freshly baked one for $2.70. Go ham!

I gave up trying to order. They seem to block the phone lines, won't take orders at the door Covid policy or lazy employees? What's the difference? It's NOT WORKING!  and the online ordering app does not seem to work. These people only seem to accept orders from Uber and Grubhub. I guess the emplees/half-assed managers have not figured out how to block those yet.  I guess the owner loves paying the big fees to third parties instead of getting 100% direct from the customer. 

Complaint to qdoba via email generated an automated apology which sounded like it was written by a stoned teenager. "Bummer"  w a promise that things had changed. LIE!  My sister had a similar story this week. Same as my experience a MONTH ago.  The just don't seem to care. Last restaurant I gave a bad review ro was Bobby's Burgers nearby. Then they closed. I am hoping Q will follow suit and be replaced by a customer and profit oriented business. 

Chipotle is a block away and their online ordering is easy and the pickup was pleasant. No brainer. Deleted my Q app. The customer rewards points never seemed to work out for me anyway. Free chips. Who wants that? Not me. I used to ho for tacos etc. Chipotle is better. 

Customer service at 40th st in PHILLY and at Q corporate SUCKS
Went to the drive thru and got some fries, because I was craving for it. Overall it was an okay experience. Nothing special.

Stopped in Naf Naf Grill in the late afternoon, & was given speedy & friendly service. The young lady who waited on me was cheerful & competently & correctly filled the 2 falafel sandwiches that I ordered. Also, she & her 2 colleagues were masked & wearing plastic gloves during the preparation. 

As for the food-the pita bread was fluffy, the falafel balls were crispy on the outside, & the additions of chopped salad, pickles, onions, tahini & harissa sauces made for moist & flavorful sandwiches. The Naf fries were like a thin potato chip. I liked the thinness of them because I didn't feel over-stuffed eating them alongside the sandwich. Lastly, the walnut & pistachio baklava were an adequate size for a manageable dessert. Most of the honey was on the bottom & didn't overwhelm it in stickiness.
Glad this Naf Naf Grill exists in this location.
The boneless chicken tenders are better than you'd think and the sauce was packed full of flavor. Will definitely come here again. 5 Stars

Always super quick, but taste wasn't great. I got a JJBLT and customized the heck out of it to add extra flavors and seasoning, but it still just tasted like watery lettuce and fatty, weird bacon. Got the giant too, which was new but just an extra few inches of meh. Good for a quick bite with crunchy veg, but you need to put cheese on it for it to have any real flavor at all. 

Came back for a JJBLT near closing time and found some super friendly staff that put some extra love into my giant sandwich for me. It was loaded and lasted me 2.5 meals, which made me happy! So bumping it up a star because I enjoyed it!
Bad customer service. Unfriendly employment. Very rude, would not recommend to a friend. 10 thumbs down.

These burritos are interesting and different. I like them, but I don't crave them all the time. They aren't really "sushi" in that you aren't getting raw fish inside or anything. Their filling options are along the lines of chicken katsu, crab stick, and shrimp tempura. Their spicy mayo is soooo spicy, so beware. I've had their bowl option, didn't like it as much as the burrito. The inside is very small, so plan on taking it to go for sure. Different option for lunch, cool but nothing absolutely amazing.

If you've ever walked past here on any given weekday, you'll see a long line within the store, sometimes it's out the door. Why? They have a solid product. But honestly, I don't mess with that line. Use the app! Plus you get points towards rewards, especially on Wednesdays: double points days.

I usually go with either a hummus or a rice bowl. The hummus bowl doesn't look like much, but more often than not, I have a tough time finishing it. The hummus is delicious, very creamy, flavorful. I prefer the chicken over the steak, which as other yelpers have said seems to be on the dry side. Gotta get the green s'khug sauce for a nice hit of spice. (It's the green one). For you thrill seekers, get the harissa (red) hot sauce and be prepared with a bucket or water or milk to dump all over yourself too cool your tongue and the rest of your body down from that mistake you just made. The falafel is also nice. Crispy on the outside, moist and not dry on the inside. Important. 

I don't even like lentils and their lentil soup made me a believer in it. So if you're not super hungry, you can get the lentil soup and an order of the fries, which are more like hearty potato chips and you're set. Don't forget the pita, which does taste what you would imagine a cloud tastes like.

Okay. This establishment definitely needs some work. It is very dirty inside and the staff doesn't have the best attitude. The saving grace for them is the seating inside. There is plenty of it.
The drive thru is usually always packed which sucks because the way the parking lot/drive thru is laid out, if you park to eat inside and then the drive thru gets packed. You're kind of trapped in your parking spot until someone gives you enough space to pull out.

It's nice to have your choice of Taco Bell or KFC. That's an upside.

I feel bad because the place got remodeled at least 1-2 years ago and it's nice, but I feel like they should just train the staff better or hire people that actually do care about customer satisfaction.

What's nice is that you feel somewhat safe in the area because this specific Taco Bell/KFC is across the street from the police district.

This is thee worst at making burgers or chicken sandwiches that don't look anything like they advertise it to be. The artisan craft sandwiches look sooooo appealing. But when you get your burger it's so disappointing. They give you a nice burger without any of the other ingredients like: Barbeque sauce or the crispy onions. They turn a great advertised burger into a great disappointing moment. I don't think the owners even care.

I've lived in this area well over 50 years. I've patronized this McDonald's quite frequently. I've seen this location go through many store & management changes, some good some not so good. I am always amazed when I visit certain locations (predominantly different nationalities) the service (majority of times) seems to be so efficient, the food fresh, customer service so much more accommodating. 
I would love to know who owns this particular location. For quite some time the drive through has been questionable of the last (at least) six months the menu board looks as though a hurricane hit it. It is coming apart & not well lit. There have been so many times when the drive thru ordering box has been out of service, so the orders were taken at the first window. My last experience on Thursday was the worse, I've been seeing these wonderful commercials on "McDonald's" crisp French fries & hot , fresh juicy quarter pounder, NONE of which was the case!!! I didn't order the meal (I didn't need to pay the extra soda tax, only in Philly) so my meal was a la cart, my large french fries alone was.$3.46 normally I wouldn't complain, but the container was not full & the fries were not crisp...reheated, just limp.The roll on the quarter pounder was dry & hard. When I tried to take the bun off the burger,  it just broke off fell apart. I spent $14.00 on a horrible fast food meal. The sad part of this is, people are trying
to support the local businesses & restaurants (due to Covid 19) but it's becoming increasingly impossible due to up charging of prices, lack of quality in food & the horrible customer service. What makes it worse is no one takes responsibility for any of the above, the owners hide behind the pandemic. Here's the big kicker this lack of quality in McDonald's is only displayed in disparities areas!!! McDonald's Corpooration should be ashamed!!!'

The staff at subway at 9th chestnut are wonderful and friendly when they see my face the ladies there already know my two go to sandwiches veggie patty and egg white foot long on wheat yes im a regular.
Thank you ladies so such quality customer service. Bridgette and Uncle Joe
Fast and good. Mac and cheese didn't look too good but was tasty

The....the manager yelled at me. Haha. I asked for a burger with no cheese. I sat down, looked at the box, and the box was marked no cheese. When I opened the container, I saw the burger had cheese. So I went back up and asked for a new burger.

The manager came over and said "No, theres no cheese on it." I showed him the cheese....and he said I was wrong!! Haha. I was so confused as the girl at the counter just told the manager "Please dont fight with him, I already made a new burger".

Besides that and the overflowing trash cans, this meal was a real let down....as much as a Burger King meal can be.

A really good idea that falls short in execution, Hai Street Kitchen & Co will attract customers based on novelty alone, but some may come out disappointed.

It was only a matter of time before the build-your-own fast food came to sushi...right? Well ready or not, here comes Hai Street Kitchen, offering sushi options in a roll, bowl, or salad. I've been hearing about this place for a while, and the novelty was worth a visit. I opted for the classic roll, with white rice, salmon, spicy mayo, and spring mix. You get exactly what is advertised - it's a sushi burrito/roll, beautiful to look at and a marvel to behold. You bring it to your mouth, take a bite and....

...the whole thing falls apart. The problem with the sushi roll is, it's not really meant to be bitten into piece-by-piece, and I ended up with the majority of the roll on my plate. The other major problem is the cuts of raw fish are too large; biting into them usually results in the whole piece coming out of the roll, and honestly a large piece of raw fish feels weird in your mouth (which is why it's cut so small to begin with). Don't get me wrong - the ingredients were fresh and the components were tasty, but the actual execution fell far short of expectations. 

I think the best option is to stick with the bowl or salad rather than the roll. It's a solid lunch spot and a cool thing to introduce friends to, but there's not enough here for me for many repeat visits.

I am a fan of the food, the convenience, and the speed, and the value! This place gets super-busy at lunch, and the servers aren't always the friendliest! However, they get slammed and they do their jobs in a professional manner. 
You can't go wrong with a large burrito the size of your head... it either fills me up for the day, or I bring the leftovers home for dinner!

My boyfriend and I came probably right during the lunch rush, but the staff was quick and efficient with preparing our food. There is very minimal seating, but the style of food does lend itself to on the go eating. But we managed to snag a table to chow down. And now the food. THE FOOD. Holy moly I can not tell you enough how wonderful the sushi burritos are!! Like hot damn. Everything was so flavorful and seasoned to perfection. I had the tuna burrito while boyfriend had the salmon. Both were absolutely phenomenal. I could not stop gushing at how yummy it was even while I was still munching on my burrito. I could have eaten two more burritos purely for the flavors and taste alone. Though one burrito left me feeling satisfied, which sometimes is not the case with sushi rolls, but the burrito was the perfect size. The price is to be expected, it's fresh, wonderful fish. But it's a nice treat! Would not be able to afford this on the regular, but you get what you pay for. The food here is exceptional and everyone should give it a try at least once! I will definitely be returning!

Way too expensive for what you get. Just order a few sushi rolls elsewhere. 

My sushi burrito was huge, but it only had two pieces of shrimp. They are packed full of rice.

Today ,I ordered 2 chicken sandwich meals with a beverage and a side. I come home and look in my bag and my chicken sandwiches aren't even there. UNACCEPTABLE RIGHT!!!!!So now , I called them about 13 times now, and apparently, their mailbox is full. NEVER AGAIN!!!!

Sushi burritos might seem like an Instagram gimmick, but Hai Street is more than just a foodie fad. Similar to Chipotle, you are able to choose your own ingredients - starting off with white or brown rice and ending with toppings such as tempura flakes. Unlike Chipotle, I did not feel excessively full afterwards - so pretty guilt-free in my opinion. 

Note: you should set the same expectations as you do at Chipotle. Chipotle does not count as authentic Mexican food, so Hai Street should not count as authentic Japanese sushi.

We ordered the Hai Street Chicken and Slammin' Salmon. Both rolls respectively had their own unique flavor to them. The Hai Street Chicken had well-done chicken katsu drizzle with teriyaki sauce mixed with a bunch of red onions. The Slammin Salmon is on the spicier end, a tiny bit much for my taste, but was still fresh and filling. 

The customer service here is also fantastic. The cashier accidentally missed my order of hibiscus tea (which was 99 cents the night I came) and gave me a free one without hesitating. While the tea wasn't memorable, the gesture definitely was.  

Also, any establishment that has Drake's Come Thru on their playlist definitely comes through in my book.

Not gonna lie, I dont understand the rave. I love sushi and I love burritos, but the two should stay separate. I really don't see anything great about mixing the two and I've always been disappointed in my food here.

"How do you do this to food?"

"It's magic."

How do you make it taste so extraordinarily good? 

Genius. 

Like its namesake Buckminster Fuller (do yourself a favor and Google him before you go), pure genius. Like all genius, somewhat idiosyncratic and delightfully unique. 

I'm going to name check the squid, the broccoli, the cauliflower (get both cruciforms at their apotheosis), the Masaman curry, the muthaf*ckin chicken Marsala--ask about the sauce--ingenious. Washed down with house lavender gin & tonics. Get the hay-infused flan because, hey, when's the last time you had something with hay? It was my first time and it made me feel like I was grass feed and free range. 

Genius + Love = Buckminster 

Clearly, there is love in that kitchen and it goes into the food. I feel like I've been ravished by a new lover.

I'm not sure how you could ever go wrong with burrito sized sushi. The line moved fairly quickly. I was not too impressed with the chimichurri sauce, which was too oily to really stay in my roll and made a mess.
Couldn't tell you the last time I went and they didn't just forget to put an item in the bag and/or not give any sauce

I prefer toasted sandwiches, but somehow I can't get enough of Jimmy John's veggie club (no sprouts or tomatoes).
The mayo is a good addition, love that guac spread, and the bread.. THE BREAD. Having good bread that can stand on it's own is not an easy feat in the hoagie and cheesesteak capital of the world.
I ordered cod burger, it looks so good in the picture but this what they've given to me after request like in the picture, poor!!

The wings look like they were made from starving chickens. The. Smallest. Wings. Ever. In addition when I entered the place there was a bunch of black women with tattoos standing around the counter having a personal conversation with one another. Then a homosexual male came in, turned around so his backside was facing in my direction, and halfway bent over near the front of the counter.

One word describes this establishment: Ghetto.
Get it together guys. Order was placed for pickup through the app and then was told the order didn't exist. Wasted 30 minutes for nothing.

Always a hit.  I was visiting in the hospital and they were located a few blocks away.  I ordered and my sandwich was delivered "freaky fast" "freaky fresh"!!  I love Jimmy John's.  I always order the regular Turkey Tom with extra meat and peppers.  I love the peppers.  They make the sandwich!!

They can't get an order right to save their lives in there. I went there a couple of Friday's ago, went to the drive-thru on my way to work around 5:30pm. Ordered three items:two tacos and the pulled pork sandwich. After I paid I was asked by the cashier to pull around to the front and they'd bring my food out to me. I did and they brought my order out. When I got my break at work I took out what was supposed to be the pork sandwich, unwrapped it, no pork sandwich. Instead they gave me a dollar menu burger that was on a stake bun. So I payed $10 for $3 worth of food. Called there several times over several days and nobody answered, the number is a 917 area code. Called corporate and still haven't heard from anyone to resolve the issue. Customer service at Burger King sucks all around from corporate all the way down to their cashiers.

After a night . .of dancing the night away at a near by club, YOU DANG RIGHT IM HUNGRY. I was literally looking up places to eat in the club LOL. This place happened to be open late so it was great that it was walking distance. 

Walked in and low and behold, a line. I mean, it is 2am we are all hungry. While in line a couple things happened: 
1) I noticed the decor. It was really nice 
2) Someone pulled the fire alarm and as adults, we learn not to panic over fire alarms like we did in grade school .. so we all just stood there LOL and continued to wait in line. Let's say the fire alarm was on for my whole duration of waiting in line and it made it hard to hear when taking my order. While waiting in line, we saw that there was a to-go / catering menu on the side, so we read that to figure out what we wanted. 

From what I observed, write your name on the box and your order. When it was my turn to scream my order across the counter :)) .. I ended up ordering the Fried Chicken Salad. To my surprise, I was . .. surprised with freaking anchovies in my salad. I was so confused, but it was apart of it on the menu. An every day person would not know what the heck a boquerones is. Well it's freaking anchovies. So whatever, I was hungry and just took the anchovies out. It just ruined my mood finishing that salad because I had to fish through it to make sure I wasn't eating anything crazy. 

As I was waiting in line, I also discovered that the mac and cheese was a staple item of this restaurant. My friends and I were excited to try it. Come to find out, my vegan friend couldn't partake in the fun activity of trying it because Wishbone includes chicken sausage. It was kinda upsetting because he had to get something else and there wasn't a lot of vegan opportunities. He ended up grabbing potato salad (which he wasn't a fan of. He said it seemed as if they added too much of a mustard base). He also had the biscuit that was talked about also. However, he said it was a little dry. He wishes that he got the french fries. That's always safe right?

My other friend also ordered a salad, but his didn't have the surprise factor that I had with my food. He also was annoyed at the fact that he had to wait like 15 minutes AFTER He ordered and paid for his food because the cashier didn't believe that he paid for it .. when that same cashier rang him up. A mess.

The tenders that were on top of my salad were okay. Nothing really special. I feel like this place is popping because it's one of the only places that is open so late at night. It is also crazy that you have to pay by the pound. Since the chicken wasn't heavily seasoned, they do push and promote you to buy the different dipping sauces that they have available.

I visited the store today to order one of the lifestyle bowls that have been heavily advertised. In the store there is a large sign also advertising for the lifestyle bowls. However when I actually went to order no one in the store  knew what I was talking about. They had never heard of the bowls even though they are on the in store sign   Their suggestion was that next time I go on the app and tell  them how to make it. I would have understood if they said that they don't offer it Aaron that location but for them to have no idea abouT an item they they are advertising is insane. If you're going to offer an item may e you should tell your workers abut it in case someone tries to order it.

honey glazed chicken wings!!!! I think probably one of the best I have ever had!!! From the second I saw these wings which sat innocently in a tray behind a glass partition my mouth immediately started salivating. Next my patience began to wear extremely thin as I had to wait for this obese woman in front of me to make up her mind as to what she wanted to eat. Finally after what seemed like an eternity (probably like 5 min) I finally got to order my wings! They were everything I had built them up to be and then some. The sugar in the honey had burned to the already crunchy skin during their cooking process giving it that extra crunch. The inside was cooked fully and still juicy and full of flavor. I think I can safely say out of the 5 or 6 places I tried in this place this was hands down the best. I would just like to emphasize that this review is solely based on their wings and nothing else, sadly nothing else seemed too appealing.

I take this route when coming back to Delco from visiting family or hanging out in Philadelphia.  Checkers always stands out because they are open very late. With that being said this is Island Avenue and the place is kind of shabby! For the most part the workers at the drive-through window are very nice and helpful, not all, but some. 

I usually stop here after going to the movies or the theater and looking for something sweet. OK, it's not your mom's bakery or Ben and Jerry's ice cream but you will find cheap warm apple pie's and ice cream cones.  They offer a nice size dollar ice cream cone, vanilla, chocolate or swirl. My sons like the bacon cheeseburger, It's cheap and to them it has a good taste. I'll pass!

Yes expect cheap food that tastes fairly decent do not look for ambience or great service!

So three of my last ten reviews have involved Burritos. I guess everyone knows what food has been on my mind of late!

It took two years of walking by them, but my curiosity towards Qdoba has finally got the better of me to the point that I finally gave in and hit up another fast food joint. And all I can really say is Holy McBurrito! It definitely delivered on size and had I anticipated that I probably wouldn't have added on those chips (of course I probably didn't have to add sour cream and guacamole onto a burrito that already had a three cheese sauce.
