But sometimes I'm a Homer at heart!). but with rice, pinto beans chicken, and everything else that I chose to add on it was worth that inevitable run to the bathroom that I'm probably going to make later. And I liked that they hooked up soda refills and had plenty of Tabasco and hot sauce for each table.

But overall it is assembly line production style fast food with all of it's strengths and weaknesses visibly present. And it would also be better if they had different tortilla options. So over all while it's a significantly better representative, it still is part of the Fast Food Nation.

One of the best brunches I've had lately,  and I'm an aggressive bruncher. I definitely left Buckminster's fuller.

We basically had the place to ourselves at 11:30am on a Saturday and service was great. John, our server took good care of us and the bartender checked in to make sure my friend's Yellow Mary (a play on a Bloody, with yellow tomatoes) was ok when she was drinking it slowly. They serve Rival Bros coffee and have a few interesting looking brunch cocktails.

The vibe (and clientele and staff for that matter) is hipster enough that the food is really good (but a bit pricey) but not too much to make you feel uncomfortable. There are a few tables in the front,  booth and tables in the back and a long bar with stools in the middle.

BRUNCH ITEMS YOU MUST TRY:
-Congee: a rice porridge with a soft boiled egg and seriously awesome flavors. I love congee but haven't seen it outside of Chinatown and my family reunions,  and was very impressed they pulled it off.
-Bologna sandwich: the cranberry mostarda perfectly smothers the baloney,  cheese and house made bread, and once that yolk splits into that you're going to want (need) to lick your plate.
-White Bean Mole with Eggs and Sour Cream: kind of a play on shakshoukka and extremely delicious.  Another plate licker.
-Biscuit- we got two, to facilitate sauce sopping. No regrets.

Don't rely on the online menu,  it varies slightly from the actual menu, which can be alarming if you're the type of control freak that needs to have a good sense of what she's going to order before she walks into a place. 

Will definitely have to come back for dinner/drinks! Highly recommend for brunch.

If you read my review on VERTS, you'll know that I'm a big fan of those place, at least relative to its most recent competitor. Naf Naf is a welcomed addition to Center City Lunch Rotation. It hits most of the essentials of a good luck spot: tasty, fast, decent portions and affordable although there are times where tasty falls short. For the most part, everything is fresh and it is busy enough during the week day that there is rotation through all of the food. They even give you a pita which is awesome because it's made in house and extremely tender and soft. I tend to go with a rice bowl with either chicken or steak, two falafels (which are typically very fresh and sometimes made-to-order) all the veggies and the harissa and garlic sauce. I usually ask for a sauce to try on the side because I'm fat like that. All in all, a welcomed addition to Center City.
The worst TACO BELL I've seen, as a food delivery you have to wait for an hour to get your order, the manager is terrible too

Should probably lose half a star for being so hard to find on yelp. 

Still not sure what the theme for this place is. Hot dogs? Bbq chicken? Who knows? All the food on display looks ridiculously good. That being said the food is only acceptable. This is unfortunate because reading terminal has so much to offer that I wouldn't waste a trip with this joint. 

Had Mac n cheese, cabbage and the BBQ chicken. The BBQ chicken looked fantastic but was totally bland. No BBQ, smoke, salt at all but it was well cooked. The mac was okay. Tasted sugary for some reason. The cabbage was probably the best of the bunch. 

I'm from the south though so maybe this style suits the local palettes. Definitely too bland for my taste though. 

Service was quite slow for scooping out food from under a heat lamp. Food is acceptable if you absolutely cannot wait at any other reading joint. But hell, they're slow enough that you could just wait in the dinics line.

Extremely slow service. Then they never apologize for being slow. Should not take 15 minutes in a drive through. They are not customer service friendly at all wish I didn't even have to give them one star

I love sushi and the idea of a huge sushi burrito makes me want to jump up and down in excitement! I finally got to try it the other day and I think my expectations were just too high. I just wanted it to be so much more than it was.. but I will say that I did like it and it is a good lunch option to change things up once in a while. 

They have pre-made combos or you can make your own. i was a little overwhelmed by the make your own option and stuck with one of the more popular choices- the Slammin' Salmon. When I asked what the difference in sizes was, I was told the godzilla was the same size, but just had more protein. Since the standard size was already over 10 dollars, I opted to forgo the extra salmon. You can choose white or brown rice for any of the rolls. I thought the burrito was filling and the ingredients were fresh. The rice was a mess and I couldn't quite figure out how to eat it without having rice and veggies falling everywhere, but I guess that's part of the experience? The sauce was good, but definitely not spicy. I would have liked more of a kick. The veggies were good, but again I just was a bit underwhelmed. For the price and the concept, this should just be better. I would try it again just because I think it's different and fun. Maybe next time I'll make my own!

Food ordered on grubhub marked "ready for pickup" 5 minutes after scheduled pickup time and hadn't even been started being made yet. 40 minutes after scheduled pickup time (not when I ordered- when it was scheduled to be picked up), food was ready.

8/9/16 update Ok, all the stuff I said below is still mosty true, but I'm SUPER bummed that they got rid of their mushroom option (or any vegetarian "main" item altogether!) I went for lunch and bailed. Please consider adding tofu or mushrooms or anything to make this more of a veg friendly meal. Thanks! 
_______________________________________

I think that Sushi Burritos might be my new favorite food! Ok, if you've yet to partake in this glorious food mash-up, its exactly what it sounds like-Its a sushi roll, but huge. You can get the standard size or the larger "Go Zilla" (strategically named to keep Toho's lawyers of their back) I got the Standard which was more than enough for one person, though on the right day I could probably eat the larger one. 

I also got the green tea which was unfortunately sweetened, but I was pleased to find that it was a very mild sweet flavor, and not sickeningly so. (I'd still prefer an unsweetened version if they offered it) There are a number of pre-set items, but I went for the create your own with the tempura portabella mushroom. Not bad as veggie sushi options go. It was crunchy and tasty without being greasy or heavy. A word of advice, its easy to tack on up-sell charges here. I can't imagine a veggie sushi roll without some kind of avocado in it, so this added $2 to my total right off the bat. My $9 roll became a $12 roll in no time. 

As for the atmosphere, I wish they had better seating options (We actually took our sushi-ritos across the street to Liberty Place and sat in the food court to eat-not the best setting, but at least we could relax a bit and talk.) They do have a few high top barstools, but its not the kind of place I could see sitting down with a friend to chat. That's fine, just know it going in that its more of a takeout spot. All in all, I loved my food. The line was long, but it went quick, and the meal it was filling without being heavy. When you're looking for "something different" this could be the spot for you!  I'll definitely be back!
Cool concept but it honestly isnt that good.  Plus the staff cant handle a little lunch pressure.  I wont go there again.

Always a good experience here!
Although the lunch line looks intimidating, they try their best to be quick.
You can choose to have your sushi in a bowl or burrito roll. I usually prefer the roll option. It's more like a huge sushi roll, as opposed to being wrapped like a burrito. Nonetheless, it's unique and fun!
-veggies are crispy, clean and fresh
-the tuna was spicy and yummy
I got the spicy tuna tartare sushi roll with brown rice, cucumber, jicama (yellow pickled radish - I think ?- that has a pear texture), & carrot with a tempura crunch. Since the spicy tuna a least had a marinated sauce that tastes like gochujang, you don't need to add extra sauce.
It was the perfect midday snack !

0 stars.  Worst take out in the city.workers never get the food right.  Every single time I go there my order is wrong no lie everytime.  I order add beans on my taco and never get the beans that I pay for

I have been to the Chicago location so I was really excited to have a Naf Naf close by! It was delicious! I had the hummus base, falafel, with salad, cabbage, garlic and hot sauce. I remember the hot sauce being spicier and wished the pita was warm, that was the only thing lacking. The falafel themselves were yummy. I cannot wait to go back!
If you want to spend 10 minutes waiting in line at the drive through only to spend 10 more waiting at the window, save yourself the time and don't go here.

I've been wanting to try a sushi burrito for some time now and this place did not disappoint. The burritos were an ample size and quite filling. Since it was our first time, my boyfriend and I ordered the Hai street chicken roll and the Crunch roll (shrimp tempura) from their signature rolls. You can customize it and make your own like at a Chipotle. Ingredients were fresh and burritos are loaded up with different veggies making me feel like this was a healthier meal. The girl that made my burrito was fast and knew what she was doing but the employees there weren't that friendly or welcoming. Nice packaging, the eating part does get a bit messy especially once you get to the end of the burrito and everything starts falling out especially the rice and the shredded lettuce. The lettuce and the fried tempura gave the burrito a nice crunch but the lettuce ratio was pretty big. Sauces were tasty which made soy sauce not even necessary.

positives: recently opened with clean pleasant interior.

negatives: generally apathetic staff after the first month passed. food options slightly less then what Ive experienced at other pandas.
management/staffs policy must be to stop making any new food several hours before close. 
have come by multiple times 45min to 1 hr before close to find only a quarter of the food options available, and whats left is dried out and old (see photos from 2 different days). meanwhile the staff is already cleaning kitchen and trying to leave asap.

if you're going to say you're open try to be professional about it

We ordered online from Wishbone for lunch today. Within minutes I get a call from them saying that my orders ready! Wow! Good thing I was already walking there. I also had no idea they sold alcohol btw - until i got to the restauran. As soon as you walk in there's multiple fridges with 6-packs of craft beer. There were also signs for cocktail options, which all looked yummy. My boyfriend got the Nashville Hot Chicken sandwich and I got the Wishboner chicken sandwich. Both were really good. I'm not a pickles person but surprisingly I loved the pickles they put in the sandwiches. We also got the Legendary Mac n Cheese and Chicken Tenders - both were ok. I expected the macncheese to be creamier... and the tenders were kind of dry. Overall, not a bad place for a quick bite. Normally they're open pretty late (for late night munchies), but due to covid I believe the hours are cut down.
HHHHHHHHHHHMMMMMMMM Biscuits, chicken, mashed potatoes n gravy are yum yum my lips are just watering thinking about it :-)
Ordered through Door Dash. Half my food wasn't there and when my wife called up to get a response they lied about the order. Will never buy from them again. Thank god Door Dash refunded me
Ordered a bacon egg and cheese on glazed donut for delivery. Holy shit it was good. Pretty slow with delivery, but its worth it.

I'm calling corporate on this location because this is ridiculous. This is not the first time that I had worse service than normal shitty service. But when I get 4 order that have no beef in them I've had it. Only reason we did not drive back is because this was our hangover food. So our motivation to go back was lacking. 
Do not go to harbison taco bell/KFC.

I read about the concept in a magazine and thought it was really cool.  I decided to stop in for lunch this afternoon.  The place is very small and mostly take out with a small counter on the wall for the people that want to eat inside.   I ordered the slammin salmon. It was loaded with spicy mayo sauce which I felt was a little too spicy and it tasted ok.  Its a lot of sushi in one bite and I immediately decided if rather have a regular spicy salmon roll somewhere else instead.  This did not taste better than a regular sushi. My sister ordered the shrimp tempura roll. Same thing..:: it was very thick and loaded with add-one like lettuce and vegetables and only had 2 fried shrimp inside where you almost cant taste it. It was also very spicy.  The concept was cool before l actually tried it.   My overall experience wasnt horrible but it was just ok.  I dont regret giving it a try but im sticking to regular sushi.

Was looking to get late night BK and phew, was I disappointed in how this place has gone down hill. No lights on the drive-thru menu, no numbers 1-5 or 7 or onion rings, AND when I ordered a chicken sandwich and fries with zesty sauce, THEY FORGOT THE ZESTY SAUCE. Not sure how this place is still open, honestly.

Been here a few times since I work on the next block over. I generally think that the food is good and flavorful. However, this last time was enough to make me not go back. The chicken in my bowl was fatty and not great.  A couple of weeks ago, I tried the other new similar place nearby, and thought Naf Naf's chicken was better. But, similar to that place, one bad batch of chicken is enough.  The only reason I gave it 3 stars was because my prior times were not this bad and their pickles are good.

I think the sushi burrito roll is a little overrated. I went to hai street kitchen to see what the hype was about. I love sushi and was excited to try the slammin salmon roll. I went here with my boyfriend, he got the chicken katsu roll. I found that the rolls were unconventionally useless, they could not stay together when eating it and we both made a huge mess. There is also very limited seating. I went to order something to drink and all they had was 4$ boxed water so I ended up spending 30$ on sushi rolls and boxed water. Overall I do not think I will be coming back. Its over priced, and I would recommend getting the sushi bowl.
Guinness book should come here to set the record for the worst McDonald's in existence.

Came into Panda on Market Street shortly after 1pm on Thursday and most of the woks were empty or near empty. They tell you it will be 5 minutes before they are done cooking. The problem is that might be one for one specific item. This is not just a problem with this Panda, it's with most of them. They will tell you this way they keep the food fresh. Have you ever seen Panda dump a full or mostly full wok because it has been sitting there a while. Also if a wok is near empty that is the portion you are getting even though you pay full price. They have been open long enough to gauge how much they are going to serve around lunch time. I know the items I want I'm not taking substitutes. The only time to visit Panda is right after they open for lunch. Never seen other food franchises operate like this where you can only come in right when they open or be disappointed.
The absolute very worst one. It's pretty hard for the staff to get your order right. the food is not that greatand the drink is watered down. I feel robbed.

I have nothing bad to say about the employees. I know they're trying their best during this time. I had the hardest time getting a refund for an order that I couldn't pick up because the doors were locked though.

I have a limited time for my lunch break, so I needed to grab food and go. The in store pickup option should not be available if the doors are going to be locked. I left without any food since the drive thru line here has always taken me 15-20 minutes to get through. Took me 2 weeks to get a refund. No response to my email. No gift card or anything for wasting my lunch break and me having to eat instant noodles for lunch that day.

Let's be clear - these are not "Japanese burritos", they are hand rolls the size of burritos. Don't expect a tortilla or beans of any sort. Also don't expect it to be all that authentically Japanese.

But these guys sure are tasty. Maybe not the best place for a sushi snob, but it gets the job done and provides some nice variety in the Center City lunch hunt. I split with a friend on free roll day and sampled both the Slammin' Salmon and the Sumo Steak. I preferred the salmon over the steak, though I'd recommend splitting with a friend like we did. You can choose either brown or white rice, placed on the nori with a sushi robot (which I clearly need to add to my kitchen appliance collection). There is a wide selection of sauces, toppings, and crunchy finishes (I really enjoyed the added crunch) that create some interesting and unique flavor combinations. There are also some super random things you can add in, like Philly cheese or roasted beets, but if you choose wisely, it can be quite good.

This will not fill you the same way a burrito will, and it will cost you the same or more ($7-$9 per roll). It's quite a unique concept to Philadelphia, and if they can find a way to make those lines move a little quicker (limited by the sushi robot speed), I'll be coming back.

How's that for simplicity? Ok, I'll elaborate -- if I'm craving fried chicken tenders, I'm heading to Wishbone. If I am craving anything else, I'm not heading to Wishbone. 

"Craft Fried Chicken" is the name of Wishbone's game. Does it deliver? Eh. They do fried chicken tenders well here. VERY well. Thick and juicy, with a unique pretzel-shell batter. You can get dark meat or white meat, and it's pretty inexpensive, at around $9/lb. Three of them fill me up pretty good and that costs like $6. But that's pretty much it. The ambiance and description kind of leaves you wanting a lot more. There are two sides, the mac-and-cheese and the biscuits. The biscuits are disappointing, the mac-and-cheese I've never had because it always looks kind of gross, like it's been sitting in the steamtray for days. The fries are okay, if a little limp.

Also, don't bother with the sauces. They're unremarkable (with the notable exception of the parmesan pesto one) and expensive. Take your chicken home naked and slother some Nando's sauce on it once you get home. If you don't know what Nando's is, google it, you're missing out.

Always wanted to try out the famous sushi burritos, but was always too conscious of my wallet for it. You'll be running around $9-10 a roll here($11-12 if you decide to supersize it). Came here with a visiting friend and, seeing as we were ready to splurge on someone elses budget(Thanks Uncle Ernie), decided to order 4 rolls Go' Zilla style. 

Slammin' Salmon: The best of what we got. Real sushi-grade salmon here, it did not disappoint. Add to it a spicy gochujang sauce which paired well with the cabbage and jicama, and you've got a winning roll.

Chili Citrus Pork: So i'm conflicted with this one. The pork was well marinated, and the go' zilla version actually came with a very generous portion of meat. That said, it's not really the sort of meat that synergizes with the nori wrap and sushi format in general; seems like it would be more at home in a regular burrito. Still good...but made me think that I could have really just had a traditional burrito instead of this sushi version.

Hai Street Chicken: Their form of Chicken Katsu. Black pepper sauce was alright, but lacked some of the more distinct hints of fruit and spices in other katsu sauces. Additionally the katsu could have been crispier, though they did give plenty of it.

The Crunch: I expected this to be my second favorite, but was actually a little bit disappointed. The shrimp tempura was not necessarily as crunch as I would have liked, and also overpowered by the rest of the vegetables in the wrap. I am a fan of the spicy mayo though.

Overall, I enjoyed most of the 'Burritos', but I'm not sure if I could justify paying that high price for what is essentially a large handroll. To be fair a quality handroll will be no cheaper, but in the case of the slammin' salmon the amount of fish left a bit to be desired. The Go' Zilla rolls weren't necessarily larger but just had more meat, and while that was quite noticeable for the hai street chicken and the chili citrus pork, it means that the traditional slammin' salmon and crunch must be rather skimpy(i thought the go' zilla versions of these should have been the normal). Also, for a place whose main sell is Sushi-style burritos, they offer barely any actual fish options. While I love salmon, there's room for variety and I expect some standby's like tuna and yellowtail on the normal menu.

Being from San Francisco, I've had the original Sushirrito- so I was delighted to find out they have this at Herald Square. Unfortunately, Hai Street Kitchen's version does not even compare. I finally got to try it today and was disappointed...emotionally and physically. 

I ordered the Slamming Slamon- it was mediocre. The way they rolled the sushi does not guarantee a satisfying bite every time- my first couple bites were blend.The salmon is served Tataki style, which means slightly cooked..eh didn't enjoy that. I would have preferred it to be raw. Rice and the seaweed were great. Personally, if you don't like crunchiness from vegetables, i would ask them to take out the pickled Jicama. It added nothing to the flavors in my opinion. My least favorite of the entire burrito would have been the sauce...YUCK, the spicyness of it took the idea of "freshness" out of the roll.

Overall, I gave it 2 stars because "Meh..I've experienced better." If you've never had one, I would encourage you to go try it. The packaging is great for an instagram photo! But overall just judging by that one roll I had---I wouldn't go back for a second roll.

Side note:
Bleh...I'm writing this while sitting on the toilet because my stomach has been acting up since I had it. I'm not blaming the quality of the sushi at all...but this is the only thing I had today and have been having on and off diarrhea for the past hour.....So.... :/

The young lady in the restaurant was very helpful, I just wasn't a fan of the food. The chicken taste like shake n bake and the biscuit was gross. The jalapeño cornbread was okay, I'll just choose another establishment when looking for chicken and mac and cheese

Sushi burrito? Of course! Why not!? This place wasn't bad. It was very filling. The burrito is huge! I shared mine with my toddler - we just got the california roll.

Their specialty rolls were very tasty also. We got the salmon roll and the shrimp tempura roll. I think for me, the ratio vs rice and the filling is important. So there was just a whole lot going on with the specialty rolls that I feel was a little overwhelming.

However, this place is pretty legit and has fresh ingredients so definitely give it a try. I think that when I go the next time, I will just make my own and opt not to have too many fillings inside the burrito.

Definitely A-OK in my book!

Chicken fingers were just oil bombs. The cornbread was sweet to the point that you could have marketed it as jalapeno cheddar cake. Lastly, the Mac and cheese was also very sweet. One vegetarian had a rather unpleasant surprise: the Mac and cheese contains chicken sausage which isn't listed on the sign.

Terrible. Quarter pounder had Hard bread like it was sitting in a warmer for hours a made hours before it was ordered 

Not the first time had this problem. Employees smoking weed on breaks in back. Won't go back.

Had to check why there's always consistently a long line here.  It does move pretty quickly and it did give me a chance to figure out what I wanted to order.  

I got the chicken shawarma on a pita.  The spicy sauce is pretty spicy so be forewarned.  I was definitely sweating afterwards.  I got the chips on the side, but it was definitely soggy and a waste of money.  

This is a high end middle eastern place, but I'm ok with the 500 other options on the street carts

The only quality I look for in a fast food restaurant is convenience and speed. This Wendy's is extremely slow (took 10 and 12 minutes on my 2 visits to get a small meal). Both times it seemed like 2-3 slow and lazy employees were standing around doing nothing with only 1 employee making the sandwiches. Management needs to do better.

So I decided to grab Wendy's on a Wednesday nite after work, I ordered the 2 for 5 deal with a spicy nugget and spicy chicken sandwich I also ordered a No 4 combo which is a big bacon classic large and an order of bacon jalapeño fries as well. The line wasn't too bad, the young lady that took my order wasn't pleasant/nice nor was she rude, I get it it's Wendy's you have lump them in w/McDonald's customer service/pleasantries go out the window as soon as step foot in the building or drive thru. I'd like to say my total was close to 20 dollars, I wasn't given a receipt and the reason for that is because they don't want you to go on-line and review the restaurant. I say all that to say this, this the 5th and last time won't deal with out being given a receipt ( scammer, double charge, or just plain old discrepancy with order such as this) I live about 10 mins away from this location so with a glance over the 3 bags I was given it appeared to be correct. Once I got home you already know where I'm headed with this. The 2 for 5 was incorrect and under counsel as wel. The chicken sandwich which was supposed to be spicy was a normal chicken patty without lettuce, the nuggets I was only given 6 it's a shame that I had too count but I did. The supposed big bacon classic combo was incorrect as well. People please understand the difference between the Jr bacon cheeseburger patty and a Dave's patty for a regular patty, I was a given a Jr bacon patty with no bacon or lettuce my jalapeño had little to cheese or no and I mean no jalapeno. There's no way to verify anything foodwise in the drive-thru. I wasn't able to verify a thing until I got home. Once I got home I threw the food away after realizing my order wasn't correct. Now I do understand that at these times there's a shortage as far as beef, change etc due to this Covid-19 ordeal but Please post signage or let customers know what's available versus what's not. I will google the location to find out the owner/general /district/regional manager are and let them know. Because this is just unacceptable these locations are fully aware of what the inventory is or isn't. Embarrassing point, blank period. If you read this review think twice before ordering anything from this location the overall staff isn't too be trusted. Please, please find a way to incorporate a kiosk to minimize the attitude and negativity of the workers ( i worked in fast food restaurants throughout HS and college with playing football and balancing scholastics you always have a choice gig/job/career wise) also to maximize the accuracy of the order, this staff clearly give little too no F's about any of the above.

This Popeyes is in a good location but the parking lot isn't the greatest. I've had issues with parking before but always manage to find a spot. I've never eaten inside and always take it to eat back at the apartment. My personal experience is a mixed review. The managers here are great! The entry level employees need a bit of work on being polite and professional to the customer. 

The last time I went in there which was on 3/23/15, I waited about five minutes in line and another three minutes for my food. I ordered an 11 piece meal half spicy and half regular. The manager even threw in an extra piece which I thought was very nice of him. The chicken tasted fresh and it did the trick for sure. I also ordered large sweet tea, it was good and would order it again. 

There are a decent amount of tables to sit at but I prefer to take my food home with me to be able to relax. I've had an issue before with "panhandlers" by the store but I ignore them. I've never used the drive-thru but there is one if you prefer it. The bathrooms are clean there from my personal experience. I just hope the employees there can be more professional to the customer.

I AM A VEGETARIAN. I will ever come here again. I was told that there were No vegetarian options. Yet my friend ordered a salad for me. And I paid for my own salad even though he paid for mine. So I deserve a refund for that. I will never go back to this place. I was treated very inappropriately by an African American woman with long hair, and another with short hair. When I asked for the simplest vegetarian option the woman at the register was the most helpful. The employees working the food told me that I couldn't eat anything on the menu. The woman at the register tonight deserves a raise.  She knew more about the menu than the women and man working the food. Regardless of her I will never return.  
Gay Pizza is more accommodating than this establishment. I'm sorry I wasted over an hour of my time here and left with a salad that still had meat in it.

positives: clean pleasant interior.

negatives: worst managed panda ive been to.
management/staffs policy must be to stop making any new food several hours before close. have come by multiple times 1 hr before close to find only a quarter of the food options available, and whats left is dried out and old (see photos from 2 different days). meanwhile the staff is already cleaning kitchen and trying to leave asap. last time I came 8 people in line with only 2-3 entrees available. they didn't even have rice left. 

if you're going to say you're open try to be professional about it

Food is very flavorful. Service is always friendly and fast. Free guac. Clean restaurant. Lots of seating always available. What's there to complain? 

I'm always satisfied after each visit and meal. :)

TERRIBLE SERVICE and the lady who answers calls on Friday night is a LIAR! I ordered delivery from wishbone on seamless - after an hour I called and the  lady said the food had been picked up. After 2 hours I called seamless and called her out and she said the driver didn't pick it up. 

Don't order from here. Go there in person if you're comfortable dealing with dumb people.

Drove by this place multiple times because I lived down the street . Anything that has to do with seafood will catch my attention . Anticipated for the day to be opened and they finally did . My boyfriend and I are both seafood lover . So after reviewing their menu online and noticed they serve lobster rolls I quickly told my boyfriend about it and the next day being today we went to go get some . We've ordered the traditional lobster rolls cold and warm and it was so delicious . It can get a little messy but why does it matter when the food is so good . To top that off , it was full of meat . We also ordered the seafood soup but I didn't like it too much . They also serve other things . So for all you seafood lover out there , you should definitely give this place a try . New edition in city and the their lobster rolls is delicious ! Very friendly staffs and service even though we did takeout .

The food is really good. I'm obsessed with the pita bread. It's so fluffy and soft. I find one bowl to be enough for 2 servings, so it's a bang for the buck. Will definitely be one of my go-to restaurants.

My qdoba app says I've beento qdoba at least 192 times. This location has been my least favorite, and the only one I've had trouble at. A

I was ordering a quesadilla and the manager took the quesadilla and pressed it before it got to the cold section where they ask if you want cilantro, jalapeños and other toppings. He acted surprised when I asked him to put on toppings after he cooked it. They also never asked if I wanted any sides, like sour cream and such like they have every other time I've been to a qdoba. 

I would go out of my way to go to the qdoba on temple.

Once in awhile, the stars align and bring two beautiful things together to create something magical. Just like Joe DiMaggio & Marilyn Monroe, Romeo & Juliet, Chrissy Teigen & John Legend, Neil Patick Harris & David Burtka, we have seen the magical convergence of sushi & burrito. All the fresh deliciousness of sushi wrapped into a burrito-sized roll. You can either customize your roll with a plethora of ingredients and sauces, or start off with one of the suggested menu items. My favorite being Screamin' Tuna. You have the option to "Go Zilla" making it big boy burrito. (Always go Zilla!) And you also have the options to make it a sushirrito bowl or salad (sans nori wrap). Endless combinations, endless possibilities. Now I can enjoy my favorite sushi ingredients in a fat handheld roll while walking, working, driving, kung fu fighting, etc. 

PS. Don't worry, I'm usually not driving. Or kung fuing one-handed.

I'm not the craziest fan of this trend, but I thought I'd give it another try since it's been almost 3 years since I've bothered.

Getting something the meshed with my tastes, I ordered the Hai Street Chicken. It was good, but definitely not enough protein for as much as it costs. It probably would have been a little more enjoyable as a bowl but I actually like the "sushi" feel more than the bowls, and since this is definitely seasoned like sushi rice, it would probably be a little weird.

Trend foods are weird, but if you're open to eating a giant sushi-style burrito thing, I guess it won't hurt to try it once.
Filthy and completely incompetent. No one here and going on 15 minutes waiting for nuggets and fries.
they don't identify the drinks, the bathrooms have them closed so that nobody uses them they have to leave it open I am buying there and eating and they don't let them use the bathrooms

I had the pleasure of trying what i'm calling a "japanito" which is a japanese take on the classic burrito. akin to a  sushi roll, the japanito consists of nori in in place of tortilla and is filled with white or brown  rice. You can get steak, panko fried chicken, or shrimp tempura and a couple of other choices i can't remember. I was with my girlfriend, i got a roll and a she got a salad bowl. I had the chicken and she had the steak. We split everything and so i got to try both. The roll was better than i was expecting. And the asparagus in that salad might have been the best asparagus i've ever eaten (seriously). the steak also had a black pepper sauce that is worth mentioning. this is a good addition to the center city lunch scene and i'm glad to have something different to eat. I'll definitely be back to get hai, man.

Decent and quick poke bowls, but not as much variety as other poke places that I've been to

Atmosphere: Casual, mostly a takeout place with a few seating areas. I haven't seen a long wait line yet, even though I have come in around popular lunch times. They generally move very quickly with making the poke bowls (5 minutes max).

Food: Pretty standard poke bowl; I'm happy with the portion sizes of tuna, salmon, and toppings that they give. My only complaints are that the bowl isn't super well blended between the vegetable base and the toppings, so you need to mix them yourself (or else just end up eating a lot of yummy protein at first, and then mouthfuls of spinach). There also isn't a huge variety of toppings - they have the basics (avocado, tomato, cucumber), but you can find these at all poke places, pretty much. There aren't toppings here that really make this spot stand out - for example, I love seaweed salad and masago as toppings, which aren't offered.

Overall:  - Overall average. The service is very quick and you get a standard poke bowl. I probably would prefer other poke spots nearby with a greater variety of toppings, but the low wait time is great for a quick lunch option.

Excited!!!! But ended up overwhelmed by the salt!!

Wing Stop is phenomenal from what I remember. The last time I had it before this was 2004 in College station , TX where I absolutely loved the wings there. I was driving by the area and saw Wing Stop so immediately had to stop, and wing it up!

I ordered 20 wings, flavors Hawaiian BBQ, garlic Parmesan, and lemon pepper wings PLUS small order of fries.


Now I will say the lemon pepper wings and the garlic Parmesan wings were just as good as I remember BUT the Parmesan was dumped on the wings. They could have toned it back a little. I was sitting in a place that I could see directly into their kitchen where my To-Go order was being prepped and the one girl making my wings just kept pouring on the seasoning.... That I was thinking "is this the normal amount?" 

I won't be getting the BBQ wings there cause I'm not a huge fan.... But also the fries were just ridiculously salty to where I couldn't finish them. I felt awful for not only not able to finish them and throwing them out, but awful from the ones I had with all that salt.... 

Overall.... The wings are cooked (fried) to a perfect platform for wings to be seasoned, but I think the seasoning this go-around was extremely excessive!

Upon entry (8/17) the place reeked of extermination/bug spray. After mulling over if I should eat there or not because of the smell I gave it a shot because I've been wanting Qdoba for so long. They had no brisket..uuugghh the portion was like a kids meal it was like the girl was giving me her food. I asked for black beans, so few I could count them (11) and  the whole bowl was tasteless super disappointing!

Wanting to try this place for awhile...Went on Friday lunch and it was crowded, Line long, but service was quick! I ordered a falafel sandwich and  authentic lentil soup. Like other restaurants of this nature, assembly line to make your food. They have shawarma and falafel sandwiches,  hummus bowls , couscous, rice or salad bowls along with extras like and fries, hummus, baba ghanoush, basmati rice and lentil soup. For my falafel, I had choices what to put in sandwich, toppings and sauces. I had the classic - cukes, cabbage, baba ghanoush and tahini sauce. For an extra $3.25, you can "Naf it up" and get fries, lentil soup, or basmati rice and fountain drink. I did Naf it up and had to have a Middle Eastern soup. Yes lentil soup was flavorful and falafel fillings made the sandwich very tasty , plus pita bread was fresh and they make on  premises. My meal was vegan and very satisfying. I plan on returning. Very yummy. NEXT TIME, BRINGING FRIENDS.

Burger king use to have great burgers got and cheeses. Now they are cold and taste awful. This is not just the Bensalem Burger King I am talking about either. All of them are awful I have stood in line for 45 minutes waiting to order while we were the only guests there. Employees are too busy screwing around and getting high. They don't give a crap about their customers and it's really sad because if they changed everything I would go back. Are used to love Burger King's burgers but it's always cold and I can't figure out why anything would be cold when were the only ones in there it should be fresh made it. They all have attitudes and are rude as hell. I hope Burger King gets it together because they're going to be taken over. If Chick-fil-A can get 100 people through the drive-through within the matter of minutes I'm sure they can handle one order in a timely fashion. It's such a disappointment in anymore. I hope somebody realizes it and gets it together because the whole business is going to go under.

I love chipotle but would avoid this location! This chipotle in Liberty Place did not have black beans ready during dinner hours, and had me wait over 15 minutes for the beans. When I asked if I could get additional protein to make up for the beans instead since they weren't ready, they said that it was not possible and that I would get charged extra. If it was just my order, I wouldn't have minded, but I was picking up order for someone else too so it put me in a difficult position. So I just had extra time to wait and write this review. While they were nice enough, I wish they could have been more accommodating somehow, given that they were not well prepared during dinner time. 

It's located in a good court, so would one hundred percent recommend picking one of the alternate options!

Do you like the idea of customized sushi rolls, in the style of Chipotle? Well if you do, then you will love this place. The ingredients are good and the sweet green tea is basically green tea ice cream in liquid form. The spicy tuna is my favorite "meat" option. Overall, the quality of the food here is great, but it's definitely squarely in the realm of Asian fusion. The sushi is about as authentically "Japanese" as The Karate Kid, but it's still a fun eating experience worth checking out.

P.S. Also... I know some people call it a sushi burrito but portions are on the small side. If you're hungry I recommend getting the rice bowl instead.

I don't get it, theres so much hype surrounding this place so I had my hopes up really high. I'm a big fan or hummus and rice bowls so I was naturally super excited for this. I'm also a fan of pita chip so if this was even close to similar it would be a winner in my eyes. I did an online order and went to pick it up. The place was really busy. Anyways, fast forward to when I actually tried my food. My chicken shawarma was dry and chewy. The hummus tastes like sabra store bought hummus and the whole bowl is wayyyyy too salty. I tried to distinguish it to a single item but it was really just the whole bowl. I felt like the sauces were thinner as well and I didn't taste any tahini and I honestly don't think they put any in my bowl. Honestly it was a salty mess. It's a solid no from me.

Ordered from uber eats, waited 67 minutes for our order to be wrong & burnt. Forgot my dorito taco, gave me nachos & cheese without the cheese, no sauces, there was also no sauce on my dry quesadilla, my fiancé's grilled cheese burrito was completely burnt on both sides. N e v e r A g a i n
Vegan options available. Extraordinarily satisfying falafel sandwich. Thank you Allah.

If you do Uber eats at this location most likely you won't get half your order I've tried twice and half my order wasn't received and food was cold or stale. The drive through is ok could be better but going inside to order the customer service is ridiculous their so rude and unprofessional.

I thought the sushi burrito was a pretty cool concept so I had to check this place out. And I was very happy that I did! 

We got the Crunch and the Mexicana. The burritos were pretty heavy but very flavorful. I was worried that there would be an overwhelming amount of rice, but no! It was a good balance between the filling and the rice. The Crunch was light and delicious. The Mexicana was more saucy but still very flavorful. The pork belly in the Mexicana is a must-have. It was extremely tender but it was sometimes difficult/messy to chew through. 

We also got the corn tempura which I really enjoyed! It's something that I could munch on all the time. There is seasoning that you can add more of, depending on how much of a kick you want. 

Definitely try this place out! But be prepared to eat it outside since there isn't much of a sitting area there.

When I first heard about nori burrito wraps I was definitely intrigued.  We stopped by to grab lunch before heading to the airport.  This location is quite small with limited seated and has no restroom.  Street parking only.

My hubby ordered the hai street chicken roll and I created my own roll which included brown rice, grilled chicken, cabbage, spring mix, carrots, papaya, ginger miso dressing & crispy shallots.  We also got the wasabi guac and chips. Overall, the food was tasty.  The ginger miso dressing is da bomb! The wasabi in the guacamole was not overwhelming, which is a good thing bc I'm not very fond of wasabi.  It's a little pricey, but worth a try. I will definitely be trying my hand at making nori burritos at home. Thanks for the inspiration!
Yum. V good. Would eat again. 10/10 thank u for the experience. This is a review. Not a tip.

While the thought of a sushi burrito might seem appealing to some, when we take a step back, it really is a gimmick.

That's not to say that the flavors aren't there, the rolls are great and a great way to have sushi in a portable form (temaki does a similar thing but you don't really see people walking down the street with a handroll...)

Overall a cool place, but I can't say that I've ever craved for their menu even when I was close by.

If someone brings it up as an idea for lunch, I probably will be game, but all in all, not an essential for sushi lovers.

The food is amazing but honestly these young African-American women working there are extremely rude. They need to be trained properly in customer service.  No smile no thank you nothing.  After I was done paying I asked her for a side of white sauce Instead of the cashier going to get it for me she told the worker who is already preparing somebody else's food to get it. Once the worker put the white sauce in the cup she didn't even pass it over to me She left it behind the counter as the other worker just kept walking by knowing that I was waiting there for it. I know she did this on purpose. It's just sad nowadays they hire these women that hate their jobs with no customer service and don't know how to represent a company properly. Wonder if they will ever get anywhere in life?

With how many fantastic local businesses we have in Philadelphia, when I tell you I've chosen to go to Panda Express a couple times now, it might come as a bit of a surprise. But honestly, sometimes the craving for greasy Chinese fast food just hits...

If you're looking for something quick and easy (and you're not concerned about eating healthy), this is your place to go. It is not authentic Chinese food -  their food is mass produced. From noodles and rice to chicken, beef and seafood dishes, the options are pretty impressive.

The staff at this location is nice and attentive. During my most recent visit, I had to wait about ten minutes for one of their chicken dishes to be prepared but usually the pans are always filled. 

The establishment is well kept and clean. With the amount of people they have going in and out, staff doesn't seem to skip a beat with keeping the place spick and span. 

I'm more than content with this location and feel it can definitely be used as a model for all of the other Panda Express sites!
HATE HATE HATE! They take forever and the people who work there are so rude. I see them treat every customer like they don't care. Worse Wendy's. I would do no stars if I could

Jimmy johns has never been my favorite but this particular location is AMAZING. bread, veggies and cookies always seem to be extremely fresh. The sandwiches come out fast and are reasonably priced. the Managers of this place know what they are doing and they take time to genuinely care about their customers and make things right!!! Will be the only jimmy johns I go to! woohoo!

Live in neighborhood gave them 3 chances. Each time they messed up a simple order. Cashiers don't know how to count or tried to keep my dollar change. And just slow unorganized.  Would never go back to this location.

Always super quick, but taste wasn't great. I got a JJBLT and customized the heck out of it to add extra flavors and seasoning, but it still just tasted like watery lettuce and fatty, weird bacon. Got the giant too, which was new but just an extra few inches of meh. Good for a quick bite with crunchy veg, but you need to put cheese on it for it to have any real flavor at all.

Beautifully remodeled place. I love the contemporary look and feel. Lady who took my order was very nice too. The only thing that I would suggest is to clean it up a little bit. The bathroom was dirty and window next to me was in stains too. Even though I got here in the morning the place looked like it was not cleaned after late evening huge crowds passed by. But people who work here are very nice and this is the most important to me.

Came to renew a reward for a free birthday cookie, and chips and salsa. Chips and salsa were great, chips were light and airy. Cookie was average; could improve upon presentation/wrapping as my critique. Most of the staff were friendly and pleasant.

Went four times, first time they were supposed to be open, but weren't. 2nd time they were out of what we wanted so we left. The 3rd time they were supposed to be open but weren't. 4th time I tried fish & chips. Seems pretty hard to mess that up, but nope. It was a really weird consistency and not good at all. For what we paid I really expected a lot more. If we didn't live as close as we do there's no way we would have kept trying it. The staff was also way more worried about talking to their friends/boyfriends than they were about helping us (both times). I have no idea how it has 4 stars, but his place won't last.

Came here for a quick bite. Nice fast casual style with a decent amount of seating. I thought I came here for the chicken but absolutely loved the Mac and cheese. They also have a nice soft drink selection. A little on the pricey side, but I would come again.

Well it was my first time having Popeyes, so I can only rate their chicken sandwich that people went crazy about. Well I will say it's pretty good, piece of chicken, couple pickles, mayo. I did not wanted to bother with getting sauces. I'm only rating sandwich, dine in was closed so cannot rate that. Well on timing I would say it was my first time so I probably should have waited where is said mobile pick up. So it took longer. To add if I were there for dine in the location not that clean, needs renovation for sure.

Do not order from here!!! Staff, Jose, is incompetent.  The food was disgusting and the customer service was beyond disbelief. When asked for a manger, Jose replied that there weren't any managers.  He was extremely rude and seemed very unconcerned about trying to resolve the issues we were having with our food. Try the other location.

We ordered from Wishbone last night on a complete whim. We had walked by over the weekend and tried the to-go cocktails (the bourbon blueberry one and the peach one) and both were super strong and tasty. 

Last night, we actually ordered dinner from a different chicken spot and our order was cancelled so by that point: we were HUNGRY and needed something quick. We thought of Wishbone because of the cocktails and ordered two sandwiches, some wings, and (I thought) cole slaw. Delivery estimate was 30 minutes but thankfully I think it only took 20 minutes since we're so close by.

The sandwiches were delicious. The bacon on my blt sandwich was perfect. The chicken was crispy. Bae liked the pickle game on his classic sandwich (the "wishboner," according to the box, lol). The wings were super crispy! I wasn't a fan of either of the sauces we tried - buffalo Bleu or the sweet chili sauce. Bae liked the chili one. I added some extra Bleu cheese we had to the buffalo Bleu sauce because I am weak and needed to tone it down. I thought we ordered Cole slaw, but we received potato salad. Bae doesn't eat potatoes so I tried it. It wasn't my jam (the potatoes weren't the star of the show with all the other greens and such going on), but it wasn't bad.

I would absolutely order sandwiches and cocktails or beers from Wishbone again. Out of all the local chicken sandwich spots in our immediate vicinity, these are the best in my opinion. I am a mac n cheese fiend so I will have to get that a try some time, too.

Thanks for coming through in a crunch (and with a crunch?) for us last night!

Just went to this place for the first time and was generally satisfied. I felt the food was rather basic in comparison to the many other vendors. The cashier was nice however other staff seem to be busy with administrative tasks. The prices are decent and they offer hot dogs, burgers, chicken and other sandwiches. I would go back however try something else.

Update: 
I'm baaack!  A couple of three maybe four classic pieces for a post happy hour two maybe three Grey Goose martinis moment with ma girrrl. Best damn chacken since I started Keto!
I skipped mac cheese and sauces, which looked appetizing and gobbled mine down naked. Yum yum give you some if I could! But I ate them all!! 
Fast food that's better than Fast Food in one of the more fun areas of the city. 
And the have beer!!

I had really high hopes because the food looked appetizing but it was a BIG let DOWN!

The young guy serving the food seemed a bit irritated and unfriendly. I ordered the chicken wing platter w/ two sides and a drink. The BBQ chicken wings was not good. Maybe ate two pieces. Mac & cheese...no comment. The string beans were okay.

It's disappointing when you visit the Reading terminal and miss out on good food.

I'm giving it 3 stars because the cashiers were really nice at the end.

this is a quick buffet of some comfort food located at reading terminal

depends how much stuff you get, but i got a good amount of food and it was $14
(2 meatballs, kielbasa, mashed potatoes, turkey, 2 chicken fingers, mac and cheese)

everything was pretty decent, hey this ain't a 5 star restaurant but it's good for a quick lunch at reading terminal

I decided to stop by today. I'm glad I did. I ended up getting the bbq chicken platter. I also ordered a lemonade. The chicken is well seasoned and moist. The green beans are juicy. What I could've done without was the roll. The lemonade is fresh and tasty. While waiting I got to hear someone sing from behind the counter. Free entertainment lol. I'll be back to try the cornbread next time.

Visited Tootsie's in the Reading Terminal Market at the recommendation of a friend. I tried I little bit of everything- fried chicken, ribs, red potatoes, mashed potatoes, Mac and cheese and cornbread. Prices are by the pound as I was pleased with what I received. The fried chicken was my favorite by far- love the seasoning. The mashed potatoes were a let down- I am pretty sure they were instant, which is a huge pet peeve of mine. The red potatoes were excellent- crispy outside, creamy inside and well seasoned. The Mac and cheese was fine, didn't knock my socks off. The ribs were okay. The cornbread was great and served as my breakfast the following morning.
I'm glad that I tried it, but not sure that I'll be back when there are so many other options.

Went through the drive threw and ordered a strawberry banana smoothie, large fries and an unsweetened ice tea. they gave me a smoothie that was about 3/4 full with full chunks of frozen strawberry and sweetened ice tea. I'd avoid this mcdonald's at ALL costs and I plan on never returning. Someone should get their workers to actually do their jobs
Food was great-- especially the mac and cheese and tenders! Everyone working here was also so kind and helpful

The absolute worst McDonalds around. Lines are always long (inside and drive-thru). They almost ALWAYS are out of something. Ice cream machine always down. They mess up your order most of the time. I stopped going to this location because it was too frustrating lol

Friendly staff, clean space, reasonable price. But frankly I guess I expected the food to be better..

The biscuit which was $2.25 a piece ( might be the only thing that's a bit over priced?) that was pretty dry.. does not taste like a real biscuit at all... Fried chicken strips are pretty good, but the breading is a bit much.. mac and cheese, which I had the highest hope for, is not as creamy, and too watery...

Might go in and try something else next time, the chili looks pretty good.
Ne service, everywhere is dirty. Employe doesnt understand a customer. Cant remember order.

I think I just ate cardboard bro. . Well the app wanted me to keep writing so, I guess I'll do it being that im not eating my food anyway. I paid $24 for stale fries and a cardboard burger. Took one bite and yeet the burger, fries is next..... sweet tea good tho....  overall, one star. Wish 0.5 was an option.

Top 3 things I like about Wishbone: 
1.Fried Chicken? Everybody got time fo'dat!
2.Like Chicken and Mac n Cheese, somethings are much better TOGETHER. 
3.BYOB. Enough said!

Pro Tip: Get the tasting menu they have: 1/2Ib Mac n Cheese + 1/2Ib Chicken + 1 Sauce + New Hope soda/or water. $11.00 
Regular Prices:
- Homemade Mac n Cheese 8.95/Ib.
- Chicken: Boneless, skinless, and buttermilk battered with pretzel crust (your choice of: Classic white, dark, or Wishbone wings) 8.95/Ib.
- Homemade dipping sauce (your choice of: Chipotle Lime Mayo-Yum!, Parmesan Pesto- not bad, Modern BBQ, Pommery Honey Mustard, Tamarind Sweet Chilli, Buffalo Bleu, and DONFIRE -Its advertised to be extremely hot! Each sauce is $0.50
- New Hope fountain soda. Not sure- but probably $2.00 or so.

They also offer:
- Sandwiches: $8.95 each. All Chicken- Of course!
- Salads: Also $8.95 each.
- Homemade sides: $2.75 each.
- Hand pies made with butter crust: $4.00 each. I've tried S'more(seasonal flavor,) didn't like it. 
- Bakery goods: $1.85-$2.85. Limited quantities. 
- Bottels: $2.95 including the "Cock Cola".

Few other things to know about Wishbone:
- Refrigerated beer cases: Available.
- Catering: Available.
- Delivery: Available.
- Service: Quick and friendly.
- Taste: Good. Forget KFC.
- Hours: Open from 11:00am to 4:00am Thursday through Saturday, and 11:00am to 10.00pm 10.00pm Sunday thru Wednesday.

Seriously. Who doesn't like fried chicken?
Four Yelps.

This Burger King I have come to since I was 12 years old so I made it a habit to try and bring my kids and I'm tell you this place has changed so much but for q good way a lot.. the supervisors and manger in this location are great getting there jobs done they are on top of everything and everyone..:

I watched this location go up in about four months and I waited eagerly for it open. I now live within a mile of a Wendy's and I am very happy.

JJ and I drove up to the drive-through after hitting the gym and grabbed some fries, a salad, some chili, and a spicy chicken sandwich. Typical Wendy's fare--the chili is exactly as I remember it from my childhood, but the fries have made a switch to a variety that looks handcut instead of frozen. Yummy food. The only problem was that the fries were cold when we got back to the house, which is not great, because we only live three minutes away.

Regardless, we were in and out of the line in less than five minutes, even though there were two cars ahead of us. This was a major plus. A small drawback was that we weren't asked if we wanted any condiments, nor were we given any. Perhaps this is the way that fast food is now, but I miss the little ketchup packets.

Finally, although I haven't made it inside yet, the interior looks all shiny and new--there are even some nice umbrellas for the outside tables.

We picked this place at random during our overnight stop in Philly. I have to say this place is pretty awesome! The chicken is HUGE! They have a huge drink selection. Mac n Cheese, Coleslaw, and Sauces were all on point too!

A friend recommended this place so I was excited to try it. Disappointment would be quite an understatement. The rice was sour, too much, and overpowered the rest of the burrito. I could barely taste the shrimp tempura, but the bits I had were good. I guess I was expecting it to taste like sushi and it certainly did not. Sure, it's a cheaper alternative, but you get what you pay for. The packaging was more appealing than the contents.

Crispy breaded chicken tenders are that exact definition - so tender and crispy (and perfect with the tamarind sweet chili sauce)!

The tasting menu includes half a pound of classic dark, white or wings. You get a side of delicious wishbone-style macaroni and cheese (with tomato, ground beef and seasoning), cookie, sauce, and soda. 

*macaroni & cheese here is by far the best Mac & cheese I've ever tasted. It's loaded with flavor!

The chicken sandwich however was not impressive, and I can't seem to pinpoint out why exactly. I recommend that folks stick with the chicken tenders; if you want chicken sandwich - best go to chick-fil-a!

This place caters to party people and opens late-night on Thurs, Fri and Sat. These nights are kind of disorderly with trash that clients leave behind and staff not being able to keep up with tidiness.
This is the most ratchet McDonald's. Your order WILL be wrong, the employees are rude, and they are so slow. I'm afraid to know how dirty the kitchen is. They need to shut this place down.

I was in line to order.  The young woman dished out the food of the customer in front of me - with gloves on -  then proceeded to walk to the register to ring up 2 other people. She handled the register,  handled cash for 1 person and card for another.  Never once removing gloves.  After she handled that she walked back over and picked up a food container to dish food.  NEVER changing gloves or sanitizing her hands!  Is the gloves for my protection or hers!  That's unacceptable!!

Solid lunch option. I had a debilitating addiction for this place for months. Get there early if your intent is a weekday lunch because the line gets out of control shortly after noon. The food is spectacular and incredibly filling. Yeah, it's a chain. It's basically Middle Eastern Chipotle. Not a bad thing. Need to go back but went too hard on Naf Naf for too long. Try the shkug.

So, there are 5 reviews on Yelp for this place (now 6.)  All one star.  There is a reason for that.  The food is good if you like this kind of stuff, but they appear to have absolutely no system for fulfilling orders.  Oh, sure, they are good at taking your money (note to the Popeyes corporate office -- we were order 70 at 9:28 pm.)

Our receipt noted mild tenders (I ordered spicy) and mild wings (my wife ordered spicy) and for some reason, they thought I wanted barbecue sauce.  But at 9:28 pm, and people standing around getting antsy for their orders (and it almost got ugly) you just don't argue.  

At 9:55 pm or so, we decided that we should ask about our order.  The woman behind the counter looked incredulous when presented with the receipt, almost like "How Dare You!"  Well, for $19.95, I do dare.  The manager said he would make it for us, and ten minutes or so later, we got our order and departed.   When we got home, we noted that our beans and rice and mashed potatoes were not included.

We will probably get a very nice automated "we're sorry" email from Popeye's corporate offering us a free drink or something, but honestly, if they don't want to give us our order in the first place, and they don't feel like it is important to get it right, why would we bother?

There are other fast food chicken options in the area.  There is Texas Chicken and Burgers, also on Cottman Avenue, and Krispy Krunchy Chicken at Roosevelt and Cottman (neither of which I have tried, but could either be worse?)  So, do yourself a favor, and don't bother.

We placed an order on Grubhub for 2lbs of chicken and 4 sauces. We only received 1lb (actually 0.6lb, we weighed it) and 3 sauces. We called the restaurant asking for a refund or a replacement for the missing items and the manager insisted that we had 2 lbs for several minutes. Once she finally understood that we only had one small box of chicken, she refused to refund or send us the missing items. She said we had to go to the store 2 miles away (we don't have a car) to pick up our missing items that we paid to deliver. I asked for a refund instead and she refused. When I told her this is basically theft she hung up on me. WORST DELIVERY EXPERIENCE EVER!

The service was really slow. The cashier was not even busy. 
Only after guy behind me complained about the wait did she finally take our order. 
Longest wait for "fast" food. 

Went back again, but this time through the drive thru
The girl working was super nice, got my order right and made sure I got everything. 
 
3 stars

The first time around our order was completely wrong. Unable to get a hold of anyone at the restaurant, but grub hub was able to help. The reorder was closer but still received the wrong order. Didn't get any of the additions I paid for and the sauce was wrong which made the poke bowl inedible. Will never go back.

The burgers are flavorful with decent size and price but it is very sloppy when you're in and get the mayonnaise slips out the ketchup spills out it makes a very nasty scene, plus the service is very very slow I don't know why. But the burgers are good but they're always sloppy and no matter how many times you tell them how to make it it just comes out sloppy so 1 start for me if you cannot fix your burger every time it is ordered something is wrong with your service

This place is seriously  the fuckin worst!! First off they never get the order right. The food is always sloppy and half assed. & even when ordering using Grubhub thinking they would actually do their job, fuck no!! They lied and claimed they delivered my food and they never did. Grubhub had no idea what they even did with my food. Never again. Fuck this Taco Bell and fuck Grubhub. I'd give this bitch zero stars if I could!! Real shit

I go here for whopper Wednesday ok for the price  the self serve soda is too high tech and had problems when I was there could not use it had to get soda from counter on the back it's ok when it works and can chose from many drinks but when it is time to reset it or add refill just too long to reboot.

This place is good as fast food goes but it's still fast food.

I can make better Mexican food at home.  And many authentic Mexican restaurants can make real Mexican food quickly without it being fast food.  What's lacking?  Multiple things:

* The freshness of the ingredients...they're okay, not bad, just not super fresh.

* The salsas are not hot enough.  The medium has almost no detectable heat and the hot is what I'd call somewhere between mild and medium.

* None of the ingredients stand out as amazing.  Everything is just a tad bland: the cheese, the rice.

* The meat is too salty...perhaps to mask low-quality meat?

* The guacamole is insanely expensive..$1.19...I can buy a whole avocado for that price.  Give me a break.  I can understand charging maybe 79 cents but charging well over a dollar is price gouging.

I think it's sad that these restaurants persist when there are so many hole-in-the-wall Mexican places that offer fresher, tastier food for cheaper.

this place has the worst service, so slow drive thru, ran out of ice cream (typical) and had trouble getting food ready on time when you do pull up to the window at the drive thru. also when asked for chicken nuggets, we pulled up to the window and they said they didn't have our order and proceeded to tell us they didn't have any chicken nuggets. excuse me you are a mcdonalds how do you not have chicken nuggets.

Well firstly they were super slow, and the girl at the drive-thru was completely disrespectful and kept rushing me, attitude all across the way, and my chicken sandwich looked like they dipped it in a bucket of mayo, felt like they did that on purpose.

This is a awesome place to get a great eating experience in philly. We came to visit from out of town and the service there was better than you'll find in most dine in restaurants. Food was amazing and right next to downtown and Drexler university.

I haven't been to a Burger King in years but someone talked me into tracking one down in Philadelphia.  It took about 20 minutes for the food to be ready, and the soda machine was broken for about another 10 minutes after that (there's only one soda machine).  The food was below average, about what I remember.

For a fast food joint I was surprised how friendly and accommodating the staff was. I phoned in when my online order was not going to be ready for another 2.5 hours! They handled it over the phone and it was ready for me shortly after I arrived. 

The location is convenient for all your center city friends to rendezvous for a quick lunch meetup! It is underneath of the Starbucks on JFK, kinda hidden in plain sight. 

The noodles were a good compliment to the saucy orange chicken. I would have liked some more color (orange from carrots and brighter green maybe from peas?) but it is fast food takeout. I'll take what I can get! 

I was not stuffed after the bowl but definitely not hungry afterwards. I am just realizing now that I forgot to eat the fortune cookie!

I've definitely had better but for $6.50 I would come back for seconds.

Good food wonderful staff. Quick service. Just a lack of seating. As it's in the classic reading terminal market. But a great place to get a good sausage sandwich. Decent prices and quick service. You gotta visit the reading terminal market in philly and immerse yourself in the local culture!!

Great quarantine option !!! My boyfriend and I ordered for pick-up by placing an order through the website. Food was ready promptly. We got a 1/2 lb. white meat tenders (2-3 pieces), a 1/2 lb. dark meat tenders (2-3 pieces), the mac & cheese, cheddar-jalapeño cornbread, and a biscuit. It was all very tasty! Both types of tenders were fantastic and you must try the mac! We got a handful of sauces - Gochujang Ranch, Tamarind Sweet Chili, Chipotle Lime Mayo, and Homemade Strawberry Jam. Favorites were the ranch and sweet chili. BIG PLUS is that they have a HUGE list of beer and it's all so well priced. Don't sleep on this place for all your quarantine cravings.

Absolute home run of a breakfast spot. I'm talking Ryan Howard 2008 grand slam! This restaurant feels like walking into Diagon Alley, small crowded entrance opens into an expansive seating area. The portions here are suitable for Eagles DT Fletcher Cox but at the price of tickets for 2013 Process Era Sixers. The Gritty-approved grits will warm your heart after watching Andy Reid collapse in the playoffs yet again. Honestly this place is a great breakfast diner spot that has somehow escaped my knowledge despite living in Philadelphia for 6 years and yet I found it after moving away from the city. Will definitely be back whenever I visit my favorite city.

I ordered Panda Express through Postmates on Saturday. I was planning to order a medium orange chicken, but it was actually slightly cheaper to order 2 smalls. I also ordered some fried rice. All together the food cost $15 and change, and didn't include the deli and tip. I personally thought that was high for Chinese food. Anyway, the food came quickly and was really good! The chicken could have used a bit more sauce, it was a little on the dry side, but still crunchy and flavorful! The fried rice was perfect after I added some kikoman! Overall, food was very good, just pricey for fast food Chinese.

Forgetting my lunch led me to experience this place for a quick bite to eat.  I was originally planning on chicken fingers but the ones I saw looked a little burnt and I saw a salad that looked delicious so I ended up opting for that and man am I so happy I did! It was AMAZING. The salad was full of fruits, veggies, cheese and nuts so it was extremely filling even though it had no meat in it.  This is a great thing to know about if you're a vegetarian.  I definitely want to come back to try their Mac n cheese though because I've heard it's one of their specialties! Regardless, I am extremely pleased and full from my salad!!

To start, don't ever confuse PE food as actual Chinese cuisine.  This is takeout style asian food and is levels below what you can get across the street in Chinatown.  But sometimes you just want that greasy mall-style Chinese food.  This place is pretty great for that.

The big appeal of this is the low price of the dishes.  One entree and side starts at $6.30.  Two entrees and a side starts at $7.50.  You just can't beat that single digit pricing!

There is a wide variety of entrees to choose from.  Some are great, some are terrible.  It may depend on who cooks for that day, or the possibility exists that the entree just sucks in general.  They have dishes that are considered "premium" that they charge extra for.  For example, the honey walnut shrimp is an extra $1 to get that entree.

The place is well-lit and has ample seating.  That's about all there is to say about this joint.  It is both cheap and conveniently located.

I got to the drive thru speaker and didnt hear anyone for 2 min so I just drove to the pickup window since it was a mobile order anyway.  The young man at the pickup took my mobile order name and politely said he will get my order.  A young lady next to him seemed to want him to yell at me or something because I overheard something about me 'just driving up'.  Since he didnt, she took it upon herself to come and berate me.  I told her I waited at the speaker for 2 min before driving up, but she gave me a snappy response that the thing beeps when I arrive and I only waited 2 sec (which definitely was not the case).  Obviously their beepy thing wasnt working but of course I didnt want her to spit in my food so I said sorry.  Then I saw her walk over to the people prepping the food, which I thought nothing of.  Until I brought my order home and found how sad of a state my Grilled Chicken Bacon Jalapeno was in.  They 'forgot' to put in the bacon or jalapeno or sauce.  So all I got was a pathetic looking piece of chicken with 2 really flimsy and squishy pieces of lettuce that were supposed to be the buns (I made that substitution in the app).  I was kind of hungry so I decided to eat it, against my premonition of it being spit on.  Probably best to avoid this particular location, although the Wendys in Conshohocken is great.

I came here after looking at a myriad of photos of Hai St Kitchen & co burritos posted online, but I left sadly disappointed. 

-1 star for service. Granted, two out of the three workers were new (I'm pretty sure), but there were just so many mess-ups during my time there that kept on bringing our experience down.

First, the worker taking our order added spicy sauce that we didn't want on the burrito (and would become physically affected by if we had too much of) and proceeded to deal with the situation by just scooping some of the sauce off of the rice and asking, "is that okay?" 
Then, she forgot to add requested ingredients into the burrito, so she just put those ingredients into containers and thought that was okay.
Finally, we ask for water, and the other newbie didn't exhibit clean practices fulfilling our request.

-2 star for food. There's not much flavor, to be honest. I was expecting to taste umami, but everything was pretty bland. We ordered the katsu and shrimp tempura burritos (both deep fried), and it just wasn't pleasant eating them. It's also quite difficult to eat the burritos when they're deep fried, and the fried aspect doesn't add too much more to the meal (flavor-wise). I was hoping to add flavor by literally smothering my burrito in the sauces that they have, but the sauces were bland, so this was not the best solution.

I've been coming to this taco bell to order food and everytime i come here they don't have what i want and i could tell that the person taking my order doesn't want to keep telling me that they don't have what i want so they say "we don't have that" in a rude way!

Incapable of completing an order. Something is always missing. I've given them more than one chance, because I wanted to assume they just had a bad day, but it's happened multiple times, and they no longer have my business.
Aileen M worst server ever!!! Food is not that great. Service is awful. Never coming back to this place.

I rounded up, but its a solid 3.5. The size of the roll is decent, comparable to ~2 1/2 hand rolls from a sushi place. Mind you, I had every intention of trying the bowl, however, the young lady said "why not try the roll?" and I had no comeback. I didn't anticipate a parry to my initial order and I caved y'all. I can't help but think about how much different my afternoon would have been if I'd have stuck to my guns and just went with the bowl. Alternate Bowl Sam (ABS)  has probably already posted his bowl centric Yelp review, but we, in the roll timeline, will never know how he liked it. Oh well, back to my experience.
They've got good flavors and fresh ingredients. The miso soup has some great flavors, however, it is very very salty and the cup was only about 3/4 full, however, maybe that's a good thing considering the saltiness.
Price wise, its a little steep for a regular thing, a little over $12 for soup and a roll, however, once in a while, I can justify the splurge.

Finally a Panda Express in Philadelphia (that we don't have to go to a basement food court to find).
My usual: Half and Half 2 item combo with orange chicken and black pepper chicken. Is it healthy? Not a chance. Will you get diabetes from eating a lot of it? Most likely. Is it delicious? Yup.

Wishbone was a staple drunk food when I was in college. Not that you need the excuse of intoxication to go enjoy their delicious fried chicken. Now that I'm a real adult, I go to the center city location and I'm still sober and in love. I kind of wish that I could say my favorite fried chicken place was something edgier like crown fried chicken (which they're also great!) but nope, it's basic, kind of hipster Wishbone with their rustic chic decor and all. Their chicken is great, highly recommend getting their pesto Parmesan sauce with it. You can always ask the staff to give you a Mac n cheese sample if you're not fully on board by looking at it. 

When I'm not getting their chicken tenders, though, what I think is underrated at Wishbone is their sandwiches. Yooooo those things are freaking delicious. This weekend I stopped by and got their Nashville hot sandwich (they change sandwiches from time to time). And that thing was decadent. With all the sauces dripping off the side, my hand is drenched and it's messy but you don't care because it's so good. Highly recommend. 

Also PSA, they sell beeeerrrrr (as if you weren't already drunk when you came here)

Honestly if you don't like your job QUIT
Nobody want to eat shit like this and not when u pay for it either.
And those who work there, you guys are more disgusting for serving this food.

I've never had a bad meal here. I usually visit about once a month since my office is down the street. I typically get a hummus bowl with falafel, cabbage and 2 of the spicy sauces.

The line is usually to the door around lunchtime but it moves really quickly.

In all honesty, I would put this panda express below a neighborhood Chinese spot. I work in this building so its convenient and easy, but flavors are processed and overly salty.
