I just tried out the new Sichuan chicken at Panda and it would have been perfect if they didn't overly salt it. It was extremely salty and not even spicy. On the front of the window it says "ask for extra spicy" and when I asked, they said they didn't have the extra spicy version. Disappointed because the chicken was cooked well and tender. Make sure you have water when ordering this item.

This is the first and only Wendy's location that I've been to that has a patio for you to sit outside to eat your food. 

We got there at lunch time and there was one other lady seated in the dining area. The cashier walked in front of us to take our order. She was cleaning the dining room area. 

I told her that we were dining in and she packed our food in a bag. The nuggets were cold and looked like they had been sitting under a heat lamp for hours. The cheeseburger was cold and the bread was pressed down as if someone had sat on it and not fresh. 

This was my first time eating at this location. I must say I was quite disappointed at the service and the food. 

I wouldn't recommend this location to anyone.

If I could give this restaurant no stars I would first of all I pulled into the drive through the girls were very disrespectful you could tell that they're really young and they have no sort of training or managers on top of the fact that I got my food in there was just a weird residue on it like spit type I don't know what it was I didn't trust it this is the most disgusting behavior and the most despicable customer service I've ever received in my life and it's at fucking Burger King

positives: clean pleasant interior.

negatives: worst managed panda ive been to.
management/staffs policy must be to stop making any new food several hours before close. have come by multiple times 1-2 hr before close to find only a quarter of the food options available, and whats left is dried out and old (see photos from 2 different days). meanwhile the staff is already cleaning kitchen and trying to leave asap. last time I came 8 people in line with only 2-3 entrees available. they didn't even have rice left. 

if you're going to say you're open try to be professional about it
Decent sandwich. I enjoyed it. Nothing out of the ordinary, but great place to stop for a quick lunch. Outdoor seating is a plus. Super convenient location. Staff was super friendly.
This place was huge. Its the closest one to me now that the one in Granite Run Mall is gone. The orange chicken is great. The fried rice could use some onions but other than that its almost perfect.
Best place in the northeast... I never been more satisfied than their customer service.. And their food is the best!

The popular choice seems to be the slammin salmon so that's what I got. Very good! Not too fishy tasting and essentially tasted like one giant sushi roll. I love the concept of this place. The burritos do fall apart a little when you get towards that last bite, but it's no biggie. The only reason it gets 4 instead of 5 is because parking is a B****. Other than that I will be going back!

This was my first experience with Popeyes and will be my last.  The staff was unpleasant and acted annoyed with the customers.  There was a visibly drunk patron who kept harassing me and my child and the manager did nothing about it but yet had no problem berating the employees over stupid stuff like a rag on the counter.  I had to wait 20 minutes for 4 chicken nuggets to be made then after all the wait they forgot to put my child's meal in my bag.  So for $40 I was harassed by a drunk who followed me out to my car and my kid didn't have a meal.  They also had no forks.  Seriously?  Never again!

I drove 4 miles just to find out they don't sell chicken tenders after 10:00. What kind of service is that? The crazy part about it the manager told me that! By the way they are open until 11:00! #popeyes sucks! I
Poor portions, serving does mot even fill half the container. Cajun rice was dried out or either npt fully cooked.
Friendly, great customer service, fresh products. Sandwich quality beats Wawa on 10th & Walnut (both the vegetables and care taken to make your sandwich are better). Recommend.

Grabbing a bite to eat before the Army Navy game found us ordering their chick strip sandwich.  The bread/roll was cold and dry.  The chicken strips were OK but nothing special.  Would try to find some other place to eat in the future.

I love Taco Bell but this is by far the worst Taco Bell I have ever been to. Every time I go they mess up my order and they refuse to admit it or give refunds. My friend is a vegetarian, so she ordered all her tacos with beans instead of meat. All of her tacos came with meat and they got all of our drinks wrong and forgot the cinnamon twists that we ordered. They insisted the order was correct and since we got it delivered we couldn't prove it so they didn't refund us. I will never go back. Drive the extra few miles and find a different tack bell.

Apparently, this Restaurant serves the most tremendous food I've ever seen! The Spicy Chicken that I have officially and recently ordered, is absolutely amazing and the fries is apparently amazing. And there I was in the line, waiting very patiently. The Spices of the amazing Popeyes Chicken Sandwich that Mukbanger YouTubers eat, was amazing. I will come here, soon.

Where have you been all my life, sushi burrito? I'm sure they're not the first to think it up but their execution is pretty good.

It's not a big place, just an L shaped counter to order at and a half dozen or so stools along a shallow wall shelf to eat at. The ordering process is a bit of an assembly line, like a subway or chipotle, which likely speaks to ambitions of expansion and franchising.

I went on a cold weekend and got the slammin salmon. It was pretty good, though eating it in my car (their few seats were full) proved a small challenge. Their lemonade wasn't worth it, I'll have to try the other beverages at some point.

I bet on weekdays, they have a crazy lunch rush, but it's definitely worth a few visits.

We went here for lunch for my son's birthday party before going to a nearby comedy show.  The manager was incredibly accommodating.  She called me a few weeks before the party to reconfirm all the details.  She made sure there was extra staff there to handle our orders.  She set aside tables for us and let us bring in our own cake.  She even gave us some delicious baklava!  Everyone loved their lunches and it really helped to make the party a success.  Thanks!

After reading all the reviews, ordered Slamming Salmon roll with brown rice. The only thing that I liked in that roll was the fresh salmon. 
I do like salmon and sushi and for some reason I thought that the flavors didn't come together in the roll. 
The delivery service was quick and the package was nice and not sure I will order this again.
And there was, it was a good exterior and a tremendous interior. Additionally, tgis is the most great fast food that I've ever had.

Dangerously close to the gayborhood and open until 4 AM from Thursday to Saturday, Wishbone is a great late night fried chicken spot next to Woodys. The chicken is by weight, so it is also dangerous how much I end up with. 

I tried all three types of chicken (white, dark, and wing). They are definitely the most well known for their white chicken strips, which were the freshest. It was also not dry! I thought the dark meat would be a drumstick, but it is actually a chicken tender - actually kind of nice that you're not paying for the weight of the bone. However, both the dark meat and the wing tasted a little too greasy, like it had been sitting out for awhile.

It's a little annoying that they make you pay for each individual sauce packet - would be nice if one or two were included with the purchase of chicken.
Best friend chicken in Philly! Found this spot after hitting the bars and loved it. We have been going back for 5 years now every fantasy football draft.

The worst customer service ever . Their rude . When I Ask for a number 7 with cheese in the burger . They had one job and they didn't do it and when I ask the lady to repeat my order . She repeated very rudely. When I pulled  up to the window they acted like I was going to rob them or something . This must be the worst checkers I had ever went in my life

I was excited to try this sushi burrito spot, but was definitely disappointed. We ordered the Slammin' Salmon and The Crunch and tried both. (They were out of tuna when we came at the end of the night.) They were both very very mediocre, lacked flavor, and had a lot of lettuce and a very little bit of fish/meat.

I can definitely make it better at home. They need to work on their flavoring. Felt like I was eating a salad. Nice try though.

I felt like I was cheating on Chipotle by going to Qdoba, but I had to try it.

I came here and ordered a burrito bowl with half chicken and half steak. I love that they don't charge for guac which is definitely awesome. They also have a queso sauce that is pretty darn good and compliments the other ingredients really well. the spicy queso is pretty darn spicy so be warned. They have a few more things you can choose from to put into your burrito that Chipotle doesn't include.This place doesn't give as much food as Chipotle, so in the end, I would say Chipotle is the better deal for the quality and taste. Qdoba is a good alternative though if you dont want to wait at Chipotle when the lines get long.
Most uninspiring chicken I've ever ate in my life. The restaurant clearly never heard of seasoning or spices, nor did they hear of mashed potatoes or Louisiana hot sauce. Hilarious.

Where do I start I totally love wingstop on Cottman ave the energy is amazing the customer service skill is great the food is amazing and aalways on time a lot of people may not agree but I actually travel down to this one and it's one near me but II will continue to keep coming to this one and the The management teAm is great I truly love the both of them the Lady manager and the boy manager they keep me going and keep my coming back and back again

This McDonald's isn't in the worst shape as far as aesthetic and design. It looks nice from the outside and the drive thru allows for two vehicles to order at the same time.

The problem is the service. It has to be a management issue. This McDonald's is always busy which isn't an excuse. You only have to travel one block away to find a Chick-Fil-A that is even busier but providing excellent service.

I'm giving it one star because there have been several incidents. One time I waited 25 minutes in the drive-thru and once you're in line, you can't get out. I have received poor service on a couple of occasions. I have also had an incorrect order once before at this location. I have called the customer service line for this location and left a detailed message about my experience and didn't receive any feedback. To contrast that, I once received cold fried at a Chick-Fil-A and left a note on the comment card. That same week I received a phone call from the manager himself apologizing and offering to make it right by giving me a coupon for my next fry purchase.

Anyways, it's not all McDonald's locations. I am not anti-McDonald's. I admire the success they enjoy and the inexpensive quick food they serve. This location, however, is falling far too short in terms of customer service.

I love qdoba. Everything is so flavorful and fresh. But at this location there are some servers that's don't serve you the corresponding portion. Half spoon of beans :/ and when you ask them for a (little) more because what they are serving is not fair they say alright that's gonna be some extra money. Not nice. There's no consistency with the portions. We usually stop by qdoba about 4-5 times a week and I don't think that's the right way of serving.

Was there 6-22 with others from work for lunch. Not sure if I was going to enjoy it. I thought it was safe enough. Salad was ok. some hot items looked canned. I will try another place tomorrow and report.....

I usually come to this place with my son, but today I'm so upset because when I order 12pc chicken only( I told her I want 7wings & 5legs  )but when I going home  only have chicken breast) and some wings. I never go back there
Great presentation, seasoning and amount of fries and sauce on the side. It was fun to walk around and enjoy the day while snacking on these fries. Great staff.

"Sushi burrito"?! I was a skeptic until I went here. It's so good! Although the actual restaurant is a tiny space, the workers there are professional and fast, making quality burritos to your satisfaction! I got the chicken teryaki and it deliciously good. It got a little tough to eat towards the end because rice doesn't hold up the insides as well as a flour tortilla!

I ordered from here today because my son wanted boneless wings and I wanted regular buffalo wings. We each got the 8 piece combo which comes with fried and a soda. The wings are just ok and wish they had a little more sauce on them but the fries were so freaking good. My son is a picky eater and ate all his fries and we both wish we ordered more fries. I'm not even a huge fry fan but they were so good. I will be getting more fries.

Mo - Not just any burrito though: a Ho-Lee shrimp sushi burrito from Hai Street Kitchen & Co. I'm going to be honest, when I saw the vendor list I immediately started to anticipate what these guys were going to bring to the table. I was not let down in any way, it was easily my favorite food truck offering. Deep fried tempura shrimp, Asian slaw, wasabi guacamole, beets and spicy mayo manifested in a cohesive culinary masterpiece. Every flavor playing off each other perfectly like a Bill Belichick offense. Chino also had nothing but fantastic things to say about Hai Street Kitchen - here's what he had to say:

Chino - Slammin' Salmon - Now one thing about me is, yes I am half Rican half Malaysian Chinese. The Rican side of me loves me some arroz con gandules buttttttt the other half of me loves some sushi. I literally could eat sushi every day like back in my college days. So this past weekend at Blocktoberfest on South St in Philly, I decided to make a stop at this Sushi food truck, mind you I've NEVER seen something like this before in my life. Shout out to Hai Street Kitchen & Co. because they make a BANGING sushi burrito. Yes that's right a Sushi BURRITO! Just picture a giant sushi roll...with with Salmon, romaine, red cabbage, tempura crunch, and all topped with Gochu sauce. Man I was in sushi heaven!!! Had a lot of flavor and nothing was over powering. Seemed perfectly balanced in taste. Now as I mentioned it had some special sauce on it, Gochu sauce, which the sauce was flavorful and just the right amount. It was a like sweet and spicy Sriracha. Same consistency as ketchup and it was drizzled on and not in the burrito. Now personally I wouldn't have minded if they used soy sauce but that Gochu sauce did the burrito justice. Overall that shit was banging and I can't wait to try some different types of sushi burritos they have. Both thumbs up for me!

The absolute worst McDonald's I've ever been in, without a doubt.

The establishment is disgusting and usually, generally unsafe (last winter, there was a thick sheet of ice on their parking lot that they refused to do anything about). The ice cream machine is usually down, and when I'd order a meal (usually a fish-o-filet), the fish would taste dry, the bun wouldn't be steamed, and the tarter sauce would sometimes be in the box, rather than on the sandwich. The fries would also taste hard and like they've been sitting.

Long story short, I've actually dubbed this McDonalds the "Bad McDonalds" when referring to ones I'd visit, and it's for good reasoning. They remodeled it earlier this year, and it STILL looks a mess. Only go there if you absolutely have to, but try not to.

The first time I saw a Naf Naf Grill was when I was in Chicago. I liked their Chipotle style of getting your food. My ordered was a the falafel salad bowl and it was good. I thought this was the first and only time I'd ever see a Naf Naf so I was pleasantly surprised to see that one pop-up on Market Street. I've since had their Veggie bowl that comes with baba ganoush and hummus. While there are several falafel spots in the city, this one has a better balance of a lower price for a bigger falafel salad bowl.
Awful service...paid $50 for a grub hub delivery...missing items...called manager...he says "oh you have to call Grub Hub...order food somewhere else these guys don't care...

The line was almost out the door around 12:45p. My chicken shawarma was delicious and worth standing in that line lol. I ate in and by 1:30p  it was ALOT less crowded, so if you can wait until 1:30p you'll avoid the lunch crowd rush!

I am not even legitimately sure of the value of reviewing national fast food chains. Regional restaurants, sure. The big name chains, not so much. In general, unless something exceptional happens or it's Chik-filA, the reviews are 3 stars or under. The Wendy's on Ridge is no different. 

Here is the order I placed on 10/08/19:

Wendys 4 for $4
(Comes with nuggets, fries and drink)
 
Double Stack 
*Alt/Special request: everything on it (all veggies and condiments on the sandwich), honey mustard dressing for the nuggets, no ice in the drink, and a sugar cookie. Size Large. 

Quoted Total: ~ 8.50

Around 2pm there was a bit of a line but it moved quickly. A dump truck rumbling and beeping in the lot made communicating at the order screen somewhat difficult but not impossible. I placed the above order, agreed to upsize the fries when asked, and after a short but not completely unreasonable wait made it to the window. 

I've noticed at this location that they hand you your cup and tell you the price of your meal at the same time. Not sure if thats in the handbook as a way to move the line faster but I find that extending my card or cash and trying to grab the cup causing a split second of weirdness. A showdown between me and the cashier trying to see which order the events happen in. *shrug* I've never fumbled the cup or anything but I thought it was noteworthy. 

My drink also had ice in it. I hate fast food ice because in addition to being gross conceptually, and notoriously dirty, its only purpose is to take up space in your cup so you get less actual drink. The machines themselves are refrigerated so your drink is cold regardless and then you'll have more of it. This is one thing I typically challenge and didn't. See my next point. 

They NEVER give receipts. When I asked for one I was told that "the printer is broken." I'm sure there's a subreddit out there dedicated to the conspiracy behind this, lol. I mention this because in the age of electronic payments I don't like not having evidence of my purchases, more specifically the order details and their prices. What if they get the order wrong and I have to contest it, what if I'm double charged due to cashier error? How do I refer to the transaction, cashier, store number etc? 

I passed the bag into my passenger seat and and like a true American I reached over into the bag to begin eating the fries. My hand touched a nugget first so I ate the little guy. I reached back again for a fry and met another nugget. When I pulled into the parking lot at my next stop I looked inside the bag. No fries. Two nuggets. The sauce they gave me was also not honey mustard; It was a weird faux ChikFilA sauce where they mix all the sauce flavors together. 

For reasons unknown, I don't always put up a stink about inaccurate food orders. In this case, perhaps because I was so close, I decided to spin the block. I drove back up to the order screen and told them what happened. She hadnt truly let me finish my statement before telling me to pull up to the window. When she handed me the bag I was likely so excited about the ease the transaction (wasn't asked for a receipt, likely because they dont give them). 

Guess what? The large fry I should have received at my first attempt was literally a small fry in a large container (see pics). I cant help but think she must have recalled my voice or order, or had known that my bag was wrong previously because why give me the large container? Did you run out of small size containers? How are you going to sell nuggets for the rest of the day? I guess it isnt worth the investigation but I really really dont like giving my money to junk food drug kingpins with mediocre service pushing red magic. 

Our collective addictions to sugar and salt guarantee that even with such piss poor reviews this place will remain in business, likely with no changes to their subpar performance. 

Cuisine: 4/10 
Service: 4/10
Decor: 6/10
Value: 5/10
Overall: 4 out of 10

I like this McDonalds. Employees usually get my order right and if something is wrong, they correct it without hesitation. It's clean inside, big kitchen which is great for workers to maneuver and not over top of the food. Staff are cordial and do their jobs. Only qualm is the lines being longer than desirable and occasional unfriendly worker.
Love jimmy johns that have sprouts! Dope sandwiches served up fast. Very tasty and light. My fave is the Vito.

Walked here from campus for dinner and was told we can't order inside and to go through the drive through or order online, so I tried ordering online and it wouldn't let me. Then I went on Grubhub to try but I couldn't select pickup only delivery and I don't want to pay the extra just to get food delivered when I'm standing right outside. Then I tried going through drive through but they said we couldn't if we don't have a car. When I called, no one picked up. So I went back inside the manager told me I had to either pay the Grubhub fees or own a car and go through drive through. Why have a location near a college campus if you don't let students walk into the store to order?

Great experience eating here. Their customer service is very friendly and kind. And the deals they have on the food is great and affordable. Fresh chicken is what you get when you order. Awesome place.

Fried chicken and beer are two of my favorite things. So when I heard that there was a spot that hooked up several varieties of chicken, and also had a solid cooler with mix a six capabilities, it didn't take long for me to want to give it a try. And as soon as I did I discovered a spot that offers all that and more.

When I first walked in I was quick to notice the rows upon rows of wings, tenders, and then some that's perfect for chicken lovers of all persuasion. Especially when you get to choose between tender white meat or succulent dark meat that's buttermilk battered with a pretzel crust. Dip lovers would be in awe of the 10+ homemade dipping sauces to choose from, and sandwich lovers have plenty of options to choose from that typically range from $8-10. Add in mac & cheese, cornbread, and other baked goods, and there's plenty more food to enjoy.

When roaming through the beer cooler I'm been able to pull out some greats from Duck Rabbit, Founders, Ommegang, Victory, and then some. And most go for cheaper than other bottle shops in the area. But teetotalers would be down with their plentiful assortment of iced teas, craft sodas, and other beverages.

Visited 2x recently. I would have given 5 stars based on first visit but visit no. 2 was a bit disappointing. I ordered 2 pitas and the man behind the counter repeated "You want 2?" Yes. Got home with only one. Also I ordered the same meal both times and visit no 2's plate gave me an absurd amount of pickles - I mean really ridiculous could have filled a jar-- and none of the sumac onions that should be part of the platter I ordered- although I did see them behind the counter with all the other salads. Visit no 1 resulted in falafels fried right as I ordered them - 2nd visit's were sitting around a bit. I might try again, as the baba and hummus are tasty- I'll hope for a 5 star visit like my first time.

The sushi-rito touches down in Philadelphia, and I'm a fan. Hai Street kitchen feels like a Japanese Chipotle with reasonable prices and quality ingredients. Just don't expect a sushi burrito the size of your head; servings are small but still filling.

I always go for a rice bowl, as I'm not a huge fan of nori. The tataki salmon is delicious but comes with a very small portion size, so make sure to stock up on veggies if you're very hungry. The build your own menu says you can only pick 4 toppings, but you can usually get away with more. I would be careful with the sauces; I ordered the miso ginger thinking it was like what most Japanese restaurants put on their salads, but it was very heavy, creamy, and mayo(?) based. Not a fan.

One thing that always confuses me is that they list prices for their pre-designed meals, but not for the build your own. I'm not sure if all the custom ones cost the same or if it varies by what protein you get, but I'm always a little surprised when I get to the register (and not in a good way). More transparency please!

Perfect little spot adjacent to the Roosevelt Mall for a quick bite to eat.  Burgers, chicken, fish sandwiches. Fried chicken and more.  Typical fast food with friendly service.  Food was above average for fast food.  The place is small but clean and reasonably priced.

They are doing pickup orders and take out orders. When I was there to order my food, they had a sign to enforce wearing a mask to be served. They are similar to Popeyes. They have fried chicken made and kept warm. They had 3 pieces - drumstick, wing and thigh for $3.20 including tax. I got the spicy version and it was spicier than the Popeyes chain spicy fried chicken. The order for the most moist to the least moist chicken would be: drumstick, thigh, and wing. I will be returning to this fried chicken spot.

Came here with my friend for lunch on a weekday.. got in around 11:50 and the line moved super fast.

I got a bowl with hummus and chicken.. it was sooooo good. Pita was fresh and the portion size was big. I must say the prices were a bit high but its super fresh ingredients so I guess that's the trade off.

I am definitely coming back here for lunches during the week!!

I might give it a third shot but I wasn't amazed the first two trips here. It's convenient to get a quick bite/drink. 

I tried their chicken tenders and wings with the different sauces. They have a variety of dipping sauces. Sauces I dipped in: Donfire, buffalo bleu, and pommery honey mustard - not bad! However, the chicken was meh. The breading on my chicken pieces were soggy, there was absolutely no crunch whatsoever. I wanted to like it but unfortunately it was a no no for me. Honestly, it reminded me of biting into a chicken wing or chicken bite from 7 Eleven... a bit disappointing with the money I spent on buying some wings and tenders. So I turned over to the legendary mac and cheese and fries. Now, the mac and cheese was pretty good. It has cheddar, swiss, caramelized onions, chicken sausage, pretzel crumbs and herb seasoning. Maybe my future visit will prove me wrong about the chicken wings. We shall see.

I wanted to love this place, I really did.

Coming from the SF bay area, I'm a bit obsessed with this sushi burrito concept. I love burritos, I love sushi, how can the idea possibly fail? Major kudos for the kid who dreamed up the sushi burrito. 

Anyway, although the vegetables are fresh and nicely diced/displayed, the main ingredient (in my case, spicy tuna), was lackluster. There was more tang than fish, and that's never good. At the $10 price point, it's a reasonable fish-based meal, but the hype was not met.

On the plus side, it's a healthy, potentially shareable meal. Oh well, onwards on my search for good sushi in downtown.

My fast food runs have been at an all time high lately, but I TOTALLY blame it on the preggo cravings. Nevertheless, I was dying for fried chicken last night. Yelp app in hand, my husband and I were on a mission to find a drive thru! We came upon Popeye's, the reviews did not let me down.

I had envisioned a terrible fast food experience, because let's be honest, they usually are. But I was pleasantly surprised to find the staff very friendly and efficient.
The food smelled as good as it tasted.  I recommend going with the spicy chicken. crunchy deep fried chicken, soooo good!! The cajun fries were surprisingly good and the biscuits were a buttery fluffy delight.  Keep in mind that I was ill from the grease attack, hours later, but it satified my cravings and I survived to tell the tale.

I will definitely come here again, if I ever have another hankering for chicken!

Have had the Steak Shawarma Pita here multiple times with a side of the rice.  The Shawarma has been excellent every time .  It has a little bit different flavor than what I'm used to as I don't usually eat middle eastern food but that works in its favor rather than being a disadvantage.  The restaurant has a Chipotle style system where you get to go down the line and select what you want from each station.  There are bowls or Pitas to choose from.  For the Pitas they cut it open and fill it with Falafel if you desire and then add the meat, any vegetables you choose and a choice of three delicious sauces.

The food is very delicious. The atmosphere is nice and the people working there are great. The only issue I have is the menu has very obscure items. Mostly all small plates but the portions are extremely small so sharing and still getting full is tough. Most of the menu items don't have a lot of substance so it's tough to make a meal out of it without being hungry an hour later. I felt like having dinner there was not the best idea due to the extremely limited menu items while snacking is also tough because who snacks on cooked cabbage and cauliflower? Everything I tried was delicious though so I am hoping that the next menu that comes out will have more filling options to make the meal more worth it. If you are hungry, this is not really the place to go unless you want to spend $$$$ on small plates that have super small portions. If you like to snack on things like cabbage or cauliflower while drinking, this would be your place. I'll try it again after they get another menu out.

Although I originally enjoyed this place my first time, I am sad to give them lower ratings now because of the inconsistency in the quality of their sushi burritos.

The main thing that varies is their quality of raw fish.  The quality of the fish can be known through its texture and depth of taste.  In light of this, their raw fish can be tough, chewy, and all together unappetizing at times.  It seems that they do not do a good job cutting out/choosing the right cuts of raw fish.  

I do have to give them props for their wasabi guacamole, which has a unique taste.  Otherwise, the price is alittle too steep for my liking given its quality of fish as mentioned.

I've had bad experiences at this Ridge Avenue store (incomplete orders, cold food, rude staff, etc.) before but I went there this morning anyway to get two free small size smoothies through a promotional of the Philadelphia 76ers NBA basketball team. What could this Wendy's screw up with such a simple order! I had previously taken advantage of this same 76ers promotional at another Wendy's in Plymouth Township and I was pleased. But this Wendy's gave me two tiny 2 or 3 oz. cups of smoothie. I was shocked. The crew in this store are lazy and slow and not very friendly. I blame the local franchise owner for tolerating such bad service.
It's Not Halal !! Seems like an error ... the staff was helpful ... they said many people ask but it's not :(
I highly recommend the Italian sausage sandwich! The people who work here are also nice. Good place for a quick bite...

From two basic betches, the best description for hai street kitchen is what you would think you'd get when your favorite sushi and the always delicious chipotle fell in love and had a baby, which is a sushi-rito! It's TO DIE FOR  think chipotle with an Asian flair. It is basically the same set up as chipotle, just the ingredients are sushi based. You still have the option of a burrito, bowl or salad. And for those that aren't as adventurous as AP and I they have chicken too! But let's be real, if you wanted chicken you'd be at Potle... At Hai Street Kitchen it's all about the sushi! Be a little adventurous and go! And let's be real, you're sure to get a lot of likes on the old Instagram. So if anything at all #doitforthegram

The service at this place leaves a lot to the imagination. It took me ages to get my SO California roll, but it was well wrapped and tasted good. Definitely would go back if they had better management!

I was starving when I got here, and left with a full belly, ready to take a nap. My husband I were looking for a place to eat and watch the game and this place had both. Because it was a game day, they had a special on wings for 75 cents. As wings are my husband's weakness, we wound up getting those (in honey garlic and lemon pepper flavors), crab sliders and the sides of fries that come with the sliders. 

I am so glad the crab sliders weren't full of mayo. They were seared little bundles of crab that were actually pretty filling. I probably could have gone without the wings, but I ate those too. The lemon pepper was delicious and the honey garlic was a bit underwhelming but still good. This is a good spot to stop in on a slow Sunday afternoon. It was not busy at all when we got there and being able to watch the Eagles was a big plus. Hopefully we get to come back some time soon.

This Panda Express just popped up on Market Street and I must admit the Panda they serve here is just exquisite! The orange sauce they drizzle on the panda meat is to die for. It's waay better than the Artic Wolf or the falcon I had the night before.  The only complaint I have is that the egg rolls were a little dry, but for it's money the food is amazing!
This is the worst Taco Bell ever! They never have what you ask for and they are very rude. Worst customer service EVER!!

Most of the time when I order here the food is good. One time I went inside ( never again) the floors were sticky , it smelled like urine , and a homeless man was in there ( also the door is locked and you have to wait until they push a buzzer to let you in... must be a really bad area) I had no problem buying the homeless man a burger , but he made the whole place smell like piss and chips  .... he should not of been inside... it wasn't a cold winter day either.... Most of the time I ate my food in the car , the drive thru can be slow at times, sometimes it's a long wait if you order more than 1 .... 1! Order... it can take a while. All my food has been hot and fresh tasting but because of my paranoia I check every food item before I devour it. Haven't found any little buggy nasties or hairs yet. I would recommend this place, just not if you're in a rush rush .

Love this place.  Preferred over Chipotle.  Alays get the smoked brisket over a salad which is delicious.  Staff is super friendly.  And love the free WiFi.  Good food, inexpensive, and wifi.   What more could you want?

Ordered a son of baconator and Dave's double medium combo no mayo...she read it back to me.. they literally gave me two uncooked sandwiches.. old fries.. I couldn't even eat the food we turned around and returned it for our money back. Disgusting.

The staff there are awesome and get the orders right every time. Food is hot and fresh never had an issue with this location. I usually go out of my way when I want Taco Bell just because I know they will always get it right.

Absolutely terrible service!! The management has completely gone downhill since they arrived a few years ago. The food was somewhat decent but when service was slow they used to close early as it was warranted, but now they stay opened when it is unnecessary and the food is cold and lacks personality. The management should be run out of town because they have no idea what they are doing and are unbearable to be around. Not a good fit for the community.
The worst place to pick up orders from. Hitting in line for 30mins plus. Terrible attitude from the big burly lady the work there.

Horrible serves, we can clearly see our food is done and already packed, but they're just sitting there doing absolutely nothing while my friends and I wait for 8mins for our order that's already made. I don't know how bad this can get.

Finally got around to trying Popeyes chicken sandwich last night and placed an order through Uber eats.  I'm not sure if it was due to the lack of attention from the app or if this is standard, but the drinks were wrong and I ordered 6 chocolate beignets and instead got apple pies.  Apple pie isn't really my thing, but my boyfriend loved them, still not what I ordered though.  The chicken sandwich was juicy but couldn't used more flavor, not sure I understand the hype as Chick-fil-A has better flavor, but still tasty enough to go back.  The Cajun fries my boyfriend got were very good, I enjoyed the rice and beans, and I tried a taste of the biscuit but they were basically hockey pucks so that was disappointing.  I assume it depends when you get to the biscuits and maybe you can get lucky earlier in the day on that one.   Despite the lackluster order I would actually return, but this particular location probably needs to train up their staff a bit more to pay attention to details and not throw in food that has been dying under a heat lamp for hours.
This place is a joke,If you have no taste buds this is a please sandwich is more bread then anything more lettuce than bread. Total crap

Quality for wings got lower and prices got higher. The wings are literally the size of your thumb. Seriously, look at your thumb now, that's the size of their bone-in wings. It's about $10-$12 for about 8 of these tiny wings that have been overcooked and covered in sauce to hide the burnt exterior of the wings. Fries are now soggy and overly seasoned that it can literally burn your tongue from how much salt was on it. Don't even bother getting wings from here. Not worth the prices.

This box-sized restaurant houses a special kind of food item.  The business model reads a lot like chipolte - pick your meat, pick your veggies, they wrap it up, you smile from your mouth to your stomach.  Instant gluttony.  You feel less guilty after eating this burrito though.  As long as you like nori seaweed instead of tortillas you're good.  I wouldn't call it a sushi burrito - it is definitely its own separate monster.  The only thing keeping it from five stars is its dependence on the chipolte business model - with a food so unique you'd hope the experience would be also.

This restaurant boasts good food, polite staff, very attractive decor, and uber-clean establishment. I had a single piece of chicken and a biscuit, which were surprisingly very filling. I sampled the mac and cheese and found it very delicious. It was my first time there, so I somehow missed the dipping sauces. The dark meat strip is delicious, however, it definitely needed a dipping sauce. I asked for butter for my biscuit and was surprised that I had to pay for that as well. The wall of specialty sodas and craft beers was a really nice touch. I will definitely be back to try other menu items.

The service was really slow. The cashier was not even busy. 
Only after guy behind me complained about the wait did she finally take our order. 
Longest wait for "fast" food.

I asked for the Dynamite Roll, but some how ended up with the Go Zilla version of the Slammin' Salmon Roll.  This honestly worked out best for me considering I probably didn't need something fried that day and I was only ordering it because I was starving.  The Tataki Salmon they used was amazing.  It wasn't cheap salmon that can taste off, no this was real deal. I do enjoy the fact that the roll was made similar to a burrito because I have been making similar rolls like this for years when I make sushi.  The only problem is that they a messy like a burrito because it is impossible to roll the sushi tight with the amount of ingredients, so I'd suggest grabbing spoons if you take this to go. 
I agree with the other reviewers stating Hai Street is similar to Chipotle and for that I'll admit it is tasty like Chipotle.

I waited 26 minutes for 3pc chicken tender & fries.... (ENOUGH SAID)
should've known when they messed up the lady's order in front of me ‍.

Ima keep this review real brief an professional cause I believe the FBI is watching my Yelp. Because the last review I posted suddenly deleted. But this place is located in reading terminal (Mecca of the indecisive dickheads) which was me & my gf today. I wanted ms tootsies but there wasn't a 2nd floor to get a shoulder rub at so I chalked that! I wanted alligator gumbo from Becks but NAHHHHH I wasn't feeling that badass today so I kept it real & regular an went to Frank A lots. For the first time cuz I wanted to try Somin new an lemme tell ya HWAT *hank hill voice* the bbq chicken was all that the Mac & cheese was all that & the spicy cabbage was righteous. The bbq wings coulda been more hot & more juicy but I got there like 5:30 so they prolly gave me the (get the fuck outta here to go plate) but overall that shit was hittin but no reason y'all cornbread should be 1.50 more that's really fucked on y'all part an the elderly cashier lady was alil mean to me an I was too cute today to be treated like that

What a shame when you make a bad decision on your one stop to RTM and this was it this past Saturday afternoon. $6.95 for what was to be a grilled bbq chicken steak sandwich was a couple small pieces of grilled chicken on a decent brioche roll and nothing more. Not only that, but they must have forgotten my order, since it took almost 15 minutes to be handed over to me. I had to ask for napkins and a fork for my wife's grilled chicken avocado salad (much better than my choice) and it came with a side of sauce (sweet, odd sauce - didn't use it). The sandwich was to come with onions too, but nope! To think I threw them a tip to makes it even worse. The 2 pierogies I ordered were OK, but they had been sitting around a bit, flat and pretty lifeless. Asked for sour cream and didn't get it. There was a decent line, so it was hard to jump back in for some, so I just ate them while I waited for my pathetic excuse of a sandwich. Lesson learned. Can't say I'll try my luck with another menu item based on this one experience. Next.

Jimmy John's is only acceptable in the following situations:

1. It is late at night and nothing else is open and you're next to Jimmy John's when the weather turns dangerous and you have to take refuge within the establishment because trying to brave the snow is suicidal and you know that every cab will be filled and you're stuck there and you're extremely hungry and you need the food very quickly because you're impatient and/or currently have low blood sugar and will suffer serious health complications if you don't eat immediately.

end of list.

I've eaten at Jimmy John's 3 times.  I've tried to give their sandwiches some fair shots.  Each sandwich I've eaten there was so unmemorable that I cannot give any specific descriptions in this review.  

I'll give it to them that they are extremely fast and it is cool to get my sandwich only a few seconds after I get my change, but their sandwiches just have no appeal to me.  It tastes like bottom-rung deli meat with cheap bread.  

This establishment could improve by upping the meat quality and increasing their spread selection.  Some honey mustard spread, for example, would help.

Qdoba historically has not stacked up compared to other quick, Mexican style food joints, however, once Qdoba adopted the impossible meat, it is head and shoulders above the competition. 

I absolutely love the lengths Qdoba went to cater to meat alternatives. Also, guacamole and queso at no extra cost to your entree is excellent! 

I highly recommend the impossible tacos and bowls!
I got the wings, they were small, not seasoned, and dry. I vaguely remember this place having good seasoning before but definitely won't be going back now.

They're literally the rudest group of employees. From the drive-thru to the window, they are rude. Rush you at the drive-thru, talk to other people while taking your order, don't speak to you when you arrive at the pick-up window, then give you attitude when they CONSTANTLY mess up your order.
Disrespectful! The BBB will hear about this. It's no possible this is normal or acceptable

Worst Taco Bell in Philly. Hands down. They've missed items in my order. They are constantly out of ingredients, like rice ... beef. Sometimes their registers don't work. I've been given a bag of nothing but hot sauce packets (I'm not even kidding: they handed me a 4 pound bag of just hot sauce packets). Do you really want people like this making your food?

The lunch line is interminable, so I ordered online.  Great option.  Your order & pay online, they just go right to the cash register to pick up.  You can laugh as you cut through the folks in the long line as you walk out with your bag of food.  

I was not particularly impressed by the food.  I got a falafel salad bowl, with onion, cabbage and hummus.  Meh.  I could not eat the falafel as it was way too salty.  There was a scoop of hummus at the bottom of the bowl, but no other dressing on the lettuce.  The fries were good.  I like the fact that they are chips rather than regular fries, and enjoyed dipping them into my baba ghanoush.  The pita was excellent.  The baba ghanoush was good as well, but with a very smoky overtone.  The baklava was OK.

I don't think it was a particularly wise choice to fill the restaurant spot in the 1919 Market building with a place offering Middle Eastern food.   There are a number of street carts in the area (right outside) that offer good middle eastern options. Cristo's cart, always voted one of the best in the city, is just across the street, and Mama's is a block away.   
I don't think I will go back.

this place is so disgusting. not only were they rude to the grubhub deliver who picked up my food they also didnt give me my drink and my order was all wet and soggy looked like they all took turns spitting in it and my quesadilla had barely any cheese in it. all because i ordered 10 minutes before they were about to shut off orders for the night. obviously these workers arent meant to work with food. theyre lazy and dont care about the people theyre serving.

Liked the ability to mix and match the sliders! Plenty of food in a box to be full after and the customer service was great. We got the Matt's slider box and the food came out quick and the burgers were moist and flavorful without being too overwhelming. Allowed me to add their wonderful hot sauce to the burger to spice it up! Would definitely go again.

Roaches Roaches Roaches!! 
That's all I'm gonna say. Just don't go here lol 
I'm sure every fast food has this problem but when your actually see it...you know it's real

New Job in a different part of the city which means new places for lunch!!!
I have wanted to try Hai Street for forever and I was psyched when the office decided to order lunch.

Everyone was happy with their orders which expansed from bowls.. ..burritos.. fish.. shrimp.. mushrooms and chicken.

I did a create your own with salmon, cucumber, spicy mayo and avocado salsa (kind of like an alaskan roll). It was delicious..a little messy to eat especially when trying to add soy sauce but what can you expect with a sushi burrito?

Everything was packaged well and they sent plenty of utensils and napkins...a little low on the soy packets...they could have labeled a little better as some things were labeled the same but weren't the same..

BONUS: They accidentally gave us an extra Ahi bowl! So one lucky employee got two excellent sushi meals that day!

Definitely excited to order again and try something a little different :)

This place may not add up to Goldie's but it's a great alternative!  The atmosphere is very clean with an easy menu to assist you in ordering food. They provide options of hummus bowls, pitas, salads, and veggie bowls. Once selecting a bowl, salad, or pita, you select the toppings and dressings/sauces you want. Think of this place as a Mediterranean chipotle!  

Definitely order some fries (they are cut like chips with great seasoning) and the garlic sauce!! Yum yum.

Seems like they had the same person cooking the food and taking the orders. there was only two cars in the drive-thru but it took about 25 minutes to get my food. I ordered the big Buford with no cheese, All I got was two patties one strand of onion and a tiny bit of mayo. I was hungry so I ate it.
The fries were cooked hard and I got an apple pie, I took one bite and threw it in the trash. 
You couldn't pay me to go back to that checkers

I came to this location knowing exactly what I wanted to buy ( a two entree plate with orange chicken and Beijing beef ).  What i disliked about the experience at this location was the pushy suggestive selling on behalf of the employee helping me. 

First, I was asked if I wanted to sample anything AFTER I had already said what I wanted.  No.  Then I was asked if I wanted an egg roll.  No, if I wanted one I would have said " I'll have blah blah blah and an egg roll".  Then I was asked if I wanted a drink and I said no. If I wanted one I would have ordered one.  

You might think that's all the up-selling they could try on me, but no.  After I hand my card over to pay, I was asked to make a donation to Children's Hospital. You can probably guess what my answer was. 

I realize the employee asking me these questions was probably required to ask them.  I just wish the management of this location would not require their employees to be so pushy and aggressive with the selling.  The food here tastes great and sells itself.

Tasty and fresh. 
The food was very good, friendly staff and quick service. Worth a visit.

15 minutes and I'm still waiting in the drive thru for my $3 order. There are two cars total, one in front of me at the window and me. Maybe two customers at the front window if that. 

And when I get to the window, my order isn't even ready yet. I can see them making my burger. And I just got quoted the wrong price. 

Total wait was 20 minutes. Fast food my foot! And I couldn't leave without driving over a curb. I'm literally writing this as I wait and it's like I'm a hostage. 

This place is an embarrassment.

Fucking delicious  my first time eating from here I am blown away, the white meat tenders are banging! My only complaint would be that I wish it came with some kind of dipping sauce, they're so good alone but sauce comes with the territory. also got the buttermilk biscuit, legendary Mac and cheese, and the maple pumpkin pie, everything was so good and was perfectly seasoned and balanced and just the right amount of everything! This is definitely my new go to!
Dont eat here. Ordered $20 worth of food that ended up in the trash. A bug literally crawled out of the nachos box. Disgusting

Ordered a Gochu-Mango Spicy Salmon Poke bowl for pick up through the Ritual app (great deals here!) for lunch one day. The restaurant was making my bowl when I walked in so they were pretty prompt with the service. They made it exactly based on my order requests - I asked for no lettuce and tempura flakes on top. The portion was perfect too.

Now for why my three star review - the salmon itself was not as fresh as I was hoping. It was definitely good/safe to eat but after having tried other poke spots around the city, my standards have been raised. Maybe this was because of how the fish was cut (skin on/fibrous) rather than the quality and freshness of the fish itself. The bowl was very heavy on the sauces and just didn't have a unique taste. Maybe their sushi burritos are better? I'll have to give those a try.

If you've ever made Korean kimbap before, these sushi burritos will basically seem like an extra large kimbap roll before you slice it.

It's a cute concept and I like the Chipotle-esque vibe in selecting your "sushirito" ingredients. They do offer some signature items, which may make it easier for you the first time you check this place out. I had the Slammin' Salmon, which was the tataki salmon (seared around the edges but essentially raw), spicy gochujang sauce, romaine, cucumber, pickled mango (loved this), and red onion all wrapped up in rice and nori. Really good! The ingredients are fresh and it's definitely a good option if you're trying to stay healthy (it's like 520 calories for the whole thing and it's super filling).

Seriously some of the best chicken I've ever eaten! Very clean store cleaned multiple times daily.  Robin the manager is super friendly and clearly takes his work very seriously. Fountain soda is a huge plus with the soda tax. I got a bad reveiw a while ago and avoided the place but I finally tried it myself a month ago and have been back nearly every day since. Truly top tier affordable fast food.
Why does the whopper not automatically come with cheese? so you can charge 70 cents more?  go to hell.

This place is absolute trash. I had gone here multiple times and there is always something wrong with the location. The final time I went there, I got home and I had chilli cheese fries missing from my order which I paid for. Another time, they took 10 minutes after I got to the drive thru window to tell me that the milkshake machine was not working and had to substitute it for a flat soda. Another time, it took over half an hour to get my food after placing a drive thru order, I don't understand why service was so slow at 2am. Avoid this dump, go to any other checkers that is NOT located on broad street, all the checkers on broad street are terrible.

Ordered online Ready within 5 minutes of pickup time Smiling person handed my order for "Pete" Returned to Office to discover order not complete Returned and same person came to help me. She turned around and asked someone if "this" was the missing items. Back to the office and lo and behold not a single sauce packet in a large order. Relatively new location but deeply disappointed in the level of customer service

Cold chicken and mean staff. I came here on the weekend and the line was incredibly long. That was no problem but as we waited in line while we were pretty far back an employee forced us to order and box our chicken then pass it to the register. As we waited the chicken grew cold. I asked if we could wait til we were closer and the employee meanly said no. Once I paid for my food and ate it the chicke was room temperature and very unenjoyable. This process could have been improved if they just allowed us to order once we were closer to the register.

Please fix your queue management and realize no matter how far in advance the scoopers work the bottle neck is at the register and the scoopers should take orders closer to order

Ordered delivery. Thought the Mac and cheese was just ok but everyone else here is raving about it so not sure if it's just me! The chicken tenders were good. The sauces all had a kick. Overall fair price for a good meal and ready and delivered quickly

After my poor experience yesterday not being given all of the food I ordered, I received a call from the manager who invited me back for a meal on the house. I will try to make it for lunch today. Thank you for this customer service and for acknowledging this mistake!

Franks A Lot, or as I call it, the Asian girl-babelious Hot Dog spot, has great food. Hot Dogs are just a small part of the goodies served up by Russell's army of Asian hotties. The Sausages and the Texas Tommy's are great and so is the Chili. (order it with cheese and raw onions on top) They have a pretty decent grilled Hamburger and the barbecued chicken with the sweet glaze is a winner too. I like the Mac & Cheese, but the show stopper are the Onion Rings! Large rings of onion deep fried in a lite, crunchy batter, fantastic. There's a little secret about this spot that I'm willing to share with my fellow yelpers, so send me a message and find out. Peace

I like to know who the owner is of this location people that work at this location are a bunch of morons they're always screwing up people's orders they got people going to the fire lane on the side of the building waiting for people orders there blocking the fire lane on top of that they they're causing a traffic backup in Jam in the parking lot people are running into people's cars total chaos at this location the employees looks as though they are high as a kite I mean these people really need to get their self together at this location this is a pitiful McDonald's the food is not fully quotes and employees look like they seen better days what in the world is going on are you kidding me they need to shut these doors at this location I'm so pissed off I don't know what to do instead of having people wait in the parking lot for their Waters they have people parking in the Firelands where you can you can't drive around and leave as it's as if they're holding you hostage the wait for crappy food and service this has to stop people really because if they keep doing that I'm going to make a big issue about it I'm going to call the news and Department of Health and I'm going to make a big issue about it

Naf Naf Grill is like Chipotle for Middle Eastern food.  In other words, you get to personalize a meal made of pretty tasty ingredients that will be filling and satisfying, though not amazing.

The highlight of the veggie bowl was the baba ganoush which had a distinctly smokey character.  The pita was fresh and tasty, but trended a bit towards white bread.  The falafels themselves were okay, as were the other salads and hummus.  The half-a-dozen or so sauce selection was nice.  Overall, not nearly as good as the Maoz veggie dish was, but with Maoz closed, it's no longer an option.

The chicken schwarma hummus bowl was definitely more satisfying, with tasty, lightly crisped bits of chicken over a spread of hummus and salads, covered with a combo of sauces and accompanied by the fresh pita.

Going during off hours or ordering online seem like good ways to avoid the midday long lines and getting your meal quickly.  

It's pricey compared to its nearby competitors, but if you need a quick meal and plan it right, the convenience may be worth it.
$1.50 for an extra large soda.  Fatties for the win!

Coming from an Egyptian person (me, obvi) I can tell you this spot is LEGIT! So many fast food spots and food carts have falafel yet none of them actually taste like real falafels. Sorry to break to you people Philadelphia and south jersey- these spots don't have really falafels!!

Then comes another Mediterranean grill, Naf Naf Grill. Okay, I see you with the camels and pyramids being represented! It's def a bowl/create your own type of place. I ordered a hummus bowl with chicken and some of their add-ons and I also added some falafel cause I was so desperate for a little taste home. To my pleasant surprise these meal would be one my best in Philadelphia. I mean, everything was so flavorful, so filling, and so authentically delicious! The falafel tasted as they should and I can bet that they make them with (chick peas) as they should be done!

Thank you for not letting me down Naf Naf! I appreciate you and your beautiful falafels.

I visit this Wendy's often and they do a great job. I usually use the drive through late at night. The food is prepped well, my order has always been right, and the employees are friendly. Can't ask for more. Thanks Wendy's crew!

Terrible experience at this location this evening. We pulled up to the drive thru and placed an order around 6:35/6:40pm. Pulled up to the window, payed, and was handed two bags. The woman at the window realized it wasn't the correct order and stopped us. She asked what I purchased and I repeated the order. They asked if we could pull up and wait. This seemed to be fine. Well after at least 10-15 cars passed us, our order was brought out to our car at 7:20pm. Yes, we waited 40 minutes for them to get our order together. And this was after I stepped out twice, and asked the woman working at the drive thru window, "How much longer should it take?" At about both 15 and 30 minutes. Each time it was, "We're getting it ready."

The bags were a mess once we received them and my wife took a quick look. Seemed like everything was there. Once home... NOPE! We were actually missing complete items, were short nuggets in the order, and some of the items weren't made as requested (I asked for no mayo on a sandwich. Big picture, that's minimal and I don't really care, but it's compounding the overall problem here.) So a lost order, a 40 minute wait in the drive thru, and missing items. I'm trying to contact customer service and I really hope Wendy's does something to rectify this. I usually don't feel comfortable posting extremely negative reviews, but the way this was handled was terrible.

i got a chicken pot pie, fries, a honey bread, and tapioca pudding... the chicken pot pie was old and soggy at the bottom, the fries were fries, the bread was BEYOND dry, the tapioca pudding wasn't my favorite but i should have read what was in the pudding. The girl at the front was VERY SWEET, only reason I gave two stars, instead of one. when i called a spoke to a man and he was very rude and told me there was no way my food was old and hung up, probably won't return. Bummed because the girl at the front was so very sweet.

Texas friend chicken is a lone location within north east Philadelphia area. Friend chicken is pretty comparable to Popeyes. Prices are a bit high but most friend chicken places are normally over priced to its on par. 4/5

I love burritos and I love sushi, so I figured I would love them together. Sadly, it just seemed to fall a little flat for me. I've tried a few varieties here, hoping to find the right one, but they've all just been consistently mediocre. The flavors in the burritos don't really seem to mesh all that well. Overall, worth a try once, but I probably won't be back.

We are vegan so we got the GG burger platter with fries. Comes on a delicious roll made from fresh seasonal veggies. We also got the sweet potato fries which were hot and delicious, Seasoned with salt and cinnamon. Everything was hot and fresh. 

The guys behind the counter were kind and accommodating. The bathrooms were clean. I'd definitely return.

Well here you've got many homestyle choices and I needed that today lol ! The food is freshly prepared and  local veggies etc Located at Reading Terminal nestled in the back is some Yumolicious food. 
I loaded my plate as much as I could with so many choices I wanted to try all I could from greens , Mac n Cheese, chicken , so, so much. I was very delighted that everything I got was very good.
Th salad bar was filled with fresh items and dressings of all kinds. The area around the food bar was clean and it wasn't messy when I went through which pleases me even more. 
The ladies working here were very professional and polite. The prices weren't over the top and for everything I got heck it was an awesome price!
One of my favorites on their bar was the sweet potatoes not sure what they did to them , but good gosh o' mighty they were good!

The freakin worst!!! I used the drive thru. When I got home, my tacos were wet and soggy! Sadly, it wouldn't have been worth the trip to take my food back so I trashed them. I ordered 3 steak tacos. The first taco was too soggy for me to even unwrap! The second and third tacos were also so soggy they didn't look appetizing at all. A total waste of my money!

Everyday I stop by popeyes no matter if it's morning or night the chicken sandwich is always not available. Why is this the case that your chicken sandwich always run out? I get different excuse everyday when ask for the chicken sandwich.

There's nothing outstanding about this BK, but nothing terribly bad about it either.  What do you want?  The food is good, the service is fair, the place is relatively clean.  It's a Burger King.

I'll say this:  The new and improved BK app is fantastic and makes ANY BK experience much better.

I find it really strange that this location recently painted one window Opaque Black, at the Drive Thru. I have never seen this at another Checkers (and there a million in Philly). I can't think of any reason other than they don't want people to see the prep area. You can literally only see the cashier and the food being handed to you.

Strange....or Dirty.... You Decide.

When a small group of awesome Yelpers calls for having a gathering at a new spot after an incredible Gold Badge Elite Event, you just have to flip the script and join in. With the group we had I expected our gathering to be perfect  no matter where we went. Especially since Ron C. was trying to challenge Jim H. to a Star Trek style battle where the winner got Jim's Yelp Hoodie. But what I didn't expect was for Buckminster's to be as incredible as it was!

Buckminster's is Michael Pasquarello's (Prohibition Taproom, Kensington Quarter's, etc) first foray into South Philly, is named for the iconic mid-century designer Buckminster Fuller, and has the owner tapping into his Polish heritage for the bulk of the menu. It also doesn't hurt that they use locally sourced ingredients for their menu, bake bread on site, and have a posh comfortable interior with a black & white mural backdrop along the walls.

Between things like their curry and a beer Sunday special, reasonably priced cocktails (their gin & tonic goes for $5.50) and a solid happy hour, Buckminster's definitely has plenty of solid deals to point you towards the Point Breeze direction. It was also good to see that they had a solid cocktail on the menu that accommodated vegans in the Vegan Flip that used apple sauce instead of egg whites. But beer was on the menu, and it was awesome that they had some St. Benjamin's Brewery on tap. 

The food menu is beyond reasonable since you'll find plenty of snacks that range between $2-6, and mains that rarely go over $20. For $4 I grabbed a chicken liver mousse and maple spread slathered on 2 house baked pieces of incredible bread. But Buckminster's menu really had me at Bacon Buddy, and with it delivering ham and bacon sandwiched between a homemade English muffin, I might just have to consider it my BFF forever!

Its rare when I make it out towards Point Breeze during my South Philly travels. But with a bar like Buckminster's that might just have to change!

I love the aesthetics in the place. It's warm and welcoming. The staff is kind and they are more than happy to help you get to know the items if it's your first time. You can sample their Mac and cheese which is amazing and simply heavenly.

The Chicken Pot Pie had a great crust in it. Crispy and the filling creamy. Together it just keeps you eating till it's done.

The chicken tenders were great. You can't go wrong with either dark or white. They are both juicy and delicious. The pretzel crust was crisp and gave a great texture to juicy tenders. It wasn't too thick and was just enough to give you what you need.

The wing was ok. It was a bit dry and similar flavors to the tenders.  

The flavors for the wishbone sandwich is pretty good. I love additions of the pickles and tomato. They add a nice acidity to the sandwich giving it a nice balance between the aioli and chicken.

The jalapeño cornbread is great. It was rich, buttery, with a small amount of heat to balance out the richness. A must have for all the cornbread lovers out there.

Amazing place overall and defiantly will be back for more.  Don't forget to grab their hole punch card for an extra freebie because I am sure you'll be back soon.

The odd night: This place is normally a well-functioning restaurant. However, upon going to pick up dinner yesterday I witnessed what seemed to be the manager and 3 other cooks joking around. listening to music, and being rude, while the counter girl was running around trying to stock, take orders, and check people out. While she called for what seemed to be the manager a few times he would come over assist, and walk away. This was not only rude with a line of people waiting about 15-20 minutes, it is very easy to turn around, and walk out. I give props to the girl, because there was a rude loud couple in front of me and she kept her cool. 

The Wings: I normally love their wings. They have a kick to them, and a unique crust which is delicious when hot. They also keep the skin on the chicken wings which I personally enjoy. Charging for sauce after buying pricy chicken is just silly. The chicken runs around $8-$8.50 a lb.

The Sides: The French fries are good when they have them, however you have to eat them there or they wind up being soggy. Even with a short walk around the corner which is disappointing. The potpie needs love the crust is too hard, and the filling was lacking in portion size, and flavor. The biscuits are my favorite, however if they don't put the honey sauce on top they are lack luster. They also have jalapeno mac and cheese, and cornbread both I haven't tried before.

The deserts: I have never tried, but they always look good. They have pies, turn overs, cookies, s'mores, blondies, and much more. As someone with a big sweet tooth they just never caught my attention.

Misc: They do have a nice selection of alcohol, and flavored drinks about the same price point at VIP market. They also have coffee from La Columbe hot and iced which is a plus. The seating area is generally clean, and they do have a local artist paint the menus. 

Overall I will probably go again, however this location while new still needs some work.
I've become hooked on the wave of sushi burritos and this place was really good. I stayed at a hotel 2 blocks away so this was very convenient for my sushi addiction.

I don't typically review fast food places, but I just ordered delivery through GrubHub and my order tasted so fresh I had to leave a review. It arrived quickly and everything tasted like it was just cooked and went straight to my plate. My previous delivery I also remember being impressed with the quality and freshness so I don't think this was a one-off!

They didn't have hard shell tacos... Not sure how but ok. Ordered a bean burrito but when I bit into it got a mouthful of onions. So I took it apart to remove some of the onions... only to discover the ENTIRE inside was onions! (See photo). They must have been out of the other ingredients, like beans, because that's all that was in there. Needless to say it was inedible. I didn't bother returning to order anything else. They got the drink order correct.

Pros: new idea, fresh ingredients, tasty food
Cons: little seating, limited beverage selection

I came here over to the weekend to grab lunch with a friend in town from New York City, who especially loves new things that she can't necessarily get there. We weren't starving and I almost considered splitting one, but I'm glad I didn't in retrospect. They are a good portion that doesn't leave you too full or wanting more. 

I ordered the Slammin' Salmon that included: nori, brown rice, lightly seared medium-rare salmon, lettuce, cucumbers, red onions, pickled mango, fried garlic flakes, and gojuchang sauce. The mango was a little too sweet for me; I prefer slightly tart, under-ripe mango when pickled for that little crunch. They were also a little heavy handed with the sauce, which made the roll a little soggy, but the spicy and tangy flavors of it were delicious. 

The burrito concept of it comes from the rice + meat + veggies, which I really enjoy. It feels like a sushi roll on steroids. To stick a healthy image, the store only sells their own iced teas (green or hibiscus) and lemonade, along with boxed water available. I asked for a cup of iced tap water and they were fine with providing that though. The biggest downside is that there are only five or six stools available for seating. It was pretty dead on Saturday afternoon, so we sat near the window to people watch, and we were in and out quickly but this is definitely not a place for a meeting or groups. The bright side is that Rittenhouse Square is close enough that you can eat in the park.

This place has plenty of buzz so far, so I hope that they continue to do well. I'll definitely be back to try some other rolls, like the chicken katsu one, but I might get the salmon again since it is so good.

This is my first time there, I discovered it just walking downtown, and I said to myself let me check this joint out, the manager is really nice, and the workers are very friendly as well, and the food is awesome, the only qualm that I really have is that they don't ask if you want salt on your fries, when I inquired about this, I was told by one of the workers there, that you have to tell them that you don't want any salt on your fries, but otherwise, the food and the service was on point. I ordered a shawarma sandwich, made with pita bread and all the fixing that you want, and I also got a fountain soda and homemade fries, they do sell some desserts, but I didn't buy any desserts. I stayed after I ate, and read a newspaper, and nobody bothered me, they just asked me how was service, and I replied great :-)

This is one of the worst Wendys I've ever been to. Whose idea was it to only have 1 cashier on a Sunday? Line wrapping around inside and upset customers.  It took a good half hour to even make it to the counter to order.  In the meantime watched people walk out upset at the wait.  I contemplated going across to Taco bell or Popeyes. Altogether it took close to an hour just to get 3 items and a drink. While in line got to listen to the manager yell at the employees smh.  I only have 2 stars because the cashier handled the situation well and was multitasking bagging orders herself.

I wanted to like this place especially being close to work and eyeballing it often. The Falafel was raw inside. Also, after taking a bite of my baklava the "use by" date is September 10th and today is the 17th!!

SLOWEST drive thru in the history of time! This has to be the WORST Mc Donald's of them all! I waited almost 15 mins to finally get to the window for them to give me the WRONG order, I asked to speak to a manager and was told they were busy?? Never go hear if you want fast food and the attitude and incompetence was astounding!

Slow service. They do not even greet or acknowledge that you are there. I had to walk out and there was no one in line! The manager always seems to be bossing the workers around and they look uncomfortable.

Love love love the Spicy Queso & seasonal Mango salad. I order from here at least once per week. I typically order online and pick up in the store, but I have gone in & waited in line. The lines move fast and the customer service is good. Clean establishment as well.

Just NOT good.  The carts on every corner---and the sauces--are much more flavorful. In fact, I tried my best but could not distinguish any difference between any of the flavors.  The chicken is salty but there is really no other spice balance.  In addition, both hot sauces have no variation in flavor--very little vinegar to balance out.  The yogurt sauce takes like nothing.  The only topping that varied the flavor even slightly--were the pickles--I liked these.  Crunchy and tart.  But even they weren't enough to liven up the dish.  
Pita was awful--a doughy mess that tasted like wonder bread.  The whole bowl tasted like different textures with no flavor.

Took my girl here the other night and wound up smashing her in the parking lot because the drive thru took so long... great lay but we got chick fil a afterwards because the food still wouldn't have been done

Great quick casual stop in the craziness of Center City! This is more of a 3.75 star place for me,  but I opted for a 4 instead of a 3. I felt a 3 was way too low for the quality.

We ordered the dark meat tenders and the wishbone wings. I think pricing is fair for the chicken. I really enjoyed the tenders. My boyfriend prefers chicken on the bone so went for the wings. He felt they were a little small but still a good purchase.

The mac and cheese was okay/good, but I struggle to call it "legendary". The pricing felt a bit high in my opinion. I would personally skip this next time.

The biscuit was GOOD. I know the price is high for a biscuit, but I would buy two. It was flakey and flavorful. So good! 

The counter service was fine. Nothing negative, but nothing special. I was helped right away and didn't need anything beyond ordering.

I went into wishbone to order a chicken basket and the workers threatened "to beat the shit out of me" (that is a quote). When i took a picture of the associate harassing me, i was escorted out by another employee. I have attached picture of both employees. Very unprofessional and very sad. I will never be returning.

Went to this place for a quick lunch-- it was solid Fried Chicken and I thought their mac n cheese was excellent. Great selection of beer at the front, and the restaurant gave a good vibe. 

I had the chicken wings (pretty good) and got the kochujang ranch sauce, which I thought was awesome. Overall, good food and it's a solid restaurant, not phenomenal nor was it special. I wouldn't drive out of my way for this, but I can see myself coming here every once in a while for a good meal.

Every single time I go to this Wendys I'm stuck in the drive thru line for minimum 20 mins. The employees never offer an apology or even acknowledge the obscene wait time. I can respect a long wait time if the food is fresh, but no surprise here the food is consistently cold and their nuggets specifically are rock hard and dry. Never going to this Wendys location again.

I ordered from Wishbone via their delivery service (ChowNow) and had a fine experience. The first night I ordered, they were having issues with ChowNow and weren't able to fulfill my order, which was frustrating. However, I received an email from the restaurant the next day apologizing (gotta love kind customer service!) and decided to order the next day for lunch.

I ordered the Wishboner fried chicken sandwich and macaroni and cheese. The mac and cheese wasn't for me (but perhaps that's just my strong preference for creamy mac and cheese). It had flavor from the chicken sausage, but I found it to be a little dry. The fried chicken sandwich was also well-flavored and good for a lunch, but is not necessarily my go-to for a day where I am craving very special fried chicken.

Perhaps one of the most exciting things about Wishbone is its very extensive beer / drink selection (so many options! also available for delivery!). If I were to come to Wishbone again, I would certainly take a closer look at that.

First time ordering from them and, although there were some high points, the low points more than offset them and I will not order from here again.  The chicken egg roll were cooked perfectly with not a drop of grease to be found but the inside was soggy.  The honey walnut shrimp were excellent in every way.  The string bean chicken breast dish was way too salty although the green beans were cooked perfectly.  The fired rice was bland and boring with hardly any vegetable.
