WARNING: Do not touch their brownies!! The sign that says "Do Not Touch Or You Buy" is not a joke, regardless of the fact that it is double-wrapped in Saran wrap.

Remembering Thoreau, I decided to live a little and touch the brownie. It was a small feat compared to Civil Rights' living of being thrown in jail for not paying taxes during the Spanish war, but it was a start.

And yes, I had to buy the brownie. Long live existentialism.
Nice and quiet. Ordered breakfast sandwiches for the crew. They were happy with the wgg white and cheese flatbread. HB had sweet peppers and oregano on his. This is the spot in thw early morning!

An A-ok kinda sandwich shop. If you get there when there isn't a crowd, you'll be served promptly and your food will be border-line fresh. Thats quite alright with me. They, like everyone else claim to have the "best" cheesesteak in town. Its okay. 

Try the cookies.

Been here 3 times and I will keep coming back for more.  I grew up eating ramen and this place definitely fulfills that comfort-ramen cravings.  The inch of Heaven is very rich and delicious, but my favorite is the gates of hell.  Gates of hell is too spicy for me, so I ask for less chili oil and it's absolutely perfect!  The husband can't get enough of their karaage chicken.  Dan, the server, is very friendly and attentive.  $9-11 per ramen bowl is totally reasonable to me.  
I give it only 4 stars because the first time we've been they didn't have any pork (however they gave us a free small size appetizer instead), then the second time we went they didn't have any karaage chicken.  The third time was the charm because everything was in stock and absolutely delicious! If you're in the area or even in a completely different area of town, definitely give this place a try!

The sandwich was good but nothing to rave about. I was not a fan of the bread. Too tough for me but I could tell it was fresh. When it's hard to bite through you just make a mess. And what sandwich place in Philly doesn't have a cheesesteak on the menu?

I was in Philly for work, and I had set out to find the best Philly cheesesteak samich. I had gone to Jims first, then Sonny's, and Campos last. Campos turned out to be the best, go figure!

The girl at the cash register can be a little rude, but maybe I'm saying that because I'm a Cali girl and not used to East Coast people, I hear they are no nonsense type of folk...lol.

But besides that, the samich is awesome! I got it with the works. The meat was moist and it seemed like they don't cut any corners. I like the extra cozy feel of the place because there is an old lady (maybe their gramma?) that helps out.  Just an FYI, this place gets packed at lunch with a line out the front door. 

If I come back to Philly, I would definetly come here again.

On vacation and just wanted a good Philly Cheesesteak (7/11/12). Asked a local who did not recommend any in the area. She asked a co-worker who suggested Campo's. We embarked on the LONG HOT. Judging from the displays in the shop, I thought I was in for a real treat. 
We just wanted three plain cheese steaks (8.00) but not knowing all the details, the cashier (922) said tricked us into getting three "works" (9.50). All were disappointed. Yes, according to the description, it was loaded with mushrooms and sweet bell peppers. "Fried onions", the whole mess looked pale, was bland and wet. It tasted and looked like it was boiled or stewed. The Philly Steak we got in the mall was a million times better (sauteed steak on the grill until brown with caramelized onions and provolone cheese). 
What were all those food critics thinking?

The Best Cheesesteak not enough people are talking about!

Family owned and operated.. most friendly staff around. Don't pass on the sides as they are also phenomenal.

No joke every single time i've ordered from this taco bell they've gotten my order wrong and i've had to either throw my food away or find someone to give it to because it has something in it I can't eat (usually cheese or sour cream, i'm lactose intolerant). It's not always easy to just bring it back because a couple times it was through delivery and one time it was drive thru and by the time I got my food (it took literally forever) and checked if it was right, they said the grill was already off...

Reading the other reviews, clearly people have strong opinions about their ramen. Some awfully dramatic comments for a bowl of noodle soup. I consider myself a pretty cultured eater, but I fully concede that I'm not a ramen expert. So if you are the ultimate connoisseur of ramen, perhaps this review is not for you. Perhaps you would like to shun me and take me off the Christmas card list. Okay. That's fine. 

But if you just like good food and don't approach it with a checklist, I would definitely describe what I had for lunch today as delicious. Maybe the shoyu broth was a little salty, but I rather liked it that way. It had a complex flavor. The pork belly, scallions, and bamboo were all presented nicely. Noodles were properly cooked.  I thought the portion size was perfect. I will come back often. It will be especially great when the weather gets cold. 

I have no problem with a small menu, which is now typed out properly with prices. I would have eaten any of the three ramen choices. The decor was very attractive, I thought. Yes, it took two chefs a few minutes to make two bowls of ramen (ours looked like the only order in), but let's be real here - it's minutes. Unless you hold some deeply held belief that ramen must be served instantly, you can handle the wait. 

I know the lunch options in this neighborhood very well and believe me, this is a welcome addition.
Not Philly's best cheese steak.  Average food & ambiance.

In agreement with Matt L., Jimmy John's, in my personal opinion, is average at best. It's good for when I just want a plain and simple turkey and cheese sub with nothing extra on it, but the best part is that when they say "freaky fast,"  they mean it!  Their subs are made in 30 seconds!  It does get crowded around lunch time though, but the line moves very quickly.  They also had an open mic there one night as a fundraiser for the Temple Singer Songwriters and Musicians Association.  I performed, and it was a blast!  Hope they have another one soon.

Personally I think Campo's has the best Cheesesteaks in the city.  I like their other sandwiches too.  They aren't DeNicks in the Reading terminal, but their pork and provolone with brocholli rabe is still pretty damn good.  I recently tried a ruben.  I love Rubens and I was not a huge fan of campos.  Just too much sauce (I don't like when my bread is so soggy it falls apart - although it could be cos I got it to go and that is why).  The corn beef was good though and the sauerkraut was tasty.  
Also, not that this is campos fault - but it tasted a little too salty for me.  I just clarify and say that I seem to be sensitive to salt taste and find a lot of things too salty as of late and this is not Campos fault.  I can't tell to be honest if its me or what.  But so I will not hold this against them and it could be just me.  Anyway, I still love their sandwiches and food.  Their oink is worth trying if you don't know what to get and want to try something different.

I've said it before, and I'll say it again - The ramen scene in Philly is not great. It is also possible I just might not be a fan of ramen in general. (but I'm Asian, so that's mildly preposterous)

Hiro has a few good things going for it. 
- The noodles are quite good - thinner and better texture than many other ramen bars
- The broth has some depth to it, even if it is on the fatty side
- The fried chicken appetizer has a nice breading
- The lunch special is a pretty sweet deal: any bowl of ramen (~$10 by itself), one of three appetizers, and a salad for just $12

There are also some things that don't quite hit the mark. 
- Way too many bean sprouts / not many interesting things to top the noodles
- Only ONE piece of pork belly (which was very fatty, but not especially tasty) 
- Very little flavor in the soft boiled egg
- The actual chicken part of the fried chicken appetizer isn't of great quality

So I guess I'm pretty ambivalent on this place / ramen as a concept.
But the service was really good, and sometimes they play J-pop. (!)

Ever since Quizno's ran the ad campaign featuring a singing rat I have been turned off.  Luckily the advertising geniuses behind the rat are not the same people behind the food.  The new commercials show larger sandwiches than Subway, and they are accurate.  At Quizzno's you will get a larger meal for slightly more money, and personally I think it is worth it.

I really wanted to like this place. Walking in, it had the look, it had the feel, even had a woman greeting you with an Irrashyaimase.
But unfortunately, fancy packaging doesn't make up for a bad product.
The ramen was perfectly edible, but I don't go out of my way and spend hard-earned dollars for edible. The kimchi was unflavorful, the broth so, so. Neither the veggie ramen nor the tonkotsu was anything to get excited about.

Very disappointing.

This was a disappointing cheesesteak.  In my quest to try all the well-known Philly cheesesteak places over the last couple of years, last night was Campo's in Old City turn.  The space looks better and more charming than most cheesesteak places with its exposed brick walls and it has a nice outdoor sidewalk café eating area which is a plus.  However the cheesesteak itself seemed smaller than most with only fried onions included.  Everything else is extra so the base price of $9 can quickly rise.  I should note there was one container of ketchup for the entire restaurant that was watery and about 1/16th filled when I was there.  The meat quality seemed good enough - just a little more maybe would be nice. Tap water is not served here .... in other words you have to buy a bottle of water.  Counter staff was neither friendly or unfriendly....just like 'what can I get you'....or 'we don't do water here.'  With all the great cheesesteak places in Philly there is no reason for me to go back with any visitors or friends to Campo's.  I'm glad I tried it to find that out!

I love Qdoba. And therefore I love this place. It's right up the street from the movies, so right after me and my friends go for a flick we can head right up the street and go here. I love the big portion sizes you get for the amount of money you pay. $6.75 seems like a lot but it's definitely worth it for the portion size you get. We usually split the chips and get a soda to wash it down with it. Just make sure you eat it slowly. You might end up with the Qdoba effect--gas, feels like you're about to puke-the general overeat feeling. So be careful with your glutiness.

EDIT: The "it" I'm talking about is the burritos.

After hearing and reading pretty good things about this place, I decided to give it a try.  I read about their meatloaf and how good it is, so I've been dead-set on trying it.  Well, I've ordered from there 3 times this past week and each time I call, they don't have meatloaf.  WTH!?  I really want it!  Instead  I've been trying their sandwiches.  Sandwiches are pretty good- they're fresh and I have no complaints.  I also read online about their chicken salad, so I decided to try that.  If any of you have ever had Wawa's chicken salad, this tastes almost identical to that...which is pretty good.

Delivery is pretty standard.  They tell you "within the hour" and they hold true to it.  For example, today I ordered my food at 12:26 and it arrived at 1:20.

All-in-all,  I have no complaints except START SELLING THE MEATLOAF OR TAKE IT OFF THE MENU!  I'm dying to try it!  :)

GREAT Experience!  Visited Philly with a group of Boy Scouts (23) in our group and they were able to accommodate us with no problem at all.  I called ahead and placed our order of 23 different sandwiches. When we arrived and told them we were there they began to make our order, so that everything was fresh.  ALL sandwiches came out hot, fresh and everyone enjoyed the experience.  The deli was busy at the time (6:00pm) and they were still able to accommodate us with absolutely no problem.  VERY Pleased and will recommend to anyone that I know that plans to visit Philly either alone or with a group.

Also, the selection here is so much better than other Cheesesteak shops that only offer with or without onions and cheese.  Here you can get an authentic Italian Hoagie, Meatball sub, Cheesesteak made many different ways and more.  Great place to visit and the prices are right in line with everyone else.

Wheneve I'm in the mood for Mexican food, which isn't often, Q'Doba is my go-to spot. Well, it may have just given my tastebuds a little boost seeing as they hv online ordering and they actually have it ready on time. Their burritos are my favorite because they're so filling and satisfying. The staff are always nice and pleasant and the atmosphere is pretty chill. This location is convenient to everything, the train, multiple buses and on a nice weather day it's popping. I've tried the Chipotle and I'm gonna stick with my Q'Doba. (It's funny bc it seems that I can't ever find anyone who likes them both. It's an either or with these two lol)
The food is good with nice price. The service is also nice here. They offer a good deal for lunch special with Ramen, vege salad, and an appetizer for 13 in total.

I wanted so bad to keep loving this place. The second time around was rather disappointing. The line still moves quick, the inside is still tight and you are jostling for a seat, the still don't have fries or anything fried but the quality of the sandwich has deteriorated. I guess the first time you eat something and fall in love with it, it's had to duplicate that feeling. It has fallen down a notch so TL's still remains my #1 place.

I love primos. I especially love primos with decent hours and I really appreciate that this primos stays open past 3pm unlike the rest of the locations in the city. While I think you pay a slight premium with this location, as pricing seems to be a bit higher - it's definitely worth it for one of their sandwiches.

Best cheesesteak of all.  Rib eye cooked to perfection. Perfect bread, cheese and roasted peppers, onions and mushrooms.  Forget what anyone tells you...we came from California and tried them all. Family owned since 1947.

Not as awesome as they claim to be. Just a regular sandwich with regular lunchmeat. Maybe it's considered a fantastic late night meal/snack to the drunk college kids in the area, but for a working professional such as myself, it's nothing I can't get at a local mom and pop store. 

I'd rather have Quiznos.

There's no problem ordering food here ,the counter people are not rude and will not send you to the end of the line.  The area is clean and seems very safe.  The food is fresh but the cheese stake beef was a little tough (not worth the drive from NYC) .$12.50 for a cheese stake and a 20 oz bottle of coke is probably the going rate around there but It didn't seem like it was worth it to me .

Stopped in here for lunch earlier today. 

Staff is great, service is great, and as usual the hoagies are slammin. 

Got a small Italian Diablo and a PBR and it came under $9. Sweet as Hell. 

Will return.
Lunch combo deal is amazing. Great service and fresh tasting ingredients. Hell yeah I'll be coming back

We tried this spot based on a quick search on my phone.  It was okay, but it probably wasn't a good idea to go for a hot sandwich on such a hot day.  My wife and I both had cheese steaks and they were tasty, but nothing special.  The potato salad was really good.  My kids tried the macaroni and cheese and enjoyed it and we also got a grilled cheese which my son ate, but I don't think he cared for it because he was used to grilled cheese with American cheese.  The service was quick and the restaurant was clean.  It was crowded which is a good sign, but it was extremely hot inside.  They could have cracked up the AC on such a hot day.  The service was fine, but the cashier seemed a bit snippy with some customers, but maybe she was just hot as well.

All I'm going to tell you are facts about this awesome new spot. Hiro Ramen is run by a dude that worked for Ramen Boy & now Ramen Bar's chef. Talking to him, he is super passionate about making a significant contribution to Philly's growing ramen "scene". I've eaten there twice since they've opened. Right now, there is no sign on the space, but its the place right next to MilkBoy on 11th & Chestnut. When you walk in, it is definitely not some corporate backed place with polished wood and marble jawn. It's a humble upstart by some guys wanting to serve up some awesome, quality japanese comfort food for this coming winter. So let's start with what 85% of you will order, the Hiro Ramen. For now, their limited soft opening menu's title dish is their baby. It's going to change a lot thanks to their desire to experiment and innovate. Fact # 1: Hiro Ramen's food has 0 MSG. I was told that, and I felt it whilst walking out of there my first time. I didn't feel salt coming out of my face, I didn't feel bloated or tired, I actually felt refreshed. They make their own blend of soy sauce for their broth. They also do a brothl-ess ramen, which is a newer thing in Japan and extremely new here in the states. I imagine it's awesome when you've had a few too much to drink, as it comes with an extra portion of noodles. I forget the name but it's the second item on the list labeled as Shio (salt) ramen. I had this my second time there due to being exposed to the concept in Brooklyn. It was delicious here. The noodles aren't to the chef's 100% satisfaction, as he told me he is going to try a thicker, slightly chewy more flavorful noodle next for this dish, which I am all in for. What does this mean for Philadelphians!? It's the first and probably only joint that's doing broth-less ramen here, and you definitely should give it a shot. Comes with all the fixins, but the noodles have soaked up the shio broth, and the friendly, super awesome staff can hook you up with some of the raw sauce to flavor it up more if you think it needs it, but it doesn't. **disclaimer** i really loved Ramen Boy, mostly because it was the first ramen noodle joint here, but I also am very open-minded about food, and love all the Ramen ive had in the city so far. Hiro Ramen stands out though because it's not what the others are doing (heavier Tonkotsu style) and it's going to only get awesome-er so go check them out.

**update** some of the culinary savvy folks on here are wanting to correct me on the whole 0 MSG thing, and instead of taking it off my review, I'm going to add that because I don't cook, I don't know or care how specific their claim is on NO MSG. If MSG is a natural occurrence in soy sauce, and a little bit can't be totally avoided, that's all well and good but I don't feel the repercussions of heavy MSG at this place. It may be that the soy sauce they prepare in-house tastes nothing like bottled soy sauce, and therefore contains minimal, to no intended MSG. I would also respect that you not message me with correction statements so that Yelp doesn't send me an email telling me that you don't have better things to do.

I had the inch of heaven ramen for lunch. The lunch special is an extraordinary bargain. Appetizer and salad with a bowl of noodles for only $12 is well priced. 

The appetizers were rather smallish in size (but that's expected for a lunch special). The salad ginger dressing I liked. Good balance for the meal. 

The ramen is good too. The menu however lacks protein variety. Basically if you like Berkshire pork belly you're in the right spot. Otherwise, you'll enjoy the fine selection of more pork belly. 

The broths of the ramen have good character. I tried a taste of the gates of hell which tasted great. It does pack some heat but not "painful" heat. 

The inch of heaven tastes great also. It's very rich though. I'm talking fatty to the extent that I feel like I had eaten the adipose content of 5 baby seals when I was done. But other than that I liked my experience and the ambiance and decor is top notch. Give it a try.
Fried chicken app is really good. Nice marinade before they fry it. The noodles have great texture in the ramen bowl.

It's Qdoba.  There isn't much more to say.  Average Mexican food for a decent price.  Seating is nice and the atmosphere is okay, but I find Chipotle to be an overall better experience than Qdoba both in general and in comparing this location to the nearest Chipotle in center city.

We stayed near Geno's, which is one of the more famous cheesesteak places, but they had xenophobic shirts in the window. So... fuck Geno's. 

I had an event at Penn's Landing, which is a convenient walk to Campo's.  We split a spicy cheesesteak and a chicken-steak w/ cheddar. Both were pretty good. I'd eat there again, but it's not going to be a destination stop. 

The staff were really friendly and efficient. 

Bonus points for having a clean bathroom that's a lot less Candyman-flashback-inducing than the ones on Penn's Landing.
Awesome sandwiches and great staff! So nice. Great place to get a sandwich and relax. They have vegan cheese!
Very "eh." Good not great. Hit the spot but not blown away. Okay service. Pricey beer

I went here on a whim for lunch and I have to say that I was quite impressed. The young lady who greeted was super friendly and informative on the menu. They had different names for each ramen dish but there was a breakdown of the dish underneath so that was quite helpful. The chef in kitchen was nice and even gave a little because I mentioned I was sharing it with a coworker because it was both our first time trying out the place. I should've ordered my coworker her own dish because it was so delicious. I ordered the Profilio and takoyaki and the ramen was made fresh on the spot. All the ingredients mixed well together especially the bamboo and corn, which to my surprise was really good. The noodles was just the right amount of firm even after sitting in the broth for a bit. I took out but the atmosphere of the restaurant seemed comfortable and I would definitely bring friends and family back. The takoyaki ball was massive and full of octopus! Do not let their outside appearance fool you because it's definitely worth the try.

I went to Campose and I will never go back. 

Charged me for a fountain water (that I got for my dog) and proportions for hoagie were very wrong. It's as if they took 2/3 of a real hoagie and then cut it in half so you wouldn't really notice. And they charge ten bucks for it. I've gotten more meat on a white bread sandwich than I got on my hoagie here. 

The worst part was the mayo. If you're going to charge me for water and ten for a small subpar sandwich, at least have real mayo. THEY GAVE ME MIRACLE WHIP/light mayo.

Places with better sandwiches off the top of my head: Paesano's, Chickie's, and of course Sarcone's. If you want a real sandwich or service, don't waste you're money at Campose (more like Compost).
Love it!!  In my view as a former Philly worker is that CAmpos is the place to go.  And friendly. Weird in Philly.  Kinda small but that's the norm for the area.

We were touring the historical district and stopped in for lunch.  This is within a short walk East  from the Liberty Bell and Old Town.  I ordered cheese steak with onion and provolone instead of cheese wiz.  Also had pasta salad and drink.  Rolls are soft and tasty.  Meat was juicy, and enough cheese to call it a cheese steak.  You may want to consider adding salt and pepper to taste.  Weather was good so we ate outside on the sidewalk at tables (very welcomed).  You have to put up with traffic and pedestrians, panhandlers, etc. but remember you are in the middle of a large city.  There are a few seats inside, but limited.  Staff was helpful, and turned around our order quickly on a busy day.  Used their website to review menu prior to our visit.  That was helpful.

Stopped here a few times after work in old city for a quick sub. Always friendly service at the counter and subs made the way I like/order. I have also used Uber eats to get campos numerous times, the cookies are delish and the order is never botched. Thanks campos!

Cheap and good. I didn't have high expectations to Japanese restaurants in Philly based on some average experience with a few ramen and sushi bars before.

I like spicy ramen and ordered gates of hell (powerful name huh?). It was pretty nice.

Took a walking tour of Independence National Park, our tour guide (smartest man alive) led us through Market Street and explained that Geno's and Pat's in South Philly were traditionally considered the best cheesesteaks in town but when his friend's visit Philly he takes them to Campo's. That was good enough for me, I went there right after the tour and got a cheesesteak with whiz. It was delicious and filling but don't forget to bring cash, they don't accept credit cards. Girl at the counter was kind of short with us, not in the best mood that day.

Fast delivery but they screwed up our order. My boyfriend just got out of surgery and all he wanted was a certain Primos hoagie when he could finally eat again. I almost called back to make sure they got the order right but decided not to bother them. My mistake. He was super disappointed with getting the wrong order. Plus the delivery fee is $5.99. Thanks for nothing!

Took my son here during an 8th grade field trip to the area.  I was so excited to try this place based on both local recommendations and television reviews that I'd seen.  

What a disappointment.

Placed my order (2 cheesesteak sandwiches, 1 bag of chips, 2 sodas=$27 and change), and was bluntly told "cash only".  No smile, no "sorry about that"...just "there's a cash machine at the entrance.  

My son ended up digging money out of his wallet and paid.  When it arrived, the sandwiches looked fantastic.  Fresh, tender bread, stuffed with meat, cheese, and veggies.  It wasn't until we took our first bite that the disappointment hit us.  Totally flavorless meat that was in desperate need of salt.  Very chewy, too.  Also, the skin on the green peppers was difficult to bite through.  It was as if the skin was made of plastic.  The onions were cooked just past raw, and when I took a bite of one, it bit me back, with no caramelization at all.  Finally, the cheese had not been thoroughly incorporated into the meat, so it was only melted in part(s) of the sandwich.

Halfway through the meal, my son remarked that the ones I make at home are much better.  Sadly, I had to agree.

Couldn't believe they had Takowasbi !! I haven't seen any other restaurant or bar here in Philly that carry it on menu!! Cool space, didn't feel rushed enjoyed taking my time eating. Waitress was Japanese, not trying to be racist but it was a rare authentic plus!!

I had the most conflicting experience at Hiro Ramen. I don't know what to make of it. 

I don't know if you've ever been to Hiro, but it's a quaint little ramen house, with rich, grainy woods, and matte blacks. The specials are just that: special. The prices are always right. I'm in the hospitality industry and regularly patronize restaurants in the area.

However the service is confusing. Let me explain. 

I've had more than one experience where the chefs and the lunch waitress are at odds. I go in for lunch regularly as I work around the corner and I adore the fast service. But I concede, I'm a particular eater. It's to no fault of the restaurant. I have dietary restrictions. I also have preferences like everyone else, right? 

One time I ordered some food to go. The waitress took my order and it wasn't very busy. She said it would be 10-15 minutes. When 15 minutes came, even before I confronted the waitress, I saw her approach the cooks. It was then I witnessed a heated conversation between the two. It seams the cook made my order wrong, the waitress was trying to correct it, and the chef refused to do so. After 25 minutes of waiting I finally received my order, with the apologies of the waitress. The ramen was delicious but the experience was odd. I'm confused why a chef is so unwilling to accommodate a guest. So lazy. Thank you to the waitress. I've kept coming back for her. The chefs, while talented, lack in customer service COMMON SENSE. It ain't about you, it's about the guest.
Ramen is average but the best in the city. Their side dishes are really worth trying if you have space in your stomach. Small little hole in the wall. Cash only.
This place is awesome! The kitchen is clean and the staff is friendly. Great cheesesteaks and sandwiches all around. I've been coming here for years they never disappoint.

Came here for the typical Philly cheese steak while stopping in Philly for the night. Service was SHOCKING. The girl behind the counter was in a feral mood but the cheese steak didn't take long and was very tasty

Definitely the go-to for ramen place in Philly. I ordered the wasabi octopus appetizer and the gates of hell. The wasabi octopus was served in a tiny portion, which was a little disappointing because I was expecting more for $6. 

But they made it up with the on-point ramen. The broth was flavorful and the texture of the noodles was just right. To me, the gates of hell was a mild spicy. I wonder if they provide spicy levels to choose from. 

The vibe from this place was great! From the lighting to its minimal decor, it could be an intimate place for friends' get-together or a date!

Japanese place owned by Japanese people. They seem more serious about authenticity here than the other center city ramen joints. I really love their garlic broth and their chewy qq noodles. Good selection of bottled Japanese soft drinks, too. Cash only-they keep pretending they'll get a credit card machine but they've been saying that for a year at least.

Italian special on a seeded roll, yummy!  Homemade mac and cheese, really yummy!  My boyfriend loves their prosciutto hoagie with sharp provolone.  I'm not a big fan of their cheesesteaks, but I had some out of town guests visiting recently and they liked the italian cheesesteaks they got with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone.

Went again in the aftermath of the blizzard and we were served by the NICEST woman. She was absolutely awesome and accommodating to all of our various needs. (we ordered for three people) She explained the current promotion and offerings to help us make our decision  

The food took no time at all and was made fresh just for us. There were no mix ups or discrepancies with our order whatsoever. Overall VERY happy and I'd definitely go back hopefully on her shift!

Campo's at the ballpark is good- Campo's old city needs work.  Cash only which is my first issue.  Seriously cash only?  Second- the cheesesteaks are difficult to screw up and so they got that down but I ordered a chicken parm sandwich and it was beyond disappointing.  The sauce was bland.  The chicken had zero taste and didnt have any of the typical chicken parm qualities youd expect.  The sides are nothing special and the two we got werent worth what they cost and were really small.  With soooo many options in old city they need to step up their game big time.

This is the worst BK, EVER. Sometimes I just want to go thru the drive thru quick and get some food and there is ALWAYS a problem. A huge line of cars that don't move, and slow service. 9 times out of 10 when you get to the window they ask (well, tell) you to move your car out to the parking lot next door and they'll bring it to you. The whole process has taken up to 20 minutes before. 7 times out of 10 my order has been wrong. 10 times out of 10 they charge me for honey  mustard because I don't like ketchup. 

I thought I'd trick them last week, I went inside. GUESS WHAT? It was just as horrible. 3 people working at noontime, 2 of them too busy talking to each other than getting my food, a huge line and no one hustling behind the counter. I think I just keep going to see if it changes. 

The food itself is your basic BK, it's just the service that bites.
Our first Philly Cheesesteak sandwich. MinMin very first, "It's good. I never tasted a sandwich like this". Very fast service.

The appetizers were good the karage, takoyaki and raw squid were better than the ramen. I got the Gates of hell with extra noodle. Something was missing in the broth, it just tasted flat and one dimensional. The depth of flavor was lack luster.

Good food, nothing special, though. Really wish it was a full version and not the limited kind (options are pretty much only chicken sandwiches, nuggets, salads, fries). I get that the food is being made fresh(er) than most fast food places, but I have had to wait pretty long on more than one occasion for some nuggets, which sucks when I'm trying to grab food on a dinner break. 

As far as I can tell, no one here seems to openly hate the gay population like the higher ups of this company. But who knows!
Yikes! I had to leave when I saw the cook slapping raw beef down on the grill before he turned around to handle the bread / assemble the sandwiches. Sanitation 101! Gross!

After failing to find Dinics at Reading Terminal Market I decided I needed a cheesesteak, one that was close walking distance to Market street.  I just got done watching Book of Mormon at the Forrest Theatre and was starving.  I looked online and decided to try Campos deli.  I usually don't carry much cash on me so it was a bummer that this place is cash only. While it's nice that they have an arm near the entrance, it's annoying having to pay surcharge to get my money.  Especially since my bank also charges on top of that.  So to the main point.  The girl there was nice and I ordered a cheesesteak philly style with wiz and onions along with jalepenos.  I ordered a side of the Mac and cheese which I was told was a good popular item.  I wanted fries but was informed that they unfortunately don't have any fried items which is good I guess if I was on a diet maybe lol.  So the cheesesteak was pretty good but not (in my opinion) anywhere close to pats/jims or Genoa.  This order was to go and I was disappointed to find that they forgot my Mac and cheese.  So the steak was good but next time I'll get the Italian which I was told by my buddy is way better than their cheesesteaks.  Service was quick so I'd give this 3.5 stars.  Still I wonder how that Mac and cheese would of been

This location is a rip off. They barely put any meat in tacos so all you taste is shell really. No pride or effort put into orders at all. It's obvious their concern is just the money. Naked chicken is nasty as hell too not even cooked properly. Anyone can half fry a chicken patty.
This place is disgusting. I just ordered 2 chicken Parms only to find out they used GRILLED CHICKEN!! Ew!! I put it right in the trash. I'll never come here again.

Better cheesesteak than Sonny's! I had the same type at both restaurants: beef with provolone and onions. Bread at Campo's was moist and chewy in a good way, meat was juicier. Sonny's bread was drier as was the meat. Campo's is a dollar more expensive with no drink refills but worth it. The owner/manager does not smile easily, but she was kind and intent on doing a good job.

Not sure what the people who wrote bad reviews issues are, but they're definitely wrong about this place. I've been to Pat's and Geno's and sure you get super fast service there and it's a good cheesesteak but if you're in Old City and want a cheesesteak, definitely try this place. Went here on recommendation of a friend who hasn't steered me wrong yet and man I'm glad I stopped here. Line was long, but hey it was noon and it's a small place. That just tells me that it must be good. Staff was friendly. The meat seemed to be much higher quality and flavorful compared to what you get down on Passyunk. It was delicious and I would definitely go back.

Don't waste your time here. The staff is so rude. There was a hair in my sandwich and when I brought it back to the register they accused me of putting the hair there myself!!! I am completely disgusted with this place. And to top it off the cheesesteak isn't even that good.

I must say the service here is amazing. Right from the start, a friendly waitress came over and alerted us of the specials. It was a nice buy an appetizer and get a free beer. We quickly ordered and even received a complementary cocktail. Great! The ramen I would say is very average. Nothing too special. Comming from famous ramen places in new york... this place is just "eh". Fortunately, the service is what keeps this place going. Would reccommend it just for a try.

In search of a great ramen restaurant in philly so I was excited to try Hiro Ramen house.
In my opinion the location is horrible.  It's situated behind a bus stop and the restaurant isn't brightly lit and the sign isn't that noticeable. 
Inside the restaurant: small and cozy, resembles a ramen house with a bar in front of the open kitchen and a few tables. 
Ordered : Apps: Seaweed salad and Wasabi Octopus
I ordered the Veggie Ramen added the marinated egg and Cha Su
First the seaweed salad didn't taste that good, it tasted like the ocean.  Not my cupt of tea.  the Octopus was different with a slimy and crunchy texture with a hint of wasabi which made it edible but would not order again.
Now the ramen: the Broth was definitely light and not oily that's the plus with the whole bowl.  The Cha Su tasted gamy and the noodles were not ramen noodles it was more like chinese egg noodles.

Overall: if you are expecting to have a good bowl of ramen than look elsewhere but if you are looking for a good bowl of noodles that is similar to one where you can find in chinatown than give this place a try since toppings are different than a regular chinese noodle house.
Hiro's inch of heaven ramen was awesome. The karaage chicken was so soft and delicious! Definitely an underrated restaurant

Eh this one was okay, had half of a cheese steak from Campo's and another half from Sonny's just 2 doors down.  The cheese steak from Campo's was just not as flavorful.  Some other differences that might sway your vote to either place is Campo's offers beer but not fries.  While Sonny's offers fries but not beer.

If you're looking at just the cheesesteak, it was okay but ive had better, even in San Diego. 
2.5 stars
Expensive, only take cash...it would have been better with the bread being toasted as it was soggy when we got it (who wants to eat a soggy philly cheese?)....

Unpretentious, no-frills, straightforward. JJ's is great for students and anyone on a budget or in a hurry. I appreciate the "Slim" options, sandwiches with just meat and cheese for only $3.50. For hungrier days, I recommend the Hunter Club and the Beach Club. These subs are not the most amazing sandwiches, but JJ's gets an A+ for speedy preparation and fast delivery.

I just moved into Old City about a month ago and while I love it here many of the eateries are geared for the young, hip ,more touristy crowd.  When I finally tried Campo's Deli  I was thrilled ,Finally a really great cheese steak in my neighborhood.  I went with my friend who had been telling me about Campo's homemade soup,,,Boy he wasn't kidding...the Italian Wedding soup is to die for,,,.My best food find in Old City thus far. Will keep you posted.

I stopped in with a friend a couple months ago after getting stuck behind a tour group of 50+ people next door. Campo's was much more tolerable. We were able to immediately place our order and grab a table. My friend and I split one cheesesteak with wiz, no onions. It was cash only and ~$10 total.

The cheesesteak arrived fairly quickly -- but not so fast that I'd question their cooking methods -- and it was quite good. Not the best in the city, but nowhere near the worst either. It served as a nice snack before dinner later on.

Plus everyone working in there is really friendly and the tables clean. It's perfectly located in Old City and is a good spot to visit for First Friday or before a bar crawl down 2nd Street. I'd return and try their hoagies next time.

I just was at the drive-thru and there was a man yelling at one of the workers and I think that's very inappropriate cuz he was cursing him out while we were sitting at the drive-thru when we were listening to him. He told whoever he was talking to that he can f---ing leave right now. I don't know his name he didn't even look like a manager. I work with the public everyday and I don't even talk to nobody like that and I think it's very disrespectful on how he talk to that person and all the cursing that he was doing. The girls at the window was very nice. And had a few other nice choice words to say.

This place is so tasty we actually ordered twice in the same week, two nights in a row.

Their chicken nuggets/tenders are all homemade fresh, which was a great surprise! 

So often "homemade" means "re-heated," but not here!

Their stuffed meatloaf entree and fried chicken entree made us miss our mothers, the food was so tasty and fresh. The sides--we had mac&cheese, mashed potatoes, coleslaw, and greens--were freshly made, not too greasy, and well seasoned.

Their cheesesteak was substantial and tasty; their chicken cutlet sandwich was enormous and well-seasoned and fresh.
From Out of state. Tried both campos and sonny's. I'd go here if you want a cheesesteak. It's more flavorful. Get THE HEATER if you want spicy.

Only gets better. This secretive (only sign is in Japanese) restaurant is tucked away...right on chestnut near 10th. Go. Its marvelous. Sit on the actual wooden furniture & enjoy a nice marvelous bowl of ramen. Real ramen. Not the noodles from your beer & ramen diet in college. 

They are still cash only, but even make room for large parties (special japanese sit IN booths).  Bring friends, and leave exceptionally noodled. 

It would be neat if they had a rotating special menu, but regardless, at once!

This Jimmy John's location was my saving grace during my semester spent at Temple University. The location was clutch and the staff here is so nice.

The service is super fast - once you finish ordering, you wait about five to ten seconds before your sandwich is ready. Prices are reasonable, the sandwiches always taste really fresh and the ingredients are never questionable. I always order their vegetarian sandwich or the Turkey Tom, both of which never disappoint. Also, they have fab chocolate chip cookies and kettle-cooked chips.

The best part of Jimmy John's is their delivery option, and the fact that they are open so late. I was always "that person" would would order Jimmy John's from my Temple dorm room at 1:30 a.m. when I was hanging out with my roommate and wanted something to eat, and they always delivered without a complaint. I definitely miss this place!

Check this one off my list from Philly 
Staff seemed like good people except for the one guy who told me the can was out of order until I let him know I was a customer
On to the food ordered the campo Italian special the sandwich was good, picture looked better on the menu different bread used coming from the land of bodegas and delis did not blow me away would check them out again for the spicy cheesesteak that I heard about

Hospital food, right? No one likes it but I'm telling you...I opt for this any time I needa buy lunch in the area. The food is really cheap and its pretty tasty w/ a changing and fairly extensive menu. Pizzas for $1.75 (its a Sbarro-sized slice), chicken tenders, fish and chips, salad bar, sushi...they got it all. 

They take cash, credit, or money on your owl card or whatever. Only thing is you need to be an employee or student of Temple U. Check. it. out.

The food is awful! I'm writing this review from the restaurant. That's how bad the food really is! The service was approximately two stars.  The food is extremely bland.  I'm beyond disappointed ...on a weekend get-away from the Nation's Capital. :-(
The girl that took our order didn't want to give us condiments. Hunh?  (Originally posted November 2012 under my other Yelp account)
My favorite cheesesteak place in the city of Philadelphia.  But i go more for the chicken sandwiches. Service is fast and friendly, and their desserts are to die for!

I have been to a few ramen houses in NY, like Totto, Ippudo, Minca, so my expectation could be a little bit high. Here's a few bullet points

- Food quality is better than most of ramen houses in Philly IMO.

- I came for lunch but I was not satisfied with its service. I can only order 3 out of 7 ramen in the menu because they run out of some ingredients. OK.

- Broth was OK and better than salty soup I got in ramen bar in university city.

- Pork belly was a little bland and dry

- Last but not least, they have a small piece of raw lemon, which added flavor to the ramen.

We ordered a chef salad for moi, a grilled chicken cesar salad for the Mr., and an order of chicken fingers with bbq sauce that we split.

The chef salad was awesome!  It really had a nice balance of all the components.  Sometimes, you'll get a salad from a pizza place and it's mostly lettuce.  Not here and the salads are big, portion wise.  The only downer was that the hard boiled eggs were cold, while everything else was closer to room temp.  They also use packaged dressing.  The Mr. loved his salad as well.  He wishes they had cesar dressing, however.  The chicken fingers SUCKED!  They were very dry yet didn't have any crisp.  Then, the meat was chewy in places and tough in others.  The bbq sauce was ok, but a little bland for my liking.  Ordering was a breeze with Grub Hub and it arrived before our estimated time.  So, a good experience overall and we will likely order from them again.

Update:  Picked up an order of The Original Tomy's Fries today.  Heaven!  Lots of cheesey and bacony goodness.  The fries weren't overly greasy or cold.  The portion is big and you could easily feed 2 people with the large size.  You might not want to share, though!

Update 2:  I'm dropping a star from my review.  I ordered a cheese and sauce stromboli yesterday.  Given the name, you would think there would be sauce right?  WRONG!  There wasn't a drop of sauce.  You have to order sauce on the side, for an extra cost of course.  Why on earth would you name it a cheese and sauce stromboli, when the sauce costs extra?  That is incredibly deceptive to customers, and shady to boot.  I will definitely think twice before ordering from here again.

ONE OF THE BEST RAMEN PLACE IN PHILLY!!! I highly recommend going before 4pm because thats when their lunch special is offered. 13$ for an app, salad and ramen. ALL DELICIOUS!! Their restaurant is pretty small so I don't recommend this to large groups of over 10 people. After 2pm the place is empty-ish, so if you're looking to avoid the crowd this is the time frame to come.

Been coming to this ramen house for years on end and have been to many ramen places in Philadelphia. Yet none of them came close to the quality of ramen this place has. Not only is the food tremendous but the ambiance is quite nice. Giving you the classy feeling of a traditional old-fashioned Japanese ramen bar in Japan. The food all tastes fresh and will fill you up but I do recommend getting seconds because it is just so good. I recommend gates of hell and black pig and the gyoza and karrage is perfect.

This is part of the Crusade for Greatest Cheesesteak in Philadelphia trip I did. Campo's Deli was the 7th stop on our list. Meter parking is around the area of this place with it cost between 2.50 and 3 bucks a hour to park. When we went inside they had a bathroom, seats and it was all inside. All pluses, the cheesesteaks ordered with whiz came out quick. They also had some cannoli's that they touted were fresh made and hand filled on the spot.  

The cheesesteaks were good, the cheese was thin and really got ever where, I heard that they weren't the most friendly people I would disagree, I heard napkins were a commodity, they had a dispenser out for you to take them. The steaks were smaller but full, it was solid sandwich. 

I did venture to get the cannoli's here, they talked them up so I had to try one. The first thing that turned me off was when I ordered the steak they have a display out for the cannoli's I asked how much were they and the girl whom I was assuming the granddaughter since it was her grandfather's filling said 4 dollars. Thinking that was a good price when we were done with the steaks I order the a cannoli, she yells in the back two cannoli's, and then try to charge me 9 bucks. I was a little shock and said to her you just told me 4 like 15 minutes ago, which she responded oh that's for just one, did you just want one? Yes, yes I did. So she cancels one of them and I get mine. First thing I notice is that they are very fresh, when you bite into them you can taste the freshness of the ingredients. You can also tell they are homemade, generally another perk. But there was something about this cannoli that I just didn't like. I didn't think it was bad at all, and maybe the girl hyped it up to much, but even if it was only 2 dollars for a cannoli here I don't think I would order it again.

Being an out of towner... the first thing on my mind when I got off that Greyhound was CHEESESTEAK!   (Sorry family, you'll have to wait).

I've heard that you're either a Geno's or a Pat's kind of person and that's it.
I tried both, even dragged them back to NY on the bus for my boyfriend to sample the both and we weren't too pleased with either.  (geno's over pat's btw).

Back in Philly for the second time and was told to try Jim's and Campo's this time around.  
My boyfriend and I were more than happy to sample both.  I can't tell you much about Jim's as it was a drunken memory.  

Campo's though... I guess I can't rate what the best of the best is, but they were definitely a cut above the other 3.  In particular the Chicken Cheesesteak.   And this is even after it sat on the bus for 2 hours.   

This was all in April and needless to say i didn't want to see another cheesesteak for a very long time after.   I'm planning a trip to Philly again and I think I'm ready for the next round....  Campo's is in the near future.
I cannot believe we have wawa, it totally makes  my  lunch break even more joyful :)))))

Is it better than Pat's and Geno's? Sure it is. But it is was not worth the $8+ bucks that I paid for a cheesesteak with fried onions.  They charge extra for the hot peppers.  And no fries.  For a better deal (and MUCH better flavor)  my advice is Jim's on South Street, Tony Jr's. on Rittenhouse Square or Abner's in University City.

Came here early morning after arriving from NYC. Staffs are not that friendly. Food is okay. They open an hour earlier than Sonny's so that's the reason why we were there. The decor is warm and inviting. 
My boyfriend had the classic cheesesteak, I had mine with mozzarella. We also tried their salad. Not bad. Not that good either.

Meh. Didn't care for the vegetable ramen soup. This review is based on my vegan opinion of the soup. The soup consists of mostly just noodles. Where are the veggies?! Just some watercress and another vegetable. I'm not certain but I thought ramen noodles had the ingredients of egg in them but our server told us otherwise. Other than the soup it's a nice spot for a lunch  or a quick bite for dinner with a nice hip atmosphere.

I really didn't have a good experience here, especially in terms of the food. 

1. I specifically asked for my hiro ramen without the pork shoulder, subbed with tofu... and they serve be the ramen with 2 slabs of pork shoulder. 

2. tbh, the ramen really wasn't that tasty. I'm no ramen expert, but simply didn't like the taste. 

I hope they improve, but I really have no desire to go back and give them another chance.

We went here on a whim on a Monday afternoon. The place was quiet and clean. The waiter was very friendly to us. Ordering is easy enough because they just have ramen dishes. The other thing that was cool about this place was the imported soda choices. For a good price you get a big bowl of ramen with delicious broth, noodles, and whatever extra toppings you decide to add (For an additional price.) The only problems were that the seats are wooden stools and that can hurt the rear end after awhile and they only accepted cash (which we were informed of before even walking in by the big sign they posted).

Decent ramen. I ordered the miso pork ramen which came with corn, bean sprouts, bamboo shoots, a slice of fatty pork, and scallions. I also added an egg, which brought the total to to $11 (gulp!). Delicious broth that wasn't overly salted, good texture to the noodles, great flavour to the pork and marinated soft-boiled egg. Certain ingredients were cold at first, which led me to believe they assemble the bowl and let the broth warm stuff up... not spectacular, given that I like my food piping hot.

I was the only one in the restaurant at the time, so the server kept checking to make sure that I was enjoying my meal. Sweet, if a little over the top.

Cash only, great happy hour special ($6 for a glass of sake/beer and an appy), super comfortable ambiance (Japanese-style wood paneling and curtains, etc).

We came here on the recommendation of a friend, who raved about the Gates of Hell. I ordered that and my wife ordered the Inch of Heaven. While both were tasty, I preferred the GoH. The spice didn't overwhelm the flavor of the broth and the noodles had a nice chewiness. This place didn't blow my mind, but I would return if every other nearby restaurant were closed.

Customer service was just terrible. Refused us water on an 80 degree day, and offered their own bottled water for $2.50 instead. 

Told me I didn't meet their credit card minimum and I was less than a dollar below. Told the customer behind me it was okay because they were friends.

i was thoroughly disgusted with my sandwich from campo's - soggy and (besides the extreme overdose of parm cheese) very bland.  not to mention the service was poor.  they messed up our takeout order and ended up charging us for an extra sandwich.  very expensive too (even for olde city).  keep your distance

The customer service is always great. 
It's clean all the time.
The food is pretty decent. 
But today I found something metal in my vegetarian quesadilla. Luckily I wasn't chewing like a horse and didn't damage my teeth. I usually don't have things like this happen to me... if only I found a winning lottery ticket in my quesadilla.

Experiencing ramen in Philadelphia has become a hobby of mine. Fortunately for me, Hiro Ramen is located down the street from where I work and I welcome it with open arms every rainy day.
The location is secretive and easy to pass by if you aren't careful, but once you enter the doors the ambiance if very warm and the employees super friendly.
I have gotten both the Shoyu and the Vegetarian Ramen. Both are amazing and satisfy different moods...depending on whether you are craving more of a hearty meat flavor or a lighter soup.
What I think sets Hiro away from other ramen shops is its broth. I find the broth here much more savory and hearty. All other ingredients are great quality as well.

Best ramen in philly. Very traditional style and I prefer it over any other ramen place in philly. The place is small and hidden -- another reason it is a prized secret. Beautiful interior. They don't skimp on flavor.

I love potbelly sandwich shop. The young girl with brown hair at the cash register is very sweet and apologized to me over and over again because I waited one minute for my online order food to be ready! And she brought it out to me! Great service at this restaurant.
Pass on this location sub par staff and rude cashier Tanisha I believe her name is. Very poor service for a place on temple campus. See my Google review as well.

The two stars is being lenient. This place is FUGAZZI. The steaks they give you are very small and actually taste worse than the ones they serve at the ballpark that have been sitting for an hour. Portions were small, taste was average and price was HUGE for what they gave me. Its a better deal at the ballpark and that's saying much cause prices are inflated there.

One star for the outside seating on market st and one star for the ballpark steaks (Heater is OK). 

Bottom line- This place doesn't even crack the top 30 in the city

I'm a fan of Campo's. Do they make the best sandwich ever? No. But I like it here.

They've always gotten my order right, and I've always been satisfied enough with my food that I went back often when I was working in Olde City.

If you do some hunting in South Philly, you can do better than Campo's, but if you're just looking for a quick fix, it's definitely one of the better options on Market St.

I really liked eating here and want to go back! The atmosphere is super cute and intimate. Great for a date or catching up with friends. The ramen is fantastic and the portions are pretty big. Last time I could only finish about half and brought the rest home.

I ordered from this place through diningin.com. I've never been inside.  I would not recommend it just based off of my order.  

I ordered the chicken cutlet sandwich but I paid a dollar extra to have the bread substitute with romaine lettuce...yea that didn't happen.  The sandwich was very greasy and made my stomach hurt I only ate half of it too.  Also the chicken...not a chicken was not a chicken cutlet it was just greasy chicken breast. A chicken cutlet is meant to be breaded.  I also ordered the tomato with risotto rice soup which at almost 5 dollars is so not worth it.

I love this place!! I've been here probably like 20 times and I've never had anything I didn't like! The mac and cheese is amazing, I'm pretty much obsessed with the chicken parm, and everything else I've ever eaten here has been great too! I'm sort of a finicky eater, but if I stray from the chicken parm  or a burger, they always take the time to get it right. The workers are great, service is friendly and fast. This is definitely one of my favorite places to eat when I want something quick. Can't say enough good things about Campo's, but I think their food and staff speaks for itself!!

Was in Philly yesterday with my family to celebrate a birthday, and we went to Campo's for lunch. Have been here many times, and the meal was a request of the birthday boy. As always, friendly service with a recommendation to try something--in this case the terrific, homemade potato salad. It was perfect! The steaks were as good as always--not greasy, good bread, good portions of flavorful steak, cheese and for those of us who got the hoagies, onions, tomatos, and lettuce. Service was superb, despite a line out the door. The cashier was friendly and helpful, and we got personal attention from several other employees, including Mr. Campo, who wanted to make sure our lunch was everything it should be--had a very nice conversation! It's where we eat whenever we are in Philly--easily the best!

WORST cheesesteak I have ever had. Hands down. And one of the worst sandwiches I can recall in my 48 years on this earth. I am a generous reviewer... I don't think I've ever given less than 4 Stars in my Yelp Career. Let me cut to the chase... fatty, thick meat, stale rolls, and red stuff on my roll. I can only pray it was red sauce from a separate sandwich. I'm a local guy and this was horrible. I have no axe to grind, but $11 for a crappy Cheesesteak is horrible. To the Dude behind the counter, TRIM THE FAT OFF THE SANDWICHES..!

Major disappointment!!!  $9.50 for a Cheesesteak Works (grilled peppers, mushrooms and onions) with provolone.  The roll was good, the flavors okay but it was skimpy on the meat .. definitely not worth the $.  
We also had a Chicken Works ..the chicken was tasteless and there couldn't have been even 3 ounces of meat on it for $9.50!!
Further, the side dish of macaroni was dreadful ..dried out and hard and bland...all that for $4.00 for the side!
A complete and utter disapointment.  
We make better Philly Cheesesteaks at home Arizona!
Service was great, very friendly and helpful in deciding what to order.  Food was quick and delicioys.  High bang for the buck if looking for delicious takeout.

I would give this negative stars if I could. They pinch you for every penny they have. We came in with a group of three who all purchased cheesesteaks. They refused to give us a cup of water out of the soda machine and made us buy bottled water for $2.50 instead. Also, at the end of her $15 meal (a cheesesteak and bottle of water), my friend asked if she could use the bathroom and an employee told her that she had to pay $1 to use it! She told him she wasn't paying and he let her use it for free. 

 The cheesesteak was cold, bland and overpriced. Literally go to any greasy food truck in philly and you will get a better cheesesteak for half the price. This place is a disgrace.

Really good cheesesteak! It's not all ground to nothing, you can actually tell it's meat. Super fresh bread and delicious flavor. I didn't try any of the sides, but I heard they were good too. Only downside is that there isn't a whole lot of seating, so if it's busy, prepare to stand and eat or wait for a table. I suggest Campos
They have a DELICIOUS vegetarian cheesesteak!! Definitely going to return the next time I'm in Philly.

Down in the historic section of Philly with my family and was looking for a quick bite. I inquired about a close by place for cheese steak and was pointed towards Campo's.

I wanted to like it as I have been told that there are much better places than the traditional Geno's or Pats. Well I was disappointed.  

The bread was somewhat stale, the steak overcooked and it was on the small size for an $9.25 sandwich. To add to this, I did a Yelp check-in once we placed the order and were waiting for the food to be ready. I saw a special that said "mention Yelp and receive a 10% discount". I went back up and asked if they would honor it. I was told nicely, sorry had to be told that before I rang you up. Seriously, in this day the manager cant empower it's employees to provide a discount after its been rung up? If its a cash register thing than throw a customer a dessert on the house or something.  Needless to say, I won't be back next time I'm in Philly.
Not the best but since there's few choice in center city for Ramen, this one is pretty good!!
Best Cheesesteak I've ever had ! Bread was very soft which was also a plus. Meat was very moist, not dry like other cheesesteaks I've tried. Cash Only!
great food! and open late, best hoagies on south street!

I went to Campo's Deli and had the Vegan works cheesesteak and it was awesome.  The bread was delicious and all of the ingredients were very fresh and high quality. I can say it was the best vegetarian cheesesteak I ever had and I would highly recommend it.  The staff was very friendly and the menu has several vegetarian options.
Yummmmmmmy! Prices are so great and the food is so good to the price. We try to get Spice Box whenever we are craving Indian and Chinese food. It's the perfect place for spice in one's life.

The food is great but the girl behind the counter is so rude to the customer. I guess she is the daughter of the owner that is why she is still there. There are many bad comments about her the way she handles service to the customer. She needs to be fired. I will never go back there again as long as that girl is still there taking orders.
cash only they say at the end when you go to pay. look, if your a business traveler that's a hassle to have to keep up with all that when you are on an expense account. come ON!
Really good food and service , called and picked up in 15min. The achari paneer roll and chicken tikka roll is the best . Make sure you get the white sauce , can't do without it.

Decent size, small but cozy.  Not a bad place to grab a quick bowl of steaming ramen. However, I still like Terakawa in Chinatown more. I think there's more meat, a more generous portion size, and a bit more selection at Terakawa. That said, if you don't feel like trekking to 9th/Race, this is a good substitute.

Revisit: 3/31/18 fries hot and crispy
Order correct. They have ketchup.  They said thank you.  Dont bother going to the other fast food restaurants on this corner-this MCD is run better than all of them including even the Chili's

This was one of my several favorite cheesesteaks in Philadelphia. Sonny's next door had a huge line, but the ultimate factor was a comment by a local that this place had better tasting one's and served BEER. My mind was set. Grabbed a cold beer and Wit cheese, onions. Did not disappoint and was great for lunch time while touring old city!

This is by far the best ramen in Center City, and my personal favorite ramen place out of all the ones I have tried! The portions are quite large for the price that you are paying. The ramen is also filled with so much toppings that you might not finish! The broth is also well made.  My favorites are the Heaven and the Hell.  The Hell isn't that spicy. I would rank it a 4 out of 10 spice wise with the 10 being really spicy.  This place is cash only and has an atm outside. I will not go to any other ramen place other than this.

Yummy black pig ramen!  A little salty, but otherwise super tasty, and the ramen was perfect. We also and the takoyaki  (octopus in fried batter) which was really tasty as well. The green tea was very grassy and good, just like I like it. We also tried one of the Japanese sodas. It's BYOB so bring your own beer or sake.

Revisit: 3/31/18 fries hot and crispy
Order correct. They have ketchup.  They said thank you.  I'm hoping all of the reasons for closure listed below were fixed before I ate here.
McDonald's #02444, 2400 Oregon Ave.
15 violations 8 serious
An employee was observed picking the nose and returning to food preparation without washing hands; an employee was drinking and eating food in the food preparation area and despite repeated warnings did not desist from the practice; an employee was smoking less than 10 feet from the main entrance door; food was held at 70 degrees rather than 41 degrees; there was an open sewage line in the female toilet room area where the floor has been dug up and pipes are collapsed. Sewage smell was present inside facility though suppressed by some chemicals; visible physical evidence of insect activity observed throughout the facility; black residue, pink slime observed on the interior of the ice machine bin; interior of walk-in cooler and freezer in need of cleaning.
Due to conditions observed during the inspection, the establishment agreed to discontinue food operations and voluntarily close until it is approved by the Department to resume operations. Inspected on Oct. 6.

Indoor tailgate at Primos? I know it sounds crazy, but consider this your pro insider tip for sports fans without tickets to the game who are also smart enough not to stand in the frigid winter temperatures waiting for what's sure to be a cold grilled burger.

Great tailgates include hoagies. The best tailgates include hoagies and beer. I don't associate with people that don't like either of the above so if you're in the minority you're not allowed at the new South Street Primos; I'm making it my unofficial official South Street clubhouse...password not required, but a love for the tailgate is a must. Hoagies. Beer. TV's. Indoor plumbing. Heat. No brainer...see ya there :)

No stars!!! I came to Campos visiting Philly from AZ and there was a huge hair and small bug in MY PHILLY Cheesesteak!!!!! I had heard that they don't give refunds and politely asked for a new sandwich and he said he could "just pick out the bug for me" was he kidding?!??? Ewww will meet eat here again worst experience eating a Philly Cheeaeteak for the first time!! They are very unsanitary. Please if you care for your health do not!

This place is terrible. $30 for two cheesesteaks and a side salad. The meat was flavorless and fatty. And yes, we had cheese on it. I got the cheesesteak with wiz and grilled onions, and Husband got the Ice Steak with grilled onions. The gluten free bun was still partially frozen and disgusting. We threw those away (after paying extra for it), and ate the meat with a fork - dipped in salad dressing to give it some flavor. I sure hope this doesn't really represent an authentic Philly cheesesteak. If so, bleh! The ones I made as a short order cook in San Diego 25 years ago were way better.

I went here because it was so close to the Lowe's hotel and the reviews looked pretty decent. Place has a nice authentic japanese feel to it. Reminded me of many of the ramen place I would go to when I lived in Japan.  I ordered the pig and miso ramen and some tako-yaki. The tako-yaki was spot on and done just right. The pig and miso ramen broth was a little oily and could have had a little more flavor too it. Especially being a miso ramen it could have been a little saltier. The noodles we good, but were not made in house. Over all I thought it was a pretty decent meal. It did not not blow me away but it was satisfying. And at $10 a bowl it's a bargain. I would defiantly go again. Just remember though it is cash only and BYOB.
Campo's had a good cheeseteak and there are many other options as well. Though there was a line in the small restaurant, the wait wasn't too bad and the staff was nice. No complaints!
If you are looking for a nice place to drink and eat you want to come to this PRIMOS.  Tiff the bartender is awesome and makes a mean drink!  Love the conversation, love the food!

Jimmy johns is great. Reasonably good sandwiches and delivery time can't be beat. I've received a sandwich in under 6 minutes. You get what you pay for, in a very fast manner! The only reason I didn't give it that last star was because it's just regular sandwiches. Lets get some gourmet sandwiches in there! some seasoning goes a long way!

I over heard the bartender & lady behind the counter talking about the way I ordered. When I was polite & patient with the store being busy. As I walked up, they stopped talking awkwardly & made a transaction in silence. I will never be back here. & it's sad because I actually like the hoagies. Oh well...  I can get a hoagie elsewhere. Be sure to treat EVERY client with respect & understanding. Here they failed to do so.

It's true this place earns at least half a star just for being close to me. This happens to be the only place I've had ramen since I moved to Philly, and in LA there is no shortage of great ramen houses. The portion here is a little small at least compared to LA, but that works out perfectly for me. Last night I had the spicy miso, which wasn't especially noticeably heavy on miso. Wasn't too spicy either, but enough that I got the idea and could still comfortably drink the broth. The noodles were pretty chewy, I like ramen noodles a little softer generally, but I think this was probably the right texture for normal ramen snobs. 

What I am going to rave about is their "dinner specials." For six dollars, they give you a beer or cold sake, and a bar snack sized plate. Last night we tried the seaweed salad, takoyaki, and wings. I'm terribly indecisive, and places like this are a blessing. The waitress accidentally brought me a sake instead of an asahi, I said it was fine, but she brought me an asahi after that anyway, sake bomb!

The deal is essentially like any bar that offers 3 dollar beers and 3 dollar bar bites for happy hour, but 1) Asian flavors, and 2) we were able to take advantage of this well after normal happy hour ends.

cash only though so keep that in mind!

Great sandwich shop franchise.  Chipotle may brag about it's organic ingredients, but in terms of objective quality, Primos has them beat.

While you'll never get a bad sandwich from a Primos hoagie shop, you can easily find superior sandwiches if you're in the south Philly area.  If you're out in Jerz or other outskirts, you're probably better off with the somewhat uninspired but consistently above average Primos.
Taste is just plain and no twist. I don't know why the store is popular. Service isn't that good either. I should go to a different store.

Not the best, not the worst.. As far as the cheesesteak goes... The meat was done right, Juicy and not burnt. The problem was lack of flavor from the meat. I got my steak with American and fried onions. I had really no complaint. The cheese was spread just enough and the onions were great. The price is a little steep with a drink included but what else is new in this city.

So the reason for the 5 stars is because the of the food and service. 

So my BF and I had a lay over 1/21/2009 in Philly on our way back for DC and wanted to get an "authentic" Philly Cheese steak, and the people we talked to in Philly suggested we go to Geno's. We did and we were pretty disappointed. My brother-in-law sent a text and suggested we go check out Campo's and order the Italian sub and pretzels. We did and we also ordered a cheese steak with the works. The cheese steak was so good. Much better then Geno's. We took the Italian Sub and Pretzels to go and on the flight home we devoured it all. The Italian sub was delicious. Probably one of the best I've had. The pretzels with the homemade mustard were very tasty. 

Ladies behind the counter were really nice and very helpful. 

Thank you for the great experience :).

When you just can't decide which creature you'd like to eat, try Campo's Stockyard Sandwich. 

A heaping meat melange of chicken, steak, pepperoni, bacon, fried onions and mascarpone cheese served on an Italian roll....  definitely recommend sharing this thing, just to postpone your inevitable heart attack for a few hours. 

Very tasty and the service was quite friendly.  I've heard they have vegetarian items but really,  I was just there to eat the faces off the helpless barnyard critters.

Somehow, customer service gets worse every damn time.


I've never seen a person work harder at doing the barest minimum.

Took nearly 20 minutes to get my sandwich and 10 to get her to acknowledge I needed to pay.

Next time, I'm not going to go out of my way to pay. If you want payment, don't ignore me when I have my orange card out and ready.

Visiting Philly and stopped here with some local  friends.
Cheesesteak was great, which is why the review isn't 1 star, but the service was pretty poor.
Was waiting in line to order, my friends out their order in in front of me, then the person working the counter asked the person two people behind me for their order, skipping myself and another person. 
Not sure if he was a regular that they knew, but that made no sense.
Waiting a solid 10-15min to get my sandwich, and the person that they took the order for was halfway done with their sandwich by the time I even got mine.

Philly's ramen scene is not that vast but decent to make Hiro Ramen House enjoyable.

They say with every good ramen is the importance of the broth.  So far I've tried 2 of the options that they offer which was the Gates of Hell (my favorite but extremely spicy) and the Inch of Heaven (very thick/rich).  Both very good and very different. You definitely have to be a fan of pork as a lot of the broth is made from Berkshire pork and be able to take the richness of the broth.  Fatty but not overly greasy.  Be sure not to order too much since 1 bowl of ramen is very filling.

I enjoyed my experience here and the ambiance is really cozy.

The cashier was extremely rude and had obviously had it with the heat and all the orders.  I've been there but don't be short with customers.  If you don't like working there or with people leave. Cheesesteaks were sub par.  Also very little room.
Place can be a bit cramped and it's not cheap. But the food is good and they have several vegetarian choices.

I went here with some friends a few weeks ago. Being from New Jersey, I've only had the chance to experience Qdoba about two or three other times at different locations and had great experiences with both the food and service. Unfortunately, this trip went a little differently. 

I walked into Qdoba at around 2 o'clock, just before the Temple rush. There was no line and I was helped immediately. Since I am extremely unfamiliar with their menu, I took about 5 seconds to browse it. (The only menu in the store I might add, located behind the counter above the cashier.) This angered the first member of what later turned out to be an assembly line of assholes. After making a condescending/sarcastic remark about me not knowing what I wanted, he proceeded to place my grilled chicken into a wrap and slide it to asshole #2. 

Asshole #2 introduced herself to me by mumbling a noise I couldn't understand, after politely asking her to repeat what she had just muttered, she blurted out 3 salsa options to me in a very rude demeanor. I chose my salsa, apologized (again) and continued with my order. She continued to fill my burrito with the contents of my choosing and moved down the line. As we got to the end, I made a final request for some rice. Rather than taking the 2 seconds in would take to put a scoop of rice into my burrito, she angrily said "OH NOW YOU TELL ME". I assumed she had to have been joking, but it turned out I was wrong. I again apologized and got nothing in return. Extremely annoyed, she then proceeded to slide my tray to Asshole #3.

Asshole #3 blurted out the 11 dollar and some change total that my order had come to and handed me a cup that I never ordered. Feeling very uncomfortable and almost bullied, I handed him cash, got my change, waited for the thank you I never got, and left the line feeling about the same size as the brain of the person who manages this fine establishment, very small. 

As I approached the soda fountain to fill up the cup I never ordered and was charged for, I was greeted by a bucket of ice, an uncovered container of cut lemons, and an enormous family of flies that decided to land all over both. 

Disgusted, I sat in the nearest booth and waited for my friends. The wall my booth had been up against was COVERED in food residue. I don't know if a food fight had gone on between the degenerate employees before I arrived or what but the flies sure didn't seem to mind. 

I know what you're probably imaging me as right now and I honestly am not that. I am a hardworking 22 year old that just wanted a chicken burrito. My ordering process took literally about 45 seconds at the most and could have been 15 seconds with a positive, smart, and polite employee working that day. I will never walk inside a Qdoba again and it really is a shame because that burrito was BANGING.

The cheesesteaks were pretty good, but nothing spectacular. A little light on the meat, no ice water and plan on bringing cash.

There is something that get's to me about a place that doesn't serve a beverage that happens to be the most plentiful on the earth!

Very disappointed in this cheesesteak experience. Not only did I find the waitstaff to be rude the cheesesteaks were less than par. The meat didn't taste like real cheesesteak meat at all and left me with an odd after taste. I should have listened to the reviews and went elsewhere.
Great Family who love to tell you the history of the philly steak sandwich
I've been craving soft pretzels since I came into town. These were stale and cold and somehow both soggy and hard. Blech.
