Good ramen. Staff was friendly and attentive, we didn't have to wait long for anything, and our drinks never went empty. 
I had the Hiro Inch of Heaven ramen. Everything about it was awesome EXCEPT, the pork was incredibly tough. Tough to the point that I almost couldn't bite a piece off without a lot of effort. Everything else about the ramen was great though. The broth was AMAZING! One of the best I've ever had. Noodles were good and plentiful, and the rest of the ingredients were good. You won't leave hungry.
This place would rate 5 stars if it wasn't for the shoe-leather consistency of the pork, and the fact that they don't take credit cards. I'd go back.

It's taken me a hot minute to visit this Potbelly, and I'm pretty much regretting every lunch that I ate elsewhere on campus.

First, this place is nice and big! You shouldn't have a problem securing a table.

Second, the lines are long, but they move pretty quickly. I got the chicken and cheddar on flatbread, and was very pleased with the size of my sandwich. It was completely an acceptable portion size - not too much and not too little - and it was simply delish!

The cheddar and broccoli soup was probably extremely bad for me, but it tasted super cheesy and great.

They have fresh baked cookies and dream bars, and their smoothies come with two little cookies with holes in the center so they can go over your straw (how cute!).

I truly loved it here. Sandwiches of all types, salads, soups, and desserts. What more could you need?

There is limited seating, but I haven't had any trouble getting seated on week nights. Myhusband and I love the Takoyaki here. The portion is huge and they are so tasty. Perfectly fried, with a little piece of octopus nestled inside perfectly pillowy potato. Their Karaage chicken app looks ridiculous and I will be trying it out on my next visit for sure. 

Now, what we're all here for: The Ramen. I like to toss it up between Terakawa and Hiro as the pork broth at Terakawa can be a little heavy for my mood at times. For this reason I really dig the Portfilio Ramen at Hiro. The Pork/Chicken broth is still super flavorful without that heaviness of your typical pork bone broth. The noodles are a little past al dente but still perfectly fine. The Portfilio comes with corn, chasu (pork), chilli oil, scallions, bamboo shoots, garlic, rice cake, and lemon. It is VERY garlicky so I recommend removing a little bit of the minced garlic that comes atop your bowl before mixing everything in. Voila, a perfect end to a chilly night or just a tasty treat to satisfy a noodley soup craving. 

I would definitely recommend trying out Hiro as it is a worthy contender in the Philly Ramen scene. Enjoy!

I love the location in Center City, but this location (at least at lunch) is a joke.

I've come here three times. Each time, the bartender (really, given the layout, the ambassador) has been cold at best, rude at worst.

The apathy of professionalism emanating from her is palatable.

As I write this, she has been gone, without explanation to even her coworkers, for 20, minutes.

To be fair, she was explaining to her friend about how she was to sick to give a blowjob last night. So she has a lot on her mind.

Whoever owns this location should review lunch security tapes and send someone they trust to review the midday.

It's incredibly sad. I'm going to find a new sandwich place to spend my lunch hours I work in this neighborhood.

Been there after maybe not going there for a few months. I had an eggplant parm.  Wife had a BLT.  

The quality of their bread has gone downhill - tasted like very soft bread with no crunch on the crust.  Eggplant parm had lots of sauce and lots of mozz and not much eggplant.

BLT was double decker.  Quality of bread not great.  Here we are in the middle of veggie season, and mediocre quality of tomato and lettuce.  And who heard of a BLT with no mayo.

Sorry Campo's - you were a go to place but perhaps no longer.

Sometimes it is necessary to write a glowing recommendation.  We recommend Campo's to everyone.  For friends heading downtown, we say there is no better cheese steak in Philly Old Town.  However, the reason we are writing today is to say that Campo's is ridiculously CLEAN!!!  As a guy who has been to almost all of the Cheesesteak places in Philly, we can say Campo's is the cleanest.  So, if you care about quality food and quality facilities this is one place you have to check out.

Well...our first trip to Philly.  We had a wonderful time, love the history.  Stopped in at Campo's after the doorman at our hotel suggested their cheesesteaks.  We weren't disappointed....so good, and the cannoli were made right there by the owner...delicious!  Will come back if we ever have the opportunity.

A 2.5 more-so...sometimes that half star is really helpful. Only because it wasn't THAT bad. But it certainly wasn't that great. They consistently have two ramen choices, shoyu or miso, and one day they were out of the miso, so that made my choice pretty clear. This place is very close to my work, so in theory it's like a dream come true- a ramen place literally right across the street?? This is probably what keeps me coming back here. It's a quick lunch that satisfies that noodle/ramen craving at the moment. And their service is quick, no fuss, and always pleasant. 

But as far as taste, both times I went the broth was too salty, without enough depth in flavor. The noodles were not bad, a bit al dente, and fresh. The pork didn't have much flavor to it, tasted more like it had been in broth a bit too long. And halfway through the bowl I usually hit my salt threshold and what becomes hunger quickly is replaces by thirst. If I had to choose, I would pick the miso of the shoyu, just because it has a little more flavor (but still high in the salt content).

6 / 11 of my cheesesteak pilgrimage (see my list!)

A healthy cheesesteak place with a warm atmosphere and indoor seating?  Is this the twilight zone of Philly?

Ok, it isn't healthy, but they are proud to say they don't serve anything fried.  When I was there I got the home made mac and cheese instead, which was good (but a bit cold).  Staff was nice and cordial, and I was actually able to catch some Idol as I ate.

I thought the whiz-wit I had was pretty good, but I was more impressed by the cheesesteak hoagie my sister got (whiz, lettuce, onion and tomato).  I think Campo's is the only place that can offer up a cheesesteak with fresh vegetables and not be completely hypocritical, so props for that.

Protip: A perfect time to come here is when you're walking around Old City...we signed up for the walking Constitutional tour and ate here before the tour started.  Driving here sucks because parking is so expensive.

Fresh out of the oven...

Tried the new pretzel nuggets and these tasted great with the cheese dip.
Also loved the blueberry lemonade.
Not a perfect 5 since I paid about $8 and it was not too filling.
Workers are very efficient and the line flies by.

Fast service, good food, and reasonable prices! 

Try 'em!

yes I know what you are thinking....she gave Taco Bell 4 stars, but hey for cheap tacos it's ok and they actually have a bean version for vegetarians. when you are in that $1 taco stuff your face mode, and loco pez doesn't have $1 taco night, then this satisfies the craving.
oh and did I mention the staff was nice so they get props in my star rating for that too
You want a Philly cheesesteak! This is the spot to come! Cool part is that they mention that nothing is fried at their location! That's a cool and healthy!
Real good Philly cheesesteak, but comes at a slightly higher price than elsewhere. Nice neighborhood for wandering around.

I've had two bad experiences already, but I wanted to like this place since I live so close. $13 lunch special sounds like a deal, but the best thing about it is the salad. The lunch special gets you three pieces of karaage. Every Ramen broth here is too salty. The chasu pork is sliced so thin that it feels like you're just eating fat. 

I ordered the portfolio which is described as having lemon (and comes with a lemon slice). When I asked for one more lemon slice to cut some of that saltiness, the waitress said they were out of lemon slices. There was like one other person eating there. That's really weird. Where did my single lemon slice come from...

Then a cockroach crawled out from the kitchen towards me at the bar. The waitress said I looked so scared as she killed it. I was actually just surprised that this meal was so bad. 

Gave it a chance. Not coming back.

Had cheese steak! Meat had no flavor, 80% bread! One of the worst cheese steaks I've ever had! Very cheap and uncomfortable seating! $ 15+ for a san beach and a root beer ? Fine if it was good! Never again

This Chick-Fil-A just opened in fall 2009 so don't beat yourself too much over not knowing that there was one in University City.  It's an "express" location so it doesn't have all of the menu items.  It's located in a standalone area on the Drexel campus w a few other fast food places.  I would've given this location three stars for not having all of the items, but it gets an extra one for its proximity to Penn/Drexel.
We loved the Philly Heater and Chicken Heater. Food came pretty quickly, was made fresh and served hot.

We all know of Primo, the wonderful local hoagie chain that fills our lives with sandwiches galore, and good ones at that. The extra exciting thing about having a Primo Hoagies in proximity is that, for one thing, Primo stays open well past the times when all other decent hoagie places are closed and snoozing snug in their beds.

Hoagie hunger never sleeps. Hey world, sometimes the ole gal fancies a delicious Italian hoagie, or a chicken cutlet sandwich, or my go-to Turkey with Cooper Sharp, lettuce, tomato, and long hots... after 4 PM. 

Primo reliably comes through cause they're open at night. Night hoagies, for ya. Particularly, it's highly helpful that they're open til 2AM Friday and Saturday. This South Street spot is always quick and friendly friendly with the service, and clean as a whistle, too.

This Primo locale has a good amount of seating, if you wanna eat in. Oh, and they have a full bar. Primo's wit a bar. That's something, for ya. They have cheapo PBR pounders, when you're in need, like for instance, while you're waiting for your hoagie. So parched, a powerful thirst....

Newly realized by me was this exciting factoid: This location has a hoagie happy hour.

HOAGIE HAPPY HOUR! That's a winning combo. 

Commit this info to memory:

Between the hours of 5-8PM, weekdays, all Primo sized hoagies are $5.99. The only caveat is that you have to eat in. You gotta order from the bar to get that bargain hoagie price. Not a bad place to be, as hoagie happy hour also features beer and drink specials too. I gots nooo problem enjoying a few while watching ESPN.
The $10 relatively small-sized cheesesteak is uninspiring and overpriced.  Steve's remains the best.
Horrible service. The employees behave like they are doing favors by working there. Management should check on the employees and the service.

Lousy. Primo's has an excellent selection of sandwiches, but this location is straight up awful. Only reason I chose this spot was because the Ritner st location was already closed. Can't tell the difference between a tomato and a hot pepper?? Hoagies are skimpy and cost more. Ritner st location is WAY better!! Thick hoagies and cheaper

Don't come here during lunch/dinner rush! 

The food is okay. If you have never been to Qdoba before, they have the regular Mexican-chained foods: burritos, tacos (3), quesadilla, burrito bowl.... If you like spending $7.50 on 3 puny tacos, be my guest. I suggest getting the burrito or burrito bowl. Fill them up with whatever you want: rice (2 options), beans, veggies, salsa, queso, guac, and sour cream. Still $7.50 and three times as much food as the tacos.

Fairly simple menu when you walk in. Seating is adequate.

Terrible!  Tasteless meat, barely any cheese, dry roll.  I have NO idea why this is on the list of top cheesesteak places.  I've tasted better from mall food court restaurants- seriously.

The girl behind the counter (owner's daughter) tried to give the hard sell for add-on's (their overpriced water, sides, and dessert), but did so in such a lackluster way that you could tell she was being made to say it.  That was actually the highlight and pretty funny.

The food was way too salty, with no other spice. It did not taste good at all. Besides the food not being very good, the guy who served me was rude and acted like I was bothering him.  I won't ever come back.
Very good cheesesteak but needed more cheese. Maybe would've been cheesier with wiz (I got provolone). Make sure you have cash: ATM at the front. I would come back

Friendly staff and atmosphere.   Ordered a few Cheesesteaks, they were up in about 8 minutes, pretty quick.  The roll was fresh and the cheese was melted in just right.  The steak was good overall,  more fatty grizzle than usual today, but was still a tasty sandwich.
Quick service, good food, and clean atmosphere. If your looking for something quick that is moderately healthy I would definitely recommend stopping by.
It's a no for me. Such a tiny restaurant. Little portion. The ramen is chewy and broth isn't made right. No no no no no!

The owner seemed rude and pushy. Could not be bothered by us. The food was not even that good but we were made to feel very unwelcome. It gave the sense that they were just trying to make money and didn't really care much about the food. There are much better places to get ramen in Chinatown.

Do not ever go there. Its disgusting. This place is so ghetto. Blast freeze machines were down. Fake Louis Vuitton bag on the cooking pan. Smashed drive through sign. Nasty service. Never going back to that shit ever again.

This location gives this brand a bad name. Employees are extremely slow at the job, waited 30 minutes in line and there were only 2 people in front of me... unfortunately this isn't the first time. Every single time i come here i get the same sh*tty service.

First thing is that they do have a GLUTEN FREE roll, so you can get any sandwich on that roll! The cheesesteak, the reuben, I mean having this option is awesome and the only one that I know of in old city.

I have had both the cheesesteak and the reuben on the GF roll and they were delicious! My husband has had their regular sandwiches and he loved them all. 

We have taken out and sat inside to eat, I prefer takeout as the seating inside isn't the best and the tables are really close together. I am sure that in the warmer weather it's probably better. 

I do wish they would stay open later on the weekends and I bet they would do more business. One Friday night all I wanted was that GF sandwich and dang it if they weren't closed.

Never had an issue with this location! It's hard to believe that any KFC would run out of chicken, especially on several occasions. Anyway, if I had some kind of an issue each time I visited this KFC, I doubt that I would keep returning for six years.

I have been going to Campo's since they first opened, and they are one of the better sandwich/cheesesteak places in the city.  

I go here for their "Godfather" Sandwich - one of my favorites.   They make better sandwiches than "Fork Etc..." up the street.  

Consistent and good quality grub.

NOTE:  Tourists flock here so be warned.
They are amazing. I love all their ramen. I literally can't get enough of them. I bring all my people here. I love you Hiro Ramen!!!

I walked in here at 9pm on a Friday night, they close at 10pm but the staff was extremely courteous. The menu is small with only 4, or 5, ramen choices and about 5 appetizer choices. I ordered the Miso Ramen. The broth was flavorful and the noodles were quite good. The toppings were not as good as other places but the noodles and broth are comparable. The ramen is on par with Terakawa in Chinatown, but with fewer choices. Come here if all you're looking for is a warm bowl of noodles to satisfy a ramen craving.

These cheesesteaks are delicious!! You've gotta get them fully loaded with Cheese Whiz. The meat is juicy but not fatty (yay!) and very flavorful. I've been here twice and had a wonderful experience both times. I definitely recommend trying this place if you're in Philly and want to eat like a local!

As 100% expected, the cheesesteak was probably the most overrated gimmick part of my vacation to Philly. Skip it. Waste of time. This wasn't anything I couldn't get at any ballpark in the country. Not worth $9, and grumpy service, also.

Happy to find a cheesesteak joint that offers gluten free buns. I do wish it was a hoagie style bun instead of the round bun though. Meat was tasty, but the bun should have been toasted first to keep it from going soggy and crumbling. Noted for next time :)

Looks like hiro is on the up&up. They have new lamenated menus w/ a choice of 4 different ramens: chicken soy, miso, pork, and vegetarian.

Had the chicken soy for the first time! Very tasty. However, I still prefer the pork and the vegetarian. Since ramen traditional comes with pork belly (a fatty meat), the fattiness of the chicken was a little weird. I don't know. I guess I would just rather be eating pork fat than chicken fat :)

PS. Jefferson Hospital Employees get $1 off! Woohoo

I've been here twice now. The first time I had the cheesesteak, some chips and a soda. The cheesesteak meat was pretty flavorless and the meat was overcooked. The roll was ok, but nothing special. 

The second time I came back and had the Stockyard after a good friend recommended it. The Stockyard is a mouth-watering mound of meat slapped in a roll: chicken, steak, pepperoni, bacon, fried onions, marscarpone cheese.  Even know I"m salivating thinking about it.

Service is quick and the food comes out pretty fast.

I wouldn't eat a cheesesteak here but I"d eat a Stockyard at the drop of a hat.

Well, this is what I get for not consulting Yelp before going hunting for a cheesesteak.  Apparently this place is a tourist trap, but it was where we ended up for lunch.  A friend of mine was visiting Philadelphia to try to decide on Penn for grad school (reason #2 for my trip to Philly), and she and her BF refused to leave without having at least one cheesesteak.  Time was of the essence (as was it being within walking distance), and this was the closest option.  According to the shopkeeper at Sugarcube (review forthcoming), these "were good enough if you don't have time to go to South Philly and try the real thing."

And good enough they were.  The two of them went for the truly artery clogging versions with cheese wiz.  I settled for provolone and pepper.  Was it tasty?  Sure.  But since I can't actually remember the last time I had a cheesesteak, I really don't have anything to compare it to.   And apparently $8 for a cheesesteak is pricey, but to this New Yorker, it was a steal.  It did the job.

Best ever Schezuan fried rice!!! I found Mumbai in USA. It was just so delicious can't express it in words!!! Best place ever!! Achari paneer katti roll was my all time fav here but now it's the fried rice!!!

I appreciate food, and I appreciate places that take the effort to make food worth eating. I stopped here today and had a standard bowl of "Gates of Hell" it was wonderfully crafted and deliciously fulfilling on a cold winter day. It was hot and spicy, but could have been spicier and a little less salty. I had never had marinated egg that I know of but it was incredible. It would have been odd as a stand alone item but incredibly in sync with the ramen.
The ambiance was very cool and was probably as close to a raman house in Japan as i may ever see. Not small but intimate. Large parties beware the place probably seats 35 people max
I WILL eat here again

I stumbled into this place because I was starving after running 6 miles and no one was there.  What an amazing surprise! I ordered The Stockyard.  Freshly made, flavor full steak and chicken and pepperoni with just the perfect balance of onions, peppers and cheese.  The cheese was just right! Perfect! This was a freakin' religious experience of a sandwich. Service was excellent. They only take cash.

After watching the Incredibles at Prince theater, my boyfriend and I stumbled across Hiro ramen and decided to have dinner here. The space is quaint and cozy. Mostly wood interior and furnitures, this gave a homey and authentic vibe. The menu is limited yet straight forwards, making the selection very easy which I kinda like. After a couple minutes staring at the menu, we decided to get Gates of Hell and Hiro's Inch of Heaven. If you like spicy food, I would suggest Gates of Hell since it was fairly spicy but flavorful. Hiro's Inch of Heaven has a soy based broth and it seasoned to perfection. The meats were a bit dry in compared with other ramen shops that I had. But the overall flavor of both were decent. The ramen costs $10 which in my opinion a very reasonable price for the portion that you get. The waitress was very attentive and she made sure our glasses of water never emptied. The atmosphere was very chillax yet cozy, a good spot for a casual date or just to catch up with friends over a hot decent bowl of ramen. 
This place accepts cash only so make sure to have extra bills handy. If you forgot, there is an ATM nearby. The reason I gave Hiro 4 stars is because of the bathroom. There was water on the floor and and when water leaked from the sink too.
Overall, I would come back here again to try other options on the menu. if you are in the area and craving some good ramen, check this place out!
This place accepts reservations and is BYOB. The Ramen was pretty good although we do wish there was more meat, and the fried chicken appetizer was delish; very friendly server.

Didn't taste the cheesesteaks  but brought them to friends in MD who said they were awesome.  Awesome customer service.  Left my debit card on the counter and Brittany went above and beyond to track me down. Will definitely try the cheesesteaks next time in town.

One of the best kept secrets in the area. I work in the neighborhood and heard there was rumored to be a new ramen spot opening up by Jefferson Hospital. Although there was no real sign at the time (probably because they had just opened), I was able to identify the place by the Japanese lettering above the front door-- right next to Milkboy. It was a quiet atmosphere inside, and my co-worker and I were serviced immediately. The place appears to have gone thru recent renovations as everything is brand new. A bit small in size, kind of a hole in the wall actually, but an interesting set up as the chefs area/kitchen is adjacent to the seating, very much like a sushi bar. 

Our orders came out quickly and I was very satisfied with the soup. You never know what to expect with ramen, but this place definitely uses high quality ingredients in their soup. Noodles, egg, chicken, vegetables. I think they said they had vegetarian options too. 

The chef assured us that they were still in the unveiling process, but I'm curious to see how well this place does once they are in full operation.   Like Viet Pho, it's an excellent cold weather meal, so I imagine they would start to crank it up in the winter months.  I'll definitely be back.
Delicious authentic ramen! The flavors were incredible  Will definitely be going back for more!

I always thought this place was a tourist trap, and boy was I right! $10 for a "chicken cheesesteak" where the chicken was not shredded, but on the roll in big, gross, fatty chunks. This is probably one of my biggest pet peeves; if you're going to sell a sandwich like that where the meat is not shredded, you should not even call it a "cheesesteak".  Top it off with paying $1.25 for a tiny bag or chips that is typically $0.50 and the fact that they only take cash and I will never eat at this place again. Garbage.

I really enjoy Campo's for lunch. The thing about their cheesesteaks is that they are not swimming in a gross pile of grease. Honestly, I don't even know how they do it (and neither does the rest of Philly it would seem) because their cheesesteaks are delicious but they are not heavy and gross like a lot of the more 'popular' philly cheesesteaks. The Chicken cheesesteak features chunks of real deal white chicken breast, that you can actually imagine coming from a chicken instead of...well whatever a chicken 'steak' usually is made from. 

The menu is pretty extensive and the prices are reasonable. This is a great outing for lunch. If you are mad about the prices (as it seems some reviewers are), look around folks, you're in Old City and how do you think they pay their rent? pure luck? NO they need to charge you money. If you want something cheaper go some place with crappy sandwiches it's really that simple.

While I on the other hand will be enjoying their fresh tasting cheese steak whilst sitting in the outdoor seating in Old city in this gorgeous spring weather.

Stopped into Hiro Ramen for lunch after shopping on Jeweler's Row and it was great.

We both ordered the Inch of Heaven Ramen and an order of Karaage (Japanese-style boneless crispy fried chicken).  I added naruto and nori to my bowl which had a beautiful dark broth (they described it at Tonkotsu, but true Japanese tonkotsu broth is almost milky white), curly ramen noodles, bamboo shoots, pork char shu and half of an ajitsuke egg as is often traditional in Japanese ramen.

The broth delicious, the noodles perfectly cooked and the pork and egg were also perfectly cooked.  My next visit, I'll add more noodles and an extra egg for sure.  So delicious!

The karaage was piping hot, fresh and very crisp and delicious.  I felt the may dipping sauce was a bit too heavy on the garlic but many would like it.  I just had a spritz of fresh lemon and the chicken as is - perfection!

The had UCC Melon Cream Soda which I love, so a perfect lunch for me.  I will be back.

I have been to Terakawa which is delicious and in my opinion, Hiro Ramen is way better than 5th to Terakawa's #1 rating.

Cash ONLY! BYOB!

This place is small, but cozy. Their service is fast, so don't worry the wait shouldn't be long.

I love coming here for lunch specials which includes a salad, appetizer, and a bowl of ramen for $13.

I've only tried Porfilio, Black Pig, Inch of Heaven, Chicken Soy, and Gates of Hell. My favorite one is Porfilio, but you honestly will not regret any of them. The best part of the ramen is the egg! Some don't come with an egg, so I definitely recommend it!

The food is very good, however the service has much to be desired. The staff is very rude. They are not welcoming and are very unfriendly. They have a very bad attitude and it makes going in very unpleasant. It's a shame because this place is in a great location and has such potential

I think I've had enough of this place. The management must be bad or something. Jimmy John's food is basically the same at any location. The only complaint about the food is when they deliberately put a ton of mayo on.

My problems with this store:

-They are always playing death metal and its really not the ambiance you want when you are eating. 

-Dirty tables when the place is empty. What else are you doing? Singing along to the death metal?

-The time when this lady was not the cashier, but taking peoples orders as far as 4 people back in line. Just a big mess.

-The biker delivery people talking super loud. Another thing about these bikers is I see them going super slow delivering food. One time this dude came and left 3 times within a span of 10 minutes for some reason when he should have been delivering people's food. 

-All the people who use the store as their shortcut.

I saw this one dude bring his old bent cup in the store to fill it up. I guess he couldn't afford a new cup so he saved his and brought it with him and then left. 

I do have to say that the bathrooms are always very clean. 

Something needs to be done about that death metal and the cocky staff.

Update: still love this place to pieces. Just tried their karaage chicken and it is to DIE for. So fresh and the lemon and cream sauce is so complimentary. Love the porfilio ramen because of the savory broth and the lemon wedge! Service is very very friendly -- nicest waitresses and chefs ever. They always check in and make sure all of your needs are met. I am never disappointed.

I really enjoyed this place. Staff were great and the food very tasty and cheap. I had a regular cheese steack sandwich and as expected, it was so good that I would have some room for another extra one ;-p

Meh .... below par. Service sucks.  The cashier is rude.  :-(    I should've done my research before visiting Philly.   It was too late when I saw some videos on YouTube -- there's a few better alternatives, like those mentioned here:   https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YcLU6UGVcdo

Only because I don't live close, I didn't take this food back. I always order 2 boxes of the 11 piece chicken, mild with no breasts, and two large orders of fries. I've come to the conclusion that maybe I should make my order myself. I get home and they're breasts in the box and the chicken was hard and cold. I guess I need to take a break from Popeyes.

My first Philly Cheesesteak.  We stopped here specifically to try a cheesesteak on a road trip and were pleasantly surprised.  The bread was fluffy, but chewy and strong enough to hold all of the meat and melted cheese inside.  We ordered two.  One was just a cheesesteak plain, i.e. shaved steak and cheese.  The second was a cheesesteak with peppers and onions.  Both were very good and worth the trip into Philly to try this local hit.  I would have to agree that Philly does make the best cheesesteaks.  Thanks for the pleasant surprise!

Just awful. If I wanted a hard pretzel, I'd get Rolld Gold or something from the supermarket.
They keep their food under a heat lamp for hours.  My pretzel nuggets were really hard and crunchy.  When I asked if they could give me a fresh batch, they said no, but offered me a pretzel instead.  I said fine.  The pretzel is a dollar cheaper than the nuggets, but they did not even offer to refund me the amount.... It wasn't particularly busy, there were three employees but they didn't really care....
The pretzels they gave me was also hard and crunchy; not fresh, soft and buttery like it's supposed to be. More like a baguette, and 3 times the price. Bad customer service.  Not one of our three orders was fresh.  Unmotivated employees. Rip off.

Enjoyed some of the best ramen of my life at Hiro. The Gates of Hell warmed me right up on a chilly Friday night, and I don't think I can ever go back to ramen without pork belly. A must-try, particularly with their awesome lunch specials! Be mindful they close on the earlier side, and cash only.
Good cheesesteaks & hoagies here, but they are overpriced considering you can get better, for less money, on the same block. And it's cash only.

I'm still looking for a *FABULOUS* cheesesteak place in Philly, but this is my favorite so far.  I really enjoyed it. I got "The works" with cheez whiz.  I do want to go back and try the "ice" with the cream cheese sauce I'm hearing about.

Came to Philly for the first time and this was the first stop for the cheesesteak. It looked like a family owned restaurant. Ordered the Works for $9.50 and a regular coke for 2.32. I'm kind of surprise that they don't accept credit cards. =( 

There was nothing special of the cheesesteak, your regular pepper, mushrooms and cheese on a roll. The coca cola was refreshing and good, i'm surprised it was fountain. I didn't like the fact that they charged tax and they only accept cash. There were seatings outside and in without charge, thank god.

Great place to stop for lunch if you want a great hoagie and it's also a great place for a nice happy hour. 
Happy hour prices are spot on and they usually have a sandwich of the month.

I've ordered the turkey tom twice online and it was fresh, FAST, and delicious each time.  Although they don't have as many toppings as Subway, their sandwiches have a fresher taste.

This will be my go-to delivery spot on the days I can't leave my office.

All of their food was over inflated for what it's worth, staff is extremely snooty toned.  We were new to the area, funny thing we went to the wrong cheesesteak restaurant. Definitely paid for that mistake! Got my order wrong at a non busy time, and their cheesesteak ripped the roof of my mouth pft. 

Paid a whole lot and I'm still hungry!

One of the best cheese steak places in town. The steak is cooked juicy and the cheese is melted nicely. The place is unexpectedly small, although there are tables outside of the place that you can sit when the weather is nice out. However, the portion is small for its price and compare to other places

Pretty close to hitting it on the nail. Chinks is my favorite but campos is a close 2nd. The meat taste awesome but I don't feel the bread compliments its awesomeness. Dont get me wrong the bread was good, just not awesome. Also hit up Tony lukes where the bread was "awesome" and the meat was not. Now all campos has to do is get their hands on some of that bread!

Jimmy John's does not have good sandwiches at all. Their meat isn't fresh at all and does not taste good and their vegetables aren't fresh either. You can taste that their tomatoes are old and their lettuce is not juicy and fresh like it should be. If you call to order they take around 40 minutes to deliver but when you order online they deliver it in 10 minutes or less...that's the only reason I'm giving it 2 stars.

Campo's is a place I to which I take visiting friends and family when they want a 'real Philly hoagie.' They can get crowded and they don't take cash, but everything is fresh and delicious. They have a large menu and will custom make just about anything for a vegetarian. They also offer a mean mixed cheese hoagie. Kind of pricey, but occasionally worth it.

Jesus Christ, if this is what people think Mexican food is, they should be handed a turd wrapped in a tortilla pooped by someone who ate nothing but good Mexican food and lots of corn.

I made the mistake of coming in here once, and my stomach is still trying to forgive me of that heinous act. People, vote with your wallets, go to South Philly were actual people of Mexican heritage reside and MAKE REAL MEXICAN FOOD. Trust me, a white dude who's failing economics didn't give a single fuck when he slapped on overcooked meat onto the over-processed flour flapjack thing and sprinkle some lettuce atop that heaping pile of diarrhea.

And the place is a disgrace on top of all the craptastic food. I've eaten in cleaner place in Tijuana. Read Mike T's review, he'll go into detail how grimy this place is and into more detail about how bad the place is [though I absolutely disagree about the absurd tasting wrapped meat concoction I was ultimately handed].

Amazing burritos in California cost $5 and are filled to the brim with deliciousness that's as hard to describe as an acid trip. Good burritos in South Philly are $7 and while not as amazing, are very good! Disgusting burritos from Qdoba cost close to $10 and are made with Hitler's own malevolent intestines and is described like an overused porta-potty. Choose wisely.

Really bad all around.  Mean service, crappy cheesteak, wiz that tasted like it had expired.  And expensive for what it is to boot.  

Totally a spot to avoid.  Sad that it's going to still get a lot of walk in business from the area.  Please don't judge philly food based on this spot.

HAIR IN 2 HOAGIES! This is a very popular place, the menu is fabulous, and I actually really enjoyed the food I got. However, I also bought food for some friends this same day. Two of them both had pulled out disgusting long brown hairs from their subs. One hair is bad enough, but 2 different sandwiches?! SERIOUSLY?! This is completely uncalled for and totally disgusting. There's no way I will ever step foot inside those doors again - GROSS!

I love their lunch special with a little salad, fried chicken or gyoza, and ramen. Can't remember how much it is but it's very affordable. 
The gyoza and fried chicken taste just like your mom would make at home (if you happen to be Asian). 

I've tried several ramen--soy broth, miso broth, and super spicy. They are all very good, with perfectly cooked noodles and satisfying portions. Overall excellent, quick, and affordable lunch option. 

Reason I can't give 4 stars is that although the ramen is good there is some room for improvement--miso and soy broth are a bit too salty, and the spicy broth is way too spicy. I know it's called "Gates to Hell" but it should be symbolic not literal! 

Although there's usually only one server, service is excellent. (Actually, there was a server that was not great but she has since left).

Loved their cannoli. Amazing cannoli. Fresh and home-made too? YES!

The cheesesteaks were also well made :-) But their cannoli was what really stood out to me the most. Cheers to eating Philadelphia Cheesesteaks in Philadelphia! (ate there as a tourist; not originally from the east coast in general)

I'v eaten here once as a convenience, because it's down the street from my place of employ.

So far, it's the best hoagie I've gotten in Philly.  It doesn't hold a candle to Meadowbrook Food Center in Jersey, but that's a little bit of a hike from Olde City.

There are things that could be slightly better, like the staff offering to scoop the bread out on larger sandwiches.  If there's one thing I hate, it's paying extra to enjoy a store's specialty sandwich and all of its flavors and then watching it fall apart on the first bite because of overcrowding.

I'll definitely be back here in the future.

BEWARE: This place charges $1.59 for a small cup of hot water.   Hmm... who charges for hot water?  Okay, if there is a charge for this, it would have been nice to let the customer know, right?  They said it's bottled water, but I bet it's just tap water! 
I ordered the plain steak w/ onions, and the steak was a little dry and not very tasty.  My friend ordered the cheesesteak and said it was "just okay".  We agreed our homemade cheesesteaks taste better!
The attitude of the cashier was pretty rude for what I thought should be a friendly city, especially in a touristy area.   Well, we just happened to come upon the restaurant, but will definitely not go back again!

I will not be coming back.

I visited Campo's as part of my road trip up the East Coast. It was my first time in Philly and my first cheese steak.

THE BAD:

-They don't accept plastic. That was annoying because I'm a traveler and don't carry cash. Also, it's 2011.
-The cashier girl seemed disinterested and dismissive. Almost a "Hurry up and get out" attitude.
-They won't give you water if you ask, not in a cup, and not to fill your thermos, not even off tap. They will only sell you bottled water.
-The restaurant had the front windows wide open. There was a bird walking around in the restaurant. It jumped on my head and pooped on my laptop bag. This is while I am trying to eat.
-I got some mustard with my pretzel. The girl neglected to tell me that it could also sub as a sinus decongestant; it was very spicy, and no warning was given.

THE GOOD:

-It was my first cheese steak, and I thought it was quite tasty. I had a standard cheese steak with fried onions and cheese whiz on the advice of the cashier girl.
-The pretzel bread was REALLY good. Honestly, I probably enjoyed the pretzel bread (purchased as a side) more than the cheese steak. The spicy mustard which I didn't know was spicy was apparently made on the premises, and thought it was too spicy for me, I imagine someone who likes that sort of thing would've found it to be a quality mustard.

OVERALL:

-The cheese steak was pretty good
-DEFINITELY get some soft pretzel bread
-Don't be surprised if your service is lackluster or you have any 'uninvited guests' at your meal.
-Be prepared to pay $7-10 to eat.

I had a chance to check out Campo's on my visit back to my home in Philly.  I am a cheesesteak lover to the highest degree. I am a Platinum belt in tasting and judging cheesesteaks.  The steak I had here was pretty good, the roll was fresh (no amoroso).  The  steak was cooked and season well (salt and pepper). For Olde City, I give it a 4 out of 5.  The prices were on the higher side for the portion that was served. This place does'nt do french fries just overly priced potato chips :)
the landlady so rude, she helped me to make decision and picked up my food. Come on, I wanted to sit down and eat! The woman looks like an aggregation of anger.
My tacos were good but I ordered  3 cheese nachos and it didn't come with nachos after the guy suggested them to be on the side so they don't get soggy on the ride home . Talk about pissed off

First time in Philly and was I so hungry. Came across this place and decided to have my first Philly. 
1. Lacked in being loaded up with meat
2. Good thing this won't be my only cheese steak stop, because if it was I would think that the cheese steak is all hype
3. The cheese should have been melted all through the sandwich and it wasn't. 

The sandwich was ok. The bread was fresh I'll give them that, but then I think chews steak I'm looking for something oozing with flavor, loads if meat, tons of melted cheese, and grease!!! My sandwich should have been close to soggy. Onto the next one.

Campo's is a great place to take your friends from out of town if one of them is begging you for a cheese steak and the other is a vegetarian.  Campo's veggie sandwiches are actually really really tasty, and I think their steaks are pretty great too- but then again it's hard to go wrong with melty cheese on meat...  We were here late one night and the girl behind the counter offered us cookies for free.  If that's not sweetie pie status then I don't know what is.  They don't take cards but their in- house ATM is helpful I guess, I think the fee's only like $1.50.  Gotta get used to carrying cash!

The employees were very rude. They complained about having to make our milkshakes because of the cleanup and "because it's winter". They were also condescending when we placed the sandwich order.  The fact they had to do any labor seemed like a burden to them. They then proceeded to conclude the transaction by talking about how Temple isn't a good school, which is ironic because TU students pay their bills. I enjoy Potbelly, but not worth going to this location.

HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE EXPERIENCE. Your food can be good but if your customer service sucks that doesn't even matter anymore. I walked in and got in line and I was next to order but the girl has two people she seemed to know come in and she took them before I me, didn't even acknowledge I was standing there. She took their orders as if I wasn't even standing there. Then after she takes my order, she has the nerve to ask me to giver her trash off a table. UMMM that's your job! Who on earth asks a customer to take trash off a table for you???? FIRST VISIT AND MY LAST!

I didn't try many of the Cheesesteak places in Philly, but this place was around the corner from my friends place and we decided to drop by here. 

We both got The WORKS for our sandwiches and it was DESLISHHHHH!!!

I'm not sure about the cheez wizz type cheesesteaks that I'm hearing about but this place was pretty BOMBB!

This is the worst Burger King Restaurant around Philadelphia, very close to where I live, just stop by recently and the whole restaurant hadn't changed a bit, I order through drive through, no napkins no ketchup even asking when ordered, went home, put comments in website, the owner call, I guest he hadn't read my comments, and asked me how can he fixed the problems? Damage done! Just want to let him know so he can put his eyes on his Restaurant, I think I do none sense. I will never come back this Burger King again.
INCREDIBLE!!!!!!!  Took my son here and we both loved it!  The food was freshly prepared and delicious.  The staff was helpful with the menu choices.  I can't wait to go back!!!!!

Sheer convenience of being a block from my office. The food is hot and served quickly.  Lunch special is typically $13 for salad, app and any ramen. Warm atmosphere you can relax in before rushing back to a busy day.
Primo's Hoagies on South Street has it ALL. Great traditional Philly Hoagies and booze. What more can you ask for?

This is the only restaurant I've encountered in the entire country that REFUSES to give customers a cup of water.

I won't be back.
Great service and the Godfather was the best. Soft bread!!! Hmmm!!!

Pretty good pretzel sticks. I received just enough cheese (comes prepackaged in a tub - like McDonald's or Wendy's sauces). I thought it was useful and impressed that they had calorie counts next to items on the menu. I was served by a very friendly employee.  I felt like she would've given me a hug if the counter wasn't between us.

This is only the 2nd ramen house I've been to in Philly so take this review with a grain of salt. The Gates of Hell is the best ramen I've had. I've been to Terakawa, Mitsuwa market in NJ and a random shop in Boston but this place had the better tonkotsu broth, noodles, and chashu (mouth waters as I think about it). The ONLY negative component to this ramen: the egg. It was perfectly cooked but the soy marination wasn't quite there.

Terrible  service here. The cashiers barely speak English, so they constantly screw up orders. Went in today for some lunch with my daughter, ordered a 3pc tender with fries and a 5 pc  with Mac n cheese....both mild. My 8 yr old daughter got 5 spicy pieces (hers was supposed to be 3pc mild) and fries and I got 3 wings with red beans and rice. Went up to the counter and told them, and this little punk copped an attitude with me and told me it's my own fault. Spoke to the manager and he fixed it....sat down to eat finally....no fork for us and our food was cold and undercooked for the most part. My daughter went up and asked about a fork and the horrible girls behind the counter ignored her, she said excuse me and they turned around and said "what do you want" and she asked for a fork. They said hell no....word for word....and laughed at her until she cried. I'm writing to corporate as soon as I get home. So angry.

Cash only. 30+ minute wait for a sandwich. 

Sandwiches were decent. Home made sides and desserts weren't bad either. Thought the meat was a little blan and fatty.

Menu has lots of choices including vegan and veggie. Bottles beer is also available. Staff could have been friendlier, but at the end of the day decent eats.
This is the best Spice End location because of the INDO CHINESE!!!! The Gobi Manchurian is my favorite thing to order.  Love this place!!

My elderly mother asked for a cup of water to take her medication.  We bought 4 sandwiches and 3 drinks, totaling over $50.00.  The owner told her "no".  He then went on to say  he doesn't give out free water because it was a sandwich shop not a sit down restaurant.  He was so rude about it, treating her as if she were a bum off the street.  We were visiting and looking forward to having a real Philly cheesesteak and yet we left having a not very good sandwich and a very unpleasant experience.  My advice... Skip this place and head a few blocks over to jim's.  Now that's a Philly cheesesteak!

A quaint little ramen shop tucked away on Chestnut just a few blocks from Chinatown, Hiro Ramen has its own distinct style. The restaurant is small and feels more intimate than Terakawa or other ramen joints in Philly, and the broth here tends to be crisp and refreshing, rather than thick and savory-- but not unsatisfyingly so. Some rather unique options include Chicken Broth Ramen, which was light but flavorful and a nice change from the thicker and more savory pork-based broths. Hiro's pork-derived broths are also good, although lighter than other Tonkotsu's I've tried. Their menu options change slightly from time to time, and they've added a few new ramen options since the first time I visited.

Unlike other ramen shops, where appetizers and sides are an after-thought, Hiro really excels at its non-noodle offerings. One of my favorite dishes was the fried chicken. It takes a few minutes to prepare because it is breaded and fried upon ordering. The chicken came out piping hot, cut into large satisfying chunks that were crispy on the outside, and juicy and meaty on the inside. The poultry used was clearly top notch, with only the best cuts of meat. It's one of the best fried chickens I've had in Philadelphia, and is really not to be missed. Also worth a try are the cold spicy chicken and edamame. The gyoza (pan-fried dumplings) were OK, but the vinegary, garlicky sauce tastes like it was flown in from Shinjuku right when you ordered.

Credit cards are not accepted.

I went to Campo's with my family after a quick trip to Independence Hall.  It hit the spot!  The staff was extremely friendly.  It is a family run, quaint little place about 3 blocks down Market St. from the Liberty Bell.  

We ordered 3 cheese-steaks and crab cake.  The crab cake was OK, but the cheese-steaks were great.  A couple of us got sides of cole slaw and my 10 year old got a side of macaroni and cheese.  Both side dishes were home made and very tasty - not out of some commercial food service operation.  I watched the cook as he made the cheese-steaks and it looks like they used very high quality, fresh ingredients.  I thought it was a little pricey, but it is in the center of a big city very close the main attractions.  We spent about $12-14 per person for sandwich, drink, and side dish (I also left a tip in the jar on the counter because they were so nice).  Oh, we did get 10% discount for mentioning that my son was an Eagle Scout after we saw a sign outside saying "Welcome Boy Scouts".

The staff took the time to talk to us and gave us great advice about getting around the city and back to our hotel.  If you are looking for something with a local flavor near Independence Hall, Campo's is the place for you!

Came here at noon on a Wed, it was empty. The restaurant is small and cozy. There was no English sign on the outside. Because of a previous Yelper's pic, I knew what to look for. Once you peer inside the door, you'll see some lunch specials marked "Hiro". 

I had the pork and miso ramen as part of a lunch special, which comes w a small salad and your choice of gyoza, fried chicken, or edemame, for $12. The salad is your typical Japanese restaurant salad w that ever present miso dressing.  I had the gyoza, which came soggy on top of the dipping sauce and the three were stuck together, having to rip them apart to eat. The ramen itself was decent.  A nice bowl of soupy goodness after a long flight. By the time I was done, more people came in, the place looked more lively. Oh, cash only!

Ordered a pizza steak today.
The roll was fresh and there was plenty of steak.
This is a great little pizza shop.

Yeah, no, please avoid this place in Philadelphia. Their cheesesteak sandwich was just ok. The Italian sandwich was left half uneaten because it had no flavor. The cashier was rude and I overheard her offering homemade desserts to others but not to us. Their sides are not included in any lunch combo sort of way, so we went for her mother's homemade coleslaw. It wasn't awful, but I've had better coleslaw from grocery stores. We pretty much threw out 25% of the lunch. Not worth it, and oh yes, in this day and age, they don't accept credit cards. People visiting Philly can skip this place and go to others. I was that unimpressed I had to write a Yelp review.

I'm a guy who loves food and likes to try out new things. After discovering the original Spice End on 21 & chestnut I was hooked and now having the location on south street is awesome considering I'm down here all the time. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone and with the wide menu choices you can't go wrong there is something for everyone!!

Qdoba, the only Mexican joint within the confines of Templetown. Yeah, I know it's not REAL Mexican food, but for fast food, it'll do the trick.

The quality of food and service is pretty standard compared to other Qdoba locations. Because it's on a college campus, it gets backed up, especially between noon to 1pm (lunch) and between 7pm to 8pm (dinner). Kind of overpriced for what you get, such as for the tacos. Gumbo and burritos are more reasonably priced, which is good, because those are my go-to Qdoba items.  

The salsa selection is pretty good and flavorful. The pulled pork is my favorite meat here, it's so tender and soft and I just can't get enough of it. Everything's relatively fresh tasting, if a bit salty. Some days, the batches of food don't seem as flavorful as usual, but that's nothing a dab of hot sauce can't cure.

We were in Philly for a wedding in the Old City. My brother lives in Philly, so over the years, I had many Philly cheesesteaks to enjoy. Usually, you can't go wrong with any place in Philly -- even if they are not the cheesesteak kings Pats or Genos. We Googled cheesesteaks in Old City and saw Sonnys. We tried to go to Sonny's, but it wasn't opened yet and since we were starving, we went to Campos, which is located a few doors down. Big mistake. First, we were hoping to get a mouth-watering Philly cheesesteak. You know the kind: sizzling on the grill while sliced and diced by the grillmaster. Not happening. The steak was lumped into the roll with wiz on it and while the steak was somewhat tasty, you had to rip it apart with your teeth. Not what I expected. Not only that, but the personnel were rude. They had a photographer taking photos of their alleged delicious food on tables in the front of the store and made us move. What happened to the old rule of "customer's first?" I guess this is Philly where rudeness rules. Also, the price for one drink, a cheesesteak, Caesar salad w/ chicken and chicken sandwich came to $40. Very disappointing.

Was in Philly and had to have a Philly cheese steak before we left. Was heading to Sonny's but kept on walking (looked a little dirty to me) and settled on Campo's Deli. Ordered a cheese steak and the chef salad and split the two between myself and hubby. The salad was terrific, the deli meat was fresh, and the homemade basil balsamic dressing was to die for. The sandwich wasn't greasy, steak was perfectly cooked - no complaints only plans to return if we're in Philly again!

4 of us were craving some ramen so went to this place. Wasn't sure how Philly ramen scene would be. My hub got spicy shoyu ramen and my parents shared miso ramen. I wasn't very hungry so got fried chicken appetizer. Chicken appetizer was very good. I actually liked their chicken than other famous chicken places in Philly. My parents thought their ramen was too salty for them. They just had noodles and left most of broth. My hub actually thought this place was decent. He finished his dish. I really enjoyed their chicken and the Korean waitress was very nice.

This is the second time I've been here and I have to say I like it more every time. The waiters are very kind and informative and the pricing is decent. I'm a fan of the Portfilio Ramen however I decided to try "The Gates of Hell". If you've ever tried the spicy ramen in Terakawa, it's a lot more spicier than that. The broth was delicious but a bit too spicy for me. I personally prefer the spicy ramen from Terakawa since its not as spicy. I'm also a fan of the Takoyaki here! I highly suggest you guys give this place a shot!
The bread was stale the meat was bland and the portion of meat was very small by Philly standards. Not good. Sonny's, next door it SO MUCH BETTER!
Bathroom was out of service, cashier had a poor attitude, no free refills and the steak wasn't as good as the peppers in the sandwich. Solid "meh" and did not live up to the hype.

My wife and I went in there for an early dinner the other day. The vegan and vegetarian options are limited, so we both got the vegetarian Ramen bowl. There was a lot of flavor, lots of vegetables and the Japanese bamboo gave it some great texture. The broth was a little salty, but overall very good stuff.

I checked the list of the Top 10 places to obtain Philly Cheesesteaks.  Campo's was listed as a place to go when you are in town (near the Liberty Bell) and need a convenience place to get a Philly.  First thing first, they do not accept debit or credit cards so be sure to bring cash (lots of it).  There is an ATM in the restaurant, just in case.  It's about $8 - $10 per sandwich and drinks and chips are extra.  They do not serve cheese fries which I was so looking forward to enjoying along with my cheesesteak.  There is dining inside and outside.  It wasn't the best Philly ever but it was pretty good!  I definitely prefer Pat's but this one worked out well.  

They had home made desserts including cannoli, but we were stuffed after our sandwiches!  They looked to die for!  

It's only a few minutes walk from the Liberty Bell, perfect distance for the kids!

Recently visited this place again for the first time. The first go around I reserved from doing a review, because I thought I'd try it again  one more time. After finishing some sightseeing I figured I'd take my guests to this spot and get their take on it. To start off, the seating space is very small. Secondly, they sell no fries with their sandwiches; only sides like potato salad, bagged potato chips, brownies and such. I ordered "The Works" which had green peppers, onions and mushrooms. My brother had the "The Heater" which had jalapeños, buffalo sauce and American cheese. The sandwiches are a decent size, the bread was spot on. That's as far as it went. Very little seasoning added to meat, to include salt. For the size of the sandwich, $10.50 is highly over-priced!!! That was just the sandwich; no side included. $45 for three sandwiches, one side and drinks is pricey! Can it be because of its proximity to Penn's Landing and other historical sites? Maybe, but it's safe to say I won't recommend it to friends or family visiting that area. Many other joints with better sandwiches, decent prices and better seating arrangements. Oh, and if you just want water, they charge for that too.

It's not the best but it's not the worst..It is pretty pricey for being on a college campus (broke students galore) but its okay once in awhile, although the price of one meal makes my wallet cry. They give hefty portions leaves you filled!

So glad they opened a rame place closeby.  I came during lunch time and was seated immediately.  I ordered the spicy miso and it definitely was not spicy enough.  The broth was tasty and the noodles were plenty.  I returned the next week and ordered the tonkatsu and the chicken platter to share.  The chicken was sooo good, get that next time you're there.  The tonkatsu was good, rich and brothy.  I look forward to returning to try the other two flavors because no matter what season it is, I am always down for noodle soup!
Philly Cheesesteak was great. My wife and kids first. Down for the day from Brooklyn and why not have a cheesesteak in Philadelphia.  What's better than that.

Good cheese steak, but no fries???  Two cheese steaks, a fountain soda, side of potato salad and a side of coleslaw, $28.  Since you can't get fries they offer the homemade sides, which are very good, but seem a little pricey.  I don't have any other truly Philly cheese steaks to compare to so take the review for what its worth.  Hopefully I will return soon and have something to compare it too.

I came to Philadelphia with some of my friends and stayed at a local hostel that offered 10% off to eat at Campo's. The philly cheesesteak was just okay but the reason I give this restaurant one star is because of the racist remark an employee gave my friend as he picked up his order. Luckily my friend took it with a grain of salt but I still feel the need to share that the service was awful and I will not be coming back.

Came here shortly after it opened.  Had the shoyu ramen.  It was pretty good flavorwise, but a little salty.
I came another time to try their miso ramen, but it was sold out, and got the shoyu again.
I will definitely come back to try their different specials, which changes based on the chef's whim.  I'm sure once they work out the kinks I can bump up the rating.
Delicious, food. Clean place friendly staff. I'll come back every time I'm in Philly.

My favorite cheesesteak in the city..... When it's a cheeseSTEAK. Counter girl needs to understand difference between chicken and steak . They always mess up when ordering multiple. And service at counter is very slow.

WARNING: I was super drunk when I ate here.... It was a cute place. Very small with Japanese decor. We came because of a groupon we bought online. I thought the food was amazing. I've been to a couple of ramen places but never really liked it. I really thought ramen just wasn't for me. This place changed my mind. The soup was delicious. Some might say it's a little salty but I liked it.

Cash only, no sign anywhere within site. Cashier gave me some serious attitude when I presented my credit card. 

I guess I should apologize, not like over half your clientale is there to see the liberty bell from anywhere but philly. 

Cheesesteak was solid, 9.75.

Here's the rundown:

Cash only - wack.
Meat quality - average
Bread - average 
Cheese prep - wack. 
Prices (given above) - wack. 

Overall, this could have been much better if they had bothered to cook the cheese properly instead of globbing it on the bread -- which had the effect of making the cheesesteak lukewarm. 

Skip, and just go down the street (the place down the block is way better.)

I've made it a goal to check out a new cheesesteak place every time I visit the Philadelphia area, and the one that won the poll this time around was Campo's. We planned to walk around Old City and see the Liberty Bell, so this was a very convenient location. It would be a challenging place to visit as a sole destination, as parking in the area is what you would expect for a downtown tourist destination. 

This is a quality cheesesteak emporium. Quality ingredients makes a quality steak. I got a cheesesteak with wiz and onions. I swear this is not just wiz from a can, but a concoction that has been altered by the alchemists behind the counter. Having been raised for an influential portion of my life in Wisconsin, I have been resistant to the concept of Wiz. But this was something more than your average wiz. Add the top notch steak and the great roll and you've got an amazing sandwich. That being said, I'd be really happy with a little more sandwich for the price, but the quality makes up for the size.

I also picked up a local soda (Hank's) and ordered some pretzels with mustard. The pretzels were all I could hope for, but the mustard was phenomenal. I want to come back and try that mustard on a sandwich. It's made fresh by Denise Campo, and that freshness comes through. It has a sinus-clearing bite that other lesser mustards have to resort to horseradish to attain. I also really want to come back and check out the Heater, which is made with a great jalapeno cheese.

This quality establishment is worth the visit, but make sure you bring cash. Maybe I can upgrade them to a "5" after another time or two.

I was visiting my sister in Philadelphia and knew I had to try a Philadelphia Cheesesteak. After looking up a bunch of places and my sister nixing all of them, she said Campos was the best she had so far. 

So I went, and I wasn't impressed. I don't believe they sell french fries, which I feel like french fries would go SO well with a cheesesteak. (Not a big deal.) So anyway, the actual cheesesteak ... the meat tasted dry, it didn't taste that flavorful and by the time I ordered a side, a drink, and the sandwich, I spent 17.00. 

I was impressed they had a gluten free roll, I got that, and wondered if that was what ruined the cheesesteak experience for me. But I mean, the meat wasn't that good either. I paid 1.50 more for a gluten free roll, that ended up making my sandwich half the size of a normal Philly cheesesteak. The roll was dry and crumbly as well. Regardless, gluten free roll or not, I did not like the service, the cheesesteak and the prices. The potato salad was pretty good though.
I had a cheesesteak, macaroni salad, and a soft pretzel with some special mustard and it was all excellent.  Campo's is clean and the staff friendly (and also clean), and the food excellent.

Eh stopped by for a quick ramen lunch and was not impressed. I believe I got the blank pig ramen.
I'm actually not entirely sure what was in it. A fatty slice if pork. Bean sprouts. Slices is those fake fish paddy things.
Broth was so-so. Didn't have any depth of flavor. The noodles were cooked well with a lil bounce, but just some regular ramen noodles.
$9 for a decent sized bowl.
Very a small place. Service was friendly, but one guy handling everything in the front can get tough.
Overall, underwhelmed.

Every time I visit McDonald's, I order a black coffee- each time I reiterate "black coffee", "BLACK" coffee- and about half of the time the drink I receive is lousy with cream, and sometimes even sugar. 

Once, I visited this location with a friend and explained this frequent occurrence to him, to which he responded "I think 'black' means that you want cream, just not sugar." I parked my car, walked to the side opposite, and with a fury that could have shred the steel chassis of my 2001 Nissan Altima easily as though it were his liberal arts degree, I pulled open the passenger-side door. I dragged my friend to the asphalt, his body falling limply and coiling swiftly like a stunned shellfish at the mercy of the hot blacktop, and I beat him to death in front of women and their children, beside the glut of cars on Oregon avenue, packed bumper-to-bumper and door-to-door, idling patiently at the behest of the impatient motorists. 

It's the food service equivalent of "for all intensive purposes", "dually noted", or "should of" (answer key: "intents and purposes", "duly", "should've"). Words, individually, have actual meaning. They aren't just a collection of sounds that you can rewind and play back. Words are more than just muscle memory; more than the shape of one's mouth. When I order my large coffee "black", I want a drink of the largest size and the deepest shade of brown.

The Filet o' Fish was cooked to perfection.

I am a fan of Campo's for philly cheesesteaks! Unlike Gino's or Pat's, Campo's philly cheesesteaks are juicy and tender. My personal favorite is the Heater cheesesteak only because I'm a huge jalapenos and hot sauce fan-it's like eating cheesesteak with buffalo sauce and jalapenos. Great combo! Just make sure the meat is cooked all the way through, I had one that was slightly under cooked and I thought it would be alright but that was a bad idea. Other than that one time, Campo's is still my favorite!

All the good review has no sense. The service is not great. The server looks at me like it was bored looking. Like it was the end of the world to serve me. And the sandwich was not good either : no taste in the meat. Go to Jim's steak it is much better !!

New-ish Chipotle right on Drexel's campus. It was pretty clean, and the service was friendly and pretty fast.

I've been doing the Whole30 program, and Chipotle is one of the few chains where it is pretty easy to dine out and be Whole30 compliant.

My go-to Whole30 order is: lettuce bowl with Carnitas (only protein that is W30 compliant, double if need be), mild & medium salsas, and guacamole. It's actually delicious AND you don't end up feeling bloated and weighed down (like you might with a burrito).

I needed a new convenient place for Indian food after switching jobs recently. For some reason my online order didn't go through but I only had a brief wait while they prepared my food. Ordered the Spice End platter and chicken tika roll. Not as much flavor in the roll as I'd liked, but the platter was delicious. If you're not a fan of spicy food go for the chicken over rice or chicken biryani.

I have been ordering from this establishment for over 5 years. I've never had a complaint until today I was treated like an animal instead of a customer. The lady who answered the phone was very rude. I will NEVER order from here again. She needs to learn customer service going back and fourth with me when I did nothing to her but placed an order wasn't cool at all!

I generally don't like ramen but perhaps I've just never gotten GOOD ramen. This place has really good ramen. 

The price was very good, 10$ for any of the bowls. My only qualm was that literally everything had pork, and I can't eat pork. It would have been perfect if there was an option with chicken meat or something. There was a veggie option though. 

I got the chicken soy, which comes with chicken broth and pork (I didn't get the pork) and I very much enjoyed it and ate the whole bowl, to the shock of my friends. The broth was a little bit too salty for my taste but it was still delicious. I highly recommend, and remember to bring cash!

Having grown up on delicious ramen houses in LA, I definitely needed a ramen fix since I moved to Philly.  
My expectations were definitely low, which is possibly why it was just okay. We had the miso ramen and it was decent. It did the job of satisfying my ramen craving until the next time I am in LA. The only thing lacking was that it needed to be way spicier.

The service was very friendly and the price was great. We got a discount with our student IDs

I love Primo Hoagies.  I love this particular location even more because it's open later on the weekends.  Thank you, Thank you, Thank you for being around!

In my most recent late night excursion, I decided to get the suprimo (fress mozzarella, prosciutto, and roasted peppers) and my boyfriend devoured the turkey swartzie before I even got to take a look at it.  As usual, the sandwiches were perfection - the bread was deliciously soft, the ingredients were fresh as fresh can be, and the staff was super friendly.

I will definitely be back for more!

This has become my go-to hideaway lunch spot. There's something very cozy and relaxed about Hiro that I find to be a great escape. The service is fast and courteous, there's usually funky music playing, and I don't feel weird sitting by myself at the bar.

I haven't tried all the ramen, but the Inch of Heaven is my favorite so far.

In my opinion, it's slightly overpriced, but then again it's center city. And I keep coming back for more because I leave with a full, content belly. Just remember, it's cash only!

We knew that we needed to try at least one "traditional" cheesesteak while in Philadelphia and chose Campo's for it's olde city location and reputation.  We had one with provolone, one with provolone and peppers, and one with cheese whiz..  All were good!  Service was prompt, even on a Saturday evening.

Don't ask how this happened, but after our trip to Canada my husband and I got seriously into eating ramen. Totally random, but we now had to find a favorite ramen place in Philly and after walking past Hiro Ramen House and noticing it for the first time, we decided to check them out. My husband picked up their three different ramen soup bowls for us to have right after I got off from work on a Saturday, and both being hungry and cold immediately dug in.

All of the soups' noodles were cooked well and still had a nice bite to them despite being take out. The Hiro Ramen, topped with pork belly, bamboo, marinated soft-boiled egg, scallion and naruto, was the best of the bunch. The broth was flavorful and not too salty, and came with an egg (which my husband, not realizing the others didn't have eggs, promptly ate. I was upset - he owes me the next time). The White Soy Berkshire Pork Ramen had the same toppings (minus egg) but was saltier, although still tasty. The Gates Of Hell Ramen, however, was meh. The only 'flavor' you get is SPICY - there is so much heat that IF there is any other flavors in the broth, you can't taste it - you can barely taste the pork belly when just biting into a piece of it alone. I can tolerate huge levels of spicy, and although I could eat and handle the spice, my husband couldn't and we didn't finish it because it didn't have flavors like the other two. We were very happy and satisfied from the other two soups, though why they don't have more/certain ingredients as part of the soup and not as an add-in I don't understand. Good, but we know a better place now for our ramen cravings.

I'm reluctant to write this 5 star review, lest it contribute to more people catching on to this hidden gem. But they deserve it, so here goes.

Hiro is my favorite ramen place in the city, and I've tried them all. The black pig is my go to order; the flavors are complex and deep. The pork is thrown on the flat top, a genius move that gives it that outer crust/char but makes the inside buttery soft. I always add an egg and a spicy bomb (a potent little bowl of chili garlic infused hot sauce).

This is a big bowl of ramen, but it isn't the most gigantic you'll get in the city. I actually love this. It leaves room for the house salad (with crispy noodles and fresh ginger dressing...literally a steal, I think it's $2 for Christ's sake) and the real hidden gem, the fried chicken. Oh my God, this chicken. It's boneless, so you think that would mean it gets dried out, but they use all dark meat and it is beyond juicy and seasoned to perfection. Be forewarned: they WILL place a plate of chicken in front of you that could melt the roof of your mouth off it's so hot, and you WILL take a bite too soon and suffer the consequences. It's worth it.

This was a decent find. A hard place unless you can read Japanese. There is no official American sign that reads Hiro Ramen House that I could see, but look for the Japanese characters and you'll be there.

Small quaint area with just a few tables for smaller groups and the typical ramen bar for the single eaters/dates. There are just a handful of options for ramen, your basic choices. And some interesting apps, no pork buns though.

The ramen prices are a bit spendy for the size of the bowl. Not much proteins or extras either. They could improve with a bigger bowl that is standard like other ramen houses in the area as well as add other condiments like corn, bamboo, etc (just suggestions). Otherwise the flavors were there and good, nothing out of this world. There are better options out there but if you are in the area, it's worth a try.

No parking other than street parking.

Happy eating!

McDonalds now all charge for tap water.
OK fine, so my credit card purchase was attempted for a $1.57 courtesy cup. 
The cashier said "cashless device , cashless device "
Right. It's card. So is that ok?
" Da machine says you cashless dat mean you ain't got no money in yo account!  Sorry! Next!"
No, a cashless device is a credit or debit card. I just used this card to buy the sandwich here. Can you just give me a cup for tap water. I'm choking my throat is dry.   
Tap water is no longer free in America - customers are now perceived as a "nuisance" - interrupting their coversatuons, just enemies at a register forcing them to "do something".  It 's not a good look at all, not for McDonalds or any other business. It's sad when this is what we have at the front lines of customer service.  I would prefer kiosks.

Still keeping some stars up there for their cleaning staff- always awesome, hard-working people that have to put up with a heck of a lot more cleaning than any other restaurant where normal people use the trashcans provided as intended. Maybe these people's parents never told them to throw their trash out growing up, or that it was ok to litter on the ground- let someone else clean it up. The best response to this date though is still the Center City Wendy's lady's two-word reply when I asked if it ever got on her nerves- " Job Security".

I was driving through Philadelphia so I decided to stop for a cheesesteak, and ended up here. First of all, I tried to order a cup of tap water, but the man who was taking my order gruffly said "We only have bottled." When I asked why, the only reason he gave was, "It's a cheesesteak place." That isn't an excuse to provide a common courtesy to your customers. The price of a Coke instead was something like $2.32, with refills costing another dollar. Then I tried to use my debit card to pay, and the man told me (gruffly again) that they only take cash. My friend, who hadn't ordered yet, didn't have cash, so he left and went a few doors down the street to Sonny's, where he ordered his cheese-steak with a cup of water, paid with his debit card, and had a generally pleasant experience.

The only reason I'm giving it 2 stars instead of 1 is that the sandwich was, in fact, pretty tasty.

Moral of the story: No cups of water, cash only, unpleasant service. If you're on Market Street near the Liberty Bell/Independence Hall and want a cheesesteak, go to Sonny's or get one from a street vendor. You can do a lot better then Campo's.

The style of cooking is close to other renowned ramen shops I have tried in New York City. I ordered the Hiro Ramen: The half-boiled egg, the pork slice with a hint of burned-in seaweed flavor, and the soup base all met my expectation.  My biggest issue is size. Compared to Terakawa ramen, I did not feel satisfied when I finished my meal at Hiro. I may come back when my mood strikes. But overall, it's a okay ramen shop.

Not the most impressive variety of sandwiches and the menu is fairly limited, but they are fast, the place is clean, and what they do, they do it well. I always feel bad for the biker delivery guys but they never complain.

One choice for a sandwich. And it's only chicken and pickles. 8 or 12 piece nuggets. And they're really selfish with sauces. And of all things, they run out of chick-fil-a sauce?!?!?! This isn't even chick-fil-a.

Uncle tomy's...what can I say, it's pretty much the only option we have in the Grey's ferry area. They are very high in price. The food is really hit or miss. The Sicilian pizza taste as though it was pre made and they just tossed toppings on it.
Great place, food was delicious, food came out really fast..I had the lunch special which is really a great price..the fried chicken small appetizer was amazing..trust me, you'll love it here.

Summary:
All the bad onestar reviews on google are 100% accure.
The guy working there  had an aggressive uninviting demeanor from the getgo. The girl was snappy and very curt. After spending more than $20 they would not provide requested tap water. 


Details:
The reviews quite accurately reveal that yes the 2 people working thete late at night were desperate
to get out and clock out. 

As I was eating, 4 guys walked in at least a half hpur before advertised closing time. They guy working there just told them  flat out that they were closed. Then a few minutes later a family walked in and the girl working there snapped at them  that they can only order cold sandwiches.

Unfortunately, we chose this place due to it being closest to hotel very late at night.
Sometimes you just want to be free and spontaneus and not be bogged down by first reading rewiews.
