It was my experience at this place that actually prompted me to verify if their behavior was an isolated incident or more indicative of  an underlying issue of fustration and discontent of the guy and woman working there.  All the negative 1 star reviews clearly confirm there are morale and attitude issues at this place.


Conclusion:
Yelp rewiews can be like free business consulting and advice to these businesses getting
detailed and analytical 1star rewiews. Any business that is smart and that truly appreaciates their customers would listen and take action to rectify the customer service issues thay are being so accurately reported by customers.

Clearly this business does not care about customers, plain and simple.
Best ramen shop in the city. Had the Gates of Hell and Inch of Heaven and both were just great. The Kaarage is to die for.

I have never had a problem in this Wendy's location, Eric who works there as a cashier is always very nice and gets my order right every time. The food is always hot, and the wait can sometimes be a little long but hey, it happens. It's not their fault if they are packed. Lunch and dinner rushes are part of all food service. The staff is always very polite and personable and the food is great. I mean, it's Wendy's, it's not a high end restaurant so I don't get what people expect when they come here. Fast food is fast food, but this Wendy's is very good compared to other ones I have been to.

Was in Philly doing the Tourist Thing and my path happened to bring me across Campo's for the obligatory Cheesesteak pilgrimage. It turned out to be a bit disappointing, especially for the price. It was a perfectly decent sandwich, but I feel like I probably would have been better off just getting a cheesesteak off a food cart - the steak was a little dry and the overall flavor was just kind of lacking.

A very good addition to the Jefferson Hospital dining options.

Prices are reasonable, the broth is very good, and the pork is big/fatty/soft.

I got the spicy miso and it was seasoned with just enough salt/spice to not be too overbearing.  The noodle was not too chewy and on the more firm side.  

They include a rack of condiments (pepper oil, red cayenne pepper, salt, etc).

Our group left the place very full and happy.

Note: CASH only, no credit cards, BYOB though.
I love the turkey hoagie with Russian dressing and coleslaw. Never have I ever had coleslaw that good.  I'd buy a bucket if I could.  I might ask actually.
The only place open on christmas day. The line was super long but nice service and pretty fast.
Just not that good. Lacked seasoning and meat was not hot and a warm slab of provolone stuffed in the bun didn't work. I really wanted this one, but it missed the mark for me entirely.

Stopped in for a quick Cheese Steak and we were all pleased with the experience. Store a little crowded with a line but it moved quickly. Certainly one of the top five Cheesesteaks in Philly. Smaller portions but good. Cash only and could get a beer with the meal. Third is not an option at all "famous" cheesesteak establishments. Would certainly go back

Came on a Saturday around 1 for lunch. Not too busy. Was served promptly.

Got the karaage fried chicken and chicken soy ramen.

The karaage was crispy, hot and tasty. Very good. Probably some of the best karaage Ive eaten in America.

The chicken soy ramen was just okay. Nothing spectacular. A little bit salty actually. The chasu and egg in it was pretty good though.

*Cash Only Business*

The 'Gates of Hell' is a must. Add gyoza and fried chicken to enhance the experience. Other than that, a fantastic Ramen House.

Was advised to go here by some locals who said Pat King's and Geno's was overrated and boy was I dissappointed. 

I hate to bash places but this was the worst representation of a Philly Cheesesteak  I have had better in other states! That's sad. 

The meat was bland, the bread was bland all I tasted was grilled veggies oh and top it off they were skimmpy on the meat for $9.50 go some where else. I should have got the hint when I walked in and there was no line of people waiting.
By Far the Best Cheesesteak Hoagie Place in Center City Philadelphia thats why there at Citzen Bank Park
Go here if you want to wait and die a slow morbid death. 20 mins for a $5 box. Good job good job.

I went with a friend and did not know what to expect. It was good and service and price were good.  I had the pork and so did friend. I will go again since close to work. I am not a ramen expert but they were good.
I got the cheesesteak.  It was very tasty but small.  Good for the tourist visiting the historic area.

While visiting Philadelphia for a conference, I found this little hot spot with the Yelp app on my phone.  As usual, we have not been let down, as this was a solid little sub shop.  It is kind of weird that it is attached to a bar, but again, thanks to Yelp, this didn't turn us away.  

This place was so tasty that we actually came here 3 times within 4 days.  The first day I ordered a chicken sub that was pretty good, but the chicken parm sub that I ordered on the second day was downright amazing.  Against my better judgment, the third day I went away from the chicken parm and ordered the buffalo chicken.  It was just alright.  They also have several appetizer and dessert options in a little cooler by the register.  On the second occasion I bought a pickle and the third day I purchased some mud pie.  Both of these items were really good additions to my meal.

Overall, this place was a solid eatery in Philadelphia and if I return to this city, I will return to the location.

Uuummm...got the "works" and it just ok. I came hungry and left hungry.  The sandwich was just adequate with good flavor, but lacked cheese and I assumed that Philly Cheese Steak sandwiches would be generous with the cheese.  The Mac and Cheese side was delicious.  Prices on the high side given the size of the sandwich.  See pictures....

TL;DR -- CASH ONLY, amazing ramen. 

So it's 95 degrees in Philadelphia and here I am sitting with a steaming bowl of spicy ramen. 

So I was intensely craving ramen and not just any ramen. Spicy ramen. This place hit the spot with both the name and the taste. I got the gates of hell ramen and wow, I gotta say it's maybe a little short of divine. With pork chasu, the pungent bamboo shoots, and my favorites the ramen noodles and the broth, everything just melded together and fit perfectly. 

I loved how the noodles were just slightly undercooked so that they still have a bit of chewiness to them. The spicy broth was actually a little spicy by Japanese standards and just enough of  a kick for spicy regulars. I also got an aide of extra noodles and it was the perfect complement to the rest of broth after I at all the toppings.

The space is really cozy with a bar space of probably size and larger tables on the other side. All the staff were super friendly. 

Also, CASH ONLY! I thought they had started taking credit cards but apparently not. There is still an atm inside. Anywho, can't get your credit card points but you can get great ramen. 

I'll be back most definitely, maybe to try something else but hey, if it ain't broke, don't fix it. It'll probs be for the gates of hell again.

A a self proclaimed sandwich guru, I am writing to say that Campo's does in fact have the BEST cheese steak and sandwich in Philly. They have a wide variety of cheese steaks (not just wiz wit) and their hoagie sandwiches are amazing also!!!

I'm going to be nice and see if I could boost their review. All other negative review is accurate lol this place truly is terrible but I avoided them for over a year now, instead of dealing with retards at the drive thru, I'm going to walk in and try it out. To my surprise .... holy crapster, it's clean. Wait.... my food is done? Ohhhhhhhh I can actually sit my ass down and eat without arguing with someone messing up my order? Kudos to the new staff or management. I will give 5 stars for the huge differences. Wish MCDONALD could do the same ‍

Just walk in for dinner. Maybe it's their happy hour special but free beer or sake with an appetizer purchase for $6!! I ordered beer and the appetizer I got, some squid dish, came with sake!! 

And ramen was pretty good too :).

Ok, let me start by saying that I have never had a cheesesteak - yeah, I said it.  This review is based soley on their vegetarian sandwiches and sides.  They have a great selection - probably about 6 or 8 veggie sandwiches.  I have had the Godmother, Hot Veggie, Veggie and Tomato Mozzerella.  All have been excellent!!  The sides are good - nothing special.

The sandwiches are expensive, but very large.  You get a choice between
 regular or seeded roll.  If you're in this end of the city, and are a vegetarian, stop by Campo's!!

This is more a 2.5 than a 3.  Damn you yelp and your lack of half stars.

Anyway, I went to Campos by my boss's suggestion.  It's right near my hood so I rode my bike on over on an empty stomach and ordered the same steak I order at every steak place: cheese, steak, and provolone.  Just the essentials, and the same steak so as to make sure I get a comparison on an equal playing field.

Based on the steak I received, I wasn't all that impressed.  Just kinda average, and the meat had a bit of gristle to it (-.5 points.  Can't hang with gristle).  I'm rocking this review retrospectively and don't remember the nitty gritty details like I usually provide ... but it wasn't that memorable of a steak.  Maybe that's saying something in itself...

I always forget how much I love Jimmy John's until I take a bite out of one of their amazingly fresh, delicious sandwiches. One of my favorite things about this place: they really ARE "freaky fast." They'll be finished with your order before you even break out your wallet to pay. We ordered delivery from here tonight and I went to use the bathroom after we made the order. No sooner had I flushed when the phone rang, signaling the arrival of our sandwiches. Great for busy people, or extremely hungry people. That alone is worth at least a star.

And the sandwiches. Customizable heaven, I tell you. They are extremely accurate, no matter how many modifications you ask for, which is more than I can say about other places.

I love the Turkey Tom. My boyfriend loves the Ultimate Porker. Fresh, delicious cold subs. Sometimes, it's just what you need. My favorite topping's the peppers. So they don't have the largest variety of ingredients, but what they do have, they work well with.
this is fast food. nothing different from any other fast food chain. four stars for convenience and drive thru. the staff is nice and service is fast.

I love this place!!! Everything I ordered from there was great, especially the Mushroom Bacon Bleu Burger. Their pizza, wings, and soups are also amazing. This pizzeria deserves all the stars in the sky :)

I have several friends who are literally obsessed with this location because A) hoagies, B) bar, C) CHEAP bar, so it was only a matter of time before I started drinking the Primos Kool-Aid too. 

Gotta be honest, I've only ever had a few bites of hoagie from here (whacked chicken and italian diablo) but they were both perfectly acceptable bites, and I'm not much of a hoagie gal anyway. I do appreciate that they offer a wheat roll option for any small sized hoagie.

The real appeal here comes from the laid back vibe, the super nice bartenders, good view of any important sporting event, and cheap PBRs. If this sounds like your kind of bar then I'd give Primos a whirl next time you're wandering good ol' south street.

Do not order take out from here ever( take into consideration I order 30 minutes before closing but they said no problem)... all of my food arrived cold took over an hour to arrive. The "lamb" is not lamb.... it's mostly ground beef with some lamb mixed in. Chicken tikka wrap, I've never eaten something so dry I had to throw it out. The only slightly redeeming thing I order was the spicy chicken. Ordered it extra spicy and it didn't even come mild. I literally double checked everything with the delivery guy and they still forgot an item he said I promise everything is in there. Wish I could've bitch smacked him with the 10$ tip I gave him. SAVE YOUR MONEY AND NEVER ORDER FROM HERE.

Sandwiches were just okay.  Nothing to jump for joy about, but I didn't want to send it back.  The potato salad was pretty tasty.  They should really post "cash only" on the outside.  Or... you know... have a sign at the counter before you order.  Yes, they have an ATM, but who wants to deal with the fees?  I feel like we could've gotten a sandwich of equal quality at a street vendor and not have dealt with the young lady at the counter's bad attitude.

I came to philly for a business trip not expecting to find ramen. Decor, food and prices were all excellent. I got the tonkatsu and the broth wasn't too salty. Noodles and pork just right although too fatty for my taste. Portions were excellent. 

Also ordered zoba udon which was weird. Zoba shouldn't use udon. Their seaweed salad is typical. 

I've had ramen in Vancouver, DC, Houston, Dallas and LA and I would rank this place third to LA (shin sen gumi and daikokyua) and Vancouver(kintaro).
Campo's has delicious cheesesteaks. Would probably go there again. The only complaint is that the steak was a little gritty so it could have been chopped more, but still delicious.

I tried ordering a Chicken Cheese Steak w/ sauce and  was told that's a "chicken parm".  At any other reputable hoagie/cheesesteak place in Philly, these are two different things!  That's a red flag!  At the counter they always mention that their mom makes the potato/macaroni salad, which is a great upsell on their part, but it's not good.  Unfortunately there's not a better alternative I've found in Old City forcing me to go outside old city for hoagies and cheesesteaks. I imagine this place survives on foot traffic like many of it's neighbors.

My family loves the Potbelly Sandwich Shop on Temple University's campus.  Shelby and the rest of the crew are awesome, the atmosphere is always buzzing, and the food is satisfying if you are on your way to cheer on the Owls at a sporting event (just a quick walk away).  But we especially like Potbelly in the fall and winter, when they bring back their chicken pot pie soup.  It's a like a hug from a loved one.  Piping hot, creamy soup with vegetables, big chunks of white meat chicken and crunchy topping. Yum!  Grab a bowl of soup, a cookie and a soda and you are set.

A family run business that embraces their Italian American heritage, which shows through their homestyle sandwiches. A bit expensive, but overall good value. 

Everything is made fresh; nothing is fried. Just asked the female behind the cashier. The dining space is quite small, and the tables are close together; however, there is a dining patio outside on the street.

There's also a clean and private washroom in the back.

Let's start with the price...I got a caprese sandwich and a diet Coke from the fountain. Total bill: $12.83. Wow...and the fountain drink was like $2.50 or $2.75 of that. Really? I mean, that's the kind of price I pay at the ballpark...c'mon. So, on price.value I would have given this a 2. However...

The caprese sandwich was really tasty. It has some shave prosciutto in addition to the sweet peppers and mozzarella. It was super, and I ate more than I should have. So, from a sandwich perspective: 4.

Seating is really tight in there. And I have a bit of claustrophobia, so I do't like that. It's a cold day today so it wasn't completely crowded, but I didn't finish my sandwich quickly so that I didn't get trapped in the corner. That would have been horrible. Seating: 2.5.

So, that rounds out to a 3. Just okay because of the sticker shock.

I love Jimmy Johns one of the best places on campus! Very friendly staff and very efficient and quick, good if your in a hurry! Four about 6$ I can get a shandwich, soda, chips and a cookie, the place is very nice inside but don't think its a place to study in...they play loud music which can be a good study distraction while your on a food run. I will continue to eat here!

Yuck.  Sooooo not my thing.  I can kinda-sorta deal with a plain turkey sub on whole wheat.

There is little nutritional goodness to be had here.  I simply hate fast food.

But it is cheap.  (You get what you pay for.)

I ordered a cheesesteak, fries and a soda from here today.  The total for the order was $20 (not kidding)  I was sorely disappointed, both in the quality of the food and the lackluster service and response to my issue.
I ordered the cheesesteak with mustard, ketchup, pickles, hot peers, fried onions.  It had nearly no hot peppers and it was missing the pickles and the mustard.  The size of the sandwich was very small,  certainly not what I expected for the price.

I called to let the shop know that my sandwich was missing pickles and mustard, and the woman who answered the phone said "well I can credit you 25 cents, but pickles are free."  Really?   I just paid $20 for a mediocre cheesesteak and your got the order wrong.  

Needless to say, I will not order from them again, and I am sure they really won't care, because they don't like to deliver to our location anyway.  I will find a steak place that cares about its clientele.
My fave ramen in Philly.  The tonkatsu ramen with added egg and spicy sauce is my usual order, despite the salt and fat overload, I keep going back for more.  And more.  And more.
Ate at Campo's with friends based on their recommendation and was very satisfied with the food. delicious!! Would highly recommend!

Typical Philly rudeness. I was here with a group of "out of towners" and the girl working the counter made sure we knew we were in "Philly." She seemed annoyed when we ordered and when I asked for 7 forks she got them but made sure to say "that's what your hands are for." Overall the food is ok, I had the eggplant parmigiana and I would definitely not run for it. My guests had the cheesesteak and were not impressed. If you want a good cheesesteak go to Pudge's in Conshohocken, don't waste your money at this place. I have no idea how this place is Zagat rated.

It was my second time eating there, but I don't think I'm going to go back again. It's a small restaurant with very limited sitting, but this restaurant doesn't seem get busy anyway, so the sitting is not an issue. 

There was only one server even during dinner time. She seemed like to stand at the counter and look at people in the kitchen making ramen instead of paying attention to the customer. They have a small menu, they offer some appetizers and a few choices of ramen. The ramen I got was so salty, and the broth tasted not as good as the ramen place in Chinatown, they added too much water in the broth. 

I went there a few months ago, they had better ramen and bigger portion at that time, and I think they raised the price, which is fine since the location is very good, but for the service and taste, I don't think I will go back again.

Going to be honest here: I don't have much to compare it to, other than those served at burger joints around the US. I don't know whether it was the quality of the sandwich -- which was amazing -- or the fact that it had Philadelphia wrapped around it, but I was in love at the first bite.

The reason this doesn't get a higher rating is the restaurant takes cash only, and offers an ATM that charges a buck and a half to use it. They also charge a ton of money for the sides and a buck and a quarter for a drink refill. That and the fact that the place is super tiny and super crowded. But it's all worth it if you want the best cheesesteak you've ever eaten.
The staff in Campo's are amazing! Food is great too. Really went above and beyond for my girlfriends birthday today. Def recommend and will be back.

As an outsider, I don't think I would be the best to judge on Philly cheesesteak. I've had this around 5 years ago and I couldn't stop thinking about it.

...It is exactly how I remembered it! Personally, I think regular cheesesteaks are just  a bit plain. Campo's have "The Heater" which is the same except it is slabbed with hot sauce and spices. It really kicked things up a notch and added some much needed flavor, I'm a huge fan!
C'mon! $32 for two cheesesteaks, two beers, and self-serve! Sandwiches were OK, but not $30-bucks worth...

I was here a few weeks ago and forgot to write a review.. we had an extremely large order for my family (I think 28 pieces with like 5 large sides) the lady who took my order wasn't the happiest but I for being so busy I waited less than ten minutes which to me being busy and such a large order was great. I wish I got the name of the girl who actually gave me my order because she was SOOO nice! I came back in after going to the car because my disabled relative desperately needed a drink and upon re entering, the same woman asked "what are you missing sweetie?" I said nothing, just need a soda. She handed me a large cup and said don't wait in that line, have a great day! 

I was nervous after reading the not so great reviews on this place but when getting home everyone agreed the food was really good, really hot and most importantly CORRECT! 
Thank you for that KFC!
Wait around 30 mins for a ramen that worse than a 3 mins homemade instant noodle. Ramen is too salty. Fired chicken is too plain.
The girl that made our sandwiches had on gloves the problem is, she used the same gloves to handle cash and use the register.  Very unsanitary and disgusting!

So Campo's has the honor of being the first place I've even been to in Philly and the first true cheesesteak I've ever had.  Overall, I thought the cheesesteak was very tasty, although $8 seems a bit high considering the size of the sandwich.  I also have to admit I was surprised that no fries or chips were included for that price.  Still, truth is it was more than enough food for me and the dining area was clean and comfortable which was more than I can say for many of the other cheesesteak stands I saw in the area.  I'd recommend Campo's if your in the area looking for a good eat.

My wife and I each enjoyed the Bacontastic burger (just $2), which was very tasty. My wife got a medium Oreo milkshake (which she loved). I was happy with a medium chocolate shake, which was a very good chocolate flavor. Both were so thick it was hard to get them through the largest diameter straw I've ever seen. It was our first experience at a Checkers.
Minus one star for seeming bothered that I wanted to order a sandwich at your business. Minus one star for higher than average prices. Minus one star for portion not meeting the price.

this place stinks. VERY overpriced for a VERY small cheesesteak. I thought mine was very fatty, and overall, flavorless. I have been once and I'll never go back. you can get a better cheesesteak from soooo many other places in the city, don't waste your time here.

I work a block from this place so after constant raves from coworkers I finally went in to get a burger for lunch. It was made completely wrong and was a total disappointment. I asked for 'very well done' and got medium rare; and I asked for 'extra raw onions, none cooked' and instead got a HUGE pile of greasy cooked CHOPPED onion bits. When I got back to work five minutes later to eat the actual burger, the bottom half of the bun was pulp. All in all not worth $10 in the slightest.

The second star is entirely because of the smokin' hot redheaded guy who was working the register. If looks and personality could equal a tasty burger this place would be five stars for sure.

Be prepared to get exactly what you expect.  You will not be thrilled, nor will you be disappointed.

No frills sandwiches made from solid ingredients with an emphasis on speed.  Hilariously labeled paper products (who doesn't like the word "DRINK" on cups and "WIPE" on napkins?)

Two types of bread, about 6 kinds of sandwiches (multiplied by various combinations of the meats).  Cookies, chips and pickles.  That's it.

My only beef:  as a default, they gut the long rolls even if you don't get lettuce.  I guess the idea is that it'll more easily fit the fixings (and you won't have things squirting out the side when you bite down), but when you don't get lettuce the squeeze out problem is avoided.

I dunno, very minor and specific problem, but it's the only place I can think of where you order a hoagie and you need to request that they don't tear half the bread out while they're making it.
the food is good but the staff needs to pay a visit to subway to see how well they organize thier assembly line. a little out of wack at quizznos.

Eew!  Taco Hell in 30th Street Station. Combined with a stripped down pizza hut.

I'd rather go hungry.
Food is meh. Too salty without much flavor  beside that. Service is slow and poor. For lunch, expert to be laye for your meeting.

Walked in hungry, walked out starving. Being from Philly, gotta say that was the smallest cheesesteak I ever ate. Should have went to Wawa. 
Very disappointed. Feel bad for tourists, they are being ripped off.

Campo's is good, if you're at Citizen's Bank Park. This location was horrific. For whatever reason, they only accept cash. Seriously, it's 2011, this is unacceptable and plus they do not make this announcement until you're ready to pay. The service was slow; it takes about 5 minutes to get your cheesesteak, at the ballpark count on about 15 seconds. I would simply stay away from this location, there are better alternatives in the area.

Born and raised in Philly.  I've had better cheese steaks from Wawa in Orlando Florida. This was quite possibly the worst cheese steak I've ever had and it's hard to mess up something when you put cheese on it. If you're gonna use flank steak to save money, it needs to be cut in the right direction. Thought I was chewing on a tennis shoe..

This place is amazing! I love the atmosphere, the workers! The customer service is amazing. The ramen is delicious. It's a cute little place. I try to go every time I am in the area! I even went for my birthday a few years back.

Vegans - skip this location of Campo's if you want a tasty vegan sandwich.  They don't know what they are doing - and they don't seem to care.

My daughter had a "good" vegetarian cheese-steak at the Campo's located in the Stadium, so she was excited for me to try the same mock cheese-steak sandwich at this location in Old City when I came to visit her yesterday.  OMG, what a waste of money - $10.25 each.  We were both shocked at how tasteless our sandwiches were!

The problem, I discovered, is that no one - at least at this location this past Sunday - had any idea what to do with seitan to make it taste good.  My daughter is not sure if they may have seasoned the seitan at the Stadium location with something like Bragg's Amino Acids or whatever, because it tasted much better to her the last time she had eaten it.  Still, she had gotten that sandwich with dairy cheese instead of the rice cheese and the onions were sliced nice and thin as they should be, which was not the case yesterday in Old City.  

The reason our sandwiches tasted so bad, I believe, is the lack of seasoning when preparing the seitan as a substitute for the steak.  It really was like eating small bits of moist cardboard!  It did not help that the onions were cut into large chunks that were also undercooked.  Same for the green pepper.  Even the dense, white club roll that works well with real steak made it much worse - and very unhealthy, too!  While that dense roll is good at soaking up the juice from real steak, it made the vegan version seem dry and even more tasteless as a sandwich.

I took my sandwich back to the cook after taking a couple of bites to see what was going on and if he could do anything to fix it.  I complained about the lack of flavor in the seitan and the onions.  He apologized and later admitted they don't eat - or even taste - their vegan stuff so he had no idea what I was talking about.  He just added a sprinkle of garlic powder and put a little more of the still-flavorless seitan on my roll the second time it was made.  I should have just asked for my money back, because I still could not enjoy eating it - and it was too unhealthy a sandwich to eat without enjoying the taste.  I really tried to eat it because I was so hungry, but I ended up giving it back to him.  It was a total waste of money and time.  Good thing I had a Kind nut bar in my handbag.

This posting is just to warn other vegans what to expect if they go to this or any of the Campo's locations.  They don't really care about pleasing their vegan customers.  It seems they put a vegan option on the menu only so meat-eaters can get a "wayward" vegan friend to come along to eat there with them.  Neither my daughter nor I will be going back there again - not when there are so many other places in Philly that truly cater to the tastes of vegans as well as meat-lovers.  I am not a drinker, but I love the ambiance as well as the food at Kyber Pass Pub at 56 S. 2nd St.  Their mock pulled-pork sandwich with vegan coleslaw is amazing!  It is not healthy food by any means, but it tastes delicious and is vegan.

I enjoyed my bowl of ramen here.  I got the Black Pig bowl - primarily because I wanted to try the burnt garlic oil, and it didn't let me down.  It gave off the fragrance I was looking for, while also adding a nice touch of umami.  The noodles are on the thin side, which didn't bother me, but they do lack the bite found in slightly thicker noodles.  The pork was good (4 out of 5) and the soup was also good (4 out of 5).  Neither was exploding with flavor, but flavorful nonetheless.  I would come back.

Important note:  This place is cash only!

So I was starving earlier and I needed food. Very fast delivery from there indeed. I ordered online and it was a very smooth process. I t got a diablo hoagie. I'm usually never a big fan of hoagies but these guys do it well. Italian bread is great but kinda hard in texture. Loads of meats stuffed right in. If you want quick delivery, check these guys out.

We waited fifteen minutes in the entryway to be acknowledged by the staff. Eventually walked in further to ask someone directly about the wait, who replied "I'm busy". If we were told it was an X minute wait we could have made a decision like at literally any other restaurant.

Waited in for food for 15min
Got surf and turf, I live right around the corner. Got home and the food was rushed box was soggy and fries were under cooked. Needless to say I will not be getting food from that location again. I can say this much, the gentleman that ring me up was extremely nice.! They all seemed very nice in there just too much business for them to handle.
Long line lady taking orders very helpful and friendly cheesesteak was good not outstanding good middle of the road place.

This family run establishment is hands down the best. Cheesesteaks to Ceaser salad and everything in between are made perfect and to order. Can't wait to go back and get my favorite the chicken Ceaser cheesesteak. If your in old city it's a must.

Cash only! My first true Philly cheesesteak. I enjoyed it! The flavor was great and I loved the steak. I got it with the fried onions and peppers. My only complaints is that I wish there were more cheese and that they didn't sell out of their other bread choices so quickly. Also wish it came with a side of some sort. Overall, the cheesesteak was tasty though and it came out quickly!

Plenty of outdoor seating, conga line ordering.  Fast service, even when the place is packed.  Quality cheese steaks within walking distance of all of Philly's main historical attractions.  Authentically delicious cheese steaks...  Enjoy!!
Cute little place. Yummy food! I had the ramen that was supposed to be spicy, but it was spicy at all...although it was still very good.

Eh, I had a turkey BLT one day and it was alright. It was my first time at Jimmy John's I just wanted to check it out. Everyone greeted me and I thought it was strange, but hey it's better than not being greeted like Wendy's around the corner. I don't really dig hoagies too much so I really appreciate some of the competition's gimmicks a little more (toasters, special sauce, crazy peppers). Jimmy John's was like a straight up hoagie I could've gotten anywhere, but minus the Amoroso.

I saw the bad reviews before going to this location, but I thought, eh it can't be that bad. I was wrong. This KFC location is horrible. I only got half of my order that I paid for. They literally replaced one of the pieces of chicken with a piece of wing. Food was soggy. Didn't give us to cookies, potato wedges, etc that we ordered. Employees were so rude. Get your food somewhere else folks.

As a college student I appreciate having a chick-fil-a so close and convenient. They got being close right, but it is definitely not convenient. They have it set up as 'grab and go' style, but it inevitably doesn't make anything quicker just slower. They don't re-stock items frequently enough, the employees sit down at tables when nobody is at the registers and when you go up they don't look up from their phones so you have to stand and wait. They are also frequently out of drinks and fries, and you can almost guarantee if they have one type of sandwich they will be out of the other. They have also frequently been out of chick-fil-a sauce.
My favorite place in Center City to get a steak wit.  Great place to go when touring or hanging out at night in Old City.  The steak is always fresh and the staff is friendly.

Pretty decent ramen. Not sure this place can survive in Tokyo (probably not), but OK for Philly.

The noodles can be a bit harder. And they have to be more consistent with the time spent cooking noodles. The variance is larger than what is allowed in Japan I think. I usually eat Hiro (soy + pork broth) ramen or Miso ramen (miso + pork broth). Both are good.

The set menu (ramen + salad + a side dish) is a great value. Go when the set menu is available. Although they are not terribly good at making dumplings (I can do a lot better).

The worst thing about the ramen joint is the service. There is only one guy serving, and the guy is nice but very inefficient. 1/3 times he forgets my salad or dumplings or the fact that I ordered extra noodle. Possibly communication problem because the cooks seem Hispanic. Anyway, he is nice even if he makes mistakes...

I think this place is behind Terakawa, and above Nom Nom, especially with the great set menu.
So this is a fast food chain, but their strawberry cheesecake sundae is pretty baller, and they have these Cha Ching specialty burgers 2 for $3. It's super clean there (and super bullet proof).

I was only in Philly for a short stay and my heart was telling me I had to try a cheese steak while my stomach was already full from a heavy PA Dutch breakfast. People kept telling me to try the joints on South St because thats where all the tourists go, but I was not down for wait 1+ hours for a freakin sandwich. So Campo's came up on my phone and it was a pleasant walk away from the Liberty Bell!

I ordered the "Heater"- a spicy cheese steak, packed with jalapeno cheddar and buffalo sauce. The meat was tender and piping hot, the cheese "whiz" was on point, not too much to the point where you get sick of the taste, and the spiciness just made it easier to chow down even though i wasnt hungry. They give generous portions, although I think thats just the Philly way. 

I wouldnt mind going back for a second bite!
Not that bad, really.  The bread was the best part of my eggplant parm.  Service wasn't bad and generally not a bad situation at all.  Prices are high but what do you want?  It's Old(e) City.

We went to Hiro's for dinner in Philly - The host/server was very nice, attentive, and happy to explain different dishes and condiments.  We both had the Inch of Heaven - the broth was delicious with deep, caramelized meat flavors.  The portions were large and well priced.  The place was clean and service was quick.  Highly recommend to try this place

Despite what others have said I think hiro ramen is top notch. Is it as authentic as some of the NY spots or over in Japan? Not really, but their own version of ramen is quite tasty. The menu was limited but then again their ingredients are locally sourced and Hurricane Sandy just hit the surrounding area. The broth of the shoyu ramen was rich and flavorful. The noodles were a little similar to Chinese egg noodles as compared to some other ramen that I had before but it was very good and well prepared to al dente. Plenty of toppings in the bowl of ramen with two pieces of  pork belly, bamboo shoots, half of a soft cooked egg, nori, and scallions. Service was great and the staff was very friendly. All this for only $8? It's a no brainer.
Solid experience.  Delicious food.  We tried a handful of the dishes and they were all delicious.  The fried chicken appetizer was perfect.
The most authentic Japanese ramen I've tried so far in Philly. And I recommend the gyoza highly, the skin is chewy and thin, love it!

Your choice of 7 different cheese steaks, including BBQ, Italian, and Pizza options. Talk about variety! 

I recently tried the "Holy Feldman" (a super-spicy cheese steak made with pepper jack cheese and hot sauce) and was a little disappointed. I definitely like spicy food, but not when it's so spicy it lacks flavor. For me, I'm sticking with the traditional cheese steak. At $7, it's possibly the best deal in Old City. 

This was my default "go to" place when I had friends visiting from out of town.
This place is awesome. Probably the best cheesesteaks in town. Great staff and great service.
We got a free beer here with our walking tour and they offer a 10% discount on the food for tour customers too.  The food was good but nothing great.  Nice lively place tho.
Ordered the chicken parm, the chicken tasted like rubber.  Very low quality.  Didn't even finish it, you are better off waiting on the line at Sonny's a few doors down.

The ramen is OK but would have expected from a ramen house rated as the best of philly, to have homemade noddles, and a more flavoured and tasty broth...
I would only recommend for the ones who have never tried a really good one, if you are a fan of ramen, please dont waste your time... and next time you re in NY just run to ichiran!!! Nothing comparable.... 
Price is cheap but still doesnt increase the rating...

I LOVE this place! I've eaten here three times in the last two weeks & the food is delicious. I love the chicken soy ramen and karaage chicken. The restaurant is consistently good & never too busy. Cash only but they have an ATM on site.

Ate at Campo's in March 2019, and liked my cheesesteak!

I was visited Liberty Bell and Independence Hall, Campo's was the closes to the area so we took a short 9 minute walk to have some lunch.

The staff were all friendly, but they only take CASH.

The cheese-steak was really good, but a little on the small size, especially when considering the price.  They also have lots of different sides.

I'm not a cheese-steak connoisseur, so it tasted really good to me.  I would eat here again.

Decent enough place.  As a Philadelphian, I'm not crazy about their cheesesteaks - I much prefer Sonny's which is just steps away.  That said, their other sandwiches are pretty decent, though relatively expensive for a sandwich.  I live less than a block away, which makes this quick and easy for a tasty lunch or dinner.  

Tonight, I enjoyed the Caprese sandwich, which was huge, but so was the price.  Actually, the $8.00 sandwich wasn't the shocker...the shocker was the $2.50 fountain soda - another $1.00 for refills!  I took my sandwich home, but the guy in front of me order a Sam Adams - $7.00!  Those are ballpark prices!

Here's the deal with Campo's...

I went in for a turkey hoagie with sharp provolone. I came out $9 poorer and that's without anything to wash it down with. A short time later I was disgusted. The hoagie was dry, the roll was stiff, the sharp provolone (which costs an entire dollar extra) didn't... taste... like... ANYTHING... and my lettuce was yellow! 

They gave me yellow lettuce like that's the best they could do...yellow. I'm not tryin to hear it. The best I can do is a YELLOW star for that.

I was in in town for 4 days and excited about getting a "real" Philly Cheesesteak - I was recommended to go here by a tour guide - what a mistake - I ordered the "works" (onions, mushrooms and peppers with Provolone) very little flavor to the sandwich which was also very dry and the steak?  - cut too thick and tough as boot straps! - Mushrooms not cooked - just no passion put into to a sandwich which is their businesses "Bread & Butter"
Campo's - you let Philly down !

Really McDonald's .16 for a packet of buffalo sauce.. I didn't ask for a discount when I ordered my chicken sandwich with no toppings.  This is a great way to loose customers, next time I will just go to chic fil a there team is much more customer friendly.

Hands down, this is my favorite cheesesteak. Ever. 

When I was younger, I'd work 2 weeks every summer in Philly, and for lunch I'd try a new place every day. I always came back to Campo's. The people are great. Food is amazing.  I've traveled out of my way just to stop back in later in life.  It's been a few years, but I think I need to make my way back there. 

But seriously,  Geno's, Pat's... sure. They're "originals" or whatever. Go there to say you've been, but you'll wind up craving Campo's after you've gone. 

Go on, trust me. I haven't lied to anyone yet!
Ordered the "Gates of Hell" ramen bowl. It was very good. Will return to try the other items on the menu. Cash only.

Finally got to try the meatloaf and unfortunately I'm not very pleased with it.  It comes with two sides and a piece of bread.  They gave a generous portion of sweet potato fries (which I love) and some mac-n-cheese that kinda tasted microwaved/reheated..  Fine with me, but what I'm not happy about is the actual meatloaf:  completely raw in the center.  Raw and red ground beef.  Completely turned my stomach.  I have no problem with ordering a STEAK medium or medium-well, but not my ground beef.  Ground beef needs to be cooked thoroughly.  Why would they serve meat that is not fully cooked?!  I took a picture of the raw meat and I'm still trying to figure out how (if at all possible) I can upload it to this site.  I didn't bother calling to complain because it's not worth getting into any kind of altercation with those people.  Ya live, ya learn!  I just won't order their meatloaf again.

my experience so far with Ramen places is that it's usually pretty salty which makes the noodles taste so good. My companion and I were satisfied with the portion for $10 and the service was great. It's good, not great, more vegetables in the mix would have made it 5 stars.
Fast, helpful staff. And gluten free options! One of the best Cheesesteaks I've had! Would recommend. Heads up though - cash only!

I have always had a great meal here. I love everything here. It is always freshly made and available. The better part about my experience is the customer service and the friendly vibe from all of the employees. The all make my day and make me want to come back.

My favorite ramen spot in Philly! The lunch special is unbeatable where you can get an appetizer, salad, and bowl of ramen for just $13! The chicken karaage app is my favorite but my friends have liked the gyoza too. The ramen broth is very hearty and delicious, with the Inch of Heaven being my favorite. The Gates of Hell is good for those who like spicy. I just wish they gave a bit more pork with the bowl, but you can always add on more.

The seating area is small so sometimes you may have to wait but I've never had to wait for longer than 10-15 minutes for a table. The outside is unassuming and easily missed, but it's right next door to Milkboy. The decorations are cute! Place is cash only, but they do have an atm you can use. Definitely recommend!

Went here with a large groups
 of students and they were so incredibly accommodating! Their patience and kindness was unsurpassed. Not only that, but the food was perfect for our kids first Philly Cheesesteak experience. The are a family run business and we were happy to support them. Oh, and their brownies are amazing!!!
The location SUCKS, bad service,  long lines, no one answers the phone,  items missing from the order

I came with my friend, his decision to go. It actually was pretty good, good service, good food. Once we came in, we were greeted with a smile. The waitress always came to check up on us to make sure we were alright. I ordered the Gates of Hell while he ordered the Hiro Inch of Heaven. And we both can say, $10 it was pretty worth it. Totally would go again.  A very cozy and comfortable to dine. Should totally check it out.

Still very cash only. Small restaurant with like 5 tables and bar seating. It's very hot in here. Between the ramen and the swelter from the summer heat, I felt very uncomfortably hot in here slurping my noodles down. Saw the prepackaged ramen noodles while they were preparing our bows, which was disappointing. Maybe they're house made and sealed in plastic for convenience? 

Had the Gates of Hell, which had a nice bit of spice that was not overpowering and resulting in lava poop. Broth was decent, but so salty. In addition, there was a disappointing amount of pork flavoring. 

My ramen ranking here in Philadelphia so far:
1. Terakawa
2. Hiro
3. Yamitsuki

Will be back to try the Inch of Heaven.

The italian sub was very good, but it was very crowded on Saturday afternoon and took about 10 minutes to order and 20 minutes after that to get my order.  $2.50 for a fountain drink with $1.00 for a refill is a little steep.

On my second day in Philly (Friday) I headed downtown.  I picked up some Septa tokens and proceeded to the Independence Visitors Center.   I spent several hours touring the historical sites.  My favorites include Liberty Bell, St Mary's Church and its adjoining cemetery, Christ Church, Fireman's Museum, Elferth's Alley, and so many more.  I asked about where to have lunch at Christ Church and was told to look on Market Street.   

As I ventured that way, I spotted Campo's and remembered reading about them on Tripadvisor forums.  So, I made my way inside and ordered a cheesesteak with onion and American with a side of "Mom's" homemade cole slaw.  I will tell you that I was very grateful I made this choice.  The sandwich was fantastic and quite tasty and the coleslaw was as good as my mom made (sorry, Mom).  The staff were quite friendly and loved to joke around with me.  It made for a  special meal and I'm glad I stopped.

My only problem:  the sandwich was so filling that I nearly needed a take home sack.  That wouldn't have been easy considering I was a mile from the hotel. So I "Forced" myself to devour it all in one sitting.
OMG. I stopped here on my way from NY down South. Excellent Sandwiches. And "Mom makes the salads" MMMMM. I love this place forget the tourist trap Gino's and head here instead

Did not live up to expectations. Ordered the works cheesesteak and mac & cheese. It was bland and tasteless. I've had better cheesesteaks in TX and can make a better mac & cheese! The staff wasn't friendly and bordered on rude. Wouldn't recommend it.

The food is okay, but it is definitely is a quick, convenient and affordable way to quench a serious craving for biryani or a kati roll. The service is good, the seating area is nice enough, and it's never too packed to where you can't find a seat. The lunch specials are awesome. For just $7.95, you can get either a veggie or chicken kati roll AND a generous portion of veggie or chicken biryani. I know there are a lot of good Indian food trucks in the area, but this is a pretty good deal for a place with sheltered comfy seating. It is also opened late night and is quite ideal drunk food, at least for me.

Super cute ramen place in an unassuming Center City location. The sign isn't obviously at all, as I thought it was a closed storefront the first few times I walked by. After entering you are transported to the ambience of a Japanese stall ramen shop. The ramen broth is delicious. The ingredients are paltry ( a few shoots of bamboo and one piece of pork per bowl for a 1 star deduction), but the flavor is excellent. The small side salad is delicious with a ginger kick.

Stopped by to grab ham and cheese hoagie for my hubs. I asked for a large and paid $10.00. I'm from Jersey, so when we say large, we expect a large sandwich, especially if it costs $10.00. I'm pretty sure I got a medium or maybe a small by other sandwich standards. 

My husband and I usually split a sandwich, but that won't be the case this time. He will kill this one all by himself. I don't plan to return to Campos to get robbed again.

Best Darn Ramen.  Granted, the only ramen I've only gotten is the Gates of Hell, but it is the cure-all for everything that ails you.  Perfectly spicy, delicious and soothing broth.  Do yourself a HUGE favor and get an extra soy-marinated egg (you're welcome).  The size is fairly large, but it's hard to put your chopstix and spoon down to take any home.  They have a great lunch special, which is $14 for any ramen bowl, an appetizer, and a drink (ramen bowls on their own are $10-$11ish).  

I cannot recommend this place enough for ramen.  Go there now!!

The sandwiches are good and I love their cheddar broccoli soup. It's usually pretty packed since they are located near Temple University's college campus.  It's always clean (tables, chairs, floors) and that is a great reason as to why I continue to visit. Usually the staff is pretty nice, but the one lady with the headscarf does not appear to be pleasant.

Hands down one of the best hoagie and steak shops in the city! The Campo family are great people and make you feel right at home! Try the Original Cin for a spicy turkey sandwich or the Flyers Ice Steak for an incredible twist on the Philly Cheese Steak!

As others have said, that cashier was rude and had an attitude.  Now I wasn't sure what "wizz" was because I'm not from Philly. So I made a joke and said "yeah as you can see I'm not from around here! Haha!" with a smile.  And she replies to me "Yeah I can tell by that ugly shirt you have on" (I had a NY Yankees shirt on) Whether you're a fan or not, you don't say something like that to a CUSTOMER.

I'm not experienced when it comes to cheese steaks, but I feel it could have been better.  Meat was dry, bread was dry, the only thing good was the cheese.  Also, 8 bucks. Way over priced.

Next time I'm trying Geno's, Pat's, or Gianfrancos. (the other recommended places)

Really nice family-owned restaurant. About as laid back as a restaurant can be. We asked at our hotel where the best local authentic Philly cheesesteak could be had. Campo's was their first answer. Nice selection. Steak. Or chicken or other meats if you want. Will definitely go again when we are in town next.

Absolutely enjoyed the entire experience, it is a family-run business where every product is made with love. The bread was the softest & tastiest I or my fiance have ever tried. Small seating area but all the better for friendlier ambiance. Convenient spot close to most tourist attractions (Liberty Bell, Independence Hall & even the Delaware River) Oh and the food perfectly defined what it means to be an original Philadelphia Cheese steak!

I can't say that there is a better $10 bowl of ramen in Philadelphia, and better than that is if you make the lunch special with a salad and an app. Take those savings and be sure to add some extra chashu. 

The restaurant can be passed if you're not paying attention and can be cramped but that's the character of the place. 

If there is a wait, I suggest waiting. It's delicious. 

The service is quick and the food is delicious. 

I highly suggest the Black Pig.

Ordered 2 sodas with my 2 cheesesteaks. Was looking at the bottle in the fridge and didn't even notice the fountain soda machine. Woman at the counter grabbed a Diet dr. Pepper from the fridge and filled up Coke from the fountain. Didn't even notice til the fountain soda was filling up and asked for a bottle from fridge because it tastes better. Woman was mean about it and wouldn't give me the bottle. Would not budge and had an attitude Charged $3 for flat coke. She finally allowed for a free refill after i asked for it 2/3 times.  I promise i will never ever go to Campos again. So many options to get food and drinks.  The whole experience reeked of Old Philly attitude.  She lost a customer for life over it and I'm telling others.

There a number of ramen noodle houses in the area, and everyone has their preferences but Hiro is right in the middle for me compared to Terakawa and Cheu Noodle.  I would rank Hiro over Cheu, but well below Terakawa.    

I like the authentic environment similar to Terakawa but slightly smaller.  The menu isn't as extensive either.  The service was good but they didn't take credit card, big ding there since the other two places do.  The price is better than Cheu.  And lastly it's a byo, take that for what it's worth.  

Overall, it's a strong ramen noodle restaurant.  Can't ding it for anything major.  But if you had only ONE ramen noodle place, I'd go to Terakawa instead.

I visited Hiro Ramen House and had the Vegetable Ramen dinner, which turns out is vegan. It was awesome. Very tasty and really good price. My son had the Portfilio which is Ramen in chicken and pork broth, an egg, pork belly, and some vegetables. It was a bit spicier and, also, really good. The place itself is a small dining room but not too small. The server was extremely nice. The only reason for the 4 star review is the cash-only policy. I will return for more tasty ramen. On my secong visit I had the "Gates of Hell" Ramen. It was, needless to say, REALLY spicy but I loved it. My family and I can't wait to go back!!!
$15 minimum for credit card purchases and they do not give cups for water. I cancelled my order and left unhappy.

Without an obvious storefront sign, you might walk up and down the Center City sidewalk before realizing the clandestine Hiro Ramen House is right in front of you.  The shop is warm and cozy with space for solo diners at the counter and for couples/groups at wooden tables.  They serve about 7 or 8 different staple ramen broths with variant add-ins, but all of them deep and flavorful.  Definitely ask for extra noodles and a spicy chili bomb if you're willing.

Hmm...looking at the reviews, I'm beginning to wonder if it was just my tastes that made me think these cheesesteaks were okay at best. It will definitely fill you up though. I got the Cheesesteak with the works, but it was a bit too dry for me. Their potato salad was good but not amazing. Cash Only.
One of the best bowls of ramen I've ever had. Incredibly, savory broth. Buttery, tender meat. Absolutely delicious! I would recommend this to anyone for any savory meal or to satisfy a ramen craving.

I love this place. :-)
I have been looking for good ramen place since I got to Philadelphia. I am a typical Japanese guy who likes to eat ramen at least one a week.
I just droped by this restaurant couple of weeks ago, and ordered Shoyu Ramen, which is ramen with soy sauce based soup.
The taste is very authentic Japanese ramen, which is very close to ramen in Japan, and I loved it.
I am glad that I could find very authentic ramen restaurant in Philadelphia and have decided to come here often.

the worst i ever had .i paid $25.00 for two sandwiches the only take cash no credit cards.and you know why.I ask the cashier for a cup of water stated that the do not have water when i see the water on the tap soda machine.i said you do have water it is on your machine .her response was we sell soda.i said is this the way you treat your customers and her respond is if you do not like it do not come back.had the sandwiches to go and the wher nasty tasting.so please do your self a favor do not waste your money.

UPDATED: safety hazard and sloppy service. 

I came in during a busy lunch hour and placed a to go order. When the waitress gave me the food I asked her if there was a fork/spoon in the bag and she assured me yes. I tipped her for the speedy service but unfortunately there was no utensils.

Then I found two pieces of string with the pork. I called the hostess back and told her this and she only offered apologies. 

There are plenty of great ramen spots around the city so I won't be back here again.

Absolutely delicious. My second time here and it is just awesome. I had the chicken works with American cheese. It's got delicious fresh chicken and mushrooms, peppers and onions. Rolls super fresh.  I can't wait to come back here. Also the staff is really kind and the bathrooms are clean. Cash only.

Black pig. Get it. This place is was better beyond all expectations. The black garlic flavor was roasty and flavorful. And the fried chicken appetizer was tender and crispy, just the right amount. The amount is on the smaller side but the texture of the noodles and the flavor of the broth is perfect. It is BYOB so bring your sakes and enjoy!

We are hosting an exchange student from Spain and we could not let him go back home without tasting a Philly Cheesesteak! We chose Campos because they offered so many sandwiches to choose from and I have a  gluten allergy. They had the most delicious gluten free bun I have ever tasted. The service was friendly and warm! We will definitely go back.

This is my favorite place to get a cheesesteak in Philly and I'm surprised to see so many low ratings. The Heater cheesesteak, topped with jalapeños and hot sauce, is delicious albeit non traditional. It seems like a lot if people in Philly are purists when it comes to cheesesteaks so I don't know if many people like this variation on a cheesesteak as much as I do. However, there are plenty of places to get a traditional cheesesteak in Philly so I appreciate that Campo's adds their own touch.

The Campo's cheesesteak also stands out because they use a softer roll than many places and the stick is more thickly cut. I enjoy the thicker cut steak because it doesn't dry out as easily and from a texture standpoint, I find the soft roll to be more appealing. The only gripe I have is that they do charge more for a cheesesteak than other places in Philly and they don't put as much meat on the sandwich. This isn't a huge issue for me; I don't live in Philly and since cheesesteaks such where I live, I'm willing to shell out a little more for a once a year treat. However, the price to meat ratio may be why some of the locals don't seem to like it as much. I do wish they sold fries since nothing  completes the fatty amazing was of a cheesesteak quite like French fries. Nonetheless, this place will always be a stop for me when in philly so I'll just own my shameless tourist status!
amazing ramen the pork is so good and the broth in the gates of hell is the perfect amount of spice. will keep coming back!

The best ramen place in Philly to me. Limited and simple menu but the ramen was perfect in portion  and the broth was flavorful. I'm glad that they decided to open on Sunday now bc it was difficult to satisfy my craving during the weekends back then.
Used to go here all the time because it was right next to school. Small and cozy place with good ramen.
Very disappointed. Meat was fatty and hard to chew. Had to throw it away. It was $13 at the Phila. Wings game in the Wells Fargo Center.
Very good!! Better than Ippudos'. The place is small but clean and has a traditional Japanese feel.

This is a very average ramen joint. The major weakness of the ramen is the broth, which just isn't very flavorful (I had the tonkotsu with the black garlic oil with a spice bomb). The noodles and the toppings were decent, and they were generous with the garlic oil. But the broth is the soul of a good bowl of ramen, and this place is lacking in that respect.
The best ramen I've ever had! Fresh vegetables atop delicious ramen and broth. The service was excellent. I highly recommend Hiro if you are looking for taste and quality.

This philly cheesesteak is pretty good.  The onions were a little more crunchy which added a nice contrast to the soft bread and steak.  The steak was not bad, but not as flavorful I would have liked.  I had to add a little salt to bring out more flavor.  The wiz was good and the sandwich was made fast.  

Overall, not a bad sandwich and will definitely fulfill your philly cheesesteak needs if you have any.

My family was in town for my son's graduation and insisted on going to Campo's "for an authentic cheesesteak" (Evidently Campo's advertises heavily to tourists. My auntie saw their commercial numerous times while staying at the hotel) For $15 my auntie had what she described as "an extraordinary authentic cheesesteak" I've lived in Philadelphia for 20 plus years , it's just a small decent tasting cheesesteak in a very touristy location that's certainly not worth the $15 price tag.

Hiro ramen is a really solid ramen joint if you've got a craving for it, like I did when I went.

Just as a heads up also before you go - this place is cash only, but does have an ATM machine inside.

I'm super picky about the texture of my ramen noodles, and I am of the school of thought that ramen shouldn't be al dente (it's not Italian food!!).  For that, Hiro Ramen does their noodles a little on the softer side and I love that.

My partner and I got the Gates of Hell ramen and Black Pig ramen.  I loved the broth of his more than mine: I was sort of amping myself up for a really spicy ramen experience with the Gates of Hell and was let down a little. It didn't even really have a kick to it.  But the broth was tasty and overall it was a solid bowl.  The Black Pig was super yummy though again, and I definitely had a case of food envy. The garlic oil in it did it wonders.  The portions actually were nice - sometimes I'm in a ramen mood but don't want to be scarfing down a humongous bowl (it's really filling noodles and soup after all!).  They also cooked our bamboo shoots in it really well, which isn't always done so nicely in other ramen places.

We also got the takoyaki as an appetizer, and that was so good.  The octopus was a tad chewy, but the batter, flavors, and generous heaps of bonito flakes were delicious.

The setting is really cozy - we sat at the bar which I loved doing at a ramen joint like this, but also didn't feel too cramped which a lot of ramen bars tend to feel like sometimes (there was plenty of table space for me to toss my humongous bag onto).  Service was super quick and great. We were in and out really quickly which was what we needed as we were catching a train right afterwards.

Basically, it'll hit the spot but I'm not sure I completely fell in love.  I would come back (to try the other broths and maybe even return for the Black Pig) but I just don't know if it's completely stolen my heart.

Great cozy little spot for delicious ramen soup amongst other specialities. Very small with seating for about 20 people at tables and several more at the counter. They offer a few dish combinations specials for lunch that all include their awesome ramen soup. 
If you like it hot this is your place. They also have a few dishes that are toned down and does not sear the roof off your mouth and num the taste buds. 

Music was a little loud for a mid afternoon lunch. But It was doable. If you're a fan of Ramen or even Pho you will love this place. Apps and side are great also.

The best Checkers that I have eating the food was very tasty well-seasoned and clean but Checkers burgers compared to other fast-food chains or small. Here you have to choose between taste or overly sized burgers I guess depending on the mood I'll go for the overly sized  lol

We ordered a whole bunch of cheesesteaks from Campo's to be delivered to our hotel as part of the after party festivities from our wedding - and we couldn't have been happier.  The staff was very helpful and even wrapped the sandwiches as halves so more people could enjoy.  The traditional whiz wit steak was everything it was supposed to be, greasy, cheesy, onions with some bite left in them.  Definitely a fan and I recommend Campo's for anyone that wants the real Philly cheesesteak experience without the madness of Pat's and Geno's.
Great place for a hoagie and wait a beer, yes they have a full bar, and if you looking to get a cheap beer so come inside and have a 1.50 pabst pint, can't get better than that.
Love this place, one of my favorite places to go with with my lover for a chill Friday night. The food is to love, and the waitress that's Cambodian and mix with glass around early 20's is the best!
Went with my kids school class.  All other options were busy.  Cheesesteaks were good but adequate, also they are over priced.  Service was okay not great.

Came here after my first review 2-3 more times taking several different people along with me after raving about it, and jesus christ the ramen were so damn salty. WTH! Now I mention this to everyone when telling them about my weekly ramen rounds.

couple of reasons why I will never come back.

I came in around 3pm when nobody & sat at the ramen bar. 
It is pretty dusty, dirty and needs to be clean. You can see the dust on the walls and edges.
My utensils were dirty so I had to clean it with the napkin. 
Cup wasn't clean.

Now the main point was the ramen - I got the Black Pig Ramen. It looked good til I saw intestines swimming around my food. I had to pick out couple of them and man...I couldn't even eat since I kept staring. I even left it so the servers could see why I didn't finish it.
Server never ask if my food was okay or if I enjoy the food. food was salty, boring, and not worth the money.
Customer service is terrible. 
I remember she was always on her phone and doing nothing.

just stick with terakawa ramen and save your money from disgusting food.

The fried chicken that comes with the lunch special is on point!!! The sauce that comes with it is fantastically delicious. Definitely get this as your appetizer for the lunch special. I got the Gates of Hell ramen to go. Maybe it's not a fair review if it's a to go order, but the soup was cold by the time I got to my place 15 mins later. The poke was melt in your mouth delicious, but the broth was just okay. I spiced it up with sriracha. Apart from that, it's in a great location, with an unassuming facade, and decent availability for seating inside.

I had a quick meal here tonight with my family, who was in town and I wanted to give them a nice meal in Philly.  This was a perfect experience for us, and very affordable for 4 people.  The service was polite and fast.  They also catered to our dietary needs (my husband and I don't like pork meat, while my brother and sister do) and were very fast at bringing the food and the check.  Would highly recommend.

Love it! The service was excellent and the sandwich was fresh and tasty.  I thought Potbelly no longer existed in the Philadelphia area. I was pleasantly surprised to find this location and it is actually better than the others used to be! Very clean dining area and great staff! Long live Potbelly!

my friend recommended checkers for the seasoned fries and they sounded delicious so I decided to try it out. it was also a 5 minute walk from my place. (warning: the drive thru opens until late but when I went at about 10:15 pm to the actual place, it was closed and only drive thru was open). I ordered the seasoned fries, mozarella sticks, popcorn chicken and sprite. I also want to try their chicken wings because I heard they're good. The cashier was very nice when I went. The food is so cheap! the quality is eh but honestly you can't expect GREAT quality from the price. Whenever I crave quality fast food and I don't feel like going to mcdonalds, I love going to checkers! they have such a wide variety of menu items, food comes out quickly, and overall delicious cheap fast food.

This place was my favorite when I went to Uarts for my Master degree. To be honest, their noodles are ok, not special. I loved their fried chicken. I visited their again last Friday, I ordered my favorite combination -- Hiro Inch & Fried Chicken. However, I was a little disappointed when I bite the fried chicken. It was not as tender as before, and the flour was thicker than before also. Otherwise, noodle was still the same.

As a vegetarian/vegan I usually am forced to try the one vegetable ramen dish they offer and most of the time it isn't that great or anything special. 

It was the same case here. However my friend who got their special enjoyed it a lot. I would've put 3 stars but based on his comment I rounded to 4 because most people get the other styles.

The food is decent to above average.  But prices are a bit steep at over $10 for a cheese steak  Throw in a soda and you're spending over $13 for lunch.

The quality is good with decent taste and fresh ingredients..   They do have some Cheesesteak variations you wont see at other places.  Theres the "Flyers Ice" with cream cheese and tomatoes  and the "Barbeque Cheesesteak" with bacon and mozzarella to name a couple.

They have outdoor seating which is great on a nice day.  Cash only, and ATM at the front door.

Overall good spot minus the prices.  It seems to be more popular with tourists than locals.

As a ramen virgin this was an amazing place to start my journey! Affordable, clean restaurant and bathroom, friendly staff and delicious food! I didn't know what to expect! The ramen was so light, I felt full but not gorges after I was finished. The fried chicken app was as expected but the Black Pig Ramen (the burnt garlic is the perfect blend of broth and flavor) was great and I added an egg!  Is not spicy at all, as is. The cucumber drink was sweet and well liked. Will be back to try another type!!!
Drove here only to find out they are closed at 10:15pm smh. The door says 11pm and also on google

Hubby and I decided to buy a pretzel from this place while waiting for our plane to board because we were HUNGRY!  Anyways we each got a cinnamon/sugar pretzel.  Yummy!  and they were HUGE!  Price was pretty low I thought @ $2.95 each.  

Menu had plenty of items to choose from, from different flavored pretzels, mini bite pretzels and sauces to dip your pretzel in.  As another reviewer mentioned they list the calories next to each menu item.  Not so great when you choose the highest calorie pretzel:( but still nice to know.

I cannot recommend this establishment enough!  

Having previously eaten at Campos - and knowing how delicious the food is- we had decided to use them to cater an event at our school. The owner was wonderful to work with. 

Their place as one of the best cheesesteak shops in Philly is accurate!

The ramen was some of the best I've had,  
it was my first time having Tako Yaki and I LOVED it, and the fried chicken was top 5 all time for me.
Best Dairy Queen I've ever been to. Alyssa was very kind. Most beautiful sundae creation you ever did see!!!!

They are SUPER STINGY with the food, barely gave any rice, any beans, any chicken. and when you ask for extra? Tries to charge you for each one. QDOBA is usually better then chipotle. Not  at this location. The food gave me. Stomach ate. It was just a little bit of food. Pay too much and go to this establishment for the crappy service and quantity and quality of the food. Eat at the Mexican food truck or go to chipotle. This QDOBA sucks !

First time and Philly with family. Stopped in here for some cheesesteak. The counter service and patience were great. Food too!!  My daughter dropped her hot dog and was crying. They replaced it and gave her a bag of chips to hold her over. Very nice people!

First major complaint, this is a cash only establishment. The year is 2019, this is a touristy area, and I'm supposed to carry around a bunch of cash?   Second, waaaayyyy overpriced for a tiny, bland cheesesteak sandwich (very much lacking in meat and cheese). Third, can't get a cup of water after overpaying for a meh sandwich, have to pay $3.25 for a small bottle of water. Just a money grab all around, and boring food; I felt robbed. No, no, no, and no again.

This was an interesting experience for sure. It's a small place but definitely not small enough to just have one server. The poor girl was running around like a mad woman apologizing to every table and messing up a lot of orders. They were out of a few ingredients so having to ask if people want replacement ingredients made it a downhill battle for her. There were a couple mess up orders just sitting there (not under a heat lamp or anything) and she would offer people the mess ups to make up for everything taking a while/being wrong. So we got this cold greasy fried chicken thing that had been sitting there for a long time.

The broth of the ramen was great and the saving grace of the meal. I had gotten the porfilio and my boyfriend had the inch of heaven. The pork they add is so thin and just tasted like greasy grill char (not what you want in ramen). The fish cake they added was also very thin. They were skimping on ingredients a bit and on the way to the bathroom you get a view of this lovely slop bucket of emptied bowls right out in the hallway. Didn't feel quite safe eating here after seeing that, but needless to say, we were fine.  

It was nicely decorated and I'm sure on a less busy day it would be better, but I wouldn't go back.
Lovely decoration. Delicious food. The soup is a little salty but I love it! Recommend extra egg.

When I noticed this place was opening, I was very excited at the possibility of a new ramen place in my neighborhood. Unfortunately, after eating there, I'm a bit disappointed. Though the broth is very good, my bowl didn't have enough noodles and was very light on toppings. It was tasty, but I don't feel like it was good value. 

One more thing: cash only.

Today I went into the broad street location in north Philadelphia by temple campus. I wanted to try out the impossible meat burrito and was very excited to do so. I ordered and my friend ordered his food than we proceeded to check out. My friend got to the register and ordered a cup for a drink then mentioned our food was together. When I realized that he only had one cup I said "wait can we get another cup?" The cashier got upset. Then I said "I'm sorry we wanted this food to go." She then proceeded to snatch the food out of the bag and slam in on a tray all while saying, "I don't have time for ignorant ass niggers today!" At that point I'm at the drink fountain and my friend is still at the register. He says to her "how am I ignorant if all I asked for was the food to stay?" She proceeded to argue with him and I told him to just walk away. I then asked to speak to a manager and was denied the right. After that we still sat down and ate our food because I decided I would call corporate. Instead I stepped outside and called the restaurant and asked to speak to a manager. I was left on hold for about 5 minutes until someone picked up the phone. As I started to tell her they story as soon as I said she called us "IGNORANT ASS NIGGERS" they hung the phone up. Which then led me to email corporate. I'm saying all of this to say I have never in my life been called anything of the nature and or treated in such a manner. I will never be frequenting this establishment ever again and I hope that the lady with burgundy shirt on gets the karma she deserves. It's unprofessional and distasteful at the very least to treat people who are paying well over the amount they should be for basic bland food! I hope that this lesson out of this will be her being held accountable for her actions and in the future hiring more level headed people who aren't easily agitated with paying customers! Shame on you Qdoba! I hope this problem doesn't have to become larger than it already is!

CHEESESTEAKS
They probably beat most places on S. Street, and most in the 'burbs, but unfortunately for Campo's they are located a couple doors down from Sonny's, who has to be the best cheesesteak in Philly.

Compared to Sonny's, I'd have to give Campo's 2 or 3 stars, but compared to the greater philly area, they are more like 3.5 on cheesesteaks.  

ROAST PORK SANDIWCH
For roast pork, they are really freaking good!  Not as good as DiNic's (who is far and away the best in Philly), but still much better than most.  For roast pork, Campo's deserved 5 stars.

Overall they get 4 stars as the average of cheesesteak and roast pork.

I chose Campo's for a school trip that I helped organize for a group of fifty-some eighth graders who wanted to sample some cheesesteaks, hoagies, and pretzels on their first trip to Philly. The Campo's staff -- and particularly Denise Campo herself -- could not have been more kind, helpful, or accommodating, despite my numerous phone calls revising or amending my order. With relatively little advance notice, Denise and her crew orchestrated the perfect spread of iconic Philly foods for my students, who commandeered the entire restaurant and enjoyed every moment they spent there. The food was hot, fresh, and satisfying. I will return to Campo's whenever I'm back in Philly, and I enthusiastically recommend this establishment to anyone.

tourist trap!!!  my wife and i ate here thinking it was going to be at least an adequate deli ........wrong.  we arent tourists but tourist beware. i ate the heeter, 2-3 ounces of meat with literally almost  half of a bottle of buffalo  sauce , no cheese to speak of and knuckle size dices of onion. the chicken salad ...pre-made and dry chicken that will make you choke, not to mention the rude girl at the register, who was the owners daughter, high prices for low quality food, they should be ashamed.

Came here a few days ago and ordered a bowl of ramen. For the price it's not bad (I believe most bowls are $10), but it's not super flavorful like I expect authentic ramen to be which might have to do with how thin the broth was which was a little disappointing. Also, it was really lacking toppings that most ramen places add. Aside from that, the noodles were cooked perfectly and the egg was great. 

I was a little disappointed because I also didn't know they had a lunch special  for $3 more and my server didn't tell me. It wasn't written anywhere on the menu, but after checking yelp it seems like it's definitely an option. 

Overall it's a decent place if you're in a rush and want a quick bite. I would come back for sure and maybe try something else!

I didn't get to eat here, but I feel like they have earned a review.  I made careful plans to get to Campo's before they closed, so that I could pick up a sandwich before I want to a game night with friends.  

They decided to close 15 minutes early.  The person picking up the rug reacted like I was the bad guy for wondering why they weren't keeping their hours.  I'll never go to this place.  That's what happens, Campo's, when you aren't faithful to your hours.

There are plenty of other places in town to get a Philly cheesesteak, even for lactose and gluten intolerant people.

Having been to many of the popular cheesesteak restaurants (Pat's, Geno's, Dalessandro's, John's Roast Pork, Steve's, Philip's, Sonny's) in Philly already, my fiance and I were in search of the next best spot on our most recent trip to the city.
