Over and over again, I saw Campo's on top 10 lists, so it only made sense for us to visit the Old City neighborhood to check it out.

Although Campo's is a deli, it's apparently well-known for their cheesesteaks. We dropped by after a Phillies game on a Saturday evening at about 7:30pm and there were a fair amount of customers eating inside and outside, but there were a few tables still available. The restaurant was pretty small, but we were able to get a seat without any waiting. When we walked in, the decor reminded me more of a bar than an actual sandwich shop. 

The menu was actually pretty big and had lots of items on it, but we went straight to the cheesesteaks. There were a few options, but we went with The Works, which was a cheesesteak with sweet bell peppers, mushrooms, grilled onions, provolone. We were bigger fans of cheesesteaks with whiz than provolone so we had the provolone swapped out for the whiz.

The verdict? The cheesesteak was pretty small, maybe the smallest we had seen yet, so if you're starving this might not be the place for you. There was an OK amount of steak, plenty of whiz on it, but a sparse amount of peppers, mushrooms and onions. The meat had very good flavor on it, mainly because it was saltier. Also, the bread was cold and not warmed up, which put a damper on eating it. The bottom line: Something was just lacking - whether it was because the meat needed to be juicier or the cheesesteak needed to be bigger, that IT factor was missing. Would we come here again? Probably not because of the number of cheesesteak options in Philly. Plus, parking can be difficult to find in the area, since it is located in a very busy neighborhood, and can be expensive at $2.50 per hour via the meters.

This store has excellent food, unfortunately customer service was terrible. My daughter, who is a minor, went to this store with two of her friends in the airport on her way back home. She has told me that the cashier was being extremely rude when her two friends told them that the order was wrong. This made me furious as all three of them were minors. I understand that there may be many people they have to serve, but customer service to everybody should be respectful.

First time I've had a cheese stake in Philly and I've lived here 2 years! I've got a dairy allergy and this is the first cheese stake place to also have vegan cheese available. 4 stars because they made our meal between others and my food was not hot by the time everyone else in my party got theirs. The staff was pretty kind and easy going! Meat flavoring was alright. If you're looking for allergy friendly cheese stakes, this is your spot! 

Gluten free
Vegan
Vegetarian
Meat lovers, whatever you want, they have it!

Horrible service when there's absolutely nobody in the store, can't put ranch on the sandwich doesn't make sense.  Also can't sell just rolls. Overall a horrible experience. I would give this no stars if I could, yikes! Go to a different jimmy john's if you can :)

*Cash only!* I'm not a native to Philly and I'm a vegetarian, so Philly cheesesteaks are not something I'm well versed in. I was visiting the city for a day and a friend recommended the place. I absolutely loved. I got the Vegan Works and the homemade potato salad. The Works was great, and the potato salad was some of the best I've ever had. Also enjoyed the family-owned atmosphere. It's a small spot, but wasn't very busy when I visited, so I was able to get a table.

Phenomenal food, I've had many different kinds of their ramen and all are amazing. Quick and friendly service, small area but never too crowded. Everything is authentic, cooked perfectly, and begging for another visit. A must for anyone who is a ramen fanatic!!

It was a good bowl of ramen with high quality broth and toppings, but the portion was small for the price. I left hungry. There are other ramen shops nearby that are much better value that I would recommend over Hiro Ramen, especially if you're hungry.

CASH ONLY. No warning, thanks to the friendly patron behind us for providing the 5 dollars we were short. The Works, the Grilled Cheese and the Pizza Steak were great. The Vegan Works was not any where as good as the others.

I ordered my meal off of Grubhub and this is probably some of the worst food I've had in the city. I ordered the heater cheesesteak, the chicken parm sandwich, the mac & cheese app, and the broccoli cheddar soup. For a nearly $10 cheesesteak, this is about 2/3 the size of any other cheesesteak that you would get in the city. All of the other food was extremely bland or basically inedible. Part of the chicken parm sandwich and the entire cup of soup ended up in the garbage because they were that bad. The best part of this meal was the bag of Herr's sour cream and onion chips, and that's a problem. 

One positive was that the delivery of our meal was prompt, but prompt delivery doesn't really matter when the food is terrible. When Grubhub reached out to the restaurant on my behalf regarding the poor food, they didn't do anything to try and rectify. Do yourself a favor and avoid this place.

This place was recommended to me and described as "better than Terakawa" and I agree and disagree.
The place is kind of hard to find. It won't have blaring signs calling out the restaurant, but a sign that said "Best of Philly Ramen" was good enough for me to identify it. Walking in, I felt like I was in an actual ramen bar. You could smell the different broths in the air.
We came in for the lunch special, which lasts from 11-3. The lunch special includes a small salad, small app (chicken or edamame), and a ramen. 
The salad was your traditional salad with orange ginger sauce, and it was dressed nicely with crunchy noodles on top.
The chicken was perfectly cooked, but what made it was the sauce. It tasted like spicy mayo with soy sauce and lemon. The fried chicken was balanced with the slightly acidic sauce.
For ramen, I ordered the Hero's Inch of Heaven. The broth tasted natural if that even makes sense. It felt pure as if the broth was not tampered with multiple spices. The torched charshu pork made it a better experience. The noodles were finely cooked. Everything about it felt homey. 
The waitress just served us our food quickly, nothing special. This place is tax free but CASH ONLY. 
Overall, I'm going back next week haha.

The Stockyard!  It is like they took 3 or 4 great sandwiches and smashed them into one phenomenal sandwich.  Bacon, pepperoni, chicken, steak, fried onions and mascarpone cheese make up a heart hardening work of art.  The place is a little small and it is hard to figure out how to get in line sometimes but the staff are pros and, even if they are busy, the wait is not long.  Also, I have found that if you call ahead, that can all be avoided.
The price is affordable, ramen is simple and tasty. This place is always on my list for a quick meal if nearby while still have something good

First time ordering from this Jimmy John's and we did delivery. There was the tracker for our order online, and it took them a very long time to process our order which seems silly since it's a cold sandwich place. I called after waiting 15 minutes, they picked up and said they would check on my order, and then hung up. I tried calling back multiple times with no answer. Finally, the tracker said it was out for delivery. I waited for it to deliver to my place which is roughly 8 minutes away for about 20 minutes. I tried calling them multiple times again and finally got an answer after the fifth or so time. She said she would call the delivery guy and call me back and right after we hung up, the food was finally there. Fortunately, our sandwiches were good but the delivery experience put a sour taste in our mouths.

I have been adventuring around different ramen places over the city for the last few months, and Hiro has been the only one thus far that prompted me to write a yelp review. 

I ordered the vegetable ramen with marinated egg and nori (seaweed), and my ramen came out teeming with vegetables, two extra pieces of nori, and lots of flavor. The bowl was huge- while it cost $11, it also will be feeding me for two days, so I think the price was absolutely reasonable. Their green tea was actually made properly out of green tea powder whisked into a froth, an experience I had missed since visiting Japan and one which surprised me at Hiro. The whole food experience- in one word- was fantastic! 

The ambiance was also quite nice- it has a quaint, hole in the wall atmosphere (possibly due to the small building size,) but also feels nostalgic for Japan- it has just the right decorations, paneling, and layout to give one a hint of east-Asia. The staff I interacted with (the chef and the waiter,) were incredibly nice, enthusiastic, and personable. 

Also- to contradict someone else- they do take card :)

This may have to become one of my regular spots!

I went to there 9:15pm today,
server kicked out me. 
I asked server what time close, he couldn't answer exact time.

I understand I went there too late, my bad. But they still had "Open" sign. He changed "Close" sign after kicked out me.

Thank you for good experience in Philadelphia.
I'm going to Terakawa Ramen.

I never come back to Hiro ramen when I visit Philadelphia.

You should call them after 9pm before go to there.

Good luck, Hiro ramen!

I ordered a tuna hoagie from this place and I was disappointed.  It was a tuna sandwich on hoagie bread- not a hoagie.  

If you're looking for a real hoagie try the deli counter at the Olde City Market on the same block.  They make a much better hoagie.

We were recently in Philly and were on a mission to try out different Philly Cheese Steak Sandwiches. We found Campo's because it was in one of the Food Network show. We loved it. The sandwiches were juicy and flavorful. Although the restaurant was small, they served everyone in a fast manner. They provide a great selection of sandwiches and hoagies. There are also several types of deli appetizer items for you to enjoy. Service and prices were great. We highly recommend it!

Classic place for Philly Cheesesteaks.  Good location on Market Street. Engaging staff - can talk to the guys cooking up the food.  Got the provolone cheese option.  Surprised by No Credit Cards policy.  Cash only.  Potato salad had too much oregano.
Had the hiro soy ramen which was delicious! Small place but better than most of the other ramen places !!! ( ramen addict) I eat ramen at least once a week outside!!

Rainy cold evening...nothing but a good hot Ramen noodle accommodate such evening perfectly. This shop has been on my radar for a while. Finally got a chance to visit. Store was about 2/3 full when visited...lively somewhat but a little dimmed light made inside less lively somewhat for Ramen shop. Sat on the counter...and ordered Pork & Miso and Yaki Gyoza. 
Pork & Miso is basically Tonkotsu Miso soup. Good flavor on soup, but wished a little stronger Tonkotsu as Miso flavor took over. If this is just Miso, it would have been OK. Good texture on Menma (banboo), but Chashu was little tough. I prefer a little more cooked for softer texture on Ramen. Corn and Negi toppings were as expected. Noodle was nicely cooked, medium-thin and curvy with good texture. One wish on Ramen was more selections for veggie toppings, like Sprouts or Cabbage. But overall, this was a good bowl of Ramen. 
Yaki Gyoza was smaller than expected; but it was not prepacked frozen pieces. Skin had good texture and inside filling was meaty and juicy. One point I wonder was some section was "cool" than hot/warm despite just served. I expected hot/warm wherever I bite in...
I understand ordered items and serving process. But I wish they could serve Ramen bowl and Gyoza plate at the same moment than time difference. 
...just another small wish.
Overall, they serve nice Ramen bowl and Gyoza!
I will go back for sure.
Best all around ramen in Philly. And the fried chicken app is a ridic value. People can debate whatever they like, but I've decided this is def my go-to when I need a fix.

This is a very good ramen restaurant located in center city Philly. It's a bit of a hike from Chinatown which has a handful of other similar restaurants but it is worth it. We went with a group of 5 and everyone got different types of ramen with their own type of broths. The broths make the dish and Hiro nailed them. The noodles were the only thing I didn't like. Dont get me wrong, they were very good but I would have rathered something like udon noodles.

I gave this place so much of my business and now I regret it. Now let me be clear: I only ordered out of sheer convenience because it is one of the few places in the area that deliver. Anyway, it seems that every time I order (for delivery) from Uncle Tomy's for about the past year or so, at least something is wrong. For example, one night a few months back, the driver had to go back and forth THREE separate times because they kept getting it wrong over and over. I have been convinced it had to be either the people who take orders over the phone are careless or the people making the food are careless - I wasn't completely sure - but after today, one thing is for certain: it stems from the owner.  

Most recently (TODAY), I ordered a tuna hoagie with American cheese and mayo (I asked for the mayo to be mixed with the tuna and also for it to be on the bread).  When the order arrived (and after tipping the driver PLUS paying a delivery fee for them to drive one block), there was no mayo and no cheese.  So I got in my car and drove the incorrectly made sandwich back to them and requested it to be made correctly.

Are you ready for what the owner did to rectify the situation?

Handed me a side of mayo and a few slices of cheese and told me to put it on the sandwich myself - and refused to remake it!! Let me remind you that this was THE OWNER who did this!  Now it makes sense why the place stinks.

Call me crazy, but if you make a sandwich incorrectly, it is YOUR responsibility to remake it, and to remake it correctly.  It is TOTALLY INAPPROPRIATE to hand the customer the missing ingredients and tell the customer to do it themselves.

After putting up with their carelessness and rude, obnoxious, total disregard for customer service, this most recent event was the straw that broke the camel's back. They'll never get another dime from me. I'd rather drive 5 miles for quality food and customer service than deal with that nonsense again.

Oh how I cannot wait to move out of this neighborhood next year!

Not bad, not great. The meat was just way under seasoned and a bit on the fatty side. I would've enjoyed the onions if they were thinner and not served in chunks. Service was good and food came out quickly. I would definitely try another spot before venturing back to Campo's.

I went in not expecting anything in particular. That should tell you that I was not biased by any other reviews, friends' comments of dislike or like. 

Pros: 
-although a tiny place, they do take reservations so you can go with a large group. 
-the service there was wonderful, we had a waiter who was attentive and nice.
-the food pricing was appropriate. The most expensive ramen was about $11
-my favorite part of the meal was the appetizer: Fried Chicken. It had a nice unique seasoning to it, accompanied with a white sauce. What I loved about it was that the pieces of the fried chicken were of dark meat! So it was juicy with the right amount of batter and fat. It was just delicious. 

Cons: 
-I had the Chicken Soy Ramen Noodle Soup...I couldn't finish the food at all because it was completely salty and borderline bitter. It was just so salty that even the noodles were inedible. So basically my bowl sat there as I ate more appetizers. Disappointed. 
-Cash Only

This is THE absolute best place for sandwiches. Amazing vegan and regular cheesesteaks served on fresh sesame rolls that they get delivered to them daily. The sides are all homemade. The place is a family run establishment and has been passed down generations. The staff are super friendly and go out of their way to provide Philly with the best food! You can't beat it. Even my husband (who is super picky about his cheesesteaks) dreams about this place! Thanks Campos!

My friend from Tokyo recommended this place to the M&M doc and I was skeptical at first. 

Recently came back from a trip to Japan. Got to try all types of amazing ramen and I confidently say this is the best one in town compared to others (don't want to call any of them out.) This is as authentic as it gets especially as you walk right in...

Environment: Dimly lit, felt exactly as if I was going into ramen bar in Japan. Great atmosphere.

Service: Nothing to complain about. They did an EXCELLENT job in serving us.

Food: As authentic as ramen gets in Philadelphia. Maybe not as good as the ones in New York or even California. Being one who went to Japan, they did a great job reproducing what is overseas.. My favorite of all time is the Portfolio. It's like a deluxe ramen and if you want extra flavor I highly recommend getting extra chasu.

Price: For $10, this was a no-brainer in the city. The ramen is comparable to other places in the city for significantly better quality. M&M out..
Best sandwich ever! Very healthy and yet flavorful. The staff is very friendly and efficient.

Their pig and miso with a marinated egg is awesome. Their ramen is very close to what I used to eat in Japan. They are not as crowded as Terakawa ramen and the service is very quick. But don't underestimate, their ramen is very very delicious.

Best cheese steaks in Old City.

It is cash only, but they have an ATM on site with only a $1.50 charge.

If you like spicy, the Flyer's Ice Steak is the way to go. The cream cheese in it adds this amazing creaminess and coolness to balance out the heat... delicious.

All their sides are made by the owner's mom. They're delicious, homemade comfort food sides that go really well with a nice hot cheesy sandwich.

I've seen some of the girls who work the register be rude to tourists (usually the tourist starts it, and Philly girls aren't afraid to say something back!), but they're always pleasant to me. 

This is always where I tell people visiting to go, like I said, best cheese steaks in Old City!

The people here are decent people for a McDonalds. McDonalds used to say "We love to see you smile". Well I think the girl who took my order kinda half smiled when I approached the counter to order my pancakes and black coffee. You can't go wrong with Mickey Ds black coffee. Not much makes me happy anymore but I can always depend on the blackness of that coffee. The pancakes are another story. SOLID. That's how I describe the pancakes. I eat them with butter and syrup like an American should eat a pancake and I sip my black coffee and I watch the world go by. I'm lovin it.
Often imatated never duplicated the finest sandwiches and steaks on the planet.Every thing made with love like they were going to eat it themselves.

If you're looking for a place with great food friendly customer service and a pleasant atmosphere this is the place to be I enjoy all their burgers they are absolutely delicious and me and my family often go here to eat I recommend these guys to everyone that I talk to if you looking for a good time grateful friendly atmosphere excellent customer service this is the place to be

I don't understand the hype about Philly cheesesteaks. I have been to a few different ones and it seems to be the same thing. Don't get me wrong, they are tasty but to say one is better than the other.
Campos is the best cheesesteak in the city!!! Quality meat, not dry at all. Great cheese and onions. Gluten free options are excellent.

Cheesesteaks were very good! Fresh rolls, meat was juicy, cheese melty just the way it should be. We tried the cheese wiz version and the American cheese. We didn't care for the cheese wiz, but that is likely personal preference. No fries here though, and cash only. I thought it seemed as if the owner was trying to make food in a more fresh and healthy way. She had homemade pasta salad, macaroni salad, macaroni and cheese and the best iced brownie I've had in a long time! I would return!
Hands down, 5 stars. This was our first stop in Philly! Delicious food and great service. Try the pasta salad!

Cheese Steak ($8.49)
Fried onions, cheese whiz 

Campo's is admittedly the best iteration of the cheese steak that I have tried in Philly thus far. The steak was slightly chewy, but plentiful and juicy. The 'fried' (read: grilled) onions were fresh and soaked up the juice from the meat. And that perfectly pliant sesame roll from Liscio's ... heaven.

But something was missing here ...

Ahhhhh yes! The cheese. My issue with Philly cheese steaks has been the consistency of the cheese. I'm used to Provolone being interspersed through every nook and cranny. The caramelized onions intermingling throughout the luscious thin-sliced rib-eye. Unfortunately, I had to scoff at the additional charge for provolone - and opted for the Cheese Whiz.   

Honestly? Perhaps this is the only way to go (in Philly at least)! The salty 'cheese' was perfectly primed to distribute throughout this cheese steak. It got into every crevice and added that certain je ne sais quois that was missing. It's sad to think that this can't be achieved with provolone here in Philly, but for now - the whiz will do donkey, it'll do. 

Campo's Special Italian Hoagie ($8.99)
Dilusso salami, ham capicola, peppered ham, pepperoni, prosciutto, and provolone. Fresh lettuce, tomatoes, onions, salt, pepper, and oregano. 

But you didn't honestly think I was done there did you? I had to go for their special hoagie - the Italian. A perfect melange of peppery deli meats - you've got salami, ham capicola, pepperoni, prosciutto, and peppered ham - melded with nicely sharp provolone. The lettuce and tomatoes brought a bit of freshness to eat bite and the raw onions (which I normally hate) seemed tempered and had enough restraint to admittedly make the hoagie. And as with any good sandwich, S & P heightened all of these flavors. 

Chicken Cutlet Hoagie ($9.79)
All-white chicken fillets, provolone, grilled tomatoes, lettuce, and onion. 

The GF went with the chicken cutlet hoagie - and I'm glad she did! This was heavier than expected, but the melted provolone was perfectly melded with the juicy chicken! The grilled tomatoes brought out a depth to the fruit that worked perfectly with this hot sandwich. This one's coma-inducing, so don't say I didn't warn you!

Homemade Macaroni & Cheese ($5.29)

 Anyone who knows me knows that I can't resist homemade Mac n Cheese. But at almost $6 including tax/tip? I don't think I'll be ordering this from Campo's again. What you're looking at is a thimble sized container, albeit filled with perfectly al dente long macaroni pasta. Perfectly creamy, but perfectly overpriced as well. I have no problem paying certain price points - but the quantity of cash should equate to some semblance of the quantity of the food, especially when we're not talking about foie, kobe, or brillat savarin.

Potato Salad ($3.49) 

Reminiscent of a German potato salad, this was a side I could definitely get behind in terms of price point and quality. The red potatoes retained their structure, but were also perfectly creamy. The carrots and onions mixed well with the vinegar and mayo - I would definitely get this again!

Overall, Campo's Deli gets the job done. If you've got a hankering for a good hoagie or heck, one of the better cheese steaks I've had in Philly, be sure to head to Old City. But if it's chilly or you're feeling lazy, check out DingingIn and get it delivered!
I love this place especially on cold days you get a really authentic Japanese feel con is very limited seating all I can say is Go for it !

Busy place but always get what you want
Just wait little then they called your number to pick up food great spot they owner always upgrade their place every time I went there the place always change which we like it.  Good Big Mac and fries

So this was our first stop and our 1st Authentic Philly Cheese Steak Sandwich. 
I have to say it was very very good!!!
We got 1 with onions and Whiz and the other with just Whiz.
Both were amazing.  The Whiz just melts into the Ribeye Steak and bread.  We had to lick it off our fingers!!!
We also tried a Philadelphia breed Ale.  We didn't care for it.
The sides of Mac n cheese and Potato salad were good but really not necessary. 
This is definitely high on our list.
Our trip to Philly is off to a great start!!

I've been coming to Jimmy Johns since I was a freshman at Temple. I'm from
The Philadelphia area, so I know a real hoagie. These are FAR from real hoagies, but decent. I have to take off stars because I know employees who have worked at this place, and say management is absolutely terrible and rude. I also know that the CEO of Jimmy Johns is a huge game hunter and trump supporter, so it's hard to support a company that isn't ethical. I usually get the veggie sandwich, which is pretty good. It has provolone cheese, avocado spread, mayo, lettuce, tomato, and cucumber. The tomatoes were disgusting, and I could see behind the counter they were prepackaged. It's not super fresh, and the prices aren't too great. Wouldn't necessarily recommended this place, but I don't hate it either.

Holy cow the ramen here is damn effing good.

I've had some great ramen back when I lived in LA in Little Tokyo but this place has the tastes and flavors that has half of those places in Little Tokyo running for the exit. The spicy pork soup base was just perfect and not too greasy (still oily). And I don't even usually eat pork. The noodles were just amazing and though I would say the noodles and meat in the soup is enough, but if you want a lot of a good thing, I'd suggest ordering your ramen with extra noodles and meat. It's so worth unbuttoning your pants for and letting your tummy out in all it's ramen-filled glory. Sexy isn't it?

The service was excellent and though this place get super busy, they were on top of our orders and the waitress came by often enough to see how we're doing and asking if we needed refills on water and such. The restaurant itself has a great authentic old-school Japanese vibe to it. I felt like I was back in Japan at a hole-in-the-wall mom and pop shops that served up amazing food. There're only a few tables and the tables hold about 4 max so don't plan on going with a huge group or expect to be seated right away, especially if you're going during peak meal times.

I can't stop raving about this place.

This definitely is one of those rare gems in the Center City area.

Oh yeah, heads up: CASH ONLY. I'd suggest taking about $20/person just for parking+tip if you valeted at the structure nearby + food or if you took SEPTA and have little extra for dessert in the area.

Price: $10+
Wait: 10-15 mins after being seated
Parking: $10 parking or $5/30mins

Been to this restaurant for many times and their ramen are really great, I like the one with the black garlic oil. The tokoyaki and Kara-age are great for appetizer too. One tip for you guys, they take cash only, so be sure to bring cash before go in:) but, price is quite reasonable, 8 bucks for a ramen.

Rainy cold evening...nothing but a good hot Ramen noodle accommodate such evening perfectly. This shop has been on my radar for a while. Finally got a chance to visit. Store was about 2/3 full when visited...lively somewhat but a little dimmed light made inside less lively somewhat for Ramen shop. Sat on the counter...and ordered Pork & Miso and Yaki Gyoza. 
Pork & Miso is basically Tonkotsu Miso soup. Good flavor on soup, but wished a little stronger Tonkotsu as Miso flavor took over. If this is just Miso, it would have been OK. Good texture on Menma (banboo), but Chashu was little tough. I prefer a little more cooked for softer texture on Ramen. Corn and Negi toppings were as expected. Noodle was nicely cooked, medium-thin and curvy with good texture. One wish on Ramen was more selections for veggie toppings, like Sprouts or Cabbage. But overall, this was a good bowl of Ramen. 
Yaki Gyoza was smaller than expected; but it was not prepacked frozen pieces. Skin had good texture and inside filling was meaty and juicy. One point I wonder was some section was "cool" than hot/warm despite just served. I expected hot/warm wherever I bite in...
I understand ordered items and serving process. But I wish they could serve Ramen bowl and Gyoza plate at the same moment than time difference. 
...just another small wish.
Overall, they serve nice Ramen bowl and Gyoza!
I will go back fo

Very cool little place to stop by for a beer and cheese steak while you are site seeing! Johnny was very nice and knew the menu well. I had the chicken valentine and it was great with the potato and macaroni salad! Very clean and nice to visit

This was my first time at Campo's.  I've always heard of them but have never tried them.  I was at a friends place watching the 2010 worldcup.  Lucky for us, Campo's is just at the corner, a long 30 sec walk!  It was in the early afternoon on a Saturday and not a lot of people there.  The lady at the register was really nice and fast.  My whiz cheesesteak with onions came out really fast and was VERY DELICIOUS!  I love how the bread is very soft and just as good as pat's and jim's if not better.  I'll have to visit here again to see how good the cheesesteak is the second time so I can rate their consistency.  So, until then, a 4-star will be good.  There's a tv there for watching sports as well as some indoor and outdoor seating.  I wish I lived closer to this place, I would definitely come here more often.  They have a cheesesteak sandwhich called the "heater" which is a spicy version.  I will probably try that next time....

I visited Hiro Ramen House and had the Vegetable Ramen dinner, which turns out is vegan. It was awesome. Very tasty and really good price. My son had the Portfilio which is Ramen in chicken and pork broth, an egg, pork belly, and some vegetables. It was a bit spicier and, also, really good. The place itself is a small dining room but not too small. The server was extremely nice. The only reason for the 4 star review is the cash-only policy. I will return for more tasty ramen.

So I'll preface by saying this place is cash only. They do have an ATM in store if you've brought your debit card. It's a nice cozy environment that has a Japanese theme with various knick knacks for decorations scattered throughout the place. I got the Black Pig, which is berkshire pork tonkotsu broth, roasted garlic oil, pork belly, bean sprout, bamboo, scallion, and naruto. I added an egg just because I love egg. So I'll say the oil mixed in with the broth is just wow. There's the savoriness and creaminess of the broth is cut through perfectly with the oil. The oil gives it a freshness difficult to put into words. The pork belly was tender and flavorful, but I do wish there was more of it. Noodles weren't overbearing. I drank the broth to the last drop. Probably going to to my go to if I ever remember to carry cash given how close the place is to me.

I went to Campo's 20 minutes before closing last night. We got there at 8:40 and they close at 9. They closed early and wouldn't even come to the door. I went to Paesano's instead and had a wonderful gluten free cheesesteak!

I'm surprised I haven't tried or heard of this place until recently but this is now one of my go to spots for ramen other than my current philly favorite Terwakawa Ramen in Chinatown.  What makes their ramen stand out is the clean tasting broth and fresh ingredients.  Their lunch special comes with an appetizer and salad - I highly recommend the karaage fried chicken!! (the best I have actually tasted in philly so far after being here for years) - super crispy and juicy.  Only downside is restaurant is cash only, enjoy!

The chicken sandwich is BACK!!! I'm not sure if many people remember that there's a Popeye's here because they're never as packed as the other locations. The parking lot is weird to maneuver.  They share a parking lot with a furniture company and a save-a-lot. The meat market is next door so expect their customers to steal parking. It's extremely tiny inside with maybe 3 tables but...you won't wait 45 minutes to an hour for a chicken sandwich. There's very little standing room so it fills up fast. Usually the pregnant young lady is rude but today the ladies on the frontline had their act together as she must be on maternity leave because the exchange was pleasant. I had all 3 of my chicken sandwiches in less than 10 minutes. It was pretty packed by the time I left but they handle the rush well.
Bad service for drive thru!! I have no idea how the manage their employees, but they really need to learn how to serve their customers with an appropriate manner!

Great Ramen spot! Cash only, and really small, but we had no issues grabbing a table later on a Friday night. Definitely get the chicken to start! I ordered the pig and miso and thoroughly enjoyed the flavorful dish. Heads up they close at 9:30 every night, which is a little early on weekends.

I recently decided to visit Campo's because I heard that their cheesesteaks were some of the best in the city (they also are the only venue in the stadiums) and they happen to be around the corner from where I work. This place is a quintessential Italian sandwich shop, right down to the exposed brick walls, and it is family-owned to boot!

Obviously, I grabbed a steak the first time I visited. The meat came chopped and just a little greasy/juicy. The provolone was adequately melted throughout and the rolls were pretty normal. The cheesesteak didn't blow my mind, but as I mentioned previously, Campo's does other sandwiches besides cheesesteaks, and they're all good (especially one of the chicken ones--the Godfather?). Definitely order some sort of a hoagie when you come here.

The cheesesteak, surprisingly, did come with a choice of side. My coworker got the macaroni salad and I got the potato salad, both of which were made by the cashier's mother. If you're looking for a classic taste for your picnic basket, you must order from Campo's. Both the macaroni and the potato salad packed a big punch in the flavor department and tasted exactly the way you'd hope and expect.
Wow! My first philly cheesesteak. Really nice customer service. Lots of options on the cheesesteaks. They have no fries but the buns are filling! Nice patio spot that can overlook the sunset.

I just stopped by Campo's Philly Cheesesteaks to grab a steak on the way home; the hunger was strong.

The service at Campo's was amazingly fast and friendly. The sandwich was top notch, well stocked with steak and ingredients requested, and delicious!

I'd visit Campo's again any day of the week for its prompt preparation, supreme sandwiches and solid service!

Been here several times before and always love their "gates of hell". Not huge portion but it's reasonable with good flavors. $10 per bowl and so about 12-13 with tips & taxes. It is cash only though but they do have an ATM on site. Also it's BYOB. Overall, if you are in the city and looking for a nice quick ramen bite, I would definitely recommend this place.

I recently visited this chipotle for the 2nd time and I was surprised by the friendliness of the staff and the amount of food they give you. It might've been just the person but I come here because I'm vegan, and I love how they give you free guac, which is a steal! I'll definitely come again if it's the same experience!

Young miss campo took our order today and she was an absolute pleasure, the brothers are doing their best. Excellent food and great seating outside with a pleasant vibe "when the brothers are behaving" that takes me back too when life was simple and food was good and brothers were in the back cleaning.
The brothers are also great;) cheers

Cheesesteak was amazing!!! Probably the beet so far in Philly, but Unfortunately had to give 4 Stars due to the fact I excepted a Hoagie roll and it was served to me on a bun. 3 doors down is Sunny's and they did have a GF Hoagie but the steak tasted like it was cooked in the microwave.

Don't come here if you are really looking for an OG Philly cheese steak. There was no meat, they were rude, they messed up all our orders and pricey for what we received. It was a good bottle of Sam Adam's though.

There are gluten free rolls and vegan cheese options for those who need dairy free. While that is awesome, the flavor is just not there. No seasoning or flavor to meat. Meat was tough and not tender. Cook was also rude to us whenever he gave us a normal bread instead of GF. Wasn't our fault yet we got the attitude.

Decided to try this place due to the high ratings. Quite a letdown. I ordered the signature ramen, Hiro's Inch Of Heaven. It was definitely only an inch of anything good... The ramen lacks flavor. The nori was stuck to the side of the bowl soaked in broth. The pork over cooked. Relative to other ramen houses I've been to, this place does not stand out. It's also small, so not something I would recommend anyone wait for. And something good to know beforehand is they ONLY TAKE CASH. If you have cards, you'll have to use their ATM or run over to one of the nearby banks, 7-Eleven, etc. which I'd say at that point is definitely not worth the trouble.
Service is great. Very efficient, prompt, and courteous.  Good prices. Best part, is that they have places to sit inside if it's too hot to walk outside while eating.
Not bad.   I came to experience a really Philly cheesesteak.  It was good but. It the best I've had.

My cousin had his 50th birthday celebration here this weekend.  He's a regular at this place and I can see why!  Staff is super friendly and very attentive! They were awesome with the kids at the party, gave them ramune and Pocky!

The food was soo good!! We had the Karaage Fried Chicken, Edamame and yaki-gyoza for apps.  The kids got French Fries.  It all tasted so good!!  We also got a small salad. 

I got the Black Pig Ramen - wow! So flavorful!! I don't know if it was the garlic oil or what, but that was some good soup!! The chashu was perfect!! Not too fatty, just enough! My 5 year old nephew loved the chashu! 

I've already told a few friends in Philly about this place and I plan on going back soon!

This is one of my go-to Qdoba locations. It's located right at broad and Cecil B Moore. I've been coming here for a while and decided to do a review. I can honestly say that service  here is always fast and friendly...today they had a line out the door of about 12-15 people before they opened and they knocked out the crowd in swift and professional manner. 

What I personally like at this location is that they take time making my quesadilla whereas some qdoba just throw the cheese on it, here they smooth out the cheese and the sauce evenly for me without me asking. The taste of my quesadilla is consistently hot and fresh, as if they literally just diced the tomatoes for the pick right before I walked in. The only thing I dislike is that sometimes they get cheese from the backside second portion near the grill and I can't see that cheese I would prefer they be consistent and get my cheese only from the cheese that's on display...I also don't like the parking here..but it's located on temple campus so the lack of parking is expected other than that..I love this place. 

-Lace©says don't yell about it, Yelp about it :-)
I've never had my sandwich take more than 3 minutes to make. Fast and nice employees. Open early and closes late.

I order their wings all the time because they are simply the best wings in the whole city of Philadelphia. They are seasoned and crispy with the sauce served on the side because WHO WANTS SOGGY BUFFALO WINGS? No one. It's gross and Uncle Tomy's is the only establishment that gets it right. I'm addicted to them and order them at least once a week. Their chicken salad and cutlet sandwiches are delicious too. Fast delivery and completely reasonable prices. Uncle Tomy's is the jam!
Sandwich was good.  Nothing outstanding. This place is Cash Only!!!!  There is no prominent sign anywhere and luckily I had cash on me.

Campos is so good! On my first visit to Philadelphia I walked over a mile to try their cheesesteak on a gluten-free bun. It was delicious and the staff welcomed me like family. Brianna especially was wonderful, making sure they accommodated any food sensitivities. I didn't leave without trying their gluten-free brownie. YUM! It was totally worth the walk.

This place doesn't get a lot of hype, but it's delicious! We listened to our Philly family arguing about the best cheesesteak in town for 4 days. This is the spot we decided to try and we weren't disappointed! Family run, great menu, lots of options, and very tasty sandwiches. 

We got The Works and The Heater, wit whiz and without onions. Unfortunately the sandwiches arrived with onions anyway (not a major issue for us, but that's why the 5th star is missing). 

The father running the grill and talking to his customers is super friendly, and his daughter at the register proudly bragged about her family's role in each of the dishes. None of the rude badgering you get from other spots when you're a newbie learning the order lingo, which was a relief! Would recommend adding this to your tour of steaks, we were happy with our choice!

First Philly cheesesteak while visiting Philly. I really enjoyed this place. The only negative is cash only. But I got a traditional cheesesteak with just onions and provolone and it was delicious. The pasta salad was really good also!
best cheesesteak i've ever had. really good other hoagies too. really great service, good environment, good food. a must visit place. thank you campo's, my dreams are complete. i shall return.

Finally an excellent alternative to Terakawa, which is amazing but often crowded. A straightforward menu and friendly service make this an A+ spot for ramen. Love the interior design as well. Great broth and ingredients set it apart from other ramen shops around the way. Go now.

It's a Chipotle. Do I really need to say more?

Okay I will. Convenience is being right on Drexel's campus within walking distance, food is fine as you'd expect, no qualms about quality or service. Would recommend because it's a Chipotle.

This is such a great place, quick and great service. It's so easy to overlook this little gem but one was you go in there IS no way you're not coming back! 
Very affordable (not much above $10) and  they're appetizer and ramen selection is goals. If you're around this place go, you probably won't retreat it! 

Ps, Cash only!

Locating in center city of Philadelphia. Hiro Ramen is one of my favorite ramen spot. The portion and flavor are just right, not salty or bland. The appetizers are amazing! The atmosphere is welcoming. I think the owner make her noodles and that is something I enjoy seeing in noodle shop!
Good food at very reasonable prices.  Friendly services. Informal dining room. Highly recommended. BYOB

Pretty sure this is the only restaurant I've ever been to that refused to give me a cup of water with my meal.  Call me cheap, but I try to avoid overpaying for soda or bottled water in restaurants whenever possible.  I was told "we only sell bottles", even though water was clearly available from the fountain soda machine 2 feet away.  The sandwich tasted good, although it was overpriced at $11.35 for a sandwich only.  I understand they would rather make a few dollars by selling a bottle of water than giving out a free cup.  But I'm already overpaying for the sandwich, and EVERY other restaurant  I've been to will provide a free cup of water (even at Disneyworld!). So the next time I want a sandwich in the area I'll walk down the street to one of the many other places, and enjoy a cup of water with my food.  They won't be getting any more of my $.  

Side note: They only take cash.

Very friendly service. Our table ordered Black Pig, Gates of Hell, Inch of Heaven and some sides... broths were all surprisingly unflavorful and my egg was old :( 
Portion for price was a great deal and our server was really nice, restaurant & bathrooms were clean.
Definitely not the best ramen you'll ever have, but worth $10 for sure.

Not too bad but not as good as I expected, either.  I drove all the way from El Paso and was looking forward to this sandwich.  Afterall, who wouldn't want to say that they had a Philly in Philly?  After some rudimentary searching online, I decided that Pat and Geno's would not be the place to go, that those places had turned too touristy.  Campo's was recommended.  While it did not disappoint, I wouldn't say it was that good.

Service was quick, although somewhat weird as we asked what were good side items.  Instead of recommending something, we got a story about how the cashiers mom made the side items and it was really good.  The potato salad simply lacked flavor as if they forgot to use salt/pepper.

Would I go back?  No and it's not because the food wasn't good.  It was good but it wasn't great and I just don't see how a Philly sandwich couldn't be made pretty much anywhere and taste the same.  Unlike a Chicago style deep dish pizza, which seems to only taste good when it's from Chicago, I just don't see the unique characteristic in a Philly.

Not worth the money. The cheesesteaks are good but small. You can get a bigger cheesesteak for the same price and be just as good. I didn't hate it but there are other places were I can get a bigger cheesesteak for the same price.

It was Sunday and one of a few places open. No sign telling you cash only, ATM machine there but it charges you an extra $1.50 to use it. We ordered 2 cheese steak sandwiches w/the works. The crew was efficient and the sandwiches were hot but that was the best one can say. The meat was bland and not well seasoned, cheese was almost nonexistent, onions were not carmelized and the bread was chewy. We have an Italian place in NC that serves much better Philly Cheese Steak sandwiches.

My favorite ramen in philly by far. Really missed the feeling of being so full after a delicious bowl of ramen in Japan and this is the first time Ive felt that way since. Really solid, rich broth and thick and perfect chashu. Most places really slack on cooking their bamboo shoots properly too and these were on point and delicious. Staff is super friendly and welcoming too. I had the Gates of Hell ramen, could be spicier so people really looking for heat definitely ask for extra spicy. Total crowd pleaser though.

Idk why i keep coming back to this location hoping it will get better. Meat is never tender. Fries are never crispy. Customer service never makes up for the poor quality of food. If the owner cares they will make some adjustments. Listen. I know its not red robin its Wendy's i get it but come on man. You can't have an item on the menu called chicken tenders and the chicken isn't tender. How does that work. So frustrating.
Their karrage is the best I've had, and their ramen is the best I've had in Philly so far..   and I've had A LOT of ramen in Philly lol

Been to this place a couple of times. The quality of the food and service seem to worsen over time. One time I had an egg that was sooo salty that it felt like I just ate a spoon full of salt. Another time I had a dumpling with a piece of hair in it and the older Asian lady server just joked that the hair is too long to belong to anyone of the cooks , all I wanted was a "Sorry about that" but nope  she just took the dumpling and laughed like it's not their fault. This place use to be good.

3.5. Took me a while to try this place that I pass by frequently. Went on a weekday around 12:30, and it was fairly busy. Ordered the lunch special ($14) which consists of your choice of a bowl of ramen ($11 on its own), small salad (seaweed salad or mixed greens with crispy noodles on top) and an appetizer (includes choice of gyoza (3), fried chicken pieces or edamame). The mixed greens salad was tasty, if a bit dry after the small amount of dressing was gone. The gyoza was fine. ..Thin skin with flavorful pork and veg inside-Although they reminded me of frozen gyoza found at HMart. The inch of heaven ramen was very tasty, deeply flavored broth and tasty noodles. But, the serving size was a bit smaller than I expected, or than what you find a few blocks over in Chinatown. The lunch special was filling, but I may have been looking for something else if I hadn't had the other items to round out the meal.

The food came out in a reasonable amount of time, and the service was pleasant. Cute decor-with tables along one wall, while solitary diners are directed to the counter which faces the food prep area.  

A good choice if in the area, and not keen on walking to Chinatown for ramen.
Cash only cheesesteak spot with great steaks. As a philly native this is my go to spot for a steak. Price is worth it and the taste is awesome as well. Love classic cheesesteak spots like Campos!

Love this new ramen spot! I have been to ippudo and ichiran in NY, but so far this is my favorite ramen. I ordered takoyaki and black pig ramen, both were magnificent! The takoyaki cooked perfectly, crispy on the outside and so soft on the inside, I gotta admit it was the best takoyaki I've had in philly. The black garlic on my ramen didn't overpower the broth, oh that pork!!! It was amazing. It's a small place and cash only! But they have atm inside.

Really love this place!! I have dined in here and gotten take out. I stopped in to order a ramen to go 7 or so months pregnant and under the weather and the staff was so kind. Since I had not been there previously, they provided me with their recommendations. They also got me a seat to wait at and gave me a glass of water without me asking. Service was quick. I have tried two different things here and both were extremely flavorful and delicious. Also had a great experience when I dined in. The food is consistently delicious. Tip: It is cash only but they have an ATM

This was my first time trying Potbelly, I have to say I was not impressed. I'm not much of a soup guy so I didn't try any of the soups but I ordered a turkey and cheese sandwich. They toasted it which was fine the bread was fresh enough that it wasn't too crunchy but outside of that the sandwich was lacking flavor. It was just so bland. The turkey was just blah the cheese didn't even have flavor it was really interesting. I guess they are used to people dipping the sand which in a soup but again, not my style. I'm not sure I'd try this place again. They did have Zapps chips which was awesome becuase they are the best chips in PA but they were out of the voodo chip flavor, THE ONLY ONE THAT MATTERS  best of luck with your soups and sandwiches but this seemed like a super watered down version of Panera....

The franchise owner of this location should be ashamed and embarrassed. Clearly they are not though because the complaints are endless and there has been no changes made. New management from the store manager to the shift supervisors are needed at this place immediately! Your employees are inclined to act just as disrespectful as you and needs to be stopped immediately. Watched a guy get the wrong order and then they blamed him and yelled at him! Then yelled at another customer who said they owed the man an apology. Doesn't matter if you are a CEO of a Fortune 500 company or part time night worker at Mcdonalds, show respect to your customer or the person who gets your check paid. Don't like you job and don't want to be there? Find another job! Disrespecting customers and your employees is disgusting.

Attention the best Philly cheesesteaks are not on Market Street in Philadelphia. All these places are just tourist traps. Save your money and find an authentic Philly cheese steak that's not overpriced dry and they charge you an arm and a leg for. I live in New York City we've got the better Cheesesteak sorry Philadelphia especially on Market Street. As far as this place they do not accept credit cards they're not with the program they're not with the times. The Cheesesteak with small and not noteworthy at all. A homemade coleslaw was overpriced and not that good. The pretzel they offered was burnt. If you want cheese whiz on your pretzel it's a 1.75 extra. We had three small coffees for $9.
Very well maintained Qdoba. Quick lines, always fresh ingredients, good customer service.
Great cheesesteaks (way better than Sonny's)!! Mac & cheese was delicious too. The owner was very friendly, overall a great experience. Will be going back there for sure!
Stoped into Campo's because my favorite place was so busy. What a pleasant surprise. Now Campo's is my new favorite. Outstanding both in service and food.

I can't say I was extremely impressed by this place. First off they are cash only, which I did not see prominently anywhere, and while I consider it a minor inconvenience it is 2019. I can take credit cards right here on my phone and I don't even run a business! 

The food was okay. The cheese steak was average with a gummy/chewiness to it. The mac and cheese was pretty good but the cost vs portion seemed a bit off.

Overall they are in a touristy area, banking on touristy people to come in and have a philly in philly for way more CASH than they need to spend. Well go next door to the other philly place and you'll have an a tastebud bonanza worth the cost to buy in! 

I thought I would sample some of the other local joints but....One and done for me.

A+++ 

Came here last night with a party of 4. We made a reservation. We love that they take ressys. It's a small spot so it's necessary. We at first were sitting in the front, but the waitress noticed that we were pretty cramped because it is byob and we had a couple bottles of wine and beer, so she brought us to the back room since it was more spacious! We truly tore it up. FYI if you have a large party, they can accommodate! The aesthetic and atmosphere is very cute here. 

The food is amazing! We got the house salad and the Hiro Inch of Heaven(?) SO delicious. 

The service was amazing. Once we were done our meals, they let us hang out and finish our drinks rather than rushing us out. 

Highly recommend. 

Cash only, though! They have an atm.

I've waited all my life to have a real Philly Cheesesteak and on a recent but brief afternoon trip to Philly, my wife, daughter, and I stopped into Campo's due to it's inclusion of gluten-free bread for my daughter.  Ironically, she didn't want a cheesesteak and went with a chicken sandwich which she enjoyed.  I on the other hand went full cheesesteak with mushrooms and onions.  it was a good sandwich but honestly, not as good as I had hoped.  Philly natives tell me this place doesn't use the famous bread known for making a good cheesesteak.  Maybe.  Maybe next time I'll make it a point to find another shop but you know, this wasn't half bad.

We stopped by for the first time because my friend was craving Philly cheesesteak. It is located on Market Street, in the touristy part od town. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised but not blown away. 

Tip: CASH only!
But there is an ATM machine inside for an extra fee.

Inside was clean with plenty of tables to catch up with friends. I ordered the Valentine sandwich which was grilled chicken, onions and provolone cheese. It was $10.25 but the employee was kind enough to give me a discount so it ended being $9. I was pleasantly surprised because the sandwich wasn't too greasy or salty or too heavy on the cheese. The bun was toasty and soft. My only complaint was that the chicken was a bit dry. 

Overall a nice place for a quick grab and go. But I wouldn't make a specific trip to come here unless I happened to be in the area.
Hey let's get a sixteen piece chicken what do you like white or dark? That's ok you get 4 of each well unless you go to this one then you get nine wings a single breast and no drumsticks.

Our tour company uses Campo's regularly and they always take great care of our groups! I have also received Philly Cheesesteaks delivered to my home and I can say without a doubt that they are EXCELLENT!!!
jj's is the shit. open late for drunk munchies and always quick. recommend delivery or walk in, will surprise you just how fast they are! glad there's one on campus

In one weekend we tried Pat's, Geno's, and Campo's for Philly Cheesesteaks... Campo's was the winner!  Best bread, best meat, and indoor seating to boot!  Loved it!  Get the provolone with peppers and onions. YUM!

Great food and great staff.

Usually when i go to a sandwich shop, I get a sandwich.  However, they have the best, and I mean the best, Caesar dressing I have ever had.  Therefore, I am always inclined to get the chicken Caesar salad.  I know it may sound weird, but try it and thee shall see!

Just didn't live up to the hype. My husband and I love the city of philly and have been several times. We always set out to try new cheesesteaks when we are in town, and although Campos has crap Yelp reviews it is posted on several"Philly's best cheesesteaks" lists. And I have no idea why. The meat was chewy, I actually gave the rest of my sandwich to my husband to finish cause I just couldn't. The staff was friendly and when ordering I asked if they had fries or what kind of sides they had. The response was all our sides are not fried and are all homemade. Ok great, if they are all homemade and she made a point to tell me that they should be good. Wrong. I got the pasta salad and my husband the potato salad, we didn't care for either. They were less than mediocre. 2/5 do not recommend.

The best ramen I've ever had. Best noodles and broth. Best value. I got the "Hiro's Inch of Heaven" bowl with the fried chicken appetizer. You could swim in the broth. The sauce that came with the chicken was also good. A small side salad completed all this for the lunch special. Got it yesterday, and I'm going back today. Why didn't I try this place sooner?!

THE best ramen choice in Philly! Their pork has a smoky flavor which really sets it aside from the other pork I've tried at other ramen places in Philly, New York and Boston. Their broth is absolutely rich and has a profound depth of flavor. The only downside is that their portion size is quite poor as it is more so a snack than a filling meal. If I'm ever craving ramen, this is currently my go to spot in the area.
Love, love, love this place! Wonderful family-run business with best cheesesteaks in Philly, hands down.

If you're for a good Philly cheesesteak, Campo's is one of the best spots in philly and the people running it are even better! I'd recommend onions, wiz, AND provolone... and the stuffed olives might be my favorite side

This is one of my favorite cheesesteak places in Philly.  And the location is much better than the other top contenders, especially if you're just visiting the city.  I've only had the cheesesteaks (though the other items look pretty good as well) and they're delicious - good quality ingredients, full of flavor, and not at all dry.  I'd recommend going here for a solid Philly cheesesteak if you're in the area.
Good Philly Cheesesteak, but not near the best out there. Upside is that you can enjoy a brew with your food.

I've known Mike & Denise for over 40 years and Mike's father 
Mr. Campo who owned and ran a butcher store which is where Mike learned much about how to treat his customers. Which is extremely well. From when he opened his first deli back in the seventies, his sandwiches were superior, made with the best meats and their loving care. Greeted with style whenever you walk through their doors. You'll find it a delicious experience but I must warn you it can be habit forming. Enjoy 
Sincerely Joseph

Before moving to Philadelphia, I lived in Tokyo, Japan for a few years. At least once a week, I went to a local ramen shop--usually to nurse a hangover--to slurp up some ramen noodles and sip some soup, with a customizable variety of proteins and veggies.

Hiro brought back that experience for me. 

The ramen at Hiro is authentic and true to the experience you get at any ramen shop in Japan. You can choose from shoyu, tonkotsu, vegetable broth, and miso ramen broth. We went for the shoyu, a chicken marrow-based broth with soy sauce and the tonkotsu, a pork marrow based broth and likely the richest type. All of the broths were rich and authentic--I'd expect to taste any of these on the streets of Japan--well worth the base price. Different broths come with different noodles--for example, the chicken shoyu ramen came with a thinner, more delicate noodle, while the tonkotsu came with a thicker, hardier noodle. Nice attention to detail!

Just please DON'T think that you're paying for the same Top Ramen, Maruchan Cup Noodle, Ichiban Ramen, or whatever 50-cent packages are available at your local grocery store.

However, I think the fine folks at Hiro ought to rethink the prices of their toppings. A dollar for a single 2" by 4" seaweed/nori sheet is kind of redonk.

The portion-to-price ratio is reasonable--if you have a huge appetite, you might still be hungry afterwards, though. Hiro Ramen is a great place for lunch and the waiters and chefs are super willing to customize your experience!
VERY DELICIOUS!! My top 3 best cheesesteak place in Philadelphia. Such nice customer service. The works was so juicy and flavorful. I'd recommend this place to everyone.
This place is a gem...must visit. Get the Flyers Ice hoagie, you won't be disappointed.

I thought this place was great - especially because they had cheesesteaks for vegetarians! There was a lot of cheese and it tasted great, especially with their potato salad. It was soft and chewy and delicious. There was also plenty of seating inside and out. The food came out fast and I have no complaints. Well, maybe it's a little pricey, but I was still content.

Small little place that we decided to  try after working in the city.   The server who said she was the owners daughter was very friendly. We had a wiz without and a Works as well as homemade  Mac & cheese made by "mom". The sandwiches were tasty and not bad size and the Mac and Cheese was delicious!  Everyone from the cook to the owner talked with us while we were there and everyone was super nice.

Charsu like I've never tasted before only because it seemed as if they grilled it before carefully placing it in this deliciously full bodied spicy broth. I've had ramen from many places and I can't say I've had the best but this one hits upwards on my top 3. The service was great unfortunately I did not catch his name but he was so helpful in suggestions. My gf's order for some reason no longer had the particular broth so she opted with the standard house ramen which also was full bodied in flavor. I was doing my best to refrain from ordering too much so I stuck with just the ramen itself. But their appetizers seemed so intriguing. Live octopus tentacles.. I'm coming back for this. The decor was not over the top, felt comfortable and even sold what seemed like convenient snacks like from a street cart in Japan. I give it 5 stars just because it deserves to be eaten over and over again.
I was planning on stopping by here, but the roads around there are so screwed up there was a 'do not enter' sign ... but no place to enter so I ended up going past it.

The staff was very efficient, in fact as soon as we entered the restaurant they made us sit and brought us the menus (which are simple with few choices but satisfying overall). We took two appetizers (the fried chicken was delicious) and two different ramen. All the ingredients were tasty. Be sure to bring cash because cards are not accepted (CASH ONLY). However, there is an ATM near the entrance.
Overpriced tourist trap. The cold hoagies are equivalent to Wawa's, just twice the $. Average cheesesteaks. Prepare to be underwhelmed.

I ordered take out and was given the wrong item. Make sure you check your food from this location before you leave . As this location is relatively new, they don't have a telephone number or contact number available online.
The cheese steak is good but the Italian Hoagie is the best I've ever had. Highly recommended.

The best ramen in Philadelphia. This shop is definitely fully competitive with those excellent shops in NYC. This shop sticks with authentic Japanese ramen and this is perhaps why it does not reach full five stars. I sincerely hope this shop does not alter the plan; stick with authentic flavor.
The best cheesesteak in the city.  The service was excellent.  I can't wait to go back and have another cheese steak.

My sons was at Shiner's for more than a week and I was depended on Shiner's and Temple's cafeteria for 3 means a day.  The quality is good "for hospital food" but nothing you'd want to eat unless you have no other choice.  Nothing that should be spicy like curry or chili actually is.  The fried chicken is killer however.
Fire gf cheesesteak :) only thing is-- this place is cash only (atm inside but there's a $1.50 charge)
Worst cheesesteak I've had so far in Philly. The meat was very dry and not allot of flavor.

Absolute trash inside and out. Usually a national chain has standards for cleanliness, quality and food. This must be the one and only Taco Bell that's not regulated by those standards because it's a disgrace. No regional managers notice this? How do you mess up every order all the time. Avoid at all costs.

Ordered a bada bing(chicken cutlet, provolone, and sauteed broccoli rabe), recently. The green were COLD fresh out of the fridge and they don't have a microwave to heat sides. Please, a hot sandwich is a hot sandwich, I had to take the greens off, and they were thrown away. First time in 10 years have been disappointed by a Primos. Bartender was wonderful!!
The price is affordable, ramen is simple and tasty. This place is always on my list for a quick meal while still have something good
It's a must on your fun in Philly checklist! The only place I'd go for a cheesesteak. Campo's is community minded, family friendly, and close to the action.
Had a bottled Yuengling and a 'The Works'. I'm new to Philadelphia, but this has been one of my favorite  touristy Cheesesteaks yet!
Touristy af, but I preferred the taste of the cheesesteak here over Steve's which people rave about. Tip: It's included in your Philadelphia Pass and people forget this. Nice workers as well.
Yumm!  I had the Gates of Hell ramen, and I am heat nut.  This ramen hit just the right combination of tonkotsu broth and chili oil.  The Tako-Yaki fritters were also a treat.

The service sucks here. It seems as though the staff is always unprepared for the mass amounts of college students that eat here. They forget ingredients or parts of your order. They run out of ingredients all the time. They take forever to make a mobile order.

Gross! THERE WERE HAIRS IN MY QUESADILLA!! Hairs in both halves of the quesadilla covered in melted cheese. Absolutely disgusting and inedible. This is unacceptable especially during a pandemic. I also sat inside for ten minutes before someone acknowledged I was waiting for food to be placed on the pick up shelf. I do not recommend going here.

The sandwich's here are spectacular!  If you you want an authentic Italian hoagie, or Philly cheesesteak,  this is your place!  Some times you need a little taste of home.  They deliver overnight and everything is fresh.   The deli and steak are quality and the bread is the perfect size and fresh.  This is probably the 6th order from Campo's and it's always deliciou.

I just left there the lady who answer and wait on you is really rude. I tried to make and order on the phone she hangs up.Then I call back to order she takes the order but continues to be rude. At the end of me placing my food she says we are only taking pre paid orders. I say ok. I proceeded to give her my card number and she being to read the card numbers back to me out loud.I ask her not to because their could be people in the store. I told her I am almost there I will pay at the store.Her answer was "well I am not starting  nothing until I get a payment from you just to let you know". So I come and the store. She says what you want. I said I just called I said i was just going to come in and pay. Her response was Oh it's a lot of people that just called an said the same thing so you need to to figure out what you got. I just said never mind have a great night.
The food is great here I eat there frequently but never seen this lady before.

The staff was very rude. I ordered a cheesesteak and got a chicken sandwich. I told them my problem and the cashier said I ordered chicken. Why would I order chicken when I came to philly for a cheesesteak. She was fighting me telling me I was wrong. And that was that. I had to eat my nasty chicken whiz sandwich. Also everything is way overpriced. Refills are extra and they only accept cash. What a joke. Never going or recommending this place. Sonnys which is close to next door is much better.

Best vegetarian ramen I've ever had! I got the vegetarian ramen with the spicy bomb and it was so delicious. The broth was really flavorful and creamy. The spicy bomb added a great kick to it. The veggies went perfectly too!
The owner and staff were all really friendly and very sweet. I will definitely be going back soon.
Honestly one of the best cheesesteaks in philly! I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for that quality Philly cheesesteak!

My cousin had his 50th birthday celebration here this weekend.  He's a regular at this place and I can see why!  Staff is super friendly and very attentive! They were awesome with the kids at the party, gave them ramune and Pocky!

The food was soo good!! We had the Karaage Fried Chicken, Edamame and yaki-gyoza for apps.  The kids got French Fries.  It all tasted so good!!  We also got a small salad. 

I got the Black Pig Ramen - wow! So flavorful!! I don't know if it was the garlic oil or what, but that was some good soup!! The chashu was perfect!! Not too fatty, just enough! My 5 year old nephew loved the chashu! 

I've already told a few friends in Philly about this place and I plan on going back soon!

We ordered 2 trays of cheesesteaks and 1 tray of roast pork.  The process of ordering was so easy and pleasant.  My guests loved the food. I would definitely order again.  Thank you Campo's for making my party a success!

Man what can I say, the bread on the subs is great.  We ordered the Works Chicken and Cheesesteak. The chicken work cheese steak is fantastic!  Great flavor.  I like it more than my cheesesteak, which was also good as well
We were able to dine inside too.
Have more workers Drive-through always takes so long Waited for 20 minutes only third in line for just a happy meal in the dining room seems like it's closed a lot

Ever been so intrigued by something on a commercial that you just had to get it? No? I guess I'm the only weirdo doing that then. 

I went to Dairy Queen because I saw the new Dreamsicle dipped cone advertised on TV. It seemed like a limited-time thing so I wanted to try it before it was gone forever. 

Found a parking spot smack dab in the front. Inside, there was plenty of seating and for the most part, the floors and tables were clean. A line began forming so I hopped in line and waited to be served. 
You can select small, medium or large for custard. I paid $3.97 for a medium. It was a lot of ice cream. I should've gotten the small. 

The flavor was really underwhelming. I was expecting a zesty orange shell on top of vanilla ice cream but the orange flavor was so light, I tasted more vanilla than anything. 

I don't necessarily recommend getting this cone, but I had a good experience with the location. Everyone was friendly and fast. Next time I visit, I'll opt for the DQ Blizzard which never fails me.

I had the worst experience at this location. I walked up to the counter at 4:23 PM, the employees watched me for ten minutes. Then one young lady walked over. This young lady only mouthed "you want to order?" Like hello I am just standing here for ten minutes reading the menu. So finally, I am able to order, i place an order for white rice and orange chicken. This order was placed at 4:33, I received my food at 4:50. I only received the food, because the chef/ cook saw my frustration. During this 17 minute wait, i watched the employees gossip on their phones, one guy walked across the counter to grab another employee, & one  talking to person from another restaurant.  Not once did anyone mention why my simple order was talking close to 30 minutes to be made. I then reminded the cashier that I ordered a soda, this young lady responds by saying "no you didn't, I didn't charge you", I looked at this young woman and said you charged me 2.25 and I have the receipt. This young lady never said sorry, she just got annoyed that I reminded her that she did not give me my order. After the soda issue, the chef asked Little Miss Sunshine Tayla (that's what my receipt read), what I ordered. Tayla, responded and my food was ready within a minute. Once my order was bagged, the second cashier ( she spent most of the time walking around complaining about who helps take care of her son) dangled my back in front of my face.  I remained calm dealing with this situation, I was just stunned. Throw the entire staff away.  The food was just okay.
Service was really nice especially during these hard times and was hard to order and pay.

Dined here Saturday night. It is very very very small in there but the food was good. The people who took your order were nice. I had the Vegan Cheesesteak. They do not fry anything so the sides are salads. Enjoy

Subway food in general is aight... I usually get the meatball sandwich with the good ole flat bread. Besides that, I had a good interaction with the manager plus the restaurant is always clean, so no complaints.

This place is right next to MilkBoy, and honestly - I had never noticed it before. I came here last Friday night about 8pm with 3 others, and we were able to get a table with just a few minutes wait.  A 4th joined us a bit later, and they were accommodate us easily by moving us to another table. 

They sell cans of beer (Sapporro, Sly Fox) for $3 which is awesome. We got some edamame for a snack to start, and we each ordered a bowl of ramen (one ordered Gates of Hell - holy spicy!). The one I ordered had a lot of spice in it. The bowl was big and pretty full with a lot of tasty ingredients - pork, egg, corn, sprouts, scallions, etc. Lots of noodles. Clocked in around $11, and I was definitely full. The beers were also nice and cold. 

I think this place is a winner. I'll come back.
One bite and I threw it away. Worst sandwich I've ever had. Unfortunately it is Easter Sunday and all respectable steak spots are closed. Truly horrible.

A man from New Jersey (who later became my fiance) introduced me to Campo's and I will never go back to Pats or Genos or the other "standard" cheesesteak establishments.  My favorite cheesesteak in Philadelphia presides in a bodega at 28th and Girard and since I don't get there much, Campo's has taken its place.

There is a reason that they have a shop at CBP and they ship nationwide, b/c they rock!  Go to Campo's for the authentic cheesesteak experience.

Great ramen and good ambience. Made it in time for the $6 app/sake happy hour special and it really was the icing on the cake. The broth was rich and full of that pork-y flavor. Will have to go check it out again soon.
Currently waiting in the drive-through line for over 20 minutes now very unsanitary. men working in front does not have gloves on employees are eating right in front of the window, mask down also.

Food was hot and tasted well. But they didn't take the time to give a proper portion of French fries. 
After spending $24 both boxes combined equaled one French fry

this is the slowest mcdonald's ever. every time i come here it is a whole ordeal and the line is always insanely long. once i finally got my good today THERE WAS A HAIR BAKED INTO THE CRUST OF THE HASHBROWN!!!!!!!!!

I stumbled here on my very first day in Philly and had an urge to come in even tho I wasn't hungry. And I must say, I'm glad I did because the ramen did not disappoint! I got the Gate of Hell with spicy broth and is probably the best broth I ever had and I tried multiple famous ones in California. I was not fan of the meat, it was dry and tough. But everything else made up for it.

This Qdoba is awesome! The employees are alway nice, smiling, and very efficient. They always make jokes, and seem to remember customers if you go fairly often. This is my go to spot on campus if I want to grab a quick lunch.

Cute little spot with a few tables for sit down, currently open for take out and dine in. Located near bustling downtown chestnut street, easily accessible. Wheel chair friendly.

They have a few signature ramen dishes, each soup distinctly different, and you can add more items to you soup if you like. Customize your own ramen. I got the second one, it was very good!

Small selection of appetizers, I could actually see the octopus pieces in the mix! 

Will come back again to try the others

Finding this place was a problem, since they don't have a sign.  I walked passed this rundown front a few times until someone told me it was right next to MilkBoy.  The decor looked like a standard ramen joint with a bar and some tables.  Nothing spectacular, and certainly not the "best looking restaurants in Center City" and MILES from "sexy."  I had 5 people in my party, and we crammed into a small table near the front. Ok so the decor is mediocre, but I'm really here for the food. Unfortunately, this was the worst ramen I've ever had (and that includes packet ramen).

There were only 3 things to choose from, "Hiro Ramen" (basic ramen with thin noodles, egg and pork belly), Shoyu Mazemen (a soup-less thick noodle with soy sauce) and a vegetable ramen.  First of all, there were 5 people at our table, and we were not served at once.  Each dish came out one at a time with gaps in between.  When we all finally dug in, it was a HUGE disappointment.  The Hiro Ramen had no seasoning at all.  It was a thin broth that tasted like it came from a packet.  But even packet seasoning at least has salt.  This was boiled noodle, boiled pork belly, boiled egg, and some brown water.  The Shoyu was the exact same thing but with thicker noodles and without the broth.  It at least had a bit more flavor, but it was all soy sauce.  All of it was greasy, flavorless, and pretty terrible.  There were no prices listed, so I kind of expected it to be expensive.  But, $9 for this crap?!  They really have some nerve. It's a good thing they had a soft opening, because they should pack up and find another career.

1.5 stars. Honestly, I hate to write this review, but this is for poor customer service.

We received a free cheesesteak voucher for purchasing the Visit Philly Overnight Hotel Package that visitphilly.com was promoting to increase tourism to Philadelphia. Unfortunately, while the perks of the package were great, this was one of the bad experiences. 

We went to Campo's on Memorial Day and despite being only semi-busy, service was poor. Nothing compared to Sonny's a few doors down who was crazy busy. We waited in line only about 5 minutes. However, after we ordered (a regular cheesesteak with onions) we ended up waiting over 40 minutes.
