That would have been fine, EXCEPT, our order was ignored and many people who ordered after us proceeded to receive their orders minutes ahead of us. That was such a disappointing experience. The workers seemed polite, however, why was our order ignored. Most likely because it was a free voucher. However, I do not know why that should come after all the other orders. We paid for a package. 

In regards to the cheesesteak, it certainly wasn't a full size cheesesteak. It was about 6 inches. In addition, there wasn't anything spectacular about the taste. Plain bread with steak slices and provolone cheese.  

After this experience, we won't be back.

Taco Bell is usually consistent but this location is not up to snuff, I've been there twice. The food was cold and they never ever give enough sauces even if you ask for extra! The staff is really friendly though.

The location is also kind of hard to find if you are in a car. It comes up suddenly and then if you miss it you have to go all the way around the block. Never got sick from this location though!
Great spot in Philly, the ramen is absolutely delicious!! The chicken soy was great!! It's cash only, no card!

Everything tasted good, especially the chashiu pork in the Gates of Hell bowl, but the broth was too salty, even by ramen standards. The normal portion is also a bit on the small side, so make sure to order lots of extras.

This is what is one of the official cheese steak places in Philadelphia. Great service, fun crowd great sandwiches and salads. It was 100° when we visited so we ate inside. It was a great place to go after visiting Christ Church which is located across the street.

I Stopped in briefly for a quick lunch run, was greeted by possibly the manager (his shirt looked different from the other crew workers). I ordered a chicken tender meal. The drive up cashier had to cash me out and gave me my receipt with no "thank you" he just passed me my receipt. The employee who gave me my food also just  passed me my bag of food a "thank you" without asking me would I like any sauces/condiments. It seemed like all of the employees were more engaged in their conversation and that would of been okay if there weren't any customers inside ...but ummm pardon me guys I was the customer there...theeee only customer there. 

The outside of the restaurant was clean, the inside was clean as well including the bathroom. My food was hot and fresh, chicken tenders were tasty, bbq sauce was delicious, water was a nice cool temp' and my biscuit was fluffy. I visited today around lunch time.

What terrible customer service. First the gentlemen before me said his fries were cold and wanted new ones (as per their policy) and the clerk complains to the manager in front of the customer that he was eating the fries. Ok. Moving on. My small fries and cheeseburger took about 8 minutes. Wasn't even busy. Decided to fill my Eco bottle w water and ice at the self fill station and get yelled at by the lady next to me that I can't do that. I ask what can't I do. She said fill my bottle. I ask why. She says 'I don't know, you'll have to ask the manager'. Ok. Seek the manager when they finally finish making my lunch and she says 'I dunno where your bottle has been, it's unsanitary'. IT'S A SELF FILL STATION. DOESNT GET MUCH MORE UNSANITARY BUT WE TAKE OUR RISKS. Jeebus! Please pray for this nation...we're a sinking ship of stupidity and ignorance.

Campo's is above and beyond the best sandwich in the city.  They are not necessarily the biggest but it satisfies me every time since they are the most delicious and truly a definition of philly cheesesteaks by which all others should be measured. 

The Campos have mastered the art of the sandwich. They are very very good people working here and they all enjoy treating you to the best this city has to offer in the way of quality. 

If you want to be really gourmet you get a bottle of genuine philadelphia root beer which will make you never want to drink from the fountain again. Worlds of difference! They also have a good beer selection. 

CASH only, ATM on site. Indoor and outdoor seating.

These guys make calzones like they don't want to make them. The owner was rude, and not in a lovable Pat's & Geno's way, and the food way below average. I was embarrassed that I'd brought my cousin who was in from California. I come from a big south philly Italian family so take my word for it. A shame because  the neighborhood needs more restaurants. My prediction: This place will be out of business soon so I'm excited to see what new restaurant takes advantage of the location.

[1156]

2/2021

Wish I checked Yelp first.  We were in the area and stopped in for a cheesesteak.  

Ordered two cheesesteaks (one size) and total was $28.   I asked for the receipt and was told it was in the bag (just the order slip w no prices).   Extra charge for credit card. Thanks 

My cheesesteak did not have a lot of meat so we were a bit disappointed.  

Staff was not friendly 

I won't be back

Disgusting. I mean, Taco Bell is not known for gourmet eats but you know, sometimes you need a burrito supreme. Just don't get it from this particular location. Tacos with the paper literally stuck to the shell, burritos that don't hold together and something doesn't taste right. If you eat here, make sure that you have the same number of toilets in your house as people. You may be putting some stress on your plumbing afterward. Also why can I not give zero stars? Get on that, Yelp....
Nice location within walking distance to some touristy spots. Solid cheesesteak sandwich while in Philly. Mac and cheese and their rice pudding were delicious

The food here is always so good but the workers at this location are idiots. None of them know the menu or anything that comes on the certain menu items. The stupidity of the workers truly never disappoints. I have never had a seamless experience here due to the employees.
Constantly get order wrong. No leadership. Bad attitudes all around. Sorry to bother you while you were working.
I had there vegan cheesesteak and it's was good! A bit chewy but the flavors were good .

We were in town and wanted to get an authentic Philly Cheesesteak within walking distance of Liberty Hall and so we came by here.  I wouldn't say this is a must stop for a Philly.  We were the first ones in the restaurant for lunch and it took a while to get our food.  They got one of the sandwiches wrong (put onions on it after we asked then not to).  The sandwiches were good, but we didn't think it was $60 for 4 sandwiches good (no sides with them).

Ordered from Caviar which was a disaster. Campo's on the other hand was fabulous. They remade my sandwich fresh after waiting an hour for Caviar to pick up. Our sandwiches were great. Highly recommended.

tl;dr: good ramen, small space, personally I prefer Terakawa but still tasty!

The long version: Came here with a group of eight and we expected to have to wait for at least an hour (PAX unplugged was going on).  Luckily, someone who had made a reservation didn't show up so we were seated in less than ten minutes! 

SERVICE: The waiters were attentive, refilled our waters, and food arrived pretty quickly!

INCH OF HEAVEN: The broth had a delicious smoky flavor!  At the end, it was a little too salty though.  The ramen was absolutely amazing and perfect.  Soft boiled egg was on point.  However, the chasiu was a little overdone and too chewy.  Also, there wasn't all that much in the ramen - I'm a little used to there being more toppings.

All in all, it was pretty good! I would come back if my friends wanted to.

During the day, this location is amazing but stay away at night! I showed up to the drive through and sat there for 15 mins. Every car in the line was frozen. No orders were handed off at the window. The same two cars sat at the first and second window and the drivers looked distraught. During the full 15 mins I waited, nobody took my order. I took my business elsewhere. Averaging out the 1 star for night and 5 stars for day, I give this a 3/5.

Ordered Hiro's Inch of Heaven takeout and it was delicious. The order was ready within 10 minutes. The broth was very rich and the pork belly chashu just melt in your mouth. The only drawback was this place only accept cash but I'll definitely be back for some authentic Japanese ramen at unbeatable prices!

There was not many people in line when my Mom and I went through the drive thru. They are currently doing construction on the drive thru, but it was still workable which was fine! The lady at the drive thru speaker was so friendly and helpful and we even exchanged a laugh together - she was very pleasant! :) The employees packaged our food with care and everything was neatly in the bag. We ordered two chicken breast $5 Fill Ups with potato wedges, a small cole slaw, a Smokey Mountain BBQ Grilled Chicken Breast, green beans, 2 regular Pepsi's, and 1 Diet Pepsi. The chicken itself was pretty good, mine looked more like a rib than grilled chicken breast. The green beans had a bizarre flavor - kind of reminded me of soup or chicken stock flavor on the green beans, and extra salty (which I did not like). The Diet Pepsi was pretty good.
I would give no stars if I could this place doesn't even deserve 1 star... terrible place and customer service.
Good flavor but pretty small for the price. Only a few seats. After a day of walking all over Philly. Not very filling

Although I didn't receive the best customer service, every single employee I interacted with had great manners. What I mean by not the best customer service; I had placed an online order, so when I got there I went to the sign that said pick up here. I stood there and had to say something to them for them to let me know that I have to grab my own order from the table(which is crazy because I could've grabbed anybody's order, vice versa). But the associate handled it very well. The main reason for the 3 stars is because the store was nasty. Stuff all over the floor, and the back salad station was a mess. Everybody knows that food workstation hygiene is the first thing you cater to. As far as the food; the quality and taste was A1.

I was in philly in business with a colleague who is allergic to gluten. She really wanted a cheesesteak so we searched(yelp of course) for recommendations on a good place with gluten free options. Camps came up near the top of our search and we decided to try it out. It was amazing. A mom and pop place where mom still makes the coleslaw herself! The gluten free bread was really great and my colleague thoroughly enjoyed her cheesesteak. Mine was equally awesome!! This will be my goto in Philly!!

I ordered a double burger and they gave me a single. Staff are always rude and dont even acknowledge your presence. If I say thank you , your welcome should be followed as you are representing a business and should have common courtesy.  They all look annoyed to be there. I'm sure there are 1 or 2 good employees but majority are RUDE AS HELL.

Cheesesteaks are ok. The bread has sesame seeds which is really nice. However, I thought the meat to bread ratio was off. They have beers in the fridge at $7 each. You can sit outside and people watch for entertainment.

This chipotle was out of chicken, rice, beans and queso all at the same time oh also they were out of chips so they gave me these as chips instead. I waited 20 mins in line for cold tacos and extra shells

Tons of options on cheesesteaks and chicken steaks. Got a bbq chicken cheesesteak with fried onions and it was the perfect avout of bbq. The chicken could have been a bit more chopped up though. Overall, great experience. Delivered very quickly.

Like others said, a little hard to find since the sign out front is only in Japanese. We walked by it a couple times before we realized it was there. This actually reminds me of the one time I went to Japan where there are random hard to find restaurants on small side streets. I really enjoyed the takoyaki balls (octopus in batter) and their low sodium broth (which is not always available everywhere). They don't take reservations, but we came a few minutes before 6 and was able to grab a table. Immediately afterwards the place seemed to get really busy. Go early because the dining area has very few tables!
The dining room is closed so you  have to go to the drive thru The line was short the staff was friendly and efficient I was able to make my order and get one in less than 10 minutes
A good guilty pleasure. Expectations weren't too high because they're calzones on a college campus but they do hit. Workers are a bit aggressive

This Wendy's is the closest one to my house, which is the ONLY reason I go here at all.  The service sucks, the facilities are disgusting, but worst of all they ALWAYS mess up my order.  I even intentionally ordered 3 large number ones with cokes for all of them.  THE EXACT SAME ORDER!!!!! And they gave me a small frosty, 2 medium cokes, 2 burgers and a chicken sandwich.  On the receipt they rung me up for 2 small #2s. Are you fucking kidding me?!?  Don't waste your time going here, as I have.  These people don't give a shit about the job they do or anyone for that matter.

My boyfriend and I order from campos frequently and it is always amazing. I usually get the vegan cheesesteak and he gets the "works" or the "heater". We also have gotten their tomato soup and Mac and cheese before. The owners are extremely nice and appreciative as well. We love it here!

Went to Campos on Monday night to try a cheesesteak, it was amazing!! The man working was so helpful and kind. He told me I could get frozen cheesesteaks to bring home to my family. Bought 5 there the next day from a sweet gal behind the counter and the kind man was there again the next day. Cannot say enough good things about their customer service and their sandwiches!! The BEST!! Please go and keep this Philly classic restaurant alive!!
This McDonald's will last you about 45 minutes waiting in the drive through. Have fun eating... oh wait, your waiting.

Horrible horrible service. Did curbside pick up and wouldn't come outside because of the rain but wouldn't let me inside either. They wanted me to wait in the 20 car drive through when I already ordered and paid

Not only does this place have delicious cheesesteaks, the staff is incredibly kind and the service is great. ALSO, I had an amazing salad. The mamas salad has an amazing basil vinaigrette, fresh lettuce, peppers onions and marinated chicken that melts in your mouth. Will def be going back
Skimpy  cheesesteaks. They charged me $1 to use my card and the charge for 3 customers later suddenly became $2 to use their card.

This location is appalling earlier today I went through the drive thru to order my lunch and was talked to like I was a nobody and when I asked to speak to a manager I was told I am the f ing manager in which time a man proceeded to come out the back door and shout more obscenities at me and the call me a racial slur. If you are of white decent I would strongly suggest you stay away from this location. And yes I will be contacting a lawyer on this manner

They charge a CC fee.  This is a cheesesteak, not a mortgage payment.  Felt cheap.  Reflected in the quality of the cheesesteak which was maybe 2/5 as the meat tasted a little dry. Much better options in Philly and they don't charge CC fees. This is the cost of doing business.

Hiro combines with its less conventional rival Cheu Noodle Bar to make a strong case for the best ramen spots in Philadelphia being squarely in Center City in the blocks immediately South of Chinatown and Broad Street. As a number of other reviewers have pointed out, Hiro is a cheap, generally undercrowded gem. 

I've been twice now, each time trying a different ramen, both of which have left me satisfied and eager to keep working through the options. On my first visit, four or five months ago, I can't remember what I did for an appetizer, but I got a bowl of the excellent "Porfolio" ramen, which combines chicken and pork broth with a potent but not-overbearing chili kick. 

When I finally followed up this past weekend, I went for the "Black Pig", a slightly simpler bowl that lets its signature burnt garlic oil do the heavy lifting (to great effect). Both came topped with well-cooked, tender, and flavorful slabs of pork belly that paired wonderfully with the noodles. I asked the waiter to bring me over some chili oil and poured a splash in, which brought the flavor to pretty much exactly what I had wanted when I ordered. I paired that with the pork dumplings/yaki gyoza. They came out about 3 seconds before my ramen, so the latter kind of stole the spotlight and dominated my taste buds, but the portion size of the gyoza was great (at six, there was one more than I would have expected, making them $1/gyoza) and I didn't take a bite of them that I didn't enjoy. My girlfriend really enjoyed her simple house salad, too, praising the ginger dressing. 

I can't wait to go back to try the "Pig and Miso" ramen (assuming I can hold back from revisiting the Porfolio), the seaweed salad, and possibly the fried chicken. Let the crowds have Terakawa, I'll take no line and arguably superior ramen bowls here at Hiro.

We had two Italian hoagies and two cheese steaks delivered from Campo's in Philly to Dallas today and they tasted like we were right there eating them.

The goods arrived packed in a styrofoam container on ice packs, yet not frozen and in perfect condition. Rolls were fresh with the crunchy crust and the lettuce and tomatoes were fresh. Plus, it was loaded with an ample selection of Italian cold-cuts and cheese.

We did help-out the cheesesteaks by taking the meat out, loading it in a pan, adding the onions and whiz they had sent and warming them all up together. In the mean time we were warming the bun in the oven. We put the two together and it tasted just like we were there. 

We greatly appreciated this wonderful "taste of Philly", as we this year will miss the annual road trip there.
Cheese steak is wondeful. I don't quite recommend the tomato and rice soup i had. The taste was too strong for me. Some desserts looked tasty too. So sad that i don't have a bigger stomach
One of the better ramen places in Center City Philly. Highly recommend for vegetarians

Stopped by here with my family on a day trip into the city, wanted cheesesteaks and found this place while walking around old city...very glad we stopped in! Super fast service - especially considering how crowded it was - and even better sandwiches!! Definitely going to be coming back next time I'm in the area

After living in PA for over 9 years, and having never been to a Checker's, we gave it a whirl at the U City location this week. 

I'm not surprised this location has 4 stars, because the woman who waited on us was SUPREMELY fantastic, kind, helpful and funny. When we told her we'd never tried Checker's before, she welcome us warmly, recommended the Baconzilla, told us all about their fries and when we told her we were splitting everything - asked us if they should cut everything in half! The staff looked like they were working hard to fulfill drive through orders, but we had the dining room to ourselves!

And the food was decent! The Checkerburger with Cheese could rival the Whopper or Quarter Pounder with Cheese at McD's any day. And that Baconzilla. Mmm. Perfection. Would skip the mozz sticks, but definitely try the fries. Also, I have my eye on a milkshake for next time!

The staff is very, very young and immature! They are probably Temple University students which is fine. The bowl they made was very small. They should do better because Chipotle put more food in my bowl. The line was longer than it needed to be. It was very, very, very, very slow and this was at 9pm. There wasn't anyone behind me and my boyfriend. So, me and my boyfriend was together and they asked if we needed 2 bags. ‍ I don't know how DUMB these girls are. Also, 1 girl had to ask the rest of the staff to be quiet with all their talk about nothing while the line continued to stall with only 4 people in it! ‍‍ It was my FIRST AND LAST time here! I'm not coming here ever again!

We stopped here yesterday to grab a bite to eat.  Mia was a sweetheart. We ordered our steak sandwiches and wanted fries and she said they don't have fried food there, but we have delicious homemade salads. She was proud to tell us each one was made by her mom. We I'd course tried 2 of them, the pasta salad and macaroni. Both were delicious!!!  All 4 of us enjoyed our meals and would highly recommend this shop.

Was so happy with the portions I got from Qdoba recently. I almost never do fast-casual, but as I was hiding from the rain, I found the closest open place to wait it out was this restaurant so I headed in just to buy a drink. The smells drew me closer to the food ordering line and then from there, I decided I needed to see what the hype was about. I loaded my bowl, got chips and salsa and a drink to make it a meal. 

The bowl stayed together in the rain and through a bus ride home. I don't usually like queso or sour cream on my burritos and bowls, but this was so flavorful and made the toppings really come together. So much flavor, they packed it in- I know other similar restaurants are always so bland, I didn't know Qdoba was legit!

My favorite of all time. Best ramen place in Philly! Not only is their ramen phenomenal but the karaage and takoyaki are out of this world. My favorite ramen is the porfilio. Owner is also super friendly! It is cash only! So make sure you bring cash (and if you forget there is an ATM on site!)

Wow okay, I guess I was expecting some half-baked experience since it's an Asian restaurant not actually in Chinatown, but I was dead wrong. I wanted to come here after seeing some reviews, and it was like we were actually in Japan when we walked in. It's the classic look of a ramen shop, and the service is freaky fast. There aren't a lot of options, but I got the standard ramen and it was amazing.

Also, have you noticed their menu prices are pretty cheap? Cheaper than some reputably delicious and authentic ramen shops in the city? And it's actually a decent competitor? Sign me up as a regular, give me a membership, a loyalty card...something! I'm in love.

That being said...wasn't crazy about the takoyaki but that's okay! You can't have it all.

I can only imagine what this place looks like at lunch time, but an early dinner time is the perfect slowness before everyone files in. Do yourself a favor and put this on your list now.

I deliciously tasty cheesesteak. This tastes way better than Tony Luke's. The four-star rating is due to the excessively high grease factor as well as a couple of crunchy unknowns found in the cheesesteak. With that said though, you can't beat the taste!

Campo's makes a solid steak, but I really love them for is "The heater" which has buffalo sauce and jalapeno cheddar. Best take i've seen on a "Authentic" Buffalo Cheesesteak. You can also find them at Philly games.

Called for delivery and was told that my pizza would be delivered would be delivered within an hour. I called to see my status on the pizza at the hour mark and was cussed out by the owner of the pizza parlor. The owner is a complete joke and is pathetic. I highly recommend that you order your food from a restaurant that respects your service. Plus the pizza is subpar anyways.
Best sandwiches in the city since the early 70's. Or at least that's as far back as I can remember!! Love everything on the menu. Always fresh and every bit is enjoyable and delicious
It's a Wendy's. Is it one of the "good ones"? Yeah, I've had no issues.

I know people have mixed reviews here, but their hoagies are the best.  Get the Campos Italian Special or the Mama Mia Special, and you cannot go wrong.  Thank you to all of the people at Campo's for making a world class hoagie!

Skip this Pei Wei!! The wait time is extremely long and the orders get messed up easily. I waited over 15 mins for my order, chicken teriyaki without onions or peppers with noddles and all I got was chicken, spinach and noodles. I did not get the snow peas or carrots as in the description. I'm allergic to onions and I found one in my meal. Extremely dissatisfied!!! Keep walking.

kidding me? They said give food to the "chinese guy" how racist are these staff?

And they screwed up my order. I only ordered a beef chalupa and got chicken.

Decidedly OK cheesesteaks here; I think that most people will be underwhelmed. Also, this place is CASH ONLY.

We were hoping to check out nearby rival Sonny's for authentic Philly Cheesesteaks, but it was a small venue that was pretty packed.  Campo's is just down the street, and is about the same size.  The cheesesteaks were solid - we got one with the works.  While not huge, these sandwiches are heavy enough to really split between two people.  However, Campo's doesn't offer fries ("we don't have anything fried here") and instead has potato and macaroni salads as sides.  That's kind of a disappointment.  I mean, people who order cheesesteaks aren't seeking health food. 

Campo's has a moderate amount of outdoor seating - inside is pretty cramped.  The service was fast and friendly.  But seriously - this place isn't nearly good enough to justify its cash-only policy.  You can get a similar quality cheeseteak throughout the city, with fries, and pay with a card at so many other places.  Feel free to pass on Campo's.
Great Philly cheesesteaks! Hit the spot after walking around. A nice cold beverage and a hot cheesesteak. Friendly folks.

Unfortunately every time I come to this Taco Bell my cheesy gordita crunch is stuck to the paper smh! EVERYTIME. The girls are usually nice but any other Taco Bell is better than here they need new management or training. Anyhow they are still the closest Uptown besides city ave and even with bad reviews they won't change.  All I can say is don't expect quality service or food here. Everywhere else I go my cheesy gordita nacho dorito taco is awesome this is the only place it's just another Taco. Bummer

I work in the local area, and the size of their sandwich and the price is an absolute joke, they charge me $14 for a chicken salad sandwich that isn't even as long as my hand. I guarantee you I will never set foot in that door ever again. They charge me an extra dollar to use my card. I was already paying $13 for a sandwich. 
The sandwich wasn't even packed with chicken salad .... That two dollar signs should be upgraded to 4 ....
Would give 4.5 stars. Broth is in the tastier side. Very simple ramen without too many ingredients but flavorful nonetheless. Takoyaki was pretty decent as well. Perfect for a cold Philly Sunday.

The girl cashiers there has a nasty attitude and shitty customer service. Got my order wrong and went back to tell them. Gave me a nasty look and rolled their eyes, what is up with that? The food is mediocre at best.

I love Qdoba but this location could improve. Very sloppy with how they plate your food. Also food items were mixed together. White rice mixed with brown, lettuce in the corn, etc. All due to rushing and fixing your food even when their isn't a line. Portion sizes also changed. You now have to ask for double rice or they'll give you an extremely thin layer at THIS location. Have to ask for double meat because most will end up on the counter tops from them rushing. Not worth the money. Go to Chipotle or make your own bowls at home. Used to be my favorite over Chipotle.
First Philly cheesesteak in Philly! Wife loved the gluten free option! My regular cheese steak was good! Nothing to write home about, but it was really pretty good!

If i could leave -100 stars I would. so I worked at dp dough for a while....i've had it with the bosses shit, he treats the customers like trash he's pulled a gun on a customer before. We will never order from them again. Always an issue and never any good customer service. Please don't waste your money on this place if you're expecting quality customer service. Food quality may be good, but that's if you even receive it. Lost a valued customer. Never again.

The burrito bowl is absolutely disgusting.  The chicken was lacking and dry.  The pick de gallo was missing cilantro and onions it was just tomato's and they basically just through an obscene amount of rice on there.  Never again
For years i forgot how good dairy queen was. Recently since covid, i started going there again. I love to get the chocolate milkshake. Its the best milkshake, relaxing.

My favorite food in the world are Cheesesteaks. Now, growing up on the Jersey Shore I believed they had the best until I tasted a real, authentic Philadelphia cheesesteak. This place is amazingly good! The cheesesteaks were so flavorful and juicy , with lots of meat, and the bread was soft and freshly baked . My husband and I can't wait to go back ! A+ for Campo's!

Good ice cream although not as good as friendly's Imo. the chocolate oreo blizzard is my personal favorite but you really cant go wrong with anything on the menu. for food don't expect much 'cause they only serve hot dogs(from what i could tell)
The ice cream isn't all natural and most likely loaded with artificial flavoring,coloring and a bunch of delicious preservatives and chemicals but you know that already don't you ?
I thought it was just OK. I got the vegetable ramen. The noodles weren't entirely cooked but they were still eatable. The service was decent.
Spot was clean inside and out, pizza was good, customer service was casual and down to Earth.  Expectations were met.

They were completely out of a lot of the options.  When we asked for chicken, they were out and asked if we wanted to wait.  We waited and they came back a while later and said that it would be 15 more minutes, so we settled on something else.  They was also no brown rice.  The food that we did get wasn't great.

You can tell when someone doesn't know to wrap a burrito and the dude working today is one of those dudes.  Everything should be spread out in the burrito and this burrito didn't have it.  It had toppings highly concentrated in certain areas.  Overall, never coming back here.

Not the biggest fan of this place... Although the customer service is quite great, the food is just above par. The meat seems to be over cooked and i find myself pulling out chunks of meat that is just to chewy for me to swallow. Make sure to bring cash!!!
I can't speak for what goes on at the there since I ordered mine of DoorDash, but the food was amazing! I've ordered back several times. Probably one of my favorites in philly

We were in town for the day visiting from Miami. We wanted authentic cheesesteaks without going to the more touristy places. Campo's did not disappoint. Everything from the bread to the steak to the cheese was amazing. You can just tell it's a well made sandwich using quality ingredients. It just so happens that our last name is Campos so my kids were freaking out. They got sweatshirts and my son declared it "the best restaurant in the world!" Hopefully we can come back to visit soon.

BEST RAMEN EVER!!! I've had ramen from many different places in Philly, NYC, Chicago and Boston and this is still the best! Gates of hell, porfilio and black pig are our faves. Been going here for years and the flavors are always consistent and yummy. The karange chicken and house salad are also very good. Mila and her staff are amazing and super nice, which is a bonus! #1 for sure.
Excellent food and friendly service from this family owned and operated gem. Don't miss it!

While doing a little sightseeing in Philly we looked up and saw the Campi sign knowing that our yearn for cheesesteak will about to be satiated and it was. 

Of course when you think about Philly and food you have to think about cheesesteak. We had a hankering and it needed to be satisfied and the famous long-standing Campos did the trick. Cheddar spread, onions, mushrooms, red and green peppers along with the jalapeño cooked, add some marinara sauce and your on the way to a tummy dance. The only thing was the lack of value at around $12 it was only 8 inches which for a big dude was not quite enough to keep me satisfied, but fortunately enough for me my 10-year-old daughter only ate half of her's. 

The Place is small only about eight tiny circular tables so if you're with a large group you're going to have to order out or eat and walk at the same time.

And if we're in that area again as Arnold would say " we'll be back."

Stay away from this location, the restaurant is close so you have to use the drive-thru obligatory! The lady on the speaker is really rude, they dont know how to talk to people! This location is the closest to my house So I have been here couple of times, they always say I dont have this and I dont have that I think is because they dont want to do it! Its sad how franchise owners dont pay attention to this!

Was looking for ramen and found this place. I ordered the black pig with a spicy bomb and it was amazing. The place is small only about 10 tables, but the service was on point. Would highly recommend this place.

It's an ok Ramen. The egg is over cook, broth is ok, noodles is ok. But very nice interior! 

For the price, you're better off with other Ramen places.

OMG so good!!  We were in Philly over the new year holiday and it was freezing!  So after a day of walking around we dove in here to warm up and meal on some ramen.  Apparently they do not serve booze.  I hadn't noticed any signs of BYOB before we came or I would've been prepared for that.  Since I saw all the bottles of sake everywhere I assumed they served it and the lady just kinda laughed and said they didn't, now I know. I had already looked up the menu and knew I wanted to try the Gates of Hell bowl.  It was amazing.  The ramen came out very fast and piping hot, unfortunately that didn't stop me from slurping it down and the heat and spice definitely burned my tongue but it was so worth it.  If we hadn't waited until our last day to try this ramen I would've easily been here every day of our stay!

Don't order delivery from this location. DoorDash called to say the order would be delayed because the restaurant didn't have any rice (??). When it finally arrived, both burritos were barely even wrapped and rice was falling out everywhere. Almost no toppings inside. Ordered sofritas and one had almost none, and I think the other had none at all. Got a refund from DoorDash but this place really sucks.
Wanted a cheesesteak while in Philadelphia. Was not disappointed!!! Everything was delicious and the staff was super friendly. Will definitely be back the next time in Philadelphia.

Workers were not wearing their masks correctly or just not wearing them at all. I've seen the guy that runs the desk at el taco. He has zero customer service skills. Pretty rude honestly. The food isn't really good.
First time in Philly, 1st ever cheesesteak.  A lady on the plane told me about Campo's, said it was the best in the city.  Exceeded all expectations.  Staff, delightful!  I'll be back!! So good!!!
Had their cheesesteak at Citizens Bank Park watching a Phillies game. They have their own stand at the ballpark. That was the best cheesesteak I ever had.

We were on a weekend trip from Miami and was looking for a good Ramen spot. We found this place via Yelp. This is a small mom & pop shop...you will near miss it if you don't look carefully! The dining space was empty when we walked in. We were greeted and sat by the server. There was not that much enthusiasm by him, asking us how many. 

One of the first things I noticed when walking in was the "Cash Only" sign and the big ATM machine by the entrance to the place. 

The menu is very limited. However the food was amazing!!! My daughter got the Fried Chicken and she enjoyed it throughly. I got the Vegetable Ramen and every bit of it was quite delicious. The broth was authentic and the noodles were cooked perfectly. 

The only reason I am giving 3 stars to this place is due to the lack-luster customer service of the server. Even though the single server was not rude he did not go out of his way to make us feel welcome. The conversation was very matter of fact, dry, and abrupt. Another reason is due to the "Cash Only" sign and the eye-sore ATM machine within 3 steps of the entrance. 

In this day and age, businesses need to make an effort to have electronic "cloud" payment methods especially now due to Covid-19.

Spice End is known for its kati rolls but I bought a falafel platter and pav bhaji after a night out with friends that left me famished. The pav bhaji appeared appealing but there was way more bhaji (dip) than pav (bread) and the bhaji tasted rather bland in spite of appearance. Friends also believed it seemed "dyed" to appear more red.
The falafel platter was so dry the falafels crumbled as soon as my fork touched them. There was barely any white or hot sauce and after consuming the platter my stomach felt unsettled the entire day. Would not return.
Cheese steak was great! Service was fast. Bring cash, they charge a $1 service fee for credit cards (eye roll)

Our server at Parc told us about this jewel of a place, Campo's Philly Cheesesteak in Old City Philadelphia. Wow! What a great recommendation. I tried the "Works," a traditional ribeye steak with sweet bell peppers, fried onions and provolone cheese (I omitted the mushrooms).  Truly the best I've ever had. The Campo's daughter Mia was at the register multitasking as the greeter and order-taker extraordinaire. Every order ended with "would you like to try some potato, macaroni or cole slaw? My mom makes them! Oh and the rice pudding too!" Don't mind if I do...and I'm so glad I did!!! 

My only regret is that I didn't go back for one more visit before leaving town. I will be back!

Pretty good, portions are small so ask for double noodle. As for the broth... it was pretty good but Terakawa is better. I've been trying to find a place that's equal or better and haven't found that yet.

This Wendy's is absolutely awful. In today's delivery, all of our drinks were missing, two of our Dave's doubles were singles, there were no tomatoes in any of our sandwiches, and one of the burgers was burnt and hard as a rock. In addition, the people who work here are so rude and don't care about doing a good job. Avoid this location.

2 stars for overpriced regular sandwiches + credit card fees, 4 stars for having a good gluten free cheesesteak. But seriously, this is the only place I have EVER been to that will still charge you an extra DOLLAR for paying with your credit card even when you spend $25+ on two sandwiches. Kind-of ridiculous during COVID, especially considering how dirty cash is and you should really be encouraging cleaner payment methods to keep everyone (including your employees) safe.

I'd give this place a zero if it was an option!!

The workers, except the manager/lead, have the worst attitude. I've been to SOOOOO many chipotle and this is THE ONLY location that doesn't know how to double wrap a burrito. The two tortillas are supposed to be overlapped! Then she had the audacity to say IT IS double wrap. Little girl, you need to watch your fuckn tone. If you're going to talk back, at least get the fact straight. 1/4-almost 1/2 of the burrito was exposed, she still tried to foil wrap it. Obviously she doesn't know shit. The whole transaction was very frustrating. However, the manager did give us a refund on the burrito because we no longer want that trash the little girl "wrapped". Even after she foil wrapped it, the burrito was still exposed. Smfh. Isn't common sense to wrap the whole entire burrito & it's filling completely? I guess you can't fix stupid. Also, they give the tiniest portion of everything. A pinch of meat, a pinch of lettuce. I'm a grown woman, I'm not ordering this to feed a baby! We love chipotle but ended up leaving extremely unsatisfied. Chipotle in the west coast is definitely a thousand times better!

Philly was a pleasure to visit a beautiful city, I was Lil disappointed with the food, Bread was not warm, meat was not the best quality, small place, So if you are in a big group this may not be the place for you. Was not worth the $$$$   Philly is known for the best Philly Cheesesteaks sorry but Campos did not deliver that! Maybe it was due to being very very busy. It was Cash Only and not an ATM on-site so that was also an inconvenience.

Manager was completely rude and caught an attitude for asking for a biscuit. Cashier rushing and sucking teeth before order even started. Really poor customer service. Wouldn't recommend anyone to come here unless using the drive through.

The food isn't even for me! The last three time I've come to this location with a one week period. They are never operable. There's always some kind of weird excuse like the systems are down or we're only taking mobile orders or we don't have any food!!! 
This causes the other location to be twice as crowded and twice as slow

CASH ONLY!! Don't worry they do have an ATM on site. This is a super small and crowded place. Service is friendly, quick, and efficient. They have a variety of sandwiches. I love how you can watch the chef grilling meats/veggies and preparing sandwich's right in front of you. 

I got the "works" Philly cheesesteak which has shrooms, bell peppers, and onion. It was served very hot, it tasted good (slightly bland), and the bread was fresh. If I came again, I would substitute reg provolone for the sharp provolone(+$1). I think this would have added a little more flavor to my sandwich. Make sure to grab a local beer to help wash down your tasty food. I wouldn't be opposed to coming back, but I would rather try out different cheesesteak places to compare them.

Hands down Best Cheesesteak in Philadelphia. I'm a Philly native-born & raised and I eat cheesesteaks at least once a week. I do eat other cheesesteaks but Campo's is definitely my favorite. If I had to pick "who's the best"... I wouldn't hesitate to say Campo's followed by John's, Pat's, Jim's & Geno's.

This is what's being served at this McDonalds... this pic is from an hour ago!
Please be more respectful of what is being served to your customer.
Breakfast mold sandwich"

I love the inside with the exposed brick and old school Philly feel. Very unassuming but the food was decent. I would have given a higher rating if my canteen was refilled. Unfortunately, the response was that I had to buy a plastic water bottle. No thank you.

I want to thank the staff at this location for fulfilling the Thank You meal to my nurse wife. They were very kind and expressed generous appreciation to her- we were not expecting such a great experience. Additionally, the staff from the pay counter to the food counter were being extra careful in handling the money/food and taking the precautions needed to keep us and themselves safe. Thanks again!

I've been trying to find a good vegetarian cheesesteak for the past few months since moving to Philly, and so far really haven't liked any. That all changed a few days ago when I tried Campo's Impossible Cheesesteak -- delicious! I got it with American AND Whiz (couldn't decide so... why not both?!), grilled onions and mushrooms on a seeded roll. It was fantastic and tastes pretty darn close to the real thing if you're looking for a meatless alternative. They also have vegan versions available. 
Covid precautions in place make pickup very easy. They have the front window wide open so you just walk up and tell them your name and they'll pass the order out the window. I used credit card and was charged a very small card fee (understandable) because I was told they're normally cash-only, so keep that in mind once things reopen. The father and daughter running the place were both very nice and helpful on the phone and in person!
Very good sandwich. The combination of vegan meat and provolone cheese was to die for!!!!! Worth the incredibly long line, which moved fairly quickly.

Best Cheesesteaks in Philly! They use premium meat, the freshest rolls and fresh onions. Everyone working is friendly and helpful. The restaurant is clean with a charming decor. I highly, highly recommend Campos! Chrisbr

First off, cash only establishment, not a bad thing but you should know. Theh have a general use atm onsite. Gluten free buns brought me here because I wanted a Philly cheesesteak while visiting. While the sandwich was OK the bun was a hamburger bun, not the type of bun that a cheesesteak goes on. There are gluten free buns available that resemble the authentic cheeses, if they had that this review would've been higher.

Stopped by here before we left for the airport and I'm so glad we did! This tiny restaurant only takes cash and has limited seating. Me and 4 friends packed around this small table and we all ordered the lunch special which was a STEAL we got an app, salad, and ramen for $13! Everything was amazing, the dumplings, edamame, and all the different ramens we ordered were great too! I got the chili bomb to add to my ramen and it made a huge difference in flavor and I added the spices on the table as well. I like my ramen spicy and this did it for me! I recommend this place to anyone who stops by Philly. It's clean and affordable for big portions!

I have tried ordering from them 4 times and have only gotten my good once. It was either canceled because they were too busy or it never came and I had to demand a refund. The staff is rude and I would suggest no one bother trying to order from them. Just got something else.
Love this spot.  Great steaks and hogies.  A great family run Philly steak shop!
Sliced right off the rib eye to order. Liscios bread makes a great cheesesteak. A good old fashioned sandwich place.

So very underwhelming. I pass here often so I decided to give it a try. I ordered a chicken cheesesteak. The turnaround was fast, unfortunately for $11 it was small. I ordered the sandwich with onions and peppers, both very scarce, like 2 slices of peppers per half. The hot and sweet pepper fixings are available upon request and given out sparingly. No water for the dining area, so I got a club soda, only one size.. all in all it tasted pretty good, melted American on a chicken cheese is always delicious but honestly nothing special.. I'm still hungry

Absolutely love this place. If you are looking for real authentic philly subs (that's what I call them) than look no further. Plus, the staff is an absolute dream. I've known this family for over 20 years. They are the best in the business. I highly recommend Campo's. Enjoy!

Going around Philly and wanting to try a different establishment's cheesesteak, a stumbled upon Campo's Deli to give this place a try.

Campo's Deli is not a particularly large place, and it is more of a simple and straight to the point place.  There was a line when I was there but it moves pretty quick.  I opted to try their Cheesesteak with sharp Provolone.  This sandwich definitely tastes different as well, as they use more of a softer bread for it.  After having the cheesesteak, I realized that I was not a fan of the softer, thinner bread, as it makes the sandwich soggy pretty quick after it is sitting for a few minutes.  The steak itself in the sandwich was not bad but it did not taste anything special.

I was also able to try their cannoli, which is homemade and made to order.  This was good!  It's hard to explain but you can definitely taste the fact it was made fresh.  The freshness comes at a price of $4 though.

Overall this is a decent experience and you should try this cheesesteak if softer bread is your style.

FYI: Campo's Deli is CASH ONLY.

Amazing! What a experience. The restaurant is a little hidden gem in the city, the restaurant name isn't shown in the front, but rather, there are Japanese words for the storefront. Felt authentic. The food was delicious too. 100/10 will come back soon. Loved the octopus & I'm glad they had melon creamy soda, reminded me of my childhood! The gates of hell ramen isn't spicy at all, & honestly, I think I prefer Terakawa's ramen. However, the ramen was still delicious. Great environment. They only accept cash, but there's an ATM locates inside the restaurant. Small menu, but quality dishes

My Favorite Ramen in the city so far. I have written reviews previously on how to score a good ramen dish and the number one aspect in my opinion is how are the Ramen noodles (not too hard, not too soft, cooked obviously etc.) These noodles came in with a solid A and I only hope upon return visits they are this good! 

Secondly, how is the broth? I ordered the Gates of Hell Ramen and yes this was spicy but I want to say maybe a six out of ten on the spice level so you can enjoy all the items in the soup, which is my last criteria when judging a good ramen soup - the items selected or added to the ramen and broth. 

Added items- Berkshire tonkotsu broth with intense chili oil, pork belly chashu, bamboo, egg. What I will say about the ingredients is the bamboo of all items had the highest score for me as the bamboo was more delectable then the bamboo I eat on occasion. I was taken aback by it and must know now what else is hidden in Chinatown and the surrounding area as there must be other items I have not stumbled upon that are unique and this delish. The pork belly had some fat in it but to my understanding alot of people actually like the fat in it and to that I say, hey to each their own.

Hold up wait a minute! These are not only the words from a Bone Thugs and Harmony song but you really do need to take pause and read what I'm about to knowledge drop...two words....Yaki-Gyoza. These are the best Gyoza I have ever consumed! They are small relative to all the other Gyoza I have ordered in other restaurants however these have a healthy taste to them and are prepared with ample heathly embellishments underneath the six pieces that are to each order, it may be less but from now on I will always be ordering two orders of this appetizer.

I can't wait to come back and try some of there other items and highly recommend you seek this place out if you are looking for some top notch Ramen and Gyoza of your dreams!

As always people SYOY!!

Awful. Order took forever because they simply didn't care. It wasn't the driver's fault. They told me  what I've seen in person...a bunch of lazy people with orders they didn't care about. Had to cancel, which screws over the driver. 

Same happened at the other BK on Columbus. Maybe it's the pandemic, but other burger places have adjusted. These BKs are just crap. Even if you do get your food eventually, it's cold and disgusting. Honestly, I do like a whopper, but I suggest avoiding all local BK's until they get their act together. Too bad.

The manager on duty was very unprofessional.... staff messed up my whole order, no utensils or napkins in the bag..... when I got home I find out they charged my debit card twice.... and not sense ring the phone..... HORRIBLE Establishment!!!

This was yet the best authentic Philly CheeseSteak Sandwich we have ever had.  we loved this place, it felt as if we were with family.  The place has great character, great ambiance and conveniently located on Market Street.  We had a great weekend in Philly and ending with the best Philly Cheesesteak Sandwich, made our weekend even more special.

Pretty good when you consider its a hospital cafeteria. The salmon with rice with the sushi is always good. Salad bar is solid. Grill is excellent try the omelets or the blueberry pancakes for breakfast!

CAMPOS 
Great sandwiches from the cheese steak to the chicken Valentine, banging ass hoagies with the mama mia and the italian special, chicken salad is on time along with the long line of fresh salads. Home made meatballs, pasta dishes, all sandwiches can be served with pasta or salad.  Home made ceaser dressing, aged sharpe provalone right on site.  Sit, have a beer while you wait , enjoy your meal as you observe philadelphia in one of its busiest areas it has to  offer. 
Campos is a must eat spot in Philadelphia. Its not better than the best because it is the best. 
Dont forget to clean up your table when you are finished. Lol.

Zero stars if I could. Absolutely no flavor and bland calzone. Not even the ingredients couldn't make this heated cardboard taste any good. The dough and sauce just.... can't even describe the tasteless thing this place calls a calzone.

Great family-owned cheesesteak shop in the heart of Old City and just steps from Independence Hall, the Museum of the American Revolution and other great historic Philadelphia landmarks and experiences.

As for Campo's itself -- love the cheesesteak (I had the works with peppers and mushrooms). Bread is soft, beef is perfectly cooked, veggies are grilled nicely. Just all around an enjoyable cheesesteak and maybe one of the most underrated in the city.

Also worth noting: they have a vegetarian cheesesteak as well, which is not the easiest thing to find in the city and worth exploring for those who don't eat meat.

PRO TIP: They offer an at-home cheesesteak kit, so you can make your own cheesesteak on your time in the comfort of your home! Apparently you can also ship their sandwiches nationwide, so I'm keeping that in mind for some upcoming gifts...

If you're going to a taco bell, there are not that many reasons to be mad. Upon arrival, I expect to be provided with some form of the slightly questionable comfort food I've grow to love (complete with nacho cheese goodness) and this taco bell delivers!

A relatively new addition to 30th street station, this can be found (alongside its partner pizza hut) near the "Little Market Street" entrance to 30th street. Service is generally quick (~5 minutes from ordering to food-in-hand, depending on the crowd) and is very clean. Plenty of space to sit at one of the tables to devour your cheesy goodness.

Complaints? Very few. One notable new policy is that they don't give any courtesy cups for water anymore. If you need some water to complement your salty treats, be prepared to shell out ~$3 for a bottle. Hours are also limited so plan ahead.

I stopped by for a quick meal on my lunch break. 1st let me say the management nor staff understands the meaning of "Customer Service" My Order was completely wrong. They gave me dark meat, I order white meat. They gave me rice & gravy, yet I order Mashed potatoes & gravy. Last but not least I was over charged on my bank card for the order. I Take blame for not double checking my order before heading back to work. I rather take the extra 5 minute drive & head over to the Popeyes on 7500 City Ave. You guys need to do better !!!

Horrible customer service. Asked the female working behind the counter a question and she just showed attitude and didn't respond. Absolute garbage attitude. Overheard them talking about customers while they where getting food. Garbage standards and would tell everyone to stay away from this specific one. Management team should definitely read these reviews because it does not live up to the Chick-Fil-A standard of customer service and the employees are extremely disrespectful and Ignorant. Was definitely not " my pleasure "

I ordered online for a group of ten. I was extremely embarrassed that they only gave me 5 sandwiches cut in half except one was in thirds. Look at the picture on the website of what I ordered and compare it to what I got. I called the shop back and they told me that one of the sandwiches was cut in three to fill in the space and that everything was correct. I had pre-ordered more for the next day which I promptly canceled. The next day they tried to charge my credit card for the 20 sandwiches. When luckily my credit card company asked me if it was a fraudulent charge I agreed it was. Potbelly then called to ask if I REALLY wanted to cancel. This place is supposed to be a franchise.  Yikes!  They need help.  Avoid this place at all costs!
Great food and loved their vegan cheesesteak:)  I missed Philly since I've moved but come back for their food and this place!
this is consistently the worst, slooooooooooowest, coldest food not even just Wendy's but fast food place I've ever been. You will wait 45 minutes every single time.

Loved it! Got the Porfilio ramen and it was delicious, noodles and egg and meat were all cooked just right. Waiter was nice. Sign on the wall had their weekday special -- pretty sure it was $15 for ramen and small salad and appetizer, seems like a pretty good deal, will probably go back and try that one. Place isn't crazy big but there's smaller tables in the front and then larger tables in the back hallway area for bigger groups. My friend and I sat kinda squished into the front corner at a little table right by the window, which was fun for us but might be a little uncomfortable for others. Overall delicious and filling, absolutely zero complaints.

P.S. It's cash only but there's an atm in the front; I didn't use it so I don't know what the fees are.

This Wendy's was good but apparently its not worth coming back until the new 2019summer staff is fired. Its 10:14am and i just got back from ordering food twice and never receiving food, thanks for wasting my time. The last time i was here i watched a young girl drop unwrapped food on the ground and bag it and the time before i overheard the drive through window operator scolding the cooks forcing them to wash there hands after using the restroom, after being asked to wait for 32mins i was given cold overcooked food that was not even correct to my order, the next time you want me to pull forward the answer is no. I will not come back to this location until you go out of your way to prove this has been addressed; furthermore i will be notifying Wendy's corporate about these incidents.
I want to point out before the new staff was hired this shit did not happen, the late night staff mixed orders up but mostly they would just forget to take lettus off or something inconsequential, and the quality was normally fair, this location likes to serve old food thats been sitting out who knowes how long if you order late at night, if they actually made it the way there supposed to it was good, but because i have had to come back around and tell you i need food made to order or my money back i can only give you a fair rating on previous employe preference. The new employees in addition to lacking a service standard have no quality standards. If you ever want me to spend another penny at this location, figure out how to prove to me you have addressed this. I strongly recommend you take the drive to the neshaminy location within the Walmart parking lot if it is within their hours the quality and service standards at the neshaminy location have been good if not excellent on my visits.

I'm not one for ball park food: A) it's way overpriced B) the lines are ridiculous and C) the food is usually mediocre at best. Well while watching the Phillies be absolutely destroyed by the Mets (seriously boys, what's goin' on?), I couldn't help but notice my seat mate's food, a Campo's cheesesteak to be exact. After another home run by the Mets, I thought to myself the food can't be any worse than the game. 

So we made are way down to Campo's and as expected, there was a long line. But it wasn't as bad as I thought, I was surprisingly entertained by other game goers and interested in how they order their cheesesteaks. How do I order mine? American, onions, and sweet peppers with a sprite please. This totaled $16, a bit steep as expected but you can pay by card at the ball park and my sprite came in a snazzy phanatic souvenir cup. 

After a few squirts of ketchup, I was ready to dig in. Have I mentioned yet I'm not a big cheesesteak fan? Born and raised in the suburbs of Philadelphia and I've had them all Pat's, Geno's, Steve's and I would always honor my own mother with the best cheesesteak award however Campo's comes close. Yummy, well cut goodness not greasy or sloppy and dressed with cheese perfectly! Not to mention these things are ready for you in the blink of an eye.

Next time you're at Citizen's Bank Park, I recommend stopping at Campos!

I don't get it.  It's good - but that ain't ribeye.  Personally don't like soft roll's.  Sonny's seemed to have more of the italian bread with a nice crust as we walked by.  Nice staff, but I don't know.....I'm going to keep looking.

I've tried a lot of ramen places, I would say Hiro has average ramen. I came here with my boyfriend late on a Sunday night and it was not busy, but our two bowls of ramen took a while. My bf ordered Gates Of Hell and I ordered Chicken Soy. The chicken soy honestly tasted like watered down soy sauce. Both of us prefer Terakawa.

Was walking in the center city during lunch and decided to try this place. I got seated right away and the server was very attentive. So I looked at the menu and it's not that much.. They told me they are new owners and still finalizing the menu.. So okay... I saw the lunch special they have $12.. A bowl of ramen(I took the Hiro heaven special), a side (I took gyoza), and a salad.. That's great for the price! The ramen was different.. It's a little fatty, not sure why.. maybe that's what the special ramen broth is.. but it wasn't bad, it was flavorful. The servings were generous! The bowl was full of noodles, a boiled egg, huge cut of pork belly, and mushrooms.. The gyoza was 3 pieces, nothing special on the taste.. The salad I liked.. They do good plating in this place btw..

I'll try different ramen on the menu next time and see if I can change the current rating
If you're looking for one of the best Philly cheesesteaks you've come to the right place. Campo's is fire!!

Delicious authentic Philiy cheese steak...
Flavorful and bold tasting.
Cannot find another tasteful version of this very unique traditional iconic sandwich!@

Excellent.  Excellent cheesesteaks.
I had the Italian (Sharp Prov and Broc. Rabe) and added mushrooms - $.75.
My friend had "The Works"/

About $11 a pop - but huges and delicious and NOT dripping with grease.

Crowded and cramped to eat there - but so. worth. it.
Teeming with tourists - NATCH.

CASH ONLY  (ATM on site)

I love this ramen house, so close and in center City! While many will tell you Terakawa ramen is THE GO TO ramen place in Philly, I do believe Hiro is up there in that same discussion. Especially recently with Terakawa having wait times of up to an hour, Hiro serves as a great alternative, I've always been able to be seated rather quickly. The ambiance is dim lit and the table and bar seating are very reminiscent of many local ramen shops in Japan. 

On to the food. Hiro has very good takoyaki, with the proper melt in your mouth feel upon eating. The sauces are perfect and the takoyaki balls themselves are nice and round, which are an important part of the food itself. Would highly recommend getting them when you come visit, even if you're here for the ramen. 

I really love the gates of hell ramen here. The spicy flavors of the broth really punctuate the whole experience, and you can add additional spice bombs into the broth if you are looking for more spice. The pork is delicious as well in the broth. Really is the perfect place to stop in during the cold weather to warm up as you're walking through downtown Philadelphia.

I didn't enjoy the food from here.  Ordered a sandwich and received what tasted like old chicken and was dry.  The broccoli soup was okay it just needed some salt and pepper. The best part of my order was the chocolate chip cookie which I'm sure was premade.
KING of the best soups, especially pasta fagioli. Roast pork Italian Stromboli is the GOAT. There's a reason they've been around forever.....bc they make delicious food!!!

DISGUSTING

These mfs left a got damn hair in my nugget. worst service and probably the worst tasting chic fil a i've ever been to. FIND SOMEWHERE ELSE

Great service. Fast. So flavorful, hearty, filling. Big portions. Immediate seating. It's not a big restaurant but I love the cozy feel. Ramen quality was amazing and hit the spot on a cold rainy day. 

The chicken was amazing. So fresh, crispy, and hot. And it was not too salty, just the perfect amount of seasoning. I would most definitely go back to this place. 

Heads up, they only take cash!

Good tasting sandwiches but over priced. Tried the classic Philly cheese steak and chicken Philly with a water and spent $33. The taste of both sandwiches was incredible. However, for that price point, the sandwiches are thin on protein and small in size. I think competitors have better prices and better sizes. Campo's is a great option If you're not expecting a big sandwich.

We came to Campo's because we were in the touristy part of town and wanted a cheesesteak.  I had been to Sonny's once on a previous trip and really liked it but 1) there was a line out the door and no seats available and 2) I needed something new to Yelp about!  Campo's did not have a line at the time but people did start flowing in soon.

The ladyfriend and I got a cheesesteak with onions and provolone and when I went to pay the cashier said " Oh sorry it's cash only".  If there was a sign on the front door then I missed it.  It's 2018, get a damn credit card machine, charge an extra quarter per sammich and get with the times.  You get tourist business and tourists don't like carrying cash.  This detail is an automatic minus 1 star for me. 

The cheesesteaks came out and they were decent.  The cheese was only on half the sammich which can be seen from the picture I posted and the meat was dried out in parts.  The bread was hot and slightly toasted which was a nice feature and the people were pretty friendly.  

I wouldn't come back because I wasn't wowed and I don't want to go out of my way to get cash out of the bank for a sandwich.  Can you tell that part bugs me?
4 stars for a simple, killer cheesesteak. Additional 5th star for the roll.  Dont know who their bakery of choice is, but they chose...wisely.  Great, great cheesesteak.

My girlfriend and I stopped by Campo's after the St. Patrick's Day Parade. We were just looking for something quick and warm. I've had Campo's cheesesteaks before at Phillies games but never really paid attention to the quality.

I had a cheesesteak with whiz and my girlfriend had the pizza steak. The steak wasn't as finely chopped as much as we'd like and was fairly gristly. The sandwiches were oily and don't compare to the many other great cheesesteak options in the city.

The restaurant is very small and has small tables to sit at. It is cash only which is kind of annoying, but there is an ATM at the entrance with a $1.50 fee.

I'm a small ramen place but service was great.

Takoyaki has chunks of octopus. It's not dry with sauce. I think they put too much sauce. Next time I will ask to put it on the side.

Pork gyoza: it's small with thin dough but the meat is tender and it just melts in your mouth.

Salad is small, nice presentation with enough refreshing dressing.

My husband enjoyed his ramen

Staff can be a bit clownish with an attitude at night shells are always stale and you will find yourself waiting a long time. Gone in during the day difference between day and night. if you plan on eating here may I advise you only eat there during the day and eat in otherwise save your money and go to the one on aramingo avenue service never disappoints
Not bad. Especially when you're hungry. I did think it was a little skinny and needed a tad bit more seasoning, I ended up adding ketchup and it was a lot better.

I had a Campo's cheesesteak at the park and I really liked it. For stadium food it wasn't too expensive and I thought it was really good. I imagine the hardcore cheesesteak fans give it hell, but I enjoyed it. The service isn't bad either, considering how long the lines get. Just be ready with your order and don't make other wait and enjoy a nice ball park Philly cheesesteak.

We live in Texas and miss the wonderful food of Philly.  We order at least once a year to be delivered here from Campo's.   Always happy to have an authentic cheesesteak sandwich with wiz and onions!  The Italian  hoagies are just as delicious with provolone.  Always fresh and delicious!

Oh.My.Gosh!! If you are wanting an authentic Philly cheesesteak then check out Campos!! They do have indoor as well as outdoor dining available and sanitizer at the register. 
Their sandwiches are good sized but trust me, you will eat it up!! They do have options of chicken, steak or vegan but go all out. Get steak and have them load it up with cheez wiz!

This little cash only (there's an ATM in front) restaurant was a wonderful find. We got there about 1:00 for lunch and had the $14 lunch combination: house salad, gyoza or karaage, and choice of ramen. Service was excellent and everything was delicious. 

We use the the #45 bus for about 80% of our transportation needs and this place couldn't be more convenient whenever we need to come into Center City.

I try my best to give places multiple times, and as a customer I should not have to do that. Every time I do a late night snack the service is bad it's like they just here because they have no choice. They never sound enthusiastic I say thank you multiple times and never hear good gestures come from them. Also when ordering they never turn the mic off so you hear everything they are saying and it's just inappropriate they really need to reevaluate business and hire people that are going to get the job done with a smile no matter what time

If I had to sum up Campo's with one word, it would be: Meh... Now, its not bad, and would be close to great in any other city. But in Philly, where there is an astonishing amount of fantastic sandwich places, average just won't cut it. and that's what Campo's is, average for Philadelphia. 

The place is clean and comfortable for a deli and the location is great. The bread is just above average (always order the seeded roll). The deli meat here is standard, but the sandwich selection is surprisingly good. I have had the roast pork here and it is juicy and the cheesesteaks will satisfy, but neither are something I would go out of my way to get. All is well until you realize how over priced your meal just was for what you got. Example: A Philly stable is sharp provolone. Now you go to a great deli like Sarcone's and there are small bricks of it lining your entire sandwich. But at Campo's? They charge you $1.50 to crumble some on top? REALLY?!?! I mean come on... I would also recommend the balsamic vinegar on any deli style sandwich, it is really tasty (but they are going to charge you a $1 for that too).

And while you are there, look around. I understand its the area, but 8 out of 10 are tourists. There is a reason, because locals aren't traveling out of their way to go here. Another crime is to call this place a "cheessesteak place." This is not a "cheesesteak place" no matter how hard the purveyors of this establishment try to market themselves. This is a deli that serves cheesesteaks. If you are looking for a real cheesesteak experience, I recommend you go elsewhere. If you are hungry and in the area, then stop in, you could certainly do worse. As far as the rudeness, you will find that at most Philly lunch spots. People in this city are bitter, being bitter is a way of life here, its part of the experience.

this place is cozy and cute. go for lunch from 11-3, their $13 deal is a ton of food (a salad, one app, and a ramen bowl) and will definitely fill you up. been here a couple times and the last time i went i got the Porfilio ramen, it had just the right about of spice and flavor. for my app i got the fried chicken and its three small pieces but really crunchy and good. the sauce it comes with is also really tasty - some kind of spicy mayo. the salad that comes with the meal is also so good!! it uses the basic ginger dressing they use at most sushi places, but they add some crunchy pieces to the stop and it was a great starter to the meal. overall real satisfied, and i even took some of my ramen bowl to go because i was stuffed. 

definitely a go to on a cold day!!
Fuck this place I order on DoorDash send me a whole different order with the receipt with my order with some busted open fucking dipping sauce hope this bitch burns down

avoid this place, even if it is the only place open. 

bathrooms don't work, service is terrible, food
Is terrible and the seating is LITERALLY cardboard looking chairs. 


just don't go.
The problem from what i could smell...the people cooking, taking my money and passing me my horrible food, were smoking weed. I will never be going back to this establishment.

This place is atrocious. The cashier was either on drugs or drunk because she kept slurring her words and talking to herself, got the entire order wrong, told us we couldn't get a side of cheese, everything was ice cold and the cheese wasn't even melted. Quesadilla wasn't cut, Anything that has shredded cheese in it wasn't even melted. In Somethings they forgot cheese and others had chicken in it when it shouldn't have. Everyone working there is dumb as fuck. I just recently moved to the area and it makes me miss my old taco bell at home. I've never experienced something so awful and full of stupid fucking people. Disgrace.

I hope your mouth is watering...so you have enough saliva to wash down this dry cheesesteak. 
Tried The Works, Pizza Sauce, and Maggie's cheesesteaks. None of them were good. Size is smaller than other cheesesteak places, meat is dry, and there's barely any cheese. 
Highly recommend you not to come here for cheesesteaks and literally go anywhere else. Anywhere. Really.

If you like standalone Chick Fil A, well, this place is nothing like that. Food is soggy and has been sitting under heat lamps a while. Service is spotty. Sometimes there is a huge line when there really shouldn't be. They can be stingy on the sauces and try to get you to pay extra for more sauce, no matter how much food you buy.

So good! I got the "inch of heaven" ramen but subbed egg for the pork belly. (The vegetarian one was too much vegetable, I was looking for a something simpler but they do have a vegetarian option). The broth was delicious as was the rest of it. Nice server and liked the atmosphere. They're cash only, FYI. Really liked it, def recommend.

I love ramen and my search brought me to this place. It's a quaint little place right next to Milk-Boy. Usually it isn't too crowded and they have the interior set up with booths and a Japanese-esque counter. I have to say this is one of the best places in the city.

First and foremost the noodles were great and cooked to perfection. The broth for Gates of Hell was flavorful and filled with umami. (Only wish it was spicier, but that's just me) The egg was well marinated. So far the best marinated egg I've tried.
The pork belly melts in your mouth, bursting forth with flavor.

My friend got the vegetable ramen. Presentation is a delight to the eyes. The assorted vegetables melded well with each other and cooked properly. The flavor of the broth is very delicate and light. For some people it might be too light. So for those that eat chicken I would recommend getting the Fried Chicken and add some to the vegetable ramen.

The fried chicken is a dark meat fatty chicken. The crispy shell gives way to a juicy soft chicken that is well balanced and isn't overpowering. Perfect combination with the vegetable ramen.

The Tako-Yaki was alright. The inside was a bit underdone, but still edible. For those that aren't into soft textures or a slight slime like texture I wouldn't recommend it.

Overall the price is reasonable, the food taste as good as it looks, and the setting is relaxing. Defiantly one of the best locations to eat some good ramen to fill you up.

Ok so I went back due to the location being so close. This time around shells weren't stale employees seemed professional. Wait time was a bit longer than I would've liked. Despite it being slow. However an improvement. Keep it up!
The best if the best! Great steak sandwiches!! Large menu family run business. Mike is the best!!

I like this place, little corner pizza shop that serves wing, soup, cheese steaks, salads & etc.
The wings are good, sauce on the side so they arent soggy. Pizza is good. No complaints, orders are on time, quick service, your in & out. Staff has always been nice, friendly and remember me when I come back. 
No kids or drug dealers hanging out on the corner, so I can walk in and out with out feeling like I'm gonna get jumped. 
Overall, 5 stars!

I honestly do not understand why Hiro Ramen is rated so high. It's like the baseline for ramen is Maruchan or Shin Ramen by a lot of the reviews I've read. 

The broth is not great, probably not even that good. What I expect from a good tonkatsu is a broth that has a noticeable pork flavor. Instead, what I tasted was giant spoonfuls of MSG. The pork, although very tender, did not have much flavor. The noodles were OK. One thing that was really good was the soft-boiled egg which was perfectly done.

The takoyaki was good but I think you can find better takoyaki in Chinatown. The other appetizers are also pretty average but my review is morely based on the over-rated ramen.

The service was really great and the staff was friendly. This place is cash only btw. I did get my appetizer (takoyaki) slightly after I was served ramen but it was not a huge deal in retrospect. The ramen was served very fast and the takoyaki needed more time to prepare.
MASSIVE  cockroach in my salad mixed in with my black beans. Disgusting unsanitary location. Stay far away!
Was in the area and thought a cheesesteak would be nice, but this is the worst cheesesteak I've ever had. Meat is super dry, very little cheese, no onions. Wouldn't bother with this place

Came in during a lull in the day. Encountered one of the rudest people on staff ever. Tall slender blonde male. Was in a blue Qdoba shirt and black hat. Regarded me like I was a huge problem and actually *flung* each item I requested into my burrito bowl. Unbelievably bad attitude. I've done food service throughout my college years. That was a decade ago, but I can tell you that having someone with such a shit demeanor dealing with customers makes NO sense. I also taught public high school for several years, so needless to say I am able to let quite a lot of ridiculous Behavior roll off my back... Even consider  reasons why someone acts out.  But on a Sunday afternoon just making a burrito bowl with someone who is being completely neutral? What the hell did I do to you? If you don't like your job, find another one. Don't take it out on customers who didn't even bat an eye at you The wrong way. The other dude working wasn't so hot, either. It's pretty loud in here between the music and the hum of the kitchen, so I had a little trouble hearing some of his questions. Excuse me... The only pleasant person on staff was the young lady with pink hair. Maybe you ought to bump her up to management and fire the other two since they don't know how to treat people.

Order was correct
Drive thru was in a timely fashion
However this is probably the worst Wendy's burger and chicken nuggets I've ever ate... Burgers were burnt to a god aweful taste.... Chicken nuggets same way too well done.... 

My work partner same rest in same order
Burger way too burnt

If you heard our Peter Tong interview a couple weeks ago you'll remember him mentioning that if a gun was to his head and he had to choose a place to eat in Philly, then Hiro Ramen House would be that place.
