Therefore tonight, despite lightning and heavy rain, Courtney and I made our way to try it out like I promised. We were definitely not disappointed.

So first off, this place is kind of a hole in the wall on Chestnut St., but when you walk in you're transported to this stylish, wood-walled eatery with tons of class. The walls really give you a Japanese vibe and set the tone.

We tried the Black Pig: Berkshire pork tonkotsu broth, pork belly chashu, bamboo, roasted garlic oil and naruto. I got the extra marinated egg because of course I did. Courtney got the Pig and Miso: Berkshire pork tonkotsu broth and miso, pork belly chashu, bamboo and corn. Hands down the best ramen I've had and I thank my man Peter from the bottom of my heart. The broth is oh so flavorful and the pork belly was perfectly tender and rich/savory. The ramen was cooked perfectly as well. The love just oozes out of it and onto your taste buds. It don't get no betta'.

I'd be remiss if I didn't mention our appetizer. We ordered the Karaage Fried Chicken: free range chicken marinated in soy garlic and ginger. These juicy chicken bites were off the hook. Super juicy and packed with flavor. The perfect meaty accompaniment to our main courses. Pure poultry bliss.

Hiro Ramen House in Philly. Check it out. Right now.
Amazing ramen house for the Philly area. The restaurant is cash only and traditional Asian service. The ramen and ingredients are amazing. The pricing is good.

Food cold. Ordered provolone got 3/4 wiz and a slight piece of provolone dangling. $4 bag of chips (5 cent bag) were stale. Drink girls were confused and I don't think they knew what they were suppose to be doing. 
Sum it up...SUCKED. 
No wonder the line was short!

Doesn't look like much on the outside and it's pretty small inside but the reviews tell you to come! So I did and I was so happy I did! 

I got the $14 lunch special, which is a great deal if considering the ramen would be $11 by itself. So add a salad and an appetizer for three more dollars and it's a great deal!

I actually went in ordering the ramen. Then realized I needed to add the salad and the appetizer so I ordered those after the ramen. Everything came out as it was ready so the ramen first then the salad then the appetizer, which was fine since that's the way I ordered it.

Everything was hot and fresh and delicious! But don't forget your cash because they don't take plastic.

Food was fresh, service was excellent. Atmosphere was good and we didn't feel rushed. We each had seaweed salad, wife had gyoza and I had takoyaki. Hard to find takoyaki and this was worth the wait. Gyoza was perfect.

Clean Subway with a well-maintained dining room, friendly staff, fully stocked and to spec toppings list, and some ever-important attention to detail.

I discovered this Subway by accident when I overshot starbucks on a telephone call.

They have $3 subs each day and the special of the day varies.

Unlike other US locations, this south philly location has sweet peppers. Also cucumbers and some other nice fresh surprises.

In LA, they have avocados and cilantro.  South philly has different cheeses and peppers. Yaay subway.

This place has been called a tourist trap. It is a short walk from the historical sights, but what is wrong with being one of the more convenient places in the area for visitors to grab a decent lunch?
I have only tried a few of the many cheesesteak places in Philadelphia. Geno's was nothing special, it's the McDonald's of cheesesteaks. I couldn't deal with the line at Pat's, Tony Luke, Jr.'s couldn't even get my order correct, and Jim's on South St. basically sux. Read my review of Jim's if you care what I think.
I have eaten at Campo's several times. I like the fact that the cheesesteak was cooked to order, and that it was served piping hot. The whiz  was messy, and dripped down my fingers. Yum. The crusty roll was fantastic.
I'll still search for the best cheesesteak in Philadelphia, but for now, Campo's tops my list.

Recommend 100%
D E L I C I O U S!!!!!!!!
Chicken,  beef and impossible burger meat. Satisfies every craving. I absolutely love this place, the cheesesteaks are so good. Had to go back to back 2 days in a row.

If you are at the game do not eat here. I ordered a cheesesteak with American cheese. She took the role and put two pieces of cheese on the bottom.  Then she opens up this aluminum serving pan with a bunch of meat inside and just puts it on the bun like we were in a school cafeteria. It tasted like pure Steak-ums. The sandwich was small and overpriced as well.

Super smooth and flavorful broth with mild meat flavor that is not in your face. The pork is tender, a little smokey, and charred perfectly.

I ordered the Porfolio and really enjoyed it. The lemon added an interesting, slightly tart dimension to the soup.

My wife and I were spending the Holidays in Philadelphia,  my hometown.   Normally, 
we do not go to sandwich shops as my wife suffers from Celiacs.  Campos was a Godsend.  I was able to get a delicious pizza steak, while my wife had a gluten free deli sandwich. We both enjoyed our meal immensely without compromise.   We will always return to Campos!

My SO and I went to this place very early so that I could get the full experience of the Campos Philly cheesesteak. I am a fan of steaks and of pizza and to put the two together was a fantastic idea. I loved both that we tried. The original and pizza cheesesteak (pictured) and as you can see I am enjoying the very first bite. I am not quite sure why this place has a low rating as the place is clean, the food is good quality and the employees were actually nice here. They have a variety of other things to try as well. Great place. Check out their menu! I was pretty happy we stopped and enjoyed their food.

The service was great, even though we got there before they were about to close they still served us as if they weren't closing at all. The sandwiches are fully loaded and tasted wonderful! I would surely come back.

Seriously.  Do not order take out from here.  I ordered a large pizza and boneless buffalo wings with extra hot sauce (an option they provide) and ended up with a very cold pizza and chicken fingers with maaaaybe a teaspoon of hot sauce sprinkled over 5 for $40.  My friends and I were very very disappointed to say the least.

It grossed me out to see them assemble their pizzas without gloves, but when I witnessed them touching deli meats and cheeses with their bare hands for hoagies, I was disgusted enough to say I will never buy food here again. It didn't help that I also saw the sandwich assembler's ass crack during this process.

If you're not turned off by that, then the pizza is extremely mediocre and the tenders are really good, if you want a review on their food.

I'm bummed because Gray's Ferry is a prepared food desert and I live down the street from Uncle Tomy's. I guess when you have zero competition, it doesn't matter if you cut corners.

Great food. Old school Philly. Great family. Everything you'd want to experience about Philly. They're serving up some great food and it's not just cheesesteaks! They got all the Philly staples. Stop down and grab something from Campo's! I don't have a picture right now, but I will update it when I do.

Two weeks ago we ordered two baconators and both did not contain any bacon. Tonight we tried again and the order was even worse. Although there was some bits of bacon on them, the burgers were dried out, not served hot, and were just horrible. Did not look at all like the photo on the menu board. The fries were cold and rubbery. They were out of baked potatoes on both visits, and out of Dr. Pepper on the most recent visit. This is not the Wendy's I have known years ago... Something is amiss at this location.
Ordered the classic Philly chessestak with provolone... Oh my... Barely any cheese in it and it was the worst Philly cheestake I've ever had... Dry and chewy meat... Very disappointed...

I created an account just to review this restaurant. Cozy atmosphere, super friendly staff, efficient service, tasty food, reasonable prices. Okay, more than tasty. The menu was cute and concise and had a good number of options but not so many that I felt overwhelmed. I was feeling not-very-hungry and so I ordered the house salad. I was amazed by it. Very fresh ingredients. Big enough to be an entree or large appetizer. The ginger-carrot dressing (had sesame in it) was nutty and had just the right amount of bite. I could have drunk a 2-liter of it. The toasted ramen noodles on top were flavorful, smoky, and added a nice crunch to the salad. Date loved the ramen noodles he ordered. GO HERE

Worst place to order I order meal & my straw was missing then my fries so soggy I don't why & when order that time nobody at the drive through or in the store but still these quality service & when I give a call in that location the person says we will give you a refund come to in Store and it was raining so heavy that time but I don't understand why you give me soggy food at the first place and then you saying that I will give you a refund I mean what do you think we're getting free we are paying for that .

Another bad McDonald at philly. Came to pick up a uber eats delivery and it was the longest waist of my time. They take too long on the drive thru and they're rude too. Never again will I accept a delivery  from this location.
LOVE LOVE LOVE!!!! Yum, the best cheesesteaks in Philly. Can't say enough good things about Campo's!

Great, clean, little Subway shop. There's a few tables for dining in the restaurant, which is nice. They're fast and make sure your sandwich is made exactly the way you want. I've never had a bad experience here.

If you are coming from out of  town and want a good cheese steak,  I would skip right over all the other cheese steak places and head for Campo's Philly Cheesesteak. Quality cheesesteak is what I call it! Service is excellent too! Love the neighborhood it just all works when you have a great cheesesteak experience in Philly! Campo's is my #1 cheesesteak.
Great food and Philly atmosphere. Campo's is one of favorite places in the city to get some cheesesteaks.

A venue that was recommended to me, I spent my day walking around Philadelphia and was told I needed to try a genuine Cheesesteak while I was out and about. I went into Campos and tried the Cheesesteak and the Potato Salad. The quality of the food was out of this world, the flavours were unbelievable. If you're around the museums in Philadelphia make sure you stop here for a bite to eat, as it's literally just down the road and located perfectly to get rid of any hunger you may have. I'll be swinging by again next time I'm in the city.
By far one of my FAVORITE spots to grab a bite to eat! If you have yet to eat here, you're missing out. You haven't had an authentic Philly Cheesesteak until you go to Campos.

The veggie melt was weird. Avocado, cheese and raw mushrooms? It's like someone who has no idea what vegetables are came up with this sandwich. Also, was told the potato soup had no meat in it, but when I tried it, it smelled and tasted strongly of bacon. Hubby had the steak sandwich and didn't like it either, it was just luncheon meat (roast beef). However, the chocolate cookie was good, service was also good, and prices were decent enough.

Not wanting to selecting any stars. I was continually cursed at by the employees for asking questions about my overpriced cheesesteak that was small portioned and bad tasting. Do not go here, the employees are definitely proving Philly the angriest city in America. Very disappointed customer.
This place is legit. The owner is super nice and the broth of the ramen is just superb.

Before coming to a Phillies game, I was told that the food in the stadium was bomb. I looked up Campo's menu ahead of time and knew that I needed to get "The Heater" and it was well worth the hype. I love steak, cheese, and spicy and this hit the spot for all three. There was a good amount of steak on the sandwich, the cheese was melty and delicious and the heat level was just right. This was the perfect bite to have while watching the game and I have been craving it ever since. I went to the game for a friends birthday, otherwise I'm not too into baseball but the next time I'm in philly I might go to a game just to get this sandwich again. This cheesesteak was better than one of the others had in town but I'm not sure if that's because it was spicy and was different so I would want to try just a regular cheesesteak to see how it squares up.

This is on the same street as a better known cheesesteak place but that place had a delayed opening for no clear reason, so I wasn't willing to stand around and see when they felt like opening, so to Campo's I went. I appreciate restaurants that are open during posted hours.

There aren't that many tables but when we went it wasn't too crowded. They upcharge for credit card purchases which is unfortunate. I got a classic cheesesteak with provolone. It was piping hot, chock full of meat, and nicely wrapped in paper to keep things nice and neat. It was super filling, but it was best to get my own rather than split to really get that beefy flavor.

The cashier mentioned her mom made the potato salad, and some tables were taken up by catering orders that were taken out. It very much seemed like a family operation. That made it feel better to support the restaurant rather than the better known places. Plus the food was really good!
Two times in a row - within 30 minutes - this location has gotten a simple order wrong. Chicken sandwich ordered .... burger received - twice! What is so hard?

If you are new to Philadelphia and want to have a local cheesesteak then campos is a must go. you will be received by a very humble host and delicious taste all made in Philadelphia. 
10/10
Used their online ordering while we were touring museums, and then simply picked up the sandwiches - easy as pie.  Delicious sandwiches, too, with good quality meat.  The wheat bun was nice, too.

I ordered a bowl of chicken pot pie soup and a chicken salad sandwich with extra mayo. Instead I was given a mayo sandwich and a spoonful of chicken salad. There wasn't even a variety of bread types. Would have preferred regular sandwich bread instead of a roll.

I highly recommend Campo's! One of the best cheesesteaks that makes Philly so famous for them! Great quality, reasonable price, & fantastic customer service! They give back to the community and are a huge Philly staple! 5 stars!

I only come here because its not far and its never crowded. That out weighs the almost always rude customer service. There's really no other reason to come here. If you have another location...go to that one!

After 30 years on this planet, I finally was able to eat my very first authentic Philly cheesesteak. It was worth the wait. The one thing I noticed was how tightly compacted and clean this sandwich was; strange thing to notice, I know, but it was beautifully packed together.  I got the regular cheesesteak, with steak, onions, lettuce, tomato, and Mayo. Simple yet fantastic.   Stop here, you won't regret it.

Does Campos arguably have the best cheesesteak in Philly. Yes they do...arguably BUT I won't rank it no. 1 in my argument but I will rank it good...really good! And the service from the family that has been running this place since 1947 is amazing. If you've been to Philly and you haven't visited the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, the Rocky Statue and Campos you haven't been to Philly!

The ramen was beyond amazing! I had the chicken soy ramen and it was Devine. It was my first times going out for ramen and it was extremely comfortable atmosphere for a ramen novice. The staff sat us immediately and our food came out very fast! It was also an extremely hot day in the city and they made sure out ice water was filled!

I don't typically read reviews for fast food places but I wish I would have done so with this one. Absolute the WORST customer service. After repeating our order twice at the order sign, and then again when we paid, she still neglected to order one as a meal. So when we pulled up to get it, they didn't have the second fry we expected. After repeating that it was the teller who made the mistake, they refused to give us the second fry.  We were told we would have to go back In the line and order the fries. WTF?! They also forgot the sauce for the nuggets, which I luckily noticed before we drove off.  And, no napkins either. Don't waste your time or money here.
The food doesn't even taste like Popeyes, it tastes like some dog food from a trash can a hobo just shat in. Don't do it, just don't

Out of all the suggested cheese steaks I tried from all the locals while we were in town I preferred this one the most .
Before you ask with CHEESE WIZ .... This seems to be a big deal to some of the locals and then some could care less either way.
Prices were fair.
The staff was friendly.
The place was clean.

Also the location for us was great to take in a few sites and try and few things  all while walking.

Pretty good cheesesteaks. There was no line, which seemed like a red flag, but I thought these were pretty good. We tried The Heater, which had a nice spicy sauce to it. And I got chicken cheesesteak which I thought was good.

I feel like it's more of a 4.5  ramen place. It's definitely not the best ramen I've had in my life but it is my go-to ramen place in the city. Their price is very reasonable for the quality of food that they serve and I love the atmosphere when I walk in. It feels very cozy and relaxing. I would say Tako Wasabi is a little gamey if you're not into raw seafood, so go for takoyaki if you're looking for something safe :) Ramen is always on top of the game.
This is the worst spot to ever order food they don't care about how long you wait for the order. They don't have no urgency. Please stay away from this store.
2nd place on my stop in Philly from NYC looking for the best sandwich. Meat was OK. Ketchup was watery made everything soggy.

Excellent cheesesteak and thankful they offer vegan cheese. We have also bought elsewhere to see which we like better but we LOVE Campo's! Will return every time we are in Philly. Thank you to Campo's for making the best cheesesteaks!

I actually love Campo's cheesesteaks, having tasted a vast majority with my hubby who is a cheesesteak fanatic! I may or may not be a bit biased, because we also had our first Philly date in a Campo's and I've pretty much incorporated it into all tourist stops for when I bring people into Philly (you're welcome campos, I expect my commission check in the mail).

Overall, I enjoy their cheesesteak because it's not overly greasey, the meat is chopped up, but still very present and seasoned. I always get peppers and onions with American, and they have yet to fail me once. Thankfully many people are more interested in the other cheesesteak option at the stadium so I've never had to wait longer than 5 minutes to get mine.

Yes it's more than their other locations, but it's a baseball game, this is pretty much the only reason I won't give them the full 5 stars....but I will give them my money! Also Chickie and Pete's is convinientely located next door, and if every you had the perfect Philly meal, it would be this! Just make sure to have a Federal Donut for dessert after. You're welcome.

I was walking around old city while visiting Philly and had just the worst service ever at Sonny's down the block(waited 30+ minutes for a cold steak). I came here hungry and annoyed and I got greeted by the owner himself and had excellent service with a great atmosphere. Highly recommended!

If you come when the food is fresh, it's just as delicious as any other KFC. The problem is they only cook fresh at peak hours and you can have a very poor experience if you come at the wrong times. In my experience staff are as friendly as most fast food places

bimp. they dont put anything in the crunchwraps it's all wrap. i make vegetarian crunchwraps at home at least once a week and they go crazy. hit me up $6 a pop hit me up! first pic is one from taco bell, 2nd and 3rd are mine

The girls at the register wouldn't look at me whatsoever. My fiancé got everything he needed no d*mn problem. My food was messed up. No biscuit no side! His fries weren't in the bag and they put it in our friends bag. They did nothing but talk laugh and be distracted. It was NOT busy!!!! Maybe a total of 7 customers and they were couples and then us three. They were so distracted and annoying. Being typical high school girls. If they can't do their job right don't work there. I work in fast food I know how this stuff is, but I also can do my job right. I can't even get ahold of anyone on the phone to complain to. Such a disappointment.

I have been coming for a long time as I can recall this as a hangout spot since high school. I still come here at least once a month to get the amazing banana split. The service is pretty good and the environment is cozy.
They are not that good. Never enough meat, stingy; and por choice for spokespersons. I don't buy it.

Hands down the best cheesteaks in the city! But to be honest my go to there is the meatballs.  I haven't tried everything on the menu but whoever I am with always rave about their meal too! My go to place when I'm in the city

Same old Dairy Queen not much has changed from when I used to go years ago trees are still the same quality as the same this is eight eat in Dairy Queen if you're looking for a cute little ice cream date they did have take-home's that you were able to select from in a small freezer to the side yeah probably will return here too

The management at this establishment is extremely unprofessional and rude. We ordered a 16 piece (chicken strips) family meal with 3 large sides & 8 biscuits and they gave us the wrong order of meat and totally forgot the biscuits. We went back to correct the situation and to speak to management regarding this inconvenience. He had zero customer service skills and made the Popeyes's brand look terrible. They actually had the nerve to make us wait again for the strips while they served several other customers. I wish I would have visited one of the other local locations.

Found this small spot by chance with a friend awhile back and have been craving their ramen for awhile now. Would definitely put this as my number one place to go in Philly as their ramen wasn't too oily, the broth was clean, and it didn't make me feel heavy or sluggish after eating the entire bowl. I would compare the quality of this ramen to what you would find in California!!

The karaage chicken appetizer was super tender as well as crispy on the outside, probably the best I've ever had.

The overall vibe of the restaurant was very cozy and home like with the authentic Japanese decor. With this being a during Covid review, the bar wasn't open to sit at but it looked exactly how it would in Japan! The sever was wearing a mask and you could see him preparing the food in the kitchen with gloves on.

Amazing spot for ramen in center city! Went here on a whim with a friend while craving ramen and I am so happy we did! The space isn't too large, but there's several tables for 2 and 4 that seat everyone comfortably. The menu isn't too large, there's only a few soups and appetizers on there, but that usually means that whatever's on there is really good- and it definitely was! I got the Gates of Hell ramen and substituted the pork for tofu- it was the perfect level of spicy, you could definitely feel the kick to it but it wasn't overbearing, the broth had an amazing flavor, the texture of the noodles were perfect, the egg was perfectly marinated, and the tofu was sooooo good (it's rare that tofu ever tastes like anything, but this one was slightly fried and marinated I think- so yummy!) My friend got the Hiro Heaven ramen and also loved it. Definitely will be coming back here! It's especially convenient being located right next to TJU hospital and campus!
Got the fully loaded cheese steak and mac n cheese. Both we amazing. The bread for the cheese steak was superior. Grabbed a homemade cannoli for the road, they looked too good not to take with.

I had probably one of the worst customer service experiences at this place. I ordered a pizza last night for pick up through Uber eats. When I arrived I was told there was no order. After telling them that the order was made through Uber eats, they discovered their mistake. I received a mediocre apology and was told they could make it in 10 minutes. Since it was cold and rainy, I said that I would wait in my car, and she asked which car. I waited in the car for 20 minutes. Since no one came to the car, I went inside to discover that my pizza was done and sitting on the shelf waiting for me to come get it. Why did she ask which car if she had no intention of bringing it to me? Their indifference was evident. Offer me a bottle of water while I wait for their mistake and bring the pizza to my car, which was right outside of their entrance. I will never recommend Uncle Tomy's Pizza at 27th and Morris in Philadelphia, PA to anyone.
Amazing place. I've grown up with this pizza and I recently found out my teacher's father is the owner. Small world, good food.

three words describe this restaurant .... "FAST FOOD HELL." i am amazed no one else has reviewed this place yet. first, let me say that ive been going to this restaurant occasionally for several years and the service here is consistently horrible. its always staffed by a younger crew comprised of mostly ladies and i swear, when i walked in today there were probably about five people ahead of me. i think two or three of them had already ordered and were waiting. the restaurant has a tiny counter with only two registers. although both registers were staffed they were moving as slow as molasses. the music was blaring, the employees were singing out loud and socializing, one was on the store's cordless phone while taking and filling orders at the counter.it was one of the most horrid displays of customer service ive ever seen. then, more employees came in, reporting for work i assume, and were lingering around the food prep area just behind the registers in their street clothes. it was just TOTALLY disgraceful and unprofessional. i dont believe this place has ever had good management bcuz if they did, this type of behavior wouldnt happen all the time. it just sucks bcuz there arent many popeyes restaurants around so im kinda forced to go to this one. im pretty certain this is a franchise location and not corporate owned otherwise id contact them to let them know how horrible EVERY experience has been in this establishment. i cant even count how many times ive gotten home to find my order incomplete or incorrect.my recommendation .... DO NOT PATRONIZE THIS ESTABLISHMENT unless you have alot of patience. sometimes the food isnt even worth the aggravation.

i wish i could leave 0 stars but unfortunately its not possible.

My son and I always do cheesesteaks either before, during or after games. We've had them all and none are better than Campos. Roll, meat, cheese and onions, always perfectly balanced. Especially the steaks at the Wells Fargo Center location, so good. The workers really seem to care about the quality of the sandwich no matter how busy they are. Our favorite cheesesteak? CAMPOS!

Staff is RUDE!!! If you don't like tourists, then don't have a shop on Market Street. Be bitter in some slum. Staff yells at their patrons and tells them to leave. An embarrassment to Philadelphia. Beware. Brought my daughter to tears from embarassment.

Tried to drive in for a quick meal but ended up waiting in the drive-thru line for twenty minutes. When we finally got the food- another 5-10 minute wait- one of the bags randomly had mayonnaise on just the outside of it and the actual food was very poorly made. Really upset with the service, would definitely not go again.

Avoid this location if you can. They ALWAYS mess up our order. And not just one little mistake. EVERY SINGLE ITEM was wrong. They can't figure out white vs dark meat, spicy vs mild, sweet tea vs unsweetened...and this last order, they forgot the pie entirely. Go to a different Popeyes unless you want random food you didn't order.

The absolute worst cheese steak I've ever had, an embarrassment to Philadelphia.  Basically a roll with the smallest amount of dried up meat ever.  Don't waste your money. Honestly as a whole Philadelphia cheese steaks have become mediocre. The best Philly cheese steak are in South Jersey now in small shops, not tourist trap chains. Oh, best cheesesteak in the park is at Cobblestone Grill, put Campos and Tony Luke's to shame. Amazing how different Campos pics are compared to the garbage they served me.
Got a cheese steak hoagie today. Gross! Small and soggy.  AND PLEASE NOTE..they charge a dollar for using a credit card. SCAM!!!!!

I love this place! They have delicious cheesesteaks. I've been coming here for years and when I stopped eating meat I could continue to come because of their vegetarian and vegan options! They also have local beer selections which is pretty cool.

Food is terrible it has little to no seasoning and a waste of meat to be honest, they have no French fries and the only thing I enjoyed was the bread and drink which honestly wasn't even good, interior design is nice though. If you're coming to Philly for a day, do not come here.
listen. just do not eat here. guy slammed the door in my face walking in and then I got the food. I have no pictures to show because as soon as I took a bite I walked it to the dumpster.

This is one of my favorite ramen spots in Center City. I especially enjoy their lunch specials that are $13 for a salad, app, and ramen of your choice. It's a great deal you can't pass up. It is cash only too.

Been wanting to try this place since hearing about it a month ago. So two weeks ago I'm walking by in the daytime and I see a Cease Operations/Stop Work Order sign stuck to the window by City of Phila., L&I. On closer examination, it's dated from this past summer (and maybe from a previous tenant or builder) - so I look in the window and see people sitting and eating, and assume Hiro is squared away with L&I, and the Hiro operator is just an idiot, bad businessperson or lazy. But WHOLLY COW, how do you open a business and not remove an official CO/SWO sign!!

But, the other night on PBS there's a show called Mind of a Chef, and the episode takes place in Japan at some of the best ramen shops. So with a craving for a good bowl of soup and intrigued by my previous observations - we walked over at 6:30pm last sat. evening.
    
Now I must say it's been fascinating to read the varying reviews. I appreciate them all and am jealous of the folks who have the "street cred" to know a real good ramen/soup shop. I like to think I know a good bowl of soup, I cook a mean bowl of soup, and this is an average bowl of soup. It was not as bad as some folks have said, but it wasn't amazing either - I'd call it decent or sufficient. (Meaning I'm not thinking about returning in the near future, but I'd go back in a pinch - and it has me on a hunt for the best ramen shop in philly). 

Iv'e been wondering if the varying remarks are due to different expectations or it's just a consistency thing with the kitchen (it shouldn't be - either you make a good stock and season it properly, or you don't). I was leaning toward the later, but now think it might be the expectations.  

Anyway, we walk in and there's a 20 something asian guy eating and admiring/examining a foot tall Transformer looking movie character. It was weird.  As we walk past him we don't see anyone until we get halfway back and three people (servers and owner) hanging out in the back see us and spring into action. The two server's were very nice, accommodating and helpful during the entire meal.

We were offered complementary japanese beer and gladly accepted it. Aside from the soup, we also ordered the octopus sushi, kimchi, and edamame. Loved the kimchi (and price $2.00). The octopus sushi was different - I wouldn't order it again.

So I'd say go and try it - and then write a review.

Ordered breakfast this past Sunday morning. The cashier at the drive through had the lowest energy level and struggled to do the bare minimum. Just took our money and handed us the bag of food. No ketchup, no napkins, no sugar, no cream. I get it. Some jobs are crap and you don't want to do it but have to; I've been there. This franchise owner needs to step up and pay more and train more to get better workers. You can bet I will never go there again.
Always get the seeded roll. Really makes a difference. I'm personally a big fan of the flyers ice cheesesteak. Italian hoagie + Mayo + seeded roll = a good time

This was a terrible experience. Not only did I wait 30 minutes for a 2-minute sandwich, I got to watch the old white man behind the counter tell non-white customers to shut the Hell up in front of women and children. I don't care how busy or stressed you are, that behavior is vile and unacceptable. They could have the best cheesesteaks in town (which they do NOT) and I would never come back to watch people get treated like that. Will be checking to see if Philly has a human rights office - this warrants a complaint. Also, they are not enforcing mask or other health measures even though they claim to.

I'm from Cincinnati and we were doing some work in Philly for a couple days. We asked numerous people in the city where we could get a great hoagie. The census was you must go to Campo's. The next morning I went and stopped into Campo's. This amazing, passionate, and caring lady took my order. Her name is Mia, come to find out she is one of the owners. Her dad was there making it happen as well. Not only did she help with the order of the two hoagies that we were eating there. I asked how do I get 4 of these hoagies back to Cincinnati? She took it from there. Next thing I know my two hoagies were ready, my four hoagies were reading in a nice lunch box with an ice pack. As the place is getting busy, I asked Mia if she had a pink Campo's shirt. Without hesitation she went back and got a container, and she had a pink T-shirt for me to buy. It was a win win!! The hoagies that we ate there were AMAZING!! My wife (back in Cincinnati) that lived in Philly as a kid got an original Philly Campo's hoagie, by the way, 9 hours later when I got back to Cincinnati. The hoagies were just as good. She also got a Campo's pink T-shirt, and she is wearing it proudly today as she is a 17-year breast cancer survivor and October is breast cancer awareness month.

Mia and team there is a reason why your restaurant has been around since 1947. Keep up the great work. It was an awesome experience!!

Horrible. This place used to be pretty good at the ballpark but I will never go again. The last two times I got a cold cheesesteak and the cheese was not melted at all. There was no line but that's because they don't even bother giving you a hot sandwich for the $12 they charge. The meat sits there precooked on their grill and then they scoop the lukewarm meat onto a roll that has American cheese slices. They hand it to you, it feels cold. Them you unwrap and sure enough, it's cold and dry. The American cheese was not melted not even slightly. 
Obviously they are more interested in keeping their lines moving quickly which means precooked cold meat and unmelted cheese. I am so pissed off I wasted my money and meal on this crap.

The chicken steak was tasteless. No salt and pepper or any seasoning at all. The chicken taste like soap from the cloth they probably wipe down the tables with. I came from Jersey just to get a Philly chicken steak and I was so disappointed. The food was horrible. I wouldn't recommend this place at all. They're also way overpriced for the kind of food there serving. The decor of the place is very dark. The cooks were also arguing back & fourth. Extremely unprofessional.

Coming here was kind of nostalgic for me. I came here alot when it first opened years ago. I always get the same thing:3 cheese chicken nacho. 

So of course I ordered what i always ordered. I think next time I'll go with a burrito, just to switch it up. 

Service was good, and the food tastes the same as I remembered.

We came at 10:20 and waited at the speaker for awhile. Nobody answered us but it's crazy cause there was people before we pulled in but as soon as we get to the speaker, silence. we even pulled up to the 2nd window: nobody. They was hiding from us. There was even a girl sitting outside on her phone. We could see inside the lobby there was obviously somebody there as there was a vacuum out and everything. Also, every time I come before 6 pm, it says the lobby is open for inside orders..the doors are always locked and they tell me I have to walk through the drive through and once I'm in the drive through a kind girl tells me I can come inside but then says I can't!  Like take down the sign off y'all doors of y'all just gonna lie. They wear no hairnets no gloves and sometimes don't wear a mask or wear it properly and I literally worked at McDonald's for 8 months we would literally get in trouble for not wearing either of those things! Bout to get a health inspection on them cause they need it! Unprofessional.
Amazing food  consistently all the time here!  The new Chiluba burrito is flames, if I do say so myself. That is all! Happy New Years/Happy Yelping!!! :)

To be completely honest, I'm not entirely sure why this location has so many awful reviews because my food (typically salad or rice bowl with chicken or sofritas) is always perfectly fine. Everything is noticeably fresh -- especially the lettuce, salsas, and guac.

The only negative aspect I've sometimes noticed is that the employees just looked drained and unhappy to be there, but who doesn't have that appearance while working in food service?? I just smile, say "please" and "thank you" to every employee that helps with my food, and I've never had any issues with attitude or anything.

Visit for yourself and see what you think ‍

Staff doesn't want to help, looked annoyed to take your order. Front employees were eating food with their gloves on then touching customer food and handling their phone with gloves on. Save yourself from food born illness and go somewhere else.

this was decent but terakawa is better. i like a good spicy ramen so i ordered the gates of hell and it was OK. the broth wasn't as complex and didn't have much depth but the noodles were cooked well (even though they never ask about the firmness like terakawa) and the egg was delicious. i felt as though the quantity here is less. i usually never finish my ramen at terakawa but i easily finished it here. 

the gyoza was OK as well, they were all stuck together which was disappointing but the flavors were good.

all in all, the ramen here was decent but terakawa is probably still my favorite philly ramen joint

I've stopped in a couple times when the Indian food craving hit, and Spice End really does the job. They have your standard kati rolls but also offer Indo-Chinese dishes like the Chicken 65. 

My favorites:
+Chana masala kati roll: this is super flavorful and filling 
+Chicken "65": I can't say that I'm an expert on Indo-Chinese food, but I thought this dish was pretty good. It's essentially a combination of take-out Chinese chicken with some different spices thrown in. It doesn't come with rice though, unfortunately. 

I'll avoid their chicken kati rolls in the future since they were a little on the dry side. Overall, solid fast + cheap restaurant. I'll definitely stop by again to try more things in the menu.

Got the roasted pork delivered from Goldbelly and so far probably the worst thing we've gotten from Goldbelly. It wasn't bad but it wasn't great. 1st they should ship all the components separately vs shipping made sandwiches the bread got to soggy and the sandwiches had way to much broccoli rabe vs pork. I would like to portion it out myself.

What a terrible experience. My husband and I stopped for a quick dinner before seeing a movie. They had five employees and it took them 20 minutes to make our meal. The food was mediocre. I will not be returning.

My aunt (a PHL native) used the Goldbelly app to ship us 2 Italian hoagies and 2 cheesesteaks with provolone all the way to Seattle as a holiday gift. All I can say is WOWWWWWWWW!! So good, it practically brought tears to our eyes (bf is also originally from PA). If it's this good after traveling 3k miles, I can only imagine how good it is when it's handed to you fresh. You just can't get stuff like this out here. I mean, yes, they have sandwiches in Seattle. But not what I would call proper hoagies and cheesesteaks. Not like this. Once it's safe to travel again, we'll def come by in person on our next trip out. YUM.
Extended hours and friendly staff. I grabbed The Works on my way home and was able to get it at 10am. Delicious.
Fake Chick-Fil-A, always soggy, over cooked, freezer burned. Service is fast but the people sure are not up to the chain's standards. It's not "their pleasure"

Was looking for a hot bowl of ramen, so Came here with a friend about two weeks ago!! Anytime I see a place offering a vegetarian ramen, I get super excited because they are either hard to find or offer just 1 option that isn't great. Overall, pretty decent ramen, would probably come again but the veggie ramen is soy sauce-based so at the end its like eating a bowl of soy sauce.

Atmosphere: super casual, lots of millennials such as myself, college kids, etc. Plenty of 2-people tables. table service, they have a bar with saki mostly as well.

Food: My friend ordered the chicken soy ramen without the pork, and I ordered the veggie ramen. Let me just say, this was TRULY a veggie ramen, this is the first time I've had a ton of vegetables given to me in my bowl (see attached picture). Usually places give you a veggie broth with little to no veggies. Also, the  veggies included things like carrots, bok ahoy, corn, etc! Lots of variety. Overall, the veggie ramen was overpowered by the soy sauce based broth they use. It was way too much soy sauce and I definitely walked out with MSG-overload. Please stop doing this to your veggie customers.

Drinks: just had water! saki available as well as sodas and sparkling water

Service: Quick, efficient, warm, pleasant

A hidden gem that somehow has survived in a major downtown section of Philly, while keeping an incredible value for their ramen bowls. I had the "Hiro's Inch of Heaven", which comes with pork belly - savory, satisfying, and flavorful in the way an excellent bowl of ramen should be.

What makes things even better is back when I visited, they were BYOB. This place is a total bargain for a quiet night out.
The best Ramen in Philly.Good thing we bought a few diferente Pocky to my son.he  loved all the flavor.

I never thought id find myself reviewing a kfc even though; over the years i was IN LOVE with their fiery buffalo boneless wing that they discontinued. Luckily the nashville tenders are a close 2nd, as well as close to my heart. KFC is my favorite fast food joint for chicken, hands down.
Campos is the ideal PHILLY cheesesteak and deli. All the food is great and the establishment has a family feel! Go check them out you won't regret it!

I love Jimmy John's and I go to this location just about every other day. The staff is usually pretty friendly, although I've seen friendlier at other locations, but the service is quick and the food is good. Also, they take Diamond Dollars and that is a HUGE bonus for us Temple students. Their service is insanely fast (maybe one minute to make your sandwich, and that's pushing it) and they also offer delivery (although I've never used it since I live right across the street, but I've heard that it is lightning-quick).

Employees here are incredibly rude. I called because GrubHub only gives you the option to call the restaurant directly if your order is late and mine was 40 minutes beyond the delivery time. When I asked about it, the first thing the guy on the phone said "yeah they push all this off on me" ... as if that was my fault ... then he put me on hold and got back and said that they didn't have my order, but i told him i placed it through GrubHub and i had the order so it did not make sense. He proceeded to yell at me that I told him DoorDash (which I did not) and I was wasting his time scrolling through doordash orders going back to 9 pm (nay the fact that I am a customer and he was actually wrong) ...then he found my order through GrubHub and was like oh its on the way- no apology or resolution. OH AND BTW- the entire call was 4 minutes long so i wasted that much of his time? The order never arrived and I had to cancel through GrubHub customer service. this place is absolute and total garbage with terrible employees, i will stick with domino's or better local spots and never order from here again.

The food is good but the staff at register is terrible they seem like they do not want to be there. And I saw one employee pick a piece of chicken off a plate she was wrapping up. Not sure if it was for a customer or her lunch none the less no customer should witness that.

Take a look at my account I think I have one other review in several years, that's  how bad this place is. Always a line that takes forever. Cashier never even said a word to me after I said hello and thank you, quite rude, I've worked in fast food yes it stinks, but learn how to atleast say hello to a customer. Asked for sauces a she just slammed the delivery window shut. I'm over that, what I'm not over is I Get my order, it's completely wrong and the garbage they gave not only was cold, but it smelled rotten I couldn't even eat it. Not to sound like a cheapskate too badly but ten bucks for a couple rotten tacos and chicken, folks do yourself a favor and avoid this dumpster fire.

Went for the traditional Philly Cheesesteak with the works and provolone cheese - every bit as delicious as reported to be- also a side of Potato salad was quite nice as well!  Service is fast, smart and know how to upsell sweetly! Glad I don't live nearby because I would justify dinner here on a regular basis!!

Still advertising their vegan cheesesteak, when the rolls are still not vegan!

Shame on you! This is so disrespectful to so many people!

I've been in the restaurant business for almost 20 years . Having that said my thing is customer service . I've been going to multiple Chic Fila's for over 10 years and never have a bad experience. Well that all changed yesterday 6/02/2018. The quality of food was fairly good but the staff ( particularly the register worker ) was rude and obnoxious. Didn't get her name but she was tiny and dressed in garb . You asked her a question and her responses were filled with sarcasm as if we the customers were stupid . I sat down with my partner and continued to watch her attitude on display .  I feel as though if you're having a bad day never let the customer see that . I pray she's not like that naturally because she's in the wrong business completely.  I pride myself on customer service so I'm the wrong person to have that tone with . Thank you

This place is a disgrace with extremely unprofessional and rude staff.. it's dirty and are out of ingredients all the time !!! I would rather go to get 711 sushi than having to come here one more time.

Came here on an rainy night looking for a comforting bowl of ramen !! This place was recommended by a few friends and I finally got a chance to stop by. It's a small and cozy place ! The menu is not big either, so not overwhelming. This place is cash only ! I ordered the gates of hell ramen and it was a bowl of spicy deliciousness!! The soup was very flavorful, meat was deliciousness, and the ramen was prepared just the way I like it !! I would recommend that you check this place out if you are a ramen lover !! I saw a sign that states that they are open on Sundays now !

I've been a couple times for cheesesteaks which falls right in the middle of the spectrum for me here in Philly. The bread is top notch but the meat quality/seasoning is subpar compared to some of the other big names in Philly. Unlike some other steak joints, they have a pretty extensive hoagie menu and unique iterations of the cheesesteak (buffalo, BBQ, pizza, etc.) which I admittedly have not tried. They actually do have a decent vegetarian menu for steak joint. Overall, average. They take credit cards which can be a plus.

Hiro ramen is a cute small ramen shop that has been open for a few weeks/to a month now. Their menu is limited but especially now since Hurricane Sandy has affected their ingredient suppliers. 

I walked into Hiro Ramen today around 11:30. It's a cozy restaurant off of 11th and chestnut, right next to Milkboy. The inside is beautiful and the little bar benches are comfortable.  I sat at the bar and  was recommended to get the Shoyu Ramen. 

The ramen came out promptly and the presentation was good. It came with an egg, two pieces of charsu, scallions, a piece of nori and some bamboo shoots. The spoons are reminiscent of Ramen Bar but THANK GOD, THEY'RE PLASTIC. If I had to deal with another wood spoon I would go crazy. But Hiro Ramen's spoons are more comfortable to use than Ramen Bar's. The spoons aren't as big and they have a slanted handle which makes it easier to drink the soup with. 
 
The Shoyu broth had good flavor and was just the right amount of saltiness for me! But it could be a little hotter in temperature. I know a lot of people have complained about the broth being to salty, but it was perfect for me. Although the amount of oil I had atop of my broth was a tad disconcerting.. The noodles were a little too thin/soft for me, but thats preferential. The egg was sweet, which I enjoyed. The only thing that brought the dish down was the charsu. The pork could use the most work. The charsu was too chewy..almost rubbery. I was disappointed because it should be nice and soft.

The portions are great, and the Shoyu is pretty darn good for a ramen shop that hasn't been open for too long. I hope they decide to expand their menu to include some more ramen choices and some more appetizers as well. I would like to see their rendition on a tonkasu broth ramen.

Over all Hiro is a solid spot for a warm bowl of ramen. The staff is friendly and the service is prompt. $8 a bowl is pretty good. It's a good contender in the new ramen scene. Please please please work on your charsu!! Once you do, your Shoyu ramen will be killer :)

Disrespectful people who work there. Don't ever go to this location. This McDonald's don't know how to treat people with care. Half of the people who work there act like they don't care for the job. This place is disrespectful
This place was amazing! I got the chicken soy and it was so good, Edamame was delicious, and the service was amazing!
We went here around 830 and they weren't accepting card payments and ran out of Big Mac buns. How does a McDonald's only accept cash AND run out of buns?!
My food that was delivered to me from KfC was awful my chicken sandwiches was hard and small I was very disappointed with their food tonight never again will I order from KfC again

I came from out of town and was referred to this establishment as one of the best restaurants for Philly Cheese Steaks. Well I can start by saying the front counter staff was not friendly, short tempered and it showed because the individual couldn't remember what we ordered and had to repeat the request. Nothing special about the steaks. All of my guest  and I said the same thing. I ordered 4 with fountain drinks and paid $58.00. 

I wasn't impressed.

First of all. I once witnessed an employee drop a mash potatoes on the ground and scoop it back into the cup and try and serve it to someone. It was gross. But that didn't happen to me so I wasn't deterred!
I came back to the drive through and they completely forgot half my order. 
2 separate occasions my roommates and I ordered it through grub hub and when the driver got there they said they "never received the order" and refused to make it.
This place sucks and the employees working there are incompetent as they are surly. Will not be returning and would not recommend anyone else to go either.

If I could give this place ZERO stars believe me I would! This place is awful the staff is rude and unprofessional (manager included) they don't pay attention and consistently make mistakes on my orders EVERY TIME I come to this place. Its ridiculous!! I had to call corporate this afternoon & that's not in my nature but something has to be done about this place and how poorly this restaurant is ran. They hire a bunch of incompetent teens/young adults that are too busy talking and joking around and on their devices to actually pay attention. I only come here cause I live down the street so its really convientant for me. However I drive so I'm going to start going to City Ave Popeyes or the one on Monument RD in the shopping center with Fresh Grocer. Whoever sees this please AVOID THIS LOCATION at all cost cause believe me they will mess up your order. If U do however decide to go here check everything down to your napkins lol while you're still inside the restaurant.
This spot is absolutely atrocious, I ordered a chicken quesadilla and the only thing that was in the box was rice. Won't ever be coming back again
Delicious ramen at a good price. I've gotten take out over five times and each has been great.

I personally prefer Hiro. We always order their kaarage chicken and takoyaki for appetizers. The kaarage chicken is super crispy & comes out piping hot. I think it is also well seasoned with or without a squeeze of lemon & the mayo dip. The takoyaki could use more octopus in my opinion & maybe a few more seconds to cook through, but overall I enjoy it.

The ramen broth & noodles are delicious.

Owner threatened to fight me, harassed me, and also noticed that the restaurant is violating health codes- saw flies on food and what appeared to be mouse droppings around the perimeter as well. Reporting this to the BBB and the city for violating health codes as well harassment. Luckily this interaction was recorded however an owner should take pride in their business, not threaten people. 


Side note- food is mediocre. Better off heating up cardboard in the mic with tomatoes and cheese and call it a day. Lunchables pizza is better than this. Even tho they're open late, you couldn't be desperate enough even if this was the last place on earth I wouldn't even give my last penny.
I don't even know if they put real chicken in my calzone. It definitely didn't look or taste like chicken. I would think twice before ordering from here!

This restaurant is available on Goldbelly! I had the philly cheese steaks delivered and they were huge sandwiches. The sandwiches are definitely a meal by themselves; they are full of meat and they come with cheez-wiz, hot peppers and onions. The roll was soft on the inside and the crust was tender and not hard. Campo's sent us preparation instructions and I found them to be helpful.

Stop sleeping on this pizza! It's simple and amazing! I love the flavor of the pizza and the customer service has been wonderful thus far! Hands down, one of my favorite places to order pizza from here in Philadelphia!!

Here's my ramen cred: I've eaten it on the West Coast, all the hip NY joints, even in Japan.

Not that any of that matters. After all, it's just an opinion.

Having said that, I can say that the Hiro Ramen that I had may be the worst ramen I have ever tasted. The broth was oily with no depth. The pork, while being cut at a nice thickness, was bland and actually a little cold. Where was that torch that someone mentioned in another review? None of the toppings (bamboo) stood out. The egg was a little cold as well and not tasty at all. Noodles were fine. I left behind noodles and broth even though the portion wasn't particularly large. Having said all this, I felt like those $10 were stolen from me.

They also have some appetizers, and I tried the spicy chicken (1st on the menu). It was boiled chicken in a spicy sauce, served cold. The chicken was tender, and the sauce was just spicy enough to tingle the tip of your tongue. Just OK.

The interior is minimalist, nothing special, nothing egregious.

Honestly, I don't want to try any of the other ramen unless they make some changes in their broth.

Sitting out here now, just ordered two Philly cheese steak subs, the Works.  Very disappointed in the little amount of steak in both subs.  If you enjoy a good cheese steak subs, with plenty of steak for the money, this isn't the place
The best place in Philly to get a cheesesteak! The interior is really cool and the staff are amazing.

A tasty, tiny 
Cheesesteak. Sweeter onion taste. 
Good single serving


*they are open and we did take out- super fast
Amazing! Sandwiches, cheesesteaks, and homemade, family recipe macaroni salad. Can't get enough!

Slowest Service Ever! I came to learn they were training a new person which is fine, I know it takes time to learn the register but it was as if they were taking breaks in between orders. It took 20 minutes just to get through the pay window and there were only 3 cars ahead of me. It was one of those, I invested this long in, it can't possibly be longer but then it was. Finally paid and it was another 10-12 minutes for my 1 value burger and a medium fries. While I was waiting to pull up to the window, they asked me to confirm my order again and then I watched 3 employees come from the cooking area to hang out with the girl handing the food out at the drive thru. Maybe if they were manning their stations food would come out sooner. After all that wait, the burger was terrible and the medium fries weren't even filled up. 

The star is because Yelp makes you give one

The entire reason we chose this cheesesteak place was based off the fact that it had Impossible meat and dairyfree cheese on its website. I made the mistake of not calling before we went there. Turns out they cook the vegan food on the same griddle, next to the beef. Super bad for vegans (who I would imagine don't want meat grease in their food?) but extra bad for my son with severe allergies. Why bother offering vegan food if it's so badly cross contaminated that it's not really? Save yourselves the trip if you're looking for a vegan cheesesteak, because you're not really getting one here.

I thought the ramen was decent, not nearly as good as the Chinatown Terakawa, but there was zero wait so they get an extra star. I would only go back if I was dying for ramen and couldn't stomach the idea of waiting however long for the really good stuff.

If you've got all day and you're super picky, I'd say go to Terakawa. If you want decent ramen and don't want to wait, Hiro is your spot.

The best ramen I've ever had. They start with a Tonkotsu pork broth that has been simmered for 72 hours. They offer several varieties of this, a soy sauce-based option and also a vegetarian option.

The lunch special is $13--you get a small spring mix salad with carrot shavings, fried noodles and ginger dressing, your choice of appetizer (3 available) and then your choice of delicious ramen soup.

I have been eating here 2-3 times a week for several months, and haven't had a bad meal yet!

*pre covid review*

We came here while visiting a friend in Philadelphia. I am a big fan of ramen and always seek out new places to try so it only felt right to get ramen in Philly too. From what I remember my ramen was the base ramen with soy sauce. My bf got the gates of hell ramen. we were very impressed with the quality and taste of their marinated egg and chasu. However the broth for the gates of hell ramen was way better than mine. Even though I wasn't happy with my broth, I am still rating Hiro 4 stars because I know that if we ever come back I would get the gates of hell and it would be 4 star quality.
We didn't know where to go for a great cheesesteak, and a local recommended this place. Spot on. The best we ever had......

I looooove qdoba it's my favorite place! I've been to qdoba all over the country. This? Is not qdoba. They lay on the rice and skimp on everything else, and it's obvious that maybe the management there gives them strict portion limits on what they can give? I got a taco salad and they have like a few pieces of salad. It was so sad. Think subway but worse.

I ordered Campo's via Goldbelly to surprise my husband on his 40th birthday and they did not disappoint! We got the 4-pack, 2 wit wiz & 2 wit out. I had my doubts about how well cheesesteaks would travel, I mean, we order delivery from a place 3 miles from home and they get here soggy after a 15 min trip. But these cheesesteaks were delicious! Nothing soggy about them. I followed the instructions and let them come to room temp and then put them in the oven at 325 for 20 min. The bread was crispy and the steak was perfectly hot and tasty! Even though we didn't think that we'd like the wiz and that we'd prefer the provolone over it, the ones with wiz and grilled onions were our favorite!! Sooo freaking tasty! Highly recommend, 10/10. We will definitely be ordering again soon. Thank you Campo's for making my husband's 40th extra special!

This review is for the inch of heaven and gates of hell ramens. I've had them multiple times, and quality was consistently superb. I can say that this is a reliable, quality ramen place without the bells and whistles.

Really flavorful, rich broth was served hot, over a bed of well-cooked "al dente" ramen noodles.  The simple, classic toppings  were all nicely seasoned and prepared with care.

As for covid accommodations, they offer take out and dine-in (before the the Safer at Home order) with handsanitizer at every table. The servers wore mask plus face shield.

Still cash only. Good price for what you get, around $11 for a bowl of classic ramen.
got the wings. came to me basically still alive, just battered. mashed potatoes were fine (hard to mess that up), but considering this is a fast food chain that campaigns off fried chicken...

My friend and I were looking for a spot to eat when we happened upon Hiro Ramen House. We didn't make it in time for the lunch special, but that was alright.

Service was fast and attentive. The place seemed moderately busy, but it definitely wasn't crowded. The interior is super cute! I would pick this spot for a lunch date. 

As for the ramen, I'm not picky. The broth wasn't extremely salty like some other places I've been to, and the pork chasu almost melted in my mouth. The eggs were very well seasoned--definitely some of the better ones I've tasted. I liked the noodles too, slightly chewy and pleasant. 

I'm definitely coming back here again to try the rest of the menu. :)

Last night someone delivered a pizza to my house even though the streets were blocked by fire trucks  and crowds had formed bc the house next to mine was on fire. And this man got through all of that and still delivered this pizza by any means necessary. Give that man an award!

Campos , not a fan of
This place for a cheesesteak , they have a good chicken cheesesteak . Don't know how they got the attention they did . Must of been from being in the sports arena .  I'm my
Option average sandwich . We're in philly 1000's of sandwich places ... Nothing on at that place jumps out at u and say were the best this or that just average ...

A thoughtful sister overnighted to my wife and I a gift pack of Campo's Philly cheesesteaks and hoagies. For this Philadelphian who moved away many years ago, this wonderful taste of my old hometown brought back memories of good Philly food and friends. Campo's does it just right.

I got food from them a couple of weeks ago. Besides being soggy and inedible with no flavor NO ONE WAS WEARING MASKS. It has been shown in other posts. They are dangerous and should be shut down. Terrible garbage food won't be missed

This is a great option for ramen when you don't want to fight the hustle and bustle of Chinatown. My friend was excited to introduce me to Hiro, since it is close to our work and she had a good experience there previously. 

I got the Black Pig ramen and added corn for $1. The prices on their website are different that the menus in the restaurant, but only by a dollar. This is also a cash-only place.

I thought the ramen was fairly good, and the amount you get for your money is nice. The broth may have been a little on the salty side and I feel it lacked depth. Unfortunately, the pork was not as tender as my friend had made it out to be. It almost seemed like you needed a knife to help cut it.

Overall, I would come here again in a pinch, but I think I would take the extra wait to eat at Terakawa.

First time in philly and came across this place by walking around. My friends and I were unsure about which spot was the best, after we asked around we were recommended to come here. The girl working the front, it was a while ago so I might be wrong, but her name was Bri and she was so AWESOME! Any questions/concerns we had she happily answered and we were completely satisfied with our choices in cheesesteaks. Definitely recommend!

This is a review of Campo's through Goldbelly. I live in Omaha, and ordered 4 of "The Heater" Cheesesteaks. I've been ordering a lot of indulgent Philly foods off Goldbelly since the start of the pandemic. These were Outstanding!!! First, the packaging was so efficient. My cheesesteaks arrived fresh and cold. Followed the directions and cooked the onions as well, and it was so good I felt like I was back home! I love the heat on these from the jalapeños, sauce, and jalapeño cheddar! Well worth the money, I'll be ordering from Campos again if I can! Wish I knew I could've ordered a tshirt before I placed my order or I would've got one of those too!

Awful awful awful. The drive thru speakers are always halfway broken, filthy bathrooms and horrible wait times when ordering inside.  Like 15 minutes to wait for a few tacos. Yikes!  I'll be staying far away in the future.

Food is ok, but the service is poor.
Cashier at front was on her phone (handsfree) the entire order.
Asked for fried rice, but received white.
Sorry not worth my business,  will not be coming back.

A PHILLY CHEESESTEAK FAVORITE!  We are new to the area and have made it a quest to find the best Philly cheesesteak in Philly.  We go into the city every Wednesday and try a new restaurant.  Campos was restaurant #11 for us and tied for our favorite! The bread to meat ratio was perfect, the bread had  the perfect softness with a bit of chew to it, and the meat was flavorful. Add to that that the prices were competitive and the workers friendly, and we will definitely be back ( but not until after we try a few more sandwiches first)!    I only have two recommendations for improvement:  
1. I wish they took credit cards.  Yes, they do have an ATM on site, but I'd rather just have the convenience of paying with a credit card. 
2.  I wish they had fries on the menu..even better, I wish they had sweet potato fries!
Says closes at 11...walked in at 1030 and they were already cleaned up for the day. I drove 20 minutes!

This is the worst Taco Bell/KFC I have ever been to. If you order from the taco Bell menu, know that your food will not be anything like the picture. If you order from the chicken side, you might not get exactly what you order. The staff, for the most part, is rude and or ghetto as hell. Not sure why the management team hasn't stepped in to improve this location. I live 2 blocks from here and drive to City line to get my taco Bell, if that tells you anything.

I really, really, really wanted to love this place but it didn't live up to the hype. The steak was tough and pieces were hard to chew, which hasn't been my experience with a cheese steak before.  The lady working at the counter was super friendly, which is what you want at any business.  I would give it a second shot if I was in Philly again.
Great local ramen spot in center city with good atmosphere and affordable prices that's also BYO. Owner is also super nice! Ramen hits the spot and the broth is very solid.

A near whole in the wall, you will miss it if you blink while following the GPS. You will see a giant ATM machine within 3 steps of entering in. This means "Cash Only" and now electronic currency. 

We almost left but we heard this was voted the 2nd best Ramen shops in town. The dining room was empty, and we were sat down by a male worker working the front. 

The menu is short and simple. Very easy to choose. I chose the Black Pig Ramen and the broth was delicious. Get the extra meat and I got the extra noodles dry, on the side. Yum. Also, you must get the fried chicken and the sauce. You can thank me later.

I will never go here again. Got 10 piece spicy chicken nuggets with cheese fries and was very unimpressed. The lady in the drive thru had an attitude first and foremost, then the cheese fries were Soo bad looking I threw them out without trying it.. it looks like the fries were green and burnt, cheese wasn't even melted, they didn't give me any ketchup like I asked and the nuggets were ok but soon as I ate them I threw up and got very sick to where I went home and went to bed with a pillow pushed on my stomach.

I am an past employee that worked there who was offered a management position . When i Say the Staff Was so unprofessional, ill mannered , racial. Before i came to the store it was so dirty mold in everything and every place you really can't believe what they was giving out. They food was so nasty and not cook right when you eat it it give you diarrhea and vomiting. A lot of the staff had to call out including me due to food poising and heard the homeless complaining about feeling sick eating there food . I give it one star cause i really like my job and mcdonalds and there really is some nice mcdonalds out there and this one just give it a bad reputation coming from a former worker.

Absolutely terrible quality. I can't lie I received my food with decent speed but lemme tell you about this food. First off, I ordered a water pounder, I received a Big Mac. A Big Mac that was cold, smothered in sauce, and completely inedible. The fries weren't salted either. The McFlurry had about 6 M&M's in it. All in all, I ate too bites of the food and tossed it. Never coming back. I now remember why I no longer come to McDonald's.

Darn it, forgot to take a photo!  Update 1/2020... They have " cheesey garlic bread" advertised but it isn't a new type of bread- they just take white bread and smear some garlic butter in it.  Still pretty good though.
I call and call. Nobody answers. I try to order online it doesn't work. Is this place even still open?

I came back to try this location again in the  new year, im sad to say as of 2/9/2020 this location is still a safty hazard. Serving old reheated and cold food, dropping food on the floor and bagging it for customers, not washing hands after using the bathroom, absolutely disgusting. 3stars 2018, 0 stars 2019, 0 stars 2020. Fire this entire staff and replace them with competent people.

I would reccomend skipping Pei Wei and choosing one of the many alternatives nearby. I ordered the honey chicken, fried rice, and an egg roll. My chicken was cooked all the way through but was extremely chewy. The fried rice was bland and not worth the upcharge. My egg roll was made first and left to sit on the counter so it was soggy and greasy. The store is also confusing with no clearly marked pick up spot for your food. If you do go it's at the end of the counter where the forks and napkins are.

This is a strong contender for the best vegan ramen that I've ever had! And I have tried a lot of ramen in Philly and New York. They apparently have two veg options, even though it looks like only one on the menu. There's a second veg and tofu with a creamier broth that is to die for. My non-vegan husband had the Gates of Hell and loved it, and thought the  vegan broth was comparable!

I ordered the Gates of Hell ramen and my friend ordered the Black Pig ramen. Both were really good, but I would definitely recommend the Gates of Hell! It sounds like it would be extremely spicy but it really isn't - I'm not great with spice but it was barely spicy at all. However, the chili oil and broth was super flavorful that I was tempted to drink it all, even though I would rarely do so. The meat was really tender and fatty and overall it was one of the best ramens I've had in Philly. The Black Pig is decent but definitely preferred the Gates of Hell, but it was pretty flavorful itself. I think the broth here is something that I really enjoy - it's not overpowering but flavorful enough that you'd want to drink it (even if it's unhealthy for you). Just a caution that this place is cash only.
Consistently good service, the sandwich is always fresh and the people are always friendly. Have no complaints. Great fast food!
Had the Hiro's Inch of Heaven. It was delicious. Highly recommend this restaurant.

The depth of flavor that hits your tongue first from the first sip of the berkshire pork tonkotsu broth, so robust, so developed, so unique. Then the perfect amount of heat lays gently across the palette forcing the slightest and fulfilling amount of perspiration on the forehead. Shaved bamboo shoots, cooked to perfection, and green onions frolicking through this pool of perfection doing nothing but complimenting the depth and cohesiveness of the final product. Standing strong in the middle, pulling together the dish, is the most tender pork belly chashu with the beyond perfect ratio of rich fat. The char on this gorgeous slice of meat was done through the teachings of Buddha creating the most humbling culinary experience. Two eggs that have been cared for in a way someone cares for a newborn. Yolk cooked so perfectly that it seems as though someone is spinning silk directly into your cheeks. Egg whites so mature with flavor from the perfection of the curing mixture. Ever so gently swimming underneath it all are these marvelous, nay, MIRACULOUS and magical noodles.  Noodles cooked with such perfect bite and chew that you instantly return to infancy without a care in the world. Gentlemen, my feet have blisters and my nipples are chafing cause I just completed a marathon through flavortown.
                        We would like to thank Hiro Ramen House for being so hospitable for our stay in Philly.
Great, friendly service. I still prefer Terakawa Ramen, but place Hiro Ramen on par with Nom Nom Ramen (about the same price point, too). Definitely a good, quick meal if you live/work nearby!

A nice little spot with good intentions. Styled to look like an authentic hole in the wall ramen joint, the empty bottles of sake lining the ramen bar seating area immediately capture your attention but serve only as decor in this BYOB. My bowl, entitled "Inch of Heaven", is a bit overconfident in its name. The bowl is beautiful with its signature piece of Berkshire pork belly as the main ingredient. The accompanying bean sprouts, green scallions, bamboo shoots, nori, and egg add color, texture, and flavor contrasts. I taste the egg and it is probably the best tasting marinated egg I've had in Philadelphia. However, the rest of the bowl fell short of my expectations. There was very little flavor in the pork belly. Missing was a slice of fish cake. If you don't have that, then maybe some mushrooms would've been nice. I just think that this place could be so much more.

I was looking for a good Cheesesteak on my recent visit to Philly, but was really disappointed as soon as I touched my sandwich. The bread was too soft, like a hoagie, and the meat was not generously served. When I tasted it, I put it down and decided to go to the next place to find a better cheesesteak. The place looks like a little while in the wall, so I had high hopes, but unfortunately the sandwich disappointed me. On my cheesesteaks, I look for firmer bread, like French bread, packed full of meat and cheese. I was really surprised that this philly was so bland. Don't waste your calories here.

They touch your food with their bare hands if need be, one time I returned a wrong order and they put the chicken back available to serve. I could have done anything to that food. It's disgusting that was the last time I visited this restaurant that does not care about quality control. Don't believe me? Make an order and return it watch what they do with it. most places throw away returned food. Too much foul things can happen these days, they have to do better

I think this is my favorite ramen shop in philadelphia. If you are a fan of spice, go for Gates of Hell. It's really not that spicy but it's the best option for spicy lovers. I got the black pig this time. Pretty salty due to soy, but later, becomes rich with the fattiness of the broth. I think I tried most here and will prob come back as this is my go to ramen shop. I also had the chicken for appetizer. It's so juicy. You think it's almost undercooked bc it's so soft, but it's cooked perfectly. So juicy and tender~
Disappointing.  They used to be pretty good, but it would appear they went the cheap route on their ingredients. I paid a premium price for a school lunch level salad.

My cheesesteak here was good, but not my favorite in the city. Bread was good, but not as fresh tasting as some other restaurants. The onions were too chunky for my taste, and I ended up picking most of them off. We added mushrooms, which were good, but that bumped the price from $9 to $10.50 ("The Works"). The cheesesteak was also on the smaller size. Usually, my husband and I can split one and feel full, but this one just felt smaller than usual. I didn't order any of the sides - so can't speak to them, but I was disappointed that they didn't have fries (I know, cheesteak and fries isn't the most well-balanced meal, but it's what I wanted). I always feel annoyed with cash only establishments, and I really didn't like that my water cost about the same as a soft drink. Overall, not terrible - but I will get my cheesesteak fix elsewhere.

Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice? Well, I'll never eat there again so you cannot fool me again! Service was what you would expect from young folks getting $13/hour. But she was on her cellphone while taking orders so was she talking to me or her phone? At least she got my order correct.

Food is god awful! Menu board doesn't say chicken sandwich is breaded and fried. They don't have grilled chicken anymore? Chicken was overcooked and tasted like dog food! Fries were cold -- you could tell they were sitting there as she yelled at co-worker to make new fries. They served me the cold, stale fries anyway (after two, the rest trashed). They were out of most the sodas. Luckily, I could order the diet coke. I wanted an iced tea, but they didn't make any today. WTF? I should have gone to Wawa like I usually do! Shame that Wawa doesn't have a dining room or tables to sit outside (Wawa in Florida has outdoor dining). Well, the next time I'm at my dad's house in NE Philly, I will make sure to avoid this Wendy's as if my life depended on it, because next time, I could end up with food poisoning!
They suck, I should've listened to the reviews... waited 30 mins for a smothered burrito and they put beans only in it...wtf?
