This is a great late night spot. I love the DP Dunkers and Roni Rolls. One of the few places I can count on late delivery from. The menu has some different things that you can't get everywhere, which is nice.

Seriously jacked up my order. 
Got some random soda instead of tea and no straw, No sauces,Pies instead of cookies, got like 10 fries total. Everything is cold. Worst of all...No toy in the happy meal.  Not so happy of a 5 year old!

Now excuse me while I go eat my dry chicken nuggets, you animals.

They raised the price of their ramen by $3 and now give less noodles (black pig was $10 and now it's $13), and raised the price of their karaage chicken. They used to give a good portion of chicken but now give less chicken and fluff it up with spinach and a lemon. I was surprised to visit this place and order my favorites, only to be met with these changes. Now I'm just disappointed and still hungry, heading home to eat more because the $25 I spent on these two items was not enough to get me full.

D.P. Dough Philadelphia currently has no staff wearing masks while preparing food. I advised my customer, and they wanted to "roll the dice" and have me deliver the food. Afterwards, I immediately ended my DoorDash shift to go home and sanitize myself and my bag. Shame on you D.P. Dough for putting your #philly community at risk.

Amazing ramen. Definitely one of the best in the city. The ramen has a rich broth, not too salty. Inside the restaurant has nice decor and the service is good. Their other foods is also worth trying .I highly recommend. The flavor profile is on point and just the amount of spicy kick that doesn't over power the food. Cash only with ATM inside .
This place needs to be shut down. The owner pulled a gun on my friend and pushed him. The woman on the cashier was also extremely rude.  They don't want your business dont give it to them

Came here for an early dinner with a friend. It wasn't that busy when we came, about 3 tables. The ramen were all the same price $10/bowl. I had the Porfilio - the borth and ramen was good. If you like spicy with a kick of lemon, you should try this. 

The restaurant didn't look too clean and the menus were dirty with lots of stains and marks on it. It was a paper menu.. it'll be better if they laminated the menu so they can actually clean the menus every night. The service could be better. Our waiter was on his phone (texting, browsing) majority of the time and we waited for a very long time before he came and got our money. Also, this is a Cash Only restaurant. So make sure you have enough cash before you come in.

I stumbled upon Campo's like most people I guess, I was out late one night in Olde City cruising the clubs and, lo and behold there was Campo's in my sights. Seemed like a friendly place and I saw that cheesesteaks were on the menu. I never heard of Campo's before and while dining there, i didn't recognize anyone i knew. I finally figured it out, this wasn't a real local spot yet and most of the customers were out of towners. Which doesn't bother me, I was excited about the vast selections available to me. The Cheesesteak was decent, but a little small and the prices were a little high, but a great location and a great atmoshere made it special.
Very overrated.  Little meat in the sandwiches.  No free refill of soda, and do not accept discounts advertised. If you want to pay by credit card there is a $2 surcharge.

I'm beyond thrilled to see Pei Wei come to the Fashion District Philadelphia!

Anyone who follows me knows that Pei Wei is my favorite chain restaurant, and may know that I frequently hit the suburbs to get my fix. A few of those have closed up, but now we have a brand new location right in the heart of Philadelphia's East Market resurgence!

This may not be a typical Pei Wei restaurant, being a smaller location in a shopping food court, but it does include a number of menu highlights - including its most popular appetizers, entrees, noodle & rice bowls, sushi, and drinks. You will have a small wait for the food, but it's never frozen and always freshly made upon your order.

There are few seats in this primary space, but there is plenty of seating just a step away within the mall corridor.

The easy way to access Pei Wei is to enter the Pennsylvania Convention Center entrance on 12th & Market, go down the escalators on the right-hand side, and the Food Court will be straight through the doors (which is also where Jefferson Station is, for Market-Frankford Line).

Unfortunately Pei Wei does not serve its delicious crab wontons or its spectacular Mandarin green tea here, nor do they seem to be a part of the Pei Wei Rewards program (you don't get credit for your meal). Although, many restaurants have similar practices to limit menu & rewards when it comes to their mall or airport locations.

But, what you do get here is Pei Wei's delicious & fresh food at reasonable prices, in the heart of Philadelphia and within steps of your home or office!

I stumbled into this place on a frigid day in March (yes... winter in MARCH! Ugh!). I was looking for someplace to get lunch and excited to walk past a ramen restaurant. Talk about the most perfect food to warm you up!

I was surprised to see how tiny the restaurant is. Had I walked in with a group, I definitely would have had to wait for a table, but since I was by myself, I was quickly seated at one of the chairs by the kitchen.

The menu is very small, with just one page of everything they have to offer. I can be pretty indecisive when presented with a lot of different options, so this actually worked out well for me. The Gates of Hell it was!

My dish came out very quickly and I was thrilled when I saw it boiling, piping hot. The ramen looked fantastic and tasted just the same! It was very flavorful and quite spicy. The pork was so tender. When it comes to ramen, I usually tend to eat all of the noodles first and push (most of) the meat to the side, but that was not the case here. I finished all of the meat, which honestly, might have been a first for me when it comes to soupy dishes!

My waitress, Tiana, was so incredibly sweet and fun to chat with! I'm not usually one to dine in at restaurants by myself, but I didn't even feel like I was at Hiro Ramen! She was lively, made good conversation, and checked in on her customers frequently. Thanks to her for lightning up an otherwise dull and lonesome lunch! 

I definitely plan to return to Hiro Ramen again. Now that the weather is warming up, ramen might not be the most common dining choice for others, but that for sure isn't the case for me!

Had big expectation for Hiro after reading the reviews and think it has the potential to be good but was disappointed. The egg and bamboo were actually very well marinated and thats about the best part of the ramen. I ordered gates of hell and it actually had an unique spicy taste but it just wanst spicy enough; I even heated up more since it was a takeout and I didnt want the cold temp to influence the taste. The problem is the grease and fat; typically I like to sip on my soup while I eat the ramen but I couldnt do that cuz it was just so oily; chashu was fat and the portion was small considering a chunk of it was fat that I had to threw away. The ramen portion was tiny even for a 115 lb girl and the extra side of noodles wasnt much at all. Definitely one of the smallest portion since I've had ramen in philly, nyc, chicago, seattle, cali and MI. Restaurant is cash only without any form of other online payment method; super inconvenient.

FYI: Cash only!! They have an ATM inside but if you're not about paying that surcharge, make sure you come with cash.

WHAT I GOT: Hiro's ten inch of heaven

PROS: Definitely a good competitor to the famous Terakawa. The broth was flavorful and the noodles had some great texture. Their pork also had a slight smokiness to it that really added to the broth. And obviously, an egg on top makes even great. I also appreciated their portion size. Not too big but just enough food to get you to satisfied. The ramen came out at a neck breaking speed too. Also, shout out to whoever decided to play some Japanese music in the restaurant. I was definitely feelin the vibe.

CONS: well...if you're not actively looking for it, you would probably miss it going down chestnut. It doesn't have the most obvious exterior and the inside is a bit dark. They also served us our appetizer (we got takoyaki) like half way through our actual meal. Um...not sure if y'all know what the meaning of appetizer is but it still tasted good so I ain't mad about it. Timing was a bit off.

As a local who always has cash on me, I must say this is my favorite place for lunch in Olde City, if not all of Philadelphia. I've been here probably at least twice a week for the past 7 years. I can honestly say there's nothing I've ever ordered that I didn't love. The only problem I have is deciding what to order, since everything is so good. 
Aside from the food, I enjoy the cleanliness, decor, and quickness. But the best part about this place is the workers. The girls at the counter have always been extra friendly and patient, the owners are awesome, and I even got some fantasy football advice from the guys on the grill. All in all, I love this place.

When you come in, make sure you are in a good mood because the staff won't be.    

Food was meh

Really solid ramen.

Went here for lunch and the lunch special is really good bang for your buck. For $14 you get a small salad, a small appetizer (choose from gyoza, karaage, or edamame) and your choice of ramen. Just be aware that the establishment is cash only. There's an ATM on site but it's a $2.50 fee for withdrawals.

The karaage was really good. The meat was juicy, the exterior was crispy, and it was well flavored with an occasional hit of spice.

I had the gates of hell. It was solid. The egg was well cooked and flavored. The noodles were not doughy and not too firm. The broth was excellently flavored although at times a bit too salty. For those who have a spice allergy-- do not be deterred by the name; it's spice level is mild. Would come again!

Here are some photos.

I am so disgusted how people do not like to do their jobs correctly. If I did that and always took short cuts there would be many unhappy people. I went to this Chipotle tonite before work at 10:45 pm. A female worker came to the door saying that they were closed and they couldn't serve me. Last time I checked 10:45 does not mean 11 pm. Now I have to work my shift all nite with no food because I drove there I didn't have time to find another place because I would be late for work. People learn to tell time

I check out this Chick-Fil-A whenever I'm a little homesick. As a Penn student, it's a little out of the way, but definitely worth the hike.

I've had my fair share of inconsistent experiences at this Chick-Fil-A Express, but it generally always has what I'm looking for: chicken sandwiches, chicken nuggets, WAFFLE FRIES, amazing lemonade, and the occasional salad! I tried the lemonade one time on a whim, and now I can never come back without getting more--even though it can be a little pulpy, but it's so sweet and delicious. I wish they gave you trays (we looked the last time we were there... might have all been dirty that time) so you can pile up everything you're getting. The food quality is generally on par with other Chick-Fil-A's I've been to, even with the limited menu. They don't always have everything in stock, and you might have to wait several minutes. But there's not really a good alternative nearby, in my opinion.

I'm glad they now let you take as many sauces as you want, as they've relocated to being behind the check-out line. Passable service, but plenty of seating. Not too sure why the reviews are so bad, but they seem to be pretty old.

The location is unfortunate, currently across from a massive hospital construction project. But, once you're inside the warm wood-paneled tuck-away, it's quiet (save for the Japanese covers of 70's rock) and fragrant with long-simmering stocks. The service is straightforward. The ramen is out of this world best in Philly level. And, I've eaten ramen all over this city. The broth in ALL the ramen is unctuous and liquid velvety, complex and rich yet fresh. No hints of old animal fat like some other places. All of the food is worthy of five stars. There is a perplexing abundance of corn kernals, somehow. Maybe it's authentic, but I just ask to skip. Always order the edamame. Do not lick the plate unless no one is looking. But it's good enough to do it anyway. It's a BYOB - a plus in my book. Cash only.

I was looking for a good Cheesesteak on my recent visit to Philly, but was really disappointed as soon as I touched my sandwich. The bread was too soft, like a hoagie, and the meat was not generously served. When I tasted it, I put it down and decided to go to the next place to find a better cheesesteak. The place looks like a little hole in the wall, so I had high hopes, but unfortunately the sandwich disappointed me. On my cheesesteaks, I look for firmer bread, like French bread, packed full of meat and cheese. I was really surprised that this philly was so bland. Don't waste your calories here.

We selected this shop for our Philly Cheesesteak experience based on web reviews. In a previous Philly visit, we were disappointed with the products from other locations "famous" for Philly Cheesesteaks. We were not disappointed. I had the "heater." It is a cheesesteak that includes jalapeños and buffalo wing hot sauce. It definitely had a kick. I really liked it. The shop is small with limited inside seating. There are a few tables on the sidewalk outside. The staff was friendly and helpful. The sandwiches were prepared to order. I'd gladly return on any future visits to Philly.

Thank you Charlotte for helping me over the phone! I super appreciated you accommodating my needs last minute. That was so very  kind of you to help and your team as well even when it caused more work!

Grew up in Bucks County but left the area many years ago. Was in town over the Fourth of July weekend and made my first visit to Citizens Bank Park, so I can now say I've seen all three parks in my lifetime, including the Vet and Connie Mack. 

OK execution of my cheesesteak. Decent roll, meat wasn't too tough or greasy for a ballpark location, but the cheese isn't melted at all. Overall, it tasted ok and I enjoyed it. I've had some better, but many worse. 

Key question, if I ever get back to Philly, would I make a return trip to Campo's at the ballpark ... "Yes".

TIPS: 
1. In addition to the chili powder on the table, you can also ask for their housemade chili oil sauce on the side. 

2. Come for the lunch special. The ramen itself is $10 and for an extra $3, you get an appetizer AND salad.

3. Cash only!

My favorite ramen spot in Philly. Yes, better than Terakawa and without the wait. The noodles are always cooked to perfection with a nice springy bite (never soggy), the roasted garlic oil for their black pig ramen should be illegal for how addicting it is, and ohh the tonkotsu broth! I could swim in it...
Great cheesesteaks! A little expensive for the works ($14), yet it gets the job done! I suggest paying in cash so you don't have to pay the $1 surcharge.

On my quest to find the perfect cheesesteak while on my trip to Philly, I came across Campo's in Citizen's Bank field. I read on multiple top ten philly cheesesteaks reviews that Campo's was one of the best. Unfortunately, after trying from eight different places, this was the worst. A with a group of other people and they weren't impressed either. First of all, the steak was over seasoned and very salty. I think I could over look this if I wasn't a little turned off by the oil soaked wrapper. The bread itself was covered and glistening in the oil. Ok, it wasn't inedible, but it definitely wasn't the pleasant experience I wished for from a top ten cheesesteak. I did like the onions and cheese whiz but you really can't mess that up (then again, Slack's Cheesesteak was a bit chintzy with the whiz, and it was white). I will give this to them, they were friendly and efficient. I got my sandwich quickly and didn't miss much of the game. Maybe I ate at the wrong Campo's (like the Original spot but I had to choose between Sonny's and Campo's). Maybe I had a bad experience today. Sorry Campo's, unfortunately, you didn't shine for me they day I went to try your cheesesteak.
Probably the worst vegetarian "cheesesteak" I've ever had. Nothing more to say. It was awful.

This is a great Chipotle to scope out the hottie Drexel boys. Hahaa. 

I stumbled upon this while on a walk through University City. While admiring the new buildings, I saw they popped this Chipotle into one. I'd been craving Chipotle anyways, so it was a no-brainer to stop in. 

While others complain about the food quality here, there was no problem with mine. This is a standard Chipotle, and we all know how they work. It was the middle of the afternoon on a rather dank Saturday, and there weren't many people here at all. The most I could complain about was that the grilled veggies were a bit weepy; but I've had worse at other Chipotles from time to time.

So what's noteworthy about this one is that they do have some great front-view window seating to catch the hottie guys(!); that's always a plus. The rest of the seating is kinda awkward: downstairs there is a huge multi-laned table in a community setting, and upstairs is rather slender with a row of seats. 

I'm taking off one star for the seating; it's just not conducive for a nice group of 2-4 people to chat about their business.

I hope you all have as good of luck with the food as I did; super-busy locations can throw your food together a bit haphazardly, and I'd imagine this place is insane on weekday lunch/dinner times.

I was told to watch out for their cheesesteak because it's rubbery, so I did the chicken cheesesteak. The line was one of the shorter ones, and flew by. The chicken cheesesteak was... okay. A bit bland and the most unappetizing color there is for food (just plain grey). But hey, I was hungry, and it hit the spot.
Been here about 15 times, never a problem. Aside from normal hurdles due to covid, they've just been exactly like any subway franchise, and a friendly staff.

Even though it's been quite awhile since I've been here, I'm glad it still tastes as good as it was when it first opened. And they added quite a few items to their menu... 

Their takoyaki is excellent! it actually has PIECES of octopus!!! The broth is still flavorful and noodle is made just perfect. 

Heaven and hell... Perfect for the night =)
Been going for years. Was a regular. First time this year.  The chicken cheesesteak was half the size and $2 more. It was totally dry too. Sad that this has gone so down hill.

This is such a sad establishment.    I can't think of one good burger I ever had here. The fries are always over cooked and cold.   The staff is consistently ghetto.   I used to love Wendy's.   No so much anymore.

So, we came out to the ballpark today and decided to do a cheesesteak taste test!  We could only afford the calories (and $12 price tag) for one each so we decided to split a Tony Luke's  and put it against Campo's, a few booths away.  For both we were purists: "Wiz Without" = plain cheesesteak, cheese whiz, no onions.  Here's the result:  Campo's - awesome fresh roll, cheesesteak made fresh, piping hot and dripping, and meat sliding out the sides.  Perfectly creamy with wizzy steak juices.  Hubby actually picked up spoons so we could catch the remnants.   Tangily delicious.  Downside - meat was a bit chewy and tougher.    Tony Lukes:  although you place the order individually, your order is picked out of a batch of pre-made sandwiches corresponding to your order. When I got back to our seats, the verdict was: roll was good, for me it bore a resemblance to a philly pretzel?! Cheese whiz was concentrated at the roll but not in the meat, unlike Campo.  The meat was more tender but a bit dried out and  felt like it had been sitting around.  Hubby called it a "Lazy Cheesesteak".  Not bad, but in comparison, Campo's got our vote!!!

Haven't been to Hiro Ramen House for many years and was happy to see it's still going strong and serving solid ramen!

We ordered the Pig and Miso (Berkshire port tonkotsu broth with miso, pork belly chasiu, bamboo, corn) and the Gates of Hell (Berkshire port tonkotsu broth with intense chili oil, pork belly chasiu, bamboo, egg), and both were served quickly, piping hot, and had balanced, layered flavor. Highly recommend if you're looking for ramen in Midtown!

An excellent place to enjoy well made, savory Ramen. 
If you're looking for a simple unadorned place to enjoy a simple menu of well made Ramen... this is the place. 
There are a limited choice of dishes...all well made and delicious. 
Prices are very very reasonable. 
Nothing fancy here... just good food at inexpensive prices. 
The decor is bare bones. 
One draw back is the bench and stool seating. It should be improved.

Fast and efficient take out service. Delicious and welcoming. Side dishes made by the cashiers mom (assuming she's the daughter of the owners) felt nice to eat and support a nice family establishment. 5 stars!

After 30 years on this planet, I finally was able to eat my very first authentic Philly cheesesteak. It was worth the wait. The one thing I noticed was how tightly compacted and clean this sandwich was; strange thing to notice, I know, but it was beautifully packed together.  I got the regular cheesesteak, with steak, onions, lettuce, tomato, and Mayo. Simple yet fantastic.   Stop here, you won't regret it.

I live here in Philly and made the terrible mistake to think that an Olde City cheesesteak joint wouldn't be too bad. Wrongo! We had a party of 6 and ate a variety of steaks, including a vegan cheesesteak. Yeah, yeah, I know, but stick with me cause we also had a couple of traditional provolone wits in our party too. Bottom line, very mediocre. Nothing particularly outstanding, just ok (little o, little k to emphasize the mediocrity). Beyond the food, two things led to the 1 star review, service and price. Service was terrible and ruined the entire experience. From the nasty cashier to the curmudgeonly old man seemingly holding the whole place down. Everyone working there had just a straight up shit attitude. Why? Beats me?!?!  On the day we were there the place was jamming so clearly the take was strong, so why so mean?  Make the food, serve it and count the cash. Speaking of cash, the second thing that gave it a 1 star was the price and what you get for it. IMHO the price was high for a decent sammy, but for a very mediocre one, it was straight up highway robbery. My recommendation...anywhere else.

Great lunch special  - $13 (including tax) for ramen, appetizer and salad. Both the Gates of Hell and Gates of Heaven ramen were delicious and great portion size. Got the fried chicken app which was super yummy as well. Salad was also a nice touch. May consider just paying regular price for the ramen ($10) and getting a full fried chicken app next time -- seems about the same price and you get more meat! I can do without the salad ;)

Update: got the full fried chicken app for $7 to share and Porfolio this time, which I felt was much more filling and a better deal than the $13 lunch special. Porfolio soup and ramen were deeelicious...just so so so unfortunate that they only give 1 tiny thin slice of pork :( For $10, the flavor is there, but the protein is not. Flavor is still worth going for though!

This is one of my favorite restaurants ever and it's definitely my favorite sandwich shop! I always order the Mediterranean sandwich without chicken or cheese (to make it vegan) and I absolutely love the zesty hummus. The sandwiches are always warm, fresh, and perfectly toasted. It does cost a little much for me (about $8 for this sandwich) but it's completely worth it. 

My sister loves the big turkey sandwich, broccoli cheddar soap, and oatmeal chocolate chip cookie.

As of October 2020, they have limited indoor dining and plenty of outdoor dining.

Would give 4.5 stars.

Hiro's is everything you want in a ramen. Warm, comforting, rich broth and nice chew to the noodles. I've been at least 8-9 times now and I hope it is here to stay!

My tips: 
- cash only! 
- get the porfilio and ask for extra lemon wedges on the side. The combo of refreshing lemon + savory broth is AMAZING! Don't think I've seen it anywhere else 
- not much seating, so go during off hours (7pm on weekdays) 
- or go during lunch special - runs until 3 pm, includes a ramen, salad, and a smaller version of an app (recommend chicken kaarage) 


Reason it's not a perfect 5 is cause they got cheap with their meat :( Each bowl of ramen used to come with 2 slices of pork, now it's only 1 piece. By comparison, terakawa ramen in Chinatown offers 3 slices of pork while their bowls are 1-2$ cheaper.

Follow whatever instincts led you to this page! We had the Hiro's Inch of Heaven ramen and the Gates of Hell ramen. Both were delicious and we each drained our bowls. The noodles and broth were excellent. There was one waitress running all the tables and, at dinner rush with a convention near by, it was packed. She was a bit over run with parties but worked valiantly through out. We were seated quickly and were served quickly. I hope she was tipped well by all. The kitchen staff and their music were also fun to watch. 

Great spot. Glad we stumbled on it.

I always see this place and I'm happy I finally tried it because this is my new favorite ramen place in Philly. Beats all the other ones in chinatown - hands down. I've tried the black pig ramen and the hiro's inch of heaven ramen. Both amazing but I prefer the hiro's inch of heaven. Ramen is ready within minutes of ordering it and it is steaming hot - which I love. 

If you come here, you have to order the fried chicken on the menu. So crispy. So juicy. The mayo dipping sauce with lemon is the perfect combination. You can't come here and not order the fried chicken. Writing this review right now makes me want to order some. Overall, I love this ramen place and this is the place I'll be going to from now on. 

Giving this a 4 stars because it is cash only and I wish they have more seating, other than that, the food is a 5 stars for me!

We just loved this restaurant while on vacation in Philadelphia. The food was excellent and the entire staff was friendly and fun! The pasta salad was delicious. The cheesesteak sandwich was incredible. We also loved the cannoli. We loved everything about this wonderful restaurant lace and wish we had it locally.

I come here from time to time and the ramen is really good! I personally recommend the Gates of Hell and Hiro's Inch of Heaven! They also have a vegetarian option too for those who don't eat meat! The broth is really rich and not overpowering and the portion sizes are good. I also really like their gyoza! Not to mention the staff is also really nice!

Note: they're cash only!

Not my favorite cheesesteak spot, but convenient  location and average Cheesesteak. My friend had the heater sandwich and said it wasn't as spicy as expected. The staff was friendly and helpful and restaurant has a lot of seating options

Honestly, the ramen here was some of the best I had had in ages! And I live in NYC which has a pretty hoppin' ramen scene! I might need to start coming down to Philly more often just for this spot! 

On a Monday night, we were looking for a simple but filling dinner; as the temps had finally dropped into the 50s on a mid-October day, ramen was calling our names. Off to Hiro we went! Small but undeniably cozy, surrounded by our waitress greeted and seated us immediately. The menu offered many bowls - virtually all reasonably priced at $10 a bowl - and we both went for the Black Pig: Berkshire pork and bonito broth, burnt garlic oil, pork belly, bean sprout, bamboo, scallion, and naruto. The bowl hit it out of the PARK, wow! I love burnt (black) garlic oil added to my ramen, so that one me over immediately. The pork belly was charred but still tender. The broth, thankfully, was not too salty, something that sinks so many bowls I've had over the past few years. The flavor of the actual broth shined through! My one disappointment is that it didn't come with an egg included, a fact I didn't realize until after I got my bowl and saw on the menu that, indeed, it was extra. I mean, who doesn't love egg in their ramen? (Well, perhaps vegans eating a vegan bowl of ramen somewhere. Ha!) 

But WOW. We left so happy, so satisfied. I've never had ramen in Philly before, and I would not hesitate to return, not even for a second! Days later, and I'm still so happy when I think about my meal there!
No fries earlier this week.  Apparently, they were transitioning from one oil to a different one.  Unacceptable!

Lunch special $13= salad + karaage fried chicken + ramen ! 

Their lunch special is such a good deal! Don't miss the chance! 

Karaage fried chicken: 
Nicely battered and flaky on the outside and juicy and tender inside! Worth every buck! 

Gates of Hell Ramen: 

I asked to have the chili oil on the side so I can adjust the spice level as I go. Noodle was chewy and adsorbs the right amount of broth! Chashu was definitely a highlight - I rarely see ramen Chashu being extra roasted on the side which gives it such an additive aroma! The ramen broth to me personally is a bit lacking in depth - I suspect they only used water and pork bones - not the rich deep kind you see in Ippudo or the likes. But with lunch special at $13, I can't complain at all! Overall I highly recommend coming here for ramen if you are in the area

On a drive through Philly we decided to stop for cheesesteaks and decided on Campo's to meet my vegan preferences. Unfortunately, their vegan cheesesteak, called the Vegan Works, is not as advertised. I was charged $1 additional for vegan cheese and $2 extra for vegan bread. I do not appreciate the false advertising. If a sandwich is called vegan, it should not require extra costs and substitutions to be actually made vegan. None of these charges were noted on the menu and vegan cheese was listed as an option in the product description. I was disappointed from the start.

I had hopes that the cheesesteak itself would make up for it but unfortunately it did not. The vegan bread, which I believe was sourdough, was incredibly tough and by the end my jaw was sore and tired. I ditched the last bit of bread and opted to just eat the fillings. The fillings were decent. Nothing I would go out of my way for, but about average. With all the extra charges I paid about $16 for a pretty mediocre sandwich.

My husband for The Works, which is their classic cheesesteak, and he was also unimpressed. 

I left Campo's feeling taken advantage of and with my appetite unsatisfied. For vegan options, I would not recommend Campo's.

I read a lot of reviews on this place, after I had already ordered Graeme on a food delivery app. While I cannot speak to their specific handling of food and social distancing and such with covid. I can speak to the quality of food, and it was friggin good. I decided to go with their cheesy bread and Mac and cheese calzone thing (bad at remembering names) the cheesy bread came with a garlic butter sauce that is I kid you not literally to die for  I know this cause my delivery driver tried to kill me just so he could keep it all to himself (kidding) but seriously i dipped not only the cheesy bread, but the actual calzone in the butter sauce cause I didn't wanna waste it. This place gets a very high rating for me due to food quality. As I said I cannot speak to any of their food handling techniques or anything they are doing in store as my fat ass opted to have it delivered so I could lay on my couch and not move, but totally worth getting again and again and again!

I loved this place. I only got the ramen, but it was awesome. I called for take out and it was ready as soon as I got there. I ordered the Gates of Hell with extra pork and added corn. The broth was thick, rich, and flavorful - not too spicy, but had a little kick to it. The noodles were everything I want in Ramen - thick, wavy, long, and a little chewy. The only thing I didn't love was the pork - you don't get much of it, and it was a little too charred for my taste. Aside from that, I loved it and will definitely be back. Just wish they were on a delivery app as the location is a little difficult to park for pick up!

Bland, tasteless, no seasoning, no salt, skimpy on cheese, onions cut in chunks and not carmelized.

What is it with the cheesesteaks in Philly?  I went to Pat's, I went here, should I try more or do they all offer the same bland combo of meat and cheese that I could make better in my own kitchen??

Two stars because the girl behind the counter wasn't a total jerk (just testy - hopefully because of the heat and crowd and not because they hate their jobs) and because the sandwich was edible despite not being very enjoyable.

My friend brought me here for a late night hoagie, stating it was one of the best in the city. I ended up purchasing a Philly soft pretzel with cheese and having them wrap my Italian Hoagie for lunch tomorrow. 

The staff was just finishing up the night and were very accommodating as their last guests of the evening. Thank you for making a Chicago native feel welcome and enjoy a solid meal for his last lunch in your fine city!

I love this place. My sister's Japanese teacher brought us here for lunch one time and ever since it's my favorite place to get karaage chicken and veggies yummy. The Hiro inch heaven ramen is really good too and they have a full bar. It may look like a little hole in the wall from the outside but it will surprise you. The service was incredible from the moment we walked into the time we left. I had never been in before so we tried several menu items, all of them were simply wonderful. I highly recommend this gem of a restaurant.

I've walked by a lot and this place seemed like it would be a good neighborhood spot. Always a decent number of people inside. There are some cute decorations and you can buy stuffs like pocky sticks or face masks at the counter. 
But, honestly, we are here for the ramen, and it was was just not good. Worse than not good. The vegetable ramen was downright weird. Not sure what was in the black broth, but it had a strange sweet flavor.
The inch of heaven ramen broth was ok, but there was one slice of pork which seemed a little meager, and tasted a bit old. The bamboo tasted like fake lemon-lime, I'm not sure where that flavor came from, but it was not pleasant. And the add on of vegetables means a small handful of mixed salad greens. I love salad greens, but 2 dollars for a few leaves? On a hot soup? The noodles themselves were fine, but given the totality of the experience, I won't be back.

I went on a segway philly cheesesteak tour, and yes you heard me right. I rode around on a segway and ate cheesesteaks. It was way more enjoyable than I thought. After trying 5 of the top cheesesteak places in philly, Campos was my favorite. There's something about their whiz to steak ratio and their bread. Muwah! The perfect combo. If you're visiting philly and want a good cheesesteak, I highly recommend Campo's!

This was stop #3 in my search for the best philly cheesesteak. And of the four spots I tried, by a slight edge it was the best!

Campos Philly cheesesteak is a spot located on market street and well regarded as a hot spot for steaks. In my search for a great philly cheesesteak, I sought out well seasoned meat, good bread and size. My scale was slightly weighted toward meat and is why I favored Campos. 

Let me be clear. The meat is not slap yo mama seasoned and %100 flavorful but there is a slight season there. Bread was good but Sonnys has better bread. And size factor is about average. Prices are spot on with other places at about $10.50.

4 stars because it was good but didn't knock my socks off. Despite this, Id go again.

Food: 4/5
Bang/Buck: 4/5

I judge Ramen on broth consistency, noodle texture, and execution of the pork. 

This ramen had flavorful and smooth broth, super tender and fatty pork, and perfectly chewy noodles at a good price. 

Hiro was excellent. I'll be back. Just one thing, I wish my server reminded me of the lunch special. I wound up sort of not getting the optimal value.
I generally come here instead of Tony Luke's if I am at CBP. The chicken cheesesteak and regular cheesesteak are also great!

Hiro is my favorite ramen shop in Philadelphia and that's saying something because I'm quite a ramen snob. The noodles are cooked perfectly. The broth is rich and flavorful and they don't steer too far away form the classic flavors. My favorite is inch of heaven.

Love this new location!! They do indian food in wraps! It's excellent after a few drinks and very portable! I was one of their first 50 customers at this new location and I could see they had everything up and running very well! They have another location, but I'm excited about this location on South Street. We stopped after a show at the TLA. I ordered the first two things on the menu. One of them was chicken tikka. The chicken was kabab style so naturally it could have been a little less dry, but it didn't bother me. I can see them offering dipping sauces or putting yogurt sauce inside if people like. Also, their regular lassi was amazing!! I've never had such a thick delicious lassi before. I don't know if it was supposed to be so thick, but I loved it!! I can't wait to bring more people to Spice End on South Street!!!
Bruh y'all said y'all open and I pulled up and it was pitch black. Mane what the fuck!

I'm a vegetarian so I didn't expect many options at a cheese steak restaurant, but I was surprised to see both vegetarian and vegan options. The inclusive menu was a great addition to a city that specializes in meat based delicacies. I tried the vegan cheese steak with provolone cheese and it was the same size and portion as the steak and chicken sandwiches. The sandwich wasn't that great and tasted a bit flavorless. I can't say this was a memorable dish or something I would get again, but I was happy to have an option. You'll need to make sure you have cash. Luckily we had some, but there weren't any signs or notices on the menu. There is some seating inside and outside, but we went on the weekend so those seats filled up. Christ Church is across the street and there are benches and nice grass areas to eat your meal on.

Horrendous Service
I was waiting outside around opening time for for a dine in only to have the employees say that they arent open. Needless to say, I was very frustrated and got back to the car to do the drive through. 
There were no cars at all and it took at least a minute of me yelling into the speaker box to see if anyone was there.
Next step is paying - you would think that this step would be the quickest, but I had the same issue. I stopped by the window with no acknowlegement, so I figured that they wanted me to goto the next window. Drove forward a few feet to have someone yell at me to pay.... which is what I was trying to do.
I guess it is what it is and I shouldn't expect much.

What's wrong with people's sense of taste? Completely under seasoned.  No salt. Dry. Shredded lamb. Like, what? If you're craving halal Cart from walnut st this sure isn't it. Just wait and go get that tomorrow. 

I'd avoid it. My girlfriend knew better and for a cheesesteak from little Italy pizza down the street. Superb.

I ordered 2 meals and the female taking the drive thru order had such an attitude. When I approached the window to pay, she told me the price. I informed her i ordered 2 meals not 1. The initial bad attitude she had from my order 5 minutes prior now escalated to arguing with me in regards to what I said to her. Ok lady, enjoy your day. I will not take food from you, give you my money, and never return to this location.

I came here while on my East Coast adventure. I couldn't leave Philly without eating a cheesesteak. I was at the liberty bell and needed to find a place stat and up popped Campo's Deli. It's downtown and the vibe is great. This is a family owned business you can tell. They are super friendly!! The only downside... CASH only... 
Now the food OMG... SOOOOO good... It's true Philly does have the best cheesesteaks... I will definitely come here again when I am in Philly...

Seating can be difficult around lunch hour but the food is worth it. I just read a lot of the reviews on here for the heck of it and I feel bad now for Campos because the majority are from out of state who are in Philly for the first time, getting their first cheese steak. I wanted to first say that every single time I've been at Campos my food was delish. I love your cheese steaks and love your hoagies. The rolls are worthy to write home about! To all the out of towners that posted reviews, I wanted to point out a few things. First, comparing to Pat's or Geno's is off the mark. They are both gross. Also to see so many negative reviews due to the fact that it was not what you were expecting. That's not fair, simple as that. Almost everyone in Philly puts ketchup on their steak sandwich so it's not a cover up. It's part of it. I have lived in Philly my entire life and have to disagree with the stereotype that we are rude. I always wondered why because I find Philly to be very friendly. I've been in many cites across the country and Philly stands at the top. Everyone in Philly has their favorite stop. They don't write bad reviews, they just don't go back. 5 stars from me because I've been here many times and I know the food is authentic and delicious, coming from a Philly. If you are reading and from out of town, it's a good place to try. Pat's and Geno's is a major tourist spot combined with drunk people that live here that ARE rude. You will end up with a churning stomach for 24 hours. Campo's is a nice place. As for the water comments I read. I don't know but that does sound like BS. Charge me for bottled water but tap water, go ahead and try it.

I was recently in the Olde City area for lunch, which is unusual, and I had to get a quick bite.  I strolled in Campo's and was greeted with a "HI-A" by the cutest older woman who immediately made me chuckle.  I ordered an Original Cin sandwich which if i remember correctly has their homemade caesar dressing on it.  As simple as it was, it might have been one of the best cold sandwiches I've had in years.  Since then, I've been back on a couple different occasions.  I had a cheesesteak with extra american which was delicious.  The bread was not overwhelming, it was all about the meat.  The last time I was there, I ate the Mia Salad which was out of this world.  It's rough to get a really good salad, not pre-made, that turns out to be a really good meal.  Chicken was fantastic, off the charts.  
I'm not sure if some of the people who have reviewed eat much in Philadelphia, Center City in particular, but the prices are competitve with every other deli that I've been to.
The staff couldn't be friendlier, they actually start to know your face.  I enjoy the fact that the girl at the register is on the ball and maintains a pleasant personality while I can sometimes be indecisive about my food.  I sometimes have to wait  5 minutes before I order in other places and I end up walking out.
Highly recommended!!!

there's lots of cheesesteaks in the city, and lots of places to go get one.  there's even lots of opinions as to who makes the best steak.  i'm not writing about the best.  i'm writing about what what must be one of the worst.  this one is known as "the heater."  

there just isn't anything good to say about this $12.50 disaster.  with a roll soaked in hot sauce, there really isn't anything else you can taste, except for grease; with meat, whizz, and onions all pretty uninspired and tasteless.  i'm not sure how they do it.  

what they did do was get that sandwich into my hands in about 2 minutes.  i'm guessing that this hot mess was mostly assembled and waiting for me well before i even got on the line.  

campos probably knows approximately how many steaks it will sell in a night, and they'll sell them.  consequently, they just don't put too much effort into making that sandwich any good. that's a shame because hey, sometimes you want a steak.  it should just be better than edible.

Yummy!

My first Philly Cheese Steak in Philly was a great one. The sandwich was not to greasy and full of perfectly cooked meat and tastiness. 

Sandwiches came fast and easy. Prices were alright..$2.50 for a bottle of water was a bit much, but I didn't care I was starving and thirsty.

If you are in the neighborhood I'd make my way into this sandwich shop.

It's a small shop so squeeze in and make yourself comfy.
Terrible. I ordered food from them on Grubhub and they were "too busy" to make my order within the time it was supposed to arrive.

I ordered the Honey-Seared chicken. While it was being prepared, I noticed one of the food handlers fix her shirt with a glove on and then top my chicken with vegetables using that same glove on her hand. I decided to pick the vegetables off and start to eat it anyway. Unfortunately, many of the pieces of chicken were pink on the edges. At this point I was completely disgusted with the food. I decided to let the manager know and showed her the meat. They offered to re-make it or to issue a refund. I opted for the refund. There was no apology for the bad food. I added two pictures but it is somewhat difficult to see the pinkness in the meat.

Food and service are always amazing. If your pizza comes out sub par in their eyes they will make you a new one and give you both. They are constantly doing promotions and giving out free stuff. Which is a big plus seeing as though it is in the middle of Temple"s campus. It's a great spot to meet up and eat with friends.

Delicious food and good portion size. I didn't feel cheated on the protein portion at all on my Bangkok Beef. After reading reviews I realized customizing was an option - something that is not made clear on the menu or by the girl at the counter. (We were very clearly first timers and there was no line - no offer to explain how the process worked.) Luckily we picked a good signature bowl and were quite happy. Looking forward to coming back and exploring the custom options!

Employees move very slow expect to be in here at least 15 minutes or more. Also no type of air conditioning in the summer so bad choice if you want somewhere to relax and enjoy some fast food employees look very miserable

Luke warm place. While my brisket sandwich was ok, it wasn't great. They just need to step up their game. Food was on the cold side, biscuit fell apart, pickles were weak, and the no homemade hot sauce on the tables, just crystal. I wanna see this place do well, and I think they can, but they've got to raise their bar.

First impressions:
Cute place. Decor is simple and clean, music is good, and the person behind the counter was friendly. Check.
Placing an order:
Not offering chicken on a biscuit for breakfast is blasphemy. Charging $7 for a bacon, egg, and cheese biscuit? That thing better be damn good. 
Post order:
15 min wait while they made sure the eggs were hot. The presentation is cute. I like the paper plate, tray, and the crystal hot sauce on the table. 
The biscuit:
The most important part of this experience. As a self declared biscuit connoisseur I take this very seriously. The flavor of the biscuit itself was excellent. It was too dry, but I can excuse that with the flavor it packed. The execution was poor. In the south when you order a biscuit with any topping other than gravy, you can pick it up and eat it with your hand. That is the point. This was an ordeal. Stop over thinking it. Simplify. Go to Sunshine Biscuit Barn with this and they'll laugh at you. I'm torn because I want this place to succeed and bring biscuits to more people, but I also want people to have a traditional southern biscuit experience.

Not often downtown Philly at lunchtime but found this place the other day. I remembered reading about Scratch in the paper awhile back so decided to give it a try. 
I opted for the fried chicken biscuit with the cabbage slaw and a cup of coffee. My meal came with a bunch of freshly made chips as well. Looked great and tasted great too.  The biscuit was flavorful and a little crumbly. The chicken had a good flavor as well,  though maybe a larger piece would work a little better. The slaw was outstanding and what fell off the sandwich, I ate with my fork!
There appeared to be a variety of store combinations as well as "make your own" options.  I would imagine this place is awesome for breakfast.  Looking forward to my next time downtown Philly at breakfast or lunch time.

I came here because of all the hype that had been circulating about southern biscuits in center city. People acted like these biscuits were going to heal my body and save my life. 

But let me tell you: these biscuits are NASTY. They taste worst than Pillsbury its really a shame. I had the Brisket Biscuit. It was stringy, a little cold, and gross. I wanted to order a Fried Chicken Biscuit, but they were all out. I tried to get the Pulled Pork Biscuit, surprise! there were none!  I wanted a side, but they were all out of sides. I stood there like "what do you even have here!!!!"

So, I paid 9$ for a crappy biscuit with sub-par toppings. Apparently, the joke was on me.

Can I have my $10 and 4,321 calories back, please?

The first thing I asked the staff was if their brisket was fatty or lean. "Oh, we cut off all the fat for you," they said.

They lied. There was more fat on my scratch biscuit than meat. The brisket had little flavor, and the horseradish mayo had zero bite. 

Shame, because the decor is pretty cute and it's a fun concept. Pass.

I fear this location is Tony Luke's in name only. The food is just no where near as good as the south philly original.  
For three sandwiches, two burgers, and two orders of fries we paid $60. For that kind of money you expect something a little better than average pizza place call out. But in my opinion it wasn't even as good as most neighborhood pizza places. 
My dad's roast pork sandwich was really dry. Cheesesteak didn't have much meat on it and was also dry. I got a chicken parm sandwich that would have been ok if there was substantially more gravy on it, but alas, this was also dry. Fries were good though! And the people working here were lovely. But unfortunately I won't be back to this location. Tony Luke's needs a little quality control in other locations.

We eat homemade biscuits at home all the time - they are one of our favorite things - so we were looking forward to having a great biscuit sandwich at Scratch Biscuits a couple of weeks after it opened.

We were sadly disappointed.

My bacon-egg-and-cheese biscuit was pretty much inedible. The biscuit was so crumbly that it fell apart before I could even take the first bite. The place cooks their scrambled eggs ahead in bulk in a pan (it says "baked eggs") and cuts them into squares. Those eggs were so salty that I nearly choked. The bacon was cooked very soft, no where near crunchy, so it felt as if I were eating nearly raw bacon. The "American cheese" that the menu listed for this sandwich was actually a white sauce (mostly flour and milk) with a little American cheese in it.

Hubs (who grew up in North Carolina) ordered a fried chicken sandwich. He had the same problem with his biscuit being crumbly. He did say the fried chicken was very good, but he disliked the slaw on the sandwich.

We decided there are too many really good places in this great food city for us to waste our money in visiting Scratch Biscuits again.
Ridiculously slow and poor service. Food was very mediocre.

I was so excited to try Paratha Roll. it reminded me of a spot in NYC called Kati Rolls.

While Kati Rolls are smaller, and you need two or three to get a meal out of them, Paratha Rolls are burrito like big.

There is so much potential here. I love the concept. The roll was okay. The big problem is the insides are bland. They need more seasoning. They need more flavor. It was a complete bust. I might as well have mixed cardboard and rubber and eaten it.

The only reason I give it two stars is because the Samosas and Mango Lasi were pretty good. Otherwise, stay away from this place.

I was excited to see that Taco Bell has finally reopened in Moravian, as I often frequent it whenever I am in University City for a quick bite before work or between exams. However, this location is disappointing to say the least. Even after they reopened as a Pizza Hut/Taco Bell joint storefront with new shiny signs, the quality of their food and service remains unchanged. They are consistent about skimping on their ingredients, and do the same for their customer service! All that being said, it is a Taco Bell. Therefore, I will do what I need to do to get my Mexican pizza!

The chicken did smell good. Unfortunately the taste was not the same. Service was quick and cold. Seemed like the employees were not happy to be there. Now the chicken, the chicken was under cooked. Bones were broken and the meat was tainted with bone marrow.

   For the most part Popeye's usually has very good chicken depending on the location, owned, and staff. This appears to be a bad location.  Hopefully it was a just a bad batch of chicken, but you're trying your luck buying here.

I checked this place out last night with my husband. We tried the Cheesesteak Fries and the Original Sliders. Both were really good! I was kind of reluctant to spend $8 on fries, but they definitely are not shy with their toppings -- we got as much steak on our fries as we would on an actual cheesesteak. Very filling, and worth the price! Will be back again!

Worst Wendy's EVER. Ate here once and got norovirus. Means that someone pooped, did not wash hands, and served me food. Never again! I'd rather eat a hoagie from the sidewalk that someone tossed out of a moving vehicle. Also, when the person sitting next to you rolls all of their possessions into said restaurant in a suitcase with wheels, it's time to leave.

So this Taco Bell is now a join Pizza Hut and Taco Bell, which is a lot more exciting than the previous A&W version. I have been going to this taco bell for years and it has remained consistently average. I have been to taco bells that are WAY worse than this (if you remember the old Drexel Taco Bell you know shitty Taco Bell's). I know they have a no refill rule but honestly, I have never had a problem getting a refill. As long as the normal staff are there, you are fine. It's overall a fine, normal, what you expect from Taco Bell, location.

If i could give a 2.5, I would've. I've been here twice. The workers are nice enough, albeit they do tend to rush you, or speak in a language other than English (i don't like that, especially when someone other than ME is handling the food). They tend to not give you a lot of the fixin's the other SaladWorks give (I've been to some where there's an overabundance of things and not a whole lot of salad, not that I'm complaining for those SaladWorks'). Many of the veggies were improperly cut; stalks are BAD (okay, snobby culinary arts student speaking here), and the buffalo chicken pieces were fatty, grisely, or just plain ew... Cost me about $10, which is a bit pricey for a poor student... meh, it's still better than some of the CCP cafeteria food...

I urge the owners of this nice looking cafe to step it up or lower the price...

pay attention to your market! you are located in south street next to one of the most famous spots for a Gyro (SSS). you are also from walking distance to hundreds of gyro carts and although they are not better than sss they are cheap. SSS has better gyros than you and they are 6.50...

Either you step up your game with fresh lamb meat or something that will excite someone to pay 30% more for your product or sadly sit and wait for the unevitable.

your sweets looked great, i make some really good ones but they never look as nice as yours, but it seems like you have way more inventory than you are actually selling which i hope does not suggest i am purchasing last weeks goods... 

all in all a nice looking place a with very nice and attentive staff, but not nice enough for me to pay 10 for another gyro, lets face it if you cant make a great gyro at a decent price, you are losing money and customers...

good luck and hopefully my advice will lead you to make changes that will bring me and many others back...

A friend and I shared the classic and the cheesesteak poutine. Both were awesome. Great prices for the amount of food you get and plenty of options to choose from that will satisfy pretty much anyone. Highly recommend this place!

If I could give this McDonalds no stars I would. I waited 20 minutes in the drive thru line to pay, then when I asked if my food had also been waiting that long, the cashier said, "I don't know, I just got here". When I received my food, the Large Fries were half full, and cold. I asked for new fries, and was forced to wait another 5 minutes. Absolute waste of time, no napkins or condiments, in the bag, when asking if my drink was pink lemonade, which I ordered in the beginning, I was told "we don't have that."
These people shouldn't even be paid the measly minimum wage I'm sure they are earning. Worst.

I would try to give this DQ a good review but the past 3 times I've gone there they were closed when their hours say they should be open.

I JUST WANT A GODDAMN  BLIZZARD

This is innovation my friends.  Finally, our two great takeout loves piled into one.  Sweetly spicy Indian wrapped like the good ol' burrito.  And the bread is perfect.  Somewhere between naan and a great homemade tortilla.  Just thick enough to satisfy your bite when you break through to the tender meat and delicious spice inside.    Go there before you have to listen to some girl from the burbs bragging about it at work.

slow,  bad service.  when i walked in there was one person ahead of me at the counter and he appeared to have most of his order already yet it took another 10 mins for the counterperson to take my order.  ordering was painless BUT she waited until about 5 mins AFTER i paid to tell me there would be a 3 minute wait for burgers so i immediately asked for a refund. apparently that process wasnt streamlined either. she disappeared into the back of the restaurant to find the manager who came out and apparently never gave a refund to a credit card before and said he could only give me cash.  super annoying.  never going back.

Wok street was decent, quick, and cheap. Staff was friendly and the restaurant was clean. I created my own bowl with white rice, beef, teriyaki etc. Beef was well cooked but I wasn't a huge fan of the teriyaki.

All in all I would eat here again if I needed a fast food option.

Love the concept of "pick your meat" and lots of cool burger choices to be had. The bun which is homemade was delicious! The sweet potato fries were good; I would have just liked a couple of choices of condiments to go with them. The burger was huge and very filling. The only negative with this place was that due to the heat, and maybe not the best AC system, we were a little hot... but I will be back!

Oh, oh god.  I have no idea how this establishment is still in business.  I waited 15 minutes for a pre-prepared block of egg being kept warm in a tin container, a really hard gluten free biscuit that fell apart the minute I tried to pick it up (and not in a 'fresh out of the oven' way), a very underripe 'heirloom' tomato, and it was $11.95.  

Do not try eating eating anything on the menu as an actual sandwich -- it's impossible.  My friend got a regular biscuit (as in, not gluten free) and hers was a mealy, fall apart mess as well.  Neither one of us could manage to finish the pile of shit on our plates.

Please, I implore you -- do not spend money on food here for any reason.

Such a redemption for me ! My first experience was at the South Philly one, abd it was nothing special. But this place was incredible ! Guy was friendly when taking our order; took my parents for my step-dad's birthday. It was his first time there and he loved it too ! Three cheesesteaks and some salt-and-vinegar fries, everything was incredible. I will definitely be going back.

Stressed out over my impending midterm, I wanted greasy comforting fast food for lunch (I also needed something quick so I could get back to cramming).  This Wendy's is directly across from Jefferson Hospital so I ran on over.  The food here isn't on par with other Wendy's I've been to in Jersey.  It was dry nuggets, soggy fries, and over seltzered soda.  The countertop looked like it had been freshly wiped, however it looks like it was wiped with a dirty or greasy rag, leaving streaks of grime on the counters.

On the positive side, the staff was friendly and got me in and out quickly and with a smile.  But their friendliness probably won't bring me back again.

The people making the Blizzards here are friendly and get the job done pretty efficiently and quickly. Not much else to say here - if you're in the mood for something cold, creamy, and calorie-laden, feel free to stop by!

This place for sure deserves better than the 2.5 stars it currently has. Something like 3.5 stars, but Yelp doesn't allow half star ratings, so I'm giving it 3 ("A-OK") because I can't quite say "Yay! I'm a fan" (4 stars).

I had the Fried Chicken Picnic Biscuit Sandwich. The flavor was good, with a pleasant heat from the cayenne ranch dressing. The biscuit was moist with a tangy butteryness. The chicken was tender and juicy and tasted like chicken, which is more than I can say for a lot of chicken at this price point.

Unfortunately, the biscuit lacked the crisp exterior I remember from growing up in Texas (with family from Alabama), and perhaps relatedly, the sandwich completely fell apart on my first bite. The fried exterior of the chicken likewise lacked textural definition. Overall, I'd say the sandwich was good but not great.

And that's the problem: there are enough very good to great cheap eats in Philly that there's no reason to come back here. Granted, I don't know of a better place to get biscuits in the city, but if you're like me, you'll prefer to wait for the "real thing" rather than settle for this near miss. Here's hoping this place gets the chance to figure things out though because it's a good concept and done right it'd be a great addition to the city's food scene. 

P.S. I haven't taken advantage of this, but from 11 pm to 1 am on Fridays and Saturdays they sell $5 fried chicken, pimento cheese, and pickle biscuit sandwiches in the alley out back. Even if the texture is unimproved, at that price that sounds like some pretty darn good drunk food.

I'm sad to leave a review like this but this place was pretty disappointing. I walked in super hungry during a shopping spree in the area and was excited at the prospect of biscuits. There was one particular one with pickles - which I also love!

I received my biscuit sandwich quickly as I was the only person there at around 11 am. However, somehow it was still cold despite supposedly being freshly made. Additionally it was so dry. Like I could barely get a bite down (ever try a saltine challenge? Kinda like that.). I took out the pickles, ate them, and left the majority of my sandwich.

I had high hopes for this place so maybe I'll give it another try if coerced by someone and maybe it was just an off day but my first experience there was NOT a pleasant one.

Absolutely delicious! Walked by and went in on a whim, and loved the experience. I got the 5 Buck Cluck, which is actually only $5 on Fridays and Saturdays, but for $8.50 I didn't mind the clever name that wasn't necessarily applicable on a Saturday morning.

The sandwich was fantastic: great, crumbly, light biscuit with lightly fried, juicy chicken, fantastic smoky and creamy pimiento cheese, and what I assume to be house made, thin pickles that added just the right amount of acidity and crunch. It's like the chick fil a breakfast biscuit sandwich but everything is better and covered in smoky pimiento cheese. 

Also the decor is really great, and everyone was really friendly. The owner was telling my boyfriend and I that their wall was painted by muralists, which shows in its unique, colorful details. They also have a card that gets you a free biscuit after 12, so I've got another great reason to go back!
Great fries ... and fried items ...... if you love that kinda thing ....has a fast food feel to it ( which I can take or leave ).       A nice little business in east girard avenue ......

This probably would have been delicious served in the restaurant--take out makes it a bit difficult because the biscuit has more time to soak up the juice from the meat. Still pretty good, though. The brisket was good and quite tender, and the biscuit was moist (and gigantic). It's a perfectly serviceable and tasty sandwich, even after delivery. The thing that would have made the sandwich a 4-star are the toppings. To compete with the brisket and biscuit, pickled onions need to stand on their own. The pickling was barely discernible, and the sauce was mild as well. Give me more crunch and more bold flavors, and I'd be happier.
Staff is nice and friendly here. I ordered chocolate blizzard. The ice cream is standard like others store. This place is not big. Good for small group

Similar to the first time I came here, there wasn't much of a line around noon.  Ordered the chicken teriyaki bowl.  This is definitely a better option than the banh mi.  Good teriyaki sauce that covers the chicken, roasted edamame, and pickled veggies.  I'd probably opt for the large portion next time, but the regular satisfied my hunger.  

My buddy got the Thai iced tea and it was way too sweet - would not get this here.

When I heard that a biscuit place was coming to Philly, I was sooooo excited, considering how much I love a great biscuit!  Today I was in the office and my friend/co-worker and I ditched our normal breakfast faves and walked the five blocks to scratch.  (Yes, we saw the previous bad reviews, but we figured there were some haters in the atmosphere, b/c how can you mess up a biscuit)?!? 

Well, now we see why there are so many sub-par yelp reviews.  1) we found it very odd that there was no AM chicken biscuit option! Wait, what? You are marketing yourself as a taste of the "south" so much so that there's a sign that reads "I'm fixing' to" on the wall, yet you don't have a chicken and biscuit breakfast option?!?! 

2) no jelly / jam options other than "peach preserves" ... I get it "Georgia peach" ...
Cute!  BUT, if you don't hurry up and add some Grape and strawberry jam to the mix, please & thank you! 

3) orange juice - ok I get it, when places get away with serving fresh squeezed orange juice and charging you $5 for it!  Initially my thought is always "wth?" But then I take a sip of juicy/pulpy $5 orange juice and consider the price tag worth it!  I was hoping for the same experience here, but the orange juice in the cup left me feeling that there was an empty Evergreen bottle or those orange juice cartons from grade school in the back, as it's contents had been poured into my $5 cup.  No pulp? No real orange juice flavor? Tasted like 100% from concentrate - whatever that means!

With all of this I was still hopeful that the actual biscuit sandwich would be good, dare I say great!  Sadly, I took a bite and couldn't stomach the rest ... I ordered the sandwich with the sausage / cheddar / onion etc, but asked for just cheddar and sausage as the onion and other ingredient seemed like a bit much for breakfast.  Unfortunately the sausage had the shape / size of a hamburger slider and the cheddar looked like some sort of soft cheese (cross between cheese wiz and nacho cheese dip) ... Again,
Not what I want to see on my breakfast sandwich!  I took an ever so slight bite of the sausage and broke off a few bits of the biscuit that weren't covered in that cheese sauce before I had to face reality - this $14 breakfast (sandwich and oj) just wasn't for me!

There were other issues - including I ordered a peach preserve on the side and it didn't make it in my order (In hindsight - maybe I was supposed to get that from the refrigerated section, who knows?). 

Despite the low rating, I hope that this place gets over it's identity crisis - decides to be the true southern broad that she was born to be, despite her 215 location!  Ditch all the extras - (no one wants onions in the morning ) and add a darn chicken biscuit and regular jam (strawberry and grape) to the menu! If and when these changes happen, I will be back and will be willing to throw some more stars Scratches way (look at my other reviews - I'm generally very generous)!!

I just went basic for my first try, biscuits and the salted molasses butter. Good biscuit, flaky but not falling apart, but huge. Did not expect such a big biscuit. Like the salt/sweet of the molasses butter also.

Best part, completely accessible by wheelchair or mobility scooter.
The term fast food should never be uttered in this restaurant. 15 min for a simple meal without any extras. Disgrace to have the Wendy's logo which otherwise is the best fast food in the country.

A nightmare aside from the sticky floors and long waits - there's always at least one crazy addict screaming in a corner that none seems to do anything about.  It's an anxiety fest, hold on to your valuables! In desperate need of a security guard. 

The wait is always at least 15 minutes (that's if you're the only one there)

The filth alone make me wonder how they pass health inspections. It's rare to see a server wearing gloves.

Drive up Erie lol. Every time I go here they forget something an apple pie a hotdog always one thing missing yet they charge me and when I go bk they claim I ate it. So please check ya bag. Today I got all cold food.

Wow, I really wanted to like this place but some drawbacks took it down a few stars. First --no coffees ready when I came in the morning. That's a service issue. Second, The biscuit I ordered was not heated through. They make breakfast sandwich like McDonald's--Piling pre-cooked egg and meat on biscuit & then heated up. The cheese was not even melted. Disappointing. Chips on the side were stale. Finally, the bacon was a cut of fat, with very little meat. The biscuit was dry-but tasty. All in all, the biscuit experience was OK but the entire visit went stale on me  so to speak

We received a large platter of the Burma from Baklava Cafe as a gift to our department at work.  The burmas were overwhelming sweet as if they were submerged in honey.  I thought it was just my taste buds because I can't handle overly sweet desserts.  But everyone in my department agreed that it was too sweet.  What a shame, the platter came with about 40 pieces and we only had about 10 of them.

I was excited to order from this place as I saw it was new from grubhub.  Ordered the Moroccan chicken as it is listed as one of their special items.  Food is inedible.  Chicken was greasy and covered in fatty, loose skin.  Was supposed to get hummus and tahini and got neither.  Instead got some greasy eggplant?  Chicken and eggplant were cold in the center and only lukewarm on the outside.  Rice looked promising but was inedible.  I spent 22 dollars for this abomination plus baklava which doesn't look that great either.  Ridiculous.

Yum! Yum! I love this new fusion spot! It reminds me of a Chinese "Chiptole" how the ordering and preparation is setup. 

Wok Street is from the owners of the Hai Street chain, aka famous for their sushi burrito. 

Generally, it is a tasty lunch treat but I did spend around $13 for a regular size Bangkok dish and Summer Rolls. Not my goal for lunch but nice food nonetheless.

They have other tasty items, like Japanese Matcha Tea and ginger lemonade and I would recommend this spot to my friends.

I first had a Scratch biscuit at a food truck event at Frankford and Girard. I had the Brisket Biscuit and it was wonderful. Full of flavor and sooo good.  I have been in the store on Chestnut at least two other occassions and I was dissappointed each time. The Brisket Biscuit I ordered today was pretty bad. The Brisket was dry without even a hint of any sauce. It was not prepared anything like the first time i tried it, and the  biscuit itself was dry and stiff. Thtee times and u r out.

I got takeout from spencer's with a friend shortly after they opened. The menu looked great as did the pictures of the burgers online (the burgers looked even better in real life!) but the phone call into the restaurant was a bit tricky. It was hard to understand the voice on the other end of the phone. We were told they would be ready in 15 but they were ready in just over 25 minutes. But the burgers were still piping hot when we ate them back in our apartment, which was awesome. The burgers were delicious and clearly made of the freshest ingredients.

The creativity in the burgers was also excellent. Mine was based on breakfast, with sausage and eggs, served on a biscuit, which proved to be very messy (I had to eat it with a fork and knife) but so tasty. My friend had a mexican-inspired burger, which she raved about. We tried the plain and sweet potato fries, which were good, but not very crispy. 

Overall, the burgers were reasonably priced. I thought they compared price-wise to any other restaurant-quality burger in university city. The hours are a bit odd, but I'm guessing they will expand their hours the longer they have been open. I'm pretty sure they've only been open around a month now. Hopefully they will, because this would be a great place to get lunch with friends.

We will definitely be going back. I would recommend spencer's to anyone with a creative palate and a preference for fresh ingredients.
The happiness I feel regarding this place being so close to me is so real right now. Get the chicken cutlet Italian. You won't be sorry.
I stumbled on this place this afternoon and went back for dinner. I ordered the fried chicken biscuit with corn relish and coleslaw. It was excellent. I will definitely be going back.

This review is not an attempt to malign and damage this business. It is honest feedback that I hope the owner will use to improve the product. 

I live for comfort food. But the taste, experience, and calories must be worth it. I ventured into Scratch Biscuits one cold morning looking for something good and tasty. Unfortunately, the food did not live up to expectations. The biscuit was fresh, but tasteless. It also fell apart as I held it. But, sandwich bread isn't supposed to fall apart; its purpose is to help hold the ingredients together.

I like the idea of this restaurant. But its core product misses the mark. Hopefully, this establishment will get a new biscuit recipe which will then have  me coming back for more.

This place is a disaster. I waited almost 30 minutes for my takeout order tonight. The soda machine was out of ice and most syrup flavors, and the floors, counter and tables were filthy, covered in spilled liquid and smeared food as well as trash.

Had to update this because I didn't give the service enough (or hardly any) credit in my last review. This place is basically run by two guys, I'm assuming the owner and a manager. Both are very friendly and seem to know everyone who comes in. They even like to guess what you'll order based on previous visits. Really nice guys and they make a mean sub. They also are great with honoring the coupons you get in the mail every other week and even let me keep one to use it again. The new pork sandwich isn't half bad by the way, although I'll stick with one my chicken subs about 95% of the time. Forget what I said in my last review, these guys are great.
I go to this Wendy's everyday for lunch,  I get the 4 for 4 meal, customer service is good,  but my only problem with this Wendy's, is there soda machine is always out of soda.

Yea the service can be pretty bad sometimes but at least they are open late when others are not, giving them revenue from bar hoppers in the night. The floor is sticky. And usually there is at least one near homeless person hanging out inside which makes it really sad to sit there and eat.

Poor Wendy's. Some taxi ran into it this past Friday at ~12:45 a.m., right before closing. Hopefully everyone was okay. It did make for some really odd news. But business is still going. Gotta give props to city establishments, they keep making their money.

I had a Blizzard here today and found them to be extremely friendly and quick.  This was in the midst of a very busy day and yet, they kept their cool in serving frozen treats to tourists and Philadelphians alike.  

As with all DQs, avoid the food.  But, there's nothing like their ice cream.

I passed this place on my walk home and grabbed six walnut baklavas to go.  I was surprised given the reviews and am only reviewing the baklava.  The baklava was extra flaky, crispy and not overly sweet!  I was just going to have one, but couldn't stop myself from going back for three more.  Next time I have a craving for baklava, I know where I'm going.

EW OMG THIS WENDYS IS SO BAD!!!!! It's CRAZY inside!!!! There are people smoking cigarettes inside, there's random signage on the ground, it smells like burning grease, and there are always people playing Magic the gathering like its 2001!!!!! The employees are nice but they're always out of stuff there!!! Last week I went and they were out of small cups so I was like can I have a medium cup and just fill it half way or something and she like gave me a weird look!! Then they were out of Sprite!!! Is this place HELL???? Also I don't think they shake the grease off the fries properly when they take them out of the fryer bc the fries taste AWFUL like dirt which is so gross. Ok so then my friend Zilin went there today and the FIRE ALARMS were going off and he said like 6 people were trying to fight the cashier that's so weird!! Anyway this Wendy's is gross and weird and if you wanna be sad go here bc it's sad here :(

Most of the employees at this McDonald's are very rude and the service is slow.  The restaurant could also be much cleaner.  The food is average quality compared to other McDonald's.  Even the drinks taste awful.  I've been there about five times and each time I've regretted going there.  The employees also act like you're wasting their time by being there as well as acting like they don't want to serve you.

OMG loved! Ate the entire pigscuit! Amazing pulled pork! My friend had the brisket biscuit. Big pieces of very tender brisket. The biscuits melted in your mouth. Also had the sweet potato fries. Amazing! Can't wait to go back!

I've frequented the Cottman and Willow Grove locations and so happy this is here! This new location in the Northeast Shopping center at Welsh and the Blvd. is ultra convenient and perfect after doing some errands. There has not been a line the 2 times I've been here so far but people may not be aware of this location yet.
