While I'm not sure of the exact size of the pizza, I'm guessing it was 10-14 inches. It definitely was enough that I had leftovers. My pizza had toppings and came to $7.95. Well worth it. 

They had to go boxes located conveniently next to the soda fountain. There was also parmesan, oregano, and pepper flakes available. 

The inside was clean looking with lots of natural light. The music was blaring but eh what you gonna do. I'd come back here again for sure. BONUS: they accept diamond dollars.

We didn't know anything about this place but decided to give it a shot, and we were in for a pleasant surprise. We tried the lamb gyro sandwich, chicken paratha and chaat. The food tasted amazing, had a lot of flavor and was fresh. Also the restaurant had a fair amount of seating. Overall we loved the place and will definitely return and recommend it to others. Also get the mango lassi!

I was very disappointed in this place.  I ordered the bacon and eggs on a biscuit and the eggs were a perfect square, which made me suspicious if they were real or processed (fake).   The bottom of the biscuit immediately fell apart.   And, even though this seems minor, given other things here, they were out of cream/half and half for the coffee.

I don't know what happened maybe summer break was too rough on them but it's totally changed. The long line is still the same but the customer service is terrible now. No one is smiling no one seems to be happy to have a job. The woman cutting pizzas and finishing them off was rude to a customer when he asked what name she called out. Mind you the music is so loud you can't really hear if you don't stand in front of that area. Pizza is still the same it just lacks the love that they had before.

This location has good customer service, even when they are extremely busy. Shout out to Blake who lightens up the day with his dry humor. Never had any issues. Pizza is good. People are good. Blaze = yay
Pleasantly surprised to find this place.  Quick, easy decent fast food.  Got the wok street chicken bowl.  Very good, healthy and full of flavor.
The greatest thing about Dairy Queen is the Milkshakes and the Oreo Bizzard  is all that and more i went down their yesterday and got a milkshake and it was good.I enjoy my self down their.Yum!!!!

One of our favorite lunch places on campus! Seriously good pizza and they get it right every single time. The staff couldn't be better.

Prices are great and sign up for the app to get coupons every once in a while.

Scratch biscuits one word "fantastic"!! I ordered the traditional biscuit with chicken slaw and ranch and it was suburb! The chicken was moist and the ranch was a perfect kind of heat!! I highly recommend if your in the city to try..it's a must!

Wet gross meat ..tasted nothing like their other locations. 

Let's just say I went to 711 and bought donuts and a red bull to wash out the disgusting taste in my mouth. 

Fries were ok.   I will never go back
Just stopped for lunch and was told the registers are down and they can't serve me! They said they have been down for almost 2 hours! Sorry but I do NOT believe it! Never going back
Took 25 minutes to get my order, and there wasn't even that many people, or vehicles.

The worst customer service I've ever seen. They didn't feel like making certain items on the menu and told customers they were "out of it" when I saw the items in the back. They also got everyone's orders wrong and refused to correct them. I love Little Caesar's but you should go to a different one.

My first impression was just how dirty the place was - I can understand that sometimes things get dropped, but the amount of trash on the floor was a red flag. They were missing many things that are somewhat important: no medium-sized soda lids, no ketchup in either one of two dispensers, and they were out of a good number of common soda syrups. The checkout and service was pretty quick, but I was concerned by how many times the cashier had to swipe my (pretty new) credit card on her machine - 5-7 times given that it goes through on the first try everywhere else. As for the food, my chicken sandwich was pretty good, but the fries were cold, under-salted, and generally bland. There's plenty of fast food options around, and I'll pick a different location next time.

After being a tourist (for a day, for fun) I needed something sweet..
Was coming across DQ when I saw their capturing photo outside, sweet-tooth was calling me!

Loved the man who took my order, he basically said I'll give you whatever mix you want, wanted vanilla plus plus (very picky with what I want) amd for that, ching-ching $4.00 only... Gotta be charming to get your sweets right, right? :) I sure got mine! More caramel, fudge and whip cream + almonds nuts.

All the best for a Wednesday walk around the Historical-part of Philly! :)

I started a job close to this Dairy Queen and I am addicted. The Store Manager Mr. Patel is always working and extremely friendly. I went there my first three days of work back to back due to my ice cream addiction of course but also because they are quick, friendly, and make an awesome cookie dough blizzard with rainbow sprinkles. I recommend this location to any and everyone. It's about to be a hot summer. See you there!

Excellent quality taco bell. Good food, they serve you UNBROKEN tacos. I eat here ALL the time. But all the tables are ALWAYS sticky on the edges, so minus 3 stars for that. It is GROSS! Who wants to eat at a table with sticky edges????
Minus another star for not participating in the free doritos taco event today (which prompted this review).
Come to this taco bell if you like sticky tables.

So being the first reviewer for this place, my only hope is that the people who run this business would pay serious attention to this review. This place has a lot of potential, but is just not attractive. I just happened to visit a friend nearby and decided to try this place. 

The appearance was too shoddy for a newly opened place. The restaurant had seating, but the tables and chairs simply looked used; some chairs even had holes in them. The floor was full of dirt.

Speaking about the food, my friend and I ordered Samosa Chaat and Chana Paratha Roll. The Samosas in the chat had a really strong smell of cooking oil, and were hardly warmed up. The Chana roll had chana masala, lettuce, and yoghurt in it. The chana masala was just edible - and had a lot of gravy in it. That made the roll too soggy and difficult  to eat. 

Also, being an Indian, I have struggled at Indian restaurants in Philly. They just do not get the difference between spicy and hot. Spicy is more flavor, hot is burning your mouth with chillies. When the server asked whether I wanted more "spicy", I was hoping he really meant "spicy", and not "hot". Yet again, I was disappointed.

I am very sure I am not visiting this place again unless I know or have heard that it has gotten better. 

The one extra star is for the effort of the owners to start a new business.

This location is always slow. Usually I get cold fries, but I was pleasantly surprised to have hot fries today but when I opened my.fish filet, it was old. Im.pretty sure if they aren't making items fresh they can only sit for a certain number of minutes before going out. My bun was hard in a sitting on a heated surface or under a heat lamp too long kind of way. The fish was cold and just gross because it was old. Usually you have to wait a long time at this location, this is the slowest fast food around. I once ordered something here and they got my order confused with somsone elses when i went to the pick up window and I literally had to repeat my order 5 times to the associate and manager just to get the right, very simple meal.  If the manager reads this, take a look at your operations. Shitty food, long waits, at least the employees are nice.

This place is horrible. Ive previously called the help line for wendys and complained that no one at this location wears hair nets or wears their hair up. They said they would get right to the bottom of that issue. I come back 3 weeks later & still the same thing. I asked the manager about it & he said they arent required to wear them. But when i called the help line that was not the case. Also, Loud ignorant employess, They stand around and talk while youre waiting for your food thats standing right in front of them. customer service couldn't get any worse than this place. Never coming back.
Slow!!!!!! They almost always screw up my order. One of of five times they get it right.

In an effort to broaden my wife's taste bud(that and I really like to go Mediterranean restaurants) I convinced her to go to Baklava Cafe instead of our usual rainy weather fare. The entire time I was worried about her as more often than not people's behaviors are changed based upon the residue of the 1st impression. 

Upon entering I noticed right away that all other Yelpers were right this is most definitely a family run cafe, which I love immediately. My wife tended to agree as well, although I'm sure the cute little 5 year old behind the counter helped in reminding her of a part of her own youth. I was never a big fan of anything sweet, but just upon first look at the pastries you could tell the owners really knew their stuff. It wrapped around the entire counter top in perfectly placed and lit arrangements. It was not daunting and you really get that cozy feel of being in a pastries shop, with the salt air blowing in from the sea when in Baklava Cafe. 

But being that it was rainy and we both had a hankering for some Shawarma we got the Lamb Shawarma. While it seemed great while we were at the Cafe during lunch, it wasn't until we got home did we truly appreciate the amazingly addictive nature of it. So much so that we immediately had to whip out Yelp and find the nearest-most-stars restaurant which had Schawarma we could find for dinner,  since we were in the burbs and Baklava was in the city. It did not measure up and 2 days later we made another track in to the city just to get more of the amazing Shawarma. We had to rush since it was Chinese New Years and we had places to be, but as we sat there in our car devouring the torpedo of joy, pausing to unwrap only to avoid a possible aluminum foil eating incident, we could do nothing but wonder what sad people we have become.

Sitting in a car parked in full view of public, bite after bites of the delicious Shawarma. We felt like we had committed a lude act in full view of public, and we could do nothing but hide our shame as we drove away panting, drooling, and sweating from our adventure in to the darker and much more depraved part of our foodie-ism.

We went around 1PM on a Saturday in Center City. There was one other party eating there. That was kind of a red flag to me that something was a little off. Fair warning: I'm from the South.

Here's the thing: the recipes are *great*. I got the chicken biscuit, which had cabbage slaw, corn relish, and a substantial helping of "cayenne ranch". I'm not really partial to ranch dressing on a biscuit, but it's not an awful combination and- you know what?- it's a play on comfort food. I'll take it. For a place that's pitching towards the sneakers-and-tshirts crowd, that's a good angle.

The problem is that those recipes aren't executed correctly. The biscuits are soggy. No, it's not that they're "not supposed to be sandwiches". That comes from not cooling off the biscuits in a well-ventilated area. It comes from the biscuits being made ahead of time and stored somewhere that allows the moisture to break down the crust so that it falls apart.

The buttermilk breading on the chicken doesn't stick. That's gonna come from once-frying skin-off breast filets instead of twice-frying so that you don't get a membrane of batter forming against the surface of the meat.

I have no doubt that the person who invented this recipe knows how to execute it so that the biscuit doesn't break apart when the diner tries to eat it, or so the chicken doesn't slide out of its own breading when it's served. The problem is that nobody else does. 

This is one of those situations where leadership is running what should be a winning fast-food joint into the ground. And it's sad, because I want a place where I can get Southern staples in Philly. Unfortunately, until their quality improves, this ain't it.

I went here one time at around 7pm on a weekday and, no lie, they told me they were out of Whoppers and Pepsi when I tried to order them. How do you run out of your signature burger, before the Big King was introduced? And, how do you run out of Pepsi? On the same night? It wasn't even like they were that busy, and it was still early. Plus, this is actually usually a busy location, being that it's right off the Betsy Ross and on Castor/Aramingo, so you would think they would keep a larger than average inventory. 

You could still order other burgers at the time as well, so I'm confused how they could run out of Whoppers. Maybe they ran out of the sauce? I have no clue. I was just amazed that something like that could happen. 

Luckily for me, I was only ordering myself a chicken sandwich, which they had, but my boyfriend was less than pleased and I ended up having to go to Taco Bell instead to get him his dinner. Ridiculous.

Great Idea but the portions for a $8.00 breakfast sandwich are really small and unsatisfying.
I had an egg. kale and avocado sandwich and it was pretty flavorless. 
They need to tweak this menu if they are going to survive in this market

Biscuits!  Fried chicken!  Blues music!  Sorry to say, I was let down.  Biscuits were meh and definitely not substantial enough to support a sandwich.  They are served on trays with thin wax paper that tear apart when you are cutting your sandwich.  The pulled pork was super salty.  Couple of things I would change: butcher paper for the trays, more substantial napkins, rethink the biscuit recipe... You have a great space and excellent service!!  Some tweaks are all you need.

I like this location, and it seems to be one of the most busiest Wendy's even during a Sunday night. Although they were very fast and efficient, I kind of wish it wasn't one of the cleaning crew that passed us our order at the drive through. That is just my personal preference and perhaps I'm a bit of a germ-a-phob. The food was pretty delicious either way, however.

Also, frosties are always a must. No Wendy's has ever made them wrong, thankfully! Certainly gives a great dessert fix.
Great cheesesteak. Awesome fries. Anyone who says any different should be slapped in their teeth.

Unfortunately I had a horrible experience at this location. I typically love blaze, but they were ridiculously rude to me at my visit today. I had to order my pizza gluten free, as I am celiac, and gotten many rude comments from the worker there. Quite disappointed.
The food is fresh the flavor palettes to choose from will have u pondering for which u like. Many options all with that down home southern flare in a chic sandwich to fit in ur hand.

I'm a little surprised to see all the negative reviews. I've been here four times since it has opened and my order has always been perfect. Nothing has been missing and everything has been hot. The employees are always nice and pleasant and as always with Taco Bell the prices are great. I love it here.

The food was really good and the prices are reasonable! The environment is just super annoying when you're in there for awhile. The music was so loud that I couldn't even hear the person next to me talking. Some of the employees were yelling and making "Whoop" noises that got old really fast. Get your food for take out and eat it somewhere else.

So spendy! A biscuit w/ tomato and a biscuit w/ avocado would have run $16! The Build-Your-Own-Biscuit option is not recommended for those on a budget. Got "The Alice Waters", basically a veggie-egg biscuit instead for $8.  OK although the Garlicky Kale was less than lukewarm. The biskit was decent but did not put Carolina on my mind.

I'm pretty sure the Spencer's side of the new Sabrina's restaurant opened up recently and from my first taste it is excellent.  I got a tomahto daddy, sort of like their version of a big mac (much better than a big mac).  It was seriously good... I devoured the whole thing.  This place should be packed on a regular basis and I won't be surprised if it is once Drexel students get wind of the burgers.  The only issue are their relatively short hours (maybe this will improve in the future?).  Price for extraordinary burger + fries (3 or 4 kinds)+ a drink = $8.  Can't beat it for this quality.  Give it a shot.

Edit: Prices were lowered for combos, even better deal now.

i like the idea of everyone can get a burger. I'm vegan and my friend only eats poultry so its great we could both get burger at the same place. Would have given them 5 stars but the bread falls apart to fast and burgers are a little sloppy but they taste good. going back to try their flour less chocolate cake.

The best of the make your own pizza places around.  I love that they have Daiya cheese and a great tasting gluten free crust if that's your thing.  It's worth a special trip if you don't live around the Temple area.
Excellent deserts and very good salad plates. Had a light lunch of grape leaves plate. Nice place friendly staff. We stop in whenever I am in town.

It would really be nice if the service was better. ..

Warning, hold your bladder if you are a male.  And is there some need for a cigarette advertising sign on the front door?  Happy meal and a carton for the kiddies??? (Yes, it is attached to a gas station, but come on!)

I dig big salads. While not in the style of Elaine Benes, Saladworks still manages to impress. The portion is huge and I hope for my diet's sake that that means equally healthy. I always get the Chicken Caesar with the Light Parmesan Caesar dressing. They fill it to the brim and it's delicious. They always wear gloves which is key for me and are very nice. The salad comes with either a white or wheat roll. I also splurge and get the tasty chocolate chip cookies. :P  

Very clean store and tasty salads!

This place is nestled in a busy Chestnut street and is amazing!  The perfect biscuit with any combination of meat/veggie and toppings.  We went for their classic Backyard biscuit for $5. Pimento cheese, pickles on top of fried chicken.  And let me tell you how perfectly cooked the white meat chicken was.  Holy cow (or should I say chicken)!?  They are associated with a catering company and offer late night eats on Fridays and Saturdays from midnight until 2am.  We will be back weekly!!!! Thank you.

The Moroccan Chicken was awful and the shawerma's flavor and thickness was too similar to "steakums". The hummus tasted like it was bought, not house made. Wouldn't recommend anything other than the coffee.

Now wouldn't it be a cryin' shame if the baklava here, the namesake of the cafe itself, was shoddy?

 If this were the sad state of affairs, I'd forevermore look upon this South Street spot with scorn. Luckily this is not the case. I particularly enjoy the pistachio baklava from these lovely people. No scorn! Smiles. Sticky smiles. 

I don't know if a person can hit a wall when it comes to sampling an incredible variety of many flaky-layered, honey-syrup-sweet, phyllo-based pastries, but I intend to find out. Has not happened yet.

Well now... if you happen to be in ghetto-land Southwest Philly and need some pizza or take out, and are in the neighborhood, 63rd Street Pizza is okey dokey.  Not quite up to my standards, but my grandfather LOVED their pizza.  One cool thing they do is put sliced meatballs on pizza, which is pretty cool.  The owners are Greek, so they don't do the typical NY/Philly/Jersey style pizza which I favor.  The do good fried foods though, decent cheesesteaks, fries, etc.  Their prices are VERY low, so it's a good bargain, although this is NOT a place I would go out of my way for.  The only reason we go there is because it's down the street from grandmas.  

Take out only.

The most wonderful...ah.  Strawberry Cheesequake Blizzard with Chocolate Soft Serve and Chocolate Sauce is absolutely to DIE for!  I know it sounds funky, but it is just what the doctor ordered for me...actually, it isn't, because it is loaded with calories and fat, but I get a kid one and eat it anyways.  It's a wonderful treat on occasion.  Yum!!!

This was my first time at a Dairy Queen and I would move to Philly for this place. They make an awesome Peanut Butter chocolate shake. I would definitely be 500 lbs easy if I moved to Philly. I'd be waddling here every day and the only exercise I would get would be lifting the shake to my mouth.

I am just a big fan of Taco Bell in general. I love all the new stuff they come up with constantly. I really love the Siracha stuff they come up with too! My fav is the quesadillas!!! I also like the free refills.

I had the most incredible experience of excellent customer service offered by the manager of the Dairy Queen on Chestnut St.  Harshal Patel went way beyond the call of duty to help me organize the perfect birthday cake for my 3 year old granddaughter! She was delighted and will be talking about her party and cake for a long time!  
I have been amazed at his desire to please me and making sure that I was happy. Mr Patel you exceeded every one of my expectations and you have a new very loyal customer! Thanks again for all your help.

This is not the place for health food. That being said, it's the delicious fried comfort food you dream of. The fries are good, but the also offer alternatives like waffle fries and tots. The toppings are unique and tasty, but my favorite is the classic poutine. The sliders are also surprisingly good. The guy who served us on a weekday afternoon, who I assumed to be the manager, was very attentive and helpful. If he's not the manager, he probably should be.

I was really looking forward to this place opening.  I had lunch there today and what a disappointment.  I ordered a biscuit with fried chicken,  cabbage slaw and horseradish mayo on the side and I also had the banana pudding.  First, they were extremely overpriced. My order along with a bottle of water was over $16 and the biscuits are really small.   I couldn't pick up my sandwich because the biscuit crumbled in my hand, so I had to use a fork. The cabbage slaw was dry and the chicken was tough.  I dipped what I could eat of the chicken in the horseradish mayo and left the dry biscuit.   The pudding was also not good. It had an almost perfume like taste.  I could only eat one bite and just threw that out as well.

Oy my first one star review... but I think it deserves it...

The bathroom was disgusting. It smelled and the sink was full of hair. The soap pump was broken so I don't know how the employees go to the bathroom and wash their hands like they're supposed to!

And their fries were stale. And I love fries. But that may be because it was 12:30am and they close at 1am.

Regardless, gross overall! I hope they fix it up!

I think I have to blame the corporation more so than the particular location. The portion size to price ratio is below an acceptable standard. It's very much obvious that a good amount of the money one would spend on a single salad goes into the overhead cost of marketing, and accounting for a variety of foods that may go bad quickly. The location yields for high traffic volume which may explain the impatient and unhelpful customer service. I've tried this location twice in the past year nearby my workplace. Would much rather get a salad from the pizza place down the street which is the same price and contains nearly 4 times the amount of produce and protein.

I mainly frequent the drive thru here and the employees are always friendly and helpful.  It's usually a quick process of ordering, paying and receiving our food.  If something is going to take a little longer, they will ask me kindly to either pull up or park and wait for it to be brought out to my car.  Today, we were asked to wait for a salad to be finished.  It took a few minutes, but when we got it home, it was fresh and nicely put together.  
There really are no complaints from the drive thru.  

We did try ordering inside, on one evening when the drive thru line was long and that was a mistake.  They are much more efficient for the cars then the people inside the building.  Lesson learned.
Absolutely the BEST fast food service I have ever received. Beth, you really rocked it. Food was just as expected from any Wendy's.

What has happened to this McDonald's?  The place is looking like a dump these days, and the employees flat out don't care!!  Today I ordered chicken mcnuggets with hot mustard and a sweet tea with lemon. I got nuggets with BUFFALO SAUCE, and an unsweetened tea with NO ICE. It was about 100 degrees, and they really served me a drink with no ice.  Where is the manager, and why isn't anyone checking for quality customer service any more?

I came here on my lunch break from a hospital shift to try some authentic middle eastern food. I ordered hummus and bread that had oregano and sesame spices on it. The hummus was delicious! The food came out fast and it was very tasty. The bread with oregano and sesame spices tasted a bit stale (as though it's been sitting there all night)- so I recommend not to get anything from the window because it may not be as fresh as you expect. Also, I ordered a smoothie, expecting a freshly made mango fruit smoothie. Instead, it tasted like sweeteners and nothing about it was fresh except for the banana she put in. So overall, I would stick to the desserts/hummus/tea-- food that they are more familiar with. But delicious nonetheless

I went to KFC on Roosevelt Blvd near Chapman Ford for $20 bucket meal plus two five dollar meals. My sister and I really enjoy KFC meals and it's taste so good, want to go back the next time to go for a delicious meals. Keep up the good work and thank.

I missed the opening day free-bowl giveaway on 5/12/16, but came in on the second day during my lunch break. There was no line and the service was pretty quick. The place is clean and modern. Though there are not that many places to sit, my group was able to grab the end of a high top and eat in. 

Their signature bowls all looked good to me, with a variety of interesting ingredients. I ended up choosing the Shoyu Steak bowl.** It was not technically steak, but rather braised beef, which was very tender and flavorful. Other toppings included red pepper, cucumber, mint, some sauteed veggies, and tamarind sauce (a bit salty; tasted like soy sauce w/no tamarind). The rice was a bit too al dente for me, but everything tasted fresh. Compared to other Asian or Asian-style places that serve similar food, I also felt they used way less oil, which was a plus for my waistline. The topping to rice ratio, however, was a bit low, considering the price ($9.79 + tax, or $10.57). The price range is $8-10 for the chicken bowl, $9-11 for the pork bowl, and $10-12 for the "steak" (actually braised beef) bowl.

The regular-sized bowl was definitely a comfortable amount for me, but in terms of value, I would find myself better off buying lunch at nearby places like Mama's Vegetarian ($7*=more food), Thai Singha House ($6*= more food), Chipotle ($7-8*= more food), or even more expensive places like Animo Juice and Farmer's Keep (both similarly priced, but more substantial/tasty/healthier). If this review was about the food alone, it would be 4 stars. However, paying over $10.50 (without a beverage) for food of this portion/quality made it more of a 3-star experience. A bowl of mostly rice (not even the healthy kind), topped with 3 strips of red pepper (literally! see my picture), a few shreds of cucumber, and some beef (all mass-produced like at Chipotle) does not make a $10+ meal. 

*these prices already include tax.
--------------
**UPDATE: As of 5/27/16, it seems they have renamed the "Shoyu Steak" bowl "Bangkok Beef" without changing the ingredients ("shoyu" is Japanese for soy sauce). Interesting choice of a new name, as I didn't taste any Thai flavor when I had it. In fact, another reviewer stated the beef reminded him of Korean marinated shortribs. Is this a subliminal way of saying "all Asian food tastes the same"?? (Jk, they probably either aren't familiar with all of the distinctive Asian cuisines out there or think the public can't tell the difference.) 
 
On the plus side, they have lowered the price of the beef bowl to $9.19 (regular) and $11.18 (large)!!

They also seemed to have re-adjusted their concept to "Southeast Asian" style. Having eaten Southeast Asian food throughout my entire life, however, I really didn't notice any genuine/substantial incorporation of Southeast Asian flavors or concepts in their menu. They pretty much took bits and snippets of Americanized/fusion versions of various Asian dishes and put them all together into a medley of not quite Chinese/Japanese/Korean/Vietnamese/Thai (plus Chipotle), which is definitely not "Southeast Asian." 

If this type of cuisine was an imaginary creature, it would be a Jabberwocky with an Asian tooth (like not even an arm or a leg). Honestly, the food tastes fine by fast-food standards (it's just over-priced) and I don't care if they sell poorly executed Asian food. But if so, then they really shouldn't call it "Asian" food and CERTAINLY NOT "Southeast Asian food" (the flavors are either not Asian or slightly Northern Asian at best). I'm tempted to check out Wok Street again in a few months to see if it will have finally found its identity and/or improved its portion-to-price ratio.

Absolutely love it here! I am a pizza lover and this is my favorite pizza joint thus far! So many options in building your own pizza and the service is super quick! Pizza came out in less than five minutes. Customer service is on point as well! Great workers!
Walked out of here today.. waited in line for 15 minutes then saw this (see pic I will post) next to the business cards.. mentioned it to a worker. Never again.

I went to this McDonald's to grab a coffee before breakfast. I thought it was very clean upon walking in so I sat down to drink the coffee. After sitting for no more than 2 minutes a mouse ran in front of me. Very gross and would not suggest coming here
Slowest line on the planet. You can't order from the app. Literally one cashier during lunch and she was working food too. Would recommend a different location

I LOVE biscuits even though it's just white flour and fat. The only thing I love more is a breakfast biscuit sandwich. These guys manage to deliver a solid sandwich. I've been here a few times always to get take out. The biscuits are very big to begin with so a sandwich is very filling. The one I got today with baked egg bacon and cheese was half the size of my head. It does become a little challenging(messy) to eat so keep that mind. I got this to go ad I don't live far but when I got home the sandwich wasn't hot it was only warm. That is not to say that the sandwich isn't delicious. And honestly I've never stayed to eat so maybe that would make a difference temperature wise. I don't love love the baked egg. I prefer a fried or scrambled egg but the is a personal preference. I think the sandwich would stay hotter if that were offered. 

I think people get put off by the price but honestly I'd rather spend the money and only go here one in a while than go to ratchet Wawa and get the heat lamp sandwich that will have me in the bathroom after an hour. Quality of ingredients matters and at least here I know it has been made fresh. I'll be back the next time I'm feeling like carbing out. I've never gotten a lunch biscuit so I guess that is next on my list.

If you're familiar with employees who get so hype over seeing their friends as customers to the point that they stop and make conversation, this is one of those places. Nothing wrong with small chatter, but if it disrupts your work flow and you have other customers waiting while you're fraternizing, rather obnoxiously, then it's a problem. 

Food-wise, quality varies but never to the point of no return. However, something hard was in the brown rice that could be dried up or something else altogether. Tables are also usually dirty, I don't have a problem cleaning them myself, but others might. Hence the one time, a customer approached me and my friends and suggested we complain. The manager, however, noticed and gave us coupons so that was nice.
the firfir was great. wish they had a soda fountain instead of bottled/canned beverages, but whatever.

Never. again. I could make a better veggie wrap in my sleep. Actually, I could make a better salad wrap while having a nightmare. Over sauced, under veggied, partially stale wrap.

NEVER. AGAIN!

Food tested: chicken paratha roll, mango lassi, mixed lamb/chicken over rice platter

Positive: white sauce in the platter was decent and the owner seemed nice

Negative: depressing atmosphere, not much taste in the meat, paratha seemed like it was a roti, and place was empty

Overall: Great concept but not worth going to until they upgrade their parathas and add some spices in the meat

Revisit: no

Health tip: food at this place is not fit for people with high cholesterol. Ask for a roti roll instead of paratha to decrease calories and oil fat.

I'm really shocked to see all of the negative reviews. I like this particular location. It's always super clean, the staff is always pleasant and there are never really long lines. I go out of my way to frequent this location. I used to go to the one in bensalem. I'm so glad this location opened. The bensalem store should take some notes.i haven't and a bad meal here. Solid 4 stars

Although the treats here are delicious the staff is clueless and they are often out of key items/ingredients.

A few experiences I have had with this location:
-Went in on a Sunday afternoon and the store was completely empty except for 1 employee, tried to order a blizzard and was told by the employee that he was 'locked out' of the register and couldn't ring up my purchase until his manager got back....but he didnt know where his manager was or when he was getting back
-tried to order a hot dog on a different occassion and the employee told me they didnt have any hot dog buns
-attempted to go there during the week and the store was closed (found out later that their water heater had broken or something)
-went in last week and saw a sign on the door for the waffle bowl sundaes - attempted to order - was told by the employee that they 'don't even bother' with the waffle bowels
-saw an advertisement on TV today about the mini-blizzards being on special for 1.99 in april, called this location and they stated that they had never head of that special

I am officially DONE patronizing this establishment because you can never get what you want.

My husband took out two bowls from them today . The food was plain as cardboard . No flavor , no seasoning  , no acidity .... complete screw up . 
 The person who cooks the food there needs to quit , his taste buds are dead . Complete waste of money and huge taste buds disappointment

If you crave McDonalds, never go here. The staff is incredibly rude and unreliable. They sometimes open the lobby very late, so its not a good place to get coffee in the morning. Everything I get from here is sloppy, every burger i get is slapped together with little to no effort. When I order a mcflurry, it is just ice cream with a bunch of m&ms on top. I highly recommend waiting for the next McDonalds, because this is the worst McDonalds I know.

This place has such neat vibe, great location and kind, prompt service. The menu is well designed and has a cool mix of Southern favorites - brisket, pimiento cheese, pickles, etc. The presentation and Scratch branding is fun. But. These are the crumbliest biscuits I've ever had in my life. Maybe that's a preference thing, but if I'm going to order a loaded biscuit sandwich I expect to be able to pick up the sandwich and have the bread hold up to the weight of the filling. I've now had both breakfast and lunch at this place and I'm seriously underwhelmed.

This goes to the owners of this Wendy's location. Your service is absolutely abhorrent to a legendary status point! This means that it is common knowledge to every and the surrounding neighborhood  who has ever been to this location that you need to carve out 30 minutes of your time from entering to exit to get what should be less than 5  minutes of service time needed for a meal to go.  Anyone who even talks about going to this restaurant is given a warning in advance not to go, but Id thought Id give you the benefit of the doubt a few days ago, but I failed to heed that warning.  First i enter and wait in a line with 5 people ahead of me and 3 cashiers so i figure this shouldn't take long until I notice that there are 5 people waiting on the end of the counter for their order, all with disgusted looks on their faces. after about a 5 minute wait, I hand the cashier a coupon for a free Baconator. She asks me "Well which one do you want?" referring to the choice of sandwich on the coupon. I say "Oh. Im sorry, the Baconator" She then replies "Oh well, you gotta tell me then, because I don't know!"  After i complete my order, she walks away before giving me the total and completes 2 other orders, and then returns to ask me again what did I order? What? So I repeat the order and she cuts me off in mid sentence with the total!! I then wait another 5 minutes to get my food and when I get it, The fries are cold, the nuggets are cold and the sandwich is NOT what I ordered, so I take the entire tray back up to the line and tell them I need the correct sandwich and everything to be hot!  Mean while the fry station employee is told about the cold items and says loud enough for anyone on the front line to hear. "Man, Shit! They betta take it like it come out cause I aint standing over this fryer, reheating shit all day long!"  Well since I like my "Shit" hot,  I waited 5 more minutes for my food and the right sandwich.  The managers don't give a damn. The employees dont give a damn.  Nobody in this store gives a damn, But please do not think because you are on temple campus that you are immune to financial failure, because with the horrendous service you give out, sooner, than later you will be gone unless you change!

This Wendy's is so slow I waited in drive thru 17 minuyes for cold food. This location needs new management this Wendy's is not one Dave would be proud of. Each car in drive thru was over 6 minutes and 4 of those minutes I sat in silence. Whay happened to 2:30 seconds in drive thru. DO NOT  GO TO THIS WENDY'S UNLESS YOU HAVE HALF AN HOUR TO SPARE AND WANT COLD FRY'S FOR THE WAIT. A total waste.

Dont bother, the biscuts are dry and crumble. The vegetarian sandwich was inedible. The chicken was dry. The cost of biscuits was outrageous. We paid 8 and 8.50 for two for a total of 17.82 with tax.  Should receive a refund. Did I mention the biscuits were cold, the kale overcooked and the chicken tasteless.  DD biscuit at under $5 is a better purchase.  I wanted to like this place, since I enjoy real homecooked biscuits.  Maybe you need to be intoxicated to enjoy.

AN AVERAGE WENDY'S!
Not exactly fine dining but average for a hamburger joint. I've never heard of any complaints here. And although they yelp that they're located in Fox Chase, you won't find them there. They're only yards away from the BURHOLME HONOR SQUARE on "Five Points." They may need some geography lessons but their food is A-OK! Also Beth Ann, the last I checked, french fries are potatoes.
I was in the mood for a Filet-O-McSquid. No McSquid to be found here and no ODB either.

Overrated.  $9 average sized biscuits. Biscuit fell apart before I even picked it up. $5 for a small order of fries. $16 for an unfulfilling lunch. Save your money people this place is just a fad and will be gone by next year.
Im a fan of burger king. I like them better than mcdonalds at times. This bk seems to be clean in the dinning room. crowded at times but good and they are acurate with orders.

The food was okay, but when they were still open they were playing their own music off of their phones and once they closed, they played music over the restaurant speakers extremely loud even though customers were still in there eating. I get they want to go home, but I find this very uprofessional and inappropriate, especially as someone who works in the restaurant business as well.

Shoo Fry!
I'm rounding up to 4 from a 3.5.  Shoo Fry offers a menu catered to the late night delight of the bar going crowd.  You will find  spots like these all over Canada and Central Europe.  Potato creations (fries, tots, etc) are topped with sauces and meats and perfect size sliders made to order.  If you like traditional poutine, this is the place in Philly.  I've heard the other French fry styles are good too.  Prices are slightly on the high side.  The slider that I had was a tad overlooked.  Overall,  it's a good place for a late night snack (or feast depending on your situation).

Amazing fried chicken!!! I had the Alice waters biscuit and shared some of the fried chicken biscuit with a friend and both items were delicious! The fresh squeezed OJ was nice addition to the meal as well. We also tried the peanut butter layered dessert cup and it was a perfect dessert!! Also, the person who took our order and served us was so nice--Great staff overall. Will definitely be coming back here often.

This location is THE WORST!!! Super super slow. On a Friday or Saturday night, the line is easily 5-6 cars long and i had the pleasure of hearing the customer driving in front of me curse the associate out after she was told they were out of the 3 things she asked for. They have messed up my daughters happy meal, forgotten her juice, fries, apples etc all on seperatw visits. Large fries are half full of old stale fries. My boyfriend hates this McDonalds but it is so close to home... but best believe that the old dry burger and fries will be the source of complaint that night.

Everyone is really friendly here, probably because not much foot traffic coming through. There's so many different treats to try, it's pretty awesome, but when we bought an assorted platter I kinda felt that the taste was just ever so slightly lacking. I'm definitely coming back because this is basically in theory the perfect little dessert place, but I just hope this time was a fluke.

I wish there was a zero star option. I am avid McDonald's goer and honestly have never had an issue until tonight. I'm the only one in line since it's a late night. I order a couple small late night snacks and the order is taking FOREVER to fill. There's two workers inside so the length at which I was made to wait was beyond me. Anyway it gets worse. So I get a couple things and I think to myself "okay, you should be fine, they probably have everything right there." I thought. I said "thank you" to the worker and they responded with "nah you have to wait for your ******* sandwich." Pause. I get it's late but come on all I said was "thank you". I'm annoyed and my boy is also fed up. So I finally get my sandwich and I go to drive away. I open up the bag to pull out my sandwich and low and behold ITS NOT WRAPPED. DAWG. There's lettuce everywhere. I waited 10 minutes for lettuce and chicken to be everywhere in my car. I'm sick to my stomach man

We were waiting in line and suddenly i saw a woman was eating fries with burger. Her fries looked horrible and then I tried to look at the rating of this place And It got F. I never saw a F..lowest I've seen was B. Surprised that how can people eat here!! Left just at that moment

Amazing late night service after the mayday concert....

The best service for $2 items

There's absolutely nothing wrong with this Quizno's, but at the end of the day it's still fast food and not worth more than three stars. With that said, this particular location is always very clean and updated, and I've never had more than two people ahead of me. The staff are friendly and seem to enjoy their job, which is always a plus. 

Subway has been getting a pretty bad rap lately, and honestly I don't know if Quizno's is any better, but I definitely prefer it over Subway. Plus, Subway stores always seem to have that weird funky smell, whereas Quizno's smells like toasted bread and meat. Yum.

Completely enjoyed brunch. The food is delicious and the staff is amazing. There are few restaurants where I felt as welcome as I did today. The owner came out and checked on us. I will be back again!

I decided to give Scratch Biscuits a go after word of mouth from from friends. I ordered the Chicken Picnic Biscuit. WOW it was huge not expecting it to be that size! I had a food orgasm just eating the biscuit...it was flaky and buttermilky. The chicken dredge was a little too spicy for me but delicious. The chips were crispy and full of bbq spice...the best chips I ever had. The corn relish was refreshing and a good compliment to the chicken.

I love Wendy's burgers. This is a fairly new Wendy's so I thought I would try it. Never again. It was approximately 8:00 pm. The cashier was rude and not communicating with the customers and if you asked a question that seemed to be a major problem. I asked for a orange mango drink and she put in a orange chill. I asked her if that was the same as I had the orange mango at another location and it was delicious. She said it was and it was not. It was the most horrible drink I have ever tasted. Weak with no taste. She, the cashier, made it personally However I was too tired to take it back. I will never visit this Wendy's again and will advise anyone I know not to. The attitude and the service was very bad.

E'er damn time, I love it!  I don't pass through this neighborhood often, but when I do, Blaze is a must-stop-&-eat. Brought 2 new friends this time, and they were impressed by the food!  Quality and taste 5 stars, service of employees including speed, friendliness, and knowledge of their product 5 stars, clean and attractive dining atmosphere 5 stars!

Excellent food but the delivery was horrible. The driver forgot my milkshake and soda. I had to wait two hours for him to bring my drinks back and he still forgot the soda. I highly recommend picking the food up.

Cute place, but fell a bit short on their namesake Scratch Biscuits. The biscuit crumbled in my hands, and was dry. It also lacked any taste. Toppings were good, but that biscuit needs to stand up to the filling! Also, the service was not great. I walked in, and the girl at the counter was busy taking selfies in front of the menu board. I stood there a few minutes reading the board before she acknowledged me and asked if I was hungry.  Once I ordered, it was just a couple of minutes before I got my food. When I finished eating, I got up to throw my trash away. Again, no acknowledgement from the staff - busy on her phone again. I was the only person in the place, it was obvious that I was getting ready to leave. Wasn't asked how everything was, have a nice day, nothing.

The staff was friendly and engaging.  Brought my family (wife and 2 kids), the lobby was very accommodating and clean!  Love Love Love their blood orange lemonade!!!  The pizza was spot on as I anticipated! Will be back soon!
I had the Tomahto burger and it was awesome! Parm fries were delicious as well and milk shake was great. We were all very satisfied with our burgers.
Great food and prompt delivery.  I only wish they would lower the delivery min to a more reasonable $10 instead of $15

If you want poor customer service this is the place to go. I visited this fast food chain tonight, waited in line for someone to take my order. I was the only person there at that moment. All the employees saw me but no one ever came to take my order until a girl by the name of jamirah came up to take my order even though the look on her face was telling me she really didn't want too. When she proceeded to take my order the first thing she said was..."you ready". I'm thinking to myself I should be ready after standing there for 5 minutes while the lobby remains empty. Not to mention you have one of the staffers spraying and cleaning (airborne )where they dump the French fries. Thanks but...No!
Waited 20 mins for my food and when it came out it was wrong. Will never come here again.

The Moravian Food Court is potentially the most depressing place to eat on campus despite its spaciousness, if you're a Penn student, because it's bleak, grubby, and you can't work, but if you're really trying to save on cash, then I guess it can't be helped...

Indeed, every sad time I find myself in Moravian, the most affordable/consistent restaurant of the few featured is the Taco Bell/A&W combo. As a vegetarian, I have limited options with the Taco Bell food, but I've always had standard Taco Bell quality food coming here... the prices *are* higher than most Taco Bells I've seen around the country, but I'm not sure if that's just a Pennsylvania thing or a Penn thing. 
The lines move fast though, and the workers are not unfriendly, so if you're looking for a quick, cheapish, unhealthy, depressing bite on Penn's campus, this is the place to go.
Management needs help. None of the workers have any idea what they are doing... Over 30+min for a steak which did not have onions which i ordered.. I took itv anyways. It was tasty tho

This mcdonalds is far from clean.  Operating on temple's campus Broad & Sesquehannna, it can get busy. However, it should never cost $1.51 for tap water in an emergency situation.  I should not have to dig for a debit card to get tap water in 82°

My wife and I have been trekking over to Desi Chaat House for some time because the other three U. City Indian places are more Americanized greasy buffet-type places.  I doubt we will do that much longer.   This place isn't high cuisine, but it's extremely tasty, nicely spiced, and cheap.  The paratha rolls are superb and really can't be had anywhere else.  The chaat was a bit drowned in sauce but still really quite good.  The puri were light with a nice light sauce to accompany.

The decor is pretty shabby, but we did take-out (delivery begins next week), and Saunders Park is a block away if it's a nice day.

All-in-all, it's worth a trip.

Ehh. Not really doing it for me.

I was here at the very beginning of when it opened, so things may have gotten a bit better afterwards as they got into it, but service was slow, the veggie burger was okay, and I wasn't the biggest fan of their fries. The biggest problem with their burger, for me, at least, was that it seemed to be an entirely edamame-filled burger. Don't get me wrong - I love my edamame, but it should be on a tray with a pinch of salt and cayenne pepper. Even in a burger, it's okay, as long as it is in moderation.

It is rather reasonable (I think I paid ~8-9$ for my entire meal), but for the same amount of money, you can go to Chewy's or Pyramid Pizza and get a better veggie burger.

Now, if you are a meatatarian, by all means, I think that this is your place. They have a ton of different choices for you, and the 7-8 different 'styles' for burgers all seem rather appetizing.

I'll try to go back some time soon in order to give it a second chance, and will update appropriately. Sadly, my expectations aren't too high...

UPDATE:
The owners of Scratch Biscuits have heard the complaints and changed their biscuit recipe. It was certainly better than the biscuit I had the first time I went there, but it was still overall fairly underwhelming. The biscuit actually held together and this time my sandwich came with a side order of mediocre chips.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Scratch Biscuits was overpriced and underwhelming. They were out of the Benton's ham at 12:15 pm, and I assure you that it was not because they sold out during an early lunch rush. The place was nearly empty and felt sterile, and not in a way that reassured me that everything was hygienic, but as if the place was designed by someone who specialized in those weird froyo stores**.

I settled for the fried chicken biscuit. The fried chicken biscuit and an orange soda totaled $12.50. The sandwich was a meager portion size considering the price, and I was not willing to spend more on a side that I was already suspecting would be fairly mediocre given the atmosphere. My first inclination was to pick up the biscuit to eat it like a sandwich, but the biscuit crumbled as soon as I touched it. The biscuit tasted OK but it was dry, the cabbage slaw was nearly one hundred percent carrots, which did not necessarily bother me, but just seemed odd, the corn relish was bland, and the ranch dressing was surprisingly undetectable. The chicken was tasty, although for the price of the sandwich, I was expecting a heck of a lot more chicken, and I was pretty disappoint to find that one of my three slices of chicken had a large portion of gristle in it.

I do not recommend anyone waste their time or money going to Scratch Biscuits.

** Turns of this location was formerly a froyo store. The new decorations at Scratch Biscuits are lazy and uninviting.

I ordered a "value meal" with a $1 off coupon.  It included a foot-long sub, chips, and soda.  The total was $8.10 ($9.10 w/o coupon).  That price would have been ok if the sub was excellent.  But it wasn't even close.  I would have been better off going to a neighborhood sub shop or Wawa.  Not worth it.

Although the food was good the customer service sucks, even though you had a long day doesn't mean you can talk to your customers anyway you want first rule of businesses customers first I will not be coming back to this establishment!!! Takes the term ratchet to a whole Nother level

Good food, fast service, affordable, and very nice decor. Seating arrangement not great. They should have more tables for 4.

The veggie bowl with fried tofu was pretty good. Loved the full size portions. Hearty, healthy meal.

This place is just plain better than it should be for being on a college campus. It's amazing flat bread pizza at reasonable prices. You can get a simple pie just sauce and cheese with sea salt and oregano for only $5.50 and it's incredible. Great restaurant

Terrible service, Terrible food 
Would not recommend. The one on Chestnut is much better
The chicken quesadilla from Taco Bell is really good - get it with A&W fries and you have a cheap but winning combination.
Horrible Drive through service today. Took over 20 minutes. They did get the order right, we kept it simple on purpose.

Took forever and order was incorrect. I was standing in line for 30 minutes before they asked me "what did you order?"  I have to wait an additional 15 minutes after that. What is going on back there??

This is one of Temple's best places to grab a bite to eat! The service is always friendly and everyone is happy. There is plenty of space to accommodate just yourself or a large group of friends. The food itself is fantastic! The topping options are endless and very fresh. Without a doubt, the best part is the ability to control the construction of your personal pizza.  Although lines can get long during lunch and dinner, the wait is well worth it!
So gross and unsanitary. The bathroom was so dirty, I couldn't even use it. I was so disgusted I threw away my soggy wrap and let. Will never come back. Yuck.

My daughter told me about Scratch. It's a nice place. I'm not a big fan of biscuits so I decided to give them a try. I got the Kentucky Wildcat. It was good but not enough to really rave about. Will I go back? Yes. Will Scratch be a go to place? Probably not.

As a lover of biscuits, I was looking forward to giving this place a try. I was unfortunately disappointed with my breakfast biscuit. The egg was square shaped and spongy, looking like it came from a frozen packet. A freshly made egg would have been much more enjoyable. The biscuit itself was tasty, dense but not dry. I do wish it held together more while eating my sandwich.
When I am craving fried chicken, this is where i want it from. The fried chicken at this restaurant is always hot and delicious! I highly recommend  this Popeye's in this area.

After regularly stopping by, I grew on this restaurant a bit more. I really like their pizzas and sandwiches, but my favorite would be their curly fries! Their service isn't the best and they're not as attentive, but the food makes up for it.

All the subs I've gotten from all Subways taste the same to me (as they should?), but I'm avoiding this one for life. They're so stingy with the ingredients! Lettuce and such should be packed on the sub, not sprinkled. The bread-to-innards ratio was a big no no for me :(

Cute Decor - lousy biscuit - 
Tasted microwaved not at all flakey and yummy 

Maybe with the sandwich stuffings makes this better but some how I doubt it

Sorry to say it was a dissapoontment

This Popeye's restaurant was a quick stop after our brunch reservations fell through before The Roots Picnic. A seemingly odd choice for a group with one vegetarian and one pescatarian, but turned out to be a lifesaver in time of desperation!

My friends received their chicken orders quickly, but I had a small wait for my shrimp box. I was a bit disappointed because they did not have catfish, and we quickly realized they were out of quite a few key items (ketchup, honey, lemonade, butter). They did compensate for their shortcomings by giving us extra helpings of sides and FRESH biscuits. 

Everyone was very satisfied with our meals on the go! Biscuits are bae.

Spencer's is my favorite go-to lunch spot. The burgers are always delicious and the parm fries are to die for.

My favorite on the menu, however, are the buffalo wings. Absolutely the best. The bleu cheese is homemade and so fresh. 

Everything about Spencer's make me swoon.

Let's start with the Paratha. That thing was vintage, it was a former Paratha. You could sell it as a shabby chic coaster on Etsy. The "cubed lamb" in my roll was microwaved gyro meat.You can cut a gyro into a square, but it doesn't make it cubed lamb.

I always feel awkward asking for the A&W menu here because the employees seem so reluctant to make it and it generally takes forever b/c they don't have any of it pre-prepped for the most part. I don't mind that part though; I'd take fresh fries and cheese curds over something that has been sitting around a while. However, like Sara, I have been told that they weren't doing the A&W side, and once, that they had NO burgers... running out of burgers is a strange thing for a burger joint with minimal traffic....

I'm sure there are lots of little faults you can find with this particular franchise, but honestly, I'm just really happy that there's a Taco Bell conveniently on Penn campus for me to get my Baja Blast and chalupa fix when I need it.

The service here is minimal, but efficient. You normally don't have to wait longer than three minutes to get your food. The quality of the food itself can vary, but for the most part, it's pretty standard with what'd you get at any Taco Bell.

I've personally never tried ordering off the A&W side of the menu, so I don't really care if they actually serve those menu items or not. Everyone comes to this food court for the Taco Bell anyway...I've rarely seen anyone come here for A&W. 

I do have a friend who says that the A&W fries are fantastic when you can get them because the employees always have to make them fresh. I'll never know because I just want my Baja Blast and tacos.

Taco Bell. I'm just happy there's one on campus.

Delicious! My "Plain Jane" was everything I wanted a biscuit to be. 
I grabbed a biscuit to go, so I didn't experience the sit-down-and-stay experience, but the woman at the counter was courteous, and like I said, that biscuit was GOOD!

Expensive but worth it...?

Definitely not. I have worked in the food service industry for over 5 years and while I've thought about wringing my customer's necks a couple times, I would NEVER speak to or treat them the way I was treated by the staff here. I'll start at the beginning.

I went here yesterday with a friend after class because it was right around the corner from our school (CCP) and I have never been. Normally, I go to the Saladworks at the Willow Grove Mall because it's close to where I live and I've never had a problem there. 

We walk in and it's mostly empty. The staff looks like they don't know why they're there and have the well known "Philly" attitude about them.

I order a buffalo chicken salad and small Maine Lobster Bisque. I paid $18.31. 

The soup has barely any taste and severely lacks the Lobster taste as well as the actual pieces. Did I mention it was lukewarm? The salad was fine except the Indian woman slathered it in bleu cheese dressing, as if that can make up for too few toppings. Also, the avocado was practically frozen, and I got beans and artichoke by some horrible chance of luck. Don't get me wrong, I love artichoke but only if it's been steamed and there's plenty of butter to slather on the good parts. The artichoke piece didn't bother me so much as the frozen avocado did.

Now the fun begins. I take my salad up to the counter and tell them I tasted artichoke and the avocado was frozen (I hadn't yet found the bean). The African American girl starts the Philly attitude first. She rolls her eyes, leans on the counter disinterestedly and mumbles under her breath about me right while I'm standing there. As if I can't hear her whispers. The Indian woman inspects my salad and declares there's nothing wrong with it and gives me a spiel about how the avocado can't possibly be frozen. I tell her she can taste it if she doesn't believe me and that there isn't anymore artichoke to be found so far because I ate the piece by accident. She badgers me demanding to know what it is I'd like her to do. I tell her I'd like her to remake my salad. Her response: "Oh no, I can't do that. The salad is 13.00$s I can't. What do you want? More toppings?" I give up and tell her I want more tortilla strips. She throws broken pieces of them on top and I go back to sit with my friend at the dirty booth.

I don't even get a bite in before I spot the lima bean sitting cozily in my salad. I take it back and show the Indian woman the bean and she again declares it was simply a mistake, I'm making a big deal out of nothing. I'm sorry, would any of you pay 13$ dollars for messed up food? The woman again starts yelling asking me what I want and I tell her I want a new salad. I want my money's worth. She remakes it herself, very angrily, without the avocado (not gonna make that mistake twice), and I leave with my friend. The fighting made me lose my appetite and I wound up having to throw it out because surprise surprise, salads don't fair too well on an hour long ride home. I will never come back here.

All in all, I lost my money, time, and appetite. I only wish I'd read the reviews before I went here. It would've saved me the trouble and my spoons. (Look up Spoon Theory if you don't get the reference). Also, I should note I've never felt so compelled to write a review in my life about somewhere I've been. The staff needs to be fired or intensively retrained on how to handle food and customers.

Heed my warning fellow foodies, reviewers, and customers. Do NOT eat here.

Horrible. I sat in the drive through for five minutes, I can hear the person taking the order talking to a coworker through the speaker. I loudly say hello? Multiple times, no response. Pull up to the first window. There's cardboard over it. Pull up to the second window. Takes them 10 minutes and multiple honks of the horn to get anyone to come to the window. Finally placed an order, but they didn't have any fries ready so I waited. Finally got my food, no ice in a warm soda. This place needs to be overhauled or shut down.
Really enjoyed my brisket on a biscuit. Can't wait to go back & try more.
I go to tony Luke's a lot and I get uncle mike sandwich with sharp cheese. It's the best.  the service is good and the people are nice. I give it 10 stars. Anna

The only time I've stopped at this location was today. It will be my final visit. I went to the drive through, and was giving my order. I hesitated for a moment trying to decide on what drink I wanted with my meal and the woman very rudely yelled at me to pull to the window to complete my order. I drove to the window, past it, and out of the parking lot. No need to scream at your customers.

I'm a sucker for a good biscuit, and I had bribed myself by saying I would come here after a doctor's appointment in the city last week. The decor is cute and the staff was friendly. I used the bathroom first-thing, and found that the sink plumbing was leaking all over the floor. However, I brought it to their attention and they seemed to get right on it. The place definitely had a feel of somewhere that had just opened and hadn't worked the kinks out yet.

I thought I should stick to something classic, so I got the "Johnny paycheck", which is just eggs, bacon, and cheese. I really wanted a Sip-n-Glo juice, as advertised, but it turns out those are "coming soon". Boo. As others have stated, the portion is pretty sad for the amount you pay, and the biscuit completely falls apart when you try to eat the sandwich. My eggs were in a hard brick shape (definitely not made to order) and the cheese sauce was so weird - very fake and runny. I honestly don't think I'll be back because I can make a significantly better breakfast sandwich at my house for much less.

The first time I went to this Wendy's location, the Foot Locker across the street was held up at gunpoint as I was leaving. It was this huge spectacle and one of my first experiences in Philly. 

When it comes to fast food, out of the big 3 I'm going to have to pick Wendy's. Their fries are the best and there is recognizable chicken in the chicken sandwiches. This location leaves a bit to be desired, though. The dining area is usually quite dirty, I'd recommend taking your food to go. 

Also, the employees are particularly surly. Although I do find it kind of funny that when they call you up to the register they say, "can I have the next cust" as if some efficiency consultant removed the last two syllables of the word "customer." But I don't like to have my food thrown at me, thank you very much.

Much improved from visits a couple of months ago.  Yay!!  Biscuits are considerably bigger and warmer.  Size of toppings larger and biscuit held together.  It's not cheap, but I was full when I left.  Had Fried Chicken biscuit w. pimento cheese sauce, and some other toppings--tasted great.  Size of sweet potato fries much bigger too.  Staff was on point and moving fast to get the orders out.  
Scratch is definitely back on my list of places to visit a couple of times a month.

Scratch Biscuit was awesome!! Had the breakfast biscuit with egg and scrapple. It was delicious. The biscuit is really well done, the eggs were fresh, and the scrapple was really tasy. The food was also served quickly and the restaurant was really cool. Loved the Hot Biscuits sign! Would definitely go again and it's a great option for people in the rittenhouse/center city area. Can't wait to try the fried chicken biscuit which looked great!
Meat was dry and tasteless. I thought I couldn't go wrong with getting a cheesesteak at Tony Luke's but I guess not. Definitely will not waste my money by coming back here again

Fresh steaming hot food served to you with a smile!  KUDOS - to the team.  
When you don't have much time for lunch - and you want something to eat that satisfies your cravings AND your senses....Please try Wok Street - I promise you will not be disappointed.  

Mouth watering dishes - all I can say is that I am addicted - thanx for bringing your good food down this end of Chestnut Street...next stop Ai Ramen - located in the Shops at Liberty!

Ok, so my wife and best bud were loitering the streets in Philly, in town for our other best buds epic wedding. We were hungry, and my wife gets HANGRY when the stomach starts grumbling.  Luckily, we stumbled upon this spot - and she of the Midwest loves her fried chicken & biscuits. I hoped this would be our saving grace.  

Walked in, it's clean, it's friendly, and it smells amazing.  A combo of fresh biscuits and meats.  Aside from a taco shop, probably one of the best smells you could want in your nostrils.  Went to order, had a variety of options.  Plenty from the menu to choose from, but we had to choose one each, unfortunately (it's the "socially acceptable" thing to do I hear).  I had the brisket biscuit. She had the fried chicken biscuit and so did the Rog.  They went with the classic biscuit menu item (I don't blame them, sets a great comparison for future biscuit spots).  Let's start with mine:

Brisket Biscuit Sandwich.  Ill start where most people would:  the biscuit.  Now I don't know where your taste buds or baking chops land on the biscuit expertise scale, but mine are of the casual "I know a good biscuit" variety. And this was a good biscuit.  It had a slight crunch on the exterior, but a wonderfully flaky, warm and chewy interior.  Not dry at all, and really had a delicious hearty flavor.  Which made for an amazing complement to the brisket and slaw filling.  Look, it isn't a bbq joint, so I'm not expecting Freddie's BBQ, but it's about as good as I could want - I am a brisket aficionado - to fill my biscuit and take it over the top.  Just the right meaty flavor, and a great portion size.  Made a delicious sandwich.  The pickled red onions added a nice light crunch, sweetness and cold factor that brought it all together with the horseradish mayo not being overpowering.  Full disclosure I omitted the cheese.  All told, the biscuit started it, and the brisket topped the experience with southern charm and class.  

Fried Chicken Picnic Biscuit:  Now theirs.  I only tried a bite of her Fried Chicken Picnic Biscuit but it was enough to tell you that you shouldn't deny yourself this pleasure.  The fried chicken was delicious, juicy and freshly fried, and most importantly crunchy.  You heard that crunch.  The corn relish was seriously amazing.  There is something similar in Mexican cuisine and I was surprised to see this on a biscuit sandwich - pleasantly surprised.  With the slaw and cayenne ranch dressing it was a creamy complement (like garlic butter on steak good) that brought it all together.  This was one corn fed chicken that I could support.  

The chips served were crispy and fresh, no complaints here...but you don't go to a biscuit joint for the chips. Next time I'll get a biscuit sandwich with a side of biscuit.  Until next time Scratch Biscuits, you saved the day and gave us an amazing meal in the process.  Philly = City of Biscuitly Love.

This was the worst. 1st it's lunch time mid week. It took 30+ minutes to get a burnt hard and crusty chicken biscuit. The chicken was so burnt the coating came right off. Nothing fresh going on here?  The biscuit was like lead. Too expensive for crap not even well prepared.

Devine! In a city with BBQ and southern cooking that are weak at best, Scratch stands as a beacon of biscuit sandwiches done right.  I had a pulled pork biscuit with cheese and bbq sauce that was warm, savory and had me scraping the container with a fork at the end.  I customized the biscuit with different veggies and it is clear that the menu was planned with additive flavors in mind so that any decision seems to work right.

As noted in other reviews, it is quite pricey for a relatively small portion. And $5 sweet potato fries round out a hearty meal but are a bit steep and perhaps should be included with a $9 biscuit. However, in a city of similarly overpriced food, at least you leave scratch saying "that was so delicious".

I was not impressed with this place at all. The fries and cheese whiz were good. My daughters chicken fingers were also good but unfortunately that's where it ends. I ordered a pork sandwich with provolone cheese and broccoli rabb. The meat didn't seem like it was good quality. The cheese tasted funky and the bread was completely soggy. I couldn't even finish my sandwich. Most of the bread was trashed. Total disappointment. I will not be back. I hear good things about the original location in South Philly. Maybe one day I'll try that location.

Constructive suggestions: 
1--switch to rolled biscuits. Drop biscuits are not surviving the fast casual process and quickly turn cold and/or dry. 
2-make portion size at least 1/3 larger, many yelpers post feeling ripped off 
3-list cheese sauces as "sauces" Menu currently says cheese--so we expect something other than sauce. 

Have had some great flavors here but had either dry or cold biscuits on 2 of 4 visits. I sent order back today and remake was cold. (Informed counter person that remake was "terrible"). 

Was sitting under a sign that says Hot Biscuits. Sigh....

I really want this place to make it--great concept, great ingredients, great flavors, but portions and consistency of main product are not working for me.

When I drove up to place my order, I was told, "one second." So I waited & they took someone else's order who came 5mins after me. Then when I got to the window to get my food, I was asked, "you got the 20 piece?" I said, "yes." Then she continued to asked me again, "did you get the 20 piece?" With a attitude & I replied "yes." I drove off with my food while they laugh & giggled. It led me to think that they had tampered with my food. They need to get rid of the employees there & start fresh. I wish I can give this McDonald's zero stars because it does not even deserve 1 star
Looks can be deceiving.. The menu can make you drool, but when you get it.. It's too oily.. They do have great service though.
Horrible wait times, rude ignorant staff. Don't be surprised if you are waiting as much as 30 minutes in the drive-through line.

As far as a little caesars goes, this is top notch!!! Friendly people all the time and one time received a great customer experience with the manager. I have been here at least six times in the past year and each one has been great!  If you want cheap, fast, and delicious food, come here!

Saw this place close to my hotel and thought it was a cool concept.  Place totally empty at 630pm on a Tuesday. Tried the chicken biscuit w/ cheese and and ordered another plain biscuit to take back for breakfast  $11  Service nothing spectacular.  Biscuit wasn't much didn't seem fresh, broke apart, had to eat with a fork....chicken was OK but I think it was old and cheese was a sauce.  Meh.  Wasn't horrible but it also wasn't what you get in a southern restaurant which is what I expected.

I don't eat a lot of fast food, but Wendy's is my favorite fast food place. However, this will be my last time going to this location. Having ordered at the drive through, my order is wrong 90% of the time. I'm not interested in having to root through my order in the car to double check the incompetence of the restaurant staff. What baffles me is the receipt lists the correct items, but still the contents of the bag are wrong/missing. Skip here and go to Whole Foods for a healthy, inexpensive pre-cooked value meal.

I don't get the hype about this place. Sure, its customized, but there is nothing special. The cheese isn't some exotic Mediterranean import nor are the dressings. 
Place is chill for hanging out and chilling, but not necessarily pizza. 
Pizza makers are great and personable. And the AguaFresca is great!

This is the WORST DQ in the history of the universe.  They have "forgotten" our ice cream cake for birthdays in our office TWICE in just a few months, with no apologies and a mere $3 discount offered for the second time they forgot. Their excuse?  They were "busy".  

Excuse me, it's late October (not prime ice cream season) and I was the ONLY CUSTOMER in the store as they tried to give me this bs answer.  This sloppiness basically ruined the surprise we were trying to give our coworkers for their birthdays.  Do NOT patronize this business!  Unprofessional to the highest degree.

Still a big fan fan after several more meals, although the chicken kabob only had 3 medium size chicken chunks on it along w/ a few vegetables - I felt it should have been more plentiful. The staff/ownership is very friendly.

The most recent order was a delivery and although the guy was apologetic for the delay in finding us, he could't follow the simplest instructions - ring the door bell at our well identifiable address sign. He calls our phone after trying for 15 minutes to find us - when he came I looked at the order slip and it had our correct address clearly written on it. He said the order taker told him we were near an intersection - just tell him to go to the address, nothing more, nothing less - it's really not that complicated.
Good Strombolis. Wings are tolerable. Hopefully, I'll never have to eat here again because it is in the hood and I got out of the hood, yo.
The staff in this Quizno's is very friendly; dining here is very pleasant.

the place is like a chinese chipotle but with wooden rustic interior (i could still smell the scent of fresh wood) lol looks like there are enough seatings for about 20-30 people.

the menu shows 4 signature dishes:

signature chicken bowl
peanut sauce with pork
shoyu steak
thai tofu with cold noodles

i went with the steak which is actually pulled beef? it's still ok~ i love the veggies choices like edamame medley and brussel sprouts. IMO portion is decent for the price.  i believe everything is under $10.  I also got to try their matcha green tea~ very refreshing!  they have summer rolls and a tofu cheese cake for add-ons~ i do wonder what the tofu cheese cake tastes like haha next time!

Drive by night fast food. Easy to read menu, fast service and affordable.Can't complain because the food here taste the same all the time. The only thing I wish they improved on is "offer some condiments!" If you don't ask and drive off -- you'll be asking "dude, where's the ketchup?
Easily the best pizza on campus. If you have a thing for thin crust pizza, this place nails it.

We've eaten here and taken out 3 times in the past few weeks. Happy to report the food is very good middle eastern. We've had both sandwiches and platters - both excellent. The platters are well worth the price - big portions! The Baklava is great as well. Oh, the salads are above average too. Also like the thin, wide pita they offer. 

They do need to add all their menu information to their cash register computer printout, so you know what you ordered and know how much the tax is - every item you purchase is named Dept 01 - it just makes good business sense to make this correction.

I was excited to try this place after looking at the menu. I went in.. ordered the cheesesteak wiz tots... and didn't receive them until 30 minutes after. (No exaggeration).. There was a total of 8 people in there, and half of them already eating. There was no urgency in the workers to try and get the food out that was being waited on. No apologies from them either. My friend left without hers.. but I have patience so I waited! Food wasn't that bad though. I expected worse while I was waiting. Huge portions would definitely split it with another person. I was upset because that place has potential .. but they need new workers.  I personally wouldn't return.. or at least to that location.
