It little Caesars. You know what you're getting. Quality and polite staff as well

My husband and I enjoyed Supper Restaurant because we consistently had excellent meals there (granted, most of them were brunch) so we expected the owners to pay the same attention to quality in their new restaurant, Scratch Biscuits. Unfortunately, we were disappointed when he picked up our order to go yesterday. 

He ordered the fried chicken biscuit and I ordered the black bean chili cake biscuit. Both sandwiches came with homemade chips and I also ordered a side of their pickles. The fried chicken and chips were completely over fried to the point they tasted burnt and were very dark colored. The biscuits fell apart and were dry. Since the sandwiches are larger in size, I think the biscuits could be more substantial to withstand the sandwich fillings. Also, the black bean chili cake tasted rather mushy and kind of bland. However, the one bright side was that the pickles being excellent- not too sweet and not too sour. They had the perfect amount of tang to them. 

Overall, we weren't overly impressed with the food and, knowing what the owners are capable of producing in terms of quality food, we're hoping it was just a fluke off night for the restaurant.

I love this place! It is just a marvelous as the ones in NYC.... been eating Mamoun's since the 80's and was so pleased to find them in Philly..... This is a must try! Try the picked turnips, will change your life! The staff is so friendly just a WINNER .... great service, fantastic quality food ..... this is my new must go to in Philly
Not even one star this is the worst McDonald's in the history of McDonald's. Every person who works here deserves to die a slow broke death.

Let me preface this.  The biscuits are okay.  Just okay.  However, what goes into making them a bit more than a two-star review is the toppings and sandwiches offered.  I've had better biscuits from a box but that seems to disappear behind the apple butter - or any of their amazing breakfast sandwiches.  I feel like if you call yourself a biscuit place, your namesake shouldn't sink behind what you put on top - it's like good corn, you love putting some things on it but if it's good enough you also love just eating it as is.  I WILL go back just for the sandwiches, but if you want a good biscuit, make your own or find a bakery because these weren't quite what I was expecting.

Authentic, great value, delicious!!  Owner and son charming and friendly. Place is very clean. I highly recommend for lunch or to satisfy that sweet tooths urge. Worth a visit to South Street just for this.
Delicious biscuits, excellent service.  Will definitely be back when I'm craving fresh OJ, a fried chicken picnic biscuit, and peanut butter shake again

Had the chicken kabob plate. It was very good and the portions were decent. I ate in Mamoun's and it was busy. I am glad they were. I enjoy Middle Eastern food and want all the restaurants that serve this type of food to do well. Mamoun's seems to have an efficient operation and having many customers means the food will be fresh.

worst dairy queen ever!!! The employees always have a attitude when you order something besides ice cream. Also you will probably never be able to get anything besides ice cream. every time i went inside to order food they gave me an excuse that they were only serving ice cream. this has also happened to my coworkers. they also close at 9 but like to close early and have removed the hours sign from the window so nobody can call them out on it. i used to love dq but this location has ruined it for me.

New location. Place is clean and very staffed up. The training team must still be helping. The concept is good. Order at tablets or at counter. My ticket time was about 8 minutes. So not a long wait for food. They were not very busy during my visit. The staff are friendly. The food is ok. Four stars for the staff working hard. If it was just rating the food, it would be 2 stars maybe 3 at best.

Just like any other Quizno's, this place provides a quick tasty sub, soup or salad.  I've been here a couple times and there has never been a crowd.  This may be because it is located in a store plaza that is a few blocks away from Germantown Ave and doesn't draw a lot of business from around Chestnut Hill.  The staff is polite, but I wouldn't consider them overly friendly.  Like most chains, I wouldn't recommend this place for a unique experience, but its definitely great for a reasonably priced lunch.

Yum! Nice concept, nice people. And did I mention, yum!

Just opened a week ago. Got a chance to chat with the owner. It's not cheap but it's in line with Center City lunch prices. I'm looking forward to trying their breakfast menu.

Should have listened to the Yelp reviews instead of insisting on trying Scratch biscuits myself. Dryyyyy biscuits and chicken. I got my sandwich with mayo and had to ask for more on the side to combat the dryness and make it edible. 

Also, the menu board displays that all sandwiches come with homemade chips and pickles. Since my boyfriend and I each ordered sandwiches and neither of us received chips and pickles, I asked the cashier who said they did not have any made. He offered to give us a side of hush puppies as an alternative, which I took him up on, because I should have been given the option when ordering or offered a discount on their pricey sandwich combo.

By the way, the hush puppies were extremely dry as well.

What a disappointment. Growing up in the south I've eaten my share of biscuits. These are flavorless, to the point it made the BBQ on the "pigcuit" seem even more bland. And it wasn't even a hot biscuit. The BBQ itself was good but on the bland side as well but some hot sauce might help. They have a drink they call sweet tea but no self respecting southern gentleman would call that cloudy dirty water they are pushing tea. The staff was apathetic at best. Overall a poor experience.

It's not bad, but it's very far from great. A bit disappointing, because it's a good concept and the place looks good. People are very nice and friendly.

The tots are decent. A bit dense and maybe need some chopped jalapenos or something on top. The comeback sauce is good.

The chicken biscuit is decent. The chicken was good, but the piece of chicken is small. Like noted, the slaw is almost entirely carrots and while it's not bad, there's too much of it. The biscuit is poorly made and mine was already broken before I even had a chance to take a bite. They really needed to visit Hominy Grill in Charleston to learn how to make a proper biscuit sandwich.

They mentioned something about lowering prices for breakfast biscuits. In reality, they need to significantly lower everything on the menu. They're charging Rittenhouse prices despite being in a really crappy location. $17 is far too much for the small portions.

My review might not read like a 1 star review. That's because one of the partners of the establishment rated his own place 5/5, as did his wife. To me, that is not proper form on Yelp and I decided to balance it out with the lowest I could give it.

I was sooo excited to see a Mamouns coming to Philadelphia.   My excitement was quickly shattered when I opted to grab my favorite falafel on a Saturday night after some libations only to  find you closed at 10pm!  that is NOT the Mamoun's way..  as a New Yorker, is the best late night snack spot till the wee hours.. I now refer to you as "the Fake Mamouns" go to NYC if you want the real thing!

My wife and I are from out of town. We went to Bobby's Burgers last time we were in town. Their burgers were good, but Spencer's burgers have them beat by far! Great tasting burgers and fries, and their prices are very reasonable. Our friends we are visiting loved them too. Definitely coming back next time we're around.

Ordered naked fries, a normal slider, and a scrapple slider -- all to-go.  It took a long time for our order to be ready.  By the time we got home (a 6-7 minute walk from the location) the fries were all soggy, but probably would have been good if we ate there.  I threw out the scrapple slider after a single bite, but the normal one was good.

As the other reviews reflect, this is one of the most run down travesties of a Wendy's most of us will (hesitatingly) step foot in. The food is a 50/50 shot that you'll end up with what you order. The staff is surly and burned out from having to deal with the myriads of homeless and drunks that wander through at all times of the day. Cleanliness would be possible with a match and some gasoline, but short of that be prepared for the skeeve factor.

Popeyes has THE best fried chicken you can anywhere.  The spices in the batter is what makes it.......if you get the non-spicy chicken you won't know what I'm talking about.  The spicy chicken is where it's at!

The biscuits are also amazing too.....I don't know what it is, but it's almost as if they put crack in the biscuits.....they are just amazing.

This particular location is just okay; it's your regular run of the mill popeyes.  It seems that late @ night towards closing time they run out of chicken, but the employees are very accommodating when it comes to that.  If you request substitutions (such as thighs for legs or wings for a leg) they will usually grant it, it just depends on who you get.  Most popeyes I go to it's hit or miss.

Essentially the chipotle of pizza. The people are really nice, the pizza came out fast, it's pretty cheap, and the ingredients are good. The crust and sauce were particularly tasty. Much better than your typical pizza place

Managers understand mistakes but medium wage employees need to learn customer service .ill give her a hint"you ain't gettin no fries".at that point my handicapped son in the back seat heard this and began crying.this drive thru employee needs to be fired.
Only bc of DENISE!!!! such speedy, yet cheerful and polite service! Is she a manager? If not, I would recommend evaluating her for such positions...
In the 15 min I was there every who ordered were told we are out of.... Large cups, green tea,  milk,  this place is kaotic stay away

I don't ever review fast food places, but I have stopped at this location 2 times when working locally.  The place is clean, and my food was better then most Taco Bell's, and served hot.  Customer service was also good both times.  If you like Taco Bell this is a great location

Came here around 8pm to grab food before meeting up with someone. Ordered two salads-no cheese- two chicken sandwiches, cookies, and a lemonade. aside from another person waiting and two people sitting eating, we were the only people in the place. After about 10 minutes i got antsy, as most fast food places, even wendy's, has my food prepared in under 5. there were about 3 noticeable people in the back: one making my salads, on her phone with airpods in as the cashier yells at her. cashier yelling about whoever took our order-it was him- and someone at the drive through who had to give us our drink. salad girl gave us our salads WITH CHEESE and got an attitude when scolded about it by cashier. cashier got so distracted yelling and gave us ANOTHER drink when we asked for forks. all this occurred in about 35+ minutes. overall irritating experience, unprofessionally and understaffed.

Disgusting!! I ordered the roast pork italiano, pork was so thick and fatty, broccoli rabe was gray and way too garlicky!! I took 2 bites and threw it out, and wasted $14, what a rip off. I'm never going back.

Worst experience at the drive thru window. The cashier was very nice but the ppl getting your order ready was extremely rude and confused. The girl gave me a small bag with 1 hashbrown and said have a nice day. Problem was I ordered 2 meals. Then she had an attitude asking "then what u order then" which then I told her my order on the receipt. Then she forgot my coffee with the meals.  I wish the previous ppl working the windows were here as these new ppl are making a bad name for this store.

Taco Bell is one of my favorite fast food restaurants so I was very excited when I found out there would be one opening in my neighborhood. We have been twice since the opening. The first time was very busy and it was the first week so I can look past the problems. This time I can't. While the cashier was friendly he was not properly trained to take simple request. I wanted a burrito grilled and was told they couldn't do that since he didn't know how to put it in to the system. This is a simple request I have done many times. It is actually even an option on the mobile app (which we actually tried to use but was not letting us add a combo to the order for some reason) Beans were clumped and hard on double decker taco. Burrito was open on one end and falling apart. Location was out of mild sauce for the second time. I completely understand it is a new location so hopefully all they need is some further training.

I really should had check Yelp before going into Scratch. The storefront was clean and nice, the walls were decorated with vintage newspaper, and the lights were bright. But it took the waiter at least three minutes to greet, and I was the only customer there. 
-Buttermilk chicken sandwich: The biscuits were surprisingly COLD, and flaky. Not even half way through the sandwich they had fallen apart completely. I eventually cut up the chicken into small pieces and finished it like it was fried rice but with broken biscuits. 

Next time I might go try the desserts.. not so sure about the biscuits.

Disappointed. I got some tofu noodle dish and it was pretty bland and tasteless. This place cannot afford mishaps like this being so close to 
honey grow. The staff was pretty helpful and I did enjoy this iced green tea drink but I doubt I'll be back.

Better off using cash. They'll double and triple charge you for a single order. How would one employee know what the other one was doing if they weren't in on it? Good thing I was able to check my phone for the transactions immediately. They were unapologetic for their mistake and were very rude to me. Then they talked about me in Spanish as I was leaving

Oh scratch biscuits.. We tried this relationship out twice and twice you've betrayed me. We came when you first opened and the food was good! But there was serious issues with your workflow. We attributed that to growing pains.

We return today to find exceptionally dry biscuits, topped with extra dry and under-seasoned brisket. I'll give you the one star for the fried chicken. The fried chicken was good, but again, the biscuit made it tough to eat. We also ordered the "demolished" yam fries. I can't believe we spent an extra $3 for a small dollop of pimento cheese. 

I was really looking forward to your banana pudding but there wasn't any available.

This visit made me very sad. I really wanted this to work out between us.
Please train your employes how to roll a burrito,every time i order over this place the food is falling apart

I am very used to traditional Shwarma and Falafel, but this place puts pickles on the sandwiches, which I don't think is a very good idea. I'm not very impressed and the cost is higher than other middle eastern food places in the area.
Love Baklava...  it was good and will be back again.  I didn't order anything, just grabbed some Baklava to bring home.. but if you are looking for Baklava in Philly, this is the place.

Don't even bother.

Seriously, that's both the staff attitude and store motto.  In the past seven years that I've worked near this particular franchise, I've watched it slowly roll downhill.

Being able to visit a few suburban Saladworks locations really makes this particular franchise stand out as the shining turd in the septic tank.  A little bit more expensive for a lot less product.  You'd think lettuce was a rare commodity the way they dole it out - you never have to worry about the lid popping off from an overabundance of salad with this place.

The place is dirty, chaotic, and staffed with employees who, while generally pleasant, have no idea how to work.  Everyone trips over each other; it's kind of amusing to watch.  

The best part of a visit is when you place an order online (so you don't have to stand in the 20-person deep lunch queue), and go to pick it up.  They'll conveniently "lose" your order, but you'll only find this out after standing at the pickup counter for about 5-10 minutes while the staff just glances at you occasionally.  After my order got lost for the third time (not in a row, to be fair) I gave up.  At least we can play "Soupy Roulette!", the game where you guess which soup they have (since they never update the website), and if it's a burnt scraping of soup paste from the bottom of the bucket or not.

Do you sometimes work holidays?  Not to worry, these guys don't- Guy Fawkes Day, Arbor Day, Take Your Hamster To Work Day, they close for everything.  I mean, it's not like they spend the day deep-cleaning the joint...so I don't get it.

Generally disappointing, occasionally annoying...you can do better, and you deserve it.  Hey, that's actually a good slogan!

Finally had a chance to indulge and can I say Sat-Is-Fied! I chose half pesto & half classic marinara with goat cheese, mushrooms, olives, spinach, onions & roasted peppers. I'm lactose intolerant so Pizza for me is usually a gamble but this was perfect. The crust was just right, not too heavy or thick. It was actually kind of lite. The size was perfect and I even had leftovers for dinner. I can't wait to return as the staff are very pleasant and the atmosphere is welcoming and comfortable. From now on this will be my go to spot for pizza!

I started this review last year, and just heard Scratch closed. I'm disappointed they never figured out how to improve the biscuits. Here's what i wrote but (not sure why) never posted:

Wish I could give a better review,  but the biscuits at Scratch just aren't good. The denser sandwich biscuit was bland and chewy, while the lighter biscuits were crumbly with only the faintest butter flavor. Neither biscuit was warm or tasted fresh, despite my being the first customer of the day. The toppings were delicious, as others have noted (especially the apple butter and sausage sandwich), but a biscuit shop must be judged by its signature product,  and Scratch had yet to figure it out.

As an aside,  the customer service was great and they have (sweet novelty) RC Cola on the fountain.

Hit or miss . Always look in your bag before you get home or you will be surprised. They can be very rude and unprofessional. Whenever O pull up it looks like a club everyone is having way too much fun and not in a professional way. Their are some good workers but as they say one bad apple spoils the bunch.

This place reminds me of a pizza place Chipotle style. Located on Temple main campus, you have the option of 1, 2, or BYO (build-your-own) with unlimited toppings at tiered prices. Came here with a friend and got the BYO (cuz why not?) and stuffed about just as much toppings as I wanted on it. Nice to note that this place does have a rather generous number of topping options available. While the pizza didn't take very long to cook (10 minutes tops, which I was happy about), the pizza was ... eh. Certainly not the best pizza I've ever had in terms of sauce, crust, and taste, but certainly not the worst I've had either. In short, it was passable and okay ... right in the middle. Not somewhere worth coming to just for a special trip, but certainly a good place to go if you're a student who is more budget conscious or looking for a quick bite to eat while nearby!
So yummy! We got a falafel and the shwarma sandwich with a side of hummus and pita (worth it!) and we tried all three desserts offered! We will definitely be back!

This review is based on two recent visits. I have mixed feelings about Mamoun's as I tended to only like half my meal each time. Maybe some growing pains at this new location. 

1st visit: Ordered the chicken kabob platter and the chicken was grilled perfectly, I loved it. Some of the best chicken I've had in years. As part of the kebab platter, I selected the rice which I didn't enjoy as it was completely covered in the house tahineh sauce. I could barely see the rice. Even had to scrape much of the sauce off the chicken as well. 

2nd visit: This time I tried the shawarma platter. Ordered the salad instead of rice and asked for the Tahineh sauce on the side. I really enjoyed the salad but this time I thought the shawarma was disappointing, not as good as some of the cities other shawarma options. The clear winner on this visit was the lentil soup, loved it. 

I would wait a month or two to allow the restaurant to get some more experience before I try again. I see the potential but the consistency is just not there. 

BK

GREAT FOR LUNCH!!! Staff is Pleasant greeted as soon as I walked in. I had the wok street chicken large. At first sight I didn't think it would fill me up but it did. The chicken was well seasoned not over powering. Everything is fresh an healthy will defiantly be back. Would have taken a picture but it looked to good an couldn't wait.
Couple of nights ago friends decided to stop and get a cheap pizza for dinner. Tasted to me like frozen pizza. Two hours later, we were worshiping the porcelain god.  Never again....

I was injured while spending the evening Philadelphia and many of the local pharmacies were closed. I stopped in to Dairy Queen and had the pleasure of meeting Carl. He was genuinely concerned about my well being and even gave me a bag of ice. I cannot thank him enough for coming to the rescue when I needed him most!

The famous Greenwich Village Falafel shop has come to Old City Philly.  Mamoun's has moved in to the busy corner of 3rd and Market Streets where it is offering its falafels and shawarmas to eat in or take out.  A recent falafel was decent enough but probably won't be the best you have ever eaten.  That's how it is at Mamoun's.  They serve good falafels and shawarmas very quickly (think almost fast food) and at low prices but they are not exceptional in my opinion.  And their famous hot sauce is def 'hot' enough ... I just don't like the flavor that much.  But I am still glad that Mamoun's is now in Philly because it gives me another viable quick meal option - especially in Old City!

I have been waiting months for this place to open up. Here it is- finally Mamouns location in the city of brotherly love. 

I ordered the combo plate with all of the meats, falafel sandwich, hummus and French fries. Everything was wonderful just like the original location on Mcdougall Street expect one thing ! THE PITA BREAD WAS NOT THE SAME AS OTHER LOCATIONS IN NYC & NJ. IT WAS TOO THICK AND GRAINY ! Please switch back to the thin pita bread that you use at the NYC & NJ locations. It makes a huge difference in taste and quality. 

Thank you !!!' I will check it out again.

Worst Wendy's on the face of the planet.   

Now I'm a pretty simple man.   There are few things I enjoy in this world... Drinkin Twisted Teas on the boat, swiping out of work, finding a clever jenga block, and a medium chocolate Frosty.   This Wendy's can't even handle the frosty.   I frequent this Wendy's far to much because, well, I'm a frosty addict.  If there was another Wendy's within 2 miles of me I would hike there barefoot and risk contracting HepC just to avoid this dump.  

Let's start with the appearance; trash everywhere.  Looks worse than the sidewalks in Chinatown on a Wednesday night (if you don't know what I mean please go check it out).  These workers could be defined more correctly as "standers."  There's always a line of 6 people or more because it's a populated area and the hospital engulfs this place.  There's also always 4-5 standers behind the counter, but do they open up more than 1 register? No.  That would require them to work.  Instead, 1 person reluctantly takes your order, then that same person slowly fills the fries and waits for the burger to be made.  They don't take another order until that person has all their food.  Meanwhile the other 4 workers just stand there.  This isn't me witnessing and reporting 1 bad day, this is every time I'm at this location.  The customers here are also the pits of the word.  I get it's a Wendy's in Philadephia, but most people are so cracked out they fall asleep at their table immersing their dirty faces in their half ingested mustard lined buns.  They need to be shooed away.  

Now, to the frosty.  It doesn't take a rocket scientist to know how to pour a frosty but it's apparently too much for this crew of standers to handle.  These people swirl the cup around in a circle motion under the ice cream dispenser as if it's an ice cream cone.  Now every time I get my frosty it's freakin hollow in the center.  Who the heck wants a hollow frosty?  This isn't a Lindt chocolate Easter bunny.  

Will I continue to get Frosties here multiple times a week?  Yes.   I can't help my illness.  But hate myself every time I need a choco frosty fix and it's only because of THIS Wendy's.  RIP Dave Thomas.  I know you would make this right.

One of the best pizza I ever had!! Can not ask for fresher pizza then blaze. My first time having blaze pizza was from left overs and it was already amazing when simply toasting it back up. But the last time I had it I went to the store and had it fresh right after it was made! I love the idea that all pizzas are the same size no matter what due to the machine they use to help them measure the size of the pizza. Along with that I really love how all ingredients are fresh and we get to put whatever we want on the pizza as long as they offer. They have many options and choices to offer from different sauces, cheese, veggies, meats, and seasoning. Besides that the smores pie they have is very delicious. The smores was quite expensive in my perspective but it's definitely worth a try. But the pizza they offer and amount of topping we can add on it is definitely worth the price !

If you're into rude service after an extremely long wait in the drive thru (13 minutes to be exact.), then this Wendy's is for you and apparently, just like every other fast food place within 10 miles...absolutely horrendous. 
I get it..it's 1:00 in the morning and you're beat. That's no excuse to be unpleasant, short, and rude when greeting customers and not have all the menu items available. Yo
I don't know how these inner city stores get away with having the most unfriendly, uncaring, unprofessional, and obviously, undertrained employees. I would really like to know how these owners and management of these franchises account for, and justify, their long ass drive thru wait times and what HAS to be possibly the worst CSR scores ever recorded...if that's even still a thing. Just to be clear, I'm not upset because I halfway expected it. I'm more sad that it seems like making sure customers felt appreciated is no longer the priority.

When in line I was talking to one guy finishing his meal and he said was his 5th time eating here in less than two weeks! And it did not disappoint. One of the best Middle Eastern foods I ever had. You can taste the freshness. Real explosion of flavor. Even the drinks are awesome. Can't wait to go back

Strange in that I walked up at 2a and even though it stated closing hours of 2a on the door, the workers didn't seem to mind and welcomed me in.  They were all polite and accommodating... at that late hour, that's fantastic.  

I got a chicken sandwich, a salad and some fries.  The fries were done fresh for me and were super delicious.  Also, they had already began cleaning, so the place was clean and stocked as well!
There is always a line and the hours are completely based off of the surrounding businesses. Staff is friendly, the line moves fast and it's clean.

I really wanted to love Scratch Biscuits.  I did love their biscuits - light and fluffy.  I loved their fried chicken - tasty with some heat.  I loved their sauces - tangy and tart.  I loved their sides - homemade hot pickles.  I loved their service - attentive and friendly.  The problem is when you put all the ingredients together you get a sloppy, crumbly, mess of a biscuit that falls apart when you try and bite it.  Just not the same when you need a knife and a fork to eat it.

This is the only Dairy Queen that I am aware of in downtown Philadelphia.  I live in the Rittenhouse Square neighborhood and walk to 6th and Chestnut Streets to satisfy my sweet tooth:  The Blizzard is my favorite!  Herschel is the manager--and maybe the owner--at this location.  He is a friendly guy who is always willing to accommodate the customer.  Look for Herschel and say hi when you visit.  I would highly recommend visiting this DQ, purchase a tasty treat, and take a walk around the historical area, Society Hill and Old City.  What could be better on a warm summer evening or any other day of the year?  Enjoy!

If you're looking for a place to take a first date, this ain't it.  If you want some delicious pratha rolls, this IS it.  I didn't come for the decor, I came for the chow, and it's good.  Great for take-out.

Hit or miss pizza, although I'm glad the grand opening of this place gives more options for Temple students who may not care for salads or stir-fry. 

Some of the enticing aspects of eating here is the ability to get your own pizza with whatever toppings you want- they even offer gluten free crust and vegan cheese for those with dietary restrictions.

Besides that, Blaze Pizza falls short. I often leave here after eating thinking "well, that was okay." Despite the numerous amount of combinations you can make, the pizza often times is lackluster in flavor. I find Blaze Pizza to be delicious when my order is drenched in BBQ sauce.

The staff are generally friendly and helpful and if you avoid rushes, there is ample seating. 

If it wasn't so convenient, I'd trek elsewhere for pizza.

This review is for delivery. My sister and I ordered the PA Dutchman. Prompt delivery and both sandwiches came with homemade chips. The chips were crunchy and had a kick- loved em. The combination of apple butter and onions was absolutely awesome. My one con is that we had to put the sausages in the oven a bit more as they were pink in the center. I'm not sure if that's the coloring of it, but I was feeling uneasy. Amazing biscuit breakfast sandwiches, and hopefully will make it a point to dine in soon.

As saladworks go, this one is pretty decent - and in the vast culinary wasteland of this neighborhood, it is a welcome and convenient (if pricey) choice.

Home of the $8.00 salad, saladworks offers salads, soups and panini sadwiches (which I never get - as I do not like them).

I have figured out the exactly right salad for me using the "create your own" option.  Thus, I rarely deviate from my "usual".

The greens are sometimes rusty - so I opt for spinach or spring mix.
I also do not care for the rolls, so I never get one.

It's an option for a quick lunch and I am glad they are here so I don't have to eat pizza every day.

The food is much worse than a typical Wendy's. Sandwiches are always cold and look like they've been sat on. Fries are underdone and soggy. Salads, usually a Wendy's highlight, are dreadful. The final straw is that there's a fight in this place at least half the times I've been there, and it's usually involving at least one employee. If you are visiting someone at the hospital and need a quick greasy meal to keep your spirits up, go down the street to Pandora's Box. *They* know how to do burgers and fries *right*.

IN SUMMARY
Food freshness: below average
Order accuracy: average
Overall staff attitude: abysmal
Cleanliness of dining area: poor
Cleanliness of bathrooms: really poor
Refills on drinks: nope
Condiments, napkins, utensils: you have to ask for condiments, but the rest are out in the open
Kid's play area: no. Good lord, don't even bring your kids IN here.
Drive-through: no

Out of all the corporate fast food joints, Wendy's holds a special place in my heart. Nothing like ubiquitous and reliable-tasting chili, baked potatoes, frosties, spicy chicken sandwiches, and junior bacon cheeseburgers. As one of the closest and most accessible big chain fast food joints around Temple's main campus, how does it rack up? Pretty typical. The quality of the food is standard; tastes just like any other Wendy's location. Never had a problem with them getting my order wrong, which is always a plus. I'd rather get takeout, as it's not particularly clean here. The service isn't as fast as you might expect of "fast food." They tend to get backed up when there are a lot of people. Beware of ordering items later in the day, because they might run out (e.g., chili, salads).

This was my best Blaze experience yet! My girl Michelle helped me from cheese sauce to sea salt without missing a beat. My pizza had just the right amount cheese, pepperoni, and mushroom. Michelle was very pleasant and kept up the conversation!
The baconator was good.  The cashier seemed overwhelmed and overworked.  She was giving attitude.  No straws.  Place smelled of burnt frying grease.  The bacon in the baconator made everything ok.

There's not much that can be said. The Shake Shack experience is typically the same everywhere you go.

+Good food
+Friendly staff

This is the first Shake Shack I've been to outside of NYC. I've noticed that their large drink is bigger (although it had too much ice) and I got a little more fries in my order. I enjoyed my Shack Stack and my lady enjoyed her Chick'n Shack.

Went here for lunch and had the bangkok beef. The food has good individual flavor but when it all came together they didnt seem to mesh well in my opinion. The food was good not great. Glad I tried it but Im most likely not going to go back or have cravings for it.

I ate there several months ago and had a brisket biscuit.  It was okay, but not $8 worth.  I decided I'd try again for the $5 deal, but haven't yet.  Today, I went in to get a biscuit box for my office, and it was a big disappointment.  The biscuit box is $13, and you get nine biscuits, butter, and jam.  It's a good deal... except that the biscuits are very dry.  They are not flaky or buttery as you'd want from biscuits to be eaten plain.  One coworker suggest that this is because they're made to absorb all the fat and sauce used when they're sandwiches.  On their own, though, they're just not good biscuits.

I only come to blaze pizza a bit. But when I do the pizza is always great! You can put anything on it! And this time it happened to be a 5 dollar pizza day for temple students! So I had to come! All the staff was wonderful! Lindsey was taking me and she asked for the deal for me(originally some of the staff thought it was only from 10-5 but it was all day!) I'm happy it was and she was super friendly. I decided to put all the difference cheeses on one and she said she never seen it and wanted try too! It was great haha. Jai, Freda and KP helped ring up my order and cut my pizza and all the other sauces on it! They were super nice and a chance to chat with them for a bit while waiting for my pizza! I like how they make it a really nice and chill environment. Def recommend coming here!
A1 Pizza, A1 staff. These guys always take care of me, Lebron needs to come out to this location to see how a real franchise is run !

LMAO OMG THIS WENDYS IS SO BAD!!!!! It's CRAZY inside for reall!!!! I've seen people smoking cigarettes inside, there's always random signage on the ground, it smells like burning grease, and there are always people playing MAGIC THE GATHERING like its 2001!!!!! The employees are nice but they're always out of stuff there!!! Last week I went and they were out of small cups so I was like can I have a medium cup and just fill it half way or something and I'll pay for a small and she like gave me a weird look and had to ask her manager!! Then they were out of Sprite!!! Is this HELL???? Also I don't think they shake the grease off the fries properly when they take them out of the fryer bc the fries taste AWFUL like dirt which is so gross!!!! Ok so then my friend Zilin went there today and the FIRE ALARMS were going off and he said like 6 people were trying to fight the cashier that's so weird!! Anyway yeah this Wendy's is gross and weird and if you wanna be sad go here bc it's sad here :(

The pizza here is great. You can pick from about 50 different toppings. The staff is always really friendly. It doesn't take long. The prices are reasonable, $8 for all the toppings you want, and cheaper prices for one-topping and no-topping pizzas. Overall great experience. Convenient for temple students. The two cons are there is no parking and the music is always way too loud.

Very rude and unwelcoming cashier.... the ice cream was great and the service was relatively fast however, it was obvious that the woman in the front absolutely hated her job. I would not recommend coming to this location.

Don't be afraid to ask the staff questions about the menu or what they'd recommend! I tried the Macdougal with shawarma, falafel, tomatoes, lettuce, onions, and tahineh sauce. I was pleasantly surprised by the tenderness and how flavorful the meat was! The falafel is also very different from other places--not like round balls but kind of like flatter discs. Can't wait to try more of their menu next time.

Wow! Great value! Great food! Welcoming people working there. Been here a few times and each time I'm greeted like an old friend. The food is served quickly and it's excellent. If anything isn't perfect, manager goes above and beyond to make it right. Eat in, take out... both are awesome!

The worst. Distracted workers on their phone and more busy gossiping. Super long wait time and very dirty sitting and standing area. The worst McDonald's location my family and friends have ever stepped foot on. Meat in the hamburgers gave almost everyone stomach problems.

This is the worst Wendy's I have ever been too. I live 5mins from it so I usually come here. But they suck. They are rude and the one thing that's the worse is that when you pull up to the pick up window, they always ask you to reverse so the time can reset and it seems like they are doing it fast. It's super annoying! Also, they get upset when you ask for extra ketchup and BBQ sauce. Like they are paying for it. I have called many times and nothing has changed

When it comes to Wendys, I'm not usually looking for great service, but this place doesn't even try. Every single time I've gone here (and I try not to go as much I can) I've had a rude cashier who seems somehow bothered by my order, and the employees behind the counter are always screaming at each other in a way that makes customers feel uncomfortable. 

This Wendys also stretches the definition for "fast food" because it always takes an extremely long time for the food to come out, even when the place isn't packed with college students. I've stood by the counter for fifteen minutes only to have someone finally notice me and ask to be reminded of my order again. 

I guess I should also note, although I'm not sure if this relates to all Wendys locations, but the food here always me feel sick a few minutes after eating it. Could just be a fast food thing, but I notice it here more than anywhere else. I don't want to think of the implications behind that in regards to kitchen cleanliness.

So I walked by this place plenty of times in center city and I decided to give it a try yesterday . I like trying new and different things . 

It was pretty empty on a Tuesday night . I should of known better but still gave it a try anyway . Place was nice and clean . 

So my boyfriend and I ordered "the Pigscuit" and it wasn't what I expected . The biscuit was really dried as I was picking it up , it started falling apart . I took a bite into it and at first I thought it was good until after the first and second bite I kind of gave up . Supposedly it was supposed to have pork rind in it but I don't think there were any . The pull pork tasted dried and it wasn't good at all . It's wasn't worth it .
I liked their meat shawarma and baklava. There was tahini in shawarma which I am not very used to. Baklava was tasty.

This place is pretty nasty. Last time I was there the dining room was unclean and my order was incorrect. The food was lukewarm and starting to congeal. I know it's fast food, but this was unusually bad.

Just don't! Don't do it! Go next door to Five Guys.

   This has got to be the worst Wendy's I have ever been to. The staff seem to be perpetually confused, basic math is beyond them and glaciers move faster. It is a crap shoot as to quality - might get crispy fries and soggy burger this time, next time it might be overcooked burger and soggy fries. Let's leave the sodas and dried out bacon off the discussion list. Wait time is also another crap shoot - some lunch hours it is a few minutes, like they were prepared and others like a total shock "someone ordered something???" The dining room is usually pretty clean even with the homeless who camp out at certain tables nursing a small burger. The bathrooms are a nightmare. I often wonder if management from corporate ever visits this store, in the many years I have been stopping in here (usually twice a year at most since I don't eat fat food much) there has been no improvement, other than the employees.
   For about the same price go next door to Five Guys - the burgers may be about the same quality but the selection of toppings and the always crispy fries put this poor excuse for a burger joint to shame. And, for those who care, Five Guys has free refills!

I want to like this place because I love the woman who runs it.  But the food ranges from nothing special to pretty bad.  

The rice tastes like something from a cafeteria.  If you are a middle eastern restaurant that cannot make a decent rice, something is wrong  Hummos and baba are fine but nothing spectacular.  I couldn't force myself to finish my spinach pie it was that flavorless.  Their chicken looks like a processed product for vegetarians who want to pretend to eat meat.  

I think their desserts are expensive and while nothing is wrong with them, it is certainly not great baklava.  My husband loves this place.  When he needs to grab food fast in this neighborhood, he always stops in here.  But, then again, he is a guy who love cafeteria food.

After a trip to NYC a few years ago and dreaming about it for years in Salt Lake City, I was surprised to find Mamoun's on our recent trip to Philadelphia. With only 24 hours in the city I didn't hesitate for a second when deciding on eating at this branch of Mamoun's. Their falafel's are so crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. They're willing to throw in some pickles and olives at no extra charge. They're super delicious with the famous hot sauce. Caution: it is SPICY! You're able to purchase it to take home and I totally did. I'm already regretting that I didn't get more than one bottle. I HIGHLY suggest that you go here and everyone get falafels!

I went to Scratch Biscuits for breakfast this weekend and was very pleased.  The friendly service, expansive menu and delicious Rival Bros. Coffee made this a hit.  I will definitely be going back to try their lunch menu very soon.  These are the guys behind Supper so you know it has to be good!  Thank you to Scratch for opening up a place in Philly that is unique, delicious and what people want - delicious biscuits in a prime spot!

I love burgers. I have scoured west philly for burgers and it's a tough area. I mean shake shack? Cmon. Spencer eta is legit. Gourmet burgers with fresh ingredients. Prices are very reasonable. I tried the Dr. I's burger. Delicious! If you are looking for a high quality burger near Penn, this is the place to be.

Staff is very rude and unprofessional.they are always cursing on front of staff and playing. Also they tend to get orders wrong alot I had to go up to the counter  3 times until they got my order right.sometimes food is cold.

4 minutes late opening. Fun having 3 workers watch as I try and open a locked door. You can tell these employees hate their job. Maybe a few can step away from gossiping at counter and clean. Burger was decent. A lot smaller than remembered. I'm wondering how if they just opened there's mess and dirt on the floor already? Also on the napkin dispenser. That's disgusting and to get smacked in the face by an odor sitting down that smells like an airline toilet. Don't eat here. I've had all my shots and hoping I don't end up sick from anything.

The only reason I continue going to any McDonald's is for their Chicken Nuggets, Fish Fillet, and Oreo McFurry's. I go to this location because its the closest one to me. 

This place is pretty big. It has an attached gas station and a mini mart and plenty of seating space. 

Now the staff at this McDonald's is something to talk about. They are so ghetto. You hear them screaming at each other while they try to take and complete your order. You hear curse words left and right. Usually the one in charge is the most ignorant. There are some good people here and they are usually the ones getting reamed for nothing at all. I witnessed a "supervisor" ripping an employee a new one in front of all the customers because he left his lunch on the counter while he went to grab something real quick. I'm glad to hear she is no longer working there although there were a couple more of these incidents before she was fired. I think if they fire a couple more of these people, this place will actually be pretty great.

The worst chicken kabab ever, extra dry and tasteless chicken, big chunks of lettuce, big rings of white onions, decent tomatoes and water, oh no it was watering tahini. 
Seriously, the worst ever. 
I'm back to the Gyro Halal trucks, tastier, more economical and delicious.

This is your typical Wendys.  This location is pretty clean and the service is good.  There's ample parking since it's in a large plaza and they have an outdoor sitting option which is always nice.  A solid option if you are on the go or just want some fast food.

Definitely good for takeout/delivery.  Stopped in on a whim and got the lamb paratha roll ($6.99).  Surprisingly good, and when I asked for very spicy, it actually had some heat.  Felt like it took a little while to get my takeout, but that may be because I was alone/they don't have any TV's playing sports to distract me.  In any case, glad I had my phone to play with.

All in all, great for some tasty food.

DON'T EAT HERE! It will take you all of 2 seconds to realize the conditions of this establishment. When you walk in, you're hit in the face by an overpowering smell of grease coming from the kitchen area. At first I thought my contacts were blurry but then quickly realized the problem was not my contacts but actually the amount of smoke in the air. 

The kitchen suffers from a poor ventilation system which allows smoke to fill the table and line area. When you look behind the counter you notice a significant amount of dirt and grime on almost every surface. Whoever is managing this location is not instructing their employees to clean properly. 

The food is also not prepared in advance. If you order something you will have to wait from them to put it in the fryer every single time. I thought the concept of fast food was to receive it fast. Instead they tell you it's going to be a wait as you watch them actively place your order into the fryer. 

I work across the street so I went thinking, okay I only have a few minutes let me grab something fast and go. This was not fast and was coupled by a sense of anxiety knowing that my suit would smell like grease during the meeting I was about to have. I honestly learned my lesson, which is DONT GO.

I'd been eyeing Shoo Fry for a while and finally made it in tonight. The owners were kind enough not only to invite me for a tasting, but to come and personally meet my fellow foodie friends and I. Rachel and Matt (owners) are truly a class act with a real passion for food, and I'm thrilled that they've brought their French fry creations to the city of brotherly love. 

I was able to sample a number of their offerings-- fries topped with everything from buffalo chicken to apples and prosciutto to pb&j (yes,really!). Truly, everything was delicious. The chicken used in the buffalo and the general tsos fries was tender and not over cooked. The fries were all crispy and fresh, and I love that you can mix it up and choose tots or waffle fries. We got some Philly cheesesteak tots and definitely recommend them. 

The ambiance is a very cute, small shop, with odes to Canada throughout. It has a fun, hip vibe that fits in with the surrounding neighborhood perfectly. All of the staff were extremely friendly and helpful as well. 

They have a location in Rittenhouse as well that occasionally has some different offerings too, and they're constantly innovating and altering the menu. Definitely worth a stop in!

Loved ordering from the kiosk. It took me and a friend a while to decide and having the kiosk was great cuz we could always cancel or change anything we wanted. 

The wait wasn't too long. It was just two burgers, fries, and a milkshake. Even though I ordered a strawberry milkshake, it didn't taste like it which was disappointing. The burgers, however, were delicious.

I feel bad giving a DQ such a low rating considering my ice cream addiction, but its hard not to when you have such an awkward experience. 

Stopped in around 3pm on a rainy Friday after visiting the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall. We were the only people inside. There was a woman at the front counter who was chatting on her cell phone and didn't acknowledge us for a good amount of time as we sat there, and an older gentleman sitting on a small bar stool behind the counter just watching us with his arms crossed. 

The woman paused talking on her cell phone, pulled the phone away from her ear, asked what we wanted and then called to an employee in the back to come and help us. She then disappeared for our entire trip as she walked into the back and continued her phone conversation. A young kid came out from the kitchen area to help us, and interaction was short and brief. As soon as the kid came up to help us, the older man sitting on the bar stool staring at us hopped up immediately and was hovering over the kid, watching every single move he made. Literally every. single. move. The employee was obviously uncomfortable, but made it seem as if this happened a lot and was normal. 

The man watching him followed him like a sad puppy throughout our whole experience, from the time he grabbed two blizzard cups to the time he gave us our change. If that's not micromanaging I don't know what is. The most awkward thing about it was that he never acknowledged us, welcomed us, or said thank you. Being that he's (I'm assuming) either the store manager or business owner, you would expect some sort of gratitude to customers. But no. 

Additionally, the blizzard cups were filled about 3/4 of the way full and were skimpy on the mix-ins, which to me seems like a nickel and dime money saving tactic. Like, is it really worth it? Not impressed, by a long shot. Sorry DQ.
Took too long for a basic order. Employees talking loud with phones out. No order established. It was not busy a all. No sign of care from the manager on duty on Wednesday's @ 6pm

French Frye's were so old and bitter . You could tell they didn't change the oil in the fryer for months . 
Coke was watered down. Horrible customer service . I never had such stale and tasteless Big Mac. Stay away !!!
If they're taking a while to ring you up, it's because they're swiping your credit card info. Beware!

My boyfriend is a subway fan, that is mostly all he eats when he's on the go. Well, it is because he's working out and stuff so he's particular of his food. Anyway, this subway is okay, nothing stood out. We got what we needed.

One of the cleanest Taco Bell's I've been to. Staff does a good job at keeping interior clean and spotless. Restroom is well kept. Parking lot is a nice addition. Taco Bell isn't a place where you eat gourmet Mexican food but when you have a craving for Mexican food, this place delivers a lot of bang per buck. Staff always get my order right. I usually get the $5 box.

Definitely the worst McDonalds I have ever eaten at waited 30 minutes for my food the forgot the sauce and when I did get it it was wrong. I ordered 4 large cups of sweet tea and they ended up giving me 2 sweet teas and 2 things of coffee. Another time I went which was last month I saw a roach climbing on the seat never again

Everybody has a nasty attitude. Asked the cashier if they could make more cookies because there wasn't any in the container, and she simply said No. they're very slow with making orders, and just unprofessional...

I ordered a 4 for 4 with only bacon cheese and lettuce on it and when I got home I had everything on it. Mind you I told the lady twice. They gave me uncooked bacon and my French fried weren't cooked and cold. They juice machine was broken and all they did was talk talk and talk and no work. They need to get fired pronto. I ordered a crispy chicken sandwich but it had no cheese no sauce and no bacon. They didn't give me any napkins and their machines for fountain drinks was out of order.

It's an o-k poke shop in the area, nothing spectacular about it but nothing horrible. I've read one of the reviews below in regards to them giving a lot of toppings - mind you, I believe that reviewer did not mean the actual protein. I was disappointed when I ordered 3 scoops of protein. It turned out they were being extremely stingy with the fish in each scoop - roughly 3-4 pieces per scoop, and if they see an extra piece protruding the edge of the scoop, they make sure it doesn't make it into your bowl. My friend who ordered her bowl with eel they gave her three tiny strips of eel and called it a day. Nevertheless, the food tasted good and fresh. I'll be heading somewhere else for poke bowl since there are plenty of options within the 3 miles radius and they're more generous with the toppings - as in the proteins, not to load up your bowl with seaweed salad and mango, I can get a salad from Whole Foods market if I'm craving for that.

P.S. I watched the employee shredding a giant sheet of nori (dry seaweed) with his bare hands while preparing my bowl. Interesting...

Horrible service. Made a mistake in the app ordering and it wouldn't let me change it. Called the phone number and it was a robot answer. 2 options - call managers office for large parties or learn about hours. Called the managers office and no one picked up, they were "having fun with guests". Now I get a text that it is ready and I haven't even left my house. Very frustrated. Food probably isn't even going to be that good and the shakes taste fake. Calls themself shake shack but their shakes are horrible.

We love to go to Shake Shack whenever possible. In Philadelphia, we got our chance once again. The burgers were great as expected and the fries were hot, crispy and tasty. We were not disappointed and ordering at a kiosk was fast and easy. They're doing it right and their consistency is excellent. We will definitely return for more at whatever location we find them in our travels.
Legit Falafel for a fast food place in old city. A little pricey, but quality of food is there 100%.

At night is the worst. I'll get se next time when I go to this McDonalds I will go inside next time because when you go late night they Jack your food up thank God I open my sandwich before I pulled off. and I didn't have sauteed onions and bacon on my sandwich.

I usually wouldn't rate a fast food place, because, let's be real, it's fast food... not Le Bec Fin. But I saw that the only review was a 1, so I just had to leave one.  I've been here maybe about 10 times.  I only go through the drivethru. My order has never been wrong, I've never had to wait, and the food has never been bad, for fast food. The people who work there are usually pleasant, or as pleasant as you could be working that job. One of the ladies calls everyone "baby" when they pay. Not in a creepy way, in a grandmotherly way.  I like the "fresh" lemonade and not the minute mad lemonade.  I took off a star because they charge extra for the fresh kind.

This has got to be the worst Wendy's ever. I don't know what they were thinking when they built it, but its very small for a campus location. 

They usually only have one cashier and one sandwich maker. This makes the lines very long and the wait even longer. Even if there are only, say, 5 people in front of you, you can expect to wait at least 15 minutes until you get your food. 

Its just so painful watching the staff move so slow and watching the sandwich guy taking minutes for each burger.

Found a hair in my burger. 
Nuggets cold and hard. 
Fries cold. 
Soda flat and just seltzer water. 
Just a waste of money, don't waste your time or money.

So... I'm walking on 3rd street and catch that unmistakable smell of falafel- and I think that it must be coming from a food cart. I go to the pharmacy and as I cross the street, I literally lit up like a child when I saw the Mamoun's sign on Market Street? In Philly? Say it isn't so! My absolute favorite 2am (grab a bite enroute to the Holland Tunnel) spot in The Village opened a location in Philly?? As soon as I walked in I asked the lady at the register if it was in fact the same folks, she emphatically responded YES! And I happily ordered my usual falafel sandwich with their special hot sauce on the side. They just opened last week but apparently the word is out, because they were packed. It only took a few moments for my order to be filled. The falafel tasted exactly like always, and while the pita texture seemed slightly different, and the hot sauce was red not green- it still had that same ferocious bite forcing you to spread it on gingerly. I was in heaven.  I kinda don't wanna tell people that it was only $5. But how could I not share? Definitely plan on becoming a "regular".

Came in for a fast food meal after being very hungry all day. There wasn't a long wait, and the employee at the register took my order quickly. After my order was taken, it seemed to me that many other customers and I were waiting quite some time for our orders. Despite the fact that there were many workers behind the counter, I waited at least a good 12 minutes for my chicken tender and fry meal. I had also placed an order for cheese fries for a friend.

Once I got my order after waiting very long, I was not impressed with the quality at all. Even though they had "dropped" a new fry basket into the fryer as I waited, the fries still seemed soggy. The chicken tender breading didn't taste very fresh. The soggy fry quality seemed to be consistent in the cheese fries I had purchased for my friend as well. I am usually a fan of Wendy's and feel that their fast food quality is solid, but this experience was disappointing. 

I hope this location works on improving its customer service and food quality.

For some reason, finding good delivery greek food in the Graduate Hospital area has been an impossible task.

Seriously unimpressed with this place, .... we ordered through seamless tonight...and I don't think I had anything I actually liked... the Chicken Kabob Sandwich could have been better - if they didnt put pickles in it? The greek salad could have been better.... if they didnt put pickles in it (notice a theme?). The hummus was very watery and difficult to use as a dip because of it. We also got the 5 item  - combo. They give you a small piece of pita to go with the 2 dips we ordered in it, which was not enough. The falafal was very dry and bland.

The service and attention to quality was really unbelievable here - I really wasn't expecting much, except a great -tasting vanilla cone.  

While you wait in this location very close to all the historic places, you can look at a lot of old Dairy Queen pictures and history on the wall... they set it up that way, and it almost seems like a mini(very very) museum in itself.  I don't know if all DQ's are like this...

While waiting, I saw a lot of people of all ages coming in for various treats - seems like a lot of adults order the ice cream and the kids come in to eat burgers and fries and soda... lots of adults ordering mini-blizzards.

Anyway, the ice cream was super-dense, watery and not what I was expecting.  It was refreshing on a warm almost spring day, but I think I will not be returning soon because the taste also was so bland.  But a super clean location, super neat and great service with a smile.

Finally, a tasty falafel place in Philly! I grew up eating Mamouns in New Haven, and was so excited to see they were opening up a restaurant here. I've felt so deprived. I don't understand some if the the reviews here- maybe it's the competition trying to keep people away?

My advice- try the falafel sandwich! You will not be disappointed, and you can't beat the price!

Pro tip - they are even better with some added hummus or baba ghanouj. Hot sauce is actually really hot (this ain't Frank's Red Hot). Make sure you grab a few napkins, it can get messy.

This was the worst experience I've ever had at this establishment.  I arrived at 12:30 am and got no service.  The sign says they are open until 1:00 am. I pulled up to the second window and saw a dirty counter top and no one in sight. Never going to this location EVER again.
Horrible service, drive thru is never fast service. Around 10pm you can wait in line forever waiting to get served. They leave the window and just stop working.

The Moroccan chicken dish is a must! Aside from the numerous Baklava sweets the lady fingers are my favorites. Service is friendly and homy. A nice spot on South St for lunch, dinner and coffee and sweets.

This Blaze location is great! The service is always kind and listens to your questions even when there's a long line. They are fast and not stingy with the amount of toppings they use. Personally, I used to love MOD, but my experiences with this Blaze has greatly surpassed my love for MOD! Blaze also has fun specials in awhile that really draw a crowd in, like: $5 pizza days, BOGOs (join their rewards program!), free drinks, and of course - $3.14 pi day. If it's your first time, I'd recommend customizing your own pizza. Don't be intimidated, just get everything you want! My seasoned best-toppings-to-have-in-addition-to-your-cravings include: spicy red sauce, lots of ricotta cheese, broccoli, brussel sprouts, roasted garlic, pesto finish. But everything is good :)

We had a plain biscuit and a bacon egg and cheese biscuit and they were both delicious. The staff was friendly and the service was excellent. And I love the homemade potato chips and excellent sweet tea.

Food was ok. Did not remind me of Tony Lukes at all. The cheesesteak was so empty. There was more roll then meat plus I felt skimped out on the cheese. It really is just the name but not the fiod at all. Long wait times and food is overpriced for what it is. I would not mind paying 9 bucks at the real tony lukes but this place its not even worth 5

Blaze pizza has to be one of my favorite fast food chains in America. All of the ingredients that they use in their establishment are so fresh and tasteful that I load up my pizza with almost everything they have every single time I go there. You can choose to have a premade style pizza or you can build your own which I always do. What are my favorite drinks that they have there is their strawberry lemonade which is fire. If you're looking for a place to stop and eat and you see a blaze, that's definitely a place you have to go.
Good pizza but they always forget my arugula and pesto and it makes me sad. I enjoy the lemonades and sodas
It's the dirty floor and tables. Waitresses are not nice. One star is just for the vanilla frosty.

Just had a brisket biscuit and it was the best I have ever had. So happy we found this southern treat.  Read some reviews about dry biscuits from other reviewers, and nothing could have been further from the truth when we went.  Also had the hush puppy's, the dipping sauce alone is worth ordering. Don't miss this spot, you have to get the brisket.

I ordered a 4 for 4 with only bacon cheese and lettuce on it and when I got home I had everything on it. Mind you I told the lady twice. They gave me uncooked bacon and my French fried weren't cooked and cold. They juice machine was broken and all they did was talk talk and talk and no work. They need to get fired pronto

Came in with a few friends one evening around 8PM. Ibe been to Shake Shack before, so I knew what to expect with getting the true Shake Shack taste. I went to the order screen to place my order. I placed an order for a Double ShackBurger in a lettuce wrap instead of a bun and a side order of Fries. 

The store wasn't too crowded when I arrived, but my food still took about 15 minutes to be prepared, which I felt was a bit long for Shake Shack. 

Once my food was ready at the counter, it looked pretty good aside from the fact that my portion of fries did seem a bit skimpy. The cardboard holder of my fries definitely looked a bit empty. Regardless, I took my meal and sat down to eat. 

Overall, I did enjoy my meal. It was my first time getting the ShackBurger in a lettuce wrap, and I really enjoyed it. The fries were delicious and crispy. I would return to this location; I just think that they could use some improvement in speed of service and fry portions. I'm sure it isn't that way with every order; they may have been rushing to make mine. 

Shake Shack will always be a simple and fun spot for me. I would go here again.
Love the veggie burger. For a veggie in me, I was.able to get my burger custom made. Milkshakes are great too.

Vegetarians beware!  I ordered the falafel sandwich and it was falling apart (as they often do) because of the fresh pita and sauce so I ended up eating it with a fork.  I found two pieces of lamb in the sandwich.  Not sure how they make their food in the back but this was pretty alarming since I don't eat meat!

The food arrived quickly via DoorDash and smelled delicious! I got a Burrito Bowl with chicken, no rice, no beans, cheese, queso, fajita veggies, and lettuce. It was a huge portion, I could only eat half of it. And I kinda wish they mixed the bowl. But everything was delicious!

The food is good here but holy moley it's expensive. $14 for a plate with rice, hummus, falafel, and chicken? That's sort of nuts for a grab-n-go lunch spot that competes with places like Naf Naf, albeit on the other side of the city. 4 stars for flavor, 2 stars for price.
This location is a prime example of why the employees don't need to earn $15/hr. Absolute imbeciles!!!

It's very famous spot in old city Philadelphia. They have really good location. I ordered chicken kebob plate and enjoyed it so much. The place is very clean and they have fast service also. Only one bad thing is their small portions. If you are looking for some small healthful snacks, try this spot.

How do you mess up a salad?  How do you mess up a salad where all of the components are right there in plain sight?  I don't know and yet, I had a hard time managing to stomach the salad I ordered here.  I just felt that even though all of the ingredients looked good to the eye, the vegetables were somewhat tasteless.  Also possibly overchilled.

Maybe I was there at the end of a freshness cycle (if there is such a thing) but between the dingy feel of the room and the tasteless salad I think I'm disinclined to give them another shot.  Sorry.

I lived in the south for nearly a decade, so I may be a little picky. I tried scratch this week after passing it so many times.  I was underwhelmed.  The biscuit would have been good had it not been so dry (perhaps it wasn't fresh?).  My biscuit was flakey and tasted buttery, yet it was already broken in multiple pieces before I could even attempt to pick it up.   The Kentucky wildcat catfish sandwich was nothing special (a shame since I love the name).   The catfish patty was pretty oily and mushy, but the kale slaw and ranch on the sandwich were good--maybe it just wasn't the right sandwich to try? 

I wish they offered healthier non-pork options like bbq turkey/chicken, or perhaps offered salad, collard greens, or other lighter sides instead of chips...I left full, but heavy...oh so heavy.  Finally, this may seem trivial, but the fork and knife was probably the flimsiest plastic cutlery I've used. 

Scratch was okay, but sadly not worth the price or calorie splurge.

Came in to the Baklava Cafe for lunch on a rainy day. Honestly, I only wanted to come in for the pastries, but since we were hungry we decided to sit down and eat. 

I got the 3 combo platter with eggplant stew, hummus, and rice w/ veggies (also came w/ a side salad), and he had the shwarma. We both ordered fresh juices as well. For me, the 3 combo was just "okay." Part of the eggplant stew were warm, some parts were hot, some was a little cold. My best guess is they probably reheated it. Hummus and rice were good. The salad was pretty simple: iceberg, some pickles, tomatos, and cucumber, with yogurt dressing. Nothing special there. He liked the shwarma but was quick to note that "South Street Souvlaki is better." The juices were a bit watered down, which we found to be pretty disappointing. 

Their saving grace? Dessert. Get the baklava. And the bird's nest. And whatever else in their little pastry case that calls out to you. It will redeem any mediocre lunch.

This is the WORST Wendy's!! I've been living in this area for 5 years and EVERY SINGLE time I come here, no matter what time of day, they take forever!!! The staff are clueless and rude! I have no idea where they hired the staff but they need to fire them all and start from scratch! I d suggest going to another location bc this one SUCKS

It's a good place to have build-your-own pizza. The crust is thin and crispy but don't expect to have an authentic traditional Italian pizza because it's missing the chewiness of the dough. I think it's more like a thin crispy flat bread.

The website has a calculator for nutrition facts depending on what you have.

Once you eat from Blaze, you'll always go back! I swear, Blaze makes it hard to enjoy pizza from anywhere else!!! When I tell you I LOVE this restaurant, I absolutely mean it!! The workers are friendly! The service is quick! The restaurant is very clean and I always have a great experience when I visit. The manager Rachel seems to inspire her team to be nothing but excellent! Now as for the pizza, the toppings have such good variety from sauce, cheese, meats, veggies, you name it! And the sizing is perfect...one of their "build your own" pizzas is great, I think, to enjoy a few slices and save a few for later! (Get your own, WAYY TOO GOOD TO SHARE) Not to mention the crust is thin & perfectly crisp, not too doughy at all! If I could treat myself to a Blaze pizza everyday, without drowning in self guilt, I sooo would!! (Haha, but seriously) So delicious! And don't forget to try some garlic pesto on the crust!! Yummy

I'm really disappointed in this location. I remember the food at the NYC and New Brunswick locations being way more flavorful - and cheaper. The falafel are often mushy and the hummus (my ex-favorite) now seems so bland. Also, most of the sandwiches I've tried here are bursting at the seams with iceberg lettuce. Where's the beef? This ain't Subway. There are multiple better places in town. 

Seating is also scarce.
Don't get Boba tea here. It sucked. The bubble was very hard and I would not recommend.

I really like this falafel place and not just because it's right around the corner from my apartment. I've been here twice and both times the server (or cashier since it's more fast food than restaurant) was very friendly and helpful. The second time it was so loud I couldn't hear myself think about hearing myself think but the cashier understood and somehow heard us and got our order right. The hot sauce is really really hot and I love spicy food. The falafel here is superb! The food is really good overall and the prices are pretty fair for being in the middle of the city. I will be going back here again.
Falafel could be a little bigger but overall good. The side of grape leaves was fresh and delicious, served with pickles, pickled beets, and olives.

The service I constantly receive from your employee, Blaze, is always amazing!! He's the first when I walk to the counter and he always remembers everyone's name somehow and our order. He really takes it a step beyond anything you need but in a way that's incredibly welcoming and it makes me want to keep coming back! Please thank him for me for his great service!!!

Been coming here for months with my girlfriend.  So accommodating and the food is amazing here.  Jay, the GM, makes everyone feel welcomed.  I'm sad my girlfriend is leaving temple but will always make the journey back here no matter what.
Service is much better than McDonalds. Good Food Too! Should go there to get a quick bite to eat!

We were at an event nearby that had some food, but not really enough to fill us up for dinner. Looking on our phones for places nearby to eat, we noticed Mamoun's! Having eaten at Mamoun's in other places, we decided to check out this location, and it was a good call!

Food is prepared quickly, tastes good, and isn't too expensive. We enjoyed our dinner there, and the staff are friendly and helpful too. I had accidentally put too much hot sauce on my pita, so the guy behind the counter gave me a big cup for water instead of the small ones you usually get.

I'd come back for a quick meal!

I went to chipotle today and was completely ignored by the girls behind the counter. I felt like I was invisible and after about 5 minutes of standing there and listening to their conversation I considered just leaving. Someone who I assume to be a manager or supervisor came out and did take notice began taking my order. Food was great but customer service was very poor.
Cold fries. Missing ingredients on a dry bland burger. Needless to say I won't go back.

Went on opening day. Great location, interior is nice, electronic kiosks for self-ordering. Takes about 10 minutes to get your food. Had the cheese burger and pie-oh-my. Overall, like other Shake Shacks, good quality food!

The staff is great. The hummus, baba, and pita are tops. The outer color of the falafel is always so dark that either their fryer is set too high or the fryer grease is dirty.  The hot sauce is just hot.... Too hot with no depth. I'm assuming they use capsacian drops. Eeeesh. The place is clean. 
No mas.

This was in the university campus so have to try it some day or other. I thought Chipotle will be the only place where I can go and eat my favourite meal everyday, but this place just proved me wrong.
First, lets talk about the ambience and the restaurant. Medium size restaurant with an open kitchen to let people see how their pizza is being handled. The restaurant has made a very good use of space and can accommodate approx. 50 people on the couches and high rise tables in the premises. They always play some good music to make the ambience more light and happy.
Second, the pizza and dough knots that I tried were quiet exciting. I thought that it would be an average pizza, but trust me I have been there thrice in 2 days to have my meals. I ordered build your own pizza but they have some predefined options too. I ordered like 4-5 toppings pizza which has 2 types of meat and 3 veggies  ( who doesnt like toppings right). The flavour of the red sauce, the texture by the cheese and taste of meat and veggies were all on the point. I can not bargain for more in that price. I might have paid an extra 50% for this type of pizza or more. This is now my place to go anytime I am hungry .  100% recommended to all my foodie friends and also take your friends along.
This is a genuine review and if you feel like you dont like it then message me on my food blog and I will remove their pictures from my blog (but be sure what you dont like). Follow me on IG by foodcraaft(foodism).

Blaze is a great option for pizza campus! I love being able to customize my orders and the staff is always so helpful. My girl Freda hooked it up! Pleasant experience, very clean, and yummy!! 10/10 would recommend.

Large, tasty biscuits and even Southerner-approved grits! Took off one star because the price is a little high for relatively simple biscuit sandwiches, but what you get is delicious. I recommend the Kentucky Klassic and the bread pudding. Clean dining room and restroom. Be warned that there's not a lot of space to eat in. Not good for large parties.

This is the worst McDonald's I've been to in my entire life!!!! After my friends and I have been waiting 15 minutes for our food to come out we finally approach the register and question the staff on what is taking so long. About another 5 minutes go by until we finally receive our food. We are finally in our seats for about 2 minutes until a worker comes up to us and tells us we have to leave because they were closing. Almost like some sort of sick joke! Knowing they were going to kick us out ( it was 11pm) they did not put our food in to go bags so we had to get bags to wraps everything up. Pros: 
- very fresh meat, bursting with savory-salty goodness. 
- evenly melted cheese, and none stuck to my burger wrapper. 
- pickles were thick and crunchy. 
- I don't know if it was a potato roll, but it was a great pair. 

Cons: 
- great burger but not sure if it should cost $9.
- only once piece of lettuce
