However, I didn't take him up on it (I'm not about to take money from a small business, no matter what my experience was). I will be coming back here often if the experience I had today continues.

This is an awesome addition to the limited variety of cheap healthy food options in center city! The ingredients are fresh and prepared in front of you so you know there are no funky additives going into the finished product. I had the soba noodles, shrimp, bok choy, and broccoli with pepper sauce and it was delicious, not to mention a TON of food. For $9 - I thought it was a deal. Especially for overpriced center city. 

The restaurant is well decorated, clean, and offers adequate space to sit and enjoy your meal. I was also really impressed that they have handicap access to the bathrooms. I was lucky to have a quick word with one of the owners who is a recent college grad which i thought was really cool. I would highly recommend trying Wok Works if your in the area!

I'm really not sure why I always have a negative experience at wendys no matter which location I go to. This time there was a thick black hair stuck to a French fry. Mind you my whole family is either blonde or dirty blonde so it did not come from us. I have lost my appetite and my desire to go to wendys for a while.  We also brought it to their attention and they did nothing to compensate. A weak "I'm sorry" so that was a waste.  Wendys you really need to do better. I have better luck at burger king.
Great food and friendly service. Ordered the Tall Wok: Hong Kong Noodle, chicken, Bok Choy, Broccoli, Jalepeno, Crispy Garlic, Crispy Shallots with the Pepper Sauce. Would definetly go back.

Eating in a college atmosphere...need I say more?


Yes I will. There's nothing like the oppurtunites my to get a young vibrant college chick. 

I love it. 

Oh and the food is always fresh because the line is always deep. The male employees could do a better job of dressing however. I don't like seeing a man's underwear ever.

Wok Works is a great lunch spot. I eat here almost once a week. The entrees are customizable with bowls consisting of a variety of noodles or rice, choice of protein, veggies and sauce. It always tastes fresh and has consistently quick service, even during the lunch rush. A great spot for lunch.

Literally one of the worst Chipotle locations ever. Everything is always burnt, bland, and simply not great as the other locations. I try to give them the benefit of the doubt because they haven't been open very long at this location (maybe 2 to 3 yrs) but this is unacceptable.

Of course I'd go back - there is nothing else to really go to! However, the food, the price, the staff are all below good! The only reason it didn't get one star is I save those ratings for places I will not return to!
I've been here a few times as a substitute to my normal Honeygrow order.  There are plenty of different options but I find the stir fry terribly greasy each time.

We can all agree we're comparing this to Honeygrow, right?  Good.

So it's better than Honeygrow in the number of options you have.  More choices of noodles, sauces, veggies, meats, etc.  Maybe not more but more in your face.  I think the quality of the noodles, veggies, and sauces are equal or higher here.  Plus Honeygrow lets you add Sriracha or soy sauce yourself whereas Wokworks has a handful of other options, including hot chili paste.  So that's nice.

Where it lacks versus Honeygrow, for me, was the quality of the meat.  The pork was chunks versus the slices at Honeygrow and I think that led to some pieces being all fat.  Gristly.  That's never good and always bad.  Plus I agree that this place is $1-2 too expensive.  Maybe lower the prices for the base noodle/rice/kee-no-ah a touch?

I walk past this restaurant almost everyday and the line is usually out the door. I finally decided to give it a try after reading all of the positive reviews and I cannot believe I did not try this place any sooner! It is going to be my new go to lunch spot! Not only does the food taste amazing and is reasonably priced, the staff is incredibly welcoming and helpful! Stacy and Irene cheerfully greeted me and guided me through the menu and recommended the best stir fry ever based on my likings. The soba noodles with the oyster sauce was to die for!!! They even brought it out to me while I was sitting outside. If you're ever in the area, don't even second guess where to go for lunch or dinner. You won't regret it!!

Best Wok I've ever had! I've been coming to Wokworks for some time now and this review is long overdue! Food is always consistently fresh and delicious! I always go for the tall wok which allows you to chose a base, protein, 3 veggies, 2 toppings and your finishing sauce. If you're a veggie lover like me, this is the way to go. Unlike Honeygrow that up-charges for  things like beansprouts, all of your woks here include cabbage/onions, beansprouts, an egg, and carrots! I also appreciate that Wokworks changes up their menu to offer new seasonal veggies! Previously they've had butternut squash and eggplant and now they have kale- yum!! Don't be overwhelmed by all of the options, there are also signature bowls available that are already pre-arranged for you! I recommend the Bam Bam Steak. The staff if very helpful and guided  me through the process the first few times- I am a pro now. Aside from woks this place is also offers delicious sides! My favorites are the crispy edamame dumplings with peanut sauce and jalapeño brussels sprouts! I am always trying new combinations and never disappointed, highly recommend.

I was expecting great things from this place, but it was mediocre at best. The staff were very friendly. The food was so bland. I had the dumplings (pork). They were greasy and burnt. Cool concept though.

worst mcdonalds ever. 

Not only is the area around this McDonald's gross, the clientele even more icky, and the employees seriously unfriendly, they don't even take coupons. I mean, all I wanted was my free smoothie and they can't even honor my coupon. Boo. I typically don't find myself wanting McDonald's, but in the event that the craving overtakes me, I will leave my office (located above the concourse) and head to Broad and Arch.

Great mac n cheese ideas!  My coworker and I went during lunch and instead of getting felafel nearby, we could not resist this truck.  We both loved the truck design - super cute!  The owner even took a picture with us in front of the truck.  But most of all, we liked the actual mac n cheese.  I opted for the margarita mac for a lighter mac n cheese with tomatoes, mozzarella and basil. I can't believe I haven't thought of doing this myself!  The combination was divine.  My coworker did the BBQ mac, which she also really liked.  We both got the large - and could have gone with the regular, but it was worth it!  Definitely going back for more when I need some quality comfort food!

Overpriced and took way too long but that would be fine if it actually tasted good. Sauce added no flavor and frankly didn't even taste like advertised, noodles were way over cooked and they make you pay for everything. Dumpling sauce was only redeeming quality, but the dumplings themselves were too crispy and over fried.

I probably shouldn't review this place because all I had was the Cookies n Cream truffle. But on the other hand, that alone deserves a review. Basically, it was a party in my mouth. My friend had one too and agreed about the party-in-the-mouth feeling. I'm interested in trying the mac, too, but I'd go just for the dessert if the truck happened to be in my path (which, unfortunately, it almost never is.)

The worst McDonald's in the city!! 

Service here sucks. Want to stop in for breakfast before heading to work? Chances are you'll be late for work due to waiting in a long line for an overcooked biscuit. There's also no guarantee your food will be good quality. Just don't do it unless you're really desperate.
Disgusting extremely dirty staff are very ignorant and when u walk in looks like the place is full of drug addicts and homeless people ... Walked in and walked out ... Do not go here !

Excellent service today. Rodney took our order at the drive-thru. Everything in our order was exactly what we wanted. He greeted up with a smile when we pulled up to the window. He was very generous with the sauces too for my boyfriend's tacos.

Worth the stop.. If you're hungry get the large sandwich. Close to the airport so easy to stop on the way in or out of Philly! 

Good stuff!

After a not so good experience I have to say I appreciate the owner reaching out to make up for it. I received one hell of an apology. I love the edamame dumplings with the spicy mayo. The best dumpling I've had yet and there's not even meat in it. The teriyaki chicken bowl with brown rice is good and I'm liking the hibiscus tea lemonade. It was very sweet of the owner, staff and delivery guy to do this. Thank you.

Stopped by this new place on my way home from work and couldn't believe how amazing the food was! I must have picked a good time to go because my food was ready in 10 minutes. The food is very reasonably priced for how great the quality is. I really enjoyed the ambiance inside of the place...all of the workers were super friendly and upbeat. I tried their Citrus Tea Slush and it was soooo tasty! It even had a slice of mango in there. I will definitely be a regular here from now on.

This is a subway. If you've managed to live your life without eating at one, congratulations! Subway has figured out how to run a cheap sandwich shop. And that's what this place is. It's sandwiches. Bread. Cheese. Meat. Vegetables. Yeah that's really about it. Sure, there are sauces, and lots of different varieties, and special combinations. But at the end of the day, it's really just average sandwiches. Nothing here will blow your mind. 

Now this particular subway is also just average. Nothing special. Customer service is fine. Sometimes they can be a little slow, sometimes they're not. Been in here a few times. They're Philadelphia-friendly, as friendly as one would expect. not southern friendly, small town friendly, or west coast  friendly. Only as friendly as they have to be.

While I sincerely hope that a better sandwich shop opens up in the area, this will be perfectly adequate until then.

Terrible experience in the drive thru. 

Ordered two kids meals and what was supposed to be the new grilled chicken with guac sandwich-- got the bags- drove home- was really excited to try the new sandwich but opened the package to find a crispy chicken sandwich with BBQ and bacon- deff not what I ordered. But I couldn't drive back. So forced myself to enjoy this weird sandwich I didn't even want. 

The sandwich wasn't good either- next time I go to McDonald's I'm getting a burger- chicken sandwiches taste strange there- ended up eating a few bites then giving it to my dog. The kids however enjoyed the chicken nugget kids meals and the toys and apple slices that came with it! 

Prob gonna give this place a break for a while or at least go inside- maybe they won't mess the order up then.

Terrible! I am not a huge fan of kfc and I never eat at taco Bell. But one day I was really in the mood for their popcorn chicken. Big mistake! It was over cooked and almost broke a tooth. The cashier was extremely rude and the area where you would grab your drink was disgusting! 

I have never been in a fast food restaurant that was kept in such a manner. Please if you are going to eat here be mindful of how fresh the food is before leaving the restaurant. Gross!

I love chipotle but, Every time I come here they never have vegetables ready. Today I came in at 4 and my burrito was made really so badly, I opened it and it fell apart / they made it so much smaller than usual. Felt like I was just eating bread
What's not to love, great burgers, wonderful fries and toppings for both!  I say Eat at Joe's often!
This place really needs to up their chicken game.  I've gotten a few wraps here that have really gristly pieces of chicken in them....so bad that I actually felt like reviewing Au Bon Pain.

This location is probably one of the worst subways I've ever been in.  

The guy behind the counter barely looked at me while I ordered, asked me to repeat things several times, and just seemed to not care at all that he was at work.  They were out of sprite zero, doritos, and teriyaki chicken.  

I could have handled all of those issues if the sandwich was at least on par with other subways, but it wasn't.  The bread was stale and crunchy, despite seeming fresh and pulled from the oven, and the onions were slimy and on the verge of not being safe to eat.  

There's another subway 2 blocks away on Chestnut.  Go there instead.

As a frequent lunch spot this place gets packed during regular lunch hour. The staff does a wonderful job at trying to get people in and out. A cool feature that they have is staff members taking orders via iPads so the line moves quickly as they. All you have to do is go to the register pay and grab your food. There is a woman that comes around if you are dining in upstairs come around passing out mints and wet wipes. It's a lovely gesture and this location isn't the worse.
Really good food! Fresh stuff from the protein to the veggies. Definitely a go to place for me. Black gold sauce is my recommendation and stick to brown rice.

I had the privilege of trying Mac Mart at the Phoenixville Food Festival's Food Truck event this past Saturday.  I had the "Heart Attack Mac" which is a standard Mac n' Cheese with caramelized onions, crunched bacon crumbles, and a parmesean panko topping (in which I swear I saw little bits of potato chip--maybe it was an accident but it was a delicious accident). So the mac was ooey-gooey and rich and super filling. It was served in a carcboard french fry boat and I'd say weighed well over a pound for about $8. Neither my wallet nor my arteries could afford for me to eat this often but it was so delicious and definitely a comfort food. Can't wait to try their Jalepeno Mac next time.

I'll add an additional star since the district manager promptly emailed me after my initial review and offered me a gift card to return which I promptly received. This morning, I returned to this same Au Bon Pain that was originally reviewed. Eh...it was okay. I mean they did seem to have more pastries stocked, but...as far as the neatness of the dining room area and friendliness of the cashiers, they have a long way to go to get MY actual money again. Especially, since there are a PLETHORA of yummy and friendly food establishments in the general vicinity. Quite frankly, with the Coventry Deli right across the street, I'm surprised that this Au Bon Pain makes any money at all. But, I digress, I have to be 100% honest, yes, I would return, but only while the gift card that I received still has value. I can't see voluntarily spending my money here. I feel bad saying that since the district manager reached out to me so promptly and professionally, but...I'm sorry, there are just TOO MANY good food establishments in the area to waste time with ones that apparently lack the training or...maybe even the desire to treat the customers friendly and keep the restaurant neat and well stocked.
Lousy food, and even worse owners. They support extreme right wing conservatives. Avoid at all costs.
Everyone that works here is amazing.  Matt delivers exceptional customer service. Great food and awesome employees.
Perfect place to pick up a sausage burrito before hopping on your SEPTA or Amtrak train.  All aboard!

So sad. I was gunning for the concept: fresh, locally sourced meats and produce, a creative menu, a 22 year old owner (no need to speculate on just HOW he arrived at entrepreneurial-ship....he is there working!). Many different starch options for the base of your stir fry are offered including rice noodles and quinoa. I opted for the quinoa, with shrimp add broccoli, in the tropicali sauce, and crispy garlic to finish. Your dish arrives in a chinese take out box.
Firstly, I hate eating out of those boxes. The food never really cools down enough to eat, and i had to dig through mounds of quinoa to get to my 4 shrimp and 4 pieces of broccoli. 
Secondly, after paying for our meal, the man behind the counter handed me the receipt and said a bowl of miso was free next visit. Great! Except when we left, the sign outside the door said, "free bowl of miso with your wok!" so really, he should have offered me the free bowl with the meal I just bought. Unfortunate.
The real problem here though is the Taste of the food. All I can surmise is that they don't properly clean the woks. There was a pervasive burnt taste that overpowered the added sauce. It was...gross. I was so hungry I still ate half of it, and smiled sweetly at the fresh-faced owner because I couldn't bear to hurt his feelings and tell him the food sucked. I will say, my husband got a similar dish (with noodles Instead of quinoa), and he couldn't taste what I tasted. I had a bite of his and that same burnt essence was there too. Perhaps I'm more sensitive to it. But truly, if you're looking for this style of cuisine, go to Honeygrow. Unless they work out their kinks here. I give 2 stars not 1 simply for the premise that I appreciate. Hopefully they can do better.

You know what? Fuck this place! Everytime we go in there, something goes wrong. The first time we went in there, we got our little parfaits, and before we leave, a fight breaks out right in front of the store and we're trapped in there for half and hour, cops never came. The second time my fright got hit on by a gay guy. Usually not a problem, until he grabbed his ass -firmly-. Then another time, we got talked about loudly by a bunch of "Rachets" in the corner. The downstairs ain't never open, and the place is generally too damn crowded. No dollar menu, and the damn frosty machine don't work half the time. Finally, zombies, homeless people who aim endlessly make this (Or try to) store their home, every night.
 
Just fuck this Wendy's, yo. Fuck it.

This place is a solid lunch spot. I went for my first visit today and was really pleased with the Yelp check-in offer (30% off!) and got a large tofu bowl with veggies. All the vegetables were super fresh and you could even see one of the employees chopping up peppers on the counter. It was a late lunch, but the place was not crowded and my friend and I easily got a seat.

The hardest choice for me was the kind of noodle and the sauce. I got the wok noodles, but the soba looked great. I also wish that I would have done the pepper sauce because the Begal sauce, while delicious on its own, was a bit lacking in flavor when everything else was mixed in. All the sides looked great too, so I'll definitely be back soon!

I love Chick-fil-A esp their Asian salad and the spicy chicken sandwich. I just hate the line here! The line moves fairly quickly, but the wait for your actual order is dreadful. And to make it worse, when they call out your name, you can barely hear them bc the mall is so ridiculously loud! They need a better system...just not sure what they can do to make things faster.

But, a plus is that service here has always been very very nice.

Made a purchase so I could get the key for the bathroom this evening. Male cashier was very rude and said no one knew where the bathroom key was.  Yes, no one has a key to a busy restaurant in center city Philly. I will never go this McDonald's again. Based upon the other postings on this site  the corporate headquarters  for McDonald's should investigate.

When I'm in the mood for fast food, this Wendy's is definitely on my short list. Since the renovations, it seems much more clean. It's definitely got a better vibe than the wendys on 11th & walnut. My food is always fast and the staff is friendly.

There is really only one group of people that should eat at this Au Bon Pain:  People who work in the office complex in which it is located and who are entirely too lazy to a) bring their own breakfast/lunch or b) walk to another breakfast/lunch spot in the area.

As a visitor to the building last week, I fell into the "too lazy to pack my breakfast" group.  I ordered egg whites and cheddar cheese on a skinny wheat bagel.  At $4.50, I figured it would be good.  It was not.  Greasy cheesy, rubbery eggs, and a mushy bagel.  Yuck!

Other times I've eaten at ABP, I've gotten their soups and they are pretty decent tasting, as well as a decent value for the price.  I will not be getting breakfast here again.

After much hearing about this place I HAD to try it. I've been in philly for 1yr and I've never heard of this place until 3wks ago. Everybody looked at me like i had two heads when I said I never heard of a chick fila.

Most times when i journey into the city, I'm usually already heading to a dinner spot to stopping by this place is not an option. Well I had to work in the city today by univ city and I decided to take the train in the opposite direction from home just so I can try this place. I was starving cause I hadn't eaten all day and it was afterwork.

Anyway, I took my train over to the liberty place. I ordered the chicken club sandwich, small fries, and small chocolate milkshake. 

I really liked the thickness of the milkshake but it could have been more chocolately...perhaps more chocolate syrup?

Fries were tasty...not out of this world but they were good. not too salty either.

Now for the main meal, the grilled chicken was also not salty which I appreciated as I'm tired of eating salty grilled chicken.

Overall I was very stuffed...the caloric intake was about 1300 which was okay considering that it was my first meal of the day and the time was 530pm...so it was okay with me.

I'll go back BUT i don't eat fast food frequently so I won't be heading here no time this yr, plus it's not on my way home or around where I live so another reason this place won't be seeing me for a very long while. however, I will keep the name in my head for whenever I'm on the road and I run into another franchise.

Those who think they could never be vegetarian, try this place out... No meat inside that truck, but you will think you died and went to heaven!  The bella donna is awesome as is the falafel salad. Ask for hot sauce on the bella donna - Makes it even better.
A+++ I want to learn how they make tofu have the consistency and flavor of ground beef... I know cinnamon is involved.

I love this place!! In my opinion, better than Honey Grow. The portions are huge, even the small! They have so many choices - and the fried chicken is organic! Stacy at the register was super helpful and let me know if some recommendations! The service is quick and friendly. The atmosphere itself is beautiful, with a modern Asian touch. They have outdoor seating when it is nice out! Definitely love coming here :) especially when they come to my work, Philadelphia magazine to bring some yummy lunch! 5/5!!! Everyone should try it.

Having moved back East from 4+ years in Hawaii, I am constantly trying to quench my Asian food cravings.  Wokworks is a great lunchtime alternative.  I've tried the Hong Kong and Chow Fun noodles, and need to try the rest.  The Tropicalia sauce is just sweet and spicy enough, and the Szechuan Pepper sauce is even hotter-- plenty for you to "feel your food."  The portions are great for a hangry day, and I'm looking forward to their free draft beer happy hour on Wednesdays, with some pretty sweet pupu specials.
Typical poor Philadelphia service, we like the food but we frequently get our orders cancelled with out notice and hang-ups when we call!

I'm definitely not a vegetarian, but this is on the top of my lunch spot list. There is a line for a reason. My favorite thing to get is baba ganoush and it is out of this world. I usually order it on top of the house salad, and it comes with pita bread. I've also tried the baked tofu and greek salad, which have both been amazing. The hummus is also fantastic. You really can't go wrong here, I've never been anywhere close to disappointed. You can also pay with a credit card, which is a nice perk. 

If you haven't gone here and you work around University city/ are a student, then you really are missing out.

3.5 stars - The Mac n cheese assortments are very good and tasty.  
It's great but it's priced too high for the portion. $6.50 for a small??? $8.50 for a medium??  The price/portion size are the sole reason for 3.5... (let's give it a 3.9 instead)

You don't have to go to the other truck that sells Mac n Cheese as you'll be saddened by their cheese sauce.
I am truly in love with this place the food is awesome aswell as the staff. I only have a 30 min break and this is the perfect place

Soo good. Look forward to it at every strEAT fair. Many options to choose from and always super nice. 

Going to be a great addition to Wells Fargo Center, during all Sixers and Flyers game!

As a soup connoisseur it's hard for me not to like this place. Usually they have four to six choices available each day. From a traditional chicken noodle to lobster bisque. It's always tasty, creamy and fresh. They also offer sandwiches, salads, coffee, bagels etc.  Prices are a bit high in my opinion but again you almost pay same or close to same at traditional Wawa and quality and taste is a lot better at Au Bon Pain. I was introduced to it in 2009 and am happy to be back.

Solid three... Would be three and a half if allowed.  This place has a short menu but brings the flavor.  The dining room is connected to the kitchen and even on a cool day is muggy and humid inside.  There a few tables a long bar table and an accessible bathroom.   At lunch time they get orders out in about ten minutes.

Don't get me wrong I enjoy Fast Food every once in awhile and I think wendy's chicken nuggets are the best of the big fast food chain but I would avoid this particular Wendy's at all costs. Everyone in this establishment looks miserable, from the workers to the people just waiting for their food. This must be where happiness comes to die.
The scene in here is always interesting to say the least. On any given night you will have people passed out at the tables, yelling, altercations, or any other nonsense you could possibly dream up. 

The lines move slow, and the food isn't too "fast" but its your standard Wendys food. You will have to put up with a good amount of nonsense though to get it.
Great place to eat. Love the spicy options, but a little too greasy at times. Other than that, delicious!
It's a great place to try Asian-American mixed style Chow Fun. I am a huge fan of all kinds of noodles. Absolutely love it!

Often disappointed. Their coupons are mostly nonsense. You get a free sandwich when you buy a sandwich, but not if you buy a combo. 

Their burgers are 'made with 100% real beef'. See the 'with' in there? that means that even though the beef is 100 percent beef, its not the only ingredient in the burger. 

Sure sounds like its only beef though. Weird. What else is in it? Why tell us that their beef is 100% beef? What else could their beef be? 

Their fries are not vegetarian and have wheat and dairy. So much for being potatoes, fried in oil.

Call me surprised when I walked into the place and saw the wok flipping and the dishes flying from kitchen to table. The staff was amazingly friendly and helpful, since this was my first time. The atmosphere is clean and cozy and the food is great. I plan to stop by regularly when my wife and I move into the area!

I go to this location because it is the closest to me that has street parking readily available.  The last couple of times I visited this location, they didn't have green peppers.  I went later in the day, almost close to closing time so it makes me wonder if they actually didn't have the ingredients or they didn't want to take more out. Either way, it's a typical Subway.

The people giving one star are not lying at all. This is by far the worst Wendy's in philly. The "employees" are rude as hell and just look as tho they don't wanna be there. Like your bothering them..well if you don't like your job then leave simple as that. They have this black lady with blond boy cut hair she is probably the worst person I have ever come across in my life. Then they have the nerve to update this location like it's gonna make the trash inside any better.. no get rid of the employees inside and it'll be better all around...worst location ever managers need to step it up, the employees should not be running it.

STAY AWAY!
Service is horrible the young lady waited on 2 prior guest and gave them attitude and told someone else to explain to the customer rude to me as well I ordered 10 pieces of chicken 2 large sides and 3 small sides. While awaiting for food to get prepared a stranger walked in off street guess another co worker street clothes jacket and all grab boxes and started to prepare food for her and her girl friend did not wash hands or anything the other workers had gloves on ask a guy was he the manager he said no but what could he help with and I explained he went to speak to the woman and she said she does not care call anyone you like Woah!!

I'm so glad I finally stopped in, I've been trying to go and take advantage of their Wednesday specials with Aria S. but never got around to it. 

I ordered a short wok with chow fun noodles, shrimp, bok choy, crispy garlic, and pepper szechuan sauce. The bowl itself was very fresh and full of wonderful ingredients BUT the sauce is extremelyyyyyyy spicy. Dont get me wrong, I handled myself pretty well in Thailand, but this was a little too intense. I definitely would switch the sauce for next time. I also order the brussels sprouts and the spicy asian pickles. Brussels sprouts were wonderful, similar to Sampan's. The pickles were incredible, definitely on the spicy side, but not overwhelmingly so. 

My concern after ordering was the amount of time I waited. I have no problem waiting, but its labeled as fast food and I'd say we waited about 20 minutes. It seemed like they could have used one more person to help cook.

TIP: check in on yelp and get 30% off!!
Food is good, the sweet & spicy sauce is spicy! Lots of veggies and meat in the bowls, recommended!

It would be easy to walk down the street and miss this little gem.  it's small, just a couple of tables, and unassuming... but the food is FRESH, and DELICIOUS. I am gluten free and they have the best rice noodles in the city.  The sauces are very flavorful.  One of my absolute favorites quick serve places- ever.  Wish they had one in my neighborhood.  Go!

Made the Sunday trip from Jersey just for the Cafe', was not disappointed. Had a bowl, some soup and Black tea. Had to take a to go bag the portion was so large. I will take the train again for another meal. I'm looking forward to it even though I'm a confirmed meat and fried food addicted guy.

The food is very good for a fast food joint that's why I give it two stars. It loses three stars because the staff is clueless, inattentive, forgetful and rude. If you're planning on ordering food here between connecting flights be prepared to wait a while because the staff is SLOW. I've experienced many occasions when the order taker will disappear from the register while a long line of customers are waiting to order. Customers are clearly annoyed and frustrated all the while the manager is walking around apparently clueless and completely oblivious to a long line of paying customers with no cashier at the counter to take orders. I believe they just don't care. When you finally get your food after waiting what seems like an eternity, they always seem to forget something that is imperative to have with your order like dressing for your salad or eating utensils. This Wendy's has lost me as a customer. They really need to get their act together. I'm sure Dave Thomas is rolling in his grave.

What can I say that hasn't already been said? Customer Service, cleanliness, etc.  all very poor.
I went in to get the half salad and chicken wrap.  Salad was not bad - but I found a piece of plastic wrap in my sandwich.  Yuck.
There are plenty of other choices in this area - I strongly suggest that you go somewhere else.  I know I will.

The Mac Mart has a lot of buzz, and deservedly so. This giant pink truck hits a spot that the other food trucks can't reach for savory, comforting, cheesy lunchtime goodness. The mac and cheese is a wee bit overpriced, but is still in the ballpark compared to other "gourmet" food trucks.

The special bowls are definitely mac heavy/topping light, but I was still pleased with my meal. The Mac Mart won't become a staple for me, but I would stop there again if the craving hit.

Also, the service is incredibly friendly. They really want you to be happy with your lunch! Which is a great pick-me-up in the middle of a long work day.
Their burgers are the best. Get the Elvis burger. Peanut butter, bacon, and fried banana. So good.

This is the best McDonald's in the North America if not the world.

The other people who have reviewed this Mickey D's and said otherwise, well...I hate to tell you, but they have had their brains ruined by heroin and LSD.  Either that, or they are  involved in the evil Yelp extortion business model.  "Nice restaurant you got there:  it'd be a shame if it were to be beleaguered by a spate of awful reviews that have a mysteriously prominent place on your business listing.  I'm sorry, were we talking about the advertising you were about to buy on this site?"

Anyway, let me bring The Serious for a second.

This really is an exceptional McDonald's.  When I last went in there and asked for an iced coffee, the teenager who took my order acted as if I had just fallen into cardiac arrest and he was racing against time to save my life.  He wasn't going to mess up my order and he damn sure wasn't going to waste my time.  Seriously, Mr. McDonald's Manager:  whatever you're paying that kid, double it.  Chop-chop, motherfucker.

Did I mention that the place was also clean, calm, and orderly?

Had such a bad experience here at temple university chipotle...such bad customer service and they give too little food in my chipotle bowl. Big disappointment and will never go back to that place ever again.

I've been to Wokworks multiple times so this review is overdue. I'm a fan - it's quick, much better value for money than Honeygrow, and service is excellent. Also checked in on Yelp the last time I was there for the 30% discount so it made for a very inexpensive lunch. I'll definitely be back!

A good idea with lots of kinks to work out.

It's great that they offer brown rice, quinoa and soba noodles for a healthier starch base. The sauces seem to be amazing, too. Both the teriyaki and peanut sauces were awesome.

It's off-putting that they charge $1 extra to add a handful of green beans (6-8 green beans), bok choy, peppers, etc. and 50 cents for cilantro. 

But it's worse that they seem not to have washed one of these veggie items. I'm guessing the bok choy. My soba noodles with peanut sauce were unpleasantly interrupted throughout the meal with crunchy bits of grit that I have to assume is dirt. If not dirt, then there is something unpleasantly gritty in the peanut sauce. Either way, ew. Major kink to work out.

Their second issue was that they covered my steaming hot carton of noodles and vegetables with ice cold, stark white tofu. It was just in there, not incorporated into the sauce or anything. I was like, is that cheese? It's very soft, so I can see why they don't toss it with the rest of the ingredients. But yuck. I was hoping to get nice, firm tofu pieces seared and coated in the sauce. I will never order the tofu again. $1 add-on veggies all the way. If I can find the ones that they wash.

The soba noodles were also a little overdone if we're getting real picky. They gelled together. I wouldn't have cared if not for the cold tofu and sand. My husband's brown rice seemed better prepared.

I will try this place again, but warily and in the hopes that they read their Yelp pages.

Oh Mac Mart, how I love thee. Easy to pick out of a crowd, Mac Mart is the blatantly pink food truck that you can't miss! I've gotten their mac n chz deliciousness before and of course had to stop by at the StrEAT Food Fest. There is always a line, no matter what. We got there right when the fest started and still had to wait about 15min. Well worth it. I've gotten a few varieties before, I remember a jalapeno one that was really good. This time around, I did the buffalo chicken. I've had some other buffalo chicken mac n cheeses before, but this one really took the cake. Big thick pieces of chicken and those tortilla crumble thingies on top added it some extra crunch oomph! If you're a mac n chz fan, def worth throwing some moola at Mac Mart!

Here's what you get from Wok Works: simple, inexpensive, hot, Asian-inspired stir fries. I'll keep this review short, just like my trip to Wok Works. On to the pros/cons:

PROS:
* Inexpensive
* Fast
* Lots of options
* Tasty food

CONS:
* $1-2 too expensive?
* Non-authentic?
* Too spicy?
* They label Sriracha "hipster ketchup"


Are you can deduce, there just aren't many cons to this place. It's a no frills, quick-stop in Rittenhouse. I'm a fan. You should be too.

I've been to Wokworks twice now and hope it sticks around!  I described this place to my coworkers as a "Hipster Noodes & Company" where you build your own bowl and get a number of veggies, toppings, protein, and sauce on your choice of noodle/rice/quinoa.  They also have some signature bowls and sides.

I went with large wok broccoli, sweet peppers, and mushrooms, fried chicken as the protein, crispy garlic and pineapple as the toppings, wok noodles, and smoke asian BBQ sauce.  I ordered ahead and wish i had said protein on the side because the breading was soggy by the time I got it back to the office - I also wish I had ordered double protein because they're stingy with the proteins.  The portion for the price is decent for the area.

It's a small place and I suggest ordering for pick up on their website if you plan to go around lunchtime.
Just had vegan burrito with seitan as my protein. It was delicious. Tasty sauce, generous portion and nice garnishes. Fast friendly and helpful service. Very fresh and flavorful.

The time is 9:00 pm. A young Indian male named Jeff walks up to the door and pulls only to find it locked. Inside, he notices two McDonald's employees (one of them the manager) flirting with two very unattractive women whose only redeeming qualities are that one could use her backside as a shelf. The two women are let out by the manager. Jeff is visibly disturbed at how they (the women) keep looking at the man in what one can only assume are meant to be looks of seduction while they eat their ice cream sloppily. Jeff looks at the hours of operation sign which states that they are open until 10:00 pm.

[Jeff]: Are you closed? :\
[Manager]: Yeah.
[Jeff]: The sign says 10.
[Manager]: We're closing because no one wants McDonald's right now.
[Jeff]: I'm. right. here. (actually raises hand)
[Manager]: ... (locks door and walks off)
[Jeff]: ... (stands there in stunned silence)
[Unattractive woman]: (giggles)

Jeff finds this kind of funny (after).

I went to the Lower Bucks County Food Truck Festival at the YMCA in Doylestown, this was one of the trucks among the ten or so. 

Mac and cheese is the ultimate comfort food. When made well is creamy, cheesey goodness, jacked up its AMAZING when done right. Mac Mart Truck gets it right!! Let me say that I do not like pesto in general but I chose the (don't remember the exact name) Mac & cheese topped with jalapeño pesto and pecorino cheese.

Talk about LOVING it!!! I think from now on whenever I eat pesto it needs to come from this truck or they need to teach me how to make it their way. It had a touch of spice, it wasn't so overpowering that you was too spicy to eat. Can't say that I loved it enough. Check out this truck if you see it downtown, you won't be disappointed.

In the middle One of the busiest part of Philadelphia, this place was a pleasant surprise. The service is always incredibly quick and you can always find a table inside liberty place. The staff is friendly and work hard, and are quick to fix mistakes.
First time here! Stacey was amazing in helping me choose the best ingredients! Fast hot fresh food! Will definitely come back in the future!

I wanted to like the place but it's mediocre at best. I ordered a brown rice chicken stir fry with snow peas, cilantro, and Thai basil with the "creamy" peanut sauce. Individually the quality of the ingredients were fine, except the peanut sauce was hardly creamy nor I could I really taste the peanuts. It also could have benefitted from crushed peanuts, but I guess it's not that kind of place.

Also the list of ingredients to personalize the stir fry was pretty limited. My food was lukewarm and not favorable despite having sauce. I will say that it was a healthy portion of food, but not quite worth the $10 spent.

Service was fine, the place was clean and has a pretty chill vibe. 

I wouldn't come here on purpose, perhaps if I'm super hungry and am tired of all the options around.

Before I graduate, I must write a review about my all-time favorite food truck on campus, Magic Carpet. I've been going to MC for about 4 years now and it rarely disappoints. While some may be discouraged by the long lines, I can assure you that it goes by much quicker than you may expect. Over the years, my go-to dish has remained the Falafel Sandwich. I often get it with sesame seeds and extra hot sauce, which makes that experience even better. Their cookies are legendary and for only $1, they are basically a steal. The specials they have on a rotating basis are also a pleasant addition. My favorites from those tend to be the burritos and the lasagnas. To be honest though, you can't really go wrong. The tofu and magic meatballs are also revered among MC patrons so I highly recommend those as well. As a vegetarian, I am ecstatic by the fact that I can eat everything on the menu. If you haven't been to Magic Carpet, I strongly suggest you do. 

Tip: While they do take credit cards (for a small fee), I suggest you get one of their gift cards so you can bypass the fee *and* not worry about having cash with you.

I was very disappointed with my meal. I got the noodles, chicken, Brussel sprouts, broccoli, and the green curry sauce. The result was a $10 container of mush. I may try this again with a different sauce or less sauce -- but I will certainly check out similar places in the area first.
Not that great - stay away from the Big Macs!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Why is this place even allowed to serve people? Holy crap.  All I wanted was a large drink.  The Coke machine didn't work, so I go to the register and the lady said Coke works....great but I dont want Coke. I asked for a refund and then she told the manager - who turned around and said "well the Coke still works".....dumb ass people. Getting it through to them that I didn't want a Coke but wanted a Sprite was too complicated of a task.  And good lord don't ask for a refund, you might not make it out of there alive. The shittiest, nastiest, most disgusting McDonald's, ever.  They don't even deserve a 1 star but you have to in order to proceed with this damn review

This is a 4.5 star review.

Delicious Mac & Cheese.  The staff was super nice. 

1st visit to Mac Mart at Love Park.

I couldn't decide between which m&c to get so I got both the BBQ & the Jalapeno.

The BBQ was very good.  The sauce was a touch sweet which is what I liked.  Other than the m&c needed to be a bit creamier and more BBQ sauce & bacon crumble, it was very good!

The jalapeno m&c had a good creaminess and the right balance of jalapeno - nice heat from start to finish but not overwhelming heat.  Delicious.

Look forward to going back for more.  Good stuff, nice staff!

I love me some Chipotle, but not from here.

First of all, the joint is TINY. I mean, really tiny. There is hardly any seating, and what seating they do have is very cramped and uncomfortable.

That being said, my real problem with this place was that there was a giant black hair in my food. Upon eating half my meal and then discovering it, my lunch companion and I began an observational conversation about the employees. None of them were wearing hair nets, and I am 99% certain I know whose head the stringy hair came from. Needless to say, we both stopped eating immediately.

Between the cramped quarters and the hairy food, I think it's safe to say I WON'T be returning! What a shame :(

stopped in for lunch this weekend with a friend. we haven't stopped for fast food in ages - roast beef sounded delicious. the cashier was a very friendly woman; lots of personality. food was delish (for fast food, of course)... place seemed pretty clean. the cashier was out on the floor wiping tables down and talking with the customers. she's a great asset in the industry! every customer that left while we were still there rang their "great service bell" and she thanked each and every one. for an arby's, this one is very decent!

Ordered a grilled chicken sandwich and it was so bad that I couldn't finish it. Service was also slow and they don't have cups for water. Not big on fast food but even for fast food this Wendy's sucked.
Excellent customer service. I had an issue with an allergy to an ingredient in the Reuben, and they went above and beyond to make it right. Great menu and food as well.

As an EXTREMELY picky eater, I was wary at first..but this place is awesome!! Everything is fresh, and they stay true to what they're all about--no added oils, extreme amounts of salt, etc. I got a bowl with sweet potatoes, soy strips, and teriyaki, and ate the whole thing and now I'm stuffed (in a good way) definitely recommend for vegans and non-vegans alike!

Burgers were pretty good.  Fries were nothing special.  In general you're probably better off going to 5 guys if you really want burgers and fries. 

The pizza was pretty good.  The staff seemed a little confused when I went.  There were alot of people working but only seemed like 1 or 2 guys knew what was going on.  This may have been because I went pretty soon after they opened, hopefully they've figure it out by now.
Wokworks is a great option in the rittenhouse area! The food is fresh and fast and the staff is very friendly. I would recommend it to anyone.

I'm a proud omnivore.  I'll try eating nearly anything that moves at least once in my life.  And I love a nice, bloody steak from time to time.

I can honestly say though that I could easily eat here for lunch everyday and not get bored.  I try to avoid eating out for lunch, but with the Magic Carpet food cart so close it's really hard not to.  Their food is incredibly flavorful, hearty and filling.

The falafel sandwich is great, but the falafel + tabouli is out of this world.  The lady who works here recommended trying it with tahini and balsamic dressing, and since then I haven't been able to come  here and get anything else though.  I hear great things about their daily specials though and one day I hope to branch out a bit.   Until then, I'll gladly wait in line for my combo pita sandwich any day of the week.  The people who work here are very nice and they're one of the few food carts that take credit (but note the 50 cent charge).

Bad customer service, very rude and impatient with my order. "Are you gonna order something?!" That's the greeting I got. Food isn't good either. But good for a fast meal/ takeout or if you like messy food. Great atmosphere tho, really an eye catcher
I needed a quick lunch during my mini lunch break, good food, prepared on time, had the teriyaki, very good
I usually come here once or twice a month, and it's usually pretty good. Not today, cold meatballs and not toasted enough to warm it up.

The worst chicken tenders I've ever tasted. The breading is horrible. It's basically not cooked! When you peel the breading off, it's squishy and you can see the flour underneath in its original form. The fries are tasteless and bland. Just NO...

Where do I start? First, mac 'n cheese is my absolute favorite food. EVER. When I first heard about this truck, I not only shrieked with glee, but did my happy dance which only comes out on very special occasions. My first experience, and every one since, has never been met with disappointment. They offer a variety of creative dishes and the flavor is always on point. Worth waiting for in the obscenely long lines, which is further testament to the quality of Mac Mart's product and loyal following. But it doesn't stop there. Marti, the owner, as well as her partners in mac, are friendly and truly appreciate their customers. They recently celebrated their 2-year anniversary, and having been there since almost the beginning, it's been wonderful to see them grow their business and develop new and fun recipes. I look forward to seeing what the future has in store!

If any place would benefit from business process redesign, it would be here, the 30th St. McDonalds in Philadelphia. 

I've never SEEN so many employees collectively involved in the mess-up of virtually every single order made. It's painful to watch, and even more painful to experience, especially when they decide it's you, and not they, who botched your order. 

One time an employee brimmed with rage because I failed to recognize that the soda she filled for me was mine. The one that was left to swelter by the deep frier, and probably had a straw in it. In fact she was so hot with anger, she nearly lept her poly-panted self right over the counter for what could very well have been a rigorous hair-pulling sesame-seed face-off.

And another thing. This location has no ketchup dispensers. Totally annoying!! When you need to eat fast and catch a train, you need to pump it. But instead, 30th St. only does ketchup packets: those tiny, impossible-to-open packets -- and only if you ask. Otherwise you get none.

1 out of 10 hamburger patties.

Went during lunchtime with my SO, 12-1. Took me over an hour, start to finish, just to get my food. We spent 15 minutes waiting to order, then a grueling 45 minutes just to get two entrees (nothing special). The expediters looked so frazzled, all the cooks were looking panicked and confused. The whole process was a mess.
        About 30 minutes after ordering someone had told us there was no broccoli for one of my dishes...I didn't care I just wanted anything. About 10 minutes later and a cook on the line screamed that our food was ready. The expediter turned around and said "No, that order is right here!" Uh oh. Could this really get worse. The expediter shoved our greasy takeout containers (with no labels on them saying what they are) into our bag and told us the next meal was free (lol). 
        We walked back to our jobs, trying to think of what to say to our bosses for being so incredibly late. When we finally got back to eat, we opened our containers and neither one was what we ordered. Completely wrong, even down to the sauce. Too bad it was actually pretty tasty...But I had no idea what the fuck it was.
        I give this place 5 months. If its still here, I will try again, and if it is better I will change my rating (seriously). This is not a *just opened* forgivable type of stuff. This is a sign there are some fucked up problems here. Please change guys.

We never got a chance to eat because the cashier George was absolutely RUDE and miserable. While we were ordering he was making hand gestures for us to hurry up. Really! If you want your eggs with a side of ATTITUDE then this is your place. George really needs to quit because customers service is not his strong suite. MISERABLE Employee-NEVER AGAIN!! Keep your money.

OK...another flight with a service animal...this was a really long trip...

After traveling for nearly 24 hours, I got the opportunity to have breakfast.  On the suggestion of the agent at the ticket counter, I ate at Joe's.  Even though it was in Terminal B and I was flying out of Terminal F, the agent was confident my breakfast needs would be satisfied.

6:45 AM, I arrived at the spot.  A couple of folks in front of me were just finishing placing their orders.  One counter guy, one grill guy.  After the folks received their receipt, I was asked what I would like along with a cup of coffee to start the morning.  

Looking on the board, the breakfast sandwiches all seem to have egg as their anchor.  To shake things up, I asked for a breakfast sandwich with bacon and cheese, no egg, along with a glass of milk (white, not chocolate).  Without batting an eye, ole' boy behind the counter says "You don't want coffee, you want Milk?" I replied that I wanted milk and he asked "You sure you don't wanna cuppa coffee?" When I declined, he asked if I wanted my sandwich on white or wheat bread.  I requested wheat.  

While placing my order, I watched grill guy prepare another breakfast sandwich, with egg, bacon and cheese.  This sandwich was built on a roll instead of bread from a loaf.  This sandwich looked very appealing, especially when grill guy put the sammy on a plate and then laid down hash browns on the side.  Whew!  

I completed my order, paid and the counter guy brought me a 12-ounce glass of milk, directing me to the right end of the counter to receive my sandwich.  About 90 seconds later, grill guy brought my sandwich in a styro box, and he directed me to the napkins along the counter.

Wheat bread peeled from a loaf...a respectable amount of bacon cooked to a turn but not to crunchyness...white cheese that has been masterfully placed for maximum meltingness...adding a squeeze of mayo on one half and mustard on the other...enjoying swapping bites for the contrasting tastes...a respectable start to a morning at the airport.

Price...adjust it with customization, especially since I left off the majority ingredient.  
Next time, I leave the egg on until I have the sammy in hand...as the wheat bread from a loaf with bacon and cheese is good, but looks so much more appealing on a roll.

Redemption!!!! 

Today is one of those days where the weather causes even hungriest among us to consider foraging for lunch in the break room.  

Its a bleak scene:  I'm  rifling through the cabinets, hoping for a saltine or possibly a  left over pastry and my Coworker  waltzes past  with a paper bag full of heavenly smells.   Chilies, cinnamon....  "Oh, (says he) didn't you know Magic Carpet had chili?" 

No. I did. not. know. that.    Monsoon and day-old bagels be damned.   

So off I run, as fast as my red Wellies can carry me. 

The chili was divine. Just the right amount of heat, a great spice combo (I'm thinking chipolte and cinnamon, possibly even chocolate... almost mole-y) .   

I wasn't reduced to having to eat coffee creamer and jelly packets for lunch. My only regret.... I should have gotten a large.

Ordered lunch from WokWorks during their opening week. They clearly weren't prepared for the lunch rush as we waited almost an extra half hour for our order and "ran out of beef" so I had to settle for chicken. I had the flat rice noodles with black gold sauce and extra veggies. It was alright, but as an Asian person I have some trouble justifying $10 for lackluster "Asian" food. The noodles were overcooked and mushy, and it needed a heck of a lot more sauce. Veggies were really just carrots and onions, I felt a little jipped there. 

Worth a shot but really wasn't impressed.

I asked for a large coffee.  I got a large coffee.  I didn't ask for a smile, small-talk, offer to donate to the Ronald McDonald House, or anything else.  I didn't get anything else.  This was expected behavior, and for that, I am grateful.

And the coffee beats anything in 30th Street Station.
Came for a quick bite after a disappointing meal at a restaurant called The Blue Duck. The food hit the spot it wasn't perfect but good enough. The Baconator and chili cheese fries is what I ordered.

This was simply the worse noodle joint I have ever tried.  I love noodle houses, and was kind of hoping this would be a Wagamama style joint close to my office.  I ordered the "wok noodles" with chicken, snow peas, portobello mushrooms and the Asian BBQ sauce.  

Watching the utterly chaos going on behind the counter was highly discouraging.  Lots of people bringing unlabeled containers down to a woman at the end of the counter.  She then had to open the container to figure out what it was, match it to a slip she had stuck to a cork strip on the counter.  Orders would pile up, and you could see she was getting rather disoriented sorting it all out.  

First, the noodles were so over cooked, they essentially became a mass of mush.  I have never had such terribly over cooked noodles.  The other issue was that instead of portobello mushrooms, they were either pale porcini's or dark buttons,  I couldn't tell.  The sauce was just...ugh.  Of course, this was made much worse by the gelatinous goo that had once been my noodles.  For this, I paid a premium rate of more than $10. 

I don't plan on returning, and I strongly discouraged co-workers from heading down.  I recommend Tampopo (on 21st), Smile cafe (on 22nd), or even the standard American style Chinese joint called Mandarin (chestnut between 21 & 22).   I had high hopes, but they were crushed.

They cater on lunch at the office occasionally, their ingredients took me by surprise for vegetables - purple cabbage, carrots, Brussels sprouts are all  in the mix, but they work wonderfully together.  They key is their sauces - and how they are used in combination.  Each time I see, I question it, after I eat it - I love it.

I ordered at the airport joes and never got my food. Asked them if they could make my chicken tenders quickly so I could get on my flight after assuring me that they could. Had to walk away as the final boarding call was called. Never ate. 

As the tv show goes, it's always shiney in Philadelphia, especially it's airport and specifically at joes.

Where to begin.. Ordered off of grubhub, delivery guy gets here and explains to me that he left my sandwiches in the car but gave me the wings. He explains to me that he will leave it at the front desk. Sounds fine, I get it, it sucks to come up to apts , nbd.   So I walk down, nothing..he didn't leave me anything, he left, with my money. I call the owner, lackluster at best with his attitude. Told him I do not want his food just refund me my money, sry, I don't trust places when it comes to food, there's a reason y the kid left without giving me my food, and I don't want anyone messing with my food after I complain.  Kid comes back, he wants the wings...we told him they're gone..trashed, as they were soggy and shitty anyway.  Delivery kid has huge attitude once he knows they're not getting the wings, tells me the owner will be back to get em.. An argument ensues. Delivery guy gets muscles only after he's in the elevator and door is closing..calling my gf a dirty skank..nice, real nice for a business

Owner said "what do you want me to do". ... Haha doesn't matter you've lost my business and everyone I know

A lot didn't make sense.  Delivery kid used the excuse he didn't drop my hoagies off bc he had other deliveries...lol..what, u were parked 5 feet from my building, why would you leave?  BS excuse..just tell me u don't have them and try some honesty..

Owner--- business 101.  The customer is always right. Especially when they are legit right.  Your employees are an extension of you. And you can't have your employees trying to fight customers... Oh yea..learn to apologize too.  

Order from here if you like ignorant fucks who don't give a shit about you, they're money source.
The Stir Fry is always piping hot and full of awesome fresh healthy flavor! Tons of sauces too! Rock on.

I was unfortunate to come across this store in PHL.   The cashier looks uninterested with rude attitude to customers as she was busy playing her cell phone all the time.   No matter how good the food is, service is still equally important.

There are 3 - yes THREE Auntie Anne's in 30th Street Station.
The "main one" where they can bake pretzels is larger and back by the bar abd Surf City Squeeze.

There is a kiosk (they cart the pretzels over) on the concorse floor (near Amtrak) and another small store near the SEPTA area.

Like obese Philadelphians really need 3 of these?  Anyhow - it's not good for you - and while a hot cinnamon sugar pretzel (especially fresh and hot) tastes good to me, I nearly always feel ill afterward and regret the 470 cals.

Skip it.  Get some fruit or hummus from Old Nelson's.
Or better yet - leave the building and go get "real" food.

Maybe I just caught this place on a good day, but to me it was fine. I got 10 chicken nuggets and an order of fries. The chicken nuggets were pretty good (especially since this is Wendys!), the fries were on the meh side, but Wendys isn't known for having the best fries for a reason. My table was a bit dirty (I'm used to having that, but it was still annoying to have to give the table a wipe down). Service was actually on the fast side. 

Again, maybe I just caught this place on a good day.

we ordered shrimp n chicken nugget meals. We waited for 20 minutes in the cramped drive thru. The food came out--i trusted that there were chicken nuggets and shrimp in the bag.  I had no idea chicken nuggets and shrimp was code for 2 chicken dinners and chicken nuggets. Idk... the food was ok tho.

"Salt bomb but quick and filling dishes" in short.

Friendly people. Nice and clean interior. Food was mediocre. Everything was salty (drinking water as I type). Not that you would expect layers of flavor from a fast casual noodle place but the overwhelming flavors were salty and spicy.

Brussel sprouts side was salty and undercooked. Wok can definitely overcook and burn vegetables on the outside but inside can be deceivingly undercooked. It was like chewing on raw brussel sprouts with charred outer leaves that were dipped in pure soy sauce.

Think chipotle meets Asian food. Ingredients are superb - organic meats and fresh caught fish - a true find for Philly. An excellent spot for lunch or for dinner. Delivery available through grub hub. Also - free beer on Friday afternoons!

I went here for lunch the past two days because I work in the building next door. For the food that you get, it's extremely overpriced. I got a chicken cobb salad and a chicken avocado sandwich. 

Chicken cobb salad- didn't have any chicken on it, and I paid extra for that. Really upsetting. It wasn't that large of a salad for $8.50. 

Chicken avo- I thought this was really good and I enjoyed the flavor of the chicken and I liked the bread. I would probably get this again. 

There are definitely better places in the area that taste better and are less expensive.

My family ate here while waiting for our flight to Vegas.  The food was surprisingly good. My chicken sandwich was large with a very delicious roll. The lettuce and tomato were really fresh too. The French fries portion sizes are quite large.  A medium was enough fries to share with my whole family of 4.

Again, a Wendy's in Philadelphia which is completely and unnecessarily slow - unbelievably slow in fact with zero people in the line or the dining area.

After fifteen; twenty minutes- I finally receive a burger which is not even warm

What's going on with inner city Philly Wendys? It is not somewhere you'd want to be as a client or employee- any of them.  They are all very poorly run here in my opinion and this city's franchises are giving a bad name to the chain


RE-VISIT #2 on 8/31:
Oh yes, this one's a solid one - star


RE-VISIT #3 on 9/9:
Burger was made 3TIMES with mayonnaise after being asked #NOMAYO

WILL THERE BE A VISIT4? Probably not. The clientele here also is lower than desireable
What was funniest was the guy making it each time would swear to me up and down that he made it himself= and there was no mayo! Hahaha I said, open it! 

UPDATE
RE-VISIT #4 on 9/10
Yes I gave them a fourth try. I ordered a Stacker (double burger) #NOMAYO.
What I got first time after a considerable wait was a super-greasy, cold and soggy burger (with mayo, obviously slathered all over both bun halves).
Second burger came out- at least not cold, it was barely over room temperature. It did NOT have mayo!! However; unfortunately it was only a jr. cheeseburger. I just LOLed hard. I doubt I'll go back to this location. 
Saving grace: I witnessed a woman wiping down the tables and busting her back to try and keep their dining room clean after numerous dirty kids. I said god bless you- it 's tough to clean up after such filthy animals like the ones that come in and eat here every day. She had such a great attitude- Hey, it's job security, that I might go back and have a potato or something some day. And then, unlike the other99% of the clientele, I will take my wrapper or tray and actually use a trash can.
To top it off, these guys walking out behind me were so rude walking out (after leaving all their dirty cups and trash on the table) that they wanted me to open the door for them. I held the door open for the other guys (who cares right, thats just what you do), but they refused to grab it.  The first door i saw him not reach out to hold the door open. Am I supposed to hold the doors for him and let him out in front of me? So, second door i just let it shut on that !@#$. Too bad it wasn't a real fast-closing door that would have been way more apropos. So partly the staff is lazy, but at least they try to fix their mistakes. Some staff is hard working and has good attitudes- much of the Wendy's in center city do not (and all chains). I'm realizing that it's not just employees- its customers that are complete d bags! No wonder it's hard to work in this environment.

VISIT 11/7/15 2:47-2:57 PM
At the front counter their Princess cashier barely acknowledged me, took the order and did not say thank you, make eye contact, or have any emotion other than disgruntled and RUDE.

It took 10 minutes for me to get my cold cheeseburger

I have actually eaten here.

Yes.

Gasp.

So shocking - seeing as I usually don't even consider fast food - but I have a weakness.  Every once in a business-trippy-blue moon, I grab an egg McMuffin here on my way to catch the AMTRAK train.

300 calories.
$2.99 (sometimes they have a buy 2 for $3 deal - but who can eat 2 of them?)

Egg Mc Muff.

What evs,

Oh - and believe it or not the Muslim ladies who run the place (at least on the morning weekday shift) are pretty darned pleasant. I was so shocked!
One of my favorite lunch spots!! Literally here 1-2 times a week. Noodles are so good it really satisfies your appetite. I will keep coming over and over again!!

I really, really, really like this place.  Wokworks is my new most favorite fast food spot. It is such a cool idea to do fast-food wok cooking with lots of healthy ingredients.  When you add in extremely friendly and helpful staff with a nice vibe atmosphere, you have a winner.

My very favorite stir fry is the build-your-own with red and white quinoa.  Add your protein, veggie, seasoning, and sauce and you have a tasty treat in front of you.  All the sauces are great from the golden nut peanut to the pepper spicy Szechuan.  But if you like spicy with flavor - order the tropicalia mango sambal.  A side of jalapeño brussel sprouts in sesame oil just adds to the combo of flavours here.

It is usually busy when I have been there so that it is a great sign this concept is catching on.  Now just expand to my hood .... and def let me take a branch of Wokworks with me back to Vienna!
The place was good at one time, Went they change management thing change!  Half done chicken n bad attitude!!!!  If  u like half done food n bad attitude u should good.
Love this place! The noodle dishes are delicious with good protein and non-soggy vegetables. The sauces are very tasty. The service is great,  and I hope this place sticks around.

I'm never even remotely disappointed by this place. Food is excellent, staff is excellent and friendly, prices now that they have the smaller bowl option are great. They always have clever marketing campaigns and specials. This is in my top 5 favorite lunch places in Philly.

Try the Soba+Chicken+Brussels Sprouts+Bacon+Peanut Sauce

Very unlike a regular Wendy's experience.  This Wendy's is always crowded.  
Pros 
They have a few staff members who are very friendly and courteous 
The food tastes just like a regular Wendy's location. 
Cons 
They have many more staff that are discourteous and find working to be a chore
The line to pickup is insane, very disorganized-they should ask names instead of numbers.
They are so slow
And if you order anything out of the ordinary, for instance a hamburger rather than a cheeseburger, 9 times out of 10 you will get a cheeseburger anyhow.
Not my fav location to say the least.
I had a great meal here, but until they open one here in Northern NJ I will only get to enjoy this place once a month at best...
It was not a nice experience for me. I usually dont like insect and I told them this and they did not do anything. You should be careful.

Meh meh meh. I had high hopes about this place, but alas- another crappy takeout joint finds its way to South Philly. Delivery took an hour and a half at 5pm, and when the driver arrived, he knocked on my door after I specifically requested that he call first (my downstairs neighbors are jerks who can't quite grasp that sometimes the people upstairs might need to use the front door). 
After fighting off the snake eye from the neighbor I took my food back into my apartment and got ready to eat. First, the garlic fries. I love garlic, in an unhealthy-probably have perpetual garlic breath-kind of way. I opened the fries and they were stone cold, rock hard, and so dry they almost sucked the moisture out of the room. There was nary a clove to be found, and they were sprinkled with a strange white powder that looked and tasted like Molly McButter. Props to them for the 80's nostalgia, but I'll stick to YouTube for that. I tossed them into the trash after the first bite.
Next I opened the salad. Um, salads are extremely difficult to mess up. Their Big Mama salad (or whatever it's called) was supposed to be artichokes, mozzarella, roasted reds, and Caesar. There were 2 small slivers of artichoke in there. For reals. I counted. I dumped the "homemade" Caesar dressing on top and took a bite. If that's homemade, their cooks must live in the Ken's Dressing factory. I spent 8 years of my life in restaurants, I can taste dressing from a 5 gallon Ken's jug from a mile away. The salad leaves were super gritty, as if not properly washed. I gave up. 
Finally- the only reason I can even give them 1 star- the PB&J milkshake! After the ice cold fries, I was expecting the shake to be completely melted, but it was still frozen and super thick. It was borderline heavenly and extremely dangerous. I rarely drink milkshakes, but I fear that I've become like a shark who's tasted blood and I will now hunt down this shake where ever I go for the rest of my life.
Just not from Wise Fries.

Chick-fil-a consistently has some of the best chicken around.  This location in particular can get crazy busy during lunch hours but the lines are usually efficient and the service is quick.  Unlike other Chick-fil-a's, you may not get the usual smiles and "my pleasure" response to "thank you" but Big Ed is often seen smiling and establishing order to the chaos.  Despite the hectic pace, they get the orders right, and the food is on point.  Chicken tenders are always juicy and not dry with the right amount of crisp on the outside and the waffle fries are seasoned just right.  You just have to remind them on the sauce you want with your chicken and waffle fries.

Seating is within the food court area of Liberty Place, and there is plenty of it!

Enjoy some delicious chicken!

Hahahahahaha this Taco Bell is pathetic. The tables are covered in chipped paint and I was just served a loaded griller in a napkin. It was wrapped in a napkin. 

Lol.

I really want to like this place. Healthy version of Chinese food? Sounded so good to me. And store looked clean from outside and also liked their name... Got quinoa fried rice with bean sprout and veggies...simply no good... I like healthy food but has to tasty to keep going back. That was my last visit... But I liked their clean container and healthy concept so.. It is two star place.

I wish they were at LOVE PARK everyday! This mac & cheese is by far the best in Philadelphia.  I would put it up against anyone that thinks they have a good mac & cheese.  Every time I've eaten it the folks in the truck were super friendly and spunky.  I really enjoyed the spinach dip and the regular is just a great go to.  My husband loves the south philly one with the sausage and peppers... YUM YUM YUM!

I never expect much from McDonald's in the first place, but this place sinks below even their standard. It is routinely dirty, and the staff is quite rude, even in the presence of the morning manager who does little to correct the problems. For a great breakfast sandwich go two blocks south on 10th St to Sam's Fresh Spot. The owners are a very nice, polite couple who use quality ingredients and cook things up fresh when you order. It takes a little more time, but the wait is well worth it. Avoid this McDonald's at all costs!

Haha, this McDonald's suddenly closed sometime after 10/31/14. 

There was no "official" explanation on the door, just a notice that former customers should try one of the other vendors in the concourse. I wonder if it closed due to escalating rent, franchisee issues, or if it was due to a healthcode violation? 

The only good "memories", if they can be called that, that I have of the place were of the free coffee samples that were available for a brief week in September 2014, otherwise the food was overpriced and they didn't even have a dollar menu. 

Good riddance!

Worst McDonalds ever.

First of all, it seems to be a magnet for hobos, lunatics, alcoholics, and the general scum of Philadelphia.

Secondly, whatever you happen to order, there will be an issue with that particular item. Order a chicken sandwich? Chicken was delayed. Order a burger? Burgers are on hold. Ordered both? Someone took a dump in the french fries.

Thirdly, food sucks. Keep overfrying the nuggets. Jesus, can't even get nuggets right.

Fourthly, support staff is moronic. Hey lady, I'm trying to fill my drink, cap it, grab a straw, and then rush back to the counter to claim  my food. Do you think you could clean the floor in that region 30 seconds later?

Fifthly, they insist on collecting my receipt when I'm trying to pick up my order. I like to keep my receipts as personal records. Do enough people steal from this place to warrant such a practice?

To be fair though, an idiot like me habitually returns which is perhaps why this place still exists. One can only hope it burns to the ground with all the people in bullet point #1 in it or I actually upgrade my culinary tastes and avoid this cesspool
The food is delicious and the service is great!  A lot of people recommended PlantPure and at first I was saying it's a vegan restaurant, but I tried it once and I love it.

I have now eaten at the panda express on two separate occasions. I travel past this specific restaurant once every two or three months. It was recommended as a fast place to eat if I was just trying to grab something.

On both occasions, I found the restaurant to be extremely clean. Even the bathrooms were in great shape. However, there was a line to order food both times. Granted I had gone there to eat lunch at approximately 12 o'clock both days. When I was there today I checked out the other reviews. I did not think it was fair to compare panda express to other local Chinese eateries.  To do that is like comparing Dominos pizza to one of your favorite local shops.

I honestly feel like panda express is very similar to Pei Wei. The food was definitely serviceable and the employees were helpful on both occasions.  If you want real authentic Chinese food, then this is not the place. If you want fast Chinese American food, then panda express is the right location.

Not that any Wendy's is particularly delicious, but it makes a nice fast food meal every once and awhile.  So know my standards aren't crazy high.  I would even be understanding if I had vomiting or diarrhea afterward--because that is part of the Wendy's package.  This place was terrible though, even by those standards.  The service was abysmal, but the worst was that ALL 3 condiment containers they gave me had congealed into a solid (see photos below).  Wendy's is at least supposed to taste good going INTO your body, that is the social contract I have made to explain why I deal with the consequences of it exiting the body.  

But on a serious note, I am pretty sure someone would have gotten ill if they actually eaten the sauce there.  I'll never know though because there was no expiration date.

You've been warned.

I went here for a quick take order last night. The space is very bright and clean. They did a very nice job cleaning up the gnarly old taco place. I order chicken stir fry with broccoli, bok choy, and spicy sauce (the three pepper one). I also order the pork dumplings. 

I received shrimp instead of chicken. Thank goodness I am not allergic. It was actually very good, and the shrimp were perfectly cooked, and on the larger size. Sauce was slightly spicy and somewhat tart. I liked it.

The dumplings were scantily stuffed, and lacking on flavor. 

My major gripe is all the above cost $18.50. Pretty expensive for stir-fry and dumplings. BUT it is Rittenhouse, so I digress...

Welcome to the neighborhood WW.

It's a Subway, so you know the drill. I'm only docking stars for this location on account of its overall atmosphere and the service. Aside from that, the sandwiches are exactly the same as at every other Subway on the planet.

Also, they haven't kicked on the A/C yet. I mean, I know it costs money, but seriously. It's like 90 degrees out.

This is about the only great place to eat in 30th and the best place for breakfast in Liberty Place.

The only downfall is their service. The people who work here seem to not like their jobs/lives/pay/uniform and are generally just trying to make sandwiches and go home.

Besides that, Pain's offerings are great: bagels such as French Toast, Dutch Apple (which I suggest with egg and sausage in the morning); they have artisan breads for your sandwiches, fresh squeezed juices, yogurt parfait, seriously jam-filled croissants and chocolate "breakfast" items and daily soups. 

This is two steps up from Cosi, and on the same level as Corner Bakery or Metropolitan Bakery.
The food is not upto the standard of most Mcdonalds. You need to be having great patience to deal with the staff here coz they don't respond that well to your questions.

I always go to chick Filaduring my lunch break & get the Cobb salad. This particular time 90% of the leave were withered brown and slimey! It was absolutely repulsive!! Called and talked to owner, Fred who stated he would replace it but couldn't make it back because I had a meeting. Check your leaves before you eat them!!

I took the friendly owner (who reached out to me) up on a free meal due to a recent disappointing experience and gave it another shot last night. Boy am I glad that I did!
