One example is I added Avocado for $0.75 to a sandwich, when I said they forgot it, the girl behind the counter pointed to this little spot of green and said that was my Avacado, I should have asked for $5.00 worth so I could actually taste it.  On the plus side, the Tuba club was great, and the bread is fresh, sooo much better then Subway, but the cuts of deli meat are also sub par and often find something not right with it.
Cheese steak was ok. Dont see what the big deal for this place is. Very over priced and bland. Better cheesesteaks in jersey.
I gave my cousin and girlfriend the whole Philly cheesesteak experience. They ordered their steaks with everything on it. To them it was subpar.

No. No. and No.
This place is great for drunk food because everything is good when you are drunk. I feel bad for tourists that Pats and Genos are known for their cheesesteaks.

The Cantina is a nifty little neighborhood joint - great place to get blood orange margaritas and free chips and salsa.  The outdoor seating is great on those nice summer evenings.  It's pretty dark inside - which i guess is great for the evening crowd - but makes it a little dismal for brunch.  Still, it's a nice location for meeting friends and having a few drinks.

Best! Cheesesteak! EVEEEEEER!

Never had Geno's, and don't plan to. Pat's is the best tasting thing you can eat.
Went there against our better judgement for nostalia's sake....what a waste of time, money and empty calories....

oh man i love pats cheesesteaks they're amazing. i drove up to philly from maryland with a couple of friends for this and after the 2 1/2 hour drive we got to pats and man it was worth it. the meat is so good and the peppers they have compliment it very well along with their other sauce. the service that i and my friends received was simply outstanding along with how quickly our food came (it was almost instant) every one should defidently try one of these things before they die its a MUST!!! I plan on coming back soon with more of my friends :)

Had to have a cheese steak from Philadelphia! So we stopped here and it was delicious! We were gonna share half and half but we each ended getting our own! They make it so fast! It's so convenient and so worth it.

absolutely the worst checkers i ever visited i love the fries so im definitely a repeat customer but this one i will never go there again even if they call me n say we would like u to have 100 gift card on us i wouldnt NO NO NO THANK U NO . I agree with the previous review if u complain they might spit on ur food, the women that was cooking my fries had a huge wig on with hair all over the place with out hairnet  and  absolutely no customer service This is how she looked serving food 
(Wheres the heath inspection when u need them)
Long line. Bland cheese steak. Costly for what it is. Overpriced. Over hyped. But ya gotta go  at least once right? right? I give the food 1 star and the legend 4 stars

Best things are the margaritas and the guac.  I've had bigger and better burritos, but he tacos and fajitas are pretty big proportions.  Recommend getting any slow cooked meat as your selection with any entrée.  The atmosphere is laid back, hipster, and when its nice out the outdoor seating is the best option.  Good place to bring friends from out of town.

Don't hate me - I live 2 hours from the nearest Chick Fil A and it's become my tradition to pop here before I get on the plane, get the sandwich meal (oh, those waffle fries!) AND also get a sandwich to go for the second leg of my trip.  I pity the people who have to sit next to me on the plane and watch me slowly savor my sandwich.  I always ask for extra pickles and they always oblige.

We went late Friday night. They were super fast and friendly. They definitely made it evident that there was a rivalry with Gino's. But a great experience and delicious cheese steak with peppers onions and provolone!

This is a newer McDonald's. The staff is nice, but, the service is slow and I don't think every crew member knows exactly what they're doing. It took me a while  to just get a fairly uncomplicated order for me and my co-worker. It is convenient to my new job in East Falls, though.

Yup it's good and fun to visit the south side of town to eat at Pat's and Gino's.  Quite frankly the best thing that happened to Pat's was Gino's and vise versa.  Make sure you know how to order...one whiz with = a steak sandwich with cheez and grilled onions.  That's the real way to do it.

I've tried Geno's cheese steak across the street and when I finally got to try Pat's, I could definitely tell the difference. They have many condiments to choose from and you cannot go wrong with any of them. It is a place to go to after a night of partying. They are open 24/7 so whenever you're hungry, this is the place to go to for a quick grub.
Try the tater tot chili omelet. It's amazing! I highly recommend T&N for any occasion but especially for breakfast. You can't miss with this quaint South Philly spot. Tell them Stefano sent you.

This isn't my kind of place but we were on our way to the park with the dog and wanted something quick.  I read some of the reviews prior and thought that we should go for it.  I have to question some of the reviewers because the burger had no taste whatsoever even with all the toppings. Anything with that much grease should be loaded with flavor otherwise why eat it? The fries were ok but couldn't eat them after having instant heartburn from my first course.  I fumed the whole walk home thinking about all the other places to better spend the calories.

The guy taking the orders for the steak was very rude, he was a jerk, when i called he hung up on me before even i finished sentence. And i was calling because i forgot something on one of the tables. 
But to be fare, they have one of the best cheesesteak sandwiches i ever had!

Being a native to the suburban area...it was always Pat's.  I've learned my lesson.  I found others that blow it away from the meat, to the cheese, to the bread.  The one thing that is the stigma is the price.  $9!  Nine freaking dollars for a cheesesteak!  Shame!  Good bye Pat's.  Thanks for the memories.

It is true that many of the lesser known cheese steak joints in the city can be superior... I still enjoy a drive into South Philly to Pats. I have lived in the Philly area for 8 years and I have done the Pats vs Gino's test a few times and Pat's has won my vote each time.

Delicious meat, not over-shredded, fresh bread that is firm but fresh and soft inside.

A true treat!

Worse service ever!!!!  We had a large group of people and the server would only come and ask one person if they wanted something then she'd scurry off before you could ask her for something.  It took forever to get the food that came out wrong, then took forever again to finally come out right. I had to ask for utensils and a napkin. I debated on ordering my last drink because I knew I had to leave in 30 min. The girl next to me and I both ordered margaritas at the same time and she got her's right away.  After 20 min I explained to the server that I had been waiting and had to cancel mine because I had to leave. I asked her how much my food was so I could leave money on the table for the group, she insisted on giving me a separate bill. When I nervously asked her if she could bring it right away because I had to leave,  she gave me an attitude.  Food was good and outdoor atmosphere was nice.
Terrible, Terrible, Terrible! Bad service (not that I was expecting top notch), horrible cheesesteaks (YUCK!) and is no comparison to Tony Lukes. Nuff said.
If you go to Pat's go with a friend and split the cheese steak and go to Geno's and see which you like better. It's a religious war, but I fall in the Pat's is better camp!

Had Geno's so I had to have Pat's too.  The service is not the most friendly but for as many 'steaks as they have serve a day you can see why they want to keep it moving.  The meat is sliced perfectly.  I ordered a wiz without and was impressed with how well together the cheesesteak stayed together with the wiz.  The biggest knock on Pat's for me was the bread.  It was a lot harder then I was hoping for.  Other than that a great cheesesteak!  Definitely would recommend trying.

Better than Ginos because the bread is better.   But I think Tony Luke's is better than Pat's.  I am sure there are better ones in Philly but I wasn't fat enough to eat 4 in one night.  3 was all I could handle.  lame

Slightly better than Geno's across the street. 

Meat seems to be of marginally better quality here and sliced in longer thinner strips which I prefer. Everything else I found to be nearly identical to Geno's.

Also, the staff was a lot nicer than at Geno's. Those guys at Geno's are hardcore dickheads. Yeah I said it, dickheads. You got a problem with that?

Finally, there is a scene in Rocky where Sylvester Stallone is chilling here. In fact, there is a engraving in the cement block signifying the exact spot he stood at in the movie! I rented Rocky just to see this scene. And it was well worth it! Take that Geno's! BOO-YA!

Sometimes you get stuck in Center City. You are a bit hanged over sometimes, too. Sometimes still, the only thing that will suffice is a cheeseburger with lettuce, tomatoes, raw onions, jalapenos, ketchup, mustard and mayo. Sometimes it needs to be a double burger. For all those reasons, you go to five guys sometimes.

The burger is a bit sloppy, which makes it perfect hang over food. The choices of toppings are endless, though I've already revealed my hand here. Fries can be hit or miss, so I tend to skip them. Lines get long at lunch, so if you are hankering for a decent fast food sandwich, get there early.

Also Overhyped just like Genos. I tried Pat's and Geno's both and Pat's had more meat on the cheesesteak compared to Geno's and the onions were slightly more cooked but still relatively crunchy/raw. Philly tourist stop but definitely not worth it for $10 a cheesesteak.
Super lecker. Leider war es etwas kalt und regnerisch und man kann nur draußen sitzen.
Pat's vs Geno's, definitely Pat's but I think Subway has a better cheese steak than these two.

Wow, this place is busy, busy, busy.  I would hate to live in the area.  Parking and traffic are bad.  Service is super fast, but the line for food is confusing with one line for sandwiches and another line for everything else.  We weren't very impressed with the Philly Cheese Steak, but when in Philly, you have to have one.

Cheesesteaks are pats are great! Meats is soft and tender, bread has just the right strength to hold all the juices and has a good bite to it. Only thing I'd say is parking can be a pain, and sometimes the peppers can be a little suspicious just because it's in a can outside in a self serve stand. Other than that it's delicious.

Delicious cheesesteaks.  Get it with onions and provolone with a side of peppers picante! Try to stop by during the week when lines are not so crazy long.  I love cheesesteaks but I refuse to wait behind more than 5-10 ppl.

While in Philadelphia for New Year's my boyfriend and I decided to do the taste test.  We began at Geno's and ended at Pat's.  Overall, I was not impressed with Pat's.  

I ordered a "Whiz Wit".  They give you more "whiz" than Geno's but the bun wasn't that impressive, the meat was rubbery and a bit tasteless to me, and the onions tasted and felt very strange.  I couldn't finish my sandwich, which is a first because I'm definitely an eater but I couldn't stomach or bring myself to swallow anything so bland with such a strange aftertaste.  I definitely did not think it was worth the $7.50 paid.

The atmosphere was friendly and amusing and they were definitely quick with the order but I know when I return I'll just stick with Geno's.

I have to resist specifically writing a review for the quesarito even though, realistically, that food item is what this T. Bell location symbolizes to me. If I WERE to do that, I'd say this establishment was meaty, melty, gooey, and best when it's covered in hot sauce. But I'm not reviewing the quesarito, I'm reviewing the Taco Bell. And as far as Taco Bells go (I've been to more than I can count), this one takes the cake (or the Caramel Apple Empanada, as it were.)

Clean, well-tended drink machines, plenty of seats.... I'm shocked that folks are not flocking here every night for late night munchies. Shocked, but elated, as it has become my personal munchie oasis after a trip to Yakitori Boy or a fish bowl at Graffiti! Nestled comfortably on Chestnut, it's accessible from nearly any spot I might visit in Center City. A must for a one-track-taco-mind after slinging back bevvies.

The staff has always been courteous, quick, and, on 2 of my 3 visits (SO FAR!), hilarious, making jokes like we were old pals. The bathrooms are clean (again: SO FAR) so use them at will.

And if you don't leave here either a) armed with a quesarito or b) bellied with a quesarito you've already eaten... you're doing it wrong.
Not the very best cheese steak in the world. It's just a place for a quick bit late at night. They open 24 hrs for this that are coming from the clubs. Try it if you must.
Great cheese steak! Dove to Philly with my dad and brother just to compare pats and Genos cheese steak and Pats def won!

For the amount of publicity that Phily cheese steaks get, you'd think the flavor would be on par with the fish from Tsukiji Fish Market or something.  It is sadly not even close.  

I ordered the famous "whiz wit" and it was amazingly bland and lifeless.  there just wasn't anything to it.  If the king of steaks comes up with this, I'm happy being a pauper.  

to top it all off, the fries were greasy and overall, it was expensive.  With more bun than meat, paying $9 for the sammich really didn't provide anything worth noting, except in a meh review on yelp.
A solid pizza with some good crust. Got the simple margherita and it was exactly right. Would def eat again when the pizza cravings hit
I tried Tony Lukes and Gino's...then Pat's.  Pat's kicks ass.  Any time I am in Philadelphia, Pat's is a must !!!
My favorite place on East Passyunk! !!!!  The chicken burrito is excellent and im in love with their blood orange Margaritas.  Great place for brunch, lunch, dinner or  drinks.

Came out to philly my first time and the first cheesesteak "jawn" I tried was pats. Wasn't really too impressed. They're pretty rude but everyone was sayin that's just how people are in philly so whatever. Place is really touristy, all outdoor seating but it's pretty limited. The cheese steak was aight at best

I love this place for the no frills basic menu and the awesome food that's made quickly to serve all the people who come through the door.  I first tried 5 Guys in Manhattan and loved it and I love this one even more because I don't have to wait in a crazy lunch hour line to get me a burger with fresh jalepenos, onions, sauteed mushrooms, fresh green bell peppers, tomatoes, lettuce, ketchup, and A1 sauce on the side.  I also love how they have fresh peanuts for you to serve yourself that you can munch on while your order is being prepared.  I always share an order of regular size fries since they just pour a giant handle-full into a paper bag (there's a paper cup in there somewhere).  The fries are always perfectly fried and delicious--crispy on the outside and plenty of hot potato on the inside.  There's fountain soda and iced tea, but I usually just opt for ice water.  

I've ordered these burgers to-go before and they hold pretty well (I'm not a big burger bun snob so the simpler the better--5 Guys uses a sesame bun).  The staff is always friendly and efficient, which is always important.  The burger isn't the juiciest burger you'll have in Philly but it's still really good and the burgers are very big and filling.  I love that they have a million toppings that you can add to your burger and that one of them is jalepenos!  Since you get so many fries, I usually opt for the smaller burger since the regular burger has 2 patties.  I have a theory that this place made goodburger go out of business since they were pretty close by to each other.

I feel like this is one of those places that people go to more because its iconic rather than super tasty. The line was super long which makes you expect it to be amazing, so when its not your annoyed that you wanted so long and that it wasnt as delicious as the line would make one think. Dont get me wrong the cheese-steaks are not horrible but I would never imagine a line to be that long for some bland steak and cheesy sandwich. 
I think go to say you've gone, but dont expect too much people you may be let down.

I did not care for this place.

Gristly meat. Chewy bread. American cheese added almost as an afterthought (not melted on the meat, just kind of falling off, like cheese you buy at the grocery store that is close to its expiration date so it starts to get crumbly and falls apart). 

Maybe my boyfriend and I offended the delicate sensibilities of the staff by asking for a side of hot pepp--

"THEY'RE BACK THERE. YOUS CAN HELP YOURSELF."

Well. Thanks. Gentlewoman.

I guess a whole hot pepper works, but how do I put this on my sandwich? Do I bite off little pieces and spit them onto my hoagie? Do I take a bite of the cheesesteak and then a bite of the pepper while my mouth is still full of meat gristle and stale bread? Or do I just throw it all out and go somewhere else to eat?

Turns out, the latter was the best option. 

Unfortunately, before we learned our lesson, we had to part ways with $20 for one cheesesteak, one soda, and the ATM fees for this cash-only place ($15 for the food, $5 for the exorbitant ATM fees not associated with this place).

What can I say that probably hasn't already been said?   If theres a better place to get a cheesesteak, I'm game to try it.  Better than any deli, corner store, high end restaurant, Jims steaks on south street, or anything else I have ever had (haven't had Genos yet either).  

But it comes at a price too.  This is a tourist trap, they know people will pay what it costs.  Exactly how much that is?  It's close to $20 per person to eat here.  I took my friend from Baltimore here late night, we got 2 steaks wiz wit, about $11 each, 2 cheese fries (massive portion btw) almost $6 each, 2 bottles of water probably $5 for both.  So with tax its about $37-38.  Totally worth it, just a once in while type-of thing.

I just went there today.  Line was in street, but closer to sidewalk corner on the diagonal.  Took about 5-10 minutes to finally get food.  Once ordered, took about 30 seconds to get.  I got a mushroom pepper cheesesteak wit onions.  

I had genos after and I must say the addition of the peppers and mushrooms made the sandwich better than genos.  Otherwise they're about the same.  I gotta say I think the cheesesteaks in Raleigh, NC at Phillys are tastier and better IMHO, but these originals were not that bad.

The only real complaint was that its CASH ONLY and that fact wasn't really obvious until you got to the counter.  Perhaps not enough tables either.  Too many tourists coming there and hogging tables for far long after they're done eating.
What is to say that hasn't already been said really... I've been here twice both times in the Winter.  Bring a jacket as all seating is outside.  Pat's is my fave in the Pat's Vs. Geno's war.

I mean what person from Philly hasn't been here because it's open all hours of the night, however it's the worst. 

The cheese steak comes to you quick but the cheese is not melted and the meat is cold. 

Everyone from Philly knows this place is for tourists, I'll go to one of my many other favorites around and skip Pat's and Geno's.

Definitely can feel the rivalry between here and Genos, which is just a stone throw away. Big deciding factor was the shorter line and Geno's flashing lights just wasnt calling out to me.
The wait was alright, moved at a good pace. 
One "beef" with this place was one of the servers gave us some uncalled for attitude for ordering pizza fries (I find out later, thats part of the Pat's charm). Shrug
I ordered the pepper mushroom cheesesteak. The meat was good but not filling nor amazing. The rolls werent great, thought they should be thicker. Main thing i liked was the cheese whiz? 
Pizza fries... no worth it, had small meat bits, wtf. for $6
Doesnt live up to the hype and I've had better at bars where you can even order beer (like Lickity Splits) and get better service

As many do, we opted for a taste test between Pat's and Geno's.  

Pros:
*The bread was definitely superior.
*We preferred the onions being cooked on the flattop
*The atmosphere was more old school.

Cons:
*Found the meat to be flavorful but dry.
*Wiz not as flavorful

So, what was our verdict? For a true original and Philly experience, Pat's is the way to go!

Enjoy the Ride,
Baker and Biker Monkey
Fantastic! Both places are really great! You cant go wrong at either cheese steak place. Be sure you know what you want prior to getting to the window to order!

Obviously we came because it is a must do when you visit Philly. The line wasn't that long, we probably only waited 5 minutes. Typical philly cheesesteak menu. I opted for a mushroom and onion cheesesteak with provolone - $10. Their bread seems to get soaked and soggy by the time you dig into it. I do like how they cut their meat better than the competition across the street though.

Okay, let me start off by saying this place is pretty damn good.

The wings; they are not the best I have ever had, but are acceptable.

When I ordered from this place I got some fries and a burger. The fries are kinda soggy but are good, and the burger was awesome. I say this because I really likes the bun they use and the ground beef they use doesn't seem fake like other nearby places.

To finish off this review I also should add that this place has NO delivery minimum (which is pretty awesome, because I hate having to get a lot of food just to have them deliver).

In conclusion this place has ok wings, but rest is pretty good.
Still may favorite in Philly.  Sorry, Geno's, Tony Luke's and Jim's.  Pat's is the best.

This is more or less an average McDonald's.  However, they recently eliminated free refills for coffee.  I find this very customer unfriendly, as almost every other fast food restaurant gives free coffee refills.  I won't bother going there for breakfast.

If you're reading this review, this is a comparison (and the same review for Pat's Steaks, Ishkabibbles, Jim's Steaks, and Geno's).  

I came to Philly with, what I believe are, pretty realistic expectations regarding cheesesteaks.  Yes, I knew coming into it that Genos and Pats were tourist traps and that their might be better cheesesteaks elsewhere throughout Philadelphia.  But at the end of the day, after trying four different places, a cheesesteak is a cheesesteak and it didn't really live up to the hype at all.  With that said, and amongst the 4 places, I would have to rank these in the following order:

1) Jim's Steaks (3 stars):  Best place to sit and eat. They had the largest dining area with an upstairs area.  It was not air conditioned though.  As for the cheesesteaks, it was the best in terms of flavor, service, bread consistency. Bread wasn't too chewy or hard.I had it prov/wit (provolone cheese and onions) and mushrooms.  Better service than Geno's and Pats.

2)  Ishkabibbles (solid 2.5 stars, maybe 3):  Very comparable to Jim's but there's absolutely no where to sit with the exception of 6 barstools.   The gremlin drink is overrated too...but I had to try it.  I had it wiz/wit (cheese wiz and onions) and mushrooms.  Better service than Geno's and Pats.

3)  Geno's (1.5 stars due to lack of smiles/service, but I'll round up to 2 for the hype and flourescent lights):  I like the bread but the meat was pretty flavorless.  Meat was in big slices and not chopped up.  I had it both with wiz/wit (cheese wiz and onions) and prov/wit (provolone chesse and onions).  This was, by the way, the first place I tried.  They have outdoor seating so if it's cold, it's not the best place to eat there.  

4)  Pat's (solid 1.5 stars.  I won't round up to 2 since it's the least favorite of the four places):  The bread is softer and the meat definitely had more flavor than Geno's. The meat was chopped up.  BUT it was sooooo greasy that it gave me an upset stomach.  I had it with prov/wit (provolone cheese and onions).  They also have outdoor seating only.  

All in all, and if I'm in Philly again, I'm going to try Tony Luke's, Campos, Dalessandro's, and maybe a street vendor next time.  

BOTTOM LINE:  Skip the hype at Genos and Pats.  One of them may have started the cheesesteak craze, but the other establishments have made it better. It's time for Genos and Pats to catch up to the 21st century.  Word of advice to Genos and Pats:  SMILE and appreciate your customers!

This place is horrible & I won't waste too much time on a review. Bland, practically tasteless steak & rude staff. The fact that this place receives any national attention and people come here expecting an acceptable cheesesteak really disappoints me. A tourist trap & nothing more. If you know Philly you know the best steaks are in the Northeast.

Where can I start been in this place since it started ,, food is average .  It don't really do it for me .. So many Mexican places now a days popping up everywhere in philly , between food trucks , and stores ... That I find my self there and not cantina for the food .....
One thing it has is a good atmosphere and great drink menu !!  Overall it's a good place

Pat's and Geno's have good steaks, both owners do a lot for the city, and they are nationally known... If you only have a few days in Philly, try both places.... If you live around the area, there are better options.

I had a bacon cheeseburger and fries. The fries were pretty good and I did enjoy the burger but it definitely wasn't the best I've ever had. The people making the food were super nice though and kept checking for my order while I waited. I definitely recommend getting the little burger as the big one is two patties and is very filling and almost a bit hard to eat because it's so big. It's quick and relatively cheap but it's definitely not the best burger.

A great "cheesy" spot in the 'hood of South Philly adjacent to a little ballpark (which would be uber sketchy if not well-lit) and near another great spot, Geno's.  However, Pat's is historic because a scene from Rocky was filmed there (look for the plaque) and they are notoriously strict on ordering etiquette.  If you don't do it smoothly, firmly & quickly, they'll send your ass all the way back to the end of the line.  This can make for one nervous-as-hell-slightly-inebriated visitor who is in dire need of midnight munchies.  So, during the long wait I struggled with "Whiz wit... or was it wit Whiz... well, that makes more sense... but wait...oh shit!" because, before I knew it,  I was at the head of the line and some big guy was yelling at me in a thick Philly accent so I blurted out the first thing I could think of... and I guess it was the right one because they served me up a pipin' hot steak'o'cheese!!  I can't really tell which one is better in PHL... Jim's was pretty damn good with a great location but a monstrosity of a line... yet Pat's is worth the trek into the 'hood just for experience's sake.
Great Philly experience.  A fun splurge if you are visiting, but I wouldn't be a regular if I lived there.

All of my expectations were met or exceeded during my first ever visit to Pat's! Why my 5 star rating... the fact that you're reading this means you are "looking before you leap". Therein lies the key to YOUR positive experience with Pat's! More than any restaurant I've ever visited, I studied up on Pat's before I came. To thoroughly enjoy this unique cultural experience I needed to get the following expectations set:
- Parking - you're in downtown South Philly, it's street parking, no parking meters (it's free), plan to drive around side streets for a while within 2 or 3 blocks, practice parallel parking, don't drive your Bentley (although I saw one)
- Before you get in line - Know the sandwich menu, know what sandwiches your party wants, and what options on each sandwich (drinks and fries are ordered at a separate window). Nobody, (Pat's or customers) will tolerate you deciding at the counter. 
- Order like a local - optional, but highly recommended... while I fully expected to fumble this one, I found that the instructions worked flawlessly which I found through a Google search "how to order at pat's king of steaks"!
- Cash only - the prices are not low. Since you already know the menu, and know what you're getting (right?), have cash ready (at each window)
- Seating - it's all outdoors, under awnings, at picnic tables, right in the ambience of a busy city street, you might have to wait for a table to vacate 
- Appearance of food - let's just say, a paper wrapped cheese steak that was assembled in less than 5 seconds is, ummm, less than photogenic (see photo of my sandwich saying "cheese!")
- Diving in - the rolls, oh that first bite, those glorious chewy rolls, the culinary fireworks display of flavors and textures and aroma! It was worth the studying, the driving, the parking, the walking, the waiting, and the price! Wow, just wow!

where do i begin...

the employees work on a fast pace so you have to order quick and correct. seriously you will get your fresh cheese steak in 5 seconds.

once i recieved my super fast cheese steak i sat down and took my very first bite.....oh my gosh!!! it was soo delicious!!! 

soft toasted bread, the jucy meat with dripping flavor, the cheeze wiz, everything.....was to perfection.....

i must say that this is indeed the best cheese steak sandwich i have tired...kudos to pats!

Pat's or Geno's? Totally Pat's if that's the choice. Cheesesteak with whiz and onions; nice amount of all three and a tasty sandwich. Sunday morning there's not a line; great breakfast idea. Not worth waiting in line for though; other places do it better.
Quality of ingredients is not advertised.  Minus a star for no wifi (they have dead AT&T reception zones in the building).

So I've heard good things so I tried them out.. The staff.. Tybriah is her name.. Recommended me the double cheeseburger. She was even nice enough to give me her loads of fries to finish because she had too much! Her welcoming and inviting personality, warrants me to come back definitely come back. And the damn cheeseburger was too good to pass up. Especially with the GOLD PEAK machine.. I am SOLD! You guys HAVE to try them.. Or should I say you "five?"

Living in many different areas, it's nice to comeback to real cheesesteaks. These are the best cheesesteaks i have ever had! No one compares! Some people would say they are expensive but paying 14.00 for a cheesesteak in cali is expensive. I have heard that this place has been offered different services that would be cheaper for them but they will not change service or vendors if it compromises there product. Thank you for sticking to your high level of quality.

If you love burgers you have to try Five Guys!
Great burgers with lots of toppings at no extra charge.  The fries are cooked in Peanut Oil and they are really good, especially the cajun ones! The place is pretty simple.  Burgers are wrapped in foil, fries are put in a regular cup and everything goes in a brown paper bag! Simple but very tasty!  This is my favorite CC burger place!

Good, not as racist as Geno's. In comparison to Geno's it's greasier and less salty. So it's up to you which of the dueling Philly Cheesesteaks you want to get. I prefer to get Cheesesteaks elsewhere.

This place is definitely the best place for Philly cheese steak. We went to Geno's before and it was a disappointment. Pats was great the bread was fresh and the steak juicy. And they have great selection in chooses when it come to cheese steaks.

Mom and Pops style. Probably the best pretzels we've had in Philly! We had the cinnamon covered pretzels fresh out fo the oven. It was warm and buttery with the perfect amount of cinnamon. A must try if you're strolling through Manayunk. Great prices too!

LOVED that they had a sign with directions of how to order a cheesesteak for tourists. My friends and I partook in this Pat's and  Geno's cheesesteak challenge. Between the two, I'd have to say Pat's won it for me.  The meat was seasoned much better and chopped up more (which is how I like it), but the onions were more on the raw side. I left the intersection feeling unsatisfied on this quest to try a real Philly cheesesteak. 

If you get a chance and are searching for really good cheesesteak, try Jim's Steaks on South St. I enjoyed it MUCH better.
Fast service hot food but I was expecting a better cheese stake  meat needs more flavor cheese wiz was good . I like to have the same flavor all through my sandwich
Good cheesesteak, classic Philly experience. I like Geno's better.
Way over priced, unfriendly service, and the meat was a little dry and lacked flavor. Kind of a tourist trap. Kind of fun if you're a tourist ;)

Overrated, i dont think locals go here

Just plain does not taste that good, beef is a little thick, slightly tough, and lacks flavor, rather than thin and tasty - not impressed at all. Provolene cheese is fine.

There was a line but itmoves decently fast

For the price and the hype, this was not terrible but it was certainlh disappointing, i dont plan on returning. 

I do think its worth visiting once just to ssy youve been there.

Pats is slightly better than genos due to meat quality.

Absolutely overrated and overpriced!!! Their food is terrible! The burgers are so greasy and they fries are always soggy and never crispy! I don't think that it is worth the money for this burger and fries. If $10.00 is worth it to all these people spending that, then there is a problem. You can go to the market and buy some ground beef, and potatoes, and you have a better and cheaper meal!

Why can't I give 1/2 stars? This establishment deserves 1 and 1/2 stars. The food was pedestrian, the service was dreadfully slow, and a few of the servers appeared to be either drunk and/or high. The rocks lazily spread across the ground in the outdoor seating area is simply a mistake. Dust and dirt were all over my legs and shoes.  I also could not help but notice the staff's dress code appeared to be "wear whatever the fuck you want." I would like to think I'm not the pretentious type, but when it's $20 per entree, I expect a little more for my money. It's sad because this place used to be pretty cool.

Simply amazing. I came here still tipsy after a Flyers game at the Wells Fargo Center after they handed the Buffalo Sabres an appropriate beatdown. I got one with wiz and grilled onions, and another with provolone. Both were delicious but I LOVED the wiz/wit one. But just saying their provolone cheese was rich with flavor, so so good. Recommend trying both. Would go back after every Flyers game. I plan to make this a tradition. Beer. Flyers. Pat's. You cannot do better. Also: the cheese fries were so hot and delicious. You should get some with your steak. Staff was friendly too but I was so focused on my sandwich and fries on the walk back to the car. What a night.

The hype happens to be just that- hype. I went to Pat's for the first time last night as part of a graduation party. Their menu style is the hack, no-bullshit, cash only, if you don't know what you want, then leave type. Very assholelish, but whatever. I ordered  a mushroom pepper cheesesteak (explicit name of menu item) wit it  (aka with onions- this is a menu rule), and I said cheese wiz, please to clarify. They placed my steak on the counter: it was steak and cheese only. I stood there thinking it wasn't mine, but was told it was mine. The only thing they got right was the cheese. No onions, no pepper, no mushrooms. They were an upcharge btw. I notified the guy at the register (seemed to be owner/manager) and he told me that they were on there. I took the steak and fingered through  it. Nothing was  there. They finally added my toppings after bothering them enough. Terrible place. Overpriced ($11 total). Please don't go. They fooled me once; never again.

Red and green salsa: yum! 
Guac: ok
Mahi mahi tacos: meh. Passable but not great
Margaritas: I pretty sure they just filled a pitcher with ice and sour mix. We kept drinking it to see if it would improve but alas down 1 pitcher between two people and we were still stone cold sober but then on a sugar high. We crashed about 30 minutes later. 

We were really looking forward to coming here, but we were soooo disappointed! Literally, it was the worst margarita I've ever had. I don't even think it could be considered a margarita. It was simply ice and sour mix. I would have preferred one of those pre-mixed margaritas that you can get in a liquor store. Disgusting. Never again.

I have only heard stories about Pat's from my girlfriend who lived in Philly while going to grad school, so on our visit through Philly, we went.  I was very interested in trying this "hype."  So, we tried the original cheese steak with onions and whiz.

As I was in line at Pat's, my girlfriend was in line at Geno's across the street.  We both waited in line and met about the same time.  What I could not believe was that it was hot hot hot out, 95 degrees and sweltering.  For a Sunday at 2:30pm, I could not believe what I was actually waiting in line for, a sandwich.

When we both met back up, with both sandwiches, we did a taste test between the two.  I thought Geno's was better, slightly, I could barely tell the difference.  Truthfully, Geno's and Pat's tasted the same to me as an outsider from Denver, CO.  My girlfriend liked Pat's better.

Personally, I think the hype is much more popular than the food and everything has just blown up.  I've heard locals tell me that the bar between the two is better than both Pat's OR Geno's.

It was a good lunch, but I'm not sure I would ever wait more than five minutes for either again.

Out of the three big tourist cheese steak places (Pat's, Geno's, and Jim's) in the Philly area Pat's is truly the King.  It has the best tasting cheese steak which is fueled by great options and the most flavorful/ steak.  It also has the most options for your sandwich.

My personal choice is the pepper cheese steak with provolone.

If you can only make one cheese steak joint I highly recommended Pat's.

Since Geno's and Pat's were right next to each other, my friends and I decided to try them both. We first went to Geno's and got a cheesesteak with provolone, and then went to Pat's and got the cheesesteak with cheese whiz. I guess if we were really doing to do a taste test contest, we should have gotten the same things on both- oh well.
In any case, Pat's was by far the better of the two. The meat was more flavorful than Geno's and the bread was soft and delicious. The peppers that they had on the side were the perfect accompaniment for the sandwich.  Their fries were also pretty tasty. 
I also thought the workers seemed nicer than Geno's.  The Geno's workers just plain scared me.  And although the workers at Pat's didn't seem all that friendly either, no one yelled at me when I fumbled with my cash (oops, I didn't have my money ready in advance... but I didn't expect a spontaneous fry order). 
Overall, as far as cheesesteak places go, I give Pat's a 4 star because it's the best of the 3 places I've been too.

Tell 'em the cheese type and wit or wit-out (onions), they already know you're getting a steak sandwich genius!  

I always get a WIZ WIT!

Don't even think about going to that other place across the street.  

Best to come here after a night of drinking.
Really disappointing tourist trap. I've actually tasted better cheesesteaks in chains. Meat was dry, entire cheesesteak was relatively flavorless.
Doesn't always open on time (7am). Not terrible for smoothies (the Bee Stinger is my favorite) but it's not the best. It's a good healthy option for a train station though.

Pat's King of Steaks makes my favorite Philly cheese steak. Yes, it is a tourist trap, and yes, every since person who lives within 20 miles of the place will tell you not to go there and name off 5 places that make a better cheese steak. BUT, it is still my favorite. 

Nothing can beat the atmosphere, the red metal picnic tables, and of course the food. Here's what you need to know:

- Know your order, when you get to the register they move FAST
- The first window is for cheese steaks only, you can order fries and drinks by sliding down to the second window
- Have cash, they don't take credit or debit
- Be ready to spend at least $10 (Cheese Wiz without is $10 flat)
- Get the cheese wiz, I know it sounds gross but it's really delicious
- The steaks here are thinly shredded, unlike their competition across the street who serves a thicker cut of meat
- You can ask for your cheese steak to go, they'll wrap it up nicely 
- Be ready to stand in line if you go at a peak time; this goes beyond just tradition lunch and dinner, be ready for long lines after any Philadelphia sports game.

Luckily didn't have to stand in a long line due to the weather.  I got the sandwich with cheese whiz and onions and it was pretty good.  While I would never eat cheese whiz for any other reason, I think it's the best bet for a cheese steak.  Was hoping to be yelled at by the order taker for my lack of ordering expertise, but he was really nice. All in all, I would go back.

Pat's verse Geno's? 

Service is no good.  Geno's is better.

Steak is OK, but Geno's is softer.

Topping ...  well Pat's has more choices and I do like that more than Geno's.

Not great...definitely not worth making a trip to south philly from center city!!
Still do not understand why is this place so popular given that it offers a 'not-so-great' cheese steak in the same city which is world famous for cheese steaks!!!

This place is awesome. I went here on Labor Day weekend with a couple of friends. We sat in the outside area, and although we had to wait a looooong time for seating, it was worth it. The outside area isn't very big, but it does the trick. There were six of us so we ordered two pitchers of margaritas one frozen one not. They were both great and blended perfectly. I ordered the Mexican Cobb salad for my entree. It was all types of delicious. Everyone else got tacos or quesadillas and they were all happy with their choice! The inside area is really dim, and the bar area is kind of small. 

The only thing I would say is I wouldn't recommend coming on a Saturday night as I have tried before and it was so packed we got overwhelmed and left.

Pat's is the King of Cheese-Steaks. I have to give the edge to Pat's because is all done right. The meat is hot and fresh. The toping are over the top. The taste leaves you wanting one more. You can not beat the amount of good stuff in this sandwich. A must see & try place in south Philadelphia.

Decent cheesesteak. Super greasy. Some grease to be expected, it adds flavor! But it should not be squirting our all over the place every time you take a bite. It's a must for tourist which is cool, it's a historical place. But there are better cheesesteaks in the city.

Went to this McDonalds today around 12 Noon,through the drive thru.I ordered two(2) sweet teas with lemon,and a SouthWest Salad.

Drove around to pick up my order,and I was told that I only ordered the SouthWest Salad.Wow.

The manager informs me that I had to drive back through the drive thru,in order to re order the teas,but I refused.

The young lady that took my order was not attentive at all to my needs,and this was the reason why my two sweet teas,were not included in my order.

Bad attitudes need to stay at home,when you are serving customers,bottom line.

i am so glad, that when i went there was a group of kids split up between pats and genos, most went to genos so there was actually some place to sit. so we picked pats to try first. 
thankfully no line so we ordered like total rookies and messed it up and the guy just laughed at us and smiled. 3 words.... it was like mind blowing lol. but he did tell us to 'enjoy' after thanking him when we got the food ((unlike genos))
the meat, small but it had flavor, wasnt dry but wasnt overly moist, and i just wanted a touch more cheese seemed like the middle of my cheese steak was perfect while the ends dry. 
and it travels well !!!!!!!!!!!! went to ny and the bread wasnt even soggy, while genos went across the street to the car and the bun was soaking wet and we had to toss it before finishing.

i pick pats!

What is with the negative reviews of this place?

It's a lot like the other cheese steak places in Philadelphia. You can't find it different from those places. Remember people this is Philadelphia, the KING of CHEESE STEAKS so of course there will be a lot of places that taste great. 

Don't expect something unique or out-of-this-world taste and that's what makes this place and once again a lot of other places great. It's a simple recipe with fresh meat.

You won't be overwhelmed nor underwhelmed. You just have to try Pat's for the rich history.
Shift leader didn't ask what kind of tacos I wanted had an attitude when I mentioned that.

I live near this place and I've been many times. I always enjoy my meal and also the margaritas. Most recently, I tried the spiced pear margarita which was an excellent choice for the fall! So delicious! The guac here is excellent! Always well seasoned. I also enjoy the complementary salsas. Generally, always consistently good and starts my meal off right.  Be aware that if you order the nachos appetizer that they are delicious but HUGE! 
The mushroom and jack empanadas are another favorite of mine. As far as entrees go, I'm a big fan of the fajitas. Always lots of food and the meat is very well seasoned I just tried their chicken tacos for the first time which were just the right amount of spicy. There is 3 per order. 

Lastly, I would like to mention that the tres leeches cake there is the best I've ever had. It was perfectly moist. If you still have room, definitely order it.

Service is always very friendly and informal but attentive, which makes me feel very relaxed. I look forward to coming back here. My only complaint is that I find the acoustics here to be terrible which I'm sure is intentional but can be very frustrating and when they're busy I'm more inclined to go somewhere else along Passyunk avenue so I can hear the person or people I'm with.
It was fine the bread is great. However the cheese wiz wasn't melted enough and I could hardly taste the mushroom. The meat was also a little hard too bite
This is my favorite Cheesestake place in the city.  The food was good enough to outweigh the rude service and over priced food.

So I was all amped up about going to Gooey Looies about a mile away for one of their overstuffed cheesesteaks that have gotten rave reviews from the locals... So long story short Gooey's was closed and a short drive later I'm at Pat's........... Am I stoked and super grateful that Gooeys was closed? Um, well at first I was, there was none of the much talked about dreadful line, the weather was nice and the atmosphere? Classic Philly charm. 
 
 As for the ordering regime it was fairly basic for me, as follows: With/whiz/ the end, I'm not  fan of anarchy ordering practices or being shouted at for improper ordering but it's efficient and keeps things moving along. About 15 seconds later my cheesesteak arrives as ordered, I sit on my picnic style table loaded cheesesteak in hand and dive into it like I'm heading to the chair. The meat was a little chewy, slightly bland, meaty tasting and somewhat tender, needed salt, bread was ultra fresh, Whiz was Whiz..... Onions undercooked and I burped them up for about 10 hours even after several Pepcid AC's. 

 Overall the atmosphere is fantastic, the locals are amazing, the working class feel of the location was epic, the cheesesteak it's so well known for? A bit mediocre, sorry Pat's I'm a little bummed the Gooey's was closed, doesn't mean I won't be coming back; just not as good as I had hoped and dare I say tourist trap?

Delicious cheese steaks!! I read a lot of good reviews and decided to try this place. I was torn between their competitors accross the street. Great choice, will come back! Only downside is that they dont accept credit cards.
Margaritas are fantastic here, favorite is the guava. The food is reliable and good, with enough vegan options. It's hard not to fill up on the free chips. Pricey though!

I try to limit my visits to Five Guys because I can literally feel my arteries clogging as I eat my wonderful little bacon cheeseburger ("little" meaning just one patty instead of Five Guys' standard two). 

The free peanuts are a plus, and the Cajun fries are the bomb dot com.

Pats is awesome. Simple cheese steak that leaves you full and happy. I could eat two ! :) they're the best. I don't know why people on yelp are critiquing them so closely. It's a cheese steak, not filet mignon. Anyway I've been coming for years and every time I visit they are the same, delicious. They are very consistent with quality and deliciousness.

 And I'd take the steak over filet mignon any day.

Please come to california pats. There is no good cheese steak place ! :( 

Love pats!

Good sandwiches and friendly service.  The cheesesteaks, chicken cutlets and eggplant parms are reliable lunch fare.  I was really surprised by the Italian Tuna hoagie.  Rather than a standard tuna salad, it had tuna soaked in olive oil with onions and black olives.  Very impressive.  

One of the best lunch options in the no-man's land between Oregon and the Navy Yard, West of Broad.
I really recommend this restaurant, whether you are with a group of friends or your partner. Very good atmosphere, good food and good drinks!!

So glad I went to Pats for my first ever Cheesesteak!! If your visiting Philly there are so many choices but Pats is fantastic!!! Historic, Real Deal cheesesteak place!! The atmosphere made it worth finding a parking spot!! Warning CASH ONLY! Plenty of ATMs around though! There is also another place across the street, Genos, if you wanna try more than one.

horrible service slow making your food even when your the only car there. I hate this place one night after clubbing I.went through the drive through the manager Ron was rude and tried to rip me off. I order one thing and everything I ordered reflected my reciept Ron tried to tell me he gave me a discount and didnt charge me for everything but I charged me for everything but didnt give me all my items. when.I addressed him he told me to go away and have a drink. at that point I got angry and told him a piece of my mind. he was like fifty still working in a fast food restaurant really get a clue.never again I will take my money elsewhere
Way to expensive for ok Cheesesteak.  Living on its reputation.  There are literally hundreds of places better, and for less money.

I think I was excited to eat at a place that is considered one of the best Philly steak sandwiches in Philly.
Kinda disappointed.  Just very average and I thought over priced.  $12 for just the sandwich?  Really.  Didn't even give you a small cup for any condiments.  
Bummer to waste a meal and the drive down for this.  There has got to be better examples of a Philly steak sandwich somewhere else.  
These guys have been open since 1930!  Take only cash!  Use your imagination on that.

Came here due to there reputation and was slightly disappointed. Seems as though the competition has caught up with them and exceeded them. I still enjoyed my visit, but it was more like going to see a historic site. In this case I was going to see the history of cheese steaks past. 

If you're a cheese steak fanatic that wants a taste of history, than by all means make sure to visit this place. If you want the best cheese steak in Philly, there are other competitors within driving distance that do it better.

over rated.  Sometimes pats is a 5, sometimes its a 4, other times its an abysmal one.  Went last week and had to give it a 3.  Bread as usual, is great.  Its fast, so thats also good.  But the meat is so dry as its just sitting on a huge pile of cooked meat losing its flavor as its evaporating away.

I have eaten here and also visited with several large groups. I agree that the service can been less than satisfactory, hence the trio of stars. 
That being said, Franz is the man - super nice guy and he will take good care of you. hopefully he gets bumped up into the role of bartender or manager soon, in light of their recent staffing "changes"... he deserves it, having handled our large groups with ease and good humor. 
The food is generally pretty damn good as well. Franz gets 4 stars, the food 4 as well, but unfortunately the rest of the staff brings down the house ... not in a good way.

My fiancé and I stopped here while in the city during our road trip at the end of April 2017.

I had seen Pat's on TV, of course, and I was surprised that it is found at a normal-sized intersection - the area looks a lot bigger and more open on TV. Be prepared to park a decent distance away and walk through a quasi-shady neighborhood. 

The restaurant is everything it appears to be. Service is very quick, but check your order before you leave because I didn't want onions and got them anyway. We were lucky and didn't have to wait in a long line. The food was good, and I enjoyed Pat's chopped steak (despite the onions) more than a certain other establishment across the road. I would've given four stars if it weren't for the fact that I got onions when I specifically asked for a sandwich without them. It's also fun to eat at one of the cheesesteak establishments I had seen on TV (there's nothing wrong with acting like a tourist sometimes, especially when you are one).

It's just one of those things you have to try! :-)

I gotta give Pat's a 4 just off the strength of the MEAT, the WIZ (which oozes so beautifully), and the speed of service. The bread and onions were fine too. It's no time or reason to bullshit and small talk. Take your order and it'll be ready in less than a minute. This place is a staple for a reason. The food is solid. Nothing out of this world in terms of seasoning and flavorfulness but the actual meat is actually very quality and plentiful. Only downside to me really is the price. I wish I didn't have to spend $20 to a cheesesteak, fries and a drink but I understand it.

Not saying it's the best cheesesteak in Philly but it's definitely worth trying at least once. It's a fun experience anyway being in South Philly and seeing Pat's and Geno's right across from each other.

For fast food, five guys is really good.  Very reasonably priced, yummy, fresh  burgers with very fresh toppings, and about as cheap as burger king.  Great fries too!

And despite that there is ALWAYS a line out the door, they move very fast, and get you in and out in no time.

I honestly don't know why this place doesn't have 5 stars. I'm not even a big fan of philly steaks but I knew I had to try while visiting. This place does not disappoint!!! Honestly, I've never had a philly steak taste SO DAMN good. Excuse my caps, I get very excited when I find an amazing food spot. And this was definitely it. So good in fact, that I came here the next night and ordered even more than the night before. It's your typical philly steak sandwich that you've had the imitations before, but never really knew how exactly it should taste. Steak, cheese, onions on bread. Bread was amazing and so was the meat. Everything was amazing honestly. I couldn't put the sandwich or the cheese fries down. 

Also, I tried Gino's as well. 100 times better at Pats. I was legit mad cause I wasted a few bites at Gino's instead of Pats. 

Oh philly, I miss the hell out of your good food.
Everytime I come back to my old stomping ground I make sure to visit Pat's and Geno's. It's always Pat's for the win.

We meandered over to the Pat's sign with the neon crown, but when I saw the line, I felt very discouraged. Luckily, the line moved fairly quickly. As a non-local, I didn't bother to learn the nomenclature; wiz, wit, whatever, but the people working there didn't seem to give us or the other patrons in line a hard time about that. Why make a simple menu complicated?
All the sandwiches are around $10. I tried a cheesesteak with a little cheese whiz, peppers, and onions. The sandwich itself was not bad, but I just don't think I am someone who craves cheese steak sandwiches. Also, I think chopped steak is a little tough. Luckily, the bread had a little crunch to it, which I like. Good bread is important to a sandwich. 
The downside is there was only outdoor seating, which was not great for a hot day. Also, they only accept cash, which I think is inconvenient and doesn't speak positively to a longstanding sandwich spot that probably has high margins and high volume.

Had Pat's and Gino's and liked Pat's overall. The steak was better and easier to eat plus there are more places to sit. I did like the bread at Gino's. I know their not known for their fries but get them! Plus you can't go wrong with a place that's in Rocky!

I really like everything about this place except that I think the margaritas are watered down. I've heard many other people say this too. It's annoying to spend 7-8 bucks a drink and not feel there's much alcohol in it. I sort of stopped coming here because of it. I've split pitchers here with one other person on many occasions and walked away feeling like it was a waste of money.
My favorite Cheese steak place in Philly. Nuff said.
My boyfriend and I love this place. We go there all the time. Great tacos, the chorizo tacos are my favorite, and fantastic margaritas. Its a great friday night date place.

Geno's is better!!

Sure sure some people will want to kill me for this but.. sorrt Pat's.. your steak was gross. 

It was my first time in Philly and as a huge foodie (I hate when people say that but...it gets the point across) I had to take the Cheesesteak challenge. 

One night we went out and had half of each, pats and Geno's. Pat's failed epically: the bun was dry, the meat was not flavorful or juicy. 

basically it can be summed up as such: Bleh

No chicken nuggets and no lettuce when we stopped by for lunch. And rude service to top it all off  it is the holiday season and I'm sure they've had a long day but damn girl, no need for the attitude. 


Update: 
I got a call apologizing for the incident and the person who made the call was extremely nice.

Came into Philadelphia and really wanted to have a genuine Philly Cheesesteak. After a great deal of research, I landed on Pat's and I have to say I was not disappointed!

I opted for a cheesesteak - provolone "wit-out" onions. The service was fast and the food was hot and fresh. Great cuts of steak were included in the sandwich and the bread was soft and acted as a great compliment to the sandwich. 

If I had to do it all over again, I'd probably get it with the onions, because I did find myself wanting another flavor included,  but overall, it was spectacular!

I wanted to take my fiancé for an authentic cheesesteak while in Philly, so why not get the original cheesesteak?  I was very disappointed that we trekked across town for this.  There wasn't any flavor in the meat or the onions.  They don't offer any sautéed peppers or other toppings that I'm used to.  It was a very bland sandwich.  Next time, we're searching for the best cheesesteak in Philly rather than the oldest.

What kind of sell out would I be if I didn't write a review in my hometown, Philadelphia?  :)

With that said, if you ever decide to do the hop and a skip away for cheesesteaks in the city of cheesesteaks, PAT'S is it!  Don't be fooled by the neon lights and celebrity photo hangings across the street at Geno's, PAT'S is where it's at!  Don't believe me?  Get one of each and witness the faceoff for yourself.  

With that said, getting the cheesesteak could be more of a challenge than finding the place (if you're from out of town).  My personal favorite is the original "cheese wiz, wit", which rougly translates to "I'd like a cheese steak, with cheese wiz, with saltee onions, please".  

If there's one catalyst for the fame of the "Philly Cheesesteak", it's the CHEESE WIZ.  Trust me, this is cheese wiz at its best and all you provolone, cheddar, non-cheesey folks need to give it a shot cuz honestly, when else do you get to have cheese wiz compared to all the other cheeses?  

In sum, Pat's the KING OF STEAKS, which is pretty self-explainatory.  And my golly, I'll be queen to that throne anyday!....

I see the appeal of this place but I suggest it only if:

a.) you are trying to gain weight as quickly as possible and drinking bacon shakes just isn't cutting it

b.) you are immortal and your arteries have some sort of self-clearing system

or 

c.) you love punishment

Seriously, I ate here and the next day felt hung over from my body having to process all the grease.  The service wasn't all that great either, even by Philly food service standards.  Don't get me wrong, it was an indulgence and kind of a tasty one at that but I don't think I could eat the food again knowing that the next day I'll feel sick.

I love Blaze Pizza! They have a wide variety of fresh, high quality toppings that you can combine in near endless combinations. The crust is thin, crispy on the outside but chewy on the inside with the perfect amount of bite, and super flavorful. Prices are reasonable for what you get and I would highly recommend Blaze to anyone.

This is the best cheesesteak place in Philly. I have been coming here since I was 5 years old. There is something about the place that is just amazing. I love standing in the street waiting for the line to move so I can get a wiz wit. If you know what that means. If not they send you to the back of the line. The line can be quite long. Anyone that visits must try here. This place is an icon.
Rude employee. Vegetable is not fresh. The lady who prepared the sandwich acted like she didn't like the work. The vege is definitely not fresh. By far the worst subway experience.

FOOD: Definitely hits the spot!   I wish they made the food upon order so the meat would be more fresh.   The bread was amazing and the cheese was just right.  

SERVICE:  They were super nice and no wait for the food.
Going to a game, after a game, later into the night, just driving on 95 near exit 20: all the right time to go to pats.  They live up to the name King of Steaks.

4 stars even though I didn't really like my cheesesteak. I've only had fake "Philly cheesesteaks" in other parts of the country, so I had to try the real thing and was told to come here. I got the real thing and didn't like it. Mainly the steak, which was dry and bland to me. The fries were damn good. The collection of people milling around the outside was pretty entertaining... a nice mix of high school students, workers, businessmen and Japanese tourists. By the end of the meal, I decided that I don't really like cheesesteak but that Philly's a cool town.
Overall mediocre food. Pat's and Geno's are both overrated. The lesser of the 2 evils is Pat's. Don't waste a trip to Philly.

Terrible customer service, I've given this place 3 tries before my review, food was cold and half open in the bag when purchased, beans were cold cheese wasn't even melted. Have the taco meat and condiments were out of the shell into the bag. I understand it's cheap fast food but come on, the employees are high and don't know what the word thank you is, it seems you have to beg for an answer.

A fun and delicious spot, I am always down for the Cantina. Best margaritas in town, awesome nachos and tacos. I love that the menu has more variety than many Mexican places, like friend plantains and queso fresco and pork empanadas. The tacos are real Mexican style, soft corn tortilla with your choice of filling, plus cilantro, onion and a slice of lime. You can add the extras like cheese and sour cream if you're so inclined. My only complaint would be that it's way too noisy!

Tourist trap!  

If you've made it this far, then you've probably already decided that you're going to do the touristy thing and see the lights. Well, at least you're here instead of across the street. Pat's is the better of the two evils in my book. I've said it before: "Geno's, has the better fries while Pats across the street is the king of (very average) cheese steaks."

There are better steaks out there but if you want the experience to cross it off your bucket list, then by all means. I'd say you should go to Tony Luke's. 

Parking is a mess and the lines for steaks can stretch long. Never fear though, the line moves quickly since they're making food in bulk. It comes out immediately as you pay.

The steaks are far smaller than most in town which was disappointing. 

Cash only!

"One wiz without". Line seemed long, but it moved really fast! Have  your money and order ready when you arrive at the window. Great cheesesteak. My stomach enjoyed every bite! Hopefully willl visit again.

Amazing pretzels. This isnt one of those places you stumble upon accidentally. You have to be looking for it to find it and even then you might drive past a few times before you see the little sign on the side of the building leading you into a gravel parking lot of what looks to be a small industrial yard. You kind of feel like you are going to a shady drug deal when you pull into the lot, but trust me it is totally worth it. It is run but a really sweet guy who tells everyone who comes in "call me when you are on your way, I'll make them so they're ready when you get here." While, I've never taken him up on this offer, there is never a long a wait and the pretzels are delicious. 

Get in the car.... or on your bike and go right now. 
And try the cinnamon ones... they are fantastic.
Great tourist spot. My bread seemed a little stale but I loved the meat and cheese. It is cash only!!

I love Pat's!!  I took a break from my mad moving rush to try the dueling cheesesteaks.  Pat's was the first one we went to.  We ordered and received our sandwich within seconds.  It had a generous amount of cheese and was delish!! Even in the rain, people were eating outside and living it up.  Fun time, good sandwich!

Pats Steaks is "Way Over Rated" I cant believe I have to give it a one star.  I ate a cheesesteak about 2 months ago because my Bro-in-Law forced six of us to go there for his birthday.  Well, the cheesesteak was dry no flavor - the condiments are outside in jars where all the lovely flies and insects can get to them. The cheesesteak meat was cool so it couldnt of been just cooked .  I didnt even finish the garbage. I have no Idea why people still want to go to this place still.  Please dont think this is what a philly steak should taste like.  I also ate there about 7 years ago and same results.  I thought they would correct there problems but people keep coming so why bother.  You are what you eat.   I recommend Tony Luke - Prince of Steaks or any place but here.

I love going to this place for lunch. Getting a meaty and juicy burger with unlimited toppings is awesome. Getting basically a bag full of fries is also a plus, and that is a regular size. I also enjoy munching on the free peanuts before I get my order. This is hand downs one of my favorite places to get a burger.
Traveling thru from Cleveland so we had to check out LBJ's spot. Great food, quick service, and good atmosphere with all of the college students.
Food not only APPEARED hot and fresh but they also gave me NAPKINS (without me asking for them)! wow!

I like when my burgers have a thicker meat, but the sandwich here was very good. The bacon bits were perfectly toasted and you get to choose from a bunch of toppings. The fries are awesome, clearly made fresh, not the frozen thing you get in most places. Overall a very good burger.
Had a delightful meal and a pitcher of margaritas on a beautiful fall day. The service was great...out waiter could not have been kinder! The three amigos enjoyed food, fun and secrets!

I used to say the only thing this place had going for them was their guava mojitos and their banging ass corn on the cob... however, things have improved.  When I would go to the Cantina I couldn't help but notice that their "too cool for school" staff seemed to serve each dish and drink with a great deal of smugness and pretense, but those days are over.  The staff was down to earth, and just plain nice; the food was fabulous; and their Sangrita is to die for.  The Bethany officially says this place is A-OK!

I am a fan of Cantina Los Caballitos.  They're easily one of my favorite places to grab food when I'm visiting friends in Philly. You will find a fun, friendly atmosphere here with some damn good Mexican food and drinks. 

They are very resonably priced. Most food items on the menu are under $10 and they come in big portions, they are also not skimpy on the toppings. Their chicken nachos are so good. I wish I had a plate of them in front of me as I'm typing this review.  

As for their drinks you can score a pitcher of frozen margaritas (about 6 or so glasses) for only $22. They are not watered down either. I had about 3 and was sitting quite right; They margaritas got me right together honey!  

Cheap food with big portions, cheap strong alcholic beverages, and a fun friendly atmosphere. Cantina Los Caballitos has it all. What more could you ask for?

3 out of 5 stars seems to indicate a positive review. Given the option, I'd go 5 of 10. 

The good: Atmosphere - this includes outdoor only. Airy, comfortable, nice neighborhood intersection. Specialty drinks - mojitos & margaritas (specifically the blood orange) are very good. Chips with salsa - simple, but effective.

The bad: Food is adequate, at best. Decent, but nothing I've had has been worth recommending to anyone except for the Cabrito, only because it's not often I see goat on a menu.

And the ugly: Service - Slow, inattentive, very long wait time between table visits. As good as the specialty drinks are, I've NEVER had a cold beer there. Inside seating feels like being in a head lock from a large, sweaty person - hot & stuffy.

Overall, I'll agree to go here if in a rare mood, yet I'd never mention it if asked for a suggestion. If it weren't for the outdoor seating, this would easily get a solid 2 star rating.

We went here on a nice day, arrived late for lunch, and obviously they had been swamped, most tables were still full.  So the service was a little on the slow side, but it didn't make us antsy.  Perhaps the nice weather helped, we were sitting outside.  I have sat outdoors to dine many times, but today I could literally lean over and put my shoulder on the SUV parked next to our table.  Ah yes, we were definitely in the city!

The chips looked and tasted homemade, and they give you two salsas, the classic red and the tomatillo.  A very nice touch, and both were flavorful.  We ordered the tortilla salads, one steak and one chicken.  Both were great, just the right amount of spice and lime.  Add to that the reasonable prices and we had a delightful time.
Thank you for being open on the weekends! Your hardworking staff feeds many of us who have to work upstairs in the lab on weekends, when all other shops around the hospital are closed.

Never got a bad burrito here!
Awesome place.
You can customize your order, order ahead, and pick it up.
Fast and Good Food.

Generally excellent hard working wait staff and atmosphere and food quality!  Went twice: 1st time was indoors for lunch (excellent knowledgeable waitress and another waitress also displayed a fine attitude and personality) and then again for dinner outdoors.  Indoors is better than outdoors since you could hear the music and I think the service is better there too.  One of the outside waitresses, the red hair one, who was not mine so I couldn't even reduce her tip, made some mistakes which affected my table.  First she brought out 8 glasses of ice water for people who weren't even at the restaurant yet right next to my table of 2 that was eating chips and hot sauce without the benefit of any water to drink.  When I spoke to her about it she acted dumb and rude about it instead of professional.  Then later when my son's napkin fell onto the gravel floor, she quickly bent down, scooped it up before he could, threw it away, and did not bring him another napkin!  Was this her way of getting even for the water problem?

great drinks and endless chips. but they recently shrunk the size of their salads significantly which sucks because that used to be my go-to entree with added protein. the salads sadly come on the same size plate they used to, so they arrive looking like an afterthought. tacos are ok, but pretty measly unless you pay for enough add-ons.

Agree with many reviewers here. Went here a few days ago during my first visit to Philadelphia because of the history of the establishment; however, the  steak sandwich is no big deal. The price for sodas and fries is ridiculous. Glad I went but never again.

I really don't see what the big deal is, especially for $10 each. I've tried a few different cheesesteaks in Philly and this place, along with Geno's, were the worst. 
I suggest saving your money and time and go someplace else. 
However, I liked the bread.
In summary, it's overpriced, lacks flavor, and parking is a nightmare. 
Reading terminal has better options.

This place makes me just about as happy as a restaurant can.  I am guilty of trying to find just about any reason to drag friends, family, aquaintences etc. in there.

If you get a nice seat in the bar, be prepared to hang out a bit.  Its not a wise choice for a quick bite... but its a nice place to be left alone to enjoy.

The atmosphere is par for the course in an nicer mexican restaurant.  You can go in jeans and a t-shirt with friends that superglue their hair... or dress it up and bit and go with your mom... and still not feel out of place.  Its such a versatile restaurant.

The margaritas are what captured my heart.  Prickley Pear, Blood Orange, Raspberry, Tangerine etc. or the basic Lime... they're as good as margaritas get.  And you can get them in pitchers too... which spells trouble in the best possible way.

They give you chips and 2 kinds of salsa to munch on.  At first look, the salsa appears to be a bust, but upon closer investigation, the salsa verde is the perfect blend of spicy and zippy.  I could eat it with a spoon- forget the chips!

Then comes the food- the Nachos will change your life.  I'm a vegetarian, and the faux-beef option is genius.  They're delicious.  If I split these with a friend, I tend to be down for the count... but when I skip the nachos, i heart the seitan and tofu fajitas.  They'll feed you AT LEAST twice.  

This place is where its at.  I'm so proud that its so close to home!

Visited here and Geno's on two separate trips to Philadelphia.

Had Cheese Whiz and Onions on mine...wasn't sure how I was gonna feel about the Whiz but it was actually pretty good.  The meat was perfectly cooked and the onions were caramelized and sweet. 

Bread was nice and soft but sturdy enough to handle the meat. Also, the staff there were not douchebags like they were at Geno's.

It tasted especially good since it was 11 o'clock at night. Yum!
Tourist trap.  Big chunks of fatty, gristle filled "beef", but don't worry because there is much more bread than meat.  Go to Tony Lukes.
They have really good food and margaritas, but the servers are so rude I've given up on this place. It's not worth it.

Went on October 5,got there about 11:30am,service quick.Had the original,with onions and mushrooms and cheese whiz,Trish had onions and American cheese.Sandwiches were not hot warm,F.F where ok, would I go back yes to try Geno's, My opinion Jersey Mike's has a better cheese steak.

Go at an off time to avoid the lines.. 

I find both Pat & Geno's highly overrated but I do suggest going at least once. Go with at least one friend and order the same items at each spot and share to compare! You'll probably get a few interesting looks and laughs haha  

These guys have gotten too commercialized.. I prefer the more momnpop hole in the wall feel. It seems like their are many less hyped but higher quality spots all over the city.. AND lots of places with vegetarian friendly options! My review is mostly based on going repeatedly with friends... and their reactions. 

But I have tried their cheese fries.. ultra processed cheese so you definitely need a fork to eat these babies.. so synthetic and bad.. but ooo so good all at the same time. I'm lucky I don't live in Philly.. they are like crack (not just at Pats but the cheese fries in general) 

I like the condiment bar.. it has that over Geno's! Although you could probably sneak over.. idk how kosher that is with the locals :P

(+) waited a total of 2 seconds for my order
(+) juicy steak, mouthwatering cheesewhiz, fresh bread

(-) intimidating cashier
(-) very greasy

Overall, I was satisfied with my cheesesteak! Pat's over Geno's!

Drove way outta my way to eat at the famous king of steaks. Hubs dropped me off so he can find a parking space. I called him a minute later to tell him to pick me up. He was shocked...."You're done?"

Theres a bunch of guys working like a well oiled machine to crank out these sandwiches. I decided to try their provolone cheesesteak. It was ok....bland. Needed more salt...hint hint. The cheese was bland...thus you need more flavor in your steak to counteract. I got everyone else the whiz which they all loved. In retrospect, I shoulda got that too. The whiz deserves 4 stars, but provolone gets 3 stars. I decided to give them an overall rating of 3 stars because when you order, it feels like the coldest conversation on earth. How about a smile? A how's it going ? Something! They want you in and they want you out....money is their game...not customer service. Hate to break it to you, but you need good food AND good service for a winning restaurant.

This is a nice space and has a great feel to it.  The staff was very friendly and courteous.

The food was far from good, however.  The chips were stale, the salsas were bland, the draft beer was warm, so I changed to a bottle.  

We ate lunch on a Sunday at around 1pm and the only offerings on the menu for lunch entrees were tacos, burritos and overpriced fajitas.  That's it! 3 choices. No enchiladas, chimichangas, tortas, tostadas...nothing.  Weird, right?

We started with the tuna ceviche listed on the special menu.  It had zero lime flavor.  I have never had ceviche without acid.  I thought that is what defines ceviche.

I had the wings appetizer..  They were actually decent.

I would never eat Mexican here again.  I will go hang out at the bar, however.  Good tequila and mezcal list, nice staff, good vibe.

My first visit to Cantina was pretty good a few years ago.  The food was good, the staff was friendly, and the drinks were great.  Unfortunately every subsequent visit got worse and worse and we just stopped going there.
I will admit that the food is pretty good, not great, but good.  The drinks used to be good, but now they seemed watered down and pretty boring.  Sitting outside on a warm evening is nice, too.
