The stocky jalapeños were a nice addition. Glad I didn't get charged for those. No line when I went. I'd try something different next time.

I read about Pat's on line and was recommended to me from a friend of mine that lived in the area.  I got off the airplane, rented my car and drove straight over on my way to work.  

I ordered a Steak and Provolone.  Dumped some Hot Sauce on it and went to town.

There might be better, but for me this was a decent cheesesteak.

Took a picture of the Sylvester Stalone plauqe and went along my way stuffed and happy.

Obviously, The KING.  Although perhaps not the most tender or highest quality cheesesteak in town it still reigns supreme.  
Best hours of operation anywhere, best wiz sauce of any establishment and their cheese fries are excellent.
The part i like the most when compared to any other steak places is the line aspect.  You may wait in line at pat's for a while but once you hit the window, order and pay you immediately receive your food.
Also, unlike Geno's, Pat's puts the wiz over the top of the steak meat so that the cheese cascades over the meat and entire sandwich.  This is the way to assemble the proper cheese steak, by putting the wiz on the roll like Genos the cheese is not well distributed and makes for a dry and less enjoyable sandwich.  
Lots of other good spots in town but when its 4 am and you have that jones for a cheesesteak there is no substitute.

Famous, but not sure why. 

Got the whiz wit.
-bread barely chewable
-steak underwhelming
-whiz bad

Had to load w ketchup to make edible.

Someone point me to the REAL King of Steaks!



**Pat's would get 1 star if I could give Gino's 0.

Tried Pat's when I first moved to Philadelphia to experience the whole cheese steak craze. I will admit it was a tasty cheese steak, however I became extremely ill a few hours after eating the sandwich. So ill that I had a fever for a night and was sweating profusely in my sleep. I have a pretty strong iron stomach but this one really took it out of me :( I'm not sure if this was a bad day at Pat's or if this is the regular quality of the food. Either way, I won't be visiting this Philly landmark anytime soon.

Stick to Jim's Steaks or John's Roast Pork.

Pat's King of Steaks is one the best places to get a Philly Cheese Steak.  Though I don't have a lot of experience with Cheese Steak, I do believe that the Authenticity of this place enhances the dining experience.  There is no coddling of the patrons as they are serious when you aren't prepared to know your order and you have quite a bit of time in line to figure it out...with instructions!  Rude?  Not at all, it's all part of the experience.  The food is good but not memorable.  The meat is slightly bland with condiments an absolute necessity.  Overall, tasty and fun experience.

Whoever gave either Pat's or Geno's 5 stars have obviously never dined at the Great Steak and Potato Co. at any mall's food court. I'm convinced that the only people who eat cheesesteaks in Philly are tourists. It's similar to how people who live in Chicago never eat deep dish pizza unless a friend is visiting. 

These sandwiches were overpriced and mediocre at best. The meat was dry and the only enjoyable quality was the dousing of cheese whiz. The outdoor seating sucked any remaining heat from our souls. 

I will give my obligatory opinion that I thought Pat's was much better than Geno's. Also points to the cashier for calling my friend "doll" in a deep Philadelphian accent.

The burgers here are so greasy it hurts.  Maybe I'm just getting old, but I find it kind of gross.  The fries were nothing special, either -- I don't get the hype about this place at all.  I'll save my cheeseburger allowance for the Fatburger that's opening in University City instead.

UPDATE: 1. There are no longer plans to open a Fatburger in University City.  Tragedy.
2. I ate here again and the burger was much better and not very greasy at all.

Since I wrote about Geno's, I'll be fair and write about Pat's to urge you not to go there too, unless you're drunk at 4 am and get the late night munchies.  Even so, I'd rather have Lorenzo's pizza for late night feasting than this monstrosity.

I lived across the street from Pat's for 2 years and probably ate there twice, and was very much unimpressed.  The last straw for me was when I ran over there in the pouring rain to satisfy a cheese fries craving and the guy at the window said if I wasn't with the group of 70 people currently ordering, I would have to wait until their ENTIRE PARTY was finished ordering.  I vowed never to give them my business again, and found out later that J&J Pizza just up the street gave a huge portion of cheese fries for much cheaper.  They also have cheesesteaks there, but as I always say, Ishkabibbles is the place to go.

The assembly-line method of assembling cheesesteaks makes for seriously inconsistent products... Ishkabibbles makes each steak to order which takes longer but is worth it!

This place has the distinction of being the FIRST place I ever ate at when I first came to Philly. It was a block from my hotel and I was STARVING. I've come back a few times since, and they've consistently delivered a great tasting burger. 

They have a pretty big list of toppings you can add onto your burger, but I usually stick to mushrooms on the junior size (their larger burger is pretty big, it's nice they have that option). 

It gets pretty busy during the lunch hour, but I managed to spend less than 10 minutes in there start to finish with about a dozen people ahead of me.

Bring a wet-nap, and be careful, the bag tends to soak up the grease!

have tried cheesesteaks at many different philly joints - and have to say "I. LOVE. PATS"

The hot sauce is terrific and so are the little peppers.

Line gets long at times - especially after bars close.  but would get a Pats any day

Ok, so a good salad is harder to find than a good man.  The gold standard for me is the warm shrimp salad at Parc.  Well, the crab and avocado salad here at Cantina Los Caballitos rivalled it.  I also thought the salsas were fantastic.  The red salsa is smokey chipotle peppers; the green is rich with cilantro.  I didn't try enough of the menu to give it 5 starts, but for what I sampled, I was satisfied.
I'm sorry to say this, but the one I had was a little dry and not all that tender. Maybe it's because it's sliced thicker.
Worth the trip to experience an institution. It is not fine dining but it is the real taste of Philadelphia in all its glory!

What's a trip to Philly without a visit to the rivals on Passyunk? 

Before I start, I want to mention that I'm from Arizona, and before coming to Philly, I have never had a cheesesteak before in my life. I'm not a huge fan of steak/roast beef/red meat sandwiches, so essentially I never really got around to trying an authentic cheesesteak (and being from Phoenix, a mediocre one at that). But I decided, When in Rome, and saved my first ever cheesesteak experiences for my first ever trip to Philly. 

Me being me, I had to try a steak from both Pat's and Geno's to compare. From all the people I survey, the favor between Pat's and Geno's is a pretty stark 50/50. So how could I try one without the other? Answer: I can't. Our first steak was from Geno's, and it was pretty good. However, I enjoyed the steak from Pat's significantly more. 

Two things about our steak from Pat's that stood out: the steak itself and the Wiz. The steak is cut differently at both places, and I'm assuming seasoned differently too. Pat's steaks seemed much heartier, with a more genuine and robust flavor than that of their neighbor. I also appreciated how the Wiz was served piping hot, and how we were given three generous lathers of Wiz on top of our delicious steak meat (this was more Wiz than what we got across the street, and seemed to be a better/appropriate steak to Wiz ratio). 

As every reviewer posts it is cash only, and expect to pay around $10 per person for a steak, drink and cheese fries/fries. Additionally, don't expect stellar service from the staff either. They get you in and they get you out. Other than that, you're not gonna get much more. But in an odd way, I liked the brief and short interaction with employees; a reflection of that rough around the edges Philly/East Coast charm that I was so unaccustomed to.

I'm sure there are much better cheesesteaks around, but for my first cheesesteak experience, I have to say I am impressed. Granted, we went for more of the tourist experience, but it was still enjoyable from a diner's standpoint.

The boy and I ventured out of CC for Craft Beer Day on E Passyunk. 
We found a clutch parking spot and made our way to our first spot. This place was packed and we were very worried we were gonna have to wait a long time for a table. Luckily two bar seats were open and we grabbed them up fast. The initial reason for coming was to try the OMMENGANG/DUVEL beers that they were offering but there was some sort of issue with the kegs and so the boy was only able to try one the WHITE ALE. He's a fan of  the hoppier brews so he switched to pacifico for his second round. We did get a chance to meet the rep from Duvel -she apologized for the keg situation and gave us both glassware. She also told us about a few other events shed be at the in the city so he could still try a few of the brews they didn't have. I decided to try one of the signature cocktails (the Las Cantina) It was quite good you can never go wrong with tequila and puréed fruit. Very refreshing and a creeper * . We ordered a small nacho so we would be able to munch while we  chilled and since we planned on migrating we didn't want to commit to eating too much. The nachos were some of the best I have ever had; they are def competition to El vez's. My second drink was the El Embassor it is usually made with rum but since im not a fan I requested it be made with vodka (surcharge 1.00) it was good and topped with champagne.  I am all about coming back to check out the food and drink scene here in the very near future. They have a pretty good HH if you're in the neighborhood.

*a drink that will creep up on you, after a few all of a sudden your drunk
For tourists. LOTS of better steak sandwiches.

... and here, I'm guessing, is how enemies are made.

Pat's-

I really wanted to like your steaks- no- I wanted to LOVE your steaks.

As someone who grew up in the Philadelphia metro area eating delicious gooey cheesesteaks from the likes of Real Pizza in Wayne, etc., I've been traveling the world for the last 13 years proselytizing our city's primary culinary export, bitching about airport restaurants that claim to offer "Philadelphia Cheesesteaks," and spreading the word about Amoroso's rolls to all who would listen.  I had never been to Pat's Steaks and, honestly, I thought I was just saving the best for last.

In San Francisco, I got my wife hooked on the Cheese Steak Shop on Divisidero, so when we got to Philly, we were both primed and ready to dive into Pat's (Geno's is not and will not be an option for us given their English-speaking only stance for their customers.  Call it racism or xenophobia, I call it just plain sad and mean-spirited, especially since they're adjacent to a Mexican food restaurant.  Aren't business owners supposed to be inclusive as a profit-maximizing strategy?  Anyway, back to the review).

So we fight our way down the sidewalk past the neon abomination known as Geno's and see Pat's looking as Philly as Philly can be.  We order at the steak window (no chicken cheesesteaks for the wife, it would seem), then head over to the soda and fries window (annoying rigmarole) to get birch beer (why hasn't this PA treat made it out of the state???).

I was so hungry I horked my steak down, but completely without relish.
In my mind, one of the things that makes a great cheesesteak is that all of the ingredients are jumbled up together because the chef has taken the time to chop it all together on the grill.  At Pat's, they take the roll, layer on the cheese (provolone, in my case), then put on the meat and finally top it off with grilled onions.

Separate but equal?  I think not.

The roll was huge, the steak ended up being pretty dry (since it wasn't slathered in gooey cheese), and the whole concoction just sort of slid, slowly, down my gullet like a fat, dry-meat watermelon.  Where was the flavor?

Sad.

Pat's.  We could have been so good together, but you're just not for me.  I'm leaving you for Jim's on South Street who, if I remember correctly, knows how to do gooey cheesesteaky goodness.

Disappointing.

Food is Great, service is ok..... they're just cheese steaks but "Whiz With" is the way to go... make sure you get those dried red chillis in oil and that hot sauce on it.. dont put too much or your stomach wont be happy w/you the next day!
With wiz son. Def the best cheesesteak in the US of A. Have your money and order ready before you get to the front of the line. Prob the only place that I don't mind eating outside.
Not bad, but way overrated. Tasted like a typical diner cheesesteak from anywhere in the country. Rude workers, outdoor seating only.
The most friendly and down-to-earth people out of all the food stands on campus. Great food and cheap, decent hot and iced coffee.
South Philly Hot Spot!!.   They have a decent selection of Tex Mex and as well as beer and tequila.  It tends to  become  extremely crowded  so plan accordingly when ordering drinks. s

I've been here twice, the first time to compare to Geno's and the second time to make sure I didn't just try them on an off day.  Turns out I'm still not a fan. The steak I had both times was super chewy, kind of dry and just not very appetizing IMO.
Overpriced and absolutely nothing special about it. Food tasted bland, fries are the cost of another meal. They charge what they do because it was on TV..don't waste your time.

filthy (fil'the) pronunciation
adj., -ier, -iest.

   1. Covered or smeared with filth; disgustingly dirty. See synonyms at dirty.
   2. Obscene; scatological.
   3. Vile; nasty: a filthy traitor.
   4. Great culinary creations consisting of an abundance of grease, fat, and what is sometimes referred to as "love."
   5. Anything with cheese whiz on it.
   6. A "whiz-wit" at Pat's

filthily filth'ily adv.
filthiness filth'iness n. 

-------------------------------------

Every time I come to Philly, I visit Pat's.  Now you think the 'Soup Nazi' was bad, the guys here are much worse....but in a good way.  It's pretty basic....you say "whiz-wit" for a steak sandwich with onions, or just plain "whiz" or "whiz-wit-out" for a steak sandwich without onions.  Order up, pay, step aside, and if you want, get some fries.  I think all the goodness from this places comes from this place comes from the fact they haven't cleaned their griddle since they have opened creating an insanely aromatic and potent "flavor zone."  

Next time you are in Philly, visit Pat's, follow my ordering instructions, and enjoy.  Geno's, across the street, makes a different kind of sandwich, and is much more sanitary, but side by side comparison has Pat's winning hand's down.  I will review Geno's shortly because there are some good points there.  Go to Pat's first, trust me.
The place was awesome! The line was legit around the cornor.  The food was served fast and each employee had excellent customer service skills... And the pizza was delicious!!!

Overrated in my opinion, but you have to try it at least once. I completed a taste test of Pat's vs. Geno's side by side and Pat's wins my vote; however, you are better off at Jim's or Dalessandro's (in Roxborough).

We got recommended to try Pats by a couple of our friends for an authentic Philly Cheesesteak. I guess thanks to Papal visit, there was absolutely no line when we got there! Woo-hoo! We ordered the cheesesteak with mushrooms and onion (whiz wit) for our flight. It was pretty good and quite different from the regular cheesesteak sandwich we had back at home in OC. The beef was fully loaded. They're a bit dried, wish we asked for more cheese. Overall, we were glad we tried out the true Philly cheesesteak.

WARNING: if you have any dietary restrictions do NOT go here. Management is super unaccommodating. The person I was with was yelled at by the manager for ordering a vegetarian option steak and called a "hipster". Buddy, your shop is on East Passyunk - figure it out. If you want a bland steak and horrible service this is your place. Also, remember, cash only so stick your ATM card in one of the very sketchy places near by.

Service was quick, factory line like.  Line long but was expected for a popular spot.  Smelled of old oil outside in the air.  I did the "one wit whiz" and the whiz was downright nasty.  It seemed like the concept of toasted crusty bread with sizzled steak, grilled onions and cheese has been commercialized and converted to fast food much to the dismemberment of a traditionally great hoagie/sandwich.  Next time I'll order it from a sit down restaurant and order it with provolone or American and skip the liquid velveeta cheese.  Price was $19 for the sandwich, soda and fries.  Not unreasonable.  The condiments outside looked a bit sketchy and unattended.  Trash cans around had a putrid foul odor like urine/rottenness.  Prob should be cleaned and emptied more often.  Positives, I found a parking spot super close and without much hassle.  Fries, soda were fine.  Service fast, efficient.  Though staff seem like robots.

Eh. We decided to try Pat's first, then Geno's. Pat's was not wrapped up, and unbeknowst to me, grease was dripping like free-flowing water off the side of my steak, and totally ruined a brand-new shirt. But this review will not be tainted by that. Pat's just isn't as good as Geno's. Although I will have to say there's not a HUGE difference between the two. I had the Provolone, without onions. For all you purists, I did try my husband's, which was Wit, Wiz. The provolone was ice cold, and the steak just wasn't all that great. The ordering process is way too fast and they're nicer at Geno's. Sorry Pat's!

Philadelphia is unique. Similar to NYC in the amount of locations you can go to where service is "Fuck You,  Pay Me!" Pat's is similar to this. It is a tourist site. I went while visiting Philly and grabbed both a cheesesteak sandwich from Pat's and Geno's. Amazing! Delicious! Not the Best But better then Geno's. I enjoyed it so much I wanted to get another but without the cheese and the guy was a complete asshole about it. You would think I was asking him for a free sandwich with his fucking attitude but whatever. Cheesesteak sandwiches are far superior to the ones over at Geno's. As I have said before I can forgive shit service when the food is good.

The food was far from good. We asked for steak fajitas and chicken quesadillas, both not tasty.

The staff was nice in general, but the place was crowded and they was not able to attend all the tables. All my requests took 20min to be attended.

The 2 beers I had was absolutely warm.

The place music was  extremely loud so I could not even  talk with my partner in front of me.
I gave chipotle 5 stars because of the quality of there food and not once have I ever had a bad plate or bad taste of food. So for that they deserve 5 stars.

We were debating between Geno's and Pat's but chose pat's because it had more reviews. We waited in line and from the time we got our food was about 20 mins later and this was at lunch time on a weekday.

The meat I thought was a bit dry and overall the experience was a bit rubbery. If you like the texture of condoms I guess this is the perfect experience for you. The upside is that the pepper were delicious but this wasn't the major reason why we came here. You're probably better off finding a hole in the wall with a shorter wait time and a decent cheese steak.

Got the sandwich with provolone and added peppers. It was okay the fries were good. Bring cash as they do not take plastic. One line is for sandwiches and another for everything else. Nice to say I did it but won't go out of my way.

I guess I never reviewed Pat's....

Something about this place has a certain charm. Growing up I remember Rocky getting a cheeseteak at Pat's, then his old boss told him to put out a cigarette because he was in training.

The people that work here are jerks and will make fun of you if you order a cheesesteak hoagie. Even though its on the menu. God forbid you want lettuce and tomato on a cheesesteak. They also break your stones if you don't use the exact specifics to order your sandwich. Dude you work at a freaking cheesesteak joint, Its not hard to make a cheesesteak. Why make it hard on me. I'm just trying to get some grub. Seriously.

With that said the Cheesteaks here....I'm always satisfied.  But you can probably get a better cheesesteak somewhere else. I just come here every so often for the novelty of this place.

This place would only get 3 stars if the vegan chicken and tofu fajitas weren't so amazing. Seriously, amazing. The smoked tofu will blow your mind. I don't really like how dark it is, the slow-ish service, or how crowded it tends to be, but damn are those fajitas good.
This place is outstanding ! Goat tacos the bomb ! Awesome patio ! Mucho margaritas ! Great salsas ! Fantastic menu. Great brunch menu. I highly recommend this establishment.

I really cant comment on the food.  It was the first time for me in Philly and I wanted cheesesteak.  The lines were so long. Around the building and down the block.  I was sad I couldnt try it because I didnt have the time to wait. so my suggestion is to leave enough time to wait in the darn line!

This McDonald's is in the perfect location to profit if it were just open late or had a drive through! Being so close to the Germantown Ave bars I'm sure they'd make a mint off the late night folks. If I can't drive through or go late at night I generally don't get McDonald's. Seems a waste of a location ‍
Service was quick and the line was short. I ordered mushroom pizza steak. I think it was good but not the level of 4 stars, might be 3.5.

"Did you get me my Cheez Wiz, boy?" -- The Blues Brothers (1980)

Wit or wit-out?  This is the language you need to understand before you go to Pat's.  This means onions and whiz if you don't know.  Now, people will tell you that Whiz is the way to go and if it is your first time, you gotta try it with the Whiz.  Just to do it once.

So here is the deal - after you specify your onion preference (why would you get it wit-out?) and your cheese preference (you can also get Provolone, American or a Pizza Steak), then you need your cash.  These guys don't take plastic.  And the first window will only take your steak order, so if you want a drink and/or fries, you need to slide down to your left and order those separately.  But these guys move FAST.

I ordered a mushroom and pepper steak wit (onions and whiz).  I got a Dr. Pepper and no fries.  It was 9:30pm and I had just flown in from Atlanta and my traveling companion texted me when we landed and said "where are we going for cheesesteaks?"  So obviously, I Yelped it.

The cheesesteak is really big, but OH so good.  They shove a plastic fork in the top for you and you will probably need it.  We enjoyed our steaks as we ate al fresco (your only choice) and drank our sodas.  The steak was thicker cut then expected and a little on the tough side (not cut properly), so as much as I loved the experience and the flavor, the meat quality left a lot to be desired.  Based on the beef and how it was cut, I had to knock this to 3 stars.

I'm definitely hitting up the competitor down the street on my next trip to compare.  I only wish I had the time on this trip.

We fell into this tourist trap, like so many others do!

We decided to try a cheesesteak and cheese fries from both Pat's and Geno's to make a determination which was best.  

All four people in our group agreed that Pat's was best.  We came through on a Monday afternoon and neither was very busy.  

I will say that the employees at both restaurants were flat out rude, which was surprising for such touristy places.  The employees at Pat's were a little more pleasant than Geno's, but neither were even close to appropriate.  Also parking is near impossible to find close by.  We got lucky and we're still about 4-5 blocks away.

After speaking to locals, when we come back to Philly we will go elsewhere for an "authentic" Philly Cheesesteak.

Second day of our Cheesesteak tour and we hit our first stop of the day, Pat's. This time we tried it with onions and provolone and it was quite tasty but not the best we have had. Service was super quick and there was no line, but the bread and meat were not as flavorful and the provolone was a bit dull. The onions were super tasty though and were the best part. Still a great option for a cheesesteak in Philly tho and I would definitely recommend!

Updating my review from 7 years ago. Still go to pats every once in a while. Most recent trip it was pretty bad. Still better than the other place, but you can go to pretty much any corner store and get a better product. After living in philly for so long, I can not say this place counts as 5 stars anymore.

I like the cheesesteaks here, but I hear they aren't the best, but I don't have much to compare it to because I don't go to Philadelphia often enough to venture out to the non-touristy cheesesteak joints.  I promise I will next time.

My family and I went on a Philly Cheesesteak tpur. We saved what we thought would be the three best places for last: Tony Luke's, Pat's and Geno's. We were very disappointed.  Customer service was nill. It was very clear that their goal was to kick out the sandwiches as fast as they could with no regard for quality. At Pat's, we didn't even get the sandwich we ordered and the meat was tough.  At  Geno's,  the cheese wasn't melted and our fried onions were pretty much raw. At T.L. we nicknamed our sandwich  'slim' because of the lack of meat in it. 
At the end of our tour, which also had us visiting Chubby's, Delassandros and Barry's in Roxbourough and Cleavers in Rittenhouse Square, we picked Barry's and Cleavers as our top two.  Packed sandwiches, tender meat, cheese mixed throughout, sautéed onions and peppers to perfection and rolls were the perfect degree of chewy.  Customer service was friendly.

Okay, I'll be the slob and defend this place a little.

It is extremely clean inside, though a little too clean... and too sterile. The inside has no personality. However, this city is so cheesesteak struck that I've noticed there's no places to get the same cheap, greasy, comfort food burger. You've either got pub burgers or McDees. This is a great alternative.

I think its cool to have a restaurant that offers unlimited toppings, which I gladly pass on. The french fries come in a portion that's humbling... which is cool, but makes you lose your appetite.

I like this place... I think it's fun grease in a fast-food-driven part of the city. Not a place you'd ever go with somebody you didn't know really well... but it's fun. I had no idea they were a chain, based on their drab color scheme, and old fashioned service.

I haven't been to the South Philly location in awhile, but my cousin was visiting from Australia so we popped in for dinner and some cocktails.  We went early (6 pm) because it is Valentine's Day and I was expecting a mob.  It actually wasn't too busy, and we were seated immediately.  Our service was excellent and attentive.  The food and drinks were superb.

I started with the plantains appetizer, which was caramelized perfectly and had just the right amount of crema and cheese on top.  I was just about finished eating this when the entrees came out.  My cousin had the enchilada platter which he completely wolfed down.  I had the carnitas burrito, and i put the remaining plantains on top as I was eating it.  It was huge and I have leftovers!

We both had a few mojitos, my favorite is always the guava.  I also tried the spicy pear, but that tasted just like a regular mojito, and there was nothing spicy about it.  Overall I was quite pleased with our meal.

Cantina's food was never really something that grabbed me. The salsas are pretty awesome but for  good mexican i either go to tres jalapenos or el jaracho. 

however, margaritas are deadly and for that i will give them the credit they deserve. if you are planning on a sloppish fun filled evening you should either start or plan on finishing with these margaritas. dear god.

Not sure what people see in this place. My girlfriend and I were across the street eating breakfast and noticed this place on our way out. We both love a good Philly soft pretzel (and have both grown up here) and we were very disappointed. We both agreed that they tasted like bread. Literally just tasted like bread. They looked tasty but when we bit into them it felt like we were biting into a piece of bread. The mustard was good and is the only reason I'm giving 2 stars. But if you're looking for a true philly pretzel you're better off going to the philly pretzel factory. Much more of an authentic taste. 

We will not be going back here.

Pretty good for a local college (Temple University) grill.  Tried the cheddar bacon burger and the Adriatic Grill Chicken wrap.

Burger was a frozen patty type, but well grilled.  Above average bun, very crispy bacon (not the raw boogers of bacon fat you get on other fast food bacon burgers) and what appeared to be actual cheddar and not the heavily processed vinyl roofing shingles you see elsewhere.

The chicken wrap was awesome, albeit a tad greasy.  Peppers, onions, and Italian dressing on it.  

Tastes great, inexpensive, and seating is confined to the outdoor patio area.  Because of that, probably best for takeout only in the winter.

wow i'm surprised this place doesn't have more good reviews! I am a first time visitor to Philly, and it was actually my first time I've ever had an authentic Philly cheesesteak and I thought it was DELICIOUS! I really thought this was a go-to place for locals, because it was very busy and the atmosphere just seemed like the place to go to! The price is very expensive in my opinion though but then again, i don't really have anything to compare it to. I liked all the difference choices you can get, and i thought fries were really good. They are very huge though, so I would recommend you half it with someone like i did :)

Across the street is Geno's, which I was way too full to try after coming from Pat's, but my friends and I ventured over there so that the big boys of our group could try one and compare the two places back-to-back. All of them said that Geno's was good, but Pat's was definitely better.

Pats Steaks is legengary but for the price it just serves as a tourist trap for people who live outside philly. You can get better service, better steak, and better prices at places like Jim's Steaks on South Street or at Steve's Steaks. I just think they are overated, but still better than Geno's

Nothing to rave about and honestly the people that work here are rude. It's just a line to take your money. The food wasn't anything to go ga ga over. I honestly thought it was average. Would I come back- nahhhhh

First, I have to say THE FOOD IS ALRIGHT. NOTHING GREAT. 
I am not sure why in the world they use PLAIN WHITE RICE in everything. I am half mexican. My father and his side are all full blood. I grew up eating authentic mexican foods. Now, I am not saying that they have to stick to being completely authentic, mexican-american can be just as good BUT WHITE RICE. Come on. That is weak. 

Now, you might be wondering why I gave the cantina 4 stars, that is because of their DELICIOUS SANGRIA and MARGARITAS. I LOVE THE SANGRIA SO MUCH THAT I KEEP GOING BACK. 

Story short, come to my house for real mexican and go to the cantina for drinks ;)

By the way, The Royal Tavern has fantastic food but their sangria sucks. Both restaurants are owned by the same people. Can someone explain this to me?

In my humble opinion, tied with Jim's for the best cheesesteak in town... And one huge perk, fast lines!  At other popular cheesesteak joints you are in for up to a 45 minute wait... No here!  The steak is delicious and the rolls are fresh.  My favorite is a cheesesteak with American, without onions add mushrooms... Delicious!

If this is the best of Philly then Philly don't got it down. Its true ...its just hyped up. I've had better Philly cheessteaks NOT in Philly. But a friend of mine said there r others in Philly that r way better. The steak at pats is mass produced. Its Wayyy over priced and overrated.  I'd rather go to a ma n pa shop down the road where they take their time to perfect an authentic Philly cheesesteak.

I was in philly for only a few hours and my friends who went to UPenn said I had to do the Pat's vs Geno's taste test for philly cheese steaks. I don't know if I had higher expectations for cheesetakes, but both of them were extremely mediocre. It needed sauce or something, because had very little flavor. It wasn't BAD, but just wasn't good. I'm sure there are better cheesesteak places around Philly.
Great place for a cheese steak though overpriced and usually a long line to wait in.  Parking sucks too.  Though the wait is worth it.  I usually bounce between there and Geno's across the street.

Don't bother.  Go down a few block's so Cosmi's

Pat's is nasty, greasy, and don't give you a lot of value for your dollar (read: little meat). Also, the sweaty guys slopping the meat onto the girl really don't do it for me

Fair cheesesteak at best. Kind of tasteless. Staff can be rude. Not a big fan of this place or Geno's. I guess they get a point for being open 24h, as this would probably be great drunk food at 3 in the morning when you don't really care what you're eating.
They seem to be geared toward giving visitors what they see as a traditional "Philly" experience more than serving a quality version of Philadelphia's signature sandwich. 
If you want a truly good cheesesteak, there are countless other places in the city that are head and shoulders above this place. Tony Luke's comes to mind right off the top of my head. 
If you want a crappy steak, but want some selfies in front of one of one of the most famous cheesesteak places in the city (famous for what? I don't know... lousy food? I guess...) then by all means, stop on by. If you want a true cheesesteak that has taste, then go somewhere else, but be sure to drive by Pat's and Geno's on your way, so you can get some pictures to show your friends back home, just don't bother with the food.

Those who get stuck at Jim's or elsewhere are just too lazy to come to P Square for the real thing.

Pat's is devoid of flash glitz and advertising glamor that Geno's needs to get patrons. Pat's is simple and classic. Don't try to fix a good thing.

These steaks are juicy/greasy and perfectly melty with Whiz. Oninos and mushrooms are sauteed. These people really care about their steak, just not you.

UPDATE: WTF happened here? Did someone sell the company? A recent visit with out of towners produced a fatty steak-stuffed sandwich. We're talking huge amounts of fat in everyone's sandwich. The meat tasted less.....good. And a conversation with my neighbors fortified the fact that we all think Pat's doesn't taste good anymore. Did they get worse or have all our palates suddenly become spoiled foodies?

Pat's came in second in my books, it was enjoyable and good. Service was quick and the cheesesteak looked so dam sexy!

The bread was soft, filled with a lot of steak along with onions and a slab of cheese wiz on top. Appearance-wise, it was the most sexiest cheesesteak I've ever seen in my life. Taste-wise, it was just good. I loved how much steak there was but it was a tad bit on the dry side. It's good to try Pat's once to say that you did and to judge it yourself.

Went to Five Guys and thought, "hey this is going to be a great experience."

I left Five Guys and thought, "hey, that was a lot of calories."

Be prepared for unhealthy. Be prepared for the unhealthy. You can load your burgers with whatever you want, but it's nothing special, and in the end it just feels like a Whopper Jr. from Burger King. Don't let it fool you!

Some facts:
The burgers are pretty soft and juiceless.
The fries are geared towards quantity not quality.
There are no shakes or malts or juices--just a couple fountain soda selections.

Some things that are tolerable:
The walls are decorated in slogans and quotes about the business. I think my favorite one was "several cuts above fast food," which is not exactly a compliment.
There are peanuts on every table--a call back to the fifties perhaps?--I will never understand.
You can't beat the price for the amount of fat and calories you're getting.

I came here with my fiancé and best friend after the phillies game. Right across from it was Geno's. I looked up both on Yelp and Pat's had better reviews so we chose to go with the rest of the foodie crowd. Service is fast. you place your order and in less than a minute and you get your sandwich in less than 20 seconds. I ordered the Philly steak with onions, mushrooms, and whiz. It was the best cheesesteak I have ever had. Before this cheesesteak I can honestly say I never understood the craze. The sandwich was perfect. My fiancé enjoyed his too. He ordered the peppersteak with onions and provolone. 

The only downside to the experience has nothing to do with the food. Parking around this area is tough. Just a little FYI for those driving out here.

I've only been here a few times but it's always been great! However, the other day was especially great! I got into a huge fight with my boyfriend on our way to dinner so everything was uncomfortable before we got to cantina. When we got to there our hostess said it'd be a few minutes wait and offered for us to sit at the bar while we wait. She was such a joy. I believe she said her name was Kaylee. While we waited and when she wasn't taking other groups names she was chatting with us about everything philly. Her personality and enthusiasm were both through the roof. It made me and my boyfriend completely forget why we were fighting and everything that she recommended that we try on the menu was amazing! We both really enjoyed our time there!!
Pat's is terrific. And, as a bonus, they aren't racist assholes like the fuckers at Geno's.

This location is so sloppy.  These employees clearly hate their jobs.  Few times ordered and my food looked like it had a rough ass day.  Only thing that saved the food was my sriracha sauce I keep.  Companies need to realize just because you're taking money from someone doesn't mean you can just give them poor quality food or service and them stay quiet about it.
Looks kind of trashy but cheesesteak is amazing!!!!! So glad I tried this before I left Philly!

This place used to be great about 5-7 years ago. Went down hill ever since. Service sub par unless you are sitting at the bar. Food is mehhh now. Margaritas are very good. That's the highlight here. There's enough competition on passyunk that they should step their game up. They win bc of location. If a new authentic Mexican restaurant opened up next door they would loose the battle. Very unorganized seating and wait time with hostess on several occasions. Go for a drink but don't expect an amazing meal. Far from it.

Overrated tourist trap.  Cold, stale bread, unevenly cooked meat and very little flavor.

No comparison to the real best cheesesteaks in Philly...go to Jim's on South Street or Chink's instead...those are the real cheesesteak champions.

Also disturbed by the vaguely racist statements posted on the windows there.  Won't be back.
Great place to get some food late at night great staff just make sure you have cash no cards cash only

It's quite a sight on Passyunk it's congested with cars and people trying to find parking. I checked the websites of the two famous cheesesteaks I thought Pat's was more interesting and had choices of cheeses but when I ordered the cheesesteak I was trying my best to avoid the cheesewhiz, not particularly appetizing I was surprised they didnt give you a choice. Yuck! If you cannot even understand the names of food additives it's best to avoid it altogether. The mushrooms and peppers added flavors but it was soaking through at every bite. The steak was tasty but had too much fat. Here's my breakdown:

Likes:
Soft and toasted bread
Mushrooms and peppers
Cherry peppers

Dislikes:
Cheesewhiz
Steak
Juice running down my hands and legs (metal tables with holes that go through)
Service - not friendly
Surrounding of the store was sparse and lacking in cleanliness

I've had Chick-Fil-A once before, couldn't understand the hype. Gave it a second shot, still underwhelmed. Just your typical fast food spot, chicken nuggets and fries and soda. Sauces are nothing special. Don't know why people rave over it.

This particular location was quick, service was good. No problems there. If you enjoy this chain, you'll be just fine dining here.

Not one of the better locations in Philly! Fries taste a day old, even when the customer before me asked the cashier to make sure the fries were fresh. Didn't know I had to ask the same. Ordered the new fresh mozzarella chicken sandwich and the buns are burnt. Chicken taste microwaved. Waste

Noisy and fun atmosphere. Good service. But the food was not good (the chips and salsa were fine, but really broken up) and my margarita tasted like it had been made from a mix. We had drinks and food at 3 bars that night and this one was no comparison. Maybe it was an off night? It's nearby, so we'll probably wander through again at some point.

Edit: The owners got in touch and were super nice. I'm willing to forgive a lot for good customer service.

I don't get the the whole obsession over Philly cheese steaks.  I have eaten at almost all of the top places and I dont get it. Pats is definitely the best, but that's not saying much. Its steakums with cheese wiz. I can get the same thing at the local pizza joint around the block from my house.
this jawn ight. its pretty. food could be better. my server was nice. but yeah. its ight.
I did a taste test with Pat's and Geno's, back to back. Yes, I ate one of each. Both had cheese wiz and onions. I prefer the chopped meat at Pat's. Yummy stuff!!

i went to Cantina the day they opened.  i've gone back there a bazillion times since then because two of my best friends live across the street.  we run back and forth from there like giddy school children.  in fact, those two friends just had a child, and we're trying to convince them to see if the baby monitor will reach over there.  uh...yeah. don't judge.

we, giddy children, get even giddier after half-priced pitchers of margaritas during Cantina's sweet happy hour.  it really has one of the best, i think.  free tortilla chips with a salsa verde that outshines Trader Joes' salsa verde (which i LOVE).  i pound these chips and the margaritas while i'm there and then don't know what hits me.  this really does remind me of being a child.... when i would eat way too much pizza and soda.
this business is right on the corner of broad and Snyder,directly across from walgreens and southern school,i found it spacious ,clean,friendly staff and the food was hot .

Pat's was the first real cheesesteak place I dined at in Philly. I recall my friend Craig taking me here. It seems to be the most famous. Other friends of mine came into town not long ago and wanted to go to Pat's.

Pat's is good, but Geno's is across the street and it is a little better.

The Franklin Institute commissioned a video called Anthem that it used to show in its IMAX theatre. There was a sequence from Pat's in there.
Cold cheese and cold soggy bun. Didn't like Pat's. We went across the street to Geno's and love it! Geno's French roll really made the sandwich.

PAT'S vs. geno's

I was sooo excited to FINALLY be in Philly for the first time because I wanted to try the Cheese Steaks. Being that I was only out there for 1 night I had to get one from each of the most well known spots, so that I could do the compare and contrast between the two.

I had heard so many times that Geno's was great and how many celebs go there and blah blah blah...and all I can say is FAIL!!!!!!

The sandwich was dry, the meat had no flavor and the onions were so raw that I had that annoying onion taste in my mouth for a while until I got back to the hotel and brushed my teeth...UGHHH...DON'T WASTE UR MONEY HERE...I've tasted better in NYC...don't be fooled by the celeb hype and the BRIGHT lights...

Then, I quickly made my way across the street. I order one from Pat's and I could tell just by watching them make it that it as going to taste WAY BETTER. The Bread was soft, the steak chopped up and JUICY, the onions and peppers COOKED and the cheese was regular American cheese, but good non the less...

LADIES AND GENTS WE HAVE A WINNER...PAT'S HANDS DOWN...
Staff was rude and sandwich was pretty tasteless. Had Geno's couple nights before and far better experience. Go to Geno's.
Chopped steak, way better than Geno's, good portion
I prefer chopped to shaved so I tried Pat's over Geno's.  It was disgusting either way.  I would suggest you try Pudge's in Blue Bell for a great steak with not soggy fries.

There was a lot of hype surrounding this place when it opened, well I  as much hype as a burger chain can produce anyway.  I feel like the hype was unjustified.  Sure, the burgers are better than the Wendy's down the block and the toppings are plentiful but they lack the "wow" factor I was expecting.  

Burgers are all made with fresh, never frozen ground beef, and this is a noticeable factor.  Fries are hand cut potatoes which is also a nice attribute.  Between the hours of 12-2 there is typically a line 20 deep, and although it moves quickly can still be quite overwhelming and confusing.  

I recommend giving the burgers a try...they aren't bad, just not good enough to be famous.

I hate to say it, but I'm going to... I think I'm a Geno's girl! 

We went to Pat's on our way back from 2 street on New Year's day. Considering we had been drinking for just about 24 hours straight, it was clear a cheesesteak was in order. 

Pat's was the first neon light we saw and we got in line (which was shorter than Geno's). We were craving the greasy disgusting meat and whiz spectacle that are Philly Cheesesteaks, but instead it was dry(ish). I want my roll dripping with whiz, and it just didn't happen. Super disappointing since I only get a cheesesteak once a year (strictly due to the fact I could eat them every single day- must set limits!). The hot cherry peppers were pretty good though- so points for that, Pats!

First of all, I find it amazing that 2 places would stir passions like Pat's and Geno's does.  We were a group of 5 and divided on our favorite.

I had Steak, Whiz, Without.  I personally did not order so I don't have a problem with the ordering process. I did..LOVE it though. 

While we were leaving some kid on a bike yelled out PATS SUCKS! Which adds to my first paragraph..would there be such hatred if Geno's didn't exist? :)
Donkeys in Camden is so much better then these steaks. Over priced and a waste of time to drive there
Sandwich was good, but I was not wowed. Their onions were plentiful, and the bread was hearty, Found service to be rude, though, so knocking them down a star.

It's Pat's need I say more? Everyone should experience Pats steaks especially at midnight after a Phillies game. The whole vibe of the neighborhood is unbeatable and the sandwiches are exactly how they should be!!! Delicious!!!!

The quality of the meat they use is what does it and they load the sandwiches up as well.

Get in line, don't screw up your order and enjoy!!!

I need to add that the peppers they have there are a favorite!!!
Loved the cheese steak and liked the bread. The meat was perfectly juicy! Wasn't able to try Geno's so can't compare.

Of course you go for the history and the location.  Trying to order like a local by doing your "wid" or "widout".  Standing around the crappy tables.  Watching the bus loads of tourists and locals show up.  Everyone having a good time just being there.  That is all part of the fun.  Not the world's greatest cheesesteak, but they are delicious!  Meat just needed a drop more salt to give it that flavor boost.  Thoroughly enjoyed it.  Have been here pretty much every time I visit Philadelphia.  If anything I liked it more recently.  I'm a provolone "wid" onion guy; can't handle eating Cheeze Whiz in any form.  Fries were also pretty good, too.  I'd give it 3-3.5 stars just for food, but clearly a 4 when you throw in the one-of-a-kind experience.
Not as good as it used to be, It has become more of a tourist attraction.  Still better than Genos

Tourist trap but better than Geno's and has better quality food than them as well.
Pat's has always been there in a bind after the 2am drink up... but there are waaay better steaks out there.

This was an interesting experience. 

Pat's and Geno's were right across from each other. So here is my take. 

Parking is non-existent at either locations. Seating is located outdoors and around the stores. There are lines at both stores too. So I was confused. Which one do I choose. So I did what most people seem to be doing. Get one from each!

Pat's lines move fast. These guys know what they are doing. You go up to the register and place your sandwich order and pick it up within a minute. No joke!  I ordered 3 subs and got them in under a minute. You pay cash. Then you move down the line and order your drink and fries. You pay cash here too. 

I ordered a mushroom cheesesteak with onions. My hubby ordered a plain cheesesteak with cheese wiz. The steak was sliced thinly. They give a lot. The sub was well seasoned, juicy and disappeared in record time. Their fries were crispy. 

Geno's cheesesteak was good too. The difference we noticed - steak was sliced a little thicker, about the same quantity of steak, less seasoning (not salty), and very little cheese (it was smeared onto one side of the bun).  It was delicious but a bit drier than Pat's. 

All in all it was a great taste comparison. We were stuffed!  Depending on your preference there is a sandwich for you on either side of the street. 

Geno's had an awesome DJ playing music to keep the folks lined up entertained. You can hear it loud and clear from Pat's. :-)

Experience the difference!!

The sad reality of cheesesteaks is most of what makes one good is the bread, not the meat or cheese. While I enjoy pat's (I think the meat is better), I have to go with genos for the better bread. I enjoy John's Roast pork better than both, but if you want the true tourist experience (albeit near no discernible night life), this is where to go.

Of course I had to stop by Pat's, during my stop in Philly on my east coast road trip. Pat's is considered the first Philly cheese steak spot in history, so my expectations were high. The line was long when I arrived, but I took my place and patiently waited, as I drooled over the smells in the air. When I finally made it to the front I ordered a classic Cheese Steak, with cheese whiz, green peppers, onions, and mayo. The cheese steak was one of the better Phillies I've had in my lifetime, and definitely better than Geno's from across the street. My friend got a Philly from there, so we could compare the two, and simultaneously engorge on our Philly cravings. The biggest difference was how they prepared their steak. Pat's has thinly sliced steak which was grilled, vs Geno's which did thicker strips of steak. I'm definitely a bigger fan of thin steak on my phillys.Pat's is definitely a great spot to stop by for a cheese steak.
I love Cantina, consistently amazing!

I was so excited to try this place!
First time visiting philly and trying the original philly cheese steak!
But I guess I had too much excitement because it wasn't anything special.

However! the jalapeño they had on the condiment section was.. AMAZING.
So spicy and sour and sweet all at the same time. I know it sounds ridiculous but I might go back just for that. the pepper made the sandwich so much better than it is. 

And I think it's a bit overpriced for the amount of steak & cheese they give...
Excellent Cheesesteak sandwich! I got the mushrooms, onions, pepper cheesesteak. It was so delicious!!

Um, well the only thing I have to say is that this is the best Philly Cheese steak to ever exist. This is a very popular spot, people travel from other states to have this so obviously there will be a line but it moves rather quickly. It's worth the wait. You will NEVER be disappointed.

Cool for the history and laid back atmosphere, but this was the worst cheesesteak I've ever had. There was no flavor. Maybe that's the way people around here like it though. If you're from the south like I am, you'll wish it had peppers, creole seasoning, and more cheese.
Well that was my fist philly cheese steak so I'm no expert but it was delicious! The bun was soft the steak has great flavour. I had the wiz and onions , maybe next time try the provolone and onions.
I had salad bowl. A lot of selections of toppings. Very fresh salmon. Highly recommend. Credit card for $10 minimum purchase

My husband and I dine here about once a month but always sit in the bar area. I have only sat in the dining area twice and both times I had a horrible experience with the service. This last time,we were immediately seated, then someone brought us chips and said our waiter would be right with us, 15 minutes later I flagged down a waitress and asked for water and said she would be right back, over ten minutes later our waiter shows up and takes our drink order, he then disappears. At least ten more minutes go by and I flag down the host because at this point it's been well over a half an hour and we have not received drinks, nor placed an order. I tell the host it's been at least 30 minutes (probably closer to 45). He finds our waiter who brings the  drink order .. of course it was wrong. At this point we don't care, and just take it as is because we don't want to wait again, we place our food order and ask for a soda,  we asked for the soda a total of three times.... it didn't come until after our meal was complete. We  were in no rush, enjoying dinner with friends, but there comes a point when waiting for something as simple as a glass of water or soda, especially after consuming spicy Mexican food, becomes an issue. I would say, we were blatantly ignored by most staff after my initial "we have waited 30 minutes" comment to the host. It almost felt awkward to be there, I don't typically write reviews, but the first time I received such awful service dining in the dining room at this restaurant I complained via email to the company directly and received no response, I had to also call because on that occasion they charged my debit card twice. The service was really truly awful, and I think people should be aware. I would give this experience less than 3 stars if it wasn't for the fact that I have always had great service at the bar.  The food is always good, but made less enjoyable by the whole ordeal. FYI, I am probably writing this more favorably than I should...

Disappointed. STAY AWAY. I was in Philly for two days and was excited to try a philly cheesesteak. I decided to go to Pat's but it was the biggest mistake ever. My siblings and I got food poisoning from eating their food. Pat's please figure out what's going on with food and service. You most likely have a sanitation issue.

Always delicious. Lines are worth the wait. I've been eating here for 25 years. I tried genos 2 times. Once when I was 16 and determined I must know it all and I might like theirs better, and once when I met my husband to fulfill his curiosity.  If you are in Philly you must have a "provi whit".
I ordered extra crispy and got extra soggy. Not one piece in the bucket was crispy. It is not like they have a big menu, You would think they could cook one thing right.

Coming to Phili I couldn't leave without having a cheesesteak or 6. I picked Pat's over Genos and I don't regret my choice at all. I got the wit double wit cheesesteak and this provided enough cheese wiz to make me a happy camper. Everything was great, but I just wish there was somewhere to eat where you could be kept out of the cold.

How have I not reviewed Pat's previously????

This is easily the home of the best cheesesteaks that I have ever had.  (Although I'll admit that I've never made my way over to Geno's to try theirs)

I have had Jimmy's before - and Pat's easily blows them away.   

I take my steaks with wiz and wit onions --- sometimes I'll go with provolone instead --- always throw on some hot cherry peppers.  The flavor is just unbelievable....  pure heaven. 

Omg so good, I'm making myself hungry as I type this. 

If I do eventually manage to try Geno's (it's just so hard to do so when I know Pat's is right across street and already serves perfection), I'll be more than happy to come back here and edit my review to reflect and tell you what I think.  (As if you'll all be waiting with bated breathe for me to do that)

There is really nothing that I dislike about Pat's other than waiting in line to get the Cheesesteak in the first place.  

If you are in Philly, you need to stop at Pat's.  If you don't, you are truly missing out on an experience.

We came in to Cantina Los Caballitos on Cinco de Mayo and had a pretty good experience.  We surprisingly didn't have to wait too long for our table even though the place was slammed (it helped that there were only two of us).  We got a chicken fajita, a chicken quesadilla, and a pitcher of margaritas.  All of the food was good - not the best we've ever had but well above average.  I liked the inclusion of mushrooms with the fajitas (although I question the lack of cheese), and the salsa verde is one of the best I've had.

I don't have any complaints, but there are a few little things that would have made my experience even better.  For one, I hate when a restaurant charges extra for sour cream, and this time was no exception.  I was especially unimpressed that it was an extra dollar for sour cream when we were already spending $55 on our meals and drinks, and we ordered things that in my opinion should come with it standard.  I also felt that the prices overall weren't the best value, and I would probably plan to come during happy hour in the future.  On the whole, though, it was a positive experience and a place that I would recommend.

My wife would rate this place higher, we went last night I had the steak tacos she had the chicken quesadilla, mine lacked the spicy flavor that yearn for when I go to a "mexican" place, she liked her food.  Drinks I had a blood-orange margarita she had a strawberry margarita they were a little stingy with the tequila.  For the total price I woulds have like to have left with a nice buzz oh, we had a slice of coconut cake...it was dry!!!
The "wiz with" here was average at best (better than geno's) but where else can you go and get rude service and soak in the city of brotherly love?

Ok I am here to give you an honest appraisal of both Pat's and Geno's.  Being from out of town, I wanted to experience each place so my wife and I purchased one "wit whiz, wit" from each place.  You will find Geno's review on their site.

Pat's was by far the more flavorful.  It actually had some spices working to flavor the meat.  The meat was tender and the onions were cooked.  Whiz is Whiz.  Not one of the best sandwiches I have had, in fact, we have Big John's Steak at home, a local chain, and their sandwich is far superior to either of these "Philly steaks".  

Both of these establishments are in a really bad part of town.  The parking is difficult.  We were able to park a block away and walk.  The smells, how shall I describe it......we parked in front of a storefront that was raising chickens.  The smell was overwhelming and it was chicken crap.  There is garbage everywhere.  Someone needs to tell these Philadelphians that they need to put their garbage in a can, not on the street or sidewalk.  So much litter and garbage it was hard to walk on the sidewalk.  

I would not recommend this place to anyone.  Go to Reading terminal market and find a good place to eat if you want a Philly cheese steak.  At least you have a place to sit and dessert is just steps away.  

Have to give it 2 stars because I have to give Geno's at least one star.  I really think this is a 1 star place.

Find a Good Place to eat, preferably outside Philly.
Tried the original cheesesteak with wiz. Genos was a LITTLE bit better.
Got me the Philly cheesesteak with cheese wiz. No line, we were the first one in line. The sandwich was ready less than 10 sec. It wasn't bad for my first Philly cheesesteak. It was an experience.

My husband never had a cheesesteak in the City of Brotherly Love and I think one of your exposures should be the eternal Pat's vs Geno's feud (otherwise, you will always wonder what the fuss is all about).  And yes, I still wonder what all the fuss is all about.  I used to live in Philly and only need to eat a cheesesteak once a year to have my fix.  For me, Pat's comes in #3 after Tony Luke's at #1 and Geno's at #2. 

I'll compare Pat's vs Geno's.  At both places, we bought it Wit Whiz.  The bun at Pat's is a little thicker, denser, and chewier.  They're also a little skimpy on the meat (I don't recall this being a problem before but it's been 10 years).  The meat is sliced thicker than Geno's and in general, a little tougher.  Overall, decent but Geno's still wins when it comes to this cheesesteak corner.

***Airport Chipotle at non-airport Prices***

This is a new Chipotle located in the food court of Terminal F (very close to the shuttle connecting to the other terminals). What makes this Chipotle five stars?

1. Cost -- No airport inflation. Prices are normal, which means about a dollar less than what I typically pay in NY for a burrito. This is virtually unheard of for fast food in an airport. I'm down.
2. Venue -- Brand spanking new, plenty of seating available in the food court. 
3. Customer Service -- Very friendly, joked around a bit and in all quite pleasurable. Line moved very quickly, and everyone knew what they were doing which doesn't always occur with new locations.
4. Food -- Delicious, as usual. They were pretty friendly with portions.

FINAL VERDICT: When I'm connecting in Philadelphia, I usually try to resist the very strong urge to get chick-fil-a and usually end up getting Popeyes or that place near Chick-fil-a that sells overpriced ($10) cheesesteaks (that are still pretty good). If you are a fan of Chipotle, plan ahead if you are going to be at Terminal F (or just make the trek there as I may in the future).

Ya it's kinda expensive and parking is a nightmare and the cashiers are short with people and it has a long line but somehow it adds to the charm. I'm not from Philadelphia so maybe I don't know what I'm talking about but I like the feel and neighborhood it feels very authentic. 

Food: So as far as I know there are 3 big name ones Pats, Genos, and Tony Luke's. I think Pats is the winner. The bread had a bit of a crunch the steak was plentiful and tasty and the cheese whiz was on point. They're very close honestly but I think Pats is just a notch above the rest.
This place is crazy!  A guy I work with took me here when I was in Philly on a work trip.  I got the Pizza, no onions.  If you go to Philly you need to experience this.

when i went to philly back in 04 my friends and i had steaks from pats and genos. we agreed that pats had better bread and genos better meat. i went again back in october and this time pat's was better all around. a friend of mine told me that tony luke's was the best in philly so i tried it and it was good but i still liked pat's more. next time i'd like to try their roast pork sandwich as well.
just cause they were first dont make them the best

Better service than the one across the street, guys are warm and friendly, not just for Philly, I mean friendly anywhere.  Not fussy - but i did goof  - I ordered whiz wit' - should have dropped the whiz - kinda overpowered the steak - more meat than accross the street too.

they definitely are the king of steaks amongst genos! worth the wait and if you are in that area. my favorite part is when all the juices combine together from the melting cheese grease from the meat and onion make the sandwich so good!!

The great cheesesteak debate! Pat's invented them in 1930, Geno's is about about 50 years old. 

In the sandwich photo, Geno's is on the left, Pat's is on the right. 

Both have provolone that is not mixed into the meat while cooking. I prefer it mixed on the grill. I also prefer Cheese Whiz, like a true aficionado, but my son likes provolone....

Geno's: softer roll, stacked sliced meat, slightly better meat flavor. 

Pat's: smaller firmer roll with more flavor, the meat is thinner so it curls up when cooked but is not chopped, better texture while chewing, more meat, costs a dollar more, 10 vs 11 bucks. 

Winner: Pat's King of Steaks!

I love Chipotle I wish they had one closer to my place.  This is probably the closet one but its downtown in a not so easy area to park so unless I wan to walk 25 minutes or a burrito I only hit it up once and a while.

Line move fast they were extra generous on the gacu which is a super plus I hate when people are stingy, especially if you are paying extra for it.  I tend to get the veggie burrito it comes with gacu but occasionally I get something else and usually add it.
I had my local guides order for me...we went with pizza wiz wit... fantastic.  Solid rolls to hold up to the mounds of steak and sauce

Pats and Geno both suck.  They are over rated over priced and have no taste/ flavor at all.. Jim's is a lot better but that is not saying that much either.  Ishkabibbles is far better in the area.    There is also a spot right across from Jim's steaks that is a bar also with great steak sandwiches.   Ohhh and not rude idiots working at either ishkabibbles or that bar spot.

I seriously don't know what I could say that would trump or add anything that hasn't been said.

I came, I ordered (cheese with onions), I added hot sauce (not available when I came 10 years ago). 

Delicious and much more tender and tasty than their neighbors across the street.

I love Chipotle! It's the best place for fast mexican food. However, this one isn't the best of them. Don't get me wrong, I come here often bc I love the food, but the lines are RIDICULOUS!!! And sometimes, I felt a if they were rushing so bad putting things together that it sometimes spills out of the bowl. And if you have never ordered from chiptole before, I feel as if they rush you. I felt so overwhelmed the first time I ever went here. It's a what do you want and they just scoop away. I felt like there was no time to look at the items they have.

So, I then resorted to ordering online. It makes the whole experience so much better! You walk in, skip the lines and watch all the stares of people standing in line thinking in their heads like..wtf!! HAHAHA. I have waited a few times, but not as long as if I ordered there.

My fav - Burrito bowl w/ brown rice, tomato salsa, hot salsa, corn salsa (yes, I know...it's tons of salsa, but sooo good), black beans, lettuce, cheese, and barbacoa. I skip the sour cream and guac (gotta watch my girlish figure...lol. JK)

I really wish there was a chipotle near where I lived. I would probably go everyday. Hmm, maybe it's a good thing I don't live near one. I'd prob have a heart attack.

Not bad but not great. Very accommodating but the food was only okay. Not to say I wouldn't try it again, but I wouldn't recommend it. 
We shared guacamole and it was good as were the chips and salsa. As an appetizer we shared wings sampler. Not sure why I ordered wings in a Mexican restaurant but I did. They were okay. Certainly not very Mexican however could be a good snack at the bar. For entrees we both had tacos. I ordered the carnitas tacos. It was two tacos & a lot of food. They were pretty good though I could barely finish one. My friend had goat tacos. He said in his first taco he bit in to something hard which put him off a bit. He finished them nonetheless & didn't mention it until the next day. 
Not bad, but a little pricey for tacos. If you're serving street tacos you shouldn't charge 9.99. On a positive note they have many gluten-free options & knowledgeable people to guide you through the menu.

two words: whiz wit'.

the directions to order: 
1. the type of cheese first (WHIZ = cheese whiz). 
2. then whether or not you want your steak with caramelized onions (WIT' = with onions).  whiz wit'.  trust me.  

the wait: stood in the street nearly in the middle of traffic, because the line was that long*.  but the line moved quickly, thanks to the efficient ordering process described above**.  i, an ex-industrial engineer - the masters of efficiency, was impressed.  there are 2 separate lines: line number 1 is for your cheesesteak order and line number 2 is for your drinks and french friiiieesss order.

the monies: almost 8 bucks for the most authentic philly cheese steak.

REMEMBER: whiz wit'.


*during this wait, i recommend one person of your party to scour (read: stalk other patrons eating/finishing up) for available seating at one of the outdoor tables.
**make sure you are ready to order when you get to the window.  or else it's back to the end of the line for you.  cant remember how?  dont worry, there's a sign with directions you can refresh your memory with as youre waiting to order.

First time to Philly I had to do the tast off betwen Pat's and Geno's.  I had them with provolone which was good.  I like Pat's better bc I find they chop up the meat and make it greasier.  The Philly people were all ordering cheese whiz so eventually I had to try that on my cheese steak and lemme tell ya....once you go cheese whiz u never go back...  loved it!  It's a lot of fun to go do the taste off amongst these two establishments.  It's a nice atmosphere and very Philly!
They have steak on bread. You can get it with cheese on it, or onions, or even some other stuff. It's somewhat expensive. They're open 24 hours. That's about all you need to know.

When in Philly, join the debate, Pat's or Geno's?!?

Located a little more then a mile from the historical sites in Philly. Not really walking distance when its freezing and you are at the sites or in downtown. The area was kind of sketch when I was there too.

Street parking. Really touristy and crowded.

Cash only. Open 24/7. Outside seating, not to clean.

Be ready for long long lines. Food does comes out pretty quick though. Made to order.

Make sure you know what you want before you get to the window and order correctly. The locals and employees will give you shit.

Mushroom Pepper Cheesesteak - $10.19 - Steak was grilled well. Bread was wet and soggy from all that fat, not a bad thing. Loved that combo with mushrooms and peppers mixed in. Just meat and cheese can get a little boring. Provolone is my cheese choice, I am not a fan of the Whiz. 

It was good, big and heavy but not as epic as I was hoping for. Better then Geno's!

All I ordered was a large fries .... that's it . I had to wait 15 minutes just for my large fries and I was late for my next stop... all because the lady in front of me had a huge order for her cute little kiddie winks  , but why did I have to wait for them to complete her order ... all I ordered was a large fries ... it takes 20 seconds or less to put it together . Fries , already made , put fries in the carton , then put it in the bag . That's it ... why the heck did I have to wait for them to make 5 orders  and a milkshake .... :/ annoyed , won't be going back if I want fast service ... once I finally got my fries though ! They were fantastically  delicious! But not worth a 15 minute wait :/ needed more salt ..

Okay yes, Im from out of town, but then again, so are the majority of these reviews. No i've not tried Tony Lukes (but i'll make sure I do next time I drop by philly). No, i've not tried the mom-n-pop's joint that you swear is better than the "tourist food". What I have tried is the joint across the street and literally dozens of other cheesesteak shops around the country.

Pat's is the best I've ever had. Period. Don't even bother going across the street (Unless you just want to see how much better pat's is)

Get it Whiz Wit with a little ketchup (yes, I know it sounds odd, just do it). Be prepared before you get to the window.... Don't get upset if they're snappy if you can't make up your mind. Just grin and bear it, the sandwich is worth it. You guys in Philly have no idea how good you have it. Such a simple sandwich that literally no one else get's right outside of your town.

My mouth is watering just writing this review.
Open 24/7. Too many Phily Cheese Steak and definitely is taste the best. Geno is across. Parking may be an issues, since this is located at residential area, and no parking.

I prefer Pat's over Geno's for the steak but Geno's over Pat's for the fries.   It's not a great steak but when I get done at work too late and don't have options, I'll stop in.   You'll see a lot if tourists or people that live in the burbs or NE who dont know better.
Had the provolone with. I could only eat a few bites, then had to toss it. Meat was fatty and tough, cheese didn't melt and was thick and overwhelming. Hate to say it but it was seriously bad. May

Placed an order for 10 4 piece nuggets and had a coupon for $4.99 for 4 nuggets fries and double stack burger. Since i had kids with me i asked if they could put the nuggets in the 10 piece boxes to save time. The owner, a very snobby female with a ton of jewelry on chastised the employee and explained what he was doing.  "That's not how things are done.  Those are MY boxes you are wasting! " Employee told me he would have to put them in 4 piece boxes because the owner said so. My cousin wanted to  approach the owner and asked her why couldn't she couldn't give the customer what they wanted.  I got mad and then asked for freshly cooked nuggets since she had an attitude. She asked who the customer was and told the employee to tell us they were fresh. Asked for an immediate refund!  Never will patronize SJM restaurants again! !!!

After reading Monica's review I had to try... the location of this place is really tucked away.

There's a tiny sign & the parking lot runs parallel to Umbria (not directly on Umbria).  I rang the doorbell & a man appeared out the doorway and asked how many.

I tried both varieties - $1.50 for two cinnamon & $1 for two large salted braids.  DELICIOUS!  Infinitely better than Philly Pretzel.

When in doubt call ahead to make sure they're open, I believe they close around 4:30.
The food was not very good and the fellow at the drink stand threatened to come outside and bash in my head.  I don't think I will go back or suggest this one to my friends.

So where do I begin?

Let's start with the sandwich.  It just wasn't that good.  At least compared to Genos.  It tasted like a White Castle hamburger.

The folks that work there were kind of jerks.  I mean come'on I'm giving you my hard earned money you should at least appreciate it.

The seating was nice.

I'll be at Geni's or Guey Louis next time.

My husband ordered with Pat cheesesteak sandwich and I took a bit to compare between Pat and Geno.  I would say the sandwiches look similar except Geno steak look thicker.  But i would say I like Pat sandwich better because the meat is softer and just the right moist in the sandwich.  Geno sandwich is too much juice that it make the sandwich soggy afterward.  Both sandwich is about 10 inches and cost about $9.  Overall, I think the sandwich is good, but not amazing.  I wouldn't come to Philly just for their sandwiches.

Five Guys is the Mecca for a cheap non Pub burger in Philadelphia, if you are just too lazy to work up your Bubba's burger at home just have your pal drop you off and circle back for you after a not so quick take out . If you happen to find the Parking gods smile at you for a meter parking chance by all means munch on their peanuts and savor the best cheap great tasting oozing  burger Philly has to offer.  You will forget to eat at McDonalds or Burger King after you savor the liberal amount of juiciness  these burgers  have. Parking is the only minus factor here because if you took a car and didnt find a meter within a mile of walking chances are your burger is cheaper than your parking. The staff is okay and the condiments are a tad to be reckoned with stick to sauteed mushrooms and onions with your cheseburger and youre on cruise control to carnivore bliss. If they only had a better selection but hey its a burger joint not Johnny Rockets. Fries are so rustic (meaning you get the peels and all) but they were great . The brown bag just adds that old school (non California tacky thing to it). Five guys Burger... please stay at Center City unlike the GAP store across you....

I ordered a cheesesteak wit and it was mediocre at best! The flavor of the steak and onions was good however the American cheese was NOT melted at all!!! If you go here only get your cheesesteak with wiz, NOT American OR provolone cheese!!! They do not serve their sandwiches hot as is evidenced by the unmelted cheese! Make sure to eat your sandwich quickly as the outdoor seating in the winter and spring only worsens the problem of the lukewarm sandwiches!

Decent cheese steaks! It would've been nice if I was able to eat it warm. But it took me an hour to get back to the hotel when it's freezing cold. There's no sit in as it is outside. They're cash only so make sure you have cash when you come here.

Finally, we got to experience what this war was about...

The only parking spot we ended up finding was closest to Pat's. We had the original intention of trying both Pat's and Geno's, but because the lines weren't stretching to Rittenhouse Square we decided to try one at a time. Now, this might have been a mistake, because by the time we got to Geno's we had already eaten one steak.

Anyways, disregarding all the errors we made in trying to achieve a fair taste test. we decided to try Pat's first, onions wit. Although, when I ordered I definitely got it wrong because I said 'onions with cheese whiz'. They didn't seem to care though and slapped together all seven heavens, the earth, sun, and the moon in about 7 seconds.

Wow. All I can say is wow. The cheese whiz complimented the steak extremely well, and though I was a little exhausted by the end of the sandwich, I can still say that every bite of it was bold, intense, and filled with flavor. I really prefer the way they do their steak because its so much easier to eat and it seems to let the fat and juice of the beef explode in your mouth. Not only this, but it seems like you get more food for the price compared to the neighbors. In addition, the onions were perfectly sautéed and so the whole sandwich was like a well-executed blueprint. This pile of grease, meat, cheese, and bread was enough to give us "the Itis" and put us to sleep.

With the consent of my significant other, we both agree that between Pat's and his neighbor, Pat's has our patronage. We both tried a couple of steaks around the area, and I definitely think we will be coming back here.
