As per my typical MO, when I'm in the States I like trying one or two fast foods joints that we don't have up in my neck of the woods in Canada. On this visit, Chick-fil-A was that fast food joint on a stopover. 

The menu is a lot more limited than most of their competition, but doing a few things well is better than doing many mediocre dishes. I went with the regular Chick-fil-A sandwich with lettuce and tomato, waffle fries and a lemonade. After a short wait, my girlfriend and I were seated in the food court area seating for our calorie bombs and people watching.

The piece of lettuce was obscenely large so I had to break it down into a few pieces to make it manageable, but it was nice and crisp and a vibrant green. The lightly toasted bun held up well and the star of the show, the chicken, was juicy and well seasoned and I enjoyed the crunchy breading.

The waffle fries were some of the best waffle fries I've had - nice and crisp and not suffering the all too frequent sogginess that they can suffer from. Extra large ketchup containers made dipping easy.

The lemonade could have used more tang and less sugar, but it was still decent.

All in all, it was a successful indulgence in one the many artery-thickening options that I, for better or worse, do not typically have.

I'm a true Philly foodie... Pats is The Classic Cheese Steak. Their secret? Bits of steak from the spatula tends to fall into their cheese wiz pot. so the flavors basically fuse. Its a good intro to the cheese steak but as far as best in town? That's debatable.

This town invented cheesesteaks, and Pat's has the rep to be the first.  That said, the first time I went is unforgettable.  There was a line of people winding around the building, but that's ok because it moves fast due to the order taker telling the indecisive people to move aside until they are certain what they want.  You can read the menu while you stand in line, people!  Don't get all huffy if you don't have the intelligence to make a decision by the time you approach the counter.  There are smarter people behind you who are very hungry, ready to wring your neck so the order taker just saved your life!  The steaks are shaved thin which makes them even tastier, and just thinking of the available condiments outside make my mouth water.  The hot spicy roast peppers make them the best!

I am reading a Lot of reviews about Pats vs Genos. But most people dont know what they are talking about..

I went to Philly Just for the Damn Cheesesteaks and I had Both Pat's and Geno's to compare the two..




To me Pat's wins, by a very small margin.. #1 because it seems to be the more Authentic one, and #2 because of how the steak is chopped...... 

My favorite cheesesteak would have to be Pat's cheesesteak with wiz cheese and grilled onions. The flavors simply blend together very well..

Geno's tastes almost identical, but it seems like just a carbon copy of Pat's to me.. But I will write a review for geno's and give them 5 stars as well.. because they taste just as good.. I just dont like the way the meat is sliced.

For me the quintessential cheesesteak would be a Cheesesteak from Pat's with Both Wiz and White American cheese, with grilled onions.. I have yet to try an authentic Pat's or genos cheesesteak with provolone , mushrooms and bell peppers.. I think It will not be as good as  a plain old cheesesteak with wiz..



Lastly  I must mention that after trying an authentic cheesesteak, the closest we have to this is called "Phillys best" and Im telling you, it rivals Pats and geno's Dangerously close...
Terrible, terrible service.   Ended up walking out after more than 20 minutes of waiting to have our drink order taken.

It's a shame that this is one of the most famous cheesesteak places in Philadelphia.  While the food can be decent to pretty good at times, this place gets an unfavorable review for three reasons.

First of all, the service is awful.  The people who work here typically make a gimmick out of how nasty they can be to their paying customers.  It's not surprising that the national image of Philadelphia is so poor when you get treated like a jerk for no reason because Pat's staff thinks that you should have the privilege to pay for their product.

Second of all, the service wouldn't factor as much if their product was consistent, but it isn't.  Don't be surprised if one of the following happens: your roll is stale, the meat is gristly, or they got the order wrong.  I wouldn't bother to tell them about it though since you'll probably just wind up getting more frustrated.

Lastly - and in fitting with the theme that they don't take pride in their business - is the state of their location.  I'm not sure if there could be a more stark contrast between Pat's and Geno's.  On one side of the street, you have Pat's, where it looks like they haven't even taken the time to powerwash the place since when the first Rocky was filmed.  On the other side of the street is Geno's where they impeccably maintain not one, but two street corners.

In summary, this review is not a recommendation to avoid going to Pat's as much as it is a warning.  Go to Pat's once or very infrequently to get the experience.  I wouldn't recommend becoming a regular here though.
When two lonely women lock eyes in Chipotle, a bond is made. A connection, an understanding between two fake-Mexican-loving overeaters.

Why has this place been around so long?? Okay Im going to start with a few things right off the bat....the guy in the back area was picking his boogars when i walked over to get my fries...BARF..he did wash his hands right after so I can give him credit for that, but, dude.....that is freaking disgusting. The meat sucks...flavor less...but the fries are good. I think the prices for the quality is shitty. Geno's across the street looks like a joke too.....the only reason I went here is because I was starving and my friend lives on that block....although i must admit i was a bit curious. One more thing....its really really dirty and gross.....i wanted to scrub myself with a brillo pad immediately!

Friends from Philly rave about Pats. Sandwich was tasty. However, cheese fries were the real winner here.

They do need to have seating inside, especially for winter months. There was a line but it moves fast. You will order and pay for sandwich at one window, pick it up in the next. Be ready to order, they will rush you through it. You go to another window to order, pay and pick up your fries and sodas.

It was an experience.

How can you NOT give Pat's 5 stars? This IS THE PLACE to get a cheesesteak in the town and the original restaurant that made it famous. I have driven through Philly, and anywhere near it at ALL times of the day and middle of the night to find a crowd here enjoying the fantastic fare at Pats. 

There may be some locals reviewing Pats and giving it low stars- but I have to disagree- if there are better cheesesteaks in Philly, thats great; but for how long have they been in operation? Are they open at 3am? Most likely you will find some fantastic steaks in Philly- but Pats for me takes the, um steak- they are the ORIGINAL, in business for 82 YEARS (as of 2012), the quality is top notch, and the outdoor seating and stainless steel counter and building exteriors bring you back to another era.

Wit or witout? (grilled onions), I say wit- but definitely READ the menu first and choose your toppings and cheese preference before stepping to the counter (see below). My favorites? Mushroom cheesesteak wit, the cheese fries are a heart attack waiting to happen but OH so good; I suggest ordering two different sandwiches and sharing a large cheesefry order.

Tips for Ordering at Pat's:

The line at Pat's King of Steaks moves quickly, so it's best to be prepared -- know what you want, and how to order it by the time you get to the front of the line!

Step 1
Specify if you want your steak with (wit) or without (wit-out) onions

Step 2
Specify Plain, Cheez Whiz, Provolone, American or Pizza Steak

Step 3
Have your money ready. We are cash only.

Step 4
Order your just your steak at the first window. The second window is for fries and drinks.

Step 5
Eat up while it's hot!

I love their happy hour deal--the delicious margarita pitchers are half price.  that is, their usual 20-25 dollar- totally worth it- margs are half that.  Nice.  I'm a fan of happy hour in general, but if i can slip in here on a weeknight before 7 to get that deal, I'm even happier!  

Their Sunday brunch is also decent.

I've been here since I was a kid. My dad and I would use to go here every night after he teaches me how to drive.

As for the food, the cheesesteaks are OK. I've definitely had better, so Pat's is really overrated (saying this from a Philly native POV). I love how they made the prices come out even as well. As for the fries, it's great with the cheese. Pat's is also a great place to get some late night food as well, after a night from the bars/clubs. Therefore, it does get packed at night so watch when you go.

Service is barely there, since all you do is order from a window. They aren't always nice, as well. Price is a little tad experience; I think it's because of its so-called popularity. It is cash only as well. There are many tables surrounding it for seating, but they might be all full if there's a crowd.

As for its rivalry with Geno's, I say the main difference is how they prepare the steak part of the cheesesteak. Pat's is the traditional (in my sense) cut up into pieces/minced, and Geno's are thin, round slices. Geno's also hype themselves greatly with tons of pictures of famous celebrities, while Pat's is more humble. I've always gone to Pat's since I was a kid, so I can't really say more for Geno's.


Recommendation: If you would like a cheesesteak that can kind of sum up the Philly Cheesesteak Experience, I'd definitely try Jim's on South Street. Be warned: line is ridiculously long during the day.

I came here on a Sunday evening after hanging out at Sound Fountain (an awesome outdoor dance party at the nearby Fountain the last Sunday of every summer month), I had a decent buzz from the sangria and sunlight and a big appetite for some good Mexican food.

FIRST IMPRESSIONS:
Los Caballitos is located on a section of East Passyunk that has seen an incredible revitalization, a breath of fresh air in the area filled with hip and stylish storefronts.  The palpable energy is captured by this Cantina, with outdoor tables completely packed with diners of all sorts of styles and scenes (a surprising, unfamiliar, yet welcome sight).  Inside, you have your typical Tex-Mex Cantina, the orange walls, the tacky (yet authentic) decor and xmas lights.

THE FOOD:
I was starving, and surprised at the prices on the menu, not expecting a filling meal, I ordered my mainstay of Carnitas in burrito form.  I was completely wrong-- the portions are very reasonable, I was stuffed by the end.  We also had chips, and my date got salad and ribs, all were very good.  I guess when it comes down to it, this Cantina doesn't push the envelope, but it does the typical Mexican American fare very well.  I've blasted other restaurants for not being creative or delicious, but even though Los Caballitos isn't really creative, it is delicious.  They have everything they should have on there, and next time I eat here, I will be more adventurous.

THE DRINKS:
Another way Los Caballitos does things right is their Margaritas.  Now, the subject of Margaritas in Philly is as debatable as the subject of the best Cheesesteak, but this Cantina has the essentials in place-- up, on the rocks or frozen, and any flavor or type of tequila you could want.  I can't really measure how powerful they were, but I know they were doing their job.

THE PRICING:
As mentioned before, I was initially put off by the higher than average prices on their menu, but the food really is good, it's served in generous proportions.  Next time I'll try an entree and see if it delivers on its price. 

THE BOTTOM LINE:
Look, there as many Cantinas in Philly as there are Starbucks, the issue becomes not which is the best, but which ones don't suck, which ones are worth eating at.  Cantina Los Caballitos is definitely worth checking out in my book.

The first time I went to the Cantina I was pleasantly drunk and my memory of it is fuzzed over with the hue of alcohol inspired benevolence. I remember really liking the chili-ribs and the Rogue Chipotle Ale.  TK said the place reminded him of a Chiles which is not what I remembered at all so we went back last night. We were in pursuit of a six pack to take back home with us.  They had no six packs but we stayed for a drink anyway.  

There was no beer I particularly wanted on the menu so I got a glass of wine (which was unfortunately served in a tumbler rather than a wine glass. Boo hiss. It was pretty good, though it had probably been out a bit longer than it should have.  They seemed to have a decent selection of wines as opposed to their sad beer menu. We had shots of Powers which tasted odd.  We weren't sure whether it was a good thing or a bad thing...eventually we decided it was good. 

I think the main problem with the place is that they are going for this Mexican thing but there's no authenticity since as   Juicebomb pointed out so eruditely it's run by gringos for gringos.  The problem I was having with the beer menu was that it had all Mexican beers and I'm not a huge fan of Mexican beer, being that I, myself, am a gringo.  I think they should rethink the whole concept, but that's just me.

First time there, guy at the window was extremely rude and seemed to be very annoyed. I asked him what was on a regular cheesesteak, expecting to hear peppers, onion, etc... what I heard was "whatever's on the board"  I ordered a cheesesteak with peppers, onions, mushrooms, and cheese.  It was dry (where's the cheese) and tasteless. "Famous" THATS A JOKE! Definitely won't be back.

The philly cheese steak is great with the cheese. That night with my friends we tried both Geno's and pat's and I end up loving pat's. Geno's cheese sucks. Not enough. The meat size are larger but the cheese not as good as pat's. But if pat a puts its cheese with Geno's meat they will make an amazing philly cheese steak. I will definitely say Pat's won my heart in the competition with their cheesiness
Better than Gino's that is for sure. But it's not the best cheesesteak, that goes to Dalasandros. But, if you want to do the touristy thing, come here not Gino's. At least Pats is edible.

make no mistake. neither pat's nor geno's would make the top 50 cheesesteak list in this city. they probably wouldn't even make top ten in that neighborhood alone. they're tourist traps. overpriced. old bread. cold meat. dirty ass facilities. 

however, if you MUST pick between pat's and geno's, pat's is definitely the way to go. service is better, and food is prepared with a little bit more care. 

but if you find yourself in this area for steaks, just walk east like two blocks and go to Cosmi's deli. it's a small shop that you'd never guess has a cheesesteak infinitely better than pat's or geno's.

As so many people have said in past reviews and well overall when you say Philly..You gotta get a cheese steak. Now where you go I guess is a whole other ball of wax, but faced with that internal monologue myself it lead me here to Pat's and boy was that an amazing choice.

At the time it was about 15 degrees outside so safe to say the outside seating area was readily available. There really isn't a whole lot of picnic tables for seating, but I can certainly see on a hot day how it could pack in pretty quickly. Between the whole Pat's and Geno saga the neon lighting actually gave me a Vegas feel which just added to the ambiance of actually just being able to do a taste test.

As you walk up to the window to order I admit I was taken back at first with the ordering system as they have that down Pat (no pun intended). The following 5 steps to order scarred me for life as it gets intimidating even with no one around me in line. Ha-ha!

Step 1
Specify if you want your steak with (wit) or without (wit-out) onions

Step 2
Specify Plain, Cheez Whiz, Provolone, American or Pizza Steak

Step 3
Have your money ready. We are cash only.

Step 4
Order just your steak at the first window. The second window is for fries and drinks.

Step 5
Eat up while it's hot!

After braving that debacle it was time to tear into what I felt was one of the better cheese steaks I have consumed to date. I actually know for a fact this will kill any hopes of finding a great local cheese steak which at least means I know what one should taste like and should look like for that matter!

For starters, the portion size of the cheese steak alone is definitely surprising as it was pretty big and filling as well. The bread was soft and easy on the teeth, but just the right hint of crisp to still provide a crunch. As for the steak it was tender and partnered with the grilled onions just blew my mind. Finally the piece de resistance, CHEEZ FREAKIN' WIZ! That was not skimped out on and it was literally everywhere as shown in my photo, but hey that sent the whole thing into a state of euphoria

In all fairness I wasn't able to get to Geno's, but I have to pace myself for Philly or I'd never go back. All in all this was a very well put together "sandwich" and Pat is certainly steer royalty for so many years for a damn good reason: QUALITY!

Pats or Genos? I have to say that Pat's is the winner (IMO), however to be completely honest, i didn't love either sandwiches and found faults with both.

Pat's was messier and more moist though which is why i declared it the winner. The flavors of both were still there. Again you can't complain when you have melting cheese, with moist beef and grilled onions. The beef at Pat's is chopped up and oily, so it is nice and moist and makes a nice mess of the wrapper. The onions however are minced small than Geno's and they have an unattractive dark yellow hue to them where it looks like they were overcooked in fat/oil. 

Again the line wasn't there at Pat's either at around 9:15pm on a Friday night, but the tables were also packed. 

The place has a 50 cent premium of Genos. Is it worth it?  I suppose, but to be honest with you all, i feel that Carl's and Shorty's of NYC make their cheesesteaks better than Pat's & Geno's. Sorry..

This was the most disgusting cheesesteak I ever had!! It was dry, and the meat looked old and unsanitary! I will never order from this place again. As soon as I had a bite of this sandwich it was terrible. Very bland! My stomach is starting to hurt now.. I don't know why this place has any kind of fame. Their cheesesteak lacks taste and texture. If your trying to get good cheesesteak, go to Jim's on 4th and South Street Or Max's steaks. A lot of colleagues talk about this spot, and I figured I give it a try and taste for myself. 

I didn't even check the yelp reviews, just so that I can have a clear mind and offer my own opinion about this place. Now I feel like I should of checked the yelp reviews before coming to this place lol.

Awesome cheesesteaks and I'd definitely say they uphold their title of "King of Steaks" quite well in the Philadelphia area.  This is only if I was grading them based on their cheesesteaks though.  

Their customer service is quick and they really don't care about their customer.  They just want you to get in and out as quickly as possible so that they can service the next person (even if they don't have a line).  

The cheesesteaks arrive speedy-quick (as in I ordered and within 10 seconds, she was pushing it through the order window to me).  I'd def go back for a quick fast food fix next time I am in the area, especially because it is so affordable (less than $10).

Rude and aggorant front of the house staff, more so condescending and mocking, than accommodating and inviting. Last night I pointed out to the busser that our table was extremely sticky, like all over. It either wasn't wiped or was done so with an extremely dirty towel. Anyway, thinking he'd simply grab a clean towel and give it a quick wipe, instead he gave me some story about the humidity. No, humidity doesn't cause stickiness to your table which makes you have to peel your menu from it. When I asked him to touch it himself, he did, then callously offered to put us back in line to wait for a different table if we didn't like that one. Sooooo you felt it was dirty too, aaaand thennnn... Passed the buck? Not really a home run with service. Also quite embarrassing when bringing two guests who'd never been after I'd raved about how great it is. I guess times have changed at the cantina. 

Also watching their front of the house manager (blonde lady) dancing around with her staff like an idiot while tables sit needing things and the place is dirty is ridiculous. Get someone in there who can professionally run a bar and up your service game. 

Minus one star for shitty attitude 
Minus one star for filthiness
Minus one star for being slow and inattentive 
Minus one star for poor management 
Remaining star is for the food, recently the only thing okay there

Save your energy and frustration and go somewhere else until they turn it around.

In the very controversial Pat's vs. Geno's debate, I believe that Pat's is the clear winner. I took a day trip with my friends from Virginia just to take the Pat's-Geno's challenge and it was well worth it. Pat's was ooey gooey whizzy goodness. The meat was juicy and the bread was perfect. Geno's Steaks didn't even stand a chance in my eyes. I had some pretty high cheesesteak standards after eating at Jim's steaks before this, and Pat's was just too good. 

I must say that I was really intimidated to order because of all the horror stories I heard of people being sent to the back of the line because they didn't know how to order properly. After being coached by a local, and practicing for a good five minutes, I swallowed my fear and took the front stage to the ordering counter. I'd like to say that I looked like a pro and that made me really happy! If you like the spice, order hot peppers on the side! Make sure you don't walk over to Geno's with your Pat's steak unless you want to get cussed out. Oh, and enjoy!

Tip on how to order:
Whiz - Cheese whiz
Whit - Onions
Prov - Provolone
"Ay, yo! Can I get one whiz whit and prov"

Steaks sandwiches are excellent. Ambience is lacking. Tables are all outside and usually dirty with food from previous patrons. Best to buy and take somewhere else to eat. Order takers are impatient when crowded. Order wit provolone (not Cheese whizz); with swiss. Add whatever topping you want (fried onions, sweet peppers, etc.), but be fast about it or they will be taking the order from the guy behind you before you know it.

By far the best spot in that strip at Temple. The people who run it are extremely nice and polite, which always makes you feel more comfortable when getting quick food. 

The gyros are really good and are made to order. The wraps and hoagies are pretty good as well. Even their sandwiches are pretty big and have good ingredients.

While spending the day in Philadelphia we decided to try the cheese steak challenge between Geno's and Pat's. After trying both of these sandwiches, in my view, Pat's won the challenge hands down.

The reason we found Pat's to be better than Geno's was because the bread here seemed more fresh and the steak was better seasoned. We also enjoyed the fact that it was cut up unlike the steak at Geno's.

In the end the staff here was polite unlike Geno's. The sandwiches tasted way better and the overall experience here was comfortable unlike the interaction at Geno's. 

The final true reason why this restaurant was better was because it wasn't filled with anti immigration propaganda like Geno's. This made our dinning experience comfortable rather than feeling as though we should be looking out for La Migra.

Food: Great food for an affordable price. I got the shrimp burrito and it was massive, heavy, and full full full. Really worth the price. My only suggestion to the chef would be to cut the shrimp up instead of putting whole pieces in there. Everyone in my party enjoyed their meal, and they had a good amount of veggie friendly options, and even mock meat! Extra yay!

Ambiance: The music, while really fun, was so amazingly loud. So so loud. I was sitting with three other people in a booth and we constantly had to repeat ourselves to hear our conversation over the music. We asked the waitress if it could be turned down, and it was for about three songs. I guess whoever was controlling the volume wasn't happy, because it started playing even louder than before. And on top of that, the speakers aren't great quality and you could hear static as the bass thumped. Meh. I would suggest coming when you're not planning on having a long conversation or catching up with someone.

Decor: Super cute. Not too crowded, fun multi-colored lights hanging all around, nicely themed.
Don't know how this place has 3 stars. The sandwiches are overpriced and poor quality. You get a huge log of bread with a palm's worth of meat. Sodium overload. It's a one and done.

You know those times when you drive past a your favorite restaurant just to get to a McDonalds because you have a craving?  Yeah that's kind of my feeling about Pat's.  There are a hundred better places to get cheesesteaks in Philadelphia.  But sometimes i need to take the drive to South Philly and have a Pat's.
A cool place my amigos  & i go all tha time i love tha margaritas frozen or traditional tha fajitas r great the servers r cool also,i highly recommend this place!!!!!!

Drove past this place several times over the weekend while working. The line was around the building every time. Finally today no line. So I grabbed Philly cheese steak. I'm not sure why the line was so long over the weekend. Because when I ordered my sandwich. Before I could step to the next window to order a drink. My sandwich was ready. 
First clue no long line today. Second clue sandwich was immediately ready. Not at all impressed with the sandwich. I really thought with those long lines over the weekend this was going to be the ultimate Philly cheese steak. It was just a lot of plain shredded steak with not enough cheese. I ordered light onions and mushrooms and didn't taste 1 onion. It was kinda dry or maybe just unflavored. I definitely think the bread was the freshest part of this sandwich. It's not horrible but definitely not what I was expecting.  
I gave 3 stars because it was loaded with meat and I'm hoping maybe I came at the wrong time. 
$12.00 cash only sandwich

First of all let me say i was excited to come here. As it was recommended by several people. We were just visiting for the day. Food ok not much flavor so three stars. Customer service a negative ten!!! Rudest place i have ever been. They need to work on this. Yes they get busy nut no reason to be rude to new customers. Next time we come nack to town we wont be returning

my co-worker friends and I have started coming here for happy hour. 15 bucks for a pitcher of margarita, delicious chips, add some guacamole on the side, and you've got a fantastic time outside in the sun. Cute bartenders on the inside, with the ceiling decorated with Christmas lights, who can resist? Wait for a table outside was maybe 10 minutes, and they text you when it's ready.
Good steaks, better then the other. Try a whiz wit! Make sure to order correctly or you'll be redirected to the end of line to try again, and remember cash only! ($10/steak is a good rule of thumb)
Over rated! Meat looks like it had been sitting on that grill for a minute. Had Geno's not good either no seasoning on both. I would never go back. But if I have to pick one it would be Geno's

So I am here eating a cheesesteak and I am a cowboys fan and the owner of the cowboys pulls up in a black bus and the yet out to eat a cheesesteak
Food was amazing 
Saw this place on food channel and was really excited to try it

Was amazing
Pat's sucks.  So does Geno's.  If you want a good steak, any lunch cart is better.  Or try the Ethiopian cheese steak at Gojjo in on Baltimore Ave.

I love that chick fila is here at all my philly connections. I have been in a rush and hady food in less than a minute. Everyone is always nice, I have nothing to complain about. They do have. Reduced menu which means they do not carry the spicy chicken sandwich but they have the chicken bios it sandwich for breakfast and that's what I love so I'm happy.

Worst McDonalds of all time.

Not spectagious, splendiferous or special in any way.

Breakfast is the staple of McDonalds, the least common denominator, the lay-up. How do you fuck up breakfast? Its actually tougher to do it wrong.

This McDonalds does it wrong every time. Every day of the damn week. Epic Breakfast fail.

I am in super spite mode due to stale McMuffins all of the last 3 times I have gone.

Dear Ray Crock,

Have your dead corpse shoot god an email and demand new management at the del ave McDonalds so I can get some decent breakfast when I am headed to my warehouse once a week.

Dammit. For a #2 breakfast, which now costs $5.34 with an OJ, you would think its a given that I wouldnt break my tooth on the damn english muffin. Nooks and Crannies my arse, more like tungsten-carbide muffin teeth.

Cmon people! I am definitely "hatin' it".

Cmon Yelp, can't I give a bankrupt Ed McMahon style half star to this p.o.s. fast food restaurant? All in favor of instituting the "half star" say "I". 

I.
margaritas, tacos and burritos, oh my! i love this place. the food is awesome and the environment is fun and warm. servers are a little off sometimes but thats on them not the establishment.
On visit from West Coast, had cheesesteak from Pat's and Geno's.  Pat's is better, hands down.  Landslide

I'm a local and I still go here occasionally.  When it's late, for me, it's either here or Tony Luke's.  I've only gone twice to each in the past six months but the first time I went to Pat's during this time, I was impressed.  Even though it was late, they steak was great.  It seemed to have more meat than usually and I left feeling pretty full and impressed.  I tried it again a few months later and was disappointed to find it lacking that heaping portion of meat and the roll was a little hard.  I guess I've learned my lesson the hard way....for now.
I don't know why would people eat here. There's nothing like Maryland cheese steaks. I am so pissed I have no words to write this review.

Great atmosphere here! Like other south Philly spots, this place oozes character and charm. 

Had fun sitting at the bar with some new friends. The bartender was comical and prompt. 

Decent food. Didn't rock my socks. Decent drinks. Didn't booze my noozle. But would definitely come back on a rainy (or not) Tuesday evening for a random nightcap!

Scared to death while ordering....

... this is it.  The experience.

Thanks for such a lovely, heart clogging, stunning health experience. 

I think I saw demons and angels for about 20 hours.  I also had a few other local shops to make sure I was getting the best before hitting Pat's, so I might have been hallucinating at that point.

Extremely mediocre and overpriced food. It's nice to sit on a patio, but not cool to be served over cooked ribs that are too tough to chew, and greasy goat. The margaritas lacked any citrus and were weak on booze.

As with Geno's the Phillys are overpriced at $10. Very tasty indeed,  my oldest son preferred Pat's over Geno's. The outside sidewalk area was filthy with rubbish everywhere we looked. Not much to review really, cheese steaks and soda....

We decide to try both Geno and Pat at the same time so we can really tell which one we like more....  We both agree this is the winner.  The meat is just more flavor.... And add-on side is well cooked. If you like spicy, get those little pepper...  They are fun to eat.

I love that these burgers are epic! I love how many toppings you can get for free! I love that it's not much more expensive than Wendy's! I love that they give you a ton a fries! I love that they actually have spicy menu options! I even love the simple sesame buns!

I love that they're open on Sundays! So suck it, 500 degrees! People in Center City eat lunch on Sundays too!

I love that they give two patties on the standard burger but wish they had told me beforehand because I woulda gotten the smaller one-patty version instead.

The only reason why Five Guys doesn't get Five Stars is that, sadly, the burger isn't necessarily super juicy. But that's okay because they're still tastyyyyyy.

Better than Geno!  It must be the chopped up meat and the grease that pours out of my mouth when I bite into it. They stick to the ordering menu and I love the cherry papers they offer outside with the steaks. I just enjoy the atmosphere here better than the competition.

The only thing Mexican about Los Caballitos is the name. Commonly referred to as just "The Cantina."

The food leaves a lot to be desired. The Cantina is owned by the same people as the Royal Tavern and the food is basically the same but with some sort of "Mexican flair" attached to it. Most of it is pretty bland and there is really nothing you can do about it--the salsa verde isn't even spicy! The corn on the cob is a nice snack ($3), and the mahi mahi is palatable (but it's mahi mahi). As far as traditional Mexican fare, tacos or burritos, they have no idea what they're doing. I suspect there isn't one actual mexican person involved in this establishment. If you're looking for actual Mexican food, go across the street to El Zarape. 

The drink selection isn't bad. They offer various tequila flights ranging from top shelf to low end. The margaritas and mojitos are available in some interesting flavors, but they feel a little over priced, but their happy hour lasts until 7pm which cuts the price of the margs in half. They usually have Young's Double Chocolate on tap and that's enough to make up for the over priced margaritas and the so-so food.

This place is literally a block from my house and I'd go more often if the service wasn't so bad. I've been there many times and I'm not sure if I'm supposed to be seating myself or not! It's impossible to get the attention of any of the staff from the moment you walk in. If you need something after your food or drinks are served, forget about it.

Ok, when visiting a city we always like to try out what is considered a signature food for that city. Although we had been to Philly several times we had not tried the Cheesesteaks so we thought we would go to one of the big name places either Geno's or Pat's. We go a parking spot in front of Pat's so that is where we ended up. 

We got the Cheesesteaks with the works, fries and sodas which came to a total of $43 dollars for three people. We are from Chicago and this was basically an Italian beef sandwich with cheese on it. In Chicago we could have had the same thing for under $30. 

That said it was something we just had to have, a Cheesesteak from a Philly institution. They were good and I really like the bread they use. If I lived in Philly I am sure I could find something just as good for a much lower price but I would be missing out on the atmosphere.

Is this really supposed to be the quintessential Philly cheesesteak? While I love the whole cheese whiz and steak thing, the meat used here leaves a bit to be desired - chewy in a bad way and not quite the thinly chopped ribbons that I prefer. The whole sandwich construction didn't seem that much better than the cheesesteaks sold at street fairs and carnivals you can find anywhere. 

I gotta say, the best "Philly" cheesesteaks I've had are found in Boston - Carl's Steak Subs or at D'Angelo's sandwich shops (gasp! at a mass market franchise!).

Wow! This was REALLY BAD! Luke-warm meat on an average roll. Ordered American cheese. Cheese was put on cold roll with warmish meat. Cheese did not melt. Same problem at Geno's. Go to Steve's Prince of Steaks or Ishkabibbles.

The tast was awesome and definitely worth going to over Geno's.  The line moves fast and they request that you order it Philly style "wit or witout onions". Definitely get it with cheeze whiz and onions because that's classic. It only lost a point because the meat was a little grissley and the Pepsi tasted a little like coke. Overall two very enthusiastic thumbs up.

I was not a big fan of Subway - not for any particular reason, just not my thing.  Lately, I have been walking by a few Subways and saw the "Sub-A-Day" promotion for $3.50 - so I decided to go in and check it out.  I was glad I did - The first time I had the Turkey and Cheese and I went back this week and had the tuna - the taste was good.  I am not giving to make it a habit, but when in a pinch and hungry - I know that I can get a inexpensive & tasty sandwich.

I prefer Cantina Dos Segundos

Went on a Friday night. The wait for 4 was 45 minutes, as expected.  Once we sat, we ordered drinks and food and waited over an hour for our meals to arrive at the table.  I would expect this from a fine dining establishment, but not here (and we dine out very frequently).

I actually had to check in with our server (I've done it maybe once or twice before, so I never do it, I don't like to, but we didn't have all night and I was very polite about it).  Our food came out 5 minutes later, but I'm not sure if that was a coincidence or not. Our server was polite and attentive to our situation and even removed two tequila flights from our check, which was appreciated. 

The food was OK, but not worth waiting 1+ hours for.  We ended up pressed for time because we had to catch the train.  But even so...I allotted 3 hours for dinner (including wait time), so even with an hour wait time, you would think we could get through dinner in two hours...especially since we aren't the "sit and chat for hours" type.  

My suggestions:
1. Visit Cantina Dos Segundos instead.  We've always had good food, good service, and never had any issues there (and we've visited on various days and times). You will be in and out of there in a reasonable amount of time and the food is better...even though it is their sister restaurant and the menu is practically the same. 
2. Don't go here if you only have a few hours....expect to spend at least 3 hours here, surrounded by sometimes loud, drunk people (at least at night).  I'm just getting old I guess (mid-late twenties)!

Great food (especially if you're looking for a vegan or vegetarian option) and pretty good drinks. Sadly, everyone else knows it. There was a 45 minute wait on a Friday night. No food is good enough for a wait longer than half an hour! Still, mighty tasty.

My two friends and I dropped in for margaritas on National Margarita Day, which luckily happened to fall in line with Passyunk Restaurant Week 2016.

I ordered my obligatory pitcher of marg for the group and we settled into some complimentary chips and salsa... and ordered guac. By my taste, the margarita was standard; but because it was National Margarita Day (and Monday), very satisfying.

The first course was a shrimp ceviche: simple, light, delicious. The second course was a beef meatball type thing over rice with brussel sprouts: decent, seemingly traditional, but nothing special. The third course was a chocolate cake that didn't do much for me.

All together the experience was ok, but I've had better versions of each of the items at other places. It does seem like a cool place to spend happy hour in the warmer months. I may be back for that.
Awesome cheese steak!  Awesome!  A must when in Philly.  I would travel 1000 miles to get there just for one of their steaks!

Well...its better than McDonald's or  Burger King, in any case.
Its great for a what it is: a simple burger & fries joint to grab a bite or a fast lunch.  So if you go in looking for nothing more than that, its fantastic.  If you're looking for a really great burger, maybe some onion rings or even something slightly healthy or inventive, this is definitely where you do not want to go.

Now I've only eaten here once - for the first time last week - and being that I just wanted a plain 'ol burger & fries lunch I was very pleased.  The burger didn't strike me much at all, but I actually thought my cajun fries were pretty darned tasty.

The place is clean enough, the service is fast enough, the food is good enough.
Personality, style, atmosphere, broad menu - not so much, but if you actually walk into this place expecting that, then sorry bud, you deserve to be disappointed!

We were obviously excited to try a real Philly 
Cheesesteak Sandwich and a friend refer us to this spot and geno's across the street 
we tried both but pat's was definitely light years better in my opinion! must see in philly for sure =)
Get the American wit instead of the yellow cheese wiz. I like to eat it with a side of marinated pepper they have at the counter. It's a good steak sandwich fresh and delicious.

Was going to do both Cheese Steak joints, but Gino's had a anniversary of Gino's death 50 cent cheese steak day with over 500 people in line so opted for Pat's. For what they are doing here this place is great. Love the wiz and the mean people that work at the counter. IMO Gino's is better but not better enough to wait in line with 500 people to eat.

Pat's vs. Geno's. The great debate. Personally, I'm not a fan of cheese-steaks but "when in Rome" right? I visited this location earlier this year around March with a group of friends.

I liked Pat's more than Geno's but cheese-steaks wise, I like Steve's Prince of Steaks because there's more variety. Pat's is chopped up and was more juicy compared to Geno's.

Tried it once, but I wouldn't want to go back.
Blaze pizza is the best pizza in town.I enjoy the pizza and customer service I received a employee named T seems to know how to treat people which seems to be lost in a lot of places these days .

Don't waste your time, go to Geno's. My rating is a combo of service and cheesesteak.

Service: If you don't say it exactly the right way, they send you to the back of the line. They're rude at the window,  just "What do you want?" in a very curt and unfriendly tone. It feels like they're annoyed you even bothered to be there.

Food: The bread is not soft. In fact, it felt like we got the last of yesterday's bread or something. The meat is decent but not juicy. The mushrooms were hardly cooked and there wasn't even much cheese on mine! I'm uncertain how many ways you can screw up a cheesesteak but Pat's found a way. 

Random annoyance: Why doesn't anyone cut these damn sandwiches in half? Picking up the entire thing feels silly and makes me feel like a child eating it.

So I finally went here today for lunch. I mean it is good but def nothing out of this world. I was surprised how big the burger was - I got a regular cheese burger and it was 2 good sized patties. The fries were good but not amazing - and they give you a ton. It was surprisingly quick for the time of day (12:45pm). I will def be back.
Too expensive there better burger places then this fudruckers and cheese burger cheese burger just to name a few event sonic.

I had to try the place that invented the cheese steak so yes we decided to go to Pat's over Geno's.  I knew what to expect as far as lines and such so that was no surprise.  I was able to find parking in the neighborhood so I was lucky.  

The line wraps around this pie shaped building and when I finally got to the front of the line I had taken note that it took about 30 minutes to get to the front.  Not as long as Jim's on South which already made me happier.

I had ordered 3 whiz wits wrapped because if you don't say wrapped they will just give you the sandwich as if you were going to eat it at a table outside and not bag it for you.  

Honestly in the time it takes for you to pay the sandwich is basically ready.  The place is a factory at pumping out sandwiches... 

Note only order the sandwiches in the long line.  If you want something else like a drink that's another line but that line is not as long and slow moving as the cheese steak line.  

Read the sign on how to order.  Don't make people beyond you angry because you're a tourist and take too long... whiz wit wrapped... 3 syllables easy...

I liked the sandwich although the meat seemed dryer than what Jim's served me.  It was definitely a different cut of meat too.  It seemed more stringy than the finer sliced up meat at Jim's on South.  

Either way I liked it and it was good although not out of this world fantastic.  Overall I like Tony Luke's best out of the 3 places I visited in Philadelphia.  

Pat's is the original though still so respect the creation and love the history.

Just as delicious as any stand alone store and the line moves fast as there are always 3-4 employees at the registers. The food is consistent, the people are friendly and the price is right. Located in a courtyard with several other restaurants, there is ample seating (or look for a rocking chairs across the way for a chance to plug in your phone). This is always my stop on my way home from Philly!

They have a sign outside that says "we appreciate your business". Must be a brotherly love thing. Or maybe its to make up for the fact that the guy behind the counter is a total prick who's about as pleasant as a middle eastern dictator. Fine fine, its a Philly thing. Anyway, within seconds of finishing your sentence you'll have your cheeseteak. I got mine with mushrooms, onions, peppers and provolone. Pretty damn good, but I prefer mine hogie style which didn't seem to be an option. The meat here is supposed to be better and the crowd seemed mostly local as opposed to the tourist ridden Genos. 

Its a great cheeseteak-- supposedly the original. It was definitely one of the 5 best I have ever eaten in my life, but was it the best outright? I don't know if I could say that for sure. They offer some condiments which included this delicious cherry tomato looking red pepper. Hot sauce, spicy mustard, and relish are other optional addons after you are served. Its hardly a pleasant dining experience but you come here for one thing only. I guess you'll hafta  try it if you're in town. You might think its the best thing ever or you might be sorta nonchalant about it.

meh. the pat's vs. geno's rivalry is better than either of their steaks.

the bad. i had the mushroom provolone cheesesteak. cheese was half melted, mushrooms were canned, meat was bland. i was a bit disappointed. i unfortunately didnt get a whiz cheese steak... which is what i got at geno's... would've been a more even comparison. 

the good. the cheese fries were amazing. the whiz cheese provides a smooth contrasting texture to the well seasoned, not overcooked, fries. in addition, their service is much better than geno's.

two stars for the steak, four stars for the fries.

go to jim's.

I've been going here quite a few times and I'm defintiely enjoy eating here. I love how the cheesesteak taste compared to other places I've gone to. The best part about this place and the one across from it (Genos) is that they open 24 hours. I have the night shift so There's barely any place open at that time. I also like how their fries are super crispy and on the onions on their cheesesteak are actually sauteed than just cooked.
This place deserves better reviews or at least less harsh reviewers. Good food, same great price, and the guy and the cash register was funny to boot. Can't knock it.

Not the best in Philly but pretty damn close. Between pats and genos this place wins in a knockout. Thicker slices of meat, more cheese, and quick service gets the out of town tourists and us locals our late night fix after the bars. Tourist pricing kicks this down to four stars but one of the best
Its not that great place... their meat was not cooked all the way. Although not chopped steaks were on point, steak, meat, not being cooked all the way made me to loose my taste at Genos. PATs is

During an epic roadtrip, we stopped by here for famous philly cheesesteaks. I split a cheesesteak with onions n mushrooms n wiz with 2 of my friends. We ate here immediately finishing up at Genos; and I'm so glad we ate this after because this was the obvious winner of the two. Bread's meh but there was more flavor from the onions and mushrooms. They give u more meat here too! Worth it. =)

Pats was good.  Both Pats and Geno's are not big on customer service.  If I return to Philly I wouldn't visit again.  Not too much different from others who reviewed.  I went to pats first.  There wasn't anyone there so the attendant started asking me to order.  I was trying to figure out what I wanted and he kept asking so I said Philly wit onions... He said cheese? I said yes.  He said shoulda told me that... No worries.  I got my sandwich and begin to eat it.  I decided to save some for later and try Geno's.  mistake... I had the other half of my sandwich in hand and my husband was in line at Geno's to order their sandwich.  I went to get a napkin.  One of the guys said... Don't use our napkins with that pats sandwich in your hand.  Those are for paying customers only.  I apologized and tried to clear up the misunderstanding to no avail.  Me... I apologize.  My husband is in line for one of your sandwiches.  We want to compare and take the food challenge.  Another geno employee came from the back and says...we paid for those not pats.  I said I understand I think their is a misunderstanding.  The guy said no their isn't.  We don't want your money.  Ok....we left.  I wouldn't recommend either.  We will try tony lukes next time.  Have fun and tourist beware

I waited for 30 minutes to get a cheesesteak and was not exactly blown away by the taste. I was weirded out when I was told to get the cheesesteak with 'whiz' (i.e. Cheez Whiz)...but surprisingly it was what made the cheesesteak. The quality of meat wasn't that great for the price...$9 for a footlong. I thought the peppers really added to the flavor of the cheesesteak (and they weren't spicy at all).

There is a separate line for fries and drinks, so make sure you don't ask to get fries and a coke in the cheesesteak line or else you will get your head ripped off.

Can't compare this place to Geno's since I didn't go there, and sadly I would have to say I've had better cheesesteak...in Texas (TEXADELPHIA)!

Don't get discouraged by the line, it moves fast! But practice your order so you say it write and the line keeps moving! And don't try to use a credit card!  Fries and sodas at the second window! 

So much better than Geno's! Geno's just has lights, glits, and glam-- the steaks at Pat's are way better!

THE BEST!!!  The Orignal (and thats a FACT!!)  This is heaven on earth and a MUST do at least once in a lifetime-  Pat's for me is the best one going- A MUST have whenever I am within the area. I have even taken a "drive" that has led me to their front door-

Pat's is good but the price point over the years has become ridiculous. For an east coaster who now lives in the Midwest, I always hit Pat's and Geno's when I pass through Philly. Pat's still has upper hand in flavorful and juicy meat. I understand inflation and the tourist hype guys, but come on... It now costs me close to $20 with a side and soda. It's still a good sandwich. The humorous ordering instructions sign is worth a visit.

The food is quite good, and the free chips and salsa are fresh, tasty, and plentiful.  Service is consistent, fast, and suprisingly attentive given the always rapid pace.

Did I mention the fab margarita selection?  If there are two or more of you it's definitely worth getting a pitcher... if you don't mind the buzz you'll carry out with you afterward.  Blood Orange is my fave, but I recently had the Cucumber and it was really interesting and perfect for a hot summer day.

If you've ever had tacos at a legit taqueria you will be slightly disappointed with Cantina's version, however.  Close to the real thing but not quite.  The burrito's won't set the world on fire either, but they are pretty good and you certainly get a lot of food for the price.

A "con" that continues unabated:  The acoustics inside the restaurant somehow seem to amplify the crowd noise to the point where it borders on being uncomfortably loud.

Fresh out of the gym in search of a late night meal and what do I spy on my Yelp "Open Now" search... I called to confirm the kitchen was still open and made a beeline for the Cantina.

The waitstaff was slightly uncoordinated so I waited a little longer than I should have in a dining area so lightly populated.  My server's pleasant attitude and excellent recommendation made up for it. The Carolina BBQ Seitan Burrito was delicious.

The next time I'm in these parts late night with a hunger in me, I'll probably visit this place again.

Enjoyed the experience at Pat's. Actually conducted a taste test with Geno's and had fun comparing the two as probably most people do. Cash only and parking can be found street side with a little patience. Well worth the visit and will certainly do it again.  Split down the middle with the group as to the favorite.

Good the first 10 times you go, but then you get sick of the lines and the high price and once the iconography of the place wears off, you come to the realization that it's really not that great.

Having said that, if you've never had it, it's one of those things where you should try it just to say you've tried it.

While I will admit that the food at Adriatic Grill is good, the customer service is enough to make me never eat there again. The woman that works the front is very rude. I've been hung up on while ordering, she's rolled her eyes in person and has said things under her breath when asked a question regarding my paid order. Usually the Cook in the back would intervene when she's in a bad mood. While he is a pleasure to deal with, he does not change my viewpoint on their horrible service. Temple has a plethora of other food stands and truck that no one should be subjected to horrible service. Eat somewhere else.

My first experience with real Philly subs was here.  I became an instant fan.  The globs of liquid cheeze on top can be a disgusting thought, but worth the gluttony.  Real steak somewhere in there too.  Can always get caught in dreaming of going back there.
Pat's is ok. It is over rated. Their meet is not the best. Their toppings are pretty good. The line can get long so pack your patience.

This is THE ORIGINAL steak place. Went to check out all the fuss. Very good steak... but just not a ton of meat for the roll. All in all, flavor is good, but size is too small for 8 bucks. Environment is cool... if you're okay with feeling pressured to get your order in quick so they can get to the next customer. Actually felt stressed as I approached, cause the dude at the counter was just yelling 'Next' over and over again every 2 seconds... and with a line around the building... u get the point. Even though I only gave it a 3, I'll still go back if I'm in the area.

This is my second favorite Philly Cheesesteak place after Geno's which is right across the street. I have been to this restaurant many times. The staff at Pat's is not as friendly as the staff at Geno's. Nevertheless, they serve one hell of a cheesesteak so I am giving this place 4 stars.

i too have taken the pat's versus geno's test and quite honestly the only difference i can see ( or taste ) is that pat's chops the meat up and geno's leaves it as it was put on the grille, so the are both equally good pat's just looks a bit dated, could use a refresh on the building

Pat's is a philly landmark. The lines are long on the weekends and I would say that the food is okay. I live a few blocks from there and have been once for the expierence. I like Pat's more than Geno's... But I certainly don't think they have the holy grail of cheese steaks. In short, lots of fun, a good photo op, certainly something you should do in philly, but all over nothing to call home about. Also good to know they only except cash, and one steak runs you about $10.
Tourist trap. But not bad. The French fries were really good though. Sadly perhaps better than the steak.

Unfortunately this is a tourist trap. None of my acquaintances from Philly recommended Pat's or the competitors across the street but I wanted to check for myself what all the hype was about. I actually found out that the hype is from tourists and not from locals. I had the cheesesteak with grilled onions and cheese whiz. The meat is scant and flavorless and disgracefully all the flavor of the sandwich comes from the whiz. There is so much grease in the meat that the bread becomes very soggy. I actually came back at a different time of the day to give it another chance but the outcome was he same.
Good cheesesteaks. Try it with their awesome roasted hot peppers. My only gripe is that they skimp on the meat.

So there is just one decision in South Philly. (at least that I know of)...

Pat's or Geno's?

I've seen multiple shows and highlights talking about the historic rivalry between the two and never though much about it since I had never tried either one, but now that I was in Philly, what was I going to do?

Well I can't actually remember why we chose Pat's over Geno's but it was good decision regardless. I thought it was a little overpriced for what you get so I was going to give it a 3-star, but I always give more weight to the taste than anything else, and it tasted very good! So a 4-star is in order.

I ordered the plain steak sandwich with no cheese (don't like cheese, go ahead and say it... I'm weird right?) but added mustard and it was perfect. I was so hungry I could have actually eaten two of them. 

Gotta stop by and try it out for yourself.

I feel lukewarm about the Cantina, although I visit it frequently. I usually just go for drinking. And they have $5 nachos that will fill you up if you're really hungry. But I also don't really like sitting inside, and the last time I sat outside, we, the patrons, were harrassed- first by kids in a car who actually screamed "ANAL SACK" out the window, and then by a mysterious bout of egg-launching in the outdoor seating area. Although I found both instances to be rather funny, it spoke true of the Cantina. Is there a reason people drive by yelling expletives? Or throw eggs at the place?

That said, I have enjoyed myself here on plenty of occasions. How could I not, if I just want some Tecate and a plate of nachos? But sometimes the service is spotty or it takes too long for a server to reapproach the table and I remember why I feel lukewarm about the Cantina. I agree that it's a bit overpriced ($30 pitchers of margaritas?!) 

Not to mention, my roommate found a roach in his leftover steak burrito. Gross.

Once again another Philly trip and once again we're at the counter at Pat's to quickly yell back, "WIT!!!"  (as in with whiz), before they trip out on you.

Ordered: Cheesesteak with whiz cheese (the famous nacho cheese)

Pat's had probably the most flavor and the winner of our 4 place cheese steak marathon.  Meat had a good texture and the onions gave it great overall flavor.  I'm a Pat's guy.

Footnote: Food channel and food reviewers should take it easy on the best sandwich ever talk.  You're ruining peoples lives.
So unpleased with the taste of the sub. First time trying Jimmy's and I don't think I'll come back. There was hardly any meat on my sub.
Best cheesesteaks. Wit whiz! Don't let the long lines bother you if it's crowded. The lines move quick but be ready when you get to the window and its cash only!

I only ever order plain ice cream sundaes at McDonald's, so I can only attest that this was one of the most enjoyable times I've had.

After a long bike ride on a cold winter's day, I bought me a sundae and sat outside in their lovely, sunny outdoor seating area.  The air was brisk, the tables clean, completely quiet and wonderfully sunny!  It was nice to be able to eat a sundae at McDonald's in the hot sun, alone and with lots of quiet.

Caveat - i can only comment on the Marquita's, since i did not partake of the fare (yet).  This i will say - i had both of the spicy Marquita's on their menu, and they were both well apportioned, and perhaps two of the tastiest i have ever pursed my lips over.

The food being served around us looked fabulous, and I am definitely going back to try it out. Combined with outdoor seating, i can SO SEE myself here for a long Sunday afternoon Mexican brunch and cocktail hour.

A friend of mine raved about this place and decided to take me. I've been there a handful of times and never been disappointed. I really enjoyed  their chicken burrito. The chicken was tender and moist. I love that they offer you chips and salsas as soon as you're seated. Every time, the chips are fresh and crispy. The price is pretty reasonable considering you're getting good Mexican food. During warmer season, there is outdoor seating. I haven't experience it yet but my friend loves it.

JJ's is convenient to CHOP - just across the street and a bit to the right of the main entrance to CHOP.  

Food - Better than Subway.  A decent sandwich, but nothing to right home about.  One thing I don't like is the way the sub was made (I had a #1: ham and cheese). When made, the bun was opened from the side and not cut all the way thru, stuffed with lettuce and tomato and then the meat/cheese was added.  When you bite it on the end, the let/tom are all on one side and meat on the other.  You end up taking 2 bites to get all that the sandwich is.  I feel, a proper sub is built in layers on one half of the bread.  I have to say, the bread is good. 

Service - straight forward: order at the counter and pick up at the pick up location.  

If you're at CHOP and in a hurry to get back to your sick child, I'd recommend it.  However, if you have more time, within a short walk are really good restaurants.  Take a break from thand find a neighborhood restaurant.
Gyro is weak with meat. Their food options all picture fries but they will give you any. Too expensive for what you get...avoid.  Manager is confrontational when you question the pricing. AVOID

Let's set things straight... 

1. Overpriced. WAY overpriced
2. Too crowded (I know it's always going to be a Philly tourist spot, but there are lots of other cheesesteak joints around that are just the same, if not better)
3. Meh.

I would travel for good food. I was told not to bother with cheesesteaks this part of Philly but I always have to learn the hard way. I mean, this place has been around for decades so they must be doing something right, right? WRONG!

First of all, the guys that work here are rude. I even did my research on how to order the "proper local way" but no, they're just DB's here. Sorry for patronizing your establishment and now, you actually have to move those heavy arms to make me a sandwich.

The cheesesteak wasn't that great at all. There's too much bread, not enough meat. They serve their beef chopped and the whiz is on top of the beef.

Locals and non-locals would tell you to stay away from this place, they aren't lying. This was a mistake I wish I could undo.

Pat's King of Steaks and Geno's Steaks are in a cheesesteak war - vying for the hearts of Americans. These two establishments are located across the street from each other and always have lines out of the door (and often into the street). One of my friends even told me that if you have a cheesesteak in hand from the other restaurant, they won't serve you! Be warned though - this place claims to be the inventor of cheesesteaks and has plenty of tourists taking pictures of the signs.

So let's talk about this place. First of all - IT'S CASH ONLY! While the line might seen overwhelming, they have it down to a science, and can get you in and out very fast. Once you get your cheesesteak you can go to the condiment bar and get things like ketchup, relish, and peppers. We got their pork cheesesteak, which was delicious. The meat was tender, the cheese was subtle and had a good tempering taste, and the bread was warm and soft.  With the condiment bar, you essentially have a choose-your-own-adventure when it comes to food. We got some peppers and relish, which were good suuplements, but I suspect we might have had an even more delicious meal if we added ketchup or mustard. 

A good way to go about this is to go with a friend, where one of you guys go to Geno's and another goes to Pat's. You can then try each other's cheesesteaks and come to a decision about this age-old debate.

Family lunch here while sightseeing.  After trying Jim's, we decided to go the the origin and try the Master's creation.  They serve these up fast and the quality is decent, but a bit on the dry side.  They do have condiments on a side bar for those wanting to douce theirs with extras.  One window is subs only with a separate window for other items likes drinks and fries.  Keeps things moving but it meaning paying separately too.  Dropped about $15 per person.

Been there, done that. Took pictures.

Dont be fooled by  the flock of "individuals" who frequent this place. Their horrible taste in cloths, music, and tattoos extends to restaurants. Easily the most over hyped restaurant in Philadelphia.  Service is terrible, food is mediocre at best, hosts are often disoriented, only redeeming quality this place has is the margaritas.  Not worth  it if there is a wait of any kind.

While we were in Philly you know we had to try a cheeseteak or 3. Growing up in Chicago we love our beefs. On my bucket list for sandwiches growing up as a cheesesteak from Philly and an authentic Cuban sandwich. So when we all (siblings) arrived in Philly, we made a trip to Pat and Gino's since they are really just across the street from each other. The other place we visited was Tony Lukes. We purchased 3 cheesesteaks from each location and took them back to our hotel to do a taste test. Honestly we were a bit disappointed. We found the sandwiches lacked flavor. Check our my reviews of Johnnies in Chicago for a great sandwich. Even the fries were just ok. The tradition and entertainment of wit or wit out were entertaining. The result of our taste test was Tony Lukes came in as the best in our opinion.
Poor service, food was middling at best, and we saw mice squeeze in through cracks around the back of the building.  First and last visit.

It's a build your own poke bowl. Topping selection is great. You can get 2 different meats, and they have a large amount of sauces. Ingredients taste fresh and for those that can't make up their minds, they have recommendations
Best i was in my way to New York we  went to see what was better geno or pats pats wins best cheesesteak I had in a very long time

Longest line out of all the options in the food court.

Pros: 
-Price is surprisingly not marked up

Cons: 
-They skimp on everything. No matter burrito bowl, burrito, taco. The portions, protein, toppings are all skimped unless you ask for more but even then the servings are small
-Employees complaining why the line is always so long
If this place was in VA id give it a 5.. but since its beside Geno's , im gonna give it a 4.

We lucked out and got a parking spot right in front but the line was wrapped around the building as it was dinner time. They have a list of the correct way to order but this does no good if its not enforced. There are too many tourists who don't know what they are doing and hold up the line. We waited over 30 mins just to get a sandwich that is as simple as it gets to make. Everyone is set up like a conveyor line constantly pumping out sandwiches. There is no way it should take this long and I think Geno's was moving alot faster. The Cheesesteak is pretty good but $9 is a little steep when I can make something comparable at home for about $4.

Another hidden gem in the Roxborough/Manayunk area. Real easy to miss this place and dismiss it once you find it but trust me this is the real deal. I know pretzels are a big Philly thing. You can't beat fresh hot pretzels daily that are very inexpensive unlike other more well known distributors. They recently raised the prices over the summer due to the economy but it's still a bargain. I love my Tasty Twisters with a hot cup of coffee in the morning, especially the Cinnamon flavor.

DELICIOUS - best cheesesteak ever!  Way way better than genos.  We tried Genos first and were totally disappointed - and went to Pats and wish we had just gone there first!!  Soft, tender, juicy cheesy hot goodness!!  Visiting from Dallas - Pats will be on my to do list for next time!!

Pat's and Geno's are both proof that the human race has no hope. Anyone who is willing to wait in line for 30 minutes, accept rude service, and pay 10 dollars for a tiny cheese steak should be checked out by a shrink. 

The steaks here are average at best and not worth the time or money. The only people that eat here are sucker tourist that are obsessed with the Travel Chanel. If the steaks were 6 bucks then it wouldn't be that bad of a deal. They are not bad but not even close to the best of what Philly has to offer.

If your looking for a good steak, Jim's and Cosmi's are both way better and cheaper. A few blocks up is Paisano's. Amazing food and some of the best sandwiches in Philly.

As mentioned by other reviewers, this is the obligatory touristy cheesesteak stop.  Overall the cheesesteak was good.  I had it with provalone and onions.  I've had better quality "steak", but this one was tasty and juicy.

It is worth the lineup once, but I don't think I'd ever add it to my regular stops for a return visit in Philly.

I love this place.  LOVE.  However, it is out of this universe unhealthy. Burgers are super greasy, loaded with whatever condiments you want, a fresh bun, mmmm just delicious.  Cajun fries are fresh and seriously yummy too.  I come here maybe 1-2 times a year, but if health/calories didn't matter I'd be here a lot more.

Service is quick and very "Philly".  Got the regular fries instead of Cajun.  Female cashier "hooked me up" and let me not only keep the original, but gave me 2 orders of Cajun fries.  Wowzers.  Not sure I needed all of those fries, but just, wow.

Not so good anymore. The last time I came here was in 2009 and it was still yummy. Somehow the taste has changed now. This time the meat didn't taste so fresh and it was a little chewy. Cheese did not improve it either. Not coming back ever.

Although a must try for anyone visiting Philadelphia I only go here when I'm drunk at about 3:00am. I'd say Pat's has one step up on Geno's. 

Just be careful that you know how to order when you approach the window so you don't get yelled at or jumped in line. I still have yet to figure out how people put up with the intimidation by the guy selling steaks on the other side of the window. I don't even know why Pat's has such rigid rules considering most people in line are probably tourist with no clue how to order a steak.

Good cheesesteaks.  Good place to stop if you're a tourist, but if you want a more genuine philly cheesesteak experience you may want to try some place you've never heard of.  Pick one, there are literally hundreds in the city that make great sandwiches.  

Pat's I like more than Geno's but they still are both a little too gimmicky.  Lacking a certain genuineness. Certainly worth trying, though.

Good peppersteak, don't like the rule about going to the back of the line if you mess up your order (on their sign).  What happened to brotherly love??  The hot sauce on my peppersteak was fantastic and WAY better than the flamethrowing hot sauce served at Geno's.  For a $10 sandwich I would say this is an OK place to sample the dueling Philly steak joints.  The complexity of flavor of the beef will not blow you away as it is not super-seasoned.  Onions and peppers shine brighter than the beef for me and add a lot to the sandwich.  Provolone was good, but got lost a bit.

One of the worst cheese steaks I have ever had.  I was really looking forward to this place as part of the Rocky experience.  Meat was chewy and they doused it with industrial grade cheesewiz.  Coke was watered down.. you get the picture.

People working there were also pretty rude.  A fair number of them are probably young guys on parole.

WORST EXPERIENCE EVER DO NOT GO THERE!!! The manager Mark was extremely rude, condescending, and disrespectful - I would NOT recommend anyone go to this location. I arrived at the Popeyes located on Grant Ave. at 9:54pm. I drove up to the window and a female said "We're closed and we put up all of the food and shut down the registers."  This location is suppose to close at 10pm, and whether or not they were scheduled to close in 5 minutes, they still should have been serving the public until their true closing time. I asked could I speak to a Manager, she went & got someone named Mark. He was EXTREMELY rude, condescending, short, and disrespectful. The first thing he said when he came to the window was "What? We're closed!" I said "You close at 10 and it's 9:55, so why can't you serve me?" He said "Because we're closed. Everything is put away - so I don't know what to tell you." I asked for his name and then asked for a phone number or website that I could contact for this incident. He said "No. You have to Google it!" And then closed the drive thru window. I am extremely offended by this rude behavior. Not only did I waste my time driving to a location that refused to serve me, when they were technically still open; but I also had to deal with the behavior of someone who in management, who is extremely unprofessional and has no respect or regard for clients. The tone he use was very offensive, and I'm not sure if it was because I'm a black female, but the young lady who was standing there laughed and found it amusing. I want to make it clear that I have NEVER made a formal complaint about any type of service I've had in the past, but this was absolutely absurd. If this is the type of people that Popeyes is putting in management roles, I don't see much success in the future.

Pat's is a toughie. If you grew up in Philly, you likely have a soft spot for it. But that also might blind you a little to all its shortcomings. I grew up stopping at Pat's before Phillies games, so its hard for me to separate the nostalgia from the reality. But I try.

Let's start with the obvious - the cheesesteaks suck. I think we all can mostly agree on this. if you actually like them, you need to experience Steve's or Chinks or Delassandros or Tony Luke's or hell, even Jim's does it way better. And for insult to injury, its a tourist trap so they charge you 8 bucks a steak. And the whole soup-nazi thing, please. It might be funny as an urban legend, but when i see tourists get sent to the back of the line because they took too long to order, I cringe for our collective image. Shitty food and shitty service is about as great a combo as swiss on a cheesesteak.

There are things to like about Pats though. The scene is a good one. I like the South Philly vibe, the outdoor seating, the baseball diamond and bball courts across the way. Its a bustling little city corner that is fun for any fans of people watching. They have really good birch beer. I don't know why I think this, I'm sure it's nothing special, but god damn that fountain birch beer is delicious!

But here's the one thing that you need to know about Pats. Pats is all about the CHEESE FRIES! They have the best cheese fries (of the whiz-and-fries-only category, not fanciness with bacon or ranch or 3 cheeses) in the whole city. I swear by this. Plus, they are priced more reasonably (3.50 is still a lot, but way better deal than the steak). There also is never a line at the fry window, so you don't have to wait, and they are soooooo good. My fiancee insists that they taste so good because they are fried twice. I respond with "you can fry things twice??" These fries are fat kid tasty, yamsayin? Seriously, do yourself a favor, next time you go to Pat's just bypass the steaks, get some fries, and soak in the vibe. All the crappy stuff happens at the steak window.
The people who work here suck more than the steaks do ... Guidos

I LIKE IT. I LIKE IT A LOT!
This place is pretty quick and their wings and multiple flavors are very good!
No complaints!

When I heard Chipotle was opening up in Center City I almost was in disbelief!!

I love me some Chipotle and this place is swanky. Yes I used the word swanky. 

Only two reasons 4 and not 5 stars is:
Place is really dirty after 7pm-ish
I don't like having to ask for more beans or rice!

We have never been to a doctor's office where EVERYONE was so helpful, considerate, understanding, efficient, competent, patient and kind.  The doctor's are extremely learned and well versed.  They offer and wide spectrum of treatment options, specifically suited for the needs of your pet  (and family).  They are responsive, and return your calls promptly.
It is obvious that the doctor's and staff adore animals.  We are so glad that they have been our family vet for over a decade.

When you think of Philadelphia, do you think of the Liberty Bell?  What about Independence Hall?  Chronically mediocre sports teams that occasionally eek their way into the playoffs only to be eliminated shortly thereafter?  Do you think of Rocky?  

 I, too, think of those things.  But if there's one arena in which Philly truly deserves its renown, it's the mother fucking cheesesteaks.  I've been to "Philly cheesesteak" shops in other cities, and it's just simply an inferior product that costs more and takes longer to produce.  PHILLY HAS SOME DOPE CHEESESTEAKS, and I am deeply in debt to my dad for taking me down Passyunk Ave yesterday to pick one up.  

Did we go to Genos?

Sir, we did not.  Everybody knows Geno's is a right-wing-a-palooza crazyfest and if you aren't Aryan you can't even eat there.  Fuck them and their politics of steakz.   No, we went across the street to the TRUE mecca of Philly steaks, PAT'S. PAT'S, where Obama had a cheesesteak shortly before losing the state to a shrill, pants-suit wearing democratic carpetbagger.  PAT'S, where you order "wit" if you want onions and choose from American or cheese whiz.  PAT'S, where the line is MUCH, MUCH shorter than Geno's, not because of less demand, but because the staff is so much more efficient that the formation of the cheesesteak appears to have been engineered by a chubby 6th year at MIT.  Here's to you, PAT'S.  May you never get a giant fake cheesesteak billboard mounted above your fine establishment.

Ordered delivery from here today and it was pretty good. Things didn't really get better or worse.

Started off with the mozzarella sticks. It was weird. When I was ordering them I thought to myself, "I don't have to ask for marinara sauce with them, do I?" and then when they came there wasn't any marinara. On top of that I think they were so overcooked that the cheese was completely gone from two of the six of them. They were just hollow fried shells.

Next I had the same boneless wings as before. I ordered them tossed in the spicy bbq sauce again but mentioned not to make it too spicy. They listened and the sauce was much better this time. The wings came with fries, not curly this time, and they were a lot better without the cheese on them to make them soggy. 

Overall, I'm still a fan.

I visited Pat's with couple friends during my short stay at Philadelphia...I was not impressed at all with this place.
