If you think that there are no losers except waistlines in the cheesesteak wars think again. Cheesesteaks make or break elections. Just ask John Kerry. He lost the 2004 election trying to get Swiss cheese here. He needs to to take that business to Boston.
Nothing is better than a fresh Pat's cheesesteak late at night! Whiz wit is the only way to go.

This place is pretty good. There are lots of options for fish, including regular tuna, spicy tuna, and salmon. You can also choose from tofu for the vegans. They ask you to choose from a few different sauces to basically marinate the fish. You can choose from different toppings. Overall, everything tastes fresh and was delicious. My only complaint is that my bowl was $12 (added avocado), I would say it's a little pricey for this type of venue. It's basically in a food court with nowhere to sit directly in front of the restaurant. If they would lower prices just a tad bit, I would consider making this a regular spot.

Tourist trap.  Advertised as the best cheesesteaks in the city, blah blah blah.  Anyone in the city knows you don't go here for a REAL cheesesteak.  Overpriced, underwhelming amount of meat.  If you want a real cheesesteak go to Ishkabibbles, Uncle Oogies, Delassandro's, or really any little corner pizza joint.
It was nothing great, i had both cheese steaks side by side, Geno's definitely had the beefier taste though Pat allows for more toppings. It was overhyped for a mediocre sandwich.

So we had to stop by here after our visit at adventure aquarium. We had to get a sandwich from here and from genos and bring it back to nyc. And so we did. Im not a fan of whiz but i gotta say this sandwich was yummy and cheesy and the nread was nice and soft. Glad we made a pit stop here!

When I think of summer, I think of happy hour at Cantina in the sunshine with a group of the finest friends. I have dined at Cantina Los Caballitos at least 25 times in the last few years and very rarely have I been unhappy with my food or service. I definitely prefer to grab drinks/food in the summer when the long windows are open in the front and there are tables outside, mostly because it eliminates a lot of the congestion the restaurant has in the colder months. Plus I can't get enough of sitting out in the sunshine with a margarita in hand. 

The food is yummy. I have a hard time switching it up as I've developed some staple snacks/favorites over the years. The salads are really yummy, the nachos are so delicious (beware, the large is super grande!), veggie quesadilla (when not left to get soggy) is so good with the mushrooms and smokey sauce, and all the tacos- YUM! They consistently have interesting specials on the board including different ceviches- a bunch of which I've tried and have all been executed really well by the chef. I almost never leave the establishment without ordering some fried plantaines to share at the table topped with scallions and queso fresco. 

The happy hour margaritas are really good, especially for the price. Occasionally they cut corners and make them weaker than they should be, leaving you with more heartburn than a buzz- but it is happy hour, hopefully they will fix that one day. I tend to order the margarita with the guava juice, it's so refreshing and perfect for a hot summer day. In the winter, I tend to steer clear of the margaritas and order off their draft list which is consistently a decent selection. 

Last, but certainly not least... I love the decor and vibe of Cantina. Without being completely tacky, it vibes Mexican culture with the perfect South Philly neighborhood appeal.

The company I work for decided to try out Chipotle's catering as an option for one of our quarterly office events for my department. I will say the food itself was oK, it came with everything that we needed (The ONLY reason I gave 2 stars as opposed to 1), however the process to get the food was extremely stressful, exhausting, and a huge inconvenience. We tried multiple times to place the order for delivery online as well as on the phone with different credit cards that worked fine with all the other orders that we made. Do to Chipotle's system issues it would not allow us to make the payment so we had no choice but to place the order for delivery which took away time we didn't have to spare. I called the morning of the event to confirm everything was in order and I was informed that the order was canceled. I had a whole department waiting and they cancelled my order without a call or at the very least an email to inform me. One of the customer service representatives looked into it and said it was a store manager that cancelled because they can't accommodate our order. They said they will place another order for a later time and I still had to pick it up. What really befuddled me is that they placed the order at the very same place that it was canceled after they claimed they couldn't accommodate. I had to go with it because at this point I was in a bind and had a department full of people to feed. Thank God we eventually got what we needed but that shaved an hour off of our time that we have to get pre-approve for these events as well as took us away from work that needed to be done that day. When I called to discuss the matter I was told that they would like to keep our business and they will have someone call me back. It's been a week and I have yet to receive a phone call. Very unfortunate. I couldn't convince my company to go with this business again if I wanted to do to the lack of professionalism.
Don't see what the big deal is about this place! I've had much better cheese steaks elsewhere. I could chef up a better cheese steak! Plus they need to lose the attitude, their not the soup nazi!

I traveled three thousand miles for this?
I walked from the nearest train station to 9th and Passyunk, and was hungry enough to eat one from both places. Maybe it's because I'm from the Midwest, but I know what good beef is supposed to taste like, but this wasn't it. I found it to be very tough and gristly. The roll was very good, as was the cheese. Unfortunately, it was difficult to get past the beef (literally!)
The ordering process is reminiscent of the Soup Nazi from Seinfeld. You buy your sandwich at one window, and God help you if you don't already have your cash out, then move on to the next window to get fries and drinks, and pay again. It's all rather silly, really.
Nothing I say should stop you from going here, though. Skip over Independence Hall and head south. You'll never know until you try it for yourself. I could have just been there on a bad day.

Our host (native Philadelphian) took us to Pat's King of Steaks for our first Philly Cheese Steak experience.  This is a very laid back place with a very intense group of staff - you HAVE to know what you want to order in the window, otherwise they WILL send you back to the end of the line, which is a good thing to speed up the ordering process :)

We were there on a Tuesday evening, and thankfully although there were some people there, it wasn't as busy as I expected (I've heard this place could be a LOT worse).  A rival cheese steak place was located across the street, and it was obnoxiously bright with lots of color neon lights etc, tries to invite people.  I found Pat's to be more intimate and welcoming than the rival.  This is an outdoor venue, I might add, so don't expect to find a bathroom, or even a *free* glass of water (you have to purchase your own beverage, including bottled water, from the next window).

This is the best cheese steak I've ever eaten in my life (to be fair, I haven't had many).  Bread was soft and meat was perfectly cooked.  I love the peppers topping you could add yourself from a vendor outside, my favorite was the roasted pepper olives.  My eyes were bulging and I was sweating like crazy from eating those hot peppers, but it was very tasty. 

This was a good place to sit down, eat your sandwich and have great conversation with your companions.  I had an extremely good time here.  Cars were driving very close to where you sit in outdoor picnic tables (you could smell some of exhaust fumes), but this certainly add some characters to the experience.

I certainly would recommend this place to anyone, and I'm looking forward to be back in Philly and to be back to Pat's!  Arriverderci e a piu' tardi!

When in Philly for a mini vacation,  one must have fun visiting the local shrines. For us it was a trip to Pat's.  So much fun, despite the ever-present line. So what did we order?  Cheesesteak!  One Whiz wit, one wiz witout, haha. We ordered in the local vernacular. Delicious,  sinful & fun.

As soon as my bf and I finished sampling Geno's, we immediately headed for Pat's. The line was equally atrocious, but there were a few distinctive differences between the two. 
1.The bread was a little hard.
2.The steak was cooked just right.
3.Needed a little more cheez whiz.

So asides from the hard bread and the insufficient cheez whiz, I prefer Pat's because I'm very meticulous about the way my food is cooked...and frankly I don't appreciate any aftertastes.
Tourist trap. I've had better cheese steaks. And they don't accept credit cards. Won't be going again.

between pat's and gino's, i'll take pat's. in my opinion, the cheese tastes better and not as runny as gino's. .that's why i'll always comeback to pat's. although i've got to be honest, i've seen some mice run around the vicinity while i'm munching on the tasty cheesteak. .make sure to get extra cheese!

Everything feels rushed here. The thing about a business is, once your popular and made a lot of money, they don't give a shit about the customers anymore. The cheese steaks are good but with this kind of service I will not be returning unless all other cheese steaks places in Philly closes. (Tony Luke's, Geno's, Jim's Steak ect.)
They're just slow and rude. Never say thank you or you're welcome. Always messing stuff up.

Good outdoor seating area.  Pretty good burritos.  The draw is really the outside seating though.  For authentic cuisine I'd go elsewhere but if you're looking for a place to get an outside drink and have a decent burrito, its pretty much your best option.
I love the South Philly style steaks but prefer Steve's Prince of Steak and Tony Luke's to Pat's- they don't deserve the "king" in their name anymore.

Yum. 
Steak, onion, whiz.  Great bread. Simple. Totally worth the stop. 

Is it the best? Probably not. But it's damn good, and hits the spot every time.  

You can argue whose is better, but I've been to Geno's, Pat's, and tons of local spots, and they're all good. But there was something a bit better about Pat's, not sure what it was, but it had a better flavor than Geno's in my opinion. 

Otherwise, it is what it is. A dumpy walk-up counter to order cheesesteaks. Not sure what people expect, but I enjoy it every time I go.

It was dinner time when we got here. Found an excellent parking spot right next to it. There was a short line that gave us time to decide what we wanted. We were torn on coming here or trying their rivalry Genos. (across the street) we ordered and it was ready within minutes (if that) The steaks were delicious and those cherry peppers were even better. I'm glad we made a stop here and tried the original steak.

I was a frequent customer for years...but sadly, the food got cheaper and then I no longer enjoyed going there. Decided to give it one more try this weekend...it was worse! No flavor, fat On the steak..just horrible. On my way out...I witnessed a mouse party in the outside seating area. 
Very sad...

Glad to see a Chipotle make its way outside of freaking University City and City Line Avenue.

As a transplant from Maryland, an area that thrives off Chipotle, it's good to have one in the city I now live in.

Cannot go wrong with almost any item here as they are all DELICIOUS. Especially the vegetarian burrito and chicken burrito.

Their guac is phenomenal for a chain, so I definitely recommend that as well.

All in all, I will be visiting this location more often when I'm on that side of Walnut Street.

There is another Jimmy John's in University City! I had no idea... Yesterday, the lunchtime line at Potbelly was so long that we decided to go somewhere else. In comparison to that, this Jimmy John's was surprisingly empty.

In fact, Jimmy John's is the kind of franchise which I find surprisingly underrated. Whenever I go to one, it's almost empty and I am the only person who orders something. Perhaps that is because the sandwiches come out very fast, but even so it's a little strange to be in restaurants where the employees outnumber the customers at almost all times.

I find their sandwiches to be almost perfect. The ingredients are very fresh, the sauces are very good, and there is a reason as to why they call themselves "Gourmet Sandwiches" even if it's not Michelin-star-level. I especially like that the sandwiches are untoasted (admittedly this is a personal preference). The only thing I personally dislike about Jimmy John's is the bread itself, which has the perfect consistency but tastes a little bland.

This Jimmy John's will certainly become my new to-go place when I forgot my cash at home or on weekends.

I have been to this location a couple of times for lunch and drinks but usually visit the Northern Liberties location Cantina Dos Segundos more frequently. Unfortunately my experience last night was not great. I went here for happy hour with my friend after work and we just planned to get margaritas and maybe some nachos if we were hungry. The waiter gave us chips and salsa and kept asking if we wanted food/wanted to put something in the oven/wanted dinner/wanted to keep our menus. He eventually took away our menus since we weren't going to order a main course. Kind of weird but not a big deal. The main reason I'm writing this review is because we went here specifically for the happy hour special which is half off classic margaritas ($4.50 usually) and pitchers of margaritas ($22 usually). The pitcher was a better deal for two people so we ordered it at 5:15 (Happy hour is 4-6pm) and it was really delicious. I went to the bathroom and left my friend cash to pay our bill thinking it would be $11 total aka $5-6 dollars since we were splitting it. NOPE! Unfortunately she didn't tell me the total of the bill until we got home--they charged us full price for the frozen pitcher which totally defeats the purpose of why we came here...for half off drinks! I would have gone somewhere else in the city if I knew they were going to do that because there are way better options for Mexican food and drinks.

i maybe wouldn't give pat's 5 stars if it weren't the epic battle between pat's and geno's. because pat's isn't the most amazing cheesesteak i've ever had, but it definitely beats geno's, and i'll admit it's pretty darn good on its own too.
last time i was in philly, i tried both. had to see who was better. the cheese whiz was what won me over, pat's was totally cheesier and less of a mess.
so this time, i knew which one i wanted, and i was just here to enjoy, not judge. i got one without onions and with cheese whiz, my boyfriend got one with onions and cheese whiz, and we split some fries. i was jealous that somehow his had way more cheese than mine, but what can you do? the fries were super tasty too, which i was almost surprised they'd both to put effort into anything but the cheesesteaks! haha
if you've never been to a food stand (yeah, i'm going to call it that instead of a restaurant, and if you go here, you'll see why) like this, be prepared with your order and money ahead of time, cuz they don't appreciate waiting, questions, or special requests. that being said, that makes them super efficient. our sandwiches were out in less than a minute.
now, prices. 2 standard cheesesteaks is $19. our fries and 2 drinks were $9 i believe. a little on the pricey side, but then again, with all the tourists flocking here, they can afford to charge a little more, understandably. but be prepared, they're cash only as well.
you go to pat's for the food, and the food alone. not the atmosphere (a few outside tables, covered from the rain but certainly not the wind), the prices (not outrageous, but still probably three times what it actually costs them to make the food), or the people (sometimes i wonder if they actually all just hate their job). but let me tell you, if you're looking for a real philly cheesesteak in the heart of philly, pat's is where you want to go!
Overpriced, outside, cheap ingredients...add to that one of the trashiest collections of patrons in the city, and you've got a real loser.

4.5 Stars?  Oh please!

Alright, since no one else will say it, I will:

This is the worst cheesesteak anywhere in the world.  It skimpy, over priced and barely edible (on a good night).

Pats and Genos compete with each other...Yeah, they certainly do.....to see who can charge the most for disgusting inedible food!

It's embarassing that our famous (and yummy) chesesteak is so closely related with this place!

PR at it's very best.
That is all....

Because of Pat's reputation, I had to go try their cheesesteaks. I usually see an enormous line and a lot of customers, but I went on a weekday at around 4PM and there wasn't really many people. Of course, I ordered the wiz wit, cheesesteak with cheese whiz and onions. It was really good. The meat wasn't dry or too greasy. The bun could have been a little more toasted to my liking though. I had some cherry peppers on the side to add some extra spice to the overall cheesy taste of the sandwich. It tastes exactly what you expect a cheesesteak should taste. I can see why a lot of people visit. It's famous for a reason.
Cheese steak was dry and salty.  Tasted a bit better than Geno's, but not by much.  Order the mushroom one, but came without?!!  Place is over rated.  Not worth the hype.

After trying very subpar cheesesteaks in central city that were supposedly "the best" finally found the absolutely best!!! OMG! What flavor and not too much bun but even it was delicious! Pat is the King!

I had to give 5 stars, because I have never had an issue with this place.  It's within walking distance of my house, the food is really good, and the (frozen = more booze) margaritas are really good.  I am friends with most of the staff which generally works in my favor, and I am friends with one of the owners. I've eaten most of the things on the menu here, and liked it all. OH i just remembered an issue! About a year and a half ago, my friend and I had an audition, and we were nervous, so we stopped in to have a margarita to cool our nerves. One of our margaritas had a bug in it. So our server felt terrible, and bought us a couple rounds of shots. We went to our audition (kind of drunk? is that unprofessional?) and WE BOTH BOOKED THE JOB! So I thank the Cantina for that. And the free chips and salsa.  The green salsa is so good I could drink it !
Not all it's cracked up to be. Go to a non tourist place for a better steak.

I love the nachos here. I love nachos almost anywhere, but these are especially good. 
Usually a decent selection of tasty/local/unique beers on tap.
Food=decent
margaritas=a little heavy on the sour mix
Atmosphere= LOUD. Always loud. Even when you're the only person at the bar.  
Shout out to Vanessa though, awesome bartender/server. Always friendly and fun even when she's completely weeded.  
NOT a good place to bring your parents.  Better for happy hour and late night shots of tequila and a Tecate.

So my family knows the Cathy family and the COO of Chick FilA. We've eaten at CFA so many times and this was the only time we've ever had what we would call an awful experience. Our food wasn't warm, the waitress was borderline evil she was so unfriendly, the nuggets must've have been deep fried in sewage or something - the breading was nowhere close to correct and they tasted awful. 

To the manager of this location, you are not modeling your restaurant to CFA standards. The young ladies at the cash register need a time-out or something. And remember "My Pleasure" is part of CFA culture. Teach your people to say it. And maybe smile. And maybe even be respectful instead of mean. So disappointed with our experience here.
So bad it's not even worth the drive. Totally overated. Don't bother. The cheese steak had essentially no flavor. Meat was bland. The only thing I tasted was the whiz.

I hope tonight is not a preview of how the summer is going to go here at Cantina. Not sure if it is the new wait staff, but service was much below what it had been in the past. 40 minute wait for a bowl of chips and another 30 for a draft beer (which coincidentally, was brought out a minute after asking a server who wasn't our own). Will be avoiding this place like the plague until the summer is over. It destroys the experience when you see FOH staff stressed.

Fun to come here once, but the meat isn't as good as you can find at other places. Haven't tried Geno's yet, but now that I live here I know I'll go there sooner or later. Plus one star for the tradition.

My brother visited me in Philly and really wanted the authentic Philly cheesesteak.  We were not disappointed.  They were made really quickly, and were juicy and flavorful.  Sadly, there was nowhere for us to sit - it was packed.  But that's a good sign, right?  I refused to go to Geno's on principle because of their sign about only serving people who speak English - and I don't think I'll be looking elsewhere.  Pat's is the real thing!  I was a little intimidated about ordering because they don't want you to dilly dally - but I guess that's all part of the experience.

I'll spare you what I think of chipotle, as that's not relevant since it's rather consistent across locations. This place excels with a nice staff and great portion sizes! I couldn't finish my bowl and I always do.

For my visit to Philadelphia, how could I skip the event of getting a hometown Philly Cheesesteak?  

I decided to go to Pat's because Geno's was a little too flashy for me with their bright Times Squre-like signs.  The lines were equally long, which made me wait in line with drool coming down my mouth from all the great greasy smells.  

After finally settling down at a table with my cheesesteak, I was happy.  Then I ate and it was tasty!  I would've liked a little more meat... the meat to bread ratio was not a good one.  The only other problem is that I've been to 99 miles to Philly in NYC now, and I like it a lot better.  It's closer to home, the sandwiches are meatier, and cheesier!  hah.

After having visited three poke places around the city, I have to say Philly Poke is more than likely the best one. They have fresh selections and their protein to rice ratio is definitely on par. I don't know about anyone else but I love to have protein and rice on my last spoonful and they don't disapoint here. I would definitely recommend stop by and check them out. Oh and remember, they're inside the store front so you won't be able to see them from the street.

Great cheesesteaks! So good to have even on a cold night (benches are outdoors). Only thing-prices are a little high. Other than that, well worth the trip and dealing with the cold. In the summer it must get packed but it seems like Wednesday nights are when to go so there's no line.

Been to Pat's too many times to count.  I consider Pats to be the yardstick to compare all cheese steakks to, and yes, many are not nearly as good or should not even be considered cheese staks, and occasinally, some joints are better.  Over all, Pat's does not ever disappoint though, the bread is a big part of it, and Pat's rolls are excellant.  Great condiments too.

Look, here's the breakdown. Adriatic grill is the place I've gone to everyday while on campus. The bottom line is that the food is great, but there will not be 1 time where they don't mess your order up. After they messed my order up once, I took it back and they fixed it. Since then, I've ordered the same thing and it was messed up 5 more times!!! By now, I should have received a free meal. I'm not sure if its the woman who takes the orders that writes it down wrong, or the cooks don't fully read during times of long lines. My friends have also encountered the same problem. Anyway, I just can't continue going to a place that can't get my order right, no matter how good the food is.

I really like the free peanuts and the fries. Here are my two cents on the In and Out v Five Guys debate:

Burger flavor: IN AND OUT - Sorry. In and out is just tastier with their special sauce (yeah yeah it's thousand island) and grilled onions. Annoyed that my Five Guys cheeseburger didn't have melted warm gooey cheese. 

Burger customization: FIVE GUYS - There are tons of toppings you can choose from. You don't get THAT much... like I got two slivers of green peppers and maybe one sliced up mushroom. Still, I like choice!

Fries: FIVE GUYS - Cajun Fries are overly seasoned but still very tasty. I prefer steakhouse cut fries to the measly skinny ones at in and out. 

Menu Variety: IN AND OUT - Milkshakes!!!!! And cool special burger orders. 

Value: IN AND OUT - Dude. It's almost $5 for a fast food burger. Meh.

Unfortunately this fast food restaurant continues to struggle. Employees are don't care. Management non-existent. I give this place a year and it will close.  They are slow and can't get orders right. No one has a clue. Horrible!

This establishment is more of a chillout place. Definitely laid back, no snobbery.

Location is in the heart of the Ave, so expect it to be packed on nights with good weather, with their outdoor seating area. Went here on my birthday and happened to be a gorgeous night.  A friend and I went and got a table outside. The bar inside is cool too, but wanted to take advantage of the weather.

Their drink selection is pretty impressive. Would recommend the Sly Fox IPA. They also are known for their margaritas. I didn't have one, but my friend did and liked the peach variety. 

They lead off with home made tortilla chips with salsa picante and salsa verde. Both dips were nice but the picante could use a bit of heat IMO.  I had their empanadas, chicken quesadillas, and a mexican-type shrimp scampi (no pasta) but I forgot the name. The food is good, but just not mind-blowing. 

The wait service is slow however. There were 2 servers working the outside, but not sure if they were working the inside as well. We were mainly there for drinks, so it didn't kill the vibe that much waiting for food, but it was still a drag.

That said I'd highly recommend going for a happy hour, or any time to grabs a few drinks. Place is chill, and the drinks are smooth. I will be revisiting for sure.

We had 2 hours to kill until our plane started boarding so we decided to get a cheese steak for old times sake. Basically the service was so bad that I would have rather eaten else where. I ordered a cheese steak with mushrooms, lettuce and tomatoes. I forgot to mention I wanted mayonnaise in it. So as I was giving money for the order I said, "can you add mayo?" He told me no you had to tell me that right away. Nothing here is free. We were  willing to pay more as he was still holding our money. But he was saying the order is put in we can't change anything. So we said alright and waited for our food. As we waited I heard the worker yelling cheese steak cheese steak as if we are at some flea market not the airport. I wish I heard him earlier because I wouldn't have ordered. He's making his company look bad since he's shouting to draw attention to his place of eating. The food itself was alright but the customer service killed my appetite for a cheese steak.
If you're a tourist and want a real Philly cheesesteak, don't go here. The beef is dry and the roll is sub par. Go to Tony Luke's or Cleavers if you want something legit.

I visited the Cantina for the second time this weekend (1st time is kind of a blur, due to several rounds of margaritas!).  We went on a Friday night, so it was busy, as was expected.  We only had to wait a few minutes for a table, and were seated inside near the open windows to the outside/sidewalk area, which was nice because it was kind of warm inside.  We each ordered a drink and a plate of large nachos.  The drinks came (Caliente Margarita [Spicy!!] = awesome), as did the free chips and salsa.  We didn't think we'd been waiting too too long, when the waitress came back and apologized for the kitchen loosing our slip... it would be an extra few minutes.  "No biggie,"  I said.  "The drinks are on me," she said.  Um, ok... thanks!  More complimentary chips and salsa arrived, and then the nachos.  The nachos were good, but we were way stuffed from all the free chips.  My BF got a beer afterwards, and our bill came to $11.  
I certainly can't complain about this experience.

The food was amazing. Everything from the tacos to the burritos to the chips and two types of salsa they give you was so tasty. The service was so quick and the place was popping. I would definitely recommend.

If you need neon and kitsch with your cheesesteak, go to Geno's.  Not enough "flavor" for you?  Add relish and ketchup, that's why it's out.  This isn't Tom Colicchio's gourmet cooking, it's a cheesteak.  Bread, steak, cheese, onions if desired.  Tourists, they couldn't spell out the ordering instructions any more clearly (http://flickr.com/photos/agreatnotion/172834329/) so don't act like it's super confusing and hold up the line.  Wit or witout and pick a cheese (wiz wit all the way).  If you can't handle that go back to McDonald's and hold up the line there.

I have not yet tried Geno's so I can't compare, but I thought Pat's was okay. I ordered a cheesesteak whiz with and mushrooms. I can't help but notice that the whiz is watered down - which makes for a very messy eating experience, more so than I already assumed it would be. 
I understand its a tourist attraction and very popular, but we barely found a place to sit down and i felt like we were being watched like hawks the whole time, which made me feel uneasy and subconsciously made me eat too fast, haha 

Next time I'll try another place.
Tasty cheese steak served hot and clean and fresh with crispy French fries and a cherry lemonade.

**WHY 3 STARS?**
Their cheesesteaks are nothing spectacular, but they are good. I'm sure you can find a better cheesesteak out there, especially in Philly, but this is the original, and perhaps a cheesesteak is only supposed to taste as simple as this. It's a couple of simple ingredients put together, and it works. You learn to appreciate it, just as you would appreciate a good grilled cheese. It's not something I would want to eat too often, but I do like it every once in while.

**Favorites**  Wit. Whiz. Eat with pickled cherry peppers. Cheese fries.

**Recommend?** I would bring out-of-towners here if they're interested in trying the "original" Philly cheesesteak. I prefer it over Geno's.

The more cheesesteaks I eat from here, the more I like this stuff.  When I had my first Pat's cheesesteak many, many years ago when I was a little girl, I wasn't impressed.  At all. I thought, "This is the sandwich Philly is famous for?" That was when I didn't know how to appreciate the flavor of Cheese Whiz.

Yes, my friend, the main flavor of this famous cheesesteak is from the Cheese Whiz.  Melded together with the fatty juices of the thinly sliced beef, it provides the perfect complement for the otherwise bland meat. If they happen to skimp on the Whiz (which happens sometimes!) then the cheesesteak suffers in flavor. The bread is nothing special, IMO, but it's an Amoroso roll. In fact, it can get really soggy after the sandwich sits for a while, but it stays chewy! The soft bread allows the flavorful cheese and juices to soak into the bread and you get this soft chewy goodness enrapturing the pile of meat. Unless you can't stand onions, definitely get it "wit onions."  The finely chopped onions add a nice subtlety to the flavor profile. Go get some pickled peppers if you like spicy.  Eat them all together and it becomes the perfect cheesy meaty goodness slathered inside a bread roll.

Cheese fries are good, if you eat them fresh.  Otherwise, the cheese and fries themselves can get chewy and/or soggy.  The regular fries are only ok.

The cheesesteak was good, but relative to expectations and other restaurants in the area, not incredible.  Pats cheesesteak tasted familiar, like I've had it in Ohio... which was not exactly what I was looking for but, again, pretty good.

Three stars to me is good, I liked it, but I wouldn't be a regular.

This place used to be the restaurant to go to for a quick buzz and a great bite to eat. With the increase in prices and their margaritas not containing as much alcohol I go here a lot less than I used to. The salads are priced high and on the smaller side and $6 for one piece of corn is just outrageous Especially when the cheese is minimal and it's charred too dark. The waiters and waitresses are still good though so for good service, weak drinks, and high prices give it a whirl.

As far as Philly Cheesesteaks go, Pat's really not that bad as many people I've come into contact with have claimed. I give it a 3.5 on a 5 point scale. It may not be the best out there but I would suggest if you haven't had it, are traveling to Philly, have the time to sightsee and are curious, just do it. It will be worth the experience at least once. I had the Mushroom Pepper Cheesesteak w/o Onions and with Wiz and I can say that I really don't regret it.
Was impressive by the BBQ brisket tacos, a little less so by the salmon, and much less so by the drinks (very weak). Cool vibe though.

its way way better than the dog food Genos is serving, but they skimp on the meat and cheese, so double up on that business.  the line is insane but moves pretty fast.   worth the trip and if you are only going to try one, pick pats for sure.

Let me just start off by saying this: *UNLIMITED CHIPS AND SALSA* comes with both salsa verde and salsa roja, which are actually much, much better than many other places that I had to pay for. 

In addition to their great drinks (especially margaritas), the food has always been consistently delicious. 

But if there's one dish I'd recommend, it would, WITHOUT A DOUBT, be the shrimp tacos. I don't remember going to Los Caballitos and not ordering them. Each taco has an incredibly generous amount of shrimp, and each shrimp pops in your mouth with a crazy burst of flavor.

I swear--get the shrimp tacos, you will NOT be disappointed.
If Philly's Best in Pasadena California Gets 4 stars then you people should be giving Pats A definite 5  Id give it a 7 if I could

I'm doing a similar review for these two rivals - I loved Geno's and Pat's. They were both amazing!! Four of us went to try both of these amazing cheesesteaks, two of us got Geno's and two of us got Pat's then we just split them. We all went back and fourth on which one we liked better but both were great. Pat's bread was nice and fluffy with the meat first then the onions and then the cheese on top. There was a lot more cheese on Pat's cheesesteak and the meat was similar to Geno's but fuller and not as juicy. Both of these were awesome. You have to try these two if you are in Philly!

Service is great here but the food is just okay. I tried to like it because I've heard so many good things, but I always leave feeling disappointed. The enchiladas and burritos are just okay, but the chips, salsa, and guac are good. Drinks are also kinda weak. I'm just not really impressed with this place.
My lord!!! Takes 20 minutes for 2 large fries. I was the 2nd car in line waiting in the drive thru. Needs more staff!!!

Genos was better than Pats

Wouldn't drive to do it again but coming from DC made for an interesting trip.

My husband is from Philly so the cheese steaks being wrong in Florida is all I here about. On a trip to Philly last Summer we hit this place up on out way back to the airport. Phenomenal! I never understood why a cheese steak in Florida doesn't taste the same, now I do! It's been about 8 months and we're both jonsing for a Pat's cheese steak!

I'm guessing though out the years their cheese steak got a bit too plain..  No offense or anything, i still love this place very much.  The beef now are less juicy and the cheese has to melt more.  As for the cheese fries, they were good but there wasn't enough cheese!  The price for one whole cheese steak is around $10 now, and the cheese fries?  I don't even know.  But it's pretty cheap of them not to give the customer more cheese.  And usually its better if you pour it out from your cup so that you're able to scoop the cheese to the fries.

I'm sorry but I just don't get it. Think McDonald's but slightly more trustworthy ingredients. The price is great and the food is always a good greasy burger and fries. Aside from that, yeah, I just don't get it.

Anytime we're in Philly, we HAVE to stop by Pat's. Cheesesteak was overcooked & dry, but still good. If you want melted cheese, get cheez whiz. Service was good, but language was a bit dirty, in both ways. I'm thinking that's probably normal in this neighborhood. Oh, and half the peppers were good, but they ran out of hot chocolate. 
:-/ If you want a really good cheesteak, go to Tony Luke's or Chinks.

Pros: cheesesteaks served up without racism (I'm looking at you, Geno's). The condiments are great-- hot pepper bar is great. Got my order in about 30 seconds.  

Cons: Premade and cold, which is why I got my order in 30 seconds. The cheese on my provolone with was not even close to being melty because the whole thing was cold. All this for $9.50? Fuck that.  

If you're looking for a cheesteak don't go to a tourist trap. Little local pizza places are invariably better, though I will say that Jim's on South and 4th is quite good, fresh to order as you watch.

I pretty much agree 100% with Chrissy R. and I can't think of anything I could say that probably hasn't been covered in the 539 reviews prior to me but here I go anyway.

I need to check on this but I'm pretty sure they source the same ingredients from the same places as their rival across the street. So, arguments on steaks are pretty much moot. The difference? Pat's chops their steaks up. Geno's does not.

So that awkwardly tough steak is a lot easier to eat than Geno's just due to the nature of their preparation.

Bonus: Pat's isn't lit up like a tattoo parlor and the place is generally more inviting.

I think this place is more about the experience and history than it is about the food. Don't get me wrong. The cheesesteak with Cheese Wiz and onions was pretty good. It doesn't have flavor that pops out at you. The meat I had was much more chewy than other cheese steaks that I had. 

Service is really fast. You need to know what you want and have your money ready. From the time you order and pay not one minute goes by to when you have your food. 

After you order your sandwich then you get into another line for fries and a coke.  Which cost another $7.00 

The fries are also average in taste. But we're not soggy. In fact they were a little on the crisp side.

Legendary Cheesesteak House competing with Geno's on the facing corner. Good cheesesteaks here, as for me I prefer Geno's, I think the cheesesteaks are better. The only way to know for yourself, is to try them.

Cantina was many, many years early to the current Passyunk boom and has a great location, a loyal following and friendlier prices than some of its newer neighbors. Occasionally the specials raise above the average and they have the most perfect chips and salsa you could imagine, but this is a place where you should expect atmosphere and drinks and be surprised by anything more.

On occasion, expect slow food preparation, disappearing servers, chips and even waters to never be refilled -- even with tons of staff working and only half of the tables filled -- and hope that the company of your friends is enough to compensate. It still does for me after more half a decade.

Touring through PA with a bunch of friends, I requested we stop by Philly for lunch as I wanted to try a true philly cheese steak that was well, from Philly. Like everyone else, I had heard about the famous Pat's and Geno's and we decided to grab lunch at Pat's. My friend, who having tried a cheese steak here before warned me that the place wasn't going to be what I expected it to be, and now, I am warning you.

This place is damn horrible. 

For 8 bucks you get a limp, tough piece of bread with some incredibly dry meet topped off with freaking cheese whiz. Eating it, I can only think to myself what on Earth makes this place famous for its cheese steak. If not for the damn cheese whiz, it would probably be impossible to take a bite out of the sandwich.

While I only stayed in Philly for lunch, I really hope this is not the best that Philly has to offer in terms of a sandwich with which its city is known for.

My single most favorite place to go at 3am on a Sunday morning with a hot Puerto Rican lady you just met!

Seriously a must stop in Philly you can go across the street to Genos and his ignorance or you can wait in the line here and be doubly satified as you would across the street.

Philly I love ya and cant wait to come back!

I do prefer Pat's over Geno's. Though even at Pat's, the food wasn't out of this world great either. Maybe they're overhyped and I expected too much before ordering? Bottom line, good to go at least once but will not go out of my way to return.

Awesome Mexican food!!! The Mexican hot dog is yummy! The tres leches cake is so good and I've never really liked that dessert. The goat burrito is by far the best frikkin burrito I have ever had, hands down!!!!! The servers are chill, the people are cool. It's just a great place. This is my second visit from Northern Virginia and each time I come to Philly I will stop and eat here.

When you think of being a tourist in Philly you think of seeing the Liberty bell and weighing in on the Pat's/Geno's debate. We tried both places and while we both felt that Pat's was marginally better, these two places are essentially the same so I might as well cut and paste my Geno's review here because the same thing can be said about both places. 

"What you basically have is a bunch of grumpy people, tired of dealing with tourists, who use an assembly line to mass produce a product using low quality ingredients. Cheese whiz and steak-umms....yum. They then charge you $9 for the experience. The fact that the city of Philly demands that you call it a cheesesteak doesn't change the fact that there are half a dozen places in my Massachusetts town where you could find a better steak and cheese for a couple bucks less. " 

A tourist such as myself has to try the place but I couldn't imagine ever going back a second time.

2 stars because the man was very rude and some of my steak was burned. Me and my husband spit a large wiz wit, it was small for a large and not really worth the $10 in my opinion! It was a nice to go across the street to see the competition but we probably won't go back.

I hear that Pat's used to have a really good cheesesteak a really long time ago before cheese whiz was invented.  I think they have little flavor, too much grizzle , and the cheese whiz just ruins it for me.  Im my opinion Geno's is better than pats, but Geno's isn't great either.  Im my opinion both are tourist traps.

Want an eye opener.  Go through all of  the reviews and only count the ones from Philly.

Yes, I like Pat's more.. They have more selections and their meat is soft and their bread is fresh.  Selections I mean you can choose to add different toppings on your cheese steak. And I love lots of cheese wiz on top !! Nobody can recreate this taste! Great for late late night hunger!

So we finally went to Pat's for a Philly cheese steak let's be realistic here the best ?hardly, It was good then again we were hungry. The people working there were acting like they were doing you a favor instead of doing their job. The sandwich was good  but small and over priced. The outside condiments bar was with peppers etc.. was not to sanitary with bugs flying around and some people grabbing peppers with their hands yuck! I am sure there are better places than this to buy a Philly cheese steak.

Just went there for the first time and I have never been treated so rudely in my life.  They were impatient, insulting, and tried to charge me twice.  Also it was probably the worst cheesesteak I've ever had.  I could get a better one for cheaper in bucks county.

I've been to Cantina numerous times in the past 3 years and I always have a decent experience. It's never extremely great or extremely horrible. 9 times out of 10 I order quesadillas, and the quesadillas have gotten significantly smaller since I first started ordering, however the price is still the same. Not pleased!

Two thumbs up for the steak sandwich here.  The line for this place is incredible even when it was pouring rain there.  I haven't tried Geno's which is it's competitor but maybe next time when I'm in town.

Last night was my first time ever hearing about this place and visiting.  I met a friend there where we shared a pitcher of margarita and both ordered food.  The margarita was on point and made it worth the $25 price tag.  The burrito I had was just okay nothing to rant and rave about but the following morning it made a great breakfast!!

The atmosphere was cool with hipsters everywhere even though I despise hipsters lol  Good place for a date or to chill with the homies!!

I went here for the first time on a gorgeous Tuesday evening in the spring.  The place was absolutely packed so perhaps I did not get the best service/impression of this place but whatever, its still getting 4 stars because "yay! I'm a fan".  Very cool place in the city to get mexican.  Their menu is creative.  The margaritas were only so so strong but I have yet to find a place in the city that serves a margarita where you can really taste the tequila and not the mix.  The red salsa was great.  We got mushroom and cheese empanadas.  They were ok, the dressing that accompanied them was absolutely terrible so I just didn't eat it.  Interestingly I had asked our waitress what it was just because it was so bad.  She felt terrible and gave us complimentary tequila shots!  I thought that was really nice.  The true gem of this place is found on the side menu.  Who knew.  Their quinoa,cucumber and peanut side is out of this world.  Unique and delicious.  Mexican?  Not sure but who cares.  Finally we got a burrito with all the dressings.  You can't really go wrong with this.  We didn't get to sit outside because it was so busy but for center city philly they have a great outdoor area.

Cheese fries are great! We did the whole steak competition w my sister and her bf across the street at the rival location. I think both are very similar. I tried the one that looks more like the underdog. The rivals are a lot flashier. It's definitely worth going and trying....it's yummy and a fun thing to do. (This competition is seen on TV)

Depending on who you talk to, the OG of cheesesteaks since 1930.  Located in South Philly, this really is a haven for a good cheesesteak..  Its a greasy, tasty, artery clogging good time.  Yep, I'm a Pat's fan.

First time trying Pats and Genos in Philadelphia. Pats is definately better than Genos! Tried both at the same time and you can definately taste the difference! I ordered the cheesestake with onions and provolone on both of the sandwiches. Pats has a distinct taste and it so much juicier. Genos cheesestake taste like any other stake sandwich. I feel that I can make this at home. I'm from New York and I've been to many places where they served cheesestakes including the mom and pops or whole in a wall restaurants. When in Philly, you definately have to visit Pats!

We came here for dinner and happy hour margaritas and we received dinner and margaritas. As for anything special about this place, eh. It wasn't horrible and the food was palatable. But compared to all the Mexican food I've enjoyed in CA, this South Philly restaurant is lacking. The salsas weren't spicy enough, my quesadilla came with an odd side of what seemed like mayonnaise, and the green rice was way too salty. With everything a bit off, it doesn't seem quite fair to be charging such high prices. The house margarita was tasty though, so at least they have that going for them.

Five Guys did not live up to the hype.  I got the regular cheeseburger (note, two patties) with mayo, mustard, and fried onions.  There was no option for real cheese instead of Kraft slices.  The burger was okay.  I do not understand the great love that it inspires in some people.

The fries were soggy and unremarkable.

On the bright side, I did get to see what a half ton of potatoes looks like.  It was stacked up in the corner.

Burger and regular soda cost about $9.

Addendum 2011-09-20: My three-year-old tried their burger with everything last week (at the Bethesda, MD location).  She gives it an enthusiastic thumbs up.  Warning: the default burger is a double.  If you want a single patty, you have to specify you want the "small" burger.  I forgot.

Addendum 2016-02-01: I'm downgrading Five Guys to two stars.  The burger tastes okay, but it is ugly and squashed looking, so I did not enjoy eating it  The fries were mealy and underdone.  Little burger and fries cost about $9.

Please don't be fooled into going to Pat's for a Cheesestak!!!!!! They are NOT the king of Philly Cheesesteaks!!!!! Their Cheesesteaks are Horrible!!!!  We are Philly natives and have NEVER thrown a cheesesteak away but their cheesesteaks are garbage and should be thrown in the trash. They're rude, they make you put everything on your steak yourself, the meat is tough, bland, and full of grit, and the bread is cold.  The whole experience was bad.  I never write reviews, but had to today because its sad that so many people think Pats is a good Philly cheesesteak place and its not even close. There are sooooo many others that are much better.  Larry's on City Line Ave is 100% better.  This was nothing but a complete waste of time and money for me.  Please don't make the same mistake.
Great experience, great staff, i had amazing cheese quesadillas w/ a smoky sour cream. the homemade salsas are "bangin" and it was very affordable. go team!

Came here after a football game after having already tried Tony Luke's. I wouldn't say it's necessarily better but, in my opinion, the Cheese Wiz is the way to go if you come by here. Definitely get the onions too as the cheesesteaks can otherwise be too overwhelming with meat

Had to check out Pat's because of all the hype. For a $10 cheesesteak I was wildly disappointed. Really not that much flavor and the bread was a little too tough for my taste. I think people should go to say they've been, but I wouldn't say it's the best philly in Philly. Next time we are hoping to check out their competitor, Gino's.

Had guac here that was literally life-changing.  Known as "special guac," it was covered in fresh jalapeno, red onion, pine nuts, and pomegranate berries.  Also had a spiced pear marg that was pretty on point.  The vibe in here is great.  I would recommend this place to anyone.

Come here for a "philly steamed steak". This was my first stop on my philly cheesesteak tour and I was dissapointed. The bread was good but the quality of the beef sucked.  Literally sucked.  I was expecting flavorful, nicely cooked and seasoned steak.  What I got instead was bland "steamed" steak.

Ehh... next time I'll try T/L.  If you're here... go diagonally across.

I usually come here for an AM night run. The place usually is empty, so it is east to get a steak. The steaks themselves are decent. Only 2 offputting facts: the staff is kind of rude and really just want you to order and get out of their face, which some people won't enjoy. Also, there is only outdoor seating so some might not like that.
No complaints here. Food was good and creative. Service was nice  I got "Da Bomb" a stuffed pancake with bacon egg and cheese.

Overrated at best. Staff is not welcoming at all. Sandwich is ok at best.   Genos is better. Not by much, but better. I'd rather have a great steak at a higher price than a ok steak  every
day. Tony lukes is better.

I do not recommend anyone waste their time or money at this place. I'm from Jersey but have been living in California for years. I came to visit family and was excited to enjoy a good ole cheesesteak again. I wanted the best of the best and head so much hype about pats that I had to try it. 

Big mistake! We went on a Wednesday at about 2pm... only good thing about the trip was we didn't have to stand in line, there was literally no one there. Walk up to the window and give my order and before I could even finish talking my sandwich was shoved across the counter at me... I though hmm ok I guess they are used to fast service. 
Well I realized they are not freshly made, my cheesesteak was cold, and the American cheese not melted. It honestly taste like shit. Straight into the trash it went along with my $10. 
My cousins and my dads cheesesteak was also cold... my cousin got mushrooms on top of hers which warmed the sandwhich enough to make it edible at least. 

I know this is philly but I was also kinda surprised that the customer service is so crappy and rude. Please don't support this business, there's so many amazing smaller places that are clean, friendly, and actually know how to make a cheesesteak.

Second worse ever, many consumed.  Next worse across street for your convenience. Rude factor marginally less here, but still would not feed to the homeless in area inday time.   Surprised at the rudeness of the whole town. Brotherly what?

Pat's was fine- mostly good for the experience. The line wasn't too long and it moved fast.  Ordering was a little stressful. :) The cheesesteak was okay (I had the mushroom steak "whiz wit"- with cheese whiz and onions).  It tasted fine, but I wasn't blown away or anything.  

I like that Pat's is a bit more "down home" than flashy Geno's across the street.

Disgusting margarita. Awful service. The food took an hour to come out and by that time I had lost my appetite- something that never happens to me. This was, without a doubt, the worst dining experience I've ever had.

My wife and I have a friend that lives around the corner.  Every once in a while, my wife will spend a weekend with our friend and they always go to this place.  During one of these visits, I went along.  My wife and friend had been talking about the goat tacos (neither would order them but they knew that I would if given the opportunity).  I was intrigued by the goat tacos.  At first glance, the place appears to be your usual tavern type place.  I like the hardwood tables and decor.  I find the staff to be an interesting group of people.  I don't care about their appearance, that is part of their clique.  I ordered the goat tacos and a jalapeno bloody mary.  First, the bloody mary was excellent, with enough spice and acidic tomato juice to get the blood flowing.

I have not stopped thinking about the goat tacos since I've had them.  They were outstanding.  They double layer the taco shells, which I'm told is an authentic Mexican touch.  This is a necessary step as the goat is braised, simmered, and super juicy.  

I've only been here one time but had a very enjoyable experience and will absolutely go back when I'm in town. 

As an FYI, this was on a Sunday around lunchtime.

We love this place for the outdoor seating and great margaritas. While sometimes the service can feel a little slow, the patio area and bustling vibe more than make up for it. It's packed in nice weather for a reason!

Let's out it this way, if you like Pat's you don't know a real cheesesteak. It is a tourist trap and people are unfortunately drawn to it by name alone. There are plenty of other cheesesteak places in Philly that far surpass Pat's. It's a good place to go if you are drunk and can't tell what you are eating.

It doesn't matter what the food is like..or the service, really.  Pat's is a rite of passage when in Philly.  If you like cheesesteaks, then you have to go to Pat's.  If you don't like cheesesteaks, you should still go.  'nuff said.
Best steaks in town BY FAR!! You only go to Geno's when the line at Pat's is too long.

I went here like 2 years ago and ordered without using their "lingo" and I lived to tell the tale. Why the fuss, guys?  Not curious to try it again, thanks. Far less creepy than Geno's but I think they have equivalent grease levels.  Not that I have a problem with that, but when I eat that much fat straight up I prefer it to have awesome, extra memorable flavor.

Even though they are north of the Mason Dixon line, they are still full of sugary sweetness "My pleasures" However, whats with the lack of spicy chicken biscuit and sandwiches at this location? Can they not handle the heat??
Great cheesesteak from there last night.  Had one wit provolone.  Will go back next time in town for wit American cheese one.  Really good stuff from Pat's!

Whew, what a line. Stopped by here to try out a Pat's and a Geno's in order to figure out which one I liked better.

Turns out, I liked Pat's better. 

The bread here is the same as at Geno's, and the meat quantity is about the same. They gave me around the same amount of mushrooms and onions, too. They actually had a lot more whiz, though, on my oily, greasy steak, so I had to appreciate that a bit more than others. However, it felt light for a sandwich - I wolfed it down and had plenty of room to go across the street, wait, and get some more.

The seating is outdoors here under the overhang, and there's ketchup, mustard, pickles (hot peppers too) and napkins outside. Sodas are expensive for size - just hold out and go to a McDonald's for more soda to drink if you really want one. Tables a bit messier than expected, though, I think they just hose them down at the end of the day.

Service was swift, blunt, and more or less what I expected out of somewhere so busy.

Overall, an okay cheesesteak that is greasy and filling but not really packed with ingredients. Satisfies but doesn't fill me, just like Geno's.

A good value burger that's convenient and quick.  The fries are solid, but not spectacular.

Personally, I prefer a burger that has more going on than just a couple pure-beef patties on a bun.  Good Dog still stands out as my burger of choice, though I am anxious to try one at Misconduct Tavern.

Was running through town as a tourist for the day.  Had to stop and pick up a couple of cheesesteaks from here and Geno's as a comparison.  Prices are pretty much the same.  But I have to say Pat's is better.  The cheesesteak was wet and greasy, but oh so good.  Worth the trip, the lack of parking, and of course the huge lines.  The sandwiches are not that big. Suggest that you get a one from each place to share!
Overpriced.  Rude employees.  Terrible, chewy, bland cheesesteaks.

I am not biased and I like both Pats and Ginos. Both of them make exceptional cheesesteaks and give you unique experiences.

The fun starts with placing the order where they post a set of instruction on how to order a cheesesteak and they server it to you in matter of milli seconds.

Me and my husband ordered a Cheesesteak with Wiz and a Mushroom Cheese Steak with wiz.Both of them are really delicious and the beef is so succulent and juicy.

This place is definitely worth the hype and a must try place not just for cheesesteak lovers but in general food lovers.

Great-tasting burgers with lots of different toppings to suit your mood and preferences. My usual is a little bacon burger with lettuce, tomato, raw onions, grilled onions, grilled mushrooms, & green peppers. A little burger is big enough for me, and a regular fills any guy I've eaten Five Guys with.

Their fries aren't that great though, usually kinda soggy and not crisp enough for me. The peanuts are nice to snack on while you wait, random but nice :)

Service is fast and friendly. I've never had to wait long in line to order or at all for a table. Open until 10pm!

Great restaurant!  The margaritas and mojitos are fantastic.  I usually get a burrito or fajitas on hungry occasions.  Their specials are usually pretty good as well.

Over the past year they have really transformed their outdoor space into a nice patio.  The only downside is that is where the smokers usually sit.  So if the wind is blowing in your direction you might get a bit of smoke with your chips and salsa.  Make outdoor dining non-smoking as well and I would sit out there more often!
Still one of the best.... Wit and Pro add some hot sauce or cherry peppers and you got the South Philly Italian steak sandwich.... Try two for the Rocky knock out!!!!
Worst I have eaten. Rude, sandwich is dry and fries are cold Burger King knockoffs. Save your money and time. Go to Gooey Looies for the best sandwich and service.

Anyone who gives this place less than 5 stars are clinically insane and have no idea what they're talking about. This place is great from the atmosphere to the food and drinks. If you're a fan of Mexican cuisine as I am you have to go here.

If you're looking for authenic philly cheese steaks - this is the place to go. But be warned - KNOW how to order it BEFORE you go to the counter  (there is actually a sign that tells you the correct way to), otherwise you end up like many others who have frozen at order time - at the back of the line.

The food here is excellent! The service was also great. I ordered fries and basic cheese steak. The food carried just the right amount of cheese - not too overwhelming, nor was it not enough. 

I guess part of the reason why they want you to know HOW to order is because your food is given to you literally by the time you can even get your cash ready to pay. Make sure to have cash as they do not accept credit or debit cards. Not too sure if they offer any promotional or discounted rates for military, etc.

Food is also very reasonable in price - not too expensive for the quantity that you receive, either. My  cheese steak was about a foot long and my drink also quite large - for about  $10.

I went to both Pat's & Geno's based on their reputation. I also saw a show on the travel channel about these 2 places & figured I would give them a chance.

My girlfriend & I split 1 Philly from each place so we could try them both.

Neither place was good.
Both places meat lacked flavor & the breads were soggy.

According to several locals, there are much better places to get Phillys in Philly.

** I think Publix in Tampa, FL makes a better Philly than both of these places.
Nasty attitudes from staff!! And how do you run out of fries on a busy day???? Steak wasn't that great.. TRY GENOS

The good:
The original "wiz wit" was a good sandwich and filling. The line moves quickly and they are very efficient. The ambiance is exactly what you would think of a classic philly steak shop. 

The bad: 
For what you get it is a bit over priced. $20 for a sandwich, fries and a drink. 
They can be rude if you don't know what you want. 
Seating is limited when busy and that is normal.

Best Philly Cheesesteak sandwich in the world. There are very precise instructions posted on the wall on how to order, and if you get your order right, you will likely get your cheessteak in under 6 seconds. Amazingly good.

Food: 4 stars
Location: 4 stars
Ambiance: 3 stars
Price: 3.5 stars
Service: 3.5 stars

Recommendations:  A great burger!  Being a west coaster living in Philadelphia, I have no choice but to compare Five Guys to In 'N Out Burgers.  The hamburgers are both well done.  These are the two best fast food burgers out there.  The edge that Five Guys has over In 'N Out lies in the French Fries, Peanuts, Topping Choices, Hot Dogs, Grilled Cheese sandwiches....

For all you east coasters who hear about In 'N Out Burger, rest assured that you have a equal, if not better option right in your backyard with Five Guys.  I don't even miss In 'N Out since I moved out to Philly.

Overall: 4 stars

"pat's king of steaks"....those of us who are natives of philly called them...plain 'ole "pat's"...yes!!!! many...many..moon's ago their sandwich steaks was fantastic!!! but!!!! with any business, the more customers you have, your quality of merchandise...amount cheapens...or should i say "cut-backs" ...i know what a pat's (philly) cheese-steak taste like from over 20 years ago....very "healthy"    (loads of steak)....  cheese whiz ....... condiments of your choice (no xtra charge)  now, those from out of state, brag about these philly cheese-steaks...it's an insult....i wish those of you could, have experienced a true "Philly cheese steak" & "not" travel to Philly to eat an italian roll

Are you kidding me!!  This place freaking sucks.  I went on a day trip to philly, and this so called 'famous' cheesesteak joint happened to be one of the places we were planning to check out.  I definitely came here because of yelp, and boy...it sucked!  

This place definitely lacked comfort.  While I was eating my cheesesteak, flies were flying into my face and mosquitoes were sucking my blood.  And they do not have restrooms!!  FYI, there is nothing special about the cheesesteak!!!!  You are better off making one yourself or grabbing a cheesesteak at a deli.  This was definitely not worth a visit.  I would never come here again nor would I recommend it to anyone.

LET ME GET ONE WHIZ WIT!!

Translation?  I want a cheesesteak with cheese whiz and grilled onions.  There's a kitschy little sign that will explain things if you're about 10 people back in line and are looking for how to order.  Granted, the folks here won't make fun of you if you spell things out and say, "hi, may I have a steak with cheese whiz and grilled onions?"  I think they get enough tourists to understand.

All three time that I've gone were usually just to say we had "been there, done that" before we skittered off to Atlantic City in a vain attempt to double our pay checks.  Overall, it's another JDAM to the gut - it will keep you full and tastes even better while you're foraging for drunk food.

Top it up with sweet peppers, a little bit of spicy relish, and use liberal amounts of ketchup.  I also recommend baby wipes so you're keeping your fingers clean after - that grease has a way of persevering over most napkins.

I'd be lying if I said I wasn't going to do it again so I won't - but man, it's not the first stop in the quest for a good steak!

Tried the Famous Pat's this evening after several recommendations from co-workers local to the area during a conference. After reading the "how to order" signs and being briefed by my co-workers ahead of time, I was disappointed of how rushed and rude the people taking the orders actually are to people who weren't familiar with these expectations when ordering. I know it's meant to be part of the "charm" of the establishment, but it takes away from the experience. The cheesesteak was OK, but very watery making the bottom of the bun very soggy.

Pets比較好吃
口味選擇種類多多
牛肉香又多汁
不用加醬料即可享受美食
去的人也比較多
分量大
女生兩人吃一個也可以

Visiting Philadelphia  last April, my friends and I knew that we had to eat cheesesteaks at least twice.  We decided to hit Pat's and Geno's since we had seen these "Cheesesteak Corner" competitors featured on some TV shows.  (I have since been informed by a native that this was a poor choice and subsequently obtained better recommendations which I will try on my visit next month.)  

We ate steaks from both stands back-to-back and much preferred Pat's.  They had a more extensive menu, enabling me to add mushrooms and peppers.  It seemed more authentic too, without the slick orange signage of Geno's.  Ultimately though, the sandwiches at Pat's just plain tasted better.  Our whole group of seven agreed that Pat's was better.  

So even if I go on to have better cheesesteaks in Philadelphia, I will always have a special place in my heart for Pat's.
Pretty awesome, definitely recommend the peppers and steak with whiz and fried onions....  they give you chopped steak while genos across street does not chop up the meet.

Cantina's an okay spot on the ever-evolving Passyunk strip. It's ALWAYS packed with people, and the vibe/decor is very chill and inviting. Their food is reasonably priced and pretty freakin' delicious - I recommend the burritos, they are GIGANTIC and only $8. The music is way too loud to have a conversation and the too-cool-hipster waiters could really care less about you being there which makes a grab-and-go drink practically impossible at this place.  Their margaritas are doused with sour mix, and barely a trace of tequila which is pretty frustrating when you're paying $20 a pitcher. Last time I went I actually left about a 3rd of a pitcher on the table when I paid my bill because my sour-tolerance had been shot. All in all, it's not a bad spot for some good mexican food, but not the most intimate setting if you want to eat, drink AND talk to your friends.
Yes, Pat's in South Philly does have the best Cheesesteaks in Philly.  If you ever visit Philly, this is where you need to go hands down!
The cheesesteak was good. The "cash only" policy and prices are definitely cons. $10 for an average cheesesteak seems a bit steep in my opinion.

Wow, I thought this is suppose to be the spot. I guess the media does have an influence on peoples opinion.

Bread was dry, meat lacked flavor, and I think I had to drown it with ketchup to give it some moisture. 

Was definitely not worth the 4 mile walk to get here.

i really liked my dining experience here. great margaritas with excellent tequila selection. i ordered the empanadas with guacamole which was reasonable in terms of price and portion (also very delicious). they have vegan entrees too. really nice waitress too and the manager (i think) was doing rounds making sure everyone was taken care of. all in all, this is a cute place to have drinks and/or eat some good mexican food!
The staff is super nice! The food is goooood mmmm.. Had the cheesesteak with american and onions, with a side of cheese fries. Both were a win.. Go here, not across the street :)
Yo Adrien, it is what it is and I can eat them three times a day.

My childhood late night after drinking Rolling Rock with the guys hangout! Of course then I actually still ate meat. I drag my buddy Eric over here on the way back to the hotel, and we head up to the window. I was fully prepared to eat cheese fries. I stick my head in and said man that smells great but i don't eat meat I anymore... the guy replies "well your f*cked..." I started laughing, but then the kid on the grill says   you want cheese onions and peppers? DONE !!! Man that was one of the best grilled cheeses you could ever have. Good for that kid becoming creative and making me a meatless Philly Cheesesteak. I'm telling you... the bread the grilled onions, the grilled peppers, and the Whiz...   killer. Ordered some cheese fries and popped a bunch of hot cherry peppers on the sandwich too. I expected to get nothing, instead went home totally satisfied!

I had been here 7 or 8 yrs ago and really enjoyed it..... I was back in Philly this weekend to visit my son and honestly it's just okay...... I can honestly say it's not bad and some people just don't like it because tourists go here, but I have to be honest and say the quality has dropped in my opinion and the value isn't there. Sonny's at Penns Landing was far better. To each his own.
best cheese steak in the history of the world.  i went here 4x in one day and will go back every single time i'm in Philly.  it's 1.5 stars better than Geno's

Cantina is one of the few places in Philly that serves goat - so it's high up on my list of regular places to grab a bite. Everything I've ever gotten here is good & the Plantains are to die for - addictive even.

If you can snag a table outside, order a pitcher of their fresh & home made margarita from their Tequila menu & stay awhile. Inside, the music can be on the loud side. I've had some serious late night conversations sitting outside after a few pitchers of margaritas and a mojito or two. Overall it is definitely a "scene" but the food, drink & location live up to the hype. A lot of these reviews warn against the "hipster vibe" but really, I just go for the goat tacos & plantains.

Excuse me yuppie foodies who have posted on Pat's Yelp. This isn't fine dining, so adjust your expectations and enjoy the experience. Don't like being rushed at the window? Read the sign and be prepared. This was my first Philly cheesesteak. Got wiz and one w provolone. Wiz rocked. Much better compliment to the greasy onions. "wit and wiz" baby!

This is exactly want I had in mind when I wanted to try a PHilly cheese steak. I was a little nervous about ordering but I guess I got it right because they didn't send me to the back of the line (like the sign says if you order wrong). The line was long but fast moving. The cheese fries looked good but we didn't try them. I got a philly wit wiz. My friend and I split one and it was more than enough for us. I'm so glad I got to eat a cheese steak from here. Definitely something to cross off my bucket list

A friend and wanted to try both Pat's and Geno's.  He jumped in line at Pat's, and I at Geno's.  The plan was to each get 2 cheese stakes, and then swap one each for a taste challenge.

First clue, the length of the lines.  Got our steaks from Pats in under 5 minutes. Geno's took 20 + minutes.

As far as the stakes go, Geno's was MUCH better all around.   Pat's still made a great cheese steak and has enough history to be well worth a visit(s).

Had some friends in from out-of-town this weekend (first Philly visit) and of course the cheesesteak was one of the main attractions.  I have taken loads of people to the historic King of Steaks, and they always love it - and so do I.  I have enjoyed this local icon countless times, in countless varieties.  Yesterday I had a mushroom steak, whiz wit - tasted as good as ever.

The argument is old as time.  Some will say Pat's, some will say Geno's, Tony Luke's, Rick's, Jim's, or any of the lesser know neighborhood spots throughout the city.  In reality, you'll get a good cheesesteak at any of these fine establishments.  But in the end, if you're in it for the experience it's got to be Pat's or Geno's.  I make this statement with the tourist in mind.  My local friends and I rarely visit these landmarks unless it's to indulge an out-of-town guest.  But I must say, explaining how to order, and the mystique that surrounds someone's first trip to the birthplace of the steak sandwich gives me a nostalgic feel.  

Although I've enjoyed more Pat's steaks than I can count, I get a special feeling when I approach the front of the line to order one of the greatest, most famed culinary creations in the world.

Pat's is definitely better than Geno's but these are both TERRIBLE. I'm from California (born and raised) and I can't believe I came here to try this even with advice from a recent local. 

My advice to tourists: DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME HERE. Go elsewhere. Go to Dinic's which is totally worth the wait and $.

I went here at 1am or something on a cold night. The steak was good, but not so good that I wanted more. I remember it being extremely greasy. It was one of those "must try" things in Philly, which is the only reason I went.

The best part about my experience? The guy in the window asked if we wanted sushi. Yeah, because we were all Asian. Niiiice.

Try Jim's instead.

Took my kids to Pat's when we traveled to Philly this past weekend. 

Mediocre. Tourist trap.

The fries were awful battered things with cheese whiz (God help us). The steak was ok. The meat was good, the roll was good, the provolone was not melted and it was pretty miserable eating a steak with a few cold slabs of cheese on it.

Personally, my advice to you if you are in in Philly is to get a cheesesteak at Lee's Hoagie House. Much better steaks.  For the best cheese fries, go to any pizza place that has real (not battered) fries and will melt mozzarella on the fries for you--that is a real Philly cheese fries situation. 

Also, parking...what parking? A nightmare at best in South Philly.

One of my favorite Mexican restaurants in the city!!  This quaint and adorably-decorated place is located right in the heart of South Philly.  It's within walking distance so I practically live there.

Let's start with the margaritas - they have fruity ones and then the regular lime.  I always go with the regular lime.  You can get a pitcher or by the glass.  You can also get it frozen or on the rocks with salt.  I go with on the rocks with salt.  Yum!

You then get an unlimited supply of chips and salsa/salsa verde.

Since I am a vegetarian, I usually go with the bean/rice burrito.  I have also had the vegan beef burrito which is EXCELLENT!  So, yes, this place is veggie/vegan-friendly.  

The black bean soup is scrumptious and I always start off with that.  

The portions are big, so come hungry and don't fill up on too many chips and salsa!
 
If you wind up having room in your belly for dessert, they have vegan selections as well as regular desserts.  

Love this place!!

Pat's has been my favorite place for cheese steaks. Despite the fact that there's always a long line, it usually moves fast. Prices are reasonable and the meat is well seasoned. I ordered a cheese steak with mushrooms, peppers and double provolone cheese. It was fantastic! I also love their cheese fries.

I love Pat's but the only reason I gave it 3 stars is that the staff are complete low lifes.  They are so rude,  There is one woman working at the soda/fry counter who is really dirty looking and so ignorant.  She was yelling at an asian guy because she was having trouble understanding him. I was standing right next to him and understood him just fine.  Again, I like the steaks, but I think most of the people who work here are on a prison release program.

Solid service. Friendly waiter who told us what items on the menu would be available to us quickly and offered us a beer sampling. 

The empanadas are giving me deliciousness chills at this moment; the mushrooms are just perfectly al dente. I actually had to stop and make time for a review after my mouth experienced these bites and then could not comment simultaneously, lest I exclaim passionately with my mouth full. Holy smoke. 

We were only in the market for a late night joint to grab a bite. Had no idea we would find a gem of food glory in our state. ;)

Come here late. Enjoy a drink and split three appetizers. So yummy. So satisfying.

Having not lived in Philly in 28 years, I had to venture here.

I know it's a tourist trap, but wow, it was worse than I imagined.

The steak itself was great, and of course the roll was, but it was just bland.  The worst part?  The mushrooms, straight out of a can and dumped on top.  Glad I got this one over with.

As far as tourist traps go, Pat's is definitely the one you want to go to. Their ingredients are 100 times better than the joint across the street. 8 to 9 times out of 10, you will get an above average to great steak (especially if you like thick slices of meat). Their prices are getting way out of hand. It's $10 for a cheesesteak with extra cheese and of you want a small order of cheese fries and a drink, you're looking at almost another 10 bucks.
