I had mushroom pepper cheese steak with onions and provolone cheese. Yummy. After a 2-3 hour drive from DC - it's all worth it for me. 

I'll just leave it at that since there's over 1500 reviews already lol. I'll leave it up to you mysterious yelp reader what you think. 

~happy eatings!

Pat's is famous for it's cheesesteaks but also know that you have to be ready to order as soon as you reach that window. The move people very quickly which is great because you can be in and out in 10 minutes when there's a long line. I only gave it 3 stars because the steak was more slab-like than chipped which I like chipped better. It was still good though!

I very rarely consume red meat and french fries, due to the kind of effect it has on my stomach.  Sometimes however, you get the urge.  And when I get the urge, it's Five Guys time.

Pretty damn impressive for a chain - these burgers are fresh and delicious.  And the Cajun fries, drowning in Cajun spices, are little potato slices of heaven.  The only problem is - your breath will be plagued with the spices for about as long as it takes to get through your system.  Ha.

Surprisingly, I don't feel like death after eating here, but it definitely makes me sluggish.  Not recommended before or after strenuous physical activity.

I know there are many bad reviews on this place and I understand why, it is expensive for what you get, it is cash only, they aren't the nicest people around, but it's a very distinct taste and I do enjoy it on occasion, one of those things I get a craving for and nothing else will do. You should give it a shot at least once, maybe share it with someone.

Five Guys fulfills a very specific niche in my life. I often find myself wanting a cheeseburger. Sometimes I am low on cash and time and am happy to spend $1.07 at McDonald's to indulge this craving quickly. Other times I want to sit and splurge and have an awesome burger, and at these times I head to Rouge or Village Whiskey. But what to do when McD's won't cut it but I don't have the $25+ I'm going to drop if I let myself walk in the door at VW?

Enter: Five Guys. 

The burgers are solid. You're not going to get locally-sourced, specialty-mixed ground beef cooked to medium rare. Instead, you get a choice: one patty or two? Cheese or no cheese? Which of the myriad free toppings would you like? Remember, you are here because this is NOT fancy or expensive. You get what you pay for. And what you pay for is damn good. My go-to order is a little cheeseburger ("little" is one patty and quite enough even for my sizable appetite) with A1, grilled onions and mushrooms, lettuce, tomato, and extra pickles. Dee-lish. I usually go with fries, you can easily share a regular order among a table of 4. You might wait 10 minutes for your burger if it's busy, but you can hang out and snack on the free peanuts while you wait.

My friend and I went in here on a Sunday night after some chestnut street shopping. We had a great time. The staff was friendly and the burgers were amazing for a chain place. a Big burger with classic american toppings (ketchup,mustard, pickles, onions,lettuce and tomato) and it was WONDERFUL. Cheese ooey gooey American goodness. I ordered just a drink to go along with my burger since they offer no combos and I don't Like fries too much. My friend ordered their smallest order of fries and ended up splitting them with me there was so much and we actually took some home too . Their drink machine is one of those touch screen ones with the drink flavoring options so I opted for vanilla Coke and was not disappointed. Happy with my meal that night, and will return.

New to the Philadelphia area tried out this location because it's in beautiful historic Chestnut Hill.  It is so many restaurants to eat I wanted something quick before I head back to class. This Starbucks up the road is clean from the outside to the inside it puts McDonald's to shame.

Let me tell you the food was awful slapped together, fries with greasy no salt. My food went into the trash. I contacted corporate headquarters for a refund they put me in touch with the owner franchise and he never wanted to refund me my money nobody taking responsibility for the dirty outdated atmosphere and food prepared portly. This location needs to be updated the owner needs to take responsibility when the food being prepared in his kitchen. After reading the other reviews on this site I decide to write my own since I was left with a nasty taste in my mouth.

Extremely fast service. Your order is in, you pay, get your change and your sandwich. The sandwich itself was decent, though greasy, and you started tasting the grease rather than the good. There's other choices, but I'd go back if in the area.

They sucked just as much as Geno's did.
Bad cuts of meat.
No seasoning.
Nasty tasting.
Staff were rude. 

When we drove up on this place... it looked so cool but I soon realized ... well after my first bit that these two places are a tourist trap. 

Nasty.

Well the hype was let down for me. I've heard of the Pat's vs Geno's steak sandwich. So I decided to go with Pat's since I heard it was much better. Well going there I didn't know it was cash only. Luckily I had exact amount for a cheese steak sandwich. Which cost me $10. And it sucks they don't take credit or debit cards. They would get so much more business if they did. Well finding parking was a pain first of all. Such a small area that I was lucky to get a spot across the road. Then the line on a weekday was super short. It does go by quick. However the guy at the register seems to not care about waiting cause he makes you order so fast. You need to know you're order and how to order before you get up to the register which is annoying cause being a first time customer you don't know. So I unfortunately ordered the wrong cheese cause I was rushed. The guy just wanted the money and for you to leave. Then I got the cheese steak and it lack flavor. The cheese wasn't melted which sucked. Overall the hype of Pat's was so bad. I possibly might return but probably try Geno's. or neither and find another place.

From the door the security was very nice and accommodating. We got a spot at the bar just when a group was leaving. The bartender was training a girl and she was very sweet and attentive. My friend got drunk and even walked behind the bar and the bartenders were easy going  about it and thought it was funny like we were all Friends. Thank u for making our night fun and easy going !

Sooo.. finally got to see what the whole "philly" cheesesteak hype was about! A friend of mine brought us here and had us get one from here and one from Gino's across the street to compare and contrast how good and nasty these are! 

I have to say that the bread and the meat both are MUCH better at Pat's and actually would never go back to Gino's. The line is about the same length in both (I'm assuming people have the same mentality as us to compare?). 

I can't give 4 or 5 star because of two reasons:
- They use their bare hands for everything, how do people not get hepatitis, diarrhea, food poisoning? The cashier guy collected money, licked his fingers to count my change, put meat on our sandwich, added cheese -- all with his bare hands. 
- This sandwich was good -- but $10? Not worth it. 

Overall, the sandwich was pretty decent and next time visiting Philly, I'd probably come again. It's more-so a "good experience" kind of like the 53rd and 6th Halal carts in NYC.
Do I really have to write a review? I have been at least 20x.  Simply the best! Have tried others-non compare!

Jason Toridasu is an amazing place to grab a quick lunch or have a full meal. The space is modern and comfortable. The sushi here is always fresh and taste amazing. Also for a very reasonable price. If a sushi roll that you want isn't available at the moment they will make it for you, and get it out to you fast. Overall Jason Toridasu is the best place to get your sushi from in Philadelphia!

AWFUL!!!!!! Came in today with my bf we just came from the Phillies game, 13$ for a burrito and drink (it's a fast food place) the food was terrible and my bf was vomiting shortly after. The cashier/girl with the tattoos on her arm was beyond pushy I said I wasnt hungry and was watching calories, she then went on to describe in detail what I should order. No thanks I'll stick to Qdoba if I want cheap (mexican) fast food or El fuego.

This is the best reason to leave Geno's line! Lol! Their line may be shorter, but theres a reason for that. Pat's cheesesteak was far superior. It has more meat, and seasonings on the meat and the whiz, well that just steals the deal. It was hot, fast, and the line flies. My bf and I tried Geno's first, (as we suspected Pat's would be better), and we were right!! Geno's steaks were dry, chewy and the bun was practically empty. There was no seasoning or flavor to the meat. You have to hit Pat's and order a "wit whiz" and youll be very satisfied. I cant wait to get back there.

The age old question...Pat's or Geno's. Personally I think both places make good cheesesteaks, it really depends if you like your steak chopped up (Pat's) or   kept in slices (Geno's). My preference was Geno's because it was easier to eat, the bread seemed a little better and I liked my meat in slices instead of chopped up.

Food is good! 
Awful Awful Awful...service.
The guy taking the order has a thick accent and speaking as quick like a rap song ....how the hell i am suppose to understand ? 
One item was missing ....
Amazing food. I loved my sandwich. I drove all the way from upstate New York just to get an authentic Philly cheesesteak. It took less then a minute to get my food and they o my take cash.

Regrettable, lackluster food and experience. I came here after perusing through the Italian Market, and after eating my sandwich, I regretted not eating somewhere - anywhere - at the Italian Market instead.

100% touristy and gimmicky, overpriced, greasy and messy, tastes like a waste of space, provolone not melted, not enough places to sit and eat, distasteful clientele.

I know that this isn't the local favorite for cheesesteaks in this city, but my tourist intuition told me to go here for a memorable experience. My sister had recommended against Geno's ("I've had better in Burbank, CA," she said), and I personally didn't care to financially support their political agenda anyway, so I chose Pat's. I'm guessing that there may not be much difference in quality or service, however.

Sorry, cheez whiz is disgusting in general. I instead ordered "one provolone wit." I paid my $9.50, and literally within 5-10 seconds, my sandwich appeared at the window. They spend more time and care making my sandwiches at Subway. I should have paid attention as soon as I picked up my cheesesteak from the counter, because the worker took out his towel and wiped down the greasy juices from the counter top where my food had just been... and as I walked around the building to find a table to sit and eat, the same greasy juices spilled right over my shirt and jeans. Gahh. Thank you, Pat's, for letting me walk around like this for the rest of the day (I spent the evening trying to scrub down my clothes in my hotel sink with a bar of soap).

I found a seat at a table as soon as a couple of other patrons finished their sandwich and left, and then sat about to eat my cheesesteak. I didn't like that the provolone wasn't melted, probably because they just slap a couple slices on the bread in the 5 seconds after your order. The meat tasted flavorless to me and the whole thing tasted like a waste of stomach space and calories to me. I rarely ever do this, but after eating my way 2/3 through the cheesesteak, I decided I was better off just tossing the remainder. Yes, I suspect that the cheesesteaks probably do taste better in Burbank...

And while I was sitting at my little table, a group of six Asian guys decided that there was nowhere else to eat, and just sat down and crowded the table with me and hovering around me as I ate. I get it, you guys are so awesome and badass that you can just overtake a lone girl's table without the shred of decency to ask if it's OK, or any sense of how uncomfortable and weird it is for me to have to sit among your thug selves as you swear up a storm talking about your cars and your women. Yes, you guys are so thug in your American Eagle Outfitters t-shirts. Pat's, if this is in any way representative of your normal patrons, I think I hate your dumb clientele more than your food.

Never again.

This was my second visit to Pat's and they didnt fail me. The meat is soo delicious and flavorful, and the service was quick despite the line I stood in (a cocktail before you stand in it helps a lot late at night ). It is cash only so beware, and parking is a little crazy. I ordered the mushroom pepper steak with provolone cheese, and onions. I didnt add any condiments except those additional peppers (they're delicious) because you dont need any. The meat makes the sub so moist.  I love Pat's!

They have become arrogant. Bread was hard as a rock...steak unflavored.. Saving grace was cheese and onions.. Well...anything will taste good with cheese and grilled onions. And very overpriced...10 bucks for less than extraordinary cheesesteak! I believe JerseyMikes are better

Not bad if you want some mexican food. This place has a fair bit to offer when it comes to a good meal and atmosphere. They have a pretty good sized menu and plenty of options to choose from along with a complimenting bar to go with the meal. The service was just average in my opinion, but the bartender was pretty good so it made up for it a bit. The food when it came out was pretty good. It was correct when it came out and it was pretty fresh. Overall I had a pretty good experience here and will probably come back in the future.

Finally made it to Pats... I've been dying to try an authentic cheesesteak for years and yesterday I got it and it did not disappoint. I got mine with mushrooms and whiz, fries and a lemonade. Omg I was in heaven. After running a 9.3 mile race earlier that morning this was the perfect end to my trip to Philly. 
The service was great. Long line that moved quick. Can't wait to visit again
Favorite steak place in all of Philly! Great staff, delicious steaks. They have several options for cheese, with our without onion, and it's decently priced. Pats is king

My wife and I once went in the McDonalds at 2nd & Lehigh. The cop stationed by the door there thought we looked out of place and warned us to be careful, eat, leave, The McDonalds at Cottman & the Boulevard is FAR worse. It is a filthy, foul smelling pig sty. Service by the semi-literate school children behind the counter (no competent management in sight) was terrible and slow. The real shocker is that the dirty, out- dated dining area seems to double as a day room for what appear to be about a dozen mentally ill and drug addicted homeless people. There was a young man in a corner booth talking and laughing loudly to himself and another gentlemen that appeared to be picking lice out of his head. The whole place is a sad commentary on 21st century America.

I've been going here for a while and the prices have been going up and the food quality is going down. However, I kept going, it was routine, they serve alcohol, my friend group was used to it.

THE STAFF AND SERVERS ARE GREAT. Good at their jobs and super friendly and cool.

Also they serve buffalo wings but don't have any ranch?? And the place was FREEZING.

First time in Philly so I went here to grab the original cheese steak. The cheese steak was honestly low quality and the eating environment kinda stunk. I had to go to a Dunkin Donuts just to take a piss.... Thriving on just its merit is the only thing about this cheese steak that keeps people coming. Jim steaks south street, Spataro's, or Molly Malloy's can make you a cheese steak that's 10x better. Don't make the same mistake that I made, listen to every local and don't go there. Being the first is great but it doesn't make it the best. The Wright Bros brought us the airplane but Glenn Curtiss made the aircraft what it is today.

Tried Geno's and Pats. I hate that they only take cash... So be prepared or you'll have to withdrawal $20 which is actually $23 after the ATM fee for a mediocre sandwich that cost $9.50. Everything about a cheesesteak counts and the only way genos is better than pats is they have better bread.

I can deal with the whiz on the steak because its supposedly what makes it a philly steak (all though I've lived in philly my whole life and pat's and genos are the only places that do this as standard). My issue is that the meat is thick and chewy.  its kind of like a roast beef sandwich with whiz instead of au jus.

I've never failed to have an AMAZING experience at this place. It's been a while since I've been but last night we came with originally 10 people in our party which was then bumped up to 14 and the hostess and staff was completely accommodating. We were suppose to have an hour wait which turned out to be 1/2 an hour - definitely started off the night right. While waiting we enjoyed pitchers of margaritas and when seated gobbled down their chips/salsa/guac starters. SCRUMPTIOUS. We shared steak nachos and I was over the moon with their Cabiritos entree (goat). It was tender and just plain mouthwatering. My boyfriend (who I nickname Tubby) housed their burrito. 

In addition to our very large group, there was another party a couple of tables down celebrating another birthday. Boy did we connect. We somehow turned the place into a karoake/dance party - wherein the bouncer proceeded to try to get us to calm down with, "Sit down, this is not that kind of a place." LOL, mission accomplished. I love it when there are other patrons who are willing to partake in silliness. It definitely says something about the fun atmosphere. Our waitress (who I'm sorry I didn't get the name of) was just plain lovely - she was game to dance along and take pictures with us.

All in all, we had a fan-tabulous night. I feel bad for the bouncer doing his job but when we left, he was totally courteous. Love this place and will be back soon! Especially since spring/summer is around the corner and that is just about the best time to hit it up!

Tourist trap in Philly, steak sandwich was decent, tasted like a Steak-Umm meat product from the 1980's with nacho cheese and a surly order taker. Cool experience, but I think it's mostly hype. Sandwich was okay, hot, and not terribly greasy, but the walk from downtown was long and next time I'll go to Sonny's.
How the hell do you take someone's order while on your cellphone? Worst service ever.

Tasty Twisters is one of, if not the actual, best pretzel companies in philadelphia, and my personal favorite. I love their new location (even if the old one made me feel like an insider with secret knowledge of a hidden pretzel utopia), and i love the owners and staff.

So, you can buy pretzels individually or in small numbers, or you can buy bulk. They make them fresh all day and they are salty, chewy, traditionally delicious. They also sell knots!!!

for people having parties, they do nub trays and have the usual variety of flavors and dipping sauces, ranging from sweet to savory.

one of the best things about Tasty Twisters, for me, is that for at least the last 15 years they have consistently and regularly sold their pretzels at large discounts to non-profits, community groups, and even worthy causes. on occasion, they have even donated them completely for free! there really is nothing better than a company that is as loyal to its neighborhood as the neighborhood is to it. 

so next time you are near Manayunk and have a craving for salty deliciousness, swing down to Umbria and look for them next to Goody's u pull it!

Stopped by when in town because I heard decent reviews. Food wasn't bad but customer service was! And woman who prepared food did so with bare hands...no gloves. Had a bad attitude from the get go. Won't go back.

3.5 stars but I will round up.  This was the second time in my life I had been here.  The first time was with my brother about 10 years ago.  Tonight I came with my buddy.  Ordered a whiz with.  A little pricey for a sandwich at $9.50 but it is the original cheesesteak so I found it worth it.  They hand you your sandwich within seconds of placing your order.  Speedy service for sure!  The sandwich itself was really good.  The steak was meaty, the cheese was gooey and melty and the onions all tied it together.  The bread could be a tad softer but it didn't take away from anything.  This was a greasy delicious mess.  I wouldn't hesitate to come back.

Went here right after Geno's (sorry to name drop). And the bread is way better than Geno's but the steak/meat in the sandwich wasn't as good as Geno's. Plus the line and hype is not all that. But it's definitely good to try different spots to compare. The price is just the same at $10 or so.

Occasion:  Lunch with European friend

So, I have a friend from Ukraine visiting the area who has never been to Philly...seemed logical to get him a cheesesteak.  Pulled up to the corner and chose Pat's, mainly because I parked closer to it and I don't really know the difference yet.  

Huge line, but moved fast.  Friendly, efficient service.  Why the one star?  At the risk of getting hate messages from Pat's lovers, the sandwich was a HUGE disappointment.  The meat was scarce and tough/dry, and the bread was excessively chewy.  Those combined to form a sandwich I could barely bite through.  I've had MUCH better cheesesteaks in many other places, without paying $11 for them.  

To add insult to injury, there was a huge shortage of seating mostly caused by people holding seats forever while the rest of their party waits in line for the food.  Where I come from, the custom is to NOT hold seats and let the people with the food have the tables!  If executed properly and courteously (meaning don't linger after eating when you can see the place is slammed), this system works well such that by the time you get your food there will be a table for you.  Sheesh people amaze me sometimes!

To recap, we ended up eating our shitty sandwiches standing by our cars and my European friend now think's I'm even crazier than the average American for even bringing him here.  

Nope.  Never again.

This place is disgusting. I love me some McDonalds but this location is messed up. I have gotten stale food from here multiple times. Sometimes there is mold on the buns, you should always check if ordering from here. They clearly are not throwing food away if it's old, they are resetting the timers to not waste the food and money. Seriously, this place is horrible. Do not eat here if you can help it. I like fast food so I am not complaining just for the sake of it, this place is not good at all. Skip a meal if you have to and stay away. I gave too many chances for this location, don't make the same mistake.

As a native Philadelphian I pretty much dismiss Pat's (and Geno's) as overly crowded, overpriced tourist traps. Their little steak sandwiches bear no resemblance to the tasty behemoths you can get at Jim's Steaks or at countless steak shops in the city for the same price or less (and with less attitude). Can't knock their hustle but there are too many better options in the city for me to ever do Pat's again.

Food is great, but service is hit or miss.  I have been coming here for years and I love their steak tacos and pretty much everything else.  Fantastic margaritas and the decor and outdoor seating is amazing in good weather.

I have had excellent servers, who are charming and knowledgeable, but I have also had several experiences where I have had the worst service in my life.  I am taking one star off for these multiple experiences.

I brought in a good friend from Miami, who is also in service, and we were ready to drink and eat like beasts.  The service was so terrible that my friend actually spoke with the server (after she literally ignored us with empty drink glasses for almost 1 hour, in an empty place) and let her know how terrible our experience had been.  This was so embarrassing.  I had just finished telling her how it was one of my favorite places.

I feel like the past several times have not been much better.  I no longer recognize the servers I used to think were so great either.  I am not sure if management has changed?  I have also had some really bad experiences with their new hostesses also. I do keep coming back for the food though.  Hopefully they get their act together again soon.

O god, another review about Pat's. Just what the world needs.... However, I'm going to do it in a different way. Proper etiquette behavior when there.

Rule #1 when going to Pats or Geenos or even Tony Lukes. Watch Seinfield's Soup Nazi ahead of time, don't ask question just do it. Because you don't want to be that Eileen... EVER! Know what you want, understand the lingo, listen to how the locals and people ahead of you are ordering, and practice it while you're in line. Don't talk to your friend while you're in line, just keep repeating silently it until you're up to the cashier and your tongue/throat has been physically trained to say those magic words. "Steak wit wiz and onion"

Then have the money and more specifically the paper bill ready in your hands, with appropriate speed when handing to the cashier, and ready to receive change. Then proceed on to receive your cheesesteak, and move to your left if you require additional fussing to pick it up properly. Use both hands as you will need it to hold the torpedo of joy that will invade your mouth, hmm that was dirty....

At this point your interaction with the cheesesteak woman or man is done, and god help you if you for one second decide to try and strike up a conversation. Then proceed on to your left to the french fries and soda section. This is less formal, and you may be given leniency on how you order, as long as there is no line. Otherwise its simply fries and soda wit wiz. No they will not put wiz in your soda, unless you're a complete idiot who engages them in mindless drivel.  

Finally, sit down at a seat or bench and enjoy your food. Follow these rules or you will be given the "No-Soup-For-You!" equivalent of South Philly. A quick verbal beat down, followed promptly by a not so kind reference on your mother followed by something which can only be characterized as you and an animal in compromising positions.

We went here on a Segway Tour of philly cheese steaks so we got to taste all 5 different locations in the area. This was our first stop on the tour and we liked the sliced meat but the cheese wasn't melted. For our first try it was good but not our favorite. The location is super cool and we lucked out with no line. Don't forget napkins. It's a must if in Philly and we are glad we tried it.
Downloaded the App. Ordered 6 Drexel special pizzas for a group. Showed up and no one was watching the printer so no one made my food. Really!  And getting the gluten free I ordered was tuff.

Don't ever go here. This franchise and franchise owner does not care about you. I stayed near by and after traveling 3.5hrs after working all day, thought I'd get some chicken and good onion rings. I can say I should have gone somewhere else. 

I got the 5 piece chicken with fries and onion rings. Chicken looked alright. But went back to eat not 2 minutes away. Food was ice cold and soggy. On top of the the onion ring were have burned off,ice cold, and in a kids meal bag. Yes I do regret not checking before I left but hungry and tiered I focused on getting back and eating what I thought was good. 

I contacted Popeyes on Facebook and they would relay that info and my email to contact me. That was mar 18 and I'm writing this on April 3. There response was, I see we have an open ticket and someone should contact you soon. 

So you can see by this review no one has attempted. 

So other then my local Popeyes that actually I know the people I will be refusing to go to any more Popeyes.
Great food. Nice fun selection of food. Tasty margaritas

As a former Maryland resident I was excited to see a Chipotle appear near my office, and the staff at this location is phenomenal.  Service is always fast and friendly, and if you're a once-a-week-or-more regular with the web orders, as I am, quite quickly they recognize you and have your bag ready to hand over when you get to the counter.  Qdoba is closer to my work, but I've not darkened their door since this Chipotle opened.

Loved Pat's.  This will be a must everytime I am in Philly.  

Pat certainly knows how to run his shop.  Although the wait is a little long, it is well worth it.  Know what you want to order a head of time.

Had a regular sandwich drenched in cheezwiz.  Or as Pat refers to it as, "The Wiz".  Couldn't complain!  Nothing like a Philly Cheeseteak to preceed a Springsteen concert.

100% recommended.  Lots of cool celebrity photos too.

My second trip to Philly and first to the cheesesteak corner between Pat's and Geno's.  Based on the reviews here, I chose to eat at Pat's and I was not disappointed.  I sat down with my mushroom steak with the Whiz smothered atop it and chowed down in touristy anticipation.  Overall, I liked it, but I think I still prefer Jim's steaks.

I normally don't stop at McDonald's except for a rare treat and today i was craving one of their salads,  but to my surprise when i got back to work and took the salad from the bag,  i was so disappointed the lettuce throughout was all brown and i  everything looked "old" and the chicken was supposed to be grilled and it was not,  it also did not smell to good,  my lunch went in the trash.  I had thrown away my receipt and from experience i know even with it they give you a hard time refunding your money.  Service was exceptional  though , so at least i got that much, but would've loved that and a good salad for lunch.

DId the pepsi challange with this place and ginos twice now when going through town.  To me there is no comparison.  This place is the king of steaks.  Still the best cheese steak ive had to date.  Next time im in town I am am going to try some of the less known places in the city and compare again.

Does this place need another review? Sure...why not?! Out of the Big 3 in Philly (Pat's, Geno's, Jim's), Pat's is my favorite. The meat is sliced thinner than Geno's, but thicker than Jim's. Also, the amount of Whiz they give you is more than any of the other places. I think their onions are better too.

Make sure you have your order ready and don't mess it up. Keep the line moving. Steaks at the first window, fries and drinks at the second. You pay separately, cash only! I always get the Whiz Wit. Minus one star because last time I was here, a steak is now $9.50. C'mon man!
Excellent food in a neat part of town. I highly recommend going. I know next time I'm in Philly, it will be a dinner stop for sure!

This was a late night trip to Taco Bell to specifically try the Cool Ranch Doritos Loco Taco. I tricked it out as supreme with beans instead of beef. And as much as I was looking forward to it, the Cool Ranchness was lost on it. Just like the Loaded Doritos at 7-Eleven, it left me underwhelmed.

The best bite of the night was the Carmel Apple Empanada. It was warm, crunchy on the outside and Carmel Apple goodness on the inside.

I also wanted to mention that the service was really out going and friendly. And I imagine this was partly because they were closing soon.

I was in Philadelphia this past week on vacation seeing some friends of mine and they suggested I at least try one of the tourist spots.  Between Geno's and Pat's, they suggested Pat's.  I was satisfied with what I had (cheesesteak "wiz wit").  It wasn't just mind blowing or anything, but it was very good!  There wasn't too much wiz, the steak portions were generous, and the availability of those red peppers adds a nice touch to the sandwich.

I'd give it a 3.5 if Yelp would let me.
Visited Pats today while on business in Philly.  It had been 6-7 years since my last visit and was as good as ever!!

I was disappointed at this machine of cheesesteak shop. They had sandwiches with slices of provolone waiting for the meat to be cooked but once the meat was added it didn't melt the cheese. The fries were not crisp... Pretty disappointing.

The cheesesteak I had at Pat's was my first, maaaaybe second, with cheese whiz. As my tastebuds were drowned by the imitation cheese, I thought a quick prayer to St. Peter for the lost slices of steak I could barely taste--for they were truly lost. 

The proportion of meat to whiz to bread was out of balance. The whole experience was a rather quick affair. Jump in line, report your order, shuffle money through the window, receive foil-wrapped bundle in return, sit under twilight zone lights, watch male companions scarf unceremoniously. The end.
Great costumer service ! They aren't super rushy like Geno's! I don't eat meat but they did have an excellent fish sandwich! My boyfriend ate the steak it was a lot more juicer ! Go to Pats!
First time here, very good, got ours with provolone cheese  may have been better with cheese whiz or American cheese , definitely next time.
Very good Pizza, loved being able to customize my own pizza! Very fast service, and high quality. Wished the pizzas were a little bit bigger.

Along with Popeyes and Wendy's this is one of the few franchise chains in the area.  The intersection is a pretty big hub and lot of traffic flows through the area so it tends to be busy.  Mainly drive through when I go.  The food itself is not good, but that McDonalds in general.  I never deviate from chicken nuggets and mainly a source for happy meals for kids.

We like Cantina, but we mostly go here for the happy hour.  If you like beer- get the Michelada-  I'm in LOVE with this drink.  The margaritas are tasty, though sometimes they are weak.  After killing a pitcher with a friend, I've often left wondering.... "was there any alcohol in that?"  I love the chips and salsa, salsa verde is the best!  But, if you want good Mexican that is A LOT cheaper- go to Veracruzana.

Context: Dinner with an Out-Of-Towner
Time of Visit: Monday, 8:00PM

So a friend visits from out of town and wants an eponymous cheesesteak sandwich: where do you take them?  Jim's, Geno's, Pat's, or other?

We decided on Pat's.  My friend was a little nervous about their ordering rules (wit or witout onions, second window for fries & drinks), which was exacerbated by the fact a class-trip sized group of school kids got off a bus after we got to the window.  I'm not afraid to admit it: I need more than 5 seconds to make sure I say my order correctly...sue me.

The staff at the counter, while not the most friendly people on the planet, were not as mean as some other yelpers have encountered in their visits.  My mushroom pepper steak with provolone was pretty good: it came out very hot, with a lot of steak.

If you're going to Pat's, you're going for the cheesesteak only; nothing else.  While I appreciate tradition and longevity as much as the next person, that doesn't mean you can lower your level of service (read: treat your customers poorly) and assume everyone will continue to flock to your establishment (excluding 8th graders on field-trips).

Everyone is raving how Philly has the best cheesesteaks. OVERRATED!!! Can't believe we walked from Center City East, the hotel, and tourist attractions to eat this. It was certainly a long walk for almost nothing. I think the walk was about 30-40 minutes from we were toured around Center City East. Definitely long lines and a lot of people, but for what. The cheesesteak was cold, bland. Taste nothing. I don't see the big deal about this place and people say its one of the best in Philly. Definitely would've had a better cheesesteak from a local place near our hotel. Actually I rather have a cheesesteak in New York where I live than eating one in Philly.

If you like Mexican/ Cuban food this is the place to go.  The food and drinks are great.  Brunch or dinner.  The price is worth every bite.  On Friday evening and the weekend it can be busy.  You may have to wait 20 -30 mins.  But it's with it.

Great pizza and awesome service! Came here with some friends during work and we all got custom pizzas. All of the employees call you by name, you get tons of options for toppings, and the prices were great. Plenty of seating on two floors and the friendliest people work here too. Shout out to Juan! Thanks!

You have to eat here!
The place that started it all. It will change the way you see any other Philly Steak Sandwich. 
Cash only.

I was the only person in line, and ordered two simple burritos. I have waited a long time and people who came in after me have already received their orders. This is ridiculous. It seems they focus way too hard on mobile orders they forget to serve their in-person customers

I ordered two salads from here and overall I thought they were decent, nothing out of the ordinary. If you're in the area and need to grab a quick lunch, then yeah go for it! But I wouldn't go out of my way to have lunch here. The portions are big and the salads are pretty filling!

Would've given 5 stars but i have to consider every aspect...been trying different philly cheesesteaks every visit to philly and its all about preference...i prefer cheddar so cheez wiz is my choice...the number 1 accdg to philly people is johns but they dont have cheddar so I'd still prefer pats...geno's is a grade below even though they say its the same...its only better for background in pictures because of the bright lights....1star less because they could improve on thevstore itself...dine in customers will still get their sandwich wrapped so somoe of the cheese will go to the wrapper...better to be eaten immediately so bread wont be soggy. Cash only and they try to make the lines fast...separate line for fries and drink which is good when you think of adding those while eating...its overpriced considering what you're getting but still worth when visiting

My first biting into Philly's Philly cheesesteak. I have not tried any of the other famous cheesesteaks in Philly. My review is just my experience at Pat's, not in comparison to the other eateries.

My my it was delicious!! The beef was hot and super tender. I got a mushroom pepper steak wit wiz. Mushrooms - good. Peppers - good. Soft hero bread - good. Cheez Wiz - makes everything that much better! No complaints! I left full and satisfied! I also tried to eat one of the peppers but holy crap, wayyy too spicy for me!

What is the big deal? I waited 15 minutes on line for an unflavored cheese steak. The fries were good. I think Steak-ums are better because I can put a little Worcestershire sauce and some adobo on it. I did enjoy the experience of it all though. That's whats it is all about., I guess.
Sandwich was delicious! But the parking was awful (NOT SURPRISED) fastest food I've ever gotten!

After Shoo Fry locations closed, I really wanted to find a spot in Philly with good poutine! My friend and I went to the Bourse to get a bunch of different food to split and were excited to see a spot with poutine. We ordered the medium-sized "Oh Canada." While there is a large option, we opted for the smaller one so we had room to try other things. $7 and change seemed like a good deal, but when the fries came out, the portion was tiny... maybe enough for a couple bites each. The taste was definitely good, but the portion size was disappointing. I won't come here hungry, but will come next time I have a poutine craving.

Who doesn't like a Mexican Cantina? Cantina Los Caballitos has great drinks, excellent outdoor sitting and a menu that can make vegans and carnivores happy.

For vegans or vegetarians, I'd recommend the vegan beef in a burrito. But don't go crazy with the burrito upgrades. I usually like my burrito enchilada style. At Los Caballitos, they put the enchilada sauce around the burrito instead of on top. Somehow, this doesn't take the burrito to the next level like it should. You can also top the burrito off with some vegan cheese. But sometimes more is less with a burrito. I nearly increased the price of my burrito by 100% with too many add-ons but only made it l ike 55% better. That's a poor return for any Mexican food...especially a burrito.
Of all the highly overrated cheesesteak spots in Philly that really only tourists go to, I would have to say Pat's is one of the better ones.
Pure tourist trap. It's serviceable and edible but extremely overrated. There are so many better, true Philly Cheesesteaks in the city.

ate here yesterday with some friends - great food! i had the salmon tacos. I cant even tell you how good they were. i am so happy i ordered them. all my friends got burritos. they all raved about how good they were. i also ordered the said of guacamole. very very good. they had a nice size drink list and it was really cute in side. cant wait to go back with my husband!

I had a cheesesteak with wiz and onions. It wasn't bad, but I have definitely had better. The guy that used his bare hands to touch my sandwich also used the same hands to grab a customer's cash. I still ate my sandwich, but I know from working in the food industry that this is a violation...

Don't except In N' Out.

This place is decent. Their PR must be great because, as Russ says, the hype around this place is crazy. It is a great burger joint if you want a step up from chain fast food.

Be sure to get the milkshake instead of Cola. And if you want a work lunch break excuse, go to the one in NJ.

Loved their cheesesteaks. So my husband and I did the challenge, although I have to admit I thought based on reviews Geno's would win, they surely lost miserably. I wouldn't recommend getting the "extra" cheese whiz from pats though, it makes eating very difficult. I would definitely make the drive over from NYC for their cheesesteaks again! ALSO THEY ONLY ACCEPT CASH!!!!
Took a $15 cab ride and ordered their famous cheese-steak which was just ok.  I truly have had better back home.  I believe this is more of the hype that anything else.
Good place for a chees steak. Liked it better than Genos across the street. Not the best we found on our quest but good

One of the reasons I wanted to come to Philly was for the cheese steaks. A couple of my friends recommended that I go to Pat's. I was really excited and hungry to go get one but the lines were long. I could understand long lines for such a place, same thing happens for Pink's in LA.

Finally got my cheese steak with onions and cheese whiz. Some people would say that the wait isn't worth it but this time it was. There have been other cheese steak places I have gone to on the west coast but they don't compare. When you go to Pat's you get an authentic Philadelphia Cheese steak. I could have gone for another cheesesteak but I didn't want to wait in the long ass line again.

One of the best experiences of my east coast trip. Definitely go to pat's when you're in Philly.
Yum.  Get the Cheez-wiz one.  They are ooooy and gooy and delightful.  Worth the ride from Cleveland Ohio to Philly!! lol
I ordered a cheese steak sandwich, WIT onions and provolone.  Bread wasn't soft all around, not enough meat, and not a lot of flavors. I think this place is over rated.

Great for any occasion! Breakfast lunch and dinner, they do catering and also can make your party a little more live by bringing the food truck!
Ask your Paisan if JEET? And take them here for a meal to remember, they put effort and authenticity in every meal

Yummy cheesesteak!  My husband and I decided to get one of each Pat's and Geno's to have the ultimate face off of who's Philly cheesesteak was better.  Well I loved Geno's fresh bread and my husband loved Pat's flavorful meat.  Both are good!  Miss it already! (Back in Cali)

Good god, this place the absolute best. I cannot get enough of their Whized ones.  Such a nice flavor that takes me back to my roots.

Every time I'm in town for business I pretty much only eat here. Love it.

The service here is horrible the staff is rude I went there 5/25/19 at approximately 7:15 p.m. I ordered asked one extra chili sauce I like my chili spicy I normally put Cajun powder in it the manager on duty at the time with that gel down ponytail was very rude and says something smart to the cashier after she flagged me when I ask for extra.

Odd and well hidden little spot, but what these folk dish out is very worth the trip. Twisted pretzels braids (they even make these into pizza if you want), regular soft pretzels, and multi flavored nuggets are pretty much all you can score here, but the product is great and price is cheap so, if you're a hustler, you could probably triple your money on the streets. 

I recently came in for nuggets, wanting a half plain and half everything medium sized tray ($15 for plain, $17 for flavored). The regular were forgotten, but the everything nuggets made up for it with their flavor and  the fact that they were fresh out of the oven (they will gladly cook you fresh dough if you give them a chance). Tray came with one small container each of cheese wiz and spicy mustard, but that is definitely not enough (especially the cheese), so plan accordingly.

Even though I didn't get exactly what I'd asked for, it was still a very pleasing purchase, but isn't that how back alley transactions are supposed to go down? Also, I'm not too surprised that I've never been here before during my life long Roxborough residency, what with it's hugger-mugger location, but I plan to make up for all that I've missed in the future.

The store front is in the corner of the warehouse within the parking lot behind the furniture warehouse at Umbria & Lemonte streets. Follow the signs and you'll be fine.

Going to Pat's was definitely experience. Grumpy employee who is probably sick of tourists not ordering the correct way, which was actually amusing after seeing someone struggle and then giving up on ordering. Cheesesteak was good, but not so much better than a cheesesteak you'd get outside of Philadelphia. Quality meat, but I'd like to rather pay in the $7 range, not $9.50. Did not try Geno's, but overheard people talking about how they thought Pat's was better.

you know how cereal tastes like cereal, milik tastes like milk, and cereal+milk tastes like cereal+milk?  Cheesesteaks here, wit or no wit, are like that.  They are the sum of their parts, and no more.  Some people out there will swear this place is heaven on earth.  Again, I miss another opportunity for Rapture.

Service was fast but expensive for not that great a sandwich,  honestly don't get the appeal of this place i ordered and in seconds had a sandwich,  no way that steak was fresh and wasn't great.  Will not be returning.

I'm mainly reviewing Pat's because I want to include it on a list. When faced with a decision between Pat's and Geno's, I immediately curl up in the fetal position and rock back and forth. I'm kidding, of course. I actually choose Geno's if forced to eat at one of them, but I prefer to avoid that conundrum altogether and get my sandwiches at George's a few blocks north.

meh.
my brother lives near the italian market in south philly.  I went for a visit.  Luckily for me my brother and his girlfriend are foodies.  I was able to taste many different cuisines in Philly.  Coming from San Francisco, there are places I don't go due to the tourist trap aura, due to the non-authenticity of it all (fisherman's wharf, chinatown etc).  But when I was in Philly I had to have a cheesesteak...and I had to go to the two most famous places, which of course are right across the street from one another,  in a big rivalry, and featured on the Food Netowrk!  How cheesy, but essential.  
We split two, both "wit whizt '?(cheese whiz)One from Geno's and one from Pat's.  
Pat's was much tastier than Geno's.  The meat was seasoned and the bun and cheese with much more flavor...
Better of the two...it seems.

Honestly, this is just a hype. It wasn't anything that I expected. It's nothing special. I am visiting and expected Pat's to be known for some good Philly cheese steak. I would recommend going somewhere else. This and Gino's is a tourist attraction, don't get fooled.

The Pat's vs Geno's cheesesteak debate is one that people love to talk about. Honestly, I thought that Pat's, Geno's, and Jim's cheesesteaks where all about equally as good, which is to say, I enjoyed them, but don't have a burning desire to return for more. 

The draw of Pat's is that it is the origin of the whole Philly cheesesteak phenomenon (although Geno's claims that they were the ones who started putting cheese on them). As other's have mentioned, Pat's is rather unassuming compared to Geno's across the street; this, when combined with Pat's historical signpost, lends an air of authenticity that some may find attractive. 

Like Geno's (and unlike Jim's) I didn't find the wait to be terrible here, but they do rush you through. The cheesesteaks and the drinks are a bit overpriced, which I suppose is to be expected for such a tourist draw. When I went here, the cashier tried to short change me $10. 

To be honest, I'd rate Pat's as just about the same as Geno's. I think it's worth going once, but it's not a place worth visiting with any degree of frequency.
Meh...I've been waiting a while to try Pat's. Sadly, I wasn't impressed. The onions were delicious and cheese was good, but the meat had no flavor and the bread was so so.

I was debating to give this a 2 or a 3 but guess i am feeling alittle happy right now so i just give them a 3 instead. Anyway I was trying both Geno and pat's right next to each other and from the look of it,. I knew i would going like pat's more. It look juicy and tender and the cheese whiz was awesome...ok ok anywhere they sell whiz then it pretty much taste the same. The line was alittle longer at pat's and I want up there and order 1 whiz /wit...it might be the other way around but i got thru ordering it correctly or at least want thru quick enough not to be send back at the end of the lines so i was a happy camper. I got a few picky pepper's and it tasted well with my sandwich. Overall I like pat''s alot better but it isn't the best cheesesteak that I ever tasted so i was disappointed enough where I didn't even want to go to Jim or Tony Luke because it is all hype for television such like Pink's hotdog in LA or Rosecoe Chic & waffle or NYC pizza are the best so I am not going listen to anymore what television say about food because they are just FULL of Sh$T!!!

So here's the thing about this place...it's touristy. So if you want to go to say you've been then go right ahead. That being said, parking is horrible (although we lucked out and got a pretty good spot), the sandwiches are a bit expensive ($9.50 each), and the sandwich itself was....well it was a traditional Philly cheesesteak but it certainly wasn't mind blowing or awesome or even great.
Would I go back? Probably not

Definitely a tourist spot, but when in Rome?

Did a side by side with Geno's and think they both had pros and cons at each establishment. Can't say I would come back based on the number of higher reviewed places in the area.

Parking is not available !
The steak they cut too thick !
Price is $10 @ sandwich  (little bite high ) !!
The sandwich bread is tough !
Well , most of the business came from tourism, how many customers will return !
Best cheesesteaks in Philly- way better than Genos!
way better the genos. i dont know what they do, but these steaks seem to be more full and taste better. love pats.

Whenever I want a real burger I come here. This is definitely the occasional indulgence otherwise ....

Great treat!

I had to!  Based on recommendations from multiple people, I decided to try Pat's rather than Ginos.  I got the classic cheese steak with mushrooms and onions and a soda.  
The sandwich was GOOD! The only thing I wish was it was a little more 'fresh' tasting... I went at a very slow time, no lines whatsoever.  I would recommend going at a busy time so you know the food is being made fresh.
It is cash only, so I had to be sure I had cash on me, which I usually don't!  
You order the food at a separate window than beverages... which was just odd and annoying to do two transactions. 
All in all, I would say it is a great stop if you are in the area! Love me a good Philly Cheese steak.

So this is the place... My fiancé brought a sandwich home from a work trip. She picked it up on her way to the airport. Even hours later, it was pretty good. 

Then a month or two ago, we flew in together and I had the chance to eat a fresh cheesesteak. It was by no means the best I've ever had, but it was meat, cheese, and bread. Hard to fuck that up. In other words, I enjoyed it. 

The signage out front was a bit intimidating. It was ordering instructions. They were uncomplicated, but it had a "hurry the fuck up" vibe to it. Also, when I ordered through the window, it seemed like they were a little rude. Not that I expected great customer service from an assembly line worker feeding faceless cattle, but I guess that adds to the authenticity... rudeness. I'm sure it's necessary when it's busy and there's a line down the street. It was pretty empty when we were there. 

The sandwich wasn't so much lovingly crafted as it was just scoop, plop, schluuuurp, wrap, and shove out the window. Part of the experience. 

Well, it was the same basic cheesesteak you could get anywhere. Nothing special about the meat or the bread. Same shit you can get any place. The cheese was wiz, so not even really cheese. It comes out of a can. Regardless, it's tasty. I would get another one. However, I don't think you need to travel all the way here from wherever you live to get "the best" or "most authentic" or whatever. There's probably a place near you with eats just as good.

Man.. the portion of Meat they give you was good.... the Bread was so good.. I would love to have that for Breakfast. I am a Fan of Cherry Soda. Although the line was long it sure moves fast. We got lucky on a parking spot but if it wasn't there.. it would have been tough.

This smoothie stall offers fresh juices on its menu and lists pineapple, orange, strawberry and apple as options. However, they will not allow yo you to order a pineapple juice under any circumstances. They insist that it must be mixed with other fruits despite the menu saying otherwise. Will not return.

When in Philadelphia a must try. The bread was fresh n chewy steak was very flavorful not rubbery at all and the wiz!!! Onions put it over the top..... I didnt get to try ginos but honestly dont care this cheesesteak was so good

Good. Nothing stellar, people talk it up but it's obviously more about tradition and the culture of it than the actual food. 

Make sure you check your order before walking away... they messed up 2 of our 3 sandwiches but when we went back to point it out the guy argued back that that's what we ordered (which was definitely not true).

Awesome cheeseburgers! AND Coke with Vanilla omg! AND the fries! Is this the best place in the world or what?! I dont usually eat beef but oh did I love the cheeseburger here! I am so glad my friends took me to this place, it is a heaven for foodies like me! Love it!

Definately breaks up the old school vibe of Passyunk Ave. 

This is the spot to drink margaritas outside and munch on some nachos. Personally, I'm not big on their food, but the drinks and drink specials are worth going! 

Great potential for people watching as well!
Yuk, yuk, yuk, yuk! Go to Delasssandros instead! Did not like Genos or Pats. OVERATED1

Don't wast your time and 11 bucks.  More hype than sandwich.  A little more meat than Geno next door but cheese pretty non existent and onions tasted prefab. Meat was also chewy.  Hold on ... don't waste your time at genos either.  Where's the beef?  Wow two lightweights.  No parking.  At $10 not gonna make me as happy as Jersey mikes or even wawa.

Came here for some Mexican and had the most amazing Lamb chorizo tacos in my entire life!

So I feel like I may have let the cat out of the bag a little early in what my favorite thing was but my mouth waters thinking about it. The tacos were recommended by the waiter, as they were one of the specials. Being that I love lamb and equate it to the taste of innocence's, I had to try them, and the Cantina delivered. The meat was perfectly spiced, and I mean perfectly. I can normally pick out something to improve on almost anything I experience and there was no room for improvement with these. 

Another plus was having Kona Walla wheat on tap. It's a Hawaiian beer that I haven't really found in the north since I had it down south maybe 3 years ago. Granted I think it's making its way up and I have even found it in some local stores, but having Walla wheat on tap was a big plus. 
Good prices, friendly staff, and great food. A formula for excellence.
Pats is a true Philadelphia landmark They use top grade beef it has the best atmosphere in the city they ship to anywhere is the USA
Best of the 2 most famous and definitely the original cheese steak. Next time I will probably go to both again. But Pats is the better of the 2.

The pizza isn't bad BUT the service is HORRIBLE. It is impossible to call the actual store when they mess up an order. We got 3 pizzas delivered to work and one of them had cheese when it was ordered without cheese due to dietary needs. We tried calling multiple times and can only speak to a call center. After asking for a refund I was put on hold for 10 minutes only to be disconnected. After calling several more times, we still haven't gotten a refund. We will not order from here anymore.

Eat here (goat burrito or mushroom quesodilla). Drink here (tecante, strawberry-guava mojito or frozen watermelon margarita). Buy your bartender a drink here (Jameson). Sit outside and smoke here (they sell smokes too). Bring your dog here (outside of course).  And mostly drink here. Toto bien.

Probably the best Chipotle I've been to in my area. For being the only chain that has a place in my heart, I haven't found a chipotle that doesn't have some sort of issue. This location is great. The staff is prompt and courteous, they listen to exactly what you want, and they're organized! Food is always stocked and warm. Gasp! I know it seems ridiculous to hear, but I have had some horrible experiences at other Chipotles. Other locations I've reviewed could really use some pointers from these guys! 

Only flaw is how tight of a space it is. I never sit down to eat there. Weird seating plan.

Came here all the way from CA excited to finally get a taste of the real Philly cheesesteak -- only to be DISAPPOINTED on so many levels. We ordered 3 Philly steaks but we weren't allowed to ask any questions. Customer service not only lacked to say the least but we were told you get what you get and if you don't like it don't come back and go to GENO's across the street. We didn't ask many questions but the 5 seconds we did take to ask since it was our first time they were RUDE!!! I have 2 guys refer to me as 'honey' - very demeaning! 

I got my Philly cheesesteak with what was supposed to be grilled onions (mind you the other two had grilled onions but mine did not and it was barely grilled and still white and crunchy. I asked them about it and that's when I was told 'you get what you get honey and if you don't like it, go somewhere else.' I've never been yelled at as a customer for asking questions but whoa this place thinks they're above it all...seriously??!!

Philly cheesesteak: everyone in our party was EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTED by how it tasted or the lack of. I've had much much much better ones in the past so I think they won't have many return customers thus the overall 3.5 rating of this place now, soon it'll be lower. 

GO SOMEPLACE ELSE -- AVOID THIS PLACE!!
Can't believe I paid 11 for a steak that probably cost them 2 to push out.  Then the fountain soda 3.50.  a worthless non nutritious meal for 14.5.  Never again from this overrated joint
The cheesesteaks are delicious! Very quick - one of the best in Philly. Only taking a star off because the guy working the window was an obnoxious asshole :-)

Okay, this is a touristy thing to do, so I guess you have to try it if you visit Philadelphia. I honestly thought the streetcart cheesesteaks smelled better but you have to try this place. It wasn't bad...I guess the cheese whiz made me a little sick and my cholesterol didn't like it too much. But please try it if you're a tourist.

They have instructions on how to PROPERLY order a Philly cheesesteak!

I much prefer putting the steak and onions over rice but I guess one would call that Yoshinoya...
Burger was okay but customer service was bad. I waited reallllly long for a simple cheeseburger

Super disappointed!!  Always heard that we had to have a cheesesteak in philly and this was the place to go.  1st they dont take cash and then the food was just way too bland.  Nothing special but atleast i got to mark it off the bucketlist.
Soft juicy meat, nice chewy bread, gooey whiz cheese, what else can I say? Don't make a mis-steak! Pat's is the way to go!!

I was kind of disappointed with the food and service after so much hype from watching them on Food's network & Travel Chanel. For $9.50 for a cheese steak with mushroom, there were no mushroom and the bread was stale! Plus the cashier was so ghetto, they treated the customers like we should be grateful for their food. This probably will be the last time I eat here
100% the best cheesesteak place around ! I'm from NY and contemplated bringing some back!
I like this place a lot.  Great food and great drinks with good prices.   My go to dish is the pork carnitas burrito.  And it's kid friendly if you are so inclined to venture out with the family.

I was told by friends to check out Chick-fil-A when I had the chance. The chance came and I ordered the chicken sandwich with waffle fries and unsweetened iced tea. The meal was nothing to write home about but the staff were friendly. I'll need to come back and try other menu items.

I lived in Philly for two years and had to move for personal reasons. when I fly back this is the first place I go to. I love the pretzels, and they are very cheap. and if whoever opens the door likes you, they will give you extra ;)

Boo!!! If this restaurant was a show and I was a reviewer like Rotten Tomato then I would give it a -1%.  First of all, the service was poor. Only one cashier during a late lunch rush at 1:29PM. place is clean and bright . Parking lot is ok . Food are fresh and delicious. Miso soup always perfect! Owner is very friendly!

I've been coming to Pat's ever since I was little.  It has always and will continue to hold a special place in my heart.  More often when I return, I don't go for the food, but for the sentimental value I have attached to this world-famous South Philly cheesesteak stand.  In the battle of Pat's versus Geno's, I'm definitely Team Pat's.  But while Pat's dominates the local neighborhood, there are much better (and far less crowded) cheesesteak stands in Philadelphia.

By all means, if you have friends coming in from out of town and they want to get a cheesesteak, Pat's should be your go-to.  After you wait in line for what seems like forever, the steak comes out fast and dripping in velvety cheez whiz and grease.  Don't even think about ordering it without onions, and for extra cheesesteak deliciousness, ask to remove the insides of the soft-yet-sturdy Amoroso roll ("guts out" in linespeak).  Next, get in the other line and grab yourself a red cherry soda (and fries if you must, though certainly not required), help yourself to some ketchup for your steak and some hot peppers and find a table.  Begin by eating the peppers whole to put some heat in your mouth, then sink your teeth into a time-honored tradition.  The meat is incredibly tender and the cheese acts both as a complement and a sauce to hold the sandwich together and accentuate the flavors.  Nevermind that it is mustard yellow and doesn't resemble a food product: this is far and away the best kind of cheese to put in your steak.

But there are many other great cheesesteak places outside the Pat's and Geno's sphere that demand your attention and put Pat's to shame.  You can find them at Reading Terminal Market, in Roxborough, farther down in South Philly, and even in West Philly.  Furthermore, unless you know how to order the right way or know what you want before getting in line, do not attempt ordering at the window.  Pat's is the quintessential Philadelphia Cheesesteak experience, but it is definitely not the best.  While it is arguably the standard by which cheesesteaks in this city are judged, there are many options that exceed the quality and flavor that Pat's serves.  Nevertheless, Pat's is consistent.  And consistency is good.

I'll never go back to this location after today.

Over-charged my Credit Card

Failed to give me a receipt for an order
Acted incredibly rude when interacting with customers
Been SUPER slow when putting orders together

Gave my a COLD coffee

Gino's hands down!!!

Still...folks, both these are the equivalent to seven 11 hot dogs!!!

Love the Chopped Steak... That is exactly why I like Pats better then Genos!

Whiz With! That is how it is suppose to be! Great sub... In a hectic part of the city, but if you have patience it is well worth the parking and line nightmares that it can have! 

CASH ONLY!!!!

Stop being a wuss, and reading endless reviews about whether Pat's or "the other place" is better.  Order one from each.  You know you want to.  Eat both cheesesteaks back-to-back, and decide for yourself.  MAN UP.

Sincerely,
K. W.

Fresh cut fries from real potatoes, not those frozen ones from a bag. Spent $20 for lunch for 2 people. The small fries was enough to share. Will definitely stop again when in the area. Would recommend for an affordable good tasting burger.

And I have to say I am glad that we've come a long way. I would not say it is the worst but it is down there. There is hardly any steak, it is in a ghetto, takes only cash. The other one we ordered, the fish steak, really cant find worse one, ended up mostly in the trash. People are rude too, maybe they figure customers like it to be yelled at, ghetto like experience.

I still treasure the experience, but as food, nah.
Pat's is the real deal. Ordering is fun and the workers give you a window into the language of the locals. Food is exactly what the Philly cheesesteak is all about.

25 years in Philadelphia.  Number of cheesesteaks consumed: countless.  Pat's rank?  Near the bottom.

Poor roll, bad meat, generally poor service, long lines, small portions, high prices.  The calling cards of a tourist trap.  They know they'll get the business so they put out a crap product.  

If you've never been, I guess go.  You'll likely not want to go back.  Try a truck for a better cheesesteak at a lower price.

3 1/2 stars.  

Every single one of my friends has raved on and on about this place and hyped it up so much that I thought there was something wrong with me for not ever coming here.  So, I finally gave in and paid them a visit.

It wasn't a bad experience, but I don't know if I'd come back.  It was just okay.  I've had much better Mexican food at much cheaper prices (El Jarocho).  And hell, La Calaca Feliz is like double the prices here and I would still rather that than this. Unfortunately, we also ordered the guacamole appetizer and it never came out. My margarita with Grand Marnier was delicious and a good balance of sweet/sour, but I could hardly taste the alcohol.  For a place that boasts about their margaritas, I was hoping for something with a little more kick.  Maybe I have to get the pitcher to get the full margarita experience.

There were a ton of flies swarming us, so maybe that's why they kept it closed.

Dirty, old food, DIRTY!! Management with cussing in front of customers, no one was wearing a hair net! Food all on the floor in the back! Bathroom was like the subway bathroom, was making any special drinks, Did I say DIRTY!!!

Pat's King of Steaks was a place that I had no real plans to pay a visit, but we found ourselves in the area and decided to give both Pat's AND Geno's a shot, trying and splitting a Philly from each location.  We began our adventure at Pat's.  

You can find Pat's off of Wharton street, and literally a stone's throw away across the street is Geno's, so these guys are competitors in the truest sense of the word. It also makes it easy to sample both at the same time if you desire (we did). 

From the moment you stand in line, there's a series of steps on how to order a steak (i.e. learn to use "wit" a lot).  We did decide on getting their Cheese steak ($11).  Pat's does have some optional toppings you can add opposite their store front which are all on the house.  

The Philly meat comes chopped and in terms of flavors, I preferred Pat's over Geno's.  Their meat was packing a little more flavor to me than Geno's, and if I had to pick between the two, i'd go to Pat's first. The sandwich is served whole, so if you want to share with someone, you'll have to tear it in half (staff would not cut the sandwich for us).

Flavor, ironically is the only win that Pat's has over Geno's, which some would argue is all they need...flavor.   Geno's has it all over Pat's in terms of price, cleanliness, customer service (they happily cut our sandwiches), but flavor is all Pat's .

So, in the war between Pat's or Geno's, I wouldn't travel to Philly to experience either of these two popular tourist spots. Truth be told, there are much more tasty sandwiches in other parts of Philly, but if you find yourself in the area, you probably will get a little more flavor squeezed out of Pat's.  But don't take my word on it.  

Give these guys a try if you're close and willing!  

P.S. cash only!

Took the challenge, and I had a philly at both Pat's and Geno's. The one thing I liked better about Pat's was there were more sandwich options, as in there there were multiple "add ons" you could order for your sandwich, such as the mushroom cheesesteak, pizza cheesesteak or other options like the hot dog. Also I prefer diet Pepsi over diet Coke, so I was happy to see Pat's served Pepsi. Overall quality sandwich, but if I was in the area again I would choose Geno's over Pat's.

I recently purchased Chick-fil-A gift cards. But, as I am standing in line to order from a Chick-fil-A in the Phildelphia airport, terminal C. My wife and I make an order only to be told our gift cards were no good.  What is the point in buying these, if we cant use them at every location. Horrible business if you ask me...
Bryan

Let me start by saying, that I can only describe our experience. Feel free to make your own judgements. Went here yesterday and our experience was terrible. We found that it was pure hype, rude cooks and staff, and in our opinion, the food was "bland" at best. In our experience, they were as impatient as I've ever seen at any establishment. Went to Geno's last time. At least we were treated like people. I'll NEVER darken the window of the place ever again! If you're thinking about going to this place, think twice about how you wish to be treated.
AWWWWWFUL.....this place thrives on the hype. this isnt even good enough to be dog food. do your self a favor and go to steves prince of steaks and get a chicken philly and a pizza roll.
It made both me and my fiance sick last night.  I got the vegetarian sofritos bowl and he got the chicken bowl.

While the prices are not inflated the portions are large, a few things feel off at this Chipotle. My pico de gallo is basically just chopped tomatoes and the beloved corn salsa is, well, just corn with a few flecks of cilantro. The staff was nice, but the food is certainly subpar, and I keep chewing on something crunchy--overcooked rice?
Pizzas decent & always hot and ready, great customer service always friendly, almost never a long wait, clean facility.

Blaze Pizza is truly iconic. An unlimited-topping pizza for $8.75? ICONIC! Thank you to Dan and the other employees (sorry, wish I'd caught their names!) for elevating the experience by providing excellent customer service with their friendliness and efficiency. Always get the roasted garlic.

Horrible service again! I only go here for quick lady minute meals. The service was slow. The poor girl working the register had no help while the other girls talked by the fry counter! I ordered 6 piece nugget and more than half of them were still sorta frozen ! Smh. They need a new manager during evenings because the young girl they have isn't doing a good job. This is my 2nd review with bad news smh
Lower quality then Mcdonald's standards.  Dirty, sticky, poor service.  Its always a creepy experience shopping here.

Being from San Diego, CA, I have high standards for Mexican cuisine.  Let me cut to the chase: Cantina Los Caballitos easily met these standards and has officially become my favorite Mexican restaurant in Philly.  I ordered the pork carnitas burrito with an add-on of guacamole (a great decision as their guac is fantastic).  The ingredients inside blended beautifully together, with the highlight being the wonderfully cooked and seasoned pork.  For $10 the size of of the burrito was on point.  I'm a big fan of margaritas so I opted for the El Dorado (tequila, Grand Marnier, pineapple and lime juice).  It was absolutely delicious, the perfect beverage on a warm spring day, and absolutely worth the $6.50/glass.  My experience was enhanced by the awesome decor and hip vibe of the establishment and the outside seating area is THE place to be on a nice day in Philly.  I am so glad Cantina Los Caballitos exists, as it will help me combat homesickness while I live in Philly.

How is this place still open??!? The service is soooooo slow. The ice cream machine was broken for about 2
Months. You mobile order and park, but they never bring out your food.. it just sits on the counter. Numerous times I have called and complained. I'm always offered a replacement meal, but I never follow through.. since I order everything through the app. I have a small child on oxygen 24/7 so it's pain in the butt to get him in and out of the car. Since this place doesn't have a drive thru, curbside pick up is the way to go, unless you go to this McDonalds.

Visiting Philadelphia for the first time, I knew I couldn't leave without having a cheese steak. So of course I had to pay a visit to two of the most famous spots in the city, Pat's and Geno's.

I came right over to this spot across the street after trying Geno's. I ordered the steak with whiz and onions. The service was fast, as my sandwich was literally out as I was paying the cashier. The moment I sat down and opened the sandwich, I knew this was what a Philly Cheese Steak should look like. The sandwich was HOT and came loaded with cheese. The meat was chopped up instead of sliced thin and with plenty of onions. 

I took a bite and was instantly hit with the taste of cheese, onions, and meat. I knew from that moment Pat's was my winner between the two. To me, Pat's felt more like a real cheese steak compared to Geno's. 

Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Pat's. I liked the fast service and their sandwich was better in my opinion. Pat's doesn't look as clean and new as Geno's, but I think it adds to the authenticity of the place. You come for the food, not for a lavish dining room seating. I would recommend this spot especially for those visiting Philadelphia for the first time.

Used to be my favorite spot in south philly but my friends and I are changing our opinions... I have to say I am disappointed.. service is slow.. portions are small, honestly I think it changed hands! Had to flag down the waiter all night! Needs much improvement!

Not sure why this place only has 3.5 stars but hopefully this review helps that. 

This place is great. The food (especially at brunch) is amazing.  The margaritas are always flavorful and made with fresh ingredients- not to mention cheap (way cheaper than uptown places!). The outdoor seating is fun for dog watching (the residents of east passyunk have the cutest puppies!) and it's always nice to get some fresh air.

This is a great place to go to after work to get drinks for happy hour and to sit outside on a nice day, but that's it.  Their food is not good, and I have experienced this on more then one occasion.  The server I had last time I went was just the rudest most pretentious individual i have ever encountered.  I could get much better mexican food for far less money.
It was fine but I have had about the same at a diner in Brooklyn. Go to say you did it but don't expect to be wowed
The original is still the best. Nobody beats Pats. From the atmosphere to the delicious taste, these guys do steaks right. Whiz wit please.

Ordered delivery from here yesterday on the Eat24 app off of the recommendation of a friend. The food arrived pretty quick. Driver called when he was outside like I had asked, some don't and I don't get that. 

Got 10 piece boneless wings in a spicy bbq sauce and an order of curly cheese fries. The wings were good, a little spicier than I expected but still really good. Fries were just okay. A little soggy. If I ordered them again I would probably get the cheese on the side. 

No real complaints though. Will definitely order again!

Yeah this place is just all right. For a quick bite it's ideal and between Pat's and Genos I did enjoy Pat's more but that being said it's certainly not the best cheese steak. Each were a little lighter on the steak than I would have hoped. As a tourist in Philly I get the appeal but wouldn't say "you have to go".

This will likely not be an overly popular opinion... Oh well... This place serves up some SERIOUSLY over priced shit. With a side of major attitude. Wow. 

Having gotten that off my chest- I understand it's famous and all and sure it's a Philadelphia land mark of sorts, a place to go and say you went, you saw, you partook, etc. But for me it really ends there. 

The cheesesteak (wit & cheez wiz) was decent, the meat is good quality at least and that's really the best thing it has going for it. It was not so much as even luke warm. My Husbands roast pork sub was decent, but meh, as well. I'm not really going to waste time on going much more in depth than that. Expect to pay a minimum of $50 for 3 people to eat a sub, small side of fries and a medium fountain drink. It would be worth while if it were packed to the brim and mind blowing, however it's far from. All hype for me.

I'm not going to write a proper review for a franchise place.  You all know what Subway offers.

I just wanted to comment on this particular location.  

If you work close to here, this is a nice little spot to get out of the office for a little bit.  They have lounge style seating, and are rarely ever crowded.  It has a very comfortable and relaxed atmosphere.  So if you don't feel like walking far, don't want to the surf the crowd at Reading Terminal, or just need to unwind, this place has your number..  

Its a great place to take a long lunch, play on your phone, or even work away from the office for a bit. Definitely pick this spot over the other Subway on Market St.

They also have self serve / free refills on drinks, which a lot of center city spots don't.
