The "4 stars" is of course comparing it to other fast food places, not saying its a 4* restaurant.

You come to Pat's for the experience.  The long, somewhat disorganized line, the apprehension of the order as you approach the window, and the gruff service you get before taking your first bite are part of this tradition.  You meet a few people in line, stare at the ridiculous, over the top light show that is Geno's across the street, and wonder if waiting in the cold is worth your time.

This review is for the food, and it's just a pretty good sandwich.  I think the bun is a little dry here, they don't put enough cheese or onions on it, and it's overpriced.  There's better within a mile radius and not nearly as long a line.

3.5 stars**

Cheesesteaks with cheese whiz was much better and flavorful than Geno's. Bread was not chewy. Overall, the cheesesteaks were average.

According to the Food Network, Philly Cheese Steaks divide the town between Geno's and Pat's. They're right across the street from each other, so I brought an empty stomach. I felt both had their pros and cons but Geno's had an overall better flavor. They're much flashier which made me not want to choose them, but they won. By no means did I feel they were the best I've ever had though. They're definitely a tourist trap! Pat's barely lost between the 2.

I am granting an extra star here for sheer nostalgia, but this place is solidly three stars from an objective standpoint. I can't believe I've never reviewed Cantina! Back when I was a fresh young ingenue in the city, Cantina was my first regular foray to the Avenue, and proper South Philly. It was the summer of 2008, and there wasn't much down on the Avenue in those days. I remember it always felt like it took forever to walk there, and that we passed little of interest. Now, the entire length from Broad/Snyder all the way up to the Italian Market is bustling at every hour of the night and day. It's insane how much this street has changed.

Anywho... I stopped coming to Cantina regularly a few years ago when it seemed the pitchers of margaritas were getting ever weaker, and the always-crappy service ever more terrible. Their food had never been anything to write home about in my book (what is with the plain white rice, guys? I don't get it) but the chips and salsa are always decent and the goat burrito is pretty darn tasty. I was showing a few out-of-town friends around the area when we wanted some lunch with drinks, which was slim pickin's on a post-Thanksgiving Saturday, but Cantina was open so there we went.

My guests were delighted, and I was pleasantly lulled by the warm glow of nostalgia. It's been at least two years since I've been, and the goat burrito tasted exactly the same. So did the plain white rice. WTF, people? All the cheese was at the bottom of my burrito, to the extent I thought they had forgotten it for most of my eating experience. I guess if I had started at the other end, it wouldn't have been at the bottom. In any event, I ate the whole thing and was pretty ashamed about it. Guests also ordered burritos, a goat and a breakfast with chorizo, and there was much contentment. I got a special margarita with guava and cointreau in it. It was tasty and plenty strong.

That habanero hot sauce on the table is spicy, be careful. But it's also damn delicious. Our server appeared to be high on copious amount of cocaine and/or meth. It was kind of entertaining. Ah, Cantina. You haven't changed much.

Bad attitude of the cashier !! It was our first time in the establishment so my wife really didn't know how to order for instance what kind of cheese or toppings . And the cashier was rushing her and mocking her and told her she doesn't speak English. She got really she wanted to speak to the manager but I told her it's ok because we're not from around the area we will not go back there next stop Geno's

It's way better than McDonald's, up there with Burger King, not quite Wendy's and doesn't hold a candle to In N Out. 

I give 5 Guys an extra star because they have 'Little Cheeseburgers.' I don't have much of an appetite and hate to waste food, so this is the perfect size for me. However, the whole props for logical proportions goes out the window if you get fries and a soda - the "small" ain't so small, unless you happen to be a giant.

I was also stunned by their choice of music. During my lunch I was treated to songs by such classic rock faves as Chicago and Toto. Maybe this was their way of making sure customers weren't lingering too long?
Waiting nearly an hr still got order wrong , another 30 something minutes for correct items.
Really fast service! Affordable prices! Delicious cheesesteak! What more can you ask for! :) I will recommend to others that are visiting philly.

I can't say I ever chewed on leather before but I imagine it would be similar to what Pat's Steaks uses for their meat. I can't give them 1 star because that is what I would give Geno's, their neighbor. My vote would be for either Jim's or Steve's.
If you're looking to get in your sodium for the week this is your place! Besides that the regular Philly is solid. Second favorite is the pizza and cheese fries.

I'm not sure what the big deal to this place is.  The cheese seem artificial to me and the steak had absolutely no flavor. The price for all this taste is outrageous ! I happen to be visiting PA and had to give it try well glad I'm crossing this one off my list for good

This place takes the cake for serving the leatheriest cheesesteaks on the planet. 

For over $9 with tax, you can practically get a better cheesesteak anywhere else, including at a shoe store.  

Ketchup does nothing to mask the flavorlessness. 

I ate here about five years ago and developed a strong aversion toward cheesesteaks that I still can't forget.

It's sad to know that so many unknowing tourists come here and subject themselves to the torture of waiting in long lines, paying high prices, followed by eating leathery and flavorless matter.
Make sure you get whiz. If you order your cheesesteak with provolone, you'll regret it.

I've been eating at Pat's for about 15 years now. 

There are a lot of people writing reviews about Pats that make solid points.  I won't go into another detailed review. But I will point out the things I have read from other reviews that are true and false in my opinion.

True: 
-You can get a "better" cheesteak somewhere else. Just research on yelp. 
-Pat's is STILL a good place to eat despite getting a "better" steak somewhere else. 
-The steak line will be long, but moves fast. Fries and soda line never long. 
-Pat's is better than Genos. 
-Parking is not always available right up front you tourists, not everyplace can be like your beloved Applebees. This is South Philly, not Orlando. 
-They have never won any customer service awards. So stop reviewing their "service." They hand you a freaking steak and you hand them money. Don't be stupid. 
-Yes, you need to know what you want before you get up there. It's not like you were not informed about this requirement. 
-Yes their cheese fries are spectacular

False:
-whoever says that locals don't go here and only tourists do, doesn't actually know any locals. Locals still go to both Pat's and Geno's. 
-if you are from California, and say that these steaks are expensive, go fist yourself. I've never eaten a meal under $30 in that entire state.  
-regardless of your dining expectations, these guys are not here to coddle your balls. act accordingly and simply eat your steak. 
-the staff, is actually quite pleasant if you are not a dipshit. 
-Pat's or Geno's do not have terrible sandwiches. 
-this is not fine dining. and 3 stars means exactly that: A-ok
-pats is never dirty
-you did not eat a better cheesteak in California. Tofu steaks are not cheesteaks. 



Bottom line is this is a good place to go.  So try it out for the atmosphere,  with a group of friends. And then yelp a better cheesesteak if you are still hungry.

We did the Geno's vs Pat's challenge. We ordered the exact same style sandwich "wit" (cheese whiz, mushrooms, onions) at both locations then cut them in half and shared. Pat's had more cheese and meat, but their cheese was way more concentrated. Geno's flavor was more prominent for the sandwich. The cheese was also not as thick and more enjoyable. However, the steak at Geno's was watery. 

Overall, both locations are quite similar and great choices. We would have to say we liked Geno's more. 

If you want a cheesesteak away from the tourist traps then go to Cleaver's. Their sandwiches are almost twice the size and fully loaded. There are many more places still to try! Every time we come to Philly we will try somewhere new.

I want to like this place; it's in a great location, lovely outdoor patio, interesting tequila/drink menu.  However, the food and service are usually a disappointment.  Food has always seemed a little off- sometimes texture, seasoning, quality or done-ness of the proteins.  Waitstaff are friendly, but often seem underinformed (ex. on the specials) or rushed.  I suppose it'd still be a good spot for a couple drinks with friends.
It's now 2016 and this place is still my favorite.

If you are looking for a great cheesesteak, this is a guaranteed hit. The roll is perfect, the steak, onions and cheese blend together just right, and adding your favorite condiments to cap it off? Never fails! There are plenty of other places that have good steaks too, but Pat's is an experience that you'll remember with a smile....and you'll be ready to do it again!
Overpriced, greasy, fatty cheesesteaks with homeless people around. So over rated!  Would not recommend at all.

TOTALLY overrated - both Pat's and Geno's. Sad. 
It's a touristy thing these days, not so much for a great cheesesteak wit or wit-out.
It's marketed well for their sake, but that's not much of a benefit to their customers.
When I was a teenager, Pat's was so worth it, we'd hop the El at Margaret and Orthodox, then take a bus, and then still walk 4 blocks just to get there.
They used to be Rock Stars.
I miss what it once was.

I just want to start off by saying that I have been here before & the food/drinks are pretty good, but tonight was unacceptable. I was told there would be a wait time of 45 minutes for a table if 3, which is fine, but I waited for about and hour and a half and still was not seated. The restaurant, which states that they don't take reservations online, started taking them...and prioritizing them over me and many others who have been waiting (in the cold I might add). The food is good, but I'm sorry it is NOT that good. I will never return.

Their meat comes frozen, then they boil it before they throw it on the griddle.  It's the real thing.

One time when I was eighteen, my friend and I came back to pat's from show n' tell butt-faced drunkypants and we made friends with a drunk guy in a wheelchair who we convinced that we would drive him home.  He agreed, but we could tell he got scared of us and just picked any old place to let him out.  I bet he thought we were in for a night of the good ole' ultraviolence.
Some people like the fat and tendon on their cheese steaks.  I don't.  There are so many other places to get a good cheese steak.
Great place for pizza.. workers are superb friendly and awesome.. I would definitely recommend here, if you like pizza.. less crust and more topping, wood fried what not.. great place ..

I have a love/hate relationship with the Cantina. I've never had a bad experience there (except for that 90% of the time the music is turned up waaaaay too loud), and I've had any number of great lunches and brunches spent with friends there, but there's just something about frequenting the Cantina that feels...wrong. Maybe because of the retardedly high number of hipsters who work/frequent the place? Maybe because I know I can get way more authentic food at way cheaper prices any number of places within a two block radius? I don't know. The food is good, and the sous chef is the most awesome dude ever. It's a bit pricey. Half the staff rocks, the other half is kinda lame. The bloody marys are a great hangover cure. I love love love the green salsa. I'm torn. But I know I'll be back.

Great Cheesesteak. Went here oh about 4 years ago and just now reviewing. We drove up here from DC whilst on vacation, grabbed a steak sandwich and headed out to the ballpark to watch the Phillies play. I did notice the so-called competition across the way but Pats had the longer line. Parking for me wasnt easy, 1st  time in Philly, its a wonder our rental car wasnt towed. So if your ever way out of town, stop by, they make a great cheesesteak. I hope to go back someday.

We came at a busy time so maybe some of this is situational.... We asked at least two waiters for more chips for the table before having to ask again until we got them. My order for my burrito was wrong but I didn't want to send it back because I was starving and we had already waited a good amount of time, it was still delicious, though. I had the veggie burrito with the vegan veggies, flavor was good. Friends were all happy with their meals and the margaritas were great, too. I want to come back again and try something else since their menu is very veggie friendly!

More of a 3.5 and better than Geno's.

Maybe I just don't get the hype about cheesesteaks because I thought this place was just alright. I guess I fell into the tourist trap of trying Pat's and Geno's and I must say, it's nothing too great to rave about. I thought the meat was thin and lean, which is good. But the bread felt like it was just meant there to hold the meat and whiz. I guess since I live in Philly now, I gotta try the more local joints and hopefully, it'll change my mind about cheesesteaks :)

sentimentality aside, being first does not always mean you are the best.  

had a couple of hours to devote to a wiz wit taste test: pat's, geno's, and jim's.

pat's was the lowest quality overall.  not enough meat and what was there was fatty and hard to chew.  as if to hide it - drowned in wiz.  

in fairness, i have had pat's before (years ago) and was more impressed then.  perhaps a bad day?  or they've gone downhill.

In the debate between Pat's vs Geno's, Pat's wins hands down. There is no debate.

The beef at Pat's is sliced thinner and more chopped up, the meat is much juicier, and they offer a larger variety of options on the menu such as with mushrooms, peppers, or mushroom pepper etc. 

The cheesesteak was tasty, I had it with onions and Cheez Wiz. I'm happy I was able to experience cheesesteak here for myself.
Worst service, and my hamburger was like it was right of the fridge and the buns were stale...wouldn't advise anyone to go here

Good.
It was pretty good. 
I came to eat famous cheesesteaks and it was better than I thought
But service is dry. Don't expect smiles
But if you want a tasty sandwich, that's exactly what you will get

A long time Delaware Valley resident, I went to Pats for the first time.  I can't say I was disappointed as it was a good steak.  Good but not quite great.  The meat was slightly dry.  There was abundant cheese, but the meat was a little lacking compared to some of the local shops in Blue Bell.  Fries are delicious and deadly.  Service was quick and friendly.

It I could give a minus star I would. I've been here several times and EACH AND EVERY TIME it's a fiasco. Why why why is it so difficult to get a couple of chicken order right? I get to work and my bosses 2 breast  chicken with beans a one breast with a drumstick. Forget about service with a smile.  I love Popeyes but this one is one of the worst.

Always liked this place until now.  We had a party of 4 celebrating a birthday.  The outside courtyard had 4 tables in the shade so we asked if we can take one of the tables.  A young lady was not thrilled but said go ahead.  We proceeded to sit when another hostess came over and asked us to move out into the sun.  She was so rude that we decided to leave instead.
We went across the street and sat in the shade at bang bang dim sum.
The dim sum was awesome!  We sat and conversed for 45minutes.  In the meantime. 2 of the 4 tables were never seated.  I went back and spoke to Anthony the manager,  he was apologetic and gave me his business card.
We ended up walking towards Barcelona where we stopped and had amazing Sangria and additional tapas.  In an area that has so much competition it doesn't pay to be rude to patrons of your establishment.  Sorry los Caballitos  you lost my business.

I keep going back and forth on how to rate this place. While I'm vegan, my boyfriend is not, so we're always looking for new places that'll make us both happy. I'd heard good things about their vegan options and my boyfriend is easier to please, so we decided to go.

We got there and waited a slightly uncomfortable amount of time before someone was about to seat us. We were then given complimentary chips with two kinds of salsas. I'm happy to announce that Cantina Los Caballitos has achieved the impossible by nailing the perfect chip to salsa ratio. 

We began looking at the menu and were happy to see that the prices were incredibly reasonable. My boyfriend pointed out on a sheet of paper (specials?) that the mimosa was $5! He decided to get one and the waiter asked him if he wanted to make that a Cantina Mimosa. My boyfriend asked what that was and the waiter explained that they just replace the orange juice with a different kind of juice of your choosing. My boyfriend went with the waiter's suggestion and got a passionfruit mimosa. We found out when the bill came that the Cantina Mimosa was $9. The waiter really should have warned us.

Food-wise, I ordered the Vegan Plate. The flavors were absolutely incredible although the portion size was smaller than I was expecting. I did leave full, but I guess I'm just used to more from Mexican restaurants. My boyfriend got the Breakfast Burrito and he was happy with it, but to be honest, I think he would've been just as happy with a burrito from Chipotle. 

I will probably go again, but I wouldn't necessarily recommend this Mexican restaurant over another in the city. It was good, but not great.
It's mediocre but the best thing about his place is that if it's 5am and you don't mind the drive you are sure to be fed.

I've never seen so many one and two star reviews for a place I consider to be a treat every time I go.

I stopped most recently a few weeks ago after landing at PHL around 10PM on an empty stomach.  And holy shit, did this hit the spot.  My girlfriend and I just sat at one of those benches shaking our heads at each other about how tasty our sandwiches were.

Don't worry about these reviews saying "ooh the meats a little fatty" or "I never liked cheese whiz" or "why do they have to be mean to me just because I can't decide what to eat."  Everyone should try this for themselves to form their own opinion.

For fast pizza, twas a lovely experience. Was slightly more than three minutes, but a vegan pie, with lots of cheese and an alright price was worth it. I've had &pizza before, and they compare in many ways, but I like the proportions here better. It's all covered in cheese, the crust is small, and there are more options for the finishes (pesto, oil, balsamic vinegar etc). 

Place has two floors, pretty huge. Came in and immediately was able to order, and the no-bars on toppings was dope. Might have to try the salads as well, but I think this is now my favorite last-minute pizza option in my hood.

Update: My next time here wasn't so swell. Pizza was very burnt, with the "roasted" garlic actually burnt as well, extremely bitter overall. I walked my pizza home, so I didn't get a chance to ask to see what they could do. I wonder if they would've made me a new pizza.

Pat's is more a place to go for the experience than for the steak. You wait in a long line, enjoy the ambiance (or not) while you gawk at those standing in line at the quasi-racist Geno's (where they serve slightly less tasty cheesesteaks), and for your effort, you are rewarded with a solidly good cheesesteak. 

This is all to say, the steak is good, but not the best; if you're going to be in Philadelphia for a while, you'd be remiss for not making it here (when you have free time). 

(Why is it not the best? Ishkabibble's serves a bigger and meatier steak.)
Came in and grabbed a pre packed California roll for $5.35 with tax. One of the best I've ever had, hands down! Tasted freshly made, packed expertly. Will come back for sure.

Simply awful. Honestly, some of these so-called "dives" are absolutely gross and disgusting. The Philly cheesesteak sandwiches were tasteless, soggy, and lacking in every way possible. I appreciate a good hearty sandwich as much as the next guy, and I understand that splurging with grease and meat can be the objective, but here, this place has a reputation built on folks simply regurgitating a myth.  Stay away, honestly.

Note:  This is part 1 of a 4 part series of an unhealthy weekend cheesesteak tour.

BAH!  How is this famous?  It's bad enough that I couldn't chew this steak-ems/rubber band shreds wannabe.  Then comes the hygienic factor.  After getting the sandwich, the guy wipes his nose precariously close to his hand.  As I looked in disbelief, my friend rightly points out that I shouldn't expect too much from a cheesesteak establishment, in fact, it probably adds to the flavor.  Tragically, I went along with his reasoning.  After two overly chewy bites, I called it quits and chucked the sandwich.  Then I was off to Geno's.
The food is great the service is fast, the location was fairly close to me just a bus ride away. That's worth taking the trip for, also the prices are not bad either.

Know how to order, go during the hours that aren't as busy. Order more than one.

Necessary rules for Pat's experience. And it's not just a sandwich, it's an experience. They're not always gushing with customer service they're just perfect at making a cheesesteak, so enjoy it. 

Forget about the place across the street. It's all about the King of Steaks, wiz wit! But seriously it's damn good. Just follow those rules and your experience will be 5-star one)

Ate at the new Five Guys on Walnut between 11th and 12th a couple days ago. In terms of flavor and hunger satisfaction, there isn't a better burger place nearby. Now, I haven't been to Bobby's Burger Palace yet, so for some I know that may not be true. But this place is close by and absolutely delicious.

They keep things simple over there. Burgers already come with two patties, so if you want less, you ask for a little burger. You get to customize what you want on it, and there are lots of things to choose from. Fries are extra, there aren't any meal deals here, so while the $5-6 burger is tempting, know that adding fries and a drink DOES bring your total to more like $10. It's worth it, though. The fries are made fresh, and actually taste it, with peanut oil, which is tasty and healthier than some alternatives. 

I'll also say this, the staff there is super nice and helpful. I got to strike up conversations with them multiple times. It's a big place, there's lots of places to sit, and it's bright and clean.

I also love that they don't advertise, and subsist solely off of word of mouth. They line their walls with their commendations from around the country. You end up feeling like you have to agree with them by the end of it. It's a pretty great burger.

This is the closest burger joint to get to my favourite from the West Coast, In-N-Out Burger, and that to me is the highest praise I can give it. When you want to fill up with something good and greasy, get to Five Guys.
This place is amazing!! I've ordered from a single pretzel to a party tray and it's always a hit! Never left overs....unless I hide some! Prices are great. Quick with your order as well.

Called the King of Steaks for a reason. Let the rival continue as Ginos tries to compete with their bright lights and fancy cheez wiz. Pats is the OG of Philadelphia. Open always, no matter when you're craving. It's old school, so cash is king. Fries are a must too. Make sure you know what you're getting when you get to the window because these guys mean business and have a job to do. 

Its a must when visiting Philly... or driving home from the airport after a long flight!
It used to be a 5,  but recently has declined, what makes it worse is rotten kids walking around trying to sell candy and being rude and you refuse to buy it.  I won't be returning there anymore

There's no good reason you haven't been here yet. Cantina is that spot no matter what season it is. Most people come here in the summer to sit in their huge outdoor area. I think they might sometimes allow small dogs but definitely not larger dogs. Be prepared to wait for drinks. (Their bar is extremely small and I don't think you could fit more than 2 people back there to make drinks.) it's like being in Mexico... In south philly. 

Ask for will, d, or mark if you're at the bar. They're the sh*t. They have great margaritas and do awesome pitcher specials if you go for happy hour. I go here about once a month and I've never had a bad experience.

Food is decent, may be a little overpriced. Definitely almost spent $20 on a burrito recently. I wish the menu would change more frequently. 

Tequila flights are serious! Get them! Drink the Bloody Mary type nonsense they give you. It's spicy but incredible. 

I have two complaints about this place. If you sit at the bar in the winter time you have to keep your jacket on because it's so damn cold. Two, change the God damned jukebox!!!!!! Lady gaga has been on there for over a year!!! That is embarrassing!!! And most of the other stuff sucks!!! Seriously! Change it immediately! I'd rather listen to morse code!!!

Way over rated, though it was better than Geno's, which we went to right after Pat's. Starting with the bread, which had a rubbery crust, right through the meat, which was good but minimal, ending with the whiz, which was runny, everything was noticeably a little sub-par. Line moved quickly, but not worth $11. My local lunch counter in Narberth was better on every count, lots of meat, crusty bread and only $8.

Food wise I really must say I enjoyed my goat. I ordered their Cabrito and it was so good, I finished it even if I was so full because I just didn't want it to go to waste! It was tender and flavorful! Their drinks was great too, I asked our server, even though I've read in so many reviews what their must-try margarita, and our server still suggested their blood orange margarita. I now know why it is so popular. It really is good...hoping to go back here to try their other margaritas and to get to sit in their heated tent! Went here on a cold cold night and it's just great to see that you can still sit "outside." This place is so lively too, very loud but for me loud is just fun! Staff are also extremely friendly and very attentive. Great place to try!

MUST READ: After reading the reviews I was eager to come here with my girlfriend. As me and my girlfriend were waiting online we witnessed one of the cooks rubbing his noise as he was standing over the meat he was cooking . I understand your human but if you're going to rub your nose step aside do watever change ur gloves and continue . Who would still want to eat there after seeing that I know I didn't !

So #4 on the search for the Best Philly Cheesesteak stop was Pat's.
We walked from our VRBO to South Philly to try the Famous Pat's. 
The Cheesesteaks was good.   Bread was nice and soft but held the Whiz.
We loved how it dripped down our hand!!!
We missed the big crowds which was great.  We could sit and enjoy and take it all in.
They have instructions on how to order so follow the rules.  If you mess it up, just go to the back of the line and try again!!
Also, they have a separate line to order the fries and drinks.
Cash Only!!

We had a great meal here! The staff was receptive to my "special order" of a tot scramble with cheddar, mushrooms, onions and peppers. The homemade tots were delicious! As good as they were in the scramble, I'm wishing I ordered a side with whiz! The quaint little neighborhood location is adorable and delicious! We were impressed that we figured out their "JEET" slogan too!

All you need to say is one "wiz wit" and you'll be on your way to tasting what a classic cheesesteak should taste like. We decided to stop by here on our way out from the city for a little early morning breakfest for champions on our way back to NOVA, and I'm glad I did. After reading reviews between this place and Geno's we opted for here based on the reviews. The place may not be as flashy as Geno's, but as they say, never judge a book by its cover. The establishment had some wear and tear to it, but if they have been around for this long, then you know they must be doing something right! Since we were early, there was virtually no line, we ordered, and it seemed just as the cashier handed me my cash back, he was handing me my sandwich right after, talk about some of the quickest service I've ever received! Now onto the sandwich, was it life changing? No. Was it the cheesesteak to end all cheesesteaks? No. But it was juicy, cheesy, delicious, and I ate it to every last bite. I think what makes certain cheesesteaks stand out from the rest are the breads and Pat's just had it going for them, compared to some of the last places I've visited in Philly for cheesesteaks. So in the end, this was the perfect quick pit stop to have some food to combat my hangover, and it did exactly that as we all left the place feeling satisfied.

Go to Blaze for cheap pizza made exactly the way you like it. They have a good selection of toppings, sauces, and crusts. You can even divide your pizza to get different toppings on different parts. It's like getting two or more pizzas in one (: the last time I got my usual spicy pepperoni pineapple on half and on the other I tried a pesto version with veggies and goat cheese. Everything is good quality so it tastes fantastic. My only aside is be careful of your combinations. I have been here three times and once I ordered a pizza I did not end up liking because of how the toppings tasted together - they have pizzas on the menu if you don't know where to start, and start more modest imo to avoid getting something with too many flavors going on! 

The crust gets nice and crisp in the super hot oven, and the whole thing is done in just minutes. Unlimited toppings for 8.99!!
Gristle and grease. Fries, steak and water $17. Just plain bad food at tourist trap prices. The city has so much more to offer.

What...the...heck? How does overcooked, dry pieces of meat covered in plastic cheese sauce with a few pallid onions on a bland roll of bread become a world renown food? How is Pat's even in business? Is this Philly's joke on the food world to hype something this bad? I was skeptical of the low Yelp ratings believing that those who prefer Geno's were leaving bad reviews for Pat's, but after visiting both, they both deserve less than 1-star ratings. The best part of the meal was the pickled red peppers and the fried red chiles they offer to go along with the cheese steak sandwich. Beyond the ridiculously bad cheese steak sandwich, Pat's only accepts cash. Between Pat's and Geno's, at least Geno's has invested in a lot of outdoor lighting whereas Pat's looks like the owners are spending all of the profits elsewhere.

DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY! The pizza was super bland and they rush you through your order. I created my own pizza and asked for extra shredded mozzarella but barely had any cheese on my pizza. The pizzas are super pricey compared to a lot of pizza places in the area. I definitely will not be coming back. The crust was super thin and my pizza tasted somewhat burnt. I was highly disappointed. The pizza looked delicious but tasted super bland. Don't be fooled by looks guys!
Yup! Good stuff for a late night run.

Ordered the fantastic Mushroom Pepper Steak.  It was a hit!  They prepare the food quickly and the service is great. Friendly people and they were quick to make local recommendations for other places.

Awesome margaritas and fish tacos!!

the rest of the mexican...I have had better

ambiance is great - fun place

Worth the walk through the historic Italian Market to this old school joint that has the best cheese steak.  Just do the cheese whiz and then top with picked peppers!!  Grab a Americano a block away at the Cafe Crema Connoli

One of the bests cheesesteaks that you will ever have. I like my prov without. My girlfriend at the time went here and Geno's to have a cheesesteak at both locations and the thing they both have in common is the long line. It was cold and worth it as a few hours later she agreed to marry me. Was it me or the cheesesteaks? I will let you decide.

Pats is the king of steaks . 
I love how fast they food your food and get it .
The bread was amazing to soak up all that cheese and meat .

Idk what's wrong with the people that work at this location, but they are not friendly at all. I pulled up to get my food. I wasn't greeted. No one said thanks or have a nice day. I asked for ketchup. The cashier gave it to me, I said thanks and he didn't say anything in return. That just rubbed me the wrong way. If you don't like your job find another. I was so irked to the point that I took the phone survey. 

The only reason I frequent this location is because my son loves red beans and rice and this is the only one on the route home from his school. Maybe they should get a rep from Chick Fil A to help teach them customer service skills.

After a ton of anticipation, and very high expectations of eating this incredible cheese steak I was left very disappointed.  Been looking forward to this sandwich for a very long time and it was all for nothing. Steak was dry, cheese was ok. Best part of the sandwich was the nice soft hero bread it came on. But other then that I wouldn't go back.
It's the same chipotle that you'd get anywhere else.  Nothing worth noting positive or negative.  I usually do t leave reviews this short but it's chipotle it's what you have had before.

I found the meat in the sandwich to be a bit tough. The bread roll was good, but overall the sandwich was really soggy. The location looks nice and clean. The customer service wasn't great, the cashier was rude and not very friendly. While sitting on one of the benches reading the menu we were approached by a man (not sure if he was a customer or employee) and told us the "tables are only for Pat's customers".

This local eatery showed up on my Yelp search of nearby places on a frigid, icy February day. And it said they serve breakfast all day! Jonesing for breakfast at 3pm I left the Art Museum and stopped on my way home. If you're from the burbs you have to get that parking is hard but a few runs around the block and you are sure to find something.  
The place is small but who cares. That was the charm of the place. You can interact with your fellow humans   I got a seat and ordered within minutes. It was very hard to decide as they had breakfast and an amazing array of sandwiches, Italian and otherwise. The hoagies looked amazing and I ordered an Italian hoagie to go and breakfast to stay.
MEAL: Creamed Chipped beef on toast with potatoes and a coffee. This was comfort food at its best and to die for. Plenty of chipped beef and the potatoes were real, not out of a box and seasoned so well they reminded me of something you'd see on a dinner menu. And the coffee ( pressing fingers to lips like the French do to signify something great). The coffee was great. In reading a previous review they say it is La Columbe? If so it was my lucky day.
I've been a suburban since I was 7 but I am still that person in the burbs who stops to talk with everyone. I met some really cool people here today and the conversation with staff and patrons flowed over my long afternoon breakfast. That's how cool this place is.  One gentlemen was a film aficionado so using a  film reference " I'll be back"

The funny thing about Philly cheesesteaks is that other cities actually do them better than Philadelphia does them. Exhibit A. 

I mean, come on.
Small joint that serves breakfast all day that has good home style food at a good price. I shall return to try the steak and eggs and or the Italian pork hoagie.

Likes:
+The cheesesteak I ordered was meaty and moist.
+The wait time in line isn't too bad. You get your food within one minute of ordering. 
+++There isn't a sign at the ordering window that is meant to offend people that can't speak English or speak it well **cough** Geno's **cough**. 

Dislikes: 
-NONE

If I ever visit Philly again, I will definitely come back here for a cheesesteak.
Very crappy cheesesteaks and nothing but tourists. Also very crappy workers, I'm sure that's their number one specialty though.

This location is either bad or good its literally a roll of the dice. I come one day my food is hot & fresh. Next time its not hot, missing items, or wrong order completely.  I just recommend double checking order because it might not he right

Was in Philly during a vacation so wife and I decided to try the famous Pat's and Genos and put them up against each other.   We got one sandwich from each shop (catty corner from each other).   We came here at the off hour of around 3PM on a weekday so they weren't busy at all and should have had time to make our cheese steaks properly. 

Verdict:  Meh.

Meat: Dry and tough
Bread: Not bad
Cheese: Provolone wasn't even melted
Toppings: Obviously canned mushrooms.

We've had better in San Diego.

Cut and paste this from my Genos review because they were interchangeable as far as we were concerned.

I'm in the military and Pat's took care of us tonight. We REALLY appreciate it. Thanks guys! Coming from Georgia, it's always great to have a REAL Philly cheese steak.  We hope to see y'all soon!!!!   We had a steak with onions, peppers, mushrooms and cheese whiz - POW that was some excellent grub!!

Wanted some solid pizza, margarita style pizza so I got the red vine....seemed to good to be true for the price....and it was. Sauce...tasted like it was out of a can..dough....undercooked...texture and composure.... watery from the tomatoes. Maybe I should guide them a little more when putting it together.

I've been to Five Guys on multiple occasions sporadically over the last few years for burgers and fries, both at this location as well as others. Today I came into this five guys (15th & chestnut) craving a burger with my boyfriend before heading to work. We ordered a bacon cheeseburger and a little bacon cheeseburger with some add on toppings. The guy behind the counter Quayan who took our order was amazing, he greeted us with a big smile and was great to interact with. He was helpful, patient and overall just provided incredible, charismatic customer service. The other guys on the line were working hard but seemed to be having a good time together while putting out a great product for their guests. One of the other guys putting the orders out (I think his name was Deven) was also very friendly. The food hit the spot. The experience was short & sweet but the employees left an impression guaranteeing our return!

Don't even expect a "here you go"-they are rude, but what can be expected? It's fast food...the chicken box satisfied my snack need-where are the chik-fil-a staff when u need them to say, "my pleasure"??
Pat's is ok I would place Pat's 3rd out of Geno's and Jim's. Cool spot worth going to. And their cheese fries are really good better than Geno's in my opinion.

I've been here lots of time and love the margaritas and food but this time the service was absolutely horrible. The waitress was annoyed while we ordered, she then didn't come back for over 40 mins. We were trying to order a second pitcher of margs, which we had to grab the bus boy for. When the margs did come out they were supposed to be frozen but appeared to be more like curdled mango puree. I used to love this place but I'll pass now

This is probably my favorite place in South Philly. Whether you're going there for dinner with friends, cocktails after work, or to party on a Saturday night, Cantina never disappoints. 

Their staff is cool and friendly, their bartenders mix a mean drink, and their kitchen dishes out really delicious fajitas, burritos, nachos... you name it! The bacon-wrapped scallops and fried plantains are definitely some of the most delicious things I have ever tasted. On weeknights they usually play great movies on the TV behind the bar (Top Gun, My Cousin Vinnie... the list goes on) and the people hanging out for drinks on Monday and Tuesday nights are usually good to talk to and interesting. It's definitely a place you can go for a drink and conversation on your own. 

Add to all of this their abundant outdoor seating in the summer months and the Tacate-and-Tequila citywide specials and Cantina is definitely a winner. Not the least-expensive Mexican restaurant on the block but you definitely get what you pay for!
I can't imagine a worse McDonald's. Pure torture every time. Complete dysfunction, rudeness and filth.

We finally had the chance to swing by Pats after living in Philadelphia for about a year. We had some friends in town and of course they wanted to try a cheesesteak. We were in the area of Pats so we swung by and it was everything that I expected it to be. Good cheesesteak but there after better in the city. I ordered mine witout onion and provolone. Good bread, fast service, and a good 3 start place.
Better steaks than geenos didn't like the fries no parking cash only but unique experience

This place was super tasty, incredibly efficient, and was a fun place to meet others from all over the country / world in line. Definitely would recommend it! It's better than Geno's across the street in my opinion (tried Geno's on prior trip to Philadelphia).

This is probably my favorite place to come after dinner, for the night in general, with the girls, or if I want to chalk and pee at the same time.

The food is great, cheap, and served in large portions. Actually - those adjectives all work for the drinks as well. This place is fantastic.

The service is quick and friendly, while the servers are always down-to-earth and equipped with some smart-ass humor to through at you.

A night at the Cantina is never a dull one and getting there is never bad either as they supply you with a parking lot and endless street parking.

The atmosphere of this place is just breezy and comfortable no matter the season and you're surrounded by a crowd that is always nice and eclectic.
It's an alternative to Geno's. I like neither place. But if I have to pick, I will go to Pat's, because I don't agree with Geno's business practice.

Food was awesome as always! Main problem is not enough employees to get the orders out. There is no space for the amount of people waiting for there orders. May reconsider the staffing as to facilitate faster service. Keep up the great chicken sandwich!
The sushi was great, the fish was fresh- definitely exceeded our expectations quality and taste wise. Will order again.

Not phenomenal, but better than Geno's. I like how they have several different kinds of cheesesteaks. I don't know if it's a Philly thing or just a cheesteak restaurant thing, but the workers were pretty obnoxious and looked annoyed at guests who didn't know what to order. I guess service doesn't really matter at a place popular for their cheesesteak sandwiches and not for making friends. The sandwiches were good, but I don't have to have them again.

It is all in the timing. Sometimes the service has been slow/off, other times it is great It doesn't matter if it is a weekday afternoon or a Saturday night. Even the quality of the Margarita's can be inconsistent (depends on the bartender?)

Complimentary tortilla chips and two bowls of salsa (a tomatillo and a red), always good.

Service: On our most recent visit, the service was great (shout-out to our server, Holly). 

Drinks: The Margarita's are fantastic. The Pineapple Marg on-the-rocks with salt was excellent. So was the Blood Orange, on-the-rocks, no salt.

Food: The Quesadilla was flavorless and boring, will not get again. The nachos (small size) with steak was very good. The steak (skirt or flank?) was very tasty. The pork tacos was excellent, generous portions. I have to always add Guac, sour cream and pico de gallo because it is a delicious symphony (they charge extra)

Pricing: Reasonable, on-par with other Mexican joints in the city.

This continues to be part of our rotation.

This McDonald's is such a mess at one point it was under great management but something happens. My kids enjoyed coming to this one and so did I. But now they are so rude they look really young. Secondly I also do Uber eats and they gave me a attitude and said I better come inside like I was stealing food when I showed them on my phone she gave me attitude so I felt bad for the customer waiting on their food but the staff did it to them.

Whiz whit!

Quick, awesome service. Cheesesteaks and cheese fries here are really tasty without the political baggage of Geno's. Also I tried the compared the cheese steaks here to Geno's a couple times and prefer the ones sold at this place each time. Bread is tasty also.

Since this is Philadelphia, and this is the east coast, definitely make up your mind before you come up to order. The line goes by pretty quickly but people get pretty impatient when you take your time to order. 

There is definitely plenty of seating, the only tough thing about this place is that there is only neighborhood parking, however that is the same case with Geno's as well across the street. Anyways definitely check out this place if you haven't already for an experience!
Crappy neighborhood and a bad sandwich. The bread was mushy. The fries were even bad. My kids sandwich was cold. It was all around bad.

Part of our road trip, we took a detour for some philly cheesesteak.  First time trying Pat's and OMG! Heaven!  Kids enjoyed it and was happily pleased with it.  The juice from the meat, onions and cheese, peppers, bread . So delish!!  The kids took a vote and Pat's was our winner!

This was my first time to Pat's. Being the original, I felt that I had to check the box. I was ready with cash and knew the lingo for ordering. Since it was my first time there I thought I had to pick up the Sandwich from the next window, vs the one I ordered at. As I stepped away, I was literally  screamed at, telling me to come back. I understand there is an up front brashness that often comes with east coast interactions, but this was flat out rude and unprofessional. The cheesesteak was pretty good, but I wouldn't say it was anything special. Due to the rude workers, I would not go back.

A must for any foodie in the Phialdelphia area is to compare the Titan's of Phialdlephia cheesesteaks. Here goes: For a purely objective taste test, I ate a Pat's steak and Gino's steak side by side simultaneously for direct comparison. Pat''s came out on top primarily because the meat is better and chopped vs. layered, and beats Gino's's by at least a full star. Did it again two years later and came to the same conclusion. For you non-believers, bring a friend and order one cheesesteak from both steak joints, split them so you have half from both. Try a bite of one then try the other, then do it again . If you still think Ginos is better you may need to have your taste buds examined. It makes sense that Gino's needs the glitz in a desperate attempt to pull people away from Pat's.

Ordered take out from Blaze, the pizza was good for a build your own. Small personal size and a very thin crust (which is my favorite). I'd go here again in a pinch but it's not something I would crave. They also have a nutrition calculator online which I did really like:
Well Guy Fieri and myself disagree once again. I can make better cheese steaks at home and not have to struggle to find parking or have the same bum ask me for money 20 times.
Tried Geno's wasn't great so went to try Pat's.  Can see why it had more people in line.   Food was hot and delicious.   Fries were okay.   Preferred Pats over Geno's
Although I much prefer a chopped, wiz, witout, I have to give the edge to Genos. Pats is just a little too grisly for my taste and tons of grease. Still good though.

Well, I figured if I'm going to try a Geno's, I'll have to try a Pat's. So I'll preface again by saying I got this delivered. To keep things fair, I did ordered the exact same thing as I did from Geno's. A cheesesteak with cheese whiz and onions. Order of cheese fries also. The bread from Pat's I thought had a little more bite to the crust and chew to the dough, which I liked. They also diced up their rib eye more. There was more flavor to it than Geno's...almost a sweetness to the meat. The fries were a thicker cut with I think an extra crispness either from double frying or a flour coating. I probably would've given this about a 3.5, but I felt it was more than okay...just not mind blowing. If it came to the battle between Pat's and Geno's, I'd pick Pat's. I've also been told these 2 are tourist traps so I'm pumped to try some other places.

We knew it was a tourist trap when we went (Yelp gave us all the info we needed to know), and the line took a little longer than we wanted. (We went around 7:30p on a Friday, and we waited in line maybe 20-30 minutes.) So we were hungry when we finally ordered. 

All that being said, we ordered the "whiz wit" (a cheesesteak with cheese whiz and onions) and a cherry soda, and we downed both! So fast. We added some salt about halfway through, and it was a little better. But it was very good. Much better than we were expecting because of the hype (and our hype-skepticism). The bread was chewy enough for me--definitely more baguette than I was expecting from all the reviews about it being soft--and the whole sandwich melded together into a beefy, salty, cheezy, wet tastiness. There are probably better cheesesteaks in Philadelphia, but Pat's was not a waste of time or calories.

(And who knew? The cherry soda was a great pairing!)
Much better than the competition, Genos. Their ingredients are fresh, unlike Genos. Much more authentic than Genos as well. Actually enjoyed their food.

this is the worst mickey deeez ever. My nigga del and his bottom bitch went here this morning and guess what happened?   My dude wanted a mcgriddle. Do u think he got one? No. You ruined his christmas by giving him a steak and and cheese. If he wanted that he woulda went somewhere else. Not to mention the pubic hairs in his hashbrown...  if i see u on the streets just know it aint gonna be good. Like seriously mcdonalds?  Get ur life together

I hate to say this as I was hoping for a different outcome, but this wasn't good at all. It's fun to say we tried it but that's it. To be honest we have better Philly cheesesteak in Utah!! Not kidding. The meat was bland and they gave me my order wrong and wouldn't correct it. Service is rude and short tempered! Because this sandwich was so bad I went across the street to Gino's, I couldn't imagine it was this bad. The service was better at Gino's they were more patient. The facility is more up-to-date, which I don't usually care about! The bread is different, a little bit more chewy for the texture which I liked and The meat had better flavor but not much. Now that might be because the cheese sauce over at Pats covered my entire sandwich so all I could taste was the cheese.  There is absolutely no flavor in this sandwich. If in my life I ever have to eat between one of these two places again I would drive someplace else instead. Not my favorite, wasn't worth my time And I would go someplace else! Not really even fun to say I ate here!

VISIT HISTORY: 
- Last visit: 2 Fridays ago with a girlfriend 
- Frequency: First time! 
- Next visit? Maybe (apparently they have a tequila flight)

FOODRINK:
- Blackberry margarita: This was one of their specials and I ended up getting a second round. Amazing! I think good margaritas are difficult to make, though many attempts have been made. This came frozen and was enjoyed very much! 
- Fried plantain: I love everything about planntain. The plantains. Not overly fried. Cut evenly. 

VIBE:
- Attentive waiter. Made sure to ask for a refill on the margarita before the first one was fully consumed
- Noise level: really loud. I made a comment about how the music was really loud (and at the time there were three tables seated including us) and he just shrugged his shoulders. Music range from rock to hip hop. Confused playlist. 
- Wait time for food arrival: under 10 minutes
- Wait time for our check: under 5 minutes

Good Cheesesteaks.  Expensive. Rude rules... I mean... I get it... It's an establishment, and well known - Not only for their cheesesteaks, and lines, but for the way you order and stand in line and go to the back of the line if you're not ready... It's good stuff, but... Well... Go for the cheesesteaks, and the experience.  Once... I'm sure there's just as good, if not better somewhere in Philly.
More like Pat's Crap O Steak ! You should have seen the cashier and cook, no teeth one was picking his nose and the cashier asked me for my wife's number wtf!!!! This place is a sh&%$ hole

I have loved Blaze Pizza for some time now. Pizza is a go to meal, but I have to be in the mood. No matter where I am in the world if I see a Blaze Pizza, I'm there! There are so many vegan options and yummy toppings. There is a new vegan spicy chorizo that you all have to try!! my favorite thing to do is order a pizza with every single vegetarian topping that they have. Download the app for coupons and free drinks and to earn points! 
Contents of my pizza : Build Your Own 
Pesto & Spicy Red sauce 
Vegan Spicy Chorizo
Kalamata Olives 
Roasted Garlic 
Roasted Brussel Sprouts 
Sweet Green Peppers
Jalapeños 
Artichokes
Mushrooms 
Fresh Basil
Red Onions
Oregano & Sea Salt 
Arugula & Balsamic Glaze
It's first time in South Philly. Wanted to try famous cheesesteak-. It has a good flavor with sweet onion but under seasoned. Service was super fast.

Philly Native and I have never been here until last year...simply because it's for tourists. But I must say the cheese steaks make excellent full snacks...like before you go bar hopping or after you leave the club. NOT the best cheese steaks in Philly but damn good. just don't expect friendly warm service..but expect your sandwich to come really fast and Delicious

Geno's or Pat's?  Pat's or Geno's?  I guess that is the question.  Well, I'm just visiting from Los Angeles, so I tried both back-to-back within 5 minutes of each other (they are located across the street from each other).
I ordered a "Wiz wit" from each one (what's with the stupid ordering system?) and I thought Pat's was the winner.  Geno's wasn't bad, but I liked the steak better at Pat's.

BTW, I've had better cheesesteak sandwiches in California.  I think these places are more for the experience, rather than the actual cheesesteak...similar to Pink's in LA.
Came to Pat's after literally finished eating a cheesesteak sandwich from Geno's. I have to say...the king crown for the better Philly cheesesteak definitely goes to Pat's. It was delicious.

I've had both the juices and the smoothies. The juices are good and I like how you can see them make it in front of you. However, they are little expensive. I ordered the peanut butter cup "smoothie" on the other hand and it was watered down and it lacked taste.

First time in Philadelphia so I thought I'd try their famous Philly Cheese Steak.  Didn't know which to pick, Pat's or Geno's.  Flipped a coin.  Pat's it was.  After all the hype, stories and building it up, I just don't get it.  It was just a chopped steak sandwich with onions and cheez wiz on a roll.  Wasn't bad, just wasn't some heavenly experience.  Not to mention the price.  $11 for an approx 12" sandwich.  The only up side, was watching all the freaks walking in the area.

Visited here while on vacation. The lady behind the cash register was rude and short. The sandwich came out fast, that's the only good thing. Went to the other station to get a soda and the guy scratched his ass right before pouring my drink. Disgusting. The Philly was definitely not all that it was up to be. Bread was hard and the steak was flavorless. DO NOT GO HERE

As good as I expected. I made sure to see the correct way to order so I didn't look like a rookie. I got one "Wit Whiz". Went to the next window and ordered a birch beer. The cheesesteak was delicious! Right amount of juice, not too much cheese to be messy, good amount of onions. Birch beer was good too! I felt good as a local, that brought his friends, made faces as they ordered "I'll have a cheesesteak with grilled onions and cheese whiz". He said, "why can't you do it like the NY'er?"

Yay me!

Stopped by Philly last weekend on a random road trip and... when in Philly, get cheese steak!

This place had lots of good reviews and it makes sense, the food is delicious and the food is served extremely quickly, probably because they're so used to large orders daily. I recommend the mushroom pepper pizza steak and adding more peppers from the condiments section.

Not too pricey, I just wish they had some kind of indoor seating, or outdoor heating now, especially since winter is coming.

I am definitely going to come back here for their cheesesteak. The melted cheese and soft cooked onion mixed in the cheesesteak was deliciousssss! Unfortunately, I wasn't able to get the fries but I will definitely get it on my next visit. Overall 8/10

Hungover after a wedding in Philly? Then this place is sure to be the cure for your brunch (or lunch) after stumbling out of your hotel room.

I've been here once back in October 2010 (see above). It was Football Season and the Eagles were playing so it was probably a bit busier than usual...but that's fine. I'm an out-of-towner wanting to sample the local fare and first on the agenda was the legendary Philly Cheese Steak...

Let's just say that Pat's was well worth the 45+ minute wait.

Mushroom Whiz Wit....PERFECTION
Cheese fries...they are fries smothered with Whiz...what's not to love?
couldn't find anything wrong "wit" either.

$10 or whatever it cost (I can't remember)...I consider it an investment into broadening my perspectives on food, local culture, and for the experience...and the overall experience was great. Pat's receives 4 stars from me until I get a chance to come back and try Geno's, Jim's and Tony Luke's.

Pat's: I refuse to eat anywhere where I am going to be treated like a redheaded stepchile because I can't speak their stupid lingo-I don't work there, I am not a waitress, so why do I have to be trained to comply and submit to this? Stupid. (This is not to say anything against waitresses anywhere.) 
Geno's: To post a sign requiring English would make me boycott  anyplace. Yeah, this IS America-the only way you are not an immigrant YOURSELF is if you are American Indian.
I'll try Jim's next time I'm in town, always heard good things.

Birth place of the Philly cheesesteak! 
I went with a Philly local who grew up decades ago with this family. I thoroughly enjoyed walking up to this restaurant with him and seeing it from a true local's point of view. Essentially, I saw  all these tough guys behind the counter pause for a minute to welcome me as an outside, talk more about their restaurant and neighborhood's history and love for the blessings they have had in life.  

Maybe not the best sandwich I have ever had...but I am definitely glad that I tried out this American original at the original restaurant and experience it with a true local. 

(insider tip: cash only)

This was my first Philly cheeseteak and I'm not sure if this is what I'm supposed to be basing my opinion off of. Either way I know I didn't enjoy this.  Dry meat, undercooked onions, canned mushrooms, and weirdos working the counter. Meh.

Stopped into Blaze for the first time last night and the pizza was super yummy. My girlfriend was pumped to see gluten free dough and the staff was friendly/helpful walking us through choices. Great spot in West Philly!
One of the best in Philly!  I suggest a "Provy Wiz Wit," an order of cheese fries topped off with a birch beer.  Provy wiz wit = Cheesesteak with fried onions, Provolne and Cheese Wiz.

Horrible service again! I only go here for quick lady minute meals. The service was slow. The poor girl working the register had no help while the other girls talked by the fry counter! I ordered 6 piece nugget and more than half of them were still sorta frozen ! Smh. They need a new manager during evenings because the young girl they have isn't doing a good job. This is my 2nd review with bad news smh

If you close at 2 update your hours. I was hungry for breakfast saw they were open on yelp and took a uber to get there. I walk through the door and I'm greeted with a "we're closed". Oh really so why does yelp say y'all close at 5. Unbelievable.
The OG cheesesteak in Philly. You have to try it during your visit, the atmosphere and experience is worth it even if the cheesesteak is OK. Plus it's pretty cheap and cheesy so worth it

What can I say.  There's the rest, then there's the best!  Pat's is the King of Steaks!

Provolone wit is my pick every time!!

You can't beat the cheesesteak we did a side-by-side comparison, with the people catty corner from them. There was no comparison we were sad we spent the money across the street. Solid with a lot beefsteak, best bread.  Wow!!! The peppers!!!! Don't forget the peppers.

We ordered this to the home for the family. The poke was fresh in the rice was warm. There was very interesting flavors and we enjoyed the food and we will order again.. 

The fried chicken was tasty and the portions were generous
Loved this place! It's like sweetgreen for pizza! Fast friendly service and a personalized pizza with anything you'd enjoy on top! Location was clean and I really can't wait to go again!
Food is great, area and location is great!!! Can't complain, food is overall good. Expect long lines on weekends but they tend to move quickly! I approve this message!

I love the concept of this place--basically a make your own pizza joint with fresh and yummy ingredients. While they have signature pizzas, I would definitely recommend the create your own. With unlimited toppings, it's definitely worth the price. I like to go with the regular crust (they have high rise and gluten free available) and the spicy tomato sauce. For toppings, I would recommend the roasted garlic--so yummy! Don't forget to ask for a finish once the pizza is cooked. I go with the basic olive oil drizzle. Overall, great place, will be back for sure.

Overated Rip Off. Never coming back.
Not impressed with flavor at all - standard at best. Also very expensive $60 for 4 people. Fries $6 for an 8 oz cup.

I was reminiscing about In and Out two days ago, and it got me thinking - is there a burger (and solely burger) joint out here in Philly that I enjoy. The answer was yes! Five Guys.

But I should be fair. You can't really compare In and Out and Five Guys. The former is light and portioned just right; the latter is heavyyyy. Every time I eat Five Guys, I feel like I should start running again. Then I order Five Guys' Cajun french fries.

Enough rambling - this is my fav place to get a quick burger in Philly. It's clean, the service is prompt, you get free peanuts and the fries are absurdly tasty. I come here whenever I'm in the area and have the slightest pangs of hunger.
Wayyyyy to much hype for Pat's and Geno's. Overpriced and doesn't meet expectations.

So like it's my first time visiting Philadelphia and heard about Geno's and Pats having great Philly cheesesteaks. We came here as a group and decided to get both to compare. Neither of them were that good. Both looked like beat down old fast food joints. The cheesesteak wasn't horrible, but don't deserve to be mentioned at all to anyone who's coming from out of town and looking for a good cheesesteak. Like please, don't tell anyone about this place unless you know for a fact they want to waste their time eating a less than mediocre Philly cheesesteak in Philadelphia. I got one from the airport and it was better than both.
來芝加哥就不要錯過，幾乎每個遊客都會來吃Geno跟Pat's King然後做個比較，我個人是覺得都很好吃，但每個人心中都要自己的喜好，這部份的樂趣請自己去嘗試。

Blaze has become one of my new favorite places to eat at. 

Location- this location is almost never packed. I am in and out with my pizza within 10-15 minutes. Parking is usually pretty good around there. 

Staff- the staff here is extremely friendly. I go there pretty often and the employees always recognize me and make conversation- which is something I appreciate when it comes to customer service. 

Food- If you haven't been here, this is the equivalent of Chipotle but for pizzas. You go down the line and pick your sauce, cheeses, and ingredients. The toppings bar is always fully stocked and the ingredients are fresh. I pretty much get the same pizza every time. It's amazing that I can get all the ingredients that I want on my pizza for just $8.25. Everyone can get what they want for a low price. If you decide to dine in and you don't finish your pie, they have cute half boxes were you can place the rest of your pizza and take it home. They have a fresh water station that I tend to skip out on because they are extremely sweet.

Upon the urging of daughter, we went to Chipotle this evening.  While I love their burritos,  this was the first time that I had the displeasure of eating a steak burrito that I did not like.  Five pieces of steak were mostly fat. I understand that the fat gives the steak most flavor,  but I'm sure that my burrito would have tasted better if the pieces of steak had been leaner. I still like Chipotle,  but I'll probably consider having something other than a steak burrito.

I went to this McDonald's for the first time ever, this past Saturday  (and my first time at a McDonald's in many years.)
What can I say- its McDonald's. The food was what you would expect. 

The customer service was excellent though. There was a problem with the latte I ordered, & I ended up having to wait about 10 minutes for it. After waiting, it did not taste good at all. 
The manager came over, apologized, & remedied the situation. 
If I ever return to a McDonald's, I'll be sure to give this one another try.

Had to be a tourist and come give this place a go, my initial thoughts were overwhelming because of the plaque on the floor and the recommendations from friends. Quite the long drive from NYC to get here but it was worth it in my opinion. 

Had to order a philly cheese steak when I arrived. The hero was nice and toasty with the steak steaming hot off the grill with the cheese slathered over the top of the steak and I topped it off with some ketchup. 

Overall had a good time and the philly steak was great. But make sure you have cash, that's all they accept. CASH IS KING

First and foremost- GUAVA MARGARITA ON THE ROCKS WITH SUGAR.

Do it, your tastebuds will thank you. Their margaritas are amazeballs.

I always enjoy their food too, though! The chips and two types of dip they bring out, i don't even know what it is honestly, are delicious. I've always gotten the small order of nachos with chicken and they are big enough to share between two and delicious. Also, their fish tacos. Always yummy! But definitely get some additions to the tacos, they can be a little bland without guacamole/sour cream/pico etc.

The atmosphere is adorable too, i love it. I'm kind of in love with any place that hangs christmas lights up all year around though, it just sets the mood.

Good stop for poke if you are looking for something fast. I thought this place gave an average amount of fish and had the typical toppings available to choose from. You can select a premade bowl or opt for a make-your-own. There's also a large size for those who are extra hungry. The ingredients seemed pretty fresh to me, but still doesn't compare to places on the West Coast for those who are poke experts. This place does have an assortment of beverages to choose from, which was nice. Overall, it will do to satisfy one's poke cravings. This place seems to be for carry out.
Best cheesesteak spot in Philly. Leaps and bounds over geno's . The sandwich was packed of meat and full of flavor. Cant beat it

People always say that Pats and Genos are not the place for the most authentic sub steaks but I am from Brooklyn NY and I have been here maybe 8 to 10 times. Each time I come here I do not get disappointed. Their whiz cheese is great and that is always what I am going to order according to some Philadelphia friends. 

Expect a fast and rushed experience. They are not being rude or anything.

I believe this was my first cheesesteak I've ever had in Philly. 

Really cool location, awesome that it's across the street from Geno's and they have the rivalry thing going.

The cheesesteak was good, I cannot complain. Fresh bread, tender meat, American cheese all served fast, I could eat here and be happy. It's not my favorite but it's pretty good... and if it's near, I'll come by again.

Bum ass employees being mad disrespectful to my family. Nobody was in line when I got there and I get rushed to order when reading the menu out of line. Food came out cold and they're completely overrated who pray off of tourist.
Not the best but it's OK compared to the over-rated Genos.
Delicious. Historic. Character. Get the Wiz Wit and a Cheese fry. The long lines and limited seating are the only reasons I didn't give 5-stars. But those things are part of the experience.

I really love mexican food and I think that the steak tacos here are the best in the city... have yet to find better here in Philly...  I love the outside when it is available.  The inside is a tad bit loud... almost too loud to enjoy anything.  The reason I gave this place 4 instead of 5 is that some of the staff members are not the nicest.  I have had several experiences with very rude hostesses... like out of control rude... to where if I didn't love the steak tacos so much I would have walked out with my entire large group of friends.  There are some really awesome servers though.  I think one is Zach, he has been our server several times and is always attentive and has a great personality. I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a cool place to hang with drinks and get great mexican food.  The vibe is awesome.  OH and I forgot to mention the pitchers of margaritas are incredible.... just wish they would do better tequila options for the frozen ones.  That is always a bummer because well drinks get me sick.  I would happily pay more for a better options there.

I went to pats because it has better reviews than Geno's. This is the only cheesesteak I've had in philly and I got the cheesesteak with onions with cheese wiz.  There might be a line but it moves fast. When you get to the ordering station you should know your order because they do everything fast!  

The cheesesteak was a little messy but they do give you a decent amount of meat. It's definitely shareable between two people especially if you've been walking through the Italian market and sampling things along the way. The meat is tender and juicy but there's still too much bread. I added some ketchup and relish ( I know that's weird) but i think that added dimension to the meat and cheese. 

I'm not sure if this is the best cheesesteak but it's decent. It's my first time exploring Philly so I had to get a cheesesteak at its source.

This was one of my favorite pizza spots on campus but I'm so disappointed in the service I received.
I ordered online at 5:20 PM, went to pick it up at 5:30 PM when it would be ready. when I got there the cashier told me to wait cus it's being prepared. After 20 minutes, it's still not ready so I asked her if it's being prepped. Then she said she never got the order and continued to ignore me. The entire crew knew what was going on but nobody wanted to help. Finally I asked the manager what to do and he disappeared in the back for like 15 minutes. I showed them the confirmation email and the charge on my credit card. Still nothing, so I just left. Although the food is good I will never ever ever be returning. After trying to reach Blaze customer service on multiple social media platforms and by email, all I got were the same generic responses. Finally filed a chargeback with my bank!

Had Brunch their over the weekend. The eggs Benedict are amazing! 
My finance had the quesadilla salad with chicken and loved it as well.
Both split a pitcher of blood orange margaritas very good. 

My only problem was how close the seating is you are literally right next to other people, not much breathing room. If you don't mind that then its very worth it. 

The waitress was great too!

Ok. Sandwich? Good. 

Customer Service? Terrible. I politely asked for a cup of water with my fries at the "Fries, etc" window, and the guy said "No."
He was so terse/blunt that I thought he was kidding and laughed. Then I looked at his face, and realized he was completely serious. He followed that with, "Sorry, no can do, babe." (Babe?! Really?).

I'm sorry, but if you can't take 5 seconds to give me a paper cup of water after I just paid $13.50 for a sandwich and fries (overpriced if you ask me) with unheated outdoor seating in November, I won't be returning. But maybe I'm just missing the point of the experience?

I was told that Pat's was a good (although touristy) place for a philly cheesesteak, so we went for a late night trip around 1AM. There was a small line but it moved very quickly. You go to the window, pay in cash, and they hand you a hot and freshly wrapped cheesesteak before you leave. It's a quick and easy process.

Personally, I really enjoyed my cheese steak. The meat was juicy and tender. The bread was soft and fluffy. The melted cheese was hot and is essentially the type used for nachos - which was definitely really tasty. 

This location is also open 24/7 so that's another plus. Unfortunately, it's cash only so it can be a bit inconvenient if you don't like to carry cash. 

However, I will definitely stop by again if I'm ever back in Philly!

Visited Philly so def had to try Pat's. Line can get pretty long but they move extremely fast. So when you get to the front, know how to order and have your cash in hand. Then just enjoy your greasy goodness. Whiz wit is def my favorite.

First time in Philly, had to try despite the 3 star average on Yelp. In short, I was unimpressed. I ordered the steak with onions, peppers, and provolone. They handed me the sandwhich practically as soon as I paid. The meat felt dry and overcooked. I was prepared for salty meat, but no need. It wasn't terribly bland, though. I suppose that's safer if they expect most people choose the whiz (which is unpalatable to me). I tried it, don't completely regret it, but probably will go other places in the future
The fries were fresh and hot. I ate there around 630 PM on a Sunday night.
Pats is delicious, but Im a Genos man. Definitely give them both a try though. The only reason I go with Geno's is the peppers. Otherwise they're on the same level.

Just got to Philly from VA, heard about the dispute over Pat's and Geno's and how it's a famous philly cheesesteak landmark. So my boyfriend ordered from Pat's and got the regular philly cheesesteak which was about 1 foot long for $10.00.  You can add other ingredients to your philly steak, but for additional costs. They have a unique way of ordering your food without telling them a whole paragraph of your choosing, they have it posted on their menu.

The place is a fast food place that you walk up to and order. They have picnic tables for seating that surrounds the entire place. You can see their rivalry right across from them.

I finally got to try a Philly cheesesteak in Philly.  I thought it was mediocre, but I really liked their bread it had a nice texture. 

It's funny, when you bring their opponents food over their territory, they will say "thats garbage" (with a jersey accent).

I know Chick-fil-A has recently gotten some competition with Popeyes making a chicken sandwich but, Chick-fil-A is definitely the OG in this game! This is a great pit stop if you have a long layover or need a fill-up before your flight. I am always a sucker for airport food stands. Their waffle fries are delicious! The weaved texture of waffle fries always make eating it more fun. I liked how perfectly seasoned they were. Their nuggets are shaped like real chicken and taste like real chicken. Usually, nuggets have that texture of mashed up chicken that is shaped into a patty. I didn't like how all of their ketchup packets were smeared with ketchup. I thought it was cool how there was live music in the food court where this Chick-fil-A was. There was a saxophone player, drummer and rapper. It wasn't the quickest service ever but the wait wasn't too bad. There's plenty of seating because this place is located in a food court.

Was this the best Philly cheesesteak in the world? Maybe not, which is too bad because a) that's what you'd hope for when in Philadelphia and b) this place is highly renowned. It was still very good though. I got mine "Provolone wit" and thought it was definitely pretty tasty. I think one risk you run with Philly cheesesteaks is dryness, but this was overall a pretty good amount of moist. It was kind of greasy, which was okay for the time being, but I do think that detracted a little bit from the sandwich. The bread was fine. Could have been a little firmer. By nature they have very efficient service (necessary when there's a ton of people lining up into the street) and the sandwiches are really big, with a ton of meat packed in them. It was a little expensive but fair enough considering the status Pat's holds in the area. I'm not sure that I would go back, but it was worth the experience as a tourist.

For the same price as Geno's, you get a cheese steak sandwich that has more meat (and the meat is actually warm!), and the provolone had a nice, sharp taste. Overall this sandwich packed more flavor.

Although not a huge fan of cheese steak in general, I was happy and satisfied with what Pat's had to offer.

I would come again.
----------------------------
PS: If, like me, you're planning a nice, long walk from downtown to get to this neighborhood in the evening, think again. Although not necessarily unsafe, you'll walk through dilapidated neighborhoods with completely empty streets before reaching your destination.
mom and brother work there . I love the cheese fries and pizza steaks !

I give this place four stars because they are good, but I favor Ginos.  Maybe its the flashy lights.  Part of me believes they are owned by the same guy who sits across the street, watching the daily chaos and listening to a healthy rotation of Frank Sinatra and Mario Lanza records.

Tasty Twisters makes two types of pretzels: the regular (with salt) and a desert one that uses sugar and cinnamon instead of salt. Both are delicious!

They bake throughout the day, so chances are good that your pretzels have just emerged from the oven -- and there is nothing better!

Bring cash -- I don't think they accept credit cards. But they are reasonably priced: $1.00 buys three regular pretzels or two of the desert ones.

And buy more than you think you'll eat -- you'll eat them.
