Service wasn't bad, and the waitress was accommodating when I asked for a separate check(My rule of thumb when there's a large group, always ask for a separate check. That way you don't get stuck paying for some slacker(s)).

The price, well 12.95 for three medium sized tacos, yeah that's a bit steep. They were good tacos, but you know, I can go to Jose's and get 3 tacos for at least 4 bucks less. 

I might go back again if I"m with a group like I was. I don't think I'd ever go there just for a meal. There are too many other good places that cost less and have quieter atmospheres.

Happy hour at the Cantina can't be beat...$10 pitchers of house margaritas, chips with two different types of salsa...perfect recovery combo for a stressful day at work! The margaritas are strong too, which makes it doubly great.

I've tried some of their fruit margaritas as well. The white peach is a delicate and refreshing change from the traditional, and the raspberry is tart with a bit of sweetness.

I am a total slave to the Carnitas burrito and tacos (depends on how hungry I am). The slow cooked pork is juicy and flavorful, and coupled with cheese and rice, the ultimate comfort food. I've had the chicken burrito as well, which is also delicious, but my loyalties are with the carnitas.

This is a great place to go for whatever occasion, whether to get drinks or drinks and food.

I like it better here than Geno's. I went here with some of my family members and we went and got a sandwich from Geno's and also Pats to compare. I like this place better just because the meat was juicier. I hardly eat cheese steaks but this was pretty good.

Good value. Punctual delivery. Easy online interface for a group order. For a work lunch, we were each given a limit of $13, and that was enough to get me the largest sandwich, the Gargantuan, a bag of chips, and a cookie.

I'd give the Gargantuan 2.5 stars. It's a lot of meat, and as much as I was looking forward to a filling meal, it didn't taste great. It was a mash-up of a lot of different cold cuts that didn't work well together, and it had too much mayo.

As expected, I enjoyed the sandwich but was not knocked out of my socks.  They rush the crap out of you, the place is a mob scene. It was enjoyable, I would eat there again but I can also make them at home.

I've been hearing about this Pat's vs. Geno's feud for years now, but being a Brooklyn guy, I don't get to Philly that much...OK, this was my first trip there since I was a kid. I grabbed the Thursday 10:20am Megabus from outside Javits and hit Philly around noonish, having only had coffee and a donut for breakfast. The bus let up off just down the street from Independence Hall, so I checked it and the Liberty Bell out first before heading to 8th Street to catch the 47 bus to Passyunk.  There they both were, Pat's and Geno's, standing opposite each other like two pro wrestlers waiting to take each other apart. Being a purist, I hit Pat's first. I've heard horror stories about mile-long lines, but being that this was 1:30pm on a Thursday, there was only one person ahead of me and being that I don't mix milchdik & fleishdik, I ordered a steak wit (onions) ($10.00 wit tax) and grabbed a green, orange and red cherry pepper as a side.  If you don't know about cherry peppers, here's some advice: The red ones, counter-intuitively, are sweet with a nice little kick of heat. The orange ones are hotter and the green ones, if you can't take the heat, you should avoid. Fortunately, I like heat. They were certainly generous enough with the meat, which, while a bit on the greasy side, was tender and flavorful. The bread was nice and chewy enough to hold up to the meat, but it was obviously very fresh.
Having skipped breakfast and being subjected to a two-hour bus ride and brief historical tour, I still had room after my Pat's steak to try the upstart newcomer, so I dodged traffic and headed across the street to Geno's, where I ordered the same steak with onions and no cheese  (also $10.00 wit tax). Unlike Pat's, where they slice and chop their meat, Geno's slices and grills, which may be why their meat, in comparison was so dry and tasteless. The difference between Pat's and Geno's was so obvious that I dodged traffic a second time and bought two more to take back to Brooklyn "wit" me. In my humble opinion, in the war between Pat's King of Steaks and Geno's, Pat's wins hands-down. (Although, to be truthful, neither comes close to the Italian Beef sandwich I had at Portillo's in Chicago.)

Eating outside on the street, al fresco, if you will... It looks perfectly lovely to sit outside the Cantina on a nice warm day with some chips & salsa, some margaritas, some beers.  It can be, but you know that scene gets super-busy and crowded. Like reeeally... and I just tend to get a little jumpy, constantly feeling like people on the street (um baba bee dah day) walking by are so close to grazing my person as they're trying to slip by.. The outdoor seating is the middle of the sidewalk. I've braved dodgin' rumps there before, alright! Only very slightly do I exaggerate.

The Cantina can be lotsa fun, muy divertido for real...but again, a big ol packed scene. Inside is appropriately cantina-esque with twinkly strings of lights.

 I do agree with others who have griped that while by the glass the margaritas are delicious, sometimes by the pitcher they seem overloaded with ice. Not always, but it happens.

Do dig the flights of tequila and dig the michelada too. Do believe I'll be back this Summer, inevitably.

Was expecting a lot from this place as this is supposedly the originator of cheesesteaks. Was in Philadelphia for day. I opted for Pat's as a friend of mine went to Geno's and wasn't impressed with it. Very expensive for a cheesesteak $11!! And fries and soda are separate of course. Ordered the steak from 1 window and soda and fries from different windows. My sandwich was literally done within 10 seconds! Meaning was already made pretty much. Meat was dry with no seasonings and the bread was soggy. 
ADVISE for TOURIST! Don't believe the hype. There's other places that are more worth your money.

Basically....

[+] Hot waitstaff
[+] Yummy Margaritas 
[+] Bangin' chips and salsa (the red salsa is better than the green one, imho)
[+] Fun ambiance
[+] Hot waitstaff

That's all you need to know.  Go!
This place isnt pretty and shiny but the food is good and in my opinion tastes better than across the street. Has more soul in the food.

Worst experience I've ever had in my life. Took 45 minutes to get 4 tacos and when I asked where my order was, the manager said "you've only been waiting 37 minutes and there's three orders ahead of you." Absolutely ridiculous. Avoid this place at all costs. By the time I got my food I wasn't even hungry anymore. And when I opened my food bag, a taco was already open and poured out everywhere. Took it back to get it refilled and it took another 20 minutes so I had to beg and plead for a refund. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Pros: 
-24/7
-Fast service

Cons:
-Dry meat
-Meat is cooked and just sits
-Bread is not warmed up at all
-Bread is bad
-Cash only
-Small serving size compared to others

I thought I'd try it because "it can't be that bad, could it?"
It was terrible, don't even bother coming here especially when there are so many better places in Philly.

What a great value at the airport, where things always seem so pricy.  Fresh, delicious, healthy with courteous service, what more could you ask for in fast food!  Great location in the F Concourse!  I always get a bowl, never been disappointed.

Kevin- Does your cheesesteak have cheese-wiz

Pats team member- Look I don't have time for games here what can I get Jew ? 

Should have went to Geno's! Screw these rude assholes.

How this place is still in business I have NO IDEA. Go to Gino's!!!!!!!

Although the food is bad for you, it does taste good. That is all that is good here. The workers frequently mess up orders. The place is dirty and unkept. The workers are obnoxious and lazy. Oh and don't even think about using the restroom unless you wanna add vomit to what was already there. Overall this place needs to make a big turn aroud. Final suggestion: If you want McDonalds in this area, the one on Torresdale is pretty good. Not a 4 or 5 star, but way better than this one on Cottman.

We came from LA to visit Philly, I swear thee best steak sandwich ever! We compared PAT'S  to GENO'S, PAT'S hands down the best sandwich ever, very flavorful, tender and juiciest meat ever. The fries with the most perfectly crunch. And the cherry coke was good too, no flat soda. And if you're an immigrant or have an accent don't go to GENO'S, Google them before going.

Used to be a great spot.  

Passyunk Ave is blossoming into a hot area but Cantina refuses to change.  Service was good and but good is inconsistent.  
Sitting for dinner at around 8:00 and had a flashlight put in my face three times asking for my ID.  Complete confrontational bro hard dick.  Avoid on a Friday night.

i love 5 Guys!
i've been to 3 different ones and all 3 have been great.
it's a place i can go to with my meat loving guy friends and still get something too. i still get made fun of but at least i can order something. i always a veggie sandwich (2.20) and i steal fries from my friends. their fries are amazing, best i have ever had maybe. you can choose from about 10 different veggies and none come with an extra change, which rules. you can also get cheese at no extra change. i never do, but whatevs. also, they serve Coke products here which is extremely important to me bc i pretty much only drink Diet Coke.

Went here lastnight around 9:30 and what a nightmare.  First we come in and tell the hostess 8-10 people for outside.  She tells us 45 min wait but inside has no wait.  We ask if we could sit inside until an outside table opens and we were told no.  So we go sit inside.  1 minute later she runs up to us and states a table just opened outside we could sit at.  We go outside and sit but realize the table is only made for 6, 8 if you are little.  We are all on a softball team so that wasn;t happening.  The waiter comes over and we notice the table next to us is getting up.  He tells us we could use that table as well when they leave.  He then doesn't want to take drink orders yet until we get the table. ughhh.  We move the other table over and now the 10 of us fit perfectly.  Drink orders are taken and 2 minutes later the hostess comes up and tells us we can't sit at the other table.  We tell her the waiter told us to but she said no.  We obviously were upset and didn't want to move so the manager comes over.  Thsi lady looks as if she has never managed a thing in her life and had the worst management skills ever.  She asks us to split up and then come back together later.  We ask for her reasoning, she says there's a long wait outside and a party has been inside waiting forever.  I ask her how is that if we walked in and waited for 5 minutes for this table.  Wouldn't they be ahead of us if they were waiting forever.  She has no answer but keeps saying WHat can I do for you?  "Leave me alone" was my answer.  She continues to keep saying the same thing over and over, "What can I do for you"  "I want to make you happy"  IDIOTTTT.  2 guys in our party leave and go to Birra.  Now we have 8 and after being frustrated we decide to sit around a 6 top and they give us a small 4 top.  hmmmmm. If you had a 4 top available why wasn't that offered to  be put next to out table or why couldn' the party of 6 squeeze around that until there was another table.  WHY move a seated table when the table that wants to sit outside would squeeze.  The funniest thing about the tables was in about 10 minutes 3 or 4 tables go up and left. WOW  

Next on to the Server, We order drinks and the waiter just sucked.  Our drinks took 20 minutes, first round of drinks.  2 drinks were forgotten and the 2 guys that left due to the removal of our table had their drinks brough and were on the bill.  We tell the waiter he forgot 2 drinks.  Do they come?  NOPE  about 10 mins later he comes back and we tell him again about the 2 drinks and the others place a 2nd round.  Out he comes another 10 mins later, long for beers huh?  What is missing, my same 2 drinks.  I finally call timeout and tell him this is crazy.  So what does he do.  He comes out a few mins later with the 4 drinks missing for the same person.  Jeez.  At this point 4 is better than none.  A few more rounds of this and the guy still keeps messing up.  He's lucky there is an auto 18% gratuity.  I feel like he "waiter raped" us and knew the auto 18% was on and just didn't pay attention.  4 of us at the table have been in the business for over 15 years a piece and are huge tippers.  We understand being in the weeds and being busy but this place just lacks quality service and after seeing the DOE DOE of a manager i could see why.  She literally was missing a few screws.  Dos Cabalito's I love ya and have been there many times.  I even took my softball team of 9 others who have never been there and HUGE dissapointment.   I'll be back but only because my gf likes your nacho's.

Can I say what a disappointment "authentic" Philly Cheesesteaks were? This place was seriously in the boonies. I don't understand why two of the most "famous" cheesesteak places are located here, but alright.
I found the signs to be humorous, but the service to be really brusque. In knowing that probably a lot of tourists come by, is it really necessary to bark at your customers and point and grunt to direct them where to go? Not only that, but I was grossly underwhelmed by the cheesesteak with grilled mushrooms. To me, it wasn't worth it. I think my favorite cheesesteak was in San Diego... 'nough said.
I love Pat's Steaks if you are in philly this  landmark is worth a try please go check this place out  You will not be disappointed And I have try Gino's as well and I'm team pat lol

Friendly and quick service. Subs are tasty. My only grievance is that they could use more lettuce and tomato, but that's easily solved by making the request. I highly recommend coming here before a game or event at Wells Fargo Center for both proximity and satisfaction.
A must stop when in South Philly!! You have to try it at least once in your lifetime!! The steaks are made in front of you and you need to know the lingo wit wiz etc.

My mom and sisters moved down to Charlotte, North Carolina a few years ago and since then every time they come home to visit, I'm forced to go to Pat's for a cheesesteak. I say "forced," but honestly, it's meat, cheese, and bread... there's no need to force me. Pat's is definitely not my favorite cheesesteak in the city, I've had better and I've had much worse. But there's something about the fact that Pat's is a Philadelphia icon that makes my family feel like they've come "home" when they take that first bite.  I've never had a bad cheesesteak here, but I've never had a stellar one either.  Overall, if you're looking for a touristy experience instead of mind-blowing flavor, this is the place to go.

I went on a midnight run to Pat's the other night from New York. It was well worth it. The reason I chose to try Pat's first was because I'm a huge Rocky fan and knowing that Stallone stood there while filming Rocky, I just had to check it out myself. 

The whiz cheese here is pretty damn awesome. The steaks here were pretty juicy and the sandwich itself wasn't as greasy as I expected it to be. Most philly cheesesteak sandwiches I've tried in New York were just drenched in oil. You could barely taste the cheesesteak and bread because of all of the oil, but over here at Pat's, they make it just right.

The service here is off the charts quick. I don't think I ever received a sandwich that fast before. I got my sandwich before I even got my change so if you're in philly, be sure to stop by.

Sub-par at best. Don't waste your time or money. I finally got a chance to try the place and after seeing it on food network and reading it's been around since 1930. I expected it to be clutch! Oh how I was wrong... You can get a better cheese steak at a Subway and that's saying something. The food trucks in Columbus, Ohio put Pat's to shame. "King of steaks" couldn't be farther from reality. I Should have known better and went to Geno's, their line was 3x longer. Live and learn.

The last time I came here was over 10 years ago. I remembered it being amazing. It was a greasy gooey hearty cheesesteak.

I drove an hour and a half from Maryland, dodged several bikers, fought for a parking spot for a mediocre sandwich all because of nostalgia. Damn the member berries!

The cheesesteak wasn't piping hot. The meat felt dry. The seasoning was eh. The cheesesteak at Wells Fargo Center was better than Pat's.

Every time I order food here, they tell me they don't have this or they don't have that. 
I have been here and they tell me that they currently do not have chicken. It baffles me that a popular place like this can not get their stuff in order. All I ever want is chicken wings, about the only thing I can guarantee that Popeyes will always have.

Ever since trying Pat's for the first time, I have been loyal to Geno's.  However, one day, while driving down to Maryland, I was faced with a difficult decision.  On one hand, my beloved Geno's had a massive line that would have taken about 45 minutes to get through.  On the other hand, Pat's stood across the street, with no line at all.

Despite the tough decision, I ended up deciding to give Pat's another shot.  After giving some advice to an out-of-town family on "how to order a cheesesteak," I ordered my own Whiz Without.  Unlike Geno's, Pat's chops their steak up and puts the cheese on top of the meat instead of directly on the roll.  
Unfortunately, this makes the cheesesteak suffer, given that the cheese gets cold quicker and does not stay in liquid format as easily.

While the roll is good and very similar to the ones used at Geno's, I prefer the meat at Geno's, which has a little more fat on it, making it juicier.  I also prefer the slabs of thinly sliced steak, rather than the chopped up steak that Pat's uses.

Although the size of the line can vary, it is usually pretty easy to find parking nearby.  As the originator of the cheesesteak, I will give it credit for inventing one of my favorite foods.  However, their current name takes it a bit far, suggesting being the King of Steaks, which currently should rightfully belong to its cross-street rival, the neon-lighted Geno's.  Nevertheless, this cheesesteak is above average, just not when compared to other Philly locales.


Bread: 8
Cheese: 7
Meat: 7
Price: 5
Overall: 6.5

Pat's all the way!! Did the typical tourist tasting of pat's and Geno's. Had the traditional steaK sandwich and it lived up to its expectations. Make sure to bring cash as they do not accept cards. The line was long but moves quick.

Midnight mini road trip! It took about 2 hours to get to Pat's, good thing it was 24 hours. 

Cheesesteak - The meat was awesome. The bread was perfect. The onions were awesome. The smell was intoxicating.... in a good way.

Cheese - Everyone said that Cheese whiz is the best, but I went for Provolone. It's not as melty and cheesy, so it feels more healthy (as healthy as cheesesteaks can be?)

Gotta come back again....
Tasteless. Bland. Dry. Rude staff. Did not enjoy it one bit. The chain 'Phillys Best' is better.
Worst Taco Bell location ever. 35 people standing in line waiting to pick up orders. Employees are apathetic and ornry. Police chase  your car.

Stopped by to grab some pies for a company event. The manager and staff threw 8 custom pies down like magic. Great selection of toppings, sauce, crusts, and finishing touches like Arugula and olive oil. A defintely spot to frequent. Portions are good and filling, a good buy!

I came to Pat's right after I left Geno's..........after all, it was just a hop, skip, & jump away from each other.............and being that this Hawaii boy made it all the way to Philly for work, by George, I had to have me my Philly cheesesteak sandwiches!!!

Pat's has been around even longer than Geno's, as Pat's King of Steaks was founded in 1930 by Pat Olivieri. He originally sold hot-dogs from a hot-dog stand, but one day decided to make a steak sandwich which caught the eye of one of his loyal customers who was a cabbie............after that, the steak sandwich was born!

Pat's has a similar set up like Geno's.........you go to the ordering counter, & order your sandwich. Please note the ordering sign, as they have instructions on how to order your sandwich to keep the line moving. 
Upon getting your sandwich, there are a few outdoor tables & seats, as this place is basically a grab & go kinda place too.

Upon ordering my sandwich, I got my cheesesteak with onions and American cheese. Just a tip gang.........don't do American cheese..........get the "Whiz" instead, as that's the true way to eat a cheesesteak sandwich. 
I guess I'm not a fan of cheese whiz, and that is why I did the American cheese..........but the American cheese didn't really go too good in the sandwich..............so get da Whiz! No can go wrong!

I liked the fact that Pat's cuts up their meats for their sandwiches...........as the meat tasted less chewy than Geno's, but overall..........it was just okay for me as I've had better at other places.

Loved the history about this place, as Pat's King of Steaks is well know in Philly.

The wait was about an hour long, it wasn't too bad to me since the weather was nice and I was hoping the cheese steak would live up to my expectation. 
I got the one with cheese whiz and mushroom and they were pretty good but I can't believe this was from Philly! I live in TX and I can get the same thing for half the price! I was pretty disappointed but it was nice to have the experience.

Before all else Pat's was our first stop in Philly. We were a bit confused on the ordering--separate window for the sandwiches and drink/fries.
Was sadly disappointed in the cheese-steak. The meat was flavorless--was it just boiled? The bread was hard and slightly stale.
We got the pizza fries and enjoyed those but after eating a few it gets really salty.
Good place to get some local color, but the food was a sad let down, plus quite overpriced.
Not the value I remember growing up, but the flavor is the same.  This place should be half the price of chipotle considering what they serve.  I was starving going in and starving seven bucks later
The fries were really good, just a small fry is big enough for a lunch. The burger wasn't impressive. Tasted just like something I could make at home, and the only cheese option was American.

1. Awesome jukebox selections.

2. Slow, but not unbearably slow, service works to diners' advantage when you're more into hanging out with your friends than you are hungry. 

3. Large order of nachos is enough to feed a family of 10. Get the small.

The food here is pretty awesome American-Mex. Lots of fresh ingredients,  flavorful and comforting all at once. This is what Taco Chulo (Brooklyn) should aspire to.  

I'll definitely go back next time I'm in Philly.

Not overly impressed but decent. On vacation we stopped in to try a Philly Cheesesteak at one of the two famously "battling" shops (Pat's vs. Geno's). I don't like Cheese Wiz so I went for a pizza steak (steak, marinara sauce, 'shrooms, provolone and onions) and it was pretty good. Hubby went for steak, provolone and onions, same verdict, pretty good. Fries were good and fresh.

What cost them points:
1 - I appreciate that they try to put out this "neighborhood joint" vibe by having their own ordering language that they thoughtfully post instructions to where you wait in line and explaining that if you mess up you will have to go to the back of the line and try again. Really? It didn't matter when we were there because there was no one else in line, but I messed up my order. I'd have been pretty bent out of shape if you made me go to the back of any line because I couldn't properly recite your strange lingo.
2 - After the above-mentioned stringent requirement that you hustle and don't waste THEIR time when we moved on to the pick up window the employees were busy playing grab-@$$ with each other instead of getting our fries and drinks for us. Double standard much guys?

Anyway, it was still a decent meal and now that I've checked it off the list next time I'll probably take the advice of family that lives in Philly "Just go into any little old neighborhood place that advertises steaks and you will get a better sandwich, at a better price."

Was overall underwhelmed. Got the provolone wit (Provolone cheesesteak with onions). Also added peppers (see picture), but if I ever took any bites that didn't have enough peppers, I would get very underwhelmed with the lack of flavor. The meat just didn't have enough oomph, and the cheese was just alright. So was the bread. I've had amazing cheesesteak years ago somewhere else in Philly (and this was after I lived in LA, so yes I was picky then too), so I would try somewhere else - but I recommend doing your research as well.

With the choice of Pat's or Geno's, we chose Pat's.  Wrong choice.
Having never been there before, I loved getting yelled at for not knowing how to order.
Staff is a bunch of idiots who think they are kings.  Their snide comments to my daughter made her throw the food and walk away.  Such nerve from little men sitting behind a window.  Avoid at all costs if you have never been there before!

My first proper philly cheese steak was more or less uninspiring.  I may just not be a cheese steak kind of guy but I did not understand the hype.  I could see how this would be great for late night drunk food but those days are past me.  Nonetheless, still a cool atmosphere and I have to commend them on their efficiency.  The line was really long when we got there and I thought it would take at least a half hour to get our food but it only took 10 minutes at most.  Props to a great supply chain model (Yes I just went there!)

I Love McDonald's but not this location. Horrible service. Waited 20 mins for a frickin medium Big Mac . They even forgot my order until I have to remind them that . Never comeback here ever again . I wish I could give 0 start for this location
Very good cheese steaks. If you prefer chicken instead of steak get there early because the run out fast. Great steak sandwich!

My favorite Popeyes in the northeast Philly area. Today me and my family got the 12 piece bonafide chicken meal and a order of popcorn shrimp. We enjoy everything from the shrimps to the chicken to the 2 sides and biscuits. Chicken are spicy and crispy. Biscuits are just right, crunchy outer layer and soft in the inner layer. 

The only 2 downfall is we waited 10 minutes for popcorn shrimp, but they told us three minutes. 10 minutes is a lot when you go through the drive thrus, I wouldn't mind if I was dinning in. Second, I ask for hot sauce, but they gave me none. Didn't feel like to walk inside, so we left without it. I would forgive the long wait if my order is correct
Cheesey Bread was very wet from the oil. Not the hottest hot and ready. I will try one more time.

My visit on June 17th was probably the WORST experience I have ever had at chain restaurant. On an average week I go through a fast food drive through about 5 times and even my worst experience prior to this does not come close to how bad my service was tonight.
     After taking my order at the screen (which did not display my complete order or my total, I was told to pull forward for my total) I pulled up to the first window (which was vacant) and preceded to wait about 5 minutes before someone noticed me, told me my total and took my money...After taking my cash she walked away and didn't come back to the register for another 5 minutes to give me my change (in this time through the window I watched at least 2 separate employees just standing around messing with their phones). Then I pulled up to the second window and the employee gives me the wrong order...I show her my receipt and have to wait at least another 15 minutes for my food (again through the window; witnessing several employees just standing around messing with their smart phones). After I finally got my food and went home to eat it my nuggets were rubber-y and my burger tasted half cooked....I will never again go to this location, I will go out of my way to AVOID this store.

Thanksgiving weekend spent at my aunt and she lives 2 blocks away from Geno and Pat's so the diet was out the door.

A trip to Philly is never complete without a cheesesteak.  
Whiz Wit, Cheese Fries and Birch Beer was all worth $13.75.

The steak were chopped, tender and flavorful.  The grilled onions were cooked just right.  The whiz was thick and oozing.  The bread was warmed by the meat filling and never gotten soggy from the Whiz.  Every bite was heaven and the cheesesteak warmed me up from the windy cold weather.

Forks are for wimps when it comes to the cheese fries.  The fries were drenched with Whiz and it was finger licking good.

Geno's cheese steaks are 50 cents more but nothing comparably to Pat's.  Pat's cheese steaks were longer and heavier.  I want my bang for the buck.

Agreed that Pat's and Geno are tourist traps but I do noticed more local Philadelphians at Pat's than Geno.
Blaze pizza is the best! I'm a student on campus and it's an easy go to. The service is great, pretty quick and consistent in quality. I like that the ingredients are always fresh.

When I came to Philadelphia, I knew I had to try the iconic Pat's cheesesteak. 
I wish I would have looked further!
The price for the portion is absurd. I can pay $7 locally for a much better sandwich that is double the size and stuffed with meat.
The meat wasn't appetizing at all, and a little tough. For the price, I was expecting it to be stuffed with meat, and there was way more bread than meat.
All in all, I think it's a shame that a place like this is lasting on their name alone, rather than the quality of their food. I hope that they start giving customers better portions for what they are charging!

Fresh ingredient - that's all what matters when it comes to Poke bowl. The only reason I took one star off is the portion, I expect a little more fish if I pay $10 for a small bowl, not just more rice or veg.

If this is what your city is known for you need to do better.  

Tried the WIZ Cheesesteak from Geno's so wanted to Try Provolone from Pats.  

$12 for this.  

Don't waste your time go to Wawa instead and get a Cheesesteak - They're 100 times better or go make your own.

First of all, they Locked joint up at 10pm on a Saturday. Are u kidding? Second of all, can't even see the drive through menu because the lights aren't on. y'all want a higher minimum wage so bad but can't even whip up a Big Mac in less than 5 minutes. Also I asked for buffalo sauce and got bbq. Cmon man, the workers put my designated driver in a bad mood so now I'm in a bad mood.

My ONLY complaint about this place is that the steak itself wasn't more tender and was a little rough. The bread, the cheese and the fried onions were PERFECT. If the steak were a little more melt-in-your-mouth tender, this would have been the best cheese steak I've ever had easily. It was thinly sliced in a way that I love but it was a bit of a chew. Other than that it was definitely a good sandwich.

The hubby and I finally took an afternoon to drive into Philadelphia to try a cheese steak at Pat's and we were not disappointed. Half the fun was the excitement of waiting online and ordering for the first time. It was also a nice day and it was fun to sit outside and people watch.   The cheesesteak was very good and we really loved the hot peppers that they freely gave out at the fixings bar.  I'm sure we'll be back!

The best cheesesteak I have ever had. Ive been to Geno's, Jim's, and Steve's as well. Pat's is by far the best one. Their hot sauce is spicy and tasty and pairs really well with the Wiz-wit that I always get. Be sure to read the sign on how to order and bring lots of cash. Their pizza fries are pretty delicious too, if you have room in your stomach for it. $10 for a cheesesteak. I have now been here over 20 times and always keep coming back for more.

It's a steak place I KNOW but ya girl gotta eat too! Okay so I kinda feel bad for giving Pat's a 3 however the other people (who ate meat agreed) I feel like I could only judge them on the fries... Because what I got couldn't be called a sandwich there was like 2 lbs of chopped onion...but seeing that veggie isn't thier thing I feel I'm being fair!.... I was so afraid to ask but when I lookwd over there was a "how to order" sign the last thing was if you mess up don't panic just head to the end of the line...lol so I did...

Jason's Toridasu is a quick, fresh, and reasonably priced option if you're in the City Ave area and in the mood for sushi. I've been here a couple times and the staff is always welcoming. Their menu has a nice selection, and all the sushi I've had has been really good. I'd add one more star if the rice was a little less dry. 

Overall, exceptional sushi for the price and conveniently located if you're in the area.
Quick service, delicious food, and generous portions! However, employees look stuffed in really small space. #givethemair

Located a short walk from the tourist area but through the buzzing streets of the italian quarter Pats King of Steaks appears to be a popular place. Go to the counter and choose what cheese sauce and toppings you want.. like Wit' or Wit'out onions... before you go, google how to order a Philly cheesesteak and give it a go!

Not the best meal I've ever had, but for a tourist.. it's a must! Then go run up the steps at the Met Gallery like Rocky!

Huh? This place should be under "historic monuments" rather than restaurants. I drive all the way from Jersey (long trip, I KNOW) down to South Philly for some chhhhheeeesesteak sandwinches bayee. What I got instead was some beef, canned mushrooms, and cheese wiz on some bread. WHAT?! This MUST be some water-down version of Pat's (and Harry's)  great inventions. 

Still, if you're a visitor, you gotta come see and at least take a picture. Just make sure to order provolone instead of the cheese wiz. 

I don't know how Philadelphians drive because parking SUUUCKS.

Literally just pulled out because i was told you were closed, at 845pm on a monday. Not even just out of samdwiches, you were just closed. Why?? People were inside eating still, so not sure why a bunch of cars were turned away. Terrible tbh. And there is no contact information on your webpage, so to yelp i guess ‍

Drove through the city and decided to stop by for a bite of this highly touted place. You'll have your own opinion of which is best, pats vs geno's, but I prefer pats because of the flavor. A bit more depth to meat and compliments the bread. geno's tasted too frenchy for me. Taste is subjective so stop on by and make your own conclusion =)
The king of steaks is right...  I will always go here before Geno's!  Wit-wiz-witout has always been my go-to, but I've recently been upping my game on the onion situation.  Tasty mo-fos, I tell you.

Over rated. The cheese wiz ruins it for me. You should be able to taste the steak. That processed cheese covers the whole experience of a good cheese steak. Buy yourself 'steak ums' and cheese wiz from a supermarket and save your money. You want a good cheese steak? Try a NewYork Cheese steak! and a NY cheese cake too ;)

The great Philly cheesesteak wars rages on but there's on one originator of it all: Pat's

Geno's cheesesteak is literally right across the road but I had to try originator first being my first visit to philly. 

It was amazing!!! I ordered the cheesesteak with onions and cheese whiz. You can choose without onions or provolone or sharp American cheese. The default is cheese whiz. The greasy melts cheesy mess was amazing as you bite into it and the flavors explodes in your mouth. The savory steak mingles well with the sweet onions and melts cheese all sopped up in the bread. 

The fries were regular. I didn't get it with cheese but will next time. 

Tips:
- CASH ONLY: be sure to bring cash. 
- meal total: cheesesteak with coke and fries will run you $20-$25 depending on extras
- separate lines for cheesesteak and another line for fries and drinks
- limited outdoor seating
- lines are long but moves very quick

Seriously, why do people rate this place so high?  It must be the out of towners that have never had a cheesesteak.  If that's the case, then yes, the cheesesteak sandwich in general is an outstanding work of art.  However, Pats or Genos for that matter, are not even close to the best in the city.

The one thing I will give them is they are open late (24 hours), so if you've been out drinking and partying, this cheesesteak at 4AM will taste awesome.  However, if you are sober and looking for quality, look elsewhere.  The atmosphere is classic South Philly, I'll give them that.  However, the sandwich is overall sub-par.

In my opinion, the best cheesesteak in the city belongs to John's Roast Pork, in fact, they may have 2 or 3 of the best sandwiches in the city.  Their cheesesteak, chicken cheesesteak, roast pork and new roast beef are all dynamite.  Don't waste your time with Pats or Genos, head down to Johns Roast Pork.

Other cheesesteaks that are far better than Pats, in no particular order:

Talk of the Town
Shanks
Chinks
Jim's
Steve's
Tony Luke's
Gooey Louie's
Campo's

You get the drift...there are better options out there.

Cant beat already made pizza when you are in a rush to just eat something quick. They have hot and ready pizza that is always accessible. On this particular day I was feeding a bunch of kiddies who were coming to visit my daughter and have a swim day. This restaurant is a go to for a fast and easy cheap meal. 

The staff is always friendly at this location and do their jobs. They actually are in the back working instead of on their phones like at other Little Caesars locations I have been to. 

The kids enjoyed the pizzas. I think the bread sticks are the only good thing and the price- but my daughter and her friends loved everything!

Stopped in for dinner one night while I was in the area. The outdoor seating is perfect for warmer weather and people watching in Passyunk. We ordered margaritas, chips and guacamole, a wet chicken burrito, and an al pastor burrito. They don't skimp out on food here: the burritos were good sized and they brought out a seemingly endless supply of chips. The guac was fresh, the al pastor was flavorful and the service was quick. I'll definitely be back to try out their brunch menu.

There is no competition. I went to Pat's with my team and votes we're 16-2 Pat's. Meat is juicy and plenty of it, the spicy peppers on the side we're addicting and please, get it wit whiz. Do as the locals do. Fries are amazingly crispy.

Pat's is everything you ever expected of a Philly cheese steak sandwich. I can see how there might be some smaller, lesser known, local establishments that the folks of Philly have hidden elsewhere, but the truth is that I recommend giving Pat's a try at least once.

If we all agree that there are check boxes that must be completed in life, Pat's King of Steaks in definitely on that list. 

I cannot avoid discouraging people from going to the competition, Geno's, across the street. They have begun a bigoted "Speak English" campaign that is insulting. Speak with your dollars, and order in any language you like at Pat's.

I wish I had a site other than Fox News to site:
http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,198757,00.html

We were driving to Boston and stopped over in Philadelphia. This was our second time here. Last time was to NYC. The time was 6:30 am. Hardly anybody there, except some homeless people mumbling random stuff. Luckily we found a parking spot right in front of Pat's. 

This time we compared Mushroom Cheesesteak of Pat's and Geno's. I personally preferred Geno's. Sorry Pat. My wife didn't seem to have a preference. Geno's was more juicy and flavorful to me.

The Cantina offers large portions for reasonable prices.  I've never left without leftovers for a couple of days!  They also have some of the best margarita's around!  I recommend the smoked tofu fajitas.  Yummmm...

Love love philly poke. The staffs are really friendly and you get great poke bowl for a fair price. I like to get salmon bowl with edamame, nori, cucumbers, carrots, red onions, mangos, fish eggs, avocado (extra charge), fried garlic, and pickled ginger. It's a pretty good portion. I'm stuffed after finishing my bowl. For less than $10 can't go wrong. Simple and tasty!

Visiting from out of town. Decided to do a cheesesteak shootout: Pat's vs. Geno's. Geno's smoked Pat's. Identical pepper steaks wit provolone. Almost no peppers on Pat's sandwich, also very greasy. Geno's had better meat (but less of it), and a generous helping of peppers. Neither one is anything special. Both overpriced at $11 and both somewhat disappointing.

Cantina is a cool Mexican restaurant in South Philly that offers a lot of vegetarian and vegan options on the menu. The Cantina has a good selection of drinks, too. There is a bar area, indoor seating area, and a patio outside. 

For the most part, the staff are friendly. I've only had one bad experience in terms of customer service (we were waiting forever for the waitress to take our order, who gave better, friendly service to these two dudes at the table near us). She kept stopping by their table and asking if they wanted water and doting over them, while ignoring us. 

Veggie Menu Items of Note: 
- Quesedia Vegetariana (appetizer)
- Mushroom and Pepper Jack Empenadas (appetizer)
- Tacos or Burritos with either Black Beans, Vegetables, or Vegan Beef 
- Any of the salads

Meh is a good way to describe Pat's cheesesteak.  The $10 cheesesteak with onions and provolone had little seasoning.  The steak was a bit tough and had I not added the onions, would only have been tasting bread.  The bun was cold and the cheese did not melt.  On top of that the side of fries were $5.  Way over priced for a side of fries.  Definitely wouldn't go back for more - nor would I be willing to try anymore.  Surprised that it made #3 on VisitPhilly.com's list of top cheesesteak restaurants.  I suspect that the restaurant is thriving because it is landmark rather than for the quality of it's sandwich.
How can you complain? The service was incredibly fast, it was literally an assembly line. Cheezewiz is a must, forget the other cheeses

For an airport eatery, the employees, service & cleanliness gets the stars. I didn't get any push back when I asked for the Guacamole from the kitchen due to Cheese lingering on the Guac on the assembly line. Plus the employee changed out her gloves before creating my Salad & without me having to request. 

A quick & easy visit.

This is a place to come for a big, greasy, tasty burger and fries. After eating a cheese burger, and splitting a regular fries with someone at 11 am....I wasn't hungry till dinner, and my afternoon snacks are sacred. 

If you're not ready to throw yourself into a meal like that, go somewhere else. 

Also: a burger is actually a double patty and a regular fries is enough for 3 people. I'm a major eater and next time I will go with the mini burger, or whatever they call it.

Nice vibe and friendly service in a trendy neighborhood. But food was not good, not consistent among identical orders at the table -- and with premium prices for simple Mexican food. Group of nine. Pitcher of margarita was OK if you like extreme bitter. Cabillitos burger was too salty and therefore not edible, as were the accompanying fries. Waitress offered to replace it with something else, which was nice, but we didn't have time. Two in our group got the Pollo enchiladas and they were cold in the middle. My fellow guests otherwise dug them. Wouldn't recommend.

I got some breakfast from T&N a while back... I can't remember if it was good or not, but I do remember their home fries being horrible.

I will give T&N another try because of all the high praise from the people below.

I went for curiosity, it was encouraging seeing all the people there. It was the worst sandwich ever!!! Trust me anybody can make it way better.
Little meat, I asked for extra cheese I couldn't find it. The bread was hard and cold. I really don't understand how these people claim to represent Philly's famous sandwich.

I got a salad from here through the Ritual app. So I came here and was very amazed by the fact that it's inside of Walgreens! And I love this Walgreens location, it has everything and maybe a lot more than any other drug store could possibly have. This Freshii place also has sushi! It seems like a friendly place, I saw they have stuff for children as well. The staff including the security guards and walgreen staff were so kind and friendly, gives such a great vibe here. The food ended up tasting delicious! I would definitely come here again for lunch or any other meal. It's a bit far from my job, but I really like their food already. Customizing the salad was easy and nice. Great variety of food and reasonably priced! I'm now excited to try customizing my next meal which will be their bowl. Saw that they also have quinoa and grains, also customizable wraps. They have smoothies/juices, something I'd like to try as well.

Get fried is located in the Bourse food hall right next to the Liberty bell. I came here for lunch on a Friday around 1:30. There was no line and no one behind the counter. I waited a minute or 2 before some came out. I think the guy was working by himself doing the register and the cooking. I ordered the buffalo chicken bowl with no celery and subbed waffle fries instead of tater tots. My bowl was $10 after tax, which is pricey in my opinion. It should have been $8 after tax. My order was ready within 5 minutes. It was really good! They didn't skimp on the toppings. There was plenty of blue cheese crumbles, popcorn chicken bites, sauce, and ranch. It was the perfect amount of food to finish by yourself, but not feel awful about it! This place was good, not amazing, but definitely solid! This would be a great place for a picky eater, as you can choose your own toppings, and who doesn't love fries?!

Sometimes it can be hard to find good wings at a good price. I ordered the lemon pepper and the garlic Parmesan wings! Oh my gosh!!!! Talkin about good eatin!!!! Wings were delivered hot to my door! No spillage, and the delivery man was very polite! Looks like I've found a new wing spot!!!

Take heed and be warned - this place is a tourist trap. Yes, trap! Once you've gotten your philly cheese steak, althlivhw it tastes disgusting you'll feel trapped into eating because you don't want to waste your money or the time you spent waiting on that long line. Do yourself a favor and just make the trek to South Street for better food and options.

I like Pat's over geno's but they are both a little overrated.

the service is quick, even with long lines. I like the way the meat was prepared.

Other than that there isn't anything special about the steaks. I've had better Cheesesteaks with cheese whiz, onions, and mushrooms, that weren't over $10

Just a bad sandwich overall.  I tried Geno's too, and there's not much difference between the two with the exception of the way the meat tasted.  Geno's meat was slightly better than Pat's but Cheese Whiz on any steak sandwich should be a definite faux pas no matter what.
McDonald's on Oxford Ave Fox Chase Pa. I'm 70 yrs old been to McDonald's forever. The sandwich was sloppy and the person at the register was rude. I'll still go to McDonald's but not that one.

For $10 per cheesesteak sandwich, you should expect something pretty decent no matter how famous the place where you get it is. This wasn't the case, though.

The taste was there, but the meat was grotesquely fatty. There was barely any meat among the onion, cheese sauce and the bread. If this was an accident, the "highly skilled" workers there didn't bother to care preventing it from happening to make the sandwich worth at least half its value. Carelessness is the route to disrespect, and vice versa, really.

If you've never been here and you happen to be reading this, you've been warned. No thanks.

Cantina is one of my favorite restaurants in the city. I've been here numerous times, always experiencing great food and service. If you're looking for a refreshing summer cocktail, be sure to try the tangerine margarita. My absolute favorite delicious, vegetarian food option is the Veggie Quesidilla.  Smoky cheese and delicious side sauce make this one a winner! 
Friendly wait staff and the outside seating tent make this a perfect year round dinner and drinks spot. Keep up the delicious work Cantina!!

I come here occasionally to buy dinner for my family. Outside is not good, kind of scary but inside is ok. Food is same as other Popeyes serves. I like Popeyes chickens. The cashier doesn't smile much but they are efficient enough. The line moves relatively quick.

I come here pretty frequently for lunch with my coworkers as my office is a few blocks away and the food is decent.  I'm generally a fan of the burritos although if you request cheese it comes out unmelted more often than not.  I also used to head to Cantina to regroup after work and get some grub and a couple beers (or margaritas) right before I jumped on the subway to many a Phillies game.  I can't tell you how many Friday or Saturday nights I've dragged friends all the way down to East Passyunk from their bubble in Manayunk with Cantina being our initial destination.  With all of that said it's unfortunate that my last experience there is what finally compelled me to write my first yelp review.

I have on two occasions before dealt with some unmentionable digestive consequences that I probably could have pinned to Cantina but was too loyal to admit any direct cause.  Finally this past Thursday I succumbed to the worst case of food poisoning I ever hope to experience after eating there with a coworker.  Both of us became violently ill later in the day after lunch.  I did not sleep that night, and I missed work the following day, and I almost NEVER take a sick day.  I will spare yelpers any details for obvious reasons but I've eaten a lot of food from questionable sources in my lifetime and it takes an awful lot for nausea to get the better of me.  Today is Monday and I've finally eaten my first full meal since I first fell ill, though not without considerable effort.

After ignoring previous warnings I paid the price.  I'd much prefer to use my powers for good rather than evil but I owe it to my body to pan this place.  I'm giving it an extra star for nostalgia and the Holly Golightly on the jukebox, but if I ever return it will surely be for nothing more than bottled beer.

I bought James L. the 1000 Places to See Before You Die book for Christmas so we decided to check off some things in Philly a couple weekends ago. Pat's was in there so we drove over after our trip to the zoo. 

We hardly had to wait on line and waited even shorter for our food. Holy crap, you better know what you want before you get to the window. The first window took about 10 seconds flat to both order and receive our famous cheesesteaks, which were about $9 each (CASH ONLY). Second window has drinks and french fries. (CASH ONLY). It's not like the self-checkout at the supermarket, where the machine says to wait until the baggage area is clear before another customer can use it...once they put out your cheesesteaks you better just throw your change in your pocket, grab your shit and go because you will just be in the way otherwise. 

For the food coming out so fast, it was shocking to find it cold. The bread and outer areas of my cheesesteak were cold, but the middle bottom of my cheesesteak was hot with melty cheese. I have definitely had better cheesesteak in North Jersey that I am now craving just thinking about. 

Btw, I think we witnessed a drug deal go down as we were sitting there eating. Black SUV pulls up and parks. Man comes up and knock on the back window. Hesitation. Man knocks again. Door opens. Man throws the tops of his eaten pepperoncinis at my feet and gets in. Black SUV drives away. So sketch!

Well, Freshii was the surprise of the century for me. Had a coupon so stopped in for lunch yesterday, why not? It's not the easiest to find as it's located inside 1 S. Broad, above Walgreens, and just around the river bend (seriously this place is hidden). Staff were friendly and fast! I ordered the "Umamii" wrap and it was DELICIOUS! So fresh, but also such a unique combination of flavors. I loved it! Would have never thought to come here, but it was so good!

Cheese fries. 

Cheese fries in a paper cup, drenched in ooey, gooey orange wiz. Purely Philadelphia. A plastic fork pokes into them. At first, the fries are crispy, but after a bite or two, they have been absolutely drenched in the cheese. 

Those fries. A bottomless pit. One at a time, but really, 3,4 at a time. Start with just cheese fries. After a minute, relent to the undying thirst for sweet, wonderful ketchup. Drown them in it. Mix the ketchup in. Push the fries down to the bottom of the cup. French Fry cereal. Soggy fries, amazing cheese. 

Two bites per fork full. 

*NOM*

Right across the street from Geno's crap steak, this place is way better.  The bread is more softer, the steak has more flavor than Geno's, and it was just more fulfilling.  

If your heading to Philly and want to try out the famous Cheesesteaks they have there, skip Geno's, go across the street literally and get it from there.

Hands down, Pats is greater than Geno's.
The server "Luke" seemed biased and was horrible.  The food was so so and the neighborhood was gentrified. Nothing to as right!
My favorite Mexican go-to.  Consistency delicious food.  Friendly atmosphere. Hipster service.

Pat's and Geno's are the postcard locations for cheesesteaks in philly.  they give a cool south philly experience and are definitely worth going to look at if you are in town.  The problem is that the cheesesteaks just arent very good.  between the two i would pick geno's but they are at the bottom of the list of cheesesteaks in philadelphia.  

for a better option check out tony lukes on oregon ave. or jim's on south street, either will give you a better cheesesteak and still give you that Philly Cheesesteak feel.  there are also a million corner joints that will make a banging cheesesteak but i live in south philly and when i'm really in the mood i always end up at Tony Luke's.

I have eaten here in the past and for whatever reason was not totally wowed by the food.  As a result, despite my love for margaritas and recent move to the neighborhood, I had not been back here for quite a long time.  This weekend, I had some friends in town who were craving margaritas, so I decided to give it another go.

I was incredibly and pleasantly surprised with the quality of our dinners (and the margs!).  This place does not take reservations, and we arrived Saturday at 8 pm, so we were expecting a long wait.  Although the wait for outside was long, there was a four-top table right by the open front wall, which we snatched right up.  

Our server immediately served us ice water and took our drink orders--traditional and jalapeno margaritas and one beer. We also ordered the guacamole starter.  While we waited for our drinks and guac to arrive, we were served with tortilla chips and two generous bowls of salsa--a garlicky tomatillo and a traditional red with a hint of chipotle.  

The guacomole arrived with another bowl of chips and was definitely excellent--seasoned perfectly with healthy chunks of perfectly ripe avocado.  

For our entrees, a friend and I split the chicken enchiladas and fajitas.  The enchiladas were my favorite--they came in a creamy red sauce and were topped with sour cream.  The chicken in the enchiladas was moist and delicious.  The fajitas were good.  I especially liked the variety of vegetables and other accouterments (like mushrooms) that came with the dish, that while not traditional fajita fare, added to the heartiness of the dish. The fajitas came with more of that delicious guac, but in my opinion (and that of my friend) could have also used some cheese or sour cream.

I will definitely be back again now that I have rediscovered this restaurants.

Bonus:  They paved the outside patio, so you no longer have to navigate through mosquito soaked gravel to enjoy your meal outside on a beautiful day!

(Wow, some reviews are severe on this Chipotle) I was just happy to be able to eat Chipotle one last time before I flew back to my "home and native land", i.e. Canada. Ordered 1 steak burrito for my husband and 1 steak bowl for myself. Both with Guacamole. Loved every bite, and was sad when it was all gone. The staff was friendly. I like the fact there's a Chipotle at the airport. Good job, PHL!
Not worth the visit.  There are definitely better cheese steaks out there.  The meat was super dry and the bread was kinda stale.
Meh, wayyy overrated. Cute shop, lots of great history and pictures...but the food...meh, I'd rather go to Arby's.

Not only was my chicken under cooked, the rude and illiterate cashier was the worst. She was unprofessional and condescending. I ordered chicken tenders and they were not fully cooked. I ripped it in different places to see if it was just a section but all were undercooked! With a nasty attitude and even nastier demeanor she said, "I can't give you your money back." I said, "ma'am I never asked for my money back. I just want it replaced." Now the less then qualified manager came over and said he would give me a replacement. Great right? Nope! He was just as awful as his employee. He took back the replacement because I said I was going to call corporate and report the awful customer service. Stay away! I should have known when I walked in and there wasn't a line at Popeyes during lunch hours. I will be calling corporate and BBB due to them serving undercooked poultry.  


Update: store called me to apologize after I called corporate. Still wouldn't go back but happy that corporate followed through.

Costumer service here is consistently awful.  Many of the female cashiers are discourteous and lack any customer service awareness.  But it's not there fault.  I Blame  POPEYES corporation and management for not investing in more quality employees. And also customer service training for their employees. It's absolutely shameful the way management allows their employees to operate with such ineptitudes. It shows the cultural apathy in which Popeyes corporation AS A WHOLE  operates under. POPEYES, you have proven that you are culturally insensitive and care nothing for your customer base.  OFFICIALLY BOYCOtt!!!

So I ordered food and repeatedly stated that I wanted bacon on my burgers. My total was $37 something. No bacon & I didn't notice until I came home & called them immediately. I spoke to an employee named Lucky, who informed me to come back w/my receipt & they would replace my order. I returned yesterday and a manager w/dreads or braids refused to honor their mistake nor offer to reimburse me stating that I should've came back. Who would return back downtown after driving all the way home? That was the point of me calling when I returned home. Horrible customer service.
Great happy hour spot. I love their margaritas pitcher and chicken fajitas. It does get pretty packed around 5:30-7 so if u want to be seated outside in the summer u should aim to arrive at 5

I will update this later, but let me open with the most important part... there was a fly in my chipotle bowl.

Manager on duty refunded me as if she was doing a me favor.

Do yourself a favor and stick to the Chipotles that you know don't have health inspection issues.

I like it... I've been going here for over 10 years and it's still pretty good. I have to say that my biggest complaint is the price and sometimes the lines can be fairly long. There's also limited parking in the area. In the past couple of years, it appears that it's been geared toward visitors and people not from this area.

The best cheesesteak I have ever had! I am not going to lie, I thought that this place was going to be a gimmick. I was very wrong. I ordered the whiz wit. The cheese wiz was very good, it was not too runny, and it had a good flavor. The onions were also very good and there were plenty of them in the cheesesteak. As far as the steak is concerned, it was flavored to perfection and of course very plentiful. The service was also very fast and efficient. I will definitely be back!

My husband and I are what you call "light weights" in the drinking world. Lets just say after a 6 pack of Mikes Hard Lemonade..things can get pretty wild.

Hey, if it costs us 1/3 as much to get the same amount of wasted as the rest of y'all then SCORE for this married couple! 

So of course Catina Los Caballitos' $20 pitcher of BLOOD ORANGE MARGARITA is a weekend favorite of ours! "Let's get this party started"!

Pair that up with the free WICKED GOOD Chips & Salsa (the best we have ever had at any mexican joint) and a couple orders of Entree's and we are GOOD TO GO!

In all honesty we DON'T just come here to get smashed, the food is good. Not the best and not really authentic (in my opinion) but really good quality and fun new flavors. We prefer this location over the Northern Liberties one because of the laid back crowd and more chill out feeling of this location.

Two thumbs up! :)
Steak with provolone. Cheese fries and a coke. Add Red sauce on steak, Perfect!

I guess sarcasm is not welcomed at Pat's. A little friendly banter between cashier and patron is unacceptable according to Sean. Never have I ever had someone slam a window in my face. I'm all about supporting local business, but this is a total turn off for me. You live in philly, learn how to take a joke and be personable, after all, you work with people all day everyday. I may reconsider going to genos next time.

During my trip to Philly, I sought the best cheesesteak in town.  I understood this was the original, but that does not necessarily make it the best in town.  I tried a number of places, and this was the definite winner.  Not because it was the original, but because it was indeed the best.  I strongly recommend it.

I've been here for an hour or two once but I didn't get anything special. Just ordered a frozen margarita (not a specialty unfortunately) and the chips & salsa. The salsa we were given was really watery. I'm not sure if it is normally served that way but they were pretty sorry. 

I will update my review when I actually order an entree and try their margaritas which they seem to be known for. 

Otherwise, service was fine. I liked the atmosphere, all the seating options and the music.

Wit Wiz!

My REAL Philly Cheese Steak cherry has been popped! What's better than greasy cheese wiz dripping down your arm? Nothing! That's what-- Nothing!

Everyone is right, cheese steaks just don't taste the same anywhere else. I'm thinking it's the bread. Their bread is very distinctive.

I like that they provide cherry peppers as a condiment. You don't find that at many places (at least in Chicago, because Chicagoans can't get enough of fatty giardinera). 

Awesome experience. A definite must for anyone visiting the city of Brotherly Love.

Decided to compare the 2 best known cheesesteak places in Philly. Since Geno's and Pat's are just across from each other, I ordered a cheesesteak from each place with a bottled water and chomped away.

The bread:
-- Bread from Pat's was way too tough/. Not only did I have to bite into the bread, but I had to literally tear the bread in order to take any bites. The bread from Geno's was way easier to tolerate.

The steak:
-- The portion of meat from Geno's was much smaller than Pat's. Also, the meat from Pat's was much more seasoned. I'm not sure if Geno's seasons their meat with anything 'cause it basically tasted like unseasoned roast beef. 

The filling:
-- I got Whiz With (with cheese whiz and with onions) at both places. I liked Geno's onions better, but the whiz was better from Pat's since Geno's was very skimpy on the whiz. The whiz is easily visible on the Pat's cheesesteak, but Geno's put a VERY TINY amount at the bottom of their cheesesteak. I almost went back to ask if they had forgotten to put it on.

The price:
-- It's same at both places. $8.25 for cheesesteak.  ***CASH ONLY***

Service:
-- Service at both locations sucked big time. I guess it's part of the whole "lure" to be rude and even curse at the customers. But I am not into this whole dumb idea of  "Hahhahaa. I just got cursed at at a tourist trap. I can't wait to post it on Facebook and Twitter!"  I still expect people to be nice, especially people who are servicing customers.

Personally, both places sucked. The food wasn't all that bad but it wasn't anything close to what I was expecting. I expected more flavor, more meat, more cheese, and most importantly, more taste.  

It's cool to check out if you are a tourist. Geno's totally had the look of seedy old Las Vegas decor going on.

I went here for happy hour with my friends and we came starving. We were unsure what to expect but pleasantly delighted! If you are able to, sit out on the patio, it has a very cute atmosphere with stringlights and plants lining the outside fence. Unfortunately, there were no happy hour deals on tacos but there were HUGE pitchers of sangria or margaritas for only $16 each. There were 5 people drinking and there was still so much leftover. Complimentary chips w salsa verde and adobo had the right amount of lime and spice from an authentic Mexican place. The chips were fresh and warm, something that is vital when going out to get tacos. They didn't cheap out on the spice so it had the right kick, instead of being toned down for tastebuds that can't handle a little heat.  I ordered the pulled chicken tacos with some sour cream and cheese. And it definitely satisfied any and all cravings I had prior. The chicken seemed to be slow-cooked in a spicy adobo sauce and is apparently a popular choice among other customers. In warm flour tortillas it held together well and the presentation was very nice. The only reservation I had was the service: granted it was happy hour so I'd like to think it is not normally like this. There were huge time gaps whenever we saw our waiter. the biggest gap was when we gave our cards along with the check, and she had disappeared for 40 minutes. We were enjoying our time but we definitely wanted to leave. 4 stars for the service, but the food was good. I definitely would come back here again.
Love me some salmon. Great service and food. Even threw in some free side dishes. Definitely recommend.

Ok - there were 6 of us and we did the "taste test" - Pat's vs Geno's.  It was 5 to 1 in favor of Pat's!  Good crusty bread, tasty chopped steak, lots of Wiz - the right combination.  Fries were okay though.  Save your appetite and just have a cheesesteak - they are large and satisfying.

We went to brunch here at this beautiful Mexican restaurant on a Sunday morning. It was a great sign when we were immediately plied with seemingly limitless chips and dip from the moment we sat down, to when we left to go. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THE VEGAN BOWL ($10!!!) even if you're not vegan, even if you're not vegetarian, even if you think meat is the 8th wonder of the natural world. It came with some spicy rice, beans, seaweed salad, crunchy vegan nuggets, corn, and half an avocado with a drizzle of delicious avocado sauce to top it all off. It was also a huge serving, which I am now recognizing is one of Philly's greatest characteristics -- large and cheap AF brunch servings. Would definitely love to return here for brunch on my next Philly visit.

Really great cheesesteak!! Do the Taste Test: buy a Pat's & a Geno's from across the street to compare. Everyone has a favorite. Locals get it "with wiz" (cheese wiz). Be ready to order when you get up to the counter at both places!! The lines are long, but go by fast! And....they are open 24/7. Do yourself a favor & try this place. A Philly staple!!! CASH ONLY!!!

We took the kids to Philly for the first time and just *had* to get a Philly cheesesteak while there!

Salty but lacking in flavor (even with the onions), we were just not terribly impressed. 

The line was long but we didn't mind that as part of the experience. 

Remember: CASH ONLY

I would give this place zero star. Everything was premade. Bread was tough, steak has been on the grill for quite some time (not fresh) and sloppy. Both Pat & Geno are tourist trap/overrated. All they worry about is how many they sell not quality. For true philly cheese steak go to Reading Terminal Market.

On the seventh day he said "let there be pizza" And from the heavens descended Blaze Pizza upon University city.  Wow, this place RULES! Seriously was just there this evening, sooo stoked to find a place that's open daily until 11pm, LOVE this places hours!  
 This really is a PURE GENIUS concept and I give all the employees a ton of credit for keeping the place running. Got very stoned before I went in, honestly felt obligated to get blazed hence the name blaze and had the pleasure of having Beth provide very positive assistance dressing up the pizza like its going to the prom and a guy named Lil cooking it to ultimate perfection and doing the honors of the Balsamic Drizzle at the end! Yes, they have Balsamic Drizzle as an option and it won over my lonely heart very very fast.  What blew my mind is the unlimited virtually endless possibilities in the pizza toppin department and best of all, they don't charge $1 or $2 for extra toppings or multiple toppings, its all-inclusive with the price, ill get to how great that is later.  
 My thin crust build-a-pizza was so awesome, did ¼ barbeque chicken with grilled onions ,bacon, and more grilled onions and bacon and some grilled garlic cloves and 4 different cheeses, it was all very thrilling and Beth did a terrific job of symmetrical placement on the pie.  Went to the very clean restroom and when I exited the pizza was already fired and ready to eat, very cool how fast the pie cooks.  The pie was delicious, loved the sauce, the cheese was perfect, and they even coated the crust with this amazing sea salt which really takes it to another level.  The combo of grilled onions, bacon, balsamic drizzle, like come on, you wish you were me and you know it.  
 Finally I can't speak enough about how great the price is. Under $10 and you get seeerious value for your dollar.  It's really nice because honestly I have been hurtin financially and unable to afford my all time fav pizza in the city (hint, hint, Birra) and this is such an exceptional alternative since Zavinos $16 pies are way too pricey for what you get and Zestos keeps closing early around 9pm and that sucks and their pizza is decent but nowhere near as great as Blaze.  
Burn baby Burn Blaze, I'll be back and back again and back some more, this place is 100% Mr.Oz approved!

While usually you get a different sandwich depending on the person making it, this location is the best. 

The people who work here don't ever skimp on the ingredients and its always clean inside. 

The only complaint I have heard is that they are too slow and take too much care in making your sub look good...
Pretzels are fabulous and the service was great yesterday!  My co-workers thoroughly enjoyed them.  I will definitely be back!

Too small, and I know that "wiz" is a Philly tradition, but -- seriously, pasteurized processed cheez food on a steak? Real cheese -- Provolone or Mozzarella -- please, 

Try Mama's in Bala Cynwyd. Betcha can't eat one yourself, but tell them to go light on the Mozzarella, or not to cook it into the meat. It's delicious, but since it's real cheese it releases a lot of grease.

What a rude lady working there, I just can't believe it. She refused to take my order just because I was looking at the menu and wasn't ready when she asked me, then when I said I was ready she said in spanish "No me importa" (I don't care) and went to take the order for the next customer.... I just left speechless

I'm from Jersey and these are the best Cheesesteaks hands down. Make sure to get it with wiz.  The free peppers outside are amazing. I dunno why everyone waits in line for genos when this place has no wait and has superior cheesesteaks.

Better than Geno's. Fast and efficient service. Tasty cheesesteak. Not the best in Philly, but still pretty good. Worth going to if you are visiting and want to try a real, good cheesesteak. Found out that lines are short in the middle of winter. Beware of long lines when the weather gets warmer.

I remember visiting Pat's when I toured through Philadelphia last Spring.  Upon seeing this place on the travel channel and hearing about it on countless occasions, I knew I had to try this place along with Geno's Steaks.  Although Pat's is not as boisterous with the multiple signs as Genos, they do offer a very good steak sandwich.  I ordered two "wit whizzes, wit peppas n onions."  Those two did not disappoint at all.  The portions were on par and the flavor with the sandwich was perfect as well.  I chose Pat's over Geno's because of the wider variety of toppings they offer.  My only wish is that they slice their beef the same way Geno's does.  If Geno's offered more toppings, their sandwiches would trump Pat's IMHO.

To begin this place obviously does not believe in customer service haha. The cheesesteak I ordered tasted bland. The meat has like no flavor.. Even the cheese was bland. I mean nacho cheese in a can taste better.. 
Onto the other things, just like everyone else mentioned parking can be difficult. Fries are OK. Area smells like urine...This place did not amaze me one bit.

The food and beverage selection is great. They make a very tender slow roasted goat. The decor is nice. The music is good. The tecate and tequila shot special is a briliiant idea. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this restaurant. 

The problem is that it is crowded as hell, which makes it loud inside, and annoying to even walk past outside, given the tables set about the sidewalk during the warmer months. Sometimes service suffers as a consequence.

As an aside, El Zerape, across the street, is a tasty, genuine and cheap mexican joint, but lacks the decor, music, and gastronomic reach. I'm just saying: options...

Well I'm still new to this whole Yelp thing but here it goes...

Chipotle has always been a mainstay on my commute to and from my job. I usually like to get a big old burrito before I clock in at the lab. TeckQuarp has a very strict policy regarding employees smelling like food upon entering the building and I'm happy to report that I just smell like fresh chicken when I arrive now. 

When I visited Chipotle this morning, I ordered my usual: Fresh chicken and salsa verde... and welp, they delivered. And even with a smile. As I type this, I get excited to stop by tomorrow (or even tonight because I getting hungy as I type this!!!)

Service with a nice smile and free tap water in a to go cup. 

Yes. I'll be back tonight!

There's a reason this place has been around so long. They have the best cheese steaks and hoagies in town. I have been going as long as I can remember. They use great bread and the best meats available. Great family owned spot that real locals go to.  My favorite is the Old Fashioned hoagie.

I had came to philly just to eat at Pat's. It was unfortunately not as delicious as I was expecting. Overall I had felt like the sandwich was missing something and the ingredients did not combine as well as it looks. I had gotten the pepper steak with mushrooms. There was barely any mushrooms and I barely tasted any pepper. Overall if I would come to philly I would want to try a different place to see if I was right about my critique.

Came here super excited to get an original Philly Cheesesteak to recieve a lukewarm Cheesesteak with unmelted cheese and what was undoubtedly canned mushrooms.  Not impressed at all, something must of gone wrong that is definitely not the Cheesesteak I was expecting.
had it years ago .  fun characters behind the counter, got mine wit  and it was really good , may never be a fan of philly but the cheesesteak rules

Going to Philadelphia for the first time, you had to try the two biggest philly cheese steak rivals so I did. Pats vs Geno's. I personally prefer Pat's, the meat was more moist, it was diced, and the wiz was a good consistency. For a super popular tourist spot, the line moved very quickly, it only took about 30 seconds for them to make my sandwhich. They had a little sign with instructions on how to order for "rookies" which I thought was funny. 3 stars because I do feel like this place is over hyped.

I went here with the same reverence I have for Nathan's on Coney Island - a legend. But maybe I just don't 'get' Philly cheesesteaks in general. This was my first time having a cheesesteak - I may have been expecting something like a gyro or Turkish street food - but it was too oily and kind of bland. Still, I enjoyed the scene.

Think it's crazy people gave this anything below 4 stars. This should be (may be) a national landmark! Great cheesesteak that all cheesesteaks should be compared to. We went and had a pats and Genos, preferred the Genos but not because the pats wasn't amazing. I recommend a double taste test as we did!

I love this place. I'm from New York & it was really nice sitting outside enjoying the breeze. The staff is really nice & attentive & the food was amazing. The drinks were good & the ambiance was bomb. I will be coming back again for sure!

Great place!!
Loved it fresh food and great staff.
Try the cheese burger.
Mary was a great server.
We should have listened to our Lyft driver and skipped this place. The cheesesteaks were flavorless and the meat was tough and chewy. The cheese fries were over salted.

Best chipotle I've been too. Very weird to say that in an airport, but it was true.  Very friendly staff, food was good and hot.  Plus it was consistently good - had it flying in and flying out of Phili airport.  Can't say enough about how nice the staff, especially the cashier was both times.  Worth a stop and very affordable for airport food.

Was there today. I guess you have try it at least once and this was my first. Overpriced as any other tourist trap so that was not a surprise.
The cheesesteak is not bad, but nothing special. The beef is mostly bland and chewy, but if you add some salt and ketchup is not bad. Bread is decent.

By the way, they have the process down to a science. It literally took 10 seconds between order and getting two cheesesteaks. These folks make a true fortune judging by the line. Not easy to get a table when its busy.
If you have not tried it i guess you should get it out of your system, but i've had cheesesteaks which where way better than this place.

This is my go to stop for food at PHL airport when I don't have a lot of time. It's conveniently located in the atrium. 

This time, there was almost no line to order which was nice. There was a bit of a line waiting for food, so I probably waited 5-10 minutes to get my food.
