Do NOT uber eats from this place. Twice I received my food cold and later than expected. They let the food sit out even if a carrier hasn't arrived. They could at least cancel the order or wait until a carrier arrives before tossing the order together. Its McDonalds. They can wait until the carrier arrives to insure the food arrives hot considering McDonald's is food you CAN NOT eat cold.
Yummy. How many calories does this thing have again? Holy Shit!

I could only compare this to other fast food joints, like McDonalds and Burger King, but for those who haven't experienced In-n Out, this just doesn't compare. In downtown, there weren't too many restaurants open late, so we liked the convenience of the late hours. It's a decent place for a fast food place.

This place was actually very good. My friend just recently moved to South Philly, and I was surprised to find such a relatively upscale place in the area. I had some suckling pig with a fruit salsa. The waiter said it's one of the best things on the menu. I have never been there before October 7th, 2007, but I can't imagine a whole lot of dishes being better than this.

I'm sure there's a lot of great little places in the area, but if you're looking for just a decent place to get pseudo Mexican, you're probably not gunna go wrong with this place.

Steak wit whiz FTW!  First, I am not going to make any claims to be some kind of cheese steak connoisseur but I always enjoy their steaks here.  Secondly, I've only had Geno's and Pat's many times, so between the two I prefer Pat's.  Just add a little hot sauce, a order of fries, and a Pepsi equals a tasty meal in South Philly anytime!

It was my second time in Philadelphia and the first time I tried...I'm gonna say it...Geno's. I don't remember liking Geno's like I did here. We went to eat after a Phillies game. They're open late which is awesome! We didn't get enough, so we went back the next day. I travelled with three picky kids and each one loved it! It's def a must to have lunch or dinner here!

A Chick-Fil-A located inside of Chicago O'hare, there isn't much different with this location in comparison to the other brick and mortar locations. The biggest downside are the slightly increased prices and that you can't scan your membership to earn rewards. 
Pricing
Slightly higher than a normal brick and mortar Chick-Fil-A, but that's expected from being inside an airport 
Food
Delicious as always. The quality definitely doesn't diminish from it being in an airport
Service
Employees are trained just as well as any other Chick-Fil-A, saying things like "my pleasure" and are just as kind
Overall
Hard to say no to Chick-Fil-A if you're a big fan. When you're hungry and just want to eat something quick (so long as the line isn't too long), Chick-Fil-A is always a great choice.

The first time I came to Philly it was just to have a cheesesteak while passing through, it was cold out so I just grabbed one from Geno's and kept moving and since I didn't have much time to be in the area I only tried theirs, this time around I decided to give Pats a try and I wasn't disappointed, as you may probably already know these places are right across the street from each other and there a few local bars in the area that will let you bring food in so that's what we did, I stood on a long line outside of Pats but I was glad that it moved faster than it seemed it would move, this place is cash only with a few seats outside so really it is a take out place, at the first window you order and pay for your cheesesteak only while the second line is for fries, drinks etc, there are a few options, but I went with one cheesesteak with onions and provolone, one cheesesteak with onions and cheese wiz, I also got fries, everything was really good, it was put together as soon as ordered and I was surprised by how quickly I was finished on that line, the food itself was really good, fries were crispy and not over salted, the cheesesteaks were good, I'm sure I could find a better cheesesteak elsewhere and I've had some really good ones here in NY but going to the original spot was well worth it and I do recommend it

Today is a sad day. Today I ate a Pat's King of Steaks Philly Cheesesteak with Provolone and Fried Onions. And I am sad because I was excited, salivating, and in the end disappointed.

Okay, people will say, its because I didn't get cheese wiz, or because I didn't slather it in hot sauce, or a myriad of other excuses. But at the end of the day, I was saddened because I expected a life changing experience. What I got was something very average. Although I will admit I will definitely try it again (and maybe go to Jim's) 

The meat was very average. I didn't taste any variety of special spices or sauces that its cooked in, just average ground steak pieces. The cheese probably didn't help - I'd say skip provolone because it doesn't add much flavor. The greasy onions just provided some texture, but had obviously been cooking so long on the grill that they had lost all the aroma they could have added to the meats. The bread, on the bright side, was fresh and pretty good, but alas, could not make up for everything else.

What do I wish? I wish I could have had butter spread on the bread. I wish the meat had been seasoned. I wish I had gotten cheese wiz. I wish a bunch of things. But most of all, I wish it would have delivered or at least tried to deliver the high expectations I had for it.

BUT. I will definitely give it a try again. This time, with cheese wiz, mushrooms, onions, hot sauce...all the works - maybe I just need a sensory overload to really experience it.

I have never had a bad steak here. It's definitely my preference over Geno's, and the best in South Philly by far. It's got just the right amount of wiz and onions without being too weighed down or worse, soggy and goopy like Geno's. It's not too fatty but still tasty. 

The employees here are actually NICE, and don't yell at out-of-towners who don't order in the exact way that you're "supposed" to. Once the entire hockey team from the Navy Academy was in line behind me, and so nervous I ended up helping all the team and their coaches order. Pat's had a good time with it, and no one left offended or put-off by rudeness, unlike at Geno's. Pat's is awesome in my book, and I will continue to give them my hard-earned money for a  yummy steak.

NEXT!

When you are in line at Pat's, you will hear this. A lot. This South Philly landmark does not bother with pleasantries. They don't have to.

Read the instructions for ordering. Get in line. Have your money ready. When it came to be our turn, I was sure I would be sent back to the end of the line for using too many words like 'please' and 'thank you' so I left the task of ordering to the expert.  I learned that 'wit wiz' loosely translates to 'hi, can I please have a cheesesteak with grilled onions and cheez wiz?'

And like magic, there it was...  the original cheesesteak I was craving. Soft bread, ample meat & grilled onions and the all-important cheez wiz. It was big. And juicy. Almost too juicy - multiple napkins couldn't help me. Was it the onions?  We will never know. 

I probably horrified those around me with how quickly I finished that sandwich. Don't judge - I was hungry! While it was not the best cheesesteak I have ever enjoyed (believe it or not, that honor resides in Arizona!) it was warm, cheesy and just what I wanted. A perfect end to my Philadelphia weekend.

To be fair I was stoned when I ordered from the window at Pats last night. That being said, two staff members yelled at me for asking where I order fries. When it's not busy, it's just confusing why you have to order at two different windows. the old lady at the counter legit screamed at me when I asked  and then the guy at the fry counter also through a fit when I was confused. Everyone who works here are assholes, and their food is trash. I went for hotdogs, would never waste my money on a steak. They randomly tow people and pretty sure they use to have a sign that stated if you don't speak English we refuse to serve you. Very nice. Go anywhere else, can't believe this place still has a following.

Let me preface this with that I've become determined to travel the US with my husband and do all the things they do on Food Fueds (except Barberton chicken because it's nasty and I can't stomach it.) Philly cheesesteaks has been high on the list and was the main reason we decided to get to Philly. We've done the ones in Cincy and St. Louis, and Philadelphia was next.

After eating Geno's, we googled the results of the Food Fueds, and since Pat's won, decided to grab one to eat on the drive home. We ordered with provolone and onions and cheez wiz and ran back to the warmth of the car because we didn't want to eat outside again.

Upon taking a bite into the sandwich, we both made a face. This was inedible. The meat was really chewy - like chewy to the point I couldn't actually rip through it and spit it out. It lingered in my teeth annoyingly until I got back home two hours later to floss it out. The cheese wasn't melted, the onions were barely there, and the meat was disgusting with way too much fat. But, I wanted to use the 10 dollar sandwiches, so I brought it home to my dogs. My basset hound actually wouldn't eat it, and stared at it for about 10 minutes before the fat corgi tried to steal it from her, in which she ate in one gulp out of fear for losing it. That's how bad it was. My dog didn't even really want to eat it.

Needless to say, not coming back but at least worth it in my food fueds tour.

Look, do yourself a favor and eat here. You will not be disappointed. While this place is very touristy, it's worth it. The steaks are perfect, the toppings are great, and you will be supporting a local landmark. A+++

Because of the location it's an easy "go to" spot. It has a pretty wide range from really good to just OK Mexican food. Some of my favorites are The Brussels Sprout Salad, Eggs Benedict, Mahi Mahi Tacos and the Empanadas. I do feel like this place is at its best when you order from the specials board. I haven't had anything from that part of the menu that wasn't tasty!

I've never had bad service from a bartender, waiter or waitress. Actually, they are surprisingly attentive and friendly. Some (not all) of the hostesses on the other hand are wild. They run around frowning and looking stressed, as if their job was open heart surgery during an earthquake. I've worked in restaurants for years so I understand that it can be hectic, but wow they seriously need to lighten up. 

Bonus points for their Mexican Car Crash, its delicious!

The most overrated, underwhelming crud I've eaten. Subway competes head on with them and that's an insult. I was all excited to go to Pat's. I took a field trip with some friends, we waited for an hour with building anticipation, placed our order according to protocol and waited again. We practically ran over to the picnic tables with our armful of grub. 

We threw it all down on the table and tore into the bag. We each grabbed our order and took a huge bite. Chewed, thought, and each in turn said, "this is it?" We were crushed. Like getting coal in your christmas stocking. I've had better cheesesteaks in NYC by far. We didn't even finish them. The whiz tastes and looks like plastic. The "steak" was chewy and tough. The fries were soggy. No wonder they are angry in Philly. The bread was okay. Their only claim to fame and it stinks. Now they only have the Liberty Bell to chime about. DON'T waste your time. 

The pictures in these reviews are more ghastly than crime scene photos. They should draw chalk outlines around the sandwiches. The only thing I can say that we may have done wrong, we weren't falldown drunk when we went. That may be the problem.

Decided to give this place a try being that I'm always passing to get sushi.

For those looking for health options this is the place 

I ordered satay and you gave the option to add protein which was chicken, tofu falafel and I'm sure more.

I will say being that I'm a fan of peanut sauce I asked for extra and I wanted to stay on the healthy side and asked for beets to be added. 

Customer service was exceptional the person who took the orders down to the male preparing the food was amazing. 

Over all I will be back to try more menu items and will definitely review, I think if you are in the area you should stop by and visit.

They are located on the second floor of Walgreens which is setup with tables and chairs to dine in.

Always great cheesesteaks. I get provolone wit. Amazing quality every time. I went to Geno's once and couldn't believe how skimpy they were with their steak. I've had a steak um that is better. Pat's truly is the king of steaks! Another cool thing about Pat's is if your into authentic throwback jerseys, you will usually find a few people on line wearing vintage Mitchell & Ness jerseys. I usually wear my 1977 Philadelphia 76ers road blue jersey. Everyone loves Doctor J there. I have to go back soon for my cheesesteak fix! Chinks and Delasandro's are great too but there's nothing like a Pat's Cheese steak!

So you brave the South Philly traffic, drive around and around looking for a parking space, stand in a long line forever, but you don't mind a bit because this is going to be an awesome cheesesteak, right?  WRONG!  I could overlook the rudeness of the guy behind the counter, chalking it up to South Philly ambiance, but I can't overlook the fact that I didn't get the extra cheese I ordered and paid for, on a mediocre assembly-line sandwich.  Frankly, I've had better cheesesteaks at chain restaurants in Michigan!  Next time I'll go where the locals go -- to Sonny's, on Market.

I hate this place. Even when it's 3am and I'm absolutely plastered, and somebody else is buying, these are still the worst cheesesteaks I've ever tasted. Or maybe they're the second worst. Between them and Geno's, I don't know which is the worst.

I took a long drive from Virginia to get some Philly cheese steak. Parking was crazy on Saturday night but luckily I found a spot after circling a few times. I tried both Geno's and Pat's cheesesteak. I got the cheese steak whiz at Pat's. It was better than Geno's in my opinion. The cheese was melting just right. The steak was juicy and seasoned well. The peppers in the condiment section went really well with the cheesesteak. The seats were limited. Also, they only accept CASH. There is an ATM but it looks shady so I would recommend to bring your own cash. I would definitely come back for another cheesesteak from Pat's.

The best cheese steak in Philadelphia. Full of meat, cheese , onions and hot peppers. Plus you never know who you will bump into when you are there. It seems that every time i go there I meet someone from the old neighborhood and even people I went to Central High School with or Temple University. You might even meet a celebrity there.

This McDonald's smells horrible. The man at the register is rude and unprofessional. He doesn't know what's on the menu, his talking on his cell while his taking orders. They is always something wrong with the drive through.

With all the buzz around having to try a Philly Cheese steak with a side by comparison of Pat's and Geno's I really had much higher expectations.  

To be honest I've had better cheese steaks not in Philly so the only big difference which people who live in this area seem to really love is the wit wiz option which is basically that nacho cheese whiz filling which you can get at places like 7-Eleven on your nachos or by melting that Velveeta cheese.  Prepare to put on the calories though.

The one thing I really enjoyed about this place over Geno's was their meat, it was more tender and flavorful than Geno's but they could use some better bread.  I think if they took the bread from over at Geno's then they'd put Geno's out of business over time with their quality.

I wouldn't return here in the future, I've had my side by side comparison and satisfied my earning to see what the buzz was/is all about so my experience is complete.

Everything here is ala carte as well, you gotta buy your cheese steak apart from your fries.  It's all cash too so at the end of the day for a combo meal you're paying more than $20 for fast food which is ridiculous.

While sitting here to eat we met some elderly couple from New Jersey that have been coming there for over 50 years, they used to live in Philadelphia a while back but every trip they make to Philly always includes stopping at this place.  This makes me believe this place is like going home to having a home cooked meal, you know the one thing your mom or family member makes which beats everything else.  So in this case Pat's was like eating a home cooked meal by mom for them.

Second time here, love this place. It's all Old Philadelphia mixed with the new inhabitants. Sure, it's touristy, it's also been open for over 50 years for a reason. Order "steak with" for what we know as Philly cheesesteak. I prefer pat's over gene's, but I like geno's bread better. You have to visit at least once, but try both spots.

I had a friend from out of town who insisted on going here.  I warned him this is just a tourist trap.  He said he didn't care just wanted to go for the experience.  Luckily it was the middle of a weekday so we didn't have to wait in line for his completely bone dry nothing of a cheesesteak sandwich.  He was extremely disappointed.  I was nice and didn't say, "I told you so."

I am not a diehard cheesesteak fan, but do suggest the place in Reading Terminal Market.  Cannot remember their name, but the good one.
Awesome food! Awesome service! Love their breakfast! I ordered a delivery and it came hot and delicious in half the time estimated.

It didn't knock my socks off, but it was a solid sandwich with better meat than Geno's. 
After ordering and grabbing your food from the window, you can load up on condiments and peppers at a separate self-serve section, which was a nice touch.

Parking is extremely limited in the neighborhood, so it'd be easiest to have a friend hop out of the car and order the cheesesteaks to-go while you or the driver loops around or makes a temporary stop somewhere. Alternatively, you can just uber here, but there's not much else to do in the area.

I got a cheesesteak wit cheese whiz and I enjoyed it. It wasn't bad but I'm not sure if all this hype between pats and genos fool people into believing they are all as good as they make it out to be. I make this stuff at home all the time and it feel like I make it better. I guess people grow up eating a certain one and have an allegiance to it and it's a fun tradition to have a cheesesteak in Philly. People should try it but the hype makes it more disapointing if anything
You have to go....but I dont think its the best steak sandwhich in Philly.
They had coupons in your weekly circular. Only screen KFC don't really have coupons and they don't have great deals or their food.

This Taco Bell changed my life. My ex wife kicked me out of my apartment and left me for dead on the street. I was wandering for months trying to find any source of happiness in my depression. And then I found it, this Taco Bell. I walked in expecting to have the same old fast food I've always had, but no. This food changed my life. It brought the light back into my eyes, life had color again. This Taco Bell changed my life, it is truly amazing.

gross, dude. i've managed to avoid any brushes with E. Coli thus far, and i'd love to keep it that way. that said, i'll stay across the street, where i can see what's going into my cheese fries, thanks.

I have lived only 15 min outside of Philly for 19 years and it took me 29 years to actually go to Pat's and experience what the world calls a "true philly cheesesteak" - I have to say, it WAS an experience.

Overall, I was a bit overwhelmed.  I have been to Jim's about a million times and I was never overwhelmed.  I was with my cousin who frequents both Pat's and Genos.  Apparently out of the two, Pat's was the one who "cut up the meat" like I like it, more like shredded.  Eh.  It was not really shredded compared to my Philly Phave, Jim's.  It was more like large slices of beef.  The roll, of course, was amazing.  The provolone cheese was not melted, it was literally just placed on the roll, they put the meat on and hand it to you... eh.  The onions were somewhat cold too, like they were cooked, moved to the side of the grill and they took the ones on top that had time to chill.  Eh.

It did not disappoint with the amount of grease though =) The experience is what you have to go here for but I don't see an immediate repeat in my near future.  

The thing that struck me by surprise was the steps to order a cheesesteak.  Who knew?  I know you order what you want but I didn't know there was a specific order to do so.  They were extremely pushy and forward here.

They make fresh juice, and it is not very sweet! (I don't like my drinks too sweet)
They have good quality ingredients and a great service. My favorite is strawberry banana smoothie.

I love chick fil a. I'm from the south and...I love it. BUT these guys at the philly airport forgot the pickles on my chicken sammich. Unacceptable- the damn thing has 3 ingredients! I'm still coming back.

This place was...ok at best. I was down in Philly for a sales meeting for my company and they surprised us by taking us to the famous Pats/Genos. Half of us went to Pat's, half went to Genos. Now, I have had the authentic "Philly steak/cheese" at other places throughout my life in Philly. I was REALLY excited to try the ones that have been on every sandwich show known to man. But it was...mediocre at best. I get it. It's famous, the lines will be long, people will be rushing you, etc. I'm from New England, home of the entitled snobs and people who think the world revolves around them. But the staff at Pat's was very rude. I knew what I wanted, so getting to the window and ordering wasn't a huge deal. But when I went to say my order, instead of listening they did everything else but. So I had to keep repeating my order to them which made them more mad. Well, if you paid attention the first time I wouldn't have to continue to say what I want. So service was terrible. We did get our food quick considering we had about 20 people or so in our party so that wasn't bad. The food itself? Eh. Living in CT, I've had wayyyyy better Philly cheese steaks. There was really no taste to it, I like my bread to have that "toasted" taste and it didn't have that at all, it was more on the soggy/soft side. I was very dissapointed. I didn't get  a chance to try any of my co-workers sandwiches that went to Geno's, but I'll try the next time I'm in the area. Honestly, from my experience, this place is WAY to hyped up. I know it's "famous" and all but famous doesn't mean it's amazing.
Great steak sandwiches, better then their rival across the street.

Zero Stars.......
They are skimping on portion size. Their chicken sandwiches are literally half the standard size .
Not cooked right. No crispy coating and dry. Poor customer  service. Attitudes all day long. Especially the glamanager. Shes too busy with her fake eyelashes. Drove to Street Rd in Bensalem and their sandwiches are the bomb. Exactly made  right. They need to close this franchise on Grant Ave. Horrible.

I refuse to bash Geno's steaks. They are delicious. How ever PAT'S its great also. they have pretty legit fries. Also the fact you can add jalapenos really makes a difference. The steaks are a bit dry, and the cheese isn't really melted. (I've eaten a lot of pat's sandwiches) every time consistently the cheese steaks are dry. The service is slow! How ever it's still a staple in the community. Go ahead and grab a cheese steak for yourself!

I don't know what it is about Chick-Fil-A, but this place is overrated. People talk about it like it's some kind of great thing. It's not.

They have below average fast food chicken. I got the classic friend chicken on a bun. It comes with pickles, and nothing else. There is not even a sauce on it. I had to ask for some on the side, and the options were BBQ, Honey Mustard, Ketch-up and Mayo. I can do better than this at a lot of places.

And, there wafer fries are just okay. They are no McDonald crack addicting type of french fry.

I do not get the big deal about Chick-Fil-A. It's really nothing special.

Yes, I realize I need to go to Tony Luke's for "real cheesesteak", but as a tourist, I have been dying to do a head-to-head comparison of Pat's and Geno's cheesesteaks.  Got the Wit Cheez Whiz.  The steak and onions are finely chopped here and the Cheez Whiz is definitely plentiful.  Bread is nicely toasted.  I give the sandwich only 3 stars because the beef is flavorless.  Next time, I will try Tony Luke's.

This is the first poke I've actually enjoyed outside of Hawaii! I've been to a number of other poke restaurants both in Philly and NYC, and I have to say that Philly Poke is the best in the area. They have a great fish to rice ratio, and they mix the fish and toppings together so that the flavors of the fish, added veggies, and sauce blend together nicely. Also, most of toppings don't cost extra so you can add as many as you like. 

Overall, I would definitely come back here again. The food was delicious and filling, and the staff was super nice. They have onigiri and other Japanese snacks that I'd love to try in the future.

I love this place! Great brunch and dinner. The burritos are huge! There's a goat burrito and it's amazing!!! You would never think it, but goat is really tender and flavorful! The fajitas are big portions. Green salsa is really good too!
Drinks are decent. Good place to go with friends! Definitely gets crowded on weekends!

My husband and I did a split & compared both establishments. If you like the plain taste of meat without any seasoning, then you will like Pat's. I personally like robust flavors, bland is not for me.

I tried this place on a whim one day and just got an order of fries. I fell in love right on the spot.  Since then, I have been back a few times and have never been disappointed in either their fries or their burgers.

I went there today for lunch and I was so blown away by the service, I had to write. I placed my order online like I always do, so that I can just run in and run out. I got there a few minutes earlier than my 12:30 pickup time, so I waited. When 12:40 came, I asked one of the nice ladies behind the counter about it. She didn't have my order but went to check the computer to see what happened.

Well, no one printed off my order, so it was not ready. She apologized a couple of times and because of their error, she gave me an extra burger patty and a free fountain drink! Most places just say they're sorry and leave it at that. I hope that I'm not getting anyone in trouble because of this review, but I just had to say, wow, and they definitely have a repeat customer because of her.

One of the most iconic places for the cheesesteaks in Philly. The line is long, but is moving quickly - just have your money ready. 

Despite the service being quasi-instantaneous, and the place not having any props whatsoever compared to Geno's steaks, the quality is actually good. 

The bread is fresh and crunchy, the steak is actually delicious and the cheese spread is adding quite a lot to the steak.

Overall, I would definitely recommend this place compared to Geno's across the street and a couple of other touristy places that serve cheesesteaks around the town.

So if you are from New York City one will ask if you are a Yankees/Mets fan or root for the Jets/Giants.  But if you are from Philly you are asked "Pat's or Geno's".

Well I have had both countless times and decided on my last trip back east to give each a try.

Once you get sixty miles away from Philly, a cheesesteak is hardly a cheesesteak and it is rarely ever duplicated in Virginia, Iowa, Illinois, Wisconsin, or Minnesota.  I have tried numerous places (I actually hit rock bottom when I went to a Subway for theirs and it was total garbage).

What makes Pat's (and Geno's) are several things.  First is the bun which is made from a local Philadelphia bakery and is tasteful and fresh.  Second is the beef they use which is top quality.  Third is the cheese wiz and onions and you top it with catsup.

The place (well the kitchen area) is very clean and the food is sanitary and of high quality.  The line moves very quick and even if you have to stand in line awhile, it is well worth it.

Many reviewers get it right when they say that you cannot tell the difference between Pat's and Geno's.  But I prefer Pat's for one simple reason.  It was the first place I tried on the Triangle and it never let me down.

If you EVER visit Philly, go to Pat's, Geno's, and if you are in the Italian Market section, stop by Jim's.

I have been to Philly once, and had only one chance for a cheesesteak, and I'm glad it was Pat's.  It was phenomenal, and a memory I've carried with me for the 12 years it has been since I've been.  I hope to be able to go back for an encore soon.

As I entered through the large glass door I was thinking 'wow another big sports player invested in a restaurant, it probably is alright.' To my surprise the service was great and I was addressed by name and the workers were very polite. I was also taken back by the pricing 6.75 for a one topping pizza seems too cheap and when I asked if it was a typo they replied with a startling, "no." Now I thought, time to wait 30 minutes for a personal pizza and by the time I got my sprite it was done, I was amazed. The other thought that went through my mind was 'is it under cooked' and when I saw it I could tell it was well done perfectly. Then started the fun part, taking the first bite. The pepperoni pizza melted in my mouth like a large glass of WaWa chocolate milk (only those who like chocolate mile can relate) anyway, it was fantastic and the thin crust was great. Overall for the price and service I can't recommend another pizza restaurant.

Compared to other cheesteak spots out here I think it is not all it is hyped up to be. It's not bad though. I just find it to be very average and overpriced. If one is in this vicinity I recommend going to Cosmi's for cheesesteaks and other hoagies.

been here a couple of times, im never taking a philly visitor here ro anywhere near the commercialized steak joints. the first time i ate here was way back when i came to philly I thought it was good, my friends meh...it didnt taste like a cheesesteak as i knew it then so much as a roastbeef sandwich as they didnt chop it up much and I recall the visit as it was cold as balls and there was portions of meat cooking individually then. been back a few times since and it really is no bettter than most steak shops in town with or without a rep, the curse of these tourist traps is teh pile-o-meat. they got a line, gotta get that money but its basically a boiled/steamed chopped beef by then which makes it flavorless and stringy, the bread has no texture or snap, chese is bulk block from restaurant depot else whatever wiz is made of... i got tired of steaks as it was regular cheap eats during school(really great lunch trucks on campus then), but "John's Roast Pork" and Georges Sandwich shop fill my cravings when they come up.
Only gripe about pats is the size of the cheese steak but after trying pats and Geno's I'm a  pats guy for sure !!! The whiz onion and pepper steak ! Had me with the first bite

Popeyes Store 11202
Jan. 25, 2017 6 PM

Manager waited on me this was the worst Popeyes I have ever ordered food from, chicken awful as were biscuits (undercooked) ! Won't be back! 
Only thing decent was cole slaw.
They suck really hardNot being harsh or anything but I'm vegan I don't like it wait what

I do not like cheeseteak, and not only did this place change my mind but it let me have 2 cheeses for no extra cost. I recently moved to Philadelphia and as a new local it is a rule to got to Pats, but i do have to do the pats genos challenge...Maybe next time

The pizza was very good and decently priced (considering I got two meals out of it). Although the pie is considered an individual portion in terms of size, I only finished half of my pizza and packed the rest home. 

My roommate and I will definitely come back to Blaze!
Well, I'm glad we had  Geno's first because Pat's blows it out of the water!  Much better steak, MORE steak, and all around better experience!  Pat's is the king!

I hadn't had a 2AM cheesesteak in a LONG time.  Had a friend downtown for the night so we went ahead.  Man, is that a great sandwich when your hammered on Tecate...  That's the only reason for the 3 stars.  As usual it was expensive and the service was rude.  And had I been in my right mind, and fully aware of the mess that I was shoving in my face, there's no way i could have given it above 1 star...  But, I was drunk.

This was the first stop in my cheese steak tour of Philly (Pat's-Geno's-Jim's in one night).  I made the mistake of fumbling my order and got called out by the cashier.  Maybe I over-prepared for the moment.  But the ribbing was in good fun - just part of the experience.  

The cheese steak with wiz was delicious.  It's easy to see why this place spawned so many imitators.  As good as it was though, I'd have to rank it 2nd on the list to Jim's that night.  But if you're actually on Passyunk deciding between Pat's and Geno's - go to Pat's.  Geno's comes a distant 3rd - not even close.

I wanted this to be more than just the experience, but alas everyone is right. The sandwhich is fine, but definitely not great. It sat in my stomach for quite a few hours. We barely waited at all, which was nice, and I can at least say I have been there.

A guilty pleasure. Sure its not healthy but it sure is good. When indulging yourself in this type of artery clogging feast you know what your getting yourself into when you walk in the door. I was beyond satisfied with my cheeseburger  piled high with free toppings and a cherry coke passing on the fries. You can only take these things in doses and skimping on the fries made me feel less guilty.  The real treat here are the hot dogs. MMMM!!! I

While on vacation I surveyed locals to receive their local recommendations for Steak Sandwiches. Oh my! Was I beyond happy they recommended Pat's. Service was quick, staff was witty and funny. I love that they have a plaque telling you were Rocky once stood. Mostly the food was delicious! I often think about this place when I'm wanting a steak sandwich and cheese fries. Wish I could teleport there! Yum!

If you're not from the East Coast (as I am not) this cheesesteak may surprise you, since you've probably never had a "real" cheesesteak.

I've been here 3 times now, so know what to expect: long lines any time of day, limited seating, and no containers for ketchup for the fries. You order and pay for your steak at one window (get it "wit onions") and get your fries and drink at the next window.

It's just fun to bring new people here just so they can say they ate here. Parking can be a bit of a chore, but that's just Philly.
The same as Genos. I wish Pat's had more flashy lights and propaganda. The line here is sometimes shorter than Genos. I wish they gave you more meat. But its ok.

First time ever. Did the Pat's Geno's challenge. Pat's wins
Here is why
The bead was great
The meat was tender and chopped up nicely. 
Just the right amount of wiz
Food handlers wore gloves
Looked cleaner.

Next time it's Pat's vs. Jim's

What's to love about Chipotle in Center City?

 - space
 - signage
 - ingredients
 - staff

The space is beautiful. A row of tables bisects the restaurant vertically allowing for two paths: to and from the counter. There are also stools overlooking Walnut Street and a wood-paneled booth. It has high ceilings and gets plenty of light. For such a narrow space, it is efficiently arranged.

The signage is simple and clear. You may choose from tacos, burritos and several different types of meats. The first sign states the local, organic, sustainable nature of the meats available: a huge selling point. 

The staff are knowledgeable, accommodating, yet still fast. I told them that I was allergic to lime, and they immediately confirmed with the manager which dishes had lime and what I my options were. There is lime in the rice, guacamole, corn, and all variants of beans. 

I went with the carnitas (pulled-pork) tacos on soft shells with lettuce and spicy salsa. The pulled pork was juicy and tasty, and the spicy salsa was flavorful yet not too hot. The soft taco shells were also moist.

Overall, the space is beautiful and the food is tasty, quality, and cheap. Solid.
Best cheesesteak EVER! This place is the best, old school, very cozy. Hot peppers on the side , was an awesome idea. Highly recommended.

Love their burgers. My usual toppings are: lettuce, pickles, tomatoes, grilled onions, jalapeno peppers, hot sauce. The fries portion is huge and I can never finished. The burgers are made super fast without compromising the quality. You can't help but be happy even knowing you are a few pounds fatter after having their burgers. So worth it!
Love the cheesesteaks here! The steak is not dry and everything is just absolutely perfect!

Fast service and quality food! Definitely recommend downloading their app, and earning points with every visit (new feature). Also, right near a Starbucks if you need that caffeine kick after the burrito sleepiness kicks in. Pro tip: order ahead via the Chipotle app to skip the line, they do get VERY busy during rush meal times (especially lunchtime during the work week).
The sandwich was cold with a slice of unmelted provolone cheese. Quite a disappointment.  It was also very dry.

I'm going to give it a solid 4, order it right and Damn it's good. Add the ketchup, mayo, salt and pepper and that red sauce if you like spicy. I ordered an extra, wit provolone and added the goods. Also had it side by side with geno's

So, apparently I've been eating Philly cheesesteaks all wrong my entire life. It was good! We got the basic cheese whiz and it was delicious! You HAVE to eat it fresh. We tried saving some for our plane ride and it was a no go just FYI for all of my travel bugs

First time here, so we decided to compare Geno's and Pat's.  We ordered a mushroom steak with wiz from both places and did a direct comparison.  Overall, I preferred Pat's but it was pretty close.  I thought Pat's had a much nicer roll, and the meat was cooked much better than the one at Geno's.  My main critique is that I wish there was more cheese, because overall it was pretty dry and I didn't get cheese with every bite.  Oh and btw their cheese fries are bomb here so I highly recommend you get those.  And just a tip, be sure you know what you're ordering when you get to the window, cause they ain't waiting for ya haha.  But dag are they efficient here, as soon as you get your change back your cheesesteak is waiting for you fresh off the grill.  So to sum it up, I give Pat's the old town crown over Geno's.  But they're so close might as well try both!

The thing I looked forward to most when moving to Philly for grad school was the cheesesteaks. And what better place to go than to the "King of Steaks." On our little tour, they told us that this is the home of the cheesesteak. And I must admit, I am quite disappointed. 

The cheesesteak has everything I love...steak, cheese, grilled onions, bread. And I usually love my cheesesteaks. What can go wrong? Pat's cheesesteak tastes...okay. It wasn't amazing. Very greasy. The bread was also a little chewy? Luckily, I split one with a friend or else I would have felt terrible afterwards. I think it was so overhyped that it only led me to disappointment. I do love the fast and efficient service although a bit overwhelming.

I visted Pat's King of Steaks after reading and hearing about the hype from friends who have been there. The place is accross the steak from their competitor Geno's. Both places had long lines but because I heard Pat's was better, i lined up. I waited in line for 5 minutes. I missed the crowd by fives minutes. I was there around 1 pm. Once you order, It reminded me of the Soup Nazi scene from Seinfeld. You have to get your cash ready (they only accept cash and tell you to borrow from friends if you don't have any) and know what you want. If you want to take your time, don't get in line. Then you get your cheesesteak instantly after you pay. Maybe because I had high expectations but the cheesesteak was not that good. The meat was dry and over-cooked. The soda I ordered was water down. I was lucky enough to find seats after a few minutes but for most people, there was no place to sit down and enjoy your cheesesteak. Overall, I have experienced better cheesesteak in nyc. It was a good first experience but not a cheesesteak I would drive from nyc to philadelphia to try. In fact, I like Carl's Steak and Charley's better.

DON'T BELIEVE ALL THESE 1 AND 2 STAR REVIEWS!!! 

It's worth the hype. It's what a cheese steak is supposed to taste like. For all  you WIMPS out there - Do you have a cell phone??? Then you can look up the proper way to order the goddamn thing so it won't be so "stressful." It's very simple: you tell them what you want, you pay, they get it for you. They don't give a shit if you don't use the correct "wiz-wit, wiz-witout" lingo. If you want an amazing authentic Philly cheese steak then go to Pat's. It's better than Geno's, but they're very similar. Pat's has more meat. Open 24 hours, you can't beat it.

I consider myself to not be as picky and critical when it comes to food, but for a spot that's gotten a lot of visits/reviews... I didn't think this was very good.

My party ordered off uber eats, and they FORGOT putting the cheese on all the cheesesteaks we ordered with cheese, except the Pizza Steak. Unfortunately, the meat didn't seem to be very good quality, and didn't have the flavor I was expecting from such a well-known place. The bread also seemed like it was hastily prepared. 

It's really unfortunate that I couldn't find a good quality cheesesteak during my visit to Philly. And dare I say, I'm not sure that one even exists with the atmosphere and lack of attention to detail with a lot of cheesesteak places I've passed by here.

I took a Friend there who wanted to try the Philly cheesesteak. We got a few mushroom steaks with cheese. The line was pretty short that day, the cashier just wants you to pay for your order and move on to the other customer. You need to know what you need in advance before ordering. The location was not too crowded that day.
I ate a lot of cheesesteak from the various vendors in Philly and frankly I was not impress by the sandwiches. It didn't have that cheesy flavor I was looking for, and the mushroom didn't look so fresh and their fries were acceptable. There is no free parking, but street parking, so plans accordingly. I wish I could give them 3-4 stars but when it comes to food or product quality that where my 2 stars go in this case I was not impressed by the food, I will give it another try and see.

It's a chain and it's tasty, what more do you want?

This Chipotle has really mastered the art of fast, healthier food.  If you walk into this Chipotle (I pronounce it chih-pot-tull) and you see a line reaching to the door, don't fret.  You will be at the front in about 5-7 minutes.  They have an assembly line working back there and they know how to move a crowd.

I go for the veggie burrito bowl.  With the veggie option, you get the guacamole (pronounced wack-a-mohl) for free.  If you want it as a topping, it's going to cost you a couple bucks.  It's pretty easy to keep vegan too which is the normal route I go.  It's under 9 bucks and it doesn't leave you hungry mid afternoon.

In the fast food world, I think Chipotull is winning and I'll continue to support them.

Pat's over Geno's by a small crapy margin!!!!
FML for having to taste Geno's then to Pat's!!!
The meat had more falvor than Geno's but really by not much.  Same cardboard texture with a bit more spices..  If I were to be deserted in Philly and Pat's and Geno's were then only two places open (what a nightmare), I would have to eat at Pat's...
Btw, if you ever need a plastic knife to cut your sandwich into smaller pieces for whatever reason, make sure to take your own from home because the idiot cashier will not help you out..  
The point:  avoid this place just like you avoided Geno's; they both suck big time and their fake so called rivalry has added to their good for nothing fame.

eh. whatever.

good margaritas paired with the whitest mexican food this side of taco bell.

During our road trip (east coast) we chose to stop by Philladelphia PA for a BIG BUS TOUR, as a tradition we have to do lunch on a famous dinner. We asked to officer where is the best place for a philly cheese-steak ! to places were recommended but as we arrived the Pat's was the most clean and nice place. Not the best for experience for rockie customer -cashier was rushing us. BUT the food, was DAMN WOW ! the pizza fries spectacular !!! The sandwich (3 different ones) We ordered and the split in 3 to try it all.  Sadly no restroom for customer. Two separates window to order (one for sandwiches / other one for sides). Only Cash (funny sign).
This place is ok but not everything its cracked up to be. This is a tourist spot but not good quality cheesesteaks in my opinion.
This is a must have Poke experience!GREAT food,GREAT customer service and awesome price!I'm a Philly Poke Junky for Life!

Its more hype than anything else. Workers kinda rude like you're bothering them when ordering. Speed is key, I absolutely agree and understand that, but at the same time I heard them be not so friendly to several customers like they were being bothered by people ordering. Its just a freakin cheesesteak.....stop acting like its life or death.

simple Sunday afternoon drive thru with 9 year old grandson turned into racial confrontation by "manager" black woman in Muslim black head covering

said I had failed to order two shakes, just ordered one saying she didn't like my attitude 
wanted to refuse service rather than handing me food ordered, trying to force a cash refund, 
finally younger worker handed food already bagged over but no receipt

When realized my grandson hadn't gotten his chicken nuggets, we came through to reorder
only to have them lock windows and refuse service until we had cars backed up in drive thru 

finally they handed over ten chicken nuggets (no receipt) 

To complain to HQ you need receipt #‼

I think something is seriously wrong with anyone that gave this place more than 1 or 2 stars.  The men behind the counter are very nice and the bread was nice, soft and chewy, just the way I like it.  That's really the only good things I can say.  I wanted to like Pats, I really did.  I came down from NYC with a friend for a quick getaway to Philly and couldn't wait to go Pats to try the original and boy was I disappointed.  Both cheesesteaks (my friend's and mine) were fatty, and dry to the point that no amount of cheese whiz could save.  This is what everyone's ranting and raving about!!! Dry meat in good bread!!!  I make a better cheesesteak at home!!!  Total waste of time and money!!
Forget brioche, kobe beef and foie gras toppings. Five Guys serves up a solid burger without the pretension or high price tag. If you've got a craving for a burger-to-go, this is the spot.

I'm sorry to be so blunt and negative to start out, but--Pat's is trash. This was my third visit to Philadelphia and my first time trying Pat's. I usually go with Geno's, but this time I decided to try Pat's to see how the two compare.

It's not even close. I ordered a cheesesteak with whiz without onions (a whiz without). It might not have had the chunks of onions the cheesesteaks with onions have, but there was definitely a strong taste of onions in the meat. It was vile. Apparently, they don't use separate grills or clean the grills very well. When I say without, I mean WITHOUT! The quality of meat and bread was also subpar to Geno's. 

I also got an order of cheese fries. Again, they were incredibly lackluster compared to Geno's. They give you almost half the amount of fries as Geno's and the quality is not nearly as good.

If all of that wasn't enough, their prices are also $1.00 higher than Geno's! It was $11.00 instead of $10.00 for the cheesesteak and $6.00 instead of $5.00 for the cheese fries. Now, I typically wouldn't blink an eye at a dollar, but it makes a big deal when I'm paying more for a lot less quality. In the future, it will ONLY be Geno's for me!

This place is good for going with a group of you aren't really hungry or if your not a picky eater. The menu is often a little too exotic for my unrefined palate. That's to say: I'm a picky water and usually end up with a boring cheese quesadilla because everything else was made fresh this morning so you have to take it with chicken or mushrooms or tongue.

had my first pat's about 25 years ago and I still love it every time I eat it.  I took away a star because the last time I was there they changed their ice from delicious crushed to cubes.  not a fan of the change.

I can't remember when I last ordered drive-through food when they didn't ask me to park and wait.  When they finally do bring the food out - 10 minutes later - the handoff is done so fast that I've nearly dropped the food. This restaurant is poorly run and service staff are poorly trained

I'm not going to lie, I typically would not write a review for fast food restaurant however, first time I've ate at a Taco Bell in many years. This place has the best employees. Not only are they cleaning in depth, wearing all their appropriate hairnets on their beard and hair, greeting customers with the other customer specs and details. No lie I would recruit every single one of them

The service sucks. The guy that took my order the past 2 times acted like he was too good for anyone.

The meat isn't good. The bread isn't good. The cheese is okay. The fries were hard..

People only eat here for the name.

shit steaks, total tourist trap.  go anywhere else literally any food truck can do a solid one they're really not that hard. if you buy steakums,cheese and long rolls from any supermarket add your desired toppings and already youre more qualified to sell WHAT IS APPARENTLY THE ONLY CULTURAL EXPORT OF THIS GREAT CITY!!!! then those assholes.
Trashy tourist fun, but it's an interesting neighborhood with history and good nearby bars and you get a good sloppy sandwich out of it. Ignore the haters and head on down at least once.

Sure it's a tourist trap and there are better steaks in Philly but Pats still make a helluva good cheesesteak. The ordering process is obnoxious if you're not from the order so pay close attention to others as they order.
I like five guys but my friend will not go there again. It was like $20 for 2 cheeseburgers and fries. The soda was extra also.

I just couldn't leave Philly without a cheesesteak! I heard this was the place to go and it sure was. Got a CheeseSteak wit (onions), mushrooms, and provolone cheese. Everything was perfect except for the mushrooms - honestly they tasted canned. While I'm no cheesesteak connoisseur, I generally know food. Meat had just the right amount of grease, cheese was melty, roll was super fresh and the onions had great flavor.

The best part? We went for an early lunch and beat the crowd. Found a spot right in front and got our food in literally 60 seconds! Must visit while in Philly.

*They're open 24/7, CASH ONLY

Very rude and gave me a sandwich with whiz before I even specified which type of cheese I wanted. When I asked if this was the only type of cheese available they lied to my face and said yes. Overall the sandwich was alright but I definitely prefer the service and sandwiches at Genos's across the street

For an outdoor cheesesteak dive, I'm absolutely 100% impressed. Fast service and delicious products. A little pricey, but it's Philadelphia, so that's kind of expected. The cheesesteaks are dynamite, the best I've ever eaten.

Be advised that the only places to sit are outside picnic tables. The location isn't bad though, and you're right next to the Italian Market!

Pat's or Geno's? Of course I had to do the Cheesesteak challenge. I have to go with Geno's! Pat's was great, lots of meat, just right on the Whiz... sadly not enough onions (could barely taste them) and bread was soggy. Pat's was a little more on the the salty side and the meat, well tasted like meat. It was a hit or miss for me, but I had to see what all the hype was about!

We went here late night after a concert and it hit the spot!!  Who doesn't love a cheesesteak?  Being from NY, we asked our PA/South Jersey friends should we do Geno's or Pat's and we got a unanimous Pat's because of their bread. I was totally stressed out about ordering because everyone before me (mind you it was all guys and I was the only girl) had the lingo down "pat." Wiz Wit, blah blah blah so when I got up there and stumbled on my words and then forgot to tell them I wanted them to go I got some stares.  BUT the cheesesteak was absolutely delish!  Best one in Philly that we had by far!
I love their margaritas.  Food is good too, sometimes the service is good, but that's hit-or-miss.

Drove from New York just for some Pat's and worth every minute.

Will definitely be back soon. 

Of all the spots, this is it. Most locals will agree.

My Husband went across the street from Geno's after I was disappointed on the hype of the "Philly Cheese Steak Sandwich", well I was so happy he thought to buy another sandwich at "Pat's King of steaks" Yummy!!!!! Finally, I knew what everyone was taking about! this place is the KING. I LOVE IT. This California girl recommends this place to anyone who is visiting philly.

**parking is tough and sitting is outdoors**

worth it!

If you buy a Pat's Cheesesteak, expect to get overcooked pieces of flavourless meat in a soggy bun.  I'm glad I came with a friend -- we shared one sandwich between us, so I didn't have to eat more than half the steak.  (I feel bad about wasting food.)

If you're looking for an overpriced cheesesteak for the sake of doing the tourist thing in Philly, this is THE place to go, assuming you'd rather not support overtly racist establishments (which you can find across the street).

The cheesesteak here is phenomenal. I couldn't believe how different it was from every other cheesesteak I've ever had. Also, being that I haven't had a cheesesteak in a while, it made it hit the spot even more. The line was really long, but we did get fed with 20 minutes or so, and standing out in the street on the line was pretty neat too. The historical sign out front makes this place the clear choice. They also give free cherry peppers with the condiments, so be sure to try a few of those too on the house. I'd drive out here from NY just for that any time.

Tourist trap for sure.

Food is mediore at best.  I can find a better philly cheesesteak at the mall.  

I would strongly suggest not going here or to Geno's across the street.  

It's uber expensive.  Not enough meat.  Too much bread.  Lacked flavor.

If you must go, definitely go to Pat's, skip Geno's!

my 1st time. even tho EVERYONE i know has been here a million times. was walking from work and it started to pour. my friend and i ducked in. it was crowed with lots of dudes. the girl behind the bar was weeded, but handlin' her business.
i normally dont go to places where i dont know any staff.  the reason is killing 2 birds with one stone, or 3? 
i want to have a good time
i want to throw a "play" to friends
and i dont want to wait for a drink. 
so when i saw this girl waiting on everyone. i thought to myself... "maybe standing in the rain is better"
but then she looked at us, told me she'll be right with me. and everything was good. 
should have gotten her name. but she has short blond hair, and calls everyone 'sweetheart". all we wanted was to sit, after a long, successful day. get a drink. and keep dry. thanks for making it exactly what we needed!
decor was cheesy cute. total pirate ship. (at least this night). and noisy. but we were the only people in the room.

So we tried Geno's and Pat's. Pat's is marginally better just because they give a tiny bit more meat (or maybe the bread is just smaller). Either way, the meat is still flavorless and the bread tastes day old. These two restaurants are meant to be rivals but it taste like they get their meat and bread from the same frozen food distributor. Don't fall into the trap. Go elsewhere....and I don't mean Geno's.

Like its N. Libs sister restaurant this is not the place to go for a quality Mexican meal, however if you're looking to get your drink on with some margaritas in a festive environment, than you can't go wrong.. Tasty margaritas which will get you liquored up in no time flat..

From the outside Cantina, with its adobe-esque walls and bright orange paintjob, looks like it will be a pinnacle of trendiness. Unfortunately it fails to deliver once you step inside, instead simply serving up a heaping portion of mediocrity. It seems entirely satisfied with catering to the beer hungry college crowd and cigarette smoking tattooed hipsters who want a place to sit around looking self-important.

My partner and I swung in yesterday afternoon for a reasonably priced meal. I'm not going to lie and say the food wasn't tasty; it was tasty food. It was really EXACTLY what I was looking for, because I had been bitching all morning that I was dying for a salad with grilled chicken.

We both ordered the tortilla salad with grilled chicken and I ordered a side of yuca puree. The major disappointment with the salad was that it was tiny. It was essentially a side salad, and it didn't appear that there were any option for a salad entree. To be fair, the waiter warned us because I asked if they could substitute the black beans with extra tomato and he said no because it was so small to begin with ;)

It was, however, tasty, and for the $2.00 add-on it was a pretty freakin' huge amount of chicken! I also found the salsa and salsa verde that were served very good, though I prefer my salsas to be mild and the complaint here seems to be that they aren't spicy enough.

What I didn't like was the sort of ongoing air of hipster superiority that the staff has. Here's a tip to the managers of Cantina: you can have a bunch of funky servers in their 20's with tattoos, piercings and feauxhawks without treating everyone like crap! At one point our server had another person bring out my tea refill and I got a mouthfull of what I thought was dissolved coffeegrounds. They CLAIMED they accidentally brought me iced coffee, but...let's just say that I actually wondered if they did it on purpose to screw with me because they had such bad attitudes to begin with.

So the bottom line for us was - tasty food at a reasonable price but an atmosphere so unpleasant that we probably won't head back.

BTW: our total meal: 2 Tortilla salads (small!,) 1 side of mashed yuca and 1 ice tea for $21.40 including tax.
Order it right.... dont hold up the line... people will get pissed.... it's a landmark for years....so you have to go... but I know a better place for steaks on South....read the review....

A BIT OVER HYPED..AND GENO'S..BUT IF YOUR IN PHILLY..I GUESS THESE ARE THE PLACES TO COME AND SEE for tourist..MY BAD.wasn't that good..my philly friends laughed at us when i told then that we went to try pat's and geno's...lololol..just was not good!! sorry.
OVER HYPED BY TV (FOOD NET)...ONE MORE THING MAKE SURE YOU CAN READ AND SPEAK ENGLISH!!!lololololoolololollol TO ORDER.

This is my 3rd time going here. They messed up my order order 2/3 times. 1st time i ordered pasta and asked for alfredo but received marinara (I did enjoy it though). 2nd time my pasta came in clumps and received undercooked meatballs. Quality of the food was good the 2/3 times. Staff was friendly and the amount of food you get for the price is pretty reasonable.

As a frequent patron of Cantina Dos Segundos, I was well prepared for expectations with food and ambiance. The parking is a bit of a crap shoot with East Passayunk, but we were able to find free parking a block or two away.

Right away, you are hit with the strewn christmas lights and dark atmosphere.  Normally I like it, but it felt a bit too dark for 5PM on a Friday night.  One of my favorite things about the "Cantina" establishments is the Happy Hour.  They employ half-off margarita pitchers.  We got a pitcher of frozen margarita for $17.  This got us close to 4 margaritas each between my gf and I.

First off I have to say I'm obsessed with their salsa verde, it's my favorite in the city.  I was pretty much full by the time my food came.  I borderline need help.

I ordered the pork carnitas tacos with pico de gallo and guac.  It came with 3 tacos and the tacos were overflowing with meat and guac.  This is how tacos should be.  You will never go home hungry or sober from this place.  Well done Cantina, well done.

Of course I'll go back, but Dos Segundos is much easier to get to due to the parking situation.

Every time I am in this Popeye's I am greeted with a smile, receive excellent customer service and delicious food. I came for is the CHICKEN. It is the best chicken around this area. I give the chicken 5 stars.

Pat's steaks are good and honestly all are starting to taste the same to me, but I'm going to have to favor the racist Geno's steaks over Pat's because Geno's isn't chopped up the way Pat's is. Same order format... Whiz wit for me please.

I definitely choose the northeast's location of Steve's Prince of Steaks. The center city location needs to perfect theirs. Seriously.

When i went there was a very short line luckily! Waited for about 5 minutes and ended up ordering a cheesesteak with american cheese (yum!). Fries were good ($5) and they have coke products. Overall, a must do while in Philly.

So Pats runs number 3 in the Cheesesteak world in my book, definitely much better than their main competitor across the street!  The meat I think is much more leaner and tender than most of the competitors.  Its one of those places that if your visiting the Philly area you gotta check out at least once.

Pat's cheesesteaks are really delicious (coming from someone who doesn't really like cheesesteaks thats saying something)

I've come here on many occasion, may it be after a long night of drinking or just for dinner with a group of friends. i have also stood in line while wearing flip flops during the dead of winter because my friends dragged me out of bed to grab something to eat.

this is definitely a place that i tell people who are visiting from out of town to go to if they haven't had a real philly cheesesteak.

Packed on a friday night. a half hour wait. got a drinks down the street instead and came back. just in time. the atmosphere gets 5 stars. definitely a fun place to go. the service was quick. waitress attentive. bathrooms clean. margheritas, is that how it's spelled, were good. 6-8 glasses per pitcher. salad was diappointing but the vegetarian quesadilla was great. mahi mahi tacos pretty good for not being from a real mexican place. on the verge of 4 stars. i just hate heavy crowds.

First trip ever to Philly, so we had to try the cheesesteaks! We tried both Pat's and Geno's, and got fries from both as well. I ordered a cheesesteak without onions. I LOVED the cheese, it was like a sauce and had such a good flavor. However, I preferred the steak in the Geno's sandwich, it had less gristle and fat than the Pat's sandwich. But the Oat's sandwich had the best flavor with the cheese sauce, which I did not get in my Geno's cheesesteak. The fries were super tasty, I preferred them over the Geno's fries (although the portion is smaller than Geno's and more expensive). Luckily when we went the line was short and the service was quick! Keep in mind they only take cash!! Overall a good experience and I'm not a steak lover!

Been here a few times.

I'm all man but I'm not afraid to say I'm a huge fan of the frozen margarita, hold the salt nonsense though of course.

I'm somewhat newer to the city and still trying to get my bearings as to where I am when out in the city because no matter where we are after dinner the first thing I say is "are we close to the Cantina?". Cant get enough of them.

I'd try the food here but that would waste valuable margarita space in the tummy.

Went tonight and was sorely disappointed.  Service was bad enough to make me lose my appetite and the food didn't help.  I used to come here for half price margaritas, we would just fill up on free chips and salsa, and we would STILL get moderately friendly service.  Now?  We didn't skimp on the food or drinks and the service was downright RUDE.  Our order for a pitcher of mojitos was messed up twice, the server would disappear for forty minutes at a time and then refuse to wait three seconds as we tried to pay the bill.  Mahi mahi tacos = gross.  I was hoping for that creamy, drippy, cilantro sour cream that is typically draped on fish tacos, but instead got glops of sour cream straight from the carton, along with what looked like the pre-shredded cheddar cheese from Acme.  The fish didn't taste fresh either, and there were no veggies in sight.  The chips are amazing and the drinks are fabulous, but honestly, the bad attitudes at this place are not worth it.

The employees at this Chipotle are nice and attentive. When so went into the Chipotle, there was no one in there except people that have already ordered and seated. By the time I was about to exit the line, the line had extended far back to half the room! It gets very busy during the lunch hour. Most of the time, you can get in and out fairly quickly. 
My only issue with this location was the serving sizes. When ordering my bowl, they would only put on scoop of rice and then shake it to even it out. This would give the appearance that the entire bottom of the bowl is filled with rice. I just kindly asked for more and they seemed to be okay with giving more.

On my recent trip to Philly, after hearing all the hype about Pat's vs. Genos, I decided I would have my own taste test. I wanted to get the most out of both meals, so I had Pat's one night and then Geno's the following night. 

Frankly, I can't believe there is a controversy here. Pat's is hands down the best of these two Philly icons. The deciding factor - the chopped meat. It was not only easier to eat, but had better flavor and taste. 

Sorry Geno's, Pat's is the tops in my book.

As an aside, what a tourist trap. For all the lights and glitter at both of these place, the service is mediocre at best and they make you feel like an ass with the whole Wit and Wiz nonsense. If you're going to charge me $10 for a sandwich, at least make me feel like you're happy I'm there to give you my hard earned money.
They're not bad at all, but, even when it comes to cheesefries...I prefer Geno's. That's just me though; take it or leave it,

For such a famous place there's nothing to write home about. Personally, I rather stay in Princeton and get Hoagie Haven's cheese steak. The meat is not as good as Pat's. But if you think about it, I drove this far, waited in a line that wrapped around the block. It better be good. The food is plain. No taste at all. 

The people there were not that friendly. I do understand that the reason is because line is so long. 

Haven't gone to the place across the street. Someone mention to try the Chicken Cheese Steak. Might try it when I pass this place next time.

I got the cheese steak wit wiz.  Haven't eaten at Geno's yet so can't compare the two.  But, I would say this was a pretty good cheese steak.  Compared to Jim's on 4th street, which is also one of the more well known cheese steak places, I noticed Pat's uses more cheese.  Who doesn't like more cheese?  Wasn't able to taste the onions as much though.  The meat was cut up into manageable slices which was also good.  Went at 10 PM on a Tuesday and had not line which was great.  Also appreciate the pepper bar that they have available.  In my opinion I'd have to say possibly the best cheese steak I've had in Philly so far.

I'm always excited to find new places that sell gluten free pizza!  I love the set up of this restaurant, and how easy and cheap it is to customize the pizza however you'd like.  I've been trying different combinations and enjoying everything I get.  Service is quick and friendly.  I am really excited to keep eating here!

Great area and pretty good cheesesteaks! I got a steak with American cheese and without onions. The lines move fast, and you get your food quick. The only problem is that the steaks are a bit greasy, but overall I believe Pat's steaks are better then Geno's. Good steaks!

I've been going to Pat's since I was a kid.  There's really no need to even bother trying Geno's.  The ONLY way to get a proper Philly cheesesteak from Pat's is with Whiz... none of that provolone nonsense.  Can't wait to have one on my visit to Philly.  I've been in California for way too long!  Oh, and the cheese fries are amazing along with a hot chocolate in the winter to keep your hands warm.

If you are looking for the best philly around, then you must check Pat's out. The parking is near impossible to find so you may need to plan on doing some walking, but it will be worth it. 

The bread is perfect and combined with great tasting meat and cheese you can not go wrong. This is not the type of sandwich you can eat in your car on the go. It is filled up so much that it will fall everywhere. 

They also have some cherry peppers on the condiment stand, but be careful because some of them can be extremely spicy!
I like it a lot better than Gino's! Steak was tastier!
Excellent brunch! And like most places, the earlier the better.

I tried the other place across the street, so it was time to give this one a try and it was a whole lot better. No nonsense and to the frigin' point with Pat's. Again, a late night venture that had me standing in a super long line, but I had my beer with me to keep me company. I got to the window, place my order and got it PDQ. The meat was tender and juicy, whiz is just what it is; Whiz but the grilled onions and peppers really makes it pop. There isn't a place to sit since it was so packed, so I sat on the curb like everyone else, popped open another beer and enjoyed my night. I'll opt to come back here next time in Philly.

I will be the first to admit that tourists suck, and generally so do the places they go to, but this place rocked. 

When visiting Philadelphia one must have a cheesesteak.  A friend who lives nearby suggested Pat's over Geno's.  We went on a Saturday night after a Phillie's game which may have been part of the issue, because the line stretched around 3 of the 4 blocks that Pat's encompasses.  The back of the line was dangerously close to touching the front of the line.  But most people were in Phillie's gear, and if its good enough for locals, its good enough for me.

The ordering system is no nonsense, like the soup nazi of sandwiches, which I happened to like because it kept things moving.  My sandwich was in my hand about 2.1 seconds after I finished ordering.  Really the only problem was that the seating is really hard to come by.  The only bench we could find sat amongst the hoards of hungry people behind us in line and we had to consume messy sandwiches while people stared at our food, mouths watering (just as we had done before them).

Also, its super small so there's no bathroom and my gf had to sneak into a bar and me into a shady laundromat nearby.  

But the meat was perfectly seasoned, the bread was delicious, but I should have gone with the cheese-whiz.  In situations like this it is best to release all pretensions.  Onions also added flavor.  Overall a great sandwich and a night well spent.

This place is all hype. After hearing so much about the famous Pat's and Geno's, our group of out-of-towners trudged to this dirty and dodgy part of Philly for some reputedly delicious cheese steaks. And it is convenient if you'd like to sample them both at the same time to see which is better, cos they are right across from one another.

The cheesesteaks are huge. But they just taste average. NOT WORTH our trouble looking for this place- it;s quite far from everything else.
Seriously, just go to Jim's Steak on South Street.

And the people here are not friendly. And NO BATHROOMS! I needed to go pretty badly and NONE of the shops around here would let me use theirs. how rude. (hence the 1 star)NEVER coming back.

The food is unremarkable. I'm not sure it even qualifies as iconic. If this is Philadelphia's version of a Tommy Burger, you'd be better off saving your craving for a Tommy Burger (Beverly and Rampart in Los Angeles) or a French dip from Philippe's also in Los Angeles. Two clearly better iconic food stops on the American national scene. 

If the drive is too far to Los Angeles, just drive to Conshohocken to Ponti's steaks. The carbone cheesesteak is drool-worthy.
I'm a fan of Checker's not so much of the speed of the service. But the food is so good I always go back. This particular location is 5 stars all the way...yes including speed of service as well.

Ah Cantina... Since they have opened, this establishment has taken a bit of a dive in service and quality.  While it occupies prime real-estate in the Passyunk Square neighborhood, it is prone to long waits for a table, long waits for service once you have a table, and lesser quality food and drinks as the years have passed.

I agree with several others who have stated that they would have given this place 5 starts three years ago.  Christine H. even stated "Every time I return I leave less satisfied than the time before. " - which is another statement I would second.  

The redeeming quality of Cantina is its large outdoor seating area.  It is perfect in the summertime. The jukebox and bathroom chalkboards are a nice touch as well.

If you are making the trek for Cantina, I would suggest trying some of the other fine mexican establishments in Northern Liberties over this one.  It is also very loud.  If you are looking for a quieter mexican establishment - look elsewhere.

Pretty good cheesesteaks.... It's a little dirtier on the outside than Geno's but had more traffic it seemed... Well at 1120pm at least.  Cheese wiz fries and cheesesteaks were actually tasty but 2 bucks for a water was hella steep, especially since it was off brand water... Oh well service was ok the young folks there were quick to get orders out.  It's more of a 3.5 than 3 though.

This place is very overrated! I have had many cheesesteaks in my life and this is probably one of the most weakest one of all. The ones the sell at the California malls taste better than this stuff. Cheese whiz really? For a city that claims to be the home of cheesesteaks this was a pretty disappointing experience.

Of the 2 Im a Pat's fan, I usually eat pizza steak's and geno's doesn't have any variety.  Other places are higher on the list for cheesesteak's but will walk over to get one of these when people are visiting

We decided to pit the two cheese steaks against each other! Pats was first. Be advised it's CASH ONLY. After coming from NYC we walked around the corner to a bank to retrieve cash and back to the window to get a sandwich with onions and cheese wiz!  
The bread is toasty but soft. The meat chopped. Just enough cheese. It's gonna be tough to beat this!! 


(By the way this was our winner)

Touristy, but I was a tourist, so that was OK. Great cheesesteak, with cheez-wiz, and I'd go there again. The neighborhood looks a little run down, but finding a cab there and back from our downtown hotel was not a problem, and it was perfectly safe.
Totally over rated. Nothing special about this cheesesteak. People behind the counter were pushy and impatient. I was anxious by the time I got my over priced steak sandwich and fries.

The menu is very small and the restaurant was very loud. I felt like the music was too loud and in turn people were speaking extra loud to compensate. That being said, the was good. I wouldn't call it authentic Mexican, but it's certainly one take on Mexican. I ordered a burrito which was good, nothing super specially to say about it though. The chips and salsa were my favorite part of the meal! I have heard that once the weather is warming and they open up the tent seating outside, the overall ambiance is much nicer and good for dinner with friends where you can actually have a good conversation.

Philly steak was average, nothing special to it. Horrible customer service. Cashier was extremely rude...I was looking forward to it so much and sadly was disappointed because of the cashier's negative behavior. Will never go there again. Their competitor Geno's had surprisingly better customer service and their philly steak was much better in taste.

I had been on the hunt for a great burrito in the Philly area, read a lot of reviews and finally decided to give Caballitos a try. It. Was. Fantastic!

It was easy to find, parking was very easy on the street, and we sat down without a wait (on a friday night), even though it was pretty crowded.

We were seated/greeted right away and had chips and salsa within about a minute of sitting down. The service was great. Our waiter was attentive without being annoying.

We both got the prickly pear margaritas, which I thought were really great. Not too sweet, and just strong enough. 

On to the burrito.
It was great. I was expecting, hoping, wishing, for a California style burrito that I had been so craving and this delivered to the T. I got the Carnitas, which was cooked perfectly and the flavor was delicious. Although you do have to order all the "extras" on your burrito (sour cream, cheese, guac, jalapenos), I didn't mind that. It let's me get the burrito just as I like it.

I almost had a mini panic attack when I reached for hot sauce and they only had Tapatio -- I'm a cholula fanatic. But we ended up swapping it with a table across from us for a bottle of cholula. 

I loved the energetic vibe of not only the restaurant but the surrounding area. I'll definitely be going back!

I was there today at 1130am getting some food. Ordered a sub and the guy doesn't ask if I wanted it toasted even though I did. Then one of the wall menus fell to the ground which is a representation of this subway location..anyways, he then picks up the sign with his gloves and then proceeds to start handling my sub and puts my toppings on my sub.  Like come on, you kidding me. I wish I was a food inspector so I could fire him right then and there.  I asked him to change the gloves and he said no no it's fine.  I said dude, no I dont want to get sick from that. He made me another sub like a little beep and wasn't very nice about it.  Wont be going there ever again.  Wasting my hard earned money for that bs..forget that.

My girlfriend and I love T&N.  Seriously awesome old school south Philly charm here plus a delicious gourmet undertone.

The restaurant is tiny and charming with a lunch counter and a few booths.  Super clean and really nicely decorated and my favorite... NO TV!
