Huge old school Philly menu with THE BEST HOAGIE I'VE HAD IN PHILLY. Seriously OLD SCHOOL ITALIAN DONE RIGHT!  The Roast Pork with Broccoli Raab is killer and any kind of meatball will make you very happy. 

T&N is an unassuming little brick south philly restaurant but inside is an experimental and overachieving gourmet heart.  Here's where things get fun and a little different:

La Colombe coffee on the counter.
Deep fried Alfredo bites
Gourmet Tater Tots
Crab fries.... With Real Sweet Crab in it!
THE BEST WINGS... Gettem cowboy style.

I first discovered T&N when we hired them to cater a film and have been going back ever since.  I would have never known if not for that chance encounter and I just can't say enough good things about them...  I've seen the kitchen, I've inspected their ingredients, they've fed the pickiest palates in the film industry take the time to visit this out of the way spot and fall back in love with all your Philly Favorites and try something a little different.  You won't regret it.

Oh and the catering is affordable, dependable and sublime.  They can handle any request, believe me; I had them jumping through ridiculous hoops every day for weeks while working on a feature film and they went to any length to keep everyone happy.

You won't regret it.

Great pretzels for low prices. A bit of a strange location, stuck in the back of a warehouse type building with an almost unmarked door, but other than that its great. Also, their hot mustard is HOT HOT HOT, so buyer beware.  Love IT

Much better than Geno's.

Order an Extra with Wiz and Mushrooms.

No credit cards and no frills.  Come in winter and freeze your balls off.

In all honesty I've had better cheesesteaks before but you need to come and try the original just so you can call yourself an enlightened human being.

I'm not surprised that one of the most iconic single-location food destinations in America has garnered three stars.

Here's the logic: We're the locals, and you're a buncha stupid tourists. This gives us license to be enormous fucking douchebags, charge way too much for our food, and give you a pretty freakin' small, not particularly amazing cheesesteak.

I've seriously had better cheesesteaks in Norwich, Connecticut.

Boom. Said it. Come at me.

Pizza fries were whatever. Great, so you took some SYSCO fries, poured wiz and lousy tomato sauce on it, and charged $6 or something.

Philly has some nice things. Lots of history, some GREAT pubs, sports teams that get beaten by the New York teams constantly. But this whole cheesesteak battle is nonsense. A white elephant, an albatross... a dud.

This was my first visit to any Blaze and I will be back! I designed my own pizza with the help of the server. I was very impressed with the speed. My pizza came out in less than 5 minutes. And it was so delicious! Next time I will try different toppings just for the experience. Service was friendly and efficient

Certainly not the best or most authentic Mexican food, but really good nonetheless. I have had plenty of great meals there and never a really bad one. I always get margaritas, so I don't really have any thoughts about them getting rid of the tequila/tecate special, but I can definitely see why people are upset about it. 

This one is far superior than Dos Segundos, both food and drink wise. Margaritas are delicious. Chorizo tacos, also delicious. And most importantly, the nachos are second only to the POPE.

I ate Pats and Genos back to back within 10 minutes for lunch and definitely prefer the Pats vibe and grub.

The smaller of the two, they focused on making the meats so tender they fell apart and added plenty of cheese wiz. They also had these little black peppers that went perfectly to add a kick and the cherry peppers helped cut through some of the richness of the cheesesteak.

I'm sad to say that Holly Moore's updated review was spot on. Pats has gone down hill. I was there on Sat. night 11/9 and even though there was a line, I noticed that the line at Geno's was much longer. Anyway my buddy and I decided to stay at Pat's, what a mistake. We ordered our sandwiches and I ordered two to bring back to Brooklyn. The one I ate there was just alright and had much less meat than the sandwich I had 4 months ago, one of those that I took home was full of gristle and not the small pieces that you sometimes find but big chunks of it throughout the sandwich. So much so that I had to disassemble the sandwich to eat it . Sorry Pat's but you get a big fail.
Better than Geno's! Same price same type of service but the cheesesteak had more flavor and came with more cheese whiz.  Hooray for Pat's King of Steak!

I am currently in five guys waiting for food for my boyfriend. I heard they were recently closed but he said they were back open so I decided to pick up food for him. When I showed up to order they told me they were cash only which I was unaware of - per my boyfriend they were never cash only before. I decided to go get my own dinner, stop at the Atm and come back to get his. When I came back there was a sign posted on the door that stated "closed for medical issues." As I was standing at the door the entire staff laughed at me when they realized I was the girl who had gone to the ATM to get money and by the time I came back they were closed. Eventually, when the staff was done laughing they let me in and I was able to place my order and pay with cash. They told me my order would be under the name "ATM." I just can't understand how an entire restaurant staff could suddenly come down with medical issues forcing the entire restaurant to close early. In addition the mockery of the staff was seriously unappreciated. It doesn't surprise me that this location was recently closed as they are so inconsistent. You can definitely find a better burger and fries in center city that is more consistent and respectful to their customers.

The cheesesteak was pretty delicious despite the fact it took a quick minute to make it. Make sure to ask them for some melted yellow cheese and go to the condiments table and grab those big red chili peppers because it brings an even better taste to the cheesesteak.

Best Cheesesteak in Philly hands down (and WAAAY better than Geno's in my opinion). In my 10 days in Philly for "work" i tried cheesesteak from about 10 different locations. THe first place I went to when I arrived in PHilly was Pat's and the last place I went to before flying back from PHilly was Pat's. I can't wait until my next business trip. I haven't had a cheesesteak in cali since.

As epic cheesesteak quests go, Pat's is definitely a prime destination.  No, the subs are not life-altering.  A big part of the appeal is in the "I've eaten there" experience.  But as famous cheesesteak places go, Pat's is top-notch.  The meat is as good or better than what you'll get across the street at Gino's or wherever else.  The cheese whiz is delicious whether slathered over meat or fries.  Etc.

Depending on when you go, there may be a line, but not for lack of effort on their part to keep things moving.  Don't get cute with your order, or even fumble around with your wallet.  Just be ready when you step up to complete the transaction, or you'll get a glare or, even worse, a sarcastic zinger.  Like I said, it's an experience.

Sooooo good. I really like their philly cheese stake sandwich!! juicy and cheap :D

There is a long line to get, but it didn't take much time to be my turn. It was kind of hard to get a seat because there were so many people waiting for seats to be opened. 

Actually, it's not a healthy food. But if you don't care about it, here is one of the places to try when you visit to Philly.
There is no doubt that the best philly cheesesteaks come from Philly. It was hard trying to decide which one to go to but we decided on this one. How amazing is this place. It just mouth-watering.

Every time I watch some travel channel show that lists Pats as "The" place to go in Philadelphia to get a cheesesteak, wait.... let me re-phrase that, to get the best cheesesteak, I want to laugh. I remember the first time I ever had one. My father took me there when I was 14. Even at that young age I knew that this was something greasy and disgusting. The only reason I choked it down and smiled is because my dad thought that he was doing something really nice for me. 

So, ok it's been a lot of years since then and since my husband and I just happened to be in the area we thought, well why not. My best advice is, don't go. Save yourself and just don't do it. It's actually worse than I remember it.

Wasn't hot Cheese didn't  melt
Dry
No seasoning 
New to Philly cheese stakes but had better
Far from being the king

This is the real deal.  The very best in Philadelphia.  Don't go anywhere near Geno's for a "Taste Test" comparison--Geno's is awful and management is bigoted.  Go straight to the less flashier corner for the true First Cheesesteak.

Great steak sandwich! Visited on October 9, 2018. If your looking for an authentic philly steak sandwich this is the place to go. If you're picky and want to compare buy 1 here and look across the street and get 1 from Genos and do a taste test yourself. Outdoor seating. Parking is limited but we were able to find a spot to park for 20 minutes while we ate.

You must be kidding me.  THE famous cheese steak I've always heard about?  I've had better at most pizza joints in central Pa.  I hate to say it, being a lifelong Pa. resident, but I've had much better cheese steaks at at least 5 places in Manhattan.  I love cheese steaks, and this was a dry disappointment.  I had a cheese steak with provolone and "wit" onions.  I've made better with Steak Ums.  I was going to compare to Geno's across the street but I lost my appetite.
Worst cheesesteak I've ever had. Cold sandwich. Canned mushrooms. Long line. Not worth the hype.

Almost as bad as Geno's.  Again, I don't get how aplace like this is popular.

Meat is dry and bland.  Not as dry as geno's, but still dry.  The bread is bad.  Almost stale.  Knda cheap with meat.  Not friendly at all and you walk up afraid of messing up your order.  Seriously?  Afraid to order?  Come on guys.

I guess it's a tourist trap -- and it's working for them.  Somehow people are still coming here to eat.  For what reason, I'm not sure.

Stopped at Pat's on my way out of Philly this past weekend. Parking is scarce so plan to spend a few minutes finding a spot. 

There were only a few people in line because it was like 11:00am.  Got right up and ordered a Wiz wit out aka my favorite.  It's $11 which is a little high but I rarely ever get to Philly post college days so it's worth it. 

The steak is very tasty and not fatty, and although I find it gross in other ways... cheese wiz complements the steak so well. 

Pat's is always solid, although I did have an issue with a soda being $3.50 despite the sign saying thank so and so for raising the price on sodas. I had just gotten one for $2 at the Reading Terminal Market the day before so $3.50 is a bit of a stretch but they can do it because you're gonna buy it. 

Pro tip: you order your sandwich at the first window and fries/drinks at the second window. You pay separately and CASH ONLY!

Horrible staff.   My cheesesteak was cold and had no flavor.  When I said something the skinny guy with the horrible beard became rude and obnoxious.   I will NEVER EVER go there again.   Plus they don't use gloves, hair nets or beard nets.  Go elsewhere. Over priced and super rude staff.

This was the original Philly cheesesteak we expected. Great flavor of the beef, lots of cheese whiz, great soft bread and  lots of sweet onions that gave the sandwich a great flavor and crunch. It was awesome! We will definetly return and recommend this place to all our family and friends.

Have you ever smelled fresh baked bread? I mean really fresh, not wonder bread in a toaster. That's what it smells like as you pull up to this unassuming warehouse. You have to search for the door (its toward the back of the lot) and once you find it you feel kind of strange standing in a.... well locker room. Knock on the door or ring the bell and shortly after someone appears and asks what you want. Well what ever you think you want;  Get More. Be kind and get a few for friends or they may take yours. At this price you can afford it. If you get there at the right time and the pretzels are right off the line they are the most amazing thing you'll ever eat. It is unlike any pretzel you can get anywhere else. THIS IS WHAT A PRETZEL SHOULD BE!!!
horrible service, horrible food, greasy! bland! waste of $, def a waste of time, you'll get chips and dip then are expected to wait hours for your meal

Stopped by to grab a fruit smoothie despite the weather to fill my hungry stomach. I am on a business trip, so I was not much aware of the some of the other stores that sell healthy food. But this smoothie place had a variety of options that you can pick and blend to meet your taste, which I found to be very suiting. I had Super Squeeze and to say the very least, it was at par with other brand name smoothie places, if not much better. It was quick, convenient and satisfying. 
Not so sure about all the bad reviews, but as a foreigner visiting from out of town, the drink tasted good, and it filled me up very nicely.
Mediocre at best! Everyone knows Tony's beats it out! But for tourists...why not? A little competition never hurt anyone...

I thought this place was great! I've only been to Philadelphia once for less than a day, so I didn't get to try as many cheesesteak places as I wanted (but that just gives me a reason to go back). 
CHEESE WHIZ. It's a must. Don't mess up and order a different kind of cheese. You'll not be happy, and go back up to order the whiz on it. A little pricey, but I guess it's due to it having a name behind the restaurant. 
No inside seating. 
Cash only.
better than eurocentric geno's, but still ehh

Well, the food is delicious, but the hipster staff standoffish attitude I can do without.

We waited about 45 minutes as the bar for a table.  The bartender ignored us for a least 10 minutes before we got a drink, and believe me, we tried to get their attention.

When seated, we ordered a pitcher of house margaritas to split.  After the mojito I had at the bar and half of a margarita pitcher, I wasn't even a little buzzed.  I'm guessing they skimp on alcohol.

The chips and salsa are wonderful, the green salsa is the best I've had in a long time.  For appetizer, we got the plantains, which were not heavily fried and really delicious.  My friend got the vegan beef nachos which were seasoned nicely and I got the steak tacos, which were also pretty authentic.  

Overall, the food was great, but the service and alcohol amount could definitely be improved.  I'll go back and brave being treated like uncool dirt from the hipster staff because the food is tasty.

Pat's Vs. Geno's, Geno's Vs. Pat's, Both of them suck, go somewhere else.

Well considering that these two places are right next to each other as well as having the most air time out of the cheesesteak shops in Philly, I was compelled to finally have a taste-test showdown between the two. 

[Anyone who has read my previous review for Geno's Steaks already knows how this ends up].

Service at both venues was surprisingly quick.  In under 10 - 15 seconds, you're ready to chow-down on a hot cheesesteak sandwich.  Both places are about equal in price, Geno's being only slightly more expensive by under a dollar margin [$0.00 - 0.99].  

As far as taste goes, Geno's steak is more tender and the bread is fresher and tastier overall.  Pat's gives you more steak, but the bread is a bit tough and when left plain [non-cheesesteak] the steak is bland.  If I had to choose between the two from the sandwiches I had, I would go with Geno's.  Nothing wrong with Pat's but there isn't anything special either.

Made a one day stop in Philly during our NYC trip and definitely had to swing by one of the cheese steak joints.  We decided to go by Pat's and I thought it was pretty good.  What was really good at first was that they make cheese steak as fast if not faster than when you order from a fast-food place. I expected a bit better cheese steak considering that Philly's expertise are the steaks.  Next time I'll check out the competition of Geno's and Jim's and see which is the king of cheese steaks in Philadelphia.

I had Pat's when a friend was visting while I was doing a stint in Philly.  I kept hearing how Pat's was featured and thought it was be good to test it out.  

I learned not to trust food network on that day.

I had a cheesesteak with provolone cheese.  The meat was dry, the cheese did not help and the hype was definitely way too high.  

I spoke with a couple of native Philadelphians and their comment was: "no one that lives in Philly would actually go to those two places."

Lesson learned.

Again, I have been told to try both Pat's and Geno's. For me personally, Geno's was better because of the bread. However, Pat's was still good. I wouldn't return to Pat's but I would return to Geno's.
The best cheesesteaks in soutphilly, a little greasy n u might be waiting a few mins but worth the wait!!!

There's always a line but its well worth it. My friends and I do road trips from NYC to Philly just for cheese steaks. I know you probably think we are crazy, but its so good. The meat is tender, the pepper and onions adds great flavor and the bread is perfect and you top it off with cheese whiz and its party time.!! There's also Gino's across the street. but I prefer Pats. Great cheese steak and I will continue to go here.!!!

Oh no, Pat's does not deserve two stars.  I gave two stars to Geno's, and Pat's is worse, so one star it is.

The meat doesn't taste like anything.  Nor does the cheese, the onions, or peppers.  It's just a spongy roll filled with wet greasy ingredients of unknown provenance.

WTF, Philly?

Foods great
Service was outstandingly terrible. Employees stood around as the line just piled up. One person was making all of the burgers as everyone else stood shrugging. Took over 40 minutes, my refund was offered but the guy threw away my burgers because they refunded me.

This tiny place is a revelation!  After driving by several times, I finally had time to stop.  Yes, it IS tiny and yes, the woman behind the counter was not very pleasant, but the cinnamon sugar pretzel nuggets were like heaven on earth!

If there is such a thing as "too much butter" these might qualify, but not really because how else are you going to get all that cinnamon sugar to stick?

Yum, yum, yummy!

I've only been once - but the next time I'm in town I'm making a beeline for this place. Fo sho.

Met up with a huge group of friends here and they were acoomdating on a busy Friday night. We waited for an age for a table but it was warm outside so we drank beers and margs on the street as it got dark - I love the atmosphere of the place. Now i'm English folk so of course my accent got some interesting looks and mostly fun banter and chats with locals - so friendly.

The food was really excellent... really. It's relatively cheap too.

It's in South Philly, one of my favourite neighbourhoods and stumbling distance from a friends house. Winner.

AVOID THIS TOURIST SCAM; COLD CHEESESTEAK; RUDE STAFF
First visit to Philly this past weekend and decided to try out this place for lunch after hearing about its reputation about being the "best/oldest." There were some tourists eating out there, but no line. Because we were a party of 5, we wanted to order a variety of thing including the famous cheesesteak. When I asked the staff if he has anything else to recommend, he became inpatient and told us that this place is only famous for its cheesesteak and I should just go read the menu if I want anything else. Before I could ask another question, he was like"if you want it, then pay now. If not, next." I was turned off by him for sure but since we were already there, decided to go ahead and buy 2 cheesesteaks anyway.  To my disappointment, I was handed two pre-wrapped cheesesteak that were COLD.  there was no pepper, no onion.  Just two pieces of bread with bunch of dry-tasting meat and 2 slabs of hard cheese.  I could have gotten a better deal from Charlie's.

I love the product no question about them made to order juicy burgers with FREE toppings galore. Oh and them Cajun fries so full of potatoes goodness but I am here to talk about the customer service I received this evening. This team working this shift on 1/2 was everything you want from a team of employees. The woman taking my order greeted me with a beautiful smile & asked me how my new year was shaping up. The men behind making the burgers were friendly and not to mention one of them mentioned how to save the company money by reducing the use of plastic bags. Maybe make the brown bags with handles? Great staff - give them all a raise!

Went to Pats and Genos today.....The good: Pats wins between the two with me but man was I disappointed...second trip here and last time was far better.We have a similar chain in Houston called Pappa Genos....and it is 10x better than both. Sorry. My kids were like why are the people so rude...Philly.

I used to go to brunch here, because it was the only place with seats available reliably at noon on a Saturday. The eggs benedict were so good -- jalepeno corn bread and bacon -- I ordered without even looking at the menu.

Then, one day, my eggs benedict came to the table and the bread was blue and there was no bacon. Apparently they wanted to change things up. I'll change this review to 4 stars when they bring back the old eggs benedict. Until then, I'll be brunching elsewhere.
Best thing on the menu is a $2.5 coke.  Poor quality of beef covered with lard of cheese is not what I was expecting for $10. Very disappointed with my first Philly cheese steak in Philly.

Straight up SHITTY. Customer service is horrible. They literally took 40 minutes to take 2 cars then had the audacity to not even even acknowledge me when I pulled up to the mic. Had me thinking the whole time they were busy when in reality they were waiting for me to speak. IGNORANT. UNDERSTAFFED. UNPROFESSIONAL. Don't go here!

Let's start with they called me to tell me they are out of coffee. What kind of homemade kitchen runs out of coffee? (I asked the girl and she was annoyed) I think my omelette came with like 5 tots which tasted oddly like maybe fish sticks were made in the same basket. The eggs over easy were basically hard cooked, bacon over cooked, and toast under toasted. Clearly we ordered too late in the day and they didn't feel like making a good breakfast but if you advertise hours then support them. Did I mention they were out of coffee? My advice is don't order from this place.

This place was fun! Stopped here after grabbing food around the corner for some much needed margaritas and chips/dips/guac. Can't say that I was disappointed. I thought that everything was pretty good! The guacamole and the margaritas were pretty well priced. I thought the classic was a little to sweet for my liking, but I went with the blood orange instead and that was a much better option for me! I like the roja salsa best out of the dips we tried. This place is fun, but I think I'd like to come back to enjoy a margarita on their awesome patio space! Looks like it would be a lot of fun!
Hands down the best! Wit whiz for days!!!!

Okay, I would first like to say you can't beat Cantina's happy hour.  Also, they give chips and (good) salsa when you sit down, which is amazing if you're always hungry like me!  I started going here when I moved to Philly last year in November.  The winter was great, the bartenders and servers were friendly, the food is orgasmic, and their margaritas are phenomenal. I've recently starting frequenting again now that I am back from NY after a few months and I'm sad to say that while all the above remains, except the friendly staff. 

A couple weeks ago I sat out front as it was a beautiful day. I waited about 20 minutes for a server to come, which I think is more than fair, before going inside to order a drink.  As soon as I returned, I was greeted with a terrible attitude because I ordered my drink with the bar and was told "well you could just keep ordering at the bar."  Not very nice.  My intention was to relax after a day of work, not ruin the beginning of someone else's day over $3.00.  I have many years serving experience, so I always try to sympathize, never complain, and tip really well regardless of service.  Things happen, but you should never have an attitude with your customer. 

Last night I was crudely turned away by the hostess after requesting to sit outside.  She was more than okay with; actually she seemed glad to know that I was going somewhere else.  I finally tried Bing, Bing! due to the fact that I can't eat somewhere so close to my go-to Philly spot Cantina.  It was incredible and I'm glad I tried it.  While there I wonder how many guests end up at Bing, Bing! after being turned away at Cantina due to rude staff?  My male friend pointed out her super obvious dislike of me the second I walked in.  Actually as he put it, the hostess, a larger girl, skinny shamed me.  She took one look at me and was super nasty.  This happens as a female regularly so I didn't say anything.  The fact a male pointed it out, meant she was pretty obvious.  Which one can only assume a job greeting people, probably isn't the best for someone that is judgmental to people based on anything outside of restaurant relevance. 

I'll continue to visit Cantina, solely for the food and drinks.  I can't speak for the whole staff, I'm quite certain there are great employees there.  I understand things happen, I just don't know if I could tolerate a third instance of bad customer service there, so I hope it doesn't happen.  I didn't write this to complain either, I love Cantina, I just think they can do better.

Waiting in a long line with high expectations only to be disappointed.  For the $10.00 price of a sub I would expect to receive a sandwich where the steak and cheese filled the roll.  There are plenty of sandwich shops in Mass. & N.Y. that make far superior cheese-steaks, don't waste your time or your money.  Additionally if Pat's continues to skimp on those ingredients I don't think they will have to worry about those long lines for long!
Horrible experience. A perfect definition of a tourist trap. The cheesteak was so dry that I could hardly finish it.

I can say I at least tried it. I ordered the pizza cheesesteak with provolone from the first window and cheese fries from the second. The sandwich lacked flavor, the provolone wasn't melted, and instead of putting the pizza sauce inside the roll, it was somehow only outside. Secondly, the cheese fries were too cheesy and were completely soggy after just a few mins. 

I appreciated how fast the lines moved. I even tried to read ahead on how to order so I wouldn't be the hold up. Unfortunately, there were 2 girls in line who didn't see the large "cash only" sign or realize they make the sandwiches as you're ordering and you shouldn't step far away from the window. They weren't treated too kindly by the workers or regulars in line LOL. 

It was fun to experience the famous Pat's King of Steaks, but I don't need to go back next time I'm in town for an Eagles game. I plan to try a steak place thats less stressful and actually has bathrooms for customers!!

Eh...I just don't get it! 
I've oficially now had Pat's, Geno's and Jim's all once now...yes..I know there are more..BUT
Pat's=Geno's and Geno's = Pat's
Same greasy, too soft bun with loads of cheese...
I was slightly day drinking at the Italian market festival and decided I'll give Pat's a go since I haven't had it yet (the line was much shorter than Geno's), my neighbor's daughter wanted fries, and I needed to walk past to get to the auto shop.

Super quick service I ordered, and my sandwich was already waiting for me while I paid!
I get the novelty of just meat cheese and onions and "ordering properly" but some customization would be nice. However I did order my sandwich "togo" but it wasn't wrapped or in a bag...once I saw some people with bags I decided to go back..get a bag and some extra papers and wrap up my own sandwich. 

And whats with the separate windows for the sandwich, fries and a drink? Are these two separate lines? Do you have to pay separately? So confused..

Honestly...I think I can make a better cheesesteak with some steak-ums, provolone and a crusty roll.

You know back in my day, I remember when I could get one of these cheesesteaks for $7!  You know, like a few years ago - literally?

I went here last week on a visit to Philadelphia and found that the price of a regular cheesesteak was $10 now.  What kind of inflation are they running here?  The place known for their cheese whiz had me going gee-whiz when I took out a $10 bill.  BTW, I hate how these places make all this money, yet can't afford to get with the credit card acceptance program.

Anyways, if you were unaware, this place is right across the street from Genos.  Wish I checked the prices at Genos while I was there.  Didn't even bother ordering a drink or fries.  Just because the word 'steak' is in 'cheesesteak' doesn't mean I should be paying steak prices!

We drove for an hour to get here. WORST PHILLY CHEESE STEAK EVER. I am not sure how and why they are famous. Meat was not good. It was chewy and tasted weird. The cheese was disgusting. The onion was not even caramelized it was something else. It's a poor sandwich. What a waste of time to drive all the way up to try this indigent sandwich.

Cantina has been one of my favorite spots for a while now. It has solid food, outdoor seating in the summertime, and the staff is always genuinely friendly and helpful. The prices went up recently but it's Passyunk and I like it so I shrugged it off. 

We go in for an Eagles game and we're hanging out at the bar, and there's an older guy in a Westbrook Jersey at a table. 

During the first half he's talking to the staff by their first names, ordering a lot of drinks. He goes into the bar stock of citrus cuts and grabs some limes and we figure he's just a regular.

A couple shows up and sit with him- his friends- and that dynamic changes. It becomes clear that he's the owner of the restaurant and he gets domineering fast. He starts loudly demanding the attention of the bartenders, getting more expensive free drinks and bragging about it when he's getting it for free. 

He dresses down an employee in front of other staff and on the floor of the restaurant for something in their work. I guess he thought that was impressive. 

All told everyone in my party felt uncomfortable but we stayed for the whole game because it's the Eagles. But we agreed that we don't want to give our money to this guy anymore, so we're not doing Cantina or it's sister restaurant in old city. 

We'll go to a neighborhood spot instead. The food isn't worth the price or the owner.

Slowest Taco Bell I have ever been to. Every time I come here I feel like they are training a new staff and they have never seen a Taco Bell menu. Doesn't mater what time or day you come here expect to wait 15 minutes for two tacos even if you are the only person in line.

Fan of both Pats and Genos.  Pats roll is on the dryer side and both places chop their steak up differently.
Bring cash an your order for a quick transaction.   

If you are a tourist watch out during the high traffic times and just sit and eat your cheesiest where you bought it.  Freshness is key.  

Free peppers are sweet and spicy!

This place is the worst. We went through the drive. Our orders were supposed to come eith fries and drinks. We didnt receive either.Weactually had to rurn around go inside tge store which defeated the whole purpose. Oh and tge 1$ tacos are the worst.
Nice place!! Passion fruit margarita was amazing and the free chips with salsa were pretty Good.. definitely be back here!

I'm embarrassed to say that  I have lived in the city for almost a year and have not explored the wonderful Ave of E. Passyunk. After a Saturday Phils game recently we ventured over to this haven of fun people, restaurants and shops and after careful consideration, chose Cantina Los Caballitos. These days I'm usually glued to my bb looking up a review on a particular restaurant before venturing in but for this one, I decided to be spontaneous and just give it a go. Right away I was smitten by the adorable little outside area with tables and lights. SInce it  was off and on raining, we didn't take a chance and instead headed inside for a table. We scored a table right by the bar and in perfect timing since the crowds were slowly coming in for dinner. Everything was perfecto, the pork empanadas were by far my favorite to date. The tacos I sampled were heaven as well perfectly balanced with meet and toppings.. Since I only had a small sample of what this place has to offer, I will be sure to head back soon and bring some friends with me- I'm dying to try one of their margaritas. The tequilla selection was overwelming to say the least.

Came here at the last minute n the mood for wings. Service was unbelievable. Counter person we awesome, food was great. Can't wait to come back. Was going to grub hub it, but will pickup anytime they were so fast. Awesome wing place. Got the honey bbq and the golden garlic. Wings awesome. Cheesesteaks were great. Fries were great. Would definitely recommend.

Yes it's a tourist trap.

Yes it's overpriced at $8.50 a steak

But dammit with sliced steak that was tender and seasoned, some whiz and a little hot sauce it was sooooo good!

It is too commercial... yea.. but it is still very good!  I have plenty of Philly Friends that LOVE and HATE this place.  I happen to be one that loves it.  Anyone that hates this place is just from another neighborhood.  Sure Jim's is great, Dalessandro's is legit, but Pat's is as good as both of them.
I love this place.  The sandwiches are very  good and the service sucks... what more can you ask for!  Anyone that says it sucks and only tourists come here... explain the line around the corner at 2 AM on a Saturday.

This is my favorite spot to hit late night. Anytime I am away for a while, the first thing I do when I land is go straight to Pat's to get welcomed home. Really quick service, fantastic meat-- and of course the cheese wiz! Across the street is the bright light tourist trap Geno's, but this spot is worth the wait if theres a little line. Wiz Wit!

As any other Philly first timer I had to stop and grab one of the original cheesesteaks at Pat's during my summer X-country roadtrip http://KananAcrossAmerica.blogspot.com.  

The Verdict: Love the authentic experience, the lady taking my order even had that 'hurry up, I'm watching a Phillies game' attitude that I found comical, however the steaks ain't all that.  I mean I devoured it because it was my only meal of the day, but their at best 'okay.'

I highly recommend if its your first time in Philly, but I wouldn't go back.  WARNING: Cash Only!

I've eaten here so many times over the years. I think they opened around '06..when the ave was just starting to become more of a "thing' than just a "thing." I like the food...but what brings me here is the atmosphere. I am a sucker for festive outside seating with twinkling lights on a breezy summer evening. That's what we had. We ordered nachos, enchiladas, wet burrito, chorizo tacos, margaritas, beer and some shirley temples for good measure for the underage. Our service lacked a bit. Non-attentive service for food or drinks or hot sauce, etc...but I didn't let that stop our joy. It was my birthday dinner, celebrating with my kiddos who found all of the food up to par and they kept the atmosphere festive. The charm of eating outside on Passyunk Ave also offered a drum-line that stopped in front of the outside seating and played beautifully. I'll keep coming back. It's sort of a summer-destination-place.

This place is just OK, from the food to the service. I've tried a few things from here, and all were pretty boring. The one thing that actually had flavor, which was a salad, was way too spicy. Just OK.

I'm not sure why I keep going back here. I started going when I moved to South Philly about 2 years ago. It used to be a decent place to go but it's been going downhill everytime.

So why do I keep going back? I wish I knew.
I guess it must be the rude staff, the vegan beef that always tastes like vegan sloppy joes, or the fact that they can't ever seem to put the guacamole I order on the side like I always ask. Instead, it gets lumped all together in the burrito at the bottom. 

That must be why I keep going back. Most people will complain about the hipster swarm that seems to be drawn to faux-authentic restaurants like these.

At least most of the portions are large.

3rd visit to Pat's in as many years. We ( my wife and I ) drive down to Philadelphia every once in a while from Central New Jersey . I know there are probably better cheesesteak places in Philly but I like Pat's because of its history. All in all the cheesesteak is good and I have no complaints . It taste even better when I happened to be there after a Flyers game . I personally didn't attend game but the fans added a Philly ambience. After all what could be better a nice day a Flyers win and a good cheesesteak. My wife likes Jim's steaks on South Street

Some people will look at my star rating and wonder HOW IN THE WORLD DID I GIVE A 3! Well its my opinion of what I ate. So I will say we bought 1 sub from Pats and 1 sub from Genos (I'm going to post about them next) and we split them so we could both have some of each. Pat's sub was moist actually so much that the juices ran down my arm . My problem really is that they do not add tomato or lettuce or mayo to the subs and it wasn't really seasoned. They do provide salt, pepper and oregano at the window for you to add on your own. The cost was 10.50 for a whole sub which is the only way you can order it. With all that being said if I had to eat from there again I would but I would know to bring condiments.

Was so excited to see this in the PHL airport, however was treated so rudely it's hard to want to come back. They did not say hello, just waved me to the register, and they don't say "my pleasure" which is customary to chick-fil-a. The line also took a while, which is so unusual for this company. I also asked for no bun and she stared at me, then made sure it had a bun on it when I received it. This chik fil a makes the company look bad overall and was sad to see this.

After hearing about this place for years, I wanted to check it out.  I've got to say that this was one of the more disappointing experiences I've ever had.  The sandwich was cold, bread was stale and worst of all, the meat had no flavor.  I'm from Chicago, and I'll take an Italian Beef any  day of the week over this mess at Pat's.

Let me resolve an age old Philadelphian dispute: Pat's Cheesesteaks are better than Gino's Cheesesteaks. I know this through no empirical evidence nor intellectual enterprise. In fact, I have never once tried a Gino's Cheesesteak, but I have been raised on the principle that the Irish know far more about how to slop red meat and cheese whiz on fresh bread than the Italians do. 

I believe Pat's is better than Gino's because Father Chuck told me it was true, and Father Chuck, at the time, was the finest man I had ever met. And like the Catholic upbringing that introduced me to 12 years of Parochial schooling, faith in Pat's is better left untested. So here's a story that might raise a few eyebrows: a young and handsome Catholic priest decides to reward some high school kids for volunteering at a soup kitchen, packs the little angels into the back of his mini van, and begins speeding down the Schuykill Expressway to an almost abandoned looking spot in Southeast Philly save for two long lines of zombies waiting for their fix of the good stuff. The children are then subjected to a flurry of curse words, grill-burnt hands, dead animals, and a meal that's so damned greasy and filling, they'll soon find themselves unconscious for the entirety of the car ride back home. 

This all as a result of Father asking us if we've ever had a Philadelphia cheesesteak. When the answer was a unilateral no, he feigned offense. "May the Lord forgive your neglectful parents." He then set forth some ground rules, I still live by:

1. Beware the Philadelphia Cheesesteak moniker: if you're in Philadelphia and you're eating a cheesesteak, the odds are it will be good. If you're at a place in the suburbs or another state that serves "Philadelphia cheesesteaks", it is a lie deserving of a flipped table in the hall of the Pharisees.

2. You can get all kinds of fancy and wonderful cheesesteaks in the city, but if you're at Pat's, you go traditional and get the whiz. It's gross, of course, but tradition is tradition. If we can handle transubstantiation each Sunday, I think we can handle a little whiz.

3. Finally, as we already determined: Pat's is better than Gino's. No reason. Just canonical truth. 

Father Chuck proved to not only a good priest in a world full of monsters, he was the best of all role models. During my high school years, Father taught me how to swear in three languages, drive like an absolute maniac, and to believe that good deeds really do matter to God. Above all else, Father Chuck taught us to memorize our cheesesteak order before walking up to the counter or risk a brutal verbal assault from the staff behind the counter.   

The ephemeral Catholic Church of Father Chuck's world was one where giving back was cool. Father Chuck was cool, so serving the homeless at a soup kitchen and playing piano at a children's hospital was most certainly cool. I truly loved the man and the life he seemed to live. I think Father Chuck could tell that and finally sat me down and asked if I had considered the priesthood. After a few hours discussing more about the vocation, I took his advice and spent a weekend at Saint Charles Borromeo Seminary. As an awkward teen already living a life of forced celibacy, the priesthood didn't seem so bad. Sure, you'd have to wear itchy clothes and say a lot of masses, but you could always pack up and head down to Philly and eat that incredibly flavorful steak on freshly baked bread.

As you can probably tell by my other reviews filled with incessant swearing and talks of orgies, poop, and violence, I did not become a priest. I also only went back to Pat's Steaks on one other occasion. I was with my then friend, Kaitlyn. All was going well until Kaitlyn brought along a blind date to tag along with us to Pat's. To my memory, the young man was awkward and sweet, though I can't for the life of me remember his name. What I do remember is the poor bastard stuttered his order and was immediately called a "fucking moron," by two of the grill cooks hoping to move the line. I of course came prepared and had my order memorized, and Kaitlyn and I were married five years later. So what's the message here? Go to Pat's Steaks, and trust your heroes when they say they can lead you on a path towards a lifelong vocation. Perhaps some day they will.

My 2nd favorite Cheesesteak next to Steve's Prince of Steaks

CHEESESTEAK RATING: A-

They use a chopped steak and plenty of it. A good amount of grease but not to much and a good wiz.

Touristy like Geno's but really good!

Maybe it's just me, but Pat's and Geno's rank the same for me. In fact, I believe everything is the same and they are only fooling us ;).

Cheeseteaks - Whiz is most classic popular, but I'd lean towards American if they have it. The line moves along very quickly so don't fret, young grasshopper.

To satisfy your cheesesteak craving, Pat's will get it done. But if you have checked off Pat's from your list then there are tons more places to try in Philly... spread the love!
Try the blood orange margaritas, as well as the chicken tacos!

It's not my first time coming here. The famous dueling cheesesteak joints in Philly. Yes this here is the better of the two as far as I'm concerned. We tried both steaks years ago the first time I came here, and yes,, Pat's is the better of the two.

Located in the middle of a residential neighborhood, Pat's is the unassuming little humble spot. It doesn't have the flair of the other guy, BUT if you take a closer look, the line is a LOT longer here than there. The reason for this is not brand loyalty, but real honest to goodness good ass cheesesteak. Once you're in the premises, you'll see all the pictures of the celebrities and sports teams all over the walls and vaulted ceiling. This shops tells the story that it's stood the time as one of the legendary cheesesteak shops in all of Philly.

I'd definitely come back,, and will tell people about this famous dueling cheesesteak joints here in Philly. I'll even tell them that this spot is the better of the two.

Life is too short, get up off your couch and experience it first hand.

This is my first Philadelphia review and what a better way to start by reviewing a place that serves the icon of Philadelphia food culture: The Philadelphia Cheesesteak. I went to this place with a friend from Cherry Hill, New Jersey a while ago, and he said to me that this is something that every tourist to Philadelphia should experience, and it was recommended by another friend who is originally from Ambler. This is the first cheesesteak place I have been to in Philadelphia. While I would not visit this place often if I was ever a resident of this interesting city, I found the Cheesesteak here to be tastily adequate.

I ordered a Cheesesteak with Cheez Whiz as the cheese, which is a processed cheese sauce. My friend got the same thing, and we shared a cup of fries. The steak itself was chopped up bits of meat, probably would have tasted really mediocre if it was not for the Cheez Whiz which made it tastier. I found the bread probably a few steps above mediocre. I thought it was a tad dry, but the grease from the beef made the bread really soft, chewy and flavorful. 

As for the fries, they were pretty tasty with the right amount of salt, and the texture had the right amount of crisp that made the fries almost addicting to eat. 

Despite eating a somewhat tasty cheesesteak, I think it is a little pricey, since I paid almost $8 for the cheesesteak. Fries are almost $3. I think it's because this place has got so famous that it is slowly becoming really touristy. Service is extremely effective. As long as you read the rules sign while you stand in line, you can get your food in a few minutes after you order. Since we were eating on the tables outside, a few flies came in and irritated us, so they definitely need to figure out a way to prevent insects from coming in. A great advantage is that this place is open 24 hours so it is not a bad choice for food after a night out in the city.

Overall, this is not a bad place to get a somewhat tasty cheesesteak and fries. I know that there are better cheesesteak places in this interesting city, and I am still in the hunt for best Cheesesteak in Philly.
Delicious and fresh sushi. Service couldn't have been better. Great spot for quick lunch or dinner pick up. I'll definitely be back.

Stops #3 and 4 of a cheesesteak tour I took with a couple buddies last weekend.  Gotta do the Pat's vs. Geno's challenge (a brilliant marketing strategy, I might add...who cares who wins, they BOTH get the business!)

Anyway, the whole cheesesteak thing started with Pat's in the 1930's, so we included the comparison on our trip, thinking of Pat's as our baseline.

First of all, it's an assembly line...took us about 30 seconds to get a sandwich in a crowded city block.  Roll, meat, fried onions, whiz, wrap and done.  Seemed kinda institutional.

However, the taste was better than expected.  We were warned that there are better tasting steaks in town, which is true, but this "touristy" experience was still pretty good.  The meat was seasoned well, the roll was nicely chewy and the whiz just tied it all together.  But much like the Anchor Bar in Buffalo (originator of buffalo wings), there have been improvements to the original.  But Pat's is still a nice experience, placing #6 out of our eight stops (behind Sonny's, Tony Luke's, Campo's, John's Roast Pork and Jim's Steaks.)

First time ordering today and will definitely add this spot to my delivery rotation. Homemade Tots had a great crispy coating with a creamy potato filling.I would say the best potatoe side I have ever got delivered.
I got a "provolone with" and it was disappointing the meat needed salt and pepper to enhance the meat flavor. The grilled onions were yummy.

3.5 stars. This is basically just expensive junk food. Kind of like doritos in steak form. It's good, I enjoyed it. But this isn't exactly a food destination in terms of quality or pricing. In my measure Geno's willingness to go the extra inch toward junky-ness put it a notch above Pat's, which was equally as junk-foody but with pretension to being better quality.

I have been here several times and always have a great time! It is a fun, friendly atmosphere with homemade chips and tasty margaritas! What more can you ask for.  This is a great place to meet up with friends after work or to come for a first date.
Extremely disappointed. The only reason i gave it another star was that its across the street competitor Geno's was worse.

This good Mexican restaurant opened in my neighborhood last summer, and I really really like it.   The food is good ( I recommend the fried corn on the cob also the chocolate banana empanadas are amazing), and the margaritas are excellent.  The decor is nice and it is a good hang out spot if you're looking for place to have a good drink and people watch.

I ordered teriyaki rice bowl with falafel. The bowl was full of fresh veggies and the taste was awesome. Teriyaki was refreshing.
The portion is huge. I had it as my lunch and evening snack. It was that good.
Drinks are amazing too. I had the recoverii juice and it tastes awesome! One has to try it.

Wanted to try the original cheesesteaks so I went to both Pat's and Geno's. The only difference was I got Whiz at Pat's and provolone at Geno's. Overall, they're both about the same though it seemed like the bread was better at Pat's. Overall I give the nod to Pat's but honestly, you can get better cheesesteak than you'll find at either one. 

It was amusing to hear the people who didn't know how to order getting scolded.
Pretty cheap and delicious cheese steaks! I'll come here during next visit in Phily, cause the food's worth it.
Slow understaffed and never gets orders right. One of the worst McDonald's Avoid always!!

A delightful, inexpensive, Mexican restaurant on East Passyunk. Their drinks menu is creative and fun, and a great place to start daydrinking. I ordered off of their specials menu and was not disappointed by their refried beans. They were also one of the only places in the area open for 4th of July, which is very much appreciated.

A day trip calls for a Philly Cheese Steak quest! Last stop: Pat's King of Steaks. 

I'm not sure why Pat's King of Steaks has so much hype against Geno's Steaks. We tried the Philly Cheese Steak Whiz with grilled peppers and grilled onions. The only thing I like about this cheese steak is their whiz. The rest didn't taste good. The meat was sliced and it didn't have much flavor. The bread was tough to eat as well, as if the bread was sitting out for a while.

There was a long time to order, but make sure you know what to order when it's your turn. The line goes fairly fast and the people are quick to make your cheese steak. Pat's King of Steaks also accepts cash, which makes the ordering faster. I forgot to mention, but there are 2 separate windows: one to order cheese steaks while the other window is for sides and drinks. 

I was disappointed in this place just like Geno's Steaks. Rivals? More like relatives that's for sure. I couldn't find any difference between the 2, besides their whiz maybe?

I can give this place another try when I come back up to Philly to visit.

On a short trip to Philly, my dad and I had to go settle the great debate once and for all: Pat's or Geno's. We walked up to the window, nervous about ordering wrong, when one of the old time regulars helped us through the process all while entertaining my three year old by making his nose squeak. We found a table and split out sandwich. The steak was deliciously seasoned, juicy, and tender. The gooey cheese complimented it perfectly while it ran down my chin. We cleaned up, thanked the owners who were outside doing an Uber Eats photo shoot, and went across the street. The entertaining regular told us not to waste our money, in jest, of course. He was right. After consuming a lesser cheesesteak we walked back over to head to the car, told them by unanimous vote they won, and spent a few minutes talking to the owners again. They came out with a t-shirt for my son. Overall, the food was amazing and the experience was an absolute blast. Now that I'm back in Indy I'm craving another sandwich.

As much as I love pizza it was fairly disheartening when I started a gluten free diet, come to find out these guys have an amazing GF dough, so many fresh toppings to keep the possibilities high and a spicy red sauce! Need I say more? Check their menu because the options certainly don't end there. Customer service is as great as l the pizza too, thanks! (Also vegan cheese if you rock with that, something for everyone!)

After we sent our first pitcher of margaritas back for being sickeningly sweet and lacking tequila, the second pitcher wasn't much better.  The food was average, at best.  They need to take a lesson from El Vez or El Rey in CC.  Will not be going back.
This place still has the best cheese steaks in philly other then geno's with either one you can't go wrong peroid!

Great little hidden spot underneath the Panera Bread at Presidential City. Have had their sushi 3 times now and have enjoyed it each time. They have a pre-made section where you can just pick up, which is convenient. This is our first time dining in and we got the Tropical Tuna Tartare roll; it reminded me of poke because it had fresh pineapple and was delicious! Jen particularly liked the shrimp tempura roll, which was made to order for us.  The rice was actually warm, and the tempura was especially crunchy. Overall, fresh ingredients and great service. Will be back again!
Came to Pat's a day after experiencing Geno's, and I think Pat's sandwich was slightly better. The flavor of the meat better, but Geno's cheese sauce takes this one.

cheesesteak with onions and chiz whiz! WAAA WAAA WEE WA!

After an hour drive from Atlantic City we decided to head to the city of brotherly love for lunch and it was worth the trip! I was salivating for the famous cheesesteak on the drive there. Although it was over 90 degrees and the line was overflowing to the streets (thankfully no one got hit by a car in the process of waiting) I didnt mind getting a little tan in the process. If you turn 180 degrees the competition (GENO'S) was just across the street and they had pretty much the same amount of customers overflowing to the streets.

Originally our plan was to order at Pat's then head to Geno's for a comparison but after one cheesesteak at Pat's it was a wrap! GREAT FOOD! Who would have thought of cheese whiz? Now it got me thinking what other savory meals i can cook up and put cheese whiz on top.

yes, yes and more yes to Pat's!!! Thanks Philly for the love.

EXTREMELY OVER RATED!  One reason we drove all the way from Washington DC is to try out this place and the other 'famous' cheese steak place right across.  My personal opinion is that both places doesn't deserve higher that one star.
Food:  1/5.  Extremely bland and no flavor at all.  I honestly believe that this, and the other place,  are the worst place that I have eaten a cheese steak sandwich.
Price:  1/5.  For the quality of the food, extremely not worth it.
Overall, it was a disappointing experience.  We were thinking that we would end up deciding which one serves a better cheese steak, this or the other one across.  It ended up we were deciding which one was worst.  Completely disappointing.  But of course, this is just my personal opinion.

Although we were seated instantly, no one came to even give us water. We waited about 15 minutes before leaving. I saw one server ask if he was working out table and they told the other server no, but the people that were seated behind us were served by that same server. I'm not sure if there was a mix up but it definitely left a bad taste in our mouths
For my first ever cheesesteak, I'd say it was delicious. Didn't feel the hospitality ordering like I usually do in Georgia but overall, it's worth writing home about.

Blaze pizza is the best! I'm a student on campus and it's an easy go to. The service is great, pretty quick and consistent in quality. I like that the ingredients are always fresh. I've had a couple of servers, but the one that really stuck out was Mickey, she's always welcoming and friendly.  

Update: recently discovered their smore desserts which you normally wouldn't think would go with pizza but it's actually amazing

I'm sorry, but this place just did not live up to expectation.  Tony Luke's is the best beef.  This stuff tasted like Grade D meat with no flavor topped off with the nasty wiz sauce and some unimpressive and watery grilled onions.  It just wasn't good.  Look the place is a tourist trap.  There's lines around the damn block everyday.  With that type of assemply line operation it just ain't gonna be that good - and it wasn't.  In fact, it was a bad experience.

There's a battle between who's better?!?!?!?! Really?!?!?!? Don't buy into the hype.

Pat's is better then Geno's hands down. There is no competition between the two...(meat has flavor, portion is bigger, the Wiz is Wiz like and isn't runny {I still don't get how Geno's wiz was runny?!?!}, you can add peppers and mushrooms, and the bread is better). 

With that said:
 
IF YOU DON'T LIVE WITHIN A FIVE MILE RADIUS do yourself a favor and go to your local supermarket. You will need to a buy a onion, a nice soft bakery sub roll, a bottle of cheese whiz and some steak 'umm (or shaved beef from the meat counter if available). Dice and sautee the onions and then cook the steak. Cut the bread. Heat the wiz. Spread the Wiz on the roll then add steak and onion. 

TaDa! You've just created a cheesesteak BETTER then both Geno's and Pat's!

If you must go then save the $9 bucks you'd spend at Geno's and buy two from Pat's!

(BTW I know there is also a debate over Wiz or Provolone. Go Wiz, the provolone adds little flavor)

This is a really great breakfast place.  This is our  new go-to place, over Penrose or Melrose.  There is not a lot of seating, but it wasn't crowded when we went.  I ordered over easy eggs, which were perfectly cooked, and scrapple.  My husband ordered pancakes, which were delicious.  Everything was made fresh to order.  I highly recommend this place for breakfast.  We will return for lunch at some point, so I hope to update this review.

Although I've yet to try Jim's (supposedly the best of the three) or Geno's, I can reliably say that Pat's dishes out a fine cheesesteak. The line moves pretty quickly, the seating arrangement is plentiful and the vibe is chill. I'd suggest getting your cheesesteak "Wit" (i.e. with onions). They have birch beer and root beer too so that's kind of awesome tas well.

I had to check this place out since I've never had a "Philly cheese steak", and the rivalry between Pat's and Gino's was interesting, so our group checked it out. The line was long, but they were quick; I was so surprised my steak came out 4 seconds later! The fries are great because they're crunchy and soft. I'm sure there are other better cheese steak places, but you have to start broad to refine your taste :) 

Also finding a table was difficult, and it's hard to eat the sandwich sitting down since it's soggy and dripping everywhere. My suggestion is to have a friend scope out a table while one stays in line - the experience is much better when it's not dripping all over your clothes.

Menu says Sweet Iced Tea and Iced Tea. So I ordered Iced Tea. Response "we don't have unsweetened tea. I responded that the menu says you have it. She responded "we don't have unsweetened tea...  seems the 2nd tea canister is filled with coffee...  and they do t have Senior prices!!

Try number two.
Melissa W,  such a pro. Orders, "whiz wit" Success. 

The sandwich here at least looks like a bit more thought was put behind it, it comes out looking a heck of a lot better than Genos. There is more meat,  more appetizing grilled onions. Softer bread. Taste wise, it could use some tang, like come jalapenos or something. 

I can't say its the best I've had still. But still a lot more appetizing than Genos. My vote for Philly Sandwiches still lies at Hershels

Sandwiches run about $8 each before adding all the extra toppings

This place kind of sucks but somehow remains incredibly popular. With all of the good options for Mexican food in Philly, this place ranks pretty far down the list. It's a great place to sit on the patio, get a drink in the Summer, & eat some simple chips & salsa. But don't expect anything else to stand out. Service is generally weak & understaffed & the food is mediocre.
This has got to be the umpppteeenth time I had Pats over Gino's . Its juicy overall. Made pretty damn good. Eagles up.

I went here for the first time Saturday and had a such a good time we went back sunday - both times I think we were there for 4 hours!

The food was really good - chicken tacos and guac were amazing. Nachos enormous and unlike most places you get nachos where everything is just piled on top, these have layers and layers. The only thing that wasn;t that great was the crab ceviche my friend got. 

Now onto the best part - Tequila!

It has been a while since I saw that many diff tequilas available. We started easy with pitchers of margaritas. Then on to the flights. This makes no sense to me...shots of don julio are about $10 a piece - yet you can get the 1 producer 3 tequila flight of Don julio with 3 shots for $13. Casa Noble is a $16 shot - and again you can get a flight with Casa Noble and like 3 other shots for $16. 

And the jukebox might have the greatest selection I have ever seen. Everything from Siouxsie and the Banchees to M.I.A. to Bob Dylan to Prince. 

all in all a great spot to chill with friends on a lazy sat or sun afternoon.

White red headed bro working the register  on the night side never gives enough cheese for the cheesesteak. Stop skimpin dawg. Don't make me even think about considering Genos. More cheez.

xx

So I'm a fan of the fast food burrito-kill me. I let my friend in on my little secret, and now we're both crazy fans of the fast food burrito.

First of all, it's really hard to find a seat here during the lunch rush and the dinner rush. That's just the way things are. Second of all, you'll defiantly have indigestion and mad diarrhea if you try eating this before you wait 5 hours from when you ate before. 

The burritos are huge and cheap (it's fast food) and you can build them yourself. I recommend pinto beans and white rice.

Over rated!!! Please do not waste your precious $11.50. While visiting Philadelphia, one of the must dos was trying a philly cheese steak! We tried Geno's and Pats, which seem to be pretty popular, one in front of the other. Very visible signs.  In our opinion, Pats was much better than Geno's. We bought their most  popular cheesesteaks which is basically  flavorless meat and whiz and we also order cheesesteak with mushroom. 
As a family of 5, we all came to the consensus that it's overrated. On the other hand Geno's fries were pretty good! 
Happy with Wawas cheesesteak!!

Had to try the famous Philly Cheesesteak from the big two of the Cheesesteak rivalry--Pat's and Geno's. Both were disappointing. Pat's is a little better though. Both remind me of "Steak-Ums," which I always thought were pretty good for a knock off Cheesesteak at home but not close to the real thing. Unfortunately I was wrong. These places probably actually use Steak-Ums. Pat's was pretty flavorless and not impressive at all. It's a better Cheesesteak than Geno's though. But, Pat's is dirtier than Geno's. How disappointing this was!

Recently went to this place for the first time. Where do I begin? The staff in general was clueless, it was almost comical. It was as if they had had no training whatsoever. My companion wanted a salad and the guy behind the counter acted bewildered; eventually one of the employees pointed to a little plastic container that held a mélange of ripped-up tired lettuce that had obviously been sitting around for hours. It was put into a tiny clear plastic box. Then my companion explained that he wanted toppings--more astonishment and disbelief--and after coaching them a bit he took his pallid, limp-leaved salad to the cash register to pay. I ordered a pizza, and on top went canned quartered artichokes--the outer leaves were tough--great dollops of an astringent marinara sauce, ricotta, and here's the kicker: rank diced garlic that clearly had come from a jar. As I stood waiting for my pizza with the employees milling about in a disorganized fashion I watched other pizzas being brought over from the oven, and for the most part they were quite clearly overcooked, somewhat browned, even. Mine was not, however. The crust was pleasingly thin, the dollops of marinara were unwelcome to say the least, the ricotta was mild and milky as it should be, the diced garlic was pungent and vile. I really don't see how a pizza place like this can survive. The service was chaotic and disorganized and slow and the food was pretty terrible! I will say that the pizzas are a nice size for one, but I cannot imagine going through this culinary ordeal again.
Worst pizza I have ever tasted. I just had one bite and I couldn't even finish the slice. The garlic powder is a lot which made the pizza taste bitter.

Best outdoor seating on Passyunk.  If you've turned your ankle in the stones on nights past, no worries, they've just poured concrete over the whole outside dining area.  

I love Mexican food but I never know what I'm ordering here.  I 'm never disappointed.  It's all good.  I come back for the ribs.  

Enjoy!

Ordered a mushroom cheesesteak wiz wit. Parking could be tricky unless you get lucky (parallel parking). The line moves fast and you better move with it or else get in the back of the line. Don't panic, you'll end up with a cheesesteak and it will be worth it. The cheesesteak are a little pricey but the flavor is FULL and the peppers you can eat on the side are AMAZING. I left full and happy to eat at the place Rocky chose to eat his cheesesteak.

I definitely like pats over Geno's any day but if you want the best cheesesteak in philly you have to go to delsandro or clevers. Pats and Geno's are more tourist location and are the most famous places but they're the the greatest in philly.

I am a fan of Chipotle. I eat there quite a bit in San Diego. I have been traveling through PHL more often recently and have had the opportunity to try this location 3 times now. The food is just not as good as regular Chipotle. The chicken is of a lower grade. I know nothing about chicken, but what I get at this location is more sinewy. It seems like they are using more of the chicken - parts that don't normally make it into their burritos.

The salsa is also not as fresh. The tomatoes are mushy. It's all just a lower grade.

While I've been to Philly a few times before and had cheesesteaks, this is the first time I've tried one from the two biggest names in the city.  I chose Pat's to try first as they're the older of the two.  Geno's, you're next. 
 
ATMOSPHERE:
We must've stepped on dog poop because we luckily found parking right across the street from the restaurant.  As we pulled in, I saw the line that spilled out onto the street.  I was thinking hell no, forget it.  But you know what?  The line moves pretty darn quick, so just do it!  Hordes of cars kept coming and coming with the line at Pat's and Geno's taking turns ebbing and flowing.  Everyone entertained themselves while waiting to get to the ordering window, especially in selfies with the neon biz sign.  Once you near the ordering window is when you'll see the menu and "how to order" signs.  The first window handles strictly sandwich orders.  If you want sides or drinks, you order and pay again at the second window.  Picnic table-style seating wraps around the fluorescent-lit covered lanai.  There are no restrooms or place to wash your hands.  Napkin dispensers are readily available to mop up the messy job at hand.
 
MENU:
Steak sandwiches in 13 varieties, roast pork, hot dog, fish cake, fries in 4 varieties.  Water, soda, coffee, tea, cocoa.
 
3-STEP ORDERING:
It's beneficial to know what you want by the time you get to the window as things move swiftly.  Step 1: Choose your sandwich.  Step 2: Say "wit" AKA "with" if you want grilled onions in your sandwich.  Step 3: Order your cheese type (cheese whiz is the liquid stuff, provolone or American).
 
FOOD:
Mushroom Cheese Steak - $11.04
I got mine wit (onions) and cheese whiz.  The odd price is so that the total rounds up to an even amount with tax.  No time to deal with change here.  Does it live up to the hype?  I say, sure.  I'm not a cheesesteak aficionado but I thought it was good.  The bread was soft, the rough-chopped steak tender and flavorful with the liquid cheese adding more savory notes and the fresh mushrooms a nice earthy flavor.  It's quite a large sandwich, probably close to a footlong but I finished it!  Had I taken time to read the menu better, I would've ordered the sandwich with peppers too. 
 
SERVICE:
It was a chaotic, comical mess but in an organized way LOL.  I've never paid for and received food so quick in my life, literally within 20 seconds.  The guy taking orders was cool, even double checking that I really wanted onions and mushrooms on my sandwich.  I added on sodas but was told it's ordered at the next window.  Wham, bam, thank you ma'am!
 
TIPS:
Cash only.
 
Open 24/7.
 
OVERALL:
It's something you should experience when visiting Philadelphia.  It may not be the best cheese steak around but these guys are legends in their own way.  We'll see how Geno's compares next time.  Follow/friend me and you'll know soon!
Great soft Philadelphia soft pretzels. I personally love the whole wheat ones but please order ahead. Get some spicy mustard. Five star.

Okay, maybe all of the bad rap that Pat's has gotten over the years is dependent on when the critics are going, because I visited late at night on a Thursday (ie, no rush and the place was less active than usual, even though the line was still long) and really didn't have any problem with the servers. That being said, they were still curt with my group, but it was like getting slapped around by a sibling-- do you forgive them immediately? Yes. Welcome to Philly, tourists.

Attitudes (or not) aside, the steaks are big and classic, but they've gotten overpriced over the years and clearly cater to the tourists. A really good buy for that late night grease craving are the fries-- they're crispy and wildly unhealthy at the same time. Better for late night after a concert, when the tourists have left for the day, than for lunch or dinner.

Pat's King of Steaks. Sliced meat with melted American cheese, scantly sprinkled with chopped onions neatly packed into a chewy roll (maybe 5 pieces-to be bitter and hyperbolic). It was surprisingly clean and ordinary. Liked Geno's better because the bread was toasted, the steak was oilier and they gave me a whole lot more onions.

Ahh the Cantina. I live about a block away and have visited many, many times.  I have what you could call a love- slightly dislike relationship with the Cantina. 

Things I love:
- That it is so freaking popular and our out-of-town guests ALWAYS want to check out "the orange restaurant with all the people sitting outside".  We actually took some friends with New York there twice in one day because they loved it so much.
- The food is overall pretty delicious.  I've rarely had a bad dish.  Some of my favorites include fajitas, veggie burrito, huevos rancheros, and of course the amazing salsas (that come with free chips, score!)
- The drinks are awesome.  Margs (all flavors) are great and beers are reasonably priced. 
- Lots of outdoor space! So glad they finally turned that empty lot into an outdoor dining patio.

Things I slightly dislike:
- The service can be sooooo sllllooooowwwww.  Which is awesome if you want to chill out, drink, and munch on chips.  But watch out if you want to grab a quick bite.
- The music inside gets really loud at night.  Wow, I sound like an old lady.  But if you are on a date or with friends you want to catch up with, it can be difficult to hear each other.  Make sure to sit outside if you fall into either one of those buckets.
- Food is a teensy bit overpriced.  Just a teensy bit.  And I don't like that you have to pay extra to add on cheese or pico de gallo to burritos, tacos, etc.  I feel like those should be standard, with guac being offered at a premium.

Overall, I always enjoy coming to the Cantina, esp when we have friends visiting.  The food and drinks are always good and its a fun place to hang out.

GROSS 
I will NEVER understand the love for this place. It's gristle with whiz. EW! There are SO many other places to choose from. I hate when this place is recommended for people visiting Philadelphia, too. What an EMBARRASSMENT. Not to mention, the workers are SO rude!

Pat's is a Philly icon and appears on everybody's "best of Philly" bucket list. I ordered the philly cheesesteak with wiz only and fries. The french fries were finger-licking good, extra crispy, and thick cut. The sandwich itself was average, but the bread stood out for being toasted to perfection.

Being from Texas, my husband and I were super excited to try our first true Philly Cheesesteak. We had heard great things about Pat's - so we made a beeline over there to try it out!

When we got there, it seemed we were definitely in the right place. The line was completely around the corner! 

Our mouths were watering - we were so anxious to get to our table and taste this beautiful thing we had heard so much about.

Unforturnately, it was a huge disappointment. The steak tasted a little burned and the bread was super chewy. We realized we must have fallen straight into a tourist trap :-( 

We thought surely a true Philly was better than that - it just had to be.! The next time we were in Philly, we listened to the locals and went to Jim's. Now that - my friends - is a Philly! And the line wasn't nearly as long - even a lunch time!

Wish I could recommend Pat's, but I just can't....

I've waited my whole life to have a Cheese Steak in Philly. So I went with Pat's it's famous and I've seen it on T.V. boy was I disappointed. The line was long but moved quickly. Seating is limited so if you're with someone grab a seat if there is one open while the other person orders. Cash only luckily there was an ATM across the street. There's a way to order that you must get right before getting to the window. The whole process seems rushed and I noticed it in the food. I got a Cheese Steak with peppers and provolone. The meat was dry and not flavorful like many people say. The cheese didn't have time to melt into the meat even with letting my sandwich sit for a minute. The peppers and onions sat on top so every bite wasn't an even mix of flavors. The fries were okay. Nothing to go bananas about. Will I go there again no. At least I can check it off my list.
The most mediocre sandwich I've ever had in my life. I've seen the ad's and was expecting great quality in a hoagie. Didn't happen. Signed, Starving and disappointed

My visiting daughter and family wanted to try some "famous cheesesteaks", so off we went to the two big rivals, right across the street from each other.  The family was all waiting for my daughter and I at Pat's, while we were at Geno's. 

I'll start with first impressions: My daughter desperately needed to use the rest room and Pat's told her to go over to the park adjacent from them!  We did and there was no rest room!  Geno's was right there, so we asked them and they slipped her into the back and left her piddle.

Now we get to friendliness, cleanliness and decor.  Pat's is old and dirty and has not spent one dime of their profits to stand out in these three fields.  Geno's on the other hand has put a lot into these areas.

Now for the cheesesteaks:  Even though we were all headed to Pat's, my daughter and I were so impressed with Geno's that we ordered our steak and fries there. The other 5 in our party stayed at Pat's. 

My daughter and I took our order from Geno's over to Pat's to eat with the others ( tacky for sure and I would have rather ate at Geno's because of the cleanliness and decor). 

First of all, to order a sandwich and fries at Geno's, you must order them and pay for them separately at two different windows,  I can see where this works for them at busy times, but we were the only ones there.  

The meat at Geno's is much, much better than at Pat's.  Everyone, but my stubborn son in law agreed.  The bread is better at Pat's.  The onions are raw at Geno's and sauteed at Pat's.  With a grilled sandwich I would have preferred the sauteed, but I did order a cheesesteak hoagie, so that may be the reason. 

Pat's uses more cheese.  I had provolone. 

All in all, if you add it all up, Geno's definitely has the better of the two cheesesteaks and wins hands down for decor, cleanliness and friendliness.

it was a cold day! i couldn't enjoy the cheesesteak as much because i was packed in layers of jackets and shivering.  I think it's because it was my first day back in the states coming from the islands, where the weather is always hot and toasty.  We had the cheesesteak with cheese whiz.  I LOVE WHIZ. i would eat more of it right now if i could.  We ate here before picking up some cheese fries from geno's.  The meat was nice and juicy and the bread was very fluffy and warm.  I think i still like Rick's cheesesteaks a bit more from what i remember.  Give me more, i don't mind eating steak all day long especially with the lack of fresh beef in the caribbeans.

T & N has been my favorite place to eat since the early
 80s.  I love their food, especially the sausage and greens on a roll. The people are wonderful they make it feel like home. Please visit them once, you'll never stop visiting them. Peace and Love

i'll be short since theres tons of reviews on Pat's already. 

So, I never had a real cheese steak. Being from California the closet thing I got to a cheese steak is from the mall food court. Yes insert (laugh). :)

So my advice is if you're not a local and think the mall's philly cheese steak is good, wait until you try this.

Yes, theres a line and its cash only. Theres an atm nearby though. Happy eating.

2.6/10.0

We tried Pat's instead of Geno's due to the latter's xenophobic publicity in the past.
