Haven't heard of the people of Pat's being xenophobic assholes, but the person who took our order when we were there (a Saturday night) was at the least a regular asshole.  

They have obnoxious instructions hanging on the wall that explain how they expect you to order your sandwich.  They are very clear that if you screw up the way they want you to order, they'll send you to the end of the line.

I found this to be off-putting but really got the full experience when I got to the order window.  The employee was purposefully obnoxious--either seeming to go along w/ the all business//wit or witout//whaddayawant routine or, in my opinion, just using that as an excuse to get his own rocks off via  a little cheesesteak order line power trip. It was pathetic.  As soon as I said what I wanted he loudly and rudely corrected what I had said by spitting it out in the Pat's code.  When I asked if he recommended cheese whiz or provolone cheese, he screamed "WHATEVER YOU WANT!".  When I was done ordering the sandwich, he told me to move along.  I asked if I could order a drink as well and he screamed "YOU DON'T DO THAT HERE!.......IN THE OTHER WINDOW!".
It was disgusting.  All I could think was what a loser this cheesesteak order window bully was.  

I've seen others describe the all business/high-stress ordering scenario with stars in their eyes as if it's part of the fun.  Those people are cooked.  Always thought it and it was confirmed when I got to experience it first-hand.  Made me regret giving them my $$ before I even got my mediocre cheesesteak.

The cheesesteak was OK.  Not terribly upsetting, but not the best in Phila.  Ehh.  I'd give the cheesesteak a 7.1/10.0.  I'd give the service and non-eating experience a 0/10.0.

Meeting friends in Philly, was invited to do as many tourists do which was go out for Philly Cheese steaks. As an invited guest, I didnt check Yelp (huge mistake) as to the choice of venue. The only thing I did confirm is that they had a non-beef option...Roasted pork.

Overall, no easy way to put this...But the roasted pork on a hero roll was one of the worst tasting foods I have ever put in my mouth...Or should I say the most tasteless thing I have probably ever eaten. The only positive, if it was a positive was that it wasn't bathed in grease like the beef cheese steaks. The hero roll itself was tasteless and obviously made 1-2 days earlier in some mass production bakery. The roasted pork or what they claimed was roasted pork could better be described as a non-beef steak-umm. It had NO taste whatsoever. Obviously the short-term cooks never heard of salt, pepper, or any spice for that matter. One good thing...The diet soda was able to wash down the barely edible sandwich. 

Unless one is near starvation or every other restaurant in Philly is out of business, one should avoid Pat's

I love this place! 
When I get off work tired and need to grab something to eat before going home this is my go to. It's is super convenient. There is parking in front of the restaurant so I don't have to drive around to find a spot or walk much. The restaurant looks clean and everyone there is really nice and friendly. 
The food... Some rolls are already pre-made and stored in a fridge but everything I've had always tastes fresh. You can just walk up and grab what you want and pay. You can also order rolls that are not in the fridge and they'll make them for you ASAP. They also have appetizers like salad, gyoza, shumai and many Asian snacks and drinks. You can eat at the restaurant or take it to go, and whatever needs heating up they'll do it for you before heading out. 
I was here last night and I'm back today for lunch. I will for sure continue coming back and supporting Jason's Toridasu.
I love it!!!!!!!!!! The staff are nice and most importantly they have one of the best smoothies and drinks :) it's very clean and the drink comes out fast! Definitely must try!!!

So yeah - if you don't live in philly - you're probably going to say Craps (pats) and Beno's (geno's) are the places to go for steaks.  Let me be clear, if you are one of those people: please do us all a favor and jump from the ledge next time you get a chance.  It's bad enough living in the ATL and having to listen to everyone talk about how great these two disasters are.

I may have only eaten at these places a combined 5 or 6 times but i know a tourist trap when i see one.  Two reasons to go to either pat's or geno's: A) You're a tourist and your tour guide is one of the cruelest SOBs on the face of the earth or B) You're smashed and riding shotgun in your buddies pickup truck while driving through philly singing "I'm a Little Teapot"

Okay, so yes I say Craps scores slightly better than that junk across the street... but again - the bar is pretty freakin low here. As i said in my review of Geno's: Either shoot yourself in the face many times over - or go to one of the 300 other spots in the city to get a cheesesteak.  Delessandro's, Tony Lucas, and Steve's come to mind - but there are a slew of others.  And please - this is not about the frekain WIZ.  If you like it with cheese wiz - i won't stand in your way (i've had a few tasty cheeze wiz steaks in my time)... but that does not make Pat's good.

BACKGROUND OF DECIDING ON PAT'S VS GENO'S:

Final review I'm planning on writing on my Wilmington/Philly Memorial Day weekend trip.  Although I thought of another business I may write a review of in Philly.

Prior to May 2018 trip, I had visited Philly in March 2015, and a friend had recommended Jim's Cheesesteaks on South Street over Pat or Geno's.  I was not a fan of Jim's, which I may write a review on Jim's too if I get around to it.

I did some research into Pat's & Geno's.  I had told my Philly native friend, who lives in the DC area now, that I was thinking one friend could go to one and the other go to the other, and we split the sandwiches, but that would've been a hassle if we had done that.  She strongly recommended Pat's over Geno's criticizing a national news story regarding Geno's.  I didn't really like it either; not enough to boycott but something I took into consideration.  Plus, the reviews were a little better for Pat's.  

Also, when I walked by both, I couldn't even find prices for Geno's, which bothered me.  The prices for Pat's were clearly listed, and while expensive by cheesesteak standards, at least the prices were clearly shown.  Also, Geno's seemed dirtier to me.  

Additionally and perhaps most importantly, there was a historical marker plaque for Pat's saying that the cheesesteak was invited here in 1930.  There was no plaque for Geno's.  This confirmed my decision to go with Pat's. 

EXPERIENCE & FOOD:

My two friends & I waited in line, which was out to the street.  My friend joked we were going to get run over waiting for a cheesesteak, and I further joked that it would be worth it for an excellent authentic cheesesteak.  A guy behind us in line chimed in joking, 'Don't you know? That's how they get their meat!  From the people getting run over.'  I laughed although cannibalism is no laughing matter.

I mentioned to my friends, you may cash, right?  Because this place is cash only.  They both said they had cash.  The guy in front of me in line asked me, 'It's cash only?'  I confirmed it is.  He think he went to the ATM while his g/f or friend he was with held his spot.

The line moved fairly quickly.  Looked like it could've been a 30 minute wait, but it was more like 15 minutes.  We get to the front, and they are very strict about how you order the sandwich.  I said Philly cheesesteak 'Witout Onions' first.  I paid the $11.  They got me the sandwich right away, and simultaneously, I realized I didn't mention the type of cheese I wanted, which I mentioned.  The guy rudely said, "You get cheese whiz; next!"  For the record, I would've gotten provolone, but I was ok with the cheese whiz.  

Something unique was that you ordered the sandwich first and then you went to the second line to get miscellaneous things like drinks, fries, etc.  I figured the sandwich was big, and I didn't need fries.  Also, didn't want to spend $4.50 on a soda I didn't need.  I had already spent $11.

Both my friends got $4.50 soda.  I asked my friend if he could ask for a water cup for me.  I observed them say they didn't have a water cup.  I had a feeling they were going to say that.  Normally, I would be boycotting a place that didn't give a water cup (See my 1-star Popeyes review on 409 8th St SE, Washington DC as an example of that), but I let it slide in this very rare instance because this place was an institution of cheesesteak in Philly.

The Philly cheesesteak was far superior to Jim's, and it was so delicious.  It was unlike any cheesesteak I've had before in my life.  There are maybe 2 or 3 in the DC-Baltimore area that are about equally as good in taste.  But something in the flavor of the meat was really quite amazing with Pat's.  Also, I really liked the Cheese Whiz.

SUMMARY & WATER CONCLUSIONS:
Taste of the food is 5-stars.  Brash customer service & no water cup knocks it down a star to 4-stars.  Overall, I would give this another try since the sandwich was so good.  

Also, after I ate my sandwich, we popped in a convenience store since I was very thirsty.  I paid $0.75 for a bottled water in a convenience store 1 block away.  I had my friends guess the cost.  My Delaware resident friend guessed $3, and my Maryland friend guessed $1.  He said that he could tell by reaction in the store that I was happy with the price.  I told them $0.75, and they were like wow that was good.  I politely reminded them they paid $4.50 for their soda while I paid $0.75 for my water.
I don't understand all the hype about this place. The food is nothing that you can't get at a don pablo and they make great flavored margaritas everywhere. Am I missing something?

If you love Philly cheesesteaks and want something original THIS is the place to go. Honestly, I do not like Philly cheesesteak sandwiches at all and that is why I only knocked off one star. Me being a person who knows this is not my style of food still was curious and wanted to give this iconic place a try. I made the first mistake by not ordering without onions ‍. If you go, and are a rookie, pay attention to the sign to listed to the right where you order, it tells you how you should order. I only ate probably 1/3 of the sandwich before I couldn't eat anymore (the onions really got to me). The 3 other people I was with finished my sandwich, theirs, and another from a competitors location. (According to them there was no competition and that this was hands down the best Philly cheesesteak in existence). Also, bring cash!!!!! Most places like this and even around Philly only accept cash so be sure to always carry around some extra cash.

The first time I came here, I ordered online and got a lot less toppings than I expected. I think it might be better to order in-person here so you can tell them exactly how much of some topping you would like since there are unlimited toppings! That being said, it's hard to beat Blaze Pizza's price point for a personal sized pizza with unlimited toppings. Unfortunately, I feel like the quality of Blaze's ingredients are not the best- I've been to other unlimited topping make-your-own pizza places and Blaze's pizzas are just not as good. I always feel like the ingredients are maybe a little too salty- I have to drink lots of water while eating one of their pizzas.
We ordered a "Philly Cheese Steak Sandwich"  ..............tourists.

It's ok. That's it. It doesn't deserve to be king, but it is better than Geno's. Decent amount of meat on the cheesesteak,  which I guess is cool, but i wish it had more flavor. I should have asked for extra cheese. That is the redeeming quality I've discovered after my third cheesesteak in a single weekend. 
Went on a Saturday night. Zero line. Plenty of seating outside. 
Do yourself a favor and go to Tony Luke's

Maybe it was an "off day" but I didn't really get what has this place so busy all the time.   My margarita was small, weak, and not tasty.  The chicken enchiladas were meh and the guacamole was bland.  I would try this place again in hopes that I missed something the first time, but I'm not in any rush to get back there.

I didn't enjoy a cheesesteak here. I ended up taking a deep breath, hitting the ATM and going across the street to Gino's. My boyfriend and I had never visited either establishment, and didn't know what to expect.. didn't have cash and was so excited by the thrill of things that I ordered and didn't know it was cash only. 

Let me just start off with.. I don't care where you have your cash only signs. All of your lines block things. 

Also, After going both places unnoticed there is a complete disregard of the fact that most of their clientele is tourists who may have not been before and don't know what they are doing so why be so rude when ordering and why make it so quick to the point where the person ordering can't even breathe? Ridiculous lack of customer service if you ask me... after all I do feel you should take the time to get to know your tourist clientele. They are probably the only ones keeping you in business. Won't be back, not interested.

When the Cantina first opened, I was new to South Philly and found that it was a great place for excellent vegetarian and vegan food and delicious margaritas... a fine spot for all occasions.

However, four years later I no longer truly enjoy coming to the Cantina. Perhaps it's because I'm getting older and more crotchety and losing patience with hipsters. Perhaps it's because I know there are better places to go within a couple blocks. Perhaps the quality of the food has gone down. Perhaps it is darker and noisier now than it was four years ago. Perhaps I have just gotten sick of going there. It could be any of these things.

If you decide you want to go, and you are more than welcome to make that choice, here are some tips. 

-Because the restaurant can be so dark inside, I recommend going during the day so you can actually read your menu. During that time it tends to be less crowded too, which is an added bonus. 
-The House margarita is great, and so are the flavored margs, particularly the blood orange. 
-As far as food, I have enjoyed their burrito with vegan beef. Also their nachos, which you can get with vegan beef as well. 
-They always have a ton of specials and mark which ones are vegetarian/vegan.

My first Philly cheesesteak experience was... underwhelming.

I ordered the whiz without and as I ate it, I could only think of the various sandwiches I've had in my life that taste better (nearly all of them).

The bread is bland, the steak is bland and the Cheez Whiz is.. well... Cheez Whiz.

Arby's is better.  Potbelly is way better.  Subway is better.  And after I walked across the street, even Geno's is better.

It's worth swinging by Pat's just to see the weird collection of people there (girls in prom dresses, tourists, bikers, probable gang members), but your food is going to be a disaster.

Incredibly rude staff. I know it's a fast food burger joint and I'm not walking in expecting to be treated like I'm at a Steven Starr restaurant, but these people treat you terribly. A little kindness and respect goes a long long way in this world.
The worst sandwich I've ever had, very low grade cold cuts, left a nasty after taste for hours. Could be because I compared to subs in NY and NJ. I'll never eat there again.
After a night out in the city this would be ideal fill your belly and don't eat a MISTEAK

Always make this a stop when I get back home in the Philly area. I go with the wiz without and cheese fries. Even when it is 20 degrees out, the outdoor seating is just fine when you have a pat's steak in your hand. Geno's sucks!

We all know, you can't come to Philly and not have a cheesesteak.  In my opinion, Pat's is a lot better than Geno's. The reason is, I like the steak chopped up in my cheesesteaks. Over at Geno's it;s more like slabs of meat. I also liked the flavor of the steak at Pat's as well.  To each its own. They were both good, it just comes down to personal preference. I did stop by Jim's but didn't like it one bit. It was tasteless and a waste of the hour we spent in line. 

Just like my Pink's hot dog review, Pat's is not just a place to eat, it's an experience!

Best Philly Cheese steak I've ever had! My husband brought the family to this place and it was a great experience. From what I hear there are always people lined up outside this place and now I know why... But get this, these guys are literally making your order as soon as the words fall from your mouth... Hot & Ready! What really tipped me over the edge was that these guys had GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE and that's what sets them apart from the competition in my opinion.

There's no shortage of steak or cheese on the sandwich, nor is there a shortage of cheese on the fries. Bring cash, and be prepared to pay AT LEAST $15 a pop. Drinks are like frickin $3.50, and you don't even get free refills. My wife and I both really enjoyed our sandwiches and fries, but this is a place you only go to like once when you're in town.

What a huge disappointment. So expensive to. I was on a mission to try both. Both are a waste of money. Both was $32.00 and worth $3.00 WAWA IS SO MUTCH BETTER! Yes! WAWA! WAWA is like a 7/11. I hang my head in shame. What a waste of Cab fare. Driver..... take me to WAWA.... near South St. Thanks Yelp

Wife and I were excited to stop here at such an institution.  We were traveling from NYC and stopped at Pat's and split a cheesesteak - with onions and cheese wiz.  After we ate by the way we went across the street and split a Geno's cheesesteak to compare (Pat's won the battle but not by much - and not that great).

We were extremely disappointed with the quality of the meat.  It was very chewy and tough.  Completely lacking any seasoning or taste whatsoever.  The roll was ok but not toasted or that fresh.  The onions were ok.  The big thing that is surprising that there is no camelization on the meat or onions - it was more like they were boiled.

Overall it was very unremarkable generic tasting food.  We've got better cheesesteaks down in Florida.  Next visit in town we will try Sonny's.

You can tell the owner takes pride is his product. Always courteous and thankful for your business. The ingredients are fresh. I love the dragon balls. The combination of cooked salmon pieces, rice, edamame and nori is on point. Shrimp shumai is great too. If you're in the mood for poke or sushi - this is your place.

This is the worst McDonald's you could ever go to, never Ever ever ever ever ever go here. My apple pie fell apart when I took it out the box because it wasn't done, French fries were cold and my sweet tea taste like it had 2 cups of sugar in it

I know what you're thinking: "ANOTHER poke bowl place in Philly?" That's what I thought, until I tried Philly Poké. Ordering a bowl is much easier than the NoLibs version, and the seafood is way more fresh than the current poké spots in Chinatown. On the go? There's pre-made (made fresh daily) sushi rolls in the refrigerator, along with refreshments (Kona coffee!). What I like about Philly Poké's iteration of the popular Hawaiian dish is that they mix your ingredients before laying it on top of your bowl of white rice, red rice, or lettuce. FYI, they have furikake and togarashi for toppings!

I went to the new Five Guys that just opened on Walnut between 11th and 12th and boy was it fresh! Bright lights, white walls, nice clean floors, lots of seating for a fast food burger joint, very soild.

If you want to look like a nerd, make sure you tell the cashier that it's your first time at a Five Guys and wait for the revelry. The choice of unlimited toppings is a nice quark, but for some less decisive people like myself, this could be a nightmare. Give me some solid, predesigned, tested and approved choices and I shine. Leave it up to me and I'll be ordering once I wake from my trance and I pick my jaw up off the floor.

I managed to shake off the greeting and pieced together a bacon cheeseburger with mushrooms, grilled onions, lettuce and barbecue sauce, threw in some cajun fries and a fountain beverage. Big plus for the Gold Peak tea dispenser spitting out multiple types of iced tea; my eyes lit up as I approached the machine knowing that I was in for one enjoyable cup of sweet tea.

If you're the type to blot the grease off your pizza with a napkin before you indulge, first, stop doing that, second, you may need a small sapling's worth of napkins for this bad boy. The greasy goodness is a pleasure to the palate with a nice bun to bookend the deliciousness. As soon as I bit into my burger, I was very pleased with the combo I created. The burger was great and I will be returning when I need to scratch that greasy burger itch because it definitely hit the spot. Next time I go I'll opt for the regular fries rather than the cajun style, just a bit too much for my taste, but I'm also not a big fry guy, so take that at face value.

Overall, great burger, great tea, solid fresh cut fries and one happy belly.

This place is absolutely disgusting ! My boyfriend and I ordered from there this morning. I was really excited for breakfast. I ordered the grik omlette which came with toast and tots and a side of homemade turkey sausage. I gave my boyfriend the tots which he said were mushy and gross. My omelette was super watery. It was supposed to be egg whites feta tomato and spinach. They basically made egg whites and threw a block of feta - the size of a butter bar, sautéed spinach and sliced tomatoes in the middle ? That is not how you make an omelette. It should be diced and mixed in with the eggs. Please don't get me started on the homemade turkey sausage. It tasted like burnt dog food. I made my boyfriend try it and he spit it out. He got the bomb which he didn't care for. I would never order from this place again. The only thing that was edible was the side of wheat toast that it came with. So I basically could have made myself toast this morning and saved myself the trouble. Yuck !

This place blows away Subway and because of the bread Wawa and 7/11.  Probably the best chain.  Excellent sandwich with plenty on the great bread.  Good service in a busy area and friendly people too.

Yeah, I guess it's kinda like going to the Wiener's Circle for a Chicago Style hot dog, accompanied by a verbal assault when you come to Chicago. Just ask for ketchup on your dog and you'll see what I mean. Same at Pat's King of Steaks, so allow me a little tourist action, Philly. I was brought here by a seasoned local anyway! 

I loved my Steak with Cheese Whiz and onions. And accidentally did not follow the Rules and ordered my fries at the Steak window! Aw, geez, boss! Yeah, that wasn't good! But the cheese steak was! We can't get an authentic cheese steak in Chicago, so, thanks boss!

Philly hype!  Had to stop by and try a historic Cheese Steak. From the two window ordering set up to the stringy over cooked steak, not a great experience.  The roll was tough, the meat was just in the middle of the sandwich and they must think the cheese wiz is made of gold. Fries were good, even though you have to order them from a different place than the sandwich.  Very inconvenient.  Three stars just because the atmosphere and outdoor seating is cool.  Ambience should be a bonus, not the reason for visiting.  Food should always be the draw.  Raise your game Pat's!   Have to try Geno's next time.

Ignore all negative comments and stop by Pat's when in Philly.  The way I see it, there are two main groups of haters.  First are a group of  some (not all) people who are elitist cheese steak snob locals that say "Pat's is touristy and [insert another local shop name here] is so much better."  And second, are a group of people who are used to their regional cheesesteak styles that may include strange cheeses and newfangled toppings like alfa alfa sprouts and God know what else that do not belong on a true Philadelphia cheesesteak and disappointed with Pat's.  

To the first group I say. Give credit where credit is due.  There's a reason why Pat's has been a Philly staple for almost a 100 years (okay  more like 88 years) and they have lines out to wazoo at all times of day.

To the second group I say; YOU HAVE BEEN DECEIVED. The authentic Philly cheesesteak on the menu at your local Friday's or hole in the wall sandwich shop is NOT, I repeat, NOT a Philly cheesesteak.  A true Philly cheesesteak should be served on a local hoagie roll (usually Amoroso's) with thin juicy slices of season ribeye steak, sauteed onions, and cheese whiz.  That's it.  No mayo, no ketchup, no lettuce, no banana peppers, no hot sauce... No! Just no. Stop it. Saying Geno's is bad because you are used to your local area cheesesteaks is like going to China and saying the food there sucks because you like Panda Express. 

Anyways. I love Pat's.  They consistently whip me up a nice juicy cheese whizzy cheesesteak. Anytime I'm in philly I make sure I stop by.

I wish I could give this review one star, because my experience was so terrible!  This was by FAR, the absolute WORST McDonald's I've ever frequented.  I visited this location on Thursday, August 16, 2012 approximately 9:45 pm.  When I went to order my food and drink I learned the machine used to make sundaes and milkshakes were down.  It didn't seem as if anyone was trying to fix it, either.  The other thing I noticed was that when the cashier indicated the price for my order, she took my cash and didn't process the transaction through the register, which was quite surprising.  She actually took out a calculator and gave me the change from her computing.  This was strange and leads me to believe that she and perhaps other employees were pocketing the money.  I asked for a receipt, for which she gave me a receipt that was completely faded, out of ink, and therefore, unreadable.  It feels like her and other employees intentionally do this so that we cannot reveals details of our experience when one complains.  I sank into the grill chicken sandwich which was ok, not hot, but otherwise gave them a little leeway.  Next, I munched on some chicken nuggets, which were cold and not fresh.  I should have taken them back but I didn't trust the staff at this point.  I noticed that NOTHING was clean in the seating area, drink machine, and the restroom.  It was absolutely filthy to the point that there was a large amount of trash underneath some tables!  There were no napkins in the seating area to boot.  

I will not frequent this restaurant again, not even if someone paid me!  I reported this horrible experience to McDonald's corporate office.  We'll see what response I'll get....

Could rate it 5 on a 10 scale, but will round it down to a 2 star rating instead of 3, because this place gets plenty of hype already and the counter guy had an attitude. Pat's is better than Geno's. Still , I have had better. The bread was meh. The meat was decent. THe cheesewiz was well... cheesewiz. Travel shows need to stop hyping these two joints. I had to add a little black pepper to the meat. Seasoning is meh.

I asked the guy politely if he could slice it threeways. The dude purposely just slices it two ways and when I asked again if he could cut it one more time, he gave me a rude response saying maybe my friends should just stop being cheap and buy their own sandwich. What the jagoff should realize was we already had other sandwiches and what we planned to do with the sandwich was none of his business.

Absolutely the worst McDonald's I've ever been to in my 55 years. Even though I'm a resident in Chestnut Hill (loaded with great restaurants) sometimes I just want a quick burger and fries. My husband and I have given this fast food chain more chances than we would ever do with a sit down restaurant, but today is the absolutely last time we will ever walk into into this filthy and understaffed chain. 

Known for its fries, who knew that this chain continues to fry in oil that tasted like it was many months old...gross and greasy. The burger was cold (cheese hadn't melted) and slapped together. There was no ice in the ice machine and no one seemed to care...

The owner of this franchise should shut it down (sell or lose its franchise rights) and START FROM SCRATCH by consulting with a location that is always friendly, food is delish and hot (Hunting Park is consistently great).  Isn't there a formula they need to adhere to in order to keep the franchise? If so, this one is violating every covenant of McDonald's. 

Not loving it and wouldn't miss it if it closed...yuck.

Ok so my nephew bought me one of these cheese steaks and also one from Geno's. They were both very good, very cheesy and both breads excellent. They both were loaded with lots of cheese and steak. But Pat's sandwich had an unmistakable flavor of sweet onions that's hard to miss. So if you like the taste of sweet onions this is the one for you. On the other hand if you don't like onions then Gino's is for you. In my humble opinion both are delicious and worth the trip.
By far this place is mediocre. I want to eat the original PHILADELPHIA Steak sandwich but it didn't cut it.
Not great at all. Coming from the West coast I was excited to try the original. Bread was good, meat had no flavor. Definitely a disappointing experience. Won't come back.

Went on a Philly Food Tour this past weekend and Gino's and Pat's were my first stops. Of course, I couldn't help but compare the two...
Service: Gino's. Hands down!
Bread: Gino's. Sooo fresh, great texture. Delicious!
Meat: Pat's. They give you more.
Cheese: Pat's. Again, They give ya more.
Sandwich overall: Pat's. 
The Geno's cheesesteak was dripping...I guess juice from the meat. The Pat's cheesesteak was dripping cheeeeeese. When I'm in Philly, I'll be gettin' BOTH Pat's and Geno's cos they're both great in their own ways.

Disgusting!! Never ever again.. this was the worst cheese steak I've ever had. The meat tasted like it had been reheated several times before it was served to me.. old and dry... I can't believe they have the nerve to called one of Philly's best cheese steaks restaurant.

Was so excited to finally check out this place due to their extensive vegan options. They surely didn't disappoint. Had an awesome server named Heather who catered to our odd requests and was so accommodating. Nice outdoor space to enjoy the warm weather, potent drinks and delicious Mexican food. I got the vegan nachos with soyrizo which I highly recommend. It was considered a small portion, but it was a pretty damn big portion. Can't imagine how the large serving looked. Overall, I was very satisfied and can't wait to go back to try the other vegan food!

Cash only. If you like a cold cheese steak with non-melted cheese, as well as an unfriendly server, this is a top place to frequent. Could not care less about the Gino's or Pat's comparisons. However, Gino's was served hot, the staff were so friendly, and the cheese steak is a dollar cheaper for some reason. Maybe an off-day but there was a staff of eight when we got to Pat's. To serve two cheesesteaks frigid cold literally is quite poor quality.

Holy crap.. this is the worlds slowest Taco Bell. 45 mins, I kid you not. We were one of the first group of people to roll in at 2am and it still took 45 mins. They take your name for the order and then claim that they called it. No, no you didn't. I have been like a ravenous wild animal waiting at this front counter for my food. I would have heard my name being called. They remade my order and still forgot two of my items. It's a hot mess in that place, day or in the middle of the night. Be prepared for a long wait, incorrect items and dirty tables.

It's definitely one of the finest examples but don't kid yourselves into believing this is the best. There are plenty of other places far exceed this version. The place across the street is basically the same

Lines are long and theres nothing fancy. Even tho the lines are long they move very fast. There isn't any special spices or many options. What you will get is a soul satisfying taste of really good steak and a spatula of liquid goldand amazing bread. The Wiz isnt good for you. Its salty and oooozzy but it is the blanket that wraps you up and tells you that everything is going to be ok. It brings the sandwich together. Its the reason you order the sandwich. It will warm you up when you come here on a cold winters day. 

Are there fancier cheesteaks (Yes)


But there is something about the father of cheesteaks that will keep you coming for years. I LOVE PATS.

Really unpleasant experience all around.  I've tried this place a few times because my daughter loves a fast food outing and this is by far the closest.   But the place feels like a dive bar - dim lighting, loud bar,  sticky surfaces, a few sad patrons.   The drinks often do not work.   The fries are usually really dried out.     It is just really crappy all around.
Very greasy and overrated. Paid $22 for two cheesesteaks and another $12 for two fountain sodas and a small cup of fries. It's definitely a one time stop just to say we went but will never go back

one of my favorite places in all of philadelphia. for the margs and the chicken nachos. above all the rest. im just always happy when im here because im getting amazing food at a great price and im among good neighbors and friends.

Disclaimer: one of our team members tends to be overly-critical.

That being said, our visit to Pat's was awesome! The cheesesteaks were delicious -- the bread was perfect for soaking up the whiz and the steak was so good. You gotta go to Pat's! Plus, Geno's is racist soooo there's only one right decision. 

The reason this doesn't get a 5 is because (despite objections from the Philly native in our group that this criticism is blasphemy) it was really freaking cold and there is no indoor option. Our hands really got so frozen while trying to do the thing where you use your finger to lick up all the cheesy cheese on the wrapper.

I know that this place is advertised as one of the best place to get a cheesesteak hoagie.  It is not.  If you want a thin piece of cheap steak (whole) on a bun and you put on condiments, then this is the place for you.  

In my humble opinion, this is a tourist trap.  If you are a Philly person, you know this is not a great place for cheesesteak bogies.  If you are a tourist and you just want to go to see for yourself, please go, just know that the food is not all that it is advertised.

I'm sure there are better cheesesteaks in the wonderful city of Philly, but I'm more facinated by the age old competition between Pat's & Geno's. 

So who makes the better (not best) cheesesteak? All hats go to Pat's for 2 reasons: The meat portion is larger & the texture is greasier. In my opinion, Geno's excelled in the flavor department but I didn't like the fact that it has less meat compared to Pat's. Also, both sandwiches cost the same at $7.50. 

I do recommend you order it "wid" onions & provolone cheese in place of the non-organic cheez whiz.
None better.  No need to go across street to Genos.  It's always my first stop when I come back home!

LOVED IT. I was with two other people and we shared a cheesesteak at both Pat's and Geno's. I liked Pat's better, personally, but another person in my group liked Geno's. Get the cheese whiz - it adds great flavor.

There's NO better... waited in a line wrapped around the building last night and it was more than worth it. 

Do yourself a favor and go! 

PS-- don't be fooled by Geno's flashy lights... you want Pat's!

This has to be the worst McDonald's! The worst part is that it's in chestnut hill?! The place is dirty and the staff can't keep up with lunch rush. Stood in line for 15 minutes then another10 waiting for the food. They didn't have a working ice maker and the staff ignored you when requesting for the ice. They seem to do a a lot of Uber pickup orders, and seems to come first before the customers waiting in line. Sad to be in chestnut hill and be this dismal

Yes I know it may be a tourist trap but everytime I find myself in Philly, I usually make a trip out to Pat's if I can - it's definitely the novelty and I'm sure you can find better cheesesteaks elsewhere but Pat's is definitely is up there and to have good memories with friends to go along with it - I'll take it =)

First off I've tried both Pat's and Geno's - unless you've completely lost all your taste buds through old age or eating way too much hot sauce - Pat's is the clear winner. The meat is chopped rather than in dry slices like Geno's. The bread at Pat's is also more toasted. Plus any place that surrounds itself in neon lights like a mini times square is overcompensating for something.

I usually get the original cheesesteak - wit whiz (with onions and cheese whiz) - amazing! Prices have gone up though to 9.50+ a sandwich - I was lucky to come when there was no line, if I had to wait more than 30 mins - probably would reconsider. 

Overall great place to get your cheesesteak fix

Fifteen years ago, when my pudgy, middle-school mouth got its very first taste of a cheesesteak it was a provolone with from Pat's... and the bill came to a cool $5.25.

The price has changed, of course, but Pat's has remained basically the same. Overrated? Sure. Snarky, no-frills attitude? Of course. Delicious-as-hell? You betcha. But that's all part of the recipe for a perfect cheesesteak. Good service isn't about being polite and wearing a fake smile--it's about always getting your food in less than five seconds and being open 24/7. Because nothing's better than a cheesesteak for breakfast at four in the morning.

Side note: I've never been to Geno's, nor do I want to. Maybe it's their ridiculous neon lighting, or their borderline obsession with police memorabilia... ah, who am I kidding. It's their "This is America: WHEN ORDERING PLEASE SPEAK ENGLISH" sign that guarantees I'll never be a customer.

Authentic cheesesteaks delicious!
We came here After spending the day in Philly and we ordered three cheesesteaks with. The staff was super friendly and the location was nicely tucked away in a neighborhood. 
The staff was super friendly and it was nice that their was some outside seating available.
Can't wait to return to South philly to  eat these again.

Pat's vs Geno's?  All hype, they're both just ok.  I can't tell if there's clearly one better than the other.  I ordered the same thing at both, Philly cheesesteak with onions and provolone.  Pat's in my left hand, Geno's in my right.  The bread looks the same.  Pat's meat is shredded, Geno's is thinly sliced.  Was it worth the wait at the two, no!  The guys at Geno's were clearly nicer.  Was it fun running back and forth? I think so.
This cafe has lots of healthy options, great service, and environment. I would highly recommend anyone to visit!

THIS LOCATION IS HORRIBLE!...the person taking the orders at the drive thru was extremely short with me and rude as all get out. Instead of explaining that I could have ordered an additional side with my combo..they gave me nothing. Been here 3 times and something is always missing from the order...sauces...pies...and they never give utensils! I am new to the area and was happy a location was so close because love Popeyes, but I am going to have to find a new one...no matter how far I have to drive!

Thus far I have only been to Philly one time. So I am not the best judge. But I do love cheesesteaks. Maybe there are better local places to grab a cheesesteak. But with so many options, if you're from out of town like me and don't know which one to choose you will likely want to at least try one of the two most iconic spots in Philadelphia. Genos or Pats. They are similar, main difference of how their meat is sliced. Genos - sliced, Pats is more chopped , which personally I find to me better and more tender. The provolone is nice and sharp, the cheese wiz - amazing and the peppers have a roasted sweetness that's awesome. The bread is delicious. It was worth the three hour drive, the several block walk in freezing temperatures, the waiting in line of 25 people and eating outside in the cold. Very worth it. In my humble cheesesteak opinion. Best tip: know what you want BEFORE you get to the counter. They serve thousands of those things a day and don't have time for uncertain dawdlers to make up their mind. Use google, read the menu before you get in line or use this review: do you want a steak, a cheesesteak, or peppers and mushrooms  ? What kind of cheese do you want: Wiz (cheesewiz/ liquid cheddar) American, provolone- or all three. And with or without onions. Those are your choices. You order and pay for just the cheesesteaks at the first window and drinks or sodas at the next one. It's not super cheap and it's cash only. Come prepared. Genos across the street is the same price for the cheesesteaks so if you're over there looking for a better deal cost wise- think again. Pats only has outdoor eating.

I hadn't been here in awhile for brunch, and I remembered I enjoyed it, so this past Sunday I decided to go again. I arrived about an hour after open, as I walked by I saw one couple eating out on the patio. I went inside to be seated and not one person or employee was to be found. I saw someone in the kitchen, and he cane out and completely ignored the fact I was standing waiting to be seated. After about 5 min I contemplated leaving, but then I decided to walk through the restaurant out into the patio to try and find someone to seat me. As I walked outside a girl came in, at first I couldn't tell if she was even an employee. Turned out she was and she seated me. I decided to have the breakfast burrito, I added bacon ($4 extra!), however very little bacon actually ended up inside the burrito. I was also given 6 measly pieces of potato, and a half-filled container of ketchup. I settled in to eat and enjoy my meal as much as I could, however, the employees decided to have loud, personal conversations right next to me, on the exciting topic of "what if people were dogs, and dogs people". Irritating and annoying. 

I used to like this place but I won't be going back. When all was said and done my meal cost $22. NOT WORTH IT. It's a crime to charge an extra $4 for bacon and not even put much in this burrito, then also skimp on the potatoes.

Just like any other Chik Fil A, this place was packed with people. Also like most other CFAs, I found friendly staff, short wait times, and excellent customer service. I would definitely get food from this CFA again.

Driest cheesesteak I've had in all of Philly. Barely edible. Pat's and Geno's are collectively the Kim Kardashian of Philly cheesesteak joints.

I had the cheesesteak with provolone, mushrooms, and peppers. Eating the meat was like eating sandpaper. I know Pat's is a Philly staple, but it's more of a check off the box for a tourist. It's famous for the sake of being famous. If you're looking for a good cheesesteak, trek a few blocks north to Jim's on South Street.

Was in the neighborhood and hungry. This place is located inside the mall. Food is good. Chicken tenders were crispy on the outside and extremely moist inside. The moistness honestly had me  questioning if it's all white meat like they claim. Fries were  soggy, but definitely tasted of truffle. They did however have a weird aftertaste. They give 2 sauce for the tenders without you having to ask which is greatly appreciated. Took off 1 star for price and soggy fries. $16.18 for tenders & fries is steep. You can get plain fries and tenders $11.07 which isn't bad. I don't mind paying for great food however if you're charging $8.09  for parmesan truffle fries, they need to be better. Great customer service.

THE BEST wendys around. They never disappoint. Its the only fast food place near me that i will eat at. The staff is great and the service runs quick and smoothly. Im never in there for long (unless its a busy day) my orders are alwags correct and they taste delicious. There's only one thing they could step their game up with and this is the bathroom service. There is always a foul smell lingering around the bathroom and the stalls look disgusting. Im glad the outside doesn't look like that. But other than that , i love this wendys and im a satisfied customer!

Pat's is an experience that both requires and gives some perspective.  I say that because, prior to getting a cheese steak at Pat's, I always assumed that all of my previous cheese steak experiences were sub par because I had been dealing with sub par cheese steaks.  However, after eating at Pat's--the reported best--I gained the perspective that cheese steaks are what they are, and I'm just not the biggest cheese steak fan in the world.  So the question becomes:  was Pat's really not that good, or was Pat's really good at something I just don't care about.

I  think the answer lies somewhere in the middle.  As my friend Chris R. told me, Pat's cheese steaks are the ones for the tourists and the ones for foodies are located somewhere else.  So, I'm not about to give up on cheese steaks.  Chris also told me that a 3 am Pat's stop should be on the itinerary for a trip to Philly so it wasn't a wasted trip.  Taken as a 3am snack, I think I'd rather just get a waffle at a diner.

All in all, it's just an ok sandwhich.  It's a pretty cool experience though, waiting in line at 3 am with the late night, rowdy crowd where what you're wearing doesn't matter, and the only thing that does is if your doing wiz or american, and wit or witout...i just wish any of those combinations resulted in a 4 star plate.

What a waste! I was in Philly for a few days with my family and decided to give this place a try because of how "well known" it was. My family & I ordered 5 sandwiches, and to be honest.. they all really sucked. Dry, no flavor, it just tasted like you were eating bread. Not to mention that it was $10 for just the sandwich with no fries or drink... I would never go back here and would tell visitors their money would be better spent elsewhere

first time having a steak with whizz. not sure i have ever been the same since. 

it is what it is, a greasy fatty sandwich, the type that i love.

Not so sure how Pat was deemed "King of Steaks". I ordered a mushroom pepper cheesesteak with onions and cheese wiz. I don't know if it was the cheese, meat, or bread, but something about it just tasted off. It actually left me feeling queasy. I went to Max's last time I was in Philly, and it tasted more fresh and flavorful. I would recommend Max's over Pat's any day. Maybe Max should be the new king...

I have a recollection of this being juicy and greasy and a guilty pleasure delicious, but my last order was pretty dry (other than the whiz of course) and was not a huge fan of the meat. Either I was wrong or this has changed, but either way I won't be checking out pats again any time soon.

Waiter made us uncomfortable.  He was annoyed we didn't order enough and that we brought the pitcher of margaritas from the bar.  Why even ask and What else did he expect us to do during a half hour wait.  If we wanted good Mexican we would've ate somewhere more authentic up 9th st.  I shouldn't have to explain why we are there for a few drinks and appetizers while enjoying the nice weather outside.  It felt like he purposely made us wait for an iced tea.  Not worth it.

Wow. This was the best cheese steak I've ever had. Bear in mind, I'm a Georgia boy with little cheese steak experience, but I am a big foodie. I got extra steak "wit" onions and whiz and then got some of those hot peppers on the side. I sat right there and ate the whole thing, and it was cold as nads out there. This place is really something.

So I was hype to go here after hearing they Have Vegan options..Well the Joy crash landed when i walked in to see the Vegan options buried between the Non vegan options which i deem disgusting and careless...The vegan Chorizo has pieces of real sausage in it from them grabbing meat toppings around it as well for the vegan cheese i think this stuff should be separate cause cross contamination is gross and kinda insensitive to others diets when my pizza finally came out of the overnight it was pushed aside by a pizza covered in ham and mozzarella as if the juices from that didn't get on my pizza..My stomach hurt later that night i will not be returning to Blaze  or will i recommend t

No complaints here. I got a number 2, the mini 4 count. Has he brown were crispy. Lemonade was sweet. And the 4 minis were fresh. They had a very long line but every seemed to be in a pretty good mood. I would come here again.

HORRIBLE! DIRTY! SLOW!! Disgusting!  Went to this location of Chestnuthill! Now I ask myself WHY! This place is slow with orders.  There was only one person ahead of me and my order took 25 minutes! At the same time the cashier tried to give me fries that have been sitting a long time period. Not good! Got my food home. I ordered the crispy mc chicken which was cold and a burger which was also cold.   Didn't realized until I got it Home.  It's a shame people come to have a good experience with food and we get the WORST! Did not enjoy my meal at all! Will not return there EVER AGAIN!  I WANT A REFUND!

Also- the staff was not working more so talking and wasting time!  If I could give NO STARS. I would!

Just your run of the mill burger joint. I think the burgers are overpriced. There was only a few other people in there eating, so it was nice and quiet. I was surprised how long it took for them to make my little cheeseburger. There was one employee meal ahead of me and it really took an unreasonable amount of time to get my burger. So I would not consider this 'fast-food', but 'fast-food' quality. Luckily, my train was running late, so I had plenty of time to relax.

Oh Cantina, I think I love you. 

I've stopped in here for drinks and dinner on multiple occasions and I never leave disappointed. Whether you're sitting at the bar, eating in the dinning room or enjoying the fresh air at an outside table, you can order anything from their scrumptious menu, which mirrors its No Libs sister restaurant. 

And just like there, the chicken tacos (all three of them) continually make me smile every time. They are so flavorful with just enough spice in each and every bite of the filled double tortilla. Hopefully someday I'll venture out and order something different. I just can't help coming back to them repeatedly.

I also love the endless chips and two salsas to get things going, although it's tempting to keep eating them up until you're full before you even get your meal. Of course, no meal is complete without one of their refreshing margaritas. Although not very large, they are reasonably priced, especially during Happy Hour.

If you find yourself on E Passyunk, make sure you have CLC on your To Do list. 
4.5 Stars.

So while in Philadelphia I decided to go cheesesteak hunting.  I watched a couple reviews and read some articles about where to go and decided on three places: Pat's King of Steaks, Tony Luke's and Woodrow's.  

So Pat's, what a let down. Really the only thing they are doing right is the speed in service. But the steak was over cooked, the onions ok, bread was a bit chewy and it was severely lacking on the cheese wiz.  Really sad about this one.

'Wit Whiz." Translation: Steak sandwich with sauteed onions and cheese whiz. When you finally reach the window at Pat's, you'd better be ready to order or ya might get hassled.

For my first trip to Philly, naturally I had to have the cheesesteak, Pat's and Geno's being the two biggest names on the block - literally. These two cheesesteak giants are right next to each other. I chose Pat's because my host for the weekend said it was better and it had a longer line.

After a long day running around being a tourist, when I got my cheesesteak I couldn't wait to scarf it down. The hot peppers and hot sauce added to the experience a bit, but honestly I now realize I'm not a big cheesesteak fan in general. I guess that means I'm just not meant to live in Philly.
I loved Pat's! Fast and easy. Recommend to anyone who is looking for a good philly cheesesteak!

It's a classic, and I prefer it to Geno's, but there are many better options out there. The bread is OK but not warmed up and ends up being both a little too chewy and crunchy. The meat is decent quality but slightly thickly sliced for my preference. It's chopped decently - not too fine or coarse, which is good. A respectable effort, day in and day out - not the best around, but at 1AM it might be the only option nearby.. and it'll definitely do the trick then.

One word describes this place - shit.  

I'll go to Jim's or Tony Luke's next time like I know I should have.

Better than the las vegas strip across the street in terms of taste ... but the place is a dump , and the people there treat you like shit  but then again its still not half as bad as if you go across the street, and speak with the slightest HINT of an accent.

Pricey, dirty, but tasty .. and like ive said bafore there are better steaks out therem where they actualy wipe the tables

I waited an hour for my delivery and My chicken wings were over cooked, burnt, bare bones, and flavorless!! I'm really upset and hungry. It was so bad I ate one and left the other 9 wings in the box and trashed it.

I feel terrible about their ANTI GAY stance. but still i had to try their food at least once to be objective. I had heard SOOO much about their juicy chicken breast and I was skeptical since we all know it's hard to have a good chicken breast patty.  I had their chargrilled chicken breast...and YES..it was juicey, tender and yummy... unexpected and surprising DELICIOUS for a FAST FOOD CHAIN!!!!!   yes....it surpassed my wildest dreams about juicy chicken breast (a usual oxymoron for me) ,and yes it was yummy.  I'm tempted try to their chicken nuggets since i heard they were good too! But honestly I would not come back since I do not agree with their anti-gay views.  oh well.   also, i tried their waffle fries and they were just ok...too soft and maybe they should have left it in the fryer for 1-2 minutes longer to toughen it up...it was too soft to hold my ketchup! so maybe 4 stars for their chicken breast but 0 star for their terrible, antiquated, backwards view on the gay community.  so I guess we'll meet with somewhere in between with 3 starts mostly for their food, since I'm not sure we are suppose to rate them on their unintelligent , ignorant  views.
It takes over 30min just to get your order like come on really it's every time with this place I would hope they would get it together an on top of that playing in the back

If I could give this McDonald's zero stars I would. How is it possible to have the worst McDonald's ever in a beautiful upscale neighborhood like Chestnut Hill!?  

I vote for getting rid of this place and substituting a Chic-Fil-A or Shake Shack!

My boyfriend and I LOVE the food and the staff at T&N!!! Everything we have ever had has been fantastic! I am a HUGE fan of their  breakfasts, and their Escarole soup! I say, if you are in South Philly it is definitely a great place to stop and eat...

Lucky for them this is the only Wendy's around. They treat their customers like we should apologize for spending money here. It's run by a bunch of teenagers. I understand Philly is miserable but I promise it'll be okay.

I will make damn sure I never go to Pat's again and will tell my family and friends the same. My female friend ordered some cheesesteaks to go and was asked to hang out with the guys at the counter for a while. She declined because it was cold and the guy at the counter said he would keep her warm. Again, she declined and said she's happily married. Then the guy got short with her. Finally, when she asked for her change the guy pulled it back and said he needed a hug before she could have it. She declined again and asked for her change two more times before he finally handed it over.  Maybe explain to the workers what harassment is and that holding someone's change hostage so the creepy jerk at the counter can get a hug is at best unethical and worst sexual harassment.  She didn't want me to post this, but no one deserves to be made to feel that uncomfortable.

I am so glad I decided to stop in here for breakfast. As soon as I walked in I could tell it was going to be good. It's very casual and I felt right at home even though I live 2 hours away in NYC. The owner is very friendly and attentive. I had the "chili tot scramble" it was delicious and such a huge portion and my husband had the "western omelet with home fries " he ate the entire thing. I will definitely be back the next time I'm in Philly and am going to tell my friends about this great place.

Being an out of towner, I wanted to try a famous philly cheesesteak. I didn't know I had to order one in the local vernacular. 

Got whiz wit.....it was ok, kinda small for the price. I think I've had better in NYC.

Came specifically to Philly for this!! For a place claiming to be the inventors of the cheesesteak, I expected way more. They are super overpriced for the quality that you are getting ($11), it was the most bland sandwich I've had. The steak was dry and had no flavor and the bread sucked. The only good thing about this were the onions. If you're thinking about coming to this place- DON'T! You can find a way better cheesesteak at Subway. Super disappointed and will never come here or recommend it to anyone. Also the people preparing the sandwiches weren't wearing any gloves when making them.

They ran out of burritos.... that's like going to the gas station and then running out of fuel... what in the F!!! People were nice but chipotle is good wherever just a bummer they don't stock inventory...





Yeah






That's it

This place is the bomb because they have great prices great food and everything's a buck and mc Donald if your looking at this review don't change. Thing it's perfect 50 stars if I could give u 50 stars I would

Pat's Steaks were damn good.

As a tourist, I did the rounds of several major cheesesteak spots and can say I thoroughly enjoyed Pat's. Their cheesesteaks were packed! The meat was chopped and packed thick- and it was dripping cheesy goodness! I'm not from Philly, so I can say this without any bias- Pat's was legit.

I'm aware that Pat's is considered a tourist cheesesteak shop, but this is one tourist shop I'll keep coming back to. Out of all the cheesesteaks I tried in Philly, this one was the fattest and cheesiest- I loved it.

Really good and really cheap here!  Had the cheesesteak and fries.  The fries seemed to be those ones that you buy from Costco and then fry, but the steak must have been fresh.  For what you pay, this is a tremendous value.

For a number of years I was down on Pat's.  I think it's because it became the place to be.  I tend t shun the "in" places.

Here's the thing, after a disappointing day doing things north of the city, I decided to pop in the city on the way home for a quick bite.  I found a place to park right out front.  I was fortunate, of course.  South Philly parking is for professionals.

Anyhow, I ordered a mushroom cheessteak wit.  It really doesn't get any better than this.  The sandwich is handed to you immediately as they are efficient as can be.  The cherry peppers on the condiment bar are fabulous!

I really can't think how a cheessteak can be better.  This is full of meat.  If you're in Philly, you're getting whiz.  The roll is very good.  What more is there?

Yes, I am once again a Pat's fan!
Never heard of a McDonald's running out of ice cubes. Simple meal takes for ever. Terrible staff. Nuggets both cold and soggy.

I just ate here and order the chicken tenders and a really cool fry dish called the "rocky balboa" I have to say that they might've had the best chicken fingers I've ever eaten in my life, and there fries are absolutely amazing. If I could give this place a 6/5 stars I would.

After a 7 hour drive, this was everything I had hoped for.  Tasty steak in a very fresh roll, topped with onions and cheese wiz.   Had the cheese fries, too.  Better than I expected, as I'm not a fan of battered fries, but these were really good.

Came in on a Sunday afternoon and only had to wait a few minutes.
Shortest line won, pretty good steak sammy but the fries were cold and sucked. Nothing else to say but my review is tooooo short to post

Typical McDonald's, has a kiosk so you don't have to deal with the cashiers. Drive-through is pretty efficient. Inside is pretty clean however can officially have rowdy people. This is a normal McDonald's. Sometimes they don't have the special promotional items eg the Shamrock Shake. They occasionally run out of other items.
Hey, this bit of Pat's Steaks history is on eBay, and I thought I'd share it here for fun!       http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&item=171106503689

I don't get the hype to be honest. Maybe I'm just not crazy about philly cheesesteak. The flavor was just ok, maybe needs more seasoning on the meat? The portion is huge for 1 person since the bread is pretty thick and long. One thing i really liked was the large pickled peppers (goes really well with the cheesesteak). Line was long but moves quickly. You need to know what you want and talk fast when you're in the counter. You don't have time to think when they are getting your orders. Only CASH here.
Seriously underwhelming compared to the real thing - feels like every airport chick fil a I go to the food quality is way, way worse. Staff was great but food was not at all up to their standard!
Ordered mashed potatoes. They forgot a spoon or fork. Guess I'll just eat it with my hands

Went to this spot with 7 friends, it was pouring rain and there was no line, we all decided together to go here rather than Geno's across the street which also didn't have a line.  I ordered my sandwich and before I can even order a drink or fries my sandwich was in front of me which is disgusting because that means it wasn't fresh and again there was no one there besides my friends and I . I came all the way from New York to have the famous sandwich that was freezing cold and beyond mediocre, the only thing hot was the cheese but it tasted old, the fries were AIGHT but mad cold. Again, no line, this place apparently rings bells but rang all the wrong ones for me. OH AMD THE PEOPLE WORKING THERE WERE NOT POLITE AT ALL- I'll go to Jim's any day

Been meaning to try this place for some time. I would highly recommend making a reservation if you're coming for dinner. 

Reserved a table the day before for 2 people Friday night dinner 6:45pm. Just to give you an idea an idea, we did not get seated until 7:15pm. The places was packed and countless people getting told minimum 1 hour wait. 

The location is right in the heart of South Philly with lots of things to see. Inside felt like a mix of old school Mexican cantina meets modern hip taqueria.
The wait staff were very attentive and friendly and food came quick and tasty! 

We ordered Chips & Guacamole, a Veggie Quesadilla and a Chicken Burrito and tried the infamous Frozen Margarita. For dessert tres leches. The guacamole was good, nothing I would say extraordinary, the quesadilla was average, the portion size was unusually small and tasted like it needed more flavor. The burrito on the other hand I thought was a slam dunk, although it needed some salsa which I added myself. 

Took a star off for the additional wait even though we had a reservation and table placement was slightly awkward as we were sitting in front of an emergency exit. 

Overall great ambiance, good for smaller parties of 5 or less. Clean, fun environment. Although it got really loud and felt at times I was screaming to say things to other people. Will be coming back and trying other items!

The best cheesesteak I've had to date in Philly! The steak had a great flavor and the combination of all the ingredients just made it better than Geno's in my opinion. They don't have to try to be flashy to grab their customers. Their simplicity and ties to their originality show why they are the king of steaks!

Pat's and Geno's are right next to each other and I am sure most have heard of the legendary rivalry. I would not call either place the best in Philly or even in the top ten. Pat's however makes an alright classic cheese steak and has become a tourist destination.

For the most part the lines move quickly so don't be worried about a long line. The guys who work there are focused on moving people through.

I have tried the beef, pork, fries and various topping combinations. Some times if I order something that isn't a classic cheese steak the guy I order from is super rude about it. I had a friend who can't eat beef. I got pork and the guy looked at me and said, "Really? Are you serious?!" He then clicked his tongue and motioned me along. Other times they are simply professional and trying to get the line moving quickly.

The bread is usually lightly toasted and they give you a decent amount of meat. I would recommend the provolone unless you want to give the classic cheese wiz a shot. They do an alright job and the food is a little better then fast food. As for the fries, I could take it or leave it. I have sometimes gotten a steak where my onions are almost raw and I am not super into that. they are usually a little more consistent. If the prices were any higher I would give this place a two. It is okay food for the price. It is not a terrible introduction to Philly cheese steaks.

My absolute favorite Philly cheesesteak place. I always get the cheesesteak with cheese whiz and onions. The prices are around $10 which isn't bad. There's two windows you can order. One window is just cheesesteak and other cheesesteak like things and the other window is just for drinks and fries. There's a counter where you choose from the different types of peppers as well, free of charge. It's kind of in the middle of nowhere but there's still a lot of people and not far from Chinatown and the city center. There are also seats and benches with covering. 

Tip: you have to eat it right away because once it gets cold or if you get it take out, it taste different, still good but not as good.

Food  and service were fantastic but the music is way too loud and too young of a crowd for me. The couple next to us we're making out and playing the hand slap game that 5 year olds play during recess. Had to get out quickly.

The lines are always long for Pat's famous steaks and it's definitely fun and exciting for a first timer. The food is good but it's not amazing! Wouldn't say it's the best cheesesteak but they do well.

At 7:30AM today, I proclaimed I wanted tacos to what I thought were the only ears who would listen. They mocked me; however, Taco Bell was listening. They erased my shame with a delicious breakfast burrito & my heart was again full.

See picture, they wouldn't even let me say this with the picture. Supposed to have butter and hash brown with the Big Breakfast,not ketchup and more salt.Thats what happens when they're playing around inside.
Wow, Pat's lived up to its name.  The succulent meat with the cheese and the onion on the hoagie.

I have gone to this taco bell countless times and have never encountered any issues... today was the worst for customer service ever waited 45 mins to find out my order was given to the wrong customer.. manager gave me a refund and said they would remake my order no charge. I never got my remake finally after a little over an hour I left... cashier was super sweet and apologized multiple times I felt bad for her I wasn't the only customer who had been waiting a long time for food..
 Will be a long time before I go there again if I ever do

I just noticed I never wrote a review for Pat's when I was in Philly in April...  I don't know how I missed this one!


I did the touristy thing in Philly... a cheese steak from Pats... and a cheese steak from Geno's. Side by side... ready... go.

I realize this is a touchy subject in this area... when you like your cheese steak... you LOVE your cheese steak... and I think I like Geno's better.

I'm ready for the hate mail...

Pat's is good.  Don't get me wrong.  It's better than anything I would get in Northern Virginia  - pretending to be a sub... but I like the meat, and the bread better across the street.

Sorry Pat.  I still love you!  xoxo

I really enjoyed the pizza however the process of placing the order was somewhat confusing. When you walk in it's a very nice standard fast food style restaurant. There are low chairs, high pub tables and additional seating on the second floor.  As for ordering the pizza when you walk up to the counter and look at the menu above only the crust styles and number of toppings with the price is listed. The crust options are original which is thin, then there's another that's a little thicker closer to New York style the third I don't remember. This is where it gets tricky, when you look at a menu or a board  you'd think it would tell you all of the ingredients available. NOT HERE! When you look through glass there is salad bar assembly line you pick each item and tell your pizza maker so they can create your pizza. I mean down to the sauce you have to say I want red sauce you better be specific apparently there's two styles the sauce is not clearly labeled. I asked them to give me whatever is traditionally used on a pizza and I moved down the line.  At the end I was asked if I wanted salt and oregano. Since I don't normally make pizza I don't know if you add salt and oregano.  Cheese has enough salt so I passed. There needs to be some type of baseline ordering system helping people who are not familiar. Maybe ordering sheets to check your choices. Because the redhead dread was no help! 

Now that I have an idea of how the process works I will definitely be back. My pizza was delicious and it had a nice balance of all of the ingredients and the sauce was not overly sweet.  In my mind the nine dollar cost for the freshly made pizza of your choice is a great deal.

Poor service - ignored me as soon as I came in and I proceeded to wait 5-10 minutes to order at the counter. The woman behind the counter didn't take my order until she finished talking with her coworkers about the weather and I eventually called out and said I was ready to order. On top of that, I found that my pizza had some broken/chipped finger nail polish in it after I opened the box. Threw out the pizza and will never go back again. This place is the worst.
Rude staff, no hygiene and very ordinary cheese steak. Jim's is much better.

Such an Over Rated place!!!! Their meat was not cooked well and we definitely like out meat well done! Very crowded place, they take ONLY CASH and you have to know beforehand what you want. Save your money for some other place, believe me. My husband is a Cheese Steak lover and he wanted to try this place after hearing so much about this place but no way we are going here again.

This would be a great spot to meet up with friends. Walking up I noticed how many people were joyously enjoying the food at atmosphere of the place. I opted to sit inside because it was chilly for me during my afternoon visit. There were fresh tortilla chips and two types of salsa brought out after my water; free and delicious. Both salsas were bang in'! I love that they have a nice variety of vegan options on the menu! I ordered the vegan(seitan) wings; I did the sampler, so I could try all three flavors offered, habanero buffalo, tamarind barbecue, and ponzu mojo. All of the flavors were on point! I couldn't really pick a favorite of the 3 because I loved each. I believe there were 3 of each, so 9 total. I say "I believe" because I had 2 mango frozen margaritas which had me a bit lit and smiley lol. The service was great even though it was quite busy; my waitress understood my hand signals for another margarita and check please lol, you go girl! 6 out of 5 stars to this spot!
Lots of juicy steak on a chewy roll, just enough Whiz.  Don't forget to get a birch beer and god to the fixin's bar to add cherry peppers.  This is the world's best cheesesteak, period!

Where to begin ... my boyfriend and I waited on a line to get some real deal Philly cheesesteaks ... and I feel like for 10 dollars, there wasn't enough steak in between those buns (kind of upsetting) I feel because this establishment has been there for so many years (all cash business) they can get away with not packing your cheesesteak with a lot of meat. 
Thank you for disappointing me, 
a true meat lover 

Will try Geno's across the street next time!

Very cute place with good service. Food is ok. Disappointed that the enchiladas are pre stuffed so you can't vary from the ingredients listed. Ended up with nachos with barely any cheese, but my waitress was kind enough to bring me some additional cheese.

Definitely better than Geno's.  Fries were better than expected.  But, honestly, the line between good/mediocre cheese steaks in Philly is pretty slim.  So, I'm not sure why everyone is so up in arms about whose is better.  You're more or less going to get the same thing everywhere (which is a good thing).

This place sucks. Don't let them make you think that this is what a philly cheese steak is, because it is not burnt dry steak served by someone who is rude and does not care. Any other place  is better.

I was the basic tourist and had to try both Pat's and Geno's. Honestly they're both about equal, basic cheese steak & kind of rude staff, everything I hoped it would be. Not my favorite steak in the city but one of those places you have to try before you leave.

Avoid this place.  The person who gave me my order was rude, like he was doing me a favor.  The food was barely edible, not getting sick is the only plus side I had with it.  Just face it, fried chicken in philly is like ordering a filet mignon in a seafood place..the two dont mix.  Go to the South like in Georgia and you'll see what real fried chicken tastes like.  Until then, dont waste your time or nerves on this place.

As a foodie, I was so excited to try a cheesesteak in Philly that I wasn't prepared for the disappointment of realizing that it may be one of those tastes you have to grow up on to appreciated (like Kraft Mac N Cheese or In N Out). I didn't realize what I was getting into, that it would be cheap cuts of meat with cheese whiz on it and sub-par bread. There's nothing gourmet about the place or Geno's across the street (we tried both). The real win was finding the food stalls a short walk away.

5 Stars?  Really?  Yup!!

Well, first off, I love Taco Bell no matter what.  I know it's junk fast food, but I still love it.  It's one of the few fast foods I refuse to give up.  Since the only other location is in the Gallery, I don't eat it that often.  But then, they decided to open a block from my building.  I heard a heavenly choir the day I saw the sign go up.  

The location is new so it's crazy clean inside, which is a rare sight inside a Taco Bell.  The employees are all super friendly (of course I go fairly early when it's not busy so I don't know how they are in a rush) and will usually chat with you while you wait for your food.  The food is just standard TB, nothing special really, but still somehow very delicious.  

If you're a fan of other TBs, you won't be disappointed.

It's now 2019 and this place is still on my list but not my favorite. A lot of it had to do with the fact that it has become popular enough on weekends that without a reservation it's often a 30 to 40 minute wait, and the people you're waiting with are mostly from South Jersey.

This spot used to have a punk vibe and more of a local feel but is now just another Mexican restaurant for white people (like myself) that sells $15 enchiladas. Don't get me wrong - the $15 enchiladas are tasty and their frozen margaritas are still my favorite - but it's not a place I'd pick as my first choice anymore.

Omg just don't go here and with go to jims or Steve's.    This is the worst cheesesteak. Even after washing my hands.  They continue to smell a racoons a** .   It was actually making me and my friend gang how bad it was.    Terrible.  Tourist trap!!!!

So i compared Pat's philly cheese steak with Geno's across the island and i found i liked Pat's cheese steak a lot more. I think i like the ribbons of steak more as it captured the cheese in its ribbons. The bread was very soft and easy to hold. Super warm to the touch. Lots of condiments, but we really didn't need any for this delicious sandwich. Not as much seating space as Geno's though.

CASH ONLY ENTERPRISE! $10 for a sub!

Careful, there are quite a handful of homeless people that mutter and come towards you to interrupt your meal!

Disgusted with the service. Waited 20 minutes to order a sandwich. Walked up said hello to cashier no response. Ok she probably had a long day. Ordered my sandwich said no pickles. Apparently that was too much for them to handle. I was told no "special orders" I won't be back.

I came here on the first day that they opened. I got sushi rolls and the owner offered me a complimentary beverage. The staff were very nice! Sushi was absolutely delicious and fresh. I've been coming back ever since.

Their happy hour margarita pitchers are HUGE & an awesome deal. Split it between two people and got sufficiently drunk!  

You get chips and two complimentary salsas, a verde and adobo I believe. They were super yummy, I wanted to drink them. 
My sister & I both got tacos. You get 3 per order and they have a decent amount of meat! My sister got steak and she absolutely devoured them (usually a slow eater lol). I got the al pastor, unfortunately I was sick before coming so I was only able to eat one  but it was delicious!! I ended up getting the rest to go and it was a great midnight snack when I felt better. 


Overall: fun environment, friendly staff, great happy hour deals, yummy food. 5 stars.
Delicious pizza best in the area and it's really cheap too. I'd definitely recommend it. Can't wait to go back. The people who work there are all very friendly and helpful and efficient.

I give this place one star. I'm originally from Florida and was down visiting in New Jersey. I always wanted to try a Philly Cheesesteak, so I drove down to Philly (1 hour 30 min drive), because of the reviews on Google.

Let me just say "Total Disappointment". The meat lacked flavor no salt or pepper. The provolone cheese was like one slice, over powerd by hard mushrooms and soggy bread....

Totally not worth the $12 also they charge $3.50 for a small coke.

Take my advice and find somewhere else. I have had way better Philly steaks from out of my own kitchen.

They get three stars for failure to read and follow instructions. 

Ordered via Doordash, ordered two cheese steaks with mayo and ketchup both had neither. Cheese fries with cheese on top received it on the side. SMH... So irritating!

Helloooooo Yelp!,

Hi everyone, this is my numero uno review eva!  Whatttttt up?!?

Not to say that I'm a cheesesteak pro or anything, but! I did go on an all cheesesteak diet for a day while visiting Philly to truly determine FOR MYself, which cheesesteak is........ the KING OF CHEESESTEAKS!  When I say ALL cheesesteak diet, I mean breakfast, lunch, dinner, and midnight snack! (Don't judge me... =\)
