After trying Pat's, Jim's, Geno's and Pat's again, by unanimous decision... still!.... king of cheesesteaks!...... "Pats!...  King of Steaks! since 1930."

To describe how bombtastic this sandwich is, you gotta imagine the feeling of a hot summer day.... you're looking for a place to cool down, a place to relax and just enjoy yourself, like a nice cool swimming pool. That hot summer day is HUNGER, and that oh so refreshing pool is CHEESE WHIZZ!!!!

Pat's just knows what they're doing "wit" the whizzz, it just has the most perfect consistency.  Not too watery, not to thick, but just oh so right....  So good, you can fill a cup with and drink it.  And that's what they did!  They fill a cup with cheese whiz, throw some fries in there, and there you have it.  A cup filled wit whiz or you can call them cheese fries.  But who in their right mind would order that?  Certainly not me.... maybe....  Mmmmm whizzz.....

Besides the oh so great cheese whiz, the steak is just heavenly and those pickled round peppers and crisp chili's are no joke.  Those lil extras take Pat's to a whole nother level.  Those peppers are what makes Pat's.... Pat's!  I couldn't find better from any other place.  

With that said, yes I'm on the Pat's bandwagon, but it's well deserved.  Me and Pat's are one now.... or should I say were one...  Now go get yourself a cheesesteak wit onions and whiz!  Don't get too fancy!

Until next time peoples!
Keep on, eatin on!
Horrible needs a complete makeover with staff. I suggest u either train staff in customer service or hire new workers that will be able to work
The taste is not that great as expected or advertised. Drove long way just to break heart.
Delicious sandwich but the bread was stale. The ordering was easy and worth the wait in line.  Cash only and ensure to be aware of what you want unless you want to be sent to the back.

I don't know why this has so many crap reviews, maybe I have to try more cheesesteaks haha. But in my opinion, nothing beat this sandwich at 3AM... So hot you can get with onions or without. It was everything I expected it would be. Would recommend it over Genos

Got a cheesesteak (with whiz) and honestly, was not that surprised or please about it.

The bun felt greasy and yet didn't taste that good and clearly was just a medium to consume the rest of the ingredients, didn't really bring anything else to the dish. I could've just ate this in a bowl without the bun and I would've enjoyed it just as much and save the carbs.

The steak itself, maybe just a personal preference, I would've preferred it to be more shredded so you can get more surface area for the cheese and for easier bites. Enjoyed the mushrooms and onions with it, but honesty I didn't feel like I had a phili cheesesteak in phili when I came here. Just meh

This place is great. I stop by here to get strawberry banana smoothies which is my favorite during the summer time. And I love that they just started doing hot tea options for cold weather. If you are the one who goes for the fresh healthy choices, this is the right place to go. Staff here is so nice, and they are willing to remake the drinks if you do not like how it tastes. They are flexible to change the ingredients from the menu and just overall warming and honest with their food and drinks. 

I will definitely come here again for the smoothie and other hot teas. Love it!

I'm 36 and this was my first cheesesteak...in my life...ever! What better place to go to than the place that created the sandwich. 

Ordering is simple but you have to be quick! I went all in and got Wit Wiz. The sandwich was huge! I probably shouldn't have eaten it all by myself but I did. And I ate fries as well. And had a soda. All were delicious. My belly was happy and I'm glad I got the experience.

$8.25 for a personal pizza with any toppings you want. I did the red sauce with a few types of cheese, salami, tomato, and garlic. For me, the crust was better than Snap, which would be the most similar in this market. Skip the salads but don't skip the agua frescas.
Still missing a little something from the cheesesteaks. Still really good and definitely better than the India across the streets. But would definitely go there again

The cheesesteaks here are ok I guess, but certainly not deserving of the hype they get. However, the thing that sticks out about this place is the piss-poor service. Are all new hires required to take a course on how to be the biggest pricks they can possibly be to customers?

The asshole taking orders had a real attitude and refused to give me the change I was owed. He didn't even count the money before putting it in the register, and kept trying to move right on to the next person and insisting I gave him the exact amount. I figured it wasn't worth holding up others from ordering their overrated cheesesteaks to keep arguing with that douchebag.

Oh yeah and God forbid you don't place your order using their stupid lingo. Seeing how it is more of a tourist attraction than a place for locals, they might want to try not giving people who are unfamiliar with their lingo a dickish attitude if they're not perfect at ordering. They're obsessed with keeping the line moving fast, yet it probably moves slower because of the confusion created by requiring people to order using their pointless, made-up lingo.

I've probably been to about 50 different McDonald's and this one is probably the worst. They often for get items in the order. They are super stingy with their condiments. There was also one occasion I got food poisoning after eating their food.

Worst. Ever. Placed my order on an an in store mobile screen. Arrived before the rush, 1:37am order completed. Waited to check in for 30 minutes, didn't want to be rude. They claimed they must have deleted it. They stalled for 10 minutes and then they placed it again for me at the register using my phone. Forgot to correctly enter 4 of the items because the "Taco Bell order font was too small for them to read" on their own order. Another 30 minutes later -  forgot 3 of the items for no reason. completely rude the entire time while we were in there for 1 hour and 13 minutes.

When we first got in the store, the cashiers were lauphing loudly. And while we were telling our order, they were not paying attention and still laughing. The tables were dirty, it was a total mess..There was no ice in the machine and all drinks were bad
I really don't get what all they hype is about? I can get this kind of cheese steak any where! I went to both places and split it with my husband nothing to be amazed about ppl

Four stars for the large and pretty outdoor area and margaritas. The margs are tasty but hit or miss as far as how strong they are. The nachos and quesadillas are good. My friends are I are always disappointed by the tacos.

They provided the Chipotle level of quality that I expect, at off-airport prices. $7.15 for the chicken burrito. Lots of airport workers were eating here, (look to where the locals eat, they say) so that's another endorsement. It's in concourse, and near gates, B.

So we came to Philadelphia pretty much specifically to try Philly Cheesesteak sandwiches. Asking several locals of course got several answers.... After all the hoopla we made it to Pat's and found it was truly the best of all.

The meat was properly cooked, seasoned and cut... cheese was poured on top on a soft bun anid it really was good.

To compare we also tried the competition across the street and found it was not nearly as tasty.

If you're looking for Philly Cheesesteak sandwich you'll be very satisfied with Pat's. Only thing is it's a little away from downtown but worth it

I was in town for the Army-Navy game and of course, everyone says go to Geno's and Pat's. I was surprised that Pat's only has 3 stars for being such a popular place (and Geno's has 2.5 yikes). 

My boyfriend wanted to grab one last cheese steak before heading back home, so we stopped by on a Sunday morning around 10:30a.m. There was still a good couple few eating already, so we each grabbed a sandwich, both with mushrooms, cheese and peppers. 

The food came out super fast which is a pro, but compared to John's Pork Roast Pork (which makes everything to order), the quality didn't cut it. The bread was pretty soggy in some parts of the sandwich, the onions weren't grilled enough to be soft. I did, however, like the peppers at Pat's a lot more. And I loved the huge heap of whole peppers they have on the stand -- spicy but delicious. Overall, the sandwich was a little bland for me and I had to eat a few of those peppers to get through. 

Definitely seems more of a drunk food spot , esp. since it's open 24 hours. For a quality cheese steak, I'd go back to John's Pork Roast!

--- Short Synopsis ---

Pats and Geno's are a must stop (tourist) destination for any Philly visitor! Pats more so because it is better and the original!

Pats cheesesteaks are about the steak! In terms of proportions of meat to bread, Pats seems to have a nice good amount of steak. This is both a blessing and a curse. 

--- Detailed Review ---

For parking, there is street parking nearby as people come and go from Pats and Geno's. Pats has specific instructions on how to order, which is placed right before the ordering window. Just read and follow instructions. You can practice while you're waiting in line. For example, a cheesesteak with onions and cheese whiz would be "one wiz with." Pats, like Geno's, is cash only and a normal cheesesteak is (currently) $10. This price range seems to be the norm around Philly.

My favorite part of Pats cheesesteaks is the meat! They put a nice portion on the cheesesteak and it oozes out juices and grease! With this in mind, make sure you eat it over a table, so the juices and grease don't get on your clothes. 

With the large amount of meat, the (soft) bread and onions can fade into the background of the cheesesteak, which some would enjoy. Personally, I wish the onions and bread had a more prominent role. Also, the cheese and onions are put on top of meat/cheesesteak. This allows for a greater visual appeal, but makes it less practical to eat. The onions and melted cheese can easily fall off the sandwich onto your hands, face, table, etc. As stated before, make sure you eat over a table to avoid the drippings getting on your clothes. 

Nonetheless, still a delicious cheesesteak!

Pats is definitely something to try if you're visiting Philly!!

Filthy...tables all dirty, workers handling food with their hands...disgusting!
Afraid to eat there because of filth & germs!

This McDonalds is horrible and GHETTO! Mostly the customer service....the workers are extremely young, rude, and don't get your order right...there were a pack of workers standing at the pay window.  I saw two of them playing clapping games in the background, the other one was staring at me like she wanted to fight me. Lol Where is the manager here?

I've had three cheesesteaks in Philly and this is my favorite one. Why? I like a sandwich that is NOT dry. I got a cheesesteak with cheez wiz and cooked onions and mushrooms and I thought it was delicious (by delicious I mean fatty, hurts my stomach, and makes me want to hit the gym as soon as my food digests). Lots of outdoor seating. I did not spy a bathroom. Cheesesteak and a drink will run you $12.

Make no mistake, this is HANDS DOWN the worst McDonald's you'll ever visit, if you decide not to heed the countless warnings above and below this one. Do yourself a favor and just go to the location at 2400 W Oregon Ave., it's literally 5 minutes away and 110% better.

On my recent trip to Philadelphia I had to have a Cheesesteak and Pat's was the first place we decided to try.

There was a line but these folk have it down in terms of moving people through quickly. All your hear as your get closer to the window is multiple people yelling: "Next!" "Next!" But no complaints from me, as it was pushing over 90 degrees the day I was there so the sooner I was out of the sun the better.

In terms of the Cheesesteak- It was ok. I certainly wasn't blown away. I loved the bread it was served on. Fresh and tasty. We went with the steak, cheese whiz and onions. Together they made nice combination. However, the meat by itself was a little flavorless. No seasoning what so ever.

Overall, a good sandwich but I don't see myself rushing back the next time I'm in Philly.

Note: Cash only

When I was in New Orleans I asked a local where I could get some authentic southern fried chicken.  Much to my surprise she chuckled and said that she honestly preferred Popeyes.....so I had to try it.

Now I haven't eaten fast food since I was in high school, with the exception of Taco Bell and Chipoltle.  I am reviewing Popeys restaurant the same way I would critique any food producing establishment that takes my money...with brutal honesty.  Also, I was dared to write a review for this place so I couldn't pass up the challenge. Here it goes:

It was a cool September evening. I was in my apartment when I found myself being drawn to my kitchen window by a buzzing red and yellow light.  Like a moth to a flame I left my apartment and walked towards the red lights which led me to Popeys Chicken. I was welcomed by oil drenched air and a chicken gizzard smell which stayed on my clothes for a few days. The staff didn't really give a damn that I was there and they hit that point home by not responding to my request for recommendations.  

I ordered the blackened chicken combo with mashed potatos and rice and beans and while I was eating it I could hear myself getting fatter.  I entered a size 6 and left needing a car cover as a jacket.  I also found myself wanting to get a lower back tattoo and pick up truck as I finished my second piece of chicken.

After I waddled home, I lost all interest in current events, cross word puzzles, and soy lattes. I vowed from that night forward to only wear elastic jogging pants and eat all of my meals out of cool whip containers.  I stopped going to work and found a side gig grooming dogs under the table since I was too lazy to get a real dog grooming license.  Every time I get the urge to be productive and wear real pants I combat the feeling by walking to Popeys and ordering either the shrimp po boy or the large tub of Mardi Gras Sauce.  I don't quite remember my life before the Bayou Secret Sauce but I wouldn't trade my dependency on blood pressure pills for anything...well maybe for the double fried crispy dark meat bucket.
Solid spot.  Good place to eat outside when it's warm.  No complaints.  Better places in east Passyunk, but solid if you're wanting the Mexican.
There chicken burritos are amazing !!! Best in the city well worth the 13$...i live around the corner and been going there for years the margaritas and there Cadillacs are amazing

I came here to try their famous Philly cheesesteak and I arrived here around midnight on October 20th. The sandwich was a tad bit dry for my liking, each Philly came up about 11$! This is a cash only place, but there is atms around the area. The location was pretty nice because there was a bunch of bars around. They're also open 24/7 so when i arrived there wasn't a line and no wait for your sandwich
Bought a sandwich from both spots. The cheesesteak tastes better than Geno's, but the fries and building needs work. Truly a tourist sandwich. I don't have to go back.

Gino's or Pat's,,, decided on Pat's this morning. And, taking a bit of a risk, instead of the usual provolone, gonna finally try the Whiz.

Got the  cheesesteak, Whiz, wit. I guess the best way to describe the cheese wiz is, if you like the cheese in Kraft Macaroni & Cheese, you will probably like this cheesesteak. 

I'd have to say the cheesesteak was pretty good,  about a 7. But, now that I've tried it,  will probably go back to my old way, a mixture of provolone and sharp provolone "wit"their grilled onions.
.
Made for a great breakfast.

Now I know why the name King of Steaks! This was the winner of the Philly Cheesesteak Sandwich. We got the whiz with onions and let me tell you every bite was perfect, perfect balance of onions, cheese and steak. This was my ultimate favorite Philly cheesesteak sandwich. 

We also order some fries but they weren't fresh or hot, seems like they were sitting out for a while (not ideal for me) but they had a good crunchy to them. 

I didn't like the sitting or the fact that the sandwich is not wrap when served (compared to Geno's across the street) 

But overall this is the place to get your Philly Cheesesteak Sandwich!

This place is pretty good.  It's right across the street from Geno's and since the line looked really long at Geno's, I thought I'd try Pat's instead.  There are clear instructions at the side of the ordering window so you know how it works.  

Step 1: Wit or witout onions.
Step 2: add ons/ type of sandwich
Step 3: pay

Next window is for sides, drink, etc.  

Tables are outside and fairly clean when I was there.  You're pretty much surrounded by neighborhood traffic.  There's a pepper and condiment bar that consists of big, yummy pickled peppers, ketchup, mustard, and black pepper.  

My sandwich of choice: provolone wit onions.  Pretty good.  I've actually had better in California, though I'm excited to try some Philly Yelp recommends for better cheese steak.  I know that Pat's and Geno's are more for tourist and there are better finds elsewhere in the city.  

Pat's was good for a lazy afternoon after the Italian Market. Cheap, fast, filling, and yummy.  Worth a try.

I haven't tried all the spots on Temple's campus, but I like this one. The prices are good, the service is fast and courteous, and the food is decent. So far I've had a gyro, the buffalo chicken sandwich, and the french toast. All were pretty good for fast food and hit the spot. Not exactly exciting or sublime, but fine and what I was expecting.
This is a very sloppy sandwich but it's so delicious and not greasy. Heads up please make sure you know what to order. The line is long but it moves super fast. Everything is delicious

Quickly becoming my favorite place for vegan Mexican food in Philly. The burritos are incredible. I had the wet option with vegan chorizo. Easily the best burrito I've had since going vegan, just delicious - and huge, you definitely won't leave hungry. I've also had the vegan fajitas with seitan , smoked tofu, and mushrooms. This was also amazing, the smoked tofu is especially tasty.
Why are they considered the "King of Steaks"? They are the worst!

The Best Cheesesteak in the United States!! Since 1930 that says it all. The People that work there are Great Hard working people and the food is AWESOME!!! Thank you Chef Frank for carry on the Family Tradition

This Chick-fil-A puts the restaurant name to shame. The staff was rude not only to their patrons but to their fellow co-workers. No one cared about getting the order right or doing a good job. Our food came out cold and dry, as if it had been sitting under the heat lamp for hours. Don't waste your time, even if you have 3+ hours to kill in this airport.

I'll summarize this place as horse meat on a soggy 
Roll with something that is suppose to be cheese but
Is more like a yellow chemical, service is vulgar and annoying!

Super soggy. We don't usually eat at KFC, but tonight we were craving it. When we got home and opened it up, it was heard trying to find 1 crispy piece of chicken! Ridiculous. Also they were out of potato wedges.

Thankfully last Friday all of the issues I bitched about in March were more or less corrected.

The store was very clean and the staff was actually cleaning the entire time we were there.  Partially that was accomplished because even though it was during what I would have assumed would have been a busy lunch rush, the place was deserted.  Over the course of twenty minutes every table got wiped, the soda fountain nozzles all were taken off & cleaned and all trash was taken out. #impressive

The food itself was typical Subway dreck where even when it's right it's still only right to a point as the bread was too soft almost like it was underdone and the apples in the cooler were mostly brown but whatever.

For better or worse it's cheap, it's filling and the location is perfect for when we're in town.

[Pt 2 of 2]

As it was my first visit to Philly this summer, how could I not try Pat's & Geno's?  I know it's a tourist trap and the line takes about 15-20mins during weekend lunch hours.

The cheese steaks at Pat's looks appealing, with a huge pile of chopped rib eye beef overflowing out of the roll.  With grease dripping down your hand with each bite, it's a greasy mess to eat.  It requires at least 3 napkins to eat.  I also got a huge chunk of meat that wouldn't break and I almost choked on it.  The tendon wouldn't break so I had to spit it out.

I prefer Geno's just because it seems like the healthier option.  5 out of 5 people in my little road trip agreed.  The flavors were very similar.  They must use the same seasoning (salt & pepper).

Service was unfriendly and we were treated like cattle.  We were rushed to order and they moved onto the next cow.  There is a ridiculous 2nd line for drinks & fries.  However I prefer the fries from Pat's.  They had a good crispy exterior, as if they were thickly battered.  

I got the cheese steak with the provolone cheese & onions.  Food Feuds with Chef Michael Symon from the Food Network came here and they won the giant trophy on the show but only cuz Pat's had whiz on their steak.  I don't think it was a fair match since they compare apples to apples (or provolone to provolone) like I did.

By far one of the best tasting cheese fries I've ever had in my life.... can't figure out if it ranks first or second but without a doubt it's in the top 3... after I left I wish I got two order... sooo much delicious cheeeeese. Was wondering what if I had gotten extra cheese OMGGGGGG

Got to this place in a good time as there was zero line. It is a good cheesesteak, but cannot say it was anything amazing or worth any better than a 3 star. Would i go back? maybe, but there are definitely better spots out there for cheesesteaks. I had the wiz/wit (cheese wiz and onions). Again, good, but can't say I would recommend this spot due to great food.
I went to buy a chicken sandwich and when i took a bite the chicken was slimy and tasted like fish the first bite in

I really liked how you can do a personal pie, I did half personal, half red vine. It was really good, they also have different sauces and cheeses to choose from if you wanted to mix it up. They also have an upstairs seating area. Would deff come back here!
Best soft pretzels!!! It's amazing to live just less than a mile here. Me and my toddler love their pretzels. He always asks for it!!

This place has the worst customer service. I bought the philly cheesesteak and I brought it back to my car. Because of the oil, I put the sandwich in a plastic bag and I decided I wanted more cheese. So i went back and they said I could pay a dollar more so I said sure and gave them the sandwich. They said they cant because it doesnt look like their sandwich. I literally bought it a few minutes ago but they still refused. Wtf is this service?

Atmosphere is great. Very clean and well lit (I'm not a fan of dark eateries). Food was very fresh and yummy. I love the fact that we can choose how much ginger and wasabi we want and they don't charge extra. Service is fantastic as well. Very friendly and helpful.

The employees here are pretty much affronted by the prospect of doing anything. They look at you when you walk up to the empty counter like you have 19 heads, roll their eyes, sigh, and ask if they can take your order, while you're clearly still reviewing the options. Then tap impatiently and sigh some more if you take more than 10 seconds to decide what you want.

The fries are always cold, the burgers toppings are slapped on haphazardly with ketchup on one corner and a pound of mayo all over. The nuggets are like ice every time I've had them here. Avoid. I'd rather eat at Ikea.

Extremely casual place...in a little corner and busy al the time: that's how good the cheesesteak is! In my opinion, this is the best Philly cheesesteak...cheese with onions...they even have a sign that teaches you how to order the steak. It's no big deal if you order the wrong way at all for newbies like me the first time I tried it. Employees are super friendly even at their busiest time which is I think in the afternoon. The line moves quick though and watching them prepare the cheesesteak is awesome...and they're fast! Some people prefer Geno's ...I'm not a fan of their steak...stick to Pat's and you won't go wrong! I swear and I love food! 
This is a must for any visitor in Philadelphia...if you have a long layover at the airport, uber or lyft is about $10 maybe one way so you can try the best Philly cheesesteak in my opinion.

Went here for dinner after running the Philadelphia marathon. The fantastic supply of vegan options drew me here and this was great food for a hungry runner. They offered complimentary chips and two types of delicious salsa. I ordered the vegan chorizo burrito, which was tasty, especially so accompanied by celebratory margaritas. I drank the classic on the rocks, which were good--not the best marg I've ever had, but definitely yummy (sounds like from other reviews there may be better options when choosing a margarita here). My only complaint is that they nickle and dime you on things--$.50 to add some pico to the burrito, $4 for what turned out to be a small smear of guac., and $3 to make the burrito wet (an option I didn't take). 

But, service was great (at the bar) (and when my partner couldn't even identify any guac. in his burrito they removed the $4 upcharge), and the neighborhood bar atmosphere was great for someone visiting Philly.

Tasty Twisters is a small bakery/pretzel easy to miss but could be a solid spot. Stopped by this last Friday for a pizza pretzel. I haven't had one in years! The place seems a bit odd though. Nobody works the counter area. There is a doorbell to ring for service. That itself is and issue. The line was quite long and the wait was extensive. The lady quoted me 5 minutes but it took 25 minutes! That's a long time for a pretzel and it's just flat out ridiculous. If I hadn't paid in advance I would have walked out. I love supporting small mom and pop businesses but they need to step up their game. The pretzel while good simply isn't worth the wait.

I grew up in Northeast PA and I was told, "You only go to Pat's." Don't tell my friends but yesterday I tried both Pat's and Geno's side by side. I am thrilled to say that the winner was...Pat's!

I'll be honest, the cheese steaks are very similar in taste. Pat's has a creamier and more flavorful cheese. Geno's was a bit greasier, which affected the taste. 

Yes it is all unhealthy, but yes it is delicious. Go to Pat's - you won't be disappointed. They don't need the flashy colors or lights, it is just good food.

I would otherwise never come here (ever) but two things led me to their door. I got a T-Mobile Tuesdays offer that I simply couldn't refuse and I suddenly remembered all the pre-covid hype over that chicken sandwich that mysterious disappeared. 

The strip mall this Popeyes is at is filthy. I can't understand it. I begrudgingly proceeded on. It was clean inside, a few folks in line and for the most part all keeping their distance and all with masks.  

But two employees who were supposed to be fulfilling orders were casually having a conversation about..... of all things.... other job interviews. They were actually standing in front of a line full of people, tongs and empty chicken baskets in hand having this pow wow until finally the woman at the register reminded them that they were already at a job. 

When I finally get to the front I tell her my name because that's all I need to do. Ordered on the app. My food should be bagged and ready to go. NOPE.

She says yes Renee your ticket is right there and pointed to it sitting in an order window in front of piles and piles of glowing orange fried chicken. So I move aside and wait, and wait, and wait until I finally I snap at all of them and ask why is my ticket still sitting there and four people behind me have left with big ass orders of chicken!! WTF y'all!! That's what it took for me to get my meal, unbelievable. 

A young man finally got down to business and stuffed that box full of as much chicken as he could and threw in an apple pie too. On the positive side, that chicken was good.

This is a pretty solid fast food chicken joint.  I ordered 15 bites, 3 tenders, and some sauces via Doordash.  The tenders and bites are super crunchy, and they came just as the name implies--hot and tender.  The sauces were nothing to write home about, though I do have to commend them on getting their Korean BBQ sauce to actually taste like gochujang.  The Honey BBQ was way too smokey for me to enjoy though.  The good thing about the sauce, however, is that for the $.50 price you get a LOT.  Overall, I'd say if you like chicken tenders, give this place a try!

Haven't been to this location, in a while until a few days ago , and it was horrible.  I asked for a baconator without the bun and the looked and laughed at me , like it was impossible to do.I had to walk them thru the process of how it's done at other location. I ordered the triple and they gave me a double , and I paid for extra bacon an recieved none (extra). I will never purchase from that location again.

The service here is incredibly incompetent. I observed a manager (woman with Black hair) engage in a full blown argument with a party of 15. From what I heard, the service was so slow that they missed the happy hour. I can attest that the service here is REALLY slow. I also have never seen a manager engage in an argument with guests. Inside of a conciliatory tone, the manager assumed a condescending one. I left the restaurant with no intention of returning. I would hate to be the next victim of this terrible service. The food isn't even Mexican.

I had the cheesesteak wit onions, wit provolone, and fries.  Had the souvenir soda, but I was thinking the souvenir soda was just a cup, but it is one of the souvenir type cups from an amusement park, with the bendy straws and cap on the top of the straw.  The cheesesteak was a bit dry, the fries were good, and so was the cheesesteak.

Stopped in during a lay over.. a typical food court style Chipotle. The line was wrapped around to the other business. The staff was really efficient by working everyone through as fast as possible. I counted at least five people working just the front serving line. Each one of the toppings had just been recently cut up and placed out. I ordered a burrito. Everything is a la cart... you can ask for chips and a drink if you want.

I had the cheesesteak whiz wit (with onions), and it was the worst cheesesteak sandwich I've ever had. The meat was not chopped, which is not a big deal except that it was tough to chew and had absolutely zero flavor. The bread was a soggy mess, and the cheese whiz didn't have much flavor either.

Better than geone's because there's more meat, it's less salty and has better flavor! 

However keep in mind it's $2-$3 more expensive. 
BUT net net, both were pretty bad cheesesteaks. But if I had to pick between the two (pats vs geone) id pick here. 

Am I ever going back to Pats? No. 
I'd give Geone like one star. 

Go to Sonny's for a better cheesesteak.

This is pretty much a tourist trap along with Geno's across the street.  Ordered a cheesesteak wit and onions and a regular cheesesteak and they were bad.   My son said the sandwich wit tasted like a hot pocket ha ha.  Very little meat inside and stale bread.  If you ask me I think they paid to be on tv shows (food network etc.) Save your money and go to one of the other cheesesteak places in Philly.

Bottom line of the story that I had with this place, I ordered a Cheesesteak Sandwich but what i got when i opened the wrapper is that there's no cheese on top. So I went back to the cashier to ask for cheese on top, and that i'll even pay extra if anything. What I got in return was rude attitude "That steak does not look like ours, so we can't add cheese on top. You probably got this across the street and came here for cheese, we can't help you". This response is outrageous and disappointing. Never coming back here again.
Steak was good not the best i had  , very fast service and great customer service

Great pizza you can customize with as many toppings as you want. The blood orange lemonade is the TRUTH...a must have. Jake was awesome & hooked our pizzas up. Check this place out to get a quick meal that worth every penny!

Simply stated: No self-respecting Philadelphia native would ever eat here. What you will find here are tourists, Rangers fans, "bros" from South Jersey, and people who just plain don't know any better. The meat and cheese are always cold, the rolls soggy, onions undercooked, and there is hardly any meat on the sandwich at all. It's not the impression you want to get of a cheesesteak.

Do yourself a favor and go to John's Roast Pork, Gooey Louie's, or pretty much anywhere else in South Philly that isn't on that tourist trap corner.

While we are talking about a cheesesteak spot, this place is heavily hyped.  Bright lights, features on the Food and Travel channels....the whole nine.  How can you not think that you're in for an amazing Philly cheesesteak experience?  One that makes you want to start running up the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art and jumping around in victory like Rocky Balboa.

Yeaaaaaaaaaa.......NO!  I came on a Sunday evening to check out and compare Philly's finest in comfort food.  I realize that nothing could match up to my beloved chicken finger sub but I'm an open minded person when it comes to deciding what would finish in 2nd place.  

Service was shoddy.  Order taker was very nonchalant and disinterested.  I'm a city boy myself so I get it in terms of the blue collar attitude for a blue collar meal but still.....etiquette?

The cheesesteak itself was pathetic in terms of appearance.  It looked haphazardly tossed together, cheese whiz slopped onto it.  Another glaring thing was it was missing.....the rest of the meat!!!  Cheesesteaks are known for being packed with meat are they not?  Did a badger manage to get to mine before it reached my hands?  If I had a voice like the narrator from "Unsolved Mysteries" we could sho' nuff figure this thing out. 

Alas, I took my measly little sub and ate.  Meh....meh.......MEH!  It was ok and I'm probably being generous.  Very bland and not very fulfilling.  Relatively inexpensive ($6-$7).  Good thing I had other spots to check out because otherwise I would've left Philly a sad and hungry person.  So much for brotherly love!

I wish I could give this McDonald's ZERO stars! My bf and I came to this McDonald's because it said it was open 24/7. IT IS NOT. We came at 12:45AM and we saw workers doing absolutely nothing. The drive thru had caution tape around it, but the machines seemed to be working fine. When we drove up to the first window, we were told to move to the second window and no one answered us. When we peered through the windows, the workers had headsets on and everything. If you guys aren't open 24/7, it should be stated. Have a sign or SOMETHING.

Amazing food and amazing staff! Mickey and Kevin were so patient with my husband and I as we took forever trying to decide from all of the amazing choices. 
Food came quick! Lots of topping choices and fair prices. 
The Wilsons will definitely go back!
Overrated... hot sauce states weird, don't waste your money!! Jersey makes better cheesesteaks... :)

This is honestly the worst Chipotle I've ever been to in my life. GO TO A DIFFERENT CHIPOTLE. NOT THIS ONE. I'm telling you!!!!! There's this one guy who thinks he's so tough, he works almost every single got damn day and HE PUTS THE SMALLEST F$#KING AMOUNT in whatever you order. Oh you want a burrito? They wrap it up and it's a fucking tiny little square, that's how fing empty it is. I was the only one on the line and this guy sped through racing about to have an asthma attack breathing heavily all over my food and putting little droplets on my burrito over here acting like there was a fcking zombie apocalypse....couldn't give me a normal amount...I honestly walk 5 more philly blocks just so I don't have to go to this terrible chipotle. If you go to this location you're wasting your money. OHHH you ask them to add a little more because they put basically nothing on??? They say that'll be EXTRA or that'l be DOUBLE....are you serious???? Never experienced anything like this place. It's mostly this 1 guy but he works every single day so you will obviously get him. So am i judging this whole place basically on one employee? Yes. But he's the one who puts every single thing on every single one of your meals so basically no I'm not. Moral of the story is fire that tool bag. Does he get paid more if he puts less food in your order????? He seriously must. AVOID PLACE UNTIL THIS MAN GETS FIRED

I was making a list for Yelpers looking to travel to Philadelphia. This was the first place I thought of. Since I was already looking at it I decided I'd take a look at he reviews. Anyway all this made me realize I've never reviewed it! 
I've been eating at this place since I first moved to Philadelphia. I like it better than the northern liberties location. Partly due to nostalgia but mostly due to the amount of space. So much more room at this one. Meeting friends and sitting outside is one of my favorite past times. 
I've been here for drinks, brunch, events, dinner.... you name it. 
The chips and salsa you get before each meal is fantastic. I always save it to sprinkle on my meal later. The vegan fajitas are my go to dish. I love it. I love it the next day too. If I was picking favorite dishes in Philadelphia and not just restaurants this dish would make the top of that list. I wouldn't consider myself a Mexican food super fan. so I don't know how it stacks up to authentic Mexican.  I know it's pretty goddamn good for Philadelphia. 
I actually was just here last weekend. I got the two eggs meal. Two eggs, rice, chorizo and beans. It was delicious. 
In short if you're planning a vacation and you plan those around cool places to eat....
I get the Wit Wiz!!!! It's so good!!!! Better than Geno's in my opinion. I love the wiz and the cooked onions with the steak. It's really simple but so good. Worth the experience.

The chips and salsa made my heart LITERALLY sing. Perfectly salty, crispy and indeed...bottomless. Served with heaping bowls of verde and red salsas that tasted fresher than fresh. Triangles of heavenly bliss chips. 

The rest, is a blur. So many chips. So much salsa. 

Oh, right...that salad with chicken lasted me TWO MEALS. Excellent as well. 

Indeed, I'll be back for that Blood Orange margarita (it was a bit early for me, but...). Holy hell, this place has got some goods. Go get 'em.
The first time I went to Philadelphia for cheesesteaks I try both Genos and Pats. Since that day I never looked back and stuck with Pat's King of Steaks! So don't eat a miSTEAK!!!!

This place is awful.  The breading on the chicken strips is very thick, crusty and has no flavor.  I tried the spicy dark sandwich and it was inedible.  The sweet sriracha sauce was like sugar syrup and they use way too much.  Not sure why you would label a sandwich spicy and then lather it with this disgusting sweet sauce.  I was so disappointed with this meal.  I saw the bad reviews, but wanted to try it since it is new.  Needless to say, I'll never go back.

There was more breading on my chicken then actual chicken.  Maybe they should call this place HNT crispy fried breading instead.

First time in Philadelphia so I wanted to try the original (don't @ me)! I got a whiz wit peppers/mushrooms. It was solid! After a day of traveling, it was what I wanted: quick comfort food. Pat's/Uber Eats had it to my hotel in 20 mins. It's not going to blow your mind. In fact, the way you're imagining that it tastes is exactly how it tastes. I'd definitely recommend it as an alternative to chain fast food.
Placed an online order and it took the over 2 HOURS to get it ready.  I don't know what's going on at this location but maybe it's time to hire some people that want to work.  This place is a joke.

Came to this location after hours. I pulled into the drive thru only to sit there for 20 mins. After knocking on the windows and calling for someone they finally got on the mic and said that they were closed. This place sucks! And they never get your order right.
Phil Gattuso punched his Lunch Bucket List here at Pat's.  For this, and the excellent food, 5 stars.

This is the worst and slowest Taco Bell I have been to in my entire life. 45 minutes to make a chalupa seems excessive to me, but I've never been in the gauntlet of a Taco Bell kitchen.

That being said, there is nothing better than a delicious 7-layer burrito smothered with hot sauce at 2AM after a night out. My feelings about this Taco Bell are thus conflicted, and so, three stars.

We waited 30 minutes for someone to take our order. Then I had to flag down someone just take our drink order, who wasn't even our waitress. We would have just left but we already started eating the chips and felt bad just walking out. Then it took another 20 minutes for them to bring two weak mojitos. We planned on eating dinner and ordering more drinks but we couldn't wait all night for someone to notice us. This was my second unimpressive visit and I will not be back.

The pizza is good and I love their lemonade varieties. But just a tip for people with IBD/IBS, I get viciously sick every time I eat here. That is my own choice to eat it. The only other thing I don't like is when workers make comments about what you order and kind of shame you over it. Let me build my pizza and eat what I enjoy please.

After watching YouTube Videos for Reviews, my husband and I were actually afraid to try Pat's because the people we watched on YouTube didn't list Pat's as one of their favorites out of all the cheesesteak places they tried. BUT.. we went to a highly recommended/favorite spot (which I will keep unnamed) and was highly disappointed. My husband and I decided that we should eat another cheesesteak elsewhere to redeem the cheesesteak glory and we decided to come here. We were very surprised on how good it actually was!!

This is a cash only establishment I believe, so make sure you have cash on hand. You order your cheesesteak from one window and fries/soda from another window. They are 24/7 and we came at like 9:30AM. Haha. 

We ordered a cheesesteak with whiz, onions, and peppers. Side of fries and soda. The cheesesteak was literally done in like 10 seconds, which concerned me since it may be a bit old, but whatever. I already bought it. Fries took about 3-5mins.

Cheesesteak was DELICIOUS!! Not too wet or dry. Had lots of cheese and I love cheese!! I don't think their meats are seasoned, but the cheese and peppers give it flavor. We were shocked on how good it was. They do have pickled hot peppers on the side, which was a great compliment to the cheesesteak. The bread held everything together nicely. The fries were good. Nothing special. I wished they cooked it a bit longer. 

Overall, we would totally recommend this place way way way before we would recommend the other place we've eaten. We were happy to eat this cheesesteak right before we left Philly!

McDonalds corporate really needs to come in and investigate what's going on in this store. You always have 10-15 children working here just tapping away about their personal lives in front of all the customers and half of them just sitting at the tables not even working and just chilling with their friends. Very unprofessional. On top of that, the people at the registers are always rude, showing the customers how much they don't want to be there. I never seen one person working here have a smile on their face and always looking like as if someone just died in their family and the world was out to get them. Maybe it's just the location, but out of all the different McDonald's I have ever been to, this one is by FAR the WORST one I have ever been to and seen. Plus, they skimp out on the food, especially the fries, so don't be surprise if you see it only being half full. It's considered to be the "norm" over here. I guess they need to save every little penny they can make especially with all the children that don't actually work here to get paid for sitting around and chilling with their friends.

This is the absolute most disgusting McDonald's I've ever visited. Inventory is always out of stock. Orders take excessively longer than usual to fill. The last time I went here, I had to wait 15 minutes for a single McDouble. Do NOT waste your time here.

Pat's the best Philly Cheese Steak in town, a must go when in South Philadelphia, located by the Italian Market. I never had them better, just almost as good, or worst. 

Don't feel intimidated when you come here for the first time, and before ordering you are reading the 'Rules of Ordering PCS'. Just order and when you get it wrong, well just get another one after you finish the first. My motto at Pat's is; eat two and then one to go.

 '3 is the Magic Number'

This is just a place for true Philadelphians to take tourists as real Philadelphians don't frequent Pat's or Geno's... they go to Tony Luke's, John's Roast Beef or Jim's!

This is merely a tourist attraction for those who are truly not in the know as to what is the best and where to go.
It's great for the price and awesome that you can create your own pizza and make it healthy! Not the best pizza but when you're hungry its perfect.
Simple you want the Best you go to the Best Pat's King of Steaks! Now they have delivery all over United States!! I was the first to order in the USA! Hey Philly Michigan says Hello

I just moved to Philly and wanted to see what a cheesesteak is to locals, so I came here with some friends who said they like Pat's. I've always loved getting Philly cheesesteaks whenever it was on the menu when I was living out of state...but I really don't like Cheese Whiz and I'm probably going to get stoned for this. I wasn't impressed. Okay, I got the Pizza Steak, not the original...but I don't know what the hype is about besides the history. Also not that friendly of staff...the line was long and they only accept cash and were about to give us the boot in line for not knowing what we wanted when we got up to order lol.

Wish I could give zero stars I didn't eat here I couldn't it's DISGUSTING!! What is the health department number? I went into the bathroom and it was shit every where on the toilet and floor! Rule of thumb if the bathroom is dirty the whole place is dirty ps I could not stomach it to snap a picture

SO SO DELICIOUS!!!! amazing customer service and fast!! we were looking for a good sushi place and just came across this place. The gentleman at the counter was so nice and even invited us to come back tomorrow!
I personally love it here even though it's a tourist spot, it just has that special taste. The fact that it's open 24 hours is also a plus.

Ok our family from Los Angeles decides to visit both places for the show down.   Being from LA, we don't believe in cheese wiz as we have a more refine taste.   We ordered the cheesesteak with Provolone and onions ($11) from both.   We sat down to try both.  Looking at both cheesesteak, initially they look exactly alike, except Pat's seems to be juicier as we unwrap both.

The meat in Pat's was a bit more tender than Gino and definitely more juicy.
Gino was too dry and chewy.  Both buns appears to be the same but with the juices flowing out of Pat's, it made it easier to chew through the buns.

We decided to go back to Pat's for another cheesesteak but with mushrooms and onions($12j, again nice and juicy but the meat seems to be more chewier this time.   The mushroom appears to be like those canned button mushrooms which I really don't care for.   

Overall they are not too bad. Skip the fries with cheese($6j small cup.  They are awful.

Back in LA, I rather eat a good roast beef sandwich or pastrami sandwich from The Hat with chili fries, for the same price.

This place has the absolute dumbest employees. Went in to get a gallon of Cane Sweet Lemonade for $5.39 paid with a $10 and got change of $4.61( trust this is all important). This broad goes to the damn soda machine to fill up the gallon, ummmm no miss!! Gimme me my money back. So shes gets the manager who tries to give me $4.61 and tried to argue me down that she was right. Finally got my money back but geez they cant even count.

Recently move to the Philly area and you better believe I get asked about how many Philly Cheese Steaks I eat a week. Well Pat's has definitely helped to keep my numbers respectable and keep my LA friends jelly.

I have had cheese whiz and white cheese and I can't believe I would say this, but when at Pat's go cheese whiz, it delicious. 

Quick tips, CASH ONLY, nothing worse than coming here starving after a late night and not having cash, luckily there are ATMs a couple minutes away that will be happy to charge you $3 for a withdrawal.  They have 2 lines one for food one for drinks. Also when you're in Philly people want you to order fast, so make sure you know what you want before its your turn, don't be a noob.

Great fries and according to my fiancé better than Genos. We tried both while we were visiting and being a vegetarian I can at least vouch for the fries being way superior to Genos. Sorry Genos! Pats is the original and is the way to go. I also love their cheeky signage.

While in Philadelphia we had our own challenge of which is better. My opinion is Pat's for the win. The bread was very fresh and had a great flavor. The staff was quick to take our order and our sandwich was ready in minutes. Plenty of seating. Very clean area. If you are going to choose only one, pick Pat's for your cheesesteak sandwich.

Where's the meat?  This is a cross between a tourist novelty and a profit mill. Definitely not for the serious foodie! In my opinion the people that give this high marks have either never had a cheesesteak proper,  have minimal taste in food, or they just think they're supposed to like it because they come here with other people who also think that they're supposed to like it - kind of reminds me of pet rocks!

Horrible 1st time experience there. First of all the trash outside the restaurant was busting out of the dumpster. That was a complete turn off for me but we were hungry and decided to give the place a shot. We order our food but when it was time to order drinks they pretty much was out of all the good soda including lemonade. With that being said I got a drink I didn't want. So when it was time to get our order at the drive up window, this kid hands my girlfriend a dirty can of soda and gave me a small drink even though I was supposed to get a large one. He said he was getting me a second drink because they had no large size cups left. At that point I told my girlfriend to get our money back! We got our money and went to Taco Bell...

Im TIRED of the crummy service!!!! Inattentive, slow to get food, every staff member is in their own world. Good margaritas but the rest leaves a lot to be desired. I keep trying, but I think Im maybe done with it all....
Terrible customer service and even worse delivery service. Never use this place. Just trying to help you out...

Solid three stars for food,  ambience and service.  I wasn't exactly overwhelmed with joyous feelings but not crazily disappointed either.  

My dining partner and I arrived at about 915pm on Memorial day Sunday. Honestly,  when he suggested this place, I kinda cringed because of the usual mess of a parking situation. But he assured me that most folks had done down the shore, there were plenty of spots and there were! Yay! No wasting a quarter tank of gas trying to find a parking spot in South Philly's super crowded streets. 

We wanted to dine outside, so we were told that there was a twenty minute wait.  We looked around a spotted millions of empty tables and they didn't seem short staffed, but um okay.  Snagged two seats at the bar and I tried a blood orange margarita on the rocks with salt. He had a mango margarita, no salt or sugar. Drum roll...... I was slightly disappointed. The taste was great, didn't really have much tequila and at $9 a pop I want some kick!  He said his drink was fine, but he really wasn't a drinker so what did he know? Lol. We got the your table is ready text, settled up the tab and sat our table.  

Sitting there having my margarita, I had some time to look around and take in the scenery.. This place is uber hipster-y. Is that a word?  :::shrugs::::.  Or should I say, the folks that frequent the restaurant. Anyway, the noise level here is LOUD.. Like I'm at a Naughty By Nature concert screaming "Hip Hop Hooray" loud.  It was annoying, that I practically lost my voice trying to talk to my date. Ugh. I would not bring someone here on a date ever again. Just can't hear the person. I know my server got tired of me saying HUH?!?. Somewhere outside was a dog howling. Behind us was a some college crowd of folks that clearly just turned 21 and having their first round of drinks.  Lots of screaming and yelling. My annoyance meter is creeping up slowly but surely. 

Anyway, the place is dim and dark.  Kinda sexy but the noise takes that down a notch. The patio is huge and can seat well over 20-25 tables easily without fear of the server dropping hot coffee on your head or bumping into the next table.  The chairs are not made for long time dining and sitting.  You eat,  drink and be gone.  Lol . Those chairs are metal. Metal and metal. 

Now,  onto the food.  Most of the menu is in Spanish I believe and to be honest I didn't understand some of it.  There were some English descriptive words though. I ordered the Cabrito dish which was some pulled goat dish . I'd never tried goat so why not? He ordered the enchiladas. Server brought out a warm bowl of chips and two glorious bowls of Verde and Rojo(a) salsa... Ohhhhhh baby, love at first sight. Both had a slight kick.. Nice! Me want more!!! 

Twenty minutes later and my plate arrives.. On one side, is the pulled goat with roasted garlic and a cucumber salad. On the other, was literally a SPOONFUL of white rice with what looked like a sprinkling of cilantro and refried beans.  My plate looked so damned empty,  I was sure that I was missing something. I'd think a "platter" at a Mexican restaurant woukd come with tortillas. So I asked another server if it came with tortillas and he gave a flat NO. But does offer to bring some out.  After six or seven minutes,  plate almost gone...comes my super warm tortillas.  They save my life and stomach because I knew I was going home hungry. 

The pulled goat was OK. The taste was flavorful but a bit tough and hard to chew.  Loved the refried beans.. Plain old white rice with cilantro, keep that away. Or at least give me enough to fill me up.  Sheesh,  a spoonful? Sweet Lord.. That wasn't enough to quiet that howling dog a few tables over.. 

At $17, I'd like more food.. Seriously, I was still hungry after leaving.  

Overall,  would I come back? Probably. For happy hour or any time they have a special. I don't think they serve your money's worth here.  And on any other day, pair bad parking with overpriced food and drinks, you'll probably be pissed .

You know what you're going to get when you walk into a McDonalds. Unfortunately that expectation is good tasting artery clogging food and mediocre service by employees who don't really want to be there. Imagine not even getting half that - because that is what you will get at this location.

RUDE does not sum up the employees of this location. One employee attempted to argue with me over the type of sauce that I originally requested for my order of nuggets. When I wanted to trade the sauce she gave me back for what I originally requested, she demanded 15 cents while the manager stood there shaking her head laughing at me. I know that she did not care about her job by the way she threw my order on the counter when it was ready and yelled "nuggets.." so arguing over 15 cents was for no reason other than inconveniencing me.

I did write corporate who followed up with me in a few months to see if the store management or regional management contacted me, which they never did. This all took place over a year ago and I have never went back and still tell the story to everyone I know.
Nothing to write home about don't get the hype. But since we were in Philadelphia we had to compare both Pats and Genos neither were great. But our family leans more towards Genos

This is one of the stands that really put the Philly Cheesesteak on the map.   It's definitely the most famous, but I would say it is not the best.   It's good, but not great.   The meat jsut didn't seem as tender or flavorful as some of the other fine purveyers of cheesesteaks in this city.   But if you're just visiting, you have to come to Pat's because everyone back home will ask if you went there.

I prefer my steaks "provolone with", as in "provolone cheese, with onions".   However, this time, I got at "whiz with" (cheese whiz with onions) because my wife wanted to split a Pat's steak and a Geno's (across the street) steak with me and taste them head-to-head.

I have to say that Pat's came in second best.

P.S.  Pat's is open 24 hours and it's cash-only.

Place is trash! From the over priced sauces that they don't even fill up or home make, to the salty chicken, BAD customer service, microwaved food, sloppy looking staff........I highly recommend you don't even waste your time or money.

I made a Yelp account just to review this place. This is HANDS DOWN the worst McDonald's in the city. People regularly drive away  from the  restaurant because the wait is so long. I've waited 20 minutes before anyone even took my order in the drive thru, received food that was only partially assembled, and on multiple occasions have been told the store could only accept cash. Service inside the store isn't any better. The folks working there are very rude and disorganized and the store is dirty. Let's be real, McDonald's does one thing, and they do it poorly, but this place still finds a way to fail at meeting even the lowest standards.
Workers are rude, bought 12 piece chicken and they charged extra for each individual sauce... makes no sense

I have no idea what everyone is talking about. Got a cheesesteak with cheez whiz as recommended. It was not great. Not the worst ever but not what I expected atall. The meat had a weird flavor although there was a ton of meat. I personally did not like it. My fiance would rate his as a 1 star also and he had his with onions. Pain in the ass to find parking only to be disappointed and didn't even finish 1/2 of my sub. I've had much better in DC. Wouldn't go again.

The sloppy joe version of philly steak slider is a feature here for a toonie $1.99. The crusty bread is a testimony to an effort to give the customer something substantial to  hold onto before you get the ooze. It all oozes out of the bun. I believe that the cheese performs best  in the microwave, and is designed to retain heat enough to burn a lip if you are not careful. But, I really am not here for the slider, I came to try the raspberry cheesecake cookie, which was less than a dollar and made the smile come to my face. I think this cookie is worth my visit. Something to smile about!

Hands down the best steaks! They are juicy, flavorful and delicious. Load'em up with the peppers and grab some napkins. You are gonna need them! The fries are good, but nothing special. Parking can get crazy around that area, but be patient. People come and go all the time. Be sure you rehearse your order before you get to the front of the line. 1 with, whiz!
FILTHY! Look these guys up on the L&I website if you need more proof. They leave the food out by the dumpster before delivering and I've seen mice.

Updated review: still a cry baby business with a butt hurt persona. Dear God don't even write anything negative or you'll be a hater. Hate on what? Shittttty food, shittty service, and shittttty weaklings that runs the place who can't take criticism. Sometimes it's best to just take what's written and change what people are not happy about, instead calling people name for people being honest that they are simply unhappy with your service. Now I understand if it's 1 or 2 reviews but it seems others are on the same page with the attitude of this establishment is highly unprofessional. Considering it running by "men"? Well.... "Man up! Pull your skirt up, stop crying over review just because your puuuuussy hurt" Jesus I feel bad for George busting his butt and Wei running his mouth destroying the business. You are seriously arguing  with people for their opinions. In all honesty I totally forgot about this place until I receive a notification which is comical. Here let me help you with some business: "everyone who's reading this, please order from this place, I dare you to write a review less than 5 stars, and I kid you not it's more entertaining than watching a live comedy at Helium."  sad truly sad.

This place gave me diarrhea so I didn't have to stay at work. I love Popeyes. I had the chicken tender combo, I could have sworn the lady said "what two sides do you want" but when I said mashed potatoes and macaroni and cheese she said "you only get one side" it was embarrassing beyond belief but it was worth it for the diarrhea.

I have yet to visit a Wendy's location that has good customer service, short lines and clean. Why call it fast food when people are waiting 15 minutes in line with ONE cashier? This location was a total mess. Dirty tables and floors. Unkempt bathroom. For a family restaurant, why wouldn't there be a changing table for moms and their babies? Quality of food and service is just poor all across the board. Makes no sense.

When I first experienced Pat's, this was the cheesesteak that others strived to beat in terms of taste and quality. It was sandwich heaven. 

Unfortunately, the passage of time has not been good to Pat's. I now recommend that you go to Pat's only when you are forced to take a tourist or you've had way, way, way too much beer to drink.  

The beef is dry, not well seasoned and i'm guessing it's USDA select grade. The provolone is tasty but the bread is barely average.  

Unfortunately, Pat's had turned into a caricature of its own old self.  maybe with the gentrification of South Philly, Pat's will up its game

I miss the old days!

Holy cow what a waste of money. I order the "Signature" sandwich.  And this is what I got. One chicken tender on roll with BBQ slipped on. I check in the bag 3 times to make sure a 2nd tender didn't fall out. But you can tell by the sauce there was never a 2nd one there.  $9 with a soda and fries! Even if the sandwich had the crispy onions it was supposed to have, it is still a huge disappointment.  I don't expect this chain to be around long.
The food was good until I found a piece of wrapper inside. Lost my appetite. The lemonade was good and the food was good up until that point.

Literally the chipotle of pizza. They made my order wrong and apologized and I ended up with two pizzas! Both of which tasted fantastic. I can get a regular pizza anywhere but for me to choose between ingredients right in front of me... and for a reasonable price. I'll chose here anytime.

Had never heard of this place until we pulled up in front of it. I knew I was coming to Philly to sample cheesesteaks but had no idea there were options outside of a plain cheesesteaks. Service was prompt. As I went to record the workers fixing the cheesesteak, my order was already prepared. The cheesesteak was great to say the least, but I plan to visit other spots to compare across Philly for a more accurate account of who to crown the best-stay tuned!

Here's the deal:  I've tried some really great burger places, but Five Guys is the best chain, and even rivals independent joints.

Highlights:  Fries are abundant!  Service from staff is polite and more than excellent.  The new-stye soda towers have SO many choices.  Lastly, and most importantly, the burgers are SO GOOD, that my wife, who is NOT a burger fan AT ALL, will not only not turn down a Five Guys, but she will finish her burger before you, guaranteed!

Tip:  If you go by yourself, it can be a tad expensive.  However, if you go with a friend/spouse, etc, you can easily share a regular fry and drink with your own Little Cheeseburger each for about $15 total.

*This review applies to all of the Five Guys i've been to in Harrisburg and Philadelphia PA and that random one in NJ that we went to!

Love cantina! Close to home and the bartender Edwin is the man! He's super attentive and makes beautiful cocktails. Funny and hard working. I had fish tacos the other night which were juicy and flavorful! My boyfriend is a chef and therefore so critical of food and he's been raving about them all day!

Rude just rude. Hangs up on you if you make a complaint criticism. His favorite line is "you are banned" okay Donald trump from ordering. ... please There's a million places to order from. They will call back and Harrass you. Look at all the responses on yelp. They are like children that can't take criticism. Let me tell you, fries are soggy. Pizza is dried. Garlic chicken wings have no taste. Terrible just terrible. Never again.

The food was mediocre all orders of my fries were soggy.....Ordered over 100.00 worth of food. Threw in a 22.00 tip hoping that maybe my order would be right but nope..... I was missing items, gave the store a call to let them know....they said they would text me and to reply with a picture of my receipt which I did. Never heard back from them, did not receive the rest of my order or a refund.....Bad Business!

Took a friend for a true Philly cheesesteak and he was wowed. He got the mushroom and it was loaded with them. The fries are awesome. Sodas are $3.50 for a small. The sign says to blame the city for the cost.

Stopped in Philly for the legit cheesesteak and I must admit I was disappointed. I got the steak with onions, peppers and wiz and it was just ok, surely nothing for me to make a point in stopping in Philly for. You can probably find a better one locally or at some of the less fancy places around town.

I came here with a close friend back in September '17. It's a great place to go to but make sure you're ready to order right away. I ordered the cheesesteak with provolone, onions, and peppers along with fries and a large soda. It was awesome.

Definitely not a "normal" Chick-Fil-A experience. Food portions much smaller, salty and nobody was smiling. I would say this is either a new CFA or they were not trained in the concepts and foundation of this great corporation. Smile!

I wish I could give ZERO stars. This is the worst mcdonalds ever. The staff is rude and INCOMPETENT. Went in this morning to get breakfast to go. Waited over 20 minutes due to the idiot's who work there getting EVERY order wrong. I finally got my food checked it and they didn't give me my bacon egg and cheese biscuit, I tell them and they ask me are you sure you ordered it wtf is that yes I ordered it..smh I get home and it's only an egg and cheese biscuit needless to say It went right in the trash. I haven't been to this mcdonalds in yrs for the same reason you would think after all this time they would hire competent workers. The last time my order was wrong the lady at the drive thru told me " you gonna eat what the fuck you got cause you ain't gettin nothin else" Don't waste your time or money here

I have fallen in love with the drinks and nachos. The steak nachos are the best. The main course meals are also insanely good (go for the goat or steak). 

The service is great; Katherine made the difference. She is probably the best bartender in the area. 


Long review short: the service and food is awesome. Please visit!!!

Pat's was a great experience.. I really enjoyed the atmosphere and the way to order. Made you feel like you were a regular. However, comparing to Geno's, I gotta give the nod to Geno's. Pat's was very good and you can't go wrong with either spot.

Solid 4 star overall. Kevin loves this place, much more than I did... Messy sub and all! In my opinion, the fries are the best part of Pat's. They are seasoned fries - the best type of French fry. Thing is, for 5$ they should at least match the amount of fries you get from Geno's 4$ fries. The sub was dry, both of our opinions. And I didnt like that the onions were just on the top of the sub and not spread out or even alot of them on the sub. I didnt like the bun here cuz it was chewy. We both liked that the steak was actually chopped instead of just sliced like at geno's. It's a 1 and done place just like geno's.
Jake n kev

My favorite cheesesteak in Philly, hands down. A must stop if you're coming into town. Fresh bread. Perfectly seasoned and cooked steak. Sautéed onions and cheese. There's lots of good cheesesteaks in Philly, but none better than the original, Pat's.

Forget what the locals say. Pat's was the best cheesesteak I had in Philly so far. It's exactly the gooey cheesy one your looking for. They all have good steak, but it's really about the wiz they use. Pats cheese is the best. Go here and don't share

Absolute worst chick fil a, the line was 45 mins and they had one person working the cashier. People have flights to make connections there should be more cashiers to accommodate to the 300ft line of people! I waited in line for 35 mins and then had to leave to make my connection. Worst experience

Was taking a road trip down to Maryland for the long weekend. My boyfriend and I decided to stop here for dinner after constantly hearing about Pats (and Gino's) on Food Network. Really wish we didn't make the stop...

A complete waste of time and money. You wait on this long absurd line for crap food. When you get to the first window you order wit or witout (onions) and chose your cheese. Plain, American, provolone or cheese wiz. Then you pay. The worker gets your sandwich out in under 60 seconds. The next window is for fries and beverages. Kind of a waste of time in my opinion for two windows doing different things. If both windows had everything, things would be quicker. 

My boyfriend got a philly steak wit American. He said it was dry and the bread was nasty. I ordered a roasted pork witout provolone. Driest pork I've ever had. 

Fries were super ..meh. 

Everything lacked flavor. 

Don't believe the hype! 

Pat's??? More like Crap's.

I generally dislike Grubhub culture and try to avoid delivery, but sometimes late at night on my days off, I can go for a greasy low brow late night cheesesteak delivery.  

First impression, the food here is expensive!  I guess it's because it's the only place open this late. 

The delivery driver pulls up and doesn't even get out of his car.  He makes me come out and grab it from him while he's still sitting in his car.  I thought that was especially rude considering I had tipped 15% and they also collected a delivery fee on top of that.  

I can forgive that.  If the food rules, the delivery driver is less of a concern.  Wrong.  The "chicken wings" were just just chicken wings barely fried or cooked.  Just slimey chicken skin in a NASTY BBQ sauce.  They did not taste fresh.  I couldn't stomach one.  

There was a weird taste with the cheesesteak as well - barely any cheese - fried onions still very crunchy.  Very liquidy.  Nothing tasted fresh.  Just overall bad.  I could've gotten a better cheesesteak at the deli down the street.  I ate about a quarter of it and I was so grossed out I couldn't finish it.  

Grubhub had prompted me to write a brief review of the place and I had written an abridged version of what I had just wrote above.  A few days later, I get a text from the business saying that they aren't accepting business from me anymore because of my review and that my review was "total garbage and fake" as they put it in the text.  

I would not have ever ordered anything from them ever again based on the food, but the text banning me from their services was really over the top and they should be ashamed of themselves for their food and service.  That text prompted me to write this, so others understand this place is to be avoided.  

I suspect the glowing 5 star review from Roman V is a total fake actually by how it is written and how drastically different it is from the rest.  

Never again.  Not under any circumstances will I order from this place again.

I ordered a large sprite and these speds gave me a large water 
How tf you mess that up yo

Talk about the ITIS!

For $9-9.50, you get a big sub piled high with thinly shaved steak, (wit) onions if you want, and a choice of cheeze whiz, prov, or American. Great stuff!

Don't let the line fool you though...it moves fast!!

Met some friends for some COVID outdoor brunch. The outdoor space is spacious and the color scheme is fun. The drinks were okay- not the bold taste I was looking for considering that have such unique flavors. 

But enough about that .... the chorizo (I ordered the breakfast burrito) was the best I've ever had to date! I will return just for the chorizo!

This was my favorite cheesesteak place when I worked in the Philly area years ago, and I haven't been back in over 10 years. When I saw a deal to have it delivered to my home via Goldbelly, I could not resist. It was a blast from the past, and very nostalgic. The steaks arrived packaged and frozen, so you can keep them frozen until you want to eat them. When heated up in the oven, they were were good, real good. But nothing is quite the same as standing in that line, smelling the steaks cooking and getting your fresh cheesesteak right off the grill. Can't wait to get there in person again and have a fresh cheesesteak off the grill.

Unfortunately they close early. Went there at 6:30 and they were closed already, cleaning the counters. Looked good but I had to go to Hip City Veg on next block (fabulous!). Two stars cause they were friendly at least.

I found it interesting that the sign at the airport didn't acknowledge it was Chipotle but my bill did.  The food tasted the same as any other Chipotle so I am not complaining.  I was able to eat a quick meal between flights.  The staff was friendly and it appeared to be clean.  

As always, the chips were great.  If they didn't make so much noise I would have taken them on the plane with me!
Called the restaurant 20 times looking for a refund because they failed to deliver my food but still charged me. They are extremely incompetent but I guess so am I for thinking they wouldn't be.

If you just came here and ate, and then flew home, I think this is a 4 star sandwich. However, and it's a big however, if you go elsewhere (Jims) you'll see there's little competition. The bun is actually tastier than it looks, but the fact that the meat isn't 'chopped' is a big red flag for me.
If you like Whiz, this is solid... no complaints there.
Unless you happen to just walk by, I would Recommend trying elsewhere for your fix.

We came here for some drinks and appetizers on a beautiful Saturday afternoon. There were 10 of us, but we didn't have to wait long for a table outside. My boyfriend and I had the peach margaritas on the rocks and the frozen Mango margaritas. I preferred the mango- it was pretty sweet but really delicious. We all picked on nachos and chips and guacamole. The nachos were tasty, and and it was a good portion. Our server was friendly and often circled back around to make sure we had everything we needed. The drinks did take a bit of time to come from the bar, but on a Saturday afternoon I didn't think it was anything out of the ordinary. Overall good experience and I would like to try other items off the menu!

For as much money as I spend on my order, I'd expect a little more food. I spent over 7 dollars on fries and was given a small box barely filled with minimal things on top, the tiniest pizza rolls I've ever seen, and small mac and cheese fried wedges for a price that I would've expected a lot more from. I know that ordering for delivery is always a gamble, but this place doesn't have a very big menu and doesn't give portions that will satisfy a party. I really wish restaurants wouldn't try to earn money by giving delivery orders a less-than-suitable amount of food. Can't you just be fair?

Can't go to Philly and not get a Philly cheese steak! Service is great and fast. Fries are amazing! Not too soggy not crispy. The fries are just right! It only got 3 stars because as a repetitive customer they are not as favorable as they used to be. But it's definitely one of my Philly faves.

When I first dined here I was so confused at the 3 stars they had. But after dining here a few times it makes sense. I was brought here by a friend over 2 years ago. I got the carnitas tacos and they were phenomenal. Honestly some of the best I've had and I've been to Mexico several times. The margaritas were also great the passion fruit, guava and when in season the watermelon being my faves. The service was great and the complimentary chips and salsa didn't hurt. 

I was happy to make Cantina apart of my weekly rotation from that initial experiences. However fast forward to 2 years later and tonight has solidified it for me; IM NEVER GOING BACK. So over the 2 years I've been coming here consistency has been the biggest problem. At times I would get the carnitas tacos and it would be dried out  and bland. The guacamole all too often lacks salt and the margaritas are hit or miss. Now margaritas I can definitely blame the bartenders. Some are better than others. Some bartenders put way too much sour mix or not enough of the fruit purée and yes even sometimes too much tequila and the drink isn't balanced. 

In addition to the carnitas tacos I absolutely loved the garlic shrimp. The sauce it comes in reminds me of the broth you get when you order mussels (shallots, garlic,white wine a little lemon for acidity). It's absolutely divine and they give you grilled bread with it. I always order extra bread and I ALWAYS don't stop until every drop of that broth is gone. But sadly they even ruined that for me. The coconut shrimp is good very similar to the ones from red lobster.

I haven't came here in 3 months but I was hungry. Since they kitchen close at 1am and it was midnight and slim pickings for eating in the area, my cousin and I made our way here. We ordered garlic shrimp, carnitas and chorizo tacos. The carnitas tacos was dried out and bland and the guacamole was bland. Big surprise. I sent the garlic shrimp back. Instead of the beautiful opaque garlicky goodness I'm used to it, the bottom of the bowl was filled with oil that appeared to have burnt fresh garlic in it. The shrimp was cold and bland. The bread was cool but with no sauce to dip it in what's the point. I'm sorry I absolutely wasn't paying for that monstrosity. As if the mediocre food wasn't bad enough when I got the check I seen that we were charged $4 to add guacamole to each orders of tacos. The last time I was here it cost $1 to add guacamole to tacos.
