I was extremely pissed. The guacamole portion was barely enough for 1 taco let alone 3 and they had the nerve to raise the price. I also noticed that they tossed the price of other things such as the introduction to tequila flight. At this point I'm over it, I heard they are other great taco spots in Philadelphia and those place shall be getting my money from now on.
Well they have the Big bufords and they are absolutely the best!!!!!!! Great food....bad neighborhood....fast drive thru. ..Thank the Lord.

This place has the best food around. I haven't had anything on the menu that I didn't like. Let me tell you, I have been to Supreme Oasis quite a few times and I am never disappointed. The food is delicious and the customer service makes the entire experience worth coming back.  Today I got the fish nuggets  platter (beyond delicious), cabbage (cooked perfectly, not mushy) and candied squash (you've got to try it). My daughter got barbecued chicken wings (finger licking better than good) and my son got a cheesesteak that he said was really good. I almost forgot about the navy bean soup. So good. The deserts are worth the extra calories. The Apple bean pie is superb, the pineapple upside down cake is the perfect sweet balance and the original bean pie is so tasty  you have to try hard not to eat the whole pie in one sitting. The outside of this place looks ordinary but when you go in you will be amazed with the customer service and after eating the food, you'll come back again.

Manager Lady at register was not very welcoming. Told me i could use credit card only i came over to that lane  then told me cash only.   Then the ice cream machine was broken when i wanted a shamrock shake, go figure.

Avoid this location. They gave me a wrong order. I asked for a cheesey gordita crunch and they gave me a chalupa......I've been going to Taco Bell for years now and chalupa and the gordita crunch are nowhere near similar. Don't know how the person making it didn't realize what I asked for. Nonetheless, the chalupa was fine but I asked for a gordita crunch. 
I recommend the location on JFK boulevard instead for more accurate orders.

Maybe I am just not into cheesesteaks but this one was extremely bland.  I ordered a Mushroom/ Onions with Provolone Cheese and overall it had really no flavor.  The mushrooms were boiled There is a stand with black hot peppers ( black?) and large whole green and red peppers but there really wasn't a way to slice them to add to the sandwich.  The fries had a crispy texture outside which was tasty.  Overall, I was dissappointed.  Will not be returning.

Ok so I went to Pats the other day I've been there before. I ask for a steak sandwich the guy who takes the order and the money very nice. The  guy next to him who is making the sandwiches I tell him nicely can you cut it in half He just rolls it up Looks at me as if I just killed his mother and hands me the sandwich Guy get a life you couldn't cut the sandwich in half what a d......  I won't be going there ever again when I'm back in Philadelphia I went to Geno's next door. Very nice people and they cut the sandwich in half such an easy task.I think Geno's is better any way. By the way I was there yesterday Saturday July 20 at around 12 noon. If the owners of Pats are reading this maybe you should school this asshole on manners and to please the public especially with someone something so simple

Not the best chicken sandwich I've had by a long shot. The cheese was melted and spread all over the place. There were not a lot of hash browns. They really held back. 

Service was good and fast. I'd like to go back and try the same place for lunch. Maybe it would be better.

Q: Who loves Burgers? 
A: Literally everyone. 
Sometimes, the way to a person's heart is through a juicy hand-formed burger, made to-order --and there's no where better than Five Guys Burgers. I'm not talking about gourmet burger here, just a tasty, and satisfying burger. 

Five Guys Burgers and Fries serves burgers, dogs, and sandwiches.
Five Guys Burgers and Fries features fresh-cut french fries (Five Guys/Cajun style).
Five Guys Burgers and Fries have the crazy Coke freestyle machines.

Tips:
1. If you do not want to end up with a food-coma, I advice you to get the "Little Hamburger/ Cheeseburger". You are welcome! 
2. Add as many topping as you want- All FREE!
3. If you ordered the famous fries, which you should, get the regular size. a) you will get an overflowing bag of fries, no matter what size you have ordered. b) You will save about $1.76 ( R: $3.19 L: $4.95).

Three and Half Yelps.

This place has good cheesesteaks and the french fries are cooked perfect and there honestly is nothing bad to say about this place.  The food comes out fast and the line moves quick and its worth the wait if its busy before or after a sporting event.  However, Oh Brother Philly in Old City has an excellent cheesesteak and their variety of french fries are better. You can even get cheesesteak fries!!

That aside, you won't regret hitting up this cheesesteak hot spot but beware, there is a new comer who is putting up quite a good fight for king of steaks!!

We've been in the neighborhood for about 6 months now and finally got up to Cantina Los Caballitos for lunch yesterday. As some have noted, the music is a little loud and I can imagine levels might easily get out of hand on a weekend evening with a full house. 

Service was prompt and friendly. Water and chips with 2 salsas arrived immediately. We both thought the green salsa was especially tasty. I had the "wet" al pastor burrito, and DW fish tacos. Both were delivered quickly and both were tasty and plenty filling, though if we were both planning to order the tacos I'd probably also get something extra, though DW was happy with hers. The al pastor burrito was quite a bit more than I'd normally eat for lunch and since we were eating later than usual it was more than enough for the rest of the day.

Overall - very good food, pretty normal pricing for the area. We'll be back.

My first and most recent visit to Los Caballitos was pretty unmemorable, and so it's among the last to review in the year. South Philly is chock full of Mexican eats, but it's always fun to find new spots. That being said, I don't think I'll be adding this one to my list.

Okay, let me back up. If you're looking for some decent chicken wings, 100% come here for some drinks and wings. My boyfriend and I split wings as an appetizer and got each of their sauces. The best one had to be the habanero buffalo but they were all decent.

I was boring and got steak tacos, but he ventured out (alright, he's Mexican; it's not that much of venturing) and got the Cabrito, a braised goat dish that was pretty good from the bite I stole. The meat in my tacos was a bit stiff and I wasn't too inspired by either salsas we got for the table. Tacos are a staple so I was a bit bummed.

Our tres leches cake was kind of a dos y media leches since the condensed milk was ambiently soaked in the cake before it got to us. A perk was the lemon curd at the bottom since I'm a sucker for lemon (pun intended). 

The service was meh, but I guess they were busy with their outdoor clientele since it was summertime. The restaurant is dark as ever so you might need your phone to read the menu. Overall, an okay experience with some mostly decent food, but nothing (besides the wings!) completely blew me away.
Cheesesteak is alright. The meat was a little too chewy. I think Dealesandros is better.

I absolutely love this place. I work nightshift at a nearby hospital and this place always saves my night when I realize I forgot to bring my meal. The Night Owl's food is always delicious and the delivery drivers are always on time and super friendly. This is my go to spot now in the middle of the night. If you're on the fence, just place the order. I trust that this place won't disappoint you!
I'm from Minnesota, this pizza is the best pizza I have had in a long time! Price, location, pizza was amazing! If ever traveling in this area again will be eating here!
The worst McDonald's ever, 40 mins to get my food I would've left but I gave these muthafuckas $10

I'm a Philly native. I grew up as a Geno's fan and never had Pat's until today. My boyfriend (a non-Philly native and has no loyalty to any steak place) and I wanted to do a side-by-side comparison of the two steaks with the same ingredients: "Whiz Wit" (AKA cheese whiz with onions) with ketchup and hot peppers. We came to the conclusion that Geno's was far superior to Pat's. Pat's had an incredibly long line (about a 30-minute wait). The wait for Genos was much quicker, about 10-15 minutes. Pat's had a nice, balanced sandwich (perfect amount of meat to roll to cheese), but found that the bread was slightly stale and fell apart with meat and cheese going everywhere! My first bite was without any ketchup or hot peppers, and the meat was quite bland...and so were the onions. The hot peppers aren't hot at all, and I definitely felt disappointed. But, what do I know? I already have my loyalty to Genos.  My boyfriend did feel similar where he preferred the meat and bun from Genos but liked the balanced sandwich from Pat's since there was definitely more meat and cheese in it. Both sandwiches are $11 and at the end of the day, I would rather have good, less meat than more of it and the sandwich being bland.

No Drive-Thru. Not open late. Not much of a McDonald's if you ask me.  The one thing this McDonald's has going for it is its location.  It's walking distance for many of us in the Chestnut Hill area and is one of the more attractive McDonald's I've seen.  Other than that, it falls short.  The service is very slow and any time I use a coupon they have to have a team meeting to figure it out.  Not a huge Mickie D's guy, but I, like most my age, appreciate a nice fast food drive-thru late at night.  Come on.

After years of seeing Pat's featured on Food Network, I knew that I had to come by to pick up a cheesesteak during my trip to Philadelphia.  When I first landed at the airport (after a redeye flight from across the country), I knew that my first stop would be Pat's.  I got a cheesesteak with cheeze wiz and onions.  It tasted pretty good at the time.  But, about 30 minutes after I finished eating (as I was driving back to my hotel), I became severely nauseated.  When I arrived at my hotel, I was pretty much ready to pass out - I proceeded to fall asleep for a good three hours.  After waking up, I had the pleasure of dealing with other symptoms associated with food poisoning (I will spare you the details) for the rest of the day and night.  It was the most horrendous night I have ever had while on vacation.  Right now, I am in my hotel room writing this review as I try to handle day 2 of this food poisoning mess.  

I really wanted to love Pat's, I really did.  But if a sandwich is going to put me out for 2 whole days, I really will never come back.  I am scarred for life and am pretty sure that I will never eat a Philly cheesesteak again.

Hands down the best steak and cheese subs!! I believe it's better than the competition. Prepare for the long wait! Make sure to have cash! It's cash only! And read the sign before ordering to prepare yourself.

Service was absolutely terrible. Rude person taking order and waited at window without being greeted for 5 minutes. Food was decent, but portions were poor and they didnt have several things we tried to order, including the right bag to carry food in. It'll shut down before the end of the year.
Underwhelming. Came at peak lunchtime on a weekend and got dry, chewy, unseasoned steak. Bread was very chewy also. Fries are mediocre at best. Only upside was the cheese wiz and jaw workout.

Pat's serve their beef "chopped" whereas Geno's do theirs "sliced". Taste wise, they are very close. 
If you're thinking of doing the same taste test, I recommend sharing the 2 cheesesteaks with 2 or 3 people. 

Overall, my preference leans towards Pat's as the bread had a better bite. Geno's bread was rather sloppy in comparison.

Pats is definitely overhyped. I've been to Philly many times but the person who took me was hung-go about Pat's. It was good, but not the best cheesesteak I ever had. I've even had better ones in NYC! 

The good part of Pat's is we didn't have to wait long and there was a lot of seating. We got there around 7pm on a Thursday night. Wouldn't go again, but glad I got to experience it at least once!

Ordered food when we got home at 2:15 am. Food came at 5. 5!!!! I know it was late, but come on. On top of that, the food was freezing cold and disgusting. Don't ever eat here, ever. Downright sickening.

It's ok.

The food arrived on time, was hot and tasty but missing our sauces.

It's little details like that which can be annoying.

Will take your money and not process your order. Spent 30 minutes on the phone with the "supervisor" who could not explain to me why my order could not be delivered or processed, even though my card was charged. DO NOT DO BUSINESS WITH NIGHT OWL.

As a side note: I have ordered from this place very frequently for over a year and reached out to them trying to fix an issue with the processing on their site for ordering VS. Grubhub and get treated like trash. No thanks. Bad business.

Editing my review since I can not officially respond to the comment the business owner left:

1. I left the review so you would lose revenue.
2. I feel bad for any employee you have, because if you talk to guests this way, I can only assume you're worse to your employees. I hope they find new jobs. (Feel free to reach out to me if you are one of those employees looking for another job in the industry.)
3. I can and will not support a business that is rude, incompetent and will communicate with half respect to their guests (which is why I gave you a bad review in the first place). 

Once again, don't waste you money. They may get your order right the first few times but when they mess up and are as disrespectful to you as they were to me, you'll be right here on yelp making sure people don't spend their money here. :)

I would like to say a super thank you to everyone at the KFC especially the very nice lady at the drive thru. I'm a truck driver and obviously my 18 wheeler does not fit in any drive thru. She let me place my order on foot when no other place in that area would. THANK YOU..
"Why the fuck you add salad dressing to the bag when you ain't even add the fries?!" Three women yelling at each other for 30 minutes while we were in the drive through waiting for cold ass food

TEAM PAT'S KING OF STEAKS ALL THE WAY!

So a couple of friends and I were visiting from Las Vegas and was told we needed to have a Philly cheesesteak while visiting Philadelphia. The locals told us we had to either try Geno's Steaks or Pat's King of Steaks. We didn't know which one to go to so we tried BOTH! Yup you heard it right, we ate at both spots and let me tell you, Pat's King of Steaks was wayyyyyyyyyyyyyy better than Geno's Steaks.   

They gave more meat, cheese was well melted, steak was moist and full of flavor and the bread was nice and soft. Put that all together and you get a fan like me! I highly recommend this place. Both steakhouses are located across the street from one another. 

TIPS: 
*They only take cash so make sure you bring cash (ATM is located in the area but fee is high) 
*Parking isn't easy, it took us about 20-30mins to find a parking but it was totally worth it. 
*Location is really run down so I don't recommend going at night. 
*Separate lines for Philly, separate line for fries and drinks. 
*Not a lot of seating area.
Preferred over the other guy across the street, extra Whiz is the move. If I'm in Philly I still find myself coming even if I try another place also
Philly cheese steak is so messy but tastes so good!

Night Owls is one of the few options in Philly delivering food all night long. What sets them apart from other places is the clear menu, quality ingredients, and food customizable to your taste and health requirements.

The delivery was faster than expected, and we are on the other side of town. The food arrived steaming hot and was enjoyed by everyone. The seafood pizza with shrimp and real crab meat was to die for. The fries were crisp and light. The cheese steak was very delicious and prepared exactly as we requested. 

We highly recommend Night Owls for your late night cravings.

I remain loyal to this place because this is where Mom used to take me when I was a kid some 30 years ago.  Although since then I have come to prefer other Philly cheesesteak places over Pat's, they're still quite good most of the time.  I will admit there have been times I was disappointed by a Pat's steak, but they are rare, and it hasn't happened in years. Unlike the place across the street I've tried many times, which has never held a candle to Pat's.
The best and nicest staff! Clean and the food is always on point! Grub hub delivery was excellent and courteous!

I am never up at midnight but because of the Villanova game i was out late. We ordered from Night Owl and I have to say their cheesesteaks and pizza are the best! I thought I had my favorites in the city but after trying Night Owl i have changed my mind. I may have to  stay up late one night just to order again.
Didn't have anything I wanted to order then I was stuck in line because I couldn't back out. They took forever with the 2 cars ahead of me, so 20 minutes wasted.

We flew in late and got to the hotel totally fried, almost midnight. We got our food in under half an hour from initial call to delivery, it was perfect late night grub, and the customer service was above and beyond. Totally recommend.

Tourist post alert: we, like so many others, did the Genos and Pat's comparison. Verdict was Pat's came out slightly ahead based on fractionally better bread (for my preference) and they're a little more generous on the meat.  I appreciate the history at Pat's, as they are credited by many as the inventor of the cheesesteak sandwich, for which to will ever be grateful.  I've had better cheesesteaks in my life, but you still owe it to yourself to try the original.

I guess all the hype didn't measure up, meat wasn't season is was blend. Love the fries and the environment is awesome seen the place get pack and everyone lineup to get their order correct is hilarious and trying to get parking was a challenge itself.

If you are a tourist who wants crappy food and to be abused go there. 
IT IS A TOURIST TRAP

We were on the fence about Pat's versus Geno's. Our Uber driver, a Philly native, recommended Pat's. There was no line when we got there during the day on Thursday. Sadly, the experience did not live up to the hype. My stepdaughter and I got the cheesesteak with provolone and my husband got the cheese whiz. Our cheesesteaks were pretty flavorless even though we got them "wit" (onions) and the meat was dry. I've had better cheesesteaks all over the US. Pat's may be the original cheesesteak, but certainly not the best.
There are better cheese steaks in Jersey.. Yes, I said it. This place has gotten to big for itself. Just the attitude of the employees makes you just want to stay away.

The cheese steak is worth the drive from Center City which is most likely where you will be touring in Philadelphia. The neighborhood is save and very Italian. This place does a lot of business and is open 24/7. 

The cheese steak is amazing. I recommend getting the onions and surprisingly the cheese Wiz. So it is ordered "Wiz Wit". The "wit" is the with onions.  The bread is amazing. 

The fries are a little too batter fried for me but may be better for people that are out late partying. 

A must go to Philadelphia. It's a USA landmark and does not disappoint.

Okay, everyone has a bucket list right? This was the only reason I traveled to Philly from NYC....so I could eat a phillycheese steak IN Philly. One of the most disappointing experiences of my life, other than trying to walk around in the humidity. This place is a complete tourist trap, because the only people you see here and across the street are tourist. Everyone's shoving a soggy roll of bread with some flavorless meat into their mouths. Dry or juicy, they'll take it. I even saw a table that brought their own Pringles and drinks. It's really that serious....

$11 for a Cheese Steak. I took 2 bites and tossed the rest into the trash. I can't justify ever eating another one in this life time. You literally walk up to the window, tell them what you want, and they hand it to you. That's how big of a trap it is, lol. It's also cash only! The number of tourists coming here, and it's cash only. Now, THAT'S how you avoid paying taxes :-) Just saying...

I was here on Saturday night with a group of 8. They wouldn't take my name and party until our entire group was there even though there was already a wait. By the time our entire group was there, it was a 30 minute wait. Luckily, they have a decent size bar so we ordered some drinks. I gave the hostess my cell number and she informed me that they would text me when our table is ready. This would have been great but the restaurant and bar are very loud, so I couldn't hear my phone vibrate or ring on the highest setting so I had to continually check my phone.

We were seated outside near the back wall. When we were seated, I took note that there were a bunch of empty tables outside and I couldn't understand why they didn't push a few together sooner to get us seated. Perhaps there wasn't enough staff to handle all tables being full? 

The service was very slow. It took way too long to bring our drinks and most of us were just ordering beer. Then it took a long time to get dinner. At least, we got chips and salsa. I thought both the red and green salsas were just ok and one of them should have been spicier. . One of the servers must have picked up on us being a little annoyed by the slow service so he offered us complimentary guacamole. It would have been nice but they never returned with any guacamole. 

While we were finishing up eating, we noticed mice running around right next to our table. These were very brave little things and they even ran under our chairs. Granted, we were outside in the summer time and I did see no-kill mice traps along the wall so I wasn't too freaked out.

The slow service bothered me more than the mice. After we were finished eating and just wanting to get the h*ll out of there, especially since two members of our group were waiting across the street after seeing mice, we had to ask for the check multiple times. We mentioned the no guacamole that was promised and the mice situation to our server. She then asked if we wanted her to bring us some guacamole. After being in this joint for 3 hours, we couldn't wait to be on our way. She spoke with the manager and came back to tell us that they would comp some drinks which was nice and made us happy. We split the bill on a few credit cards and that got messed up- some people were charged more than others and one person was not charged at all and another person charged twice. We wanted to get out so bad that we figured out who owed who what.

On a good note- there is a lot of outdoor seating- more than any other place I can think of in the area. I had mahi mahi tacos and enjoyed them. The food is good and prices are reasonable. You can find some more authentic and slightly tastier Mexican food at some hole in the walls on and off of 9th Street, but this place is nice for hanging out with a group outside. I just wish their service would improve. The poor service will probably keep me from coming back.

I just can't deal. I think you've self sabotage your own business. Therefore now earning yourself another 1 Star. What type of business owner does that? Going back & fourth with people just because you cannot handle what the world has to say. 7 months ago so long ago. Get over my review and move on. You do know at the end of the day it's just a review & the customer is always right. The new location I guess you can say it looks cleaner than the last but definitely smaller. Waiting time is long just like before understaff in the kitchen probably because too cheap. "Sloth mode" 

At first I thought it was a franchise hoping the people here wasn't as bad as the last place since I happen to be visiting in this area but negative because I recognize the tall Goofy looking dude. 

They  just move their business to a smaller building. I wonder why they down graded to a smaller building in a sketchier location? Maybe they couldn't afford rent. Maybe they got kicked out because of their attitude. 

I was here not too long ago what I witness was the tall guy yelling at the old lady (Regina or something like that) that was delivering for him. Boy did she snapped on him. "I'm old enough to be your mother" you obvious don't respect elders let alone respect for employees so now you have unhappy employees a ton of negative reviews followed by responses that you so dearly deserve. 

I wish you guys the best you just can't run a business with arrogance.

Crowning yourself a King is a pretty bold move...even if it's just: 'Lord of Meat'. 

So I went to Pat's King of Steaks expecting a 'royal' treatment.  To my dismay, they do not even speak The King's English here.  Instead, you'll have to get by on Philly street slang when ordering.  If you're not well versed in cheese lingo, then you may want to know that getting 'whiz' on your steak is a good thing (and not in the R. Kelly sense). 

I ordered a plain cheesesteak...which means, salted beef drizzled with American cheese on a long roll.  That may seem like a bland description but once that salty beef enters your mouth and you feel the creamy cheese sliding down your throat....,ummmm, maybe I should stop typing for a minute.  

.......
.......
.......Ok, I'm better now.  Let me try that again. 

That may seem like a bland description but that sandwich is anything but bland.  Each bite may cut your lifespan by a week...but, seriously, is there anything you could do in a week that would be better than those ten glorious seconds each bite lasts?  I think not.  

There really wasn't anything 'royal' about the interior of the place.  Well, unless you were comparing the sanitation efforts to those of a medieval dungeon.  

One other point to note is that there are a lot of characters in and around this place...and I'd say most appropriately classified as 'jesters'.  Some of them were ordering sandwiches, some of them were making the sandwiches...but most of them were standing around outside asking for free change (sadly, none of them were willing to dance or juggle for it).

It's touristy but I love it! I take all first timers to the city to experience this iconic location along with Genos for the cheesesteak challenge. I love explaining to them the proper way to order and then having them nervously order themselves. I love that you can come at any hour...and we have. I recommend after dark so you get to experience the neon lights and hustle. We always leave with a smile and fun memories they talk about until the next visit.

This place is completely overrated! I went there for the first time about 4 years ago. I was a cheesesteak virgin! I waited until I went to Philly to try my first cheesesteak ever ( I'm from Cali currently living in Texas ). We drove from D.C to New York, stopped in Philly ONLY for the cheesesteak, I was so excited, popping my cheesesteak cherry in Philly! We got one from Pats and one from Genos!! Both were crap!! Nasty boiled meat! No flavor at all!! We took a few bites and continued our drive to New York with such disappointment! I cannot believe these places are recognized, recommended or advertised on major TV stations. We were told these are the places to go for a cheesesteak, don't waste your time or money. We found better Philly cheesesteaks at the Truck Yard in Dallas which are made by Philly natives. Definitely not a place I would ever go to again. After eating at Pats and Genos, I didn't eat another cheesesteak for over 4 years because I thought it was disgusting!! AND YES, I'm posting the same review at Genos.

You know, the food is pretty decent for fast food, but I'm not sure how my ticket was completely skipped over despite it not being a particularly huge crowd for a weekday at post-lunch hour. Luckily, the woman who rang me up noticed I was still standing there and expedited my late order. I'm not shocked since this isn't the most organized Five Guys, but at least the food makes up for it.

Well if I was going to be in Philadelphia, this had to be one of my stops.  I've been hearing about Pat's cheese steaks for years so I was very excited to try one.  I did my research on yelp so I know exactly what I wanted, a "mushroom cheesesteak wit onions".  I've read many a review talking about how rude the people were here; however, when I went up to order my cheesesteak, I said what I wanted, they took my cash, and less than a minute later my cheesesteak was in front of me.  They seem to have a very efficient system going doing booming business all these years, and they were not rude at all.

As for the cheesesteak itself, it was pretty darn tasty.  Pat's sells some legit stuff, and if I had to choose between here and Geno's across the street, my choice would be Pat's every time.  I feel that anybody who is visiting Philly needs to grab a Pat's cheesesteak for the novelty.
I have now tried most of the cheese steaks in Philly and this is by far my favorite. Worth the wait!!!

Very good cheese steaks and cheese fries. I personally like them better than ginos  
Always get fried onions, mayo, & ketchup.

If I could put 0 stars I would. The food was cold, no one was wearing gloves...NO ONE, and there was a hair in the chicken. Paid $33 for the 12pc meal and I wish I hadn't. Total waste of money, never again.

I am so upset and hungry...

I had thawed out chicken to cook myself but was so tired from working all day that I decided to order Popeyes. It was a little later than usual since I took an unexpected nap, however, my order had been placed by 9:30, an hour before closing. I ordered the 8 piece family meal which was already overpriced at 17.99 plus tax with a 3.99 delivery fee. I would also like to note that the "delivery" family meal comes with only one large side and 4 biscuits. Anyway, I patiently await my order.

If a picture speaks a thousand words... just see for yourself what was delivered to me. Trust me it looks even worst in person. I can't even comprehend the how and the why of the chicken being in that condition. The chicken is clearly old. It was greasy, yet dry and hard. 

I am trying to describe it, but a, at a loss of words. The only thing that comes to mind is yuck . It is inedible and it should have been trashed.

If Popeyes is sending out food in this condition I have to wonder about the cleanliness of their franchise on Grant Ave...I wonder if they are following enhanced precautions, let alone standard. Makes me wonder about the worker who sent out this order...are they disgruntled? Upset that the order came in late? I wonder did they dig this from the garbage and send it out ...makes me wonder a lot of things....but one thing you don't have to wonder about is me ordering from them AGAIN!

This place disappointments me. It has everything I'm looking for, Mexican food/drink, outdoor seating, young crowd. BUT the food is HORRIBLE. My boyfriend and I have eaten here several times, he lives across the street, but we tend to get elsewhere to eat. One time I couldn't even take a third bite of my chicken burrito. I've never had bad mexican food until I came here. On the upside though, they're margaritas are excellent and I love the green salsa. I will never come here to eat but I will admit its a great place for just drinks and chips + salsa. I would only recommend it if you are already in the area, would never go out of my way for it. Philly has plenty of better options.

These are GOOD...  Look if you want the best Philly has to offer well then you found it...  This is one of the best out there.

If you can't appreciate a great cheesesteak wit whiz then don't go to Philly stay in your lame little town and get that crap that you call a philly cheesesteak....

You can walk down to DiBruno Bros and get some awesome cheese as well...  

I can't wait for the summer and our trips to Philly....

I used to go here when I was dead broke. I was feeling nostalgic, so I stopped by after a hiatus of at least five years. The food is terrible. It's not good in a fast food sense, either. You can taste how old the grease is. You can see how dirty everything is. The lack of enthusiasm from the team. It's a cesspool that churns out garbage food. Just go anywhere else or just have sleep for dinner. It's not worth it.
Chick-Fil-A might just be the only thing redeeming about PHL.
This location continues to go down hill. Shame the investment that was made to upgrade when the service has gotten worse. 10 mins at the drove thru while a worker drinks a shamrock shake while I wait

I tried three cheesesteaks side by side. Geno's, Pat's, and Jim's. All three were good. Pat's had good flavor. Amount of cheese was on the lighter side. Not my top choice but a solid choice nonetheless. See my reviews on the other two.

The outdoor seating and the location of Caballitos tend to bring a lot of people in, but the foods needs a huge upgrade.  We ordered ceviche, wings, and some other dishes I can't remember right now, but everything was below mediocre.  Service was alot better than our first time but still very slow.  I would recommend going to Cantina Los Caballitos for drinks only.

Came out here to try some famous cheese steaks (also because everyone said it was so much better than Geno's). 

Man..... I have to admit I was a bit disappointed (maybe my expectations were too high and I was just expecting something to be mind blowing amazing). The steak was a bit bland and dry (didn't have a whole lot of flavor here and it wasn't as tender/juicy as I've had from other Cheesesteak places), and the only thing that made my meal tolerable to get through was the cheese whiz. 

Thank god for Cheese Whiz because otherwise I wouldn't have been able to finish this. My friend ended up getting the cheesesteak with the provolone and she pretty much experienced the same disappointment I did haha. 

Now it's not an awful cheesesteak joint, but it's also not great or good enough for me to want to come back. 

Oddly enough, my favorite cheesesteaks remain in New York and California (Phil's Steak Truck and St John's respectively)

My family and I went to both Pat's and Geno's across the street to compare which one is better.  We got 3 different cheesesteaks: cheese wiz, provolone cheese, and white American cheese.  All 3 with wit.

Unfortunately, neither was the winner.  They were quite disappointing.  We felt that they were not at the same caliber as Dalessandro's or Joe's.  Overly hyped.  Meats were not as fresh or flavorful.  Onions were either undercooked or overcooked.  

If you still feel like you want to try them, I would recommend:
At Pat's - get it with white American cheese.
At Geno's - get it with cheese wiz.  

I would avoid one with provolone cheese from either places.

Oil:water::indoor seating:Philly steak joints.

-A brief recounting of how your gentle correspondent came to eat hot cheesesteak whilest shivering in frigid cold and cursing the gods of weather-

In all my time in San Francisco, I have never lost my absolute contempt for the wimpyness my fellow citizens express at the slightest hint of actual weather.  Temps below 58 degrees, rainfall beyond a slight misting, and even the slightest hint of wind drive people into a Chicken Little-esque panic.  Meanwhile, I've lived places where the high was occasionally -10, and I've watched a tornado make its way through a valley while on horseback, wearing only a t-shirt.  Am I saying I'm better than my neighbors?  Not necessarily.  But maybe.

Right about the time I was sinking my teeth into 6 inches of hot cheesy steak, this attitude was coming back to haunt me.  See, I had accidentally journeyed back into the land of real weather (and real cheesesteak), in the form of Philly in October.  And, apparently, the gods of wind and rain had missed kicking my ass for the last several years, and attempted to make up for it by visiting upon the greater Eastern Seaboard a fall storm of truly epic proportions.  And all I had brought with me was some long sleeve shirts and my rain jacket.  Plenty enough protection for San Francisco winter, but sadly inadequate for a Philly Phall storm.

You simply cannot visit Philly without devouring a cheesesteak or 2 or 12, and so a group of us headed out to the Great Corner, wherein Pat's King of Steak faces off against another cheesesteak legend.  I opted for Pat's, because both restaurants were equally devoid of any kind of real shelter or heat.  It can safely be said that few visitors attacked their cheesesteak and fries with greater ferocity than I, if only because I knew I had to get that cheesesteak up in me before I could escape to the artificial heat of the nearby sports bar.

Lasting impressions: be authentic and go for the Velveeta cheese; fries aren't great; the hot peppers would be more enjoyable if they were sliced rather than served whole; I'm glad the bell peppers were optional, because I'm very allergic and I was nervous.

Receive a shipment on my birthday of 3 Pat's cheesesteaks even though I live 8 miles from Philly. Box came with directions to heat them up and add the cheeeze whiz. Phenomenal! Crunchy bread, great tasting steak and peppers and onions topped with the cheese whiz. I'm not a cheesesteak person, but with Pat's I'm now a convert!

i don't usually review places on here, since yelp reviews seem to be generally pretty right about most places, but this place really doesn't deserve its low rating. I'm honestly confused about what the problem is, at least in my experience ordering tonight (grubhub) it was what late night food should be. the food was piping hot and delicious, and anyone who'll deliver out to villanova at 1am in a sunday is alright in my book. customer service was above and beyond, i noticed one review in particular attach a screenshot alleging rude customer service. maybe they caught them on a bad night, but my experience there couldn't be more different, definitely one of the most professional and convenient places i've ordered from.

I took the taste test and I prefer Pat's. The roll was nicely toasted and the meat in my "wit with whiz" (aka with onions and Cheeze Whiz) was shredded. The other place's roll was spongy and the meat was whole slices.

I also like that Pat's has other things they'll mix into the cheesesteak, like peppers and mushrooms and suchlike.

Parking is a pain. Sandwiches and drinks and fries are CASH ONLY. Good luck.
Stop reading and pick Pats over Genos!  I had both and Pats is better hands down. Extra  cheese Steak with! . Yummy!
Slow and sketched our.  One girl nice.  One girl a total biotch.  lol  But was worth it to find the ODB story im here.   lmao

Nope.

I know Pat's is one of the most frequented places in Philly, but as much as I want to be excited about that, it's a big Nope for me. Incredibly greasy (the oil seeped through two layers of wrapping paper), poor service, low-quality meat, and a $0.25 bottle of water for $2.50. I just can't get myself to give it more than 2 stars.

I won't be back. Any other suggestions for getting a great cheesesteak, fellow Yelpers?

Props for being the reported inventor of the cheesesteak, and for being better than Geno's (across the street).  I've had much better luck finding a table here, and the general experience is better; less attitude, an impression of better cleanliness.  The beef is better seasoned, has less gristle (still more than it should) and is much moister.  If this moistness is described as "grease," then yes, the Pat's cheesesteak is greasier than the Geno's version.  I've never experienced so much grease that the bread was saturated, unless the sandwich was left in its foil wrapper for an extended period.  Not as good as Jim's or Dalessandro's, but better than Geno's.

Visiting Philadelphia, my son took us to this great pizza place where we could get a really good pizza designed for my "Keto" lifestyle. The pizza was so fresh, hot and no skimping on ingredients! We shared a White Top Cauliflower crust and Meat Eater Keto crust, both medium, plenty for the three of us and a slice leftover for later. The place is clean and even during busy lunch hour, they were fast and friendly. This is a good place to visit with friends or family, to enjoy a quick meal alone, or just  carry out. I was told they deliver so I'll try that next time.
Their cinnamon pretzels are amazing!

Couldn't give this spot a rating on GrubHub for some reason, but I'm here. Got really drunk watching GOT and playing video games, realized I was hungry. Ordered a cheese steak, and got a 100% real deal cheesesteak, no steak-umms BS. Delivery was swift and courteous. I hope this spot can stay around forever, Philly needs it.

One of my favorite places in Philadelphia to get non-Authentic Mexican food. Just because it isn't authentic doesn't mean it won't leave you completely satisfied. One of my favorite dishes is then smoked tofu and seitan fajitas. This is a meal for one if you hava a huge appetite or for two to share. The portions on all of the meals are quite large but this one is unusually huge. 

Come for the margaritas, stay for the tomatillo salsa. 100% vegan or carnivore friendly. Good luck finding parking.

What a hidden gem on City Ave!
This Korean-Japanese resturant is a nice, chill place to stop by for lunch! The interior is nice and inviting! The bright colors and lighting makes the place a nice spot to avoid the dreary weather outside. I will definitely be back!
Geno's is better and Dalessandro's in Roxborough blows them both out of the water. Convenience and late hours are what makes it almost tolerable.
Loved it. Never had a "real" Philly Cheesesteak and this place did not disappoint! Several places to choose from and without a recommendation, Pat's  was a winner!

I want to start off by saying after reading all these bad reviews, people who can't understand opening a new place takes a few weeks to a month to get everything straight should NOT even try it for a few months. Your ignorance is NOT needed.

I went here on Saturday night to form my owN opinion of this new spot. I wanted to go in and order since it was my 1st time. I ordered two #3's w. The bites one w. Regular fries and one with Sweet Potato fries. Also ordered a dark meat sandwich. Each meal came with 2 sauces. However I am a sauce queen so  I was more then happy to pay for all the extra sauces I wanted to try. Also. Would like to say the cashier was super sweet! 

I waited a few minutes and I was asKed if I wanted tenders since they were done and the bites would take 5 more minutes. I was willing to wait! They were not busy so who wouldn't want to wait for fresh chicken. More then 5 minutes passed then ten minutes passed. The manager noticed and was so apologetic, then the cashier apologized and 2 owners came  out and apologized! I was so thankful all these people were so concerned. 

I finally got my whole order, everything was in the bag all the sauces and ALL! 

I could be mad for no rreason, but I know this place just opened! Give them a lil time! 

The CHICKEN  was actually delicious! Its not frozen, and cooked perfect. I also thought ALL 6 sauces were really good too! I can't wait to go back!

Kudos to the owners and management! Keep your head high and things will all work out!  We loved it and will surely be back! And to those who can't be patient maybe give this place a few more weeks and i bet you will enjoy their food!
Rudest window staff who yelled "show me your phone" when I ordered on Grubhub and said the name I was picking up for. Then asked me my name anyway. Get a better system? Food ok.

The King of Steaks indeed!  Every time I fly into Philadelphia, it doesn't matter what time of day it is, I drive straigh to Pat's for a cheese steak.  My family is from Pennsylvania so it's a staple and a tradition to get a Pat's steak no matter what.  Make sure you know what you want when you step up to the window to avoid a delay in ordering or getting skipped for not being prepared.  I ordered the steak with onions and whiz and it is still my favorite cheesecake I've ever had.  They have a ton of these amazing large red peppers to add on top if you like spice on your cheese steak.  I added a couple on one side and they were spicy but added a great extra flavor to the already delicious cheese steak.  I can't wait to go back next summer for another family wedding and will be heading here as my first stop!

97% of the time they mess my order up. 5/10 times when I go to the drive thru they don't have my order ready &I I have to pull over and they are supposed to "bring it to me". Well on several occasions they never came out and I had to get out of my car (in the rain - the reason why I went to the drive thru in the first place) and go inside and find out where my Big Mac meal is.. then they usually they mess my order up (I don't eat cheese so whatever I order I say no cheese) and if I don't check it before I get home and guess what??? THERES CHEESE. And a lot of it. Usually unmelted - yuck. Then there a 40-something year old "manager" (mean that in the loosest of terms) guy there "running things" and he has the audacity to get an attitude with me for having an attitude with them for fucking up my order - how rude *Stephanie Tanner voice. If it wasn't so close, I'd never go there. #MrProTip

We ordered from Night Owls and I had the cheesesteak which is THE BEST CHEESESTEAK I have EVER had!  The portion of meat is more than generous on the sandwich, it's cooked to perfection and the roll was very fresh.  I have lived in Philly for 54 years and have had cheesesteaks from everywhere. This is a solid place.  This place is open when everyone else in town is closed, another plus for late night hunger pangs.  I am definitely a new repeat customer!
I ordered yesterday and let me tell You, the food was hot, chicken was delicious, like it had just come out the grease.

OK another disappointment!! It tasted just a bit better than gino,but just above trash! Over priced and over rated. OMG the  scum level of all food. 
The steak was  not good at all so was the nasty microwave cheese. I rather have frozen food than ever going to these two steak places

My boyfriend and our friends decided to explore Philly for a weekend. They decided to stop by lunch at Pat's. For those who are not familiar with Pat's, it's an outdoor establishment. You'll have to walk up to the counter and make your order. 

My advice is to check out the menu beforehand or be prepared to get your order. They do not like the waiting game. You order and pay kind of speed. I ordered the wiz and onions. It wasn't bad nor it was great in my personal taste. I thought it was dry and the beef had no flavor. It was chewy. Overall, if we were to come back and somone wanted to go here...I wouldn't oppose.

Ever since I was a cheese steak I dreamed about being served from the king of steaks, but after one visit I rather roll off the table. 

The whole sandwich is bland and that's it.

I don't get the appeal of this place. Visiting Philadelphia for 48 hours, a cheese steak was at the top of my to do list. For $10, I was underwhelmed. Yea, the cheese whiz is interesting and complements the meat with the saltiness but other than that, I didn't think the sandwich itself had much flavor. 

Ohhh for those not in the know, this place isn't in the best of neighborhoods in South Philly. Walking there from downtown by myself at 11 pm at night with no working cell phone was probably a bad idea...

We did the Cheesesteak taste test, starting at Pat's I had the steak "wit" & provolone. ( added hot sauce ). The meat was good, but the bread was not fresh. Gino's, across the street, was a little better. The roll was fresh, and I liked the cheese wiz. I recommend doing your own taste test, because as you can see, opinions differ widely. Either way you've made it to the "Mecca" of cheesesteaks.

Extremely slow service. One cashier and several staff standing around. I would not recommend. Corporate should flush this store and rebirth a new one. Easily 5x longer than any other McDonald's I've experienced prior. Immensely disappointing experience.

I've been to Pat's multiple times and it's absolutely the REAL king of steaks! I have yet to try Tony Luke's, as I hear it's also very good, but compared with regards to Pat's compared to Geno's there is absolutely no competition. First, they do not need any type of over the top promotional decor to attract customers because once you try their cheesesteaks you know who to go to for your next one.

I'll do my best to describe their "Cheesesteak Wit". Once you receive the cheesesteak, you can head left to the condiments where you can add hot sauce, ketchup, whatever you want onto it, but I prefer to keep it the way it is because adding anything else would just interfere with the original taste. Once you take a look at the cheesesteak you immediately notice that it IS greasy, oily and full of steak juices. The bread just soaks up all those juices and softens up quickly so you have to dig right into the cheesesteak ASAP. However, the moistened bread goes fantastic with the juicy steak and abundance of cheese they put on it. The bread is not hard, so it's very easy to digest with bites of the steak.

The flavors of soft slices of juicy, hot steak with the cheese wiz are blended so perfectly here. The juices incorporated into the bread make chewing and digestion very easy. That is why Pat's is the King of Steaks!
Tourist trap, overrated! I am sorry but if I am in South Philly for a sandwich, I am going across the street.

Honestly if it was possible to give the place (-) STARS I would.

First off, If you are going to be an asshole to your customers please make sure your food is good enough to make us forget about it . God forbid somebody asks for fried onions instead of saying "Wit" like a fucking illiterate neanderthal.

Second off, Is it thin sliced ribeye or thin sliced rubber?
Do you guys use seasoning? I can assure you salad oil does not add flavor it just makes it greasier so you can swallow without chewing so you don't have to go through the agony of actually tasting the food. 

What a fucking horrible place.
I wish Rocky would have ran past Dalessandros so out of towner's dont waste there time.

Waited 10 minutes in line just to order in the drivethru. Only one car in front of me. I ordered the buffalo chicken sandwich. It was just of. The crunch was good but the breading was absolutely flavorless. The buffalo sauce was good. Sandwich was kind of thrown together. Was disappointed with this place. It's edible but it definitely needs the sauces. Definitely better options around. Even supermarket fried chicken is better!

Even though I am NOT a cheese steak lover (I rarley eat them - maybe 1-2 times a year), and I like Jim's better than Pat's, I prefer Pat's to Geno's.

I am also friends with a member of the Olivieri family - so I have to like Pat's better,

I order (quickly) a chicken cheessteak 'wit provolone and 'shrooms.

Too bad it's always so packed there's nowhere to eat. What a greasy mess!

I am convinced beyond a shadow of a doubt, that Pat's put something in the Whiz.  I know it.  How else can I explain my manic addiction to these things?  That insane ordering system and the punishment of being thrown to the back of the line is some miscreant's way of demanding perfection in exchange for partaking in a *plain steak wit'* which for you neophytes means *no cheese, with onions*.  Pat's unassuming, slightly dilapidated storefront pales in comparison to the glitz of Geno's flashy, whorish neon establishment across the street.  But Pat's emerges victorious in the cheese steak battle of battles: a blind taste experiment conducted by me, cheese steak neophyte.  I tell you, between that and the fries slathered in Whiz, Pat's may be the only reason I would venture into South Philly.

Loved. My husband and I drove to philly from New York just for cheesesteaks. There was a line when we got here but it goes super fast. They have two windows, one for cheesesteaks and the other for fries and drinks. Cash only. The cheesesteaks came out right away, the meat is cooked perfectly, with just the right amount of cheese. The cheese fries are great, we didn't even order extra cheese and it comes pretty heavily coated in cheese. My husband likes geno's but I prefer pat's!

A co-worker spoke if this place that I did not even know existed. My pizza is so flavorful. My crust in thin and gluten-free. Topped with tomato sauce, vegan cheese, vegan spicy chorizo, and roasted broccoli. Yum! Staff was friendly and the musical playlist was great.

The food was pretty good.  Our family decided we didn't live cheese whiz, but that was our fault not ordering the provolone. The bread and steak were really good though.  

Pat's is in a very urban part of Philly right past little Italy (the street where Rocky ran in Rocky 1, 2 and it was in Rocky V as well).  I don't know what it would be like at night, but lunch was fine. 

I'd go again, just get the steak with provolone.

First time ever at Pats and have to admit I was underwhelmed with my cheesesteak. Isn't this place supposed to be the best in PA? My sandwich was made in record speed though but the meat was dry. Went with whiz and onions which was the only thing making this cheesesteak work.

Too bad I read the reviews after the fact and realized I went to tourist trap and could've gone to a number of better places. 

Next!

The picture doesn't do it justice. 
This cheesesteak was delicious! I ate half and had the other half for lunch the following day. (And even reheated it was still great!) They are heavy handed when to comes to the steak so that's a great thing!

The cheesesteak I just had is not only the worst I have ever had, it is among the worst items of food I have ever paid for at a restaurant in my life.  It was served barely lukewarm,  with unmelted cheese, stale bread, and  seemingly unheated canned mushrooms on top.  It was also served about 30 seconds after ordering it, which probably tells you everything you need to know about the method of preparation. 

On top of that, it was ridiculously overpriced.  I don't know how this place enjoys the fame it has.

This is amazing. I sit to write a review on a place that has already been Yelped over a thousand times. There isn't much I can add to what hasn't previously been said, but I had one of the best tasting Philadelphia Cheese Steaks ever. It's a local institution, late night gathering place and the rivalry between Geno's and Pat's just adds to the fun, the excitment and the competition over which street joint (yes, both of them are dive-y street joints), in Philadelphia, has the best Cheese Steak. Though I fear assassination from one of the follower's of Geno's, I'll have to cast my vote and lot with Pat's. I'm sure some of the one star ratings for Pat's are undercover Geno's fans and I'm sure that some of the one star rates for Geno's are likewise Pat's fans; but don't tell anybody I said so. I'm sure that no self respecting Yelpite would stoop to such cowardly low life tactics, but then again, this is Philadelphia, isn't it?
WHY DOES PATS THE CREATOR OF CHEESTEAKS HAVE 3 stars ?!!!!! That's BS . Probably a bunch of yuppies tourist rates this place. The started the CHEESTEAKS ! The steaks are always consistent

I'm not a cheese whiz fan, but I went with the flow and had the cheesesteak with onions, cheese whiz & mushrooms. It was so delicious!  You order your sandwich in one line and then order your drinks and fries in another line.  Line goes fast as they have it down!  Don't ask any questions as they are very short with you and kinda rude. Maybe that's the Philly cheesesteak originators attitude?!?

Pat's was said to be the place where the "Philly Cheesesteak" or "Steak Sandwich" was created, so you just had to go there. Our first time in Philly we did just that and stopped here to eat and grab the original cheesesteak. 

There was a line but it went pretty fast. The guys running the place were pretty rude and basically, yell at you to take your order and move on. I ordered the original with fries and a drink. We all sat out on the picnic benches they have and ate our food. Yes, it was good. No, it wasn't anything special. I guess a Philly Cheesesteak is the same pretty much everywhere. 

It was a cool place to go to and eat at just to say we have been and done that. I guess you could go here once for the same reasons but it's not a place you're going to rush back to every time you're in Philly.

The service at this location is horrible these people really need to get their act together when you order a combination meal they only put a little teeny bit of fries in the carton they have a real nasty disposition when you go through the drive-through these people are slow as molasses they are horrible the food is given to you cold and is not hot they try to rush you out of the way and yet they're still slow as molasses and always get your order wrong these people are horrible where did they come from who is doing the hiring I'm so pissed off I spend my money here and hope that they have changed I come back and it's the same over and over again something has to be done police they're ruining American fast food restaurant this kind of behavior can bring this business to its knees all because of lazy and competent employees
Very good steak. Much better than Geno's I must say.

When your drunk there great. Sober the meat is tough & grossly fatty. 
Do yourselves a favor, look actors street. 
Everybody goes to "GENOS " !

Terrible service, the lady who took our order actually yelled at us for 3 minutes because she didn't hear us say no onions on one and onions on another. I get that it's a quick grab for food but she was extremely rude. Then proceeded to talk on the phone about how many people called out and ridiculous the place was. Cheesesteak was also not great, dry meat, cold cheese and tough bread. Overall bad experience which is disappointing after traveling so far to come here.

Long before COVID this McDs was el shitshow. Long ass slow lines no matter the hour of the day. Want a wrong order? You've come to the right place! Save yourself the headache of dealing with inept staff and go to Wendy's. Folks there give a crap about having a job. Fuck this place.

I'd give no stars if possible. The people who work there make it obvious that they hate working there every time I go. The girls working the drive through sound miserable over the intercom. And they wanted to charge me 27 cents for a sauce when I just bought a meal.... I've never been to any fast food restaurant and been charged for a sauce. McDonald's you've lost my business. Save yourself and go to Wendy's down the street in ridge!
It was terrible service everyone is rite I didn't get my food after I paid for it  it took 3 hours call and someone not even from the store said it was coming never came waited 3hours.,..

I've ordered from here through DoorDash 3 times now and it is without a doubt the best late night fast food in South Philly. Delivered on time, hot and fresh, with pretty sustainable packaging compared to others. Favorite items were the cheesesteak and battered onion petals, and the fries that come with most items are great too. When you have late night munchies you can not go wrong with Night Owls.

Went because I had to see for myself. I'm no foodie but this really is a tourist trap. Guys working seem totally uninterested in what they are doing and it shows in the cheese steaks just slapped together. I'm used to talking if i've got to wait in line. Everyone in line was out-of-town which was good since I'm new but bad since it really let me know that it's for tourists. Will try the other place everyone's talking about.

I loved my cheesesteak here!!! It came out super fast and was seriously amazing! Get extra napkins, lol! 

The only bad thing is a small soda is $4. The restaurant has a sign up though calling out the local government for passing some law that makes the soda so expensive

I left them a poor review on Grub Hub because I had a bad experience and the owner texted my personal cell phone number calling me a liar and "banning" me from ordering again. It was very aggressive and very unprofessional. There was no need to ban me, I'll never order from here again. Texting my cell phone and calling me a liar?? Wow. I've never experienced someone with such audacity. That's my PERSONAL cell phone number and they absolutely abused GrubHub by texting me on it. I guess I should be worried they're gonna find me on Facebook and harass me there too. Everyone gets bad reviews, it was a dispute on the timing. Deal with it in a professional way or don't own a business.
Overrated tourist trap. Go there as a check the box exercise only. Better cheesesteaks found at your corner pizza place....& yes, same with Gino's across the street. (Pat's is marginally better)

We really went here for the experience - what claims to be the 1st place for Philly cheese steaks while we were in Philly? Sure! We were going to go to Geno's across the street because we were told it's the best but it was busier & we were hungry. 

I can be a bit weird about meat & quite frankly there was too much fat on my meat for me to enjoy the sandwich. The fries were good and I tried Birch Beer (a type of root beer) which was fun. I don't think it was a meal worth $16 though!

Be prepared to order when you walk up or they will tell you to step aside and let the next person go. You order & pay for your sandwich at 1 window & if you want fries and/or a drink you order & pay for those at a different window.

The other people I was with are less picky than I am & they all really liked it. Some of the kids got hot dogs too which one of the workers said they started out with hot dogs there so I guess it was ok. :)

AWFUL....has PUNKS working there. I came in from a flight and it was 10:30 pm. Made it easy and ordered 3 'meals'- cheeseburgers which included a drink. I told the car order person 3 bottled waters.  I am assuming by this time the person that took the order was now the person distributing the food (not collecting the money).  He gave me the food and 2 waters and shut the door and I beeped lightly to get his attention. He angrily came to the window, and I told him I am missing a water. He asked for the receipt and I showed him, and I shoved it arms length and said something like "You didn't order no water there is nothing on here, so you got 2". I then told him I don't care what is written on there, I did order 3 to make it easy, in addition IT COMES WITH a drink anyway so  I just need my water. He couldn't get past it and I repeated that I am still owed a drink regardless of what happened behind the scenes....He again angrily gave me the water and slammed the window so hard it reopened. CLASSLESS.  I should mention Mr. Punk put in extra fries in the bag...so this also proved he does not know what he is doing and needs anger management classes..In addition, I saw 3 other cars on the side have to go up to his window for some things.
The steak was bland and shaved! Nothing special unless your  looking for a quick lunch on the go and of course was inn South Philly already!

I have been coming to Cantina for more than ten years now. A friend recommended it once as a laid back but delicious south Phila restaurant. My family and I have been coming here ever since. The menu at Cantina has changed a lot over the past ten years to include vegetarian and vegan friendly items, but the quality of the food, drinks and service has always been top notch. 

Some of my favorite dishes at Cantina are the chicken wings, the corn on the cob, the ceviche specials are always delicious, the tortilla salad (and I love to add avocado), the side of Brussel sprouts and the fajitas! They also make incredible margaritas (tons of flavors) and their bloody Mary's are delicious! The homemade mixes they use for these drinks are always so fresh! 

I live in NYC now, but I never tire of Cantina on my visits home :) :)

Not that good more hype and fame then a good cheese steak! Canned mushrooms who puts that on a cheese steak!!  I'm more disappointed then anything I've heard all the hype about them.

 I guess it's cause people watched a movie so it made this place famous! they have a lot to be thank for for "rocky" cause with out that few monuments of fame this place wouldn't even be a mark on the map let alone still in business!!  

Don't waste your time and time you will waste parking doesn't exist, tour buses of Chinese one after another!! 

I don't personally have a recommendation to a replacement but a friend said to me not to waste my time and go to johns roast pork"
14 East Snyder Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19148

I should have listen to him!!

Requiring that kind of money requires a High school diploma, reading and math skills. Also, basic communications skills will help. I called back to talk the manager whom barely spoke English. George is the man. Always making sure his staff is on point! And he could be hiring more drivers

I can't say enough about night owls fast food. Cheap prices and open late is exactly what you need in a heavy college area and they have both. Prices are reasonable even with delivery. You can order directly from their website with no delivery fee which is awesome. If you do decide to order from a third party app I recommend Uber eats. Door dash has a 5 dollar fee. Only complaint with delivery is you cannot track because they do their own delivers, but i appreciate that they call when their a few minutes away and then again when they arrive. Food is high quality and delicious. Quantities a little small but reasonable. On top of everything their take out containers are environmental friendly which is awesome! During one experience my Uber eats order had a technical error so they quickly remade the food and sent it right to my place with great communications. I can't recommend night owls enough! Thanks for feeding me so late hahah

Umm...YUM! The bread, the cheese, the meat  I had my own cheesesteak taste testing competition and Pat's for sure won. I even went back and told them. Can't believe I even tried anywhere else. Look forward to my next trip to Philly!
Don't waste your money. Way too overpriced & the meat has no flavor. The bread is alright but wouldn't recommend this place. Fries were good though
Waited 50 min for my mobile order. When I asked them, they said the order got lost. Other mobile orders in store was waiting a long time.

This is the worst McDonald's and the worker's here need retaining on social skills. I came in on Wednesday,  July 5th at about 7:40p.m. to get my grandson a happy meal of 6 nuggets and fries, the fries were damn near dark brown as me, the cashier was yelling and playing as if no manager or responsible person was there.
    I watched as the young cashier went to moving very slow and yelling at another person who appeared to be the damn manager. The orders weren't properly taken as the customer in front of me said, I'll never come back here again. 
     The INDIA DESCENT manager acted as if she was one of the kids, leadership reflects respect, it was very evident the worker's didn't respect the manager, customers, nor themselves.
      There needs to be changes and structure in this establishment if corporate was in here they would be so professional and not sloppy and so uncurtious.
Your typical delicious chipotle. Good for quick Mexican. Friendly staff, but I've had better chipotle elsewhere

I love to eat poke and this is my first order in Philly Poke. I ordered onigiri with spam, 6pc of shrimp shumai and I made my own poke. I was ordered a lot bc I thought only poke isn't enough for me, but I'm surprised bc they gave a big portion and also they give lots of protein (I choose salmon for the protein btw). I think Philly Poke will be my go-to place to order poke!! Love it!
Samson killed 10,000 men with the jawbone of an ass. I'm pretty sure this Wendy's is losing about that daily in revenue from the same instrument.

When it comes to ticketing and delivery of food, I've never a place exceed so much. However, there are a few problems with Pat's King of Steaks. There is virtually zero parking around the area, customer service feels rushed for newcomers to the restaurant, and overall the actual steak taste unseasoned.

When you hear about Philly, one of the main things you hear about is the rivalry between Pat's and Geno's.

I ordered my cheesesteak with onions and Cheez Whiz.  It came out in a flash as the line moved fast.  The guy in the window was very impersonal and businesslike as he kept saying "Next!" as the line proceeded.

The cheesesteak itself was attractive and good, but I can't say it had a real "wow" factor.  It's one of those tourist things you just feel you need to experience.  Two locals had warned me that Pat's and Geno's are overpriced and nothing special.  Both shared another place to go for better cheesesteaks.

When in Philly, visit both places, but be forewarned that you probably won't be blown away by either place.

This place is better than Geno's, but worse than Jim's. I like the way their chop their onions smaller here, but they don't mix the cheese in as well and their rolls are usually a little bit more stale than Jim's.

Grease

Next is Pat's.  The Philly staple.  I have actually been here 3 times and all 3 visits resulted in the same dilemma.  Pure grease basically pouring out of the sandwich.  One time I was completely wasted and I think I actually enjoyed this grease stream.  The other big problem here is that Pats doesn't put much of this greasy horse meat on the sandwich so it's another Philly cheese steak that is loaded with cheap cheese wiz.  

I won't be back to Pats, sorry another fail.  

Thanks

Compared to Geno's the steaks here are smaller and they cost the same.    Another star off for cash only business. 

Geno's accepts charge cards and their steaks are larger. 

There is also a much smaller seating area compared to Geno's.  More lighting on Geno's makes it easier to see your food when you are drunk.
Ordered from here one late night and not only was the delivery quicker than expected, the food was on point!! Will 100% order from here again!

The original. It was great went wit and whiz and provolone for the cheese and did not disappoint. The onion to steak ratio was impeccable and the cheese whiz really tied it all together. Would go again if I lived in Philly.

Everyone's gotta have the "famous" one, but there are many better steaks around the city. There's no heart in the food just quantity. Asked for American, got wiz slapped on and it thrown in my face. Meat wasn't even hot, just warm at best from sitting in a pile on the grill.

Chick fil A in general seems to be hit or miss lately and this was definitely a miss. I ordered 2 chicken egg and cheese biscuit and both were cold with a tiny piece of chewey, tough chicken. Tasted awful for a sandwich I regularly love and eat. The tiny piece of chicken didn't even take up half the biscuit on both sandwiches. I could definitely tell this sandwich sat a while before being served to me.

They forgot my chalupa. It is a pretty dirty crappy Taco Bell...but what do you expect...it is Taco Bell. My girlfriend loves it, I might die from eating it but as long as she is happy.  They forgot my chalupa.

Fantastic pizza. Best ever!  No exaggeration. Custom build your own. With a huge variety of healthy ingredients and wood oven baked !! Great selections of beverages and really tasty salads. All the ingredients Are super fresh with various delicious sauces. Talk to Alfreda or Micki who along with the rest of the staff take very good care of you personally. This is he fast food concept of the future.

Ain't nothin "gourmet" about these sandwiches. In a word: yuck. The turkey was slimy loaf product. That pale processed-feeling shredded iceberg lettuce. This was ordered in-store with no service complaints, was ready very quickly, and the order was accurate... but to me this was just overpriced subway/wawa; I threw 75% of mine in the trash(it kills me to waste food, but this was the kind of sandwich that it felt more wrong to keep putting into my body rather than the garbage) and ate the remaining 25 out of sheer necessity.

For the positive, the location is clean. I ordered sandwiches using the Subway app, which allows you to request more or less of ingredients. I asked for more of almost all vegetables, and there were maybe 4 pieces total (of each) on a foot long sub of onions, green peppers, and banana peppers, and barely any lettuce and spinach. Scrawniest sandwich I've ever gotten from a Subway.

X marks the spot. One of the most well known/infamous, albeit coolest and interesting "food fights" is Pat's vs. Genos

Who has the better cheese steak?

A question that cannot be simple to answer, for everyone has their own choice, and theory as to why...

I wont go into who has the best, because so many like to mention the less popular places that claim them to be more delicious.
  Keeping it between these two spots, there is indeed a bit more life at Geno's, and is clearly more flashy than Pat's; but, in this food feud, it certainly isn't equivalent to a decision one way or another.

You will truly have to take the trip to E Passyunk Ave and prepare your ordering method as you wait on line to see for yourself, and become the next professor of perfect Phillies. 
  I took the drive from NY, and got there at 3 am, the lines for both Geno's and Pat's were around the corner; At Geno's, the people waiting on the line were more fun and friendly, more outgoing, than those at Pat's.

All that said, X truly marks this treasured spot with the road crossing in the middle of these two steak stands; Both open 24hrs and both drawing their loyal fanatics, Hold your own taste test and see for yourself. Let me know what you think too!

My opinion of Pat's is on par with their running mate across the street, but my heart goes to Geno's since they were my very first.  

Love of cheese steaks was new for me and it was a confusing time in life, how could a guy choose just one meat?

All this being said I've run rampit around philly, knocking up all the pretty phillies I could wrangle.   They all have their own shine and their own down sides, but that's just the crazy game of love... I'm still talking cheese-steaks if you've gotten lost.    

okay, my time is up, go try everywhere you possibly can and message me your favorites!

Here @ Pats if the lines short I'd suggest grabbing a provolone cheesesteak wit onion

Manager is professional and helped out the best she can.but the staff had a attitude for no reason. 
Like if you don't want to work at Wendy's find a different job that best fits you.
Cause my order was messed up and went back to get it fixed and they messed it up again..I will never eat from there never again. 5 thumbs down.

Came down to finally try one of these "amazing" cheesesteaks from philly. First stop Pats. I ordered the American mushroom cheese steak. The guy was rude, the bread was cold, the sandwich was dry, the meat had no flavor or taste. No wonder it had the shortest line for cheese steaks in the area.

Wow. Is all I can say. Stopped here on a rainy and dreary day just to give it a try. My husband loves cinnamon sugar pretzels and is used to Auntie Annie's being a hit or a miss. This pretzel was 100% a hit! It was so soft and they made it to order. So delicious!! I had the twisted braid and that too was so fresh and soft. Husband said he's never going back to Auntie Annie's again! Customer service was also great too!!

Took a Lyft to the famous Pats with Geno's just across the street. Ordered a cheesesteak sandwich "wit" with onions and provolone cheese. It was ok. Nothing super great about it. It needed some dressing of some type and more cheese. The fries were yummy tho. Cash only!!

Definitely a good cheesesteak but didn't come close to the one I had from Dalessandro's! 

Meat to bread ratio was good. The flavor of the meat just needed some love.. more salt or seasonings would do it. The roll was delicious as always! 

I ordered a mushroom cheesesteak with grilled onions and whiz.....wished it had for grilled onions for flavor. 

Not a horrible cheesesteak but not the best.

This place is really great if you want to grab a quick lunch or dinner. The burgers are really good for the price you are paying for them, which is incredibly inexpensive. The fries are fine, nothing too outstanding about them but they definitely aren't bad at all and this place gives you a lot of fries- maybe more than some people can eat in one meal. The atmosphere however is a little distressing. The place is awkwardly shaped and arranged and too spacious (it's usually empty when I go in, so maybe that's why I think it's too roomy), & it just doesn't look very clean. The first time my friend and I went there I really didn't think I'd wanna eat anything from a place that looked like that...the floor just looks kinda dirty. But hey, it's a quick burger place not a 5 star restaurant so I really can't complain about the atmosphere too much. Service is fine, never had anyone be rude or anything. Good place if you are trying to save a few bucks on dinner or lunch or want to eat fast.

I think the food is absolutely delicious. I've been vegan over 5 years and have frequent most of the vegan businesses. The wings are some of the best I've ever had. The Mac and cheese is good and I've had the string beans and Brussel sprouts are pretty good. My favorite item has to be the seafood salad!! You will never miss the real thing! My last visit I also tried the banana pudding cake. My only complaint is the portion size for the platters starting at 23 dollars I think the portions should be bigger. It would totally be 5 stars if the portions were worth the money. The quality and taste is there but it could be less expense I've or bigger portions.

Definitely not the king of cheesesteaks. This is my first time in Philly so I wanted to try this because it was one of the original cheese steaks apparently. My mistake. This is the worst cheesesteaks I've ever eaten. Meat had no flavor. Bread did not taste fresh. The food was dry and small. I spent $20 on it due to cavier fees. It should have been $4.

Came to Philly on vacation and had to try out Pat's. Seating is very limited compared to the crowd and the line moves so so so fast. They were literally asking for my order before I made it to the window. You order cheesesteaks at one window and then sides and drinks at the next. I got a cheesesteak with mushrooms, peppers and onions and the cheese wiz. It was so good! But I did have to stand up to eat it.

Enjoy my Two visits to Pats in November. Sandwich was loaded with steak.  First visit I had one With Provolone, second visit was with Whiz

I preferred With Whiz.
