rude drive  through service! They don't fallow safety protocols!  Saw employees talking and not having their masks properly covering they're mouth! Today was my last time ordering at this restaurant!

i have never in my life left a review online of a restaurant-but i need philly to know about this place. i live in the suburbs & got home really late from work in center city, without having eaten all day. i was super hangry & exhausted, to say the least, so i ordered food from grubhub from night owl (w/out realizing they were in south). they reached out right away to let me know they were wrking on my food & it might take a bit longer to get to me given that i live 40 mins away. they were so so nice, i've never ordered from a place so accommodating-customer service is 100000/10. the food was so good-i got a cheesesteak & fries. it was still warm by the time it got to me & the cheesesteak was seriously top tier. the cheese was melted all the way throughout the sandwich & the meat & onions were seasoned perfectly. i could go on-but you get the gist. would recommend a million times over!

When in Philly try a "real" cheese steak right? I looked up the most popular ones, and read about Genos VS. Pats, right across the street from each other. So we figured we'd try one from each. We tried Genos first, and then went over to Pats. You definitely need to know exactly what you want when you get up to the window. These guys don't play around. No one was rude, they are just very to the point, and all about getting the food out quick. I preferred Pats as far as the meat, I like the more "chopped up" steak. Genos meat was more like thick slices. Pats bread wasn't as soft though, so I mostly just ate the filling out of the steak. The cheese wiz was really good though on these Philly steaks, I had never tried that before. So between Pats and Genos, I'd say I preferred Pats overall. Just be sure to order correctly- I was listening to other people order before and after us, and you can tell the locals from the tourists for sure. The locals simply for a "wiz wit onions".  Really funny.

"Open 24 hours"... or when we feel like it. That's the way it seems to be in some of these 'neighborhoods'. Pulled in around 7am on a rainy Monday morning... didn't feel like coming to work? Answering the phone? I SHOULD'VE grabbed something at the Wawa when I left the house. Now I've got to harass McDonalds corporate over these problem locations.
Update- So I'm writing this review as I'm sitting at the window... finally a woman unlocks the window and says 'we're not open'. Okay....
This place is solid every time we've ever been! We love the vegan options and have wonderful Margaritas every time
Very mediocre sandwich. Steak was hard and without taste. Too little cheese. Fries were soggy.
Best cheesesteak in Philly and the world! Staff is helpful, fun and professional! People that have bad comments are angry and jealous! It's beyond delicious!
The food is disgusting. The steaks have way too much gristle and fat. I do not understand why people claim the food is good.

Order the pizza wit.     Trust me they have the best pizza steak anywhere.





Been coming here for 50 years the one and only original.
Great food, great service.  I am a night owl myself and appreciate that places like this are open late.

Definitely not the best cheese steak in the area, but it's a fun touristy place to stop. Just bring gobs of cash.

Basically, you walk up to one window where you order your steak (my fave is whiz with onions). You fork over $8.50 - then you wait on line at the next window and order fries and a drink - and fork over another 8 bucks or so. Then you try and hold the steak, cup of fries and soda while wandering around looking for a free table or loitering in front of people that appear to be finishing up. It is a bit of a juggling act. There is no indoor seating or bathroom to speak of.

They do take credit cards, but it takes longer to process and you get lots of dirty looks from the cashier and people in line behind you. Tip: Have your cash out and ready for when you step to the window.
Hands down the best in philly. I don't know why this place is so poorly rated. It's incredible! Best cheesesteak I've ever had. Plus they have large sweet peppers outside to add on top.

Great area and pretty good cheesesteaks! I got a steak with American cheese and without onionsThe lines move fast, and you get your food quick. The only problem is that the steaks are a bit greasy, but overall I believe Pat's steaks are better then Geno's. Good steaks!

To put it shortly:
Dear heavens, this place is the BEST. The absolute, best Mexican. 

More details, maybe:
My friends and I came here to celebrate one of our friend's birthday, as it was his favorite place. We were greeted-with cheer, and the friendly hostess immediately led us to our table. Then we were served and checked on frequently. 
From start to finish the service was fast, friendly, and on cue. 
We were four, and the menu was intersting. I believe we ended up ordering everything on the menu. And we loved everything we ordered.
I would personally recommend the Camarones al Ajillo( garlic shrimp as an appetizer), Pescado (mani mani for your main course) and crème brûlée, which most of you, probably, know it is my my favorite dessert. It was a sad moment when the last bite of the crème brûlée was devoured, I had to order another one.

I can't wait to go back to Cantina Los Caballitos.

Four and half Yelps.

Everyone told me I couldn't go to Philly without trying a cheesesteak sandwich. I chose Pat's since it looked to be a more humble establishment and in my experience the glitz and glamour don't equal good food. The young guy taking my order must've had a hangover from the night before because he was just plain rude and obnoxiously arrogant while I placed my order. When I paused to ask him if there's a problem he told me to hurry up and "spit it out" as if to embarrass me. Huh? WTH?!? Wrong girl on a Sunday am buddy. I ended up ordering one sandwich despite being hungry and got a beverage instead. The one taking the order needs some customer service classes - especially in these COVID times. People can just cross the street and get a better sandwich from a racist bum. I asked for provolone cheese and he gave me wiz instead! Overall a bad experience for me. I could've gotten the same sandwich in NYC, better tasting with way less attitude and aggravation and not travel 2 hours for Millennial Entitlement!!! NEVER AGAIN!!!

After watching numerous shows and documentaries about the rivalry between Geno's Steaks and Pat's King of Steaks, my BF and I decided to do our own comparison (http://aprilsims.com/philly-food-review-pats-vs-genos).

Both places are located across from one another in South Philly at the crossroads of South 9th Street and East Passyunk Avenue.  In the middle of the "x" on one side is Pat's and across the street in the middle of the "x" is Geno's. It is a strange configuration, however it has been working for this neighborhood since the 60's and as the saying goes "if it ain't broke, then don't fix it."

From Pat's we ordered  a mushroom steak wiz wit. (wiz=Cheese Whiz, wit=with onions) .

From Geno's we ordered a steak provolone wit.

We sat down at a table halved the subs and began our comparison.

In this food challenge Pat's beat Geno's hands down. The bread from Pat's was soft and warm and the meat was sliced thin, seasoned, juicy and tender. We did not think we would be fans of canned/jar cheese (Cheese Whiz) on a sandwich, however it worked and it was a pleasure to eat. On the other hand the bread from Geno's was a little tough and chewy. Their meat was sliced thicker than Pat's and did not seem to have any flavor even though we had onions and cheese added to our cheesesteaks.
It was fun for the "experience" of going to Pat's, but the cheesesteaks were not very good!

*Overrated.
*located directly across the street from Geno's.
*NO bathrooms!
*eat here just to say you ate here. But the food is nothing to brag about.
Bread is so delicious.   We love so many places I. Philly but Pat's' wins our hearts every time.   It also helps that the family is so precious and after talking they gave me a Pat's ma

Ordered 3 Cheese Steaks wit onions and provolone. Would it kill ya to use a little flavoring on the steak? Some salt and pepper? Very bland. The cheese was sliced so thin, I thought they left it out, and the ratio of filling to bread - mostly bread. Also $5 for a cup of fries? Come on! This was not a good experience.

We walked 24 blocks to this place from the Liberty Bell. I was looking forward to having a real Philly cheesesteak from Pat's. They claim to be the first and all.

Waited forever in a huge line that wrapped around the block onto the street. I had my order all ready. Got mine with cheese wiz. Not enough cheese on it. The sandwich was bland and left a lot to be desired. Nothing I would ever want to eat again. I've had better cheesesteak sandwiches in LA.

We also got fries with extra cheese and that tasted okay. We had to get in a different but shorter line to get that and the soda. The cheesesteak line is just for cheesesteak.

Seating is hard to find and pretty dirty. The employees are rude and you see and hear them joking around and cussing at each other.

I was heading to Panera Bread on City Line Avenue and parked in the lot in the back. However, when working towards Panera, I realized that a new restaurant, Jason's Toradasu had opened right next door.

I had been to the Jason's Toradasu in Ardmore a few times, but this location just opened on Monday so I decided to check it out. 

I walked in and was warmly welcomed by the cashier who came around and explained their menu to me. They had some grab-and-go sushi rolls and salads. However, you could order anything from their menu and have it freshly made. 

I decided to go ahead and order one California roll along with their Sweet Potato roll. I was immediately given the California roll, but was told the sweet potato roll will have to be made. 

The restaurant was pretty empty when I was in so finding a seat was pretty easy. I was there during off-hours, so I don't know how crowded it can get. 

While I was starting my California roll, my sweet potato roll was dropped off. My California roll was very tasty and I loved how fresh all the vegetables were. The sweet potato rolls were ok. The sweet potatoes we're actually a type of purple yam, which was tasty, but nothing stood out about that roll. 

Also, the staff here was really nice and gave me a free drink because it was my first time at the new location. I decided to get a San Pelligrino juice. 

Altogether, the new Jason's Toridasu on City Line Avenue serves some tasty sushi in a nice environment with friend

This place was great back in the day but it has been getting worse & worse as the years go by. I rarely go anymore but my wife likes the nachos & I like the vegan wings so we stop by every once in a while. I ordered the vegan wings to go just now & they were a total disgrace. $14+ for 6-7 measly little squares of fried seitan, not at all like they were the few times I got them when I dined in. 
I would have taken them back if I lived closer.

I went to the Chipotle in Havertown, next to Panera at Township Line and WC Pike.  The food here is awesome, but you already know this.  Organic and local ingredients, who can argue with that?  There is a good variety even for my kids, who are very picky about what they eat.  The only reason I won't give five stars is because parking is pretty challenging with the Giant and all the other stores in the lot.

I used to Come here all the time, from south Jersey. I seen the app to Oder on Yelp and pay from cash app. I first went to check because I new this was always a cash place. The old guy yelled man yelled at me and said he never heard of this cash only. Very rude . Outside very dirty. Never again. Went to Geno's so pleasant so clean. So good

Nothing beats living next to 24 hour cheesesteak heavens! Like when your really hungry just get up take a walk and grab yourself a cheese steak from Pat's Steak. Lived here forever and eaten at both. I just like the taste of the steak at Pat's much more that I completely forgot what Geno's steak taste like! Haha. Pour the condiments on my onion whiz cheesesteak please: relish, ketchup and mustard! ;-) Add my cherry coke and my small cheese fries. Don't forget to head to the gym later because all that food you just ingested! Lol. No wait! Maybe just starve the next day to balance this meal you just had. Either way, it was definitely worth it.

Lena and I ate lunch here the other day while driving through Philly. I have eaten at both Pat's and Geno's before, and thought it would be fun to do so again. The actual sandwich is very tasty. I like the cheese wiz and onions, however, my complaint about this place does not stem from the quality of the sandwich. 
It's this: I HATE the fact That they compete with a cheese steak place across the street. I also hate that they have barely any seating, and That they only accept cash. Seriously? Why? Why not accept cards too? 
And is 11 bucks the going rate for a cheese steak? Maybe if you served it with fries.....and 3.50 for a soda? It's almost like they are turning this place into  a gimmick tourist attraction. So this is my reason for leaving a neutral review. I likely won't go out of my  way again!

My favorite cheesesteak of the three we tried in Philly. Being that cheesesteaks are a supremely uncomplicated food, it's difficult to pinpoint exactly why THIS one impressed over others, but I think it was the proportion of onions, amount of whiz, and the moistness and particular method of chopping the meat.  It all just added up for me.

I had the French Toast with bacon, scrambled eggs, and homemade tots. I ordered off of UBER eats so I don't really trip off presentation. 

My bacon probably would have been good if it wasn't burnt and the crumbled into pieces.  I don't know if they did it to fit in the small section of my to-go container or what. They definitely could have put my scrambled eggs there and my bacon next to the French toast. So that was disappointing. And like I said the bacon was burnt. The bacon was thick so it probably would have been great.

The homemade tots were fried mash potato balls delicious. I was kind of upset because they only gave me like 4 but they were very filling.

The French toast was regular.

Overall the meal wasn't anything special nor was I expecting it to be. But the tots stole the show. I'd order again but I think I would rather go to the restaurant and eat in. 

Sorry no picture ‍

So, made a quick visit to Philly and took the Geno's vs Pat's challenge. The ordering process seemed to be pretty similar. Both were cash only. Pats claims to be the originator of the cheesesteak. So I order one with provolone cheese. The bread was basic. The meat was shredded and had some flavor. The provolone cheese was melted but stuck to the side of the bread. Not mixed I. Which would have made it better. Still liked it better than Geno's.

AFTER WAITING THREE HOURS for my food and texting the CELL PHONE Number (bc this is NOT a real business!) My pizza finally arrived. I Wish I could post the video of the "seafood" pizza that I received. I paid $36 for a TERRIBLE looking cheese pizza that had baby shrimp and what looked like PULLED PORK on it. And it STINKED to the high heavens!! I gave that BS RIGHT Back to the driver who said to me "Imma call Grubhub and get your money back. But when they call, don't answer, or you won't get your refund..." I looked at her like she was a damn fool and shut my door. I called the "business line", the "owner" answers (you can CLEARLY hear he's driving a car!!) and says "Night Owls!", like he's in an actual place of business. We argued and he hung up on me. I promptly contacted YELP Live Support to receive my refund. NEVER AGAIN!!!!!!!!!! DISGUSTING!

[1177]

4/2021

Wow! This is probably the worst Wendy's I ever visited.   I went thru the drivethru..  The line was very long.  The cashier/worker was NOT friendly.  Made me feel like I was doing her a favor.   

Something was also wrong w/ my food.  Soda was flat and food was "off".  I can't explain it but it was not right.   I've had Wendy's plenty of times.

Anyway I tossed my food since my stomach started to hurt.  I will NOT be back.

Pat's or Genos? Genos or Pat's? Its like asking me if I am team Edward or team Jacob?
Well, I prefer Pat's- the bread is better. I will have to say that eating one of these can get messy, I had cheese whizz drop everywhere.
Pat's is good, but its not really worth the hype to be honest. I came here after dinner, and there was no line!

If they build a monument to the ODB here I will give them another star. 
I've been in the drive through for 23 minutes. All I'm getting is a large coffee. 
They are all in there fighting about taking orders.

OK, you go here for the greasy, beefy, cheesy, onion-y steak sandwiches only.  Everything else on the menu is moot.  Here is where you go to experience the famous, if not notorious, Philly Cheesesteak.  The bread is warm and soft to the touch.  And when you bite into this you taste the whole gamut of flavors all at the same time working in harmony together in one convenient masterpiece right in the palm of your hand.  

First timers beware.  I was scared to order at the window.  In fact I don't remember the last time I ordered.  I get the hubby to handle the grueling task of ordering.  By that, I do mean the hurried, rushed feeling that you get when approaching the window.  You need to follow the rules of ordering; think of Soup Nazi for you Seinfeld fans.  This is Philly for ya, but I love coming here.  But, seriously, Pat's people have personality and I would not change a thing about it.

We usually take out and drive off because parking is challenging and the streets are narrow.

This is the place I definitely take my visitors to fulfill the Philly Cheesesteak curiosity.  I've been visiting for more than 10 years now and I can always rely on it to be exactly the same almost to the point of calling it comfort food.

By far, this is the best all-around Mexican place in the city! Mexican is one of my favorite cuisines, so I've tried lots of places. Their chicken enchiladas and margaritas are to die for.

They have lots of seating available inside and outside. Usually there is a wait, but they will take your number and text you when your table is ready. The service is always very friendly and professional and food has always come out quickly. 

As mentioned, their alcoholic drinks are high quality and delicious. If you like margaritas, you won't be disappointed here. They have several flavors available, including unique ones like guava, passion fruit and blood orange.

When we visited Philadelphia, I had to go to the two famous Philly Cheesesteak places.  Are they tourist traps?   Maybe, but I enjoyed going to both places.  Pat's King of Steaks was our second stop.  Found street parking right next door to the competition. Our timing was perfect for both places because there was no line of people at either restaurant!!

We wanted to do our own taste test competition so we ordered the Cheesesteak with cheese wiz and onions from both places. We both agreed that both sandwiches were delicious.  We also both agreed that Pat's King of Steaks sandwich was the best of the two!!!  The meat just tasted better!

Pat's may not be as bright looking as the competition across the street, but they are the champs in my book.

Would I like either place, if I was not a tourist?  Did I fall trap to the nostalgia of it all?  I don't really care.  All I know, is that both wifey and I thoroughly enjoyed our Cheesesteak sandwiches wit and with the wiz!!

Some racist fucking people in there! Let someone else dine in and chose not to say a word 

I ask the counter lady if dine in is open she said yes. He walks out and confronts me. I calmly explained what the woman told me behind the counter no resolution for the customer. They have a day to rectify this situation or i will be reporting them to the health inspector. A month after opening and it's already dirty

Know what's Philadelphians? Wooder ice. Butterscotch Krimpets. Scrapple. And soft pretzels jawns for breakfast. 
Know what's not Philadelphians? Getting sick of Cheesesteaks. Loving Rocky more than we do. And NOT liking Philly-style soft pretzels. Oh yeah, and Wawa withdrawal. 

Bet the last time you had soft pretzel for a breakfast on-the-run, wasn't too long ago. I had mine few days ago from Tasty Twisters.  Chewy, sweetish (lightly salted) and warm, fresh out of the oven in a brown paper bag. 
If you find yourself in Manayunk, do yourself a favor, and give Tasty Twisters a try. 

Four Yelps.
After we had a bad and not fresh sushi lunch at the sushi house in Jenkintown, we head over to grab some chicken sandwich. There was little wait when ordering but our order came out fast.

Being the staple that Pat's is, it was the first place that I ate at when I visited Philly.  I stopped by at around 9:30 am.  Yeah, sort of an odd time to go for a steak sandwich but I wanted to avoid the long lines and be able to find parking.  And I managed to do both.  

As of now, there are almost 4,000 reviews on Yelp and Pat's is currently at 3 stars.  I'd say that's about right (I'm giving it three stars as well).  My sandwich was fine but it wasn't amazing.  I probably didn't have the freshest meat in my sandwich as I went really early in the morning.  It was fairly dry and didn't taste like a whole lot.  But the fries were fresh and I put some hot sauce on my sandwich so it all worked out.  

There is some outside seating in case you want to dine on location.  You also need to know that it is cash only.  The staff was friendly enough. 
 
I feel like eating at Pat's is much more about saying that you've eaten at Pat's because it's an institution as opposed to eating there because it's the steak sandwich in town.  I mean come on, Rocky ate here.  And it's marked by an engraved tile on the floor.  All of this being said, you've got to eat here at least once.  I think I'll check out some other sandwich shops around the city for the sake of comparison.

The food is passable Mexican food. It's good, but not the best in the city. The only thing I actually crave from there or really ever rave about is guacamole (but I put guac on just about everything, so that might just be me).

What's both a plus (as a 20 year old) and a minus for me is they don't card. Like obnoxiously don't card, so I feel like whenever I'm there I'm surrounded by teenagers sipping on margaritas, being loud and obnoxious.

Overall? It's okay. Good if you happen to be in the Passyunk Square area, but not really worth going out of your way for.

On a brisk, sunny Sunday just past noon, there's a chance there's an iron chair outside of Los Cabalitos calling your name. Once seated, enjoy a Big Bowl o' Guacamole - a Big Bowl of Right! It's the summer guacamole - suffused with a little lemon, maybe? Crisp red onions are scattered throughout the soft, just ripe enough avocado. Have a Tacate with a lime and invite a sense of contentment and calm into tu alma. And if you hang on for a few hours - a possibility, as the staff will never give you a second glance for overstaying your welcome - well then, get sloshed at the bar. There's always a fun, clamorous, zestful party at Cantina in the night.

Came down to Philly recently, and decided to do the big Pat's vs Geno's tasting.  I much prefer the look of Pat's at a glance; it's a simple stand with a few picnic tables, no flashy lights or gift shops.  I found the guys behind the counter to be gruff to the point of being rude; I'm from Brooklyn so I'm used to brusqueness, however watching them with several customers this was beyond that.  You order quickly and simply, Soup Nazi style.  On the bright side prices were reasonable even thoug it's cash only.

Meat was flavorful but on the dry side like it had been sitting out.  The bread really dominated the sandwich, and while it was good bread, this definitely needed more meat.  On the other hand the provolone was nice and sharp and the onions were perfect, however the sum was a really good--but not great--cheesesteak.  Worth comparing to Geno's etc, but not worth a special trip.

First time in Philly and even though we've tried other lesser known cheesesteak at Reading Terminal we still wanted to try Pat's.  It was a let down. Steak was bland. Provolone was not melted. Steak was warm but not enough to melt the cheese. They seemed to be pre made as we got them as I was going through my order. 

Glad we tried it though as I prefer to find out for myself and make my own opinion.

This was one of the better cheesesteaks we had on our Philly tour. I really love the bun here. However this place is cash only. So make sure you bring cash.

Came here one afternoon on our tour of Philly to try as many cheesesteak as we possibly can. This one was actually a pretty good one. The bun was actually quite tasty, it was toasted and a bit crispy which I really liked and had a really good consistency and texture. There could be a little bit more meat inside the sandwich but that was OK. They also had unlimited amount of sauces and all you can eat pickled peppers. That was a really nice feature.

Do you watch out for the little birds and pigeons that tries to come in and steal your food. Outdoor patio seating is great.

As over-hyped and bland as a tourist trap can get.

All the grease, price, and wait without the flavor, character, nor experience.

I've had way more tasty cheesesteaks (with cheez-wiz) at random NYC diners than Pat's.
Closed by Health Department.  Very unfortunate but the conditions must be of significant concern for this outcome.
Do not order on DoorDash they do not do credit they do refunds that never come back to you! They also keep their app on knowing they system is down to collect the money ! Ask me how I know?

One of those must try things in Philly. Honestly, it was okay but you should try it once. Have exact cash ready to pay and order with the right lingo! If you're going the classic route (and you should) - say "one wit wiz". You'll get a cheesesteak with grilled onions and cheesewhiz. I also tried Geno's across the street and I can't say there's a ton of difference.

I'm giving this four stars bc I don't want to cheat on genos. First time ever having a cheesesteak . I felt like a virgin who just discovered an orgasm. The cheese wiz was hot and messy and I loved the grilled onions . Why not more cheese on my fries ? Maybe a size up for my pants while I'm at it. The cooks were friendly and it came out super quick.
The steak sandwich wit the wiz was terrible. The meat must have been on the grill for 1/2 an hour. It was truely shoe leather. I would have rather had a steak ummm sandwich.

Double wiz wit + Pizza wiz wit = One happy little Drewgins (who reeks of onions).

You've all heard of a Philly Cheese Steak.  Well, these are arguably the best ones out there.  Are you in Philly?  Go the extra mile and come to Pat's.  Don't judge this wonderful sammie from anywhere else.  Go to directly to the source!  IMHO Pat's has the best combo of tender steak, fresh bread and tons of wiz from a large can. 

The routine is annoying the first time you order, but it's really not that difficult of a concept.  A few times I have gone to the window and ordered chicken wit broccoli. I laughed.  They did not.  I still got an awesome steak.  Take that Pat.

This is the worst McDonald's I've ever been to in terms of service. The drive thru line moved at a glacial pace and when i finally got up to the window (15 min later) they had a completely different Oder. They asked me to pull forward to wait and that someone would bring it out to me.... that was 10 min ago... the people behind me at the window still haven't gotten their stuff either. Idk what's going on but this is insane for a McDonald's

Visited this McDonald's at 4:45pm on February 27th. Outstanding job by the young lady that took the order and the money. Very pleasant personality and made me feel that my business was appreciated. There should be more employees like her. Outstanding example of customer service!
This was the worst cheesesteak I've ever had. It was served like warm, the cheese wasn't melted and they used canned mushrooms. The steak had no seasoning or flavor. The fries were decent.
These cheesesteaks are so good! Make sure to get all the toppings and cheese wiz. Plenty of outdoor tables and they literally make it for you in 10 seconds.

Friendly, fast service with lots of choices makes Blaze a good lunch choice. They have several signature pizzas that already have the combination of toppings and sauces worked out or you can make your own. It's the same style as its competitors for personal size craft your own such as Snap and Mod Pizza. 

I came in around a little after 1:00 PM on a weekday and there was no wait and a few people in the dining area. The staff member was really friendly and although I ordered the BBQ chicken pizza which already has set ingredients on it, he confirmed to make sure I wanted everything when he made it and made sure the levels of the BBQ sauce at the end were to my taste. 

I got the pizza to go since it was a beautiful day. However, it looks like there is plenty of indoor seating if you want to eat in. The pizza was your standard fast casual pizza, but the topping ratio was perfect. I was full but it didn't feel too heavy. I will likely return for lunch soon.
love, love, love. The meat was thinly sliced and oh so flavorful. The "whiz"  is truly something special (perfect for a cheesesteak, that is). I tried out Gino's too and it just does not compare.

Very disappointed. Dry with no seasonings. My cheesesteak wasn't even hot and my cheese was not melted. Save yourself the trip and head over to Dalessandro's if you're looking for a better cheesesteak.

I've come here quite a few times and am NEVER disappointed. The staff is super friendly and upbeat and work quickly. The ingredients are always fresh and portion sizes are a great value for the price range. I'll continue being a repeating customer.

I closed at work the other night and didn't feel like going out and mostly every other place that delivers was closed. I came across this place on Grubhub and figured since it was late and I was hungry I'd try it. I was a little weary after seeing some of the negative reviews but I definitely wasn't disappointed! The food was fresh and still hot which I was surprised about because I live in NJ. Which was another HUGE bonus. On top of all of this the food took only about 25-30 minutes to arrive which is great as seeing I've ordered at places right around me and it's taken well over an hour to arrive. This place is awesome and have the cutest little boxes. Keep in mind that if you do live in NJ they will charge for the toll fee which is totally understandable. We'll definitely be ordering from here in the future.

Most of the people who gave these Philly Cheesesteak places 4-5 stars must be tourists in Philly.  It's truly disappointing experiences for me as I have tried many cheesesteak shops in Philly, over many occasions, and none is worth my time and money.  
It's definitely better than Gino's (right across from it)
but to have a real cheesesteak you really have to come down to Al's Steak House in Alexandria VA.

2.5 stars for this Pats
Went to Subway to order a sandwich and they're closed before 10pm. The restaurant was clean as if they closed hours ago. I'm calling corporate in the morning.

Bread was soggy, Meat was boiled or something, Clearly didn't give no F**** at the trash they decided to serve me. Fries were okay but their prices are outrages for the trash they sell. Bucket list for my friend, only reason I came in here. Will NEVER be back!
The worst cheese steak ever!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Just do yourself the favor and don't even try it !!!!!!!!!!!!
A bit overrated, whiz and onions on steak are good, steak has nice flavor, portion was weak though and its overpriced. Jims is much better.

I've been here two or three times and honestly each time I remember why I don't come back. It's actually just a tourist trap... there are much better cheesesteaks in town (see Sonny's Famous Steaks). Before I went to Sonny's, I thought cheesesteaks were just bad because of my time at Pat and Genos. I might sound harsh, but if you look at my reviews I rarely give out anything below 3 stars. The bread is rubbery, meat is to chewy... wow. I agree that it's fun to try out both cheesesteaks and compare them, so props to their marketing I guess.

A friend convinced me to try this place instead of Geno's, and I don't regret it. My first ever philly cheesesteak was heavenly. I got a "whiz wit", which was stuffed with greasy steak, cheez whiz and onions. My order was ready before I even had the chance to pull out money. Also, this place is CASH ONLY.

The description sounded kind of gross. Seriously, cheez whiz? Don't be all bougie and pre-judge though. This is one of those "don't knock til you've tried it" situation. It's actually a pretty wholesome meal if you think outside the box. There's protein (steak), carbs (bread), dairy (cheez whiz), vegetable (onions) and of course plenty of essential oils. I will definitely be returning!

Surprised I haven't made a review for this place sooner. If you ask any of my friends, they'll tell you that if I could eat 1 thing for the rest of my life, it's poke, from philly poke only. I wasn't a fan of poke when I first had it at a different location, but after giving it a second shot at Philly poke, it became my favorite food. They have a lot of options for protein, toppings, and sauces and everything is perfectly proportionate in my opinion. I'm a big fan of spicy mayo and they are always happy to fulfill my request when I ask for more. Their service is also amazing, I love talking to the staff who always seem happy to serve me. The owner is always in a good mood, and always checking in on me whenever I come. I love having short conversations with him about my school and work life, and he loves to know that I continue to make the hike from my hometown in south jersey to philadelphia just for their poke. I haven't tried any of their other foods because I am always in the mood for poke, but they do have other options to choose from! And they have an entire fridge section of fun asian drinks if you so choose. I come here all the time whether it's reuniting with my city friends, an after-class meal, or whenever I'm craving philly poke. During pre-covid times there would be plenty of seating indoors in chinatown square, but they recently added outdoor seating! I'm super loyal to philly poke and I won't get my poke anywhere else, it's my favorite place to go!

I prefer Tony Luke's.
Parking sucks.
The line is usually always long but it moves fast.
Cheese steak is good.
Can sometimes suck to find a table.
If it's cold it sucks to eat outside.
Best when visited after a night of drunk madness.

Ordered from here a few times. Food is okay, but a bit too pricy for the quality. All of the messages about the owner sending messages to personal phones are wild but true as I've gotten a few. 
My biggest issue is that their online menu is very convoluted. 

You are told to select options on the menu but they aren't available. Put me off from ordering in the future.

First off, I wanted to post this review on here instead of Grubhub so that people who come on here and see the negative reviews won't get scared off like I almost was. Luckily, I had seen the high rating on Grubhub and trusted it. 

So glad I did. 

I got their signature chicken cheesesteak, Carolina gold wings and fries with whiz. At 1:30 am, and being a good distance away from them I was expecting everything to be cold and soggy by the time I got it. So you can imagine how shocked I was when their driver called me 20 mins later to say he was almost there. 

I don't even know how they cooked it that fast!

When it finally arrived the driver was super friendly and I could feel the heat from the bag. 

Needless to say, everything was exactly as I ordered, hot and crispy.

Do not let the negative reviews on here push you away, this is definitely a great spot for a late night meal!

First visit to Pat's, it's the originator of Philly Cheesesteaks so this was a no brainer.

Ordered the wit onions and cheese wiz which I could be totally butchering. I really do require the instruction sheet or a 101 on ordering these things.

I liked this cheesesteak second best to the three I tried on a short weekend trip.

I liked the bread and the meat but I think I'd order extra cheese wiz next time.

The meat is chopped which definitely seems to be the way I prefer it vs sliced.

Service is top notch, arrived to no line, ordered and was handed the cheesesteak in less than a minute. Serious 5 STAR service, the cashier was also wearing a really cut cheesesteak hat. I may need to Google it, I don't even really eat meat, or white bread but yet I want a cheesesteak hat (i don't even bother trying to understand my thought process anymore).

I'd return but there's another spot I did like better than this one.

CASH ONLY.

5 friends and I couldn't decide on Pat's or Geno's. So we decided to split up in 3s to order 1 cheesesteak each and we'll share it and compare which one is better.

So 2 friends and I came to Pat's and ordered a cheesesteak with wit and provolone cheese. We 3 ate our portion first since the rest of our friends were still on line to order at Geno's.

Honestly, Pat's cheesesteak tasted amazing! Super flavorful! When our other 3 friends came with Geno's, they also ordered a coke and cheese fries. We couldn't compare the fries(all wells...) but omg.... I gotta say, Pat's win!!! My other friends agreed too. Geno's cheesesteak was a bit dry. Maybe it's because they didn't order it with wits... lol

Definitely overhyped. Order the mushroom cheese steak on Uber eats when I needed a late night meal. The meat was flavorless so that was disappointing. It also came with grilled onions, which I didn't mind, not sure if it came that way or if they made a mistake. I had provolone cheese on mine and I feel like they didn't put enough cheese. I actually had to pour a salt packet on my sandwich because it lacked flavor, so I would say this was disappointing for my first Philly cheesesteak experience.

This Wendy's is really not good. The lady on the headset for the drive through was rlly nice and so was the girl at the first window but the food.... was bad to say the least. I got a medium meal w chicken nuggets and a frosty. The fries were so cold, soggy and limp. I literally could squeeze oil out of the fries they were so saturated and so so soggy. totally inedible. the nuggets were cold and when i got the bottom, my last two were not regular nuggets they were spicy. I really don't like spicy things at all and didn't notice before i ate the first spicy one. it was rlly unpleasant to end the meal with that, so technically i rlly only got 8 nuggets. Basically it just wasn't a good experience. Additionally, it was pretty crowded and usually that means they are actively cooking fresh food, especially fries. it's confusing to get such bad food when it's decently busy.

It's one of those places everyone either loves or hates so I had to try it. I held my cheese steak five inches above the table and watched the grease just run out of it.  I haven't been back since.

If you are hungry for junk get McDonalds it's cheaper and will stay in your body for an hour as opposed to Pat's which evacuates in less than 30 minutes.  Hope you parked close bro!  You don't want to get caught unaware on the walk back to the car.

Ordered the family meal. The amount of food vs the price I paid doesn't really add up. They were out of one of the sides I wanted so they replaced it with what they told me was a large salad. But how am I supposed to feed a family with the mini side salad they gave me. I asked if I could replace it with rice and some beans on top and they said no bc that was considered 2 sides. They didn't give me the sauces I asked for, and once I arrived home to actually eat, the food was absolutely terrible. The chicken was bland to say the least. The fries had no seasoning, and the corn ended up being the best thing i ordered but I mean can u really mess up sweet corn? Terrible service, terrible food, overpriced for no reason. Save your time and your money

We have seen this place being busy for months, so we decided to have brunch there. I ordered a breakfast salad without tomatoes or onions and with cheese added. What I received was a salad with onions and quinoa (which was not part of the description and which I don't like) and without cheese. I let them know and our waiter explained and said they would rush a fresh one. When it came back there were still quinoa pieces in there and it tasted and smelled of onion. Still no cheese. We were out for brunch and I was hungry, so I ate some, even though I did not enjoy it. That is my fault, but I imagine that, instead of preparing a fresh salad someone quickly and unsuccessfully picked out the larger pieces and served it again. To top it all off, I felt nauseous and unwell for the rest of the day.
In conclusion, if you care about how you are treated as a customer, or even just about receiving the food you order and are expected to pay for, go somewhere else. I would not even trust this place enough to prepare a to-go drink for me now. And of course, I will tell EVERYBODY of my acquaintance about the experience. The place makes brisk business,  so they probably don't care about one disappointed customer, but I thought I'd share so you know what you might expect.

Bottom Line: I prefer Pat's cheesesteaks over Geno's but once was enough for me given the lack of parking and lack of a leisurely dining experience.

For a long time I've been curious about Pat's and Geno's, probably thanks to features on TV.  I finally made it to Philly and tried them both.  I definitely like Pat's cheese wiz without better than Geno's because Pat's bread is soft while Geno's bread is chewy.  Another differentiator is that Pat's steak is chopped up while Geno's is more intact slices.  Both cheesesteak stands are located in a cramped and dirty part of Philly where parking is hard to come by.  You order at the window and then if you're lucky, can a score a spot at a picnic table.  I was at Pat's in the dead of winter so there wasn't a line and our order came up immediately.    I would have enjoyed my experience better if I could have eaten the $10 cheesesteak in a more temperate location with access to a bathroom.
