I had actually tried to check the yelp reviews quickly while in the drive through line, but for some reason this location didn't show up for me until I searched again later. Too bad for me

Simply delicious. Get cheese wiz on your cheesesteak...even if you think you dont like it you need to add that. I got my original sandwich with extra cheese and my husband went across the street and wished he would've got one at Pat's. Ha! Told him!

The world famous cheesesteak spot is a must visit when you are in Philly due to the iconic nature of the restaurant. But, compared to other cheesesteak places, Pat's is far from the top, and can sometimes be dirty on the outside. Overall, average place but is elevated by its iconic status.

I've only been to Pat's just one time, so this review is solely based on what I had that day.  I had a Mushroom Steak Whiz Wit'out and while it was very meaty, probably more meaty than any cheesesteak I've ever had before, it was sorely lacking in Cheez Whiz.  Well, there was a ballgame going on that day, so they were really busy and I could vouch for that.  It was still great regardless.  I'll have to come back here again maybe when it's not so super busy so I can get a cheesesteak that's not rushed.  Hopefully sometime soon!

Amazing cheesesteak! Ordered it from Gruhhub and it was still warm and delicious. It was also quick. Only thing is they forgot to add my onions and peppers, which I paid for. Besides that, definitely recommend!

Honestly I haven't been to Pat's in a few years. I went to Saint Joseph's University and this was always the late night run to spot for cheesesteaks. Nothing like standing on line and freezing your ass off for a great cheesesteak. 
When i was there a few years ago, it was as good as I remembered. Wiz Whit! it was juicy, tasty and cheesy. A great thing that was made out of simple ingredients. I understand that it now costs about $9 bucks, but worth it for the nostalgia for me at least. 
Yes there is a certain way to order and there are multiple signs and instructions on how to do it. You should know how to order when you get to the guy. The reason is to keep the line moving. 
I have never been to the place across the street. Actually not even sure they are still in business?
Philadelphia, Rocky and Pat's!!
I stopped in Philly for the day, I prefer more of Dalessandro's because its chopped, but depends if you want to wait. But Pat's wit whiz is really good.

Hit the drive through at 10:15 sat in the lit up menu waiting fir a few mins until I hear someone yell "we're closed". Google showed closing at 11, Yelp shows midnight, ok maybe they closed at 10, so I pull through the drive through instead of backing up and there are two cars waiting for food! It took TEN a minutes meanwhile 4 cars pulled in as well so I couldn't back out. This location continues to disappoint.

The girls here were definitely not paying attention today. They forgot my drink and they forgot all my friends children's drinks. That's a lot to forget. When I went up to the counter to ask for my cup she gave me a blank stare. At least the kids had fun in the McDonald's playground.
Good steak sandwich but not the best by any means.  Worth stopping by to check out and check off the bucket list.

Went through the drive through on 9/16/20 at 4:45 in the afternoon ordered a 3 peice tender meal and was charged 20.00 dollars.  I did not see this charge till I was home and I do not live in the area.  The young women stole from me.  I can not get through to the office no one is picking up the phone.  If you like being stolen from this is the place.  I am disgusted with people.  Shame on her.  DO NOT EAT HERE OR USE YOUR CREDIT CARD!

This was the first place we went after getting off the plane. Parking is crazy in this area, so grab whatever you can find. The best thing about Pat's is the older man who is outside the building and gives the place some character. The cheesesteak sandwich was fresh and I loved the bread. We had mushrooms, onions and cheez whiz on the sandwich. Know what you want before you get to the window.

Loved Pats!! Loved the workers (who were so friendly, welcoming and funny) as well as the food. Got the steak sandwich with onions and whIz. No wait and once ordered I got the sandwich in less than a minute. The steak was your typically shredded beef for Philly cheesesteaks, which was delicious. The whiz didn't overwhelm the sandwich at all and the bread was very good. Not too soft and not too hard. Can't wait to come back soon.

Good customer service and speedy drinks.
Decent prices and the smoothie was good but I've definitely had better.

Would like to try their juices.

Despite the bitter rivalry and committed fanbases, I thought both Pat's and Geno's were amazing! Trying both was definitely getting the best of both worlds ;)

At first bite, Geno's seemed to be the winner for me since I liked the texture of their bread more, and the fillings for both seemed comparable. However, the more and more I ate, the more Pat's grew on me! The juices from the meat were overflowing and the chopped up bits just went so well with everything.

My verdict? Pat's was the winner for me :) Can't wait to try more amazing Philly cheesesteaks in the future!

The folks at this place don't seem to know that when you ask for a salad it should have more than 1/2 cup of lettuce in it!  Worst chipotle I have visited!!!!  Oh and the sour cream looks as thin as heavy cream.

I've had lots of cheese steaks, some in recent years when visiting the Philly area, but most of them from the Chester and Media areas where I lived in the 60's and 70's.  They were to die for.. Fast forward to today when my 15 year old and I ordered with provolone and onions at Pat's while visiting our eldest son who lives in Philly.  I was so excited to introduce my hoagie/sub-loving teen to my favorite childhood take-out (well besides pizza).   Well he ate his in about 1 minute and said it was ok.  Clearly, I had built this up too much.  When I got two bites into mine, I found just a big bunch of gristle that I could not bite through.  It was gross and definitely not like the meat I remember having at any other place.  The prov was not melted, there was more gristle than meat, and the sandwich was too dry.   They obviously don't care about repeat customers if they serve such grisly meat.  I don't care how famous they are!  For $9 it should   SO sorry that I bothered going there.  I could have had and definitely have had a cheaper better cheesesteak at the Reading Terminal Mkt. or lots of other places.  Will never go to Pat's again.

I told him not to, but my good buddy and fellow Yelper Tom E (https://www.yelp.com/user_details?userid=g8j2ci2FcvmocszcO6ypNw) drove from the suburbs of Atlanta to my place in the city, during rush hour, to deliver a birthday gift that included one Pat's Original Philly Cheeesesteak. The cheesesteak had been flown in that same morning. Thank you, Tom.

For those who don't know, Pat's and Geno's are the most popular places to get a cheesesteak sandwich in Philadelphia. They are old and they are competitors. "Pat's King of Steaks" is the "inventor and originator of the cheesesteak sandwich." They've been in business since 1930. During one of my visits to Philadelphia, friends and locals steered me away from Pat's and Geno's, both of which are popular with tourists. Instead, I went to Jim's Steaks South Street: https://www.yelp.com/biz/jims-south-st-philadelphia.

It would not be fair to make a comparison of my experiences with Pat's and Jim's since I had to reheat Pat's cheesesteak at home while I had Jim's cheesesteaks fresh at the restaurant.

You can purchase Pat's cheesesteaks by mail-order through Goldbelly: https://www.goldbelly.com/pats-king-of-steaks. The cheesesteaks were shipped frozen with dry ice packs and reheating instructions. The cheesesteaks were already assembled and wrapped in Pat's signature logo'd white paper wrappers. The Cheez Whiz was packed in separate containers. At the time of writing this review, Goldbelly offered Pat's Original Philly Cheesesteaks in sets of four ($79 or $19.75 per sandwich), eight ($129 or $16.13 per sandwich), and 12 ($169 or $14.08 per sandwich). Shipping was included in the quoted prices.

Reheating was quick and easy. Instructions were to bake at 300 degrees for 10-14 minutes until the bread was lightly-crisped and the meat heated through. The Cheez Whiz could be reheated in the microwave or in a saucepan. I reheated the sandwich in my old toaster oven so it took a little longer than 14 minutes. I used the microwave to melt the Cheez Whiz.

I was impressed with how the sandwich turned out. It looked just like the cheesesteaks I saw of Pat's online. I had the "Wit" onions and Whiz version, but you can get "Wit-Out" onions and change the cheese to Provolone or American if you want. I think I may have baked the sandwich a little too long because the outside of the hoagie roll started to crack and it was extra crispy. That was okay, though, because the inside was warm, soft, and delectably chewy. The bread was good. There were plenty of tender morsels of quality ribeye, but what brought everything together was the melted Cheez Whiz. Mmm... That melted cheese coated the steak and eventually found its way to the bottom of the sandwich, soaking into the bread. This made each bite rich, flavorful, and really satisfying.

There aren't many ingredients - bread, meat, onion, cheese. Pat's found the right combination of quality, taste, and texture. If you're considering purchasing some of Pat's cheesesteaks via mail order, let this review be a vote of confidence. At the time of writing this, you can only get the Original Philly Cheesesteak via Goldbelly. The Mushroom Steak, Pepper Steak, Mushroom Pepper Steak, Pizza Steak, Fish Cake, Hot Dog, and Fries are not available online.

Enjoy.

I rescind a previous review in which I praised the fajitas, would have everything to do with the chef. 
My last two visits the service has sucked so extensively that I swear I will not give this establishment another dime. Today was strike three! Enough said!

I have heard from the locals in South Philly that this place was a tourist trap, but I wanted to be the critic. I would almost give 4-5 stars for the vibe at this place because it's pretty busy with plenty of outdoor benches. Even has a stone  by the order booth that shows that "Rocky" was filmed at this spot. The cheesesteak with provolone I bought for $11 was a difference story. Bread was too chewey and the steak was also dry and chewey. Not even close to the quality of Ishkabibbles up the road.

Pat's oh Pat's.... my #2 cheesesteak in Philly. (Second only to Tony Luke's)

This is the archetype of the cheesesteak, it's classic form. 

Not as robust or hearty a sandwich as a Tony Luke's, but authentic South Philly just the same. The meat and cheese are scraped off the griddle and slid onto the bread. Served to you with the roll agape, its contents oozing & steaming. 

Pat's is THE place to go late night after the bar. 

Upon arrival at Pat's you will notice the interesting juxtaposition of rival sandwich shops at that intersection. Much has been said of both. Fierce allegiances exist on both sides. Pat's has the character & consistency. 

That other place is just a neon caricature owned by an outspoken xenophobe.

Where do your allegiances lie, noble Philadelphian?

Mine are with PAT'S. 

My advice: Provolone with, after midnight.

Only slightly more edible than Geno's. This tourist trap doesn't even taste good at 4 am. Now that's saying something! Both Pat's and Geno's are cheap, fatty cuts of flavorless meat, served on stale rolls at a premium and shoveled out by the dozens by rude staff to tourists that are just don't know any better.

The only people in Philly that will tell you Pat's or Geno's are the best cheesesteaks in Philly are people that are CLEARLY not from Philly. 

Sorry but I wouldn't feed these to my dog.

The best steak sandwich! I love this place. So I was introduced to this place around 2012 when visiting Philadelphia. I automatically knew this was the best steak sandwich I have ever tasted. Me and my boyfriend drive from New York City to Philadelphia every few months just to get a sandwich and go back home. Everyone says we crazy but it's BOMB & Worth every trip all the time! Can't wait to go again!

Ordered cheese fries from this iconic Philly stand. I do not eat meat, otherwise I most certainly would have indulged in a phily cheesesteak. I love these fries. They were perfectly cooked on the outside and soft in the side. The cheese was not too salty. My only qualm with this store was that it was a little overpriced for cheese fries. However, I guess since its so famous it has the rights to overcharge for fries. Def give this place a try especially if you're not a native Philly goer.

I generally poo poo fast food restaurants however if I must partake in QSR I typically go to Chick-fila that being said I have been to Chipotle twice in the past week. 

This Chipoltle is in an extremly busy part of CC however they move very quickly and the food fills you up. You can choose three different tacos whether it be soft shell or hard for $9.99 not bad not bad. Also, you can put almost any topping in it but be advised if you want queso cheese your looking at another dollar.

Also be advise the hot sauce is pretty freaking hot and imo ruins the taco/burrito unless you really like hot sauce on your meal.
Great hoagies fast service and good food that you'll enjoy! The line gets long but it moves very fast.

Good, reliable cheesesteak with no frills plus delicious French fries. A little out of the way for a tourist, but worth the trip. I was worried about the COVID set-up and the hot peppers but thankfully they give it to you in a plastic bag. I'll always come here when I'm in Philly.
WOW. I have been to at least 30 poke places all over the US and Philly Poke is now one of my favorites. Fresh and tender fish, great toppings, quick service. I'd eat here weekly if I lived in Philly!
3.5. it was honestly really tasty, but literally the smallest wings I've ever eaten. At a dollar a wing they should be bigger

Ok, mornings at the airport are always funny.  Like Forest Gump would say, you never know what your gonna get.  I'm not talking chocolates, I'm talking customer service.  I was greeted with a smile, order taken, money paid, receipt given and a nice "please wait over there for your order".

As I was "waiting".   I was digging through my computer bag.  I hear someone say #1... number 1!  I think ... I'm not #1 by any means, but apparently today "I am"!  And what does this get me.... SIR, you ordered a #1!  Here it is ... and the lady behind the counter puts the bag down and walks aways.

Maybe the receipt should not have said #1479.

I look at the lady next to me, she rolls her eyes over what just happen.  I yell out.... "Have a Blessed Day"

  

Better, happier people today! When the management replies an extra star is always warranted.

Wowwwwwwwwww!!!! I've been researching for weeks to determine where I was going to have a famous cheese steak on my one day trip to philly. After days of analyzing the data, researching photographs, making pros and cons list I decided on Pats. The research paid off. Everything was perfect. Yes they are assholes here but you are in philly and that's to be expected. My girlfriend was licking cheese wiz off the paper wrapper. That's how you know it's good.

Let me first say that this does look like a really shady building since it is down a tiny little alley off Umbria Street and in a very plain, large brick building. But once you get past feeling like you're going to make a drug deal, you'll get the freshest, best pretzels in the city from a factory where they're made. Last time I was there, plain pretzels were 4 for $1. 

And it's the best when they're coming right out of the oven. Mmmm...

I've been to Philly a bunch of times and in all my visits, haven't noshed on a Philly cheesesteak. The group I was with on this occasion unanimously agreed that it would have to be from Pat's as we weren't hungry enough to get ones from each to compare. Plus, I don't each red meat that much anymore and didn't want a total stomach upset for the 2-hour ride back home. Pat's was good, we got ours witout but with wiz. Make sure you get the lingo down before ordering and heaven's to Betsy, you don't need to preface the sandwich with Philly - you're in Philly. It's like saying chai tea or ATM machine when you're there. While no one in our group dislikes onions, we figured if we're sharing it's easiest to get witout. That's an intentional drop of the H, don't @ me.

The meat itself was good, not as greasy as I had mentally prepared myself and the cheeze wiz, while normally I would classify it as an aberration of the American cuisine, fit in perfectly. The bread was meh, a bit on the stale side. It didn't soak in the grease at all which was, interesting? Now that I can answer 'Yes!' to the 'Omg you were just in Philly, DID YOU GET A CHEESESTEAK?!' question that is so often tossed my way, I'll be happy to venture forth and try the more gastronomically adventurous ones in the city.

Everyone visiting Philly has to have a Philly Cheesesteak and I did not pass up the opportunity. What better place than Pat's, the creators of the original cheesesteak. 

After researching the correct terminology to properly order, I got a "wit w/ whiz" (aka Grilled steak with onions, and Cheez Whiz). Also make note this place is CASH ONLY and you order cheesesteaks at the first window, then fries and drinks at the second window. Don't mess up the flow or I hear they will bump you to the back of the line.

Overall the flavor of the sandwich was very good. The hoagie roll was incredible; one of the best I have ever had. They chopped and almost diced the meat up which made for easier eating. I just wish there was more of the meat as pieces of it were far and few between in some bites. The grilled onions were heartily chunked and cooked perfectly, and just the right amount of Cheez Whiz.

Honestly at the end of the day, this place is a bit of a tourist trap as the locals I spoke with said there are far better places for a legit Cheesesteak in Philly, but for a tourist like me, it was a fun experience to at least do once!
It's Pats.  It's the original cheesesteak.  What else do you want?  You want a cannoli, go somewhere else.

Any trip to Philadelphia would not be complete without at least eating one cheesesteak sandwich so on this occasion had a few hours before my flight I decided why not try both at once. 

I went with the cheese steak with onions, mushrooms and provolone cheese and have to say that Pats compared to Gino's had the upper hand on multiple levels as well as it seemed like it was a crowd favorite as the line that I had to wait in for Gino's was not as long is the line for Pats.

Overall I think it is a good experience, but not necessarily worth five stars I think it's really merely a tourist adventure or way for people to feel as if it's the same place they can come back to you and know what you're going to get each time. 

The biggest thing that stands out to me is the steak quality and taste. It's good to see the steak being cooked right in front of you and then moments after that it being placed in the hoagie. The onions are cooked properly with the mushrooms and not just thrown in the mix. All this with some provolone and it is with the 10 bucks!

My only real complaint about the cheesesteak was the bread I felt as if the bread was a little bit lacking, but the other items overshadowed it at the end of the day.

king of cheese steaks.. I don't think so.. #1 attitude of the order taker is typical Philly rude and maybe I didn't order right..(and i'm from Philly) I ordered 4 wiz steaks w/ onions and mushrooms on the sidewalk with snow blazing around me and asked to order fries.. and told to move to another window 3 feet your the left.. the steak had no taste and fat content was at a max.. should have gone to Geno's across the street... or better yet BIG JIM'S on south street... the parking is just as bad but the Steaks are so much better...

I got mango habanero wings, the sauce was delicious I wish it was on something else... 
The  chicken itself was tough, dry and looked weird? Mostly likely because it wasn't breaded, which I didn't expect. It was just white chicken with sauce on top, it want even browned... 
Also the wings were tiny.

This is just a mediocre tourist trap. Definitely not worth $12. Bread is chewy. The meat tasted like reheated boiled steak. I gave the second star because of how they slathered the cheez whiz. Go to Sonny's if you're able to. More inviting atmosphere, more customizable sandwich, more variety in the menu.

The drive thru team on 6/29/21 12pm are KILLING it. I ordered and received my HOT food in literally 60 seconds. I've never been served so fast anywhere. I live in Chester, but will always keep this location in mind when I'm anywhere in the Philly area. Thank you guys, you made my day.

Had a group of friends visiting California and had to show them the Pat's vs Geno's rivalry. We got lucky and got parking right next to the restaurant. Got a cheesesteak with provolone (usually get cheez whiz). The meat was a bit dry and needed some more salt and pepper. Overall, not the best cheesesteak I've ever had but have to go once for the history behind it.

This is a solid enough spot in Old City to stop if you are doing the tourist thing especially on the weekends when they are rarely busy.

The store itself was neat and clean with the exception of the men's room which looks like they've contracted with SEPTA to keep it clean. (i.e. it's freakin' filthy and the toilet seat/bowl is falling apart.)

Both employees were friendly and on their game and the sandwiches were done perfectly.  Worth noting is that they currently have a manager's special that on weekends and after I think 5 or 6 during the week they'll give you two regular footlongs for $8.99.

Now that's good and cheap eats.

PAT'S vs GENO's

My grandma lives a couple blocks from Pat's, so I've been going here every so often for most of my life. I would have to say that nothing has changed at this famous, classic eatery. The place has always been CASH ONLY and open 24/7, 365 days a year. Lines would wrap around the block, even in the cold. People have come from far and near for a Philly cheesesteak. 

I have always preferred Pat's for cheesesteaks, since it has more flavor and is less dry. My favorite has always been the mushroom cheesesteak wit whiz. If you're not gonna get whiz cheese on your hoagie, then what are you even doing?

If you're in Philadelphia for the first time, I definitely recommending stopping by the famous sandwich in its birth place. I bet you won't be able to eat a cheesesteak in another other state.

Super meh. I flew from Minnesota to Philly for one day just to eat cheesesteaks. (Great deal on airfare). I went to Pat's, Geno's and Tony Luke's. I thought a yard of cheesesteaks in 10 hours was probably enough. At Pat's I got a mushroom pepper cheesesteak wit with provolone. The mushrooms were canned and the peppers with pretty uneventful. The ribeye was tender but bland as hell. Yeah I'm from the Midwest, but I actually like flavor. The bread was chewy and held the sandwich together well. That was really a highlight of the sandwich. Service fast and friendly enough. When I go back to Philly, I don't need to rush back here. Pat, I'm sure you used to have a great product, but those days must be in the past.
If you don't care about what you serve to paying customers, you shouldn't be in the food business. Plenty of other choices on the avenue.
Not sure what's going on with this franchise. Drive-thru lines take forever. Lately they're closing an hour and a half early. Seem to be having a very hard time during the pandemic.

This was my go to restaurant for years, until now. The customer service has continually declined  (Even pre pandemic). My friend and I went around 8:20 on a Friday evening. They were pretty busy but most tables were finishing up. The hostess (white women with blonde hair) was busy and when she finally came over, she said "we are done seating for the evening". I don't know any new requirements due to Covid, but I was confused because I was there a few weeks ago and we were seated around 9ish. Since we were there and hungry we decided to order take out, online. While waiting for our food, two white women walked up and asked for a table. She said sure, give me a minute. The hostess walks over to the 5/6 tables that are now empty and starts to clean it off for these two women. My friend says out loud to her "I thought you weren't seating anyone else tonight". She didn't look up and finished cleaning the table. She for sure heard him because she walked over and apologized to the women, stating they were done seating for the night. 

Maybe she was busy when my friend who is a person of color asked for a table and she said they were done seating. Maybe she was flustered because she is working in a restaurant during a pandemic. Maybe when she realized 5 tables were now open, she had room to seat these two women who happened to be white. After going back and forth, trying to give her the benefit of the doubt, my friend still felt extremely uncomfortable and hurt.  Maybe it had nothing to do with his color, but it sure felt like it. 

Both employees we communicated with were very disrespectful. We went to the pick up window and asked for our food and he came back to tell us "they made your order for here, I asked them to pack it up". At this point it was 8:45 and half the seats were open. We felt uncomfortable and honestly didn't want to support the restaurant any more, but we already paid for it. 

I will no longer come back to this restaurant or recommend it.

Food here is diarrhea. You feel like eating diarrhea and you will go home have diarrhea. Hygiene at this store is absolutely terrible. There was also needle I the bathroom. I am traumatized by this taco bell. This store should be closed and the franchise owner should never be allowed to open any food business. Absolutely shameful. Pro tip make sure you have access to a bathroom after eating here cuz you need it.

I don't know how you feel but I don't care just want to share my opinion THIS PLACE SUCKS steak taste plain no vegetables no cheese I guess the management change since last time I went but never the last there better more reasonable places then this NON king of steaks

When in Philly ...

It was time I went and found out what all the hype was about, so I made it a point to also try Geno's, which I did before I hit Pat's, only because I was feeling lazy and hungry and my car was parked slightly closer to Geno's. 

I left my experience from each place giving a narrow edge to Pat's. It seemed the steak was a tad more seasoned here, or perhaps it was the fact that this place seemed slightly grimier than Geno's and whatever lack of deep cleaning gives a little more character to their cheesesteaks. In fairness, however, I ordered provolone versus whiz at both places, which I'm sure is a violation of the rules according to most cheesesteak experts. 

I hate that they're cash only in 2016, but I see they have no problem getting away with it.
They sent 12 pieces of old chicken. Its not that hard to get fast food right. HORRIBLE WASTE OF MONEY.

Three words: Jasmine. Brandon. Sean.

The staff is truly what makes Blaze litty titty!  do a MAKE YOUR OWN for $9.45 with unlimited toppings. And they will werrrk their magic. Tonight I did: a mix of spicy and reg red sauce.Mozzarella, feta, and Parmesan cheeses. Artichokes. Mushrooms. Roasted garlic [if your on a date, this should be a group decision]. Green peppers. Basil & spinach go last! Too it with oregano and some sea salt [when your blood pressure be in that low low]
Check it out...
I got s Big Mac that I haven't got in literally years/ the roll was stale and completely fell apart

I enjoyed the story here. Little sushi shop that hadd to shut down for a while, came back as a fried chicken shop. Enjoyed their chicken wrap and chicken rice bowl. Restaurant was clean and organized. Would I go back?? Perhaps. I think adding chicken salads or wings would be good. They say fried chicken is next!

Whether your drunk or sober, a cheesesteak from Pat's "King of Steaks" is not a good idea. The corner of 9th and Passyunk is the cheesesteak mecca. Tourists travel near and far to get a sample of an authentic Philly cheesesteak. Expect to see people with cameras and fanny packs. Spoiler alert: locals DON'T eat Pat's or Geno's....well unless they're in the neighborhood and have the drunk hunger pangs, but I'll digress.

My brother came to see me from out of state and said that a friend of his said "you gotta try Pat's", so I begrudgingly did even though it was my first time here too. Looking at the prices, I thought it was incredibly overpriced for what you're getting. You better follow their order guidelines to tee or expect some serious man sass. A woman in front of us asked if she can get the cheesesteak cut in half. He raised his voice and was still working robotically "no, we will not cut in half" she asked again and this went on for a good 30 seconds. I was surprised to see him raise his voice at a woman that looked like he could be his grandmother. It was awful!

The cheeseteak: Nope. Nope. Nope. Bland, unappetizing. Even fake cheese (wiz) couldn't even save this sorry excuse for a sandwich. You're probably thinking "well why don't you put some ketchup or mustard on this?" My response: Get outta town! That's not authentic cheesesteakness! The mildly redeeming part of the meal were the fries, which would be pretty tough to screw up.

I didn't particularly like the homeless people basically playing the role of busser and hoping that they would get some type of donation from a patron. I like to eat in peace, thank you very much. So this place is a no go for me, now and forever more.

So its probably been about 5 years and I was craving for a juicy cheese steak.  So I opted for Pats famous Steaks in Philly.  As I arrive in had to drive around a couple of times to find a parking spot but I did shortly after.  Walking up I see the line is about 20 deep but don't worry this is normal and it goes fast.  Within minutes in order " wiz, wit"  which means a steak with wiz cheese and wit which means cooked onions. So cheese steak with wiz cheese and onion.  3 seconds later its in front of you.  Walk 10 paces to left and order your drink and fries of you wish.  Remember PATS is CASH only.  I was then lucky to find a seat and then I dug in to soft bread, dripping wiz and large amounts of steak.  Yummy.  After about 30 napkins the steak was done and all I needed was a recliner and remote lol.  My steak was $12 and well worth it.  Keep up the great job Pats I will return.  Dont let picture fool you the steak was 12-14 inches long.

Extremely poor quality for a chain that relies on consistency and quality of product - absolutely correct. I love the chips, and these tasted and looked so radically different, just like store bought chips. No taste, no salt, no lime. I asked for a refund as I was not going to eat them and they gave me attitude.

Do NOT come here.

Is it the greatest cheesesteak in the world? could be. What it does, is give you a nice cheesesteak with really good service out great place to sit back in Philly and absorb the feeling of being in a good working class philly neighborhood. I would definitely recommend coming out and enjoying a cheesesteak..

This is our favorite place for pretzels in Philly. They're always hot and delicious and ridiculously reasonably priced. I can't recommend them highly enough.

BTW the payment info in Yelp as of this writing is incorrect. Tasty Twisters DOES accept debit cards but there's a $10 minimum purchase.

We stopped here on the way back from Boston to Washington DC to enjoy an authentic Philadelphia cheesesteak.  My wife discovered Pat's after some Google research of some of the best places to eat.  We tried Geno's and Pat's the same evening and all seemed to enjoy Geno's more.  We ordered cheesesteak, wit, wiz....aka a cheesesteak with onion and Cheese Whiz which we understand to be the definition of a cheesesteak.  We also ordered regular and cheesefries.  

Despite enjoying Geno's more, none of the five of us were impressed with  Philadelphia cheesesteaks.  They lacked flavor.  It was like eating unmarinated meat, onion, and bread covered in cheese.  I've had better cheesesteaks at other places around the country so it was a bit disappointing this was the standard that everyone references for cheesesteaks.  My son said if we ever return to Philadelphia, that he doesn't want a cheesesteak...and I think the rest of the family agrees.

Parking was problematic as there is nothing besides street parking and it was chaotic when we arrived.  There was a guy trying to make a few bucks who was directing traffic and said he would watch our car.  We returned and he was nowhere to be found but we sat nearby to watch the car as we didn't park in a proper spot.  A cop passed talking on his cell phone and didn't blink an eye so we figured we were alright.  

Pat's seemed to be about the speed.  Cheesesteaks were ready within seconds of ordering.  The cashier had attitude which I didn't appreciate and even my kids commented afterwards but I guess the attitude is normal for Pat's from what we've read.  I ordered two cheesesteaks, he gave me one, so then I asked about the second as another rep put one out, and he counted them for me...1...2.  I decided not to rip his head off and moved to the next window to order fries and drinks, also paid separately.  I made the mistake of asking the guy if he had a drink carrier, he looked at me, and then walked away.  Lovely people at Pat's.  It was a bit challenging to carry multiple drinks and fries.

In comparison to Geno's across the street, Pat's is a bit primitive and inefficient.  It's something you have to see for yourself.

I ordered food from Night Owls late in the evening. When the food hadn't arrived after an hour, I called their phone number and it went straight to a cell phone voicemail. The food never arrived but my credit card was still charged. I think this might be a scam aimed at Philadelphians desperately looking for late night eats!

Food was fine, this is a solid place for late night food. I was really happy they were willing to deliver to me and felt the fees were absolutely in-line with the distances the drivers have to travel. My main reasoning for less than 5 stars was that I was left with a sore throat after eating a cheesesteak with SPK. Not sure what irritated my throat but I noticed after two bites a sharp pain in my throat that has only gotten worse since. I am guessing maybe the pepper? I know the management/store monitors reviews so this will most likely be updated once I hear from them. The portions were great and the food has been great in the past. Just can't give a higher review if it hurts and I can't finish my meal!

The Mecca of Philly cheesesteaks!!! This is where the story of creating a Philly cheesesteak started!! These cheesesteaks are some of the best I've ever had!! I like my Cheesesteak with onions and cheese whiz! The provolone is a popular pick too! The fries are better at Pats than Geno's! There are two lines; one for ordering a cheesesteak and the other for ordering drinks or french fries. This is one of my favorite things to hit in Philly everytime I am there!!

Three stars for some pretty freaking bomb cheese fries other then that..... MEH

Long line after a T Swift concert naturally. 

Was Impressed by the cool sign and history behind the place 

Two stars for a subpar cheesesteak which I broke my vegetarianism for because yolo (and I heard good things.) Not worth it. Flavorless and stingy on the cheese. 

Appreciated the whole numbers for pricing because of the CASH ONLY factor. 

And I must say I like the street side ambiance for sheer touristy attraction vibes.

All in all I might love this place after like 8 beers as a drunk Taco Bell binge substitute.

Worst service ever!!! Went through the drive through, the lady taking my order wasn't polite, kept saying anything else after I spoke, when I pull up to the window she handed me the wrong drinks, didn't even look at me, then handed me the wrong food, and got an attitude cause SHE MESSED UP.. I asked her for extra sauces didn't even answer back, then I pull off and she didn't put straws in my bag for the drinks.. if you hate your job get a new one!!! No manners what so ever and rude..

Alright so this was a must for me before we left! I wanted to go to south Philly for the best cheesesteak! 

We stopped in at Pat's King Of Steaks!
So first off it is a cash only location, which is ok with me. I ordered the cheesesteak with Whiz, and I will tell you this! It was amazing! 

While sitting there this man comes up while sweeping and asks us if this is our first time there, then starts to tell us the history of the place. Come to find out this man was Frank the owner, and his daughter was also sitting there. He explained that his father and uncle started the business. 

Got to see all of the photos and signatures of all the famous people that have been there. I even got to take a photo with Frank. This was a great moment, always nice to meet the owner of an establishment that has been around since before my time

Side note his daughter also thanked me for visiting even though I was a Yankees fan lol gotta love it! Also she took the photo

Pros: Lots of meat! 
Cons: Didn't meet my expectations of a really Philly cheese steak. 

I live in Jersey so my prime purpose to visit Philly was to get a delicious Philly cheese steak. This sandwich was good but I felt like I could've gone anywhere in Jersey and gotten a same or even better tasting cheesesteak.

Should be 0 stars.  The absolute worst McDonalds I have ever frequented.  Employees are not hospitable.  There is always something wrong with the orders.  I come here mostly for a "quick" happy meal for my kids.  The quick is in quotations because the last meal I got was through there drive thru AND it took over 20 minutes!! Is that fast food?  The line just doesn't move!  SAVE YOURSELF THE AGGRAVATION AND PROBLEMS BY DRIVING AN EXTRA 8 MINUTES TO THE MCDONALDS UP RIDGE.  I promise it will be faster and better service and better order accuracy and quality.  I try to avoid this location with every fiber in my being.

I get this is for fast food cheesesteaks, locals love it, seems to always be a line regardless of which time I go, I think I prefer Geno's though, I went for a late night visit mid August and the meat was just way too salty, same with the fries.

Maybe I'm just getting older who knows.

This "King of Steaks" is a Philly institution, albeit famous more due to history and incumbency, rather than genuine food quality.

You'll request and pay for your cheesesteak from a grumpy staff member managing the order window. They only take cash, so make sure you have some. A traditional order would be a cheesesteak "wit" onions and with cheese whiz. Once you pay, they'll whip it up for you and have it out in less than a minute.

The sandwiches themselves are so-so. The meat is a bit dry, the cheese is pretty weak, the bread is quite bland, and the overall flavor experience is lackluster. Compared to Geno's across the street, Pat's has shredded beef (vs. sliced) and much less cheese flavor impact, but the sandwiches here are less messy and easier to eat.

Pay a visit if you want to try a Philly classic. But one visit will probably be enough - if you want a good cheesesteak normally, there are better places to look.

Ordered through uber eats and I'm just trying to figure out is it me or can the employees not read ? None of my order was correct how can one mistake macaroni with fries ?? No sauces nothing  was correct smh watered down drinks DONT ORDER FROM HERE !! Ever

Pat's is well worth the hype.
So much that in fact we went twice in one week, driving completly out of the way back from NY to Ohio adding an hour of driving time just to eat another cheesesteak.
Ok 5, since we were pissed that we just got one to share the first time.
We wern't hungry and got one at Genos and one at Pats just to compare, but as soon as we bit into a bite of Pats we were all over it, talking about it the whole week and finally gave in, drove back and got 5 more with wiz, peppers, mushrooms and onions and some of the awesome green and red peppers they have at the cart out front which rounded it off perfectly.
Lines are a mine long but the guys are quick, yes $9 per sandwich is steep but it will stay on your mind forever.
About once a year I get a craving for meat but if I lived closer to pat's I'd eat it daily.
Usually there is no way I touch beef or god forbid cheese wiz, but this is so f*cking good there is just no way around it.
No words can discribe just how good this is, just thinking about it makes me want some again right now.
Nothing can compare, if you are anywhere in a 1000 mile radius, do yourself the favor and go to Pats!

I'm not one who travels all of Philly, looking for the best cheesesteak. I'll be honest- I haven't even tried Geno's. I was born into a Pat's family so that's where I go and I have no complaints!

My mom and I go to Philly every couple months for an appointment of mine and it is always a tradition to sit down to cheesesteaks and cheese fries after. My mom taught me that a Hi-C goes best with this combo and I've come to learn that it is delicious!

We always get cheesesteaks wiz wit! I'm personally not the type of person to get anything besides cheese wiz because it ends up being too dry for me. The onions and mushrooms top it off! Their fries are always so warm and delicious and there is cheese throughout! I love that there is cheese on the bottom and that you don't run out of cheese and have dry fries!! 

I've only been here about 20 times in my life but every single time I'm in damn heaven! It is my favorite treat ever when we travel to Philly to get cheesesteak and fries! 

I cannot wait to be back and cannot express my love for this messy delicious sandwich!

It's legendary and you have to go to say you were in philly, however don't expect much more. The food was ok at best, seating is limited, the experience was rushed, but it is what it is so enjoy it for the philly experience once

King of cheesesteaks.

I have had many cheesesteaks in my day. Many. This has a flavor, a texture, and an old school experience you can't get in most places anymore. The sandwich was nice, tight and complete, the cheese came together with the texture of the steak. I drizzled a little hot pepper juice on top. It's worth it. People making their comments have had things LIKE cheesesteaks and forming opinions based on what is only similar, this however is the OG, what a cheesesteak sandwich is supposed to be like.

The battle is over in my book. 

Will return to Pat's, easy pick for an amazing sandwich.
My bread was so stale it broke n flaked off as I picked my sandwich up. I couldn't even eat my sandwich because the bread was so bad

Is Burger King is truly the pits the drive-thru is horrible there's a line all the way back up Fort Wayne Avenue towards Chelten Avenue this is pitiful who do they have running this store is as if no one is attending the drive-thru lyrics to come through and take charge and do the job that they paid to do not to mention getting the orders right this is the fourth time I've come through there and nothing but chaotic situation at night someone really needs to fix this this type of thing will bring that business to its knees and is not correct it all points to the people that's being III to run this place no care attitude disrespectful Behavior doing god-knows-what in that store it's just horrible somebody needs to say something or do something in order to keep this business alive because I'm not going to return there until I see an Improvement or hear of one

Used to go here often because it was in walking distance.   Drinks always good , wait long but food just ok.   Well met friends for brunch here this afternoon and it was terrible both the food and the service and the attitude of the waiter.    There were four adults and 2 children.    We were served chips and salsa relatively quickly .   Nathaniel came to our table to take our order.   We had 2 burritos, one requested with pinto instead of black beans and no rice.   One huevos rancheros and one chicken nachos.   Not too terrible for the waiter.   He even read back the order to insure accuracy.    Food came to the table before the drinks arrived, rather strange but ok.   The nachos had no chicken on them they took them back to the kitchen and added chicken on top to already now cold nachos.   The burrito came out packed with rice and black beans.    We waited for the waiter to come back to the table but he never came to send back.   We had to call him over and he made a face as if we were annoying him.   I'm really sorry the kitchen was unable to follow the direction.   He said "I even told them no rice and add pinto beans" ok well it isn't right.  Then he said "what do you want me to do" .... Umm try to correct it .  There was no rush on behalf of Nathaniel to correct this rather leisurely the entire table was done eating when the burrito came out which was untimely.   
      The waiter made not one attempt at an apology, he made not one attempt to stop back to our table to clear a dish or ask if we wanted refills on drinks.   We were planning to have another round of margaritas but he seemed annoyed that we were even patrons at this point.   
      We watched as he waited all the tables around ours refilling drinks and clearing tables.   He never made eye contact not once.  We had to ask for the check after a long 15 minutes of him not even making eye contact with our table.    
        We were not expecting 5 star service but at least make an effort.   Times are tough and restaurants have been through some hell in the past year .   All the more reason to appreciate your job and the patrons.    I was not unreasonable and we were not bitchy we eat in the city all the time.    This was one familiar place we kept going back to or even the sister restaurant in no. Libs.   Definitely on our skip list now along with our friends. 
       We did tell Nathaniel that shame on him for being that way.  We were by no means blaming the kitchen blunders on him but his ignorance and lack of concern cost the restaurant business and a bad review.    All in all 133.00 for food and drink, would have been more but waiter didn't think it was necessary to wait on customers.    So Nate if you read this understand we never blamed you but a blameless apology works really well in these situations.   Your body language was volumes louder than your voice.

Steaks were great.  

I had been to Geno's twice and never to pats. So this time it had to be Pat's.  

It was a long line, but a very quick one.  Got near the front of the line and I only started reading the 'how to order' sign which had hilarious comments and it was already my turn.  The order went smoothly and I was off to the fries and drinlks window.  The steak meat looked great where you could see them frying it up through the window as I passed. After I got all the food, I was glad my girlfriend was there to help me cause it was a lot of stuff to evacuate.  

We thought we'd have to leave with the food and eat it in the car because all the seats were occupied on the way in.  Fortunately one opened up as we headed for the car.  

First let me say the fries were excellent.  Kind of a crispy flavored fry.  Definitely a nice surprise.  After we sat down a guy who cleans the tables came around and offered us some napkins.  He was quite a character and engaged many of the patrons in conversation.  I think he is a great ambassador for the place, really liked his demeanor.  The steaks were great we had ours 'wiz wit'.  Good stuff, nice rolls.  There was a little bit of gristle in the meat we didn't care for, but you'll have that with real meat.

The place was clean and nice looking.  The staff were courteous, industrious and efficient. I would definitely go back.

As for Geno's I think it is just as good.  There is something to be said about going to the source and ';rockin it from the cradle', but there are great steak shops all over Philly and in the surrounding areas as well.  

Gotta do it if you're there, but some local shops are just as good.

Enjoy!
Im sorry i hadnt read these reviews. Terrible x2. Aweful! Messed the order up more than i could have ever imagined. No quality control at this location.
I pull up...Order breakfast burrito and apple juice. "We don't have burritos or apple juice". I swear these McDonalds in the city are messed up like 80% of the time.

Wow... All I can say is wow. Stopped in with my friends for a quick lunch on the go; my friend orders a chicken sandwich and it had MOLD on it!!! A huge piece of mold which they claimed was burnt butter--What do y'all think? Does this look like butter to you?

This is my now second experience with Night Owls. The first time was delivery to a bar and the second time was tonight with pick up. 

First time delivery around 12:30am: We ordered pizza rolls and chicken tenders and fries. Food came in about 20 mins via Grubhub and was hot and tasty. The only bummer was the pizza rolls could have been fried a tad bit longer as the cheese wasn't totally meted and it wasn't all that hot but I must say I prefer that to over cooked and dry. They were still good... nice and soft how we like. 

Second time pick up 3am: When we arrived it was definitely set up for delivery and we were unsure if we could even walk in... you can! And there are a few seats by a window but it's very tight. We immediately felt in the way the best way to describe it at 3am was like a NASCAR pit. Tons of delivery orders and a definitely controlled chaos. Even sitting in the window area we felt very underfoot. There are no menus you must order online so it's best to order ahead and pick up and get out of their way!!! We ordered the chicken fingers and fries again, Buffalo wings and a cheesesteak. Despite ordering thru an app and having to write my extras in a comment section (extra cheese) they did not miss it like most places it was right on my steak! I like the way the food comes in eco friendly packaging and it kept the food super hot all the way home (I just bit into my steak and even an hour later and it's still hot on the bottom of the box and nice and warm and the cheese is still pulling)  Now.... they made me break my diet trying the steak and fries it was worth every single bite but the wings (which I can have on a Keto diet) were OUTSTANDING I hope they can live up to them again cause I will definitely try them again. The wings sauce (mild) was a good quality tasty sauce, they had a nice crunch but also kinda fell off the bone some. I usually only order flats no drums but since it was online I just took them how they come.... I hate drums but theirs were so good! I tried to select blue cheese but it wouldn't let me add it on but guess what?! Didn't need it they were perfect. The fries were hot and had a crisp but also a softness (I love that ratio). As for the tenders I'm sure they were as yummy as the first go round as I didn't try them I had enough to eat!!!  this is so happily a late night place I will call on again and again! A must try! 3's the charm so I'm really hoping it's not a fluke and this place stays on point!!!
The cheesesteak was very chewy. Very fatty. The bread and everything was good, but Probably won't be back.

I say depending on your preference on how you like your cheesesteaks will determine whether you like Pat's or Geno's better. I ate pats first then genos back to back to judge for myself. All i can say is........ I'm team Pat's alllllllll the way!!!! My first reaction taking a bite of Pat's was a mini orgasm in my mouth hahah. The bread is soft but still maintains structue to absorb the oils and cheese mixture from the onions, cheese whiz, and steak. It can get messy, but there is so much flavorr. Pat's has the perfect mix of oil to cheese to onions on the shredded steak. It's a party in your mouth. Ugh my mouth is watering just thinking of it. If you like flavor and oils, go to Pat's. I took off one star because compared to Geno's the establishment wasn't as clean as Geno's. But I say the shadier the establishment looks, the better the food!!!!!

This place is disgusting. I'm surprised the board of health hasn't shut it down. Nothing seems sanitary, I walk inside and immediately want to walk out. I used to stop in when I was desperate for something quick and easy but no more. Food quality is pitiful. Employees are rude. Don't waste your time or money.

Very slow service

Bathroom is disgusting, filthy at 10 am

Big parking lot

Food was prepared properly

Totally overrated. Ok at best and I have had better cheese steaks.

I wanted to go here mainly for the experience but that was probably the "best" part. The cheese steak was alright. There was some weird ass ordering system and the signs were kind of amusing. But I guess the whole "Hey we're a bunch of grumpy ass dudes making cheese steaks" schtick isn't really that funny in real life.
perfect quick lunch. great, fast service. loved the white top pizza sans bacon. filling and satisfying.

I ordered the big buffalo sandwich just the sandwich, it's Sunday night, there's nobody but me in the drive through. I was given the wrong sandwich, and it didn't even have Everything it was supposed to have on it in the first place. Just sauce nothing else. I've been here before and have no complaints, good food. Just get your shit together. Your staff don't give two shits. Pay them more or something, figure it out.

Big line to start the morning, but they were churning out the orders quickly. Same quality that you would expect from any chick-fil-a. The chicken biscuit was smaller than I'm used to, but it may have just been the odd one out.

We wanted to try famous Philly cheese steak while in town so we picked this one based on the popularity. We decided to get one from Pat's and one from Geno across the street to compare. Prices were same at both places.

Verdict: Pat's won over Geno's based on taste and customer service 

Although the line was long, it moved quickly. Once you place your order, you get your sandwich within minutes. You don't even need to ask them to slice the sandwich in half...they do it automatically (unlike Geno's). The employees were friendly and didn't give you an attitude (unlike Geno's). We had the mushroom Philly cheese steak with provolone cheese. But surprisingly the cherry peppers were so good and made this place the winner in our books.

So I enjoyed Pat's for the experience more than anything else. I liked how the restaurant was later out and being able to see the chefs prepare the sandwiches. The pepper steak sandwich was pretty good. I will say the fries are much better than the fries from the place across the street. Good eats.

You somehow manage to ruin my already low expectation experience every time.  Simple orders are made correctly about 20% of the time (not exaggerating). Food is cold and stale 90% of the time (not exaggerating).  Service is not friendly 95% of the time.  Your location (Andorra) has compelled me to write the only two yelp ratings i've Ever completed. You must have rampant drug use, and no competent management.  There is literally no other reason I can think of for why you SUCK so badly.  Pull yourselves together, or SHUT down and let someone else who actually gives a f*** reopen.

I'm not really sure what goes down at night, but you're out of luck if you are looking to receive an order. I've had good experiences during the day, but nighttime is a completely different story. We saw a couple people either hanging out or complaining at the drive-thru window. When we drove away from the restaurant we saw employees through the window just chilling out in the lobby.

worst mcdonalds ever ! i came in on monday july 16, 2018 the manager was disgusting she had the worst attitude she was cussing infront of the customers and was giving us the worst attitude im calling corporate she needs to be fired not manager material at all !!

Not the best cheesesteak in the land. I was thinking of if your in philly you have to try one correct? Perhaps, but the hot and readiness of the food to accommodate the masses also lowers the quality. The ingredients arent as fresh as they could be and the bread wasnt that great either.

The prices were crazy. Im a out of towner so when i saw the prices I was thinking geeze lousie. A cheese steak and an order of fries totaled 20 bucks? At home we could go out and get a nice plate... maybe even a real steak and a potato for that much. But hey who am I and what do i know? Oh yea only cash as well.

In philly and your visiting.... save a little money find something more high quality and that takes longer than 3 minutes to make!

This is the worst chick fil a location that I have ever been to. They  were very rude and nasty and I never heard the 'my pleasure' response. To add insult to injury, when I boarded my flight I realized that they got my order wrong!!! They really need to do better and train their staff on customer service!

I rated 5 stars back in 2016 when I first started visiting Philadelphia. I won't have a cheesesteak anywhere else but in Philly. Lately, it's been a hit or a miss. On some trips when I come out it's good, sometimes, not so good. I even brought friends from California and boasted the whole time that Pat's was iconic and the best. After having it for the first time, they weren't thrilled about it and neither was I. I came out in August 2020 and explained at the window that I was taking some back home and needed the cheese separate. They actually did it for me and I put in the freezer and ate it a couple of weeks later. I then came out for New Years' 2021, and the dude at the window wearings a 76ers mask was being a dick and said they don't do that, never have, and never will. So I ended up bringing home some soggy ass cheesesteaks. Anywho... later that night, I drove to Delassandros and I was actually surprised that the price was close to Pat's except they had a ton of meat and cheese on their steaks! All these years being loyal to Pat's only to be treated like shit at the window, telling all of my friends about it, bringing friends to the Inventor of the cheesesteak, I was wrong. I guess I was blinded by the hype of it all. These cheesesteaks are not as good anymore.. people are right, it is a tourist spot..

Seemed like it was the only spot on the Ave that was open tonight (due to the snow).  Picked up some "nachos" (it was 75%beans and 15% chips), enchiladas and tacos (both dry and bland). Service and quality have gone downhill over the years. Very Unfortunate.

Pat's versus Geno's...the dice versus the slice!

We stopped by Pat's first since the overall trusty Yelp rating was so much higher.  The three of us split two: the cheesesteak wit whiz and onions, mushrooms, and peppers and a cheesesteak wit whiz and onions.

The two main differences between the infamous rivalries: 1) Pat's has a more extensive menu, 2) Pat's dices while Geno's slices their meat.

Of the two we ordered here, I liked the cheesesteak wit whiz, onions, mushrooms and peppers.  The peppers added a really nice tangy element to the cheesesteak.

The cheesesteak wit whiz and onions sorely lacked flavor.  I was disappointed...so of course we had to go across the way to Geno's for comparisons sake and ordered the same thing.  Geno's was much more cheesy, juicy and overall flavorful!  Perfectly seasoned!

So, if you love the extras like I do, go to Pat's and order the cheesesteak with all the extras.  If you're a purist, go to Geno's for a flavorful cheesy-meat explosion in a bun.

This is my second time trying their food. I reaffirm my opinion that it's just okay. The meat is a bit on the greasy side. And $9.50 for one cheese is not exactly cheap. There are many other places in Philadelphia I found to serve the same food, only tastier. I think this is just an example of good marketing; a combination of food network and rivalry resulting in a tourist attraction. Cash only.

I came here on a recommendation from a few friends, I don't have too much cheesesteak experience so I'm basing my judgment on everything all around. Putting away the only negative of cash only, I ordered a Pizza Steak, having the sandwich coming out immediately after I said my order. This place does not only have fast service, but the steaks with the sauce are much better than any other cheesesteak place that I have gone to.

You want an au-thentic Philly cheesesteak?  Everyone will tell ya Pats or their competitors across the street, Genos.

Both places do sell cheesesteaks, and neither place is close to the best in the city.

Why go to Pats or Genos?  They are worth a miss but the 9th street market is worth a long look if you are a foodie.  

Fantes is a must for serious cooks, cooking equipment fetishists and a look back 30 years to when there were stores specializing in just one category rather then the current pluthera of big box stores with the finest products from China and India on sale 365 days a year.   

Isgro's has some of the best pastry you will find anywhere in the USA.

Anastasi's seafood is a good place if you want to buy good fish and seafood to bring home and carefully make - not much to look at though...

Spice corner will sell ya just a pinch of this or that hard to find spice.

There is a place called DiBruno's.  They have all kinds of meats and cheeses, olives, oils etc.  I am a big guy and one time the guy was getting my order and I was looking.  With fine urban salesmanship the guy who FWIW looked more Irish then Italian to m, said something else catch your eye, my friend?  I said look at me, pal - everything here catches my eye!

If you want to explore the Italian market and say you have been to Pats then go.  If you are reading this, however, you likely know how to use Yelp and will be able to find a better cheesesteak...with no trouble.  Not bad but...

Today I just performed my Pat's vs Geno's assessment.  1st - Pat's is an average cheesesteak.  While in Philly the last few days, I've had a cheesesteak everyday.  And I've had cheesesteaks outside of Philly...so I consider myself an expert.

But comparing Pat's and Geno's, Pat's is more flavorful.  Pat's gives you more meat.  Lastly, I liked Pat's bread better.

However, the next time I'm in Philly, I will not come to Pat's (nor Geno's), as I think you can get better cheesesteaks elsewhere in this great city.

Very unfriendly staff. I feel like i'm pulling their teeth when i order. No "thank you", "have a nice day", "enjoy", or anything of that matter. When i'm waiting in line to order it seems like they are unhappy that you are there. I understand it may not be the most exciting job, but with any customer/client facing role you have to put on a friendly face. Every visit to this location has been poor.


UPDATE: Visited the establishment again and the sandwich they gave me was half wrapped so in the bag everything fell apart. Do not order from this establishment

I think this is such a cool place to visit!  It's just such a part of the Philadelphia vibe, and makes for a nice compliment to the day if attending a Phillies or Eagles game.  I've just tried Geno's and Pat's in Philly, so I'm not the person to ask if there are better cheese steaks in town, but I always enjoy a Pat's steak, much better than Geno's in my opinion.

Promised my little girl I'd bring her a real Philly steak, then I ended up side tripping to Jersey for a couple of days and ate it. So I find myself staring down a non-stop drive to Ft Lauderdale sans the promised grease bomb. Did some yelping as I head south above Lo! Pats really is the , open 24 hrs and 15 min (late night) hop off 95. I got 3, she received hers and I remain Big Daddy.

I've lived in the suburbs of Philly for over a decade and it's now, when I came back to visit family that I was willing to try the hyped up Cheesesteak from Pat's.

The BF and I were driving around downtown reminiscing about memories and decided to take the 13 minute drive and get a cheesesteak from Pat's.  Don't ask me how we snagged a parking spot two feet from Pat's, we totally did.  

Ordering is simple, for me, pepper cheesesteak wit with provolone (I'm not a cheese wiz girl).  Food was ready before we finished paying.  Separate window for drinks and fries.  

We grabbed one of the many tables surrounding Pat's and started eating.  I loved the peppers, onions, and provolone with mine, it was a wonderful combination and the peppers gave a sweet note with every bite.  It was a little greasy, but what cheesesteak isn't?  We both devoured our cheesesteaks and enjoyed every morsel.  The bowling ball that hits the bottom of your stomach afterwards is a completely different review.  It tastes so wonderful going down that you're willing to put up with the discomfort afterwards.  

I was pleasantly surprised by the tastiness of the cheesesteak at Pat's.  I can't say it's the best I've ever had but it's certainly a winner.

*Cash only to all those newbies.

Customer service is very poor. Wendy's does not close until 3am and I got there at two. I went to go place my order and nobody greeted me or told me to wait a couple seconds. I waited a total of 10 minutes before a worker said something to me. They told me they were only taking cash and at that point I drove away because of how upset I was. Mind you I was also upset because I was not greeted at all. This is the Wendy's I usually go to, but after tonight I will not be coming back. The workers are very rude.

Worst experience , slow service and cold fries!!!!!! I use to go to Wendy's because of their great fries and great service. This is an added and much needed business to our community. Come on Wendy's management team get over to Wayne and Chelten and work with your staff. Until then I am promoting Burger King fries!!!!!!

I wish the customer service was as good as the chicken. Sept 11, 2020 at 8:03pm, I'm going through the drive-thru at 2550 Grant Ave; store #11202. After completing my order, I asked for the total of my order. I didn't know that it was such a problem. I've visited this particular establishment before and there never was a problem. When I drove around to the window, I hear the employees talking loudly about how I asked for my total when I placed my order. One employee went as far as saying, how he doesn't play with these damn customers. How rude is that? I explained to the female who I gave my card to that I normally get the total when I place my order so that when I get to the drive thru window, I have money or card in my hand. After I'm given my order, I have my husband check the bag for accuracy, the employees me that everything is there and I should pull forward. She states if anything is wrong that I should then come into the store. My husband didn't thoroughly check the order because when I got home, my order was wrong. I truly believe that knowing the parts of the chicken is not a requirement to work at Popeyes chicken! I really enjoy Popeyes Chicken but their employees really needs to be trained by Chick Fil A employees. At least raise the bar. Popeyes hire duds!
Delicious food and strong margaritas! Their outdoor seating it also cute and will keep you cool on even the hottest days. I highly recommend their burritos and will be back many more times.

Lackluster food, the price is on par but definitely not good, the potato salad had too much celery seed & black pepper...the seafood salad was dry...the Mac & cheese lacked everything, there was way too much seasoning in it and it had a sweet after taste.  My salmon cakes still had the spine bone in it so it wasn't an effortless eating as I had to watch out for those bones...But the baked salmon & rice was good and so was the candied butternut squash, the recipes definitely need some revamping

Y'all need to shit this McD down and never open it again. Service is terrrrible. I asked for a large sweet tea I might as well asked for a small because she didn't even fill it up.  The only reason I'm giving it one star is because the girl was pleasant and I asked for fresh fries and they gave it to me. I shouldn't have to ask for fresh fries but whatever. Shut it down and don't reopen it. The number doesn't work so you can't even make a complaint.

Loved my Poké bowl from Philly Poké this past weekend!

I got a delicious & fresh mix of brown rice, tuna, cucumbers, scallions, edamame, seaweed salad, fried shallots, and the sesame miso sauce. Everything was so good! 

We also got some Spam Musubi -- I only really wanted 1 but when we asked, we ended up with the pre-packaged tray that had 2 regular and 1 with egg. Not complaining - it was delicious.

Never again they take too long for bull crap food. No branding on take out containers. Bad food cold food. It's boarder line poppy store, bodegas food. I can tell they are not clean in there also. Uniforms very dirty and untidy workers.

Tables dirty. Staff has attitude. Bean, rice...  not ready when ordering. Zero passion for their job.  I love this chain but this location continues to really under perform!!!! Not just my opinion, see people leaving the store as well on numerous occasions. Get some real management in this store please.

I just ordered something from this place and was charged $30 I received 10 chicken wings and a brownie. They never gave me the Dr Pepper that I ordered. This is way too expensive trust me I'm not really worth it

HORRIBLE. I wish I could give it 0 stars. I ordered a large #9 with no pickles or mustard and a 10 pc nugget. I got home and saw that I got a medium fry, the burgers had mustard and pickles, and there were only 8 nuggets in the box. The only thing they got right was the water. Absolutely ridiculous that they get away with this horrible service and I'm stuck with the wrong order and I paid too much for what I got. Not to mention, they didn't even acknowledge me at either windows. They just stuck their hand out and continued to talk to co-workers with no masks on. I called when I noticed, got laughed at, and hung up on.

We recently started a new overnight security detail at the Linc whenever there is an event. It is hard to find good food after midnight. Last week we ordered burgers and mozzarella sticks and they were outstanding.

Tonight we ordered cheese steaks and wings and the wings came without the sauce. Night Owls went above and beyond and not only brought the sauce but new wings. That speaks volumes about their business and I can assure you we will be ordering from them in the future. The wings were absolutely delicious.

The delivery drivers were both very pleasant and courteous as well.

5 star quality after midnight!!!

Not what I was expecting ... this is the definition of fast food. This is what it feels like cheesesteak is supposed to taste like.

I only tried the classic cheesesteak without anything else. The fries are kinda breaded and go really well with the sandwich.
The food was seasoned good but the oil must have been a little old because my fish was dark and drenched with oil!

Horrible meat, unseasoned and all around dry sandwich.  I am soooo disappointed in the cheesesteaks around town.  I need a real hidden gem the next time I am in Philly.  I hate the fact that you have to stand outside and eat your meal as well.  The benches are never cleaned and condiments juices are everywhere.  I will be trying any other cheesesteak spot in the city next time other than this one..smh.

Did a taste-test with the hubby: Geno's vs Pat's.  Pat's wit (onions), peppers, whiz was hands down the best.  Also tried provolone, but nothing beats the whiz.  Eat. The. Whiz.  Guys working at Pat's were friendlier and funny.  Don't miss this experience!

Honestly a the cheese fries are the only reason I am tempted to round up to 4 stars... but the steak itself really wasn't all that great. At least it's a step above Geno's but that really isn't saying too much either. Just kinda dry meat, not quite enough of it or grease for my taste, and a decent selection of sodas - birch beer is a fav for sure

A wonderful woman that was making food in the kitchen around 9pm on 9/17 was so generous and kind, and promptly fixed our order when there was a minor mistake - also the cashier was so kind and attentive. This Taco Bell has definitely been improving their service with the hiring decisions they've been making lately

Upon landing in Philly, my cousins and I decided that it was wise to hit up some iconic cheesesteak spots for my first meal in the city. In doing my research, Pat's seemed to be the destined place to visit. The spot was nestled in an Italian neighborhood of Philly with parking being a bitch. We literally went around in circles for 20 minutes and finally walked our way to this joint. 

 Pat's was busy. Across from Pat's was another cheesesteak joint known as Geno's that seemed to be equally busy. Obviously, we knew we had to visit Geno's right after to do a comparison of the two. 

 Pat's had some seating al fresco. The menu was pretty simple...cheesesteaks and hot dogs and fish cakes...and cash only.

CHEESESTEAK WITH PROVOLONE ($11.00): This was just ok for me. I liked the steak but the cheese didn't really do anything for me. I thought the flavor of the meat with the onions went well together, but it just needed more sauce and flavor.  

MY FAVORITE DISH. CHEESESTEAK ($11.00): Cheesesteak wit whiz. This was my favorite. I love the steak with whiz. I think that's how the Phillys do it and the only way to do it. The cheese seasons the steak and makes it creamy and luscious. I love it and its the only way to do it. Onions and all and the bread held up to all the meat.  

Overall, I thought Pat's was pretty good. It's a simple menu of cheesesteaks with the type of cheese of your choice. I personally think its advised to order the steaks with whiz. I could eat multiple of these. We didn't bother with the hot dogs or the fish cakes cause our focus was on the cheesesteaks. Be prepared to wait. There is always a line but it goes by pretty quickly.
