Stopped by chipotle for breakfast. Employee was not friendly. Maybe it was too early for her liking. Personally she should not have been at work because she appeared to be sick. She had a runny nose, which is disgusting especially working around food !!! 

I still ordered my food, checked out. As soon as she completed my order she blew her nose by the drink machine with her gloves on ! Just disgusting.

I haven't even ate my food yet and I lost my appetite.  Send her to the back to clean or do something else, but being on the frontline sick around food is so hazardous.

My go-to late night order. The food is fine, nothing spectacular, but their cheesesteaks are good. The best part about this place is their hours. There is not a single other place in Philly that will deliver food to me after a night out, so I always use Night Owls. They also text you coupons and stuff, which is cool.

My wife and I have ordered delivery from this location over a times and they have delivered us a completely wrong meal at least half of the time. It has gotten so bad that we swore never to order again. Multiple times I have driven to the location after my delivery came because it was so ridiculous that a human being could make such a cacophony of errors on a single order. I love chipotle but I warn you: do NOT go to this location.

Longer than usual wait for mobile order .not super horrible .
had a very nice older woman with black hair wait on me ,she was a doll .
food was right ,and they gave me napkins .
only 4 stars cause ,it's McDonald's, hello.

Finally, a build-your-own pizza location on Drexel Campus and University City!

There are many things to like at Blaze Pizza: the thin crust to keep calories low (relatively), the cheese-free option for my lactose sensitivity, the rich selection of various toppings, fast-fried, personal-size, and at a price under $10.

It's a convenient place to grab a quality pizza, though the wait can be long sometimes and the seasoning is slightly too salty to my taste (still better than most pizza places).

What a sad experience this was... the only reason I'm even giving it 2 stars is because all I had is the french fries and a bottle of water, so I can't comment on their cheese steak. The fries were not fresh and they came a tiny cup... but somehow they had the nerve to charge me $7.50 for those two things. I'm sorry, but that is beyond expensive. Not worth the money.

Another well marketed restaurant. Worth going to like a tourist attraction. The bread was a little tough. It was soft, but just hard to rip off. The meat here is better than Geno's across the street. We just got it to go so I can't comment on the atmosphere. But people sit outside. 

Cash only.

I rarely post reviews for fast food chains but experience was horrid that I feel like others should know. 

I ordered two coffees, a latte, and a hot chocolate on the kiosk. I wasn't sure whether they were taking in-person orders but the kiosk is right there as you walk in, so why not?  I'm about to pick up my order and the employee says that there do not have lattes nor hot chocolates.  I ask about mochas, cappuccinos (and other items on the hot McCafe menu) and they simply say that they only have coffees.  Why couldn't they mark this on the touch screen menu?

Okay.  So we ask for a large coffee in lieu of the two non-coffee items but ask what about the $ we already paid for the latte and hot chocolates?  Little did I know this would cause so much distress. They said that they couldn't process refunds for things ordered through the kiosk.  Only when they brought out a manager did they say that I could just pick a replacement item off the menu, which is still really unacceptable given they didn't have any other hot beverages.

What an experience.  I was hoping a non-contact kiosk order was safer and faster but boy was I wrong.

Ordered pick up in doordash got the chicken mole. They forgot the corn tortillas and the mole had no kick to it even after reheating... the chocolate taste and the spice taste wasn't there, worst chicken mole I've ever had. For reference I live in San Diego.. I've had a lot of chicken mole. 

The Brussel sprouts were good and cooked to the correct softness. The white rice was as expected. 

All in all the meal and forgotten tortillas were not worth $18 plus tax.
Staff was awesome! Pizza was fast and perfect! It was very quick and attentive service. Clean restaurant also! I'll be back!
Took forever & the food was extremely salty and the spicy sauce was kinda disappointing that I wasn't able to finish my sandwich. The only good thing I order was the sweet potato fries.
Long line but I did go around dinner time so I expected it, service was great and staff was very friendly!! Food was very tasty!!!
Pizza was Just ok - I've had much better. I wanted a salad but the lettuce looked wilted. So I passed.
They are ignorant when you complain about there food they hangs up on you if you make a complaint criticism on how bad the food is -5 stars

I'm not sure how much I would love this place if I ate there when I was sober (I'd probably love it even more than I do now), but I stumbled over to this place after seeing my friend in a play, then getting some drinks together. I got a "wiz wit" and it was simply phenomenal. He got the pizza fries which were flavorful as well. Pats is a great place, the service may poke fun at you in the wee hours of the morning, don't take it personally. If you play along with them and laugh with them, they will love you forever. And isn't that classic Philadelphian? No culture lost here, and thank God. Prices were a bit high ($8.15 for a half wiz wit) but altogether worth every penny.

Had Pat's like a decade later! Was in town and felt like having that authentic cheesesteak of Philly. They are pretty good sized, but still a bit pricey. I ordered two cheesesteaks and a mushroom cheesesteak and it was $34. I love the way they make the beef and love how melted the cheese is. Overall, a tasty cheesesteak. Things to keep in mind: the restaurant is located in the heart of downtown Philly, so parking is difficult, and the only seating is outdoor seating on bench tables. Be sure to also take cash with you as they do not accept other forms of payment.

Over rated.  Traveled to Philly to get this sandwich that is in a lot of movies and everyone says you need to get when in Philly. The meat has no flavor,  the cheese tastes watered-down. I guess I went for the experience, but I wouldn't do it again.

During our visit to Philly was decided to do our own Cheesesteak taste test with the 2 best in town.

We went to the place across the street first, and then came over to Pats to try the other. 

Sandwich was very tasty! Every bite was amazing.

There is no question why these 2 places are historic!

If I could give a zero or lower I would. Place says it's open til 4:45am but doesn't "receive" the order when they only take online orders. I called to ask about my online order and they said they didn't get it and then he hung up on me. I called back 4x before he answered and told me it didn't go through. I said I understand technology isn't perfect but that I had guests and needed some food to be ordered and asked to complete over the phone due to the tech issues only to be told no and hung up on again. Worst customer service experience of my life.
Historic spot, came here when I was visiting my buddy at Temple. Food was great and a fun atmosphere.

The food isn't bad, but I will often get a burrito that's only about half as long as when I get it from another location. Also if you come after about 8:30 pm, be prepared to not get what you want. They run out of food quite often and have to close an hour or two early. The employees seem a bit disorganized, mobile orders don't ever get put on the pick up shelf on time and just sit on the counter behind the register.

Had to try the classic! There was no wait. I ordered through grub hub but it said there was a 30 min wait. I went up to Pat's and they made my sandwich right there so no need to wait. 

PROS: 
- good amount of meat 
- flavorful 

CON:
- very messy

If I had to choose between Pat's and Geno.. I'd have to go with Pat's.
Came for the history but quite disappointed with how incohesive this sandwich was: unmelted cheese and large pieces of onion. At least you can watch the basketball games at the park while eating.
Homophobic 'christians' ... Jesus would puke !

This is worst than Geno's. Again they give you a sliver of meat all minced up and the cost is ridiculous. Do not believe the hype that this place and Geno's has the best cheesesteaks. It is false... Better off going to the local deli.

I ordered food here for pickup based on reviews on Main Line page.  I actually ended up driving for 30 extra minutes because I got lost.  Yet, my 3 yo super picky underweight boy ate some of the chicken and shrimp burger.  He is so picky he doesn't eat McDonald's or Wendy's.  While eating, he said "this food is yummy."  So, I'm going to have to move closer....sorry no pics because we gobbled up the food.  As a side note, I did spicy mayo on the side for both burgers and that ended up being perfect because I don't like my food too saucy.  I used the spicy mayo for my fries.

Update:  I'm going back again the next day...

THEY GAVE ME A MOLDY GREEN BREAD!!! Never going to Subway ever again. He sold me a moldy bread and didn't even consider compensating for the fact that I took a bite of this moldy sandwich. This is by far the worst experience I've ever had at Subway. It's disgusting! Your a sandwich place and your main product is moldy? I can only imagine what else is expired in there that they sell to their customers. What a disappointment.

I have been a regular here for 10 years. I dine in, take out and have referred friends. ALWAYS a wonderful experience. I decided to enjoy the weather and dine alone outside today. I was blown away by a new menu item: Vegan Bowl. I noticed the item and Shannon who is so AWESOME recommended the item when I commented on all the new vegan options. I enjoyed the bowl so much I am getting one to go. Thanks Shannon!!!

don't order online here I did plenty of times but last night was different I ordered regular fries but I received the small fries I complain several x the staff kept lying saying its regular I been there countless times I know the size difference I'm not dumb since I had a train to catch only reason I didn't ask 4 a manager 
I won't buy fries nomore or order online

This is the worst Taco Bell I have ever been to. The employees are lazy and the management is horrific. Half the time the order is wrong and forget about complaint to them. They will not care. Save your money and don't waste it here.  

These people should be embarrassed by the quality of service they provide.

This place was a miss for me. The rice felt stale to me and the ponzu sauce was extremely salty. This was not worth the $11+ I paid for it and most of it went into the trash. The cashier was really nice though.

Five guys is my go to burger place, hands down!

The meat is always fresh to order, the option is always up to you to build and it never disappoints. The bacon is always crisp, vegetables always fresh and the fries and always hot.

Just writing this review makes my mouth water. They package everything to go which I think is great since your burger never falls apart if you eat it in the wrapper.

Never messy not too greasy and always made to order.  Cant complain about 5 guys!

Okay, I'm guilty. I did it. I paid the insane prices for absolutely abominable food. I'm part of the problem. Don't make the same mistake. Don't give in to the propaganda.

I've been to Philly several times and have yet to find a cheesesteak that's better than I have had at my local Jersey Mike's. After finally succumbing to the hype, I finally broke down and tried Pat's. Needless to say, my one-star rating means I'm still searching.

As with all of the other places I've tried in Philly, there must be some appeal to slapping a flavorless hunk of shaved meat and onions on a dry roll. Not even Cheez Whiz could help this 8" long piece of the Sahara Desert. I mean seriously, a little salt and pepper would help immensely because it's a sad commentary when the fries and Coke are what make the meal palatable, not the signature item on the menu.

I think what irks me the most is the glaringly obvious, complete and total lack of care that goes into the food. For $70 to get 4 cheesesteaks, 3 fries, and 4 drinks, at least put SOME effort into it.

I won't try Geno's across the street because it's more of the same hype that keeps it and Pat's in business. Avoid Pat's and let's put an end the scourge of this overhyped monstrosity.

Terrible manangement at this location. People who work there simply don't care. They don't show any expressions when they take your order. Takes forever to get the order done, as the staff just chat with each other while taking your order, stop to take a break whenever they want. Food quality was average compared to other locations.

The food area behind the glass was very unappetizing. It was messy. They were low on or were out of several items like mild salsa and guacamole. I ordered a veggie bowl and the grilled vegetables were almost raw. The cheese was old & balled up in chunks. They were out of receipt paper.  The employees didn't seem to take pride in their work.

When you invent an absolute legendary food item, something known the world over and copied by many but never duplicated, you are Pat's King of Steaks.  As far as the steak, no one beats Pat's.  The bread is good, but it does have a tendency to fall apart.  The sandwich itself isn't as salty as most other places which allows the flavors to blend and dance in your mouth.  The steak has some bite to it and a great rich flavor.  I ordered the mushroom pizza cheesesteak wit onion and cheese wiz.  The flavor is subtle but wonderful.  Hot, juicy and wonderful.  It goes down so quickly I was actually was more hungry after I ate then when I started.  One of the draw backs is they only take cash.  But, just like many other places they have one window for sandwiches and another for fries and drinks.  This helps things move along quickly, but, follow the rules.  Pat's doesn't have time for people to think about their order.  Know what you want before you get to the window.  It doesn't matter, everything is awesome!

Since this is a historical landmark, it is covered with pictures and memorabilia.  It's worth the trip to just see it, but, if you don't get a Pat's cheesesteak, it would be like going to the Caribbean and not scuba dive.  It a MUST eat place.

It's chick fil a and it's the airport. 

So the quality is the same as anywhere so that's good. 

It's the airport so the wait was forever. 

It's a good option over the other overpriced low quality food options 

Just make sure you have enough time.
Service is clearly miserable and under paid because they give zero Fcks. You won't be treated with respect from the staff or receive a quality meal so don't waste your time.

*Quick update that they did issue me a refund.* 

Ordered their kale ceasar salad as pick up/take out.
It was bagged up before I arrived. 
When I arrived back to my office (1 block away) and pulled it out there were live fruit flies under the lid crawling and flying around. 
So it went in the trash.
I will not order from here again.
Pat' or Geno's? How ' bout NEITHER! Both suck. If you want a real cheesesteak, try Barry's or Chubby's in Roxborough. Don't waste your time in line at Delassndros.
Now this is PHILLY CHEESESTEAK!  Delicious!  Get it with Wiz!  Yummmmmmy!  It's messy, so grab some napkins!  Fries are delicious too!

$$$ But nothing short of excellence. Homemade amazing burgers and countless fries.. not the best for your waist but def good in your tummy!
Janet L

I ordered a mushroom pepper steak with american cheese. I have one word.. DISGUSTING! The meat was dry without and seasoning or flavor. My cousin's and I drove two hours from NYC. Two of my cousins have visited Pat's multiple times. This was my first time but my cousin said she surprised.  She didn't like her cheese steak either. I won't be back.

Placed an order and was told it would be on its way.  There wasn't a way to track it - I asked if there was an eta of when it may leave (10 minutes or an hour?) and was told "no I'm not in the store and I just am the operator for the drivers" 

There should be some type of accountability as to when the food should leave the store and when I should expect it.

If you're up really late, like, just left Voyeur after hours night club, and want good quality good food to cure the upcoming hangover or intense munchies, order from here. I didn't want to order from here for a long time because I assumed that this place would be like any "up late pizza place" to serve the drunken college student; awful, terrible greasy food that lacks any taste. I took a risk tonight because at 4:30AM, I wanted pizza, and this was the only place open. 


5 Reason last to order from here:

1) My delivery was unbelievably quick. 

2) The driver was super friendly and called me when he left the shop.

3) The presentation of the food was average, but was packaged extremely well, using good quality paper products.

4) LOVE AT FIRST BITE the pizza is thin and with a great crunch. The tomato sauce was a basic neutral sauce, and paired well with the mozzarella cheese. The cheese was high quality, not rubber looking and tasted like a fine mozzarella. My mozzarella sticks were perfect! However they did give me a skimpy slice of a cheesecake --not happy!! Does not match up with their other food products portions. While I got a large handful of entrees and appetizers, the dessert did not match up. It needs to be a larger slice.

5) The food made me want to write a review haha!

The point of all of this? Just order from here!

Of all the Philly cheesesteaks, I think Pat's wins as the classic and most ideal philly cheesesteaks yet. The prevalence of oil in every bite was not an issue in Pat's meal as it was in other cheesesteaks. And their cheese wiz was better than most simply cause it was warm and seemed most fresh. The bread was soft and absorbed all flavors. But the beef was outstanding and outdid everything! Each mouthful was delectable and, seemingly, levels better than the beef in other philly cheesesteaks. Really well done!! Even though the spot is thoroughly advertised, I thought the cheesesteak completely lived up to the hype. So while you mull on the elusive "Is a cheesesteak a sandwich?" question, stop by Pat's and pick up a hearty meal. 4.5 out of 5 stars. KC approved
Overrated tourist trap. Go there as a check the box exercise only. Better cheesesteaks found at your corner pizza place....& yes, same with Gino's across the street. (Pat's is marginally better)
High prices, crowded corner, nothing special. The rivalry keeps people coming, but I wouldn't say the best cheesesteak in the city is on that corner. A little greasy and not my favorite texture meat.
best margs, dog friendly patio seating, best staff in south philly. couldn't recommend more!

Pat's is the TRUE King of Steaks in Philly.  BAR NONE.

The taste of a Pat's Steak is everything you want in a South Philly cheesesteak.  Quality products from bread to meat to cheese... Pat's delivers.   Also, if you're a fan of peppers... or want to try to go out on the edge once or twice... try their cherry peppers on your steak sandwich.  You can have as many or as little as you want and you will NOT be disappointed!

Let's face it, though.  Lots of folks complain about the price.  I just tell those complainers, "You get what you pay for."  While a Pat's sandwich may be just a little more than the other guys... they deliver in quality.  Why settle for less if you're going to treat yourself to a cheesesteak?

And those guys across the street with their flashy signs, their bright colors, and their PacMan video games (well.... i don't think they have pac man...) THEY DON'T COME CLOSE.  

I haven't lived in Philadelphia since I was a kid.  Yet I will literally go back over the bridge JUST to have a Pat's steak.  If the line wraps around the building, FEAR NOT!  The service is quick and the wait is well worth it!

Going to Pat's reminds me of my grandfather.  He used to take me there all the time when I was a wee cheesesteak lover.  Make visiting Pat's a tradition in your family and your kin will NOT be disappointed!

What a disaster.  The chicken tenders are amazing but it's impossible to get any!  I can't tell you how many times I tried to go there when it was supposed to be open and they weren't. 

I arrived at 12:10 today. Sat at the drive thru.  Nothing.  I drive around the building and I see people inside.  So I go back to the drive thru.  Nothing. 

I pulled up to the window and knocked on it and someone finally answered.  "Are you open?"  "Not yet - we're still prepping". "Well what time do you open?" "Usually 11:30 but we are still prepping".  I was told they needed another half-hour.

It's only a matter of time before this place goes under.  Management obviously has no standards and people are just late and miss lunchtime on the weekend.

Frustrating!

If i could give them a 0 for customer service i would. I went to buy cheesesteaks with my uncle and my smaller cousins , and I asked the guy at the front if it was possible to cut it into 6 pieces. But the guy cutting the cheesesteak answered me with a big attitude, saying:" ARE YOU KIDDING ME!? HOW AM I CUT IT INTO 6 PIECES!? AM GONNA CUT MY FINGER!". So yeah instead of a yes or no answer, if you ask them something expect them to answer you back with a tone and attitude, so rude . Not worth the experience. Just got 1 cheesesteak from them and then went to GENO's to buy the rest.
Horrible McDonald's to order from. Starts off with horrible service all the way to horrible. And that's whether they get your order correct or not, most likely not.

Wow, I did really like the chicken sandwich!  It's the fast food service and atmosphere that gives me chills. The resturant was not as clean as it could have been - No health violations but c'mon, just sweep up a bit and put on the facade that you care. Interaction with the cashier was also strange.
I'm not a fan of fast food but sometimes it works.  Really good sandwich just wish I could order online and pick up with no human interaction.  LOL!

Overrated, but had to try it as a bucketlist item! I remember eating a Philly Cheesesteak in the 5th grade and it still remains a fond memory... for my tastebuds. Pat's was not good as I had remembered a "philly cheesesteak in my memory", but it was still worth the visit.

Recommend the Wiz Whit. Cash only. No bathrooms around.

Got the crispy shrimp wrap. It was delicious and got my stoke levels up beyond expectations. Inside the location was a clean fresh setting.The vibes are sure to get stoke levels high. 

Definitely recommend.Prices are fair and portions are dank and very respectable. 

Will be back for sure to explore the menu further.

Blaze is one of my favorite places on campus to get  dinner. You can make a pizza any way you want with someone helping you the whole way. I recommend getting the garlic pesto underneath red sauce, it's a ton of flavor for no extra cost. I have never been disappointed by them.
Still the BEST Philly cheese steak anywhere. I'm from California and we have nothing like it

It's not even 9am and this place is trashed. Every table is dirty. The floor is gross.

This place is such an embarrassment to chestnut hill. I don't know why they don't just shut this place down until they can hire actual staff to run this place.

This Philly and everything about they're food was top notch . Everything was quick, fresh and way better than across the street . I was in town for 3 days and went here twice . The ingredients were fresh and they load u up . Go here now

Yeah, it's touristy. And apparently it's cool to hate on it. But after staying in Philly for seven days and trying four different cheesesteaks, including some lesser known "better" places, Pat's was my favorite. 

Soft roll, real steak, and plenty of whiz. Best of all, it's served piping hot, so the whole thing turns into that melty, gooey mess that you look for in a good cheeseteak. Worth the hype.
The meat seemed tougher as opposed to the last time I had a cheesesteak from here. I always make sure to stop by if it's been a while. Whiz with only. Craving satisfied

Dropped by on a whim cause they are offering free guac to celebrate National Avocado Day! Convenient location and the food is consistently fresh! The staff are super friendly and attentive. Ordered my usual half chicken and half steak burrito bowl with a side of chips on the side. Their guac is a hand-mashed masterpiece that really hit the spot. Chipotle never disappoints!

Come here for the Cheesesteak not the customer service!  These are not only the best Cheesesteaks in Philly, but the home of the original. This is where this sandwich was invented in 1930 and continues service to this day. However, i imagine Back in the day they had better customer service, now they almost rudely yell at you for coming there to eat! Ha 

No smiles, no small talk, just pay and 30 seconds later have a delicious cheesesteak slapped in your hands. 

Then go to a separate window for cheese drenched French fries. 

However, at the end of the day you don't come to this location for small talk, you come for AWESOME CHEESESTEAK... and it delivers. Time and time again. Also, i recommend the cheese wiz, that makes all the difference in the world!

I come here probably twice a week for lunch for a variety of fruit smoothies.  My favorite is raspberry/banana, but I've tried many other flavors.

Solid menu but I stick with smoothies and don't mess around with all those fat burning/cleanse juices.  

Staff is always super friendly and very quick with orders when it gets busy.  

I've never had a problem here, everything is always super fresh and tasty.  It IS pricy at $5+ a pop, but I think worth it.

Went to Los Cabalitos on Friday night and had such a great experience. Nathaniel was our waiter and was a pleasure to have the whole night. Was incredibly attentive  to my friend and I even when the place was packed. Wonderful food and Nathaniel assured me he would be cautious of my severe allergy to gluten. Can't wait to come back as it has great food and even greater service!
Rude service with mediocre cheesesteaks. The cheesesteaks were somewhat dry with little cheese. Plenty of other places to try.

Extra Cheesesteak Wit Whiz

Tips for Ordering at Pat's

The line at Pat's King of Steaks moves quickly, so it's best to be prepared -- know what you want, and how to order it by the time you get to the front of the line!

Step 1
Specify if you want your steak with (wit) or without (wit-out) onions

Step 2
Specify Plain, Cheez Whiz, Provolone, American or Pizza Steak

Step 3
Have your money ready. We are cash only.

Step 4
Order just your steak at the first window. The second window is for fries and drinks.

Step 5
Eat up while it's hot! Honestly, when it comes to Pat's, I figured it would be best to "borrow" their Tips for Ordering (pasted above). That's really all you need to know.... Whether you want a Steak, a Hot Dog, a Pork or a Fish Cake, the most important aspect of Pat's is knowing how to order. The food? Well, it's in the title..."King of Steaks" No, seriously, every bite is complete Cheesesteak Bliss and you SHOULD believe the hype!

cannot get a single order correct! do not waste your time and money with these fools. go somewhere else or to another location if you want to get value for your money and actually get the food you ordered

I am tourist from Florida. I admit this outright. 

I did the challenge on Monday July 7th at 3:00pm. I headed to Geno's and Boyfriend grabbed Pat's. He had only ever had pat's and I said this was unacceptable. He also didn't want to get whiz and I said we had to get whiz at both to have a comparison. He reluctantly agreed. Because of this, I have to idea what the process was like at Pat's all I know is the their birch beer fountain soda was 50 cents more than Geno's. 

We got one wit whiz. It was not what I was expecting. The chopped meat had a meaty flavor but more like standard pot roast tasting beef. The onions were great all carmelized and buttery. Their bread was weirdly soft and bland. From the looks of it I expected more in both taste and texture. It is a good sponge but I think we got a slightly dry steak than usual. I looked at yelp pictures of soaking buns and juicy meat and ours didn't seem that way. There wasn't as much whiz as I would like. I didn't think their whiz tasted as good as Geno's. In Short, Geno's won in the whiz category.

Now, because the boyfriend always got a provolone steak at Pat's he was craving his favorite. We skipped french fries and ordered another steak from pats, this time one wit provolone. Wow, what a difference the cheese made. I think our meat was a fresher batch that was juicier as well. The onions were once again great. The chopped meat flavor was complemented by the generous provolone serving. This was what you think of when you think "cheese steak". 

So Geno's for Whiz and Pat's for Provolone. That is my contribution to the challenge.

I will add that if pat's used the bread at geno's that they may have won both categories but unless they are serving up super juicy meat and not being stingy with the whiz there is no way that bread makes sense. It is merely a vehicle and in such a simple sandwich is really should be more than that.

This Taco Bell is still garbage. Never had a single chalupa or burrito that was properly made. The way make the food seems like they got two year olds in the back acting like the food is play doh 

Also what kind of Taco Bell closes at 11 on the weekends. Anyways, don't eat at this location.
Best cheesesteak I've ever had, I've lived in Philadelphia my entire left. The original!

I have been a regular here for 10 years. I dine in, take out and have referred friends. ALWAYS a wonderful experience. I decided to enjoy the weather and dine alone outside today. I was blown away by a new menu item: Vegan Bowl. I noticed the item and Shannon who is so AWESOME recommended the item when I commented on all the new vegan options. I enjoyed the bowl so much I am getting one to go. Thanks S
I just had to return for another vegan bowl and sangria. Alan is great!

The cheesesteak was great and this was my first time ordering as I live out of state. I felt it was worth the money, and worth the drive into the old neighborhood to eat there. My hangups were that they don't accept cards and that ordering is intense. Its like if you don't know exactly how they expect you to order expect to get the looks and attitude of, 'learn to order, and hurry it up'. It was my first time there keep in mind. The food was great enough to likely come back if I'm in Philly but the customer service and restaurant atmosphere was too intense and I could see it keeping people away. There bread is from Jersey btw. It tasted good.

Classic Philly cheesesteak.  Meet is well seasoned, bread is crunchy on the outside and soft inside, must get with wiz.  Onions added a beautiful touch to complete the whole meal.  Add some cheese fries if you're still hungry.  Cash only and can be really hard to find parking.  Must try as it's one of Philly's food landmarks.

Mark is the best bartender server ever. The margs rival el vez but at w lower price point. The nachos are so good. I highly recommend it. Also love the tacos. But as I said they're margs are the best!! Ask Marc to make them. For your. Your won't be disappointed

I have dined here regularly for a great many years. It was always the perfect spot to sit outside and have some appetizers and margaritas, especially since they were always open late and had a massive patio. 

I've planned on writing this review for years and never got around to it. I keep coming back for the outside vibes, reasonably priced margarita pitchers, and vegan beef BUT I have never had such consistently horrible service anywhere else. And I'm honestly shocked myself that I continue to come back and expect something to change. 

There's one server I've been stuck with several times, and originally I wanted to post his name because he was that awful but were in the middle of a pandemic and it's not the time for call outs I suppose. He completely ignores you. Is incredibly rude. A few years back I brought my whole family here for my post-graduation dinner. It was their first time visiting and I could of taken them anywhere but I chose here. We all ate entrees, got appetizers and rounds of margarita pitchers for the group racking up a pretty high bill and enjoying spending time with each other. However all I can remember is how rude this server was, he blatantly ignored us when he was walking around our section and we were trying to order more drinks/food. I would slightly raise my hand or try to get his attention (respectfully, I've been in the service industry for many years and understand how to be a decent human being even when receiving poor service), and he would literally look up at the ceiling or look away after seeing me/my family members were looking to order something. Then, after waiting this extended period of time to no avail, the host comes over and says we have reached our "2 hour limit" for sitting at the table and have to leave because they need to sit someone else there. Mind you, they don't even accept reservations so this is a random walk-in that they wanted my family to leave for even though we were still spending money and trying our best to order more items while being completely ignored for the majority time we were there. Also worth mentioning I'd gone here a great many times previous to this and stayed well past a 2 hour window (from small gatherings to big birthday gatherings) even with their being a crowded dining room and never once heard of this "rule." Regardless, we didn't try to even negotiate at this point because why give an establishment any more of our money if they clearly don't want our business? 

But unfortunately, this was one of a many incidents of horrible customer service, completely understaffed shifts, desperately waiting for someone on staff to remember we (and the tables around us) exist so we can place our orders. Even though one specific staff member stands out as the worst, it has been clear this is not any individual staff members fault, and that the management, and coinciding scheduling and culture, is to blame for their inability to provide even semi-decent, relatively timely service. I don't think I've ever seen one of their employees smile even once. 

Now, on to the reasons that I have foolishly kept giving them so many dang chances despite all this aforementioned tomfoolery: 
*Vegan  Beef  Nachos  (not to be confused with the vegan nachos with vegan beef - they're not worth it just get no cheese if you're not with the dairy) 
*Honestly, just like vegan beef everything (esp. The Wet Burrito) 
*Wings with PONZU MOJO Sauce, must try!
*Platanos Machos 
*And their food specials can be pretty dope 


Also should be noted that during this pandemic fiasco they are offering to-go quarts of margaritas (pick-up only), and only have outdoor seating/any seating Friday & Saturday nights. 

Worth giving this place a try if you've never been, but don't say I didn't warn ya....best to have a snack before you go and bring your own water bottle so you can enjoy the outdoor chi and be prepared to wait a while.
Took 10 minutes to get to someone to answer at the drive through just to serve me a freezing cold sandwich. The employees are miserable and the food horrible even for a McDonald's.

We did the Pat's and Geno's comparison. Pat's had a harder roll, more cheese wiz, softer onions and drier meat. Geno's had a softer roll, less cheese, crispier onions and meat juice that dripped out. So, I'd say that in my opinion, Geno's wins, but we still think Jim's on South Street is the best. Also -- and it's really important -- our server did not wear his mask properly; it did not cover his nose and we saw his upper lip. Not good! In addition, the outdoor seating is very crowded and not COVID-friendly -- the back of one person in my group was touching the back of the person at the adjoining table.

Very disappointed in the cheesesteak, it was dry and the cheesesteak was not seasoned AT ALL. The sandwich was made in 5 seconds and it was tasteless, very disappointed, this is a tourist trap along with the place directly across the street! Thumbs down!

The food is super average. I would rate 2 stars but am giving the restaurant 3 stars because 1) I came with my brother and any time spent with him is a good time 2) the server had such a relaxed, kind personality. 

I ordered Birria tacos which looked bomb and tasted OK. I also ordered the vegan chocolate cake which was again, average. I did appreciate that the cake was not overly sweet for my tastebuds. 

There are many authentic, delicious Mexican food spots nearby in South Philadelphia. I do not consider Cantina one of them. #HereForTheFood

I came into this location for the first time while bringing a friend, and I was honestly pretty happy with my experience. I'm a pretty big Taco Bell fan, and I was bringing my friend I for the first time. The employee behind the register was extremely friendly and was definitely entertained by my extensive knowledge of the Taco Bell menu.

Both my friend and I placed our orders within a pretty short amount of time, and the employee at the register was kind enough to give us free drinks when I mentioned how much I enjoyed Mountain Dew Baja Blast. 

In about 5 minutes, our food was brought out by an employee from the kitchen who greeted us in a very friendly manner. I had ordered a Chalupa Supreme, Beefy Fritos Burrito, Nacho Fries, and a 2-Pack Cinnabon Delights. I thought all of my food was well-made, and I thoroughly enjoyed my experience. Our table was also clean, and the restaurant was not too crowded around 9PM.

Overall, I would come back to this location. Service, food quality, and atmosphere were good. I don't always have good fast food experiences in the city, but I definitely enjoyed this one.
Used to be great. Now, not so much. Had about 4 tablespoons of grease, meat not seasoned with any salt or pepper. Onions cooked separately and thrown in at end. Less than mediocre.

Trying several while in town, and I have come to the conclusion it may not be taste as a preference, but rather if you like your meat chopped or more in strands. Flavor comes from the cheese/ toppings added, meat in general is not flavored as it relies on the whiz or provolone. 
I prefer the longer strands vs chopped. Also whiz def makes the entire experience on the saltier/ flavorful side. Cheese fries at the bottom were def saltier than expected. 
Pay in one window, pick up in other, def good ordering system. Has bench seating, first come first serve, but did not have any issues getting a seat

Terrible service. The first time I tried to order it was 5pm and the girl told me "they were not open at the moment". I tried a second time, the only thing they had available was tenders and fries. Nothing else. 
The third time I sat at the window and no one said anything, no service at all. There were clearly people in the restaurant working. 
Will never go back.

One of the better "fast" food type burger options in the area but just ok in the grand scheme of things. 
Service is usually pretty unfriendly with the cashier speaking so softly and quickly that I can barely understand what is being said (and you can only say "I'm sorry, can you repeat that?" so many times before things get awkward. 
No attention to detail is paid so beware if they get your order wrong and you wait till you get home to check...you might end up paying for a bacon cheeseburger that doesnt have bacon, etc. 

On the plus side, the place is very clean. There are at least a few tables and spacious...definitely bigger on the inside than it appears from the outside.
They denied service to my friend and i for not wearing a mask. All While serving 3 individuals in front of us without mask. The girl taking the order was not wearing a mask also.

Long lines but it moves quick so don't be discouraged.   I got the provolone which was a little dry, I think Wiz is the way to go.   There are 2 separate windows, one for cheesesteaks and one for everything else which was confusing but it helps the line move.  The fries were great.

I have not been back to Pat's in over seven years. There was a short line but they move quick. Much quicker than Geno's across the street. The cashier has no patience with you asking questions and looking at the menu. They want to take your order and move on.


I ordered the cheese steak with whiz cheese. I tried Jim's steak and Geno's before this. This was by far the worst of the 3. The cheese steak had very little onions and cheese. It felt like I was just eating a plain steak sandwich. I was disappointed yet again.

There are so many things wrong with this Wendy's. There is a reason why it is rarely a line in the drive-through. Customer service is ass. It is very frustrating trying to order through the app (i know this location has no control over this). They often forget something in your order such as the dressing or a side. Then when you try to bring it up to the staff they are straight up rude. I don't understand why they are so slow when they are no customers waiting in line SMH. Chick-fil-A is definitely worth the wait most days lol. Some please fix their disorganized system!

So I'm a tourist in Philly. It's only natural (and obligatory for that matter) that I try THE PHILLY CHEESESTEAK. 
Now, I love a good drama so learning about the battle of bests between Pat's & Geno's made it even more exciting to try this local staple. 
Pat's King of Steaks® was founded by Pat Olivieri in 1930. Pat had a modest hot-dog stand at the base of the famous Italian Market in South Philadelphia. While it seems Pat's was the original, I think there needs to be some updating. The place itself seems very old. You better know what you want and have your money ready when you get to the window. There is a zero tolerance here which made me so anxious. There is also a way to order. Wit (with) or wit out (without) cheese. Specify Plain, Cheez Whiz, Provolone, American or Pizza Steak. Cash only & have it ready! Window #1 is just for the steak with window #2 being for fries and drinks. 
Again, everyone raves about the whiz. But when I saw it on someone else's sandwich it seems really runny. I decided to be adventurous and get the cheese steak with provolone instead. It was a mistake. The cheese was not melted and the texture hindered me from enjoying the steak. Once I took off the cheese it was a much better experience. The steak was a little greasier than the competition but it was still good.
Just ordered a cheesesteak with fried onions and just got this super small steak hoagie with barely any meat in it. Check out the photos.

On three separate occasions I've been denied service here. All three times in the drive through. The morning crew has always been very polite and fast. It's the late crew that seems to make their own rules. 

The first time I was told flat out "we out of food, find something else. Whiteboy." 

The second time I was told that the card machine was down as the woman who everyone knew apparently in the car ahead paid with her card. I remember because she had to get out of the car to hand it over when she dropped it on the ground. I was told cash only. 

And the last time, last Sunday. I drove up on my motorcycle. It was early and wanted breakfast before my 19 hour shift. And was told that they can't serve me on a motorcycle. I've been served dozens of times on it. One gentleman actually suggested last year that I get a cup holder so I don't have to order al a carte. 

Clearly this McDonald's isn't checked up on. And if it is. No one cares.

I ordered a sushi/roll/sashimi boat here for my party and the boat was absolutely amazing (see my photo)!

I stopped by 3 days before my party to place the order, the manager carefully explained the types of boat they can make. My partner picked it up on the day of the party and it came with all essential side dishes (ginger, wasabi, soy sauce, and edamame). The whole experience was smooth.

My guests loved the wide variety of sushi/roll/sashimi on this boat and they enjoyed the edamame soy beans very much!
This is the slowest McDonald's I've ever been at. Every single time.  They don't even have dine in service right now and they are still insanely slow.

I have to give a special shout-out to King  because King is amazing and always makes evenly distributed pizzas. I always get mozzarella, parm, and mushroom... so pretty basic. I get mushrooms in every slice and bite of the pizza if King makes it. Another girl made my pizza before and she haphazardly puts on cheese and puts a dash of mushroom...  and I'd get a slice I pizza with a single mushroom and another slice two.. Key to a good pizza... equal distribution of toppings including sauce and cheese. King nails it.

Even if King does not make it, the pizza is still great. It's just a bonus if King make it. Thin cripsy crust that's cooked perfectly. Even places like Nomad Pizza where it's $14 for a standard margherita pizza burn their pizzas to a crisp and you can get a mouthful of ash.

May be a further hike for the Penn kids, but it's worth it if you want a good pizza. Don't forget to treat yourself to their refreshments. I like to get their passion fruit refresher and mix it with their lemonade with a splash of citrus soda.

Servers are horrible, 40 minutes to get a pitcher of margarita's, over a hour to get food, and it wasn't even busy. Ordered chicken salad server forgot to put in chicken, waited 15 mins for chicken.Very cool manager made up for bad servers with tequila shots and comped a entree. FYI Make Alex the food runner a server, took care of every table servers neglected.

The cheese steak was sooo delicious. Especially after I ate Genos. 
I went to Genos first because it was closer than Pats. When I saw the cheese steak at Genos I was pretty disappointed and then I took my first bite, and I was sooooo disappointed to the point that I didn't want to waste my money on another cheese steak. Luckily, last minute I decided that I should at least give pats a try since I probably would never have an opportunity like that again and I was so glad I did. 
The meat was good and had a slight sweetness that tasted perfect with the salty cheese. They also had these delicious pickled peppers that made the cheese steak even better. 
It was a good experience and when I go back to Philly, I know where I will get my cheese steak.

Can't decide between Pat's and Geno's? Neither could I until I actually showed up to the famed intersection.

Geno's is really in your face about everything. It has loud billboard signs, brightly lit interiors, and even a gift shop next door. Nearby, workers hype up the rivalry between Pat's and Geno's with a Godzilla vs. King Kong photo opp. 

On the contrary, Pat's is really low-key. It doesn't have brightly lit signs, the workers appear to be more laid back, and the menu isn't electronic. I elected to go to Pat's over Geno's because it felt less like a tourist trap than Geno's. 

Pat's is cash only, so make sure to bring cash! If you forget, there is also a brand new Chase ATM right next to the store.

My family and I drove all the way from the Bronx here because we heard that Pat's King Steaks was the best place to get a Philly cheese steak sandwich.  Unfortunately we were disappointed,  the meat was bland and the bread soggy.  I've had better "Philly cheese steaks" in New York.

Maybe next time I'm in Philly I'll try Geno's...

This was a late night treat. So here's the run down after dark. For me being as young as I am, these guys were cool and very down to earth. Someone my mothers age would've found it to be the oddest set up around and/or probably would've said it doesn't look like a reputable establishment. Me I didn't care I was hungry. One gripe is not having paper menus and having to order everything online while already being there. But truth is, the food was f^*#%=g amazing and they made it to my liking. I appreciate that extra gesture so I had to give 5 stars. I would definitely go back and recommend this spot to anyone coming in from a fun night out.

Yes, it's a touristy spot.

I still wanted to try Pat's out. We've been to Geno's before but finally got a chance to try out Pat's, which is right across the street. Stood in the long line. There is a sign before you get to the ordering counter guiding you in how you should order. It's helpful because this allows the line to move quickly. The cashier was super quick and direct. I'd say in under a minute, he took our cash and handed us our sandwiches. 

There is some outdoor seating available, but it does get packed here. Condiments, peppers, napkins are within reach. We really enjoyed our cheesesteak sandwiches. They were packed with juicy meat, gooey cheese, and diced sautéed onions. The bread was fresh and held the sandwich together well. 

So glad we finally got a chance to try Pat's. We definitely enjoyed Pat's more than Geno's. However, Geno's will always have a special place in my heart because it was the first cheesesteak I ever tried in Philly. Both are worth trying at least once. 

Cash Only! There is an ATM nearby if you forget.
So so good.   Great service.   Cheeseburger Taste like mom made in our kitchen.   I have loved everything I've ordered. Highly recommend!

I will not be ordering takeout from this place again. I ordered the "create your own bowl" and they did not add the sauce I selected or the avocado (which I was charged extra for). Other people on my order  were also missing avocado and/or the sauce. I'm not sure if it was just because there was no sauce, but the bowl did not taste good. When I order a poké bowl, I'm expecting fresh salmon/tuna. This did not taste fresh.

I've ordered from here multiple times, but tonight will be the last. It sucks l, but I hope their delivery drivers find new places to work. The owner or supervisor that I spoke to on the phone tonight was so incompetent I couldn't believe it. 

Here's what happened:

Gf orders delivery through their website. We order from them often initially through grubhub, but since we enjoyed the food so much we decided we wanted to support them directly and order through their own website. Plus there's a promo code "OWL" that they literally have sent text ads to us directly which gives you $4 off your total order. Cool, right? Gf gets text bank confirmations for every transaction and gets one directly after ordering our delivery. However, on the website it says there's been an error. So I give them a call...

I literally spend 20-30 mins talking to their supervisor (Leigh or Wei, or whatever their name is) trying to explain what has happened. By the end of it he tells me that not only do I need to call my bank a cancel the transaction (cool, thanks bro), but that they weren't taking ANY responsibility for the error and couldn't get our order completed until we went BACK ON THEIR WEBSITE AND REORDERED. Why the HELL can't you just complete my order through the phone while I'm talking and/OR just admit that your website fucked up and get the order completed?!
Absolute nonsense and zero customer service. 

Never again. 

Don't waste your time. 

Go to "Three Countries Pizza" instead. 20 mins faster than their estimated arrival.

Every now and then I have to try the tourist traps just to see how they're doing. 

I don't come here often anymore. Pat's was the first cheesesteak place I ever came to as a kid. It was a mainstay for me into my 20s. Then I learned that the city actually has other cheesesteaks. 

I've had a lot of those other cheesesteaks. My tastebuds have reset. How would those tastebuds react to the Pat's of today. 

They're ok. 

They're just ok now. 

It's still a good amount of juicy meat. It's still a half decent roll. 

But it's no longer special to me. 

Now it's just an overpriced sandwich that I can get better at 13 different places in the city now.

Pat's King of Steaks reminds of the fable, The Emperor's New Clothes. 
After picking up my California friend at 30th Street Station, we wove our way down to  South 9th Street for a taste of Philadelphia - the renowned, Pat's.  My 12 year old son came along when he heard we would go for cheesesteaks.  

The environment around Pat's is terrific.  People all over the place.  The queue to order.  The Rules for Ordering.  The smack in the puss aroma of burning grease and onions.  The whole migila.  I felt my own excitement rise the closer I came to the ordering window.  I felt the vicarious thrill as my son ordered his first Cheesesteak Witout and Provolone, and a Birch Beer.  Truly, a right of passage. 

Yet, when we sat down at a red metal grate table and began to devour our sandwiches, I noted my son's displeasure with the amount of fat and gristle he had to  spit out.  I, too, was surprised to find red meat in my tumultuous pile of steak, onions, mushrooms and cheese.  Uncooked.  It felt careless. I did not mind that each time I picked up the load to have a bite, and equal amount fell out the back end of the 'wich. That was to be expected from an unfortunate roll incapable of holding its load.  Still, I did not feel like picking up the canned shrooms  and steak pieces to eat them.  

5 Stars for the institution and historic icon that is Pat's King of Steaks. 
2 Stars for the actual product generated from this amazing operation.  

3 Stars for the King who needs to look in the mirror and realize he may be wearing only his reputation.

Mehh. This was my first time getting a Philly cheesesteak in Philly and it was okay. My boyfriend and I were on our way to New York from Virginia and decided to do a pitstop along the way so it was like an early grub for us at like maybe 7:30AM. 

I do like how the location looked with the lights and everything but the food itself wasn't anything spectacular. We ordered the Philly with steak, onions and cheese wiz. I don't know if it's because the bread was just cold and I'm sure that's the way to eat a cheesesteak but I wasn't into that. 

Maybe I need to try another one next time I'm there or at another location.

Me: could I please have queso with my chips? 
Employee: we don't have chips
Me: the board says you have chips and salsa, where are your chips? 
Employee: we close in a few minutes so we stop offering them
Me: it's 7:30 though 
Employee: Yes
Me: okay, no chips for me I guess 

Worst burrito I've ever had. And they are open until 11. This is where I insert an eye roll

For being a pizza chain it's the best. You pick everything you want on your pizza right in front of you  and done in like 5 mins. I only been at the one in Disney Springs so I don't know if they are all set up the same way. And their homemade lemonade is the bomb.

Thought it'd be cool to have a "battle of the cheesesteaks," as Geno's Steaks and Pat's King of Steaks is directly across from each other. 

We ordered a cheesesteak with provolone and onions. I preferred the cheesesteak from Pat's over Geno's, but still disappointed. The cheesesteak wasn't as dry, but still not flavorful (maybe it was fat juices). The bread got soggy as well. 

This place is cash only. Prices are listed to the nearest dollar with tax already included (no need for coin change). 

Not sure why Pat's neon signs weren't on at night on the day that I went.

Surprisingly, there were only 6 people in front of us when we came here!! My cousin parked his car illegally, we hopped out, got in line, ordered, got our food all in 7 minutes!!! 

You pick what kind of cheesesteak you want-- cheese, onions, order... pay. Ca$h only.
The condiments station is right behind you from where you placed your order. You have to get into a different line if you want french fries, which we didn't try.

Outdoor seating. Very vintage haha. Geno's is literally right across the street. Talk about competition. They are very generous with the amount of meat they put into your sandwich. It gets pretty greasy so load up on napkins. The bottom part of the bread gets soggy too, so it'll just make you want to inhale the sandwich before it gets too soggy.

Ordered 4 "steaks wit" delivered from Goldbelly and could not have been more disappointed.   Arrived frozen as expected.  Packaging was good but product quality was awful.  Bread was tasty but that's about all that can be said.   Meat was very dry and of limited portion.   It was difficult to find the "wit".   Maybe one thin slice of provolone cheese and a few onion bits.   Bad experience for a premium price.   Tanks for nuttin Pat.
Was nice. Much better than their competitors across the street! Excellent amount of cheese wiz along with good steak.

So we have 25 minutes till boarding begins- you think it would be plenty of time to grab a sandwich. Nope...it took 15 minutes to get a sandwich. I love Chick-fil-A but this location doesn't have their act together.
The silver lining I had something to eat on the flight

I was truly impressed, we ordered the original Phily cheese steak and it was so good! The bread was fresh, the steak flavorful and the "cheese whiz"(I was VERY hesitant about) was delicious!

I have to thank our Uber driver, we where headed to the airport when he asked if we had tried the Phily cheesesteak, we hadn't. He drove us over to pats and even offered to buy us a cheesesteak! So sweet, we bought him one and got one for us. Great experience.

"Pat's King of Steaks" was good. The building has no inside dining, so dress warm in the winter. The building is older and The you line up on the side and the have two windows. One for the famous cheese steaks and the other for fries and drinks. After heading to both windows you find seating located around the restaurant. They don't take credit so remember cash. It was time to find out if they were king. They give you a ton of cheese and onions on the hero. The steaks are chopped up small. It does have a lot of flavor and the bread was soft. I was disappointed in the fries. They were thick and delicious, but they don't give you a lot. I would say I liked Pat's, but king is a lofty expectations. I would go back, but  I definitely wouldn't recommend it as a goto.
Restaurant is an absolute dump. Employees are rude as all hell. Taco Bell is pretty awful to begin with but this particular Taco Bell manages to make it even worse.

Nice location with ample parking. The employees can be more preoccupied with gossip on occasion but that may be to steam the monotony of the job.
They renovated the interior and have expanded their variety of salads. Yummy!!

Came here on a whim as I've wanted to try HNT chicken. Got in the drive-through and placed an order for a single sandwich.  Told to pull around.

There was a single car in front of me waiting for their food. After I literally sat 15 minutes listening to a few songs on the stereo and looking at my phone and Yelp reviews of HNT, I realized that I probably made a mistake wanting to try this chicken. With the time I wasted in line, it was time to go.

No sandwich, just time to waste watching the car in front of us also wait an unreasonable amount of time waiting for their food, which also didn't come by the time I left. Not sure why it was so slow, but something wasn't clicking inside.

Greasy cheesesteak. Smelled like white castles. A tad dry. Needed salt. But despite that it was GOOD and TASTY!! the bread was perfect and so soft. The French fries stole the show honestly. They were really good!!! Idk what kind of fruit punch they serve, nothing like back home in Indiana, but it was yummy. Workers were polite! Didn't get to compare to geno's tho we just had pats! Bf says the hot dog was really good!!

Messed up 2 out of 2 of my orders.  Asked for napkins and ketchup and didn't receive either.  Fries are always old and cold. Ordered a sour cream and chive baked potato - no sour cream to be found.  Asked for LTO on my burger - no LTO to be found.

I don't know how this place doesn't have more stars, I loved it! It's tempting to go to Geno's with all the flashing lights and decor but Pat's has the best cheesesteak, between the two and debatably, the best in town! I've had the cheesesteak with whiz cheese and onions (side note - just say "with" and that means with onions!) and the cheesesteak with american cheese "with." Both were great! Good bread, good meat, good cheese, can't complain! Only negatives - the fries weren't my favorite and it gets crowded on the weekends so it's hard to get seating.

Waited in the drive thru for 20 minutes for 4 double cheeseburgers last night. Whenever we go in during the day the service is fast enough but night time they're understaffed and they act like they don't want to be there, which I don't blame them for. It's late, they're understaffed, and there is 10 cars in the line less than half an hour before close.
I'm super patient but it's so sad watching these girls have to deal with this kind of workload on top of what they have to do to close up before leaving.

Me and a group of friends got in line to purchase nuggets and fries to share and enjoy. They told us if we are buying anything we are not allowed to sit down and have to take it on the go. They said that because we are teenagers but we were not loud or obnoxious. We were going to use our money on their food but I guess not. Also, there were other people sitting down eating. Just because we are teenagers does not mean we are going to keep away customers. Thank God Taco Bell is right next door because I would gladly spend it there anyway.

CHEESESTEAK WAR - Geno's vs Pat's 

We took a long road trip from Atlanta to Maine, making stops all along the way at places I've been wanting to try for years. Everything from authentic NY pizza and pastrami to authentic Maine lobster rolls were preset into my GPS navigation.  Well, I don't know how I could call myself a food lover and not have an authentic Philadelphia cheesesteak from the two originals, so on this trip I rectified that!

I've never been to any of the states north of the Carolina's on the East coast and decided last year we are going to curtail our preferred mode of vacationing (cruises), to spend more time touring all the great places we've been missing around our own country. After all, our boys are getting older and there is only so much time we have left before they might not think it's cool to hang out with us... LOL

~~~~~~~~~~

THE EXPERIENCE
I was a total tourist during my visit to Pat's. Taking pictures, laughing with locals and hamming it up with the kitchen staff. It may just be my personality, but we don't generally have problems with people. I've read a lot of reviews about the staff both here and across the street @ Geno's being rude, even saw it on a Food Network show. However, they were fantastic with us. My excitement to be there must have been infectious because they even came out to take pics and cracked a few jokes. 

As usual with touristy places, you are bound to run into others who came a long distance just to try them. We ran into one couple also doing a steak comparison and had just finished their first steaks @ Geno's. They made for an enjoyable conversation as we shared our crazy food adventures. It always make me feel better to know that I'm not the only person in this world that travels for food !

~~~~~~~~~~

THE CHEESESTEAK
I HATE Cheese Whiz. It is a violation of basic food decency and have been repelled from any establishment that even suggests putting it on my food. So when I found out Philadelphians prefer it, I made it up in my mind I would give it a try so as to have the most authentic experience possible. Under protest of course, because the backup plan was to throw it away if I didn't like it and order another with provolone, the cheese of the food gods!!!

I was stupefied at just how amazing whiz can taste on a Philly cheesesteak. Not in a million years would I have guessed I would love it as much as I did. But then again it could simply be the way Pat's blends it with the meat. It's not just poured on top as I expected. No, it's mixed into the blend of beef and onions during the cooking process, setting of an orgy of deliciousness.

I'm a Chicago native. The meat in our cheesesteaks is much more finely diced, almost to the point of looking like ground beef, which is how I prefer my cheese steaks.  Pat's does not chop their beef up nearly as much, but it is certainly more finely chopped than its rival Geno's for sure. It make the sandwich easier to eat, more tender and in my opinion, creates a more balance flavor between all the ingredients. Most people mistake the finer chop for a lesser quality meat, but nothing could be further from the truth. I'd be willing to bet the meat each uses probably comes from the same vendor. They just slice and season it differently.

~~~~~~~~~~

FINAL THOUGHTS
Food is a personal experience not always based on how good something actually is, but how good it is in comparison to other life experiences. It may be tied to memories with loved ones or a bad experience with a past relationship. Whatever subjective feeling you have, no one can really take away how the inner you reacts to it. 

As for me, Pat's was probably the singular most soul satisfying meal I had during my entire three week vacation up the East coast. Took me back, way back to simpler days. I love food (all food) but you should know by now I'm not fancy. If I were food, this sandwich is truly me on a plate. My eyes rolled back in my head as my taste buds screamed 'Don't stop, git it, git it!'   Winner - Pat's.




SIDENOTE: See my review for Geno's to get the comparison between the two.

He said, "No, If I was giving you the stink eye you'd know it" and kinda grinned. I said, "Okay, just checking." We got my order and left, but my friend (who lives around the block) said, "Wow, that's the nicest I've ever seen him!" 

As to the steak itself, it was okay. Gotta say, I've had better tasting sandwiches. (Sorry, it's true.) But now I can say I've had the genuine article, with the genuine experience to go with it.

I ordered a filet o fish for the second time at this location(8500 Henry ave.)  thinking it would be better this go around, but I was WRONG. The sandwich was below room temperature and the fries tasted like leftovers. The look I had on my face you would've thought I was having a stroke. I was extremely dissatisfied once AGAIN. It was at that moment I knew I had F**ked up. That location has given me TRUST issues with all McDonalds everywhere. It should be demolished and used for a parking lot. It doesn't deserve any stars IMO. But it won't post my review unless you give it at least one star.‍

We already don't love this location - the food is never all that good and the service is ok at best. Tonight takes the cake, roll in at 11:30pm because online it says they're open til midnight. We sat in the drivethru for a while, other people joined us in line, and no one took our order. We drove around the building -- no hours posted anywhere and just two teenage girls inside not giving a s*it. Not going back, glad we're leaving the area soon.

I snuck over here for breakfast recently. I chose this over my personal favorite Penrose Diner to try something new.

Man I am so glad I did.

When I decided to order the Tater Tot Scramble, I expected the tater tots we are all used to getting. And I would have been happy with those because they are awesome in their own right. 

But this place takes the tater tots to the next level with their homemade take on them. This dish with the homemade chili as well is something special. It's worth a special trip. They take the time to make something unique instead of just opening a can of Hormel and pouring them over eggs and Ore Ida frozen tots. 

Heck, I would have been happy with that.  But I'm glad they go the extra mile.

Just plain ewww... This has to be the worst McDonald's I've ever been to. The fries are beyond greasy they taste like they were made the night before. Dirty tables, floors, just plain yuck. Stay away!

Well during Covid19 what is there to do not much but you can take road trip and grab a great Philly cheesesteak. This one was my sons favorite and mine too the original. Quick to take you please 
bring your cash, it's cash only but there's an ATM. I got one with onions my son without but both are so good. Since 1930 it's been around and I can see why. Be prepared to search for parking and I'd go in a group but enjoy it it's so worth it!

I saw all the hypes from the YouTubers and stopped by on my recent trip to Philly. 

I got there on a late Saturday afternoon and it was impossible to find a parking spot nearby. I parked about 4 blocks away.  

There was a vey short line and I order 4 cheesesteaks. They brought them out instantly even before I was able to take the cash out of my wallet.  I asked the cashier if those cheesesteaks were mine and the guy behind him said "are you stupid or just dumb!"  

Despite the insults, I did not argue and moved to the soft drink and fried order line. Those guys were a lot more professional. 

Overall, the cheesesteaks were small relative to the ones at Reading Market but tasty. But we all liked the food. 

However, I won't go back nor recommend others to go because:
- the sandwiches were pre-made - not sure if they are fresh
- the staff hated the customers and treated us badly
- it was out of the way from central Philly and a hassle to get back onto the Turnpike (bad local traffic)

I wished I had my GoPro out capturing the staff with attitude- I just may have gotten a viral video on TikTok or YouTube!

I got the kale strawberry banana smoothie and it's very good. It's not too sweet which i appreciate. The woman who made the smoothie was fast and friendly. They seem to have it down at this place, it's professional. And not terribly expensive like some smoothie places can be.

When I opened my cheesesteak there was no meat on the front end of the sandwich so I had to pull off the top of the sandwich.. not a fan of the condiments sitting at the curb anyone can put something in it .. a bit unsanitary for me.   The meat was very bland... 
Picked up my son from Philly Airport and he wanted a cheesesteak.. I have eaten better cheesesteaks in New Jersey  Juniors Cheesesteak in Verona NJ best Cheesesteaks ever... will have to try Geno's or Sonny's next time.. Definitely overrated... they just don't care... you need to step up your game.. a lot of competition out there.. 

Very very disappointed!  Worse Cheesesteak ever... I heard Sonny's was better then Pat's and Geno's But the best Cheesesteak I have ever had is Junior in Verona, NJ.

For me, this place is perfect for a quick, affordable lunch break. I didn't have the chance to try their poké bowls, but all their prepared foods are fresh. They have the best 5.50+tx deal for the salmon and avocado roll on a daily basis. It's cheap compared to other places. They provide excellent customer service even if you're only buying their prepared foods.

This place.. Ijust had to take a deep breath because it's just horrible. I meant to write a review months ago when I first experienced the horrible serve but it was my birthday  lol Luckily those people are no longer there. I went back with a friend recently ..the first experience was enough to stomach so I just sat and waited. The 1st time I went they were rude, unprofessional.. manager included. They were talking about things they hated about customers. My fiancee was HOT. He wanted to say something but I said no because they still had our food. More recently there were new people.. friendly, polite but they have no idea what they are doing. The line was SO long...to the door long. It was bad. Understaffed maybe. Not to mention that they give the smallest pieces of chicken in a 3 piece. I get it. Big piece then small pieces but no.. hers were all small. We actually laughed because after 20 mins of waiting to order and 6 mins of waiting for the food .. it ended like that.  It's just always something with this place. I do not recommend at all.
At first it was a chilly day so it took away from the flavor a bit, but this place is phenomenal, make sure you know your order when going to the front. Gotta try it.

So my a-hole coworker suggested we go to HNT for lunch today instead of Boston Market.
Wish I had read the Yelp reviews ahead of time, but I agreed to try it out.
The food was tasteless, over salted and overpriced. Broccoli was not fresh, quinoa was like old oatmeal, and sweet potatoes were undercooked and hard as a rock. We had to go next door after for another meal just to clear the taste out of our mouths.
I give it till the end of February before HNT shutters.
At least I get to pick the next restaurant me and my a-hole coworker get to go to next time!

Pat's sucks. It's overrated and not even in the top 10 best cheesesteaks in Philly. The staff was rude and messed up our order. Do yourself a favor and go to the real king of steaks, Geno's across the street.

Definitely the bottom of the list for Philly Cheesesteaks! They may have been the innovators but most other places have improved upon the original. That can of Cheese Whiz sitting on the grill that they ladle over their grisly steak on a soggy roll appeals to some but I've had better. They are good at marketing and it seems as though the tourists think that Pat's is the place to go.

Visiting the city for the first time we had to stop by to do the taste test between Pats & Genos to fulfil our food network dreams. Both are farther from the city so we ended up taking a car here and in a tourist spot so parking isn't the most ideal. I'd recommend some other type of public transportation if you want to get to the area. 

As for when we arrived Pats is a simple place with picnic tables outside where you will enjoy your meal. We ended up getting two cheesesteaks - one with wiz and the other with American to test out the different options. Fresh & hot I enjoyed the meat portion that came with Pat's subs. Since the meat was a little more chopped up it allowed the cheese to flow in between the crevices of the cheesesteak. Was it extraordinary? Not really but for a tourist spot it was filling and was a size we were able to share between our group. Thoroughly enjoyed the wiz option over the American so might need to add that to my future orders.

I am starting my review while standing in a line that is in the middle of the street (no one said tourist were smart). I've been here before and I'm proud to say I'm a Pat's Guy. Years ago I did my own taste test of Pat's vs Geno's and I liked Pat's better.  Geno's location is too flashy and clean for me. I know Geno is not hurting because the end of his line is also in the middle of street almost touching Pat's. Yes there is a lot of horn honking from the angry Sunday Drivers!!!

There is so much action here.  I waited in line and ordered my sandwich with ease...10 years ago when I first ordered a sandwich I was so nervous because there is a warning that says if you screw up you go to the back of line.  And I did not want that to happen.

I ordered my sandwich...Wiz Cheese Steak with Onions...and not a problem with the counter...guy had my sandwich before I got my change...oh yeah cash only...I would love to collect the money here.  9 bucks get you one sandwich...it is probably more of a 6 buck sandwich but it has become an institution...I blame those damn food network shows for driving the price up and people here.

Pat's keep up the good work and remember you are an institution...never for get that!!!

Wow! Simply the worst food accompanied by the worst service and most disgusting rotten old juice used in passion fruit margarita I've ever experienced. Stale chips followed by cold shit soup. If I can't drink something containing alcohol its worse than the taste of a burnt peppered asshole! I'm still nauseated......yuck! Stay away from this one!!!!!!

Because it's been around for so long, Pat's earns its business through its rich heritage, earning it a culture of its own. Because of its big name and the story of its rivalry with the place across it, Pat's draws patrons from different corners of the globe including those from the City of Brotherly Love. As a result of a huge volume of business that usually results in long lines, it earns a reputation from its utilitarian service. 

To streamline ordering, Pat's has two different areas for ordering, one exclusively for sandwiches, and the other is for fries and drinks. There's an area where you can load up on condiments, such as pepper and ketchup. They do not give you any napkins, even though there is a fresh stack of napkins clearly behind the window. They expect you therefore to get them yourself. 

They also expect you to know the proper lingo in order to order a steak. There's a sign by the front that tells you how to order a steak there. It includes a warning that if you mess your order, you're obliged to head to the end of the line to try all over again. If you want a cheesesteak, you're supposed to state what type of cheese you want. You're getting a choice of provolone, Cheese Whiz, American. Don't be fancy and attempt to order Swiss, feta cheese, camembert, or roquefort. Next, you're given a choice of onions (wit) or without onions (witout). Mushrooms are 50 cents extra after tax.

Even when we arrived at 10am when there were no lines, they expected us to get up to speed with what's going on. Know the lingo. Know where things were. 

I ordered a mushroom provolone wit (mushroom cheesesteak with provolone and onions) for $10.50. After I placed my order, my meal was ready in less than a minute. That was how quick the whole thing was. The bread came a little soggy, but the steak was pretty good. They chop the steak here and serve it with cheese. If you want sliced meat, you should go to Geno's. 

In my previous times of visiting Philadelphia, I never went to either Pat's or Geno's, knowing of the lines. But because it was Crystal's first time, we decided to go. We came here for the experience, but I can say surely that there are other places to have lunch (or a cheesesteak) aside from the two joints on Passayunk Avenue.

A must stop if you are in Philly. Pat's King of Steaks and their rival (across the street) have had a long running competition of who is best.

I was lucky when I came here that there wasn't too much of a crowd. Make sure you know how to order before you get to the front of the line.

The food is ready fast so be prepared for a delicious cheesesteak and a good sized portion.

I also went across the street to try the other guys. I can tell you....I am a Pat's guy. 

They were both good, but I would vote Pat's.

Quick, easy option at the Philadelphia airport. Wasn't too busy around 5:30 pm, so I was able to order and get my food within 5 minutes. Quality was good as any other Chick-Fil-A, just a bit over priced as expected for an airport.

It was 2009 when I went. 2:30 am after clubbing. Was with several friends. I am from Oregon and Philadelphia was quite an experience.
