As we waited forever in line, it was worth it. And the entertainment we witnessed was crazy. This poor fella was sitting in his Mercedes eating his cheesesteak, right next to the window. And these guys were just harassing him. One had the audacity to whip his penis out and rub it in the guys window. Mind blown. And not a cop around. Driver just kept eating his cheesesteak. 

I went to Genoa's across the street two days later before I flew back to Portland. 

Both places are equally badass.
If this is what cheesesteaks are supposed to taste like, I am NOT a fan. The meat was tough, chewy and flavorless, the cheese was gross and the bread was hard to chew. Overall, just not good.

Will never go back. The customer service I received was so poor. The sandwich was dry and flavorless. Go to Geno's across the street. Better service better taste! And to the man at the counter, just a reminder I'm the customer, you better get that attitude and wipe it off your face at the window. You don't talk to me the customer like I'm an idiot and start yelling how to form a line and then yell out next means who's up next to order a sandwich. As the customer we pay your bills and make you rich and by the look of it Geno's line pisses all over your line. There was no line to form because no one was on it. You work so fast you don't even know how to properly wrap the sandwich never mind put it in a bag. Your business should be embarrassed.
Never disappointing even after years- wish the normal cheesesteak comes with more cheese. Not the best way to represent the legacy for the visitors.

It's not like it used to. It gave me too little meat and was disappointed with my husband and me.
I've been driving three hours in New York This is not really the meat is much smaller!! 


It's not the taste I always expected. They're saving meat!! 
-.,-

Wins the cheesesteak challenge every time. 

We brought my niece to try the famous Pats and Genos and it was delicious as always. There was so much wiz it was all over us by the time
We were done but so worth it!

Outside seating is available and there is a pepper bar to spruce up your steak.

Every time I come to South Philly McDonald's one of two things happens:

1. They reconfirm my order incorrectly at the 1st window
2. They try to give me the wrong order at the 2nd window

It's even more hilarious when both things happen. I still keep coming back though.

When I came here for the first time I realized just how delicious a cheesesteak sandwichcan really be. I had their classic cheesesteak "wit wiz " , my fave ! I'm not the biggest cheesesteak lover,  but this one was one for the books.  Although I must say that my first time versus my second time here was a little different, I noticed that the meat was not as tasty vs my first time here , but still very tasty ! Will always stop by here when I go to Philly !
Less ugly then Geno's. Better wiz. Will only go if it's 3am and I'm drunk. Still just a damn sandwich. Go somewhere else if it's a normal hour of the day.

The original rivalry - Pat's vs Geno's. I stopped at both one night to do a side by side comparison of the two. And Pat's came out the winner. 

The main difference in the two sandwiches is the steak. Pat's chops their steaks up and then pours the cheese on top and then the toppings. So everything melds together and it's great. Geno's has a slab of meat that they then pour everything on top - and it's just not as good. So if you find yourself between the two one day and the lines are about the same - I'd go for Pat's.

One complaint I have, and this is probably about Philly and/or cheesesteaks in general. The term 'wit' sounds a lot like the word 'whiz'. So if you're trying to get a cheesesteak with whiz only, it's possible that you will wind up 'wit' which means "add onions to my sandwich, please." And anyone who knows me knows that phrase will never come out of my mouth - ever. So I wound up going home with a whiz wit, instead of a whiz witout. Not the end of the world, I was able to scrape the onions off, but I feel like I sacrificed some whiz in the process and therefore didn't get the full effect. 

Even so, even with the order snafu, Pat's won out over Geno's.

Worth trying once because it's an iconic Philly place, but I wouldn't go back again. We ordered 3 cheesesteaks. 

Bread: too chewy and hard to eat, especially with the equally chewy meat.
Meat: really grisly, tough, chewy
Whiz: bland

The cheesesteaks were good but not great. We then walked across the street to Geno's and ordered the exact same thing. Geno's is SO MUCH BETTER. I'm writing a review on Geno's now...

Pat's vs Geno's a tale as old as time a song as old as rhyme. My wife and I visited both these fine establishments got one cheesesteak from each and then cut them in half and split them so we could decide which was better unfortunately we forgot which half was from which cheesesteakaria and thus kuldnt come to a final decision. We were going to try to get too more steaks but trust me we were FULL. Whichever half was Pat's was very good 4 sure.

Y'all can't read.   :D
Not to mention the attitude from staff...
Seriously, don't constantly screw up orders then act like the customer is inconveniencing you by asking you (politely) to fix it.

Disgusting, greasy, fake, Tex-Mex, wannabe, bland, dirty, roach infested establishment. With so many other great authentic Mexican restaurants in the area with byob, stay away from this overpriced selection of lard based dog food!

I walked to the Cantina from center city one hot summer, a friend and I ate and shared a pitcher of the cucumber jalapeno margarita ouside.  It was incredible.  Later that year I took some friends there after talking up this same drink.  After trying it they were not disappointed.  Aside from the outrageous wait, grungy waitstaff, loud atmosphere, and lack of convincing atmosphere, the Cantina is a place I'd definitely take friends again.  Lastly, the burritos are huge!

Many of my friends recommended this place and Its so simple, and so right. You walk up to the counter; order your sandwich and hand It right back to you. The other side is for fries and drinks. 

The fries were so good that I went back to get a second one. I also made a 20 minute detour on the way to the airport to grab another one on my way out.
Good cheese steak but not great. It was really messy for me, steak was bland, cheese was bland, bread was average. I had to add mushrooms to make it intresting.   Tip: cash only

Brought some out of town friends to see "a philly establishment". Walked away disappointed and embarrassed. The staff bullied a young family that asked for no bread and just steak (their son was allergic to bread). The plump little man and his odd looking staff didn't hesitate to call the family as$holes and tell them to move along. I thought that was the worst of it. The worst was the 3rd world fast-good quality meat and flavorless cheese. This "establishment" wouldn't last a month in any other city, but for some reason Philly enjoys being stuck in the mud, held back by swamp rats with faded tattoos, flipping pisspoor processed meats. I'll be having a roast beef at Cherry Street next time..

This definitely seems like a very touristy place, so you can expect long lines! But the service is fast, so the line moves quickly!

Get ready for some greasy goodness! The Philly way of eating the cheesesteak is with Cheese Whiz, which my not sound very appetizing, but I promise it's good! And for those who like eating it the good old fashioned way without Cheese Whiz, you can go for that too! But don't forget to order a side of fries and a drink! Just don't count your calories afterward.

This place is a legend, and actually preceded neighboring Geno's.  So it's 'the original.'

And it's a darn good cheesesteak, it really is.  And it's big.  Get it wit cheese whiz, don't get one of the other cheeses. 

We had to get a cheeseteak because we were in Philly, but the real winner was the neighboring bar where you could BYOC (Bring Your Own Cheesesteak) and have a craft beer.  No restrooms at Pat's or Geno's so it's a great place for that too. 

In summary, it's a touristy spot you kinda have to go to at some point if you've never been to Philly.

Fast moving great food.    Line was semi long but really moved fast. One window for just ordering cheesesteaks and the next window to order fries and drinks.   Guy at the second window is very hard to understand and when another customer didn't get the right change back the guy didn't understand what he was asking.   Quite pricey but for once in an extreme blue moon what the heck. 

I got the Cheesesteak 'wit' onions and cheese whiz.  Love how it's not slabs of meat and instead more chopped.   Pretty greasy but delicious. Fries I could have done without.   Wasn't a big fan of them. Overall great experience.

Just ate my first cheesesteaks ever for a Philadelphia Fourth of July visit with some friends, and we decided there was nowhere better to start than with a Pat's and Geno's sampler.

The rivalry lived up to it's name, as the two places are directly across form each other. 

Between four of us, we split up and got a Wiz Wit and Wiz Witout from each place.  Pat's was noticably faster service (by about two minutes of waiting time) from end-of-line to steak-in-hand.  I will admit that I was partial to Geno's taste when all was said and done, but Pat's cheesesteaks were just fine and tastey. 

For parking, we cheated a bit and stopped in at the ample Acme lot a block or so down, which worked great.

I don't know if this is HNT's standard business model but my experience was awful. I wanted to try HNT and wait 20 minutes in the drive thru  only to get up the ordering board to be told it would be a 15 minutes wait for 12 classic tenders meal and this was at 12:30 PM lunch hour. If you can't get your act together you're not going to be around for long.
#pitiful

I've had multiple orders from this place.  Tbh I'd give the food 4 of 5 for what it is but I give a huge premium on their service and that the operate so late.  Let's be frank, they cater to drunks etc, prob the hardest market to appease.  If you are coherent enough to place an order and answer your phone you're gonna have a good time.

Delicious, but, and please don't kill me, I liked Tony Luke's better.

This place is super fast.  When you get to the front of the line it takes maybe 5 seconds after you order for them to shoot out your sandwich.  Therefore, even if the line looks long, it moves fast.

They have a sign showing you how to order the cheesesteak.  I got mine with American cheese and wit (meaning with onions).  I should have tried the cheese wiz.  

Even though it was in the high 90s and all the seating is outside, all the tables were still full.  Therefore, we had to creepily stand by tables until someone left.

The only reason I liked Tony Luke's better, is they melt their cheese.  Even though this sandwich was really good, it would have been better with melted cheese.

Pats and Geno's are both a waste of money.... There's nothing special about a guy putting an unseasoned, overcooked, and overpriced piece of meat on a roll and tossing it in the customers direction...

Hummmm what can I say about my 1st experience about the Infamous Geno's & Pat's (unfortunately you can't speak about one without speaking about the other [it not my fault yall set up that way] so please note that my comments will be the exact same on Geno's yelp page) 

Well my wife and arrive in Philly about 11ish and this was our first stop.....1st time in Philly why not stop at the Infamous "Tourist Trap - Pat & Geno's (I'm starting to think they should squash the rivalry and just combine the two...it's not like they both are any better then the other).....Ok I'm getting ahead of myself. 

So we find parking (and yes we had to search near and far to park) after finding a parking spot over and around the Mulberry bush we then walked several blocks till we found ourselves in the crossfire of the two PAT'S & GENO'S..... My wife and I came up with a game -plan she would get a Cheese Steaks from Pat's and I would get one from Geno's and we would see who's the best. 
After standing in line for about 20 min a piece we met back up in the middle of the street (because I overheard some folks saying that the two places do not allow each others food and products over in their respective areas) A bunch a nonsense if you ask me...... 

So in the middle of the street on top of a mail box we have the two Cheese Steaks sitting there side by side....I take half of the Geno's and my wife takes half of Pat's so we bite into each half expecting and thinking that we are about to taste heaven itself...........WOMP WOMP WOMP!!!!!!!!!!!!! A total disappointment..... 

In my mind I was thinking..."if this is the best that Philly has to offer then Philly may want to rethink what food they want to add there name too." 

Pat's & Geno's both: 
- Had VERY bland Cheese Steaks (hardly NO flavor to either one) 
- Not enough Steak 
- Very rude (as if I the customer owe them something in addition to my 8 dollars) I have never met a group of individuals that have a well-known establishment treat and look at there customers as if they are mad that we choose to stop here. 

Bottom line....coming to Pat & Geno's was worth the trip here ONLY to say that I have been there but the food is not worth bragging about or even coming back too if I am in desperate need or craving for a true Philly Cheese Steak. 

Too conclude or trip in Philly 8 hours later....I called a buddy of mine who is a Native Philly Residents and he informed me about a spot in North Philly called "Paganos".....we stop here on our way leaving Philly and if you want to know the rest about this GOD SENT PLACE....then you have to read about its page.

http://www.yelp.com/biz/paganos-steaks-and-hoagies-philadelphia#hrid:PLWl2w8WgwYOueR_A2hXrQ

Horrible ! From customer service to listening skills to food ! The girl that took the order through the drive thru was SO RUDE .. has an attitude off rip.. she messes up , walks away , manager comes .. " fixes " it STILL WRONG 
SERVICE SUCKSSSSSS DONT APPLY TO WHERE YOU DONT WANT TO WORK :)

Night owl fast food is a rip off, I ordered food online and they took my money and never delivered. This place should be avoided no matter what. If you get the late night munchies you would it would be more satisfactory to deep fry your own shoe and eat it. This establishment makes me wish zero stars was an option.

I have been meaning to post a review on this establishment for some time now. The delay is attributed to the fact that the food would smell and look so good that I would forget to take pictures. 

Shon has an awesome establishment that provides the best of both worlds, catering to vegan and non-vegan. I have previously ordered the vegan salmon with vegan mac and cheese as well as the fried vegan shrimp with bang bang sauce, which was great! I have also tried the vegan party wings and the vegan chicken po boy. 

Today, I ordered 3 vegan shrimp tacos on a soft shell along with 3 vegan ground beef tacos with the toppings on the side. I also ordered the vegan chix steak and had the pleasure of trying the navy been soup . 

Shon has mastered versatility in regards to her range of dishes. This establishment provides large portions and is full of amazing flavors while also being cost effective. In addition to the food, the positive energy keeps making you want to come back!

I ordered food here for pickup based on reviews on Main Line page.  I actually ended up driving for 30 extra minutes because I got lost.  Yet, my 3 yo super picky underweight boy ate some of the chicken and shrimp burger.  He is so picky he doesn't eat McDonald's or Wendy's.  While eating, he said "this food is yummy."  So, I'm going to have to move closer....sorry no pics because we gobbled up the food.  As a side note, I did spicy mayo on the side for both burgers and that ended up being perfect because I don't like my food too saucy.  I used the spicy mayo for my fries.

I usually don't indulge in a big lunch but the pictures looked so good I just had to try it My friend got crispy chicken wrap and I got the crispy chicken bowl. Absolutely amazing. Great taste and crunch with just the right amount of spice. Easy to find and easy to park. We will definitely be back.

I've been here one too many times because it's a classic. Getting a wiz wit (for non philly ppl, it means whiz cheesesteak with onions) is my late night munchies addiction. Depending on when you get here, lines will be long enough where you'll get close to the street, then it could be completely empty. Normally if it's a game day or late at night when the after party dwellers go, this place becomes a mad house. I'd give it a try to say you've been here and given it a try. Would I say it's the best in the city? Prob not, but it's just like saying who visits NYC and doesn't try a slice of $1 buck pizza? Again, prob not the best but you get that flavor of the city and that's something you won't forget.

Been there on a couple of occasions, and like what natives of the area say, it is a tourist trap. I am not a native of the area, but a tourist; therefore, I went there. My first trip there was in 2007 and I took the bus from Center City on my way to the Phillies game, and I missed my stop and had to walk a few blocks in an area that I had never been in before. When I finally made it there, I perused the menu and got a cheesesteak wit, All in all, it was good; however, there are better in the area that I have been to in Philly.

I'm driving down to Florida and had to stop by. It has been years since I was here. Basically the same. Nothing to write home about. Your basic cheesesteak. Nothing great. Nothing bad. Basic. After I started eating it I went back to the window and purchased a side of pizza sauce & sliced provolone to add to it. It kicked the flavor profile up a bit. Better than I started with. Good for a Sunday late night 1:00 a.m. snack. It did its job.

Hey. It's PAT'S. What do you want? One of the things I miss and crave the most from home, and one of my guaranteed stops when I'm home for a visit.

As many have mentioned, it's right across the street from Genos, and those of us from Philly are pretty loyal to one or the other. For me, Pat's steaks are just more flavorful, better made and more delicious. I also think their fries are better. And they serve Coke. And, when you look at the two businesses, it should be apparent which one is better. Genos must need all that neon for a reason. #Justsayin.

One note to all of the reviews about rude behavior: It's part of the thing. Call it ambiance or whatever, it's part of the experience of getting a cheesesteak in South Philly. At Pat's you are expected to be ready to order, to know HOW to order and to not hold the line up. If you can do those three things, you will get what you ordered lickety split and enjoy a delicious meal. It aint fancy, but it's not supposed to be. If you don't like it, go to the Four Seasons and leave the rest of us alone.

If you are new or just visiting and are nervous, that's understandable. We're not unreasonable. So ask the people around you while you wait in line. Or follow my handy guide for newbies...

1. There are TWO lines. One for cheesesteaks and one for fries/sodas. You can't get fries in the cheesesteak line. You can't get steaks in the fries line. It is best to bring at least two people. The cheesesteak line is almost always longer, so the person in charge of fry ordering should wait until their partner is fairly well along in the cheesesteak line before stepping up to the window so that you both come out with food at the same time. 

2. Fries. You can and should get cheese fries. They are drenched in Cheez Wiz and are AWESOME.... the type you have to eat with a fork and the type where there's a big pool of cheese down in the bottom of the cup.

3. CASH only. Don't ask about credit cards. You'll look stupid. Like the Soup Nazi on Seinfeld, it's best to have your cash out when you order.

4. Ordering. Do it right. They have gotten a bit more lenient in recent years, but there was a time in which a bad orderer would be sent to the back of the line. You say two words and two words only: the type of cheese followed by WIT or WITOUT (ie, with or without fried onions). Yes, you can get other cheese and other stuff but I highly recommend Wiz Wit for your first time out (see next point below). The only other words you need are numbers (as in "TWO Wiz Wits").

5. Wanna be branded as an outsider? Order something other than Wiz on your steak. Yes, there are other cheese options, but orders with Provolone are like announcing you're not from around here. You traveled all the way to an odd corner in South Philly to sample a REAL Philly cheesesteak. So suck it up and order a REAL steak -- WIZ WIT is all you need to say.

6. Tables. Red picnic tables line the sidewalk all the way around Pat's. Ideally you should bring a third person whose job it will be to troll the area for an available table and snag it while your other two people do the line thing in point #1. I've gone to Pat's at all hours of the day -- steaks for midnight snacks, steaks for breakfast, and it's extremely rare to go there and find a bunch of empty tables. At the very best, it's not jam-packed. So having a table scout can pay off big time during busy times.

7. Parking. Pat's and Genos are located pretty much right in the middle of a neighborhood, separated by a neighborhood baseball field. The only option is street parking. It's tight and hard to find sometimes. If you suck at parallel parking, bring someone who knows what they're doing. Not the place for rookies. Or take a cab from a safer locale.

That's it! Good luck and happy cheesesteak!!!

Most overrated subs I have ever had.  Fake cheese, hot dog rolls and more fat on the beef than actual meat.  Their sub is perfect match with the city Pats is located, Philadelphia, disgusting and gross.

You may or may not get what you ordered but it's MickieDees. Ordered a quarter pounder got a Big Mac. Fries are always hot so that alone may seal the deal if considering this newly renovated, slot machine of an otherwise typically predictable fast-food chain.

I haven't had five guys in forever. I am gluten free so struggle a bit with quick service and fast food options. Five Guys however didn't disappoint, I got a bacon cheese burger wrapped in lettuce and the best part of my order was that the fries are not cooked in a cross gluten fryer. A greasy delicious treat close to my Philly apartment.  

We did curbside pickup during the pandemic, they have an app you can order from. It's very easy and fast. Food was hot and service was great.
Their sticky buns are amazing. The danishes were made fresh and they were so sweet. Great customer service.

- The portion so small compared with price
- Chicken very hard n salty breaded so thick , not fresh cooking 
- I ordered Bowl meal , the rice heated with microwave, vegetables so old, just 4 piece bite chicken n the chicken was old, hard , salty n just taste like fried dough.
- not providing with any sauce even ketchup, so I ask hot sauces n chipotle sauce n they ask me to pay for $2.14 for the sauces.
- stay away from this restaurant they selling old food and better go to Popeyes chicken just inside Philadelphia Mills (about a cross the street) fresh chicken n good sandwich n you don't need to pay for the sauces

Truthfully, this was my first time ever at a Chick-fil-A and it had to be inside an airport.  The prices were inflated but that was expected.

I wasn't too hungry though at the time, so I didn't order any of their sandwiches.  Instead, I opted to try their Nuggets.  I thought they were pretty tasty, though a little bit on the small side compared to other fast food nuggets.  I like the sauce options like buffalo sauce, bbq sauce, ranch, honey mustard, Polynesian, and their special Chick-fil-A sauce.  I opted for the buffalo sauce and it went well with the Nuggets.  I probably should've gone with the Chick-fil-A sauce though.  Maybe next time.

So my first Chick-fil-A experience wasn't too bad.  The Nuggets were good but weren't much to get excited about.  I'll have to try their sandwiches next time to give a fair review.  For now, it was just A-okay!

Took a spontaneous trip to Philly with the parents today. We were between this one and Genos. Never really had many cheesesteaks, but i ordered one from here. Overall, not too bad. Taste was good and bread was good. I feel like maybe it lacked a little bit of flavor? But that could be just me. Overall good experience and fast service.

I normally would have given a higher rating, but I had a horrible experience yesterday.  I have already contacted corporate.  I eat here at least once a week.  Yesterday it was about 3:30, and I was eating and suddenly the room reeked of cigarette smoke and got really cold.  I look to the door, and 2 customers are standing IN the doorway smoking cigarettes, blowing the smoke outside but standing IN the restaurant smoking.  An employee was right next to me emptying trash and I asked her to please say something to the customers.  I only have partial hearing and she mumbled something and I didn't hear her, and then she just simply walked away and continued to collect the trash and let the customers smoke in the doorway.  That was incredibly unacceptable.  I tried to call the restaurant just now to speak to the manager and the line was busy so hopefully I'll get through later or I'll just stop by.

No no no no no no no. No.

I remember the first time I went to Pat's and Geno's during Spring Break (this is before I discovered Yelp); my friend and I were coming from Myrtle Beach,SC to Brooklyn, NY and decided to stop here for a 'midnight snack'. I ordered a cheese steak with provolone from Pat's and one with Cheese Whiz from Geno's, onions in both. After eating both of them , I decided that Geno's is the King of Steaks and doused my friend with his soda as an official declaration . Okay that didn't happen, but I was thinking it.

Enough reminiscing, though. It has been nearly six months and Caleb P. is back in Philadelphia and it's official: the only thing keeping Pat's and Geno's alive is pure publicity. 

The simple fact is this: These two places serve the most delicious cheese steaks ever made. Delicious? Actually, a better word would be: horrendous, disgusting, grotesque, disturbing. Rather, any combination of the previously listed words would be more appropriate than 'delicious'.

After coming here the second time, I realize that the Cheese Whiz masks how poor this cheese steak is. Order everything and have provolone instead of Cheese Whiz and you will discover how unbelievably tough, dry, and lacking the meat is. I won't say any more, rather I will let you find out yourself.

The thing is about Geno's and Pat's is summarized in the last sentence of the previous paragraph: "....rather I will let you find out yourself." I can continue on how tough the meat is, how limp the bread is, or how overcooked the onions are. I can rant, throw a tantrum, scream to the world, but that won't stop anyone. Curiosity and skepticism will continue to bring wave upon wave of people to these joints and nothing will stop them. Their popularity has reached Paris Hilton-esque proportions where any publicity is good publicity.

What bothers me is the fact that people differentiate Pat's and Geno's as two separate entities, when it is clear that they both are equal establishments. What angers me the most is that Pat's and Geno's are famous for how delicious their cheese steaks are rather than notorious for how atrociously terrible they really are. 

$7.50 for this? You must be joking. I rather have my tongue cut off.
Likely one of the worst run restaurants of any kind, anywhere. Beyond slow, nobody cares about anything. Place will be out of business soon or change owners. Pathetic.

Tried Pat's while in Philly and loved the cheese steak! Close to Geno's in the type of sandwich (not as oily and the bread is less carved out). The bread was fresh, meat tasty and we loaded it up with extras from the condiments section. Its a cash only place! Must try when in Philly!

I'm a philly native so I know to stay away from places like this. But also as a Philly native, I decided to finally give them a shot. I ordered twice two weekends in a row. I feel as though there was an inconsistency with both orders. The first time, the roll and whiz were fine for the most part but the sirloin was too chewy.  The second time, the provolone wasn't even melted and the role was spongy and drippy having absorbed so much grease. There was a layer of grease covering the inside of the wrappper as I removed the sandwich.  There was no flavor to the sandwich at all. Both times I walked away disappointed. There was no magic invloved in the making. 

The experience left a lot to be desired. Management needs to step up its game. 

I wouldn't recommend Pat's to anyone and likely wont be going there again unless I hear there's new and improved management.

Had an amazing experience at this Blaze Pizza. First off, the company structure is brilliant. Personal pizza sizes only for the right demographic (i.e. college campus). Your team here are all quality people and you're lucky to have these employees: Bria, Liz, Beth, Tara, Lil, Caleb, & Jaida. I'm sure every employee here is phenomenal, but these were the people I had the pleasure of speaking with.

I was forced to come here when i could no longer get dominoes, papa johns etc. I was a fan of little caesars as a kid, but its just not my style pizza anymore. They possibly have something new on their menu. But, the crust/dough is very below basic, and the cheese and sauce is average.

Always a little more expensive in the airport! The serving size is smaller too. The employees are nice not much interaction it always fast pace due to long lines.

I ordered salad bowl, no rice, half steak and chicken , cheese and medium sauce. It was keto friendly and delicious!

I love Five Guys. It's the best burger in town, by a mile. This location has friendly staff and timely service. It is also filthy, the bathrooms are never clean and don't have a baby station, tiles are missing all over the floor, it is dark and always looks closed, and basic cleaning looks neglected.
Given the reviews, I thought this place was going to be pretty bad, but honestly would say that it's a pretty solid Philly cheesteak.

Hours make absolutely no sense. Google and yelp say This location is open 24 hours. Went to the door, and it was locked. Read the hours on the door which said "inside closes at 11. Drive through 24 hours" on Monday. It was 10:15 when I arrived. 
I then went through the drive thru and was told "we're closed" 4 cars followed after me. 
Why do i feel as though these employees falsely close early just so they can stop working ?

This is a fun distraction for tourists who are interested in checking the sites and taking photographs of cheesesteak rivalry. However, if you're looking for high quality cheese steaks, I'd look elsewhere. The steak at Pat's is dull, borderline soggy and not much different than a cafeteria meat. The bread was also dry and flaky, but all in the wrong way. If you like good steak or roast pork, try John's Roast pork for award winning sandwiches.

I love chick fil a and go pretty much every chance i get, this location was the WORST service i have ever received from the company. The service was rude and messed up our order and didn't even try to fix it. The "my pleasure" was no where near the picture but not even close to the biggest problem.

Pats is ok. Generous amount of steak which has good flavor. Bread bun is good.
This place is always busy so seating is on a first come basis. 
Not much else to say really.
Great time. No lines today. Can never go wrong with a WIT WHIZ. Now I'm in a cheesesteak coma.

Pat's King of Steak or their rival, Geno's Steak? Each across the street from one another, I had both and the consensus with my two other companions made this one a clear cut WINNER!! The super tender and juicy steak is more chopped up. We added mushrooms, onions, green peppers and provolone. For me, the green peppers and the chopped steak did it for me. I also think the steak was a bit more juicier than the one at Geno's.

I think it's just a matter of preference. Both of these places deserves to be named Best Philly Cheesesteaks. How else would you explain people coming from around the world just to try it. It's been in many Food Network's shows. 

Come, enjoy and judge for yourself. It's worth a visit in the heart of Philadelphia.

This is a very poorly run location where they care very little about their customers or about the service I came to the window of the drive-through and waited for 10 minutes before someone could say anything to me I repeatedly said hello and no one answered until finally someone said wait as I ordered I asked for my meal and along with it I wanted nuggets for my babies in the car and they said we don't have any nuggets as I drove off I saw that they had chicken tenders and all I respectfully did was ask can I please have chicken tenders instead I saw that you guys offer that she said you have to either get out of the car come inside or go back around which there was a very long line due to the fact.She said I couldn't edit my order after I came to the window and did not wish to be flexible in terms of simply making me a new order for just the tenders person was very aggressive with me and I was in a very docile manner in which I did not irritate nor did I raise my voice I've been there before and the food was always so so anyways I do not recommend going there if you do not wish to deal with rude behaviors and poor quality foods the door to the back was open and trash was present Today is Tuesday ninth of June at 6:20 PM 2020

We tried both Pat's and Geno's side by side, and they were both quite tasty. I ordered a mushroom cheesesteak whiz wit. I loved that it was super cheesy, the onions were cooked a bit more, and that they loaded it up with (canned) mushrooms. I don't mind the mushrooms being from a can, but I would have liked them to been grilled. The bread is a bit soft, which makes for a messy eating experience. Please be aware that it is cash only. There is an ATM across the street, but it's a $3 fee. I'm sure there are better and cheaper cheesesteaks in Philly, but we had to try the touristy places first.

I'm FURIOUS.

I stood in line for HALF AN HOUR. Literally using up my whole break, and there were only 2 people in front of ey when I got there. Their service is TERRIBLE. 

T E R R I B L E.

They just stopped taking orders for about 15 minutes and allowed the line to reach all the way out the door. 

When someone FINALLY took my order, I got my drink but there was no ice. I asked for a refund. It is over 90 degrees outside I'm NOT paying for a hot drink. Then when the employee told her manager I wanted a refund, she refused to give it to me, she instead sent the young lady to the back with my cup and she came back with maybe 4 ice cubes in my cup. ARE YOU SERIOUS? At this point I don't have time to refute the issue, I have to go back to work being that my whole break is now taken up. 

On my drive back I reach in my bag to eat some fries. 

THEY'RE FREAKING COLD!!!!!!!!  The chicken tenders are also COLD!!!!! I open my Mac and cheese, and they barely filled it up! 

I will NEVVEERRRR ORDER FROM HERE AGAIN! They need a regional to take over that place immediately !

When I first dined here I was so confused at the 3 stars they had. But after dining here a few times it makes sense. I was brought here by a friend over 2 years ago. I got the carnitas tacos and they were phenomenal. Honestly some of the best I've had and I've been to Mexico several times. The margaritas were also great the passion fruit, guava and when in season the watermelon being my faves. The service was great and the complimentary chips and salsa didn't hurt. 

I was happy to make Cantina apart of my weekly rotation from that initial experiences. However fast forward to 2 years later and tonight has solidified it for me; IM NEVER GOING BACK. So over the 2 years I've been coming here consistency has been the biggest problem. At times I would get the carnitas tacos and it would be dried out  and bland. The guacamole all too often lacks salt and the margaritas are hit or miss. Now margaritas I can definitely blame the bartenders. Some are better than others. Some bartenders put way too much sour mix or not enough of the fruit purée and yes even sometimes too much tequila and the drink isn't balanced. 

In addition to the carnitas tacos I absolutely loved the garlic shrimp. The sauce it comes in reminds me of the broth you get when you order mussels (shallots, garlic,white wine a little lemon for acidity). It's absolutely divine and they give you grilled bread with it. I always order extra bread and I ALWAYS don't stop until every drop of that broth is gone. But sadly they even ruined that for me. The coconut shrimp is good very similar to the ones from red lobster.

I haven't came here in 3 months but I was hungry. Since they kitchen close at 1am and it was midnight and slim pickings for eating in the area, my cousin and I made our way here. We ordered garlic shrimp, carnitas and chorizo tacos. The carnitas tacos was dried out and bland and the guacamole was bland. Big surprise. I sent the garlic shrimp back. Instead of the beautiful opaque garlicky goodness I'm used to it, the bottom of the bowl was filled with oil that appeared to have burnt fresh garlic in it. The shrimp was cold and bland. The bread was cool but with no sauce to dip it in what's the point. I'm sorry I absolutely wasn't paying for that monstrosity. As if the mediocre food wasn't bad enough when I got the check I seen that we were charged $4 to add guacamole to each orders of tacos. The last time I was here it cost $1 to add guacamole to tacos. I was extremely pissed. The guacamole portion was barely enough for 1 taco let alone 3 and they had the nerve to raise the price. I also noticed that they raised the price of other things such as the introduction to tequila flight. At this point I'm over it, I heard they are other great taco spots in Philadelphia and those place shall be getting my money from now on. 

UPDATE 3/9
First 70 degree day of 2020 my boyfriend and I were in the area and he was craving a burrito and begged for us to stop in. Service was slow and inattentive. Carnitas taco portion has shrunk. Tacos were okay. Not the worse I've had here certainly not the best. From what I recall cheese always came in the burrito. Not anymore $2 up charge for cheese in a burrito. I had the passion fruit margarita he had the strawberry both were meh. The icing on the cake was us both fighting over the toilet when we got home. The only thing I had besides the food from there was a plain bagel & cream cheese for breakfast. So deduce you're own decision.  He now agrees. NEVER AGAIN.
The mozzarella sticks are good , the fries are too even tho they came with no ketchup or anything, the cheesesteak is smaller than expected & not very flavorful but it's not bad.

I don't know what all the hype is but I don't see it. The food is expensive and not spectacular. I don't know maybe I should have gone across the street to Geno's but oh well. It's also cash only and not cheap.

I actually would give this another 1/2 star for 4.5 stars.  Ate here over the Labor Day weekend.  Since I am having weight loss surgery soon, I wanted to try "authentic" philly cheese steaks from the two icons as part of my pre-surgery "bucket list".  My wife stood on line at Pat's for me while I was at Geno's.  Her line moved slightly quicker and the staff was very accommodating and let her wait for me as they took people ahead of her and then allowed us to order when I was able to get over there, without having to wait on line all over again.  I think I read reviews saying they were rude, this proved to me they are not rude.  I ordered a cheese steak wit onions, whiz and mushrooms.  All I can say is, after eating only 1/2 of the sandwich right there (had to save room for 1/2 of the Geno's for a head-to-head), it was hands down one of the best I have ever had.  I have had equal to it, outside of philly, but it only disappointed in that I had hoped it was better than what I have had before.  I only gave 4 stars (again, I'd give it 4.5 stars if I could) because I am holding out hope that there is a better cheese steak sandwich out there, but this is as good as I have had anywhere.

I going to say this, since I moved to the area I have been picking off one by one 'THE BEST PHILLY STEAK' and Pat's was the 1st to make me want one again for dinner ( I didnt) but me and my friend visiting in town mouths were watering at 8 pm  after our 2 o'clock meeting with Pat's.  This was her first 'steak' so her opinion is biased, but she definitely loved it...

I love the challenge of finding a seat in the outside eating area.  I literally watched someone dive to a table, stalk someone for their table, and just eat really close to the restaurant while sitting in the car.  My friend asked the one question...What happens in the winter time?

Pat only got 4 stars because the bed of flies on the wall while we were eating.

Love love love the coffee. They actually ask you how many cream and sugar instead of just assuming. Had to visit twice to ensure that that's actually how they take the order daily.  I was taken back by that. Getting coffee anywhere except my own kitchen 711 and occasionally Dunkin donuts. This is a whole new world to me. Lol now I'm a huge fan of the sweet tea. Nuggets leave a strange taste in our mouths. And I nearly ran some random lady over just hanging out on the curb beside the speaker. It was fine she wasn't hurt she carried on her conversation I believe with her smoke. Lol. I'd recommend. Great coffee

Saw a lot of different reviews about this place. Some on GrubHub some on here. Some just crazy. So I was hesitant on whether or not I should place an order. Glad I did. Food was made the way I asked and it arrived faster than their estimated time. When I texted to make a change it was done. They got a cool feature where they send you a text when you place an order and if you have any changes you can text that number back and they'll take care of whatever it is you're trying to add or change. Very cool. And the best part is that the food was actually really good. I expected some okay late night food but this food was actually really good. Definitely my new late-night spot.

Not entirely sure how to rate a cheesesteak since this was my first one. I just knew I couldn't leave Philly without having one.

Apparently a South Philly staple. The neighborhood reminded me so much of Brooklyn. I enjoyed the murals everywhere.

I suppose I should rate the food. There was a hefty lump of beef on some amazing bread. Can I rate this on bread alone? As good as a baguette. Asked for onions and provolone. Is that normal? Can someone tell me?

Anyway. Don't know if I just don't love cheesesteaks or this was just mediocre. Help.

Cash only.

If I come to Philly and want a cheesesteak and see this spot claiming to be the inventor and originator of it... it better stack up to the claims. And Pat's didn't do that. The service was blah. Try a little at least. They handed us the sandwich unwrapped and uncovered. This is why Geno's across the street had double the crowd. They work on their presentation, both of the locale and the food, and it goes a long way. Pat's has a better Cheesesteak than Geno's, but it takes no pride in its product. Shame.

On this same day, my friends and I tried out Larry's, Geno's, and Dalessandro's as a little ranking experiment and this was unanimously in second place, but not because it was the second best. It was simply the best of the worst. The first place went to Larry's because it has an amazing cheesesteak that far surpasses the other three we tasted, it had great presentation and neatly rolled up the cheesesteak, and the staff actually cracked a smile once in a while.

Heard all the hype and wanted to see for myself. Made sure to rehearse the order so I wouldn't be sent to the back of the line. Luckily for me there wasn't anyone else in line so they would have to deal with me either way. 

I go over to the counter with the line just o make sure I got the order down pat Wit (with onions) Wiz (with cheese whiz... Honestly can't understand why that's even an option. You BETTER get the whiz, lol). I stammer out "wit wiz" and brace for impact cause I'm not sure if they are just gruff here, or mean like Wieners Circle in Chicago. The lady says to me "you want onions on it?" AAAAAAGGGGHHHHH! I spend all this time making sure I got it PERFECT and SHE got it wrong. Oh well.

As far as the sandwich, it's pretty good. That bread is doughy and soft, yet firm so it can't rip (like Phillippe's French dip in LA). There's hot peppers, hot sauce, ketchup, relish and mustard, though I assume most of that is for other menu items. I wish they had some mayo haha! 

I'm gonna try Geno's on the way back to my Airbnb and I hear Jim's also is the shizz. So many food spots, so little time....
Not what I expected. Definitely over rated over hyped.  I prefer dellesandros, ishkabbibbles, Max's
they got rats be aware, I seen them outside eating in the trash & then running in the back door that was open

I have been going to Pat's since a little girl with my whole family. We would eat on the benches. I still go there today, although the prices have risen a lot, but the amount of steak remains the same. You have to get the hot sauce on the side.  It hott, bur good.

I've always had good experiences here, and I go here a lot. Nice employees, and the food is always good. They've made special orders for me and gone out of their way to give good customer service. Highly recommend this location!

I came here over Labor Day weekend and was just so satisfied from start to finish. My bubbly, yet focused and efficient waitress Jeanine, greeted me warmly at the door immediately upon entering, despite the restaurant being super busy. I took her margarita and burrito recommendations (the seitan burrito, wet and margarita tradicional) and was SO satisfied. Both were amazing. Go here. Request Jeanine. Have the best experience.

Yeah!!! My Cheesesteak with wiz finally came in the mail!!! I love GoldBelly. The fact I can support a local business during this nasty COVID19 is great! I got 4 Cheesesteak with onions and wiz on the side. Came nicely packed and ready to eat!!! Can't wait to have it for dinner tonight. My husband and I were there last year and damn, they were the best Cheesesteak sandwiches ever. I'm so glad they are on GoldBelly so I can order these delicious sandwiches.
I ordered two beefy crunch burritos here and they forgot to put beef in them. Incompetent workers, thanks for wasting my time and money.

this Burger King is so SLOW omg , be expected to wait 5 years for even the most simple thing you order. They are either very understaffed or just not wanting to work  at all. They always run out of something, drive thru backed up. Employees with annoying attitude.they should honestly just close this place down.

Food here is decent and those margarita specials are pretty good. I think the biggest reason why I come here is because the service is great and everyone truly goes out of their way. I go with my fellow friends and we facilitate a parent group together. Since we go with our babies, we need space for our strollers and because covid is still weird, it's perfect to be able to sit outdoors and request for heaters to be turned on! Which very good to warm us up. The staff has definitely seen us a million times and they've always been the most helpful - they once made space for us to park our strollers  
I obviously love their tortilla soup (posted a picture twice different times, haha) the seitan strips in it are tasty and go well together. Try the green chile cornbread! It's perfect!

Whenever I see a chick fil a, of course I have to stop! This place by far was the worst chick fil a, that I've ever been to. The cashier ringing me up was very rude and it was so odd that they served Pepsi instead of coke products. They had no chick fil a sauce what so ever and it was early in the morning which was off too. When I received my food the chicken in the chicken mini meal was the size of a nickel, smallest sandwiches I've ever had at chick fil a. Just all around bad.

This is the original Philly Cheese steak! I love coming up here every couple of years to get the Cheese steak wit wiz, wit pepper, and wit onion.  Their fries are really good too. Right now with Covid we didn't have to wait at all! Normally it would take 30+ minutes to get a sub. This place is a Philadelphia gem.

I live in Florida but originate from Philly. Our kids ordered cheese steaks for us shipped via UPS. I'm skeptical but they arrived and we warmed as instructed the next evening and, wow, they were really good. A bit of home enjoyed for sure, good job.

This place I would say a classic spot, you should visit while you are in Philadelphia. 
The cheesesteaks are pretty good, there are a variety of pickles like pickled cucumbers and peppers and jalapeños. 
The lines are insane though. When we were there in November it was like 40 minutes wait. But we came to this place specifically, so we waited. There were outside  tables last time, where you can eat.

Waiting for someone to have a procedure completed at Penn Medical stopped for a sandwich at this location. Being Friday in Lent opted for the Totally Tuna... very good.. all ingredients fresh & bread was fabulous... overall a good experience
The French fries are not good. They look like they have been fried for a long time. They are nothing like fresh ones.

What an absolute shitty cheesesteak! This is pure and simply a tourist trap. They are using their reputation as a way to serve mediocre, dry, tasteless meat covered in salty cheesewhiz on an okay bun. The portion is skimpy ... the price is insanely high for what you get and the staff is rude. I honestly would put this on par with Subway. Yet, each time I find myself in Philly, it's usually at a time where this is the only option for a cheesesteak and I forget how bad it was until I order it again.

The day before I ate here this time, there was a shooting outside the restaurant. While the neighborhood is MUCH improved from even 5 years ago, it's still nowhere you want to wander around in alone after dark. There are lots of scammers outside as well. Kids will come up to you asking you to buy a candy bar for their football team. You give them a buck or two and they pretty much tell you to fuck off. Don't fall for it. They'll wait until you have your wallet out after paying and then hit you up for the donation.

The parking situation is insane. I'd suggest parking in the nearby CVS lot, which is somewhat protected, and walking over if you must go here. The street parking spots are amazingly tight and most of the cars have pretty good amounts of 'battle wounds'. Even if you can parallel park like a champ, you may come out and find your car worse for the wear.

So what exactly is a cheesesteak here like? A dry, overcooked and void of seasoning or taste pile of meat. Melted cheap American cheese or orange salty Cheez Whiz. The dry roll is the best part of the sandwich but there is so few meat in it that all you'll taste is roll and melted cheese. You'll likely be full after and can walk across the street to Geno's, which is another tourist trap serving below mediocre cheesesteaks.

There are far better places in Philly to grab a cheesesteak. The local spots are likely the best ... Campos in Reading Market also does a decent one. Unless you want to say you've been here or there's no place else open, you'd likely do better in your hometown at a pizza or sub shoppe than at this tourist trap. No credit cards in 2021 as well. There's really no reason to go here other than the fact this is where people used to go in order to get a good sandwich.

I reviewed Pat's back in 2013 so I'm not sure where my review went? (so annoyed). Anyway I will re-create this review from what I remembered. Between Pat's and Genos, Pat's was better to me. The steak here is chopped a bit more so the cheese is coated around more. I liked mine with just onions and no peppers. I remember being hurried while ordering because they wanted to keep the lines moving but there was a specific way of ordering and I just kind of froze lol. Anyway I liked this cheesesteak a lot. So to me, it's Pat's all day over Genos.

I have spent the last 18 years going to Pat's. Used to live on the corner of 10th & Federal and my old neighbor worked there for years. I was loyal, sent every friend and family member that came into Philly to get a Pat's steak. After a hiatus and now being on keto, I thought a steak sans roll would keep me totally on plan. So I stop at Pats and ask for a steak no roll and the guy says he can't do that. I say you can't just put it on paper and he says "no, I'm not allowed". Big guy in the background yells "eat it off the roll". What they don't get is that you put the cheese on the roll first, by the time I unwrap the sandwich, it's impossible to even get any bites of cheese because it's totally stuck to the bread. So I tell them nevermind and I walk across the street to Geno's and ask the lady if I can get a steak no roll and she says "no problem, hon, I'll put it on paper". No snarky attitude, no "I'm not allowed to", no problems whatsoever. Considering the money I've given to Pat's over the years, to be told they can't give me a steak sans roll is ridiculous. Never again. I will never spend another cent of my hard earned money at this joint.

There was so much hype about Popeye's chicken sandwich, I had to put my 1.5 cents into the conversation. I saw the online videos and postings, so I finally had a chance to see what the fuss is about.
The last time I tried to purchase the sandwich there was a cruddy sign on the door to Popeye's saying out of chicken sandwiches. I was dumbfounded, not understanding why they couldn't have any of the most popular sandwiches to hit the market in years.
So, I chilled. 
I went to Popeye's after hearing that the coast was clear and they were saying"come and get it" Y'all come on down you hear, no cruddy signs, no long ass lines, we got 'em!
The sandwich was great, big, thick, crispy and juicy. A nice hefty sandwich with a fresh soft bun and a touch of mayo and a tangy pickle. 
I prefer their sandwich over all the rest. It was quite a wait, but it was worth it.

This breakfast, gyro and cheese steak place capitalizes on the desire for your money if you really needed a cheese steak. 

Actually it's not too bad. The foot long sandwich is filled with grilled onions and cut up steak. The sandwich could have had more cheese. The cheese was beautifully melted and married with the meat and onions. It hit the spot. I'm sure it's not the best cheese steak but its just passable and necessary if you're craving melted cheese and thin cooked slices of meat. One could share one sandwich or eat one half now and the other on the plane.


Had no issues with service. Although it wasn't that busy.

With ice tea drink and steak it came to under 10 bucks. Overall, 3.5 stars.

About an hour ago I went to this location's drive-thru & as usual was asked to pull up pass the window to wait for our food. Based on previous experiences, you don't want to do that at this location because they'll leave you waiting and forget about you. They just want to cheat their timer. So, we refused & said we'll wait at the window. The "manager" was pissed! They then hand us our bag (I verified all the things was from our order) then they asked for it back (It was missing items). She decided to leave us there & have employees go out and serve those behind us. I then see employees digging in our bag & removing items while 1 of their employees tried to block our view. We asked him why are they digging around and playing with the food. He replies the the fries are cold & they're giving us new ones but I know they were piping hot because I felt them myself. We then ask for a refund because we can see them contaminating our food. So, of course they leave us waiting. We ask for the "manager's" name but conveniently no one knows (Short, stocky, African American woman with long blondish braids passed her behind). It took us about 1/2- 45min just to get our money back because she was refusing to even come to the window. I have both purchase & refund receipts so you can see how long this whole ordeal was. DO NOT EAT HERE! THEY ARE RACHET & SERVE DIRTY HARMFUL FOOD! I guarantee corporate could pull up footage of them (A group of at least 3ppl including the "manager") contaminating our food.
This location is down the street from me but I'll gladly drive out my way to avoid this place!
Pat's was awesome! Be ready to order once you get to the window, they don't mess around! Only 4 stars because they put a TON of cheese on (if you get cheese wiz). However, it was delicious.
My favorite Mexican in all of Philadelphia.  Hands down...nuff said.

There's always a debate...Pat's or Geno's...and I'm a Pat's fan!!!  Doesn't matter how long the line is, that's the one I'll be in.  Plus if you're smart, you'll get yourself some cheese fries or a soda first THEN get in line so you don't pass out from starvation...The line for the fries/soda is separate and usually non-existent.

I usually get my cheesesteak as "provolone wit".  Make sure you know what you want and order it right, otherwise you ain't getting fed!!
Haven't taken my bf yet cuz he doesn't eat cheese...and what's a cheesesteak w.o the cheese?!?!

I always feel so nostalgic about Pat's!  It was my first cheese steak in philly when I first started traveling for work. I remember researching how to order and what to order. And it was the best experience of my traveling experience!  Fast forward to today, almost twenty years later and I still love to eat here. It's  definitely changed over the years, but still hits the spot. I will definitely be back again and again and again.

Went to Pats around 5:30 on a Saturday the line was wrapped around the block and it took approximately 24 minutes to get to the window which seems normal for the time we got there. Before the actual window there are signs to help people order which definitely is a huge help for people who don't know what's on the sandwiches. 

Once actually getting to the window it literally took 30 seconds to get the sandwiches and pay which was awesome! This place is super well organized and the cheesesteak was awesome. I would definitely recommend and absolutely don't let the wait deter you.

Pat's gets one more star than the notorious Geno's because it's slightly less xenophobic. And the owner isn't as much of an ass clown. 

Otherwise see my review for Geno's and you'll get the idea.

Early Tuesday morning on my way to work. Stopped at Mc. Donald, drive through was fast although I had to get out my car to go in. I ordered a bacon, egg and cheese and got a sausage, egg and cheese. I did hear the manager tell them that they need to get the orders out correct. Got to work to eat my breakfast and of course my bagel was hard. I also ordered a plain coffee with cream and sugar on the side. I did get cream and sugar on the side but my coffee wasn't plain. Get it together people. I still gave it a two stars but needs a lot more of team work and effort. Good luck!

Undecided on Pats vs Genos so i went with Pats. Parking was very easy and no line so i ordered and my order was ready immediately went to my car and demolished it very good so much meat and bread was very soft and fresh. When i went back to dump my trash the line was forming ai looked across the street and crickets.
Good Cheesesteak. I have had better cheesesteaks though. A good touristy place and the food wasn't horrible. a Fun place to watch all the people too.

So I was an employee at the restaurant and I have two kids of my own so they they deactivated my account because I haven't shown up to work in a while but you don't pick up the phone when I called this please do take forever the employees talk too much they talk to each other they don't know what to do with themselves they talked with a bad attitude like I'm mad because they deactivated my account and most likely I'm fired if I go in so they're terrible and then a review I give you 0 Stars

I was determined to support this black owned business last Saturday. I drove and hour to get to this restaurant. I noticed there were a  few people ahead of me and they looked like they had an attitude for waiting so long. I placed my order and they said 20-25 minutes it will be ready. 2 1/2 hours later our food was ready. Yes I said 2 1/2 hours LATER! We only ordered a Po Boy sandwich and fish hoagie with 2 slices of vegan strawberry cake. 
The people that ordered or called in before me waited around the same amount of time.  Not one apologize..... The food was just mediocre. The disorganization of the this place I would have to give one . Have coming from New Jersey and have gone out my way to support this establishment was quickly dampen by the poor customer service, disorganized service system and lack of professionalism. We can and must DO BETTER!!!! Ashe'

We all know 5 Guys. Great burgers, an OD amount of french fries, delicious shakes.....this one is no different. The location is different, though. West Chestnut Street after school lets out is.......vibrant. This is where the local teens choose to roam and kids being kids, there's a lot going on most times. I appreciate the 5 Guys Staff for working to keep the restaurant a place of business free of loitering teens and others who could ruin a fast-casual dining experience. It's the little things like their diligence that makes the difference between grabbing a quick bite there versus heading to another eatery and it's very much appreciated.

if i could give this place zero stars i would, this place did not pass my low standards. the bread was soggy, the steak was unseasoned and didn't taste like anything it was also hard to chew. there were flys everywhere and half of the time i lost interest of the sandwich because it was so bland. if you are coming to Pittsburgh as a tourist to try the "famous philly cheesesteak" try going to some better place because i would never come here again! the employees were also very rude to the customers when asking questions about the menu. this place is 
H O R R I B I L E !!!

I visited Tasty Twisters twice last week, and on both visits, none of the staff were wearing masks (despite currently being required by the City of Philadelphia for all staff and patrons). They also did not have any signage indicating a vaccine requirement.
 
On top of that, when I visited over the weekend, one of the bakers was taking a smoke break a few feet from the front door, and he was openly hostile to mask wearing, talking loudly in a belligerent manner about people wearing masks, and using profanity when referring to them. It seems like the regular customers don't even bother to mask when going in the bakery.

I don't understand how the people operating this business can condone the behavior of employees like this. I was wearing a mask and felt unsafe just standing at the counter because the baker was getting angrier and louder and cursing mask wearers. If I hadn't already paid, I would have left the bakery immediately.

A whole meal (drink, fries and a sandwich) for under five bucks. In an airport. Yes. That is correct. Sandwiches are always fresh and well made. Fries are good and crisp. Service is excellent. They have free refills too!

Pats is open 7 days a week 24 hours a day. Whenever you go there will always be someone in front of you. Always. But the line moves very fast. Let's be honest. The only reason to eat these processed cheese whiz, slimey processed "steak" sandwiches is because they are an iconic Philadelphia food. Celebrities, politicians and tourists from all over the world flock here to try either Pat's or Geno's or both.... 

The food itself? Meh. We tried Geno's, Sonny's, Lorenzo's and Pats. Pat's was the least favorite of all. 
Pats had the friendliest staff but the worst tasting meat. 

Read this about health infractions: http://m.wgal.com/news/pats-cheesesteaks-in-philly-gets-11-health-violations/37716570

That says it all.....

WORST! (Drake Voice) 

Came here at 3am on a Saturday night and waited for over 45 minutes for food. The car in front of us waited forever as well with no communication from staff. The girl at the window was visibly high on drugs and just kept joking about the car in front of us complaining about the wait. She said "Did they want a sandwich with no meat?" as if waiting this long was normal. Thennnnnn....they asked for the receipt because they had no idea what we ordered and we were the only ones in the drive thru at that point. 

When the food finally came, it was missing fries.

Very respectable brunch destination in East Passyunk. My dining companion had raved about this location for their excellent take on eggs benedict, so naturally, we had to make a weekend trip. Customary to most Mexican spots, we were immediately greeted with a basket of tortilla chips, paired with two homemade salsas (verde and rojo). The salsa verde in particular held a subtle spice and lingering flavor. I couldn't stop scooping.

As far as the main attraction, the Mexican-influenced benedict did not disappoint. I loved the jalapeno cornbread base and the chipotle hollandaise sauce drizzled on top. The poached eggs weren't too set (always a concern) and the breakfast potatoes were crisp and colorful. Well done, Cantina!

I was in this area for another event and arrived early so I stopped in and had a couple of cocktails and an appetizer, The cocktails were made very fresh, homemade drink mixes and delicious food. Kay was my bartender and very efficient, worked neatly, and was very focused on customer service. The food came out in a timely manner and was excellent. I enjoyed a seasonal special Honeydew Gaspacho and two Verano Adentro Margaritas, I am not a big margarita fan but loved these, the best I ever had! I highly recommend this place!

Pat's is known for their cheesesteaks. Get their cheesesteak with whiz cheese and onions. They're generous with their meat portions. They're thinly sliced. Only thing is ask for more cheese bc they go lightly on the cheese compared to Geno's. If you want fries, go to Geno's for better tasting fries.

I did my research before visiting Philly for the weekend.  And I knew I had to check out THE Pat's King of Steaks, the OG of the Philly Cheesesteak.  I made a list and checked it twice, I was to come here, then cross the street and try Geno's and eventually visit a few other places to triangulate the cheesesteak data.

My control sandwich at all FOUR places (that's right, I went to 4 places in two days), was a cheesesteak with whiz and onions.  Pure and simple.

Since I felt a deft sense of respect for Pat's, I wanted to like this sandwich a lot more than I actually did.  By no means was it bad or a total disappointment, but I also didn't feel like I had to travel 99 miles from New York to eat this thing.  It was good, don't get me wrong, but did it blow my socks off?  Not in the least.  And to be honest, I really WAS wearing socks.

The setup is a bit uncouth.  The sidewalk red tables and benches remind me of  Coney Island -- when it was dirtier (think back to the 90's).  The few piegons loitering around also added to that visual rendition.  The guys here don't really want to crack a smile at you, they're not exactly rude, but they also don't appear to care that you've come a long way to try their famed cheesesteak.  Whatever.  Kill my fairytale.  

If the cheesesteak itself was amazeballs, I don't care how dumpy the place, or the surrounding neighborhood was, I would have gleefully embraced it all.  But the meat was chewy, there wasn't enough whiz & onions on my steak, and it just wasn't memorable.  And we had to pay $8.00 for that.  

In my grand tally of the four cheesesteak joints we went to (Pat's, Geno's, Ishkabibble's, and Jim's Steaks), I would place Pat's tied for 3rd place.

WOW, what a hidden gem..... While riding thru S. Philly yesterday, I had come across this little breakfast place and decided to stop in...  I am glad I did.... Very small but cozy.... Had French toast and bacon with potatoes and a ice tea and  I do want to say that it was great...Friendly service and quick...  Thanx Ralph for the good conversation I had with you and explaining the history of the restaurant....  I will be back  !!

This review is hot off the press, we just received a deliver order (DoorDash) about an hour ago. I'm highly disappointed in the pizzas we got. I am a huge snap pizza fan and my coworker suggested I try blaze. Similar business model, personal pizzas with unlimited toppings for one price. I especially love this because I love toppings and paying for each gets expensive, I also love a good thin crust. Blaze just didn't do it for me, the crust is so so but what really bothers me is how stingy they are with the toppings. We didn't go over board, we did 4 & 5 and each slice was listing something. The taste overall was bare minimum. The best thing was the garlic knots, they were very good, I'd eat those again any day but the pizza won't get my money again. This was a 2.5 but the knots rounded it to a 3 star.

Got the pokebowl and matcha pudding. I like the effort they put in by adding a personalized thank you message with your name on the delivery bag. The prepackaged pudding is not my cup of tea, but I like how they include it on their menu. The pokebowl would have been perfect only if they haven't put too much onions. It overwhelmed the whole pokebowl. I still love this place.

Philly Cheese Steaks. If a city is tagged onto a food, it has to be amazing right?! When you google cheesesteaks in Philly the age old war of Genos vs Pats comes up. More blogs say Pats is best so I had to try! 

Pat's King of Steaks was a very underwhelming experience. Where do I start? There was nothing amazing about this. The unoriginal beef flavor, the average bun, the lack of seasoning. This cheesesteak started okay but tasted worse with each bite. Ive never hated meat but by the end of this sandwich I felt like throwing up a little bit. My girlfriend felt the same way to. I imagine this is food tailored for drunk college kids at 3am on a friday night. 

The amount of cheese is generous and the sandwich was the largest of any cheesesteak I ate in the city.Staff is super nice as well. Standard cheesesteak prices, about $10 but not worth it. Food is solid 1.5 but other perks bumped it up

The staff is super nice but I won't be back and don't recommend it. Unlike the name suggests, this sandwich is not king.

Food: 1.5/5
Bang:Buck ratio: 2.5/5

In my opinion the reviews are spot on for this place.  This place is full of contradictions.  It is a tourist trap, however, it is in the middle of a residential neighborhood that is full of locals.  It is the original, but has been surpassed by other places.  In my opinion, Pats is worth the visit due to the nostalgia.   To get here you have to drive thorough one way streets with cars parked on both sides of the street.  Parking is a nightmare here, no parking garages, strictly street parking.  I highly suggest you come at odd hours like we did at 10:00am, it is open for 24hrs.  We had to drive around and wait until someone moves, you have to be quick and really know how to parallel park.  Otherwise, I highly recommend taking a cab.  Near where you order is a walk of fame for Rocky Balboa where he stood.  The neighborhood is quite quaint and the art work is on the buildings is very authentic, again one of the few spots that, I have been to that draws tourists but is located in the heart of where the locals live.  

We ordered a mushroom cheesesteak and a regular cheesesteak.  The proper way to order a cheesesteak is you first designate the number of sandwiches along with the type of cheese.  For us it was two whiz.  Than you specify whether you would like onions or not, so our order was "two whiz, one wit, one wit out."  Place is cash only and again lines are long, have your order ready and cash ready.  The cheesesteaks themselves were good, good quality meat, and melted cheese whiz speaks for itself.  The bread they use is a white hoagie, and is a lot more chewy than John's bread, and John's has a much better selection of cheeses'.  That being said, if you can you should take time to visit the original.

Blaze is definitely one of my favorite spots to visit if I'm in the mood for fast and good pizza. I usually go to the one on Temple campus but it closes earlier in the summer and decided to check out this location. When I went, the shop was very understaffed and busy and this lead to some problems with our orders. Nevertheless, everyone working there was very kind and did everything they could to correct the orders. 

I can always expect a good quality pizza when I go to Blaze. I highly recommend getting the Build Your Own Pizza. There are plenty of toppings and sauces to choose from to make a very customizable personal pizza. The build-your-own is only about $8 and I really feel like you get your money's worth for the amount of pizza you get. Overall, it's great place to go if you're craving for some fast good pizza!

I visited this because I was in Philadelphia for the first time in my life, and I've  always wanted to try a Philly Cheesesteak in the city instead of elsewhere. My friends and I had to come here because well, it's a tourist trap and we're tourists. 

If I were you, I'd only come here once, just to say that I came here. After eating this abomination of a sandwich, which was unflavored and as dry as Arizona, I can confidently say that this is the worst sandwich I've ever had in my life. Overcooked and unflavored meat, the bread was mediocre, and you needed to pay extra for like the peppers? Jesus christ. For the price, I expected something edible. 

Also, the tables that they have are pretty gross, so I would wipe them down with a napkin and stuff. There were also tons of flies. Yuck. 

Come here once for the charm and never again after.

Horrible and disgusting greasy abhorrent sandwich !!!! 

Do not buy from this place its not worth a one dollar bill !!!!

Bro. No.

Horrible. Glorified 7 Eleven steak sandwich. PLEASE GO TO ANGELO'S, DELASSANDROS, OR JIMS....

I used to eat this steak after work 7-8 years ago working bar shift in Philly. It has lost SO MUCH quality since then. Just go elsewhere. $36 for 2 steaks and 2 waters. Cmon.

This location has had a broken drive thru speaker the last two times I came. Service is slow and you can expect to wait a minimum of 10-15 minutes for 'fast' food. No greeting when I pull up to the drive thru window, just a cold 'I hate my job' stare. It is located at a very busy intersection. I'm still looking for a decent McDonald's in my Philly area.

Wasn't how I remember from a few years ago. The meat was dry, there wasnt really any flavor. The cheese was mostly all over the wrapper and not actually on the cheesesteak. Probably why the meat tasted dry and flavorless. Disappointed but was still filling I guess.

FAVORITE!!!
Friendly, efficient servers. Wonderful guacamole and fresh chips! 
We live in the neighborhood and look forward to taking our guests to Los Caballitos. (We do prefer to eat outside when possible because we are "hearing challenged" when the music is too loud. We are 60 and over.) Our cheerful hostess tonight was Dee-andra. We got an outside table in 5 minutes. In the meantime we sat down at the bar and Alan quickly whipped us up the exact drinks we requested (we have particular needs in this area), and they were DELICIOUS!!! Service with a smile!!! Elaine was our initial server, and graciously moved us into the shade when our guest started melting due to the sun. ;) Our server Matthew then took over and served us delicious shrimp, slow-cooked goat, and enchiladas de pollo. Our chip bowl and drinks were refreshed without asking. Matthew also gave us a little education about types of tequila. 
A delightful late afternoon supper for three gray haired folks!
Walked out after waiting today in a line for 15 minutes that simply wasn't moving,  as staff was making food for pickup and delivery orders instead.

Not the best not the worst. I find they move quickly and 50% of the time get the burrito ratio down. It's the other half of the time that keeps me from coming back and picking the other across broad. 

Today I got all the way through ordering (hello spicy salsa!) and then found out they were out of cups for water. I asked for just a normal sized cup and the cashier mentioned it messes up their inventory.

I get that but I think management should have found a way around this or ran a block over for some water cups. I would have gotten my meal to go or not gotten the spiciest salsa. C'est la vie.

I'm not sure if the verdict is out yet, but in the war between Pat's and Geno's for your Philly cheesesteak, Pat's is the clear winner for me. First, I usually don't venture to either Pat's or Geno's unless someone is visiting me from somewhere afar. And many-a-time, these same people would want to try both Pat's and Geno's, so I've definitely had both plenty of times.

I always get the mushroom steak with whiz and onions (yes I know there's a Philly way of ordering but seriously? I refuse). 

The meat at Pat's is better. The steak is more tender and juicy. I like the juices that run down your arm as you eat the sandwich. It's salty, it's warm, it's great after-drinking food. 

I almost always also get an order of cheese fries (just because the whiz on my sandwich isn't quite enough whiz yet) and an order of Birch Beer (kind of like root beer) which goes oh-so-well with the cheesesteak.

The cashier had a bad attitude yesterday she gave me the look of disgust and hatred and basically threw my money at me. The look one her face was kind of scary. The bad unfriendly attitude was not appreciated at all. I call it Phillytude. I also did not get my beverage.

Why 4 stars?  Because it's the best Cheese Steak sandwich I've ever had.

   ---   ---   ---

What can I say that hasn't already been said?  If you visit Philadelphia, this is a requirement.

If you are expecting your life to be transformed based on the taste alone, you will be disappointed.  That being said, I've never had a better Cheese Steak.  

The entire Philadelphia culture is engulfed at Pat's, and I mean that in the most affectionate way.  Here is the routine:

1) Stand in line.

2) Use this time to decide on your order.

3) Practice reciting your order under your breath.

4) Arrive at the front of the line where someone behind the counter will barely acknowledge your presence.

5) Proclaim, "Whiz Wit, fries and a drink" within the first second and a half of said vague acknowledgment.

6) Hunt for a table like a needle in a haystack.

7) Enjoy the goodness.

My second visit to Pat's, this time with my boyfriend! So happy I was able to share a REAL cheesesteak with him!!
