Nothing but good things to say about this Philly staple! 
Aside from out of this WORLD cheesesteaks, the cheese fires with cheese wiz is just insane. For some reason these cheese fries hit the spot harder than any other cheese fry concoction I've had before. 
Every-time I am in Philly, I am making my Pat's pit stop!!
Service was really slow. Staff was not friendly at all. I've been there a number of times and I've had the same poor pullout of service

It was a decent Philly Cheese steak, first time out and wanted to see what all the buzz was about. Maybe I just had it overhyped and set my expectations too high, overall, still a decent cheese steak.
These guys are fast and amazing!!! Pleasant people no attitude like McDonald. Very fast not a long annoying wait. Love it I'll come again

We spent a day in Philly on our way home to Syracuse. Cheesesteaks are our favorite sandwich, and we've had the best of what Syracuse has to offer. (Spoiler alert: None of them are in the same league.) Through our visit, we had marked five places to get cheesesteaks while in town. Genos and Pats were more for their history and relevance than anything else, but it was nice starting here and working our way up.

We had stopped by Geno's the night before since all the other places were closed. The next morning we came to Pats, since none of the places were open yet. I love that they have the food ready less than 20 seconds after you've placed the order. Wrapped and everything, but still assembled fresh. We also appreciated that they broke down the cheesesteak jargon on posters for us ignorant outsiders. We got our cheesesteak "wiz wit". Wiz for the cheese, which we had never heard of until coming to Philly. "Wit" meaning "wit onions", as opposed to "wit out". We loved it in Philly.

The bread was soft, and the onions were cooked all the way. The meat was in full, thin chewy slices. They don't cut the sandwiches in half, which was unfortunate for us because we ate this one in the car outside of Swann Memorial Fountain. The sandwich was messy to the touch, it took some serious doing to get this thing into two pieces and eat it without cheesing up the whole car. But we managed, and we'd do it again.

We voted Genos over Pats, and all other places over both. There's a lot of Kitsch surrounding both "original" locations, and it's made them both soft. Still though, absolutely no complaint coming from out of town. My rating of 3/5 is based on context. I'd go out of my way to eat at Pat's any day if it were in Syracuse, but I'll never come back now that I know what else is available in Philadelphia.

If I could give this place ZERO stars I would. Long lines for no reason besides the excellent marketing skills both Pat's and Geno's has regarding rivalry or who was the originator of the sandwich.

Anyway, my husband and I got 2 cheese steaks: one with cheese whiz and the other with provolone. We also got french fries and a soda.

PROS: Food comes out quick 
CONS: Quick food has its consequences. Our cheese steaks barely had any cheese!!! Our onions were slapped on one side of the sandwich. Also, the steak is just really bland!! No taste whatsoever. Hurry up and eat your sandwich quick because it wont taste any better cold! The fries literally had nooo taste! Most likely ccooked in really old batter. Youre definitely going to have a hard time finding a place to sit. The concession area where they have their peppers, ketchup, mustard, etc. looks very unsanitary with flies. Definitely overpriced: we spent $24 on 2 sandwiches and $13.50 on 1 soda and 2 fries. 

Genos wasnt any better but if i had to pick between the 2 it would definitely be Genos just because it looks much cleaner and presentable.

Full disclosure: I came as a tourist. I was told NOT to go to Pats and Genos because they are considered trash cheesesteak sandwiches. I went to both, and honestly enjoyed them both. I tried the "Whiz Wit" style where they put the cheese whiz on, and understood why that's so popular (at first sight I thought that was disgusting).

Honestly, you can't go wrong with Pats or Genos. Pro tip: if you're lactose intolerant double up on the lactaid (take 2). No stomachache, just food coma.

With fast food chains, you have to take reviews with a grain of salt if they're a few months old. I think that staff can be a revolving door so the experience can change drastically based on the current team.

I have to say that I have had no issues with this location. As a matter of fact, I've received excellent service and found that the staff go out of their way to make sure you get what you need and accommodate you if they're sold out of something. Seems that the people working here are generally happy to be there and genuinely kind, which is always a plus! 

I'd like to note that I made orders at this location from evening to early night. I know that time can be a big factor with service and overall experience -cough cough WENDYS cough cough- but, everything has been consistent here! :)

Worst poke bowl I've ever had. The rice was stale and dry, as mentioned in other reviews. Nothing special about the flavor.

The onigiri was delicious, so it earned a star.

This is a quick and easy option at the PHL airport.

It's a Chick-fil-A, you know what you're getting here. And it's the airport, so you know that you're paying more. I caught it at a good time, mid-morning so it wasn't too crazy busy. They seem to move through the line pretty quickly.

Chicken minis, hashbrowns, and a lemonade- the breakfast of champions before hopping on a flight. If you're not getting Chick-fil-A sauce, you're doing it wrong. Now if only we can convince them to open on Sundays.

I had been dying to go to Philly to have a cheese stake.... Finally, this week, while driving to New York from Florida, I convinced my husband to detour and stop in Philly so we could get an authentic sandwich.  I did my google research and since Pat's and their competitor were in the same area, we thought great. We can try both!  Pat's disappointed.  The meat was cold, and lacked flavor. The bun was hard.  Overall I have had better at places outside of Philly.   The competition across the street tasted better. but still, neither place was worth the stop over.

So know this is outside only.  But boy do they whip up the cheese steaks so fast.  Big windows so you can watch them prepare the food.  We ordered with provolone and and the original cheese wiz.  Soooo delicious.  And the condiment stand... the hot peppers are amazing. 

There's a few places right in the area.  This is the only one we went to do and we'd say the food was good.

I got the mushroom cheese steak no onions, it was ok. Whiz cheese is a must, steak was dry cause they make it and just heat it up when you order, mushrooms were ok. Fountain Coke was delicious lol. Fries were also really good, had some breaded seasoning that made it crispy, minus one star for I've had a better sandwich.

Well, when you're in Philly for the first time you might want to visit one of the "beat" Philly cheesesteak places in town. However, I normally don't partake in these places for fear of "the hype" being overrated but this time we decided to try it out.

Pats and Genos are claimed to be the top places to get original Philly cheesesteaks and they are literally across the street from one another. We decided to go to the one with the biggest line (although neither had much of a line at the time we went) so nevertheless we went to Pats

We ordered a Philly cheesesteak and we both were underwhelmed. The fries are already made and are sitting on a stand already in a cup so as you can imagine they were cold. The cheesesteak wasn't very cheesy or flavorful. Overall, I think I ate a few disappointing bites and then called it quits. Tossed it in the trash and headed to go get something good to eat. Also, the staff wasn't friendly or helpful and maybe that is what is to be expected, I'm not sure but it was pretty disappointing. My takeaway from the experience is you can't win them all, I guess I can say I tried the "famous" Pats King of Cheesesteaks. ‍

& the Winner is... Pats!!! Kinda rude at the window... But steak sandwich was good, Cheese fries were the Bomb!  We had an awesome time having our own little taste battle.  Pats was the clear winner, 6 out of 6 voted for Pats. Keep up the good work guys, and thanks for the delicious food.

Oh ya! Came here to try the king of steaks...and I knew I made the right f*c*ing decision lol...found parking right on the sidewalk of this establishment. ...just hearing the people talk made me feel at home, a lot of yelling and bad mouth...5 stars right off the back...now to the ordering...you have two windows, weird as shit but okay feed me...one window to order your cheesesteak and the other for fries and drinks lol...had my cheese steak with wiz and onions and I effed it all up with there skinny fries....met a magician this day and the dude at the register window asked what he was...a magician ...asked if he knew this trick...make himself disappear lmaoooo...I died laughing...coming from a jersey city guy, pats made me feel at home with the way they act and simple order just to get my meal to me asap

Not a bad place to do the tourist version of getting a cheesesteak of you are visiting Philly.  It is almost a right pf passage to come here and compare to Geno's across the street.  Definitely more of a tourist type place, its a fun experience.  My favorite thing to do when I have friends visit is to get a cheese steak here and at Geno's (especially since a lot of out of towners insist on going to these two places since it is so hyped up for visitors) and split with friends...this way you can do the whole "taste test" thing and decide which place you like better.

Speak any language you want and come over to Pat's for a real cheese steak!  

Screw Geno's!

Blows Geno's out of the water. My fiance shared a cheese steak with onions and cheese wiz at both Pat's and Geno's. Pat's uses the chopped method when it comes to their meat. Pat's is cheaper by 50 cents than Geno's and you get way, way more meat. The bread is also a little chewier and you can actually taste the cheese on this sandwich. Definitely beats out Geno's any day for us Wisconsinites! Just make sure to bring cash!

Looking for a cure for constipation? Look no further!

Sometimes people just keep coming back to places because that's where they've always gone or they're new in town and rely on advice from strangers. Here's how to tell what kind of cheesteak you will like:

1. Meat sliced or chopped? Pat's is chopped, which I find to be a cover-up for a poorer quality beef.

2. Cheese or whiz? You can order provolone, but they use Whiz, which is about as close to cheese as Coffeemate is to milk.

3. A good roll. Nuf said.

4. Grease factor. My sandwich was unbelievably greasy; I used 10 napkins just to keep grease from spilling from the table onto my lap.

5. How clean is the restaurant?

It was ok. The meat was sweetened with the red and orange peppers, and I enjoyed the fries. But the bread was spiffy immediately upon receiving the sandwich. No parking, and seating was extremely limited.
They are horrible, the management can not control the staff language cursing and them slacking off. Do not recommend.

Went for a late lunch/early dinner st 3pm , when me and husband were out running errands. We found this place and figured we would go, both like Popeye's, what a mistake! First, they were out of fries and had to wait 10 minutes for them and then after that wait they told me they said they were out of chicken breasts  and it would it be another 15 minutes! How can chicken place run out of chicken?! Changed my order just to get out of there, do waste your time going NOT worth it

I decided to drive thru Checkers for fries. Don't bother trying to pull in if you're going Southbound, unless you like navigating mazes of 1 way streets. 

The parking lot is unkempt. Weeds, trash, busted fence & checkers signs.

No curly fries. The ones I got were okay. 

I don't think I need to go there again.

So I'm walking home after an awesome night of karaoke.   Its midnight, which I guess technically makes it Monday morning, I have to leave for work in 7 hours, and I'm effing starving.  Oh, and by the way, its the middle of a blizzard.  So I get close to home, and there, shining like a beacon, are the two cheesesteak battleships of Passyunk Ave, Pat's and Geno's.
I round the corner, and the decision is before me.  Under the most inhospitable conditions, Geno's stands alone, bright lights and neon, but only employees in sight.  Through the whiteout haze, I can see that Pats has half a dozen people in line.  If waiting in line during a driving snowstorm while a competing neighbour is line-free doesn't make for a ringing endorsement, I can't think of what does.
I order a whiz wit, and then add the ketchup and hotsauce.  Perfection.  Of course, my brain and my palette know it's a vile, grease drenched pile of chuck on a sponge like roll, but for the time and place, thats the point.  I've had way better steaks, but those aren't an option right now.  In the here and now, Pat's is exactly what I needed.

probably the worst McDonald's ever.  It's dirty, there are an insane amount of flies (everywhere, including my orange juice!), the staff is unprofessional and it took 21 minutes to get my food right.  I've ordered, eaten and paid at a sit down restaurant in less time.   Skip this McDonald's, there's one on South Broad.

I was given a chance at the 'cheesesteak' challenge (Pat's vs Geno's) and had to take it.  

We were passing through and thought, 'Hey, let's stop for cheesesteaks'!

I ordered a cheesesteak 'wit' (which means with onions), and added mushrooms, and provolone.

The service was very quick here and the employees don't mess around.  If you start asking questions, in their mind...you are just holding up the line....it's pretty funny to sit and watch people order....

I opened the wrapper and....no magic fairys flew out.....it looked like a regular cheesesteak....I was a little bummed, but I ate it anyway.

In all honesty, it was just ok.  I have had better cheesesteaks in SoCal...
The bun was soft, the meat was nice, and the veggies too, but there was no binding ingredient to make it come together.  The provolone slices were thick and cold, and that also hurt the sandwich score.  Normally, I am a 'contrast of textures and multi temperature' guy, but in this case, melty cheese would have been better.....should have gotten the whiz?

Just ok sandwich but fun experience.....
Better then Geno's but still disappointed.. both does need lead up to the hype.. overrated!!

Pat's is one of the few food destinations in America that deserves a pilgrimage -- so we made one, on the way back home to Illinois from the D.C. area. We were lucky enough to get there during off-peak hours so we didn't have to wait in a long line. As a non-Philadelphian, I wanted to make sure I knew how to order the famous cheesesteak. They've got a handy guide next to the window, and I did my best. They seemed to understand what I wanted so I think I succeeded, but I suspect there was probably something I fumbled there. 

I ordered a "cheese wit," a cheesesteak with onions. Not wanting to mess with tradition, I got it with Cheez Whiz. That sandwich sure validated the extra travel time home. I love simple sandwiches, especially with the basics I love and none of the things I don't. That said, a sandwich with delicious thinly sliced ribeye, gooey "cheese," and sauteed onions goes straight to my heart (and definitely to my stomach). The bread did well to hold everything in and was waxed with a nice layer of grease, a mark of a good sandwich, so says the Fresh Prince at least. (He counts as a Philadelphian, no?) 

Everyone enjoyed their sandwiches, though my girlfriend and her dad are still partial to Chicago's Italian Beef. Nevertheless, the sandwiches were so good that we didn't even venture across the street to Geno's, even with all of its glitzy glory.

Just a tad bit better than Genos. The cheesesteak was warmer but still bland. No flavor at all. There's a bunch of places where you can get much better cheesesteaks that take credit cards, nicer, and have parking. Pats and Genos are just tourist attractions.

On our stops during our trip to the East Coast, we stopped by this place to try. We read about Pat's and Geno's, so we tried both. The sandwiches were good but the cheese whiz tasted watered down and was missing quite a bit of flavor. The fries were good. It was a bit odd that fries are ordered at a different window. Also, keep in mind if visiting, this place is cash only. Have cash ready to pay for your food as there is no ATM on site. There is an ATM across the street at the bar/pub entrance. 
I tried the original steak sandwich with cheese whiz.

I don't eat beef so  I rarely set foot in this place. but the fries and milkshakes are extremely worth waiting in line for.  some of the best that I've had in Philadelphia. The place could just use a little more variety in the menu selection. after all, if they get this much hype for how huge their burgers are, then picture what they could do with a chicken sandwich?

Overall fantastic experience! We parked in central Philly and ubered here. We tried both Geno's and Pat's and I must say Pat's is better! Pat's has more cheese and the bread really absorbed the juicy flavors. The wrapping was great and contained the oils whereas Geno's leaked through and actually burned me through my shirt. Yikes... 
Pats's has a delicious onion and pepper blend and the meat tastes authentic and not cookie cutter. TIP: when ordering just say "with" after your order to imply that you want onions. That's what the locals seemed to do. 
Also, JUST CASH is accepted. The aesthetic is very traditional and you really feel like a true philly goer when eating this sub! Highly recommend, but try them both for your own judgments!

This location is inside a new walking food mall by the liberty bell, where there's more to look for and enjoy! But I had the pleasure of meeting the owner and for him to suggest his best! I had the 716, fries fresh pulled roasted chicken with buffalo sauce and blue cheese & my boyfriend had the Philly cheese steak fries! And for dessert funnel cake fries covered in chocolate sauce and strawberry sauce! If your looking for one of the best customer service locations with the most easiest to love finger food, this is your place! Have a bite and enjoy the love!!!! Definitely visiting again soon! Thank you so much for the great experience!

Philly, you are doing poke so very wrong. If my protein from the start is an added $1.50+, what am I paying for? Poke is literally raw fish, I'm not interested in a $9 bowel of rice with a surcharged fish topping. After a long day of traveling the city, I ordered delivery. My mistake, without being in store I couldn't menacingly glare as my bowel was put together with a pound of rice, three edamame, and no sauce. Maybe my sauce was forgotten or maybe the thick coating of fried onions soaked it all up? Again, the fish is suppose to be the star! Sure, fried onion seasoning is nice for added crunch, but not blanketing my mountain of naked rice. I ordered 2 scoops of fish, an extra spend to even get to any essence of poke. While edible, this was a terribly dry and bland poke bowel. I can see if this is the only option in all of Philadelphia, but if you've actually had poke somewhere else before, don't waste your time.

Awful.  The steak was greasy, grizzly, and flavorless.  The woman who took our order was a pushy bitch.  The place was filthy.  It has gone significantly downhill since we were here two years ago.  With so many great steak places in Philly, I doubt we'll be back.

You better talk the lingo or get back in line. Good thing we had someone in our crew from Philly and took us to good ol' Pats. There's a line no matter what time you go. Prices are good but you better know the lingo.
  Parking is all around. Philly cheesesteak was good. Very cheesy obviously. So if you're a fan of cheese definitely try the whiz cheese. It is pretty fulfilling. I was in Philadelphia and just had to try it... no regrets at 3am in the morning but Cali time Midnight so I was good!! Lol. Make sure you know what you want or get back in line

There have been battles and brawls won and lost over which house of Cheese Steak is best in Philly. After watching a recent Anthony Bourdain show which featured the two Philly Cheese Steak giants, I knew I wanted to come see the battle myself. On my most recent weekend trip to Philly, my friends and I drove over to partake in some cheese steak tasting.

If you're in the vicinity of these two Cheese Steak palaces, all you have to do is sniff the air to know you're nearby. The smell of cheese, onions, steak, and oil is very distinct. You might even feel your mouth start to water. Since this is Pat's, you don't have the neon lights blazing in your face. The way the menu is set up, you need to glance at the big words on the wall... pick your stuff and quickly order once you're at the window. Pat's basically puts up a "how to order" guide and makes it quite easy for you to put together your options... wit (out) onions... then wit what cheese, pay and then wait for like a few seconds before your sandwich quickly appears. Pat's is no joke, they have this cheese steak making process down to a science. 

I feel like this type of food is best reserved for eating after a night of boozing. However, if you are like me, and want to see which is the better of the two, I prefer Pat's for sure. My friends Kelly C., her bf and I each shared cheese steaks from both places so that we could have a comparison... hands down we all love Pat's and believe his is the king of steaks! I don't think it's the best in the whole world.. but for the Pat's vs. Geno's  battle, come see for yourself firsthand, but we stand by Pat's.

I just moved here from Miami, and I didn't know cheese steaks could be this good!!!

They taste even better when you are leaving a bar at 2am, although the lines are long this time at night, its worth the wait!!!

A trip to Philly isn't complete without coming to Pats!
This location doesn't pay attention to delivery orders at all. If you order delivery from here, expect that it will take 2+ hours to deliver if you're lucky enough to receive it at all.

South Philadelphia born and raised, at pat's king of steaks is where I spent most of my days.
Sure people will tell you it's a favorite of tourists, but there is a reason! It's delicious!
Bring your appetite and a Philadelphia attitude and know if you want it wit or witout before you get to the line. 
Load up on the deliciousness before you get sent to live with your auntie and uncle in bel air.

Blogger JL Jupiter posted a video about Supreme Oasis and he featured vegan food. Being a vegetarian, I ran there . I was in Philly and decided to order dinner. Got there about 4:00. It was people waiting outside who had placed their order. Only 3 people allowed inside do to COVID. I placed my order of fried Brussel sprouts, vegan shrimp platter and vegan chicken sandwich. I checked on my order several times after being told it would be a 45 minute wait. I got so hungry that I tried to buy a piece of carrot cake. It needed to be frosted so wasn't able to purchase before my food was available. The food took over 2 hours. I had enough time to go visit a friend in the area. 

The customer service is good. The guy manning the door shared his fries with us. It was like family waiting for Thanksgiving dinner to be ready. 

The food is outstanding. It's the best vegan chicken sandwich, vegan shrimp, Mac n cheese I ever tasted. The squash is next level. I can't wait until I'm back in Philadelphia so I can order food again. The carrot cake was okay. I will try other desserts when I visited the next time. 

Calling in your order is an option when they answer the phone. They are extremely busy cooking the food and taking in persons orders. 

Food is a 10 stars but the wait made it 4 stars.
Out of basically all toppings. Even overheard the girl say that she doesn't want to get another one out ( over an hr before closing)

The original! 

Pack the steaks less tight, golly. A bit on the greasy side but it's Phila bro. Order with cheese, or onions. Bring a flask of booze..

Rebel review: 3

Normally the presence of grease, cheez-wiz, provolone and surly service in the same sentence dooms the offending establishment to the Yelpian oblivion of zero stars. However, when you're navigating Philadelphia's famous quadrangle of Passyunk Avenue where Pat's and Geno's cheesesteaks ladle their magic out by the ton, they easily become your favorite meal of the month. 

Normally, you wouldn't get me near canned mushrooms much less the science experiment they call cheez-wiz but together they conspire to delight my pleasure center even though they bring more greasy ooze to Philly than a convention of Elvis impersonators.

I prefer Pat's but just barely. Truth is I love them both. I'm just waiting for McDonald's or Wendy's to discover the Cheesesteak and turn it into a test kitchen abomination wolfed down with gusto in flyover country. Am I the only one who thinks the McRib sucks. Besides, I still haven't forgiven Sarah Lee for ripping the soul out of the humble bagel. An easy five stars when only the original will do.

YO Geno, in the battle of the cheese steak on "E Passyunk Ave" I command you to kneel before THE KING!, 

ALL HAIL KING PAT!

Pat's offers you a mouth watering sauteed meat in bun, smothered in onions & provolone. OK, I know some of you fools like WIZ, but hey its my review not yours and I dig provolone! Grab a coke & some fries with that order and BANG your set! 

I'm sure you would need OBAMA CARE if you ate here more that once a week but then again OBAMA CARE is "FREE" so you should have some spare change for 2 of them.

I've always loved Cheese Steaks sandwiches so imagine my anticipation of what was to be my first official Philly Cheese steak! My friend who was going to Uni in Philly at the time brought me to Pat's and all I recall is her coaching me while we were in line to ensure I ordered the right thing as to not piss off the folks who work there. She told me to either order a Whiz-wit or a whiz-wit-out. Uh...how come I couldn't order a provolone-wit? I was told Whiz is the way to go so I went with the whiz and that would have been a fine choice if the meat tasted better. The meat tasted too bland and too much like meat. i prefer my meat seasoned. 

Next time, I'm getting a provolone-wit or trying out Geno's!
By far, best cheesesteak in Philly....or America. The first. The original. The only. Tradition tastes better at Pat's!
So far Pats Reigns Supreme! Their sandwiches are juicy and succulent! Geno's tend to have a drier sandwich. What else can I say!!! ??

I loved my first poke bowl from Philly Poké! I opted to create my own and went with white rice, tuna, cucumber, jalapeño, seaweed salad, masago, fried shallots and a little bit of spicy sauce. I asked for wasabi and soy sauce on the side. 

My regular-sized bowl was a nice amount of food, though I would have liked a little more protein. I can't imagine needing any more rice but maybe the larger bowl comes with more protein as well? In any case, the ingredients tasted fresh and delicious. I'm a great poke bowl creator, if I do say so myself. 

Philly Poké is located inside Chinatown Square on Race Street. There is cafeteria-style seating in the back of the market. I will definitely be back again for more of that poke!

Bring some cash and get ready for an awesome cheese steak. There is an ordering code posted before you order. I use it, never seen someone not use it and them say anything but go with the lingo. 

Service is fast, about as fast as you pay the man he hands you your order. But is about 10 bucks for a cheese steak so make sure you have the cash!

Pat's is my favorite cheesesteak place in all of Philly. I know that so many people have such varying, strong opinions on which place has the best cheesesteak in Philly, which just means that it's a very personal choice--and I guess this review gives me the opportunity to explain mine.

First off is the food - which is the real reason why we are here, right? To me, Pat's steaks are perfection - it's meaty and pretty lean and flavorful, the bread roll is delicious, the cheese is always on point, and those bursting red cherry peppers seal the deal for a great sandwich. The fries remind me of crispy, thicker Burger King fries, which is awesome in my book (they seem to be coated with some kind of sparse batter that adds to their crispness). 

My own particular "pièce de résistance' is the basic cheesesteak wit onions and provolone. It's a testament to how good this item is when I don't need to order it as a pizza steak (which is my typically favorite cheesesteak sandwich). Sorry Philly diehards, I'm just not a cheese wiz kinda guy, and never will be. 

Which leads me to point #2 - my mind is stimulated, my tastebuds are happy, and my tummy is full when I leave Pats. IMHO $11 is getting pricey for a cheesesteak, but at least I'm content when I'm done with my meal here. You just can't underestimate how much that particular mix means to a consumer. If you feel more fulfilled after shelling out your hard-earned dollars, then it's a great place to be. As I sit in the outdoors seating with friends, basking in our glow of grease digesting through our arteries, we have great chats through the energy of tons of people that swirl around us.

And point #3 being that Pat's location is vibrant and energetic. Sure, Pat's is a tourist trap; but it's easy to deal with when you've enjoyed the food and it's a fun to place to be with happy tourists abound. I guess this is why Pat's has a long history here in the City - because it's genuine and people are drawn to it because of that. Even Pat's building is much more modest than Geno's neon-clad pretentiousness (I don't mean to start a civil war here!). Pat's may be a tourist trap, other places may arguably have better quality ingredients overall, but there aren't many places left in the city to get a fun cheesesteak experience for under $11. 

There are very few spots in this City that I think of as my 'happy places' - places that balance delicious food with reasonable prices and great surroundings - but Pat's does happen to be one of them.
Place is dope, definitely more user-friendly than Gino's. I felt like Pat's has been doing Steaks consistently classic forever and that's why I chose them.

Not a Philly native. My first and last time here. Ordered my cheesesteak with extra American cheese. Meat was flavorless. Was disappointed to say the least. I will definitely be sticking to a Dalessandro's (worth the drive & line.)

Friendly and solid tex mex.  Chips are sometimes stale-ish but the salsa duo is surprisingly tasty.  Menu is very ambitious but never quite seems to hit a homerun.  Bonitas/snacks are the way to go.  Little plates, baby, little plates.  That's the way.  

Look for seasoned corn-on-the-stick coming soon.  Tasty.  Pork skewers were perfect.  Veggie quesadilla mushroom heavy and perfect amount of cheese.  Little plantain fritters are a must and the steak burrito is as big as a 7-year-old's head.  Nachos are good but it seems to depend on who's working as to HOW good.

Very loud.  Hipster heavy.  Friendly staff.  Popular outside seating.  Local!

Just like any other Chipotle (point of chains) so I won't go on and on.

1. They offer sofritas. For my fellow vegetarians or alternative eating friends, try them! They're very well sauteed! Apparently they have a ton of sodium (thanks Mayur C.) so if you're sensitive, check it the deets online. 

2. During lunch time, this line is basically at the door and ridic intimidating. It goes go by VERY quickly though. Pros: goes by quickly. Cons: You better know wtf you want to order cause there is no time when you are up there to ponder between black bean or pinto.

Out of all the icons serving Cheesesteak in the Brotherly Love mecca we were taken here as guests. Tuesday early dinner. Line was only 6 or so long at the the time. 

Got one wit wiz and an orange soda. Grabbed a picnic table and sat down to eat.

Bread was very good. Steak with onions and wiz were just ok. Table of girls next to us had split up and tried Pat and also Geno's ones and declared Geno the "winner". 

Fries ok, hot and crunchy. Cash only so leave credit card in your wallet.

Would return once I hit the rest of the places with supposed best in Philly. Jim's would be next.

Another 3000 yelp restaurant!

I'm a firm believer that Pat's deserves 5 stars. The cheesesteak is that good. Fries are also amazing. The reason this is a 4 star review is simply because of price - fries cost $5! I'm sorry but we're not in NY. Clearly overpriced banking on this tourist attraction. Also there is limited seating because of its popularity. 

Definitely would recommend, and definitely will visit again. However only for take out!

Five guys is not just a restaurant, it's an experience. Be prepared to be filled with extraordinary flavors of all kind, mixed together with food from the Heavens. You get to choose and create your own burger, but it comes to you better than even your mind can imagine. I am never disappointed when I head to Five Guys. The price is not an issue when you are being fed food at the pinnacle of food.

My family and I were visiting Philly to see my cousin graduate. We figured that having a Philly cheese steak was essential to any visit here. So after a fun day of exploring we stopped at Pat's King of Steaks!
They were fast and effective. Not the most hospitable, but that can be neccessary at some of these busy places... and it was busy. 
We had 3 hot dogs and a philly cheese steak with the works (I added some spicy peppers. It was great! I do recommend getting extra cheese, because the standard left me wanting more.

I would recommend this restaurant.

Worst chipotle in the city. It was the best a year ago, but the staff can't keep up with the orders. It's obviously the owner's fault because there's never enough staff. Those web orders are what's killing them. I ordered at 7 and it said the earliest it would be ready was 8. It's 8:45 and there are literally 20 people waiting for their orders. I think I'll be here for a while too. This is Chipotle. Do not come to this one.

Was here for the grand opening free pizza day and it was definitely worth the wait! For those who are unfamiliar with how Blaze and other similar places work, it's basically a Chipotle for pizza: you get in line, and build your pizza from the bottom up. You chooses what sauce, meats/vegetables/cheese you want, they throw it in the oven for just 90 seconds to cook, and you add any last toppings or drizzles you want. Maybe it was just opening day adrenaline but everyone here works so fast, cranking out pizzas in no time.

For only $8.25, you can make your pizza with any toppings you want or choose from one of their specialties. I got the "Link In"- italian sausage, roasted red peppers, sauteed onions, mozzarella, and red sauce; I asked for extra pesto drizzle after baking. The crust was thin, tasty, and just a bit crisp. There was just the right amount to support all the toppings but not enough that you end up throwing some away. The ingredients were fresh and yummy, and the single pizza was big enough to satisfy me for lunch.

It might not be the fanciest pizza you've eaten, but definitely give this place a try if you want fast, affordable, customizable pizza that doesn't skimp on taste.

I came, I ate annnnnnd I conquered.  Conquered the chips and salsa that is!

Gotta love mowing down on the fresh chips and salsa and then ordering a taco salad to be "good."  Which means more tortilla chips being sprinkled on top of the salad.  Whatevs.  That verde sauce was killer!  The regular salsa was OK, but the verde....let's just say I could have licked the bowl clean.  Let's be clear....I did not....but I could have!

The grilled shrimp taco salad was also excellent with tortilla strips black beans, cucumber, tomato, cilantro vinaigrette.  Who doesn't love a good cilantro vini!?  But was it "good" for me?  I'm just gonna go with yes!  Just because it was yummy.  

It made me a little sad to not order a marg...but you gotta draw the line on some days....so maybe another!

Cantina los Cabalitos is quite nice. I thoroughly enjoyed the food, drinks and overall atmosphere. 

I ordered a delicious pork burrito which was jammed packed with rice, pork, guacamole, jalapenos and most importantly, cheese! Oh, and get ready- the burrito itself is probably gonna be the size of your head. I couldn't even finish mine past halfway.

My friends and I had a pitcher of Endless Summer which I found to be fan-freakin-tastic! You can really taste the jalapenos in this lovely concoction so if you love a nice kick of sweet and spicy in your drink, you should definitely try this.

Oh and another exciting point for me is the fact they have chalk in their bathrooms and you can write/draw/scribble on the walls!

The only qualm I actually had with this place is that the music was way too loud at some points, I could barely hear who were sitting directly across from me when they spoke and vice versa. 

Otherwise, tasty and fun!

So this place is amazing! I had the fish nuggets, Mac n cheese and string beans! I also had the pineapple upside down  cake and bought a bean pie for good measure! Everything was good!! Everything! Here's the thing though, it isn't a restaurant. It's like a stop in and pickup spot! Probably cuts down the overhead for the owner but you just order and grab food and leave. It is really cold, so wear a jacket... and they have great veggie and vegan options from cheese to non-meat options of the meals they serve! It's pretty awesome, no pork products whatsoever so that's a plus too! I'll definitely return! Pretty good soul food and the staff is super friendly!!

Don't bother asking if the fruit smoothie is Vegan, you may find that a fly in it like I did, or at least it's wings. 

The smoothie was reasonably at 4.50 and the location is convenient. The complimentary fly is what got me buzzed. After finding the fly I came back to the cooler where the fruit is stored. I found multiple flies buzzing around. And the saddest part might just be how preventable the situation was. The cooler is left open by about two inches, more than enough room for a hungry fly or ten. 
Maybe this was an off day but I won't be back to chance it. 
For the record they do offer cool options like fruit bowls and coffee smoothies so its particularly unfortunate that these were the results of my patronage.

Considering the fact that there are like a million reviews for this place - probably not necesary for me to review it as well - but hey. Here goes nothing. 

I've been a customer of cantina's for a few years now - and I love it. They have a ton of vegan / vegi friendly options, as well as a ton of non vegi / vegan options - and I've never had something here that I didn't really enjoy. The food is usually, dependably good. I've tried their nachso (with vegan beef), their plantains, their burritos, quesadillas, soft tacos, hard tacos, etc. You name it I've had it - and I've loved all of it! Additionally, there is a great happy hour special that they run on the margaritas - and the margaritas here are good. I've also tried a few of their flights of tequillas - and enjoyed all of them! 

Definitely trek here.

I hate this location. I eat enough Chipotle to know I'm getting skimped hard on the meat at this location. Whenever I have any requests, some tall blonde schmohawk has to come in and turn down my request. If it weren't that every other Chipotle provides the same exceptionally great service, setting the bar high, I would think I was being unreasonable. Instead I just cry on the inside and die a little while I bite into mostly tortilla. This place basically makes me a vegetarian but I'm probably slowly becoming anemic from iron deficiency. GIVE ME THAT MEAT BABY!!

Extra stars given because the blonde guy wasn't here today and the rest of the team (sans meat provider) were efficient and polite and wrapped one fine "steak" burrito.

Part 1 of the Pat's vs. Geno's challenge. Yes, very touristy. I had the provolone cheesesteak with onions. This was the winner. The initial eye test did not favor Pat's. The bread was thinner and the steak pieces were smaller. The price was $1.50 more expensive. Good thing the visual is just the first thing. The taste was incredible. The steak had better seasoning. The bread was the right size as a carrier without filling you up. The onions were caramelized to perfection. If you need to choose just one go with the original...Pat's.

Much like spots like El Rey and Adobe Cafe, if I'm looking for for some authentic Mexican cuisine I'll go elsewhere. But the beauty of Cantina Los Cabalitos is that it gives you mucho mucho mas reasons to go and enjoy its atmosphere than any other not so traditional Mexican spot out there - like brunch on every day of the week, a destination spot for outdoor seating, and the best margaritas in Philadelphia.

Long before I enjoyed any meal here (aside from the addicting tableside chips and salsa) I've had at least one margarita to coordinate with each color of the rainbow. even jalapeno and the elusive black currant! whether you go frozen or on the rocks you get the perfect fruity blast of alcohol, and a damn good deal if you order by the pitcher with some friends. But if you're loco enough to enjoy you're tequila straight up, then you have mucho varieties to choose from and even a couple of flights.

Another serious plus to Cantina is that for a spot that's not completely authentic Mexican, its menu comes closer to hitting that mark than most of the other similar spots out there. I was able to chow down into that fact finally 
(still a slacker sometimes) at Yelp Brunch Club when I had an incredible plate of huevos rancheros with refried beans, flour tortillas, and chorizo for good measure. It was one of those dishes that just tasted epic in its simple execution, and it wasn't just the spicy Bloody Marys that I had along with it warming my taste buds!

Add in all of the above and you have the reasons why Cantina rises above you're typical destination bar, and delivers another winner for the Khyber crew.

I visited here while I was in Philly on business, because everyone said that it was a "must visit" experience. I have to admit, the food was great - the ultimate comfort/treat food, and really affordable too. The only problem is, the noise. I visited during lunch time on a weekday and the place was packed, so it was hard to find a seat. It was really noisy too.

Service was quick, and the food was filling and tasty. I would have preferred eating somewhere quieter, though.

If you're in the area and fancy an authentic fast-food experience, this is a nice place to eat, but it's not somewhere you'd go for a formal meal. Maybe I just had the place described to me badly since I'm not from the area, but I'd just like to emphasize that it IS fast food.
I visit form Baltimore to Philadelphia stop to eat Popeyes chicken that clean Resturant good customer service I tray there spicy chicken best I love it

Good food, better experience
I popped in here randomly while shopping on Passyunk, and I'm glad I did. It's a nice neighborhood spot to pop into here and there. 
Food comments: I got a margarita and carnitas tacos. Both were above average, but not amazing. The carnitas tacos were fatty, but super flavorful and I ended up being surprised by how much I liked the meat. The tacos were also pretty filled, which is always appreciated. 
Other comments: The service was outstanding, and I contemplated giving a five because of it. I wish I knew my server's name, so I could give her a shoutout, because she was so kind and customer-oriented. She nearly ran to the register to put my order in before happy hour ended & she was managing a crap ton of tables very well. My food also came out very quickly. As far ambience, I sat outside and enjoyed their outdoor space - open, covid-friendly, simply but nicely decorated. 
Overall, it is not going to be the best Mexican food in the city, but Cantina is a great spot still and the people make the experience even better. I recommend going!

I know Pat's and Geno's are tourist traps, which I usually hate and avoid at all costs. But I've always wanted to try them both. So I pushed the tourist trap embarrassment aside and went all in. 

Pat's bread is as expected. Nothing spectacular but soft yet hearty. The meat isn't super flavorful. Better than Geno's, but still very little seasoning. This won't go down as the best cheesesteak of my life, but it's fine enough. 

Pat's wins the battle for me between these two.

This place was aight. 

Perhaps it's that I wanted it to be superb, because there's honestly (in my opinion) a lot of good Mex and Tex Mex in this city.

I was here with a huge UYE group this past weekend, and got there late. The host and staff were really great about quickly adding a chair to one of our side tables for me, so that was a plus.

They also seem to be very veg and vegan friendly, here, so if you're looking for vegan Mex, they've got it.

In spite of that, the food that I had here was kind of hit and miss. 

I got:

The shrimp ceviche, which was delicious, and only 9 bucks. Get it!
The pork empanadas, these were okay, but a bit oversalted.
The chorizo Burrito, which was also okay, but very oversalted.

Maybe it's the fact that it felt like 100 degrees out, but my two hot dishes were too salty for my taste. It also took a while for the food to come out, except for the ceviche, which was fast, and by far the best thing I had there.

So, 40 bucks of me being in a tasting menu kind of mood later, I found myself slightly disappointed.

However, I'm resolved to return, because I saw some really good looking things that other people got, that I want to try.

As for the service here was as good as it could have been for a group of 25, so I won't complain there. The waitstaff was rushed, but attentive, and I can only assume the kitchen was working as fast as it possibly could.

I didn't get to try the margaritas because I was saving myself for a drive out to the burbs to see my family. Definitely have to come back for that.

All in all, worth the first try, and at least one more to see if there are other menu items that will bump this place up to a solid 4.

On another note, I feel like my reviews are getting clinical/boring.

So, with that said, penis.

What's the difference between Pat's King of Steaks and Seinfeld's The Soup Nazi? Well, at least one is led to believe that the Soup Nazi's venerable restaurant offers good soup. Pat's King of Steaks most certainly offers mediocre food with Soup Naziesque service that is as unnecessary as it is uncharming. Being barked at in a line of 50 at 3 AM when half the line is drunk? Understandable! But being barked at--like my party and I were--at 1:30 PM when the line was never more than two deep? Unacceptable.

Could Philadelphia host one of the world's greatest dining tourist traps? Yes, Sir!

One of my fav for a philly cheese steak- must order with onions and wiz cheese....if you haven't been here, it's outdoor seating and no public rest room and across from Gino's...place it pretty iconic...you have to park on the street.
Bad service. Be prepared to wait a long time and don't care about If it's hygienic. Bad franchise. A wood at all costs.

Soo .... Infamous Philly cheese steak sammiches were a complete letdown.  I suppose I shouldn't have expected too much from a sandwich drizzled in cheese whiz but I just had to know what the hype was all about.  Long lines, cash only, hot weather, and less then ideal sanitized condiments seem to be the name of the game.  Find some seating with a random person to enjoy your $10 sandwich and now i can say that I have enjoyed a Philly cheese steak sandwich in Philadelphia.  Bragging rights aside I probably wouldn't return, but still recommend one goes if one would also like said bragging rights.   Cheese whiz on anything should be outlawed.  Am curious if the provolone would taste any better?  It was an experience :)

Five Guys is a welcomed burger franchise relatively new to Philly and it gives us a great choice when it comes to the All-American Hamburger. I love those juicy burgers with all those toppings and the delicious sesame seeded bun. I like my burger with A-1 sauce, mushrooms sauteed onions, jalapeno peppers and ketchup. The Fries are great! I always loved skin on Fries the best anyway. Five Guys uses fresh burger meat and every sandwich is made to order, so you may have to wait a little longer than for a Big Mac. But that's okay, you can munch on free peanuts while you wait, or you can talk to the manager, Diane. She's nice and very knowledgeable about their product. So give it a try, you'll never go under the golden arches again.

Today was my first time in Philadelphia, and the first thing my boyfriend and I did was fall into some tourist traps. I had back-to-back cheesesteaks wit whiz from Pat's and Geno's. Sure, I've had better cheesesteaks elsewhere. If I'm just comparing the OG's though, Pat's was hands down the clear winner for me.

I ate Pat's first, but I knew instantly after one bite of Geno's that I liked Pat's much better. The cheese whiz was salty and flavorful. I honestly didn't think that Pat's cheesesteak had much seasoning to begin with, but the cheese whiz was the saving grace of the sandwich. Pat's has my vote for the great cheesesteak debate.
Tried both Pat and Geno's. Both of us agreed the cheese and bread is better at Pat's. Do the taste test and try one of each. You really can't go wrong with either one.

Fiancé was so hyped about Pat's, he was raving about it all day while driving. Although I was annoyed by it, I actually held a reasonably high expectation after hearing, oh it was on tv, oh it's so popular, blah blah blah. We made it finally and got lucky scoring a parking spot right in front. He was super duper stoked by then. His eyes lite up like a little kid. We got in line and ordered the usual. 2 cheesesteaks and a side order of fries. 

WHAT A DISAPPOINTMENT!!! It is totally overrated. The cheesesteaks are mediocre, and it is definitely all about the hype, not taste. We both agreed it didn't even tasted as good as the ones from home (Los Angeles) I didn't even finish mine simply because I didn't want to eat it anymore. We got our orders literally right after we paid, which stated everything was pre-made, the meat wasn't even hot, and there's barely any cheese. The fries was total garbage, one word, soggy. The table behind my fiancé was completely mesmerized, I was thinking and wondering to myself if his tastebuds were dead. The only reason why I'm giving it 2 stars is the AYCE jalapeños and salsas. 

I hear Geno is even worse so don't even bother. Just check out their reviews. These 2 joints are definitely all about the hype. If you want real good cheesesteak, hit the Reading Terminal, Carmen's is the way to go. I'd say best cheesesteaks in Philly that we've tried.
Horrible service. I thought this was fast food. We have been in line for at lease 15 mins. All we ordered a 3 sausage biscuits, sausage McMuffin & 2 hash browns this unacceptable

I came to this location 4 times this week to purchase shamrock shakes for my kids 
Three days in a row the machine was down,
Finally on the fourth it worked but did it? Mmm
No because when I sipped the nasty sour foam with a hint of slimy mint syrup i spit it right back out.
What a waste of time and 12$. Tasted like dog $&@$ 
The staff there oh my I wouldn't even know where to begin with how unprofessional EVERYONE is.
Beyond annoyed.

Great cheesesteak! Line moved quickly and efficiently. It was $11 for my cheesesteak with onions and cheese. Also tried Geno's which was comparable. There are tables to sit outside and enjoy your sandwich.

I went to Cantina Los Caballitos with a few friends last night after an outdoor yoga class at Bok Bar. We had about a 15-20 min wait and were seated at a nice table in the corner of their outdoor space, which is lovely. I highly recommend it if you just want to have some margaritas and snacks. 

I ordered the mushroom burrito. It was good but nothing special. I thought it was pretty bland overall and could have used some extra flavor in addition to maybe a pan fry for the tortilla once it is done. Two of my friends ordered fish tacos, they had asked if pico came on the taco (which is what it said on the menu) and our server responded that it did not, so they both ordered it, one on the side. However it did seem to come on the tacos, but they were not bothered by it. 

We also ordered a pitcher of regular margaritas which I also thought were good, basic margs.

Overall we had a nice time, Cantina Los Caballitos has a nice atmosphere, I would come back for margs and maybe some guac but probably not specifically for the food.
It was okay meat needed more seasoning, best thing to me was the cheese fries. I guess I expected more for all the hype.
By far, the worst chipotle. Customer service was trash, food was bland, portion sizes were small, it was 5p on a Saturday and they were out of menu items!

The rivalry between Geno's and Pat's has been going on for quite some time from what I understand and on my trip to Philly this past weekend I made it my mission to try both and determine a winner. Unfortunately for Pat's... Geno's won but let me explain why ill sum it up in three main categories meat cheese and bread.

Meat:
Pat's: The meat at Pat's is shredded and there is a bountiful amount 
Geno's: The meat is sliced and extremely tender

Cheese:
Pat's: way to much cheese wiz on the sandwich almost a full on cheese sandwich 
Geno's: cheese wiz wiped on the sides of the bread and just a little added to the meat

Bread:
Pat's: Soft but not as good as Geno's in my opinion
Geno's: Soft and soaked up all the juices from the meat creating a soft luxurious sandwich 

The fries here at Pat's were delicious I must say and had a great flavor over all. I also really liked their choices of soft drinks. Any place that serves birch beer is a winner in my book. Parking around here can be a bit of a bitch but that's not Pat's fault.. I just wish it was easier to find parking in the area. But hey it's all worth it in the end once you bite into that cheese steak.

Kayla is awesome and so personable. Roxy is very bubbly, seasoned and efficient. Parker definitely sets a great first impression. The bartender Dylan is just as fun as the first day here. My family has been coming here over 13 years and counting because they offer vegan options, and the restaurant never ceases to amaze me!

If you're visiting Philly, I believe everyone must come here to at least taste where it supposedly all began.  There are better cheesesteaks in the area, but none can claim that they were the first.  Because of this, they get 4 stars from me.  And don't let the sign in front fool you, they don't send you to the back of the line if you're unsure how to order properly.

Long lines for an overprice mediocre product, made and served assembly-line style are not my thing.  The meat is slathered in some gross and gooey neon-orange sauce (that is about as much cheese as I am Cherokee*) and placed into a roll-shaped piece of white bread.  It's got all the ambiance of gas-station McDonalds that got dropped into a bad frat party.  But at least there's some entertaining people-watching.  And I didn't get ill eating here.

*I am, alas, zero percent Cherokee, which is unfortunate.  But not as unfortunate as that whiz sauce.

I honestly would give 0 stars if possible, the owner is the most rude, arrogant person in business that I have encountered. After I waited for almost an hour after ordering my food, I called the establishment and was informed that they had mistakenly cancelled my order. When I requested confirmation of my refund, I was yelled at, belittled, and talked to like a child by the owner. He literally hung up on me 3 times after my request, and had the audacity to ask me if I thought he cares about a refund. Never again!!!

Your boy from Philly right here! This is not a Philly cheesesteak. It is solely a tourist attraction but if thats what you're looking for, Pat's and Geno's are your main men. 
The only reason this doesn't have one star, is because they are open 24/7... huge plus when you're drunk at 3 a.m. Any cheesesteak can appear good at 3 a.m.
(Notice how most reviewers visiting from outside of Philly give it 4 or more stars, but most people from Philly give it 3 or less.. hurts our reputation of a truly good cheesesteak)
Overall not from Philly, test it out, realistically its better than whatever nastiest you call a cheesesteak back home #steak-ums

I went about 2 weeks ago and ordered almost the same thing I did tonight and the same combo I ordered two weeks ago came with fries, now I guess you have to ask for them because we didn't get any with our combo and we repeated the order twice and whoever is in pickup window 1 said no your meal doesn't come with fries which doesn't make a bit of sense to me that had ordered the same combo two weeks ago and I got fries not to mention I didn't even get a receipt so I'm not even sure if I was charged for fries or not and anyway I can't go to McDonald's and not get some fries come on now like really, but honestly everything else was freshly made and not to mention one of the few McDonald's you can get milkshakes from without them telling you the the milkshakes are not working. Still I'm a little disappointed for not getting fries with my meal was the menu changed between 2 weeks ago and today?! I'm confused! I'm sure I'm not the only customer who has gone through this situation.

As a first time tourist in philly, I knew I had to come here! 

I will base my rating off of comparing Pats to Genos since they're right next to each other.
Pats bread had the perfect crunch. The ratio of meat, cheese, and bread was amazing as well. Overall, each bite was evenly distributed with deliciousness. 
The meat used much more stingy and cut up compared to Genos and had a similar consistency to bulgogi. 
Also less cheese was used.

Pat's a close 2nd compared to Genos. Some of my group liked Pats more. Overall had a good experience and would recommend it to other tourists as well

Apparently I'm a glutton for cheese steaks and I didn't even know it.  If you've ever had a cheese steak anywhere in Chicago, you'll know they just don't compare to the original from Philly.  Now, I had never sampled a cheese steak here in Chicago, but I can tell you that I sampled four different restaurants in Philly and Pat's was by far the best.

As you can read in my review of Geno's, the establishment kiddy corner from Pat's, the xenophobic bigotry was a turn off enough to not even want to eat there, but the food was also bad.  Pat's was just higher quality, period.

The service was great.  The guy that takes your steak order is a little hard to understand, but he totally gets the job done if you make sure to read the sign that says "How to Order."  If you're ready when you get to the window, he'll mumble what he needs to and ask for your money.  Definitely not rude service and ordering is really, really quick.  Your sandwich comes out the same window, so don't walk away without it!

Proceed down to the next window to order sides and drinks.  These people were very friendly (not like the people at window #2 at Geno's) and they were interested in where I was from and that other kind of stuff.  Prices were a bit less expensive and the service is friendlier.  I'll take that (even with higher prices) over rude jerks any day.  

There's no bathroom at either establishment, so beware.  We took a cab down here and back (about $15 total), so it was worth it to go to this part of town for lunch.  There's nothing else to do here, anyway, so you may as well hold it and just go back to wherever you came from.  Definitely worth a bus/cab ride down here just to get a delicious cheese steak.

The Original home of the cheesesteak, invented the steak sandwich in 1930.

Pat's King of Steaks is still owned and operated by the Olivieri family. 

The Fresh Roll, Grilled Steak, Peppers & Onions.

Eating on the street adds to the experience too.

Geno's Cheese Steaks just across the street, must have both.  Be careful choosing one over the other as your favorite, this has been known to drive a wedge between family members.

So, this is one of my favorite places to take out-of-towners on a Saturday night.  Truly the best dinner and a show option in Philly.  The thing is though, you don't know what kind of show you're going to see.  Here are some of the shows: a crackhead smoking crack in the lobby, a fight behind the registers, the racist employees beating Asians in the street, someone stealing a bicycle, delivery driving screaming at the employees because of long wait times, a table of four all with buttcracks sticking out and staring you down, a junkie shooting up in the corner booth, or one person trying to run the entire restaurant.  I really love this place.  I have to, unfortunately, only give four stars though because the bathroom is pretty gross every time I've used it. 
 Otherwise, a five star experience!  BRING BACK THE BEEFY CRUNCH BURRITO!!!

3.25 to be exact.

Looking for a Philly Cheesesteak? Well this one is your typical Philly Cheesesteak.  Between this place and the one next to it, Geno's I'd go with Pat's. 

Pat's is known to be one of the famous Philly Cheesesteak spots, and while the cheesesteaks are not bad and a good size, there have been many other cheesesteak spots in Philly that have popped up which in my opinion serve superior cheesesteaks.  However, do not get me wrong, with all the lights and glamor here, a tourist will not be disappointed.  

As a tourist tip, make sure you order this way for prompt service:

Step 1: Mention if you want onions on your steak
Step 2: Specify type of cheese (plain, Cheez Wiz, Provolone, American, or Pizza-style) Step 3: Pay (CASH ONLY!) 
Step 4: First window is for ordering your steak only, while the second window is for fries and drinks.

My favorite steak here would have Provolone, and I like the fries here too!

The classic, the iconic, the king... of steaks.

I've lived in Philly now for six years, and everything you've heard about Pat's is true. They are the original and they are fantastic. The service is speedy-speedy, especially because there are two windows: one for your steak sandwich, and the other is your drinks/fries. You just walk right up and order (for me, it's a whiz witout), the steak is fresh and ready to go, he slaps the whiz on the roll and in maybe ten seconds or less you're ready to go.

Something people never talk about, though, is the price... It's a little way pricey, like over $9.00 for a cheese steak, but for a taste of classic Philadelphia, it's definitely worth trying if you're in the area. The way I figure, you're not just paying for the steak sandwich, you're also paying for the right to say "I've had a true Philly cheese steak". You're paying for the ambiance, the experience... But don't get me wrong, the cheese steak itself is certainly worthy of the price.

It's definitely a little tourist-y, especially because of just how famous it is, but that's not really a problem. There's plenty of seating, and it's relatively easy to get to. If you're driving in, odds are you won't find a parking spot, but that's generally true no matter where you are in the city. But the Broad Street Line stops right nearby, so it's a nice place to have lunch if you're already out.

I don't know what else I can say that hasn't already been said among the hundreds of other reviews. Though my one review is merely a drop in the bucket relative to the total amount there are, that in itself speaks to the sheer quality of Pat's Steaks.

Be sure to join the league of people who can say they've had a taste of history and get your steak sandwich today!

We have heard a lot of recommendations for this place and we finally decided to give it a try. We went around 7:30 and although it was pretty packed, we sat right down. It remained busy for the entire time that we were there (about 2 hours). Although, a lot of people were chatting and enjoying themselves after their meal was finished. 

We told the server that we were first-timers. He was excellent. He gave recommendations and was very patient as we decided. We did not feel rushed at all throughout the dining experience. He brought us multiple servings of chips and salsa, which were delicious. 

We both got different margaritas and we enjoyed both of them. For dinner, we split several things. The nachos, which we were told were very large. If you've had large portions of nachos, you will know that these were not even close to large. They were good and they were suitable for this meal, however, if you are splitting them with other people, I highly recommend the larger size because they aren't very big. We also got the plantains which were delicious and we split chicken tacos. My boyfriend enjoyed those more than I did but they weren't bad...I just preferred our other two plates. I typically save room for dessert but we were tapped out so I cannot comment on desserts here. 

We will definitely return. The service and food were both enjoyable. I look forward to coming back in the spring so we can sit in their outdoor seating area. 

I will say this, it's pretty loud inside so if you are looking for a quiet, intimate dining experience, this is not the location for such an event. It's more of a causal, energetic place to talk, eat and enjoy some cocktails.

OMG. I've never really had a real Philly cheesesteak before. I've been to some spots in California, and other spots, but never from where the legit stuff is at. So where do I go when I finally get to Philly? Pat's of course. Now why Pat's and not Geno's? I honestly just went with my friends' recommendation. Geno's looks pretty flashy with all them lights around it, while Pat's looks like it hasn't changed forever.

If you're coming for a quick snack, be prepared to wait in line for about half and hour, but just rest assured. It's well worth the wait. One thing that your should note is that there are two lines. The long one is JUST for cheesesteaks, while the other, shorter line is for drinks and french fries. 

Wiz Wit. Just remember those two words and you're set. Cheese wiz on a sandwich makes ALL the difference. I've had cheesesteaks with provolone and other cheeses, but cheese wiz is definitely the way to go. The guys here literally just slap the wiz onto your cheesesteak. One of these babies will run you around $9, which is so worth the money. By the time you finish waiting in line, you're ready to scarf this thing down. The meat is both juicy and loose. Because the meat is chopped up, it's easy to eat and bit into. I think I ended up killing off my cheesesteak in less than 5 minutes. I don't have much that I can compare Pat's to, but shoot, this is definitely the best cheesesteak that I've ever had. If you're coming to Philly, then this place is a must. 

Cash only here, so be prepared to come with at least $10 a person. Parking is all street parking, so be prepared to search for a spot like a hawk.

Not your average fast food burger joint. I've been here many times before and it's a staple for my treat-yoself days. The major points that make it stand out from other burger joints are 1) unlimited peanuts, 2) unlimited toppings, and 3) generosity with the fries!!

The customer service is great, I have never received a wrong order or missing parts (not easy when people get topping-happy), and a "medium" fry is actually a large, since they add in an extra handful of fries after they fill the cup. I do think shake shack narrowly wins in terms of burger taste, but Five Guys Cajun fries are in their own category. There is room in this city for both restaurants that make a mean burger.

While I was extremely disappointed by Geno's Cheesteak across the street, Pat's Cheesesteak was quite simply the bomb!   In fact, I was so enamored with my sandwich that I went ahead and ordered a second one even though I was completely full.   I figuratively stuffed my face with this bready meat & cheese goodness.   I'm salivating just thinking about it...

Walked to this infamous Philly cheesesteak joint with my bestie after the rock n roll expo. We both were hungry and ready to devour Philadelphia's staple sandwich. We both ordered a Philly cheese with provolone and onions. Then walked over to where the condiments were with mustard, hot sauce and peppers. I happily loaded my cheesesteak with every hot pepper. I immediately took a bite and it was DELICIOUS!!! Meat was tender, cheese melted, onions buttery with the right amount of grease. The peppers complimented well with this ingenious concoction. We both finished it while walking back to the apartment. I gave it 4 stars due to the soft bread. I'm a sesame hero fan with a crunch. People try it!!! don't listen to the bad reviews! Form your own opinion once you take a bite out of meat heaven!

I wanted to edit my Cantina review because they have really improved in the last year. They have new management, new staff and new food. I love the atmosphere in the bar area--it's friendly and not too loud to have a conversation. I usually end up having a beer or two and one special margarita. Most recently, I had a cherry margarita. It tasted like a cherry limeade--I'm definitely getting another one! 

Brunch is my preferred meal at Cantina. They always feature new specials and delicious Bloody Marys and Marias.

My favorite picks at Cantina?
-goat tacos or burrito
-plantains
-ensalada de nopal
-breakfast burrito with veggie sausage
-pastel de chocolate (chocolate mousse with a bit of hot chili)

If you want to get the most out of it, head to Cantina during a weekday or night--or for a late brunch (try between 2 and 4pm). It gets VERY crowded on weekend nights so plan ahead.

Amazing customer service , everything was fast & efficient. All of our needs were met with the assistance of the young lady Raven. She is an outstanding staff member. The entire staff was OFF THE CHAIN !  Best Taco Bell ever !!!!!!

First time in Philly. First stop is this place!

The Line: Just make your decision in line because you will be grilled if you don't know what you want by the time its your turn. Learn the jargon! 

Food: I love cheesesteak so I love this place. The cheese wiz sauce is awesome and thats really all you need to know because thats all you should get first time here!

Overall: Tourists welcome please come here bc I know you will anyways.

Absolutely the worst Wendy's I've ever been to....Seriously!!!! Ordered 3 things, a cheeseburger with out mayo, a medium lemonade and 5 piece nuggets, simple right!?! My thoughts exactly. Instead I received a cheeseburger with what seemed to be extra mayo, I mean the thing had globs oozing from the sides, a lemonade and no nuggets.  Giving them the benefit of the doubt, I kindly informed them of the mistake in hopes of a quick fix so I can be on my way.  Nope....the correction consisted of a DOUBLE cheeseburger (with mayo of course) and SPICY nuggets. To make matters worst, there was no one in the line ahead of me (should have been a sign) so my order should have been to the point and clear.  What was supposed to be a quick 5 min trip to Wendy's turned into a half hour ordeal.

Love the sandwich  philly wit came to pick up after a Philly Sox game.Bring cash and trying to park was crazy a native a from Houston .Didnt get Pa no beer from a convenient store was okay had a good time in Pa.

Given that this is definitely one of those tourist spots, I don't go outta my way to grab a steak from Pats but when I am in the area, I don't venture out here unless it's like 1:30 am on a Tuesday night just to avoid a crowd of sorts. 

But like I said, Pat's is a tourist spot as is Genos but I'd highly recommend anyone to grab a steak from Pats before they swing onto Genos for the sole reason that Pat's steaks are chopped oh-so finely and is full of flavor whereas Genos gives you a legit slab of meat plus cheese.  

I'm not saying that Pat's is the be all, end all of cheesesteaks but it does live up to it's rep and it's pretty much melt in your mouth goodness. 

Whatever you heard about the staff is probably true. The staff's pretty intimidating but it's probably for show.
The cheesesteak is great. Make sure to get lots of cheese whiz. The only problem is the safety of the location. But it's worth it if you are ordering off GoldBelly.

I went to Jason's Toridasu when they served sushi and when the menu changed at first I was heartbroken. BUT the new menu is so amazingly delicious that I quickly forgot my heartache. The food is so good in fact I ordered it back to back days. I had the chicken rice bowls both times and the side salad. The rice bowls and packed with food and flavor. The chicken is super crispy even with all the sauce on top. The spice mayo and the tonkatsu sauce are so good I wish they bottled and sold it. The side salad is probably the best salad deal I have ever ordered. You get half a ripe avocado in a $4 side salad. I will definitely be back to try more of the new menu.

Tourist attraction, but rightfully so, these guys technically invented the Philly Cheesesteak. This place is much more classic and simple (nothing like Geno's). But like Geno's their seating is covered picnic tables wrapping around the building. Although the rolls at Geno's across the street may be a little better the sandwich and the steak is better here at Pats. So come here so you can say you've been to the birthplace of the sandwich but if you want shorter lines and more food for the money go to a better cheesesteak place like Tony Lukes.

Eh...

I could honestly just end the review there. Pat's, the King of Steaks? Perhaps more like a naked Prince Harry? That works. 

Being that its notoriety spans the globe, I suppose I just expected more. It wasn't awful, but it definitely ranks in the bottom percentile among other cheese steaks I've had everywhere outside of Philly. 

On the plus side, it was as fast as a greased pig getting my order, even though the line spanned about 20 deep. For a quick bite, their execution was flawless. As for the taste, not so much....

I love a good 'za -- especially one I can personalize to my exact liking. And that's exactly what I get at Blaze. You can start with a base of whatever you'd like, including any of their signature pizzas. I usually begin with a base of the red vine, and add as many additional toppings as I feel like sprinkling on that day. Then, I love to top it off with some balsamic drizzle, and voila!

The pizza makers and bakers are all so friendly, and happy to explain the process if you have any questions. Overall, it makes for a fun meal, and if your dinner partner also gets his or her own individual pizza, then y'all can exchange a slice of your creations. That way I can be mostly good with my veggie-laden red vine and still enjoy a slice of meat lovers without feeling too guilty. ;)

Overall, a fun and fast way to do dinner!

A tourist trap 100%. I came from San Diego in hopes to find some good cheesesteaks, San Diego has way better cheese steak than this place. Very bland food with pats, it's so bland that's why there's ketchup station

Had to come as a tourist. Over hyped. Cheesesteak was dry and average taste. Get the fries! Those were delicious. Wait time in like is about 10 mins but you get your food right away. There's outdoor seating around the entire locations.

If you're going to order the standard, classic Philly cheesesteak you can only order it one way: wiz with.

I was staying in Philly for the weekend and got in a little late so my friend and I decided to grab cheesesteaks from Pat's and Geno's. Honestly not my first choice, but they are both open 24/7 so it was the first that came to mind so late at night. 

I was surprised to find that a cheesesteak was $10, but shrugged it off. Pat's is most certainly a tourist spot, but it's not a trap. These cheesesteak are most definitely original Philly-style cheesesteaks and won't shatter any dreams. 

Are they the best? Probably not. Do they satisfy my cheesesteak craving? Yes. 

That being said, Pat's is much better late at night than during the day. There is almost no line and, more importantly, the steak is chopped to order. This makes for a less-dry and tenderer steak. The onion's aren't too overwhelming and mingles well with the wiz. Some complain that there is too much wiz and not enough onion; they should try Geno's. 

Pat's is better in my book, but only marginally.

Unfortunately, not the best cheesesteak I've had during my time in Philly (See my favorite at By George! in the Reading Terminal Market). But I'm a Pat (my bf is a Geno). 

I liked the shredded beef and onions. Got with provolone but definitely get the cheese whiz since it adds flavor and salt to the sandwich.

Bring your cash!!!! Cash only. 
Awesome cheesesteaks! My favorite place for some unhealthy food in philly! The meat is juicy and sooo flavorful. Every bite was a good bite that I wanted more and more. The classic cheese whiz was just as amazing as the mushroom-pepper cheesesteak. 

The people here ate not as nice as at Geno's because they didn't cut the cheesesteaks into smaller portions for us when asked. 

Ay, good food but not so nice service hmmmm...Geno's or Pat's for future visits???! decision decision!

Went to the drive-thru and sat there for 30 minutes. One of the cars honked just to see what was going on and then finally a worker spoke in the intercom screaming "honking won't get you your food any faster". Both windows had 2 people working and I am sure 2 more in the kitchen. They charge extra for sauces...I got a large fries and it was literally the size of a small. Very poor service!

Be ready to order when you get to the window, or else.....
As for the cheesesteak , it is really fresh and the bread is perfect.  The steaks get cold fast but still taste great. Don't expect indoor seating or even a bathroom, but be prepared for a long line which can wrap around the building on occasion.  If it 's you first time to Philly you must make this iconic restaurant a stop.
Oh... and they are open all night!

Occasion: Touristing it with the husband

Eat Geno's first and get it out of the way. Pat's is better, there shouldn't even be a competition. I enjoyed the sandwich for what it is. Definitely liked the way they chopped up the meat and preferred their bread (crunchy on the outside but soft without being too chewy inside). Also I am a fan of the cheez wiz. You must also get a side of fries wit wiz. Might as well.

Also we walked from Old City to South Philly round trip and recommend it. It might help you feel less sh*tty later.

My girlfriend and I took a three day trip to Philly - our first time, so why not try cheesesteaks.  I tried Campos - very, very meh - so on a friend's recommendation I decided that we should try Pat's the next day.
