This is without a doubt my favorite chicken and rice spot. They have a good variety in their menu and the prices are average, and they are open late. I feel that there chicken and rice platter is not as greasy as other places but still packs the flavor so you don't feel as sluggish after eating.

I've been a huge fan of Shake Shack for quite some time and I was totally excited to have them open up a location in Philly. I definitely wasn't going to wait in those crazy lines when this place opened up though. After the hype died down, I managed to stop in twice to no wait.

All in all, their burgers are a bit on the small side (something that's always been true). Are they delicious though? Yes. Are their fries good for being frozen? Yeah. Are the burgers a bit greasy? Sure. Is this a bad thing? Depends on who's asking.

I think I'm over with going out of my way for Shake Shack but I'm still a fan of their burgers. Not much of a milk shake person though.

I was really glad to see this Taiwanese restaurant open in Chinatown! I shared a jumbo squid with my friend and I had also ordered my own chicken bento box. In terms of service, they took a while to get the food ready even though my friends and I were the only ones in the restaurant at the time. In terms of the food, I thought that the fried coating had a very superficial taste that didn't quite penetrate into the meat and I was left rather unimpressed.

A previous reviewer said they are heavy scoopers here - and they weren't wrong! I've been to many Chipotle's, but here's one where I feel like the amount of food that got in my goal was actually worth the price. I found the steak a bit spicier than other Chiptoles, so I probably wouldn't get steak there again, but hey, it also could have just been the day I went.

Some of the best tacos in Philly. You have to enjoy the mix between korean and american. Got a mix of 3 tacos (bulgogi, double fried chicken and spicy pork on special). Packed with flavor and I can taste the Korean and Mexican flavors. Delish

I'm giving them a 4th star because they are one of the few places that brew organic ice tea that is not, I repeat NOT, brewed through machines that brew coffee as well. This allows for pleasant ice tea taste and no nasty old coffee filter after taste. I'm looking at your DD. They also brew it year round which is another huge plus for me. And a final kudos for outdoor seating that doesn't take over the entire sidewalk that is placed on the shaded side of the building. So you can sit outside without getting baked even if there is no umbrella at your table.

Customer service was good. Food was McDonalds quality. We ordered medium #1 and #4 both fries were below medium size portions. Quite a few letters being loud in the lobby. Went to the men's room to use the urinal and there wasn't any urinal cake set so it was dirty and smelly.  2 stars for the place less if customer service wasn't up to par. I'd recommend using their drive thru instead if your aren't comfortable with the atmosphere stated above.

Shake Shack is doing it right! I was impressed with the flavor profile, definitely a step up from normal fast food. I had the Bird Dog with spicy tomato-simmered onions. Low calorie and more delish than your average chicken sausage. My boyfriend had the Shack Stack which was SO FREAKIN' GOOD. The cheese-stuffed shrooms and shacksauce are on point. When in need of some delicious, greasy food I'll be back. Also the employees were adorably nice.
The shake shack burger is very good and the fries are stellar. My preference for the shakes would be the vanilla milk shake. Great for lunch or dinner.

Not many places i can chill outside with a burger and a milkshake of decent quality. To those who hate..this is a semi fast food joint smack dab in the middle of phillys drinking scene..be happy its not a mcds or another low quality fast food chain and just run with it. You wanna get fancy, your in luck, village whiskey is across the street. I dig this place to chill old school style w a burger n shake.
Stopped on my way to NYC I ordered a jewish hoagie it was  very good very fresh jewish hoagie it was delicious

I'm not a huge fan of Chick-Fil-A myself...it's fine, but I prefer Wendy's and Five Guy's and BBP and lots of other "fast food" places much better, but my coworkers love Chick-Fil-A so sometimes we pick up lunch from this location. The Gallery isn't the nicest place, and this food court area is somewhat dirty and oftentimes has trash strewn about.

I will say that the service is great - the employees are always smiling and willing to help, and last time I was offered a free Cherry Coke. Sorta weird, but also sorta nice. I'm surprised by other reviewers saying anything negative about the service...I've only ever received quick, efficient and friendly service.

Ok, I get the shake shack hype now. My experience was great. The food came out fast, hot, and delicious; I was thoroughly impressed.

Positives- I got a double cheese burger and a side of cheese fries.  The fries were hot and crispy and cheese sauce was on-point, son.  The burger was put together well, fresh lettuce, and tomato, Martin's potato roll, the meat was seasoned well, and cooked to medium. Personally, I thought it was incredibly satisfying and one of the best burgers I've had in a while. The cheese was good. I couldn't taste the shake shack sauce to well in my burger, but I was OK with that. I could tell the ingredients and beef were fresh and good quality; which is a big deal for me.

Negatives- It's pricey. I won't BS you. And I felt like I could have gotten a few more fries.  The burger was also a bit greasy.  But you're eating a Damn cheese burger; that's to be expected sometimes.
Insanely good! The Crispy Hipcity Ranch Chich'n is so so good! It absolutely exceeded my expectations. Must try for vegans and omnivores alike! Better than chicken!

Double Smoke, Single Stack, Strawberry Shake, Crinkle Fries, Concrete = yummy in my tummy.

Burgers are definitely good. I'd say probably better than five guys, and definitely better than In-and-out. 

Concrete is great. Would definitely come back.

I love that Uptown Turkey and Loaded Baked Potato soup both super delicious and the prices are reasonable. Not only that but there is wait staff that bring your meal to you. It's a cute little place for traditional American dishes

This review comes with a preface~

I was in NY a year ago and walked by this place that was just crowded as hell with a line out the door, it was all bright, glittery, and "hay look at me!" I cringed. I don't do those sorts of places. I didn't even look to see what the name was. So I was in NY again a couple of weeks ago and interestingly enough... after having a burger (see my 5 Napkin review) I got back on to 8th Ave and started walking the same direction I did before. Again I passed this obnoxiously crowded place and this time I noticed it was Shake Shack. Err. I thought Shake Shack in Philly can't be this bad. And actually I tried to get in there one time months ago, but I didn't have the patience.

So yesterday I said eff it, I'm goin in! I only had to wait about 3 minutes.

[Enter the review]

I've finally become desensitized to expensive burgers. I barely flinch anymore. I didn't think the fries would be a winner so I just went with the double smoke stack (bacon cheeseburger with peppers) and a fifty/fifty. I was surprised to see so many people ordering doubles. I rarely do that myself.

I have no complaints about the burger whatsoever. It was great. The peppers were a nice touch. What really would've done it for me are crumbled bleu cheese and BBQ sauce. But the drink... half lemonade half iced tea is rip off. It's not even sweetened and it costs almost $3 for a reasonable size. That's a scumbag move. I don't see the value in that. I had to use sugar packets to get it right. I'm fortunate they had desert spoons so I could stir it. I wouldn't expect a cafe style bottled simple syrup in a burger joint so this should be sweetened already. The packets are lame. And I don't wanna hear anybody talkin about not everybody likes it sweetened. That's nonsense. This isn't a teahouse. This is fast food.

It was too cold for a shake and too cold to sit outside. The inside seating is lame. I mean really. And the to-go bag/box is cool, but the food is exposed and doesn't keep anything warm. Overall, it'll be SOME time before I come back.

It's a good burger. The fries are a little salty.  I like that they have cups for the water tap on the wall.  

It doesn't really live up to the hype and long lines.  If you want a serious burger, walk across the street to Village Whiskey or make your own. If you're looking for a juicy burger on the cheap, Shake Shack will do if you don't have to wait very much.

Atmosphere makes a difference to me.  I've been to the original Shake Shack in NYC, so it's really about what makes the Philly one stand out.  Well, for starters, indoor seating with Indy rock music is always a great start.  In a city with limited liquor licenses, it is great to see they got one and serve Brooklyn Brewing amongst other beers and wines.   I went with the single with cheese and a Coke Zero.  Crinkle cut fries are nothing unique so I passed to save room for a Concrete.  The burger is a great juicy and flavorful one and the onions were perfectly ripe.  The concrete though was the top attraction of the meal - vanilla custard, Termini Bros Canoli shell, lemon ricotta, and strawberry purée mixed together made for the perfect end to a great meal.  I highly recommend stopping in for the ever growing in popularity, burger.

The food was excellent, very fulling. Custom Service was great. There was a guy working there, named tasheed and he was seriously the nicest person I have ever meet. As soon as I was done my food he came by and grabbed my plate for me, I also saw him going around individually asking people if they needed anything, and asked them how the food was. If that isn't called customer service I don't know what is.
The worst vanilla shake ever.  Do they know to put syrup in it ? Ice cream plus milk is NOT a shake. It is ice cream and milk.  So disappointing. Zero stars on the shake.

Nice addition to the area and a new spot to add to my lunch rotation.  I enjoyed both the chicken tikka kati and the mixed vegetable kati.  The mixed vegetable had way more flavor and spice and my carnivorous self has a hard time admitting I liked it a whole lot more than the chicken.

I agree with other reviewers....the hot sauce is good but could use more flavor (garlic, onion, something) and the white sauce similarly neededs a little something more.   Also, would be nice to have an appetizer size portion of something on menu - samosa?  and/or a side salad to have when just having kati.  One kati was not enough but two was too many.  

I'm definitely going back.

I came here during dinner hours,  and it was quiet and empty. I ordered the spice end platter,  as it seemed like the signature platter. I really liked the amount of rice and chicken! It tasted very good,  and was pretty spicy,  so people sensitive to spice,  beware! The cashier at the time was also courteous,  so that was a plus.

first time at HCV today! i always forget about the HCV on broad b/c it looks so tiny next to all the big store fronts like capital grill and wells fargo! 

i've heard HCV was somewhat legendary in the vegan food frontier in philly, but i had no idea what item they're really known for.  (i'm a little behind with the times) so i just ordered what sounded appealing to me.. i went for the disco chick'n sandwich that came with garlic aioli.  i honestly didn't know what "chick'n" entailed.. but i figured i'd give it a try.  i was 90% sure i wasn't getting actual meat LOL and i was right! lol so deceiving just by the whiff of the sandwich lol.

it definitely did not disappoint! the sandwich was very juicy! and the sauces were amazing and went so well together! i have no idea what they put on it but it was magic!  great surprise at lunch today! i would definitely return to try other things! don't let the meatless meat fool u, the sandwich is quite filling!

Yummy chopped salad (roasted chicken, bacon, avocado, bleu cheese, tomatoes, green onions with iceberg/romaine lettuce & sweet and spicy house vinaigrette) with & really yummy loaded potato soup. I wait patiently every week for Wednesday to come around so I can go get me a bowl of loaded potato soup.

One thing though...
WHY DO YOU CLOSE AT 5pm?? I went to corner bakery yesterday, so happy but when I got to the door.. IT WAS LOCKED. I was not a happy camper when I got back to my boyfriend's car, & he knew it. Besides the one downside that Corner Bakery doesn't open past 5pm, I think it's a great place to get a satisfying soup/salad, sandwich/salad deal. (Kinda like a cheap Panera)

The only real reason I go, is for the loaded potato soup. Mmmm.

I thought my original review was in need of some updating since going back to CA and having my beloved In 'n Out. (I had previously said that my fast food burger favorite was still In 'n Out.)

Shake Shack, although on the pricier side, is definitely better than In 'n Out. It's simply a greater burger that uses high quality, well seasoned meat. That's the difference. When I went back to CA, I was actually disappointed with In 'n Out. In other words, Shake Shack ruined In 'n Out for me!

Shake Shack will cost you more than the average fast food burger but really it's in a league of its own. Worth the price you pay.

The burgers are great for fast food but their prices just jumped up from pretty pricey for fast food too crazy for fast food. Burger, fries, and a float cost $20. Would be five stars if not for the price hike.
Ordered Kathi roll and Biryani, they could have tasted better. The location seems good, however they should focus improving the taste.

I wished we had one of these in Baton Rouge because this place was so delicious! So I splurged and got the Shack Stack burger which was very delicious, filling and amazing! I don't know who made this burger up but it's the best idea ever! So imagine a cheeseburger with a fried Portobello mushroom that's stuffed with Muenster cheese sitting on top of the meat patty then add lettuce, tomatoes and shacksauce and you've got the most amazing burger ever! It was so messy to eat but that's how you know it's a delicious burger right? So I didn't get any fries or their famous shakes because the burger was huge and I knew I was gonna be so full (and I was) but from what I heard they have some of the best shakes and frozen custards in town.
     I also loved that on the menu they have a couple of items for your pup that you can buy. They have "Bag o Bones" which is a bag of dog biscuits and "Poochini" which is a dog friendly custard mix with peanut butter sauce and some dog biscuits in it. That's so original and cute. If that's not dog friendly then I don't know what is. They also have several tables and chairs outside so people can enjoy their delicious burgers and shakes while their pets enjoy their treats too. The staff was very friendly and our orders came out pretty quick despite the amount of people that were in line. I will definitely come back again to get another Shack Stack but this time I'm gonna have to get a shake to go.

The buzz for this place has been fed by hype from "bridge and bridge" people as well as transplants who really really wish they could have lived in "NYC" but had to settle for Philly instead.   Going some place to be seen is sad; it's especially sad when that place serves burgers and shakes.  Being impressed with a long line is a sign you're lacking something in your life.

I went, because I wanted to confirm that it was all hype, plus I love me some burgers and shakes. I just wasn't any more impressed by this place than I am by any decent diner that serves milkshakes.  Sorry, kids, you're buying into a slick product again.  But it's OK, because you look cool while doing it.

PS:  Doobies has had bowling alley tables since before they were cool, and don't make a big fucking deal about it.
Love love love their chicken and rice platter!!!! So flavorful and delicious!! I always visit this place every time I am in Philly. I've also had their paneer Kati rolls which are delicious!

Subway is the only 'fast food' I eat, and this location is probably my favorite in the city.  The bread is always fresh.  One the best parts about this place is that they always have plenty veggie patties on hand, which for a vegetarian, is a nice option.

I got a footlong Veggie Delite yesterday and it was a good, cheap dinner.  The components were decent for what they were, albeit none of high quality or in their prime.  The hoagie was well made with the right amounts of oil and vinegar and seasoning.

It's pretty well kept in the dining area, and the staff has always been professional and quick.  I've never had a language barrier at this location, and I go in once a month or so.

Nothing earth shattering here folks, it's still a Subway, but it's a decent one.

Spicy, flavorful, and fabulous!

Kati Rolls are something wonderful.  Think Naan wrapped around the delicious indian cuisine!  The Kati rolls are actually a Roti with paneer (cheese), or lamb, or cheese, or veggies wrapped inside with onions.   MMMMMM!!! I could honestly eat these every day!
 
I came here two days in a row and tried three different Rolls.  Lamb, Paneer, Paneer.  They were all spiced well.  The Lamb had the most kick.  They also give you a red pepper sauce and a raita (yogurt sauce) which blend well with the flavors.  The Mango Lassi was very thick, creamy, and not too sweet.

I've been to 2 different places that sell Kati rolls.  The size and flavors of the rolls here were comparable.  

I talked with one of the men, asking many questions.  He was helpful and seemed to enjoy explaining things.  They make the Roti (bread) on site.  

Walk by, try it. :)

I ended up at Snap Kitchen because I am on a pre-bikini diet and desperately needed to eat something, really anything, other than salad. Unfortunately, Snap Kitchen was not a good solution.

Deviled Eggs
The deviled eggs were terrible. The ratio of tahini, yolk, and seasonings was all kinds of wrong. It was like eating sour hummus on top of egg whites. Yuck. 

Kale Hoppin John
This is a bowl of rice, hummus, kale, sweet potatoes, and seeds. It needed texture and flavor.

Vegetable Lasagna
The vegetable lasagna was actually good. Lots of flavor and good texture from the variety of vegetables used. 

And the prices? Well, if you are someone who needs a lot of calories to get full, your wallet will be unhappy. Don't do this to yourself unless you are on a sad diet. Please. I'm still hangry.

I have been to this place twice since it opened and have loved it both times. The staff is extremely nice and hospitable (even to stumbling drunk people) and the food is great!
I have had all the chicken and lamb rolls and they have all been as good as you can get in Philly. In fact, they're even better than the New York kathi roll spots. My particular favorites are the Chicken Achari, Chicken and Egg and Lamb Kabab Rolls. 
This place is great at what it does and that is good food with great customer service. Do not go in expecting a fancy decor and a 20-page menu. Menu is small but great and the decor is not much to write home about. However, if you want some spicy indian kathi rolls which leave you wanting for more with every bite then this is where you want to go.
Yes, please. $25 for two burgers, fries, and two shakes. A bit expensive? Yep. Delicious? Double yep.  The fries are super salty (I'm a fan of this, but I know others may not be).

Came here this past Saturday, possibly quite intoxicated but all the more makes me more open minded about food. My boyfriend and I ordered the bacon cheeeeeese burger, fried chicken sandwich and a hot dog and of course 2 cheese fries. The bacon cheese burger was great, bun could be toasted better but the quality of the ingredients inside made up for it. The fried chicken sandwich was great! I thought the texture of the chicken was perfect but could use more spread, whatever was in there. The hot dog... I don't know why I ordered it but don't. It's plain it's boring. The fries, good as any crinkle fries. I would maybe come here again but I think there are far more better burger joints in Philadelphia but for something fast, I would recommend it.
Why is this place so popular? Fries are great but thr burgers are no better than Wendy's
This spot is great!  We had two different types of tacos and a rice bowl.  Everything was delicious.  Food came our quickly and the service was friendly.  Definitely going back.

The workers at this location are always rushing you and they all seem miserable. They always run out of stuff and never have anything prepared. They won't make more and ask if you want to wait if it gets late, it's just "no we're out move on". I love chipotle but this location is horrible.

I feel like this place is a hidden gem.  The reason is that I was walking by one day, and decided to walk in and check it out.  I had no idea what it was all about.  Let's just say it was one of the best decisions I ever made, lol.  My 2 favorites are the Aloo Paneer Roll and Beef Tikka Roll (beef seems slow cooked and so tender).  The flavors are just amazing, and really a party in your mouth.  Also, the times I went there, I was greeted with friendly smiles and respect.  Knowing it was my first time there, they asked if I liked the food and made sure everything was to my liking.  2 thumbs up guys, keep up the good work.  I will def be back many more times.

Nothing special about the burgers, namely the generic and bland buns. The fries can be found in any freezer section at your local grocery store. Unimpressed and won't be leading the charge to go back anytime soon.

I did notice they serve alcohol.  I'm also not a shake person.  I guess those two things are what keep people coming back, because it sure isn't the burger or fries.

I love everything about Hip City in general, but the extended menu is AMAZING. Breakfast for vegans/vegetarians can be so complicated, and it's amazing that you can grab breakfast so quickly and easily. Staff was super friendly per usual, and my food came out within 10 minutes. Breakfast for your buck is also an incredible deal so don't be a fool and go for it.

They brought free samples into my work today and I took the Vegetarian, which is provolone with an avocado spread, and alfalfa sprouts & tomato & cucumber slices. It was delicious!! Only thing is, next time I would definitely get it without mayo, just made it taste kinda cheap. But looking at the menu they gave me, it seems like the price is pretty good for what you get!

The best fast food place out there, period.  Waffle fries are generally great, but can be undercooked.  The chicken sandwich is a greasy, pickle-juice infused delight.  McDonald's tried to steal their receipe but it's just not as good.  

Only Sonic rivals it for east coast, chain fast food.

Great, affordable, flavorful food. I've ordered food from Spice End a number of times, and also have eaten in. Especially great that it's open late at night for that snack when you're out. 

My favorite is definitely the Paneer Tikka roll. The paneer is so well cooked and tender, and the mint flavor fits in just right. SO GOOD. I also enjoyed the lamb and chicken rolls, and they were also good, but not as good as the paneer tikka. I've also tried the platters which are also pretty good, but I'd say the kati rolls are definitely the specialty here.
Always good food....the selling point on this restaurant is the awesome service you will receive.....definitely worth the trip

The chicken was really really dry.  Tasted as if they had precooked the chicken so it lost a lot of the moisture and there were burnt areas on the chicken as well which tasted bitter.  The sauce was sweet and tasted like a decent teriyaki.  Not sure what makes it much different than most other teriyaki chicken you would order elsewhere.
The customer service was great. The area is great, too. However, the milkshake we got was completely melted. We had a group of 15 and about half of us were not satisfied.

Went here this afternoon thinking there would be some fun things to try out. I have never been to this chain so I didn't really know what to expect but thinking a burger place near Rittenhouse, there had to be something about it! Burgers and fries, that is it. 
Not sure what the hype is about. 
Ordered a burger and a hot dog. Both came out on a toasted buttered martins potato roll.  Don't get me wrong, I love butter, but both items had soaked through the paper products they were served in. Greasy. 
The fries were crinkle cut and basic fries, nothing a little salt couldn't help. 
I guess this place is a BBQ place for people nostalgic about their back home, back in the day BBQs. When dad mashed a burger down flat on the grill and man buttered all the rolls in sight!
Staff was very friendly, I'd go back for a shake and the staff, not the food.
I love the location of this place. It's near everything. The sandwiches are great. I'd rather eat here than any other place on Market Street - or Blimpie's.

I did NOT have a burger, ok? This is a burgerless Shake Shack review. Place opened in June 2012, and SS is about to explode onto Philly, with planned openings in both University City (watch out, Flay!!!) and King of Prussia.

Oh Danny Meyer: thank you for your genius!

Never could make it to Madison Park....so why not Philly?!

The place is stunning. Well done; so stands out at the corner. Very modern, very airy...does not feel like a burger sit-down joint. Like very much. 

Ordered some cheese fries and a banana bourbon small frozen custard. Too full to enjoy their 100% Angus patties.

Def meh on the fries. Zig zag cut, I didn't find the outside crispy enough, or the inside fluffy enough. Cheese sauce was not doing it for me. Not creamy enough, though flavor was ok unique. 

Custard was the best thing about my order. Sooooo, so enjoyable. Took the delicate cup with a slow hand, and savored the treat. 

Spendy place for burgers and the like.

Ok, so I've heard nothing but hype about how good this place is and I must say that I am highly disappointed!  For $12.99 I received a burger with toppings that was slightly bigger than a slider, an order of fries and a large lemonade. The burger was ok, fries were cold and lemonade was iced down!  Do not waste your money people! I've had better burgers at Burger King.. a larger size to boot. This is definitely no bang for your big buck!!! Sad.
The best place to eat after being out all night in Center City! Amazing staff and delicious food.  I always get the Paneer Tikka Roll and Mango Lassi.

I'm a little surprised I never reviewed Shake Shack before, since I've been here a few times and I'm absolutely in love with it. No other burger is as perfect looking and as mouthwatering as the Shack Stack. 

After coming home from a trip to LA and Vegas, dejected and miserable because I was unable to get In-N-Out, I sought out Shake Shack for solace. I'm not really sad I missed In-N-Out anymore, because no one can be sad while eating a Shake Shack burger.

The burgers here are delicious! I would love to get my hands on the meat ratio they use, because their patty is meaty, juicy, and just fatty enough. They are consistent in their use of perfect looking ingredients - center cut slices of bright red, perfectly ripe tomatoes, and beautiful, crisp green lettuce leaves - not that sad white/light green crap they have at McD's so often. And what else to sandwich all this perfection than in a lightly toasted Martin's potato bun? (I read one review that said Shake Shack doesn't toast their buns - but this is wrong. They toast the insides lightly! For sure!).

Definitely the best thing about Shake Shack is their consistency. I feel that I have had the same, identical, delicious burger the first time I came here (a year or two ago) as I did when I came here last (last week). The Shack Stack burger (with the crispy, cheese filled portobello mushroom) is to die for! Just wait a little before digging in, because the cheese is seriously very hot, and you don't want a burnt tongue when you have something truly awesome to taste.

I am not a fan of crinkle cut french fries, but Shake Shack fries don't do any harm. Not bad, but nothing to write home about. It is the standard accompaniment and I will always order them alongside my burger.

For dessert, the Liberty Shell concrete is perfect! I love cannoli's, so I was ecstatic to try it out in ice-cream form. I wish they would add a bit more of the cannoli shells (Termini bro's!), but you don't really have to fix what isn't broken, I guess.

The service here - although not a wait staff - is actually pretty awesome. They offer to take away your trash/tray once you're done eating, and the cashiers are always friendly. Maybe sometimes too enthusiastic at times - one time they chanted my name loudly as they called my order and proudly announced that I was their like 136th customer that day. I was confused yet amused.

I would rate this place 5 stars if the price were a tad bit more agreeable, but still, Shake Shack is one of my favorite burgers ever.

First impressions: This place is pretty good, it's worth the try.
We got here at around 5:45 ish? There was only one person in there, maybe a few people getting pick up. The interior was great, and they have a drink with a bottle of a "muscular man" called muscle milk. Interesting. 

The Ordering: We ordered obviously, the popcorn chicken, what they're known for. 2 orders (each $5) and two sauces (I think they were 25 cents or 50 cents each, don't remember) . The price was okay for the amount of chicken they gave us. The worker seemed kind of bored and looked a little bit like he was doing us a favor. He was kind of unhappy.

The time + The Looks: We waited a little bit and got our chicken fresh, piping hot. It came in one of those red and white cartons. The chicken was in a bag with two skewer sticks. But the sauce. The sauce. It was a solo cup with only a thin layer of sauce at the bottom. Seriously? That's not enough!! 

The taste: The chicken was delicous! I've had Taiwanese popcorn chicken before and this was the best I've had! The coating isn't too much and the batter has a hint of sweetness at the end. It 
was really tasty and I would really get it again. Be careful tho, it was piping hot. The sauce was good, the honey mustard was your typical honey mustard. We got the sriracha sauce which I didn't try. If you want, ask the guy for more, he'll give you more. 

Overall: I would come here again! The atmosphere of the place was lovely and the food was very good. They have other menu options too, bento boxes and other snacks + drinks. 

And btw, the wifi is chi ken lovers and the password is their phone number, just get one of the fliers on the counter, the number is on there

Love this new location in the heart of CC - definitely going to come here more often now that I won't have to walk all the way to Rittenhouse! It's smaller than the one on 18th in that it has just 1 row of seats by the window, but has more room for people to stand and wait for their orders. Truly catered toward takeout. Just as efficient as the other location - when it gets busy, can be a little slow, but they churn out the food pretty quickly. Always worth the wait for great quality.

My boyfriend and I ordered our 2 favorites - the Fajita Wrap and the Crispy Hip City Ranch. They were both BETTER than they usually are at the old location, as if that was even possible!! At this location, they put avocado in the Fajita Wrap, which adds a creamy, fresh element to the wrap. For the Crispy Hip City Ranch, the chick'n patty is thicker and larger, making the sandwich more substantive.

In addition, this location is offering a NEW breakfast menu - really stoked to check it out when I get the chance!

A bit disappointed with this location. The food is not what I'm used to with this chain. The Kung Pao chicken was very over cooked. Same for the Chicken with Mushroom. Hopefully they will improve their quality with time. It seems all of the Philadelphia locations put out the same quality. I've been to the ones at Comcast Center and Granite Run Mall.

Surprised that this place got such good reviews here.

My food was well below average and I wouldn't order again.

Our first time and everything went well.  Food prompt and tasty.  Always wanted to try the food but the NYC store has people lined up down the street.  Now I know its worth it and will frequent as many locations as possible.

I was visiting Philly and heard a lot of good things about the chick'n shack so I decided to give it try. 

What I got:
Chick'n shack
Strawberry milkshake 
Fries 

The chick'n shack was amazingggg! So good. Personally like it better than the shack burger. The reason for the 3 star rating is cause I feel jipped out of my French fries. Paying 3 bucks they barely gave me any fries! So I was disappointed in that. In my picture below you can see that the fries are even filled to the top. Other than that the food was amazing.

Yummy burritos and friendly staff always make for a pleasant experience at the 12th and Walnut Chipotle.  The seating area by the big window facing 12th Street is also great for people-watching, but if you don't have the time to sit and eat, they're more than happy to prepare your meal to go.  This location is also convenient to a number of the neighborhood bars so you can grab a bite amidst your bar-hopping, should you be craving Mexican!

If I lived close to this restaurant, I would probably come here everyday to eat the Chicken Platter. Chicken was tender. Was awesome with extra white sauce and hot sauce. Just go easy on the hot sauce as it's the super spicy variety.

The Chicken Platter would be perfect after finishing a night of clubbing at 3 am. They give you enough food that it's probably good for 2 people. Pretty awesome.

Steve from catering was super helpful. I called on a Sunday morning for a custom sweets box (I wanted breakfast items added bc it was for a brunch) and he had it ready in 30 mins with my custom items added. Thanks for the awesome service!

Don't be fooled by the hype... The long line is just that and nothing more. If you're in the mood for sub-par burgers, being treated rudely by employees when acknowledged at all, and watery shakes, this is the place for you. If not, use the time you would have wasted in line to head to BBP.

Let me start by saying - It is most definitely worth the wait!!!

Several friends had told me about the Shake Shack coming to Philly..  I had no idea what the hype was all about and what I was in for.  I went with high expectations and I have to say they were all met and/or exceeded.

While standing in line a host was walking among the crowd and asking if anyone had any questions and/or wanted to see the menu, I thought this was a nice and friendly welcome.  The menu is impressive considering I had been told this is a "hamburger joint."  Heck they even serve draft or bottles of beer and wine.  I chose to have a Smokehouse burger, fries and vanilla milkshake.  

The smokehouse burger is available in single or double size, I went the the single.  They top a juicy patty of meat with cheese, bacon, chopped cherry red peppers and shake sauce.  What is shake sauce you ask?  It is a special blended mayo - I don't know whats in it BUT its GOOD!  The salty flavor of the bacon melted with the cheese and red peppers was incredible.  I was satisfied with the single size and fear that with a double you may taste too much burger - if that really is even possible, too much burger?? HA!  The fries were fresh and cooked nicely, not soggy and not too crispy.  The shake was very good, it was silky smooth.  By far one of the best i have ever had.

After I had scoffed down my meal, a manager came by and asked how everything was and if there is anything that SS could do to improve their service and/or menu.  "Don't change a thing Shake Shack!"   

I will be back...

I don't understand what all the hype is.  It's just a fast food burger with a slightly better dining room than Burger King.

I had the Shack burger, which was a little to greasy for my tastes.  The roll tasted like it was buttered and then grilled, making it was too sweet and oily.  The patties are on the small side, and although I'm all for portion control, a single burger isn't enough for a lunch.

The fries were average.  Not good enough to crave or go back for, but not a disappointment.  They're not salted so make sure you lightly salt and toss them before eating.

The 50/50 milkshake was probably the best part of the lunch, but still not something I'd go back for on it's own.

I guess this is a better alternative than going to McDonalds with your kids, but I can't place this in an actual restaurant category, this is fast food no matter how trendy they make the experience or how pricey the food is.

If you're in this location, you're pretty much committing a sin by eating a burger here and not skipping the line and going across the street to Village Whiskey for what is one of the best burger experiences in town..

I told my friends I was going over to Dollar Value, but I lied, although I did go over to Dollar Value, but my motive was to go to Popeyes.

I ordered the $10 5 piece.  It was delicious and then Ingot to a FRIED LEG WITH NOTHING BUT BONE AND SKIN. Now how did that make it to the fryer, better yet my box.

Come on man!

This location does not keep a clean kitchen. Tomato pieces and jam were on the inside of my husband's plain toast. My son then threw up after his buttered bagel due to his egg allergy. He didn't order anything with egg. Management denied that any of our issues occurred.

This has got to be the worst McD's I've ever seen. First, I just LOVED the urine smell when I walked in. Now, I'm not 100% sure if it was from the store itself, or from the kind of people that frequent this location. This place was just dirty inside and out, and since it's in the ghetto, the people in line looked like walking Post Office mugshots. 

Service? If you mean when they ask you what you want and then walk to the rear of the store where the rest of the employees gathered to do nothing, then yeah, they were awesome at that. 10 minutes for a cheese burger? Wow. Well stay hot McGhetto's. I wish I could give this store negatice stars, or drop NAPALM on the store and start over. STAY AWAY FROM THIS PLACE! ugh

Below it's asking me: 'Good For:" How come "nothing" isn't an option?

How can a self-identified food enthusiast NOT go to Philly's first Shake Shack on opening day?

I entered the line at 8:48 pm. Even though the kind employee assured us we'd be out of the line with food in 15 minutes (girl, please), from start to finish, it took a grand 52 minutes. But oh man, was it worth it. Especially after a solid night of Center City Sips, Shake Shack completely hit the spot.

Get the 'shroom burger - definitely superior to the beef burger (the temporary vegetarian blindly asserted, having no real basis for her comparison). The portabello patty is crispily fried with a tender interior, oozing two kinds of cheeses from within the patty itself. Order a side of crinkle-cut fries and a Center City Pretzel concrete. Naturally, dip the fries in the frozen concrete, and you will be happy.
Veggie rolls are more quantity than any other restaurants in the city .. one can enough .. Panneer also good .. easy quick eaten place .. except parking you can have comfortable food

The perception that was being created is that the level of customer service or lack there of, is based on the area that the entity is in. I hope this perception does become true. Poor customer service. I didn't get napkins or sauces, in which I asked for. Extremely long wait in drive through.

I enjoyed this chipotle as I do any other.  This one did not particularly stick out in my mind as far as the food goes because they offered the same choices for food as the others.  The place itself was very cramped and a little uncomfortable standing in line because the tables were right next to you so you almost felt like you were hovering over their food which I did not like feeling like that and I am more then sure they did not appreciate it as well.  The line was long when I got here but, they were on the faster side of some chiopotles they were really churning and burning to get the line moving which is always a plus.  The staff was friendly and efficient because not only were they going very quick they were getting everyone's orders right.
The food is always top notch and I have to say that although people say it's 'a  bit expensive'  you certainly get what you pay for. 1.8 times the cost of McDonald's at 1000% the quality.

It was my first time trying indoor Shake shack burger in Philly, and I think the experience in NYC is better.. There burgers are great to have in winter when you eat under the heaters and shivering ..

Ok, everyone raved about this place but it was so crowded when I went that I felt like I had to stake out for a table. The burgers were delicious, flavorful but boy were they greasy. I looked like I ate a bucket fried chicken with all the napkins I had to use. 

Now, I didn't have the shake but my friends did and they loved it. I probably will never order a shake only because I'm not really a shake person but I trust my friends taste buds so I think you should definitely give their shakes a try. If you are craving a really greasy, hearty burger then order one too.

I love subway but have been a few times before work because it is on my way. Always have a limited bread selection and not that fresh. Wouldn't let me use their restroom and didn't do the promotions that the other restaurants are running.
this mcdonalds still has fruitopia strawberry passion awareness or whatever it's called.

Though i have long been mourning the loss of Jojo's and their fried wontons, I was giddy with excitement when I heard an Indian street food joint decided to take over  ... 

Kati rolls have long been a street food staple of urban populous in bustling cities like Kolkata and Mumbai and have recently garnered some attention stateside, mostly in NYC. Though I admit it did take a bit long for philly to catch up on the trend, I am glad Spice End is doing it right.

One has a variety of options for the fillings , but the concept is simple, a plethora of flavors from spices, marinated meats and dash of seasonings all bundled into one thin crispy paratha, to pack a punch all the way  to the last bite.

We sampled the Achari chicken and paneer .. Which was well marinated and tangy cos of the Indian pickles (more of a lime or a mango base in contrast to a vinegar base). Also got a Frankie ( the egg and chicken ) or as I call it the Mumbai burrito where the Paratha is doubled up with an egg base on the griddle. The aloo (potato) paneer had a nice kick to it too.

They all went well with the red and the white sauces provided on the side, so i guess you can't go much wrong from blindly picking one from the menu. Though if you do feel lost, the staff is nice and friendly enough to help you pick something. I will prolly try and go back and try the platters sometime soon ... 

So If a ravenous hunger pang beckons 2 of these rolls should do the trick ,  though one roll will easily satiate those late night munchies given that they are also open till late on most nights.

P.S : They also stack ThumsUp and Limca in the fridge, some potent Indian soda if you feel inundated with spices.
I've got the Pop Corn Chicken Bento and it was quite good. The chicken was very crispy, and the portions are very big, I can have my lef over for diner. The price is affordable, I will come back

The crinkle fries have made a comeback and I'm glad they did!!! I'm still not in love with their burgers but they are not bad either. I love the custard here and milkshakes honesty, these two items keep me coming back for more!

whatever happened to customer service?  the staff here blows.  they are all teenagers, and it alarms me how bitter they already seem to be with the world.  you are young!!!  

the corner bakery is another offender - order a bagel with butter, and you'll get it unprepared.  meaning, you have to go over to their little counter, cut up ice-cold butter more solid than the flimsy knife you're trying to use, have your bag slip from your shoulder in the process and its weight takes out the stack of napkins and pile of utensils next to you, while trying to resituate yourself your scarf falls on the bagel, and meanwhile, other customers are heaving sighs and rolling their eyes because they want to use the tiny space to sweeten their coffees.  f-y'all - i'm forever more going to buy bagels from my local bakery, and make them at home where it's not a struggle against society.  so done with the corner bakery and its snooty high schoolers.

id give this place 10 stars if i could! its always a clean enviorment the food is ALWAYS fresh and good, service is always great  and staff is always friendly, and this paticular local. isnt so over crowded to where you feel like you have to wait forever. i recomend the classic burger of course along with the original crinkle fries that are back and i actually get the portabella mushroom burger that ozzes cheese. the price is ok concidering the taste and quality.
My sister has been talking about this place for years, and I finally get to try it. There isn't anything compared to this in California...

Great food. No godlike food. This vegan will convey even the staunchest of meat eaters- believe me, I've done the legwork. 

Props to the cashier, who expedited my order, cause she understood I needed a vegan meal before my bus left back to NYC!

This place is amazing, they have really good food and flavor to their meals. I get general Tso all the time but have tried a lot of the menu and you can't fail with anything you order. The staff is friendly and nice every time we go. Definitely one of my favorite lunch spots in the city

Shake shack is only okay. The prices and the portions are kind of crappy compared to a place like 5 Guys. The shakes were alright, but I'm always willing to try again. I luckily didn't have to wait too too long (like a lot of people said I might have to), and the service was friendly, because if I did wait longer it would have slipped to 2 stars. This place really is just okay.

KFC is KFC. Sure, anyone above 35 will tell you how great they used to be back in the day (they were).  And anyone today will tell you how far they've fallen from the lofty ideal the colonel penned once upon a time. But occasionally you stumble on an exception. I've eaten here about a dozen times in the last couple years. Every time the food was fresh and the service was good. Sunday morning at 11? Perfect. Tuesday night after work?  No problem. Even Friday night for an 11:30 crack like chicken fix. A part of me worries that I've just been lucky and the next time around them find a way to sabotage my optimism, but alas that hasn't come to fruition yet. They do a good job here (phenomenonally excellent job by KFC standards) and people shouldn't hesitate to get their fix here if they happen to be in the neighborhood.

Food usually pretty decent for fast food but the service at this particular location is abysmal. If you can live with that, go for it, if you require even the tiniest bit of customer service then avoid this location
Coreanos is in a great location and has awesome flavors ! Definitely worth checking out and trying all of the unique taco choices. The Spanish rice and guacamole are delicious.
The food is as great as I remember from the one in NYC and the staff is excellent, you won't be disappointed eating here.
Never been here .. Food was great! Something different from the everyday items you find when you are out and enjoying the day

Horrendously slow service - came at night around 9  and waited over 15 minutes for a burger and fries. Was not crowded at all and large staff 
Doesn't take me that long to cook a burger at home.....shame because food is good.

Pretty much every time I pass through Philly, I stop at this Shake Shack.  Being from Chicago means I can only treat myself to these when out of town, and aside from the locations in New York, this location is my favorite.

I came to Shake Shack with an open mind.  When they first announced that this site was going to be a Shake Shack, I was admittedly disappointed that another NYC franchise was trying to break into the awesomeness of Philadelphia, but as construction progressed and they planted the vertical garden and made the area much more beautiful than it had been, I wished them well and was anxious to try the new burger place in town.  Today, I finally made it in and tried the SmokeShack and Cheese Fries with a drink for ~$13.  There was nothing stellar about any of the food, and the portion size (tiny greasy burgers) was not worth the cost or the wait in the ridiculously long line, imo.  I will say that the employees are great and friendly and I appreciated that, but as for the restaurant, it's not even in the top three burger restaurants on Sansom Street West of Broad.  I'm in no rush to go back.

Generally the staff is accommodating when it comes to your order.   Today however, around noon I was informed that "there was only breasts and wings - white meat in the original recipe".   No dark meat - legs or thighs.   I proceeded to enter the establishment as opposed to the drive through because the so-called"manager" appeared to have attitude when I asked for clarification.  I wanted to know if my order would consist of 5 wings and s breast - I refused to accept a bucket of wings for a 6 piece $10 special.   When inside another young lady accommodated me by mixing fried with baked which was ok with me.  This "manager" should be trained on how to accommodate customers with a better attitude and leniency!   She should also be somewhat tidier in her appearance - very unkempt with dirty hair.  Needless to say I was disgusted because I've never experienced this with any other manager or worker!

it never fails. every other time we go something is wrong or missing...you go there takes 3 people to place 1 order..including the supervisor.. you place and order and something is wrong or left out..asked for mixed reg and spicy got all regular asked for side of small mashed potatoes..get home ..ta da no potatoes!! i mean this is not rocket science people..and fast food workers want $15 and hr?!??! The chicken is ok..but they need to drink some wake up or energy drink they are all half asleep!! And the place was not busy at all..one woman before me. I can understand a busy lunchtime..or dinnertime..really pathetic service.
I'm no way a food critic and have no idea how to articulate my taste buds. I just know when food is good and this is a good burger.

This is not a place to bring your future in-laws to impress them. This is not a place to bring a major CEO of a company. This IS a place with great food, relaxed staff, nothing fancy, and did I mention the great food? From the awesome kati rolls, to the chicken-n-rice platters, it's just good food at a good price. It is the best in Philly? Maybe not. But on a random day when you are hankering for a solid kati roll, with spiced and tender chicken, this very well might be the best spot in Philly.

I don't really get it.  The place had a huge line.  When I got to the front and ordered, I was asked if I'd ever been there before.  Umm, no, but I have been to a fast food joint.  He explained that the buzzer thing would ring when my food was ready.  Yes, I've seen those magic devices before.
Had a veg burger, fries, black and white shake.  The burger was good and different - a fried portobello mushroom stuffed with cheese.  Problem is, first bite and motten cheese comes squirting out.  Still, tasty.  Fries were mediocre.  Shake was good, but it's a shake, kinda hard to screw up.  
Here's what I don't get:  the cost of this fast food meal was $16.  The portions were small, and unremarkable.  It's a friggin burger, fries, shake, not much different than what you get pretty much anywhere.  That's fine, but let's not pretend they invented something.  Spend your $16 on the best burger in town and a beer next door at Village Whiskey.

Really not sure what the fuss is about shake shack. Didn't find their burgers to be anything other than a burger. It's slightly above fast food burgers... is that what the hype is about? Please someone enlighten me. What is so great about this place?

Gotta love $5 foot longs in the city. When you're trying to stretch your paycheck, go here. Just listen for a bit. It's good, not great. But you come here for lunch when you are at work which is probably miserable anyway. You feel down cause work stinks. You can spend $5 and get a foot long sub which will pick you up! 

Each sub has the calories count listed. Your afternoon at work is dependent on how healthy you eat at lunch. Go eat from a food truck and let me know the ratio of time at your desk to time at the toilet. 
It's clean. I am observant when it comes to food establishments not meeting code and this place represents. If you come in prime time though, there is a long line because everyone wants their sandwich toasted. My recommendation would be come at 11:45 or 1. 

The food is the food, I don't need to review it. It tastes like Subway. I am just saying, for half the price of Primo's you can get a GOOD hoagie, chips, and a drink. Try it out. 

Also, get yourself a Subway card to earn points for free food in the future.

Oh when I see a chain I walk the other way, oh when I see a chain I walk the other way....sing it with me.

This experience was delicious, the chocolate milkshake has a deeper almost dark chocolate or dutch processed flavor to it. 

We split the smoke shack, the chopped cherry peppers were fantastic, the burger was cooked medium well, bun soft, bacon crispy. What more could you ask for?

The fries were crisp, not oily and the cheese sauce is thick and rich, it doesn't resemble a processed cheese food product at all. 

Thanks Shake Shack for melting my frozen chain avoiding heart.

It's been more than a year now I started going to this restaurant. I have to say this food is pretty addictive, plus they serve late night. I almost tried everything on their menu and tastes good overall. I advice to try this if you are craving for late night Indian food. I like vegetarian platter, chicken biryani with extra chicken and pav baji. 
Their spicy levels are pretty low.

Philly, you're so lucky that Shake Shack settled in your town, but you're definitely missing out on the true experience. There was no line out the door (fine, that's a plus) but there is limited indoor and outdoor seating. Take out is definitely the way to go here. I came on Labor Day with a friend and we ordered shakes and burgers to go. Our orders came out within 10 minutes, but the bags and cups were covered in cheese from other orders and we weren't given napkins. Little things, but little things are annoying when you're wearing a white t-shirt and fashion a yellow cheese stain on your chest because the linemen couldn't keep their hands clean. Overall friendly people and a great location just minutes from Rittenhouse Square, definitely the best place in the city to get your NYC fast food fix.

If you've never been to Shake Shack: thing greasy burgers smothered in cheese and special sauce with fresh lettuce and tomatoes; think Five Guy's style fries that actually look like they were made from a real potato; think creamy delicious shakes made from whole milk; think beer and wine. Doesn't get much better if you need to cure a hangover or raise your cholesterol.

My company placed a large order with this location through the online system for lunch. The order had 2 inconsistencies which we promptly called to make arrangements to have fixed. The woman in charge that day did not seem very friendly or accommodating which didn't make me feel good about receiving replacement sandwiches. Mistakes happen which is perfectly okay, but the way in which mistakes are handled should be dealt with in a more polite manner.
Food was good. But the sauce in ordered was spilled and messy. The pickle sauce was bitter but I would hope to get more sauce for 50cents.

A really great, fast burger. Decidedly fresh served by a gentle and charismatic staff. I had the Smoke Shack and loved every minute of it, from the sauce, to the bacon, to the spiciness of it all.

The pre-cut frozen fries aren't exactly mind-blowing, but with the extra aioli I got, they improved. I didn't try a shake this time, but I'll have it next time I stop by. And they could shave a few bones off of their burgers and I'd be happier.

Shake Shack tows the line between fast food and sit-down-eating nicely. Unfortunately, that's not really a line that should be towed. It's ultimately a great product--and it would be four stars, if it felt more like a full-service joint.

yes.  yes.  and...well....YES.

i hit up shake shack around 5:30 p.m. on the day of its grand-opening.  i'm familiar with  the D.C. location in DuPont Circle.  when i heard it was coming to Philly....i cried tears of joy.

yessssssss!

after debating for 10 minutes whether or not we should stand in line, we were sucked in by an uber-friendly hostess who provided us with a laminated menu.  

we ordered the shackburger with bacon (his was a double), cheese fries, and two fountain sodas.  a bit on the expensive side....but well worth it for a good burger, great fries, and really great service.

perfect crinkle cut fries...golden and fried to perfection.  my fiancee siad the salt was fried into the potatoes...whatever that lmeans...

we took our food, sat in Rittenhouse Square, enjoyed the scenery, and were pleasantly suprised by how GREAT everything was.

i've been to PYT....the burgers are for show.  dress them up with fancy names and things that don't belong on burgers....i just want meat, a good bun, some fresh toppings, and a decent sauce.

if i could give more than five stars, i would.  

i WILL be going again....really soon.
Service was fast. The workers aren't friendly won't say rude but could greet customers better. I had the burrito bowl with brown rice chicken. Rice a little under cooked

I was so sad that I could only give this kind of review. I have eaten at other Shake Shack's and they have always rocked my world. I specifically went out of my way to NOT eat at a banquet I was attending to come here afterwards. 

I ordered the single Shack Burger and a strawberry shake. I took one bite of my burger and it just wasn't cooked. It was completely pink inside and I just didn't want to risk some food born illness because I realllllly wanted the burger. It was just too late in my evening to ask them to make me another one either. 

The service was super friendly and my shake was really good too! I think if I went back to this location again I would just specify to make sure my burger is well-done but that should be the standard.

Love Jersey Mikes for fresh and consistent hoagie sandwiches. I've been to locations between NJ and VA, and I've had a positive experience with all of them.  The service here at 30th St Station was very friendly and the food was fresh. No line and my sandwich was prepared quickly and exactly how I asked for it. The roesemary parm bread was quite tasty.  For me, the mini sized sub is plenty of food.  

Only negative is that it was hard to find a clean table and it would be nice if there were power outlets near the tables so I could recharge while enjoying my lunch.  Also the trash cans both needed to be emptied as they were full to the rim.

But I will definitely come back next time I need a bite while waiting for a train at 30th St Station.

This corner bakery is the perfect spot of the quick lunch break. It feels like your in an actual restaurant and the food is beyond affordable! It also taste really fresh. I also really recommend the to go orders if you are in a rush! It's ready very quickly and packaged perfectly!

If your staying in for lunch there is plenty of seating!

I love Snap Kitchen.  The ingredients are so fresh, and I know exactly what I'm getting.  I love that so many items are gluten free.  The portion sizes are perfect and it's easy keeping track of calories.

I love shake shack don't get me wrong. And one of the things I LOVE about shake shack are their concretes.

Unfortunately, something is totally off about their Liberty Shell. The description looks good in writing: vanilla custard, Philly-style soft pretzel, caramel sauce, marshmallow sauce and banana. In actuality, it's like chewing on soggy croutons in vanilla ice cream. The concept is great, but the execution needs some tweaking. 

Still, as a sweets addict, I won't be deterred. Definitely will be back for their other frozen treats!

I love shakes. I waited months for shake shack to open, with my nose pressed against the windows.  When they finally opened, I hit the Shack and hit it hard: shakes three days in a row.  The third time was not the charm.  I used the express/cold line and waited for my shake while at least six full meals went out the door -- with customers who came in after I did -- and then, since it turns out they lost my order (it's computerized!), I had to yell over the counter to reorder and the shake was missing one of the items I wanted.  Anyway, I gave them another shot a couple of weeks later, and had a similar experience, only this time the express/cold line wasn't being called to the register.

I left sputtering and the guy at the door came after me.  It turned out it was Alan, the general manager.  We talked a while, he fixed the shake issue and assured me that they were working out the kinks...and that he was committed to making everything better and more in line with what folks have expected based on the NY stores.  I haven't been back yet, but when I walked by the other day, Alan and another manager were outside with the team giving them service instructions.

We'll see the next time I go back.  I'm not willing to give up on getting my shake fix that easily.

So there's a time and a place for everything. Sometimes you want a healthy lunch, other times you just don't care. If you're going to Shack Shake, your current appetite is on the extreme side of not giving a fuck. There is no option you can possibly order that won't take years off your life...and that's just fine. Shake Shack is really excellent if you're in the mood for a cheat meal.

However, this type of indulgence ins't always for everyone. The burgers are greasy. I mean, they are really greasy and fatty burgers. It might take you by surprise when you get your order. And god forbid, don't let the burger sit for even a minute after you get it, the grease will overtake the bun. If you don't have a fat-tooth, one patty will suffice. The fries and shakes are standard fare as you'd expect.

There's also beer, which is awesome, including bottles and at least one draft. Have a beer during lunch at work. I dare you.

Overall a good addition to the philly lunch scene. My visits here might be a little more infrequent than other spots, but that's only due to the fact that I don't want to be obese.

If I'm ever on fire, I want you to put me out with a shake shack milkshake. You're going to need two, maybe three of them. Don't use anything lame like a fire extinguisher. Even though I'll be thrashing on the ground in agony, I'm willing to wait.

Let me just say, I don't eat red meat, so I doubt it had a chance of ever making it on my go to list. But the mushroom burger was pretty good, a bit small, the bread was squished and the mushroom is fried with some cheese inside (btw during eating you will lose all of the cheese from the bottom). The fries were really good though. I like the set up and the ordering system. I wish I tried the desserts, that probably would've increased my rating. But yea, I don't think I get the hype. =(

A day off from work allowed me the rare opportunity to venture into the city for lunch. When I arrived at Shack Shake, I was surprised to see the restaurant empty @ 11:30 am.  I started to wonder if this could be a bad omen.  This was my first time so I needed some time to ponder over the menu.

It is almost impossible for me to pass up a burger with apple wood smoked bacon. Because of this predisposition, I ordered the Smoke Shack.  In addition to bacon, the burger also has cherry pepper and Shack Sauce.  I really enjoyed the heat from the cherry peppers.   It gave the burger a nice kick.  The bacon added an element of smoke and salt.  By default, Shake Shack cooks their burger to a medium rare temperature.  It dawned on me as I was almost finished eating my burger, that my server did not give me the option of ordering a single or a double burger.  I wished he would have, because I wanted more when I finished.  The Liberty Shell concrete was okay, but it was nothing exceptional.  The fries are also lackluster in my humble opinion.  I have never been a fan of crinkle fries.  They remind me too much of the fries served in my elementary school cafeteria. 

My Shake Shack burger lived up to my expectations and I was glad that I did not have to wait in a line.  Their hamburger is very good and something I would go back for again.  The service was nice and friendly, however; I think the servers should not assume that visitors have dined there before and treat every customer as a new one.
Chicken Salad on Rye bread was such a treat. The ingredients were so fresh and crisp. Yummy !!!!

I toiled with which rating to give: 3 or 4.  I essentially decided upon 3 thanks to Yelp's description. Shake Shack was A-ok and I'm not a fan.  The setting: late lunch.  The menu: burgers and uh, cold stuff, I think and some more burgers or something.  The atmosphere: that awkward period in between standard munching times. 

I looked upon the menu and decided on the Shake Shack burger with cheese.  I ordered, though, a cheese burger thinking the two were the same thing.  Nope.  As we waited for our food, we waited.  I like the decor and the no frills atmosphere of what seemed to be a modern take on the burger joint.  But it felt forced.  Like a marketing team had come in and picked out the right stain on the wood, the right tables and just the proper lack of sitting space (despite the giant kitchen) necessary to instill a feeling of satisfaction that I had indeed found a seat.  I wouldn't call it elitist, per se, but not welcoming to the uninitiated.  I had no idea what the C line meant.  Yes, I figured it out that C line meant "cold" food stuffs. 

As we got the point where I was about to ask after my food, someone brought it out.  This is where I realized that a cheeseburger was not a Shake Shack burger with cheese.  I had received meat, cheese and bun.  And it was tasty and freshly cooked, to be sure.  But it did not have the lettuce, tomato and whatever else was supposed to come with the Shake Shack burger. I suppose that's my mistake, but it would have been nice for the guy at the register to ask if I wanted any of that.  Then again, we were in just before tea time and perhaps he was off his game.

Normally this place is packed, so it can't be horrible.  It wasn't.  But I'm not convinced it was worthy of such a devoted following.  Unless the lettuce tastes like happiness and the tomato tastes like a first kiss. 

The fries were great.  Philly knows how to make some fries.
Horrible service. Workers eating pizza on food line in front of customers. Refusing to give full portions and make fresh food at 8 pm . Less than one star

Where's my Jumbo Squid ??? That was my initial thought when I saw my order. I ordered the Jumbo Squid Bento Combo and it did not look like the advertisement at all. I asked the cashier what was good and what she recommended. She recommended the BBQ chicken or the squid bento box. I felt like I played myself. (+_+). Next time, I will eat before because there was a fair amount of food but I felt I still needed to eat more.

Overall, the food taste well but could have been cooked warmer. The squid was oddly burnt so I was not sure what happened in the kitchen.

I know hamburgers take the limelight here, but I gotta profess my love for the hot dog.

Perfect crunch, decent bun, interesting flavor. Also scallions? It's ideal for late at night when you just need a hot dog fast and Shake Shack happens to be down the block....like when you attend a show at Helium.

I also ordered a cheeseburger sans tomato, which I put in a Tupperware and brought with me to work the next day. Probably a little weird, but it surprisingly held well despite the grease.

I know I also ordered some sort of drink as well, maybe a milkshake? I've had them also while not in a happy-daze, so I can absolutely vouch for the authenticity of my statement when I say that I like the shakes at shake shack.

Could be wrong about the hot dog, but I doubt it.

It wasn't as good as cheers cut (two blocks away). Drinks were too sweet, I got the milk tea in a naked lady bottle. The chicken was slightly burnt, with too much breading. Prices in my opinion are also a little too high.

It's great having this tiny HipCityVeg location on Broad Street. Though it's small in size and can get busy, it's never overbearingly so. Hip City is always delicious, I'm such a fan of the Ziggy Burger and the sweet potato fries. I've always gotten in and out at lunchtime from this here in pretty good time.

its a shame because this place could easily be 4 stars possibly even 5 but the problem is that while this is one of the only "fast food" burger places i can think of that allows you to cook your burger rare the patties are just too thin and the cooks too unskilled to make it work. it either comes out med well or raw. i think only the first time i went was it cooked close to correctly. 

the fries are nice when they are waffle but when i went to the west philly location they were shoestring. i was confused. the cheese sauce is good. haven't loved the hot dogs or sausages by any means. 

its nice they have beer. i feel like they kinda gouge ya on the soda prices but maybe im making that up.
Place has a functioning restroom. The food has yet to kill me. Tried the other stores around me. They wouldn't let me use their restroom.

Honestly the worst burger I have ever had. The burger itself had little to no seasoning on it. The bun was sooo stale and the burger was also not to temp at all. Fried chicken sandwich was also not very flavorful. I think Kensington quarters does a much better job at their spot in fishtown than this fast paced spot

The food was delicious and he was courteous. Got a burger and a vanilla concrete with banana. Outstanding. 

Thomas helped us out during walnut walk on Thursday. He's headed to DC to open another store, good luck my man. I'm happy and excited for you!

It's kinda new in Amtrak 30th station.
Instead of Subway, I tried this place for turkey hoagie but it was nothing special as well as overpriced. Disappointing...

The server was friendly and patient. I got the chicken and egg roll. So good! Make sure you have some self-control when spreading the red sauce over your food, because I didn't..IT MIGHT BLOW YOUR MOUTH! I think a piece of me dead as I was biting into the egg roll..  I love spicy food but that was just too spicy. They are also open till 3 am!

My sister and I were dining at the Shake Shack at 20th and Sansom approximately two weeks ago and we had a horrific experience due to the service of one of the employees Allison(A brown skin African American woman). She was extremely rude, unprofessional and made disrespectful comments under her breath after we asked her to clear our table. At that time I was not aware that the employees were not waiters as this was my first time visiting this establishment. Allison responded to my request by stating rudely "We don't do that here". She proceeded to walk away while saying "I should have stayed in the kitchen doing ice cream or something I don't have time for this". I do not know if this young lady was having a bad day or not however, I have never received such poor service from an establishment and thought that this would be a nice place to have dinner. I was wrong. I Have told everyone not to visit this establishment due to my experience. I will also leave a review on. I'm in the process of obtaining the contact information for Corporate Services.

This location is a bit cramped, and when I went, it was very disorderly, trashcans were all overflowing, and condiment stations were all a mess. That being said, I went at a busy time, so that may be a large contribution to that. 
The food was good, not great , I had a burger and a shake. A bit over priced for the quality, but it was a decent burger for a decent price in the end, although not a shake shack I would go to for the atmosphere.

I've never had a bad experience at Shake Shack! Burgers always taste good (I typically get the Shack Burger while my boyfriend swears by the Smoke Shack) and the lemonade is fresh. I love how they have weekly specials of different milkshakes, it makes it easy to convince yourself to get one "just to try". Only downside is that this place is kinda expensive. $15 for a double shack burger, cheese fries, and a drink. But I guess you do get a lot for your money!

Burgers are delicious. They have that famed crispy crunchy texture. My favorite is the smoke shack. Fridays are pretty decent as well. However it can be Mayham in there between all the bros and tourists. I try and avoid it at peak hours. Plus the seating is not comfortable. But I will return over and over because the burgers are that good.

Ok so I know I wrote another review a month ago but that was a month this is now. I went there sat nite. In my previous review I wrote how if there's a problem they fix it for you well Not Sat! I asked for the cheesy beefy melt the cashier keep trying to sell me the mexi melt. I didn't want the mexi melt. She also said the cheesy beefy melt is not in their system. Excuse me but it hasn't been in their system for at least a year & they always made it for me. They usually just rung me up for something for the same price. But she refused to ring it up. I mean it's not that hard to make they always have the stuff that goes in it. I told her what was in it & she said she can't make it. Well she wasn't making it she was the cashier. I was hungry & tried of arguing so I paid for my other food & ate in but let's just say I won't be back for a while! So the morally of this story is if you had a problem before they helped you,now not so much!

The service here is horrible. I told her 8 piece chicken tenders and she said she doesn't have that when it clearly says eight piece chicken tenders on the boards. The girl was also very rude and they were so slow. I don't know why they were slow if they had four people on the job and the place was empty.

Shake Shack Burger greater than a Five Guys Burger, but not quite as good as Bobby's Burger Palace. 

Definitely worth getting, but not worth waiting in line.

I'm always on the search for a good cheeseburger.  I discovered the shake shack via the internet and I was curious.  I heard nothing but awesome things about it so I had to check it out.  

Shake Shack has been open less than a week and you can tell.  When we got there the line was out the door.  They had people outside to hand out menus and answer questions. All the employees seem to have a really positive attitude.  About 30 minutes after waiting in line we finally made out orders.  I had the shake burger double with fries and a fifty fifty, which is basically an Arnold Palmer.  My girlfriend had the Shroom burger with fries and a milkshake.  We had to wait about ten minutes for our burgers which if they are cooked to order thats how long it should take.

My burger was delicious.  Any burger that squirts grease on your fingers is the way a burger should be.  It was juicy medium, all burger are cooked medium, and the fries were really good.  Not the best but good.  My girlfriend enjoyed her shroom burger as well.  It was cheesy and when she was done it didn't feel like she had a brick in her stomach.  That is very important to her.  

The Fair shake, vanilla milk shake with arabica coffee, it was thick and the coffee taste wasn't to overwhelming.  

All in all THE HYPE IS REAL.  

The End

I know Jimmy John's is a chain and yet I still like it.  The one on the corner of 11th and Locust is especially friendly and clean and attractive inside.  The subs are fairly priced and varied.  Quality is very decent.  Service is quick.  This is a chain sandwich joint that def works for me.

Only negative - you pay extra for hot peppers that to be honest aren't very hot and are barely noticeable in a sandwich.  If I'm taking my sub home to eat, I add my own peppers that actually have a bit of heat.

We never had Indian Food Before Me and my wife where in Center City And needed to eat lunch we wanted something fast so are appointment was across the street from spiced end. I was surprised I tried there lunch Box special it came with a Kati Roll and rice with lettuce and tomato it was delicious and very affordable.... I give these guys a 5 star will definitely be back again

I was embarrassed by the Shake Shack staff who assumed that I did not know that the 'Shroom Burger was vegetarian, and proceeded to tell me that there was "no meat in that, Ma'am." He then corrected me when I called their "custard" "ice cream." There was no reason to call me out like that. However, we were then able to joke about it, so that was nice. Also, the 'Shroom Burger is way too small, us vegetarians are hungry too!

While on my way to a gelato place, Shake Shack came into view.  I immediately ditched the gelato idea and headed straight for the decadently creamy richness of a Shake Shack custard treat.  Their custard is so much more velvety than most, but I would have to say they did skimp on the mix-ins a little.  Good thing I was full from my meal, otherwise I would have had to get a burger too!  Can't wait for them to open a location in Scottsdale, AZ in 2016!
Not bad for fresh hot burgers but a bit overpriced for the quality. It's a nice building and I did enjoy the atmosphere

Sweet Jeebus...what is the longest you have waited for a burrito bowl (if you total the time from "I'll have a burrito bowl" to payment).  I'm going to guess on average it's 1.5 minutes to 2 minutes.  Well these doofuses took 10 minutes.  Not because they were understaffed, but because the employees were clowning around and straight up watching me and three other people wait.  On top of the bunk ass service they were out of everything, gave meager ass portions and were rude as all hell. Pimps were mad that we were getting food an hour before they close.  Made friends with the guy in front of me in line and we agreed it was the worst chipotle we have ever been to, and I travel everywhere for work... So I've seen some embarrassing chipotles.  The guy left super deep about the experience and I told him the only thing we can do is Yelp about it to warn other future disappointed customers.  It gets 2 stars because the food was standard.  Everyone please write your congressman or local councilman about my experience. We can take this to city hall ppl!
