What we've got here is an Indian version of Taco Bell with less flavor.  

They really should add flavor and do this food properly.  I've had plenty of Indian food at this sort of low price point which was great.

for about fifteen bucks you can get a double cheeseburger, fries and a shake.  i wasn't disappointed by any mean because it's good.  i got the shake stack, which is a burger patty stacked with a deep fried cheese stuffed mushroom patty.  the crinkle cut fries were perfectly crispy all the way through, no soggy mess.  also the shake just hits the spot. however, i honestly think that i'd be just as satisfied if i had a burger, fries and frosty from wendy's for half the price.  for some reason, shake shack just doesn't provide the same charm or "it factor" of in-n-out.  as silly as it sounds, i'd be happier if there was a white castle that moved to center city to fulfill my late night cheap burger cravings.  shake shack would be alot better if it wasn't so expensive.  i also know that i can get an equally good (if not better) burger and fries for fifteen bucks at alot of the gastropubs in the immediate rittenhouse area and throughout the city.

...it's honestly more of a 2.5 stars place when food service is accounted for. 

Normal price that you'll spend here is $11 for a meal. The food is classic fusion, taking from the most basic reproduction of Mexican and Korean cuisines. The portions can sometimes be cheap on the protein, but that depends on the "chef." The asian guy with tortoise glasses will skimp you on pretty much everything--an experience derived from multiple encounters with him. It's pretty insulting to drop 11 bucks on a bowl just to get canned kimchi, canned radish, a few shred of lettuce, a teaspoon of canned corn, and a few pieces of fried chicken over a bed of rice that doesn't even fill the corners of the container.

The tortilla shells for the tacos are also outsourced somewhere, and they have a fruity chemical smell. It seems like nothing at this place is made in house except for the protein and rice...

I've tried giving this place a few chances, and the other chefs usually do their customers right. Unfortunately, it seems like the main guy who runs the place (and is there the most) would rather skimp on his guests than provide exemplary service.

Oh shake shack, you never disappoint me whenever I give into my temptations only to regret the bloated feeling later. chocolate peanut butter is my go-to milkshake. the hot dog was good, but made my stomach hurt later. cheese fries are always a delight. I'm not really all that impressed with their burgers. if you're a drinker, they have beer on tap, a nice touch. new bike parking right outside.

finding a table when it is busy can be a real pain in the butt--but the outside seating helps when the weather is nice. the staff has always been super friendly and helpful...and quick!

In true foody fashion, after I went and grubbed out on a Village Whiskey foie gras burger, I had to come here and get ... another burger. Because why? Because I LOVE Shake Shack!

I didn't even know they had Shake Shack in Philly, so when I passed by it after dinner I had to go in. I dragged my entire entourage of now 8 people to come with me, and also convinced them to have burgers because they had never tried it before even though they live in Philly.

O.M.G.

Sorry but I love Shake Shack. I think it's way better than In n' Out (I might get massively flamed for this ... ) and I loved it here with no exceptions. Just talking about it makes me miss it :(!

I was in Philadelphia for a show over at World Cafe Live and I was in the mood for ice cream only to find myself with a double shack and a root beer float in my hand.  I live in NJ so I'm really close to the original shake shack in NY, so I'm no stranger to the shake shack goodness.  

I was sad that Philly has switched over to the hand cut fries... Those crinkle cuts were like drugs!  Just sayin.

As a student, chipotle is a perfect place to eat good without spending a lot of money. Most of the time I would order the burrito bowl and it would fill me for hours until I am hungry. A chicken burrito bowl without drinks or chips is only around 7 dollar which is very student friendly. Plus the food is always fresh, it is not fast food restaurant where you are not sure if the meat you are eating are processed meat or real meat. Chipotle keep it real and prepare the food in front of you! 

The staff on this location is really nice and friendly. The seating arrangement is well-thought-out. Highly recommended for people that don't want to spend a lot of money but want amazing Mexican food.

Not. Good. Ordered the lamb platter and received a dish with crumbly, dry, tasteless lamb, unseasoned and undercooked rice, white sauce that is basically seasoned mayo (consistency and all), a few shreds of soggy lettuce, and to top it all off, wet pita (which is usually my favorite part of a platter like this). I hope this was just a bad day at Spice End because if not, I'm not sure what these other reviewers are tasting. I've had far better at the food truck on Drexel's campus...and for less than 1/2 the price.

Good burger. Excellent black and white milkshake.   Crinkly cut fries come back this fall.   You give this place your money and you get food in return.  What more do you want from a fast food joint?  The employees are quite pleasant too.

Good food is everywhere but good service is what really counts. We left the casino at 2:35 AM & just wanted to grab a bite so we decided to go to Taco Bell which was closing at 3:00AM. I called them at like 2:45 AM & requested if they could take the order & we can pick it up. After a bit of resistance the person agreed. To my horror I put the address directly from the Yelp app which connects you via Apple maps to your destination and we ended up in the middle of nowhere(nearby AMC). So I called them and Stephanie was kind enough to guide me all the way from the AMC to their place. We arrived at 3:01 AM got the order & left happy & full. Thanks Steph - you're the best!

I love this place. I'm not vegan but I come here with my bff who is vegan (she has a hard time finding food that she can eat when we go out ) but hip city veg has a good variety from cheesesteaks to burgers and shakes. SOO good !

Going gluten-free, one of the most difficult things to give up for me is cheeseburgers.  I was SO excited to find out that for only $1 extra you can get a gluten free bun at Shake Shack.  The burger was delicious and inexpensive.  I will definitely be going back!
No line when I went. Burgers are juicy and fresh. The milkshake is perfect! The cashier was really helpful since this was my first time. They have out door seating and indoor seating and take out.

tried the shake shack tonight for the 1st time.  we got the dbl smokeshack burger, the shroom burger and fries.  the smokeshack was very good for a fast food type burger joint.  the shroom burger was also good.  buns were fresh..  the fries are average and prices a bit high.  the place is clean and gives you free filtered water which is big plus..

This place continues to impress. They continue to introduce new dishes covering a variety of flavors and dietary restrictions. The turkey chili is a favorite of mine, the Tex mex chicken bowl is definitely not traditional flavors but tasty & healthy, and the vegan dan dan noodles that I tried today are flavorful and have nice heat. I usually prefer hot meals to sandwiches & salads, so this is a great fast option with a calmer and friendlier feel than most fast casual spots. I'll be back!
INSANE amount of sugar in their juices. Really, they consider this healthy? Their juices should be illegal 44g in one drink? Crazy.

This is my go to, day to day Indian food in Phily.  The lamb kathi rolls have an amazing mix of tender lamb, green chutney, spice and a delicious paratha (bread) wrap.  At 300 calories its a very special treat.  Being a Bong (Bengali sweet freak), I like to add the Mango Lassi to one kathi roll and Spice End spicy and white sauce to the second.  

When I splurge, I go for the lamb and chicken platter.  Again, the perfect amount of spice to complement the tasty lamb, chicken mix.  If youre feeling adventurous get the "great balls of fire" Spice End style platter that will have your tongue dancing!

Chef Akshay had me try the new vegetarian Samosa chat and its really great.  The tamarind chutney and vegetable mix is just so delicious.

Finally, owner Meet has trained the staff to wear beaming smiles and create a great customer experience.  

Thanks Boyz, you make me feel like Im in India with my mom.

How can I explain?  The kindness of the staff this morning in showing me around and pointing me directly to exactly what I wanted and need to buy so I could have the best at work lunch I could ever wish for, that is game changing.  I may not be able to come a lot, but if I'm in a total jam, I know I can count on Snap Kitchen.  Thank you from a very stressed out and caring person. :)  Ps. Yes the naked beef was just what I needed.

This KFC needs to be close or get new management because they're giving KFC a bad name as a franchise.

 I went to shop at Franklin Mills Mall yesterday, November 1, after shopping at jcp my friend and I decided to walk outside the mall and look for a place to eat. For our surprise KFC was nearby so we said, let's sit down and eat at KFC. As soon as we enter the place it didn't look very welcome neither appealing to eat, but well I just said "What the heck, let's give them a try". WOW, what a BIG mistake we did. First, I notice the there was no one at the register as we enter the place. There was a young girl cleaning a table and she 2 minutes after we enter the place she noticed that we were waiting and she ran to the register to take our order. Once she took our order I noticed that she went in the back to prepare our food. WAIT, WAIT, you just touched money and going to prepare our food. NO WAY! However, I noticed she put gloves to prepare the food but I didn't like the simple fact that she went from cleaning the table, to manage money, to prepare food. This tell you that this place has very poor management or not management at all. Our food was NOT FRESH! In the back kitchen you could see like 3 more people and, a lady with the red shirt talking loud to the young girl in the front, while also taking orders from the Drive thru. The place looks a mess, the lack of communication was very visible and that's BAD BUSINESS. 

Now the food. 

The food was awful. The chicken was very salty, cold, greasy and old. I seems like the food was cooked hours ago. The boneless chicken I ordered was very salty, I've got 2 pieces with fries and a biscuit. The fries were also salty, greasy and old. Honestly, I didn't bother the taste the biscuit and I didn't finish the chicken because all the salt I tested every time I took a bite, plus the grease. 

As we were leaving the place one person from the kitchen came out to smoke a cigarette. And people that owns these places, PLEASE, PLEASE, try NOT to hire people that smoke cigarette and are going to work in the kitchen. That is very disgusting to me because many of them go back to the kitchen and they don't even bother to wash good their hands. This was a very bad experience and I will never go back to this KFC.      



Spanish:

Este KFC tiene que cerrar o conseguir una nueva administración porque están dando mala fama a KFC como una franquicia .

 Fui a comprar en Franklin Mills ayer, después de las compras en el JCP mi amiga y yo decidimos caminar fuera del centro comercial y buscar un lugar para comer. Para nuestra sorpresa KFC estaba cerca, así que dijimos , vamos a sentarnos y comer en KFC. Tan pronto como entramos en el lugar no parecía muy bienvenido ni muy agradable para comer, pero dije "Qué diablos , vamos a tratarlo a ver" . WOW, esto fue un gran error que hicimos. En primer lugar, me doy cuenta de que no había nadie en el caja de registro al entrar en el lugar. Había una muchacha limpiando una mesa y ella, 2 minutos después de que entramos en el lugar se dio cuenta de que nos encontrábamos esperando para que nos atendieran, y ella corrió hacia la caja para tomar nuestro pedido. Una vez que nos atendió la misma muchacha fue a la parte posterior para preparar nuestra comida. Espera, espera, ella acaba de tocar el dinero y va a preparar nuestra comida . ¡Qué RAYOS! Sin embargo , me di cuenta de que ella se puso los guantes para preparar la comida, pero no me gustó el simple hecho de que ella pasó de la limpieza de la mesa, para administrar el dinero y luego a preparar la comida. Esto deja decir que este lugar tiene muy mala administración y que no hay buena supervisión. ¡La comida NO estaba fresca! En la cocina atrás se podía ver como 3 personas más y una señora morena hablando muy alto a la joven en la parte delantera, mientras que también se encontraba cogiendo órdenes del servi-carro (drive tru). El lugar parece un desastre, la falta de comunicación y era muy visible. Eso es un mal negocio.

Ahora la comida:
La comida era horrible. El pollo estaba muy salado, frío, grasienta y viejos. Me parece que la comida estaba preparado hace horas. El pollo sin hueso que pedimos estaba muy salada , tengo 2 piezas con papas fritas y un biscuit. Las papas fritas estaban muy saladas , grasosas y viejas. Honestamente, no me molesté en probar el biscuit y, no termine de comerme el pollo por toda la sal que probaba cada vez que me comía un bocado. Además de la grasa que tenía el pollo. 

Cuando nos íbamos del lugar, una persona de la cocina salió a fumar un cigarrillo. Y la gente que posee estos lugares , por favor , por favor, trate de no contratar a personas que fuman cigarrillos y van a trabajar en la cocina . Eso es muy desagradable para mí , porque muchos de ellos van a la cocina y ni siquiera se molestan en lavarse bien las manos. Esta fue una muy mala experiencia y nunca voy a volver a este KFC, y lo más seguro no pise otro KFC.

Whatever you order, make sure you get plenty of the yogurt sauce. Wicked good.

I've only tried the rice platters and they were solid. I think the Spice End Combo was the best. Next time, i'll try the kati rolls.

took a morning trip into the city just to try the breakfast. ordered the HipCity Breakfast Sandwich with a sausage patty and a hash brown. Loved the sandwich! The tofu egg patty is so great. Ordered the mayo on the side as i wasn't sure if i'd be in a mayo mood that early. Would have been good with cheese on it.

I've finally had the opportunity to try their shakes and, based on what I've heard & read about, I was sorely disappointed. I had heir coffee milkshake and, frankly, it reminded me of something I might order at a McDonald's (not that I vividly remember food there). In other words: cookie-cutter, generic, ho-hum. Slightly good but nothing to write home about. Forgettable, waste of money.
Great food service much better them the rest at the mills  fast food joints at the mills are rude but this place is good enjoy

The food was great. I got popcorn chicken and chicken cutlet. The crispiness of the chicken was something i would definitely come back for. For the most part, the staff was also really sweet and offered genuine services. However, DONT GIVE CREDIT CARD TIPS everyone! Those credit card tips DOES NOT go to the staffs.
This place is terrible. Horrible service. Awful music. Disgusting raw food. Save yourself the hazzle.

Did the spices get burned in an epic fire here? I ordered the lamb platter and for $10 I expected something decent at the least. The lamb was dry and tasteless as was the rice. The white sauce just seemed like a glob of thick mayo. The pita was barely palatable. So. Utterly. Underwhelmed. I would not recommend this to anyone. I could get a $5 lamb platter off a halal truck that tasted better AND comes with a drink. 

It gets two stars for being edible. And clean.

Im prefacing this review with a disclaimer: I grew up eating Kogi, so my baseline for Korean fusion is always going to be kogi. Accordingly, please take my review with a grain of salt. 

I ordered the bulgogi beef tacos and chips and salsa. I originally ordered the half rotisserie chicken but they were sold out of it at 2 pm. 

Positives: come on Tuesdays!! The tacos are $2 each if you buy a minimum of 3! The chips and salsa were delicious and a very hearty portion for only $4. 

Slightly less positives: the meat in the tacos was definitely not bulgogi. It was pan fried steak without any of the typical bulgogi flavor or seasoning. I also am now realizing that my taco was missing an ingredient from the menu description (missing the radish). See photo upload. The taco was only dressed with a tiny bit of sauce (again, not bulgogi seasoning... tasted kinda like normal Sriracha?) and shredded iceberg lettuce. The lettuce really was a let down because typically, Korean fusion tacos will accentuate the bulgogi with some kind of pickled kimchi slaw. Again, maybe it's unfair that I am comparing it with kogi, but ice berg lettuce on a Korean fusion taco is a bit odd. 

I would personally not recommend the bulgogi tacos, but I am still very interested in trying the rotisserie chicken.

Wow this place is not kind on the wallet. I stopped by here after work looking for a snack but left with just an iced tea. I will say though, the staff is really friendly and I love the concept and look of this place. Just wish I could justify spending so much on a refrigerated entree.

It's a simple great tasting quick burger. The fries compliment the food well,  nothing crazy, yet so much better than your average McDonald's meal. You can get a beer made by Brooklyn brewery,  a soda or an in house milkshake. 
I think there is an atmosphere here that's maintained by the staff - very friendly. It invites you to come back again. Excellent experience here at this small chain - stop in and grab a double shack burger!

I love when I can eat healthy without meal prepping, without spending an obscene amount of money, and without having to deal with fruit and veggies that go bad way too quickly. So, Snap Kitchen gets me.

Place an order online, pick it up, and get on with your day. Snap Kitchen offers meals that don't get funky in the microwave -- you know what I'm talking about. But if you think the microwave gives you cancer, you can also reheat it in the oven. Every container of food has rehearing instructions, transparent ingredient lists, and a list of diets that food item is compliant with (think; whole30, paleo, vegan, etc.). Amazing.

I went to pick up my order and it wasn't packed up, so when I gave the associate my name he was really frantic to get me on my way which I appreciated. However, he missed one of the items that I ordered 2 of (PS Snacks Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough) and that was IMPORTANT. I caught it and he gave me another one no problem. But I definitely suggest you check your bag before leaving to make sure all of your goodies are in there. 

The food is great, the concept is great, and the service is great. I will absolutely keep Snap Kitchen in my reservoir of top lunch spots in the city. 

Pictured: harvest kale salad, provencal flatbread, gunner greens juice, and a baby cactus from the office.

There's lots of hype for this place, but I'm not sure it deserves all of it. Yes it's good, but it's not 20-40 minutes in line good. As a tip, if you want shakes you can go in an express line. The shakes are great, but I can't give more stars over that. How hard is it to make a surgared-ice cream drink tasty?

I've had two different burgers and one of their hot dogs. The burgers were smaller than I'd like and the hotdog was a normal size. Both tasty but both could be better. Their special shake sauce didn't seem to be anything out of the ordinary and the fries were standard.

It's also pretty expensive for what you get. On that note I have been a repeat customer cause it's convenient and on off-hours there is no line.

I like this place.  Went with my boyfriend.  We got cheese fries, a milk shake, a single burger, a double burger and a beer with a total bill of $28.00.  It is overpriced but it's in Rittenhouse so it's to be expected.  The food was good and I liked the atomosphere.  You can sit outside which gives it a few extra points.  The cheese fries ruled and the shake shack special beer was awesome.  I'll be back.

So I walk by this Shake Shack the other day. Was surprised how few customers were there. Then I learn that Inside Edition did an expose on this particular restaurant recently and found all kinds of rodentia foraging around the place after hours! The vermin expert's concern was the possible contamination of the food. I'll be sure to stop by for a rat burger, WITH cheese! The two go hand in hand, right?

All kidding aside, you won't believe what happened when Inside Edition returned a week AFTER the report aired...

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wFq2EL4-q3Q
Friendly service, great tuna salad sandwich, good chips. The prices are very reasonable. They should clean the windows though.

Went there for lunch. Something different. Burger was not cooked properly. And left a mushy mess. Husband asked for a item it be left out and they not only didn't leave out the item but added more. Shakes are left to be desireable. For 2 burgers and 2 shakes and almost 40.00. Lunch elsewhere would have been better. Definitely on my list of not returning. Place was packed so I'm not sure if my order was just a fluke or people just don't know better.

I've been to a location in NYC, so I was excited to finally try the Philly branch. 

First of all, the milkshakes are solid.  And they offer malts.  Anything malted in my book deserves an A+.  

The burgers are solid; not too greasy, and I find that I'm full after one, but not the kind of full where I can't move for hours after consuming said burger.  

This place is always busy, so I recommend getting your order to-go.  Head to Rittenhouse Square and grab a bench, sip your peanut-butter/chocolate malt, and people watch while you wait for the goodness to digest.

First Shake Shack experience, and it hit a home run.  Which is fitting, since I ended up at a Phillies game later that night.

The line, at first seemed long.  But it moved so fast that it was hardly a wait.  The counter guy was fun and friendly and didn't make me feel like a total ass for ordering a plain burger.

The food was out in like 5 minutes, piping hot.  The crinkle fries were divine, but I'm a total sucker for crinkle fries. Burger was hot, juicy and yummy.  The serving size of both was bountiful.  

All in all, a wonderful lunch that I would partake in again.
Burgers, fries and local brew. Exactly was I was looking for. The chocolate shake and "liberty shell" were great too!

No Chipotles are made alike! I must say after two times coming here for a pick up of a burrito bowl; it has been less impressive and my expectations have not been even acknowledge. During my online, it updated my pick up for a later time, which I am fine. I got there at exactly the same time as the pick up time but I did not get acknowledged or greeted as I waited by the pick up area/cash register.

What was odd to me, besides the poor service, was that people who came and ordered got served before me. Basically, if I waited in line and ordered, I would have received my food sooner than ordering online. 

Overall, don't blame the Chipotle brand just the peeps working here. I have given a few weeks since the second incident, so I am not still hyped from the incident but nothing has changed. Still feel this location sucks. Luckily I can find another location.

So happy to have a new non-sandwich, healthy lunch option near my office. There are a lot of great options with eggs, chicken, beef, and even some seafood. Most entrees come in 3 different sizes which is great depending how hungry you are or how many calories you are looking to consume. All items come with calorie count to easily pay attention to what you are eating. I love all the side options such as a side salad, chicken salad, dessert, hummus, etc. prices are fairly comparable for the area. I got the Asian chicken salad which was delicious. The layout of this store is a bit awkward, trying to navigate the salad section and the microwaves and utensils when it is busy is difficult. Regardless, I'll be back soon!

Just tried their new crispy chicken sandwich, so great!!! I was a little jealous of all the gooey cheeseburgers oozing and sizzling but I know those are good and I will get it again. 
Shakes, concretes and fries in point

This place will make you be that much more sad that Philly doesn't have a Panera. 
Not worth too lengthy of a review as it is a typical fast food / service kind of place. The menu just isn't all that interesting and the taste just really is lacking. It is in the bread. Panera just wins out on better bread and more interesting combinations of cheese/proteins.

I just left this McDonald's after grabbing some breakfast. I'm a temple student and I commute into the city. I don't really like it either. My morning are rough and I was starving so decided to through the drive through. The gentleman that took my order was very friendly and professional. We even giggled with each other when he got tongue tied. The young lady that gave me my order greeted me with a beautiful smile and was also super friendly and professional. Both these employees had not only made me smile the entire way to class but they make me want to come back for breakfast more often. Thank you to both of you for making my rough morning just a little bit better!!! I will be coming back soon my breakfast was wonderful, my order was correct!!

I LOVE IT HERE!!!!! The food is pretty good and their root beer floats are amazing along with all their other desserts. They also have free filtered water! This is a great spot to just pop in and out, or sit for a while. It has that fun city atmosphere. There are always a lot of people but I've never had trouble finding a seat. They have tons of seats outside too, which is my favorite. 

The service is great, everyone is very friendly and welcoming. I haven't had one bad encounter. The price is not too bad. I'd only say they need to work on perhaps more combo options that lets people get burgers and say fries and a shake. Buying everything seperately does add up annoyingly.
One of my go to places for lunch break, Kati rolls are good but the chicken biriyani is a must try. Make sure you use the white sauce it makes everything delicious.

while not a blow-your-mind breakfast place, it's sufficient to fill your stomach at a reasonable price. i ordered the anaheim scramble with a side of potatoes and a small bottled oj (total: around 9 bucks and some change.) the eggs and potatoes were mediocre but filling. no complaints here as i knew what to expect.

as a gluten intolerant diner, i can't attest to the quality and/or deliciousness if their pastries. however, these flour-laden items looked tasty. 

pleasant dining area and staff. one of the nicest "panera"-type places i've come across in my travels.

Nothing special. The burgers are decent (there are definitely better ones in Philly), the fries were meh (but I do love crinkle). I didn't get a shake, so maybe my opinion would be different if I did......but not by much.

Based on the price, and the size of the burger, I wouldn't exactly recommend this to anyone. I've had better, I've had worse.

Kati Rolls in Philly!!!! Yes and they absolutely are healthier and tastier than their counterparts in NYC. How can I describe, the ingredients are fresh the meat always tender and the roti is perfectly toasted and not super greasy. My favorite are the paneer rolls. All the rolls come with 2 sauces; a nice creamy yogurt sauce and a hot sauce that is by far hottest stuff I've eaten in a while. Don't be foolish and stuff your face with that hot sauce, the next morning will not be pleasant I promise you.

The best part about this place is that it's open late night so after a night of binging you can actually eat a decent meal that won't charge 1000 calories into your body.

Oh and before I forget, make sure you check in on Yelp to get 10% off your order.

We already know all about the food but let me take a minute and talk about the staff and the amazing service they provided. Raced over from north philly to make sure my boyfriend can try Shake Shack for the first time (he needs a reference point for when we go to In-N-Out in two weeks lol) but got here as they were closing. I hate being that customer but let me tell you, they were so friendly and helpful, like made my night freals (shoutout to Clarence aka Gabe and the rest of the closing crew). Seriously, come through to this Shake Shack location, bomb food per usual, but the people are exceptional. Thanks, guys!
I had the best sandwiched fresh and nice better 100% than subway i had the sandwich i enjoy it so much so yes this is the one of the places i will go too :-)

Honestly the worst fast food place I ever been to , they're rude . Every time I go through the drive threw they laugh and say what over and over . They messed up my order I ordered a chicken sandwich and a cheese burger . They asked me what I ordered like 3 times while I was waiting for my food and asked if I ordered a bacon chicken sandwich and I said no . Then they call "a cheese burger and chrispy chicken" which is what I got and I went home and they gave me 2 chicken sandwhichds one with bacon . I called and told them and they were rude , and giggling than the lady handed the phone to someone else . And my fries are usually cold . I hate this wendys so much . AND THEY HAD NO DRINKS EXCEPT FOR SPRITE ZERO AND DIDNT THINK TO TELL ME THAT WHILE I WAS ORDERING .

OMG I am in love with this place. I work in Center City and often times am unable to leave my office to grab lunch. So when I saw that they deliver and the only minimum was a sandwich, well I was over the moon. Plus the fact that their subs were awesome made it that much better. Everyone was so friendly.

I have been grabbing lunch from the halal cart at 20th and Market for the past two years and one of my coworkers suggested I try out Spice End.  I got the typical chicken and lamb over rice and it was 10 times better than the cart food.  Very fresh chicken and lamb and they give you bottles of their white and red sauce to put on yourself.  If you like spicy food, their red sauce is delicious.  While I usually finish the cart food quickly, I took half of my lunch back to the office for an afternoon snack.  For $4 more than the cart, your get a large portion that is made to order.  Very nice atmosphere in there as well.  This is my new lunch spot in Rittenhouse.

Decent food. Rolls are of good quality and tasty. Platters are just not bad. You get limca here. Just 3 stars because of the staff behaviour (not willing to give enough napkins, I can't believe it. But, he apologized later for doing that). A good place to try rolls. Quick snack, when you are hungry.

I love Chipotle!!! It's the McDonalds of mexican food, but a lot more edible. I mean...by a lot. This one is pretty close to my office, so I come here from time to time. I've been here both during peak and off-peak times and the service is fairly consistent. Fast and delicious. I do have to take a star away because my office did a mass order a few months ago and the order was all out of whack. Despite the mishap, I would still spend my money here.

The fried chicken here the bang man
It really good the service is good and fast 
I like it friendly services. Thank you guys
Please keep up the good services
We had achari paneer rolls and they were delicious. If you are looking for a fancy restaurant then this is not the place for you. Good for takeouts or for grabbing a quick bite.

Review pertains to the Concrete only:

It took me this long to post a review because I was so very disappointed when I received the Rittenhouse Squared flavored Concrete single. Very expensive for what you get - pictures are worth a thousand words. It was decent tasting but the presentation was horrible- as if someone had scooped more than half out.

Would you rather

Spend $18 for breakfast from a franchise place with a full kitchen and full staff that takes 25 minutes to get your food  ---OR---  Spend $8 for breakfast from 2 guys in a cart that can hardly speak English but could serve 50 people in the same amount of time?

I made the wrong decision this morning.  Stick with the trucks.

I've been here for lunch also and the soups aren't bad.

This is a solid late night food option. Kati rolls are delicious and filling! Paneer and chicken were my favorite. The platters are a little on the pricier side, especially with so many food truck options around town that sell similar (but probably more oily/less healthy) platters for half the price.

This review is focused on concrete (frozen custard blended with mix-ins). The pre-created options seemed a little intense, so I decided to make my own: a half portion of  Vanilla with Chocolate Toffee. After having dinner just down the street, the half-sized portion was way too much - I would have been happy sharing this given the heaviness of the custard. I liked the chocolate toffee, which was like a Heath bar, but wish there had been more of it.

I want to start out by saying I agree with Lexy M. This place is awesome but other than for the thrill of my first time there, I wouldn't stand in line for 30-45 minutes for this place (the line is part of the experience, which is why I am ok doing it once for my first go). 

I went right in the middle of a center city lunch rush and from the time i got in line to the time i left with my food was about 34 minutes (not as bad as I expected). The line moved pretty swiftly considering I was outside and almost at the end of their windows when I began.

Employees walked up and down the line offering menus, and when one overheard someone talking about gluten free diets, the employee offered him a gluten free menu. That's customer service. It's been a while since I've seen customer service so good that they anticipated someone's needs before they even asked for it. They also gave out custard samples in line and collected our trash. I liked that I had something to do while I waited.

I ordered the SmokeShack burger which was delicious and the chopped peppers give it this amazing sweet taste that will leave you going "hmmm" in a good way. It's not the healthiest option on the menu but I wanted to go all the way. There's also yummy smoked applewood bacon and the burger was cooked PERFECT despite the fact that I didn't really specify (can you specify? I don't know if that's an option). 

I also got a shake. Beware: the peanut butter shake is yummy but it is seriously the highest calorie shake on the menu. I had NO idea and was a little disappointed when I pulled the nutritional information and checked the calorie count. Let me put it this way - it's over 800 calories. The other shakes aren't as bad.

Lastly, they give you a nice little remote that lights up when your food is ready which is nice so I didn't have to stand around obsessively listening for my name to be called.

I'll enjoy when this place calms down when the newness wears off. Shake Shack is pretty cool in my book (and they also have a lot of great sustainable practices as well as using tons of local ingredients - all things I support).

Just hit this place after the auto show. It's in a food court kind of situation so you have a ton of choices. I ordered the beef tacos and some dikon kim chi, and a can of diet soda. Total cost: $13.42.

The tacos were superb. Overflowing with beef and guac and veggies. Three small but filling tacos in corn tortillas. $9.00 felt a little high priced but every bite was perfect. Bring napkins because the tortillas fall apart.

The kim chi was nearly inedible. It tasted like it just had tobasco dumped on it. I choked it down because it was a tiny serving for $2.50, but I would never order it again.

Will come back for sure, but will know what not to order in the future.

This place is really good when it comes to burgers, their bacon burgers are so good and with their cheese fries those are sooo good my family goes there a lot. Their lemonade is SO amazing and I just think its neat that they have those alarm things when they buzz that's so smart I go to the one next door to plaza too you should go!



Catherine age 9

Just split a shake burger, basically a standard cheeseburger. It was delicious and definitely worth $5. Swallowed it down with a Jack's hard cider which was also quite tasty. Sat outside and enjoyed watching Philadelphia life go by. Lovely burger joint

Shake Shack is my favorite burger spot here in Philly. Their burgers, fries, hot dogs, AND ice cream are all beyond delicious, made to perfection. If heaven was a burger place, it would be Shake Shack!

I've only been here during the lunch rush so that may color my review.

This place reminds me a lot of NYC - you better know what you want when you get in line - think the soup Nazi - otherwise you will get a Philly attytude. 

The portions are an acceptable size - just right for lunch. The service is quick though the help at times seems disorganized. The last few times I have had lunch here I ordered and paid online ahead of time (at least an hour) and half the time my order was not ready when I arrived, and once I was ten minutes late.

Overall, I like the place since it is close to the office but the staff could use a shaking up as another yelper mentioned.

Pretty good burger, very buttery (including the bun). Everything is really fresh. The fries are good, too. However, I'm never full after I have the fries and burger and I feel like I should be because it's pretty expensive.

For a franchise, Corner Bakery Cafe has some high quality food and a comforting atmosphere. Very similar to Panera, Corner Bakery Cafe offers breakfast, cafe style food, and an assortment of pastries. Their quinoa oatmeal and spinach sweet crisp salad are my two favorite items on the menu. If you ever pass one of these, you should definitely stop in and try it out!

It would be stupid of me to blab on about shake shack because instead of sitting here reading this you should really just go eat it yourself. Seriously, go, lazypants. 

I live a whopping two minute walk away and therefore eat waaay too many burgers but I don't hate it. 

Perfectly seasoned meat, soft potato roll, fresh lettuce and tomato, melty cheese, and of course the shack sauce, in which I am almost certain that they put crack because I literally wake up craving it. I'm talkin 7am burger craving... Disgusting but true. I am a loyal devotee to the plain ol' shack burger but have heard good things about the other burger varieties (aside from the shroom burger). Have also taken bites of the various hot dogs, wasn't disappointed, though I'm not a huge hot dog gal. 

Milkshakes are thick, gluttonous calorie bombs- AKA what a milkshake is meant to be. 

Crinkle cut fries could probably have come from an Ore Ida bag straight outta the freezer but I wouldn't even care as long as they're smothered in that fantastic cheese sauce. I want to bathe in this cheese sauce.

The wait is usually not horrific, they have free filtered water/ also serve a decent beer, and I bought my future neice/nephew a shake shack onesie so clearly I'm a fan. 

Whoops, looks like I blabbed on anyway. Aaaaaaand now I'm craving.
Great burger joint. Fries and dogs are great too. Milkshakes are good but overpriced imo. Always a goto spot when I'm not sure where to go.
Popcorn chicken is very good and I recommend it. BBQ chicken not worth it. Bento is ok but I would probably just end up getting popcorn chicken again next time.

Wish I had read reviews for this Chipotle before ordering.  I ordered online for pick up for my hubby and myself after a long day.  Chipotle needs to change their standards for salads to include more lettuce. Don't get me wrong I like all the ingredients but the primary ingredient should be lettuce.  Also, my salad had just a few bites of chicken. Maybe they were being stingy because I picked up at 9:30pm and they were running out for the night or they really want you to pay for extra meat, but I could hardly even tell there was any.   The staff was really friendly which is the only reason that I have 2 stars and not 1.

I've been here several times now and still am not sure what all the hype is about. The burgers here are a slight upgrade from the ones at McDonald's and are on par with the ones at Five Guys. For maybe just a few dollars more, I could get a much better burger - larger, made of better quality ingredients, and WITH fries - from a fine dining restaurant. On my last trip here, the cashier tried to make conversation with me and then short-changed me by a couple dollars. Not cool. During past experiences, I've also tried the shakes - and maybe it was because of the flavor they had available that day, but the shakes were flavorless and tasted more like vanilla than their intended flavor. On the bright side, if you go during down times, it's a good place for a casual beer & burger gathering with friends.

After trying Shake Shack ice cream at various events, I decided I needed to finally visit the store and get the full experience. 

My boyfriend and I visited Shake Shack on a Saturday night around 7. Although there was no wait to put our order in, the seating was limited. There is a big menu displayed on the wall, additional hand held menus can be found by the entrance door. 

We ordered milk shakes, fries and a burger to split. I was surprised to see the burger served on a regular potato bun, regardless it was delicious. The fries were even better, crinkle cut and crispy. We ordered holiday flavored milkshakes which are sadly no longer in season. The Christmas cookie was delicious. 

Here are a few of my other favorite things about Shake Shack:

-If you are just coming in for ice cream, or "concrete" there is a special express "C-Line."
-The tables are made from recycled wood, like from a bowling lane. 
-They have a bike club that meets monthly.
-There are speicial menu items for your pup!
-Oh, and the concrete is delicious!

Being an Indian from India, my expectations for kathi rolls is rather high and I can't say this place met my expectations, but I will say it came close. It tasted a bit Americanized and lacked the true flavor of a kathi roll. 

Tried the chicken tikka kathi which was decent sized but one may not fill you up if you are looking to have a full meal. 

Would have given it 3 stars, but +1 for being open late making it a good after bar food option. 

~$5-6 for a kathi roll, $11 for 2.

This was my second time to Shake Shack and I was not disappointed. I got the SmokeShack burger and was delighted. It was a little spicier than I imagined it would be, but the bacon and sauce balanced that out.

I am only giving 4 stars in lieu of 5 because the crinkle cut fries are gone (sadface) and the straight cut fries don't last as long in the cheese sauce. Also, they probably jammed in one too many tables in the seating area, and it was a bit too tight.

No matter what, I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone, and I can't wait to go back. Great place to take out-of-towners looking for a casual and delicious meal.

I'll admit it.  I'm shamelessly addicted to Chipotle burrito bowls.  The ingredients are fresh, and I have no idea what they marinate their chicken in or what secret ingredient they use in their guac, but there's just no recreating it at home.  

I will agree with the general sentiment that the line is always long, but it moves pretty quickly.  Also, don't bother with the online ordering at this location.  Almost a half dozen times (...should I be ashamed that I have THAT much experience with this?) I've arrived and my order hasn't been ready.  I've gotten every reason in the book: "online ordering is down", "the receipt didn't print", "we were waiting until you arrived so we could make it fresh"... I could go on.  Just wait in the line.

Maybe it's just because it's shiny and new, but I love this Chipotle. To be fair, I love all Chipotles, but this one tops them all for convenience to my apartment. The staff is friendly and generous with the barbacoa, which is always a bonus! I like the seating arrangement as well, with the long tables instead of smaller individual ones. I guess they had to do that since the location is rather small, but it really works. Very homey feeling.

They have really good food. It's just a bit pricey.

I always come here with my best friends. It's in a nice location. I usually get the shack burger, lemonade (or what ever mixed lemonade mix they have), and the fries. Within the past few years, they switched from crinkle cut, to shoe string, to crinkle cut and boy are my friends and I glad that they decided to switch back to crinkle cut!

I love this place!!! First of all, the staff was so nice and helpful. I bought 5 different meals and they were all delicious. My favorites were the beef stew and the beef stroganoff. The small is a perfect size for one. Working in the medical field i don't have time to go out for lunch and struggle putting meals together all the time so this is perfect. Small meals range from $5-9. They are so flavorful and healthy I am so excited his place opened up shop in philly and even more exited for the rittenhouse square location!
You just have to go and experience it for yourself. I can promise you won't be disappointed! Not your typical chain place.. has an awesome vibe with great food!

yes, i know it's somewhat frowned upon to review a chain. but the first time i had jimmy john's, i realized i had been missing out. you see, i decided a while ago that i don't particularly care for cold cuts. we used to get along just fine, but sometime after my stint as a vegetarian ended i never got the taste for hoagies back.

that was, until.. the VITO. the bread here is made in house, it's so fresh, and the staff have always been friendly to me. they made a believer out of me despite my resistance.

oh, and sweet 90s music in here! i like.

I'm seriously shocked that this has such a low rating. Shake Shack is definitely my go-to place for a great burger! Yes it's kind of pricey, but it's great every single time. Their fries are always perfectly cooked too! Definitely give it a shot.

Stopped on a Tuesday night. Slow, so food came quickly. I ordered the shack burger, cheese fries, and a peanut butter milkshake. 

Overall, I really loved the burger. Cooked medium, it was juicy and had the perfect amount of roll, meat, lettuce, and tomato. So many places forget that portion sizes are important when making a sandwich. I want to taste everything in one bite! It's really good, but I've had better. 

The fries are crinkle cut, and mine were prepared perfectly. Crunchy and not overly greasy. Their frozen, but very good for that type. I personally prefer fresh cut with skins. I can see a lot of people liking their fries.

The peanut butter milkshake was outstanding! I will come back just for them! Creamy with the right amount of peanut butter. Much better than I anticipated when ordering. 

They sell beer, the atmosphere is decent with music playing. The table I ate at was salvaged from a bowling lane. Pretty cool. Service was really good, welcoming. 

I'll be back at some point. It's definitely a high end fast food type of place. You can get better burgers, but these are different in a good way.

I absolutely love Chipotle even with all the food scares. I always get the Barbacoa, which is kind of like pulled beef with delicious seasoning. This place is usually good, although some times the service is a little slow. The staff is typically friendly though.

A Father's Day outing to Shake Shack got no resistance from the kids.  Good sign, because I was sure that the long line would elicit moans and groans.  But at 1pm for lunch, the line was about 25 deep and we were at the counter in 10 minutes. Bu then, we were handed the pager and used the intervening 25 minutes before we got our food to jockey for a table.  Takes a little patience, location and of course, strategy, but an appropriate table should open up.  Be ready to swoop, courteously, of course, and stake your claim.  Just don't come with the kids' friends (there were 16 of us) if you can help it.

The burgers were very good.  Juicy (or if you have it in your heart to disparage, greasy) beyond all expectation (have lipitor at hand), good beefy Lafrieda blend (if only I had remembered to order medium rare) and bright fresh leafy lettuce and tomatoes made for a very good sandwich.  The eldest daughter got the 'Shroom Burger, which ever so slightly bested the meat sandwich.  Oozing with cheese and fried to a crisp, the moistness and deep woodsy flavor of the portobella was satisfying.  The man-cub got the best of both worlds with his Shack Stack.  

The all important fries were ok.  Crinkle cut and crispy, but it lacked the rich potato flavor that Five guys and Nathan's fries have.  Maybe make them it bit thicker?

The Rittenhouse Concrete was fabulous.  Chocolate flavors with depth and cocoa wattage and the crunch of La Colombe beans. Impressive.

Service was very helpful.  Menu stated that you have to explicitly request lettuce, tomato, etc, but we didn't and we wanted.  They insisted that they make new burgers with the said toppings and delivered (with a comp order of fries) to the table.  

Bathroom was clean and tres modern.  The paper towel dispenser was really a hand dryer.  Clever.

New destination for the family for burgers.

First introduced to this place by my gf's friend. We don't have one of these in NYC. Was pretty excited. As I first walk in, my first opinion of the place is close similarity compared to Panera in regards to the food, decor, and ordering. But Corner Bakery is clearly cleaner and chic compared to Panera. They also offer more options of tea, coffee, and sweets. I liked it.

I went with a friend and we each got a concrete ice cream. One had Termini Bros cannoli shell and ricotta which was very tasty. 1 point. 
The other had philly pretzel which was simply horrid plus it was missing some ingredients. minus 2 points. 
Then I noticed a woman sitting next to us had what looked like the cannoli. I actually asked her if that was what it was since it was so much better looking than mine with the ingredients overflowing out of the cup. Minus 2 pts.
We were approached by one of the worker's who asked about our shake and offered something else when we said the pretzel was putrid, but I think that was because the first attempt that they made broke through the cup when it was picked up. half a point for effort
I might give this place another try if I was in the area, but I wouldn't go seek it out. The burgers seem ok as they are made with decent meat, but the bun looked undesirable. The long lines and corporate, haute-fast food vibe also turn me off.
This location should not be qualified as fast food. Taking 15 minutes to get from the menu ordering to the front of the window is not fast.

Simply fantastic. The best part is that I don't have to worry about my dietary restrictions or portion control because they pretty much have that all covered ahead of time. The spicy salmon is my favorite. And their juices/shakes are excellent! Also the brownies - yum!

Great kati rolls. My fav is their achari paneer rool. Mixed veggie rool is also very good. Once a week at least. 

Give it a try.. you wont be disappointed!!

I don't understand what all the hype is about on Shake Shack. The burgers at other locations has to be better for SS to have all this recognition. The burgers in Philly were so greasy that the bottom bun soaked it all up and became unappealing. What happened to putting lettuce on the bottom so the grease doesn't ooze onto the bottom bun? The burger was also cooked unevenly and it was medium on one side and well done on the other. There's nothing good about the fries either - nothing more than your flash fried frozen back of fries that you can get at the supermarket. The process needs to be more efficient here as well because when we got our shakes, they were all melted as if it was sitting there in the warm kitchen while our burgers were being made. I'm really glad I went late at night and there was no line.

The good things that I liked about SS that gave it another star was that the dining area was well maintained and clean, they serve beer, free water dispensed in the dining area, and I liked the hot dogs better than the burgers. The toppings and ingredients has a lot of potential to be really good, so until next when everything is more refined, I'll give it a shot again and update this review!

i have never actually been to this place but they deliever to my office every few weeks for lunch meetings and wow!!! most fabulous sandwitches! i have never seen a menu or known exactly what the sandwitches i have eaten are called, but they are always so unique. i like being surprised when its corner bakery. today i had a chicken salad sandwitch with nuts and rasins! last week i had a roast beef with avacado and tasty dressings. just well thought out sandwitches.
Great food and service. I forgot to ask for lettuce and tomatoes when I ordered. But I asked for it afterward, they still gave it to me on the side.

Corner Bakery is a reliable restaurant to hit on your lunch break for salads, soups, pastas, mac and cheese, and sandwiches. The food is decent but nothing is absolutely stellar. What's nice about Corner Bakery is that you can carbo load with comfort foods if you want or you can chose to take the healthier route and get one of their salads. They have a huge variety of sandwiches and salads and they also offer a "pick 2" option. I tend to go with the pick 2 option so I can try half of a sandwich and half of a salad. I recommend the rustic Italian Panini, if you're willing to accept that it's 950 calories (yikes). 

Corner Bakery is conveniently located right across the street from the Comcast Center. The restaurant is quite large with a lot of tables. There is a genuine restaurant feel here and it's affordably priced. I love their chips and cookies... I just wish the food was better.

My friend in Chicago smartly pointed me to this sandwich joint, which is stupidly close to where I live and work. I'm in trouble- the aroma of the bread when you first walk in is intoxicating. Combine lightning fast sandwich assembly plus friendly staff, a delicious sandwich in my hand, all at amazing prices, and you finally have me turning away from the comfort of Wawa hoagies. 

On speed- seriously, I barely had time to mentally process my order and they'd already made it. But maybe the speed was enhanced by my delirious hangry state. 

Next time, I'll ask to double the tomatoes and lettuce on the Vegetarian sub. Definitely will keep the bacon+.

Positives-Fast friendly service. Fair price
Negative-have your employees take the time to make the breakfast sandwich with common sense. If the croissant is falling apart maybe you should not use it for a customer's breakfast sandwich. The whole thing was falling apart and could not be eaten like a sandwich. I had to use a fork. And this is not the first time I have experienced this here.

Shake Shack is a pretty good burger, but I wasn't absolutely blown away. For the price you're paying, you're gonna get a really juicy, well seasoned burger, but like I said--nothing stellar.

The fries are the shape that I like (love krinkle cut) but I feel they didn't have enough flavor. And the cheese they put on it? Yuck, it's whiz! It's not even tasty whiz either.

The custards are super delicious though! I wouldn't come here and order a burger again, but I'd definitely come for the milk shakes and the custards! It's kinda like a fancy blizzard cause you can pick the toppings that go into it and the ice cream is way more delicious.

We had a delicious breakfast here while staying downtown. Portions were hearty. Service was quick and friendly. Huge seating areas. 

The only area which seemed neglected was the bathroom which was dirty, had no paper towels, and TP was just sitting on handicap handrail instead of inside the dispenser (super gross!)

Burgers are delicious. They have that famed crispy crunchy texture. My favorite is the smoke shack. Fridays are pretty decent as well. However it can be Mayham in there between all the bros and tourists. I try and avoid it at peak hours. Plus the seating is not comfortable. But I will return over and over because the burgers are that good.

Hangover cure for the win! Greasy burger, check. Crazy good cheese fries, yes. I dont consider this place gourmet- but hits the spot when you want to 'cheat' and not do it driving through disgusting "golden arches." Its a bit hard to find a table when its too cold to sit outside - less space because noone is sitting outside (A+ for outside seating by the way) but tables seem to turn over quickly.  I dont know what they put in their special sauce -but sign me up again. My burger was just what I needed on a (post friday night) cold saturday afternoon.

My friend and I got the roast chicken tacos and my other friend got the salad bowl. Both were below mediocre.. there was a lot going on but no flavor. I was excited to try this because I love Korean and Mexican food, and this concept was awesome. I know they can tweak it and make the food better, because there is potential! But I would not eat here again

Just stopped by today, the line was pretty long but the customer service was great. They had employees outside handing out menus and free samples of the days custard which was coffee & donuts.  Once inside and your order is made, the wait is pretty quick.

I got a SmokeShack, cheese fries, and a black and white shake.  My brother got the ShackBurger.  The burger I got which is a cheeseburger with smoked bacon, chopped cherry peppers, and shacksauce.  This burger is fantastic. Salty, well-seasoned, ground Angus bursting with flavor, and just enough grease. The bacon was plenty smokey and added a perfect porky crunch to this masterpiece, while the cherry peppers took care of the need for a bit of heat and some vinegar tang, and the Shack Sauce rounded out the bunch with a zippy, creamy, extra dollop of cholesterol. The bun and wax paper combo did a perfect job of keeping all of the accounts in order while I was busy trying not to bite my hand with overzealousness. Is this the perfect bacon cheeseburger? It's one of the best, no doubt.

The fries are crinkle cut.  These little potato accordions were crispy, well salted (but not overly so) and smothered in the delicious Shack cheddar and American cheese sauce. Definitely worth a go. 

Overall I have to say this well worth the hype and one of the best burger joints in Philly.

Just stopped in for a danish and coffee before a meeting. They have coffee with unlimited refills and a home made version of a blueberry pop tart. Extremely friendly and helpful service and just what I needed this morning.

I thought I'd try this as we don't have them back home. The burger was decent--the usual greasy burger with a slice of American cheese on it. The sauce they put on it makes it much better, though. The fries were crispy, and the shake was thick and rich. It wasn't the best burger I've ever had, of course, but it was a solid meal and worth having again.
3 and a half stars. Burgers taste yummy. But their small. Fast service. Place is crowded. Food warm. Beer nasty... Too pricy in my opinion.

This was my 1st visit here. It was my 1st time at any Shake Shack. I knew the burger would be good cause the scent coming out of the place was amazing. I got the Concrete (the chocolatey one) that was delicious. The burger was really good but the fries had a blah taste to them. I got the half & half to drink. It was good. It tasted homemade. With all that being said it has been too long since I've was there & I want to go back.

Amazing halal food and a great restaurant w nice staff and plenty of seating. Prime for late night and getting plenty of food for a good price. If you're from NYC it's very similar to Halal Guys there

I love HIP CITY VEG but I have to start commenting more when the food is messed up or the order is wrong This is the worst location out of them all. We love the breakfast options but the cooks are horrible, rude and always gets the order wrong. Best location is in DC like I posted before. This morning, I Paid for my sandwich to be one way but the cook didn't deliver. I didn't find out until I was far away. They receive 3 stars because the manager refunded my money with just a phone call. However we drove from Cheltenham for breakfast to get what I love, not something else!

Being from NY, I was skeptic trying this place out for late night craving.  Good thing it was open late and not crowded.  

Ordered the Paneer Tikka Kati Rolls to go -- the order took about 10 minutes to get ready.   Given that there were two other people in the place, would have expected a little speedy preparation (guess the NYer in me likes fast pace and service).

The food was delicious - wrap did not seem to heavy and paneer was very moist and chewy.  The green chutney inside was perfect blend and it did not have too many onions to leave that after smell in your mouth.  The two sauces available on the side are white sauce and hot sauce.  ** Spicy Alert ** for the hot sauce so please be careful.  White sauce was great but a little thick in texture and hard to dip.  I did not see any of those sauces in the actual rolls.  I wish they had the extra green chutney also on the side.
Although everything is oversalted, this chipotle is my go-to place to get a guacamole salad.  The staff is strong and the place is clean.  ... And the music isn't horrible.

I love this place.  Where else can you get a real breakfast sandwich to go, i.e., an egg, cheese, and ham paninni?  They've got yummy breakfast food, from breakfast panini to oatmeal to fruit and yogurt parfaits, great coffee, scrumptious bagels and mini bundt cakes, good rolls, and even yummier lunch choices.  They've got sandwiches, salads, soups, etc. etc.  You can take out or, if you want, place your order at the counter, pick up your numbered ticket, sit at a table, put the ticket on the little holder thingy, and they'll bring you your food.  Easy as pie.  Oh, I think they have pie, too...  The only thing that I don't like is that I tried to take friends here for Sunday brunch once, and they were closed.  Turns out they're not open on the weekend.
everything from snap kitchen is wonderful!! i love eating here because it's healthy and makes me feel great!!

OVERRATED, I think the place is pretty mismanaged, I mean it just opened up in Philadelphia and it's no longer clean and just sloppy.  Employees don't really care about service, it's obvious to anyone.  If your told you had to wait at least 30 minutes before your burger order is ready, you would think "this must be an amazing burger."  not even close, fries are disgusting too, artificial.  The burger itself was ok in terms of juiciness, but no flavor and clearly low quality beef, the hot dogs are just terrible.  Now for the Milk shake, it's Good, not great.  but then again, how hard is it to make a milk shake, that ice-cream and milk in a blender. This is another trendy NYC product, don't believe the hype, Five-guys is clearly better in quality and service, and elevation burger destroys it in every category.

Lots of variety on the menu. Taco happy hour is a great time to try a few things! Very tasty and well priced. The meats were well seasoned and the other toppings complimented them nicely. Fusion well executed!

Yum! Yum! Yum!

I had never explored the world of kati rolls until my boyfriend took me here to try an "Indian burrito." I love the achari paneer roll, it's my favorite. It has this amazing spicy tang and is a must try!

Spice end is a great option for something quick and delicious or/take-out. Oh and definitely try Limca, it's a  citrus Indian soft drink. I'm not much of a soda drinker but it's definitely a nice refreshing treat.

The staff is slow and you often have to repeat several times what you want. They give the skimpiest servings out of any chipotle I have ever visited and will charge you extra for what should be the full amount. They're always out of an ingredient and you'll be waiting 10 or more minutes for the Ingredient to come out. Save your money and walk a few extra blocks to 15th and walnut or liberty place.

I'm the dutchess so I guess I should write a review. I love this place! I used to live around here and there is a few taco bell's around me where I live now but I keep going to this one. Why you ask? The food is always hot, fresh and yummy. The time in line and the time it takes to order is fast. If there is a problem they can usually fix it for you. Very clean. restaurant and bathroom. The drive thur is fast also. That is why I keep coming back.

Spice End attempts to recreate the New York, quasi-Indian street food classics kathi rolls and platters. They succeed probably better than anyone else in Philly, albeit at a steep cost.

Platters come with meats layered on top of rice and are served with 2 sauces (very spicy red and creamy white), toasted pita, and an indifferent salad of iceberg lettuce and tomato. The sauces display less thickness than the iconic NYC ones but mirror the sauces' taste pretty faithfully. The fluffy rice tastes light due to a lack of excess seasoning and grease. The meats we sampled were all well-seasoned and cooked, and the Spice End platter (essentially the chef's personal rendition of classic chicken and rice) outshone the others with large, juicy chunks of aromatically spiced chicken. Though we didn't sample any kathi rolls, I've heard from numerous sources that they're decent.

Pricing acted as the sole negative of my Spice End experience; platters clock in at around $9, a few dollars more expensive than the cart versions. Spice End offers very decent recreations of beloved street foods, and is definitely worth visiting when the insatiable craving for platters strike. If they reduced their prices a bit, this could easily become a regular destination.

Thanks to all this hype, there is now no line across the street at Iron Chef Jose Garces' Village Whiskey, so I can enjoy my serious burger and a Connemara peated single malt Irish whiskey in peace, all the while laughing at the line outside Shake Shack.

THANK YOU SHAKE SHACK!!!

[OK, Shake Shake burgers are a pretty decent deal (not costing $26, like the ridiculous foie gras-topped Village King at VW).  So there, this really is a 5-star review of Shake Shake!]

Sláinte!

This place just wasn't good. If they're not careful, it's going to reflect poorly on the main restaurant in fish town. Which is sad cause that place is everything. Take half the talent from there and bring it to their burger stand, and then it would be decent. 
The burger was well done, dry, and somehow cold. The cheese on it was just placed on top, not even slightly melted. The mushrooms were also cold. 
Also got the fried chicken and it was super lame, the bun was so stale. There was barely anything else on the sandwich. 
I hope they change out the staff cause there needs to be a drastic change in order for them to really succeed. But it's in the heart of all colleges so they'll do fine.

I hate to give a place one star, but this place has consistently disappointed.  It's like the staff just doesn't care at this point.  I walked in for a pastry today and asked for it warmed up.  The young woman at the cash register couldn't have been any more miserable or disinterested.  She took my order, and never even so much as bothered to walk over and place my pastry back by the kitchen so they could warm it up.  I had a meeting to go to, but I just wanted to see how long I would stand there before she noticed.....an eternity goes by and she finally comes over and says, 'Oh, I guess I didn't put your order in' and then non chalantly takes her time and doesn't even say I'm sorry.  This has happened time and time again.  It's the morning people, folks have to get to their jobs and these folks walk around like they are miserable and could care less if you have somewhere to go.  I actually stopped going here a few months ago and just went in on a whim hoping things had changed, but they haven't!  Save yourself some grief and don't go here, especially if you are in a hurry.

Promising menu and also the plate looks like the photo.
Even the ingredients for the Anaheim scrambler are better than expected for this kind of venue.
BUT getting the eggs and potatos cold/half warm is really a bummer at 8:30am

Coffee is as it is everywhere....

I admit, I default to this place when I can't think of anything else to eat, but it's only because they take credit cards and they're less than a block away from work...

This is a VERY busy lunch destination, and they have table service, but that means you stand in line at a register to order and pay for food and then try to find an open table with your little number and wait for someone to find you with your food.  Getting a table is so much easier now that they've expanded into another store front next door, so the army re-con vibe of table-finding is now pretty much extinguished.  

I must stress that the food runners are very nice, but they only bring you your food.  I've seen WAY too many older women yelling at the runners to bring them silverware, etc.  The silverware (it really is metal) is next to the soda fountain and various stations around the restaurant and it's self-serve.

The food here is meh...pretty tasteless, but not bad.  I recommend their panini over anything else as I've found heating makes them taste more like something.  The soups are really good.  The deserts and pastries are AWESOME, but really expensive.  A lady behind me in line the other commented on the fact that a 2"square brownie costs $2.29.  A whole bundt cake can go for as much as $30, which, while cheaper than bakeries, isn't really as good as the bakery's.

I definitely recommend their catering services.  They are reasonable, satisfy most dietary restrictions, and they are ON TIME with their deliveries.  Plus, if works is paying for it, go for their crazy dream bars or the maple pecan bars.  You'll thank me for it.

I love, love, love Snap Kitchen and particularly this location. The staff are super-friendly and accommodating which makes you feel very welcomed. Have picked up a variety of meals ranging from the Almond Pancakes to the Naked Beef and the delish Bison Hash. Will definitely be a regular here....
This place is overhyped and very overpriced. The salad was not good and the sweet potato fries were an extremely small serving for the price.

I had my first Shake Shack experience on Sunday, and luckily got there when the line wasn't too long. My boyfriend and I went for it and each got a Shack Burger (cheeseburger with Shack sauce) and split fries, a hot dog, and a vanilla malt milkshake. Here's the break down:

-ShackBurger: 3 stars. Had a decent flavor, but could barely taste the shack sauce, and from what I did taste, just tasted like mayo. This burger has nothing on 5 Guys.

-Hot Dog: 2 stars. Just a regular hot dog...split and grilled. Okay, but nothing special.

-Fries: 4 stars. Great texture and salty...really good.

-Milk shake: 5 stars. I would come back to Shake Shack for ice cream....but everything else kind of disappointed.

It was fun to eat there and everything was really clean. Also, everyone in line looked so happy and excited to be there, which was kind of funny, since most people waiting in line for something are miserable. 

I'm glad I went, but don't really feel the need to try it again, except for maybe another milkshake...

I wasn't too impressed with this chipotle. The burrito bowl was skimpy. They had a near empty peppers and onions container and tofu so they gave me the scraps that were left and no more. The guy in line after didnt get any peppers or onions  in his bowl. I should have listened to the other reviews.

The prices are a little higher than a normal burger joint, but this isn't a normal burger joint! The quality is great. The service is pretty quick. It's good for large groups. Outdoor seating is available and there are tons of bike racks outside, too! Street parking can be tough, but it's prime location makes it easy to walk there. The Philly themed desserts are also awesome. Definitely try this place out!

The worst. This location used to be really good. The staff was quick and friendly, but recently there have been some dramatic staff changes.  The new staff is not knowledgeable about the menu, they are beyond slow, and the machines for hot chocolate, ice cream, and milkshakes are always broken. I come here twice per month on average so for these machines to be broken ever single time I enter is unbelievable! Plus the wait time is horrendous. There can be 5 people in line (all ordering one item)and you will still wait 25 minutes to place an order. What makes it worse is that while you're waiting, management and workers will be talking and laughing behind the counter.

Please avoid this place if possible.

Everyone knows that Chick-Fil-A is awesome, so there's really no point in reviewing the food, but I'll do a quick review.  Their chicken is always juicy and flavorful, the fries are always screaming hot and salty, and their homemade diet lemonade is yummy (and made with Splenda so someone like me who can't have aspartame can actually have a diet drink!).  And the new ketchup packets that are good for dipping?  Genius!!  

So now to review this specific Chick-Fil-A.  It's in the gallery, which for me is always a "get in and get out as quick as possible" experience.  The employees at every place in the gallery are always so rude, EXCEPT at this Chick-Fil-A.  They are always so polite, they smile (a rarity in the food court), and always get my order right.  It actually makes the experience so much more pleasant.  

I really, really wanted to rate this Chick-Fil-A 5 stars, but I couldn't because I never want to eat there.  And it's not their fault, it's just their location in the gallery, which is always super crowded with people screaming at each other from one end of the food court to the other.  So when I go, I end up walking back to work and by the time I get there, the food needs to be reheated.  But even reheated, the food is excellent.

Shake Shack is overrated and having eaten here multiple times I have never understood the hype. I appreciate that their meat doesn't contain hormones and is generally more sustainable sourced than other chain burger joints and as a sugar lover I always appreciate a quick shake stop. My particular gripe with this Shake Shack is that the possible mix-ins for a concrete (their name for ice cream blended with other sweet things) are never listed anywhere. This means that you have to ask at the counter and hold up the whole line.
Just went there for a burrito and the employees were extremely polite and service was very fast. Awesome Taco Bell!

Shake Shack is great. I love their cheese fries and burgers. The meals are delicious and very filling. The taste is consistent as well, so I know what my food will taste like whenever I go. I usually order the double burger that has bacon on it. The bacon is always perfectly cooked (not under or over-cooked), which means a lot. The outdoor seating at this location is a great addition. Sometimes the line seems long, but it moves pretty quickly. Expect to wait about 10-15 minutes for your food (after ordering) if it's very busy. 

I gave it four stars because it's pretty pricey. Also, they're stingy with the cheese sauce for the French fries. Maybe the burger prices will go down if they get rid of those wasteful to-go trays they give out.

Trendy over tasty. Shake Shack is basically Johnny Rockets with modern decor and a lot of idiots willing to wait in a hour-long line for average food. Yes, it's new and cool and there's been plenty of hype, and don't get me wrong, I actually liked Shake Shack...but I just can't justify spending 15 bucks for a kiddie size shake, decent burger, and crappy fries.  

I came here with two friends on a rainy weeknight and the line had only about 8 people waiting. We ordered from friendly staff, had the luck of getting a table right away (warning: the seating area is very limited- be prepared to have people stare at you while foaming at the mouth over the prospect of claiming your table), and our food was ready in about 10 minutes.  

-SmokeShack Burger: nicely cooked, the meat was fine, they skimped on the bacon, the bread wasn't soggy despite the grease...and though I really liked the cherry pepper spread, there could have been more. The burger still lacked flavor or a wow factor. You'll finish it off thinking, "eh, it was good but nothing great."
-Fries: interesting cut, decent amount for the order, but they were ice cold.  
-Black and white shake: I really liked the shake, it was thick and had good flavor. Then I realized I paid $5.50 for all 4 ounces of it. 

Verdict: If you are drunk, hungry, and someone else is paying, this place would be spectacular.  If not and you haven't made it to Shake Shack yet, you aren't missing out.

I've loved Jimmy John's for years. A college staple in the midwest. 
Best bread on a sub ever and 49 cents for a loaf of day-old is still a great deal. The place can feel a little kitsch, but for me it's all about the food.

And they usually live up to their motto: "Subs so fast you'll freak." They can usually knock out a great sub in seconds. It makes going to Subway and Quiznos (ugh) feel like an eternity.
 
Remember to ask for mayo/mustard packets if you grab a barebones "Slim" sandwichFor a secret menu option, say "LBI" if you get a sub. And they have a frequent sub card (11th sub/club free).

A huge bonus for me is that they take credit cards and they deliver.

Being a loyal Shake Shack customer in nyc, it was a nice treat to have a location in Philly. Scored a no wait in line and got the smoke shack and custard. Great combo. Service is fast and the staff is always really nice and helpful. The staff does not mess around about cleanliness. My smoke shack was hot and juicy and my vanilla custard a nice compliment instead of the cheese fries which are also out of this world.

I went here for the first time today. 

The line was quick and during lunch time. I got the mac n cheese and broccoli cheddar soup. 

The mac n cheese was pretty okay....not the best....but okay...

The soup.....NEVER again. I had to take a few spoonfuls to really be sure....it tasted like the broccoli was never washed. There wasn't a cheddar flavor either. I had to toss out a soup that cost almost 8 dollars. I kept the bread bowl that I got cause I can't pass up sourdough bread and also I dip it into my mac n cheese. 

I may go back and try something else....but the soup was horrible. Too bad cause I work right around the corner. I will go across the street for the soup from now on.

Love this place I'm happy and full every time I heve my reg which is salad (love their home made salad dressing) salad with brown rice, Pico, corn, sour cream, cheese and more lettuce love it consistent and never fail me
