The chicken was a bit greasy, but it's fried chicken right?  It was also reeeeally hot.  Maybe we had to wait a little, but I'm glad to know that the chicken wasn't sitting under a heat lamp all day.  I will be using up all of those KFC coupons I got in the mail.

Certain people I know have been counting this down for months, and for once the opening was just as smoothly operated and worthwhile as you could imagine (take notes, Morgans Pier).

Despite the line throughout opening day the customer facing staff appeared upbeat and on the ball.  That counts for something.

And the food was spot-on as well.  Having been to locations in DC and NYC the food was just what you want from this place.  Juicy, simple burgers with crisp fries and locally inspired Concretes.

Didn't have beer or wine this time but it's nice that the option is there once I inevitably return.  Plus they say sidewalk seating is on the way.  Welcome to Philly, Shake Shack.

Lunch today, I had the BBLT -- a balsamic addition to the classic BLT. It was done subtly -- balsamic can really be a punch in the mouth, but this was perfect; it added a certain something to the sandwich. Very well done.

I also had the tortilla soup, which was delicious, except that the tortilla chips on it seemed a bit stale to me. I scooped them off and had the soup. 

The manager, Mike, was walking around making sure people got through the ordering process as expediently as possible, so after lunch I walked over to him and complimented the BBLT, and mentioned that the tortilla chips seemed a bit stale to me -- he was demonstrably grateful, shook my hand thanking me for letting him know, and then bustled off to check on the chips himself. 

Based on how eager he was to fix the problem, I would add a star rather than take one away for the soup. That's a manager that cares about his business -- well done, Mike!

So the first time eating at Chick-Fil-A was in philly and I was not disappointed.  They get 4 starts due to the speed my food came and it was made on the spot since I ordered it a little different.  I ate the waffle fries, mint oreo shake, chicken sandwich and a chicken sandwich on wheat with provolone.  That with honey for my fries and I was set. I actually got a free chicken sandwich since they gave me the wrong one to begin with so  that is a plus.

For fast food, the chicken was greasy or drench in oil and the wheat bun was good.  The service at this place was good and the staff was always smiling and this was in the middle of the week day.

I would have gave 5 stars Bc that disco chicken and add avocado is amazing. But the young blo cashier is so damn RUDE. GIRL QUIT IF U DONT LIKE UR JOB. she got mad Bc I ordered and the nice guy cashier was giving me my change and I asked to add avocado. She got mad saying next time it will be $1. I said take the dollar now. She said no (with all her attitude) he already closed the register. I wanted a brownie but didn't want to give them any more money Bc if her rude ass go to the one near Macy's the staff are much friendlier

The food was great and it's awesome that they are open so late on the weekends. The staff is very friendly and very helpful. I would recommend their spice end platter! Always my go to place on a Friday night.

SO surprised at the other comments and ratings!  I wasn't disappointed nor was I was super impressed.  The line didn't discourage us.  Took about a half hour in line to place our order and another 10 minutes to receive our food.  It was the second day open and 1pm when we got in line.  I was impressed.  The staff was definitely friendly and knowledgable and the 2 people that were working the crowd inside and outside were awesomely hospitiable.  
Even more important than the service is obviously the food.  Heres my honest opinion...
The price point was right on.  I was full and didn't feel ripped off.  The burger bun was too soft and cheap.  The standard burger doesn't come with onion and pickles. The 'special' sauce tasted more like pink mayo than anything.  The meat itself was juicy and kind of flavorful but the bun couldn't handle it and kind of desinegrated.

The fries aren't fresh cut and the soda machine is behind the counter so unless you ask for refills, you might not realize you can get them.

The hot dog with kraut, spicy tomato, onions was good.  I'm never really blown away by hot dogs unless they are dollar dogs at Citizens Bank Park, grilled at a backyard BBQ or at Lucky's Last Chance in Manayunk. 

I will go back to get a milk shake or a concrete and maybe try the grilled mushroom sandwich

My chicken with ramen was outstanding and left me totally stuffed. My friend got the Thai chicken (excellent!) and the squid (a little tough, but still tasty) and would also give this place 4 stars. We agreed there is not enough traffic in here for how good the food is. Cool vibe inside. Clean.

Had the shroom burger and it was good. Quite surprised that the cheese would ooze out with the first bite---quite a good surprise. Not a fan of burgers personally but it's pretty good. Only time will tell if i will crave it in the future. Also kind of pricy for the size of the burger...it's not THAT gourmet.

Great burgers!
Kinda pricey and there will be a line depending what time you go, but make sure you go.

Chipotle is my favorite "fast food" place as it's actually healthy (minus the sodium) and cheap. I always get the Steak brown rice bowl. Like other reviewers have pointed out, this location does tend to give you bigger servings than average so that's a plus for value. 

This location is next to the 12th St Gym, so you can expect to see a lot of good looking fit customers grabbing a bite after their workout. Good for people-watching if you're into that ;)

Just like the ones in NYC ... this Shake Shack shakes what its daddy gave it (Danny Meyer). 

Love the portabella burger ... can't get enough. 

Shakes/Custards are pretty good. 

GF had it for the first time and was impressed.

Stopped by on a Sunday around noon ... juuuust beat the rush. After us - the line was out the door. 

Perhaps it's because it is newly opened, but the employees were giving out drink samples to those waiting in line. A very nice touch.

This is a great place to go for a burger with friends. The food is good and is served quickly every time. The staff are always friendly and will walk around to make sure the customers are happy. They also have outdoor seating, which is perfect for the nice weather. It is worth all the hype!

Shake Shack shouldn't be in Philly.  I don't say that to be mean, but I say that because there are far better burger joints here that aren't the following: overcrowded, overpriced, and over-hyped.

I've been a few times with friends and I generally like the atmosphere.  SS really classes up that corner, but Village Whiskey across the street gets the award for best burger in Rittenhouse.

While the food is good, it sells burgers on its name.  Because of the fame of the NY locations, they came to Philly to get into the exploding food scene here.  It worked.  I, like many others, ran to their door and were hoping to be blow away be the promise of a toe-curling foodgasm.  Like many, I'm left wanting.

Don't get me wrong.  The food is good, but is easily forgettable.  The only thing I don't like on their menu is that mushroom burger.  The hot cheesy, creamy liquid that erupted from the volcano of a patty came with no warning and was not that appetizing.
Shake Shack is a guilty pleasure. You will wait a while in line and for your food but it's sooooo worth it. The shakes are overpriced for a small, though-- no matter how creative the flavors are.

I went here for a business lunch, well a little free time during the middle of the day. 
I walked from my meeting in center city to get to this place. 
I found the interior inviting and menu wall very clear. 

I was able to get an order in quickly. I'd say the woman taking the order could be more friendly. But, it is a small complaint. She took the order and got me to move on. 

I found a seat facing the street. And I love that because I like to people watch. 
Within several minutes my burger and chocolate shake were ready to go. 

I was not sure what to expect other than good shakes and a burger. 
I was pleasantly surprised by the burger. The star was the beef and the flavor of the beef came forward clearly. I think this is one of the best tasting burger's I have had. 
It is a little messy in appearance when I received it. A basic cheeseburger, but whatever spice they put on that is wonderful. And it was juicy. 
And on to the sip of the chocolate shake. Wow, that was clearly a chocolate shake. Rich chocolate flavor pops onto your tongue. Rich and strong like eating a chocolate bar. 

I enjoyed this place and will gladly return if I am in the area and want a burger.

OK... so I'm a bit late to the game here... but I'm skeptical when people rave about burger joints... becuase while they're great for carnivores, a veggie burger is a veggie burger is a veggie burger.  Or so I thought.  The only reason I'm adding to the clutter of reviews for this place is because I absolutly was blown away!!!

The boyfriend and I swung in on Sunday night around 6p.  I went for the portabella burger, fries, and a carmel shake.  The boyfriend must have been hungry.  He got the Shack Stack burger, the DogMeister, a black and white shake, and a coke... oh yeah... and those fries I ordered?  We split them!

I was blown away by my shroom burger.  The little fried sphere seemed questionable at first.  Why is a portabella so round?  Oh because they stuff it full of cheese and fry that too.  Case closed!  Yum.  I expected this thing to be an inferno, but it was pretty easy to eat, and i like how the bun has like... a back wall to it that keeps the sauce (oh the sauce... WOW!) from dripping and making a mess... and more importantly... it kept it in line to go into my mouth!  

I thought the fries were pretty good.  I like how the crinkle cut made extra surface area that I could put katchup on.  My boyfriend 'didn't like them' though he still managed to put down a pretty healthy amount of them.  I prefer Five Guys fries, but I'll eat these any time too.  

Next up was my shake.  I'm far from a connisour.  I think the last shake I had was a Shamrocker last March... and before that... the previous march... but with a name like Shake Shack... it's on!  The carmel was pretty amazing.  The consistency was perfect.  I hate when you can't get the shake through the straw... and they act like its a good thing.  So thick!  Well if I wanted a thick shake, I'd have asked for ice cream.  Shake Shack was perfect.  I had a sip of my boyfriends shake, and his wasn't quite as amazing.  He got a black and white shake, but it really just tasted like chocolate... like... strong chocolate... rather than the more subdued black and white shake taste.  This was coming from him.  I don't really know any better.  He seemed to enjoy both his burger and his dog though.

Bottom line- this place is phenomenal.  That burger has hung in my mind like the raincloud over the cartoon characters head.  I want more!!!  That being said, I think it's really great news that I live on the other side of the city!  For caloric purposes, I'd likely get the portabella next time, but skip the fries and share a shake... but I had to learn that for myself :-)

I always drive to the halal guys when I'm craving for this type of food, glad I found one in Philly that will take my cravings away :) It's not NYC cart food but it will do, a little pricey but it's good. Friendly service too

So I had to go visit this place as it receives so much hype from the one in New York! And if you're new to Shakeshack, after you order from the register, they give you a little plastic contraption that will light up when they're ready for you to pick up your food so you can seat yourself first instead of standing around waiting for your order. 

Of course, I had the Shack burger. (Being that it's their house burger... and one's house burger should definitely be telling of how good the rest of their food is in general.) It was delicious! The burger patty was juicy, the bread became very flavorful from soaking up the oil and meat juices, and that shack sauce really tasty and ties the taste all together. If I had to describe the shake sauce, it's kind of like their own special mix of mayo with a hint of savory sourness. It tastes good though, trust me. Although I wish the burger was a bit bigger given the price - it's about the same size as a McDonald's burger, except double/triple the price.

I also had a Black and White shake, since I just kind of had to try the shakes from a place called SHAKEshack. It was  a vanilla shake with fudge chunks blended into it. It tasted alright, but it was a little too sweet and way too thick for my liking. Probably wouldn't get a shake again if they're all the same consistency.

Lastly, I have to give an A+++ for their staff, they're definitely very nice and friendly despite the hustle and bustle of 30+ people in line. They also passed out little samples of smores ice cream while people waited in line as to lessen the long wait time impatience of customers. Was not needed, but definitely a very nice and tasty touch!

I'd definitely be up for returning to try more here with friends!

I visited Shake Shack today, having heard all the raves about the original in NYC. I was definitely not disappointed.

I went just before noon and there was hardly any line, although by the time I actually got my burger, the place had filled up. I ordered the SmokeShack burger. My first impression was that it looked awful small, but when I bit into it, it was pure deliciousness. The patty is so juicy, flavorful and delicious, the applewood-smoked bacon was to die for, and that Shack sauce is addictive. The pickled cherry peppers added a nice hint of acidity to complement the richness of the flavors.

It was small, but I felt perfectly satiated after eating it. Not overfull, but I wasn't hungry again for another five hours. I also had the Abita root beer, which I thought was extremely thirst-quenching and tasty. It was not overly sweet, either.

I didn't order fries. The lady at the counter tried to push them on me ("No fries?!") but I thought that sounded like too much food, and if I had room left over, which I didn't, I would have ducked into Capogiro across the street. When I saw other patrons' pitifully small and very Ore-Ida-looking crinkle fries, I was so glad I didn't waste money or calories on them. Shake Shack really needs to step up its fry game, that is just sad!!

All in all, I would definitely go back. No, it's no Village Whiskey, but it's definitely a solid entry in the category of moderately-priced burgers. I'd like to also echo others here in saying that the service is very friendly. Not so much at the counter, but there are staff in the dining room who greet you, offer to take your tray away, etc., and that is a super-nice touch!

Great hole-in- the-wall Indian Food. Is it quality Indian Cuisine? No. But if you're hankering for some quick Indian Food before you hit the bars, or want to indulge late at night, this place hits the spot. I'll definitely be returning.

The Spice End Platter is off the chain!

I got a message from their customer care and they invited me to stop by for a free shake. I told him that I moved to California and I didn't see myself going back to the East in the near future. So he asked me to share my address. I was happy cos at least they cared. 

A couple of days later, I got a gift card from Shake Shack: one free shake, valid only in Philadelphia, PA, expires in October. 

Well done, Shake Shack! If there were minus zero star, you deserve more than ten thousand. 

Original review: 
My boyfriend and I stopped by for late lunch on an early afternoon on Sunday. the line was insane. but we waited anyway. 

the burger was very very mediocre. the bun was dry and almost soaked in butter...village whiskey right across the street has way better things to offer. and on top of that, the woman who took my order got my name wrong. when my boyfriend's order was ready, the guy said his name wrong. 

best burger in town? who do u think ur kidding?!

Quit saying Shake Shack is east coast In-N-Out. Its not. There is no comparison. 

I am from the west coast where we love our In-N-Out, and when I moved out here there were people telling me, "you have to try shake shack, its our In-N-out." Nope, sorry. Not only does it not compare but in my book its not even good in a different way. Let me break it down west coast style:

I bought a burger, fries, med drink, and figured a shake too since they are the Shake Shack (caramel flavor). All total That cost me (1 person) over $17. Wow. Ok. 

So the first thing I try when I sit down are the fries. Meh. These fries were so bland and unimpressive I think Costco fries have them beat. Then I take a sip of the shake. MEH! Seriously? You are called Shake Shack and youre gonna give me a bland boring shake that tastes like nothing special? Wow. Im serious prob could have gone down the street to burger king and had better. The coke was a coke but small for being $5. Finally, the Burger was decent but in spite of being told by everybody how big it was I found it small and wimpy.

I will say one good thing here and its why I gave any stars at all. I did like the flavor of the burger. It had peppers on it which I liked. I had the Smoke Shack burger.

So in summary, if you're a west coaster and youre used to the mecca known as In-N-Out (which did live up to the hype for me, btw), then save your money if you come here, and just order a burger and a water. If I ever go back thats what I'm doing - I honestly would not even get fries and a shake there again even if they only cost $1!

I'm so happy there is finally Taiwanese fried chicken that I tried Cheers Cut and Chi Ken both in one day! 

I definitely preferred the taste of Chi Ken and its Bento box plating. The ground pork over the rice is delicious. The service was fairly quick. I wanted the ramen but they didn't have that yet. It seems like a couple of other menu items are not ready either. I do wish they could be a little more generous with the tasty side vegetables though. Can't wait to be back!

When they said the food would be ready in less than 5 minutes, they weren't kidding.   This is by no means "fast-food".   I ordered Chicken Teriyaki and Rice for $7.99 at lunch, and I was pleasantly surprised about the quality and quantity of food that I got.   This place is a gem and I'd highly recommend.

Drunk Indian food.

This place is for that niche clientele looking for Indian food post partying. It has all the go to staples with a no nonsense way of ordering and consuming. I visited the location towards Logan Square, but there's also a location on South Street. The access and hours are nice - within walking distance of the museum district, and open late for some good greasy nomming. 

Inside, there are small tables set up for indoor dining, and the process to order is fast casual, with register in the far right corner. It's fairly clean, but overall the decor is no frills - casual and minimalistic. Depending on when you go, the crowd in numbers is varied, usually late at night a more imbibed clientele are expected to make an entrance.

The menu is littered with kati rolls, biryani platters, paneer plates, chaat (of course), pav bhaji, etc. There are also specialty drinks (mango lassi is pretty decent!) Overall, hits all the cravings for Indian food - heavy on the stomach, light on the wallet. I found the service simple, though sometimes there's a language barrier, so just have to be careful when asking for changes to established menu items - the customization to the options may be limited. 

If I'm feeling the urge for Indian take out, this place always comes to mind. I wouldn't come here for a dine in experience, but the food is solid so would recommend for anyone looking to appease their Indian cravings.

Not bad. I absolutely love chiptole don't get me wrong but I don't know if it because it's in center city and I normally get it in the northeast but their portions were sooooo small.  I got barely any steak in my burrito and it was so tiny compared to my regular.  It was still pretty good.  This one's very crowded but I'm probably just not use to the lunch rush in the city lol

All sizzle, no steak. 

For as much hype this place gets, I was expecting at least one OMG this is good moment but came away with the feeling like I'll never get that 20 minutes of my life back. 

Forgetting the line and the staff who stand at the counter and just stare at you like they've just seen their first human instead of offering to assist--this burger and fry joint is as mediocre as they come. I get it. The raucous crowd, the party-like atmosphere, the PC we're greener than the other places hipster attitude is not worth overpaying for a grossly greasy burger unless you're wowing me with the seasoning and or prep and toppings. Zero out of three.  

You will not see me again.

My favorite sandwich/salad place by far. Everything is delicious and plant based. Service is fast and always great. I rotate between food options as I love everthing but I always get a side of sweet potato fries because they rule. Their condiments are also ridiculously good and vegan!!!!! Yay!

I got the double shake shack burger and cheese fries, and it was delicious. Definitely one of the better tasting burger joints. Only complaint is lack of seating and no place to refill your drinks. I would recommend going after the normal lunch time rush, I went at 1, to avoid the long lines.

Ordered the anchari rolls and chicken and lamb platter. The rolls were good. Moderately sized. It's basically a chicken wrap with just chicken, onions, and a green spread. Not exactly a robust wrap. The chicken reminded me of a tandoori chicken flavouring. It was ok. 

I did not like the chicken and lamb platter. It tasted and smelled like boiled ground meat. It didn't seem like it was marinated or flavored in anyway. I had to douse it with the white and red sauces to make it taste somewhat edible. I'm not sure if it was supposed to taste like that. The red sauce was good. It was spicy. 

The restaurant is small. Not many customers on a Sunday evening. Most people came in for to-go orders. Parking is street parking and generally bad in that area. 

I'm not sure how this place has such high ratings. The roll was ok and the chicken and lamb platter was just bad. If I needed a quick bite to eat and I was in the general area, I might come in for a roll.

They were challenged today by probably the largest crowd they've ever seen (Eagles Super Bowl Parade) and the staff at this Corner Bakery welcomed thousands of Eagles fans into their restaurant who needed to use the rest room and those of us who just wanted to stay warm. The panini's were pretty damned good too!!! The line moved fast and the food was hot. They were very well prepared for this massive crowd and went above and beyond with their hospitality!

Having dined here several times over the last few weeks, it is worth talking about the pluses and the minuses. Lines aside, the quality of the burger is good, though they are all cooked to the same temperature. The buns are potato but add nothing to the burger. The quality of the toppings is top notch. The smoke shack burger, a bacon cheese burger with a spicy sauce and hot peppers is a nice blend of heat and smoke. And you definitely only need to get the single patty. Not a fan of the drinks (lemonade or water).

The service here was great and the food was delicious! The line wasn't long and the wait time for the food was fast. Also, the dining area was very clean and the condiment section was neat and trash free. I highly recommend this place for a lunch date!

As a former New Yorker, I was happy to see the Shake Shack make its way to Philly. Of course, I have since quit meat and thought, I'll go get a shake and one of the shroom burgers.  One bite and I had to  toss it. Super deep fried & greasy, and when I bit Into it this hot as hell cheese liquid went all over. It really was unpleasant. Next time, I'll go over to Franklin Square Park (awesome veggie burger at the Starr stand).

Didn't know what to have for dinner so my friend and I decided to just have something close and opened late. We found Chi Ken on yelp and proceeded to walk there. It's only a 7 minute walk from our hotel Best Western Plus, so that's a plus. 

Walked inside, and there was only a table seated so we were able to seat ourselves. We weren't sure if you go up and order or they come to us; so we sat down at first, but after nobody moved, we went to the counter and ordered. I got the popcorn chicken bento (7$) & the oolong milk tea (3.50$). I read reviews saying the food may take a while to come out but ours came out real quick. Less than 10 minutes. 

The food itself wasn't the best, but it wasn't bad either, definitely not for the price. Chicken wasn't flavorful but it was nixe and crispy. The sausage didn't have flavor either. The best part was probably the pork on top of the rice. The tea was good though. Definitely worth every penny of my 3.50$. Customer service was not bad too. Didn't say much but he wasn't rude so that's all good.

After going to the one in New York City I looked up Shake shack in Philadelphia and bam we have 2 here I would of never known... Anyway I tried this one and it was even better than the one in NYC I got the smoked shack burger, fries and strawberry shake...I was so ready to eat I forgot to get a before pic but got one mid way through my meal...I had a big order which was done quickly my kids and hubby loved everything... it was fresh and delicious, no complaints here ...you won't be disappointed go head give it a try it's worth it...

So I have complained since moving from california 4+ years ago that Philly is severely lacking in Mexican, quality Thai, and real teriyaki. Not some half assed chicken and gross sauce on a bed of onions which is complete blasphemy to proper teriyaki. So I heard about this new spot and didn't realize teriyaki was such a thing in Seattle, but that was cool. Back home, ma and pa teriyaki spots are all through town and everyone has their fave. This place FINALLY brings proper teriyaki justice to Philly. I would normally go with classic chicken, but I was in a steak mood, so I ordered a steak bowl with extra meat, brown rice (I prefer it to white) and no potato salad. I have to admit that was one thing that threw me off. I'm used to bowls like this with maybe some grilled veggies/broccoli, but never had with potato salad (which I'm not a fan of), maybe it's a Seattle thing. The folks inside were SUPER friendly and the meal was ready quick. It was a warm, humid day, so i took it to go to eat in comfort of cool building. The steak was quality. Not sliced bits of mystery beef, but hearty, beefy steak with a bit of pink left in center, thankfully. The beef was well seasoned, not overly chewy/properly beefy, and the rice perfectly cooked. The bowls are topped with sesame seeds, scallions, and their teriyaki sauce which I will testify has the proper consistency and balance of sweet and salty/savory. They put some on the top and then provided a small container for to go order. While I appreciate that they avoided the sin of over saucing, the bowl needed more sauce, perhaps more on top or a larger than thimble to go container. Initially, I was skeptical of the portion size to value ratio. I ordered the most expensive bowl with extra meat since I missed breakfast. But in the end, I was stuffed and I was happy. I think part of it is a function of just city prices vs home prices and it makes sense. I want this place to succeed and continue because I enjoyed each bite and it brought some of the best coast finally to philly. I will be back to try the classic chicken. My only suggestions would be more sauce offered (may be as easy as asking for a second container) and possibly a grilled veggie side rather than potato salad or green salad substitution

This was my first ever time at a Shake Shack and more of a rushed decision as we were all starving and it was close by, but it did not disappoint. There was a little bit of a line, but compared to some of the other reviews, I guess we should consider ourselves lucky. I was waited on by a really nice older gentleman, who said my choice of the Smokeshack burger was a great choice and one of the best selling burgers so far (sure, he coulld have just been full of shit, too, but I think he was genuine). The burger came out within 5 mins of ordering and it was just what I needed! A little greasy, but I also don't mind that. Their was a ton of flavor and the bacon and toppings were all tasty. 

I wish the burger was a little bigger for the price, but I can't complain too much about it. I will certainly be back again, especially when I am looking for a smaller meal!

I'm not sure why it's called Shake Shack when the burger is the real reason to go. Must be the alliteration.

Don't get me wrong, the shake was okay. Super thick and creamy, like drinking solid ice cream through a straw. No wonder it looked kind of small, if it were any bigger people would suffer lactose-induced arterial embolisms here all the time. But toward the end of it (strawberry), it was getting too sweet and a little gag-inducing. Overall, it was a pretty standard (albeit thick) shake, so I'm not sure I would pay $5 for it again. 

On the other hand, the burger I will go back for, again and again. My first bite into this succulent burger was supremely satisfying, as was every single bite that followed. While first looking at it, the thought of getting ketchup flitted faintly across the back of my mind, but one taste of this burger told me ketchup would be wholly unnecessary. The meat was so moist and juicy, the lettuce and tomato crisp and fresh, the cheese and sauce melding this perfect amalgam of ingredients together on a light and fluffy yet appropriately chewy bun. The single burger, at $4.55, is a good size to leave you wanting just a little bit more and also not feeling fat. 

When taking price into account, I daresay that this burger almost rivals that of Village Whiskey (slightly less than half the price, but slightly better than half as good), which is good news for people who don't want to wait 3 hours for a seat across the street.
Get me the shack burgers on a platter and I'll be good to go! Everyone is so sweet and the atmosphere is good for just hanging out.

It has been about a year since I came to Shake Shack on Sansom.  I was so excited to have it again and wow was I disappointed.  Let's start with the fries- WHAT HAPPENED TO THE CRINKLE CUT FRIES?  Instead it was a container of soggy fries with no crisp at all.  This was my first disappointment and it was big as I loved the crinkle cut fries!  Next onto the Burger.  I had the Shack Burger.  I remember the burger being delicious with the perfect amount of sauce.  This time, the burger, lettuce and tomato were sloppily plopped onto the bun and there was on little dollop of sauce that barely coated the 1 cm location on the bun.  What a rip off!  The sauce is key to success.  After adding my own ketchup and rearranging my burger, lettuce and tomato onto the bun, I was able to eat this and it tasted fine, but was missing the sauce!  Next, the custard- here is where they really put me over the edge.  We were getting ice cream for 4 kids and these cones and cups were so sloppy they were dripping before they even brought them to me.  It was a mess and barely had any sprinkles on them.  For so much money, I would expect more sprinkles, and a more carefully crafted cone and cup of ice cream.  I do not get how they get away with slopping everything together.  This place is way over priced and has gone way downhill!  Go back to New York or clean up your act!
Awesome burgers! Customer care was amazing and  they have very friendly staff. Great experience.

Shake Shack a place to go to escape the doldrums of fast food. It's get pretty busy during rush hour but the line moves. They ambiance is very inviting and has outdoor seating. Music was just a little loud for my liking. Prices are a little steep for what you get. You get better quality $7-$9 for a burger. $5 for a hot dog and $5 for a shake. Alcohol is available which is always a plus. Shake taste great but still too steep for what you get $5. The staff were very friendly and professional. Only issue I had was after I left  they forgot to add my hot dog to my order after I already drove away.  I guess I can't escape the fast food doldrums after all.
Great location as well as the light cation at 38th and chestnut. Fresh food each time I visit.

Stopped by HipCityVeg for a quick snack, if a vegan philly sandwich qualifies as a snack... :)

That sandwich was INCREDIBLE! I use to love philly sandwiches when I still ate meat so I was intrigued about how the vegan version would be... Honestly, no need to eat meet AT ALL! My only comment would be regarding the ketchup. To me, the sandwich didn't need it. Anyway, still an excellent sandwich that I could have every day...!

Good enough burger, yummy fries, decent shake.  Honestly, just a little underwhelming for the money.  Burgers.org has a better burger for the money, if less of a sleek and new space.

Of course, if you want a Burger of Excellence, visit Village Whiskey, Sketch, or Grace Tavern.

Best Indian fast food in the city. They just introduced Pavbhaji and Vada Pav on the menu and they are amazing. Completely bombay style and delicious. Almost 3 years to this place and they have won the lunch/dinner/latenight fast food crowd in center city. This is our go to place in philly after night outs. They also opened up a food truck recently on Drexel campus in university city. Need to check it out soon.
I know people will probably disagree,but this place was okay and not as great as I thought it would be. For the price I feel like this place has nothing on in n out burger in California. Too pricey.

Fastest delivery ever 12 minutes from telephone order to delivery of sandwich in a building!  No delivery fee. Quality of ham was fine, very very thin slices of cheese (provolone) bread is mediocre not great hoagie bread but for $5 consider it ok.
Employee was very rude on the rude on the phone and hung up on me when I asked him a question. I will never go to this Burger  King !

There was a ton of hype surrounding Snap Kitchen's entrance into the Philadelphia market. There will be about a half dozen stores. 

I think there's one important thing that we all need to keep in mind when trying out Snap. The sell pre-made, take-out options. To quote my husband after the visit, it's like "glorified lean cuisine." 

I think if I had a better perspective of this going into my experience, I may have enjoyed it a little more. 

Don't get me wrong, the store was bright and clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. I was greeted promptly and asked if I had any questions, even before I had the time to think of any. 

I ordered the Chicken Butternut Squash Macaroni in medium, since they were out of smalls. It was good, don't get me wrong. However, based on the hype over Snap, I was expecting a gourmet orgasmic explosion in my mouth. It contained nice chunks of butternut squash, a healthy portion of ground chicken and just a dab too little of goat cheese. I had to mix everything together after microwaving it at home. The macaroni itself was just a little blah. Maybe it was healthy macaroni? 

I'm intrigued by the concept of Snap, but not quite sold yet. Between my macaroni and my husband's turkey meatloaf, we ran a tab just shy of $20. I feel we can get something comparable in both price, size and nutrition at Whole Foods. I'll try Snap again without a doubt, however I'll go in with the added perspective of a take-out meal versus gourmet experience.

Great place to get Indian food when you are on the run or you are looking for a quick takeout. I love their Biryani, Paneer achari roll and Mango lassi. I think they serve the best mayonnaise in town, freshly made every day and I like that their spicy red sauce does not have the strong acetic/vinegar taste to it. Friendly staff and quick service!
Great menu. Great cheseseburgers shakes fries! One of the best burger experiences I've had !

Hits the spot just right. Burgers are fresh, tender and tasty. Not small but not too big.

Four stars for the cashier's attitude.

With Village Whiskey sitting right across the street, there's always a tough burger decision to make when heading over this way. 

If you're looking for the lower price and quicker option, Shake Shack is for you. Delicious yet thin burgers. I think it's safe to go with a double even if you generally wouldn't order a double burger at another restaurant. 

Obviously the name eludes to their milkshakes and they are also pretty good. 

If you're not a milk shake person, they have a few decent local beers on tap as well. Generally always an option from Victory brewing. 

As for the space, it is a rather small building so the line can wrap all the way outside on busy days. It also gets a bit crowded near the counter where you pick up the food. 

Because of the size it's also tough to find seating when the place is busy. Fortunately Rittenhouse Square is right around the corner and is a very nice place to take your food to go.

Quick, easy lunch in no time at all.  You are in and out of this place in five minutes, and when you're running from a busy work place just to pick up lunch so you can run your a$$ back to that lunch place to get right back to work--this is a place you should go to.
The bread is pretty tasty, the staff is friendly, and the sandwiches are good.  I am partial to the 'Beach Club' sandwich, and have had a few BLT's as well.  
I'll def go back.

I give Shake Shack the A-Ok. The place got much hype while it was being built, based off the original in NYC. I would have to say that the burger was just - good. Not bad, but good. In a city with GREAT burgers, I wouldn't rush to come here again, but if I was in a  hurry and needed a quick meal and was walking around Rittenhouse, then I would stop here.

The fries were weak-sauce. I'm not a fan of crinkle-cut fries and find that places never make them quite crispy enough. What I did like about the place was that it was so clean and the service was stellar. A woman came by our table to ask if we needed napkins or anything else at least a few times - shocking for just a burger and fries joint. 

Supposedly the shakes are delicious - but I have a dairy allergy so I haven't tried them. If you're in the mood for an easy, fast and inexpensive meal near center city, stop by the Shake Shack.

Delicious!!! Affordable DELISH Indian downtown. So sad they don't deliver to Art Museum. But that just means I go get it. Big portions. Love the creamy white sauce I've never had with Indian before. I had the chef's specialty chicken platter & the chicken biryani. I've gone back for more chefs specialty just because I make good biranyi myself. & there's more meat in the other dish. Yumm-o.

This place lives up to its reputation. Me and my girlfriend both had the shack burger I had a double and she had a single. The entire burger was amazing. All fresh ingredients and the bus was softer than a baby's bottom and the burger was so juicy and you can tell it was made with no hormones or additives. All natural beef and extremely tasty. Also had the cheese fries with their own cheddar cheese which has a unique tastes, if you order I suggest you ask for extra cheese their a little skimpy on the cheese but so good. And I had the vanilla while my girlfriend had the strawberry shake and they're small but really good and worth the $5....I strongly recommend every burger lover to go check out the Shake Shack, I can't wait to go to New York and visit the original location.

Very rarely do I have poor service AND a poor meal, but this established accomplished both. Now let me start this by saying that I have Chipotle at 2 other locations which were actually really good. This place, however, needs some serious changes. First off, the people working there have no sense of customer service. They are rude, inconsiderate, and just sit behind the counter talking to each other instead of interacting with their guests (especially the tall black guy with earrings, if I took over this place he would be the first one I'd fire). Second, the food was just plain terrible. My steak was cold and the chicken my girlfriend got was burnt but also served cold. There are plenty of other fine options in the area so avoid this place at all costs!

Likely you've never heard of Chipotle, so thankfully I'm here to review it for you. Solid and quick food. Honestly I just wanted to review it because I am giving everything 5 stars and really wanted to give a place 4 stars and Chipotle seemed like the perfect choice for that.

It's about 50-50 everytime I go whether they charge me for a 3-pointer or not. Sometimes I engage with the cashiers about it and try to get the 3-pointer rate, but honestly I think it's not supposed to be a 3-pointer so I don't bother anymore. Instead I just hope to get lucky.

After visiting this chipotle I can understand why they've been making so many people so sick across the country

This is the third chipotle that I've eaten at in as many weeks

this one is dirty the staff at rather untrained they talked internally rather than serving customers 

and I could not believe that they did not have lettuce a five minute wait to get lettuce with a burrito bowl

I would walk down the street and eat anywhere but here

I've been to Snap every day for the past 3 days. While my debit card is hot from all the swiping it's been doing at Snap, my stomach is happy because I've been filling it with delicious Paleo delicacies. 

I eat a Paleo diet at home, so it's nice to have the same options when I don't have dinner leftovers for my lunch the next day. No more disgusting Wawa salads or unhealthy sandwiches for this girl when she's hangry! 

Is Snap the cheapest option for a grab-and-go lunch? No, but it's probably the healthiest, easiest and quickest, not the mention it's ridiculously delicious. I've had the meatballs, beef stroganoff and many of the breakfast items - all were packed with flavor and amazingly delish. My husband enjoyed some lamb lasagna and literally talked about how awesome it was all day. He doesn't even do that with my cooking!

The staff is very helpful and they have microwaves on premises if you need to eat in a rush. While I'd prefer to bake my meals (baking and microwave instructions are on all containers), that's not an option during my weekday lunch hour. Most meals are hot and ready in about 2 minutes!

Snap has a rewards program, which I'm sure I will reap the benefits of soon. For every dollar you spend, you get points. Once you reach 200 points, you get $10, which is equivalent to a free meal.

Thanks, Snap, for bringing your bad ass self to various parts of Philly. You were desperately needed.

This place needs to be shut down. I initally went in for an iced coffee and was rudely told they don't sell iced coffee, then was offered a sausage burrito,  as if they were similar products.  Then as I was leaving, I saw one of the workers in the kitchen drop a piece of food on the floor and casually pick it up to put on the sandwich he was making. 

Pretty sure you would be risking your life if you choose to eat here.

This is by far the worst McDonald's in the city. It is the only one I've been in that has armed security. There is a foul smell of urine and mop water, to go along with the flies. The service is awful, I had to wait 15 minutes for two cheeseburgers even though there were only two other people in the store who also placed small orders.
Avoid this McDonald's.
great burgers. all food is great quality. price isn't bad for how great they are. easily recommend!

I love a good burger and crinkle fries! The burger wasn't dried out like other places, and it wasn't too greasy either. The fries were crisp and still hot. 
     Service was atypical, there was a pretty long wait since its was pretty crowded. I'd love to visit again and try one of their milkshakes!

I love me some Popeyes. I love the chicken, biscuits, and mashed potatoes. It's all good to me. I usually spend about $30 for the family deal. A good quick solution for dinner.

One thing I need to say about this location is that it is unbelievably depressing. They really couldn't care less about the atmosphere of the place or decor. No frills here, folks. Just walk allll the way to the back to order your food, and if you choose to stay in (I would never!), there are a couple of seats for you. 

Service wise, I don't care and they don't care. They aren't overbearingly nice and they aren't surly. Don't be surprised for lack of eye contact. They just get their job done. I'm fine with that. I just want to get the hell out of there ASAP and they probably do, too.

The location is South Broad near Snyder and I don't normally have problems parking around here. You can park on the yellow median, on the east side of Broad, or on Snyder. It's also accessible by Septa via the C, 79, or the Orange line.
I love shake shack! The line was long but overall it took me about 30 minutes to wait in line and then wait for my food. but the food is soooooo good. totally worth it.
WOW! Coreanos burger is out of this world. Burgers in chinatown??? whaaaaa???!!! NAILED IT!

I've been to the original Shake Shack in New York and this one in Philly is definitely more grand, with indoor seating and stainless steel everything. I only went for the shakes this time around and we were lucky to go when there was no line. However, for 2 milkshakes, we still had to wait 10 minutes for them to get made. I think that's a little ridiculous for a restaurant who's namesake is milkshakes. The shakes were delicious and creamy but not too heavy that you got super full from drinking it. For some reason though, I think the shakes in Philly were a bit more watery than the shakes in New York.  I will go back for the burgers and update to see if they are just as good as the ones in New York.

3 tacos for $10. You can only choose 1 kind. Can not buy single tacos. How am I suppose to try different ones without ordering 3 of each?? Got the bulgogi tacos. I've had gazillions of tacos while living in Texas. Pro tip: use 2 tortillas or they will get too soggy and fall apart! So disappointed to see 1 tortilla to each taco. The bulgogi meat was bland. Didn't find the taco tasty or creative. Ate 1.5 tacos and threw out the other half bc it was so wet and not yummy. Had better $1 tacos. The owner should check out LA Burger and Chi'lantro for ideas on delicious Korean fusion tacos. 

Customer service was poor. I stood there waiting to be greeted right in front of the gal. The cook saw me and I said hi. The girl looked up and was unenthusiastic, no greet, no smile, and no bye. I had to do all of that! I was their only customer that time.

I think I am certainly one of the people that were expecting a lot from all of the hype around Shake Shack. Went for the first time today. Long lines and the place was jam packed for lunch. But, things did move pretty quickly and tables opened up pretty fast. The burger was decent. Nothing amazing, but it was a good quality burger. The fries were crispy with a good amount of salt (which I liked). I would probably come back here once in a while and might try a shake. But, I was expecting an amazing burger. I probably should have lowered my expectations a bit. It is glorified fast food after all.

I usually end up here after aimlessly walking around looking for something tasty and can't make up my mind. It's not bad really, but nothing to go out of your way for. I'm pretty disappointed by their soups overall. Their chicken pomodoro panini is good but I usually feel gross full after eating it, which is never fun at work. Dispite that, I somehow end up here once a month.

Really happy this place moved into the rittenhouse neighborhood. This place is a great alternative to grab a quick bite to eat. The teriyaki chicken is phenomenal. The price for the #1 (7.99) is the same price you'd see at fast food places, but this is a significantly better option. I work near by and will be coming on my lunch break often.
Lack luster spot, it's a fast casual burger but there are way better places to grab a burger at that price point in philly.

Paneer lovers rejoice!  

Spice End's aloo paneer kati roll packed some serious flavor.  Generous amounts of cheese and seasoned potatoes were spread evenly over the warm, chewy paratha & rolled up neatly into a dense little package.  The cooked onions and green sauce (chutney?) also added nice flavor. 

If you're like me and sriracha tastes like ketchup, then you'll have to try the big bottles of Spice End's hot red sauce.  This is what all hot sauces should be like - where heat takes precedence over salt.  

I cooled things down with a deliciously thick and rich mango lassi. With half a lassi & half a roll left over this $11 meal covered both lunch and dinner. 

*Special thanks to yelp & Spice End for a 10% off check in offer!

Delicious food and healthy after a great walk. Awesome awesome awesome yyyyyyyuuuuuuummmmmmtyyyyyyyh

Oh and healthy

Staff seems tense like a theatre company right before opening night.  . After waiting online like i was buying concert tickets old school style, ordering and then holding this electronic buzzer off to the side, I wonder if there should really be a buzzer in my hand and not something else of my own.    

Was the burger good?  Hell yeah.  Yet management should be more concerned about improving this timid staff on efficiency and less time turning burgers into celebrities and having people wait online like a club.  The word for today children is DINING IN!
Need more of these in the city. Love that they are open early. Friendly and efficient service.
Chicken dog is wonderful, the shakes are pretty good, and the service is super friendly and helpful. It doesn't hurt that they serve wine, too!
The Kati rolls taste good and are well priced. Unfortunately, I felt nauseous after eating here and have since heard friends with similar complaints.

Three stars for the mango Lassi, and I'll throw in another for the food!
I got the lunch special, which is a good value for the variety, but the portions were way too small by Philly standards. I had a side of flavored rice, and a kathi roll.
The Paneer kathi roll was definitely bursting with flavor, I enjoyed every morsel.
The biryani on the other hand just looked like rice with some food coloring.
Now the mango lassi is a whole other story. Thick, creamy, and not too sweet, this reminded me of the Lassi my mom used to make.. I go back here every time now, only to pick up my fix of Lassi!!

I like Shake Shack a lot. Especially nowadays that every burger you order in a restaurant is so thick you can barely put it in your mouth. Between my love of thin burgers and my hate of McD and the likes, Shake Shack is an excellent option. 

I'm giving it three stars because yesterday (11/2/2014) we went for lunch and the food was unreasonably greasy--buns, meat, fries, everything was dripping oil! By the time I sat down with my tray the white paper wrap was transparent from having soaked so much oil. 

I should have returned my oily burger and fries but I was in a rush. I just can't get over the oily bun.... it had never happened before, I hope it was a one-time mistake...

Don't deny it. You salivate at the thought of the warm waffle fries, the crispy chicken sandwhich, the cold tea... you're drooling right now. Or is that me? 

Either way, this place is off the charts amazing. I'm a southerner and I'm tired of crappy sweet tea! Chick fil a is my go to for the real thing. Sweet, cold, and refreshing. Did I mention free refills? Cause they got em! 

It's about 6 to 7 bucks for some fries, sandwhich, and a bigbutt tea. Is it worth it? Heck yeah. Don't you dare go anywhere else! Except on Sunday. Then I'll let it slide. I appreciate that they do that though, it's keeping with their beliefs and traditions of the south. I dig it.

The only thing that gets me is it ain't open late in Liberty. Why do they let me down like that? It makes me tear up just thinkin' about it. (The one out by IKEA is I think. )
The Paneer tikka was amazing, probably one of the best paneer Kati rolls I've ever had.

I work nearby, so I hit up the place about once a week, maybe twice.  While the prices are higher than other Wendy's restaurants, I have found that the employees seem to be a lot friendlier than just about any other Wendy's restaurant I've been to, my order is delivered fast, and they have yet to screw up my order.  (See my review about the Upper Darby location.)  The higher prices are attributed to the location (inside 30th Street train station); however, there are other chain vendors with prices matching locations outside the train station, including Dunkin Donuts & Subway.  For example, I've seen $1.29 items at other Wendy's locations marked up to $1.69 at this location.  Dunkin Donuts and Subway do not mark up their menu items and are open later.  This location loses stars for their high prices, but keeps a few stars for their friendliness, efficiency, and accuracy.

After trying Shake Shack a few times, I am still not sure what all the craze is about. I think the burgers are good but they are really, really small. I would need to order two burgers to make it a meal and they are $5 each. The fries are just OK too, nothing special, and they are an extra $3. What keeps me coming back are the Concretes. A Concrete is blended frozen custard with mix-ins. With the exception of my last visit, every Concrete I've had has been really good. They offer a Special Concrete each day of the week and change it up quite a bit.  I really like the truffle cookie dough mix-in and usually stick with it unless I'm feeling more adventurous. I recommend checking out this place but don't expect to be blown away by the food. Also, it's pretty cool inside and they serve beer too.

Anyone who would not give this place 5 stars is just jealous they cannot make such an outstanding burger at home. My go to is the Shack Burger, but I've also enjoyed their out-of-this-world chicken sandwich. Seriously, this place gets it RIGHT. If there is not enough shack sauce on your burger, go up to the counter and ask for a side. They are so accommodating to requests and literally the most badass chain I've ever been to. Their cheese fries were created by the gods themselves. Sometimes this particular location you can tell the oil has been reused a few times but I DON'T EVEN CARE because Jesus himself made that cheese sauce. 

Also, one time for my boyfriend's birthday, we both got free beers and a free custard. I mean - come on people !! This place is where it's at for fast casual delicious burgers and the usual American fare. Even have some decent hotdogs and custard. (How can one establishment be so perfect at so may things?)

Got the bulgogi tacos. They were really expensive and just not good. Bulgogi just doesn't go in a taco, especially with the tasteless dress listless toppings they put on the taco, it's just not tasty. The only slightly redeeming aspect was the tortillas themselves seemed freshly made and were tasty.

I like hanging at the Corner Bakery. It is definitely one of my hangouts in the city when I get there an hour before I'm supposed to be at work. There is a ton of a room to grab a coffee, sit and read- unlike certain other coffeehouses in the city that have just enough room to get your coffee and leave in the morning.

The wi-fi was very slow for me, I'm not sure if that was just my experience or universally, though. The food I've had so far hasn't been incredible and the coffee leaves a lot to be desired. The atmosphere is what brings me back.
Shake was pretty good but the burger got saltier with every bite.

Stopped in here a few times. Probably won't return, but you never know.  I think they lure me in with the beer.  The burger itself is kind of boring.  The meat tastes bland, as well as the cheese, and I'd like more choices in toppings.  Roll looks like a Martin's Potato Roll, which is a plus; but not enough to save this one.  

The crinkle cut fries are also pretty bland and boring.  They look like they work well with their cheese sauce, but I'm not a fan of cheese fries.  They seem almost identical to satisfries at BK to me, and I haven't heard anyone screaming from the top of the hills about satisfries. 

Staring out the window at Village Whiskey, you also kind of feel silly chewing on this burger.  It's supposed to be a step above fast food joints, but it only is in price.  There are plenty of better options around for a fast food burger: Square Burger, 500 Degrees, Smashburger, Five Guys, etc.  That's just off the top of my head.  This place is a let down.

Came to this place two times already and this will be the first writing the review for two events that will be combined into one review because there was no drastic change in ratings.

Usually I always come to this place before work because the meals always fill you up.

First time, I did not know what to order so I asked the employee... to put together anything as long as it is not spicy. And dang... she delivered. Whatever she put on it tasted great. Their beef is the best beef I have ever tasted in my ENTIRE LIFE so far. It's cooked just right and it's so flavorful when you bite into it. (picture of it will be located below)

Second time, I ordered chips with guac and grilled tomatoes and green sauce(not sure the name, sorry). They put a great amount of chips in the box and the guac is definitely a must try... amazing and fresh.

If you are looking for a place for Taco Tuesday or just a place with good food in general, I highly recommend this place. Great customer service and amazing food!!

Review for their tacos will be coming soon!

Wanted to check out what all the rave was about on the east coast with Shake Shack, so we definitely had to fit a meal in here. I got the special bacon cheddar and fries. I really enjoyed the bun....I think it is potato bread. :)
This location was nice because it is right in the city and there is a parking lot right across the street.
You have to check this place out. Surprisingly good food. Leaves you wanting more. I'll be back soon to further explore their Menu.

Met a friend in Philly en route to New York and needed to grab some food at the transit station. We enjoyed splitting a sub, which was definitely bigger than a Subway footlong. The guy at the counter was friendly, and he sliced the meat right there, which was nice to see. Sandwich was good - nothing amazing, but it was good.

Cute "market" atmosphere. We came for Taco Tuesday so the prices were great ($2) but otherwise it's $3 each. The girls at the counter was adorable and friendly. The kissing star is because we were not super empresses with *all* the tacos. The pastor and bulgogi were really good! However, we got beef, double fried chicken and carnitas and none of them were good. We were all excited for the double friend chicken fir some reason, but it was dry and meatless tasting. The guacamole was great :) moral of the story, stick to the two good meats and it's a great place.

I was born and raised in SoCal on In-N-Out burgers. I heard that Shake Shack is the East Coast equivalent, so I was pretty excited to try it. My friend and I ordered the Shackburger, fries, and a vanilla shake. The burger was okay. The bread was very smushed and it was not well-toasted. The meat was good, but it did not seem to have enough lettuce and tomatoes in it for me. The vanilla shake was more liquidy than other shakes I have had, so it was more like melted ice cream than an actual shake. The fries were delicious though. It is the crinkly type. Usually, these type seem to be soggy to me. However, these were crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Perfect fries. Overall, I would pass on the burger and shakes and come only for the fries.

Thank you Snap Kitchen for coming to Philly! Snap Kitchen is perfect if you want to eat healthy, loose weight and save time. Since the meals healthy you can't try it out with having really high expectations for the taste. However, the meals taste great if your goal is to eat healthy and loose weight. I used to meal prep myself but between the time it took me to food shop, cook, clean, and the cost, it made more sense to buy meals from Snap Kitchen. For the past month I've been getting most of my lunches & dinners here. I can already tell the difference in how I look and feel. My favorite meals are the coconut shrimp, vegetable lasagne & chicken teriyaki. I hope to see new meals added or have a rotation of featured meals. Also, you get 10% off if you belong to the Bellevue Sporting Club!

I was born and raised in North Jersey and recently relocated down to South Jersey. First that thing I had to do was find a place to get Halal food. I found this place through a Google search and decided to try it since it would be crazy and impossible to get my regular Halal food in New York ( Ultimate Favorite! ).. Anyways, the space is small but just right and it looked clean I guess so I went ahead and ordered the lamb and chicken over rice. The first time eating here was pretty good actually.. Only thing I did not like was that it wasn't as hot as food should be if it had been just made, but I ignored it. Second time around was about a week ago and I placed a pickup. Something seemed off to me, the whole atmosphere was not the same but again I ignored this also. The food again wasn't as hot I would have liked it to be but it was still average. On the other hand, my boyfriend ordered the lamb over rice and was fine until about 20 minutes later. He started feeling so sick, nauseous, and you can only imagine what else. Now I am not sure if it was because of the food so Don't quote me, yet what else was I supposed to think if he was perfectly fine before he ate here. It left me a bit concerned and after getting the weird vibes the times I have gone, I am not sure if I will be going back anytime soon..

This is an amazing burger place. For a quick meal in the center of it all in downtown Philly, this is the perfect place to go to. The burgers are so yummy, although I think you need 2 to be full. They make them quick, there is seating inside and outside which accommodates your mood. I've had better burgers but I can't complain about this. The meat is well done and tastes great. Their French fries are also amazing. I haven't tried anything past those two, but I wouldn't be afraid to give them a try because their food is good quality. I technically give them 4.5/5 just because for the price of the burgers and French fries I would expect to be fuller, not ordering a second round of burgers

People were waiting in huge lines this summer for this?! It's a slightly better fast food burger. Plain bun, pretty greasy meat. The fries are dry and lacking. If you want a GREAT burger, wander a few blocks to Good Dog. You can also do better at nearby Devil's Alley and Bobby's Burger Palace in West Philly.

Shake Shack is the closest thing to In-N-Out there is on the East Coast (sorry Five Guys fans). It's simple- their burgers just taste better, their shakes are tastier, and their service is significantly better as well. 

I've been here twice in the last two months, and both times I've been impressed. Although I've had Shake Shack before New York, Istanbul, and Dubai, I'm still constantly surprised at how tasty the burgers are. Usually, I get sick of fast food pretty quickly, but they have JUST enough diversity on the menu to allow you to not get too sick of eating the same thing. Besides, apparently each spot has its own special flavored shake (Philly's is Rittenhouse ^2).

Most recently, I got the Smokeshack and a small order of fries to go. Their fries are crisp and seasoned well- so much so that I couldn't even wait to eat them, I just polished them off as I walked home. The burger I didn't eat for a good 40 minutes after I ordered it (rookie mistake), but it was still delicious.

Also, the person at the register was very patient and helpful, and actually smiled while taking my order (which is more than can be said for Five Guys). Even this small detail improved my experience!

The only complaint I have is that the to-go orders don't have the burgers completely covered. Just like In-N-Out, the burgers are served in a cardboard box, but the tops of the burgers aren't covered, so they get cold more easily. But like I said, the burger was good even when 40 minutes afterwards, so it's not a real complaint, more of a comment.

Overall, their burger was a 5, fries were a 5, and the service was a 5 as well. This is the first place that comes to mind when craving burgers.
This place is a dump and I wish they would close it down and build something that properly represents the neighborhood.

After much convincing (read: nagging) from my fiancee I finally gave in and decided to try Shake Shack last weekend. From the beginning let me be honest with you all, I LOVE burgers, and even the word "love" might be an understatement, so keep that in mind while reading this review. With that being said, I found the burger at Shake Shack (ShackBurger) to be small for the price, a bit under seasoned, and having a bit too many vegetables compared to the meat. While it was very tasty, it was hardly anything to write home about, and it's definitely not worth a 90 minute line (as can happen during the lunch hour), or the price. I've seen a lot of people on Yelp hating on the fries, and while they are undoubtedly of the frozen bag variety, they are still good (with the cheese sauce they are delicious).

Surprisingly the favorite part of my meal was the hot dog (don't judge my gluttony), which was cooked to perfection on the griddle. Split down the middle, cooked to the point where it wasn't too crisp nor too soft, and placed in a delicious soft bun, it truly is the best "dog" I've ever had in Philadelphia. My dining partner got two dogs with peppers and onions and despite being full actually ordered another one for the walk to the bar (please don't judge him either).

Long story short, you have to try this place at least once. While it may not be like the Shack in Manhattan it is still pretty good (albeit pricey), and if they continue to improve I'm sure they'll become a fixture of the Philadelphia food scene.
Finally! Best teriyaki in philly as far as I can tell. I've been there twice so far and the food is fresh and spot on. The 2 guys working there are super friendly. Will come back for sure.

I don't really like hamburgers too much unless I'm in the mood. I hate cheese and I hate shakes...or at least I thought I did until I came to this place. I came here to meet a date and a few of his friends. We basically ordered everything on the menu...lol. Most of the burgers were good though a bit too much cheese. I didn't like the shroom burger too much. I got a fair trade shake(coffee). I was expecting the worst but it was pretty effin good. I will definitely come back to this place when I'm in the area
this place is bullshit. the food tasted like shit and expensive. i dont understand how people like it. i dont trust yelp reviews anymore.

Very good burger and, although it's small, it's much cheaper than a bigger burger at Bobby's Burger Palace, for example.  You may want to order two if you have a big appetite.  Fries were average.  The most disappointing part of the meal was the chocolate shake.  Completely unremarkable.  I expected a lot more from a place that actually features the product in their name.  

The restaurant was crowded when we went and there was a line to order, but they do a good job of keeping it moving.  Staff was friendly.  

I'd go back if I was in the area running errands, but wouldn't go out of my way to return.
I grew up at The jersey shore and Jersey Mikes was a staple!! So glad they are in Philadelphia and I can get some of the comforts of home!! Always fresh and always awesome!!!

Whatever-- I'm getting cheese fries.


AND THEY WERE SO GOOD. But for real, wish they had more vegetarian options. The only real vegetarian option as far as burgers go is a mushroom burger, so I got that. It was a lil small (so my fat*** got 2), but still crispy and delicious. Oh, and they have outdoor seating!

Sad day - I have been raving about the shack since the weekend it opened.  We waited 65 minutes for burgers before the sidewalk cafe was open and were waiting in front of the pizza joint.  I said it that day, that it was my favorite everyday burger place...and I even went back to grace and the oyster bar to make sure I wasn't giving it an extra 'new' bias.  My decision was confirmed twice, and I had been happily returning weekly to every other week - with the same consistent result...double shakeburger, cheese fries, and a shakemeister.  I went off-script one time and tried the smoke shack and the shack-cago dog - both of which were tasty, but no match for the shakeburger's balanced deliciousness.  My favorite things about their burger are the meat (it's perfectly seasoned and cooked to just the right temp for a burger joint like this) and then the bun.  The soft moist bun is perfect and the part that I think makes it even better is the fact that they aren't completely separated...this gives you a vessel to soak up all the juices and then decide at the end to play it healthy and toss the drenched nub...or go ahead and indulge and dominate that last bite (ps - I always choose to dominate it...sorry arteries)

We went back last week and, while the line only took 2 minutes - the result was a sad disappointment...my TWO favorite parts were missing...the meat was somehow under-seasoned, closely overdone, and my bun was separated!  Yikes!  And the problems compounded - the fact that the bun was separated caused other structural issues - so my burger ended up being all over the place.

I will certainly re-visit to see if it was a one time thing, but if anyone is listening - get back to what you were doing so well (and consistently) please!!!

I guess that the food is good there but I had hair I my food so that destroyed my appetite. We had to wait for a while to get our coffee so we had nothing to drink to our bagels. I might give them another try.

I've had the spicy chicken and garlic one too. It's pretty good but the wait times are ridiculous because they have one person in the front and back. The passion fruit fizzy drink was good but mildly warm each of the two times I got it. Would I get it again, probably not. For the amount of money spent I'd rather eat at bon chon

Been here twice gotten the same this fries and the shroom burger.  Very disappointed with this place! 
I'm a vegetarian and I've tried a lot of veggies burgers in the past.  This one is 6.25 ish for a rather tiny fried ball of grease on a soggy potato bun. When I bit into the grease ball my mouth was scaled with liquid gross cheese. The fries look like they came from sysco frozen and refried.  I only got half through my meal before I was grossed out and left.  For a dollar more I could of gone to hip city and gotten a burger that tastes good and is adult portioned.
Great food and nice people but these folks could stand to tighten up their operation a bit. Often slow and a little too dramatic. Lol

Came here with family while visiting sister-in-law for the weekend. They confused my husband's hot dog order and gave him a burger instead. Minor mistake but Derek, the manager apologized and fixed the order and let my husband keep the burger. 

Derek also generously treated our family to all 3 concretes! SO delicious! My favorite was the Liberty Bell concrete with cannoli shells and ricotta, but the Rittenhouse and Center City Pretzel were delicious too. We are from Austin and Derek printed out the recently-opened Austin location menu and gave us a discount card so we could check out the place at home. He also gave me some ricotta to take home since I was sad I couldn't get the same in Austin. Derek was such a nice guy and really made our first Shake Shack experience great. We will definitely be back! Thanks Derek!

I work very close to Snap Kitchen and I so wish I liked it more.  It is so hard to find gluten free food when eating out, and I love that almost everything at Snap Kitchen is gluten free.  But the problem is that it is so expensive!  Basically you are paying for extremely pricey lean cuisines.  I got the watermelon salad but it was nothing really exceptional.  I think this is a cool idea but it's just way too expensive.

I am practically in a coma writing this review because I went ALL OUT here. A few co-workers and I took an 11:30 lunch thinking we were going to beat the 12:00 lunch rush but to our dismay, the line was out the door.   After 40 minutes in line, we finally got to the front.
I ordered the Shackburger, Fries and Cholcolate Milkshake. YUM

The burger was really good and the potato buns they came on were a nice addition.  

The crinkle cut fries were yummy and the milkshake was rich and divine. Really though, how can anyone screw up a milkshake?
The staff was really nice, the food ready quick, and it was delicious.  I got the #1 boneless chicken teriyaki to go, and I would definitely go back!

Beef burgers are yummy burgers, just fyi :P 

Philly Shack attack (finally)!  KISS: Keep It Simple, Stupid.  Had a Shackburger single with crinkled fries and a black and white shake :P  Om nom nom, the combination couldn't have been better (but maybe curly fries instead?  -- poke poke -- ) :-) If you had breakfast before having this shacktacular lunch, you'd probably be in trouble, because how would you be able to have all of the components of the meal?

Next time - custard?  Mm mm :P

Spice end has great kati rolls for relatively inexpensive prices ($5.95).  You absolutely have to get the white sauce on the roll, and if you dine in they'll give you an endless supply of white and hot sauces.

I have to say the Shake Shack's reputation had me intrigued to try the menu, well to say i was slightly disappointed would be an understatement.  If you're looking for a burger to be cooked to order, not here, asked for a burger without cherry peppers, when i got my burger it seemed like I must have said extra cherry peppers,  they were falling off the meat, it took me forever to to get all the peppers off.  For what they charge, the size of the shakes and amount of fries you get should be criminal.  I mean an order of cheese fries was like 7 fries, the shake was what i would  consider a small.  In my opinion there are much better burger places to frequent.

Sometimes my room mate and I would go to the Jimmy John's on 17th off of Chestnut but we stopped going after the veggies (esp. the tomatoes seemed to be less then fresh). But my bf worked shortly at another Jimmy Johns so we decided to grab a quick sandwich at this location. I got my usual, the beach club and he got the vito, which i believe is something akin to an italian hoagie. Several things are lacking, first of all, the place was packed with employees, maybe 6 to 8 behind the small counter, standing there watching us eat, a bit overkill (maybe they expected a rush?), and second they don't have sweet peppers, which is my favorite addition to an italian hoagie. I'd go back when I need a quick sandwich, but it's not my first choice.

Yes, it's soo conveniently placed, and yes, the options are plentiful, but I really hate [this] Corner Bakery.

Pastas and sandwiches have huge caloric counts, so I usually settle on a salad if I'm forced to eat here. The salads always (seriously always) make my stomach hurt about 15 minutes later. Something about it does not sit well.

Let's be real though, the sub-par salads are not what motivated me to write this review. The service is. This is the type of place where you can/will stand at the line for about 4.5 minutes before anyone asking you if you'd like to order. You can even say "excuse me... is this line open...?" and you will be told to wait. This is extremely frustrating, given the fact that most people here from 12pm-3pm are here on a time-limited lunch break. 

The physical dining room is spacious... that's about the only compliment I've got.

Amazing! Was hesitant to try a sub from a place in not familiar with. Stopped in and had one of the best Italian subs I've had in a very long time. Fresh bread and sliced to order subs. Don't miss this place on your way through worth the entire trip for one of their famous subs!!
I love the Shake Shack and it is my new favorite spot in Center City, Strawberry!!!!

Do not order your food online for pick-up here!!! We had a group of 6, placed an order for pick up, arrived at the location for the appropriate time listed on the verification email and continued to wait 30mins+ for our order! It was a massive waste of time- especially for a 1 hour allotted lunch break. Also when I finally got my order & went to eat it- it was wrong... Such a disappointment. Will never order lunch here again.

This is probably the worst indian food at philly. the chicken biryani with no taste and no salt to taste, with the chef expecting customers to eat lettuce along with its stem. Vada pav soggy with oil. Not recommended for people to eat here except if they have really no option!!!!!

So good! The food truck is located right outside of my office which is a plus. Tons of food for only $10. Usually lasts me two days. The staff is really friendly and willing to answer questions despite being busy.

I'd rather have potbelly...

But oh well yet another chipotle. I mean some days I'll be in the mood for it I guess, it's a little better than qdoba, but less options, but it's further away...

So hard to make a decision between the two.

Burritos are alright, I mean what do you expect from a fast food joint with the typical "mexican" ingredients in little containers being plopped down on a tortilla.
The barbacoa is a nice thought, but it's really not that flavorful.

Best burger I have ever had. Hands down. Amazing. And on top of it the customer service is great! I think eating another burger now would feel like cheating. The only thing bad about this place is it's not across the street from me.

Every bit as solid as the ones in NYC minus the lines. The service here is also really great - they will walk around and make sure you're doing okay. The last time I was here, I showed up 10 minutes before closing. No attitude! Kudos to the folks that work here. Highly recommend.

If you want a traditional burger and some cheese fries... this is the place to go. Their mushroom veggie burger is pretty good, but very messy. The prices are a little to high though... thus the 3 start rating. The food comes out pretty fast, so I like to eat here when I am on the run and around that area.

Potential Energy (n.) - The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position relative to others.

Shake Shack, by virtue of its location and fare, could be one of my favorite spots in Philly. As it is now, it will be a place to go for a milkshake or concrete, but not for dinner.
