I ordered a bacon cheeseburger and was sorely disappointed to find that I had spent $7 on the same size patty and the same quality bacon served on the Jr. Bacon Cheeseburger at Wendy's. The fact is, if you're going to charge that kind of money for a burger at a self-titled "fast food" restaurant, it better be a large patty and cooked bacon. Down the street at 500 degrees, I hear they serve large, mouthwatering burgers for around the same price. 

I agree with the other reviews regarding the desserts. The milkshake was delightful, and I will certainly return for a concrete or two (don't look at me that way!). In all seriousness, it's a cool spot right near Rittenhouse with a really easygoing feng shui. All the same, I don't think I'll be going back for an overpriced burger any time soon. I would recommend taking friends along for a shake, or maybe for a large order of fries. I saw several people with bottles of wine, so it may be a BYOB (though maybe they were just taking matters into their own hands). 

In the meantime, if Shake Shack decides to increase their burger size, someone hit me up because I'll go back in a heartbeat.

the place is one of the better burger joints in philly. on nice days, there are huge lines. at times u might have to wait 20 minutes or more to get your food. my favorite selection is the shack stack, milkshakes are good too. you'll be lucky to get a seat (if not you could just take it to go to the park)

The veggie burrito bowls are phenom! I usually go here because of the relatively little wait time. The staff actually pay attention to what I want rather than mess up the order as has been my past experience in the other Chipotle Restaurants in Philly. A must-eat place in the city!

Love Shake Shack! My wife and I were looking for an affordable date and went here. For 38$ we each got a sandwich, fries, an ice cream item, and I got a beer. 

I got the chicken sandwich just to try it, but I still think the burgers are the way to go here. Fries are excellent and I liked the Rittenhouse concrete. Also appreciate how they incorporate the local culture/businesses in their concretes.

I still think Chick Fil A has the better chicken sandwich, maybe just because they have Chick Fil A sauce. But this one was a worthy competitor. Better than the federal donuts fried chicken sandwich IMO
I love the food they have. They are very appealing they have a great staff. He food was so great that it made my hunger very full I love it so much. Great place to hang with friends and family

The burgers are pretty good. I just wish that they didn't charge extra for every little thing I always get the Shack Burger, which gives off a little bit of everything. The vanilla shake is also  worth trying.

SHake shack is good for what it is - an affordable but hearty burger joint. I usually just get a cheeseburger which always hits the spot.  Milkshakes at good too, but they will run you $5 - a little more than I'm usually looking to spend.  Overall, though, the quality of the burgers is what keeps me coming back

Haha it's a McDonald's? It has free wifi, which should be a public service provided by the government. Thanks America for leaving that up to a fast food restaurant. 

Anyway, it's a funny McDonald's. Like any other mcdonalds except more hectic.

Came here just the other night around 10 towards closing (11pm) after hearing all about the hype and how good it is in NYC. My friend who is a hamburger buff thought it wasn't that great and what we ordered didn't even look that good. The kitchen was a complete mess as I saw staff making our shakes and 'concretes' desserts with pained faces, sloppily mixing the dessert I ordered into a goobly mess. The custard was melted and was all over the exterior of the cup. For the money I was paying and the menu description I was reading, I expected a better presentation. A $1 ice cream cone from a truck would have been better! The place looks nice and inviting for groups but I expect an improvement of quality and cleanliness in the food they are serving. And to the management/staff: don't just throw the food together!

OPENING ON MONDAY NOVEMBER 19th 2012


Jersey Mikes is coming to Amtrak 30th Street Station.....near Drexel, U Penn.....saw them doing a trial run with select customers this weekend (Nov 16 thru 19th).....i hear they are sampling food (FREE).

Have tried their cheesesteaks and deli type subs.....both are YUM......the deli subs are unbelievable for a fast food type place.  They slice fresh cuts right in front of you and build your fresh sandwich just like an old fashioned NY deli.

They will also be located right next to a brand new WENDYS HAMBURGERS.......i can see it now.....a Jersey Mikes Sub coupled with a FROSTY from WENDYS !!!!

Can't wait for this great addition to Train Station food choices.

Joe C.

I've been to this McDonald's.
The Big Macs taste the same as any other McDonald's.
The fries are a little bit better though.
Oh, and BTW no ODB.

This burger tasted like McDonalds to me honestly, if not less tasty. Fries were cold and disappointing. I could not even taste the patty, it was gone in 2 minutes, and I felt pretty gross and sick afterwards. I guess its the name, not the burger...will not go back or recommend. I would eat at 500 Degrees on 15th and Sansom with my eyes closed any day, nothing beats theirs, same price if not less. Might I add my sister and 2 other friends got sick from Shake Shack.
I absolutely loved this place. Great serves. My Girlfriend and I shared the Lamb Platter it was a great size.

i love chipotle and this location is very small. i kinda like it because at the times i go, it isnt very crowded. the food was great as always, but the customer service is something that has to be worked on for some employees. the music was too loud in there, so the employee and i had to scream at each other to make my order. the person running the register seemed like she just wanted to go home, she kinda gave me that mcdonalds employee customer service. besides the customer service for a few people, the location is great!

Disclaimer: I'm brown and have had and loved the original kati rolls in a shop called Nizam's in Kolkata, India. With that in mind, I ordered my kati rolls with not so ridiculously high expectations and was prepared to enjoy this joint's own take on this old, famous, street food. We got delivery and the food came earlier than expected. We tried the lamb kabob, chicken achari, and paneer tikka rolls. As a meatatarian, I was surprised to find my favorite was the paneer tikka roll. The paneer was super soft and the coriander chutney was legit. The chicken achari had a good flavor. The lamb kabob was disappointing. I was expecting large chunks of tender lamb but the meat ended up being shredded up and mixed up with too many spices. The flavor ended up being confusing. Also, the sauces were halal cart sauces and not appropriate accompaniments for the rolls. The white sauce would be better as raita (yogurt sauce) instead of this weird mayo herby stuff. I know. As an Indian I'm being too critical. 

Overall a solid place for Americanized kati rolls, not too authentic but good. I would definitely come back. Try the paneer tikka! And they're open late and deliver!

The order wasn't taken correctly at the speaker and then when I corrected it at the window, the cashier had an attitude!  Maybe it was the eyelashes hanging over her eyelids which caused her to mess up my order and overcharge me but even when I brought it to her attention, no apology or anything.  Horrible customer service! The food wasn't even that good! Never in my life will I return!

Food was very delicious! I can literally devour 2 or 3 kati rolls in one sitting (I'm not fat because I'm sure you can too!). However, considering of the location, I wouldn't say that their food is cheap. One kati roll costs you $7 and $10 for a platter; this reminds me of how cheap & bangin' those chicken & lamb rice platter you can get from the halal food trucks. 

Another thing, aren't restaurants legally required to serve you tap water? I could be wrong, but I wonder if they'll refuse to bring me a tap water if I ask for it.

Ordered lunch from here via Grubhub, for myself and with coworkers, on a Saturday Afternoon. Ordered the following with unsatisfactory results:
Veggie Platter - Described on online menu as "A vegetarian's delight, veggie and rice" turned out to just be tomato and iceberg lettuce over pita bread and rice.
Paneer Tikka Roll - described on the online menu as "made with cheese", arrived with what appeared to be egg.
Lamb Kabab Roll - dry and bland.
We also got Mango Lassi for all 3 of us and it turned out to be the only salvageable part of the meal. one of my coworkers brought it back to complain, but the guy in the store would do nothing, so we got a partial refund from the online service later that day.
disclaimer - they did all us when the food was ready to be picked up, but I wasn't able to answer it cause I leave my phone with the rest of my belongings in the back of the store, so I can concentrate on customers. when I originally went to pick up the food, the guy at the counter didn't express any concerns about our order, but when my coworker went back to complain he said 'but we called you to see if you would have a problem with your order being just tomato and lettuce' andsoforth. Guy, if you really cared, you would have mentioned it before you took my money in person and let me walk out the door.
the mandatory star goes to the mango lassi.

Definitely my favorite food cart in Center City, if you haven't been there you need to try it ASAP! The food is extremely fresh, service is great (friendly and good conversation every time I've visited), and the flavors are amazing. My favorite sauces are the general tso's and the chili garlic, if you combine either one with any of the many meat/noodle options and top with the lime wedge, it is sure to hit the spot! I like the flavor you get from having the meal cooked in a wok as well. You won't be disappointed with the endless combos and options at the wok works cart.
The staff was very disrespectful. The guy ringing us up gave us a lot of attitude when we were ordering. We asked for straws since there wasn't any and he just looked at us and walked away.

I'm typically a sucker for burgers from nearby Village Whiskey, but if I'm trying to save a few bucks (or a lot of bucks if we're talking about VW), I gotta say I was pretty impressed with their standard burger. It's 1/2 the price of the VW burger too. Bang.

Stopped in on Tuesday. It was excellent. The potato salad is as good as everyone says it is. It is a great side for for the chicken teriyaki. There use to be a chicken teriyaki at Liberty Place in the food court. Seattle Teriyaki is so much better in taste and quality.

All of a sudden, I am craving a beach club sandwich :-P

I declared my #1 sandwich place for a power work lunch yesterday.  Inspiration?  At, oh, 10-10:30 in the MORNING, the Kimmel Cancer Center staff was treated to samples of Jimmy John's sandwiches by two very friendly and upbeat (for a Monday!) jj reps :-) : "hey, do you want a sandwich?" --- and I was sitting in the lounge area, looking like I had the Monday blues, mind you.  A bite of the Turkey Tom, and I was reminded of how wonderful that Beach Club sandwich was (the only difference between the two sandwiches is the additional ingredient of avocado in the Beach Club, fancy fancy).  

Don't be discouraged by the price if it's your first time at Jimmy John's on 11th and Walnut.  You need to try one, plus their huge helping of pickles.  It's just THAT good :-)

Shake Shack is my guilty pleasure. I have been here a couple times, and every time I have to order the Shroom Burger. It's a mushroom, seemingly deep fried or something, STUFFED with gooey hot amazing cheese. Absolutely amazing.

It might be a little overpriced (I'm pretty sure I could buy the burger rolls at the grocery store...) but in my opinion, I feel like it's worth it because that burger is perfectly delicious every time.

The fries are also really good! Crinkle cut fries that are a little crisp on the outside - perfect.

I've never actually tried a shake yet, but I'm sure I'll get there eventually.

Worst, slowest drive through in the history of drive thoughts. As a matter of fact, I'm currently going on ten minutes of waiting in line, after ordering. That much more time to marinate in the guilt  of eating this slop.

I have been eating at Shake Shack ever since it opened and I have never once been disappointed.  It is clear that they emphasize quality customer service--all the employees are always friendly, enthusiastic, and ready to serve. No matter what I'm in the mood for, I can always find something on the menu to satisfy my craving; whether it be a chicken sandwich, a cheeseburger, a cheese-stuffed, crisp-fried portobello mushroom burger, or a cheeseburger topped with a cheese-stuffed, crisp-fried portobello mushroom burger!  Not to mention the fries (both plain and cheese-topped) are yummy as are the shakes, custards, and concretes (speed-blended custard with a variety of mix-ins; you can either choose from the seasonally rotating menu selections or create your own!).  Although Shake Shack tends to get crowded especially on evenings and weekends,  it's always a fun place to come alone or with friends to enjoy some high quality fast food!

As advertised!   Very good.  Almost a perfect meal for me.  I'm not a big carb eater and I was able to substitute a very nice salad for the rice.  I had the boneless chicken breast.  The meat was tender and tasty.    You can get brown rice if you want.    I will definitely be back.   I took food to go and next time I will ask for a little more time on the grill for a little more of the crispy edges.  But that is just personal taste.   Price was right!
Had awesome chaach...rolls were pretty decent. Reccomend you to go just for drink. Small place...mostly did take out.

Worst chipotle I've ever been to. Stick to the one at 15th. I've been here multiple times, and have never been satisfied with the food nor the service. Bland meat, dry rice, and they dont even have the courtesy to strain my mild salsa, so I end up with a puddle of tomato juice at the bottom of my bowl. Just terrible. I will never come back to this location.

I went here yesterday with my Dad for lunch while walking around Philly and it hit the spot! Both of us have been to the one in NYC in the park and loved it, and have been meaning to give the Philly location a shot since I live four blocks from it. I had the double hamburger with bacon and my Dad had the double shake shack burger with raw onions and a vanilla milkshake. It tasted exactly the same as when we had it in NYC, which means it was delicious! 

This is the best burger you can get from a fast food place, other places do not hold a candle to it. The burgers are extremely juicy and very flavorful, and you can tell that they use the best ingredients because of how it tastes. The only problem is they are gone too quickly! The other good thing is that the line is never long like it is in NYC. We were able to order and get our food within ten minutes, which is less than half the time I waited on line for a burger in NYC. 

I was concerned that the quality would suffer due to it being a different location in a different city, but I'm happy to say that it is not the case. If you think Five Guys is the best, do yourself a favor and hit this place up. My Dad was a Five Guys fan until trying Shake Shack, now he only goes back there if Shake Shack is not an option. Yes it is more expensive than other burger joints, but it is definitely worth it.

We were there around 4p and had popcorn chicken and jumbo squid to go. Perfect snacks for 3 ppl. They were so delicious. Absolutely love the food and the place. It's not a fine dinning place, but a cute, super causal hangout eatery. Will definitely revisit

I've utilized the Corner Bakery for a few lunch meetings at work. And it's always a hit! They have a great variety of sandwich choices and the sesame seed bread is very fresh. We typically get a few different sandwiches (turkey, roast beef, tuna, veggie), a salad, cookies and chips. We always fight over the leftovers. 

Everything is always prepared as expected and ready for us to pick up at the agreed upon time. 

I would definitely recommend the Corner Bakery for catered lunch if you are in center city.
MAYO is not RAITA. come on, we might be american but we know yogurt from mayo.

At least I can say I've been here!

I checked out Shake Shack on Wednesday and thankfully didn't encounter the long wait I expected.  The customer service here is spot on.  The guru of hospitality, Danny Meyer, has taught his staff well.  One of the things I picked up on was the subtle and rarely seen customer service tactic of staff keeping eye contact with customers when taking their orders.  While most customers probably didn't notice or care, perceptive ol' me did and I appreciated it far more than the usual aloofness and fakeness which is too often the norm from servers.  When the dude ringing up my order asked me how my day was going, I actually think he meant it.  And even if he didn't, he at least pretended to.  Makes you feel like you're respected and makes you want to return.  Although, in my case, I'm not going to return.  Here's why...

Shake - I ordered a black and white with malt.  My taste buds found no malt but they sure found the $.50 charge on top of an already expensive $5.00.  I mean, seriously,  $5.00 is preposterous for a shake that was no better than what you'd find at the golden arches.

Burger - I got the double SmokeShack.  The dude asked me how I wanted it cooked.  I replied "medium rare".  He said they can only cook it medium or rare (WTF?) so I said, OK, I'd like it rare.  It came medium.  You charge $9.00 for a puny portion (yes, it was juicy; yes, I loved the pepper spread; yes, they give you thick applewood bacon) but then can't even show the minimum level of attention to detail?  Sad.  And they really have no excuse because they weren't that busy.  

Cheese fries - The cheese was very sinful.  I was skeptical of crinkle-cut fries but they were fresh and well seasoned.  Very good overall.

So, yeah, I can say I hit up the Shake Shack but call me a one/off.  500 Degrees, I'll be knocking at your door next.

I was not going to write about this, but when I saw the review from "J.B." on 4/9/15, and realized that the exact same situation had happened to me, I decided to write it.
  The food is not the issue - its good hoagie-type sandwiches, made to order.  The problem is I had an identical experience to J.B. with regard to credit card theft.   While I could not PROVE it happened there, here is why I am certain it did:  I was out of the city for 6 weeks.  I returned home on March 16.  I used my credit card TWO times between March 16 and March 17, once at my super market and once at JimmyJohns.  That afternoon I got the dreaded "fraud call" from my credit card company.  There were 3 bogus charges, all in the suburban Philadelphia area.  While I suppose it could have been stolen on line and just by random chance was used in this area, the odds are against it.  I stopped in to JimmyJohn's the following week to discuss it  and the woman who identified herself at the manager couldn't care less.  Not the least bit interested.  
  There's a serious issue here with regard to the people who work there and credit card theft, and the company should address it.  Meanwhile, customers be warned!
I've been twice and both times my order took 15 minutes to come out.  it was a very simple order (burger, fries).  Did I just have bad luck twice?

Absolutely the best tasting restaurant in the tri state! Their flavors are so hard to duplicate, believe me I've tried! With great prices, amazing food and their around the clock hours, perfect place to go for any meal. Big shout out to all the staff as they are all super nice and friendly!

I was looking for new places to try in Philly and this came up highly rated and for a good reasons. The food is/was delicious, staff was friendly and want you to order something you will enjoy. Ask them anything and they will give you an honest answer and opinion. I will be coming back and order from here a lot!

I've tried both rolls and platters at this place. Their beef rolls and potatoes rolls are fantastic but I'm never going to order those platters because they just don't taste good. Four stars for the rolls and two stars for the platters.

Love this place! I love getting the tacos or the rice bowl, bulgogi and the double fried chicken are my favorites. It really hits the spot, and the tacos are surprisingly filling. The girl at the counter who helped me was really great, and I love the glass bottles they offer, especially the pineapple Fanta!

The shack burger taste soo good me and my boyfriend split 3 and the fries are good just wish it wasnt in that small container. Weird- when we asked for a refill on our soda they threw the cup away and gave us a new one lol

My boyfriend and I visited HipCityVeg over the weekend and were both pleasantly surprised by the quality of both the food and service. As a person with a nut allergy, it isn't necessarily easy to find a vegan restaurant that caters to my dietary need. The manager went above and beyond by looking in the recipe book to ensure that the Philly Steak did not contain any nut products. It certainly rivaled the best of the best cheesesteaks I've had before. You will not be disappointed if you pay this restaurant a visit!

I never went to the one in Rittenhouse (or anywhere else), but when this opened, it always smelled amazing when I walked by, so I had to try it!

Having never been to Hip City, I thought the Bistro Bella would be a safe start. I got a side of sweet potatoes fries with sriracha aioli. 

Even though I got it to go (and takeout is usually never good), it was amazing! Usually, I don't like artichokes, but damn. They were on it, and I had no problem with it. The bella was delicious, and all the vegetables were fresh (believe it or not, I've found dead lettuce in my salads at other restaurants). The fries were SO GOOD. Though, I've found that sweet potato fries pair better with some sort of maple syrup type dip. The sriracha was a weird flavor combination, sweet and "hot."

The staff was very friendly, and the cook even held up my sandwich to show me how good it looked after it was finished (I found this funny, and it made me smile).

My only problem is it's so tiny inside, there's nowhere to stand to wait for your food without being in the way.

Look, I'm a hardcore carnivore, but this place is so good!

The Shack gets 5 stars all day.  I love shake shack, one must order the shack stack burger.  When the portobello mushroom infused with muenster and cheddar flavor explosion commences in your mouth and you are dumbfounded with pure american gluttony you will know this is the best fast food money can buy.  I love the crinkle cut fries and you can wash it all down with their Brooklyn Brewery beer. 

ITS SHAKE SHACK and the convenience of not waiting in a 30 minute line like in NYC is unparalleled.
Bento boxes are great, BBQ is a little tasteless, no ramen in stock yet. Nice ambiance with Korean music. Check out the muscle and lady milk teas for their containers. Good portion sizes.

Finally made it to Shake Shack, we happened to be driving by on the way to Trader Joe's and decided to stop in to give it a try.  I got the mushroom burger.  It was different - it had two portabella tops with loads of cheese inside, breaded and fried.  So - it was vegetarian but not vegan. You can't order it without the cheese (I tried!).  The fries are crinkle fries and good.  The bun is a potato bun.  Hubby got a burger and it looked kind of small.  We also got the chocolate/brownie/coffee concrete on our way out which was good.  Everything was just that:  good. Not great.  Nothing impressive.  Nothing that we are going to run back for.  I am debating between two and three stars, sorry SS - going for the two stars.  I can't believe people waited on ridiculous lines for it!

Honestly best beef tacos ever! Customer service is friendly & they provide several websites to get their food delivered(UberEATS, Grubhub & Caviar.) They also take orders over the phone to take out. The combination is great! Would def. come back!

The Seattle specialty of teriyaki has come to Philadelphia.  This quick eating spot on Sansom Street is indeed fast as they will prob have your order ready in less than five minutes unless there are a lot of peeps ordering at once. The good news if that this is def authentic teriyaki Seattle style - down to the accompanying cold salad.  Here it is potato salad ... it could just as well be macaroni salad or cole slaw etc.  The chicken I ordered was totally tasty - tender with a slight flavor of having been grilled.  There was Sriracha sauce to add a little heat.  The only thing I would have wished for is a condiment on the counter of either teriyaki or soy sauce to add to the rice. They do include a small container of sauce but it is not nearly enough for someone like me.  I also noticed too late that for a small xtra charge I could have had brown rice which I def prefer. This is a filling meal.  And the service was very friendly!  Welcome this little taste of Seattle to Philly!

Fast, friendly, fresh and cheap. Was craving for roast beef.. so I ordered big john sandwich. The meat, the veggies and the mayo.. they get along so good. A good portion with cheap price. Definitely a good alternative to subway or quiznos.

Make me hungry all the sudden as I type this.. D:

Going to try their totally tuna next time..
I could have gotten a cheeseburger off of McDonald's dollar menu and a Wendy's frosty and saved myself the $10 difference. Would have tasted better too.

Here is my haiku review:

Excellent burgers
Like Five Guys but more costly
Don't drink the draft beer

Since the line out the door is generally longer than my lunch break permits, I jumped at the opportunity to try this hyped-up New York originated burger shack when I caught a break in the crowds. Although I had been receiving mixed reviews, this place is a gem.  The burgers are juicy and remind me of the closest thing on the East Coast to an In N Out Burger. 

The cheese fries are quite the indulgence, with a savory cheddar dip that is mouth watering. The staff here is kind and accommodating and the ambiance is very "green". 

According to the signs, Shake Shack is now officially a BYOB, which seems weird, considering the setting and menu. The only alcohol I'd suggest bringing in the cooler are a couple of IPA's to pair with a burger.  

Bottom Line: This place is like Disney World..an over priced tourist trap, but you've just gotta go to experience it.

This is an ok place. Don't expect to be blown away by some amazing, delicious, life-changing meal that will forever be remembered as your greatest meal. It's ok. They don't do anything wrong, and I've been a few times due to convenience. The rice platters are a bit overpriced in my opinion, and the naan bread just isn't very good compared to other places. However, the rolls are pretty tasty and filling and are honestly a pretty swell deal. The dude who took my order was nice, and the food came out relatively fast. I went twice for a quick dinner, but think that this place operates more as a lunch joint. Overall 6.4/10 (completely arbitrary)
ok i gave this place another try...this time i asked for NO salt on my burger and no salt on my fries...it was good..still over priced...and still five guys beats them.

My son loves this place so I am happy- But this place is always busy- there is no communication between staff. There is always one person working the meat, salads and register on their own. All the while they are calling out over their shoulder for assistance. expect at 25-30 min wait online. I only wait again, my son loves this place. 
dont expect a thank you.

I love the cheese fries!!!!
I think I like the burgers too but I don't remember from 12/2012. Will let you know :-)
Closed 20 minutes early after going out of our way to get there. Cook was outside smoking a cig before close

I got the chicken and rice platter. It is a lot of food! I wish they gave your more naan though. Everything was seasoned and tasted really good. The place was empty and our food came out really fast. It tasted great reheated the next day also.

Shake Shack opened at THE most appropriate time for summer.

Last night, before heading over to laugh ourselves silly from Aziz Ansari's 'Buried Alive' stand up, we met up with our friends for dessert Shake Shack style. Our friends had already had a Shake Shack dinner that evening (I don't even want to know how many times they've eaten there since our first visit) but were happy to go back for frozen treats.

They, including my fiance, all got the special coffee and donuts flavor, with none other than Federal Donuts' own donut pieces scattered atop the coffee custard - SUPER delicious, I wasn't content with the one bite I was allowed. I HAD to try one of the concretes, and I LOVE the Philly-centric menu specialties so after deliberately FAR too long, I chose the Liberty Shell (vanilla custard, Termini Bros cannoli shell, lemon ricotta, and strawberry puree) and added some fudge on top. OMG delicious. The crunch of the cannoli shell gave great textural contrast to all the cold, creaminess of the entire dessert. I HAVE TO TRY THE OTHER CONCRETES! Thankfully, summer in Philly will provide many, many more disgustingly hot days that will require cooling off with delicious frozen custard.

This is at the old @ramen location. The place is kind of hilarious as they just have makeshift hand drawn paper signs covering any trace of @ramen. But then they served the food in old @ramen branded bowls. 

The cashier has the world's quietest whisper of a voice which was almost inaudible over the blaring music. Good music selection though. But they should probably aim the speakers away from the cashier. 

The teriyaki meat is quite good and the portions are sizeable. The meat was served with diced coleslaw. Wtf. Where is the macaroni or potato salad everyone else raves about?! Slaw and teriyaki was a terrible combo and whoever okayed it should be terminated. 

The white rice is soft and fluffy too. So good. 

The side game is really weak. If they can step it up they would be a 5 star joint no doubt.

Randomly stopped by here when I was craving teriyaki chicken. Seattle Teriyaki didn't disappoint! The prices were reasonable and affordable. Friendly and quick service. I definitely want to stop by again to try their other dishes. I'll see you again soon, Seattle Teriyaki!! :)
Best breakfast sammy ever!! I got it on an everything bagel and added avocado and the sausage, I could eat this everyday. The hashbrown tasted just like McDonald's :-) amaaaaazing

The line was short. I was really hungry n i decide let me try their food since it just open. The food was bad. I had a plate(2 entrée) fried rice and sweet chicken it was just horrible. I can say the fortune cookie n egg roll was good.

Went at 11am and got take out. Place was PACKED! No line when I went in. When I came out the line was out the door. Place is smaller than I thought it would be. Service was AWESOME! from the greeter to the cashiers! The burger was good but too small (patty and ounce wise) for me but it was good flavor.  Took off a star because the togo waiting area was right in the area where people where going to sit down and eat and everyone was bumping in to me because it was so tight! Would I go out of my way to come here? Most likely not but if I am in the area I'd most likely go back. Hey its WAY better than the crap they serve at Five Guys!

Very delicious. Had a chocolate shake and grilled "chicken" sandwich. Kinda awesome to be able to get comforting, delicious, fast-food that is vegan. It has been a long time since I have had the non-vegan version of either, but to me, the chocolate shake tasted very realistic to a malty sort of shake. Very good. Didn't seem particularly healthy, of course, but that isn't really what you go to fast-food for. I am sure I will be back.

very good authentic kati rolls. This is the kind of restaurant that i had been luking for a very long time and found it finally. They have really good quality and authentic kathi rolls. The closest u will get to the ones found on the streets of india.

I know, I know. The pork problem. Blah Blah Blah. I don't care- I like Chipotle. Its a quick and convenient lunch option close to my office. Sure, sometimes the line is long, but the staff moves it pretty quickly. The flavor of the food is consistent and that's what I look for in a chain restaurant like this. 4 stars for being convenient, relatively quick, delicious, and predictable.

This place does not live up to the hype.

My double stack burger was tasty, but way too small - I finished it within three minutes of sitting down. 

The fries were average but nothing special.

I had a concrete with cookie dough and banana, which was the best part of the meal. 

If you want a fast food-style burger, I recommend saving your money and going to Five Guys.

I went recently and it took about 10-15 minutes to get my food. It was during lunch time on a week day so that's not bad. It got much more crowded after I ordered. I found a seat inside but it was very full. I enjoyed the burger and thought it was DEFINITELY better than Five Guys (which make me sick). I go to 500 as well, and this is just a different kind of burger. I did not like the fries at Shake Shack and I had a strawberry lemonade, which was ok. I would return but I would skip the fries.

The best chipotle in the city!! A sweet staff that is attentive and willing to make customers' lives easier and better. I accidentally ordered on the app from the wrong store. When I arrived the manager told me he would honor my order so I didn't have to walk again in the rain. He even called the other store to let them know I wouldn't be coming in and that they would be handling my order. So nice!

Love Shake Shack!  I always get the chicken shack and the rest of the fam get burgers. All are delicious!  Today added the hotdog but did not really enjoy it. Too many toppings. Fries are delicious and crispy. Last but not least love the shakes. The holiday options were great!  Kids each orders one - the Cookie and Peppermint.

I walked in here around 5:00pm maybe. I haven't eaten at chipotle in awhile so had the urge to have a steak burrito. I've never been to this specific location but it's the closest to where I reside so it was an easy decision. I drove her and parking was easy (probably just luck or it was a Sunday). 

I walked in and their were about five others sitting around eating and conversing with one another. I walked up and the gentlemen asked what I would like. I told him and he prepared my request, the second lady on the line wasn't so nice. She seemed short with me and wasn't professional at all. I asked for more corn and she just put it on there. I felt like I was troubling her. I know it's just chipotle but she clearly has an attitude.

She should leave it at the door when she walks into work. She's getting paid to be there so theirs no excuse for it. I said thank you and I didn't get any response from her which I thought was rude. The third lady that cashed me out was nice so overall it was ok. Maybe she was having a bad day or something but she wasn't professional and just think she should have common curtesy when she's working and getting paid.

The burrito was good and can't complain about that. I usually don't go on about a specific employee at a establishment but felt it was necessary. She was rude and not professional. The place was clean but when I went into the bathroom and wanted to wash my hands their was no soap in the dispenser. 

I will go back there for sure and hope that employee is in better spirits. I gave it 3 stars this place because of the lack of customer service from her and no soap in the dispenser, the place wasn't full so don't see why one of them couldn't refill it.

always missed kathi rolls and everytime i went to New York, i'd eat some there and bring some back.. so happy to have found this place in philly!!!

love the Aachari Paneer roll.. really yummy.. the paneer is cooked well..
the chicken tikka and paneer tikka rolls are good.. but not as good as aachari paneer.. 
the chicken is slightly dry..

the aloo roll and aloo-paneer roll are just ok.. found them pretty bland.. the mixed veggie roll - as a roll it wasn't good.. the mixed veggie by itself with roti would have been good.. 

the white sauce and red sauce they give with the rolls are YUM!!!!!!!!!! the red sauce has a good kick to it..

the veg biryani was good..

i have always ordered food for take-out.. never sat at spice end and eaten..

good food for late nights!!! and definitely very filling..

Finally, a place for quality healthy take out in Fairmount! Up until now we've been short a place to grab healthy to-go options that's not the high prices and craziness of Whole Foods. The store had a lot of variety, lots of people ready to ring you up, and wide open/ easy to grab displays. 

I tried the pecan crusted salmon and the mashed sweet potatoes. Both gluten free and really delicious. Generous portions and appropriately priced. 

My only suggestion is the first time you go, you may need to spend an extra minute to get yourself acclimated to where things are. I feel like that's true of any store you go to though. 

Can't wait to try more great options!

Another Shake Shack! I'm not complaining, their burgers are great! They're the same as every other Shake Shack but also just as expensive. It's nearly $5 for a single patty, fast-food-styled burger. It's delicious but I'd rather spend a little less. They also take longer than I'm comfortable with to serve up just a cheeseburger so that's another lost point. It's also an injustice that there's not enough sitting space here. Have the owners not realized that this place is capable of forming block long lines of hungry patrons? They're all going to want to sit down eventually and this Philly branch does not give the name justice.

Their delivery service is poor, they take about 2 hours to deliver to a center city address. It's a nice quick bite , not so heavy. It's not authentic Indian and not sure what those white n hot sauces are.

Went for lunch on Sunday. No line! But the food took 15-20 minutes.

I've already fallen in love with NYC Shake Shack so I had high hopes for this Philly one. 

Their burgers were delicious as usual. I got a single shake burger & my sister got the shroom burger. Delish. If only it was cheaper - I'd go back more often.

A modern take on the old-school idea of getting an old-fashioned burger and shake. Fries are bangin, sandwhiches were pretty great too, along with shakes. What stands out? The stellar staff. Every single employee was friendly, accommodating, and conversational. Definitely will be back.
Very open and big for being in center city Philadelphia. Meet with a mentor here for lunch, and very friendly staff and good for a quick breakfast.

I'm completely disappointed in myself that I have walked by countless times and always say "I need to try it" and it took me until yesterday to follow through! Well I can say that I have been missing out! I ordered for lunch on a Tuesday around noon and they said it would be ready in 5 minutes. I went there in about 10 and the food was ready and service was great. They even had parfaits, cookies and brownies that were available to purchase. 

My only issue here was that I could not pick what sandwich I wanted for my first visit here. I was not sure if I wanted a buffalo bella with chicken or a ziggy burger. I went with the ziggy burger for my first time and oh my goodness it was NOT a regret. It is a veggie burger with tempeh and the most delicious and creamy sauce to ever go on a burger and lettuce, tomato and onion. It was unreal. They were not shy with the sauce and my mom got their nuggets with sweet potato fries and I was dipping the fries into the sauce that dropped on my plate. We opted for the spicy aioli instead of the black bean dip for the fries and that was a great choice! Their nuggets were also unreal. My mom is not a vegetarian and she typically doesn't choose to eat meat-free items but she said that these were so great and she would be back to order them again. 

Everything was amazing and I can't enjoy it any more that they made such tasty items that are all plant based. I feel more comfortable about what I ate and they offer salads and juices/lemonades. If you have not been here yet then you must give it a try asap and not miss out like I did for so long!

This is what they consider to be a burger. It's a joke. There's barely any meat and it was mainly all bun. The chocolate milk shake was disgusting and fries were cold. Oh and did I mention the drive through is super slow?

My favorite burger in the northeast.  I have eaten at 3 locations in NYC and this one in Philadelphia.  I've had the Smoke Shack (my favorite - love the pepper relish and sauce) and the Shack Burger.  Love the fries too.  Crisp and delicious!  Best of all, draft beer including their own brand brewed by Brooklyn Brewery as well as seasonals they always have.  Love Shake Shack!  Will be going back again and again.

Tried it for the first time yesterday. I had a small cheeseburger without all the sauce on it so i could taste the meat and it was just fair, but the bun was very good. I also had a chocolate shake which was tasty but seemed to me to be more like the consistency of frozen custard rather than a freshly made shake with real ice cream.  Staff was very attentive. I'll stick with Five Guys.

Ordered on ubereats yesterday and was iffy when the food got here super fast (sometimes when it's that fast I assume the worst) but I was very wrong! The chicken was piping hot and crispy, I asked for no thighs which Popeyes never ever get right and they loaded me up with only breasts wings and legs (large 12 pc order for family) the mashed potatoes where also extremely hot and tasty. Dad said that was the best Popeyes chicken he's ever had!

The burger is the Bomb. If you ever want something super greasy and a heart attack this is the place to be. Crispy cheese fries to cure your drunkness. 

If you watching your diet this is not a place for you. 

I would recommend this place.  Good eats. Ps you can get alcohol here too.

Delicious!  I love their chicken kati roll sandwich and the one that comes with egg!  Great sauces too!  I'm sure everything there is good!  The atmosphere is not pretty, but we get take-out so we don't care. Highly recommend for take-out!

Sometimes you eat because you are hungry, and other times you eat because the food is right there and the inner grown-up voice inside of you that says "no, stop, don't - but you are full!"  is muffled by the sounds of fries in a deep fryer and ice cream in a blender being whipped into shakes...

I'll let you guess why I popped into Shake Shack last night... My girlfriend Jodi (whose inner control voice was also obviously muffled) and I went for an early dinner at Zama, followed by a show at a local theatre.  We walked pass SS on our way from dinner to the theatre and both thought yummmmm, but were super proud of ourselves for passing for a healthier / lighter fare at Zama.  

As the lights came up during intermission of the show... we both looked out at each, and without more than a nod, we were out of those seats and headed to SS!  We never made it back for the 2nd 1/2 of the show, as we pulled up two window seats and downed our peanut butter & vanilla milkshakes and of course, our side of fries!

Can't wait 'til my next trip back - as I was definitely eye-stalking the girl's "creamsicle float" two seats down from me...

Delicious kati rolls and awsome mouth watering Biryanis!!! On top of that CHHAAS (Buttermilk) makes me reminds of my mom. I Love Paneer (Cottage Cheese) and this is the best place to have it as a Kati roll coz they make it as grilled tikka type paneer with delicious marination. Not at all expensive and stomach filling.

We were running a couple errands around here and decided to pop in to grab a quick dinner on our way home.

It was a pretty normal Chipotle.  I felt like the line moved slower than at our normal Chipotle, but it wasn't long before we were out with our burritos.

Other than the slightly slower line, everything was just what I'd expect and our burritos were just as delicious and fresh as always.

This place is the real deal. They make the paratha on premises, so it is nice and fluffy. I had the lamb roll. It is awesome. Don't ask me how they get the meat so tender. Effing delicious. The ambience is pleasant. Tall ceilings. But the art is a bit lacking in the character department. Also not as cheap as one might hope. To get full one needs to rolls at about 6 bucks a piece.

Fiancee and I went for dinner. "Plant Manager" was very friendly. Fiancee is gluten free and ordered the Bistro Bella, however, we didn't realize that ordering it gluten free meant it became a salad. It didn't do well as a salad since it was composed mostly of mushroom, tomato, and arugula. Dressing was minimal as if the order was still a sandwich, and ingredients were added as whole pieces instead of manageable bite sizes. I'm not gluten free or vegan. I ordered the Philly Steak. Not bad for a vegan cheesesteak, but either the filling needed more flavor or the bread needed to be thinned out. However, both of us got milkshakes, strawberry and chocolate, and they were delicious! Seems like a good place for vegetarians or vegans - not so much if you're also gluten free. Pricing also seems a little high.

Edible fast food but there's always a bit of drama when I ask for sliced jalepanos on the side. Last time they emerged from the cooler with 2 whole peppers and handed them over. I sliced one with a plastic knife and brought the other home with me.

Alright, now this New Yorker can say that I've tried Shake Shack. I know, what the heck? I've never eaten at the infamous Shack Shake (now with many NYC locations)?! Yeah, well, I don't like waiting on line for food. I've also only recently started eating burgers (cue gigantic *gasp* and fainting in shock).

So the Philly location spurred our friends to invite us to try them, and I thought why not? I decided to make sure we wouldn't be waiting on a line for freaking ever by getting there kinda early for dinner on a Thursday, and there was barely a line leading out of the door. I actually let people go ahead of me while waiting for the others to show. Of course no space inside to eat, so Rittenhouse Park provided us with a venue to eat.

I was surprised by the size of the burgers - tiny! - but at least my bird dog was a regular size. Split and grilled, it had a nice snap with each bite. Everyone else obviously got one of their burgers (Shackburgers and Smokeshack) with fries, and our friends got chocolate and strawberry shakes. They were drooling over the burgers from the first bite, and at the end of the meal declared they could definitely eat another, despite being full. Fries were fine (they really liked them), and our friends loved the shakes and how thick they were. A nice burger addition to the area - but thank god the park is so close! Every bench had people eating Shake Shack as we walked through :)

For a good late night place to eat I would highly suggest going to spice end. This place is known for their Kati rolls which are amazing and highly recommend getting either the chicken or the lamb. Out of the two I would go with the lamb as I feel that the meat goes well with the vegetables and it's very fresh. The two sauces that they have are a yogurt one and a hot sauce both complement the roll very well. The prices are pretty cheap and if you check in on yelp than it's 10% of your check which you can't go wrong with.
burgers. cheese. buns. fries. shake. dessert. Shackeffing awesome! Don't ask for more.

The prices here are fair for the amount they give you. For $7-$9 you can get an entire meal -- popcorn chicken, rice, and several sides. 

It's cheaper to get a meal ($7-$9) than just an order of popcorn chicken ($5) because the serving of chicken is the same, the meal just has all the extra rice etc. 

The quality is pretty good, it's all fried snacks and some drinks. Can't really go wrong with that 

If you like dipping your fried snacks, be ready to pay for it. Ketchup packets are free but any other sauces like honey mustard or Thai chili sauce are $0.25 and they give you a very tiny container of it. 

Very spacious inside. The atmosphere is casual and clean. You order/pay at the register and have the option of dining there or taking it to go. 

Fast and easy meal option that's on the cheaper side.

I was super exited to hear a shake shack was opening in Philly. Having partake in their wares during my trips in NYC a few times before. But there is no reason that every time I walk by SS people are lined up outside as if Kate Upton was giving free lap dances next to the ketchup dispenser. I digress...in my opinion the burgers are pretty decent and I personally am a pretty big fan of the shakes especially the racially harmonious black and white.  The fries are a skip for me.. I personally think SS should send one of their fifty minions they have scurrying around the kitchen down to 5 guys and get some proper fries. Could you get a better burger?..most definately and a better milk shake?...maybe, but both at the same place? Not in Philly bub. 
PS if you say Bobby's Burger Palace..I will hunt you down and remove your tongue with my bare hands.

I love this place and I lunch from here 2-3 times a week.  It's one of the best vegetarian sandwiches (number 13 all the way!) that I've been able to find in the city.  The food is low-cost, fresh, and is ready before I can check in on FourSquare.  Today I tried their delivery for the second time and my order that was confirmed by e-mail at 11:24 was in my hands by 11:32.

The people working there have been extremely pleasant in my opinion.  They usually remember my order (I ALWAYS get the number 13), joke with me if I'm not in for a few days, and are just generally nice people.

One last thing: bring your business card.  The drawing for free lunch for your office is real, and I won it last month.  They gave me enough sandwiches to feed my department and even made a separate veggie sandwich for me so it wouldn't be smeared with turkey and roast beef.  The deliver guy wouldn't even accept a tip for this delivery.

Overall, This is my hands-down favorite lunch spot.

As far as the food goes, its great!!!! everything i ever had was tasty and a nice large portion (enough to save some for a later snack) and the location and atmosphere are very nice. Most of the staff was friendly and polite but not all.

Used to love this place - would order and pickup lunch for the whole office and it was great. Easy online orders, always ready on time. Now I've been three times in a row an waited OVER half an hour each time. 

Nobody says sorry or offers any consolation. The staff is rude and doesn't keep me updated as to why they're SO late.  Very disappointing, was hoping they'd treat large pickup orders with more respect. 

Guess it's time to move our company's business to Qdoba.

I found the food and service to be consistent with their other locations, which is excellent - only this one offers breakfast items too. Very smart for the location which gets a lot of daily grinders. Yes, right at Broad & Sansom!

This is the smallest HCV, with only three seats, but if you snag one, it makes for good people watching out the window. To me it feels like a small takeout place in NYC, which is pretty cool.

I just hope they repair the door; every time someone comes or goes there's a sharp "whack" sound that's startling. For this reason I carefully guided the door closed when I left.

Overall this is exactly what this neighborhood was missing, and if I worked in the vicinity I'd be here daily. Totally recommended.

I don't understand the hype about this place.  I have always wanted to try Shake Shack because everyone on facebook is constantly posting pics.  I never really had a chance to go up to NYC to try it and was very happy to see a location open up in philly.

I heard about the long lines here and decided to go around 3:30.  The line wasn't too long, about 10 ppl in front of me.  The line moved pretty quickly but the wait for the order to come up took some time.  The total wait to get my food was about 20-25 min.  My order consisted of the smoke stack, bird dog, shroom burger, cheese fries, a strawberry shake and a fifty fifty.  The burger was good, but nothing special.  I really liked the buns they used but the chopped peppers had too much of a vinegar taste.  I would not wait in line for 20 min to order this again.  The bird dog was a regular overpriced hot dog.  The shroom burger was deep fried crap. The cheeses stuffed inside just didn't taste right and the mushroom had a bitter aftertaste.  Definitely not ordering this again if I come back.  The cheese fries came out warm and the cheese sauce was horrible.  This is philly, bring on the cheese wiz!  The drinks were great.  I would like to try the concretes and floats next time.

Overall, the burgers and drinks were good but all overpriced and I would not wait in line to order from here again.

When I first tried this place in NYC, it was a 4. The more and more I eat here, the more I love it.
I've now eaten at a location in NYC, Dubai, and now Philly. Always good, always consistent.
This place is all about the beef. It's juicier and beefier than any other chain, fast foodish burger you will have. The special sauce is more than just thousand island dressing (like all the other places) - it has a sweet mustardy twinge. 
Being from SoCal, this is essentially blasphemy, I'm supposed to be devoted to In & Out... But I can't. This place is just way too good.
Don't even get me started on the shakes. :)

The Corner Bakery Cafe is hands down one of the best places I have found in Philadelphia to get a good/hearty/real oatmeal. Their old-fashioned oatmeal is delicious, especially when you request it with fruit and whatnot. 
I love how it comes in a huge container also, I can pretty much enjoy it all day at work. Along with the free toasted Cinnamon raisin bread, that is lighted coated with sugar. YUM!
I also found this place aimlessly walking around trying to find something quick and easy for breakfast, and that wouldn't ruin my diet of the week.

As a McDonald's lover, I didn't think it was possible to dislike eating it until I went to the location on Girard... twice.

The first time I frequented this location it was 2pm on a Sunday and I've never before felt as uncomfortable in a restaurant. Between the obviously drugged out clientele and the unfriendly, half-asleep cashier, I wanted to leave this establishment as soon as possible and ended up eating my meal in my car.

The second time I went, I opted for the drivethru. While the service was better and smiles were exchanged, the food was not up to the McDonald's standards.  The soda was short on syrup and the burger/bun were both overcooked. Burgers are not easy to eat while driving, I will admit this, but the mayonnaise had missed the burger for the most part and was globbed on the outside of the box, ended up on my steering wheel, pants, and hands.

I agree with Jill though; the fries were good.

The food is average at best, but I feel what's really annoying about this place is the substandard customer service. I mean, the chicken sandwich would have been fine had the piece of chicken been slightly larger, and not horribly overfried. Perhaps that item is not the place' s specialty, but it was the only option open to me. When I asked whether the burger, which the sign above the counter described as "100% local pastured meats," was in fact grass fed, the employee stationed there said "yes," and then upon further questioning answered "no," until he finally settled on "well, I don't really know, we get it from a guy locally, I think his stuff is good." That final answer put one in mind of some sleazy huckster selling meat of questionable origin from a street side stand. I'm sure that couldn't possibly be the supplier of this resturaunt, but I can't imagine what other conclusion could be derived from that response. Then I proceeded to order, but was told in a rather rude tone to use the touch pad at the checkout counter. There's nothing wrong with that ordering method on its own, but the way the employee informed me implied that I was somehow stupid to know to use it, despite the lack of any instructional signage whatsoever. When I finally got my sandwich, I took it to my table and opened up my bag to pull it out, only to find that the sandwich was so lazily assembled that the chicken fell out of the sandwich and into the bag. The sandwich itself, once I reconstructed it, tasted ok, and based on the food alone, this would have been a 3 star review at least. The employees at the establishment, however, obviously don't take their jobs very seriously. In addition to what I have described, and perhaps the detail most telling of their utter incompetance, the two men I had the displeasure of dealing with had unkempt, scraggly beards, and neither felt it prudent to cover them with a hair net. Had I found a hair in my sandwich, this particular indiscretion would've been at the top of my review. Considering this resturaunt is part of a collective food court, I would recommend patronizing one of those other eateries instead.

Great homey atmosphere of a restaurant, like a homey Panera with a more intimate service staff. Broccoli Cheddar Bread Bowl was a little light on the soup and heavy on the bread. Quick service and cozy dining room.

We were in town for the weekend and ate here multiple times! Food was absolutely delicious - try the smokehouse burger. The staff was very friendly and able to answer any questions we had about the menu! Limited seating in the place, but plenty of seating directly next door without having to walk outside
Great burgers and fries. Was a bit too busy, but I was there Friday night so I guess it's to be expected.

This chipotle location just might be my favorite! The staff is always friendly and patient with their customers and greets you when they see you. Service is quick like it should be. I ordered the bowl (I always order a bowl) but this time, there wasn't as much rice as I remembered. I was kind of disappointed, but it was still a great meal!

Make no mistake these are great burgers, but I wouldn't say they're any better than Five Guys. A regular burger and a large drink was just under $10. They serve alcohol and Coke products. I haven't tried their shakes yet, and they have a weekly special flavor. 

There is more seating than I would have expected of the location, and if you're lucky you can grab a table outside. We ate in the park that's not too far away which was even better than eating there - which I would definitely recommend if the weather's nice. Luckily, haven't had to deal with the infamous line or even wait too long for my food. 

If you've never been to Shake Shack, definitely try it at least once and then spend the rest of the day walking around Philly.

Long line to get in and to wait to be served, but I loved the atmosphere. I ordered a Pepsi and a Monster Cookie. The Pepsi was way too carbonated, tasted like carbonated water. The Monster Cookie was huge and decent.

Literally a bakery on the corner. Seems like a nice little place. We stopped in and got a couple slices of the Cinnamon creme cake. They definitely aren't messing around with these slices. They were gigantic. And the cake itself was moist and the cinnamon topping nice and crumbly while adding a little crunch.

I came here with my 3 yo niece and ordered her a regular hamburger and ordered myself the Smokeshack and a side of fries.  We went at a perfect time around 11:30am with plenty of seats to choose from.  The restaurant was nice and clean and the service was friendly. 
I enjoyed my Smokeshack.  I especially liked the chopped cherry peppers to give it a little bit of a kick. 
What amazed me the most though was how much my niece loved her burger.  She ate the whole burger herself. Usually I have to fight with her to eat more burger and less fries but she hardly touched the fries at all.  
It was a fun time for me and my niece :)

After a successful day out on the road seeing clients in Philly I was hungry for a tasty something to eat while waiting for my train back to New York. I wanted a satisfying sandwich. Behold Jersey Mike's Subs! There a a bunch of fast foody types of places to eat in the food court at this train station but a good old fashioned hoagie was calling my name!

This place is pretty solid. Half sub for $6.79 or a giant sub for $10.69. I ended up with a 99% fat free half turkey and provolone sub on a really soft hoagie roll. Gotta get it with the works "Mike's Way" - onions, lettuce, tomatoes, spices, and red wine vinegar & olive oil blend. Delish!

They crank out the sandwiches quickly and they taste really good. Plus, they don't skimp on the ingredients. Along with some sea salt & vinegar chips I was a happy man.

Nap time on the way home!

When it comes to Korean / Mexican fusion, a good model to follow would be LA's Kogi trucks. Unfortunately, this place did not do that. 

The first strange thing about this place was that they were offering a nacho special for $12, which was more expensive than the majority of their menu. What's so special about expensive nachos? To me, it came across as a lame pricing strategy. If the nachos are $12 and tacos are cheaper, then the tacos must be a good deal... Anyways, we didn't get the nachos.

So we looked at the tacos. You can only buy them in groups of 3, and you can't mix and match. That means if you want the bulgogi tacos, you have to buy 3 of them, which costs $10. My wife wanted to try the twice fried chicken tacos, so we ordered those at $9. 

Next came paying for the food. We paid with a credit card. When we got the receipt, the girl behind the counter made it a point to put an 'X' on the gratuity line and an 'X' on the total line. Keep in mind, this place is in a food court. There is no service aside from the girl taking your order and the guy making your tacos. I know, I know, some similar places you do leave a tip, like coffee shops or pizza by the slice places, but it's usually based on the overall quality of the food and/or the experience. Anyways, I just thought that it was lame to put an 'X' next to gratuity. I know how to read a receipt...

Then came the final test: how did the tacos taste? Well, not very good. The ingredients used were tortillas, rice, a teeny tiny bit of corn and black bean salsa, and fried chicken bits which weren't even as good as typical Korean fried chicken. To say that I was disappointed would be an understatement. 

So why 2 stars instead of 1? Well, it would take a lot to give a place 1 star, and since this place just opened, I'm giving them the benefit of the doubt. But my advice to them would be please, do your customers a favor and study a place like Kogi. At Kogi, you can order individual tacos that actually taste like Korean fusion. You can also order burritos, sliders, and other items that aren't currently on your menu. I get that the rent in that food court is probably high, but if you want to get people lining up, you have to do a better job at your menu, pricing, and overall quality of food. 

As a final note, as we were leaving the food court, we couldn't help but notice the healthy portions of the Halal Guys menu, which was similarly priced but looked twice as good. Seeing that made the experience that much more painful. Ouch...

I like this Jimmy John's.  I can get my consistently good #6 vegetarian from JJ's anywhere since they're all the same.  BUT, this one is good because the employees are above average nice.   

Once this particular Jimmy John's delivered me a sandwich in 5 and a half minutes.  This is not a lie.   I couldn't have walked downstairs, taken everything out of the refrigerator, put it on bread, and put it away by the time this dude showed up on his fixed gear with a sweet mustache with my sandwich.  Now I'm upset if it takes 10 minutes.  Spoiled.

The only thing I hate about Jimmy John's is the sign "Free Smells."  Stupid.

Had some time to kill waiting for my train.  Got an Italian hoagie at Jersey Mike's Subs.  All I can say is awesome!  The best hoagie I have every had.  I actually ordered an extra one to take on the train on my way to D.C. and ate that one on the train.  Great fountain drinks too.  Can't say enough good things.  Will definitely come back next time I am in Philly.  Really a special treat!  Wish my grandkids could have been with me.  I'll get extras for them next time.  My wife actually got upset with me that I didn't bring extras for her and the grandkids.  Next time I won't forget.  That faux pas put me in the dog house, big time!

Um... talk about guilty pleasures!  

I'm typically always dieting.  Which I am right now... so my Double Smoke Stack Burger I had this weekend is my current biggest guilty pleasure.  OMG.  (Double Cheeseburger w/ Applewood Smoked Bacon, Chopped Cherry Peppers, & Shack Sauce)  I think I was in heaven while I was eating this burger.  How have I not tried Shake Shack until now!?  I'm sorry to sound like a teenybopper, but OMGOMGOMG!!!!

I thankfully was smart enough (aka told by my boyfriend) to skip out on the shake/concrete this visit because I was freakin' stuffed after my burger and shared fries.  I cannot wait to go back to try one of those because the toppings are super creative and I am having dreams about them.  

I think this place is WAY better than Elevation & Five-Guys.  YUMMMY!

I went today to Shake Shack after having been a couple of times in NYC and not feeling the hype. After this visiting this location, I can see the love, though.

I had a SmokeShack (basically a bacon cheeseburger with red pepper instead of tomato) and a rootbeer. The burger was cooked to diner-y perfection with grease, etc, etc. My only gripe is that the drink prices seem pretty inflated (almost $4 for my rootbeer).

What will probably keep me coming back is the service. As there was a long wait, I was hurriedly trying to put my debit card back in and be as quick as possible when I was ordering. The cashier went out of his way to tell me to take my time and make sure I had everything. In addition, the girl handling the "pickup order" section could not have been more pleasant and friendly. 

As for the restaurant itself, there are some tables but I wouldn't try to go here (at least until the hype dies down) with a large group as it's kind of a crazy atmosphere.

I stopped in early for a breakfast sandwich, I had the lox with everything it was delicious and fresh. There was capers, chive cream cheese, red onions, smoked carrots and cucumbers . Delish, I can't wait to try another type of breakfast sandwich very soon!! The cashier was also a delight , very welcoming!!

I was on a budget. I had a coupon. It was 95' outside and I didn't want to walk more than a block from my office for any kind of food no matter how good it was. This is the story of how I ended up at Corner Bakery with a tuna fish sandwich on toasted harvest whole grain bread. Really, there's not much else to it. With coupon my sandwich (piled high with extra veggies), chips, and pickle came out to a shade under $5, the line seemed long but it was air conditioned and felt wonderful, before I knew it I was in and back out again having only spent about 5 minutes on line. The restaurant gets really crowded during the corporate lunch hour, but I wasn't staying...I wanted to be back in the confines of my fuzzy walled cubicle as quickly as possible. The food was mediocre, nothing I'd really spend their full price on, but given the circumstances of the day this was a great choice.

This place is legit. I got a Shack Burger Double, some Fries, and a Black & White Shake.

The burger lived up to the expectations I had from all the hype surrounding this place. The fries are also very very good. Crinkle-Cut Fries are my favorite and they were not greasy, oily, or soggy here. It was crispy and not overly salty. The shake was also a good way to end the meal.

The wait was not too long for Opening Day at 1:30 (Maybe 20 minutes total). Service was great and the staff was friendly and insightful. They talked to everyone and gave out samples of their custard while people waited in line. They cleaned the tables once people left and I noticed they also responded to any order errors immediately.

Comparing this place to 500 Degrees and Five Guys (in terms of Burgers and Fries), I would rank them in this order:

1) Shake Shack
2) 500 Degrees
3) Five Guys

How do I know the GF loves and knows me? For the day before my birthday, the GF sent me off to get a surprise massage at Body Restoration and then had me meet up at Rittenhouse. From there, we set off to Shack Shack.

Shack-cago Dog [$4]
Rick's Picks Shack relish, onion, cucumber, pickle, tomato, sport pepper, celery salt, mustard

This time around, I was in the mood for a hot dog, so went with a Chicago-style dog, split and grilled on the flat top. Despite this, the dog could have used a bit more snap especially since the bun was soft. Still, it was delicious, with the celery salt making each bite. 

Shack Corn Dog [$4.50]
Vienna all-beef hot dog, Shack-made corn batter, Ricki's Picks sweet corn relish

For Memorial Day, Shack Shack had a special, which should really be a special every day of the year. The sweet crispy batter yields to the snap of a properly juicy dog. And the sweet corn relish had some great twang to provide some brightness to each bite.

SmokeShack [$6.25]
Cheeseburger, Niman Ranch applewood smoked bacon, chopped cherry pepper, ShackSauce 

And of course, this being Shack Shack, we had to get some burgers. The buns are soft, but that yields to a richer experience due to the contrasting crispness of the burger and bacon. The cherry peppers add some acidity to make this one of the better burgers on the East Coast.

'Shroom Burger [$6.75]
Crisp-fried portobello mushroom, melted muenster and cheddar, lettuce, tomato, ShackSauce

And the shroom burger is a beast of a vegetarian burger, with the blend of muenster and cheddar adding a creamy heft between the crisply fried portobello. Be warned though - it's a veritable explosion of molten cheese lava in your mouth! 

Fries [$2.70]

The one sub-par experience though? Shack Shack got rid of their trademark crinkle-cut fries. So sad, especially since these were a limp, greasy mess. But good news on the horizon! The crinkle-cut fries will be back in the Fall, supposedly better than ever with artificial ingredients removed! Just another reason to stop by Shack Shack every chance I can get.
I only have it 3 stars because the only thing I've tried here are the shakes, and let me tell you, they are artery clogging deliciousness.

One of the best fast food burger shops around. The meat is perfectly cooked, the hot dogs are good; my only gripe is they got rid of the crinkle cut French fries. I love crinkle cut, the only thing better is steak cut.  If you get a burger fries and a drink it will run you around 12 bucks which is on par with the industry.

Their vegetarian burger is ok, but unique in that it is made with 2 portobello mushroom caps stuffed with muenster and cheddar cheeses, not some tofu or bean patty. The fries & shake were also good. This is not a bad place. But Roam Burgers in San Francisco and the chain Counter are better options for gourmet vegetarian burgers.

Wow, I can't believe people are so into this place.  I got the Shack Stack (burger with the fried portobella).  I thought it was lacking flavor on top of being well done and small.  Has this place heard of seasoning?  The fries were pretty much tasteless too.  I should have known after seeing how many kids were in the restaurant.  If there are a lot of kids in the restaurant, the food is generally nothing to write home about.  

On the positive side, they had some great root beer by Abita on draft and the staff was really friendly.  Unfortunately the positive don't outweigh the negatives so I won't be back.  I would much rather spend three times as much for food that is ten times as good right across the street at Village Whiskey.

Not impressed.. Over priced and over hyped for a burger that tastes like Wendy's and costs double. The burgers were also small in my opinion. The fries were nothing to write home about.. I didn't get a chance to try the shakes..

At the Shake Shack in Center City, I experienced perhaps the best customer service I have ever encountered. This is the story of how the manager Derek Applegate exemplified leadership and made me 10x more likely to return.
First, when I told Derek it was my first time at a Shake Shack, he exclaimed, "hey everyone, it's Chris' first time at Shake Shack! Let's give him a round of applause!" A great welcome.
I was then saddened to learn that sesame seeds were an ingredient in the buns :-/
As someone with a sesame allergy I am used to needing to avoid hamburger restaurants *cough* Five Guys *cough*, so I was prepared to just eat my burger on lettuce and make a mental note not to return in the future.
However, all of that changed when Derek personally delivered my food - including a bun that he grabbed from the restaurant across the street! Not only that, but he gave me two vouchers for free milkshakes!
Needless to say, I will be back. Thanks to Derek!
I love this place. I live a few blocks away, but it is my go to place. The lines get annoying at lunchtime, but the menu is great. It's takeout for vegetarians.

I've had the chicken and rice platter and Achari chicken Kati roll here. Quite frankly, the food has been pretty bland but the delicious hot sauce, which I'm under the impression is homemade, fixes that up in a jiffy. I guess the beauty of this situation is that there's an element of customization? The guys who work here are plenty nice, the restaurant is clean, and the service is incredibly quick. It's definitely one of my favorite places to go for a quick meal on that stretch of Chestnut!

The manager Derek here is one of the most caring managers I have ever spoken too. We ordered on grubhub and after waiting an hour and a half, I called to see where our food was. I learned it was grubhub's fault and the food has been ready. Derek apologized for all us having to wait so long and offered to remake our food when the driver got there.

I couldn't wait to try these burgers and I was not disappointed. 

I ordered a Shake Stack which is the combination of a Cheese burger and 'Shroom burger. This included the Shake sauce (which is delicious), a portabello mushroom, cheese, lettuce, and tomato. The flavors mixed so well together and it all tasted freshly made. The bread also tasted great.

The staff was very friendly and accommodating which made the experience better. 

Cons: 
-The dine-in area is small and it was very crowded. So patrons had to wait for seats before they could sit down to eat. 
-The fries aren't the best. They were a little cold when served and weren't like the ones I've seen in pictures. Not very flavorful. 
-If you do not like medium burgers make sure to state how you would prefer your burger cooked.

Overall it was a great place to dine-in for a good entree.

I wish I could rate this a half star. It took us over 30 minutes to receive our food despite repeated conversations with "managers". I gave this place two attempts and both times they messed up my order and took a long time to do it.

This was my first time at this location. After shopping in center city this was on my bucket list of places to go. Order to go. I ordered the shack cheese burger, two double cheese burger, one mushroom burger (the double - mushroom  and beef patty), fries an one soda.

My burger was great. The crinkle fries were not my fav but it was ok. The bad thing was I paid for the mushroom burger and got a cheese burger.

I was already home so I didn't want to go back into center city for one burger. Lol. The place is nice. Similar look to the KOP store but no parking here. Hard to find parking.

I will preface this with I have always loved this place, however, because of my experience last night and this morning I am truly frustrated. I ordered my usual salad to go and upon arrival home  , I found a long black hair mixed in my salad. I immediately called and explained the situation. After being on hold for 10 minutes I was offered  a refund. The person at the desk asked for my name, order, email and cell number and I was told to pick up my receipt slip verifying the refund any time the next day. This morning on my way to work I stopped to "pick up" the slip. After trying to quietly and calmly explain while I was there, the man taking orders asked for my name and order Quickly. There was no record of my refund, no receipt printed etc. I waited while he texted the manager for 15 minutes before I asked if he had heard anything. He did not bother to write any of my info again or give me an update. This was truly a terrible experience and they have not handled this well. I would appreciate a resolution. Whitney Congress

In my opinion there are two types of chipotle employees: the ones who scoop deep, and the ones who are dead to me. Haha fortunately they are not skimpers over here!!

I'm a shameless chipotle addict, similar to many others I'm sure. Luckily for my mid-section, my new apartment is a little more of a hike from here. The line is always pretty long, being smack dab in the middle of bustling midtown village, but this location is just as, if not more, efficient and I'm never in line more than 5 mins, even if the line is all the way around the place. 

I just can't stay away, so I'm happy to say this is a clean, happy, quick location with plentiful seating where I can fill all of my greatest chipotle desires!

This place is tops.
I ordered a ziggy burger, sweet potato fries, and kale lemonade (ok, and i also ordered the choc milkshake) and it was all delicious. The burger was a lot tastier and more substantial than the hashbrown-consistency burgers i have gotten at other places that serve vegetarian burgers. This burger was juicy too. The sweet potato fries were amazing. The kale lemonade had a good, familiar taste--a very pleasant drink. The milkshake was right on.
Oh and the staff were super friendly.
They are super friendly. The "plant manager" ran food that was forgotten out to our car for us. Great service and good food....it's not steak and lobster. But not too shabby for vegan

I was in Philadelphia again waiting to go Home on the Train.  Since the NE corridor and Acela trains don't originate in Philly, they're often late to 30th St.  Yes, my train was late.  Thankfully, Jersey Mike's was there to save the day.  I had time to get a sub to take home south of the Mason-Dixon Line where getting a good quality Italian is more difficult.  I don't know if they have a jingle.  If not, I'll get working on Jersey Mike's song.
