I got the Chicken Teriyaki set. The food was ok, but nothing remarkable or notable. Maybe if you're nearby and dont have many options or just want something quick and easy to grab and go. But if you do have more time, I recommend going some place else for lunch/dinner.

What a tease. The menu looked great, but the product wasn't. Easily the worst burger I've ever had.

This burger stall drew me for its advertising of local beef and offered some tempting  combinations of beef, sauces, onion rings, mushrooms, cheeses etc. I ordered a mushroom and cheddar burger (medium) with mushroom sauce (no bun) and pickled veggies as a side.

The grille is visible and I saw 6 cooked burgers off to the side. When the cook took one and plopped it on the grille, I assumed he was doing a final heating of someone else's order- imagine my disappointment when I realized it was becoming my order. Who knows how long that precooked burger had been sitting there? Then I saw American cheese get dropped on top. Again, thought "Must not be my cheddar burger" until he then put it on lettuce rather than a bun. It sat on the counter a while, while he did other stuff. All I was waiting on was the pickled veggies which took some time to round up. 

During this time, my friends had gotten their own food at other places and were waiting for me at the table, and there was no way there was time for him to re-do the order without inconveniencing my companions, so I took it without complaint. Big mistake.

The mushroom sauce had been forgotten. The undersized burger was topped with just the unwanted American cheese and a few mushrooms. Despite my ordering "medium" and the burger having been on the grill twice, the center was close to raw.

The pickled veggies (just cukes and red onions) might have made up for the burger debacle because the serving was generous, but the pickling tasted "off" and the cukes were limp.

Overall: nice concept meets nasty reality and reality won, ugh. This food court has many options; look elsewhere.

This place rules.

Came across it totally by accident but walked in because it smelled so good. Filling portions, friendly people, fast service, delicious teriyaki.

Pretty much the only fast food place I will let my kid eat at.
The kids meal with 4 nuggets, fresh fruit and lowfat milk is a pretty safe option.

You can get a grilled chicken sandwich (they charge extra for a whole wheat roll).

You can get a side salad but it's loaded with shredded cheese which I try to pick off.  I sometimes get a diet lemonade.

Not too bad.  But it's still fast food.

Great fast food place. My go to orders are either the lamb kebab roll, chicken tika roll or spice end platter. Food is fast and fresh as well as extremely tasty. The owners are also super friendly and great people. This place is open late and a perfect cure for late night munchies. Top notch food that is served fast, but is also very good.
I had al pastor salad bowl with red salsa. Very good. I wanted to give 5 stars but they don't have carnitas, which surprised me because I went there 11:30 AM

This was my first visit to a Corner Bakery. After searching for places near my gym for an adequate breakfast, I settled on this location because of the breakfast platters. I arrived at approximately 10:30am and was informed that they were out of potatoes, so I nixed the platter idea. I ordered a commuters croissant sandwich. A few minutes later while seated and waiting, I was informed that they were out of croissants as well. Not a good look on my first visit. The large Europa coffee was nice. The panini substitution was good. The prices are even better. And I liked the diner feel of the place. So, I may give the place a second chance.

Don't ask for a quesadilla. For starters, they do not know how to make them. My friend and I just stopped in since she wanted to try the new location. She ordered a chicken and cheese quesadilla, and the cheese was not melted at all, nor was it cut into triangles like at most other places. Just one big flat, unmelted tortilla with chicken and cheese. The gentleman who made the quesadilla also was noticeably annoyed that she had the nerve to ask if they make them. They could have told her no, and then she would have gotten a burrito, but instead they huffed and puffed and made her a bad quesadilla. When she got to the register she asked for a side of salsa, and got this response "We could give you salsa, but then we would have to charge you for a burrito". The manager then explained to my friend, in detail, that she could buy the salsa, but since they operate on a "point" system, they would need to charge her for a burrito instead of a quesadilla, should she get salsa. Since she was not getting rice, or beans, or corn, or sour cream with her meal, like she would have with a burrito, she might have considered this, but she declined. Chipolte has fantastic chicken (on this quesadilla in fact- it was awesome), incredible quacamole, and they can make a mean burrito. So in short, go here for a burrito, but don't try to branch out too much.

Love everything from the food to the decor! Great location in the city. The staff was very nice, good recommendations, and may I say the best shake shack burger I've had because in my opinion they're usually too greasy but this one was perfect! Free wifi too! Personally, I like it way more than In-n-out.

So I never got to the Shake Shack in NYC but had heard amazing things.  When I found one was coming down the street I was super excited.  I went shortly after opening and have been back a few times experience remains the same...  The burger is tasty. The fries crispy.  Watch out for the 'Shroom burger... the molten cheese and juice get ya every time.

The one thing they have are the ice cream concoctions called "concretes"  if your in the neighborhood it is worth a shot.  However if your in Northern Liberties or South Philly not worth the drive or walk.

Jimmy John's is, simply, wonderful. The staff here are incredibly friendly and I love how they get so excited whenever anyone orders a pickle. Even at lunchtime when they are the most crowded, they always make their good quickly and get the line down. 

Not to be forgotten is the unwich--all the deliciousness of the sandwich and at least 1/2 off from the calories. That being said, the bread is delicious and I will often get day olds from here for only $0.49 if I need a baguette for something.

I can't believe I haven't written a review for Jimmy John's yet! It is just blowing my mind!

I get Jimmy John's at least once a week for my lunch at work. They must be sandwich magicians over there because I will literally pick up the phone, order, and POOF! Within 5 minutes the food is here, every time. Seriously...I have never waited more than 5 mins for my food. I am in love with them.

Go to: #9 Italian hoagie with added hot pepper and a side of bbq chips. Their bread is out of this world and the chips are extra crispy.

Feeling healthy? No problem! Get your favorite sandwich on a lettuce wrap instead of a hoagie roll.

Go Jimmy John's! I am a fan!

Seeing how this is a chain, I was not very excited to try the food. But my! was I surprised by the tender and juicy chick'n shack and their fries!
The bun was soft and ready to melt in the mouth.  It kept the best things together - chicken, mayo and pickles. 
I also liked the fact that it did not overwhelmingly fill me up.

The place is not crowded at all and I liked their no hassles buzz system to call out when the order is ready. 

Paid Parking is available across the street and ample bike locking stations just outside shake shack.

Food was delicious (as always). My only gripe is parking (limited in the area) and cleanliness. The other locations I've been to have at least one employee that goes through the restaurant and wipes down tables after each use and cleans up as needed. However, I didn't see one here. Other than that the staff were nice and our food came out in a timely manner.
It is so hard living down the street from The Shack!!! We stop in here at least once a week for some of those melt in your mouth burgers and fries. I can't live without their concrete shakes, too.

Spice End, you are good Indian food but it makes me worry when I order the chicken biryani platter and more than once, have to stop chewing because there are small bones in the food! Come on guys, I like knowing my chicken is fresh and not the processed meat but can you try not to be sloppy and leave bone in there? I'd appreciate that!

I got the Smokehouse Burger, he got the Chopped Med Salad - half romaine lettuce, half spinach. Both were sooooo good!! Everyone at the S Broad Street location was so nice. I'll be back if and when I come back to Philly!

One person's junk (food) is another person's treasure. Or should I say drunk food? That's exactly how it went down last night at Shake Shack. 

We stopped into Shake Shack for a late night bite. My husband and I both went for variations of the hamburger. I wanted mine with cheese without the tomato and ShackSauce. He wanted his without cheese or ShackSauce with the tomato. Another person in our group also ordered a burger, yet ordered it differently from us. A little complex, do you still follow me? 

Well I was super impressed that the employee at the register took the time and effort to confirm the specific orders. How many times has your burger order been messed up in your lifetime? I can't even count mine, but I know the number is large. 

So back to my initial point, I was happy as a clam with my burger. I knew it wasn't gourmet but the greasy goodness was perfect for a late night bite. My husband was completely grossed out by the greasiness of his burger, perhaps he needed another beverage to help make his late night grub a little more enjoyable. 

The Shack Shake burgers aren't gourmet but can hit the spot during an appropriate moment. My food was three stars, but I'll give it the extra star for excellent service for a fast food joint.

Great place, but I took a star away for inconsistency.  Sometimes they give a good amount for your money with the burrito bowl, other times they barely fill it.  Also, they run out of ingredients often.

After a few memorable trips to locations in NYC, hubby and I ventured out to philly's very first Shake Shack.  Since I am 9 months pregnant, we planned ahead and arrived there at 3:30 pm in hopes of avoiding a long wait.  We are obviously geniuses since we only waited 10 min in line to order then another 10-15 to get the food. 

I got my usual single shack burger with a root beer and hubby got a double hamburger.  We split a side of cheese fries and I got the coffee malt shake for dessert while he got half order of the Liberty Place concrete.  We sat in a nice booth and dug in.  The burgers were really juicy and yummy but the patties were thicker and less crusted than we had in NYC before so we we were a little disappointed.  As a root beer lover, my root beer was super crisp and refreshing.  The fries were not greasy at all which was great and cooked to perfection.  We both loooooved the desserts we got - thick, flavorful and quality. 

The service was really great as many have commented here already. 
Their price point is definitely high ($31 for our meal) but you shouldn't eat this meal too often anyway :) It's a heavy hitter fo sho.

Their food is good, no doubt. But they often run out of food. I just waited on a long line only to be told they only had half of the menu in stock. I understand running out of food, but don't waste my time if you were unable to accurately predict the amount of food you would need.

The line is too long and it moves slow. The server's are not smiling they look like they don't want to be there and they were too slow on the trays of food. The restaurant looks great and clean but there team or of general tsos Chechen before they cook more. It's not in the best of areas as well.

I've been to NYC several times but never made it to Shake Shack. When I heard they were putting one in Philly I got very excited. 

I came here with a good friend after he won about a grand at Harrah's on the poker tables. I suggested that he buy us dinner with his big winnings and where better to go than the newly opened Shake Shack.

I ordered the double SmokeShack burger with applewood smoked bacon, chopped cherry pepper, and shack sauce (burger was perfectly cooked and very juicy with high quality meat). We split an order of crinkle cut fries (frozen fries but they were crispy when we got them). I also ordered a strawberry shake and it was so creamy and delicious. 

This is a place to come when you're in the mood for a classic burger experience.
Its not the best burger I've ever had, but I would put it in the same class as In-N-Out and Five Guys. I'm already planning my next trip here...four days after my first visit!!

If you want the best salad, go to Corner Bakery!  It is reasonably priced.

You order, get a number, sit and wait for the runner to bring your food.  Be sure you grab your utensils though when you get your beverage.  It gets very busy at lunch, so get there early to guarantee a table.  Also outdoor dining in the summer months.

The menu offers so much, but I must admit that I have only eaten salads there.

I am really addicted to these kati rolls. Like, I find myself waking up and craving them. I want it for lunch, dinner, late night drunk meal... all the time. There was a point I had to limit myself to only come here once a week. It's actually scary. 

I love cheese. A lot. The paneer tikka and achari paneer rolls make me close my eyes and die every time I eat one. Aloo paneer hits the spot when I want a little potato. I put lots of white sauce and red sauce on every single bite and savor these babies til the end. I'm getting creepy now I think.

I want to try the rice dishes, but I can never resist getting a roll. I'm so happy this place is 2 blocks from work. Can't wait to eat my next one!!

For those of you who are unfamiliar, Taiwanese Popcorn chicken is a special style of chicken that you eat from a bag with wooden skewers, street-food style. It's a special craving in and of itself. At Chi Ken, it costs $5 for a bag of popcorn chicken, and there are 3 flavors available (original, garlic, and curry). Fair warning, not much difference between the original and garlic flavors. They also offer chicken cutlets, fried squid, and bento boxes if you're looking for more than a snack.

However, there were some serious RED FLAGS:
1. Worst offense: They offer a 5% discount for a 5-Star rating on Yelp. I can't respect a place that tries to buy ratings like that - that is invalidating the entire purpose of Yelp.
2. They refuse to give you a cup of water - you can either opt to purchase a drink or pay $1 for a measly cup of water. Excuse my French, but that's bullshit. Offering your customers water is a common courtesy, and charging $1 for a measly cup is ridiculous. I understand trying to make money but this is so obviously taking advantage of customers.
3. Staff is RUDE AF. Especially re: water situation. When I asked for water, the waiter said "ONE DOLLAR. NO PAY, NO WATER." then promptly turned around and walked into the kitchen. Kthxbye. Not going to pay for your creepy naked man/woman-shaped bottles of cryptic fluid. Need proof? Scroll down and look for Mandy W's 1-star review and the owner's horrible response, accusing Mandy of making things up.

The only reason I'm not rating this place a 1/5 is because their popcorn chicken is really quite 
good. But the red flags I've mentioned are INEXCUSABLE. Despite my cravings, I refuse to give my business to such a stingy, petty establishment that clearly does not value their customers. I will not be returning and DO NOT recommend this place.

Love shake shake. Great simple burgers. Excellent fries.
I eat here frequently and always use the app. A few times recently my app malfunctioned and my order went through twice. Both times I was easily refunded the extra charge and the second time the manager went above and beyond to right it which I wasn't looking for or expecting. But it was really nice of her. Great service all around.
I hate this place with a passion.  why do they make me go here why why why. Owners when are you going to fire these idiots and hire real workers.

Ok so I don't usually eat fast food or review it on yelp but I reallllllllllllllly had to because this place KILLED the fast food game! I mean the service was slow for how little people were in there on a Sunday afternoon, but otherwise, it was AMAZING.

The environment was typical fast food chain, but it was clean and tidy. Nothing was out of place. The staff were very friendly. I have never eaten at a popeyes before so I really didn't know what to expect. I ordered like the 8 piece family meal for me and friends with biscuits and mashed potatoes and gravy. We also got one of those oreo cream pie things. 

The chicken- holy heck for fast food fried chicken it was moist and tender and delicious. I mean I was truly surprised how much I enjoyed it.

The biscuits- moist and fluffy and buttery. I mean I could have eaten 10 of them. 

The mashed potatoes and gravy- for fast food mashed I was impressed. They were not dry or bland, they had flavor and would so good. I wasn't a huge fan of the gravy solely for the fact it wasn't my taste palate. Otherwise A+.

All in all this gets five yassssss's out of five from me and if you are looking for cheap, fast food fried chicken with friendly staff- go here!

The food at Panada Express on Aramingo Ave is really good but the service is beyond terrible. I ordered some food around 9:30 and I am just now receiving my food at 10:20pm. This is utterly ridiculous. I don't think  I'll ever go back there until I know the service is 100% better than what I experienced.

This place needs to be shut down, it is so dirty and gross.  The tables and are so dirty with left over food, ketchup, salt, pepper, and who knows what else.  The staff was beyond rude and ignorant.  It was like we were annoying them by even being in there.  The also had rap music blasting on the TV when we walked in which in my opinion was not family friendly at all.  After seeing how they handled the food in the back and how and carless the staff was in the kitchen we decided to leave and go else were.  I will never in my life go to this locatation.

Taste wise the food was pretty good, but for the price, it wasn't very filling, ended up going to five guys to get another burger. I don't like the carry out set up, it's just sitting in a tray, inside of a bag, uncovered. Which was extra bad cuz I had to walk 3 blocks in the cold before I was able to sit down and eat it
Anaheim was good and I did it with chicken . Worth the cost of $ 6.43. Lot's of seating!

Went to this Wendy's for Chicken Sandwich today and got more then I bargained for, rude drive through guy/girl (I swear I couldn't tell) I ended getting the meal and I thought "boy does my diet coke taste a little off" well since it 90 some degrees out I figured I'd still drink it! Well 2 sips later something horrible entered my mouth! I spit it out onto the drink and to my surprise it looked like either some kind of bleach pellet or a sanitizer disk. Well after spitting washing my mouth out brushing and a 2 minute throw up session. I figured I should call them so they don't poison a little kid or something. 1st girl who answered the phone was an idiot (and that's putting it nicely) she said they don't have bleach or sanitizer in the store at all. (If that's true then it is very disturbing). Asked to speak to a manager who told me she didn't really believe me! (Wasn't looking for anything just maybe "oh sorry let us check so we don't kill someone!") do yourself a favor and go somewhere else for the love of God! I will try to post the picture of my drink with whatever shit was inside of it.

We walked in at 11 am on the dot and were told breakfast is over. They should really extend the breakfast hours!  This is really a two star review but I'll throw in an extra star because it's a vegan option in the city.  We tried the burger and it was awful - it tasted like a Boca burger.  If you're going to serve vegan burgers and you're using pre made frozen stuff we can get in the supermarket at least price it accordingly.  Super disappointing experience.  The iced tea pre sweetened with agave tasted awful. The cool thing is seating next door but wish they had a bathroom.

Great burger spot. I wouldn't call it "fast" food, we did have to wait about 5-10 mins, but they had a fairly large lunch crowd. Anyway, I prefer to wait for fresh food rather than a pre-made, wrapped up burger. If I wanted that, I'd pay less and go to McDonald's. 

For $25, we got two burgers, fries, cheese fries, a milkshake and an Iced Tea. Not too bad considering we'd probably pay $15 for crappy fast food burgers. 

The Shack Burgers were great. Lettuce, tomato, cheese and Shack sauce. Juicy, warm and flavorful. The fries were SO GOOD! I love a good crinkle fry, and when you cover it in cheese...well...I'm all in. It wasn't just regular old cheese whiz slathered on there, either. The sign said it was a homemade mix of Cheddar and American. As a cheese lover, I could not get enough!

Milkshake was good and I loved my Fifty-Fifty-- half Iced Tea, half Lemonade.

They had a little bit of everything-- even snacks for your dog! I don't have a dog, but I see dog-lovers in the city just loving this. 

Their frozen custard selection looked great. Would definitely love to stop in here for dessert sometime.

And lastly, they serve booze! Draft beer, bottled beer and wine. Always a plus!

Fack this place. srsly. I kind of love Taco Bell every now and again, but this one can suck a big fat one.

it cost more to get a burrito "fresco" style and all it means is that they aren't giving you cheese. Dude, you're charging me more for less? I wonder which MBA program the manager went through to figure that one out. 

Anyway, they made my order wrong. twice. And all I asked was for a bean burrito without cheese....

Coreanos has got to be the best place in Chinatown Square! I'm a fan of fusion food in general, but Korean-Mexican fusion is my personal favorite. They have salad bowls available, but it's clearly all about the tacos at this joint!

Tacos at $9-10 for 3, which is a reasonably good deal. My boyfriend and I ordered the Double-Fried Chicken Tacos and the Bulgogi Tacos. Both were amazing - packed with flavor and piled with toppings! The Double-Fried Chicken tacos combine Korea's famous double-fried chicken with a southwestern twist. The Bulgogi tacos showcase classic Bulgogi (slightly sweet, soy-marinated beef), sticking to mostly Korean flavors (like a gochujang sauce), but served in a soft-shell corn taco.

I'm all about the flavors Coreanos offers, and I will definitely be back for more tacos soon!!

Gets a bit crowded during noon lunch rush. Seating is in a hotel lobby, so people are constantly walking in and out. But there's ample seating. Have to ask for key for hotel restroom. So, all of that is a bit of a pain. But maybe familiar to Philly residents. 

But, it is worth it for the food!  The Philly cheesesteak didn't look like much at first. But, I devoured it. And it was plenty by itself. But, once I tried one of my husband's sweet potato fries, I ate half of those. So dang delicious!  You will get full. And it's all a bit greasy. So, remember vegan and vegetarian food isn't automatically healthy or low fat.

The food here has been consistent, but I'm really baffled at the service. When someone orders online, and shows up to pick it up, why would it take longer to get that order (much longer) than new customers who have come in and ordered? I sat and watched people come in, wait in line, order, and get their food multiple times before mine came up.

I asked the manager about it, and he said that it takes at least a half hour to process the order. What? It takes a half hour to process a pre-paid sandwich? It just doesn't compute.

Finally got around to visit Shake Shack!  My husband and I headed over for a late lunch on Labor Day- the holiday and the rain held off the crowds- we only waited about 5 minutes to order.  I went with the Shack Burger, he went with the Smoke Shack and we shared an order of fries and an Abita Root Beer. Total order was about $18.  Wait time for our meal after ordering was about 10 minutes.

I'm going to start with service- the employees here ROCK.  And I don't use that praise lightly because many fast-casual establishments have employees that act as though they'd rather get run over by a truck than serve you your moderately priced lunch.  But at Shake Shack, everyone seems really excited and friendly.  It was refreshing

Now I didn't try the shake (will do so on my next trip- I promise!) but the burger was worth the trip.  Super juicy and flavorful, great meat-to-bun ratio (I like when the patties are on the thinner side) and tasty toppings.  The lettuce and tomato were nice and fresh and crisp.  The fries didn't wow me.  They were over-salted versions of the fries my mom would cook for me in the oven when I was a kid.  Tasty, sure, but wouldn't make me go out of my way for them.  The Abita root beer was great but at $2.65, I wish I had realized they had free tap water in the back.  Dang!

Overall, this spot is pretty legit.  Not sure if I'd wait in line for an hour for it (I'd probably head over to 500 degrees if I saw that line) but it was a nice visit and the food was good.

I've tried the hot dog, hamburger and cheeseburger here, all were good but the cheeseburger was my favorite.  The burger is tasty, a little but not overly greasy, and cooked well.  The service was pretty quick, about a 5-7 minute wait.  The cashiers here seem friendly and somewhat efficient, and the grub is pretty good!  Definitely satisfies a hankering for a burger!

I went to this McDonald's a few days ago, and you really don't want to sit in there and eat, it's better for you to get your food on the go, because there is a lot of people in there that will be asking you do u have change to get something to eat, and homeless people in there, the service is ok, but it could be better, customers should not be hearing the employees personal business out loud.

If i could give this location a 0 star I would. I waited patiently to order on the line. Once I was called to order the african American woman at the register she had some sort of orange brown wig idk but she was rude as hell. Banging on the register, trying to rush me with my order. She kept giving me an attitude to the point where I said forget it walked away and ordered on the machine instead. I like to order with people ca the machines because that's how we keep people with jobs but clearly this woman doesn't want her nor does she need it because she really isn't professional. She lacks the skills or costumer service and should be left to continue mopping floors and taking out the trash. She should
Not have any interactions with costumers because she doesn't have the skills too. 

Waited over 40 mins for my food and once received the fries were cold & another woman at the counter simply apologized. They didn't give me a cup for my soda, I had to ask for it. She gave a large instead of a medium (I guess because of the long wait).

stopped here for lunch today and i really enjoyed my chicken pepper thai noodles! it was really flavorful and everything was cooked really well. my only wish was that i wish the noodles retained more of the sauce, they were still pretty white when i got them. i like my noodles to be drunk with sauce! the 2 men in the truck were so nice and the truck itself was so cute with flowers all around it. 

for those that are having some trouble locating it, it's located right across from dilworth park, on 15th next to TD bank!

In general, don't know what all the hype is about. Ordering was easy but it did take a while for the food to be ready. Serving sizes are small for its price and taste is average. I much prefer In-N-Out over shake shack.
My coworker and I went to Shake Shack during lunch and we all liked what we had ordered. I had their hot dog with cheese fries and it was delicious! Super fast and friendly service!

Corner Bakery is across the street from my office building, so it's naturally become a part of my midday noshing rotation. It isn't bad or amazing, just in-between, predictable, just fine for lunch. 

The bad: coffee isn't great; turkey sandwich on pretzel with caraway studded Havarti just had a bad flavor because of the caraway overload; baked goods - ehh, just not worth it to me.

The good: my go-to is the Asian Wonton Salad, which is pretty tasty and high quality with roasted chicken, edamame, cherry tomatoes, cucumbers, red bell peppers, carrots, green onions, cilantro, and crispy wontons with mixed greens, napa cabbage, and ginger soy dressing.

It's usually pretty chaotic and busy in here, and sometimes their order-then-wait-until-your-number-is-called system can get crazy and confusing, but I've never had a problem getting the correct order.

Coreanos is without a doubt a hidden gem in Philly.  I am a taco fanatic, and I truly believe that you cannot find better tacos around.  David, the creator and owner, has really created some amazing food.  The first time I came with friends and we all tried different tacos.  I had the carnitas tacos and fell in love.  They are so juicy and flavorful.  They are hands down the BEST (and I'm not embellishing) the BEST carnitas I have ever had.  The salsa verde has the perfect amount of heat and freshness that breaks though the juice in the carnitas, and the Daikon Kimchi adds the perfect crunch.  The flavors mesh PERFECTLY.  I dream about these tacos.  The second time I went I tried the Bulgogi and the double fried chicken tacos as well as the carnitas tacos during their AWESOME happy hour special (4:30-7 everyday each taco is $2.50!!). Everything was phenomenal.  David really has a great sense of flavor!  The Bulgogi taco had the perfect balance of spice and sweetness, and the meat was chopped in perfect bites.  The ratio of meat to vegetables was perfect!  Every bite was so delightful.  The double fried chicken taco is a MUST.  The chicken once again was in PERFECT bite sized pieces and was so so so crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside.  It is the ultimate piece of fried chicken.  The white rice is such a great foundation for the taco in the tortilla.  Its adds an extra layer of texture and and taste that brings the whole dish together and the corn salsa I could eat with a spoon.  OMG what fantastic seasoning!  All of the tacos are served on two layers of the tastiest soft shell corn tacos.  I have never been disappointed by the service or the food.  It is such a cool spot and I look for every excuse to go!  If you don't eat here you are really missing out!

We stopped in for a quick lunch in the midst of shopping on Chestnut Street.  We opted for the chicken and egg kati roll, which was surprisingly light and tasty, with just the right amount of spice.  The chicken was moist and perfectly cooked, and complemented well by the coriander mint chutney.  All of this at a reasonably priced $11 for two rolls.

For the love of Jesus and all of the Fast food Gods... This place was excellent. Fast and friendly service mixed with juicy burgers and cheese fries. It was my first time and I have to say it was one of the better burgers I've had in some time. I felt like Homer Simpson at...the Shake Shack. (Hmmmmmmmm....burrrrgggerrr)
Worse service ever! They always forget something in the drive thru and the inside employees are rude as hell.

I'm Gonna make this review quick because I hated everything about this place although unlikE a lot of other people I didnt wait in much of a line so I'm just gonna break it down

Bun--McDonald's 
Meat--cheaper than McDonald's 
Toppings--had the hot?? And it was a bunch of red crap that we will call peppers I also had a concrete?? And it was nothing special what makes me most upset is the bill came to 12 bucks and Wendy's is much better and it would've only cost me 2.00

When I arrived in 30 stations, I notice that this was one of the few establishment that was open early in the morning, so I went to Jersey Mike and I saw the great diversity 
 of the menu and Affordable prices, I decide to give this a chance.

Of course, if you go to Philly there one thing that you most eat and that is the Cheesesteak. 

I order the Chipotle Cheesesteak wit and Bacon! with was delicious,  I personally really enjoyed the chipotle cheesesteak, with was super cheesy, slightly salty, and bacon was very good. The portion of ingredients on the sandwiches was a lot, that very time a had a bite some of then drop on the plate. I will come more to give a taste to the others type of Cheesesteak, but the coffee was back, I recommend go in front to DD.
Terrible service and low quality ingredients! This establishment would receive better reviews if they employed capable workers. Chipotles in the suburbs are far superior! Not coming back!!!

This place use to have to best chicken ever but over the years they fell off big time the chicken is to grease and salt but some people still like eating there my favorite chicken place now is popeyes!

The quality of the burger is consistent here with other locations. But man, the service is really challenged. I really get the impression that the crew must be highly stressed and underpaid. Every time I come here, I'm either missing an item from my order, or the toppings on the hamburger are completely wrong, which is surprising given that I point to each and every one of the toppings on the menu and say "everything please." I'll still continue to come here because the food is tasty, but I really hope that the employees here really have everything they need to succeed. It's a tough job, especially with these crazy long lines.

Wow! This place recently opened up on Lancaster, and I'm impressed! From the super kind cashier, letting us try the dessert option (galatoboureko) to the huge platters, I can already tell this place will fit right in the neighborhood. 

I got the bifteki platter and tried the gyro platter. The bifteki is stuffed with cheese, which made the flavor awesome, but the best deal was the gyro! The meat was sliced thin, but piled high with mounds of spicy feta/tzaziki, plus perfectly oiled potatoes or french fries. Also, a side salad, if you like that! 

Calamari was good perfectly cooked, but a little on the small side for the price. Heard that the tiramisu was good too. 

From my group, I heard that this was the closest tasting Greek food in authenticity to real stuff, and I agree that the spit has great flavor, the meat is well cooked, and the staff is ready to make your night great and fix you a meal you deserve! Head in on weeknights late, or try it for lunch! Can't wait to try the other Greek dishes they have on the menu.

I haven't had a bad experience at this Wendy's, located at Academy Plaza.. The service is adequate and polite. I stop here when I need to go to Beneficial Bank. There is also a Rita's, Dunkin' Donuts, and an Acme in the plaza. There is plenty of parking. 

So stop by and take advantage of their dollar menu (including fries, soda, chicken sandwich, or jr. bacon cheeseburger).

I chose to wait in the line, so I'll save all the negative comments about how long the line is.  I knew what I was getting into, and I came prepared to wait.  

I've been waiting to try Shake Shack since I hiked with three NYC inhabitants in Peru, and for 3 days on the trail all they did was talk about the best burgers, fries and shakes in the WORLD from this glorious place called Shake Shack.  

Two years later, one opens in Philly.  Dream.  Come.  True.  
Only it didn't.  

After ordering my burger, fries, shake and a diet coke (I'm a thirsty girl), the polite man behind the counter said "$17.34 please."  No, no, sir - I don't want all the burgers you have in the establishment.  Just ONE.  And this is the price.  

I was sad to fork over $17, but I was still excited about what was coming.  And then it came.  The burger was fine.  The fries were good.  The shake was ok.  Are any of them, respectively, the best anything I've ever had?  No.  Were they worth $17?  No.  

I might go back here, but my expectations are to get an ok burger, ok fries, and an ok shake, but pay BEST-EVER pricing.

It's your standard Jimmy Johns experience. The service was quick and nice however my sandwich (veggie) was very low on vegetables. If I'm paying $7+ for a tiny sandwich I'd appreciate more than a few pieces of vegetables. However I will probably return if I ever crave Jimmy Johns!
Standard take out for a late night in the office.  Aloo paneer is so good.  Really haven't had a bad meal here.

It's a Wendy's. Ya know, fast food and whatnot. Unhealthy food that many Americans eat because it's something quick, tasty, and filling.

Anywho, I've never had problems with this Wendy's. Staff's always cool, my order's are always correct, and there's never any gross things in my food or anything like that (knock on wood).

A surprising disappointment.  Came to the Shake Shack on a super hot day to satisfy my curiosity craving for a concrete.  There was no wait in the C-line.  Tried the soft philly pretzel concrete.  The description sounded amazing.  However, the product was utterly disappointing.  It came in a cup with the messy custard already having melted down the sides and it was already partially liquified.  I thought they were called "concretes" because the custard stayed near solid in the process and you could turn the cup upside down?  Apparently not.  The "pretzel" pieces are terrible.  No self-respecting Philadelphian would call them pretzels.  They have to go.  The unmelted vanilla custard, however, was good.

My first time trying Jersey Mikes! Wow, I've been missing out (this chain isn't readily available where I've lived) but I'll certainly track it down when traveling now. Freshly sliced cold cuts make all the difference, and the portions are extremely generous for the price. I enjoyed the club and will probably skip the bacon next time (I don't really enjoy crispy bacon which is what they used). 

Also, I appreciated the sandwich options- not too few, not too many with a manageable number of toppings to choose from.

This place is the fucking worst. They gave me the wrong shit then say that's what I ordered. I ordered the number 10. They give me a sausage egg biscuit. Places in the hood are the worst. I hope they close down. Then they always ask off your paying with cash or credit. What difference does it make? What till I get up there and find out.

I saw Danny Meyer's interview on CBS. Could someone please tell him that the burgers and fries are too salty even when you request no salt and wait the extra time? Also I want a large diet soda not a baby sized one. This isn't NYC we can order large sodas here in Philadelphia because Philadelphia is not a nanny city. Please take note chain restaurants that you need to adjust  to the city not the other way around!
Pretty solid, standard chipotle. I've always found the line moves, they are rarely out of ingredients and the service is friendly.
Food is too expensive for the portion and quality you get. Also, everything is SUPER salty.

Advertised as a shop to pick up meals that are very easy to prepare (just throw in the oven or microwave), and healthy, with all nutritional facts outlined. I have ordered multiple items from here - some, I would definitely re-order, some I'd stay away from. 
 
Atmosphere: It's laid out just like a section of the grocery market where you can buy microwaveables, but with nutritional facts outlined / standardized across all products. They offer more niche, healthy options, all labeled to accommodate dietary needs (e.g., paleo, keto, gluten free). Very friendly to different diet preferences, for sure!
 
Service: Honestly a big strength of this franchise. I've always had very pleasant experiences with the cashiers and workers at this location! They are very kind and willing to explain products to you.
 
Food: A few of the items I've tried - 

Romesco chicken/salmon: I personally recommend trying the romesco options: these sauces go well with the food, and add some creamy flavoring (though the naked options - no sauces - are probably healthier). I prefer these over the chimichurri options, though it depends on what flavor you're going for.

Barrel Creek Provisions Fermented Vegetables: Thought this was WAY too sour - I was surprised the cashier recommended drinking the juice! I took one sip and threw the rest out; way too difficult to drink, would not recommend. 

Little side-offering of steak: No flavoring at all on its own. I'd probably steer away from these, unless you have seasoning/sauces yourself to flavor this.
 
Rx butters - Good for when I have high sugar cravings, and keeping me from consuming mouthfuls of chocolate.

Side note: Get their app / be enrolled in the rewards program if you're a frequency visitor! The app allows you to order in advance to see if items are in stock, which is usually pretty accurate. There are a few locations scattered throughout the city, and they are sometimes stocked differently. When you enroll at first, they give you a few free items too (free breakfast options, generally)
 
Overall: 4/5 would still come back for some meals that I enjoy, but grocery store microwaveables are definitely more affordable (and there are definitely healthy options too). You'd have to consider if it's worth spending the money (a bit pricier) for food you're just going to microwave or toss in the oven.

It's shake shack what can I say? Tastes like every other shake shack. Fries are splendid, burgers are small, the custard is heavier than the cow it came from. If you are craving shake shack or just want to get a burger and fries, roll thru. It's a bit pricy for fast food but that's what you pay for quality.

Came in with some friends to satisfy our fried chicken craving. The restaurant was fairly clean and not too crowded around 8PM. The employee at the register was a bit incompetent and kept asking me to clarify my order despite me being as clear as possible and repeating it nicely. 

Regardless, our food cane out shortly, and all of it did satisfy Popeyes standards. I had ordered a 3-Piece Spicy Tender Meal with Cajun fries and a biscuit. I actually ended up getting 4 tenders in my box which was a pleasant surprise. The fries were crispy, the biscuit was great, and the chicken was delicious and flavorful.

The bathrooms I had expected to be a bit crummy were actually fairly clean. There is also a parking lot at this location despite it being in the city. Even though service wasn't the best ever, I was satisfied overall and enjoyed my food.

my daughter is vegan so I took her here last week after work. I got the smokehouse burger and OMG it was the best burger I ever had!!! Shameless to say I have went back two more times for it!! I can only image what everything else taste like but if you have never tried the burger I highly suggest you try it!!

Popped in here for lunch with some co-workers the other day. For walking in just after noon, it wasn't slam packed but it's also December and people are on PTO or checking out all the holiday stuff. I ordered a bowl of Broccoli Cheddar soup. It was good but seemed a little watery compared to some of my favorite broccoli cheddar soups that I have had in life. It's not a bad place to get a quick bite and it's affordable. Overall, just a-OK.

PURE ASS. 

Decided to hit this spot up after the gym while I used the Laundry Cafe nearby. Big mistake!
My chicken sandwich was hard and the Whopper was cold and crusty! I worked in a BK in high school and it was never like this. Prolly cause I care about food. 

This was like I was biting into Asscheeks. 
And I'm not talking like Rhianna cause I'd eat those cheeks viciously... 
I mean Hermit gamer in the basement of his moms house eating Cheetos and beating off wearing the same draws for a week type of ass. 

Don't go here.

I'm not usually a burger person but I would not pass up a burger from shake shack! It is always juicy when I ask for well done (who gets well done? ME!). I've been to two other locations, King of Prussia and Drexel campus. I prefer this location because of the fries. Always crispy and not greasy crinkle cut fries. The other two places serve thin, dry strips of potatoes. Service is always good and prices are not bad for the quality of food.

I FINALLY stopped in here today to check out all of the hype, and I am so happy that I did. I was seriously so enamored with everything Snap had to offer, from the entrees to the beverage choices to the snacks. If you like fresh convenience, this is your spot, without a doubt. I grabbed a matcha mint iced tea and it is really refreshing. I also got the "naked beef" with cauliflower and snap peas for dinner! A small is a great lunch portion, or maybe dinner if you are having something on the side. All of the food looked very fresh with clear "sell by dates." The workers were really friendly and efficient. They do not recommend freezing the meals, instead shopping every ~3 days for your weekly fix. 

Their rewards card sounds really legit. For every $1 spent = 1 point. When you hit 200 points, you get $10 off. For someone who is crunched for time often and does not want to cook for one, Snap kitchen is THE place. I am really looking forward to trying their entrees- all of them look really delicious!!

It's McDonald's, so I expect you have an idea what you are walking into. It's one of the original and most popular fast food joints in America, and has spread all over the world. You likely come here for fast and cheap burgers and fries. While they have expanded their menu, these are still the biggest draws.

From a taste standpoint, this McDs is just as good, or I should say the same, as any other spot. The service is pretty good. But you do need to check your order. I've had a couple of experiences here where they went a little shy on the fries. In other words, my medium sized fry box and a small order amount in it.

We came in for a quick bite tonight and got a chicken platter dish and veggie platter dish. It was flavorless, the rice was dry and had some very over cooked peas and strings of carrot in the rice but NO other vegetables except for a stingy few pieces of iceberg lettuce randomly sitting on top of the rice. The chicken actually had pieces of chicken. Some of the pita was wet and the part that wasn't wet was dry and brittle, ie: stale. $9.25 for each dish and it went right in the trash, it was that bad. 
Easily one of the worst meals I've had the 10 years I've lived in center city Philly.

Amazing, best burger I have ever had, awesome... and those were the comments from the table behind mine.

I have to say, the burger was amazing.  Sets a new standard.  The burgers and shakes were worth it.  The fries they were ok, nothing to write home about.  

The menu was confusing to me, so I just went up to the counter and told them what I wanted vs. trying to figure it out.  The woman working the counter was helpful and asked me a few questions to make sure I was getting what I was looking for.

I would recommend finding a seat right away after you order.  They give you a buzzer to pick up your order.  Seating is limited.

Corner Bakery is great if you want to get a light breakfast or lunch for an extremely affordable price. I ordered the egg and cheese on a panini with potatoes on the side. I thought it tasted pretty good, but I wish the portion size for the potatoes were a little more because it cost an additional $1 to include them.

The pastries that they carry are also really tasty and great to take on the go for a quick bite.

I will definitely go back because the price is great and they have a wide selection of breakfast items.

This place is a ripoff I asked for a two piece dinner with white meat spice with a side of coleslaw and another two piece dinner with white meat mild. They changed me for each piece of chicken separately and they didn't give me any sides. When I went back thinking they just forgot they told me no because I ordered white meat it's no longer a deal like this was my first time ordering this meal. They got me this time but never again KFC here I come
My new favorite place in Philly !! Reminded me of Mumbai street food. Go for the Kathi rolls, they are divine.
Stop by today, tried the beef tacos and was impressed. Cooked well, sauce on the tacos was great highly suggest giving it a go so head over to race street in Chinatown and give the place a shot!

Great food, poor seating. Get this to go.

I had the grilled boneless chicken and the fried pork dumplings. The chicken was well-marinated, crisp, and tender at the same time. Surprisingly good. The dumplings were outstanding - one of the best I've had in the city, much better than the dumplings at most ramen and Chinese restaurants.

My party wanted to dine-in but decided to take out instead. The door was wide open which made the restaurant way too chilly!
All my friends recommended this for me and now I will recommend it to others. I especially like the milkshake. Burgers are also good.

I'm not good at writing a review. Shake shack is definitely one of my fave burgers in philly. Love their burger and French fries . I haven't try their shake yet. Will definitely write another review once I try the shake

Terrible experience! My advice is to hire new adult workers who know something about some kind of customer service...or perhaps provide training or better yet DONT hire them if they don't care. 

They were out of fajita vegetables and brown rice at 8:30pm and were incredibly rude. Also, apparently there is no manager when I asked to speak with one.

Worst customer service!

I'm soooo happy that Shake Shack brought in a little bit of Manhattan into Philly. I can finally tell my friends on the west/best coast that Philly has something that manhattan has! Now I'm just waiting for an In-N-Out to open in Philly.

But back to the food- In terms of fast food burgers IMHO this is the best that it gets anywhere in the United States.  

Food: 
ORDER THE BURGERS. ESPECIALLY THE **SHACKBURGER**
-The Meat is nomlicious. It's literally like an orgasm in your mouth.... No wait that sounds wrong- It's literally like your mouth is orgasming. 
- Veggies are fresh, not Cali fresh, but still pretty fresh. 
FRIES are good when fresh, CHEESE FRIES are heavy, but pretty good. 
SHAKES are alright - they are fast food shakes, so don't be surprised if shake shack doesn't turn out shakes as good as a real burger+shake diner would. 

Ambiance. 
Place is clean and modern looking, People there are chill. 

Service 
Fast, Nice, and Polite. I was about to stand up and take my tray to the trash and one of the shake shake guys called me a "SIR" and offered to do it for me. This has never happened to me at any Fast Food Burger joint. Props Shake Shack Phlly. Props. 

Anyways, if you're a burger connoisseur you gotta try this place. 

Here's my ranking for the UPPER ECHELON of Fast-Food burger joints btw
Burgers/ Meat quality: (Best) Shake Shack , In-N-Out , Five Guys (Worst)
Price: (Least expensive) In-N-Out , Shake Shack , Five Guys (Most expensive)
Fries + Freshness: (Best) In-N-Out , Shake Shack , Five Guys (Worst)
I only tried two things here - tofu wrap was WAY TOO SALTY and the side Asian salad has a weird after taste.  May try breakfast but stay away from these two items!

This place has since repurposed itself to be a teriyaki bowl instead of a ramen place. I think it's a good move. The chicken teriyaki is much better than the ramen that they had before here. 

The chicken thighs are grilled and comes with rice and a side of potato salad.  I probably should've opted for the side salad instead. Odd combo with potato salad. The chicken was a little dry, but there's enough sauce to make it tasty. Sauce is good. You can taste the ginger in there. 

Would come back.

I've been waiting to find a good Kathi Roll place in Philadelphia, and finally I moved to Center City and happened across Spice End the other day. Unfortunately, it looks like my search has to continue.

Don't get me wrong, Spice End is good. They have a decent selection of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian rolls, but the prices are a tad high and the rolls themselves aren't anything too special.

I tried the paneer tikka roll (cottage cheese with spices), the paneer and aloo (cottage cheese with potatoes), the egg roll, and the mixed vegetable roll. Of the 4, my favorite were by and far the paneer tikka and mixed veggie. They were well spiced and good eats, but the heaping amount of dhania (cilantro) chutney put over top was very off-putting. On my second visit I asked them to lessen the chutney amount, but it was still too much, and I wonder if they even made any changes.

In all, not bad, but the chutney ratio and generally high prices for the food make this an average place in my opinion. Kudos to them for having Limca - a nice refreshing lemon drink by Coca Cola more common to East Asia.

what can i say? tear it down. it smells. it looks dirty. it is dirty. the bathroom is so bad, it is not 1st world. health inspectors must be overlooking the place. the service is barely there. graffiti inside and out. broken everything. the place needs to be torn down and rebuilt.

Arrived hungry in philly close to midnight... this place totally hit the spot!! It is close to rittenhouse square, a quick walk from our hotel. The rolls are massive, pretty flavorful and deliver handsomely on the late night grease and carb ticket. Move over please Kati Roll NYC. Thank you. Recommend the achar chicken roll, lamb kabab roll and chicken tikka...
This is my first time been shake shack, it is great experience. Love the cheese burger and French fries. Service are great.

Went here with a couple of friends. I got the Rittenhouse^2. A bit too many coffee beans, but otherwise, I was in chocolate heaven. I ordered fries too, and they were pretty good. I wish this place had more seating. We had to wait for a table to open up for ten minutes and the prices are a bit high. If I'm in the Rittenhouse Square area again and I'm hungry, I may go back, but Shake Shack wouldn't be my first choice.

I had been so excited that a Chipotle was opening up closer to me, and this Chipotle did not let me down. The line was pretty long as it was opening day, but the skillful burristas moved the crowd through quickly. My chicken and fajita veggie burrito bowl was delicious as usual, and now it's 4 blocks closer! Beware -- they may have a heavy hand on the sour cream so request only a little if that's your preference.

Maybe I'm too old for this joint....or I just remember actual burger shacks.  When I heard that people were lined up outside this place I thought I was missing out on it...or  just plain out of it.  Their burgers are on the smaller side, prepared only one way and yes good... good quality beef, but nothing memorable.  The fries are pretty pedestrian, certainly don't taste like fresh cut to me.  The veggie portabella burger was thin and  overly deep fried.  The shakes were good, but  the whole menu is premium price for slightly  above average fair.  I think 5 Guys is a far superior cholesterol laden experience.  On the plus side the building is ascetically pleasing and yes.....they have beer!

I wanted to give this a place a try for awhile now. Their choice of putting the plates on display outside the restaurant was a smart one. The giant fried squid looks especially appetizing. Upon entering the store however, you feel less inspired. I went there during the day time and maybe the lighting wasn't appropriately lit, but it feels dark and kind of sad. There wasn't a lot of customers or music or workers or anything really. 

The place is set up like a bubble tea joint. I thought it was a restaurant but it's more fast food, pay first, get order and sit down. We ordered fried chicken bento and braised pork on rice. The waitress didn't really know her menu so we decided to stick with the basics. The food itself wasn't bad, although nothing spectacular. The braised pork on rice was good and decent for the price. The fried chicken however, was much smaller than what's displayed outside. The chicken was a bit undercook as well. Note that any sauce to go with your meal will cost an extra .25 cents. While it's a small deal, I'd prefer them to add this cost to the actual meal. It's like paying for ketchup when you buy fries, it's really unnecessary.

Overall, the food is ok, had this been anywhere else, I would've given a higher score. In Chinatown however, the competition is strong and Chi Ken is simply not up to par. There are just so many good places around, I can't recommend going here especially. If you are curious or happen to park nearby, maybe come in for a small snack but save your stomach for better eateries elsewhere.

Somewhere between 3 and 4 stars.

Baseline: Kati Roll Company in NYC. My favorite there is the Unda Aloo, which is egg and potato in a kati roll. Spice End does a decent job, but the rolls are not quite as good as the place in NYC. The price is about the same as the one in NYC ... except this is Philly. In NYC these prices would be good; in Philly, they are a bit on the high end.

One area in which they are lacking is the potato roll. What really makes the potato roll sing is when there's a layer of egg, which costs an extra $1. The chicken tikka roll isn't bad, but it isn't anything special.

Bonus: they deliver, and they're open really late (3am or 4am many nights).

The cashier was very friendly nice and the service overall was great. Ordered the philly steak but wasn't a fan of the ketchup. I think I would have liked another item on the menu but I was excited to eat a "philly steak".

I get Spice End delivered on drunk nights and during late work nights. I would say 8 out of 10 times, it's amazing! I highly suggest ordering the Spice End Platter (spicy), Chicken n Egg Roll (w extra red and white sauce), and Chhaas (request it to be cold, trust me) to quench your thirst from all that spicy flavor :)
If I order a sandwich with avocado and the avocado is actually nice and ripe rather than hard and unripened, as is generally the case, I'm happy.

Sorry to say!! I had two bad expeirences here. I tried this place twice and here is what happened. The first time the ground lamb had bone fragments in it. There was enough to prompt me to let the staff know about it. They just opened at the time and they were very apologetic. I was looking to give constructive feed back when they asked how was my meal. I went back today and there was a string in my chicken roll probably from a kitchen towel. I pulled it out of the roll it was about 4 inches long. I explained to the gentleman behinde the counter this was the second time and showed him the string and again a very nice appologie. I just will not go back and felt I should share this information maybe the mgt will read this and do better QA in the kitchen.
Another example of excessive stupidity. These employees cant make correct change or give refunds. Watch these people, they steal your money and double charge your cards.

OK I'm kind of embarrassed to say that last night was our first time at Shake Shack. My boyfriend and I parked in a metered spot hoping to get a table, but no luck. We ordered anyway and decided to get the food to go. The cashier was super friendly; he made recommendations when he saw us staring at the menu in bewilderment. "First time?" he said. Yes indeed. We ended up ordering single smoke shack burgers based on the cashier's recommendation. The food smelled so good that we sat in the car and ate. We didn't want to ruin the flavor by getting all the way home and having to reheat our meal. The cherry peppers were a bit too hot for me but my boyfriend loved the flavor.  We also got an order of cheese fries. Seriously so good although they do look like Ore Ida as other reviewers have mentioned. So the great thing about eating in a metered spot is that when you still have an hour left on the meter you can head back for dessert. Because we're greedy (thank God we work out) we went back and ordered half concretes. My boyfriend got bananas and peanut butter sauce mix-ins. I ordered the Liberty Shell, a mix of canoli, chocolate, lemon ricotta and strawberry puree. He loved his. I thought mine needed more strawberry puree but it was yummy nonetheless. So the question of whether fast food places like this get a 3 vs 4 from us is always "would we return?"  The answer is a 4/5 for shake shack. I just wish they had more seating available.

I was met with a combination of utter disappointment and extreme fullness upon visiting shakeshack.  The reviews, hype, long lines, articles, aura of shakeshack is pretty intense.  My expectations may have been high, but, given the reviews, hype, long lines, articles, and aura, I feel my expectations were warranted.

Came on a nice sunday afternoon, lines were not too long and moves quick.  You dont get much time to peruse the menu, and if you do, a bunch of people end up ahead of you.  I ordered a single smokeshack, cheese fries, a fair shake, and a victory prima pils. Spending more than $20 at a fast/trendy-food place was unreal, but, maybe it would be worth it. 

Drinking a beer always makes waiting for food easier, but, overall it didn't take too long for the food to be called.  

The burger was....okay.  The bun was, a bun.  The shack sauce was whatever, standard creamy, spicy, sweet situation.  The toppings were solid.  But its a burger.  The actual burger was so disappointing.  Thin, lifeless, low self esteem.  The burger needed some time in the weight room.  While I'm sure they buy high quality, local, sustainable, organic, grass and coconut water fed beef, they just need more of it.  Their burgers are too think to even really request a cooking temp.  The cheese fries are krinkle cut and crispy.  They try to sell lower fat as a pro, but, honestly, if you're ordering cheese fries, nutrition is not your primary concern.  Does anyone really like krinkle cut anything?  The best part of the meal was the fairshake.

Some people are into this type of burger.  A white castle-esque, thin burger that you can chow down.  And by all means, I'm for it, but not for $6.  

So, $20-some and circa 2000 calories later, I felt full, but, thoroughly underwhelmed.  Note, my repeat, confirmatory visit was met with similar findings.  Nonetheless, this place will always get great reviews, and have long lines, and will attract visitors, and make magazine lists for best burger.  I just hope the accolades lead to better food.
Miserable place.  Slow and unfriendly. Food is boring     Management is terrible.   Skip The Corner Bakery.

My oldest daughter and I needed a quick snack before our next event and bopped into Spice End. We ordered the chicken tikka roll and the paneer tikka roll. It's just what we needed. The rolls were flavorful and hit the spot. There was a discount for buying two and then noticed when I did the yelp check in I would be set for another discount for my next visit. This is one of those places that serves the good purpose of eating tasty food at affordable prices when you are in the mood for a no frills but satisfying experience. We could have easily had a good meal here but were on our way to somewhere else in a few hours so this stop made perfect sense as we satisfied our taste buds with the rolls. I would be remiss to not mention the lassis, some of the best I've ever had...with a wide variety of flavors. We had the rose and the mango and were delighted with the smooth, creamy deliciousness. I am looking forward to going back. PS I think I need to mention that my middle daughter, who attends Temple sent me a photo of food that she ordered with the caption, "amazing-ness". I asked her where she ordered from and she said, "A place called, Spice End."  So there ya go.

Maybe 2.5 stars. It's really not that bad. The burger is a kind of McDonald's on steroids (in terms of guilty pleasure fast food it's pretty good). I had the smoke shack with bacon. Fries were weak. Frozen crinkle cut drizzled w Wiz. On the other hand it is licensed , so beer/wine is an option (perhaps a necessary one). It is pretty cheap which works to its advantage. Geographically challenged in that it's right across from one of Phillys best burgers the Whiskey king (but you can have a meal for two with drinks for the price of Garces extravaganza with duck fat fries - you might want to save up!)

Conveniently located in Center City, Spice End is great fast-casual meal option. I ordered the chicken over rice and pav bhaji. The pav bhaji is out of this world (warm fluffy bread with vegetarian curry), but the chicken over rice, though tasty, paled in comparison to other chicken over rice options in the city. 

The customer service here really stood out. The cashier who took my order was very kind and checked in with me multiple times to make sure I enjoyed my meal. The dining area is kept very clean. I will definitely come back to order the pav bhaji.

I really hoped this was going to be my new go to place at Citizens Bank Park, but  I'm sorry to say it wasn't that good at all. I work on the road and have had burgers in gas station that were better at a third the price and no line. I'll try Pass and Stow or go back to Harry the K's.

Everything started out perfect as me and my boyfriend had a late night snack. I kept seeing something out of the side of my eye but couldn't catch it. Finally everyone seen the mouse that was running around the dining area. Told an employee and she said oh lucky I don't have to go in the men's bathroom where the mouse went. That was very unprofessional.  After seeing the mouse everyone left the restaurant in disgust. The manager ran out to give us coupons for free burgers and fries but I will not be returning to this restaurant.

I stopped by here for a quick bite.  I was lured by the Beyond Meat burger with Gouda.  For a plant-based alternative it was not bad!  It was on the pricey side of $10 for the burger alone.  Seating is limited - 3 stools at the front.

The food is very different and is delicious. I love the rolls and it's one of the only places that has Pav Bhaji! The flavor is very unique. Definitely recommend eating here if you're looking for something different or miss street food!

This is the first Hip City Veg location I've been to that has breakfast. It was exciting. I got a Maple Peanut Butter Banana sandwich, hashbrowns and a vanilla milkshake - which is somewhat of a dream breakfast for me. This is not a place to go for a healthy breakfast though I'm pretty sure they have salads or bowls but I completely ignored those menu items.

The sandwich had way too much peanut butter so it was hard to eat. Hashbrowns are those standard flat patties and they are awesome. Fried and oily and potato-y. Clearly I am not vegan for my health. The milkshake was awesome as always - thick but easy to drink with the straw. In total this meal probably had 20,000 calories so take a long walk after or maybe run a marathon if you're into that sort of thing.

Like all Hip City locations this place is small with no seating inside however there is an unlocked door in the back that leads to the office lobby next door with seating and tables. The staff can point you in the right direction.
I got an egg McMuffin that was green on the inside. I ate two bites before noticing. Disgusting. Hope I don't get sick.
Raw bacon. Sparsely placed avocado hard as a rock. I contacted the store with the photos and my feedback and did not receive a response.
brought a chicken sandwich，almost lost my teeth on my first bite ！ the patty is hard as rock，meat was dry，worst experience ever！
This was delicious!! The ranch on the crispy chicken sandwich blew me away!! This was BETTER than chic fil a. The chick n tasted like real chicken and the order came up quick.

Not bad. Not great. I was looking for something quick and just happened to have a sweet tooth so I went with a watermelon cucumber juice drink & a vegan (I think) chocolate mouse. The drink was actually pretty good. The mouse I chucked. One lick of the spoon & I could tell it was LOADED with cinnamon. I dipped my finger into the mouse to see if it was just sprinkled on top, I was eating it in my car on the way home. But nope. Nasty cinnamon loaded all through. Disgusting. Who does that to chocolate mouse? They have a limited menus & seem to have more items coming. I will probably try again but I'm kinda scared. For now I'm sticking with whole foods or Trader Joes for the price point

I hate being that guy that says, "It's just too small!" I am a server after all, I hate hearing that and 90% of the time it's an entitled guest who has no ability to grasp that food cost is a thing.

But maybe that is the case 

In terms of food, this burger was great. Very tender with good sauce and some onions that added to it. A solid, good burger.

But the size was small. So small it was funny. It looked like one slider out of three sold at a decent restaurant for $12. Had it been sold as such I would happily have paid that twelve bucks. But at $9 for a single slider I'll say no and stick to Goldie or Pituco pizza if I want a bite to eat at the food court.

If you're going to offer gluten free buns you should stock them... my girlfriend has celiacs and at 8:30 you should still have gf buns. Otherwise we just won't be coming here again we will make the trekk to bear burger instead.

First time here and it was actually good , the guy behind the counter helped us pick out good burger and shake combos. Food was amazing , kinda hard to find seating but we managed to get a good table. Price although seem a bit too high but the taste of the food was really worth it , maybe

As I am engaged in a constant struggle to find affordable food for lunch near my office, it was refreshing to see that most of the selections here are under $10. It's not a huge place, but there is enough seating for a comfortable lunch. 

I've only been here once and had a chicken tikka roll to-go, which came to about $8-ish with tax. I felt like the roll was a comfortable amount of food, and was able to eat it while walking 3 blocks back to my office. However, some might say that there are other places around to get a better amount of food vs. price ratio. 

Also, I was disappointed that the chicken was a bit dry, and there were fewer veggies in it than I expected. I had this same roll before at a Yelp Elite event, where the chicken was a bit more moist, and there was a dipping sauce to add to the flavor. Given my limited lunch options within walking distance, I will likely be back, but I probably won't be in a hurry to do so.

What a disappointment.  I really don't understand the hype.

My husband and I were so excited for this to open in our neighborhood.  Really pleased to find a time when the buzz died down so we didn't have to wait in the long lines.  Wait time was 9 mins.  One of the few positives we took from this experience.

I had the Shack burger and my husband got the one with the fried mushroom on top.  Burgers were forgettable - small, over cooked and under seasoned.  My husbands burger was very messy and oozed cheese; this still didn't add to the flavor profile.  Fries looked like those you can get in the freezer section of your grocery store.  Needless to say, they tasted as they looked.

The best part of the meal was the root beer.  Adding insult to injury, we had to walk past Village Whiskey on our way home.  What a waste of a dinner.  Now we know.

Every single day I struggle between "I wanna look good naked" and "treat yo self....

mc donalds is cheap but it would be more affordable for you to go to an actually restaurant then a place that services you trash... in a long run if you indugle in this food all the time you will get all the heath issues or even just get fat and you still need to spend more money on fixing those kinds of issue...

Not only is the food bad for you here but....This McDonald is a dump...and located in such a bad area... 

-Dirty 
-Bad serivce 
-Getto 
-Bums 
-Broken chairs 
-Gangs 
-Bad neighborhoods
-Robberies
-Disgusting bathrooms

Constantly needing to tell myself to step back...and take a deep breath....this place is disgusting!!!

Amazing vegan Philly steak and Sweet potato fries!
The service was great!  A little pricey, but it was worth it!There are 2 locations, close to everything!  Thanks!

Convenient because it's in the Philadelphia 30th Street Station and in a pinch you can grab something there and bring it onto the train. Compared to other vendors at 30th Street, it has great selections, the freshest ingredients and the staff is friendly too. Other places are good, Jersey Mike's about the best. AND if you promised someone at home (NOT MENTIONING ANY NAMES) that you'd bring back Philly Cheesesteaks but forgot...this is a pretty good "Plan B". Don't get me started on the best Philly Cheesesteak, Mike's is good in a pinch! Try it.

Went here for a quick takeout on a Saturday afternoon. One of our friends had already been here and recommended they have nice rolls.. not as good as 'The Kathi Roll Company' in NYC, but still good. So i went with it.

the place had just 4-5 tables occupied besides my group. we ordered 2 lamb kebab rolls, 2 chicken achari rolls and 2 achari paneer rolls.  

the takeout wasn't quick in any way.. it took around 40 minutes to get this order. i love kathi rolls so i swallowed the issue and went home excited to try out this joint selling so many varieties of veg and meat rolls. 

After reaching home I first tried my most favorite variety - Achari chicken roll. it was a huge disappointment!! there was nothing 'achari' about it. Achari word comes from achar.. which is a Hindi term for pickle. its supposed to have pickle flavored curry chicken in it.. but this one just had a green peppermint chutney and some chicken tikka rolled in a white-flour roll. bummer! nothing achari! why call it chicken achari then.. uhh. the only saving grace for this roll was that it was packed with the chicken tikka.. so was heavy. but dont take my word for it.. i eat light.

well, i moved onto the next one lamb kebab roll.i was almost full, but i had to know what the other roll tasted like. had a few bites off the lamb kebab roll. it was strange.. i have never had a lamb kebab roll beforr so can't compare, but the lamb was grounded and not juicy and had very little flavor! it tasted like it only had salt. everyone in my group commented the same that lamb roll is not good. 

after that i tried the achari paneer. it too had nothing achari about it. the paneer was tender but didnt tatse like tikka or achari. it had peppermint and one other chutney. 

I also got another takeout order while waiting for my first order. that order had chiken tikka roll. when i ate that, i was struck by the fact that this was exactly how the achari chicken roll tasted! so did they run out of achari chicken and used chicken tikka ingredients in achari chicken roll hoping the customers wouldn't notice? or do they really don't know how to make achari chicken rolls?

While at the shop, we all got their peppermint lemonade and it was delicious if not a littke too sweet for some. so when I think about it, i realize their tastiest item was the peppermint lemonade! lol! 

This deserved only 2 stars IMO.. but the low cost menu and peppermint lemonade earned them the 3rd star! I should probably point out that i was comparing this against the legendary Kathi Roll Company in NYC when i went here. as per my friend, i was expecting a drop in flavors already but not a complete goofup on the ingredient-list..

Tried Spice End at a Yelp event and I'm definitely looking forward to trying it on location again.  We tried the Aloo Paneer roll - filled with marinated cottage cheese and spicy potatoes, and comes with a mint-coriander chutney. The Chicken Tikka Roll contains freshly grilled chicken that's marinated in the classic Tikka spices and is also served with a mint-coriander chutney and onions.  Both were very flavorful and tasty! Well done!
Worst customer service , very rude when i asked to go to the bathroom and when i went there was no toilet paper

Deff a good spot if you're really starving and want to eat something tasty. Not too many healthy options, but like it's fried chicken what do you expect. The food is pretty banging though. Deff a solid spot.

Excellent burger. Buttery smooth meat. Smoke shack is amazing. Good kick. Good sauce. The new crinkle fries are top notch. Glad they got rid of skinny fries. Price could be better $15 for burger fries and coke not good. Tiny drink too.  Had to get up for a refill.

Following an fulfilling albeit pricey dinner at Il Pittore boo and I decided we'd find satisfaction in the warm embrace of cheeseburgers and milkshakes. I've read the reviews and the thread of SS but I had to go in with clear eyes and a full heart (FNL shout out!)  in  order to give it a fair "shake". 

So it was a beautiful night and we had no problem with the long line and we actually treated it as part of the experience. From standing in the back of the line to sitting at a table with our food it was about 35 minutes. We decided to split a double SS burger and each get a shake. The beef is grass fed which is ten times healthier then corn fed. In fact, grass fed beef has half the fat and calories and twice the amount of aminos soooo who's got beef with that?  

The bun was soft and buttered and we got extra pickles which were fresh and thick sliced. It was not greasy at all and I was able to stay clean straight to the last bite!! Plus it didn't give you that "Now I'm a Fat F" feeling you get following a Five Guys burger. We sat in front of the TV at a able that was made from an old bowling alley in Brooklyn and watched Jim Thome hit a ball 5000 feet to centerfield. 

I got the Rittenhouse Concrete but they were out of the chocolate truffle cookie dough : ( I love mocha flavored anything so I enjoyed mine a lot. Boo got a vanilla and peanut butter shake and I actually liked hers a lot more than mine but whatevs. 

Everyone was very nice both employees and diners. It's important to remember that just because a place is hip and trendy doesn't automatically make it invalid. SS is a fantastic addition to the PHL food landscape and I plan on going back soon.

You know how a lot of times you see ads or commercials and the food looks beautiful? My food at Shake Shack was beautiful in real life. The ShackBurger was topped with crispy green lettuce and the tomatoes were such a vibrant shade of red, it made me wonder how they got that way...pesticides?...genetic mutations?...who cares! I don't even eat tomatoes and I was amazed! The fries were crispy golden perfection. The vanilla milkshake was very satisfying.  

The place is casual, but clean so it makes it feel upscale-ish. I'm not sure it's worth the line I've seen span out the door, but its definitely a good place for a quick flavorful bite to eat.
Amazing food. I am becoming a regular here

Haters may say "it's airplane food" but that's okay bc more for me!! I go in here probably 4 out of 7 days of the week and it's truly a life saver when I need a healthy snack or a super quick meal and I haven't had time to make food that day.
