If you care at all about health and nutrition I can't see how you would dislike Snap Kitchen. They make healthy simple meals like you may cook for yourself at home, but they are tastier. In addition to this they list all allergens/nutrition details and have TONS of options for vegan/vegetarian/gf/whole 30 diets. I think certain items are definitely a lot better than others, but I can't say I've ever had something bad here.

I recommend the butternut squash macaroni, kale hoppin John and the banana maple oatmeal. Make sure you do look at the prices before you make a decision here because they are quite different depending on the item and if you are careful you will spend less than $10. 

I also feel like eating here can be a hack to your own cooking and help give you healthy cooking ideas/inspo as I've recreated some of the meals here with success.

Worst location ever. Has gone down the shi*tter within a few months. More sauce than meat or chicken on sandwiches. As you watch the kitchen and see the execution and view your meal one can only wonder the cleanliness of the operation. Had chicken nuggets. 2 dried fried greasy pockets of air. Rest of the chicken tasted like fish and had a rubbery consistency. Chicken shack, chicken was less than half the size of the roll and covered in mayo. Burgers now also have more sauce than meat. No box in the bag for takeout. Order mobile orders you get a  notification meal is ready. Get there wait for 10 mins then get your food as it was sitting in the window the whole time. Such a shame. Well on a positive, no shortage of spots in the city! FYI was told a refund would be issued 3-5 days.....9 days ago. Then asked by the general manager to meet and apologize in person. No just maybe get the place in order. Half of a piece of chicken on a chicken shack. Wish I showed the amount of mayo and had other pics of the nuggets and burger. Btw I used to eat here once a week. Such a shame. If you can't afford the rent... move.
Love this place, but they always put too much dressing on the salad be warned otherwise great stuff.

Ordered 2 plates through Uber eats. Both with chicken teriyaki with brown sauce ( specifically write this in the note section) and both did not have brown sauce on the chicken. So basically grilled chicken.  Food is usually good but it would be nice if they followed directions.

This was my go-to Shake Shack when I had orchestra rehearsals by Rittenhouse Square and I've always found the food and service to be consistently good. Like any other Shake Shack, the vibe is modern and upbeat. It can sometimes be difficult to find seating at this particular location during peak times (especially in the fall/winter when no one wants to eat outside) but I try not to come here too often anyway because the calorie counts listed on the menu scare me.

When calories are on the back-burner, my personal favorite is the Shack Stack, perfect for hungry and indecisive people like me who can't decide between meat and mushroom. The crinkle cut fries are a must-get- always fresh and crispy. The shakes are pretty good, but again, for a place that's called Shake Shack, I feel like they should have a larger selection of Shake flavors. They have your typical flavors (vanilla, chocolate, strawberry), and then a few seasonal flavors. However, I LOVE their strawberry mint lemonade. They also have concretes but for all the times I've been to Shake Shack, I've never had them.

We've also done online ordering/pickup via the Shack App for this particular location and my orders have always been ready at the times I selected on the dot. Shake Shack is always a reliable option for a quick meal!

What can you say about Shake Shack that's not already been said? Juicy, tasty burgers; crisp hot crinkle cut fries: beer (yes real beer) on tap and quick, friendly service. They say of New York "If u can make it here, u can make it anywhere." Shake Shack started in NYC. Nuff said. GO!

I went here last night and forgot then to write my review. I have always been a fan of Shake Shack! I am someone who a BIG appetite and somehow those little shack burgers can fill me up! The Shack and Shroom burgers are scrumpcious. If you add Cheese Fries to the burgers, you will be in for a highly calorie meal but definitely a delicious one!
My chicken sandwich tastes like the chicken itself was a family pet raised with the utmost tlc....awesome place

For starters: the food would definitely earn this place a five star review - so by all means if you are going for just that then do it. The service, was disappointing. They had messed up my bistro Bella order and I was asked by the cashier if I'd wanted them to remake it, but I didn't have time to wait. It was still delicious. I also got the sweet potato fries - they were some of the best I've had in my life, but the cilantro black bean dip (and I love both those things) was disgusting. Fortunately, they were fine on their own. Lastly, I got the orangesicle milkshake, DO THAT. I haven't had a milkshake in years because I was worried that I'd never find a decent vegan one, it was worth it. They were over priced - especially considering the awkward and limited seating.

I came to this place the very first day it opened. I was excited about the potential to have some really great food! Unfortunately, I think the price is high for basically a small chicken thigh and a lot of rice and hot potato salad. I generally don't pay almost 8 dollars for a couple hunks of rice. If there were two chicken thighs it might be a different consideration.   Will not go again.

Piece of junk restaurant. The whole point of the mobile orders is to skip line and order ahead. I ordered ahead and waited under the mobile order spot for 20 minutes before someone told me I have to wait in the long line.

After my first visit, I added Wokworks to my "best food I've ever had from a truck" list, and it's a small one. So is this truck. When a place serves me addictive drunken noodles that keep me coming back like soy sauce-laced crack, well... They've made the grade, and then some.

In case I wasn't clear, I ordered the drunken noodles, and you should, too. A generous offering of chicken and shrimp is the default for this dish. So is a bounty of fresh, crunchy veggies cooked just right. They still feel like they've got life and nutrition in 'em, which gives the dish serious texture. Much appreciated.

The wok is where it all happens. The ingredients are seared together in perfect harmony. Noodles, proteins, veggies, and flavorful sauces mingle till nirvana is reached. And then? The cherry on top: a smattering of crunchy wonton chips and springy scallions (if you want). I taste a garlic happiness punctuated by a delicious spice in each bite. My mouth is happy. My heart swells in gratitude. 

I'll be back to try more things, and that's a promise. The drunken noodles feed my belly and soul but the allure of general tso's, lo mein, and create-your-own is real strong rn.
Second time I've tried to GrubHub order from this location and they cancelled it, during normal hours. Annoying as shit.

Bistro Bella sandwich was EXCELLENT! Everything about it was on point.. yum!  I tasted one of the lemonades and that was a brilliant flavor wake up for my mouth too. Everyone in my crew was very happy with their food. Manager was also super friendly and kind, welcomed everyone as we entered and thanked us for being patient as they were pretty busy.  A+

My good friends know I loves me some Chipotle. Answer me this Walnut St location in Philly.  Why is the the trash inches away from your forks?  And you wonder why people get sick in many of your locations. GROSS it needs to be ADDRESSED!!!

Stopped in the other day for a quick sweet fix, really wanted a shake...but I ended up ordering one of their "concretes" which is a custard/ice cream blizzard kinda thing. I got the Rittenhouse concrete, and it was really good and very rich! Loved the ground coffee bean bits in the concrete as well as the chocolate cake pieces (I think). My boyfriend ordered the Pumpkin Pie concrete, and it was also very good! Both are worth a try!

Didn't get to order any real food or shakes, but their fries/cheese fries look divine! Will definitely be coming back when I need fulfill a burger/fries/shake craving!

The 4 Ws of Shake Shack:

WHAT:
This modern day "roadside" burger franchise makes burgers, hot dogs, frozen custard, and shakes. Yes, they even serves wine. From humble beginnings as a hot dog cart in NYC to new locations in places like London, it has now become an global foodie sensation. 

WHERE:
Located in the heart of Rittenhouse. You cannot miss it. Just come at lunchtime on any given day and you'll see the masses of hungry carnivores lining outside this establishment. 

WHY:
1) SHACK BURGER($4.60 for single, $7.20 for double)- flavorful and juicy beef stuffed inside a sweet, savory bun. 100% all-natural Angus beef. No hormones and no antibiotics  added. 

2) FRIES ($2.70)- Crispy and crunchy on the outside, perfectly soft on the inside. You may also top it with their special blend of cheddar and American cheese sauce! YUMM!

3) CONCRETES ($4.25)- Dense frozen custard ice cream blended at high speed with mix-ins. DELISH! You may choose to customize or choose from a selection of varied combinations. 

BREAKING NEWS: Waiting patiently for the CRONUT version concrete to come to Philly. Apparently it's "better than sex"...

WHEN:
Take Shake Shack for what it is. Not the cheapest. Not the most expensive. Not the fastest service (long lines). Come here without expectations and you'll find it's a great tasting burger place with really good fries and awesome frozen custard.

Preclosed early... walked in and they just stared at us. I asked what time they closed, as everything is advertised as 10 pm close time, and the girl working whispered "10." I asked again because no one else spoke up or even acknowledged my existence and the man said 9:30. I'm extremely upset. The group of us who walked in have no problem taking our business elsewhere--what a shame since it was our favorites. Unacceptable.
Picked up our catering order today and found out they charged my card twice $199 each.  Called to have them fix it and still waiting for a call back.  Totally unacceptable.

COLLEGE STUDENTS STAY AWAY!!!

I usually love chipotle, but this one is the worst out of all I've been to. The main issue is their portions and the old, brown guac. Every time I get an order from there I pay $9.25 to get a half filled bowl with barely any toppings and brown guac. When I finish eating it I'm still left hungry which never happens with chipotle. 

I say stay away because although the food is still edible, you just get nothing for what you pay. For ten dollars you can get a ton of food at a food truck on campus or somewhere else at a restaurant. It's just not worth paying full price for half. 
I hope this chipotle will fix its portioning because I miss my burrito bowls :(
Pretty flavourless biryani and they wouldn't even give me tap water. The bad pop music didn't help.

It's a hit or miss with this particular location. Meaning: based on the day, time of the day, etc will dictate the kind of service you receive. I've gone to this location for a year and probably won't go anymore, especially since you can go to Lee's Hoagies down the block and spend the same amount for more substantial food quantities. 

As stated: the customer service isn't the best, but if you don't mind the staff gossiping to each other, goofing off and some eye rolls, you'll be fine. 

Their hours of operations aren't finite. So if you're running to get a hoagie 30 min before closing time, be advised that on multiple occasions the night shift manager has closed the establishment early. So place your order ahead of time or just go to wawa.

We got lost several times attempting to locate Spice End. I was determined to find the restaurant, however, and was glad to find that it was worth the trek. 

The menu was extensive, providing me with many vegetarian options to choose from. The service was good, and the prices were decent. What made Spice End truly great, though, was the food.

After lengthy deliberation, I ordered Samosa Chaat, which I have never before tried. It was wonderful. The portion was slightly larger than I was able to eat, but it was so delicious that I ate more than I might otherwise have. The samosas came swimming in a spicy sauce with tender chickpeas. The sauce was not hot, temperature wise, which was a refreshing complement to the samosas. The samosas themselves were hot, almost painfully so; I couldn't quite tell if it was temperature-wise or spice-wise, or, most likely, both. They were crisp, even as they sat in a pool of sauce. The sauce, as well as the samosa filling, was quite flavorful. From the cool, smooth sauce to the tender chickpeas to the crisp and cream of the samosas to the light crunch of the garnish, the entire dish was a beautiful marriage of textures, flavors, and temperatures. 

If ever I should return to Philadelphia, I will definitely dine at Spice End again. I was most pleased with this restaurant.

Wow.  Great place great food.  First time trying this spot and very impressed. Had the chicken teriyaki and dumplings (I over did it).  Great flavors in both. I would so much rather spend 7.99 for something this good and fresh as opposed to some over priced chain place. I can't comment too much on the restaurant itself.  I ordered online and my order was ready as soon as I got there.  In and out in under a minute at 12:30 on a Friday.  Well done all around.

I got the roasted chicken rich bowl. The whole to go box was full. The bowl was very flavorful and filling. I wasn't able to finish it so I had leftovers for lunch the next day. It was even better . I can't wait to go back to try the double fried chicken (they didn't have any left when I went that was about 830 on a Saturday only issue. The price was reasonable 13 bucks not to bad.

I am at the Corner a bakery cafe with my good friend Margie and her Grandaughter Laeanne. I have the bakes potato soup.... so good and worm for this windy day in the windy cityZ I really like the atmosphere in here it is like a Panera bread but it's not! Mrs Bert at the register was very nice to me. Overall a pleasant experience I hope my girly Fran gets here! Soon

I came to Philly from LA and figured if I asked for vegan Philly Cheesesteak, that they would run me out of town.  Found this place immediately and got the vegan cheesesteak.  It absolutely did not disappoint and exceeded expectations.  Great roll, great "steak."  Mushrooms cooked to perfection.  So far, a highlight of my trip.  Staff was super friendly.  The space was nice.  I liked everything about it.   Will go back before I leave and try the breakfast.

Look. Indian food. Conveniently placed nearby, offering convenient bite-sized chunks. I had a serviceable chicken biriyani, prepared quickly and with some care.  The "Spice End" chicken platter is pleasantly spicy.Nice folks. Glad to know it is there.
Mediocre sandwich. Definitely overpriced for what I got. Limp bread. Roll that was totally cut in half. There was more food falling out of the sandwich than anything. Very messy for "on the go" food

Holy! moly! this place is amazing! big portions and the take out containers are clean and microwavable, The staff are friendly and make the experience well worth the visit. The hummus is creamy and the platters are plentiful , with lamb and steak. Taztiki sauce was thick i wasn't too keen on it but the hummus was spot on and the pita bread was grilled nicely. the stuffed grape leaves were alsd fantastic. On a Saturday they got pretty busy early and they still handled the rush well. I was waiting for this place to open and i must say i was impressed they didn't dissapoint.

Called for take out. Don't accept calls for this. Downloaded and installed app. Mobile ordering for this location was not available. Went in person order takeout came up as an in house order despite the takeout clearly marked on the receipt. Got the food home and my bacon burger had no bacon, charges were on receipt. All in all $26 for two mediocre sandwiches, an order of fries and a shake is a bit ridiculous
Ordered the Bulgogi Tacos. Way too salty & didnt taste all that great. Could only eat 2 of 3 pieces.

No more reason to walk down the street to Qdoba.

I stepped into the new Chipotle last night for a quick take out dinner before going out to see a show.  The place is clean and bright with an enthusiastic staff manning the prep line.  A very friendly manager stood behind the crew greeting customers and making sure everything ran smoothly.

I ordered a beef burrito and a side of chips with salsa.  The nice, fat burrito had just the right amount of each fresh ingredient and I am happy to say there is now a burrito place in town that isn't shy with the sour creme and a place that now understands that hot sauce is supposed to really be hot.  Thank you Chipotle!  The side of chips was a large serving in its own big brown bag.  They were light and crispy and tasted wonderful when dipped in the side of salsa that was devilishly hot.

Great job Chipotle!  As the four stars say, " Yay! I'm a fan ".

Spice end is a great option for quick, tasty, and affordable halal/indian food in center city. The kati rolls go for about $7 (give or take a dollar) and their red and white sauces are to die for. I called to order for delivery the other day and was told they didn't offer the "buy 2 rolls get $1 off" deal via phone. So I used yelp's new online ordering app instead (which is awesome, btw) and received my food 50 minutes later. We ordered the chicken biryani platter, the spice end platter, and 4 kati rolls, and everything was delicious! It was my first time having the biryani and I actually much preferred the flavorful spiced rice and whole pieces of chicken in that to the typical chicken and rice platter I usually get. If you've never had it before I absolutely suggest trying it! The pita or naan used for the kati rolls is also great every time. And the best part is, it's open late to satisfy your midnight cravings :)

I did the whole Shake Shack thing this past weekend because Philadelphia thinks their cool now because they have this place. Nothing like waiting in a long line for underwhelming food. I mean it is a burger and shake, you can't really mess it up, unless you have your customers wait 25mins in line and then over charge them. Unfortunately, I knew this was going to be the case but just had to check it out. Ever hear of an oldie that is being resurrected, Gino's. Check them out: ginosgiant.com, not some hipster joint from NY making philadelphia yups feel important, but it is very good!
I don't think I will be back to shake shack, nor do I understand the fanatical Yelp reviews. Yelp should incorporate some sort of factor into their filter to prevent trendy disappointments like this from happening
Good but no dine in or place to sit just take out

I don't know, I guess me not being a fan of chain places in the first place is what's making give this unhappy review or the fact that these hoagies aren't really delicious at all!  

This is my first & last time eating here;
#1 this place is filthy and beyond messy, I know it's a super busy place but that's not excuse... All the other shops in the station are also high volume but they're clean from what I can see.. 

#2 the hoagie alone just wasn't flavorful or appetizing at all.. I got the jersey shore; cappicola, provolone and ham.. Really light on the meat, the bread was so bland and the onions old.

The girls that worked there were nice but they did seem overwhelmed..

Prices are ok. Again, if you're able to get a hoagie from a local shop or pizza shop please do it! If you're hungry and just grabbing lunch on the go try to find another option and use Jersey Mikes as your last resort lol

Q.  What's dirtier than a Taco Bell?

A.  A Taco Bell that's underground!!

But seriously, it's Taco Bell. You know what the food is like. This is just slightly dirtier and with no seating. If you're like me you'll hate yourself for eating there but its inexpensive and tastes good.
Service was average. Be careful not to scratch your car in tight squeeze of a drive through. Seriously shorted me on the fries what is this shit. I paid 7 bucks for this sub par meal.

Updating my review. Still one star. First time I went I found something in my sandwich. I decided to give them another shot. Second time I went they literally jumped on my case for taking MY receipt. Apparently they have some sort of system here where you're not allowed to have your own damn receipt. They keep them to make your order but there's no possible way you could know that  if you don't frequent this spot. Needless to say I'm done for good. Subway for me.
Great food and great vibes!  Wide variety of food and drinks to choose from. The staff was so friendly and Josh helped me make a selection and it was such a great experience

Mmm.. delicious kati rolls. The chicken tika may be my favorite thing this side of Broad. That being said, their delivery sucks, takes forever, and never follows my delivery instructions despite charging a delivery fee.  Doesn't take points off the food, but I really wish they did a better job on the delivery front.
Food taste old and cold. Staff looks sad. Wrong order was taken. Kids menu was there but they had nothing available from it. Will not come back.

Grabbed a couple of burrito bowls to-go with a friend. People were friendly and they gave a small-decent portion size. Nothing negative to say about the place. It's very conveniently located. Would come back again!

I've been to the Broadway location in NYC before, so I knew that when I went to the Philly location, I would be in for a line. Even at 8 PM. Though the line moved quickly, it was still really crowded (buzzers for the orders are handed out) and every table had people at it. The annoying thing about this was that people were holding seats when they hadn't gotten their food yet. This bugged me because I was not planning to linger at Shake Shack-- I was planning to get my burger, eat it, and leave. But my boyfriend and I were forced to ditch our dine-in trays and take our burgers to the pizza shop down the street to eat because the tables were half-full and a lot of people didn't have food. More of a problem with the clientele than the restaurant itself, but more two-toppers would have helped.

The food at Shake Shack, as always, was yummy. The burger was juicy and had fresh Romaine lettuce (a commodity! Not iceberg!?) and the cheese was yummy, too. My only complaint is the price. Sure, it's city fast food in a boutique location, but paying nearly $5 for a burger is a little outrageous.

Most likely will return to see if the shakes are as good in Philly as they are in New York.

yeah- i never review. this is beyond a joke. even a packed drive through should not be taking this long. ordered my sandwhich 28 minutes ago i havent got to the window. drive to another fast food joint and get your fix. this is borderline funny. wish i could give 0 stars. i never review, i am just so bored.
Go here all the time. Food is prepared fast and the staff is usually friendly. They have the best vegan "chicken" I bring my parents here and don't tell them it's vegan.. they don't even notice.

I'd return! Seems like many would -- the place was slammed on a Wednesday during lunch. I went with the Smokehouse Burger: Impossible Burger with crispy fried onions and BBQ sauce. The bun was surprisingly a highlight.

Well, what can I say, it is a McDonalds. The staff here always seems to get your order wrong.  You had better repeat it at least 3x if you want to get what you ordered.  Given the turn around rate of cashiers and other workers (I almost never see the same person at the drive thru) it is no surprise.

Micky Ds earns its 3/5 stars by being exactly what it is: fast, greasy, delicious food after a night of bar hopping, a late day at the office, or any other time where it becomes impractical to cook. No surprise here.  While your arteries and gastrointestinal tract may protest in earnest, either by boisterous poop or the early onset of atherosclerosis, the slimy salty goodness of the Big Mac or the wonderful lard doused fries soaked in salt and drenched in ketchup can not be underestimated. 

Sure you may die an early death if you eat here too often (one Big Mac burger contains usually almost 100% daily value of sodium, fat, cholesterol- basically everything your doctor told you not to eat).  But damn, at 239am after a night at the bar with the boys does it taste so good.  Wash it down with the syrupy goodness of high fructose corn syrup Coke and you might as well be in heaven. 

Due to my anal retentive perfectionist nature I did check the facts on the big mac.  85mg cholesterol (28% daily value), 960mg sodium (40% daily value), total fat: 27g (42% daily value).  Per McDonalds Website, accessed 10/7/14.

Not quite as bad as I thought.  On that note, "I'll have a number 1 with a Coke."

This place is A LOT like Cosi (by a lot  I mean only the names have been changed to protect the innocent a lot...) - only their bread is not flat, instead comes in normal little roll form. 

It is neither anything super special or so terrible you cannot swallow. 

I like that it makes me think I am eating better or healthier because I get their salads but I am sure the dressings more than make up for any nutrition I might be getting out of the greens.

Last week my friend and I went for a coffee. I ordered a latte for my friend and a coffee for my self using the ritual app. When we got there they were working on the latte and gave me a coffee cup for my coffee. Went to fill up a coffee, it was cold and surely made long time before. I told the girl at the register and she asked the manager to take care of that. It took him 7 minutes before he even came over and started brewing another cup. At this point I was very disappointed as they did not even say sorry and I was running late for my meeting. I'm short terrible service.
Excellent establishment! Quick lines, fast food, great coffee, happy employees. Defiantly recommend the cheddar and bacon panini for breakfast!

Their food is delicious by all means. It's sort of on the pricier side but I guess that's expected of any plant-based/veggie food joint in a city. Can't say it's a go-to place due to the price but I'm more than happy to eat here when the occasion presents itself! Thanks for opening up on Broad St!

I love how there's new limited time menu options, and how they have Chicken Bites now!! The employees always move out fast and are efficient! So I got the chicken bites (six bites) with barbecue sauce (it was the perfect amount of sauce) and the Fifty Fifty (iced tea/lemonade).

I absolutely love, love, love The Corner Bakery! Just had them cater a business breakfast and lunch. The food was delivered on-time and was presented well. Very tasty and fresh! Everyone raved about it and one of the attendees was really happy to learn that there is a Corner Bakery by her home. The only bad thing is that I wish I had more lunch meetings!!!!
This is the teriyaki I've been craving for so long in Philly!! Perfect quick and delicious meal.
Food was delicious but service was meh. The location is great and very spacious. This location is usually pretty packed but it never feels too crowded.

Not bad, but not necessarily worth the wait or the hype. Burgers and fries are greasy-good, but I think you get more for your money at somewhere like 500. The only thing worth the price is a Concrete milkshake, and you might almost be better served getting a gelato milkshake across the street at Capogiro.

This is a review of why I think it closed and why I never went even though I passed by it during it's grand opening and several times. I've also ate atthe old  @Ramen(which i disliked) and the old Giwa(which was pretty awesome). TBH, the food to me looked too plain like just regular chicken Teriyaki and in that prime location in Rittenhouse you need something outstanding to gather the crowds. This would've probably worked much better in like U City, Temple or somewhere with more students but maybe not the Rittenhouse crowd as much. I also didn't go because I don't think rice + chicken + potato salad/coleslaw works. Maybe for fried chicken but I'm not eating plain white rice with more carbs. I think a healthier alternative would've better(i.e. brown/multigrain rice). I also would've preferred like steamed/sauteed veggies or a soup with the dish instead of just cold potatoes. Also, the $10 bowl was quite small and Teriyaki to me is already sweet, but a sweeter $10 Seattle teriyaki is too much for me to put down. I would've totally preferred a more authenticate Japanese style fast casual of like gyudon or rice bowl, dumplings, takoyaki, or go Korean and just do Korean tacos or homemade gimbap. Unfortunately, never got to try but hope they still come back better and work on their pricing/portion/quality for the crowds.

Taking me down memory lane . I was actually excited when I seen panda opening up in the area because back at home in Boston , we had one at the mall and the food were always good . The last time I've had panda express was during my six flags tripped last year but the food wasn't all that great .

I decided to stopped in for dinner takeout since I was shopping at a store near by . I walked in approximately around 9:10pm and there were barely anything left to ordered . As you can see pictured I had two sides that's almost identical because that's all they had left . Place stated it closes at 10:00pm so why aren't there any food left to ordered when you have almost an hour left til closing time ? The food were good although the celery in the lo mein kind of threw me off and plus it was like left over that was scraped from the wok .

Service was good . Place was nice , spacious, and neat . I would definitely returned but probably an earlier time so I won't run into this kind of problem again .

Did you know you can eat an entirely vegan or vegetarian meal here and be satisfied?  I had a terrific lunch that included all kinds of beans and veggies.  It was fresh and tasty.  the location is central, the place is clean, although crowded when I was there, and I enjoyed the flavors all around.

I've tried other locations, but this location in the Philly train station is the best.  My train stops here to change engines before going on to NYC, and I never miss my chance to order a Philly Cheese Sandwich here.  It is fabulous!  Fresh bread crisped on the grill with loads of steak, smothered in tasty, well cooked onions and peppers, all topped with delicious cheese.  Yum!

It was the end of the night and I was ready to go home.
My cousin made one last stop to this chi ken place and

tl;dr a hole-in-the-wall Indian joint in Rittenhouse, geared toward lunch and late-night takeout

Spice End is somewhat of an anomaly in the Rittenhouse District. Restaurants typically fall into one of three buckets: the in-and-out convenient stores (i.e. Wawa), the eclectic fast-casual, and the chic dinner service. Spice End falls somewhere on the spectrum between the former two, cooking up Indian plates into the late-night scene.

The space is large, filled with many cheap-looking tables and a pressing a small ordering counter into the counter. Spice End channels some Desi influence with its jarring red-and-black walls, but the chipping paint and large photographs of overly upscale food create a somewhat cheesy vibe. Plastic-y tables and linoleum floors echo the same sentiment, just in case you still hadn't realized that Spice End is a dive. The staff borders between uber friendly as you order to non-present after you pay. Food is brought out on cafeteria-style trays with plastic cutlery and the classic white paper napkins.

I appreciate that takeout is made easy with the aluminum takeout containers, and the serving size is somewhat bigger than the halal food carts scattered about the city. But I wasn't all too impressed by my actual food, the Chicken-n-Lamb Platter. When it came out, the dish smelled delicious, and I'm certain the meat was freshly cooked. But it would be an understatement to say that the food looked unappetizing. The minced meat looked like cat food and was served beside a "salad" (it actually was just lettuce) limp pita. While the meat was tasty, perhaps even a step above Halal carts, the rice was flavorless and the pita was lukewarm and overly chewy. I had to douse my bowl in red and white sauce for it to be enjoyable. The only case I imagine finding myself at Spice End again is if I'm desperately searching for cheap, late-night takeout in Rittenhouse.

Being from California it's been hard to find a place to fill the empty hole in my soul aka my stomach that In-n-out burger was able to do so well. Aziz Ansari talked it up so much I had to give Shake Shack a run at the belt (was that a pun? or double entendre?) So here is my rundown of Shake Shack Vs my golden standard which is In-n-Out. 

Burgers - Solid burgers, just a little greasy for my tastes for how thick they are. I've eaten at this location and the University City one. Sometimes they nail it, sometimes not so much. Ingredients are fresh tasting and the sauce is good to go. 

Fries- Oh man, crinkle cut fries are like def leopard and acid wash sweatpants, they take me back to my childhood. As long as they come out crispy the fries are on point.

Some awesome things that Shake Shack does:
1- Serves alcohol. Beer, Cider, wine. They have good stuff like Yards and Jacks. I like me some Cider.
2- Atmosphere and service - Always have a good experience with the staff.

Something not so awesome -
Price - a little up there for the amount of meat you get and just overall for a burger place that is kinda fast food, but trying really really hard to make it to the upscale burger party without all the necessary "ingredients". 

Shake Shack is a solid go to if you want a good burger, a shake or drink, and good vibe for hanging out while you eat. If you're looking for a better burger for around the same price I would recommend Spot Burger or Bareburger for a similar style but more substance (there's another one!)

This is hands down my absolute favorite treat lunch! I love everything about shake shack! For a fast food joint the burgers are perfection: juicy, flavorful, always just perfect. The bacon is crispy, the cheese is melted gooiness! The fries are also just as good.  I rarely have the chance to enjoy shake shack but when I do it's yummy glory.

The food is good but the portions are never enough ever 
Each time i go my protein is always 2 scoops worth & a whole lot of rice for nothing

We ate here when there was a St. Patrick's Day parade so they were only offering a limited menu. The cafe wasn't busy, but tables were still left with trash on them and the bathroom is a pretty abhorrent site to behold. Since it was limited menu, my fiend and I both ordered the apple chicken sausage wrap. It was good, nothing fanciful. 

There was also some disconnect with the cashier. She forgot to give me the number to put on the table and my receipt and she just walked away. She seemed kind of spaced out but eventually after trying to figure out wheremy number/receipt actually were I still got all my food. She also apparently placed my coffee cup on the counter but I didn't see her do that. It would have been nice if she had told me.

Good burgers terrible portion size, was the equivalent to a happy meal. The burger was the size of my hand and my hands pretty small. I heard shake shack was like the in and out of the east coast so I was pretty excited to drag my boyfriend along to try it. However even though the place itself wasn't terrible the sandwiches need to be bigger for the price. I usually feel pretty stuffed after eating a burger but was sadly underwhelmed when I finished my sandwich in the span of 5 minutes or less.

I really do not see what the hype is all about with Shake Shack.  I do not mind paying for a good burger, but I want to be full when I am done.  

I do not think that a kid's meal should be $13-$15.  There are way too many BETTER burger joints in the city to waste that kind of money of a below average meal.  

To me, this place is like Wendy's on steroids.

I would rather spend the extra few bucks and go across the street to Village Whiskey or take a ride to Sketch.

Again, I do not see what the hype is about..."to each is their own."

My absolute favorite vegan restaurant to visit when I'm in the area. The staff is always super friendly and love helping customers. It's very small waiting space here so be prepared if it's crowd and you're claustrophobic. 

I'm a fan of the lemonades and buffalo style chic'n sandwiches. The chic'n sandwiches are one of the best sandwiches. They won't fool a meat eater, but they still taste better than most mock meats. They are made from both soy and wheat gluten, according to one cashier I asked. 

It's definitely pricey to eat here but it's the center city so that's to be expected. It's about $10 alone for either the buffalo bella (sub chic'n) or the hipcity ranch (buffalo it). 

One thing I haven't liked so far is the jerk salad. I felt like it didn't have enough flavor but that's just my perspective. The jerk salad seems to be one of customers' favorites. 

This is the only location that serves for breakfast. I always get their breakfast sandwich and occasionally request for sausage to be added. It might to startling at first for people who aren't used to the bitterness of tempeh, but I've grown to love eating this to start my day off. 

They do not provide a wide selection, but they have tasty enough options that you won't care. They provide some juice options, a few smoothies (get the orange creamsicle; it'll fool you for sure), some sandwiches, salads, and a few sides. The sweet potato fries taste delicious dipped in their vegan sriracha aioli. 

All in all, it's a great grab and go stop for the traveling and working vegans. Minor flaws don't take away from what a enjoyable meal stop this is.

Disappointed. In part its due to the large hype surrounding the opening of Shake Shack's first Philly location. I wanted it to be great but it's just not what it is in NYC.

Tasty burgers but a little too greasy and honestly gave me a stomachache the last time I ate one. I got the SmokeShack burger which has bacon, peppers, and "ShackSauce" on it. The fries are pretty delicious and I always order a side of cheese.

The real reason to go to the Shack is for the concrete milkshakes. They have multiple mix ins and you design your own. The best I had was a fall special of pumpkin pie mixed with vanilla!

Terrible service, this place has all the opportunity to be successful but they refuse to have any customer service. Not to mention it's so dirty in there. Horrible, I made the mistake giving this place a 2nd chance but will not do that again. I live a block away and as much as I want to have good Indian food that is cheap, this is not the place. I prefer places that respect their clients. This place has zero class.

Totally tasteless food.  Falafel platter was plentiful, but tasteless.  No seasonings at all.  Came with tasteless rice.  Lettuce and tomatoe without anything at all on it.  Even the pita was terrible.  White sauce worse than mayo.

If you like long lines, young attractive clientele, organic anything, fair trade coffee, local draught brew, refurbished table tops made out of bowling lanes from Brooklyn, easy recycling and biodegradable dinnerware and an occasional random person who works there coming up to your table with water and ensuring that your time at shake shack is an "enjoyable experience," then shake shack is for you. Notice how I left out food? There is a similar business that does this type of thing, what was it...oh yeah! Starbucks. Shack shack really sells you on the experience. The food is an after thought. It is not that it is bad, it taste pretty good, but is it worth it?

The ingredients are high quality. The crinkle cut fries nostalgic. The patties small. The buns fluffy. The shack sauce...I did not notice it.  Pretty much everything here is unremarkable. You won't go here spitting your food out but you also might not feel so good dropping down so much coin and time out of your life in order to enjoy the "Shake Shack " experience. But hey, I suppose it is better than dealing with the standard unglamorous clientele of most fast food joints.

In sum, you could get better (and cheaper) at other fine Philadelphia establishments. For chains, Five Guys lets you stack everything but the kitchen sink into your burger with fries that puts everyone to shame. You could go to Bobby's Burger Palace for something on the more beefier and unusual side with onion rings that break your toe if you dropped one. Or you can go to my favorite, 500 degrees, for a 1/2 pound rouge burger clone that is more remarkable in taste without any of the "experience" BS.

Hilarious side note: You can get a half bottle of Pinot there for ~$50. At a burger place.

I stopped in here for a quick sit down breakfast on my way to work, my first impression was a great relaxing atmosphere. Ordering is quick and easy, they have a vast menu for all different kinds of breakfast lovers. You can either order it for here or to go, they give you a number and for in dining, it is open seating and they bring the food right to you! They bring absolutely everything you could possibly need before even having to ask for it.

Super hearty portion, although the food came out slightly room temperature. Adequate flavor and adequate taste, nothing that really stands out. I would say this is a good place if you're in a rush and need a quick pick me up! Also, the food is at very cheap prices for those who aren't looking for an extravagant breakfast.

I came here with my brother because we were in town for Made in America concert and were staying at a near by hotel. We were looking for a quick bite that wouldn't take long and wouldn't cost much. I found this place on yelp and gave it a try. The location was great because it also given us options for other places to eat while staying near by. The guy working there was pretty cook and friendly with light conversation, the food was good with a little kick. All in all it was a good choice.
This taco Bell has the rudest staff. The lady who just took my order looks like she just woke up and she didn't even care to take my order correctly.

I came here a week ago to grab dinner with a friend after a successful workout. Since we didn't want to counteract what we just worked on, Hip City Veg came into mind. I tried their chipotle fajita wrap which was delicious. I love the grilled veggies and the chicken was perfect. Topped that with their green tea and I was full and  happy. Definitely worth checking out!
Also -- there are additional seating options in the lobby of the attached building.

The Caramel shake and the double shack burger with the shack sauce...ohhhh emmmm geeee!!!!! This has got to be the best burger joint in philly. I mean I travel real far to get a burger from this place and it's worth it believe me once you had shack you'll never go back!!!!

Good for dine-in/ take-out only! *Do NOT order delivery!* Tried the following rolls: Paneer tikka, Achari paneer and egg roll. Both the paneer rolls are really tasty..yumm! The sauces are good too. After going there for lunch a few times, I recommended it to my colleagues and we decided to order lunch from them for a meeting. The lunch order arrived cold after a delay of ~1.5 hours. Their service is not stellar either. If you are willing to overlook a few things then go grab those paneer rolls!!

I stopped in to Spice End for the second time today and I must admit that I wasn't impressed. I had the spice end chicken over rice for 9 dollars after tax. The chicken tasted and smelled really weird. I can't explain it, but it smelled a little like dog food. The staff was really nice, but I was it impressed by the food. To their credit I will say that I walk by this place on a regular basis and its not unusual to see many Indian people inside enjoying a meal. I almost wonder if the problem is that this place is authentic and I'm just not used to real Indian food. Either way this place isn't for me.
Shake Shack is THE place to be for good hamburgers ! It is absolutely delicious and the staff is very friendly !

It says so much about a company when they take customer service seriously, and Corner Bakery cafe knocks it out of the park. The food is fantastic too of course. My coworkers and I celebrate office birthdays with "breakfasts", where we typically order a couple scramblers from Corner Bakery in addition to other stuff. Today there was a small hiccup with our order, but it was important enough for me to call and speak to a manager. Tom, the manager, and Wendell were extremely helpful. Tom refunded my entire order amount and included a couple coupons for the trouble as well. Wendell walked over to drop the cash and coupons off to me- I have never heard of anything like that. They definitely went above and beyond. They turned something that could have been awful or even just unpleasant into an experience with which my entire office was impressed. Love ya, Corner Bakery Cafe! Thanks.

Shake Shack, you rock!

I love this location because there is never a long line. I've never had to wait for more than a couple of people to order before me. This is amazing compared to the super long and cold wait in NY!

The staff is freakishly friendly here. They are always smiling and having a good time. I love it! They're so happy even when they are taking your trash. Can I have some of what they're having? lol

Smoke shack burger is my new fave when I'm craving bacon. The cherry peppers add just the right kick. Order it! You won't regret it!

Seating can be a little tough to find so snag a table first if you come in a group!
Great food and great vibes!  Wide variety of food and drinks to choose from. The staff was so friendly and Josh helped me make a selection and such a great experience

I LOVE SHAKE SHACK. I will forever be a Shake Shack fan. All of the stores in Philadelphia do not disappoint (and it is a good thing they don't!)

From the SHROOM burger, to the milkshakes and concretes, to the fries, this place does it right. I can always expect a great experience everytime I walk into a Shake Shack, and that is why I love it so much. Not only does the food always taste great, but there is a certain consistency there that I love + appreciate.

I also always love the store designs. Such a fun, welcoming and warm vibe.
Hands down my favorite place for a gyro.  I like that they listen to me and put stuff on the side. Order. Couple of times and  been consistently delish.

On this rare day, I craved Taco Bell. I've only had Taco Bell probably 5-6 times in my life. But this day, I really wanted it. 

We walked in to order because there were 4 of us and we didn't want them to mix up our orders in the drive through (one in the group is vegan). I got a 3 soft chicken supreme taco meal. 

The soda machine was not well taken care of. All the sodas in the machine were flat. Then it took over 20 minutes to my food. It was the longest I had to wait for fast food. Imagine waiting in the drive through for 20 minutes. By the way, I watched the workers prepare the food. The drive through line was 3 times faster as the dine-in line took their time. 

Now the tacos. It was so disappointing. The only thing that made it edible was the hot sauce, because I drenched it in Diablo sauce till I couldn't taste the taco anymore. It's safe to say I'll never order Taco Bell again.
great food. Loved the pani puri :)

Until recently I didn't really know tikka masala from green curry when it came to Indian food. What's chutney? But I've wisened up after eating a spicy potato paper dosa this summer (carbs wrapped up in carbs, how could this be bad?) and wanted to try Philly's offerings. After consulting a friend who hails from India, I tried Spice End and was pleased. I had never had a kati roll before (go ahead, judge) and was impressed. $6 seemed like kind of a lot for one roll because I probably could have eaten three of them, but the roll was SO good and the chicken had that yummy chargrilled taste. The place isn't fancy, but the guys are so nice and the food is delicious.

Oh my... I used to love this place until today... Let me tell you the full experience "Today" I wanted a Steak Burrito, first they messed up my order I told them no beans.. So okay they are making it again but I had to wait because the Steak was not enough, they made the burrito with rice already and put it on the side.. So I've been waiting for 7 minutes and alas the steak is done.. They were going to use burrito and side they prepared at the side, common sense, the burrito and rice is now cold, I told them I don't want that give me a new one, the lady then prepared a new burrito but was going to scrape the rice on the other burrito, COME ON!!! The icing on the cake was the guy wiping the table... He was using 1 small towel to wipe the table where the grill was and used it on the tables where the ingredients were. And the towel touched the ingredients... SO imagine that.. Now I know why all types of complaints are being published about Chipotle

I come here whenever I have errands to run nearby and want to grab a quick casual bite to eat. Today I stop in early enough to try their breakfast since it is only offered at select locations. Ordered the AM Philly, breakfast wrap, and the lox & loaded bagel. SO GOOD - just as I predicted. Really impressed with the food here. Service was also great, staff members have been consistently on point.

Great food and a wonderful staff! Yesterday I had the Philly Steak, today I went with the Lil' Golden Nugs. Both meals were delightful and filling. I highly recommend this place for a quick healthy meal!

They give you the littlest amount of food possible.  This is ridiculous.  Every time I go in I have to say "more please" because the amount of food they give you is NOTHING!!The chips we recurved were stale and not enough in bag!
I paid so give me what I paid for!!!

I've heard of Snap when I was in Houston, TX last November. I didn't get to try it there. When it opened in Philly, I did stop immediately. I also try spread out the word to a few of my coworkers that want to eat healthy lunch meals. 

SK offers a variety of meals. Whether you want low carb - high protein, high fat- high protein, and many other nutritious options. It's like someone prepped your meals for the day and your're taking it from the refrigerator. Anyone who preps their meals for body goals purposes understands this. :) You pick it up from the shelves, pay and go. There's an option to heat it up there but I see a lot of people have it to go. 

Busy center city area folks, it's definitely a must try.

I was checking yelp to find a good food nearby. Wokworks is a cute food truck with not much menu to offered.

I tried their chili garlic steak and drunken noodles, both were good! The spice level is perfect and the flavor is great. Pay 22$ which i think it is a fair price.

It's not a bad sandwich but if you're going to eat this why not get a juicy sandwich from subway? Probably the same meats..(jimmy johns guy: no it's not the same meats, subway is plastic" ok jimmy john, whatever you say bro.....We know Jimmy Johns isn't a legit deli. You know who buys from Jimmy Johns? The same people who eat Pizza Hut and Little Caesars. Do yourself a favor, get a bit of class and order from a legit sandwich shop. Spend the extra buck and how bout not eat a fake meat sandy? does that sound good?  want to not ruin your body? quit eating little caesars, quit eating pizza hut, quit eating jimmy johns jimmy. My friend ordered delivery and it came QUICK though, so props for fast delivery.

Great location in the bustling business district in downtown Philly. The cashier was very helpful and helped suggest food ideas for my picky eater I was getting breakfast with.

The food was prepared fresh and fast and was very filling and delicious.

Just a great representation of why I love this chain!

Rudest cashier ever. The food is alright but not enough to justify me dealing with the most ignorant food service worker i've ever encountered. Super condescending and blatantly rude, won't say hello and will mock you if you don't know what's what on the menu (sorry i don't work there too and know everything there is to know about what they offer!). Someone needs to fire her.

I ordered some party subs for a safety meeting. They were great, Steve the manager went above and beyond to have it ready for pickup at the time I asked him. Steve and his team are always on point and friendly. If you want a good sandwich platter get it from Jersey Mike's, they put Wegman's to shame. The price was well worth it.

I just went there for the second time...just to make sure it wasn't my imagination...but the reason for the two star pretty much is for the price and size of the burgers.  They're like the size of a McDonald's burger with extra toppings.  The milkshakes were ok.  The fries were great.  I think they get a lot of overflow from VillageWhiskey patrons who don't want to wait 2 hours for a table.  The staff was super nice, but I'll keep looking for my best burger place in philly...

Had the pork gyro tonight - pork being the most authentic variant of gyro ... when you see it on the menu you know the place is legit. Topped with the most traditional of gyro addons - potato fries and got the spiced feta spread as well. It was fabulous, so so good. Greek salad as a side rounded it out perfectly. Baklava was top notch as well for a finisher, just right amount of honey saturation. Food prep was quick, the place was really comfortable and service friendly...no complaints will be back as much as possible!

Not true Indian food. 
Paneer platter- avoid. Tasteless and not filling, especially for the 8$ price tag.
Chicken biryani was better, but not the best.
Mango lassi was delicious with a $4 price tage.
Funny smelling ambience with a clattering drink fridge. I think folks know to avoid it- it was empty on a Saturday @ 6 PM. 
Save the trip for someplace else. Unless you enjoy leaving starving and unsatisfied.

This is my go-to place when I'm working in my Philly office at the Cira Center. As I'm walking to work in the morning, I'm thinking about going to Jersey Mike's later that day. The sandwiches taste really fresh, the bread, the ingredients and the meat. The service is always friendly and efficient, just the way I like things to work!

Ordered during COVID for pickup. The website makes it really easy. 

Ordered the taco argues salad with chicken and chicken nuggets. 

The taco salad was way more filling that I expected. The dressing was good, portions were good. 

Regretted getting the nuggets because I was fairly full from the salad. Also, online it asks if you want them with buffalo sauce, Miss read that it was tossed in the sauce vs on the side. Wish we got regular. So just double check. It tasted good but overall not a buffalo sauce fan.

I got the vegetable biryani and paneer achari for a late night delivery. I was really craving indian and this was open! I wish the paneer achari was spicier, had more pickled onions and maybe just more toppings to make it a fuller, more interesting dish. The vegetable biryani was pretty disappointing too. I had asked for extra spicy and they did send me hot sauce on the side...but not enough! It's mostly just plain rice and needs a lot more veggies ..maybe more potatoes, cauliflower, onions, peas, carrots. Just amp it all up! More spices and more veggies!

So far I have been to Jersey Mike's twice and they have not disappointed me! 

For lunch today, I got the chicken cheesesteak with grilled onions. It was delicious! I'm always greeted with a warm smile and fast service.. the military discount from work seals the deal!

The chicken cheesesteak DOES NOT disappoint on the meat or that amazing soft cloud of bread that holds the well seasoned meat in. What cheesesteak you know doesn't need ketchup?! I could take a bath in the juice. 

Before I cry because I have no more of my chicken cheesesteak left, let me wrap this up. I will definitely be back for that Godly chicken cheesesteak.
One of the best Indian options in Philly! Channa masala is an evergreen favorite

We were in town for a wedding and came here for brunch. It was the best decision. We arrived early and were greeted by manager with free water since we had to wait. The food was tasty. Simple and good for a hangover. I had the shroom burger and I would definitely recommend it for veggie fans.

What's not to like about this place? Burgers are always on point, fries are delicious and all of the other snacks and shakes could help this place open up a milkshake store by itself. Huge fan of the chicken shack if you want to mix it up from the burgers. This specific location is great because the lines are never too long and there's always a spot to sit. Good spot for outdoor dining as well.
Was there on Sunday, October 20, 2019 @ 6:00pm. My friend & I ordered the Mike's Famous Philly cheesesteak & both of us got extremely sick from food poisoning!

I first had HipCityVeg 3 years ago while visiting Philly and was dying to return. I thought the other location was small, but this one might be smaller. There are 3 seats facing the window and then additional seating in what seems to be the lobby in the building next door.

My favorite has always been the Crispy Chicken Ranch, however I was slightly disappointed because it was dry; too little ranch and too much "chicken." 

The gentleman who took our order suggested an amazing off menu sandwich with BBQ and avocado, the "Wizard." It was delicious! 

Carrot Ginger Lemonade tasted kinda like regular lemonade, but I remember the Kale one being good. 

I'll be back the next time I'm in Philly!

My all time favorite burger. I don't care how many more gourmet burger places keep opening up. Nothing beats a good ol' shake shack double. The burgers here are made to order and the perfect amount of meat to bun ratio. Too many gourmet burgers are piled high with patties that are humongous. Not my style if I'm going to have to use a knife and fork to avoid all the toppings falling out and ketchup dripping all over my fingers. Shake shacks burgers are like an upscale Wendy's cheeseburger. Still has that good classic feel with the right amount of moist goodness. Five guys does not come close in comparison! Their burgers are trash and priced about the same. Crinkle cut fries are my fave style of fries so that's just an extra bonus for me here at shake shack. Their milkshakes are pretty good too but only come in one size. Give these burgers a try, you will not be disappointed

I went to check out Shake Shack two weeks ago for the first time and it was pretty good. I went again today and was VERY disappointed, esp since I had been anticipating it all day. I think zero star would better describe my view of this place.

What went wrong?

1. We went at 8:15 p.m. and there was no line, but we waited 20 minutes for our food.

2. The buns and the patties were misaligned, so the burger started falling apart as I started eating it.

3. The buns were so soggy and gross. The first time, the buns were cripsy and fluffy.

4. The patties were overcooked, thus dry and favorless.

5. We ordered the Rittenhouse^2 concrete and Walnut Pie custard. I waited another 15 minutes to get the desserts and there was no line then either. I walked by the dessert station to see what was going and and noticed the four employees fooling around and eating the dessert themselves.

6. When I got my concrete, it was a mess. Ice cream was dripping on all sides of the cup. The employee didn't give an additional cup or offer to make a new one. $7 dollars for a mess. I had wrap a napkin around it to eat it. 

Shake Shack has so much potential but the unmotivated, poorly trained staff will bring this place down.

I won't be coming back to pay for horrible service and bad food again...
That was a $5 shake? Oh. Ok. Not sure what makes it worth $5. Even my 11 year old child was underwhelmed and complained it was too thin. Disappointed. .

The popcorn chicken is a must-try! It is super delicious with flavors that tickle your tastebuds. That was the first thing I tried from the place and it has me wanting more. At first I never really notice the place even though I am often in chinatown, but after a friend let me try its chicken, I went straight on yelp for its location hahahaha.

Since I had been craving some delicious, flavorful food decided to order a take out from this place on Saturday night. Their service was on point - food came quickly than the time anticipated by the person who took the order. 
I ordered the chicken and lamb platter - a little odd of a combination.  I was a bit disappointed to get a very dry platter which I wasn't going to get it moist with the white sauce which looked like mayo with lots of spices. The only part of that dish that i liked was rice. Was cooked very nice. If I'll have to order food again from this place will be another choice for sure. Maybe they deserve more stars than three.

Food is OK for fast food but the place is always pack not with people eating if you get my drift, just people sitting around talking loud. They did just remodel the place so hopefully it'll be a better atmosphere when dining in
Amazing crispy chicken and huge squid. Possibly the best fried chicken place in Chinatown. High recommend for people to try it out. Bento boxes are super cheap.

This is a new indian street food place.  They mostly have kati rolls (which are like indian burritos) and a bunch of platters.  I just went here this morning and had a chicken and egg roll.  The quality of the food was pretty high for the genre.  The meat was well cooked, and the roll was pretty good in a chewy way (like they should be).  The sauce in the roll was awesome (very dilly), and the onions made it good.  The price was fair ($6 per roll), but one roll is not quite enough.  They do offer a buy-2-get-$1-off deal, but I think 2 would have been too much.  Maybe a platter is the way to go.  We'll see next time.  I also saw one of their lassis.  It looked good even though I didn't have it.  The place was also very clean and well decorated.  (They have a very cool light fixture, and the pictures on the walls are exactly what you'd expect at a clean, nice indian street food place.)

First of all, if one more person compares Shake Shack to the great In-N-Out, I will punch them in the throat! Just kidding, ya'll. Maybe. 

Cons: 
-One would think because this place classifies itself as a fast food burger joint, that the prices would reflect that but it's still $25 for 2 people! 
-Their fries are always limp and close to being soggy, oily mess. 
-Their burgers are plain, they are missing some sort of secret sauce that should make their burgers unique and pop with taste. Or maybe their ShackSauce isn't just up to par with my taste buds. 
-It takes a long time to get your food. They give you a device that lights up with your food is ready. It's the same device that Olive Garden gives you when you have to wait around 20 mins or more to get a table. Not so "fast food", I guess. 

Pros: 
-they have a clean facility and that's always a plus. Even the bathrooms. 
-they have a menu just for dogs. Love that they cater to the furry children too. 
-they have a variety of sweets and desserts on the menu
-they have lots of seating indoors and outdoors
-they have the cutest "to-go" bags in which to take your meals home.
I appreciate the concept, but the food is just not that tasty. For the price tag, I don't think it's worth the money.

So yeah, a lot of people were looking forward to this place, it's apparently a big hit in New York.  The first 3 times I passed by here, it had lines out the door.  Today, no line at all.  NONE.  I am quite frankly very puzzled at how anyone can think their food is even as good as Five Guys.  Here's why:

The burger bun was so soggy, it was like eating a wet paper towel.  The bun, if dry, was nothing remarkable.  The "Shack Sauce"  was so tasteless, I couldn't tell what was in it.  I don't know, maybe they didn't put enough of it on the burger?  Tomatoes and lettuce added a "fresh" component, but little flavor.

The fries tasted frozen.  For a long time.  They tasted like they weren't wrapped up real perfect in the freezer and had that kind of taste you get when the food picks up all the other flavors of random ickyness in a freezer.  They had a good outer texture, however.  Crinkle cut.  Salted  the right amount.

The shake, vanilla, you could of course argue doesn't have as much flavor as chocolate or strawberry, but I struggled to find much vanilla flavor at all.  It tasted like frozen cream.  I've had much tastier shakes at McDonalds, when I used to eat there.  After watching all those scary films about fast food, I don't eat there anymore.

The price for the burger 4.55 and fries 2.65, ok, not terrible.  The shake?  $5.  Good grief.

This whole meal was so mediocre it makes me weep that so many people seem to like it.  Here's why Five Guys is better:
1. burger toppings, a dozen of them, build your own, you choose
2. fries are cut fresh in the kitchen, you can see the potato skin on them still, and cooked in peanut oil
3. flavor, flavor, flavor

This place doesn't have it.  You come in here, you are paying for the buildout, basically.  Nice wooden walls, stainless steel everywhere, spotless kitchen full of more stainless steel.  Looks impressive at first sight, but that is it.

My coworkers and I go here often at 8pm for lunch. Line is many times long and takes forever. They are almost always out of baked potatoes, or sometimes it's fries or soda that's out. Employees are sometimes playing or not doing anything. One time my coworker and I came in because no one answered at the to go microphone, and we found one poor kid working and the rest were sitting at two dining room tables! It's sad. If I see a line I go to Little Caesars! Pretty poor business if you ask me!

Looked over my credit card statement this past month and saw that they had charged me on two separate days for purchases - I had only gone to this place ONCE. The amount charged for the two days was different as well so clearly it was not an accidental duplicate. 

I have reported this to my credit card company. 

The food was decent but I will not be back again. I would recommend everyone who used their card to read through their statements carefully.
The chicken tikka roll is really good, and the lamb kabab roll isn't bad either.  Slightly pricy but worth it.

As I've stated in other reviews, I'm a Southern California native.  

It would be hard to write a review about Shake Shack without mentioning In & Out.  The two are often compared by visitors from the East Coast.  However, I'll leave the comparison for the end of my review.

We ordered a few of the new Bacon Cheddershack burgers, fries, and the locally brewed Shackmeister Ale.

Burger:
It was good!  Definitely in a different class than In & Out.  The patty itself is vastly different, and delicious in it's own right.  The bun is really good as well.  Super high quality, and really tasty when combined altogether.

The chedder was a nice addition, but I do not feel that it made the burger any greater than it already was (with the bacon, that is).

Fries:
Seasoned just right.  I'm a big fan of In & Out fries, and these were different (in a good way).  The crimped shape and crispy exterior gave the fries the right texture.  I'm a fan.

Shackmeister Ale:
Again, I'd have to mention that I'm a Southern California native -from North County San Diego, specifically.  Craft Beer is also our thing.  The Shackmeister Ale doesn't quite stack up to the hop heavy IPAs and high ABV ales that I am used to, but it was a refreshing addition to the heavier burger and fries.  It was provided just the right amount of refreshment to the meal, which leads me to believe that these guys know what they are doing.

So: How does Shake Shack compare to In & Out?  Well, it's in a different class.  Shack Shack costs a bit more, but you certainly get what you pay for.  However, it's hard to beat a straightforward burger, made with fresh ingredients, for a minimal fee.  

The answer is: you can't compare them.  They are apples and oranges, both great in their own right.  My taste buds will have a special place in their hearts for both of these burger franchises.

You know something must be good when it creates repeat customers - like my bf. He loves hoagies. Loves 'em more than any other food. The boy could live off of them for the rest of his life and be happy. So he's always on the lookout for better hoagies, and finally he ended up at Jimmy John's one night when he needed a late munch. Next thing I knew, he was dropping over there on weekends for lunch, ordering in after a LOOOONG day/evening in lab - and all for Jimmy John's sandwiches. 

They're not his absolute favorite (or amongst the runners-up), but they are a no-fail sandwich place, pretty much open whenever he's hungry (which can be any time of day). He'll even choose them over Wawa, his childhood hoagie/snack stop that I thought he'd never give up. He especially loves the speed at which they construct their hoagies because then he gets to eat them faster ;) The staff here seems like their college student aged, and they're really nice - one time their cash register kept breaking down whenever they tried to charge cards, and they were so apologetic about it I wanted to give them a hug and say its okay. But I can only imagine what its like during the school year around lunch time...

This place has created some interesting memories for wife and I, our most memorable (but not favorable) memory was when my wife and I ate here during St. Patrick's Day. Let's just say it was hectic and extremely uncomfortable, almost making me foodie rage. However, we both remember the burgers tasting amazing. We decided to try Shake Shack again, and after taking a leisurely stroll to 20th and Sansom, we ordered our SmokeShack (bacon, cherry peppers and shack sauce) and ShackStack (burger with a cheese stuffed mushroom on top), and realized that our bus was leaving soon, and that we're so tired for walking that sitting down may spell certain doom for the both of us. Instead we asked for our burgers "to go". It was disappointing to see that they do not wrap their burgers for take-out. lAfter 2 hours in transit, we arrived home, Take out didn't do those burgers justice, having to reheat them felt like a crime against foodies. I don't suggest you take out, unless you work or live close by.

Ehhh, wasn't a huge fan. The chicken I had was on the dry side and a tad burnt. Also after it was done cooking, they just drizzled the sauce on top. I like when the sauce is cooked in with the meat so it's nice and flavorful. 

Service was also very slow. They had a ton of meat grilling, but yet it took forever to get my order. Maybe if they took it off a lil earlier, it wouldn't have been so overdone and I would have gotten my lunch in a reasonable time.

There are few things I crave more than Korean tacos so naturally I had to try this place while checking out Chinatown Square. I decided to try the double fried chicken tacos simply because they sounded pretty awesome. The wait was really reasonable, the portion was huge however, the tacos themselves were ok. The chicken was a bit dry but perfectly crispy.  The salsa on top provided the needed acidity but it was falling off the chicken.  All in all this place seemed cool and I'm sure once they work through opening week, they will make those good components great. I'd definitely give them another go.

wait time was incredibly long. seemed like they forgot about my order until i complained 5 times. they also "ran out of burgers" at 1:42pm, which i cannot understand how that happens at a place with burger in the name. garbage place don't go

Looking for something fresh, quick and packed with spicy goodness on my Yelp24 app that was close to my center city office following my noon conference call (who has a call at lunch time?!). And there you were. I marked it for 12:30 pick up, rather than delivery, so I could run out and get some fresh air & as I walked in at 12:25 they were packaging my food - Hot right off the grill! I had a veggie combo with rice. Spice Level HAWT. Service was greeted with a smile, I was addressed by my name, which rarely happens. Unsure if I would ever dine in - Lunch rush made it quite the tight squeeze but nevertheless would definitely order from there again.

This a new place in Chinatown. Portions are generous, food is fresh, place is clean and cute, free wifi, fair prices. Just one aspect: Service could be better. I told the cashier that it was my first time and she didn't really knew what to suggest. Also, she forgot to mention that people usually purchase sauce to accompany the food. These little details are important because it affects the experience and the food flavor, specially if the restaurant is trying to bring new customer who aren't familiar with Taiwanese food. I tried the Popcorn chicken Bento, and I bought the Thai sauce. It was good, you should try it.

Super friendly staff that really cared to make the experience as great as possible. I wasn't just a customer, I was a friend. Shake shack is the place to be for good burgers (and even COULD IT BE?? CORNNNNDOGS available only on holiday weekends). Enjoy.

What can I say? Delicious food, drink, and cruelty free! The disco chic'n is a favorite. Breakfast is good too but lunch beats it. It's small so be prepared to take food to go but there is some small seating in the lobby area next to it. You won't even know it isn't meat, I swear. It's amazing!!

Fun place for burger and shakes, with lots of great outdoor seating in the warm seasons. Super casual, no fuss. The burgers are good, but for me, they're just a bit on the small side. The fries are very dry and potatoe-y... All in all, a good spot for above average fast food.

This is hands down, no contest the worst McDonalds I have ever been to.  Been 3 times, twice waited for more than 20 minutes.  Food came out incorrect both times.  Third time tonight, they were only accepting cash.  I had no cash and had no way of getting out of line because they box you in with a curb.

First time eating here & it was a great experience. I had a free sub card from awhile ago so I decided why not give it a try! I ordered the #6 veggie club and boy was it good! I thought it wouldn't fill me up but good gracious it did. 

Their roll is so fresh and soft which made my sandwich that much better. The staff was friendly and I love the fact that the change their gloves after making every sandwich. It's not like a freakin assembly line like they do at subway. Well done Jimmy John's you've earned a new customer !

Really great Philly Cheesteaks.  Consistently good.  No BS, just the real deal.  I like the Chipotle Cheesteak.  Recommend when at 30th Street catching the train.
Bravo Jersey Mike's!

The food quality was good but The service was so incredibly slow especially for being a food court location. A very long line and at one point while waiting, not a single employee was actively receiving orders as the lone just continued to grow. No kids meals or Mac and cheese are served at this location which is odd especially since it is at a mall.

No photos, but worth a visit.

Must get: ziggy burger and chick'n sandwiches
Meh: curry tofu wrap
Missed out: desserts

I am neither a vegan nor hipster, however, I can appreciate a good sandwich. Hipcityveg is a small joint, with maybe 2-3 seats for the casual visitor to enjoy their food. The staff were friendly and pleasant and we were able to order without any significant delays. Of note, the food is made on order, so you may need to wait a while. I was surprised by both of burger/sandwiches that my friends got. They were scrumptous but so...small! The faux meat didn't taste like meat...but I never expect nor care for an exact mimicry. However, the tempeh/soy equivalent was very well seasoned and had a great mouthfeel. I did not like the curry tofu wrap, as the wheat wrap itself was overwhelming and robbed the flavoring of the curry.

Many of the options were about $8+, so you definitely may need more than one to stave off your hunger, but if you're vegan or just like plain good food, hipcityveg will hit the spot.

Food: 4 stars
Price: 3-4 stars
Service: 4 stars
Ambiance: 3 stars

So fed up with this location I just have to write a review. I've been disappointed with the quality and value of every single, and I mean every single sandwich I've ever purchased from here. And maybe its just because it's the busy downtown location why everything always seems to be lackluster (but then I remember the delicious, and consistent Panera Bread a 7 minute walk away). Anyways, today's "tuna salad" sandwich fell short. Based on flavor alone, I'm not sure it was even tuna...and the scoop wasn't distributed well through the bread leaving me to munch down wads of bread and just tasted like watery tomatoes. In other words, zero flavor. But it'll keep me from passing out post-workout. Previous sandwiches always let me down in the presentation department and usually look sad and unappetizing once I get them back to my office just across the street. Not to mention the amount of unnecessary packaging for a pick-two. 
I usually only stumble in here as a last resort because there aren't a lot of options in this quadrant of center city for a quick sandwich on the weekends.

I've heard other locations are better, but this location....I'm tired and I just want a decent sandwich.
I got the veg Biryani. Not as many vegetables as I would have guessed, but the spice makes up for it. Staff was prompt and courteous.

This is the second time I ordered a sausage and scrambled egg breakfast hoagie and there was no sausage on it. $9 for a roll with eggs on it. I hate the wawa on chestnut st but at least they give me what I order.

Look, you don't need another review to know Chick-Fil-A has great food. You also don't need a review to know they have the nicest people working there. They are so sweet, I got a cavity last time I was there. But try the shakes, they are outstanding. Also, download their APP, it gives you free  food sometimes, and you can use it as a debit card when you're short on cash. However, it doesn't work at the airport, so bring cash there. I usually get the same thing when I visit; 2 sandwiches, waffle fries, and a diet Dr. Pepper. But they have so much  more. And why do I always get a craving on Sundays when they're closed?
Awesome service. A fast food joint where the manager actually walks around and touches tables. Well done.

Stopped in for lunch with a friend - first visit, very impressed. The Philly Steak was very good (although it would be nice to have a whole wheat sandwich bun option, which I didn't see) and the Smokehouse Burger as well. Very good sweet potato fries, too. I will say that Sriracha Aiolli that comes with the fries was good, but also very typical aiolli - nothing special.
