My friend got the chicken tikka kati roll and he really liked it. I will deff be going back. Glad to find a place that does platters and actually does it right.

Went here with family (7 of us) and tried a little of everyone's food. Very good burgers and loved the loaded fries with cheese on them. So good. 

My husband and I went in for a strawberry mint lemonade to drink while the family was eating their burgers (we wanted to eat somewhere more upscale later on, but also love fast food) 

Imagine our delight when the server said 'don't worry about it'. 'huh?' 'no, i mean, it's only a drink. You don't need to pay anything. Enjoy!' 

What a sweet gesture... definitely earns a glowing yelp review. 

Also BTW the shakes are amazing here (tried the very thick and indulgent salted caramel one). But be warned, the calorie count for their one single size ranges up into the upper hundreds of calories, 840 I think was the highest, and it doesn't say which specific milkshake that applies to! It's no Five Guys but it's good!

do YOU know about gaypotle?

gaypotle (n): a magical place that appeared when i wished for it; a multi-seat fishbowl style complex from which you can creep on ghood dwellers; the east-of-broad [more convenient] location of equally tasty establishment referred to as chipotle. see also: heaven, scrumptious.

get some wifi and i'll promptly move in.
wow....quality sandwitches at a fair price. huge size, overstuffed, still cheap! love it here. great branding too.
I love Jersey Mike's subs, but was extremely disappointed that this location refuses to accept coupons that I receive from Jersey Mike's Email Club. False Advertising.

Spice end is the newest kati roll and platters take out, fast food, and restaurant joint - all in one! To make it even better, Spice End is located in Center City and open until 3am on weekends!

I would definitely recommend it to everyone. My favorite kati rolls include the aloo paneer roll, paneer tikka roll, and achari paneer roll. The briyani is also amazing as well. The staff is extremely friendly and very accommodating. The inside is very clean and there are plenty of seats available inside. I would definetly recommend this place to everyone!
I ordered a vegan cheesesteak and it tasted just like a real cheesesteak.  The brownie is amazing and tastes like the real thing. This is my new spot when I visit Philly.

Delicious giant club. Ultimate porker is great. Service was quick and not bad. They were friendly and nice. Sandwich is awesome. Staff asked all necessary questions. Will recommend it and come again. Jimmy johns great sandwich shop.

If you're really, really, really hard-pressed for cash and you have a craving for Taco Bell, I suppose this mini-restaurant suffices. There are no chairs or tables, but the cashier is usually friendly. 

Sometimes the food is warm, and sometimes it isn't.

They close rather early, sometime around 6:00 pm on weeknights? Not many restaurants are open late in the Concourse late at night, which is unfortunate for late-night commuters.

If you go during peak times (late morning/early afternoon/PM rush) and you stop by for a quick food fix, don't be alarmed if you are approached by people asking for change/money/food. It goes with the territory, you know. Some will brazenly approach those waiting in line.
I go here all the time for lunch and its really good.  I haven't had anything bad yet but I wouldn't call it healthy.  It's like a greasy version of Panera.  The chicken pomodoro panini is my fave.
1st time here and only stopped for fries and a BW shake and they did not disappoint! Soooo good. The real deal. Busy all the time though.

Cold stale food I would not recommend this place to anybody looking for anything appetizing even if it is a MC
crapper Burger

What a disappointment! I normally love the Shack Burger at the Madison Square NYC location, but the Philly one paled greatly in comparison. It was dry, the sauce was bland, the tomato wasn't ripe and they forgot the lettuce. Maybe they need a demonstration in how to cook a juicy burger and make the sauce properly from the NYC location.

If you're looking for ambience and artfully-executed food presentation, this is not the place for you.  If you're just about the food and don't mind some spice, then try this place.  I love the achari paneer roll with generous doses of the red and white sauces :-)

Their Cheese fries are amazing. And don't get me started on the coffee malt !!! You could tell it was the servers first day but I didn't mind they were really nice , even though we got there like 10 minutes till closing!

My job had me work in Philadelphia temporarily for a month and, lacking a kitchen, I was presented with the classic traveling work dilemma of eating out for every meal or.... eating out for every meal.  Enter Snap Kitchen!

I signed up for their 5 day/week meal plan, getting lunch and dinner every day and allowing myself hospital oatmeal for breakfast (I swear, it is delicious).  The price was very reasonable.  I was consistently impressed by every meal, but here are some winners:

Bison Quinoa Hash
Chicken Pad Thai
Chimichurri Chicken
Beef Lasagna
Mango Beet Poke Bowl
Turkey Chilli 

What really stuck out, though, was the customer service.  Snap was on my walk from the hospital to home so I figured doing pick up just made sense.  On more than one occasion, it was getting close to closing time and I was still at work.  Invariably, they would call to see if it looked like I was going to make it in and, if not, offered to keep it refrigerated overnight.  Additionally, when they were out of something I ordered, a real person (!!!) would text me with specific suggestions for substitutions.  It just made everything so easy.

Icing on the cake?  I found some of my new favorite snacks!  Healthcare professionals take special note, because all of these are easily carry-able in your scrubs.

Thunderbird Bars: I think I could just eat these all day and be happy.  My all time favorite is the Pecan, Goji, and Pistachio bar but Cashew, Fig, and Carrot is a close second.  They are all super filling and great for a quick snack,

Barnana:  These are chewy bites of banana with the option of with or without peanut butter.  For me, peanut butter is the obvious answer (always), but the plain are just as tasty. 

P.S. Cookie Dough: I love cookie dough.  I could easily sit and eat it all day.  Great thing about these are that they are A) salmonella free and B) made out of beans!  There are chocolate chip (garbanzo bean), peanut butter (garbanzo bean), and fudge brownie (black bean) options, all of which will satisfy your craving.

My only complaint?  They aren't in DC!

Fast food Indian! Yay! It's so good! Really good prices for the area too. I had the Paneer platter and it was great! Just enough food to satisfy you.  The paneer is light and flavorful. The rice is perfectly moist and the pita is soft. The spices they top it off with add just enough savory flavor to balance everything out. Everything was fresh and fast.  If you need a quick and delicious Indian fix,  this is your place.

These guys are no joke.  The food is ample, fresh , spicy and delicious.  Ingredients are always fresh and delicious.  I've tried a number of their selections and have not been disappointed in any of them.

This place is my go-to for rolls and mixed dishes. You can't go wrong with any of their rolls (ignore the prices, they're huge and absolutely worth it) and their combo dishes are to die for. Make sure you try the hot/red sauce before you apply it because it takes a while to get used to.

Went there today while working in center city Philly. Decided to try the chicken teriyaki. Best choice I made in weeks regarding lunch lol. Food is grilled in front of you. Excellent portion size. Music selection was pretty good as well. Chill environment to stop in and grub real quick. 10/10 times whenever I'm in center city I will be going there.

Work time lunch place, always packed from 11 am to 2pm weekdays.  Proximity, size and location surely dictates why the suits are always populating this chain place.  It sure can't be for the outstanding food or the kitchen that works at a glacial pace.

Like anyone who works in this area of the city, Corner Bakery, like Cosi, is a lazy no-brainer option to grab lunch if you've got the tenacity to wait 10-20 minutes for a to-go order.   I try not to make a habit of it so I go there once or twice a month.  Soups and salads are the way to go, just make sure they do the dressing on the side as they like to drown 'em.  Also, don't expect that you're doing some healthy eatin' either, a quick inspection of the nutrition information makes you go into instant cardiac arrest.

The question that I always ask myself is that why does the food come quicker when you're eating-in? Doesn't an "order to-go" receive priority? If you're just plating pre-made salads shouldn't it take a couple minutes tops?  Also, and more importantly, why do I keep coming back here? AND... If a tree falls in the woods and no one's there to hear it does it make a sound?

Really delicious food! Tons of flavor and feels very authentic. The kati rolls are definitely the item to get but everything else I have had was good, too. The only item I did not love were the samosas.

Although it is your typical chain restaurant, I really can't complain about this location! It's very close to offices and Jefferson campus and the hospital, very central in the city. Their service is extremely quick, sandwiches made almost immediately. They ask if you want mayo and if you want the roll cut (I advise yes). It's as cheap as any other jimmy johns. I've never really had any problems with it. For some reason I really like their thick cut chips. 
I do know that Jefferson often gets catering from them for certain events and I don't believe there's ever been any problems! Large platters of sandwiches and cookies. Their cookies are delicious by the way.

I left Seattle five years ago and have been on the hunt for decent Teriyaki ever since. I gave up on eating Teriyaki outside of WA after experiencing one too many bland and soggy dishes. This place is legit. The meat is grilled and the sauce is thick and exploding with flavor.  I did think it was a little weird to get potato salad with it, but it was tasty. Add a teriyaki and gyoza special and you'll own my tastebuds as long as I live in Philadelphia.

Guess kfc is getting better or we lucked out this day -the crispy chicken was piping hot and delicious and the sides were very fresh-better than popeyes which is extremely hit and miss as they always threw in a dried out piece of chicken.  That is why we decided to try Kfc again.   We will convert to kfc in the future as long as the quality stays top notch.

Jimmy John's is my favorite place to get a fresh sandwich.  I haven't had JJ's since I moved from Charlotte to Philly and tonight I decided to stop by. 

I ordered my usual: the #12 Beach Club on wheat, with no mayo and I added onions and oregano.  Amazing!  It was just as fresh as I had remembered it... the crunch of the fresh sprouts really makes the sandwich. 

This was definitely worth walking through the thunderstorm.  :)
Not Bad, But Not Worth the Hype, Its really just another burger joint

I don't understand the Shake Shack hype.  If I want fast food burgers I'll go to McDonalds for $1 McDoubles. If I want a better burger I'll go to Village Whiskey (literally right next door) for $10. There is nothing particularly special about this chain--I feel like most people rave about it because it came from NYC. 

Five Guys burgers are cheaper and better. 

P.S their fries suck.

Corner bakery is a good spot for business lunches, right outside the Comcast center in the heart of the business district downtown.  I eat here alot for lunch since I work close by.  The food is kind of expensive for lunch ($10+ once you add tax)  but the food is really good so its OK.  The sandwhiches are hearty and on very delicous bread.  The salads are big, and you can even get a half/half combo.  They have pretty good mac n cheese as a side order to your sandwhich.  I usually order the California Grille panini, which is eggplant and lots of veggies with artichokes on a whole grain bread.  I love this one.  I even ate breakfast here once, had cold steel-cut oatmeal with walnuts and crainberries, it was delicous!  There's also plenty of seating inside, the place is pretty big.  Order at the counter, and either take to-go, or carry your order number to a table and the wait staff will bring it to you.

I learned of Spice End through a photo on Instagram. The photo showed a familiar round aluminum to-go plate with white and hot sauces covering rice, meats, and some pita on the side. It looked LEGIT. I was then eager to hunt this plate of chicken and rice down to compare it to the NYC Halal Guys. Sad to say, but after I had the first bite, I wasn't too excited anymore. The rice is basmati rice, the white sauce was more like tzatziki sauce than the Halal white sauce, and the plate is expensive! I did, however, like the chicken and lamb that was in the platter. 


Didn't satisfy my Halal Chicken and Rice craving, so I probably wouldn't be back anytime soon.

The burgers are good, the fries are good, and they're overpriced. The most natural comparison for Shake Shack is In n Out, which everyone is kind of trying to copy these days. They do a pretty decent job with the burgers (totally different type of fries). 

The biggest difference is price. You can get a double double with fries at In n Out for $6 or so depending on location. Shake Shack? $10.50. If I'm paying $10.50 for a burger and fries I expect one of two things: tons of food or verrry good quality (think nicer place like village whiskey). 

I'm glad shake shack is there because if I NEED  burger fast, that's where I'll go, I just wish their prices were lowered, because then I'd probably go a whole lot more often.

Oh and their cheese fries could use some grilled onion on them.

The food was good, as street food goes, until you realize you're paying $10.  That combined with all the attitude from the woman taking my order (who couldn't seem to get off of her phone) make it only ok.  Should be listed as $$.

You really can't go wrong with shake shack.  Plus, they serve alcohol.  Its a winning combination, burgers and beers.  My only riff about this place is they need more selections for vegetarians.  My only choice here is the shroom burger with cheese, fries, and drinks.  I wish they were a bit more vegetarian friendly.  You also got to love their ice creams, shakes, and custards.  

Be careful when you bite into the shroom burger, hot cheese will ooze out and it is  piping hot!

Went there for lunch. Placed my order and asked for a cheesecake brownie, the cashier gave me attitude saying they didn't have any left and that I would have to wait for more to come so I agreed and sat down. I finished my food and had to ask someone where it was ten minutes later they brought me a frozen brownie. I made the mistake of going there again with my mother and found 3 long hairs in my food. Disgusting !
Burgers and shakes are excellent stuff. Fries not so much unfortunately.

PHILADELPHIA: any time spent with Brie really works up an appetite because we try to explore as much as possible in whatever town we're visiting.

We were craving breakfast and found HipCityVeg, a small plant-based chain in the city. We went to their 121 South Broad St. location, very close to Penn Square. It's a very tiny place, but you can bring your dog into the restaurant to order and then sit at their tables in the vestibule of the North American building which is attached to the place. Sitting in the lobby gave Brie the opportunity to meet so many nice people and get lots of pets and give lots of kisses.

The food is excellent and we recommend the HipCity Breakfast sandwich (tofu egg, organic soy mayo, & tempeh). Prices are also reasonable. Can this place come to NJ??? Even a worker said he's not vegan, but loves the food! We love any place that's dog friendly and animal cruelty free.

Still five stars, but have now also tried the:

-chili glazed salmon with coconut rice and snap peas (the rice in particular was slammin)
-deviled eggs
-tuscan kale snack

:) :) :)

Can't be better. 

If you're complaining about spending $6 on a great burger, just go to McNausea and get a $1 ptomaine special. 

Or go across the street to Village Whiskey and pay $26 for a burger.
The worst ghetto people and unclean gave me food poisoning absolutely horrible. Go to the Popeyes on island ave instead

Best place to eat proper chicken biryani in Philadelphia. Being from Calcutta, I can say Spice End makes outstanding kati rolls which are very fresh and great in taste. Since they are open till 3 AM on weekends, great for post clubbing snacks.

This location is inside the train station fyi.  This is like franchise or something because they don't honor anything club rewards related to earn or use points. They didn't accept a coupon I presented them. The food is up to par, it was tasty. Won't come back to this location due to lack of honoring rewards club.

Came here on Tuesday: tacos are $2 each! I was surprised because there was no sign up, so I guess it's word of mouth. So I got an double-fried chicken tacos. The chicken was pretty good, it was moist and seasoned nicely and was crispy. The rest of the taco (corn tortilla!) had nicely seasoned corn and beans, plain white rice and a thick Korean chili sauce (ssam) and came with radishes and lime. I didn't care for the ssam or lime because I felt like it took away from the flavors of the taco itself. 
That being said, the only person working there was really nice. If I'm near Chinatown Square, I will try some of the other options here.

I order from Jimmy John's for work meetings on a regular basis because they are convenient and my team really loves them.
I have never been a huge fan, but once in a while I'll add a sandwich for myself to give it another shot... today was one of those times and I was disappointed.
I faxed in the order at 11am to be delivered at 12pm. Everything was written down in detail, but somehow, they forgot a bottle of water and my sandwich came with the sprouts although I had requested for them to be taken off. The tuna salad in my sandwich didn't taste like much and there really wasn't a lot, I mostly got stuck with the hated sprouts (seriously, do you guys not like regular lettuce?) and bread. 
Overall a bad sandwich which I'll never order again. 
In the defense of Jimmy John's, the employees are super nice and the service is very quick, and I guess as long as my team is happy, that's all that matters. But I won't be eating their food again any time soon.

The portions are a little small for the price but I could not believe how good the food is. They put all the calories, fats, etc. On the packages. Friendly staff and It's quick and convenient. I could bot believe healthy food could taste this good.

Been here 3-4 times now out of late night desperation and tbh not a fan. I know they offer more, but I'm always craving chicken over rice, which is over $11 with a bottle of water (they do not offer cups???) which I could get from a nearby food truck and it would be at least twice as good, less than half the price, and faster. White sauce tastes like almost straight mayo and the rice is v bland. Chicken is v finely shredded and kind of skimpy. You're paying for the convenience here, not the quality.
Burgers are good, I always order med rare and they seem to be cooked perfect and  seasoned well. Staff is great and very helpful.

Uh...I don't even eat at Popeyes at all.  And I don't live anywhere near this part of town.  But stumbled across this news story from August 1 2019, while I was googling something else.  Thought I'd do a good deed in issuing a PSA: For the love of GOD, DO NOT EAT HERE. Someone took video of the restaurant while it was closed and there were literally "dozens" of mice running across the floor, bumping into each other.  Never seen anything like it.  NASTY INFESTATION.  If you absolutely must have greasy, cheap, takeout fried chicken - go somewhere else.  Sucks that you can't give zero stars on this app.  You've been warned.
Believe the hype. And oh my god those crinkle-cut cheese fries. Also, the employees were very friendly. Also, I want to go back right now.

I've ate from Shake shack 3 times ever. Once I dined in at KOP which was great. I've ordered twice from this location through DoorDash. The first time wasn't bad. The wait for my food wasn't long probably 35 minutes altogether. My food was still warm. Last night I ordered and to keep it short I had a few issues with the Door-dasher. Luckily I'm honest because he was going to give me someone else's order too. From the time I ordered and got my food it was about 50 minutes. My food was cool. I ordered the smoke shack my daughter had the shack burger. I couldn't help but question what the difference between her burger and their regular cheese burger was. I felt when I dined and when I ordered the first time the burger was much bigger and the fries portions were also larger. In fact they used this little box container to put the fries in this time, before it was a bag that most fries come in. I'm not sure if it's just this location doing it or if it's because shake shack has grown but this was a turn off. The quality and quantity of the food are how you keep customers.

Here for conference from OKC. searched for a vegetarian friendly place. Although close to my hotel, it took me two tries to find it. Had the crispy buffalo chikn sandwich and it was beyond delicious. Wish we had a franchise in OKC. Staff were nice also.

In a city of subs and cheesesteaks, why come to Jimmy John's? Surprisingly coming here has consistently been a positive experience. 1) staff is welcoming 2) food is fresh and good 3) you can customize with sandwich made quickly 4) dining area is clean 5) refill machine available 6) decent portions.  I recommend getting the number 9 night club Italian for $5.99. Bread is soft and cold cuts are a decent quality considering this is a chain. Food prep area seemed clean. Note one of the cleanest bathrooms in the city is connected to this store thru the building next door.

I'm writing because this if my first shake shack experience. 

EXPENSIVE! I know everyone can do the math, BUT
2 burgers, 2 shakes, 2 fries = 34 dollars and some change. 

That's fine if the the portions fit the price. This shack burger (single) was smaller than the JR cheeseburger at Wendy's, that's right the JUNIOR burger at Wendy's. Three bites and this burger is completely gone. The burger is so small that the tomatoes they put on are the size of nickels, just so they're not hanging of the edge. 

The fries.. they're crinkle-accordion style fries. so immature, and AND they come in this tiny little container. The sauce tasted like they melted a kraft single in a jar, oh wait, I'm sorry a generic kraft single... let's call it a cheese square.

Don't come here if you don't like wasting earned money. If you happen to stumble upon a suitcase full of money, then and only then is it worth it to come here. 

Very clean establishment and very fast service. They're shake was very good. This earned them 2 stars. 

There are so many better places to get better quality food, bigger portions and a cheaper menu all around the area. 

Thanks for reading.

This place is the bane of my existence. It pushes and pulls on my emotions daily. The smell wafts into the air for at least a mile. 

The biscuits and chicken are so goddamn good. However I get sick when I eat there. 

It's way better than KFC or Boston Market. I have high cholesterol and I know I can't eat these greasy shit anymore. Even the fries squirt a little when you bite into them. 

Everyone working here does not want to work here. I don't blame them. 

Last month they got robbed and a fella with a gun ran through my place of business. 

Conclusion: Popeyes on woodland is dangerous in more ways than one.

The quickest place to grab a bite at 
Every single time I go I would only have to wait about 5 minutes  or less for my food and haven't experienced it yet but probably 10 minutes max when it's busy 

The chicken teriyaki bowl they have is very delicious. I believe they use chicken thigh which in my opinion is a good choice because it's tender , juicy , and flavorful. Plus they cook it with a nice char on the chicken and gives it a good crunch.

 The teriyaki sauce just goes perfect with the chicken  and rice . They will garnish green onion and sesame on top  which gives it's a nice color. 

 I also had the steak teriyaki , which is also a good choices for all you beef lovers. They don't over cook the steak and again they have a good char on it for a nice crunch.
 Check this place out ! Plus if you're in the mood for some good donuts , Federal donuts is less then 100 ft away !

Every time I come here, it's just as good as the last time. The food is amazing, filling, and cheap. The employees are always super pleasant. Your food will be done and in your hands in less than five minutes. Sure, they use @ramen branded bowls, but who cares if the food is good? Seriously. Go here. You won't regret it.
This is a good play on the New York City version of Platters and Kati Roll. The Kati Rolls and Platters feel way more flavorful and less greasy (which is a good thing) than the NY Originals.
Food is good. It is a little pricey but not too much. It is worth it to get a healthy meal.

Whoa.  It almost seems like it's a trend to hate this place.  

I wasn't wowed, but I definitely didn't regret my trip to Shake Shack.  The line was tamer today than I'm guessing it's been for the past month, so we only waited about 15 minutes from the time we walked in the door until we got our food.  Not fast food, but definitely not slow food, either.    

I went with a single hamburger with pickles, tomato, and lettuce.  I thought the meat was flavorful, it was cooked thoroughly, and it was tender.  The lettuce and tomatoes were pretty typical and the pickles were awesome (they use the thick-cut deli style pickles on their burgers).  People keep hating on the buns, but I had no issue with mine.  And a lot of the reviews say that they are unhappy with the size of the burger, but I thought the portion was spot on.

We split an order of fries and I found them to be tasty.  I finished off my meal with the small homemade lemonade and I was ready to go back outside and combat the heatwave.  I didn't leave feeling disgustingly full.

All in all, not the most amazing place on the face of the Earth, but certainly not the major disappointment that I was expecting after reading the many Yelp reviews.  Gosh, we're becoming a mean little community!  If we can afford to try a $16 meal at Shake Shack, our lives aren't so bad, right?  Group hug, everyone.

Eh. 

I know they get a lot of traffic and I try to be extra friendly, but I'm still treated with a cold expressionless face from every employee at this location. They also routinely underserve me and I'm not sure if it's because I'm petite, but it's quite irritating having to ask for the same amount of food as every other person in line. "Can I please have more meat?" "could you please add more lettuce?" This gets really old and makes me sound like a whiny customer. 

On the upside, it tastes good and I always enjoy my meal.

Been giving them chances after chance after chance and they never get it right my fries or either not cooked all the way after waiting in line through the drive thru for a good half an hour. Today my chicken sandwich was over cooked. I honestly did not each it. It was as if Wendy's had cooked it twice.  I've honestly had it with this place and I'm not longer going to waste my time or money and just pack me a lunch each day for work now I thought it was a nice cheap or affordable lunch but it's something I can't even enjoy.

Discovered Snap Kitchen right at the end of my first round of Whole30 and was SUPER mad about it, because I wish I had known this amazing place existed from the beginning.  For ANY type of dietary restriction, you can find something here.  Even if you don't have a dietary restriction but you are looking for a quick, healthy meal on the go, Snap is the place for you.

It's quick and convenient, but not cheap. The price tag comes with healthy food no matter what, though. I also love that they have microwaves for you to heat up your meal and eat in-house.  They also deliver(!!!) and they have a rewards program! So if you are planning to come back frequently, make sure you enroll.

Okay, here's my take on Shake Shack.  First of all it's busy, very busy but I like places with a buzz so that's a plus.  The service is incredibly friendly.  An older man next to me got up to get some condiments and one of the workers told him to next time tell her and she'll get anything needed for him so he doesn't have to get up from his table while eating. Another plus. It's def cool looking for a fast food place.  Plus # 3.  The food was very good as well - a tasty Shack burger and fries hit the spot.  The 4th plus. 
 Any downside .... well yeah.  It's def a little bit pricey for fast food and the portion size.  The burger isn't that big nor is the portion of fries.  So one minus.  
Total:  4 plusses, 1 minus.  I'll def head back again.

I was hoping this new Panda Express would be another lunch option for me and my coworkers but sadly the food was just mediocre at best. The staff was very friendly and food was very fresh. The dining area was also really nice and clean; but then again they are super new. 

Since this was my first time, I got the big platter with 3 entrees and 1 side. This was way too much food for 1 person, but I really wanted to try a variety of their dishes. I got the chow mean noodles as my side/starch and the following three entrees: orange chicken, honey walnut shrimp, Shanghai angus steak. The latter 2 dishes were "premium" selections so they cost $1.25 extra each. I also ordered the side vegetable spring rolls which actually come with 2 in an order.  

Verdict? The chow mein was dry but flavoring was ok; the orange chicken was crispy but way too sweet;  walnut shrimp was very fresh and decent but pretty heavily breaded; angus beef was ok. The vegetable spring rolls were kind of wet in the middle...I'm thinking it was slightly under fried but I didn't bother to ask. I didn't finish the spring rolls after 1 bite and I didn't finish my food.  This place has potential but the food didn't cut it did me.

I am really not sure what the hype about shake shack is. Don't get me wrong, the burgers are good. But for the price and ravings I expected more. The fries were likewise underwhelming. 
Definitely will come back for shakes though!

I must say that its one of the cleanest places I've ever worked and had the best cheesesteaks around! If you are not from philly ans want a quality cheesesteak this is the place to get it! Absolutely delicious subs also! The staff are very helpful and friendly especially the manager. Some of the newer staff somewhat makes the workers who have worked there longer look bad by nit really going with the flow of the more experienced crew but other than that this place is awesome. The dedication of the workers and managers is amazing! Would recommend to anyone!
Awful everything cold. Fries soggy. Seemed they were closing at 730. Floors soaked ice machine down. Manager seemed high. Just awful.

I stopped in here after a quick search yielded this new spot in Center City. I came for a quick, filling lunch, and that's exactly what I got. 

I ordered the $7.99 Chicken Teriyaki, and after telling them I wanted to eat in, they said for me to have a seat and that it'll be out shortly. I waited less than 5 minutes and the food was ready. It was definitely a bigger bowl than I had expected. Many pieces of chicken, and a big hefty portion of rice - definitely worth the money. It came with a side of macaroni salad, which was tasty, but I didn't eat much of it because expensive calories. 

The staff was super nice! They greet everyone who enters and everyone who leaves. They just opened up and are really excited to do business, so go ahead and give them some love! 

One thing I would like to see is some veggie sides, maybe something cucumber or edamame, because the potato/macaroni salads are a little too heavy (it'd be good to have some options).

Ordered a customized classic burger - patty was a bit salty and greasy (so use a plate), but the fried onions were a nice touch, and the sauce really tied everything together. The cheese fries were crispy and exceptionally well seasoned, gone within minutes. Short wait for order, and staff were cool and sociable.

This newly established Taiwanese fried chicken place was, IMO, a tad better than the other one that opened up in Chinatown. The quality of fairly similar between the the two, but you can't beat the price and amount you get here compared to the other one.

I've been here twice and I must say I thoroughly enjoy their popcorn chicken combo boxes. The drinks aren't anything too impressive, but the food compensates for it! They also charge for even normal tap water which is absurd IMO.

Another downside was that they were superrrr slow getting or order made. Literally waited for over 30 minutes for like 7 orders to go. Hopefully they speed up as they get into the rhythm of things, but if they don't by the next visit then I'll have to dock a star.

Terrible service, and terrible management - took 20 mins for a milkshake, and that was only after asked. There is also an employee who screams order names at the top of her lungs, terribly unprofessional. This location is the worst Chick-fill-A I've ever been to.

I don't usually eat burgers, and I cringe whenever I have to eat fast food burgers. I just don't enjoy the horrible, greasy, UGHHHH feeling I get afterwards. But when I had my first Shack Stack, I was blown away! The beef was tender and juicy, but my favorite part of the burger was the deep fried 'shroom, filled with melty cheese that oozed out after each bite. But after eating here 3-4 times, the excitement sort of faded away. The burgers are overpriced and way too oily. The buns sometimes come out soggy and are too small to hold everything inside. Eating it gets pretty messy. The hand-cut fries are a hit or miss; sometimes they're nice and crispy, other times they're soggy and limp.

Dirtiest Chipotle ever. 
Floors look they haven't swept all day. 
Counters and tables were filthy gross. 
No ice in ice machine. 
Grill filled with burnt meat that hasn't been cleaned all day. Just gross. What's going on???

I could eat their chicken tikka wrap every day. Requested mine with no chutney (hate cilantro) and no onion (allergic) and it despite a slightly odd look, my wish was granted. The cashier was very friendly. We were there not long after they opened for lunch on a rainy Sunday but there were already several patrons. 

I also got a lamb wrap but was so full from the chicken I hardly touched it. It was good, but without the raita (lactose intolerant, I know, FML) or chutney it was a bit dry. Not their fault for my issues. I also found the texture a bit different than I expected- less pulled meat, more ground and a bit mushy, but it tasted good.

Two rolls was too much for me, but some might not be entirely satisfied by one. Luckily, they're only like $6 or something! A lunch for myself and friend of two rolls each and a bottle of water was only $20 with my Yelp check-in deal. Not too shabby! I will be back for that chicken tikka for sure...

I'm from California, and it's hard to get delicious and decently priced Korean food in the city.  Coreanos is the perfect fix for me!

I ordered the rice bowl.  You choose your protein and toppings.  I got bulgogi, gochujang, kimchi, and veggies in it with salsa on the side.  The kimchi and bulgogi actually tastes like kimchi and bulgogi.  I was so happy about how authentic it tasted. The gochujang made the bowl a little sweet, but it was delicious.  The portion is generous (that you can save some for later!), and all of this was $12.  I was able to pay with a credit card, so the "cash only" statement may not be true anymore.

Friendly service + authentic taste + decent price = will be coming again!  Looking forward to trying their other dishes!
Gonna keep this short and simple 11$ for a double burger than barely fills you up and sits in the window for 5 minutes and is lukewarm? thanks but no thanks. Not great customer service either.
Pizza was good but staff very rude and rush u. One guy did not wear hear net. Flies all over the place. Not worth it when and pizza is nearby and clean!

For late night food, Spice End gets 6-stars!  Seriously, their offerings are delicious no matter when you get them, but add to that being open until 3 AM!!

Food Quality:  I know I started this review with details about how late they are open.  No, that does not mean its just 'drunk food' that no one would ever enjoy sober.  In fact, I was introduced to Spice End complete sober and amazed by the rolls.  I recommend the Lamb Kabab, but was equally impressed with the Chicken Tikka.  

Food Quantity: A single roll might not fill you up if you've had nothing else to eat, but is certainly enough to put some food back in your system.  I haven't had a platter yet, but they seem to be more sizable.

Price:  Seriously, dirt cheap.  And they take credit.  Oh and check in w/Yelp for a nice discount.

Everything Else: I don't what else you need to know to check this place out.  The Mango Lassi is sweeet!  They have teas and other drinks.  The place is clean (even at 2-3AM) and the staff is friendly.  They have veggie options as well!
My dad brought some nuggets and fries. I thought it tasted good but after a hour, I felt nauseous and my stomach hurt,

Don't come here if you're expecting any type of fast food. I've been waiting over 15 minutes for a standard Ziggy burger and have been getting vacant stares from the staff. It is extremely annoying. I have no idea how the food is since I may never actually get to eat it.

It's decent. Decent burgers, decent shakes, decent service. Not my go-to spot if I have my heart set on a good burger for lunch. I've been here twice and I'll only go back if I'm with friends who really want to go here.

3.5 Stars - my new favorite cold Sub / Hoagie fast food restaurant. Located in the Philadelphia 30th St. train station. 

Pro's

- Meats are freshly sliced in front of you - fresher product vs. their competitors

- Love getting the subs "Mike's way" which includes drizzled Olive oil, red wine vinegar and fresh spices 

- Wide unique selection of hot and cold subs

- Generous portions and good quality for a fair price

- The fresh cookies are excellent

- Three sizes to fit all appetites

Con's

- Not much to say here, it's a good product for fast food sandwiches 

- This is the only location I've come across since moving to the US 4 years ago, wish there were more in Phily 

Bottom Line - Good fresh sandwiches, perfect for a quick bite before / after your train trip. A definite step up from Subway. 

BK
Best new spot in Philly. I've been 3 times and always try something new. Everything's been fantastic!
It's a Taco Bell. I've been going to this one since the early 2000's and don't really recall any issues with the food or staff. Although it did burn down once so...there's that.

This place is the absolute worst. Just waited 30 minutes start to finish, they are out of many things, then lost my order, cashier was really rude. I see 4 people in manager outfits but somehow this is the slowest, most mismanaged chick-fil-a I've ever been to.

This place is an offshoot of the famous Kensington Quarters, with the same great staff and burgers, but now mini-sized as part of the Franklin's Table Food Hall on UPenn's campus. For carnivores, the burgers are of course excellent, but even for vegetarians, they have a fantastic mushroom sandwich. Delicious!
Great service! Super nice and very nice music! The platters are super filling and the white sauce and hot sauce is great as well. Highly recommend (:

With Pita Chip right down the block, this place just can't compare. I had a souvlaki (chicken) gyro and was disappointed by the giant slices of onion and tomato in it. I went in hoping for a fresh, healthy gyro and ended up eating pita, fries and chicken doused in tzatziki. My BF had the lamb/beef which he thought was good, found the thin slices very traditional (he is Lebanese), but a friend thought they were too thin. Also, for 9 dollars with tax, I just expect something more. Maybe the gyros just aren't the way to go here, but we will not be back. Instead, go down the street for a greater selection of DELISH mediterranean cravings.

For what you get here, it can't be beat--price point is absolutely stellar.  My boyfriend and I were looking for some casual, healthy food on a Saturday night in the city where we DID NOT want to be a part of the crazy, hectic nightlife.  We stumbled upon this spot by happenstance and wandered in--quite honestly, not expecting much.

Boy were we surprised--we got healthy, quick, delicious, simple food--that we would have paid a lot more for at a fancier spot--for a very very good price.  I think one pizza and 2 salads--maybe set us back $22?  

Also, even though it was a Saturday night and they had to be at work, the employees at the counter were super helpful and sweet and friendly.  I don't usually expect such great  customer service on a Saturday night.  Plus we were able to sit and enjoy our food and hear ourselves talk, which was much appreciated with all the chaotic drunken mess of people in the city.

Will defnitely come back for fast, affordable, better-than-the price value and great customer service.

It's not fancy but it is spot on and I really loved it.

In the Food Court area of the grand Amtrak 30th Street Station is an outpost of the sandwich chain - Jersey Mike's.  This chain started in the mid-50s in the Jersey Shore town of Point Pleasant and has since spread to well more than a thousand locations.  It is not however big in Philly (after all this is Hoagie territory) except for this outpost in the main train station.  Jersey Mike's is bright and friendly ... and all the lunch meats & cheeses are sliced right in front of you for your sandwich.  I chose their famous Roast Beef & Provolone sub.  It did not disappoint and was the perfect food to take with me on the train.

Almost everything I've had is good so far.  I did not like the Mango Lassi, the yogurt taste was too tangy for me. My favorites are the Chicken Biryani, Spice End Platter, and the Lamb Kabab roll. The food is very spicy so I always make sure to have a drink ready.

Simply put, I had one of the best wraps I've ever had at this place. I opted for the chipotle chicken wrap (it comes with no sides unfortunately). The wrap was absolutely delicious. Every bite I took was worth every penny (no exaggeration). The place looks really clean inside and the service was quick. Unfortunately it being in the heart of philly there is no parking so if you plan to come here, you're going to have to do some waking. Prices were on the higher side but you're getting good quality and quality of food which offsets the price.

The day has come.
Finally after years of reading about how awesome
Shake Shack in New York is. How the burgers are end all, be all.
Only held to the highest standards, using only the finest meat purveyor
in all of Meatopia, thee "Nobody beats our meat" Pat LaFrieda  with a
custom Shake Shack meat blend. 
After putting off so many times going to NY to try it. It's finally here.
Last year word got out that it was coming to 20th & Sansom st. 
I hardly could contain my excitement. 
Most don't get gitty over this shit, but me being the burger slut,
I got a meat chubby.
That's right a NY icon of burgers is coming to Philly. Shit yea.
Excited I was (Yoda-ism). 
Counting down the months was long indeed.
Alas, I got wind just a few weeks ago it was opening June 6th.
Instant beef boner. So planning my first visit the Saturday after they open I
get a fantastical surprise. A special invite to a private VIP party the night before
opening. HUH??? YEAH!!!! Now if I couldn't be more excited, I sure as shit was.
Greg at the Shack sends me a email inviting me. 
You Sir are awesome. HELL YA, my cockles are warmed!  
I RSVP'd as fast as possible.
Me and all you can eat burgers for free, I can do this.

So I cut out of work early to make it down there, It was busy.Yikes.
We check in, no problems. Nice. Got our wrist bands, I guess so people
couldn't wander in and grub free food. Feeling excited. I walked around for a
minute and Greg found me. What a guy. We spoke about some things
and answered all my questions with a smile. Super cool dude. 
You sir are shrine worthy.

Now, I need food. 
I kept looking at the awesome servers hustling around with
trays of all the Shack goodies. I stopped one of the servers to try
my pink elephant. The Shack Burger. Tears almost welled as the meat 
approached my mouth. I was almost to nervous to bite it.
What if it let me down, there was so much hype built I would feel 
shitty if it didn't blow me away. The moment drew closer as
my hand forced it into my meat-hole. 
YOUGOTTOBEFRIGGINGKIDDINGME
was that redonkulously mind blowing. After inhaling it in 11 seconds
I glance around for more. Give me more, lots more. Stat!

I figured it might be rough trying to get more food, but I was wrong.
The crowds thinned out near the most important spot in the place.
The kitchen doors. Me and the wife planted around the prime local as
all the servers had to swing by us.
One after the other servers kept the food train flowing. 

The meat was so perfectly seasoned with salt & pepper and had that 
perfect crust. The LaFrieda custom blend  of beef for the Shack 
was tear worthy. Not sure of the fat ratio but the beef blend is chuck,
brisket and sirloin. The patties range around 4 to 5oz of heaven. 
Mr. Lafrieda if I could hug you I would.
A great big beefy hug you meat genius. Bravo! The meat party all
rested on a super soft slightly sweet Martin's potato roll. Roll 
retention was in check.
I dug how the cheese beautifully blanketed the meat like a long winters slumber.
All the toppings were crazy fresh, and the bacon was crisp and sublime.
I though for sure some of the many burgers flying out the the kitchen 
wouldn't be consistent, I was so wrong, but happy as shit. The 
kitchen staff blew me away of how well it handled the mob of 
hungry grubbers.
 
I can't leave the potato out of this.
The Shack was rocking old school crinkle cut fries,
which were nicely crisp and salted just right, but I have 
to implore you to get them with the most ass slapping smooth cheese sauce
I've ever tasted.
Hows blended cheddar & American cheeses to coat the fries with. Huh? 
Only the most perfect topping, Fuck ketchup. 

As if I needed more meat, I had to try the Hot dog
which  was sourced from Vienna hotdogs. I was so full from eating four burgers,
but I had to do it. Shoving the wiener in my face had to be done. Hey, not that one.
What a nice grill char to it,but the Chicago toppings really set it off.
It too rested on a potato bun, nice choice keeping it all together nicely.
Loved it. 

Custard. Let me say it again, AHHHH custard. So smooth and velvety. 
I was told the butterfat content was high and you could tell. I couldn't 
even think of any others that came close. All the mix ins were good, but the 
Liberty Shell was the winner. Wow Wee. I was surprised of how well 
it all came together. Second fav was the Rittenhouse 2.
As if my ass needed more sweet I couldn't resist washing down 
my custard with a chocolate shake. Pig I am, so what.

The staff was beyond awesome and they were so on point, it was amazing.
With the throngs of people they were super friendly and always had a smile on.
I had asked a few of them for certain things and was promptly brought it.
I would expect this service at a fine dining restaurant but was shocked to find it here.
Another kudos for the Shack.
They never give enough sauce!! And I say "fire AND hot sauce" and they only give me hot sauce!! Also they were OUT OF BAJA BLAST

Honestly? I know some people like this place, but i was disappointed. The food here made me bloated. It irritated my tummy. Now i am bloated, and I feel gross :( tried to order healthy salads and instead wound up feeling disappointed. Plus the food wasn't satisfying

Horrible service, bread was hard and stale. The "owner" was extremely rude. Paid extra for bacon and when calling to inform them they did not put it on he argued over the phone until we brought the sandwich back and showed him. Extremely terrible place.

I picked up my food to go last week after finding out it had opened up the week before. Online ordering was a breeze and they offered delivery but I had to see it for myself. I was extremely excited that a dedicated kati roll place had opened up in Center City and was open late. Their menu is sparse, but I think they are trying to focus on getting a few things right, and I think they succeed!

I tried all 3 paneer rolls (tikka, aachari, and aloo), and they all hit the spot just right. I do wish the tikka paneer was more tikka, but that's just me being difficult. Otherwise, great spices, nice onion and chutney kick, and their roll was not as greasy as the NYC joint makes theirs. Definite plus (even though late night, you might crave the grease)! I would probably get 2 of the tikka rolls again as the alooo paneer (potato and cheese) roll was mild and the aachari paneer (pickle and paneer) roll had a good, but overpowering flavor. I would actually recommend the aloo roll for beginners and the aachari for a more acclimated palate.

They take a while to make them, because even coming in 30 minutes after I ordered, it wasn't ready, but you can see them making each roll through the little window in the back, so I didn't mind. Also, the mango lassi was pretty good (again, I'm just picky and wish it was colder!)

For the uninitiated, each roll is about the size of a mini- burrito and fits perfectly in one large sized hand. That means it's not super filling, but it's good for a heavy snack, and if you get multiple it can easily be a moderately priced meal. If you do go for multiples, get the 2-for-$1-off special as long as it lasts! Each roll doesn't come with extra frills (but they do offer a great white sauce and red sauce if you want to mellow or kick up the spice, respectively), so don't expect what you are used to from a traditional Punjabi restaurant like papadam or chutneys or even rice (unless you order the platters).

This place is going to be a hit, I just know it. Next time, I'll make sure they make my paneer extra tikka!

I'm obsessed with Snap. This place was my saving grace when we moved to center city but my fiance had to go out of town as soon as we moved in. I love to cook but hate cooking for one. Plus I had to unpack a lot in order to even be able to cook anything. They have healthy, filling meals that are reasonably priced. I buy a few meals here every week for lunch and occasionally dinner. They have a great variety of meals. Some are labeled if they're approved for different diets. Their rewards program is awesome so make sure you sign up!

Friendly staff as well!

I was out enjoying the great weather and saw this new place at 19th and Chestnut. Snap Kitchen seems to promote fast, healthy and well-prepared fast food. What that means that the food is prepared fresh each day and placed in the refrigerated section, then customers can either pay and leave or pick up, heat it up on site via a microwave, pay and leave. 

First off, it is a great concept and a great alternative to the all the Chiptole, food carts and pre-package lunch options in the city. However, a major con is that the food is VERY expensive. For example, a kale smoothie starts at $7.99. The size is no bigger than a Naked Juice at CVS. It is not hard to crack $25 for a meal at Snap, if you get a drink and probably about two healthy meals. 

They serve: breakfast, lunch and dinner options and even a small serving of oatmeal is just over $5.00; a small serving of two pancakes is the same price but you will be charged an additional $1.00 for maple syrup. I am sure the food is super tasty given I saw many people grabbing salads and other goodies off the self, but there is no "bang for your buck." 

On the bright side, they do have a rewards card, that is free, and every dollar you spend can go towards a discount on future meals...I believe it is every $50.00 you spend.

The philly steak was delicious!   Service was great even when they were very busy with the lunch rush.  The kale lemonade was also delicious - kind of a mild flavor that wasn't too sweet or sour.  The sweet potato fries went well with everything.

I ordered online today, this was my third time doing so.  Unfortunately it was not a good experience.  I scheduled my pick up time for 12:45pm.  I arrived about 12:42pm, of course I did not expect my food to be ready yet.  As I was checking the bags that were awaiting pick up, a Chipotle Employee asked me my name, I told her, she said she'd check on my food and then she disappeared.  It was approximately 12:51 at this point, I continued to patiently wait.  I went to the bathroom, I finished and came out,  still no food.  At this point it was about 12:54 and I figured the employee and Chipotle as a whole had forgotten about me, so I stood off to the side of the line, in hopes of getting the same employee's attention, at this point she was ringing up customers.  She did notice me and said 'I didn't see a ticket for you'.  I said nothing, she then said is your last name ____________?  I then said 'yes', she then pressed a button,  a white receipt came out, and she passed it to her coworker and said '_____ can you make this?'  No apology, nothing.  Her coworker made my bowl and passed me my bag at 12:59 pm and said 'Here you go'.    I got back to work (late) and to top it off my food was disappointing,  the chicken tasted like mildew and was extremely salty I couldn't even enjoy my lunch, I threw about 75% of it away (see pic below) .   This was my 3rd time visiting this location in about 2 weeks and this time was very disappointing.   If anyone cares, I won't be back unless someone reaches out to me with at least an apology.

Are you out of your mind?!? THIS. PLACE. SLAPS!!! Let me start off by saying I'm not full time vegan, but my smokehouse burger was better than 90% of beef burgers I've ever had. That's for real man, no jokes over here. this burger had me thinking about the choices I've made in life, I'm talking about contemplations and all that. Big ups!

OK... So this is my review of the Spice End.  I had 3 rolls, Lamb, Chicken and Beef.  HOLY SH*T!! Was I pleasantly surprised.  I took one bite of the lamb and couldn't put it down. All of the flavors worked real well... the onions, cilantro and spices with the tender lamb was on point.  I found the other two rolls to be as equally delicious.  I loved the fact that the beef was handled with care as it was roasted. You can actually see the pieces of beef and not shreds of God know's what.  It's amazing because I guess I wasn't prepared for how delicious it was.  I dressed mine with the mayo sauce and hot sauce. Say it with me... PHENOMENAL!!

Yet another great visit at another great snap kitchen.  THis time it was because of Matthew.  The employees really really make this place.

Are you listening, Management?  I hope you are paying attention and treat them well and incentivize them:)

Matthew totally made me laugh and also helped  me pick out my meals for about 10 minutes one at a time.  I had the turkey chili and it was my favorite item to date.  The veggie beef lasagna was also very good.

the hot chicken...not my favorite--it was actually gross--and I even heated up in the oven rather than microwave because I have had the experience that chicken in the microwave can end up tasting funky.

However, I cannot fault them for this because 2 out of three....certainly ain't bad!

I've gotten around to eating at every spot in Chinatown Square, and I've got to say that eating at Coreanos Philly was something I really enjoyed. I'd be willing to eat there again anytime, whether with friends or just by myself. The food was really good when I got it. I had ordered chips with guacamole, grilled tomatoes, and some sauce which name escapes me at the time, but it was delicious. I'd also like to mention that the customer service was pretty good itself, no complications with my orders whatsoever and when I needed anything else, the employees were willing to help. Overall the experience there was great.

Oh eeeeew ew ew ew re disgusting I just waited in line here for 15 or 20 minutes to get to things which were not even hot, room temperature, lukewarm that I immediately threw out. Isn't McDonald's the place where you can get a fairly straight forward and inexpensive standard fast food? Not here, total headache and disgusting food

Classic & good Indian food! Had the Ritual lunch special so my meal literally cost $1. Ordered the Spice End Platter and it was spicy and delicious. Their white sauce is WONDERFUL. The rice was perfectly cooked and moist - however I would have liked more lettuce/pita to soak up the heat of the chicken/rice. Also, definitely more of a take out place than dine-in, as the decor is seriously lacking. Would definitely come back for pick up again in the future- nice and friendly staff!

So the verdict is 3.5/5 stars, it's a good burger. As my buddy described it, that's the "smallest $9 burger I've ever seen". The meat is good, moist, no lettuce and tomato, they've added the special sauce and red onions (seems to have been scooped) on the side. Will I come back?  Prolly not.  I have other places I can spend my hard earned money, the $6 veggie burger 3 blocks away is a better buy and it's tastier (Cucina Zapata)!  However, I can't wait to try the falafel or sushi joints in this complex

It's hit or miss at the this McDonald's - usually it's early in the morning or later at night when the problems begin.

I was there today at approximately 6:35 am. There was no one at the counter. 

As I an older white women - the whole black staff including the "manager" dressed in full Muslim garb walked in the back of the store 

The only person was a young man who was working the drive through. 

He was very nice and accommodating. 

My food was made as 5 or so women stood around - and not one of them got my food.

I was waiting to see how long it would take for someone to give me my order which was $9.54. No one budged until I asked for the manager.

She reluctantly got my food and no apology or anything.  when I asked for more ketchup she totally ignored me. 

This store needs to shut down for a half-day for diversity and customer service training.

This was the 2nd time in a week I was discriminated against.

I Will never ever go back into that store which is only a few blocks from my house. 

Disgusting

So the drive-through is run by people who have an ignorant attitude and no customer service skills. When I tried to order my food the woman didn't properly explain to me the situation so I was confused. When I asked her what she meant I got an attitude when I pulled up to the first window to pay I had voiced my concerns with the man at the window yet he decided to reprimand me and give me an attitude back and make me feel like I was wrong. He wasn't a manager he was just a punk. When I did speak to the manager I explained that I never complain and I mean I never complain but I was given such horrible treatment by these people at the drive-through that I didn't wanted to happen to another customer. The manager was kind and understood and apologized immensely and reassured me that the two workers would be dealt with properly. I will never go to that Wendy's ever again and I'm sure they could care less whether they have my business or not
Love It here, so delicious and the presentation is amazing. The employees are very polite as well.

After waiting for literally thirty minutes for my half sandwich and soup combo, I finally asked an associate to just give me any soup they had as I watched my half sandwich sit on the counter. I get back to my office to see what my half sandwich consisted of. See picture for attached. 

I've never had a problem with this Corner Bakery location before, but this was the worst customer service I've received. Staff had bad attitudes when people simply asked where their food was after patiently waiting for 20+ minutes. Pic attached if my turkey avocado sandwich that had a total of 1/2 piece of turkey that was so slimy I removed it entirely from my sandwich.

Hidden gem! Come quick before the word gets out, and the line gets out of control!

The sounds coming from the kitchen already told me this place is legit, non-stop joking around in Greek and veggies being chopped fresh. Service is fast and friendly, we got the lamb and beef gyro platter and pork gyro (recommended by the guys)

Lamb and Beef Gyro: 
Heaping helping of meat. We're talking nearly a full pound of lamb and beef, sliced thin to maximize that caramelized goodness

Pork Gyro: 
Greek carnitas, a mixture of crispy and melty pork seasoned simply with salt. Delicious. Same monster portions as the lamb/beef

Greek Salad:
Fresh veggies, high quality feta cheese and olive oil with a hint of oregano, the quality of the ingredients really shines.

Fries:
Crispy and light, not greasy at all

Tzatziki Sauce:
Definitely homemade, really refreshing and creamy with a hint of garlic

Wholesome food and friendly folks, great addition to the neighborhood! We will be back!

This series of restaurants are amazingly good for serving up vegan meals. It's fast and seating is limited in some locations so call ahead to ask. I have visited several locations in Philadelphia for breakfast and lunch. I think you can't go wrong with whatever you try.

First visit and ordered some takeout from seamless at this place. Had Chicken Tikka roll, Lamb Kebob roll and a chicken rice platter. Both rolls tasted okay - it would have been good for a street vendor (supposedly how they started out) but bleh for a restaurant, which they are. The meat was a little dry, but the roll was stuffed with it. The rolls are pretty small. If you are a man, you are going to need to eat two, which breaks the sub $10 lunch budget coming in over $11, but hey, you get a $1 off. 

The platter seemed like it was the better deal with the amount of food. However, my dining companion found a millimeter by 1 inch long piece of metal right in her platter. I hope one was not in my rolls and I already ate it inadvertently. I didn't dock them any stars for this because she was able to spot it before eating it. 

I would try this place out again however. 

Food Quality/Taste =  3/5 Stars
Portion Size Given Price = 2/5 Stars
Decor = 4 Star

Note: Some of these reviews below are suspect.

Shake Shack rarely disappoints. I heard so much about the chicken sandwich so I was anxious to try it. It was good. The chicken isn't well seasoned but it's cooked well, juicy and crispy. I'd definitely get it again. Also, the fries I had seemed like maybe they were the last of the bag because they were all itty bitty sized with a few regular sized thrown in. The only menu item I truly find lacking is the milkshakes. Each one I've had taste really foamy, I guess it's over spun, and it's off-putting.
Staff is great. Very nice. The place is very clean. In the time I took to write this I witnessed 2 drug transactions. In the dining room. The people they late hangout here, users, and dealers.

Had a Big Mac from here and the bun was burnt. Had a salad and the lettuce was old and soggy. The salad was so old the cheese on it had melted from the room temperature surrounding wherever they store them. Smh. It never crowded at the location, but they always take long. It's just a sucky place in general.
Worst ever. Nuggets and fries always old and barely warm never hot. Shit show inside of strung out drugged out kenzo junkies. Ewwy!
Idk what the chicken nuggets were made of last night or but they were burned I've never seen Wendy's nuggets in that form on my life...

Got prepared food a couple times, only once was the order correct. Multiple times items were missing or food had strange things added to them. How does that even happen? How do you put tomatoes instead of mayo? Is it deliberate? I only ask because most employees seem to spend their time talking

Hmm.. I didn't actually get a shake here I went here for lunch with some coworkers and tried the shake shack burger. I got the small sized burger. The bun was soggy and their specialty sauce was sort of salty -- they said it would be hot but eh. 

After you stand in line and give your order, they give you one of those buzzers that let you know when your order is ready to be picked up from the front. 

Went on a Friday during lunch break and it was packed, you couldn't get a seat inside but we sat outside (in January so I guess that's why seats were open). The inside of the place isnt dirty or anything, just too jammed to be comfortable. 

My review may be a little biased ( I didn't actually get a shake and I don't like greasy fast food) so I might update later if try it again.

Wow.  Such a let down.  

I will gladly continue going to the original Kensington Quarters.  However, the burger from this satellite branch at the Penn Food Hall was not nearly as flavorable, was significantly smaller, and with fries was only a few bucks cheaper than the original restaurant's price point.  Never again will I settle for this.

Oh and you guys are over cooking your fries.

Just had the worst experience I've ever had with Jimmy John's. Usually, my food delivery arrives within 5 (max 10) minutes of ordering. But today I'm still waiting and it's been an hour. When the 30-minute mark arrived, I called the store and was told that they never even put in the order since it didn't "show up" on their screen. I never would have known unless I called. So I was told they were making the food and it would arrive in 10 minutes. I get a call from them 20 minutes later that I can call tomorrow to speak to a manager--and find out they still have not sent my food out for delivery. All I keep being told is that it was the previous shift and claim they have no order delivery tracking system BUT the tracker on JJ's website kept updating. All I want is my food, and I only ordered from Jimmy John's because they're known for being fast. This experience was terrible. Won't make this mistake again. UPDATE: had to call again from a different phone number since they would not pick up when I called from my phone and they basically told me they're not sending me my food. Unbelievable. I wasted over an hour on this situation and they repeatedly lied to me.

So embarrassing confession, when considering where to move in the city, one of our major factors was the new apartments proximity to a Snap Kitchen...no joke. Snap has completely transformed our weekly routine. I went from cooking hours each day, to finding super yummy pre-made meals that my hubby and I love! Double win, great food and the nicest staff ever!

Make sure to get their rewards card, it's free and you get $10 off of every $200 you spend. Trust me, if you buy every week like we do, you'll hit that bonus quick. The food is affordable though, we actually save money with better, pre-made meals here than we do when actually grocery shopping. 

I would confess my favorite foods but I don't want them to sell out, haha! I love you, Snap!

Their service has gone down once their popularity has grown. Their food is still amazing, but they seem to nickel and dime you more now. 

I have a NEVER been to any restaurant that refuses to give you free tap water, let alone an INDIAN restaurant. It's such an integral part of the subcontinent's culture to offer your guests water that even the hole-iest of holey hole in the walls in both the U.S. and India offer all guests access to water. I frankly thought it was illegal for restaurants to refuse giving tap water for free, but even when your friend is choking on some spicy food, you have to cough up a few bucks to help them here.

I loved this place. Now I have to consider other places because of this one issue. I used to roll my eyes when other reviewers would choose one negative to bash an otherwise great place, but this kind of speaks volumes as to the care this place has for people who eat in their own restaurant. 

Point this out when you go and demand that they change!

Hands down!  Shake Shack is way better than In-n-Out.  More variety of burgers, more tastier burgers, and more friendly staff.

1. I was greeted with a smile when I walked up front to order. 

2. I ordered a medium double Smoke Shack burger and a coffee shake.

3. In less than 5 minutes, they were ready for pick up!

The Smoke Shack burger was so juicy.  It was warmer than the ones at In-n-Out. The little spice from the cherry pepper was icing on the cake. The sauce wasn't overwhelming.  

You might or might not have problem keeping your hands clean, but i surely couldn't.  Don't forget to lick your fingers if the juice and sauce got onto your hands.  They are finger licking good!

The coffee shake is rich and definitely has a lot of coffee flavor.

This place is way better than the one in the San Francisco Bay Area location.

Two thumbs up!  My tummy agrees.

Wendy's. The "Cheers" of 30th St station...they don't really know your name but you come there so often they always have a friendly "hey" coupled with a smile as you're handed your order. Lunch is the absolute worst anywhere in center city/university city but these fine folks keep their lunch rush to a minimum. With the name system on the screen, you're able to see when your order is ready in real time. They have a Coca-Cola Freestyle so the drink options are endless. They are joined with Jersey Mikes so be prepared for a tight fit, but usually not for long. There's a few tables inside but you'd have better luck out in the eating areas of the train station. These are also in this millennium and take mobile and door dash orders! So pop in and grab a frosty...I'll take some nuggets!

It's a Taco Bell; avoid it. This is cheap, fake food, which harms the body and offers next to no nutrients. Even at its best, any Taco Bell is worse than other Mexican food options. Don't let the taste or the advertisements fool you, this chain is a joke.

I really enjoyed it here, I came to philly one night with a couple of friends and my one friend suggested we try this place since she was there the week before. 

  We all ordered and found a seat even tho it was crowed. I ordered a bacon cheeseburger with fries, my friends ordering different burgers as well. The meat was great and the fries cooked perfect with just the right crunch. 

  As we were eating a worker came over to us with two bowls of ice cream, they called them concrete because they didn't move if you turned them upside down, he decided to show us and turn it over on his head and of course it didn't fall. He gave both of the cups to us, one of them vanilla ice cream with cannoli pieces in it and some strawberry jelly, The other chocolate with chewy coffee pieces in it. We all reached for our purses but he stopped us and said "it's on us for you lovely ladies" we thanked him and continued to eat and then all shared the ice cream we were given for free. 

  Later on the manager came over and introduced himself and asked how we were enjoying everything, we told him thank you for the free ice cream and the food was delicious he was glad we enjoyed and went along to asking other customers how their meals were. 

  Staff is super friendly and food is great and I'm not just saying that thanks to the free Ice cream!

I'm loving this place. I've ordered several of their popcorn chicken flavored already and it is so good. Crispy but still juicy. They serve chunks of fried chicken in a sizable portion. I'm definitely going to frequent this place whenever I get the chance because I'm definitely a fan of the popcorn chicken. The pricing is pretty inexpensive for what they're serving. I'm definitely coming back to try some other things off their menu.

Dont usually go to wendy's but salad was pretty good but what deserves the 10/10 was the lady working there was A M A Z I N G, it was 9pm after a long day and they ran out of full size salads so she gave me two 1/2 salads and was really nice, and gave me extra napkins!!!!

I didn't realize you could make Chipotle bad. The ratio of everything was way off. Too much sour cream. Too little meat. So much salsa the whole thing turned to a soupy mess. This was my first meal in Philly and has really put the whole city in question at this point.

Snap Kitchen is a dream for anyone who wants delicious, fresh, food, that is still nourishing and healthy! The thing I love most about snap kitchen is that they have so many different types of dishes. They have salads and the classic meat/carb/veggie combo, but also pancakes, lasagna, and desserts! I get so tired of getting salads or skipping sauces to have healthier meals, so all the options at snap are a dream. 

Snap is also completely transparent with their nutrition information! Their dishes come in small, medium, or large sizes, with nutrition facts including grams of fat and protein right on top of each container. They also sell little containers of sides like cauliflower rice or sweet potatoes, so even the pickiest eater or someone on a restricted diet can find something delicious to eat. 

If you're in a mood to treat yoursef, try the Chai Cashew Shake. It is a delicious blend of nut milk and spices with 8 grams of protein and 16g of fiber -- and it is sweetened naturally only with dates. 

After discovering Snap Kitchen, I may never cook again...
Went in for a burger and a shake and it took 30 minutes, the staff is rude and clearly there is no management.

Good:
The food is standard McDonald's fare.

Bad:
Some spaces in the parking lot have large divots where the front tires go (give it gas to climb back out of there!).
When I visited, there was no line. Upon approaching the register, the young man behind the counter stared at me for a moment, seemingly wondering why I was there. Finally, he muttered something and seemed surprised when I ordered food. He brought my drink, said nothing else. After waiting for my food for a while, the young man re-appeared, again seemingly surprised that I was standing there. When he asked what I wanted, I told him that I was waiting for my order. He to a spot, about 3 feet farther away on the counter and said to wait there. A few minutes later, I got my order.
This place has a desperate need for employee training and management.

Sept. 1 2019- review still unchanged. Food issues.
Ordered one spicy chicken sand, but unfortunately it was undercooked. Biting in gave a seriously rubbery crunch, no flavor, it was completely soaked somehow, and all of its outer 'batter/crispy coating" simply slid off the to the incorrect cooking.  Wendy's really disappoints. Same owner as the recently closed store on chestnut st.? If so, he also has broad st & snyder ave.- which started off great but went downhill quickly.
Wendy's may be excellent- but not in Philadelphia Proper, based off of this reviewer's extensive 4 yrs of research, retesting, examining, questioning, and thorough investigation. They arent going to get stars easily. Remember their " ghost pepper" fries that were 0% spicy? Lol . Didn't bother to photograph more improperly-made Wendy's food, we could fill a whole website on its own.

My experience at this particular chipotle is usually never good. When I order online and go to the store at pickup time, my order is never ready and they only start making it when I get there? What's the point of even ordering online. I work across the street and schedule pickup when I have a few minutes to step out but it usually ends up taking an extra 10 minutes and without any apology. I also notice there is always new staff here or so it seems like they are training because they burn my quesadilla or cannot wrap a burrito and another staff member always has to help. Today I went and got a quesadilla and it took over 10 minutes, the girl at the counter had to go get someone else to make it and I was the first person in line. It's disappointing that one of the worst Chipotles is across the street from where I work.

Sometimes you just need a burger and hand-spun PB&J ice cream! 

Normally my go to after drinking would be pizza because it takes seconds to come up and it's a eat & walk back to the apt because you are going so tired that you might just fall asleep with pizza in your mouth kind of night. On that note a few months ago I went to a Phillies game and had a few- I was with an avid 5 guys fan and I just had to take him to try these burgers. I think 5 guys is overrated, greasy and bland.

These burgers were anything but overrated, greasy and bland. They must use 85/15 chuck because the flavor on the meat was lean but had enough fat to keep your mouth salivating bite after bite. I am a stickler for a good bun and this was toasted and buttered to perfection. The lettuce had a crunch to it and the cheese was melted properly. 

After we ate the burger I couldn't really fit in the ice cream, but I forced myself to have a spoonful and it was heavenly! I had not had real ice cream in a long time. It almost tasted buttery in texture.

TIP: must try and save room for the hand spun of the day.

I don't eat at Shake Shack often; maybe 1-2 times per year. I have been to this location when it first opened many many years ago. Due to my health I don't eat much carbs, but I do truly appreciate Shake Shack offers lettuce wrap (basically hamburger patty, tomato, and onions or pickles). They will also give you the Shack Sauce on the side of you ask for it. I really enjoyed the flavour, however, it is literally so difficult to eat this without meat juice dripping and lettuce coming apart. A A plus for an effort, but a C/D for practicality. It was almost easier eating this on a plate with a fork and a knife. I will not complain too much because it is a great option to low carb eating. I do have to say I was a bit bad and indulged in some crinkle fries (nicely crispy, and yummy with the Shack Sauce), and a frozen custard in a cup, pure yum!

I ordered food from here through uber eats my God the food had gotten me sick for 2 days extreme headaches,diarrhea,upset stomach I was extremely sick and the food taste horrible each time very salty food

Great burgers, shakes, floats, even hard cider! Great fast food burger joint, we were thrilled when they moved into the neighborhood years ago, my husband and son even stood in the giant around the block line on the first day! 
Have to admit I preferred the thin fries when they first opened, now they have thick accordion fries. The kids love the thick fries, and I am the minority. Usually we get the smoke shack burgers, the cheeseburgers, basic hamburgers, shroom burgers, fries...right now they have a special barbecue cheese bacon fries which my son devoured.
