It is a great place to take any visitors or family from out of town, but it is also perfect for weekly shopping.

In my dreams, I can shop exclusively at Reading.
Very fun! Loved the people and the shops.  It is crowded though, and I do not recommend bringing a stroller.

BRING YOUR WALLET!!!

Some of the BEST meat cutters and pastries, bread bakers, cheese shops and (OYSTERS!) fishmongers in Philadelphia.... mostly because they're almost ALL from Lancaster County.  This used to be exclusively Amish and Italian (I've been going there for 60 years!) and it HAS gone downhill in quality a little in that time, but the overall quality of available products is still far and away superior to just about any shops in the tri-state area, except for specialty food stores.  Not even Weaver's Way in Germantown can beat them, but:

It comes with a price.  A steep price.   You'll find lamb is 20-25%more expensive than imported New Zealand meat, but SO much nicer and fresher.   Fish are clear-eyed and firm, no slimy scales and can be filleted as you like, while you wait.  Pastries/baked goods are fresh, tender and delicious, albeit each carries a hidden five pound penalty... It's worth it!

DO visit if you have the chance, and bring a refrigerated or a "cold bag" with you for the meat and fish.

Your tummy will love you!

When you walk in to this Mecca of a market , you are overwhelmed with choices, Everything  for everybody . Wanna cook your own stuff, butchers and fish mongers abound. Amish farmers with Hugh produce and farm vegetables. Cant wait to eat , the list is endless, from Philly cheesesteak to roastpork and broccoli rabe , Deli style pastrami and corned beef, to greek gyros and pizza, I Scream, You Scream , candy counters , bakeries, Breakfast lunch & dinner ..Just Pick 
Some very interesting choices , some very good , some a waste of money .
Choose wisely , There is a reason some vendors are busier then others . 
I tried the overpriced pastrami on rye with Cole slaw. If you ever had Real NYC Deli. Give this a rest. Cheesesteak sandwich is better in some kioks, then others ... look for longer lines with locals . 
There is a seating area, however based on what time of day , Good luck grabbing a seat . Some vendors offer counter seating ( Limited ) . The best time to go is about 10:30 AM. Fresh prep of food for vendors, Breakfast specials and Hardhats chowing down , the quiet before  the storm. By noon the place is crazy.  Its a good place to site see & munch
The only thing that could make this place better would be for them to stay open a little later for people to pop in after work.

Great place for locals and tourists.  We took some out of time family visiting the city and stopped for ice cream.  Wish more shops were open on Sunday but that's only because it seems a bit empty with half the place closed.  Still worth a visit!
Fantastic food everywhere you turn!  It's a must see, go check it out.  They have such diversity in the food that it offered and you can even find beeswax, candles and unique bar soap.

A haiku for Reading Terminal Market:

Senses tingle here
Fresh food and wares call your name
Buy and taste delights
Pretty good, just a basic fried dumpling with a cup of sauce on the side. Will go back for a quick snack sometime.

everything you could ever need or dream of, they have it here. busy at lunch time during the week and weekend so it's tough to fit into the normal lunch-break, good people watching spot.  definitely a cool spot to take visitors from out of town.

I don't even know where to begin.  This place left me literally speechless.  I could probably write a 5 page review, but I'll spare you and give you the highlights.

*Parking is a pain, almost $30.00 for two hours... unless you get it validated!   GET IT VALIDATED!
*Tommy DiNic's... best sandwich ever!
*Termini Bro's Bakery... yummy cannoli, do yourself a favor and get one!
*The Head Nut... teas and spices, and snacks galore!!
*The Famous 4th Street Cookie Co... I recommend the White Chocolate Chip Macadamia Nut.
*Four Seasons Juice Bar... Good Lord I wish we had one of these near me!  

Those are all the places we hit in my short 2 hours here.  I feel like I could take another trip to Philly and spend at least a week in Reading Terminal Market and just eat my way through.  The people who work and live near here are so lucky!

I've reviewed each of the above places individually too... check em' out!
Love this place! You can get anything here and everything is so fresh. I had a crawfish broil with the crawfish i got at the fish market. delicious!

I don't know what the problem is with finding a BBQ place that actually smokes their damn food. First, I went to Phoebes on South st and there wasn't a TRACE of smoke in their dry chicken. 

So I tried King Grill and the chicken was moist and delicious but AGAIN...barely a trace of smoke (more than Phoebes, which had zero smoke, but barely).

The veggie rice was very good.

I absolutely loved this place. So many great things to eat that it makes me sad I can't stay in Philadelphia and go here every day. Check out the Dutch breakfast place for fresh, home cooked food and friendly service.

Oh yeah, I'm  coming back!!!  When I come back to Philly, this will definitely be on the list of places of places to go first.  The enormous offering of food offerings is staggering.  I might browse first, then start all over to choose.   Don't go there starving, or you won't make past Hershel's deli.  A fun place. Had an authentic feel.  Highly recommend
Had so much fun getting little bites from different vendors. There were so many options. Love it here!
Love this place! I used to live near by off of 13th and race but since moving to Fishtown I miss coming to Reading for Amish Donuts and the Juice bar!

Reading Terminal Market is a fantastic location for if you're a foodie! There are many options of places to eat at, all of which serve food fresh and ready to order. The snack stores inside of the Market serve snacks that are made by hand on location. While there are often crowds, this is a good thing. The crowds are explained by the amazing food in every corner of the market. It's totally worth the trip!

AWESOME.  We made our way over this past weekend, and although it was sensory overload, it was delicious sensory overload.   I think it will become a regular party of my Philly visits, as there was a whole list of things we wanted to try.  

The things we did try that rocked:
a wheel of brie+figs and toasted almonds... mmmm...
cupcakes at the flying monkey
dark chocolate covered pretzels by mueller

First and foremost, there isn't too much in the way of craft beer dine-in places in the Pennsport area where I live, so this is the walkable go-to for my boyfriend and me. I like that they have a menu that rotates and offers off-beat foods like buffalo sweetbreads, and I normally get mussles or whatever seafood special they offer. The large plates are big enough to take half of it home with you. The desserts are pretty tasty, and only once have we not been a fan (a peanut butter bacon thing) and the waitress removed it from our bill as a courtesy. The beers and specialty drinks are delicious, and I've never had an issue with service.

This is my go to place for some fresh fruit and vegetables shopping and to get fresh meat.  There are bunch of restaurants and the place is always packed. The place is very touristy. They have discounted parking near by. Whenever we have any out of town guests,  we always bring them here for some Amish food and cheese.

This place is amazing. They have every and anything you can possible need when it comes food. From Greek, to Asian cuisine, you will be able to find it here. I have never found such diversity in one building before. The vastness is what makes this as impressive as it is. The good food, sounds and smells all contribute to make this a place worth visiting. If you can't find anything that peeks your interest, I would truly be shocked.

I LOVE this place. It was honestly very stressful and overwhelming the first two or three times I visited because of the vast amount of vendors and people especially when it's busy. However I learned to really like the craziness and bustle of this place. You can do your weekly grocery shopping here and get fresh fruits/veggies, meats, seafood, cheese, condiments, bread, etc. And it is also good for a hot meal for lunch. So many different ethnic vendors. Something for everyone and for tourists visiting Philly this place is a must. Best part is everyone can get what they want to eat for lunch and not compromise for the whole group. Definitely stop by Beiler's for a doughnut afterwards!

Pretty cool place to stroll through! Plenty to see and taste! Prices are on the higher side but I guess that comes with the territory. You can find so much here and definatly something for everyone here. All sorts of food snacks desserts and grocieries that u can find here! Definatly worth the trip! Must visit!
I love this awesome place. you can easily find something that suits your appetite. Especially try Philly Cheesesteaks which is identified with Philly.

Absolutely no complaints. Fun place to go and see a variety of food and grab things to eat.

Very similar to Boston food market and DC union market with the design of a large number of places to eat on a small space.

No complaints.
Fun place to explore a ton of different food options.  Almost too much to choose from!  It was very busy so a bit of a challenge with a toddler in a stroller.  Would love to go back and just shop.

Great place to go to if you don't know what you're in the mood to eat.  Walking throughout Reading Terminal, you'll be sure to land upon a place that suits your appetite.  There are lots of different venues to peruse through.  Also, a great place to people watch.
I love it here. You can walk around and try different things from different parts of the world. The food is always good and the staff is always nice. Only, sometimes it gets too crowded.

Best place in Philadelphia. Wonderful for taking a stroll around and grabbing food on the weekend. If you're looking for something fresh that has the variety to feed an indecisive appetite, you won't be failed by RTM.
An experience! Very crowded but has truly everything. A create mixture of a variety of different local and exotic foods as well as crafts and shops.

For me, as a self-declared food glutton, and fan of local goods, i can honestly say my life in philadelphia would not be as bright if it weren't for reading. I work across the street so the obvious choice for me is to pop in and grab pretty much whatever is making my mouth water that day. Then, in the evenings as i leave work, i consider what i would like to cook that night for dinner. A couple texts between my fiancé  and I and voila! we have decided what delicious, local and fresh dish. 

Some locals might claim this is just a tourist spot but to this philadelphian, it's a very dear part of the philly that I love so much.

Absolutely obsessed with Reading Terminal Market. The made to order food is, of course, phenomenal but it's also an amazing (and affordable!) place to do my grocery shopping. The merchants are friendly and helpful and are always open to letting you try things, giving you advice, or offering great meal pairings. It's also a great place for Philly-themed gifts and one-of-a-kind items.

Not too many places in Philly that give you complimentary sticky buns with your brunch! It was an adventure finding this place but well worth it. Got the duck confit hash and the duck was cooked perfectly. Disclaimer: the biscuits could feed a family of 4. Proceed with caution. 

Their drink menu is huge and pricey but the bar is cozy. Perfect to drink beers on New Years Day and lament with the staff about your hangover (which may or may not have been our experience).
Must see in philly. Lots of different food vendors mixed with a farmers market. Must try the Amish donuts!

The people here are always very nice. 

I went last night and ordered a salad without chicken, fried, and a lemonade. I waited forever for that salad...and by "forever," of course, I mean seven minutes I started to believe that they had planted seeds for the lettuce and were waiting for it to harvest. 

But the manager came over and said that they were making a fresh salad for me. Apparently, they prepare them with the chicken on them already. The manager said that he figured I was a vegetarian and didn't want to give me a salad that touched meat. 

I really appreciated the thoughtfulness and attention to detail. This manager certainly exceeded any expectations I had of chick-fil-a, and I was equally impressed by how attentive he was to what was happening in his restaurant.

How much do I like Reading Terminal Market? Let me count the ways:

1. Iovine Brothers Produce - Even at the cheapest of supermarkets, I couldn't get a whole bag of the freshest, highest quality vegetables for $5. Same goes to the nuts and snacks on the southern wall, where else can you buy them in such a state of quality at such prices?

2. Godshall's Poultry - Instead of the yellowed, hormoned chicken you get from the supermarket, these are the freshest, tastiest chicken you can find in the city. And fresh chickens do make a difference in taste. Of course, they do have ducks, quails, turkeys and eggs.

3. Martin's and John Yi's is where I get my meat and seafood, Martin's is always a few bucks cheaper and John Yi captures me with their neon signs.

4. 4 Seasons Juice Bar has the tastiest fruit smoothies and blends around. My favorite is Pineapple (for sweetness) + Banana (for texture) + Orange (for taste). Nothing beats a 20oz No.4 in a hot summer day.

5. For your dessert needs, Flying Monkey has the best cupcakes and lemon bars in town. Termini Brothers has a killer chocolate covered banana on a crescent cookie. You can also visit the ladies at Famous 4th for a fresh baked cookie. For something completely evil, you can go to the Amish bakery for a cinnamon roll with nuts AND frosting.

6. Shanghai Gourmet's American Chinese food is as good as any place in Chinatown. Try their fried rice or the Shrimp in Lobster Sauce, it's not on their menu but the jumbo shrimps in the silky luscious sauce is to die for. (gulp)

7. The Spice Terminal will fulfill most of your gourmet needs. Bee Natural has a wide variety of honeys. For cheese and charcuterie, you can visit Salumeria and if not for anything else, go to By George for their pasta sauces, they'll even sell you pizza dough if you want to make something at home. 

It's a vibrant place with lots of other places to discover and it's a great place to walk and browse when you have the time. Just don't stand in the middle of the aisle and block traffic, it can be crowded. Cell phone reception can be on the low side, and it's hard for the working folks to pick up groceries on their way home since most of the shop will close business around 5, but there's the weekend. The Amish generally won't be there from Sundays to Wednesdays but most shops open Mondays to Saturdays and some even open on Sundays.

Pros: variety of food and lots of it, decent price

Cons: limited space to sit when it is crowded, taste can be hit and miss

I love this place. I could walk in here for hours just trying one thing to another. It has pretty much all the things that make my stomach happy, me being a food enthusiast. The price is decent. I also like how the whole market seems to always be energetic and buzzing with excitement. There is a crepe place, which name escapes me, that I love. I did say the taste can be hit and miss. But I'm giving it 5 stars? Well, because of the variety. When I found out I didn't like something, I knew I had other options, and lots of them.

I would come back here if I'm in town.

Pretty cool selections of joints from which to choose; but, lines way to long!!  Don't go there with a bunch of little kids, there is nowhere for little ones to sit, no boosters, high-chairs fahgettaboudit.  Looks like a fun place to take visiting guests and people with time on their hands.  The burger place across the street is pretty decent, there was no wait at lunchtime last time we tried to eat at RTM.

Delicious food, large portions, good price, and fast service. 

This is a great place for take out or a quick and casual lunch.

I definitely enjoyed the rose lassi, and would go back for another one if I weren't out of state!

As a local, I usually just buy groceries at Iovine Bros. and the Head Nut here, but for the guilty pleasures, here's my list:

DiNic's Roast Pork - it's in the name
Beiler's Doughnuts - Apple Fritter is the way to go, don't be seduced by anything else (unless it's the Blueberry Fritter)!
Metropolitan Bakery - the sour cherry choc chip cookie w/sea salt

I can only base this review on the cannoli I ate from Termini  Brothers. It was everything I hoped, for filled right before eating. Super crunchy shell and sweet and creamy on the inside. Don't forget to get a number just like a deli counter.
Was there the other day.  I had been there before, yet not for years.  Was totally overwhelmed by the amount of different types of food and the crowds.  Yet had a good time.

This market was easily my favorite spot we visited on a recent trip to Philly. I am pretty sure we could have eaten almost every meal of our trip here and been content.

They have every kind of food you can think of here, from Mediterranean to Indian to Mexican to Philly cheese steaks. They have a lot of stands devoted to fresh fruits and vegetables, meat and fish. They have a number of bakeries with cookies, cupcakes, cakes and donuts. They have spice shops, bookstores, honey shops and souvenir shops.

I personally really liked the Amish breakfast spot with the sandwiches. My husband had the pork roll sandwich and really enjoyed it. I also loved the red velvet whoopie pie from the Flying Fish bakery. We ate lunch here and got the philly cheese steaks at Carmen's. I could have eaten at a lot of the other shops too though!

This is a really fun place to walk around and try a variety of Philly foods. The prices are generally reasonable and there is plenty of seating available to sit down and have a meal. Many places are cash-only and the market can get very crowded on the weekends. I only wish they were open for dinner too!

A must-visit in Philly!

This place is ALL about food. So come with a serious appetite. Intensely crowded place. Long waits for food during lunch time, no matter what day of the week it is.

Save room for Bassetts ice cream!

Just be aware that this is primarily a place for tourists. And people who work nearby (for lunch).
Lots of cool food and shops to explore. Super crowded on the weekends though. Definitely try out the Philly cheesesteak and cheese fries when in Philadelphia!

Going to Reading Terminal Market is like an event in and of itself. There are so many amazing sights, scents and tastes! This place is one of the many things I love about Philadelphia. Anything you want, you can get it here. There's even a bar!

Not only can you get any kind of food you want from a number of sit-down places, you can also pick up fresh seafood and produce--why would anyone shop at the regular grocery store? The prices here are great. 

And the Amish bakeries..OOH the Amish bakeries..Make sure you get there before those booths close, because you do not want to miss out on all the varieties of breads, pastries and pies. My friend introduced me to Shoo Fly Pie from one of those places, and I will never be the same again. Shoo Fly Pie is basically sugar and molasses and butter in a yummy pie crust, and not much else. But when you think about it..what else do you need?

I'm very lucky I work close to this place. Or..maybe, not so lucky, since I am tempted to spend most of the money I make here.
This place is typically packed. It's fun and all Philly. I love the freshness of the food and all the choices.
Great food, great variety! Great for people watching! Kraftwork (?) grilled cheeses in Valley Dairy was great, try Valley Thunder with Brisket and Mac & Cheese!
Much better than their competitor chi ken. Their signature ninja crispy chicken is huge and freshly fried to order. Ninja nuggets are also good

The Reading Terminal Market is so cool.  It basically has everything you need (food court wise) in one spot.  My husband got the TOmmy DiNic's cheesesteak sandwich with the broccoli rabe where I got lost and confused with all the goodness surrounding me and went for the Jambalaya and Gumbo.  (Although a bit salty, this review is strictly for the Terminal Market).

We were so in awe with the hussle and bustle of everything.  And everything looked scrumptious.  My bff got a pound of Amish chicken wings.  Fried to goodness.  Her daughter (less than 2 loved em).

We finished it off with Bassets Ice Cream on a sugar  cone.  

DO: Make sure you stalk then grab a table quickly.  We had to wipe ours down a couple of times from the previous patrons but it fit all of us so we were good.
DO: Make a round or two of the whole place before you decide where to go.
DO: The ice cream.  It's really delicous and rich on a nice humid hot day.

DON'T: Get lost.  It's a big place and you can easily find yourself all in circles.
DON'T: Get the gumbo.  It was pretty salty.

I absolutely LOVE this place. It just smells sooo good when you walk in. My folks moved to this neck of the woods about 30 years ago when I was in college, but I never actually lived here and didn't know about this market until last year. All those trips to visit over the years and I didn't know about this market?!! I can't believe it! 

Well, I know about it now and have been 3 times in the past year (3 visits to the family). This is now a must-do for me whenever I visit. The food in this place is incredible. The pizza! The ribs! The Italian sandwiches! The delis, Thai and Chinese food! The cannoli (filled when you order them)!! There's so much great food here. There are also some very nice markets for fresh meat, fish, and vegetables. 

Here's the strategy that works for us: When I visit, we go mid-week and get there around 11 AM. Then we walk around for about half an hour to see what gets our taste buds going that day. Then we eat! And eat, and eat! We always have a cooler in the trunk of the car for this trip so we can bring home some of the wonderful looking fresh meats or fish. 

This is a must-do if you visit anywhere near Philly. It's a must-do if you live here. I really wish there was something like Reading Terminal Market where I live.

Sensory overload indeed. It doesn't matter what entrance you choose to come in at, nor does it matter the mood you were in when you got there. This place is huge, has lots of everything, and you will definitely find something you've never seen before somewhere in a corner here. Lots of vendors selling various wares and items litter the conglomeration of shops and the outside ring has food just waiting to be eaten. It's a great place that, with an unlimited supply of funds, one could stay here all weekend.
This place is a head turner. Full of culture and diversity. I ate so much from so many different places. Hands down my favorite stop in philly.

One of the best indoor markets I've been to, Reading Terminal is both a local delight and a tourist attraction. It is a foodie's haven, but also has other quirky shops that'll capture your attention for quite some time. 

Notes:
* Must try the places with long lines because they're obviously good. 
* Dutch Eating Place and Tommy DiNic's have those long lines.
* Don't even try looking for spaces in the general seating area unless you fight for them.
* Save room for dessert - Termini Bros Bakery, Chocolate by Mueller, and Famous 4th Street Cookie Company.
* Sometimes, it's worth being extra cold even in the winter - Bassett's Ice Cream.

Love this place. Some many choices. Now it is really busy must of the times I have been here. If you are in a group the best thing to do is walk around and get an idea of what you want then divide and concur. Make sure one of you is looking for a place to sit if you your staying. This is a must stop when you are in town.
This is seriously the only to go place in the airport with healthy snack options. Whole fruits, nuts, lara bars and kevita. Yum! This will be my go to any time I'm in terminal E!
Patience needed during peek hours!!  It gets crowded real quick!  Otherwise, a great and diverse selection of food and desserts.

This may be my favorite place in the whole wide world! 

If you visit Philly, and you only have time for one lunch, this is where you go! Great coffee, Chinese food, Amish desserts, chocolate, soul food, ice cream, crapes, Thanksgiving dinner, and of course...Tommy DiNics. 

I cannot overhype The Reading Terminal Market. It's that good and better.

I go to the RT for that Amish chicken place. 
The smoked wings are ridiculous.

What a customer service. Tried to use the Phillies tickets to get free breakfast sandwiches. But since they are not open for breakfast, and tickets were only good for the next day, they gave us lunch sandwich.

I love their chicken sandwich in the first place, now loving it even more.

Love the RTM, its a great place to just go in and grab a quick bite to eat or grab some goods to take back home. Needless to say this place can be deadly on the wallet especially if you like a lot of items in there like I do. Come hungry and then shop because trust me you will want to purchase everything in site.
This place is like heaven. some of the best food all in one place. A produce section and a lot of specialty grocery items.

Love this place!  I always have an idea of what I might eat before I go--turkey platter?  crepes?  If I don't have some idea before I go, I walk around hungry but undecided for a good hour!  For anyone visiting Philly, the Reading Terminal Market is a must see!   And go hungry--you will be glad you did!  My favorites stops are the fresh turkey dinner with mashed potatoes and gravy, or the true French crepes, sweet or savory.  I'm not stuck in a rut, I just can't resist these two spots!

We try to stop at the local downtown markets when traveling. It is one of our favorite things to do. This particular market was very busy and filled with a variety of local favorites to enjoy We enjoyed walking around and sampling some of the foods. There is a large seating area in the center of the marketplace.; good luck getting a seat.  DiNics was very tasty and Termini bakery was fabulous! The Almond pastry and Pecan Caramel Bar were incredible. Both could be addicting, so I'm glad we don't live close enough to indulge frequently, but I will be dreaming about both of those for awhile! The only disappointment was that we visited on a Sunday and many booths were closed. I would think weekends would be one of the busier times for them.

Also,we encountered several beggars both inside and outside of the market. Then we later saw them on cell phones eating at the food court with others. There should be some added security to prevent this from happening to patrons shopping. 

TIP -  the parking lot across the street offered a discounted parking pass for $4 for 2 hours with a validated purchase from the market.

Perfect place to grab lunch. Dozens of choices to please any picky eater. Whether you're here to quench your thirst or hunger, you'll definitely find something that'll please you! Just be careful to not stand in the middle of all the hustle and bustle so that you don't get run over by wandering tourists lol.

If I lived in Philly, I'd be living in the RTM!!! Yup, LIVING there! I was that fascinated. I love love love small vendors cooking up incredible, delectable bites. The croissant at Market Bakery was sooo good! It was flaky, buttery, delicious! I was a little sad that I had to share one with my boyfriend. Capuccino at Old City Coffee, yep, definitely 5 stars. It was strong, rich, foamy and piping hot. I struggle with this temperature issue at lots of coffee joints, including Starbucks. I want my coffee to be hot when it is served. I can adjust it to be less hot, if I want. I can't go the other way!
I digress. 
The cajun shrimp and crab pasta salad was good but I couldn't find any crab in it. The cheesesteak at Carmen's, DELISH! We got ours with roasted hot pepper and mushrooms. The heat was a definite plus!
Finally, Bassett's icecream was a good way to end brunch. 
Definitely coming back here when I visit Philly again!

One of Philadelphia's gems, Reading Terminal Market boasts something for everyone. A foodie's paradise!  This is a must visit if not once but several times if ever in the area.  From sweet treats to raw oysters, all the way to fresh produce and some of the best prepared foods you can find.  The cuisine ranges from BBQ, Dutch breakfast, to cajun all the way to Asian.  

One of our favorite finds in the market includes stocking up on fresh jerky and meat sticks (sounds weird but dont knock it til you try it!), which you can buy by the pound and take back with you for a great road trip snack.  

A thing to note: Try to come on any day but Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, as there a lot of Dutch/Amish that close on those days with goodies you don't want to miss.  Also, although it is crowded, it is all very much worth it.  My only regret is not finding Reading Terminal sooner!  Wish we had something like it in Boston!  Truly a gem!
Excellent food and shopping right in Center City. It is one of my favorite spots to go to for lunch.

LOVE this place for everything from produce, to meat from the butcher, fish from the monger, treats, coffee and local produce and meat.  Eating here is one stop shopping.  Wish it was open for longer hours on weekdays tho!

Crowded but for a good reason. Waiting on a long line for anything is always worth it. Don't think it's just a place for lunch and tourists, it's got great and cheap produce for your weekly food shopping

This Market is Philadelphia! if you can only visit one place in Philadelphia, this is it.
Shop, eat, browse and gaze in wonder.
I have been coming here since i can remember and i am going to start Medicare in May, it has been my favorite place my entire life.

Everything you want in one place. Literally, a plethora of food and products all in one location. It is a great place to hangout with friends and for a meal. I haven't had a bad experience yet, except for looking for seating, but everything there is great.

I don't think there are enough words to describe Reading Terminal Market and it's an impossibility to review every single vendor in there! The market is big, usually crowded (especially on weekends) and there are food options as far as the eye can see. Whatever you want to eat, they have it and more!

When we came on a Saturday afternoon at about 12:30pm, the market was bustling. It felt like every tourist in Philly was here. From the moment we walked in, our stomachs began growling from the smell and sights of all of the food. There were so many delectable places to eat from our heads were spinning. However, with that said, I did have a few key observations, specifically about the vendors:

Pearl's Oyster Bar - From reading reviews, this is probably one of the most popular spots to eat at because they serve seafood and apparently very good seafood! When I passed by, the place was packed, although they had one of the largest seating areas of any vendor. 

Beiler's Bakery and Belier's Donuts - By far, the most popular desserts/pastry vendor in the market. The line for the donuts was the longest line I saw for any vendor and for a good reason as the donuts looked ridiculously amazing! We ordered a  1/2 dozen for ourselves and are still feeling the effects of how good the donuts were!

Molly Malloy's - They serve tavern/gastropub type food. We ordered the Chicken Pot Pie from here as recommended by many online blogs. The Pot Pie was good, but not great. Although filling, it could've used a bit more flavor.

Beck's Cajun Café - The employees were handing out samples of their soups and Jambalaya, which made it all the more difficult to pass it up after trying out their food. As the name indicates, they serve Cajun, Louisiana style foods --- gator meat, po boys, Jambalaya, Gumbo, etc.

Basset's - The only ice cream vendor in the market and, not only is it rich in history, but rich in many flavors! The employees here were extremely generous with the scoops of ice cream they gave on the cones we got. They were some of the biggest ice cream scoops I had ever seen.

DiNic's Roast Pork - According to the hype, they have arguably the best Roast Pork sandwich in Philly. Unfortunately, we didn't have the stomach space to store the sandwich, but it's on my to go list. The line for the sandwiches was pretty deep too.

There were so many vendors and so many places to eat, I could go on and on about the vendors. If you come here on a weekend, just be prepared for the crowds. It will get hectic and, although there are tables towards the back, its a first come first serve. Trying to find an open table during peak hours can become an issue so many customers actually walk and eat as they go. It's all part of the fun of coming here and exploring the different types of foods served here. It's a must visit if you're in Philly!

Organized very intelligently. There are obvious sections throughout the entire market making it a joy to stroll through. You will suddenly find yourself in the honey and handcrafted soaps section, or the eye popping fresh produce section. Everything here seems fresh and local. The prices are affordable and each vendor is willing to tell you about their wares. I saw the coolest mushroom stand here, with more species than I've ever seen in my life. My friend and I bought some gifts for our friends back home since we were travelling in Philly.

Add this to your Philly bucket list.  This place is AMAZING!!!  On my next trip I'm renting a hotel near this place so I can get there more easily.  The Reading Terminal Market is filled with foods of every variety.  Some awesome cheese steaks, fresh seafood, donuts, ice cream, candy and so much more.  Everything we ate was delicious.  

My only advice, come hungry.  Come very very hungry.

Endless options! There's so much to choose from, yet the two times I've been there for lunch to eat, I went to the same place, Profi's Creperie. It was pretty good! I also got Mocha Chip ice cream from Bassetts Ice Cream. They give you generous portions. In fact, after all that ice cream, I kind of wished they had given me less. I had originally been scoping out a fruit tart, but there wasn't a single one in sight. That was a letdown. My cousin also tried clam chowder from Pearl's Oyster Bar. That was a disappointment, too. Nevertheless, I'll be back!
Gotta say, happy hour here is great! The crowd is fun and the deals can't be beat! The staff is accommodating and kind. Have fun!
They got the nicest people working there. The guy who took my order Sterling needs a raise. Give him about $15 an hour. Went in there during their lunch rush and git out pretty fast. Great place

Great market. I love the availability of local honey, whole chicken, raw milk, etc. if you like food this is a must stop- a lot of variety of quick eats. Wish I had something like this close to home. I visited as a tourist and would be interested to know if local like it too.

Was excited to go here and first impressions were good. After more exploring it became apparent that the choice and quality of most of the food was limited, with one or two exceptions. The prices are high.

I love this place .The food choices are outstanding .Start with the fresh produces and work your way around the baked goods, chicken,chocolates,coffee,prezels Chinese food ,Southern cooking ,juice bar,fresh turkeys,beer and cocktails .You want a decent fair priced meal with food on your plate you need to come here.OBTW if you don't like noises and crowds please avoid this place, But the noise and the crowds  is also part of the charm

It's a great place for lunch, TONS to choose from. There's a sandwich shop right in the center that I like, and the sweet shop near the entrance. The folks from Lancaster are always very friendly, too. (And if you ever get selected for Jury Duty, this is where you'll be going for lunch; probably the only good thing about that!)

I remember wandering through Reading Terminal Market once several years ago, but I don't remember being all that enamored.  I'm pretty sure this was before I turned into a Food Network junkie, before I ever cooked for myself, before I had any kind of appreciation for fresh, quality ingredients, and certainly long before I began Yelping.

What my friends and I thought would be a pretty quick trip turned into a two-hour exploration.  Because it was a Sunday morning, the Amish vendors were closed, but since I have yet to sample their wares, I didn't miss them.  There was plenty to choose from: produce, spices, meat, cheeses, seafood, baked goods...  Maybe it was just the novelty of the place, but I felt inspired to create.

When we had finally filled our shopping bags with various fresh finds, we decided to get something prepared to eat.  We ended up at Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties, where I tasted my first falafel and lamb shawerma.  Delish!  We ended at Flying Monkey Patisserie where, forced with too many choices, I ordered a brownie to eat at that moment, plus 4 different cupcakes to take home.

Since there are less merchants open on Sundays, RTM was not that crowded during my visit.  I was satisfied with the choices that remained, but am definitely curious enough about what wasn't open to brave what I hear will be a pretty chaotic weekday.

Everyone who visits Philly needs to make time for Reading Terminal. It is a cross-section of Pennsylvania, with delicious Italian food, Asian grocers, amazing baked goods from the Amish, and local produce and dairy products. We would all be better off if we did our grocery shopping here. 

I also love Molly Malloy's, because sometimes you want a beer and a sandwich in the middle of the day.

Prepared foods, produce, fresh meats...the market is a wonderland!  The cheese market is great, the sausage guy has great stuff, and there's a Metropolitan Bakery outpost.  Oh, and Flying Monkey Patisserie.  And the shop that carries Wilbur Buds (drops of chocolate created BEFORE Mr. Hershey introduced his own version nearby, hmm).

Great place for tourists and locals alike. Get a great lunch or some reasonably priced ingredients for dinner at home.  

I also love the fact that you can try different kinds of scrapple at various breakfast joints. They've even got a scrapple festival.

This review started with four stars. But as I wrote the review, I convinced myself that it deserves five.

A great place to shop and browse. The veggie section is a must.

Only negative is bookshop in the back sells the vile anti Semitic and anti American rag "The Final Call" the propaganda organ of hatemonger Louis Farrakhan's Nation of Islam.

Variety is the key! If you are a visitor to Philadelphia you will see so many styles different cuisines under one roof - all of them respectable to fantastic. 

If you are a native of the city and haven't yet visited - get there!

I was debating between 3 and 4 stars for this place, the service and the drinks were definitely 4 stars but I felt that the food could use some work and I will explain.  First we showed up and were able to grab a high top and settled in.  Our waitress was very helpful and always seemed to be around when we needed her.  We started off with the pig ear lettuce wraps.  These were very tasty although I do wish there were at least 1 or 2 more strips of pig ear in them but hey I guess that's a little nitpicky.  For dinner we split the wings and the short rib sandwich.  The wings were good, definitely a good size and good meat on them,  the house wing sauce which was a soy-hoisin sauce was interesting and good.  The short rib sandwhich was good but there was hardly any short rib on it.  The bun was probably 3-4 inches thick with hardly any meat so it mainly felt like I was eating a bread sandwich.  The sandwich was supposed to come with kimchi but I couldn't even tell if it was on there to be quite honest.  It was a bit of a letdown, so that is why I am giving it 3 stars.  We tried the S'more for dessert and it was good but I felt like there wasn't enough graham cracker and marshmallow, don't get me wrong the chocolate granache was good but it was extremely dense and rich and just completely took over the dish.  I would like to go back and check this place out again and try some different things.

Great first timer!  This is Foodie heaven!  Came down on a Sun around 2pm and the place was already jammed packed.   Thanks for the tips from fellow Yelpers, we tried the famous Dinic's sandwiches (provolone with roast pork) and they were quite good.  I was the 50th one in line but it was well worth the wait.  Washed it down with a blueberry, pineapple, banana smoothie from four Seasons Juice bar.   For dessert, had the famous 4th Street double chocolate chip cookie and it was soft and really tasty!  yum!  We missed the Amish stores as they were closed on Sunday.  Tons of food and things to buy but will have to trek back on a weekday (less crowded).   Only peeves: 1) the cleaners didn't clean the tables in a timely manner and empty water bottles and napkins littered all over the floor.   2) Parking is a pain though (can't find those special lots they keep advertising $4 for 2 hours on their site will try to find it next time around.    Tip:  I found large parking lot on 9th (between Market/Filbert) connects to the Gallery at East Market and it was like 3 hrs for $10.
Interesting market - similar to Boston's Quincy market - but more condensed, large crowds but great little shops.
This place is AMAZING!!! Whatever you are in the mood to eat, you can find it here. The portions are outstanding and the service is fast. I have not been to a place in here that I did not like.

Im not sure... why they have so many good reviews... I mean, the place is all right. nothing too special about it. Bunch of food/shops things you can eat at. They also sell fresh fruit, veggies, fish, seafood. The whole place is relatively clean, but not the most shiny place either. If you are around the area, you can check it out, but dont expect too much - maybe your experience would be better than mine :)

Stopped in today to pick up lunch and
really enjoyed the food there. I had the Paneer Masala Kati roll and the vegetable Biryani. The Paneer Masala roll was very tasty and they did not skimp on the paneer! The vegetable Biryani was delicious and had just enough spice to it.
They give you a nice serving of the Biryani for the price and I'll be saving more than half for another meal. 

They offer up two sauces to accompany your dishes. One is a white sauce that I thought was going to be similar to Raita but turns out it was very mayo based. I really would have rather had Raita but it's free so I don't want to complain too much about it. It would definitely help cool down some of the spice. 

Also, I was a little disappointed to find that they served me pita bread instead of naan. It was good fluffy pita bread but I'd much rather have naan with their food. 

I will definitely go back as it's super close to my office and very tasty. It's nice having a quick take out place to go when I have a craving Indian food. Also, the staff were friendly and pleasant so go check it out.
Everytime we go to philadelphia we go to the reafing market at least twice. Food is excellent and so many choices. Only problem is not enough seating at lunchtime.a must see
Must go place. From donuts to funnel cake, BBQ to pizza this place was amazing. PS you can eat anything for breakfast.

I would love this place if they had chicken or beef or some other fresh protein. They offer "chicken sausage", which looks disgusting, and smoked salmon, which I don't think belongs in a salad. Everything else is great but the lack of lean, healthy protein options makes this place incompatible with my omnivorous diet. Too bad, because it has such potential.

This place is a foodie heaven! If you go...go hungry and carve out a couple of hours so you can meandor around and experience it all! I started at the far right side of the market where I got a directory and worked my way through. There are cheesesteaks (of course), seafood, pastries, soul food, Chinese, Cajun, Italian, Greek, cookies, fresh produce, flowers, fresh meat, and so much more.  There are several stands that cater to organic produce and dairy products as well. They also have stands that sell hand crafted soaps, chapsticks, specialty German items and everything in between. There probably isn't anything you can't find here. TIP!!! Parking in the city is not easy nor is it inexpensive. Park for $4.00 in one of these conveniently located garages:
11th & Arch Streets (Expert Parking)

12th & Filbert Streets (Parkway Garage)

With $10 purchase and merchant validation. Limit 2 hours. BE SURE TO GET YOUR PARKING TICKET AND RECEIPTS VALIDATED BEFORE YOU LEAVE THE MARKET!!! THE DISCOUNT IS NOT HONORED WITHOUT THE VALIDATION. 
If you find yourself in Phialdelphia, it is worth a trip to this market. If just for the history alone (this market has been around since 1892.)

Places I've tried and highly recommend!!!

DiNic's: Get the hand carved beef brisket, I really think it tastes better than the roast pork, which kind of lacks flavor

Hershel's Deli: CORN BEEF sandwich!

Bee Natural: Really love their Honey in the Raw

Bassetts Ice Cream: I recently tried their Pralines and Cream... wow!!!

Dutch Eating Place: Unfortunately only open Wednesday-Saturdays, but this place is always my top choice. Their Amish breakfast is the bomb if you don't want to travel all the way to Amish country!

Oh, Mama!  Why have I not had the pleasure of the Industry's food till tonight?  Stopped in for dessert, but had to get the Duck Confit Doughnuts - get them people - buttery, savory, duck balls with goat cheese which are fried can never be wrong.  They were out of the polenta cake and subbed a Smores-type dessert with graham cracker crust, chilled dark chocolate ganache, and toasted house-made marshmallow.  It was pretty good, especially since the smokiness of the marshmallow lingered in my mouth long after the ganache had melted down my throat - yummm and such a good dessert for that oh so sexy someone - oh, but I get beside myself.  We also had the cheese plate, with three semi-hard cheeses, one each from goat, sheep, and cow's milk that were accompanied with honey, toast points, jelly, and sliced apples.  

Their cocktails seem pretty legit - I usually drink vodka, but I had a sip of a drink my friend got that had fernet - if you like fernet, you'll like it. 

Can't wait to come back here.  Oh, p.s., we stopped in on a Thursday night, which was right in the middle of their quizzo - anyone good at trivia?

A review on the venue and not so much the stores and shops within:

If you live in the Philadelphia metro area, it would be a crime not to visit at least once.  Super convenient to by public transit especially SEPTA's Market East Regional Rail station.

The variety, the personality, the diversity of culture.  Sociological studies could be done here.  You can't not find something delicious to eat for any mood or diet.

Shining stars include the Pennsylvania Dutch place that serves wings and Termini Bros. Bakery (best cannoli I've ever had).

It's a Philly institution for a reason. it's great for lunch and also for picking up your fresh produce. If you're there to eat you've got to visit Dinic's, my favourite is the brisket with provolone, but you'll see most people ordering the pork. It's pretty great too. We could spend hours, and we sometimes do, wandering the small shops and buying products from the small artisan producers.

It is a must visit if you are in town, but try and avoid the well known places in the middle and venture to the back and sides. Some hidden gems include and olive oil store "The Tubby Olive." It is an adult candy store with free samples of delicious oils and balsamics. 

Beck's Cajun Cafe has some great Po Boy sandwiches and let's you order half of two types --  it is worth trying the oyster. And of course they put Chicory in their coffee. 

The Amish donut stand makes them hot and almost to order. Bacon and Maple is my favorite. And, yes, it is worth every calorie. But they aren't there on Sunday.

Generally worth getting to the Terminal around 10. Lets your venture freely without crowds.

Reading Terminal is a defining location of Philly--so how could I not like it? With everything from charming Amish farmers to trendy food artisans to good ol' blue collar cheese steaks,  Reading Terminal fully encompasses what defines Philly cuisine. (Just, please, don't go on the weekends).

How can you not LOVE the Reading Terminal Market?  It's a taste of everything Philly in one location.  Is it crowded? Yes.  Can parking be a pain?  Yes.  But will you have a culinary experience liken one other? Yes.  

For a full experience don't go on a Sunday, the Amish stands are closed (I think they're closed Monday's, too), so you'll miss out on some delicious treats and what feels like 1/4 of the market will be closed.  

The Market has changed a lot recently- a few new stands and brand new bathrooms.  It feels cleaner and more customer friendly.  We always stop by The Original Turkey - it's the best!!!

Went yesterday asked for a salad, the girl came back with a pan with a small amount of wilted lettuce. I asked if they had anymore she said it was out. I said to her chipotle out of lettuce ?!?!!! This was because of her ignorant who cares attitude. Miraculously when I barked back at her ( giving her what she fished out to me) there appeared a fresh full pan ! Amazing if these people don't want to work and want to bring thier streety attitude to the workplace, maybe they shouldn't have a job there. I'm sure there would be someone that would gladly take the job. Not good food service knowledge !!!
Btw was in there at 4pm July 16,2018. The girl I'm talking about was first in line asking what I wanted. I'm sure chipotle can narrow down who this ignorant employee was and rectify this problem .

Only giving this one star because zero is not an option. Terrible greasy flavorless food at a high price. If I had known how awful the breakfast sandwich would be (spongy fake egg, artificially smoked bacon), I would have just had the toasted everything bagel (no texture, vague onion flavor). Bad coffee: brown colored hot water. Nice servers though: it's not their fault.

This is the best market in Philadelphia. Forget Whole Foods and Trader Joes. This place has all of the fresh veggies, candy, butcher stalls, fish markets, and PA Dutch food you could imagine. And the people watching is pretty great too. Bonus points if you check our Herschel's corned beef special. Yum!

I really like this place.  Want ice cream? check.  Want gumbo? check.  How about a vegetarian cheesesteak sandwich? check!  The Reading is a great place to take out-of-town guests, but it's also fun for townies to come for lunch or just to ppl watch.  When I'm in a rush for an ingredient, I'll sometimes stop in here at the spice market for it.  There's also an international food store - sure, they're a little pricier than Whole Foods, but hey - when ur in the midst of awaiting your dough to rise, sometimes you just don't have time to drive to the supermarket.

Some of my favorite places are: the Amish bakery on the NW corner of the market.  They make really good Raisin Bread (you can also watch them making cinnamon rolls), Iovine Brothers Produce (students get a 10% discount on Wed and Sun), OK Lee Produce (students get 10% discount everyday), the Basic Vegetarian (again, vegetarian cheesesteak), Beck's Cajun Cafe (beignets on Wed, also have really good gumbo and jambalaya), and Dinic's (the line is always around the corner for their sandwiches).

Some places take cash only, so it's better if you come with some.  If not, there are ATMs throughout the market.  

Besides food, there are stands that sell jewelry, cookbooks, kitchenwares, candles, lotions, souvenirs - just come check it out if you haven't already - there's usually something for everyone.
Great place to go and grab lunch or baked goods, must try the Amish pretzel it's so good!!!

I would go back to Philly just to visit the market again. It's an absolute East Coast must-do. I tried Old City Coffee, Meltkraft, Birdies Biscuits, DiNic's meats, Bassett's Ice Cream, Beck's Cajun Cafe, and Loco Lucho's Puerto Rican, plus bought [super affordable and fresh!] grapes at one of the two produce stands and specialty chocolates at the Pennsylvania General Store. Everything was absolutely delicious and the energy is amazing. I cannot wait to go back.

First time there last week.  Way too crowded and loud.  Every single person was so nice except for the cook at Spataros.  He was so rude, barking at everybody. He screamed at me for asking if the cheese I ordered was on the sandwich, standing there in his stained undershirt. YUCK.. Will NEVER go to this establishment again. The other servers were nice and helpful.  The chocolates were out of control delish! Parking was a pain. There was some other stands that I would have liked to have sampled and some of the produce and other stuffs looked great but it was a bit much to deal with.

This place is great! Rose lassi!?! Genius! 
The important thing is to consider this place to be a fast food type restaurant. Either grab n go or sit down and gobble up your meal - which is essentially how Kati rolls are supposed to be served. To some of the other reviews- yes they have a variety of options like biryani - but the place is for KATI ROLLS. its in the title. Biryani is not a super easy dish to make in a small fast food kitchen. Takes time and care. Don't expect it to be like a restaurant and demand that level of customer service. The people there are always pleasant when I come in - but I usually know exactly what I want. I have to say their paneer rolls are waaay better than their meat rolls. One time they forgot to give me the discount and reimbursed me while I was eating, even though I had not noticed. Very nice of them. If you're going for the first time definitely get the paneer Masala - I am willing to say that it might be their BEST roll and what I always pick up. All their other paneer rolls are great. Go for it even if you're not a vegetarian (avoid it if you're lactose intolerant). 
Also - if it's your first time, do yourself a f(L)avor   (Get it!?!) and get the rose lassi. You will not be disappointed.

This is such an amazing place. I was so overwhelmed but in a good way. Im a huge foodie and wanted to try every place in the terminal. Its a total day of fun for sure. Great eats!!! Its a must try when in Philly

A great way to visit the Amish without having to drive to Lancaster.

The riffraff on Filbert Street is mostly harmless and can actually be entertaining at times

This is just one of many farmers' markets in Philly but has the distinction of having a majority of Amish farmers and products. Whenever I'm visiting my family in New York I love eating this Dutch Potato Bread. I always thought the Dutch reference was to the Netherlands but now I've realised it meant the Amish. Silly me. One advice is if you want any of their product to make sure you get to the market before 3pm-ish because bang on they will pack up and leave. We had a late lunch of a Turkey sandwich and gravy. It literally is a sandwich smothered in gravy. A fun market.

A new addition in Chinatown - got the chicken combo and it was pretty tasty.

Looking forward to trying the squid next.

One word:  DiNic's.  Get the roast pork sandwich.  Seafood mongers have the freshest fish in the city and its the only place I know of where you can get a variety of fresh fish roe for frying (not the sushi stuff like Salmon and Flying Fish, think any female fish carrying an egg sac.)

Do you wish to have sensory overload? If so, head to Reading Terminal Market, right quick!

The colors, the smells, the hustle-and-bustle of the people who are looking for good eats, and then the good eats... Oh. My. Gosh. It is just an amazing place to...exist. They have seafood, Amish donuts, great chicken, roast pork sandwiches and other deli sandwiches, the country's oldest continuously operated ice cream parlor, and the list goes on and on.

We had very little time to spend in Philadelphia, but our visit here is most definitely one of my most favorite things that we have done. I will be back, and when I do, I will make sure I am truly famished. There are just too many things I want to eat from this place!

It feels wrong to love Chick-Fil-A. 

I'm not talking about the moral code / political opinion of the company, but the fact the chicken remains stupidly addictive while also being stupidly unhealthy. My only CFA experiences have been from down south - all great - but the city of brotherly love did not disappoint. 

It was a complete meal: waffle fries, a hearty yet sugary milkshake, and a juicy, tender chicken biscuit to top it off. A friend was rockin nuggets and some sweet tea, which were definitely tasty in their own right. And we were able to scarf it all down after failing to score some John's Roast Pork (http://www.yelp.com/biz/johns-roast-pork-philadelphia) due to their strict afternoon hours.

But in the end, the service, cleanliness of the interior (and bathrooms!) all score big points in fast food land. Not that there is much to love about fried food on the go, but there is just something about the chicken that makes this experience worth repeating again. We need one like this in NYC.

Best place for anything you could ever possibly want food wise.  We always plan to stop here when ever we go to the city.  Have a delicious breakfast or lunch and pick up something special for dinner.

Love this place! There's a donut shop there that makes the best donuts. You'll know it from the mile long line if you go on a Saturday.  I highly recommend visiting on a weekday, if you have the option.

The food choices is amazing. I hate the long lines and it is hard for me to find a seat to eat. I use to go the gallery to sit down but it is under construction. The energy is like no other but those improvement would make it so much better.

This market offers something for everyone. Coffee, tons of food options, groceries, cute souvenirs and housewares, an insight into Amish farming, and you can even get a decent Philly cheesesteak. It gets busy but still is manageable even during the lunch rush. Best part, as a tourist, is that they have free wifi! So you can start off your day at the market with some delicious food, and plan out the rest of your day while you eat.

Love this place!  Need a fresh cut of meat and want to talk directly to the butcher?  Want a whole fish for dinner, but don't know exactly what you're looking for?  Go to the Reading Terminal Market!  It's a fun way to spend a Sunday morning, strolling thru the stands, sampling the merch.  For breakfast, try the Dutch Eating Place (long lines, limited seating, but it moves fast) get the blueberry pancakes and turkey bacon-bit of a splurge, may want to walk home and skip the sub or taxi :)
Noisy, Crowded, but whenever I'm in town I go there for the Corned Beef Special and the Cannoli's at Termini's.

LOVE THIS PLACE

It is truly a foodie heaven with everything from baked goods to cheesesteaks to gyros in sight and walking distance. Tried the Boston Cream donut from Beiler's and a cheesesteak from Carments. Both had the longest lines (lunch hour rush) but were worth the wait.

LOL @ people calling this a tourist trap, overrated, not worth the time... It is downtown and within walking distance to every major location center city Philadelphia has to offer... OF COURSE tourists will come here.

This place is pretty awesome...tourist or not. It has a little or a lot of everything, and there is a good chance if you're in the mood for something... you'll find it here.

This place will be here forever... no Yelp review is going to change that lol.

Awesome place to see a mix of Philly food and people culture ! Love all the options  and would have been a 5 star but very uncomfortable walking out being  hounded by addicts as you walk in and out of the entrances . Little too cramped and crowded at times .
Amazing place. Very Philly. Bustling food court with fresh and diverse options. Foodie haven for sure.
Overwhelming amount of foods to choose from but a definite must! Being your fat pants and eat as much as you can! I can't recommend any particular place but only that you try as much as you can.
So cool!! Has many small food stores located inside. My favorite has to be Carmen's cheesesteaks and hoagies!! Amazing taste!

Interesting market with a really great range of groceries, fruit preserves, meat, cheese and wine just to name a few. It's noted as a must see local, historic attraction on Philadelphia's tourism website. 

Nice food court with lots of tables and seating. Ending up getting ice-cream from Bassett's and wine from Blue Mountain Wine.

If you're a tourist in Philly, you should definitely stop by.

This place is amazing if you are at all a foodie, or just like to experience and taste a city! This place has something for everyone here! My suggestion is bring your wallet, appetite, and make sure you have plenty of time! To many places to try and cram in a hurry!

Yay for Reading!  Why is it pronounced "redding" and not "reading."  English is hard.

I get all my produce here, and it's usually super fresh (hey, that's the name of a grocery store) and super cheap (that'll be my grocery that competes with Super Fresh).  I really like the Iovine Brothers and the Lee Produce places.  The one dollar grab bags always crack me up because they're always filled with things that don't go together: carrots with apples, mushrooms and celery, dogs and cats..

I also love the organic food stand that's tucked in the back.  They have a really nice variety of fresh apples.  

As for the Amish, it's so nice to see them making pretzels and other yummy things.  I've had a couple of things from their shops and they're pretty good.  For you sweet tooths out there, they have a ton of amazing desserts- Amish and not.

The only that that really bothers me about the place is that some of the vendors sell really lame knick knacks, but I guess that means I should just avoid them and not say anything.  But I did.  So there.

This is a great place to be a tourist or be a local.  It's a nice attraction and also a place that sells great products.

So what's keeping you at home?  Get on your buggy and make your way out to the Reading Terminal Market.

I absolute love anything resembling a farmers or flea market, so of course fell in love with this place. I stuffed my face with Amish donuts and bought some herbal tea from this organic shop. I doesn't over an hour going up and down the aisles. I probably shouldn't of went hungry. They had everything to eat you could ever want. Food coma!

Gee, let's put aaaall of F's consumable temptations underneath one roof & see if she won't go crazy. What the hell was this- a test from Buddha or something?!?!

Good lord, it seriously took me MAD will power to pry myself out of this joint. The spot with the southern food was aaaaight, the BBQ was bangin', the cookies were phenomenal. 

But the cherry on top- the ridiculously low priced sweet goodies the Amish were selling. EVERYTHING made freshly from scratch at great deals. I toootally stocked up on almost everything they had to offer.

*Deal tip: swing on by about an hour before closing, people start to sell their freshly made goods at deeply discounted prices in order to get rid of them.
Love this place. So many options. Seems like locals come here as well which is nice. Highlights were the ribs and mac and cheese balls. Oh yeah, the cannolis!
Best lunch in the city!  Best selection, most authentic food in Philly.
I try to go every time i visit my sister. we walked around, and had lots of fun.

Perfect place for tourists and locals. Affordable produce, specialty bakeries such as Terminini's, Cheesesteak, chocolate, meat, fish, diner, and  the amazing donuts. This review is for the Riehl's deli. Very friendly staff you can try it first. They have cheese too. You have to take a number. Accept card payment.

Agreed that getting parking validated is a pain, but I love this spot as a local bus-ride away.

Countless options, awesome food, huge pieces of meat and crab.  A great place to swing by whenever you're prepping for a dinner party.  

A bit overwhelming on the first trip but it's okay, you'll keep going back :)

I went in there hungry so I ordered the meatball sandwich and a bowl of chili and it was a let down.The meatballs were fake and from a box and the chili had that phony sweetness which makes me think its from a canI found it to be expensive too.It bothers me because Mazzoni's deli is only a few minutes away and they have real delicious homemade chili for alot lower price and a far superior meatball sandwich.The staff here was extremely nice and quick I just have a problem with the food itself

So good to be home! 
LOVE a good Amish breakfast and pan fried scrapple with maple syrup !!!
As good as life gets!
This is the place to get any delicious goodie you want to eat all under one roof.  A Philly must experience.

TLDR: perfect for the late night munchies, can't go wrong with the mk special, and skip the drinks (unless it's the mint lemonade)

I love Masala! There's nothing like a Kati roll or chicken platter after a night out, cause this place is open til 3am!! The service is very friendly and consistent. Never had a bad interaction in the 10+ times I've been there. 

Tips: if you go past 11pm on a weekend, chances are it will be packed with very hungry, very drunk customers. Also they have various student discounts so just ask! The red sauce is spicy, but definitely more manageable than halal guys. They're super generous with the sauces, and I've definitely taken more than a couple of those red and white sauces to put on my other dishes. 

The only downsides I can think of are 1) even though the platters are based off those halal platters from NYC, I'm not sure if they are actually halal 2) the whole menu is kinda pricey, especially since the Kati rolls are on the small side and 3) their drinks are hit or miss - the blackberry one tasted like cough syrup, but the mint lemonade one was amazing
Good food, horrible service. Not friendly, they don't talk any more than to ask your order and tell you how much they owe.

If you have never been here then you have to visit. Whether you live in Philadelphia or are visiting, it is a one of a kind experience. There is such a variety of food that you will never be dissapointed. There are even gift shops and a used book store! It is very diverse and all inclusive. Even if you are a little claustrophobic and don't like busy places crammed with people, you should fight through it and get out of your comfort zone and go try it!

Well, I'm probably digging myself a hole straight to the depths of Yelp hell, but the Reading Terminal Market is overrated. Maybe I don't appreciate what RTM has to offer... maybe I had this grandiose idea of what the place would be like in my head... maybe I just suck. Who knows. 

Too many people. Tight walkways. Lines wrapped around booths so you have know no idea where they start and where they end. No concept of walking on the right. Dirty bathrooms. Rude bathroom attendant. Eating areas are cramped. Meh. 

Hate all you want on the city of Cleveland, but they have the West Side Market. I imagined that the RTM would be similar, but man was I wrong. The West Side Market has high ceilings and a more open feel to it. Feels less congested and easier to navigate. Sorry Reading, but I'll take the West Side Market any day over your hot mess.

So much to see...so little time!
I have loved this place since I was a kid-it's a must see for all Philadelphia visitors!

Impression:They always list this place as a top 10 thing to do in Philly and it's a no wonder! If you've been to Seattle's Pike Market, then this is a more urban and New England version of it. It has produce from farms, heritage varieties, fresh eggs, cheddars, deli, meats, and bakeries that offer mouth watering pastries. There's also a large variety of food stands and stalls that offer a very impressive variety of foods from barbecue, to breakfast, desserts, Indian, African, and Hillel foods. 

Prices- That's what everyone always wants to know especially if it's a tourist attraction. So in terms of produce, it's not bad priced. Not as high as whole foods, but certainly not your Italian Marketplace where you can haggle your way down to pennies. One can probably get some quality farmer produce for a reasonable price of like 1.99$/lb for apples or 2 for 1$ corn to give an idea of the ballpark range. The food is also pretty reasonable priced. You can get a whole lunch set for less than 10$ and the portions are large. You can order most foods for less than 10$ here. 

Hours- so this place is open until 6 pm on most days, so if you're going to go, do not bank on this place on being your dinner place, because chances are most of the produce will have been sold off, stalls are closing, and you may be left with whatever is leftover (meaning smaller selection). I recommend hitting this place for lunch or even late afternoon stop as you wrap up your activities. 

Food: What to try- there are a few places that have their original site outside the marketplace. Meltykraft and Metropolitan Bakery have their own stand alone branches outside of this marketplace for example, so I recommend trying places that cannot be found outside- this may require a little more research, but the Indian food place for 9.99$ lunch set looked amazing and line moved fast. The Amish desserts are also a hit here as well. 

Amount of time recommended- you can probably spend a couple of hours in this establishment. It is massive and overwhelming. It has almost everything, so don't go in starving because you'll probably just wind up sitting at the first place you see and stuffing your face and then be sad you can't put down the amazing looking treats ahead.

A great place to browse, shop for fresh groceries and eat! Reading Terminal has an vast selection of cuisines, ranging from Mediterranean to Southern homestyle joints. There are also different dessert options to choose from - ice cream, bakery goods, Profi's crepes, and Flying Monkey cup cakes! Oh my..

This place gets packed, especially during the lunch hours and over the weekend. Despite the amount of people, it doesn't stop me from getting my weekly fix of crepes!

If you are parking at the lot on filbert, be sure to get your parking ticket validated for a nice discount. Simply bring it to a vendor of your choice and ask nicely :)
Reading Terminal is a great spot to be an active eater.  Go enjoy some food and take in the sights.

This place has it all from ice cream to cheesesteaks, and everything in between! You want marmite? They got it. You need some co-op produce? Check! Seriously, it's great for tourists and Philadelphians alike. Also a great place to go looking for gifts!

It's not all that often that I venture over to this side of town, but I think I kinda like it.

It's almost unexpected to stumble upon this smart corner restaurant. Its one large room with wood paneled high ceilings and an open view kitchen create a warm and inviting all-seasons appeal.

The food is interesting with a smattering of eccentric options present, from sausage and mussels in a spicy white ale-based sauce to savory guinea hen with Parmesan crusted corn on the cob.

This is clearly a great spot for weekend brunch or late night dinner in what I'd imagine is the next up and coming Philly neighborhood. Cool.

Was just strolling around my hotel and by accident landed in this little piece of heaven. One mouthwatering food stall after another. If you love food more than people, as one of my special friends tends to say, then this is Shangri La.
I bet half of the stalls here would make it on my yelp list.

this is like a farmers market held indoors! many different food options from dutch to cajun to bakeries and coffees to pretzels and ice creams.  theres a mini produce market in the back as well.
lots of people and lots of see, eat, and do.

i can eat breakfast here everyday!
Love the Amish place for breakfast, Apple dumpling with ice cream cannot be beat!  Also Rick's cheese steaks are the bomb!

This is a mediocre restaurant cafe. They have a selection of salads, paninis, etc, which are overpriced and slightly above-average tasting at best. 

I got the Chicken Mozzarella panini (I think), and it was okay. It was like $8 though, which is ridiculous, considering it is literally bread, chicken, cheese and tomatoes put together. I also asked for a glass of water, and the lady told me they only had bottled water, which is ridiculous - they have a sink and I only wanted tap water. I bought an iced tea instead, which was mediocre, and of course, overpriced. 

I think Chickie's & Pete's, Auntie Anne's, and Jamba Juice are better options than this place at the airport. Wasn't a huge fan at all!

What a delicious, fast, fresh, and friendly lunch. This was a brand new concept in quick serve food for me. I ordered the Kimchi-wa. With every bite, there was a different taste and texture. The cucumber juice that was house made was very refreshing. Overall a get dining experience.

Who doesn't like going to a fun marketplace with a sensory overload of food, produce, and other miscellaneous items whenever they visit a new city?

While it may be on the smaller side of marketplaces in the U,S,, Reading (pronounced "redding") Terminal Market does not disappoint with its variety of good food (you should try a roast pork or brisket sandwich at Tommy DiNic's).

Note that it's just a 5-minute walk from city hall!

Wow! Never seen such a stunning place! Its awesome and breathtaking! Im a tourist coming up from Germany and I never saw something like that in Europe...  we are saying  "Da bleiben keine Wünsche offen!"

This is one of those places where you learn of it's existence and feel robbed that you missed out beforehand.

Sure, some of the items are trucked in "Dole" boxes of produce and others might be things you may find at the local grocery store but there are gems in this place that make the drive worth it every time.

My personal favorite: The Amish pretzels that you will never have anywhere else.  Perfect buttery delicious pretzels surrounding homecrafted sausage or ham and homemade american cheese.  Yes, the combination is about the best thing on earth and I promise you, nothing else you will find comes close.  I'd drive an hour and a half for one of those.

There are alot of places that I don't ever recall by name like the place that has deep fried scallops and fries, many fresh squeezed orange juice vendors, preserves, produce, meats etc.  

This is a real gem, you owe it to yourself to check it out.  I'll be visiting this weekend in fact!
Awesome paneer kathi rolls, biryani and chaas...staff was friendly and service was quick. Loved our first visit and will definitely go again.

I would be okay being imprisoned in this place.

Between Dinic's sandwiches and Beiler's hand-rolled doughnuts . . . WOW!

The food options here are incredible.  Thai, deli, bakery, produce, Mexican, Italian, sushi, sweets, produce . . . 

A MUST-VISIT for anybody's Philly itinerary.

Fantastic experience!  I think I visited the Terminal Market every day I was at the Pennsylvania Convention Center (which is adjacent). There are a wide variety of food purveyors and great people watching. 

The only drawback was that several of the shops, particularly those with Amish operators, kept odd hours.

Wife and I visited Philly from NYC.  Found MK to have really flavorful, delicious, authentic Indian food conveniently wrapped to have there or on the go.  Platters were delish too.  Also, found it reasonably priced, especially considering healthy, fresh ingredients.  Service was good too.  Ate there 3 times during a week stay. Highly recommend.

You could lose your mind here (and your waistline) plowing through the variety of great food -- from ribs to peanut butter to cookies to huge prawns.  Only tried the cinnamon oatmeal cookies at 4th street cookie company which were yummy.  Fun place to walk through on the way to Independence Hall.

I was just saying the other day: why is there no Indian fast food? Turns out there is, just not where I was looking. Great taste, incredibly fast. If this were located near my home or workplace, I'd eat here at least weekly. Super friendly staff too.

I had to leave and take a break after about an hour... it was sensory overload. So many delicious smells and sights and flavors! When I came back, I was a bit better acclimated. It's not as large or as expansive as the Mercato Centrale in Florence, but it's pretty big!
One of the mainstays there is DiNic's, which makes a revered roast pork sandwich comprised of three ingredients: Roast pork, sharp provolone and broccoli rabe. The cheese provides a tanginess and prevents the pork juice from soaking through the roll; the pork is slow-roasted and delicious, while the broccoli rabe provides some crunch and offsets the sweetness of the pork. Justifiably loved by many.
The many Amish stores there are also worth checking out; there's a fresh-made doughnut shop that's excellent and a country-style diner that serves breakfast fit for powering field hands.
I had a great time there and would urge anyone to spend time there, especially on your first trip to Philly.
Huge selection of ethnic foods all over the place ; shopping stands ; mini farmers markets selling fresh produce for really cheap! Love this place because you can wander around it for hours.

Reading Terminal Market is one of the best establishments of its kind left in the country. Sadly, markets are becoming more and more rare, as people tend to do more shopping at megastores and eat crappy prepared food in food courts or strip malls.

This market has an excellent array of food stalls, pantry items, and fresh produce. In my opinion, the best establishments in the market are Iovine's produce market, The Head Nut (which has bulk food, spices, coffee, etc), John Yi Fish Market, and Beiler's Hand Rolled Doughnuts. These business are exceptional and some of the best of their kind in the city.

In addition to those listed above, there's a smattering of other very good food stalls. Some places are definitely overpriced, and others are just not very good at all.

But, there's something for every taste here, and it is definitely an experience to go. If you're only in Philadelphia for a day, it's worth it to go to Reading Terminal Market so you can have the experience once. 

I am lucky enough to live just under a 20 minute walk away, so I try to make a trip once every 10-14 days to stock up on certain food items for my pantry/kitchen since it has some of the best produce (at Iovine's) and fish (at John Yi's) in particular.
