Sure, it's not like some of the bigger and better markets if you compare it to other cities in the world. But, guess what? Philadelphia isn't Tokyo or Dehli or Mexico City or any of those places with better market situations. Considering the plight of the America market, Reading Terminal market is certainly one of the best in this region of the United States.
Think Pike's Market but replace the coffee and flying salmon with Amish donuts and Italian sandwiches.  It is massive and worth visiting on a lazy weekend afternoon.  Bring your appetite.
I noticed right away how clean this place was!! We had the most flavoral wraps full of Indian food that I love. Open till 3:30AM too, which is awesome.

Very busy Saturday pearls oyster bar  great waffle and of corse oysters ! What a combo fun place to go you can get almost any food you can think of including of course Philadelphia cheesesteaks walk around and just get the feeling of old Philadelphia where at one time this was really the place to buy your produce and meats

Well, duh.  Reading Terminal is great.  Dutch Eating Place should just serve breakfast 24/7 -- you can tell when it's not breakfast time, they empty out.

The ribs place is great.  Iovine's has good prices on some produce.  And it's all in a tiny area -- what is there not to love?
Great late-night stop. Flavors are great. i got the Masala Chicken roll. Staff is very nice and attentive. Restroom and environment is clean.
If you are looking an awesome food experience, this is a must visit when you are in Philly!  Once you go, you will want to return again and again.

This place is awesome!!! History, Good Food, great people watching and an amazing cross section of Philly.  
The Reading Terminal Market has been my market for the last 10 years-  we moved into the neighborhood ten years ago and I was thrilled to find a world class market two blocks away.  We always got to Iovine for our produce and Giuntas for our Meats- John Yi is the only place we will buy seafood.
The Amish Corner has amazing deli, candy, bakery, pickles and dairy-  Go to the Dutch Eating place for Breakfast-  it is worth the wait! 
Get there early on the weekends otherwise you will have to wade through a sea of tourists and avoid the market between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM during the week.

Really affordable and delicious food. My husband had the Hand-rolled Pappardelle which was by far the most delicious thing we had all night. Highly recommended. My only complaint is the seat we had outside was a little smelly with the sewer being so close. Not enough to ruin the meal - but if you sit outside ask for a seat on Reed.

A true gem and a must-see stop for anyone lucky enough to be in Philadelphia. What a genius move to have this place next door to the Convention Center. I cannot say enough good things about the convenience of going to ONE stop and having food options for days. The delis and Mennonite restaurants are the real winners here, but just don't go on Sundays when all the Mennonite/Amish businesses are closed.
The Amish have the best wings ever! Craft beer is great too!

I could get lost in a place like this and never come out. Sensory overload is almost impossible not to experience, since you're bombarded with foodstuffs from all angles. 

Bonus: penny smashing machine!

Came here with my boyfriend for a bite to eat before a show at the Academy. I've had Indian food plenty of times, but never Kati rolls. Very happy we tried this place! It was clean and the staff was very friendly and helpful. Food was awesome. I got a chicken tikka roll and a paneer masala roll. Both were fantastic. Packed with tons of flavor and very filling. I probably could have just had one and been satisfied. The guy behind the counter recommended we try the sauces they had available, and explained what they were (a yogurt based sauce similar to raita, and a very spicy Indian hot sauce). I like when food proprietors are excited about and proud of the food they serve, and this guy clearly was. At his recommendation, I mixed some of the hot sauce into the raita and put it on the tikka roll - it was awesome. If you like spicy, definitely give the hot sauce a try. The paneer was excellent, very moist and nice, big chunks. My only regrets are that I didn't add egg to the roll and that I don't live closer to center city! If you live in the area or find yourself down that way, definitely give this place a try. You won't be disappointed!

They make their own nutella syrup here folks. HELLO? Bomb. I go there everyday during my lunch break, and they know my drink. No fuss. La Colombe coffee and cool staff, but not like the whole hipster thing, just nice, nice people. Smoothies, food, baked food excellent and they have gluten-free stuff for those of you who partake.  I am not a big studier with Wifi (never, at all, not in my stage of my career) so if you are concerned, I just don't know. Ambience is not a concern for me, but it's modern, clean but groovy. Suits my needs, good peeps and products, and 5 stars all the way if you are in the the drexel/west philly/near the bridge area

Felt like Grand Central Market in LA, but WAY BETTER.

Lots of selection for food, meats and bakeries!

Every place I checked out was reasonably priced, it was difficult to choose a place to grub from. Most definitely check out Bielers for donuts..99 cents is all you need to know. The line was quite long but it moved quick!

Some of the places close in mid-afternoon so be sure to double check if you want to visit. There's Amish people. So cool. Never seen them before. 

I wanted to ask so many questions..I wonder if they will ever read this review?

This is a "do not miss" attraction in Philadelphia. Particularly if you are in the Convention Center as you are right next to it. So many wonderful cuisines, fresh produce/meats, kitchen specialty items, and unusal spices all local. The Amish are there through Saturday, not on Sunday. Their baked goods are too die for. I have gotten hard to find spices from The Head Nut, special cuts of meat from the butchers, fresh flowers and the best chocolate chip cookies you can find. Great prices too. I live close so I am able to shop periodically, lucky me!

Lines, long lines, nothing but lines. Keep in mind this was a Sunday afternoon. Every place we tried to eat...there was a line. The worst part was that it appeared the eatery employees did not seem motivated, at all, to try to move the people. They moved at a snail's pace and the line just kep on growing. Maybe they thought it was cool to have a crowd in front of their establishment.

I went to Industry on a weekend night and it was packed, but somehow our group was able to get table service. The layout was a standing bar area and tables. The open warehouse feel was attractive to look at. They food and drink menu was diverse and interesting. The people at my table seemed to be enjoying themselves.

The drawbacks I noticed on a busy night was the noise. It seemed impossible to have a normal conversation at the table and shouting didn't seem to help. My ears rang with the din. Another issue was the bathroom, situated in a corner of the room. It was hard to fight through the bar crowd to get there and there only seemed to be one stall.

Industry is an incredibly attractive place and can see why it draws a crowd. I would definitely go back, but may choose a weeknight next time.
So many choices for breakfast, lunch, dinner, dessert and even groceries, gifts and essential oils. My only gripe is the cost of parking but there's nothing to be done about that lol

Definitely need to come here if you are visiting Philly! It can be a little overwhelming, so if you're coming for lunch make sure you have an idea of what you want or you will be walking around for awhile.  I come here a lot to get groceries, really cheap produce.

Wide variety of cuisines to select from the numerous stores here. Its really what you call the melting pot of food in Philly. From amazing ice creams at Bassets to the amazing rib sandwiches at Rib Stand and the yummy kebob roles at Kamal's..this place has it all.

I recently hosted my sister's baby shower at Satis Bistro.  It was an adorable venue, with delicious food and marvelous service!  The waiters were so kind, and even assisted with carrying the gifts from my car to the restaurant and back again.  I would host another event here if I lived in Jersey City.
Love this place. Employees treat you with respect and have a sense of urgency. Great for fast food. Wish the lines could be shorter!

This place is overwhelming. There are too many good choices! Not that it's a bad thing but WOW. Lol. Food was amazing though. Ended up sharing w/ my daughter because she couldn't finish her food. Fried rice was firrreeeeeeee.

Great appetizers - Mac and cheese (balls), beignets and pig ears were really good. 

Burger (single patty) was disappointing. Nothing special. 

Dessert (s'mores) was really bad. Cold.

Also, service was VVVVEEERRRRYYY SSSSSLLLLOOOWWW considering it wasn't that busy. Our server seemed to take forever with everything except the bill
Love the reading terminal market! Can't get away from the Reubens!

This is the hottest spot in Center City to visit.  You must try 2-3 of the sandwich places, the best is Dinic's, with a great roasted pork.  From one end to the other they have everything that Philadelphia is famous for.  Be prepared for lines and massive crowds.

Love, love, love this place!!!  Highly recommend it for everything between a quick shopping experience to grabbing a cup of Joe, flowers, ice cream, candies, fresh juice to a hearty breakfast, lunch or dinner. I would go here everyday if I lived in Philly.

Holy crap, I live a short train ride away, and I can't believe I waited 29 years before coming here!  This place is pretty much a binge eater's paradise.  There is an absurd variety of food here; I cannot think of a type of food they don't have. My stomach could only fit so much, but the pork sandwich, General Tso chicken, vegetable lo mein, and soft pretzel I had here were top-notch. (And while my heart and taste buds would have loved to finish off with ice cream, my brain said don't even think about it!) It probably wouldn't have been a good mix anyway :)    Well, my visit here was during the week between Christmas & New Years, so I'll keep telling myself that the crowds aren't normally that bad....right???   Anyway, this is definitely a go-to place in center city.  For the variety, prices, and extreme degree of yumminess - the RTM cannot be beat!

Good selection on snacks, drinks, goodies, and last minute items if you're on the run. Expect to pay more than you usually would, but that's the price of convenience. The actual store area is clean and fresh appearing so that's a plus

it becomes a crush that feels claustrophobic at times: try to go to this great place when it's not the rush hour - you will find it difficult to get seating there. Perhaps take out the food. The Dutch Eating Place is go to.

I have no words. This place is beyond wonderful. If you are in Philly- do not miss this gem. A few personal faves: alligator sausage and chix&corn soup from Cajun place. ALL the pretzels from Millers pretzels. Kale salad from tootsie something.  And if the fish market has fresh soft shell crab- EAT IT!!!

I think this place is overrated.  There are a ton of places to get food but I think the seating situation is terrible.  Outside of a few places I have really been let down on the food I've gotten here.

granted, I visited a little after 9 am on a Friday, but a lot of the stalls were closed :(

somehow, i imagined this place to be bigger. pike place in seattle seems to have a ton more vendors. this place looked just like a mall food court. 

my friend wanted to try a cheese-steak, but the one we got here was not good. the gator gumbo at Beck's Cajun Cafe was good, but the po-boys were 90% bread (cold, and stale).

I can't in my right mind give this spot any less than a perfect score. You've got everything from Dinic's Roast Pork sandwiches to Hershel's Deli (both five star establishments on their own) in the same spot. 
Beiler's Donuts are worth the hype, and the Soul Food place I tried had really great comfort food. 
If you're in philly for a limited amount of time I honestly feel like visiting this market is an absolute must
Best place for food in Philadelphia!   Whatever u want it's here.  Always get gluten free things to take to wife when here

I love RTM!! I love that there are so many choices and that there are plentiful seating areas. But if you plan on going during lunch hours, be prepared to have a crowded experience and some difficulty finding seats. But really, I think that is a testament to how great RTM is!

Love the many vendors and types of food available...prepared and raw...seafood, port, red meat, etc...baked goods, drinks from Lancaster...and the ethnic jewelry vendors as well as the fresh produce and too many others to tell.  Never disappointed nor food that was not optimally fresh.  You will not regret purchases from her for a meal at your leisure  and home...Enjoy!  I certainly do...and travel regularly from NJ to patronize.  I was so excited 2 days before Christmas to be able to purchase some smoked turkey for my collard greens as all market and meat stores in Jersey were sold out!  Reading terminal meat vendor came through with flying colors!!!!  No regrets...ever!

If you like farmer markets.......on acid...this is the place!  A diverse array of food and items to purchase at a decent price!  A lot of diverse people frequent this place and the variety of food is mind blowing!  I highly recommend the experience.  Be aware that it closes early during the week.  The lunch crowd can be overwhelming but the people navigate the hustle and bustle pretty well.  Of course being in an urban environment, you get the occasional crazy look but nonetheless, it's worth experiencing.

Reading Terminal is awesome. I go on average twice a week for veggies and fresh fruits for smoothies. Right around the corner from Iovinne Brothers is the cheese place where the guys are extremely helpful and informative. They turned me on to Labne kefir cheese, which is now a favorite.

Was only here for a weekend but came twice. There are a lot of food options here and a couple little shops. Similar to Chelsea market in nyc except all the stores are open layout. We bought some cake from the Terminal Brothers, and wanted to get donuts from Buellers(?) but were stuffed and they were closed on Sunday because they're amish. There are significant lines at Dinic's and the ice cream shop but we managed to get a seat at the bar for some sandwiches. There's also a cute stand for natural honey and bees wax candles which makes for good souvenirs!

Has absolutely every type of food you would be in the mood for! Ate at George's and it was delicious! Best cheesesteak I've had! They were very accommodating since I am gluten intolerant - very very crowded on a Saturday, but totally worth it!

Ive only been here once. The one time I went it was a seriously phenomenal visit. The donuts were amazing and literally melted in my mouth alone with this fresh bread with cream infused in it. I am going back again this week for lunch, super excited!

There is something for everyone. The atmosphere is a bit from crowded but for a big city that's a bit slower in pace, I think Reading gives the affect some tourists are looking for. Lots of dessert options too. If you're there for brunch (and not on a sunday) go to the Dutch Eating Place and get a hot apple dumpling with heavy cream. You won't regret it!

Took a weekend trip to Philly and decided that this was a good decision for lunch. The weather didn't hold out for us so being inside was nice. Due to the cold rain, it was tough to find a spot to sit and eat but the selection is unbelievable!

We walked the entire market and then made decisions on what to eat. Grab a map at the little kiosk or do what I did and print a pamphlet ahead of time from the website. It was very helpful.

We can't wait to go back and try more another weekend!
Love this place, I buy all my vegetables here. They have great food with good price as well. I only wish they would close later in the evenings.

We arrived on Sunday afternoon as the vendors were closing. We were able to purchase some fresh fruits and veggies. My biggest regret is not bringing any cash (most of the vendors only accept cash). We will be going back to Philly in a few weeks, so I'll update this review then.

Love this place! So many food options. One of my favourites is Dutch Eating Place for breakfast - you'll want to get there for 8am otherwise you'll be waiting in line. The whole place gets really busy around peak hours but there's something for everyone. There's limited seating - it's more set up for takeout or grabbing a quick bite to eat
I just love market for its vibe!

A MUST during a day trip to downtown Philly!  The Reading Terminal Market has a cornucopia of dining options from Italian to 50's style diner to mediterranean to Japanese to gourmet cheeses and candies.  My personal favorite is the falafel but I am not exactly sure of the name of the stand where I got it from.  The market has a couple small shops but I never had enough time to explore them.  If you're a Philly area resident like me and have out-of-town guests visiting from far away (try California, where I am from originally and have many relatives who still reside there), make it a point to bring them here!

Very very busy and claustrophobic but if you can get past that this is one of the best farmer's markets in the Philadelphia/Greater Philadelphia area! They literally offer every shop of every kind under the sun (vegan cakes, meat, cheese, burgers, gourmet chocolate, etc). Definitely check it out if you're ever in the area!

Are you kidding me? Does the Reading Terminal need any reviews? Or are you here for the recommendations? That's the only reason why you should be looking up reviews for the Reading Terminal.

Bomb dot com. I haven't tried everything in the market, and that would be a pretty ambitious goal, but I've tried enough things to say this is one of my favorite things about Philly. Food so good, you'll end up going back to the same place over and over and over and just delay achieving your goal to try everything.

At least that is what is happening to me.

DiNic's is a must. Be sure to add either broccoli rabe or spniach AND the sharp provolone! Boy, is it SHARP!

And then Bassett's for dessert. If you're there on any day, but Sunday, don't forget to check out the Dutch Corner!!! Because you will crave it on Sundays when it's closed!

Possibly the worst food I've ever eaten in my life. Totally deserves negative 1 stars. 

I decided on this place because it looked like the healthiest option in the terminal. I ordered a grilled chicken & avocado panini, a blueberry muffin & a water, and the water was the only thing I could stomach. 

I waited quite a while for my food & then had to rush to my gate, so it was only after I settled into my seat that I started to smell the food. It didn't exactly smell like food at all. I've never really smelled that odor before. I think it might be what yoga mats smell like when they're on fire. Anyway, I had to check that the odor was coming from the food bag, because it seemed so toxic. Yes, it was the food.

But the thing is, I was hungry & I'd just spent $15 on all of this & was hunkering down for a transcontinental flight. I decided to take a look: gray avocado, chicken covered by a layer of clear slime, one piece of limp iceberg lettuce on a roll. I cleared off the avocado & tried a tiny bite. I've never tasted, or perhaps untasted chicken like that before. It had no flavor, and practically no texture, and was definitely coated in un-identifiable slime... Not to mention the bread was now soggy with said slime and the chemical smell.

I quickly wrapped the sandwich back up & called the flight attendant to take it away. The smell was starting to make me sick & I couldn't wait for her to come by later in the flight with the trash bag.

I wasn't too upset, because I still had a giant blueberry muffin, and how can you go wrong with a muffin?? By making it tasteless! I suppose it's remarkable how they managed to get nearly no discernible taste into a baked good like that. Only the "blueberries" tasted vaguely sweet, but certainly not tart or any taste that someone blindfolded might determine as blueberry. Considering the large mass of carbs & gluten in my hand that tasted like spongy air, I wrapped the muffin up & put it aside too.

20 minutes later I had an Alaska Airlines Reuben sandwich in my hands. $6 and vastly superior. Tasty! No hint of chemical toxicity! Texture! 

I will never,ever go to this place again. They make airline food seem like Morimoto.
So many choices. So many people. So few tables. I love the vibe and atmosphere of this market. I am not a fan of busier days when people are hovering above you to snag your table. Eh well.

There is so much in this market and everyday my wife and I walked through it we noticed  something new. 

If you are there for the Apple Dumplings make sure you don't go on Sunday as the Dutch side of the market is not open on Sunday's. 

I tried Tommy Dicnic's and I must say it was a great sandwich. We got there for lunch and the beef brisket was not in stock. I must say, do a little research on how to order your sandwich. This helped us be able to order quickly and feel comfortable about what we ordered.

The pork sandwich, wet, with broccoli rabi and cheese was a HIT! It was large enough for two of us to split it as a snack. We decided to try multiple things around the market.... Don't let the long lines scare you..

DICNIC'S TIP: If you find a seat at Dicnic's sit down and you won't have to wait in line!!!!

Overall, there is so much in this market it is hard to explore in one day. Take an appetite and try a little bit of everything! You won't be upset!

Simply just one of the best places to go in any city anywhere.  Delis, restaurants, book stores, ice cream, bakeries, butchers, fish  monger, sandwich shops, diners, produce, Amish merchants; all in one place...and all of them great.  Whatever you need, you will find.  The worst part of the Terminal is that there are too many choices and great options.

Every trip to Philly requires a trip to the Terminal Market. There are so many delights, it's a food lovers paradise. Some of my favorites:

M-F, 4-6pm $1 oysters
Ice Cream
The Fair Farm Stand in the corner has the most awesome cheese counter
The Amish breakfast sandwich place

The cheese counter is my absolute favorite... All the cheeses are from local farms in Pennsylvania and a few in New Jersey. My favorite one from the most recent visit was an ash-covered soft goat cheese that was creamy and a little sour.

There's more lunch choices than a week business trip or a vacation can exhaust. I still have to try some beef jerky and cannoli's. Not to mention the cajun food and Philly cheesesteaks.
Awesome place for special treats that you won't find around town in addition to favorite Philadelphia fare

Crazy good sandwiches (I love me some smoked turkey with swiss!) but as far as the atmosphere goes...not so much.

Getting there is a little loopy - you have to walk around the building, down the outside stairs and next to busy, busy City Ave. I was there for lunch and there was an acoustic performance going on, which is cool for sure but just not at lunch. It was so loud (with said music as well as the hustle, bustle and chaos of the noontime crowd) that the people behind the counter couldn't hear me & I couldn't hear them. After repeating my order about 5 times the sandwich was made to order (pretty quickly, too, I might add) but instead of hanging out there as planned I paid, threw it in my purse and scooted out of there for the quiet respite of my car. I'll try again for sure, but I hope they save the musical performances for a later time slot.

A little on the expensive side but so worth it! I come here for lunch and they are friendly, quick and use quality ingredients. I wish there were more places like them! Also they are open super late for night owls like myself :)

2.5 Stars.

These reviews are probably written by tourists or out-of-towners, but here is the inside scoop from a local:

It's overcrowded and thrives on its history. Does it have the best food? No. Does it have the best grocery market? No. Does it have the best bar? No. It's all mediocre, at best.

Locals go to local farmers markets that are full of local farms. Check out the Food Trust for a listing of when and where! Google 'Food Trust Philadelphia'.

The meat places are hit or miss in the RTM. What irks me is some advertise grass fed, but the animals are grain finished. They're salespeople. Snakes in the grass.

The seafood markets, well, again, look what you're buying. Most of the time the fish is dry looking and fishy smelling. No bueno.

The bar is meh. Philly has too many great bars to deal with the crowds of RTM.

Ok, Beilers....well, they're a game changer, and the only reason I visit. They have the best baked goods. Period. 

Dinics, too. They're also great.

So, there you have it. Go at your own risk!
Nice lil spot for an afternoon hangout, its kinda similar to Chelsea Market in NYC but much bigger and the food options are plenty..a must see when in Philly!

Good, hot, flavorful food that's budget friendly and made to order.   Had the chicken masala roll after late night out and was the only thing open in the area, but did not disappoint at all and well worth the visit anytime of the day.    They were really busy and good made to order so there is small wait.   Friendly service!

I don't know how fair this review will be considering I've only ever really ordered one thing at Potbellys, but I love that one thing so much that it's worth a review! The uptown salad is my go-to item on their menu. The apples, grapes, blue cheese, cranberries and candied walnuts (MAKE SURE YOU GET THESE), all with the chicken and balsamic dressing go so well together and make for the perfect lunch that hits the spot. The chicken enchilada soup is also super yummy, and their frozen drinks are always a treat, although I would say their fruit smoothies taste more like milkshakes. Overall fast and reliable in the middle of the work day!
This place is awesome!  So much choice!  It is the best food court I've ever been too.  So many fresh and delicious options.
If you're at the convention center or find yourself walking around the city, make sure you visit. Great food, drinks, dessert and lots of great specialty shops.

So much to see and eat in here!! I wish it was open late and did not close at 5. Beliers doughnuts are a must. The line gets long but its worth the wait. Carmen's has the best cheesesteaks. We even tried a Chinese place the was good. They also have cookies, fudge, juices, gifts, soaps, and lots more.

Great place to dine out for various foods, desserts, etc...You can't go wrong coming here. The place is always packed, but still cooler inside then the hot asphalt. There are tables outside, but it's hot and smells like urine.

If you are hungry after a late night with friends this is probably your spot.  If you are one of those staunch supporters of what I believe their rival is which is Spice End go try Masala Kitchen for yourself and compare! The dishes have more flavor and will definitely hit the spot after a night out in the town. Just dont expect fine dining here.  It is what it is. Kati rolls and their MK chixken and rice are go to dishes.

The industry is always just okay for me. I always want to love it more and make it my local go to bar however I am just bored most times I am there. 

Food is okay. Def worth trying but nothing spectacular. Except the fried green tomatoes which are awesome. For a place located in south philly in a very animal friendly neighborhood I am surprised they do not have any vegan dishes at all. Even for brunch. This for many years kept me from going there on a regular basis. 

Beer selection is usually good. I don't feel like it has ever been easy to score more than one maybe two seats at the bar so this is not the place for a group to hang out. 

I think if I actually worked in the industry which many I know do I would love this place more. It definitely serves its purpose and is good but nothing more than that for me.

For what it's worth, you can get absolutely delicious home-made style food from a variety of different vendors. 

I will say, I wish I would have known that some of the most renowned shops are closed on Sunday as per their religious tradition. If they kept open availability, I would probably give this 5 stars.

Everything here is amazing.  But do yourselves a favor, skip the line at DiNic's and go to Border Springs Farm.  Get the lamb shoulder sandwich (although everything is amazing).  Feel free to send me a thank you afterwards :)

Amish breakfast was very tasty they run a counter service.  Around the corner from the Amish place you can find Very good creamy ice cream.  Not quite the same as I remember, but it is worth a trip if in the area.

Came by for dinner for the first time last Friday night. Everything turned out well except for my entree. I ordered the pasta, which tasted house made but didn't seem like the cook actually stirred the pasta once hitting the water. The pasta came clumped together and crunchy in parts that weren't separated during cooking. The porcini mushroom sauce was absolutely bland. The braised veal was also bland but cooked well. 

Honestly I was just disappointed with how a simple dished turned out so wrong. It's a shame since you can pretty much go anywhere in philly to get a similar drink based on their cocktail menu, but good food would had continued to bring me back.

Upscale hoagie chain with decent soups, cookies, and shakes. Potbelly is definitely better than Quizno's or Subway, but its not the world's greatest hoagie. Try a "Wreck on wheat," and be sure to get a cup of chili loaded. The employees at this location do a great job.

I truly loved this place so much! I've been to many major cities that have markets like this, and I have got to say that the variety of stalls at this place was amazing! Everything from ice cream stores to flower shops to little trinkets...definitely a must visit, especially if it is your first time in Philly like it was mine! 

I would personally suggest to make a lap around the place maybe once or even twice (I did twice) only because there is so much to choose from and you can't obviously eat so much. 

I started with Bassett's which by the way is so amazing! The salted caramel swirl is an absolute must, I paired it with a mint chocolate chip. 

Then I went to Wan's seafood for some amazing friend seafood! The scallops were 85 cents a piece and the jumbo shrimp was $2.75. 

The ambiance was that of a typical market. Very loud and a lot going on. I wouldn't suggest coming here with a lot of little kids, especially if you are afraid of losing them because this place can get pretty crowded! 

Only quirk about this place is that seating is incredibly hard to find, so don't bank on it! But for a place this great I'm not surprised!

Oh good, another bar without Guinness.

Industry is another ultra-hip pub, which has paid a great deal of attention to the light bulbs, and thank God for that. On a blustery November afternoon, I want to make sure that my local pub has the very best lighting options. Some people may disagree, and say that having a nice pint of Guinness and a shepherd's pie might be just the ticket. I'm so glad 'The Industry' resisted the urge give people a familiar pint & bite, opting instead for bone marrow & chocolate stouts. Got sarcasm?

My friend and I decided to try 'The Industry' this week, as we were both open to the idea of trying a new watering hole. As we walked in after work, we took seats at the bar, and were the first patrons of the day.  We waited more than 15 minutes before anyone from the staff decided to acknowledge our presence, but at least they had shirts with snappy saying on them! I asked for a Guinness, which they did not have, nor did they have anything comparable. Okay...how about a lager or a pilsner which isn't cloyingly hoppy? Bar owners...You Need a couple Fastballs!!!! Be hip...be boutiquey...be artistic, but do put at least two staples on the chalkboard. I don't want a stout which tastes like coffee or chocolate; I want it to taste like beer. I don't want need 4 I.P.A's competing for the 'most hops award'  available to me; a good lager would be fine. Also, I am rarely am overcome with the urge to have a pint & bone marrow, or a pint & sweetbreads, or a pint & tartare...seriously? Come on gents. 

I get what 'The Industry' is trying to do, and to an extent, I like when people (including my own) have their palate pushed. That experience, however, is usually reserved for fine dining, not pub fare. This place is definitely a pub...with TV's...in south Philly.  A more honest look at who they are, and how their identity actually functions seem in order. I'll keep an eye out for any changes, as a like to support local business, but I'm in no hurry to get back.

I am writing this review of Slack's Hoagie Shack in the Shoprite Shopping Center on Ark Road in Mt. Laurel.

I have not eaten a hoagie in YEARS.  On an impulse, I decided to stop in today.  What a reward!  I got a "Godfather" hoagie.  Prosciutto, capicola, salami.  The meat was thinly sliced, rich, and tasty.  The bread was fresh and chewy and the seeds on the roll added to nicely to the taste!  I loved this sandwhich.  Every calorie was well worth it!

Definitely letting everyone know. In for SI/EI LOF. Oil was left dripping all over the place, the oil cap was missing. As usual the tires were NOT rotated. They even went as far as NOT to fill out the inspection stickers. Awesome job on my brand new truck. Really living up-to there reputation. Way to go guys!

No idea how this place isn't getting 5 stars across the board. The Ghost of Mary. I mean come on. It's amazing. God damn I  am craving one right now. Or 3. 

The Hillbilly Philly is what I would request for my final meal if I were on death row. Not kidding.

Everything I've had here - Sandwiches, breakfast food, cocktails, cornbread - has been spot fucking on. Don't ever change, Industry. And I'm so happy you're near my house.

Amish people, fresh baked goods, fresh seafood, fresh veggies, variety of different cultures and cuisines, pickles and beef jerky for days. This place has everything and is so unique from anything we have down here in Texas including Amish people, yes. I come here and I don't even know what to eat or what to pick up. Homemade pickles and jerky from the Amish is a must. I go to those two places first. Then I'm craving Indian food, Thai Food, Chinese Food, Soul Food, Mediterranean food. So I end up walking around for half an hour, making a round through the entire market TWICE and still can't figure out what to eat.  

A lot of places is cash only but there are ATM machines scattered throughout the market. I usually just take the subway here and walk to avoid parking because parking in the city? Forget about it. Don't do it, don't even think about it. Just don't.

The food was pretty good!

We ordered through UberEats and it was a quick delivery! We ordered a lamb and chicken platter and a paneer tikka roll. The portions were generous and filling! 

I ate the paneer tikka roll. Onions and chutney are also included in the roll (and you can opt for other veggies to be added into the make up) and it's a savory mixture when paired with the well seasoned paneer. The restaurant provides a few packets of their hot sauce in case you want to amp up the spice factor! 

Enjoyed the food and the service. Will return for a dine in experience!

Unbelievable experience . So much going on from doughnuts being made right in front of you to chocolate covered every thing.The largest non commercialized Food Court.
/ farmers market / seafood / poultry / Beef / Sausages. You name it..

Amazing Kati rolls... !! 
We tried the Achari paneer, paneer masala and paneer tikka along with Mango lassi. The best of the lot was Achari paneer..
Quick service and courteous staff..

this place is AWESOME.  it is a must-see for those traveling through Philly.  i've only been once, so i was only able to try food from 2 places, but they were both EXCELLENT.  and everything is so cheap!  it is crowded, but it's tolerable and the crowd/commotion kind of adds to the aura and excitement.  i can't wait to come back here and try more food!

i found a guy who was selling sandwiches that were knock offs of rutgers grease trucks.  apparently, after talking with the guy, he told me that his brother used to own one of the grease trucks over 10 years ago and that i was only the second person who ever came through the market knowing about grease trucks.  i was shocked to hear about this random connection to drunk college memories as well as the fact that i was only the second person who put 2 and 2 together.  i got a "fat korean" which consists of fried fish fillet, korean beef BBQ (bulgogi), cheese, lettuce, tomato, french fries, mayo, ketchup and sriracha all squeezed onto a hero.  it's the kind of sandwich that punches you in the gut when you're done, but you still want more, if only it could fit.  i'd take one of these over a cheese steak at pat's or gino's any day.

Reading Terminal is a staple for anyone visiting Philly or for any indecisive group that wants to eat well. There are so many options, from seafood, to soulfood, to desserts (don't miss the Bassett's Ice Cream- Cinnamon is my favorite!)

I would recommend taking a few hours just to check everything out. Try to get smaller things that way you can try items from a few vendors. I do recommend Delilah's Soul Food!
Awesome market! You can get many different types of authentic ethnic food from many of the best restaurants in the city. Must check this place out!

Just an awesome place. Definitely recommend this place when you come to Philly. Place closes at 6pm so get there early. Lots of sweets, fresh meat, great spot for lunch and drinks. The terminal itself is a great part of history.

Needing to grab some equipment from the nearby Comcast office, my companion and I chose the Industry as the location for a recent, Saturday morning brunch. The decor and ambiance upon entering seemed promising, as the dark woods, relaxed vibe, and high-ish ceilings suggested a great place to grab a bite and a drink. Though we weren't drinking, the tap list had some unique picks and the cocktails seemed well-thought out. 

Unfortunately, the food failed to meet expectations. It came out fairly promptly, which is always welcome when running errands. My shrimp and grits were just fine, though rather boring. Nothing really elevated the Industry's version of this brunch staple above any other of the city's renditions, so it failed to leave an impact. Similarly, the vegetable scramble was simply average. We appreciated the seasonality of the vegetables included (winter squashes and root veggies), but the dish needed something interesting to enliven the palette. Breakfast potatoes had a nice crunch but lacked seasoning. As a devout believer in the power of biscuits, I was disappointed by the Industry's' dry, bland cheddar ones.

Perhaps sticking to the more indulgent "hangover helpers" on another visit will yield superior results. Still, unless I'm in the neighborhood I see no reason to return to the Industry for brunch. The food did not impress (though certainly, with the exception of the biscuit, did not offend) enough to warrant a dedicated brunch voyage to Pennsport from elsewhere. For a drink, however, I look forward to checking this spot out and enjoying the vibe.

A must-have on any eating tour of Philly.  Get the pork sandwiches from DiNic's, they are some of the best in the city.

And get some cookies at Termini bakery- or even better- GET A CANNOLI.

Or, if you aren't obsessed with Italian food, sit at the counter at Pearls and have some seafood while you people-watch.

Staff is incredibly friendly, they bussed my table when I finished eating, and offered to get me a refill. Girls at the registers seem to have fun at their job, overall seems like a very well run establishment. I usually just run through the drive through, but I'm gonna have to stop in more often.

I love love love the RTM. Italian Hoagie from Salumeria. Boneless Rib Sandwich from the Rib Stand. Cookies from Hope's. Grilled Salmon from Little Thai Market. Sang Kee, The Original Turkey... omg the list goes on.  Working across the street I was there all the time! I was so spoiled with food. And now I have a new job in the middle of nowhere. Sigh...

I live on the same block as the restaurant and really like it quite a bit. They use good quality ingredients, change the menu to offer seasonal specials, and have very interesting and delicious cocktails. The short rib entree (when available) and sandwich are amazing, as well as the kimchee tater tots, wild boar ragu (mmmm!!), and my husband loves their burgers. I was a little disappointed in the Fois Gras PBJ and the Mac & Cheese Balls -- just not very tasty. The seafood BLT when made with fried oysters had a humongous piece of thick fresh bread, but 4 oysters so small I could barely see them, and the bacon & tomato were disproportionate to the size of the bread. They have a cocktail which I love and have never seen on any other menu - a Ghost Mary, made with tomato water instead of juice. So it's clear and very light. It's one of the best drinks I've ever had. I appreciate that they are clean and good neighbors, and while the service is always good in the restaurant, the staff is not always very friendly when you walk past and say hello. The atmosphere is good for dining in the restaurant but they also have super-speedy pick-up, which is great for those nights with no time to cook. I definitely recommend and will keep going back.

A veritable moving feast for the senses, and in my humble opinion, the best public market in the country.  All of the stalls feature something unique and delicious.  The Amish contingent are a wonderful part of the market, they have a few amazing shops and are always friendly and helpful.  The butchers are all great, and you can't beat the produce prices/quality.  Nothing needs to be said regarding the superlative D'Nics, which is one of a slew of great eateries within the market.  The four dollar parking garage is another great feature as well.
Our new neighborhood bar. Great drinks and food. Party of 5, sat outside until 10pm brought it inside and same great service ... plus a visit from Spider-Man. We will be back for sure!

Oh my God. Why can't DC have something like this?!?!? Reading Terminal Market is a must stop when you are in Philly. It has just about every type of food you can think of, all delicious and all at a very decent price. It tends to be crowded on the weekends (and now especially since Dinic's won "best sandwich in America"), but it's totally worth it. Every meal I've had here has been good. It convienently located right in the center of the touristy part of the city, so if you are visiting Philly YOU HAVE TO GO. There's also spices and breads and any food you can think of for sale besides the eating places. Every time I go to Philly, I make it a point to stop here. Best place in Philly, hands down.
If you don't get a roast pork sandwich at DeNic's, you're doing Philadelphia wrong.
There is such variety here that basically everyone can find something. Or you can get good ingredients n go home and make it. The produce is fresh. The shops are colorful and fun to look through

I got the chicken and lamb platter. Great meal, very filling and most likely leftovers!

With this place you know exactly what you're getting. I can't really handle spicy, so I got the mild because the medium was a bit too spicy for me last time. 

Excellent and quick service with very friendly staff!
i went to by georges for my first meal in philly! i was looking for a good vegetarian cheesesteak and this was the perfect place. so flavorful and totally delicious!

I like Popeye's.  This is more about the service that I got - they wanted to upcharge me because instead of consenting to getting liquid poison for my beverage (coke, pepsi, etc.) I asked for bottled water.  "I'll just have tap water, then."  I had to prompt the cashier for a bag and utensils as he seemed oblivious to the fact that I had a backpack, roller luggage, and things in my hand already.  

Pay attention.  I get that it's an airport, but great service gets you great reviews.  Mediocre service, especially on such a short interaction, gets mediocre reviews.

They have many different food places, where you can eat or snack. Check 
out the nice bakery that serves different kinds of very delicious bagels
 right next to the smoothie place, which isn't bad either.
Whenever I've been there usually in the morning during the week, I've also seen Amish-dressed people selling their goods. 
On
 the weekends around lunch time, it gets very crowded and you have to 
expect to wait in line for some minutes until you can make your order.

Came here about a week ago for lunch but I didn't eat inside. After leaving the drive thru and eating my food on the way back to work, I noticed that the chicken tenders I had received tasted a little gummy. Once I got somewhere I could stop, I opened up one of the chicken tenders and low and behold: they weren't all the way cooked! You could literally see the raw chicken. I didn't eat there like I stated in the beginning and my lunch break was coming to a close so I had no time to go back and complain. I really hope this never happens again because besides this incident, I never had a problem out of this location and it's convenient because I live in South Philly and it's close. I don't think I'll be returning for a little while though.

The choices are myriad.  My brother and I wandered down many aisles before I settled on an Indian restaurant and he decided to test the Cajun restaurant (we are both originally from Louisiana).  I found the chicken Marsala to be a bit bland.  As to be expected at a tourist place, I guess. The naan, however, was wonderful.  My brother said the red beans and rice were not Louisiana style but acceptable.  I missed out on Apple dumpling! I went back for that treat and found that the vendor had left for the day. It was around 4, so plan ahead.

Greasy. But the chicken is sooooooooo tender and good for that quick grab a bite that I can not help it! I order just the basic chicken sandwich for like $3 and some change. Nothing else cause of greaaassssseee. Lol. I am always disappointed when they are not open and I pull into it and then I realize..oh it is Sunday. It is interesting a place that sells chicken but not beef. Thats the first thing I thought when I first here. And a fast food that doesnt open Sundays was kind of odd also at first. Im always a drive through but when I did get a chance to go inside it was okay. cozy. Forget if they have wifi or not.

After hanging out downtown that morning, we decided to stop by the Reading Terminal for lunch.  We were there on a holiday weekend and there was also a Volleyball Tournament of some sorts going on at the Convention Center, so the lunch crowd was extremely chaotic.   It was rather challenging to keep up in a group of four where three of us had never experienced Reading Terminal before.  However, as expected, we lost each other a couple times while looking for a restaurant that didn't have a line completely wrapped around the corner.  This wasn't upsetting because this is a world famous spot.  I totally understood why it was so crowded.  Didn't upset me at all.  I found it rather exciting and adventurous.  I was also grateful they had street signs on the corners which helped us locate each other.  The maps were useful, too.

There were so many restaurants to choose from, but figuring out how to order your food while faced with crowds of people and ridiculous long lines was indeed a challenge.  Thankfully, everyone we encountered was quite friendly and the locals I spoke to were willing to explain the process.  No one seemed irritated by my questions.  I felt welcomed here.  

We fell right into place and found a restaurant that didn't have a long line that we could all agree upon.  We also walked around the entire facility and peeked at every shop.    
We were all very pleased with our meals from the Thai Food Market.  We look forward to returning and trying out foods from other restaurants.  

Notes:  Crowd control is a must!  Line indicators/markers/signage would help tremendously.  More seating for patrons to eat their food would also be helpful.

A must visit place when you are in Philly. A wonderful mixture of prepared food and fresh ingredients for those who want to pick up that special cheese, meat or even produce. 

Stop in here and have a cold beer while wandering through the spectacle.
Great for looking and snacking . Despite raves, lunch food is rather ordinary and uninspired with the exception of Sang Kee duck noodle stand.
Heard a lot about Chipotle, decided to try out their steak tacos and wasn't impressed. The meat was tough, fatty, and too spicy. Taco Bell is a lot better than this place.
By far the best destination for great eats in Philadelphia. Inexpensive casual and best of all local!

Food halls are on trend right now, but Reading Terminal Market has been ahead of the game for years. Being in Pennsylvania, a large part of the market is made up of Amish businesses such as Beiler's (one word - donuts), Smucker's (great breakfast sandwiches), Dutch Eating Place (order the hot apple dumpling), and more. There are also sandwich shops like Tommy Dinic's, Carmen's, Beck's Cajun Cafe (order the mac n cheese balls), ethnic food stalls serving Chinese, Indian, and Thai cuisine, and bakeries such as Termini Bros, Flying Monkey Bakery (get some whoopie pies). Not to mention great ice cream, cookies, fresh smoothies and juices...all this and so much more, in addition to fresh product, deli meats, and cookware. I'm not exaggerating with I say Reading Terminal Market is one of my favorite places - period. It's a Philadelphia institution and food lover's heaven, and a must visit when in town. I haven't been anywhere comparable in the country, and there is a charming and welcoming feeling about Reading that newer, more modern food halls lack. I always make a stop here when in Philly, and hope it's not too long before I visit again.
I was just blown away by this market.  So much great food, wonderful people, cool setting and great vibe.  It is a must visit when coming to Philadelphia.
One of the best places in town. I've been here a number of times; burger, chicken sandwich with egg, buffalo chicken meatballs and mac and cheese croquettes/ my faves!.The mousse dessert... amazing!
great place for shopping and grab agreat lunch.... many options , great atmosphere

Oh no another review of Reading Terminal Market, but it is that good. I know its a tourist trap, and that it is crowded and so forth. But surprisingly compared to most "root shopping market", I'm looking at you Fisherman's Pier. Its really still true to the roots, and still has all the good food and things that Philly natives like. 

Not just from a eating perspective but also shopping perspective as well. They have a great selection of great meant vendors specializing in the off beaten track fares, as well as the good old fashion sources of protein. All fresh, tasty, and at a fair price.

Then the restaurants inside Reading Terminal is actually really good. From the buck a shuck oysters, to the artisanal lamb specialty stores, and all the way to the classic Johnny DicNic pork. 

That old say, do as the local do? Well Reading Terminal Market is as the locals do!

Usually crowded but worth the wait. Lots of variety. Seating area in the middle. Parking nearby is ok. Always tried something new each time and always a good experience. Always get the fresh baked cookies from the cookie company at the end of one of the corner aisles near an entrance. Great cookies.

Reading Terminal Market is truly one of a kind. Every stall here is worth a visit. I'd even consider moving to Center City just to be able to shop for groceries here on a regular basis more conveniently. Not to mention, it is one of the best lunch spots in the city.

Absolutely love this place. Whenever I have friends visiting I always take them to this Philly staple. So many different options to chose from. I tend to stick with the Mediterranean options and am always impressed. I also always stop by for some fresh produce or fruit. 

Of course it's necessary to end the trip with Bassett's Ice Cream or a 4th Street cookie.

This is such a great place to shop for anything. From antique books to great pastries. There is also a couple quaker stands and one of them, a eat fast diner stand, is great for breakfast...and cheap too!

Oh my lovely Reading Terminal Market...you kick any NYC markets' ass I am so sorry yet delighted to say. With the Amish markets, DiNics, some kick-ass Cajun food, cookies, whoopie pies, oysters and coffee (in two trips...not one!), it was almost mind blowing how great you are. And you have a beer "garden" where I can sit and eat anything I want...sigh, I will miss you terribly.
We went for the roast pork sandwich with sharp provolone and rabe at DiNics and stayed for all the other yummy things.

A tourist favorite as there's always something new to discover at the Reading Terminal Market. You'd find something from every cuisine including American barbeque, Chinese, Mediterranean, Indian and Italian. We usually go there to pick up fresh produce and enjoy fresh donuts at Beiler's - one of the handful staples of the market. Old City coffee is a must to end your trip after a sinful portion of Dinic's, Sang kee pecking duck house and the 'scrapple' at the Down home diner.

It's an unavoidable institution with such fantastic variety of markets, vendors, and restaurant/drink options.

Don't be deterred by those who say it's a tourist trap!  It IS a tourist-heavy area, but that doesn't mean it's undeserving or fails to deliver genuine quality and uniqueness.  Tourists go there BECAUSE it does not cater to them...plenty of locals are there far more often than the tourists.  Many of the vendors have been operating there for 40+ years, so consider what that means.
I loved this place! There's simply not enough time in one's life to enjoy all of the different food/shops. It's a great spot in Philly.

I had a really good experience here. You get to choose the greens/meat/veggies/fruit/dressing you want on your salad, the salads are big, and the prices aren't inflated like most airport restaurants. The selection was good, the staff was friendly and seemed to care about getting my order right, and the ingredients were fresh. Much better than I expected from an airport salad.
If you can't find something you love here you must have no taste buds! tons of options for any taste with Denic's being the best of them all!

How awesome is this place? Very awesome! 

You can really get lost in here - so many great things to See, Eat, and Shop. This is a huge market with lots of different foods from all over. You really have to come here and experience it for yourself.

We went here this past weekend and everyone (children included) had a great time. Wish I lived closer so we could shop here more often.

I only gave it 3 stars because it was my first time and it was packed. We couldn't get any food due to the lines everywhere. It was crazy. I'll return when we don't have the kids to eat my way through that place. The sights, the smells. It was new to me. I wouldn't go on a Sunday when its packed, when there is an event across the street.. will try to go when its not a peak time. My fault. But everything looked awesome.

Prepare to be overwhelmed by choices.  I feel like I can eat here everyday and be satisfied with my trip. Torture is being full but seeing all these goodies to eat. I found a way to stuff down a cookie from Hope's cookies and it was well worth it. I ordered the caramel pecan and they guy asked if I wanted the one that was dipped in chocolate?  Who says no to anything dipped in chocolate?  

Come around 4-5 PM if possible (after checking the closing time of the places you want to go of course) to avoid the huge crowds.  There were still mini lines everywhere but it was manageable.

Horrible service. Very very very slow. Staff need to be trained to be efficient and fast. In general the concept of Chipotle is fast serving and to go, but this one has failed at all levels. 

Have to stand in line for 30 minutes anytime of the day you come to this place. I have been to this place 4 times and its always the same.  Who would like to stand for 30 minutes to get their food. It's very disrespect-able to the customers .
Love Reading Terminal Market! Come early and grab lunch at Dinic's. Love the roast pork w/ sharp provolone. Reasonable prices and you can find almost anything!

Ahh reading terminal market. One of Phillys staples. SO MANY CHOICES. haha. you can get any type of food you want - for any meal. From produce to brunch to crepes to japanese to greek to ice cream to cupcakes and coffee. Everything your heart desires in one place. It does get crowded on the weekends and hours vary certain days. but def worth the visit. 
Any type of food you want - if you have a group who cant decide what better place to go.

Obsessedddddd!  This place is amazing, I now go once a week for all my fruits and veggies.  It is a bit packed some days, but for the amount I save I can handle the crowd.  Great fresh food, various vendors  serving anything you want or desire to eat!
Literally everything in this place is amazing. It can get way too crowded and it's very expensive...but the food is fantastic.

I have been doing my grocery shopping from Iovine Brothers produce market. 
L Halteman shop is the best for meat and cheese (in entire Philly in my opinion). Jonathan place is kind of expensive, I can get same stuff from trader's joe at much cheaper price though. If you are a tourist, there are lot of choices for restaurants.  I get chocolates from PA general store . Best chocolates(if you like chocolates without much sweet stuff) and cookies. Very crowded ALL THE TIME :)
fun to go with visitors from out of town. like the variety of food, baked goods, and groceries.

WARNING:: Sensory overload will be imminent if entering this establishment. 

The sights will amaze you. You won't be able to decide what to eat. There are so many fantastic restaurants, you can't really make a wrong decision. If I may though, I highly suggest Tommy Di Nic's and Country Breakfast. 

The smells will fill your nostrils with more pleasure than that crazy night back in your sophomore year of college. Use your sense of smell to guide you to your dream meal. 

The tastes will blow you away. Nothing like a Tommy Di Nic's roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe, hot peppers, and provolone. Your taste buds are not ready. 

Unfortunately your sense of sound and touch might not be as pleased. You will feel cramped. Slow moving people, ogling everything in sight. You will hear loud crowds. This is a place to be, thus there will be noise. If there is one thing you'll hear often, it'll be "That was delicious".  

Trust me though, you'll gladly sacrifice those two for the other three. This is a must stop if you're visiting the city.

SO MUCH FOOD AND SO LITTLE TIME! You can literally find ANYTHING and EVERYTHING here! I come here to buy bulks of candy/chocolate for my little cousins, and the stop by for a quick lunch. It's a bit fast-paced and rowdy but definitely worth pushing through crowds for.

This place is fantastic!  They have everything you want or need. Two cheesesteak places, multipolar sweet shops, Icecream, seafood. Even jewelry and fresh produce. They have seats that you can sit down and eat or get it to go. Great for lunch. Close to hotels and shopping.
We love this place. It gets crazy busy but the food options are all above average. Definitely check out to grocery store for some killer deals on really good fruit and veggies.

Probably one of my favorite places in the world. Seemingly hidden in a warehouse in center city Philly lies one of the best food experiences you'll ever have. Filled with professional looking stalls from every cuisine, each and every one of them is an institution in their own right. From the Ditch Eating Place to DiNic's, to Hershel's East Side Deli to Kamal's, you'll find anything you'd ever want to your heart's desire. Too bad it's not open much later during the day for a later dinner. I always try to stop by when I'm in Philly.

Great place to visit on an empty stomach! Try all the 'thanksgiving' sanwhiches. Bring empty bahs BC you will want to fill them with delicious treats. NOT stroller friendly. It tends to get very crowded. People are also ruthless and very pushy! They will cut you in line or take your seat! Bring your 'game face'.

This market is one of the most successful blends of "tourist trap" meets "where the locals do their food shopping" that I have ever encountered.  

It's the place to be if you want to buy Thai food, spices, coffee, tea, cupcakes, a rutabaga, honey, Middle Eastern food, baklava, roasted turkey, fresh turkey, baby spinach, an awesome sandwich, a single chicken breast, 100lbs of chicken wings, steaks, milk, cheese, bread . . .  The list goes on and on.  As long as you avoid Tokyo Sushi, you literally cannot go too wrong with any of the classic or newer vendors. 
 
If you are a local trying to food shop, weekday mornings are the quietest and weekend mornings (before 10) are usually manageable.  Expect a big crowd at lunch time and on the weekends, especially if there is anything sizable going on at The Convention Center.  Avoid at all costs during The Flower Show.  If you are a tourist . . . well then . . . just get on in there and be prepared to throw a few elbows as you make your way through the crowds getting a feel for Philly at its finest.  Just please don't come to a dead stop to look around and take pictures in the middle of the aisles.  Thanks!

I know markets. I live in Cleveland and we have the West Side Market, for goodness sake!

Are there any Clevelanders reading this?  ::Looks around::  okay good. I am pained to say that the Reading Terminal Market BLOWS away the West Side Market and furthermore, any other market I've ever visited.

Now that I have that off my chest, let me tell you I was a kid in a candy store (Yes, don't worry they have a candy store). Any kind of product or food you could want is enclosed in this indoor market with over 100 vendors. High-quality, respected vendors in a beautiful space.

I didn't get to spend as much time here as I would have liked, but this is a must see for me in Philadelphia. It gets a little crowded, so plan accordingly and be patient, but it's so worth taking the time to navigate through the aisles to check everything out.
Just the kind of place I was looking for.  Between the salad and smoothie, I paid like $14, but it was tasty and it is the airport...terminal D btw.

I had some time to kill before my bus left to head back to DC, so I decided to explore Reading Terminal Market. Many people had told me about it, but I didn't really know what to expect when I went there. There were so many options when I walked in, that I wasn't sure where to begin. I ended up just walking around for a while, just to see what was available. You could do a great deal of shopping here or even just stop in for a bite to eat. Not everything was open when I was there on a Sunday, but there was enough for it to be enjoyable. It wasn't overly crowded either, which I'm sure is rare. Yea there were a lot of people walking around, but very few places had unbearably long lines. I definitely want to spend more time here, so I can't wait to come back!

This place is awesome.  I loved the variety of food options and shopping fun.  I would have spent two days here.  the convention center is just across the street and is a perfect location for attendees.  Everyone needs to visit.  This place made my Philly stay PERFECT.

Definitely a place to visit!

I've been here thrice during my one month visit. 

For the cheesesteak, I've tried Carmen's and By George! And I honestly like By George!'s better. A tip - Spataro and By George! Are closed on Sundays (among other stores) so the line at Carmen's get really long. I recommend going on other days to be able to visit all the shops. 

Bassett's Ice Cream is really good too! More on the creamier side. 

The donuts from Beiler's Bakery (closed on Sundays) are really good too! They run out really fast also. I tried the one with colored cereal on it and it was awesome. 

The chocolates from Mueller's are good as well! Even their sugar free options.

Amazing place, for visitors and locals alike. You can get pretty much any kind of food, fresh groceries, artisan cheese, even Amish specialties if it's not a Sunday. The market is always bustling and right in the center of everything. My favorite spots are Iovine Bros, the falafel place, and By George. I also understand that DiNic's has some great pulled pork sandwiches for you meat-eaters out there!
This is a great place to explore all things tasty. It felt welcoming and appetizing. There's so many places to check out. I enjoyed my experience here.
Really crowded but some awesome small businesses. Especially bakeries. Produce area is great too. Good prices.
Great fast food place. Nice ambience. I had a chance to eat panneer roll and potato roll. It was simple and easy food.

Love Love this place. Always a treat every time I go. I usually buy my groceries from there because its maybe 20 cents cheaper than conventional super markets. This place is awesome to just hang out with some friends sampling all kinds of foods. They're open super early and closes around 6pm.

There is really nothing more to add about the Reading Terminal that hasn't already been written. The place is extraordinary and if you visit Philadelphia this is a must. It's always packed because the food is outstanding and there is something for everyone. The crowds can be a bit disorienting and overwhelming at times so if you hate crowds try to hit it around 2pm just to get the lay of the land. Once you get a handle of it return for breakfast, lunch, or dinner and take it all in. Enjoy!

I love coming here even with the crowds. I would recommend to go on a Wednesday or Sunday because the fruit market gives students a discount. Who doesn't love a nice discount?

The food is also really good I always go to grab chicken samosas and something from one of the MANY bakeries. I have never had a bad experience with any of the places that I've eaten at. I love how everything is fresh and ready for purchase. 

Always a treat to be at Reading Terminal!

This is definitely a place to come to if you are from out of town but also if you are local and want great food. You can pretty much find anything you desire to eat. From chocolates to seafood to Asian cuisine, the choices are limitless.

Awesome. Doesn't get better. Go hungry because you will want to (and should) try everything you pass by. Cannoli at Termini are a must for a sweet tooth. Tons of amazing Amish foods (made the old fashioned way). YUM. A Philly institution.
Expensive, but good! LOTS of choices!! Pay your parking tho, so you don't get a ticket!! Lol..

A Must stop when in Philadelphia. They have everything! it is a blast just to walk around and try different things: soft pretzels, roast pork sandwiches (di nic's), donuts, cookies, ice cream, mexican, sushi,...ok you get the idea. they have produce market, spice market, sea food market, anything-you-can-think-of market. you could spend hours here. 

it can get a little crowded, and some of the line get long but they move along and most line are well worth the wait. i wouldn't recommend coming in with a stroller unless it is fairly empty. my wife and i did it once...yeah that wont happen again.

In all of the years that i have gone to Chick-Gil-A, I have NEVER EVER EVER had a bad experience except for today! My "waffle" (can't even call them that today, more like bottom of the bag) fries were greasy! My chicken sandwich was cold and greasy! This has NEVER happened to me before. Chick-fil-A usually has exceptional customer service and the quality of the fast food is exceptional as well. I truly hope that this was an isolated incident because I usually truly enjoy coming here for a quick bite. My heart is really crushed right now

Quick and simple- reading terminal is finally upgrading, bringing in new amenities, and they have some great new storefronts and eateries. The good places are even getting better. I can't wait to see what else they have in store for 2013!

Reading is one of the best places in all of Philly. I've tried so many different things here and I've never been disappointed. If you're ever in Philly, definitely try the crepes place and the donuts!

This place is an iconic, amazing, foodie paradise.  I've lost count as to how many stands they have, but they have quite the variety, from very local to sort of local (Lancaster County).  They have a million options for lunch and dinner.  I always try to find a new place to try every time I go there.  From turkey dinner to vegan cupcakes and the freshest raw seafood, they have it all!

The Reading Terminal a MUST whether you're visiting Philadelphia or have lived here your entire life. You want Chinese? Boom! they have it. In the mood for a delicious roast pork sandwich? Well you're in luck considering Dinic's has one of the best in the country. Or maybe you want an Amish pretzel, a half rack of ribs and a delicious ice cream cone for desert. What do you know, its all here too. Jokes aside, this place has everything you could want to eat as well as a produce market and small knick knack shops. Make sure you come hungry because you'll leave satisifed and, believe me, you'll want to come back again and again to try everything it has to offer.
Oh yeah, I'm  coming back!   Be prepared to spend time checking out the amazing variety of food selection stores, all under one roof !

This place was so much fun. There was so much to try. The homemade ice cream was amazing as well as the sample of chicken pot pie soup and lemonade I tried. Oh and the homemade carrot bread. A huge assortment of fresh products. It was fun watching some of the Amish making stuff from scratch. And the thing that shoots out rice cakes. It was packed on a Saturday for an early lunch, but pretty dead when we came back on Sunday for breakfast since the Amish and most of the other vendors were not there. They also had farm animals and music outside when we were there on Saturday. 

I wish I had a place like this closer to home. I will be back next time I'm in Philly!
This place is heaven! I come to Philly every year in October and visit this market thru out my entire weekend stay. The cookies, cakes, sandwiches and everything else is jus amazing!!!!!
Awesome place, loved all of the food options and freshness of everything. A little crowded during lunch, but was still a pleasant experience.
Nice, a must see place for everyone. I stay nearby and I go here to get my groceries every week. A large variety of good food and good service. It's overcrowded during the weekends, just enjoy it,

I have been in many markets with the same concept. Usually they are overpriced and the food is mediocre. The Redding Market makes every other market of it's ilk pale in comparison. Not only are the prices absurdly low, the quality, taste and range of offers is exceptional. No matter what you want, I'm sure it can be had here. Yum on!

Been one of my favorites for many years...you can get anything you want at RTM. Over my latest 2 day visit, we had red beans and rice, cheesesteaks, PA Dutch breakfast, shoo fly pie, coffee, wine, and more. If you are in the area or attending something at the PA Convention Center, it's a must do.
I came here before moving to Philly and loved the place. Every restaurant is good, some are great, like Hershel's. In my opinion the best option in Redding terminal.

I haven't written a review in so long but this place is so great that it deserves one.  I came down from NYC a few weeks ago just to see what Philly had to offer.  The city was about what I expected (not bad) but this place was a real gem.  It's pretty convenient, right in the middle of town near city hall.  It has just about every type of food stand you can imagine.  There was so much good food that I came back 3 times before going home!  Tommy Dinic's seemed to be the crowd favorite but unfortunately it was so crowded that I never got to try it.  My favorite ended up being the pastrami sandwhich at Hershel's East Side Deli.  I'd trade Eataly AND Chelsea Market to move this place to NYC!

Everything you need is right here.  The Amish and other locals bring their best here, so lots of fresh meat, fish, seafood, vegetables plus lots of great little places to eat.  Had the best turkey sandwich of my life here.  Plus there's pretzels and donuts and ice cream and Cajun and roast beef and wines and chocolates.  This place is heaven on earth, I just wish I lived closer.

I love coming here. There are lots of vendors with fresh produce and fresh homemade juices, pastries, and other foods. I don't think I could ever get bored coming here. It does get very busy on the weekends, which makes it a bit tough walking through the market. I can't wait to go back!

A Wendy's has been here for years, however, they somewhat recently tore it down, and built a new one from the ground up. Looks more like a Chipotle, or a Qdoba then a Wendy's. They even have Starbucks style couches to sit on. Nicest Wendy's I have ever been to.

The food, unfortunately, is typical Wendy's. Wendy's for the kids out there USED to have great burgers. Great. Then in the 1990's sometime, they went downhill. Maybe when Dave himself passed away? Dunno.

Since the area is close to the airport, and the airport hotels, I should throw in to the out-of-town visitors looking for a quick fast-food filling, that this Wendy's is in a safe, almost suburban type neighborhood.

I've only been to one other location, so hard to compare them. 

I had a good experience the couple of times I'm come here. Chicken if flavorful, juicy ( not dry) and tastes fresh. I was surprised to see that they come around and refill your drink if needed, kudos!

Chicken nuggets and their spicy chicken are my favorites.

Only reason for a non-5 star was because one " bad apple" employee wasn't as friendly as all the other co-workers. Being a little nit-picky.. but Chick-Fil-A prides itself in having great customer service and for example always saying " my pleasure" when you thank them etc. She would say " sure" or " mm-hmmm" and walk away. Just a little nugget of a note.

Otherwise, very clean, friendly, and tasty spot!

Breakfast was good. They were open super early which was nice(430am). So much better then the other choices around the terminal especially the Jet Rock cafe. That place is the worst place in the airport.

Never thought I write a review for chick-fil-a but here we are. One of the best fast food places I've ever been to. Their food is always fresh and fast. Unlike other fast food places chick-fil-a is clean the food is made with quality ingredients and the staff is nice the trifecta. If you walked in with your eyes closed you would think your walking into a restaurant not a fast food place. Nice job hopefully they keep this up.

This place is hit-or-miss.  Usually a hit but when it's a miss it's often by a lot.

HITS:  Prices are good.  I can get a BIG salad, bag of chips and a drink cheaper than just a salad from other places close to campus.  Online ordering - saves a LOT of time when you go to pick up during peak pick-up times (see MISSES for more about that).  Convenient location (on campus, across from both HUP & CHOP), fresh & good tasting food.

MISSES: Because of the way it's set up you may sometimes tell three different people what you want before the person who's going to make your salad asks you what you want (order online, you won't have this problem).  If you go anytime between 11:30 and 1:30 it gets CROWDED (again, order online).  If you go at non-peak times and don't order online the staff might not be helpful (case in point, I was in there yesterday with SIX people not doing anything and no one would take my or the guy in front of me's order).  Occasionally the online order gets "lost" and isn't ready for pick up (on the upside they will move you to the front of the line and make it pronto -- this has happened more than 3 times, it wasn't a fluke incident).

Overall, it's a decent place on Penn's/UPHS campus.  Food is tasty & cheap.  I use a meeting at the hospital to get a chicken salad salad a few times a month and I've been known to trek over there for food even when I don't have a meeting.
This place is great!!! The variety at Reading Terminal can't be beat. I go here for produce, specialty foods, lunch...you name it, they've got it! If you are a tourist visiting Philly, it's a must

Talk about sensory overload! Reading terminal has just about anything you could possibly think of. On a snowy day, I took the train into central city and had myself a grand o' time! One stop you could get oysters, then jump to another vendor for roasted Chinese duck. From there I moved onto a cookie and then a donut and then and then! Yes, that was all consumed by one person(me) in about a 4 hour period. This is an awesome place to stop for locals and tourists alike. Tip- the produce/farmers market has very reasonable prices.

Living in parts of Philly, especially Old City, means that getting fresh meat and veggies can be a challenge.  Luckily, RTM is just a quick jump on the El to 11th and Market.  

Martin's meats is our go-to for meats.  OK-Lee veggies are right there, too.  

The prices are fair and the quality is generally quite high.  

We've never actually eaten at the various food stands, but for fresh veggies and meats it's the place to go.
Love it here. The bakery is amazing and they have a delicious gluten free granola.

Loved this place! So many places to eat & check out! And it was packed with people on a Monday at noon. That says something. We stopped & got the most amazingly fresh cookies & a pot roast sandwich...it was to die for! I wish my stomach could have fit more so I could try tons of others eateries. So glad we came here!
Terrible farmers market, rude and obnoxious local crowds, mediocre food, super dirty market. Stay away. Instead go to Seattle's Pike Place market or Atlanta's Underground (that's crowded too).

I could spend hours in here! Very cool place with lots of interesting vendors. Mostly prepared foods, made to order foods, delis, specialty foods etc. So. much. food. 
The place was packed on a snowy Saturday so it made it hard to really wander and look at things. But we enjoyed Amish hot dogs and then wine at the winery!
Great amount of choices. Great food. Regular folks of all ethnicities getting along famously. As it should be.
