Packed, stressful, not enough seating, food is mediocre. Go early or pass it up if you've been to something similar!

Who doesn't love RTM? I mean, I guess there are a handful of people who decided to give this place 1-2 stars but they are far outnumbered by those of us who adore this place (yea, that's right 4-5 stars). 

More than the food, it's the vibe that I'm in love with. So this place does get obnoxiously busy on Saturdays and yea, you might wait 10 minutes for your Amish baked goodies on any given day at lunchtime. But its worth it. Where else in the city do you get this kind of variety (and from LOCAL producers)? 

This is the place I take all of my out-of-town friends to and is the only place that everyone enjoys. If you can't find some facet of this place that you enjoy, well, then you might be a mean one, Mr. Grinch.

Here you will find your average Subway shop providing their standard offering of sandwiches, drinks and chips. I did not have any issues here, and my wife who works in the food service industry didn't see anything alarming like the previous reviewer claimed.

It still tops out at three stars just because it's your standard cookie cutter franchise and there are just so many specialty sandwich/sub shops in this area that I would find it hard to choose Subway over them unless it was the only one open when I had a craving for a sub.
Definitely a fun place to stop for unique foods you may not find anywhere else, but sometimes it is overly crowded and touristy.
Reading terminal is great. I love a good indoor market with tons of shops carrying specialty items, and baked goods to eat while you walk around.

Reading Terminal Market saved us on a rainy Saturday in Philadelphia.  Heck, this would also be a great place to go in the middle of the summer if you wanted to escape the heat.  In other words this is a great place to go anytime of the year.

Being that I currently live on the west coast I would have to say that this market reminds me a lot of Pike Place Market in Seattle.  This market happens to be entirely indoors, but it is the same concept more or less.

You want meat?  Come to Reading Terminal Market.  You need linens?  Come to Reading Terminal Market.  You want killer pretzels or handmade donuts?  Come to Reading Terminal Market.  We ended up getting both of the latter and both were just about great.

You can spend hours going through all the nooks and crannies of this building.  It was highly enjoyable and I wish that I had something like this where I live.  Actually maybe not.  I'd probably spend all of my money there.

Just expect huge crowds of people! Lots of choices for food, I certainly have my favorites but I won't list them since it is really dependent on what you want to eat.  When I used to live down in Philly (and still when I am visiting on an all day trip) I tend to stop into the market to pick up some goodies to take home.  

Best time to go is first thing before the lunch crowd, or after 3pm.

Best place I have been in a long time . Being from Boston which doesn't have a place like this I was so happy to be in this place . Love love love it . If you like to cook and love food. This is heaven in one place
This is the best place in Philly, perfect spot for any meal and great for tourists and locals a like.

The terminal has the best produce, Amish donuts, tomato pie, meat, honey, fresh juice, coffee, fish, cheese, spices, candy, and kebabs on the East Coast. Did I forget anything? If it I did, it is also the best of the best because nothing being sold at Reading Terminal Market is less than superb. Forget Whole Foods, this is the legit healthy (or not) shopping experience. Just don't go during the lunch hour if you dislike crowded places - this is a very crowded space and that can be irritating. If you do one thing in Philadelphia go here. The liberty bell is way less fun and tastes much worse.

OH WOW!!! I have always heard great things about this place and now I can finally attest to all the amazing reviews! 

A little about the experience:  First, the place itself; walking in is a treat within itself and so easy with all the entrances that are available. The air is filled with aromas from all different foods and cultures that just seem to blend so perfectly well together. The bustling from all the locals and out-of-town"ers" makes you feel like a true city folk. All the vendors are nice and knowledgeable of the area; which sure helps a first timer like myself when trying to navigate the market innards. However this wouldn't be needed if a directory was put up somewhere which was my only complaint about the whole place. My first thought was oh this place is going to have a couple of little places to eat inside, to my delightful surprise it also contained fresh looking meat markets and fresh vegetable stands located inside, it was quite a treat to see. In addition to all the food YOU CAN EVER WANT they also offer little stores filled with knick-knacks so you can leave with two types of souvenirs one to eat and a one to keep. Not to mention if you ever seem to be a little short on cash no worries you can find ATM's scattered throughout.

Now a yelp-ers favorite part of the review: the food. I personally went to Herchel's, Dinics and the famous Beiler's Bakery. Lucky for me when I first entered, the bakery was staring me right in the eye holes tempting all my taste buds with their aesthetically pleasing cakes, muffins, pastries of all sorts and the ever so tantalizing Beiler's Doughnuts which I had to part-take in. Unfortunately by the time I had gotten there all the Boston Creme doughnuts (which happen to be my favorite doughnut were all out (sad face)). So I went in without a plan and was not totally disappointed. I went with a Red Velvet doughnut which to my pleasure was quite the pallet pleaser, it had the red velvet taste down to a "t", Other doughnuts included a Salted Caramel apple, Gingersnap and "The Elvis".

Dinic's is located more towards the middle of the Terminal market taking up quite a bit more real estate than others. They offered delectable sandwich choices and the staff was pleasant and knowledgeable of their product. 

I knew I couldn't leave without trying Hershel's deli.The menu looked delicious so I couldn't say no to grabbing one of their scrumptious sandwiches. So i then found myself standing in line. They offer your run of the mill delicatessen sandwiches, however I wouldn't be wrong to say that they do them a little better than most, in my honest opinion. 

All-in-all this place is must-go if you ever find yourself in the City of Philadelphia; with its wide variety of stores and fresh produce as well as meats, you can't go wrong with a trip to Reading terminal market!! To quote the famous actor and Governor of California Arnold Schwarzenegger "I'll be back".

My go to place for just about everything foodie!   Desserts, lunches and dinners are within walking distance inside the market. Amish delights, fresh seafood and meats, Down Home Diner, Pizza and Snapper soup... just to name a few.  Also a fresh vegetable market!
No need to shop anywhere else
Downside is parking you car.  Take ride share or public transportation
I love this place. Donuts, cheese, coffee, vinegar, sausages...what else is there in life?

Absolute Favorite! We take all of our out of town guests here as soon as we can. It's a great place bc they can get a feel for the charismatic Philly atmosphere and get classic Philly dish while I get whatever the heck I want! Of course we always end our visit with some ice cream from Bassetts
You can find everything under the sun here. It's a wonderful place full of great places to eat, fresh produce, fish and meat. Specialty shops, and anything else you can imagine. Love!
i guess worth checking out just to have checked it out, but this place is like a freaking zoo, complete with overpriced junk food.

Loved this place! Great food! Good atmosphere! Went on a Sunday evening so it wasn't too crowded, so I don't know how it would be on a busier day. Our waitress was friendly and sweet but didn't do that annoying this where a waitress comes over a million times during the meal (that drives me nuts)! The beer cheese fondue is WHERE IT'S AT! I highly recommend getting it if you have anything with fries!
A Philadelphia institution. Fun place for lunch and a good place to go shopping for fresh and local food. The homemade ice cream is always popular. Worth a visit for locals and visitors alike!

I stopped in as I tracked every week.  The eggs and sausage were as expected, warm, not hot, and tasted like they had been there for 1/2hr.  No great surprises as they have them in the window, so you know what you are signing up for.

Incredulous that clerk now keep coin change and don't provide it unless asked.  While not concerned over $0.39, just curious whether trained to nickel and dime the customer, or not trained and consciously ripping off the customer.  Either way, I won't be back.

Get me out of here!  What a Zoo, people bumping into you from every direction.   Not a place to sit, relax and enjoy your meal without a crowd.  One thing this Market does not lack is finding something to eat at any price.    
We ended up goi g to o Le Pain Quotidien on Walnut Street instead and shared the Grilled Chicken & Smoked Mozzarella Melt that was delicious - our Server Amar B was fabulous!  He made sure we had everything we needed, and we gave him a generous tip since he was so nice.   So, if you you want a variety of food choices, and don't mind crowds at a cheap price this place is for you.

This market came highly recommended by a few friends who had visited Philly before. 

First impressions is that this market is endless. This is a local/organic food lovers heaven! There are a wide variety of stalls that sell anything from fish to spices to honey. But one thing they all have in common is that the food stuff is high quality. I bought some Cajun spices from the a spice stall and can't wait to use it with some chicken/steak. It can be dangerous to visit this market when you are hungry because you'll probably want to eat everything in sight. No doubt, you'll leave with a full stomach and an empty wallet.

Massive selection of various foods to eat and all pretty low priced.  Its a bit of a weird mix of local market meats and then clearly touristy attractions.  
That said there is just no seating, so I don't suggest really coming here if you have any kids.  Its just not an option to stand when you have a kid or more with you.

We enjoyed the experience walking and eating in The Terminal Market. It has all kinds of delicious foods stands and pastries. I had The Combo #2 at Glick's Rib Shack. You get 3 ribs and two sides. I chose mac & cheese and coleslaw. The mac & cheese was perfectly moist and cheesy. The spicy sauce I highly recommended for the ribs. My husband had lunch at Beck's cajun cafe. He loved the Shrimp & Crawfish Etouffee over white rice. I asked for a sample of the jambalaya and it was sooo good. But sadly I just ate so I could order one for me. And for dessert we stop at Beilers Pickle Patch for a Maple & Bacon donut (Please buy two donut. Is a match made on heaven). My husband liked his apple fritter. Over all we love it!!! We want to comeback and try more food stands.

Wow, what a an amazing place. I only had one day in Philly, so this was one of the must-stops. My bro and I decided to have some lunch here but we were having a very hard time deciding, as there were way too many tempting choices! We had to systematically go up and down all the aisles to make sure we saw all the vendors to make the best informed choice. In addition to all the prepared foods there were purveyors of all kinds of other goods, such as produce, meats, seafood, and crafty items. And all along the perimeter of the market were restaurants too--most of them chain restaurants, it looked like, but if that's more your speed it's nice to have that option. After perusing ALL our options, we finally decided to get lunch at the Wursthaus Schmitz (separate review). It's pretty hectic and crowded, as you may well imagine, but it wasn't too bad, and kind of added to the atmosphere. Fortunately they have lots of seating. 

STEPH JUDGEMENT: A sensory overload--in a good way!
It's a nice place to grab lunch, don't go on a Saturday during tourist season unless you want to feel like a sardine!

I loved it. The crust is thin, crisp and flavorful. The special, with squash and tomatoes was sweet and savory. The pepperoni spicy, cheesy and tangy. The plain was worthy condentor for plain 'za. It was delicious but my least favorite of the offerings.
This McDonald's is super dirty nobody clean the tables we were there for an hour the employees were very rude messed up my order The absolute worst fast food spot I've ever been too

Amazing! I really enjoyed coming here and sampling a bunch of different vendors (Beilers for donuts, old city coffee, melt Kraft for amazing grilled cheese, the big ice cream place with the blue and white logo). Gets very crowded on weekends though, and wish it was open later. Tip- if you go like 20-30 minutes before closing some places are trying to get rid of products and will sell it at a heavily discounted price!!

It's like the better Subway.

Potbelly has high quality sandwiches made at the speed of any fast food sandwich shop. It's like someone took Subway and said, "I can do that better."

They have a decent selection of sandwiches, a couple of soups, some macaroni salad, and cookies. Oh, and their shakes are the awesomeness.

Great spot for that quick sandwich that sticks to your ribs.

This is a must do in Philly.  It gets super crowded but for a reason.  Some really great food at this place.  It can be hard to find a table but I think thats expected with a place this well-known.  It's definately a Philly institution.
This is probably one of my favorite bazaar. I think there are more than 70 shops side by side . Many organic food and fruits,chocolate shops,souvenir stores .

Ok guys, sorry I couldn't give a 5 because this place is amazing but simultaneously overwhelming!!! Like whoa overwhelming. Anything your heart desires to eat is here, at various places, and based on the ones I've tried they're all top notch. It's also a great place to go in groups because everyone can get what they want! The lines are typically super long (at least at lunchtime when I go) and not always fast moving. But everyone who is in philly should go at least once!

Walking into Reading Terminal Market is great for when there are many options and there are plenty of places to satisfy everyone's palate. Upon walking in here, it very much reminded me of the Essex Market in NYC but bigger and a little bit better. From smoked meats, local goods and sweet delectables, there is so much to choose from. Although it can be quite confusing which direction to go, there are maps that are on the wall to help guide you to the vendor you would like to visit.
The location of the market is conveniently close to popular parts of the city. It is a short walk to the old city where you can visit and tour the liberty bell and independence hall. Also close by is philly's Chinatown. 
A good tip to keep in mind if you have a car to park is that the Reading Market has two parking lots on 12th and the other on 11th that offer discounted parking. You just need to take your parking ticket, spend at least $10 in the market at one of the vendors, ask the vendor to validate your ticket and you are set. It will give you two hours of parking for $4. After that the rates increase, but still a pretty good discount.

Reading Terminal is like a classier version of the Pennsauken Mart. There is a myriad of shops and foods and what not to explore. I was there for 2 reasons recently; 1) to take the Philadelphia Chocolate Walking Tour and 2) to eat a pork sandwich at Dinics because it was on Man vs Food. The chocolate tour was meh, ok....different chocolate samplings around the city. The misses is the chocoholic, so it was more for her than me. There was a gelato place at the end of the tour that was pretty awesome.....damn...I can't remember the name. (I shall update after I use my google-fu), The sandwich was actually pretty good even though I should have went with spinach instead of broccoli rabe. Lesson learned. Variety is the spice of life so if youre looking for a little spice, check out Reading Terminal. Oh, and they validate parking if you park in the lot across the street. Pretty damn sweet in Philadelphia any time you can get that.
Whatever it is your looking for, odds are you can find it here. Food, groceries and gifts. It's all here and all great quality.
I like the they have a play area for children.  They do not have a self service drink area so the staff have get your soda pop or iced tea. The French fries are also good.
This place is incredible. Its like Disneyland for foodies.
I like ninja chicken and friend giant squid . Taste excellent.also green tea grapefruit and black lime tea . High recommend. Yum yummy!

Okay, it is a tourist magnet but if I were local, I'd still go there once a week.  It blows away similar food halls in other cities.  The Amish presence adds a nice touch and we had breakfast at the counter of the Amish Kitchen and it was killer.  Went back for lunch as the variety is overwhelming and yet the quality is consistent from rib joint, to sushi to the oyster bar.  Just outrageous.  Needless to say I stopped there on my way to the airport to load up on food for the ride and the fresh turkey sandwich rocked.
It's a good thing I don't live there, between the Amish donut place and the big bakery (pumpkin donuts?), I'd be on Biggest Loser.

I highly recommend coming here if you're in town. If you have any uncertainty about what food you want to eat you'll be provided so many delicious options here. I ordered a philly cheese steak because that's what the city is known for and I was not disappointed. Wish I spent more time here to explore but you can certainly take 2-3 hrs of your day just sampling and trying the food. I will be back!

This place literally has something for everyone. Went grocery shopping at Iovine Brothers (extensive selection of fruits, veggies, everything in between, nuts, and organic food) then got the maple syrup yogurt from another shop. Amazing when frozen! Heard the juices, cheesesteaks, and ice cream are amazing too so will need to be back!!
I am givin a 4 cause the foods on point most times and the service is good for mickey Dees. Play area is not a place to go though.

Always a good experience!  We end up coming here sometimes after seeing a movie and because it's so close to the theatre.  We've had the same bartender both times.  Not sure his name but both times he's always done a good job.  Being in the industry I definitely like coming here even if it's always a random occasion.

Awesome! Can get very crowded but usually worth it once you find your meal spot. 
Great fresh fish meats and poultry.

Came in on the Sunday of Labor Day Weekend (2015) and this place was so full of life! Lots of places to eat and shop and a live band playing in the middle of the seating area. It was so hard to choose where to eat because all of them offered something that looked and smelled absolutely delicious! The only downside was more than a few places were closed, probably because it was Sunday. We ended up grabbing a sandwich from Tommy DiNic's that did NOT disappoint. This is definitely a must see if you're in Philadelphia.

This place has so many different food vendors-go HUNGRY. Be aware though, this place gets PACKED especially on the weekends. I love taking out of town guests here-this way they can try a bunch of Philly flavor all under one roof. BEILER'S donuts and Basset's Ice cream are a must. I was really excited for Kevin Parker's famous Fried chicken-but it's a bit overrated in my opinion. Be prepared to wait in line here. 

As a local, I enjoy going here on my days off of work during the week day to get my weekly produce. There's a spot right in the center of the market that sells super fresh and cheap produce. If you're a student, enjoy 10% off! There's another spot located in the back where you can taste test a bunch of different cooking oils before you decide to purchase. I haven't seen other places like that in Philly-thought it was pretty neat.
Lots of fun eateries!! Inexpensive yummy local famous food. Also have many dessert choices. It's indoor,so it's a perfect hang out/lunch spot especially during hot summer days!
So many options, don't go too hungry.  Best place is the Valley Shepherd Creamery!
Simply the best indoor market in Philadelphia. Whatever you're looking for you can find it at the Reading Terminal Market.

A Philadelphia institution and must see for all tourist. Yes when all is said and done the old reliable Terminal Market is still the best breakfast and lunch spot in Philly, as long as you can deal with the constant over crowding and fighting for a seat etc. Particularly good are the Amish restaurants and take out home grown veggies and farm raised chickens. Really to die for! Wonderful other choices , like Dinic's, Salumeria for sandwiches. Various Bakeries are excellent as well, and they even have a wine cellar there?!  Soul food and middle eastern, Asian eateries are wonderful,, really everything (except the Down Home Diner , avoid at all cost) But even arguably better than the restaurants are the various fresh fish, produce, outlets sprinkled thru out the terminal. The best fresh fish fruits and veggies produce money can buy Again if you are visiting Philly, I highly recommend you stop by and visit the ONE and only Reading Terminal Market, a unique Philly Staple that you just wont find anywhere else.

If I closed my eyes, I could imagine I was back in one of my favorite places on Earth...Grand Central Market in NYC. A local friend steered me toward this highlight of our visit to Philly. A historic farmer's market in the city center, Reading Terminal Market is crammed with specialty food vendors making it nearly impossible to narrow down a meal. Deciding on dessert, however, was no problem whatsoever...a strawberry, walnut & Nutella crepe from Profi's Creperie. Lecker!!!

This is one the best Indian food I have had. You can pretty much go with anything and chances are that you will like it.   
I live in California, and by default I get to try different cuisine and lots of restaurants, including Indian. I have travelled to so many cities within the US, but nothing came close to this restaurant (Indian cuisine wise). 
I would consider this as Indian fusion, but a fusion worth trying.
For what this is and where it's at....this place is awesome. Tons of prepared and fresh food vendors all under one roof in center city.

Had my first try at Masala Kitchen for lunch yesterday and was blown away. I was a bit skeptical as I've always had my favorites in Philadelphia and the thought of fast food indian just didnt sit too well But OMG their chicken masala roll is AMAZING!!!!!!! It is ridiculously good! 

I want one now. I want one daily! I wan't one every meal if possible! 

I love that it is so cheap and I love that they are opened late! All kinds of love! Will be returning to try their recommended Chicken Kheema next. Can not wait!

Worst cashier ever! Went in there for a small box of milk. She couldn't ring it up so she went to look if it had a price from where i got it from. She walks really slow tells me there's no price like I'm some wizard who is supposed to tell her what to do. I told her I really need the milk for my baby. My baby's nose starts bleeding really bad and she's like I have to call someone for the price. Like holy hell! I have a bleeding kid in my arms and your moving as slow as molasses for a freakin milk that cost $1.25! Train your workers better or hire ones that can react faster to situations that can be handled independently with common sense.
Very crowded. They have maps, which is helpful, because it's almost impossible to find your way through the sea of people. Couldn't find anything vegan though, other than produce.
i love this place! mmm... my go to spot is the amish rib stand. sucks that they are closed on monday and tuesday.
Always have a good meal here. I've talk to a few employees and they really care about food safety. For fast food it's great. A little pricey but for the quality of the food you get it is worth it.

Cool space with a nice bar. We went for brunch and was glad to see the offered some lunch option ( I'm not really a breakfast guy).  Beer selection is good and the BBQ pork sandwich was good. Friendly staff. Would like to try their dinner menu soon.

I could live here. No, really. Last time I went, I spent three hours in here without realizing it. I live less than half a mile from this place and I have to stop myself heading out there every day. I have a feeling that my weighing scale and wallet are both going to be feeling the effects of living so close to RTM before the year is out!

I think the reviewers here have done a more than adequate job of talking about how wonderful this is and where you should go, but I'll add my two cents in anyhow.

OK, so if you do live in the area and come here to shop for groceries, come either in the mornings or after 3pm. Also, if you're a student one of the produce places  (forget which aisle it's in) offers a 10% student discount. Because it's terribly crowded otherwise. Lunch time here is pretty crazy. But, even though I hate crowds, I'd brave even the lunch time crowds for this foodie heaven.

Can't praise the Amish baked goods enough. Their various breads--peach, apple cinnamon etc are YUMMY and they make the best gingerbread I have ever had. Oh and the apple dumplings with heavy cream...I think I'm going to go out right now and get myself one, haha. The international cheese place has a great selection at reasonable rates--it stocked all the English cheeses that I love (Blue Stilton, Wensleydale, Double Gloucester). The Thai place is wonderful too. The red curry was too much for just one meal--I ate it over two. Dinner *and* lunch for just $7!! 

There are SO many places here which I plan on gradually exploring over the coming months...I'll add to this if I come across anything exceptional. But if you're in Philly and haven't been there yet, GO NOW.

The Reading terminal is a place that you could find yourself lost four hours. If you walk you will find something new at every turn. It would take hours to visit every shop, you will have to be there from the time it opens until the time it closes. While shopping at the Reading terminal you will find tourists well as regulars. There are families that have been shopping for generations at The Reading Terminal, my grandmother. my aunt, now me. There's something family and familiar like about the Reading Terminal. You can shop for meat, vegetables, coffee, tea, candy, pastries breads and smokes. There are also deli's and restaurants, stop and have lunch or purchase a souvenir.

Many small businesses got their start here. Some have moved onto bigger and  better things. But it is a place where all can come to find something that they need in their day or in their life. It is a fast-paced environment for most of the stores that  handle a high-volume. Please be prepared to know what you want to order. Most of the stores will walk you through the process or give you some pointers as to the best buy or the most popular item. I say grab a friend and have lunch!

Loved our visit to Philadelphia, and really loved Reading Terminal Market which was just a few blocks from our hotel.  Every kind of food that you can think of is represented in RTM. Over the 3 day visit, we stopped by here 4 times! Love the food - love the atmosphere!

I really enjoyed this place; I would give a full five but they're just getting started - give them a little time. I had the BBQ duck and my gf had the Thai roast pork - both were excellent! They garnished the duck with jalapeno which was surprisingly a GREAT touch. Fries were a little on the salty side but they still managed to be unique and tasty. Service and atmosphere were great; got a nice rustic feel and it was comfortable to sit outside on the sidewalk:  for those who aren't familiar with the Pennsport neighborhood, it has a Queen Village feel without the traffic (both cars and people) and parking hassles, rendering it a perfect neighborhood for this type of place. They have a fantastic beer and liquor selection, as well. Highly recommend folks check it out.

I love this place. I have been going here since my first summer job back in the 80s. There is always quality food. I have never had a bad meal here.

If you going for lunch - head over a little early to beat the crowds but even when its mobbed thing move pretty quickly.

It's possible that I spent an afternoon here sampling cheesesteaks, pretzels, Amish baked goods, and ice cream. It's also possible that I was by myself and almost missed a flight back to London while waiting for a fresh batch of cheese-stuffed pretzel bites to come out of the oven. 

Oh, the thin line between pathetic and devoted...

A gem in the heart of Philadelphia! Find everything, from organic produce, local honey, Amish poultry or eggs, the freshest seafood and fish, superb meats. And that's only for the market part; you find such varied foods that you travel instantly to far away lands, or stay home with the best Philly cheese steaks! Sweet tooth no problem! Even wine tasting with real baguette and stinky cheese is possible, like in Paris!  There is also some craft for unique presents.

I try to go to Reading Terminal whenever I have a free weekday afternoon.  At first this place can be incredibly overwhelming because it gets so crowded you can barley move.  This is a great place to visit with family because there is something that is bound to satisfy everyones tastes.  I wish they were open later because sometimes I want to stop by for dinner.  Parking near here is a nightmare so don't bother. Certain places aren't open on certain days (I went this past Monday and the Amish dealers were closed). My advice, pick a day later in the week and go when the lunch crowd dies down, making your trip less hectic with more options.

I love Reading Market! I've worked close by and always enjoy dropping by. They have pretty much everything you can imagine here, though it can get a little confusing and overwhelming to navigate the stalls, especially on weekends when there's a large crowd. 
I especially like the selection of fruits and vegetables (although it's a little pricier than at the supermarket) - you can find some unusual selections to experiment with at home, which is great. Boiler's Donuts is great too - definitely try out their selection of homemade donuts, they're delicious!
What's really lovely about the Market is that even after being here several times, you can still wander around and discover new things every time. I'd recommend coming here just to browse around for a while, you'll be surprised by what you find!

Loved this place.  It's a conglomeration of restaurants, groceries, and other merchandise under one roof.  We enjoyed walking through the merchant stalls to see what was being offered.  They had a butchers shop, fresh fruits and vegetables, a variety of restaurants, bakeries, candy store - you name it, they probably had it there.

We ate breakfast at the The Dutch Eating Place (an amish style eatery).  There was a line, so we figured it had to be good, right?  My husband had the blueberry pancake and turkey bacon special.  He got 2 blueberry pancakes that were as big as the dinner plate they were served on.  I had the 2 eggs with toast and scrapple.  I'm not sure I'm a scrapple fan, but I had to try it...  My husband and I shared our meals and couldn't eat it all!

I'd definitely recommend checking out the Reading Terminal Market and the Dutch Eating Place.

Potbelly Sandwich Shop should execute a solid meal at a reasonable price. 

I stopped by for lunch during a recent visit at HUP. This place is just a short walk over the skybridge from the hospital. The restaurant is clean with plenty of seating outside and limited seating inside. The only complaint I have on a restaurant logistics standpoint is that the restrooms are quite a trek away across Penn Tower.

The ordering experience is streamlined nicely. It works much like your typical national sandwich joint. Order, move down the line, and pick your toppings. Pro tip: if you order a whole pickle, the staff will announce it in unison. That was entertaining in and of itself. I ordered a sandwich, a whole pickle, and a coffee. That came out to $6.97. It can be difficult to go out to lunch for under $7 anymore. I think that price is more than fair. 

I would describe my food as okay. The coffee and the pickle were good, but the sandwich was underwhelming. I had the Skinny T-K-Y with a little bit of mayo, lettuce, and tomato on a multi-grain roll. My roll had a slight plastic taste, like it sat in a bag too long. The roll was also on the dry side. Otherwise, the sandwich was balanced as far as meat, cheese, and veggies go, but it really lacked flavor. It just didn't have that wow factor.

The last point I want to touch on is service. I have a hospitality background, so my expectations on service tend to be high. This place just lacked a certain fluidity that I believe is found in good service. The staff didn't always engage in an upbeat and positive manner, although they weren't negative either. They also didn't have a sense of guiding customers through the ordering process, which I believe is critical. Like the food, the service wasn't outstanding but was not awful either.

If you're looking for a quick meal that has good value in the HUP area, this restaurant is a safe choice. That said, I would rather explore the other options in the area for something more creative, tasty, and executed with more attention.

We came here during the Democratic national convention. It was packed with reporters and people this was on a weekday even then it wasn't too bad there was lots to see and lots to do plenty of room to walk around tables to sit and eat were hard to come by but we managed a family of four. I would recommend coming here without any type of bags or things to carry as you will just hit people walking past them lots of the stalls here take credit card as well as cash. There is plenty to eat and plenty to see and buy. You can buy fresh food fresh meat to cook, you can buy premade food, you can buy ice cream, fresh made donuts, Amish food, pretty much anything. Lots of the stalls offer goods that are you the handmade or Amish or of the Pennsylvania Dutch style. They do have some restaurants that are available to eat in. Things like an Amish diner I believe as well as other sitdown restaurants with bar stool type seating. A great place to come if you have a few hours to kill and you need fresh produce, groceries, meats, etc.

If I worked close by, I would be here everyday for lunch. They have everything in this market and plenty of delicious food! Having a lot of options can be a bad thing, but better than not having enough options, right?!

It definitely gets crowded, but rightly so. I mean people congregate to where there's good food...that's a given! If you love good food and people watching, you'll love the market!

There's a couple of places I'd like to try in here, but I get turned off so quickly by how crowded it is I get the heebiejeebies and then I run out. It's always the places I'm not interested in that I can walk right up. Hello ice cream! There's just never a time when I come in here and it's not crowded. It blows my mind. There's all kinds of crazy mofos lurking in that tunnel too.

I must say, the touristy business women are attractive.
This place was great! So many different things to choose from...cookies, meats, chocolates, honey, candles...just about everything! When in Philadelphia check this out!
I love taking out of town guests here--they love it and so do I. We've eaten at various spots over the years, bought fabulous meats and produce there, and picked up really special gifts.

Really like the concept of simple and fast Indian food in a to go wrap (the way I had it) or a platter.  Unfortunately, the roti wrap was on the smaller side and did not hold up well to the fillings (I had Chicken Masala), and there was not very much in the fillings, and the filling did not have much of the sauce, which is one of the best parts of Indian food.   Hopefully they will refine and improve the execution of the concept, as it is a really good concept that just needs improvement in how it is delivered.

Reading Terminal is good with tons of different foods to choose from! I do  think it is over priced & hard to find a place to eat during lunch times. Vegan options are limited. However, everyone in Philly needs to go here a few times. Watch out for the numerous pan handlers though!

A friend told me about this place, and I love it! It's a fabulous place for local food, gifts, daily items, etc. It's like an indoor open-air market, with fresh produce and homemade treats, as well as honey, candles, prepared foods, groceries, etc., etc., etc. Not on the typical tourist track, which is a great thing! Taste local, go here!

This is a fun place to visit. There is a good variety of merchants represented here (including Amish vendors). They even have a bar and wine tasting area inside the Market if you need to indulge. The food options are plentiful. You can also buy fresh cuts of meat and fresh fish.

I've decided to stop by here since it was the only place I saw by City Hall and glimpsed "McDonald's" in the distance. The restaurant looks extremely outdated, like it's stuck in the 1960's. It needs a major renovation and revamp. It didn't look very clean either, as some tables still had food left, napkins, etc. There were a lot of homeless and sketchy people here, hogging up the soda fountain. The best part was the cashier, she was extremely sweet and had a smile on. The burgers were made right, everything was good. Wifi worked fine as well.

What a place-I was actually surprised that it wasn't that enormous of a place, but that's good!  Prices at most places weren't bad at all, and it's well run, and very clean!

Walk around and experience the sights and smells of what is an eclectic and diverse food city.  From all of the treat shops to the produce market, it's tough to resist buying a few of everything.

The world's largest (debatable I'm sure) food court is how we described this to our boys, who are semi-adventurous for their ages.   One had a fish sandwich at Wan's, the other a cheesesteak and fries from By George, where to me the prepared Italian dishes looked quite appetizing.  Frank's has good ribs, cornbread...but their mac and cheese was the highlight.
Outdoor seating with dollar oysters at happy hour, great beers on tap, a huge seafood BLT sandwich with loads of fries. Wait staff was prompt and friendly. I'd definitely return!

This is just one of those very unique places in Philly that you must experience. If you are a foodie, prepare to spend some time here. They've got locally grown produce, Amish specialties, fresh flowers, meats, cheeses, desserts, and other foods you've been missing out on all your life. Reading terminal is rich in its' history as well as in its' food. 

Prepare to be over stimulated, it is usually filled with tourists and locals. Also, some of the places are CASH ONLY. Some of my favorite places to go are for their sweets. You must try Bassett's ice cream, Beiler's donuts, and Termini Bros (esp for their cannoli with choco chip cream cheese filling or cream cheese carrot cake!!)

FYI- there is $4 parking for 2 hours at 2 garages nearby if you spend $10 at the market (with merchant validation)

Will continue to shop/eat here!

I love to cook, I love to eat, I love to oggle fresh local produce and cuisines of all kinds... That's what makes Reading Terminal Market such an exciting place to visit. I can't imagine ever tiring of this joint.

 It can be quite a crowded scene at times, and almost overwhelming with so many merchants to check out, so many bites to try, but really that's what gets me kinda intoxicated about the trip- such vast variety and quality. I navigate through, I make the rounds, circling through a couple of times to make a plan before I finally make my purchases.

HIT UP: Tommy DiNic's for roast pork,
Salumeria (hoagies), The Rib Stand (boneless rib sandwich), Dutch Eating Place (Breakfast), Basic Four (Vegetarian), soooo many other places too.

 I particularly LOVE being able to frequent Reading Terminal Market with a bunch of people who don't mind sharing so that we can smorgasbord that mutha.

A Foodie central.  An over-eater's mecca. A chronic snacker's delight.

Reading Terminal satisfies one's every need, but only when it's not packed.  I just can't handle it here when I have to fight my way through the narrow paths between the stalls during busy lunches and mid-afternoons on the weekends.  So go, early on weekends, late afternoons during the week and you'll be (or I will) just fine.

Food from around the globe, whatever your heart desires, it's pretty certain you can get it here.  Pennsylvania Dutch  (Amish) food counters (are the tops and have the best bacon, sausage, meatstuffs what-have-you, jams, honey),  organic/free-roaming butchers, fish/seafood mongers, Specialty cheese shops, spices, gourmet sauces/marinades/oils/vinegars,  plenty of produce, desserts, so many eating stalls - a international variety , flower/plant shops;  they truly have everything.  

Be sure to stop at Dinic's (if you can weather the astronomically long lines) for your traditional roast pork sammie, Amish Lancaster Co. for freshly-squeezed Orange juice and canned goods, Metropolitan or Le Bus Bakery for bread, Old City Coffee for well, coffee; Flying Monkey Pattisserie for cupcakes, Famous 4th Street Cookie for well, cookies (only get them when they're freshly baked right out of the oven, you'll know), Bassett's for ice cream and Termini Brothers Bakery for cannolis.  Almost all the eateries that surround the proud sculptured pig are a sure bet.  Best yet, try it all for yourself - you're guaranteed to find a handful of places that will tantalize your taste buds.

Bring loads of big heavy-duty bags and patience. Get your parking (make sure you park at the lot on 12th at Cuthbert) validated for $4 by any of the vendors and shop, eat at your heart's content.  Menu plan for a few days. Go hungry.
Always a fun place to stop and look around! Great food!

my friend and I decided to have an impromptu sunday funday, which started at the industry. i was a bit hungover from the night before, so i had to be cautious about what food and drinks to order. we met aaron, the best bartender EVER, and he gave us some great recommendations. i got the mint choc chip doughnuts, which were unlike anything i've ever had before. delicious!!! my friend ordered the cannoli cupcakes and they were to die for! both meals absolutely amazing! then we took advantage of the $5 mimosa's. i was very slow to start drinking haha but they tasted SO good I got right back on the horse! aaron the bartender hooked us up and he was so nice and personable. we had a great time there and I'll definitely be back since I live in the neighborhood. we couldn't have asked for a better way to start our sunday funday! thanks!! i highly recommend this place to anyone in the south philly area!
Parmasian cheese as salad topping looks real but taste like plastic chips. Dressing is colored water with a some sugar and a hint of raspberry scent. Quinoa must be from last week.

Not accommodating...drove from Gladwyne to try because saw in Philly mag. Wouldn't serve me a drink and tonight is my 40th bday!! I didn't bring id because had a new purse?!  And haven't been carded in years. With my hubby who is 50? And we were ready to drink and eat up!! Their loss!

This is a foodie's HEAVEN! I repeat HEAVEN!
Fresh ingredients all around making everything taste a 100 times more delicious.

If you're not carb cutting, I say got get yourself a pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and extra sharp provolone from DINICS! This way, while you're waiting on line for BEILLER'S doughnuts, you have something to munch on! Their line can get pretty long, so avoid the crankiness and get yourself a sandwich! By the time you get to the front of their line you'll be in better shape to start pointing your fingers at all the yummy-goodness! I personally enjoyed the maple-bacon, apple fritter, and the cinnamon roll. IF YOU'RE GOING TO LISTEN TO ANYTHING ON THIS REVIEW... LISTEN TO THIS... Get yourself a DOZEN!

Took a day trip to Philly and had to stop by the market from reading all the reviews on Yelp. Reading Terminal Market definitely did not disappoint! Came here today which is the Saturday after Black Friday, was a bit crowded for our liking but it wasn't unexpected. We had parked near and visited the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall first then walked over for lunch. 

I would definitely grab a map to get a good lay out of the place. It can be overwhelming with so many stands! Food wise we ended up with:
- duck lo mein from Sang Kee Peking Duck 
- Philly cheesesteaks from Spataro's
- rib plate with mac and green beans from The Rib Stand
- strawberry lemonade from Jonathan Best Gourmet Grocer
- chocolate covered pretzels and strawberries from Chocolate by Mueller
- cheesecake from Termini Brothers Bakery
- whoopi pies from Flying Monkey Bakery

Wish we could have tried more things! This place reminds me of Pike's Place in Seattle a lil bit.
Essential Philadelphia culture and a good place to buy a Philadelphia-made gift to take home if you are visiting the city. Do not miss.

Reading Terminal is reputable for their marks in Philadelphia history. Reading Terminal has a variety of things from delicious diverse food cuisines to beautiful flowers in the season and different fabrics/textiles. Also a notable thing about this place is the multi-cultural exchnge as they allow different groups to perform from time to time. A definite must-see for any tourists or philly-native alike.

This is probably as close at it gets to those open markets you can usually find anywhere else in the world with a decent climate.  The best is just to walk around the labyrinth of stalls, sampling different foods and drink.  It is a good thing this place closes early, because I would imagine late night inebriated people would have a heyday at the terminal. 
There are a lot of Amish products sold here.  Definitely try the desserts and baked goods sold at Amish stalls. (I am sort of curious about how the whole Amish interaction with the bustling modern urban market works out.)
  This place could definitely be featured on an episode of Portlandia, as everything seems to be organic, environmentally-conscious, and a niche product.  But it is a great place to hang out in the afternoon, see a wealth of interesting tourists and locals, and sample the local grub.  Nothing is really that cheap here, it's like "Whole Foods pricing," but the quality is premium and with Philly flavor.  If you splurge a couple of dollars for a quarter pound of artesianal cheese, it's worth it for the atmosphere, and the feeling you get of buying fancy locally-made dairy products.
This place is so yummy and has food for everyone.  The market is enjoyed by tourists and locals alike.
An iconic place. Awesome food, traditionally Philly favs, vendors and just plain awesomeness. When coming to Center City you have to stop by here to eat...period!

RTM is one of the coolest places to visit in Philly.  It's a great melting pot of cuisines and people all smashed into a large building.  Lots of local purveyors and vendors with anything from sweet to savory for your to try and enjoy.  There's even a bar in the back to grab a beer and/or watch a game.  Some of the best cookies I've had (Hopes) are from Reading Terminal.  The (Pennsylvania Dutch) pastries and food are all excellent from various pickles to the great salads (seek out Turkey Salad.. AMAZING) to their fabolous baked goods; just be sure to go Tuesday through Saturday since they're not on premises Sunday/Monday.

This place can be described as foodie heaven. There's a lot to choose from and so much to see. Reading Terminal houses foods from all over. There's Cajun, Chinese, Thai, Indian, Italian, Soul food, Philly favorites, bakeries, fresh produce, the deli, even a bar! The best time to go is during the week. The convention center is right across the street so it can be a bit overwhelming on the weekend with all the tourists.

Love this market!  It's great and has every type of cuisine that one could ever want.  During lunch this place is packed with locals, convention goers and tourists.  It can be difficult to find seating.  However, worth taking the chance. 

Whether you need cheesesteaks, pizza, a hoagie, water ice, vegetarian dishes or dessert; this place has it all.  It is also a great place to pick up fresh produce, baked goods or meat.  It's a shame that more cities don't have places like Reading Terminal market!

A "must-see" to get the full Philly experience.  A market teeming with local vendors, you will have your pick of the litter when it comes to food options. Sandwiches, soups, baked goods, cheeses, fresh meats and seafood, produce, nuts, canned goods,  etc. There are places to sit and eat or you could just grab something to go.

honeygrow (temple U!): quick, accurate and delicious!

On 12/21/16, my company hosted our quarter meeting and needed a quick and easily customizable option (for a variety of tastes) for about 18 employees. We called honeygrow and they were beyond accommodating. They took my order through e-mail (made for an easier process for us) and were able to have the food ready at a specific time (a break-point in our long meeting). The food arrived hot, fresh and made to order correctly. They even use compost-able and recyclable utensils and serving dishes--a huge plus (and, necessity) for our company lunch! My co-workers loved the noodle dishes (Garlic Stir Fry was among the favorites) and the salads are delicious and filling--enough to make you forget you had just a salad for lunch (holiday cookies were abundant at this meeting). Overall a fantastic order and eating experience. Can't wait to use another 4-hr meeting as an excuse to vedge out on honeygrow!
Tons of options. I could eat here every day for the rest of my life and die a happy man.

This place is awesome! There are rows and rows of food vendors. You can get hot dogs, ribs, sandwiches, cookies, ice cream, and so much more. There are also a few storefronts to shop at for books, flowers, coffee, and spices. It gets really crowded though and it's definitely a little overwhelming. My friends and I had to walk around a few times before we could pick what to eat!

Stopped here for a "make your own" salad at 5pm on a Wednesday. They were low on salad- had one romaine and spring and organic. Got the romaine- added the fixings to make a Cesar salad (egg, shredded parm) and then was asked what dressing...said Cesar...they were all out and would not be getting anymore today. Felt terrible but ended up leaving without the salad- can't put ranch on a Cesar salad! Hope the service and selection improves in the future!

Favorite lunch spot in Philadelphia.  They have over 100 food vendors so a plethora of options for everyone.  From cheese steaks, gourmet cookies, Amish stands, multiple coffee stands, etc the Reading Terminal Market has something for all hungry travelers.

I really like the atmosphere here.  Recently I was here and had a great cup of soup and sandwich but it is pretty pricey and you can eat the same food at the actual restaurants represented in the market for much less money without the crown.  

Although expensive, if you have a lot of indecisive people or people who can not agree on what to eat, this is where to go, you can get anything you want and everyone can have a different type of food!  Great shops and specialty places are also here.
SUPER fun! A must for any tourist or new resident to the city.

An integral part of Philly - for tourists and residents alike. I love the fresh produce at the grocer and the Amish donuts! The stand w/ the beeswax candles and lip balm is also very reasonable w/ great products.

I love this place! I was at the convention center for a few days for a conference and was ecstatic to find out that the convention center was next to the Reading Terminal Market.  I pretty much spent all of my time between conference sessions wandering the stalls at Reading and looking at or eating a variety of all things food-related.  I was excited about the cookbook stall which had a decent selection of mainstream cookbooks, but the books were all so pristinely displayed that I was hesitant to thumb through them.  I was inappropriately enamored with the Amish food stalls, as I consider that type of thing to be "exotic" coming from California.  I wish I had had an opportunity to make good use of the produce, meats, fish, and cheese sold in the various markets. Overall, this is a great place to immerse yourself if you love food.

I love this place! I came here as a visitor first. Promised to myself I will be back the next chance I get. I moved here for a job and still love coming here! Hershel's deli is my go to sandwich - corned beef pastrami reuben. Possibly the best sandwich. Ever. I still come here once every 1-2months. It's just worth it. I bring all my visitors here too. You have to go and just explore. Definitely worth your time even as a visitor or a resident of Philadelphia.

Such a great Philly spot! I was able to go a few years ago for lunch and on my most recent trip stayed right next door. The place is always filled with people and the offerings are very diverse. We had ice cream, french fries, oysters, grilled cheese, cookies, craft beers, and a smoothie over the course of our trip. The great thing about the market is being able to find pretty much everything and anything you are looking for food-wise.

The shopping items are a little more limited, but still made for great browsing.

Only thing to be wary of - it is a very busy place. I saw a few parents with strollers looking like they were having a hard time and it took us quite a while to sit down to eat (there were three of us). It seems like during the day it is a pretty consistent level of busy, so be prepared for that!

I've eaten here before while waiting for a flight. Not bad food. But 5 minutes ago, I was in the restroom and followed one of their uniformed employees out. The guy never washed his hands,  just went back to the restaurant and to handling food. Last time I'll ever eat there.
I love this place! A little bit of everything for everyone, always!! Great environment and I don't mind the crowds either.

One of Philly's absolute must-go spots. Whether it's for fresh produce/meat/fish/herbs or for an amazing quick meal or treat from one of the many food vendors, it has something to satisfy everyone. Anytime family or friends are visiting from out of town, I always take them for a lunch at Reading Terminal Market and it never disappoints. One of my favorite things/places of the city!

Lots of great food at the reading terminal makert. Make sure to go early to get all the goods, I know I've went close to closing before and the Millers pretzels were all sold out and the Beillers donuts didn't have to many options left. Parking can be difficult on the street at times, but usually not to hard to find a spot. There is also parking garages located close by.

A must see if you're visiting - great foods and produce (di nick's roast beef obviously, ice cream and the pickle patch!) - cool atmosphere 

otherwise (if you live in philly) try to avoid this place during high traffic because it can be a nightmare.

A little torn here -while this was a really cool place, it was a bit chaotic for me. It's like a big, crazy grocery store -and then you continue walking and there are other shops too. For those in my hometown in Chicago, it is like the 26th Street Discount Mall -but higher quality goods and a lot more food.I did find a cool stand that sold all natural body lotions -it was called Herbiary. I think the chaos distracted us a bit from really looking around and taking advantage of everything it had to offer. I'm sure the beers the night before didn't help ;0).  So my advice would be to hit this place up early before it gets super crowded.  If we had not been as tired / hungry, this would have been a cool place to really do some shopping. I think we were just not prepared for how busy it was!

Love the hustle and bustle and the old world feel of so many vendors under one roof. The smells, the people watching, the variety of products and of course the amazing food make this an ideal place for lunch or to pick up some ingredients for a fresh dinner

There's nothing to hate about this place except their bathrooms. Love the variety of food options as well as that crazy market-place feel! If your not a crowd lover, and don't care to see some history, don't come here. 

PS - you've gotta feed the piglet!!!
The absolute coolest farmer's market in the world.  Makes Pike Place Market look like an touristo indoor shopping mall.

This is a great location to go to experience a little bit of everything. From delicious bakeries to meat markets reading terminal has a fantastic selection. There are tables available  to sit and eat or just enjoy the passerby-ers. They not only have a wide food selection but also a other nick-knacks and shops.

This was my first time going to the East Coast so I did not know what to expect. I did my research of things to do around the area and found this market. The atmosphere was very welcoming as soon as you walk in. Tons of desert areas around as well as comfort food. We stopped by for breakfast at the seafood place recommended by one of the advisors. It was a twist on breakfast (sea food ) but definitely good. If I had a reason to go back I definitely would but maybe on an empty stomach.

Overall it was one of the better places I saw in the airport, but it wasn't amazing. The salad greens were all fresh, the employees were all pretty friendly, and the prices seemed fair for an airport. My salad with organic greens cost $8.50 I think.

My complaint is that they vegetable toppings I received were super skimpy, but my salad was overwhelmed with the blue cheese I wanted. I mean, I love blue cheese and all, but isn't the cheese more expensive than some veggies (usually)? If so, why overload me with cheese when I want a salad.

I would go back though if I were in the airport in that terminal.

If you can make it at a not-super crowded time, it'll be much easier to move around. Even if it's crowded, take in the sites and smells of this place cause there's no other place like it in Philly! Don't forget to get some ice cream on the way out, too!

A must-see for both tourists and locals alike, with dozens of stands selling fresh produce and seafood, plus many others selling prepared food from a variety of cuisines. There's something for everybody, whether gourmet cheeses, Asian or Middle Eastern cuisine, cheesesteaks, or whoopie pies. 

Service at most stands is usually fast enough to accommodate the large crowds, and there's usually enough communal seating spread throughout the establishment so that you can enjoy a bite on the go. It's open early in the morning but does close fairly early (usually around 5-6pm), so come here for a smorgasbord brunch or lunch affair, or to pick up stuff to take home.

Can't go wrong love this place! Anything your hearts desire is waiting for you there. You are truly only limited by your imagination. Light, decadent, refreshing, wholesome, pure, organic, heavy, sinful, what is your pleasure? It's almost like the Hotel California. You can check in, but won't want to check out!

Great market in Central City Philly. So much food so little time. They have everything and then some. The food and goods is all fresh and local. Great spot for lunch if you can pick just one. The Amish kitchen is great for breakfast and the Amish fresh presses juice was fantastic and reasonably priced. Can't wait to go back and try something new.

I've been coming here my whole life, and I'm old. In some ways I liked it better in the old days. Pre convention center. It's still amazing but it's mostly lunch places and I always like it for my daily shopping. If you don't got at 8:00 am on the weekends don't bother . It's a nut house after 10:00. If you have out of town guests this is a must stop. And I do like lunch. It overwhelms me with so many great choices. I miss the old butcher shops like Harry Ochk's . It's Philly at it's goody best.

OMG so much food! I wouldn't do it justice in any length of a review. Just know you can't miss this if you're in Philly. Check out Yelp for individual recommendations on the storefronts within. I definitely wished we had checked this out sooner and gone here for more than one meal. After much deliberation and a bit of anxiety we decided on the juice bar, pork sandwich and a baked good.

NOTE: the Amish stores are, obviously, closed on Sundays!

This is an eclectic market filled with amazing smell of food and spices.  Just a wonderful place to be around, explore and taste.  It does have limits on their sitting, and it gets real busy, but a great place in philly to visit!
I don't recommend going here for a cheesesteak. Saltiest fries on the planet at By George. However many, many other food choices and cool place overall.

Love visiting this place whenever we have an event to go to in the city.  So many places to eat under one roof, but we always go to Dinic's for our usual Brisket sandwich.  No one makes it better than this place!

PLACE To walk by, it reminds me a taste of Barcelona for the market part. If you're hUngry tRy to know where you want to go before being there! The multiple foods turn your mind and you don't know where to head! And every thing looks good, from oysters to ice cream, shawarma sandwiches and beers....

What is there NOT to like about this amazing, vast and treat-filled space? Maybe that's there's too many choices. Boo hoo for me. Beautifully conceived, designed, layed out. Bright, cheerful and full of wonderous sights and smells. It would be amazing to go here when I'm in no rush at all... We even decided to stop here for lunch at our way back out of town only to find out they were closed on weeekdns.. much to our dissapointment...
Nice place; plenty of eats! Good prices. A bit crowded at lunch with tourists and PHL natives.

Love going here. The cheeses are phenomenal (Riehl's), the breads amazing, great ice cream and chocolates!! Don't settle down until you've walked through the entire place and had an opportunity to decide what to try, there are so many delicious choices! Once you've decided and ordered, sit and enjoy in the food area in the center at the back. Don't leave without going to the bakery and getting donuts for later! For me the drawbacks are the crowds (but, hey, it's a popular place!) and I wish there were more vendors of "craft" type items and not so much just food.

I was here on a weekday afternoon and it was absolutely packed with people.  Lots of different shops to look at and lots of places to eat.  I can't imagine what it would have been like on a weekend day.  

The only reason why I'm not giving it less than 5 stars is because it's in sore need of places to sit down and eat.  Lots of places to eat but then you have to stand up and eat if you can't find a rare place to sit.
So much fun to visit and so many amazing food choices. It is a must visit if you've never been to Philly.

Love all that the terminal has to offer... except I can't stand the crowds of tourists and convention center patrons on certain occasions. Also, I wish some of the vendors were open a little later past 5PM..

I went to Reading Terminal Market just to get sheep milk for my puppies. I'm not a big fan of overcrowded - pricey market. I don't know whats special about this place.. maybe I need to spend more time there...
Awesome place to visit!  Crepes at Profi's were the best!  We got pizza crepe and a pesto chicken and tomato.  Some many restaurants to pick from!!!
They have the best donuts especially the glazed strawberry filled donut ( recommended)

On my brief visit to Philadelphia this weekend, Reading Market was my homebase. It was my reference point when my internal compass failed, my shelter for when it was just too cold to walk and explore outside, and most importantly, my treasure cove of an incredible variety and expanse of more foods than my little brain could fathom. You can find anything and everything: the proclaimed best sandwich of the country, the freshest squeezed juices from locally grown fruits and vegetables, and amazing handmade donuts and other baked goods from the Pennsylvania Dutch (beware that their shops are closed on Sundays).  I think I discovered a new shop each time I visited in a corner I hadn't yet explored. Saturday was definitely the busiest and super packed of both locals and tourists; lots of human funnels in most, if not all the walkways between the maze of shops.  No words really are able to fully capture the unique experience of the Reading Market, and it's a great excuse to visit the city of Philadelphia, if the cheesesteaks do not convince you enough.
We love this place - the food is fresh - the ambiance is great - the service is outstanding and the beer choices on tap are ample.
Great selection and good variety of different foods and flavors. Highly recommend if you are in the center city area.

This market is so awesome. It was my first spot after checking into my hotel and I spent almost two hours exploring this amazing place. Upon entering the market, I was overcome by all the various shops. In every direction, it seemed never-ending. There was soul food, Chinese food, donuts, bakeries, fresh produce, fresh seafood, hoagies, cheesesteaks, crepes, etc. The list goes on! I had the intention of going to Tommy DiNic's for lunch. They're famous for their roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabé. The line wrapped around the entire counter and to the soul food seating area. Many other shops had long lines as well, with eager and hungry folks waiting for a bite to eat. 

There is something for everyone at this market. It's a blend of Farmers Markets with fresh fruits, vegetables, seafood, and meats to various shops that offer food to eat right there and then. It's enormous and often packed, especially on the weekends. If you wanted to, you could spend all day or all of your vacation at Reading Terminal Market. There's just so much to see and do. Absolutely recommend coming to Reading Market, if not for a bite to eat, at least to see it for yourself.

Reading Terminal Market really is such a fun place to check out and definitely worth visiting when in the city of Brotherly Love. I loved its convenient location and proximity to so many other city attractions (including the Greyhound bus station for those just here for the day) and with about 100 different vendors all under one roof, it's difficult to get bored. 

Looking to get your ice cream fix? Look no further than America's oldest ice cream company, Bassetts (I still dream about their strawberry ice cream). Wanna get the whoopie pie crowned the best of Philly? Flying Monkey is your stop. Have a craving for Thai food? Little Thai Market is what you're looking for. And the list goes on! 

Everyone that I met there was so friendly and helpful and coming from NYC, the land of the overpriced, I was often shocked by just how affordable things were. The one downside is that it closed so early (at 6pm) and I think it definitely is a place that would still be packed late into the evening. 

It is truly a haven for all things cooking, food, crafting, and so much more! So next time you're in Philly, definitely make sure you give this place a visit, you definitely won't be disappointed.
One can never go wrong at the reading terminal. A Philly institution that just gets better with age. Try the gyros,at Olympia they are very tasty

A must see on any visit to Philly.  Abundance of food choices from Asian, to French, to Mexican and more.  Awesome corned beef sandwiches.  Candy. Cheese.  Ice cream!    If you are at 30th street or Suburban, it just just a 5min train - they are running every 5-10mins.   Don't miss!
One of the most unique places I've ever been. Every city should have one of these! We ate there three times in a weekend. Must see in Philly!

I haven't been here in a while to shop for food, however, my mom often goes here to pick up spices. The food here is great and pretty diverse -- you can basically get anything here, from pastry to cheesesteak. It's kind of like an flee market, only with granite counters and cashiers.

The plain slice was super delicious. The special slice which had peppers and onions was even more delicious. I expected to encounter some artisanal douchiness, but thankfully there was none. Just friendly faces.

Great place to take visitors or stop in through the week for lunch. They have a huge selection of different food places, limited seating though and the close at like 5pm so its not a Dinner spot. Also when anything is at the Convention Center this place is packed and hard to walk around. But the food is good you can always take it to go.

Decisions decisions! So hard to choose a spot. There is a little of everything here. I saw Philly cheesesteaks, pork sandwiches, delis, local produce, hot pretzels, ice cream and so much more!! I tried the pork sandwich with provolone and sweet peppers at dinicks. It was a melt in your mouth kind of sandwich. Very impressed by the way the meat was done. The bread was fresh and had just the right texture... not too hard and not too soft. Be prepared to get messy, as this sandwich has ALOT of (tasty) juices that run. The sandwich totaled to $10 tax included. A little pricey if you ask me, but worth it. I also had Bassets ice cream. The flavors I got were coffee, chocolate, and moose tracks. Three scoops in a cup totaled $5 tax included. Decadent ice cream and so thick! Definitely satisfied my sweet tooth. I also had a hot pretzel... Forgot what the name was, but it was the only place serving hot pretzels. They were alright. Nothing special. A pretzel totaled $2.25 I believe. My reason for 4 stars and not 5 is that this place is SUPER crowded at rush hours. Hardly any place to move. It's an "on the go" kind of scene so don't expect to find restaurant kind of seating.
Great assembly of just about any type of food you could want! You could eat here three times a day for weeks and never get bored! Don't miss this wonderful place when your in town!
A great way to spend a day of shopping ad eating with some amazing Restraunt ,  butchers and bakery's there is somethings there for everyone

I love any kind of public market.The French Market in New Orleans, Pike Place Market in Seattle,  Farmer's Market in L.A., I've been to all of them. Reading Market is one of my favorites. It's right in the middle of  Center City, which makes it a very convenient place for tourists to pop into when they're checking out downtown Philly. (There's a broad range of places to eat.)  It's a good example of local color, what with the Amish vendors. And it has some unique features that give it a quirky charm all its own. I liked the old guy who played the piano for tips, for example. And the book stall. And the way market workers wheeled flats of produce right into the middle of the the crowded public areas. (A nice retro touch.) But I especially liked the beer bar set right in the middle of the market. Reading Market is prime people-watching territory, and it was a stroke of genius to put a bar in the middle of it-----the only thing better than people-watching is people-watching while imbibing a tall cold one.

One of my favorite places in the city. Great options for dinner and great options for dessert. Definitely a place I would bring people from out of town. Gets crowded and seating is scarce at times though.

I really liked this place. A little hard to enjoy as it was INSANELY PACKED, but I guess you can't blame other people for wanting to do the exact same thing as me. And I went on a Saturday. I definitely want to come here during the week to enjoy it a little further. But great selection of food, produce, sweets, etc. Quite the experience. But it was seriously so packed I do have to give it three stars.

How can you not love this place with all of the variety to choose from. You can go here with a group and everyone will find something and leave happy. Some of the markets are closed on Sunday and lunch hour is a madhouse.
Love this place. Bassetts ice cream is the best ice cream i'v ever had! Lunch time is crazy busy.

Awesome place a, definite to visit. Great smoked pork, philly steaks, choclates even cajun. Two great seafood markets aswell as meat markets. My boy picked up four giant porterhouses and they were delishous. They have organic produce to cheese and even candle making. Heck just visit it if your in Philly you will not be disappointed.

This is a good spot of you want a quick snack. Some items are overpriced, so you have to take your time to find the reasonably priced items. My wife tried the chicken salad with fresh fruit. The chicken salad had just enough mayo to hold it together, and was quite good. She added a pack of mayo to get it just right. The blueberries were hit or miss. Maybe they were out of season. All in all, we'd likely come here again.
OMG, they have everything! Love the food so much, they have a wide variety of all sorts of wonderful delights, that you can not find anywhere and everywhere. . I Love It. . .

I love everything about this market but wanted to give a shout out to the Pennsylvania General Store. They have THE BEST cookies in the entire place. Not that flying monkey crap stand or the one at the main entrance which sells the black and white cookies (which are decent).  Do yourself a favor and get cookies from this stand. You'll thank me.

One of the most amazing places in the country for foodies!! Hands down this market which I have been to 4 times now and have sampled many of the different restaurants within the market, and can confidently say they are all amazing! The level of authenticity and pure love for fresh produce and ingredients pours through the market. Cultures of every corner of the world are on display here, and the tastes go from exotic to comfort foods with just a few steps. Try everything here and go broke, it will be worth it, trust me.

Yesterday was my first visit to the Terminal market, and I enjoyed it. I've never been to anything like it. I like that there are so many different types of food in one place: Greek, Indian, Mexican, Cajun, Southern, Italian, and Chinese.

The first thing I had was gator gumbo from Beck's Cajun Cafe. It was their first day open, and although they were missing 1/2 of their menu, what I ordered was it was tasty.
Next, I ate a steak taco from the 12th Street Cantina. I wasn't too impress with the dish or the service.
Last, I stopped at LeBus Bakery for an assortment of pastries. So far, the only thing I've eaten is the dark chocolate chip cookie, and I enjoyed it. I think I'll eat the maple pecan scone next.

Anyway, I enjoyed seeing the fish and meat markets, the chocolate stores, and the natural store that sells raw honey.

I wanted to try the salad bar, but I keep thinking that the tongs are covered in germs (not everyone washes their hands you know).

I'll go back again. Hopefully next time, my parking validation will work. I had to pay $4 to get out of the deck.
A cornucopia of gastronomical delights, with special shoutouts to Miller's Twist, Original Turkey, and Beiler's Donuts. Good luck finding a place to sit between 11am and 2pm.
Literally the best place on earth. There is nothing like the Reading Terminal anywhere else in the country. You can entertain, grocery shop, and/or stuff your face. Seriously, you need to go here.
Love this place. Great variety. Book store is awesome. Try a cheesesteak or roast pork at Dominics

I am so jealous a place like this exists...nowhere near where I live! I knew it was like an open market kind of place but I loved it when I went inside. A bit busy (as expected) but so many different places to choose from! My husband, cousins, and I wandered around the place for a while before deciding on what food to get for an early lunch. Since I don't get much cajun food at home, I went with the rice and beans from the cajun counter and my husband got a breakfast po' boy. My cousins both got food from the Mexican place right around the corner. (Thankfully nobody minded us sitting in the same eating place, where we didn't all buy food from).

We also got some coffees from 2 different places whose lines looked long, but went very fast. I eyed lots of cookies and pastries but opted against it after my very filling rice and beans. If I lived or worked nearby, I'd probably go to this market all the time and try all different foods. Unfortunately the Dutch places aren't open on Sundays so we couldn't try those. Very cool, varied spot.

Now that I lead food tours, and several of the stops are in Reading Terminal Market, I have even more respect and appreciation for this market. Did you know that all the vendors in here are completely local? They have to be in order to even be allowed to sell their food in here. Also, there really is a complete selection of everything from Dinic's roast pork sandwiches (which make me want to quit being a vegetarian when I look at these overflowing meat sandwiches, complete with greens and cheese on a soft roll, just oozing deliciousness), to the best pretzels EVER at Miller's Twist (pretzels that are dipped in butter and are soft and flavorful) , to fresh cookies at Famous Fourth Street cookies... it's incredible. Fresh produce, fresh cheese, fresh meats, fresh hoagies, fresh cheesesteaks, fresh fresh fresh...and with about 80 vendors total, you have a huge selection of choices of cuisine. Oh, and there's a cute bookstore, too, along with some Amish specialty shops, and the "Spice Terminal," if you want more than just food. 

And! One thing that's really awesome is that Reading Terminal Market has recycling containers for plastic bottles everywhere, so you can bring your bottles here to get recycled. 

I am in love with this place. It can definitely be overwhelming, especially on the weekends around lunchtime, but totally worth it. And the smells are amazing of all the freshly cooked, homemade, local food. Yum.

We come out to Philly every year for a tattoo convention and this market is right across the street. I wait all year for Dutch corner omg! Best pretzels ever and I buy all their dried beans and jams and candies.
This is an absolute must if you are in Philadelphia. There are many great places to eat as well as go shopping for cheeses and meats. There also is a bar in the back to grab a quick beer.

Food is great. The cauliflower grits and devilish eggs were great. Fast fresh and heathy, i have a busy week he'd be didn't have time to prep my meals. This was a great alternative. I will be going back and I downloaded the app
