Awesome place for anyone that loves food or people watching...but only if you don't mind a crowd! I've been here various times over the years and it's always bustling.

Dinic's roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe is a must, but if the line is too long, any of the other food stands offer great, quick grub.

Wonderful place for produce, meats, olives, even wine. The seafood stand is one of my favorites - large selection, fresh, fairly reasonable prices.

I love coming here to eat and check out all of the different vendors.


Its like walking thru a big kitchen with so many things to eat.  The hard part is picking one, the prices are right too.
Like my review is gonna make a difference ;) Outstanding and delicious.

Pros: you can find almost any kinda farmers food here. Meats seafood candies wine you name it. Some are cheap like the Dutch breakfast area, some are expensive like little amounts of whatever delicacy they make.

Cons: smells funny, looks weird and crowded, you can get lost, no areas to sit to eat, you can lose your stuff here
Awesome to go for great food. Every time someone comes to visit me in Philly I have to take them here and they love it!!! So many amazing options to choose from that its almost overwhelming!

I went to Keven Parkers at RTM! I cannot say enough about how delicious and plentiful the food was. The little side seating area could use a spruce up. The beverages are delicious! I was satisfied with my meal!

It's alright here there's a lot of good food and the variety is actually amazing but the reason why I take a star off is that it always gives me the sh*ts and these sh*ts follow me for weeks for some reason. It's like a curse on my tummy that reading terminal market bequeefs upon me after my dining experience
It needs a  personality treatment and major renovations. Historic doesn't and shouldn't mean horrific.

I love Reading Terminal Market!  It reminds me of the Mercado San Miguel in Madrid. Upon entering the market, my senses immediately came alive from the wonderful smells, and all of the different foods. The only difficult part is deciding where to eat. My daughter and I enjoyed a gyro at Olympia Gyro and it was certainly among the best gyro I have had!
Just wander and have fun and spend money on all the cool stuff, most so much cheaper than anywhere else.

We don't "do" fast food - but when you have a 2-4 year old and need a play-room this is a great choice.  Our daughter gets a 4 nugget kids meal with fruit (instead of fries) and lowfat milk.  Then she plays - sometimes for a whole HOUR in the play room.

A great break for mom & dad.  Cheap.  Not too nutritionally horrible.  (But we don't come more than every 2 weeks.)

However, recently our daughter discovered that they serve Lemonade.  Our lowfat Milk days are numbered.

NOTE:  Recently (May 2009) the play area has gotten stickier and dirtier.  It needs a good floor to ceiling cleaning.

I came here on a nice Sunday afternoon. My friends have been there before and it was my first time. It reminds me of being in Chelsea Market, but with a much better section of produce and places to eat. I was sad to see that most of the shops were closed on Sundays or opened at a later time. 

From fresh produce, meats and seafood. You have lots of choices. If you are craving something good to eat. You have choices of Chinese, Mexican, Cajan and even Middle Eastern Food at this place. It's cooked right in front of you and you can sit right there and relax. It's definitely worth going to again whenever i'm back in town.

This is a great place to go and grab lunch.  There are a large variety of options and most of the food there is very good.  Prices are also reasonable.  The downside is that everyone knows this is a great place to grab lunch so it can be uncomfortably crowded and it may be hard to get a seat to eat.
Awesome place to shop especially if your a foodie but I wish the prices where more reasonable and not priced for the tourist.

LOVE this place.  Tons of options, culture and good food. Whenever I have visitors, I take them here.  Only criticism is that it can be very crowded at times, to the point where it is difficult to get around.  Long lines tend to go quickly though, so still worth it - just try to find a down time.

I almost skipped this because some places I had read about are closed on Sundays. It's so huge that I didn't even notice what was closed. This place is AMAZING and I was sad I only had one meal here. I think the only thing that would make it better is if the vendors would sell smaller portions so you can try more things. We split sandwiches at Dinic's and Meltkraft. Bought some goodies from The Tubby Olive and tried desserts from the Flying Monkey and Termini Bros. Everything was SO good. Pick up a map when you come in if there is any where specific you want to go otherwise you'll get completely distracted...not that it's a bad thing here.

This place is absolutely bananas!  They have every possible type of vendor you can imagine and plus it's in the heart of the city.  A true Philly institution!  If you have never been to Philly or just visit every so often, the Reading Terminal Market is a MUST STOP!

Valley Shepard Creamery has wonderful fresh mozzarella and roasted tomato sandwiches. I swear there was a pound of cheese on my sammy. This place is just wonderful. We went on a Sunday, and although some places were indeed closed, there was still more than enough going on to slightly overwhelm me.  The high star rating this place has is well deserved.

One of the first places I recommend for any out of town visitor who likes to eat.

It's only gotten better in recent months with the addition of Valley Shepherd Creamery, Beiler's doughnuts and Border Springs Lamb.

Even though I've moved out of walking distance, it's at least a weekly stop for me to pick up produce at Iovine Brothers, who do great (and very well-priced) fruit and vegetable trays.
Always love stopping by the Reading Terminal Market.  Check out the yummy German food kiosk:)
This restaurant is new renovated clean and pretty bright environment for lunch and dinner!!! P.S. Thanks for the medium mocha frappe today on April fool.
Fast. Fresh. Delicious. Like Chipotle for salads and bowls. A bit overwhelming for first timer but Kimchi-Wa bowl was great. Summer hours 11-3.

An absolute treasure!  It's iconic, it's full of great food, it's a tourist mecca - you simply have to go there if you visit Philly.  Though it's open on Sundays (when we went), about 25% of the stores are closed (in particular the Penn-Dutch stores, but some others as well).  An absolutely wonderful place to shop for fresh meat, fish, vegetables, and OMG the CHEESE stores are amazing. There is plenty of cooked food available to eat on the spot too - pork sandwiches, cheesesteaks, vegetarian Indian, Chinese, soul food, crepes, and a load more. Yummy Bassett's ice cream too! Parking downtown can be super expensive - about $14 for an hour in the lot across the street, so take public transport or shop around!
Has a huge variety of vendors and variety of food. Seating place is hard to find, so take it to go.  I would highly recommend this place

From organic meats and fruits and vegetables, to chocolate, to gyros, to roasted duck, to pizza, to ice cream, to fresh fish and seafood, to homemade bakery awesomeness, the Reading Terminal Market is a one-stop shopping food mega mart.  They also have flowers, cooking utensils, handmade soaps, cookbooks, and other stuff in this huge facility.

If there is a large convention next door at the Convention Center, be prepared for huge crowds inside, but it is worth the effort to get through the throngs to whatever you're looking for.  The Amish are not there Sunday through Tuesday, and they are a big part of the Market.

Went here with my father.  We tried various vegetarian items from them plethora of vendors that are available here.  

Forget the food (which was delicious btw), if you are in Philly check this place out- even just for people watching lol.  We had a great time and felt good to check off visiting such a historical place.
Amazing market. Great environment and energy. Something for everyone!
Awesome space. Get the Dinics roast pork sandwich, 4th street cookie, bissets ice cream and a flying monkey whoopie.

This is a Philly must. It has an amazing array of places to eat as well as many places to buy great food and cooking ingredients. The olive oil shop at the back is an interesting place even if you're not interested in buying anything I'd recommend going there just to taste the various combinations of olive oil and balsamic vinegars - odds are you'll end up buying something. 

While many places are really good, if you like your meat you have to try out Hershel's Deli. Go to the sitting area in the middle of the market and you'll see it. It has an absolutely amazing set of sandwiches with perfectly made meat that'll send you straight into a food coma. Enjoy.

Great market to go to when you're around philly. Pretty much any kind of food can be found here. The grocery in the market seems to sell good quality meat and produce. This place is definitely not a bad option to look around for breakfast. The Omish donuts are well known here and shouldn't disappoint any donut lovers.

This is a food mecca of all things Philadelphia does great.There are a wide variety of amazing places to eat as well as some of the freshest quality produce. I personally recommend DiNic's, Beck's Cajun Cafe, Hershel's, Wurst Haus Shmitz, and Molly Malloy's. Go Early morning or late afternoon because the lunch rush is a mad house! Saturdays and Holidays are the same but it is a great experience.

How could a huge, indoor food-stall market get any better than Reading Terminal Market? I'm not sure it could. 

Full of many different local Pennsylvanian offerings, I could hardly contain my excitement when we walked into the market - especially in the Amish corner! Awesome, awesome place that no one who is even remotely into food should miss when visiting Philadelphia.

This place is amazing for foodies.  There are types of foods for every palate during every time of day.  I have taken family members every time they have come to visit to experience what is Reading Terminal Market.  Some times there are long lines but usually well worth it.  My wife loves the pickles and honey that we pick up while at the market to take home.

It's been over a month since I've made it home, and I'm still having dreams about his spectacular market. Everything in Reading (pronounced Redding) Terminal is fantastic. I wish I had a market like this close to home. How many markets are there where multiple establishments make the food network and travel channel?

From breakfast to lunch to dinner, you could barely tear me away from this place when I was at a conference in downtown Philly. I may sell everything I own and just take up a warm spot next to the doors. People would bring me their leftovers, right? What more could I ever need?
There's lots of great food and a wide variety of souvenirs at Reading Terminal Market. The crepes - every morning.

Amazing selection of food, you can pick up prepared food, or take it home and cook it. Lots of other items, too, though the variety of food is enough for all in your party to find something they like. Fun to just stroll.

Great place.  It's a great tourist and resident spot.  It's quite possibly the only place in Philly where you can get a taste of EVERYTHING available from a food standpoint: Chinese, Soul Food, Baked Goods, Fresh Meats, Ice Cream, Cheese Steaks.  It has it all...

I can get really really crowded, but if you can navigate it, it's worth the hustle and bustle...

Philadelphia always offers exceptional experiences. 
I love going to farmer market, so there is no way that I could miss my chance to visit the renown Reading Terminal Market. It turned out to be one of the most lovable place I've been to in Philly. I went "wow" when I stepped inside because how large and crowded it was. I am a small town girl, so it was the biggest market I've been to. 
They have so much delicious food and beautiful crafts and arts. The vendors are incredibly approachable; I still regret to not having tried the famous donuts place because they had a long waiting line. Anyhow, I enjoy some beef jerky and delicious meal (at a vendor I can't remember). I also got some fresh vegetable and grapes to go. I wish I could spend more time there.

I'm a huge fan of urban markets no matter what city it is.  I love to explore these places.  I haven't hit up all the vendors yet, but I'm working on it.  I'll admit that I don't live far from the Reading Terminal and didn't start taking advantage of it until recently.  It's a great place to go for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.  They have a little bit of everything.  At least for me, there's always something to satisfy my taste buds.  

The real benefit to me is all the fresh stuff you can find here.  The produce is great and reasonably priced.  I also like the butchered meats and the cheeses that are offered here.  You can't do your grocery shopping here but it's always nice to get stuff from the locals.  Then there are the desserts.  I have a bit of a sweet tooth so I love to indulge when I come here.  

Fun place to always go.  Everyone should experience it at least once.

This is a must do for anyone visiting Philadelphia.  An incredible assortment of food options and just a fun place to be (if you like crowds!)  Our group had a very eclectic array of choices ranging from the Philly Cheese Steak eater, to Chinese, to an incredible Italian sub.  For desert we all picked a selection of candies from Chocolat.  Great fun and perfect for the travelling family that can't agree on a lunch spot!

Tons to choose from! Lines are crazy so don't go there starving because you will have to wait but definitely bring your appetite. Stop and get a map so you can navigate easier through the shops. Bathrooms are clean.

Awesome experience...It took me 40 mins to decide to figure out what to order ... Place is a perfect outing on a Saturday afternoon where you'll eat a nice lunch and wrap up direct from the farmers groceries! Loved it ...highly recommend!
This place is so big! I want to find the flying monkey brownies.  the places we went to were ok - I liked the one cookie place a lot.  I would like to go back and take some more time to explore.

I absolutely love Reading. You will never ever be disappointed in your visit. Granted, weekends can be quite crowded and hectic, but it is a fun time to people watch. 

The best part is, there is something for everybody, every time you visit. Food, flowers, ice cream, chocolate, baked goods, smoothies, shopping...you name it, and it's probably at Reading.  I've tried quite a few places inside, but two I need to highlight. First, (I'm sorry but I don't know the name of it) the place right across from Bassett's ice cream is a little food place that has phenomenal smoothies. It isn't a generic smoothie that you get from a frozen packet or machine. Nope, real, tasty pure fresh fruit smooth. So good. Second. Beiler's bakery. Woah. I don't even like donuts. This place has thee best donuts and much much more. I recommend the blueberry fritter. No joke they are probably the size of my head and are only $1. More importantly they are beyond addicting. They practically melt in your mouth. 

I love you Reading but you sure can ruin a girl's healthy eating kick.

Went here with a large party for late night snacks and drinks this past winter, it was great.  It was a Saturday night and it wasn't overly crowded like most other south philly establishments.  Solid, tasty food.  Also went during the day for brunch with my 1 year old son, they were very accommodating and friendly.
The dark chocolate covered pretzels are good and the Amish pickles can't be beat.  Great place to spend a few hours looking and trying food.

Go to Bassetts for ice cream and the juice bar for fresh squeezed juice. Everything else was mediocre. They do have a nice Christmas village display complete with awesome looking trains during the winter holiday. In my opinion, that's the best part.

Really cute market that is worth a visit!  Huge variety of prepared food to choose from, including Chinese, Indian, Middle Eastern, Italian, and deli foods, plus multiple dessert options and a grocery.  Reasonable prices and lots of seating area, although we went during an off time when it wasn't too crowded.

Reading Terminal Market is a must stop when you got to Philly. 

Love at first site and tastes...

I love this place so much! RTM is a great place to spend an afternoon just wandering around, grabbing food and shopping for knick-knacks. 

A personal favorite would have to be the used books corner. Always something fun in there.

Let me be frank; I absolutely love the Reading Terminal Market. LOVE IT. It's without a doubt my favorite place to go on the weekends. It can be overwhelming being there are so many choices to eat, to shop, etc. If you can't find something you like here then there's something wrong with you.

Not only is it a great place to eat but to shop too; there are vendors that sell products other than food. 

A warning; it can get extremely crowded on weekends. Crowded as in shoulder to shoulder (the lines for the vendors can get very long, Beiler's Donuts being one of them). If you're a tad claustrophobic, like myself, it can be a little overwhelming. But worth a trip!

Fun place to visit, whether I will actually shop here is a different question. Like any other market, watch out for the tourist traps, have fun but be judicious. I agree with other reviewers saying that it is a much better market than Grand Central in NYC. A must-visit if you are in Philly for a visit, and even if you live there.

Reading Terminal Market...when we will we see each other again... I cannot get over your variety of tastes, color and smell! 1st taste was that famous roast pork sandwich at DiNic's.......after I saw the portly guy from Man vs Food inhale one. What about dessert....dried meats...bread....fresh fruits and veggies...and beer. I can easily spend the whole day here and have all my 6 meals covered, plus grocery too.

Came here with a friend on the fly before a movie and honestly not much to report about this place. We were seated at the long communal table in the center of the restaurant to avoid waiting (we didn't have a reservation). I had a catfish sammie special and my friend had the fried chicken sammie. Both of our meals were enjoyable enough and the service was pleasant but overall I wasn't impressed. The one thing that surprised me about this place was the number of children present in the restaurant - I counted 9, which seems a lot for a place centered around alcohol.

I will probably have to give this place another go (mostly for beer selection), but for now I'll put it in the 'satisfactory' column.
Reading terminal has an abundance of choices. Fresh produce is quality and dirt cheap. The seafood and PA Dutch spots are always a tasty choice. It can get a little crowded but it is well worth it.
So many stores and a huge variety of different types of food.  Beiler's, Dinic's and Bassett's are just some of the great shops here.  I only wish it was open later, normally closes at 6pm.

Anything you are looking for is probably at the Terminal. Fresh produce, chocolate, meats, cake, specialty coffee, hot sauces, fabrics, jewelry. It's all there. Shop, have lunch, shop some more. Expect crowds and lines. And to buy more things than you planned on buying.

Stopped in after getting a groupon a few week before the new year. I had a minor incident with my meal then but boy was I NOT disappointed when i gave them another go round seeing they were covering my meal. 
The staff are a delight. This time a young lady took my order and she was super pumped to tell us(the boyfriend came this time) they have $1 dumplings on that particular night. And my eyes lit up! I didn't really wanna take advantage of their kindness but i mean these dumplings are killer. I got just about all the signature dumplings and an order of the cheesesteak pasta. That pasta tho. I had no idea such a creation existed. Now to top off everything else they have an in house honey bbq sauce(among other flavors spicy on top of that) and i mean i almost used a hell of a lot and it is almost too good. suspiciously good. I asked the young person if they sold it by the bottle and i got a "not yet" and i'm still smiling.
i know you are wondering why i didn't give them 4 stars outright, i had a one time mistake experience. therefore i will have to go back many more times before i outright denounce this place. It's always wise to give them a try yourself. :) happy eating!

Such a fun trip to take -- we always take the train and head down for cannolis at Termani's and the best brisket sandwiches at Nick's.  It's a bit touristy, but there are more people there doing their weekly shopping than tourists.  It's always crowded and very hard to find a seat, but there's a reason for that -- the food is great at so many of the places!
best priced (and fresh!) produce in the city

Huge market! Honestly the biggest I've seen compared to some in LA and Toronto I've been to this one beats them all. Lots of all sorts of options to choose from and each of them are equally tasty.  I had a full meal for only 7 dollars so honestly you can find some great food at a low price or you could go for other pricer options but definitely tons to choose from.

My husband likes this place and that's the only reason I eat here. It is completely overpriced!!! $24 freaking dollars for 2 burritos and 2 small sodas. That's ridiculous!!!! My chicken burrito had a piece of bone in it that I almost chipped my tooth and chocked on. I can and have made better burritos in my own kitchen. They need to turn the music down. They have the music so loud you can barely hear the girls when they ask you questions. I do not go here willingly nor do I recommend it. The only positive thing I can say is that their portions are generous. I'd rather go next door to Popeyes. It would be a hell of a lot cheaper and I'd be more satisfied.

Wish they sold little rooms in the Reading Terminal Market that you could just rent out for a month, and come back as a healthier version of yourself.

This review is for those who haven't visited the Reading Terminal Market yet.

If you've already been there... you'd know..

You walk inside the market expecting to find what you're looking for and exit. But as you stepped in, you've just embarked on an amazing journey to a magical land... Okay maybe I'm getting off topic. But it's only because I genuinely love this place.

The Reading Terminal Market has been my inspiration to get back to my Persian roots, by cooking some delicious Iranian cuisine. You can literally find any ingredient you're looking for, AND I MEAN ANYTHING, and it is the freshest!! (To all the Iranians out there, this place is fantastic to find ingredients for Ghormeh Sabzi  .)

Aside from the fact that you can find the tastiest organic product from any vegetables and herbs, to meats and fish, the energy in there is really remarkable. Friendly faces all around greeting you to try free samples, or even some times learn more about what they have to offer.
I cannot believe how many different vendors are densly packed into this building. Flying Monkey (pastry shop) was awesome.
It is touristy as hell but there are a ton of good food options. Great to bring out of town friends there, you can see some Amish folk with out being dragged out yet again to Lancaster County.

Reading Terminal Market is packed with culture:  great food, great music and fantastic people.  It's pretty incredible to walk in here and see lines and lines of people waiting at almost every counter.  It's only a few minutes away from the city center and is a great place to try a little bit of everything!

Ice cream and the Philly Cheese Steak... thats why I went and it was awesome!

As some people have said, you can come here for lunch everyday for the whole year and never eat the same meal twice.  It's accurate! 

You'll love the live music -- it's definitely so refreshing!

I love the atmosphere of this place, it has just about anything you may be looking for and targets just about everyone. Looking for fresh produce to a specialty from another country? Looking for the worlds oldest operating ice cream parlor, take a visit to the Reading Terminal Market, they have it all!

Thanks to TripAdvisor and my gf's predilection for getting the '#1' of places we went here. I was expecting another crowded tourist trap selling overpriced stuff that I'm sure locals would get for cheaper at a farmer's market. Well, yes and no and I was happily surprised. Yes, there are crowds, yes there are some pretty touristy things but there's a lot of good food and deals to be found. Despite the push of the holiday crowd it was a pretty good experience and walked away with some good eats and finds. The cider and the cheap donuts makes it good, Smucker's beef jerk and bacon make it great.

LOVE reading terminal. Love Iovine's produce, the butchers and fish markets. I come here for all of the grocery items I can get. The amish bakeries are amazing and the diner inside is phenomenal. Worth the trip.

Reading Terminal Market is pretty big and it kinda feels like walking around in a big maze. You'll see some places selling Philly cheesesteak (obviously), fresh seafood, homemade pastries, homemade chocolates, and many more!!! I recommend walking around the market first before deciding on what to eat and also having a friend to help reserve a table since this place is a tourist spot and it can get very crowded.

The places that I tried so-far:
1) Tommy DiNic's- I had the roast pork with broccoli rabe. It was OK, but nothing memorable.
2) Spataro's Cheesesteaks- I had cheesesteak with mushrooms. I also ordered the tater tots. Both were good.
3) Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagies- I had the classic cheesesteak. There's saute onions, mushrooms, cheese wiz, and peppers (i.e. sweet or hot). I really like the sandwich and it's so flavorful! I also got the coleslaw. It was good but there was too much mayo. I'll comeback here again for sure.

Be sure to put Reading Terminal Market on your list when visiting Philly. Come here for breakfast, lunch, or an early dinner.

Great selection. Immediately on coming in you see all the produce you would expect from Farmers market but then there are tons of little restaurant counters. Got a pizza slice from one place and carrot-banana smoothie from other. Good quality for affordable price and had a place to sit and eat.

Love this place! Anything you could want, you can pretty much get it here.  Really cheap and diverse produce in the back right corner.  If you can't find what you're looking for, ask one of the people who work there and they'll help you find it or give you a good alternative.  They're pretty knowledgeable.  The only downside of this place is it gets crowded on weekends and at lunch time.  It's pretty difficult to find a table if you're trying to eat lunch there.  Definitely worth checking out though!

I wish I was there now!  This was one of our favorite stops on our trip to Philly.  I think we ate here like 3 times in 3 days.  Huge selection of food types.  Everyone will find something they like.
Find the cannolis.  The best I've ever had BY FAR!

Omg. Where has this place been all my life. Best quick lunch or dinner anywhere on campus - unlimited veggies, delicious sauces (I combine black bean and garlic yogurt), and reasonable prices! The food is always so fresh and filling and the staff are friendly and fun. Juices are healthy and delicious too I work across the street at HUP and we now finally have somewhere good to go for lunch!! Omnomnom

Reading Terminal is one of a kind.  Its rare for indoor markets to be this large and contain such a VARIETY of ethnic booths and food...in fact, it can be delightfully overwhelming at times.  You can ALWAYS find something you want at RT and i dont care who you are or what you like.  Support the friendly businesses tho, alot of rude lazy people at some of them.

This place was so much fun. I wish I could eat more! Had the best grilled cheese here and the ice cream from Bassetts was so creamy. The philly cheesesteak from George's wasn't that great because of the bread they used. I've only been to Philly once but maybe best to try a cheesesteak outside of the Terminal Market? Also, I can't believe I missed that this market has the best Fried Chicken according to Food Network at Keven Parker Soul Food. Gotta try it next time I am in town!

I love this place!! I am a huge fan of markets and this place a variety of stalls and small shops and bakeries. It was my first time coming here and I would definitely come here again. There are a lot of hidden food spots that I feel I've yet to discover. 

Reading Terminal Market is a mixture of a farmers market and a supermarket. There are flower shops, bakeries, grocery stalls, food stalls, drinks, and other knick knacks. I actually came here to meet up with some old high-school friends and it was the perfect spot. We came here around 3:00pm on a Friday afternoon; I saw high school students, college students, couples, kids and parents...this place is great for everyone! My friends and I were able to walk around and enjoy the different stores, get a drink, buy food,  sit down and eat, shop, etc. Reading Market is definitely a nice tourist spot and there are some very interesting things to see...and taste! For example, there is one stall that sells chocolate-covered onions. Not that its my sort of taste, but it isn't something you see everyday at your typical supermarket.

I'm sure there are a lot of people during noon time and dinner time, but it was not very crowded when I went during mid-afternoon. Definitely recommend coming here - whether to hang out or to visit as a tourist spot!

Well it is an interesting place and the hot pork sandwiches were yummy but it clearly lacked the flair of many urban regional markets as well as the variety of food stuffs. I would rate this as a good place for lunch but otherwise a tourist trap.

One of the very best public markets anywhere. 

Lots of great options for breakfast, lunch, casual dinner or just food to take with you.

If I could put together a perfect market that includes every single cuisine I love in one place, it would be Reading Market! Everything from Mexican, Greek, ice cream, books, produce, meats, Chinese, etc. Only drawbacks is that it can get crowded and there isn't much seating.
I would highly recommend getting an Italian sub from Salumeria. High quality meats, great ratio of all ingredients for a good price. 
Explore and enjoy!
Tons of variety! You really can't go wrong, but I love Beck's Cajun Cafe and Wan's Seafood. Go explore yourself and find a place to fall in love with! :-)

Years of silent prayers to the Chipotle gods have been answered.

There's finally a store in Northeast Philly! And apparently I'm not the only one with an undying love affair with Chipotle. There's literally a line to the door all day and every day since their grand opening. Service has been a tad slower than I'd want but it's expected from a new place. But the employees have been very respectful and friendly.

You cannot go wrong with anything you order here. I usually alternate between a burrito or a rice bowl depending if I have extra calories to spare that day. The food here is worth the wait evident by the hordes of people going in and out here daily.

Tip- Download the Chipotle app and order your food in advance to avoid the lines! =)

Very reasonably priced and tasty food - I'm glad I stumbled upon this place!

Masala Kitchen offers two types of dishes - Kati rolls and platters.

Anatomy of a Kati roll: Some form of protein/paneer/vegetable paired with crispy onions, wrapped in a layer of egg (if you choose for 50 cents) and a thin roti (made fresh!). I tried the chicken masala roll, and while it was not quite as photogenic as some of the Yelp pics suggest, it was still tasty! The makhani sauce was rich and creamy, and the onions were quite sweet. For $5.50, I found it to be a bargain, and filling enough if you aren't too starved.

The platters are basically a variation of chicken over rice - I tried the MK' special, which had a lot of flavor, was really spicy (even without adding hot sauce!), and again, very filling. They also give you a TON, good enough for two meals, so again well worth the price. Overall, I'd say it matches the quality of some of the better chicken-n-rice joints in NYC.

Other tips:
-Open late (until 3:30 AM) on fridays and saturdays
-they have self-serve hot sauce and white sauce dispensers if you need any more.

Loved this place!! Saw it on Food Network, and wandered past it today, so I stopped in for a quick light lunch. 

the 8 oz. serving of lobster bisque had more lobster than some lobster rolls I've had in my home state of MA!! Will be trying the lobster roll touted on TV ASAP

One of a kind market with anything you could possibly want from Amish food, cheesesteaks, Roast pork from Dinics or salad from Ms. Tootsie's. Also I don't know the name of the Amish place but they sell great beef sticks. The place to go if no one knows what they want to eAt. Also Termini Bros Bakery is the best- separate review for them
This my first time at this Chick-fil-A. It's pretty clean and chills. Better then going all the way downtown to the other one.

The food choices here are very good BUT every single thing is served in plastic or styrofoam :( EVERYTHING!!! There are NO "here" cups/plates/utensils. It's absolutely ridiculous!! Even when eating at a counter there, the only choice/s are styrofoam plates - not even paper!! 

When I mentioned this to the workers and patrons most did not care one bit. When I explained that every piece of plastic or styrofoam will eventually end up in the stomach of a sea animal they made fun of me and called me a hippie.

I find it interesting that if someone cares about the environment and the wildlife and not themselves, they are the "bad guy". I should be more narcissistic like them? It's a sad commentary on our society if you ask me - not that anyone is asking me...

Hershel's East Side Deli has great food, it's where I ate the most. The people who work there are really nice and agreed with me re: the plastic and styrofoam. There is also a freshly squeezed juice bar but sadly if you order a large (32 ounces) they give it to you in a styrofoam cup which kept me from returning.

Overall I'd have to say I wouldn't go back to the Reading Terminal Market - the environment is just too important to this altruistic tree hugging hippie.
Nice place with feeling, commerse and want to spend money feeling! Go here and get hungry, as I did!

Probably one of the best fast food places I've ever been. The staff is very friendly, its fast, clean, and the prices are really good. I love the waffle fries with the lemonade that has free refills.

I'm not a big fan of what Chick - Fil- A does politically but I love their food.

This place is without peer.  The varied food choices are dizzying and it's smart to go in a group to maximise your choices! While many will (justifiably) mention De Nic's broccoli rahb sandwich I prefer their meatball sub (a hidden gem). I never miss an Italian hoagie at Salumaria's (with extra hots and artichoke). All washed down with a 4th street cookie and some bassetts ice cream!

It's always a great time at RTM, I would like to see a stronger effort to alert customers to gluten free and veg options (maybe a star on the map?) . Sometimes it's hard to find a clean table, but busy is good! Great people watching.

I love this place... too many choices though!  All are top notch and legit.  DiNic's Brisket is an incredible sandwich.  Bring back the beer garden vibe.  The restaurant is ok, but I loved the fact that I used to be able to have a beer with whatever food I brought in with me.  I took away a star because that change spoiled (but didn't ruin) the spirit of the RTM.

Foodies paradise.  They have everything in there.  My faves are Beiller's, Hope's cookies in the Pennsylvania gen store, Bassetts Ice cream, Dutch eating place and tommy dinics.

Sad that the Smuckers place was closed on the sunday we went bc my hubby really wanted to take home some since we don't live in Philly anymore.  

I do think that some stuff can be a little overpriced, but the Amish food is the best buy esp for the type of food and price.  Their doughnuts are amazing and only 95 cents.

Also a little disappointed that there weren't a lot of fruits in the produce stores.  we were hoping to get some honeycrisp apples.  We did get champagne mangoes though.

Overall, I highly recommend this place even if you don't want food.  they have candles, books, houseware stuff.

Ok ok....Philly can be proud on this market. It is on par with San Francisco's Ferry Building Farmer's Market or Toronto's St. Lawrence Market. Legitmately numerous food options that satisfy the foodie and don't hurt the pocket book. Unfortunately I went on a Monday and the Amish section (based on reviews is great) is only open from Wed-Sat. 
The places that looked busy included Sang Kee Peking House (Chinese), Franks (BBQ), Thai place, Delilah's (Southern) and some Italian specialty place. Hard to decide, but I was hungry and settled on Delilah's (Oprah's favorite mac and cheese). Platter with two sides, $9.75, full meal and tasty. Great place to pursue and grab a tasty lunch with friends. Nothing too fancy and if you're a local, probably a great place to grab some meats and specialty items. Worth the lunch stop when in Philly.

Absolutely love reading terminal, absolutely hate the crowds. If your visiting don't go on the weekend if you can avoid it, it's way better off weekend and not during peak lunch time. An incredible amount of food vendors serving up some of the best food philly has to offer.

This place was recommended by a colleague and I went while walking around Philly with a friend. So many choices and the movement of people during lunch was impressive. There are bakeries, coffee shops, ethnic markets, restaurants, and more! We went at Pearl's Oyster Bar because they had seating. I had a kale salad and the fish tacos. The salad had a delicious flavor combination while the tacos were hearty and delightful. The waiter tried to discourage me from over ordering but it was all well worth the filling! I can't wait to go back to Philadelphia to try another one of the eating choices here!

As a tourist, I have to say I was underwhelmed.  The market was crazy crowded.  There was no place to sit. You had to wait in super long lines for food.  It was hard to find anything.

Yes, there's a lot of variety.  Yes, the food I had was great and I found some knick-knacks in the shops, but it was a stressful visit and I felt very claustrophobic.

Had I gone without kids, I think it might've been slightly better.

Reading terminal is an awesome place.  The restaurants and take out counters are great and there is something for everyone.  The Produce sections are unbeatable when it comes to price in center city.  The only reason it is getting 4 stars instead of 5 is it's a little tough to navigate until you get the hang of it.

Great service..but they need to have a bigger burger.  

Overall - love the place.  It has a great cozy feel -- good for hanging out and getting drinks as well as for dinner on date night.  Mixed drinks are strong - just the way i like it.

and it's close to the movie theater - makes it easy to grab a quick bite in between movies
I've been coming here my whole life. They offer a wide variety of prepared food, baked goods, and produce. It can get quite packed on the weekends, but it's worth braving the crowd.

The RTM is a great place to go for lunch, but it's not exactly the most amazing food that you will find in Philadelphia. Sure there is a lot of it under one roof, but I can name 3 places for crepes that are much better than the stand at the RTM. 

Yes, the Amish stand is good. And Foster's has sweet spatualas. But overall, the place seems grimy, sweaty, and congested. 

Check it out once. That's all you'll need.

Over the years I have naturally enjoyed the market to get a quick bite, grab some produce, or feed my sweet tooth. There are days where I walk in and can freely roam exploring what new items are in. Other days I get to see the excitement of tourist and locals "excusing" their way to a vendor in order to feed their bellies. I personally like the quieter times which is after lunch. 
Lines move quickly although and all the vendors have great service. The downside is that some vendors are overpriced but, overall it's the place to go. 

My favorite spot is the Dutch Eating Place. Great food and great service. When I worked down the street, their Turkey sandwich with gravy was my go to! Walk a little further and you can pick up Delish Hope's cookies at the Pennsylvania General Store.

Talk about a cultural melting pot of food, shopping and people watching, RTM has it all. I still haven't eaten at every establishment in there, but trust me, I'm working on it!

If you like to eat, do a little shopping a people watch, this is the place to be!

I'm in love with this place! It was my first time today and it was wonderful it's lie a little village on the inside. It's really crowded though so be careful button the upside it has a little so helping you find the shops you're looking for. Definitely get some pickles while you're there!!
Like you died and went to food heaven. Go! This is Philadelphia all the way. The people watching the variety it is a must.

Tried the chicken and rice platter, Achari Chicken Roll, and Aloo Paneer Roll. The rolls were good but Chicken and Rice Platter was incredible. Will definitely be back. Also tried Kala Khatta drink, which was mediocre. A lot sweeter than expected.

Wish I would have come to this place first instead of wasting my time and money going to Geno's (yuck). The Reading Market had everything and then some. The sub sandwiches were super yummy, I think I ate two within an hour (don't tell my wife she thinks that I only ate one, lol) 
The bakeries were yes, yes, and yes. I had some kind of Carmel pecan cheesecake that was so good that I almost called home to Houston and told my boss that I quit cause I am moving to philly!
I will for sure be eating at this place a few more times before we head back to Houston.

Foodies version of the Pearly Gates

If you're in Philly and you bypass this place, your making one HELL of a mistake! I loved this place so much that I'm flying across the Pacific ocean and the continent just to sit in this marketplace to enjoy an amazing Dutch breakfast prepared by an Amish family, have an amazing roast pork with broccoli rabe sandwich for lunch from Dinnick's, and go crazy with trying to figure out where to have your final meal of the day from the plethora of food booths before they close the market for the day.

...And yes Lisa, you were right. It's St. Peter, not St. Gabriel, that guards the gates into heaven. Forgive me.
I'm vegan.  There's like 3 things to eat there.  It's OK if you are starving, but mostly a GAG-FEST if you don't want to eat body parts of excretions.

Dining mecca or tourist trap? Ummm... five stars for both! My friend and I came here on a quest for a hangover cure... as we walked in, we were instantly floored by the sweet aroma of freshly baked cinnamon buns and made a mental note to return after we ate substantial food. Only moments later, we found ourselves reaching for a fresh pretzel... unreal! A few free samples later, and we decided that nothing cures a hangover like Thai food. For $5.50 each, we got a generous helping of spicy shrimp curry (amazingly flavorful and spicy!) and veggie pad thai (honestly, the veggie pad thai didn't do it for me - not moist enough). For another $2, we were gulping the very best shrimp tom yum soup. It was partly sticker shock from non-NYC prices and partly the outrageously flavorful food... but I'm hooked on Reading Terminal Market! On the way out, we picked up a whoopie pie and a cinnamon bun from the Amish bakery... both very good, but not quite as surprising as the pretzel. If I lived next door to this place, I'd be a very happy (and fat!) girl. You need a few hours to wander around... and several meals to appreciate the wonders!
So many places to eat and so much shopping to do!  We popped in to escape the rain and ended up staying for most of the day. If you're in the Philly area I recommend stopping by!
Food is pretty good however it can be pricey depending on the type of meal that you choose but it is well worth it on an occasional basis.

Part farmer's market, deli, and specialty food store all rolled into one!  Amish vendors are a bonus.  They are there Wednesday through Saturday and make great pickles.  

Lots of food to try. I was here on business and it is right near the convention center.  It was great to pick some fresh fruit to bring back to the hotel for a healthy snack.  

The ambiance is great.  It does get crowded at lunch time but that is to be expected.  

My only negative is that they use lots of disposable items: utensils and plates and that they don't appear to compost.  Composting would be a natural fit here and could serve community gardens.
So many options! I love this place. Anything from fresh produce to a shoe shine. The eateries are wonderful, especially Herschel's deli
Loved it here. Wish my tummy had more space to to more food and drinks. Would definitely come back and recommend to others visiting the area

This place is awesome! So many foods to try.

What I had:

Tony Dinic's - roast pork with provolone and broccoli rabe and roast beef with provolone and broccoli rabe. This was okay, prefer roast pork over the roast beef though.

Beiler's donut - strawberry filled and apple fritters - pretty okay, better than the donut chains.

Kamal's peach, strawberry, and guava - very refreshing!

Miller's Twist, sausage in a pretzel and cheesesteak in a pretzel - Not a fan of the sausage in a pretzel. I would say the cheesesteak pretzel was one of my favorite's at the Market. 

Bassett's Ice Cream - Pistachio and green tea were so fresh! 

I will certainly be back to try everything else.
Yes! As good as everyone says. Lines are long at the hot spots but they move fast. Whoopie pies at the Flying Monkey are incredible- get one!

Greatest place in University City. Way to go Penn!! 
Great staff and Gazpacho is off the hook.

A huge variety of food places, basically a giant food court. It can get annoying on busy days since it's sometimes hard to walk around when there's a lot of people there, but the wait and bustle is worth the different cuisines they have to offer here. Love stopping by Beillers on the way out for some donuts.

Holy Toledo! There are waaaaay too many food choices here. And when you're belly is grumbling it's hard to choose. There are plenty of tables where you can chill and eat. FYI, some of these restaurants do not accept credit cards. Have a stash of cash just in case. From what I saw:

-Seafood market
-Southern Jambalaya
-Sweets bakery
-Po Boys
-Sushi/Japanese
-Sandwiches
-Ice cream and fruit smoothies

And I'm sure there's more. I walked that thing twice over before I choose jambalaya and friend mac and cheese balls for my dinner. Prices are pretty average. you may be paying $10-$15/person depending on what you choose to eat and drink. 

This market is not the quietest or cleanest I've ever experienced but just having the selection made it enjoyable.
Great place to check out if your visiting the Philly area.  Lots to explore and great fun to try.  Will definitely come again.

RTM is a local essential that keeps getting infiltrated by tourists.  Yes,  the apple fritters from Beilers, the roast pork and provolone with broccoli rabe, cannoli from Termini Bros, and ice cream from Basset's is worth the wait,  but could if you could wait in an orderly queue that doesn't block me from getting trimmed to order pork shoulder from Giunta's, or raw milk from Lancaster Dairy, or wonton roast duck at Sang Kee, I would be rather grateful.

Was so looking forward to coming here, but disappointed to see the scaffolding blocking the main sign. Weak! :(

Overall, it was just too crowded...

It's so clean and new here! Much nicer on the inside than the McDonalds that's right next door. 
Sadly, that's the only good thing I have to say. To be fair I don't eat a lot of fast food and this was my first trip to this Wendy's so maybe it was an off day? I ordered a cheap 6 piece nugget and one of the $1.29 burgers. Both of these things were already prepared but I spent 14 minutes waited it on my FAST food because a woman came in to give the female workers a Christmas card (they started immediately squealing THERES MONEY IN HERE!!) - I guess she was a regular? Idk. And then a girl that ordered her already prepared fast food well after me got her stuff first because she was yakking to the girl worker with the messed up teeth. Again to be fair that girl has a fun personality and I'm sure she's a blast to work with but as a customer who expects to be in and out, but Is forced to wait -what I consider an excessive amount of time for food that simply needed to be pulled out of a drawer - bc your job is your social time?? No thanks Wendy's! I'd be expecting more from such a new place. Manager on the computer playing around in the office.. smh. Not sure what I expected but it wasn't this.

Love love loveeee The Reading Terminal! There's so much diversity and so many different foods to try. From Bassetts Icecream, hamburgers and fries to Chinese food. Something is bound to catch your eye and it's a great place to explore!

My goodness where do I start. 

No literally, where do I start. Upon walking in and finding this not-so-secret market, I was immediately in sensory overload, so many lights, people, SO MANY SMELLS. It'd take me literally a week to try every stand in this market. 

So we came in at about 4:45pm and many stands were closing already. Tried Dinic's roasted pork sandwich and it was just average. not that moist and peppers didn't add much to the flavor. 

Also tried the last donuts at Beiler's and they were okay. Wish I could've stayed longer to try the other places but so far it looks like the restaurants in the greater Philly metro might be better. This place is mostly touristy hype.
This place has everything! It's not open very late at night though. They have groceries but the prepared foods is really where it's at. It gets super crowded on the weekend!
Food heaven.  Whatever you want to eat now or whatever ingredient you need, you can get it here.

Just go! Old city coffee best in the city.   Get a pound of old city blend you won't regret it. And of course a hot apple fritter on the Amish people are  in town. The first place you should bring any visiting tourist to. Just go and enjoy everything it has to offer. If you can go during the off hours that's a very good idea because it can get very busy.

Never again. I ordered through ubereats , I got a burger,  cheesesteak , a side of yams and a side of Mac & cheese. My total was about $24. It didn't take as long as I expected but I got no napkins & no fork or spoon to eat my sides.. The cheesesteak was horrible, it taste bad like the meat was old or something. My boyfriend liked his burger , or at least didn't complain about it. The yams was okay but they looked suspect. And the Mac & cheese wasn't classic Mac & cheese. All The extra ingredients made it taste much worse. Sorry I won't be back.
Best food in philly all in one place! so many food vendors and not enough tummy space to sample them all! It was crowded but every place i went was worth the wait. This is a must see/do in Philly!
Yasss, easily the best option if you want to 'eat your way around Philly' without worrying about actually leaving one place.

I have been to this location multiple times previously and had good service. On this occasion I had a legitimate coupon for a free sandwich with no expiration date. When I tried to use the coupon the manager told they had "discontinued that program a year ago", whatever that means. When I told him that I had used a similar coupon in "that program" about a month ago, he basically called me a liar.  
To me it's not even about the food but the principle. If you are going issue a coupon with no expiration date you should honor it not demean the customer. 
I always admired their company values and business model, no longer

This place is overrated.  There are better indoor markets elsewhere with higher quality food and more variety - e.g., SF Ferry Building, Boston Quincy Market, Seattle Pike Place Market.  We got an okay cheesesteak from Spataro, a warm apple dumpling from a PA Dutch place, and a cone from the ice cream shop.

The Reading Terminal Market is absolutely fantastic!!  Pretty much all of your cooking needs can be found here, and it is high quality, fresh, and delicious!  Meats, fish, poultry, spices, cheeses, produce, baked goods, even books - this place has it all.  I always hated grocery shopping, but I love the experience of coming to this market to get all my ingredients.
There are a great variety of places (from crepes to fried clams to Thai to beer) to get breakfast or lunch while you're there as well.  
One of my favorite stands is actually an Amish stand that sells fresh-squeezed juices.  The blends are incredibly tasty without the overly sweetened and processed taste of your usual juices.  I recommend the orange lemonade!

One word. LOVE. This is my happy place. You can't go wrong with so many of the gems housed under one roof. Everyone loves DeNics. No doubt. Roast Pork is amazing and they get the hype, but you can't go wrong with Martin's for meat, the Amish counter for breakfast. Molly's for a beer. I could go one and on.

I absolutely love this place! My partner and I just moved to Philly and we usually come every weekend. The market has a little of everything. We pick up our produce and do a little shopping, as well as try out the many restaurants the market has to offer. My personal favorite so far is Smuckers. Their fish & chips are so delicious. And the cheese fries. Also enjoy the candy shops and even the butcher. Definitely a fun place to go!
Lots to choose from. Favorites include coffee & cannoli from termini bros & any gyro from olympia gyro!
great place for food.only problem is its too big..u get filled up by the time u find what u want, i guess thats a good problem. dinics the best spot in there tho

I love the market! It's a must-visit for out of town guests, and I frequently stop by for my grocery needs as a regular ol' Philadelphian. When you go, check out Beiler's Doughnuts, ruining healthy diets since whenever they were established. Those 95 cent apple fritter's will be the death of me! And I'll die happily!

If you're in Philly, a trip to the Reading Terminal Market is an absolute must.  There are endless food vendors/various markets, and truly something for everyone here.  On the weekends it gets crowded but it's worth the trip that's for sure.  My personal favorites here are Dinic's for roast pork sandwiches and Bassett's for delicious creamy ice cream.  I can't wait to make a trip back here soon.
Must visit amazing foods thruout the place cannot complain left with Bellys full and two bags of goodies

I ordered the combo fried giant squid and my boyfriend ordered the combo samurai crispy chicken. It came in a cute, bento style, to-go box and it comes with an assortment of different sides, like - radish, cucumber, cabbage, and seaweed salad. The sides were a great balance with the fried squid/chicken because it can be a little bit too heavy and greasy. When you choose combo, you can either pick fries, rice, or minced meat (minced meat comes with rice so its a win win if you want both.) 

For my side, I chose fries - not the best fries I've had. It did not look appealing at all. McDonald's fries are better than this place  I would definitely pick rice or minced meat next time I go. That being said, the squid was not bad! Not super crispy, just a little bit of crunch. It did not have much flavor so the soy sauce helped. I also wish it was super hot but it was warm. Still not that bad. I just personally love my food burning hot. I tried my boyfriends chicken and it was decently crispy and very flavorful. It was a little bit dry. I think if they cooked it longer, it will definitely be dryer. His chicken tasted like it was straight out of the fryer because it was nice and hot! 

Overall, I will come back here and get the chicken and the drink! A couple things to know before you go here, seats are very limited and its cash only but they have a atm inside.
So much variety and culture! So many options! So many great smells! Eat there then order other things for later, and while you're at it do some of your grocery shopping. Not to be missed.

New place.  Young staff.  Could use a bit more experience with English only customers but they're trying and polite.  The food was a decent value.  I had the sliced giant squid meal.  I should've take a pic but I was very hungry. I'll come back to see if other menu items are good too

Always a great place to go for some good food! I always enjoy bringing tourists there for lunch, with all the different choices available. It can be hard to find seating, but with so many great choices, including DiNic's pork sandwiches and Sang Kee, it's hard to go wrong!
Really great sandwiches. The sandwiches look kind of small but don't be fooled...they will fill you up. It's a great place to grab a quick and tasty lunch. The employees are always pleasant.

Great place to eat almost anything, but terrible seating.  Favorite is Greek near the west wall. and ice cream along the wall.  Amish Breakfast cool.  Lots of ethnic cow and pig choices.   Maybe with embedded Sushi Roll.

Need to put clones of this along the Turnpike.

Awesome market.

Nestled away off of 4th street, lies Reading Terminal Market. What looks like a massive grocery store from the front is actually a large market of food places of an assortment of differing kinds of food, ranging from Asian, middle eastern, even to Amish! (there were in fact, a lot of Amish food).

Although the ventilation was horrible in this place, the idea of this market reminded me a lot of Quincy Market of Boston.. just a much larger grander scale. You could easily find breakfast, lunch, and dinner in here, without a problem.

If you're looking for a place where everyone's tastes can be satisified, as well as looking for a hole in the wall place in Philly, definitely go to the Reading Terminal. It's famous- I even spoke to a Food Network show which was filming a segment on the Flying Monkey cupcakes in there.... how cool is that.
The turkey samich place is mmmm....drool worthy!

Must see place in Philadelphia even if you don't plan to eat. 
SOO many options of everything!! A lot of tastes (seafood, coffee, sandwich,...). 
I miss we don't have a place like this in the DC area.
We had a cheesesteak sandwich that tasted great but don't expect cheap places over there.  We came back for breakfast the next day and had a great omelet on an "amish style" stand.

Reading Terminal Market is absolutely amazing!! There is all sorts of food--colorful produce, fresh-baked breads, fat sandwiches, bomb ice cream flavors. There's so much to see and eat; the hard part is deciding...and probably finding a seat. I'd definitely recommend checking this place out!

If I had to choose a McDonald's (and unless I'm so desperate, let's hope it never comes to this), then this is the one I would go to. This was my McD's growing up and as scary as it may sound, I've seen some of the same people for the last 5-10 years working here. Those are the ones who will give you the best service, it seems. For others, it may just be a temporary thing, so you may not get the best.

A lot of the McD's have gotten upgrades so that they look similar to the one near CAPA. When this location got rid of most of the booths (which were frequently inhabited by the seniors), it began to look a lot more empty because of the extra space. The booths in the center were replaced by higher stools and small tables. At least it didn't look as dingy anymore.

I never liked the new "habitrail" feel of the Play Place that took over about 10 or so years ago. Growing up, we had an AWESOME play place. Grimace, Hamburglar themed attractions.

There is metered street parking on Broad and the surrounding areas. It is conveniently located near a bank, 2 pharmacies, a dollar store, and public transportation. Southern is also nearby so don't be surprised seeing this place crawling with kids.
Lots of food, to choose form on Wend, Thurs, Fri and Saturday.

Don't do it. A friend and I came here last week to get some happy hour food and drinks and I was excited about the dollar oysters. I ordered 6 of them to start and my friend got 3 mac and cheese croquette things (they were also $1 each). When the oysters came out, they were so small it was comical. It wasn't the shells that were small, so it can look confusing, but the amount of actual oyster was a joke. I don't know what kind they were, but they really shouldn't serve them. Those oysters aren't meant to be served... Anyways, let's go next to the mac and cheese croquettes. These things were so bland and flavorless! I was given half of one and took one bite, not finishing the rest. I wish they would have put salt and pepper on the table, but I guess I'm glad they didn't because I would have had to drown it in S&P to give it some flavor. We thought maybe these two items just weren't good because they were cheap and happy hour things, so we decided to get a few other things. Big mistake. We ordered the sweet pea dumplings and a side of their sweet potato, brussel sprout, and bacon hash. The first thing I noticed was that the sweet pea dumplings were EXTREMELY small for the price ($9) and you only got four of them. I thought to myself that they better be damn good for that price. I first took a bite of the veggie hash, and was absolutely appalled. How do you ruin vegetables and bacon!? You drown it in disgusting spices, that's how. One bite and I immediately knew I was sending it back. Next we tried the dumplings. Thinking about it now, I don't know how I thought sweet peas inside of a savory dumpling would be a good idea. It was just weird. The sauce it came in was like an asian dumpling sauce...and sweet peas DO NOT pair well, flavor-wise, with asian flavors. I don't know who came up with this idea, and who taste-tested it and thought "mmm that's good", but they need to have their taste buds checked. We sent everything back and got dinner elsewhere. 

Everything else on the menu had a weird asian-flavored theme. I don't get it. What are you trying to do? Be edgy or something? Just serve food!

As for the drinks, I got a glass of happy hour wine (which was a very very small glass...even for the price) and my friend got the weird bloody mary thing with tomato water instead of tomato juice. I thought it was okay, but could understand why she hated it.

First time here...we've been wanting to come for a while and tonight the stars aligned...very attractive decor...I had my go to drink...an old fashioned...the variations on these are to numerous to count...but this one is probably the closest to the recipe I've had...none of the ingredients overwhelmed, very tasty...kudos to the bartender for that...wife and I split the cheese platter...all the cheeses were tasty, the marmalade went well and the french(?) bread was charred nicely...then the long awaited hamburger came...cooked perfectly...I don't think I've had a burger that good before...made me want more! The side of fries were tasty...reminded me of McDonald fries...but better...and I mean that in the absolute nicest way! Perhaps the one word to describe the industry...is balance...all the ingredients were well balanced...none drowned out the other...and all you were left with was one good bite after another...bravo!

So I gained three pounds over two days.

Not only are there forever food options, most of the food or snacks you try are just fantastic and made with serious thought and consideration for your darling taste buds. 

I feel deep sadness and regret for the people I see going into the Wawa nearby. Why?! Why would you deny yourself the magnificent oral and olfactory adventure that is the terminal. This place is especially awesome if you and your friend(s) don't want the same thing. Break for 10 minutes while you surveil the area and pick a meeting location for your subsequent feast. Try it at least once.

Awesome place to eat while downtown. You won't eat the same thing twice here. So many merchants and restaurants,there's something for everyone. Including a beer garden after a rough day. The place is clean,the food is great. 
But if you're there for lunch,get there a little earlier. It gets crowded fast and seating may be difficult to find. But that's because of its popularity. 
I recommend the Terminal when down town.

There's a lot to eat and see. If you're going for the doughnuts at Beiler's prepare for a wait as that line builds up quickly. Go find the little old Greek ladies and get their Dolmades (grape leaves).

Boyfriend and I were catching a wrestling show up in Philly and we decided to come here before the show. It's amazing and there's so much to take in, truly it's incredible. I recommend trying the ice cream place, the southern cooking place (with their watermelon iced tea!!!) And Fox something for corndogs, my apologies for not remembering their names!
The Reading Terminal Market is my absolute favorite place to shop! They have a wide variety of items and the food is to die for!

Yes a must visit! so many options to choose from. It is packed with a lot of visitors and prices are a bit high however it's a nice place to grab food and find a table to have lunch. Good option if your here with a party so everyone can get what they want. 

The tables are cafeteria style and they have disinfectant for you to clean your area. It does get busy so when you find a table take it.

A must see, a unique experience unlike any other of so many local establishments of all sorts crammed into a miniature city. However I found it more difficult than expected to locate various vegetarian options and the density of pedestrian traffic is a little overwhelming sometimes.
Wow!  So much to see, do, and eat!  A lovely way to spend an afternoon~  Great place for a date :D
A must-visit place in Philly. Tons of food options and great shops to buy unique knick knacks. You have to go more than once because there's just too much to choose from.

This place is crowd, noisy, aromatic, and I just love it. So many food to pick, and everything is so worth it. I think I can spend the whole day here but then my stomach would not be very happy with me, neither would my wallet.

This location is POPPIN. I opted for CFA while I was at IKEA, needing something fast in the middle of lugging furniture around. The line was nearly out the door, but they really busted through it. The customer service is really awesome here and you can tell that they are used to the volume of people that hits it. I don't find the food to be anything too special, but it is something I hit once in awhile. Waffle fries and cookies. That's all I need.

What a great find in Philly. The market had so much stuff to try and everything looked great. We ended up picking Tommy DiNic's due to it's fame and we're glad we did. If I lived in Philly, I'd definitely come here often.

So many great shops and restaurants. If you can't find something you like here then just give up. The Mexican restaurant, the one bakery (monkey something? - maybe), and the Bassats ice cream are a personal favorite.

This is a must-do for visiting Philly. This is a one stop shop for fresh fruit & vegetables, fresh baked breads, meats and fish, coffee, locally grown/raised foods, unique and specialty foods, flowers --you name it. There are also a couple of restaurants as well as tables to eat your "to-go" sandwiches and other treats. Since it is entirely indoors, it is great for a cold day and my son loves running up and down the aisles. We always find some new exotic food item to try. It is also really easy to get here by train ;-) If you drive, the garage is is $4 for 2 hours if you spend $10 or more in the market and get your ticket validated.

Came on a Saturday that an event was happening at the Convention Center and it was PACKED!! Unfortunately that forced me to get in and get out but I was very pleased to see the selection of vendors the market houses! I got some delishhh Mexican food and some sweets from Flying Monkey! All in all its a cool shopping place. I will be back!

I would be off the charts in giving stars! LOVE this place. Seriously. The amount of choices are insane - favorites are Termini Bros. for italian pastries that are to die for. Also DiNick's - the roasted pork sandwich is HUGE, a good price and tasty. I like sitting at the counter and eating amongst everyone else. Coffee...the seafood...smells....just an amazing must see experience!

Went here today to try it out for the first time looking for something healthy to eat. I was angry standing in line and the girl skipped over me and went to someone else for their order. I moved up in line and was told i need to order first before going to the register i said i know she skipped over us and didnt take our order. 
So i waited a minute then a nice gentleman that works there apologized and took my order that made me a little happier. I ordered a bowl with steak lettuce pinto beans and brown rice food was edible but not worth the price sad to say every bite of the steak was chewy and fatty. Very disappointed and will not return to this place in the future. Not worth it.

Food here was fine.  That's about all I can say.  Prices are reasonable and you get good portion sizes for the platters, but taste didn't really stand out to me.  I didn't try the paneer masala roll, however, so maybe I'll need to revisit.

An incredible place that is a must hit in Philly. Tons of food selections, most of which are very reasonably priced. DiNic's is a MUST try. Going on the weekends is a surefire way to ensure all vendors are open, but be prepared for it to be very crowded and hard to walk around.

Convenient place to lunch after walking around Philly, especially since it's close to the famous LOVE sign. However, I was very unhappy with my experience. I ordered "3 plain McDoubles, just the cheese" and went on my way. What I actually got was one regular McDouble, one with ketchup and onions, and the other with just mustard. I don't understand how this sort of mixup could have happened...

Can I give less than one star? Originally quoted 30 min delivery with the food to arrive around 630. At 7, I called and asked how much longer it would be. I was told my food left at 606. So, you mean to tell me the food has been sitting in the driver's car for almost an hour?? I live literally 5 minutes from this place. Pizza dough was RAW. To top it all off, the driver refused to bring my food to the door and made me walk out to the street to get it. Worst $23 I've ever spent. Over priced trash. Will never be ordering here again. Or at PH anywhere else for that matter. They all seem to have 2 stars or less in this city.

The ultimate fun place for bored conventioneers. They have every type of delicacy you can think of, ranging from vegan and vegetarian to meaty heaven and delectable ice cream treats.

A MUST whenever in Philly, and even more so to take a healthy breather from an upstairs convention.

Love the Reading Terminal, but try to avoid going during 12-2 as much as possible. That is the absolute worst time if you're in a hurry and can't afford to be lost in the crowd. Other than that, it's definitely an experience.

The Reading Terminal Market was full of food vendors, craft shops, a bookstore, and an amazing produce market. It certainly was a feast for the eyes, but due to the early closing time on Sunday, my friend and I weren't able to experience any of the food for ourselves. We were disappointed about that, but were pretty excited just walking around for a little while and looking at all of the shops. The thing that really stuck with me about the place was that people were not friendly. We were taken aback when we were kicked out of the market. We were making our way outside at the time, and it was jarring to be yelled at on the way out. Woah.
Must see spot in Center City. Plan to get something to eat (meal, snack, dessert) as there are many options to choose from.

Everything about this place was awesome. The happy hour is amazing. $3.00 local beers. Buck a Shuck. $1.00 Mac and Cheese things which comes with this awesome sauce. The look was amazing. This place is next to my childhood grade school so of course I wanted to go in and check it out. Guess what, I'll never do it again. Cause the day I went, I got the most neglectful and disrespectful bartender I've ever had in my life. It seemed to me that he went out of his way to ignore us, which I don't get cause the only thing we where asking for was you know, food, drinks, more food, more drinks. We weren't even trying to make small talk with this bartender cause it just seemed like this bartender was having a bad day. Which is obviously bad for you guys cause I don't think I'll ever come back. 
I totally recommend people to have their own experience of this place. 99% of the people that go probably won't have this same experience. I just wanted to tell you. Cause it's been about 4 day later and the service that I received is still annoying me. 
Best Regards.
I've always heard about the Reading Terminal Market, and a few short weeks ago I was finally able to experience it. This place has such variety and I cannot wait to go back and discover more things.

There are a few markets similar to this one in Southern California, but none of them compare to the bustle and variety of Reading Terminal Market! Parking can be a bit of a challenge in this area, so you might be better off taking public transportation, depending on how much you plan on buying.

There's vendors selling meat, bread, pies, coffee, candy, and so much more. If you're overwhelmed by crowds, you could probably spend hours here. I know I could! I was here more for sightseeing than running errands, but I enjoyed myself all the same. There are a few common seating tables if you're having a meal or just hanging out. Great place to feel the vibe of the Philadelphia community!

employees are rude and service is slow. I work around there so I visited a few times but it was bad more times then good! I am just overall disgusted with the service of mcdonalds in general now due to the visits of so many bad service locations.
Great place for breakfast, brunch, or lunch!  Wish we would have known about this on our first day of our long weekend instead of our last day!

I heart Chick-Fil-A! Out of all the fast food chains, they have the best chicken sandwich. I like that their buns are whole wheat. Whether I walk in or drive thru, customer service is top notch. They greet you with smiles and sometimes even help take your order to a table, I had my kids with me at the time and they brought my tray over. My kids also have a clean play area once they are done eating.

I love going here! I always make a trip before a party when I want to get some interesting snacks for a party. I can find cheeses, nuts, candies: all perfect snacks! It's a fun place to check out, and I'll go back for more whenever I can.

Great place to grab breakfast /lunch whatever. Make some great sandwiches. However sometimes some of the vendors can provide you with some pretty lame cuts of beef (ruebens/cornbeef, ets) call them out if they do. I cant give specifics cuz i dont recall the exact vendors. There is some phenomenal food/groceries/baked goods within this market.

This sandwich is everything. The pastrami is tender, well seasoned not salty and taste great. I would recommend you stop past this location the next time you're at the reading terminal. The prices are a little steep for a sandwich.

A friend in the area kept raving about this place, so it was nice to be able to stroll in for lunch and see what the fuss was about. And what fuss, there was almost every type of food and drink imaginable in this once-terminal station. Great open air market atmosphere with all types of food to eat.

Lots of different local snacks, desserts, food, beverage, cheese, sweets, gifts... the list goes on and on. Definitely check this out for a big variety of cool market and foodstuff.

RTM is probably one of the coolest places in the city.  I go weekly for produce and fresh meat, as well as amazing lunches and fresh juice.  The variety of things you can find is incredible! The only downside is that when there are conventions or events in center city, it's packed, but I guess that's part of the experience :)
Pro tip -- you can park at the garage across the street (at 12th & cuthbert) and have your parking ticket validated at the produce stands if you spend over $10, so that you only have to pay $4 :)

Probably the best lunch time Indian food in Center City. Just found out about this place and will definitely be back. Got the lamb roll and chicken tikka roll. Both were very good. Lots of flavor. The hot sauce on the side also added flavor. Prices reasonable and comparable to other places nearby.

Reading Terminal is a very large indoor market, with lots of restaurants stands, grocery stands, and stands selling a variety of other things. There's a reason it's popular with locals and tourists alike: this place is full of delicious food. It can get busy on weekends, and it's easy to get lost, but the food is worth it. Some of my favorite places are Beck's Cajun Cafe (great if you like spicy food) and Beiler's donuts, but nearly every place has great food. It's definitely not the cheapest, most meals will run you $8-11. However, this is definitely a must-do for anyone visiting Philly.
SO FUN!!! Perfect place to keep your eye busy with all the cool things, it's indoors, and no matter what your party size - you'll enjoy it!! Even by yourself

This massive food market is a must-visit for everyone!  With such a wide selection of foods, there is surely something for everyone.  There are so many stalls bustling with visitors, it's easy to get lost!  

Quick run down on the things I tried:
Beck's Cajun Café - fried mac and cheese: deliciously gooey onomnom
Tommy DiNic's - roast pork sandwich: line moves fast and worth the wait
Flying Monkey - butter cake: pure sugar bomb, don't get this

It's Chik-fil-A. No need to describe food, you know it's such good fast food. This particular location is usually extremely busy, but the line inside goes quickly and like most Chik-fil-A's, the service is incredible. Stay away from drive through if you can. Only 4 stars for the stupid "not open on Sunday" rule. Gotta change that.

Reading Market, how convenient you are. All fresh things in one place. All specialty items right there at my fingertips.
