Reading Terminal Market is just like a small Italian or Parisian street with all the stores you need in one place. What makes it so fabulous is every "booth" specializes in one thing or another. Flowers, candy, BBQ, honey, Italian baked goods, sandwiches, crepes, ice cream, pretzels, nuts, organic produces, a butcher...shall I go on? 

I'm a New Yorker, and wish something like this was in my neighborhood. In NYC we have Grand Central Terminal Market, which is good, but this is a bigger scale with more options. Everything looked really fresh and I wanted to try one of everything, but tried to not go crazy and just had a cannoli from Termini Brothers (http://www.yelp.com/biz/termini-brothers-bakery-philadelphia-2#hrid:4LM9uZs4Tv9UdhzaHEc6ZQ/src:self).

If I lived here, this is probably where I would shop. Even the flowers looked amazing and healthy, and each different vendor had many choices of their product. Most vendors were helpful too, I asked questions and the honey bee vendor let me try a few of their products to try and find what I was looking for. 

Go here if you have the opportunity. Even if it is too look around and possibly sample a few things. Totally worth it.

If you want to die of a food coma you come here.

Everything from cheese steaks, burgers, and pastries are sold here.  The cheesesteaks are huge, greasy, and packed to the point it's overflowing. Literally a heart attack in a bun.  The market also acts as a grocery store and you can buy a lot of fresh fruits and meat. Really has something for everyone.

It's extremely crowded during the weekend with people walking up and down the isles and seating space is so limited. You really have to walk with a purpose and get lucky with the seating. It's very overwhelming just the amount of people in such a congested space.

As for the food, I went to Flying Monkey to get dessert, you can't miss their stand as the stands awning is huge. I got the Elvis cupcake and the cookie dough brownie. Extremely good, especially the brownie. The brownie is great for anyone with a sweet tooth. The price wasn't bad as the cupcake was about 3 bucks and the brownie was about 4 bucks.

I like this market more then other markets such as such as Eataly in New York and Quincy Market in Boston. Eataly is all Italian related and Quincy Market just isn't as big.
Alive with people and jam packed with amazing eats. Foodies heaven! Bring cash as some places don't take debit/credit. Limited seating. Best cheesesteaks and haogies at Carmen's.

This is a must! A friend brought me here because I am visiting. It's a little bit of everything. Booths with chocolates, fresh meat, vegetables & delicious things to sit and eat. Oh & the cheesesteak they have a pretty good cheesesteak!

Seriously, what's NOT to love about this place? The food choices are endless and authentic. Sweet, savory, cheesy, meaty, vegetarian... you name it, it's there. If I'm ever in Philly again, I will definitely be going back.

Such a cool place with so many options. Could definitely walk around for a couple hours and not get bored or even see the same thing twice. Overwhelming for me as an introvert but if you try to think of what type of food you want to eat before going it'll make the experience much easier and better

I love the food here and the energy. I would shop here more often for meat, fish, and produce if I lived closer. The one thing I cannot get over, that drives me nuts, is how crowded it gets. I know it cannot be helped, but I cannot stand pushing my way through endless crowds.

My fiance and I came here this weekend as part of our dinner and a movie date, and were so pleasantly surprised by our time at The Industry. (We were equally pleasantly surprised by Jurassic World 3D, but that's another review for another time...Oh Chris Pratt...) The restaurant is much larger than I was expecting, with a sizable bar, lots of tables, and a row of high seating that runs down the middle of the space. Although we almost exclusively sit at the bar when we go out, it was a beautiful night, so we opted for outdoor seating - plus, the inside was actually quite loud, even for us, so al fresco it was. 

The drink menu at The Industry does not play - they offer tons of beers and wine, plus have a pretty inventive and affordable cocktail menu. I was feeling adventurous and ordered something totally out of my standard beer wheelhouse (a Ginger Lemon Radler by Boulevard)  and it was amazing and my dude was very happy with the red wine he chose. Foodwise, The Industry has jumped on the gastropub bandwagon with a vengeance - think bar food meets comfort food meets ingredient from super left field. Case and point: foie gras PB&J (no, I did not order that.)

We started out with the fried mac & cheese balls, because, I mean, fried mac & cheese. Despite probably being a heart attack on a plate, these little guys were delicious and actually felt very light - they were crispy and creamy, but not greasy. Apparently we both felt like eating something raw after that would negate the calories, so I had the tuna tartare mini tacos and my other half had the beer tartare. Both were incredibly good, although I thought the tuna was a bit small and a bit expensive for what actually showed up on my plate. But I always appreciate an inventive and tasty menu, and The Industry definitely nailed it on that front.

The Industry is a great addition to this up and coming neighborhood and will surely only get better with time. We'll be back!

The Reading Terminal Market is a famous enclosed public market in Philadelphia that was first established in 1892. The urban farmer's market is located on 12th & Arch Streets and is a foodie haven. There is a very wide variety restaurants, fresh and local produce, meats, seafood, diary, baked goods, confections, fresh flowers, coffee, Amish specialities...anything! The selection is incredible and it is fun to explore more than 80 vendors which are mostly family-owned. The market is a very popular spot at lunchtime where you can grab a quick lunch. There are some areas in the market where you can sit and eat. Sometimes the lines can be long but it is always worth the wait. www.readingterminalmarket.org

The "must do" thing in Philly. The Reading Terminal Market is as much Philly as the Cheese Steak or Roast Pork Sandwich. Be sure to get some cookies at 4th Street and Bassets is really yummy. Dinic's roast pork is the best in the world and from Wednesday through Saturday the Amish are there selling their goodies and wares. 

It does get VERY crowded but a total genuine Philly experience.

Neat place with a dingy feel. I bring friends here for the experience (much like Quincy Market in Boston), but I don't go often myself. I don't care for the atmosphere (always overly crowded and wayyy to many competing smells) but when I do go, the Soul Food spot never disappoints. Huge portions, delicious menu, friendly staff.
Great place love it i would recommend mu friend's and family many stores and restaurants to choose from very friendly employees
I frequent this place on a weekly basis, it has a lively and colorful atmosphere. It has a great array of food choices for breakfast and lunch. It's a definate must see if your visiting.

Something fantastic for everyone 
I wanted a Gyro and my wife Salad - simple - Olympia.  But my wife wanted ribs too so she picked up a pound of spare ribs at The Rib Stand and met me back at Olympia.  Ribs were good with the Pita bread and salad.  For dessert ice cream from Bassett's.  Must be 50 other places to try here.   I will read all the other reviews and plan out attack for tomorrow
Smoothie was so sweet I couldn't finish it. Good waste of $6. If you're looking for a light/healthy snack find something else.

I'm a Jersey girl.  My Philadelphia culinary experiences are usually planned and carefully executed and based on some review I read or heard from someone I trust.  Although I appreciate street food and Philadelphia's many informal foodie rituals (cheesesteaks, soft pretzels, etc.), I just experienced the Reading Terminal Market for the very first time.

Yes, of course I'd been there before.  Its in the middle of everything and its hard to miss.  I'm not a complete dork.  But if memory serves, I think the first time I was there I could only manage to find the 4th Street Deli cookie counter and the second time? I met with clients for breakfast and I think I had only some of those homemade Amish granola bars and a lemon square.

Whatever!

My boyfriend, Jon, took me there recently, while waiting for his car to have some detailing finished at High End Stereo at 12th and Vine Streets.  This was a whole new experience: a Saturday afternoon.  Plus, Jon's well-versed in what the Terminal Market has to offer; he works just in the neighborhood.  He knows the Amish schedule (No Monday, Tuesday) and can navigate through the barbecue chicken, ribs, pulled pork and the pastries.  

Everything looked and smelled so good!  I can't imagine working there and having to mingle all day with the sights and smells of food, flowers, art, perfume and people.  Its intoxicating!  I saw fresh seafood.  I saw butchers chopping ribs for the barbecue.  I even saw hot sausage sandwiches with fried onions and peppers getting sweet sauce poured over them, leaving a stream of steam in its wake.  Wow!

It reminded me of when I was a little kid and my mother would load us all in the car at the butt crack of Saturday dawn and drive us to the Englishtown, NJ open-air market (rain or shine, warm or cold) for shopping and eating, but this is much better: no cold and just as great for people watching!

Jon had some barbecue chicken that day and I managed a chicken salad sandwich and homemade lemonade.  Best stuff ever!

Next time?  I'll hit the butcher and the florist and bring some of that goodness home!

LOVE everything about this place.

I do groceries here a lot and there is a student discount on ( I think ) Sundays and Wednesdays.

The Amish guy with the fresh juices is great.

CANNOLLIS.

Also did the cooking class here and it was really fun.

Great place to bring people who are visiting!

Love going to Reading Terminal Market whether it is to pick up some fresh produce from Iovine's produce or to grab a quick, gourmet bite. Love eating breakfast at the Dutch eating place (blueberry pancakes are the best and the apple dumplings are amazing).

If you are visiting Philadelphia you NEED to stop by this place! There is a lot of history housed here and you can find yourself lost a bit in the maze of this indoor farmer's market. It's a tourist spot so it's going to feel overwhelming from the crowd but it's worth checking out to shop, eat, and just look around.
Reading terminal has everything you're looking for when it comes to food. I love just walking through and trying different foods from here. My favorite is Bielers and the cheese shop.
Great food, too crowded at times but if that does not bother you,The grill cheese place towards the back is the best!

Where do you start?? This was a problem place for me when I worked in Philly. It was only about 5 blocks from my job...Where else can you get so many different and DELICIOUS types of food!!! I love to go on a Thursday when the Amish stands are open...they truly have the best ribs in the market!! Flavorful and juicy!!!  Just delicious!! DiNics-best roast pork sandwich in the city!!!  Bassets ice cream is to die for!!! Cookies from 4th street cookies are expensive but worth every penny!!!   My boyfriend thought he had died and gone to heaven in this place!!! We had way too many bags when we came out of here because he wanted to eat a little bit of everything!! LOL Absolutely the best there is!!!

I've been to the industry quite a few times. The service is great, food always comes out to my liking and delicious beer on tap! If you work in the industry, they give you 20% off, I always take advantage of that. :) It's great for date nights or if you want to grab a few drinks with your friends.
Awesome place to visit in Philly. Tons of little shops makes for a very wide selection -- something for everyone.

What a fun place filled with people and great food smells. My friend and I walked nearly all of it and while we didn't dine here, it was such a fun place. There is something for everyone and all ages. Meats, seafood, cheese steaks, ice cream and cookies.
Tourists and locals are welcomed here. I liked the live music too.

The Market is awesome.  Going there is an event, an experience--more than just shopping.  It is a feast for the eyes, the nose and the brain.  The variety of really good food is beyond measure.  For example, there is a cheese shop where one can buy cheeses from around the world as well as goat cheese and other varieties, many of which are new to me.  Go to the butcher and choose the cut of meat you want and at the fish market you can stare back at the fish lying on ice.  Of the Market also offers live lobsters.  For people like me with a sweet tooth, there are a few bakeries and pastry shops.  The variety is endless.  The produce shops are amazing.  I can buy a box of blackberries for one-third or less of what I pay at the supermarket.  Same with many other fruits and vegetables.  Another treat lies in the various Amish shops that provide some wonder food and bakery items, as well as a variety of other things.  Go on a day other than Sunday, though, if you want to catch all the shops including the Amish ones.  Bulk spices and bulk tea is another welcome addition--it reminds me of being in places like the UAE.  Reading Terminal Market truly is a gem--the greatest challenge is resisting buying a little of everything with excellent quality and reasonable prices, one can quickly buy a bit too much of one thing or another.

One of my favorite solo activities is to wander around Reading Terminal for an hour or 2. I grab a to-go beer from Molly Malloy's and then just ROAM. My favorite spots are Little Thai market and Hunger Burger. Also Martin's quality meats really hook it up and the Dutch beef jerky spot. Great spot for people watching and introspection while being surrounded by all sorts of characters.

The area around the market is a bit iffy, with things typical of cities, such as busy traffic, rude drivers, homeless people, offensive odors, etc.

Once inside, you'll feel more comfortable as you wander up and down the aisles making the difficult decision of what to eat.  (Although most of the stands are counter service food establishments, there are stands for things like cookbooks, local produce, a butcher shop, and the like.)

Different stands make different impressions.  Some seem clean, streamlined, and "professional"; others seem rougher, as if the owner didn't give a hoot about presentation, relying instead on the quality of the food.

On two visits, we enjoyed our meals which included baked mac & cheese, perogies, cornbread, banana cornbread, samosas, and beer-battered onion rings.  Both times we went, the seating areas were dirty.

Certainly recommended for the food choices, though.

Came here with some friends. It wasn't as crowded as I had expected for a Saturday night, but that changed quickly. Loved the atmosphere--nice bar, friendly patrons, golden oldies music, and definitely industrial with the metal tables. 

The food, on the other hand, left much to be desired. The menu can best be described a as eclectic. It boasts bahn mi sandwiches next to biscuits n gravy followed by dishes like mushroom cannelloni. I had the fish and chips (tempura-style) and my friends got wings and the mushroom cannelloni dish. My food wasn't nearly worth the $16 it cost me. The friend with the wings was the only satisfied customer at our table. The rest of us left and got takeout from Ruby buffet. 

This was a great place to meetup for drinks and conversation. They've got you covered on typical post/pre-movie snack foods (read: wings and fries). But not exactly the best place for a satisfyingly tasty meal.
Always fun, good for people watching, and hasn't been turned in to a corpratized tourist trap... real local businesses are what makes this place great.

I thought it was a bit pricey for the amount given (comparing to food trucks) but it's a solid late night option. I ordered the chicken keema, chicken tikka, and paneer tikka rolls. They were all quite dry in comparison to the masala roll.

I do like this place a lot although its not somewhere I needed to go more than once.  If I worked in the area, I think it would be a good lunch spot to take advantage of the variety of places under one roof.  Its not cheap but there are a lot of quality food places and vendors selling goods from their places of origin.  I think the prices are high to take advantage of tourists, considering the seating is so-so.
My first time at Redding Terminal Market.  It truly exceeded my high expectations.  A huge selection of high quality food stands.  A must for any trip to Philly.

I am obsessed with this place.  Did you know there is discount parking nearby???  Too many excellent options to list.  Walk around.  Enjoy the amazing foods.  Enjoy the chaos.  Enjoy everything about this place.

Good food. Very crowded but a lot of choices. 
Great way to enjoy Philadelphia food.  Try Molly Mallow's cheesesteak sandwich.

how could you not love this place? They've really turned this large, urban, historic indoor public back around after some down years. It's been thriving with lots of tourists, conventioneers, and locals. Most everything you'll get here is delicious. 

They've previously had a cheesteak venue that was horrible get replaced, which made me feel good because out-of-towners shouldn't have a horrible first cheese steak. Great selection of foods in separated stalls. There's also some diners (Amish one is my fav), produce markets, deserts, fresh meats and cheese shops, some specialty and foreign goods. It's also very close to Chinatown and it's markets. I've seen Food Network special events shot here and culinary exhibitions. 

A few of the shops and diners have small seating areas, mostly at counters. There are also a good number of public tables in the middle with a high turnover rate. This place has people in it all day long but really is packed around lunch time. 

There is some metered street parking and nearby expensive lots, some reasonable a little ways away, but lots of foot traffic here from center city business district, convention center, and hotels. 

You should have no problem finding something delicious to eat or cook here.

There are so many things to eat and see and buy here. I like taking out-of-town friends to this location, setting them free, and telling them to buy food until they burst. The only thing that I always forget to take into account is the hours--it's best to go around lunchtime or the afternoon, because the Terminal closes at dinnertime. In addition, it can get a little crowded, as space is at a premium here. Be prepared to maneuver delicately.

Must stop at: the Asian smoothie place near Bassett's (another must-stop). The Termini Brothers satellite shop and the Fourth Street cookie place. Also at DiNic's (obviously). Oh, and there is a great Middle Eastern place called Kamal's, as well as a fantastic creperie a few aisles away. Finally, the Lancaster merchants always have amazing baked goods (like cinnamon buns!).

Foodie paradise!

Roasting pork. A store filled with cheese. Fresh fish lined up for display. Tea, tea, tea. A tower of fruits and vegetables. Is that a waft of sweet fudge? YES. YES IT IS. And it's all within walking distance. 

I honestly don't know how I didn't A) spend more time here and B) spend more money here. Guess I have some self-control after all. I say, don't believe all the hype about some of the more popular joints in here (ehem Dinic's) and go check out some smaller shops. I had a blast at one of the Amish candy places and bought some stellar fudge (and take it from me, I used to work as a candy maker!). The cheese booths kept calling my name, but my wallet kept me from purchasing multiple cheese wheels (CRY). 

I love options and I love food, so if you love being overwhelmed by awesomeness, this is the right place for you. I could see tourists and locals alike coming here for a fun afternoon or a quick bite. Yum yums!

Various markets. Go for the steak sandwich at Carmen's. They're delicious and, personally, I think better than Pat's or Geno's. Also try a pork hoagie at DiNic's. Very unusual and, if you like roast pork, a definite treat.

Otherwise the place is very touristy and crowded compared to Washington's Eastern Market or Cleveland's West Side Market.

I have never been let down by a visit to Reading Terminal Market. I had a strawberry and nutella crepe for breakfast that was very good, the fresh produce is so cheap I have filled my back pack many times for less than $20. We once got a lamb shoulder from the butcher in the middle that was really good, I would buy meat from him again. Cheese shop right near the butcher had some of the best cheeses I have had in America and the guy was very informed and offered many samples, which was nice. And the Termini bros stand is not to be missed for a perfect cannoli! I only wish it was open later than 6 pm weekdays so it would be possible to stop by after work sometimes.

I worked in the Terminal for a little while so I have a non-glossy view of this consortium of businesses. For anyone confused, this is nothing like a farmers market. There are a few meat places and an occasional veggie stand but it's mostly a bunch of tourist traps. 

Most of the restaurants are sub-par and have a large markup because tourists flock here. That doesn't go to say there aren't a few great eats here. I would definitely recommend Sang-Kee, DiNiCs and Pearls. You can't really go wrong with anything on those menus.

A big plus to the market is the Amish side toward Arch Street. Bailer's Doughnuts will put you into a sugary food coma and the wait at the Dutch Eating Place is well worth the wait (Don't miss out on the apple dumplings). 

Just a note. If you are new to the city and are looking to save a little cash while eating fresh produce, go to Iovines. This is still a family run business, the produce is usually great quality and the prices are great. Usually lower than big grocery stores. You can regularly find berries for $.99 a container on special in the front.

There are definitely some great spots at the terminal but overall it's for tourists and the shops are generally more expensive than the equivalents anywhere else.

My husband and I wanted more of a nontraditional wedding venue, with amazing food, and room to dance the night away.  That is exactly what we got at Reading Terminal Market.  Planning with Stormy was easy and laid back.  She was a treat to work with, and was always available to answer my questions.  

No words can describe the experience that my husband and I had on our wedding day!!! The staff was so incredibly kind and helpful, and everyone from vendors to waitstaff seemed happy to be there.  It was amazing to see the market transform into the wedding of our dreams in just an hour!  Every detail that I asked for was perfectly executed.  It was amazing to see my vision come to life.

Our guests had an amazing time too.  I really think they appreciated a change from the normal wedding venue.  They were in awe of the markets transformation and everyone raved about the food!!! My only complaint is that my husband and I didn't eat a thing!  We were too busy celebrating!  Luckily Stormy sent us home with a doggie bag!

Cheers to RTM!!

What's not to love?  Good, traditional food from all over the globe and many local favorites as well.. Sometimes there is live music... I even saw a few couples getting married there on Valentines day.... Wonderful place to be
Fun for a day out in town. Good food vendors and merchants. Very casual. Often crowded.

This place was packed! You may feel like sardines at times as you maneuver around. The locals said that during lunch hours, this place gets super busy, and of course we were there during the lunch rush. 

Reading has a wide selection of foods and local products (artisan items and fresh produce). If you're wanting a smoothie then check. If sandwiches are more your thing then there are a couple of spots. Needing dessert? Check!

Our friend said there's a Dutch area where you can grab breakfast and see the staff in their traditional attire (at times). It was closed when we ventured here, but he said it was something worth checking out. 

Reading is a good spot for food. If this is on your list as you're visiting Philly, it's not a shopping market or anything that will take too much of your day. If you're there to look then it takes about 10 to 15 mins.

The most visited attraction in Philadelphia and for good reason.

There is a decent variety of food to be found here: French, Vietnamese, Halal, Indian and your typical American steaks and burgers.

This may exist already, but it would useful to have a map of the facility. Sometimes it's difficult to find the exact place you're looking for.

This has been such a pleasant surprise here in Philly. Discovered it with a couple of friends and have been a regular ever since. The flavors and price can't be beat. Quick and efficient service. 5 stars from me.

Ordered the Chicken Tikka roll here as an amuse bouche for the tasting menu at Indeblue. 

The roll is soft and fluffy naan. It is filled primarily with chicken and Indian tikka spices. The spices were excellent. They were salty, complex, and just a touch of spicy.

The chicken was cooked just a bit too far. I'd say they do the standard 165 chicken. This leaves it slightly dry, chalky, and resilient to the bite. 

I enjoyed this roll. The chicken was slightly over-executed.
So many choices and everything is great! You also get a discount if you visit while on jury duty!

There's something for everyone in reading terminal!

Grocery shopping for produce is spectacular. It is a little more expensive than the Italian Market but the produce is a better quality and lasts much longer.

Count yourself very lucky to work close for a top notch lunch spot. It can be crazy busy and a little disorienting for your first few times. Totally worth it, once you get the lay of the land. You really cannot go wrong with places to eat here. 

Here are my favorite 3:
Valley Shepherd Creamery & Meltkraft Grilled Cheese: Rivals Dibruno's for a cheese spot. Grilled cheese sandwiches are the best I've had. Valley Thunder (cheddar, brisket, mac n cheeese) is sooo good and try the Melter Skelter

DiNic's: Maybe the most popular draw in the entire place and is wildly busy during lunch. Expect a big wait but it is a must try for their famous Roast pork (close 2nd to John's Roast pork) and roast beef. The place has a ton of hype and deservedly so, the wait can be much. 

Wursthaus Schmitz: Part of Brauhaus, this place is definitely worth a try. Do yourself a favor and get some sausage and schnitzel in your life!

Came here twice in one day! Tried the paneer masala, aloo paneer, and the chicken tikka roll and I have to say the paneer masala roll was the obvious winner. Also, the white sauce takes the food to the next level. It's somewhat similar to the white sauce served with chicken and rice ( mayo base).

If you have been to Kati Roll in NYC, you will know that this place is basically the same idea but with a few more options ( platters with rice). I just recently moved to Philly from close to NYC and I'm ecstatic I found a Kati Roll place here as well :)

Very fun spot, and one of the few sight seeing places in Philly I enjoy going over and over when new visitors come. Avoid lunch hour tho! The lines wrap around corners and its hard to walk between 12-2. But if you go in the morning you might be lucky enough to get one of "the best donuts in Philadelphia" at Beiler's. ( I AGREE ) If you come in the afternoon, many places are doing happy hour. But don't go too late, this place closes promptly at 5 pm and stalls start shutting down before that. Fun ambiance, locally grown food and products. You can see the whole thing in a 30 minute walk, or you can enjoy hours in here eating and shopping.
Love the variety.  Many delicious choices.  Just a bit crowded and difficult to find a seat.

Reading Terminal Market is like a cross between an (indoor) outdoor market and a food court. It's one of the top tourist attractions in Philadelphia, and you should probably experience it at least once during your visit.

With that said, you should know that it's a little overwhelming. I would give it closer to 4 stars on weekdays, but definitely three stars on the weekend. EVERYONE goes to this market. Seriously. I couldn't handle the crowd!

But once you can come to terms with the sheer volume of people, you can focus on the food. I personally found it to be a little repetitive. I mean I like sandwiches as much as the next person, but there are like a half dozen delis in there! There are stands run by Amish vendors, and those have special hours. I can at least tell you the places I tried:

Hatville Deli (sandwich)
Mezze (sandwich)
The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company (cookies)
Sweet As Fudge Candy Shoppe (candy)
Chocolate by Mueller (candy)
Market Blooms (flowers)
Iovine Brothers Produce (fruit)

So, you should go. Be in an adventurous mood. It's at least an experience. You *will* find something you like here. (And if you can swing by the Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe & pick me up some lime fruit slices, that'd be great.) Just be prepared to dodge the crowd!

If you can't find somewhere to eat here, then you're not doing something right.  This place is AMAZING!!  I always request working the Philadelphia Auto Show, just so I can come into town and frequently visit the Reading Terminal.  I also make peace with the fact that I will be spending a lot of money because it's just too god to not take advantage of. So many delicious options!  You're sure to find something you like, definitely something you love and probably something you'll want to try again.  One of the best places on Earth for sure!

Okay, but certainly not up to the hype it often gets.  The physical environment needs serious work.  People are nice, general vibe is good, lots to pick from...but the place is dirty and in need of help.

Look at Grand Central Market at the Grand Central Terminal in NYC or the Ferry Building in San Francisco, for example.  Philly needs to clean the place up for the shoppers and the vendors.

Suburban Square has a "farmers market" that had a nice tuning up--the food isn't so great in some spots, but the physical market is nice. 

I agree with the people who say venture beyond RTM.  There are plenty of better places to eat all over the city. The food here is not that great.

[I stopped writing this review at this point and got up and went to the market]

I just got back from taking my family down to the market for lunch. 

Everybody spread out and tried a wide variety of  things.  A crepe, which  was "fine but not that great."  A smoothie which was "really good."  Fries from Franks ("frozen fries...they suck.").  Some Pierogi's from Franks ("pretty good").  I had a pulled pork sandwich from DiNic's.  I wouldn't bother getting another one.  It was, amazingly, totally bland.  

Termini Bros., as always, was perfect.

Unfortunately, this Potbelly Sandwich Shop has closed.

Their food was definitely good. That wasn't the problem.

Its entrance was completely separate from the other eateries facing the Target parking garage.

Not enough foot traffic along that part of City Avenue.

Absolutely love this place and have been going since I was a kid.  Lunchtime is pretty hectic but they have such a variety of vendors that you don't mind the crowds.

I started a tradition with my granddaughter and she and I travel down the day before Thanksgiving, pick up some baked goods, have lunch and then hop back on the train.  I love when family comes to Philly to visit because this is a place they always want to stop at.

Wow, this place was a top highlight of our Philly visit. Bakeries, eateries, meat markets, florists, and other cute stores fill this space. I enjoy anything Amish so seeing them in action made me happy. One could easily spend an hour or two checking out this market.

Love, love, love Reading Terminal Market!
so many choices! i love the food selections and its a great atmosphere other than all the homeless people taking over the place and panhandling
Great place to experince different cultural foods.

Oh, the classic. Love, love love. I do my produce shopping here and my fatty self even plans out my walks home from class so as not to pass by here, or I WILL go in. Some people have complaints: it smells, it's crowded, most people don't take credit cards, blah blah. It's stuck in its ways people, and let it be! It's all part of the ambience, and I love it for all it's loud, shouting, ocassionaly smelly, cash-only self. The culture and food are fantastic. Go here if you haven't been, just to experience it.

So I've gone back 3 times since my negative review. It's been much better each time.. The bartenders and servers have been great and the food has been good as well. They have some great specials going all the time. Happy hour $1 Mac and cheese croquettes are awesome. I'm glad my most recent experiences have been great and changed my feelings on the spot.. Since I live around the block.

The market is a very cool place to visit. You can find almost anything that you want.
Great butcher shops and fantastic bakeries. There are a bunch of really good places to get a sandwich or bowl of soup.
It is really really crowded most of the time but that's the only real downside.

Definitely stop in this place if you are anywhere near downtown.  Great place for lunch, I'm just bitter every cheese steak place was closed on a Sunday!  They have veggies, honey, crafty things, seafood.  Reminds me of an indoor Pike's Market without all the tourists. (And apparently it's pronounced Redding-why don't they just spell it that way?)

Philly Cheesesteak was excellent.  I like mine with mayo, cheese , onions. Great tender,  juicey meat with nice heated roll. Good crunch and juices combo. Fries and drink for under 10 dollars. Wife had fried chicken and fries that were also excellent. 
A few tables or take out. I had a smoothie nice fruit....

Wow, this spot literally blew my mind. If you're looking for something to do, something to eat or just plain whatever. Make your way here and watch the hours melt away.

Once you walk in, you are literally greeted by mom and pop shops all over the place. Grocery shops, food stalls and dry good items. Heck yea!! It's like sensory overload!! From fresh fish to meat to cheese to produce I will guarantee that you're gonna have a hard time keeping the money in your wallet. Trust me, you will spend on something here.

Today, we came to eat,,, and it's not hard to find something to fancy as well. Everything from Mediterranean to Chinese to hoagies to burgers, you'll find them here. I haven't tried all of the stalls here, we had Tommy Dinics, but I can bet you they're all pretty good. You fancy making your own food? Buy yourself some fresh fish, some produce and a bag of potatoes, go home and cook yourself a kick ass meal. Don't feel like turning on the stove?? Fine,, buy a box of crackers, there's some cured meats and cheeses and create yourself a charcuterie board.

I could go on and on about this place and how awesome it is, but wouldn't you rather be experiencing it first hand??

Life is short, go experience awesome things.

Weeeeeeeee!!!

Whether your a meatlover or a hardcore vegan they got something to delight everyone. The Amish food stands are open Wednesday thru Saturday. Great eats from east to west, and north to south in this foodie heavenly delight.... I can tell you there are at least Five big cookie bakeries or combo coffee shops. They all are mouth watering hide them b4 you walk in the door at home cookies. You'd do better to find out about all the different choices you have b4 you arrive bc there are so many to choose from it's mind blowing.  Nerve racking if you're attacked to a large group. A must to check out on your visit here. Just don't stand in the middle of the isle making Philadelphians crazy. You have to be good at weaving and dodging thru the crowds during the week. Well pretty much until closing..... Enjoy

Great place to visit while in Philadelphia. So many options for fresh food. It is so hard to decide. We also had the opportunity to attend a private, after hours, party where we sampled many different food options, oysters, shrimp, Philly cheesesteak, falafel and more!

First time in Philly, just a random trip, and came across this little hidden gem. Nothing fancy, but cute, quaint, and delicious. Hubby ordered the Unda roll, paneer tikka and mix veggie roll. I ordered aloo roll. All the rolls came warm and oh so tasty! We were stuffed. Friendly staff and nice atmosphere. Oh and mango lassi is a must try, tasty and comes in a convenient bottle which we carried as we walked the rest of the city.

Wonderful adventure with my daughter. 

I highly recommend experiencing the sights, sounds, and foods

If you are in center city Philadelphia make sure you go to the reading terminal market. This is the site of the old Reading railroad closed down many years ago for train service.
Its crowded, fun, food delights. In the corner is a small restaurant. Get scrapple, eggs and fried potatoes and you will be a true Philadelphian. The cost is low too, this place is like a small diner.
Pennsylvania dutch people come down from Lancaster County and sell boneless chickens (also known as eggs :) and cheese, baked goods, dressed in their traditional clothing. Its the real thing folks. Local people buy vegetables, fruit, meat, seafood, everything you would want for a home cooked meal. Tourists can try everything, you buy something and take it to one of dozens of tables all over the place.  Share a table with other tourists or locals.  Pennsylvania had a state liquor board system with state stores so you can only buy beer to go and there is a bar for full service cocktails, wine and beer.  All the stuff is good, repeat good, you won't be disappointed from a cheese steak wit onions, or to a hoagie with everything. anybody putting mayonnaise or ketchup on a cheese steak should be tossed into the Delaware River. And no lettuce or tomato either. Its meat, onion, hot or sweet peppers and a roll from Amorosos.
Reading terminal has everything... best cheesesteaks in town, best espresso in town, best breakfast in town, produce, baked goods, Amish market, one of my favorite places to eat.
love reading terminal market. great meat & produce selection
Amazing everything! but wildly crowded, you really have to spend a lot of time fighting through the crowds.
Crazy amounts of variety. Great, local atmosphere. Food lovers guaranteed to love it.

One of the most interesting places to go to on a day off, desire for unique and foods full of flavor! You can find foods that contain the most sweets, salts, sour and etc. at this market. It becomes really, really packed most days and makes it tough to sit down and REALLY enjoy your food, but it's very possible to do so. I have a few favorite shops, like the place in the middle of the market that is famous for their pork roll sandwiches, my goodness so unbelievably good. There are many Amish stores in this market that sell foods that really make me feel at home, especially the cinnamon buns.
An amazing Philadelphia experience! A must see if you're new to the area, or even if you're a local. Can't beat it!
This place is awesome! Anything and everything you could want from fresh fish to aged cheeses! I so wish this place was near me!

Go here for breakfast or lunch!  This covered market has 30+ food vendors and offers everything from crepes to Afghan kabobs, to tasty gyros!  You can also get some fresh produce, a beer at the beer garden, sample some amish cooking or get a Grand Marnier truffle!  Looking for fresh fish or lobster?  They've got it!  Want some fresh lasagna or pulled pork?  Yeah, that's here too.  I went around 11:00am on a Wednesday, it was busy, but not crowded like other reviewers have mentioned.  We were able to find seats easily and enjoyed our lunch while listening to a live piano player.  Gotta check this place out if visiting Philly.  It's just a 7 or 8 block walk from the historic district.

This place is great, it's a must stop for me when I'm passing through Philly. Dicnics as well as many other eateries are worth the calories. Oh least I forget, I always buy a couple dozen from Wursthaus Schmitz!!!!!

This is a must see in a trip to Philly. I loved everything I purchased here, and they had such a variety of local food. The quality was amazing from bagels with house made cream cheese to Amish pretzels. Donuts were epic and I took a dozen back on the plane!

Fun food market around center city Philadelphia. If you are a tourist you should definitely stop by. Try the coffee places, walk around the flower vendors, buy honey from the honey man, and try the Pearl Oyster bar for some sit down brunch.
This is a Philadelphia staple. If crowds stress you, wait until non-peak hours. The market is a sea of humanity and good food. Prepare for sensory overload.
Great service, helped me pick out a perfect beer...Allahabad Black. Yummy burger/fries, wild boar ragu & loved the chocolate dessert.  Easy walk from IMAX!

I love this Market! The place is a world. I say this because of all the variety of food that any tastebuds may want. Do not come hungry or else you won't be able to pick which place to dig in first. From soul food, Chinese, Vietnamese, American, German, even Italian. The best lobster macaroni and cheese is found here. 

From home made candles, soaps even raw honey are sold here. Fresh spices are also in here. Desserts? Don't go anywhere else's, this Market serves the best desserts! I don't think they meant for you to  get out at all. 

I've been all the world, but this place is on top of my lists as the most unique market of all. Do not miss to stop by here if even you're in town. Wish I had an empty suitcase coming into Philly! My next visit I will definitely have a spot just for Reading Market shopping!

Although the RTM draws comparisons to Seattle's Pike Place, Philadelphia's Reading Terminal Market is far less gungho and far more clean. The RTM is more of a large indoors food court, with a labyrinth of a layout and lots of wonderful vendors to check out. A small handful of shops were closed on the Monday we visited, and the hours aren't spectacularly accommodating, but it's a nice place to grab a bite.

Reading Terminal Market is the shit. Seriously, can you think of a better market in any other US city? I can't. This place has it all. From Amish to Thai, to South Philly, to Greek to Chinese, you could spend days eating in the Market (and I have). I plan to give specific reviews for each vendor, so I won't go into too much detail about my favs, but the market itself is a serious Philadelphia highlight and treasure. For those that have never been, the Market is located around 12th and Arch, is indoor, and used to share it's venue with a train station. The market underwent major renovations in the 1990's, and has about 80 shops and stands that sell prepared food, and the raw materials ie. meat, fish, produce, etc.  

Major highlights for me include Termini Brothers for pastries and cannolis, Iovines for produce, Martins for bacon and sausages, the Asian place that does smoothies, Bassetts for ice cream, and the Cajun spot (Beck's?) for gumbo when I get that hankering. Jack's Down home Diner is also a go to if I have had enough, and need a booth to sit down and relax. I am usually in the Market on weekends, and do have to note that many stands are closed on Sundays, especially anything Amish. Saturdays can be, in the words of the Bodes, BANANAS. When I say the place gets packed it can be an understatement, so be prepared for crowds, and watch where you stand. You will be pushed, shoved, bumped, and stepped on if you do not pay attention. There is nothing worse than an obese, fanny packed tourist clogging the narrow aisles declaring "Look kids, its one of those Aim-ish guys!" 

Despite the crowds, there is always something happening in the common spaces, such as live music, or if your lucky, the occasional Philly sports celeb signing autographs. I believe I bought some salsa from Mitch Williams a few years back. Bathrooms are clean, but can be packed. Also the RTM is super close to Chinatown. Parking can be a bit of an issue, but of late I have discovered some great metered spots not too far away that have been pretty empty. I am not giving up those secrets, though. On a closing note- If you are thinking about getting a DiNic's pork sandwich, either get there around opening or closing, or be prepared to wait. I've seen lines with well over 50 people in them. Also, in my opinion, the sandwich is not as good as Paesano's (see my review), so maybe you can keep the dream alive, and hit up the Italian Market, as well.  I've done a double market day only a few times, but have filled my fridge for weeks.  Good luck, grasshopper.

Ive been visiting Philly for years now and never stopped into the Reading Terminal Market before, what time I have wasted! the aroma of all the different foods and candies and coffee here is worth the trip. A crowded little market filled with everything from unique restaurants to a raw oyster bar to bees wax candles. Wish I had more time to stop in and really explore everything that was inside!

I really like this place, but they lose two stars because they close ridiculously early. 5pm? REALLY?  This place gets third-world crowded, so if you go, make it on a weekday.  The RTM is losing a LOT of my business because they close so early.

I love Reading Terminal and if it were possible to move in, I would. I ate everywhere and everything and loved it all! I couldn't get enough of the awesome breakfast at downtown diner or hot turkey at the dutch diner, seafood, pretzels, cheesesteak, it just couldn't get any better. I LOVE not just Philly but Reading Market!

SHOP 543 - excellent food, friendly service , and incredible views of the ships while dining. Yes, you pay a little bit more because you get so much more in the quality of the cuisine. I am not talking huge portions (portion size is fine) but definitely not the 'ordinary' lunch choices when you dine here. But, for the 'ordinary' lunchers, you will make out fine here as well.

Reading Terminal Market is amazing. You can enjoy any food imaginable. From a greasy hometown cheesestake to a cleansing fruit smoothie. Don't take a loaded wallet because you'll end up spending it all. There is so much to experience at reading terminal and I'll be back soon enough.

Huge enclosed market in the heart of Philly with about every kind of food that you could ever want. Definitely check out the groceries, which are definitely worth the walk, especially if you live in the city.

Best. Market. Ever. There's so much ridiculously good stuff here that you forget that one of the places is Tommy DiNic's. I live in Atlanta. I wish that instead of the Kroger or Publix they had a Reading Terminal Market near where I live. If that happened, I would certainly be triple my current body weight and basking in the glory of delicious obesity. It's almost torturous going through Reading and trying to commit to only one place! I only think that by choosing one place, I forgo another place. It's torture I tell you, torture! If you haven't been here, this should be at the top of your list of things to do in Philadelphia. Arm yourself with Tums, Pepcid, and Nexium. And enjoy it. Best. Market. Ever.

When it comes to food, you can find anything here.  Wait, let me rephrase.  You won't food anything average or bad here.  It's almost like all the food vendors wants to show off who has the biggest muscles here.  Everything was awesome from the roast pork subs, hand made pretzels to the fresh donuts.  I highly recommend taking a tour to get the history behind this market as well.  It completes the experience.

Best place to visit when you have a terrible hangover. Many would disagree and say it gets way to crowded if your not feeling up to par in the morning. Great selection of greasy fat sat food varieties that make your hangover go away. Pastrami sandwich or my hangover fix favorite chili cheese dog with the works. Yep sounds gross right but it works every time. Sometimes you need a over flow of extra fatty goodness to sop up the alcohol still swooshing around in your gut from the night before. Trust me it works and this is the place to get a variety of tasty treats to easy the pain away.

There are lots of really fantastic finds in the Reading Terminal Market.  I was in town for fives day for work and I can't tell you how wonderful it was to get fresh produce and healthy snacks to balance out days of frequently crappy restaurant food.  

There were some amazing stalls that sold teas and herbs and sorts of goods.  If I hadn't had to fly I would have loaded up!   I also wish I could have gotten my hands on some of that amazing looking seafood!  

My only real complaint is that I wish they stayed open a bit later.  At the very least I wish all the stalls stayed open until the market closed.  Unfortunately, many seemed to be closed or closing about an hour before the whole market did.

Ok I know what you're thinking-- another gastropub. But it's a good one. If this is your neighborhood bar-- you're one lucky bum. Mac and cheese croquettes? Yes. Part of the happy hour special?? YASSS. The kimchi tater tots were a lot more interesting sounding than tasting, but still fun. The burger was delicious and gone in two seconds. I like the range in prices for food, so you can get small stuff or go on and get fancy and get the large plates. I do like the atmosphere-- small, but not claustrophobic. Definitely worth a happy hour visit at least!

Best sandwiches I've ever had. They toast them, which is a huge plus, and there are a huge assortment of toppings (oregano, oil, peppers, lettuce, onion, mayo, mustard etc.).

They also give you the option of adding mushrooms or bacon for a little extra.

Delicious whole pickles available is an additional plus.
I enjoyed reading Terminal Market. so much to see so much food. I sampled the Cajun food and it was very good. so I will be going again

Whenever I go to this side of town, I try to plan it around when this market will be open.  It's basically just a large, indoor market where a lot of people working in this part of town will come for lunch and to grab some goodie groceries and a few knick knacks to go.  There's so much though it's easy to get distracted so if you're on a time limit, go in with a plan.  But there are a lot of fresh produce, specialty stands (everything from cheese, chocolates and meats to soaps,) and Bassets ice cream so it has everything I need in life to be happy (and clean).  I think I used to think it was kind of expensive, but after nearly 5 years in CA and shopping SF markets, I don't think so anymore.  

  :')

I've only visited Philadelphia once but I could happily spend all day at Reading Terminal Market. I love Dutch Eating Place for their counter breakfast. But there are amazing stalls all over, from bakeries and cake stalls to butchers and wine bars.
A must go! A lively indoor market with endless food opportunities. The diversity is is very fitting for this city of neighborhoods. Check out DiNic's for a roast pork sandwich

Super cool market! You can eat any and everything here and it all looks amazing. Only tried DiNic's here, but next time I visit Philly I will have to try more! I cam here around 9am on a Saturday morning and this place wasn't super packed at all. All the stands were open and everything looked superfresh. Definitely a place to visit if you love food and specialty items!

You can't visit Philly without going here. Reading terminal is the epitome of Philadelphia life, such a great melting pot with everything you want. Be sure to check out Beilers, the best homemade donuts in the city. Also great hidden treasures like Molly Malloys and Pearls Oyster Bar. The possibilities are nearly endless! Also make sure to stop my meltkraft, the best grilled cheese in the city by far!! Either way, you'll always have a good meal at reading terminal.

The breakfast at the diner was delish! 
This place is HUGE and I got lost trying to find the ladies room. You could spend the day there.
Sooo much variety of great food it's amazing! Donuts, bakery, bbq ribs, Indian, Chinese, gyros, amazing ice cream! It's never ending deliciousness...left in a food como...lol

lovin' it so far!

it's fantastic that this is accessible on a late night and usually on my way home!  although, it's couple dollars more than your food truck meal.  the food here is fresh and clean! one platter portion can easily feed me for 2 meals! 

i also shared the take outs with my bf and he had no idea that it wasn't the halal guys! MK has got it going! it would be great if they offer falafel too!

PS. don't forget the 10% off coupon with your check in!

This is a great place for tourists and locals alike! I come here all the time to buy produce, bread, and cheese at many of the different food stands. It's a great place to shop because if you can't find something at one shop, you're bound to find it a few steps away at another one. They also have a great selection of lunch options -- Chinese, Greek, Indian, and of course cheesesteaks. I always bring friends and family who are visiting Philly here, and it never disappoints.

Places not to be missed:
Beiler's Bakery
Le Bus Bakery
Iovine Brother's Produce
Bassetts Ice Cream

Awesome, wonderful place.  There is something here for everyone. If you are in the mood for anything from Thai curry to chocolate covered onions, it is sold somewhere in this Market.  I would suggest Sang Kee Peking Duck Wonton Soup, Dutch Eating Place, Bassetts Ice Cream, and DiNic's Roast Pork Sand which (featured on Man vs. Food). The building itself offers restrooms and three separate seating areas to enjoy your goodies (FYI, they get filled very quickly).

Also, be sure to hit the Market on a Tuesday - Saturday because the Amish stores are closed on Sunday and Monday and they are definitely a must-try!
Stumbled upon the place while heading home from a night of cocktails... OMG... so good! Affordable, open late and so flavourfully yummy! will def be back!

La Fourno trattoria  this restaurant is a find for us.  We really never go to south street.  But who would believe 636 south street would have a hidden treasure.  We had one of the best Italian dinners the four of us ever had in 
Philly.  The Shoenfeld's and Weintraub's who love to try good restaurants downtown in philly and NYC.  Found a gem tonight.  The service was superb, the meal extraordinary.  The salmon was sone perfect and generous, the veal parmigiana was the best we ever ate.  Special salad was great and dessert outstanding. We highly recommend you trying this Italian gem.

The market has a huge selection of food outlets and it's always busy. Personally I find it a bit overwhelming on weekends and around lunch, so I'd recommend not visiting during those times. However, if you like a bit of bustle and loads of dining options, you'd struggle to find anywhere better in Philadelphia.
Lots of great places inside. 12th Cantina and DiNic's are a MUST!

Ashton Apartments on Wilshire has great service.  We actually never moved in, but the help we received from Alexandra Trudeau was incredible.  She answered all our questions and provided anything we asked for promptly.  She was friendly and so accommodating.  I highly recommend speaking to her if you are in the market for a luxurious place to live.

The Reading terminal is a lot like the Milwaukee Public Market but on crack.  

If you're from out of town, definitely plan to go at a non peak time or else you run the risk of being engulfed by the masses and carried away into a sea of schwarma.  

Don't miss: amish pretzels, grabbing a drink at the bar and people watching, or an authentic philly cheese steak

I also really wanted a miniature rhubarb pie that was being sold by one of the amish vendors, but never got back to it.   

The only thing I was really disappointed by was the miserable organic selection at the grocery section, despite a huge banner that says "organic"

Sat outside for dinner this past Saturday. Such a great find! Loved their extensive beer list; it was nice to see some different breweries highlighted. We split the oysters, watermelon and feta salad, and korean pork BBQ sandwich. Everything was excellent. Service was also wonderful. Will be coming back.

Amazing selection of food vendors. This is definitely a must for any person stopping by in Philly. I stopped by on a weekday and the marketplace was still pretty busy. It seemed like a mix of regulars who worked around the area as well as tourists. There are plenty of seats throughout the market, so I wouldn't be too worried about that.

Love them! Check out Valley Shepherd Cheeses  - best grilled cheese in town and the Produce place (there are two, both great but the corner one is dynamite!). Love love love. I suggest for both locals and tourists!
Really cool place with lots of options. The pork sandwiches from Dinics are awesome. If I lived in Philly I would shop here regularly for groceries. Can get pretty crowded.

One of my favorite places in Philly. I come here to buy my veggies, deli meats, bread and sweet treats. The amish have the bakeries on lock and make some of the most wonderful donuts, pies, and cakes! Their cheese and deli meats are always a million times better than anything you can get in a store and their prepared foods are great too! The 4 Seasons juice bar is amazing as well! Be careful coming around lunch time though-- this place gets mobbed!! Way too many people to enjoy your time-- you're better off coming mid morning or after lunch.

For starters, this place is overwhelming.  With that being said, you need a plan of attack before purchasing any food.  Please take this as a warning that if you buy something to eat at the first place you come across, you will be upset because the next place you come across will be even better than the first and it's an endless cycle.  My advice: Do a dry run of the places so you know where you would like to dine.  I started out with an roasted pork sandwich for Dinics.  The line wrapped around the counter, but it was worth it.  The sandwich was HUGE!  I then saw people walking around with ice cream and knew that was what I had to head to next.  We stopped at Lancaster County Dairy.  I had one of their specialty ice creams which was coffee ice cream with peanut butter cups in it.  Mmm!  Seating is kind of scarce, but people didn't seem to hang around for too long after eating, so you will eventually find a place to sit down and enjoy whatever you purchased.
Always an adventure...whether you want a meal, or flowers, or great pastries!  This is a must experience.

Unbelievable customer service for a fast food restaurant!!! I've eaten a lot of fast food and the customer service has gone down over the last 35 years of my life. I love fast food and I'm a little over weight. Here is what I experienced:
- the person taking my order didn't take the next order until my order was complete
- the booths were easy to sit down in because I have a belly to fit into it. I don't think the booths are wider but the table is shorter in depth
- a manager walked around and asked every one dining in if they needed anything including asking everyone if they wanted a refill and even took away my post meal tray

I am very impressed!

PS Classic chicken sandwich with jack cheese was unbelievably good!

I was running errands in the neighborhood and walked past this place quite by accident. I'd been hearing lots of great stuff about it and wanted to try, so I walked in. My impression was that this place does in fact live up to the hype. I had brunch there and the service was very good. I ate at the bar and the bartender was super-nice and very friendly and welcoming. They have a decent draft list--not very long, but there are some really nice selections on there. They also have a full bar, although I had a beer and didn't try any cocktails.

I ordered the shrimp and grits and although in some ways it is a simple dish, a lot can go wrong and I was pleased that everything about it was perfectly executed and showed some admirable technique on the part of the kitchen. The shrimp themselves were cooked just exactly right--still so tender and of course they were delicious Gulf shrimp with oodles of flavor. The grits were hearty and comforting without being heavy. They put two poached eggs on top and that was a heavenly yolky touch.

The decor is sleek yet homey and inviting. I'd definitely come back here for a dinner with friends or for drinks. I really felt that everything about my experience there today was on point.

This is the Kraftwork of South Philly, and I mean that as a serious compliment.

My boyfriend and I stopped in here late on a Thursday night. We were quickly seated, given water and menus, and told about the specials.

The atmosphere is so cool. Well laid-out with interesting decor, it's clear that someone is paying attention to the details. The space doesn't feel crowded, and there is a variety of seating options - large tables, small tables, bar seating, and outdoor tables (though that stops at 9 or 10pm).

Beer list: a great selection of craft beers and "the usuals" for the uninitiated - I had a hard time deciding what to drink.

Menu: This is where The Industry doesn't get 5 stars. The meat-containing options on the menu are in line with pricing at similar places, but the vegetarian options are obscenely overpriced. My boyfriend had a cheeseburger, which was large (and tasty, apparently). It came with a mountain of really good fries that I selflessly helped him to conquer. My entree consisted of 3 sweet corn arepas with mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes, and a small dollop of creme fraiche. It was just okay, nothing amazing. Those ingredients in that quantity just don't add up to a $15 price tag. 

Overall, a great spot for beer-lovers, omnivores, and... trust fund vegetarians. I'll definitely be back for drinks.

NATIONAL TREASURE STOP #3

Yes, this is the place where Diane Kruger got her cinematic start as she courageously hid behind the counter from Sean Bean and the bad guys. Yeah, I made that up, but I didn't make up all of the many unique items that you can get at Reading (pronounced 'redding') Terminal Market like:
- Pickles by the barrel
- Donuts
- Freshly baked sticky buns
- Huge breakfasts at the Dutch Eating Place
- Cheeses
- Groceries
- Bassett's Ice Cream for the country's oldest ice cream shop
- Roast pork sandwiches at DiNic's
- Cajun food at Beck's

This market is old and charming. Plenty of seating throughout the market so a great place to get some food before you head out to Independence Hall. Bring cash.
It's ok. Farmer's market and Amish folks have good stuff. Not wow in general .

Various eateries and businesses. From cheese steaks to wine & cheese to rotisserie chicken to fresh fruit & veggies. A little bit of every thing. Try Herschel's sandwiches, Big enough for two people. Termini Bros. Bakery...delicious!!!

The real life Philadelphia version of Diagon Alley, Reading Terminal market is the place to go for fresh produce, fish, meat... and just about anything. This collection of food vendors is a great place to find whatever you need for your next dinner party. The produce is some of the biggest that I have ever seen. The grapefruits were the size of two fists! Also, the Amish sell freshly baked bread and pastries during the week. Yum! Reading Terminal is also a great place to walk around and just look at all the unique foods and wares for sell.

This is as Philly as it gets. To go to Reading Terminal is not a visit, it is an experience. I frequent this place and always take anyone who visits Philly to this unique Philly destination. Be it any weather it is always a hit. My fav restaurants are Kamal's, Beck's Cajun, the fish and chips place (I forget its name) and the ice cream place. I have also purchase fresh meat from there and it is darn good. Be careful not to get lost (I still get lost in that place after more than 10 visits) and make sure you check out the train exhibit.

This is SUCH AN AWESOME PLACE to walk around and just explore! It can get a bit packed during lunch hour so try to come off-peak times. The market is set up so it's pretty easy to navigate because it's in a grid form. There are maps around area so it's easy to find your way. There's also a couple of small seating areas and some restaurants have their own seating area. 

There is just an abundance of good here! All sorts of food: Chinese, Indian, Seafood, Philly cheese steaks, Southern, bbq ribs, donuts, pastries and dessert, and more! There are also some other types of vendors: bookstore, honey store, salami and cheese, groceries, and farmer's market? 

The only thing is that the popular places may have a long line so it may be a bit of a wait, but it's such a cool place to just visit and walk around in!
So worth the long lines. Go early to avoid them. They seek everything and the fruit is really cheap.
Yep, it is as good as it gets.  We eat here whenever we are in the area.  Be sure to try Carmens for a hoagie and check out Beilers for donuts.

This really is the quintessential Philly must-see. Really fun on a crowded Saturday afternoon with dozens of food stalls, mostly manned by genuine Pennsylvania Dutch shopkeepers with great foods from probably the best doughnuts you can get (get in the looooong line and wait!) to made to order gourmet corn dogs, DiNics Philly roast pork sandwiches and even a fully stocked Irish Pub with attached seating where you can bring your food and grab a beer to wash it down. Packed with tourists for a reason, so enjoy!

Absolutely one of Philly's best attractions and lunch spots!
Shop there for dinner parties.
Love Hirschel's Deli counter for lunch!

A great Philly experience. There are office workers mingling with tourists and families in town for the afternoon. Everyone comes for the huge portions at unheard of bargain prices. Everything is fresh and made from scratch. Outstanding bread, produce, fish and meat also.

I usually stop in here when I'm already in the area for something else, such as the Philadelphia Car Show. If I lived closer I think I'd be here every day. The Reading Terminal Market has a little bit of everything and its all amazing. 

Unfortunately they close early so I can only make it there on weekends. Its always pretty crowded on weekends but very well worth it. 

Parking ( I got this from their website)

You can park for up to 2 hours for just $4.00 in the 12th & Filbert street garage.

Here's How:

    * Park ANYWHERE in the 12th & Filbert garage and receive the parking discount.
    * Bring your parking ticket to the Market with you.
    * Any Market merchant will validate your ticket with your purchase of $10 or more.
    * Upon returning to the garage lobby, you will place the parking ticket into the pay station and your parking rate will be reduced to a flat rate of $4 for up to two hours.
    * After two hours, regular garage rates will apply.

Stopped in here this morning because it was the only healthy option in the terminal. Pleasantly surprised by the menu selection. I was in the mood for a smoothie of the fill-me-up variety, not just fruit juice. Chose the muscle builder one in a size small and it hit the spot. Good of you like peanut butter with your fruit. Nice and freshly made to order. It was about $6 so I don't feel it was over priced for what I got in relation to where I was. 

The service is what is somewhat lacking here. I understand not liking your job but I don't want to be afraid you might not care enough to make my food correctly. The register clerk was cheerful and made up for it. 

I'd go here again if in the terminal.

They have it all!!!! It's a one place stop and it is different.
Visit around any holiday and you will fall in love with this place

I have been here twice now and every time I always find something different. Its located just outside of Chinatown in a pretty big building. The food selection was HUGE! We ate at some appetizers at Sang Kee duck house and liked it so much we went to the actual restaurant. All the food looked so amazing and there were so many variety that you can satisfy any cravings. They also had some really good ice cream, chocolates, sweets, candies, etc. It really does satisfy every cravings. Also, the vendors here are really nice and they have some really cool handmade things that you wouldn't get anywhere else. The veggie and fruit stands have food that were cheaper then the regular store prices. Too bad they dont have this in Washington DC or else i would go here everyday. 

If you are in philly and end up in Chinatown you should definitely stop here. You will find basically everything.
I love it! Every time I step into Reading Terminal, the memories flood back to me. I try to get there once a month at least. Love the energy and the food!

As expected, crowded with lots of good food and reasonable prices. Cheesesteaks from the place next to Termini Bros. bakery (forgot their name) were very good and the bakery was outstanding - cannolis were some of the best we've had, including NE Pa., NYC and upstate NY. Filling did not turn watery even on the second day. Limoncello cake, chocolate mousse cake and tieramasu cake were loved by our group. No one wanted to share. Will try more shops on our next trip.
Not to be missed!  All kinds of wonderful food, fun to just look even if you don't want to eat - a true Philly staple.  Especially if you're visiting make sure to check it out.

Food was meh! Nothing special to note nor anything horrific to report. It was all "fine". Drinks were nice enough with the exception of the bar having no blender so margaritas etc weren't possible. Real positive of this place is the staff. Attentive, friendly and efficient. If you find yourself in the area pop in for a drink! You won't be overwhelmed but you certainly won't be disappointed.
Nice place to visit while in Philly. Dutch Eating Place ( great b'fast ), Beck's Cajun Cafe ( alligator ), Dinics ( awesome roast pork/broccoli rabe hero )...

Their tomato pie is best I've had in Philly, but the plain pie is no slouch: thin crust, cooked well, flavorful sauce. I'd put it up against any slice. These guys are a worthy successor to Beddia, no doubt.

I am beyond impressed by the quality, flavor and variety of foods available. If I didn't have to eat more healthy then well I'd probably be eating here! The chaas is amazing btw and so is their Chicken Tikka Kati Roll.

Possibly my favorite place to eat in the city. Great environment, even better eats. You can get anything from sea food and burgers to award winning grilled cheese. They also have some of the best ice cream you've ever tasted. Overall amazing experience and would highly recommend

I am a sucker for Sunday mornings at the Terminal Market, however I only spend minimal time inside. I like to get there early to get my fruits and vegetables and get out-it becomes too busy and crowded for me! It's pretty great though if you just want to grab a bit to eat during the week or have friends in town who'd like to taste a variety of food in the city.

Went here for Sunday afternoon snacks, around 2pm. This place is great and I'm a big fan of marketplaces like Pike Place and Chelsea Market, so I had to go visit. It's located conveniently near the Convention Center, so if you're ever in town for an event there it makes it perfect for grabbing an affordable meal. 

For a Sunday a lot of the vendors were open. It was nice to just walk around and see all the varieties of food available. It seems like they have everything  from Indian to Mexican to Kosher Deli to Crepes. Along with prepared food, there are numerous meat, cheese, produce, bread, bakeries, chocolate, etc vendors. It is a foodie's heaven as any market is.  It was pretty busy around the one entrance we came through as a produce/meat stand was right there. My companion and I setted on some fried chicken from Delilahs which I was told was beat by Bobby Flay during a Macaroni and Cheese smackdown challenge thing. Afterwards we went to Flying Monkey Bakery for brownies and walked around. There is plenty of seating, as most food stands have counter seating and there are tables and chairs located throughout the market. The only downside is that there is one bathroom and it's pretty small so you probably have to wait.  

Aside from food, there are several plant, gift, etc vendors. It's definitely a place you want to check out when you're visiting Philadelphia, especially when you are hungry and indecisive, because I'm pretty sure you'll be able to find something there! If not, then there is something wrong with you.
This place is so fun and the food is excellent!  I had a great almond croissant and a Philly cheesesteak!!!

I went on a Sunday and kept reading that the lines get crazy as this was true, in my opinion the lines move so fast that it doesn't feel like a bother. They have stations set up that will prevent getting lost. There are a lot of eateries and I am def coming back to try more. Only thing is next time I will bring wet wipes because it can messy. I was fortunate to try 3 different places here. I got the Olympia Gyro's, Basset's Ice Cream and than to finish the food coma I got some cookies from The General Store. 

Olympia Gyro's- They were so good, soft warm pita bread with freshly sliced lamb. The Gyro sauce compliments the wrap nicely. Nothing over powers another its just the right blend you want.

Bassets Ice Cream- Massive scoops. I bought some for my sister and she was amazed when she seen her cone. I got the Butterscotch Vanilla in a waffle cone. It was both creamy and sweet and the waffle cone was satisfying. It was a big cone.

PA General Store- I got Top 3 best cookie I ever had in my damn life. I got the Lemon and White chocolate, The Turtle, and the Original Chocolate Chip Cookie. I would def shop by the pound next time. Don't make the mistake and not bring back extra for home.
Great general market; third and fourth generation market-stalls for produce, meat, groceries of all kinds. Especially love the Italian bakery Termini Bros.

The Reading Terminal Market is right by 12th and Market and behind the gallery old market east station and now Jefferson Station. . They have a other of stuff and variously from meats to pastries even restaurants.  Has been around for over half a century. It is a diamond in the rough for those of us from and raised in Philadelphia. I highly recommend this place to any tourist.

We went here on our vacation and I loved it! It's crowded so maybe not the place for small children. We got small servings of all sorts and then sat and had a feast. If you're visiting Philadelphia and love food or culture this is definitely for you!
Its a pretty neat market, but definitely a little over-rated in my opinion. Try going on a weekday when it is less packed so you can try more!
So much variety in one place!!  One of my favorite places to go when in philly.  Several different places to get a cheese steak and all quite decent.  Be prepared for long lines on the weekends!
One of my favorite places to go in the city! Plus I do my grocery shopping here. Great prices on Meat and Produce
Great place to bring tourists, lots of good, high quality food, but it's just so crowded and I'm not sure you can get anything here that you can't get at DiBruno Brothers.

Great! A wonderful selections of meats, produce, cheeses, seafood and just about everything in between. Sure it's touristy but what a place if you're a local. So much great foods under one roof with relatively reasonable prices. I'm game.
fresh vegetables, reasonable prices. great tasting baked goods (especially the donuts). great place to spend an hour every weekend

Still the best! ------I'd give it 5 stars if it weren't for all the tourist traffic. Stick to weekdays to avoid the ridiculous and obnoxious tourists.

-Iovine Brothers Produce
-Amish pickle barrels
-Molly's - Gotta love grabbing a shot and beer while grocery shopping!
-Dinic's
-Jonny Yee's seafood is the best in the city!

The list goes on and on.

There are a lot of positives about RTM:

There is an abundance of food options. If you're in the neighborhood and want something fast and tasty, this is a good place to go. You can choose to sit down and eat (like at Molly Malloy's) or you can grab something fast and walk around with it (Olympia Gyro).

I am also particularly fond of the home made chocolate retailers. Yum!

The main reason that we go to RTM, though, is for the humanely raised and organic meats. There are several Amish stands that specialize in selling *real* meat (not genetically modified, hormone-injected, tortured animals). You should check them out!

Parking can be a real bitch, though, so you're better off taking public transportation if you're not going to have too many bags to carry. There are also hordes and hordes of people, so if you've got social anxiety, this is NOT the place for you.

This place is like FOOD HEAVEN! Over 100 years old going strong and its a huge indoor market.  There are food places everywhere you turn in this market.  Everything from fresh made candy, to cooked duck, fresh produce, seafood, ice cream made from scratch, hoagie sandwiches....there is so much!  I grew up going to this place my grandpa would get me the rotisserie chicken wings they are so mouth watering.  Also, the Amish would come all the way from Lancaster on Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays to serve their fresh goods.  If you come to Philly and you have never visited the Reading Terminal, you are truly missing out on the culture.

I have been to Philly many times and confused as to why I've never been here. Anyway....This place is like a foodie heaven. They have everything to eat here. And it's fresh and good. 

They have fresh fruit, vegetables and meats also. 

I bought lunch meat and fresh bread. Some ribs. Smoked wings. Wanted Chinese food but didn't get it. Kevin Parker has a soul food stand in here. Picked up the specialty tea and a soul food dinner. 

I also had orange strawberry lemonade samples which led me to purchase some.

I tried gator gumbo which was delicious.  I had some pistachio ice cream from the ice cream place.

Trust me when I say this place is foodie heaven i mean it.  I have to go back on a Sunday so i can get the beignets from the cajun stand.

Food Heaven.  I love it here!

My first time going to Reading Terminal Market and it will not be my last. There's so much stuff to see and so many different foods to try, you literally can spend hours there. I had one of the best black and white cookies of my life. It's nice to walk around and people watch but obviously the best thing is the food. It was actually quite clean including the bathrooms.
