OMG so cool! This was definately one of the highlights.  I much prefer this place to the Ferry Building in SF as things are actually affordable.  Such a great place to stop in and grab almost anything to eat.  The best part was buying jam from the Amish.
Love it!!! A great adventure for date night. So many choices . Friendly and very clean for a market.

I've only tried one item - the tikka masala roll - and it was very underwhelming. The chicken tasted dry and there was barely any sauce. Also, not much flavor...which is strange for an Indian dish. No motivation to come back.

Visiting Philly for the first time, I was brought to the Reading Terminal marketplace. I was blown away! There's so much going on! In a good way. It felt like a busy outdoor food market, but inside! 

First things I immediately noticed were the variety of vegan options from many of the different vendors. I had some great vegan muffins, cookies, and treats. Very easy to get some much needed coffee. There was something for everyone.

I saw that they had a Filipino market event the weekend before. Too bad I missed it, but it's cool to see they host cultural events like that. I would guess it's a regular type of thing.

Definitely a must see if visiting from out of town. This place is on the top things to do in Philly and now I know why.

Loved the concept, however the market needs an upgrade! You get a ton of options: cheesesteaks, burgers, donuts, candy stores, butter specialities, ice cream, groceries, and so much more. I was actually visiting from Virginia for the day and only had time to do one thing - and I don't regret my decision.

Of all the places we could have visited for lunch, we of course chose Carmen's for their classic cheesesteaks. I've made it a tradition to try a different cheesesteak every time I visit philly, and this was probably one of the best thus far (second to Barclay Prime's if you count that)! The classic I got had mushrooms, onions, and sweet peppers, with the iconic cheese whiz on the bread. Full of flavor, however a little on the salty side with the cheese they used. The bread was my least favorite part, as I have definitely had better. It was kind of rubbery to me, but I did buy a few more for home and retoasting them made a huge difference. 

If people were to ask me what my favorite Philly cheesesteak is, I would refer them to Carmen's! (Also, Obama has been here too!)

This location is cool. It seems like their bread is too doughy. This Chick-Fil-A isn't as nice in some other areas I've been to. 

I took the two stars off because chicken sandwiches from here weren't nearly as hot as the other Chick-Fil-A's I've been to. 

But way better than going to a BK or McDonald's.
EVERYTHING IS DELICIOUS HERE.It's like my mouth died and went to heaven. Nothing else to say....

This place, on the first floor of the Reading Train Shed (a National Historic Landmark), is the largest tourist attraction in the city--beats the Liberty Bell. But it has fresh food merchants as well as a diner, and take out counters of almost any type of food. Cheesesteaks? got it!  Pennsylvania Dutch food? you bet! I love Reading Terminal Market for what it is, the place that sees everyone;  those that use food stamps (the highest number in the state); City Hall workers; convention goers, and residents hungry for lunch or dinner.

Finally a Snap in Rittenhouse!! Welcome to the neighborhood!! I was in the mood for something  healthy and fast for dinner so I decided to make a quick stop in on my way home from work. 

I left spending $16 on dinner but- I got the devily eggs, the chicken tikka masala, and the curry chicken salad. Yum! The eggs were fantastic and the yolks were replaced with hummus.  Great twist on a classic.  My chicken entrée was also satisfying and although the sauce was a bit on the sweeter side ( I was expecting more traditional Indian flavors) it was still very good.  Chicken salad was good but pretty basic and I wasn't a fan of the texture but super healthy and full of protein. 

I especially love that this place offers paleo options, carb conscious entrées and snacks, sodium friendly dishes, and gluten free options.  AND - these are offered across the board for all of their breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snack choices! SCORE. 

I'll be frequenting this place on the reg. 
Also- don't forget to sign up for rewards card!
great place - good selection of eats, interesting mix of  people (Amish servers, office crews, and wide eyed jurors), great CC respite.

It's a landmark and an icon you shouldn't miss if you have never visited. If you have and you're seeking nostalgia, you won't be disappointed. After a 20 hiatus, my heart was happy to find the Italian bakery with the pignoli cookies- as wonderful as ever!

My new favorite place for lunch!  The girl behind the counter was so helpful.  I asked for her recommendation and I am so glad I agreed!  I had the Keeme and the Masala rolls with the sauce she told me put on and omg I LOVE THEM!!!!  Both of them. I will be back. So yummy!!!

This chick-fil-a knocked customer service out of the park!!! They were pretty busy but the staff seemed to be working overtime to ensure food came out in a nice fashion. 

I also tried the cookies and cream milkshake which was $3.50. I like to think of myself as a milkshake connoisseur and these milkshakes were phenomenal. They exceeded in the areas of flavor, amount, and cost. Most milkshakes in Philly are around $5 small and seem to disappear in 30 seconds. This milkshake was on the thicker side so I really felt like I got my money's worth! 

In terms of the staple good, it was to be expected. The nuggets and fries hit the spot!

So many food choices! I was in heaven when I visited here. Lived in Philly all my life and just made it here recently. There's something for everyone here whether you want seafood so something sweet. There's take out food or you can eat in if you can find a seat. You can also shop here which is cool because mostly everything is local and fresh!

Wow, where to start. I grew up going to the Terminal and frequent it now with my family. It is perhaps the most fun place in the city to grab lunch or breakfast. You can get anything you want to eat -- our favorites are the huge blueberry pancakes at the Amish counter in the back, the Mexican foot at the Cantina, and the new grilled cheese stand. The Terminal is such a Philly experience that it shouldn't be missed by residents or visitors to Philly. 

A visit wouldn't be complete without dessert from either Fourth Street Cookies, a hand thrown soft pretzel dipped in butter from another Amish stand, or Bassetts Ice Cream. 

This place is Philly's own slice of heaven.

One of my favorite places in Philly, full of amazing food stalls, fresh produce, specialty items such as aged olive oils and herbs.

Yes, it is typically very packed but the hustle and bustle is worth it for the vast array of items available all in one place. I love its proximity to the Convention Center means a lot of out-of-towners get to experience this amazing piece of Philadelphia.

I can't wait for the City Kitchen to get going in full swing as I would love to take some cooking classes!

I LOVE PUBLIC MARKETS!!!!! 

I was a happy girl prancing around sampling, oooohing, Ahhhhhing and just bright eyed with all the possibilities in this place. One of the oldest public markets and I let me tell you it didnt dissapoint. 

The first place we wanted to visit was the Amish bakery and chocolate shop. They were closed and not there that  :( BOO I was so looking forward to yummy baked goods made with homemade everything. 

You know what made up for missing it? MY FIRST REAL CANNOLI !! Can you say happy dance? The Termini Brothers provided the most fresh, authentic and like your face good cannoli ever. I really wish I could have one right now. 

We then had about 3 different kinds of crepes at the Creperie. They were skilled in making some great crepes. Tasty. 

We had such a great time here.

Had two of the masala paneer rolls, mango laasi, and rice and honestly really enjoyed the meals.  The paneer rolls were very flavorful and the mango laasi was so yummy and thick. However my complaint was that this place is pretty expensive! We just ordered two rolls (which shouldn't be more than $2-3 because they are on the smaller side) but they were over $5 each!! Our total including delivery was more than $25 which is definitely too much for the little quantity we got.

New favorite place, hands down.  On Labor Day (and maybe it's a Monday thing?), they had $5 mimosas, beer-mosas, and Ghost of Mary - the menu describes it as a deconstructed Bloody Mary, our waitress explained it as veggie-infused alcohol.  It'll probably seem weird at first sip, but keep going - it's strangely good. 

Definitely a Monday thing is their burger and bubbles special - different burger each week, paired with beer or champagne, special price.  

On separate occasions I've tried the veggie scramble and duck confit hash, and both were fantastic.  The turkey bacon was nothing special but they prepared it as we asked (as crispy as humanly possible).  I tried my friend's falafel sandwich and it was stellar - who knew they'd do Mediterranean so well.

The menu's not terribly extensive, but I'll bet even picky eaters can find something that makes them happy, and more adventurous eaters won't be bored.  Prices are totally reasonable, the room is dark wood but lots of windows make it an inviting space, and the some of the staff make for delicious eye candy - win-win if you ask me.

Here once a week.  Cons: They deal with tourists all day, so sometimes you may not get great service, at some of the spots there.  But overall, I buy all my chicken, fish and alot of coffee there.  
Its a fun trip.  Better than going to the supermarket.

I came here after learning that the owner of Good Dog opened a new bar in South Philly. I have to say I prefer The Industry for it's cleanliness and ambiance. There is a lot of space between the tables and bar which you don't get at Good Dog. You can tell it is industry-themed, as they've posted bar rules everywhere. This is definitely a place for people who will respect the bar scene and not for rowdy sloppy crowds. 

They have a pretty good beer selection, and our bartender Mike was very friendly. We also ordered the bone marrow and lamb's neck gravy, which were delicious. I'll definitely be back for the lamb's neck gravy when it gets chilly in the fall!

Not a spot for the indecisive. You will walk around wanting something from every stand. This is a great spot for locals and tourists. Also, a unique spot to bring a date, would definitely impress me. Everything is reasonable and its always an experience. Great people watching!

Things you can't miss: the Amish's homemade donuts (go with the banana cream), the savory crepes, Dinic's pulled pork sandwich with broccoli rabe, and termini brothers canolis to name a few!

For the full experience avoid this spot on Sundays. You will miss all of the Amish treats.

This place has so much to offer! You walk in and there are people everywhere. Good luck finding somewhere to sit because the eating area is packed but it is well worth the search to find a seat! 
 There is one place that serves Curry salmon over white rice and broccoli and its delicious! the salmon is cooked so delicately that it breaks the moment you touch it with your fork. The sauce on the salmon seeps onto the rice on the bottom that gives it a smoked taste.  
 This market has clothes, trinkets, food you name it. You could spend hours in here just lurking around at it all. If you want some fresh produce definitely check out Iovine Brothers!

Love this place.. soooo
Many food and very affordable. From seafood to burger to Mediterranean to Asian and desserts.. can't beat that cuz it's all under one roof.. one days isn't enough for a visit. Because my stomach can't hold everything I want to try.. lol..
Not only is it a classic tourist destination,  but the food is great!  Check out the Cajun place.

Edit: much more savory. Amazing service and food. Remind all my friends to go here especially at 1am!

The quality of service is superior to Halal Guys; however, it is not as savory when it comes to the rice. The chicken is good but not great. If the seasoning is strengthened, this place will definitely have my 5 star approval. The bread is also not as crunchy, at least when comparing takeout between the two competitors.

Made a trip to the RTM last night and it was amazing, as usual.  Walking into the RTM is like taking a step back in time when people actually shopped their local markets.  Although those times have past (in the age of Giant, Acme, Super Fresh, etc) the one thing that holds true is that the quality at the RTM is far superior and full of ethnicity.  10 stars if I could!

Oh my goodness. This place is unbelievable. You absolutely have to go here if you are visiting Philly, ideally for lunch or an afternoon snack. Even if you're not even hungry, this is a place to see - it is that impressive. 

My understanding is that this is an old train terminal now transformed into a gigantic marketplace. From Indian and Chinese food to baked goods and even a small bookstore, this place has so many unique items. 

There's tables in the middle where you can bring your food and eat. Definitely have to experience firsthand as words do not do this place justice!

The only thing I dislike about Reading Terminal is that it is so far from my house. I really only get to go every so often when I have friends visiting from out of town! Perfect place for tourists and locals, alike. I usually have a divide and conquer routine when I walk through the doors. This way, you save on time, hit all the spots, and when you find a seat, you can each try a little bit of everything! The stands I always hit are: Dinic's (roast pork), Herschel's (pastrami), and Meltkraft (grilled cheese). For dessert, Basset's (ice cream) and Beilers (donuts). Everyone raves about the fritters at Beilers, but theyre much too sweet and oily for my liking. On the other hand, the plain glazed and powdered cream donuts are life changing. I'm hoping to branch out and maybe check out the Dutch Eating Place or maybe some of the seafood stands soon!

Tip: if you're bringing a car, you can park in the garages marked for reading terminal, grab a voucher, and get it validated by any vendor in the market when you spend over $10. 2 hour parking for $4!

THE place to go in Philly for foodies and for high-quality ingredients.  All kinds of shops and food vendors in this place; if there's something that you want food-wise, it's likely that you'll be able to find it all under this one roof.  The location is really cool, too; it's an old train station that has been turned into this awesome foodie paradise.  If you love food and are visiting/live in Philly, this is a must-go place!
Absolutely amazing!!  You can find almost anything you are looking for all under one roof.   Seating can be tough to find, but DiNic's and all of the other great merchants make it worth it!!
Love Beiler's donuts and butter cake from Flying Monkey bakery. Also place with lobster mac and cheese is amazing. Always buy my cheese and crackers here too.

The best paneer I've ever had! I got an Aloo Paneer Roll and Masala Chai and my friend got Chicken Masala Roll and Rose Lassi. We both loved our meals. Can't believe I've never been here before! Total find.

Extremely mediocre. I got the turkey chipotle Panini-the pickled onion was just not working. The employee working the cash register was being very rude to the other two employees and you could tell they were miserable. She was very unprofessional and obnoxious. It took about 18 min to get my panini and there was no line, so don't come here in a time crunch.

I have a deep love for Reading Terminal Market. This truly is Philadelphia at it's finest.  There are only 2 issues I have with this smorgsboard of food. The first is that it is almost impossible to decide what to eat. The second is that the amish are not there everyday. Is there anything sadder than when you go to lunch at reading terminal on Monday hoping for some apple dumblings, scrapple, assorted freshly baked breads and fresh deli meats only to find 1/4 of the market is barren and cold? It's at this time when I remember my other options including the turkey cranberry and stuffin' sandwhich special at The Original Turkey and a giant peanut butter cookies at Famous Fourth Street. 

So, try to avoid days when the Amish stands are not open, but if you happen to stumble upon the market even during these off days you are still in for quite a treat. Good luck deciding what you want to eat before your friends have gotten their food and area already half way done.

You can find a plethora of goods at Reading Terminal Market. In one outing, you can have breakfast, lunch, and dinner, as well as get your grocery shopping done. I have not had one disappointing meal from the Market, and would highly recommend it during a trip in Philadelphia.
Amazing place for a big appetite. There are plenty of places to choose from, but one of my favorites is the Thai spot with the Curry Salmon. Try it and you won't be disappointed!

Love it here! The numerous shops and restaurants can become a little overwhelming but there is definitely something for everyone. A must-do on anyone's Visit Philly list! There's always something going on, and it really doesn't matter what you're craving Reading will have it there and ready for you in no time. If you're feeling extra hungry definitely stop by Valley Shepherd Creamery & Meltkraft for an artisan grilled cheese. They are fabulous.
Super busy place with tons of food choices.  Many venders with everything from cheese to meat, ethnic food, bread, coffee, and cookies.  I think this is a must see when visiting Philly.

Reading Terminal Market is one of the great places to go in Philadelphia.  It's vibrant, energetic and a sensory overload - in a good way.  You have many choices of places to eat and to shop for fresh meats, fish, deli items and odds-n-ends you don't find in many places.
To get the best feel of what Philly has to offer, this place is a winner for sure!!

I've been there a few times, since I'm from Philly  We tend to walk around to see all the different vendors first.
Then we sit down to order at a counter or table (depends on what we have a taste for)  They have the best fresh fried fish plates  
I'm looking forward to eating there again when I visit

My mom always said if you don't have anything nice to say don't say anything at all. So I didn't. Until my third visit to Industry.

The space is fantastic: industrial, sexy, large, spacious (especially for Pennsport) and ample outdoor seating. The bar is pretty big, has a good selection and apparently draws a good crowd for quizzo.

For the first time, the service was fantastic -- our server was friendly, helpful and on the ball. In the past, service was super slow and vaguely surely. 

But the food is what's got me on the fence between 3 & 4 stars. The menu is huge with many appealing options. In past visits, I felt like I made the wrong choice: dumplings were small and flavorless, burger wasn't well cooked, eggs were lukewarm. 

But this time everything we ordered was stellar -- from the free coffee cake to the coffee my parent's raved about to the special (a Dutch baby which is basically a stuffed pancake, in this case with poached eggs  and fennel sausage), the BBQ Korean beef sandwich AND the biscuits with gravy. It all rocked. 

It did take awhile and it wasn't overly busy but I'll wait for something that good.

Which Is why I am torn. If I were just rating it on my visit last weekend, it would easily get 4 stars. And I'm cautiously optimistic about trying it again. Soon. So when I do, assuming it's on par with my recent visit, I'll, update my review with the extra star I feel like it will likely deserve.

The food mecca of Philly. While not condusive to the kosher minded,the amounts and types of hot food available will fit anyone.TThe stalls seling ingrdients from flour to spices is mind blowing.here is even one that sells their hot food by the pound and offers dozens of choices.Just make sure your eyes aren't bigger than your wallet.If you hit Philly,putting the Terminal is a must add to your tour of the city

I had the lamb Kati roll, extra spicy, and the rose lassi. It was pretty good! The naan was soft and warm, the lamb mixture was flavorful. Some of the spices were not fully ground up, resulting in the occasional bite of whole cardamom. Apart from that, the prices are good and the service is fast. Ordering ahead online is a huge plus. I can see this being a great late night spot also.
I always go for The Original Turkey!!! It's like Thanksgiving all year round!!!

Friendly staff but since this location opening I've been there so far a total of 4 times and they are always OUT OF SOMETHING and the wait for the missing item is always 1/2 hour to 45 minutes. I've even been there at opening (EXACTLY 11am) and there was no tomatoes and the pork still had to be cut up, as well as other items that still needed to be brought up to the line. It's very much a disappointment and inconvenience when these things are happening frequently. I've always gone to the chipotle by Neshaminey Mall and that location has been there for A WHILE and NOT ONCE have I ever been told they are out of something or that I have to wait for something. I'm from the northeast and thought this chipotle opening up was great and would be more convenient since its closer but I'd much rather make the drive to the other one knowing ill get what I originally wanted and came for.. Not sure what's going on with management and operation at the Cottman ave location but you need to get it together.

So much under one roof. From cookies and desserts, to cheeses, to fried chicken! I did not get a chance to sample enough vendors. It was early on a Sunday and I was tired. Not my best performance. But overal, this is a great space. It is well organized, and had more than enough available seating. I was surprised at how clean it was and that fact that there was no lingering nasty food smells! Looking forward to paying it another visit when I am back in Philadelphia.
Try the pork sandwich, and the cookies, and the ice cream... really everything is great there!

Fun, but....almost no gluten free food (except a small selection in the bakery) and very little vegetarian stuff to take out or eat in (except the Indian stand) - the produce areas have little or no organic...so, if you have a dietary restriction or like to eat organic go elsewhere....the little kitchen store is very overpriced too....but it is a fun place to visit once or twice every year or 6.
Went here once. Got the Bassett's ice cream and that was awesome! We also ate somewhere else, but I can't remember where. But that was good too. Very crowded but worth all the trouble.

I have definitely reviewed Reading Terminal Market before but my review has disappeared :(

Regardless, this is a great market.  They have odd hours so make sure you get there early.  There are TONS of food places to shop around.  There is a huge assortment of cheese, meat, and candy.  I'm a fan of the Amish shops because they always have the best fudge and yogurt covered pretzels.  The only reason I had to knock off a star is because it gets very crowded in here, which in turn makes the place very warm and sometimes uncomfortable.  Still a great place to visit whenever you're in Philly.

Spoiled with choices.  I prefer the Dutch Eating Place for their extra large scrapple serving that comes as a side with a delicious pancake breakfast.  Afterwards, in true fat kid fashion, a stop at Beiler's for tasty doughnuts is a great way to pack on some additional calories.

Produce, preserves, legumes, wine (small selection), meats, fish, mouthwatering pastries, prepared food, plants.... and books even. Reading Terminal is fairly well-rounded market. Most places inside seem to only take cash, but they have ATMs inside. DiNic's was probably my favorite spot for something warm and delicious to eat. We ordered an italian pulled pork with sharp provolone and sweet and spicy roasted peppers. I normally don't eat this category of food, but wow--it was amazing.

I visited the other day and was amazed by the variety.  However, it was overwhelming because of all the options and all the confused people walking around making walk ways narrow.  With that said, I left with amazing chocolate covered pretzels.  It's safe to say that I enjoyed the variety of sweets offered.  

But, as a visitor from NJ I don't think that I'd come back just for the market.  Still, that doesn't take away from the chill atmosphere Philadelphia constantly provides.

Crowded but the best thing conferences can do it what they did when I recently attended a conference in the Marriott on Market:  give attendees a gift card to the Reading Terminal Market and let them pick their own meals.  The variety ranges from grilled cheese to Philly cheese steaks to pasta to barbeque to donuts to salads to cookies to oysters.  Seriously.  Whatever your people want to eat can be found  The only downside was the limited seating.

The food is the same quality as any Chipotle but the staff needs to be retrained. I've been to this location a few times and it's the same issues, every visit. A 30 minute wait because the food line seems to be confused and/or chatting - or maybe they just don't care about customer service.

My first stop is always Iovine Brothers where I can usually get a ton of produce for under $20, then I go to Old City Coffee to get my Beans for the week and the wine cellar for my vino for that night's dinner. I take the trolley from West Philly after work and it drops me right there. I love this Philly landmark.
Delicious burger and seafood blt. Awesome beer list and great/friendly service! Will definitely be coming back soon!
Iovine brothers, the Amish corner, it's all great.  Only downside is that it gets packed with tourists every weekend.

This is my favorite place to go & make up a meal to cook as I go.
Fresh meats, breads,fruits & veggies and cheese galore.

It's pretty much always busy so be ready for a crowd, but so worth it! A Philly treasure!

With so many choices and so many varieties, how does a person just pick one? I explored Reading Terminal Market for hours and love this type of setting, where I can get small snacks and meals from a bunch of different places and wander for hours checking out various stalls and what they offer. This is a must go in Philly, especially for out of towners. I have to say, I'm glad I don't live too close or I could definitely see my packing on major pounds from this market alone. Excellent concept and place!

This is a great place you must visit in Philadelphia. Many organic foods you can find here. We usually buy our honey and olive oils from here because the quality is just amazing.
One star off because of no free parking.

Looooove this place!!! I've been coming here for years and the food here never fails. You can get all kind of food here from all over the world. My favorite stand are Franks I love their chicken, hands down the best!!! If you have a picky friend who only wants to eat a specific kind of food I guarantee you find that specific food here! Super diverse and everything is really affordable. The best eats in philly. If you are looking for a fun, diverse and super cool eats this place is it foodies.

This place is the Mecca of food. You can find all types of assorted foods and goods. The place is bussling with people from all walks of life. It's hard to just pick one spot. A great place for tourists.
Love this place. Came with a large group and everyone was able to find something they wanted. Service is quick even during busy periods.

A philly yelper without a review of RTM? Impossible.

RTM equals love, basically. You can find something to satisfy whatever crazy craving you are having at that exact moment and then some.  Always a great place to take visitors too -  total crowd pleaser -plus you get to finally convince your friends that philly IS a cool place to live.

Come in and get lost in the commotion and wafting smells of deliciousness. Here's a short list of some of my favorite merchants:

Iovine Produce: CHEAP, high quality produce.
Downtown Cheese: Expensive but oh man, the appenzeller.
Tommy DiNic's: Best.Sandwich.of.My.Life. No big deal.
Little Thai Market: $5 for a huge portion of chicken, rice and creamy red curry sauce.
Old City Coffee: It's an addiction.

Come here on a weekday, if you can. This place makes me nervous on Saturdays.
Oh, and bring some cash.

I absolutely LOVE this place.  Lots to see and lots to EAT!  My brother and I were in Philly for a wedding and I had to visit this place to eat at DiNIC's!  Seeing this place from Man V Food was my source of finding out about this place and the PORK! O-M-G

So much to see and so much to eat at Reading Terminal, but this review will cover DiNICs.

When we first walked up to the counter we saw mounds of delicious pork behind the window!  You can see perfectly cooked pork just sitting there waiting to be someone's meal!  This was heavenly and awesome...i think i was drooling the whole time in line and I was in some sort of hog trance...lol.  You can see the oven in the back they use to cook the pork and also the awesome dripping from the pork they use as gravy when they dip the pork again when they make that sandwich.  I got mine with the green spinach-type pork sandwich.  That first bite was out of this world.  You don't get this in Texas for sure.  This place definitely made up for Geno's and Pat's.

Philly to me is not known for the philly cheese steak (i think texadephia here in Texas is a thousand time better), but for that awesome pork sandwich at DiNIC's!  I will definitely be back! Enjoy!
Great place to visit if you want to sample a lot of different cuisines and equally great if you want to do some unconventional grocery shopping.  I recommend it if you have some free time!

It was our second visit to Philadelphia and second visit to the market as well. We went to the Carmen's to get our favorite philly cheesesteak and Bassett's to get our favorite ice cream. We tried the "Philly's #1 Pecking Duck" from one of their Chinese places but it wasn't #1 honestly, there was fire alarm keep going on and off and at one point everyone was little confused but we were told by the information center's lady that we don't have to worry about it and if anything happens that she will be leaving. haha. Such a cute market that is actually serving a role as a market (not like a chelsea market, which became the place for tourists only).

Lots of good food here.
I cant help it, I'm a big fan of DiNic's roast pork sandwich.
Some friends were in town and we drove into Center City to prove to them why
 "Man vs. Food" voted them the best sandwich in America!

Easily a great location for locals and out of towners alike.

Where else can you get market staples, gourmet foods, candy, fresh seafood, artisanal cheese, Peking duck, hot gumbo, a cheesesteak, and an ice cream all within a few steps of each other? (And that's not all!). 

Definitely check out Bassett's and splurge with a big cone of two of their fresh flavors. Did you know that they are the first ice cream parlor in America?  Their ice creams still hold up and are some of the finest. 

Great people watching, shopping and eating.

Clean bathrooms too!  Definitely park in a garage. Street parking can be difficult with the ever changing temporary rules. You don't wanna get towed.
I'd say it's a "must do."

Sigh... I would love to write what I really feel.. but my wife likes this place..  hence the three stars otherwise it would be lower.. I do however like the decor.. and the mega sized drinks they got going.. and that's the extent of my positive review.. the food is salty.. feels greasy (I know it's fried stuff).. it's so greasy that they offer u disposible gloves to eat with.  I had the combo with the beef and chicken.. and let me tell u.. If I was blind.. I wouldn't have been able to tell u which meat was what... none of the dipping sauces were good..

There really isn't much I can add to the Reading Terminal Market so I will just review my personal experience. It will most likely be repetitive of other reviews for it, but oh well. 

First, we waited until Sunday to go, which I now wish we wouldn't have done since some of the PA Dutch vendors were closed. It was a rainy morning though, so venturing to the Reading Terminal Market was a timely idea since it is all inside. 

It was sort of like an indoor farmer's market, much like the sheltered waterfront market in Seattle. Different vendors selling all kinds of food items, many having a dine-in option, or at least counter service. You truly should come hungry. There are lots of items to choose from to sample, and buy to take with you. We actually came in the morning, and grabbed enough fruit, peanuts, and cheese that we just ate what we bought as we walked around all day so it was a really great option. We also bought some jams, cheese, and vegetables to take home with us. 

The only negative (but not worth a reduction of stars), because of it's location, there are some homeless people and scammers who know that tourists are there and ready to pounce on so there is that. We did have a few homeless people ask us for money, and another guy who tried to tell us that he had a kidney transplant and needed money to get back home, but we didn't let that damper our experience. We've been taken by this kind of things many times in the past. It has sort of become standard of our experiences nowadays.

I'm not a vegetarian but am a total veggie person and was stoked when I had a class nearby. I'd heard of this place but never tried it before. 

I went after class and there wasn't any line. The woman who helped me was patient as I asked questions and decided to make my own bowl. I got broccoli, edamame, carrots, onions, and green beans. Then I got quinoa and cilantro sauce. 

I didn't try any of the extra additions like avocado or meats but I may next time. 

My vegetables were perfectly cooked and all the flavors together were delicious. I'll be back many times this semester!

I've been to Reading Terminal Market dozens of times and always have a pretty standard routine, which I'm starting to believe that most people have a routine or atleast a set of Reading Terminal Market guidelines which is completely individualistic. What I mean is. I always have to start RTM with a vitamin B12 and wheatgrass shot from the middle eastern fresh juice place, then I wonder around looking for food, I always have to stop at the chocolate place and look at the hideous chocolate covered onion which I have tried by the way, end up eating either crepes, a hoagie, a collection of small treats really whatever tickles your taste buds that day.I pretty much end RTM by hitting up bassets. Thats my routine in a nutshell and I know everyone has thier own. 

Its the best part of RTM there is literally something for everyone. my reco is when you go with a group of friends just leave and do your own thing (unless you're doing the dinics thing) then don't be an ass and make your friends wait in line while you explore the glory of the market, wait with them, talk about the last night and how reckless it was. 

Sorry I got on a tangent, I actually feel like this whole review is a tangent. 

Go to Reading Terminal Market! eat lots of food and enjoy life because this is as good as it gets.

i love love love this place, where else can u go for a one stop shopping for fresh produce, yummy freshly baked goods, real southern cooking and ginormous crepes? it reminds of me a bigger and better Essex Street market in nyc.

A must see in Philadelphia. This market has something for everyone, including DiNic's (pork and beef), Wursthaus Schmitz (German), a deli, seafood, bakeries, coffee, ice cream, cheesesteaks, cajun, produce and more! The market is very popular and becomes crowded during lunch hours and on weekends, but it is definitely worth a visit. 

There are numerous seating areas but sometimes you must be patient if you are in a larger group that wants to sit together.

The ambiance is lively and if you are lucky, there will be someone playing live music.

Click that little red "X" at the top right hand corner of your screen and go right now.

Good excuses not to go:
Friend or family member will die if I leave right now.
House will burn to the ground (with pets inside)

Bad excuses:
I have to work.
I'm too drunk (Take the train).
I accidentally flushed my keys down the toilet (See above).
I am getting married today.
I have to study for a blood test.
I could go get laid instead.
Delicious food and great service. So happy to have another great casual lunch and dinner option in midtown village.

Every time I go to Philly I have to go to Reading Terminal.  Anything and everything you could possibly want can be found there.  I always go to Dinics for a brisket sandwhich with sharp provolone and greens.  There are many other great places.   Anything Amish is great!
so much different food to try, unfortunately many of the places are closed in Sunday, will have to come back again!

Great place to hang out with a group of friends. So many delicious options and you can literally hang out here for hours- eating, browsing around, eating some more and even catch a taping of a Food Network show. Husband thought the cheesesteak @ Carmen's was the best he's ever eaten (although the line was crazy long and they got his order wrong). Sang Kee is always good if you're in the mood for yummy noodle soups. Of course Delilah's is also a place to grab some good food- their mac n cheese is a MUST. Our kids (one of them being a really picky eater) devoured their fried chicken and mac n cheese. I was pretty disappointed with the gyro sandwich @ Kamal's however.  

Sooo many options for dessert too. We tried Flying Monkey for the first time since the Food Network were featuring them for a new show. The cupcakes were just ok although the best one is their signature Flying Monkey cupcake (rich chocolate cake with banana chunks and vanilla and chocolate buttercream). Bassetts ice cream is always a good place to stop by too. I like it that they are very careful in how they serve their ice cream for those with peanut allergies. Overall this is a great place to visit  you like having many delicious options and this is a great place to bring out-of-towners too!

I have yet to come across a place like this. Truly - RTM is one of a kind. From Pork hoagies, fresh chocolates, organic teas, to herbal health remedies, RTM serves people from all walks and wants of life.

Take the stroll - be mindful of others - try to avoid the lunchtime rush if you can
:)
Love this place. So much to eat and buy. Brought home pounds of bacon from the Amish

Worst chipotle experience I've ever had. Lettuce was brown, meat was cold, no fried vegetables, no eating utensils, coke was dispensing water and the chips were unsalted with no salt available to add it myself.

Superb little eatery in philly downtown area for indian street food lovers..  tasty and fresh made.
Left me satisfied

I love this place for all the amazing stuff to eat, but also for the incredible diversity. All classes, so many ethnicities...in terms of customers and businesses. So many new things to see/eat -- maybe a different version of an old favorite, or something totally new. Spent many hours there, but also have stopped in and been able to get out pretty quickly. Yum!

Over 100 restaurants inside.  This is the place to visit while in Philly.  You will be in food heaven!  Philly cheesesteaks, donuts, truffles, all kinds of sweets, oysters, lobsters, Chinese food, Indian food, Pakistani food, you name it, it's all here!  I can stay here for days!!!
I could have spent all day eating a wide variety of delicious foods. Sampled the Flying Monkey's Elvis Cake quite tasty.

What can I say?      From Famous 4th street cookies to Hershels East side Deli........Whatever you're hungry for, you can eat there or find all the ingredients necessary to prepare a great meal at home.

This is a great spot for lunch in Philly.  The hustle and bustle of the market is energizing and there are countless food options, some better than others.  I live in DC, and this is like a bigger version of Eastern Market.  Some places are specialty shops that look like they've been there for years because they turn out a high quality product.  Other vendors look no better than a typical mall food court operator, so pick your lunch spot carefully.  Still, it's a cool experience.

This place was really packed the Saturday we came. Our hotel was 9 mins away so we decided to uber to avoid parking. We got there around 3pm. I tried the sausage and peppers, pierogis and cornbread from Famous Franks A lot..the cornbread was da bomb! Beware of the long line!. I also wanted to try the hot apple dumpling from the Dutch eating place but they ran out, so I got a grilled sticky bun which was pretty good. We sat in the general area, it started to clear out a bit so we were lucky enough to get a seat. I'll be back when next I come to Philly just to try that famous apple dumpling and I'll be sure to come early.

This alone (albeit there are many other reasons), is a great reason to live in the Greater Philadelphia area.  A 'foodie' wonderland!

...to be continued...

Not a bad spot to grab a late lunch and crank out some Yelp reviews. Location is very convenient in Morgan Hall- right on the corner of Broad and Cecil B.Moore, outside of the Broad Street Line station. The interior design and ambiance is pretty consistent with that of the center city location. Outdoor seating adds a nice touch, especially during this time of the year when it's still really nice out. Unlike the center city location, this place is not extremely packed, which is a huge plus.

Food is ordered on touch screen monitors and food options include various types of salad and stir fry. For those who are familiar with the honeygrow in Center City, this location does not offer the kale'atta smoothie, however, I believe all other food items are the same. This is a perfect healthy alternative to Temple's campus food. Service was friendly, but a little slow. Although there were no orders in front of me, I had to wait for about 10-15 minutes before my  stir-fry was ready. But from what I know, this place recently opened (about 2 weeks ago?) so I can be understanding of this. Aside from the service, I was quite satisfied with the food quality. My stir-fry came with a lot of toppings and vegetables, base-protein-vegetable ratio was on point, and I received all of my ordered ingredients. 

Definitely not the most affordable food option you'll find on campus, but the quality is worth the price in my opinion. Great addition to Temple's campus and I look forward to being back!

Beefsteak's best known for their bowls, which are essentially grains (rice or quinoa), topped with boiled vegetables, sauces, and some toppings. The idea is pretty similar to Chipotle, and you can either make your own or choose a pre-made. 

I had the Eden, which consists of a bed of quinoa topped with boiled (or flash-steamed I suppose) broccoli, edamame, zucchini, green beans, fresh sprouts and scallions and cucumber salad, and finally cilantro and garlic yogurt sauce. $8 is expensive for what is basically a bowl of vegetables but the staff are all very kind. A woman named Barbara walked me through the entire process after I told her it was my first time and that really made an impression on me. The bowl was also a lot more filling than I expected, especially since it wasn't packed to the point of overflowing as I had been hoping. 

Last but not least, I do suggest getting a drink. They're fresh, not overly sweet, and they have 3 to choose from: lavender lemonade, apple beet, and cucumber apple kale. Would recommend to anyone looking for a custom healthy meal.
This place is a goldmine! Has everything from fresh cut fruit to baked goods to specialty grilled cheese sandwiches. Options for everybody, and many a food occasions!

Reading Terminal Market is amazing.  Whatever you are looking for, it is probably here.  I wish that I worked nearby so I could go to lunch here every day.  The Amish market was closed because it was sunday, but it was still amazing.  There were more cuisines than I can remember including Greek, Middle Eastern, German meats, local cheeses, Chinese, noodle bars, salad bars, sushi, Thai, crepes, seafood, spice market, all sorts of bakeries and desserts...  I don't know, everything.  

There is not much seating around, and it is jammed in there.  I would enjoy eating there for a quick meal, but a lot of this is more useful to take home with you.  

I even found purple sweet potatoes, which I have been looking for months.

Average. Maybe slightly below. Definitely overpriced. After Pat Szoke left as the head chef, I started eating raw pancakes and food prepared by average line cooks. Great beers at a premium. Brunch is the best value, however, they need a standard bloody Mary on the menu. The ghost of Mary is a transparent version of the original that's inferior.

That being said....sit down late night, absorb the great service, pump the touch tunes juke box and crawl out the door. Average and expensive but really fun to drink there.

Ordered the whole fried giant squid and the grapefruit black tea and it was the best combination. The girl who recommended the tea said it is made with fresh steeped green tea, sugar and half a fresh grapefruit. Its acidity helps cut greasy taste that you would normally have on your tongue after eating fried food. The squid was pretty fresh and even though it was served on top of shrimp crackers, it's pretty good portion for the price. The young girl who helped us was very knowledgeable with their menu and spot on with her recommendations.  Definitely worth it, especially since you get 10% off with yelp check in!
Love it- Great organic products here. The ice cream is a must.
I ordered two chicken masalas and they didn't really blow me away, I was left hungry. Sure, it was good but I guess I may just be spoiled with home cooked indian food

2nd time around in Reading Terminal Market...still love it! It's like you see something new each time you go...great place for breakfast and lunch...so many options to choose from.

Examples:
seafood place
coffee
loose tea
chocolates
desserts
books
jewelry

If you are visiting, this is definite a must-stop. Skip the hotel bf if you stay nearby..come on over for yummy coffee and variety of breads/cake! :)

Tip-bits:
If you arrive when the RTM is about to close..the security guards would "chase" you out...:(
Dutch vendors only there from Wed-Sat
Restrooms to the left of the cupcake/bookstore in the middle where Philbert guards! :@
Terrific place to enjoy a good meal - the variety was great and the local feel even better!
Horrible place. It was dirty and when we walked in it was smokey from the fryer smoking from old oil. Then we had a huge hair in our food. Won't go back

Despite the name of beyond salads, I'm not sure anything else is worth trying. With a name and logo such as this, one can expect to find "green" and fresh products. In a sad reality, the parfaits are nothing but chemical fake flavored powder yogurt with saggy granola and frozen strawberries. 
The so called smoothies are nothing more than frozen fruits, sugar and ice. 
The employees are nice and do a great job selling what look healthy. 
If your diet consists of fried food and roadkill stews, than this place will provide you a healthy change. But for the more food aficionados, this place is just an illusion. Think twice before buying anything.
This place is unreal.  So many many options,  definitely something for everyone.  Even if you aren't eating its worth stopping by just to check it out.
So much great food, so little time. No trip to Philly is complete without a stop here for lunch. I also highly recommend the Bloody Mary's at Molly Malloy's, they just may be the best in the city.

I'm from New York but I might consider staying in Philly because this place is just so AWESOME. 

Everything Amish made tastes amazing. I haven't been able to try all the market has to offer but I will. This place gets really busy on the weekends. Try going sometime in the afternoon, Tuesday thru Thursday would be the best days to go. It will just give you a better opportunity to take it all in. 

If you want local, freshly grown vegetables cheaper than what they charge you at trader joes or whole foods, this is the place to be. 

The only thing that disappointed me was Sang Kee. Their roasted pork just didn't taste authentic. Trust me... I've tried a lot of different "cha su" pork, I even went to Hong Kong just to eat it. Sang Kee wasn't up to par, but other than that, this market is just everything anyone can ask for.

Great variety of food. 
Must visit for first time Philly fans!
Canolis are great!
Try Asian food too!

While walking in Chinatown I saw this place finally opened. Well it's time to try it. I haven't had Taiwanese Fried dishes for so long. I actually went here 3 days in a row to try the Squid, Chicken, and Beef. Not the combo just the regular dish. I also had the grapefruit green-tea (Must have!) the serving is pretty big. The place is not really that big, so if you have a big group be prepared to eat your food outside or somewhere else. I went at lunch and it can get packed. They only accept cash, and have an ATM inside the restaurant (which is convenient). The squid, chicken, and beef were really good, the squid was not chewy at all I think they boiled it pretty good before frying. Just one complaint.. The chicken had bones! I thought it was a whole fillet! The bone was actually around 1/4 to 1/8 in size. I think this is something that they need to address or maybe tell the customers that it *contains bones*. This was the complain of my colleague as well.

So many good places to eat and not enough belly space. Anything baked by the Amish (they seriously know how to bake) is amazing. Termini Brothers is another fabulous dessert place. DiNic's, Four Season Juice Bar, and Old City Coffee are some of my favorites. There are too many good places to list...grab some foodie friends and go!!!! There is free 2 hour parking near by, but it's so easy to take the bus, subway, or regional rail. Chinatown is also close (another plethora of delicious food). Bottom line, if you are trying to watch your figure, don't come to the Reading Terminal Market. Otherwise, eat your heart out and make that food baby!

I love Reading Terminal Market!

What's not to love?  I know fast food gets a bad reputation, but not at Reading Terminal Market.  There's a limitless selection of restaurants that provide fast quick eats for a good value.  PLUS if you're not in the mood for ready-made food, try your luck with the numerous vendors of fresh veggies, fruits, and spices.

The atmosphere inside is also something to note.  There is always a constant buzz of people coming and going.  Scents and aromas from the numerous vendors fill the air, I assure any visitors of Reading Terminal that they will come back for more.  Or you can be like me and  try one, two, five establishments per visit.

When I moved to Philly Reading Terminal Market was one of the places I instantly fell in love with, and I still visit religiously for my lunch breaks (I have a personal mission to eat at all the restaurants in the Market, so far 6 down, a million left to go).  Every visitor should stop by!

I love going to Reading Terminal. My only complaint is that it can get very crowded and/or loud. But everything else is awesome. If you are touring Philly, you have to stop here to try some famous Bassett's ice cream and Amish pretzels. So much to do here, even if you just want to people watch. It is the epitome of a melting pot.

Is this review even necessary?  Yelp feed keeps prompting me, so I'm officially declaring my love for RT with the written word.

Cheap, quality produce.  Get those seasonal goods at Iovine or O.K.  I love the random farmy or foreign things you wouldn't find at your typical grocer.  Like extra local mushrooms, aloe stems, and elephant garlic.  Those heads are like woa.

Hmm what else do I like here.  I usually stop by Flying Monkey on my rounds and gawk at the fantastic creative concoctions, like vegan pumpkin whoopie pies and Guinness cupcakes.   The pumpple cake always gets a good stare from me too (apple pie in vanilla cake, atop pumpkin pie in chocolate cake, all nested in rich buttercream).  Or I watch the staff make stuff.   I probably creep them out.

Oh. and Tootsie's salad bar!! They use produce from Iovine and other market purveyors.  I load up on quality grilled chicken and greens, sampling the Southern comfort foods if I'm intrigued.

Then I might bop over to the Cajun cafe or whatever it's called.  You know the place.  They are always passing out samples and everyone is like NOM ME.

Oh and I get my candles at the Bee's wax and honey spot.  Perfect for gifts and personal olfactory pleasure. 

Then of course Four Season's juice joint.  The fruits and veggies of your choosing, blended with ice.  No sugar! yippee.

Welp.  That about wraps up this brain train.  Enjoy, tourists!
Atmosphere is great, nice surprise for the neighborhood, but the food was pretty unfortunate.  Wish it was better...

I just like walking around and using all of my senses. The noise, the smell, the texture, the color, and of course the taste. I think I went a bit extreme...went in with a full wallet and empty stomach...came out stomach full but empty wallet... good thing I left my cards at home...
You can practically move in here and not want for anything. This is a lively market and wonderful place to eat. Tons of choices. Great ice cream. Ambience is crowded and busy. Go!

This place is a foodies dream come true! There are tons of different restaurants, boutiques, mini grocers, bakery shops, and more. It's a shame that they don't have a market like this where I live. 

One of my favorite places to visit every time I come to philly!

I wish there was a 6th star for this place. Reading Terminal Market is unlike any food/shopping experience you have had in the past. With almost 100 different vendors, it is the perfect spot to grab lunch, or a very early dinner (it closes around 6) with those picky eaters you might be friends with. The market also has a great history surrounding it- it opened in 1892 and occupies the Reading Railroad's basement. You know the Monopoly Railroad card you always fought over? Now you can take part of the action in real life.

The market has an eclectic array of restaurants serving up dishes like roasted pork sandwiches, crepes, sushi, Mexican, traditional Amish chicken/donuts/breakfast, peking duck, ice cream, cookies, cakes and homemade candies. You can also find vendors that sell Italian sausage, fish, fresh meats, produce and so much more. It is the one stop shop for lunch, dinner and dessert.

Some suggestions:
If you want a traditional Philly style "hoagie" (what we call sandwiches), that tops the traditional Philly cheesesteak, head over to Dinic's. They feature a roasted pork sandwich with provolone, sweet/hot peppers and broccoli rabe. Messy and drool worthy all at once.
Martin's Quality Meat and Sausage has great pork sausages, chicken sausages, and Italian sausage. This place is a perfect spot to pick up tonight's Italian dinner. You will impress everyone around you, not only with your cooking skills but with your ability to decide on which type of sausage you want. This place seriously has everything....
If you have a sweet tooth, definitely hit up Basset's Ice Cream- every single flavor you could imagine in cones and cups, dishes and sundaes, milkshakes and packed pints. A great family establishment with tasty ice cream to boot.

You can't go wrong at Reading Terminal (unless you decide NOT to get anything, and then that is just sacrilegious and an insult to Philly), just make sure you bring cash for CASH only hot spots and try not to become too overwhelmed. Don't worry, it happens to the best of us; being indecisive is a gift.

One of my all time favorite places to visit in Philadelphia.  When I lived there, I didn't realize what an awesome place Reading Terminal is.  All of the food places are great!  Their offerings are unique and I love the set up of the terminal as well.
As someone not from the area, Reading Terminal Market was a really cool place to go to. Cheesesteaks? To die for. Ice cream? Out of this world. Definitely go check this place out!

Reading Terminal is the best place in Philadelphia.  It IS Philadelphia.  All local purveyors, tons of history and just all around awesome!  Great shopping, great people watching and where all of the city intersects.  Go explore the market over and over again.  It is ever changing and always entertaining.

A great place to find cafes, shoppes, bakeries, fish markets, everything. I love it! Great place to find gifts, eat on the go, or just browse the fresh meats, veggies, confectionery goodies, and just about anything you want to eat. :) A must do for a trip to the Friendly City! Just take a cab, walk, or bus, don't try to park anywhere in Philly...

I used to intern right over on 12th and race which is a block from reading terminal, so I've eaten here plenty of times.  I have to admit that it's stressful walking into this place because I am extremely indecisive! So many choices! My favorite spot here is the Thai food stand all the way in the back! It's delicious!  I would avoid the all-you-can-eat soul food buffet, the food was dry and over priced.  The chicken wings when you first walk in are a good hit as well! If you're looking for amazing coffee stop at the coffee shop right at the entrance, they make a mean mocha!

Do:
- Get fresh fruits, veggies, meats, fish, cheese, baked goods. I couldn't believe how fresh and cheap the produce was. I wish we had come here at the end of our trip so I could take stuff home with me.
- Eat lunch here. So...much...food.
- Check out the display in the back with info about all of the other major markets in the country/world. Super neat. Shout out to Eastern Market in DC.
- Be adventurous and buy something you wouldn't usually. In the back corner there's a store with all kinds of dried herb/spice/rub mixes and dried fruit/nuts/candies.
- Bring Tylenol if you get headaches when people bring small children in strollers to crowded places.

Don't:
- Buy from the first counter you see. There are multiple shops selling everything, find the best deal or best looking chocolate/apple/sausage/whatever.
- Be in a hurry. There will be tons of people on a weekend. That's part of the experience. Allocate time accordingly.
- Start impulse buying until after you've had lunch or at least a snack.

I have so much good eats here:

1) Beck's Cajun Cafe - jambalaya for breakfast
2) Old City Coffee - strong but smooth coffee
3) Termini  Brothers - best Cannoli ever 
4) Hatville Deli - perfect Pastrami on Rye
5) Metropolitan Bakery - flourless chocolate cake
 
Must come and try everything, you would love it!!

What is not to like here? I gravitate toward farmer's markets when I travel and I think that Philly has a solid thing going. The air is saturated with deliciousness. There are great representatives of the food of this region.  There is also a nice variety of international selections. You get authenticity with a dash of hipness here and there. Iovine's is the best place to buy produce in the city. If you don't like crowds definitely avoid lunchtime. Try everything. Right now I am craving the salmon from Little Thai Market with an apple dumpling from the amish stand for dessert.

Had high hopes for this place. I'm Taiwanese, I go to Taiwan every year, and I know what good Taiwanese food tastes like. This is not it. Probably one of the worst meals I've had in Philly Chinatown

I got the Samurai fried chicken -- it was soggy and tasteless. So was my friend's fried octopus. Diet coke was flat, and you can still taste the soap in the water. The best part of the meal? Probably the white rice.

Don't try asking for a cup of tap water. Because they won't give you any. The two girls just said they didn't have any and can't give it out. Seriously? You have to buy bottled water.

You pay for the food at the counter. You have a chance to leave a tip after you pay for the food before your food comes out. I regret that I gave them a tip before I had all that trouble with what I was consuming.

I do think the waitresses/cashier when I went in are innocent; they looked a little clueless. So I wasn't going to argue about it. But the food and drink suck. Don't patron a restaurant where you can't even get a cup of water. WATER.

Fantastic place to purchase your fresh foods and to try unique, local selections.  I find that the market offers affordable fruits, vegetables, and hot food, but if you want the more unique sauces, baked goods, and groceries, you will pay more here.  This is a must visit market for visitors and locals alike.  

Favorite outlets include Beilers Donuts, Iovine Brothers Produce, and Martin's Specialty Sausage.

I got lost in this place... but didn't care because in every direction I went in I was surrounded by the freshest and most delcious smelling foods whether it was Chinese, Italian, Thai, Fried Chicken, Seafood, Wine.... you name it, it was there!  Think Eataly just 50x the size with a diversity of cusine.  Truly a mall of food!  If ever in Philly, check it out.

Great atmosphere, friendly staff & awesome bloody Mary's! For our first Philly dining experience this was fantastic. The breakfast tacos were ok, but the drinks and music and crowed were the real winning attributes! We will be back for sure!

What is in there today, and it was not terribly busy. I had to miss fortune of meeting an extremely arrogant, better cashier named Rashun. Was extremely bitter and impatient and at one point it almost looked as though he was giving my 10-year-old Daughter nasty looks. The sky was speaking to me like I was something Bonita his shoe, and clearly has no business in service of customers. I will never again set foot in that Wendy's if that is the level of employee they hire.
Good food, good beer, prices are a tad bit high , but the service makes up for any flaws this place might have.

Love this place! Any day! Any time! Always interesting vendors and people watching. I love the Tubby Olive for vinegar tasting! My favorite vinegar is the fig - great in almost anything from roasted mushrooms to drizzling on pears and blue cheese. Yummy!

The only thing that irked me about this place is how packed it gets and how there aren't many spots to sit, so you'll likely have wait a while to plant your tush down to enjoy a meal or take it to go. But either way, all the vendors I've tried here have always given me something to talk about (still over the moon about the Dutch place...mmm those apple dumplings)

There are so many options to eat that everyone in your party will be satisfied. In addition, if you're just visiting town, it's a great place to bring back a knick knack. It's location is convenient to the bus terminals and the Pennsylvania Convention Center so you know that is the case (such as me). Just check the hours they are opening because they aren't open too late (some vendors are but most aren't)

Reading Terminal Market, I'm certain, embodies a certain time in Philadelphia's history. Imagine a bustling street full of vendors of all sorts and origins. 

There's a joyous business in reading terminal market. It's similar to what I imagine a candy store to a kid is, for an adult. Whether it's a rush for lunch, a hang out with friends, a visit as a tourist, or just a lunchtime stroll, there's something for everyone at Reading Terminal Market. Many times, I don't even spend anything there, but rather just walk around and see the myriad varieties of food. Of course, if I had more money with me, I would just love to try out every store, Amish pastry, or organic ____. Definitely a gem of Philly.

OMG! I could spend days in here.... We did spend days in here and I went back once. There are a ton of places to eat and tons of little shops. I highly suggest picking a hotel within walking distance if you are in the area vacationing. It was the best place to walk to for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Can't wait to get back!

Chick-Fil-A rocks!  I think there has only ever been one location that I've been to that hasn't deserved at least four stores.

However, this location is: THE. BEST. EVER.

The nuggets and the fries are seriously perfect every time I've been here.  Sometimes you can get a lot of those weird looking fries, you know the ones without the holes?  No one likes them.  I've never gotten more than one or two in a box here.  That's impressive.  The nuggets are also bigger than any other location that I've been too.  I'm glad this is the closest location to me!


PS. Shut up about the gay comments people. Did you really think that a Christian company that is closed on Sundays was going to say that they support gay marriage? C'mon people!

I just went last w/e and I forgot how cool this place is. It was a rainy miserable day and the RTM was a great place to go since it is indoors. We ate some sandwichs, bought some seafood and crabcakes for din-din, and bought way more sweet treats then we should have. There is a huge section of all Amish made cakes, pies and breads. They're cheap and so good. I didn't know it but Hope's Cookies from Rosemont even has a store here. They make really, really yummy cookies and other treats. There's a Bassett's ice cream store, too. Pretty much whatever you are in the mood to eat can be found here. This place is a lot of fun and def a must-see for people from out of town or visiting.

I love this place! You can get anything from Chinese food to Philly cheesesteaks. 

Also, you can get souvenirs, handmade crafts, and other knick knacks.

If you go during the Pennsylvania Dutch Festival (early August), they'll have homemade pastries and ice cream. I got some ice cream, and it was delicious. It was definitely worth the $3. 

This place is good for lunch, but keep in mind that it might be hard to find a place to sit. I wouldn't try going here for dinner, unless you like eating dinner extremely early, because it closes at 6 pm.

I've been going here since I was a child. There's great food and a variety of people. Beilers, and all the fresh produce stands make it worth it. On top of that there's delicious food stands and places to eat inside such as the Dutch eating place that is always attentive with a great selection of food. Their turkey melt, burgers, and chili are my favorite items on the menu!

HOPES COOKIES. Enough said. These are the best cookies in the market-- hidden in a little corner, but they are always soft, always rich, and always a winner. Don't miss this in the chaos of the market!

Very hectic and busy but usually an overall good experience. This is another "tourisy" thing to do in Philadelphia. Many popular businesses displaying their goods. It is a pretty big market so allocate an hour or more to walk around and have a few tastes.

Greasy ,low quality ,small portion unhealthy food, I'm wondering who gives this food 4,5 star !!! 
I rather eat at McDonalds, at least it tastes good !

It's okay, many places to eat but not a lot of good one.. I really love the Hershel Pastrami sandwich and the Greek pork gyro, the sauce on the Greek gyro was amazing.. the halal wasn't so great, meat was very dry and the nunn was burnt.. overall it's a good place to begin in the morning since they close early then slow work your way outside of the city into China town and everywhere around it..
love bringing visitors here for the experience. lots to try, a lot of great specialty stores and a fun way to spend a saturday morning.
This place is the cornucopia of foodie-land. Never a letdown because whatever you are hungry for they got it. Nuff said!
The food was awesome at tootsies but unfortunately it was so crowded I could barely move through the crowd and I couldn't try food from anywhere else

I couldn't disagree with the other review more. I too am stoked to have a place across the street from me. But after sampling the crispy pig ears, bone marrow, and steak frites, I was very happy. The cocktails seem to want to be speakeasy. But may need some tweaking. 

I sat at the communal table and within 15 minutes found myself chatting with blonde, twin doctors. So overall, I had a good time.

I look forward to many nights of stumbling back across Moyemensing.

it's open!!!!!

Was craving chipotle before the snow got too bad but didn't feel like driving. Something told me to call, no answer (would've given 5 stars if they answered). Then went to the app and it seemed like I could order online (which I couldn't do before) so I thought hmmmmm maybe I'll check Yelp! 

That's when I noticed they closed in 15min so I sped over. Clean, courteous, and fast! Didn't hurt that the ladies on the line were very attractive!

Welcome to the NE Chipotle

Masala kitchen is perfect ! If I can't decide what to eat or where to eat; I know I can't go wrong with Masala Kitchen. 
For their vegetarian options: paneer masala and aloo paneer are the best ! I would recommend getting the "masala" version of the rolls, because that includes their home-made tomato curry sauce which is delicious !!! 
For 1 person; two rolls or 1 platter is usually pretty filling, which puts you at around $10 - $12 per person - which for philly is not bad at all. 
The staff is good, professional and quick. 
Wish they'd start delivering to university city again, their drinks weren't so expensive, and they had a yogurt sauce (in addition to the white sauce they have). 
I am definitely returning multiple times!

All of my friends recommended this place for when i'm in philly and I was so glad I went. 

So many great places to eat!
I've only tried Dinic's (roast pork sandwich) and Bassetts (ice cream) so far, but I definitely want to come back to try other places.

It's definitely hard to find a table to eat at... but I found that you have to look for people almost done eating and then swoop in once they're done. 

It's also a nice place to get some air conditioning from the hot weather outside. It was 94 degrees when I was in philly.

A must see if you're in the Philadelphia area! It's a large indoor market with limited seating. It is usually crowded due to its popularity. There is a variety of locals vendors from meats, crepes to ice cream and pretzels. I love the market style and you can pick up a few grocery items when you're there as well. There are often Amish based restaurants coming all the way from Lancaster with the most amazing homemade goods. There is definitely something for everyone here. I would recommend going for lunch or a snack!
Lots of different kinds of food and drink.  Can get really crowded - lots of tourists as well as locals.

I would guess that locals all have their own favorites and habits at the Terminal. I know which veggie stand to go for which items, I know to get to the Thai place early to avoid the lunch rush (salmon curry!). I know you can't beat Beiler's doughnuts and coffee special, or that Miller's Twise pretzels stuffed with egg and your choice of meat are the perfect handheld breakfast item. 4 Seasons Juice Bar is always phenomenal (although they run out of some staple fruits too often - how this is possible for a place located in the Terminal is mind-boggling) but the Middle Eastern eatery has a great banana-honey smoothie. There are things I'd never do in the Terminal - like buy a cheesesteak or pizza. But the sandwiches at Hatville Deli are incredible. At the Terminal, you have to deal with some price inflation (read: avoid the flower stand) but all in all, it's a fantastic place with something for everyone.

I was visiting my fiance who is new to the area. We decided to go check out Reading Terminal for lunch. We were walking around a lot trying to figure out what to eat. We ended up at the cajun place (can't remember the name). The lady working there was quite rude and seemed really annoyed that we were eating there lol. The food was good but I wouldn't say amazing and it's not cheap either. Next time I visit, I want to try other places in the market.

How could you not give this place 5 stars?

It's freakin' awesome! 

Having lived in Memphis for many years, it took me a minute to get into the flow. This place is busy, and people move with purpose. I had to shift into "East Coast" mode---which means I sharpened my elbows, quickened my pace, and stopped getting flustered when the little Asian girls walk under my elbows in their quest to buy pretzels.

There's no time to mess around, so get your order in place before you get to the front of the lines. 

You can get anything you want in here. Hundreds of food stands means thousands of choices. I opted for the icons----soft pretzels and a Cheesesteak. They were delicious.

If I lived around this market, I would be here every day. Fresh Seafood, Meat, Sausages, Cheeses, Produce, and Vegetables would make your cooking as fresh as you could afford. 

Whether you want to sit down and join in the fun, or carry some food out the door, this market will be fun for everyone.

Food paradise with some many unique food dishes from Philly like their famous Philly cheesesteak, I believe there are at least 4 places in here, lots of cheese and chocolate places, this place was rammed to the max, everything stand is a line up, even the chinese food stands

We tried our first Philly cheesesteak at by George, got the cheese steak with american cheese and it was soooooooo filling and good, one sandwich feeds 2 people, also tried a cookie place that was so soft and gooey....this is truly a food market, one of the best in the country in my opinion is better than Chelsea market in NYC

This place has keep its originality and I wish I could have tried other foods like the donut place seemed to very popular but that Philly cheese destroyed me

A must visit whenever in philly

Be ready to spend a good few hours or even half a day here...

WARNING: DO NOT COME HERE when you're SUPER HUNGRY...because you'll literally want to buy and EAT EVERYTHING!! 
The BEST advise is to come here with 4-5 other fiends, so you guys can each other something different and try LOTS of different food!

When I first came here, I was amazed, awed, and fascinated by the HUGE variety of food they could offer. Honestly, anything you could name or could not name! Chinese, Italian, Indian, Japanese, African, South American, Spanish....seriously, it was like a cultural food paradise! So many flavors, colors, aromas. Plus, many places let us sample the food first! It was truly amazing especially since there aren't many markets in the area that's like this. 

Besides delicious main courses-entrees, they also have desserts, such as chocolates, ice creams, and fresh-cut fruits! It's a very fun, exciting and adventurous place! 
WATCH OUT for the people though! It can get very crowded and packed at times, so be aware and don't lose your friends! Another pro is that they have lots of seating.

Love Reading Terminal! A must visit when in Philly!! I recommend going early.It gets very crowded which can be frustrating, but still worth the visit.Nothing better then a pastrami sandwich at 10:00am, Clearly, Philadelphia is the absolute best city for delicious sandwiches and Reading Terminal is one stop shopping. The best Pastrami sandwich in the world at Hershels East Side Deli which beats anything in NYC. A pork sandwich with sharp provolone and greens at da nics, mouth watering. .We always get one sandwich from each place so we can sample and share.
Besides sandwiches there are tons of other restaurants, shops etc....

The only reason I didn't give this 5 stars is because it does get very crowded but crowds aside, this is 6 star!!

I love reading terminal market. (RTM). so many options, so little time. They have great options, they have TONS of options. Great restaurants for eating in, or great places to buy locally (and some not locally) sourced fruits, veggies, and meats- pay attention though, not everything is local, so if that's your goal, just ask around. 

Most of the store owners are friendly and you can usually find exactly what you're looking for. 

As a matter of advice, I would say avoid this place at noon on a weekday- no no, toooooo busy. And avoid it on weekends all together- can you say tourists palooza? I can, i've seen it. But sincerely, I love this place, they have so much variety you really can have whatever you like.

Despite the constant weaving through throngs of tourists, I love Reading Terminal. It's become one of my weekend rituals: grab a juice and a bite to eat, get lost in the aisles finding cool stuff, spend so little and get so much at Iovine Brothers, then wheel my granny cart full of fresh produce all the way home. 

Also, being that it's great for tourists, if I have friends visiting for the weekend, Reading Terminal is a great 2-for-1: show my friends something cool & touristy, but still get my weekend routine shopping done. Win win.

I always get the cheesesteak dumplings here. They're absolutely amazing. Big, lots of filling, and deliciously fried dough. Very clean space and the service isn't super friendly but fine. The art and decor is pretty unique and refreshing too!

The Reading Terminal Market is like an indoor flea market of food...forget food halls...this place is huge.  You can find fresh meat and seafood as well as hot meals and packaged specialty items.  Unfortunately it was very crowded on an early Friday afternoon...but it opens at 8 a.m. on Saturday.

Very busy but I love the variety. There is something for everyone. This includes vegans and vegetarians. I also like the mixture of food, salads, desserts and fresh produce and meats. I think this is a good option if you are with a group and people and no one is clear about what they have a taste for. The only issue is the long line you might have to stand in.

I was excited to try the "non-traditional flavored" dumplings but I was not too thrilled with them. I had Cheesesteak, Shrimp & grits and crab cake (I didn't see it on their menu but they offered at sampling). Cheesesteak was okay and I wasn't a big fan of the other two picks. I would have appreciated more if the dumplings were juicier. 

Maybe I will try their noodles next time.
Best place in Philly to shop for food and eat. . . This is the place the "real" Philly cheesesteaks are made

Absolutely love this place.....great variety of food....kinda crowded on Saturday afternoons.....I personally do not like crowds especially how tight people are in there....My best place is the produce corner....has everything you would need and the prices are fair.....A little upset when the spice store closed in the back...A must to go to when downtown Philly....pick up some cheese, wine and sweets....
Wonderful food experience.  A must see if visiting philly.  Beilers donuts are off the chain!!
So many options! We were here to eat at Carmen's. However, we wandered the whole place and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. A must see if you come to Philly!
