Stayed across the street at the Marriott and was told by the employees that this was as must go to place. At first I was hesitant but I am glad I made the decision to go. It was amazing in there. Food from everywhere, all cultures. The facility was also very clean which was amazing for how many people they have going through there. They have everything you would want to try. I had gator gumbo which was amazing, also some crepes that were amazing. Everything else I didn't eat looked amazing also. I suggest if your in Philly and hungry stop by here. Guarantee you will not be disappointed. Based on all the great reviews you can't go wrong here. I'll be back!!!
My Idea of Willy Wonka's Factory.  Every conceivable food known to man under one roof!!  Just wish it didnt get so packed around lunch.  Oh well.

Chipotle is amazing. Fresh food, large portions, and great fast service. The chicken burrito bowl is my go to. You can choose whatever you want, however you want it. The only complaint is that the sour cream portion is always too much so I've just stopped asking for it. That's only this particular location though. The prices are reasonable and everything is so flavorful. On Halloween wearing a costume gets you a free burrito!
Awesome place to try out chicken and rice. Open late and very friendly staff. Chicken Rice hits the spot and biryanis are real good as well.

3 stars for the excellent customer service, but the food, meh. I came here for dinner and had heard good things about their fried chicken sandwich. It wasn't the hillbilly version, just their standard fried chicken "breast" sandwich. This chicken "breast" was thinner than a McDonald beef patty, making the 'sandwich' just a giant blob of bread dough. Also, the fries were cold. 

The Thai chicken salad was decent, and the falafel alright. The apple cobbler was a flavorful cup of mush.

This is the real deal. When I lived in Chinatown I used to come here every week to buy fresh produce, meats and eggs. Iovine is awesome. Always fresh and always affordable. The dollar bags in the back are a steal. Also Godshalls has quality poultry and the guys that work the stand are super friendly. A rather new favorite of mine, is Guintas for both poultry and red meat. The smoked turkey and pig parts are fresh and taste great in soups. Perfect place to shop for groceries and ready to eat food. Highly reccomended - but be prepared for the crowds on the weekends.
I got the roasted pork with broccoli rabe!! Out of this world!!

So many options of food, bar in the back at Molly's, fresh food markets and a definite tourist must. We ate at Dinics and he sandwhich was huge with enough toppings and meat to go with the large fresh buns and friendly service! A definite do if you've never been tourist or not.
Awesome delicasies of every variety - including goodies for a vegan like me!

While there are certainly cons (quite a couple actually) the Reading Terminal Market is an experience that overwhelms any minor annoyances such as limited seating, crowded pathways, and terrible layouts.

The solidarity you feel when you are in a line with a group of strangers and you all order the exact same menu items. The focus it takes to duck hoards of families and tourists all milling around, staring up at oversized menu boards. 

Everything I tried out has been incredibly delicious but there are so many other, equally but differently delicious options that I've never ordered the same thing twice.

Can't say much more than what's already been said. Must see if you're visiting Philly. Awesome experience, lots of fantastic vendors. Hershel's makes a killer Pastrami Reuben, and that's only one of a million options!
Go to DiNics!!! OMG AMAZING! Then go to the Amish donut shop, every donut is worth the calories! Everything in this place deserves to be put on a pedestal and worshiped!

Not impressed with this gourmet market. Definitely a TON of choices and lots of fresh options (e.g. juice, baked goods, sushi, etc.). Truly a meat lovers paradise + some vegetarian options. Extremely crowded & difficult to navigate; I'm sure it's not so bad during weekdays when it's less touristy. I would've liked to have seen more healthy options; the two juice bars I stopped at wouldn't even do a custom juice blend as they told me everything was carrot based?! Disappointing.

Foodie Paradise!!
If you are in town and anywhere near the Reading Terminal - go check it out!! The foodie in you will thank you! Anything your little heart desires can be found here when it comes to food. The place is always packed and always delivers. We love going here with a group as everyone can get what they crave and then all meet up in the middle and eat together. Everything is in stand/kiosk format but there are a lot of tables in the middle and throughout where you can sit once you figure out what you want at this magical place. You can also do a little shopping like veggies, fruit, coffee, chocolate, meats, bread.... YUMMY! 

NOTE - there is also a bar to get drinks at.... great success ha!

Really good selection of tasty eats, fresh produce, dairy, and meats and fish.  All under one roof.  The most impressive was the fish/seafood selection.  There are also several bakeries and some amazing looking cakes.

I haven't been here in awhile whereas I used to go weekly to shop. Well, now i would like to go weekly again. They have added new tenants and updated the bathrooms. I love a lot of the vendors and if you go with a bunch of people , they have something for everyone. weekends is packed, so, if you have to go then, my advise is early. I went during the week after 8am. I could even get breakfast at some places. Not all vendors are open early or on Sundays, but, it's worth a trip whenever you go.....prepare to be overwhelmed. This is a cool place for shopping....

Love wandering the passages at Reading Terminal Market and especially enjoying all the food and treat finds. Good place to snag a special gift for the out of towners but also a place for locals to enjoy, buy fresh produce, fresh meat, or a prepared meal. Lots of restaurant kiosks to choose from with a diverse selection of food types. Some days it gets very crowded though so bring some patience with you if you will be going at peak times. This is a must see when in Philly.
I love the market and frequent it on my lunch break since I work in Chinatown. Definitely a special staple of Philly!

Hands down the best thing to do in Philly if you love food. This place is crazy, so many shops and restaurants. Everything from spices, to candles, to fresh produce, pastries, to donuts made right on the line in front of you. I love DiNic's pulled pork sandwich with rabe.
tootsies salad bar and the amish cheese market are the greatest. i love everything about them! the produce places are super cheap and good quality

For a contemporary take on dumplings, come here! We got the fried version so they could hold up best as take out. Vegetarian options included Spinach and cheese dumpling and a cauliflower dumpling. You can mix and match 5 for $7, or get one of the combo deals. 

Noodles for vegetarians: portobello mushrooms and veggies can be substituted for any meat. To be honest, I hope they consider adding more mushrooms and also add tofu as an option, as vegetarians still need a good protein source. 

A very good start, but I would like to see more tofu or seitan options for vegetarians in the future. 

If you want authentic, go to Chinatown. If you want a twist on dumplings with fun flavors like cheesesteak, peach cobbler or cheesecake (!), check this place out!

This was a nice change from our past visits to Philly where we spend most of our time and meals in Chinatown.  We've been visiting more frequently while DD is checking out options for college.  Her top two are both in Philly so I wanted her to soak up the Philly experience to help her visualize herself there.  Luckily it is only two hours away!

So, we've walked through RTM before but not as a planned destination- this time was a designated stop in our itinerary.  I was afraid parking would be a problem as I could tell from signs that there was an event taking place but lucked out and found something on the street a block away.  It was nice and early and not quite the lunch rush.  I saw a couple with suitcases and just smiled as other reviews I had read suggest not to be "that guy" :)

We browsed our way through the aisles making sure to criss cross and scope it all out before committing.  Opted for some roasted spare ribs from Sang Kee Peking Duck, baked ziti from By George and a sushi roll from Tokyo Sushi Bar.  None of it was anything special to write home about, but it was fun and lots to check out next time.  I do regret not picking up some sweets, but there's always next time!  The kids had a great time but were too famished to appreciate it fully.  They just wanted me to hurry up and get something.  You can't rush an experience!

I can attest to the fact that the food here is fairly authentic down to the last detail. I have gone back twice now and have tried pretty much everything on the menu. I particularly love their rose lassi.
Can't think of a better place to get produce and meat !!! So Fresh, Great Variety and well priced...
Great place if you are in Philly!  Great way to sample local food from many different vendors.
If you come to Philly this is a must do! You will be overwhelmed by choices and fresh food and produce to offer! Go to franks try the pineapple cornbread and the bakeries are all very good!!

I should have turned my sister down when she said lets get Chipotle. Firstly, I have never liked their food the two times I've tried it years ago, but today was the absolute worst. I got the pulled beef or whatever that was, it was so spicy it overpowered everything else, so I can't even begin to talk about the rest of bowl. I paid for a drink but the ice machine was empty so I left the cup behind. I forgot to mention we were in the line for 45mins waiting to reach the counter. There was so much confusion with the staff they charged me someone else's meal, which by the way was wayyy cheaper then my food should have been, didn't realize until I checked my receipt in the car to make sure they didn't overcharge me.

So I came here for DiNic's and left here feeling like I wished I had planned a whole day here. Being someone that loves to eat, I could see myself slipping into a pair of sweatpants and spending an entire day here eating. 

You name it, you've got it. That is pretty much the best way to explain the Reading Terminal Market. You can come here for groceries as they have what looked to be an extensive produce section, or you can get meats, seafood, or just about anything else you would need to make a top notch dinner at home. Now there are also restaurants here where you can order food and then eat in one of the seating areas located in the market. There is such a diverse choice of ethnic foods here and I would like to try all of them. Some of them I noticed on my quick trip here were an Indian, Japanese, Chinese, Middle Eastern, and Cajun. There is also a bar, if you prefer to drink your meals.  I was not prepared for all the places located in this market, so I was a little overwhelmed as I saw all the different places to choose from.  

I think I might just have to plan a day trip to the Reading Terminal Market and see if I can eat my way out of here!
Great quick affordable lunch. Just wish it was slightly closer to my work.  The chicken and paneer masala rolls are delicious!
I could spend hours looking around this market.  Great gifts for medical professionals, particularly the chocolate hearts and lungs!   Try the ham too :)

A must for anyone visiting Philly! This is the city's main farmer's market, which is hosted within an old train shed. Its history is absolutely fascinating, and when it first opened WAY back when it held almost 400 vendors - can you imagine!

My first visit here was apparently on a "quiet" day, which basically means I had some breathing room in what was still an absolutely packed space. 

But there's a reason this place is always packed: it's fantastic. You can find EVERYTHING here if you look long enough. Breakfast food, sandwiches, gyros, sushi, bakeries, desserts, beads, an entire stand dedicated to selling flavored honey and beeswax, and of course, Philly cheesesteaks - and that's just to name a small number of the stands and types of food you can find in here; it's an absolutely amazing place to just get lost in. 

Bring your adventuring spirit and appetite when you head in here for sure, because you will get a heaping plate of food no matter where you go to eat! And give yourself pleeeenty of time to explore and enjoy the place!

My friend took me here knowing that I would love it. I felt like I was in my element when I am in this place. The fruit, veggies, meat, seafood, pastries, flowers, prepared food and food made to order. The ripe, fresh food draws you to each stand while the smells pull you into many different directions. 

I was impressed with the selection and quality of the food the vendors there were there. I had a crepe for lunch, pastry for dessert, and got a cupcake for later on. If I lived in there area I would have purchased some fish for home but I didn't think it was worth it to freeze something to get it up to Boston. 

The restroom facilities were very clean. There was an attendant in there that checked the stalls after they were used to make sure they were clean and had toilet paper. I was really impressed how they ran the facilities here.

Fancy good food is a hard find. This place is great. The seafood blt is amazing. The brunch is to die for. Carmalized bananan pancakes fullfills my sweet tooth cravings and the shrimp and grits is the bomb. I do have to add that there coffee is very good. I will be coming back to enjoy brunch more often.

Calling this a "grocery" is a bit misleading.  They do sell groceries, in that there are some stands selling fresh produce or meat - I seem to recall that having a few of these to serve local buyers who live nearby is a condition of the market continuing to operate.  But mostly, the Reading Terminal Market is a big noisy crowded bunch of prepared food stands, with a couple sit-down restaurants thrown in. 

The food served here varies from Chinese to cheesesteaks to seafood to diner fare, and it all ranges from good to very good (though I think Philly has several better places to get a cheesesteak if you're spending more than a day or two in town). I especially like the pizza sold by the large Italian stand,  and on certain days of the week there is an Amish shop inside that serves good breakfast.  There's also a historic ice cream shop that has been selling ice cream longer than any place else in USA and has sold to Presidents, etc.  The market building itself is historic and it's good to see an old building being put to a creative re-use, particularly in this part of the city where chain stores and blight need to be fended off.  If you are staying or working within walking distance, the Market is definitely worth a stop for lunch or snacks. 

Having said all that, given that to go to this market I have to drive in or take public transportation in from Chesco, which has its own awesome food places and Amish markets, the Reading Terminal Market has been kind of a three-star experience for me over multiple visits. The biggest problem with the place is parking. If you come by car, be aware there is little or no street parking and you will have to park in a garage.  There are a couple of garages that will give you a couple hours of deeply discounted parking with a ticket validated by a market vendor, but finding the garage entrances in busy traffic can be tricky, the time you are allotted to park is cutting it close if you wanted to see the whole market or eat at several places, and you really have to watch the time because if you go over your time limit at all then the price goes way up to over 20 dollars.  Also, the last time I drove down there, I had an argument with the parking cashier who tried to charge me 27 dollars although I had a properly validated ticket and was not over my time limit (way under).  She was on the phone and just couldn't be bothered.  I wondered how many tourists would not have realized she made a mistake and just paid the grossly inflated fee for under 2 hours of time.  I recommend walking or taking public transportation here if you possibly can.

Next issue is that the entrances and exits of this market often have aggressive panhandlers who harass shoppers for a handout.  I've had the experience of saying no or trying to walk away and having one of these street people chasing after me shrieking and verbally harassing me because I somehow "disrespected" her by not responding to her demands for money. No security or police presence in sight once you get outside the doors of the market. 

Finally, this place gets very crowded on weekends, so if you are coming to eat, plan on fighting the crowds and standing in a long line to get your food.  Many of the people visiting are tourists and as such hold up the line further by asking questions, asking for special orders, not being totally familiar with payment methods, and/or blocking traffic in the aisles before or after they get their food.  This is a "kid friendly" place which means that there are a lot of families with kids dodging about, strollers, etc. creating more congestion. It can also be hard to find a place to sit down with your food and many of the tables and chairs are the uncomfortable sort that you find in high school cafeterias. I'd really rather take my food home to eat it, but given that I live some distance away, taking home melty ice cream or pizza that will get cold is not a good option. The earlier you can go and beat the crowd on the weekend, the better.  

You can also tell this place was not originally constructed as a market or food court because, unlike some other cities where the markets have higher ceilings and an open-air feel, this place has a pretty low ceiling and little air circulation, and when crowded it gets hot and feels cramped. If you come in colder weather, be sure to dress in layers you can easily shed, or you'll be roasting to death by the time you've made it up and down the aisles. 

Bottom line:  good place to go if you can walk or bike there or you're visiting and want a taste of Philly all in one place.  If you live in the burbs and can more easily drive, walk or bike to other markets and restaurants in your own area, then maybe worth doing once or twice but not on a regular basis, in my opinion.
I love this place. Really fun!!! Too many options. I am always here when I am in philly. Very lively and fun place.
Had some really excellent pumpkin cream cheese cookies from the Amish bakery in the corner.  Delicious!
Omg how can anyone decide what to eat or buy here! The choices are endless! It reminds me of Lexington Market in Baltimore

I love the vegi and fruit store when you first walk in. They have great prices for what I spent $10 there I would of spent double or more at Walmart. Some places can be a hit or miss that's why I didn't give 5 stars. I got Cod fish from one of the market and it was no good it had a bad smell to it, I didn't notice till I got home.

I've been here a couple times and there is no place quite like it. From the outside it almost looks like a run of the mill deli or average supermarket but once you are inside you know that is not the case. Reading Terminal is basically a warehouse filled with small food stands and shops, think mall food court just infinitely better. No matter what you are in the mood for they will have something for you. Some of my favorites are Beiler's Donuts, where Amish bakers make AMAZING donuts like the Elvis which is a jelly donut with peanut butter frosting and bacon. Then there is DiNics, where they make giant slabs of roast pork, slice it, throw it in some jus, put it on a bun and top it with broccoli rabe and provolone.

There are so, so many more places. You have to go there if you are in Philly.

LOVE THIS PLACE! It is a mad house at lunch time so go early. You can get all your food needs HERE! Seafood, produce, soul food, blueberry pancakes, fresh jam, hoagies, and infused olives. Any picky eater can find food. Honestly, Reading is an experience even if you don't eat.

Loved the fast pace ambiance! It's open until 6 so hurry. Traffic is pretty bad in the afternoon so budget your time. It's close to city hall and the mall. 

Pros: bustling place with lots of food options 
Cons: closes too early
Love the market! So many delicious food spots to try, while also carrying an array of unique gifts.
Love this place! If you're there hour-30 mins before you can get cookies for half price! Yum

Sometimes I find myself lost in the RTM. The colors and smells drifting in the store take me to another place, another world. As an aspiring creative chef and food writer, this place gives me alot of inspiration. But yeah, ok enough of me.

The fresh produce for one, is great. Any type of fruit, mushroom, herbs that you can imagine can probably be found here. Every time I come here, something new is to be found. There's always a variety of many many things from baked goods to Thai to delis to vegan desserts. Seriously, I cannot come here enough!

If you reside in the city, or if you're just visiting, you'll definitely enjoy the market. I live just a couple block from RTM and I'm here a couple times a week. I do 95% of my grocery shopping here because its very fairly priced and everything is always fresh. I also stop in here for lunch regularly because again, its fairly priced, and 9 times out of 10, its a great meal. Some of my favorite places in here are: 

Iovines for produce, Giuntas, for chicken and steak, Martins for ground beef and their finger link breakfast sausages, literally the best in the city, Bielers for my fat girl doughnut obsession, and the wings at the Amish Market are literally the most amazing thing you will ever eat. I get them packed to go, and throw them in the oven for 30 minutes to make them crispy when I get home, the smoked wings are the best, by the way. I also regularly go to Fair Food for Little Baby's Ice Cream, pricey but worth it, Muellers for any type of gift for coworkers, because everyone loves chocolate, and my favorite stop for brunch on saturdays and sundays in Pearl's oyster bar, they have awesome french toast and eggs benedict that will blow you away. The market is defiantly worth stopping by, especially if you live in the area for groceries!

One of the essential stops for a tourist visiting Philadelphia. From the eclectic mix of Amish baked goods, locally sourced coffee shops, and misplaced confectionery shops, Reading Terminal Market is an experience comparable to that of Seattle's Pike Place Market. 

Only one major problem; the entire thing is indoors. If you're like me and enjoy just a tiny bit of space, this definitely detracts from the vendors.

Whereas Pike Place has the benefit of being an open air market, Reading Terminal forces you into rudimentary queues akin to a rush hour NYC subway car.

4 stars because it's a unique and excellent form of quick immersion in Southeastern Pennsylvanian culture.

Docking one star because the mass herds make me feel like I'm at a state fair/flea market.

One of if not the oldest food markets in America. This place rocks. If you plan on visiting Philly and you consider yourself a foodie then plan more than one trip here. They have the ubiquitous cheesesteaks and seafood stands and cheese mongers and bakeries and Amish diner and confectioners and on and on and on. You can also see some of Philly's finest here, meaning their police and paramedics having a bite to eat.
Plan carefully as the Amish are only there on Wed. And Thur.
Had the best pretzels here made fresh by Amish girls.

What a find. This place is amazing.  Tons of great spots to grab a bite to eat. Famous Cheesesteaks, fried chicken, brisket, baked goods & lots more.  Been going here daily while at a conference and very pleased with choices and quality.
Crazy crazy place, I love it! Such an electric mix of food, culture,  and people. I saw people from all over the word exploring without fear or prejudice. It is an amazing experience l

I found this place by accident! Thank you yelp app for leading me to this market. Probably one of the most interesting places to see in Philly. =)

I could have wandered around this place for hours, but I only had 45 minutes. There is seriously so many vendors selling different specialties and food, I felt like I had found my paradise. Sandwiches, chocolates, seafood, baked goods, smoothies and ice cream!

I happened to wander into a space selling used books too, and I perused the selections before I went off to buy a smoothie, a pork sandwich and a philly cheesesteak. There were so many things that caught  my eye. 

The space is large (I feel like I circled a few times and got lost) and there is a decent amount of seating inside to eat and people watch. I also saw a section that sold fruits and veggies. 

Will totally be back one day if I'm ever in town to sample and enjoy everything else they have here! I love variety!

theres so many good stores here and almost all of them have gotten level up, the new way to pay with your phone! its (Finally!)completely free and totally safe to use. you just hook your card up to your phone and pay through an encrypted bar code. no one ever gets your info so youre safe from identity theft. Plus level up acts as a loyalty club so as you you spend money at the places you normally shop you get money back. the philly pretzel factory offers $5 back on every $30 spent! if you havent gotten level up yet use this code to get a bonus $5 global credit to use at any level up carrying location!!! 9WHRC2 and no worries the code never expires! come enjoy philly with a few extra bucks!!! ^.^

Everything you could want from a market standpoint with lots of energy & local flavor. Great location. Across the street from the Market East train station. Especially recommend Metropolitan Bakery for breads & Molly Malloy's for lunch.

Great market when you are looking fresh vegetable and fantastic meats. Only one problem, the crowds of tourist just milling around lost. 
Love Iovines for fresh fruits and Veggies. And Martine for the best chicken and turkey products.

I can't believe I haven't already written a review for Reading Terminal. Now is the time. I'm probably in the minority of people in the City who love but don't Love RTM. 

I think this place is great for finding those oddball foods that I might otherwise have to look for on Amazon, or for snagging a bite to eat when I'm in the City for lunch-hour. This is also a great place to come for cheaper-than-store prices on produce and finding tasty, local, gourmet products like Metropolitan Bakery, DiNics Roast Beef, Flying Monkey Bakery, etc.... along with all of the cheese stands and butcheries. If you have a favorite cheese or meat, and you can't find it most places in Philadelphia, this is the place to look! 

However, the crowds here, the smells of rotting fish, the often-closed back half of the Market, and difficulty in finding seats to enjoy the lunchtime delicacies, make me a little less appeased by RTM. 

Overall, I return again and again, and there's always something new in store. If you're a visitor to Philadelphia, you can't pass this up.

Great neighborhood spot. We like almost everything on the menu but usually fall back on the burger, smashed chicken sandwich or one of their salads.   The happy hour and brunch are great as well.  Really just a really good place to go anytime for a bite or a drink ... Or both

Well It's full of tourist's and a bit pricey, But the selection is pretty great and I live within a 2 minute walking distance so It's very convenient. Big fan of going early to get the fresh amish offering and another reason why buying a bread box, yeah I said bread box, on groupon was an awesome idea.

carlucios
northfield, nj
I love Reading Terminal Market! It has everything! I love Tommy DiNic's!
Everything a good foodie wants to eat all under one roof!! Each time I visit, I discover another wonderful vendor...my favorite place in Philly!

Go here. Honestly no better advice for to do's in Philly than to visit this place. There is something here for everyone! Luckily for us we stayed right next door so we could come here multiple times. Want breakfast? They have a diner and breakfast sandwiches. Want a hoagie? They have them. Need fresh meats? They got them! Want a philly cheese steak; hell yeah they have amazing ones here! It can get quite crowded but no lie, it's worth the crowds.
Pure fabulousness. They have everything from cheese, seafood, fruit, donuts, chocolate, cake candy, donuts and seafood. Super busy and super crowded but worth the visit.
Wonderful endless selections! And all delicious. Highly recommend to both locals and visitors.
love going to Reading Terminal Market! great food! great shopping! perfect for foodies :)
Everything here is amazing. The atmosphere and all of the choices of food are so diverse it is almost impossible to chose!

The first time I went, I was with a group of friends and we only had drinks. The service was great and the drinks were good. 

The second time I went with just my boyfriend on a Sunday before catching a movie. We ordered food this time and I was less than impressed. The BBQ sandwich I had was overly salty and dried out. For the prices being what they are, I really expected a bit better. The service the second time was abysmal. Now I know Sunday afternoon is a down time for bars and restaurants for the most part but my boyfriend and I waited for our drinks (a dirty martini and a beer) for over 10 minutes even though the bar was not busy- it took that long for our server to come back in from having his cigarette. Being a server of 12 years myself, I am extremely understanding but his attitude was poor from the start (which didn't seem directed at us for any particular reason) and then he took forever with the drinks and bill. I pride myself on tipping 20% as the MINIMUM but for this I had to go with a 16% tip just out of principle. Hope they can get their service and food back on track soon. I will not be returning anytime soon- there are just too many good restaurants in this city that have far superior food and service.
Simply the best representation of the variety of food Philadelphia has to offer. Great for locals and tourists alike.
Last time we ordered from here we got awesome sauces with our dumplings that really enhanced the flavors, this time absolutely no sauce. Very disappointing!

Reading market is a must see - but be prepared for crowds, a little chaos, and some long queues. The variety is great, but I'm not sure the many 'best in America' claims are really on the money. Highlights for me were the donuts, the grilled cheese, and the chocolates.
Didn't eat during this visit, but enjoyed drinks in a unique atmosphere.  Staff was very friendly and offered advice on drink preferences and guided drink selection.
Awesome market. They have almost every type of food here. It's amazing. The donuts here are so good.

I miss living in Center City for only a handful of reasons and the big one is Reading Terminal Market.  It does get a little crowded, especially around lunch time, but there are some amazing deals to be had on great food and fun trinkets.
Great please to eat. For the best cookies anywhere go to the PA General Store.
So freaking cool , first time here and the food selection was incredible , not to mention all of the delicious deserts ! One of a kind market place !! Will be going back !

Great sandwiches!  Delicious cookies!  $1 bags of chips!  Cream Soda!

I had never been to Potbelly before, but I will definitely go back.  The grilled chicken with cheddar was delightful.  I got mine with tomato and mayo on Italian bread.  The bread was toasted to perfection.  

My only complaint, and it's more of a caveat than anything else, is the ordering system.  It's not rocket science, but it's good to know that there is a unique system to ordering.  You order your sandwich first.  Just the basic "I'm having turkey" or whatever.  You can also pick up your drink there from the cooler.  Next, you order your condiments / extras (lettuce, tomato, onion).  There is also a display of chips to choose from (only $1).  Finally, you put it all together and pay.  We were fine, but the family in front of us (who had to be from out of town, on a college visit, and mom was definitely a helicopter parent), seemed terribly confused.  

Anyway, I will probably be here again soon.  It's right inside the hospital grounds, so if you need to visit a friend or get testing done, it's a great lunch spot that is super convenient.

I stayed in Philly for the weekend and my hotel was (unintentionally) super close the the Terminal Market. Score! I was so excited that I could walk through the Market and browse all the different foods this place has to offer...Sooo much variety (wear stretchy pants lol) It was so PACKED but that didn't stop me from stopping by every day while I was in Philly. I would definitely  recommend you have cash, although most of the vendors accept credit most of the vendors are very fast paced and it was a lot easier for to pay cash instead of charging everything. I know this review is kinda vague so I will sum it up like this...if you're in the downtown convention center area take some time and visit Reading Terminal Market... It's awesome!

5Star because the place is huge so you can find something you're down for that's really good, no sweat. That being said, outside of some of the crowd favorites that are basic and satisfying, some restaurants specifically are better or worse than others objectively. By grouping Reading Terminal Market as just the market instead of allowing each restaurant to be represented and in turn individually rated and reviewed by the community.

Reading Terminal Market is a wonderful place both for the transport element and the massively diverse cultural food market filled with wondrous smells. The floors stay pretty clean, bathrooms are a toss up but what can you get its Philly. Place stays well protected and cops are abundant; often you'll find a group of blue vested men just sitting at a table enjoying their gyros and pork ribs armed to the teeth and still laid back. At the same time, police will always be on patrol for any dangerous activity or suspicious individuals. 

I enjoy the place, what can I say.

My first stop in Philly after dropping off my bags at the airbnb location I was staying at.

The Reading Terminal is an amazing place jam-packed with all sorts of delicious food stands, ranging from sandwich places to indian cuisine and pastries/icecream. Definitely a great place to spend a couple hours sharing different food with friends.

I stopped at a couple different locations which will have reviews to follow: Tommy Dinic's (Roast Pork Sandwich), Rib Stand (Boneless Rib Sandwich), Bassett's (Icecream).

There is also a nice selection of produce,meats,and seafood. With the seafood selection being the best of the batch. I saw some shrimp that were easily larger than the size of my hands!!

The Reading Terminal is definitely a spot you must check out for both the wide variety of food as well as the experience!

I LOVE it there!!! So hard to make food decisions here!

Beck's Cajun Cafe - Po Boys, Jambalaya, and Fried Mac and Cheese Balls

The Original Turkey - grilled turkey Ruben sandwich

Whoopie Pies from Flying Monkey

Grilled Cheese from Melt Kraft

Lemonades from the Amish Stands

Cookies from Termini Brothers

LOVE EVERYTHING!!!

It definitely gets crowded here during holidays, lunch time, and weekends so plan accordingly and be patient!

One of the best there is!  Great choices.  Fresh produce.  Select cut meats.  Always bustling.  Always busy.  Great shops/stands/restaurants.  My favorite place is the Thai place located mid center.  Try the salmon curry w/broccoli and rice and you won't be disappointed.

Recently went on vacation to Philadelphia.  My cousin took us here for the first time and was overwhelmed by all the food vendors they had and fresh  produce section.
If youre ever in Philly, go here and stop by Beilers bakery. Baked goods are made fresh daily and one of the best pastries/doughnuts we ever had!

Growing up with Pike's Place in Seattle sets a pretty high bar for farmer's market quality.  Reading Terminal does not disappoint -- cheese steaks, Amish pastries, and buskers by the dining tables.  No fish means no weird smells, to boot.

Oh, and everyone pronounces it 'reeding' market, awesome!

I really want to love Reading Terminal Market for all it's variety and chaos but it's too chaotic. Every time I walk in there, hundreds of people are rushing past you, bumping into you, and you feel rushed to hurry, get your food and get out!

I have tried a few of the stands there but my favorite will always be Bassett Ice Cream shop!

I've been here a bunch, always late night, and haven't been disappointed.  Then again, it's hard to get disappointed when there's greasy, filling, tasty food in front of me, whether it's a kati roll or a pizza.

Their paneer rolls are solid...the paneer tends to be a bit dry in everyone except for the achari paneer roll, mainly due to the achar (pickles & sauce).  I think they can probably afford to fry the paneer a bit longer to give it a more crispy taste than a mushy dry taste, but for late night, it's still great (as I can eat paneer all day every day).

My friends have mentioned their chicken & rice and biryani's are decent, as well.  I'll try their paneer platter one of these days, but usually just stick to a kati roll (or two) when I'm there.  Their mango lassi is super tasty and definitely get that to wash down the kati rolls, as they can be spicy if you're not used to it.

Overall, a decent late night spot...but the quality would have to prove slightly in order for me to make it a destination for lunch and/or light dinners.
Love A OK produce stand (I think that's what it's called).  The small on in the middle.  Their produce is cheap and great freshness.  You can't go wrong here anywhere.

Looking at what Snap Kitchen really is, an alternative to cooking that's also healthy, I'm on board.

I initially went in expecting the finest of gourmet cuisine and was a little disappointed, however it's still better than what I can whip up and the time saved is priceless. Well, not priceless. It's actually a little costly. For a breakfast of the Spinach Goat Cheese Scramble and Chicken Tikka Masala, it came to around $18. I guess it's all relative though. It's less than we'd spend if we went to a restaurant but more than we'd spend if we cooked it ourselves.

The variety is great. If I didn't find the scramble which consisted of a few of my favorite things- goat cheese and egg whites- I would have had a tough decision to make. 

Everything I've had thus far has been tasty. Not the best I've ever had, being that it is a pre-packed meal, but surely tasty enough to do the trick. 

I look forward to standing there and contemplating my next meal. That thought and choice process is still easier and quicker than cooking it on my own!

Wow what an awesome place! My husband and our parents spent the better part of a cold afternoon hanging out inside the market. 2 of them staked a table while the rest of us wandered and brought back random philly treats. 
Shoofly pie, juices, pretzels, cranberry pecan chicken salad, turkey sandwich, you name it we had it. Also my dad had the best espresso he's had in a long time- and he is very picky about his espressos. 

I wish we weren't just visiting and could take home some fish or meats from one of the amazing fresh butchers. 

It's a great place to satisfy all tastes in your family and enjoy something so unique to Philadelphia!
Right after we finished eating, we saw a rat running across the restaurant.

I've been to a lot of public markets - Pikes in Seattle, Fishermans Wharf in SF, Fanieul Hall in Boston; but the Reading Terminal Market is the best. 

Huge, diverse, overloading your senses with sights, sounds, crowds, smells and the atmosphere of dynamic human engagement. 

It's a combination of food courts/restaurant, food vendors of all types - fishmongers, picklers, chocolates; and assorted bric a brac. 

It's fun and lively. Good place to take the family. Lots of locals there mixed with the tourists. 

Highly recommend it!

Love love love this place for lunch.  Lots of good veggies and combos to make eating veggies and eating healthy fun.  Would love to see more suggestions for combos as the variety of selections is intimidating and I like just being able to pick a dish.
If you can't find what you are looking for here then you don't know what you are looking for.  Absolutely best eats from all over the Philadelphia area!

One of my Philly favorites!!! 4 Seasons, Olde City Coffee, 4th Street Cookies 12th Street Cantina and the place where they make the fresh donuts are the places I frequent.

In a pinch, I go to Mezze and the rotisserie chicken place on the Arch Street side.
It doesn't get better than the salmon at the Little Thai market. And try to keep track of when the Penn Dutch Fair is in the terminal. The amish donuts are TO DIE FOR

Don't expect gourmet food here, but it's worth a stop just for the experience. Noisy with big crowds, and slightly overpriced, but it's a great place for lots of tasty treats. I highly recommend Basset's ice cream (the Gadzooks Blanc flavor is my favorite).
The food is ok but takes forever to get a set lunch (20+ mins) when there is actually no one in line. Service is very slow from their kitchen. Won't recommend if you consider fast food.

I work a few blocks away from RTM, and I wish I had an unlimited amount of money, so I could eat lunch there every day.  
Iovine Brother's produce -- the cashier gave me the student discount on Wednesday (thanks to my youthful appearance)! Produce is fresh and reasonably priced.
Miller's Twist has delicious pretzels. 
The Amish stands have great homemade peanut butters, jams, etc. 
Always tons of great lunch options-- can't go wrong with sandwiches anywhere, really. Love the Four Seasons juice bar. There's Thai, Chinese, sushi, mediterranean.
4th St. cookies are the bomb as is the dessert places right next to it (can't remember the name).  
This place is a must-go for travelers and city-dwellers.

I live nearby and have been here a handful of times since they opened. 

Pros: Food is good, waitstaff is on point and will take care of any issues. 
Once on brunch a pastry brush bristle was in my wifes meal we mentioned it to the waiter and they took the item off the bill. Beer menu is stocked with goodness and they do weekly specials.

Cons: A little pricey more so when you consider portion size to price. 

Definitely worth checking out.

Very cool market right in the city...both times I have been to Philly, I spent a couple hours wandering around.  A whole lot of things going on, so we had a seat in the beer garden to soak it all in.  Interesting meats, cheeses and other interesting things to look at, I recommend this as an awesome way to kill an afternoon.

Only downside is that it gets extremely crowded, and it closes by about 4pm on a Sunday.
this place is a wanderlust for a variety foodie like myself.

The Reading Terminal is a wonderful place to eat, a lot to choose from, a variety of. Food and drinks and. Very tasteful desserts!! 
It's a must try..

I love this place... a must visit in Philadelphia. Great places to eat, cafes, ethnic restaurants, fresh fruit and sea food market. 
Excellent dessert and pastries.

I don't know why i just don't go here first when i come to Philly to work.  The food is really the best - i love the baba ganoush platter - the parsley said is so refreshing and the baba ganoush is the best i have ever had.  That mint / rose water lemonade is flipping fantastic!

This place was amazing. so many different places to try. It was like a swap meet of restaurants. each aisle was labeled as a street and there was enough room to walk around. I wish i had more time to try out all the different kinds of food. From philly cheesesteaks to chinese food to mexican food this place had it all. The hard part about this area was you werent able to yelp all the restaurants through nearby search so to find out ratings on certain restaurants, you'll need to type each individual place's name or you could go in blind and make it an adventure!  I would suggest the second option. If I had a reason to come back to philly, it would be for this one market place.

We tried several restaurants at the Reading Terminal. Some were a bit disappointing. Our expensive pork sandwiches were so dry... Philly cheesesteaks, not so great. 
But over the course of 3 days, we found our favorites. The blueberry and apple fritters at the doughnut shop. The handcarved pastrami sandwiches at Hershels were the winners. We even went back to get some more sandwiches to take on the plane for dinner and doughnuts to bring home to share. Long lines but well worth it for those 2 favorites.

Great energy (be prepared for the lunch and weekend crowds!) and variety of food and restaurants.  My favorite place to eat there is the Thai booth that serves huge filets of grilled salmon with rice and broccoli.  They also have Pad Thai and curry but I always get the salmon.  You can find anything and everything foodwise in the market.

Omg talk about overwhelming. In a good way though. My friend and I walked here to have lunch after we finished what we had to do. We walked around and settled on what we would eat. There are a lot of good places so it was tough. 
We also stopped to get coffee at a store which has good coffee. 
If you are in the area stop in for lunch.

Reading terminal offers a taste of all the flavors of Philly, in one convenient spot.  For anyone visiting Philadelphia it is a must see.  Although, it has its drawbacks. For a typical lunch spot the meals are usually a minimum $10 and the place is full to the brim with tourists throughout the year. Quality of food is always pretty high throughout the market. You can park in a nearby garage for $4 or be a true Philadelphian and take the subway here, it's only a 2 minute walk away from 13th or 11th Street stations. Come here and wander through the stalls and experience the hustle and bustle.

Here are some highlights for the non-tourist:

Iovine Brothers offers a wide variety of decent produce at a good price 
Tootsies eatery allows you to build your own meal from it hot and cold buffet, you can get a decent size salad for about $7, and it has cheaper desserts compared to the rest of the terminal.
Beilers fritters are a must. 
Dinics is a classic and Old City Coffee is great.

This place is amazing. The fresh variety of foods available here boggles my mind every time. The Amish places are my absolute favorite no doubt. The place way in back next to the bread bakery place is the best for chili! cheap too. GREAT lemonade. Best I've ever had actually. The fruit places are cheap too. I saw blood oranges for 3 a dollar! Those are expensive suckers and that was cheap! White asparagus too! The meats aren't bad either and that old used book store is adorable. It's a wonderful place and I just can't say enough about it. If you're visiting do yourself a favor and go! :)

This place is amazing! It's an absolute must if you're in Philly. I went to Beiler's to get doughnuts all 3 days I was in town. Their apple and blueberry fritters were fantastic. I also tried the Shawarma at Kamal's which was delicious and the Thanksgiving sandwich at Original Turkey was also solid.

I loved this place! At first, I was somewhat overwhelmed with all of the different food vendors. I did not know where to start! Once I got passed that initial shock, I realized I was pretty much in food heaven. I ended up trying Dinic's Roast Pork and Beef, Dutch eating place, and the Beiler's (donuts). I was not disappointed at all. I plan on coming back and trying new places once I visit again
GREAT FOOD SELECTION !!! most places do cash though so that's a drawback, but such a philly gem !

A true Philly icon.  You have all kinds of amazing eateries - go to Dinic's for the Roast Pork w/ Sharp Provolone and Broccoli Rabe if you are a first time, to fascinating little shop (think farmer's market type of places), Reading Terminal Market is always bustling with activity.  The biggest drawback if you eat there is it is very hard to find a seat at lunchtime and if you don't live or work nearby, it's very difficult to find nearby parking (and if you do, it is usually at an outrageous price.)

There is a Philadelphia food tour service that is anchored in Reading Terminal Market and that is a great way to experience it for the first time.

Small wraps, not very tasty, and the breakfast food under the heat lamp looked suspicious. The cashier was indifferent towards me, but she was friendly with other customers with her same/similar skin color :-/

My nephew went here on a field trip and asked to be taken there again. We made a whole trip around it and actually went twice. It's very overwhelming and crowded with very little seating but that would be the only negative things I could say. This place is LOADED with great little shops and so many varieties of things! We had food, and milkshakes and smoothies. We bought cookie cutters and passion fruit curd and spice rubs. I wish there was something like this everywhere! Parking is expensive but that is everywhere in Philadelphia and if you spend 10.00 at any merchant inside they validate your parking and it's half price!

Awesome place for everything Philly. Great local food spots, chocolates, breads, pastries, cool peeps. If you only have a day or two in Philly I would hit this place for an hour for lunch or something.

"Tourist trap"
"Waaaayyyy overrated"
"Waste of time"
"Yada, yada, yada"

That's what I heard from Debbie Downer and Negative Nancy who were having a threesome with Pessimistic Pete.  They can keep those experiences because I loved my time here.

It's market paradise for those who love food and homemade goods.   The most popular ones are Bassett's (ice cream), Tommy DiNic's (cheesesteaks/roast pork hoagies), George's (pizza), Beilers (baked goods), whichever place has the Peking duck, and the fried chicken spot with the food network sign.  You could spend the whole day here getting fat and happy unlike the three bumbles I mentioned earlier.

The thing to do is order your drinks/food from wherever, sit at one of the tables and munch while you people watch.  Strike a conversation with those next to you as they're likely a tourist or a local.  If it's a local, they'll tell you where to go for fun and what to look for (unless your a Giants, Cowboys, or Redskins fan; they'll likely give you the finger).

It reminds me of those night markets when I was in Taiwan but with Philly flare.  Lines get long depending where you're at but move quickly so you better know what you want to order or they'll let you have it.  It is Philly after all!

I'll be back with a bigger appetite and with my friends Hungry Hunter and Eating Earl!

I loved our visit to Reading Terminal Market! There is no shortage of things you *want* to try so it's just a matter of figuring out how to try the most of everything. It's concept is very similar to places like Pike Place (Seattle), Grand Central Market (Los Angeles), etc...

Lines for some vendors were certainly much longer than others, but most still moved fairly quickly. Staff at most food stands were also incredibly friendly and willing to chat up locals and tourists alike. Most visitors to Reading Terminal Market are also very friendly - I really only had one passing negative incident where a man pushed me out of his way and into one of the display cases at the Pennsylvania General Store. 

Of all the things we tried, my favorites were easily:

1. Beiler's Donuts: the fritters are a must. We even flew some back across the country to the Bay Area. A little reheating and they were just as fluffy and springy as bought fresh!

2. Herschel's Deli: while the pastrami was good, the corned beef was the real winner. Excellent flavor, stacked nice and high, good slaw. Yum.

3. Carmen's Famous Cheesesteaks: wiz is cool, but I like my real cheese. Their provo sauce is made with a mixture of provolone and cream cheese. Their steak was also of a much better quality than that of Pat's/Geno's.

We also tried:

1. Dutch Eating Place: probably should have gotten something sweet as it seemed like this is what they are really known for but the chicken pot pie was still pretty good.

2. Hunger Burger: fresh lobster mac and cheese came our when we passed by...it was a non-negotiable order at that point.

3. Miller's Twist: I don't know of a baked pretzel I've adored more as of recently...

4. DiNic's: The roast pork was okay, definitely not the best sandwich I've had

This place is a food lover's paradise. Coffee and chai (they make it with fresh spices and Assam tea)from Old Street Coffee was awesome. 
Belier doughnut had an unbelievable queue so they must be good. The Dutch place was super crowded and was quite cheap for the serving size (pancakes for $8 or so from memory). The cookies from 45th at cookie company were great too. 
I could just roam around and look at food stalls here all day haha. 
Apart from food, you can buy fresh produce, jewelry, kitchen stuff,  flowers and cookbooks. Street side parking said $4 for two hours.
This place is a foodie's paradise!  It makes French Market in Chicago look like a hot dog stand.  My coworkers and I ate here every day for lunch while we were in town.  Do not miss this local gem!

We went in search of Tom Dinick's famous pork with broccoli rabe sandwiches and he did not disappoint.  The line was long but moved quickly and there were bar stools around the stand inside the market.  We shared a sandwich and it was plenty big and filling, finger licking good.  To put it in perspective, we also sought out the famous Philly Cheesesteak at Pat's and it didn't hold a candle to this juicy treat.  Oh, almost forgot, there's just one ice cream place in there and it's the old fashioned creamy kind, enjoyed some delicious Moosetracks!

There is literally every type of food here you could ever want. Cheesesteaks, baked goods, deli sandwiches, Chinese, Pakistani food, Indian Food, fresh ground coffee, grilled cheese, pizza, Mexican food..you name it this place has it! There are also places for fresh produce, cheese and meats. 
It can get very crowded during lunch. So much so that we actually skipped eating here because we would have had no place to sit. If you can, grab something and go somewhere else to eat it if you know your way around. 
The next day we stopped by again before the lunch crowd and had some old city coffee and a donut...oh my goodness it was wonderful. 
What a fun and interesting place to visit. Dont miss it!

Hungry? Visit here. It has everything from root beer to fish! The best place to grab some fresh veggies and make a wonderful dinner! From crepes' to soul food to drinks to fish to danish it is the best place to go!

Great historical landmark in Philadelphia! Buy fresh Bronzino from a fish monger, incredible meats from the Amish farmers, and the best fruit in town at Iovine's. The list goes on and on. You can eat breakfast, lunch, and dinner here all weekend from every type of ethnic restaurant imaginable. What a blast!

A public market that's actually a useful, functioning market and isn't just an overpriced tourist attraction. Intriguing.

Recommentations: 
Grab a totally Amishtacular breakfast, for like 5 bucks you can get gigantic fresh pancakes with the works. They are only there certain days of the week, so call ahead (wait, do the Amish use phones?)

Be prepared to stalk the big crowded seating area to get a table, and mentally prep yourself for a random person sitting down next to you to eat. Much like the state of Pennsylvania and the native Amish population - the terminal is kind of small.

When you eat, be sure to sit near the guy who yells about Pennsylvania cheese. ("Buy my cheese! It's very expensive! But that's because it's the best!"). An honest salesperson. Old skool.

Buy some cheap pies from the Amish. They're very homemade and very reasonably priced.

Hit the farmers produce market. It's also surprisingly inexpensive and definitely "Super" and always "Fresh", unlike the same fare at certain nearby grocery establishments.

Many Options
-Great for any tourists to visit or non-tourists
-Varieties of Food
-Great Atmosphere

Great everything traditional Philly Food. Italian roast beef sandwiches at Dinc' s, the best donuts ever!( superior to Federal Donuts) at Beilers. And can't go without buying a fresh pretzel from the Amish. The seafood counter in front of Old City coffee( best French Roast beans) has the absolute freshest, healthiest, deliciously prepared seafood platters, and one of the  best variety seafood in the city. Don't forget to stop at Metropolitan Bakery and any item will not disappoint. The Flying Monkey has great Butter cake and coffee pastries. Riel Cheeses has best value, greatest variety, and freshest lunchmeat and sliced cheeses that beats the supermarket packages any day. While you are there, pick up the best chicken pot pies you can bake at home and prepared jarred hot pickles. Learn more about the Readi g Terminal in my next review!

Free wi-fi!!  OMG, how cool is that, given that I can spend hours poking around here.  12th Street Cantina was pretty good- they have prepared Mexican foods, can make something fresh from the menu, and have staples ingredients like posole and quesos that you purchase for home cooking.  yum.  They didn't have horchata- booooo!  Salumeria was celebrating their 25th anniversary and handing out delicious (free) cupcakes.  I bought an incredible 3 year aged cheese that was exactly what I wanted- sharp, calcified, memorable.  Great coffees, fresh juice, etc.  Don't dismiss this as a tourist trap.

The Reading Terminal Market's one of my all-time favorite spots to shop for holiday meal treats, fresh produce, delightful gifts for new home buyers. Fun place to catch up with friends & clients. Can't wait to take the family for our annual visit to see the Holiday Train Exhibit.

This place has everything you craving from, roast port sandwiches, cheesesteaks, donuts, jerky, candy, Chinese, Thai, beers, pastries, cookies, spices, fresh fish, pastrami, corn beef, fresh oysters, beers, and whatever else. If you can't find something to eat here then you don't belong! I traveled all the way from Maui, HI for Tommy Dinics roast pork sandwich and believe me, that shit was the f'n bomb man, if I lived here I would be a 300 pound happiest fatass alive.

Neat little spot. 
Service was awesome! In spite of walking in with a very large group, our waitress was prompt and completely on top of things.  The food was ok, very average 'pubby' food although they had some interesting twists on sandwiches and a couple awesome appetizers (especially the mac and cheese croquettes and buffalo chicken meatballs).  However, sometimes all you want is just a plain ol' burger (with a side of really good fries) in a really friendly joint.

Talk about variety! The Reading Terminal Market is a great time. Especially if you have friends or visitors from out of town, it is a great tourist attraction. A great place to people watch, walk around and get phenomenal food and treats. 4th Street Cookies are phenomenal!

We ate a place called pearls oysters for breakfast. Super delicious! I had the breakfast special. Veggie benidects. Toast topped with eggs, spinach, avocado slices served with home fries. My co-worker ordered the grits. They were the best and I don't eat grits often cause everyone can't cook them right. The service was also very good. Can't wait to return to Philly just to eat here.

First place I stopped in Philly and still the place I go to very often after my move here. It's a place that also sells cheap fruit and veggies. I have tried almost everything and I have usual now like the Italian pulled pork cheesesteak in the middle of the market, the donut joint that everyone waits in line for, the salmon curry at the thai place, and the turkey place towards the center as well. They have quite an eclectic variety and highly recommend going here.

One of the city's gems, Reading Terminal is the best place to go for a lot of things and I will list all of the ones that I go there for. Ice cream is always a good one and the food in general that you can get is awesome, the Greek and Sang Kee counters are probably my favorites other than DiNic's of course. If you get there pretty early you can just walk right up to DiNic's and get a roast beef and to me it's totally ok to have one at 9 am. I only go to Smucker's now for meat and bacon (sometimes I cheat on them with Kensington Quarters now). The bacon prices are the same or cheaper than the supermarket and the quality of what you are getting is miles better. For seafood there is no better place than John Yi's seafood, they consistently have the best and freshest selection of seafood and everyone who works there is super friendly and helpful. All in all there isn't a better place in the city where you can get everything you might need in one spot. Iovine Brothers produce is also a nice little gem in there, this place makes me happy to live in Philadelphia.

Now, how can you not love the Reading Terminal Market? I work as a tour guide in city, and love bringing tourists to this Philadelphia gem. They are always overwhelmed by the sights, sounds and above all the smells as soon as they walk in (I always bring them in through the Amish bakery section by the northwest door for full effect). The food and goods are all local-not a national chain store in the place. Whether you're visiting Philadelphia, or or a long time resident as I am, do NOT miss the Reading Terminal Market experience.

If your coming to philly make sure you stop at Reading Terminal Market. This place is amazing. There is a vast variety of food, fresh fruits, veggies, chocolates, ice cream, and plenty of other things. You name it it's here. Check out Blue Mountain winery the selection is great I loved all of the wines I tried.

Have been in college in philly for three years now and finally made it there! Suuuuper crowded and hard to move around and see everything. From what I hear it's busy pretty much every day and all the time. There was a Latin band playing outside the day I went, so it was a really festive environment.
Oh, shit.  What is this place and why doesn't Pittsburgh had one?  You could spend days in here trying to eat your way thru this place.  No lie.  Avoid it, if at all possible.
The donuts are always fresh and nice. I also love the Amish diner. The only downside is how crowded this place can get, for a less busy visit, I'd recommend going earlier in the day, during the week.

There's such a great vibe to this place. Every time I go here, there's somewhere else to eat and explore.  Every variety of food you can think of... from diner options, Jewish delis that rival anything NYC can pump out, sausages, bbq, baked goods, pretzels, and of course Philadelphia cheesesteaks. This is a great place to roll to with a crew of friends, everyone can get the food they'd want and then you can all commune in one of the collective seating areas and share.

Not only is the food great, but the vibe is great and unique with a great old school flavor. Newly inspired places like this are popping up in other major cities, but you should definitely hit up the RTM to get a taste of one of the originals.

I went to the Reading terminal with a few friends. We went on a Friday about 11am. We got our lunch almost right away. I ordered from Franks. I got a cheeseburger and fries and a soda. I asked for well done and the burger was med but it was good. the fries were great and there was a lot of them. Then we walked around. Our trip to RTM was good.

You can't beat this place. I look forward to coming here every year at Thanksgiving. You do yourself a disservice if you don't show up with an appetite. One of the things about Philadelphia that I miss the most.

Great spicy foods.
Friendly and nice smile customer service.
Love it!!

Wahhhh there's so much to choose from I don't know where to start!!

Busted out my Yelp app to see what's worth my time since I'm only in Philly for the day.  Dinic's was definitely at the top of the list.  I also got to try the infamous whoopee pies.  The lines move pretty quickly in general so long line didn't necessarily equal to long wait. 

Restrooms were also surprisingly clean for such a busy place.  Kudos to that!

I live in San Francisco and visited my boyfriend's family here in Philadelphia for Thanksgiving.  Holy mighty hell, the vegetarian cheese-steak was the most delightful thing ever to cross my lips!
The crowd was sweaty, noisy and rude, but I enjoyed it all.
Two words: Foodie Heaven!  This place is amazing, and is home to such diverse offerings that there is sure to be something for everyone!  Don't miss it if you are in the city.
The market was excellent with many local shops and restaurants. We ate Tommy Dinics sandwiches and toke apple pie with us. The fried chicken was also tasty.

I have a love / hate relationship with the market. While I love that it's right there at Mark East with wonderful selections for lunch and farm fresh shopping, I think it is also a victim of its own popularity. At lunch time it is often so crowded that you can't even move down an isle. People often just stand around and have no awareness that they are creating a human traffic jam. Thus, I try to avoid RTM like the plaque between 11:30 and 1:00 PM on weekdays, but sometimes the call of Dinic's roast pork or beef overrides my aversion to crowds.

My only complain with this place is that it closes so early!  You can get some of the best deals just before closing though.  If you want to eat, come two hours before it shuts down or most of the vendors will have already started packing up their delicious foods.

You're going to want to make a point to stop at DiNic's, Bassette's, and the Creperie.  Also stop in for Amish weekend or head over to AJ's Picklepatch for fresh preserves!

Live everything about this place. A couple of places to not miss are Olympia gyro, beilers pickle patch, becks Cajun kitchen, Miller's twist, and fourth street cookie just to name a few of my favorites. The vibe is super crazy but totally something to see!

Great place to people watch, shop for foodstuffs, and eat delicious sandwiches or pastries!

My favorite eatery I've tried in the Reading Terminal Market is Hershel's, though I wouldn't push Dinic's out of bed, either. It really looks like you can't go wrong no matter where you eat, and I love the amazing selection of different (and fairly inexpensive) cuisines.

If you live locally, this seems like a fantastic place to pick up fresh fish, meat, or produce for very reasonable prices. I can't comment on the actual quality of these items but it sure is an eye-feast. And the fish counters all smelled clean as can be.

Why only four stars? The Market is dizzyingly crowded on the weekends, and there isn't nearly enough seating to accommodate the ravenous mobs looking to gobble their purchases. It was so crowded I actually felt anxious and uncomfortable. I much preferred my weekday visits.

I'll admit it, Reading Terminal Market makes me feel a little jealous of Philadelphians. I'll be back on my next visit.

A well lite, spacious and clean indoor market offering a  wide selection of vendors ranging from eatery, arts and craft, florist, fashion and grocery.  Locals and tourists (that would be moi) alike crowded this place daily!  Upon the first day of my first visit to this lovely city, my tour guide took me there and we walked through alleys of delicious goodness!  I had breakfast, coffee, cookies, flowers and yummy philly cheese steak!  On busy days the line for philly cheese could take 30 mins!  Well worth the wait!  I devoured my quickly and told my tour guide i need to be back for more soon!

This place is the bomb-diggity! It's one of the coolest places around, and definitely the coolest market I've ever been to! You can get anything there, and I mean, Ah-NEA-THING!! There's over 80 different vendors, selling anything from yummy imported chesses and susages, to home made ice creams and chocolates, to veggie, Indian, Thai, Mesican restaurants, wine shops, butchers and fresh fruit vendors. Get the idea?! I love going here, getting a freshly made pastry and hot chocolate, and just wandering around and taking it all in. It is awesome!!

An iconic Philadelphia location where you can get just about anything. From produce, fresh seafood, great butcher selections, flowers, or even a great meal for lunch or dinner. The Reading terminal market has everything you would need. A a great place to run some quick errands and grab a bite to eat.

Lots of good variety, and very reasonable prices for fresh fruits/vegetables.  It's hard finding good produce in the city, at least at a reasonable price.  Very crowded, but that's because everyone else loves it as much as I do.  Going on a Sunday before it closes isn't worth it: a lot of the vendors aren't there on Sundays and it's packed.
Reading Terminal Market has everything that you need everything is fresh good or good for you

Food good with great diversity. Anything from Dutch pies to Halal shawrma to cheese steaks. Caution, do not remember which cheese steak shop but kind of bland and cheese sauce pretty bad. Other than that great food and grocery shopping area.

Love this place.  Great place to pick up produce, meat, baked goods, or a fully-cooked meal.  I like the variety, quality, and price of produce and meat here.  And while you're there, grab a meal from any of the amazing restaurants.  The crowds of gawking tourists can be pretty annoying at lunchtime.  I prefer to go at the end of the day, when it's less crowded.

Like a going on a field trip! So many wonderful sights and smells. Food of all kinds to try out. Plenty of places to sit down to eat. 
Sandwiches....home made pastry....home made soft pretzels.....chocolates in all shapes and sizes.! ....the biggest fish I have ever seen for sale.

A great adventure and place to enjoy lunch, dinner or snack!

At Bassett's had a double-decker of their glorious ice cream on a sugar cone (the best way) during the week of the DNC.  For five dollars it seemed as though I received almost a pint of the most delicious peach and mint chocolate chip.  In comparison, I had just eaten two of the tiniest scoops of ice cream at a farmers' market for almost the same price.

Been eating there at Bassett's since I was a kid (back in the Dark Ages), they are still the best.
Too much deliciousness in one building...was completely overwhelmed with all the choices!!! Yum!!

If anything, come to see the Amish at work. It's so authentic and cool (not even trying to be creepy).

Anyhow, I ended up going to the BBQ Stand and got some ribs but I was pretty torn because there were about 1 million other restaurants I wanted to eat at. I will be back whenever I'm in Philly.

You can't get better.  The atmosphere, the food, the drinks, the shops, the people, the location....you need to go here. Now. And get a pork sandwich from DeNic's. 

Now.

Better than Pike Place in Seattle, Granville Island in Vancouver, and Chelsea Market in NYC.  Probably tied with the Ferry Building in San Francisco. 

I've been told this place is for tourists.  Well I guess I love playing a tourist, cause I'm here every frickin' week buying steaks from Martin's, fruit and veggies from Iovine Brothers, and fresh juice from the amish guy near the east end (try the Victory blend).

Love this spot! I am from California, but make stopping here at some point in my Philly travels a priority. Love all the little authentic shops, bakeries, and shops. I always encourage everyone to stop by when in Philly.

If you have hours to wait for delivery, go for it! Even carry out is long at this location. My pizza was so soft and barely cooked, I had to put it back in the over. I love pizza but, wont be ordering from this location ever again.

Everyone should go here.  It's a bizarre and fantastic market.  It's basically perfect.  

Tommy DiNicks (spelling?) has awesome pork sandwiches.  Old City Coffee has bangin coffee.  The produce market has some things at a good price.  The spice shop is great but I think it might have closed so...it WAS great, if that's the case.  The bakery is great, they have every kind of ethnic food possible, prepared and also ready for sale for home cooking.  It's probably the best place to take a group of folks for lunch because there's no way in hell someone will walk away unsatisfied.  

It's just awesome to walk around this place even if you don't buy anything!  It's like a zoo for gourmet food.  Take the kids!  They'll be attracted to all of the beautiful everything sold on site.
My husband and I wandered in here this past fall. Really neat market with a variety of food. Nice atmosphere and friendly people. Check it out!
This place is a boon to conference goers housed nearby...a variety of food stalls as well as artisanal products and fruit. Slightly cramped and bustling but it all adds to the fun.

Boasting a rich historical legacy and connection to our region, the Reading Terminal offers a unique atmosphere, endless freshly-prepared food options, and an "out of the box" experience, making it one the most desired event spaces in Philadelphia. An ideal option for a non-traditional wedding, corporate or social celebration!

We were expecting to spend at least half the day here but I think 3 hours tops is good enough to explore the entire market.  It is a few blocks walkable distance from the tiny Chinatown which in turn is about a 10 minute walk from the Liberty Bell & Indepedendence Hall. 

Some places we hit: 
1) Dinic's Roast Pork & Roast Beef Sandwich $7 + $1.20 for 2 toppings (Either cheese & pepper or Cheese & broccoli). We grabbed a seat at the counter and ordered a roast pork sandwich which the waitress said was most popular there. It was very juicy and tender. However noticed that most people ordered the roast beef which looked very appetizing. Note to self: Order roast beef sandwich with broccoli on top next time.  
2) Bassett's Ice Cream: Homemade goodness. $3.50 for 2 scoops : pistachio & peach (loved the peach)
3) Miller's Twist: Cinnamon soft pretzel $2.10. Highly Recommended by me and Adam Richman (MAN V FOOD!).
4) Bee Natural: Honey galore. Bought two bottles of Butter bean ($14.59 for 48 oz) and Blueberry honey ($4.50 for 12 oz). A lady gave us a taste test of this.

Next Trip: Carmen's Cheesesteaks & Hoagies for the hoagies (the line was as long as Dinic's).
Amazing variety, so if you and your friends can't agree on a place to eat, this would be a fantastic place to go.  Most of everything is delicious!
Cant go wrong with most of the vendors here for food.  Get a pork or beef from Dinics and a cookie from Fourth Street Cookies!

Great place.

I wish all cities had this type of market.  The way a food court should be, not the corporate chain-restaurant filled schlock they have in the malls these days.  Multiple food stalls.  Variety of every type of food- diner, asian, middle eastern, seafood, etc...and amish.  Also a bunch of non-food stalls.  Great produce also.  I wish I had something like this where I live.  I would never need to cook again.

I had the amish breakfast - pancakes and bacon.  The pancakes were decent but the bacon was TO DIE FOR.  Not the crappy thin stuff but the nice thick slices.  I'm salivating just thinking of it.  After that, I splurged with a soft pretzel.  OMG!!!  Right out of the oven.  So hot and soft.  Finished it even before I got out of the place.  I wanted to try so many other stands but my stomach failed me - too stuffed.

Just a warning.  Great ambience if you like the down-to-earth, in-your-face, about-the-food-only environment (which I love)  Don't expect 4 star dining wait staff.  Most places are take out only.  Others have stools and a counter.  There are communal tables that are open to everyone but be ready to sit next to strangers.

My husband and I live near the Industry restaurant and wanted to give them business since we knew one of the owners. I must say that the service  acceptable. However, the food was down right nasty. I chose the burger which I thought would be very good since Good Dog is well known for an excellent one. The meat is of the brisket type and did not make for a tasty burger. It tasted like a crunchy bread sandwich that I could only muster two bites of. My husband had the shrimp sandwich which was subpar (to me it tasted like a nautical bread sandwich). On a positive note, our waiter was extremely concerned and offered another entrée when he noticed that I did not eat mine. I politely declined since I could not bear to eat another bite of their food. I really wanted to like this place because of it's location. It is a hip joint and could be wonderful if the food was not so putrid. I am sorry Industry. I will not be giving you any of my business in this economy. I would rather go to Royal.

This particular location is notorious for screwing up orders especially if you order through the app. Save your time and your money and travel to the City Ave location instead.

UPDATE: Before I made this review, I reached out to the store and to HG with no response from either regarding the situation. However, I find it odd that they have time to comment on Yelp before responding to calls and emails about their service.

I've been here several times. I have not even made a dent in trying to taste everything this place has to offer. But everything I've had so far to date has been very good. There is an enormous selection of food and deserts and more. The atmosphere is bustling and it's so lively. There are a lot of tables and seats but you'll want to try to grab a spot as soon as you see one because they tend to get snatched up pretty quickly. It's definitely a place to visit if you've never been to Philly before.
This place is a must go if your a tourist. They have amazing food, produce, and etc.

What's not to love? One stop shopping for everything great! Almost all that Philly has to offer (and then some) under one roof, open year round! 
Too many great eats to mention... 

I suggest walking or taking the subway since traffic and parking can get a little hairy and expensive if you don't know where you're going. They do have a parking garage though if you insist on driving.

This place is like a dream come true. I think yes, maybe other places I've been had some kind of a similar market where goods were sold and delicious, delightful, amazing foods were offered, but it seems like almost every business in this market is a hit.

We tried the famous Tommy Dinic's and even met the owner who was so friendly he threw in extras for us. We tried the original turkey sandwich, which was the most delicious, and largest sandwich I have had that was FRESHLY carved ... ever! And the cookies and pretzels and ice cream delights.
