The only thing that was sort of sucky is that not all of the businesses here are open all of the days that the market is open so we were not able to try out the deliciousness of Dutch Eating Place, but perhaps we were saved according to Steve T. as it literally was an abandonment of hope of eating less once you enter. 

If you come to Philly and you don't come here, you really have missed out on a LOT. Not just one, but many, many restaurants, vendors, and delights that you would be hard pressed to find elsewhere.

Less mentioned, this place also sells produce, seafood, fresh cheeses and other grocery related items that are fantastic. I was nomming for days in here, even a fellow visitor noticed me everywhere in the Market and said "you're still here! eating!" ... hah guilty!

I love the Reading Terminal Market! There vendors have exceptional service and the quality of the food is unmatched for the Philadelphia area! 

You can get fresh meat, homemade grains, and basically whatever else you want for a reasonable price.

Awesome place. Went to Beck's for breakfast and had Po sandwich, they're homemade Cajun mayo was the tits. Ivones produce has the freshest fruits and vegetables at a great price will def be back to both and more.

Still one of my favorite places in Philadelphia.   My husband and I had grilled cheese sandwiches from Valley Shepherd Creamery and Meltkraft Grilled Cheese.  They were delicious!!  The sodas were also really good.  Different flavors and made from sugar cane (no refills).
I had the 'VALLEY THUNDER', which is (12 month) cheddar, BUBBE'S BRISKET and baked macaroni & (our) cheese.  Absolutely phenomenal.   Great bread and cheese makes all of the difference.   My husband had a mozzarella grilled cheese with spinach and tomatoes.   He really enjoyed it.  
We also got some donuts from Beiler's Bakery.  Again, really good.  I love their bacon caramel donuts.  We bought 4 different flavors.  The donuts are always fresh and the line is long, but moves quickly.   I love this market.  There is always something for everyone.
A true Philadelphia experience.  A must if you are in the city of Brotherly love!  They have everything, from the Amish to Zapoli's.
Loved the paneer masala roll. It tastes like butter paneer! Chicken masala and paneer achari were just okay. Good thing is that they do home delivery - I live close to the Franklin institute.
I absolutely love this place. I wish I lived closer so I could go for shopping more often. They have the best seafood  ever. I highly recommend it to everyone!

This is a great place to go, especially with good Friends.  Stop by any of the food stands and expect to receive a good meal.

This place gets insane on the weekend so if you can go on a weekday.
Amziang place, big chicken bigger than my hand lol, love the squid, but mainly love the the Lime Black Tea!!!
I love this market! There is truly no place like it. You can find a little of everything. This place is great in quantity and diversity as well as quality.

It doesn't get better than having hundreds of merchants across a variety of cuisines that include restaurants, bakeries, confectioneries and produce stores, all under one roof. Expect to get everything from fresh produce, meats, fish, artisan cheese, groceries, ice cream, flowers, grilled cheese, baked goods, crafts, books, clothing, and specialty and ethnic foods. 

Fun fact: According to Wikipedia, three of the vendors today are descendants of original market merchants from 1859.

Reading Terminal Market can draw large crowds during the weekends, so avoid the lunch hour and other busy times. 

This place is like an endless maze with a new surprise at every corner. My favorite is  Beiler's Donuts that always has a long line, but it moves fast and you get to see them make the donuts from scratch while you wait.

The second I walked in, I knew I would love it.
My family and I went for lunch, and we each ordered something from a different vendor.

My brother got the grilled pork sandwich from DiNic's. The meat was moist and the roasted peppers, definitely made the sandwich even more delicious.

My mom got sausage with homemade saurkraut along with cornbread from Frank's a lot. Good portions.

My cousin got a caramel and apple crepe, which was actually really good, because I expected a mushy apple (like the ones in apple pies), but it was sweet and had a bit of a crunch to it, which was a pleasant surprise!

I got the philly cheesesteak from Spataro's with mushrooms and peppers. It was okay (I personally think the steaks from Pat's or Geno's is better). And I also got coffee from Old City Coffee, strong, but good.

We also went there for lunch the second day and it was just as yummy.
I love Reading Terminal at the Holidays.  What a great day today shopping for food and gifts for my family and friends.

Reading Terminal Market is a foodgasm!! The delicious choices are overwhelming. I used to work at 15th and Market and we went to lunch here as often as possible. I want to eat lunch here every day for the rest of my life.

And, the Termini Brothers cannolis ... wow. I know there's a god because he invented beer and cannolis.

Monk's Cafe and Reading Terminal - for me, that's Philadelphia.
Excellent stands, big fan of Herschel's deli, Martin's Meats, Downtown Cheese, Iovine Bro's produce and Metropolitan Bakery.  Insanely croweded at lunch time, though, so go early.

Underwhelming... I was expecting a lot from this place. The idea is great, it was just lacking flavor. I had the chicken tikka and paneer roll and both were disappointing. Generally Indian food has deep rich flavor and I didn't get that here.
Favorite stop in Philly for fresh vegetables and any variety of food. Would recommend one of the many deli counters.

hey this is a nice place for Indian cuisine the chicken biryani taste very good and it's sufficient for two people along with Biryani they also serve chapati and lettuce salad all comes in just $10 if you want you can also try rules as well as Indian drinks.
More pictures. Large converted train terminal into small eating stalls, handmade chocolate, fresh meat and vegetables.

Love this place! Ended up here this afternoon because the Christmas Village was a let down. Never a sad thing when you end up here though.
The crowd was moderate when we arrived...about 1. But got busier as the day went on. For being just two days before thanksgiving the crowd was exceptionally friendly. 

Beilers bakery was BOOMING with people buying pies and pastries of the sort. Happily the donuts line was not as long as a Saturday so we took advantage and jumped in line for a half dozen. Really excited to try as we never have! They had their pumpkin donuts so I'm pumped to give them a try! 

We ate pizza and a sandwich. Totally forgot the named the place but it's all the way in the back.  Pizza was yummy and my boyfriend said his sandwich was okay. He said it would have been better if it was warmer. But overall, good experience for lunch as we were able to find a place to sit! Everyone at the tables were so nice and chatty. (And commenting on the cuteness of our little one!) 

We got some delicious sausages from the Country Food vendor and we can't wait to eat them as the last time we had them they were so good!

This place is always a pleasure to visit. 

And for the record to anyone heading here...check out Becks! It's super yummy New Orleans food! And if they have the alligator-GET IT!!

The atmosphere here is pretty good..the waitress was really nice. Great Beer selection. Had myself the "Mad Elf" on tap which was really good for only $5 plus they have speicals on drinks n food everyday..just check their instagram to find out what they will have that same day...Had the "Industry Burger" with bacon n fried egg...it was delicious but wish the sandwich bread was better like a "Hawthornes Cafe" bread...other than that....I like the place...would definitely come back again..

Is it crowded? Yes.

Is it worth it?  ABSOLUTELY.

Even if you're introverted, and aren't the biggest fan of crowds, I'd urge you to find some time (perhaps an off-peak hour?) to walk through and explore this market.  They have a little bit of everything for everybody.  I don't know if there's another place in this city quite like it.

If you're visiting Philly, you MUST check this place out! This is one of my favorite places in Philly and I always end up taking my friends and family here when they visit. There's so many different types of vendors here, it's the perfect place to satisfy any type of craving you may have. My favorite is Beiler's Bakery, they sell Amish donuts that are DELICIOUS. There's Dutch food, Asian choices, Cajun options, Polish pierogis, coffee beans, cookbooks, ice cream, an oyster bar, and so much more! 

It may get overwhelming at first with the huge crowds and long lines, but it's not all that bad! With all the food options in front of you, it will all be worth it!

How can you not love the Reading Terminal Market?  The sights, the smells, the people, the goodies.  I've been coming here since I was a teen in the early 80's.  It has changed quite a bit since then but the vibe is still the same.  
I love it!

I can be seen here basically 3 times a day.  

First at Le Bus bakery for my 1.25 hazelnut coffee.
Second at Hershel's Deli for my 3.09 ridiculously large in size "small Maztos ball soup.
Third picking up cheese infused with black truffle (SO good) and produce across the way at a stand that offers 10% off for college students.  

If you don't sense my enthusiasm for this market let me make it more clear for you:  I LOVE THIS PLACE.  I can get almost everything I need, and most of the time below grocery store prices.  And when the Dutch come in I think the best smells come out of that place I have ever laid my nose on.

I have said this before, this is about one of the only things I like about this god foresaken city, and bless its food filled heart.
Excellent! Fresh fruit, veggies and delicious baked goods.

If we were in Philadelphia for a week, I'd gain 50 pounds, because I would eat here for lunch every day and then stock up on sweets.  If I lived close by, I'd come all the time for the marketfresh items I saw but couldn't consider because I'm not checking a bag when we fly out.  There are so many amazing places to choose from.  We tried many items and were not displeased with anything we consumed, but I'd highly (as in it is a MUST) recommend the rib sandwich from Glick's Rib Shack and the Corned Beef sandwich special from Hatville Deli.  Go here early in your Philadelphia visit because you'll want to go back.  And if you decide to get some ice cream from Bassett's (which you should), listen to your husband when he says you should get it in a cup and share as two scoops is too much in a sugar cone!!!
Fun shopping and a great selection of food choices from wonderful pastries, cookies and donuts to lunch and dinner fare. Best early.

This is one of my most favorite places in Philly- if you haven't been you need to drop everything and go now. From fresh cheap produce, deli and seafood counters and spice shops for the chef in you, to some of the best food I've ever had in my life.

The Original Turkey place provides real off the bone thanksgiving-esque turkey from meals w your fav home style sides like Mac n cheese, greens or mashed tators, homemade turkey soup, turkey salad to the classic turkey sandwich on a variety of fresh breads w tons of great toppings to chose from. Did I mention you can get a 1/2 sandwich, which is huge, chips and a drunk for under $7? It's unreal!

The Amish stands are a huge treat but are closed Sundays and Mondays- from pretzels 10xs better than Philly pretzel or auntie Anne's, a bakery with fresh sticky buns, whoopie pies and cakes, and then their sit down diner style restaurant with chicken and waffles, great burgers and the best chicken corn soup! 

If your into sweets The Flying Monkey delivers but don't forget crepes, dipped cookies, fresh made chocolate, and the Italian bakery w the best carrot cake I've over had-sorry I don't know all the proper names--- you can't go wrong here. My only negative and it's not even bad but Dinnicks roast pork is not my favorite- drive to tony Luke's and skip the cheesesteak and go right for their roast pork w sharp Provo and broc rain!

Also the garage on 12th offers a $4 parking special if you have a business in the Terminal validate your ticket!
This is a well-known treasure but a treasure nonetheless. I enjoyed this a lot better than Chelsea market. Such a variety of food. Prices are totally reasonable, which I did not expect.

Awesome! We hit the crepe place three days in a row and for breakfast crepes or dessert crepes they are amazing.  My husband and son had 3 plates or oysters and could not have been happier and the service was amazing.

We visited philly for a day and I gotta say, this place is a must stop. There's a huge variety of food in this market ranging from American, Indian, Asian, Mediterranean, donuts, fudge, oysters and anything you can think of.  We opted to try Dinic's for their pork sandwich since they were all over the travel channel.  I wanted to try Bassett's as well since I've seen them on TV also but didn't want to ruin my appetite for dinner at Morimotos! So I'll definitely have to try that next time.  There's a Reading Terminal Market parking garage. It's $4 for two hours if you purchase $10 worth from a single vendor.  Make sure you bring your parking ticket so you can get it validated at the discounted rate!
Busy and overpriced, but as a tourist it's a must see. Comparable to Quincy Market in Boston. CROWDED. Again, as a must see I give it 5 stars but be prepared for their prices and the long lines.

1. The spice shop in the northeast corner
2. The kitchen tools shop in almost northeast corner
3. The dutch diner
4. The donut shop in northwest corner
5. Tom's diner right in the center

If you know your orientations, I gave you the address to most amazing shops in RTM. Enjoy :)

This is the worst chick fil a I have ever been to. My salads are consistently watery and the food is never as good as the other franchises. Today I went through the drive thru and ordered chick fil a sauce for our meals. Of course, no sauces were provided. Who wants to eat nuggets and fries without sauce? Never had a single issue with any other franchise around the country.

AWESOME OLD SCHOOL MARKET......  For foodies and people who like the freshest fish meat and breads etc.  If you rate this any lower than 4 stars you obviously don't get out much.  This is one of the oldest market in the US.  There is a variety for everyone and I do mean everyone. I have always had a great experience here. Some of the vendors had been here for many many years. This market is made up of small business owners. So spend your money here, there are no big box stores at this location.

A friend and I waited in line on Monday. It was our first time and we did not really know that process, I really feel that they should have the first line server at least ask are you new to us? This way we can get our money's worth, I ordered a bowl and didn't really know what items they had that I could put in it. When I finally caught on because I listened to the person behind me I had to ask the food servers to go back with my food bowl because I was new to the concept and was unaware what I could get. Everyone was nice about it, but I feel if someone asked ahead of time I wouldn't have been a bother. The serving size was ok. Quality of the food was good. Price was a little high thou, considering the wait and portion you get.

LOVELOVELOVE Reading Terminal Market (which is apparently pronounced like "Redding"? according to my philly friends). So many choices that we couldn't decide on just one. I shared Keven Parker Soul Food Cafe (leg and thigh w/ one side - mac&cheese), Sang Kee Peking Duck (peking duck roll), Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties (lemonana - mint, rosewater, and lemon juice/smoothie), and Beiler's Donuts (coconut custard). Everything was amazing and I wish I had more room in my stomach for everything (and maybe money). It was slightly crowded but it was lunch time and a very popular tourist location. There were numerous seating areas in the middle of market and other seating at certain merchants. I would definitely come again and try different places!
Can't go wrong...Sang Kee, DiNics, Hershel's, Termini's...as well as some very good butchers and fish mongers.
Must go! Food everywhere. DiNic's sandwich in the back was really good and quick even with a line.

I've loved this place since I was a kid.  You can buy everything you need and lots of things you don't at Reading Terminal.  As a rule, the prices are better than Headhouse Square Farmer's Market and even Clark Park Farmer's Market (both of which I also recommend).  

 Baguettes: Metropolitan Bakery

 Cheese: Salumeria

 *Scrapple: Dutch Eating Place

*If you don't know what scrapple is, it would behoove you to find out, quick!

This is our first time in Philadelphia and we randomly chose this restaurant as our first place out! We were a bit apprehensive at first because when we came in we didnt know where to go/sit or if there was a hostess, and when the girl who sat us did come upfront she was a little unsure and quiet.  However, that wasn't a big deal, and the waitress we had was very, very friendly and efficient.  The atmosphere is cool, but not a fan of the tables and seating arrangements. Slightly cramped. The food was AMAZING though. There was a slight wait with the food, but that was more than okay. It is actually nice to go to a place where they take pride in what they cook. You could really tell when our food arrived that the time was well spent on preparing a beautiful and delicious meal, and my husband and I loved that. The service wasn't rushed, it was relaxed and we had a great time.

Really good food. What a tasty meal the chicken wings sauce was not that great and undercooked. The falafel was very nice and looked so pretty. It was perfectly crunchy and butterfly effected my Godzilla mood and was so awesome. The French fries are awesome

Ive been to reading terminal about a dozen times since moving to Philly and its always a good time. I like how busy it gets with people shoulder to shoulder. Theres always something different to try and I love the pretzel place and the produce market - they have fresh squeezed orange juice for sale!
I love all of the choices offered but you have to be ready for loud controlled chaos. Finding a seat is always difficult too.

Yiu just have to know which stands are gimmicks and which are legit down home food and treats.

always get the donuts...

Absolutely amazing selection of vendors surrounded by amazing history. I recommend getting a roast pork sandwich from DiNic's. We did the food tour, which was really interesting and resulted in many samples from the market including snapper soup (it's turtle, and delicious).

Always wanted to get in here. Wasn't sure what to expect. Inside are a bunch of little stores with food, produce, and other little shops. Got a cheesesteak at one of the places and it was terrific. Great place for lunch and a cool place to stop into.

Got their at 345pm and DaNics was already closed and I really wanted to try the pork rabe. So I went next door to Hershel and had the reuben special. OMG it was so good and I was stuffed until the next morning. Paid about $9 for food, drink and tip. Great place and lots of other neat shops in this place. Next time I fly to Philly I'll go back and maybe get there in time for the pork rabe!

Reading Terminal Market makes NYC's Chelsea Market look like a prison for yuppies. Chelsea Market is small, drab, desolate, crowded, and full of overpriced crap that no one really wants except the few, the proud, and the hipsters.

Reading Terminal, on the other hand, is a colorful, bustling center brimming with food stands. Even on a Sunday, the place was still quite active. There are fresh produce stands (which have delicious goodies!), delis, ethnic stands, and cheesesteak stands. Prices are fair; and vary depending on which stand you go to. Good luck picking a stand, too, the variety is immense.

I even found a machine with free Reese's Pieces!

I wish I lived nearby. If I did, I would come here every day for my fresh groceries!

A Philadelphia landmark that fills locals and tourists...and jurors, oh can't forget the random convention people all craving good eats. If you're afraid of fairly large crowds, then this place isn't for you during the weekday lunch rush hour. If you want fresh produce or a cheesesteak or just cheese, this is your place! Tuesday through Saturday I think are the best days to go since the Amish vendors are there with their comfort food and sweets. There's something for everyone here!

I was just in Philly for an event at the Convention Center, and ate at the Reading Terminal Market 3x for lunch.  I read the Yelp reviews and I'm shocked at how excited everyone is over the food at this place.  

Yes, the choices are endless.  And yes, it's awesome to have so many options to grab a quick lunch.  But the quality of the food, while not bad, is pretty much food court fare.  3 lunches from 3 different vendors and it was all just fair at best.  1 just plain disappointing package-tasting corned beef sandwich from an Amish vendor, 1 bready crab cake plate, and 1 hotdog that was worth every penny of $1.50.

Normally I'd be tempted to give this place 3 stars simply for the convenience and variety, Because everyone is raving about how great the food is, I'm gonna attempt to instill a little balance by tossing out a 2.

Went here on Sunday so i missed out on all the amish goods, but otherwise they have everything you'd want. I got some ice cream from Bassets and it was awesome. Definitely worth checking out while in philly
Such a great selection of interesting food. Can't wait to come back I only wish it stayed open later!

Always surprises me how clean and friendly everyone is who works here! They bring your food to your table, often bring around free samples of cookies or icecream and kindly remain attentive to needing another drink or napkins. What fast food spot does all that!? I'd give this place 4 stars but the food sometimes is not as great as usual.

Can you say a whole lot of stuff located in one place? So many things are located in here I just don't know where to start. You can get food, flowers, ice cream, candles, candy and many other things. If you like local markets then you really should check this place out. If you want to come here and eat then get hear around lunch time since that is when most of the places are open. Most places accept credit card but bring cash just in case.

I love how unique the East Coast is, and that you can get Amish made products here.  

Go to Beiler's Bakery and get a cream-filled glazed donut.  They're made fresh, right in front of you..I think they're around $0.90?  Enough said.  I could eat about 10 of them in one sitting.

I'm visiting from out of town and decided to take a look at Reading Terminal since my hotel was close by. 

After walking in, I decided that this was my happy place. If you love supporting local food, then this is a place you need to visit. Be sure to have plenty of time on your hands when visiting so that you can check out all of the options and because many of the vendors have lines. 

I plan on going go back at lest once a day to see what I can eat.

Must-visit if you're in the area or living here. Foodie's paradise, with tons of items you won't find (or be hard-pressed to find) elsewhere in the city. A lot of old, locally famous/traditional vendors that go way back, lots of Amish vendors, etc. Great place to take in the culture and food of Philadelphia. And a lot of the produce is cheap.

If you haven't been here and you're a Tourist you didn't visit Philadelphia
If you haven't been here an you LIVE in Philadelphia, you're a tourist!
I visited this place while in Philly last January. It's a place that's worth checking out if you go. They offer a variety of food and gifts. Also good to just people watch...
We all love it right? What can't you get here? You can't get bored here. Yeah it's touristy but it's fun especially for the kids

I went to KFC tonight with my husband and one of are young people wanted to fight with us why I don't know but all KFC did was push us out with old chicken that cost us $25 do that make is that's right when the other prone started it that's why we can't by where we live because things like this why the company isn't checking on theam
Great touristy place with no complaints simply amazing. Great ice cream, they have everything groceries fresh fruits, every type of food.

I stayed at the Hilton around the corner and snuck away from my group of friends to scope out this place.  I had seen the colorful fruits and veggies from the windows and thought "Hmmm, I'll check this out"

Sensory overload but in SUCH a good way!!!

Later, my friends couldn't decide where to eat and I suggested this place since it has tons of eateries with hundreds of types of different kinds of food.  There are a few Amish booths that have dry goods and delicious treats for sale.  Boy, can the Amish cook!  They have no holds when it comes to cream (HEAVY whipping cream mind you) on top of desserts and prices set so low I feel like I'm ripping THEM off.  $2.80 for a 6" apple pie with ice cream or whipped cream - seriously?!

Brisket, Gyros, Philly Cheesesteaks, chocolate freshly made in front of you, bakeries, Sushi, delis, fish markets, fruit markets, dry goods - it's all here.  It will satiate even the pickiest eater, but the hardest part is just trying to decide what to eat.....

I'm not too experienced with markets like these but I love this place.  I like farmers markets and I find the one outside of the Penn bookstore on 36th & Walnut or the one in Rittenhouse Square just don't cut it for me.  Reading is open all year-round and even has student discounts on Wednesdays and Sundays (just bring your ID)!  

I've ordered porterhouse and NY strip steaks and ground sirloin (3 lbs for $7.50!) from the butcher shop right near the entrance (Giunta's Prime Shop)--the steaks were awesome even when I pan-cooked them a couple days later b/c I was too lazy to go to the grill.  The whole chickens from Godshall's Poultry LLC are awesome and my sister who roasts whole chickens all the time says these are the best chickens she's ever seen--very little fat and the meat tastes great.  

Four Seasons Juice Bar is off the hook.  The most amazing fruit drinks I've ever had (and I'm not crazy about fruit or juice--Jamba Juice and Smoothies King are ok but this place is really unique).  If you like super sweet drinks/juices or smoothies, this place isn't for you because they are SUPER fresh and I doubt they add any sugar to their blends.  Out front, they have boxes and boxes of fresh fruit and vegetables (peaches, mangoes, strawberries, carrots, broccoli, ginger).  They have crazy blends like carrot, mango and spinach and the like.  For each 16 oz. drink, they mix in 4 whole carrots.  I stick to pineapple, strawberries, and mangoes.  

I get kalamata olives all the time (the best I've found in Philly) from the cheese shop in the middle of the Terminal at the Salumeria (their cheeses aren't so great--tasteless mozzarella for example).  The turkey w/ mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, etc. from the Original Turkey is surprisingly tasty.  I didn't like the pastrami reuben from Hershels East Side Deli--there was no Russian dressing, just some sauerkraut, tons of fat-laden meat and the bread fell apart immediately (this was definitely no Famous 4th Street or Rachael's Nosheri).  

My default grocery store is Iovine Brothers Produce since they are the biggest and freshest in the Terminal but sometimes I'll go to the smaller produce shops like OK Lee Produce for some greens and basic fruits.  I've gotten tuna steaks, king crab legs, scallops and salmon fillets from John Yi Fish Market and Wan's Seafood.  They are both fine but I'm not a huge seafood person so I can't tell you the nuisances between the two.  The market has an ice cream shop and tons of more restaurants.  It's a great place to browse, grab lunch or do your weekly grocery shopping!

I just bought $50 worth of cheese and cured meats and balsamic vinegar from Downtown Cheese (the owner is also an artist!) so I'll let you know how they are!

I'm a big fan of this place. As others have said, it can definitely be crowded but it's worth it in my opinion. You can get just about any type of food here. I love the fact that you can come here to sit and eat for lunch or buy food to cook for dinner. They really have it all and there's so many different types of food from traditional American cuisine to Greek. You really can't go wrong. The hardest part might be trying to decide on one place. Reading Terminal Market is a must stop if you're visiting Philly.

What an experience to come to this place. If you like to eat and sightseeing, it is a good place. There are a lot of varieties food from multi countries. The only negative is the parking space and expensive parking fee.

If I wanted microwaved frozen dumplings I would go to hmart. I didn't expect authentic dumplings from a place serving cheesesteak dumplings but if the main dish you serve is dumplings than at least make them fresh and cook them properly. 

In addition to the rubbery microwave feel you hate with a dumpling skin, the contents of the dumplings were pretty bad. My wife had one little nibble of each of her dumplings and threw out the majority of her meal.

The place is cute and the service is friendly but I will not be returning.

I do love this place. The ambience (history!), variety and quality of food are all, if not unique, very rare. I see negative reviews from drinkers, but if you are serious  about drinking, If you want to drink good beer go to Monks or get take out from the Foodery. 
Yes, the prices have gone a bit bistro, but this is the big city. Tasty fun for all ages!

From hot meals to handmade ice cream, fresh pastries to local fruits and vegetables, ethnic cuisine to cookies and chocolate -- Philly's famed Reading Terminal Market brings together food from around the world. It's a veritable garage sale, featuring a million things from a million different cultures as well as delicious locally-sourced foods, ranging from Italian truffle oil to German sausages to local Whoopie Pies. One could spend an entire day just exploring the whole place. If you're feeling daring, try one of their famous chocolate-covered onions!

RTM's fame as a city landmark is undoubtedly well-deserved. But beneath its bustling facade lies a much more sinister truth -- that a surprising proportion of its shops and stalls hawk low-quality wares, catering to the daily hordes of brainless tourists who grace its halls. Buyer beware; Kamal's Middle Eastern is abominable. Market Bloom's flowers are rarely fresh. Items that could be found at a grocery store tend to be of equal or lesser quality, and horribly overpriced to boot. Meat by the pound? Don't even think about it.

That said, RTM is a must-see for out-of-town-ers. Just be cautious, and make sure you've got an empty stomach!
If you are in Philadelphia, stopping here is a must! Cheeses, meats, and baked goods as far as the eye can see..

When I arrived in Philly, I had no idea that such a place as magical and wondrous as the Reading Terminal Market existed. Going off a tip from a friend on Facebook, a quick Google search showed my hotel was only a couple of blocks away, so off I went in search of something new. When I arrived and stepped inside, I couldn't believe my eyes.

I was instantly transported from a dreary cold and rainy day to a vibrant market full of shops and people milling about. I entered by the fresh produce and thought, "it's like a farmers market". Wrong. This place is a little bit of everything. Farmers Market. Grocery Store. Restaurant. Fish Market. Bookstore. Winery. Lancaster County Amish goods. Cakes. Pies. It's a you-name-it, they have it kind of place.

All of the shops are fairly small but packed. For those of you in Indy, imagine City Market sized businesses, but picture 150-175 of them on a single floor about three times the Indy City Market. Picture lines of people 30 people deep waiting for hand rolled donuts from Beiler's Bakery. Picture small restaurants with seating for only 10 or so people turning out every type of food you can imagine from all over the country. Picture me walking around trying to absorb every piece of this that I could, all the while wondering why Indianapolis doesn't have something so amazingly awesome. 

Philly, you've won my heart and you've won my stomach. Places like this make me want to come back every weekend just to find another shop that I didn't know existed, but am better for knowing that it does.

As a newbie to Philly, this was a great way to meet the city. Tons and tons of things to see and perfect for the overly hot day we were walking around in (since its indoors and cool).
Excellent place to shop for produce, meats and fish, while also grabbing an egg, cheese and scrapple breakfast sandwich.

We went last friday nite. it was not that busy yet.
we ordered the pork skin chicharon- i thought it was a little stale and I just thought that it will be fried freshly right on the spot.
Pork nuggets- the best one i didn't know that it was shredded pork inside 
mexican st corn- the best smokey corn ever. will order this one to go another time
general tso's chicken- i thought the taste is more like an orange beef sauce

will come here again to try other dishes in the menu

A little touristy, but plenty of gems in this market. I highly recommend the roast beef with sharp provolone & broccoli rabe. The roast beef was juicier, more flavorful & cheaper than the brisket. We were really excited to try the Italian sausage, but we went late (2pm) to avoid the madness at lunch time & they'd run out of meatballs & sausage, so it may be a little tricky to find the sweet spot between wading through the market chaos & being able to order whatever you want. 
We had breakfast at Pearl's one day- great waffles & a good value for breakfast.
We sampled 6 different doughnuts from Beiler's one afternoon when the line was reasonable. They were all good, the texture & flavor were excellent, but a bit sweet for my taste. Next time I think I'll go to their bakery right across the aisle & get a piece of mega-crumb cake or pecan sticky bun.

First time in Philly & our hotel was right across the street. The 1st thing we did after we checked in was to head to the market for late lunch/early dinner. 

It was definitely crowded - Black Friday at 4pm. Duh! But we were able to safely navigate with a 7&8 year old in tow. 

The variety is out of this world. I wish we had more time & stomach room to be here longer. As it was, we were there 4 days & ate there 3 of them! Seating is definitely an issue, but since our hotel was right there we took our food to go.
Heaven. You can find absolutely anything and everything you could possibly want or crave. Definitely a must do when in Philadelphia.

This major tourist trap is nothing more than a mall food court.  You can do much better for a cheese steak almost anywhere in Philly; and why not join the debate about Jim's or Pat's or Gino's.  You can also get oysters and shellfish elsewhere.  The best options here are the ample amounts of cookies, pastries, chocolate, and desserts.
You need to go here. Best when its not completely packed but great for any kind of food or grocery you want.

very cool place- anything you want-it's all there
felt safe and comfortable
decent food

Solid and prompt.  One of the best non-food-truck places to grab a meal in the Penn/HUP area. The sandwiches are good, the salads are good, the desserts and shakes are good. My favorites are the Wreck and the Roast Beef sandwiches. ALSO: hot peppers!!!

I do have the suspicion that the sandwiches are getting smaller each time I go. Somehow the sandwich still manages to be a satisfying meal.

Beat the lunch rush by going at 11:30 or 1:30 instead of noontime. It makes a huge difference.
Amazing amazing amazing! Best coffee, donuts, pancakes, etc all within one incredible establishment. Just wish it were open a little earlier / later.

Reading Terminal Market is one of Philadelphia's treasures.  There are (?) dozens of stands at the Market-- fresh produce, fish, meat, prepared food, bakeries, Bassetts Ice Cream (called the best commercially available ice cream in the country by the NY Times), killer pastries of every description, Delilah's soul food (her mac and cheese won Oprah's mac and cheese cook off and I'm not quarreling with the results, it's amazing) the list goes on, and on, and on.  In my opinion, the Terminal is  the single best place for lunch in downtown Philadelphia.   The only problem is that you have to choose between Peking duck, falafel, fried oysters,  and barbecue. Leave room for dessert.
Not the crown jewel of the Wendy's franchise by any stretch of the imagination. Wendy ought to be ashamed.

I don't know why I stop visiting the Reading Terminal. I use to visit the Terminal every Sat when I was in college for fruits and vege. I started again last weekend. My husband and I love to go to Martin's to get their homemade sausages and their meat and Iovine for their produce. If we are early, we would head to Dutch Eating Place for their pancakes and turkey bacon. My favorite lunch is going to Hershels for their pastrami sandwhich or Little Thai Market for their $5.50 Thai lunch boxes. The Terminal is a place where you can get a diverse assortment of food and get fresh produce for your home that beats the supermarket prices.

Food choices are endless!!!  We spent time here wandering around on NYE.  Ended up having a great piece of pizza, but you name it, they have it.  Pastry, Greek, Chinese, German, PA Dutch, seafood, meat counters, the list goes on and on.  Easy parking across 12th Street.  Super close to Chinatown and a close walk to Liberty Bell.

This is the kind of place I like to go to when I am traveling. It involves locals and their food (and oh yeah tourists of course).

There is a piano player.
Loved the pretzels and pickles made by the Ammish. 
The veggie restaurant was great with fake tuna and chicken salad.
Bought some chocolate covered pretzels here as presents.

This place is great for brunch on the weekends. The food is consistently fresh and tasty and I've never had trouble getting a table, even with a large group. The servers are really friendly and attentive, but not overly so. My favorites are the fried green tomato salad and the shrimp with grits. So delicious! 

The only main complaint that I have is that there are very few vegetarian options. I eat fish but no other meat and prefer to stick with primarily vegetarian options when I eat out. I think it would be really great if they added a sandwich or burger to the menu that was vegetarian. It would also be nice to have some lower priced beer options.
This place is a must.  Loved Terminis bakery.  The Canoli...AWESOME!!  Sparatos cheese steak and fries...2 thumbs up!
Awesome food, great shopping, and unique finds!  The selection of food, especially on the days when the Amish are there, is second to none!

A very impressive place! I have never seen so many different food options in one convenient location. It's also a great place if you are looking for gifts/souvenirs. There really is something for everyone. If I visit Philly again, I will definitely come back to the Reading Market.
I love it hear so many to choose from alligator gumbo to sweets and delicious Amish breakfast
The best spot foodie spot in Philly. A fun experience with an abundance of extra delicious and well-priced food.

Philadelphia and Philadelphians are extremely lucky to have such an amazing place.  It reminds me of similar style markets in Europe.  You can find just about anything under the sun, in the food world, at Reading Terminal Market.  Whatever your favorite cuisine, you can find it here.  Whether you're hungry and looking for something prepared now or looking to stock the fridge at home with meats, cheeses, and veggies, this is the spot.  Check it out.  You won't be disappointed.

Lots of options here! Donuts, Indian, Chinese, Thai, Greek, sandwiches, crepes, meats, cheese.. I could go on and on. 

There's an amazingly cheap grocery with tons of fresh veggies, a flower stall for fresh bouquets.

Tried the Greek place with a fresh gyro. Their meats are sliced fresh off of the heat spinner, and the lamb was super flavorful. 

Super crowded though, be prepared to lose someone.. we did.

Visiting Philadelphia for my family reunion, the Big Bus rolled past Reading Terminal Market and displayed the incredible array of foods. I walked in and was so overwhelmed. I wanted some of everything!  I didn't buy any food because I had just eaten. But I made a note to return on another visit. I would recommend Reading Terminal Market.

WELCOME TO FOOD HEAVEN!

Add this place as a must visit when you are in Philadelphia.

What a great place to visit! You will have to contend with the crowds and line-ups (and that is the only downside) but it is all worth it.

There are way too many awesome food offerings to list and you will be overwhelmed with the decision of what you want to eat.  Therefore one visit to this place won't be enough. l definitely will be back!

Nice to see quality of product and top notch customer service to the forefront. Stopped for breakfast and was very satisfied (again). From the friendly greeting from Harriet at the counter to the manager walking through the dining area making sure everyone was having a pleasant experience.

Fantastic stop while in Philly. Food galore. A must-do while in the city.  Great stop for breakfast or lunch.  We ate at Molly & Malloys, splitting the deviled eggs and a philly cheese steak. Both were deee-lish.  Also picked up some chocolates, cheese, a baguette loaf (which was warm and crispy) and some ice cream. Great end to our first sightseeing day in the city.

Great place for a fresh food market, homemade sweets, and a Philly cheesesteak. Head to the middle and you have found the best cheesesteak ever. It was so good we went back the next day. Forget about going to the tourist places to try one. 

Walking distance to several hotels. Go early as it tends to shutdown earlier than we were ready to be done for the night.
Come hungry!  Wide variety and it's all good.
I love Reading Terminal But just a word of advice "Get there early". I don't like crowds.

One of the true gems of the city--my family has loved this mecca for generations.  What do you want, chocolate?  Cheese more your thing?  Oh, fresh produce? Artisanal culinary goods?  Shrimp the size of your hand?  Well, whatever you're searching for, they've got it...and it'll be the best you've ever had!

If you don't know what to do, Reading Terminal Market is the best place to shop and eat. From food to grocery shopping, there are numerous things to do in this market. It is endless. I have been there a few times and I haven't even finish exploring, :D

Let the journey begin !

I am reviewing Potbellys for my wife.  She was pick-pocketed of her iPhone and wallet during lunch with coworkers, and when she notified the store manager he didn't care one bit.  Awful customer service and human decency.  On another note her chicken salad sandwich was flavorless

This place is a food lovers mecca !!!  When you walk in the door, I swear you hear Angels singing and life just gets 1000X better.  There is more food choices than one can fathom and ALL of them delicious. Just walk around and take it in, this place is amazing.  Im making a super sad face right now because I went there to get the FAMOUS DiNics roasted pork, broccoli rabe & provolone sandwich and, when I got to the booth they were SOLD OUT !!!  I almost collapsed in the aisle; a did tear up though.  That being said, I got a fantastic Greek Lamb Dinner Platter.  Great price and a great savory and satisfying choice.  Ill be back tomorrow, to get my pork sandwich at DiNic's.  ill be sure to get there before 3pm.

This is a great spot with friendly staff and always a solid beer list. I wish they had better meal options for a vegetarian---I always end up with a couple of apps, which are always delicious, but I'd go there more often if there was a delicious veg entree (NOT pasta!).

This is my favorite one stop food place. It's good for breakfast or lunch and great for groups because everybody can pick what the want and then sit together.The gyros are amazing, the cheesesteaks are great, and don't forget to get dessert at Beiler's donuts!

I am a bit biased as I live in the Philadelphia Metro area.  I always enjoy a trip here.  A good choice of foods and merchandise , plus the people watching is fun.  Down Home Diner is a must as is the Amish market and a treat from Termini's as well as a roast pork sandwich.  If you are in Philly it is a great way to spend some time.

As senior Philadelphian, I started going to the Reading Terminal when I was a kid, and that was 70+ years ago.  Nothing much has changed except the signs have gotten more modern and the food better and multicultural. You visitors to the Convention Center, forget the fancy resaurants.  Walk accross the street and roll up your sleeves.  A lot cheaper too!

Wow, while in a family visit to Philadelphia we read about the Reading terminal market. As a Cleveland girl I know firsthand how crazy busy and fun these types of food markets can be as we have our own beloved West Side Market. 
The reading market couldn't be more unique. A cross between foodie heaven boutique stands and small food related retail booths. 
While my town market is more of s grocery store experience where most foods are purchased to take home  and prepare. The seating areas at the reading terminal along with the larger proportion of pre made delights are more suggestive of buy and try now.
Which we did with great glee.
We started with breakfast at the Dutch eating place. The bagel sandwiches my family had could have been better had the bagels been toasted but my blueberry pancake breakfast was delicious.
My son preferred his 1. ham egg and cheese pretzel and his 2. Bacon egg and cheese pretzel from millers twist. 
My daughter lived the pickle assortment at Beilers. While we didn't buy any the donut line and boxes being carried out suggest Beilers is also the place to go for crazy good donuts.
Temporary stand offerings of gin and vodka tastings at boardroom liquor and banana pudding tastings at Nina's topped off our treats. 
Can't wait to visit family again next year to return.

Came here not on a busy Saturday. But for the combo, they didn't have minced meat rice. So early and they didn't have it. A little disappointing. 
The ninja crispy chicken (xl) $7.95- it was ok. Once they cut it and put in the box-the bottom chicken pieces get soggy. The crispy coating comes off the chicken. Only the top pieces were good. The chicken taste rubbery
Bean curd- was the good, the coating is not too crispy.
Beef teriyaki combo- the beef was cooked medium. Soft but lack flavoring.
Grapefruit drink is refreshing. 
Cash only- but they have an ATM machine
Great place to purchase fresh groceries at a cheap price!!!
It is great What can I say. I stop here every time I come to Philadelphia. Great food at great prices. And always an adventure.

Amazing!!! Please please visit this place when you come to Center City, Philly. They have everything from a deli, fish market, Pennsylvania Dutch Foods to soul food. You must try some cookies from the Pennsylvania General Store.

This is a must visit place in Philadelphia. I loved this place and the food,deserts,cheese, philly cheesesteak delicious, honey, etc. They have it all. They also have the nations oldest ice-cream place. Don't eat too much so you can try their ice cream.

Obvi 5 stars (one of the best places to go in the city) but really each shop should have its own review. Most are 5 stars anyway though. Everything I've had in here has been excellent and very cost effective. Maybe quit looking at reviews and just stuff your big fat face! Don't complain about the crowds either, that's what happens when ish is this good.

This is considered FAST FOOD?? Chick-Fil-A is definitely one of the rare fast food chains that is trying to break away from the fast food joint mantra. Reason being, is the service which for fast food is above average, surprisingly clean, and lets face it the Spicy Chicken Sandwich they are KNOWN for is damn tasty. 

I order the #4 Spicy Chicken Sandwich combo with a small chicken noodle soup, along with a Cookies & Cream milkshake (SO GOOD). My order was taken, and the food came out very quick. The cashier who took my order also brought my meal to my table, and was very courteous in doing so. I did not see this coming, overall the sandwich was the best part and the meal was pretty filling. 

I rarely eat fast food, but if I have to choose Chick-Fil-A is to be considered. The A in Chick-Fil-A is well deserved.

I have a love/hate relationship with Reading Terminal Market...more specifically... i hate the crowds and everyone else knowing how amazing it is. It has every option you could possibly want for lunch. From cheesesteaks, greek, thai food, mexican, and a salad bar. 

Fair warning: Fridays the terminal is insanely crowded. If you are not a tourist, I'd avoid it unless you love crowds and people walking around aimlessly with no clue where they are going!

I love Iovine Produce and OK Produce, I usually stop by every couple of weeks. Fresh, cheap produce and wonderful customer service! 

I started looking around Philly for cheap produce markets and this hits the spot! I've been to several places where the produce was cheap but rotted a day or two later, this place is NOT like that at all. I love coming here because I can eat healthy without breaking the bank.

This is one of my absolute favorite places in Philadelphia, possibly in the whole country.  It's like walking into a bygone era, when local producers came into the city daily with fresh meats, produce, cheeses, flowers, breads, spices... except this still happens!  Everyday!  

The maze of independent vendors and the dozens of delicious lunch joints dot this one-of-a-kind experience.  My sister goes to the market several times a week not only because it's one hell of a shopping adventure but their prices are fantastic on the highest quality ingredients.  

This is a landmark establishment and has been part of the fabric of this wonderful city for nearly a century.  It is so heartwarming to see the market bustling with every city resident, young and old, rich and poor, black and white... forget the supermarket, THIS is how city dwellers were MEANT to shop! 

What a true institution.  At the very least grab a cheesesteak or some ice cream when you're in Philly at this place.  Unbelievable!

RTM can be overwhelming if you on the weekend but it's a gem during the week.  There are numerous stalls with any kind of food you can imagine as well as wonderful gifts.  Some of the best stalls are closed on Sunday or Monday so plan your visit accordingly.

My girlfriend frequently shops here and I have been a few times... you can't really beat this place in the city for selection and price, although personally for me it's too crowded. But if you can get over that part of it, it's probably the best place to go for fruits, veggies, etc.
Amazing place to buy everything! I recommended to everyone.

I don't know if this place deserves more than 3 or 4 stars. It's got a lot to pick from: food, souvenirs, and shopping - but it's crowded, loud and full of pushy and overzealous people. There was nowhere to sit after getting food (a small food court that was crowded and a pure trash infested wasteland) and it was confusing to maneuver around. There was no clear map anywhere and it was difficult remembering where we parked. Oh, and the parking. It would have been nice if it was clear in the parking deck how to get your parking validated. We had to go back inside the market after leaving to get the receipt validated by the merchant I bought a $15 coffee mug from. As a foodie and earthly tourist who has traveled all over, I can't say this is something I'd do again.

the greatest place for lunch in downtown philly. 

about a zillion food places housed in the old Reading Railroad train shed at 12th & market--yes, the same Reading that is in Monopoly, as in "take a ride on the Reading".  

For many years now, a great food joint.  

a great dessert joint.  bassett's ice cream and many coffee places.

you can buy fresh fish octopus or squid here.  meats & veggies.  many odd spices and foods.

the coup de grace is they connect to the convention center above, to the suburban east commuter station below, to market east mall to the east, to city hall to the west, and to the Marrriott across the street.  

a superb philly tradition!

The second I opened the door and glanced inside I already knew I loved this place!  It is a market centered around food, not so much on knick knacks.  But everything looks ridiculously good!  The placed was packed on a Monday afternoon.  Our first stop was the Famous 4th Street Cookie Company, we opted for one that was covered in chocolate which had the texture of frosting, the cookie itself was so soft and delicious!  For lunch I could not decide what to eat, I ended up having the artichoke, spinach, mozzarella sandwich at the Mezze, it was ok, not too much flavor and lots of bread, but still enjoyable.  My husband had a cheesesteak sandwich which he enjoyed, I tried a bite and it was tasty, warm and spicy!  I wanted to try Bassett's Ice cream, it looked so wonderful and tons of unique flavors but I already had plans to visit The Franklin Fountain while in Philly.  Must visit even for a quick stop if you are in the area!

We try the various restaurants at the market and are constantly amazed at the quality and diversity of the market. I get there by PATCO, at few blocks away because parking is expensive, and a problem if a large convention is in town. There is no lack of business,though.
 Philly may have a nice convention center, but is lacking parking.

I love this place i always have a great experience and there is so much to choose from i love the cheese shop Downtown cheese and deffinatly the produce stands.  LeBus bakery great bread it makes me wanna have a big bowl of pasta and sauce to dip it in.  Old city coffee everytime i go in the fall and winter i gotta have the double mint mocha it so minteeee!  Rick's Steaks always the best place for an oldtime philly steak and whiz.  Tokyo sushi bar is great they make it so fast and right in front of you great if your in a hurry for lunch and want something light.  By George Pizza & Pasta has great sandwiches.  Everything is great here its deffinatly a place to visit in philly on the regular.
What can i say?  A must visit, even in town for one day.  Brevity is the soul of wit.

I had a really good meal here. The buffalo sweetbreads were delicious, the beer list was excellent, and the service was great too. I also love that they have outdoor seating because there is not nearly enough of that in South Philly. This place is a great addition to the neighborhood.
Really great steak frites, loved our server, too. The space has a great vibe.

Decoration goes with the ambiance. Cost of items are a little high specially when side orders are not included with the sandwiches. Side orders are charged extra. Sandwich portions are small. Metered parking only.

If you live in Philly or are visiting, GO HERE!  Every type of food you can imagine.  If you can, avoid on Saturday mornings or weekdays during lunch, because it can get crowded.  If you can't find something to eat here, you're crazy!

Reading is an adventure for your stomach. It's just got so many options, you can't possibly see everything in one trip. You can find pretty much everything here, and it's always fresh and delicious. You can buy loose leaf tea, sauerkraut, pickles, fish, cheese, meats, bread, cookies, candies, spices, flowers, anything! You can watch cheese be made, watch chocolate be molded, watch meat be butchered. It's an experience you have to have for yourself.

Super cool place. Reminds me of the Westside Market in Cleveland, Ohio. I wish we would've had a longer stay in Philly so we could have had more opportunities to go back and check out the other dining options. I will definitely return when we are back.

Best Chick-Fil-A, especially for it to be in South Philly.  The service is excellent.  It feels like a regular sit in restuarant, not just your average food restuarant.  There is music playing and you are never waiting long.  The employees greet you with a smile and give you whatever you ask for.  They even line up the ketchup packets in this Chick-FiL-A.  When your food isn't ready, they ask you to have a seat and they will bring it to you.

Food is always hot and crispy, never soggy.  It's fresh and a peaceful little place.  Very clean as well.  They even have little faux flowers on the table.
Loved this market, especially trader joes.  many other great shops

I stumbled across this place while touring the campus of Temple University, so I decided to give them a try. First let me start off by saying that the restaurant was spotless! There was only one employee working which was weird but she handled things pretty well I guess. I didn't appreciate her talking on the phone while she prepared my food but whatever. Anyway- THE FOOD= nothing to write home about. I created my own bowl and selected chicken as my protein. Oh boy was that a mistake!! The chicken had a really weird taste to it that I honestly can't describe. I ended up picking the 5 tiny pieces of chicken out of my bowl and throwing it in the trash. The vegetables, noodles and sauce were just ok but there was no wow factor. This place may be great to some but I was totally underwhelmed.

A must-go if you are in Philadelphia! Reading Terminal offers something for everyone! The variety of food seems almost endless. It's always very crowded with tourists, but locals still love to come here. I buy my produce and meats here every week. I prefer to go in the mornings before it gets very crowded. The lines for the donuts at Beiler's can get very long, but so worth it. There is ample seating provided in the center areas for you to enjoy the food. Just about anything food related can be purchased here, including spices, canned foods, special ingredients, etc. You can also get your parking validated here for a discounted rate at nearby garages.

If you're in Philly, you HAVE to pass by the Reading Terminal Market and make sure you have an empty stomach when you do. They're open Mon thru Sat from 8 AM to 6 PM and Sun from 9 AM to 5 PM and they're closed on the major holidays.

I'll get to the food in a second but they also have/sell Flowers, Plants, Seafood, Organic/Specialty Foods, Housewares, Books, Crafts, and Produce. Now onto food, they have BBQ, Mexican, Delis, Greek, Chinese, Cheesesteaks, Cajun, Thai, Pizza, and the list goes on. Even though not all of the places will have their own seating, there is a common seating area somewhere towards the middle. 

I'll def be returning here next time I'm in Philly!
Favorite place to grab a quick lunch while in Philadelphia!  Live the Amish food and so many choices.   Tried the Peking Duck today with pork and bok choy and it was delicious!

I've given it a lot of thought, and if I had one day left to live, I'd probably spend at least half of it in Reading Terminal Market. Not on the beaches of Hawaii, not amidst the lights of Paris, but in a crowded aisle in a market in Philly that smells of donuts and sausage and curry, passing by busy stands of fresh fish, colorful candies, and sandwiches. 

Yes. Give me 4:30 PM on a Sunday afternoon, with clerks calling out that the cookies at the Famous Fourth Street Cookie Stand are now just one dollar. Give me authentic bratwurst. Give me tourist-y souvenirs that are themed with Philadelphia landmarks and Pennsylvania Dutch kitsch. I *love* this place. 

If you think I'm being hyperbolic, please consider the fact that I once traveled two hours via public transportation while in kidney failure just to eat gumbo from Beck's Cajun Café. Seriously. The gumbo (and Reading Terminal Market, in general) is that amazing. As far as food goes, this place has everything you could ever want. Cuisines from diverse regions of the United States as well as the globe. Also importantly, most stands (except some of the gift shops) are reasonably-priced.

Such a fun place to go if you want to try multiple different types of food in one day! Reading terminal reminds me greatly of the Chelsea market in NYC. There are tons of different desserts, Delis, ice cream shops, and even Amish owned shops! (Just be aware that Amish owned shops are not opened everyday! They do not work on weekends!) there is live music on some days, a vegetable shop that provides a discount to students on Thursdays, and so much more. Definitely a place to go if you're visiting Philly or if you're hungry and want to try lots of different food!
Great selection of Amish sweets! I esp love the ice cream and cookies. Another must go is the Cajun counter. Their bread pudding is to die for!

If you want a truly Philly experience you have to make a stop at the market. Butcher's, Fish Mongers, Amish, fresh local produce, variety of cuisines and most importantly fresh baked cookies. Ok that last one may be my thing but damn it, it should be everyone's. I love it here. The atmosphere alone is not to be missed.

I pretty much stumbled upon The Industry by accident, but it was a happy one at that! We stopped in for brunch on a random Sunday after everywhere else we could think of was jam packed. Despite being very crowded, we were seated immediately by the friendly hostess. We were served a delicious, warm sticky bun in lieu of the tradition bread or chips as served at other places. I ordered the burger and the Ghost of Mary drink. My burger was so juicy and tasty, I couldn't believe it! I actually finished a burger for once! It definitely comes highly recommended. The fries were fantastic as well.

The Ghost of Mary was a disappointment to me. I understand the menu said deconstructed, but this tasted NOTHING like a Bloody Mary at all. There's no spice, no zip - nothing. It tasted to me like water had been poured into a glass where tomato juice had just been. It almost had a very boring salsa-y taste to it. I was pretty bummed about it. The drink was sort of refreshing, just totally not what I was looking for.

The decor in this place is really wonderful. I especially love the meat cleaver door handle! All of the staff we encountered were friendly and welcoming. Overall I highly recommend The Industry and will definitely be returning!
The go to spot for everything food. Always keep an eye on the unique hours, but make sure you stop in if you're new to Philly or here for the day. You won't leave disappointed.

A Boston native, I went here by recommendation, hearing it was similar to Faneuil Hall. It is so much better than that! There are more vendors and stands than you can imagine packed into that space. Any foodie could stay here for hours. 

I personally enjoyed the $1 blackberries, and huge create your own salad bar, with everything from chickpeas to chicken wings. I enjoyed the local fruit and vegetable stands as well as the variety of ethnic foods. Be sure to grab a chocolate dessert on the way out!

If you are looking to avoid your typical chain restaurants while visiting Philly, this is your place to go to.

What a cool place!! Tons to see and to try, but it gets very crowded and it is hard to navigate your way around (almost the reason why I was going to give it 4 stars.)

A good place to go to get food for a party or a present for the hostess of a party.  You can come here every day for months and you'll probably never taste everything you can.  

A must for locals and tourists alike.
Love this place. A must see if you are visiting Philly. Excellent food. Great service.

I love theis place, Beilier's donuts is the only place i will wait 20 minutes in line for. Then I get to compenste by going to Iovine of (usually and) OK produce. I love the head nut in the corner of the market.

First- Parking- We parked in the 11th & Arch Street- it was $4.00 for 2 hrs of parking with validation from a vendor that you spend you spend $10.00- easy and - ya I almost forgot, but at the last minute when buying blueberries at .99¢ a pint and other fruity/ veggie stuff I remembered. So it was $4.00

We got there about 12:30 pm-- so obviously smack dab at lunch time, but after walking around a bit and doing my shopping, we decided on lunch- because at the rate of shopping I was doing while hungry....I was gonna buy everything.

Reading Market reminds me of a little bit of Pikes Place market (minus the tossing of fish- if you have been to Pikes you know what I am talking about). Reading has plenty of produce stands, fish and meats counters, nuts, soaps, grocery, pantry staples that are hard to find and olive oil stands and the endless options of foods to choose from at lunch rush or for the sweet tooth in all of us, pastries, cakes, cookies and candies. There are gelato vendors, shakes and of course flowers for your home to make it all springy and pretty or just buy a bunch and give to someone you love, just because.

They have an amazing oyster bar if you love oysters, Greek Food, Italian, Middle Eastern, Soul Food, Thai, you can literally choose anything and be happy-happy-happy with it. I personally enjoy the roast pork sandwich,  the pork is tender, flavorful and so juicy the broccoli rabe is bitter-garlicky-spicy goodness with the melty provolone cheese YES!! I ate half and brought the other half home for the MR. (cuz he had to work and couldn't come with us. 

So my purchases were cheese, pate, pastries, candy (of course), fresh veggies, fruit, a huge cow bone cut in half for Kona & Luna at a reasonable $2.50 lb or something like that. Anyway- I loved my visit and shopping time, if I lived in Philly I would literally do all my grocery shopping here.

Loved this market, it was so wonderful! The Amish soofly pies, Philly cheese steaks, fresh produces and more.

I could spend couple hours easily just looking around and eat good food.

I wish they have samples that we can taste of those sweets, savory and fresh fruits like in Europe.
Thank you Philly!

SO fantastic. It was chock full of food heaven. Very very crowded but I can see why- there were so many good food stalls. We tried a cajun place and of course the famous pork sandwich. Would have gone for dessert if not so full!
This is a really cool place to visit in philly, they literally have everything in one place. I loved all the sites and smells while walking through.

I was looking for somewhere to eat while running errands downtown.  I got a sandwich from Herschel's East Side deli.  I forgot how thick the sandwich was.  I ate it down with a fork to make it easier.

It was loud and touristy, but I was expecting that.  Whatever you order get it "to go" as finding a seat is not fast, even if you have someone scouting ahead for you.
Great venue to try all kinds of foods.  It would take a week to try all the great places.

This is such a fantastic place--I love going here!  Smucker's for their sandwiches, the Dutch Eating Place for pancakes, the candy shop which also sells dried fruit, even the bookstore at Reading Terminal is worth visiting... Wear comfortable shoes and get ready for crowds-- however--unless you visit during off-hours.

Glad i asked my tour guide where I should eat while in Philly. She recommended Reading Terminal and I was a little unsure about it at first but boy was I pleasantly surprised. They have some many options for food it is close to impossible to decide. Look around before you make a final choice. For desert have Bassett's ice cream it's the BEST!!!!
This place is the best for foodies. Tons of restaurants inside it. If you're visiting Philadelphia, this is a must visit. You won't be disappointed. Nice place to hang out on any day.

This is a foodie's HEAVEN! I repeat HEAVEN!
Fresh ingredients all around, making everything taste a 100 times more delicious.

If you're not carb cutting, I say go get yourself a pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and extra sharp provolone from DI NICS! This way, while you're waiting on line for BEILLER'S doughnuts, you have something to munch on! Their line can get pretty long, so avoid the crankiness and get yourself a sandwich! By the time you get to the front of their line you'll be in better shape to start pointing your fingers at all the yummy-goodness! I personally enjoyed the maple-bacon, apple fritter, and the cinnamon roll. IF YOU'RE GOING TO LISTEN TO ANYTHING ON THIS REVIEW... LISTEN TO THIS... Get yourself a DOZEN!

Reading Terminal Market is a great place to browse and to enjoy the bustling atmosphere. I wish I had more time (and appetite) to truly enjoy this market and EVERYTHING they have to market. Come here for a huuuuuge variety of food, types of cuisine, and dessert options. 

Of all the things we could have bought, we decided to try the grilled cheese shop, due to its popularity before $8 you get an ooey-gooey cheesey sandwich with a side of refreshing and salty dill chips. Deliciousness. We don't often eat that much cheese, so we were glad to share this one sandwich. Trust me, it's rich enough. And even though it was perhaps a bit too rich for the both of us, it was totally worth it. Sooo good. 

Surprisingly, this place has a variety of grilled cheese options. It can get a bit overwhelmed, but I recommend just going for the classic. We added tomato and bacon- also a nice touch. 

Remember to event cash- not all shops accept credit cards. While there are several ATM, it's nice to bring cash ahead of time to avoid the fee.

They say the heart of a city is found where it's culture lies, and we all trace our culture back to the food we eat. This holds true for Reading Terminal Market.

This market is the heart of downtown Philly. Make sure you check out Dutch Eating Place. Best Apple Butter in Philly!!!

awesome
cheesesteaks
coffee
meats
thai
mac and cheese

Pretty good for a market. Have lots of options and all good ones. Was so confused as to, which food stall to pick.
Options to buy produce and meat and spices and such as well. If I were living nearby, this would have been my regular hangout spot.

The variety of food here is unmatched anywhere in the city, let alone the tri-state area. My favorite by far is The Original Turkey where you can get hot turkey on a long roll topped with stuffing and cranberry sauce. Finish that off with an ice cream cone from Basset's Ice Cream and you'll be a happy camper for sure.
So many choices it was difficult to decide where and what to eat but that's a great problem to have

A trip to the convention center means a trip to RTM. Love love LOVE all the options for eating. I always take home a bag full of goodies from the Hatfield Deli, and or Flying Monkey. The slow cooked pot roast sandwich is my go to 99% of the time at Smucker's Quality Meats and Grill. The Indian place and Cajun place are awesome too.

Reading Terminal has every food you can possibly think of I'm not sure how you couldn't like it. If you are looking to try foods from other cultures or just plain old comfort food you will be right at home. The best place to go to get a feel for the Philadelphia culture and a nice place for yourself or the whole family.

One of my favorite places on earth! This place is spectacular for so many reasons. You can explore on your own and experience marvelous artisan items, like fresh bread, pastries, jams and jellies, candies, produce, and dairy items. However, you can also come here with a large group and please everyone with their cuisine of choice!

I've been here twice. The first time I was with just a friend, and we really enjoyed the shopping experience. The second time I was chaperoning an eighth grade field trip, and it was the first time the whole week that nobody complained about food because everyone was able to get what they wanted. (Unfortunately, I made the poor choice of going to Tokyo Sushi....avoid at all costs!). There are even vegetarian and vegan options at most locations. You can find something for everyone, and then you can all eat together in one of the several seating areas and enjoy the vibrant ambiance of the market!

I love this place. It is one of the best markets I've ever been too. I'm both happy and sad that I gave up sugar otherwise I could have easily put on ten pounds from indulging in all of the delicious looking baked goods and sweet shops I saw. The Amish breakfast spot was great. Basic hot breakfast at a great price.

I go to Reading Terminal every week to grocery shop, mostly at Fair Food Farmstand and The Herbiary. My husband and I absolutely love the selection of local foods, including all the goodies and fresh produce the Amish have to offer! When friends from out of town are visiting, we are always sure to bring them here to show off all of the wonderful things it has to offer, including some great places to sit down and grab a bite. Metropolitan Bakery, Market Blooms, the spice shop, and kitchen store are also favorites of ours. 
Whether you live in the city, or are visiting, you should make it a point to check out this historic and awesome spot!

We come here regularly to satisfy our curious-must-try-new-cuisine belly. I absolutely love Reading Terminal. I'm a foodie and this place offers so much choices, it'll make your head spin. My favorites (for now, since I've been here in Philly for only 5 months):

Salmon Belly from Little Thai Market
Dinic's sandwiches
Bassetts ice cream
Famous 4th st Cookie
Mezze Mediterranean Food
Termini Bros Bakery
By George Pizza, Pasta & Cheesesteak
4 Season's Juicebar

The farmer's market is awesome to, fresh fruits and vegetables. Oh heaven, every time I'm there. Except when it's swarming with people then that's another story.
Even though it's becoming a prepared food tourist attraction, the Amish & few old standbys still make it a worthwhile stop...

There was a lot about Philly that I didn't care for, all of which was forgotten when I visited the Reading Terminal Market.  I'm from Massachusetts and I heard some tourist in there say, "This is just like Quincy Market".  Yeah...no.

This is the greatest shopping experience for anyone that digs food.  I give HUGE props to Giunta's butcher stand.  Best steak I've ever had and the service was friendly, even busted my balls a little bit.  Prices were excellent.

If Reading Terminal Market were a woman I would have sweet, sweet relations with it.

Suffers from commericaliazation, don't even bother to come here on the weekends if you are not willing to wade through the tsunami of tourists and looky-loos. The worst comments come from people who seem to think they discovered something new, when in reality its been the same forever(at least the 10+years Ive been going); dont complain about lines/crowds if your a tourist who hasn't lived in the area or visited the market regularly. Puhlease....just save everyone the trouble and stay in your burb market area, we appreciate not having to wait for you to make up your mind while standing in front of the cashier(s).

One of the best and most diverse markets I've been to! 

I'm amazed by all it has to offer and all the options, even for a vegetarian!!

Tons of fresh produce, nuts, cheese, bread, chocolate, pastries, jams, sauces, specialty items, flowers..  the list does not seem to end. 

Huge variety of food, snack and dessert vendors as well from all different regions/ethnic backgrounds. Love that. You could come here everyday every day during a week and get something completely different each time. 

It wasn't overwhelmingly crowded the times that I went, except on Saturday.

If you don't want to break the bank.. several vendors are participating in the $7 meal deal with at least one meal combo on the menu for $7. 

I could easily spend hours here.. makes me so happy :)

I love coming here when I am in the area. There are so many food options and you could probably eat here everyday for a whole year and order something different. There is seating inside if you prefer to eat there or you can take your food with you. They have everything from Termini Bros cannolis to the Flying Monkey bakery, Beilers donuts and so much more. It's a great place to try something new as there are so many ethnic food options! It can get extremely crowded around meal times but that's to be expected! This is a cant miss if you are in Philly.

Lots of reviews here so no to belabor the point, this is a must see. If you are stuck at the convention center, skip the crap food choices there and head to Reading Market. For me, Hershel's Deli was the bomb. The brisket sandwich and turkey sandwiches were to die for. I joking said "it was so tender, it was like eating meat butter". Get it grilled for sure!!

That said, it is delicious and HUGE. It's not for those who are looking for small portions. I will be there next year again for sure.

Sorry, but this place is as weird as it looks. None of the flavors match, everything way too salty, totally overpriced. For me, a big miss.

Edit: It has been about an hour since eating my gross Kim chi bowl and I feel disgusting. Really, you'd be better off buying a lean cuisine microwave meal- same amount of sodium and probably tastier.

Ummm, I don't know that I really need to tell you why this place is great.  There are just too many reasons, most of which are obvious.

However, I will say that you MUST go to L. Halteman Family for all of your butchery needs.  They have been my go to for years now and never let me down.

They recently started carrying wagyu (ribeyes, flanks, etc.) and their scrapple is the BEST I've ever had.  Any time I want to wow my family or friends, I grab some tasty beef or poultry from them.

I hate crowds, I hate people, and I hate lines. But despite that, basically, this is one of my favorite places in the world. As many times as I've been here I still feel like there's always still so much to discover, taste and experience. Some of my favorites are the L. Halteman Family meat and cheese stand, the 4th Street Cookie Company, the honey stand that keeps me in giant vats of honey... The list goes on.

After hearing many mixed reviews I finally made it to The Industry. It was okay. I liked the loud, noisy atmosphere, the mix of classic alterna-pop, and the beer menu. 

The food was a mixed bag: kimchi tater tots were lighter & tastier than I'd expected. The truffle dumplings were a little over the edge salt-wise but also savory-delicious. The fried green tomatoes got a little lost in breading, but the salad they came with was nicely dressed. 

My sandwich was no good, though. I got the house special Seafood BLT. If it's a special I feel it should be "special". I feel like that sandwich was thrown together without anyone even trying it before it landed on the menu. The bread was too large & too thick and the ingredients were lost inside.
