There was supposed to be aioli, but I only encountered a hint of it. The tomato was mealy & tasteless. While the mackerel was nice, it was no match for all of that bread. 

If I return it'll probably be for appetizers & beer.

Fantastic market with many vendors inside where anyone can find something for them to enjoy. During lunch hours and the holiday season, this place can get packed, but not enough for me to lower the rating. It is crowded for a reason and a wonderful spot to visit.
I just love going in this place the food is so fresh so eye appealing I don't mind paying for top quality food so much variety never disappointed
Great for prix-fix meals on the go.  I look forward to their expansion in the coming months.

Doing Philly with Danis! Philadelphia Museum of Art (Pop), DiNic's (Italian pulled pork with broccoli rob & hot longs!, Beiler's (berry pie & sticky buns), washed down at Molly Malloy's with an Evil Eye IPA (Philly), Perpetual IPA (Hersey) & Hard Cider

I loved this place. Great produce, cheese, baked goods, food stalls, seafood, butcher shops, flowers and coffee. As well as dry goods and general merchandise some even made by the Amish. My favorites are the bronze statue of Philbert the pig in the heart of the market and the chocolate and peanut butter covered pretzels at Mueller's. The soft pretzels were also pretty awesome, you know it's a good thing when you see local business people coming in and buying paper bag loads of the the stuff. This place is a great testament to Philadelphia and it's heritage.
SO many options for food I especially love DINICS Brisket sandwich and Millers pretzels.  It can be cramped with people HOWEVER i have never had a situation where I waited in line for very long!

I might be going to far but this may be the Indian version of Chipotle.  The food is amazing the pictures in the restaurant really don't do the food justice.  I had the MK special and it was absolutely out of sight everything from the sauces down to the quality of the lettuce and chicken was absolutely amazing.

It's a shame that me and my coworker stopped by this place on our last day in Philly. There were sooo many food options to choose from. Before stopping and eating at the first place that entices you, walk the entire terminal to make your final decision. The terminal is definitely a must.
You can get whatever you're craving, and you can be pretty confident that it will be delicious. Definately worth a visit.

Reading terminal has something for everyone, and it never disappoints! This is a must visit for out of towners, and a frequented place by locals like myself. They have foods ranging from amazing doughnuts to fresh produce, allowing my family with its wide range of tastes to always find what they are looking for.

Seriously one of the best places I visited while in Philly. It is truly a foodie's paradise. I can't really comment on the parking situation because thankfully we were staying at a hotel around the corner. The market is hectic in all the best ways yet efficient at the same time. Lines everywhere, but to my amazement they always went quickly. Food is literally in every corner. I had trouble narrowing my lunch destination to just one place. There was good food everywhere. My favorite had to have been Hershel's Deli. Every tourist needs to try that place.

Wish we had time to try Meltkraft!

The place is a heaven for the food tasting. So many vendors and so much food! Love it! I tried only the smoothie because everywhere were long lines (Sunday afternoon), I wanna definitely to come back !
A must visit for tourists and locals alike.  Top on my list of things to do for visitors.
Great destination for locals for fresh and artisan foods. CAn be a little crazy on weekends, so try to go during the week.

This is one of the coolest markets ever! I love the wide range of things I can buy here. It's like Wegmans on steroids. Haha! I would recommend visiting this place, especially if you're just visiting Philly.

There are so many different vendors here that I basically go to RTM to look around like a tourist. From sweet to savory to inedible, RTM has it all. I recommend going to the Harvest Festival, which I thought was very fun.

I love the Reading Terminal!  I can go shop, eat, and take people from out of town-it's a standard for us to take people there when visiting- I  meet people for coffee there or at brunch. It has everything! the best fish the best meats, the best coffee -the absolutely best coffee- chocolates, flowers, and a wonderful fruit juice smoothie place we always go to. A great Thai take out -long lines!- I buy my spices there, cheese, freshest eggs and also seasonal stuff! A historic place, authentic, a must when one visits Philly but also great for us who live here. Easy to park across the street.

The Reading Terminal Market is awesome. I have been at a conference at the conference center above the market all week. I've had a number of meals there, and they have all been great. The ingredients are fresh, the preparation is good...  What's not to love. If you're in Philly, you should certainly stop by.
So good!! The chicken masala Kati roll makes for the perfect snack complimented with a mint lemonade. Very flavorful and mixed with the white sauce gives it the perfect kick.

Very good for what it is! It's a quick snack place - nice decor, friendly service, and tasty. I tried the Masala Roll and the Chicken Tikka Roll; the Masala one was a bit better in my opinion because it had the tomato sauce, so sort of tasted like Chicken Tikka Masala in an Indian bread. The platters looked really big (did not order.)

I never thought I'd find a market to rival Pike's Place in Seattle, but this came pretty close. I entered the market from the southeast corner, so I was greeted with the whiff of chocolate chip cookies when I walked in. I wove my way through the aisles and saw such an impressive array of fresh fruits and vegetables, an amazing variety of meats and fish (dare I say, better fish than Pike's Place?!), a huge variety of eateries (sandwiches, crepes, mediterranean, gourmet, vegetarian, Mexican, Chinese, etc.etc.), cheese, flowers.... I could go on and on. Luckily I came on a day when the Pennsylvania Dutch and Amish were here, with loads of fresh dairy products and baked goods. I came first for breakfast, but couldn't really decide, what with so many choices, and ended up with fresh oatmeal from one place, fresh squeezed fruit juice from another place, and coffee from yet another place. I came back in the afternoon wanting a sandwich, but unfortunately both Rick's and DiNic's were so crowded, I just ended up getting a hot apple dumpling from the Dutch Eating Place (http://www.yelp.com/biz/dutch-eating-place-philadelphia). Yum. I also went around and got some gifts for my family, including a bottle of PA wine and a nice big filet of bacalau. If I had had access to some cold storage, I would have loved to get some Amish butter, more baked goods, and more meats. This place is a real treasure; I wish I had a market like this in my city!

This was probably my favorite thing that I did while in Philly for the weekend. I love markets in general, but this was by far one of the best ones I've been to. SO much great food and amazing smells! And authentic Amish eats! I picked up some things to take to the bf's family's house, including homemade fudge, pickled okra (yep, and it was awesome), rice cakes, homemade jams/jellies among them. For ourselves we picked up a bottle of Pennsylvanian wine for dinner, and snacked on giant pickles when we got there, and later some authentic Amish PRETZELS! Seriously, my mouth is watering just thinking of them. 

There seemed to be a whole separate side where you could actually grab food, sit, and eat. We didn't make it there, but next time I'm in town, I'll carve out enough time to sit there...and eat my body weight in Amish pretzels. :)

As far as must-dos go in Philly, this would be at the top of the list.

This is just plain outstanding.  It's a wonderfully lively, bustling large space with stands/restaurants covering all types of food -- American, Middle Eastern, Indian, Chinese, and Korean, seafood, vegetarian, coffee, desserts, etc. -- as well as shops hawking fresh meat, seafood, and vegetables, plus general wares including flowers, jewelry, candles, souvenirs (of course), housewares, and on and on.  There are loads of sights, sounds, smells, and (especially) tastes to take in.  The prices vary widely from shop to shop, but they are generally very good.  If you don't like crowds though, time your visit carefully...if there is such a time when the market is actually calm.
The Reading Terminal is my food mecca. Fresh and local produce, poultry and meats, not to mention all of the vendors selling delicious sandwiches and snacks. And local honey?!?!?! Yes, please.

This is a tourist destination that everyone visiting Philadelphia should go to. 

This is an affordable and diverse market that everyone living in Philadelphia should at least visit once.

This is one of the best collections of small casual restaurants I have ever seen. I sometimes feel sad when I visit that I can only eat one lunch per day.

This is as it appears on TV. Everything is true.
Amazing chicken biryani, huge portion, great price. Definitely best street Indian food in center city.
Yummmm, everything u can think of here besides what u find in whole foods is great. Love the atmosphere and enormous selection. Will come back for new things every time :} love it :}

This is a great place for visitors to Philly and locals, too. It's a unique, very large indoor market. Plenty of food options, both to dine in and to take out. All kinds of meats, cheeses, desserts, pastries, coffee, tea. Amish food stands. It's an experience, but be ready for long lines and a lot of people. This is a popular spot. Note that there's a parking garage to the west of the market.

If I was a local, I would know what time to come here on what day. Instead, I was visiting Philly on a Saturday.... soooo crowded. I didn't eat anything... which is shameful. Instead we just grabbed a beer at the bar. I will figure this place out in the future, and I am sure it will be awesome.

I love that reading terminal is in Philadelphia and that its so close to my office. The head nut, little Thai, metropolitan and Salumeria, are my go to spots. I also like the sandwich offerings at by George. People watching and the random piano player are definite reasons to make the terminal a regular lunchtime haunt. Stay away during conventions-the place gets mobbed (also during the flower and auto show weeks).
Great place with so many little hidden gems! There is a huge selections of different foods to try and everything is pretty reasonably priced.

I couldn't buy anything perishable because I was travelling, but if I lived in Philly I wouldn't go grocery shopping anywhere else!...Assuming I had a more generous budget for the high-quality, market-fresh food they were selling. Those lamb chops and sausages are so enticing, and the produce was a great selection. There were so many food stalls I couldn't remember them all even after two trips around. I know it's become increasingly touristy over the years, but there's a reason some secrets aren't well-kept!

I love Reading Terminal Market. There are so many options to choose from. DiNics (roast pork) and Herschels (pastrami) are where I go to for good sandwiches. Iovine Brothers have great fruits and vegetables. I tried the duck lo-mein at Sang Kee Peking Duck and it was delicious. You can't go wrong with anything in the Terminal.
From the most delicious tender steamed dumplings to the roast pork and roast beef sandwiches the Reading Terminal Market has it all!!

Slightly overpriced ($10) and very S L O W. 

There was no one waiting in front of me for their food, and two other people in the process of placing their orders on a touch screen. This creates the illusion of efficiency, but then be prepared wait for 15-20 minutes as one of the 10 people behind the counter cooks your food. Wtf is everyone doing back there? 

The one in center city is about 2x as fast. Please work with this location to understand how to produce the same exact stir fry in a reasonable amount of time.

Quality is high (8.5/10), but only worth it if you have 20-30 minutes to get take out food.
Awesome draught list. Great for groups. Cool neighborhood bar. Specials keep the menu updated.  Atmosphere casual and cozy.

The Historical Reading Terminal is the Epic Center for the ultimate dinning or food shopping experience.

There's a restaurant to suit every taste bud!!!

This Market has everything you need. There's Tasty pastries and mouth watering sandwiches. Candy, chocolates and fresh flowers for all occasions. 

There is a large selection of: meats, poultry, turkey, cold cuts and large varieties of cheeses. 

Everything is fresh and good. You have a nice selection of produce, nuts and gourmet coffee. 

A great place to have breakfast!!!!The Terminal is the blue print! A staple in Philadelphia's history!! Enjoy!

best place to go shopping in the city! Fresh fish at Wan's, produce at Iovine's and meat and poultry at the Haltemans. I go there twice a week for years now. Also the experiance is fantastic, walking around, seeing everything in their glass cases; getting to choose exactly what you want. I highly recommend it!
I would consider moving to Philadelphia just so I could come to the market often. Especially if Beiler's Donuts was open (that is, on every day except Sunday and Monday).

Reading Terminal Market is a foodie adventure and a must visit for out of towners. Its crowded and chaotic here, but with so many delicious items to try and see, browsing can feel like a culinary safari. It gets very tight along the stalls, so do have patience as you go through. There are two large seating areas which are sufficient unless you're here at peak hours. Everything is well ventilated and lit, with ample air conditioning. Plan to spend about 2 hours here if you're from out of town, and try to visit at an off hour.

The food choices are epic. I enjoyed cajun, cheese steaks, italian sandwiches, hand made chocolates, pastries, and I made eyes at the fresh seafood stands and barbecue. There are also several stores to get specialty honey, produce, fresh meat or seafood, and bakeries. The cannolis at Termini Bros were a big favorite. I liked the Becks Cajun and DiNic's Roast Pork sandwich too. 

Bathrooms are well maintained. Parking is nearby in a deck, keep your ticket to get validated so you get a discount.

everything you need - and i mean EVERYTHING - all in one spot!  

just avoid it like the PLAGUE during the week of the Flower Show!
They have it all from chicken wings to exotic fish. Great place to people watch taste test and enjoy the local fare. I stopped into the Cajun restaurant to have breakfast and it was really tasty.
Love the selection of great foods here. Beck's Cajun Cafe, Dutch Eating Place and By George's are my go-to places!

Best place to go if your group can't decide on what type of food to eat. There's everything from Chinese to cheesesteaks to fried chicken. During the weekday, it's best to go after the lunch hour. Because it's downtown, it's ridiculously busy between 11:30 AM and 1:30 AM. 
Great tourist spot to hit if you've never visited the city before.

Imagine Grand Central Market (LA) + Pike's Market (Seattle) 

*I think what drew me the most is the place for all the Amish desserts. Philly is actually very close to an amish community and every single Saturday they have 1/2 off desserts cause they all go back to Amish country on Sunday so they have to hawk all the desserts

**Awesome spot and I wish you could put it like 20 feet from my house so I could get fresh fruit, great amish desserts, and awesome food all day bro. 

JY

I think Reading Terminal is great, as long as you are prepared for what's in store. Long lines and huge crowds! The food I have tried is always worth the wait and I love the mini market in there, fresh vegetables for reasonable prices! Must see for tourists!

I love everything about this place.  The rustic meets industrial decor, the super friendly and sincere waitstaff, and the wonderful cocktails.  I didn't get to try any of the food, but the food menu items looked unique (Indian BBQ chicharrones and General Tsos wings) and the food coming out of the kitchen smelled delicious.  

From the moment I opened the door with the welded butcher knife handle, I knew I'd love this place.  Reclaimed wood paneled walls, industrial light fixtures with filament light bulbs, and a great cocktail list.  The Lucky Loser cocktail was fantastic with everything  you could possibly love- bluecoat gin, pimms cup, muddled mint and cucumber, and ginger beer.  I can't wait to come back here!

Impressive local bar. My sister and I sat at the bar and didn't get much in the way of a bedside manner from the bartender, but we enjoyed the beer list and the names of the mixed drinks, and we split an order of the fondue fries which were delicious and exactly what we needed before heading to our final stop.

You will never find another place as awesome as this.  This is a huge food market.  There are people from all cultures and backgrounds here making food and selling goods.  It doesn't matter what you want to eat you will find it here and it will be amazing.  There were foods and cultures from places all over the world.  Not only the food but there are so many people from different cultures from the area that come here to eat.  It's truly a really awesome place to be.  There is paid street parking and there always seems to be a spot because people are constantly coming and going.  I went to a creole place and had an alligator po boy with creole mustard.  So tasty and sweet you wouldn't even know you were eating alligator unless you were told.  I also had some alligator gumbo which was a bit spicy but it was so awesome there.  I would suggest people go here or even the market in general and eat at all of the little places because each one was more interesting then the next.
I used to love both the stir fries and salads, but after finding a BUG in a piece of chicken in my salad, I will not be going back.
Probably one of my favorite places in Philly! All the desserts there are worth your time and money!

Love this place! So much to see, eat, and do.

My favorites are the juice bar, the tea place, and the place with all of the natural soaps!

Spend the afternoon here, grab some treats, enjoy yourself!
You can find basically anything you want or need here. Candles, honey, snacks, meat, breakfast, lunch, dinner.
It's busy, but totally worth it. They also started validating for parking from what I know.

A great food market both for eating and shopping. For eating, I suggest you walk around once to scope out your choices. Then with food in hand go towards the back to eat for a more comfortable experience.

Burger is good, but I agree with the other reviews most of the other items are too expensive or only so so. Inside is pretty but loud and dark. According to the manager, the outside is a smoking area with no signs and no ashtrays. And definitely not kid friendly. Go to Moonshine or For Pete's Sake if you have anyone under 13 in your party.

Awesome spot! There is so much to choose from. I usually grab a box of the fresh chocolate covered pretzels to take out West with me to gift friends. Although a bit greasy spoon, the breakfast place owned and operated by the Mennonites is my jam! Fun to sit and people watch. Be sure to say hello to your neighbor and meet someone interesting!

My favorite spot in Philadelphia. Wander, munch, people-watch... it doesn't get better than that. I mean, you only have to go two feet to get an A+ cheesesteak from Carmen's and ice cream from Basset's. Also nice is the parking validation.

If I lived anywhere near this place I'd be here all the effin' time.  This is a food lover's paradise!  Any time I visit my folks (who live about 45 minutes away from this market) this is a definite destination for me.  The last time I was here (May 2018), me and The Hubs shared pizza from By George and a pork sandwich from Di Nics.  We also bought Italian sausages from Martin's Quality Meats and pasta salads (again from By George), as well as some amazing-looking asparagus from one of the green grocers to take to my folk's house for dinner the next night.  Oh yea, let's not forget some amazing cannolis from a vendor whose name I didn't record (but I know where you are!).  Oh yes, I will be back...

This is by far the best roll place in America. OMG! We ordered a chicken masala, paneer tikka and aloo paneer roll. All of them were so delicious, I was reminded of my favorite place back home in India. The guys are courteous, place is vibrant and clean. We ordered a chicken tikka and achari paneer to go too. The cashier girl was so happy knowing that we came all the way from NYC, that she gave us a chicken kheema roll complimentary. A must stop for anyone visiting philly. Prices are reasonable too. Give it a shot guys and I bet you will be delighted. I am gonna come back soon.
A great place to shop, dine and people watch!

The Amish stands on their own are worth a trip - unfortunately these stands are only open wed-sat so plan your trip accordingly - specifically to miller's twist for a soft and buttery pretzel - yummy yummy!!

As someone who is befuddled when confronted with seemingly endless choice, lunching in the Terminal is a prospect that seizes me with dread.  At your fingertips you have Japanese, Chinese, Indian, Middle Eastern, Mexican, vegetarian, a huge swathe of delis and of course the Amish (although I heard they might be Menonites) and much much more.  The Terminal is big and mazelike, usually filled to the gills with the geriatric and others with nowhere else to go.  

The stores selling produce pretty much rock and you can get any kind of meat or cheese you want.  On that note, the Terminal is not for squeamish vegetarian or vegan types because its shoppers are subjected to museum-like displays of animal flesh. 

I reccomend 12th Street Cantina, Basic 4 Vegetarian (back from my meatless days) and the Pennsylvania Dutch Eating Place oh and shout out to my store, Blue Mountain Vineyards where you can buy wine from a vineyard in Pennsylvanis (yes, Pennsylvania has vineyard).

I love this place! This is eatery is great for a person who is on the go and don't have time to maintain a balanced diet. All the food is tasty! I literally don't go anywhere else to buy breakfast or lunch and if I know I don't have time for dinner I grab that too!

Wish I had more time to explore this market and try more foods/drinks here. You can tell just by walking through that they have a lot of delicious foods from different parts of the world and that people are enjoying themselves.

Crowded, Expensive but such a wide variety of things to buy. Unfortunately we went on a Sunday when all of the Amish stores were closed. A ton of helpful informed store employees. So many things to see, taste, and do too much for a one day trip I can't wait to go back again. Just not on a Sunday!

If you've never been... this food emporium is as good as it gets.. From the fabulous sandwiches at DeNic's, the apple turnovers at the Dutch Eatery, the baked goods, the ice cream and the other great ethnic foods..you have a hard time going wrong at any stand here..

I love bazaars like this, but this because of some reason seem more chaotic then fun weather you are trying to shop or eat. I have been several times but there have never been a time where there is less of a crowd. I must also say that they have great finds here, but you kindda need to know where to go and how to navigate without getting into the crowd which is difficult.I also want to say that I usually love the crowd, but this crowd I don't know.

Very cool place with an assortment of stores and restaurants. Some of the things you can do... buy groceries or fresh produce, eat fried chicken or Chinese food or blueberry pancakes, buy chocolates and candies, get coffee and cookies. It didn't take too long to walk around the entirety of RT, so if you have some time to spare (15~20 min) check it out and buy some goodies.

If you are in Philly this is a must do! Amazing places to eat and so many choices you could come there everyday for something different! Reminds me of a place I went to in Copenhagen. I wish we had one of these in Orlando!
I love this place so much. I can buy fresh fruit, cofee, backery here. the most important thing is that the quality is good and price is reasonable.

This place is a must when we have friends in town...and we recently moved to Philly and have lots of visitors.  Dinic's for roast pork, prov, and broccoli rabe...forget pat or Gino's cheesesteaks...THIS is the quintessential Philly sammie.  Also love the turkey place for a stick to your ribs carved turkey dinner with all the fixins.

Nice place to go for lunch. Lots of options, all kinds of food. We had the doughnut...to die for! Also the pull pork sandwich very good. Everything look delish. 

Must stop if your visiting.

Many businesses only take cash, so be prepared. A very wide variety of prepared foods, but limited seating. This is a cultural mecca of all sorts of foods and is a great place to browse and experience the sights and smells of a large, indoor market. If you don't like large crowds, you may get grumpy. A Philly highlight.

I really enjoy going to the reading terminal to shop for my regular groceries which i had not considered until recently.  The Iovine produce is perfect, come early to avoid the crowds and if you are driving park in the lots for $4 with a confirmation stamp.  Excellent for all food items and especially cheese and produce.
Just a really incredible experience with food, but very crowded!

Me:  
Damnit, Washington DC, get your shit together.  You don't have a good IMAX, you don't have a namesake food, and you don't have anything as good as Reading Terminal Market. 

DC:   
I have Eastern Market..... isn't that like it?

Me:    
ha ha ha, no.  Eastern Market is terrible and more importantly, it is a flea market. There is no Denic's at Eastern.  I don't remember seeing any whoopie pies, good coffee shops, unspoiled produce, or Amish people rocking their dresses, bonnet thingies and hairy legs while hocking Amish grub. . . . Nice try, DC, get away from me!

DC: *sigh*



Translation: Reading Terminal Market is freakin awesome. Go eat everything. Also, parking sucks, you'll probably have to walk a bunch.

Keepin it real
~M

The food here was great. We ordered 10 dumplings half fried half steamed. They have half a dozen or so flavors to choose from. We got the cheesesteak, buffalo chicken, asian pork, chipotle chicken, and broccoli and cheddar. All of them were delicious. On Wednesday they have $1 dumplings. We will be back for sure.

All I can say is WOW!  The Reading Terminal Market is the best I have ever been to.  This is a foodie's dream come true.  So many choices that it will send an indecisive person into a tailspin.  Trying to determine what to eat for lunch has got to be a difficult decision because everything looks delicious and exciting.  We arrived looking for breakfast and since it was late, we happened upon Smuckers which made a hearty and tasty bacon, egg, and cheese on a roll.  Tons of produce and fresh meat selections that the locals tend to take advantage of.  This is an absolute must for all tourists.  I would recommend using transportation to and from because it can be a bit of a hike.

A mist the throngs of tourists, and limited seating, is a gold mine filled with culinary variety. A delight to witness in person. All of the aromas permeating the air as you walk up one aisle and down the next, is invigorating fellow foodies. A treasure to behold, housed in an old,once active train station dating back tot he mid 1800s. A must see for anyone visiting or residing in or near Philadelphia. They offer discount4ed two hour parking with proof of food purchaser at a lot across the street on 12 th. Just be prepared for varying size crowds and limited seating aviliability.
A little overpriced, but still quality.  Loved by tourists and locals alike.  Great vibes, difficult to find seating.

Not usually a fast food fan but I came with couple of my friends today. The customer service was amazing, especially the manager (Ryan) asking if the customers need anything, etc. I thought it was very sweet of him to go out of his way to help us. Will definitely visit here again.
A lovely place to hang out! A lot of restaurants, great food, great drinks and really great place. We enjoyed this place very much and we recommend everybody to go there!

If you live in the city and plan on cooking it's a great place to pick up some fresh ingredients for your meal.  A lot of the food vendors located there in my opinion have started to go down hill when it comes to quality / quantity vs price.  I remember when the hoagies and steak sandwiches were stuffed with meat and toppings of your choice.. now you get one slice of meat an pay 1.00 for every additional topping you choose.  Some of the favorites are still there.. Hershel's, Denics Pork, and a great homemade doughnut place when you first walk in at the corner of Arch and 9th.  Not a big fan of any of the new comers I think for the prices you get better food and service at some of the local restaurants... and at least you can sit.  This place is for tourists and quick meal if your at the convention with no time to venture off.

Ever since moving to Philadelphia from the San Francisco area, I have been having farmer's market withdrawal because I used to spend my Saturdays meandering around trying interesting foods and buying super fresh produce.  I was afraid that I would never find a place like that in Philly until I checked out Reading Terminal Market.  

Reading is HUGE with a mind boggling variety of produce, meats, and pre-made food stalls.  The produce is super cheap, and I normally walk out of the corner Iovine Brothers Produce with my week's worth of groceries for around $10.  Of course that's not all I look at or spend because there, I could waste away hours looking at the different ethnic food stands, chocolate shops, bakeries, and desserts (I have a huge sweet tooth!).  

One day I hope to try everything, which I'm sure will take me years since I only visit once a week.  But I'm up for the challenge, and I look forward to every Friday when I get to wander around Reading, relax, try new foods, and buy cheap yet fresh produce.

Been to Reading Market a few times in the summer, but I have never seen it more packed than last Saturday (rightfully so, as it was one of the coldest days in the last few years). You can eat to your heart's content and there are grocers and knickknack vendors sprinkled throughout. Like other tourists, we went to DiNic's for a pork sandwich, Beiler's for donuts, Miller's for pretzels, and Sweet as Fudge for chocolate and nuts. More hype than what the line was worth, but a great way to spend a couple of hours on a cold winter day.
Tons of food options and even cheap groceries (OK Grocery, in the center), what more do you want?

Really cool place to find an interesting meal.  There is a large variety of food to choose from.  There are coffee shops, ice cream, and candy stores too.  The best part as a visitor was that this feels like a place where Philadelphians like to go.  It doesn't seem packed with tourists.  Fun place to eat.

How does this place not have 5 stars? Shame on you Yelpers ;)

Everything that you need is here: Termini Brothers for your cannoli weakness, Iovine Brothers for groceries, and the Turkey place (shame on me for forgetting the name) for the BEST turkey sandwich you'll have in your life. 

If you are visiting Philadelphia, go there for lunch, you won't regret it!

This location usually provides great service. Which is probably why I didn't check my order before driving away from the drive through.  My fault - won't do that again as I didn't have everything I ordered.  Food was fine but hard to swallow paying for something I didn't get.
Really good pizza. I bit saucy on occasion (pepperoni). The special pies are always great. Only wish I could customized the whole pie experience, its new but has a lot of promise!

Food: many small shops, mostly chinese take out food (at least 10) or Phili cheese steak, some bakeries, chocolate shops, farmers market, ice cream, oyster bar. Tried the cheese steak at "#3 in the market" since #1 and 2 were closed that day, for a 30min line it was very average, perhaps better than cafeteria phili cheese but nothing too amazing. Tried some baked goods, plain and pretty expensive ($5.50 for a scone). Obama ice cream was pretty good. 

Location: can't miss it, big building lots of entrances. Does have places to sit, but gets pretty packed on weekends. A lot of people ends up eating standing up. 

Service: does not exist. The cheese steak places are too busy to greet you, just yells for you to move forward. Clean after yourself. Place is not dirty but definitely not the most clean, esp the places you can sit.

You can't go wrong at the terminal. Working right across the street is probably one of the best (worst for my waistline) things that have ever happened to me. 

There are so many different places to eat here, which I'm sure each have their own Yelp reviews, but overall, 5 stars. There are a lot of really yummy places. Some of my favorites are the tomato pie slice at ByGeorge, the salmon from the thai place, Hershels, Beilers (OMG THE BEST DONUTS I HAVE EVER EATEN IN MY ENTIRE LIFE), the cannoli at Terminis... The list goes on. I guarantee that you'll find something you'll like.
There is nothing in the world like this place (at least in my limited experience of the world). I'm going to keep this review short & sweet. Just go!

SO MUCH FOOOOOOD!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
It's a bit overwhelming trying to make a choice of what to eat!
I didnt really see anything special about this place.

What a cute Market! We came here while waiting to check into our hotel. For breakfast we ate at The Dutch Eating Place. We tried the blueberry pancakes and the Apple Cinnamon French Toast. So soft and fluffy. I also have to mention the slab of butter they put on it...definitely not the place to go if your on a diet. Lol. Next time I want to try the apple dumplings. 

The market has various restaurants, produce, dessert, and meat stands. Great place to roam around.
Very cool food market with pretty much anything you can imagine.  Lots of people walking around.  Philly Cheese steaks, seafood, chocolates, flowers...

Probably have been to this place more than I would like to admit considering I am not a tourist!
If you live nearby its great for produce from Iovine's
Grab a delicious thick and creamy ice cream from Bassett's
A sinfully delicious baked good from the Amish bakery on the end
or my favorite, a no non-sense gyro from the greek vendor in the center

This is also my go-to place for buying cakes for co-workers etc as they are very reasonable in price and super decadent and rich (I think Paid maybe $15-18 for a giant cake which would have set me back at least $35-40 at my local bakery)

I would say my last visit was not the same as it was 10 years ago, it seems to be predominantly food vendors whereas before there was a mix of food and other storefronts
ie a kitchen place (they have a replacement one now but its not like Foster's!!), spices, a dog toy place 
There was just a lot of options for unique gifts and now I only see a few of the original stores still standing

Anyways if you are not a fan of crowds or enjoy sitting to eat a meal
DO NOT VISIT ON A WEEKEND 
period
its controlled chaos

I love early morning before work and midday when we decide to take a PTO day at work, those are the best times to really enjoy yourself but I'm also not a fan of large crowds

I would also say people compare this a lot to SF Ferry Building or Boston's Fanueil Hall or Chelsea Market
I have lived and visited nearby all and I still have a soft spot for this place as its very affordable and down to earth, but maybe that's why after living all around the country I decided to finally plant firm roots here!

PS--Bring Cash! most places take card but it just makes life easier for some of the smaller shop vendors

Really close to my area, a good enough drive to almost feel like a trip. Easy location. There are tons of places to eat, there are produce stands, pretzels, sweets and treats, delis. You could easily spend quite some time here. Cheap affordable. We really like the gyros and the Cajun place there!

Thanks to DJ M. for reminding me about the great things in Reading Terminal Market. As I described it to someone back home, "it's like Pike Place Market in Seattle, but older, and without the flying fish!"

Locals can get fresh produce, fish, artisan cheeses and more to take home. Lucky them! 

Lucky everyone- we can all enjoy the great food vendors like Tommy DiNic's (roast pork w/provolone and broccoli rabe like a local), Flying Monkey whoopee pies, and on and on!

I also liked the knick knack vendors, and they range from souvenirs to one of a kind artisan items. I bought my nephew a table runner chalkboard from the vendor who has the colorful Mexican bags. She was super helpful, and let me know I can get the chalk "markers" to go with it from any craft store, even though she was selling them too.

There's a nice Information Booth here as well, that has tour information for Philadelphia, and a map of the Market! There are relatively clean bathrooms here, good to remember if you're in the area and gottagorightnow. All in all, I loved this Market!

I'm always a big fan of Reading Terminal. What's not to love? Dozens of food vendors, hundreds of food choices. We always bring people here when they're visiting us from out of town. There's something for everyone...kids, chocolate lovers, vegans, big eaters, picky eaters....you will not go hungry! 

Avoid on a Saturday, if possible. Also avoid during the Flower Show. The crowd becomes so thick it's hard to see the different food options avaiable.

This place is certainly hustling and bustling! Expect lines at peak hours for sure.

There are so many vendors here. You want fresh bread? Someone has it? Meats? Sweets? Check and double check. Produce and fish? As you wish!

Honestly if you are visiting Philly or live there, you owe it to yourself to check out this market.

Love this place. If you are in Center City, Philadelphia and don't know what you are in the mood for, or are looking for something fresh, there is no better place than this. There are so many options! The fresh produce and meats, to the unique little gems you find here; I feel like there is something for everyone. It is usually buzzing with a crowd so finding a place to sit is a trick. I try my best to get my things to go and find somewhere else to sit down to enjoy. If you do nothing else in Philadelphia, you have to see this place to believe such a thing exists! Just remember, the place does close a little early compared to the rest of the city so make sure you get there before 4pm or you could miss a few vendors.
Great Addition to the neighborhood.  The food was great and the Service  was awesome.  Will definitely be back!
One of the best places in the City of Philadelphia. While admittadly it is a little touristy, it is still worth going for all the food, ambiance and meats/cheeses.

I can't believe this was my first visit to RTM.  I LOVE food and this market was heaven to me.  I only wish I could have spent the WHOLE day because there are SO many awesome stalls. Prices were reasonable too.  Poor me doesn't live that close but can't wait to go back.

Came here for the first time with hubby and out of town guest.  It's nothing like the farmers market I miss from california but its busy and has lots of different foods, meats, cheeses, and baked goods to try.  We enjoyed cupcakes from the flying monkey stand.  Also had an apple dumpling from the amish stand which was ok.  We also bought some tasty specialty honey.  I would come back again. It's also nice to see the diversity of people in the market and families enjoying the food.  If you are walking to the market watch out for the drivers.  More dangerous than nyc drivers.

I went thru the drive thru today. i ordered the tendercrisp sandwich. After leaving I opened my sandwich and took a bite. It was soggy bun with a dark meat soggy chicken on the roll with some kind of sauce on it. I rarely eat at KFC because every time I do I am not satisfied. I think I will just stop going

I worked in the market at metropolitan bakery and I actually enjoyed going into work. The Market has an amazing vibe that is undenialable. The sights and smells have pretty much remained the same throughout my life. I was often brought to the market as a child and the thrill is still there. My top picks:
Bread: metropolitan
Cheese: downtown cheese(andrea is the best)
Sweet treat: termini bros
Produce and dairy: fair food stand
Breakfast: dutch eating place

Try the Market along with your normal weekly shopping, always bring out of town visitors to the market, and continue the tradition with future generations!s
This place is wonderful! Just dont be stupid like me and go on a Saturday at 4 during the car show, haha. Great food, great prices on groceries!

Always super crowded, don't get your hope up on finding somewhere to sit. They will be e pensive but all of the food is great. There's even a small produce spot in there and several a meat/seafood vendors.
Olympic Greek Restaurant was great! The Gyro's were fresh and fantastic. Reasonably priced. Would eat there again!!

Wow. Just wow. This place is a seriously overwhelming on the first visit. There's just so much to gawk at or pick at and/or buy, and I didn't plan it well the first time I came in. I've been here twice already, but I still feel like I didn't check out everything this place has to offer: flowers, fruit, cheese, gifts, and restaurants. 

My main goal was to pick up some fresh fruit to take back to my hotel because I haven't been eating as healthy as I'd like to be while I'm here on business. Not only did I get some fruit, but I also picked up a cupcake, a cookie, a jar of organic apple butter, another cookie, and a brownie (I believe I ate it while shopping around). If I were wee bit closer to this place, I'd go here for lunch or breakfast as often as I could...or if it were open later (closes at 6 PM, I think), I'd grab dinner here. It's the perfect place for healthy and non-healthy eaters alike!

There are tons of great options here, by my personal favorite is Beck's Cajun Cafe. Alligator gumbo is spicy and so delicious. The servers are great at upselling -- I just can't resist the jambalaya rice & cornbread.
We loved this experience!!!! Especially Hershel's inside! AMAZING Pastrami Reuben!!!
Really wish I had looked at Yelp before ordering my food. Tuna wrap was average at best and too soggy. The prices are way too high.

SO sad about it.  I live not too far... was hoping for so much more.  It looks awesome.... the beers are great... but the food will leave you wondering why.. and UHG... i don't want to say too much more.  Get the food thing worked out and I will be back.. all the time... and I will take away this review. -Here's Hoping
A fantastic gem in our town. I wish I lived closer, I'd go every day to buy fresh food. Lots of fun for visitors. So many cool things to see and do.

Oh Reading Terminal Market! I love you for what you have to offer. I  hate you for what you do to my diet. You have so many vendors, most of whom serve exquisite food. It is so hard to decide exactly what to eat. I wish I could spend a day sampling the fare. Alas, my stomach is only so large. Though last night I did find a place that was only mediocre, I still love you the same. Don't ever change!

The first time i came here i was overwhelmed in the best way. You can get everything from homemade fudge to alligator sausage here. It can be verrryyyy crowded around lunchtime/the weekends but that's expected. There is such a wide variety of things to eat that you'll want to keep going back. 

You can also do some great grocery shopping here. You can find really good and fairly priced produce, dairy, and meat. Favorites are Dutch eating place, becks, and beilers.

The original and supposedly the oldest market that sells fresh meat and vegetable on one side and on-the-spot cooked ethnic cuisines and delicious sweets the other side. Mario Batali and Todd English, come and see how a real market is run so you can take some back to your fancy copycats in New York!

Delicious food, awesome crew! Absolutely loved it!! Their Kati rolls are out of this world. Portions are well thought of; you can have one Kati roll as a snack or quick bite or multiples as a meal. Looks like this joint is going to get frequent visits from us!

This place is so much fun for food freaks!  So many options available in a huge facility.  I always have fun wandering around here and having too much to eat : )  You can try so many types of cuisines that I can't even list them.  Plus you can buy farm fresh ingredients, preserves and the like from the local Pennsylvania Dutch.  It's like a food Mecca here!
Gitta live this place.  Still has vendors selling raw food and a nice mix of those and prepared food vendors  Dont go there hungry if you are shopping for groceries

I LOVE THIS PLACE!!!!! They have basically anything you want to eat including desserts!!! Plus, there's a fish market, meat market and even a vegan booth....EVERYTHING!!!! Even with the long lines and mobs of ppl....This market is absolutely & simply AMAZING!!!!
All-time favorite foodie place! Go during off hours when it's not as busy, and you HAVE to get Beiler's donuts!

Great place and a beehive of activity. I'd just had lunch which was incredibly unfortunate because from the farmers market to the food court style dining I loved this place. This is one of the largest indoor community markets I've seen and had I not been a visitor to the city would come here often. I can't offer a review for the food but it's an experience. Worth checking out when in the city

Lots of people for good reason: the food is great! We purchased some donuts from Beiler's and some banana pudding from Sweet Nina's. I love that banana pudding. It's run by a husband and wife I think and they are super sweet. I barely shared any of that pudding with my husband it is that good.

LISTEN UP !!!! This new little gem has become my all around go to spot . They absolutely know what they're doing ! The feel of being at your grandmas house is a great touch . Please please please stop through ! I literally tell everyone I meet ! I would love to see this business really pick up and become something amazing ! $7.99 all you can eat !? Count me in ! With that being said , West Wing , can we add mac and cheese to the menu ?! Pretty please ?!

There are very few places I've visited that seem more like a writer's description of a marketplace come to life than here.  For a domestic sort of awe, this counts amongst the most impressive and inspiring indoor markets I've ever visited.

Having had many opportunities to entertain out of towners or simply enjoy a donut in the afternoon, Reading Terminal never disappoints.

Overcrowded market with nothing fancy. Just a tourist trap and living in Philadelphia I say please don't fall for this trap. There are far better markets than this one. It's a waste of time and the food is nothing amazing. Just over hyped and cashing in on the tourists. Produce is also overly priced. I would rather go to other supermarkets. But trust me you won't miss anything besides the crowd in this so called hyped up market
Terrific.  Authentic and fun.  Can get VVEERRRYYY crowded at lunch, filled with jurors fro the nearby courthouse, office workers and tourists.  You WILL find something delicious to eat here.
Of course it gets 5-stars.  Visiting from San Francisco, it is such a great experience to see local vendors offer wonderful food under one fun roof.  You have to have this checked-off on your list.

Iovine Brothers is as cheap as grocery gets!

Best thai food
Baked good you can spend a whole month on
Bassetts!
Famous Dinics Sandwich [i dont like it though]
Italian food at George's
and endless Meat, cheese and fish
Live piano music

Just go. You can take me with you too if you like. This is my Friday rehab after work.
Iconic Philadelphia site that both visitors and locals love and patronize. Eat, shop, socialize.

The beer and cocktail selection is some of the best in South Philly. With a good range of taps and bottles/cans as well as a very well-stocked liquor cabinet, you can find anything you'd want. 

The food is at the same level. With some unique selections alongside some typical bar staples, Industry makes going out in this part of Philly an all in one event. The atmosphere is also beautiful and well worth the visit in itself.

I would say hands down the best place to do a lot of your grocery shopping. Produce is amazing  fresh and less expensive than other grocery stores around. Of course this is it the only reason to go here. So many cute boutiques that have such a variety of things to offer. Always find something new. Love love love it.

Love the Reading Terminal Market...one of Philly's true food treasures. Located in the heart of Center City, this place is as much for tourists as locals. I know when I work across the street, office mates and I end up here for lunch quite often. If you haven't been, it's literally dozens (50 - 75?) of individual vendors all set up in a football field sized marketplace. There is seating integrated throughout, but it is sometimes too busy to grab a seat (M-F, 12 - 2). The vendors ranged from fresh fish and vegetable purveyors, to cheesesteak joints, Amish bakeries...you name it. There's lots of great sandwich places...and even a handful of places that do a great job with Mediterranean, vegetarian, etc. It's such a diverse place in fact, that when I lived close by, I used to visit the Market on Saturday mornings and use it as a fresh farmers market. Certainly worth the trip...and due to it's wide selection, the kind of place you'll want to visit on a semi-regular basis.

So many options! No matter what kind of food you like this place will not disappoint. There is carry with you beer with endless food options. We love a roast pork sandwich, falafel, or fresh cookies. No matter what you eat it's a great experience and even better food!
Market is HUGE and has a great variety of foods. Definitely a must when visiting Philly!
Best Philly Cheesesteak sandwiches in the world are prepared and served right here!
What's not to love about this place. Many vendors, great produce, unique dining choices.

Range of vendors from groceries to prepared foods.
Eating options abound from around the world. Baked goods, International foods..
Amish stands only open Thu.- Sat.  The best bacon is at Halteman's.
Don't go on Saturdays unless you're not afraid of a crowd.
Iovine Bros. produce has student discount days on Sun., and Wed. need ID.
Need to bring cash as some vendors have a credit limit.
Get the best and freshest seafood at Jon Yi's.  Definitely worth the price.

The best place to buy groceries in the city.
Every type of honey imaginable at Bee Natural
Reihl's deli and cheese shop sells huge smoked bones for dogs at a great price
Molly Malloy's has a great beer selection and is a nice place to take a rest.
Ice Cream at Bassett's is amazing!
Need to stop by Miller's Twists for the best pretzels.
Arch St.  Has a parking garage.  Any vendor can validate your ticket to make it $4
Landmark in Philadelphia.

Don't go on a weekend as it's chaotic with foot traffic. You can barely walk a foot without stepping on someone else. The claustrophobic need wait for a weekday. But the wait is worth it. This is a true Philadelphia staple to visit. Hundreds of unique vendors all in one stop. My favorite is the spice shop that offers everything I could want.
Reading Terminal Market is a Philadelphia institution.  Meat, produce, baked goods and every cuisine under the sun is available.

Reading Terminal Market has a huge variety of vendors selling different kinds of food. Some food is good, others are not so great. One of my standards: apple dumplings from Dutch Eating Place. 

Be warned that it can get very crowded. If you buy food to eat, it might take a while to find a free table, especially on weekends.

Wannabe "Halal Guys" or the new King of the foil platter?

Let's be real, everyone wants to be "the Halal Guys." That cart in Manhattan has expanded to multiple franchises around the world and it now seems people want to copy their formula (look at Chicken and Rice Guys in Boston or Ali Baba in New Haven). So, how does Masala Kitchen stack up?

Against Halal Guys, its not really close. But it depends on what you compare. Masala Kitchen's "special" platter was special for all the right and wrong reasons. Imagine a spicier "Halal Guys" chicken on top of a bed of rice and that's essentially what the chef's special at Masala Kitchen was. On top of that, quite literally, the sauce was completely underwhelming. I kept squeezing the bottle into our platter and never found myself satisfied. Their white sauce doesn't pair well with the "chef's special" and it certainly isn't the heavenly combo at Halal Guys. Underneath all that unfulfilled potential is the soggy, overcooked rice. The texture of the rice was just way off and too overcooked. How do you mess up basmati rice? If they fix the rice and spruce up that sauce a little bit their platters will definitely be a worthy competitor, but for now, I can't recommend them.

On the other hand, I can definitely recommend their kati rolls. Both the chicken tikka masala and tikka boti (beef) kati rolls were definitely solid. They make their parathas ("pita rolls") fresh, on-the-spot and it certainly makes the kati roll experience that much more enjoyable. The crisp but chewy texture of the rolls wrapping the excellently seasoned meat is hard to beat. Squirt some fragrant mint-cilantro chutney inside and its easily one of the best Kati rolls I've had. With that said, I won't hesitate to go back for some Kati rolls.

Kati rolls? Do your thing MK. Chicken platters? Try again.

Every time i go to Philly i need to stop by here. There are about 100 different vendors and so many awesome options to try a great variety of foods. 

I still need to try all the spots but i recommend going with a big group of people and trying as many things as you can! Fun time as well

I thought this place was in Reading PA !! I can't use any electronic devices or the authorities can traingulate where I am, so I couldn't get directions. I drove all the way out to Reading, PA and when I got there I asked around, no one helped except this one guy Carlos said "yea follow me aound this corner it's over here", next thing I know I woke up in the bushes in some park with no pants or shoes, wallet gone, and a huge bump on the back of my head. I spent a week in a state hospital, my friends felt bad and afterward took me to the real RTM and guess what, no club to the head! Just great food and people, and...em...um, wait what was I saying, Hmm not sure who I am right now, I'll call you later.

Chaos and fantastic food at every turn. Yes, it is a crazy place, but it has anything and everything you could possible want in the realm of food. Prices are average, but across the board, the quality is excellent. 

It is an experience everyone visiting Philly should have.
The veggie biryani was not just biryani. The veggies were soggy, ratio of rice to veggie was too less, tasted bad -totally disappointed. Dont think I'll ever go back.
Fabulous Puerto Rican buffet! Very friendly owners and delicious food! Try the savory empanadas!!

This place is amazing. A must visit for any tourist. 

My favorite vendors here include divita meats which I utilize for an annual bbq, the Amish stand where I get the best OJ in the world and delicious pies, and finally there's a bunch of sandwich shops like the Jewish deli and cheesecake place. 

I go here as often as circumstances allow such as going to the auto show across the street or business at city hall.

A 2lb Steamed Lobster with drawn butter for $15! 

Hell Yea!

Business meeting at the hotel across the street, came here twice. The seafood counters mostly sell to take home, but ask and ye shall receive. Ordered my lobster and 15 minutes later chowed it down at the dine in table opposite the merchant.

If I ever go back to Philly, I'm heading straight for this place.  Talk about sensory overload - sights, smells, sounds, TASTES.  Good lord.  Go with an appetite and lots of time to spare.  The Amish have the best breads and pastries (Beiler's is my personal favorite, pumpkin bread and gingerbread, gimme gimme gimme).  It can get quite crowded so if you're claustrophobic, be prepared.  The seating area can get pretty disgusting - I know that's because people are pigs and not necessarily the Market's fault, but minus one star for that anyway.

Simply writing a review for Reading Terminal Market does not do it justice. For those unfamiliar, RTM is a large building consisting of many small businesses and stands ranging from groceries to eateries to miscellaneous goods. Only the listing on their website or a visit in person can give an accurate feel of the scope. 

Overall, the place is clean and you're able to find just about anything food-related you might have a craving for. Be prepared for an overload of options and  to spend a good deal of time here- even a simple walkaround can take an hour or two. Most businesses and eateries have their own review pages and websites for those curious. 

Two important things to note: 1) The Pennsylvania Dutch retail section is not open the same hours as the entire market due to their beliefs and scheduling. This section is normally only open Wednesday to Saturday. 10+ of the stands are qualified as PA Dutch, Amish, or Mennonite and as such missing them is a significant chunk of the market.

and 2) Parking is generally done in garages near to the market, though it can get expensive quickly. Even locals are sometimes unaware that if you do end up making a purchase, ask the vendor to validate your parking ticket for a significant reduction on 2 hrs of parking. (Though still not free)
Love this place!!! The market is the place to be for good good food. Its a must go when visiting philadelphia. From fresh cheese to fresh produce and meats. You can find almost anything.
I enjoy coming to Reading Terminal Market.  Always nice people and fresh food.

It is an amazing place to eat, buy fresh food. It is fun, there is a great atmosphere. I like to go here with my family to grab a quick lunch or share a breakfast. 

****

C'est un lieu fantastique où vous pouvez manger et faire vos courses. J'adore y aller avec ma famille pour partager un petit déjeuner ou manger sur le pouce.

Ordered home delivery through Grubpub. Fried fish was okay. The fries were not crisp because they were in the same box as the fried fish. The peach cobbler was a lump of gummy dough in syrup with two slices of peach. Please stop serving dessert or get a cook who knows how to make desserts, or simply buy your desserts elsewhere for your customers.

Pretty much the best spot in Philadelphia! It's the place you can find everything you want and things you didn't know you wanted. So many great spots to eat and even grab a cold beer to go! If you go during lunch time you must like small spaces because it gets extremely crowded!!

No. Don't go here if you want a decent Indian meal that has good flavor. Both times I went, the rice platters were always dry and I find myself drenching it in white sauce to give it taste. I've also gotten the paneer tikka roll which you would assume is oozing in tikka sauce or something but not at all- just dry chunks of paneer wrapped in a chapati roll that I had to drench in white sauce to give it flavor. I don't understand what the hype is- if you want real Indian food go someplace else. Also, poor customer service- cashier just ignored us when we tried to ask a question about drinks so we just grabbed drinks and sat down. Ugh- not planning on coming back..
Great place to grab lunch and do some shopping in Center City.

Cant say enough great things. I drive from Wilmington every weekend for the produce on its own!! Super cheap, place is clean but super busy. Huge savings on parking too in the two garages around it....check website for address, but parking goes from up to $35 to $4 if u spend over $10 at a vendor. They have restaurant for literally every kind of food you can imagine as well. This place would make living in Philly totally worth it!

Oh man! This was the very first place I visited while in Philadelphia and I have to say I really, really, really, really loved it. I mean, this place has everything! Cheesesteaks, check; donuts, check; breakfast, check; fresh meats, check; fresh produce, check, check, check!! 

It reminded me of a mixture of Chelsea Market and Eataly in NYC. I tried a few of the food places there and I wasn't disappointed. This is definitely one of the places I enjoyed the most from my visit to Philadelphia.
So much great food, so little time.  Did Carmen's famous Cheesesteak and Creole's soft shell crab po' boy.  Both great!!!

I always come here thinking that I will find a vendor who has some amazing gluten free bread or cookies or well, anything. I never find it.

The produce selection is great. I wouldn't eat at any of the stands as I am deathly afraid of cross contamination. Too bad.
Great place to grab a fast lunch or to entertain out of town guests.  From cheesesteaks and roast pork sandwiches to out-of-this-world donuts and Asian food, the market has it all!

Coming here makes me wish that I had two stomaches to  be able to sample all the different kinds of food being sold here.  For the LA folks, this place is like the Farmers' Market on La Brea times five.  I loved the variety of foods sold here.  From Amish bbq to cheese steak sandwiches, and Ice cream to cheese purveyors.  This place is guaranteed to make everyone's bellies happy.
Get there before the lunch crowd!  Lots of choices, all of them good.  Steak sandwiches, roast pork or vegetarian dishes...all great!  And the dessert...oh my!

Amazing place!
Whether you are looking for cheese, veggies or meat at a good price & high quality ...
Or you are trying to have a nice meal after a day in Philly center-city ...
Or just in for a treat of frozen yogurt ...
You are at the right place :)

Reading Terminal Market does have a few hidden gems, but overall it's not a huge stand out to me. I LOVE Hope's Cookies and the Amish Market (their BBQ is AWESOME). I haven't really been wow-ed by the other vendors in RTM. The produce is hit or miss. Flying Monkey has NEVER had red velvet cupcakes when I stopped by. You'd think for such a popular flavor, they would make a larger quantity per day. The other food vendors are okay, but nothing worth going out of your way for. Avoid RTM at lunch time since that's when it's plagued with tourists and convention goers. So in short, when you hit up RTM, stream line for Amish BBQ followed by Hope's Cookies and you won't be disappointed.
Delicious food.... Definitely gonna visit again next Friday night.... I recommend Chicken Kati roll and chicken biryani....

Love the fact that EVERYTHING and ANYTHIG you want is there.
Plenty of parking options...easy access with pulic transportation too.
Great VIBE

Don't know why it took me so long to write this review but here it goes.
You can't go wrong with the produce here, the veggies/fruits are reliably fresh, really as far as I'm concerned it's the best place for produce. 

Favorite finds include (and this list is derived from vendors): heirloom tomatoes, curry leaves, turkish delights, chorizo, jalapeno jam, crabcake sandwich, and shawermas to name a few. I love this market, can't get enough of it. It's the first stop I make with out of town visitors and usually the last. Good place to get something for the plane ride.

this place was just a wonderful eclectic moshpit of different foods from delis, soul food, chinese places, seafood, cajun, smoothies, icecream, and bakeries.  apparently its also has a lot of amish markets but unfortunately they weren't open on sundays.  it was fun venturing around and just seeing all the different food stands and the actual produce mingled in this shop.

i loved beck's cajun food stand!!!  i was interested in eating the multiple delis and chinese places and the cajun food looked so good in their displays.  My friends and I split the jambalaya, gumbo, alfredo pasta, and shrimp/crawfish pasta and it was just perfect from flavors to texture.  I'm starving for it now.....ahh i'd love to visit reading again when i trek back to philly sometime in the near future.

Can we talk about food heaven?

It doesn't get better than the RED-ing Terminal. Yes, spelled reading, pronounced reding. This place has just about everything you can imagine. From produce, to bakeries, to seafood. If you want it, the Reading Terminal probably had it. When I visited Philadelphia I tried to eat here as many times as I possibly could. The only downfall is that it gets insanely packed. One time I visited was a Saturday around 3pm and I could hardly move around. I chose the place closest to me to eat because I could not stand being around so many people. Other than that, this place is amazing and I highly recommend it.
Love what they are doing here. Each dumpling with tastier than the last and the service was both quick and friendly.  If I'm ever in the neighborhood again I would absolutely come back!
Lots of good eclectic eateries here.    Really is a must see in a culinary tour of unique Philly spots.

We went to this restaurant after doing the walking tour of the city to enjoy the food. 

The food was not good at all . We order aachari panner , paneer tikka rolls . There was no difference in both of them .

Beilers Donuts and Becks Cajun Café with Alligator Gumbo, oh my I've died and gone to heaven. Tons of great vendors. Parking is a pain for at least its discounted it you buy something, which we always do.

Tourist?  Local? Day Tripper?  Reading Terminal hits the spot! If you're here to see the sites of Philly, you'll be pleasantly surprised by this downtown mix of restaurants, shops and local flavor...including a piano player on weekends.  If you're a local, why shop for veggies anywhere but here?  They are the freshest and so much cheaper!  I KNOW the owners get up at the crack of dawn to get the best produce the ports have to offer.  Yes, the PORTS.  These guys go to the docks to pick out their produce.  And they are the first there.  Day Trippers, where else can you get a warm turkey sandwich smothered in coleslaw on rye that'll last till you arrive back home?

4 words:
pumpkin loaf with creamcheese!!!!!!







(amish booth pronto)
Great little spot-it's fast, has yummy mango lassi and the kati rolls are delicious..highly recommend it and I'm Indian, so that accounts for something!

Suburban people are there on the weekend and it's a mob scene. Keep it for the week days. The Dutch counter is a personal fave for a great breakfast that is quick and cheap. Termini Brothers for a Cannoli. !! ! But I love this philly staple
We had so much fun here! Highly recommend food lovers sign up and take the tour. We learned a lot about the history of the market and got to sample some of the food as well!

I went here to celebrate my birthday. It was an amazing experience, truly. The food, service, and beverages were excellent.

Alison was a great server who accommodated our party of 20 incredibly well. She was jovial, informed, and quite hospitable. She was facile, able to meet the needs of our demanding party (and birthday boy).

The buffalo chicken meatballs was delicious and had almost a pate texture. My favorite drink was the Pale Disguise (Tully, Dewars, lime, honey)--simple and elegant (another recommendation of Alison). Nice domestic crafts too.

My entree was lights out too. Braised pork shank over baked beans and wilted spinach. It was gigantic and succulent to the end. I'd eat it every time! Highly recommended. And it was the envy of the table: a true show stopper.

Some of our party complained about the size of the $9 burger (perhaps a bigger roll would have satiated them).

Other than that, our experience was awesome. I'm endlessly thankful for it too. Great work, from all the servers and staff who hosted our very fun and memorable party.

This place is pretty good and definitely worth coming for happy hour (which ends at 7). Happy hour includes $5 drinks and $1 varies foods. My girl friends and I took advantage of their $1 oysters and got 20 of them. The oysters were served really fast and you could tell they were fresh. 

As for dinner, I shared the 1lb wings with a friend and got the industry burger. The wings were big and well cooked. I loved the favor of them and how tender the meat was. My burger was also pretty good as well. I loved how they had so many sauces you could choose to go with your burger. I picked the spicy mayo one.

The service was really good as well, the waitress came to check on us several times, making sure everything was alright with our food. Drinks and meals were served fast on the moderately busy night I came on. If you were in the area, I would recommend giving this place a shot.

Big indoor market with tons of delicious vendors! I just love the energy and variety, and I've never gotten anything that was less than delicious. I take everyone who visits Philly here and it's always a good time. Highly recommend for an interesting lunch experience!

Love this place. It screams PHILLY! There are so many different kinds of foods here! Parking is always a problem but if u park in the garage across the street and u spend $10.00 at RTM parking will only cast $4.00.  You can spend hours and hours in here.

Reading Terminal Market is a piece of the city's historical fabric.  Thousands of visitors pass through daily to hit up the variety of food stands, buy produce, pick up a cake from Termini Bros., check out the wine selection at Blue Mountain Vinyards, and pick-up some knick-nacks from a variety of sundries stalls. There are many storied names in the market (Iovine Brothers produce, Delilah's, Miller's Twists, Bassett's Ice Cream, the list goes on).  The place is great to visit if you know what you want, but it's so crowded at times and there are so many aisles that visitors from out-of-town will get lost if they do not have a plan.  If you live in Center City, you will come here on at least a monthly basis for food and produce. 

The bottom line: It gets crowded, it's sometimes difficult to remember where things are, but you have to go to Reading Terminal market at least once for the experience. You'll have to keep going back to deeply appreciate and understand it.

Tons of food places! Quite touristy. We got there around 1:30 pm and it was still packed with lookie lookers. Lots more offerings than the Marketing in my home town. Fresh made  donuts, Greek stops, of course the Philly cheesesteaks! The gal at the help desk was very polite.

This place!!!!! I don't even know where to start! The smell, the taste, the people, the concept itself is amazing.  I'm so greedy, I had an amazing grilled cheese sandwich made from cheddar, brisket and mayonnaise, cheesecake, donuts, cheese steak, cookies, cream soda...I didn't eat it all at once, instead i just kept filling my shopping bag and I took it all home! 

It's easy to walk and navigate thru.

This business started in Taiwan in night markets in 2006. Since one of the most popular night market food were fried chicken, I had high expectations because I've been to Taiwan a few years ago and loved it there. This place did not meet expectations unfortunately. 

We ordered the Ninja crispy chicken (XL) ($7.95) to share with a pepper topping and Taiwanese teriyaki sauce on the side. Since we got the chicken in XL, the employee offered to cut it up for us. They also had really thin plastic gloves that you can wear while eating the chicken. That was nice to have since I've only ever seen that in Korean fried chicken places. 

The chicken was good but it wasn't amazing like I had expected. The teriyaki sauce was more like a thinner version of plum sauce. I did see that they had an enlarged crispy squid but I think I might pass on that. I'm glad I went there to try it but I probably will not be going back.
A little bit of everything for everyone.  Word of the wise, don't fill up on one thing so you can visit multiple stores and have a true Philly experience.

I didn't know what I had when I lived in pa, and now I wish there is a reading terminal next to me especially those Amish stands. One of them sells beef jerky, don't miss it if you are there. It's probably the best beef jerky I have ever had, and I have had a lot of them. From Internet to local stores and restaurants, from east coast to west coast, from Asia to America, this is hands down the best. I recently went to one of the local rated best beef jerky in OC CA, and it can't even get close to what the Amish has in RT.

Having grown up in an area where Farmers Markets were an everyday event (2 separate daily markets and one weekly) in my hometown. These days you can find some really good weekly Farmers Markets in many towns and, occasionally you find a daily like the Reading Terminal Market.

We walked in and I was home again. The hustle and bustle of vendors setting up, the aroma of fresh baked Artisan bread, the smell of just brewed hot coffee - mixed with the occasional off-scent of freshly butchered meat or fish - totally transformed my world for a few minutes from hectic "day-to-day-today" to a more bucolic boyhood.

If you want it, Reading Terminal Market most likely has it. From eats to sweets to handmade chocolate treats and handmade crafts. Sit down and enjoy a cup of distinctively fresh coffee while watching the scurrying workers around you. Or grab a breakfast or lunch from one of the many stands set up and waiting for you to sample their fares.

There is simply too much to describe in one brief review, so I strongly encourage you to go and see for yourself. It's a step back in time with some modern adaptations on the market I so fondly remember.

You got a couple of hours to spare! The city is crowded and you are running out of options and being too indecisive. Let me help you, get in Reading Terminal Market now! 

You got tons of options right in front of your eyes from Roast pork sandwiches, to fresh falafel sandwiches, cannoli's that'll make you cry and if you forgot your groceries for the week, the markets got your covered. Slow down and enjoy the sheer beauty of plentiful! There is just plenty of things to see, eat, buy or just walk around. 

You won't regret it. Top destination for us and we'll back again. Worth the hype.  Thank me later!
A great place to eat with a variety of good food. My personal favorites are The Original Turkey for a healthy sandwich, smoothies from Kamal's, and pretzels from Miller's Twist.

Oh Reading Terminal. How you make me wish I was a better foodie and could handle myself better in crowds. 

Reading Terminal is the only place I must take out of town visitors when they're in Philly. No, not the liberty bell. Not the Rocky statue. Not Pats or Genos. This place.

Something about being able to say "I'm going to the market" and coming home with freshly butchered meat, local produce, artisan cheeses, fresh bread, and a bouquet of flowers makes me feel like I'm in a different time and a different country.

Oh and that little kitchen gaget shop? Gets me for at least $15 every time...

Excelent. Cozy, the food it's awsome. I got a Medium rare burger perfectly cook and onion chips, crispy and tasty 
It's a good place to share some drinks with friends or your love and scape from the city.

This place is great when you've got food or book needs and you're stuck between stops at the train station. Just wonderful. There is probably nothing else like it in Philly a beautiful station with plenty to do. Love it.

I have to agree with Steve's review- I'm not one to review chains, but this one gets a nice one because of the service. They are always ready to accommodate the customers and that can go a long way. They already have the best chicken sandwiches, so adding great service is a great way to keep this place in our rotation!

Awesome! My first review.  I passed here yesterday and it smelled good, but I ate next door and all I could do was think about it.  I ate here the next day and it did not disappoint! I had the chicken masala and chicken kheema roll. Both had great flavor...but my favorite was the chicken kheema and the mint lemonade was delish! Would definitely recommend and will come back next time I'm in Philly! They should franchise...it was so good.
Service was good but eggs tasted like plastic mush. Maybe add salt next time. Salad items looked pretty good.

This place is a little piece of heaven, Philly heaven!!!  I got cheese steaks, pumpkin bread, watermelon candy, fruit cocktail, yogurt pretzels, and drinks. And I can easily say this was one of my favorite places in Philadelphia to visit.  There's just so much to see and smell and touch!  It's similar to Seattle's Pike's Place Market but almost grander...almost...I have to say you tie. hehehe

Regardless, of all the places I could have gone, I spent the most time in the Market.  It was awesome!

I got chicken n lamb platter and mango lassi take out. Staff was very nice and clean ambiance was definitely plus. Also location is very convenient. I only had this menu at halal guys in nyc so I can't really judge about food. One thing I noticed was it was less saltier. Not sure if it is good thing but for me it was ok. White sauce was more like mayo to me. But they have sauce counter on the side so you can take as much as you want to. Lassi was delicious but container was tiny.. Seems like everyone likes their rolls so I should try next time. Since it is clean and so close to me I will probably going back there.

Great great great selection and a fun place to spend a little time browsing for trinkets, housewares, hand-made artisan soaps or tablecloths or even dinner ingredients!

I was disappointed to have missed many businesses that are only open Wed - Sun. 
but one would have to KNOW that information to plan a visit. The left most wing of the market was dark. 
I'm sure, when all merchants are there and open, it's even more fun!

Never disappointed in the products, just the rudeness of people.  So many places to shop for fresh veg and fruit, keep your eye out for the lowest prices.  Smoked meats and beef jerky are a must have!  Very fresh fish at John Yi, always super nice staff there!

OMG! This really should be the last place you visit in Philadelphia before you head home. Keep in mind that a quarter of the businesses will be closed on Sunday. We grabbed roast pork, broccoli rabe and provolone sandwiches from DiNic's. They survived the ride, even with the terrible George Washington Bridge traffic, and were immediately devoured by family member's who expressed their foodie satisfaction.
