Multiple items were purchased from Condiment's, who mentioned they ship packages frequently. 
Expect crowds, noise, and all the other wonderful things this glorious Market has to offer.
I like walking through the aisles to see the different stalls. Spending some time at Reading Terminal is a neat way to experience Philadelphia. Groceries are very inexpensive at the market.

OMG!!! That's what I thought when I walked in here. It's a market indoors. There are many vendors here, ranging from crepes to meats to flowers. It's almost overwhelming the amount of choices you have when going here. The only thing I didn't like was the lack of seating. You have to look up the vendors before you go  or you'll be walking aimlessly forever.

Good food and selection of restaurants. I love visiting so many stores here. It is really one stop shopping, and has a store for most of your needs. Parking is pretty much all around the area. I try to circle around the perimeter, until I find an empty spot, because the parking lots can be a bit expensive.

If you leave this place hungry, you have failed!

Favorites (in no particular order)
Olympia Gyro (used to be Olympic, but thanks to the IOC they had to change their name)

Valley Shepherd Creamery & Meltkraft Grilled Cheese - just go to their instagram @meltkraft ; pictures tell truths and their food will not disappoint....unless you dislike cheese or are lactose intolerant.

Smucker's Quality Meats & Grill - Amish people making food with butter....objections?  Bacon, Egg, and Cheese and the eggs are cooked in front of you.

Beck's Cajun Cafe - Fried Mac and Cheese Balls :) and the Trainwreck.  Neither are really that Cajun but they are delicious and they have a great menu.

This is the kind of place that no matter how long you have lived in Philadelphia you still go to, its a consumer staple.  I'll recommend this place to anyone that likes to eat.  But if you find eating to be a chore....not the place for you

Parking Tip - park at 12th and Cuthbert lot....you can get it validated by any of the vendors and it will be a little bit cheaper, NOT free!
Get Blue Mountain wine and mozzorella wrapped in pruischutto.

Fabulous place. I got to work here for a week shooting all the photography for the foods. 

I got some awesome donuts and sticky buns at Beillers. 
Really great nuts from Iovines. 
Ate at Becks nearly every day. 
Wonderful loaves of bread from Metropolitan bakery. 
And there was an Amish stall that make really good pretzels and ice cream that I can't remember the name of.

Reading Terminal is incredible! What more could you ask for? Delicious eateries, Amish produce, meats, and pastries, aromatic coffees..... it's heaven in one building!

A word of advice - if you want to avoid the crowds, don't go on Saturday or Sunday afternoon! 

Can't wait to go back!

An philly institution.  There is every kind of food you could possibly want.  But it is really crowded too especially around lunch.  Nice place to go an visit when in philly but not sure I would go all the time.

I love the Reading Terminal! It's too bad I'm not a local because I would eat there every day if I lived in Philly. How do I even describe this place? It's like an indoor farmer's market-ish place. Everything you could ever want food-wise can be found here. My mother-in-law took me to buy produce and deli meats, but we also ended up stopping by for some awesome sandwiches, Italian food and hoagies. (We were abnormally hungry that day, apparently.)

There are literally so many food options, you'll have a tough time deciding because everything is displayed right in front of you and the smells are absolutely incredible. Before we left, we bought some homemade pastries made by the Amish (which were way better than anything I've ever baked in my life).

Such a cool experience. People milling around everywhere. Vibe is busy and fun. People were playing live music. Excellent place to go for tourists and locals alike.
A must in Philadelphia.  Make sure to take some time and stop in here for lunch.  Many different options.  Enjoy a cheese steak!
Had a cheesesteak that was awesome. Also went to George's where the tortellini was also terrific. Village of food. There is definitely something to find to eat for even the pickiest of eaters.

RTM is a regular stop for us during weekend shopping trips.  Last week, we finally discovered the new cheese shop, Valley Shepherd Creamery, in the newly refurbished back avenue of RTM.  What a spectacular addition to an already spectacular market.  We tried numerous cheeses, including their amazing made-on-the-premises mozzarella.  This is a much more flavorful version of fresh mozz and we both loved it.  We left with two hard cheeses for later that day but then went back - when we got hungry after much shopping - to have one of their toasted cheese sandwiches.  OMG, simply the best!  Go!  Try it!
This is a great spot if you want to visit Philly and get a lil bit of everything. The combination of different food with the lil shops , deli it was a great mixture and cultural melting pot.

As I was walking through the market, I had a permanent grin on my face.

So much of this reminded me of Chinese market stalls back in...China. The way each different stalls were separated. I absolutely loved it for nostalgic reasons as well as what was offered in the market.

Places I remember stopping in: the jerky place, the donut place, one of the places that offered pull pork. My stomach and cholesterol levels begged for mercy for as my 5 senses danced in delight.

My trip to Philly with friends was supposed to stop me at a few other places, but that idea went out the window when one of my friends said lets just stay here for the duration!

Terminal market, I'll be back with some milk pills to eat that ice cream. Soon. Real soon.

My first visit to The Industry was on New Years Day after the Mummer's Parade and it was packed because of the close proximity to 2 Street. The decor is welcoming and industrial - chic and on a cold day spent outside their heat felt so nice. 

Despite the bar being two deep, the bartenders were super friendly and very quick. I had the Yards hand pump and it was a welcome respite from the lager cans every dive on 2 Street was selling. 

By the time S met me after work, he had to wait in a short line to get in, but we ended up grabbing a table to grab some appetizers. Both the buffalo chicken meatballs and the mac and cheese croquettes were divine. I loved their buff sauce and would probably come back just for that. 

Our server was really, really sweet and very good as well and filled up the water I was drinking obnoxiously fast every three minutes without me asking.

This was conveniently located one block from my fabulous hotel. It was nice to be able to walk to it. I was told it's one of the oldest markets and it had everything there. We walked in from the chocolate pretzel section the delightful baked goods looked so appealing, then the sections opened to a variety of areas for fresh produce, seafood, philly cheese steaks, chinese food, juice bar, coffee, cookies, delicatessens, Amish selling fresh poultry, bologna sticks and very good bacon. The highlight was a young man playing jazz on his portable piano it was fantastic! My two favorite stores were Hershel's East Side Deli and a store selling kitchen knick knacks. At Hershel's East Side Deli there was a line of people waiting for sandwiches the beautiful pieces of pastrami,briskets and corned beef. The meats were heavenly! I was tempted to buy a whole pound of briskets but I couldn't destroy my 95% vegetable diet at the moment. As for the knick knacks - I found a floating duck tea infuser haha!! And we bought some flat kabob grill skewers like the ones usually used by the authentic middle eastern restaurants, these with nice handles.

I enjoyed my trip to Philly especially discovering the Reading Terminal Market!

Words can't describe how much I love this place.

From onion chocolates, homemade honey to duck fried rice, the oldest ice cream place in the  and apple dumplings, The Reading Terminal is by far the best touristic place in Philly and best place for foodie travelers.

Throughout my week in Philly, I went back to The Reading Terminal 4 times. Kinda crazy right? I mean... They literally have everything there. I kinda feel embarrassed to say this but I wish I had spent more days to just try everything there...

Prices are decent depending on what you buy but if you eat, you will most likely spend the same amount of money.

Things I try or bought or recommend:

1. Dinics - great pork hoggies
2. Homemade Honey from Delaware: blueberry, orange, raspberry flavors
3. Apple dumplings
4. Bassetts - oldest ice cream place in the world
5. Duck Lo Mein
6. Buy fresh ahi tuna and mozzarella cheese

I'll be back Philly. I promise.

Tons of great eateries.  Can't miss this place when in Philadelphia. The Flying Monkey makes a great butter cake, Termini Bros made a mean buttercream stuffed cupcake, and Wursthaus Schmitz Fried Bologna sammich is worth a  stop.

Have it a 4, for diversity of products available there ranging from chocolates, coffees, sit in food court, Veggie, fruit, meat, etc sold here! I did avoid the crowds by being there for breakfast at 8ish in a Sunday morning as it was a nearby breakfast place. Def worth worth checking out.

I really don't know how to asses this place with stars. There are so many vendors, the conditions vary based on time of day, upcoming holidays, and even what trade shows are going on across the street. 

In general, I really like the market. Giunta's Meats is a favorite of mine. I'm also a big fan of DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef, as well as Hershel's Deli. The market has really gotten better over time, but it's also getting increasingly crowded.

You have to be alert while walking, and stopping in the middle of an aisle to gawk is frowned upon (yes, even by me). Seating can be very difficult, especially during lunch. If you love the hubbub of a bustling market, this is your place. If you want a quick, convenient, calm, easy option, this is not your place. 

Dear tourists: When you come to our market, chose seating that matches the number in your party. That is, do not take up an eight person table, and three extra chairs for your bags just to seat four people. Additionally, if you are going to stop and gawk at one of the vendors, move out of the aisle. This is like stopping in the middle of a highway, because you saw a cute bird on the side of the road. It's disruptive and arrogant.
I love Reading Terminal Market! It is a place for foodies, the market has all sorts of food from ice cream to awesome pub food. Also the place where you can find DiNic's roast pork sandwiches!

Literally there is no way someone can walk out of here upset. Young and old there is something for everyone. An absolute philly classic. My favorites are 4th street cookies, Beilers, Dinic's, and the roasted turkey place (can't miss it). Of course Bassets and Termini's are classics and you can't go wrong with anything Amish. As a local for Fred veggies and meats or as a tourists to visit a philly classic, it's a must do.

This is one of those loves, that will never fade with time.. until I get diabetes and die. 

Reading Terminal, you are superfluous with food galore! The only downside I've ever experienced are the ridiculous crowds of tourists, and the feeling of being overwhelmed because there is SO MUCH FOOD, so many options!

My favorites include the classic Roast Pork with provolone and broccoli rabe at Dinics, and the Salmon lunch special at Little Thai restuarant. 

my suggestion: GO WITH AN EMPTY STOMACH, full wallet (cash only at a lot of spots), and just wander up and down the aisels. Try what you want, walk by what you don't. You will leave extremely happy, full, and probably waddling like a penguin :) 

ALSO they have yellow watermelon in the summer... TRY IT. or don't. leave more for meeeee

Take public transportation or walk here
Parking is terrible..
Crazy busy lots of crowds..
So plan that with little ones when visiting.. strollers are not so good in the crammed crowds..
Tons of food...
Fun atmosphere...

If you've been to Boston Quincy market..this is similar..but 1000 times larger

This is a MUST VISIT for anyone visiting Philadelphia. As a native of Philly I've been here many times and now that I reside out of state I always return and bring friends who have never been. Go early in the am when they open if possible to avoid the massive crowds and lines. Dinic's, Miller's, Termini's and Beilers are a few favorites.

Great sandwiches. I'd recommend them over the 'Sub chains' any day! ..

-They are generous with the cheese; you can actually savor that provolone in every single bite..
-unlike subway sandwiches..they don't load your sandwiches with all sort of sauces that often end up subduing the taste of the rest of the ingredients
-likeable atmosphere
Awesome place where you can find everything you want. Also great to meet up with friends or have a quick lunch!

I love coming here for happy hour because the beer list is varied and the prices are awesome. $3 local draughts, $4 house wine, and $5 cocktails! How can you say no? The bartenders are always really friendly and attentive. 

The food is good, but is a bit pricey for what it is. The burger is pretty badass because it is comprised of tender, juicy brisket and is well-worth it's price tag.

Look around and you feel like the chicest of lumberjacks. Really cool but very modern wood detailing and plenty of spacious seating. There is also outside seating available if you would like to enjoy your meal/drinks immersed in the urban outdoors.

Once a week they have 20% off your check. You can find out what days if you follow them on Instagram or Twitter. They also do brunch on Sat-Sun. until 4PM along with 3pm-5pm happy hour.

Bonus: Their taste in music is awesome.

Love this place! I'm here at least once a week. The paneer is fantastic. Not at the traditional spicy level, but plenty of flavor and value. The folks there are always really nice too. Good quiet spot to have conversation if you choose to dine in.

I remember going to this be-all, end-all of food courts about five years ago, indulging in an oyster po' boy.

I was a po' boy on my porcelain throne for the 36 hours that followed that adventure, but the food was absolutely delicious. I chalk it up to this weak strain of AIDS I have finally trying to catch up with me. Yeah, nice try, HIV! You're going to have to do a whole lot better than a little diarrhea and nausea to keep this Sherman tank from running roughshod!

Since I can't remember the names of many of the places, my broad rules would be to avoid anything "Cajun" there & just get eyeball-deep into the ice cream. It's truly that amazing.

Oh, and believe the hype about DiNic's! You won't want to smack your mama, because you love her and that's cruel, masculinist garbage that we should've left in the Bronze Age. You will want a second sandwich, though, and that's as good a sign as anything.

Best bets: go during the fall or winter on a weekday in order to beat the throngs of tourists, and don't be a jerk. Watch what everyone else is doing, do that, and you'll be just fine. Matter of fact, you'll probably enjoy yourself twice as much as you would if you were Ol' Uncle PushyPants!

And hey! If you see me there and you don't look like some sort of terror, I'll even let you get a lick or two off of my cone. Trust me, you'll love that!

C'mon down and have a great time with us! Very few of us are mean! We have some snobs, but not too many meanies and grumps!
I love this place. If you don't see what you want?  Just look harder. There are soooooo many food selections.  So much to see.  So many people to watch. An epicurean delight and fun too!!!!

I have been coming here FOREVER! I am 53, and my GRANDFATHER brought me here as a child, as did my mother. I am NOW visiting with my husband. We live in Cape May, NJ, but make it a point to come here several times per year. We stock up! I LOVE the cheese place in the back. LOVE Iacovine Brothers produce, fresh juices, dried CRANBERRIES, and snacks!
And, of course there is Herschels BRISKET, and HOT PASTRAMI! But then...there is METROPOLITAN BAKERY...BUY ANYTHING, you won't be sorry! LOVE this place, the re-do was VERY beautifully done, love the events and entertainment, ESPECIALLY at Christmas...SO festive! I DO, however, miss the VERY period bathroom stalls, and the PINK marble...they should have kept that! And the shoeshine guy is fantastic, I always wear my Dr. Martens when I go, for that reason! Parking is extremely convenient, and I appreciate the discounted ticket for shoppers!

I've purchased from Green Leafs twice now while waiting for flights. The first time I bought a smoothie and the second time some nonfat frozen yogurt. Both were great!

The smoothie tasted good but not fantastic. I forgot what kind I got, but they have a super extensive menu and you can even customize a bit (kinds of milk, yogurt as base instead of milk, etc.) Tons of fruity options as well as chocolatey rich options.

The froyo was awesome too. I got a nonfat swirl with chocolate and vanilla, and topped it with peanut butter and Reese's pieces. It was expensive -- almost $5.50 for the cup. But it tasted great and I knew I had to pay a premium for airport food. She put the peanut butter at the bottom of the cup, which I was wary of at first but then fell in love with by the end of my treat.

What is not to love about this place!? They have every type of food imaginable. It is all high quality and there is something there for everyone. This is a must stop for food when in the City of Brotherly Love!

If you're in Philadelphia you just have to come to Reading Terminal Market.  Markets are always great places to wander during a trip, especially when you're looking for a quick breakfast or lunch to get you going through sightseeing, shopping, walking around, etc.  Reading is a very good market.  Comparable to Toronto's St. Lawrence Market, except almost entirely staffed by Amish people.  Look for gigantic baked goods (I saw a slice of angel food cake that was about 1/3 of a cake, I'm not kidding), hot pretzels, and fresh dairy.  

I stopped at Dutch Eating Place for breakfast while making the rounds here and was not disappointed.  The Spice Market was an ambush on the nostrils, but in a pleasant sort of way.  My friend got a pint of fresh organic milk from Lancaster Co. Dairy, and it was nearly a sedative for him.  You can also find plenty of meats, cheese, fish, and produce as you meander the stalls.  Regardless of what you're looking for, or if you're in town visiting, Reading Terminal Market is a worthwhile stop.

This place is a plethora of food.  I love it! So much quality food to try, so you won't be disappointed.  I say come early on the weekends because it gets packed and difficult to walk through (hence, the 4 stars).  Other than that, I think it's a great place to bring family and friends that are hungry and don't want to pay high prices at a sit down restaurant.

I love this place. I was in Philly for a conference across the street at the Convention Center and I literally ate breakfast and lunch here for three days straight. It was so convenient to just cross the street and grab a quick bite to eat. There's also SO MANY options to choose from. You can have Chinese, Italian, Mexican, Cajun, American, and so much more! 

My favorite places were the Dutch Eating Place and Smucker's. Their portion sizes are so big that you almost can't even finish it all! 

I also love all the Amish stands in the Market - their breads and candies are so good that I brought some to bring back to NYC with me. Everything is super affordable too!

Price: As every Farmer's market will be, it has its ups and downs. Some places are pricey; others offer a bag of vegetables for a dollar (making avocados a steal.)

Variety: Well, you can get everything from silly home decor (liberty bell christmas ornaments and chocolate phillies logos?) to Carmen's $$ Cheesesteaks, to amish pretzel dogs, seafood, soup, and lebanon bologna. There are your token candy corners and vegetables galore, and it's a great place for jams and jellies, especially those kinds you're not used to seeing in Philly (mint, mulberry...)

I'm from the country and Reading Terminal is a step into the markets at home, with the smell of cheesebox wood and butter and dill pickles and deli meats. You'll get personal service and an assortment of Appalachian to Jersey coast accents :)

First I want to say or ask why are the Amish missing in action on mondays, thus always saddens my heart, I love their breakfast, when I'm handling my business in town, I always stop by there to get their enormous pancakes, cheese eggs,  grits, and home fries, and freshly squeezed O.J. (it's a killer breakfast) :-) The staff is so nice, most women, pretty and natural, and so sweet, feel like I'm on the set of little house on the praire, and I also love the meat market area, always grab a steak or two to cook later, super fresh ! Hey I will keep this short, stop by there and show them some love ! Peace

This place is a hot mess.  But I love every single thing about it. 

It's loud and hectic but full of just about anything you might be looking for- fresh produce, counter after counter of meats, cheeses, and baked goods.  Oh the baked goods!

We spent well over an hour wandering around and finally settled on a Boneless Rib Sandwich from The Rib Stand (http://www.yelp.com/biz/the-rib-stand-philadelphia#hrid:mN-jilQ6AgwBRYEDz6PO9g) and several snacks from Beiler's Bakery (http://www.yelp.com/biz/beilers-bakery-philadelphia#hrid:2FZHu1jUHxo8Y4oXKGVQfQ).  So good!  Can't wait for another visit. 

Other notes:
- It's set up like a grid which is nice, and there are several exits.
- Some of the food stands have places to sit inside, but there are a handful of large seating areas in the middle of the market.  
- There are also a bunch of tables/chairs outside along 12th Street.
- The bathrooms were surprisingly really clean and stocked.

i have a love/hate relationship with the terminal. yes, they have amazing food selections. produce, meats, seafood, local, organic, etc. all amazing and affordable. but, its the damn congestion of the place that gets to me. the other shoppers have absolutely no regard for other people. i get barreled into at least 3 or 4 times when i'm there. it makes me leave and not continue my shopping because i get so frustrated. i now have a new method where i only go on a wednesday or thursday morning about an hour after they open. less congestion, more great shopping. awesome place, too many people. good luck on a saturday, i hope you get out alive.

Redding terminal market is a great place for lunch, knick-knacks, and real grocery shopping.  For groceries, Iovine's market is a fantastic place to buy produce.  They have great quality and the prices are incredibly cheap.  There are also several butchers and fish shops, and one or two great cheese shops with very knowledgable staff.

If you are sight seeing in Philly this is a must go to!! It is huge and has everything from fresh produce to buy and cook yourself to tons of different places to get cooked meals. My boyfriend and I ate at a small place with Philly cheesesteaks! It was so good!! There is every type of food joint there you can think of though so the whole family or group can enjoy something different. There are plenty of places to pick up dessert as well!

For a farmer's market in an urban location, it can't be beat.  A few boutique shoppes with unusual food related ingredients and gifts are fun to shop.  Overall, the Reading Terminal Market has what seems like over 100 fantastic stands to visit, from butchers shops to flower stands to coffee stands!  It is Philadelphia's most unusual grocery store!
I'm kind of obsessed with this place. The Dutch Eating Place had the most delicious homemade apple dumplings. I'm drooling just thinking about it!

This is a wonderful place to grab quick & tasty Indian food! I loved the Chicken & Lamb platter, the combination of white and hot sauce was awesome and the meat was really well-balanced in spice and flavor. I love how this place caters to a late-night crowd on the weekends, as my roommate thought the kati rolls were incredible and what a killer late-night food that must be, am I right or am I right? Seriously you should check this place out for some savory Indian bites.

Super fun finger food! Not every flavor was a winner but my husband and I enjoyed trying them all. 

Shrimp and grits was the clear winner!

I highly recommend the pork shank at this place

In addition big points for having nugget nectar on tap
I love the food stands, I love the fresh cheeses and meats, I love the Amish pretzels.  I adore Termini's everything.  Don't go here. It's mine, mine I tell you!
Good quality food, bakery, coffee and other stuff. LOVE this place!

Variety: cheap things, expensive things, all types of food...you can get anything you want
Beiler's Donuts are especially good!

This is one of the coolest place to visit in Philly, there is a ton of awesome food and even wine and beer garden for those of you who want to get your drink one.  

Out of towners, please save a lot of room for eating here, there are too many awesome choices, gyro's, dinic's pork sandwich, delilah's mac and cheese, hershel's east side deli pastrami sandwich, i could write stuff all day about this place, really fun!

I love anything food hall. Seriously. There are so much options at the Reading Terminal, and honestly it can be overwhelming. Absolutely come HUNGRY, and make sure to have space to buy things to take home. The donut place is inside, as well as anything Amish. Next time I have to save space for the Amish diner, it looked amazing. There is plenty of space to sit. Park at the lot across the street and make sure to get validated to save $ on parking.

I love this place!  Definitely a go-to for visitors with it's convenient location next to Jefferson Station.  Even though it is typically crowded, the people and lines keep moving, making it less over-whelming.  I've tried a few places in the markt, including Hunger Burger's sausage, egg and cheese breakfast sandwich (top notch), Weckerly's ice cream sandwiches, Beyer's donuts, and one of the coffee joints.  Meltkraft is next on my list!

I have been going to the Reading Terminal Market since I was three years old! Throughout my life, different vendors have always remembered me as the little girl who was with her father. 
I send everyone new to Philly to the RTM. It really is a special place, and no one ever is disappointed! 

The quality food you can get here, right in the middle of the city is amazing. It smells amazing, it tastes even better. It's a nice place to go for lunch if you're doing some shopping or work in the area.

Excellent place for some excellent authentic Philadelphia anything! Lots of different choice goods food, drinks, and old school vibe. A little hard to get around in because it's easy to get lost. Other than that, great a place to visit! Also, it's very difficult to find from the convention center. There should be more signs.

This is in an indoor market place with many variety. From bakeries, seafood, Italian food, and much much more!! Reading market can be extremely crowded during lunch time. Very popular place for tourist and locals to buy food and other grocery produce.
I'm pretty sure that this place just changed my life. My diet will be easy,  breezy now!

They say Disneyland is the happiest place on earth, They would be wrong. RTM is the happiest place on earth, everything we tried was the best we've ever had. From the pizza to the ice cream to the sandwiches, everything was excellent. I foresee myself visiting there from Indiana a few times a year now that I have tried it.

This place is Amazeballs! I kid you not!

There is no way to go wrong at Reading Terminal. They have som many food options. So many good options. So many really really good, in fact great, in face Amazeballs options.

The biggest drawback on the Reading Terminal is that it closes at 6pm. Dude, this is way too early for such a great place. I mean, how are we supposed to have time to eat dinner there. I have to do a drive by at 5:30pm, and hope places still have good options, to get me some grub for dinner. Booty!

But seriously, if you have not been, you must go here. Do your homework on the spots inside too. Some are the bomb. Some are okay. And, you'll have to make a tough choice.
If you're visiting Philly and you'd like to see/eat/visit someplace awesome and local, come here! It gets crowded at times but it's worth the trip. A Philadelphia institution indeed.

Best best best as it gets. Even if you're only visiting this city for an hour, must visit any of the stands at Reading. Cookies discount at end of day. Favorite roasters at Old City Coffee, my go-to is Sumatra and Six-Bean Espresso. Griggstown Farm Chicken Pot Pie (frozen) at the Fair Food Farmstand is a winner. The Head Nut is a good weekly shopping place for your dried foods/spices.

On a recent trip to Philly, we decided to do lunch here.  This place is HUGE.  So many options, so, chances are it will have what you are craving.  One of the side effects though, is that the place was also packed.  I got just your typical burger, but had to wait in a line atleast 20 minutes long.

Came here for lunch time, because i didnt wanna eat. But i need a place to sit with my friend. We choose to try the fried squid because it looks so good from outside. Like giant fried squid! It was the first visit for us, and the place is okay. Bit small, but its weekdays so its only us there hahha

We ordered the squid for 8 dolars something. But it didnt look like the display at all. Lol. 
However, it taste good! I will again to try their drinks, looks refreshing on a hot day like today.
A tad overwhelming for the visitor to philly. I imagine it can be a fun place if you have your favorites. Extremely busy at lunch as expected. Wish I had recommendations

I was really fascinated with this market place in Philly. My friend took me here and I had a great time! It has everything from grocery stores, meat markets, fruit markets, Indian restaurants, Chinese restaurants, gyros, bbq, herb stores and a Bee Natural store (natural body products store). 

I really liked Herbiary. I picked up a tangerine lime shea butter which smelled divine and the tester sample was very moisturizing. 

I also liked this one grocer (I cannot remember their name) where I picked up this freshly made raspberry lemonade which was very good! I wish I had purchased more bottles. It definitely had the homemade taste with the raspberry seeds that had sunken to the bottom of the bottle. 

I wanted a gyro but didn't know which one to try and I hadn't consulted yelp before heading out. 

I wanted some Chinese but out of the three we saw: 1) the first one- no one was at this restaurant's counter and they seemed sketchy especially with the "No refunds allowed" policy they had posted, 2) the second one- this restaurant was closed, and 3) the third one- didn't seem appetizing from the pictures. We ordered some smoothies from Kamal's and we were sourly disappointed because the smoothies were rather watery and they had an artificial, almost chalky taste. However, Kamal's validates. 

Apparently there is free wifi but I was unable to connect.

Almost a year later, we came back.  During lunch found duck lo mein at one of the chinese restaurants which was tasty. Considered coming here for dinner as well, but even on a friday they close early. Good thing Chinatown is just a couple of blocks away. But definitely still love the variety of options. We love our food halls in NYC, so not hard to love this place.
Great place to goto if you have a group with many tastes. My wife and I went several times she like things I do not get into.

We've eaten here two or three times a month since we moved to the neighborhood in August. The staff is friendly, the menu interesting, and the food is always well prepared. We have taken many friends here and they have all loved it.

If I lived in Philadelphia, I would get fat off of eating too many homemade Pretzels made by the Amish.  Having initially visited on a Saturday and trying this amazing pretzel, I was depressed for at least a good four minutes on Sunday to find their stand was only open Wednesday through Saturdays.

You can find anything from eateries and groceries to homemade dolls here.  At first, walking in feels like you've entered a crazy maze.  Noisy.  Lots of people.  After a while, you find your way.  

Best thing, your money supports local producers.  There certainly is a unique charm about that Reading Terminal Market that is irreplicable anywhere else.  

Loved it!
My wife worked in the city for many years, and we shopped often at this great market and eatery.  Highly recommended!

This is a Philly institution that I make a point of visiting every time I'm in town.

Farm fresh produce, great meat/fish/poultry selection, lots of great goods from the Penn Dutch folks and great food stalls = heaven.  Too bad I can't really buy a lot of groceries to bring back to NYC in the summer but I do try to grab food here and bring back a few Amish pies when I can.  Beiler's bakery makes a damn good shoofly pie!

Folks here are friendly, the food is great and most importantly, I just love the atmosphere of the entire place.  It's always great grabbing an apple dumpling to go and eating it right by the casual piano players who pop by and play a few nice tunes.  It's just a nice, friendly and relaxing place to pass the time and get some shopping (and eating) done.

I hope this place never goes away.  I'd really miss those apple dumplings and killer pies

One of the best places in Philadelphia to eat in my opinion! I don't want to repeat what everyone else has already said, because my view on it is mimicked to a lot of the other reviews, but I will say that there is quite a large variety of different foods ranging from French crêpes, to delicious Bassett's ice cream. The only thing I dislike about the place is the parking. The only place you can seem to find to park are $25 parking garages, but I guess that's just being in a large city. Other than that, I'd recommend this to anyone visiting the city!

3 stars because the sandwiches are pricey and the place not always clean.

Apart from that, Potbelly is my go-to place when I forgot my cash, even though it is a little pricier than, say, Subway. In general, however, their sandwiches are better - the bread and meats seem of better quality and if you like your sandwiches heavily toasted, you'll find them perfect. (In fact, you cannot get them un-toasted.) I have a tendency to always get their Italian sandwich - definitely their best in my book -, although the meatballs and the pizza sandwich are great as well.

I always thought it's quite a miracle how chain restaurants have their distinctive taste - Subway sandwiches always have the Subway taste to it, and Jimmy John's taste like Jimmy John's no matter which one of their many different sandwiches you get. Potbelly is no exception and I often find myself having a craving for it.

Best place to try local Philly cuisine. I live nearby and shop here regularly for my food. You can buy pretty much anything at fair prices. The quality is very good. 

I always bring out of town guests here and they absolutely love it. It's a fun place, the excitement of a town market is something that is lost in American Culture. 

My only qualm is that it is not open later in the evening for dinner.

It is an amazing place where you may find a wide range of cuisine. There are not only common cheese steaks but also French crepes, Vietnamese soups and a lot of sweets and fruits. After a trip, when you don't know what to eat, reading market is worth to visit. If is a magic spot with delicious plates, not so much expensive.

4th Street Bakery was AWESOME!!!  Workers were super friendly and helpful.  Bassett's Ice Cream was crowded but they had a system and kept the line FAST, and they had SORBET, which was wonderful since I can't eat dairy.  Flying Monkey Bakery guy was chill and explained all their products and how best to refrigerate & didn't rush me.

Go for the red curry chicken at the Thai restaurant in the center.

Donna Wolfe

I love this place! It's the hodge podge, classy flea market paid buffet style type of place. There are so many vendors and stalls of different cuisines and other crafts sprinkled in with tables. You can eat a whole meal from one place or try multiple cuisines from multiple venues.. it's really up to you the patron.  Strolling through the isles you will find your own adventure and be met with friendly smiles and hellos.
The market is wonderful! So many great options for eating and drinking. It can get a bit crowded though hence the 4 stars instead of 5.

I don't really go here to eat as I live so close by so I'm not drawn to that stuff.  Overall, the restaurants are overpriced in the inside for the food quality you receive.

What I do recommend is the fresh produce.  I go shopping there all the time for that.  Always great produce that is fresh and not gross looking with pesticide film you see in grocery stores. yuck!

I would not recommend getting the seafood here.  You have to be very careful.

This is not typical fast food. The employees say, "My pleasure," just like they do at the Ritz! Honestly, I have only encountered warm, kind, friendly service here. I trust the food. It's real chicken and not formed meat. Blah! My kids love the indoor playground. It could probably use a good cleaning, but, regardless, this fast food joint could teach some local fine dining businesses a thing or two about customer service.
Delicious, quick, and affordable! We had the Chicken Kheema Roll and Paneer Masala Roll. Both were filling and worth the money. Friendly staff and great service.

I love it! Everything you could possibly want is all in  one place. From the crepes to the meats to the produce not one thing has ever been less than wonderful for me. I highly recommend it for a quick lunch spot, or a place to buy produce or dinner. So impressed.

Anything and everything you could want to eat under one roof, and almost everything is good to excellent. Great coffee and pastries for breakfast, lunches, etc. One of the great places in Philly whether you're a tourist or live here.

Fast.   Decent choice of food.   Good coffee.   Organic ingredients.   Had a naan vegetarian wrap.   Was better than I expected for airport food!   Sandy the cashier was a lovely surprise .   She has a great attitude and serves the customers very well.
How can you not love this place?  They've got DeNic's!!!

Great spot where you can find food for the whole family. The pork at DiNic's is unbeatable. If you are looking for PA specific items and really good desserts, check out the PA General Store. A great place to grab food or for a family day out.

If your a foodie, this is the place for you. They have everything from fresh baked specialty doughnuts to the best sausage shop in town. We stop and had chocolate covered graham crackers and butter crunch cookies from the chocolate shop. Went to the meat shop and had a meat sampler of roast beef, corn beef and pastrami. Nothing that I had was not great. I purchased some garlic white wine sausage and the hard to find andouille sausage. We also had garlic wings which were cooked perfectly with amazing cornbread.

Ah, Reading Terminal.  I love this place and don't go there nearly often enough.  It's got everything.  Whatever food you're craving, they have that, plus Amish people, to boot.

Highlights:  Termini Brothers (best cannolis in the city - and they even have vanilla, hard to find elsewhere, but my favorite!), Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. (yum), the Amish rib stand, the falafel place, the French creperie stand, the seafood people, the fresh produce, the fresh flowers...  Actually, everything here is good.  And this list isn't even the tip of the iceberg as far as their selections.  

The only downside is that it's really crowded at lunch time, so it's hard to walk and find a place to eat b/c the tables are usually taken.  But it's worth fighting the crowds for the food.

Vibrant, energetic space with diverse offerings of great food. Really clean and inviting. Located next to convention hall and bus terminal, it's been either my first or last destination each time I've visited Philly. This weekend I happened to get off the bus at noon on Friday and go in for lunch. It was maddeningly, outrageously crowded (bus loads of students on 8th grade or senior class Spring Break trips?) but still worth it.

This is a must-see in the city, I found that it wasn't just a tourist trap. Even many locals make the market a regular stop. I really liked all the food I tried, but what really pushed it over the top for me was getting to stare at all the real Pennsylvania Dutch people who run many of the stalls. Hey, I'm from California, I've never seen them before!

I really wish I could've brought home some of those whoopie pies, they were AMAZING. That was the stand-out item for me. But due to their delicate nature and chocolate coating, they would not have traveled well. I did buy their pecan brittle, and that was very tasty.

The ice cream at L.D. Bassett was good. Not wow, but good. Our sandwich from DiNic's was really good, but I'm glad we split it in half to make room for everything else. I also liked the chocolate peanut butter cupcake from Flying Monkey, very moist and the frosting wasn't overly sweet.

The only disappointment for me were the chocolate chip cookies from the 4th Street Cookie company. Where's the cookie? It's all chocolate. I prefer my cookies to have a nice balance between the chocolate chips and a buttery, brown-sugary dough. But there was hardly any dough, and the dough that was there had a weird fruity sweetness. Do they sweeten with fruit juice or something? I got a really weird after-taste. I guess people like them when they're warm, because the chocolate is melty. But once they cool down, they're just not worth it.

I live and work close by so I usually eat here once a week. I always order it ahead of time. I love that my typical order is saved online. You don't have to wait in line just go to the front and pay. It seems they do overcook or cook the vegetables on too high so they get over blackened at times. I'm really addicted to the dressing but watch out for the calories.

Two words: over stimulation (but in a good way)

Reading Terminal Market is a farmers market and specialty market with ready to order food places/restaurants, and coffee places. Did I miss something? I probably did, just b/c there's so many things happening in this market. You'll love this place if you like options and can handle crowds. As for me, I give this place a 4 star despite being over stimulated and unsure of what to eat, drink, or buy. I think this is definitely one of those places that you have to visit when you are in Philly. It reminds me of those open markets in Asia... or like Eastern Market in DC, but definitely way more packed with people and food.

I got asked by 3 different homeless people for change before I could Ben make it to the door. It smelled like piss outside. At that point I didn't even go in. Is it wrong to review a place without even going in? Is it wrong to review a McDonald's?

I love going to this place.  Lots of variety in food and a good experience to treat visitors to.  But be aware that many of the stalls are closed on Sunday, so if you want the complete experience, with lots foods beyond the norm - like pickles, Pennsylvania Dutch Treats, etc., get there between Monday through Saturday.

I am a frequent visitor to the terminal as I work right next door to it. The terminal offers a lot of options for foodies. The most busiest spot is usually little thai market( the salmon platter is delicious). If you come early morning between 9 and 10 am the terminal is less busy and you are least likely to be in a line.

Came here on a Sunday afternoon for brunch, and was very pleased with the decor and ambiance of the place. However, the rest of the experience did not match...

First, we ended up waiting for about 20 minutes before we had to hunt someone down to take our order (even though they were just chillin near the kitchen having a blast). One of us ordered coffee, and he also had to hunt someone down to get some coffee after 10 minutes past without a single drip. After about 25 minutes of waiting for our food, we called a server (not our server, because she seemed to have disappeared) to ask about our food. We saw him talk to the chef, and then confusingly look around the kitchen (which is never comforting), and THEN pull out ticket to the chef. The server came over and stated, "He is working on your ticket now." GREAT, thanks. After our food was served, our server disappeared again and we had to hunt down another server to get our check, since she seemed to have forgotten we were there. 

I got the huevos rancheros, which was bland and TINY. i'm a 5'3 110 lb girl and don't eat much, but finished my plate hungry. My friend ordered a corn place, which also TINY. The burger and hangover food options looked pretty hearty, at least. 

Overall, poor service, even when the place is half-filled, and small portions. Supposedly a place where people who work in the "industry" would want to eat, but i've worked in restaurants, and I would not eat here by choice again.

The reading terminal market is so amazing! There are so many food vendors to choose from. From smoked turkey legs to delicious Amish donuts that are made fresh on the spot and they are so amazing. The line can be pretty long but def worth the wait. I'm looking to head there from NY just to get some donuts!

Great place with a bunch of places. The donuts from beilers bakery is to die for. The line can get long, especially on weekends...but totally worth it. So far I've been on Saturday afternoons twice. Definitely less crowded when the weather is colder. Parking is not the greatest, however if you can't find a place to sit down they have some tables near the bathrooms. They don't have chairs back there, but eat your food and get in line for another item! :)

Room Temperature burger, cold fries.  When you're a McDonalds, and known for your fries, you're really doing a disservice to the brand by serving cold french fries.  Napkins!? Nah. Wipe your grease on your pants. Ketchup? Nope. Clientele couldn't be trusted with either a napkin dispenser nor a ketchup dispenser at this location, apparently:  make a trip back into the store to request packets. Bonus star for having Skynard on the radio. No door on the stall.  If you've been in jail before, you'll feel 100% at home in this McDonalds.

Tons of choices!  My turkey hoagie with everything was delicious and reasonable. Hubby went with cheesesteak of course, but it was disappointing and dry. Fries were $3.69 and plain even though it said sea salt. Wanted to try funnel cake as it looked delicious, but was trying to be healthy.

I love Reading terminal.  
There is a farmers Market as well as various cultural foods and vendor.
 Consider it a shopping paradise under one roof.

Parking is discounted with a receipt across the street on 12th street.

I want to live inside this market. There's every kind of food you could want, with a range of prices. It's a bit overwhelming and it took me a few laps to settle on something to eat, but that's what's great about it. Theres a general seating area that had plenty of room on a Friday afternoon so,you can sit and eat meals from vendors without counter service.

Excellent food!! Amazing vegetarian options. We kind of tried one of each in our large group. Everyone was happy with their order!! Spice level can be adjusted. Tastes fresh and authentic!! Highly recommended.
Super crowded on the weekends, but still a wonderful place. Great for locals and tourists alike. Ive been in philly 10 years and shop here for meat, produce, spices, and tea regularly.

I ate lunch here while I was on a business trip and loved it so much I went back the next day. Great variety, good prices, and excellent quality. The first day I went to Spartaro's Cheesesteaks. Now, I'm not from Philly so I don't have a lot to compare it to, but it was phenomenal. The next day I went to Molly Malloy's, which I believe is the only place there with waitstaff service--everything else you order from the counters. I got the bacon, lettuce, avocado and tomato sandwich and it was to die for.

You can find whatever food you want in the freshest quality in huge portions with reasonable prices. lunch, early dinner, breakfast, brunch, dessert, bread, coffee, groceries, meat, etc etc. I LOVE this palce and I think everyone has to visit at least once. Everytime I have a visitor come over, Reading is a MUST TO GO place on my list for them. and I 've never disappointed anyone. GOOOOOO check it out!
SOme of my favorites are: Pastramis sandwich from Hershels, Beiler's bakery's bagels, Old City cafe, Termini Borther's pecan bar, Iovine Brothers Produce, Deliah's fried chicken and cabbage.

Reading Terminal is a Philadelphia experience. If you are visiting want a real pretzel the Amish bakeries inside cannot be beat (and as a visitor you can see some real Amish.. oh lala).

 If you are a local, there is no where better to get fresh produce, meat and fish. And for everyone there is a wide selection of different foods to cater to every pallet. Reading Terminal is fun, delicious and a cultural experience.

Whoa - so much delicious food. Totally overwhelming at first.  Much variety with a favor towards places selling sweet stuff.  Dutch diner type place with amazing apple dumplings with heavy cream for only $3 and a bakery with the most delicious sticky buns for $5.  Saw a place I regret not getting homemade beef jerky from, too.  Wish I lived in Philly so I could capitalize on the seafood and produce stands to cook my own goodness.  Awesome that there are Amish food stands as I feel their goods certainly mean quality, care, and freshness.

Located centrally in downtown Philly it's easy to get to. I've visited on multiple occasions, it's great for large groups because there's something to eat for everyone. My favorite stops are Dinic's for their better than any cheesesteak pork sandwiches, Beiler's Bakery for Pennsylvania dutch specialties, and Smucker's Quality Meats for grabbing hand cut bacon for breakfast the next day(scrapple fans can also get their fix). The market can be an absolute mad house on weekends and during peak dining times, making it cramped and hard to find a table. Lines at Dinic's can reach epic proportions but the sandwiches are worth the wait. Parking in the area is outrageously expensive so take public transport if that's an option. Chinatown is in close proximity for a quick visit as well.

Favorite lunch spot in Philly. Bueller's donuts are AMAZING. Love Hunger Burger. So many different vendors, I never get the same thing twice. Seats at the tables in the middle can be hard to snag. Tend to bring any out of Towner's through here for greasy hangover food.

Love zany, crowded, food marketplaces that capture the heart, soul, and passion of a city? I do. Reading Terminal at lunch time on a Thursday is packed, energetic, and fun.

Oh wow the sandwich places, Italian joints, Jewish bagels, Amish pretzels, fresh seafood, produce, and meats, meats, meats. Tables jammed with folks in food heaven, eating everything from cheesesteaks to pulled pork to Indian veggie options and chocolate dipped cookies.

I got some baked goods from Metropolitan Bakers on the far edge. The market has many Amish stalls with Amish workers including one featuring pop corn, honey, jarred goods--picked up some gifts there. Picked up chocolate gifts from Mueller's. 

I didn't have time for a big messy lunch sandwich then but later enjoyed my pretzel and gruyere ham croissant. Want to go back soon.
Great spot! The food is good and the people pretty cool as well. Our civic association hosted a neighbors night there a few months back. We had a blast! We will definitly be returning again.

Oh my gawd.  My only regret is that we went here when it was about to close and hardly anything was open.  The fish looked amazing, and so did the chocolates.  We got a cheesesteak which was yummeriffic.  Next time I'm in Philly I'll set aside hours just to wander around here.

I finally made it over to The Industry to see just what the fuss was all about.  This Pennsport pub, which garnered waves of praise among critics and foodies alike when it first opened, just didn't hit the mark for me this time around.  While the food was actually pretty good, it was the drinks and the service that left a bad taste in my mouth.

Coming in for brunch, we were promptly seated and told about the cocktail specials: $5 Ghost of Mary, and $5 mimosas.  The Ghost of Mary, which is their take on the classic Bloody Mary, wasn't exactly my forte, but I figured for the special it would be ok (going forward, I will always take my Bloody Marys with tomato juice no matter what).  My burger, however, fared much better.  The meat was perfectly cooked, seasoned well, so juicy, and surprisingly, none of the ingredients (including the fried egg!) fell off the bun.  In fact, I would even go as so far to say that this is probably one of the better if not best burgers I've enjoyed in Philly for a while.

Although our food came out fast and service was generally good, when the check came, the cocktails were shown at the regular price.  When I asked the server about the price difference, he agreed it was weird, then walked over to the service area, and came back to let me know that the discount price only operates during happy hour (between 3-6).  At no point did he acknowledge that when he offered us drink specials on arrival that it was only during a certain price window, not during brunch.  He didn't even offer to adjust the bill or apologize for the confusion (just a simple "yeah, the $5 price is only valid from 3-6, sorry).

So to sum up: good food, weird service.  Not sure I'm going to head back soon.

i love reading! i always take visitors here, and i never leave empty handed. whether its coming here for groceries or fresh juice or bread, or fresh seafood, i always walk out happily satiated with plenty of goodies to enjoy at home :)
Came here for oysters but unfortunately we were there for brunch and they don't do oysters for brunch but everything else was absolutely amazing! Will be coming back very soon! Service was great too!

They have many different food places, where you can eat or snack. Check out the nice bakery that serves different kinds of very delicious bagels right next to the smoothie place, which isn't bad either.
Whenever I've been there usually in the morning during the week, I've also seen "Amish-dressed" people selling their goods.
On the weekends around lunch time, it gets very crowded and you have to expect to wait in line for some minutes until you can make your order.

Tons of delicious options, hours are weird but if you can work it out its worth it. Also the parking garage beside it will give you discounted parking if you show a receipt from the market, just keep it in mind because parking on the street is rough.

I love this place so much! Definitely one of my favorite places to get salad on Temple's campus. The owner is a Temple grad, and most of the food is locally sourced. I always order a create your own salad, I.T is a little expensive. However, I believe the price is worth I.T as the food is local and absolutely delicious! The wait time for food is fast, and is always awesome. I love coming here!

Neverending array of crafts, meats, veggies, cheeses, fruits, restaurants, gifts, and anything else you can imagine.
Highlights for us were By George cheesesteaks, Herbiary herbs, the fish market next to By George, and the cool coffee place around the corner from there.
Wish we had half a day!

There is never a time when Reading Terminal Market isn't crowded. Of course, holidays and weekends are the most chaotic. It's also really hard to find a place to sit.

Even still, I will never let a friend visit me in Philly without checking out Reading. So many awesome and diverse food options. It truly is a smorgasbord of the very best Philadelphia cuisine. My most recent delicious discovery is the Singapore style noodles at Golden Bowl. Spicy, delicious, and plentiful. Also, you shouldn't walk out without 6-12 Beiler's donuts to go. Yum!

This is a fun place to walk around, but it's way too many people when I came here. There are lines for most of the restaurants and no seats. There are so many restaurants that it's so hard to choose one (or two) because all foods look so good.
It's worth a visit if you haven't been here yet.

Holy cow!
My buddy's build-up of the Terminal didn't even come close to doing justice to this place. The massive former train terminal packed full of any kind of foods, deli's, desserts you can imagine. Indian to Amish. Beef jerky to gourmet chocolates. Deli meats, and lunch counters. It was packed during lunchtime but it was worth the experience. 
Very very cool

I had high hopes for this place. I split a beef/chicken/squid combo with a friend. Everything was fried TO DEATH. The breading was thick, brown, tasteless, and crunchy. Parts of it were too hard to be chewed. The meat was so dry it was nearly impossible to tell if it was beef, chicken or squid. Maybe it was just this batch that was overcooked, but sorry, Cheers Cut, I won't be back. If you only do one or two things on your menu you need to do them consistently right.

This place has no words to describe other than "food heaven"! Everywhere you turn every corner and crevais has a grocery store, deli, ice cream shop, Chinese, you name it it's in there. It's like the flea market of all food sources. 

I went for two days- my first day I ate at HERSELS EAST SIDE DELI- and ate a brisket sandwich that was out of this world!!! It literally blew my mind. I sat across from the deli and the person who made my sandwich exchanged a look of agreement after my first bite. The brisket is soft tender juicy, the mayo was light, the toast was toasted and hugged the meat so gently. The spicy mustard was just the perfect amount of tang And i love white American and the fact that I asked what kind of American cheese do ou have my server answered white like "would you really even dare disrespect with ANY other kind of cheese". I could kiss the cook 

The second day since it being my first day in philly ever I had to eat a Philly cheesesteak so went back and ate at SPARATOS CHEESESTEAK DELI I believe it was called. And again. Another great call. 
White American cheese- steak- hoagie (sooo gooddtomatoe lettuce and mushroom peppers )

It's a no brainer.  If you're in Philly, you have to go to Reading Terminal Market.  

We were fortunate to have stayed in a hotel two blocks away, so were went to the market at least one, if not twice, each day.  There are a mix of sit-down and casual restaurants, as well as stands selling local produce, ice cream,  cholocates, pretzels, fresh fish and seafood, honey and preserves, and the list goes on.  

We spent just as much time wandering around looking at the various offerings as we did eating. We tried deli, Greek, hoagies, and more. It was awesome, and a very affordable way to have breakfast or lunch.

A fantastically popular place where there is lots of good food.  I made the mistake of going at a peak tourist time on a Saturday afternoon.

Seats were full, walked around carrying food shoulder to shoulder, ended up leaving due to hunger.

The Boyfriend Review - Had to leave and find a restaurant in the area, or else have a Hangry girlfriend.

Love this place!!! You can anything and everything here ranging from cheesesteaks and seafood to Peking duck and sweet treats. Just be prepared for long lines especially during lunch hours. Ordered a make your own salad from Tootsies which was very good. If you plan on eating here rather than taking it to go you'll find a middle section full of tables, plus some of the stands offer seats and barstools.

The best food market that I have visited in the US hitherto. There are so many stalls. RTM is a must visit while you're visiting Philly. I suggest visiting around noon or later so that all of the vendors have a chance to fully prepare. 

I've purchased from about a dozen of the three dozen or so vendors, and I continue to find awesome new merchants each time I visit!

Unquestionably, RTM is one of America's must stops for food enthusiasts!
Masala Kitchen is so good! MKs Special Platter and the Paneer Platter are my favorites!

I cannot say more than enough. It has every kind of food you can imagine. Park across the street at the parking garage and with a receipt its free. Dinic's won the best sandwich in America on Food Network and well deserved- but you'll wait for that pork sandwich ( and you should). The chocolate place has a chocolate shaped like an ear in homage to Tyson but the truffles are a do not miss. Ice cream in the front is great- love the coconut & pumpkin. Even the cookies in the front are so good ( i only buy 2 or I'd eat a while dozen). We have eaten all kinds of food-- make sure you starve yourself all day and eat your way through....
really great stuff. not cheap. DON'T go at lunch time it's a mad house.

I really have to say I'm a big fan of Reading Terminal. As a quick stop to get one of your favorite foods, or just as a place to meander around, and find something delectable to your taste buds, this place seems to have it all. The best time to go are during the week from 2pm to 6pm to avoid the lunch rush, and then after 4pm on weekends. Parking is only $4 in many of the surrounding parking garages, just remember to get your tickets validated. Street parking is also available. 

I strongly recommend the Original Turkey, Herschel's Deli, or any of the Amish foods.
Great indoor market for seafood, groceries, and meat.  Also have good food stands.....

This is the number one visited tourist spot in Philadelphia. Please do not let the word "tourist" deter you. There is every kind of food you can think of here and some you didn't. A few of my favorite spots:
-Hershel's, (or Uncle Hershel's as me and my siblings like to call it) stop here for the best reuben of your life.
-Beiler's donuts will make you a believer.
-Kamal's has the absolute best falafel I've ever tasted and amazing fresh juices and smoothies.
-a trip to reading terminal is not complete without a stop to Bassett's for some Philadelphia-style ice cream.

I could seriously write about this place all day. Take the train or bus if you don't want to deal with traffic and parking. If you park in the garage directly across the street with the big sign that tells you it's discounted if you get it validated inside, it's not lying. If you have a few people with you and don't mind driving in city traffic, it is definitely a bargain.

Another tip is on Sundays some of the vendors are closed due to religious beliefs, but a lot of the other good spots are opened and it is usually not quite as crowded as a Saturday.

Chick fil a always has great customer service and you'd expect it to drop off being in the heart of the city, but it doesn't. Service and the food are still top notch! Everything taste fresh and the customer service is above and beyond!

My wife and I tried The Industry for the first time last night and really enjoyed our quick visit. I pass by this place at least once a week on my way to band rehearsal and I'm now glad I have place to pop in for a quick bite and beer. Although we only had a few burgers, we enjoyed them very much. My wife substituted the fries for a side salad which was a cucumber salad and was very refreshing. I was intrigued by quite a few items on the menu and look forward to sampling more in the near future such as the Pulled BBQ Duck, Steak Frites, and the Kentucky Fried Guinea Hen. Decent beer selection including local brews and good bottle selection as well. I can never say no to dessert so we ordered up the doughnuts and enjoyed them very much.

We look forward to sampling brunch in the near future and popping in for dinner again soon.
It has the best and freshest meats, eggs and produce. Also features some things from Lancaster, Pa.

This place was my favorite thing about Philadelphia. It had so much GREAT stuff.  As a Clevelander, I'm loyal to the West Side Market, but I have to say I had a glorious fling with the Reading Terminal Market while I was in town.  We saw this place on the food network, and decided we'd hunt it down once we got to Philly.  We were delighted to realize it was right next to our hotel.  The biggest problem?  There were so many great places to choose from that I felt like I missed out on a ton!  You'll deal with crowds when you are there for a convention, but there's lots of seating and lots of choices.  While I had several rushed experiences for breakfasts and lunches during the conference, I came in for a more leisurely walk through on Saturday morning, and enjoyed it so much.  What a great mixture of a fantastic food court and a fantastic market.  Loved it.  Can't wait to head back to Philly just to come back here.  My recommendations would be to try coming during off hours if you hate crowds, there are definitely times of day when it's more quiet, and you have your pick of lineless vendors.

Going here makes me feel like a Philadelphian.  This is certainly one of the best things Philly has to offer.

I am in love with RTM.

Who doesn't love Reading Terminal Market? Its food paradise in the heart of Philadelphia! This is the best place to go to for fresh produce, meats, seafood, dairy items, and baked goods. 

Forget heading over to your local supermarket 'cause you won't find a better deal than here, and these vendors (all LOCAL!) are the best of the best so you know you're getting tasty eats regardless of which particular stand you go to. Its so large that there are always several vendors who offer similar items, so you can do a quick price comparison before buying (which I always do when shopping for seafood), and if one person doesn't have what you're looking for another one is bound to.

This is also a hot lunch spot with a ton of vendors offering anything and everything you can think of: salads, japanese, chinese, middle eastern, crepes, sandwiches of all forms, soups, homestyle cookin', and sweets galore! My favs are the Amish, who have several stalls in one section that you can hit up for baked goods (WHOOPIE! pies are a must), pretzels, candy/confections (mmmm, FUDGE), a pickle or two (or three) straight from the barrel, or a sit down, home cooked meal. If you can't find something here to love, I imagine that you aren't human since you clearly have no reason to eat.

This place is always pretty crowded, but lunch time and the weekends especially are packed. It can get very VERY hard to navigate around lines and tourists who just stop and stare at anything shiny. Plus, unless you've been there as many times as I have, you'll most likely get turned around several times and have no idea what street you're on when you manage to find an exit. But that's just part of the fun of it.

Came here to grab a drink and ended up having a small snack as well. We sat at the bar and ended up staying for quizo. The service was great, the kitchen made a mistake and then took care of it within just a few minutes and apologized multiple times. The small food items we got were delicious and I will definitely be back to try more. Their beer selection is great and they have quite an interesting selection of specialty drinks as well! 

To get 5 stars I need to try the full menu and their drink specials would need to include some more standard non specialty beverages (I'm a plain person). Definitely worth checking out!
Too crowded, overpriced and shady with the homeless.  Prefer Italian Market.
So much fun! You can eat your way through this Market and still get lost with all the options! This is a great place to hang out or bring out-of-town guests.

My all time favorite spot to take people visiting the city for the first time. Great location within walking distance of many great Philadelphia features, and offering so many different (and delicious) food choices, you really can't go wrong. 

I do wish that their seating area was a little larger to accommodate people. It can be very difficult to find a space to sit down, especially if there are more than 2-3 people in your party.

I was wandering around the area after work looking for some places to eat. After 5 minutes of wandering I realized it was Easter and that is why nothing was open. I have never been a fan of kati rolls in general since trying them for the 1st time in NYC years ago, but decided to give it a chance since it was pretty much the only thing open.  

Place- Can easily walk to it if in the city. Pretty spacious. A lot of seating to accommodate for busy lunches and after drinking adventures. I decided to take my food home instead of sit around and eat it.   

Staff/Service- The guy at the cash register was great. Very pleasant and helpful.  

Food: A decent variety on the menu between the kati rolls and the platters! I went for 2 vegetarian rolls. 

1. Paneer Tikka Roll: I LOVE paneer tikka. LOVE might even be an understatement. This roll did not live up to my expectations. The naan itself was waaaay too oily and the paneer was extremely dry. Could have used more masala. I even asked for lemon juice since I love lemon on my paneer. Did nothing for it.

2. Aloo Paneer Roll: This roll was pretty darn great with some lemon juice on it. The naan itself was still very oily, which I was not a fan of. The potatoes added a great kick of spice to the roll. The paneer in this roll wasn't as dry as the plain paneer tikka roll. 

If I was a fan of kati rolls I would prob come back. Unfortunately the massive amounts of oil keeps me away.

A little bit of everything for everyone! I love spending an afternoon here sampling odds and ends at various establishments. It's huge and has a little bit of everything for even picky eaters. It's a great indoor market, but it does tend to get loud.

This place is amazing and living one block away means that I go everyday. From fresh local produce, cheese stands, chocolate shops to a variety of food offers. Only thing is on the weekends around lunch time it can be very crowded!
This place is amazing and a must stop every time we visit Philly.
This market has something for everyone!!  Superb selection and everything I've had from here has been excellent.
Great place to eat or shop because of the wide selection of vendors. A must-do in Philly.

A real gem.  Unlike Faneuil Hall in Boston and Harbor Place in Baltimore, locals actually can shop here for fresh foods to cook at home.  Food is a bit more affordable than those venues- had a great order of dumplings for under $5.  

I'm not into this cuisine, but for those that like Pennsylvania Dutch cooking and baked goods make sure you don't go Sunday as those stands (20% of the stands probably) are closed for the Sabbath.

I wish I could have had a couple hours to walk around this place and soak up everything it had to offer. We got coffee, cookies, and later lunch here. There are options for every cuisine, taste, and diet here. I really would have liked to try some of the Amish fare - maybe next time. It was pretty crazy busy on the weekend, I imagine it is better during the week.

This is hardly a 'market' so much as it is a hundred different corporate establishments with satellite locations in one place. If you're looking for a taste of Philly - Reading Terminal Market is the place to be! If you're looking for a farmer's market type experience, you'll most likely be disappointed.

It's ok. If you can find a Subway...you'll be better off. 
The prices are a bit more expensive than Subway. And not because the sandwiches are bigger. Even so, this location was clean, quick, and friendly.

Good for lunch when you want fresh ingredients on a sub.

This is perfect if you are craving chicken and rice or kati rolls. I tried the chicken tikka one and my date tried the chicken achari. The mango lassi came in a nice packaging and the music was nice too. Very fast delivery especially since we were worried about parking time.
So many great places, from seafood and steaks to desserts, you gotta go! Dinic's roast pork, beef and brisket is not to be missed!

Best Advice to Navigate: Start from one side and work your way down each aisle. Many offer samples. After you've seen everything - pick your favorites. Flying Monkey was a standout with their pie IN cake. The Grilled Cheese place (MeltKraft) was so very very very very good - and unfortunately, the Elvis donut at Beiler's Donuts (banana, bacon!) I didn't get a chance to try because we had to leave for the train and the line was wrapped around the shop! I'll get it next trip. If you see something you want and the line is short, better get it while you can!

A fun and delicious addition to South Philly. The staff were very friendly and explained everything since it was our first time. The prices are great, good selection of drinks, appetizers and entrees. 

The outdoor seating was wonderful. I will definitely come again.

Put Reading Terminal Market on your to-do list if you are visiting Philadelphia! This is a place that offers all kinds of food and good and despite being a tourist-friendly location, the pricing is reasonable and the quality is superb!

While you are looking for hot food eats like Philly Cheesesteak or desserts like ice cream, Reading Terminal Market has it all! The Market also has shops that sell meats, produce, and seafood and it seems like even locals like to shop here. Heck, if I were a local, I would come here often too! My mom, who is a health freak, insisted that we needed fruit for our meals so she brought apples from a local produce stand in the market. Our family was surprised at the cheap price, and was even more surprised at how fresh and delicious the apples were. I haven't had an apple this great for a while!

Don't miss out this awesome marketplace! If a tourist attraction is also a possible local favorite, then you know this is the real deal.

Can't imagine saying anything bad about RTM.  If you want to avoid tourists, the best times to go are on weekday mornings.  My husband and I love coming here for before-work breakfast dates.  Sometimes, we stop at Schmucker's to get gluten-free breakfast sandwiches (Moses and his wife are amazing people).  Then, we get our coffee from Flying Monkey in the next aisle.  You also can't go wrong with Downhome Diner.

I also love RTM for groceries.  Iovine's is great for produce.  I also love Fair Food--they host the Lancaster Farm Fresh CSA, but also have a nice market (Weckerly's ice cream sandwiches = so, so good) and very lovely staff.

Great for a quick meal or for an afternoon of shopping. Even though it's always full and busy, the lines move quickly. So many venders and restaurants, everyone can find something to enjoy. Make sure to get a sandwich at Herschel's and Dinics. A hidden gem is the Brie grilled cheese at the cheese stand.
Lots of selections.  try out the Thai food place and get the salmon dish.  Good price and tastes amazing.  Nothing like grille salmon with coconut sauce.d

Breakfast, lunch and dinner!

I had the good fortune of working across the street from the Market for the few months that I worked on a project in Philly.

This was my go to breakfast and lunch spot.  I rarely ate dinner here because they close at 6pm.

The selection and diversity of food will blow your mind.  While over half of the vendors are Amish, there is just about any type of food you can imagine here.

The prices are cheap but the quality and taste are excellent.  Just thinking about this place makes me happy!

If I lived in this city I would eat here often.  Such a great selection!

I had to get a cheesesteak.  Made just how I like it.  And boy was I happy...for hours.... 

I was there in a snowstorm and most of the stands were closed.  But I could have spent hours looking at each booth.

Love it here - the vibe is boisterous and alive.

The BEST of Philly all in one place! First market of it's kind in the country. Get a Hershel's pastrami Reuben or a roast pork sandwich from DiNics. Italian hoagies from Salumeria are also excellent. The Rib Stand has a great rib sandwich and the turkey at The Original Turkey is to die for. Hatville Deli has an excellent corned beef special. Beiler's donuts are awesome but they have lots of hydrogenated oil/trans fat so don't overdoes on these.
Cottman Chipotle. Smaller portions than any other chipotle I've been to. Sloppy burritos. Meat I is OVERLY spicy. Slow. The food is still good but it just doesn't compare to the chipotle on 16th.
Good summer produce, fresh from Jersey.  Good spice shop too.

Industry is one of my favorite neighborhood places. It's truly a breath of fresh air. The cheese plate is always great, the beer selection is awesome, and Anna,  our regular server, is so friendly, and does a great job making us feel comfortable! Crispy pig ear lettuce wraps, and tartar are some more of my favorites. Love that the kitchen stays open til 1am. Keep doing what you're doing Industry!
A very delightful place with local foods that will please any and everyone palates!! If you're in Philadelphia, this is one of our staples! You must visit!

I spent 2 days in Philly for a seminar and made a visit to Reading Terminal Market both days :-D 

I just love the variety of shops you get in here. From spices, baked goods, raw produce and meats to snacks and hot meals! You can find it all inside this market. So far from all the food I've tried from breakfast to desserts it has all tasted above par or better!  

I know I will go back whenever I visit Philly and perhaps one day I'll have tried all the restaurants hahaha!!!

Great fun place with lots to see, buy and eat.  Just love the atmosphere and always take friends from out-of-town.  Some decent Thai for lunch, Mexican, and good variety of cheeses at various vendors (Downtown Cheese, if they are still around).  Can be a bit overwhelming on a Saturday with little elbow-room to maneuver.  Some pretty good deals on produce if you shop carefully and look for the deals.  Some overpriced stuff, too.  Nice potpourri of many of Philadelphia's small food vendors all under one roof!  If I ever moved away from Philadelphia, this is something I would always remember and definitely miss.

Personally I think RTM is overrated. Yes, you can theoretically buy some of Philly's best food here; if you can actually get it, that is. Most of the vendors here are textbook examples of how not to set up businesses: inefficient food preparation, messy serving, slow check-out, etc. Combine this with the fact that there's so many people that you can't move 5 feet without being jostled by someone. So, so, so many tourists all the time. You couldn't feasibly shop here with any frequency; RTM is a place to go for a one-time novelty and then go get your actual food someplace else.

If you love food (and, to a lesser extent, crowds) you will love RTM.
