It offers nearly every category of food you could want, multiple fresh food grocers, a beer garden, a diner, butchers, seafood stands, snack shops, candy stores, and even authentic Pennsylvania dutch (on weekends) selling cakes, pies, breads, etc. It makes everything extremely accessible, too, by being located within the same building.

It does get very crowded, especially on weekends but, to me, that adds to the charm, making it an excellent place to people watch in Philadelphia (while staying warm and VERY well fed).

For the tourist, it's a MUST SEE. For the Philadelphian, it's the mecca for great, inexpensive, different foods.

Eric B's review and mention of Philly made me HAVE to review this.. esp. since a coworker is about to enter grad school @ UPenn soon... 

Go to this adorable, kickbutt market if ever you're in town to enjoy the sights and history of Philly. Everything that you could possibly think of is here... er, dare I timidly suggest, the Pike Place of the East Coast sans all the fishmongering shows?

One amazing time, trying to thaw by nipping into places intermittently... have gone for a visit to "Brotherly Love" land  in the dead of winter...still, so thoroughly thrilled to have run into the Terminal Market after a visit to the train station (and, of course, to Chinatown!)

Wink; thanks Eric!
They have a great selection of dumplings! All of them taste very yummy. I will definitely come back here!

So many awesome shops, from Amish bakeries,  to spice shops,  youre guaranteed to spend your money here. When you're done your shopping stop by Dinic's roast pork for a roast pork sandwich with long hots. Way better than a cheesesteak!  Always end up spending hours here, so plan your day accordingly!
Best service, better than most of restaurants in Philly. Pleased with the food and by the staff every single time. Very well managed. They really care about the customers.

This market has tons of eats. From seafood to meat. Free wi-fi tons of seating and was visited by famous eats celebrity andrew zimmerman. For 3 days in philly, I ate various food and wish I had time to try everything. This place is always crowded and busy so there is no off-hours where you can stroll unless opening time.

I give this place 5 stars all the way around. I wish I could give them more stars. This was my first visit there and I had a great experience. The two girls working there were extremely friendly and explained the food choices and how everything was organized . I'm on a 1200 calorie a day lifestyle and its nice to know that I don't always have to do a full week of meal planing if in out I can grab something from snap kitchen for some variety. The food was really good too, it is not lacking in the flavor department . Also the means are extremely healthy. All of the nutrition information is on each reusable food container so it's amazing for someone life me who actually likes to know those kinds of things . I will definitely be returning again, and I'll be sure to tell me friends about them.

Reading Terminal Market is a hectic place with a ton fantastic food of all varieties. My go to place for a lunch here is the gourmet grilled cheese from Melt Craft. Any of the grilled cheeses with a cup of the incredible tomato soup and the chips it comes with are the perfect lunch. I highly recommend trying a variety of places and grabbing a cookie or cake for dessert before you go.

This is a nice sized bar in the pennsport area of south philly. I live local, and my wife and I were super excited for this place to open. Rumor of the owners of Good Dog involvement had us super excited. We went on the 2nd nite it was open. We had the Pork appetizer, I had a burger, my wife had a fish sandwich. The wait staff were very prompt, courteous, and fun. I will say we were surprised by the renovations, and liked the décor better then when it was the witch.

The meal, unfortunately was truly underwhelming. The dumplings were ok, but for the price we expected more. The wife's sandwich was pretty good, but had no real seasoning. My burger was ordered to medium, and burned. The fries were ok, but very shoggy. The drinks were nice as they honor happier hour M-F which was a nice surprise. I had the Whiskey Sourpuss which was loaded which got made with a heavy hand, which I enjoyed. We went back to give them a 2nd shot earlier this week, both of use ordering burger. This time my burger was good to order, but not spiced at all. My wife's burger was again overcooked, and remarkably smaller then mine. Shoggy fries again. Drink with a heavy pour again.

Problem is the place was very underwhelming. Maybe we shot with too high hopes. The place is pricey for their food portions and the quality of the food. I would honestly say the burger was no better then burger king, which stinks because we were really psyched about this place and its so close. Its worth taking a trip. Just don't expect anything all that special. They have lots of table space, and we went during busy times, and go sat right away. Bathroom is downstairs and is clean. There is street parking, but its South Philly, luckily this place is on Moy's corner, so there room in front of the school across the street. Nice staff, clean environment, just disappointed by the food. We will give Brunch a chance, but if that underwhelms we likely will not return.

Came in after hours for the eTail East event. Got to sample food from a variety of vendors and walked around when it wasn't busy. A great experience.

Best part was that we got to sample the philly cheese steak so many different ways.

Spectacular. One of the best places to visit in philadelphia. You can get anything you could possibly imagine. Delicious prepared food for a quick lunch, or all the ingredients to cook the most elaborate thanksgiving mean.

This place was exceptional in the true sense of the word.  The concept of the place--a quick-serve joint that serves "warm vegetable bowls"--puts this little fast-food shop in its own category.

You can choose one of their "suggested" bowls or build your own.  As someone who is addicted to novelty and choice, I just had to build my own...even if I didn't know what I was doing.  It was a mess, a thoroughly delicious mess!  First you pick out vegetables like you would at any salad place.  Then--and this is the unique part--they steam them for you for 90 seconds.  Meanwhile, you move to different finishing stations where you add (1) a grain (2) a protein and/or (3)toppings.  The combinations are almost infinite!

All the vegetables look and taste fresh.  The fixin's are similarly flavorful.

As someone who loves originality and making-my-own decisions (I was a willful child), this place was made for me.  I'm also a health-food nut so you have to take that into account--this is the fast-casual restaurant of my dreams.

If I had to include a couple of mild criticisms of this place so that people don't suspect I'm a shill it would be these.  (1)  their cucumber yogurt sauce needs to be garlickier! and (2) too many of the dressings appear to have added sugar, which undermines the healthiness of the establishment.

I've only been here once but even before my meal was done, I was planning what to order on my next visit...
I love this place. Lots of specialized foodie shops, great produce; fun and interesting shops that sell books, textiles, flowers, etc. Go any day except Sunday, when the Amish vendors are in church.

Awesome indoor market place with all sorts of goodies from southern comforts, randomly shaped chocolate dipped stuff, Amish donuts and baked goods, unique deli sandwiches, fresh produce, to local butcher shops. I used to be able to throw down 3,4,5 plates at any buffet, now I'm tapping out after half a sandwich and a cup of coffee  I'm in town for the weekend, we'll get in some other goods before we head back home.

I came here with my bf on a weekend trip to Philadelphia. I love markets and after looking into some things to do in the area I decided that we had to stop by. My review will be a mix of us going initially on a Saturday (when it was crazy busy) then returning the next day where I actually got to experience the food. 

 Y'all.....we must have gone on the worst day possible! Our first time visiting was on a Saturday and there was a volleyball tournament going on at the convention center across the street which meant that 2 billion people were at this market! Ok...maybe not 2 billion but a lot. This made it difficult to walk around to all of the vendors/restaurants. 

*Location- It's a busy area and we parked in the garage right across the street for $4 (2 hour max with $10 validation). 

*Food- SOOO much food!!! I was initially overwhelmed by the amount of food there was around me. (Note: this is not a bad thing.) After settling in we tried fresh blueberry and strawberry lemonade from a stand (sorry can't remember the name). It was amazing! We even brought extra to take home. Next, we ate at Pearl's Oyster bar for brunch on Sunday. I had the chicken and waffles benedict. *Le sigh* I really wanted to like this but I just didn't. The eggs were over cooked, the waffle was bland, and I don't think you can call that chicken breast (they more like crumbs of chicken breast). Next, my boyfriend tried a chocolate chip cookie from a stand across from Pearl's which he loved. We really wanted to try a few other places but some were closed I'm guessing because it was Sunday. Booo....

*Overall Experience- I loved that there are amazing vendors and there was no way for us to try all of the greatness that was around us. On my next visit I plan to try some of the famous foods that were closed. If you're visiting the area you should definitely stop by. It's a busy place but well worth the trip. 

*Tips- Beware that many vendors are closed on Sundays. Also, there are restrooms and free wifi. Come hungry!

We arrived at the last hour and missed out on quite a bit. We knew that going in but it was the only free time we had where we could make it work. The interior of this huge building is filled with stall after stall of every kind of food imaginable... from roast pork sandwiches with rabe to chicken tikka masala to fresh filled cannoli! This places has got it all. 

There is also a fairly large produce mart right inside offering all kinds of fresh produce. If cheese is more your thing, or seafood or even meat, there are numerous stalls offering just what you need! 

Sit and eat or take home and create! I wish I had 3 more hours, an empty stomach and a much larger fridge the next time I visit!
I love going to Reading Terminal! It has a large variety of places to eat and none disappoint.
expensive of course cause of the tourist trap but fresh food and love the cookie place.   take out a loan for a few cookies cause you will pay but its so worth it

The Mecca of deliciousness and diversity. I'm from
Chicago and I wouldn't dare come to philly and not visit this place at least once a day. If not more. Could easily come for a week, eat delicious and different  everyday here and spend under 150/200 dollars for the entire week. EASILY.
Still retains the flavor of the old farmer's market, and now with an added assortment of gourmet foods and lunch places from many cultures.

In Philadelphia to host an exhibit at the Convention Center and had no idea how lucky I was to have access to the market every day for breakfast and lunch. I never had a bad meal. Favorites were the Miller Time pretzels, Beiler's donuts (I will dream about the PB cream donut for the rest of my life) and Carmen's for cheesesteak. You can't go wrong with any of your options though.

This is a favorite place for us to visit as often as we can. You never leave hungry and without bags of something. Neat neat one stop shopping stop whether its yummy cupcakes, cheesesteaks, fresh fruit, candy, or lots of other goodies. 
Just go, it's an adventure.....

Living in Pennsport neighborhood, there aren't a lot of places to go eat. We're lucky enough to have Federal donuts and Grindcore house in close proximity. So, The Industry is a welcome addition to our hood. I've been to this place three times. My first time, I tried the whipped tofu dip which was very good. It's considered a snack on the menu so the portion is quite small. They have a nice draft selection which I've explored each time I've dined here. I can't really comment on the cocktails since I haven't tried them.  Since then, I've tried the lamb neck gravy which was delicious. It comes with bread for dipping, and the waiter was kind enough to give me more bread when I ran out. I've also tried the scallops, and the shrimp BLT which were all very good.

Finally, I came here for brunch on New Years day. It was great. We got a seat right away, though we did come in right when it opened. I'm not sure how busy this place gets during peak brunch time on the weekends. They gave us complimentary sticky buns which was a nice touch. The coffee was great and I loved my dish, which was the duck confit hash. I substituted the toast for their cheddar biscuit to satisfy my hung-over state. It was ridiculously huge. I couldn't even finish it. My whole group enjoyed their brunch as well. I can't wait to come back and try more food. My only gripe is that some of the items are pricey for small portions. I think they are going for more of an upscale theme, which is fine. But I would stay away from certain items if you're really hungry. (i.e. scallops) Or share them with the group, tapa style,which is what we did.
This place is just awesome. So many options under one roof and everything I've had so far has been really good. If I worked in close by, I'm sure this place would be my go to lunch spot every day.
Great. Has groceries and cool restaurants in a market-type setting.... cheap.

Awesome! What a great find in Philly!! It is a bit crowded but well worth it, everything we tried was amazing!!
I loved the Indian food and our son tried his first alligator here. 
Even if you don't have cash they have an ATM. 
I would strongly recommend touring the whole market first so you can then choose your favorites and enjoy!

Good place for good food. As a result, the place is always packed to the gills with tourists and yuppie foodie assholes on weekends, so you gotta either come early, or come on a weekday. If you want to get high quality and (relatively) cheap produce, make sure you drop by Iovine Brothers.

Super crowded, super chaotic, but it adds to the charm of this place. My group and I used the divide and conquer method. We each had one food assignment to purchase, while one of us scouted a table. We loved Denic's roast pork with broccoli rabe and sharp provoline, it's so different from a traditional Philly Cheese! Beiler's donuts are amazing, but very rich and heavy...you have been warned! Termini Brother's cannoli was nice but a little overhyped. Becks' Cajun fried mac n cheese balls were pretty good. We had THE BEST samples of different flavored turkey sausages at Haltman (sp?) Family Country Foods. We came back the next day to buy a bunch to take home but unfortunately, they close on Sundays. The Amish really know how to do meat right! We ended up at Martin's Meats and they also have a vast selection so we bough turkey andoille, turkey chorizo (the best!), turkey hot provolone, red wine and garlic, and more. Downtown cheese had an AMAZING truffle cheese that was around $50/lb. but we couldn't resist and purchased a sliver to take home. We used it on a homemade grilled mushroom pizza with a truffle cream white sauce...!! Many other food stalls we didn't get to try. Good luck finding a seat!

Great place for all types of food whether your looking for a light lunch or dinner.  It also has a great variety of desert foods such as Termini's Bakery.  The size of the aisles are lacking though and usually full of many ignorant tourists.
Overwhelming ! So many different types of food and places to eat. Must see for yourself. There has to be a food for everyone's liking here.
Whether you live in or around the city or you're just visiting, reading terminal is for all and is always great. Numerous markets and countless food options. Almost always packed but worth the wait.

As overly reviewed as it is i have to say that millers is one of my sole reasons for coming here! I am very much a fan of the market and the crowds it draws makes for great people watching ....

Come here on an empty stomach

I love this place.  I won't go into too much detail as I think everyone who lives in Philly needs to come here.  Personally, I like being here in the early morning as it's not as crowded and you get the freshest portions.  But the weekend crowd is cool because you get that bustling market feel.  That is if you don't mind standing shoulder-to-shoulder with people, especially if there's a convention center event that day.

As a newcomer to Philly, it was slightly overwhelming to stop here with a local friend for breakfast. I slightly regretted that we only stopped for a quick breakfast. I wish we had budgeted AT LEAST an hour for me to wander around. Although it was probably better we didn't because I was hungry at the time and probably would have stuffed my face and emptied my wallet. I ended up getting crepes with fresh fruit and nutella (at least the fruit was healthy).  I was surprised at the variety of food available. We just happened to be there during the Philadelphia ComicCon and it is right by the convention center so it may have been more packed than usual. However it didn't take long to get our food and we still found seating at the counter.

Can't get any better when it comes to a great variety of food. Also, great for produce and meat/poultry/seafood shopping - so convenient if you live in Center City and aren't near a grocery store! Only slight problem is how crowded it can get around lunch time, and around times when the Convention Center has a big event.

Can be horribly crowded on weekends and it's a bit pricey if you're doing serious shopping here.  But, it makes for a pretty fun, cheap date activity.  Check out the chocolate covered onion at Chocolate by Mueller, nab some cheese samples, get a toasty cookie from 4th street cookie company.  

Also, this place taught my how to say Reading correctly.  So next time I'm playing monopoly with friends, I can snootishly correct their pronunciation.
best place to go for the atmosphere.  It's Philly in a nutshell.  Plan to eat and browse.  It will be crowded during the holidays, but that is part of the beauty.
The atmosphere and display is a 4-5 however the actual food is on average a 3. The sweets and produce though are 4-5.
An incredible selection of eat in and takeout along with farmers market for produce, meats and bakery items
Possibly the most eclectic collection of really good food in the region. So many vendors under one roof it is mind boggling. Walk the aisles, smell the aromas, choose what you love!

Pretty cool, lots of stalls, a great place to go as a group for food because everyone can get their own thing. From barbecue to Chinese this place has everything. Lots of fresh produce and fish/meat stands. Not much more than food, no real crafty things like some markets. Don't leave without getting a cannoli!

Really sad that they're closed :( 

My boyfriend and I used to get the large fried chicken, and bring it up to the apartment to feast on. They give you gloves so your hands won't get too dirty, and the sauce that comes with the chicken is paired perfectly. The chicken is so juicy too!

Things to get that go really well with the chicken: grapefruit green tea, and ninja nuggets (chicken on chicken)
you can order ahead by calling them, or on wechat. they also have a yelp check in discount!
A good place to go n grab a bite wud like more chicken sandwich varieties though not very pricey either

There are places where you get exactly what you see, and others where the overall experience is better than the sum of its individual parts. Without having actually eaten a meal here, the food/restaurants didn't seem better than a well-selected restaurant outside, but the collective community of restaurants, meat/fish markets, produce markets, bakeries, and miscellaneous stores certainly made me wish I was hungry.

It's a delightful and spacious market that's worth a visit even if you're not looking for something to eat. We ended up with just a single eclair and a bag of apples, more as souvenirs than for actual food value. 

A great change of pace and atmosphere after touring the historical sites of Philly.
My favorite place in the city- really authetic and there's something for everyone!

I absolutely love this place. Always something delicious to try and new people to meet. 

Giving it a 4 mostly because it can be a little pricey.
This place makes me wish that I lived in a Philadelphia so that I can try all the amazing food stands inside.
Excellent venue. The food was great, the place was clean, and the atmosphere was lively. Would definitively visit again.

Oh Reading Terminal Market how I miss you. You can get any kind of food, spice, book and some damn good pancakes from the Amish.
For all of you porkchop eaters out there.........Harry G Ochs Meats is the place to go in the Terminal. They have the BEST stuffed porkchops I have EVER had in my life! The guys at the counter are super friendly, but get there early cause the chops go fast.

AMAZING food quality, taste, variety. Friendly people, lots of energy, people having fun and laughing over great food in a historic location just a stones throw from where the forefathers created our nation. Just the smell and feel of this place makes me dream that when I die I'll get to heaven and there will be a RTM there! One of the best food experiences anyone can ever have, hands down, bar none.

I love Reading Terminal Market! It can be pretty crazy the first time you go, and a little overwhelming! I would recommend the Dutch place that has burgers, pulled pork, etc. The burger is delicious, can't go wrong there! But...the pulled pork is AMAZING! I would highly recommend this! The fries are also really good, you can watch them cut the potatoes and drop them in the fryer...so good!

So I was in philly and in the mood for buffet style... it just so happens that this particular restaurant was in the location that I was close to. So I looked up the rating on Google and 
they had a really good rating so I came here to try and I am totally, totally, totally, totally, totally totally satisfied. Loved itn the people there was awesome. Enjoyed everything

I've heard good things about The Industry, so I was looking forward to brunch there this morning, but I was definitely not impressed. 

My husband ordered the biscuits and gravy and wanted to add two over easy eggs. There is a side of scrambled eggs on the menu and fried eggs and poached eggs are served with other dishes on the menu, so there was no reason to think that this would be an issue. The server took the order, but  came back a few minutes later and said the chef did not have room on the grill to make over easy eggs. We were a bit surprised by this bizarre denial of our request, but we rolled with it and my husband said he would just take a side of the poached eggs instead. The server said that this was not possible either. We pointed out to her that poached eggs are already on the menu with the shrimp and grits. She simply shrugged and told us that the chef will only offer scrambled eggs as a side- no other eggs. We said that we didn't care about the price, but she interrupted us before we could even finish that statement and said that she couldn't do it.

This kind of rigid adherence to the menu might be acceptable if the food was unbelievably amazing, but that was just not the case. My veggie scramble and my friend's meat scramble were pretty good, but nothing spectacular and the berries in my bowl of fruit were all smashed. My husband's biscuits and gravy were just ok...not bad, but not as good as green eggs and our friend's shrimp and grits would be considered inedible south of the Mason Dixon. 

We had high hopes for the industry, but most definitely will not be returning.

I've gone here twice now for the market portion (I've never tried any of the vendor/restaurant-style food places).  Both times, I was just stopping in for some fresh veggies and cheese.  While the selection is decent, the price seemed about comparable to the big chain grocery stores (maybe a little cheaper on certain items).  The downside is the CROWD.  There are times when you literally can't move, it gets so crowded.  I have nothing against tourism (I love to travel!), but fighting a crowd of people who are stopping every 5 feet to take pictures is not the ideal grocery shopping experience for me.
On the plus side, a lot of places here take LevelUp as a form of payment, so if you bike/walk over with nothing but your phone in your back pocket, you're still set for success.

So yes I was here, January 11th, last week and once I did my thing walking around seeing the Liberty Bell Center and all.  I walked through the chinatown area and made it here to the Terminal Market.  I had not been to Philly for a while so it was nice to finally check this place out.  I did like walking around seeing all these nice food options here.  I got here initially early but was not ready to eat too heavy.  It was my mistake, was not sure when DiNic's or the Reading Terminal Market would close in general but I missed my chance to eat the famous Roast Pork sandwich that I saw on Man Vs Food!!!!

I did eat at the Ice cream place, I was told to check that out and it was worth it (so good).
-Philly I will be back, I need to eat that Roast Pork sandwich.  So now I have something to look forward to in a future visit.

P.S. the Bathrooms looked pretty sad here.  I used it of course because I just had to go but this reminded me of some kind of grade school mishap in the bathroom, where some little kid left shit everywhere on the floor included, well every where except in the toilet.  There was plenty of space to walk around the problem areas and just get to the sink to wash your hands or whatever.
Reading Terminal Market is an incredible place, to eat, shop, and hang out. I buy all of my produce there and the student discounts are awesome!

We ate here the last night of our trip to philly. It was really good! We had the cheese board and and lamb kabab. I rarely eat meat these days and this lamb was so worth it!!! Very good! We had the Chocolate mousse for dessert and it was delicious. The bar looked like a lot of fun. We were wishing we could take this place back to Savannah with us!

everything you'd want in a market. Itialian food, ethnic food, misc crafts, amish goods. I was in town visiting from the west coast and the eggplant parmisean sandwich I had was full of deliciousness and nostalgic goodness.

last visit was day before Thanksgiving 2015 heeheehee.  Very crowded, but I love this place.  I'm a meanderer and a lover of food in general, so I enjoy visiting here. Its a potpourri of offerings, good, bad & ugly, depending on your perception, but never boring.  Plan a few hours there , like a day trip, and see what YOU discover.

Convenient location downtown with tons of options. You can buy fresh conventional and organic produce, chocolates, baked goods, meats, fish, olives, soaps, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and other goods. Additionally, there are plenty of ready to order items such as Indian, Italian, and soul. For the vegan, I even saw a few desserts marked as vegan! Prices are decent, some really great. Artisan goods are on the higher end, but I found organic romaine lettuce for 99 cents!

Super delish. I was sad to miss the Amish family that does home baked goods and food. I guess they only show up from 8am until 12pm unless they are sold out, which happens often. At 1pm we missed them. Maybe next time! so many great delish choices and everyone was very helpful and friendly. We tried three or four different stands and left happy!

This place is packed and a little overwhelming BUT they also have interesting specialty items. This feels like a chef's paradise.

Both times I was there I wound up going to the Chinese counter and really liked the dumplings and the duck I got.
Best place for food in Philly, anything and everything.
I love coming here! They have great coffee, fresh produce, amazing pastries and vendors. I never get bored!

I eat here at least a few times per month. I always marvel at how quickly and efficiently they move the line. My go to choices are the chicken salad or wreck on flatbread. They are always tasty! I top it off with to-die-for oatmeal chocolate chip cookies. Staff are always friendly, too. A nice change of pace from my workplace cafeteria.
Great experience and lunch when touring historic Philadelphia. Dinic's Italian Beef was amazing.

Buck a shuck oysters for happy hour are always a winner in my book! They were delicious. There were drinks on happy hour as well.. local beer, some wines and cocktails on discount.  
I got macaroni and cheese croquettes and the kimchi sauce they were served with was amazing. It was all nice and spice and vinegar. Pureed kimchee is GENIUS and I am in love. I also got the baby head lettuces salad (funny name and I like it!). Potatoes on a salad are also genius. Potatoes should be on everything, including salad. I liked the creamy lemon dressing with the shallots, leeks, and mushrooms. I got shrimps on top too, big and grilled perfectly.
The friends got the wings and a cheeseburger. I was told the wings were good, but she wished they were buffalo wings. The burger was good, and I snagged a slew of yum fries.
I will be back! I just wish it was in Fishtown...

I wish I had a market like this close to where I live because I would be here a few times a week to shop and eat.  It was packed on a Saturday but that didn't stop us from checking out all the places.  We tried a few things here and they were all good to excellent.  The only downside was not being able to try everything.

Love the variety here.... there is everything you could ever want. Restaurants and meat/fish markets. Anything you have a taste for Reading Terminal market has it. Its like a maze in there smelling different smells and seeing a lot of diversity. It's kinda big you could get lost.

This is one of my happy places in Philly. As I'm sure it is for lots of locals and tourists alike.

Some of my fave stops: Termini for cannoli, Beiler's for doughnuts and cookies, Kamal's for Middle Eastern food and smoothies, Salumeria for some of the best hoagies in town, Fair Food Farmstand for quality (though pricey) local produce, DiNic's for roast pork sandwiches, and several great butchers and seafood vendors. 

Wish I had a bottomless belly to hit up all these places at once!
Good for people with flavorless pilots...if you are looking for a good blane sandwich this is your.spot!
Solid food options here that address all tastes.  You really can't go wrong -- definitely worth a visit for lunch if you are staying nearby.

This is one of our favorite places in the world to eat and buy fresh food, and has been there for years and years. From the broccoli raab at DeNics to the ice cream at Bassets, there is nothing bad to say about this gem. Go if it's not crowded; go if it's crowded - it's all worth it. The Amish merchants are closed on Sunday (duh) but there is plenty of other choices to make up for that. If you're visiting Philly, and are short in time, skip the broken bell and have yourself an awesome feast at RTM instead - you won't be sorry. If you drive, there is discount parking at the lot across the street - two hours for something like $4 or $5 if you get your ticket validated at one of the shops. If you take the train,  Market East station is next door. The Convention Center is upstairs. Do you get the idea? Go now!
Delicious delicacies. We are from the north but have lived in the south for 5 years and have missed so many foods. This was a place for us to hit all of our food memories. Highly recommended.

Fantastic food and polite and attentive staff. My companion and I had the tartare which was beyond delicious. Just the right amount of lemon and capers. We also has the sweet pea and truffle dumplings which I really enjoyed. I loved the hint of ginger. Delicious. I got the wild boar ragu which was so flavorful and the meat was tender and sweet. My companion got the duck which was a special and she loved it. Tender, the right temperature and the flavors married well. We started off with a Rotation Cabernet which was so enjoyable and ended with an after dinner drink with our coffee/tea. Can't wait to go back. Highly recommend this establishment.

I discovered this place after a recommendation from a friend when looking for a solid quick bite before catching a Philly Orchestra concert at the Kimmel Center.  The service here is polite and quick and the food here was a pleasant surprise.  I was just expecting a run of the mill fast food indian joint, but I got so much more! Their rolls were perfect for on the go eating and the platters were healthy portion and flavorful.  The kicker was also the mango lassi! It hit the spot after a lot of brisk walking to avoid the rain.  I would return again for quick bites before catching a show anywhere on Broad St.

Wow what can I say Everything Under One Roof all you can eat in some places many selections, ice cream to steak, soups Two Nuts always a great place to go to lunch a lot of good visitors and travelers passed through here wonderful atmosphere friendly services.

Besides the crowds its the best place to get a taste of the city.  From cheesesteaks to roast pork to amish desserts.  The hours of most establishments are designed for lunch. 

Definitely check out Bassetts Ice Cream for a cold taste of philly or Terminis for South Philly Italian dessert goodness. 

DaNic's is the way to go for a sandwich.

One of my favorite places in Philly. 

Reading Terminal is a 2 block walk from my office and about 4 block walk from where I currently live. I pass by it everyday on the way to work around 8:30am to 9am and it's already packed with people. You can find anything and everything here from gourmet food to diner breakfasts to fresh made bread or even home made cheese. It really is the melting pot of Philadelphia. I could spend hours in there roaming around, eating all kinds of different foods.

Saturdays the busiest but you may also want to avoid lunch traffic on weekdays as it is frequented by everyone and their moms which means you'll have to fight for a table to eat your food or spend all of your lunch break waiting in line for a meal. They close early on weeknights.

I feels strange to write a review for a fast food restaurant, but this particular Chick-fil-A deserves 5 stars. 

Always been a fan of their food---always fresh and you can't go wrong with any of their chicken products. Chicken strips with the Chick-fil-A sauce is my go-to. 

I have to mention the excellent customer service here though. Everyone was friendly, and for the 15 minutes I was sitting down I was offered a refill on my Coke twice by two different staff members, and each thine they asked if the food was good, etc. Absolutely impressive, especially for a fast food place!

Love this place.  This is like a mega food court, except better!  The parking does suck, you have to find street parking, otherwise the parking structure is like 6 bucks for half an hour or something ridiculous like that.  When you first walk in, you're overwhelmed where you start, then you just kind of get into a groove or a method.  The only that sucks is that since I probably won't ever be back or at least for years, I wanted to try everything, but I had already had lunch.  So I settled for a cookie and tea.  That would have to do.  I wish there was something like this in LA!

An awesome market. So many food vendors, most of which are really cool and unique. I liked their dutch eating place, though I've had better french toast. Still, it's pretty tight and I've heard the donuts are amazing.

visited on saturday the 14th of april  about 10:00 in the evening DIRTY, DIRTY, DIRTY  rude employees acted like they could care less if we ate there or not. After asking for ice cream machine was told machine is broke asked for a frozen coffee that's broke too. We turned around and walked out. Please close this location before somebody gets food poisoning.

Amazing place to soak in all the diversity that philly has to offer. Great place to have breakfast or lunch while visiting philly. Great place to get produce and fish.  In the heart of center city so very accessible a MUSt do for anyone visiting philly.

RTM is a must do experience while in Philly. Pearl's Oyster Bar is the best brunch in Philly IMO. Famous 4th Street is a must for delicious, warm cookies. Great chocolate choices at Muller's, Termini's, and the PA General Store. Fantastic local choices for groceries in meat, cheese, milk, and sides of any dish you may desire. Old City Coffee is a must as well for a fresh cup or bag of beans to take home. There are also fresh veggie & fruit stands. RTM for the win!

This review is for the delivery service. I ordered a delivery through yelp (and they did charge me their usual delivery fee). After a while I get a call from the  Yelp Eat24 team that the restaurant has informed them that they do not have drivers and want me to pick up my food instead.

This is bizarre on so many levels. First, if they do not have drivers, why have they opted for a delivery service with Yelp? Second, if I had the time or resources to physically visit the restaurant, why would I pay extra and order for a home delivery?

In a nutshell, this is an extremely unprofessional behavior on behalf of the restaurant.

Came here with some friends last night for some beers and a bite.  We used to come here all of the time when it was the Witch, but as the Industry, I've only eaten here once, and it was opening week... and it wasn't awesome, so i decided to give it another go.  We do, however, come by somewhat frequently for a GLORIOUS beverag,e called 'Mummers Punch'.  It's basically a hangover in a punch bowl, but its oh-so-fun to drink.  For $45, you get a punch bowl with a little umbrella ladle that contains enough boozy goodness to serve a few rounds amongst a table of 4.  Well worth it.  So much fun!

Ok fasforward to last night- came in at the end of quizzo, and got seated right away at a nice lil table in the corner.  Service thru and thru was TOP NOTCH!  They were on their A-Game, yet struck that balance of keeping the beers coming, but not rushing you, or being too attentive to the point of annoying.  5 stars there.

We started with the arancini which came out pretty quick.  The balls themselves were a bit on the small side but there were 6 of them... so that works for me!  They were totally delicious.  The sauce that you dip them into, however, I didn't particularly care for.  It looked like marinara, but it had this smoky peppery taste to it.  Nobody else seemed to mind it... but not for me.

For dinner, my boyfriend and my friend both got the burgers.  As a vegetarian, my options here were limited.  There were no sandwiches I could eat, and the entree seemed a bit more serious that I was feeling at the time.  I had ordered a salad my first time in, and recall being disappointed with the size/excitement level of it, so i went for something that was called "Veggie Tofu Dips".  I expected some sort of fried tofu, crudite and chips that you dip into a side of dip.  The waitress warned me that this would be small, but that was ok.  I wasn't THAT hungry.  What came out was a plate of potato chips and a little jam jar of dip that must have had silken tofu whirled into the dip.  Not what I was expecting.  It wasn't awesome, nor was it awful.  I certainly wouldn't recommend this to anyone, nor would I order it again for myself.  The taste wasn't that awesome that i'd encourage anyone to split it either to be honest.  It sure was a led balloon.  After eating a bunch of chips and french onion dip (should have run to wawa instead?) i felt like a grease trap.  We finished our beers, went home, and I went to bed.  I woke up around 3:30a still feeling a bit icky.  It's my fault for eating the whole thing.

Those who ate the burgers seemed to make out tremendously better.  I'd give this place 3.5 stars if i could, but with the choice of 3 or 4... and judging from my personal experience, i think 3 are warranted.  it was an A-ok experience, but nothing that I'll be running back for.
Love this place, first time their it was crowded but it was lunch time. I love the fact the place caters to everyone needs. Wish they had one in New York

I don't think there's much else I can add to the Reading Terminal experience, but it was such a charming little spot that I had to write a review on it.

Tips:
1) Come between Wednesday and Saturday, especially this week due to the festival, since that is when the Pennsylvanian Dutch come and fill your hearts content with food. Since I came on a Monday morning, some of the vendors weren't open due to that.
2) Try the fresh fruit smoothies. I got a 20 oz of the refreshing watermelon/cantaloupe/banana for only $4.15 with tax. Made with real, fresh fruit, no preservatives or added sugar - just plain ole goodness.
3) Beer garden in the middle of the day? Sure why not! Average prices of beer on tap. $10 for two Blue Moons and we got our parking validated (:
4) What do you get when you mix seafood, Asian flavors, and Western subs/sandwiches together? You get an Asian fusion, seafoody Fat Korean to pair with that refreshing Blue Moon. (YES they have fat sandwiches at the market!)
5) If you park in the lot across the street, parking can be validated by a vendor once you purchase $10. However, this is only worth it if you spend less than 3 hours in the market. Otherwise it's a flat rate of $28 between 3 and 12 hours.
6) If it's hot out, come to Bassett's early in the morning to beat the rush. There tends to be a line at the counter while people try different flavors and other nonsense. This makes the line unbearably long.

Reading Terminal is such a nice escape from the city, and it's such a large foodie haven. I'm afraid that after frequenting RT, my DC Eastern Market may not be enough for me now...
This place is amazing. I love the different variety of foods and products. They need more seating options and the place needs to be bigger.

My friends and I went here last night for Dining out for Life, but my 5-star experience started 3 days prior to my dinner here.
The manager called and left me a voicemail telling me that there was bar trivia from 6:30-8:30 but that it would most likely be winding down by my reservation time and that we would be able to enjoy our dinner.  I thought that was great!
Our dinner was excellent.  Food was fantastic (fried green tomatoes + arugula = genius!) and our waitress was attentive without being in our face.  Beer selection is great and I really like the modern rustic feel the place has.  Only dark moment was when we chose the smores for dessert-the marshmallow topping was burned, just like at a real campfire, but it tasted like we ate a spoonful of ash.  The waitress was super cool about it and brought us something else to replace it.
All in all a great place.

Reading Terminal Market is the obvious place to go if you're a tourist to Philly. You've never been to Philly if you haven't gotten a meal here. There are countless places to eat, grab coffee, drink a brew, or just chill and maybe catch a special event. Don't miss out on the Dutch Eating Place for breakfast or Beiler's Bakery for donuts.

Reminds me of the Lexington Market in Baltimore... but so much cleaner! I love this place. I wish I could find a little back room and set up a little apartment. I'd eat here all the time. You'll find all your quick fast foods here (but healthier and tastier). Lots of ethnic foods as well as various American favorites. You can also find some Amish stores in the back of the market and pastries that will beckon you. Every time I come to Philadelphia, I must make a stop by here! It does get a little crowded and forget about finding seating during lunch time, but most of these places have ample seating during non rush hour! My favorite places are Amy's in the back where you can buy great kitchen supplies, the fresh produce, the "peking" duck section where you can buy Chinese BBQ pork and roast duck. My favorite! They also have a great crepe place and ice cream parlor. Well worth the trip! No parking here. You must walk or take the train.

Ordered pick up! The food was ready very fast, I ordered the chicken masala roll and lamb roll. The yogurt/white sauce thingy that came with the rolls is amazing. The chicken is honestly a little dry to me if eating without the sauce. But it fits very well with the sauce and gave a good texture together. The only thing is that the rolls are a bit small for me, I guess two rolls are about right for my appetite ahahah, would gave 4.5 if I can. :)

Great place for fantastic food. They have a ton of great choices to choose from and the food I got was super good. I just got a burger, but man what a great burger it was. It was cooked to perfection and was exactly what I wanted. Friendly and fun place.

Would love to start and end every day of my Philly trip here! Many different vendors and a lot of locally sourced ingredients in a whole variety of food options. Some market type vendors, and many other options for prepared food. Love it.

Loved this place! For lunch I grabbed a roast pork sandwich with sharp provolone from Dinics which was great! But the main reason I'm writing this review is Bc I came in off the hot philly street desiring something refreshing. Not only was I greeted by a number of friendly good looking men... But they proceeded to make me one of the most delicious drinks I've ever tasted. "THE LEMONANA".  Never have I ever been so enamored by a beverage in my life. I would pay an exorbitant amount of money to have a personal tap of this in my house. When I first got this drink it was served in one of their medium sized cups .... I drank that down in about 5seconds. So I went back and requested that they make me "THE LEMONANA" in the biggest cylindrical container they had, to which they happily obliged. 
It's located right under the big neon sign reading "fresh juices smoothies" across from golden bowl and next to market bloom. If you love lemonade or are interested in tasting the most delicious drink on this planet you should make the trip to the market and find this place !

Well they don't have many vegetarian items that seem worth the money, but all of their meat foods look really great. All of my friends recommend the Industry burger.

I really love this place for a casual-but-fun drink. The atmosphere is awesome and the staff is really helpful.  The drink menu is interesting and the staff provides great recommendations.  Great for bringing friends and dates; something about Industry always enables awesome conversations.
Greatest selection of originial Philly food in the city!

I think the sandwich is okay, but way too small for the price you pay for. I think subway has a better deal on that. However, I do love Oreo Milkshake here. Be aware, there are times when some waitstaff makes very diluted milkshake, but 80% of the time, it's excellent.

Love Reading Terminal.  Great place to get fresh produce, flowers, and more.  If we go to the Convention Center we always stop at the Reading Terminal for lunch but so does everyone else.  It is vey crowded at lunch because of all the options.  There is always police there/in the area so I feel safe.  You definitely have to go once for the experience and you'll want to keep going back.  Make sure to try a DeNics Pork sandwich and Bassett's ice cream - yummy!

Reading Terminal Market has a great selection of different kinds of food to eat,. So far I've been to Dinic's for their pork and broccoli rabe sandwich (must try!) and Smucker's for a breakfast sandwich which is probably a weird thing to rave about but it was actually really very good and reasonably priced. I definitely plan on checking out their grilled cheese place the next time I'm in the area.

It's also a great spot to walk around and check out the fresh produce (the last time I was there I got some huge artichokes!), baked goods, jams, jellies, baking mixes, gifts, etc. The only downside is that there isn't a lot of seating and it tends to get pretty crowded in there. During the warmer months they have some outdoor seating but not nearly enough to accommodate the amount of people that are coming in and out of there. It's definitely still worth checking out and grabbing a bite to eat!

gotta grab a pastrami reuben at Hershel's!

shout out to Beck's Cajun too :)

Meltkraft - I'd say not worth the hype..

Oh man. I love this place. What more could you want? Everything from bakery foods, produce, cheese, meats, fish, fresh pre-made foods, local favorites, pastries, coffee shops, local winery area, a beer garden, and other artsy shops. I could only shop/eat food from here and I'd be totally happy.


Only down sides- it can get seriously crowded! Also, some of the places might be a bit more expensive than a traditional stores, or locations outside this area. Still...not reasons to not go. Its amazing there!

The culinary heartbeat of Philadelphia. If I could only eat under one roof for the rest of my life, it would be here. The selection is overwhelming, the energy is high, and the competition for your dollar is cut-throat.
Lot's of great food and groceries!  Some of it better than others, so everyone will have a different experience.

This is the greatest food place in the world, bar none. It's like a Whole Foods version of a mall food court. 

Dinics lives up to the hype. Beiler's donuts are out of this world. Chocolates are delicious. Ribs and fried chicken mmmmm. The Thanksgiving Turkey joint. 

Other than the sushi place, which you should avoid at ALL COSTS (seriously look up Tokyo Sushi, how many places manage an overall 1-star rating on yelp?) you really can't go wrong in this market. 

Avoid the sushi.

Eat anything else.

At 11am on our way back to jersey after breakfast, we stopped by to pick up tea for the road and saw this next to it. It is one of the best fried chicken speciality places, pretty authentic Taiwanese style. And the squid is amazing and must try while hot!

I come here very often during my lunch hour.  Customer service here is top notch. Service is fast.  Food is consistent and good.  Price is more than most fast food places but it's worth it for the quality of food that you get.  Their milkshakes are excellent!!

This was my/our third trip to the RTM in 20 years with consistently great experiences.  The RTM features a collection of places to eat, shop for food (fresh markets) or just to shop.  Ethnic experiences from Amish to Italian to Soul to Philadelphian are feet apart.  Some have been written up on your favorite cable food/travel channels...many have not.  But...overall: it's a blast.  Go with a small group and graze: order something, share and move on to the next establishment...repeat for a few hours.  You'll be surrounded by a lot of people in a unique environment that buzzes with energy.

Downside: it can get crowded, especially on a weekend.  The seating is ridiculously limited.  But, I'll go again the next time I'm in town.
Great place with great quality foods and unbelievable selection of options. My favorite is Hershel's Jewish deli for the best corned beef, pastrami, brisket and turkey this side of NYC.

This is one of my go-to places for quick Indian food. I've tried their paneer tikka and paneer masala rolls, chicken biryani platter, and paneer platter. I like their paneer but always which it were in bigger pieces.

As someone who doesn't like spice too much, the chicken biryani was a bit too much for me but the white sauce made it better. Their late hours make this a prime place to go at multiple hours of the day!
This is a must eat place if you are looking for Indian or halal food. All of their food is excellent and great customer service.
I love this place - Nanee's Kitchen (in the back) makes the best Chai tea! Only thing is the market is always so packed with people - I never sit down in there for that reason.

An essential Philly Mecca of markets meshed together in one spot. Hershel's East, Franks a Lot, Keven Parker Soul Food, Down Home Diner, Dutch Eating Place, Termini...even a bar/restaurant (Molly Malloy's!) are all here. Whew. I'm heading over there just thinking of all these wonderful spots.  See ya.

Awesome dumplings and great service!

If you've never been here you need to check it out.

A wonderful variety of local food! 
I personally love Terminis bakery for their chocolate bananas and cannolis. 
It does get extremely crowded during peak hours so I usually like to go on sundays.

Went in at lunch and it looked like a clean and new place. I wondered how long it would take to get runied in that neighborhood. Not long. While I was in line someone said " so when is somebody going to fill the soda dispenser? " The workers just looked at each other. The man is probably still waiting for soda. I left without ordering.
Loved this market, we there were one here in Hawaii lol Love the variety of foods, from the restaurants to the produce! Must place visit for the visitors!

Wish there was more seating during busy weekday lunch time. Good selection for lunch. Moderately priced bakery items and ethnic cuisine. You can still eat healthy though with salads. There are also deep fried goods too. I like how this location is well situated from conferences and hotels.

This place is sensory overload.

To call it a food court would be an understatement. It's a farmer's market. It's sit-down counters. It's full of seating. Okay, I guess it's just a giant food court.

It's easy to be overwhelmed with the options, but let me just help you - go to Tommy DiNic's and get the roast pork sandwich. Or go to Beck's and get some delicious gumbo or a fried alligator po boy. Hell, you can even get Peking duck here. Or if you get there early enough, snag a seat at Dutch Eating Place (which I hear is amazing, but too packed when we went on a Saturday afternoon).

Sure, the place is crowded and touristy, but I would so recommend going here just for the scope of it all.

I'm sure this place is fun ... when it's not overcrowded like crazy. I guess it was bad timing for out-of-towners to check it out on Saturday morning but WOW. You can barely move around and lines at every booth. If you're claustrophobic or have anger issues, do not come here during busy hours. My family and I split up to check out different places to eat but once we got our food, we were standing around looking for a place to sit. People are like black friday best buy shoppers, they will elbow and shove their way to an open spot. I wouldn't be surprised if there are fights here all the time. It also took an hour for my cousin to get his philly cheese steak, which was pretty good but no food is worth that wait, especially when you're hangry and have no place to sit.

This is a fantastic food hall, containing stalls that sell fresh produce, meat, prepared items, non-food items, and baked goods.  There are also a wide variety of restaurants preparing food fresh, either to eat there or take away.  I was so happy to see the variety, as it could have been nothing more than pretzels, ice cream and cheesesteaks, but there is so much more!  

While not all food vendors are of the same quality there were a few that stood out to me - Dutch Eating Place, Sang Kee Peking Duck, Termini Brothers Bakery, DiNics.  Once place I really wanted to try but was not able to was the Soul Food Cafe.  The fried chicken looked so good.  

it's worth taking a lap or two to check out what's what.  Prices were reasonable, the portions leaned towards generous, and the quality was pretty high.  While seating may be an issue during periods of high density I didn't have much of an issue during multiple visits.

It's worth a visit, at least once, during a visit to Philly.   Note that the Amish owned businesses have limited hours (they are posted at the market entrances).  Some places take credit cards but I'm not aware if all do.  I did see at least one ATM inside.  This market is located above the Jefferson Station  and is fairly close to the historic sites and Chinatown.

Reading - pronounced "Redding" apparently, as I was corrected quite often.   My savior in Philly.  Want something healthy?  Tasty?  Sinful?  Across the street from my hotel?  
Every lunch I had was spent here - getting freshly carved turkey breast from "The Original Turkey", salad from "Tootsie's salad bar", sushi from "Tokyo Sushi Bar" - this sushi chef was the fastest I've ever seen, and the sushi was amazing.   If I wanted to stay with my healthy eating choices, I'd also stock my hotel fridge with fresh fruit from Iovine Brothers Produce - they also made the BEST fruit salad.  I kid you not.  Ripe, succulent, and juicy.  (Insert dirty joke here)
If I wanted to be naughty, oh it was easy to be downright perverse here.. The cornbread from Delilah's - the best I've ever eaten in my entire life hands down.  Melt in your mouth, buttery goodness..
And the grand finale...Ir-freakin-resistable cookies from The Famous 4th Street Cookie Co.  Oh holy hell.  I had to have one every day, if not only for one bite and then hand it off to one of my friends who cursed me for giving them the additional calories, but silently blessed me for leading them to cookie heaven.  I tried every flavor.. All were delectable.  But if I had to choose?  The peanut butter chocolate chip and the white chocolate macadamia nut.  
Can't we move this to Los Angeles?  Please?

Very nice indoor public market. Reminded me of Grand Central Market in LA, but this public market is so much better. The grocer and restaurant stalls in this store are all real nice.  I stopped by the Dutch Eating Place and had an excellent breakfast. This is a really nice place to visit, even to just walk through and be tempted by the delicious looking items. I saw many real good items, especially from bakery and grocer stores, that looked real good. 

If you're coming from the airport, this is just a short walk from the Suburban Station that you can reach by taking the train. The train is real convenient here, very easy to take from the airport and only $6.75 for anone way trip.

It's probably a good thing that Yelp exists because the amount of food conversations that I have in real life is pretty ridiculous and usually needs to be policed.  One great example is when I have an in-depth conversation with a coworker about the best burger in Philadelphia.  An outsider may have thought our heated conversation was about religion or politics.  Nope, just about pieces of meat on bread.  So my coworker says that The Industry has the best burger in Philly.

Oh really?  This will need to verified by Jill L, immediately.

My husband and I headed over for a quick dinner on a Saturday night.  First thing I noticed was how open the space was.  Some of these South Philly joints feel like the walls are closing in on you.  Not here.  We were quickly seated and were given the challenge of choosing a beer off their (very good) list.  Prices seemed to be in line with nearby establishments.

So we reviewed the menu, despite already knowing what we were getting.  The menu here is... eclectic.  If you are not an adventurous eater, you may not be happy here.  BUT you can always get the burger which is pretty cheap ($8 for a single patty) and can be customized with additional patties and toppings.  The basic burger comes with lettuce, tomato, Cabot cheddar, and pickle mayo.

I thought the burger was pretty amazing.  The best in Philly?  I don't know.  But definitely one of the best you can get for $8.  

So why 3 stars?  I feel like the location isn't the best.  If you have a car, you are fine because there is plenty of parking.  But I feel like it's a bit too removed from many parts of the city- including East Passyunk where I live.  The other reason is that there are too many what I call "strange meats" on the menu.  I'm a wimp when it comes to meat and alot of the menu wasn't appealing to me.

I'd definitely be interested in putting on my big girl pants and trying some of the menu items that look scary to me, because I'm sure I'd find them delicious.  Also, it seems like a great place to get a group together for some drinks.  The Industry, I will be back and will be looking to add some more stars to my review!

One stop shop for everything; fresh produce, French pastries, cheese, meat, seafood and some wonderful dining choices all under one roof. It is a city by itself and a great place to shop and walk around. It is lively and bustling and is unbelievable that everything is going on inside one huge umbrella.

If you're hungry but not sure what you're craving, and you want to also grab some produce on the run, go here.

If your elbows are sharp and you're ready for a crowd, go during the weekday lunch rush.

A definite Philly staple, no matter how you look at it.

The sights, sounds, and smells of this downtown market are intoxicating! It was across the street from our hotel so we ate breakfast there every morning and lunch once too. Many different cuisines offered plus a produce market. This place can get extremely busy (Saturday afternoons) and that can take away from the enjoyment. You pretty much have to hover around the tables and pounce when someone looks like they are about to finish. It was much more enjoyable weekday mornings after everyone is at work. Recently became open seven days a week, 9-6. However, because each stall is operated individually, you can't be guaranteed every stall will be open the entire time. Had hoped to pick up some energy soup and veggie burger mix at a natural foods stall on Monday before leaving town but at 10:45am, there was still no sign that the stall would open that day.
Always lively, people everywhere and being surrounded by a plethora of food options! Food heaven.

Reading Terminal Market is one of Philadelphia's many gems! There are so many stands that sell various products. I love checking out the stand that sells products made of honey! Everything is so natural and the prices are wonderful for the caliber of their goods! There are many food places to try and enjoy various cuisines! The candy stand is full of fun, colorful items that will have you stopping before you even set your eyes on all of the products. This market is indoor and is so spacious, which makes for a comfortable visit no matter what time you go! It is never too busy and you can enjoy yourself whether you are sitting indulging in some wonderful ethnic eats or walking around exploring. I recommend this market to everyone and anyone who loves to try various products from food items to flowers and bath and body products! This place has a little bit of everything that will keep you coming back for more!

Went for a Saturday afternoon Burger and Drink. No complaints about the bear. The burger was maybe one of the worst things I have ever had. I got the Double Burger. It came out Grey, and inedible. Made me sick even looking at it. Looked old, and sickly. I love burgers and have had a few here that were good. Overall the last few times I have been here the food has truly gone downhill. Used to be one of my favorites. What happened? Chef/Ownership Change?

big group of many different things to eat and drink there. It was a mad house lots of quantity and little quality that I could see. Would not return there but at least I can say I went there. I went to the famous "carmine's" which was horrible but I found a juice place that was great. Poor quality and lots of quantity .

This place is new so I will be back to give it a second chance. However, I did want to put my experience out there. The first thing I noticed was how incredibly loud it was.  I got used to it but it is definitely not a good place to go if you want to have a nice talk with someone. 
The food itself was pretty terrible. I had the market BLT fish sandwich while my friend had the porchetta.  Mine consisted of poorly battered fish, sad lettuce and ONE piece of bacon on a buttered roll.  There was no aioli, or any sauce of any kind.  It did not taste like anything.  Absolutely nothing. My friend didn't fare much better.  We did tell the waitress and she kindly brought us pickled mayonnaise. Unfortunately, it tasted neither of mayonnaise or of pickles. The server did take one sandwich off of the bill which was nice. She did, however, bring our bill with the coaster that said "If you can't afford to tip, you can't afford to drink in a bar. Go to the liquor store." They need to get rid of these, they are not cute.  
The menu doesn't work with the neighborhood in my eyes. It was too pretentious and the prices too high. This neighborhood has struggled with attracting and keeping restaurants.  This place needs some tasty, accessible food. Unless "The Industry" makes some serious changes it won't be sustainable.

I love this place! Their fresh produce is dirt cheap and super clean. I buy the majority of my groceries from the Reading Terminal on Sunday's and if you come with a student ID, you get an additional 10% off! They have the BEST olive oil with a zillion different flavors in a store called Tubby Olive; I'm obsessed. There's an old country diner that sells the best breakfast (catfish platter recommended) and the wait time isn't too bad. There's a delicious Cajun eatery called Beck's Cajun Cafe and their New Orleans themed food is to die for! I'm a huge fan of their fried oyster and shrimp poboys! You can even make them do 1/2 and 1/2, but be sure to ask for extra remoulade and hot sauce. I'm also a fan of the ice cream parlor near the entrance and the grilled cheese joint in the back will make you slap YO MAMA!

Great selection of food, shops, bakeries...but it can be unbelievably crowded and packed with people. Try to find an off hour to visit the market, or else it's just not as enjoyable. All of the long lines for food are typically worth the wait, so grab a snack and enjoy the scene.
five stars--my wife and I could spend the whole day here eating great food and people watching.

Fantastic market- plenty of great food! There are a lot of great trinkets and Philly products. Great fresh local produce and meat. It does get really busy so plan to wait in line a lot. There are two parking garages that offer discount parking with a validated ticket. Head to their website for exact directions. Perfect place to be when you're not sure what your next activity in Philly will be.

Chances are, if you're visiting Philly, you're gonna check this place out. If not, you need to. The legendary Reading Terminal Market lives up to its legendary status. You can find literally anything here. Exciting, bustling atmosphere, and even better smells. You don't want to pass up a trip to this place. The parking garage across the street is the easiest way to park. $4 for 2 hours. You can't beat that. Make sure you come hungry.

This place is a mecca of all foods.  You can find anything your heart desires. The juice place was somewhere I stopped frequently for breakfast (fantastic way to start the day).  I would recommend the savory crepes along with the famous donut place with a bunch of funky delicious flavors.

You can't go wrong any where here!
The paneer platter is to die for, which is only made better by the fact that platters here are generously portioned.

Solid neighborhood joint. On Mondays they have "burgers and bubbles" special. Thursday's are Quizzo night. They have outdoor seating and large TVs inside for watching games. The food is solid gastropub style, always served with a heaping pile of fries.
My favorite place to go for food since moving to the area...I feel like I'll never eat everything they offer...but I'll try haha

The trout amandine was the very best we've had (and we're from Manhattan!!). The steak frites, on the other hand, was well reviewed on these pages, but didn't woo-hoo us. Festive ambiance and friendly wait staff. You'll have fun.

Oh boy,..I don't have room on this page to tell you about all the wonderful treasures in The Reading Terminal. My favorite spots to go is Godshalls Poultry where I buy all my Turkey Products, they have fresh meats. Another is Jovine Brothers Produce where I get all my fresh vegetables for really cheap prices. The Golden Fish Market for fresh fish and shrimp! Plenty eateries to pop in an have lunch, my latest place Hatville Deli where they slice the meat fresh onto the bread...yumm. Oh and don't forget about the Amish fresh baked donuts...I could go on and on about the Reading Terminal just go an take plenty money you won't be disappointed.

Lots to choose from at the RTM - it is crowded so be prepared. There are some seats in open areas if you can grab some food and then find a seat or if your like me go to the restaurants like Molly Malloy's which also has great food and enjoy your stay. The best sandwich as shown on t.v. is here at RTM, if you like slow roasted pork! Check out DiNic's in the middle of the market.
Most of us Phila. residents have been coming here all of our life!
Oh so yummy berry rolls at Metropolitan Bakery!  Crazy good sticky buns at Beiler's bakery!  Best duck in the city at Sang Kee!  I love my kitchen fish towels from Amy's Place!  And so much more...
Love this place. Whenever I'm there, the pleasant memory of childhood'd come back to me. The trains, the smell of grandma's cooks, the Christmasy decorations... Oh I wish my family were here with me.

Reading terminal has always been a cool place to visit when in old city philadelphia. There's so many food places to choose from while inside. This place can get very crowed and it's easy to get lost in here. If you do come to philly, definitely check it out.

Gorgeous on the inside and much bigger than other markets in the same still. Really wonderful choices. It gets very busy but there are some many options that if you are really in a pinch, you can get any food you want.

I don't have anything bad to say about Reading Terminal Market.  I would recommend that you get here pretty early to avoid crowds.  Iovine's is pretty great for produce and I haven't had a bad experience with any of the butchers or fishomngers, though I do prefer (if time allows) Ippolito's and Esposito's

The biggest trouble that I have with the RTM is the variety. I usually have to walk around at least twice before I can settle on something to eat. A must see for locals and visitors. Bring your appetite. This isn't your average place to go.
There are some great vendors here and there are some that only survive because it's always packed with tourists. Watch your pockets, it's shoulder to shoulder in there.

OK so this was my first excursion walking to Center City since I have moved.  I've been to Philly a few times but never actually went in to RTM.  IT's BANANAS!  Literally bananas everywhere for 69 cents a bundle.  I am not sure how busy it is on weekdays, but Saturday was pretty much jam packed I actually got knocked backwards by some lady but it was ok a nice gentleman was immediately behind me to catch my fall.  Pretty much any sort of produce, meat, cheese, fresh fish, bread, sweets, candy you could want is here.  Price vary, I suggest walking the whole place to look around before making too many purchases.  Most places have little lines, but they move very fast and efficiently.  Some good deals are to be had, I bought grapes tomatoes and onions for under a dollar each.  Also adorable tiny cacti were all over one booth.  This is about an hour walk from 44th street but a very enjoyable leisurely one.  I will go again perhaps for sushi or just to buy a bucket of raw whole fish mmmmm...not sure what I would do with them.
This place is a bit overwhelming but wow!  So many things to choose from.  A bustling place with some good food and interesting little shops!

This is a great place to grab a quick breakfast or lunch. So much variety! I visited twice around 8-10 am and the dutch breakfast place with apple dumplings seemed super popular. Fresh donuts, a million types of cheese steaks, gyros, Amish goods, honey products, candies -- the list goes on. 

The market is like 95% food though. Was hoping that there would be a few more non food local products.

I was really excited to try Humpty's Dumplings and I am a huge fan of dumplings, dim sum, and Asian food in general. I was a bit bummed that most of the menu was not Asian inspired, although I was very willing to give the "non traditional" flavors a try. 

We went on a weekday and it was not crowded, but there was only one guy working so he was pretty busy. He was friendly and helpful, but didn't seem 100% confident about what he was doing. I hope this was an off day, but the bathroom was also filthy. 

We each got a "combo meal" which includes a noodle bowl, 5 dumplings, and a drink. It's $18 and pretty overpriced if you ask me. It seems like the dumplings are premade and frozen until fried/steamed. There wasn't much of a kitchen and I didn't like that there was a big slab of raw beef sitting on a sink in the back that was close to the hallway to the bathroom. If I saw that before ordering I might have thought twice. 

We tried the steamed pork dumplings, which were the closest to traditional Asian dumplings. They were tasty and came with a good dipping sauce. We also tried the fried buffalo chicken dumplings. They could have used more hot sauce. It felt more like eating a buffalo chicken bite more so than a dumpling. The dumplings had a lot of filling, and the wrapping was very thick. 

We tried the noodle bowl of the month, which was an Asian BBQ bowl with slaw on top. It was slightly greasy, but had a nice flavor. I wish it had more vegetables in it. We also tried the cheesesteak bowl. It was basically mac&cheese with udon noodles instead of mac. The peppers and onions cut the heaviness a bit and it had a good amount of cheese steak. The bowls were super filling and we only had a few bites before packing up the rest to take home. I probably wouldn't come back, but I can appreciate the novelty of this place.
This is seriously the best Chick Fil A! The staff is really nice and helpful. The salads are on point. The manager is nice, and the food is fresh. Yum!

The best place for someone who's indecisive... or just like to eat!  One of the oldest markets in the US, it's been around since 1892.  We were there on a Saturday morning around 10:30am and it wasn't too packed.  We got a brisket sandwich from Dinic's (pretty good), duck wonton soup from Sang Kee, fried mac n cheese ball from Beck's Cajun Cafe and butter cake & whoopie pies from The Flying Monkey bakery.  The sweets at the Flying Monkey are amazing! The butter cake has a really interesting crunch gooey texture.  My husband loved the whoopie pie.  

Great spot to grab a bite!
Wonderful place for quick bites, snacks, groceries, produce and food. Something for everyone! Definitely go there.

This place has hit its stride. It's still not my favorite spot for food, but I've had some good meals here, and it's a nice option to have in the neighborhood. The drinks are always great--I'd especially recommend the Ghost of Mary at brunch or anytime!

This was my first time at Honeygrow, and honestly it will not be my last. Custom stir fry......that is potentially the best idea ever. The service was a little slow, and they were out of the meat my dad ordered but the employees were really nice. All in all it was a good first experience.

When I came here on a weekday evening, they ran out of their A1 Ninja Crispy Chicken special at 9:41PM so my friends and I ordered the smaller version Samurai Crispy Chicken. The order took a while to come out, and there were not that many pieces. The restaurant is on the smaller side with a couple of tables inside. I would want to come back to try the large chicken that they're known for, hopefully which is better!

I love this place. It's just a cool place to walk through. You can find some of the coolest items and best food in the city here. (That's what I'm told anyways)

I'm from the south but then lived in England for a bit. They have markets like this in the UK everywhere so it was a bit nostalgic.

Talk about sensory overload.  The din, the visual assault, the aromas, the throngs of shoppers...I loved it.

There's something, of everything, for anybody, at Reading Terminal Market.  Beautiful produce at affordable prices.  Ready-to-eat world cuisine from India to Japan to Belgium.  Fish markets and butchers.  Bakeries and fromageries.  Pennsylvania Dutch stalls and honey stands.  All-herb stalls and French textiles.  Kitchen gadgets and plants.  RTM has you covered better than any supermarket ever could.

My favorite stalls were:

~The Herbiary with its essential oils, medicinal herbs, and home remedies.
~Kauffman's Lancaster County Produce, which had a dozen flavors of covered pretzels, beet and okra chips, and a zillion other novelties from Dutch country.  Not to mention eminently friendly vendors.
~Amy's Place kitchen wares.  I love a good gadget, and this stall is full of 'em.
~Fair Food Farmstand.  All the produce is local and organic from small-scale farms, with an emphasis on humanely-raised meats and sustainable agriculture.  Yesss!

I'd like to pull a "Career Opportunities" in Reading Market.

I love that there is so much fresh. local food and such a huge variety. It's really awesome that it is so close to the train station, so I can stop on my way home. Knocked off one star from perfect - could use some more organic options..and later hours - i make it by the skin of my teeth every time .

This place is a lot of fun! Great atmosphere, hustle bustle, so much to look at - kitchen shop, candy shops, flowers, meat, fish, cheese, produce, lots of food stalls. Our group of 5 split up to each find what we wanted to eat for lunch, then got a table in the center area. Some of the food lines were pretty long, but I found a short line at Beck's Cajun and was very happy with my etouffee.
So many good places to either eat or buy food. DeNic's has the best Pork and Roast Beef Sandwiches. Martin's Meats is by far the best for home Sausage! No one in the City comes close!

Oh my God! Where to begin? This place was overwhelming! I needed several days to eat my way through here! I will be back. The smoked and rotisserie chicken wings along with their rotisserie carrots were fantastic at Dienner's BBQ. It is tucked away in the back of the Amish corner. Go there! Also if you like soft pretzels, you must to go to Miller's twist pretzels and more! The best I've ever had! Be sure to get there honey mustard dipping sauce if you like honey mustard. I can't wait to come back to the market.
This is an amazing place. I never have enough time here to see everything. It can get pretty packed here, but it's a very unique experience.

Over-priced. If the food tasted and looked better the prices would be reasonable. However, the food is where this bar utterly fails. 

The menu. I can only speak for myself, but I just came here for the third and final time, and finally stumbled upon the secret to not leaving this bar frustrated: don't order any food.
