The previous time I looked the menu up and down, could not find a single item I found appetizing (except fried green tomatoes with arugula and balsamic, a dish that should never cost $10), and settled on a rather anemic portion of fries for $4. The dishes I have ordered or tried with friends: whipped tofu, too small; the soup by all accounts was flavorless; fried green tomatoes, not enough salt and too small for $10; veggie fritters, looked boring and unappetizing; the burger, on the small side, it's ok but does not compete in the Philly burger scene; the Seafood BLT, disappointing (the fish was fluke that one day); pulled BBQ duck, bread to goodies ratio way too high; sweet corn arepas, not very sweet, tasted like sauteed mushrooms over bland corn bread mix, and a total ripoff at $15. Basically everything about the food elicits one of two reactions in me: "ripoff", or "I let my dogs eat pig ears, so no thank you". Vegetarians: do not patronize this bar, unless you like punishing yourself. 

The drinks by all accounts are good but pricey, the beer selection is decent but does not stand out against countless other bars with way better food. During happy hour ($1 off a $6 drink, thank you so much), or if you qualify for the "industry discount", the prices are more reasonable, like an average Philly bar. 

The music is too loud, causing the classic din of screaming conversations and louder music in constant competition. 

The waitstaff are good at their jobs. 

The interior decor is very snazzy. 

Besides the food, the other thing that really drives the point home for me are the "cute" bar rules/commandments. These are not funny and come across as highfalutin and better-than-thou. These guys even had a brief social media campaign where they made the same kind of "bar rules" out of quotes from negative Yelp reviews. Condescend much? First they rip you off, snickering at your back as you walk out the door, and when you get home you see that they mocked you on the internet as well. Well, I certainly won't be back. 

I wanted this place to be great, having just moved to the area and being a big fan of the Good Dog, but it's just not. Instead it's just arrogant and alienating to its own customers. And I won't be going back.

I love this place and its on my places of must stops whenever I visit Philly. Think of it and it's in here. I can't remember the names of some of the vendors I've frequented but I know the Creole food spot is banging. Also the ice cream place by the exit. Last but not least there is a diner which serves excellent breakfast fare.
2nd trip back to Philly. You have to go to Reading Terminal Market. Have yet to have a bad meal

Need to shop for some produce or seafood or meat? Hungry at the same time?

Well, Reading Terminal Market has it all! Everything from a Pennsylvania Dutch bakery to fresh seafood can be found at the market. Not only is it easily accessible via the metro, it's a fun place to go and experience life.

But, be warned! It's a popular place and the weekends can get quite crowded, making it hard to find a spot to sit and eat. And yet, when I overheard someone exclaim "There's too many people in here!" I almost yelled back, "I guess you haven't been to Asia!"
Pretty Good beef bowl! I went around 8pm on a Sunday was no lines. The place was really clean and very efficient.  I will be back most definitely

I  love the fresh veggie and healthy option add-ins on the menu. The first person that you meet takes your order and your name, greeting with a big smile. The assembly line of staff then uses your name to say hello, and smile while making sure that your order is exactly how you want it. A smile also greets you at the register. This place makes me happy not only because of the quality of the meal, but also because of the friendly, smiling staff. This past week at a busy time on one of the warmer days, the owner/manager walked down the line offering water to those waiting! Beefsteak on Penn's campus is doing it right, really right. My new favorite place for lunch.

I love coming here. Great fresh produce. Great pizza place. The diner is delicious. The chardonnay at the Blue Mountain Vineyard is one of my favorite chardonnays on the market. But my favorite thing about RTM? APPLE. DUMPLINGS.
Enjoyed a great time with my girl friends.  Good food and service.

I will never eat here again nor recommend this to anyone. We bought an ice cream in a cup and our two year old wanted to have a cone, plain cone. The lady then charged us a full price for an ice cream cone, just for the plain cone. 
I cannot fathom how a non-customer service restaurant can operate in the airport while being so unprofessional and flat out greedy! 
I will never EVER eat at this greedy restaurant again and I hope all you other parents out there do not support an establishment with such a complete lack of customer service values. HORRIBLE AND SHAME ON YOU GREENLEAFS. Although with green in the name it's clear they only care about short term profits.

One of my favorite places in Philadelphia! As the individual vendors all have individual reviews, I will be reviewing the venue itself instead of the plethora of vendors in the market. 

RTM is very chaotic and it's real easy to get lost in, but it only adds to its charm. There is really something for everybody here, from sushi to dessert factories. If you were to show someone Philadelphia, RTM is a great place to start.

SUCH a fun place. I lived in Philly for years and would come here at least weekly to do my grocery shopping but it's also fun just to walk around and look at things.  The produce is fresh and so cheap.  The restaurant stalls are good.  The Pennsylvania Dutch goods are also yummy.  My favorite places are the iovine brothers, the butcher's right next to it, Flying Monkey makes beautiful cakes, the cheese shops are yummy and will give you samples.  There's a great spice shop/kitchen supplies shop

Ok, I know it sounds more than a bit strident and maybe I sound more than a bit mental, but I'm extremely accurate and have been eating at places like this for over 40 years.  Here's a copy of what I just sent to Potbelly corporate:

This was my first visit to a Potbelly...and, unless there are drastic changes, my last.

Just reading the "Our story" and "Our food" sections of the web site tells me all I need to know.  In the past, there may have been an original store that was famous for great sandwiches.  Then during the franchise process, a board room meeting where accolades are heaped upon the company about "how wonderful we are" and "how amazing our food is".  No one has the nerve to ask if it';s true.  It isn't.  As soon as I opened my turkey and Swiss sandwich, I could see in an instant and before discovering that they not-at-all-busy sandwich maker was too busy talking to actually include any Swiss cheese, that the turkey was "jelly turkey", which is the lowest quality formed turkey breast available.  It's translucent, watery texture is visible from across a room.  This has absolutely nothing to do with whatever quality sandwiches began the franchise and everything to do with placing price above quality by someone who has zero connection to the food. If you don't think that food quality plays a big part in the restaurant business, then doom is waiting for you. For another $.50, the company could use at least passable turkey.

Also, I was deeply surprised by the dearth of choices on the menu.  I thought that a store specializing in sandwiches would have...special sandwiches.  The options on the menu are so basic, it's a joke.  Mayo or mustard?  What is this, 1952?  Where are different flavored sauces, edgy mustards, horseradish or barbecue sauce, wasabi mayonnaise.  Where are sweet peppers, bacon, grilled onions and mushrooms...nothing!  Is that them, hidden in the "extras" banner?  This is Philadelphia, where we know sandwiches.  Jelly turkey is a tip off that nothing on the menu is prepared with pride, but only an unblinking eye on costs.

Well, that attitude just cost you a customer.
Love this place! Smuckers, Bielers and the produce place are amazing! $5.00 to park 2 hours is wonderful. Wish the parking would stay cheap after 4 hours, but a wonderful place to be.
kind of expensive, but the quintessential philadelphia food stop. my favorite attraction in the city. overwhelming with delicious things.
After a nearly 2 year boycott on the chain, Chick-Fil-A finally buckled and I once again feel free to enjoy their delicious nuggets, waffle fries, and diet dr. pepper.  What an amazing meal!

This is everything. 

This is Philadelphia.

Walked in with a friend on a cold philly night 
Place was almost full and noisy.... Greeted by the host and promptly seated 

1. Deco - 4/5 low lighting and nice alternative/rock music with a boisterous crowd guzzling drinks around you

2. Price - 4/5 quite reasonable (6-7 for an imported beer, 3 for local during happy hour).... 

3. Food and drink - 2.5/5 food is acceptable... Wasn't particularly impressed with the beef burger but liked the lamb skewers. The fish blt was a tad too oily per my friend. Fries were good but nothing memorable. 

4. Service - 3.5/5 promptly seated. Orders taken promptly (appreciated when it's quite busy) and wait staff accommodated request to taste the beers prior to ordering them. Didn't like the fact that coats need to kept by the side instead of being offered to be taken away. No additional area to keep your coat either. 

5. Overall - 3.5/5 would not mind hanging out again but won't be on the top of my list.

Eh. I feel Andrew Zimmern betrayed me. As much work as it took me to get here, I was expecting more. I like the set up and the variety of eateries but it was quite crowded. I know it was a weekend but I was hoping everyone would be at the beach. The highlights of this trip was the validated parking and Mariah Carey playing on the tv at Kevin Parker's Soul Food stand. I may give it another try on a weekday if I am in the area but driving 1 1/2 is too much for me.

This market was pretty fun. There was a convention in town so the place was hella packed.  There wasn't as much stuff to buy as there was just food to eat, not a bad thing, just don't have too much expectations if you're looking to shop.  The lines were crazy long for anything remotely like a cheesesteak probably because this place is a bit of a tourist trap.  Anyway, I still enjoyed myself so 4 stars for sure.

Hey, everyone outside. Come in here and lets walk up and down the isles as slowly as possible. Grrrr. 

I love markets but they are hard to review because they are created of so many components. Let me just write whats on my mind and you decide.

Easy to find, i walked here from the Convention Center. The second i walked in it was packed out with people walking without a purpose. I get people browsing, cool, but i was starving an in a rush to find something.

Variety, its got it. You can get all types of food here from Sushi to Chocolate and Deli meats. I chose to eat at By George (no good) check out my review on it.

After i battled the crowd and got my food i sat at one of the public tables. It had food all over it and the ground. The area was generally dingy and gross. Also i noticed a few homeless (or so they looked) roaming around inside. I sympathize for the situation but i felt generally uncomfortable at some points. 

I am not shutting this place out because of the size and options. I'll try it again for sure but just seems a bit dirty and crowded for my liking.
This is a great indoor market.  The restaurants in the market are delicious.  I really liked all of the other booths too.

Got the lamb kebab kati roll. The lamb and the green chutney to spice it up was delicious, but the roti-roll  needs improving, it was soggy. Typically Kati-Roll's are thick wraps with meat and masala stuffing. Masala chai was good. I think they will improve over time. Will give them another try when walking thru that part of town sometime soon.

This is a great spot to go to if you are a tourist or a local. My little cousins who are 7 and 9 call the market "The Mall of Food!!" They love coming here. I come and get my groceries here with my boyfriend often. We try out different restaurants for lunch and usually get something sweet before we leave from a bakery shop or candy shop. This place has a little bit of everything so I'm never disappointed. (I also enjoy people watching here, it's a great place to do it.)

I loved exploring all the great little eateries and delis that are housed in this market.  There is such a nice variety of different places including ice creameries, bakeries, BBQ/soul food places, Chinese, sandwiches, Thai, oyster bar, coffee, Amish stands, etc.  It reminds me of the Ferry Building in San Francisco, but with a more comfort food, blue collar vibe.

While we were there we sampled things from Dutch Eating Place (Amish), Bassetts Ice Cream, Dienner's BBQ, Tommy Dinic's, some Chinese place, Flying Monkey Patisserie, and an Amish vendor that sold fresh squeezed juice.  Everything was generous, freshly made, well serviced, clean and fairly pried.  

A definite must see when in Philly.  Hours are Mon-Sat 8-6, Sun 10-5.

Such a fun and filling way to spend the day.  Tons of delish food options.  Specialty spice shop is one of my favorites.  The Amish have gone made pies, breads, cinnamon buns.  It's a part of Philly culture.  Definite 2 thumbs up!!

I am going back to philly just to go here (and to Monks Cafe!). It's a 4 hour drive, but the market is incredible. What a way to enjoy a weekend!  Everything foodie under one huge roof - price range from insanely cheap to kind-of-high-but-worth-it.   Highly recommend the German cafe and deli (Wurzhaus Schmitz), the Tubby Olive balsamic vinegar store, Giuntas meats and the 4th Street Cookie Company. All amazing!  Foodies heaven!

Pretty sure I was the first to review this, but I guess the first time Yelper who gave it 5 stars (and gave it the wrong address) must either work there or be friends with the owner. Anyway.

Not sure why Yelp is not removing the 5 star reviews (that I've been flagging) from "yelpers" that have 1 review on Yelp. Its CLEARLY obvious they have ulterior motives and arent here to give you an accurate review.

If you give this place 5 stars, then stop writing reviews - cause you have the palate of a dung beetle.

Ok, first things first. Didn't really care for the pompous "bar rules" sayings I kept seeing on the bar and in the menu. "if you cant afford a tip, don't come to the bar - go to the liquor store". Really? Heres MY tip. If you depend on tips to pay your rent, then you should have reconsidered your career choice. Moving on.

The food. Lets start with the tartare. I think it was just raw hamburger meat (and you STILL couldn't get it right) with an egg on it. The potato chips to eat it with were a horrible idea also. If you need tips on what a good tartare should taste and look like, go to Stateside.

The wings; 9 wings for 12 bucks? For 12 bucks, give me a dozen wings - end of story. They didnt taste bad but weren't very memorable either.

The burger; 1/4 pound wafer sized patties? I could have gotten past that if the burger didnt just taste like a pile of grease and salt. I also opted to pay the 3 dollars for bacon, which somehow didnt find its way to my burger. My friend DID get his though and it was literally one piece of bacon cut in half.

The  beer; Selection was so-so. Second street Brew House blows it away though.

Service; Wasnt really "with a smile" and was spotty but given the experience with the food, it was about on par.

Theres honestly nothing here that would make me want to go back. I wanted to love it because I can walk there but there are many other places I'd go to before I ever went back here.

Side note; I keep hearing "the burger is good - try it!"

Listen people, if you're ANY kind of actual burger aficionado and have had burgers from Greys, Whiskey Village, Rouge and Royal Tavern, then this will be one of the worst burgers you've ever had in the city - TRUST ME!

And by the way, Brian, you forgot a category for the Industry buddy. How bout "I only have 50 reviews of places I have eaten but I think I know more than you, I call you poor but 50% of the posters on Yelp have eaten at better places than me and I'm insulting people for posting - the SAME exact negative things that I just posted about."

Thats pretty smart buddy. You really outfoxed the masses there chief.
Had pulled pork, ribs, amish sticky buns, molly beer!! There is so much to have that you can have a brain burst with so many flavors and food to choose!! A definite place to go!!

This was by far the highlight of my entire Philly experience. 

Really amazing, fresh food. So many stalls that I could eat here for days..

I'm still a bit partial to my Borough market in London, but this comes a close second in my favorite places to binge eat.

Fantastic market!! An absolute must when in Philly. I couldn't think of a comparison because it's got it's own feel. It was my first time here and I didn't have a list of what stands I wanted to try. It's fun that way because you get to explore more and surprise yourself with the different foods you find.

For the meat-eaters DEF try the fried chicken over at Keren Parker's friend chicken stand. It's the best fried chicken I ever had. And it's voted as the number one fried chicken by the Food Network. It's def true!

For dessert I stopped by Profis creperie and had the strawberry, blackberry cheesecake crepe with raspberry syrup. It was delicious! 

I didn't get to stop by Beilers Donuts. The line  is extremely long but apparently it moves quickly. You'll notice throughout the market everyone carrying boxes from this place. I am coming here the next time I am in Philly no matter what. You can smell the donuts from a distance.

This Center City (midtown) gem is the reason I moved to Washington Square West.  Not only do I go for my weekly groceries, but I go for the End-Of-Day cookie sales.  Take a stroll and just look at all the selections available.  30 types of jerky, shrimp the size of a baby's forearm, fudge to die for, etc.

I love you reading terminal, marry me?
Typical Farmers Market and Food Court. Avoid this place around lunch and on weekends...

I could easily give this 5 stars, but the day I went here the Amish were not and the continued whispers of "if only the Amish were here" were constant reminders that I am a tourist and that I was missing out on a lot of the charm and flavor they add to this tasty space.

The only other thing missing I felt was a hospital triage to help overeaters restart their hearts after sucking down Delilah's famous Oprah's heart winning mac n cheese or inhaling a Tommy Dinic masterpiece of slow cooked brisket wit provolone and peppers.

The only place i would skip would be the sushi joint...or just go sashimi style as the rice was tasteless and mushy and caused the only frown in the place.

Best visited in the off hours as the lunch rush lines can be too annoying, but it is a city of beautiful people and your chances of meeting a hottie lawyer increase...so just know what you're getting yourself into.

Awesome selection of foods, desserts, groceries, and everything else.
A must visit for those visiting Philadelphia and a good place to get not-as-standard souveniors/gifts. 

I really like the jambalaya here :)
I probably tried all of the dessert places and they're all quite good.

We usually go to RTM in Philly only when we have company from out of town. So, despite the sporadic visits - it never disappoints. Weekends are crowded but lively and friendly. It is great to be able to buy some fresh fish or meat, sample a few cheeses, and have a cheese steak there - all in the same stop. This is one place that most folks WISH they had near their home!

Overrated.  About 90% of the things sold here you can get around the corner from your house at the local grocers.  I was there Sat.  Very crowded.  People stepping on each other's toes.
  
Bassetts ice cream is very commercialized and run like the the local Wendy's, and not all it was cracked up to be.  This one of the reasons I chose to visit was because of all the hoopla I heard about Bassett's.  Two baby scoops of ice cream for $5.  Braums ice cream that I used to visit was 10x's better and much cheaper.  Ben and Jerry's tastes even better than this.  
 
Much of the cooked food here is over priced and underseasoned.  It reminded me of an upgraded mall Food Court.  

Parking was $8 for 2 hrs.  Driving around RTM is typical horrendous  hectic downtown driving.   

One of the few places that I did like was Herschels East side deli.  The roast and corned beef were worth the price, very tender and moist.  

At any rate, save yourself the hassle and gas.  Why fight your way thru a crowded food court for chicken, fish or ice cream when you can get that almost hassle free at the local grocers.  However, if you like crowds and ppl watching than this might be your thing.

I lived in Philadelphia for two years and this is by far my favorite part of the city. The market is extensive with dozens of food vendors and some craft items. My favorites include Beck's for their po boys, By Geroge for cheesesteaks, Sang Kee Peking Duck for peking duck spring rolls, and Beiler's for their apple fritters. You can spend hours in the market and find everything your stomach desires. I always brought visitors there and everyone loves it! I wish there was a reading terminal market in every city!

Wow. 5 star dining at 3 star prices. I had the Industry Burger...short rib/brisket blend with red onion, and cabot cheddar on a potato roll. One of the best burgers I've ever had. The ambience here was perfect...warm and friendly atmosphere. The service was impeccable. To top it off, they have a great beer menu, including my all time favorite the Paulaner Heff Weisse. Will definitely be coming back!

I'm biased... nothing can touch Pike Place market but this place is pretty awesome. I loved the produce shop in the back. They had great prices and the best part was the shelf full of bags of mixed produce that were all only $1!

I would honestly move to Philly just to be able to eat here regularly.  

It is a foodie's HEAVEN!  

I can't actually say much that hasn't been said before, but this place is amazing.  I loved all the fresh cheeses, honey and jam made by the Amish merchants.
Love this place.  If you can't find it here, you won't find it anywhere.  So many delicious options, it's nearly impossible to decide where to start.  Highly recommended.

Who needs those fancy "bulk up fast" products when you can just spend 30 minutes in Reading Terminal! I came out nearly 6 pounds heavier. If I can see these kinds of results, anyone can!

Believe in yourself.

Since we're visiting Philadelphia, Reading Terminal Market is on my list of places to visit.  I'm giving it 4 stars because there are so many shops I would like visit again.  We got the Reading Terminal Market around 10:45 on Saturday.  The food vendors were not very busy.  We did not have to wait at any of the three places we visited.  

We walked into and saw a lot of fresh produce with really great price.  Since we were hungry, we went to DiNic for the Roasted Pork Sandwich with cheese and green ($8.75) first.  We then found Delilah and got the Southern Fried Chicken, Mac n' Cheese and corn bread ($9.50), finished it off with Peanut Butter Swirl and Butter Pecan ice cream from Bassetts ($3.50).  The portions are pretty big here.  My husband and I shared everything and we were stuffed.

Roasted Pork sandwich from DiNic was good with the Sharp Provolone.  My husband enjoyed the pickled yellow pepper on the counter with his half of the sandwich.  We did not like the food at Delilah at all.    The chicken was juicy, but had no flavor.  The skin was crunchy, but had a slightly burn taste.  The mac n' cheese was soggy and lumpy.  The corn bread was dry.  Ice cream from Bassett's was good, but we didn't think it was really special.  

After we walked around for a bit, we got some nectarine for 99 cents a pound.  It was fresh, sweet and juicy, best thing we had all day.

Saturday's are the best at Reading Terminal Market, great good variety, great energy and a ton of happy people....basically it's good food, family, fun vibe, even though it's with people you've never met.

My favorite items on the menu to date include: fried green tomatoes, homemade beans with pulled pork and their burger! Happy hour is great here and brunch on the weekends isn't bad at all. The beer selection is big and doesn't dissapoint. Never a wait and service is fast!

Best Market in Town! Tons of places to explore and get local fresh produce, cheeses, meats, totally love the fresh sausage places.

Some places are expensive, so browse around and you can find good deals. The vendors are super friendly. Not the cleanest place in the common eating area, but it gets a ton of traffic. 

The Spices/Nut shop is the BOMB for loose by the pound spices. I will never pay full grovery store price for spices again. I got a HUGE handful of bay leaves for $1. Compare that to 10 leaves for $6.99 and it doesnt take a rocket scientist to figure out where to go in the future for spices! 

Must stops are the Beiber's donut place, and the Olive Oil/Balasmic Vinegar vendor. So many gems in there. 

Closes earlier -- not open late at night!

This is by far the worst Popeyes I have visited. I bought a 6 piece chicken tender combo,there weren't too many choices at 1:30 in the afternoon, go figure. I got three whole tenders and three small broken pieces that didn't amount to a tender, about small amount of fries dried out by the heat lamp and a small broken biscuit. To say I was disappointed is an understatement, especially since I didn't have time to return it  once I opened the box

What more could one ask for?  Every kind of food purveyor under one roof centrally located in the middle of Center City .  Was probably ore of a kick before the fixed the place up and tourists make it a stop but its still a great place to eat and shop.  You have to have a smile on your face when you come out.
Talk about a smorgasbord of GOOD EATS! From fresh seafood, to classic philly cheesesteaks, ice cream made in-house, and dangerously fresh cookies, there is no way you will leave hungry!

Other reviews here seem to be lumped into a few categories.  

First, the "oh it's not the Witch so I don't like it group".  If the Witch was so great why did it go out of business?  

Next, the "oh the burger here isn't very good" group.  Ordering a burger here is like getting a Bud from Monk's and complaining that it wasn't served at the proper temperature the commercials tell you it should be served.  Go outside your comfort zone a little bit and try something new.  If you want a burger go to one of the crap corner bars on Two Street.  That's not what this place is for.  Please do NOT add a chicken or roast beef sandwich to the menu.  Stay different.

Last, the "oh this place is 'obnoxious' with their prices" group.  You are at the very least poor and should not be dining out.  Since you utilize Yelp I assume you have an internet connection, whereon The Industry has a website with all prices listed You must be oblivious as well.  Again, if you want 25 cent wings go to Dee's Place or one of the dive bars a block over.  This is not the place for you.

Now to the review.  Drinks.  Started with the Pennsport Fizz and was underwhelmed.  Didn't seem particularly strong as others suggested, lacked much flavor or anything at all.  Nothing I'd order again.  Had the Brotherly Suds collaboration beer next.  Was quite good, which I'd expect for a beer that was apparently worked on by every brewer in the Greater Philadelphia region.  Overall the drink selection is very good, and a reason to come back.

Now to the food.  Overall it was a disappointment.  As previously stated I love that they had the balls to put new things on the menu despite the obvious distaste for adventure by many of the neighborhood denizens.  BTW I live three blocks away, so I'm not some Center City slicker rolling up thinking I'm all high and mighty here.  

We started with the pork nuggets and crispy pig ear lettuce wraps (imagine such a thing!).  Great ideas, but poorly executed.  Now I love Frank's Red Hot.  I put that shit on everything, as they say.  But the pig ears, as well as the guinea hen I had later were way too heavy on the stuff.  Masked every other flavor.  When I had a piece of either that somehow eluded the spice they were very good.  Pump the breaks on the Frank's, you guys.

We had the guinea hen, like stated, as an entree as well as the veggie fritters.  Guinea hen was a sizable portion of meat virtually indistinguishable from chicken except for it's shape and size.  What skin I could taste other than Frank's was crispy and very good.  Too bad I couldn't taste much of it under a sea of orange sauce.  Meat was a bit dry but not off-putting.  Accompanying Mexican street corn was interesting and something I'd eat again though.  Fritters were dry but the arugula pesto and leftover Frank's in moderation helped.  Nothing we'd order again.

Interior was nice, service was good so no complaints there.  Just gets two stars removed because of the over-abundance of Frank's on the pig ears and guinea hen and because nothing really stood out here, although I will return to try more options here since this seems to be the best neighborhood option at the moment above For Pete's Sake and Ugly American.  At least it's different.  Different is good.  Embrace it.

Went to the Industry yesterday for my first time.  Was OK.  Wanted to try it since I heard it was pretty good, and my friends are regulars there since they live close by.  We sat outside for a round of beers.  It was Philly beer week, so they were doing a tap takeover of Colorado beers.  Pretty decent.  Our server had slim to none personality but she was attentive and we didn't wait long for service, so that was good.  We closed out and sat inside the bar to be in the A/C, and closer to the bartenders since our friends knew him well.  The 2nd round of drinks by the same waitress, even though we moved inside.  The place was empty, so not surprised she was like the only server.  She let us sample a few beers which was nice.  Although none of the beers were that great, they were OK.  

Food, we had pulled pork bbq sandwhich, that was really good.  Comes with thin cut shoestring fries.  We also had the mac-n-cheese balls, which were bland and not very cheezy.  Was expecting more cheese.   Lastly, had a chocolate n peanut butter cake dessert, which a different server said was amazing.... I disagree.  My friends and I both thought the cake was dry and flavor-less, and there wasn't much to it.  Overall, the place is OK, but food was not as good as many other gastropubs in the area.
We took a stroll here before running Philadelphia's marathon! You can find everything here! Awesome market with great vibe! Everyone should explore this place when in Philadelphia!

I LOVE THIS PLACE!!!

So many selections and all such great food and at great prices.

My friend and I came back here just to visit the Flying Monkey Bakery! YUMMMM

There are tons of seating and it wasn't difficult to find a spot considering there are TONS of people in there. It's packed, but the wait isn't long at any of the stands.

Reading Terminal Market is a food lovers dream! I would venture to say, this puts Quincy Market to shame. Do not leave Philly without stopping here for a meal. It can be a very overwhelming place, but I find it helps to go in with a plan or at least some idea of the places you want to try. I did some research and decided to go with:

- DiNic's for the classic roast pork sandwich. This was excellent! You can go with or without the rabe... I might go without next time because it can be a bit overpowering and mask some of the more subtle flavors of the pork and provolone. 

-Termini Bros Cannoli - Really good! A nice crisp shell, that somehow had a lightness to it. The cream was mild, with a very subtle tang and a hint of cinnamon throughout. It was not too sweet and you could actually taste the ricotta. which I appreciated. 

- Famous 4th St. Cookies - This was the only disappointing place to me. The cookie I tasted reminded me too much of Pepperidge Farms.

- The Dutch Eating Place - This was pretty good. Everyone seems to order the Hot Turkey, which I would love to try next time. We got the sloppy joe, just for the sake of nostalgia! I also tried  shoo fly pie for the first time. This came from Pennsylvania Dutch next door. 

Also consider trying the Peking Duck place. It had great reviews, but we just couldn't eat another thing. Reading Terminal is also a Farmer's Market, so you can purchase grocery items and homemade treats to bring home with you.

Enjoy!

Visiting from NYC, definitely enjoyed the vibe and ethnic variety of this super busy gourmet food market. All your food craves can basically be satisfied at this one stop shop and it's conveniently located just a block from our Loews Hotel. Would love to come back.

READING TERMINAL MARKET IS AMAZING!!! Its been there atleast since the early 1900s and you can find EVERYTHING there!! There's chinese places, french places, bakeries, candy shop, meat shops/butcher shops,  I LOVE IT!!! I've only been there once but I'll be going there a lot more in the years to come. 
    i HIGHLY reccommend anyone to go there... as long as you can deal with crowds..

WOW!!! this place has it all foods from all over the place true Cajun foods with gator meat and whole ducks and produce and shopping why go anywhere else when all the fun is here at Reeding? the gals and I has a blast shopping and tasting all kinds of yummy foods. there was one down fall a few of the vendors only took cash so there was an atm there to extract cash but of course there was a fee... I could have gotten my sweets with that fee and the other down fall was the one place I went to try a philly cheese steak was awful and there was no extras like pickles there was a little entertainment there when we went on Feb 21-22 and that was neat but steer clear of the attitudes some of the vendors have all in all a fun place to spend a day
This place is bomb. I got the donuts from the Amish stand in the one corner and WHOA. Real tasty.

This has got to be one of the great jewels of Philadelphia. I have friends who live in the Midwest, and they insist Philadelphia is absolutely the best convention town. Why? Because of the Reading Terminal Market. In other cities, to get lunch, you have to walk a distance and generally end up eating in hotels with overpriced and pretty ordinary food. The Reading Terrminal Market is just next-door to the convention center, and it offers and astonishing array of wonderful food. From Philly's renowned cheesesteak to Thai food to Lebanese food to Chinese food to German food. Pretty amazing. We go there every week. The problem is so do a lot of other people. We used to go regularly on Saturdays, but it got too crowded. Now we go on Fridays, and Fridays is getting too crowded. Maybe Thursdays?

Got the paneer Masala Kati roll today for delivery and a mango lassi. It was really good! I'm indian so I didn't expect it to taste that authentic but it was beyond my expectations and the lassi has the perfect amount  of sweetness! I'll order again!
I LOVE visiting this place when I'm back home in Philly.  Make sure to try locally produced yummies you haven't tried before.  I've never been disappointed!
Returned here while on jury duty a few weeks ago, still a great unique place with so many choices. It's pretty crowded in the summer, but you can handle it.

My new favorite find in Philly! This place is full of all types of food vendors, bookstores, jewelry and craft shops, fresh local produce, honey and preserves, desserts, ice cream, bread, fresh seafood, and tons more. I wish I could've had more time and tummy space to sample everything!! And I loved how it feels like a real local market right in the middle of downtown.

This place is the most wonderful and most dangerous place ever. It's literally a mall of food. You can do your grocery shopping here (produce is usually pretty cheap), get a fantastic bread and cheese pairing, and some crazy good (and good quality) meats and go home and make a great dinner for yourself. 

Be wary though, you will want to buy everything because everything in this place is wonderful--keep your wallet in the hands of another. I recommend the reuben sandwich at Hershel's (I get it with pastrami), also some local Amish dessert breads, and there's a great cheese selection.

Oh my gosh. The selections. This place is very very packed on the weekends. If you have kids, it might be a little troublesome getting everyone corralled together. Seating is really limited, but that goes with the atmosphere of the place. So many little food places. Almost any type of food is there. I've been a couple of times now and it's all delicious. Just don't be in a hurry.

Reading Terminal Market, I confess my love for you! 

I remember the first time I came to the market. It was overwhelming and honestly one of the most exciting food experiences in Philly! The options are endless! I couldn't decide on one thing to eat and the beautiful part was that I didn't have to choose just one spot for lunch. You can have Greek food with Indian side dishes, Italian food with German accents! The options are actually endless. I still haven't worked my way through all of the stands, though this is a challenge I gladly accept. 

One thing to note is that the Pennsylvania Dutch run stands are closed on Sundays (I know it's heartbreaking.... Don't show up on Sunday expecting to have a big Dutch Eating Place breakfast with pancakes, french toast, and ahhhhhh my mouth is watering just thinking about it). 

The real tragedy is that I live in Washington, D.C.... However, I'm up in Philly almost every other weekend and you bet that I go to Reading Terminal at least once per weekend. If you live in Philadelphia and don't go to the market then you, my friend, are missing out!

Mostly I love RTM for Iovine's and L. Halteman's meat selection.

I would give five stars if every food stand was amazing, but unfortunately most are ok-to-good. The Down Home Diner is a decent spot for breakfast, you can never go wrong with the Dutch Eating Counter, and Dinic's roast pork sandwich is pretty amazing. The cookbook store is always worth a stop if you enjoy cooking, and be sure to get yourself a 4th Street Cookie, a Beiler's donut, and some Bassett's for dessert. You piggy, you.

Don't know what kind of "mood" you're in? Just take a stroll through this classic Philadelphia market. Japanese, BBQ, Amish, Jewish Deli, American, Indian... you can't possibly leave here unsatisfied. 

This is one of the go-to places I like to take guests from outside of the city, there's really something for any taste pallet!

you really cannot lose with Reading Terminal.  the options are vast; everyone can find anything.  my personal faves are: the Thai spot for their salmon &get the sesame ginger glaze instead of the traditional sauce.  you're welcome *wink wink*  .. shanghai gourmet makes the best rice noodle soup.  veggies always fresh &delicious.  brilliant broth !! .. kevin parker's spot is a little above average.  expensive as all get out, but it's always nice to have a good downhome soulfood option on site..   the amish are fantastic, no matter what you order, but make sure you go on the right day to catch them. i like the amish diner.  their turkey burgers are not the biggest but are thee most delicious.. gotta love termini bros and their canolis. simply YUM !!.. there's a chinese place that's located in the 2nd or 3rd isle if you are entering from the 12th st side, and they make wonderful chicken dumplings.. and i'll end it w/ franks-a-lot (i think that's the name).  anywayz, i dont eat franks, but their bbq chicken wings are fabulous.  charcoaled to perfection.  grab a cornbread too -- DEELISH !!

Had a great time there!! I took my three daughters down there over spring break in April, 2015. It was definitely worth the trip.  

Enjoyed seeing all of the local favorites and seeing what the excitement was all about.  It's not as big a place as the open-air market in Baltimore, but it's still a great deal of fun.  The ice-cream place down in front is wonderful. They do a local blueberry ice cream that is to die for.

Make this a definite place to stop (after seeing the Wannamaker organ) when you're in Philadelphia. You won't regret it.

Reading Terminal Market is a great way to get any type of food you want in one location. It is great for groups that want different things. Their is plenty of affordable food with such a variety that is hard to match. I recommend Dutch Bros Company for breakfast which the best seasonal Pumpkin pancakes.

I always get the Wreck Salad with the non-fat vinaigrette dressing--I don't know what they put in the dressing but it's delicious. I always get extra on the side.

As far as price goes, I can't comment on the sandwiches, but $5 and change for a salad isn't bad in my opinion.  Plus they're big.  I'm always full after eating one.

The drink selection is also good--I happen to love cream soda and black cherry soda and they stock both of them.  Their milkshakes are also good.

Finally, the staff are always extremely pleasant to deal with.  It's nice to have such positive interactions with them despite the restaurant being packed and the line out the door.

This place is great. There is something for everyone here. We were able to get a taste of Philly here for lunch and dessert. Oh, and, maybe we were sheltered by where we were staying (Home 2 Suites) across the street and waking between our hotel, downtown and Independence Mall, and South street for cheesesteaks but the people of Philly are great. Yeah it's like other urban areas but everyone has been friendly and helpful. One On vacation just has to put things in perspective. Don't be a hindrance to those on their way to work. We are on vacation and they are not in a rush so we don't get in the way. I like the city of Brotherly Love and this their treasure the Market is awesome. It is a must visit at least to see where National Treasure was filmed.

This is the real thing! Not a tourist place like Faneuil Hall in Boston with its national chain stores like Sunglass hut, but a larger, 100% local, fantastic food experience in the Reading Train Shed (think the original Monopoly game).  REAL PHILADELPHIANS use this place, too. It's not just for tourists. And, its right next to a fantastic Chinatown.

Of course, tourists should also cross over to the west side of Center City, walk around Rittenhouse and Fitler Square, and along the Schuylkill River, but this is still a great place.

Dont go to this place hungry... you will walk in circles, soooo many choices! You are likely to over eat, but not like thats a bad thing. Pastrami sandwiches stacked to the ceiling! This place is the real deal for anything fresh! Recommended to all that visit Philadelphia

The smells alone are worth coming here, but don't just settle for that.  Go with a group and order a bunch of different things so as to get the full RTM experience or just be greedy and gorge yourself on all the treats.  There is a reason that travel/food/cooking shows come here - it is part of the identity of Philadelphia even more so than the cheesesteak itself.

There are so many reviews that it is hard to add to the conversation without repeating myself, so I will just stick to the sweet stuff.  Flying Monkey Bakery is one of my faves and has boozey desserts, which let's be honest, is one of the best combo's around.  Bassett's ice cream is some of the better icecream this city has to offer- plus with their local inspired flavors (WHYY Experience, Gadzooks, etc) you know that they are as integrated in this town as RTM itself. Hope's Cookies are chewy goodness.  There are also a bunch of old timey candy vendors and hand made chocolates.  See that is the thing with RTM, for as many times as I have been there, it is hard for me to get to all the vendors.  They need a punch card so you know which ones you have tried and which are still on the list.

This place is incredible. The variety of choices is absolutely stunning and the people watching can't be beat. We had a delicious Philly cheesesteak sandwich (first time) for lunch. It totally lived up to its reputation. We bought four turkey sandwiches for a picnic on the way home...marvelous.  What a unique treasure this market place is. Bravo for Philadelphia for sustaining this treasure.

If you are hungry and not sure what you want to eat, this is the place to visit. There are so many food stands to choose from it is hard to make a choice! Our group opted for the homemade PA Dutch Chicken Pot Pie, Sausaage, Peppers, and Onions Sandwiches, and Beef Jerky. We went on a Saturday and we had a small problem of trying to find somewhere to sit to enjoy or food. There was seating, but not enough to handle the large crowd.

The Cheesesteak counter and the pulled pork counter were by far the busiest in the whole building. The lines wrapped around the aisle and snaked to the next. 

They have it all...hot, cold, fresh, and dried! So much to see and smell! Taking a shopping bag would be helpful if you would like to take some tasty treats home. 

This would be a fun place to take the train downtown to visit!

Make sure to go hungry!

Only thing in Philly worth seeing. It is amazing and I want one in my town. Has everything, beef, pork, seafood of every kind, chicken, ice cream , veg, fruit, pastries, candy, drinks eating spots, you name it it there. Not in a Wal Mart form either.

Its just a must see in a disappointing town. I was in town for about 4 days and spent a good majority of it at RTM.

Whether it's your first time or twentieth time, you have to go to the Reading Terminal Market.  It's Historic and has many vendors, including American or International food, meats and seafood, produce.  They even give you a parking voucher to lot across the street. It's located across the street from the Convention Center.

This market is awesome! A little pricey, but you get what you pay for. Foods are fresh and tasty. You can also shop for everything from small souvenir magnets to handmade crafts and textiles from other countries!

Went here back in July of 2013.  A verylarge selection of diverse food.  I got the Samosas.  Very light and very tasty.  
I noticed that all of the prices in the Terminal were very reasonable.  There is also a very popular area with Amish baked goods.

This is a much needed and great addition to the area. I have been here twice now since it opened. Once late night for drinks only, and once early for dinner.  The night I was there for drinks, it was quite loud, but not unbearable. The service (even for the 2nd night) was fast and friendly and the beer selection was great. The cocktails seem fun too, but that's not my bag.  I enjoyed being able to the a beer on engine, a nice draft craft and if I wanted a can of PBR. 

When I returned for dinner later in the weekend, the joint was busy, but not late night crazy and the sound was much more managable. The service was fast, friendly and enjoyable. My companion and I ordered the pork nuggets, which we loved. I had the pulled BBQ duck and he the burger. Both were great, I really enjoyed my sandwich. 

I moonlight as a bartendar and while I won't need to use the Industry late happy hours or staff meals, I think it's a great idea and fun. I can't wait to come back to try brunch and more food over time.

Side comment: For those of you who can't take the industry jokes on the cards and whatnot, grow up. Or, go to the liquor store.

You can find just about anything to eat in this place. From Amish products to fried onion rings! 

They had so much I tried nothing lol. I felt a bit overwhelmed and being in a diet doesn't help! They had some yummy looking donuts that I wanted to buy :( but didn't. The bad part about this place is the parking and sitting! 

Oh boy, it's a race to get a table with chair. This place is on the middle of China town and the penn station. 

It's a must stop in your tour of Philly!

I was misled by other reviewers who compared their MK special platter and chicken and lamb platter to Halal Guys in NYC.  I was expecting Halal Guys and got something quite different so I was disappointed. 

MK special Platter: I would not get this again. I agree with other reviewers that the white sauce helps with the flavor but overall it is not as flavorful as Halal Guys. The rice is just unseasoned plain rice.  It comes with a little bit of salad, but not sauteed onions and tomatoes like Halal Guys.  Same goes for the chicken and lamb platter below

Chicken and Lamb platter: I would not get this again

Paneer Masala kati roll: From now on I will stick to their kati rolls.  This was very flavorful and I topped it off with some white sauce.  It is on the smaller side so maybe I will order two for dinner next time.

So many choices!  All excellent.  If you're in the mood for baked goods, you have to go to Beiler's - they have the absolute best fritters and donuts and all kinds of wonderful, delicious baked goods.  THE BEST!

I am in philly for 2 days for a work conference and was walking around with a coworker when we stumbled upon this gem. It may not look at big from the outside but once you walk in..it's like a whole different world. There are over 70+ vendors and they have everything between deli meats, steak cuts (like a million kinds), fish market, every kind of food place you can think of and even little shops that sell just about anything! Love this place!

This place is honestly a foodie's heaven. Any type of food you want, restaurants, take-out, and markets, and all reasonably priced. The Tubby Olive has amazing Olive Oils and Balsamic Vinegars (the best is the dark chocolate balsamic vinegar). There is a donut place towards the back (I can't remember the name) that has the most amazing PB&J donut. All I can say is that when you are in Philly, make sure you don't miss this stop!!!

What's not to love. Not exactly a take-a-date kind of place but definately worthy of taking a date to Bassets! Best homeade icecream EVER. Only good,quality stuff at the market. Of course you could find thing cheaper but not fresher or better. Love this place for the nuts and ice cream. The chocolates are fantastic too. Oh and the donuts...what can I say? We do go here from time to time just for the occassional treat but we've had lunch here too and it's just so darn good. A must see if you're just passing by...worth the time to browse around.

It's touristy, crowded and loud and always seems to have a different foul odor every time you turn the corner, but somewhere in that indoor maze is a place called OK Produce that sells produce that are literally just that - okay (as in overly ripe and a little funky) for super cheap. I left with two brown bags filled to the brim for a mere 8 bucks. Don't know what I'm going to do with 5 lbs of poblano peppers so now it's time to get creative in the kitchen.

For those who have visited Pike Place in Seattle or the Ferry Building in San Francisco, this is Philadelphia's version of an indoor market place in/near the city's downtown area. Having said that, it is quite touristy. 

Visited Sunday and Monday and several shops that we read about on yelp were not open. :/ Not sure if the winter storm had to do with the closures on those days but was a little disappointing.

Parking garage across the street is $4 for two hours if you buy something over $10 at Reading Terminal. Probably the cheapest garage in Philadelphia's city center.

Foodies dream!!!!  Food! Food! Food!  Mostly foods
Location is very central surrounds by hotels & restaurants

Walking in the Reading Terminal overall is an overwhelming experience but once you get your bearings right and focus, smelled and taste amazing different kinds of foods! From hoagies to Italian to Chinese to cheeses teaks to halal to Mexican; all is represented! The fresh meat, cheese, produce, seafood...!!!!

The place is crowded & noisy as massive amount of tourists and Philadelphia's. Difficult to find parking space

The donuts place is a cool stop, they make different pastries. An unexpected highlight was the infused olive oil and vinegar spot-- you should  try everything.

The Amish merchants make donuts & fresh baked cinnamon rolls? Smoothies make with fresh fruits from the farmers market.

Should try Philly Cheese steaks, Salami, Beef Prosciutto, Pickled veggies
DiNic's is one of my favorite sandwiches in the world, warm Pretzels &
Chicken wings with different flavors.

Definitely a good way to spend a few hours
Perfect place for tourists and locals to hang out!!!!!
What's not to love about this place???!!! Some stands can be a little pricey for what they're serving, and the crowds can be overwhelming, but even when it's crowded, it's still worth the trip.

A must see when visiting Philly.. It has everything from wood earrings to kitchen seasonings. Its a good mixture of vendors with all the foods you can think of. I was able to have coffee, a rib lunch and take home a bag of loose tea leaves and seasonings.. I could have also picked up my fresh fruits, meats and breads if i wanted. Be sure to stop in take a walk around and see what you can discover.

Pretty awesome place the other reviews did a great job of summing it up. It's a huge market with food, groceries and other cool stuff. It's pretty easy to get lost so if you see a place that you like and want to come back to it later because first you want to look around, I suggest you just eat there first because you're probably not going to find it. Or it will take you some time. A long time. Reading Terminal Market is definitely a must see attraction in Philadelphia. It's pretty amazing. However, if you're someone like me you can get pretty over whelmed with the plethora of options and lose your appetite or simply get fustrated and go to Panera down the street. My best advice to the indecisive people like me is to know what you want before you get in there. Seriously. Before you enter decided on what you want to eat. Do you want American or Chinese ? Sweet or salty? Trust me. I'm helping you out. Also make sure you have CASH! It's just a lot more convenient. Happy feasting

Fun place to walk around and explore. There's tons of interesting shops and plenty of restaurants too. We had a great time sampling cheese, chocolates, etc, many of which were very good. 

Families be warned though, this place is routinely packed and while the atmosphere is bustling and fun, it's not an amazing experience when visiting with small kids. The aisles are jammed up, there's almost no seating in the dining area and the bathroom facilities were disgusting. 

Also, I would recommend Yelping up your lunch choice before ordering. We assumed any choice would be a good one since this is a well known food location, but we wound up with some very sub par Chinese food. 

In the end, definitely stop in for a visit if you're in the area. It's definitely a good way to spend a few hours. Just leave the kids with a babysitter!

What happened? My favorite local bar/restaurant had a really Bad Night!
 And my companion was a chef from LA. We couldn't have been more disappointed - especially since I gave it such high marks prior to our lousy experience. 
Drinks were blah, watered down & tasteless; fried deviled eggs were slimy with way too much truffle oil: fish and chips had two teeny tiny pieces of fish cooked just right alongside a huge pile of undercooked fries. Watermelon salad was overdressed with barely any feta and the watermelon was maybe a day too old... I could go on....nothing was good or prepared well.

Wendy's has a sign on the front door that says open at6 am every day, when in actuality they don't open until 7:30 am when I question the young lady (manager) , she proceeded by addressing me as " YO" so I mentioned to her that the staff from McDonald's are in need of jobs due to they're resent closing, she says look"YO" I'm in here with one other person and were trying to get this" Jawn" opened,  Now what I'm complaining for is because all of the people that go to work and need to be in early are expecting Wendy's to be open so that they can purchase they're breakfast and get on they're bus, Wendy's is losing a awful lot of business due to the shortness of staff at this store. And there is older white woman at the register taking orders, she has the worst attitude that I've ever experienced and I've been in the resteraunt business all of my life, I wonder if she knows that when you work with the public, you should always smile and have a happy go lucky attitude!!! 
                Just saying,
             Theresa Ciarrocchi
       Thank you!!

Whenever we are in Philly this is a must stop. We always go to Dinic's which has hands down the best sandwiches I have ever had in my life and we also have Bassets Ice cream. Oh lord fatty ice cream heaven. If you get your parking ticket stamped by any vender in the terminal you only pay $2 for 2 hours. Great deal! Love this place!

horrible. rude customer service. i told this lady to leave half of my order without certain ingredients and she didn't listen at all and hit me with a "i didn't understand what you said", walked away, and still charged me for it -- wth ??????

If you can't find something here that suits your appetite then you should stop looking. Can be a bit of a tourist trap - best on weekdays when there is no convention in town. Great produce from Iovine's, DeNic's Roast Pork was rated best sandwich in America, Termini Brothers Cannoli..but my personal favorite: The Herschel's Special - House-made pastrami on rye with coleslaw and thousand island. Actually, I am done writing this. My mouth is literally watering and I am headed to get one. You should too.
I love this place!  Whatever your palate desires, you can find it here.  Even fresh produce.

I love this market, I have been there 10 or 15 times, every time I go there is a new shop I am always surprised. You can go to buy fresh produce, aged cheese, or even dinner. There are fancy chocolate stores, bakeries and an iced cream. You can get just about anything and its all home made.

Really enjoyed the dumplings!   We first discovered HD at the Italian festival last year.   This new location is a welcome addition to the neighborhood.  We had Buffalo chicken, cheesteak, and roasted pork dumplings.   Fried perfectly and delicious!  5 for $7 is a good value.  This is not an Asian dumpling restaurant.  The dumplings are in a different class than steamed dumplings.  Fried, tasty, Philly goodness!  Enjoy!
This was in my rice bowl. The nut that's in the middle of an avocado. This shows the workers are not careful.

The reading terminal market has a little bit of something for everyone. They have a variety of cuisines, great food options - Greek, Mediterranian, Indian, Asian, American, etc. You can shop for knick-knacks, keepsakes, jewelry, groceries, etc. Have a drink. I like this place a lot. The only reason I am not giving it a 5star is because it closes too soon 6:00PM? Wish it was open for dinner.

A friend and I went to Industry tonight for their Burgers and Bubbles special. We also came during happy hour and took advantage of those specials as well. To start, the ambiance was great. A nice rustic bar feel. Not a huge restaurant but a good comfortable size that I'm sure fills up on the weekends. 

Now onto the food. We started with the Mac and Cheese Croquettes that are $1 during happy hour. They are basically just friends balls of Mac and cheese. They don't sound super exciting but they were absolutely delicious. Perfectly fried and the sauce that came with them was delicious. We also split the Kimchee tot appetizer. They were also great with a nice crunchy outside and a creamy delicious center. For our entrees we both got the Monday Mystery Burger -- it had caramelized onions, fried pickles, dijonnaise and Swiss. The burger was smaller than you usually expect from a restaurant (they always seem so monstrous!) but it was the perfect size and to die for. Best part of all ALL of this food only cost $36 (including two sparkling wines). 

All in all I thought this place was great. I will definitely be back (especially for their Monday burger deals!)

Worst experience ever!!! Really bad service! Saw his older lady being really mean to the customers. When it was my turn, she threw away my receipt to the trash by mistake. When I requested my receipt, she picked it up from the dirty trash wet with liquid to me. I asked her whether she can reprint. She refused and later handed me another receipt that was not even mine, which I can't use for company reimbursement. Terrible service! Will not be back.

It's my favorite place to eat in Philadelphia. Tootsies kale salad is so good. Bassetts Ice Cream is so good. Bielers Donuts, so good. Every food stall is so good. Get the roasted chicken from one of the Amish stalls. Ok Produce has good deals on ripe, ready to eat/cook fruits and veggies. Iovine Brothers is fresher and has more selection. I absolute adore Reading Terminal Market!!

I love going to food markets, such as this one because I feel there are so many hidden gems in every corner. Back in NY, I really adore Essex Street Market and Chelsea Market, but this one was even better! There were so many vendors and different foods to choose from. The different aroma from fresh seafood to pizza to brisket sandwiches just filled the air and left me salivating each time I turned the corner.

This market was pretty packed on a weekend, yet still very spacious. I loved how there's many seating areas throughout the market. The New Yorker in me wished this market would stay open around dinner time and open on Sundays as well. Nonetheless, I know I will return!

This historic market is one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. I bring all my friends who visit me here. This place is just oozing with culture and what it really means to be a Philadelphian. It's a great place for locals to shop, eat, visit, and hang out. For visitors/tourists, you cannot visit Philadelphia and skip out on Reading Terminal Market. You will not regret your time here.

Reading Terminal Market is a Philadelphia landmark and is a must-see place containing lots of eateries, butcheries and produce vendors.  I don't particularly find the prices appealing but it is cool to check out from time-to-time.  The Market is under new management and they are constantly trying to upgrade the vendors and services, so things look promising.  Avoid this place at all costs if you have a hangover - the zig-zagging of people will make you crazy!

So much food! The sub shop has a special spread for their Italian subs that is amazing. The different meats you can buy here are great. Whenever I leave I usually take a load of cheeses and racks of ribs with me. It's always a treat when I can get here.
Best place to eat lunch, shop for dinner, and buy local gifts. Been a patron there since the mid-80s. Go there!!!

Fun place. It's packed with people, so you have to like that kind of thing. I only had time to stop at one place and got a Philly cheesesteak, so I will be back to grab some produce, ice cream, donuts, pretzels...

A Philly landmark.  A tourist must-see.  Yet nothing is overhyped or overpriced about Reading Terminal.  I tend to waste too much time looking at all the options - the trick is you can't make a wrong choice and everything is priced around the same point.

We had a chance to visit this food and craft building while on an overnight visit to Philly.    On a recommendation from our hotel desk mgr, we ventured off to find the 'famous' Philly Cheese Steak.   The market place houses many 'amish' vendors selling breads, baked goods, home made jams, kettle corn, and almost everything that you can pickle.   The rest of the market place is home to many food vendors and other crafty type goods.    Note:  be sure to check the hours(opening/closing).   On a Sunday, a lot of the places don't open until past 9am and some places are not even open on Sunday.

I was not prepared for just how amazing this place is. My friend warned me but I expected mostly fresh produce and meat stands like I guess, not the culinary hodgepodge that this place was. This was one of my favorite places in Philly. They have every cuisine imaginable. I wish I had one more day to my trip to eat my way through the market. I unfortunately didn't get to try a whole lot because I couldn't get past the cheese steaks! This place is a true gem and no tourist should miss it. So happy it was across the street from my hotel.
Love the variety of stores and atmosphere! Great place for fresh produce.

I love coming here, but I prefer going alone since it's so noisy and packed! There are merchants selling anything you could think of! I love the Head Nut, I buy loose tea there frequently and there is such a large selection, at a good price! Iovine bros is great for a fresh selection of produce. The breakfast wraps at Smuckers are delicious! I love it all!

This place is a Philadelphia institution but unlike Pat's and Geno's this institution is well worth the visit.  They have everything you could ever want.  

Downside:
Unless you love an insane amount of people I'd stay away on Sundays.

Just to bask in the authenticity of this "ode to joy" in downtown Philly is worth the trip. Luckily I get to visit while also seeing my family. We can make it an all day eating affair that borders gastrointestinal danger and delight. The danger is in visiting , buying and eating food from so many different purveyors the delight is also in visiting, buying and eating food from so many purveyors. 
Sausage sandwiches , soul food , Rocco's king of hoagies , seafood, beef, chicken, pork all done in in a rather authentic Philly kinda way.  The Terminal market is one of the gems of the culinary world, blows away the ferry plaza in SF(not for gourmet food but for real food) and delivers great family memories. 
I will never forget the faces that walk by  as I last ate a  sausage sandwich. infact , I will never forget the sausage sandwhich. I heart reading terminal.

When I pop into Reading, I primarily stick to one corner, which has Iovine Brothers Produce and Giunta's Prime Shop.  These two stores can supply about 80% of my grocery needs each week for prices that continue to surprise me ("Really? $11 for this whole bag of produce??").  Overall, I'm happy to frequent these sellers for the great prices, awesome selection, and helpful, nice employees.  

However, the hours can be a bust:  closing at 6pm means I'm rushing in from the trolley stop after work and doing a mad dash for those one or two extra necessities for my dinner recipe. I think it's usually worth it though.  The yellow plums I got last week were divine.
One of my favorite lunch places. $5 shrimp pad thai? Can't beat it.

I do 90% of all of my grocery shopping here.  There is something here for everyone!  From the fresh produce, numerous fish mongers, 4 or 5 butcher shops.  There are also a large number restaurants within.  Head here for the best Reuben of your life!  Wonderful new place that sells fresh mozzarella made on site.  I could go on for days about Reading Terminal Market.  Do yourself a favor and check this place out!  For foodie folks in from out of town this is  a must!

Variety is the spice of life. If you're into food, and not sure what you want, definitely come here. It's hard to choose from all of the eateries in this one location. The only issue here is having too many options!

I love this market.  I do the majority of my grocery shopping here and love the quality and variety of fresh fruits and vegetables, seafood, meats, and cheeses.  On Sundays and Wednesdays, students can get 10% off at some places.  However, if shopping on Sunday, beware that a number of stalls will be closed.  It does get very crowded on the weekends, but if you go in the morning you can beat the lunchtime rush.  There are several diner-type stalls that cook up a fantastic breakfast!

Best Place in CC to buy fresh produce. I have yet to be disappointed with Iovines prices or Produce. Great charcuteries and cheese mongers nearby and the butchers are not as good as the italian market but at the same time who always has time to head down ninth street for a cut of lamb

I absolutely love this place!!! This place is so unique that everyone who comes to Philly should at least visit reading terminal. I go here for lunch almost every other day. Some of the food stands can get kind of expensive but its totally worth it! Don't forget to go to Dinics and get some Ice cream at Bassetts!

Stopped in here today as we were walking around Queen Village. Bright and creative space to which we were welcomed by counter person Mya and Church (?). the cook. We had steamed Asian pork dumplings and as an indulgence, fried Shrimp and Grits dumplings. Both were very tasty, but I think I liked the Asian pork best, perhaps because they were steamed which made them delightfully chewy.  
Shrimp and grits took me back to my youth in the south and my Grandma's shrimp and grits. We will be back to try the salads and noodle bowls and the other flavors of dumplings too. Great addition to the neighborhood.

Wonderful selection of culinary delights, sweets and treats from from favorite cupcakes at the Flying Monkey to the delicious Amish chicken wings at Dienner's.  Peruse used books, have a glass of wine, buy kitchen gadgets or just sit and people watch - the Reading Terminal is a cool place to be in the midst of Center City.
Absolute great place for a food-centric stroll.

A trip to Philly isn't complete without a visit to RTM. It's like an indoor bazaar in Morocco, vibrant, bustling, and filled with exotic (and familiar) sights and sounds and smells of Philly's best eats. Hot pork sandwiches, cold fresh oysters, raw Penna Dutch cow's milk, all available for reasonable prices. Visitors that I bring here are always jelly that we have such an amazing market in the heart of the city. Parking across the street is convenient and reasonably priced. Awesome-sauce!
So much to do there! And great food & produce! I have went to 2 cooking classes there at La Cucina. Wonderful experiences! Definitely will go there any chance I get when I am in Philly. :)

I love this place!!!  Everytime I come here it is a feast. There's a shop for anything you want to eat here. I usually start by getting an array of awesome olives at one place and a few pieces of cheese at another for appetizers.  I follow that up with some oysters and sometimes a lobster,  which they will prepare for you on the spot. For main course,  I love the lamb sandwich or the Amish spot has great barbecue. Or there are plenty of places to grab awesome Chinese,  Greek or some traditional Philadelphia sandwiches. End it off with out of this world cheesecake or canolis and a world class expresso. Whole I'm eating dessert,  I usually have one of the friendly girls put together a flower arrangement at the flower shop with the most beautiful and healthiest flowers in town. This place is AWESOME!!!

Ate here almost everyday during the Democratic National Convention, and I'm glad I did! I'm from Los Angeles, so I as attracted to the market atmosphere and the variety of food it offers. The place is huuuuge and has something for everyone. I had my first Philly Cheesesteak every here & it was so delicious. When I return to Philly, this is definitely a place I'm visiting again!

If you don't like Reading Terminal Market, you're a communist and I don't trust you. 

This place has pretty much everything you could ever want to eat. As a matter of fact, if there is no version of Reading Terminal Market in Heaven, then I'm going to be extremely surprised.

There's so much diversity in deliciousness here. Cheesesteaks, brisket, roast pork, chinese, thai, pizza, ice cream, mac & cheese, crepes, burgers, gyros, soul food, roasted turkey, cookies, pretzels, cakes...ah darnit, now I want to go there.

If a friend is in Philadelphia for a visit and you don't take them here, you have failed. As a matter of fact, this might be considered a betrayal. 

As a (tiny) negative, it can get crowded and sometimes difficult to find places to sit. Also, food apparently has calories (sp?) which make you fat if you consume too many...and you will want to eat everything here. 

If you're reading this review and have never been here, drop everything and go right now. Unless it's your phone. Don't drop your phone. You'll need it give this place another five-star review.

Why I live yelp. In the city for only one night and wanted to find take out. Would never have found this on my own. Had the rolls: tikka and the one with home made cheese and spicy potato (can't remember the name). Be sure to take a container of their spicy red sauce and their flavorful white sauce for dipping.  A great meal!!  And woman at the counter was super friendly too!!

It's a pretty decent place. The service was quick but that may have been because it was a late weeknight that we were there. We got the ninja nuggets and they were nice and crispy. The sauce we had I think was a sweet soy. I poured it in my nuggets and shook the container and it ended up being too much sauce so I recommend adding just half first if you plan on going that route. All in all I would definitely be coming back.

I come to Philly about once or twice a year just to get away from NYC. Philly has really good food and this place is a big highlight too. Reading Terminal is really fun to explore at if youre in the area. I came here a few times with friends and its typiclaly really packed. It's basically a giagantic food court with different cultures of food everywhere. I loved the gumbo they had at the gumbo vendor. At first me and my boyfriend got one to share but after we finished our first we wanted another but the line was like another 45 minute so we just got Indian food at a stand instead. The indian food there wasn't as good as the places I regularly eat at. I also got a fruit juice. It was super fresh and tasted refreshing. They also have a donut and cheese vendor.

I can't get enough of this place! If you're visiting the city, Reading Terminal Market is a must-see. There's something for everyone, from the biggest foodies to the pickiest eaters. Even if you're not there to chow down (but really, what else would you be doing there?) the market is always bustling and everyone should experience its fun atmosphere.

Just stay here for a three course meal with lots of options! Crepes, sandwiches, cheesesteaks, chocolates, donuts, ice cream, cupcakes and more! 

Parking is validated and lots of seating around.

Stay away if there is a huge convention because it will be too congested.

Came in for a quick bite and shared the chicken keema, paneer, and aloo Kati rolls between 2 people. Delicious. Hit the spot. Right amount of spice and my Indian parents would approve. Great friendly service and a clean bathroom. Would definitely go back and try the rest of the menu!
Killer market in downtown Philly! Lots of food and market options. Reasonable pricing. Come hungry.

From D.C to Reading Terminal is worth the drive, this place is huge and has so many options. There's speciality grocery stores within the market, that's how everybody gets the produce to cook and make their own stuff in their restaurants. Went to the famous donut shop and the Phili cheese steak oh yes everything in their is good

I have never felt the need to review anything on Yelp before eating at the Industry. However, this place was so horrible, I want to warn everyone to save your money. 

After our favorite local restaurant, The Witch closed, my husband and I were super happy that another place was opening in its place! 

...Fail. 

I don't mind paying good money for good food. However, I paid over $20 for three scallops? with cream of wheat? and that was the large plate.

I left the eatery feeling ripped off and sent my husband off to go get some real food. 

My husband  liked the food more than I did. He had the mussels & sausage and thought that the portions were also small.  I did not bother drinking, but my husband had a few martini's which he said were good. They probably have to be good to take your attention off the ridiculously small plates. 

Save your money.

Went to The Industry for Sunday brunch. We had the pancakes with caramelized bananas, side of bacon, Meat Scramble with a cheddar biscuit (HUGE and Delicious!), fresh orange juice, and black tea. The pancakes were fluffy and delicious, there was a slight lacking of caramelized banana to pancake ratio, but overall the dish was good. 

My dining partner had the fresh orange juice and said it tasted good. Their Meat Scramble had nicely cooked eggs, sausage that wasn't greasy and had a nice taste, and the biscuit was to die for. My bacon was a bit overly smokey for me, but nice and crisp.They provided us with comp sticky buns that were chock full of nuts, and oh so sweetly delicious. The portions were decent to large. 

The decoration and atmosphere are nice and inviting. We would definitely eat here again. I can't comment on the beer selection or spirits because we didn't have any or look at the selection.

I'm vegan.  There's like 3 things to eat there.  Found everything I would ever eat at the Indian food stand.  Got Pindi Chana (chick peas) that came with a little salad... Normally love this dish... This one was just OK.  It's OK if you are starving, but mostly a GAG-FEST if you don't want to eat body parts or excretions.

Great beer selection. Interesting food offerings for this neighborhood. Cool space.

Was here for Philly Beer Week and had some nice beer choices. Friends had mix drinks they said were delicious. 

Came back and had more beer and the Bahn Mi sandwich which was good - nice and spicy, fresh. The shoestring fries were good also. Friend liked the Falafel sandwich.

Pro: Beer choices, Decor, interesting food choices. 

Con: The weeknight we went they have a burger and wine special that was unclear on the menu. The waiter didn't do a good job of explaining it. One of us opted for the wine special and it wasn't good. I guess they're trying to be ironic by offering Lambrusco or Brut Rose in old fashioned small wine glasses at $5.50 a pop. She just ordered her next glass from the regular wine menu after that.

Food lovers paradise. This place is incredible, unlike any other place I've frequented in the US. They have everything foodie related here, whether you want a quick bite to eat, full meal or something to cure your sweet tooth they have a ton of options here. There is this dutch diner, can't remember the name but if you have the patience to wait I think you should go. While I didn't get to go because I was pressed for time if the lines were any indication of how good the food is then you should definitely check it out! I did get to eat at DiNic's and I loved it so much that I came here the following day!

Tried one of each of the dumplings! They all magnificent, especial the cheese steak and the Asian pork are the best. Great costumer service, even with one guy here and the sauces are really good. Wish I live in philly because this place is great!
