Great place to go, very much like a European Market. Much to see. Much to eat.  

The parking lot across the way in incredibly expensive. $32 for two hours. Search for another parking lot a few blocks away.

This definitely isn't authentic Taiwanese snacks / food. I was excited to try this place out and I was super disappointed . I ordered take out apparently that only takes 2 mins and it will be ready for pick up , that already gave me a sign that it wasn't going to be great. I got there and picked up my food I wasn't greeted or anything I paid she gave me my food and I proceed. I got the giant squid bento and it wasn't a giant squid more like deep fried soggy calamari pieces that has been sitting there for too long. The food was soggy and cold mind you I only took my food two blocks away. It was pretty taste less too. Wish I could of actually like this place.  Disappointed

So many food options, surely you can find something you'd like.  I got a whoopie pie for $1.50, fresh whipped cream.  Also, I had breakfast at a diner I can't remember the name of.  Service was quick which I appreciated as I was very hungry.

Well if it wasn't for my quest to hit all the top 50 bars from 2012 in 2013 I probably would of never ended up here but I am so glad I did this place is fabulous,  I wish it was closer to me I might make it here more frequently.  Food was good, nice drink selection.  Atmosphere was great.

Love the atmosphere and menu in this place. Most of the staff and bartenders are really cool. My favorite thing to do is order a bunch of stuff to share, check out their specials, and taste a bunch of the cool brews and concoctions behind the bar. Really good stuff.

Love the market! I could write about all the things offered but I would be writing all day. So many options of food and products like clothes, and jewelry. Everything is fairly priced and there is something for everyone. They also have the best treats like cannolis and cappuccino flavored cupcakes.

Do you want to find chocolate in the shape of a brain?  Do you want to find local wine or sangria?  Do you want prickly pear honey?  Do you want sushi grade fish?  What is your wacky food fetish (you bad, bad boy)? Almost every quircky to completely blaze food item can be found at Reading Terminal Market.  As soon as you walk in the door, you are overwhelmed with the sights and smells of food.  Even times where I went that I wasn't hungry, I had the incredible urge to gain twenty pounds munching on the gigantic sandwhiches and pasta dishes arranged so beautifully by the vendors.  It is a little overwhelming for those looking for the first time, but I suggest strolling through the whole place first and then going back through to sample and grab some items you will be sure to love.

Herschel's deli is by far my favorite food stop here.  I don't even like pastrami sandwhiches normally.  But even thinking about the smokey, melt-in-your-mouth pastrami from here has me drooling on the keyboard.
A heritage spot with amazing food, drinks, and atmosphere. There's nothing you can't find here and I've loved everything I've ever had here. Love the honey/beeswax shop, too!

Fantastic! Huge variety of foods and artisan wares to get! I went on a Saturday afternoon around 4 or 5pm and this place was bustling but not too crowded. As most people do, I waited on the pretty fast line to try a roast pork sandwich from Dinic's since their hand carved Italian pulled pork was gone. That was delicious and I will be writing a separate review on their own yelp account. Like I said, there were so many choices and delicious looking and smelling dessert/bake shops to try from. Finding seats was not difficult even for the group of 6 we were.

This is by far the only reason I like Philadelphia; Reading Terminal Market is a cultural oasis in a mundane desert, and possesses a variety of foods, produce, restaurant stands, and products that I love simply looking at-certainly a visiting foodie's paradise.

The reason this place receives four stars is due to the crowds; it takes awhile to find a seat, and even longer to order once you've explored the entirety of the place. 

So far, I have eaten at what I like to call "The Turkey Place;"  you can't miss it. Facing the main seating area, it possesses many freshly roasted gobblers for one's slicing pleasure; I got a cranberry sauce, stuffing, and turkey sandwich, and though it was expensive, it was gut-busting and absolutely delicious. The homestyle sides such as macaroni and cheese and greens, however, are less exciting; stick with the sandwiches. 

There is also a Middle Eastern Joint that serves a variety of specialties, particularly hummus, baba ghannoush, grapes leaves, falafel, etc. This was incredibly expensive, I thought, at $6.17, especially when all I received was hummus, baba, and an eggplant stew which seemed to consist more of peppers than of eggplant; the pita was also quite thin, and lacked the fluffiness that others possess. 

The "stew" and the baba were good, but I could have done without the hummus, which had an odd taste that I can't even describe. I was still hungry, in fact, so I ended up purchasing one of their spinach pies for the road. Unlike spanakopita, the spinach-minus-feta is stuffed inside of a bread-like shell rather than flaky phyllo; it was good but a little plain. This particular place also sells juices; my friend purchased one and really enjoyed it, saying it filled her up. 

The various green grocers have tons of fresh fruits and vegetables, while the fishmongers and butchers have endless varieties of cuts and sea creatures. I've never bought from these guys because I don't live here...and I don't think I should let raw meat sit out for the bus ride home. 

Particularly enticing "stores" are the ones that sell cookbooks, kitchenware, unusual jams/jellies, and spices; definitely give those a try. 

Next time I'm out there, I'll be sure to get Bassett's ice cream, and maybe try an amish kiosk or two; that stuff is so exotic to me-heh.

It's hard to find anything bad to say about Reading Terminal Market. 

When I first moved to Philadelphia a few years ago, it was the first place I wanted to visit because of it's appearance on the Food Network several times. I was expecting something much less than what I actually found. This place is huge, and has a selection that rivals any market I have seen in the U.S. as well as abroad. 

The selections range from the famous DiNiC's Roast Pork to the incredible and authentic Cajun cuisine by Beck's Cafe. You can also find a beer garden, freshly made ice cream, fruits, vegetables, and so much more. Candy shoppes, bakeries, incredible coffee and diners, it's almost too much to be included in just one Yelp review.

The entire place is labeled with street names, making it fairly easy to navigate despite the intimidating size for first-time visitors. In addition to shops and restaurants, there is ample seating in the middle for you to enjoy whatever delicacies you try during your visit. 

It's also always expanding. Over the past two years alone I have seen several new shops appear, as well as renovations to older members of the Reading Terminal Market family. 

The only downside - DiNiC's has been known to sell out well before closing, so make sure if you're visiting and want to try their famous Roast Pork sandwich that you get there early and try to avoid the lunchtime rush.

Recently visiting the Reading Terminal Market in Philly while visiting for the weekend. 

It's a cool place, and there's a lot going on. They had a bunch of fresh food, meats (that I know nothing about), cheeses, desserts, and sweets. I was pleasantly surprised at the wide variety of cuisines that were available. 

We had some food from one of the deli's, a greek place, a chocolate maker, and a baker. A cool way to kill a few hours.

vendors I like the most:

iovine brother produce
dutch eating place
Beller;s donut

Salumaria is in my top 3 of hoagie places. Beiler's has delicious dirt pudding, spicy pickles, broccoli slaw and smackaroni(which is potato salad and macaroni salad combined. I get the bulk of my produce from Iovine, but am mindful to only buy organic, I've found that almost every fruit or veg that wasn't organic has spoiled within a day of purchasing. Several meat markets to choose from which all offer meat packages - open to change to your liking for the kosher or halal eater. My biggest pet peeve is the lack of seating, or even reliable seating, as a lot of the tables are wobbly and the chairs tend to be broken. Great place for ice cream too!!

En tant qu'Européenne le Reading Terminal Market me fait penser au marché couvert de Barcelone, La Boqueria ! Des produits locaux, frais, typique et atypique, en somme un lieu qui vaut le détour ! J'ai pu y goûter les fameux cheese steack, spécialité de Philadelphie, et y rencontrer des Amish et leur produits 'homemade'. Je conseille fortement à tous les touristes, expatriés, ou étudiants comme moi d'y faire un tour. Seul bémol : énormément de monde au moment du déjeuné et peu de place pour s'assoir.

eh. i "get it", i just dont like it. too crowded and overwhelming. i like going to smell the smells but ive never had a great experience finding anything i want there. the sushi place inside is the pits. ive tried some other places and havent been impressed. mostly i think bc of the surroundings. but i always go back so it cant be that bad.

Great selection of vendors. A foodie's taste of heaven. Visited DiNics, Chocolate by Mueller and Termini's on a Monday (Columbus Day) and they were busy. 

If in town, would definitely be back.
Absolutely love the market. the environment is bustling and the food is so diverse. From cheese steaks to seafood, its all in this market. I suggest bringing cash but there is an ATM inside.
Fun place to wander, something for everyone.  From fruits and veggies to meats and breads, and every sort of cuisine imaginable,  A feast for the senses!

This is one of my go-to places in Philly for a quick lunch or cup of coffee. The variety of cuisine can satisfy most cravings. I usually grab a Philly cheese steak - hey, when you are in Philly, you need  a cheese steak!

The place was packed, drive through rapped a round the parking lot.   About 7 people in line.  I waited four minutes to order and sat down, with my little numbered sign, my son walked over to get napkins, looked up and food was at table.  Excetlent job by manager and crew.

Love the Reading terminal! Hersels deli is the best! Try the corned beef special. It is out of this world. Worth the wait in line. Corned beef was so fresh it was still warm ,cut to order and placed on the freshest Rye bread.

Had Masala Paneer kati roll and chaas. Masala Paneer was amazingly delicious and I d suggest that if you are veggie. Fresh and tasty. And Chaas here was legit too. Had a little more than the enough amount of jeera, but that is the highlight of the drink.. Must try both. Now I don't wanna leave Philly

Good for foodies. Lots of different options. (not too many vegan choices, but still fun to check it out).  Super dense, which makes it a great place for tourist short on time but who to get a taste of everything!

This is definitely my must visited spot in Philly. I stopped by here during my every single visit. There are a lot of vendors and restaurants to meet everyone's needs. 

My favorite places are Beck's Cajun Cafe, Miller's Twist, The Rib Stand, and Beiler's Donuts and Salads. And I loved how new places were opening up, restrooms were renovated and seating areas were rearranged throughout the years.

The parking deal is definitely a plus for this place.

This place is right by the hospital so it automatically get a large crowd of people coming through. Based on that the staff here really had to run a tight ship. That included having people take you order way in advance (when you're in the back in the line) so that way they can start prepping your food faster. I appreciate that although I think online ordering and pick up is the most time efficient.

The food isn't super interesting, but I have to admit the sandwich I get 8/10 of the times is great (the Mediterranean with chicken, no roasted peppers and extra artichokes!). 
Nothing to write home about, but a great lunch place.

Absolutely have to come here every time I'm in Philly. So many yummy and awesome foods to try and sweets everywhere. Some of my favorites are the Beiler's Bakery and donuts, there a far to many goodies to narrow down just one favorite. Love their homemade donuts, made on site, and they have many really good salads and fresh sauerkraut. Famous 4th Street Cookie Company has the most delicious, soft cookies! We always take some home with us. Best grilled cheese sandwiches at Valley Shepherd Creamery & Meltkraft. There are toooo many things that are delicious here.

Just about any food, grocery, ice cream  item you can think of and this place has it. Packed with people but thats the fun part. I've had creole, ice cream, greek, philly cheese steaks, and sushi in here. all are bomb!

This was a really fun place with a lot of variety. It's a really no frills experience- it's a mass market of different vendors serving up madd quantities of food. There are tables throughout. You can get everything from ice cream to roast beef to falafel to alligator here. Wherever you start, I definitely recommend Bassets ice cream before you head out!

You just can't argue with a crowd.  This place is amazing, but friggin crowded.  Very hard to get something to eat here in the early afternoon due to crowds of people in line for lunches, unless you don't mind waiting in line.  I Pass when it comes to lines.  Seating is very limited for the number of very successful food venders.  You name it, they have it.  Chinese, Polish, Amish, Fish, BBQ, Deli and just about any other ethnic or local food restaurant you may want to try.

We have only been successful at scoring a lunch at one of the Chinese food venders on several of our walks through and it was amazingly good.  There is no problem when it comes to getting you cakes, cookies or ice creams since the shops are less crowded.

It is a great place to walk around and smell the smells of all the food.  Plenty of fresh meats, fish, cheeses and produce, in addition to cookies candies and most anything else you're looking for in food.  I think they are on the pricy side of meats and seafood, but I'm not living in the City where their are very few grocery stores.  Maybe that's what they pay.

Down sides the lack of table space and very crowded isles.  Additionally, if you're a tourist and looking to walk around for the remainder of the day it's hard to pick up any fresh produce.

Absolutely ANYTHING you can think of is here. Want some fresh ice cream? Got it. How about Thanksgiving dinner? Check. Homemade honey? Yep. Even a book to read while lunching? They even have a little book store.
I grew up in Philly so I'm used to Reading Term but I never realized how cool it actually is until friends not from here ask me to take them on a tour here. So I guess I'm a lucky duck for knowing this place inside and out.
My favorite place to visit when in Philadelphia. I always look forward to seeing all the different vendors.

Always a fan of big marketplaces--especially those all under one roof. I was there on a Sunday, so don't think it was as bustling, since not all stands were open. We sampled a tea stand and purveyors of cookies --got a black and white/ night and day (?) cookie that was awesome, as well as a little German type market that had lots of marzipan options, as well as many other items you won't find at most shops.There was one part of the market that appeared to be filled with locals, gathering raw items for some home-made recipe. There were a few chocolate stands. The bathrooms were clean.

gotta love reading terminal
beillers pickel place is a must visit
dinics is a must visit
termini's is a must visit

can't get enough of this place.
everything's fucking phenomenal. visually a downgrade from nyc, but experience wise - wow. amazing food. 

foodie's paradise.

So I've been here twice and I've ordered all of their best selling / highly recommended items ( I asked the cashier as well as verified with reviews already posted by yelpers)

The first trip I ordered the MK special  with chicken and lamb ..extra spicy . It was funny as the flavors don't really remind me of Indian food . Think more Cajun . The white sauce was underwhelming . Reminds me of water down ranch . I wasn't a fan of the hot sauce either .

The second time I ordered three rolls and rose lassi ! I got the chicken masala , the lamb , the aloo paneer , and chicken pepper .

Meh . Average quality . Heavily spiced and not in a good way . Well seasoned is a different story .

Three stars for the food !

The rose lassi was delicious but it's really hard to mess up a yogurt drink that consist of three ingredients .

Price points were almost fair . Could be slightly cheaper for what you get .

One star for service . They are really reluctant to give you the discounts they advertise . I've been here twice . I detected attitude from both people who were working the cashier .

Overall two stars .

I miss the Indian and Pakistani restaurants back at home in LA and Toronto .

Take a stroll through Philaldelphia's historic Reading Terminal Market and take in all of the bright sites and tantalizing smells wafting through the air. This place is a mecca of Philly's Phinest eats.  You can make a day of exploring the market, and it is an especially great location for a date. Go for lunch, dinner, or to sample a little bit from a variety of vendors, and pick out some beautiful flowers for your sweetie while you're there!  Whatever path you choose, you won't want to miss the DiNic's roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone!
Beautiful place, many shops, good prices (if you know where to look).

The worst Chinese fried chicken I ever had! Do you expect bones in fried chicken ever? The server said we should wait till they called our number, but 15min later nobody called and our chicken is really for no one knows how long! 

Favor is also not good! 

First and last time here.

Alot of great places to eat at and purchase foods. I have been to a few of the places in here. We eat here every year when the flower show is in town. 
There is currently some construction around the outside of the building. Other than that. It's easy access.

Very cute place!  I loved all the variety of foods and all the little stalls whether it was crafts, desserts, drinks or foods!   I think this location is perfect and there is something to offer everyone!   The positive is that they have tables (although I can envision it getting super crowded during lunch and hard to find a seat) and big bathrooms!  I was surprised the bathrooms were relatively clean too!   

Beware, the amish close early.  I think at 4.  We wanted to try their foods and were disappointed they closed.  Reading Terminal Market is easily walkable from Chinatown and the Rittenshouse Square area.   As for parking, I am not sure since I parked at my hotel and walked over.   I came after the lunch hours so I don't know how busy it gets during peak time.   This is a must if you are coming to philly to visit or even if you are a regular and looking for something to eat.

I really like this place for a few reasons: everything is cheap (~$5), tasty,  and service is fast and friendly. The only thing I don't like about this place is its location-- being on the far corner of campus makes it a little harder for me to justify actually going.

I've tried several of their sandwiches at some point or another and in general, after requesting all of the toppings (all free), I always find them very tasty. That said, the sandwiches are always a mess to eat, so I recommend taking a few napkins and a fork with you before you leave.

The salads here are not bad as well. My biggest complaint is the use of lettuce as the green. Naturally,  I think you can get better deals elsewhere, but not a bad deal by any means.

Overall, very solid choice.

This is definitely not authentic Indian food. This is the fast food version of it. Terrible! I do not recommend this fast food restaurant. Please search for a sit down, authentic Indian food. I had yelp this location to take my friend to his first time at an Indian restaurant, I was more disappointed than he was, it was not what I had in mind at all.
Lots of diversity and probably the very best  pork and broccoli rabe sandwich in the country !

A Philadelphia treasure. Great place to walk around and shop for just about any food thing you could want. It gets pretty crowded but it adds to the ambulance. Every tasty delectable treat you could possibly want is housed in here. Check it out. I can pick up dumplings for lunch, shop for my grocers and get fresh sea food, then get a ice cream cone for my walk home.

Definitely worth the crowd ! This place is an amazing indoor market with so many choices to eat, I would've stayed there all day if I was left to my own devices. Yes, it is packed ... Yes, there are a lot of tourists .. But it is sooo worth it. There is literally anything and everything you could ever want under one roof. This place absolutely has something for everyone..gluten free options, desert bars, gyros, cheesesteaks, po boys, fresh fish, live lobsters in a tank .. I could go on and on ..its ridiculous . If you are adventurous , I suggest you spend a couple hours here trying out the different food options.. You will not be disappointed .

Reading Terminal Market is an absolute must for a first-time Philly visitor! It is enormous, so utilize the maps and signs scattered around the sprawling building. Come hungry, too, because they have every single kind of food from every corner of the map in this place. A quick google search will tell you where to get that perfect Philly cheesesteak, and there's a fair few dessert places as well. Have fun, don't get lost, and plan to walk back to your Airbnb to help digest all that food!

Oh how I loved this place! I've been longing for it since we left Philadelphia. So much good food here. Definitely a must! Spend three days at the hotel upstairs and had all of our food needs met here. Recommend the Dutch Eating Place!
Breakfast of grease on a biscuit and something called hash browns that more closely resembled cardboard in flavor. But at least the coffee was barely tolerable.

Excellent food for the price. 

I first came here during their grand opening. There was a private party for the family of the owner, and I was the only customer inside. I was ready to order a few rolls, but then the owner stopped me and said any rolls I wanted to try were free today.

That's amazing customer service.

Since then, I'm happy to report the place has exploded in popularity. You can't go wrong with any of the chicken rolls, but my personal favorite is the paneer masala roll. Add the white sauce (to how much your diet can handle) and you have tasty combo. 

Is it the most authentic indian food? No. Is it hella tasty and a great deal especially if you're hungry at night? Heck yes. 4/5 for the food but overall 5/5  for the nice staff and that opening day gesture by the owner.

Since I moved to the area, I've visited Reading Terminal Market many, many times! Every time I try to buy something new but I always find myself going back to Bassett's Ice Cream for dessert! I've never actually had a bad experience coming here, though it can be very crowded most of the time and I wish it closed later in the evening.

The Terminal is basically a Philly landmark that everyone should be required to take their out of town friends to at least once... it's a no-brainer. If you don't you're a shitty host.

Too much stuff here to go into specific details, but this is THE definitive Philadelphia bazaar.

It can really be hit or miss depending on the vendor, but there's an excellent selection. My favorite is the specialty olive oil and balsamic vinegar stand, I have yet to find a decent regular butcher there. If you're looking for interesting soaps and incense, you'll be right at home here. Avoid the prepared foods sections, you can find those in any other food court in Philly. Also here, Amish means quality! Get those pickles, folks. They sure are tasty.

This is arguably the nicest assortment of food you will find inside one place in the downtown area of any major city.  Visiting Philly for the first time, I had a completely different vision.  I thought it would be similar to this big indoor Flea Market with a bunch of people trying to hustle me for a fake gucci bag or some knock off sunglasses.  I was pleasantly surprised to walk over from the Loews hotel to see a bunch of men and women in Pilgrim outfits at different vendors serving, baking and displaying almost anything I wanted to eat.  Cheesesteaks, chocoloates, cookies, pretzels, a produce market, fish market,  bakery . . . . the smell of chocolate cookies and fried onions never smelt so good.

I walked, but parking seemed easy.  I believe if you purchase 10 dollars worth of stuff at the market you get 3 dollar parking on Filbert and 12th, so that is real convenient for those of you driving in.  The place is huge so go in with an open mind and be ready to try an assortment of stuff at your own pace.  The food is delicious.

The only knock I got on this place is the hours of operation.  They close at 6 p.m.  A place like this in the middle of City Center in Philadelphia should be open to atleast 9 p.m. . . . I can only imagine how packed it is on the weekend when people aren't rushing from work trying to make the closing.  Also by me going on a Wednesday morning around 9 a.m. . . . not everything was open.

Overall, if you are visiting from out of town I would say this is a MUST do in Philly . . . anything and everything you thought of eating in Philly is right here and with reasonable prices.  I am very much a fan of this place.  Just don't expect to go here after a long day of touring, because it might not be open.

I honestly don't even know where to start. If you don't consider yourself a foodie, I garuntee you will be after your first few minutes walking through this place. To simply put it, the Reading Terminal Market is heaven. I'm surpised they don't have a Golden gate and angels at the entrance. There is every kind of cusine you can think of and it is all authentic and as fresh as can be. A few of the restaurants in there have been featured on food network tv shows. And many of the places are Zagat rated. For you sweets lovers, they have a whole aisle of just that and if you don't see what you're looking for on display, there's a few places that can make any dessert/ cake you body/ mind desires. This place is so amazing, I can't even say what my favorite restaurant is. There's just waaaay too many! To add to that, they also have amazing coffee, book stores, a nut stand, Amish stand, ice cream stands, cookie stands, an oyester bar, exotic grill chees stand, bee wax product stand, fresh bread stands, a few vegetable and seafood stands with unbeatable prices and products, just to name a few. They occasionally events/ shows around the food court which makes it almost too much to handle. Annnd difficult to navigate. Speaking of navigating, that's my only complaint about this place. It gets super, ridiculously, unbelievably crowded on the weekends. But that's only because it's clearly one of the best things that Philly has to offer. Simply put, if the Reading Terminal Market was the only place I could eat for the rest of my life and the next life, I would be perfectly ok with that. So do yourself a favor and treat your taste buds to total euphoric pleasure.
-You're welcome ;-)

want ice cream??

BASSETS is where its at!! so yummy!!!

tubby olive is so neat! deffinatly a different place to try out and experience different balsamics and oils!!

The food here is great and service was attentive. We went for brunch and coffee is excellent. 

However, it was so loud that I left with a headache. We asked if the volume could be turned down which they did, for about 10 mins. Then it went back up and we were back to shouting at each other. Not what I want to do on a Sunday morning.
I love Reading Terminal market. They have great one off restaurants. You can always find something amazing there. They even have great chocolate at the Pennsylvanian market.

It's really nice to have a place like the industry in the neighborhood.  The staff is friendly, the food's great (if a little pricey), and the atmosphere is comfortable.  We've been for brunch, dinner and drinks and haven't been disappointed.
Always a pleasure to walk around those aisles and grab something in all of that different places. Great to eat and to shop.

I didn't know the Reading Terminal Market was full of fresh produce, restaurants, and local homemade gifts. It was nice walking through seeing different kinds of options they had. The local seafood stands had Stone Crab!!
They also have a beautiful toy train set in the middle of the facility!
One star off for tourist trap. Nice to explore once though!

Can't find a market like this anywhere else! I'm a Philadelphia native, and I can't get enough. I've lived in other cities, but nothing compares.  No matter what kind of food you're looking for, there's a place in this market. There's also tons of local specialties, and even places to get good gifts for friends or relatives!
Nice variety of stores and outlets, tons of amazing food and experiences for you and our family.
Amazing food at every turn. Highly recommend Dinic's Roast Pork Sandwich!

We went here for a post dinner snack. I only tried the Chicken Kheema Kati Roll and it was amazing. The chicken was minced perfectly and very flavorful. The Kati Roll had green cardamom, cinnamon and cloves. I had asked was the roll to be made spicy and the spice level was manageable.

We even tried the hot sauce and white sauce and absolutely loved it. In the next visit, I know what I will be ordering ... MK special chicken and rice

The decor is decent, but the dining area is small. So it may be a bit difficult to find seating with a big group
I really dislike potbellys. They don't have a large menu. My sandwich was small and I satisfying. I went once and will not be returning.

THIS PLACE IS AWESOME!

I spent over 2 hours just walking around looking at everything for the first time. I couldn't decide what to do or buy or eat, but I wanted ALL THE THINGS. The ambiance is fantastic here.

The people cooking, serving, and preparing dishes all make each of their offerings look delicious. The vendors each do their utmost to present the best goods, most quality selections, and excellent standards to their very popular market.

I was there not only during the week, but at an off-peak time during a regular work day and the place was still packed. They offer so much: cheesesteaks (obviously), ice-cream, Asian food, Greek food, Indian food, a vegetable market, a bar (or two), a florist, breakfast, lunch, and dinner options, as well as candy, snacks, goodies, tasty treats of all kinds, and even butchers!

If you're new to Philly or plan to travel here, just go on and save at least 1/2 a day on your trip to check out Reading Terminal Market. Totally worth every second there.

Very interesting place. Food of ALL types - from seafood, to a grocery area, to cookies, amish donuts, thai food, gumbo...it goes on and on. It is crazy busy here at all times, tight quarters, limited seating to eat, prices slightly overpriced throughout but makes up for it in variety and accessibility. Cool place to go with people.
I LOOOOVVEE this place, so many options to choose from just go hungry and you won't be disappointed!

One of my favorite places in Philadelphia. A large variety of almost anything. I try to stop here every time I am in Philly, just to see what's new, find some things I don't need, but can't live without, and stop at some of the delectable food places. I cannot go home without having at least one or two of the turkey sandwiches, stop by the coffee store, butcher and German deli. And that's just for starters.
The farmers market, ice cream, and cheesesteaks are also worth a stop.
There are usually some minor changes with new vendors, etc. There is ample parking that is reasonable close by.

Hinter dem Namen Reading Terminal Market konnte ich mir anfangs nicht wirklich vorstellen, was sich dahinter verbarg. Doch die Überraschung war umso größer, als ich herrausfand, dass er ein großer Markt für frisches Gemüse, Fleisch, Meeresfrüchte, Backwaren, Bücher, Kleidung und und und ist.


 Über 80 Verkäufer tummeln sich in diesem Markt. Es ist laut und ein wenig stickig. Vor allem hat sich der Markt darauf spezialisiert frisch zubereitete Gerichte zu verkaufen. Hier bekommt man Amerikanisch, Italienisch, Japanisch, Thai, Chinesisch, Mexikanisch und Speisen und Getränke aus aller Herrenländer.


 Heutzutage sind aber noch nur noch 3 Verkäufer aus Originalfamilien der Gründerzeit des Reading Terminal Market.


 Vor allem Mittags ist hier die Hölle losHier holen sich die Leute ihr Mittagessen aus den umliegenden Büros. Ebenfalls ist der Markt direkt mit dem Marriott Downtown und dem Convention Center verbunden.


 Und für die, die auch mittags weiterarbeiten möchten, gibt es im Reading Terminal Market komplett kostenlos W-Lan.
Great place to grab a bite and and a pint! Got some real nice mozzarella cheese too!
Enjoyed the air of energy and happy people who enjoy the coming together in this warm city.

I wish we had a place like this in Portland Oregon!  Honestly hard to venture out when you have different foods from all over in one place.  This is a must go to and eat!  Unfortunately they close early, so get there with enough time to walk around and get something to eat!

There's only one bad thing about the Reading Terminal Market- and that is the crowd it pulls in! But that isn't necessarily a bad thing.

There are so many amazing places to eat in here!

There's a stand that sells homemade lemonade - the orange lemonade is the BEST!

I love Wurhaus Schmitz- led their by my favorite Philly bar- Brauhaus Schmitz. Potato pancakes to go or to eat there!

D'nicks roast park is another favorite stop... the best sandwich ever!

Fourth Street cookie has the biggest and best cookies ever!

The chocolate store in the one corner makes crazy chocolate shapes. They once had a chocolate covered tastykake and it was the best thing I ever had!

Basessts' Icecream is another one of my favorites.

You really can't go wrong with going here! Plenty of seats to sit at and eat in the middle of the market.
So much variety and a must see when you are in Philly. Be careful if you are short on time around lunch because it's very busy then, but they have the lunch crowd down to a fine science
I was not pleased with the service. The servicer was rude and slow. The nachos wasn't fresh and bowl was a small for the amount I  paid. This will be my last time at this Chipotle.

Went on a Monday night.  Not very crowded as one would expect.  But they were open.

I agree the decor is warm and welcoming.  The service was very comfortable and friendly.  Loved the Steak Tartar, it is heavy w/ lemon and capers, which is always good in my book.  

But....I have to say the mains were a bit lackluster.  The wife had Steak Frite.  Good solid frite's if a bit short (avg. was 2 inches in length, kind of odd) but the flat iron (or was it skirt) steak although done perfectly was a bit iron/liver tasting in flavor and texture.  I had the spare ribs, and mashed turnips (I think that's what the mash was), but then they put the string beans into the mashed stuff around the meat.  I haven't mashed up my plate of food since I was 9 yrs. old and used to mush my turkey, corn and mashed potatoes together and swirl them around on my plate.  That is kind of what it felt like to eat this dish.  And the meat although tender was rather skimpy in the portion and just OK in the flavor department.

A solid three stars.  Two for food, four for ambiance and service.

This place is neat! It has everything! A lot of great places to eat inside! It can easily get crowded. We ate at Tommy DiNic's which has scrumptious cheesesteaks. I was looking forward to trying Miller's Twist's soft pretzels but they were closed on Sunday. Boo! We tried Bassetts Ice Cream and it was really good! They can make milkshakes too. I didn't see much souvenir shops like I've seen at similar markets in other cities. Maybe I missed it?? We still enjoyed visiting this place and we recommend checking it out!

Came here with a friend and we split two rolls. We got the Chicken Masala Roll and those Paneer Masala Roll. The food was pretty tasty, and it ends up being an indian food burrito, I just wish there was a bit more filling in it! Maybe some rice, chick peas, and a cucumber salad and they have a seriuossssss business going on. 

Other than that, the white and hot sauces were tasty and added a lot to the flavor. The mango lassi was a pre-made and super thick drink. I love lassi's and know a good one, tasted fine but just too thick! 

I can't completely complain though cause for two lassis and two rolls it was pretty cheap.
So much delicious food here! Only downside is it's a victim of its own success - huge crowds make it a kind of stressful experience, unfortunately.

I don't know if there is much more to say than this is the best place ever. Any kind of food item you could ever possibly want from fresh pressed juices to a 10 pound whole fish! Every place is as good as the one before it and everything is incredibly fresh. The people are extremely friendly as well. Beware that it gets INSANE crowds over the weekends and crazy lines during lunch, but it's well worth the wait!

Love love love the Reading Terminal Market.  Whether friends and family are coming to town, going for a bite at lunchtime or shopping for groceries, the Terminal cannot be beat.  


Some of my favorite stalls are:
Godshall's Poultry (Turkey steaks!)
Martin's (all the different sausage flavors are awesome)
Iovine's Produce (always carrying what's fresh so you should eat it soon after purchase, so much produce for excellent prices)
Miller's Twist (butter anyone?)
Market Blooms (these are the longest lasting blooms in Center City with artists for arrangers)
The Head Nut (Coffee at reasonable prices)
Metropolitan Bakery (their baguette cannot be beat)
Dinic's (roast pork is worth the wait in line)

I could keep going, but that's the beauty of the market.  Lots of variety and more to try and explore.

can i say "Oh My G-d"..... 

if i ever go back to Philly, this is the place I'll go. It has everything. and I mean everything. It's a labyrinth for all six senses. The smells are overwhelming and the selection is astounding. You can go there to grab lunch if only you could make up your mind as to what you want! you'd go there to pick up a fresh steak, seafood, fruits and veggies, or a homemade treat. You could even pick up a gift for somebody's b-day - books, jewelry, kitchen stuff from traditional to funky! 

I'm running out of words. 
I want to go back.
Visiting Philly looking for great eats best prices check out the market. From land to sea it's all here for your indulgence. Eat-up. Cheers

We really enjoyed the different vendors and the food we selected was really good. Two of us ate at a booth specializing in roasted turkey and one of us had a burger.  The best part was Bassett's Ice Cream - it was absolutely delicious. BIGGEST problem is that we went there on a Friday night for dinner but the place closes at 6 p.m., not a great plan for dinner.

Absolutely the best place on Earth. Truly something for everyone. The Iovine's fresh produce, Godshall's poultry and Martin's meats and sausages to name just a few. Dinic's sandwiches, Olympus pork souvlaki and the Dutch Eating Place for amazing creamed chipped beef on home fries. Miller's Twist is a must too.

There is not a single thing wrong with this place. Variety, quality, and quantity! If I lived closer I would come here weekly. When in Philly this market is a must! Go hungry and leave happy! It can get pretty crowded and some places have lines but don't be discouraged, it's worth the wait!

this place is mediocre at best, as far as "markets" go. there are better/cleaner/cheaper markets all over major cities in the US. but -- RTM does have some iconic establishments - dinic's for one, is a favorite. it's a tourist [trap], but i suppose it must be visited on any first-timer's trip to philly!

This place is a feast for the eyes and mouth.  You can find pretty much anything to eat here at the Reading Terminal Market, as there's aisles and aisles of food, from cooked food to consume now, to raw food to prepare at home, to sweet desserts and candies to give to someone special.

This place reminded me of the Granville Market in Vancouver, Canada, or the Grand Central Market in Los Angeles, and to some extent Pike Place in Seattle.  I'm sure like those markets, this market changed over the years.  You can get breakfast or lunch here by walking up to the food kiosk and plop yourself on an open stool, chat with the guy next to you, and then grab something from the bakery as you head out.

Even though its semi touristy, the prices are not completely outrageous.  At one of the deli counters, their shaved meats were about $4 a pound.  A supermarket in California charged $7.99 a pound for roast beef, so this was quite a bargain.

You can spend hours here, but if you're a tourist without a car, hauling your goods can be a problem.  I did stop at Flying Monkey Bakery and picked up 4 bars of the Butter Cake, which were amazingly good (but messy!).  

It is definitely a must stop if you're in the Philadelphia area.

While a technically a "working" market ,Reading Terminal Market is really just a cleverly designed tourist Mecca.....here's how I know. Try finding any visible information on how to take advantage of the $6.00 for 3 hours of parking for market shoppers at the parking facility across the street....without knowing that your ticket has to be punched by a market vendor you'll end up paying $30.00+ plus for the same time.
That being said I really love this place,crowded,raucous,exciting,and absolutely filled with all kinds of great eats, We availed our-selves of the rather disappointing Italian pulled pork and beef sandwiches with Broccoli rabe at Tommy di Nics and some excellent stuffed pretzels at the Amish.
There are so many little nooks and cranny's to explore in this rather small venue and I can't wait to try some more of what Reading has to offer....just watch the parking.

This is a haven for people who love ethnic food. May be the best place in Philly for its variety and potential for one-stop shopping. There must be at least 50 booths here, and virtually every ethnic group is represented here. There are numerous fruit and vegetable stands supplying any veggie fruit, nut, several fish mongers, a terrific  spice shop, delicious pastry and bread booths,  a kitchen gadget shop,  sandwich places, e.g.  Most of the food is fresh and house-made. The used book stand is somewhat pricey, but the books are interesting and unusual. There is even a booth that sells only cook books.  I found that a good time to shop is on Monday morning before lunchtime. You can usually get a seat if you wish to sit down with your food and the isles are not as crowded. Try to allow a few hours there, as it will take you that long to explore all the Market has to offer. Have fun!

You have to love the Reading Terminal! It has everything that any food that anyone wants in their Philadelphia experience all condensed into one market downtown. I recommend buying one of the Amish soft pretzels  (perfectly buttered and salted) and one of the homemade lemonades or strawberry lemonades. The terminal also features stands with fresh produce, deli meats, and fruits, as well as tables with paintings and nick-nacks all over. This is a must-visit if you are visiting Philadelphia!

Reading Terminal is one of my favorite places in the world!  Anytime I'm in Philly I must come here.  While it is famous, it's by no means a tourist trap.  Products here are excellent, and if you live nearby you can easily get great meat and produce for not much money.  It's also a great gateway to amish country as there are tons of amish vendors here!  All food stalls that I've been to have been great, and you'll find a huge selection of fresh baked goods, grilled meats, and food from around the world.

It's also home to a Hope's Cookies location, which may be the greatest cookies in the entire world.

Reading Terminal Market may very well be my favorite part of going into the city.  It is a must-do on any city visitor's list and a do-veryoften on the list of anyone who calls themselves a Philadelphian.

I have too many favorite vendors to list them here, but I think the most important thing to say is that you need to just experience the market!  Don't try to get in and out as quickly as possible.  See the sights, smell the smells, hear the noises - it is just an amazing part of city life that we don't get to experience when we are going through the Starbucks drive-thru, picking up milk at Wawa, and rolling into the parking lot at the Acme in the suburbs.  

Wander through the market and pick 3 or 4 different vendors that you would like and then decide on one and go back.  Even better, go with 3-4 friends and try a little bit of everything.

I have only ever gotten prepared foods here, but I know many friends that do their raw foods shopping here and I understand the butchers and fishmongers are amazing and have unique items that you can not find elsewhere.  

Finding a seat can be a contact sport and don't be afraid to ask to share a table with a fellow Market shopper - it is part of the experience.  

Lastly, don't forget to get your parking validated - it is only $4 for 2 hours if your spend $10.

Terrible service. Counter staff were half awake this morning, no eye contact, like zombies they barely wait on you.
My breakfast was gummy cold eggs, translucent bacon that tasted like plywood. Everything was cold.
I had to beg for a napkin.
Tables dirty, spilled coffee on the floor.
It seems that I one cares here, so your breakfast could end up like mine, awful.
Avoid this place stall costs 
Sincerely

Cash only place. We Tried the diced beef and tea. Diced beef is very sweet, so is the tea. Maybe should ask for low sugar for everything. Food is served fast. Beef is deep fried so you can hardly tell fresh or not. But would like to go back to try other things. The lime tea is huge and too sweet for me.

A good option to get a taste of Philly all in one place. 

Molly Malloy's is a great place to grab breakfast. 

Beiler's Bakery has good handmade donuts, but beware they are very sweet

Spataro's has really good cheesesteaks. Always ask for whiz!

Bassett' Ice Cream is amazing!

I went to this location last night. Everything was fine as far as the employees. The person helping us knew plenty about the items on the menu and was able to answer the questions my gf had about all the different salads. We ordered a salad and two of the meals. The problem is I got home and realized one of the sandwiches from the meal was not in the bag at all.

I am absolutely addicted! Best affordable lunch around the area.  I always get the Healthy Sprout roll, which is filled with lentils, beets, cabbage, etc.  It is perfect with the spicy sauce.  I also get some chaas (buttermilk) too.  Super affordable, flavorful and always fast!

Wendys is wendys. A cheap, fast food chain with a just "okay" selection for food on the go. The reason I gave THIS wendys such a high rating is because I live around the corner from this one. I get done work late most nights and every time I go to this particular wendy's i am always greeted with such great attitudes and even though the food is just "okay" i would so rather go here for the great energy, rather then mcdonalds or burger king any day.

Reading is an nice place to go with a variety of restaurants, snack foods and other items.   Just a little pricey because it is in "Center City" and a tourist site.    Being from Philly it is A-OK for me but for the average tourist it is a great place to visit.

I wish i could give more stars, 5 are not enough for this gem.
We at the moment are living right across the street.
What can i say?
Fish Markets, check!!
Butchers, check!!
Produce, check!!
Pastries, check!!
Poultry Market, check!!
Diners, check!!
Check, chrck, check!!!!!
AMAZING PLACE!!!!!

Driving from eastern Massachusetts to the Beltway Region(Megalopolis Region ) can be one of the most nauseating experiences in the USA. Not because of the drive but what you see. How many Macys, Walmart, Old Navy, and Kohls do you see ? Probably infinite ! But in reality thats what the northeast corridor feels like. Coming to a place like Reading Terminal Market is a major relief. There are many food, produces, and home made gift outlets throughout this building. All of them are occupied by local bussiness, farmers across the regions, and of course the Amish. I would highly recommend visting any of the concessions owned by the Amish especially if you do not have the time to venture out to Amish Country in Lancaster County PA because it is one of the few places where you can find Amish goods.

Came back here for the ribs from downhome diner and it was insanely yummy! 

The wait was not too bad, even on a Sunday, the terminal was packed.  A lot of the diner patrons were sit-ins.  I ordered a rack of ribs.
http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=-Cw2rJx6v8gHgWOBXL3SsA

I also went to Dinic's to try another type of sandwich besides their famous pork sandwich.  I tried the pulled-pork and beef.  It was alright.  Their famous sandwich was more tastier with the brocolli rabe.  But man, the line was around the corner!!  It took like 1/2 hour to order the food.

In any case, the Reading Terminal is one of my fave places to visit while out in Philly.  It is vibrant and sooo much fun!  Love all the shops!
An institution in our city; almost sensory overload with so many people and so many choices where to eat.

If you are looking for a  Gastronomic Adventure You have come to the right place, desserts, breads, Italian, Asian, and  seafood just to name a few , The terminal  also allow you to experience the beautiful sides of our creative and unique crafters.

There really isn't a bad thing you could say about, basically, an upscale food court. You can find literally anything and everything in this place from amazing cheesesteaks to locally grown beets. It's definitely a place that takes a few minutes to get used to if you've never been, as it can be a bit hectic and anxiety-provoking, but you'll get over it once you see all the amazing food and other items for sale. I'm pretty sure there are black market sales going on in back rooms, that's how many things they sell. Who knows?
If you're visiting the city, it's a great place to go, especially if you have no idea where to eat. It's pretty accessible and has a parking garage that the market will validate for 3 hours maybe?

Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagies & Cheesesteaks is a must. Amazing...everything. The cheesesteaks are phenomenal and the cooks are super nice, unlike other cooks at some cheesesteak places around the city...

Bottom line: You won't regret going here, even if it's just to walk around and look at everything.

First time and it was a bit overwhelming when the guy approached us in the line wanting to know what we wanted to order and we couldn't even see the menu yet. I guess if you know the menu your ok, but he was a bit annoyed that we couldn't rattle off what we wanted. Then the lady at the counter who wanted to know what condiments I wanted on my sandwich "mam"med be twice! I'm not that old - but actually, it's more about the fact that I simply wasn't aware of the proper procedure to moving through the line. All that said, now I know and I'm sure I'll "perform" better the next time. I will return since we must frequently visit the hospital and  the sandwiches were indeed great tasting for what they are. My husband truly enjoyed the soup which is also a plus. 

Worth the learning curve
The best market around fresh meats some reasonable prices etc.I love this market. Great place to shop.

This is a must for good food in Philadelphia. Different and very good options. 
Go there hungry and be prepared to have great food, good prices and an amazing atmosphere.
Prices are reasonable.
An absolute must visit if you are in Philly!! There's truly nothing else like it! Tons of vendors in one location. You can find any tasty treat your heart desires!

I could not stop saying "wow" and "oh my gosh" to everything!! From the AMAZINGGG food/desserts to the various other vendors including candles, jams, cheeses and fresh produce- this place is AWESOME. I can't recommend it enough. So many places to eat and see!! I can't remember the names of these restaurants/vendors but you GOTTA Try the trainwreck sandwich- and the 3 meat platter (brisket, pastrami and corned beef). I could see myself visiting here very often if I lived here!! A must see in Philly!!!
Unbelievable! I could spend hours there. Truly heaven for foodies and connoisseurs! I'll be back with a big bag and lots of money in my pocket.....

You will be overwhelmed, you will be very overwhelmed.  In a good way though!  It's like we took spanish tapas markets like the botequin and the san miguel market and americanized them.  Little shops sell their specialties and everything is SO fresh.  Goods are also sold here (doorbells, nick nacks).  Reading terminal is very close to the bus terminal and city center, so this is a convenient location at the beginning, middle or end of your trips.  I went to the Dutch Eating Place, which is amazing and affordable.  However, there were lines to dine at many other places so I would look around and choose wisely!

Great addition of little stands and hawker stalls in Philadelphia. A walk through the market and one can experience cuisines and dishes from all over the world including the local favorite Philly Cheesesteak. 

When I came here with my friends, we had gator jambalaya, gumbo, Philly cheesesteaks, mango lassis, Indian iced tea and cookies from the local stands. The market is generally packed with customers and tourists so navigating through the narrow corridors is often hard. There is often long lines at the more popular stands. 

One complaint I did have however, was for the cleanliness of the dining tables and seating areas. When my friends and I went, we sat at a table that was oily and littered with crumbs. At least they provide sanitizing wipes, so I guess that makes up for that? 

Overall, I have a decent experience at Reading Terminal Market. They do close at 6 P.M. so get your grub-run in before then!

Whenever I have visitors, I take them here. There is something for everybody, and it is always a great time. It's super busy, so get comfortable with people standing really close to you.  We love Dinics, the spice/candy shop, every dessert area, and the jerky/meat stick vendor.  I can't go in without buying something I don't need, but definitely want.

Reading Terminal is the quaintest, most awesome place in Philly, as far as food goes. I hate that my favorite places inside don't take credit, but I guess that comes with the quaintness. Scallops, kale, and sweet potato drizzled in honey from Pearl's is something I get at least once a week when I walk to the Terminal on my break at work. The lamb hash from Border Springs Farm is incredible for breakfast. And don't get me started on the produce, I could go on forever !
The produce selection is great and a good price, plus lots of lunch counters,etc. wish I lived just a wee bit closer

It's a great place to go if you want to buy quality meats, seafood, produce, bread, spices, kitchen gadgets and other wonderful things in one building. Reading Terminal is lively and fun to walk around and look at things.

It's also a convenient place to grab lunch as there's a wide variety of cuisines and options. Sometimes it's tricky to find seatings, but you walk around and find something somewhere.

Although I can no longer indulge in cookies due to wheat allergy, I used to love cookies from Famous 4th Street Cookie Company. Their cookies are one of the most wonderful gifts from Reading Terminal. Bassett's Ice Cream is decent, too.

The only drawback is the parking situation. Street parking isn't always easy to find and it's 1 hour max.

Also, it's busy during the week, but tolerable. I'd never come here on the weekend when it's crazy packed unless I don't have a choice.

This is my favorite thing about this city. The terminal market has everything you would ever need. It's a place in which you can dabble in all your guilty pleasures. 

This market has everything from homemade pickles to cheeses to fudges to pancakes to fresh bread to gyros to cheese steaks. If you want to eat it, this market has it. 

The lines are long but the people watching is endless so time flys by faster than you expect even in some of the longest lines you will probably stand in. This is one of my all time favorite markets. 

Beiler's donuts is a must. It's one of the most spongy and bouncy donuts you will eat. They make the donuts right in front of you! Try the apple fritters!!! This place has a line that passes Dutch eating place and the fudge shop. 

This market has bee wax candles to little gift shops. It pays to stop by this market to pick up some little gifts and keepsakes. 

Another place you have to try is the Dutch eating place. The restaurant has great specials. Get their Ruben sandwich. This place is a must for breakfast.

One place I do not recommend is tommy dinic's. This place makes me angry cause I waited in line for so long just to get a low quality sandwich. I was expecting their sandwich to be delicious because of all the hype. I was a bit confused as to why people were so excited about this place. I really was so confused and I am still confused by it. I also feel like I will forever be confused as to why people are so infatuated by this place. It's really not worth the wait nor is the hype real. They don't have a huge depth of flavor profiles in their sandwich. I give dinic's two stars. But their service is quick and very friendly. 

Overall, this market is a must when in the city. It's worth your time and all the extra pounds you will most definitely gain.
Can find anything from Italian delis, gourmet coffee, seafood, cheeses, fresh produce, restaurants, etc. Can be difficult to walk around, but is worth it.

Uh excuse me why are you reading reviews? Do you really need to see the 100+ reviews stating this place is glorious? Because it really is glorious. Food on top of food on top of food. Delicious cakes, mouthwatering cuisine, awesome grocery items ranging from gigantic shrimp to produce, and just ... amazing. You can't go here and NOT buy at least something. I wish this place was closer but, alas ... it's a trip to go here. Not to mention it's CROWDED but this place is POPULAR so to be expected.

Do yourself a favor and hit this place up. You're not going to be disappointed. Well, you might be disappointed when you realize you can't buy every damn thing in the store but that will eventually fade.

Where do I start? Foremost I shop here for all of my meats every other Saturday morningI always go to the same great reliable purveyors-For Poultry, no one but Godshall, for Fish-John Yi and LHalteman's for everything else
The big surprise of this place is that the meats cost no more than a good quality supermarket except the quality and freshness is much better here.
Great place to people watch and take in the sights if you are a tourist. Hands down one of the best "farmers"  markets in the country

Which of the following do you enjoy?
a) markets
b) places that threaten to beat shoplifters to death
c) food
d) crowded places

If you answered any of the above, this place is for you!  I love love LOVE markets like this, and knowing that Flying Monkey Patisserie lives here was even more incentive to stop by!  I enjoyed an almond cupcake and was blown away by the variety of whoopie pies they offered too (snagged me a red velvet). 

I added actual nutrition to my lunch by getting some alligator gumbo that was mighty spicy and satisfying.  You'll find your fill of chocolate, ice cream, Italian food, Cajun, Thai, Chinese, sandwiches, Mediterranean, and candy here! 

What more could you ask for in a market??!

If you're ever in Philadelphia and want to visit a landmark, skip the liberty bell and come here and then maybe go back to the liberty for a walk once you're full. Seriously, this place makes me all kinds of excited, happy, nervous, anxious, in love and many many more emotions. Yes it may be completely overwhelming with the amount of people and vendors in this place but please make your way around the place! I like to make a complete circle around the entire place then work my way to the middle. There's cheese shops, Philly's famous cheesesteaks and roast pork sandwiches, fresh produce, fresh meat and fish markets, Indian food, Amish food, Chinese food, southern soul food, a florist, a book store, a delicious creamery, a bakery, oh and the list continues. If this has not made you get off your butt from where you are and head to philly, I don't know what will! Come to the Reading Terminal and all your food dreams will come true, at least mine has. (:

I love the reading terminal!! There's truly something for everyone! Bakeries, produce stands, cheese steaks, gyros, Chinese food, a grilled cheese place, pizza, a crepe place... And that's truly just to name a few! Besides being crowded around lunch time and probably dinner too, it is a fun place that everyone should visit.

One place I have to stop at whenever I visit Philly - just the vast amounts of crazy variety in one place - wheatgrass shots at one end, pork rolls at the other, Metropolitan bread mixed in - I'm in heaven :) Bathrooms are nasty though - don't use them!

I love all the variety you can find here. However, it is ALWAYS so crowded that it diminishes my enjoyment. I end up feeling overwhelmed and like I just need to make a choice, quick. Finding seating to eat, especially if you aren't alone, kinda sucks.
Just can't miss this place.  Outstanding experience just to walk around and see all of the choices...but great food options as well.  Had a Philly cheesesteak today.  Choices are endless.

Avoid if you have even mild anxiety about being trampled by cheesemongers, charcutiers, and/or tourists

Was able to buy an apple quickly and run out of exit #52

San Francisco tries to tempt me with the uber-posh, 100% organic, nauseatingly yuptastic Ferry Building.  Yet all I want on a Sunday morning is the Reading Terminal.  The Amish pretzels, Termini Bros., the ice cream, the roast pork sandwiches.  This place is what pregnant dreams are made of.  This is my own slice of heaven when I'm in town.  Double oink.

There were sooooo many options and I had the hungry burger and it was DELICIOUSSS! And I show a donut shop that had the most appetizing donuts I've ever seen! Like maple bacon and there were many other options of food as well! So I definitely recommend, was a bit crowdy but it was worth it!

Some of you may be thinking why review a fast food chain right? Well this particular one really stands out. The customer service is unbeatable and the place is always super clean. The manager himself comes out and asks everyone if they need anything. They clean up your table and refill your drink for you. Better service than a lot of restaurants with food that's double the price.

I love RTM.  My friend and I went the other day and we were both marveling about how unique it is.  I've never seen anything like it in another city.  I don't make it here as often as I would like to, but its a great spot to bring Philly visitors.  They have absolutely everything there including wine.

Not as bad of a tourist trap as I thought it was going to be.  The crowds on the Saturday afternoon I was there was fairly fast-paced and courteous for the most part.  The produce and seafood looked beautifully fresh.  The prepared foods made me wish I had more time in Philly to try all the treats.  We only made one (incredibly delicious) stop at the Miller's Twist for soft pretzel goodness, but trust me, if I had more time, I would have had tried more of the goodies Reading Terminal has to offer. I heard Dinic's is awesome and also recall people swearing by the Pennsylvania Dutch Diner there.

I love it here....truly a local jewel in our crown. It is crowded, large, at times overwhelming, but still perfect. The people watching is great, it always seems to have a great combo of tourists and locals. But the food....there is something for everyone. I could wander around here for hours on end. We are lucky to have this place!

Who doesn't love local city markets? They have a little bit of everything, amazing energy, and some of the best eats in the city! If you feel overwhelmed by choosing, look for the place with long lines... that's usually a sure sign it's got something worth trying. I would say this place has an equal mix of ready made foods, desserts, groceries, and other goods like kitchen supplies, soaps and pantry items. I'm pretty sure anyone could find something they're looking for here, and you can also usually find seating outside near the doors.

Believe everything you've heard about Reading Terminal Market and then some. RTM features a dizzying selection of specialty foods, ethnic foods, and wonderful eats - from sweet to savory - to satisfy any appetite. It's a foodies wet dream. 

Most people have heard of RTM and check them about because of the fanfare that Dinic's Roast Pork sandwich has received from the Travel Channel. I might take some heat for this - the sandwich is really good but a bit overrated IMO - but you do yourself a disservice if you have the opportunity to try one and don't. But you also do yourself a disservice if you go to RTM, eat at DiNic's, and don't explore or try anything else. 

The wife and I took the complimentary ride from our hotel to RTM, arrived at about 10:30AM, and spent about 90 minutes or so there. We started at Old City Coffee before heading over to DiNic's, and we also tried Miller's Twist (my favorite) and Flying Monkey Bakery (Whoopie Pies FTW!) We explored The Head Nut (insert joke here) and my wife enjoyed reliving her childhood while exploring Wursthaus Schmitz.

A few tips for the RTM n00b:

1. Read the review of my new Yelp Elite friend and Philly local Steven B. He covers many of the basics. Definitely make sure you go on a day where the Amish vendors are open!

2. If your mission is to try the famed Dinic's Roast Pork, plan strategically. The wife and I were in Philly Friday and Saturday, and we decided to come early Friday morning, guessing that would be the least crowded. We were right. We got to DiNic's about 10:45AM or so, and were lucky to get two seats that hat just opened up. 

3. The place gets crowded FAST. Be prepared for crowds. It wasn't crowded at all when we arrived, but by lunch time the market was packed with local workers on lunch break.

4. Plan ahead if you are a tourist and you want to purchase items to take out with you. This was our mistake. I planned to explore the market, but DiNic's was my main mission, so we came early and planned to go do the touristy stuff (Independence Hall, etc.) after. Unfortunately, this did not allow us to buy any product except what we stuffed in our bellies. Next time we visit Philly, we are considering staying at a nearby hotel to alleviate this issue.

Anyone who loves food and dares to call themselves a "foodie" will love this place. If you don't love Reading Terminal Market, you have no soul.
Great food really recommend!!! My aunt took me went there one time and the food is amazing and the service in there is really fast. love this place, I'll come back again

One of my go-to places in Philly. An absolute haven for all foodies, or anyone just looking for a great meal! There are so many food choices that it can actually be overwhelming! 
I always opt for DiNic's, and then stroll around for some desserts. I love the Amish bakery stands, everything is always fresh, delicious, and ALWAYS without that chemical taste. The donut stand is out of this world, the Elvis donut being my favorite. I can honestly say there isn't a single stand in the market that I don't enjoy, it's an amazing place!!

Organized very intelligently. There are obvious sections throughout the entire market making it a joy to stroll through. You will suddenly find yourself in the honey and handcrafted soaps section, or the eye poppingly fresh produce section. Everything here seems fresh and local. The prices are affordable and each vendor is willing to tell you about their wares. I saw the coolest mushroom stand here, with more species than I've ever seen in my life. My friend and I bought some gifts for our friends back home since we were travelling in Philly.

Must see for any tourist, must revisit for any local. The Terminal features everything you can imagine but many people get caught up in the most touristy spots and miss some of the best food in the place. I love Dinic's, sure it's super touristy but its the original philly sandwich and its a huge portion that is always consistently good. The only way to do a dinics sandwich is roast pork add sharp prov and long hots..I add rabe too. 

Some of the less known places: 

Sang Kee Peking Duck has the best dumplings in Philadelphia, and it looks shady enough to scare away the tourists. Order the steamed meat dumplings. Im not steering you wrong

Glick's Rib Shack - get the sandwich, it's deboned rib meat and cheese on a hoagie roll. Pretty damn good.

Dienner's BBQ chicken: Screw that soul food place which is touristy and panders on stereotypes, this is the only place to get fried chicken in the terminal, and their other flavors and wings are damn good too.

A must go to when in downtown Philadelphia. DiNics has a special place in my heart here however why stop there? So many varieties for made to order food and grocery stores for any taste. Whether you crazing seafood, pastries, a sandwich, or just a quick snack you'll be sure to find it here.

The reason I go to Reading Terminal:

There is an Amish Bakery in the way back against the wall.  They sell whoopie pies that are 5" in diameter and 2 1/2" thick.  They are sold for $1.  That's unheard of folks.

Great location. For the area... they do thier best to keep it clean. It also has a kids play area.

Although I never see kids in it.
Pro tip- buy your fruit and veggies here if you live in the city. Produce is very inexpensive compared to Trader Joe's and Whole Foods and is super fresh!

The service was great. The food was absolutely perfect. The bartender was the best. He heard me mention that it was our anniversary and made sure a dessert was brought over to us. We will definitely be back.  We will make sure to tell our friends.

I remember my first trip here YEARS ago. I didn't really understand the attraction. Having now lived in Center City, I can say I thoroughly enjoyed going here for a bit of groceries, a bit of good food, communal seating, and some great people-watching!!
Love the variety of stalls in this place.  My favorites are Termini Bakery and Metropolitan has the best bread.  Always great places to find lunch.  Don't forget Bassett's Ice Cream on your way out!

Haven't been to Chipotle in a while and will not go back. Went for fast dinner and most of not all hot foods were empty and looking sad. The place was so unappetizing that I left . I have eaten at chipotle.many times in the past and had good experiences . I don't leave low ratings but this place really deserved it
A must see when visiting Philly. The Amish doughnuts can't be beat, so don't even try! Great food and great prices. No complaints.

A recommended must for visitors of Philly that like food. A big market, full of surprises and locations serving good food, as well as fresh produce and groceries, flower shops, bakeries, you name it...
With a McDonalds on the corner of the most busiest intersections of Philly and high traffic flow of customers, why have bathrooms suitable for just one person? Ridiculous.

This is a must for any visit to Philadelphia.  I used to live near by, and I still try to pop in whenever I can just so I can walk in, breathe in all the fabulous food smells emanating from the different stalls, and take in all the colors and characters of the people who fill this place with the spirit of Philadelphia.

Once you walk in, you'll know why this place is constantly featured on the Food Network and the Travel Channel.

Fresh flowers? Check.
Amazing ice cream?  Check.
Award-winning cuisine?  Check.

I'm not sure which days they're there, but the Amish come in from the countryside and make the most amazing "broasted" chicken.  Yum yum.  Licking my lips just thinking about it.  They come in early and leave early, so try to catch them!

There is something for everyone in this place. It is sensory overload for food, coffee, desserts, veggies, wine, or just browzing. I went in 185lbs, I came out 210lbs. From Soft Philly Pretzels to Amish delights this place has it all. Go hungry, come out bloated! I wanted to eat everything at every stand in the place. The seafood there is insanely fresh. If you are a cheese fanatic you may never leave. Go there!

Holy moly!!! This market is huge! My eyes lit up in every direction I turned to.  It has everything you can imagine.  All types of fresh meats and seafood, desserts and pastries, burgers, pizza, sandwiches, cheese, crepes, fresh smoothies and juices, Chinese German Indian Pakistani & Middle Eastern food.  This place is just foodie heaven! They even have an oyster bar and a regular bar with TVs.  I wished I had more time to spend here to try all the different food options.  A must visit place in Philly for sure.
There are a few stands that accept SNAP (food stamps)  and all employees are always nice
A nice urban spot to have a quick bite/drink, I will definately return if I'm in the area again. Great atmosphere inside, although we opted for the outside area that was also good.
Looking for real iced tea,heres the place to try 'n let it flow your soul with Chick-Fil-A Iced Tea..not juz chicken winner

must go, must see.  i go almost every time i am in the city. lots of fun treats and huge variety of food, plus great people watching and stuff to see.  i highly recommend the pickles. no, seriously. the amish know what sup.

Reading Terminal Market is Awesome & a MUST for Foodies!  It's like SF Ferry Bldg and Emeryville Food Stalls 10x bigger & food stalls everywhere.  They even had street names inside.

I only got to check out a few things because of limited time & stomach.

Tommy DiNic's - Must try their Roast Pork w/ Extra Broccoli Rabe & Provolone Cheese $8.50 & $2 (rabe & cheese) - can CHARGE IT.

Bassetts Ice Cream - President Obama likes the Mint Chocolate Chip Ice Cream there.

B. got a Gumbo dish from Train Wreck - he liked it.

I got a couple cookies from Hope's Cookies - Tasted ok not that special.

GO!!
Great tourist spot with a large variety of foods and small businesses to see. It gets super crowded on weekends but is well worth a walk around. Pretty much everything here is good :)
Lots &  LOTS of good food here.  Just about something for everyone.  You definitely want to go hungry.

I love reading terminal!! Wish it was not so crowded on weekends but what can you do? Its a great place!

I can get relatively cheap produce, meat, seafood, grab lunch or a drink with friends, etc. It is a nice day out and a nice alternative to going to a grocery store. The only problem is is narrowing down where to eat!! So many good options. I also really enjoy that they have a bar so you can grab a drink if you need a break from shopping.

Just pay attention to the hours. I believe it closes early on Sundays.
Foodie? This is a Philly landmark, some of the food vendors are one-of-a-kind, some are very touristy, go for the experience, not the food.

The food is the food - it's chic-fil-a, it's fast food. This place stands apart in that the service, cleanliness, and attitudes are well above average. I don't just mean for fast food, but for any restaurant. Show up at lunch time on a weekday and you'll see the parking lot full, the drive thru full, and yet you still will find bathrooms and tables clean and ready. My order was taken quickly and with pleasure from the staff. The place was packed to the brim but yet a worker still came by to refill my drink. Later she came to take my tray. This isn't an exception, it's the rule.  Bottom line? This store is on point.

I will keep this brief since prior reviews say it all. Reading Terminal Market is a great place to walk around and pig out. There is something for everyone there from roasted Peking duck to freshly made chocolate. Florida, where I now live, does not have places like this and it is really a shame.

Everything is here, all the great spots. Busy and high turnover of people on weekends. Packed seating area but people are always coming and going so you'll find a spot. One of the best markets I've been to.
Very cool place to visit with about 100 different food stalls. Something for everyone's lunch, and well priced produce. A must visit (albeit a bit of a tourist trap)!
There's a lot so it's overwhelming. The food is fantastic everywhere, and the groceries are so fresh and cheap! Wish it was open longer.

My favorite place to eat in Philadelphia! Who couldn't love it with all it's options. You can get mexican, vegetarian, philly steak, hamburgers, pub food, bakery items--you name it they have it! 

I have several places that you will have to try...

1. Basic 4 Vegetarian Snack Bar: amazing. I recommend their Classic Veggie Burger. You may also try the Class BLT with soy bacon. I loved this bacon. At first I was nervous not having tried many soy products but it tasted so similar to the real thing minus all the yucky fat. With either grab a cup of lemonade and grab the nearest seat you can find! 

2. 12th St. Cantina. I used to eat here all the time before I stopped eating red meats and chicken. Plus, they offer their own seating so you don't have to fight for a table. Although, it's not the same!

3. Ice cream from Bassett's. 

4. Metropolitan Bakery and Old City Coffee for your grab and go!

You have completed my essential reading terminal guide.

Now all you have to do is get lost in the crowd and find the next best thing!

I do not recommend the vegetable gyro from Olympic Gyro. I just didn't take to it.

If you don't like crowds you won't like this place but keep an open mind and explore because the Reading Terminal is A LOT of fun!

Great place. Large. I stop there for fresh produce from time to time. During my last visit I stumbled up an herbal shop with plenty of cool teas. You can find coffee and much else here as well. Only 4 stars because some places and items are pricey.

Monopoly fans may recognize the Reading Terminal Market as part of the now famous Reading Railroad in the game, but Philadelphians may now associate good food with the Reading Railroad.
