This historic market outlasted the railroad, but kept the name. It is located in downtown Philadelphia with entrances on North 12th Street close to SEPTA and the subway.

The market has evolved mostly into a large food court, like most other public markets throughout the United States. There are still a good number of fresh food suppliers including butcher counters and produce stands, but most people head here for prepared goods and meals. Most of the individual businesses have separate reviews on Yelp.

Inside, the atmosphere is fun and crazy. There are lots of people and few directional signs making for a lot of confused people. This is not usually a problem since there are so many choices and unique options. The market opens early, but also closes early. This makes breakfast and lunch easy, but not so much for dinner. You can grab some raw meat for a long train ride home!

Anyone who enjoys food should visit Philadelphia. Anyone visiting Philadelphia will probably find something to enjoy at the Reading Terminal Market. It is still a bit rough around the edges, especially for suburban folks, but this is a fun and cool place to get your grub on.

Don't eat here!

The people that own this place are rude and disgusting, as is the restaurant itself

Went in to grab a sandwich and walked right back out after placing one foot inside this hole in the wall establishment.

This place should be condemned and the owners should not be allowed to work in the food service industry,

Two bad things about RTM (pronounced "Redding", I believe):  1)  They close too early!  We tried to stop in for dinner on Friday but were rejected.

2)  There's too many choices!  We came in for an early dinner/late lunch Saturday and spent nearly an hour trying to find what each of us wanted.

As a bunch of tourists, my sister, her boyfriend and I were completely surprised by this place as we walked from Chinatown back to our hotel.  There were so many sights, sounds, and smells to take in.  Definitely someplace to stop by in the city.  Oh, and as the place approaches closing, look for bargains on baked goods!  I got a delicious raspberry chocolate cookie for 75 cents!
probably getting a little too touristy and expensive but still great hopefully will not get back to the way it was
RTM has something for every foodie. Dinic's is always packed, and they run out early (especially the brisket). RTM is a don't miss, must-stop.

Wow!  What an awesome place.  Keep in mind that "market" is a misnomer, as what Reading Terminal is, is an amazing court with a congregation of suprisingly many good food stalls.  It's not a Pike Place market, or a St. Lawrence Market, but it is it's own unique, awesome food paradise.  I don't get why we don't have anything like this in NYC (no, Essex Market doesn't cut it - what a joke).  If I lived in Philly, I would be here every day.

This may not be the place for gourmet diners, because it really is just a bunch of food stalls put together.  It's a place where you can get crepes, pastrami, emu eggs, honeycombs and Amish bread in one place.  You could buy meats and groceries here, but I'm not sure that's the focus here, unless you want Amish meats, which are good quality and cheap.  Bathrooms are not bad - Pike Place bathrooms are worse.

Pro-tip:  anyone can go into the beer garden, even kids, and you can bring food in.  The only rule is one drink per person (which includes sodas).  So instead of paying $1.70 for a fountain drink outside, might as well use pay the same amount at the beer garden and get a table too.

Parking is $28!  If you spend more than two hours there, that is.  And it's easy for a tourist like me, sampling everything, to go beyond the limit.  I spent 3 hours in total here.

If I ever left Philadelphia, this is one of the places I would miss most. Its the ultimate one-stop-shop. I take all visitors and new Philadelphians here. From Termini's to the Dutch Eating Place it's really the best place to eat and people watch. So why only four stars? What happened to The Basic Four vegetarian place?! I ache over its closing...

This market is one of a kind. The myriad of food and drinks is incredible. If you are looking for a place to take a friend from out of town this is it. 

I would recommend going during the week to avoid the ridiculous crowds which hoard the market on the weekend.

Love, love, love!  The only thing I don't like about The Reading Terminal Market is the hours! I wish it was 24 hours.  I love everything else, even the lines and the crowds. It's special and popular.

A perfect spot on a day when the weather is not ideal outside and you want to kill a couple hours snacking, dining, drinking, shopping in a cool marketplace atmosphere.  I enjoyed my time there during my trip to Philly last week.

I love German food and there is a stall toward the back of the market where they cook up a nice pork schnitzel, potato pancake, and german potato salad.  It would not compete with the best German restaurants I have visited, but it is very passable for a fan of that style of food.  I enjoyed it.

Then just step across the way and have a beer (I forget the name of the place....but it is directly across from the German spot)

If I ever moved far away I would miss the Reading Terminal. It reminds me of an indoor mall focused around food. It's a fat kid's dream to eat here because they have a little bit of everything. From fried chicken to vegetarian, from crepes to muffins, from cheap Amish breakfast to expensive fancy cakes---a tourist would need a big appetite to check it all out. 

Bring your patience because the lines can become gruesome, the bathrooms can be a disaster and the table seats can be all taken up. Still, I love it for its variety and fantastic food.

Why would it be less than 5 stars? I guess it's crowded but that's because it offers so much and I take that as a good sign, obviously. We mostly go here for the lovely selection of raw milk and meats from the Fair Food Farmstand but we've eaten lunch at a few of the stalls and bought some very tasty cookies here before, too. It's a great place and we are grateful to have it in philadelphia. We drive an hour to get here! I guess my only beef is that a validated ticket only gets you a $2 discount in the parking garage... mostly in other places, validation gets you free parking (we spend 60-100 bucks here sometimes!) but such is life. Now we've taken to dropping one of us off and circling the area until we get our goodies lol!

Took my mom to Pearls for clam chowder and crab mac and cheese. Fantastic!  She loved them both, and had cookies from 4 st Bakery.
Perfect end of the day.
 I love the terminal's food court. Its a wonderful treat as they have everything that my picky family can enjoy as we all want something different. 
The bonus is everything is fresh. A great place to stop and enjoy a meal during any Center City travels.
Everyone here is very friendly and all about customer service. The food is always good, but it's better to go inside and order since the drive thru line is constantly packed.

Absolutely everything you could ever imagine inside! If you're not quite sure what to eat, after a stroll through here, you'll then be confused which place to choose...and then still return for your next meal to try something else! The options are endless. I promise you'll find something you like!

Reading terminal is like an Amish market in the middle of the city. You can get just about anything here. Donuts, seafood, Asian fusion, cheese steak sandwiches, Even produce!! If have been here quite a few time while passing and I look forward to coming back again.
I tried their Paneer Masala roll, and it was delicious, juicy, and filling :) this is my new favorite place now!
This place has every type of food you could ever want.  Without question, the best place to go for a quick bite in Philadelphia..  maybe even the world!

If you can't find something you like here, there's something wrong.

The market is an interesting combination of hot/prepared foods meant to be consumed immediately and grocery-type specialty meats and produce. 

The market is extremely crowded on Saturdays and sometimes Sundays, but you will still be able to move.  Highlights for me are DiNic's Roast Pork and the Flying Monkey, but everyone has a favorite once they've been a few times. My close friend is partial to the Turkey place where you can get Thanksgiving dinner year-round.

There's always something interesting to see/smell/hear.

Ive only eaten at a handful of places, in the RTM, but theres DiNics , which is good enough on its own to warrant a visit there, other than that to be honest, theres so many damn places I cant remember the name of them all .  I know thm as "that cookie place"..etc. 

Right across the street from the hotel where the valet stole my phone, hard to get to in terms of parking unless you're going to park in a lot, or at the Radisson downtown ... where your phone will disappear like David friggin Copperfield if you aren't careful 

If you're near City hall in Center city Philly you really cant miss, they have everything in there .

This is another fun place to take out of town people.  A fun experience but I wouldn't necessarily come out of my way.  The groceries from the produce place always look fresh and the prices are pretty good too.  I don't know how I feel about buying my meats from here.... But I like the hustle feel to the place too and it reminds me of a market from back in the day but with modern conveniences.  The rows are tight and it can get busy here on the weekends and during lunch time.  I have to say the bathrooms are some of the nastiest I have seen (including port-o-potties) but other than that Reading Terminal is pretty clean.  We often stop in for Bassetts ice cream.  I don't know why since it tastes the same as any other ice cream but I think it's the novelty of the place.

I love this indoor Farmer's market!

It's filled with an eclectic medley of food from all over the world (and all very tasty!), fresh veggies, fruit, meat, seafood and kitchen gadgets.  In the mood for a full on Thanksgiving dinner?  You got it!  An infamous D'Nics pork sammie that almost always sell out before closing?  Yup, you can find that here.  How about a chocolate covered raw onion?  They have that too.

You get the gist.  You name it, they have it!

Just a FYI: everything Amish is closed on Sundays due to holiday.
The paneer masala roll and the MK special chicken and rice were on point! Great tasting, cheap and they deliver!
One of those great spots frequented by locals and tourists.   Not a tourist trap. The locals eat and shop here!!
I loooove this place!!! Haven't been in a while and have been trying to get back.. eventually I will:-)
This place is awesome and so much fun! On the weekends it's busy but all the booths are open and has a great vibe. Great place to go for lunch or grocery shopping.

Dinic's for the pork & broccoli rabe sandwich 
Oyster Bay breakfast of chicken & waffles eggs Benedict- YUM!! Also the shrimp & grits my boyfriend loved!
All the produce is super fresh
Love beef jerky? 5 cases of it!

Great place to pick up fresh fish and meat. If I lived in Philadelphia, I'd be here weekly!

Great place to browse, eat, and shop!! Cool and touristy, I always bring family and friends who visit. It gets really crowded on Saturdays though, so be sure to visit from Sunday-Friday to avoid the cramped feeling.

A unique food hall in Philadelphia, the Reading Terminal Market provided an abundance of food options with a dearth of time available to try it all. The options available range from the Philly Cheesesteak to Mediterranean cuisine and everything in between. I ate at the 12th Street Cantina, and the food there was particularly good. The atmosphere at the Reading Terminal Market makes it a necessary tourist attraction, and the only downside to it is the 6pm close time. Overall, I would recommend the Reading Terminal Market to anyone looking for a unique food hall with an abundance of options.
So many options to choose from. I recommend 12th St Cantina if you like Spanish food. You can find practically anything here!

I discovered this little treasure shortly after moving into CC 3 years ago. It is my "go to" place whenever I want something quick and tasty. I'm not crazy about wraps in general - so I usually stick to the platters. My two favorites are the Chicken and Lamb and the Chicken Biryani. I'm a pretty big guy with a healthy appetite - but either platter ends up being two meals for me. Others have complained about the service. I would agree that they are not the chattiest bunch - but I've always found them to be courteous and polite. With tax the platters come to $9.72 - a rare bargain for this quality of carefully prepared authentic Kolkata street food.
Definitely a great place to stop in while on the go. They have so many varieties of food that I think would satisfy most. I am gluten free and the options are amazing. The staff is very friendly too.

You can get an incredible Amish breakfast (complete with a pound of butter and bacon grease), a delicious fruit smoothie, stop off at the butcher for some freshly chopped steak, and grab all the spices you need to marinate it, all within 10 minutes. 

Candy shops, seafood, butchers, spices, drinks, sandwiches, short order breakfast...and dare I say it.......oh I dare...beer. 

This place is also complete with a shoe shine stop and a piano. 

Sure it gets a little crowded, but what do you expect? It's like Disney World for the middle age man...you have women in bonnets cooking breakfast, tons of meat, a guy shining your shoes, some entertainment on the ole upright and a bar. If that ain't livin'...
The dumplings are delicious, and the service is fantastic. The cheesecake dumplings are particularly great!
Wonderful variety of delicious food, beverages, and cool gadgets. Excellent people watching also!
Fun place to go to get food, lots of options.  It was very crowded though.  Definitely a place to go to if you are visiting Philadelphia
I'm a huge fan of going here for breakfast or lunch.  Crepes, cheesesteaks, pork sandwiches, Amish bread.  So so good!

If you're planning a trip to Philadelphia, I highly recommend a visit here. I especially like going there for lunch. It does get crowded, so get there early. Then you can sit, enjoy your lunch and watch the flood of people...great people watching.
ex, c xccxx xczcxc crevices x cXXxx,cxxxcxxfccxcxzcxcxx xsx,xzxxvxczcZxzczxxdcxxccxxccSCvfx cx c c

Oh my GOSH!!!  THis city and it's market's are amazing!!  Puts the French Market in Chicago to shame, same with the Milwaukee Public.  This place is off the charts....I was stressed out at how much I could stuff in just being in Philly for the weekend.  Skip the cheese steak rivals and come here, food is amazing!  Had the pork at        Di nicks and the oyster po boy at the Cajan place, both were off the charts good!!!
P.s-it is open on Sunday but soooo many vendors are closed.  :(
Love it.. Everything you might want to eat , you can find it there . The Terminal is a Mall of Small restaurants ,Breakfast , Lunch or Dinner  Junk Food , all Day Long...

Holy agoraphobia Batman, there are too many people here! But that means it's good right? Yasss.

Reading Terminal Market (pronounced Redding, according to locals) is downtown, was walking distance from our hotel, is always busy, and is full of diverse delicious options (tho you may not have a place to sit when you get your food).  

If you ever go out to eat with me, you know my first 5 or 6 orders are just practice...even worse in a location like this with tons of vendors...

Oooh, I want apple turnovers made by Amish chicks!
Wait, I want a pork sandwich!
German food, that's it!
OMG fresh oysters!
Mmmmmm crepes!
Lobster, definitely lobster! Wait no, they're too cute swimming around in that tank.

Nah, I'm just gonna eat healthy I said. Cut to us standing in line for fried chicken and waffles at Keven Parker Soul Food. 

As I'm eating my delicious meal I'm considering my many dessert options - 
Cookies/Cupcakes/Crepes/Ice cream/Fresh fruit/Fudge 

But, after waiting so long for lunch and eating every last bit of food (5 fluffy little waffles, 3 pcs of fried chicken, and the bestest cheesiest gooeyest mac n cheese I have ever had and this watermelon sweet tea I sucked down way too fast) we were full and tired and done squeezing though people and waiting in line. 

I would totally recommend this chaos to anyone visiting the area, just be ready for the crowd and get there before the hangry sets in.

Great assortment of markets, breakfast/lunch/dinner/treat spots, and other various stores. Where else can you get soul food, crepes, cheesesteaks, ice cream, chinese, seafood, and pumplecake (pies baked into a two layer cake - visit the Flying Monkey)? Almost every type of food you can think of is here, which makes it great for groups, tourists, and out of town friends. What doesn't make it group friendly is how crowded it can get during peak times. Seating is limited, and much of it is reserved for patrons of a particular shop. They do put some tables outside when it's warm, so try to snag one of those and escape the craziness.

Some things are overpriced, but some of ridiculously cheap. You just have to know where to go. Iovine Bros produce is one of the cheaper ones, with most of it's offering hovering around $1/lb. If you're looking for a deal, come right before closing when the vendors are packing up. Places like Famous 4th St cookies offer 'dollar holler" where all cookies are $1 towards the end of the day.

FOOD GALORE!  What more can I say!
Foods from all over the world and an amish market place!!
Make sure you are hungry because you are going to want to get a little bit of EVERYTHING!!!

Talk about busy!!!  A group of us went to the Flower Show, and ventured across the street for lunch.  We could barely walk, it was so crowded.  After finally depening on a place to eat, (DiNic's), we got in line, and it didn't take long to find seats and order.  Fast, good, enjoyable, with great atmosphere.  Don't go if you want quiet ambiance!

Wow!  When Pizza Beddia closed and this place opened there was no difference. Very surprising how good the special veggie pizza was!  Had to get the tomato pie, pepperoni, and special.  Hopefully they sell pies in the future!

Such a wonderful place! Every time we go we find something new to try, although DiNic's will always be our favorite! From shopping for groceries, produce, and fresh spices (Head Nut!) to grabbing a great lunch, to being undecided for dessert because there are just so many options.... Reading Terminal is always an amazing trip.

If you've never been, it's a must.  Delicious and varied food.  

If you work nearby like I do, it's a great option to include in your lunch hour weekly rotation.

If you have sensory issues or anxiety in crowds, try avoiding lunch hour and definitely avoid days when Philadelphia is playing host to a national convention or a worldwide clerical leader.

Some, but not all, entrances are wheelchair/stroller accessible.

I went to this place during the Chinatown Festival. Looking for Asian-inspired foods, I came across the Humpty's Dumpling's food truck. These dumplings were unique in that they were deep fried, but came at a steep price. 5 small dumplings ran $7. The winners were asian pork, the chipotle chicken was a little on the milder side, and the cauliflower dumpling was great! I just don't think they were worth the steep cost - but I am happy I tried them out once.

This is a fun place to bring anyone who visits Philly for the first time.  A lot of great variety with some classic Pennsylvania/Philly foods like several Pretzel stands and Amish food stores.  The ambiance is great too since it's indoors but all of the stands are not separated by walls.

The Terminal is as good as it gets in terms of varieties of great food carefully prepared by independent venders!  I've been eating lunch here on and off for over 30 years.  (At the start a cone at Bassett's Ice Cream was $.95!!)  My favorites at this time are the Down Home Diner and Dinic's Roast Pork.  You can also do all you grocery shopping here for fresh, local, often organic meats, fish and seafood, produce and breads, as well as coffee, tea, spices, other baked goods, etc.   Lunch at the Terminal if you are visiting Philly is a MUST.
Great shopping and great vendors. Can get busy so if you're local and plan to do your grocery shopping here, go during the week.

The Market is a collection of vendors selling everything from dinner, cookies, fresh veggies and meats to souvenirs. It is loud, sometimes crowded on weekends (very crowded, hence 4 stars and not 5) and very fun. This is one of those places that a tourist should not miss, come to have lunch and by a few things to bring home.  Don't forget to try a hot, fresh pretzel.

There is no place like it every thing is delicious and fresh. If you haven't been go and don't be overwhelmed by the crowd just go with the flow and who knows what gem you will stumble upon. One of my favorites is Dieners bbq and the juice stand right across from it. The only reason it's not 5 stars is because they closed the beer garden. It was the perfect place to go after collecting all of your delicious treats to sit, get a cold pitcher of black and tan and eat. It was a place for locals our private little nook.
Love love love this place! A true Pennsylvania experience. Give yourself lots of time to explore this Philly gem!

The cashier, Paula service is so bad. I have been to this Chick-fil-A several times but this time is so disappoint. She never say thank you and speaking without look at me. Most ppl who work here their service is good only her is not good. I came here 2.05 of Aug 13 she is on the third cashier from the left. I won't come back here again!!! Never!!!

I have gone here various times and was excited to get back from break to try it again yesterday. I typically create my own items on the menu as they give you the option to. However, I was indecisive about the dressing choice for my salad. The staff was super friendly from the minute I walked in, they even offered a dressing recommendation and let me try it. As a temple student, I find poor customer service at just about every on campus eatery, however I am specifically writing this review to comment on how well the customer service team at this location is. I frequent eateries like this such as sweet green, fuel, and never receive customer service or quality like honey grow ! Highly recommended
I always love this place when we come to town. The vendors are thoughtful and all about customer service.  The food is delicious. The entire place oozes character.

It was my first time going to this location. It was clean, the guy was really nice and order was correct. I say this because we had multiple orders (apprx 10) and he was great about it all. We used groupon which they easily honored. They had different flavors, I guess because of the season, while they weren't my favorite or as good as the previous everyone seemed pretty content in general. I personally was not impressed by the asian pork. The other dumpling with broccoli rabe was way better. The chipotle wasn't terrible but I was looking for a kick. I was told the spinach seems like frozen spinach but still okay. I would suggest get some icing dips for the deserts. Please bring back the cheesecake one as well as the broccoli rabe and meat. It is a fun "meal" because you can order one of each flavor and try something new. 

I will definitely go back either way. Just plan to wait for the flavors to change.

Reading Terminal...How I love you...let me count the ways. 

The first piece of advice I can offer is to take a lap around the market before commiting yourself to the first delicious treat that you stumble actoss. There's a lot of real estate to cover, you're best bet is to window shop first and commit later. From savory sandwiches to sweet treats from antique trains to novelty goods you're sure to find something for everyone here. 

If you have a need for Amish goods you have several options but be mindful of the hours. The Amish vendors tend to leave earlier than others and do not open on Sunday. It's well worth working around the time restraints; the pretzels, donuts and butcher offerings are my top recommendations. 

Stop for breakfast, stay for lunch and buy fresh ingredients for dinner. You're welcome.

Had a misunderstanding over an advertisement on the app. No big deal. That is until I was. Belittled verbally abused by an African-American Muslim girl from behind the counter who indicated I was slowing up her line. Her belligerence and my desire to get the hell out of there forced me to spend money I really didn't want to only because I didn't feel like going to another restaurant such as this and be abused by somebody worse than this young lady if that's possible.
I have a good bit of money left on the Chick-fil-A app. I would sooner flush it down the toilet or give it away ever set foot in that restaurant again which is a shame because my eight-year-old daughter loves the play area

name of the game: Variety.

i like this place because you can get just about anything you want...if you have picky friends and can't decide on a restaurant, just bring them here. 
highlights: 4th st. cookie (huge cookies...you're bound to break out after having ONE), ice cream....they give you so much...so make sure you share, amish pretzels, rib stand...

I have been to Afghanistan and India and are this kind of stuff in NYC forever, this is the best chicken Briyani the world has to offer. They just nail the sauces and bread which is crucial. It takes me a long time on saturdays to get there but I'm always so happy afterwards it's worth it. There Kati rolls are spiced perfectly. They are super nice too. I had an event catered from there and the food was gone in seconds, it was breakfast time too! Very professional.

Fantastic market! We didn't expect it to be open on Sunday (and there were fewer merchants operating) but we still managed to get a great breakfast.

Great selection of produce and gourmet items.

As a market this is a place where you can get just about anything.  Need a custom cut of meat, no problem.  Need an unusual spice, you can get it.  The quality of the food and produce is excellent and there are many choices so don't go to the fist purveyor you see.  Cheese, seafood, soul food, Asian cuisine galore, Cajun, southern, German beer garden, Amish produce and bakery, everything!
There are lunch counters with every delicacy you can imagine.  You can also arrange for catering or take out.  There is ample parking nearby and the market offers validation if you shop there.  
A word of caution if there is a convention or if go to the market on a Saturday.  Go early; this place is can be a zoo.
LOVE this place! They have so many great food spots that it will satisfy everyone! If you're visiting Philly it's a must.

Simply put, you can find anything you want here - and all at great prices!! But no matter how distracted you get by the tempting smells and delicious food, don't leave without a Beilers Donut!!! It'll easily be the best $0.95 you've spent in a long time!

This review is for Beiler's bakery particularly the prepared salad. My favorite is the cranberry walnut salad and the buffalo ham which is spicy. They sell it by the pound in different sizes of containers. It's right next to the donuts

So many good options. I always go to Shanghai Kitchen for the best and most fresh Chinese food. My order is always done in 5 minutes or less and I have yet to find anything nearly as good anywhere else in the city

I loved walking around here and being able to have a choice of anything you want to eat!  

Ate breakfast one morning at a diner-esque sorta place with only a counter to the far left side of the place... it was fantastic!  

I can't wait to go back to Philly!
Great choices. The doughnuts are freshly made and simply out of the world. The stall with the cheese sandwiches was amazing.

If you're in Philadelphia you must stop at Reading Terminal Market. It has become my Saturday tradition and there's something for everyone here! At Profi's Creperie, I highly recommend the Nutella and Banana crepe, but they also make a great breakfast sandwich with fresh croissant.  The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company sells cookies by the pound and it's easy to get carried away with the warm gooey goodness. The authentic amish donuts at Beiler's Donuts and Salads are ridiculously fantastic, seriously. The line is always super long. BEWARE they are closed on Sundays. The Cheesesteaks from Carmen's are just OK. The roast pork sandwhich at DiNic's is great! Wursthaus Schmitz also does an awesome bratwurst and potato pancakes.

Next up on the to-eat list:
The Original Turkey
Rib Stand
Soul Food Cafe
Dienner's Bar-B-Q
Must visit if you come to Philly. A real, Culture, as well as, Culinary experience, in the Heart of the City. It has everything that typifies the City.

I always enjoy coming here. The local meats and dairy are really cool. There are some great prepared food items to try here to. Hershel's pastrami is a real hidden gem that you should check out on your next visit.

This place is literally FOOD HEAVEN! It is a massive food mall and ANYTHING you want you can literally have. From dessert to soul food. From salad to gyros. From Chinese to Cajun or Mexican or Italiam. You can even buy fresh produce and meats. 

Great experience!!!
When in Philadelphia you must check this market out. Everything you can think of is sold here. Fresh breads, fish, meats, desserts. It's quite an experience

First time here let me say the service that we received was top notch! We sat outside and it was kind of a chilly night. The waitress greeted us quickly, made us aware of the specials both food and drink. We were just a little outside of happy hour but she said she would still make sure if we wanted something from the happy hour menu we could. Pretty cool i think she took out drink order I got the mummers punch I highly recommend that I should have gotten the bowl of it which would give you 5 drinks. I ordered them single dummy me. The manager came out to bring a food order to the table behind us, as he walked back to go into the restaurant he asked if we wanted the heaters above us on. Yes as the two lovely ladies I was with didn't bring jackets.We ordered an app off the happy hour menu General Tao's chicken wings, wow very good promising we thought. Then the burgers came wow did these come out of the same kitchen, Not at all what I would call a burger sorry Industry you went from a 4 to 5 star to a 3. Might have been a one if not for the drink, apps, service. We did order desert we ordered the pumpkin donuts. All though they were good and hot not much of a pumpkin taste, the crème anglaise was banging, as was that damn cheese sauce they give for the fries. They should serve that as a drink I would drink it seriously it was that good. So to recap, Service = 5 no question. Drinks = 5, App = 5, Burger -5 that's right negative, cheese for fries = ++100, donuts = 2, crème anglaise = ++100. Would I go back again yes on the service alone I would but next time we will try another entree.
Nice if you can handle the crushing amount of tourists.  I haven't really explored the whole thing because of this reason.
Man I Looove The Reading Terminal Market The Dutch Bakery's Are My Favorite And I Brought Beef Jerky Out Of There And man it's so good

Staff looks very upset, non caring, not welcoming at all. Put soy sauce in box with Dumplings and sauce was everywhere. My dumplings came loose at the bottom and they were very soggy. If you don't like your job and don't want to put out quality food, quit!!!

This market was right across the street from our hotel.  It was our morning destination each day!    Might I suggest the following:

Spataro's (Philly Cheesesteak Breakfast Sandwich)
Molly Malloy's (Spicy Hash, yogurt and granola, steel ground oatmeal)
Market Bakery (Fantastic bagels and croissants)
Old City Coffee (Great locally roasted coffee!!!)
Kamal's  (for daily smoothies)
Beller's Donuts (Every kind of flavor you could possibly want)
Termini Bros (Grab the Cannoli!)

Besides foods, there are bookstores, a French linen stall, herbs, teas, etc.

This place is flat out awesome.  I'm not sure what the name of the produce place is, but it's perfect.  I think it's only on Sundays but they give student discounts so hold on to that school ID after graduation (all you cheap asses...... like me).

For starters, the terminal discounts the parking if you spend over $10; $3 parking in center city - can you beat that?  Second, go grocery shopping and sit down at almost ANY of the little shops because they're all awesome.

The only reason I'm giving them 4-stars is because of what they're doing to Rick's Steaks.  Not that I'm a huge fan of any cheese steak place other than Delassandro's, but Rick's is a small business that has held up their end of the lease for close to 50 yrs, if not more.  The RTM is kicking them out simply because they want a bigger "cheese steak name vendor."
Great place to get meat, lunch, ice cream, coffee, fresh juice, flowers ... And very crowded on weekends lol

Reading Terminal Market is probably the first place I would bring family or friends when they visit Philadelphia.  It is a fun experience, and pretty accessible via the train system.  There are dining and shopping options for just about everyone.  There are Amish bakeries and butchers, candy shops, a great roast pork spot, foods of every ethnicity, produce shops, cheese shops, a book shop, and much more.  
Being a New Orleans native, I was surprised to find a New Orleans stall with fairly legitimate food (I am quite picky about that).  
You can get almost the entire Philly food experience in one go at Reading.  Dinic's offers a great roast pork sandwich, you can enjoy Amish cheeses or baked goods, and there is a tourist-like shop in the back with local items.  If you are in Philadelphia for a conference, this is a good way to get the experience quickly.
The market will be crowded almost around the clock, so be prepared for that if you have small children.  Kids will love the candy shops and the Bassett's Ice Cream.  One candy shop has chocolate-covered onions for the most daring.

I love this place! There is so much variety! I especially love the Amish pastries & donuts. This place can be overwhelming if you're trying to find people to meet up, but luckily there is a center aisle for seating and eating. This place is great for local products, and I like to support the locals because it is their livelihood. Plus they put passion into making their food and that is what counts nowadays! Definitely, if I come back to Philly, I would stop by multiple times just for the pastries. Yum!

Wow... This place is amazing!!!  I was visiting Philly and I came here on a Saturday afternoon with a friend.  It was completely packed! So many choices for food and desserts.  I enjoyed visiting the market to grab a quick bite,  but it was hard maneuvering through this crowded place.

Oh the Reading Terminal Market!  What can I say about you?  I dream of days past when I walked through your stalls and smelled the glorious smells wafting from within.  

Being a Californian I only get there a few times a year but I look forward to it every time.  Its a MUST stop when I am in Philly.  Crepes, cheese steaks, Southern food, Chinese food....the options are endless!!  

Love the Amish people in their nike sneakers!!

Has a little bit of everything -- go wild and try it all!!!

You really can not go wrong with a lot of the places. The only con is that it does get very crowded and thus seating may be a little hard to come by. 

If you are visiting the city - this is a MUST visit

Actually made a night of dinner and drinks with my fiance on Sunday.

Service was great the entire time. 

We ordered the following to eat:
-buffalo sweetbreads
-fish special (wahoo)
-fries

All excellent! 

After a couple beers, wine, and 3 mixed drinks our bill came to about $76 plus tip. Definitely looking forward to my 4th trip and many more to come.

I never thought I would see a place like that here in the U.S, it's amazing! However I have to consider a few things, first is the time they close, it's just ridiculous! I went there for dinner at 7pm expecting I would find it full of people and the doors were closed already! Also on Sunday only about half of the stores are opened (I believe many of the owners come from traditional places around PA) which I understand, but if they want to develop tourism they should really reconsider about all these things.
Tasty tasty burger and peppery fries and deep amber beer. Enough said.
Love coming here. Always have a large selection for the things I need and it just always a good time walking around. Can't beat the cheap produce at Iovine's either!

I really loved Skillets, it was nice to sit outside, and the staff was really friendly..we came to eat just after noon on a saturday. This was a slightly slow time, as I think we were in between times..The food was tasty, the service was good and friendly, and I would definitely take my hubby here for a nice breakfast. you can even bring fido, and they give them water etc...
 I like to patronize the local eateries when ever I can, as its good for the community...

After visiting a patient across the street for a few days in a row, it's nice to have a dependable great lunch here with friendly people. Roast beef and the Mediterranean sandwiches were good. The cookies are a must, chocolate chocolate chip and sugar cookies are worthy of their own store.

Every time I've visited Philly, I've made it a point to stop here. Everyone should, because it is the best day of food you will experience here or really anywhere. The only bad thing about Reading Terminal is that I haven't yet developed the stomach capacity to eat everything that I want to in one trip. If you live in the area and you haven't tried this place, do so now, but at your own risk--you might be coming back every day and gaining 10 pounds in the process. I know I would. 

Here are my favorite places to check out:

-the amish pretzels (so deliciously buttered)
-Dutch Eating Place (the Amish also make a damn good breakfast)
-Bassett's Ice Cream
-4th Street Cookies

The produce and the flowers are also fresh and beautiful. Basically, this place is paradise.
Really cool place - an all indoor market with great food options. Love stopping in for cheesesteaks and cannolis!!
Pretty decent food, wait staff is extremely funny and helpful. Definitely worth checking out.

This place is the worst. First of all it's filthy, they let homeless people , crackheads and prostitutes use the bathroom and basically just hang out throughout the whole place.  The kids that play in the play place are filthy and rude it's sticky and gross constantly.  The people working there are so rude and miserable I am sure they hate their lives and their jobs.. The worst part is they allow pan handlers to loiter right outside the door they do not make them leave and they  harass and beg for money from every single customer coming in and out.  I would not step foot in this place if I were paid to..  Stay away! Far away!

The perfect venue to experience Philly's diverse food selection and community. Come with an appetite and you'll leave with a full belly and a appetite to try more. Only downside, the place gets packed! If you're not into large crowds open to close then this might not be the venue for you. But if you want to see one of Philly gems, head on over!

The food. So. Many. Options. Foodie's heaven.

So many things to recommend: Bassett's Ice Cream, Beck's Cajun Cafe, Hunger Burger, Jonathan Best Gourmet Grocer, Famous 4th Street Cookie, Flying Monkey Bakery. And so many more left to try. As always! Will add more as I go.

I stopped in the other night for the first time, and was very impressed. One of the three very friendly staff people approached me right away and asked if it was my first time at Snap. I said yes, and he offered to give me a full "tour" of the place, which I appreciated. It's not a large place, by any means, but the wall of refrigerated food offerings was a bit overwhelming for a first-timer. The food is organized by meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner, salad, soup, snack, beverage, etc.), and there are lots of options. Many things come in multiple sizes, to cater to different diets and appetites. The food is well-packaged and clearly labeled, and the labels include the list of ingredients and really thorough nutritional information (calories, fat, carbs, sodium, protein, sugars, etc.). Gluten-free, paleo, low sodium, low carb, and other such classifications are also on the labels. Almost everything in the store is gluten-free. 

I had a really hard time deciding what to buy, because everything looked and sounded so good. I opted for the Grass-fed Bison Quinoa Hash, because I'd never had bison before; the Grass-fed Beef Meatballs and Peppers and Grilled Kale Hoppin' John, because the salesperson recommended them; and the Naked Chicken, because I figured it would go well on top of a salad. I've eaten everything but the meatballs at this point, and have been really happy with all that I've tasted. The bison and quinoa hash was really well-spiced and flavorful, and it kept me full way longer than I expected it to. The chicken came with spicy, roasted cauliflower and garlic snap peas, and was delicious and filling on top of a bed of arugula (though I'm sure it would be good on its own as well). My only complaint so far is that I could have eaten a bit more of the Hoppin' John, and it only comes in one size. I think it might do better as a side than as a whole meal, but I'd definitely buy it again. 

Overall, I've been very pleased with my Snap experience and I plan to go back again next week to try a few more dishes. I've heard others say that the prices are a bit high, but as someone who does a lot of cooking AND a lot of ordering out, I would say that the meals seem fairly priced. I paid $37 for four meals--and received a complimentary bottle of their cold-pressed Antioxidant juice, which was nice. (The juice has cayenne and jalapeno in it, so it's spicy, but good!)

This place is friggin' awesome.    It is a huge market that has a lot of local vendors selling everything from fresh fish to Amish sticky buns to flowers.   I seriously wish there was something unpretentious like this near me...the SF Ferry building wishes it could be like the Reading Terminal Market.  The best thing about the place is walking around looking for "People Love Us on Yelp" stickers :)

Tips:

Looking for fresh produce? Go to the produce stand in the middle by the food court. They have great .99cent bags and if you have a student ID you get 10% off, and they have a great selection of items. 

Looking for eggs? Smuckers not only has a great grill to get lunch, but they have farm fresh eggs for $2.65/dozen. They also have LevelUp

Looking for natural/GLUTEN FREE baking and cooking items? There is a little convenient store with various kitchen food necessities and have very decent prices (compared to Whole Foods) and it is again toward the middle of RTM. 

Looking for an adult beverage? Maggie Malloys just opened and I hear great things! 

Looking for natural tea and health cures? Herbiary (right around the corner from the diner) has a great selection of teas and natural products and cures. I believe they also take LevelUp.

Looking for wine? You have options, there is a local wine store in reading terminal and a block away on 12th headed toward market is a PA liquor store with a great wine selection. Beer is not sold here however. :(

I like Reading Terminal Market every now and then.  It's a bit overwhelming the first visit and you tend to buy everything in sight.  After that, you know what you want--get in and get out.   It is a great place to take relatives for a visit in the city but if a local, I probably would never go there.   Good for the experience, you definitely want to go there at least once in your life.  Bucket list.
We had  blast.  What a wonderful market.  Any kind of food is waiting for you there.  Definitely go on a full stomach otherwise you might tear the place apart.

I love this place! It's a great indoor shopping area with tons of little shops and food places to go to. Can be crowded on the weekends and during lunchtime so seating is difficult to find sometimes.

My favorites: The ice cream shop with Bassett's ice cream is to die for, and I love to get my produce at Iovine bros. There is also a honey shop with raw honey that might be the best honey I have ever tasted. Check out the Amish store for amazing dairy products.

DiNic's and Spataros are a couple of great hoagie places if you are in the mood for a substantial lunch. Definitely check this place out whether you live in the city or are just passing through.

Excellent cluster-bomb of a place with a little of everything for every taste.  The quality of the establishments here is pretty high.  It's a fantastic place to come and watch people while enjoying some good food.

I'm already looking forward to spring so that I can walk over and enjoy lunch here!
Get the oysters! If I lived inside this market for a week, just maybe I would cover a fourth of what I wanted to try.

You get a nice toasted sandwich from Potbelly although its a little on the small side, if you ask me. The shakes and smoothies are the bomb even if each shake has almost a full day's worth of calories. Another plus is the fact that its conveniently located across the street from HUP and CHOP. They also have plenty of outdoor seating for those nice, sunny days.

Fantastic market!! An absolute must when in Philly. This spot was recommended by my wife's boss. A great recommendation I just wish they were open beyond 6PM. Every delicacy you have a taste for you will find at Reading (Pronounced "Red-ing"):  Philly food, Check.  Italian Food, Check.  Soul Food, Check. Asian Food, Check. Indian Food, Check.  Seafood, Check. The list goes on and on.  We spent at least everyday enjoying the various meals.  Highly recommended when in Philly.  Cheers!

Warning: if you bring out-of-towners to Reading Terminal Market, they are sure to show up on your doorstep again asking to go back. Reading Terminal is also known to cause sensory overload. 
This is THE primary choice for lunch when I have friends from out of town visiting. I have yet to eat at the same stand twice and have never been short of pleased by my meals. Be prepared to be a bit overwhelmed with your culinary selections: there is everything from Amish comfort food to Iraqi inspired treats.
The actual market is also worth visiting. Extremely fresh fish, vegetables, and fruits can be found on the side near Market East; a great place to stop on your way home from work (the market is open until 6 pm on week days). Also, the prices are fabulous! 
The best part of Reading Terminal for at-home cooks though would have to be the Spice shop, located near the Beer Garden (yes, there is a beer garden; beer selections are meh though). They have every spice you can think of all for MUCH cheaper than you'll find anywhere else. Note: the spices are packaged in little baggies, so you'll need to have your own containers to transfer them into.
 I will be here soon to stock up on my fresh foods for the week, and cannot wait until another friend visits so I can try yet another stand!

I can't even begin to describe how luscious, decadent and wonderful this place is to me. Truly a cross-section of humanity where food is the common denominator. I've been to several farmer's markets around the US, but Philly's is tops in my book. I hadn't seen the Amish since I'd gone to college in this State. It was oddly fascinating to see them so....affable.

I was fortunate enough to pop in here 2 days straight for lunch and breakfast, respectively. How I wish I could make this a regular haunt.

As a side, I will say if you're able to find a table to sit and eat, the people-watching is absolutely choice.

I absolutely love going to the Reading Terminal Market.  There are so many different things to check out and different foods to try.  The market has ended up being one of my go-to places when I have visitors in town.  The only downside is that it can get insanely busy so if you don't do well in crowds you might want to avoid this place during meal times!
WOW!!!!  Thats all I can say.  If you want to go to food heaven this place is very close to it.  There are lots of choices to choose from.   Go and have fun.  There are almost too many choices.

Convenient.  Crowded.  Rodent infested.  Cash only.  Did I mention convenient?

To be fair.  Good, bad, and mediocre vendors must coexist.  Did I mention convenient?
One of my top spots to bring visitors in Philly, they are rarely disappointed.

I just discovered this hidden treasure last summer.. and I'm telling you!  If you love food, this will be your haven.  You can find Amish bakery and kitchen goods, unique smoothie combinations, french food, desserts, pizza, italian, cheeses, honey items, lots of seafood and fruit (for good prices).. there's a great chocoate dipped cookie place there.... and even philly cheesesteaks.... I haven't even mentioned HALF of what Reading Terminal Market has to offer.  It is simply an energetic and ecclectic environment for food lovers.. just don't take someone there who doesn't like crowds.. they may be a little intimidated!  But it is a MUST for any Philly visitor!

This place is just....paradise.

I've been here a few times over the years, and it is so jammed packed you can barely move. Now, I don't know if it was because of the heat, but this past Friday afternoon and Sunday early afternoon, it was oddly empty! I could easily just sit down somewhere if I wanted to. 

They have every kind of food imaginable there (I bought some BBQ from the Amish merchants and it was RIDIC, it was so good).  Plus, you can do your grocery shopping (meats, veggies/fruits, seasonings). It's in a really good location as well.
This is my first time at Potbellys.  The food is good but not great.  I was expecting more savoury food. Then my sandwich was like $7 and only tasted worth $5. Maybe I ordered the wrong sandwich.

I love reading Terminal for grocery shopping. Just know you won't find soy milk at any of the vendors. Love buying meat from an actual butcher and Iovines has a great selection of produce. Spices abound at the Head Nut hiding in a back corner. Stop for a beer at Molly Malloy's if the crowds around the Flower Show and Thanksgiving stress you out. Some of the food vendors are meh - like the Indian place that wraps samosas in pie dough. Thai is way too salty. Instead get a sandwich at DiNicks or pretzel wrapped treat at Miller's Twist.

The service here has definitely changed. The people are a lot more friendly and efficient. Still a bit slower than other places but the atmosphere and the attitude has upgraded. I also would like to shoutout to the girl who always makes me an a foil pepper whenever I ask for a tortilla on the side. She's friendly and welcoming despite a short encounter (which is ultimately a good thing since that means the line moves quickly.) I don't feel rush during this quick exchange of words. And if I misspoke, she will ask again or repeat in a way where I don't feel embarrassed. This chipotle team is definitely on point.

Reading Terminal Market is both a great place to get lunch and a historic tourist attraction in the heart of Philadelphia. There's dozens of places to eat and many are truly amazing. My recommendations are the pork sandwich at Tommy Dinic's with ice-cream at Bassetts for dessert - but it's hard to go wrong anywhere here. Seating is limited, but you can generally get a table if you keep your eyes open. Discounted parking is available nearby - check the website.
If its food related... you will find it here. I love this place. Take food home or eat there for an awesome people watching experience.

This is my second favorite place in all of Philly. It's the second place I take anyone that has never been down here before and it never fails to disappoint. The beauty of this place is the selection that it contains. No matter what your searching for, your gonna find it when it comes to food. All that diversity in one area is so convenient and stupendous. My favorites gotta be miller's twist, dinic's, carmen's and the ice cream place.

If you're in Philadelphia, you must check out Reading Terminal Market! It appears to be a very hip and cool place to go walk around and buy and try some food. They have everything from meat, to ice cream, to cheesesteak and to even a local bookstore. 

Unfortunately, the day my boyfriend and I came there was a street fair going on and the Terminal was MOBBED. You couldn't move one inch without running into someone. This was a disappointment since I wish we could have experienced it more since it seems like such a cool place. We made the most of it though and did buy a cheesesteak from a local vendor. I'm sure that they usually aren't this crowded and most people will get a better experience then we did. 

Come here hungry and check out at least one or two places before you leave. Definitely worth it!! I'd give them another try the next time I'm ever in Philly. 

Cheers!

I wandered around RTM a few times during my stay because it was nearby and interesting. I bought some decent cookies from a bakery and had some freaking marvelous ice cream from Bassett's. Everything there looks and smells good. The whole market is busy and hectic and colorful. I only wish that Dinic's hadn't run out of food when I went there. I also wouldn't mind trying the famous chicken wings one day.

Way too crowded with vendors and in a mostly disorganized fashion.  Not the cleanest/sanitary place to be.  Hunger Burger had terrible service.  Cheesesteaks at By George were good and the service was good.  Pike Street Market in Seattle is quite a bit more comfortable and interesting.  Quincy Market in Boston way outshines both.

I have never in my life had a few beers and then got a craving for bone-marrow.  Put some nachos on the menu or something...trust me, no one will complain.   

I really want to like this place.  I live about a block and a half away and the area is in serious need of a good bar/restaurant.  

First off, the place has a minimalistic decor but its nice.  Restored wood lines the ceiling and most of the walls.  The bar is simple with a chalkboard drink list.  It is small but seems to have a decent amount of seating.  The kitchen is in the back but open so you can check out their handywork.  The open layout allows you to see the two tv's from anywhere in the restaurant although I think the layout also makes the place a little loud. 

As for the beer list, it is OK.  They had about 10-12 beers on tap, a few beers were interesting and the rest were local staples, no macros except for the obligatory $3 pbr pounders and high lifes.  Seems to be a lot of love going to Philly Brewing Company as they had the most beers on the draft list.  The nonhappy hour prices are OK, in the $4-$6 range for a beer.  I'd be way more jazzed about the place if they did half off happy hours but as far as I know they only do $1 off all beers.  

As for the cocktails, I didn't try any but they have a list of some of their own specialties.  Once again, I'd be more interested in these drinks if they would settle down in price to more of the $8 range rather than the $10-$12 range.  The group sitting next to me ordered a punch bowl called Mummer's Punch.  It's 4quarts of punch to share and looked fun.  It is supposed to serve 4-6 people and costs $45.  

Menu wise I'm not sure what is going on here.  I think the chef designing the menu was over-ambitious, unaware of what the clientele in the area is looking for, and would prefer to be cooking at a gourmet restaurant rather than at a South Philly bar.  Basically, the only thing on the menu that you would recognize as pub food is the burger and wings.  The other options include things like bone marrow, pulled duck bbq, and tartare.  Don't get me wrong, I like all sorts of food, and I would be interested in trying some of the things on the menu but the menu should be more balanced.  For example, if you want to offer bone marrow then fine, but offer pulled pork bbq instead of pulled duck...sometimes I don't want to order food and hope that its good.  I want to order something that I know I like and then hope that the restaurant makes it really well so I end up loving it.  Price wise, the menu is a little too expensive as well. They have 'small plates' and large plates' I'm not sure how big the small plates are but they are in the $10 range and the large places move up to the $18-$22 range.  So basically, if my wife and I go here, have a beer or cocktail each, then each have an entree we are looking at spending $60 plus dollars.  That's a lot of money for a bar in Pennsport.  I'll go to The Village Belle for a dinner in that price range any day.  At least you are getting some non-bar ambiance there. 

I did see someone with the steak frites which looked really good but at $18 most of the entrees are too expensive to make this a place to go and get a beer and dinner when I don't want to cook.  

The service was good even though the place was crowded.  And when you consider that I was there when they had only been open for 2 or 3 days, it was running very smoothly.  

As far as the places association or their claim to cater to people working the the restaurant/bar "Industry" I didn't see it.  I don't know if they offer a discount to industry folks, but it didn't appear to be advertised on the menu or anything.  The only thing that seemed to give a nod to the industry were little bits of advice given on menu's and coasters and things such as "Tip: Never start your order with, "this is going to be a pain but...".  There is also an offer on the drink menu to buy a round of shots or a six pack for the kitchen.  I guess this caters to "the industry" but mostly just to people who work at "the industry" and not the restaurant biz in general.  Overall, I don't really care about "the industry" theme.  I'm not in the business so it doesn't have any impact on me, I just thought they might have a little more playing off the theme.  It mostly feels gimmicky 

With all of this said, I want to note that this is my initial review.  The place is young and I live so close I'm sure I'll be back.  I want the place to find an identity that is more appropriate for the neighborhood and clientele.  I'm not saying serve coors light and fill the place with Mummers.  I just mean, recognize that The Industry is not in Center City or Rittenhouse.  If you are catering to people in the "Industry" realize that you have to understand that you are a bar and have to offer a good happy hour or nightly specials along with understandable food at a reasonable price not gourmet-based food.  I'll be back, but I'm hoping for change.

If you're a local you know to avoid this place at all costs. It takes a long time to get subpar tourist trap food and then you have to wait to find a seat at a table of which there are few. I'll never understand why this place is packed every weekend with tourists waiting to spend their money. Do yourself a favor and pick another local restaurant. Don't eat at the equivalent of a historical mall food court.

I was blown away on my first visit to this market, there is so much to see inside, tons of  eateries and shops, I had a very hard time choosing where to go, what to see and what to eat !! Foodie heaven !
from corned beef on marble rye to cold Yuengling on draft this place has it all! oh, and they also have FREE wifi

What could I possibly say that hasn't already been said? This place is an institution - a gem - a must. There are too many choices - smells that are enticing to your senses - visual displays of foods and people so colorful I found myself just wanting to stand still in the middle of it all and take it in - but the crowd doesn't allow for pauses - you have to roll with it. If you take too long trying to decide what you want it's almost certain something else will catch your eye and you'll be on to the next thing.

Enjoy this place - it's special.

If you live in Philadelphia, and you've never been to the Reading Terminal Market, shame on you! The market is a cultural icon to our region.  There is so much diversity of stalls, products and eating establishments, it would take 20 trips to Reading Terminal to hit 'em all and try something from each, (unless you can mix completely divergent food types - I can't).

If you are a tourist visiting Philadelphia, you should absolutely take a few hours to tour the market and get something to eat while you're there.  Off the top of my head, I would say check out the crepe place (forget the name), and get one of the fresh fruit filled crepes.  Absolutely delicious!  Or if you want to sample some unusual beer, as well as some delicious sandwiches, try Molly Malloy's.

I've been to the Grand Central Market in LA, and it's OK, but not nearly as diversified in it's products and stands as Reading Terminal Market right in my own backyard.  You should go.

I love reading terminal market. I go there for groceries and lunch all the time. The produce is ridiculously cheap and the food stands are all so delicious and are from every genre of food you can imagine. I would highly reccomend the DiNics Roast Pork sandwich with greens and cheese.
Great place with many options. Unfortunately, it's a tourist trap and it's always packed with people who have no idea where they're going. I suggest going early in the morning.

Stopped in here during a day trip to Philly.  I only wish I had picked up some homemade fudge during this stop!

First off, I stopped at Spartan's for a yup, Philly Cheesesteak with the Whiz & fried onions.  OMG!  Soooooo damn goood!!!!!!  Wish I could have eaten another one or at least....bring one home!

Walked around & saw tons wonderful things.

Ended up stopping at Tea Leaf for a wonderful cuppa Bourbon Vanilla tea.  Made to perfection by the wonderful lady who greeted us.  And I treated myself to a mug with a strainer here.  

Before leaving, we stopped at Bassett's for ice cream.
I scream
You scream
We all scream 
for ice cream!!!

I can highly recommend the Butterscotch Vanilla.  Yummy!!!

I wish I had a place like this here in NY.  It was a great market!  Lots going on.  Definitely very crowded, but everyone was really nice.  I got bumped several times & people apologized.  Wow!  Definitely not NY!
Love this place. Unique spot with great history, and the food selections and tastes are phenomenal!
Awesome! Just good old fashioned home cooked Philly food at its greatest! So ethnic and sooooo goood!!!! A part of our history and culture here,

So many options!!! From Molly Malloys to Dinic's roast pork, you can't go wrong at Reading Terminal.

For desert, try the Cheesecake at Termini's bakery.

I'm also a big fan of basset' ice cream.

I wish they were open later on weekdays, but I have no complaints about the eateries. A standard Philadelphia gem :-)
This market reminded me of Quincy market in Boston or Fisherman's Wharf in SF. I like these old school style of tradition. I was very happy to find out the most yummy whoopie pies I ever had.

Overall, I love this place! It's packed with a HUGE variety of places to eat and drink and has pretty good food-although I wouldn't come here to get my philly cheesesteak.  The downsides to Reading Terminal Market are: 1) how packed it can get--it can feel a little overwhelming when you just want to go in and grab a grilled cheese sandwich and sit down when there are throngs of people trying to do the same thing; 2) how rude some of the employees can be--it feels like they assume that everyone who is a customer sucks because they are probably a tourist and it's annoying to have to explain to customers where to stand/etc. However, it's still a great place to grab a cup of coffee or lunch and there are a LOT of options.

LOVE this place. This place reminds me of a cross between Seattle's Pike Place and NYC's Chelsea Market. We came around 11am on a Saturday and as time passed it definitely got more and more crowded but i didn't mind the crowds. Old City Coffee has a nice menu but I wasn't blown away by the coffee or overly sweet latte. Our bbq lunch hit the spot though not the best food Philly. Love coming here for cheap fresh groceries (basil, bananas, etc) in the center and then a few other quality items towards the side of the market (arugula, portobello mushroom, heirloom tomatoes). Love the maple bacon that we had for breakfast at home today and getting ready to slice up some more yummy tuna and salmon sashimi that we got from here.

Restaurants have been kinda underwhelming except Hershel's which makes a really good pastrami sandwich.

We validated our parking when we bought our groceries which came out to $4 for the 1-1.5h of  parking. I'm used to suburbia where parking is free or at least meter parking is cheap/bountiful so this was the only part that  bothered me a bit but it was fast and stress-free --so very worth it I'm learning =]

I cant wait to go back and eat more samples. I've heard that the amish bakery sells things for $1 after 3pm Saturday since they remain closed til Tuesday.

If you can't find something to please your palate here, I pity you. I love the Mexican cantina, the fresh vegetables, the unfrozen poultry, the german hot dogs, and the fact that just about everyone there appreciates good food.

If I'm ever wondering what to get for lunch in Philly and I'm close to Reading Terminal Market, I head here. There are so many options, and regardless of what I've chosen, I've never been disappointed. One of my favorite things that I've found here is homemade ginger lemonade. It's so delicious!

Food inside Reading Terminal is great, especially Tony Dinic's sandwiches (which have the best provolone cheese I have ever had in them). Would highly recommend to anyone looking for a casual lunch with pretty much any type of food they can think of.

This place is absolutely delicious.  Healthy, made-to-order Indian food in either wraps or bowls.  Lots of vegetarian and gluten free options, spicey sauce to add.  We really (really!) loved it here and will certainly be back.  They're open super late for that late night dinner.  Made for an awesome lunch the next day and was so reasonably priced.

I go here at least once or twice a week and it's my favorite place on temples campus!! Both the salads and stir frys are extremely good and worth the price!! The only things that I've notice are that sometimes when I get salads they're out of certain things and the wait always takes a very long time even when they're not busy. It could just be the time that I go at but the food is delicious and worth the wait!
This place has individual restaurant stalls with every kind of food you can imagine in a very cool bustling high energy setting. That is all you need to know. Go there.

This is a great place for a quick stop pick-up and it's very close to most hotels in Center City. We originally visited the area to pick up some snacks for the hotel but there's a variety of stands for freshly cooked meals and raw ingredients as well if you want to whip up a meal with your own personal touch. I think they do close a little early for me  but that's just because I function more at night and do most of my errands late. We shopped around as they also had some local art and jewelries for sale.

I placed a large order through GrubHub. It's Friday afternoon and they canceled the order saying they were out of several items.  I ordered a burger and fries, ribs and a half chicken.  Those are some basic things - it seems pretty sketchy to be out of so many things on a Friday..

It is the magical hidden gem in Center city. You can find pretty much all the fresh grocery, meat, seafood, wine, coffee, desserts, prepared food, etc. that you need. Great place for a lunch stop. Unfortunately the market closes too soon and the Amish stores are not open on Sundays. So if you are especially interested in the Amish stores plan your trip accordingly.

I'm in love with chick fil a service. The service at this chick fil a was amazing and is actually one of the best ones I been to even though it's not my usual spot. When I was ordering my meal during breakfast hours the cashier did not get annoyed at me for not knowing what I want since I never gotten breakfast from chick fil a before. She was very accommodating with me wanting an orange juice instead of soda or anything. As for ordering my husband coffee I change my mind on regular and vanilla a few times since I wasn't sure what he wanted when he was parking while I ordered but the cashier did not rush me and was very patience. I love how they check around the table even during breakfast hours to make sure everything was fine and as well as help us took our trash away and brought us the food to begin with.

This place is always great! The crowds, vibe, & the selection of food, markets, & goods make it a wonderful place to check out. I always get lots of food shopping here, while enjoying the different food vendors. The only thing that's a bummer is it closes early & the surrounding PPA parking is hourly until 4pm. So if you can take public transportation here or walk, so you don't get a ticket or feel rushed. This is a must on a to do list! A must every season to checkout the new goods! Bring out of towners here or direct them to come here.

Definitely a must-go if you are in Philly! I try to go somewhere new each time and I'm blown away each and every time. Tommy Dinic's and Hershel's are probably my favorites. There are some really great places for sweets and desserts. To top it all of there is a nice bar you can grab a drink at. Check it out you won't be disappointed!
Pretty good Kati Roll. Comparable to NYC Kati rolls. I'm a huge fan of their paneer roles.

Took my mom and brother (visiting from out of town).  Amazing options available, and the food was awesome with reasonable prices.  One star taken away because general cleanliness of the overall facilities was a tad lacking.

Ever wonder how the Amish at the Amish stand get to Center City?  Where do they park their horses?  I've no idea.  But, I'll take some sticky buns and an apple dumpling with cream on the side to go.

Best fresh squeezed juice.  Again from the Amish.

Best Rotisserie herb chicken.  Again the Amish.  

Sigh.  Only in PA.

Not much to add about the Reading Terminal Market with over 3,000 Yelp reviews but it still is a must stop for anyone visiting Philadelphia. My father used to bring my brother and myself there when we were kids in the late 60's and early 70's. I remember all the butchers and only a few restaurants and saw dust on the floors.  He would treat us to Bassets ice cream. We used to always get our turkeys from Moyers and once borrowed their large Phillies banner to take to Shea stadium when the Phillies played the Mets (my Uncle lived in Queens). The building's history can be felt when walking around.

The Reading Terminal Market has evolved and now has a lot more eating establishments. Yes it is touristy, but it still remains a really cool place. It does get crowded but that is part of the charm. There is something to eat for everyone and deciding what to choose or finding seating might be difficult, but the experience and diversity of food is worth it. Tommy DeNic's and Beiler's Bakery are probably the most popular and naturally the most crowded. There are so many other establishments worth trying and the market is something that is uniquely Philadelphia. I just wish I could go back in time and be there again with my parents.
SO many options. every kind of food you could think of, including a deli and butchered meats/seafood. If you're ever looking for a bite in the city, please check this place out for your own good!!!

Great place to find a place to eat or buy fresh food and treats. The variety is fantastic it it has a great feel of a place that has been around a long time. It is very busy with people and sometimes hard to find a seat to enjoy your food. Great opportunity to meet new friends.

I love going to markets like this! I worked at Pike Place Market in Seattle so I can greatly appreciate going to see other markets. I love the variety and hustle and bustle that is going all around. Seeing all the fresh produce, meats and quick eats is so exciting. I had a really great time 
wandering around looking at all the vendors. I recommend; Termini Brothers Bakery, Dinic's Roast Pork, and an Amish pretzel.....I tried the egg, bacon and cheese pretzel and it nearly sent me to the moon....WOW that was tasty!

I arrived at 12:30 so there was quite a line already but it went fairly quickly - the staff seems very efficient.

I ordered the Farmhouse salad and requested cheddar cheese instead of blue cheese and they happily obliged. It was a generous size and the ingredients were fresh. the Potbelly vinaigrette was light and delicious. I also like that they post calorie content on each of their menu items and low calorie options are easy to identify. The drink selection is a bit pricey ($2 for a bottle of iced tea or lemonade). 

There's a nice terrace to enjoy your lunch outdoors and the location directly across from the University of PA hospital is hard to beat (especially if you're wary of food trucks - which I am).

Very interesting foodery/indoor market. There's a variety of stands that serve food (crepes, doughnuts, jerky, and more) and some even have seating too!

Some of the shops are kind of boutique-y in nature, but it's still worth the visit. If you have out-of-towners who have never been, this is definitely a spot at which to stop!

I probably eat here at least once a week. Great selections and decent prices. You have to be careful with what time you go because it can get very busy with tourists and folks at the convention center.

Carmen met us with a friendly, energized greeting and she was absolutely on top of her game. We were happy to have healthy options and Carmen helped to answer questions to assist us in making selections that met my husband's dietary restrictions.  There were many options for soup, salad, and a tasty panini available to sample. Carmen was fast, efficient, and helped us procure a healthy bite to eat that was wholesome and satisfying. Also, the rest of the staff seemed to work well together, be well synchronized and as we were eating I observed this courteous and efficient service being extended to many other patrons who came after us.  The portions were generous and yes, it is more $ than you would pay in town but very reasonable for an airport.

(to the tune of "Pieces of Me" by Ashlee Simpson)

On a Monday, there's less waiting.
Tuesday, lines are fading
But most weekdays, crowds at lunch.
And on weekends, check those long lines
There's no ending, but I feel fine
'cause I come right after brunch.

Crowds, I hate those crowds so much....
But the produce and the meats, they're all so CLUTCH!

Ooooooh
It seems like I can finally find the things I really need
From fresh fish to sunflower seeds
Ooooooohhhh
It's as if this place has really got something for everyone
And to people watch, so fun.
All the people, people, people they feed.
All the people, people, people they feeeeed.

Reading Terminal, once a destination for me before I moved to the city, has quickly transformed to a spot I frequent for weekly groceries, specialty items, or even a little treat now and then. I've got my tried-and-true favs (Iovine Produce, Martin's for meats, Hatville Deli) and my favorite spots to bring out-of-towners (Beilers! Dinic's! Flying Monkey! Dutch Eating Place!) There's no better way to WOW a party than offering to bring desserts, and just making a platter of RTM goodies. From whoopie pies to canoli, black and white cookies to chocolate in the shape of nearly ANYTHING, this place is a goldmine. 

Weekends make things a little tougher, and, honestly, a lot of weekday lunchtimes. Tourists will stop in the middle of aisles, or (dressed in their comic-con finery), ogle menus and take pictures, halting progress. But that's kind of a part of the whole thing, isn't it? We are lucky enough to call this amazing city home, and RTM is definitely a Philly gem I'm proud to share with anyone who's just coming to visit.

Prices are great, convenience is greater, and I'll brave the crowds when the quality is that good.

I go here for all my fruit and veggie needs at iovine brothers. For fresh produce their prices are reasonable and they have student discounts on Tuesdays and Sundays I think. Will confirm next time I'm there. I am now a regular. Plus if you don't mind they have a small offshoot somewhere towards the middle that sells anything that was close to going bad for even cheaper. You have to be careful but may find a few good things left
Love it! It's indoors, nicely air-conditioned. There is a great selection of food, and specialty items.  Come hungry, walk around first, then decide what to eat.

My favorite spot from my weekend in Philly. Im a complete sweets freak and I got lost in all of my options. We grabbed a quick lunch at the vegetarian stand...i forget the name of it but holy moses was the chicken club excellent. inexpensive as well. Then we headed over to the general store type place where i drooled over their selection of candy/caramel apples. oof! 
Can't wait to come back!

I am a huge fan of the RTM. There are so many wonderful, authentic, and eclectic places to eat inside this establishment. Even if you are just going to grocery shop (I recommend Iovine Brothers) it is always an experience. I've enjoyed seafood from Wan's and thought that the people working there was extremely friendly. Terralyn is a nice little boutique with handcrafted soaps and other beautiful gifts. There are always fresh flowers for purchase at the market, delicious crepes to be eaten, and hundreds of friendly faces. Don't miss out on the roast pork sandwich from Di Nics- it is worth the wait! 

Whether you're looking for a quick bite, a few groceries, a gift for a unique or artistic friend, or a fun place to go for a daytime activity, the RTM is always a good choice.

One of the must sees in downtown Philadelphia is the Reading Terminal Market. I didn't know exactly what this place was until I actually ventured here on a Friday after sightseeing in the historical district. The Reading Terminal Market is basically a larger than life indoor Farmer's Market that mingles like a Chinatown as well. There's plenty of vendors and food choices that will make your head spin. I probably spent a good hour here and buying a few things before heading back to the hotel on Walnut Street.  Pretty much anything and everything food wise you can get is here. 

Located on 12th Street, the Reading Terminal Market  is centrally located in downtown Philadelphia. Many bus routes converge here and it's very walkable from all points in downtown. It's quite busy here and it  tends to be loaded with a lot of people surfing for good deals on anything and everything.
