It reminds me of a indoor Chinatown in a way, where all the vendors line up tightly and it's more or less a mom and pop operation for each vendor that's represented. Good deals can be had here and I took advantage of it.

Prices here can be wholesale and retail at the same time, depending on what you are looking for. There is even a shoe shinning operation at the back of the market. I'm not sure why tripadvisor told me that this is really a must do, but it wasn't as good of a visit that I thought it would be. While it was cool to get deals and see how the locals and tourist folk do their business in some crazy fashion, I have no doubt that the Reading Terminal Market is as popular as they say it is. Overall, I would recommend this place for shopping and something to do.

Support local!

B

When I wrote my review for Reading Terminal Market in 2010 I called it "the single best place in Philadelphia."

A lot changes in 4 years. The market has a little bit but I have changed a lot more.

In that time I have converted to a vegan diet. The market has some new stalls but its overall vibe (meat and fish heavy unhealthy Philly fare) has not. 

I still enjoy a stroll through the market (so long as my gaze avoids the meat and seafood stalls) but those walks are just nostalgia for my first years in Philadelphia when my wife and I were first dating. Way back then (the ancient era of 2004-2005) she and I would go to the market for a the special at the Hatfield Farms deli counter. Back then whenever I had time to kill, I would do it at Reading Terminal Market.

As my tastes have changed the Market has barely budged. It feels stuck in a past where people ate like they did not give a damn. Maybe I'm being too hard here. It could just be my age. I loved the market in my 20s. In my 30s, I usually only order something from the Four Seasons veggie juice bar. 

I recently sat at a table at the Market to grade some student work before I met up with some friends. As I was sitting with my Four Seasons juice I was asked to take part in a survey by a woman researching for Reading Terminal Market. My overall feedback to her: "this could be such a great place and I would recommend it to friends if only it had some vegan take-out!"

To be fair: Reading Terminal Market has the vegan cupcake at Flying Monkey (quite good) and Molly Malloy's which is not a bad place to hang out. And of course Four Seasons for some really good cheap veggie juice.

Aside from that and coffee I don't spend money there. Its managers should take a walk on South Street and enjoy some of its vegan take-out. Imagine what Reading Terminal Market could be if it included some of that!

Great market, full of life and colors. You can find fresh fruits and vegetables as well as great restaurants and bakeries. Is a must go in Philadelphia.
Most of the places (restaurants) are close on Sunday. Check the webpage before going
I could probably come here regularly and still never try everything. This place is amazing. No matter what you're craving you can most likely find it here. It can get crowded around the lunch hours.

My wife's cousin who lives in Philly took us there yesterday. I have to admit that is is a great place to experience. I wish I lived closer so I could shop here often but we live in New Jersey. So I will have to be content with just visiting on occasion. The variety of food is astounding. So fresh and inviting. It is a great place, with the history of the train terminal as well. We definitely will come back if we are in the neighborhood.

Wow, where to start. I grew up going to the Terminal and frequent it now with my family. It is perhaps the most fun place in the city to grab lunch or breakfast. You can get anything you want to eat -- our favorites are the huge blueberry pancakes at the Amish counter in the back, the Mexican foot at the Cantina, and the new grilled cheese stand. The Terminal is such a Philly experience that it shouldn't be missed by residents or visitors to Philly. 

A visit wouldn't be complete without dessert from either Fourth Street Cookies, a hand thrown soft pretzel dipped in butter from another Amish stand, or Bassetts Ice Cream. 

This place is Philly's own slice of heaven.

Reading Market could single-handedly convince me to relocate to Philly. Every time I go--which is pretty much every time I visit Philly--I leave there blissed out and I always discover something new. I've eaten at Carmen's (no relation to Carmen's in Bellmawr, N.J., which is a shame because they have the best mixed cheese sub on the planet) which is only passable as far as hoagies go. Rick's Steaks, however, is the culinary equivalent to a mind-blowing one-night stand. You know what you want, you get it, you can't get enough during, and you leave feeling fully sated and definitely sure you'd do it again (even though you shouldn't). There is a Mexican food stall that makes killer nachos, and way in the back this time I discovered a bakery that makes the most delicious little cupcakes that blows away any I've found in D.C. or New York. I'll need to look up the name. They said they do mail order for brownies but not cupcakes--bummer--but make sure you stop by for one.

A must-visit when in Philly! Eat breakfast at one of the many spots for farm fresh foods! Anything your heart desires you can find there. The chocolates are made in all shapes, and if it's seafood you want, cheese you need....it is here! Breads, desserts, cut flowers, and even artwork is displayed proudly. This is a heady experience and a treat for all ages....what w wonderful place!

Love this place. So many things to look at and taste. Each time we go to Philadelphia we have to come here and try something new. Definitely my favorite part of Philadelphia. It can get really crowded, so be prepared during lunch or dinner hours to stand on line at certain stands and hunt for a seat (though you could just stand at eat , but that could be tough depending on what you buy). There are a variety of different foods, such and sandwiches, chinese take out, seafood, bakeries, etc, so definitely something for everyone. 

We don't live in the area, so we don't buy anything at the market section. However, there are a few meat and vegetable and fruit vendors there if you're interested in grabbing some of those items.
It just comes down to this: I can always find something at Reading Terminal and mostly likely it will be at a decent price and taste delicious.

This reminds me of smorgasburg or Chelsea's market in NYC. There is a variety of things to eat whether you want a little snack, a meal or dessert. There are also some supermarkets around to purchase things from. I love all of the options but it takes a long time to pick out what you really want. Saturdays are packed! Sundays aren't as packed and some places are closed early so there's no real middle ground. Regardless, if you're in Philly and in the area it's a cool spot to check out!

I try to do most of my food shopping here. Every 2 weeks I go to John Yi for my fish. Although they are expensive, the fish here is incredibly fresh. I splurge and get the wild king salmon which is about 20.00 a pound. They give me a 2 pound slab and take off the skin and it looks so beautiful. I think it is sushi grade. When I am ready to cook it, I slice off what I need and just grill it. It is better then bad sex!! I get at least 5 meals out of it. The salmon is so fresh that I can keep it in the refrigerator for about a week.
Then it is off to Godshall's for my fresh chicken. I always get a chicken breast not split. When I bake this the chicken comes out juicy and fresh. It is good for 2 meals.
A great place!!
AMAZINGGGGGGGGG Next time I'm going to get all the makings for sushi.
Amazing market for find everything good about the food. You can find Cheese, charcuterie, bakery food, Chinese and so on. All small thing from everywhere. You can eat here too and enjoy your dishes.

A great indoor farmers market/specialty food shop/eatery-cafe. Even though I checked it out at the tail end of its hours of operations, it looked like this place had booths of fairly equal proportions to fresh foods to specialty foods to eateries.  If I had an appetite during my visit I would've surely stuffed myself trying to sample all the eatery offerings.  I've fallen in love with Reading Terminal Market and all of Philadelphia it represents.  I must revisit with a group so I can try all that this place has to offer.
This place is extremely over whelming because there's just sooo many options but you really can't go wrong with whichever place you choose.
What could I possibly say that hasn't already been said?  There aren't many places in the world like it.  And if there are, they're copying off of Reading Terminal Market.

There wasn't anything really remarkable about this place to me. It's just sort of your average neighborhood bar. I would have only given it two stars except for two things:

1. The punch bowls that are good for groups (and the drinks in them are yummy.)

2. The ladies room was actually pretty clean for the entire time I was there, which is no small feat. 

So overall, not a bad place to go but not somewhere I'd seek out either.
love it, definitely gets a little too crowded and touristy for my taste but other than that great place.

$.69 for any size coffee you say?  Breakfast sandwiches comprised of egg, meat and cheese crammed between two syrupy pancakes?  Granted eating here 3 times a day will take 10 years off your life, but once in a while never hurt anyone.

This place was great!! So much to choose from. Everyone raved about the pork sandwich from Dinics but I found it meh, I wish I could have tried something from every vendor but the lines were very long.
I love philly and this market. Amazing foods and pastries there. Oh and I almost forgot  about Bassets ice cream!? SO GOOD! :)

Amazing! Unique! But be warned: it can get overwhelming

First time here? 
Must try: Herschel's for corned beef, Beiler's Donuts for donuts, of course!

Been here?
Great finds: Iovine brothers for awesome deals on literally every type of produce; Head Nut for an ASTOUNDING assortment of herbs, spices, flours, candies, you name it (some of my faves they offer: lavender, nutritional yeast, 00 flour!)
SOOO many counters for meat, fish, cheese, chocolate

COME HUNGRY! You'll be back :)
Try the biscuits and gravy and the stomachectomy to cure your hangover! Their entire brunch menu is delicious.

I want to give it 5 Stars but I can't. My 4 Star rating has nothing to do with the taste of the Food. However it does have everything to do with the crowd. But before I get to that let me tell you that if you walk in here and can't find something that you absolutely LOVE than there is something wrong with you. Ladies and Gentlemen there are no bad meals here. And trust me you won't have to walk far to find a completely different genre of food if you don't like the one you stop at...no worries just turn left or right and you are bound to find something to cure your cravings. Now back to the crowd issue. Good luck if you are a person who doesn't deal well with feeling cramped up and like you can't move. The worst hours to go in my opinion are the typical lunch hour of between 11:30 and 12:30. Oh yea and if you plan on sitting down somewhere inside to eat...forget about it.

We went for their Sunday afternoon brunch. They had a wide variety of meals to choose from on their menu. I chose the huevos rancheros. It was an American twist on the traditional Mexican breakfast. To. Die. For. It had a good amount of spiciness. My husband chose the chicken biscuit sandwich. Just beware that their are bones in it. We didn't expect that on a sandwich. It was delicious as well!! We will definitely be back for their brunch. I think, their brunch menu is way better than their menu the rest of the week!
Great market overall. The German deli, the Cajun restaurant, the Amish restaurant are especially great. Also, the sushi bar, produce market and cheese counters make the trip worthwhile, too.

LOVE THE READING TERMINAL MARKET!!!! We take the greyhound bus to Phily...takes a little over an hour and the bus stop is right by the Market. Pop in....and start with Miller's Twist, the most delicious little hot dog wrapped in a buttery pretzel...they are worth the trip alone! Then you need donuts and cheese steaks and beef jerky! Oh and don't forget the chocolate chip cookies and the deli meats sliced so perfectly thin. Best food market I've ever been too!!!

Place was great, plenty of culture for our day tip to Philly. I would recommend going in the morning when their is lots going on. I think it closes around 3pm. 

We got pretzels from the stand in their and they were great! This is coming from a amateur pretzel eater.

Some of the best Kati rolls I've ever had! My only complaint is having to pay for sauces, because everywhere else I've been they come free with the purchase. But the rolls were tasty, warm, and filling, which is the most important part. The restaurant is also quite cute.

All I can say is WOW! What an authentic experience. It's overwhelming in a good way. If you time. There are so many food vendors and varieties. Amish selections, Philly Cheese stakes, and really so many fresh produce and local food selections here. A ton of great restaurants. I ate at Molly's and it was so good. I also purchased some holiday items like dented beeswax candles, local honey and some local wine. A couple of sheen wine coasters too. This is an amazing place to experience if you are visiting Philidelphia

Yes, this place used to be dirty, gross, but they have stepped up hygiene, non-smoking, all vendors have strict guidelines in cleanliness, Love , love the Amish cafe, sit at stool, eat whatever you want, breakfast, huge dutch apples, specials are on board, includes drink dish & side..for usually $4.95 -$6.95 can't beat it!! Wait for seating, but goes pretty quick. Love it there, whatever your heart desires, from Sang Kee , Thai food, Philly cheesesteaks,great places & vendors. Yes, for out-of towners, it can be Overwhelming ..but what a great place!!!

A food flea market/farmers market which never loses its intrigue!
A must experience and return again and again.

What a mad house with crowd!! But I have to say I dig places like this that gives you the one-stop-shop for food, sweets and meat! Unfortunately, it was so crowded with few seating area and many places had very long lines or sold out items :( I guess we should have come in early to beat the crowd. We did get a grilled cheese sammy from Valley Shepherd and it was delicious, short line but 15minutes wait for cook time. 

Even if you are not eating here, be sure to swing by to check it out. It's always fun to look around.
Good drink great service - BUT. Ordered the grilled shrimp kabob special and it was very tasty. But just 3 small shrimp for $19?  Seemed awfully stingy.  Will make me hesitate to go back.

First, keep in mind that the 2 stars are an overall score. The food deserved 1 star. 
This is yet another place where there's a HUGE disconnect between the glowing yelp reviews and the reality.
The place was nice, ambience great. Beer selection was great. Bathroom was spotless. Service was decent.
The food came out SUPER QUICK, but maybe that was the problem.
The food was terrible. I got something called the Stomachectomy. It was described as pancakes, scrapple, sausage, and an egg, etc. When it came, it was three large pancakes with an egg on top and scrapple and sausage in between the pancakes. The pancakes were the most disgusting thing I ever ate. They were doughy and rubbery. They tasted like they had been pre-made. They didn't taste at all like pancakes. My girlfriend tried some and spit it into her napkin, refusing to swallow it. She said they were "worse than microwave pancakes". The sausage was probably the only edible thing on the plate. The "house-made" scrapple was weak. That was probably one of the most disappointing meals I ever ate, especially when you consider all of the yelp hype. 
My girlfriend got the Thai Chicken Salad, which she described as "edible." She also said she's had better salads at Friendly's (yes, the Ice Cream chain she takes her kids to). She put the salad up to the window to see it in the light, and we both agreed that it didn't look fresh. She said the dish lacked seasoning and was generally lame and unsatisfying. 
We both agreed, we would come back for drinks, but never for the food. 
Who is writing these yelp reviews? This is another case where I have to wonder if family and employees are writing them or the owners are paying a service to pump up their yelp reviews. Don't take my word for it, try it for yourself. Big letdown.

Wow. So much in a great space. Centrally located off market on 12th. I walked from my hotel. Really busy at 10am which is nice for the merchants and not too crowded for the customers. 

Food! Food! Food!  Mostly food. Some crafts and locally sourced alcohol. I can't even list all that I saw:  Greek, dumplings, deli, bakeries galore, coffee, meats, sandwiches, Cajun, desserts, ice cream, cheesesteak, heroes, soul, breakfast, lunch and dinner. 

If I lived near here I'd shop for my meats and veggies and fruits and breads. Amazing selection of everything, including some Amish merchants. 

Definitely worth the visit.

Reading terminal is a place one MUST visit when in Philly! It's super fantastic! Anything you want is at your disposal....snacks, treats, sweets, market value groceries & high gravity brew. 

It's a gem! Words just can't describe. Make sure you go earlier in the day or before sightseeing, it closes at 6pm on Friday:/ 

Anywho...grateful recommendation for us & passing it on to yelpers. #visitphilly

Happy everything!
my favorite part is the fair food stand for my weekly produce. great local veggies and fruit at reasonable prices.
A little crowded for introverts but there are so many delicious options, you'll get over it quickly. On top of that -- despite the afternoon crowds, I always seem to find a seat!

I absolutely love this place. Always something delicious to try and new people to meet. 

Giving it a 4 mostly because it can be a little pricey.

I find Reading terminal to be a crowded trap that sees you wait in line most of the time. 

Lots of options but the crowds make it a no go for me. No sense in waiting in line for 30 minutes thee are plenty of city restaurants better than wasting time in reading terminal.

The food was just ok.  I was expecting more with a crowd waiting to get in for brunch at 11am.  I got the sausage gravy and cheddar biscuits.  It came out room temperature, gravy was kind of bland but the biscuits were banging.   I wouldn't come back to this place again unless I start to see the reviews get better.

Reading Terminal Market? There are no words to adequately describe my love for you. Yes, I stay in Philadelphia for my friends and family, but next to my them, you are the reason I will probably never leave Philadelphia. There are practical places like Iovine's where I can get relatively inexpensive, quality and often unique produce, the Fair Foodstand with locally grown produce and products or wonderful bread bakeries like Le Bus or Metropolitan. Termini's, Flying Monkey, or Chocolate by Mueller where I can satisfy my cravings for sweets. My buddies at Giunta's or Martin's Sausages that provide me with the best meat, especially bacon, in the metropolitan area. The great John Yi Fish market that always provides extremely friendly service and great products.

Of course too are all the great Amish merchants, in particular Haltemann Brothers, Kauffman's and of course my favorite, the Bellier's bakery where you can get the best whoopie pies in the world. Or the independent home cooks that sometimes sell their wares in the center court, from applesauce to kettle corn. 

And without rambling on too much more, there are all the great restaurants...the amazing hoagies from Salumeria (who happens also to have an amazing cheese and olive selection), the fantastic pork sandwiches from Dinics or the duck lo mein from Sang Kee Peking Duck and the places I still haven't gotten to try yet.

So, if you are coming to Philly for anything, you *must* go to Reading Terminal Market. Try any of the places I mentioned...you get my guarantee.

This place is pretty good. The sandwiches are similar to Subway, but made a lot better, in my opinion. And I'm a huge fan of the milkshakes! I'd go here just for those. But the sandwhiches are totally worth it too.

The place is a little tricky to get to, you have to pull around the back, park in the garage, and then walk back around the building and down some stairs. But its not really all that inconvenient.

This is a good place to grab a quick lunch if you don't have a whole lot of time for a sit-down meal.

I absolutely loved this little market. It has everything you could possibly want to buy, food-wise. My husband, father, mother, and I got breakfast there the two days that we were in Philadelphia and could barely decide on what to get! Everything is fresh and homemade, which is refreshing and fun. We chose one of the Amish diner-type booths to eat, and my parents got smoothies from another both; everything was delicious. There are tons of different specialty shops offering everything from candies to spices to kitchen equipment. I honestly could have spent a few hours wandering around, but we had plans, so we only spent 30 minutes or so exploring. I wish I could go back every day!

This was a great stop on our way back from Dorney Park we stopped here thanks to Adam (Man Vs Food) Richman If I lived in this area this would be a great place to go everyday. It's for locals and tourist alike the only set back is parking but this goes for any stop in any big city,so sit back enjoy the food or read a book from the used book section and relax...

This place is great.  You can get just about whatever you want served fresh here daily.  It's great for groups with different eating preferences because there is something for everyone.  

A few of my favorites were: Meltkraft (grilled cheese), Cookie Co , Dinics Sandwiches.  I haven't worked myself through the entire market, but I'd go back to Philly just for Reading Terminal Market
Great food and so many options!  Great crowds too, though.  Otherwise it would be a 5 star.  Try Hershel's Deli for the absolute best pastrami and corned beef!!!!
This is a place where no matter what food you are looking for you'll find! A great Philadelphia experience! So many choices and locally grown veggies! Amish food galore!
A must-see in Philly! Lunch hour is craaaaaazy crowded, but that's part of the fun if you're up for it.
Best place to pick up vegetation and baked goods. Yum yum.
I agree with most people here. New visitors to Philadelphia.. this is a must stop. Close to subway, close to Chinatown. Open during weekends. What more to ask?
Very good food and service eventing is fresh made a soon you pick you orden thanks you

Great place with something for everyone. Make sure to check out the Amish booths and the warthog statue (just because it's there). Once in a while, they'll have some sort of fair in there and those are awesome especially when they have FUNNEL CAKE!

I never drive to go to RTM, as I consider driving around there akin to a horrible nightmare, but if you do, park in the garage and get your ticket validated for a discount. It's in walking distance to nearby hotels and very accessible via Septa.

One thing that always annoyed me was when I went there on everyone's lunch break. The lines will be long, the small aisles will be cramped, and it will be painful to find a place to sit. You may be lucky and score one of the picnic tables in the back near the piano but you'll be sharing with others.

Been here a few times
Loud but great atmosphere
Today stopped for brunch
A mimosa and breakfast sandwich
Not your typical breakfast sandwich
Delish 
Priced right
I will be back

Spent a week out in Philly last November and came here for breakfast 3 times. The food is delicious and the crowd isn't too bad but to put that in perspective I'd be one of the first people in there because I'm an early riser I went another time later in the day for a late lunch and it was much more crowded but to me the the food was definitely worth the wait. There are so many options to choose from and I enjoyed it all from the donuts, pretzels, the Amish restaurant, chocolate store, and the sandwiches. If you are in Philly and want to stop some place with a lot of good food options this is it.

Whether you are visiting Philadelphia, live in town or in the burbs, this is a must see. Whatever type of food you are craving, you will find here. A Philadelphia institution.  Mornings and afternoons are the bet bet since the market closes at the end of the workday.

What a great place to sample different foods and get a good feel of what this town is all about, especially for a tourist!

Planning on making more trips to this place.

As a tourist, I could spend all day in this place. As a foodie, I wanted to spend all week trying the delicacies of each booth! From cookies to cheese to sandwiches, you will definitely find something worth your tastebud's while. 

Tips:
Sunday is not a great day to go - many of the traditional booths are not open for business. 

Bring cash!
Almost too many incredible choices. Minus one for the absolute mad house that it always is. If you're visiting Philly and don't mind crowded places, this is a must-go.

This is the greatest indoor food market in North America.  The colors, the sounds, the smells, the tastes, and the cool feel - every sense is used in a visit to the Reading Terminal Market.  Fortunately it retains its tradition and old look despite its modern infrastructure.  It's the best place in Philly to food shop and one of the best spots to eat.  There are too many culinary highpoints here to single one out.  But one thing I can tell you to def do is to put a coin in the nose of the pig statue in the center of the market, make a wish, and then rub the snout for good luck.  Now you're a real Philadelphian!
love the energy and the variety. Peking duck and Sang Kee is a fav.

I'm a Philadelphia native, and I'm amazed at the variety and vitality every time I come down here. I haven't yet tried everything, but I'm working on it, and I know I like DiNic's roast pork. Adam Richman was spot on!

Great diversity in terms of food choices - anywhere from authentic Mexican, Italian, Asian to American. Also a lot of dessert and coffee shops! It gets really crowded during lunch time but it's prime location. Amazing grilled cheese and a donut shop.

This place has it all. On my most recent visit to  Philly I ate Amish cookies & donuts and enjoyed the crab cakes at the Pearl.  Previous visits have found me worshipping at the altar of Dutch Eating Place's apple dumpling.  I will be back, oh I will be back.

Love coming to the market whenever I visit Philadelphia.  They have anything and everything you could imagine.  This is where people come for their fresh produce, meats, dairy products who live downtown in a high rise.

I love all the restaurants in the market as well, I always love getting a cheese steak sandwich from Karmens when I visit Philadelphia.

This place is a SIX STAR!  We traveled north on the recommendation of pretty much everyone from Philadelphia and the multi hour drive was well worth it.  As we arrived late we didn't have much time, but we ordered a pretzel, a felafel, some chocolate and bought a few sausages for the road as well.  All of it: A+.

Pretzel beat out the NYC street pretzel, which surprised me (though it's far lower profile) - lower salt and more substantial.  The felafel was awesome, though I'm sure you can get a good one everywhere these days.  That one was particularly delicious - lots of greens.  

Great on price, super high quality.  Great environment with must be hundreds of different establishes.  I'd say this is the strong equivalent of Fanheuill Hall in Boston, Mass and that it probably has no equivalent on the East Coast.  To me worth a trip from wherever

Minor quibble.  We were there at closing and the custodians truly shove you out the door.  So be sure to get everything done with some time to spare.  Everyone's nice until closing time, don't expect to beat the clock and make out big because...they really push you out. Literally.
It's an awesome place to visit. Great food, cheese, olive oil and a variety of items. Only problem is parking.
eclectic mix of food + beer garden + amish people + people watching = good times

LOVED THIS PLACE! I love farmer's markets and this one is so awesome. My senses went in overload just trying to take in everything I saw. Great food! I seriously wished I had 5 stomachs so I could eat everything I wanted there. Amish bakery and stalls had great honey selections. 

If I go back to Philly, this is a sure place to chow down.

I love walking in this place and smelling all the freshly baked things.. I mean it's like anything you could like is here.. .. they have all types of foods.. from mini produce markets,, where you can pick up your farm share.. to sushi.. to a bakery with delicious treats! 

I ended up here most recently because of JURY DUTY! the best part of that long terrible day was going into the market and finding my favorite; most recently discovered at linvilla orchards; apples.. THAT MADE MY DAY! it's just delightful.. if you have jury duty many vendors will give you a discount.. and they also have cheap lunch specials.. 

The place gets packed.. however they do have so man entrances and exits that things flow decently. 

it's like a gem smack dab in the middle of center city.. you've got to love it!

"If you dont have enough money to tip, you dont have enough money to drink at a bar. Go to the liquor store." So says a handout from The Industry Bar. Funny thing- I might never have enough money to drink there...

After a loooooooong time waiting for this new place to open, I was absolutely ecstatic to try it out when I heard about the opening on Wednesday. My first meal was brunch on Sunday. It didnt go so well. 

My wife got the espresso martini. Delicious drink, but seriously, $10? It seemed slightly smaller than a typical martini to me, and though delicious, wow thats an expensive drink. 

This was the theme, it seemed. I ordered "The Stomectomy." This would seem to be a signature item of glutinous wonder, ala the famous Kitchen Sink at Green Eggs. Three pancakes, with bacon, sausage and housemade scrapple, all topped by a single fried egg. 

One problem- it didnt have scrapple. I realized this about halfway thru my meal, and by the time I received said meatstuff, I was 90% finished. Furthermore, the pancakes were literally undercooked and almost runny. The egg? Well, it was overcooked and stiff- what should have been yolky goodness dumped all over the massive concotion instead was a hardened yellow thing, with a brown, rubbery bottom. I hate over cooked eggs. 

It should be said that my party loved their pancakes, and I can say wihout a doubt that they were delicious. 

The space is beautiful. Modern but not loud, in terms of both volume and design. 

The staff was overworked and not able to keep up with the demands of their tables, but I get the feeling that they were busier than expected. They get a pass for that. 

Four people at brunch, only one alcoholic drink cost over $70. That's too much, I think. 

My instinct is to give Industry 2 stars. However, it was one of their first brunches, and I feel like they deserve another chance. I need to try the burger. I want to see a dinner service. Still, I feel like the menu and pricing as it stands will not succeed in the blue collar Pennsport neighborhood. It seems like a serious, serious miscalculation.

If I hadn't taken my adderal prior to experiencing Reading Terminal Market, I may have imploded. It's like Disney Land for foodies. 

In one corner, you can pick up a sheepskin rug, sheered from a farm in Virginia. 
In another, you can gorge on black and white cookies.
The variety is never ending, and each vendor is better than the next.

Personally, this is as big of  TO DO for tourists as the Rocky Stairs.
Awesome experience every time! Variety of food to choose from! Never disappointed! This has to be on agenda during your visit to Philadelphia!

Outstanding! This is my new favorite place at Penn! They have a menu buy really you can just get whatever your heart desires; subtract anything you don't want and add any veggies or grain you want for no additional charge. They also have meat options if that's what you want. The sauces are phenomenal. 

What really sets this place apart though is the service. The staff is so helpful, friendly and excited. They are actually excited to help customers. And the experience can be a bit overwhelming at first (so much to try, so many options). I know that I really needed the help. I was greeted with a smile and guided through the menu. Everything was explained to me and suggestions were made. My overall experience here was great. I will certainly be back.

Place gets crazy at lunchtime, but I would always make it a point to have lunch here at least once a week when traveling for business.  DiNic's has an amazing Italian sausage, also love Beiler's donuts & 4th Street Cookies.

This is my favorite place to visit in all of Philadelphia.  I come frequently for business and am disappointed if I cannot swing by at least once per visit.  I am a foodie and this place is nirvana.  Words cannot adequately describe the hustle and bustle or the mind boggling selections there.  It needs to be experienced.  On my first visit, it was almost too much to take in at once.  Sensory overload, and I am a New Yorker!  Whatever you have a hankering for will be there.  Just be patient and you'll stumble on it.

This is a food heaven, and you could easily get food coma here.  This place is just as good as the farmer's market by the SF pier, the Quincy Market in Boston, and/or the farmer's market nearby the Grove in LA.  Yet, the feel is unique and different from all the markets mentioned above. 

This place is extremely busy when we ate lunch here on a Tuesday.   There's a convention center nearby.  Needless to say, there were a lot of people from the convention center.  Luckily, they put a lot more seating than last time I came (in April 2011).  Still, it took me a while to look for a table, and while I was waiting for my husband to buy food, I was asked way too many times if they could sit at my table.  If you decide to eat here during the week, be prepare to wait online for food and to wait for a table for your party.

Also, since it's right in the middle of Philadelphia, it's very difficult to find parking outside of the market during the work week.  And the traffic is terrible like any other city.

OMG this was one of the highlights of our quick getaway to Philly. We ate at Becks and scarfed down a fried oyster platter that had delusions fried potatoes with jalapeños and cornbread. Then my husband got something called the heartbreaker? Or something?? Or maybe that's what it DOEs to your heart - it was pastrami, salami and cheese god knows what on a roll. Tasty but greasy as hell Next we topped it all off at Bassett's Ice Cream which was soooo good- creamy and not too sweet.

Great market with a variety of different deli and ethnic foods, vegetables, fruits, cheeses and a variety of other items.  A lot of the popular places to eat have long lines so be prepared to wait a bit but overall the lines move fairly quickly.  A lot of tourists and the market makes for some great pictures.  Within walking distance to other Philly tourist attractions.  This was the primary reason for my visit to Philly but it turned out to be one of many sights to see in the area.

I am certainly repeating what other have said about this place, but I will share my experience. We love the terminal. It's a great place to bring people who are new to Philly and get an exciting and bustling experience. Lots to see. LOTS to eat. 

We have eaten at many of the vendors. You really can't go wrong with any. We loved the Amish doughnuts. Overall, fun place to swing through on your tour of downtown Philly. Eat it!

Can't decide on what to eat?  Then get your bum here right away.  Everyone has been here at least once.  If not, then go.  Even if your not hungry,  the smell and sights of the food will delight you.  Plus there are also nice shops within the market.  I recently discovered Meltkraf in here, grilled cheese heaven.  The fruit shake place tastes fresh and refreshing.  The cheese shop employees are very helpful and they had quince paste.  I love that there are now numerous places to sit and eat.  They do keep the place cleaner than before.

Its ok, I've lived in Philly for the majority of my life but I honestly don't get the hype of Reading Terminal. You can go in there and a variety of things like cake, cookies, candies, cheesesteak, Chinese food, soul food, groceries just to name a few things. Its always over crowded and seating can be limited depending on the time of day. My favorite spots here are the Famous 4th street cookie company Keven Parker's soul food café and Bassetts Ice Cream.

Cool place to go if you're a foodie and want to try a large variety of sandwiches and snacks. The place gets very crowded and seating for all the delicious food tastings is at a minimal. I recommend the cheese shop. They make some killer grilled cheese concoctions. Not good for little kids, don't be the asshole trying to maneuver a stroller around.
There are no words to describe this Philadelphia treasure! Support the local and independent vendors as often as you can!

When you get a free day to walk and explore a single building in downtown Philly, come with some cash and an empty stomach. You won't want to miss out on some of the great eats inside Reading Terminal and be a part of the hustle and bustle of the marketplace.

Some things that really sucked about coming here, the parking was ridiculous. I went on an off-day and it was still super busy and the structure (where I ended up parking) was pretty expensive. I felt really rushed to eat my food then get out. Next time, I'll have to try really hard to find street parking or maybe even a paid lot which is cheaper than the structure. Also, inside, you pretty much have to fight for a seat and hold down the fort while your friends order and bring the food because even though there's a lot of seating, there's a lot more people.

If you can walk down here and park further away and don't mind searching for a table/seats then this is a really cool place to check out.

Parking: Structure across the street $6/30mins or limited 2-hour street parking

This place is Food Channel Fantasy Heaven. Bakeries galore. Hot sandwiches. Green drinks. Salads. Fresh fruit. Chocolates everywhere. Just chocolate heaven. Similar to Chelsea Market in NYC but with a much homier, friendlier vibe. 

Do yourselves a favor and check it out!

The Reading Terminal Market in Philly is pretty amazing.  This place has just about everything...

We visited the following places of note:
1) Tommy DiNic's for some Roast Pork Sandwiches
2) Salumeria to get some Capicola and Mandaroni Provolone Cheese
3) Chocolate by Mueller for some delicious chocolate
4) Old City Coffee for some Kona Coffee

*YUM!*

Reading Terminal Markets offers so many delicious things to eat and purchase.  I love coming on the weekends for lunch and having my choice of gyros, roast pork, breakfast sandwiches, and some of the most delightful donuts in this city.  It is true that on the weekends the crowds can be crazy and it can be hard to walk through the aisles and browse, but if you know where you're going you can go in one of the exterior doors nearest your destination and cut out some of the hassle.  

Olympic Gyro makes awesome gyros (go for the platter and you get a heaping Greek salad on the side!), Beiler's Donuts are cream-filled gluttony (the banana is an old standard, and don't miss the banana ice cream at Bassett's-best banana ice cream EVER).  DiNic's is a classic and draws huge crowds of tourists and locals alike but I tend to skip the lines in favor of Olympic because you can pretty much always get a seat right away. 

 Also the Amish diner counter slings breakfast foods insanely fast- you've barely finished ordering and they already are putting plates down in front of you!  Very standard fare but worth it in a time crunch.

Also The Tubby Olive, a little shop that sells flavored olive oils and vinegars, is a great place to get a hostess/mom gift and they have tons of different styles and flavors that you can try in the shop.  A little pricey for olive oil and vinegar but a fun gift idea for someone who likes to cook/make salads.  

Also Reading Terminal Market is super conveniently located in Center City so it's perfect in the middle of a day on the town.  Watch out on Sundays though because many of the Amish shops are closed and you can't have any donuts :(.
This place is everything. Literally!! It has everything you can imagine. Love Keven Parker's and Beilers!!

I love Reading Terminal Market! It's got an amazing amount of options for food and goods. There's almost nothing you can't find here, and the atmosphere is filled with gastronomical excitement. Be aware that the lines can be long sometimes, and the market can be crowded.

Nice place to buy food but I find it to be more of a tourist trap. I prefer other areas of Philly for my Italian food. Defiantly a must stop for people visiting Philly but not what I would recommend for the locals. Great crapes for breakfast.
Anything and everything is here!  Well mostly anyway.  I love coming here for lunch and buying organic meats and produce at a ridiculously cheap price.  Great place to people watch.

The pita I had was good.  The chicken platter I had the seasoning was good but it was beyond hot. It was inedible it was so hot.  I ended up having to throw it out.  I'm not sure if that's the normal heat level for the food or someone got pepper happy

Service was quick and Plenty of open tables to sit at during lunch time. 
I got chicken tikka khaki roll and it was constantly falling out while taking a bite. It was not secured properly. There was barely any masala in it besides green chutney. Poorly made. I loved the rose lassi though. It was really good and worth the money. 
I prefer spice end over masala kitchen.

I came in and had a chicken combo it was really good. It is cash only but they have an ATM inside. The service was friendly and there was a TV which was playing some show that wasn't in English. Still was pleasant to sit and watch and eat I have no complaints. I didn't think that the portions were small. The seating area is narrow though so if there is a large group you might wind up sitting near the windows with your back to the door.

Amazing place.  Food stands covering pretty much everything and a zillion ethnic styles available.  Meat, fish, pastries, deli, all under one roof.  Prices looked on the high side but not bad.  They also have a bar to sit down and have a cold one after walking around.  Wish I had seen this place before eating or I would definitely have gotten something.  A must see when back in Philly.

When I worked as a travel nurse in 
Wilmington, DE a few years ago, I loved going into Philly to eat. The Reading Terminal Market is a DO NOT MISS for any foodie in City of Brotherly Love. Amazing choice of cuisines, and the caliber of the food is nothing short of amazing. .

Just an observation.....why would anyone w/ an ounce of common sense wait more than 10 minutes for food? I'm thinking that if you wait any longer than that for a taco or burrito, that would be your fault. Who's forcing you to stay?

SO AWESOME!!!!!!

It totally reminded me of the pike place market in Seattle, which means it's CRAZY AMAZY!!!

There are so many cool knick-knacks you can buy as gifts, (as I did), and you can splurge on taste-bud dancing, spine-tingling food, (as I did).

Everything there is great, but the two places you MUST go is DiNics and the beilers donut shop. SO GOOD!!!!

This place is essentially Quizno's with slightly better food and a less fast-foody atmosphere. The menu is very limited and consists mostly of about 10 different types of sandwiches, as well as milkshakes and ice cream.  They don't seem to do one thing that Quizno's does that sceezes me out.  Some of the meats at Quizno's get put in a little plastic basket and dipped in what looks like hot, dirty mop water before being put on your sandwich. Didn't observe this at  Potbelly.

Great but touristy and elbow to elbow at peak times.
I like the hustle and bustle but not to the point of bas aisle management and alot of stands get overlooked becaise of snaking lines for popular ones (like donuts & bbq).I am based in NJ and can get pretty much the same quality `Amish` at any of 5 places within the same drive so I pretty much only go when vibing something different.I dislike the parking situation but I get it,its `urban`. I enjoy the slection at the organic co-op style stall up front,really neat stuff and nice staff. Alot of baked goods along the way..For variety A+, for the packed nature A-..The pixxa place near the door across from produce had the driest grossest looking things in the hot buffet. Termini Bros gave us Iced Tea when asked for Iced coffee.Would we return? Yes,but not as a destination like we made it,we would have to be doing sometihng nearby. Hershels Deli looked like good pastrami being thrown down,but we were so full and already had eaten so we passed.

So much fun to visit! A great place to have a meal if you're just visiting. Favorites were Old City Coffee and the flower market. We had drinks at Mollys, which were good. If I were in PA any longer, I would have been back for several meals.

A great selection of good eats! I love the Creole restaurant. I was pleasantly surprised at how well seasoned the food was. This place has everything from healthy juices to cupcakes and banana pudding.
I love this place! It's always so vibrant and full of neat things to see, buy, and eat. Pro tip: I like to go pick up some spices and fresh produce before splurging on an ice cream cone.

Who doesn't love reading terminal? They have everything you could possibly want, and since extending their hours a couple years ago, it's made it easier to get these things. 
I regularly go there for produce, seafood and local raw milk.
It's a must see for visitors so bring all of your guests! 
Absolutely go there for lunch some time, but try to go on an off hour, not right at noon, because it gets super busy.
The Dutch eating place is the best for breakfast and although they are usually pretty busy, they keep things moving.
Love love!  Buy groceries here once a week.  Two hours free parking in the structure.  Nice local grocery items.  Cheaper than Whole Foods.  As a local I recommend.

Hi, Taiwanese person here. Got all excited when I saw this place opened in my area, but I was not impressed with this chicken. Okay, I normally don't go crazy over fried foods but I was feeling nostalgic of Taiwanese fried chicken...I think what's lacking is the five spice powder. Not sure if they used any, but my impression was that it lacked flavor and was dry. I found another place in town that I think is better, but some of my friends have had better experiences here..probably won't go out of my way to come here unless someone credible told me they really improved it since they first opened. Also seating in this restaurant is so limited so it would be hard to bring a big group here.

My favorite place to visit when in Philly! Such a diverse market with tons of great finds! Not to mention a great selection of food joints! 

Upon entering, the aroma of different foods instantly strikes up your appetite! 

The market is conveniently located in city center near the convention center! 

Definitely on my top list of favorite places!

Simply put Reading Terminal Market is one of the reasons I continue to live in Philadelphia. The fresh produce and meats, the amazing restaurants, and the exquisite desserts are heavenly. Not everything it the market is an absolute winner, but that's only because you can walk 2 ft over to another booth and get something mind-blowing. Essentially when walking the market you can never go wrong, just miss out on the actual best roast pork, grilled reuben, or chocolate chip cookie.

This place was amazing! We went here twice while spending a week in Philly and it did not disappoint. I wish I had more time to visit every place and that there was more room. Due to the small space, it can become overwhelming. DiNic's pork sandwich was great and Carmen's had the best Philly cheese steak I've ever had! Make sure to stop by Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. for some delicious treats!

If you have a taste for KFC, I suggest that you try any other location then 57th Baltimore ave. the service at this location sucks. The cashiers are rude, and the manager is just as rude as they are. Well I guess that's why they have the job that they have, because they'll never be able to work anywhere else. Me myself, will drive the extra mile to get better service.  They actually deserve no stars, but you got to select a star.

Reading Terminal Market makes a trip to Philadelphia worth it. 

Think... Seattle's Pike's Place Market, Los Angeles' Grand Central Market, New York City's Chelsea Market.

But I personally would rather go here than the other places mentioned above.

First time here! Was told by the locals to come and I wish I would have been here sooner. We did get some dessert, but it has a FAZILLION restaurants, candy shops, market, etc. Great idea! Great ambience.  Definitely worth a shot!

This place is massive. Tons of things to see, booths to check out and you will never, ever starve to death here. All kinds of ethnic treats, local staples and everything in between. Also are stalls of goods and sundries as well. We were there on a Saturday evening, probably half an hour before they closed. Packed to the gills, even then. This place is pretty much an entire city block, so be sure to give yourself plenty of time to look around and decide carefully what you REALLY want to sink your teeth into. Otherwise you may experience doughnut envy or sandwich regret. And no one, no one, deserves that.

Came here for the first time and it was fun! Avoid the lunch time rush though, it gets really crowded. Come with an empty stomach and fill it with lots of yummy food. We had some homemade chocolates, a Philly cheesesteak, I bought some spices, kale salad, some honey to go, and got some fruit for the road.

Wow! If you go in here a lunchtime, your head will spin! So many options! So many people! So much fun! Once you start navigating through the river of humankind you begin to grasp the possibilities. Sandwiches, salads, ice cream, fruits, veggies... the list goes on. Once settled in, you see the people. Workers squeezing in a lunch, locals for produce, tourists for the experience and that list goes on too. So, what are you waiting for?

I came here one night with some friends after a few drinks in the area, suddenly craving some spice and flavorful food from the motherland. I usually don't eat Indian food out in Philly - haven't had anything remarkable at a few places I tried, but the kati rolls here were impressive! The prices are very reasonable for the amount of food you get - I ordered the Chicken Tikka and Achari Paneer rolls for a total of about $11. The food came out fast, they gave me the Achari chicken instead of the paneer, but I didn't mind, they were both delicious! I will be coming back to try the other options!

As someone else pointed out, a few minutes after we came in, the room got a little smoky, so if you plan on sitting down for a while, you might end up leaving smelling like Indian food. But if you plan to take out, eat it quick or else they may get soggy.

This place was heaven. So many variety of food in such a compact area. The only problem is that there are so many people here during lunch hours. That and the fact that it closes early than I'm used to. There is such a diverse range of food that I'm pretty sure you can find what you want just by walking around for 15 minutes. Chinese, cajun, soul food, BBQ, dessert, breakfast, candy, groceries, there is just so much to this little terminal. There is also a seating area that had a piano and live music. It was very cute.

The pretzels at this amish looking section was so incredible. Buttery goodness with mustard dipping. This was definitely the most memorable thing after eating some ice cream and jambalaya and trying out gator meat gumbo.
This place has everything you could think of to eat.  All the stands are high quality and tasty.  I dont get there enough.

I love coming here for fresh veg and fruit (Iovine Brothers) and shopping here at Reading Terminal is something everyone should experience. 

Although you probably don't want to bring small children during lunch, it gets more than a little crowded.
Philly classic, always great for breakfast or lunch. Check out the Amish stand, ribs and apple dumplings are some of my favorites.

I just moved to the Pennsport area and was excited to see this bar around the corner from my house. A friend and I went for drinks and appetizers on a Sunday night around 9pm. The place had a good crowd, out door seating and a good vibe. We had the macaroni and cheese bites, the buffalo chicken bites, and the tater tots. The macaroni and cheese croquettes were the best then the tater tots. Would be reordering them. The buffalo chicken bites we both agreed were not good as they had too much buffalo sauce in them and were mushy. Overall it was a cool place that I am excited is in my neighborhood.

amazing, That's all I can say. This place is a pregnant woman's dream. I've never been pregnant but when I do and I have food cravings, I'll just go here and eat from ever vendor! The amish pretzels are the best
I eat there from time to time, there are plenty of food selections. I would suggest visiting the Reading Terminal Market.

This McDonald's is horrible! It's always pretty dirty; being that it's in a location that gets a lot of business, you'd think that they would go out of their way to ensure it was cleaner. Another thing that really frustrates me about this location is that the play place is closed more than it's open. I love pretty close to here, which is why I go to this one and my daughters look forward to the play place; more often than not it's closed for no apparent reason which disappoints them. The McDonald's on Oregon Ave, which also has a (nicer) play place, seems to always be open. The point of having a play area in a restaurant is for the kids to play and I'm sure that's why many parents go to this one, however, it's disappointing and frustrating that they hardly open it. The food is just like any other McDonald's for the most part. The only "saving" quality of this location would be SOME of the employees. Definitely not all because some of them are straight up miserable.

I love this place. I love the variety of the vendors, and everything I've eaten  here has been finger-lickin' good. 
My faves: 
-cannoli from termini bros 
-doughnut from beilers
-coffee from old city
-cheesesteak from Tony Dinics

This place is amazing! It was listed as one of the places to check out in Philly. It was right around the corner of my hotel so this was my first stop in Philadelphia. The atmosphere is crazy but everyone is very nice and helpful. If you don't quite know what you want to eat and need options this is somewhere you should be. We saw everything from pizza to donuts, vegetarian to Asian. The market has dozens of shops, most selling fresh food or produce. It definitely can be a little overwhelming if you aren't ready for the amount of noise and people but it is definitely worth the trip. With so many choices you may find yourself going round and round seeing where your taste buds lead you.

You can easily get lost in unique balsamic vinegars and olive oils while also tasting great chocolates or even food showcased on cooking channels. It is also indoors which is a plus to escape hot or cold days in the city. The diverse little markets and restaurants make the Reading Terminal Market a Philly a must see!
I had beef tikka. Friendly and quick service. Food was hot and flavorful. Will return to try other rolls.

Love the Reading Terminal, even when it gets super crowded. Such delicious food all over the place. I make sure to take all out of town guests here for the experience. Just wish it was open later during the week so I could get there after work more regularly.

Glad to have it in the neighborhood to get a drink. Burgers are great, corn on the ob great, everything else has been so-so to inedible. Servers are fun, though and beer list is good. Atmosphere is good.
Excellent selection of food. I love the Mezze Mediterranean place, the creperie, Dutch fried chicken and apple pies. If you are craving it they have it!
This is my favorite place me and my 8 yrs old son was taken pictures we ate and played all night well from 12to 4 best day ever

Foodie paradise.  Immaculate. I only wish we had been a bit hungrier when we went.  We had pretzels from an Amish stand, peirogies from a deli stand, and ice cream from Bassetts. All superb.  The meats and produce looked super fresh, with reasonable prices.  Wonderful selection of jams and jellies, nuts, olives, cheeses, oils, flowers.  The most delicious looking donuts that they make in front of you, in so many flavors.  Can't wait to visit again!
Pretty much any type of food you'd want!! I stayed across the street and popped over several times during my visit. They have the Amish market on the weekends as well.

I'm a fan! My friends and I were were looking for a place to grab something quick to eat when we ran into this place. 

FOOD: Reading Terminal has it all; bagels, breakfast sandwiches, coffee, tea, and freshly-squeezed juice. I tried them all :) 

LOCATION: We came at a good time (early morning) so it wasn't hard to find a place to sit. There are tables available for you to enjoy your feast. 

*TIP* I recommend grabbing a freshly squeezed juice from one of the stands. I don't remember what this place is called but it's towards the back where the produce is. 

Will I come back? Well, I'm not from around here but yes! I'll make my way back if I'm around.

After passing this small place by car and seeing they are open til 10, we walked over.
Clean and neat, we each ordered the 5 dumplings with the salad. Our first time there feeling brave. And it was really good!
Not greasy and full of flavor. A great light meal. I recommend anyone to go over and enjoy. We'll be back!

Went there this Monday with a co-worker. The place was clean and it is a typical Halal food place. I ordered their signature Chicken over Rice... I would say the first few bites were super great and it reminds me of NYC 6 Guy Halal. However, the taste became so so later on. I think the portion of rice is too much that I got tired of the food in the end. I will give this placs another try next time and maybe try some other dish on their menu.
Hands down the best place to eat in Philly.  If you aren't into crowds, be warned that it's almost always packed. The lines move quickly and the food can't be beat.

Oh my god! I love this place! So many food choices. I could live here! This marketplace would be the reason I move to Philly. I would get an apartment right above and eat every meal at the Reading Market Terminal. From Cajun to Philly Cheesesteaks, cookies to cheese cakes, it doesn't get much better than this place in Philly. Its a few blocks from Historical Philly, so if you are in the neighborhood, drop by and get some grub.
Awesome burger place. Tons of great food with wonderful service. The staff is super friendly and the place is nice and clean. I had a great time and a wonderful meal that wasn't too expensive.
Some of the best seafood, fresh Vegetables, dutch country milk juice, cheeses. Some of the very best salads, ribs and chicken wings.

Why cant all cities have affordable, year-round farmers markets that sell food? Its such a great idea to have so many small businesses and farmers come together to sell fresh wholesome food- -- at DECENT prices!
My all time favorite market in Philadelphia with a plethora of food options from pretzels, to burgers, and Chinese food.
Really crowded on weekends. Too many sweets to choose from. You have to get the roast or pulled pork.

This is one of my favorite places to visit in Philadelphia.   Other cities have markets in their downtowns, but this is the gold standard.   Like other markets, there are a lot of food vendors here.   However, unlike other markets, it's HUGE and there are so many grocers here that you could actually do your weekly shopping here.

Tourist, tourists, and more tourists. I usually avoid weekends and holidays. Produce is cheap at Iovine brothers, lovely Dinic's sandwich, solid fishmongers, and great apple dumplings at Dutch eating place. You'll find what you need in one stop; it'll just take a while to find the most efficient route through this maze.
What great choices!! A bit of everything. I love going there for lunch when I am in Philly at the Convention Center

Obviously the Redding Terminal Market is a must. This place caters to every type of person. Everyone can find something that they love here. My favorite places are Hope's Cookies and the Amish Bakery. YUMM.

Make sure you park in the lot which gives one a much lower rate. Di Nic's has the best roast pork. Bassett's has the best ice cream. Metropolitan has the best chocolate chips.Then walk to Chinatown and buy a peking duck to take home.

Sure the tourists are here, but the tourists should be here--there's something for everyone. I go for blueberry pancakes with my husband but also the seasonal train show and cider donuts with my nieces and nephews. Where else can you eat, get a lil history, and buy a lavendar candle, cumin and jar of honey in the rain?

Nice beer selection and great food. The pig ear lettuce wraps are (unfortunately) no longer offered. They were incredible. The hillbilly Philly is a perfect hangover brunch. If you're a bloody mary fan, check out their ghost of Mary.

So many diverse options all under one roof! The Market has something for everyone at reasonable prices. You can find hoagies, cheesesteaks, fried chicken, Asian cuisine, grilled cheeses, doughnuts, Italian pastries and the list just goes on! 4th street cookies are out of this world. Let your taste buds guide you once you walk in and go with a few people to taste as much variety as you can!
everything you can think of. lots of good quality food and local organinc produce

Everybody talks about Reading as if it's a national treasure but I am sometimes let down by the market.  It's not that it's a good idea to have such a wide breadth of local flavor all in one place it's the execution that's lacking.  

What I mean is that most of the local flavor is represented but it's represented poorly meaning that most of the food is mediocre which is too bad considering you can walk a couple blocks to get the best of (insert food style).  In most cases, it's not who makes the best of a certain type of food but who can afford to pay the rent there.  What would really make the pace special is if they chose the top vendors as opposed to whoever can pay the most rent.  

The other issue, and this is a big one, is the lack of being open on Sunday.  This is really a chicken/egg issue.  Are most businesses closed on Sunday because of lack of business or is there a lack of business because most of them are closed?  All I know is this seems to be an epidemic in what is a city the size of Philadelphia.  In order to attract people into the center of city during the weekend, it has to be open first.  I understand that many of the businesses have religious reasons for not working on the Lord's day but this is akin to Chinatown shutting down one day a week in New York.  This is supposedly a world-class city so why does it feel like I'm in the middle of the midwest when I'm in Center City on a Sunday?

Pretty decent. The late hours and the healthy options really change up post-bar food options in the area. 

I had a few hit or miss experiences, but the hits were all fantastic.
One of THE BEST places in the whole city.  Lots of great food and options.  A little crazy when a convention is in town or for lunch during the week, but always worth the time.

A thorough review of reading terminal would probably take ages. So Im going to keep it brief on this one. Reading Terminal is a Philadelphia landmark, if you eat food, you should definitely check it out. You will be entranced by the plethora of produce, shops, mini-restaurants and general awesome ambiance. This place is pure joy.
Love this place it's a foodies dream! It can get a bit overwhelming because of all the choices of food and the weekend crowd. This is always a must whenever I come to Philadelphia

Push your way through the crowds to find pretty much anything your heart desires in this old train depot. Amish/Mennonite baked goods, meat and salads are not to be missed. Stop by termini's to pick up a fresh cannoli. Sit in the food court and hope someone will sit down at the piano and play.

Real solid place.  Food is good, great draft selection.  I'd give it 5 stars but I think certain things on the menu are a bit over priced.  Its great to have a place like this in the neighborhood and not have to walk all the way to Passyunk.

Excellent place. Great options. Open super late. The panee roll is perfection and the chutney is very flavorful.  I wish we had places like this in Houston.  Friendly staff and the place was packed at 3am.  Good sign.  

They place is clean and the location is really convenient. Go support.

what a difference a day makes. 

The amish bring such a different energy and aroma of tasty goodness its worth scheduling your life to be back here the next week to partake in their offerings.

Though the crowds still get a mighty crazy, the people are still not too hurried to show a little courtesy and flash a smile when approached with one. The little surprises around every corner continue to appear and unless you live here 24/7 we are all tourists to a degree and just need to learn to be more open to new opportunities of learning from a larger pool of the population.

Went for a quick lunch. It was good food loved the chicken tikka masala roll. Good prompt service and food was great. A good way to taste nice Indian food that you would find in india ie. Rolls. Definitely recommend it for all! Go check it out.

First time back here in ~20 yrs.  Good to see many familiar vendors and lots of new stuff too.  No matter what your individual taste, there is something to please just about anyone.  For me, it was sampling some German for lunch (Bavarian sausage sandwich), since for the most part, that it not easy to find where I currently live.

Of course, at peak lunch hour, finding open seating can be tough, though generally no worse than in any urban market in any major city I've visited.  The staff seems to make a really good effort to keep the Market clean, despite the volume of patrons.

Our group browsed around for a while, sampling some 'Old City Coffee' and of course a few sweets.  The dark chocolate pretzels were the perfect dessert for me!
This place is amazing with lots of food and choices. From sweet to salty, you'll find something you like for sure. The best market I've been to so far. Definitely a must stop!!!
Cool place , good food & many selections. Try Molly Malloy's , Chef Bob Fischer is a food icon .

1800 reviews can't lie right!!

I love this place. Being a foodie (aren't we all) this place was heaven. A huge variety of foods from any genre imaginable. You have everything from bakeries to delis to asians serving peking duck (hanging in the windows just like you would find in Chinatown).

We went there on a Sunday afternoon and though parking is a bit of a pain, there are some meters closeby that charge $3 per hour and a maximum time of 2 hours. I only stayed there for about an hour, but I am sure you can "refill" the car without penalty.

They also advertise discount parking rates at two closeby garages for $4 for up to two hours with a valid $10 purchase at the market, which I think is great for business.

I wish I was in Philadelphia for longer than one day. I was able to pick up some fresh veggies from the market, a few cookies from 4th Street Cookies and a Brisket Rueben from Hershel's Deli. Everything was great. I would have loved to try DiNic's as per the food channel, but the line was longer and I was craving a Rueben. 

There are some tables in common areas to sit and eat as well.

Seafood selection there is also amazing. I witnessed the biggest shrimp I have ever seen at $28.99/lb. 

Definitely a must in Philly.

Two places you MUST go:
1. Bieler's Bakery ( must try the fritters! But donuts are excellent too.) 
2. Little Thai Market ( order the grilled salmon with red curry over white rice. It's the sole reason the line is always super long)
The pastrami sandwich I had from the deli here was better than the ones at the Carnegie Deli and Katz's in New York.  That means it was plenty good.

Tons of choices under one roof! I found alcohol-free food flavorings here and the shopkeeper was nice enough to write down things I would like to see at his store in the future.  The place is buzzing with variety and excitement and the fresh produce is beautiful..... If you're in Philly and haven't been here yet, GO TODAY!

The Reading Terminal Market was founded in 1893 and has evolved into a major dining destination.  It is a food Mecca where you can taste just about any type of food you desire.  The Reading Market has something for everyone.  Every type of food to enjoy and ravish.  Prices are reasonable, but flavour and choices are abundant.  The Reading Market also offers something for FREE.  If you are like me, and addicted to your iPhone....your battery is always hot.  At the Reading Market they offer a service to charge your cell phone for free.  It is a locker that you can leave your phone locked up while you grab a bite to eat.  How cool is that?

Met my gal pal C at the Industry for happy hour. We both ordered "the Mildred" cocktail which was delicious and extremely easy going down. For food we sampled bone marrow, pork nuggets, crispy pigs ears and fried green tomatoes. The food was good.  Drinks very good.  Since the Industry is so close I'm sure I will be back.
An absolute must-do when you're in Philly. Only challenge is where to eat because everything looks and smells so good.

This place was really cool but crazy crowded!! It's definitely a tourist spot.  It has so many good places to eat.  It was cool to walk around and see the different shops.  I came for the cookies.  4th street famous cookies.  They were delicious!!  Wish I was hungry to try other places but we ate before we came here.
Best pastrami sandwich ever at Herschel's Deli.  Headed straight from the airport to the deli to have the hot pastrami sandwich....yum!

I never really went to chipotle because it is way too far for me, but ever since they opened it up on Cottman, I love it here! 
Service here is excellent, they are very fast and gets my order right. Employees here is very friendly. Atmosphere is good here there are plenty of seats to sit and eat with friends and family.

I always love this place.  And I give it the rare, for me, 5 stars.  Is every place 5 stars? No, but should every one have an exceptional experience there? Yes!

- I really like the gourmet burger place's mac and cheese.  And this Indian Food Place was solid.  Everyone should check out a Cheese Steak and Amish Pretzel while they are there (I personally think the ones here are better than Pat's or Geno's).

Here are some tips -- if you don't like crowds, don't go.

Plan to spends some time there - 1.5 to 2.5 hours, minimum.  I can't think of a food part they don't have covered.

I have reviews for other places individually.

I've only been here once so far but feel the need to write a good review. I'm quite surprised by the negative ones so far. (And no, I do not know the owners in any way. I wish I did so I could get this 20% industry discount I keep reading about.)

First, I will admit a bias: I want any good restaurant in my neighborhood to do well because I enjoy having good places such as these close by. So while normally I would go a few times before writing a review, I'm jumping the gun a bit now to give them my props.

We went for dinner, and I thought the prices were extremely reasonable and much cheaper than you'd pay in center city, so I'm surprised by the complaints there. Maybe it's more of a large plate issue; we only ordered small plates etc. For example, we had pork nuggets for $6 and a burger for $8, and I thought we got a decent amount of food for what we paid. Yes, the burger was thin, but some of us (like me) prefer our burgers that way, and you can double it for a little bit more money. It was definitely a solid burger. All the dishes we had were good; the fries are especially delicious. My husband is a bit of a beer snob but enjoyed what they had on draft, and those prices were also reasonable.

The service was attentive and I like that they leave water at your table. It was a bit loud in there, but the restaurant has a nice ambiance and we will definitely be back.
If there is a food quart in heaven this it! Olympia Gyro is amazing! Plan on eating several times!
The worst pizza ever...it was cold...hardly no cheese and tasted horrible....not ordering here ever again. I'm giving one star because I can't put 0 rating.  That's how bad it's was...yuk yuk

Every time we visit Philly we come here for lunch! We usually go to Hershel's and get the Rueben, it's delicious and so fresh! There's so many different places to eat that everyone in the group will find something to get. Last time we went there was a little table for Birdie's biscuits, and it was the most amazing biscuit we've ever had. I hope next time we go he's there again! Totally recommend people going to get some quick food!
Best place for lunch and shopping in Philly hands down! I especially love the Amish bakery and butcher stalls.

It's going on 23 years that I've been a regular here, so I've been coming here long enough to see vendors come and go. Doesn't matter; I can always find a new favorite among my standard go-tos. First, what's now called Olympia Gyro has THE BEST gyros in the area!!! You have to drive 40 miles to even get close to its runner-up (Olympia Restaurant in Vineland, NJ). Bassett's Raspberry Truffle Ice Cream is a-ma-ZING! The Dutch Eating Place is a great place for a quick breakfast pig out. Take-home fresh pastas from George's or fresh produce from Iovine's. Munch on chocolate chip with walnuts cookies from Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. or chocolate covered pretzels from Chocolate by Mueller. Create your own salad with too-many-good-choices-to choose-from at Tootsie's Salad Express or fill up on falafel, shawerma, or kebabs at Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties. 

Ignore the crowds; the Market's location across from the Convention center guarantees crowds - but that's GOOD! That means the market will be around for a very long time - and that's GOOD!

Can I really say anything that hasn't already been said? Probably not. Reading Terminal Market was everything I wanted it to be and more. It was busy and crowded and it had one of everything. My recommendation is to check out the Amish booths, as they serve wonderful deliciousness such as "Peanut Butter Delite" for EL CHEAPO. Also, half-dill pickles, which are the best. In addition to all the food, there was this totally random guy in the back selling books. So awesome. New favorite place.

This was one of my favorite places in Philadelphia.  As a local, it was a great place to come and get fresh produce, cheese, and meat in the mornings before the crowds arrive.  There are all kinds of places to get a quick meal, but my favorite for breakfast is the Dutch Eating Place.  They always have wonderful pancakes and sausage and you can get a homemade apple dumpling to take home for later.  If you are a fan of people watching, you can certainly see a lot here between the locals, the tourists, and the people in town for a convention.  Finish off your visit with homemade ice cream in a pretzel cone and you have a perfect day!

Now that I've moved to New York, I still haven't found any place that quite replaces Reading Terminal Market.

If you're a foodie this is the place for you. Tons of places to try from breakfast to dessert. I of course had a cheesesteak and it was delicious. But there's tons of places that you can eat from. Also there is deli and produce flowers. A must see if you're in the area.

I love everything about this place from the baked goods to the seasoning the fresh meats. The Dutch have the freshest products. And if you get your parking pass stamped it's only about $4 to park. Once I was done shopping for home goods I sat down for lunch before leaving

Cute place. They have food stalls where you can grab a casual bite to eat or an ice cream and sit down and relax. Also a produce market inside. They close early however so don't expect to go for dinner, unless it's early dinner! Closed by 6p and I notice many places close even earlier. I think it's more of a casual lunch place. It's definitely worth a stop by if you are in the area.

I shop here when I want to cook the freshest food for dinner. Fresh food with great prices. If you want cheaper seafood go around the corner to Chinatown and bring a translator.  NOT enough actual markets like this around. Second only to the Italian Market.

This place is awesome. I literally spent 3 days here and kept finding new things! I also spent those same 3 days eating here every meal and barely made a dent in all the places you could eat. What a shame. I can't wait to come back here with a cooler so I can transport all sorts of good things back to Virginia with me! This place was best described by another reviewer as the "Disneyland/world for foodies." Spot on.

The Reading Terminal is a must do item for almost anyone visiting Philly. If you're in town for a convention it's a convenient choice for a wide array of lunch options. If you're a tourist there's great people watching and shopping. If you're a Monopoly fan you can stop a take a photo. (It's the terminal, or end, of the real Reading Railroad!)

On my trip I stopped in for a quick beer while killing some time and had a great conversation with a local who was in for lunch. I will say beware of pick pockets and thieves as the woman next to me had her purse taken right of the back of her chair!!
so much to see and do-- I always pick up vanilla hazelnut coffee at Old City Market and a wine tasting at blue market is a nice retreat. It can get a little crowded, but definitely worth it.
Always crazy packed with people, but they have some of the best food options and prices you can find around. I highly recommend this location for visitors of philly and just PA residents in general!
