I think I'm going to be able to get a new one for me and you, but I don't think I'm going to get my nails done with this new version of the best thing ever.

This is the first place anyone visiting Philadelphia should hit up. Yes, its packed with tourist all the time but there is a reason why so many choose to come here. If you get there early definitely get breakfast at the Dutch Eating Place (open tuesday-saturday). Dutch Eating Place is the perfect place for a simple good breakfast- my favorites are the omelets and pancakes. DiNics is a must for their roast pork sandwiches, the lines are worth it. And if you are local or new to the area, this is the best place to get your fresh meats and produce. Iovine Brothers has the freshest and cheapest produce around.
This place is the best. Whatever you're in the mood for you'll find it.  Been coming here for years. If you can't get it here, you can't get it

It's like Disney World for your mouth. I am so, so upset that I didn't have time to really explore the place properly, but what I did try was fantastic. Beck's Cajun Cafe had delicious gumbo- if you had ever told me I could get decent Cajun food from a stall in PA I would have called you a filthy liar. I don't even like beef jerky but the fresh jerky made by....whoever makes it here, was actually good. Regrettably I didn't have half an hour to wait on line for a pulled pork sandwich :(  The fresh produce, the meat, the baked goods...I'm going to have to come back here at some point and just fill my friends trunk full of goodies. It's a shame we don't have anything like this in NY, I think what comes closest is Chelsea Market and that's a laughable comparison. I'd KILL to have this place in my backyard.
SO good!! the dumplings are delicious and the chicken pot pie noodles are amazing. Salad was also really tasty!! You can't go wrong with any flavor of dumpling (:

I made a beeline for L. Halteman Family (the Amish fresh meat counter) for a selection of their turkey sausages and smoked maple turkey bacon. Afterwards, I had to make a pit stop at the crowded amish bakery stand in the back of the terminal, for a slice of their lemon pound cake. With so many delectable selections, it is always a tough call to make.
Redding Terminal is the largest market with the most varieties that I have seen in the U.S. They have something for everyone and I promise that you will leave very satisfied.

Best market I have been to in my US travels.

It was like holy food heaven when I walked in.

Reading can be hard to navigate so make sure you look at the map so you do not get lost.

Very very crowded. So be ready to bump your way through to where you want to go.

Remember cash is almost a must when you go to any market!

Great for food and groceries! Advice, go to Chinatown for souvenirs.

RTM is the kind of place that makes you wish you had an infinite stomach so you could eat all the things. 

All the things to eat:
DiNic's roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe. This is the true Philly sandwich.
Hershel's brisket sandwich. 
The Fair Food Farmstand has amazing local products, like heirloom apples and ethically raised meat.
Termini Brothers for your Italian sweet tooth. 
Bassets for ice cream.

We have been to The Industry a few times for happy hour, dinner and quizzo, but today we tried their brunch menu for the first time and it is definitely my favorite. Portion sizes are moderate and easy to finish. The meats (sausage, scrapple, etc.) are made fresh weekly and made a huge difference. The drink menu was awesome too! I always loved the staff, atmosphere and vibe at The Industry but their brunch menu made them finally stand out!
Came back and pounded a Secret Girl raspberry cocktail in 10 minutes so that we could make a movie on time.  The bartender told me he liked my style.  Yep, this place is still good in my book.

Pretty good new addition to the university dining rotation but the servings are stingy and they don't give you enough quinoa or vegetables. The healthiness is much appreciated though and this is reliably healthy because it is essentially steamed vegetables and that's it!
When i came here in June "13", this was like a food paradise. All kinds of foods here with crowds of people.

I miss this place, since we moved to San Francisco 8 years ago.
Why did law school have to end?
My husb and I used to go here every weekend for lunch.
Miss the nasty crowds of Philly, SEPTA, the cheesesteaks, the Eagles.

Fantastic spot similar to the Pike Place Market in Seattle!

Inside you'll find lots of hot food eateries for breakfast or lunch. A huge section was closed today because it's Sunday, and there are tons of Amish-run businesses.

There is a creperie (we went to Profi's), Keven Parker's famous fried chicken soul food joint, chocolatiers, bakeries (we went to Metropolitan) and tons of places to get super fresh seafood including sushi grade tuna, Scottish salmon, the biggest shrimp ever, crawfish, clams, oysters, etc., freshly made sausage, a cheese vendor, ice cream vendor, fun jewelry vendors.

There aren't lots of farmer vendors inside but there's a grocer there that has fresh veggies and fruits.

It's directly across from the Philadelphia Convention Center, so next time a conference brings you to town, you can come here daily for lunch and get something different each time.

Great place to take my friend visiting from out of town. Seating can be tough when packed but its all a part of the experience. I am hooked on millers twist soft pretzels and dienner's rottiserie chicken is amazing!!

This place is a double whammy for me. I'm a huge foodie and I'm into trains. I could have eaten myself into bankruptcy and a coma here. The historical tidbits on the wall were interesting for my train nerd side, but the food...OMG.

I agree with the recent reviewer who wishes this place were in New York - then I could frequent it more often. It really reminds me of the exhibition buildings at the Big E (the New England equivalent of a State Fair) with all the delicious food.

Wander, try everything. Don't eat yourself into a food coma!

Pick the filling of your choice, stuff into a wonton wrapper, and deep fry it. Yes! That's basically what it was. It is a smart concept but nothing special and out of this world. It was worth trying but again, it did not "WOW" me. If you are craving deep fried wonton, this may replenish your craving. If not, save yourself $7 for 5 deep fried wontons.

Overall, great customer service and individuals. Also, nice space and vibe.
Love it here! Sensory overload, some of the best sights, sounds, and flavors the city has to offer.

I already had an excellent experience for post-Caffe Valentino drinks on Sunday (Get the Ghost of Mary!) and decided to come back for Burgers & Bubbles with a girlfriend last night.

A solid choice.

$1.50 Highlifes and awesome food. The place was also still poppin at 1 AM which is rare for a weeknight. My bill only came to about $39 with a burger and atleast 10 drinks (beer & cocktails). Awesome service once again. Thinking of becoming a regular even if it is kind of a hipster spot.

Prices are higher then normal but, center of Philly. Convenience is the factor here all these places in one spot. Every place is pretty solid, it's a great choice if your with a bunch of people who want different stuff. Touristy, yes... But in a good way.

I always end up planning trip itineraries around food and alcohol. I recently paid my first visit to Philadelphia and we were looking for a light breakfast so my husband suggested stopping by the Reading Terminal Market. Boy am I so glad that we did. I would be in absolute heaven if we had a place like this at home. This market has literally everything to offer. You can eat Mexican, American, Indian, Chinese, Oysters, Thai, etc.. etc.. etc... There's the oldest ice creamery in the country, the best coffee I've ever sipped on and some Amish donuts that will change the way you think about donuts! We got crepes, we shopped for fresh produce, we visited with local artists, we browsed an herbiary. Seriously, you can't go to Philly without visiting this place!

I really enjoyed this terminal market! It was one of the most amazing experiences ever. I got to witness the Amish community and different foods from other cultures. I had my first homemade pecan sticky bun from the Amish shop, Beilers and had a roasted pork sandwich from Tommy Dinics! They have the best slow roasted pork meat I've ever had! Soo juicy and tender. Overall the market was great! Lots of food to try. I just wish the seating was wider and better
