What a wonderful and fabulous place. They have everything you could possibly want to eat. From soup to nuts. Every best of in Philadelphia is in this place. You will simply love it. You can even walk out with flowers and food to go.

Love, love, love going here! Sooooooooooooooooooo many choices of soooooooooooooooooooooo many food places! From soup to nuts, to the Best Gyros, to cookies! The Amish Bakery is to-die-for! Wouldn't miss stopping at Reading Terminal when I'm in the area!

This place is food heaven. If you love cooking and food, this place is the place to be. You can buy anything to cook for dinner here. I love, love, love the Amish Pretzel place (i can never say no to the jalapeño stuffed hot dog pretzels). You MUST try the following: Louisiana cajun place (crocodile gumbo), 45th street cookies (OMG macadamia nuts with white chocolate), sang kee (wonton duck noodle soup), the fried chicken place (can't remember the name), DiNics roast pork sandwich (sometimes 30 min to 1 hr+ line-- make sure you order it with sharp provolone, long hots and broccoli rabe), and Hershel's Farm (pastrami sandwich). ALL deliciousssssssss. 

I also love buying fresh groceries and meats here.

I love this place.  So much incredible food it is hard to choose what/where to eat. This visit I decided on a Turkey Special at Original Turkey. It was outrageous.  Dessert at Terminis.  It does, understandably, get crowded.

There are some excellent choices here at Reading Terminal Market-- but be wise as to which place you decide to eat at. Some eateries are just sloppy fast good on the go, and others are good eats. Check out the plates around you-- there are so many choices!
Some good shops, some mediocre.  One of the things you must see when you are in downtown Philadelphia.
Great place for produce!  Awesome prices in center city.  I live near city hall so i somt have many places to get healthy food.  I go to while foods for rest of my groceries and Moma organic
The cannoli was wonderful!!! The Easter treats, breads, and pastries looked phenomenal. Very friendly staff working at this location.....

Awesome atmosphere. Crazy ton of food options for lunch or breakfast or treats to take home. Not horribly priced at all for being such a tourist spot. Bring cash! Some places to eat are cash only; not all, but some. Definitely a must go to spot while in Philly!

Great atmosphere and really good drinks...the food was ok nothing to write home about.  With so many bars in this city with great food I most likely wouldn't come back here to eat.  Service was good and efficient

We live in Philly and get produce from Iovine Bros. every weekend.  The market is always crowded, but you can't beat the prices and variety.  Overall this is a really fun Philly spot - if you're visiting even for a few hours, it's worth checking out.

I went to the market for the second time. There are lots of places to eat and purchase fresh fruit and produce. It is crowded especially during the holiday seasons. overall, I like reading terminal market and will come back when I back to philly.
Aside from the smell of the street outside its a great place to go. Prices are quite high in some spots and fair in others. Can not really go wrong here place is a gem.
So many awesome stands in here. A great salad place, a great produce place, cheesteaks, beeswax, juice bars, wine, something for everyone.

Must check out when in Philadelphia!! There are so many food options throughout the whole place that you don't know what to choose. Definitely make a point to walk around and look at everything. There's great places for fresh seafood, cheese, sweets, donuts, and even coffee. There are maps so it will be easy to find what you need. There are several sitting areas to enjoy after picking up your food.

This place is great for a sandwich and a milkshake. The sandwiches, especially the "skinny" sandwiches, are great. The hot peppers are better than most places and the store is not over priced like a lot of nicer fast food places. Try the mushroom melt... it's fabulous!

This is a must stop on any trip to Philly. More food options than you can eat. We chose DiNic's. We chose wisely. So good. 

It's almost overwhelming how many options there are. We had an awesome cannoli as well. There was a huge line for donuts which we opted not to get in. But I kind of regret. Something for everyone.

This is the coolest place in philly! (food wise). You can find anything here! From the awesome jams that the dutch community sells to the delicious pastries! 
My fave place to eat a philly cheesesteak is at Rick's. (hence the profile pic). I got the phill steak with pepperjack cheese, onions, mushrooms. It was SO delicious. We were even able to go behind the grill and cook some up! The price range is fair, awesome place!
I've eaten at the Flying Monkey, it has sweets like pistachio cupcakes to delicious brownies. this is a must! 

The place itself is amazing, there are so many cultures and it's constantly busy that it's just awesome. You have to go! Bring cash!

This made me extremely jealous not to have a market like this in Salt Lake City. Reading Terminal Market to me is the equivalent of the Boqueria in Barcelona. Fantastic market with top notch, down to earth local eats.

RTM is awesome when you are looking for unique bits to eat and even specialized ingredients. The only downfall is it can be quite pricey. For instance Iovine's Grocery carries many fresh produce items like the Italian Market, but can be 3X more expensive. The other downfall is that it is a huge tourist attraction, so if you are a local avoid the weekends and opt for a mid week shopping trip.

I have been to the Reading Terminal Market once and it was chaotic. I am not a fan of places like that. The food was good though. One of my co-workers has a 2nd job near there and he does occasionally buy me excellent cannolis. That I would highly recommend if you like that type of stuff!

Liberty Bell Diner is my favorite place to go for breakfast, lunch or dinner and is open 24 hours. Mostly I go there for lunch and dinner and everything on the menu is delicious. There's early bird specials, businessman's special, and special menu for seniors, all at a great price. There's no alcohol served, like some other restaurants but you won't need to drink when you come here. I like how you feel like family and when you hear "Everyone, may I have your attention, someone's having a Birthday so let's sing "Happy Birthday"...how nice that they make you feel special like that. Such nice people and the food is great especially for the price. I'll tell you what I like, first, it's the chicken parm which covers the whole plate (delish). Also, the chicken and beef pot pie is yummy. I keep getting the shrimp scampi over white rice....out of this world delish.
They say they close at midnight on weekdays but they denied us entry at 11:45. Pet peeve. Don't misrepresent your hours. If you don't serve until the stated time, you aren't open until that time.

I finally came here for the first time with my boyfriend the other day. I've heard so much about this place, so we were excited to check it out. We got a parking spot right outside of one of the entrances, so we paid $2 for an hour. I saw that you can also get your parking ticket from one of the garages validated to $4 for two hours, if you can't find street parking. It was a Monday afternoon, so it wasn't too busy. An hour was enough for us to roam around the market, get Tommy Dinic's, Hope's Cookies, and some fruit and produce to take home. The market is pretty much like any other market you would go to. You have your various seafood places, some Italian pasta spots, sandwich places, desserts, a few jam/sauce places, and fruit/produce. There is also a couple Asian food spots in there, including Sang Kee's (from Chinatown & UCity), which I found surprising. That's smart of them to have a spot in this popular American market. Reading Terminal is nice, but nothing really special compared to other markets I've been to around the world. I guess it gets all the good reviews because this is pretty much the only big market in Philly.
Crazy environment with crazy good finds. Worth the chaos.

Amazing market, wish I lived near something like this.  So many options for food!  Great seafood options including some of the biggest shrimp I've ever seen.  Awesome meat and cheese shops.  Plenty of already made take home options.  And a doughnut shop that I've never been to, but must be awesome from looking at the line.  Highly recommended, but be ready for touristy crowd and long lines for certain items.

When I planned my weekend trip to Philly, I knew I had to go somewhere that was going to satisfy my foodie soul. I did some researching and came across this place. After reading reviews, I knew I just HAD to visit and laid out a list of all of the shops I was going to stop at. We came by on a Friday afternoon, around 1:00 pm and it was PACKED. It was insanely crowded. It was loud, crazy, busy, crowded and frankly, quite overwhelming. My boyfriend hated it- it was just so busy. And there wasn't a method to the madness, you just kind of had to walk into the crowd and try to figure out where to go from there. The complete and utter madness of the joint is why I deducted a star. I knew ahead of time that if you spent over $10 in the market and you saved your receipts, you could get parking for $4. Pretty awesome deal!

Here are the vendors that I purchased items from:

Termini Bros- Their cannolis are to die for. This is the second time that I've had them in my lifetime and I've never been able to find cannolis that I like better than these. What a delight. I HIGHLY recommend stopping here. 

Miller's Twist- After reading countless reviews raving about their pretzels with honey mustard- I had to try some. I am honestly not a big pretzel person (I know.. I'm a crazy person). I never order them at restaurants, never buy them for my house.. maybe it has something to do with the fact that I used to work at a german restaurant and ate them a lot there.. I don't know. Even though I don't love pretzels, I just HAD to try these ones after reading all of the reviews. WOW. They were literally, unbelievable. So tasty, so different, so fresh.. the best pretzel I have ever had. The honey mustard was so good and was the perfect pairing with the pretzel. I was blown away. 

Fair Food Farmstand- When I came across this adorable farm stand in the midst of the insanely busy reading terminal market, I was super excited. They had fresh & locally grown produce among other local goodies. I went for a Baba's pink lemonade kombucha, which I loved! I never saw that flavor before and it was really tasty and refreshing.

Bassetts Ice Cream-  I heard this place was a must try, so I headed here to try some yummy ice cream after devouring so many savory items at the market. I wanted to try a blackberry cheesecake but when I was informed they were out I went with the classic moose tracks, which is always a good choice. It was super good and hit the spot. 

By George! Pizza- YUM. They had sooo many yummy food items to choose from but I decided to try the eggplant pizza- a slice of it. Red sauce, cheesy with roasted eggplant - yummmm. It hit the spot after a long day of walking around the market.

Herbiary- What an awesome little shop! There were so many things to look at, lots of holistic oils and lotions and herbs among other things. I purchased two "dream balms" , one for me and one for my sister. I love it, it smells wonderful and is very relaxing. 

Overall-- I had a great time. Yes, it was insanely busy.. but for a foodie like me, it was totally worth it.

We LOVE Reading Terminal Market! We shop Iovine Brothers for all of our produce...Giunta's for local, good quality meats...The Head But for spices and coffee...you name it, you can probably get it here!  A fantastic alternative to Big Box Stores!!! A great place four tourists and locals alike.  It's always packed but that's the beauty of it.  A true community vibe. Great for lunch, a snack, or a treat! I hope it's still around for me to take my kids to some day!

I'm from Seattle with Pike Place Market and I must admit that Reading Terminal Market is better (in a big way for food selection and space overall). 

If you are visiting Philly, add this to your "MUST do list".

Try to beat the lunch rush, it is completely jam-packed during lunch hours and opens during business hours on weekdays.
Great place here a good bang for your buck I love getting simple things like lunch meat and Wings/burgers from here !!
Whether its the fresh produce, butcher cut meats, or huge cheese options I always find what I need.

Many restaurants to choose from here! Several chocolate stores which also had sugar free options thankfully. Bakeries with yummy bread and a super market to boot. Wish the hours were longer that's all.

i go here every time i go downtown,i try to avoid lunch hour since that time is immensely crowded and cant sit anywhere,but i like variety of food and other things that make it what it is ,there is actually just one place in the entire market that i dont like that is a bar type atmosphere,my out of town friend wanted to go there ,we sat down and they told us we had to order a drink a piece,i dont drink and they told me i had to leave,so after she created a scene we left,but other than that i do like the market.

I love coming to the Reading Terminal Market because they have a wide variety of food! If you never been here before, it may be overwhelming. Make sure you walk around the entire market so you can get a feel for all the different types of food.
If you want something sweet they have multiple different bakeries you can chose from. If you wanted to get fresh meat and/or fish they have that as well! While you are at the market, you have to get out Dinics! They have an amazing roast pork sandwich, but you have to get there early because they will run out. Another on of my favorite places to eat is Beck's. They have multiple different Po Boys to chose from, but you have to order the Train wreck. It is amazing and it will satisfy any craving you have. 
If you have not been to the Reading Terminal Market then you have to get there ASAP!

I LOVE Reading Terminal Market, and we look forward to eating here just about every time we head to the city. But my experience there yesterday has jaded me, possibly forever. Tokyo Sushi was a NIGHTMARE that cost me $67 for a few pieces of the WORST sushi I have EVER tasted. DISGUSTING dumplings that the smirking beast behind the counter had the balls to take out of the microwave, splash with a packet of cheap soy and hand to my husband. I looked at them, smelled them, and threw the $10 pieces of crap in the trash. I want to give the market a 5 star review, but I can't until Tokyo Sushi is gone for good. I am mad, real mad. And real stupid for not Yelping it before I ate there...

Man I wish more cities had places like this. Anything you can think of is in this place. From restaurants to grocery stands. I ate at Tommy Dinic's. I had the roast pork, sharp provolone and broccoli de rabe. Damn good sandwich. I need to go back again. Either way, if you're in Philly, make sure you stop here. Give yourself some time too. Make sure you have the munchies...

It was love at first sight once I stepped foot inside. This is heaven to any food lover! There's so many choices that you'll have to keep coming back before you can even try them all. I highly recommend getting portions of your meal (appetizer, entree, drink, dessert, etc) at different stands in order to try as many as you can during one trip. There's also a grocery market on one side!

Every city should have a place like Reading Terminal Market! Talk about one stop shopping. We traveled to Philadelphia on what we call our siblings trip. I have 3 brothers and a sister. They all have a spouse or significant other. We even have some nieces and nephews now. So we take a trip every other year and this trip was to Philly. We absolutely love Reading Terminal Market. If you can't find what you need here, you won't find it anywhere. They have a ton of food places, butchers, bakers and probably candle stick makers. We went here every day whether we were looking to buy fresh fruit or cheese or just to eat. We all tried different foods and different venders.One place that we all agree was our favorite was the homemade pretzels. There is something about a Philadelphia pretzel that is unlike any other pretzel you will ever have. I know if we ever get back to Philadelphia again, I am going here to eat some pretzels.
Oh my god, this was fun!  Pick your flavor, they have it.  If I lived nearby I would never cook.
This review is for Iovine. This is a great place to get fresh and cheap produce. How can you beat 99 cents a pound for organic tomato. They have a dollar a bag section.

A wonderful market right next to the Market East train stop. Lots of wonderful vendors with many types of food. Asian, Middle Eastern, American, Bakeries, Coffee, and lots more. It is always crowded and difficult to find seating, but totally worth it. I also enjoy browsing the store-type vendors such as books, spices, and hand-made gifts. I have never went wrong with anything I have bought/eaten here. Yum, yum yum!!

Great and varied selection, but does get pretty crowded .... well pretty much all the time from 11-3pm. If you can look past the crowds (especially doe eyed tourists) you can find basically anything and everything you could want for breakfast, lunch or dinner.

I absolutely love this place. 

I've tried soul foods, cheesesteak sandwiches, and more and they were all delicious!

It's not super clean, it's always very busy, and people aren't too friendly but I think that's what gives character to this spot.  And I'm okay with it. Lol

Btw...don't forget to have one of the merchant validate your parking ticket if you park across the market. It's $10 off (more money to buy foods with...haha!)
Really great place to get food.  My favorite is the Amish doughnut place and the Roast pork sandwich with sharp provolone with broccoli rabe.  Its the best trust me.
Love it! Soooo many options! We had great turkey sandwiches and gyros! Cookies and donuts are delicious
Great selection of local favorites.  Don't leave without trying DiNics roast pork sandwich. Fuggethabot cheese steaks--this is the real deal in Philly.

Without a doubt one of my favorite places in Philly. Real food, sold by real people. We do most of our weekly grocery shopping  here, which has freed us from nasty mainstream supermarket chains. In addition, it's a terrific breakfast and lunch place; I'm lucky enough to work within walking distance, so I can come several times per week and never have the same thing twice. The vendors are super-friendly and helpful. If you're a foodie, this is your natural home.

What a cool place.  The kind of downtown food and shopping market that I can only dream of Charlotte having.  We're trying with the 7th Street Public Market but, it's not even a fair comparison.

So much to choose from that it literally is mind boggling.  I feel like I would spend part of every weekend here buying seafood, meat, produce, snagging lunch at one of the huge variety of eateries contained within.  I only got to Tommy DiNic's for the roast pork, sharp provolone and broccoli rabe sandwich on this visit and it was awesome but I just wanted to try so many other places.

Nice job Philadelphia!

Reading Terminal overall is awesome.  It's the mecca for all things food.

It does get confusing going around the market but every twist and turn has something for you to check out.
Food out the wazoo! Great prepared food for immediate consumption, or fine meats, vegetables, & ingredients for the most outrageous of recipes.  Fun to eat and stroll, people watching as you go.

I really like the Terminal Market. It's definitely worth a visit when in Philadelphia with so many different places to eat and try, everyone can get what they want. The only cons I can think of are that it can get crowded and loud and finding a seat can, at times, be difficult. I wouldn't ever let the crowd scare me away though, lines move fast and the food is good.

I find that whenever I come into this place I get what I need as well as a bunch of things I didn't know I wanted :). I decided to stop in for lunch and today's pick was MeltKraft (grilled cheese awesomeness), and Iovine produce. 
I do hope one day the Reading Terminal gets a map but I can't think of anyplace else is rather get lost in.

I was told to pay a visit here by my friend as I consider myself a bit of a foodie and this place definitely doesn't disappoint.  There are food choices up the wazoo and they all look good from your deli, to your Indian, to your Chinese, to your vegetarian options even.  There are fresh meat and seafood vendors there as well as a relatively large produce selection from two different vendors as well.  In summary, there is pretty much something for everyone here, whatever your craving or taste may be.

Personally, I was able to pay a visit on two separate days, & if I had a larger stomach, I probably would have tried more of the different food options available, but I was only able to sample Hershey's club sandwich and Bassets double scoop (strawberry & mango) in a waffle cone;  both were delicious.

All in all, I believe that Reading Terminal Market is a must stop for when you're in Philly, just because of the general ambiance as well as the selection of very very delicious looking food available.

Awesome big food market with everything you want. Food court, shopping, desserts, everything from around the world.
Would definitely come back!!!
Homemade cookies. Flowers. Smoothies. Crab cakes. Veggies. Cheeeeeeese. RTM is a great place to spend a Saturday afternoon. I heard they're open on Sundays now too.

I LOVE reading terminal my boyfriend and I go there but have a hard time deciding what we want to eat because we're extremely indecisive and I'm allergic to peanuts and IT IS NOT PEANUT ALLERGY FRIENDLY. Most of the restaurants there use peanut oil in their food and it's quite annoying. I went to this place called Charlie's the service sucked but their food was pretty mediocre

I really wish NOVA had something, anything, even remotely of close to Reading Terminal Market. 

It's so massive and everything looks so yummy it's easy to stand in the middle of the aisle mouth agape trying to figure out where to even start. For me the staples to hit are DiNic's, Flying Monkey Bakery (make sure to take home some whoopie pies!), Bassetts Ice Cream, and Blue Mountain Vineyards Cellars. 

Also worth mentioning is the Golden Fish Market that has every type of fish imaginable and Kauffman's Lancaster County Produce that has every type of jelly known to man.

Oh, come on, guys!! For airport food, this place is the healthiest you can get in Philly!

Personally, I love these guys. I mean, come on--they've got fresh green juice with ginger for me!! They juice it right in front of me, and let me pick the exact contents I want. 

Along with that, they've got ORGANIC greens for salad, and the salads are good-- I use avocado instead of dressing and I'm perfectly content with that. 

Bottom line is that I can get all the green-joy I want in this place, and they deserve a good review!! 

Lastly, the managers are really nice here. Yes, sometimes you get a sourpuss worker, but you get that anywhere. Who wants to work in a "fast food" joint in an airport? Cut 'em some slack, and enjoy your healthy meal! :p I paid $14.02 for my meal, and that's an airport bargain for 'ya.
Readin terminal is a must. The food here is by yet the best. They have a wide varity of food to eat. Every place I tried at this location has been awsome.

Meat was cold, taco shell was cold, bean was cold, and even the lettuce was cold. It was my first time and my last time.  Service was good though.  But the food was to cold and it didn't taste good.  I was craving for taco and didn't want to drive to far to get real authentic taco.  Loco Pez in Fishtown is good or my to go taco truck on G street and Huntingpark ave is good. Love their tamales

Great place to go grocery shopping for produce. Quality is great and it is so much cheaper compared to the grocery/convenience stores around me. The fifteen minute walk from my apartment is definitely worth it. Not to mention they have meats, cheeses, chocolate, coffee. Good place to go for lunch. A lot of the lunch vendors have seating at their counters, plus there are several large areas with tables for eating. There is an ATM on premise, but if I'm not mistaken- all the vendors I've been to accept credit cards. There is always live music outdoors. The only drawback is that is it very crowded. I've definitely seen field trips come through. It is significantly less crowded right before it closes, but by this time a lot of the vendors have closed, so you just have to know that going in. Great place to go for those that have never been to a large market before.

Wow everyone gave this such great ratings. I thought it was a bt dirty and smelly and whatever you need you can get from better places all around the city.

There were homeless people with coffee wandering around, and some of the food I wouldn't trust. The one reason you should go: Beiler's Bakery (Amish baked goods).
The business. Go here, eat everything. Diener's BBQ, Dinic's, and Hershel's deli. It's a gastronomic wonderland. Don't forget La Divisa meats for the best quality beef, lamb, and pork!

There are so many different little vendors! Don't go unless you have an hour to walk around and see everyone! Chocolate shops with amazing truffles and delights, hot fresh Thai food, 20 types of jerky, head cheese, scrapple, ice cream, and hundreds of cheeses. It's a foodies paradise. The only sad thing is that you are limited by the size of your stomach!  :)

An overwhelming place for an indecisive person but in a good way! So many choices - they have their own streets within the building! It's worth walking around the whole thing to figure out what you want. There's a good variety of options. It's also right next to the Marriott Philadelphia Downtown.

Only con is that they're only open during the day.

The lioness and I love this place.  If we ever moved to Philly I would recommend living in this market.  You just need to fabricate a bed somewhere and use the public restrooms for showering.  This place has everything you can ever dream of.  It was so amazing we ate here two days in a row.  I hate repeating places to eat while on vacation but this place had so many things to try.  I wish the Ferry Building in SF could be as cool as this place.

One of the best places on earth.  Tons of variety and choices.  From take home groceries and prepared foods to fruits and veggies this place has it all.  Make sure you have cash before you arrive.  Most places are cash only.  And parking can be a bit tough.

I have had nearly everything on this menu. For casual dining, this place is very good. I love the steak tartare and the Thai chicken salad. Their kitchen is open until 1AM, which makes them a great late night option. Service is quick and friendly also!

The staff is good and the food is good like that of any Chipotle.  I gave it 2 stars only because I've been here twice now and each time the line has been ridiculous.  Maybe that's a good thing bc it means people like the place but it's not worth the wait for me.

Reading Terminal Market is a dream come true for me (and was a nightmare for my wife). 

I like options, and RTM had plenty. I like places that specialize in things. RTM had places that specialized in chocolates, ice cream, wine, pickles, and jerky. I like unhealthy food. RTM had virtually anything you can think of.

My wife doesn't like crowds. RTM has them. My wife doesn't like cramped quarters. RTM is as cramped as can be. My wife didn't like the giant cockroach she saw scurrying on the floor at one of the produce vendors.

Well, I guess you can't fault her for that.

What a great spot. I'd come back here in a minute! The sights sounds and smells are all fantastic. This is everything amazing about Philadelphia under one roof. This was on our list of things to do in Philly but it should have been first on the list!

Great experience for Incredible food options.  Very busy and you may have to stand to eat, but the selection of food is well worth it.  Pricing varies by each venue, but the prices overall seemed very reasonable for the amount of food that you got.

I was in Philly for the day and got hungry so naturally I looked for whatever was closest and sounded good. This brought me to this place and I was very excited to that I came as soon as I walked into the place. The food was amazing and the staff was really good. They have a pretty good selection of both food and spirits, but since I had to drive later decided against the latter. Great place though.

Philly is worth one whole point higher in a 1-10 scale because if this fantastic destination. No matter your tastes there is something for everyone that will exceed their expectations. 

This is probably the number one destination for anyone visiting the city. This type of gathering of independent businesses (no chains) is a model for all cities and towns to emulate. 

Nothing exceptional comes from a chain restaurant.

Oh goodness, where do I start?

You won't find anything like this. Not in New York, Boston, or anywhere else for that matter. Every venue has something special to offer. No two are alike. 

I forget the name, but you have to try the ice cream. I think I saw on the Travel Channel that the place is the only venue that still exists from the start of the market yearssss ago.
I go to the place when I'm in the city. Great food , comfortable to get around. Not to busy. The BBQ is to die for !!
We shared one of the best pastrami Reuben sandwiches we have ever had.  Then, we picked up a Pineapple Upside Down pound cake, which we took home; it was amazingly good.
If someone from out of town asks you where they should visit during their time in Philly, this place should be #1 on your list. Start here.

This is a food paradise, as being a life long San Franciscan all my life, I find this haven is hard to beat! The minute I walk in, I was shock n' awe by the area and variety of food emporium this is. 

Tourist and locals mingle among the market place and there is something for everybody. You will not walk away hungry and just for this one day....Forget the diet! Better yet, get some fresh fruit & produce, wolfs and lambs can walk together here.

Sometimes you just need a breather to get out of the hospital and take a walk. That's where Potbelly's comes in. 

Get The Wreck, which is their version of an Italian hoagie. Talking with hot peppers and pickles and some root beer and you have a happy place.

Just resist the urge to hip check the guy standing in line taking your order on the tablet. He is only doing his job (jeez, I hope he worked there).
Lots of great selection here!  Easy to get just about any type of food, including fantastic deserts. I recommend a visit here for anyone visiting Philadelphia.

I know there is EVIL in this world because this place is too close to my job!!  I want to eat breakfast and lunch here -DAILY - luckily have restraint - so I try to keep my visits to once a week.  I LOVE the choices that are offered here when I eat lunch or I shop for items for home cooking.  When I have visitors from out of town, I bring them here to sample the Amish Cuisine and all the other speciality restaurants.  At times choices can prove to be pricey, but if you are a Yelper - you should know which places have the best deals...Some of my Fav Place are Dieners Chicken (reviewed), Smucker's, Beck's NOLA Cuisine (reviewed), Godshall's & Martins Markets, Hunger Burger (reviewed), Nick's Roast Beef and I few others that names don't come to mind. 

Do your best to avoid during BIG conventions, but if you are here during a convention and want to check it out - do us locals a favor - don't stand in the middle of the aisle - try to be kind and enjoy the EXPERIENCE!!

I love Reading Terminal Market. It has such a wonderful sampling of so many different types of fresh foods and restaurants. The market is located in an area where parking is very difficult. If I want to catch a lunch with a business colleague, I'll just take an Uber down there.

Reading Terminal Market is a busy hub of activity; a quirky biosphere of tourists, locals and vendors buying, sighing [at the long lines] and plying.  While I appreciate the history, tenacity and in some cases brusque moxie of the RTM and its denizens, my first visit became a Dickensian experience as I sifted through retail debris to find hidden gems.  

The building retains remnants of bygone eras; bits of stone and architectural features hinting at the days of steam engines, horse-drawn carts, and the hubris of the 1920's.  It also reflects elements of social decay and the unfiltered byproducts of congested city living; patches of graffiti, cardboard condo residents (some verbally aggressive) and filth. 

Inside you are met by a cacophony of sounds, colors, and aromas.  Determined to "carpe diem" the hell outta the place, my SO and I forged-ahead through the crush of people and visited almost every shop, stall and huckster.  Some of the highlights:

- Iovine Brothers Produce.  Decent selection, many fresh options, reasonable prices and among other things, cold-pressed juice.  Had I been putting together a meal, much of my shopping could have been done here.

- Fair Food Farmstand.  A small but quality selection of organic and/or local edibles. Stinging nettles and kombucha both found a place in my shopping bag.

- Paprika Letterpress + Design.  A delightful proprietress using a century old printing press to create unique paper products for every occasion.  From modern to vintage, joyous to satirical, there is something to grab your attention. 

- Market Blooms.  Little can beat the beauty of fresh flowers.  Nature is the ultimate artist.

- Beiler's Donuts.  Ubiquitous.  Everywhere you turned someone was holding a box of donuts with Beiler's printed boldly on the top.  When we finally found the source there was a line that looped around their space and extended beyond. It looked like it would take an hour to get a donut, so we moved on.  They looked and smelled fantastic.


Final Verdict:  Quantity over quality.  Dozens of mediocre shops selling pedestrian food, blah produce and uninspired crafts. Enough sugar and bad-coffee to leave the cities population sleepless for weeks.  However there are some business worth visiting and supporting - just be prepared to wait.

Stone cold classic. Whether you're from Philadelphia or are just here on a short visit, you've got to pick up something to eat at Reading Terminal. Just strolling through it is a feast for the eyes and nose. Coffee, tea, books, fresh produce, fresh-baked breads, goods from Amish farms, cut flowers, herbal remedies ... it's all here!

YESSSSSSSS!! So believe it or not... i've lived in Philly for 20 years and i've never been here until 2 weeks ago LOL. it has EVERYTHING you can imagine. it gets crowded, but who cares! it's worth it. the food i've tried here is amazing and you won't be let down. it's a must if you're ever in the Philly area.

Every time I come here I am always torn & not 100% decided. Obviously there's several offerings and choices (sometimes the atmosphere after dark is a little bit questionable i.e., sketchy) overall though, I'm pleased the food is good the service is good great place to walk around and check things out! Especially during the daylight hours and when the weathers nice! I will definitely be coming back, a solid 4.25 stars!

We have been to markets in Morocco, Italy, Tunisia,
France, England, I could go on...RTM can compare
favorably with all of them.  It is very much like the 
markets in Italy in look and feel.  Huge variety of
edibles and tchochkes, something for every taste.
Yes, Tom of Glenside, if one wants vegan, the 
offerings are somewhat limited.  Check out Tootsie's
at the back, lots of veg there.  Best:  the kale salad
with citrus dressing and cranberries.
I stopped in for some quick eats on my weekend trip.  If you haven't been there, you should go. Its' like a open market of restaurants. They have everything.
my favorite place in Philadelphia.  I visit at least once a week to do my grocery shopping.

Although it can get crowded, it's a good one-stop grocery shopping for me.  I much rather support these vendors than the big corps.  If you're going on the weekend, just make sure to get there early for the best picks, plus it isn't as crowded.  The lot across the street is a good place to park, just make sure you get your ticket validated by one of the vendors.

Can I give six stars? Ten? Two thumbs-up, five stars, and whatever other maxed-out rating system is what this place gets!

This is food Heaven, and no there's no Peter at the gate to ask you questions. Fresh produce, locally sourced honey and jams, bakeries, ice cream shops, fresh seafood stands (w/ amazing prices btw), a bar, awesome food stands (DiNic's!), people watching...AHHHH, I wish this was in Denver. I don't anticipate moving to Philly anytime soon, but I would live there just for this place.

If you live nearby and don't go here, shame on you. If you're in town visiting, come here at least once. Ugh...writing this review makes me sad that I can't go there right now. Every major city in America should have something just like this.

LOVE the Terminal!! Use to work across the street so was there all the time. Worst thing to deal with is tourists who stand in the middle of the isle trying to figure out where they're going, while us working stiffs are trying to get in & out for lunch. The Metropolitan Bakery has the most fabulous sour cherry and sea salt cookie EVER!!! Lovine Produce & Johnathan's Grocer are always a stop and the Little Thai Market is always worth the wait. The Salmon house specialty is spectacular. With live 70+ vendors there is always something for everyone. Sure miss it!!

I love this place, from Iovine Bros Market (great produce and vegetables at excellent prices) to Martin's Meat (great quality, selection and prices) to all the great food vendors (Sandwiches!) and of course the real, honest to goodness Amish!

This is a MUST when visiting Philadelphia! It is a little chaotic, noisy and crowded but you just have to deal with it. The food is fantastic! I've only eaten one thing that I haven't fully enjoyed and I've tried a lot of stuff! This is seriously my favorite place in Philadelphia besides Iim's for a cheesesteak!
A must visit while in Philly! An excellent choice to make sure everyone in your party is happy with Breakfast or Lunch choices... plus you'll find plenty of great food to take home with you!

We stopped here for breakfast.  There were so many places that I forgot where we ate.  We got some breakfast sandwiches and breakfast sides that were great.  I have never seen so many vendors in one place.  It was truly a unique experience.

First impressions really go a long way, and our welcome here last night left about as bad a taste as their overpriced dumplings. Although the range of flavors was diverse and fun, their prices are too steep for something you can get better in a frozen food aisle of ShopRite. Save your time and money by just ordering dumplings from some generic Chinese bodega. The service was lifeless, the atmosphere was hardly even worth the idea of late night drunk food, and by the time you got enough to be satisfied, you'll probably have to take out a loan from your local bank.

This market is awesome! They offer a wide variety of food for such a small establishment. My only complaints are the prices, which can be understandable for some of the places depending on what they offer, and the lack of air conditioning. If you go to this place during their peak hours, aka weekends, it gets hot and packed very easily. My personal favorites are Martin's Specialty Sausages and Famous 4th St Cookie Co.

If you're looking for options, then you've come to the right place. You will find everything from Philly Cheesesteaks to fresh shucked oysters at this place!  It does get quite busy at lunch time thus making it difficult to find a table especially if you're with a group. But whatever you're craving, you're bound to find it here. There is even an Amish bakery with fresh baked cinnamon rolls!  Other vendors include candles and linen.

I like coming here because there's an eclectic vibe to it and there's a lot of things to buy here. Lots of flowers, candies, food, etc. On the other hand, it is very touristy and very crowded. Difficult to get seats in here if you want to eat here, and it's extremely hectic and loud. However if you're new to the area or just stopping by, I highly recommend coming here at least once to check it out and get something to eat! There's a great place in here that serves delicious crepes. Check them out.
Friendly, knowledgeable staff that shared current promotions and gave me a solid rundown of the whole concept, which is pretty different from a lot of restaurants and takeout places.
Easily one of the best pizza joints in Philly, located on a stretch of Girard that desperately needed a quality place to grab a slice on the go. Highly recommended!

LOVE this place! Any time we're in Philadelphia, this is a MUST-DO thanks to the sheer number of food options available. You could spend an entire day getting lost in here....make sure you go when you're not on a time constraint so you can really take in everything there is to see, experience and eat here!

Cons: It's ALWAYS jam packed and crowded, so stay away if you're claustrophobic at all.

Love this place. Really quick and amazingly good. When I discovered MK, I went back for lunch for the next 4 days in a row. Super friendly staff. Great addition to the neighborhood. My fave is the paneer masala roll.

I can attest to the fact that this place serves quite good rolls. Don't think twice if you are in mood for Indian style rolls. Out of Paneer, Aloo, Aloo-Paneer and Mix-Veggie rolls, I liked Mix-Veggie the best. Their dips aren't any good. I felt that their Veg Biryani was good but nothing special (caveat: I had Biryani for to-go and ate it the next day)

Hands down the best place to eat breakfast or lunch in Philadelphia. The place has so many options for almost any palette, but it gets crowded around lunch time so if you can, try going mid-afternoon to avoid waiting in lines.

I think that everybody should visit this place. Great food, beer, etc.Great prices too.
I am always amazed when I visit this place. Additionally there are tons of other places to visit nearby such as Chinatown. If visiting from out of town, there is a huge Marriott across the street from the market.

What's there not to love about Reading Terminal Market?! It's essentially got everything anyone expects at a market - ice cream shop, cheese vendor, deli stands, and even one that's owned by an Amish group (correct me if I'm wrong...sorry!). So many different selections there, and it's always such a hard decision coming here with a limited budget. 

Even better, Chinatown is essentially right next doors. Go for a nice bubble tea or authentic Szechuan cuisine just one block down! Plus, Dim Sum Garden always has amazing food! The Gallery is right by the market, too; so if you're not in the mood for Chinese Food, maybe you're in the mood to do some shopping. 

I'm not rating it 5 stars for two reasons: Reading Terminal Market is great, but unfortunately, being in the center of the city, it is a bit small. I hope one day, the Market will go through an underground renovation and add a basement! Also, I wish there were an easy exit/entrance by 11th street. I've discovered a sketchy exit onto Arch/11th, but it's used for trucks to load and unload. Regardless, it saves me time and effort, and lets me zoom through the market whenever I make a trip to Chinatown!

I like that I had a place to relieve myself whilst en route to the shores of New Jersey, but really, the toilets at this joint are pretty disgusting.  Reminded me of public toilets in Scotland.  A veritable BOG.

Lots of fresh food and unique ingredients at an easy convenient place! 
Try the cannolis and fresh jam!

I came here on opening day so my review will be based on that.

I ordered the tomato burger, no meat for those unaware of the offering.
It was a thick slice of tomato, some sprouts and a salty mayonnaise sauce. It wasn't worth 6$ especially since it didn't fill me up and because the picture at the restaurant shows the same burger with more toppings on it which the restaurant did not say were included. I want to like this place and i plan on returning again to give it a second try.

This place definitely feels like a souped up version of Spice End. The ambiance is very lively and the menu options are pretty extensive. On my quest to find a place to get after-hours chicken and rice, this place comes to the top of my list. The quality of the chicken is amazing: juicy and very well-seasoned. You can pour on as much white and hot sauce as needed. The mango lassi is so thick and delicious; probably some of the best that I have had here in Philly.

The Reading Terminal is great! They have everything you could ask for, and then some! Many grocery/produce options, and eating places. They definitely have something for everyone including Asian food, desserts, Mediterranean food, pizza, etc. You name it, and they got it! I always look forward to coming to the terminal each time I'm in Philly.

I got a plain slice today. It was $5 with tax but was almost the size of 2 slices so I feel that I got my money's worth. It tasted good and I'll be back to try other flavors. Bonus: the guys working there called me miss instead of ma'am

I have lived in Philly my whole life and I regret never going here sooner. There's so much going on, so many stores, and it feels like a little town that's filled with so much life. I'd recommend it very much to those new and old to Philly because being there is a real experience. My only warning is if you have high anxiety like me just be forewarned it can be very overwhelming.

Wow! Such variety and atmosphere. Good prices, good quality.

It would rival Melbourne's Queen Vic Market except that there's no place for entertainment or dedicated organic section or wine tastings. And it's all indoors, but given the climate, you couldn't have it otherwise

Whether you're a local or a tourist, great place to saunter and sample local fare.
great selection of food here. wish i had more time to eat!
I leave in Southwest Philly and drive all the way over here just for this place; it's that good.

Random find for a Saturday mid afternoon brunch / lunch before heading to the movies on Columbus drive.. Convenient location! Tons of parking.. $5 dollar mimosas when we went.. Really interesting cocktails on the menu and most of all great food!!! We tried 3 different brunch items and they were all good.. The donuts were great too! Fried tomato eggs Benedict was my fav.. Defi recommend if find your self in south philly area..
Sensory Overload! You can pretty much find anything you could need here.... Just be aware that there is always going to be a crowd.
Perfect place for a quick grab of tasty Indian food! No complaints, all menu items are tasty. Pricing is nominal. Paneer Masala Wrap is the best dish.
Enjoyed the atmosphere, variety of vendors, selection of eateries, etc. Friendly place to visit and get a taste of the diverse culinary influences in Philly. Wish I had more time to explore.

A Philadelphia institution essential to visit for anyone who enjoys food! Not much you can't find under this roof. An ideal, budget friendly place to bring a family with various tastes or levels of adventurous eating. Avoid on Saturdays and during big conventions if you don't enjoy a bit of elbows and body checking through the aisles as part of your shopping experience. There are some less worth it spots (all "American" style diner, cheesesteaks, the bad choices are, I think, obvious to to pick out) but they are far, far outweighed by the Philly roast pork, po boys, Pakistani kebobs,  pastrami, and middle eastern pastries that abound. Not to mention the cheese counters of various specialities, produce and juice options galore.

You can never go wrong here.  Cheese steaks good.  Cookies good.  Chocolate good.  Fruit good.  Ice cream good.  Amish food good.  Seriously it really doesn't get better than this.  To date no other markets I've been to compare, and I've even been to some out of the country.  Kudos Philly!
This is a must go for every tourist who loves food like me!! Such a huge variety of food. Yummy

Outstanding food and service.  Consistent and delicious had an amazing meal that made my day. My kids love the shakes. We need one in Brooklyn asap! I need one closer to my home. If they delivered i woulf only eat Chic-fil-a. .lol

Just as long as you brace yourself for the price, you're likely to enjoy this place! 

When they were prepping the food, all I could think about as I pulled out my card was, "$11 for that?!", but then when I started eating it, I was far more appeased. I had the kimchi bowl with some protein added - it's a solid amount and rather tasty actually. It's also a great concept - the whole flash steaming vegetables thing. I thought I would never return but lately I've been kinda craving it so thumbs up for the actual food. 

The service is only so-so though. I was kinda confused about how it all worked during my first visit and they weren't very patient with me. And it seemed like they were taking their time doing other things (moving boxes, wiping down counters) while my food was just waiting to get passed down the line. 

Not a bad healthy addition to Houston, but I'd be tentative to give it more stars given my experience!
It's like all 5 continents under one roof- simply amazing!

I went to Philadelphia for a quick work trip, and figuring I wouldn't have time, I didn't do any research in advance. I am SO happy I stumbled upon the Reading Terminal Market.

I only went to the market in the morning during the week and it was not crowded at all. I was able to walk through the aisles, look at menus, talk to the folks who worked there, and easily find a seat to eat at. I can't even imagine what this place is like during the weekend, and honestly, I'm happy not to find out! 

The market is a mix of small restaurant types and market stalls. The produce, fish and meat all seemed very fresh and the place was just clean all around. I found all of the people working there to be very friendly and helpful, but again, I imagine it's not so nice on the weekends. Such an awesome indoor market -- would love something like this for the Boston winters!

The best thing about Philadelphia - I could eat here for a month and still not have tried everything. You can find the best of Philadelphia here - from cheesesteaks to Amish Pretzels (note: The Amish don't come in the beginning of the week though), Chinese food to Perogies. 
Plus side - great food for great prices! Also, lots of produce, flowers, and other speciality food items. 
A must for anyone visiting Philly for the first time!
Way too crowded for me. I wouldn't say I hate crowds but when people are up your ass every time you turn around it's hard to shop. I'll never go back

The Reading Terminal is like no other place you'll experience, not even in New York. While New York does have the Chelsea market, the two places couldn't be more different. The Chelsea market is filled with the pop-up shops, toy business ventures for rich people to throw money at that will charge you $4 for a salty donut. 

The Reading Terminal is cramped - so take your backpack off - and full of worldly delights. Want to go to the Far East? Go to Shanghai Gourmet. Want to go to the Lower East Side in the early 1900s? Go to Hershels - the Reuben and pastrami sandwiches are to die for (and better than Katz in NYC)! Want some donuts made fresh (most likely while you're waiting in hour-long line)? Go to Beilers! Want a godly pork sandwich? Go to DiNics! Once you taste it, you'll never think of pork the same way again. 

Come hungry and be prepared to wait for your food, but I promise you it is well worth the wait.

Food nirvana is the best way to describe this place. Everything from matzo balls to the best grilled cheese sandwiches you'll ever have to fresh produce and seafood and the pot to cook it in.  On Sundays several of the vendors close up shop, so to get the full experience plan for another day.  A couple of hours is good to wander through the market and take everything in. The cheesemaker in the back is beyond belief (Valley Shepherd Creamery?). If you love cheese, this place has your number.  And the sandwiches from Melt Kraft? Absurdly delicious. Dessert can be had at the Flying Monkey Bakery, or a huge, fresh baked cookie from the Philadelphia General Store.  

Come here with an appetite and someone to help carry everything back to the car!
Great variety of food! Even for people w/food allergies. Gluten free, Dairy Free, Egg Free, Nut Free, Soy Free, Vegan, & Vegetarian!
They have everything here. You can't go wrong with all the choices of food. The Salumeria is one of my favorite fooderies but Mezzi, Dinics, Border Springs and Flying Monkey are all great vendors.

I know I'm going to catch some flack for this, but I don't looooove RTM. I much prefer the Italian Market for most produce and meat items. RTM pricing seems a tad higher and much more touristy.  I will say that beef cheeks are nearly impossible to find in the city, and I checked with all the butchers in the Italian Market - one pointed me to RTM! I need to go check it out.
Such a nice variety of food!

a philadelphia staple... 
there is a variety of food from many cultures. the amish come to philly bringing their buttery baked deliciousness! if you are a tourist, THIS is the place to go to try some of the areas little treasures. and if you are a resident, the local markets are pretty reasonably priced. HOWEVER, on the weekends it is super crowded! holidays = super crowded!! so you'll need to be prepared for that.
my favorite lunch is the fried chicken salad from the country diner.

There is no doubt that this is a Philly landmark and it offers something for everyone and is good for hanging out with friends. But, it is overly crowded, taste is mediocre, and prices are high. This place is jack of all trades but master of none.
Got takeout, veggie platter and mango lassie. Was disappointed with both as I found the food bland and too spicy and the drink too thick. Great concept.

A place that needs no reviewing, it has been an integral part of Philadelphia since the city's founding.  

For produce I recommend Iovine's, everything is so fresh and affordable!  Coming here is a true highlight of my week and it makes every meal a little better

Termini has the best cannolis, I like the vanilla with chocolate chips.

Go to Beck's Cajun Cafe if you're really hungry and enjoy the best hoagie you will ever have the "train-wreck po boy" with Andouille Sausage, Steak meat, Salami, Onions, and Cheese!  It's like a cheese-steak for champions!
Fresh meats -Fish and great cooked food....loveeee this place!

It's reading terminal. I've been astounded with all the shops in here on a consistent basis. Of note are Iovine brother's produce and giunta's prime shop. It just doesn't get better than this place. My tip - try to get there during the week. It's packed on the weekend.

Walk in and inhale, daddy's home! This is my favorite market anywhere in the world. People rave about French markets but I live and shop in them every week and I long to be at Reading Market. You can not beat it for variety and freshness whether you are shopping for goodies to cook at home or looking for a bite to eat. This is a foodie's paradise where you can indulge in food from every corner of the world and buy produce from people who are still passionate about what they make and sell.

Whilst chillin in PHL, I yelped myself to this place. I was aimin for Le petit bistro, but couldn't find it (I'm not good w being smart). So to the salad store I went. Had the Asian salad and enjoyed it. Dressing on the side worked as the chicken and other stuff had enough crap on it that it still tasted good. I was happy w the salad and the greens will be good for my poop. Yay!

Awesome market with a lot of good spots for food!  

If you're ever in Philly, you should definitely visit.

I go to the Reading Terminal at least once a week to buy my vegetables and eat lunch. I love the options that it has to offer, and the produce prices at Iovine Brothers are nearly unbeatable. Whatever you need in terms of food, you can probably find it here: imported cheeses, fresh seafood (I'd recommend John Yi Fish Market), spices, produce, meat... you name it. Mostly everything is reasonably priced, too. If you're looking for lunch, you'll find Chinese (Shanghai Gourmet is delicious, especially their Hunan Chicken), Thai, pizza, vegetarian options, hoagies, cheesesteaks... pretty much anything your tastebuds could possibly crave. I love the Reading Terminal!
Recommended by my Indian friend. I came here for paneer roll, but was surprised by Rose lassi, haha!
Are you looking for a one-stop-shop that's packed nuts to butts?  Well, you found the place. Avoid between 11 AM-1 PM or you'll feel like cattle trying to traverse the place.

I just love this market. I'd likely stop in nearly every day if I lived in the area. There hasn't been a single time I've walked in and walked out without buying something from one of the merchants. Yesterday, a lunch at Olympic Gyro followed by some Amish cakes was just a great start to the day.

Plus, there's always interesting characters floating around outside.

Awesome resturant week deal!  GREAT food..compliments to the chef! very unique and wonderful flavors... big array of beer and drinks..awesome/friendly service from the bartender..cool atmosphere/nice vibe.. will def return!

I don't know why non Indian people say this is not authentic Indian food. Kati rolls are something like street food in India and this is pretty authentic Indian food. Obviously this concept is not very popular in the US as most Indian restaurant serve the same old curries and bread, and so most people may not be familiar with Kati rolls. Love the food here, they are open late, there is 1$ discount for order of 2 rolls, what's not to like?!

Foodie heaven.  Really a four and a half, docking 1/2 star coz no alcohol to be found.  Seafood? Beef? Oysters? Froglegs? Pastries gourmet and homemade?  This place has it.  Glorious place.  If you wanna eat organic or vegitarian this place did not forget about you.  Map it out, make a plan coz this place is dizzying.

Four stars only because of its closing time (6pm).  It takes a bit too long to get there unless you really work next door.  The alternative is wading through the weekend crowd.  So even a half hour extra (6:30) would make a huge difference.

Otherwise, it's just perfect.
So much variety. Best thing I've had was a cheesesteak from Carmen's

Things to know about the Reading Terminal: It is REAL, not some food mall or superstore. You may well see the business' owner or kids bagging up your turkey, or making your sandwich, or filleting your fish. You should go expecting to talk to strangers, to the people working the stalls and so on. It's no grab-and-go thing, it's an experience that is part of living and cooking.

It is sometimes really crowded, especially when big events are at the Convention Center, go early or late.  Don't drive if you can help it... bike, or use transit - SEPTA's Market East Station PATCO, and NJT will get you from nearly anywhere to the RTM. Bring your own tote bags or even a backpack! Granny carts can be tough, especially on the weekend. You might stash yours, then return to load it.

When you go, keep track of what merchants you visited... and always seek out new ones... if you don't you can end up not seeing the whole Reading Terminal Market.

Finally, before you go to Whole Foods, or some other mega market, make a shopping list and see how much you can get from this wonderful place... like Barcelona's famous Boqueria, the RTM is a treasure and we are lucky to live near it.

-- Michael McGettigan, director, Trophy Bikes PHL
We had the general wings and the burger (with a fried egg). All the food was good and the service was fantastic. Great people! Brought us a dessert "from Philly with love." Great atmosphere.

Green Leafs is a quick serve soup, salad and sandwich bar located in the Philadelphia airport. Staff seemed a bit distracted and did not provide a friendly welcome. They have a medley of different salads to choose from or to make your own. Ingredients seemed fresh and plentiful. Price points are reasonable given salad weight. There is also a soup and sandwich component to this establishment. The food was OK to slightly lower than OK, hence the MEH. If the service was better, I think it would get to a 3-star rating. Perhaps it is a nice change from the typical burger and fries at the airport. Good luck and enjoy your stay in Philadelphia!!
Always a stop for us when in Philly.   Wide variety of different types of food.  Have some time to spend and enjoy.

Food is typical fare. Had McCafe Mocha and chocolate shake on a warm Sunday which tasted ok. Bad review is for cleanliness of the location, and the bathrooms that were locked (like you would find at a rundown out of the way gas station), dirty and without toilet paper. Unacceptable for a downtown location across from the Convention Center.

Terrible food, very unclean. On Christmas Eve this place being one of the very places open we decided to give it a try. The kati roll was ok. The rice platters were horrible. Took the paneer platter and veg Biryani. Bad taste.. no flavor. Rice laden with cinnamon. To worsen it found strands of hair in both the platters. Ewww. Will never be trying this again.
SO many great vendors here, especially love the Herbiary and Beck's Cajun Cafe.
Variety of food, donuts hyped, I really did not like it that much. Try out the chicken, it's soft and tender.

I went to this market specifically for DiNiC's roast pork sandwich, and it was worth every minute in line. It's fun to walk around the entire market and look at all the vendors, selling everything from fresh produce to meat to baked goods to fresh juice drinks. There's something for everyone and most likely, you'll find 5 things you want so go hungry. My favorites include the roast pork sandwich, whoopie pies from Flying Monkey, and a mocha from Old City Coffee. There's a juice bar that's pretty good too and Bassetts Ice Cream is supposed to be great. Sadly, I have never tried to ice cream because I'm lactose intolerant, but it sure looks good!
Nice place to walk around, great food selection. I thought prices were really good.

This place is a MUST VISIT in Philly!!  In town for two days but would visit daily if i lived locally.  An eatery for every taste, fresh fruits and vegetables for every chef (and experimental chef) and there are cookies. Lots and lots of cookies and pastries and things covered in chocolate ALL OVER THE PLACE.  Not to mention fried things. Lots of fried things.

I'm from NY - so I may be hard to impress when it comes to deli goods.  The corned beef Reuben at Hershel's was AMAZING!!! For 10 bucks - it was well worth it.  Piled high and the corned beef was tender and fell apart like butter when I bit into this perfect sandwich.  The potato salad at .93 was a perfect accompany to this heavenly experience. Grandma's Sunday special was also corned beef - so the bar is high - you do the math.

Oh..the next day we had sushi from the place next door.  Tokyo Sushi Bar. Philadelphia roll and egg rolls.  Fish was fresh but roll was average and egg roll was sopped in oil .   It  seemed kind of overpriced for what we received but the chef was friendly and appreciated our business. 

Famous 4th Street cookies were closing down, so we purchased a few cookies for a dollar a pop.  The sugar cookies were heavenly but my date ate the rest and didn't share feedback..so get your own and you be the judge...

But what is with DiNic's not being manned but seemingly open on the first day, and messy and one loud non-eating patron sitting at the bar stool on the second day? I know they are working on the new location (across from Hershels) but I was really looking forward to their pork sandwich. The lack of interest by employees (who were non-existent or leaning on something) was a complete turn-off. Good luck with that!

Can't wait to go back with a cooler packed in ice ready for goat cheese and pepper sausages from Martin's!

Everything to eat is here! It's fresh and delicious, not necessarily nutritious...mmm, Bieler's donuts.....seriously though, some of the best steaks, burgers, and produce are purchased at this oasis in the city. Literally anything you want to eat can be found here, and at pretty reasonable prices. It's usually packed however, especially during lunch time, and on the weekends. Great spot to bring visitors - very Philly and hustly bustly
Awesome place food from all over and not from a can... mostly Italians and middle eastern great place to find gourmet items not to be missed while in philly

Better than "mmkay!"

Stopped by for lunch with a colleague. Everything was fresh and delicious, with a respectable level of spice! Loved all of it. Plus, the Kati rolls were such a great value at only $5.25!

Will definitely be back.

A must see for anyone visiting or living in Philadelphia. It represents all that is good in America, abundance of fresh food, knowledgeable vendors and a sense that you're at the right place. Bring a hearty appetite.
This place is my second home. I love the fish and fruits aisle. Definitely a place to check out !

Very cool venue, there are a lot of options so there's something for everyone. I got a boneless rib sandwich from the rib stand, and it was DELICIOUS! It comes with a hot or mild bbq sauce (I opted for the hot and stand by my decision) and the sauce definitely adds to the sandwich. I have to say me and my friend liked my sandwich more than the cheesesteak he got, I highly recommend it! 

There are also a large variety of sweets shops, including a chocolatier that is known for onion truffles, and another stall that has chocolate covered bacon! Needless to say it's a must see.

Only thing is a lot of the stalls close early, we arrived at about 3-4 and many were closing. If you intend on trying a lot of different stalls I recommend getting there early. Also, park farther away and walk, your chances of finding parking nearby are slim to none unless you want to pay an arm and a leg.

This is a must visit in Philly -for the sheer versatility of it. Anything and everything you want is here. This is similar to Quincy Market in Boston. Some recommendations are oysters, Rueben (from Hershel's East Side), Gator Gumbo, and fried mac n' cheese (From Beck's Cajun Cafe).

Hard to find seating.
Loved it. Lots and lots of great food! Something for everyone. Make sure you get your parking validated so that it's only $5 for 90 minutes.
Tons of great food. Love the Cajun food stand best gumbo in town and the gator was actually good. If you can't find something there then you never will.

A place where you can eat and shop at the same time. When we were here last weekend, there was a string ensemble playing at the food court area. There are many restaurants that you need to try, so come hungry! Must have the Bassett ice cream! The terminal is located near Chinatown and the City Center where you can walk off your meals after.

I traveled with 7 hungry teenagers here and they were all able to find different food they liked from sushi to burgers to barbeque to southern to Philly cheesesteak, the variety was amazing. There was also a bakery, a chocolatier, florist, tablecloth and blanket boutique, an amazing assortment of booths and stores! Everyone was happy and the historical flavor and melding of people was really fun!
Must visit when in Philly, simple as that! Too many great spots to review, just go and enjoy.

I fell in love with this place in 2000 or 2001, a few years before the movie National Treasure, had a chase scene here.  The Reading Terminal Market was the first place where I learned you didn't need to buy everything from a grocery store.  I ordered amazing meats at the butcher and bought fresh produce.  Over the years, when I worked close by, I frequented this place multiple times a week and there are always great places to eat.  

I've been here for private parties, weddings, and just whenever I can get the chance.  DiNic's is one of my favorite sandwiches in the world, so I spend most of my time there.  I love the Pretzels in the market now too.  So buttery good.  Check this place out if you are in town.  A ton of tourists join locals here, but it's worth it.
Excellent experience for visitors and locals. Be prepared to be overwhelmed by lots of people.

This place is basically an awesome indoor farmers market. You literally have everything you could possibly want in one place. 

It has a very old style feel while also having that edgy vibe that only Philly can give you. They have fresh seafood, sandwiches, Thai food and whatever else you can possible think of. I went to the coffee shop in and sat at a table with my GF, while enjoying the sights of the market and all it had to offer.

This place is pretty awesome for either having a meal in a market atmosphere or simply doing some shopping in a place where you have literally every option you can think of. Definitely will be making it a point to come here more often when I'm in Philly.
not bad for a market type. some good food ,not gourmet but passable!
Mind blowing variety of food! Philly cheese steak! Pastries! Name it! They've got it!

This place was great! Super excited to march around and check it out. Was sad I hit on a day the Amish vendors were not open but otherwise everything looked very tasty. I'm looking forward to going back sometime soon and really diving in.

barely made it in before closing at 6! co-worker and I were in town and this place was highly recommended by others..I love international food markets. too bad it was so early to eat at 5:30. we forced ourselves to eat. the place is huge.

even when i don't really need to buy anything, i absolutely love to come here. i love the wandering, the scents, watching the machinery at the chocolate place, just people watching in general....

when i am here for food, i tend to gravitate toward profi's for savoury crepes, the falafel @ kamal's, spanakopita @ olympic, and golden bowl for noodles of any kind. the husband and offspring dig bassett's like it's going out of style, but i am neither here nor there when it comes to ice cream.

while they wait in line at bassett's, i like to sniff all the flowers at the stand across the walkway. it's a good way to pass the time, even if it does my allergies a disservice.

One of my favorite places in Philly, hands down!

There's almost nothing that I love more than a great farmers market. The Reading Terminal Market has something for everyone. You'll find some of the best food and coffee here and the place is always full of tourist and Philly residents alike.

Some of the best dates I've had in this city started out with a trip to this fabulous place for brunch! I'm in love with the energy and food selection of this place -- there's always something new to explore and I'm never disappointed.
Great place to people watch and get some great food!  It can be a little overwhelming and I found out that a lot of the places close earlier than 6pm but I'm just sad that I'm so far away.
It's got everything you need and more great place for lunch people watching coffee fresh everything and Amish what a place

Even if you don't eat at Reading Terminal Market... it's a great atmosphere.  A great place to check things out.  They have great options and all different kinds of food and baked goods.  It's a great landmark in Philly and if you go to Philly and don't stop in Reading Terminal Market for at least a walk-through, then you've missed out.  But I've been there many times and they have some really good food spots.  I really like the Lamb spot that sells sandwiches.

This is the single best place in Philadelphia.

I could leave it at that but I'll go a little deeper.

If you are visiting Philly, you have to include Reading Terminal Market. Best to go Wednesday through Saturday when the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants are open. The market is open Sundays but a number of merchants are closed. 

You might think it is a tourist trap. It is to a degree. However, most of the people there are locals. Tourists can't sustain the meat, fish and produce shops that are there. So no shame, none, ever associated with it. Its not like being a New Yorker and going to Times Square for a meal.

The market is closed at 6PM, which is one of the few drawbacks: it has no evening hours. I hope one day that will somehow change.

Also, it can be overwhelming. Lunch rush is intense and finding a seat to enjoy that roast pork sandwich can be a challenge. I went there during lunch rush of the week between Christmas and New Year's and I have never seen it that crazy. So that's not the best time to go because hundreds of suburbanites like myself get the same idea to enjoy Reading Terminal with their day off.

For breakfast the options are limited. There is the Down Home Diner which is decent but I'm not kvelling about it. Some of the stands do breakfast but I haven't really tried them. I finally tried Profi's Creperie and it is pretty good.

My suggestions about food if you're there one time during a Philly visit: If it is Wednesday-Saturday, go to the Hatville Farms deli counter and get a smoked turkey special with iced-tea and potato chips. Hatville Farms is one of the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants and I swear that the smoked turkey special is the best thing in all of Reading Terminal Market. Plus, they have stools at their counter so you don't have to go looking for a seat. 

If it is Sunday-Tuesday, go to DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef. The line will be long but it moves fairly quick. Get the roast pork Italiano with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone. That's a Philly sandwich! 

Reading Terminal Market, you are what makes New Yorkers jealous of Philadelphia!

Comments: These guys had an Allagash tap takeover when we visited. Came during the day- chill vibe, good group of patrons, fun ambiance. Food menu looked updated, gastropub fare, maybe a tad pricey. Open air ambiance was a plus. No sampler flights really, but could get free splashes of tap beers. Not sure if this place has a good tap list normally, but 10 or so specialties this time around was impressive.
Seattle has the pike place market , philly has the reading terminal market which is nicer then the pike place market and with out the urine smell.

I LOVE the concept and wish we had something like this in Northern Virginia. We were lucky enough that the reading terminal was right next to our hotel & we swung by before it got busy. It's amazing how many restaurants and little booths they fit in here! Although I probably wouldn't eat at most of these places, it was an awesome experience and the few places I did eat at, I loved so I would definitely come back one day but I don't think it's a necessity.
Love this place! Amazing selection, run by pros with all different specialties. One of the best things about Philadelphia, hands down.

This place is a must-visit if you're new to Philly or in the City Hall/Market Street area and want a fun "local favorite" lunch option.  However, be warned - if you go on a weekend afternoon (of during the lunch rush during the week), it WILL be packed and it WILL be frustrating to move around the place.  But it's packed because it really just is that awesome and trust me, it's worth it.  No matter what you're craving, this place will have something to satisfy you and it will be delicious and reasonably priced.

No trip to Philly is complete without a visit to the Reading Terminal Market.  A foodie's delight with every type of cuisine you can imagine, all under one roof.  

My first trip there, I stumbled upon the Dutch Eating Place and I had their delicious blueberry pancakes.  The next visit, I stopped by a seafood restaurant (the name escapes me) and had the biggest scallops I have ever seen...also delicious.  Another time, I sampled a Philly cheesesteak for lunch.  I've been there at least three times and I still probaby haven't done a complete walk-through, the place is just that massive.  

Be forewarned, it can get crazy crowded at lunch time.  Security is there to make sure you don't form a line in the wrong place, lol.

I had a great time walking around the market with my friends! I'm originally from DC and frequent Union Market which is half the size of the RTM and I absolutely enjoyed all the food stalls! 
Also, as a chocolate lover it was really exciting to see all of the sweet and savory stalls with chocolates, cake, cookies and many more!
I truly enjoyed my time here and will definitely visit again in the future!

What's there not to like about the Reading Terminal?! 

Swing by the Tubby Olive and taste test olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Walk out with five bottles of the most delicious olive oils that are great as dips and on salads! 

Drop by for lunch and there's endless options. 

Swing by for a beer and hang out! 

Walk around and taste all the delicious desserts! 

Love cheese and fresh cut meat? The Amish do it right! 

Definite go to spot while you're in center city.
What an amazing place!  You can find anything you want here from the best hoagies to obscure game meats. Great variety, good prices, awesome people.

This is one of my favorite places in Philadelphia! The prices are reasonable, the selection is wide, and the competition is tough so places are challenged to keep it tasting great. If you're going to the convention center it would be stupid to eat the overpriced convention center food when this is right next door. If I lived in philly I imagine I would do some of my grocery shopping here too as the produce and meat and seafood were so fresh.

Omg! I wish we had this in DC area! So many food options to choose from, fresh market to go grocery shopping, and even inexpensive beautiful flowers. Came here on a Friday during lunch time and it was a busy place. 

Enjoyed Tommy DiNic's for lunch! Amazing food - definitely try that out. Took awhile to find a table because it was packed. But I'd love to come back here. 

If you park in the garage across from the market - make sure to bring your parking ticket inside and get it validated for a LOT cheaper with a minimum market purchase of $10.

I love the dim lights and rustic feel of this restaurant. The second row of bar seats is really cute. Our server was really attentive and was able to answer questions about the beer. (A HUGE plus for me)  

I was pretty disappointed with the food. I had The Industry burger. It was described as "1/4lb ground Pat LaFrieda brisket" which must mean "thin frozen patty" with no seasonings.
