My boyfriend wasn't feeling well so I ordered him a $10 mixed green salad to go. I got home and they had just thrown a salad into a cardboard box. They didn't even use a liner or anything. He did enjoy the salad.

Our poor server had the worst table ever seated next to us. I left her a funny note and a good tip. We'll definitely be back for drinks- I'll pass on the food.
I had the paneer kathi rolls for sad desk lunch--their food is fast, but uninspired.
Various local food and they are all good. So many stores to choose from and so crowded for reason.
Not bad of a place. I liked their spicy southwest chicken sandwich. Little crunchy on the outside and juicy inside. I would recommend this place.

Okay, if you're in Philly, you have to check out Reading Terminal Market. Although the place is a bit of a madhouse because of how busy it is and seating can be hard to find, the sheer number of great eateries here makes it a place that you have to go to for lunch or an early dinner.

As a life long Philadelphian and a former Saturday employee at the Market I have to say there is no other place like it in the city. From Shopping to noshing all of your needs can be met.  Yes it get crowded especially on the weekends but its always fun. When I worked here it was breakfast from the Amish, lunch at Dinic's and shopping for my meats, seafood and fresh fruits and vegetables. Most of my pay was funneled directly back to the merchants but we ate well all week. You never know who you will run into here as well. From politicians to former players, it's a great place for people watching.
a nice little place but so far of the places that i have tried it didn't make me want to head back there unless i have to do something at the convention center...
Get a DiNiC's pork sandwhich with broccoli rabe. So good! It's a popular place at lunch time so look for the long line.

This market is great to try out various food items.  There's so much to take in and try.  We got a pretzel to snack on..buttery goodness, soft and fluffy with a touch of salt.  The dipping cheese puts it over the top, highly recommend!   The sandwich from Dinic was great as well, juicy and full of meat.

Love the reading terminal true Philly girl so much to choose from I came here today with intention on getting some pecan Carmel Cookie s from the Pennsylvania bake shop located on arch street side of the market. Best cookies hands down soft and chewy

Absolutely love this place! Mind - blown.

It's a huge market with so much to experience and offer, from restaurants to wine to food-to-go, and then some. I went to an Amish restaurant for breakfast, and it was so damn good! Seemed like THE place to eat and be at. We were so full afterwards that I couldn't look at any more food nor overwhelm my senses further, so I didn't explore much else, but from what I did see, I could definitely say this isn't your average, annoying tourist trap and well-worth the visit.

I love Reading Terminal Market! So much variety and a lot of tasty options. From Dinic's cheesesteaks to Bassett's ice cream( get the frequent licker card, you get a free one after 10 buys) , the market is magical. There are so many places I have yet to try but all in all, bring an empty stomach and your wallet!

If you are in Philly, even if only for an hour or two, you MUST come here.  I've been coming here for years and I haven't had a single thing that I didn't love.  
Favorites: Olympia Gyro gyro, Hershel's corned beef reuben, Termini Bros cannoli, everything Amish
Amazing paneer and Kala khatta. The paneer is so soft that it reminds me of the paneer one gets in India. Will come back
There is a variety of deliciousness available in different price ranges. I love the Amish bread & cinnamon rolls. It's also very close to the Masonic Temple which is a must for anyone visiting.
You kidding me?!  Philly's Best!  If they had beds, I'd wouldn't leave for a week.
I work across from the Reading Terminal.  Dinic's is a fave, HungerBurgers Mediterranean salad is so good, ummmm artichokes.

Wow, check it out, another 5 star Reading Terminal Market review.

If you're in Philly, this should be on your must-go-to list for at least a meal.

The food here is great.  If you can't find what you're looking for, you're too picky.  From Wed-Sat most of the Amish folks will be here and I HIGHLY recommend getting breakfast at the Dutch Eating place which is nested toward the back of the market.  Their blueberry pancakes are perfect and their homemade apply turnovers are so worth it, if anything get one to go.

Most of the market is what I would classify as the United Nations snack fest.  Everything from falafels to pulled pork sandwiches, Asian cuisine, just everything.  

Termini Bros has a shop in here, don't pass on the canolis, they are renowned for their pastries.

I would not recommend Down Home Diner - they have a dining time limit.  I understand they're busy, but really?

When you go to Four Seasons Juice Bar make sure you pick yourself up any choice of smoothie..they'll make you come back and come back and come right on back. I selected Hawaii Passion my first time here and haven't tried anything else cause' I'm hooked. 

When you go...tell me your favorite :-)

I love RTM - so many options! Spices, prepared food, produce, meats, gift items. So great! Definitely gets super crowded around lunchtime and on the weekends, so I wouldn't recommend coming with a baby stroller or food cart. But it's fantastic!

Sonntag morgen  auf der Suche nach einem Frühstück außerhalb des HotelsViele Cafés etc. haben geschlossen  und so entdecken wir den Reading Terminal Market. Hinter der alten Fassade verbirgt sich ein ganzes Labyrinth an tollen Ständen und Shops, die alles mögliche feilbieten  von Fisch, Sushi, Fleisch, Wurst, Gemüse, Obst und und und. Auch der Frühstückshungrige bleibt nicht lange hungrig  sei es nun ein Crepe, ein French Toast oder eine Eierspeise, für jeden Geschmack ist etwas dabei!!! Wären wir nicht vom Frühstück so satt gewesen, wären wir schon zum Mittagessen wieder da gewesen.

This really is one of Philadelphia's greatest treasures, enjoyed by locals and tourists alike. Be sure to stop by DeNick's for the best sandwich you will ever have in your life, and then go across the market to the PA General Store. They will set you up with some treats at every price point. 

All the stores in between are a treat as well.

Masala Kitchen is my favorite restaurant in the neighborhood. They have plenty of Kati rolls which is unique for the area, and they're open very late. The service is friendly, delivery is offered, and any special requests are taken care of. Hopefully more people come in since the restaurant is still new.

OMG my school went here on a class trip in middle school!  It was the first and last time I've been to the Market.  I wandered around with a few classmates and we ate Chinese food for lunch and matriculated throughout the place until I felt like I found out what it would be like to be an ant in an ant farm.  There was even a news story going on and we tried to be in the background but the chick who was the reporter shooed us away.  This was one of many fun class trips to Philly that serve as reminders of why I love New Jersey.

I loved this place for the six years when I lived in Philly and missed it when I moved west for four years. Now we're back and it's gotten even better. More variety, lots of new places to eat, excellent fresh meat, cheeses, fish and produce. Wonderful sweets and ethnic foods too. Great bustle and energy.

Admittedly, my standard for city markets is pretty high, using Seattle's Pike Place Market as the benchmark against which all others will be compared.  Philly's Reading Terminal Market holds its own against this lofty standard.  While not nearly as large as Pike Place Market, it still holds a solid variety of vendors, from butcher shops to fishmongers to fresh produce and other vendors that make it an actual working market not a tourist trap with a bunch of kiosks selling souvenirs and other Made in China crap.  Of note, the Sunday early afternoon crowd definitely seemed to be made up with a lot more tourists compared to the Monday crowd, as it was considerably less crowded and chaotic on a regular workday.  Reading Terminal Market also offers a numerous food counters serving a wide array of regional and international cuisines from which you can sample.  It can get very congested with customers/tourists especially around lunchtime in large part due the place being packed with vendor stalls and narrow aisles between them.  However, it's worth your time to check it out.

Good food options.  The ice cream joint located near the front is just ok.  The cookie place across from the ice cream place is great. I also like the different sandwich shops and the fresh food markets.  I would give the place 4 stars if they power washed the floors on a regular basis.

I love markets like this, so I tend to visit them everywhere I go.  Reading is definitely one of the better ones I've been to.  So many food options, so many shopping options, and a really fun vibe for out of town guests.  Good for your weekly shopping or a touristy outing.

I was in the Roxborough area this afternoon and came across this Subway. It looked good so I decided to stop in. 

A man who I believe was the manager or owner quickly came out and warmly greeted me. 

I ordered two sandwiches one for now and later. I hit the Roast Beef and the chicken teriyaki. They also were selling the new Lay's Do Us a Flavor Chips, which I decided to check out. I got the everything bagel and cream cheese flavor! 

Since I bought a lot, the owner was really nice and gave me a complimentary chocolate chip cookie! 

The Roast Beef sandwich, which I had at the restaurant was really good. The meat was tender and tasty. The fresh vegetables also helped top it all off!

This Subway also immaculately clean. The tables and floor are spotless!

This Subway also delivers via UberEATS, which I saw during my most recent visit.

Altogether, this is a great Subway to get a bite to eat at!

I stopped by Industry on a recommendation from my Philly host for the weekend. It's got a nice interior design as well as a few tables worth of outdoor space. There are also heaters above each outdoor table which was very very nice. It was around the brunch hour and they had a brunch menu that includes food and drink options. The draft beer list is solid. The first order of business was pairing something sweet with a good stout, I settled on their donuts with a stout. The stout was poured well. The donuts were a little over done but they came with a good dipping sauce and still paired well with my stout.My entree was a brunch special, salmon with a lemon aioli, a poached egg on a English muffin open face  and served with breakfast potatoes. It was exactly the flavor profile I was looking for. The salmon was fresh, not fishy and balanced well with the lemon. The egg was nice and runny once I pierced the yolk. The breakfast fries were good as well. They brought out a piece of coffee cake as a friend had a little issue with their order. The coffee cake also paired really well with my stout! I tried the brunch cocktail which was a beet, ginger, vodka and soda water (maybe champagne), it was strong but good. Overall I enjoyed my experience at The Industry and I would recommend at least checking out brunch. It seems they also have a variety of good specials during the week and for HH so if I'm in the area again I might have to swing by.

The food is good and tasty. The mango lassi is nicely packaged and tastes AMAZING. So does the Chaas. But I ordered delivery once and got a long hair in my food. The second time I ordered I got a staple in it.

This market is one of the most impressive examples of how diverse the United States really are. Wandering in from the bustling center city Philly one is greeted with many languages, foods and people. This market not only has great selections of produce, Halal food, Chinese food, Philly cheesesteaks etc. it also boasts Dinics steak and pork stand where the some of the best sandwiches in Philly are made.

Well, cleanliness is not on the menu at this Wendy's. The restaurant is nearly brand new, but the floors are so greasy that your not walking, more like sliding across the dining room floor.. No napkins, no lids at the drink station. 

Service ..... Really,,, line nearly to the door and one person at the front counter. Plenty of employees back of the house cleaning but no one taking care of the customers out front. If the owner reads this: your business needs some "Management" and a good store cleaning with a good Grease cutting soap.

My favorite place to eat in Philly when visiting my girlfriend.

1) Pretzels from Miller's Twist are a must. Don't forget the spicy mustard!

2) Iced and green tea from the leaf tea stand is amazing

3) DiNic's is ovverrated, it's good but don't expect anything extraordinary...certainly not the "best sandwich in America"

4) Still looking for a good pizza place though.....

Excelente calidad y variedad de comidas (dulces y saladas, grandes puestos de panadería). Degustaciones en varios puestos, y atención personalizada y muy atenta. No pueden irse sin probar el Philly Cheese Steak, típico de la ciudad y presente en cada uno de los puestos.
Evitar en horario de almuerzo porque hay mucha gente y la espera se vuelve un poco pesada, mucho más difícil es conseguir donde sentarse en ese horario.
Se puede comprar para llevar, o comer allí. Lunes a sábados de 8am a 6pm y domingos de 9am a 5pm. Si consumen algo por más de U$S10, pidan la validación y tiene 2 horas de parking a U$S4 (1th & Arch Streets ó 12th & Filbert Streets).
Love this place for all my fresh meats and produce! I particularly go to the Amish, since the taste in their meats are fresh and without hormones and GMOs.
If you want a taste of Philadelphia, this is the place to come. Termini Bros Bakery, Dinic's Roast Pork Sandwich, Amish soft pretzels, Bassett's ice cream - Reading Terminal has it all!!
DiNick's Brisket sandwich with spinach is the best sandwich I have ever had.

Love this place...all the sights, sounds, and yummy treats.  LUV the dark chocolate pretzels from the Chocolate by Mueller...breakfast of champions!  I had bad luck with John Yi Fish Market.  After reading some reviews, I thought it was a safe bet and ordered a cooked lobster to go.  They told me it would take 20 minutes, but I thought it was because I was in a queue.  I didn't realize that they were going to bake it for 20 minutes.  Seriously, it was the toughest lobster I have ever had.  The claws were tough and dry like cardboard and I am not exaggerating.  What a $21 disappointment!  The raw fish looks good, so I think the only issue is their lobster abuse.

My first time in Philly meant that I had to make a trip to the famous Reading Terminal market.. And I was not disappointed. In fact I loved the vibe of this place so much that I came here twice on my 2 day weekend trip.

We tried the cheesesteak at Spataro's which was not as flavorful and greesy as I had hoped for a cheesesteak to be (hence a star less). The coffee from Old City Coffee was a great change from my usual go-to, with a nice full bodied medium roast coffee. I loved it's old school vibe and servers making sure to give you the coffee exactly how you want it. 

On my second time here I stopped at the Pearls Oyster Bar right at the entrance for a hearty diner-style fare. My husband got the eggs Benedict which he really enjoyed and I got the berry compote french toast which was perfectly sweet and just what I needed. And they have unlimited coffee refills!! *gasp* 
We got a chocolate milkshake from L.D. Bassetts which was really nice but a little too rich for me. Unfortunately, after all the food and the I couldn't  try their ice cream for which it is famous. Until next time! 
I walked around the market and wished that my stomach and appetite were large enough so I could try everything here (which is a HUGE selection of various cuisines) since everything looked and smelled de-lish. Next time I am coming back to try the dutch breakfast place and get an assortment or their local cheeses and groceries.

The food is good. But the service is poor. Rude workers that double charge and don't even know the correct prices for what people order. They have messed up my order at least 3 times. And they don't even apologize for it( the staff). That's the part that tells me no more chipotle for which is so sad because I love the food.

Reading Terminal Market was exactly how I pictured it. I've seen it many times on television but never visited until recently. There are dozens of vendors and also provides a good amount of table seating for a market of this size. The only downside of coming here was the parking. The parking lots around the area were a bit expensive and street parking looked very limited. We drove over to Chinatown and got lucky with spot. It's about a 5 minutes walk from Chinatown which isn't bad at all.

Places that I've visited and tried.

1. Bassetts Ice cream is a must!
2. Molly Malloy's Chicken pot pie had a bad crust but overall was still good.
3. Beck's Cajun Cafe was dynamite with their Gator Gumbo.
4. Tommy DiNic's roast pork sandwiches were great. They're not greasy like cheesesteaks.

We peeked at other vendors but were too full to try anything else. I will definitely come back to Reading Terminal next time I visit Philly and try other things. As for now, I highly recommend the Gator Gumbo from Beck's and Ice cream and shakes from Bassetts. Those were my two top picks during this visit.

The Redding Terminal rules. It's best to go outside of the 12-1 hour if you don't like crowds. The businesses are used to being busy so they're efficient, it just gets packed. 

Sometimes on the last Tuesday of the month, one of the vendors hires a small, green leprechaun to run around and hand out gold coins. When he runs out of gold coins, he gets pissed. His real name is Stuart Lu Jennings, but when he's mad he prefers to be called Harry McBillingsworth. If you don't call him by his preferred name he can react poorly and scare small children. He prefers to hang around dessert food establishment and call people, "his beautiful little Irish potatoes". He's strange.

I used to live near Pike's Place Market in Seattle so I'm a tad biased here, but I'll try to put that aside. 

Positives: nice markety vibe while still being pretty clean, good prices on produce, cool things to look at, and great location in the middle of the city.

Negatives: not quite the variety of quick dining options that you would expect at a market in a large city.  I know we're in Philly, but everywhere I looked there were sandwiches. The Amish country food looked pretty good, but other than that and an Indian place, I didn't see many a myriad of options. 

Seafood selection is sparse and on the expensive side. Worth going to to pick up your fruits and veggies for the week, but not worth bringing your friends here when they visit.

Went there with a group of 5 of us last night.  It was quizzo night so a bit louder than usual but they warned us when we called.  We were fine with it and had a great meal with a wonderful wait staff.  We had Mac and cheese croquettes, fried green tomato salad, hamburger, veggie salad, chicken and cod.  Everyone enjoyed their food and the service was very good.  We will be going back.  Only one tiny suggestion for improvement for them is to have better overhead lighting in the area of seating on Moyamensing Ave. side.  It was extremely hard for us to see our menus in this area.  Way too dark there so if you go just opt for a table in another area of the room until this issue is corrected.  But go for the great food asap!
Crazy crowded, but lots of great places to eat.  Must visit when you come to Philadelphia.

I wanted really badly for this place to be great since it is steps from my door. The burger I had was a half step up from mcdonalds and the bbq pulled duck jumped into a vat of cumin. The atmosphere is coo,l decor is great ,beer selection wonderful, service was excellent but the food left alot to be desired

It's been awhile since I've been to a Chipotle but I just had to say today my bowl was prepared perfectly and the staff was so friendly and chatty! I especially have to shout out Monique! Great job to whoever is supervising this location!

I ordered online but one part of my order couldn't be filled. I ordered pizza, 2 orders of wings and a pasta. Neither pasta option was available. (They did inform me before I came to pick it up so it wasn't a surprise when I got there) I come for pick up, the register is filthy, there was no greeting when I arrived and although my food was in the "heater" it was cold.

Went here today for the very first time. Everything was great. Service, drinks, and food were superb. They especially get the 5 stars for how fast everything was. Literally the fastest drink and food service I've ever had. No more than 3-5 minutes for a new drink or even an entree. Highly recommended.

I'm in love! This was the perfect rainy Saturday morning activity on our visit. Reading Terminal Market is just wonderful. The size of this market is overwhelming, but they offer so much under one roof; crafts, organic goods, fresh produce, seafood, fresh meats, authentic German sausages, wine, cheeses, baked goods, places to stop and grab a snack - the list goes on and on. It gets busy and crowded. Be prepared to wait in line at the more popular stops. Also note the Amish vendors are closed Sunday and Monday. A visit to Philadelphia is not complete without stopping here!
great palce to visit for a variety of goods. I defiantly recommend the coffe

It's ok.  Average small toasted sandwiches.  The menu looked like it had some good sandwich combos.  I got a sandwich and a drink for under $6.  Not sure what there theme is, but it's interesting inside.  I look at it as something to eat with no destination items.  

Depending on the time of day, it may be easier to park at Commerce Bank.
Excellent market and restaurants. It can be a bit crowded during lunch time, but otherwise has reasonable crowds.

love this place My fave eateries here are
Beck's Cajun Cafe= fried mac and cheese, cajun alfredo pasta and whiskey bread pudding
Creperie place
vegetarian place- i forgot the name
next time i'll try the by geoge

I lived in l loft less than 1 block away from 03-06 when I was single, just so I could come here everyday. I prob spent thousands a month from the Amish cartel to sang kee, pearls oysters and the down home diner. I'm not even counting all the $$$ I spent on fresh squeezed oj, which was $10 every other day. Great place but going everyday and doing my shopping there almost led me to become one of the homeless that inhabit the corners. From what I understand these unlucky souls used to be attorneys and doctors before succumbing to the delicious addiction that is contained inside the old reading railroad station.

Awesome place with lots of food options. Farmers market is really good, you can get variety of fruits which may not be available everywhere, like shaved fresh coconut. 

Great options for desserts, there's a nice crepery, really good ice cream place and a place which sells fresh baked cookies and other goodies. Highly recommended if you are in center City Philly. Only downside is it is not open late in the evening.

ALL of the food is a bit overpriced but if you visit Philadelphia it is a quintessential experience. As a resident, all that I ask is that you not be the millionth tourist to stand in the middle of the isle, no doubt in a circle, with a stroller, at noon so that no one get can past you.

Paradise for foodies. Everything literally everything we had a bite of food from here is delicious and the taste and memories of those still linger on my mind. Will be visiting again when I'm in philly.

It is definitely a mass of humanity, but if you can navigate a crowd, this place is a must. Great place for a foodie to grab a bite. Everything you can impossibly imagine and then some. Different types of foods, baked goods, florists, books, wine...you name, it's there. Some of the lines can be long, but if you're in a hurry to grab a bite, there are plenty of just as tasty options that you can get your food incredibly quick. Everyone I've encountered that works there is great, as well.

It's pretty touristy sometimes, but it has great things in it, like the Flying Monkey Bakery that makes super delicious desserts, the Amish juice shop that has great natural juices (including Victory Thirst Clincher), the Amish rib place that'll give you a super rib sandwich/potato wedges/mac n' cheese and soda combo for under $10 that's usually my meal of choice from this place...and some places like Dinic's that have gotten national attention for how good they are.  It's a pretty neat place, def a place to visit if you're not from around Philly.

I've only been here once but was really disappointed with the food, especially after hearing good things about this place from a few people. It was a slow night, service was decent. I ordered something super simple and it actually couldn't have been worse. I had a salad that was flooded with Gorgonzola cheese with a tiny piece of unseasoned, over cooked steak. It was surprisingly awful. My girlfriend and I finished the first courses and left. I will be going back soon to give it a second chance.
This place is amazing. As good as it gets in Philly; from Dinic's Roast Pork to Beiler's Doughnuts - you cannot go wrong visiting Reading Terminal.

AWESOME PLACE TO VISIT!

Tons of great food. 

Must visit when in Philly. 

Well worth the wait for food.

This is probably my favorite place to go in all of philly.  And a must see stop for tourists visiting. My only complaint is that during peak times - between 11am and 3pm, especially on weekends,  it becomes claustrophobic and virtually impossible to navigate within the massive crowds.  My advice is arrive close to opening and bring an appetite, even most of the lunch places open early...Roast Pork from DiNic's at 10am - sounds perfect :-)

This place does NOT accept credit cards, cash only!!! There's a money machine inside that'll happily give you cash for a fee. The food was decent, I've had much better PR food in the state. There was no dessert like others commented about. Customer service was very lacking as well.

Didn't know what to expect, more like Quincy market in Boston but I couldn't be more wrong. What an amazing place. It was so hard to make a decision on where to eat and then what to have as a treat. Hope to visit the area again so I can go back
Great area to catch some local food and flare.  Crowed and tons of tourist but a wide variety of food and specialty products from across the US and PA in particular.

I never understood what the big deal was about Chick-fil-a especially to warrant all these huge new restaurants cause the menu is so minimal. 
The chicken sandwiches are pretty good for fast food but the waffle fries are the real stand-out. 
The peach shake, when in season,  is amazing with chunks of real peaches.
The playground is a huge help if you have little ones. The best bribe to get them to eat. :)

Whenever I visit Philadelphia, I run as fast as possible to this market.  I dream of it.  I wish it was in NYC.

I don't think I've ever had a bad meal here.  My favorites are Franks-A-Lot, The Original Turkey, Little Thai Market, Famous 4th Street Cookie Co, Termini Bros, The Dutch Eating Place and Beiler's Bakery.  Of all of them, don't miss the Amish stalls surrounding Dutch Eating Place and Beiler's.

I wish I could be at Reading Market all the time.  What others have said about the crowds is right.  This place is standing room only, mosh pit crazy, rush hour subway ride crowded and it's not an over statement.  So hold on to all your patience and jump into the scene.
Great food.  Fantastic service and management with a smile.  Very clean and nice simple decor. Highly recommend it!

Oh I'm speechless in a good way! Reading Terminal oh how I love you! This is a place I could literally stay in all day long IF they had a gym inside hahaa ! All the vendors from deli's, fresh seafood markets, produce stands, Amish bread! Yum!! 
Not only that but all the places to eat from American to overseas! It's like once you walk in you can tour the world by eating! How awesome is that?! 
I have never been in anything like this before so I was fascinated by the vast food choices as I walked around.
If you are visiting the area this is absolutely one place you need to come. I cannot stress enough how awesome this place is heck I'm getting excited about going again as I write this review!
It's an experience I will never forget and each place I ate was delicious! One thing to note though it gets really crowded! So, when you do get something to eat seating is rare haha, but don't lose faith people are very nice and will make room for you! I call this type of eating family style! Great meeting new people while experiencing fabulous foods!
I'll be back!

Come on man??  Really - we need a review of the Reading Terminal??  
Its one of the greatest places you can go on the planet.  PERIOD.  It is Philly and has the tastes of the surrounding countryside.  There is a cool little bar in there too.  Just love it.  need something for dinner, for lunch - You want great fishmongers?  You want great meat and sausage?  You want something Amish?  You want chocolates, fruit, a gift ??  
DONE, DONE, DONE.

Great tourist place, but definitely not a place I go as a city dweller. I would take visitors here, but there are no great food places inside (it's all standard!). 
If you are from New York and know the Chelsea Market- this is NOTHING like it and not nearly as cool. 
If you are from the UK and love the Borough Market- again, nothing in the same ballpark,. 
Reading Terminal has a mix of chinese food, greek food, ice cream, lots of Amish stands. You can't even get good priced flowers here. 
It's cool to visit once, then you're done.

Stopped by during end of Philly Beer Week. Place looked awesome, nice big bar, plenty of additional seats. Tap list was OK, thought there would be some better ones considering what Good Dog usually has on tap. 

I'll go again when it's not beer week and check it out.

The perfect fast food getaway. When I mentioned fast food, It isn't McDonald, this place is something far better. Food quality, service, cleanliness are top notch in this place. I wish I live next door from this place.
Super place! Very bucolic - soothng atmosphere. Excellent food and service.

I love this place!  Started going here years ago anytime I was in Philly, but it's been ages since I'd last been here.  Got to stop by a few days ago on my way out of town, and it was just as good as I remembered.  Didn't get a chance to have a full meal as I had just eaten, but I had a few snacks and just enjoyed the smells.  Can't wait to go back and enjoy some fresh seafood next time I'm there.
Enjoyed my visit to the market. Visited Philly for the first time a few weeks ago and glad I did. The parking special was awesome and super convenient.

Go here. It's a ton of fun. Check out the juice bar and the shawarma place. You won't regret it. Honestly, I shouldn't even be writing this review because the market is so well known. If you're visiting Philly, make sure to go here. If you're a local, please check out the fish market (Johnny yu's) for your next meal. It's so, so good
I wish the prices were a bit lower, but the food is great!

Cool place. A taste of everything cuisine wise. A little pricey but i think its worth it for what this place offers. Only downside is this place becomes a mad house once noon hits. The crowds can be just as overwhelming as the choices of food. Food is worth it as well.

Reading Terminal Market is an integral part of Philadelphia's culture and history.  You will find wonderful restaurants and vendors throughout the market and a truly unique atmosphere.  If you are in town for even one day, come check it out around lunch time; you won't be disappointed.  For those of you whining on Yelp about it being crowded, please stop embarrassing yourself.  Its a 150 + year old market in the middle of one of the largest cities in the USA; it's supposed to be busy.
A tourist must see! Such a cool place to visit when coming to Philly. Come hungry and ready!

Very eclectic selection of food and crafts.  Got to try Shoo fly pie but it's the Miller's Twist Pretzels that I'm still dreaming about!  Picked up some unique crafts too, e.g., a pen set that had a fork, spoon and knife attached as tops so you can eat and work at the same time, LOL.

Eh... It is all I can say. Walked in to a ghost town and it was NOON. Worker sitting on counter when I walked in. No hello from either of the guys there. Felt like I was imposing to order. Worker never even got off the counter when I ordered through when I paid. 15minutes later....he is still there. Sandwich is mediocre...average .  They toasted bread but meat is cold and warm in spots. Kind of a turn off. Girl behind counter was very nice though.
Love it here. Great food, great original cocktails and great service. A little pricey to go all the time but definitely worth it every once in awhile. Also has brunch which is a plus!
I was looking for quick and easy food after work and this hit the exact spot. I had the chicken masala roll and it was awesome! Excited to come back and try other rolls.

If your in downtown Philly this is a must. Super fun and cool indoor market. I recommend walking around trying a little of everything if possible. They have an array of different cuisine and some fun local beers. Bring cash and walk around. I will be back.

There are so many options to eat in reading terminal market. I always get confused as to what I want to eat but one thing I am always certain of is the Lancaster juice store. I have dreams about that delicious orange strawberry lemonade. Just know that they aren't open on Sundays.

this is a staple of the philadelphia community... im biased a bit because ive grown up around this place. i will say however there is a good amount of food that can not be replicated by any other place in philadelphia... try going on weekdays when it is not too busy.

The Best must visit food stops in Philly. I won't say every vendor is top notch but if you browse enough you'll find the best vendors. A little something for everyone. I go every time I visit definitely a scene: Oysters, Cheesesteaks, cheese, jerky, corn dogs, Cajun, lobsters, butchers, a BAR!

a little bit of everything in 1 spot! Yay!
One of the cool spots in Philly!

This is one of my favorite places of any city in the world! The concentration of such supreme food in one place is awesomely overwhelming. K. Parker has one of the best chicken wings in Philly. DiNic's roast pork is probably the best sandwich in the US. Peking Duck has a dumpling soup that will change your life. And Beiler's has the best donut you'll ever eat. And these spots are only a few in a massive market of top quality choices. Whenever I get visitors, I bring them to Reading Terminal and it just blows their minds.

Dropping my daughter off at bus station today - Looking to grab a quick breakfast and found this gem. Everything you could possibly want is here! Wow! So much to choose from wish I could eat more. Take home is a must.
I really miss Terminal Market. Been everywhere in the states and nothing comes close to it.
Hmm... Awesome indoor market - Wander around and make sure to visit Termini's and get a banana (just tell the lady at the counter)

Once again, thank you 'Redding' Terminal Market. Hurricane Sandy forced me to stay in a hotel around the corner, and only you offered fresh eats on the fly. The Mezze mediterranean lasagna was hearty and flavorful, but their salmon a bit overcooked. I also picked up a lb of super chewy cookies from one of their bakeries (ugh, can't remember the name and am too lazy to walk over to the table to look at their bag). That's what happens when you can't decide, stuck in a long line, and a baby strapped to your chest. So far, I've had the pumpkin, the turtle, and starting my way into the macadamia nut...mmm.

Most incredible open market I never seen. Every type of food you can possibly imagine they have. If you're ever in downtown Philadelphia it's definitely one you need to put on the bucket list of things to do.

I wanted really badly for this place to be great since it is steps from my door. The burger I had was a half step up from mcdonalds and the bbq pulled duck jumped into a vat of cumin. The atmosphere is cool, decor is great ,beer selection decent, service was excellent but the food left alot to be desired

I honestly don't know what else can be said about Reading Terminal that hasn't already been said.
There is a reason why this place is frequented by locals, celebrities, even the president himself comes here when he's in Philly. I could tell you about the Dutch place, cheese, fudge,produce, baked goods, donuts that people line up and wait willingly for, but this is something that you truly must see and experience for yourself. Be prepared to spend a good amount of time here, especially if you are a serious foodie.

Really good kati rolls, outstrips others in the city for sure. The ingredients taste so fresh, and the flavors are very distinctive, which I appreciate, since a lot of fast food Indian tends to slap a vague tikka masala over everything and call it a day. The rolls look small, but two rolls left me feeling like I was going to explode. I'd recommend the paneer tikka (cottage cheese with onions and spices) and chicken masala (chicken in a creamy tomato based sauce).

I have traveled to Philly for over 10 years for work and this is hands down the best place to go for lunch.

There are so many choices that it can be overwhelming if you are not sure what you want to eat, but there is something for everyone.

It can be very busy at lunchtime especially if there is a convention going on and it can be hard to find a seat.  Your best bet is to try and go after 1pm it seems to thin out a bit.

I definitely have my favorite places but I always try to go somewhere new on each visit.

Stop in you won't be disappointed!

What's bad to say about this place? Whether you're craving freshly baked cookies that are literally just coming out of the oven or clams on the half shell, you are sure to find it all here. This place is my go to if I have time early in the morning and want to indulge is a fresh donut. This place is ALWAYS packed on the weekends. FYI - a lot of the Amish stands aren't open on Sundays.. The produce stand (Iovine Bros.) is nice and always clean and well organized. This market is always buzzing with patrons. They sometimes play live music in the designated "seating area" which is in the middle of the market. Local produce, in-house made chocolates and cakes, spicy Indo/Pak food, Jamaican delights and so much more are all housed under the same roof. Come hungry because you will definitely leave happy!
Very cool place. Lots to see and eat. Many different varieties and stores. Would definitely need to go again on a day where i can take my time exploring.

Amazing selection of food and other products! Whether you want to grab something already made or you're buying fresh meats, produce, etc to make later, there's going to be something for everyone here. 

Expect big crowds and long lines during most times, but it's more than worth it in the end. Also, if you're hoping to get something from the PA Dutch vendors don't come on Sundays because their stands will be closed!
What a great market!  Far better than Grand Central Terminal market in NYC!  Anything and everything can be found here...my favorite part of the market is the Amish section...

Heaven on Earth for hungry people...you better have self control or you could be eating cookies, ice cream, and candy for lunch ! everything fresh and priced right. HAVE THE BASSET ICE CREAM- just arm yourself with napkins- you will need them . Had Thai soup one day, rib dinner the next. So fun to browse and people watch. You gotta go !!

I love Reading Terminal Market.  It's totally worth pushing your way through the tourists to get some unbelievably cheap groceries.  My favorite spots are Iovine Brothers for cheap produce, Martins for amazing and inexpensive fresh meat, Metropolitan Bakery for sliced bread, The Amish baked goods stand for rolls and pies, and The Amish cheese stand for cheap, good quality cheeses.  I get most of my groceries from Reading Terminal and always bring famiyl and friends whoa re visiting for ice cream and a cheesesteak.

$15 minimum on card. What? The overall cleanliness of this place has more to be desired. Trash was not emptied and overflowing; worker preparing our food did not cover her sneeze... Ordered the fried giant squid as well as the calamari. The batter leaves more to be desired, it does not hold well against the squid and falls apart really easily. Wasn't crispy. Sautéed squid was solid, and very flavorful. Will be back maybe to try the chicken cutlet.

There is something for everyone at Reading Terminal Market. This is the perfect place to bring guests you are hosting who are visiting Philadelphia. It is in a great location that is near other attractions and each person in your party can choose what stand they want to visit. It can become crowded - especially during typical lunch times so if it is nice outside I suggest walking around, getting your food to go and then eating outside. Be sure to take pictures - all of the vibrant colors can lead to some really great shots! I highly recommend the fudge from the "Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe"

I love markets like this. Only thing is I wish I were her visiting rather than on an assignment. My then bf told me to check this place out when I was in Philly for a project, so I dragged my entire team that's used to doing lunch @ the Palm or somewhere in the vicinity of where the client was located out to Reading. I had a quick walk in the market and was intrigued. I would have wanted to explore the eateries more and try a couple out but the problem with having a client expense budget is.... my colleagues wanted fancy schmancy lunches rather than what was offered at Reading. Bleah, so like I said, right place, wrong time.

We ended up doing lunch at Maggiano's which was just outside Reading. BTW, I bet we could have had a tastier lunch had we decided to eat in Reading instead.

Yes it gets SUPER crowded (especially when conferences are in town / lunch time) but it is very unique to have such a bustling and crowded market with tons of diverse food selections.

Definitely a must-see for out of town visitors and for when you want that special sandwich or dessert.  Also, several fruit and vegetable grocers have an astonishingly display and variety of fruits/veggies at great prices as long as you don't mind waiting on line for a few minutes. 

It's super impressive - definitely bring your friends!

My friend and I love to treat ourselves to lunch at the Couch Tomato!  The food is always great and so is the friendly service.  The soup was amazing and the salad was scrumptious.  I honestly recommend it and look forward to my next meal there.

I'm definitely a fan of Industry after going there three times now. It has some different and interesting menu items which is refreshing.  Every time I have ordered the bone marrow small plate and I will probably order it every time I go back. 

I was hesitant to order the Pig ear lettuce wraps basically because I give that stuff to my dog usually. It turns out it was tasty and a little more crunchy than chewy. It's really not what you are expecting.

I finally ordered the burger last night and it is a serious contender in Philly. It's all brisket which gives it an awesome fatty flavor. The only downside is the single patty is only 4oz. and you will probably want to add a second patty to get a regular size. If they had a single decent size it would probably be better.
I fell in the love the second I walked in. This was our very first stop when we arrived to Philly. This market has everything which is awesome!

This is probably my favorite place to eat in Philly. They have every type of cuisine. I've only ever gone during lunch time so it's always ridiculously crowded, but well worth it. I pretty much always get the 4 cheese white pizza and gnocchi at By George. I've never had to wait more than 5 minutes. I love Head Nut which sells every kind of nut, candy, etc, and the candy and chocolate shops are all amazing!

Reading Terminal Market is a fantastic place to go to for food. I'm personally very partial to the Dutch Eating Place (their Grilled Reuben is an American Treasure), which means I don't like going here on Sundays (when the Amish stands are closed).

There are a lot of other good things here, and it makes for a great bustling experience where you go with a bunch of friends and all get something different to eat.

One of the best places on Earth, IMHO.

With fresh produce, amazing food, a bar, coffee spots, and every flavor of chapstick you could imagine, what more do you need?

Love, love, love.

Raise your hand if you have never purposely gotten lost and wondered aimlessly through this place! I could spend HOURS here just roaming around and taking everything in with full enjoyment. I have only been there enough times to count on one hand, but so far that is enough times for me to be curtain I like it. I am from Cleveland(ish) Ohio and we have NOTHING like this there! I love 4th Street Cookies! Oh man talk about a chocolate overloaded sugar induced coma! So worth it. Try the chocolate chip cookie dipped in chocolate! I have found the best produce there! I also am planning on going back and going on a dry goods binge. I plan on buying crazy pastas, grains, teas and spices next time I venture in!

This place is amazing! We went to following:

Tootsie's Salad Express: Had the fried fish, fried chicken, mac and cheese and some potatoes. I thought the fish had the best taste, everything else was a little bland. Not my favorite in the market.

Flying Monkey: The plain whoopies pies were delicious! The pumpkin was a little too sweet for me. Also, lemon bars were yummy!

Mueller Chocolate Co.: My only regret is that I didn't get more chocolate. Had the almond bark and milk chocolate coconut, SO GOOD!!!
Literally has everything. Pad Thai at the Thai food stand is the best around and Beilers when the line isn't crazy is heaven. Beilers does donuts, and do yourself a favor and try them

Got our lunch today,  a little bit costumer line but all cash registers were open to speed up the order process.

Employees all wear clean and neat uniform, they even deliver food to costumer tables when the food isn't ready rather to have costumer stand and wait.

Manager walk around and greet costumers, tables cleaned up every time costumer done with their meals. 
One of the waitress offer me for a refill, I asked her just to add more ice cubes for my ice tea, and she happily help me with that.

Feels like eat at fancy restaurant rather than a fast food chain.

Famous as it is, the market is nevertheless a rather overpriced tourist trap yet good for a walk through and finding little snacks and food items for everyone. Everything from pastries to honey and hoagies and crafts are present, including those provided by the foodsellers from the Amish countryside. As a prominent Philly establishment, it's strategically placed right by next to the Convention Center and Chinatown, and a short walk away from the City Hall. A bit crowded but fun to visit in the morning and brunch hours.
I get the appeal - this place is awesome! Just about every type of food with delectable Dutch-Amish shops!
This is a must visit site when your in the Philadelphia area, they have the market, small famers and vendors to visit as well as many small places to enjoy lunch and good amish supplies.
Have you had their cake!? The slices are as big as a whole cake! Looking to impress someone on their bday with just one piece go here the funfetti is

It's noisy, crowded, hard to park at, and worth enduring all the inconveniences as there is just so much awesome to choose from!  Sure, it's touristy, but unlike most things geared towards out of towers, this place is so unique and authentic, it's a must visit.  If you can't find something here to enjoy, you're likely unappeasable.

This place makes me miss philly !  You really experience the culture and food philly has to offer by walking around the market and exploring all the different stores .   This should be your first destination upon arrival and after go say hello to rocky he's not far !

My new favorite place! Wish we lived closer!!
So many to choose from; definitely something for everybody! 
Bring cash as some places don't take cards- 
We also parked in the garage across the street and there's a discount if you have your card validated from one of the stores.

I love Reading Terminal market because there are so many options in one place. It's a great convenience for me and I enjoy everything I ever purchased from the multiple shops and stores. Certain hours are better to go than others.

Cute market in a central location. It's not as cool as Seattle's Pike's Place but it's probably on par with LA's Grand Central Market.

We sampled food from a few food stalls and I enjoyed walking through the market. Definitely a fun place to check out.

A fun place to explore. This place has everything from fresh produces to cookies chocolate ice cream and more.  Park across the parking deck and bring your ticket with you and ask for a validation with any purchase for 10$ or more and your two hours parking is only cost you $5 and with out the validation cost 16$ for an hour.

I love this place. So many options. It has as many positives as it does negative. If you drive, just plan to park. Avoid Saturdays and Sundays if you can. Prepare for the amish to be closed whenever they want. BUT man, molly malloys, iovines, the fresh smoothie place, millers twists, flying monkey, all are worth the time and effort!

This is my second visit to this great city and I can't believe I missed the Reading Terminal Market on my first visit. This is a must visit - right after the liberty bell.  OK - for get the bell come here first.  This place is crammed with food venders serving some of the best food ever. I stopped at Hershel's East Side for a pastrami Rubin  -  there must have been a pound of meat on this baby.  So good, I should have a stopped but I didn't.  Next stop will be Di Niks for the Italian pork sandwich.  I'll be back for that.  My wife said and I quote "we should move here".  Are you  kidding me, I'm a New Yorker by birth ... That would be sacrilege ... But I'll be back for the food.

I simply cannot describe the magic that is Reading Terminal Market. If you are visiting Philadelphia, do not miss this quintessential, bustling locale. Whatever you seek can be found beneath the roof of this 19th century train station packed from wall to wall with restaurants and vendors. What's best is to wander the aisles until something unexpected catches your eye. I especially recommend Kevin Parker's Soul Food and Hershel's East Side Deli. Do not miss this place.

I'm originally from Philly, and this was always my go to brunch spot. Now whenever I visit home I make sure I grab brunch here. Hands down some of the best brunch I've had, very low key vibes with great service. This is one restaurant where I never feel rushed (and I can spend 4 hours brunchin') and every server I've had has been great and super chill! Try the crab skillet (amazing!) and get the biscuit (totally worth it). Can't wait to go back during my next visit to Philly!

A plethora of food items to choose from in this food hall. You can have your dinner and dessert all in one place which I find very convenient. It's a very big touristy place to go to (which a tourist like me) had a good time at. I didn't get to try one of the vendors which had 'worlds oldest ice cream' but I'll make sure to go back and try it one day.

After reading reviews, i had more expectations on the rolls.But i was very much disappointed after trying their pepper chicken roll.

We ordered chicken biryani and pepper chicken roll. Roll was just ok, not great. Not much taste and the outer layer is very soft, Chicken lacks flavor too.Coming to Chicken biryani, quantity is very less for 10$. It is just like some chicken curry mixed with rice, not a typical biryani.

Food: 3
Ambience: 3

Everything you could imagine is here! Affordable prices for great meals from different places around the world, unfortunately I always miss the Amish area, because I always go on Sundays. I highly recommend to bring cash; not all the places receive credit cards.

Great place for lunch. 5 minute walk from city hall and just 10 min from China town. Whatever you're looking for they have it, everything from Indian, Chinese, Mexican, Greek to Southern food.

They also have great produce, meat and specialty  food stands. Whether your a local a tourist, this is definitely a spot to check out.
The Reading Terminal never disappoints! There are so many delicious options, you can't go wrong. However, I would avoid at all costs on Saturday and Sunday afternoons as it gets very packed.

Wow this place is amazing!!  If you visit Philly this place is a must.  The variety and quality of food will blow your mind. My wife and I have visited two day in a row and will probably go back tomorrow:)
Feels so healthy and tastes so delicious! The cilantro sauce and the black bean sauce are both great.

I stopped by The Industry this weekend with my 10 month old and the rest of the family. They were very accommodating with my little one and we sat outside and ate. I had  fried chicken and waffles, but wasn't aware that it was super spicy regardless the food was good and I will return to try out other things on the menu. Oh yeah I also had the Mac N Cheese with kimchi definitely worth a try and my little one loved it too.

It's a Philly favorite & a Must stop for visitors to the area.  Featuring many local Philly favorite foods, a variety of restaurants and a few small gift shops.  Also a great fresh produce spot.  DiNics pork is a must as is a Termini Bros Cannoli.

One of my favorite places in the city. Beiler's donuts are excellent and even if the line is long, it moves fast. I also love Dinic's for the roast pork sandwhich, always worth the trip. In general, one of the best places in the city to get a great lunch. Only downside is on the weekends it is crowded, but I've always found it was worth dealing with the crowd
Love Reading Terminal Market for lunch. A must try spot when in Philadelphia. There is something to munch on for everyone and they have an excellent farmers' market too.
Make sure you get some chocolate chip cookies when they are HOT and don't forget the candy shop right next to it.  The cookies are right at the front door. The best ever!

Wicked cool!
What can I say that other reviewers have not?

This wonderful foodie landmark offers more options for a meal, grocery, and knick knacks than most small towns! Am I exaggerating? Come here and find out!

The market may be crowded, as I came here during lunchtime on a Sunday, but the bustle can be perceived to augment the atmospheric energy and excitement. 

I will be sure to come back on a Saturday instead, as more food vendors (particularly in the Pennsylvania Dutch section) are open. I have yet to find out what this "Apple Dumpling" is all about! ..Till next time - 5 stars!

I love public markets and so Reading Terminal Market was a must-do on my visit to Philadelphia. RTM is a huge public market with a lot of vendors - there are an overwhelming amount of options! From fresh produce, to seafood, to meat, to cheese, you can get almost anything here! You can get pastries, coffee, tea, ice cream,  Pennsylvania Dutch, Chinese, Thai, Mexican, Cajun, burgers, cheesesteaks, and more! There's even an oyster bar inside. Great variety! 

Stopped in at lunchtime on a weekday and the place was just packed with people everywhere. No surprise that it's a popular stop for locals and tourists to get some lunch. The line at Beiler's Donuts was the longest, as was the line for Hershel's East Side Deli. There are communal seating areas, but at lunchtime the tables were filled. I came back the next day early in the morning and while not everything was open, there were definitely less people and less chaotic. 

What I was most interested in was the Pennsylvania Dutch businesses. There's a sign by the Dutch Eating Place that says the hours for the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants being Tuesday or Wednesday through Saturday, closing up at 3PM on Tuesdays and Wednesdays and closing up at 5PM Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays. But I was there on a Monday and Beiler's was definitely in operation, though Dutch Eating Place was closed. Aside from Beiler's and the Dutch Eating Place, there's also Miller Twist that has soft pretzels and ice cream, and Riehl's which has cheeses, and Smuckers which supposedly is famous for their pot roast sandwiches. Other Pennsylvania Dutch vendors sell crafts and jams and honey. I returned the following day on a Tuesday to eat at Dutch Eating Place (separate review). 

Overall, RTM is a fun place to visit and a great option if you're not sure what you want to eat - there's bound to be something you're craving if you walk around long enough. I tried tea from the Tea Leaf, tea from Old City Coffee, ice cream from Bassetts, jambalaya from Beck's Cajun Cafe, a donut from Beiler's, a soft pretzel from Miller's Twist, and breakfast from Dutch Eating Place. Wish I stayed in Philly longer, so I could've tried even more stuff!
Definitely a fun place to visit. And a great place to keep returning to. So many good choices for food. Lots of bustle and energy.
This place is simply amazing! Everytime iam here isee something new. Such a magical place.

The food is good!! Atmosphere very friendly so you don't have to worry about not be from the neighborhood, They are very welcoming . The cookies for dessert are AMAZING freshly made! Clean environment and great prices I will be coming back!

So So.

This is a really big food court.   If you enjoy exploring a food court with better than average offerings this is it.  My style for the same price is a restaurant to be taken care of.   There are some places in here that need some help with quality.   Hershel's East was good.  The Dutch place needed improvement.  

For me, overall a waste of time and energy when there are better places around for a nice meal at the same price.

This place is so amazing. I'd you have someone visiting this should be at the top of the list for Philly attractions. 

My favorite is the Reuben from Hershel's. Holy cow.

The donut shop is also out of this world. Im not a donut person at all but was blown away by the Amish bakers

Every time we have out of town guests, we take them here. There is nothing else like it! The produce is also incredibly affordable that we tend to do our shopping here as well. Special and unique place. Beware though...it gets very crowded and hard to navigate through the aisles.

I love this place!  The dutch pickle place in the far corner makes the best spicy pickles.  The Dutch Eating Place is a great for breakfast, and the Turkey sandwich stand makes a turkey, cranberry, and stuffing sandwich (Thanksgiving on a roll, to Jersey-ites) that is amazing.  There are crafts, and lots of knick-knacks to browse.  If you're a "cheese-head", like I am, stop at Downtown Cheese.

I really liked this place. I had an appointment nearby but had some time to kill, so I stopped in for a breakfast sandwich and cup of coffee. The coffee was good, the service was fast, and the egg & cheddar sandwich was warm and fresh (made-to-order). There was plenty of seating available, and I enjoyed the eclectic collection of things hanging on the walls and varied music that played over the speakers. I sat here and read/ate/drank for quite a while (maybe 45 min) and was left alone to enjoy.

Best part- my breakfast was under $4, which is cheap for a convenient location in the city.

The market is so fun! I was in Philadelphia working at a conference and we went to the market for lunches and sometimes to pick up a snack or dinner on the way back to the hotel. Crazy busy and crowded, but huge variety. Everything I tried was delish.

Have lived in Philly for 4 years and only just visited Reading Terminal Market yesterday. I was missing out! I've been to similar markets in Boston, DC, and in my most recent visits to Barcelona and Madrid and RTM is just as awesome and its right in my backyard!

Boyfriend and I went in on a Saturday and though it was bustling with activity it wasn't too difficult to meander our way through and find a table once we chose our respective dishes. (I picked Meltkraft (?) he chose a crepe place). The number of options was great as 1. we can never agree on where to eat because we both always want different items, this satisfied us, and 2. you can go here 100 times and not get the same thing twice. So many different options of food and goods. The employees were great with helping us find something we would like, even when they didn't work for that other booth -- it has a great community feel. I suggest asking the other workers what they recommend if you're looking for the best [insert delicious food here] as they work and eat there daily so they have some great recommendations. 

I will definitely be returning to RTM in the future, though they do close early, so perhaps only on the weekends!

Reading Terminal Market... what can I say. One of Philadelphia's finest landmarks and tourist attractions (rightfully so), it really can take up an entire day to go, walk around, people watch, and take in the sights and smells of a vibrant Philly foodie culture. It's a really hard place to describe - one really needs to go and spend an hour or two just walking around in order to really take it all in.

From Lancaster farmers to beeswax candles to wineries, this place has it all. Some of my highlights include: Bee Natural, The Original Turkey, and the Famous 4th Street Cookie Company, amongst others.

But in any case, whether you're looking to go buy some fresh produce or even go for a leisurely stroll, the RTM experience is one that you're surely not going to forget that easily.

Let it be known first off that is extremely difficult to review an entire market with countless shops and stores, but I will do my best!

Overall, this market is absolutely phenomenal. If you are looking for an experience that is revolutionary and one of Philadelphia's best attractions, than look no further! Inside of this wonderland, you will find plenty of shops that sell perishable items, meats, cheeses, candy, breakfast/lunch/dinner, and many more. One of my favorite things to do is to check out of the different venues that sell cookbooks and foreign spices and herbs to make your own meal.

After reading the reviews, i'm going to to disagree with some and say that the Reading Terminal Market is nothing like Faneuil Hall in Boston, OR Chelsea market in NYC.  Those spots, while fun, were established as top dollar tourist destinations.  
The RTM, on the other hand, has an authenticity that I have not observed in these other places.  Under one, very crowded roof, you have it all.  Any and all cuisines you can imagine as well as local farmers, bakers, cheesemongers, butchers and restaurateurs working side by side.  
There is no corporate feel and no "anchor" establishments.  All price points are represented.  You can walk in with $1 and leave with a warm pretzel.  It is crowded and noisy, but it is real, and clearly a market for the people of Philadelphia.

As someone who lives in the suburbs, I used to come here just for lunch while in the city. Now that I work nearby, I do a lot of my regular grocery shopping here. I am never disappointed by the freshness or quality of the products I buy. Iovine's produce is a cheap and plentiful stop for all your fruits, veggies, and herbs. If you want the best sausage, go to Martin's.  Riehl's cheese is the best. I especially enjoy when I know that I am going to have company, so I have a reason to get a nice cake at Termini Bros or a dozen cookies from 4th Street Cookie Co. or the PA General Store. 
For lunch though, I enjoy Beck's Cajun jambalaya, pierogies from Franks A Lot, or chicken tikka masala from Nanee's Kitchen. No day is complete without an ice cream from Bassett's or donut from Beiler's Bakery.
I love that I always find something new here.
Pro Tip: Go on a weekday in the morning, or just before they close. Avoid during the Flower Show.
Their milkshakes and waffle fries makes it all worth it alone.  Other food is decent,too.
Always crowded. But l have to stop in anytime I'm in the area. They have everything !

If you like to eat and sample different things, you need to check this place out.  It's open everyday starting at 8am.  Some of my favorite spots are Hershel's deli for the pastrami sandwich, salmon curry at Little Thai Market, breakfast with freshly squeezed OJ at Dutch eating place, Beiler's donuts, pretzels at Miller's twist.  You can easily spend a couple hours just walking and eating here so worth a visit.

Love this place, I would eat here everyday If I could. So much variety in this market you can enjoy eating virtually every type of cuisine you can think off. Also you can purchase  fresh produce, dairy products, exotic meats and seafood, freshly cut flowers and much more.

If you're looking for a variety of foods prepared fresh daily for a reasonable price, look no further!! Gems found in this market whether it is eating brunch/lunch/dinner, buying fresh seafood, meats, coffee, flowers, ect., or grabbing some amazing desserts!
so charming & authentic...must stop on any Philly visit. I'm so glad we're preserving old world gems like this & Pike Place Market in Seattle...

Reading Terminal Market should definitely be on your to-do list if you're visiting Philly!  Everything you can think of is here...all different kinds of food from sandwiches to meat to sushi to pasta to crepes to everything!! Very good candy shops too!!

I bring all my out-of-towners here. I (we) love it every time. It's packed but it's definitely worth going. Plus they deliver on instacart !!!

Beiler's has the best donuts I've ever had and the oysters at the Oyster Bar are always fresh.

My boyfriend was raving about this place and we finally took the trip to Philadelphia and check this place out. It was a food haven for foodies. I was overwhelmed with all the options of deliciousness. We had a roasted pork sandwich with provolone and broccoli rabe which was just amazing and a burger with roasted mushroom, onion in the delicious sauce with a side of lobster macaroni and cheese. So amazing. Don't forget to stop and get some chocolate covered Oreos and chocolate covered strawberries.

One of my favorite places to shop. I get my fresh vegetables from Iovine. Meats from  Martin's(spicy Italian chicken sausage is the best!)  I try new cheeses at Valley Sheppard. Spices from the Head Nut. Local raw honey at Bee Natural and I almost always stop by  Nanee's Kitchen for dinner on the way out the door.

mm, this is one of my favorite places in the city! Every time I go I love to stop at The Dutch Eating Place and enjoy a hot turkey sandwich or the chicken pot pie (if you're expecting a crust, the pie isn't for you...it's more of a delicious Chicken and Dumplings, and it is absolutely core-warming) The portions her are huge, and I highly recommend their fries. As a fry lover they are some of the best I've ever eaten.

Whenever we're done we like to go get a cone of Amish ice cream and wander around looking at our favorite shops: The spice shop, the candy store that has chocolate toffee pretzels (best in the world!!), and the honey store to get beeswax candles or honey sticks. It's also very nice to look at the flowers and before we leave to grab a slice of cake from the bakery next to the Dutch Eating Place.

By the time we roll out of here (literally, by this point we've gorged ourselves SOO much walking is no longer an option) we've had a great time that was totally worth the price.

Love this place, heaven for me. 

I really enjoy visiting farmers market and the like. So this place did not disappoint. I could browse forever in places like these. A variety of eateries: Cajun, Italian pull pork and even sushi. Along with fresh produce stands, butcher shops, and your fish monger. The whole market is enclose inside a building. That's definitely a good thing during the winter. I say this place is better than Seattle's Pike Place. It gets packed on the weekends. So be prepared for long lines at certain places like Tommy DiNic's. 

Crowded and touristy may be. But I think this place is awesome. Worth going.

Once of my favorite places in the world! It has such a great vibe and the combination of all the great lunch places with all the great produce and fish. Was a longtime fan of the 12th Street Cantina -- how more partial to Beck's Cajun. Love the flower place as well.
This place is great! A must-see tourist destination. Great food inside like Dinic's and their pretzels were awesome!

Love it so much - great for every day, great to take guests for a BIG slice of Philly culture, and one of the only places I can reliably find (fresh when in season) Halibut - being from So. California, this is a favorite fish. I'm not a fan and have not adopted the E. Coast Talapia - yuck! Anyway, Reading Market has been and continues to be a favorite of locals and tourists alike for a reason - because its awesome.
Absolutely amazing! Crowded but worth it! You can find every type of food you could ever imagine.
Good variety. Great produce.  Love the salad bar at Tootsie's.
So fun! Everything I've ever had has been delicious. Little busy esp. on weekends but it's worth it.

This is a nice place and is famous for their Cathedrals I ate a roll and that was really cheap on pocket and green taste so I will definitely recommend you to just eat any of the Roll which one cost more than $5 and you will be really delighted
Awesome spot lots to choose from vegetarian philly cheese steak was awesome. Deserts and options both vegetarian or vegan available at several vendors
Great food, great people, decent amount of seating. If you're in Philadelphia you MUST check this place out.

I have been going to the Reading Terminal Market for at least 25 years.   The market has changed over the year with more vendors and various upgrades but the quality of every vendor and every selection has always been above 100%.   This place has it all.  From fresh meats and vegetables to fresh food foods that you can't believe.   

You must go hungry or won't appreciate all it has to offer.  
The roast pork is awesome, the Amish fresh cooked chickens and pretzels are to die for.   The fresh meats are like my local South Philly Butcher.  

I grew up in this neighborhood and the Reading
terminals was always a treat to go and shop.  From candy to unusual meats, there is a lot to choose. 
Highly recommend.

LOVE this place. There is something for every palate here. Easy to reach via subway or car and worth getting to. A delicious break from sight-seeing. You can grab and go or take advantage of limited seating. Always my last stop before leaving town to avoid the pain of searching for road food.
Reading Terminal has a great selection and has great prices, however it is always crowded - so be prepared.

During my visit I went to:
Beiler's
Flying Monkey
Dutch Eating Place
Miller's Twist
Termini Bros
...and I walked through frequently

All I can say that hasn't been said is that it is without a doubt the best market of its kind that I've yet to visit.  While not as eclectic as the San Francisco Ferry Market and not as large as Baltimore's Lexington Market it is the kind of place where there is something for everyone - down home, organic, simple, artisan, vegetarian, carnivore, local, or tourist.

Um, how do I even begin? This place is AMAZING.

Firstly - being a CA native, I was in dire need of fresh produce. TJ's? Nope. Superfresh and Whole Foods? Meh. Luckily, someone mentioned Reading Terminal Market as a cool spot to get all my grocery shopping done while grabbing some ready-made eats.

The place can be a little overwhelming/crowded, but just take your time and explore the diff stands. Now that I'm getting more "domesticated," I def love walking around and checking out the various meat/seafood/produce/bread stands. Seafood is the best quality/price I've seen in the area, and produce is ridics cheap.

Will def need to try DiNic's, the Reuben stand and many other spots but this is my go-to shopping spot moving forward.

Quick tip: Student discounts at nearly all of the stands on Sun and Wed!
PHENOMENAL!!! You can spend days in there. Buy the best and fresh products. Eat delicious EVERYTHING.
Great place to eat and such diverse cultural experiences. No way you don't.love this place. Try a Amish breakfast

LOVE THIS PLACE. Doesn't matter if you're a tourist or a local. I've come by here to get produce and lunch on several different occasions. I take the trolley into town from University City and shop. So many great places to grab food from. You will get a little lost inside, but there are maps to guide you. I had Nanee's and Kamal's and they were great. Pretty low prices as well. Bought fruits and vegetables from the produce shops and they were fresh.

This place is overwhelming but there is no shortage of choices for dining options.  Anyone can find something to eat here.  I had a Thanksgiving dinner sandwich, which was exactly what it says - Thanksgiving dinner on a sandwich, complete with stuffing, mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, and turkey.  It was delicious though too much bread and not enough potatoes.  My wife had a cheesesteak from Carmen's.  The meat was very dry and had no flavor.  Beyond dining options, there are several shops selling anything from soaps to olive oil to wool goods.  It is easy to get lost here and you could honestly spend a couple of hours wandering from stall to stall.  Overall, an excellent Philly experience.

Cold food. The lady who was putting the order together (I didn't get her name) I'm assuming it's the same lady another Yelp member called her out was very rude not only to myself, but everyone in line I heard her cross paths with. The gentleman behind the counter as the cashier (didn't get his name either) was very rude as well. I even seen him grab the card out of the guys hand (customer) in front of me without even asking for payment. The guy in front of me said thank you and goodbye to the guy behind the counter and he didn't say anything in return. Horrible customer service and cold food.

YARTMR
(Yet Another Reading Terminal Market Review)

I don't get here as much as I used to.  Sure I ride the train back into philly into market east everyday but by the time I arrive, all the shops are closed.  I used to live about 6 blocks away and this place was like my home away from home.  Sure it's touristy but I didn't care.  I could get meat, fish, produce, chocolate, bread, flowers, spices, a cup of coffee and a cookie all in one place.  

Like other Philadelphia institutions, this place is a real gem.  It's a good place to shop every week.  It's a good place to visit for a one off time.  Everything is fresh and it's all got a philly attitude to it.  I believe they have cooking demonstrations on Saturdays (sometimes)

It's fun to be a tourist every now and again.

A must visit stop in Philadelphia for tourists and even locals. This terminal has numerous of very popular shops that have amazing food. Most good places have a long line but they are worth it. The place is surprisingly very clean and has a lot of unique shops and fresh produce. You won't be disappointed!
One of the best indoor markets around. You can easily get lost in the place - but you loosing a friend is gaining random treasures.

Listen, anything and everything you could ever want is to be found here!
Food beyond the mind's eye! Galore!
Exotic fruits and veggies as well as the norm.
Cheeses and meats of all kind. Beverages, jams, sandwiches, candies, handmade household items, and more.

THIS PLACE IS AMAZING!!! I loved being a tourist here, and just walking around discovering all the places inside. Foodie heaven! Loved the Amish bakeries, freshly mad donuts and cookies, and sandwiches. Wish I lived close so I could do my weekly shopping here! 

It is literally everything you could want in an indoor market. I went there 2 days in a row and left still feeling like I needed at least a few more days to experience more meals. Only tried it for lunch, and wish we had tried breakfast too!

A must visit for out of town guests and many options to pick from!  Everything you could possibly want to try under one roof.  Termini Bakery and Beiler's donuts for desert are a must try!  Beware on Saturday and Sundays, lines are long, the space is crowded, and seating is limited.  Bring cash as many vendors do not take credit cards.

What a gem of a place. Reading Terminal Market is such a fun and valuable resource. This is a great place to grab lunch or people watch, and an amazing place to get local, organic produce, dairy, and eggs. The L. Halteman Family's Tub Butter is heaven on earth.

Some places can be hit or miss, but the good ones make up for it. Beiler's (donuts), Bassett's (ice cream), Hunger Burger, and the Thai stand with the $7.50 salmon (toward the back) are all amazing. Honestly, the donuts are the best I've had anywhere and the salmon is huge. Great place to eat and explore!

Just a quick update...wife and I stopped by again to have another burger...and it was just as good as the last one...tasty and well cooked...fries were nice and crispy.  Nothing like consistency to keep the diners coming back.  Black bean and pork soup was very good also...I can see this place being our go to joint for the burger jones.

Wonderful experience at Masala kitchen! A different twist than a typically served Indian cuisine. I like their concept to serve Indian street food on the street of Philly downtown. I had paneer tikka and healthy sprout Kati roll both are really delicious. Specially sprout well cooked with different veggies like beet root & cabbage, like the green chutney flavorfull (not watery). Nice, funky small gem in philly downtown. Definitely be back and recommended!!

Reading Terminal is the best thing that has ever happened to mankind, aside from the discovery of fire, the wheel, and Emma Watson.  If you like putting food into your body, Reading Terminal is ground zero for stuffing your face full of delicious treats.  I've lived here for years, I go there not uncommonly, and I still find it to be an emotional experience to watch pastrami and corned beef being cut at Hershel's or watching sandwiches get put together at DiNic's.  You could eat at Reading for every meal for a month, start over again, and not get tired of the place.  From Wednesay through Saturday you also have the extra company of the Amish, who during that week have managed to bake like a million pies, cakes, and fruit breads with frosting on them.  FROSTING ON THEM.  ARE YOU KIDDING ME!?!?
