I CAN'T GO ON I'M GETTING TOO EMOTIONAL

This is what every city should have. This market has a great selection of all types of foods. It's fun and engaging. Prices are also below what one usually pays at grocery stores. It's worth a trip for shopping or to just look and have a coffee or snack. Go Philly

What an awesome place!

Me and my wife just stopped here for about 30 minutes before we went to an appointment and we were amazed with how much food there was to pick from. We had some of the Rotisserie chicken from I think Dienner's and it was awesome. There is Greek food, Halal food, burgers, bakery, bread and bagels, ribs, fudge, chocolate, ice cream, etc. It is a cool place to check out with your spouse or to take your kids. Your looking at needing about 2 hours to check out the place and all the cool things they have there. Parking can be a challenge though and definitely avoid this place around lunch time.

I see where people are coming from, calling it a tourist trap, but I don't think that's completely accurate as I know many locals including myself who enjoy stopping by. At times it can get overwhelmingly crowded with people squeezing and shoving in the narrower halls, so I try to come at off times. 

It's like LA's Grand Central Market, a massive building filled with all kinds of vendors. There's fresh produce, every cuisine ranging from Indian to Cajun, kitchenware, spices, butchers, and bakeries. Now that's not to say that all of the vendors are good. Honestly, I've found the food to be pretty hit or miss, and the vast majority to be average. Maybe I'm missing the good places, but I still like this place for its vibe even if not for its food.
A cool place to bring guests - but a little overwhelming, personally.  They do have a little bit of everything as far as food variety goes - and the Dutch food is delish!

I love food markets and food stalls, so it's no wonder I love this place. The last time I was in Philly, Mr. Joy and I visited RTM every single day, sometimes, multiple times a day.
I appreciate that the market is set up like a grid. Navigating can be a little confusing if you've never been here, but you're sure to find something good to munch on, especially in the baked goods category.

Bassett's Ice Cream - oldest ice cream shop
Beiler's Doughnuts - freshly baked doughnuts & delicious fritters
Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. - classic cookies
Meltkraft - cheesiest grilled cheese sandwiches
Miller's Twist - freshly baked pretzels, and pretzel rolls
Tommy DiNic's - roast pork sandwiches
Termini Bros - great cannolis

What should I try next?

Convenient location?  Check!
Large number of selections?  Check!
Indoors so you won't freeze in winter?  Check!
Has obscure amuzing items?  Check!
Affordable prices?  Check!

This may be considered blasphemy, but I think it's better than Seattle's Pike Place.  Oh and this is total blasphemy, but I think it IS better than San Francisco's Ferry Building Farmer's Market.  Okay maybe not.  But if those three markets exist in any one city, I think I would definitely go to Reading a lot more frequently than the other two.

Whenever I am alone in a town other than my own, I like to disappear in obscurity.  I like to blend in with the locals crowd and be as inconspicuous as I possibly can.  This place definitely allows that.  I could walk around for hours and still discover new things.  

I tried one of the Chinese food place, but it was awful.  I can't say for all of the Chinese food in there, but I think if you really want some you should just go to Chinatown a few blocks away.  The Amish places are definitely God-send.  Very, very good hot apple dumplings.  Iovine produce is great because they provided me with reasonably priced healthy snacks and fruits. The fresh juice place is pretty awesome.  And don't forget Old City Coffee, I love the homey feel to it.

I only wish this place opens past 6pm...  Then it would be truly truly mah-velous!

Our favorite Pennsport bar and restaurant!     There are plenty of great bar food staples complimented by eclectic specials.   There are also plenty of twists on old standbys like the kimchee tater tots.   The servers are always friendly, funny and welcoming.   The service is fast.   And the bartenders are not only fun to talk to, but they are really skilled.   They know their beer really well and go the extra mile to make cocktails the way they should be made.    Always a great experience and in the many times we have gone, have never left disappointed with a single thing.

This is my happy place!!! What's not to love? The absolute BEST food...whatever it is you're in the mood for, its here & it's amazing!!!! I'm seriously wondering if the vendors are required to pass a taste test to be permitted in this place

On Sunday morning, most places are not open.  We went to Down Home Diner for breakfast.  It turned out to be just OK.  But with so many more places to visit and try, I will definitely visit again the next time.
Great food and selection. The reasons for a 3-star rating are the overly expensive parking and the crowds! Wow, too crowded for my taste. Will not return any time soon.

I wasn't really blown away by Potbellys.  To begin with, I felt that there menu was rather basic.  My girlfriend is a vegetarian and there was only one sandwich that didn't include meat.  She ended up getting a chickpea salad and I got a ham and cheese sub.  I was disappointed by the lack of options for topping on the sandwich.  They didn't even have honey mustard or vinegar!  Both the sandwich and the salad were tasty but nothing really spectacular.  I felt that both were overpriced given the quantity and quality of food.

On the plus side, the girl at the front was extremely friendly.  She felt bad that they didn't have the vegetable soup that was advertised so she gave us a free cookie.  She was very kind and polite.  The place itself was clean but kind of randomly decorated.

Overall I don't think I'll be going back to Potbelly.  it's just not worth the money!

Great atmosphere, every ethnic food you can think of, which enables you to taste a small portion before you head to a local ethnic restaurant and are overwhelmed by the various selections. I'm not a rib person, but the small Amish rib joint has the best beef/pork ribs I've ever had. Whenever we have visitors from another city or country for that matter, always agree this place has the epitome when it comes to ribs. In fact, we had family in from PR and they loved so much, they took home 2 racks!!

This place reminded me a lot of Grand Central Terminal in NYC but bigger. Every stall looked enticing from food to books to kitchen accessories. Unfortunately we went right after lunch so we weren't hungry. Since we went on a Sunday, we didn't get to check out the Dutch Eating Place. We were also thinking of picking up a sandwich at DiNic's for later but the line was pretty long and we weren't feeling it so next time for sure! Overall, I love the crowd and culture.

Lots of options to customize whatever you get.  It's basically eating an experiment because sometimes they're heavy on the portions and other times they just do whatever.  Coming in after 8pm there's usually a long line and the wait for your food could range from 15 - 20 mins depending on how busy it could be.
I like a lot of the things here but hate being surrounded by disoriented families from the suburbs.

This place has a mecca of food. Some places are better than others, but I love the plethora of options here. you can get Roast Pork/Brisket at DiNics, Roasted and Carved Turkey like Thanksgiving, Chinese Food, Thai, Fried Chicken, Burgers, Sushi, Bassett's Ice Cream, Donuts and bakery items by the Pennsylvania Dutch and fresh produce as well!

It's great to try a bunch of different places each time. The prices are also incredibly reasonable too. Just avoid coming during peak times as it can be very crowded and the lines get long.

I can't believe I'm writing a review for Chik Fil A but I have to say, this particular location (near the IKEA in S. Phila) was amazing.  I've never gone to one before, so I was derping and hemming and hawing looking at the menu and the lady behind the counter was really nice and patient.  Then, while I was eating, the manager came around to each table, asking everyone if everything was OK.  I saw him talking to a family, and then he was clearing off the table for them because they were busy with their kid!  Later the assistant mgr (I assume) went around and did the rounds too. Never seen anything like it in a fast food place.  The sandwiches were really superior!  I am not affiliated with this franchise or company or whatever but whoever runs this place has got their stuff together, very impressive.

The equivalent of walking down fifth avenue for my wife. Or is it park avenue. Whichever one it is with all the ships in nyc. 
This place is a foodies paradise. Especially go for the Amish bakeries along the north and northwestern parts of the market. Beilers bakery and adjacent Amish stores are the gems of this place. But they're only open certain days of the week so check beforehand. 
Other shops are good to and you can certainly spend half a day in here without exploring everything. 
There are also non food markets here. 
Tourists flock here by the droves so be prepared. But well worth it!
Fresh food and grocery, some nice fun little things too. A bit expensive, but it's a fun place to go.

The  terminal
Is clean, friendly, welcoming and I love coming here for lunch.  Park across the the street in the garage and get your parking ticket stamped and it's only $5.  Not bad at all

My ultimate favorite place in Philly! This place has everything in one location. I love that I can eat all types of foods. 

This place is always packed weekday or weekend! But it's worth the experience. 

Here is a quick list of some of my favorite stops:
Bassetts ice cream
Beiler's donuts
Dinic's
Sang Kee Peking Duck

Truly a hustling, bustling foodie heaven! A must-see if you are visiting Philly. I really love the energy and overall vibe here. With that said, there are so many promising eateries with crazy long lines, it's easy to get overwhelmed when you walk in. 

Best method is to 1) come with equally eager companions 2) divide and conquer. 

Have your friends/family stand in different lines and buy a little bit of something from multiple places so that you can maximize the foods you try :) Don't forget to bring cash!

There is a HUGE variety of food and it's often really hard to choose what to eat because there is choice overload. I tend to get super lost every time I visit and end up just ordering at the same place every time (Little Thai Market for pad thai!!!). A lot of places are cash only and there isn't a lot of seating if you're with a group of more than 2/3 people.

wit..witout ?   save yourself  ,  get here for the best PORK or BEEF sandwiches  
sweet or hot peppers , shaved & aged Provolone  a great way to power thru lunch .
Superb & consistent

Seriously, what is not to love about this place?! You can get anything and everything you want. Stop in for lunch, sity down or grab it and run back to work. Even relax with a drink at Molly's. And then dessert on your way out.

My favs: DiNic's roast pork and beef, Hershel's, Terminis, Bassett's, Hatville deli, Beiler's..

Open everyday, year round. A MUST stop in for tourists and locals.

I could spend hours walkin through this mega market if it weren't for the hords of people in my way.  But, seriously, this is a great foodie mecca.  Do try the pork sandwich at Dinic's and a fresh filled cannoli from Termini Bros. There are a number of tempting other spots, including fresh pies, fudge stands, ice cream, crepes and lots of other delights.  Try to go with someone else to split the job of hunting a table while the other person stays on line.  While lines may look long, they do move rather quickly.

Don't ignore this foodie landmark - the Market has basically everything - from local fresh produce to ice cream and sandwiches. 
A bit crazy in there, though, so don't expect to have a  ceremonious meal.
Everytime I bring my ass to Philly, to see the fam, I roll by Reading Terminal. I love this place. It be cheap here too!

finally made it to this place!!! my friend and i had a pho date in chinatown and passed by on our ways back to my car...slight detour...but omg i love this place! too bad my friend and i were stuffed because there were so many delicious options. i DID walk out with some great produce for cheap and beautiful handmade soaps during this trip though. i will def be going back soon to try all the other wonderful goodies!!!

parking is tough so def recommend public transportation. it's a fun place tho so have fun!!!

I get it.. it's a busy spot with a whole range of things to catch your eye. I did find however that my experience in there was a bit lackluster. Lunch time is a very very busy thoroughfare so I recommend going a bit before/after to avoid the local traffic.

Came by here just to walk around, having just had brunch nearby.  Place is pretty interesting; LOTS of food options.  Just got some cookies and coffee and walked around seeing the vendors --- the stand with all the different honey was probably the most interesting.

Didnt get a DiNic's sandwich this time, but by all means, if you're here and hungry that should be your first stop.

A must see in Philly. The markets inside are so fun to go through, the food is awesome, such a huge variety. The amish donuts are out of this world, always hot and fresh!! I can't wait to go back, we go once a day while we're visiting, and grab all the fresh fruits and veggies we can before we go back to NYC!

I've been coming to the Reading Terminal since I was a youngbull. Literally anything you have a taste for, you will find here. Now on to my FAVES!!!! The gyro place is so so so soooo good. Get the classic gyro (with lamb and their special sauce) and you will not regret it, I promise. Then, right next to it you have 12th st Cantina, it's a Mexican restaurant. Their servings are huge so make sure you go when you are really hungry, I recommend the nachos with all of the fixings, yum! And I cannot forget about the cookie place (can't remember the name) they have a variety to choose from (they're better than Insomnia Cookies, shhhh lol.) They have Chinese, soul food, seafood, Amish (rotisserie chicken so good), BBQ, vegetarian, literally anything you can think of. YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT!

You haven't experienced Philadelphia if you haven't been to Reading Terminal. It is one of my favorite places in the city. With a myriad of ethnic food options, meat, baked goods, produce, spices and more, Reading Terminal probably has anything and everything you'd ever want food-wise. It is also a great place to people watch, whether from a table in the center of the market or at one of the many food counters. No Yelp review can do this establishment justice. It's a wonderful place and truly Philadelphia. Go if you can make it!

I haven't been here in a while so decided to hit it up for lunch.  Finally today worked out for my friend and I and we walked there a few blocks.  Hitting the terminal at noon... uhhh not a good idea.  It was packed.  I wanted everything but couldn't decide on anything.  I could have spent 20 minutes just cruising around the fresh flower stand.  The place is just great.  It was so crowded though and working with an hour for lunch wasn't an ideal situation for what all of my senses were yearning for -- which was in fact everything.

BUT -- I ended up at this "Everyday Gourmet" stand - mostly because there was no line.  I got the most delicious and perfect lunch for what I was craving (it's a monday, folks, I needed vitamins in the veggie form).  The portabello mushroom topped with this cheese and artichoke concoction that looked like a crab cake was stunningly divine.  Heated up and blessed with some fresh spring mix on the side, I was loving it.  It was so tasty.  Even if I did have to eat it while sitting on a wall outside, I was pleased.

My friend and I are going back but only when we have hours to spend amongst the many stands/smells/tastes.  If you haven't been there in a while, it's definitely worth the trip.

Healthy sprouts roll alert!! So spicy inspite of telling them my spice levels. They should really start paying attention to the spice levels and not serve something just because it is already prepared. Their lassi's are alright and food is quite reasonable.
This place is way cool.  Like the Grand Central Market in LA.  It's directly across from the convention center, so if you're there for a show, definitely plan to lunch here.

The batter is not great for a place that specializes in fried things. My chicken was not crispy and still had the taste of uncooked flour.  

I am still giving them 3 stars because the food was cheap and substantial. I will not return because I prefer the competitor.

It has a variety of food available. One could go there and practically get anything that you may be craving. There is Italian, Mediteranean, Asian, German etc. If you feel like eating healthy there is a sald bar, if you want some coffee they got it, they even have FRESHLY made doughnuts for 0.95 and they are to die for!!! The only bummer is that it closes pretty early so if you're like me and like to take your time in the day be sure that you give yourself enough time to get ready and check out the awesomeness that is Reading Terminal Market.

This is a nice indoor market and a city staple. The best day to go is Saturday, because the Amish merchants are all in. I absolutely love the produce stand in the middle of the store - they have such fantastic deals on produce! There are many cute shops, but mostly pretty expensive. The prevalent odor of seafood is also a bit bothersome.

Man, this place is awesome.  A true Philadelphia must-see.  Amish foods, the oldest ice-creamery in the country, delicious meats and sandwiches, great breads, awesome German food, and plenty of other great finds.  It's in a convenient location for much of the city, too.

There's something for everyone here. I went in on New Year's Eve day, and it was super crowded so we did not stop to eat or drink. It was fun walkong through the isles of delicious foods and patiseries.

Went to brunch her for the first time Saturday morning around 11:30 and got seated right away. The staff was really nice and helpful especially not knowing what specials and drinks were good. I had the passion fruit special mimosa and it was so refreshing and nice drink to start with, then switched to the Ricky Rose and that was strong but tasty. The beer menu was long so a lot of options for beer lovers. As for my meal I had the vege scramble which was so good and a cheddar biscuit. I recommend that! Overall I would come here again to try other drinks and food. Everything looked good and liked the atmosphere.

I love it there!

I mean...I'm from boston and quincy market is the same type of place but this was better...seriously BETTER

Ihad all the foods....ok I tried to have all the foods but I was only there two days
i stayed literally across the street from RM at the Marriott and it was just a short walk over..so over I went

and over
and over
and over

I had so many of the things

foodie paradise in philly....who knew?

Fantastic produce market, flower market, and a slew of amazing food and goods vendors! The Amish and Dutch spots are always spot on with their food and baked goods. Beiler's is amazing - their blueberry fritter is a must have. Can be crazy in there during the tourist times (spring/summer lunchtime and weekends). Downside is the tight schedule that keeps people from utilizing it if they work a 9-5 without much flex in their schedule.
Great place to try different types of food, deserts, or even grocery shopping.
I miss working downtown and being able to go here all the time. Th terminal has such an amazing variety of food you can't find many other places! A must-go.

When in Philly, this is a MUST! I'm so sad that today was my first time coming here after being in Philly multiple times. What was I doing with my life??

This place has everything you could want (and more). And that could even be a problem for people like me, who are bad at making decisions. I think I walked around the whole place twice before deciding on somewhere to eat.

Everything, everywhere looks so good! I honestly can't even remember the place I ended up eating, but I had lobster mac and cheese and a cob kind of salad. SO. GOOD. I also got some coffee from the coffee place near main, front entrance. Also SO GOOD. They had handcrafted syrups!!

I wish I had more time in Philly or lived somewhere close because besides places to eat, the reading terminal also has lots of produce, delis, and other local/homemade things.

I stopped at a couple of the sellers and purchased some candles and honey! 

Really great place. The only bad thing is obviously it does get crowded and I imagine at certain days and times, it's hard to find somewhere to sit so you can eat.

This review is for Wursthaus Schmitz. You can get German sausage, potato salad,  cucumber salad, spatzle, red cabbage which is awesome, sauerkraut (regular or with bacon). All of them are very authentic and can satisfy your craving for real German food. It sell imported German candies such as Kinder. At Christmas time they sell stolen, ginger bread cookies from Germany. They have shelves filled with German grocery items. Don't forget to stop by here when you are at Reading.

It's such a great location, a short walk from our house, we used to go there when it was the Witch. We want to love it, we really really do! I'm sure we will keep trying it, in the short term, because it is the only game in town but that is changing - THANKFULLY! We've been hearing good things about Moonshine but haven't tried it yet and Caffe Valentino is opening a beer garden soon - perhaps the competition will improve our next experience at The Industry.
Pro: atmosphere is lovely without being pretentious
Con: the service is pretentious without being worthy
Pro: really interesting drink selection
Con: food menu is trying a little too hard to be cool and different
Pro: happy hour is fun and reasonably priced
Con: regular menu prices a little too high for what you get 
Con: some of the staff needs to chill with the attitude - we get it - you are in the INDUSTRY but if you want repeat customers you might want to consider a little customer service.

Everything you need to satisfy your hunger in one bustling building. Yes it's crowded and yes it can get hot but boy your taste buds will be enlightened to new levels after you get out of this market! Pulled pork sandwiches, fruit-ades, pickles, whoopie pies, cookies and fudge, oh my! 

Good luck navigating around but getting lost in here is a treat itself. Have fun!!
Sooooooo tasty!! You gotta try it!! It takes awhile to cook, but we carried it back to the hotel, with a stop for take out dumplings in between, and it was soooooooo dang delicious!!!
Love reading terminal. My fave is the ice cream and then next to that getting fresh fruits and veggies from the market.

I like markets and this is one of the better ones I've been to. So much to see and taste and buy and experience. I start early and make a day out of it.  It's a slow stroll not a dash, so bring a gym bag/backpack, your appetite and plan to take your time and take it all in.

Avoid the weekends if you want to browse. Weekends are great if you know exactly what you need.
Weekdays outside of lunchtime are perfect to walk around and enjoy the people and the delicious  food. 
Go with friends and each pick one thing and share. 
Everything I had was excellent. 
Friendly employees. 
Busy. 
Have patience.
I've only been here once, but it seems like a great place for lunch, not to mention the Famous Le Bus Brioche Rolls!:-)  My only complaint is that it's "Cash Only".  Who caries cash anymore???

We were in Philadelphia staying at the Hilton Garden Hotel and asked the front desk if there was someplace good to eat within walking distance.  They recommended the Reading Terminal Market and said it was just around the corner.
We had no idea what this was but took the walk and was pleasantly surprised to find everything inside. Tons of places to eat about anything anyone could want, a market, bakery, etc.....
We chose the deli and opted for the corned beef sandwich.  It was huge and tasted fantastic.  There are so many choices that you could go there every day and have something totally different each day.  
The Reading Terminal Market is certainly a place to stop, especially if you have a group of folks with different tastes.  
It is a bit hectic inside and not easy to maneuver around the place but there is no shortage of interesting things to find inside.
We would definitely go there again the next time we are in Philadelphia.

I am going to get the bad part out of the way immediately because the experience of the Reading Market is absolutely superb. The one exception to that is parking. There is ABSOLUTELY no easy way to pull up and go in inexpensively or conveniently. There is parking across the street in multilevel parking lots which are often full & expensive. Aside from that fact, which I think can be improved on if they put their minds to it, the multitude of food aisles to walk up & down are exciting & delicious. You can go in for a snack or you can eat an entire meal or bring home groceries for a week. It is fresh and creative and flavorful at every single turn. You can grab fresh meats, fresh fish, prepared foods of any desired sort, desserts galore, and many beers & wine in their beer garden. It is a gastro-experience of gargantuan levels. I personally have been going here for over 30 years regularly. There are also many non food vendors such as gifts and crafts of a very nice quality, spice shops, & floral shops. There is a whole 1950s looking counter that goes along the entire front which serves Philly's famous & notable sandwiches & food fare. You have soul food, Italian foods, Mexican, Japanese, Chinese, regular sandwiches, English pub fare, and on and on and on. There is a large seating area whereby you seat yourself. It is relatively maintained but can get a little messy at busier times. You also have bathroom facilities which are monitored and kept up. It is located directly in the center of Philadelphia's downtown and directly across the street from the Philadelphia Convention Center.

Environment: Extremely busy, extremely culturally diverse, this is as good as it gets in regards to culture-shock. They have everything from groceries, to legitimate Amish places, to eating German food.

Service: Most shops are on par with the quickness and attentiveness to the service they provide.

Food: Food here is absolutely amazing. My favorite is finding Beck's Cajun and Beiler's doughnuts. These places offer some excellent homey food at an incredibly affordable price with excellent taste.

Restrooms: It's a public restroom, don't have the highest expectations.

Price: Great price from all the stores here! Nothing here is outrageously expensive and I wouldn't say I've walked in disgusted with the amount I've paid.

This place is amazing. Love a good market in a city, and this place has everything one would need: produce, cheese, meats, pickled stuff, fish, bakery, doughnuts, and much more. There is always something to see and I love the vibe. It is always fun to just walk around and browse the market.

My boyfriend and I stopped by here a couple days ago since this was open late. I liked my MK Chicken Platter. Reminds me a lot of The Halal Guys over in Chinatown. I wouldn't mind coming back and trying their Kati rolls. I also had the mango lassi which was pretty good as well. My boyfriend on the other hand didn't really like what he had which was the chicken and lamb platter. I think really he was looking to enjoy something else for dinner that night which contributed to his not liking the food. And the cashier was pretty nice and very patient as we didn't know what we wanted upon reaching the front of the line.

This is one of Philadelphia best attractions whether you are a local or a tourist. This market is a foodies paradise, filled with many different styles and flavors of cuisine. Even if you do not want to eat it's fun just to look around. However good luck not craving something yummy while your experiencing all those smells in there! 

There is everything from gourmet food, to fast food. Bakeries, cheese shops, seafood shops, dan which shops , dinners, it has everything! 

While this place is made up of many different buissness, i found most places to be on the slightly expensive side. But I guess with all the foot traffic the businesses get paid well. You can fine places in here with decent prices, you just got to look around the whole market first before you actually spend money (that is if you are being money conscience). 

Also know that it gets VERY crowded in there! The isles in between the different restaurants are small, so prepare for traffic and hold on to your kids . Please do not be THAT tourist walking in there with suitcases!

We stayed next door at the hilton for a week for a convention across the street, so I was at this market at least once every day. My first trip on a Saturday afternoon was really overwhelming and I felt like I couldn't stop to check out the food vendors or shops without getting trampled by people who seemed to know exactly what that wanted. There are plenty of food and drink options in the market, so even the pickiest of eaters won't go hungry. My favorites were the metropolitan bakery, the donut shop, old city coffee and the matzo soup served at the deli. Come on a weekday if you can where the lines and crowds are far less intense and you can take your time walking around without a fear of being run over by determined pedestrians.

The steak was literally red. The food was cold. No fried vegetables and my beans didn't taste done at all. They were hard and white in the inside. I did not enjoy my food and regret buying It. Now my stomach hurts! The customer service was that great either!

I loved it! Thinking of all the variety of foods to choose from and all the yummy food staring you in the face makes my heart skip a beat! We walked here from the historic district, and it was a little bit of a hike, especially for my 76 year old mom. If Philly had taxis available like NYC does, we definitely would have taken one for my mom's sake, at least. It was very crowded though and loud. And it was a little hard to find a table to sit at to eat. But all of these cons will not keep me away the next time I find myself in Philly!

The Reading Terminal Market was just okay, for a tourist like me who is used to the likes of Chelsea Market and Grand Central Market. I visited on a Sunday, and a lot of the popular places were closed (even the famous donuts!). The location is fantastic, right by the convention center and next to a bunch of hotels. The place was still completely packed with visitors, crowded and hectic. 

I tried Meltkraft, which was okay.  Would love to come back and try the famous donuts one day!

RUDE AND INCOMPETENT STAFF! So disrespectful! I did NOT have a difficult order at all, and they literally could not comprehend it and then were SO rude to me when I pulled to the window! "Your order is too confusing" and of course everything was wrong. Do not recommend this location!

This has been on my list to try for quite some time, so we decided to grab a few drinks and bites before seeing a movie.

Happy hour wise -- I really like what they have going on here. Let's talk about $3 drafts, $5 select cocktails, $1 oysters, and $1 fried mac and cheese balls ( croquettes) --all of which were delicious!

We also tried the $9 buffalo chicken balls, which were good but fell apart too easily. My partner also got the seitan tandoori with jasmine rice, which was really well seasoned and really enjoyed that dish as well.

The worst dish we got, which I would give 2/5 stars was the gnocchi. I was terribly sad and disappointed. Starting with the positive - the sauce was amazing -- really well seasoned, buttery, cheesy, and the oyster mushrooms complemented it well. The WORST part of the dish was the gnocchi itself. Advertised as " ricotta gnocchi" and I hate to accuse anyone of anything, but I am seriously almost 99% sure that was not ricotta gnocchi, or that if it was -- it was frozen and not fresh. And I'm serious, I eat a lot of gnocchi, I make gnocchi at home -- I am so certain it was potato gnocchi. If it was indeed ricotta, I apologize, but I wouldn't state this if it wasn't so bad or far off. It was not soft, it was not fluffy, it was not gnocchi like you should imagine. It was hard to bite, like you actually have to cut it with a knife. It's not gnocchi that is soft, melt in your mouth, or that you can break apart using your tongue and top of your mouth. This was hard, like literally hard to pick up, rather STAB with your fork . I cut a piece open and took a picture to try to show everyone.. but it's dark and hard to see. 

Overall -- I really enjoyed this bar. Friendly bartender, good service, mostly good food, great happy hour , just bad gnocchi.

One of my favorite places to eat and shop in the City!  The fair trade organic produce market is a favorite of mine, in addition to the Dutch shops, tea and coffee stores.  They seriously have the best produce (greens) I have ever tasted.  They also carry grass fed organic milk in glass bottles at fair prices.

There are so many different places to eat in here than it would be difficult to review them all.  Let's put it this way, do you want vegetarian food?  Fresh farm meat?  Eggs?  Cookies?  Cakes?  Cake baked my mennonites?  Thai food?  Falafel?  Ice Cream?  Spices?  Tea?  Coffee?  A burger?  A cheesesteak?  A vegetarian cheesesteak?  Pretzels?  Candy?  Used books?  A public restroom?  Flowers?  Fresh fruit?  Fresh organic fruit?  Fresh vegetables?  Fresh organic vegetables?  Milk?  Soy milk?  Breakfast?  Lunch?  Dinner?  A convenient place to meet a friend?

I think you get the point...

No matter what want in the food department you can get it here!  And if you have a wide diversity of friends who all like to eat different things then bring them here and they'll all find something.

One note: it tends to be very crowded during the lunch hours, as half of downtown comes here for lunch!

Snap kitchen is the perfect spot for quick grab, heathy food options. They've got everything from protein bars to smoothies to chicken and rice. Everything is refrigerated, but they have an in house microwave available to heat up the more savory food options. 

NOTE: The sign on their front door says this location will close on Nov 16,2017. Apparently they will still be available for delivery and in person at their rittenhouse square location.

The burger is delicious, as are the mussels, sausage, and various salads and soups of the day. With a couple of exceptions, the rest of the dinner menu feels too elaborate or heavy (weird meats and animal parts, very few veggie options) for a neighborhood spot.

I only made it to brunch recently and was blown away by the food we ordered. Shrimp and grits (creamiest grits and perfectly juicy shrimp), bruleed grapefruit, and the Hillbilly Philly (a hot mess of awesome consisting of fried chicken, gravy, and biscuit) were all stellar. And no wait!

My experience with service is always great (though I live nearby and tend to come at off-peak hours). Beer selection is modestly sized, but always rotating through interesting stuff.
Hectic. Everyone freaks out about how great this place is but personally I have always found it chaotic and confusing.

The weekend crowd was bananas, but Monday wasn't so bad. I was pretty bummed that they aren't open for dinner. OK yes, technically speaking, they are open for dinner... but only if you're retired and looking for the early bird special. Who eats that early?!

The Pennsylvania Dutch apple dumplings and sticky buns had me drooling, but I wasn't up for the mosh pit I'd have to wade through to get them. They're only at the market Wednesday-Saturday, so I see what the big deal is.

We ate at Olympic Gyro for lunch and Down Home Diner for breakfast another day. Reading Market gave our food budget a break on that trip to Philly, leaving us extra cash for dinner!

I go to the Terminal quite often, and I love it.  Good eats, good selection, many faves, and always a treat!

For lunch go do:
- Diennier's Rotisserie Chicken: go ahead and get that half chicken or pound of wings.  YUM
- Beck's Cajun: I love it and you will too if you like spicy--and they let you sample!
- 420 (?) Smoothies! (the one next to/near Bassett's Ice Cream and across from a bread place) they have the freshest and best smoothies, and they do wheatgrass and bubble tea tapioca stuff for you affectionados that like that health kick to your drinks
- Thai Food: the grilled salmon is OMG good and a huge serving of salmon; the spring rolls are delish, and the chicken kabobs/skewers are awesome by themselves w the yummy sauce (note: extra sauce is extra, but if you like sauce, do it!)

For dinner treat do:
- Keven Parker's Soul Food Cafe: new and yummy and same owner as Ms. Tootsie's on South Street, but pricey! Treat Yourself to this one
- Thai Food (I get the salmon all the darn time, Yelpitos, it doesn't disappoint me ever!)

For Dessert Treat do:
- The two cookie spots (I don't know their names, so bad, but after 4 pm on the Basset's Ice Cream side you can grab cookies for $1 and the other one is near the wine spot on the Arch Street Side closer to 11th Street) and the "oh i have a sweet tooth" for the Flying Monkey (love everything I have tried there) 
- and Termini's mini bakery ... cheesecake and lemon curd and ... I could go on!

For just a treat do:
- The pretzel twist!  fresh hot Philly pretzels that beat Aunt Anne's in my book

For food shopping:
- The Amish Stands are the best! Fresh bakery! Fresh Cheeses! Wholesome salads and desserts! After 4 pm everything is $2
- The Ok Produce Stand: $1 bags of fresh fruits and veggies
- Godshall's Poultry: the only place I get Turkey Scrapple from
- Seafood: shop around, almost always a sale somewhere for lump crab meat 

For crafts and other stuff:
- I usually shop around, but I love the bee hive for honey.

Philadelphia landmark and treasure!  As a local I get all of my produce and fresh meat here for reasonable prices downtown.  Plus it has so many unique and interesting shops that you can always find something spectacular.  Can get a bit crowded with tourists, but that's its general appeal and why we should be proud to share it.  Beiler's Donuts are UNBELIEVABLE, it is a must stop shop!

We all went to Philly to see the USS John F Kennedy, now retired and rusting in the shipyards... as that's where it all began for my husband over 22 years ago. After checking into the Ritz Carlton (which I HIGHLY recommend), we headed to Reading Terminal Market for some nosh. After reading a few reviews on Dinics, we tried their pork sammies with broccoli rabe... and regretted it almost immediately. Something was just "off" about the taste and smell, and the pork had very little (if any) spices. Nobody finished their sandwich, but wandering about the market was fun, and some of the other food vendors looked like they held great promise. We returned the next morning when my husband had an egg n sausage sandwich and I had a bagel with cream cheese and lox from Hershel's East Side Deli and it was fresh and oh so yummy. Funny story: the young guy behind the counter said "Do you want wudder in a cup or wuhdder in a bottle?" BAHAAAAA... so CUTE! I just LOVE that Philly accent!

I love this place. I spend almost every Saturday at Reading. It's great for grocery shopping. The produce and meat markets have literally anything you could ever one. The food option are incredible as well. Whether you are looking for baked chicken, cajun cafe's, or a great roast beef sandwich...Reading has it ALL.

Just about everything to eat under the sun to eat. Chocolate, bakeries, Mediterranean, delicatessens, burgers, Chinese food, butchers, produce, smoothies..... so much more but amazing. Also has some shops in between. Mueller Chocolate company was mouth watering and had the best English toffee ever. Had Reuben, turkey dinner, sweets and Greek food. Great place to eat and get to go.

Awesome place to visit if you have time to browse. A lot to see and can get incredibly crowded. NEVER go peak times (lunch and weekends) because you will not be able to move. VERY touristy so have to deal with tons of looky loos taking selfies and blocking the aisles.

I ordered take out kati healthy sprout roll and it was really good. 
I regretted not getting more than one though but will definitely be trying their other items.

The chicken tikka roll and the paneer tikka roll are the best I've ever had. They were both moist, balanced in flavor, and enhanced by the yummy white and hot sauces. I'm a huge fan of this place. The only downside is they have a relatively high minimum of $20 for ordering through GrubHub.

Ranked as one of the top 5 things to do in Philly, so I went.  Glad I did.  This is a colorful, bustling place with fresh produce multiple eateries, candy shops, bakeries etc.  find your favorite.  I found super cheesesteaks and awesome donuts but much more to see....

my first time at this location. staff is friendly but the portion was considerably less than I'm accustomed to, the flavors weren't as bold as I like and they were out carnitas. however the decor is simple, beautiful, trendy and relaxed. I still love Chipotle but I'll stick to my usual location

Cool place to grab lunch. Best thing to get is the pastrami sandwich at Hershel's. You can also get a beer to go at Molly Malones. Definitely prepare for a crowd on weekends -- had much better luck with finding a table on Monday. Biggest complaint being the people who take their laptop and work. There aren't enough tables for them to be doing that shit!
The cheese slice was unexpectedly crisp, tart, clean delicious. The guys running this joint have big shoes to fill and they're no slouches. Really impressed.
So many great things under one roof. Where to begin. Numerous food vendors, meat markets, seafood and cheese. Flowers, chocolate and everything Amish. A must when you come to Philadelphia.

The Industry has definitely grown on me as I've come here more and more. I've found the service to be relaxed, consistently friendly, prompt without being rushed, and super helpful if you need help choosing a beer. The attitude in this place makes it a great neighborhood hangout.

I like the fact that it's a chill, quiet place I can have a conversation. Although, to be fair, I haven't been here that late at night.

The food is good but nothing mind-blowing. Brunch is better than a diner but not in the same league as Honey's or Green Eggs. The burger (4oz patty, though you can order 1 or 2 additional patties) and fries is a solid choice. Everything looks delicious and portions are what you would expect.

I do like the fact that The Industry tries to be a little fancy, but I'm a little turned off by some of the price points. Charging $10 for a banh mi seems kind of ridiculous when I can go to the market up the street from me and get one that's $3. Same for a falafel that costs $6 anywhere else. And that cheese plate for $14 needs to try a little harder to be worth $14. I realize this makes me sound like an old lady, but I also go to bed by 11pm on most Friday nights.

I have visited the terminal about a half dozen times at this point... And every time their is something to catch my attention. Whether it's a mouth watering roast beef sandwich at Dienicks or a baked vegan treat at the Flying Monkey, their is truly something for everyone. This is a staple location in Center City. Make sure to stop by!!

i loved it  alot   alot of  nice  restaurants  and   shops   and   got   a great  meal willl for sure  go    again   this   place  has a  nice  selection  of  shops  and  restaurants  wow   this  place is huge

If you are in Philly...Go!  There is such a great variety of shops inside.  Enjoy the great food.  DiNic's, Old City Coffee, and Beiler's are my favorites.  Try everyone else too.  You can also get great ideas from the restaurants and then walk the market and pick up all of the freshest produce, meats, cheeses and fish to make nearly anything.

This is a fun place to go and get something to eat, though it does get crazy busy during meal hours. I came here several times the last time I was in philly and stopped by with some coworkers for lunch during a conference this most recent time. It was extremely crowded. We first staked out a place to sit and we had one of us reserve the spot while the rest of us got food. I got cheesesteak (which you have to do when your in philly) with american chess, peppers & onions. The line was very long but they were efficient. Food was delicious which be due (partially) to the delicious bread. The sandwich was also huge! If I had a fridge I would definitely take half back for dinner.
Great place!

A true foodie's heaven! You'll want to come here hungry! 

There is absolutely something for everyone here... and then some! 

Chocolates, cheeses, coffees, cookies, cheesesteaks, pizzas, meats, seafood, gelato, pastries, not to mention all the specialty foods 

Everything is extremely fresh & there's no wrong place to start digging in 

Snagged some local cinnamon honey & chocolates.....we got there too late to try the famous Apple Dumplings & they were closed Memorial Day Monday - boo! 

But next time, my pretties.....for sure!! The plan will be to come for breakfast & eat my way through dinner!
Always busy. Good selections and variety. A favorite of mine for people who are visiting Philadelphia.

Visiting Philly from California. This is our first time staying at the Residence Inn Marriott which is two blocks away from Reading Terminal Market. 

The Market closes at 6:00pm which we thought was unusual. We would have loved for it to stay open until at least 8:00pm, preferably 10:00pm. At 4:00pm the Amish bakery in the back of the Market offers many baked goods for $2.00. We bought half of a pumpkin cheesecake pie for $2.00, simply amazing. The pie was delicious! The sweet girl behind the counter would not accept a tip.

So many choices So little time. We walked around the marketplace and sampled different flavors of hummus, cheese, curd, and more. We were tempted by the many wonderful smells wafting through the market. 

Apparently the Bieler's Bakery is a popular place for donuts and people were standing in a long line to purchase. 

When you enter the Market, there is a welcome/information desk which was manned both times were there. People were stopping by to ask for directions or other questions.

The Market is a stop on the Big Bus tour.

For groups of people who have no idea what they feel like having or can't come to a compromise on the same restaurant - just go here, split up, and meet back at a table.  It covers absolutely anything you'd want - great thai, greek, roast beef, indian, brisket, middle eastern, cannolis, ice cream, coffee, you name it.

Crazy busy indoor farmers market akin to Pike's Place in Seattle Washington. Lots of different fare and food and a good place to waste a few hours but if you are not into crowds and higher prices then beware this place is a nightmare! You should go at least once though and check it all out.

Love everything that this place has to offer, from inexpensive produce to many different types of eateries and finally you get to top it off with many different dessert options! 

This place is always packed on the weekends, so I try to avoid it, because its just overcrowded. I definitely recommend this place for tourists, as its one of my main shopping location!

The market can get so crowded that it's not for the faint of heart. Don't lose track of the people you come in with! Pretty much anything you want to eat--either on the spot or to take home--is here. Somewhere. And most of it is very good. Some specialty items can be very pricey, but if this is the only place you can find them and it's what you want, it's worth it. I've taken out of town guests there just to share the experience with them. It's an adventure even if you're not hungry or interested in shopping. When I have time to kill before catching a train, I always pop in to see what's happening. There's always something different that I hadn't noticed before.
One of my favorite place to shop! Another place to get fresh variety of foods! And they have everything Your heart desires!!

So glad I was able to stop at Reading Terminal Market on a recent day trip to Philly. It was especially packed as it was the weekend of the Philly Marathon, but it was worth braving the crowds for some great food. Although our lunch sandwich left something to be desired, we had good luck finding great meat and our thanksgiving turkey at one of the butchers. We also took home some great oils, pickles, and middle eastern snacks. It was difficult to find a spot to sit down and eat, but if you are patient and keep looking, one will open up eventually. Parking was surprisingly easy at the garage across the street... just remember to get your ticket validated and it will knock the price down quite a bit. I am excited for my next trip to Philly so I can try some new stands inside the market.
This place is awesome! So much amazing food. We ended up getting an Amish breakfast with scrapple and blueberry pancakes. Too many great things from which to choose!

A great place to just walk around and browse, find good deals, or find rare, hard-to-find foods. It's awesome, and you can truly find anything. I'm a huge fan of the cheese stands, as they have great selections of fine, local cheeses. 

Word of warning, don't come here at lunch. It's absolutely nuts, which tells you how good the food is in there, but it's an absolute madhouse.

Very nice interior. Nothing fancy, but it's all there. Food was a bit disappointing. No spices that are so essential for Indian Cuisine . They are open very late, so that could be a late night option.

What an amazing place. Reading Terminal Market is similar to Atlanta's Sweet Auburn Curb Market (which I adore) but on steroids. I'm not as well-traveled as some of my fellow Yelpers, who have compared RTM to other big cities' markets, but of those that I have experienced, I am just head-over-heels for Philly's huge market, full of incredible food stalls and shops.

AT and I came here with Min Y. during our visit of that crazy dude (who gifted me a book for Christmas called "Womanskills: Everything You Need to Know to Impress Everyone" [dude, I know that books shouldn't be wrapped in quotations, but should be bolded or underlined, both of which I cannot do in a Yelp review]). I knew I wanted to hit up Termini Brothers for some cannoli but as AT and I wandered around, our eyes just grew and grew. Yeah, I'm Vietnamese and my eyes probably can't grow much bigger than they are, but you know what the hell I mean. Anyway, we grabbed some coffee from Old City Coffee and hovered in the Beiler's Bakery/Beiler's Donuts and Salads corner, where the lines were massive. I just enjoyed watching the Pennsylvania Dutch bakery folks doing their magic but Min is impatient as a mofo, we figured the wait wasn't worth raising his blood pressure (hahaha, if you're reading this, Min!!).

I grabbed my cannoli and we mostly just looked around. Next time we are in the City of Brotherly Love, when Min will lovingly take us to see Liberty Bell, his absolute favorite landmark in Philadelphia, I'll make him take me back to Reading Terminal Market for some grub. Not because I'm not capable of finding my own way but because I enjoy pestering the hell out of him. Because he gave me Womanskills.

[#Yelp365: 24/365)

Loved Reading Terminal Market. Has literally been my go to place when I come to Philadelphia. Their produce is remarkable. I love that I can do my grocery shopping and grab a bite to eat while I'm there. So many choices and they are all great - you cannot go wrong with the food choices. This is a great place to visit on your tourist stop. You can spend hours at Reading Terminal if your heart desires. Its basically an indoor grocery shopping/restaurant/dessert cuisine stop.

Was definitely a zoo, but if I lived in Philly, I would come here all the time. I had a delicious chicken cheese steak sandwich from By George, and friendly service. We magically found seating and were able to settle in for lunch. Hubby got a sandwich from DeNic's that was great. He wished he had an extra stomach so that he could eat the whole thing. 

It's a little too crowded to make walking around enjoyable at all, but that's not the fault of the market.  If I was there during a less crowded time, I would have enjoyed spending more time there looking/walking around.  

There definitely seemed to be something for everyone there.
The best for everything!!  Highly recommend for a quick bite, grocery shopping or indulging in a sweet treat. This market will not disappoint.

The Reading Terminal Market was right across the street from our hotel, so it was incredibly convenient place to grab a meal.  The market it clean and has a zillion choices, but its more like a fancy, well designed food court than a real food market, like Cleveland's West Side Market.  Other than that, I am a definate fan!
Great variety and fresh choices. If you go on Sunday be ware of tons of people, which makes food shopping a lot less fun! Best place to get fresh fruits and vegetables in the city for a great price!

This place is great for tourists and locals alike! You can find almost anything food-related and other knick knacks too. It can get a bit crowded on weekends so definitely try to visit on a weekday if possible.

Tourists NEED to check out the various Amish stands (for honey, jams, pastries, etc), Bassetts Ice Cream, and Meltkraft if you're into grilled cheese.

This is a great place for locals to get produce, meat, and fish! Don't expect to find frozen dinners here - this is not the place. Also, come prepared to know your prices! Some things are cheaper than others here. But if you want high quality stuff, this is as good as it gets (other than a farmers market of course). If you're a student, go to Iovine Brothers (produce) for 10% on Wednesdays and Sundays!
touristy and often too crowded but still a great city market in a great city.
If you only have time to go to one place in Phili, go here.  Seriously.

Despite the good stuff, you probably don't want to visit if you're claustrophobic.

I spent a lot of Saturdays going to Termini Brothers for a cannoli early in the morning.  Today, since I'm not living here, I launched myself from the motel a bit late.  I didn't even bother to see if Termini Brothers were there since it was afternoon and I'd already eaten.

The place was so crowded that I was uncomfortable.  Of course, all of the produce looked good, and there were multiple Asian lunch counters and the Amish were there as well.  The meats and cheeses looked amazing.  If I could just take them all home with me until I can move back here, I would.

One thing that seemed odd were people taking large dogs through the entrance on Filbert St.  If there isn't some pet care inside, would you want to eat with dogs around you?  I wouldn't, and I've had dogs.

Overall, this is an amazing place with so much to see and try.

The #1 downside is that it gets extremely crowded...crowded to the point that you won't be able to walk or even move. 

Many people come here for their lunch break, so if you are stopping in for lunch, be prepared to wait in line for a LONG TIME.

It's nearly impossible to find a seat, so be prepared to eat standing up.

The variety of shops/eateries is amazing. Every kind of food you could crave. Definitely worth stopping in the next time you are in Philly!

I came here for dinner and liked it.  Then I came here for brunch and loved it.

I'm not a huge fan of brunch, mostly because of the hype, the crowds, the wait, the overpriced mediocrity, etc.  But this place is as unpretentious as they come.  Since it's far from the Green Eggs crowd in center city and the Sabrina's crowd in Art Museum, it's never been overly packed and I've always managed to get a seat right away.  Plus the staff is super friendly.

We went last Sunday around noon and the minute I opened the menu I knew it was gonna be a life or death decision for me....every single item on the menu sounded fantastic.  I actually think it's more varied and interesting than their regular dinner menu.

I was torn between the steak and eggs, the burger, and the smorgasbord of scrapple, pancakes, and other types of breakfast foods all piled on to each other.  I ended up opting for none of these and got the Frank's Red Hot fried chicken over biscuits and gravy.  It was a nice heaping portion and absolutely delicious with the perfect flavorful chicken skin.  Plus, it was a great hangover cure.  My boyfriend got the burger with bacon which looked amazing and the fries were salty and crunchy.

They have a really great drink selection and tons of weekday specials like half price burgers and Quizzo.  Will definitely be back here for brunch again so I can get that mess of Scrapple and shizz.

Note: I was really craving a normal spicy Bloody Mary and they only have a "Deconstructed" one which uses tomato water instead of juice and the server was honest with me and told me his friend wasn't crazy about it, especially if you're used to that strong hair of the dog.

Over priced and over-hyped tourist trap.  The glory days of the Terminal are long done.  The people who manage it now are catering to higher end customers.  by giving them less quality and higher prices.  Used to be the best place to shop for everything and anything you could think of.  Most of the best eateries have been chased out by high rents.  RIP Terminal--we knew you when,

Great spot - super busy, which I found exciting and an experience enhancer. Definitely recommend the roast pork sandwich at Dinic's. Beiler's donuts, while special, are overrated in my opinion. Overall, the kind of place that you can get lost in and just enjoy. Make sure you give yourself enough time to see everything if you're visiting for the first time (2-3 hours is probably sufficient).

I'm not saying anything that hasn't been said a hundred times before, but this place is awesome.  I just wish it was open later so I could eat dinner there too when I'm in town because there are so many options.  This is a must anytime I am in the area.

It can get crowded at lunch, so be prepared to wait in line for some of the best stuff.

Was catching an early morning flight from PHL and grabbed a veggie sandwich for breakfast on the plane. Bit into and nearly GAGGED!! The dried tomato had mold on it and the cheese was rancid. One half-bit was enough to give me stomach issues for the rest of the day. AVOID this place!!
Great place to eat and people-watch. Reminds me of the grand central market in downtown Los Angeles, but bigger. great atmosphere and fair prices. Lines weren't too long either.

reading terminal is where the city goes to eat together. the range of people is amazing. and the camaraderie is undeniable.  Sometimes I wish the food was better but at least there are many choices. Some favorites: Metropolitan Bakery, one of the best around. The music at lunchtime. The coffee and tea places. And the improved beer garden.

I was overwhelmed by the plethora of different store shops and eating stalls.  I felt like I was back in Tokyo with the crush of people running around.  What a great place to sample food from around the world while never leaving Philadelphia!

If you in Philly, you have to put this place in the top of our list to see.  I would almost put it first.  And plan on going back and spending plenty of time while you are there.  I probably could have eaten lunch here every day if i could have.
There is so many food stands to see and check out.  It made choosing super hard.  We split up our group and got things from all different stands and everything was excellent.  

Go here and go often.  I want one of these in my town.
Love it at the market! You can find anything you need or want! Food is fresh- especially enjoyed Pearls Oyster Bar and the crepery!

I've eating from here 3 times already. The first 2 times it was delivered to my job and the 3rd time I decided to go and check the place out.  It's a small restaurant in the middle of other stores. I actually missed it the first time and had to ride around the block again. I really like the Philly cheese and honey chipotle chicken fried dumplings. The buffalo chicken dumpling is spicy. When I went in I decided to try something I never had before, which was the cheesesteak noodle. This was served as a big portion. I didn't like the taste of this and I probably ate less than 25% of it. The vibe of the restaurant was young and artistic. There were paintings on the wall. The 3 staffers there were also young and all males. Service was fast. I see they have new dumpling options, I'll have to stop by to give these a try.

OMG Amish jerky. 
Seriously one of the best markets in the US despite the touristas.

Mice.  I went into this McDonald's last night and there were mice running around.  Even if they clean that up, they forgot half the food I ordered and the place looked dirty everywhere.  Did I mention there were mice running around?
Great, quick lunch. If you like traditional fried calamari, you'll love the giant fried squid!

Reading Terminal is a lot of fun to get lost in and people watch. There is some excellent fast food options along with a few sit down places and some really funky (in a good way) food stores. I love the duck place that's on the edge near the ice cream place, not to be too vague or anything! It does get very crowded during lunch time and on weekends so only go if you have enough time!
Great for tourists! Though new competition is pending from new Market East development. -- Hotspur.

My parents used to bring my sister and I here when we were little every year around the holidays.  It was a tradition to come here, have a pretzel at the Pennsylvania Dutch pretzel place, get candy, and visit Rick's for a cheesesteak (I know, a great diet!). 

Things have changed some since I was younger.  Now that I live in Philly I consider Reading Terminal to be more of a weekly, rather than yearly, stop.  No more Rick's - it's now located in the Bellevue. 

 I visit the Terminal primarily for produce from Iovine Bros. Produce- reasonable prices and a WIDE selection of fruits and vegetables.  They have things I can never find at the supermarket.  My second stop is usually the Spice Terminal to pick up some coffee beans.  They have a great selection and the coffee is always yum.

Only downfall I can think of is that when there's a conference at the Convention Center, it can be pretty swarmed with badged peeps.  Fight through it!  The crowds are really part of what makes it a Philly institution anyway.

I wish every city had this market in it! It is fantastic for selection of products and the quality of prepared foods especially Amish - Mennonite selections.  I tend to find myself at the Dutch Eating Place enjoying wholesome favorites like the turkey sand which with gravy and a side of coleslaw and cranberry dressing.  Any of their hot sandwiches are divine! 
Right by that vendor is a splendid chicken wing place where the wings are rotisserie . So good!  There are a few fantastic bakeries in this place also.  If I had one in my city, I would shop there every week and find a way to do lunch here all the time too!
Many choices. Need a long time to chose. Most of them taste good.
Nice little fresh produce area for quick shopping. Tons of eatery stands that I'll need to try later! I'll definitely be back to explore some more!
My favorite place in Philly! There is nothing like it outside of Europe. Wonderful places to eat and buy groceries. It's a foodie's paradise.

This is a fun place to go when you're not sure what kind of food you're in the mood for, and you want a little of this and a little of that. It also works great for groups of people who all have different tastes. I love the smoothies, the coffee, and the burgers, personally. The market itself has great energy. It could use more/better seating, and the tables are not very clean. Otherwise, it would have been 5 stars.

Great place full of a variety of restaurants/vendors. I do enjoy it and it reminds me of a tinier version of New York's Chelsea Market. If I lived closer I would probably find myself eating at a different restaurant everyday! Great place to find fresh seafood and small gifts (food wise) for friends and family.
The Reading Terminal Market is great. Every vendor seems to have great food and it is a more authentic experience than those fake sterile markets you find in other cities.

Here you will find some of the best lunch food in the city... and some of the most annoying tourists standing in the middle of the "aisles."

Reading Terminal houses Tommy DiNic's Roast Pork & Beef, named the best sandwich in the country by some guy on the food network. I can concur, the brisket and the Italian-style pulled pork are some of the best sandwiches in Philadelphia. You will also find Miller's Twist, ranked third on some other guy's list of best soft pretzels in Philadelphia, and a variety of Amish vendors with more reasonable prices than Whole Foods and that pretentious mini-supermarket on Walnut Street.

Reading Terminal Market tops everyone's list of tourist destinations, but don't let that fool you. Some of the best food in the city is here. Though you should avoid RTM from 11:30a-3pm on most days, especially weekends, if you wish to not have hundreds of tourists standing in your way talking about how New York has better food because they chose a cheesesteak over a pork sandwich.

We tried Creperies, karen Parkers soul food and Carmen's Cheesesteak.  All were delicious.  Creperies, we tried the cheesecake with berries crepe.  A taste of heaven.  I would highly recommend.  Karen Parker's soul food.  Her Mac and cheese was divine.  I had to keep my husband out of my plate.  I also had fried chicken and okra.  All was so good.   Carmen's was recommended.  Our cheesesteak was great.  Loved the vibe of the market. Bi wish we had this in SA

Beware of the sensory overload when you step into this wonderful haven of delightful, coma-inducing collection of cheesesteaks, hoagies, pulled pork sandwiches, stuffed pretzels, wonderfully thick cookies, moist cupcakes, and other beautiful items of fatty glory. 

Being my first trip there, I was not prepared for what I saw, and then for what I tasted. Every bite of anything I ate was delicious. I wish I could give you specific names of places but all I can give you is various foods and their descriptions. I had a stuffed pretzel stick that had pepperoni, mozzarella, and marinara inside which was excellent. I followed that up with a pulled-pork sandwich which was amazingly juicy and meaty. For dessert, I had a really thick cookie with milk and a slice of carrot cake. I was actually going to go for another cupcake and cheesesteak until my girlfriend halted my obese behavior. I did buy a couple of loaves of some apple cinnamon bread baked by Amish girls for our moms however.

I really have no qualms about the place. They even provide a voucher for free parking in the parking complex next door for two hours which was enough time to walk around the market, stuff my face, actually go outside and enjoy the surrounding area (there's some really cool historic buildings and outdoor plazas nearby), and then come back to buy some ice cream and then go home with 10 minutes to spare. Being from NYC, I thought we had it all. I was proven wrong when I came here and was assaulted by the freshness of their food at such affordable prices. I plan on coming here every time I visit Philly. 

New York needs a Reading Terminal Market!

It's a very cool place. You can find pretty much anything you want here and more. There's always something interesting.  It's a family tradition to go here around Easter to get Cannoli and pork sandwiches, then again in Christmas for real Amish style cheesecake  (can't be beat!).
Great prices and great food! I love ordering from Masala Kitchen. Their service is very fast and it is easy to order through their website.

Loved my experience at the RTM this past weekend! Visited for the first time with bunch of girlfriends in a quest to try and eat as much as we could and I think we did pretty well lol. It was a Sunday afternoon. There was live music and good amount of crowd. I immediately felt overwhelmed with all the food and people around me but the handy dandy map came to the rescue and we were able to navigate our way through. 
I have been to Dutch markets in Maryland areas with Amish booths and was hoping to experience it here since their food and products are AMAZING but we unfortunately came on a Sunday :(
Other downside was that Beilers bakery was closed as well. Not sure why but we couldn't try some of their pastries that they are known for. It was overall a good experience and I will definitely back again to try more things!
Overall nice place. The menu looked great but the food was surprisingly bland. It seemed like dishes were lacking basic salt and pepper. Probably won't go back for that reason.

Heard about this place from a friend on a visit before officially moving out and loved it! Have only tried 1 or 2 of the food stands, but good. A little pricey, but it is definitely a tourist spot. The donut place, don't know what it's called, but seriously, amazing! And not a bad price when the regular donuts cost the same amount as the fancier kind.

And I can't give enough props to The Chubby Olive. A great olive oil/vinegar booth inside. Was one of the only places open on our first visit (we didn't realize how early it closed) and when we told the guy we were visiting from out of state, he gave us a 15% discount, which was so generous. We only bought a small sample pack (had to get it home on the plane somehow without checking our luggage) but seriously so good.
Great assortment of businesses and venders. one of my fav spots to shop when I go into the city

This is the heaven of every food lover. You can find anything you crave. The prices at the restaurants are very reasonable and the wait lines aren't bad and the service is always quick. Make sure you try some of the deserts as well.
Fantastic variety of food!  Make sure that you stop by Termini Bros to get a canoli!  I always try a new place each time that I come in.
What can I say? This place deserves six stars. It's a Philadelphia icon that never disappoints. We shop here for produce on a weekly basis. They're prepared foods are equally amazing.

recently made my first trip to philly and for a foodie, reading terminal market was at the top of my list of places to visit.
it was super hectic and HUGE (dragged my bf up and down every single aisle), just the way i like my markets. tried the blueberry pancakes at the dutch spot.. chewy, chock-full-of blueberrys, unreal!
if i lived in philly, i would probably have to resist the urge of going to the market everyday. the meats looked incredible, as did the seafood, produce, BAKED GOODS...... drool.
anything you could possibly want to eat all in one place. genius.
A must see when visiting Philly. Everything I have had in this place is great, except for the sushi. Worst sushi ever.

Dear Reading,

Why are you closed on July 4th?  Give me one decent answer as to why one of the biggest draws in the city is closed on the city's biggest holiday.  

Imagine that you are a tourist from somewhere.  You take the plunge and decide that you want to take the family to Philadelphia for the 4th of July celebration.  You have know all about independence hall and the liberty bell but your tourist guide also points out a large market where they have tons of great food.  You and the family walk from indy hall to the market which is no small feat considering they are from the suburbs and walking is alien and weird.  On top of that, they just got the fright of their life as it was a walk through Market East and by the gallery.  But you made it!  And you walk up and find that the market is closed.  How pissed would YOU be?

It's this kind of logic/attitude/work ethic that keeps Philly from being anything but than a could-have-been.  

While we are on that subject, do you not realize that you are above a train station and that people might want to get meat sliced before they head home?  Why is it when I walk in after 5, your meat vendors turn me away because they don't want to get their already cleaned machines dirty nor do they want to stay a minute past 6pm?  

Honestly Reading.  Despite all of your local flavor and great produce, I'm am seriously convinced that you want to fail.

Ok so I walked in Wendy's this morning only to be greeted by everyone at the cashier's counter starring at me and the cashier( the white woman I spoke about the other day) pointing at me, she was telling everyone that I said she was rude and shouldn't be working with the public,and she's absolutely correct, I did say that and I stick to my words she is awful and no she shouldn't be working with the public!!
So I proceed to call on the manager Alex, he responds with " what, OH God" I said OH God is that how you speak to a customer? He says I'm busy have alot of stuff to do, so I tell him about the white lady and he says to me " Joanne? She's the best if you'd get to know her you'd love her that's how she is" he says to me" By the way are you going to make a purchase? " I said I always do I'm not one of those junkies that you allow to hang in here! Now I'm done with this Wendy's you won't be seeing me in there again, they just lost a good customer!! It's gonna be another homeless hangout!!!
              Thank you again
        Theresa Ciarrocchi
Great food, great atmosphere, can get crowded on weekends but still one of Philly's best locations. Don't miss the heavenly Bassetts ice cream.

Could be my favourite place in the world!  I went for the famous roast pork sandwich I'd seen on man vs food - and what a sandwich it was.  I think the three in front and behind me had ordered the exact same thing - roast pork, provolone, rabe.  It was amazing.  Loved every bite, the moist bread, the cheese.  Delicious.

I also had my first whoopie pie from flying monkeys - again delicious!  

I then spent the afternoon shopping on walnut and chestnut and everywhere in between - before heading back to my hotel I dropped by the market again to pick up soon for dinner.  It was about 5.30 and most places were closed by this time.  I managed to grab the last boneless rib sandwich from The Rib Stop - I'm glad I did as it was also delicious, the awesome dry rub rib taste letting the meat be the hero rather than the sauce.  Just simply delicious.

I think you could go here for lunch and dinner in a month - eating somewhere different each time - and never visit the same place.  Really fantastic - need to figure out how to work another trip here into the rest if my vacation!!

An absolute must when visiting Philadelphia.  
Last weekend we held a small conference at the Hotel next door.  I didn't have much time to visit the local restaurants but don't feel left out as the market had just about every taste I needed.  
From Breakfast  at Down Home Diner to wrapping I the weekend with Cookies and ice cream everything was delicious.  Just walking in the door you are is a treat as you take on all the wonderful smells.  
Each stall is something different.  If in a group it's easy to please everyone and meet in the middle to eat together.  Other options are several sit down restaurants or counter style seating. 
I had Beck's Cajun, The Rib Stand, Spataro's Cheesesteaks and a few more.  No disappointments.
I won't kid you the crowds are relentless.  I saw folks standing in  30 min lines for doughnuts.  Some stalls you could only see from a distance.  Most times after I had my order I escaped out a door even if it meant walking outside all the way around this huge building.  There was no leisurely shopping through the cookbook or honey stores like I wanted.  
Another down side was it closed at 6pm nightly and some places at 5pm.  A lot of places were closed on Sunday as well. 
Overall well worth the crowd!
They have so many different options for food. They have the best crepe place and donut shop!!
Where to start? There are so many things to chose from. My favorite is Herschel's. Some of the best corned beef and pastrami around.
got a very good veggie kati roll, mint lemonade. Veg biryani tastes good, not authentic biryani but definitely good taste. Service is OTC but the folks are courteous. Will visit again!
What can I say? Go-to place for food, fun, fellowship where people of all walks of life mingle in Philadelphia :)
This is something that I will miss very much, when I return to Miami. This was like being in the nineteenth century. Found great original restaurant and a fantastic coffee place.

One of my favorite sites in the whole city.  I come here often for fresh produce and meat, and the prices for those are great.

Prepared food tends to be a little overpriced.  During weekday lunch, this place is overrun with dumb tourists, convention goers, and jury members; all of whom stand around and clog the place up.

But for lunch, grocery shopping, delicous cookies, bulk spices, or just good people watching, Reading Terminal has a lot to offer.
Food was lousy.  Had to send both dishes back because they were dirty.  Only good thing was beer was cold.

When moving to Philadelphia -- the #1 thing that excited me about coming a bit south was the opportunity for Chick-Fil-A in my life.

After having to drive 30 minutes to the closest Chick-Fil-A was not acceptable in Boston.

This free standing location is awesome. They never have a line, quick, and usually with a smile on their face.

You can never go wrong with this fine chain of chicken restaurateurs. I visit them at least once a week.... Mmmmmm

It's surprisingly delightful when a new route to the office causes me to discover (or in this case, rediscover) places in the city. 

I've been coming to RTM since I was in diapers, when the visit required a trip into the city on the R2. Now that I'm in the city, I go often. Usually to grab a crepe for lunch, pick up produce, a preztel from the Amish folks, Bassetts ice cream and any number of other delicious items. But, I can't remember every having gone into the Market before 9AM. 

But, walking from the eastern edge of the Art Museum area, to Independence Hall this morning, I realized that all of my usual coffee stops were no longer on my way to the office. What to do? Of course, there was an Old City Coffee in RTM - but was RTM open at 8:15am? 

Yes, and I think I knew that, I just never tested it out. 

RTM is an entirely different place in the morning - sleepy, warm, free of all the jostling tourists and hoardes of jury duty-ers. Half of the stands are open or are in the process of opening.
