People behind the counters look up as you walk by and give you a cheerful smile. There are distinct smells of this or that, not the mix and match you get later in the day. After I picked up my coffee, I walked through the entire place to the last door and the only thing I had to dodge was a guy carrying a crate of produce on his head and an older woman buying fish. 

I think I'll be making a habit of this.

Super cool place with a great vibe; very low key and chill. Nice outside seating area, too. The menu is small but really diverse; I got a Bahn Mi sandwich and it was good but not great. The fries were delicious! I would like to try it again.
Big city market with lots of shopping and food. Great place to grab lunch away from the middle school tour groups. Was a perfect stop on our Philly trip for cheesesteaks.

May be bumping this rating up because I was so hungry, but this definitely hit the spot!  Quick walk from the Kimmel Center and open late, so it's a great place to grab a casual bite post-show.

I tried:
-Masala Chicken Roll - soooo good.  You can add egg for $0.50 but I skipped it.  Didn't need it to me.
-Mango Lassi - would probably skip this next time.  I'm spoiled by Mood's fresh lassis and this one was also a little thick for me.
...but back to the masala chicken roll because I'm craving one again.  The paratha (bread) is FRESH.  Soft and pliable, but with some crisped bits from the cooktop.  I think it really made the roll.

Try this place.

I am a huge Chipotle fan and have been eating here for many years, including locations across the region. I visit this location at least once a week because it is along my daily route. This store has high volume due to its location and can have long lines. I also find that they tend to run out of certain ingredients early in the evening. Despite the constant business, the service is always satisfactory. The staff are consistently friendly and efficient. I'll be eating here for a long time.

My favorite new neighborhood restaurant. Interesting, creative, well-prepared and fresh food; very exciting cocktails and beers. Excellent, I mean EXCELLENT service. Had fish n chips the other night... one of the best in Phila. Love Sunday Brunch menu and that wierd but fabulous deconstructed bloody mary.

I love this place. We come every time we go to Philly. Our first stop is always DiNic's and then we wander. The place is crowded and noisy. Just push your way through. Also, the lines are deceiving at most places. They tend to move quickly. Also, any of the Amish stalls will be closed on Sunday.

Ran into The Industry last night while waiting for my dog to be seen by the vet nearby--such a good find! Great beer and cocktail list, nice menu, and well-executed food. I ordered the fried green tomatoes, which were served w ranch dressing underneath and a lemon-dressed arugula on top. Loved. My friend ordered the meatballs, which are served atop a deliciously cheesy polenta. I'm vedge do I only tried the polenta + sauce, but from what I tried and the expression on my friend's face, the dish was excellent. The service was on top of its game and our waitress was full of character in the best of ways. 

Yay for The Industry!

I'd come here before 11 or after 2! Anything between then is lunch and it's super crowded. I haven't ever got lucky with seating there, so I usually eat standing or outside. I would give this place 5 stars for the food, though! I LOVE the variety that they have! And the sweets and pastries... ALWAYS fresh!

I had high hopes for this place. A friend and I split a beef/chicken/squid fried combo. Unfortunately everything was WAY overcooked. The breading was thick, dark brown, dry and bland. The meats were so overcooked it was nearly impossible to tell whether a piece was chicken, beef or squid. Sorry, Cheers Cut, we won't be back!

Reading Terminal is my connection to the city. This market represents everything Philly means to me. I've been coming here since I was about 5 years old and I don't think I'll ever stop. Reading is unparalleled in the amount and diversity of food they have here, you can find pretty much any cuisine you could ever imagine. The amount of specialty shops is literally amazing. To buy food, check out Guinta's for meats, Downtown Cheese for, well, cheese, Johnny Yi for seafood, and Iovine for produce; just to name a few of my favorites. The Head Nut isn't what the Spice Terminal was, but its getting there. To eat food, go to Sang Kee, Beck's, by George, Nani's, Kamal's, and the crepe place (emphasis on Sang Kee). I've had many friends move away from the city only to say that their local markets pale in comparison to what Reading is. Unless you absolutely must, avoid going on the weekend! Park in the garage on 12th and get your ticket validated for cheap (relatively speaking) parking, that is, if it actually works...

Worst McDonald's I have ever been in! Customer service is very poor, store is dirty and also the employees curse aloud amongst each other like they are on the street! I will never patronize this garbage spot! What a dump!

Now this is my kind of place! While I generally dislike Philadelphia, and most of its sports loving constituency, I have a deep and profound respect for their culinary scene. If you are looking for the foundation of the foodie scene, Reading terminal market is probably the best place to start. 
A vast smorgasbord of everything edible as well as non edible.  Amish food stands serving up pretzel wrapped hot dogs, chicken and sausage. Behemoth fish and meat counters that purvey some of the freshest morsels from the sea and land. And then there is Dinic's!
Dinic's is the reason I came here. For those of you not in the know, Dinic's is quite possibly the best Roast Pork and Broccoli Rabe sandwich on the planet. I am not embellishing here. This sandwich transcends mortal cuisine. Since this review is about the Market, I will limit my laud for Dinic's here, and you can read my Yelp review of Dinic's for a more detailed and introspective account of this landmark.
For a great taste of the Philadeplhia scene, drop by the Reading Terminal market and peruse thier wares. You won't be disappointed.

Reading Terminal is a smorgasbord of anything you could possibly want to eat crammed into this wondrous place.  I've been many times and personally love to get an ice cream and a crepe or grab some cheap fruit at Iovine's - though you have to use it pretty quickly because everything is fresh!

My only gripe with this place is that it can get overwhelmingly congested.  Weekdays are the best.

Being fed on rolls (one of the commonest fastfood in Indian metros) through childhood and early youth, I definitely missed a roll-place in Philly. 

The masala rolls here are good, the other flavors aren't that great, but then this is the opinion of my spice-craving Indian tongue and others may disagree with me. The platters (have tried the chicken one) aren't worth it.

P.S. I hope they are a little generous with the gravy in the rolls, coz the rolls seem too dry.

If you are in center city, Philadelphia, and you don't go to Reading Terminal Market, you have made a very, very foolish decision. You can shop affordably, or spend three weeks worth of your paychecks. The prepared food at all of the many vender stalls offers so much diversity of cuisine, and price, that there is something for everyone! You can get brick oven pizza, a brisket, and gourmet chocolates, and you can stock up on fresh vegetables, meats, and fish, to prepare at home, all within a few feet of each other. It's also a nice place to go for a little gift, because they've got adorable little soap shops, and a pretty kitchen supply store, and really cool Amish goods! It's a manageable size. Not too big, and not too small. Just... GO!!!

I've said it once, I'll say it again:  I love Philadelphia.  The Reading Terminal Market just made me love it a little more.  It's almost like marrying the woman of your dreams only to find out she loves to play all of the video games that you like to play...sigh.

First off, thanks to Philadelphia tourism for teaching me the right way to say "Reading".  Apparently it is pronounced more like the color Red versus the thing you do with a book when it's open.

For those of you unfamiliar with this place, it is a GIGANTIC open air (but enclosed) market.  I'm not going to list every type of shop and eatery.  If you want that, I'm sure you can go to their website.  What I can tell you is that if you are hungry, but don't know what you want, come wander the Reading Terminal Market for 10 minutes.  I'm sure you'll come across something awesome.

While there, I enjoyed my first falafel from Kamal's, a gigantic calzone from By George!, beer from the Beer Garden, and a cookie from the Famous 4th Street Cookie Company.  All together, a wonderful lunch and awesome experience.

Top Philadelphia attraction. If you can't find it at Reading Terminal, it's not available. I love this. They have such a variety of eateries, including DiNic's Roast Pork. We get our olive oils from here too. They also have a bar in case you just need to get off your feet. Don't skip out on the fountain drinks and cookies either.

I also went here for a wedding reception which was a wonderful change of pace.

This place is definitely one of Philly's treasures. If you don't know what to eat, stop in here! It's a great mix of produce stands, baked goods, fresh meats, and tons of different types of foods and restaurants. HIGHLY recommend the Amish bakery for donuts and fritters and Meltcraft for one seriously amazing grilled cheese sandwich. Be aware that it's crowded on the weekends (and any time there's a major event in the convention center), but aside from the crowds, Reading Terminal has great variety and a lovely atmosphere. Definitely a must-see (and eat) when you're in town.

This place was amazing. Had everything I could ask for in what I wanted to be offered when it came to food products or items in Philly. If I were to be introduced to one place for all kind of foods, it would be this place. The assortment of fresh fruits and produce to different assortment of foods makes this place the ideal candidate to be on my top 5 go-to place for this city. A must go-to for any out of towner for sure!
This place is not for a person that doesn't like crowds. It's packed, fun and all Philly. I love the freshness of the food and all the choices.

I love going to Reading Terminal market! Its really convention to get any groceries since its in one building! Absolutely love smelling the chocolates! And i always stop by and get crepes! However i dont like how a bit small it is to walk through it! But by far the best place to get some lunch.

Must stop while you are in Philly. Tons of amazing vendors all in one place. Definitely stop by DiNic's for the roast pork with broccoli rabe. Beiler's deserves all it's fame and glory, too. Every donut is incredible. These shops won't disappoint!

I can't add more but 5 stars, but 5 is not enough. This is one place I would love to have close to my work.  I would be in this place everyday for lunch. I wouldn't get tired of going because there are so many and different type of food places to choose from. If you're in Philly, this is a must see and eat.

Went to Dinic's for roast beef and italian pulled pork sandwiches. I don't if it was because I was starving or it was just that good. I went halfsies with a friend and I thought the pulled pork was better. I'd still eat either sandwich any time of the day.

Went here on a gorgeous almost Spring-like Monday with my boyfriend at around 2pm... we came hungry as previous Yelp-ers had suggested... :D

We parked at the garage across the street (get parking validated by any merchant with $10 purchase and pay only $4 for up to 2 hours!!!) which was SO convenient. Outside the market there was some emsemble playing music which was cool.

Inside I was immediately in LOVE with all the choices set out before me... Lots of little restaurants and shops. Some have their own counter and stools right in front, but there's also a small cafeteria-like set up in the middle of RTM with a bunch of tables and chairs (this is where we ended up eating... although I was a little displeased with the cleanliness of the tables, eating area, etc bc it wasn't really too crowded but I shrugged it off...)

After wandering around taking everything in... we decided on the Little Thai Market (Red Curry Salmon & Basil Chicken $6 each) everything was great although next time I would ask if they could make it spicy. I got an orange, mango, pineapple smoothie and a piece of baklava ($4 and some change) from a middle eastern shop (can't remember the name-dang it). The baklava was so good we went back for 2 more pieces before we left! 

This place was a great way to spend a few hours getting lost in some great food-Can't wait to go back and try some more places out!!

Been here once before but it was late night for drinks. This time came on a Sunday afternoon looking for  one of their trademark burgers. They did not disappoint- a triple burger with fried egg and bacon was perfectly cooked and enough for two of us to split. Definitely on the list of best burgers in the city.

Wow!!! Absolutely delicious and perfectly portioned. I came here with my husband for a late lunch and man was it delicious! I got the Paneer Masala roll which was basically a spicy chunk of halumi in a thin and crispy, crepe-like roll... add some spicy red sauce and it was fantastic. My husband got the Chicken Kheema roll which was just as good!

Donuts! Amish pulled pork!! Sausage stuffed pretzels!!! chocolate chip cookies dipped in freaking chocolate!!! Fresh fricking roasted coffee!!!! Mutha freaking overstuffed pastrami sanwiches!!!!! Brick freakin oven freakin pizza!!!!

I had heard so much about the reading terminal market, and I was quite excited to visit it for the first time with some friends the other day. One step inside and our senses were blasted with an almost overwhelming sense of busyness inside. The chattering of people around us, the wafting smells of food from the nearby stalls, the brisk pace of the regulars, it was all quite exciting. There were just too many things to choose from, but the overall experience was amazing and I can't wait to go back. The only downside is that they close before dinner time, but looking forward to going back again.
Awesome selection of everything.  Long-ass lines for the more popular places and a litany of vendors.  This is a must-see/eat in Philly.

I'm not sure how I can rate this entire market, but this place is great and has something for everybody. It's my go-to when someone comes to visit because the possibilities are endless. I come here on my off-days just so I can try out some new restaurants. My personal recommendations are going to DiNic's for a sandwich and then getting dessert at Beiler's Donuts. I always go by Beiler's - they are absolutely delicious and easy on the budget. Be warned though - it gets busy, and the best place to enjoy your food after a well-earned hunt is actually in the back of the market.

Nothing negative will ever arise in my visits to Reading Terminal Market.  There is something for everyone! Yes you'll stand in lines but they owners know this and have food ready for you and you will be satisfied in no time!  Frequently visit Flying Monkey Bakery, Dinics, Crepes, the oyster Bar, Soul Food, and Beilers Donuts.  Food is reasonably priced and prepared in front of you!

As seen on TV Reading Terminal Market is home to all different kinds of foods for all kinds of people.  Craving ribs? There's a place for that!  craving grilled cheese? yup!  Need to pick up some fruits and veggies for the dinner at home? groceries are in the back!  Got in trouble and want to bring the girlfriend some flowers?  They have it!

Great location, just a short walk away from Jefferson Station, short walk away from china town, and literally across the street from the convention center!

One of the better Indian places I've been to in the area. Great dine in experience with a vast amount of options for vegetarians. Personally, I enjoyed this more than the original Kati roll because the food here has more flavor and amount in each roll.

Reading Terminal allows only certain people to become vendors in there market. While the Dutch are millionaires they wont allow other vendors to come in. I really hate the underground politics going there. More Philadelphia small business owners need to have a chance to showcase there goods.The place could be remodeled to have more vendor space. Most of the stores dont need that much space. Also the upstairs should open for people to eat and vendors are only down stairs.. Check the dates on food before you buy. If you buy a cake from the dutch make sure its not frozen that means its not as fresh. Ask for a thawed cake. Would reccomemed for tourist especially .They will enjoy.
Quick, delicious Indian food with clean and spacious seating and courteous staff!  Found this place a block or two from the Verizon Kimmel Hall

Cool place. So many options! Actually, so many options that I couldn't decide and ended up not being able to get anything because everything started closing for the night. 

I am not going to repeat what they have to offer, other reviewers did that already. It's definitely a must-visit Philly destination though.

So I will just say that this place shuts down early. As in 6pm. Don't make my mistake and GO EARLY. It's probably a sh*tshow during lunchtime so maybe not thaaat early.
Carmen's Cheesesteaks are amazing.  They are located inside of Redding Terminal and Michelle is very friendly and welcoming.

It's hard to write a review for an entire market, but I can tell you that everything I ate here was exceptional! We stayed nearby for a weekend and ate there four times! The fried chicken at the soul food place was some of the best I've ever had; their mac and cheese was also wonderful. Get a breakfast sandwich on rye at Herschels. I got it with brisket and oh my wow, best breakfast! I also had the Italian pork sandwich with greens and provolone. Maybe my least favorite meal but totally delicious and filling. Also had the gumbo and eggs for breakfast, and it was spicy and yummy. Only issue was I got spice bread instead of cornbread. Not a huge deal. The cookies and the candy place were also great. Would go back a million more times!

I was in Philadelphia for an extended weekend around 12-12-09. During that time I sampled many cheese steaks from different restaurants. There is no question that the finest sandwich I had was at Carmen's. All other cheese steak makers should sit down and let Carmen show them how. Not only was the sandwich wonderful but the service and conversation was superb.

Really enjoyed experiencing this area of Philadelphia!

The food was amazing, the store fronts clean, the staff of each booth knowledgable. 

Since we visited on a slow day, we could get around easily. I've heard it gets so crowded you can't move around. We were very lucky to be there on a day we could really experience this wonder. 

I highly recommend putting this on your list for Philadelphia.

This place is a gem that so many Philadelphians overlook. I got ribs, chicken wings, and produce here the other day, and all of it was great. For whatever reason, the quality of food from these vendors is quite a bit higher than the rest of the city. My top three: the thai place (salmon), the ice  cream place, and the ribs place.

I've been to Reading Terminal Market a few years back and to be honest, nothing was really memorable because I don't remember what I ate there. I think I faintly remember trying the roast pork sammie from Tommy DeNic's but even if I did, I can't remember what it tastes like. So this time around, I decided to document everything, so that if I do visit Philly again, I'll know what to get (or what not to). Here is everything we ate:

Tommy DeNic's: Roast Pork with Provolone and Broccoli Rabe - this was a nice break from the cheesesteaks that we've been eating. The pork was cooked perfectly, and there was a good amount of provolone and broccoli rabe. It does get messy though, so it's not really a sammie that you could eat on the go.

MeltKraft : Melter Skelter ('Melter Skelter' Raclette 3 Month, pickled green tomatoes, jalapeño, BBQ potato chips, and watercress) - this was good, but not worth $9. I don't know what it is about grilled cheese, but I just can't find a grilled cheese anywhere that's worth paying $10 for.

Beiler's Doughnuts - bought a few doughnuts from here - one crumb, the second cinnamon, and the third I can't remember. This had the longest line. The line wraps around other stands. People seem to buy these doughnuts up by the dozen. My boyfriend really enjoyed the doughnuts but to be, they were just doughnuts. But then again, maybe it's just because I'm not a huge fan.

Herschel's: Corned Beef Sandwich - although I only tried a few bites, the corned beef was pretty good. It wasn't overly salty, like corned beef tends to be. The pickles are great.

Overall, the market is a great place to try out a bunch of different foods. But it'll cost you.

Blocks away from the center of town you must go here and walk around and try the mounds of food selections. I mean it makes Chelsea market look like a closet. The closest thing to this place is the Lexington market in Baltimore. tons of options, place is packed so be prepared and seating is hard to get when you want to eat but its there.

This is a good place to check out once while in the city. There are an inordinate # of places to it. It may not be for everyone, though, because it is extremely crowded and hard to find a place to sit. I'd say it's worth seeing if you don't mind big crowds...

Generally hard to find Indian street food , I was delighted to try this place as I was walking through the streets of Philly . Authentic , reasonable kathi rolls ( I tried chicken kheema roll) can make a great lunch or snack.

the best sandwich ever lives here.  The turkey place, and its like the thanksgiving special or something.  juicy turkey, savory stuffing, sweet cranberry sauce on yummy yummy fresh wheat bread. mmmmmm *drool*  and ps  I don't like turkey but once a year.  but when in philly i eat this sammich!    The reading terminal market is all around awesome.  From the fruit and veggie grocer in the back corner, to the old guy's meat market, to all the Omish stuff... super great.   It's always busy but it's also always good. I haven't visited all the vendors there yet.  but i do recommend the turkey place,  the meat market where the old guy is behind the counter, the fruit grocer in the back, the omish bakery up front  and their pretzel place,  they also have a candy spot that has all the old time favorite candies,  honey-bees, the soft after dinner mints etc...  I'll have to reupdate with the names of places.   A++

I love the variety Reading Terminal Market has to offer. You can find delicious foods as well as nice gifts for a dinner party here. If you can avoid going on the weekend, it will be a much more enjoyable experience as it tends to get crowded with tourists.
A little disappointed with the grilled cheese sandwich. It wasn't as i was expected. I think they've cut down on the cheese. Not quite sure. But anyway, the cookies are delicious and puffy.

Great place to try out different foods every week. Really great selection.
Hershels Deli do a stoncher of a pastrami Reuben.
Wursthaus Schmitz has amazing sandwiches and the Hungarian sausage sandwich is the balls.

While the overall market is colorful, varied, and a good place to people watch, I have been finding the quality of food from the vendors slipping. Greasy burgers, fatty pork, boney duck, underwhelming sloppy joes from four different venues in the past few weeks.

Happy hour here is great ( this is just a hh review). We came on a Monday for burgers and bubbles. $6 burgers which were the same burgers you would get normally for $9. The meat was great, cheese, and a unique pickle mayo. I kinda wish there was more of the mayo but it was fine. The bun was even great! We also got the $5 bubbles you can get rose champagne or prosseco. For those who don't want champs you get miller high life for $1.50. The Mac and cheese croquettes for $1 everyday were amazing! How could you not love fried mac and cheese!!!! Enjoy!
Good bread, good sandwiches, great peppers .... and goood shakes!!!
Great rolls!!  Absolutely Indian.. affordable food, quick service! Friendly staff  :)
Fresh fish, fresh veg, ... you'll make a great meal based on what you buy here... except... you'll be full cause you'll also stop for lunch and eat too much great already cooked food.... ahh well.

My son told us this was a go-to place to find Philly atmosphere and good food.  We didn't find that to be our experience.  The place consists of a lot (!) of retail enterprises set up adjacent to each other and separated by aisles.  The food places serve a variety of what I would call grill-food...do not look for cloth napkins. It did seem to be popular as a business lunch destination, being quite busy the day we visited at about noon.  Our challenge was sorting out where and what to eat since the crowd had filled-up many of the sparse-seating-available sections....come to think of it, that may have been what caused us to end up less happy with what we had to eat....in any event, the food was quite expensive given portion sizes and counter seating arrangements. Glad we went.  Would go again on a day we had more time to spend looking over options.  The activity was interesting and the employees friendly and in some cases colorful.
So much to see, eat, and smell! I want to try it all. I love browsing the aisles and checking out all the vendors. A nice respite from the city - I could spend a whole day here!

Masala kitchen is the best place in philly for a quick bite to eat. My favorite things are the paneer masala and aloo rolls. The Kati rolls are always served warm and fresh and are $10 for 2 which is a great deal. The best part about masala kitchen is that it is open very late on the weekend which makes it the best place to go after a long night out.

Stopped by here last weekend after a meal in Chinatown.  It was super crowded on a Saturday around noon.  They have a ton of stalls here all with different things - typical farmers market with butchers, produce, cheese shops, eateries, and etc.  I enjoyed the one store called the Spice Terminal.  They had a TON of spices, as well as coffee and tea.  They also had this good cupcake place right outside of the Spice Terminal (but the name escapes me..)

The market is pretty good since I don't know of another farmer's market in the area...I woulda given it a 5, but I expected more from a farmer's market in a city (in comparison to the Allentown Farmer's Market in the Lehigh Valley).  There was nothing really that made me feel like I need to make my way down to the Reading Terminal Market instead of going to the closer (for me) Allentown Farmer's Market.

It is still definitely worth checking out and it's still very fascinating, hectic, and awesome.

A hot mess. I arrived at 835pm tonight 11/27/17. because I was craving the Rueben that has been advertised. I get to the door and it is locked. The posted hours show open until 9 pm. I'm actually very upset because I am hungry and was filling a craving. I decide after pulling on the door 25 minutes until close to call and see if maybe the sandwich artist is in the restroom.  A young man answers the phone and I ask about posted hours and why they are not honoring them. He then stated , " We were out of flatbread so I decided to close." This makes no sense to me. I assume all businesses honor business hours and I personally did not want flatbread. Needless to say this franchise owner either doesn't care about protecting the company's image and guidelines or hires people who are under the impression that it's their business and can close when they want. Truly a terrible experience and to think I rushed to get there before they closed.  If I could give a zero star I would.  5 thumbs down.
just a great place to tease your hunger. everything is good.

its like .. christmas in july. 

everything you want and need, in one spot. plus, olde city coffee is AMAZING. oooommmggggggggg. chug a lug. shits all dope! 

good pricing, quick lines.! good smells all over the place

This place is an absolute gem. I'd say it's underrated, but it's pretty hard not to get into a giant selection of takeout, groceries, and specialty foods. Although it feels a bit like a post-apocalyptic market because of the labyrinth-like setup/crowded lanes/exposed ceiling, I think it adds to the charm and I wouldn't change a thing.

I love this place.  It can get crowded at times, but there are a lot of vendors in here that make it worth the crowd, and the lines.  Whatever you're craving, there's most likely someone there selling it.  And don't shy away from the long lines... chances are good tha they have the best food!

Welcome to sensory overload. If you're visiting Philadelphia this is an absolute must see and eat attraction. There are many famous vendors in the market place, but also a few gems that aren't as well known. The best part about it is- there is something for everyone. 

The culinary diversity present at Reading Terminal Market is like no other in Philadelphia. If you love good food and cultural experiences you will love it here. 

Make sure you come with an appetite!

Surprisingly good. I don't really frequent fast food joints, but this one is pretty good. It was well lit, clean and nice inside. Prices are as you would expect from a fast food place, $3.00 for sandwiches, around $6+ for meal deals. They actually made everything sound so good.. chicken and waffles, etc etc.
I got the original chicken sandwich. It's simple, but they do simple well. The chicken is so darn juicy and not dry on the inside -- crispy outside. Looks small, but I barely finished it. Good choice if you're craving chicken or in a rush.. and have to go to a fast food joint.

Seriously surprised by how clean this place was. Most fast food places gross me out!
Great place to get a lot of different things.  Has all the Philadelphia staples.  Take advantage of the parking by making a $10 purchase and having the store validate your ticket.

A must see in Philly! The variety is incredible. Breakfast, lunch, dinner, dessert, tea, or even just shopping for soaps or spices. Definitely don't miss the reading terminal market if you're visiting or even if you live here. Great place for getting groceries too

McRib, y'all.

That's right, because nothing sates my hunger after a hard day's search for ODB like a combination of boneless pork, fresh-slivered onions, dill pickle slices and McDonald's signature McRib sauce on a toasted, golden-brown home-style bun.

Get it while it's hot, dawg. (Limited availability, yo.)
Such an awesome place. If you are attending a dinner party you can find something to bring here

This place is a life SAVER... if you're like me "an artist on a budget" THIS IS THE PLACE!!!! Dollar grab bags will get you through the week, the Amish always have reasonable baked goods, that are sooooo yummy! Thank life for the reading!!!
I enjoy going, especially with visitors and on weekends, when the Amish boothes are open.

I'm not going to lie, I do really like this place.  Line is usually long, but fast moving, so make sure to scope the menu before you go.  
Seating is noisy and limited, so usually I grab and go.  Outside seating of course is on the other side of Houston Hall, and probably would be better if you have issues with the "lively" atmos.

As a warning folks, to be "under $10" is pretty hard to do.  All in with a fountain drink (unlimited refills) is closer to $15 (and the lavender lemonade is a personal fav), but is really, really fresh and very high quality.  Friendly folks too!  I'm only loosely veggie, but boy the gazpacho is hard to beat (hint get pumpkin seeds and crunchy onions, you won't be sorry).  Last time I was there, I did have some sausage in it, and would highly recommend it for someone who needs a protein punch.  Also any grains in it is good too!!!  I'm so obsessed with it, that I can't and haven't tried anything else on the menu at all.  Don't feel sorry for me, I just really like it and am not sick of it at all. :)  Everytime I go and try some new twist with it, and it does not disappoint.

Fantastic alternative to normal fast food! Absolutely the best option if you have dietary needs, the food is still just as tasty even if you are vegan, vegetarian, or gluten-free....that's not often how it is in most chain restaurants. I am quite honestly a bit addicted to the chipotle burrito bowl it's SO filling and is always delicious!!! Yes chipotle is a bit on the expensive side, but my burrito bowl always lasts for two meals so the price is definitely worth the amount you get. Plus I love that you feel like your getting fast food without having to consume all of the grease and nastiness of traditional fast food.
Great selection of food to choose from.  The burgers from Hunger Burger were amazing!  I'd almost have to say better than In n' Out Burger!  Needed more seating though!
The first time I walked in, it just blew me away. It's hard to know where to start. Rows and rows of beautiful, fresh, delicious food. I come every chance I get.

You can find whatever you want here, from a great Philly cheese steak to various ethnic foods to a roast pork sandwich which was named the best sandwich in America by Adam Richmond of the Travel Channel.  While there, you can buy fresh produce, meats, seafood, etc.  One of the coolest places in Philly!
Come hungry because the amount of good food is insane! Cool Amish ambience too! Unexpected fun times!

An absolute must-do when visiting Philly. Best times to go if you do not like lots of people is during the week, work hours. But then you would miss the crowded fun market in all its glory. Aim for a Saturday so you don't miss the Amish on Sunday. And be prepared to be in awe of the endless food stalls with tons of variety. So must history here! Non-food items as well. Close to Chinatown and City Hall. You won't leave empty handed!

I absolutely love markets like the Reading Terminal Market.  I mean, you can't go wrong with the abundance of food deliciousness at this place.  I'm not from Philly so this was my first visit but certainly won't be my last.  I will travel for food, specifically veggie food. I don't recall all of the veg options but RTM has so much to offer.  We were only seeking breakfast and grabbed a few orders of hotcakes from the Dutch Eating Place; those babies were huge.  My last stop before departing was the Herbiary.  I didn't get to explore as much as I would have liked so more reason to come back.

I don't even know where to begin. Let's just say that I hate crowded places but even I will brave RTM on a Saturday for a turkey sandwich or some amazing cheese and meat. Or a cannoli, whatever. I could go on and on. If you are visiting Philly, this MUST be a stop for you and give yourself a few hours to wander around and eat your way through. I love love love RTM and can't wait to go back soon.

This is a cool place and definitely somewhere to take someone who isn't from the area. At first it seems HUGE but then you realize it's not quite that big. There's lots of food options, many of them decadent that you can bring home....like the amazing doughnuts from beilers....but there's only so much you can eat while you're there. Fun place...definitely check it out!

This place is great for lunch.  Apparently Man vs Food stopped by over here as well.  

There is always a crowd, especially on the weekends.  

This place is definitely worth it.

Holy moly. A parthenon of food. So many choices, whether you're going there to eat already prepared food, or buying for cooking later, this place has everything. Docked it one star down because the crowds. When it gets crowded, it can be overwhelming. Overall, worth it though.

This place is great! I got the Georgia Gold chicken the basket with the three pieces, and it was so good. I was able to get an extra piece for free. It was crispy. It was a little salty tho. For $5 and some change, I was Able to get that the four pieces of chicken and a small bowl of sweet corn. I'll be back

How LUCKY I was to have this gem just across the street from my hotel. The weather was absolutely terrible the weekend I went but I still ventured out (a tad bit hungover might I add) but the puncturing smells of SUCH GOOD FOOD woke me right up. My first stop? 
1) Beck's cajun (came straight here on my second day as well). The Mac & cheese balls were absolutely delightful. Fried, crunchy and absolutely delicious. Each bite oozed a perfect portion of Mac and cheese into my mouth. Each order comes with two pieces (and I most definitely did opt for additional orders my second visit here). Also, the jambalaya topped with gumbo?!?! Ugh, where else can I get something that rich in flavor here in NYC. I definitely miss that the most. Although two completely different dishes, they didn't contrast each other but instead, complemented each other very nicely. Also, I tried the sandwich that they display in the glass (seasoned ground beef sandwiched in the middle) and WHAT. THE. HECK. How can something be so simple yet be forever engraved in my taste buds?! You ruined me. 
2) the oh so famous DiVi (?? I'm so sorry- my mind was completely boggled I couldn't really remember the names). Not a huge roast beef fan- or so I thought... the portion is big. I shared one with my boyfriend and we weren't able to finish (but maybe it's because we ordered way too much elsewhere)
3) the cured meat/ deli meat stand- I haven't been to Barcelona but my boyfriend has and he was immediately reminded of his food experience there one bite into the prosciutto. We were shamelessly grabbing at the prepackaged back and ripping it apart like complete savages while walking around
4) there's a corn dog stand- the chili fries!! Don't knock it till you try it. I've had fries EVERYWHERE. Literally. I always make an excuse to order fries with every single one of my meals. How fries manage to stay crispy under the layers of chili? I'll never know
What's not to love!!?? I love everything about this place. Great food and good people. My only suggestion would be to have some patience.  This place is often crowded.

Great Place!
Large selection of meats, cheeses and fruits.

I just want to keep going back until I've tried every single stall! This is a haven for someone that loves all types of food and is very adventurous. On the other hand, if you're indecisive and stumble with too many choices, you may end up being there all day. Either way, you'll have fun! I went to RTM every chance I could get while in Philly and will go there again when I return!

This is one of my favorite places in the city.   It has more eating places than food stands, but thats OK.    I usually go on a Saturday morning before it gets too crowded or sold out.  Perfect time.

I love Martin's Meats for the sausage.  Tons of variety and fresh.  

The produce my Iovine is inexpensive and local, which is a plus.  Some of the fruit can't sit too long, so make sure to consume soon after buying. 

I love the Amish stands and there are a few.  Beilers Bakery is one of the best Amish Bakeries, definitely don't pass up a donut!

Lots of good cheese from Valley Shepard Creamery and be sure to try a grill cheese.

The best gyro I have had in the city is at Olympia Gyro.  

I could go on and on.  

It definitely gets touristy, but once you get past that and get used to it, it makes dealing with the crowds a lot easier.  Also, if there is a convention in town on the weekends, it will be super packed.

I'm not too experienced when it comes to markets (I have been to St. Lawrence Market in Toronto, but only twice), but this place just seems to be such a dive. It's so big and there's so much variety in terms of food available.

One thing you have to remember is that these markets are mostly family owned and have local ingredients. Sure, they may be slightly more expensive, but you're supporting the local economy, local families, and most importantly you get food in return!

As a tourist in Philadelphia, I highly recommend this place. Grab a philly cheesesteak, because it's just one thing you have to do when you're there.

I always always always love going here. It's a Philly experience that needs to be had. The atmostphere, the people, the food and different vendors. It's a must for visitors and locals alike. I have been many times and have eaten my way around that place. Miller's has the best pretzels and lemonade. Dinic's sandwiches are to die for. The Dutch stall has some delicious take home desserts. There are also some great cuts of meat for good prices. Basically everything you want is here.
If you eat food, you'll love it here.  Wander the halls of food, and you can have whatever your little heart desires

We have gone to Philly just to eat Amish food in the market. We have been to Grand Central Terminal Market in NYC, Union Station in DC http://www.unionstationdc.com/shopping
Pikes Place in Seattle http://www.yelp.com/biz/pike-place-market-seattle#query:Pikes%20place
And several other cities that have  similar markets. This is our favorite due to the Amish food. http://www.yelp.com/biz/dutch-eating-place-philadelphia#hrid:PjeZ1xDZZEsaCkd5_NzYeQ/src:self
There is fresh produce, restaurants , pretzels, ice cream,  and everything you might want to buy as others have already pointed out. Parking is usually pretty easy. 
It is worth a trip from NYC just for the market! 
I have to give it 5 stars for having Amish food since I have not encountered Amish food at other big city markets.
Amazing place.. anything you could want to eat is here .. very busy .. very fun.. would highly record a visit if your in the area

Everything and anything you could ever want from a farmers market.  I would highly recommend going on a weekday for your everyday grocery needs, but if you want a great breakfast, brunch, or Saturday lunch definitely going to Molly Malloy's for a great burger and stout or the Down Home Diner for large filling portions and bottomless coffee just like at gradma's house.

If you are looking to get the full Reading Terminal Market experience, go on a Saturday morning, by 8AM.  You will be able to smell all the meats being roasted, hear the sounds of the market, and taste one of Beiler's Bakery famous dutch donuts (I'm PA Dutch AKA German, and these are the real deal!).  Beiler's is not open on Sundays so be sure to make it there early on Saturday to get your donut fix, before the long line begins.

Also, Olympic Gyro is one of my favorite spots located in the middle of the Market, near the front.  It is family owned and the grandmother still makes their delicious Spanakopita, which is heavenly.  No matter when I go to Reading Terminal Market, I always get a slice of spanakopita from Olympic Gyro.

I adore this place! It's a go to every time we can't agree on where to eat or if we have friends in town and want to take them somewhere unique to eat.

I have still yet to even try a quarter of the places in RTM - but Flying Monkey Bakery, Dutch Eating Place, Beiler's Donuts, and Olympia Gyro are a few I've tried. 

I also love the fresh produce stands and the fact that the Amish are represented really well here - you can't go wrong at any of their food, bakery or meat stands.

In addition to the wide variety of tasty food - I like the layout, it makes it really easy to navigate. RTM is set up on a grid and each row is labeled a 'street name' which makes it simple to find a person or place fairly fast.

terrible. i dont usually hate on a place but this one blows. chick fila in general is awesome. but this one in particular is the worst. we went there during customer appreciation day. the promo is if you dress up like a cow, you get a free meal. we have been going to chick fila for years, and the four guys at the office really look forward to it every year. we did our usual cow drawing contest and posted them on our shirts. we go there and the jerk manager says thats not good enough. seriously. on customer appreciation day. never going back there and the four of us will continue to badmouth this terrible dining establishment.
Still a great place after all these years.  Plenty of vendors and plenty of variety.  Definitely a Philadelphia institution and a good place to stop for a fast lunch or great groceries.

The soft pretzel at Reading Terminal Market is the BEST.  You won't be able to eat any other pretzels for a while after tasting the real stuff.  The way they are making it.... soooo great.    I cannot wait to go back there...  Other venders are also really great.  Some produce are rather expensive, but they are all quite worth it.

It feels slightly unfair to lump all of the different vendors into one category, and for places I've been I'll try to be a bit more specific. But I'm still rather impressed at the immense variety of shops spread out throughout the region. Sure, there might be a dud once in a while, but there are countless grocers, each who carry things you don't typically see in your typical supermarket. It can get pricey in a hurry, but there is a great selection and the things I've gotten have been high quality.

#unpopularopinion but I HATE reading terminal market. It is a complete tourist trap. Lines are long, food is subpar and seating is a nightmare. Be prepared to fight off overweight suburban moms and their hoards of unwashed kiddies. If you need your fix of one of the shops in reading terminal, I recommend getting it and getting out.

Uncomfortably crowded with oblivious and rude tourists.  They're qued up like lambs to the slaughter for cheesesteak.  I'm baffled by the directive that a cheesesteak sandwich is a mandatory ritual when in Philadelphia.  However, great food, pastry and ice cream selections abound.  Crafts are pricey and not fashionably relevant which explains the non-existent crowd at the register.  T-shirt and souvenirs of that ilk are top dollar and low quality. Epic visual, auditory and claustrophobic experience.  You might like it and I don't judge. Just watching out for those who may go fetal just inside the door.  Love to all.

Wife & I go here for her "chocolate fix" during a certian time of month (TMI?)....:) 
This place is awesome for the freshness of it's food, the variety and the wholesomeness of the Amish foods. I have to budget myself because one can go broke in here!

My only complaint is trying to find decent parking.
Great place for tourists even locals. If you want fresh poultry, try Godshalls meat market.
Amazing food. Great produce. Can't go wrong with a trip to the Reading Terminal Market.

Awesome food market- you can find anything and everything you're looking for under one roof. I've never seen RTM in a state other than bustling, and it usually take a little hunting to find a table to sit down and enjoy your food. Be prepared for it to be pretty crowded, but its all part of the experience.
Lot of variety of food. Just some of these people have eye ball problems by whatever Im just going to avoid the issue and walk by all the clutter mess.‍
Amazing market, anything you would like under one giant roof.  Quality goods and a real Philly gem.  A must see!

Reading Terminal is the place to go for fresh and delicious items. I love Basset's Ice Cream, it's my top favorite ice cream ever. Alot of the other stalls have fresh Amish items, Italian specialties and seafood. Like the tastiest Po' Boy sandwich I've ever had. Can't wait til' my next visit!

This place is bad even for subway standards. The bread was really stale. Server was stingy on toppings. Meat barely covered 2/3s of the bread. They don't even have water cups so you have to buy a drink just to have any beverage. No reason to go here again.
Best place in Philly for lunch or food to go. Been coming here over 35 years.

Step 1: Watch Food Inc. on Netflix
Step 2: Visit the Redding Terminal

Then....absorb how this country has ruined food for us. This place, on the other hand, has fresh meat, veggies, pickles, deli meat, bread, baked goods and more!

Truly an amazing place...its what I miss in NYC, because you can't have this in a big city - they can't handle the traffic.

Philly u did this one right, a gem of a place, and what we should all look at for how we want our food!!
Awesome place. Great food. Great atmosphere. Great service. I highly recommend the Freda Beef Brisket Burger. Be sure to add the bacon. Will definitely return for another meal.

If you are in Philadelphia, the Reading Terminal Market is a must visit spot. Every taste of Philadelphia, and really the world can be found here. The smells, the shops, the people, it's always such an amazing experience. 

You want an amazing roast pork sandwich, it's there (DiNic's). You want a delicious Jewish deli, it's there (Hershel's). Chocolates and candy, it's there. Amazing Amish food, yup. Delicious soft pretzels, pastries, small vendors, meats, fish, fruits, veggies, you can find it all in the market. 

There are also parking garages that give you discounted parking with a validated ticket. If you spend $10 in the market, which is easy to do, that vendor will validate the ticket for you!

More like a 3.5.

I love Indian food and the rolls here are great.  They also should get bonus points for carrying Thums Up soda (a really hard to find Indian Coco Cola).  However, I can't get behind this place enough to eat here more often.  I just wish that the platters weren't so Middle-Eastern inspired.  They're really similar to the Halal carts' platters that have pita bread and "white sauce" (some type of mayo?).  It makes me wonder why I wouldn't go to a lunch truck instead.

The place has a wide variety of everything you could imagine. If I worked in Center City, I would come here almost every day (wallet permitting).

In my opinion, every food is slightly over priced except for the actual supermarket. The pasta is freshly made and I made a delicious pasta dinner that night with fresh vegetables as well. 

It is certainly worth it to come here to experience every culinary delight you can think of

Great place but I really have to be in the mood. Cramped, crowed, touristy gourmet, over priced foods. Some good deals here and there but I think it's the name and history that sells it. Fresh and organic items everywhere!!  Love the Home Diner!! A trendy traveler's or urban socialite's dream come true!

Best place to go explore, take your kids your date your friends here it's always an adventure..I must've go here at least once a week it's addicting. Iovine, meats at Guinta's Prime Shop, $1 cookies after 530 at 4th Street cookies, Dinics is the best pork sandwich, soft pretzels from Millers, Beilers donuts and the coconut creme pie damn is good, the ribs also across are amazing can't say enough good things about Reading Terminal. It's one of the best reasons to check out Philly!

The only bad thing that I can say about Reading Terminal is that as someone who lives a short walk away I certainly do not go enough.  Every time I do go I kick myself for not going more.  I love the lamb gyro platter at Olympia and the produce market is just awesome.  There are lots of affordable options here that would be pleasing to even the most discernible palate. If you have not been here GO!

It is a crowded market place. I had some super delicious bbq ribs, mac n cheese from this Amish food place  in there. They have delicate chocolates, cookies, ice cream but, also carry a variety of food styles under one roof. It was a different experience for me.
Try the Indian place. They have a spicy baked salmon. Pair it with spinach and vegetable rice.

LOVE this place!!! 

What's not to love about?? You can find EVERYTHING you need, and everything you don't!!! 

The worst part about this place is trying to narrow down what you're going to eat because there are so many great options - save room for a Fluffernutter cupcake from Flying Monkey Bakery! 

Asian food, ice cream, Philly Cheesesteaks, Beer, Wine, Olive Oil, fresh produce, salami, cheese, Amish people, hippy stuff, smoothies...Why haven't you been here yet?!? 

Best tip I can offer (other than aforementioned Fluffernutter cupcake) is to try to avoid peak eating times (like noon - 1pm and 4-5pm)

As a native Philadelphian I have found memories of the Reading Terminal Market, the food here is excellent and there is always something interesting and delicious to try. Many people I know shop here habitually for their groceries and I get the vibe that the shop owners are loyal to their customers which they show through providing high quality products for reasonable prices. 

If you're throwing a gathering you can find all your exotic cheeses, dips, and breads here.  If you're preparing a dinner you can find all the essential spices an ingredients you will need to prepare almost every dish you can fathom. You can also find other interesting items at the Reading Terminal Market; besides food you can buy books, candles, and holistic body products as well.

What can one say?- the best Market in the USA! Love love love this place'
Hoagies, gyros, deli sandwiches all compete attention-add fresh flowers, vegies, fruits, meats and seafood!!

My personal faves- middle eastern bakery, the original turkey-amazing sandwiches

My beau and I stayed in a nearby hotel for a great weekend. The terminal was next door to our hotel. We decided to go in and grab some breakfast before the game. We ran into Pearl's Oyster Bar. Two seats were readily available at the counter. I like the feel of an old school diner in the middle of a bustling market. The waiter was cool. We both decided on excellent choices. He got the crab cake and eggs benedict and I got the oatmeal and egg w/cheese sandwich. All good choices and quick. The service was great as was the food.

Later after the game, we decided to stop in for a cookie and ice cream at Bassett's Ice Cream and Famous 4th Street Cookie Company. The ice cream is super fresh and definitely homemade. The cookies are $1 if you make it in 15 mins before closing.

I would definitely go back on my next trip to Philly.

SERIOUSLY! SERIOUSLY! I didn't there were European style permanent markets like Europe in America. it was like an American Boqueria! part Farmers Market and part Food Court this place is amazing.
I wondered to myself why doesn't NYC have one of these.

I went in early to get Dinic's Roast Pork and then returned for flowers, eggs and sausage! As wandered the aisles of produce, meats and candies. Also cheese steaks, gyros, Chinese food and even a bar. I found my happy place. It is places like this that make me happy!
So many awesome places to eat. I love the bakery, and I don't think I've ever had bad food there! Definitely worth a visit.

Ok spot for the area. Always something to try to catch the experience of while it town but avoid the main food times; breakfast, luch, dinner hours. Try to go off the main clock hours as it can be a very busy, crowded place and much overwhelming if you have never been. 

Plenty to choose from bit some spots that are listed with great ratings of course have lines you will need to be prepared to wait it.  They do tend to move quickly and the staff at each place is well adapted to the crowds and rush. All 4 places we visited were pleasant,  quick and the food was good.  Seating is scarce but there is some places that have counter seating. And there is a larger area that has multiple tables but again just not really a sitting type place due to the crowd.  An order and go place.

Such a large selection of food! Much of the food is simply excellent. But beware of high prices.

My favorite stop in here is the Creperie. Sweet and savory crepes with fair amount of food stuck inside.
Philly at its finest. If you visit, you can't leave without a stop here for a cheese steak at whatever stall you end up choosing. You really can't miss.
Wrong posting...redacted. I actually love Reading Terminal Market

I love the Reading Terminal. It reminds me of European markets because it has so much to offer. You could come here with picky friends and you would all find something that suits you.  It gets pretty busy, so if you don't like being around a lot of people, you probably wouldn't enjoy this.

As far as food goes.  5 stars just doesn't say enough.

Everything you could possibly want to taste.

I come from Chicago, and only wish there was something here that matches the quality of food at the RTM.  

Yes we have a market too but for real, this one is KING.  

*I had Dinic's but I seriously struggled with all of those choices

Try to go when it is NOT crowded, like a Tuesday at 2:30 for example.

This place is awesome! You can buy really good and really cheap produce here (Iovine Brothers, OK produce (the name is definitely a misnomer)), and also get really good food! Di Nic's sandwiches are some of the best sandwiches you will eat in the northeast. Afterwards, you can cool off with ice cream from one of the oldest vendors in America, Basset's. Reading termninal also houses good fresh meat and seafood shops, although I have personally not shopped for meat there. All in all, a great shopping environment, with a lot of treats to offer.
In my opinion of the 10 top places to visit when In Philly. The variety of ethnic food you can get her is amazing. I come to buy the produce and to buy Amish made apple dumplings. Yummo!

If you are looking for a good dessert at the market and you happen to love cupcakes then I would really recommend that you try Flying Monkey Patisserie. The cupcakes there are just amazing! I live in NY and I visit philly every few months and always have to pick up some cupcakes from this place.

The frosting is amazing and the cake itself is moist and just delicious. Great combination.

My personal favorite is the Pink Rose, a cupcake that is made with either poundcake or chocolate cake and then topped with raspberry buttercream.

So good!

Reading terminal market I Love. It is a little crowded but There use to some of these in NJ but they have gone away. 
There is something for everyone. Somethings are pricey but there are good local deal to be found. All types of foods are here. there is something for everyone. 
If you are in Philly this is a MUST Visit.

If you like food -- there is no better place than Reading Terminal.  EVERYTHING you could possibly want is there.  Walk in & you're overwhelmed by aromas abound &  a seizure of food imaginary.

Fresh baked goods, cheesesteak, delis, chinese food, fresh seafood, produce, candy shops, custom chocolates, amazing cookies, homemade ice creams.  You'll be tempted to buy and try everything.  Good thing or bad thing?!?!  My tummy says yes but my wallet says no.  =)

This place is a foodie paradise! A food mecca! A venerable feast for all your senses! You can find just about everything. I tried: 

1) Roast Pork Sandwich with greens & provolone from Tommy DiNic's: this is probably the obligatory must-eat thing for tourists. So lines are really long and wrap around. Personally, I thought it was average...bland even. 

2) Juice from Four Seasons Juice Bar: You can choose one of their selected combinations or you can take destiny in your hands and make your own juice. Improvise, don't be scurred. 

2) Doughnuts from Beiler's: Lines are long but since there're no Amish where I live, so I wasn't about to miss a chance  to try out Amish baked goods. And they're even dressed in their cute little Pennsylvania Dutch outfits hehe.

Have been there 3 times since they've opened. The first time I went, the chips were stale. The second time, the chips were better. I always get the chicken bowl which is always good. The food is consistent and the service not bad. I got thru the line fairly quickly each time. So happy there's Chipotle in NE Philly!

What can I say
Iovine brothers
Little Thai Market
Martins
La Davisi
Keven Parker
Termini Bros
Metropolitan Bakery
Herschels



I'm trying to make a purchase from every vendor in the market by this time next year

I got used to potbelly living in the mid-west a few years back and was happy to find this location on city ave.  It was lunch time and the place was not busy so maybe the idea has not taken off but the sandwich was very good just as i remembered it.
Awesome market in center city. Hundreds of options for meals, coffee, meats, cheeses, handmade jewelry, etc. Highly recommended!

my go-to spot with my roommate.  I love it here.  the bartenders are great and so is the food. 

Must try:
- Seafood BLT b/c it is AWESOME (crispy calamari with a spicy chipotle aoili sauce)
- ALL their brunch options on the weekend b/c they are amazng

Loved it! Wide variety of food to choose from. The place was very clean my favorite was the ice cream and the soul food place.
I cant remember the name of the ice cream place but it was near the entrance.
I am such a foodie i will defintely be back to try other vendors.

You'll never find such a diverse, unbelievably great, mass group of eateries in one place! No one will leave this place hungry or dissatisfied if they give this place a chance. You name it they have it, Cajun, Italian, Dutch, Asian, Greek, sandwiches, turkey, pasta, gyros, ice cream, and much more!! Fresh meats, seafood, vegetables, and bakeries! It truly is a wonderful place to visit and experience!

So many things to choose from!!!  I'm an indecisive person this place was great for me, I asked around for about an hour before deciding! (Don't judge)...this is my second time being here even tho I've lived in Philly my while life and I think this place just gets better and better every time. I ate at a place where the name escapes me at the moment but it was like a little soul food buffet and they weight it and ya pay, the fried chicken is amaze ballz!!!

#amazing. That's all.
Jk. This place really has it all. Just about anything food you can think of can be found here. Be weary of going during lunch as it will be very packed and busy. Also it has clean bathrooms!

The only place in Philly to get your Taiwanese Fried Chicken Steaks! Of course nothing can beat authentic Taiwanese Chicken Steaks, but this hits home. I've been going to Flushing to get my Taiwanese food fix, but now I can my chicken steaks right here in Philly and the meat sauce over rice (one of the best ones I've had). The squid platter is pretty good too.

This place is a Philly staple. If you are from out of town it is a must. I have been here so many times. From the Dinics Roast Pork sandwiches to the Beilers Donuts, you can't go wrong.
It is huge and so many options. Deserts to oysters. They have it all. You won't be disappointed.
It is also across from the Philly Convention Center.
It is a must, stop in for your meal. Hint of advice, don't come between 11:45-2:00pm. Packed for lunch.

My favorite place in Philly! There are so many options. I don't know where to start. The icecream is good, the Peking Deck sandwich is good.. The seafood is fresh. The soul fried chicken is good as well! Everything is great here!

Often quite crowded, and to be honest some places are not that good, and everything is a bit pricey.   General tip do not bother getting any Asian food here, go to Chinatown which is on Arch and Race Streets between 12 and 9th.  Some of the same places but will be cheaper  The jewish deli is good as with a cajun place.  Stay away from the English pub, the food there is not good and overpriced.

Donuts, beer jerky, breakfast, lunch, sea food anybody? This place has it all.  Came here in the morning and started of with a great eggs and pancakes breakfast. Waited in line for fresh Beriler's donuts which were delicious. Walked around some more and found probably the best beef jerky ive ever had sold by the amish.  Its like a mall of all kinds of different food. Really cool place and cant wait to come back.

I have visited the Reading Market perhaps hundreds of times over the past 25 years. As a vegan, I would expect more fresh vegetables but am always sadly disappointed. In fact, the quantity of butchered meat on display and the smell of blood can make for a very unpleasant experience. A great vegetarian restaurant in the Market, "Basic 4," recently closed and now houses a shop that only sells lamb! Today, I spotted entrails and baby octopus on ice -- stomach-turning. This said, Iovine Brothers is 1 of only 3 reliable produce stalls in the market. Easily, 85% of the vendors are butchers or meat-pushers ... but DO seek out the fresh food farmstand or Iovine brothers if you care about suffering on the planet and if you care about your own health and longevity. Added bonus: The Flying Monkey bakery has vegan cupcakes and cookies! This market is extremely over-rated, and be prepared to dodge/ignore beggars who stalk neighboring sidewalks for tourists.

This place is great for locals and visitors! When I lived in Philadelphia, I would come here for some fresh produce. As a visitor for a conference, I stopped by here for lunch multiple times. It gets very packed and has very little seating, but there are so many great options! I love the atmosphere of this place. Each eatery has it's own personality and sitting at the bar is a great place to get close to the action!

Interesting concept. I tried the kale frida although now that I understand how it works I'll have the courage to go in and make my own bowl selections. 

Kale Frida was pretty good although the black bean paste was a little weird. 

If you make your own bowl you can get 5 veggies and one grain from what I was told. 

You can add a protein for extra. Today I tried the chicken sausage and it was delicious. Not sure how healthy it was because it tastes really good. 


The staff was super awesome. It's like a factory line of people assembling the bowl and each one was so nice. They really were going out of their way to be pleasant. 

I ate in and was pleased to see a worker wiping down tables and keeping the place tidy. One of the guys passing through with the trash asked if he could clear my bowl since I appeared to be done. So unnecessary but thanks for going out of your way I really appreciate it!  

I'm a fan of this place. Healthy fresh and clean. I'll be back but next time with husband and baby.   I just wish they had longer hours! I would totally eat here for dinner if I could make it over before they close.

Masala Kitchen worked with us for our holiday party. The kati rolls were excellent, the service was impeccable, and it was all around a wonderful experience. We highly recommend them for casual meals or larger office parties and will definitely be working with them again in the future.
Wasn't enough time or stomach space to sample all they had to offer. Italian hero's, pastrami, desserts ....

Reading terminal market is FULL of FOOD. (A lot of great food and a lot of average food).
Great produce. Delicious sandwiches. Hershels!!! mmm.
Great chocolate! at Chocolate by Mueller! A little overwhelming at first and can be crowded, but amazing. Plenty of seating.

it's a fun place with many vendors,
it was crowded every single time we went there (on almost a dozen occasions)
I highly recommend the Beiler's Bakery, and several of their eateries. 
Reading terminal is also the only place I know of that offers chocolate covered onion (as a gag present)
a definite must see in philly

This market reminded me of Quincy market in Boston or Fisherman's Wharf in SF. I like these old school style of tradition. I was very happy to find out the most yummy whoopie pies I ever had. It had a long history.

This is definitely a tourist spot, but I come here anyway. The Elvis Cake at Flying Monkey is to die for. Also, the pastrami and the brisket at Hershels is delicious. I always end my trip with fruit from Iona Bros. and hit the butcher across from them.

This review is LONG over due. 

I came here after finishing a half marathon and I was craving something sticky, sweet and all around bad for me. 

I walked the market and was overwhelmed with the smells, variety and overall friendly nature of all I met. 

I decided on the crepes stand and ordered the breakfast crepe which was filled with eggs, cheese and some veggies of your choosing. As expected this was light and tasty. The crepe was very savory but not overpowering or dense. Which was PERFECT because I had already selected my dessert; a nutella and banana filled crepe. 

Talk about motivation to workout - this was amazing. Now I should warn you - I could eat Nutella out of the jar on a spoon but warming it up and adding in some banana makes it heavenly. 

Again the crepe was light, fluffy and a bit sweeter this time. They folded in the Nutella and banana slices to make a delectable sandwich. And to show that I am a loving individual I shared my treat with my two co-runners. We all loved it and if it wasn't for our time crunch could have eaten more. 

If you are in the area and want to see and taste a lot head on over.

Huge, huge selection of small businesses and high-quality products. It would take days to sample all the food here. The Bassett's location and the candy shop make me so, so happy. 

The only valid complaint I have is that the crowd is massive during peak hours...

Worst smoothie EVER! It's hard to mess up a smoothie....but it was so thick....and as soon as I started drinking it my stomach started hurting!!!! what the Heck! I've passed by this place a thousand times and I'm so sorry I stopped!

This place is absolutely a food lover's paradise. Coming from the West Coast, this place definitely reminds me of LA's Grand Central Market. In my opinion, Reading Terminal is even better! It is quite crowded in here, with so many vendors from all sorts of cuisines (American, Thai, Chinese, German, etc.) as well as the massive crowds of tourists. The food here is great and authentic. However, prices here are generally on the steep side. Owners are knowledgeable and friendly with their products. Make sure to stop by Beiler's Bakery for their amazing fruity pebble and blueberry donuts!
Wow what a place! Foodies paradise, you can even eat inside, great place to find good Italian food, meats, vegetables and fruits and pastries.

Amazing foot market and a must if you are in Philly.  Can be crowded on weekends but it's well worth it.  We got a little food from a few different markets. From amazing Chicken wings to a nice pastrami sandwich.

If you visit Philly this place is a must see stop! This indoor food market has everything imaginable. There are tons and tons of food choices everywhere you turn. So much so that it is a bit overwhelming! 

Boyfriend and I stopped here to get a Philly Cheesesteak. The line was long but moved rather quickly.

If you come please don't expect to find seating. All the seats were completely hogged and one lady was saving 3 seats for herself yet we never saw anyone sit down next to her. That's the only downside of this place. They really should create more seating for customers!

Amazing food & amazing selection. We went on a Saturday mid-day so it was packed. If you're okay with people, the no problem! I read the visitphilly.com article on the top ten places and I hit three. 

Flying Monkeys had great whoopie pies! November seasonal pies were lots of pumpkin combos. 

Tommy DiNic's had great sandwiches but wasn't the best I've had this trip. Plus they were out of Italian Sausage! 

Finally, Beck's Cajun Cafe was said to have good Po' Boys, but I HAD to try the Gater Gumbo! I was not disappointed!!! Yum! 

I could go to the market everyday until I tried something at each stand. 

This is definitely a spot to try even if not for a meal, but for the experience.
Absolutely the best place to go in Philadelphia. Could spend an entire day there trying to decide what I want to eat!
Very good customer service. Free wifi. Grab food and drink- sit back, relax. They will come around to ask if you want refills and clear your food when it's done. Top of the line fast food.
Love going here to get food. Haven had a bad experience yet. Plus they have fresh produce and meats and best of all Blue Mountain Winery.

Great food. I had Aloo Paneer roll and enjoyed thoroughly. Don't forget about the excellent mango lassi and some sauces for your food. My food was up quickly and the employees are very helpful. The place is clean and fresh with a younger college crowd. Highly recommended.

This place is fantastic! So many places to eat and pick up some great take home food. My first stop was at Delilajahs Southern Cooking for some Mac and Cheese. It was good...but not as good as OK Cafe in Atlanta. And I paid $5 for a small taste, which was shocking. My next visit was to Carmes Philly Cheese Steak....awesome cheese steak. I also went to Dinic's....fantastic Italian Beef sandwich. I also picked up some cake and cannoli's from Termini. Fantastic Bakery!! Picked up some cookies from 4th street.

Best food hall on the East Coast. Something for everyone and a slice of local Philly culture. I'm a Philly ExPat and I try to stop in there on each trip. There is food for every taste and a fantastic selection of fresh meat, fish and vegetables. Fantastic baked goods as well. You can't go wrong.
Chicken was burned. Chips were tougher than rocks to chew. Staff is not polite. Please avoid this place if possible!
Fun place to walk around and find treats and goodies! There are vendors for snacks, drinks, food, candy, gifts, and restaurants. So much to do and see inside!

Like many of my review, I was in town for business and saw that my hotel was near the Reading Terminal Market.  I love places like this!

I only wished my wife was with me, we enjoy traveling and enjoy walking through big open markets like this.  

The Reading Terminal Market is exactly like the markets in Toronto, Cleveland and other cities across the world.  It's full of local vendors selling fish, meta, sausage, fruit, veggies, unique local fair and peppered with eateries.

Being in Philadelphia, I had a cheese steak of course.  The sandwich was good but being from Chicago and being familiar with a similar sandwich it was hard to compare to a good Italian Beef.  However, the sheese steak was good and the experience was awesome.

You're lucky to have a such place if you live in Philly, and if you don;t and you're in town for business or to watch your local NFL team beat the Eagles (DA'BEARS!), make the stop for lunch.  It's worth it.
One of my favorite places in Philadelphia. You can get so many different things here. Defiantly worth checking out.

Love Reading Terminal Market.  A lot of variety to choose from at decent prices.  Farmer's Market, Dutch Amish baked goods/ pretzels, Crepes, Greek, chocolate/cookies, wine, take your pick, they probably have it!  Go, get lost in it and you'll find something you love.  

FYI, if you park in the lot at 12th and Filbert, take your parking ticket in and have it validated at a vendor and you'll get $4 for 2 hrs in the parking garage!

Masala kitchen is a weekly staple for my boyfriend and I . It's great for vegetarians and omnivores alike. I think these Khati rolls might even be better than the ones from the Khati roll company in NYC. I've never been disappointed . Delivery is always delivered sooner than expected and the rolls are always delicious. Plus, the prices are very reasonable !
There is nothing more to say.. this place is amazing.. cheepest groceries in Philly (outside Italian Market).  Amish sections are closed on Sunday, so beware.

What can I say that hasn't already been said?

This has to be the best market on Earth.  Anything you want is in here, and it's probably excellent.

Do not leave without getting Bassetts ice cream!!

Lots of variety, lots of fun!

You can find everything here, from a standard salad bar, to fish places, sushi, chinese, middle eastern, Italian, Greek, Jewish, German... It's going to be hard to decide on a place to eat!

Besides the food places, they also have fresh produce, fish, meats, books, crafts, gifts, candy, chocolates, pickles and jams (Amish), ice cream, bakeries, coffee...

Note: about half the places are closed on Sundays, but we found a live band there on Saturday...?!!
Head right to the Thai place in the middle of the market.  CHEAP!  Great Food!  Long line moves fast.  Excellent Tom  Kai Gai soup, Salmon Salad.  GO
Definitely a lot of different variety of food and good for tourist in one place.
I love going down to the Reading Terminal I get lost with so many of them different shops different cheeses and meats and restaurants it's such a lovely experience I go there at least twice a month

I love this place! If ever in Philadelphia, this is a *must* stop! 

I loved the fact there were so many people and a foodie's haven. Anything you can think of, they have it here. Not only do the tourists eat here, the locals, too.

I love coming to the Reading Terminal Market for lunch.  My favorite places are the Little Thai Market, where my favorite dish is the salmon with a creamy red curry sauce that is delicious.  I also enjoy the 12th Street cantina, where everything they serve is yummy, but I epecially enjoy the chicken mole soft taco platter with your choice of rice, beans or salad.    

No matter what you are in the mood for, the Reading Terminal probably has it.
this place is the best on a Sunday AM!  Try the Amish breakfast place :)

LOVE this place. 1 stop grocery shopping, even for the items you can't get at regular supermarket.
The Dutch market is one of my favorite spots in RTM.
selection is great, love the bustle and variety, has afforadable options.
First time visiting from New York and it was good. Very crowded and noisy but lots of food for whatever your in the mood for.

Time to close this McDonald's down. Had to get my money back very BAD service and they just don't care. This restaurant is very dirty and the homeless is inside and outside asking for money. The workers there want $15.00 an hour there lucky to get $7.00. Please try to fix the problems there.

Update::
Came back on a busier night and definitely noticed a decline in the food quality. It was definitely more on the average bar food side. 
-------------------------------------------------

A friend and I went to Industry tonight for their Burgers and Bubbles special. We also came during happy hour and took advantage of those specials as well. To start, the ambiance was great. A nice rustic bar feel. Not a huge restaurant but a good comfortable size that I'm sure fills up on the weekends. 

Now onto the food. We started with the Mac and Cheese Croquettes that are $1 during happy hour. They are basically just friends balls of Mac and cheese. They don't sound super exciting but they were absolutely delicious. Perfectly fried and the sauce that came with them was delicious. We also split the Kimchee tot appetizer. They were also great with a nice crunchy outside and a creamy delicious center. For our entrees we both got the Monday Mystery Burger -- it had caramelized onions, fried pickles, dijonnaise and Swiss. The burger was smaller than you usually expect from a restaurant (they always seem so monstrous!) but it was the perfect size and to die for. Best part of all ALL of this food only cost $36. 

All in all I thought this place was great. I will definitely be back (especially for their Monday burger deals!)
