Pork roast and pancakes, all cheap, oh my!

I don't think we're in Kansas anymore.

We're in Heaven.

Cheers-

One of the coolest places on earth. You can find anything you can think of to eat here. Plenty of "Pennsylvania" food here as well as international fare too. If you are visiting Philly, you must visit the Reading Terminal.

Not sure how to rate the whole market, all the vendors differ. It a must stop if you're visiting philly for its variety but it is slightly overpriced being a tourism attraction. Hershels deli is a definitive stand out as is the ice cream place.

I hecka LOVE this place!  More than a fat kid loves candy!

Every single day that I was in Philly I made it a mission to come eat here at least once a day, maybe even twice if i found time to sneak away from my work.  I really enjoyed walking around eating bits of food here & there.  It's extremely inexpensive and the portions are huge!  I love the variety and that they sell seafood, poultry, chocolate, candles & everything you possibly can think of!  I wish I could try every single vendor there, but it would take me weeks and my clothes wouldn't be able to handle it!  A few of my favorite places are listed below:

Little Thai Market - you gotta try their Salmon & cream sauce, its da bomb!
Olympic Gyro - huge gyros & so delicious
Beck's Cajun Cafe - I really like the gumbo & their cornbread!
Profi's Creperie - you gotta try their dessert crepes
Spatoro's Cheesesteaks - you cannot go to Philly & not try a cheesesteak
The Grill @ Smuckers - cheap & fast service
Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialities - great selection of meal deals there

This is my favorite place to be in Philly.  I would come back just so i can eat here!
This place is the best.  Anything you could want, they have.  Don't bother going on Sundays as all of the Amish/Dutch places are closed, and they have some of the best booths in the building.
Classic Philadelphia spot!  This place is amazing, prices great, and there is so much variety in the places you can order from.

Omg the best pizza in town and we have some awesome pizzerias in town. The dough is chewy crispy and just so gooooooood. The fact that EVERYTHING is FRESH and NATURAL prolly has a lot to do with it as every single ingredient that goes into the pizza is fresh and without preservatives.  But the guys who are creating the pizza are artisans. They care about what they make. What a gem. I'm so happy.

This place is so amazing that recently I've made sure to book my hotels far AWAY from it because I cannot control myself inside the market! Seriously! The food is just okay, but the dessert places are heaven on earth. Love the strawberry cheesecake from the amish place, the chocolate chip cannoli on the other side of the market, the chocolate chip cookie brownie in the way other corner...omg I can't even walk out of this place with just one food item! Only reason it's not a five star is because I wish it were open later. Go here for dessert, you'll thank me later.

First off, if you live in Philly - or if you're just visiting - and you've never been here, you absolutely must go. This is an excellent place to get meat and produce for shopping- especially if you want fresh seafood- and it is an equally excellent place to stroll around, snack, grab a coffee, and browse.   (On that note there is a book store tucked in the back of the market that has an incredible selection especially if you're into esoteric, occult, or off-the-beaten-path type material. Some of it is downright bizarre- I found a book here by The Black Dot that talks about the "hidden Qabbalistic and sacred geometries of hip hop", which veers periodically into unfounded but entertaining rants about sacred Egyptian magicks.) 

Really, there isn't much I can say about the Reading Terminal Market that isn't good, unless if you're agoraphobic. Also, if you go here with friends and don't have a cell phone, expect to spend half of your time trying to figure out where the hell they are.
Who doesn't love reading term??? I mean, really? They have so much in here that it's not hard to find something you'll love about it.

Went to Industry late last week for a drink with a friend and for the most part it was an ok experience.  The beer was cold, fairly priced and if you're unsure, you can try a sip.  The specialty drinks were also pretty good, I had a Whiskey Sourpuss which was good since eggs make everything better.
The staff was more or less fine.  I can't say they were exceptional and it was kind of annoying that they were all milling around the bar with nothing to do, but what else could they do since it was early and I think only one or two tables had people eating, while the bar was getting crowded.  
We had a snack and the fries were not crispy at all, kind of like warm gummy worms in droopiness, but they tasted good.  The Indian BBQ Chicharrones were very crispy, but pretty bland.
To be perfectly honest, The Industry does not stand out or set itself apart from the typical Philly gastropub-style establishment.  Ok food, decent drinks, staff with visible  tattoos and a slight elitist attitude, and music just a little too loud.

A Philadelphia icon.  If you can't find something you love here, then you have no business eating out.  Tommy DiNic's roast pork, in my opinion, is the best in the city.  And yes, I've had the roast pork at John's, which in my opinion is second to Tommy's.  We also had oysters at Pearl's, which in my opinion, was nothing special.  The charm about Reading Terminal, though, is the overall variety of greatness.

my wife , my son and I really enjoyed the fried chicken and the fried calamari here. They have this massive cup of grape fruit green tea, very refreshing. I enjoyed hat as well. Definitely coming back here again.
Great place to walk around and get treats! It gets REAL crowded on the weekends so I suggest you go during the weekday BEFORE rush hour.
Love this place! It gets a bit crowded, so bring your patience or wait for a non-peak time.

Definitely worth checking out. This market has a wide variety of things from food, desserts to books. My go-to places are dinics, bassetts ice cream and beilers bakery and donuts. I recommend spending at least 2 hours just getting lost in here to see what Reading terminal market has to offer!

I've eaten here twice and have to say that I love the atmosphere. Dim lighting and a great restaurant/bar. Always good beers to try and a decent menu. Food comes out quick which is always a plus. However, both times I have been there the bread on the sandwiches was so hard you could barely cut through it with a steak knife. Time to get fresher bread! Especially with many sandwiches on the menu!!
My favorite spot in Philly ... Hands down. Great food and the employees are great.
I like just walking around there.  Great way to spend time between downtown appointments or events

Heaven on earth for a foodie like me!! What can't you find in here?  It's full of tons of yummies!  Doesn't hurt that they've got beautiful flowers for sale either.  The stuffed meats at the Italian places look to die for, so did the cheese rolls wrapped in prosciutto and basil!  I just wish I lived closer so I could've taken more home!!  The dumplings at the dutch place were pretty tasty, though not quite living up to all of the hype, but all of their breads looked amazing!!  Just a little on the pricey, side, unfortunately.  If I had a place like this at home, I would be there all the time!!

One of my favorite places. Discounted parking with validation in specific parking ramps - make sure you keep the receipts from locations you stop at. I will say this place can get really cramped/busy especially weekends. I love Hershel's Deli, Beliers Pickle patch, donuts and Baked goods. My husband loves Carmine's cheese steaks and DiNics pork sandwiches.  They have some sit down restaurants I haven't tried.

When I travel to any city in the world, going to the local market or a festive market is always at the top of my list. It's the place to go in Philly. Make sure you make your way through the maze of vendors before deciding on your samplings of the day. For those who seek out the famous names, head to Dinic's for their pork sandwich (choose this over a cheesesteak any day) and grab an assortment of $1 Beiler donuts. From Dutch Eating Place, Hershel's East Side Jewish Deli to Nanee's Indian Kitchen there is something for everyone.

The Paneer Masala Roll was tasted great and was priced well. 

The wait was a lot longer than the others on my group and something was wrong with their ventilation because it was extremely hazy inside.
great ice cream, sushi, kabobs, and a fun enviroment!
Phenomenal! Some of the best food in the world. It'll get a little expensive (8$ for 3 perogies?!) but I guess you get what you pay for.

If you are visiting Philadelphia and are not sure of what to eat, Reading Terminal Market is easily the best place to start! My uncle suggested I go there and I could not be more grateful! 

Lots of shops for touristy things to buy, t-shirts, small kitchen items, etc. Lots of choices for food to eat and food to use in your own cooking. It really is the largest and most unique market I've ever seen! If only supermarkets would go away and be replaced by thousands of Reading Terminal Markets (although it would lose a little bit of its appeal.)

My favorite spots were Famous 4th Street Cookie Company, Beiler's Bakery, Dutch Eating Place, Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe, Lancaster County Dairy, Bee Natural, 12th Street Cantina, Dienner's Bar-B-Q, and Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialities.

The Amish merchants are without a doubt some of the best foods I have ever eaten and what makes the market so special. I ended up buying 2 pounds of various chocolate fudges from Sweet as Fudge, 2 dozen doughnuts from Beiler's, an open faced turkey sandwich from Dutch Eating Place, a Strawberry Orange Lemonade from Lancaster County Dairy, and 3 chocolate chip cookies from Famous 4th Street Cookie Company. 

If you are driving in, make sure to get your parking validated when you spend at least $10 and can park in the garage on Filbert Street for just $4 up to 2 hours. You won't find a better deal for parking anywhere else in the city. When you don't have anything else planned, you can easily spend an entire day here and you'll love every minute of it!
This place is one of a kind! First time in Philly and this place was recommended highly by locals. It did not disappoint! So many delicious food options, fun shops and great people watching.
This place has everything. And it's not just variety--you're talking high quality stuff for the old school and the nouveau foodie alike.

You MUST visit Reading Terminal Market when visiting philadelphia! There's so many vendors to see, the food is great to sample, and the vibe is so fun. Definitely get an Amish donut while you're there. The vegetables are super fresh as are the meats for a great take away to them prepare your meals at home. Not terribly pricey.

Reminds me of markets in Spain, very crowded very busy place but was really nice. Went there as a tourist hop and the experience was so good. Lots of food to chose from but I tried Beiler's Bakery which had a long long line, took me 30 mins to get to buy pastries and donuts. A little extra sweet but liked them still
Also got some ice cream at Bassetts it was awesome!!
Come here, but be ready to be in a very crowded place specially on Saturday

This place is alway a gem, no matter which restaurant you stop in you can not go wrong. My recent visit I brought my friend who was visiting to DiNic's roast pork. Being a Philly native I am picky and I can say this is my favorite roast pork across the area. But like I mentioned earlier, you can't go wrong!

I love getting lost in the market. It is so much fun just to wander up and down the aisles and see what catches your eye. Sometimes it can be a bit overwhelming, but I love doing it. Famous 4th Street cookie right at the front is famous for a reason so stop by. However, there are some days when the Amish stores are not open so you may have to make a second trip on a day they are. 

I recommend a visit.

The Industry is a pretty decent restaurant in the location that it is at; I don't know of many restaurants here. There was quite a little space inside, but it was a little dark, and there is also outdoor seating. The bar area is pretty awesome, too. Overall, my experience here was pretty good.

Food
So I had their Industry burger with the Neuske's crispy slab bacon and fried egg (made easy over) that came with fries, my friends had Pulled BBQ Duck, Steak Frites, Fried Chicken, and the Fish of the Day dish, which was a fried bass with a tomato curry sauce on the side with arugula and mint. The steak frites, Fish of the Day, and my burger were amazing. The tomato curry was very exotic, so I liked it a lot, but it's not offered every day. The burger and frites were both somewhat typical, but the taste was really good (the bacon was amazing!). As for the Fried Chicken, it definitely doesn't worth $20. There were barely any chicken with the side of typical corn bread. I haven't really tried the BBQ duck sandwich. The food overall is good, but not great. I do like the fact that items on their menu change based on what's on the market and what they want to make (the fish and seafood BLT sandwich for example), so I'll probably come back a number of times to see what they have to offer. Some of their food is pretty expensive for what it  looks/sounds like it should be. 

Service
It was really good, in a way. The server was very thorough with what's offered on the menu, and what the "Dishes/Specials of the Day" were. He was very friendly and he did a great job for us since we weren't the easiest customers. We did go up to the bar to order a shot, but he kind of stopped us and sarcastically asked if his service was not good enough so that we had to order up at the bar. We ended up ordering from him, though. He got us 6 shots because we had 6 people, but we only ordered 5, so he gave us that extra one on the house, which was very nice of him. He definitely made our time there better than what it could have been.

Pros: Service, Decor
Cons: Fried Chicken, Pricing 

Recommendations: Industry Burger, Steak Frites

Pigs in a blanket from the Amish pretzel place. Do you really need anything else?

Another Philly staple that I've been visiting practically my entire life, but they've been switching things up a bit too much lately. It seems like every time I come home on break, another one of my favorite stands has disappeared or moved...what gives??

You're not human if you don't enjoy Reading Terminal Market!! 

They have everything you could want/need! However, I always tend to drift around the Amish because literally everything is amazing! 

If I lived closer I would visit more than 5 times a year, but everytime I do visit I leave with 10 bags

When it's not packed it's simply amazing for any culinary desire. Obviously the PA Dutch food is sublime, ice cream, produce, luxury baked goods, etc etc etc. Just good luck getting a seat to dine-in on the weekends!

So, how do you review an entire market!? I'll try.

First off, if you haven't been to similar markets in other cities, let me warn you that much like other ones, this place is packed. People that live here often visit it in addition to out-of-towners.

Unlike markets in other towns, many of the prices can't be beat. Grocery shopping and butchers sell at below market value a good amount of the time so it's hard to avoid going for fresh food. Grab some muffalata or alligator sausage. Also, unlike other markets, it can be hard to walk around at times. I've pushed a stroller through the past couple years without issue (despite my phobias), but unless you're used to all the people, it can be overwhelming.

Nonetheless, the smells and sights are more overwhelming, in a good way. When family comes to visit, they always want to hit Reading Terminal, which should tell you something.

this is my new go-to.  The staff is warm and friendly and the place is very clean.  I was so down when Marabella Meatball Co closed.  BUT.. this is a most welcome change. The chicken masala roll is DEELISHUSS!  I went back the next night to get it again.  I also gave the aloo paneer roll a whirl and it's also very tasty.  I see this place doing very well once the neighborhood realizes how great the rolls are.  I definitely recommend this place.  I'm sure bar goers will be happy with the weekend 3:30am closing time.

This is a historic landmark and has been open since 1892 when the Reading Railroad built a terminal that was going to displace the outdoor markets on Market Street. A compromise was reached and the old markets agreed to new space under the railroad station and tracks. A new convention center nearly pushed the market out in the 1980s but merchants and preservationists were able to get the market renewed and it has remained as a vital market, busier then ever. Fresh baked cookies at the entrance, Philadelphia made ice cream from Bassets down one aisle and fresh bread and poultry down another. It's an amazing conglomeration of food and wine and candy and people that can be seen no where else.
Love this place! Go there to eat, grab a beer...or just hangout! Really gives you a local vibe of what Philly is all about.
love yourself and get a roast pork from dinic's and a donut (or 12) from beiler's. you will not be disappointed and you can thank me later.

I mean.. it's okay. Everyone really hyped about this place but it was kind of underwhelming. The service was friendly, very small seating area and place in general, but the decorations were nice. They have a TV but it literally plays the same old 2005-ish clip of their food being featured on some Chinese show over and over again. Cash Only place, but they do offer an ATM. 
We got combo meals, but the portions were kind of small. A single cucumber slice and a teaspoon of seaweed salad, with two slices of some kind of picked vegetable and a sauce cup smaller than my own thumb (and I have pretty tiny hands.) It was actually kind of funny how tiny they were, but then again the price was pretty affordable so I shouldn't have expected much. 
The chicken we got (I think Samurai Chicken, where it's kind of like a chicken cutlet) was basically popcorn chicken from any bubble tea place--but bigger. And the Strawberry Calpis Soda I ordered was just sparkling/carbonated with chunky strawberry jam.. kind of gross. Didn't even combine, like it was plain sparkling water with random chunks of jam. Food wise was overall really really underwhelming. 
I guess this place wasn't bad, I just wouldn't really think of going back here, especially with the low portions and average taste.

I won't repeat what I'm sure a lot of other people have written. I'll just say that this place was a lot of fun, but you'll want to mind that most vendors close rather early especially on Saturday, and of course the Pennsylvania Dutch vendors are not open on Sundays. Therefore anything you want to buy, make sure you don't wait until last minute to do so! I had a lot of things I wanted to buy on Saturday afternoon, but didn't want to lug around all day, by the time we got back to the market around 4:30(ish) the vendors I had wanted to purchase from were closed.
This is a must see stop for any visitor to Philadelphia! Great food around every corner. Pastries, New Orleans food, Italian, and of course great beef and pork sandwiches!

I am envious of the magnitude and grandeur of all this enclosed market has to offer! We came here for breakfast and nearly stayed for lunch. We sampled a refreshingly simple Amish run breakfast establishment, had steamed chai tea made in single batches, ran into the largest pumpkin on display that I have ever seen, and left our hearts with the uncut, uncured bacon.

It is always a pleasure to go there. Tons of colors, flavors, aromas. Best espresso, bread and soft pretzels in town, among many other "bests". It is difficult to sit, especially groups, but the waiting time is minimal. Then you have the history of the place itself, right below a former iconic train station. A must see and experience in Philly.
Very cool place. So many choices. Noisy but that gives it the feel of a market. I loved it!

I can't say enough great things about this place. Our office is right down the street and we've ordered lunch for about 25 people twice now. The first time we ordered individually. 25 individual orders isn't easy, but they delivered on time and were friendly and courteous throughout the whole process. The second time, we ordered from the catering menu, and I highly recommend it. The menu is simple so it's very easy to order from. They also cut the kati rolls in half so people were able to mix it up and try different types. All were delicious! They also gave us plenty of plates and napkins and an insane amount of sauce. Everyone was very full and happy. 5/5, would absolutely recommend!

I love Reading Terminal. I go here almost every weekend to pick up fresh veggies, meat, fish, and a pound of freshly roasted Old City Blend coffee from Old City Coffee Company. I always try to hit the market on Sunday, Iovine Brothers Produce has a student discount and the market is much less crowded. The only downside to shopping on Sunday? All of the Amish stands are closed. Saturdays are insane, almost not worth going. There are just wall to wall tourists and you'll have to fight for the perfect piece of fruit at the produce stands. 

Favorite shops: 

Iovine Brothers Produce (fantastic fruit and veggies)

Giunta's Prime Shop (I always pick up a few chicken breast, ground turkey, and maybe some pork shoulder or steaks)

Ok Lee Produce (not as fresh as Iovine, but if you're going to eat what you buy the same day, the prices can't be beat)

Downtown Cheese (I looooove this shop. They force feed you a cheese while you're shopping. Also they carry Claudio's fresh mozzarella from Italian Market, delicious!)

The Head Nut (replaced the Spice Terminal with a larger, more navigable selection of spices, nuts, beans, candies, etc. )

Oh my gosh!!!! As a foodie - I have wasted too much of my life having never been here!  My husband and 9 month old decided to stop in before we started our 7 hour trip home to NC and man oh man I was literally like a kid in a toy store!  I don't even know where we stopped for food, snacks, chocolate, donuts, a mufalatta, Boylan cream soda out of the fountain but everything was awesome!  I actually almost cried because this market made me so happy!!(yeah, I know I sound crazy) Seriously though - if you enjoy good, amazing food and are in Philly - this is a must stop!!!

Not much else to say besides beware of crowds and move deftly.  Don't wander around looking at everything or else you'll piss the rest of us off who are trying to get some crawfish etoufee as fast as possible.  DiNic's just remodeled and are still the kings of hot sangwiches in the market, as far as I'm concerned.  Basset's is the best Ice Cream in creation, and I've never seen a straight up Bassets bar like that anywhere else.  Many Saturdays they'll have live music in the center, which can range in genre, but is always awesome.

Came multiple times already. Really like their foods with their fair price. However, only tried once their fried stuff. To be honest, I don't really like it. Not that crispy like their advertised. But try their teriyaki stuff or squid, these are really good. Also teas are pretty good and size is larger than other place. Definitely recommended and will come again.

We had a larger party last night, with a couple of kids and we all really liked the food and drink.  The burger was so juicy and the kale was delish. Plenty of beers to choose from too.  Service was good, when they brought out the wrong appetizer, they gave us the mistake - and brought what we ordered.  The benches we were on were not the most comfy but hey, they are benches.  Also - the white napkins left lint ALL over my black sweater and pants - an odd complaint but from what I understand that's been happening since they first opened.  Not sure if anyone has ever mentioned it to them but, man, I am now!  Otherwise, a delightful time was had by all.
Wow! Just walking in and smelling all of the delicious foods is well worth it! They have everything you could possibly be looking for food wise!

Lots of choices...just wish the seating area was cleaner, less congested and better maintained. Quality...not as high ranking as quantity. But it surely has its place when eating out with a  bunch of people with strong and different tastes. 
Oh and people who work there could try and look happier?!?

I have been here this afternoon,that was so so great!!i was got the ninja crispy chicken,that's was really really big! Seems like bigger than my face!! And the fried giant squid it's pretty good also!! And  if you get there don't forget get a green tea grapefruit!!!!  You have to try that guys!!
...I am absolutely obsessed with the Reading Terminal experience. I dare you to go in there for one or two things and not leave with 25 things!!
Awesome place.  Food you can't get anywhere else.  Especially ethnic foods.  Nothing fancy, just great food and deals.
Lots of amazing places to eat! It's a huge tourist attraction so be prepared to fight the crowds, but definitely worth the visit!

Easily my favorite place nearby to buy produce and proteins.  Turkey bacon is super reasonably priced, as is the steak at most of the vendors.  The seafood selection is pretty good, and the prices reasonable.  It is a great place to have lunch and do a week's worth of shopping on the weekend.
Golden Bowl  Fabulous The Absolute Best  Do Not Miss  friendly owners absolutely incredible Asian food. You will go back again & again!!!! Great Find !
duh. This place is amazing! Every sort of person in here. Cheap produce. Nice fish. Cheap fish. fancy fish. good coffee. They have it all. And the people watching is amazing. Just the best!

This is my second visit here and I think I could cheerfully spend a whole day here, aside from the crowds! What an amazing selection of wonderful food! We started with breakfast at Pearl's which even has real maple syrup. We stocked up on sausages, cheeses and baked goods and drooled over coffees, crepes and beautiful mountains of fresh produce. I love this place!

This is Reading Market...doesn't get better than this historic place. Choices, choices, choices...all tasty, and I have never had anything but great service from all vendors. 
A must when in Philadelphia. I am lucky to live close by....and shop here frequently.

Absolutely LOVE this place!!!  I actually get all of my produce here weekly - high quality & great prices.  There's also a ton of different places for getting unique gifts & of course amazing restaurants & bakeries

I love this place; in fact, it is my favorite place to go in Philly! I love seeing all the different fruits, vegetables, meats, oils, spices, and more in raw form. You can find just about anything here, and the atmosphere is always fun! Most recently, we had breakfast at Molly Malloy's and it was absolutely delicious. The fun part about it (besides the location) was the restaurant used ingredients and products from surrounding vendors. For example, the bacon that I had came from Halteman's which was located adjacent to Molly Malloy's. I love indulging in all the candies, chocolates, cookies, and cakes! Bring the whole family as it is a fun-filled, tight marketplace where you can find just about anything.
What's not to love, it's a Philadelphia institution. Whether you're shopping for your groceries or just stopping in for a quick bite, you'll find exactly what you need. Lunch time is very busy.

Whatever you want, it's here. It's chaotic and crowded and that's what adds to its wonderfulness. Bustling people mill around, pushing past each other to get at the varied collection of bakeries, eateries (featuring anything from samosas to the best mac 'n cheese (according to Oprah)), and produce stands. It truly feels like a market, and smells like great home-made food. There are tables off to the side, too, so while you can grab stuff to go, you can also sit down, and enjoy your food as you watch the chaos from the sidelines.

Great selection! There's truly something for everyone at RTM. Some personal favorites? The cinnamon raisin bagel with black raspberry cream cheese at the market bakery, the chocolate peanutbutter ice cream in a pretzel cone at the amish pretzel shop, and pretty much any grilled cheese at MeltKraft. Ugh, you really can't go wrong, but these 3 places get my business time and time again.

Solid dumplings and friendly staff! The dumplings aren't soupy here. I'd say there are more stuffed. We had the broccoli cheddar, the cheesesteak, roast pork and buffalo chicken. All were super delicious. You have the option to order the dumplings fried or steamed. The dumplings come with soy sauce,  ketchup  and ranch dressing. Dumplings come five to an order. They also offer dollar dumplings on Wednesdays! Give this place a shot!

Awesome spot. So many kinds of kati rolls and every one we tried was amazing. I'd especially recommend the lamb kebab, but the aloo paneer and unda were also incredible. Will definitely be back to try the rest!

Two rolls is a full meal and at about 5 bucks each, it's a hell of a deal (if you grab two of the not-cheapest ones, you also get a dollar off). 

The lassis are made in house, but come in cute to-go bottles, so even if you ate too much, you can grab one for later.

Solid McDonald's food. Don't expect anything amazing. However, and this speaks more to the franchise and not the location per se, when did they start producing their own orange juice and stop using Tropicana? Theirs is less orange juice and more like "orange juice flavored drink". It's definitely. It pure and is highly watered down.

Otherwise, the staff was friendly and my order accurate and hot.

The best food for any occasion.  From amazing pork sandwiches at DiNics to some of the freshest Seafood and Meat for fair prices in the city. Its where I go for a good meal, any variety, and general food shopping  when trying to avoid the overpriced supermarkets of center city.
We live right around the corner. Great place for a beer and some food. Food ambiance. Loooove the pig ear lettuce wraps!!
Great Kati rolls! Loved the beef roll and the chicken pepperwala! Definitely coming back for more!
Really a melting pot of culinary delights!  My favorites are Becks Cajun Cafe and of course DiNics Roast Pork, doesnt get any bettter than those two locations.
You can go insane in here! OMG, from Philly cheesesteaks, to Louisiana style food to some scrumptious Amish sweets. Inexpensive and centrally located, this is a must to visit!

Authentic cuisine from all over the world!
This is one of my favorite spots in Philly.

I'm a fan of this market though oddly equipped with amish employees that dresses the part too. I would not pass up the pastrami stand or the the cookie vendor... Those were definitely unforgettable experiences for my palate. :)

Great place, but is pretty crowded. The pastry shop just inside the door, where they sell the small cakes and such, they have bad customer service. None of their cakes or muffins are labeled as to what they are. One lady asked if I needed something, I was just in awe at the cakes and said I was just looking, to which she rolled her eyes and walked off. There are nicer pastry shops around. All because it was my first time at the Terminal and was trying to take it all in. Nonetheless, it's a unique experience and plan to go back many more times!

Worst wrap I've ever had. I took one bite and threw it in the trash, the lettuce looked like it had froze and thawed and the chicken was filled with pepper and fatty. So I opted for the fruit. With was $6 and not ripe. Go elsewhere!

We ate here twice on our two day visit to Phily. We have tried all the veg rolls and each is good, the paneer masala being my favorite. The spice level is perfect and it's not too hot.
Their chaas is amazingly refreshing, a must try.

So I've probably been here like 10+ times. I always try to get a cheesesteak from here. I love the icecream as well. 

There are so many choices for what you can get. Also, this place is packed. You can think of it as like a mini shopping plaza indoors. 

Great place to show people new to philly.

Seriously?! One of the best places in the country. Get anything you want to eat here. Really a fun place to visit and spend some time, eat some food, see some people. 

Check out more here:

http://www.cnn.com/2012/06/22/travel/smackdown-detroit-philadelphia-philly/

Love this place. Easy to get to by SEPTA and has lots of stuff going on. Really nice coffee and cookies (yes, I believe there is a reason why these two are next to each other). Delicious ice cream (coffee and mint choco chip). Definitely a touristy spot if you have visitors who are into lung or nose shaped chocolate OR chocolate frosted raw onions (yes, RAW onions, the whole thing).

My go-to spot for coffee and cookie if I happen to be around the area. Won't recommend going at lunch time because it will be crowded.

Love the variety!  Found Comice pears!!!  The cheese shop is amazing!  Roast pork sandwiches were killer!  As were the the brisket sandwiches.  Used to love the Dutch Eating Place but not so much.  Ok, so much for individual details, overall RTM is a great place to spend a good chunk of time discovering great foods.
I like Reading terminal market it has a lot of different varieties of food and markets. It can get very busy. The prices are outrageous. Beiler's bakery has great pickles.

This was our first stop after we arrived in Philly after 10-11 hours in a car and we were FAMISHED. Our Airbnb host suggested RTM, particularly because it was early-mid-afternoon and probably one of the 'less busy' times to visit (comparatively....it is *always* busy).

We walked over to the terminal and were immediately overwhelmed! So many people! So many lights! Smells! Options! CHOICES! 

The fourth star in this review is simply for the initial impact the place makes as a first impression!
The food options and locations within are impressive, but unfortunately what I got did not live up to expectations, therefore no fifth star.

If you are a Philly tourist, go here for the experience and the excitement! If you are hungry but don't know exactly what you want, go here because you will find something that catches your eye.

This is my grocery store and I am incredibly thankful for it every time I make the trek.  Not only can you get meat, eggs, veggies, bread and cheese, but also cooking gear, a beer, awesome breakfast, crepes, Italian cookies for business meetings and chocolates to take back home as gifts. Love it.  It's so Philly (though you do have to pay attention and avoid when there's a conference in town).

Wonderful hub for a diverse array of tasty eats. With a scene like this it's not just the food, it's the ambience and the experience that leave a mark. Depending upon time of day, it can be suffocating and a little too much for some. There's always an opportunity to meet other people from different walks of life and make a new friend, as this is a great forum to ask others for their favorites.

I recommend coming early in the day and or at an odd meal hour with family or a friend who can appreciate the fun of shopping around and picking the highlights that catch your eye on a given day. Too many delicious things to pick from, definitely a frequent visit for me and a memorable pit stop in the city.

This is a must visit for locals and tourists a like.  It's a great spot for lunch, to purchase meat and produce or crafts.  They are open every day; but the best days to go are later in the week as that is when the entire place is open.  There is a great sections with Amish farmers that prepare homemade pretzels and great sandwhiches.

I would not recommend for food. If your looking for laid back environment it's ok. The menu looks appealing and the tastes are there on paper. As far as execution, 2 and 3 thumbs down. The meals were either over cooked or under cooked. All fried items were burnt and nothing worst than burnt batter on donuts and fried chicken. We tried most of the menu and I was disappointed with all. For those who gave this place high regards, they need their foodie license revoked indefinitely.

So, I like Reading terminal.  Don't get me wrong.  It has lots of stuff, and when it's not jam-packed crowded it's a really great place to wander around.  An amazing destination for cheap produce (ah, Iovine!), gorgeous fresh flowers, Amish meats I will never ever try, fish that I don't buy, a wide selection of honey...  It's great!  It is.  Buuuut....it *is* a bit overpriced for lunch - I mean, I have no idea what the rent is on those little stalls, but it must be pretty high.  And I wouldn't get a cupcake there unless  really needed a cupcake.  And it is just so full of tourists and people who don't know how to walk.  It's just not a relaxing, chill place - it's a hustle and bustle place.  But you should totally go check it out.

REading Terminal.

This place is amazing.  There is SO MUCH good food within this giant space it will make you dizzy.   I don't know if i can ever drive through filly again without making a pit stop here for some good grub.  #lifechanger
amazing produce.  amazing cold cuts & cheeses.  blueberry and cherry jams with zero sugar or corn syrup.  a beer garden with blue moon on tap.  free wifi.  what's not to like?

Sehr viele Händler mit Großer Auswahl an Gemüse, fisch, fleisch, Obst und selbst erzeugten Lebensmitteln. Die amish people verkaufen auch hier ihre erzeugten Waren. Hier kann man richtig gutes echtes und originales Philly-cheese-steak Essen. Es gibt jedoch auch reichlich andere speisen in dem Markt zu finden. Man findet schon was. Zu empfehlen

The BEST market in my opinion. The Amish have a restaurant that is VERY good. The service is quick, and the selections that I have had are fresh, and cooked to perfection. I recommend the Terminal to anyone!!
The lamb kabob roll is off the charts! Would eat here every day if I could (my bf does lol)

Love this place!! Everything you need under one roof. Come in for breakfast, do all your grocery shopping, produce, meats, cheeses, sweets & stay for lunch. I haven't been to one place I haven't liked

The food here wasn't the best. I'm a vegetarian so I didn't get meat making the price a fair one. However, my food was kind of flavorless. I even got garlic sauce and extra garlic but it didn't seem to help.

Awesome place to go for food! Any meal, there are so many options and awesome service. I wish we had a market like this where I live in Iowa. I would recommend this place to any of my friends or family.

This was a great find! There are so many amazing vendors in this market. You definitely need to take a walk through before determining what tasty things you will sample.  My husband and I visited Miller's Twists. Their original pretzel was probably the best I've ever had and I have eaten a ton of soft pretzels.  My husband had the cinnamon sugar sticks and let me try one and they were also amazing. We also stopped by Beiler's Bakery and got a couple of donuts for a late night snack. The maple bacon and apple fritter were amazing. Our last stop was Pearl's Oyster Bar. We shared some clams and oysters and they were great. The staff helped us choose some good ones. All in all, this was a treasure and I hope to visit again one day.

the restaurant lied and said they had prepared the food when I tried to cancel it within. 5 to 10 seconds of placing the order. how is it possible for the restaurant to accept the order and make it with 1 min I was talking to the Uber eats help.

Definitely would go back on a weekday if I'm back in the area. 
The Melter Skelter grilled cheese at Meltkraft was phenomenal. The hot apple dumpling at the Dutch Eating Place was awesome. And duck fried rice from Sang Kee Peking Duck was great. Would love to go back to try some more food here!

The food was slightly cold, but I don't expect much from fast food chains. However, the girl (her name tag said Zanish) at the register was extremely rude. I rarely call people out, but I could tell she didn't want to be there. The other guy working with her told her our order and she only rang us up for a portion of our order. When he told her we were waiting for our fries, she said," WHAT? why I already gave them their order." Uhh... No you didn't. We told her we wanted honey mustard and she told us she'll add it to the fries. When she rang us up a second time, she forgot to put in the honey mustard and only included the fries. After she realized she forgot, she said, "well whatever, just to let yah'll know, it was suppose to be extra." She was too busy texting on her phone to ring us a third time I guess for 27 cents. Shouldn't have forgotten our order in the first place.
Warning!!  It is always packed,  I'm a local Philadelphian and this is still one of my favorite places. Eclectic, with a wide variety of shops.

This three star rating is pulled up from the one star I want to give it today because of better past experiences.

The lunch I had today was one of the worst meals I've had in a long time. The roast beef in my sandwich was vile. Simply put, it was one big wad of chewy crap. For reasons unbeknownst to me, there were also random pieces of raw carrot in my roll. The only saving grace was that the trash can was in an arm's length of my seat.

The main reason I went to Pobelly today was because I convinced myself the weather mandated milkshake drinking. Even this was disappointing. It was very uneven.

Typically, Potbelly is nothing to write home about. They make decent sandwiches at an affordable price but there are plenty of better option around. After today's experience, I plan to stick to those other options for the foreseeable future.
Best variety! Love Iovine's Produce, Lancaster County Dairy, L. Halteman Family Country Foods for my grocery needs!

I think my expectations may have been too high based on other reviews but I thought the rolls were fine but nothing amazing (I did have it at 7pm rather than 3am so maybe that had something to do with it).
I got the chicken tikka roll w/ egg and it came out quickly and hot. The chicken itself was tender and cooked nicely but even with the egg it wasn't all that satisfying. Maybe I was expecting a stronger sauce or something more than the chicken, eggs and onion but I left feeling slightly disappointed.
But to be fair, it is very cheap, fast and probably a lot tastier/fresher than a lot of comparable foods you can get at that price point.

A very cute place to explore and eat. Just don't have any issues with claustrophobia. This place is packed and you will be bumping into people everywhere. There is no shortage of food, but lines are long & seats are limited so if you are eating in a group, be mindful of that.
A mandatory site visit on your next visit to Philadelphia if you love food. We made several culinary discoveries and have been tasted delicious products.
Bielers donuts are amazing!! The panini place is quite good if you have time to wait a bit! Really haven't had any negative experiences at any of the vendors!
Esp. Nonna's kitchen. Real home food Pakistani-style. AND don't leave w/out the rose lassi!

Reading terminal market, are you a foodie haven or a tourist trap? I think that you are a foodie haven that moonlights as a tourist trap. The tourists own this place, along with convention goers and business type people. My favorite place here is DiNics roast pork. There are several other places that I have bookmarked (Beck's, Termini Bros, Flying Monkey, etc) and I was able to check off The Dutch Eating Place from my bookmarks this visit. I'd like to think that you'd be able to get almost anything you need here, the exception being anything hard to find or extremely specific specialty items. The Amish donuts are amazing, but only worth eating while they are hot and fresh. I have Bassett's Ice cream near  the top of my list of must trys. 

Expect large crowds, and larger lines during lunchtime throughout the week, surprisingly enough, the crowds were light on Saturday around 10am.

Fall in love with philly here. You get amish, desserts, pulled pork, cuban plantains, creole po'boy sandwiches, and everything else in between.

There is something magical about indoor market places.. It's such a great community meeting ground, and reading terminal is no different. Every visit to philly should include a stop in.

There are piano players, a beer garden, a central food court, and just about anything else you could imagine.
This is for the chicken and lamb on rice. Very average. Chicken had lots of grizzle. Not very flavorful. Rice and lamb were OK. Not worth returning for a second visit.

This is an amazing terminal. So many good eats and cool merchants to choose from. Fresh fruit and veggies and cheese and pastries and treats!!!! I loved it! I live in north Jersey and sometimes consider driving to Philly for the day just to visit this terminal!
I love the Reading Terminal.  There are so many great places to eat.  It's a lot of fun!

Had a hoagie that was meh, had a gyro that was very good, had a coffee that was good, it was dry, warm and had everything.....placed directly next to the large Marriott convention center, this place has it all, the crowd, the energy, the food, the bums, the noise, and the essence of Philly boiled down for quick consumption......I loved it!!
Really outstanding. As long as you can deal with the weekend and lunchtime crowds, this place has just about everything you need foodwise.
DO NOT GO HERE FOR THE CHEESESTEAKS unless you want to pay over $10 for a 4" roll. If you don't believe me, check it out for yourself. The amish section is as good as any you will ever visit.

What an amazing place. Every kind of food (cooked and grocery) that you could imagine. Fresh food, butchers, specialty items and more FOOD! We tried to eat our way through but alas we could not. We did manage to eat awesome roast pork sandwiches at DiNics, cookies from 3 different bakeries, cheese, ice cream and smoothies. Can you say oink? We already have our list of what we're eating next time. Definitely having a brisket sandwich at DiNics.
One of the true delights of Philadelphia. There is something here for everyone. I love the deli personally and it's the best place for pastrami outside of New York.

Reading Terminal Market is a must visit. There's so much variety of everything here - fruit, meat, cheese, flower shops.. they have all types of food to choose from as well - southern, pizza, chinese, sandwiches, desserts. You'll be a bit overwhelmed once you enter through the doors, but I assure you, you'll walk out of here with a satisfied palette and a few extra somethings for later.

Being a doctoral student in Hoagie Studies, I can't give my highest rating to the sandwiches here, but I will say that the staff does a fantastic job with lunch catering orders, and they are super nice. 

The sandwiches are really OK, but don't expect to be blown away. One of the main problems for me is that they toast their Italian hoagie. That is pretty much sacrilege. But, on the upside, their accompaniments are quite good. The sandwiches come with thinly sliced pickles (sliced longways) and a delicious hot pepper spread. For me, the best part of ordering from here is the pepper spread. Don't miss it. 

The staff is really great. Whenever we put in a lunch delivery order online, they call to confirm, always show up on time, and the driver is always super friendly. A+ for service.
Everything you want to eat is here. So many options. Everyone will be satisfied. There may be crowds and long lines for some of the vendors, but isn't that a sign that this is the real deal?

What an interesting gem of food. Everything is here...sandwiches, ice cream, cakes, pretzels and beer.

I was drawn here by Di Nics but ended up getting ice cream as well.

Be sure to stop by everyday to try something new!

Thanks to Yelp Philly, we decided to stop here and check it out. Wow! What an awesome place. It's like a food court/farmer's market on steroids. 

We walked through the entire place to check it out and decide where we wanted to eat. We decided on Olympia Gyros (for the guys) and the falafel place (for me). I got my meal quickly, a falafel platter with falafel, salad, pita, hummus, and tabboulah. I also got a tropical smoothie. All of this for about $12. One thing that confused me is that you get your food and eat, THEN pay. I wanted to carry mine away so I could eat with the people I was with, so I asked for the bill and then headed out.

Everything was fresh and tasty. I especially appreciated the smoothie - they were juicing the fruits right there. The guys liked their gyros and fries too. The lady working there was nice as she let me sit and eat even though I hadn't bought my food there, and even cleared my trash for me.

The amounts of meat and seafood here were crazy. I have never seen so much. Lots of produce - I can imagine even more when the summer comes around. Some standout booths were:

- a shop dedicated entirely to cookbooks. Cookbooks unlike I've ever seen before, for everything under the mood and more. 

- A honey shop, with products made from honey, plus several varieties to buy

- COOKIES. PLEASE, Yelp Philly, help me out here. We bought cookies from a place that had very unique flavors, like caramel and raspberry chocolate. Some of them were available halfway dipped in chocolate. They were the best cookies I've ever tasted. I can't remember the name of the shop, and wanted to see if they are online for me to order. I checked the webpage but none of the bakeries ring a bell. I think they sold more than cookies. I'm desperate! Please PM me! 

We spent more than enough to get our parking ticket validated. $4 for 2 hours was a great deal, seeing the prices of parking if you didn't have it validated. Wow.. now I know why there are such parking issues there that they shoot "Parking Wars" in the city! I sort of wished that I was going to run into a PPA employee so I could mention it.. hehe. But I digress...

This place rocked... and I'd go back in a heartbeat!

If you are in town, come here. So many different vendors with so many things to offer. Its hard to choose where to eat with so many options available. We got lost, in the best way here. I had a specific place that I had wanted to try, since I am gluten free and had a craving for "carnival" food. My friend found a cheese steak vendor that was on point. I could spend days here eating.

The Reading Terminal Market is an absolute must-see attraction in Philly. There's a whole world of food in there, with enough nooks and crannies to just about get lost and keep stumbling upon new things you didn't notice before. I love to get hot cookies and Amish taffies, and the last time I went, I had a delicious kielbasa. There's good people-watching here, too. It's interesting to be able to see a young Amish woman on her lunch break. You can see a lot of things in New York City, but not that.

I just moved to PHL for school and was recommended this place by my sister-n-law who is from here. It just so happens to only be 0.3 miles from me which means I am able to walk which is such a blessing because this place is awesome! I get all my fruits and vegetables from here, my lunch meat and my sweet treats. It's all CHEAP (I'm a graduate student on a serious budget). This place is a gem and I'm so happy to have it.
One of my favorite spot in the city ! Such a great place to get any type of food you want. The only downside is that it is always crowded
A food fanatic's paradise. They have nearly every type of food you may think about: Amish, Indian, Mexican, Cookies, German, Italian... you will eat very well here.

This place has a lot of great food.  It's a cult phenom too - as people will travel here.  There's also a sub-place that has a broccoli raab-cheesesteak that was featured on Diner's Drive-Ins and Dive's.  A great visit if you visit the city.
All the YES to the Reading Terminal Market! One of my [modest] life goals is to try every food stand in this place.
History, culture, food, and fun all in one place. One of my favorite places in Philly. Best cookies are sold here

It's the 2nd time I've been here and it's still crowded, still smells delicious and still awakens all of my senses! I love it here, even though I feel like a sardine packed in a metro cart but it's definitely worth the experience and the food here you can't go wrong. They have live music playing from time to time as well as booths set up for gift shopping. Also, it's within walking distance from China town and a good option for when you're in town and you're caught in a downpour (speaking from experience). :)

The Industry is my South Philly go to. I live in grad hospital but I'm lucky because my boyfriend lives right on 2 street so we are frequent guests at the industry. The ambience inside is... well... industrial. It's kind of dark but it works with the wood benches and industrial lighting fixtures. In the winter time we always sit at the bar. The bartenders are amazing especially Riley and Rich. When it's warm we love to sit outside with our puppy who gets a ton of attention from the staff. 

The happy hour deals are amazing. HH is from 4-7pm which is so much better than the 1.5-2 hour HHs that are typical around the city. Thy have buck a shuck oysters that are always big creamy and delicious. They also have $1 mac and cheese croquets. Domestic drafts for $3, house wine for $4 and a few specialty cocktails for $5. On Monday's they do burgers and bubbles and Thursday they have trivia! 

Outside of the happy hour menu, the rest of the food is fantastic. I usually get the fried chicken sandwich with the onion marmalade and shoe string fries - yuuuum! The Sunday gravy is also good and the falafel sandwich. Also make sure you try the kimchi tater tots. 

I do have to mention one time I came here on Valentine's Day (I think 2016) with a few friends and they had a fois gras peanut butter and jelly sandwich and it was the most delicious thing I've ever tasted. My bf gets annoyed because I talk about it every time we're there and it's never been on the menu again :( 

They also have a really great brunch deal after 2pm on Sundays. I think it might be half price after 2pm? Not 100% sure but I remember it being a great price. 

Love love love the Industry.

I think this place is ok.  It is very busy and I am not sure just how clean each place is here.  Lots of variety.  Whatever you want you eat you can find it here. Parking the car was a real hassle. Expect to pay $20.00 to $30.00 to park your for a few hours.  The food is not too expensive for the most part.
Great place has a large variety of food that will fit everyone the down home diner is excellent

The Food Court from Heaven, I frequented this market nearly every day during my week's stay in Philadelphia.  Open daily from 8am to 5pm, it's paradise for those who are hungry, enjoy a plethora of eating options, and cash-strapped.  From Amish Dutch bakeries and pretzels to Thai and Chinese to Soul Food and Italian pizza and pasta, you'll find a wide variety of cuisines for breakfast, lunch, and everything in between for under $7.  Oh yes, you can also grocery shop here - produce, meats, and seafood galore.  With over 90 vendors, it's overwhelming if you're hungry because almost everything looks and smells good.  These are some of my favorites and so-so stops:


Bieler's Bakery: Amish bakery with cakes, bread, whoopie pies, and rolls.  You can see the workers bake the various rolls fresh that morning.  Try their famous sticky buns with raisins - deliciously sweet.

By George Pizza: I loved the Spinach, roasted red pepper cheese slice.  They reheat it in their oven for you so it's toasty and cheesy.  

Delilah's Southern Cooking: The corn bread was disappointingly cold and crumbly, but the fried chicken was tender and the mac & cheese was flavorful and rich.     

4th Street Cookie Company: Freshly baked and thick chewy cookie.  I loved my Chocolate Chip with Walnuts.  If you want to combine sweet and sweet, there's the the Chocolate Dipped Chocolate Chip Cookie.

Torini Brothers: yummy baked Italian goods, especially the delectable Amaretto cookies.  At $20 per lb, it's worth every expensive almond flavored bite.  

Dutch Eating Place: A popular Amish brunch spot - the prices are cheap for a hearty breakfast.  The blueberry pancakes are fluffy and decent, and when visiting Philly, try the breakfast "scrapple" to try at least once - crisped ground pork and grits.      

Flying Monkey: Drool-worthy bakery with more whoopie pies than I've ever seen.  In addition to my richly sweet and dense Red Velvet whoopie pie with cream cheese frosting, there are also the flavors of: classic, cookies and cream, snickerdoodle, Elvis, and Lavender & honey.  

Kamal's: Middle eastern fare along with variety of fresh squeezed juice combinations that will give Jamba Juice a run for its money.  The Mint Lemonade hit the spot.

Pearl's Oyster Bar: In addition to trying Malpeque oysters, which tasted quite fresh, I also enjoyed the Lobster and Crab Bisque - creamy and savory with fresh chunks of crab on top.  

The Grill @ Smuckers: Delicious Amish cooked Breakfast Sausage Sandwich.  The egg was fresh, sausage patty juicy and savory, and the melted American cheese with fresh slightly sweet bread roll made a filling and delicious breakfast.  And it's served all day.    

Down Home Diner: Average comfort and diner food, although I found The Country Benny (poached eggs, sausage, buttermilk biscuit, and country gravy) unappetizingly drowning in bland gravy.  

City Coffee: for your morning coffee fix, my iced latte was nothing special, but it still satisfies that caffeine urge.  

Miller's Twist: Creamy and not-too-sweet Strawberry Milkshake comes with a free Amish baked pretzel.  The soft and slightly salted pretzel, with its golden baked surface, is tasty with the cheese dip.     

The Reading Market (Redding) fills up at the popular noon-time lunch rush, especially since it's located smack in City Center with several workers in the area.  It's more spaced out and a comfortable experience earlier in the morning, unless you don't mind squeezing shoulder to shoulder with your fellow Philly friends for some cheap, good eats.

There's plenty not to like about Reading Terminal Market. With nearly a hundred merchants selling specialty foods, produce, flowers, books, houseware and so much more, you're bound to find plenty to turn up your nose at.
But even the most closed-minded individual will be able to satisfy their gastronomical cravings in this iconic Philly destination. Hoagies, cheesesteaks, gumbo, jambalaya, ribs, pizza, falafel, salads, soups, sushi, lo mein... I'm not even scratching the surface. 
The best way to learn about all the Market is by taking the guided tour, offered every Wednesday and Saturday. I had a taste of turtle soup during my tour, and learned about who really invented the chocolate kiss.
It's been an important part of Philadelphia for more than a century, and with such rich history and endless variety of sensational cuisines, this place will remain a mainstay as much as a must-see.

This is a great spot to take any visiting friends, and a great spot to grab lunch, or to go to if you are with a big group and can't decide what to eat. 

For desserts - 4th st Cookie (get the chocolate dipped chocolate chip!), and Flying Monkey are great choices. 

Sang Kee is delicious, as is the Crepe place.

The veggies and farmer's market items tend to be a bit over-priced - but to find those options in the middle of the city is a great resource!
So many good options! Make sure you come with an appetite and patience to make your way through the market!

You can always find something good to eat here. I've loved every restaurant I ordered from. It's counter style so not many formal sit down restaurants. I like that there are so many on one place but I hate that there's never any place to sit. Another thing is that there's never any parking (because it's downtown) so beware. Overall, you can't go wrong. My favorites include an Amish counter with Amish rotisserie chicken and smackaroni salad, the soul food restaurant towards the middle (they have amazing collard greens and sweet potatoes) and fourth street bakery (huge cookies).

The Reading (pronounced Redding) Terminal Market is a large indoor market that features restaurants, bakeries, food shops and delis. You have food options from a multitude of cultures and countries from locally grown, organic produce and diary to cheesesteaks, Indian dishes and soul food. It's very crowded and busy for most of the day and the only other downside is that it usually closes by 6 PM so you should make sure you go early if you are planning to eat your dinner in the market. I have stopped by quite a few times now while on vacation and I have still only tried a small portion of all the products available.
One of my favorite places in Philadelphia. I go every week for fresh vegetables and hormone free meat. The prepared food can be a bit expensive but worth it for a treat.

As a local to Philly, I'm pretty embarrassed to say this was only my second trip to the Reading Terminal Market. Wow. Just wow. I'm glad I didn't come hungry or I would have been quite overwhelmed. I was meeting my girlfriends for the start of a big day of eating. One of my friends suggested Reading terminal and based on what I've heard about the variety, it was the perfect pick,

We did a lap of the building before anyone purchased a thing. I wish I took notes to make my next trip easier. Things that stood out included the sushi, DiNic's, a stand with bacon, a fresh fish stand, a juice/smoothie place and the list goes on. 

We were able to grab a table with 5 seats and took turns getting our lunch. I love the variety at the table- sesame chicken, a turkey sand which, char grilled eggplant sandwich and a falafel. Since I was fresh off brunch, I decided to just have some ice cream. I was intrigued by the abundance of Amish vendors so picked Miller's Twist. After sample a few flavors, I decided on a small cup of banana ice cream. Perfect! Creamy and delicious.

If this wasn't the start of the day out, I'd probably go on a produce shopping spree. I can't wait to return hungry and ready to bring any purchases promptly to a fridge!

Reading Terminal Market provides much-needed character to the city. There are options for just about any type of cuisine and bounteous local items. There is no question it is worth your visit and no advanced planning is needed, though it will be busy on the weekends (and the hours during the week are not accommodating).

So Im def about to rain on everyone's parade here- but after the big hype regarding this place I was really looking forward to raving about it. First impression- hmm, interesting, cluttered, kinda dark and lots of randomness...which i expected from a market. 

Perhaps you have to take your time in a place like this...sampling, looking and observing. I wasn't in a rush and I wasn't taking my time, I strolled along the paths of the unknowns, passed a chocolate boutique that I found interesting and funny, picked up some fried macaroni and cheese from one southern vendor-good, but the pasta and cornbread-not. Sorry, dont remember the name of the place. 

My day in Philly was amazing to say the least, but i just wanted to more from this place. Eastern Market in DC still rules.

By far the nicest McDonald's in the city (that I have been to).

Let's face it.  Eating fast food in this city is an experience that makes you either want to kill yourself, the worker serving it to you, or the other patrons in the restaurant.  But this particular location makes you forget about that (kind of)... and for that I give it a thumbs up (relative to Philadelphia fast food).

Why?

The ambiance is a step up from other cookie cutter incarnations in that it is in the lobby of an older, more statuesque building near City Hall.  The ceilings are high, and the floor to ceiling windows encompass the length of the seating area providing good light and good people watching.  The cleaning crew is usually on task in an effort to make the tables and spills cleaned, and the counter people are typically a cut above other locations.  Transient and homeless campers are kept to a minimum.  AND -- You get to pour your own soda, which is always a plus for me!

One potential negative is the cold draft that blows in from the Arch St. door when opened during the winter.  In the summer, however, the breeze is quite pleasant.  The Broad St. door is a rotating circle door, which is fun.

The food is the food... and a McDonald's is a McDonald's is a McDonald's... except, probably due to the location, this one is a bit better than the rest in Philly.

First time visitor, came here with a group of friends and had a great time! Great beer selection, the mussels were fantastic and my friend said the industry burger was great. Service was fast and very friendly! We walked on a very cold night and were seated very fast so that was an awesome plus!

One complaint I have is the lighting was quite dim so reading the menus was a little bit of a strain.
Really large food market. Don't expect "cool" and "unique" foods that you wouldn't find at normal take out type places except for the donuts .  Most of the stands were typical fast food type places.

Oh my god, this place is so effing amazing.

For my fellow Milwaukeeans, you may think our Public Market is pretty cool. NOPE, SORRY, IT IS A SAD, SAD, MEDIOCRE STRIP MALL OF SAD.

The Reading Terminal Market...wow. Just effing wow. This place is like a stadium filled with every frigging thing you can think of. Total sensory overload as I tried to pick just one thing to try. Every ethnicity you can imagine is represented here, and not just food-wise.

If I lived in Philly, I'd be here everyday.

This place is around the corner from where we are staying in Philly.  You can find pretty much anything here...mediterranean, indian, mexican, burgers, and MUCH more!  It's perfect for traveling with 2 kids because we can all get what we want :)  I wasn't so impressed with my salad from Hunger Burger, but I guess that's what I get for ordering a salad from a burger joint...it was pretty soggy and didn't have alot of tang, like most mediterranean salads do.  The grilled cheese sandwiches from MeltKraft were super scrumptious though...you can even add bacon to them, yum!
A Chicago original.  The subs are tasty and the service was great.  The potato salad is full of vinegar and has a nice bite.

Went with friends for a few beers last night. Our servers were both really awesome. Great beer recommendations! Only one of us had an order of fries, but the mussels at the table behind ours smelled mouthwatering. I'll definitely have to go back for a meal.

This place is great.  It's like Baltimore's Lexington Market but maybe a little bigger, safer, and a little more in the way of yuppy shopping and food choices.  For example, they had crafts/book shops.  Lexington Market doesn't have that.  

Reading Terminal Market feels really authentic and has a ton of food choices.  I can't wait to go back.  I really liked the falafel shop.

It's super tourist, but great. There are so many awesome local stores here that you can pretty much knock out all of your grocery shopping at a great price or just get a bite to eat. My biggest tip I can give you is to avoid the weekends if you can because it's sooooooo busy.

TL;DR: Fast, friendly, affordable, delicious, seating options & delivery!

So friendly and so delicious! I've only had their platters here, but they have both been great so far. The chicken and rice and the MK specials are both worth getting and each are under $10. The last time I was there, they handed out free samples of the mango lassi which was very tasty. The workers have always been nice, answering questions and accommodating with dietary requests.

I went there this morning and I'm salty as hell. The restaurant is closed for reconstruction. I looked on the app and the website and it's not mentioned anywhere that it is closed. I'm mad bc this was the only nearby philly location that I somewhat liked. Anyway, I'll check back next time I get a chance and switch my review up bc I know normally they have have good service here.

MUST GO if you are in Philadelphia. Everything you could ever want--sandwiches, Italian meats, Amish bakery, seafood, produce, farmers' market, ice cream, etc. in this small space. I highly recommend Bassett's ice cream and the Italian meat counter.

it is a delicious mad house here. be prepared for lines. get there early as they will and do run out of items. so many merchants to visit. insist they were open later so I can eat my way through the whole place. have great merchants for jewelry, health and wellness, produce and take home items. definitely a must visit on any trip to Philly
Love this market and I take all my guests to lunch here. Everyone is happy with the variety of food and if you have out of towners, they love the shops and people watching.

Reading Market has everything. Definitely a hotspot for good eats and interesting folks. People watching is great here as well as the variety of different foods you can get. The crepes are A-MA-ZING and completely worth going down there just to try one.
I love this place. You can find any kind of food you want and some more stuff. What can I say that already hasn't been said. Been coming here since I was a kid and I'll keep on going.

This is going to be overstated. I don't know how to dine in late capitalism. Honeygrow, let me say, has good food and is a nice option for lunch. It's a little pricey, but not too bad.

But the automation and the postmodern dish construction was just over-the-top. Not only do I relate to a machine, I don't even use a menu, I essentially construct a dish I want based on the options and someone cooks it for me. That's a nice idea in the era of the gig-economy, but the solitary experience seems to be contradictory to the spirit of eating and dining. I may go again, but it definitely gives me a bit of an existential crisis.
Amazing selection and really fast service (depending on the line of course) I highly recommend the Four Seasons Juice bar for a refreshing and healthy drink.
Awesome, a foodie's dream, paradise, outstanding food, excellent quality and you don't have to break the bank, I cannot wait to be back in Philly!!!
Amazing variety of food! Beilers Donuts are a must! They have a huge array of flavors for a reasonable price.

I love Reading Terminal Market! A great blend of ethnicities, great foods and produce! The place is quite big and it's very easy to get lost, but no matter what corner you turn there is absolutely amazing food
Food was 45 minutes late, lukewarm, and mediocre. Laaaaame. Will not order from here again.

I love love love going to Reading Terminal. 

From fish shops to meat shops, 
Fruits, vegetables and candy shops to small gadgets and authentic clothing shops, 
Many many different kind of restaurants to Amish bakeries, 
Reading Terminal is the grand bazaar of Philadelphia. 

The only thing I don't like about this place is when you leave here, you will smell like food. :( They've got to improve their ventilation system.

What a great place for locals and tourists alike. The sheer amount of food options you have will leave you astounded. There are a bunch of different gems you have to try - Beck's Cajun, Hershel's Deli, Beiller's Donuts, freshly squeezed OJ from Iovine Bros... those are my personal favorites. It's definitely a spot to hit if you're indecisive (like me!).

Interesting market with fresh vegetables, fruits, fish, candies, desserts, and many other things. We even bought a bag of blueberries back to NJ. Love this place~ Hope there could be a shop to sell some small  plants or flowers~

We're in the World Series with these folks rt now, but I visited Philly over the summer and am just now able to review all the venues. I gotta give 'em their props. All's I can say is WOW... I've been to markets like this in other countries and wondered if it would ever work in the US. You can find more than just food here, soaps, scents, jewelry, trinkets, all made by individual entrepreneurs giving their own spin on things. From raw meats to cooked, produce, cheeses, wines, beer garden, jewelry shop, gourmet to everyday, it's here. Japanese, Indian, Middle Eastern, pierogies, ice cream, cheeses... you name the food, they have it. My sampling consisted of Bassett's ice cream, gourmet cheese, pierogies, heath bar and everything cookie, and bought some $1 tubs o' strawberries for my friends for later.  A unique experience! Go empty bellied and enjoy.

I would give another star because the dumplings are admittedly delicious, but beware: one of the pork dumplings I ate was packed so tightly that taking a bite caused a fire hydrant like explosion of pork juice that not only splashed across my own shirt and shorts, but even caught a friend walking next to me. Be sure to fork or knife spike your dumplings to release any pressure that has built up, likely during the frying process. It could happen to you.
Great indoor market with any kind of food you can think of. Crowded but fun and if you spend money there you get a big discount on your parking. Awesome place and a must see in Philly.
This place has all types of restaurants and local vendors available. If i lived nearby can see that being an everyday place.

A visit to Reading Termimal Market is always necessary for us when we're in Philly. You have a variety of options to eat.  Just be ready to brave the crowds of people here, especially on weekends. 

Highly recommend DiNic's, Herschel's, Bassetts, Keven Parker's Soul Food Café and Famous 4th Street Cookie. 

DiNic's - My default order is the pulled pork w sharp provolone. It's very juicy and lots of flavor. I've tried the roast pork but I definitely prefer the pulled pork.

Herschel's - I've only tried their pastrami sandwich and it has to be one of the best pastrami's I've ever had. Very meaty and tender and not fatty at all. 

Keven Parker's Soul Food Café - if you're in the mood for soul food, come try this place. I've tried their fried chicken & mac and cheese. 

Then, go get dessert at Bassetts or Famous 4th Street Cookie! 

Park at one of the parking garages. We usually park on 12th and Filbert St and walk across. But don't forget to get your ticket validated at one of the vendor's (with a minimum purchase of $10) - you'll only pay $4 for upto 2 hours.

Heard a lot of good things about this place, read a lot of good reviews. I had to try it out for myself. WOW! This place is well worth the trip and the money! The obeisance is awesome, very well price food! Highly recommend trying this place!
for a contemporary take on dumplings, just go to a museum. this place does it all wrong, and i should know, my middle name is dumplings.

Been here a couple times when I first moved to the area.  Typical subway but the vast variety of competitors in the area focusing on a more quality sandwich will win out for me every time.  More so 2.5 stars but never had an issue when going here except there is lack of anything that will draw me back.

Having traveled regularly to Philadelphia and never going into the Reading Terminal Market, i'm really disappointed in myself for wasting all those years.  I enjoy just walking through the market, eating at the various food stands is a bonus.

This review might not be very helpful, but there is no way I can describe everything great about this place in this little space. If I did have to make a few suggestions, though, DiNic's is always great, you can get some of the best hoagies around at Salumeria (ask for the house dressing on you sandwich as well), and 4th St. Cookies are incredible.

Just go to the Market and you'll understand.
Love the atmosphere! Always glad to be here. Great seafood/sandwiches/and of course yummy desserts

Went to check out the market on a Saturday and really loved the experience.

Make sure you come here hungry, there is so much deliciousness to try!

There are many vendors here, selling everything from Amish cheeses, to fresh seafood, to local chocolate.

I had fun picking up various items to take back home and try including freshly made peanut butter with honey, Amish butter cheese, and Soy Vey marinade.

Can't wait to return the next time I visit Philly!

Really fun place to go for me on weekends. I like to stand outside for a few minutes and listen to the one-man-band with the electric guitar, harmonica, and bells attached to his foot. This guy represents all things Philadelphia. If anyone deserves a dollar or two outta my wallet, it's this guy (and I do give him something every Saturday). Inside the market is pretty crowded, but if you like food, you'll get over it. Just be careful ordering something you need to sit down for - make sure you already have a seat before you order it or else you'll be walking to Suburban Station food court to sit. There's a lot of energy and a coffee/cookie stand at the one entrance that serves cups of coffee for $1 (at least on Saturdays) and it tastes really good, too.

This is my absolute favorite part of philly! I would go there everyday if I lived there!!! So many varieties of food, very clean, lots of space, great for all meals, breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner, or a snack!

Sadly, DiNic's was (unsurprisingly) not open on Sunday morning when I came, but I was able to get a fresh banana + pineapple + orange smoothie from 4 Seasons Juice Bar, a salmon benedict from Fair Food Farmstand, and a scoop of the Whyy Experience + a scoop of Irish Coffee from Bassetts Ice Cream. 

4 Seasons Juice Bar has a wide selection of fresh fruits and supplements like wheat grass to choose from and I thought their prices were reasonable (comparable to Jamba Juice).

The salmon benedict was tasty from Fair Food Farmstand, although I wouldn't say that it was particularly amazing. The portions are quite generous though; my friend got the breakfast burrito from the Fair Food Farmstand and it was HUGE - as big as a Chipotle burrito.

Apparently, Bassetts Ice Cream has a rotating menu of different ice cream flavors. Irish Coffee tasted just like Bailey's and the Whyy Experience was the perfect complement. I snuck a bite of my friend's Mango ice cream, and it was probably one of the best Mango ice creams I've ever had!

I also stopped by The Tubby Olive on the recommendation of some of my friends. They have a wide selection of different infused olive oils and balsamic vinaigrettes. I mixed the Blood Orange Olive Oil with the Dark Chocolate Balsamic Vinaigrette for a flavor that was similar to those orange chocolate candies you can get at World Market! Ultimately, we ended up buying 2 bottles of the Tuscan Olive Oil, which tastes similar to the seasoning you can find at Carrabba's.

I wish I had been able to stop by The Tea Leaf! Sadly, it too was also closed on Sunday morning. Next time I'm in the Philly area, I'm definitely stopping by again!
