Whatever food you're in the mood for, you'll probably find it a reading terminal. There is also a great bakery and butcher shop! Amish goodies and fresh made baked goods. The prices here are fair and there is usually plenty of space to sit and enjoy. My favorite place here always was the jewish deli, they have LEGIT pastrami sandwiches!!!
I love this place, it's filled with tiny little stores inside and there's always something for everyone there. I love this place. If you come to Philadelphia this is a place you should visit.
Coolest place to visit!!! Our family had a great time, so many shops, many places to eat, drink and buy crafts. This is a must see if your in the area.

Absolutely adore this place. Great for drinks with friends where you actually want to talk to each other. Has an alternative vibe but it's not overwhelmingly alternative with its Modern rustic environment.  

Food -- small menu; kind of fancy bar food; pretty good falafel; very substantial burgers; great fries

Always full but never crowded or too loud. Best for chill nights where you accidentally get too drunk.

Walking around Reading Terminal Market is a great way to spend a rainy day. They have so many booths with different kinds of food and knick knacks that you can spend hours meandering and never get bored. There's also an excellent fresh produce section on the back. It can get crowded around lunchtime, so be prepared to find a quiet corner to sit and eat and people-watch.

You could go to the market every day for a week and discover something new.  You can get every meal any time of day, get your groceries, and even do some shopping for friends and family.  Tourists and locals alike can share this place and have their needs met.  A quiet spot to read and enjoy a glass of wine?  They've got it.  Local snacks to bring home from a weekend trip in Philly?  This is the place to go.  Meeting up with a colleague for lunch?  Plenty of options.  I'm definitely going back next time I'm in Philly!
Place has everything you want. Got lunch from a different place everyday for five days. I'd come back to the city just to revisit this place.

I love this market!!  Drove to Philly for the day with some friends and when I tell you that RTM is a - MUST GO TO spot!  If you're a foodie then go RTM - make sure to stop at Beiler's Doughnuts.  They are delicious (definitely try the apple fritters one)!

I love Reading Terminal Market! Its a great place to go on a Saturday morning to look around and enjoy the food and atmosphere. This is a great place to get the famous pork sandwich from Dinic's and maybe a soft pretzel from the Amish Market. The Reading Terminal Market is definitely a spot to hit when you are in the city!
There's something for everyone at Reading Terminal Market. My boyfriend and I love to shop here for ingredients to make a nice meal.

I can't say I'm that big of a fan because the place is always too jam packed and not enough places to sit and eat in comfort without elbowing someone on accident. Other than that, the quality of food served at the various restaurants and other eateries is typically pretty good.

You need what?  Oh, Reading Terminal Market has it.  Seafood, produce, meat, Mexican, Amish, Japanese, bagels, Cajun, roast pork and broccoli rabe.  Everything!  My biggest complaint is that they aren't open past 6 pm, which makes it very difficult to get there during the week; otherwise I would do most of my shopping there.  It can also be a lot for some people due to how busy it gets during lunch hours and on the weekends, but bring out your inner South Phillian and push through those mobs of people!

"You can have whatever you like..." literally. 

Italin.Greek.Sushi.IceCream.Cookies.Beer.Fruit.Juice.Crepes.Body Oils. Accessories. Oysters.Coffee. Sweets. Pastries. & of course..."Best Sandwich in 'Merica." 

A Must-Do while visiting Philly!!
I  Always have a great time when I come the people are super friendly. My food is always hot and cooked how i like it. The drinks are out of site. I love this place.

I've been here twice and it's very good and lives up to the reviews. The paneer masala roll is hands down one of the best Kati rolls I've had- probably better than the original Kati Rolls in NYC. The Aloo masala roll was less magnificent but still solid. 

I also got the chicken and lamb combo and it was delicious. Tasted much less synthetic than the Halal guys platters, and was incredibly filling and the meat, rice and lettuce all blended together favorably. I recommend using a LOT of the white sauce on everything- it's great!

What a neat place.

Tip: Don't bother going on Sunday!!!
Tip: Don't get sucked in to ridiculous prices for everyday things. Try to make purchased of items you would not usually get. 

My favorite booths were hosted by Amish families and were closed on Sunday as well as many others for what I image would be religious reasons. They really add a nice touch to the market. We only grabbed quick sandwiches from two stands, both were great. The cookies at the North West corner were also great, warm and chewy as they were fresh from the oven. We also picked up some rolls to bring home with us. 

This is a great please to grab some items to go and eat in one of Phillise' many wonderful parks.

ANother place I like to stop in when I'm in Philly :). Love buying the Beef Jerky its amazing! The Teriyaki and Spicy are so yummy! Beware though the spicy is really hot! I also by the homade Pepper Jam! Sooooooo gooood!! LOVE THIS PLACE

If you have out-of-town visitors and you want to show them "Philadelphia", take them to the Reading Terminal for coffee and lunch, then walk over to City Hall and then down the Parkway towards the Art Museum. There, I just planned every single out-of-town, show-the-parents-where-you-live visit you'll ever have.

If they come back and insist on doing something different, fine. Take them to the Reading Terminal for coffee and lunch, then walk over to Independence Mall and do whatever it is that people do over there. Bam! I just planned every repeat, you-did-such-a-good-job-showing-us-around-the-first-time visit you'll ever have.

Damn!? They're back again? Fine. Take them to dinner anywhere near 13th and Walnut on Friday before going to a show somewhere on Broad Street (google: Wilma Theater). The next morning, take them out for coffee and brunch at the Reading Terminal Market.

If, at this point, you haven't figured out what is going on here: move to Camden.
Vary overwhelming with all the people but never disappointed in the food. My kids having a great time on their day off.
Amazing place with so many choices. Hard to go wrong with so many great foods, from Dinic's pork roll, cheeses from Valley Shephard and cheesecake from Termini's. Stroll and enjoy!

What can I say? I love this place. From the lattes and coffee at old city coffee, to the gift shops, countless food counters which I've never eaten anything I didn't like from... it's all great. The only bad thing about it is that it does get really crowded at peak times and I tried two of their bottled wines from the store that sells them with reading terminal market labels and they were horrible. Definitely check this place out if you are in philly!
Such a fabulous foodie and shopping experience!  The butter cake from Flying Monkey will literally change your life.

One of the top sites to see in Philadelphia, I'd spend a morning here getting some fresh baked goods to eat, or wander in for a lunch at the tasty diner. Pick up chocolate treats, fresh fish, meat, and vegetables, all without too much of a premium.

Come for the Amish donuts (freshly made!), loaves of classic breads, and baked pies, pick up your turkeys here for Thanksgiving, and look for the delicious ribs to the southwest side.  There are plenty of homemade jams and preserves, organic foods, and small restaurants to eat at inside, newly made ice cream, and many many snacks.

Random bookstores and craft shops also here... the only downside is that they close early, around 8 or so most days, sometimes earlier, so make sure you make it there earlier in the day!

Incidentally, the diner to the south - love the sawmill gravy biscuits here.
Love going to the terminal. Always fine what i need for good prices and the fresh meats n veggies are exacy what i need. Can be crowded on wknds but still worth it.

I guess this Philadelphia's version of Chelsea Market, perhaps it's a bit smaller but it still offers the same variety of eats, sweets, treats and delcious snacks to satisfy anyone.  Fresh pressed olive oil, Amish baked treats, fresh seafood-pizza-pasta and handmade fresh mozzarella cheese...the list goes on and on.  This is a really nice place near the historic district to come in on a Saturday morning to have a delicious hearty breakfast, fresh brewed coffee,fresh squeezed juices and find some savory and sweet treats in between as well.  Wasn't able to try all the various dessert booths but they all seemed busy and as good as the next one. Nice find!!
I swear I am going to try every food counter here. So far everything has been delicious. Great prices on produce too!

This place is straight up amazing and a must if you are visiting Philly. When we visited, the place was packed! Plus, I ate more food than I thought was possible.

Reading Terminal Market has some of the best food vendors, everything was amazing. We even enjoyed some fresh oysters on the half shell- Nom!

If you stop by, you won't go wrong!

Nice place. We were seated soon as we walked in at 5:30p on a Wednesday. Great place to sit and catch up with someone. The food came out very quickly and unfortunately so did the check. It was as if the waitress was telling us go home. I'd understand if it was packed but more than half the tables were empty. Despite this, she was nice. Prices were pretty reasonable. 

My friend enjoyed her mussels. My chicken sandwich was very good. It did not taste like it was deep fried and instead it seemed fairly light. It had a fried egg and cheese on it and the bread was perfect! I only wish, since I learned about this place from an article about best chicken sandwiches, one being a biscuit chicken sandwich, that it actually had one or two more options. Heads up, the menu is fairly limited- Not much of a selection, but worth the visit!

Possibly my favorite thing about living in the city.  I like to cook from scratch and make use of every piece of meat or produce that I buy.  Consistent quality meats, local produce and plenty of snack options.  I love bringing visiting friends there and it's a great date place in the sense that you can walk around, talk and feel less pressure than sitting across a table with someone and it potentially be awkward.  There is something for everyone and I'm there every Wednesday and Sunday!
The platter is definitely not worth the money. Chicken beryani with hardly any chicken.  Not going back.
The variety is great and the experience of walking down aisles upon aisles of fresh unique food is incredible. However, the lines are long and the prices of prepared food can be high. Worth a trip.
excellent market with a huge selection of reasonably priced stands. Roast pork with brocolli rabe, yum!

This is the daily Philadelphia food festival! There's always something good to choose from and so many options that you can literally play roulette with the vendors here and never lose! Highly recommended and perfect for a lunch break!

Not bad. Mostly food venues. Corn bread at Franks is good. Original Turkey is not bad. Ice cream at Bassett's is yummy. Famous 4th street cookies are over rated. Good place to go to for desserts, the food is just a-okay. I went on a sunday, a lot of places were closed. Boo.

Love this place. My GF and I can walk to it, so we've been going regularly for a few months now. 

I have a Big Green Egg at home and do a lot of smoking / grilling of meats and veggis so let me just say, I've had the BBQ Duck sammy as well as a short rib sammy at Industry and both were top notch. 

Great comfort food - ie Mac n Cheese croquets 

Overall friendly staff, good quality 'home made' food, and solid beer / wine selection.

Please do not miss out on this gem. We wandered around for over an hour and could have stayed longer. The food options were endless. If you want a foodie experience in Philly look no further. Highly recommended. Will be going back very soon!

After seeing this place featured on several food network shows and in the movie National Treasure, we were pumped to try it out and it has not let us down. There are a TON of vendor restaurants on the inside each with their own special foods. For a awhile we only got pork sandwiches from Danics because they are so amazing. Then we just recently tried a pastrami sandwich from Hersels. Amazing!! Does not disappoint!!
ice cream and cheese, and an old guy selling expensive organic apples..

My wife and I went to Philadelphia for a tour with reading terminal market being our first stop. It also ended up being our last stop. When we first arrived around 10am and looked around. We were astounded by what was inside. Everything you can think of could be found in here. We have nothing remotely close to this from where we live so this was a welcome surprise. We did some shopping before/during the tour and since we parked really close by we knew we were going to come back. We ended up coming back after a late lunch and shopped some more. We even stopped by the bar for a drink or two. The place was wonderful and I can't wait until we can get back there.
Would love to come back.  Every food you want to eat is here and inexpensive.   Garage parking across the market is expensive though.  Cost me a hefty $30 for only 3 hours of parking.
The French toast at The Oyster Bar was great! The entire Market is a cool and historic place to eat and shop.
Need curry at 3am?!  Not only does this place close late, but it's the BEST Indian food I've ever had.  It's a cultured kinda hipster place.

As a Center City resident, I actually shop for my groceries at the Reading Terminal - Iovine's, Giunta's, Metropolitan Bakery, and the Fair Food stand are my four regular stops.  I don't mind the tourists milling around because, hey, who wouldn't want to see what the RTM is like?  I just wish they wouldn't stand around in large clumps when I am trying to get through with my bags of goodies, but that's the price we pay.  Love the place!

There is something about the Reading Terminal market's atmosphere  that I love so much. Everything is at a few steps reach. When I was still living in Philly I would go there every week to get fruits, veggies and meats. I love how natural everything is especially with the  Amish merchants. From them, I usually get ground turkey, it's always fresh and cheap. 

It's a place where you can do your weekly grocery shopping and plus more. Sometimes, temptation gets the best out of you when you smell and see so much bake goods. I always settle with a healthy fruit smoothie. I don't remember what the place is called but it's run by Asian folks and the smoothies are made with 100% fruit with no added sugars. They also have wheat grass shots which can be requested to be put in the smoothies

No matter how much a person describes or tells you the many great things in Reading Terminal market, it's the best to go and see it for yourself.

Incredible collection of eats. Since Basic 4 closed, the vegetarian selection has hurt a bit. Nevertheless, there are multiple stands that can be called "Best in Philly" - 4th Street Cookies, The Original Turkey, Dinic's, etc. Come here for incredible food and don't be surprised to get some light live music with your lunch.

I never had a bad experience here with the staff or food.  There are plenty of cops and customs agents as well as other law enforcement people who frequent this place.  I generally roll through the drive through, which normally looks like a horrendous line, but the staff here really moves.  I normally only wait a few minutes, ten at the most.
  
They are the quickest, most efficient, moderately healthy place to eat around in South Philly.  Sure it is a chain, but this is the only fast food chain I ever go to.  I have not eaten at any other fast food chain in well over a decade.  Why bother, Chic Fil A has everything they do down to a science.

When you see a manger out on the floor talking to patrons and wiping down tables you know this is a solid place to work.  

So I have to give them a five as every possible criteria I would rate a business on they completely fulfill.  They are clean, they are pleasant, they offer a consistently great tasting product, they are efficient, they value my business and provide a safe and worry free environment in which to dine.
Gotta go here for Chocolate Covered Potato Chips - I think they're at Mueller's!

Honeygrow is my favorite fast casual spot to eat in Philadelphia! I eat here 1-2 times per week. All their food is REAL and you know that you're getting good, locally sourced ingredients when you eat here. As a health nut by default, I usually go for the Cobb salad and customize it by adding in kale, spinach, and another few add-ins. I eat the stir-fry occasionally as a treat, you can't really go wrong either way. You can customize either however you like. They also started carrying cold-pressed juices! The beet one is delicious :)

So many people that it takes away any good this place might have. 
Either prepare yourself or don't go.

There is a lot to do here. There are a wide variety of food options and some home goods. There are plenty of food booths and options. I tried a cheesesteak which was good, but not spectacular. I also had a double chocolate chip cookie which was enjoyable. Overall worth checking out but not necessarily worth a special trip if you're not in the area.

If you are from Philly or out of town...tough to beat such a condensed bunch of winners.

Hershels, Beck's, Dinics, 4th St Cookie, Rib Stand (Most underrated sandwich in Philly), Milller's Twist, By George, Chocolates by Mueller, Termini Bros, Ochs, Godshalls, Iovine Produce....All straight up winners.  

You could go to the terminal everyday for a year and never eat the same meal twice.  Most for under $10.

Great place for a non foodie to learn and appreciate different styles, and get familiar with classics.

Every city should be so lucky....now if the City of Phila would only imvest in Market East and make that neighborhood shine!
A friend recommended me this place. The food options are spectacular. You'll find a organic fresh produce market, and various food stands ranging from Asian cuisine our soul food!

I buy all of our meats in bulk from Giunta's and Godshall's and save a lot on good,  quality meats...  Plus, 4th street cookie, flying monkey, pork sammies, fried oysters, Iovine's, bassetts.... Yes, yes yes.

UMMM HELLO!!! 

If you live in the Philadelphia area, love Indian food, and have not been here... GET HERE IMMEDIATELY!

Luckily, I found this diamond in the rough on Yelp on a kate night I was hungry. The hours are awesome.

Walking in as someone who has eaten Indian food her whole life, I had expectations. Everyone which was met! They have great promotions, and discounts when you check in on yelp... all of this on already cheap food. Can't beat that.

Everything is cooked made to order. And this is authentic stuff we are talking about!

They have Mango Lassi's... which happen to be one of my favorite drinks, ready made in a refrigerator. They taste good, but I wish the consistency of them was thinner. It is VERY thick. They have other drinks in the cooler, but they are not labeled, so i disnt know what they were.

You can eat in, or take out. The music is awesomeeee.

Service is fast, the food is amazing, please do yourself a favor and stop by this place!
This is my fav place for fresh fruit and seafood. Everyone is nice. Try the Amish bakery and tbe chivken wings by far tbe best in tbe city

Truly is a must stop when in Philly. 

Different varieties of food ranging from Indian to Chinese. Tons of bakeries with cupcakes :) (red velvet in fact!) 
Bassett's ice cream is another good stop here. 

They also have a juice bar, spice shop, souvenir stores...the possibilities are endless! 

A great place to get souvenir...lot to choose from. 
I got a beeswax candle for mom. :)

Second visit to this wonderful toursit destination..My mom had never been decided on a mini road trip, located in the heart of downtown area.

Well recommended Spatros Philly Cheesesteak  since 1947....along with PA General Store, defintly a place to go for new experiences, and create a memory.

This place is heaven to my nose.
They have everything you need under one roof. Makes me wish I lived in Philadelphia.

If I was able to give 1 star I would. Today I went to Chick-fil-A, I ordered a 12 piece nugget. The manager messed up my order and gave me a #1 Deluxe meal. Now I didn't order that, imagine if I was allergic to Cheese, Lettuce, and Tomatoes.

Oh yeah, just one of the best food markets in the world.  An absolute Philadelphia gem.  If you don't believe me just ask any chef.  This is regional food at it's best and if you want "good" food then you will find regional favorites.  I can't say enough about how special this market is to Philadelphia and everything it represents.  JUST AWESOME!

I love love this market. It was my go to place to purchase my weekly groceries during my college days in Philadelphia. It is so nice to come back when visiting.
Still extremely visit during the weekends, but weekdays crowd tend to be less. It is the best place for a quick bite or just stroll around and to see the variety of shops.  My favorite place still the Dutch Eating Place - awesome for breakfast - people tend to order their pancakes (which is a generous portion) - I go for the typical egg breakfast with one of Pennsylvania staples the scrapple. Lunch is not bad - my favorite is the open-faced turkey sandwich that comes with mashed potatoes and cranberry sauce.  DiNicks (I know I spelled it wrong) is another favorite for the pork sandwich. Old City Coffee - best coffee in town at least for me.  Always bring a couple of pounds of coffee back home.
Love this place.  Lots to see and taste. Fun to wander round and look at even if you are just visiting so cant take it all home. Try the ice cream stand...raspberry and chocolate truffle is devine.

Reading Terminal Market is amazing at least. Parking is not bad considering that you are in the heart of Philadelphia. The food is Diverse as it gets from chocolate covered onions :P  haha to Juicy BBQ ribs.  A must go if your visiting Philadelphia. You might also see the Amish with they're Delicious Baking and other Amish goodies.
Excellent market for all things foodie and beyond. Had breakfast in the diner inside. Felt I had to try "scrapple" - worst thing I ever tasted, but I guess you have to try everything once!

Always a great spot for food and grocery shopping. We go every weekend and stop to get a donut first then walk around to grab things for the week. 
Can get busy around lunch on the weekends.
Reading Terminal is amazing people watching and even better eating. There are tons of amazing places to try but be prepared for crowds especially at lunch time and on the weekends.
awesome food...great shopping...I love it here...it gets really croweded and that's a kill but that one con is outweighed by the pros

It gets really crowded at lunch time and on the weekends, but it is well worth pushing through the crowds!  There are a lot of really great places to visit.  Make sure you hit the 4th street Cookie Company. Their cookies are seriously delicious. Whenever I get jury duty I always go to Reading Terminal Market. However, be warned, not every place is great; you really have to try wherever and figure out what you like!
I mean each store has their own thing, can be a bit marked up in price but you get a variety of things to choose from. Usually pretty crowded esp weekends

A must if you are in Philly.You can spend the day just roaming around the market. You can find your traditional Philly steak sandwiches to Indian food. What ever you are craving you will find it here and for cheap. There is even a all philly veggie steak sandwich.

My faves at the Reading Terminal Market:
DiNic's (either the roast pork or beef with provolone, and sweat peppers)
I dont know the name of the place buts its the only one that sells roast chicken ( wings, leg quarters, or whole or half chickens)
The Dutch Corner of the Market...

The Dutch Corner closes earlier that the rest of the market. I believe close time is 5pm.

If you go to the Market right before it closes you can find good deals on pastries.

$.75 to $1.00 per cookie vs $10.00per pound (each cookie is pretty heavy)
2 for $3.00 pastries when they normally go for$3 plus.

The only restaurant  I didn't care for was the Cajun restaurant.
Don't know what you want to eat? Have a diverse crowd to feed? Head to the Terminal. Vendors selling anything you can imagine.

Great food and wonderful atmosphere all around.  The reading terminal market is reminiscent of a nice indoor farmers market you'd find in Lancaster Pennsylvania.  The old tradition. of quaint farmers markets  in Pennsylvania is alive and well.

This is the most hectic place I've been to by far. Reading Terminal Market offers a wide selection of various foods ranging from ice cream, crepes, roast beef sandwiches, salads, and more. There are MULTIPLE restaurants and eateries inside the market itself, and it's impossible to try them all in one day. If you're ever visiting Philly, this is probably one of the most important foods spots to check out.

Love, love love it! There was so much to offer, including cheese-steaks of course! There was a performance of  a DJ with a dance battle. Little girls were rapping! It was so great! We didn't wait long for any lines or for seating. I tried both a Philly cheese-steak and the Cajun restaurant--both delicious. I wish I could have spent more time in there, but I did not have the time.
I was here once during the Car show. It (the market in general) was overly crowded and had a dirty feel to it. We ended up at the Down Home Diner. Food was ehhh ok. Staff was really nice though.
Always something new, different, and exciting. This place is like a cross-section of the Philadelphia gastronomic experience. Do not miss it!

Has pretty much everything you could ask for.

Gyros ... roast pork sandwiches (yes yes Dinic's ... thanks Adam Richman) ... cookies ... chocolate ... produce ... Chinese food ... ice cream ... everything is pretty much here! 

The only downside and the reason it doesn't get a 5 star review? All the tourists that manage to simply stop in the middle of the crammed walkways ... either go into the stall or move on please!
Needed some coffee before my bus ride from Philly to NYC. Stopped by this terminal, so many options. At the end I went with a regular cup from the Amish diner, thanks!
great place great food just not a fan of the location with so many homeless people and pissy smells.

This is Philly's heart and soul, and of course, stomach.  It's fun to wander up and down the aisles to browse and get hungry before you eat. Grab a buttery fresh Amish pretzel (eat your heart out Auntie Anne's -- this is the REAL fresh buttered pretzel!) while you wander.  Try De Nic's roast pork with brocolli rabe and provolone -- I think it was voted Best Sandwich Ever, Anywhere --- or something like that.  Or Salumeria.  Or canolli at Termini's.  Or buy a baguette at Metropolitan Bakery, and some cheese at one of the amazing cheeseries -- triple brie maybe?  Spices at the Head Nut?  Fresh fish (with head on OF COURSE)?  Oh I could just eat here the entire day.  One tip:  don't go to the big produce market the Monday, Tuesday or Wedsnesday before Thanksgiving -- it's INSANE!

This place was incredible. A must visit place in Philly. We tried numerous items at several places. A food lovers paradise. My wife and I walked through the entire market one time, saw what they had and immediately I started drooling.  My favorite  was Dinic's, I had the brisket sandwich with spinach. KILLER!!!
Good food at almost every store, not cheap though and avoid the lunch hour very busy but overall great experience

We order takeout from here pretty frequently and have never been disappointed. I always order a paneer tikka kati roll, which is so good I've never felt the need to get something different! My boyfriend loves the chicken tikka just as much. One is good for a small meal or a snack, but there are a number of vegetable rolls that are great in addition to a paneer or meat roll. They are very generous with their additional sauces and we've never had any issues with delivery. Great place for takeout!
We always go to the market when we are in Philadelphia , if you can't get it there you won't find it, I love the the diversity of things and people.
This place is dank.  The only drawback is that it's too dank and gets a bit too crowded.   Any type of food,  drink, all with an authentic Philly as duck vibe.
You cannot beat this place. Just such variety and all of it is wonderful. If you are ever on jury duty, just skip on over and have some wonderful food.
So sick and tired of being touched inappropriately while shopping there! There isn't even security around!

This place really reminds me of Pike Place Market in Seattle & Essex/Chelsea Market in NYC. For anyone visiting Philly, this is a must visit!

To me, the reading terminal market was food heaven. There was so many food stalls. With too much choices, time constraint, and limited stomach space, I only ended up eating from 2 stalls: 1) Wursthaus Schmitz (german foods), and 2) Beiler's Bakery.

For anyone that likes a delicious bratwurst & schnitzel sandwich, and potato pancakes - Wursthaus Schmitz is a must visit. Super delicious! The donuts from Beiler's Bakery was another notable mention, as it was delicious as well. 

Street parking is difficult around this area. However, there are 2 parking lots near the market, and it is $4 for 2 hours. After 2 hours, it is $10. After 2 hours there is another charge (forgot what it is). Just make sure to have your card stamped by a food stall to get this parking discount, and remember you need to spend at least $10 to get this stamp.

There are many tables on the back area of the market, where you can sit and eat there.

I highly recommend that everyone experience this iconic market.  An overwhelming amount of restaurants and shops to experience.  I love coming to buy cheese, specialty food items, bread, lunch meat, and Mueller's chocolate covered pretzels!  I don't recommend coming during lunch and the weekend when it is so crowded and congested.  There are so many people that it becomes unbearable which is the reason it loses a star for me.  But if you time it well you will be glad to have the experience.

Lovely place to come for a quick bite to eat, tons of options to choose from. I especially recommend the Puerto Rican food, the tostones are incredible. Also, ice cream! The place is visually really interesting as well, so it's worth even just walking around and taking it all in.

[Service]
Had Cheers Cut for take out for a large party of about 10 people. We called ahead of time and went out in about 10-15 minutes and they were quick and had everything set for us when we got there. It was a simple pick up and pay. 

[Food]
The chicken was great, evenly seasoned and gigantic. I had ordered the Ninja Chicken cutlet. If you love chicken and won't be bored eating a huge piece of chicken this will be your cup of tea, but if not I would not recommend getting this unless you are sharing with another person with a bowl of rice to go along with it. I had made that mistake and could barely eat the entire thing and wanted rice the entire time! So try and order the rice dishes, the only thing you'd be missing is the picture worthy chicken cutlet, but you won't regret the choice!

I go here once a week to get meats and veggies. So much better than any supermarket. Everything is fresher and less expensive. There's also a few good sit down eateries. The pretzels are fantastic. You can watch them make it, so you know it's fresh. Go early because the Amish leave early.
Such a rad place. For tourists and non- tourists, alike. I usually try 10 different things and have just a few bites of each! I come here each and every Philly trip-- well worth your time and money.

Enjoyed walking around and seeing all the different vendors. Don't recommend going
On the weekend but will try to go back doing the week.

Despite the tourists looking for terrible diners to eat at, this place is pretty amazing.

This is the best place to grocery shop in the city. Period.
 My "go to" places:

Produce: Iovines
Meats: Giuntas Prime Shop is my favorite, but Lancaster County Meats has a great selection (sometimes better) and Martin's meats is where to go for flank steaks or whole hams and turkeys.
Food: Herschel's East Side Deli (pastrami) OR Hatville Deli (corned beef)
Donuts and Pickles - Beilers. for Salted caramel donuts and horseradish dill pickles.

Where can I begin with this place? 

It was the first place that I worked and called home in my early 20's .... if you want variety on food/goods/groceries/gifts it's a one stop shop. 

In a crew with picky eaters or people with different taste buds? They have a food court and various other no mans land seating separate from individual businesses. Everyone can go off on their own and meet back up to eat together. 

It's open early so it's a great stop for breakfast and a staple for bringing out of towners. 

A little hectic during conventions (car show/flower show/tattoo convention ) but other than that it's one of my favorite places to go. 

Becks Cajun Cafe has the most unique Cheesesteak in the entire market, it's a Cajun spin off and will change your life. Dinic'd roast beef obviously a must... Carmen's is my favorite for your typical lunch sandwich and they have an awesome cheesesteak. Flying monkey is a bakery..their Whoopie Pies are amazing and they make rose cupcakes that will make you come back. 

All and all I love the RTM and I always bring people here because it's a great representation of how diverse Philly is. All they need is an Ethiopian spot and I'm moving in.
This is a great place to find a variety of great produce, farm fresh items, or just a quick lunch. Lots of variety. This is a Philadelphia mainstay that makes this city what it is.

Wow.  OINK!  Foodie heaven baby!  I've been here only twice, but can't wait to go back and explore more.  I was introduced to this wonderland by my partner who is from Philly.  It's a fresh market and food court with anything & everything and then some.

Delilah's - I was sad to hear of their closing.  Fried chicken was huge, crispy & juicy.  Greens were damn good, mac & cheese okay and the catfish super tender.

Termini Bros Bakery - We've picked up several cakes from them.  It's good but I"m not a dessert foodie.

A.J. Pickle Patch - Just wanted to try something from them while browsing.  The pickles are good!  All kinds of varieties.  

Tommy DiNiC's is on my radar, courtesy of course of Triple D.  Hopefully in September when we're back again!
Just wish there were more veg-friendly spots. Nonetheless, awesome place!

A fun market to hang out at and try awesome food!! Love everything about it. My top favs in there is Termini Bros Bakery for cannoli or cheesecake, By George for a cheese steak, Fox and Son for there funnel cake or cheese curds, Peking Duck has the best duck in the city! Beilers Doughnuts
Looks like everything's been pretty well said. Just adding my 5 stars. I could spend like a week in here, and not get bored ....

Open until 3:30 am on Friday and Saturday nights amazing. Good place, nice food and friendly staff.. Good Kati roll place in Philly finally like NYC.. Simply love it. Will surely come back and recommend.

The Terminal Market is a must see when visiting Philadelphia.  It's a great slice of life from Eastern PA in general with Amish-owned businesses, Jewish delis and kosher stores, local crafts, etc.  Restaurants, specialty gifts, groceries, butchers, and coffee bars galore. Sometimes there's live music. Usually crowded, but lively and fun.  For locals, it's the best place to go when you're on lunch from jury duty. : )
Really delicious kebab and platter food. Very reasonable price for the quality you can get at fast food ! Ambient environment !

So much to see!!! So coming back for this place. So many good food, I wanna try. It's just crowded. We had a pulled pork sandwich and beef brisket sandwich from Dinic. It was GREAT and juice. And a milk shake from a ice cream place that est. 1861 Bassetts. Very Milky taste. LOVE IT.
Sorry, I'm from Philly also. I feel like I'd be eating in the Broad Street Subway. Never even tried the food, probably good but like I said I don't want to eat in the Subway

A tourist must-see, but a bit crowded and overwhelming to visit too often as a local. Husband and I went on a great food tour which culminated in the market. Highly recommend one of those. Tips: smoothies, Thai food, organic veg market, old city coffee, and a grocery stand with all kinds of British delights (tea, marmite).
Love this place and all the options.  The amish stands are great.  One of the best places in Philly to visit!

I probably go here once every month. Which I never intended to. Because I live in New Jersey, and it's quite far.

But my boyfriend and I can't seem to stay away. Not with Tommy DiNic's and that roast pork sandwich. I've also grown quite fond of the Flying Monkey Bakery with their s'mores bar and butter cakes.

It's always a wonderful, worthwhile, and fattening experience at Reading Terminal.

A good place to grab lunch. They have lots of interesting drink options.

I got the chicken biryani ($9) and I did like it quite a bit. Maybe it could have been "saucier" though? The chicken and portions were generous and tender. 

The service was quite nice too.

I could hands down eat here everyday. From the selection of amazing meats and cheeses to each vendor, I am in love with these place. The owners are ridiculously nice and helpful, and genuinely love their food. I love it when people are passionate about their craft and you could spend all day talking to these people about the dishes they are so proud of. Make sure to get some doughnuts from here and the crepes are also out of this world! Basically, you can never go wrong by going here. I make it a point to take anyone who has not experienced the amazingness that is this little foodie heaven.

A wonderful place for a casual meal, or to buy meat, baking, produce or preserves.  Many booths are Amish run, and their food is fresh and delicious.  Add in the ethnic spots, and the choices are too many to list.  Not to be missed.

Horrible food and I'm not a picky eater. The portion is very small, the size of a taco, they make it look like you're getting a burrito. It's pretty much frozen food that you're paying to have microwaved and they didn't even do that right, it was still cold and dry on the inside.

I even tipped the girl at the counter thinking I was being nice, but she didn't do me any favors.

I will say the mango lassi was decent which saved it from 1 star, otherwise the bill was over $10 in the end for a cold snack and a drink. Definitely not planning on coming back.

This is a must for anyone who is a resident or visiting Philly.  They have an eclectic blend of vendors. All the vendors are really very thankful that you are doing business with them.  Even if they have a line around their booth.  I always make sure that whenever I'm in Philly that I go to Reading Terminal Market.   

It may be crowded, but the Amish sticky buns make it all so worth while.  Heavenly good.  I bought some for family, but doubt it'll make it to them. 

It's also a great place to grab a soda and people watch.  Such a great mix of people.  I could of stayed there for hours taking in the sights and the most curious thing for me was when I saw this big brass pig that was sitting on a clear box and people would come up to it and put money in the box and they would either get their picture taken with it or have their kids kiss it.   I was a bit lost on that one, but hey made for interesting watching.

All in all a good time and an experience, but be prepared there a lot of people that go to it and most are nice you do run across the occasional a** hole.

200+ reviews later, finally writing this jawns up. That's what we say in Philly, right?

I ain't gonna lie to you, kid. I usually only come here when people are in town visiting because it's made for indecisive people like me! Sure I want to take my out of towners to my favy restaurants, but at the same time I'm like "well hmmm, this person only eats vegetarian, and this chick has a gluten allergy, and this assh%le only eats steak..." etc etc so it can be like a nightmare coming up with a place where we can all be happy. Hence Reading Terminal where I don't have to dictate anything, I can just point you to what you're craving and we can all meet up by the tables by the piano (real, not electric today!). Great! 

The festive thing about this place is that it's not just food. They've got flowers, they've got cookbooks, they've got jewelry, they've got kitchen gadgets... So it's a great place to wander around too, which is perfect when you're sick of taking everybody to see the bell for the 100th time. And hey, I needed olive oil and a bag of green beans... and viola! I can grab those things here too. So wonderfully efficient, one stop shopping like Target but like, less evil. I think. 

The only uncomfortable thing which also makes me laugh dorkily to myself is the waiting-for-the-tables nightmare. When it's crowded and you've hit like everybody with your ginormous roast pork sandwich trying to hustle to find a table you then have to STALK the various areas and watch people eat, counting how many minutes it'll take them to finish based on their current consumption rate/conversation. I like to find the quiet people. They leave faster. But it's so awkward swooping down and crowding them when they're just trying to relax and enjoy their Amish food. But it's gotta be done. No way around you feeling my beady-eyed stare at the back of your head as you try to finish your fried mac and cheese ball. Sigh.

Do it. Come here. It's quintessential philly, baby.

LOVED IT!

I can't wait to move to Philly and do my grocery shopping here.

The highlight for me was the apple dumpling drizzled with fresh cream that I procured from one of the Amish vendors.  It was better than any apple pie I have ever had the joy of eating.  

Prices also seemed very reasonable.  Lots of selection, too.
Omg I have never seen so many food choices in one place!  there were options that catered to anyone and everyone literally so many options wow!
Great vendors, fresh food, a lively scene - what else needs to be said? I'm there 2-3 times a week.

Lots and lots of options for good food. Wish I could have tried them all! I will say the mixture of smells from all the different restaurants and meat counters made me nauseous at times. The smells make it hard for me to want to go back.
Somewhat overwhelming at first, but take a your time, a few deep breaths and you'll find you way. There's something for everyone.
Diverse / Versatile place.  Great organic food!  Breakfast and shopping are the best times, lunch is usually a mad house but fantastic none the less.

Always a fun food excursion. Very very busy today but it was Saturday and  filled with too many foodie thrill seekers. I ate at Dinics's and ordered the roast pork with rapieni. It was a perfect balance of cheese to meat to bread and i was very happy with this classics sandwich. The place was mobbed and I'd like to go back again when it wasn't so crazy

Although I know sometimes the new employees don't give you a lot in your bowl, whenever I go, the people who have been working there for a while always give me just enough! The service is great, I've never encountered someone snarky or rude. Sometimes the wait is long, but no one can really prevent that if people just keep coming in and the line only can go a certain pace, right?

My favorite location. Clean, and no issues.

Have loved this place since first coming to Philadelphia almost 40 years ago.  It's titled a bit away from a true food market and caters a bit more to tourists and the lunch crowd, but the mix is a healthy one, and real Philadelphians still come here to do their food shopping.
Awesome!!! Whatever you are looking for and whatever food you desire is here!! PERIOD

The menu rotates by the season. Even though they're better known for the bowls, my favorite oddly is the burger. Depending on the time of year, it'll either be a beet burger or a tomato burger. The aioli is tad bit strong, but all the food, including the burger, does a great job of making the vegetables the star of the dish, you forget he absence of meat. 

There's a lot of seating here, and outlets, including USB outlets. There's an odd cluster of seats in rows like a class room if you like eating alone or miss being in lecture.
A must-see in Philly! Lunch hour is craaaaaazy crowded, but that's part of the fun if you're up for it.

We came here so many times during our short trip in Philadelphia. We came around 5pm and were surprised to learn that the place closed at 6pm - which was so early! If you plan on doing dinner, be aware of those times.

Dutch eating place = AMAZING breakfast! 

Dinics = amazing pork sandwich!

Miller's twist = life changing pretzels.

So many other places for delicious baked goods, chocolates and so forth. I cannot recommend it enough as a tourist for something fast and easy peasy.

In addition to being a tourist attraction, it is a wonderful place for locals.  All kinds of food at reasonable prices.  They work hard to keep it from being another food court, but the lunch restaurants they have are great.  The Down Home  Diner is excellent and fun.  And the new donut place is out of sight.  Not to be missed.

Absolutely LOVE Reading Terminal. I have been going to Reading Terminal Market for as long as I can remember. And there has never been a day that I haven't been disappointed. I bring visitors of Philly here as well. 

I usually go to buy meat and produce and spices. I love how I can always find what I am looking for. And a lot of times I leave with everything I needed and a lot of awesome things I found and could not live with out. 

I warn you all it gets crowded because it is a great lunch spot in the city. So if you go and want to shop then come early. Make you sure you get what you want. Then stay for the ambiance and bustle for tourists and regulars getting food and meeting up with friends.

Just another 5 star rating, I mean what more could I add that hasn't been said already? My gf and I were staying across the street at the Marriott and if we were staying in philly for more than a day we would have gone to reading terminal market every day. It's that good. We walked in at around 1pm on a saturday afternoon to scope out our dinner options since we just had lunch. We wanted to try Tommy DiNic's cause of all the hype over their roast pork sandwich and brisket, but the line was long so we figured we would come back closer to dinner time. This was a BIG MISTAKE.. and i'll tell you why in a second. When we came back at 4:30pm they were sold out... of everything. yep everything and the market closes at 6 on a saturday. We were both disappointed so we settled for Beiler's Donuts, Bassetts Ice Cream, and Miller's Twist Pretzels to comfort us. Beiler's donuts did the trick. We got the maple bacon, banana creme, harvest apple 2x, pumpkin, and blueberry fritter. They were all delicious, fresh, and omg i'm dreaming of those donuts as I'm writing this review. My favorite was definitely the maple bacon. The donuts are cheap for what they are $5.25 for half a dozen. Bassetts was also good, their ice cream is very creamy. I had green tea and cookies and cream, but the ice cream here is pricey. Miller's twist was the last thing we tried and they make their pretzels really well, not overly salted and reasonably priced ($2.25 for a regular pretzel.) So glad I don't live near Beiler's cause I would get fatttttttt.
If you struggle making decisions, then this is not the place for you. We wanted cheesesteaks and decided on Spataro's. The line moved quickly and worth the wait. There's something for everyone here.

A nice atmosphere, good, if narrow selection, but overall it was absolutely delicious. I got a meatball sandwich with provolone and it was just really good, My entire meal was under $10 which is also great. The servers were smiling and friendly, and the fact that its right near the UPenn museum of archaeology and Anthropolgy makes it even better for a history buff like me. I whole-heartedly recommend it!~

I never review places but I love this place so much I had to give em props. Good price, delicious flavors, convenient and fast.
It's awesome.

IMO, Philadelphia as a city doesn't have much going for it, but this place is truly special. Anytime a friend mentions a trip they are going to take to Philly, I unfailingly mention this place  for a visit.  There's quite a number of good eats all under one roof, not unlike Midtown Market in Minneapolis.  There's a soul food place here that's a favorite of Oprah Winfrey.  You will get FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) syndrome inside this place.  Lots of variety and you really can't go wrong.  The location is really close to the center of the city, if not in Center City, so it's quite easy to get to.
Loved visiting the Reading Terminal Market on a day trip to Philadelphia. It is indeed a food lover's paradise. You name it, they probably have it. Most places only accept cash.

You know it must be good when you drive two hours just to come here for lunch! Took the drive from Jersey just to go to Tommy Dinic's for their delicious pork, cheese, and broccoli rabe sandwich. It's a must when visiting!!! Went to BEILER's Donuts for dessert. These spongey, warm, delicious doughnuts will change your perspective on doughnuts. Expect a line that moves fast (don't be discouraged). It sure is worth it. Got a whole dozen to take home. Another yelper quoted this place as a foodie heaven. I'd have to second that!!

LOVE THIS PLACE.
Definitely my favorite part of Philly (Mainly in part because they have Beiler's donuts -- the most amazing thing I have ever eaten). There was so much to do here!

Basically, it's an area filled with restaurants - all with their own specialties whether it's seafood, philly cheesesteaks, grilled cheese, baked goods, ice cream, etc - as well as little shops for basically anything you could want. They have a garden store with flowers and seeds to plant, as well as olive oil shops, candy shops, and many produce, fresh meats, and cheese shops.

This place is a food-lover's dream, and I would highly recommend it to anyone. I wasn't a huge fan of Philly, but RTM was the BOMB.

this pizza will change your life. The best crust I've ever eaten and I will think about it and compare every crust in the future to it.  I usually don't get my pizza heated up but you have to here, it's on a whole new level. Also, cooler full of free beer near the door and it isn't crappy beer either.
Everything you want is here! I've been to similar places in other states, but none do it as well as the RTM. The lines can get crazy, so definitely go during off times.

This place is so much fun. Just walking in you want to eat and spend spend spend. 
There is a wine store in the very back that is sooo so good. They have a pear wine that is native in the amish area. Everyone there is so nice and you even see a few locals. Not just all us out of towners. I definatly recommend this place as a great stop to introduce you to the city. Not to mention you can walk everywhere.

Yay for touristy things! We did a random day trip and just had to stop at the market for some food and Amish items. Very clean place with wonderfully intoxicating fragrances everywhere.  If it's your first time, walk around first to decide what to eat before committing to just one place and regretting not trying all the other varieties.  You can get jams, coffees, jerky, sandwiches, beer, poboys, and even butcher cuts.  Try as much as you can!

I wish I'd have had more time to explore this place during my trip. It's a huge building full of more vendors and food than you can possibly imagine. All of my friends were raving about the things they'd eaten from the various vendors they tried. Don't go to Philadelphia without checking this place out!
So many choices that you can't be disappointed. When I visited, I had a warm apple fritter from Beiler's Bakery and it was delicious.

Yes the food here is amazing with plentiful choices.  However, it is ridiculously crowded. Be prepared to wait a half hour to an hour in some places.  Just walking through the place is an adventure.  It's so congested that you can hardly move. Good luck finding an open table to actually sit and enjoy your overpriced meal.  The place is a tourist trap.  

Go there once, just to say you've been there.  Before you do, maybe consider eating in neighboring Chinatown.
Great place to grab a bite to eat.  So many food choices!!! The only hard part is finding a place to sit!

Always super busy on the weekends! I would recommend getting there as soon as they open. Otherwise the options are out of this world. My favorite is Dinic's - They have some of the best slow roasted pork. I always go with the sharp provo and broccoli rabe. Stop by and check it out if you are ever in Philly. Lot to choose from!

Being from Hawaii, I had only heard of the Reading Terminal from playing the Parker Brothers game, Monopoly.  Hey, little did I know or realize that these railways (Reading, Pennsylvania, Short Line and B & O (Baltimore & Ohio)) actually existed!  Not only did they exist, the Parker Brothers strategically chose these railroads for their board game because of their routes and destinations.  Well, I've gotten over my ignorance as my business travels have taken me to the great city of Philadelphia many times.

During my first visit, which I think was the most memorable, my taxi driver was kind enough to point out the Reading Terminal Market just as he drove into the porte cochère of the Marriott hotel that I would stay at for a week.  The history and touristy draw of this market didn't dawn on me until I got into my room, began to read about it (and other Philadelphia "hot spots") and found that my room overlooked the market.  I was really excited about going to check it out right away but, having just come off an eleven plus hour flight, I, instead, opted for a short nap.

When I awoke, I quickly jogged my way into the market.  This historic landmark is divided into 3 structures:  1- Reading Terminal Headhouse, 2-Reading Terminal Train shed and 3- Reading Terminal Market.  I found out that the Reading Terminal Market is located BENEATH the Train shed.  The architecture of the terminal is beautiful and was designed in the Italian Renaissance-style.  In parts of the market, you can see the engineering and construction details it took to build these immense structures.  Back in the day, it was an open-air Farmer's market.  This is a huge Farmer's Market that has been in operation since 1892.

It was dazzling to see so many vendors from various ethnicities or cultures ranging from bakeries, flower markets, fresh produce, ice cream and restaurants--All Under ONE Roof!  This market is a melting pot of The aromas, colors and sounds started to drive me wild.  I immediately started eating my way through market starting from the famed Bassett's Ice Cream (America's OLDEST ice cream company) to Termini Bros (Italian bakery - got my FIRST cannoli) and onto DiNic's (for an Italian roast pork, Provolone and broccoli rabe sandwich).   

This was a day of FIRSTS for me... I got to see and experience a bit of Americana, hear the local cultural excitement within this huge market and  smell and taste culturally diverse Pennsylvanian cuisine. Geez, I thought to myself that since I'd be in Philadelphia for a week and hadn't really scheduled any other dining plans, THIS was going to be my life-saver!  I had to try the Pennsylvania Dutch specialty, scrapple.  Ah, if you have to ask what it is, I'm not telling...it was just tasty!  Alas, I ended up dining at other noted Philly restaurants and only got to return to the RTM 3 more times to get myself to more cannoli, amaretti, biscotti, and those Italian roast pork sandwiches.

Granted, the RTM may be more tourist-oriented but it sure was conveniently located to the Pennsylvania Convention Center which is in the Market East section.  I did return to shop and dine here on subsequent trips to Philadelphia.

Oh, just in case you're wondering... The reason why the Parker Brothers chose the Pennsylvania, Reading and Short Line (Shore Fast Line) railroads for the ORIGINAL U.S. Edition of Monopoly board game was because of their routes led directly to Atlantic City.  A side note:  B & O Railroad also operated on the East Coast but did NOT serve Atlantic City.

What can I say that hasn't been said. I lived in Philly for a year and Reading Terminal market was easily my favorite place to be. In fact, I may go as far as to say that it is my favorite place... PERIOD. Obviously there is a nostalgia factor, however, this place lives up to the hype. 
Reading Terminal is situated right in the heart of center city and is located above what is now the Jefferson Station (used to be Market St Station). The market has various vendors where you can buy your high quality meat, cheese, fish, and produce. Not to mention Ivarone brothers, which has the most affordable high quality produce that I've ever encountered living on the east coast. Reading terminal also has vendors selling cuisines from all over the world. These are your must go places: Amish market area, Tommy Dinic's (roast pork sandwich), Ivarone Brothers, and Hope's cookies. The Amish area is only open I believe Wed. or Thurs. through Saturday. They have an Amish diner which is incredible (check out the baked apples). They also sell hot dogs wrapped in crispy homemade pretzels and cheese which are to die for. The Amish bakery must also not be missed and you honestly can't go wrong with pie by the slice or any of the various other traditional baked confections they offer. Tommy Dinic's is a must too. Adam Richman (Host of Man v. Food on Travel Channel) coined their Roast Pork Sandwich the best sandwich in the country. Lastly, you CAN'T miss Hope's cookies. They also sell fudge, but you need to get those cookies. Everyone heads to 4th St Cookie Co (also in Reading Terminal), which has great cookies, but nothing compared to Hope's! They have unique gooey flavors like Heath Bar, caramel pecan, and my personal favorite, Wilbur's peanut butter (PB cup chunks and chocolate chunks). 
Whenever you or anyone you know ever enters the city of Philadelphia, you must forget what your doing for a good hour and head to Reading Terminal Market!

This place is just awesome. It can be overwhelming but it's worth it. Get a smoothie and or a coffee as you decided what you want to eat. The oysters are great. The Jewish deli is great. The donuts are fantastic. Try going during the week and not at normal feeding hours to really explore.

i think i could spend all day here, eating, shopping and people watching. really didn't know what to expect when mongo said we'd be going here. what a delightful surprise. he might have regret his decision when he was dragging me out of the exit by my arm. while he wanted to try all the meat and sandwich shops (which there are plenty), i wanted to try out all of the delectable sweet spots (candy, cookies, chocolates). thank goodness for my waistline, we were in a rush and i only got to taste some heavenly cookies. but we definitely plan on going back and getting our fill!

The best lunch location in the city! You can get just about anything under the sun! Ice cream, cookies, smoothies, sandwiches, beer, you name it, they have it! Our favorites include DiNic's, Basset's Ice Cream, and the Dutch Eating Place.
My favorite place to eat in Philly! You can find anything you want and the atmosphere is great for tourists and newcomers. If you touristy is what you want, they serve great cheesesteaks!
great food. 10/10 would recommend. very crowded so it's a great spot to people watch.. if ya know what i mean
They have a great selection of fresh food. The place gets way to busy on the weekends and other than eating a quick meal. I wouldn't recommend spending your time here.

I ordered a sandwich and a smoothie.  I realized I meant to order fruit and ice and told the girl serving me I'm sorry I actually wanted a fruit and ice not a smoothie.  She looks at me like the world ends and when I turn away to go pay I see her shaking her head like "what's wrong with that person".  I ignore it until literally 30 seconds later another person orders a regular smoothie and the same girl from 10 feet away loudly yells "yes thank you!".   That was my breaking point and I walked away.  If you're going to be rude to me, you're getting no business sorry but not sorry the place across from you was way better anyways.
love this place! there is so much food variety here. It is my go-to spot on Fridays after class. I highly recommend going to beilers and east-hershel (order the pastrami).

So, I don't know. Maybe we went on an off night...

Anyway, here we go.

The Good:

We had a dozen of the happy hour buck-a-shuck oysters. They were absolutely dope. We are going back just for them!

And the $3. drafts? NICEE!

Also, the service was spot-on, and the atmosphere was super-fun!

The Bad:

I'm sorry, but the dollar-apiece mac and cheese croquets were only 5/10.  The crunch was decent, but, alas, the flavor was nondescript.  

The fish BLT was just wrong. My girl and I both really wanted to love it, BUT, the ciabatta bread was soggy (cardinal sin), which pretty much ruined it. Who knows if it could have been good if it was made with good bread.  

We took the fish BLT home and fed it to the dog...

Also...  I asked for the french fries to be extra crispy--they came super soggy...

There you have it.

Anyway:

We WILL go back for the oysters, and trivia night.

Cheers!

I've been lucky enough to visit Reading Terminal Market for breakfast and lunch the last 4 days. It has the best variety of everything I've craved while my visit to Philly. It got really crowded in the market, but the different restaurants were super quick and kept their meals delicious.
This place is great and who wouldn't like all the great options for diverse food.  Busy place and rightfully so as there is Mexican, Thai, Amish, German, Cajan, etc. etc.  You can not go wrong here.
I love, love, LOVED, Loved the variety of ethnic foods and goods available here. Must go.  This market has anything and everything.  So fresh and so inviting.  GO GO GO HERE!!

This is an indoor food market with tons of great food options. This was our second time here. Both times we had great food. The place is small and the lines can get long. Go hungry, but give yourself time to walk around and decide what you want to eat. The aisles are small so walking is tight. There is a parking garage across the street on the north side that if you spend $10 at a vendor they can validate your parking and it's only $4 for two hours. Everything looks so good it's hard to choose what to eat.

The Reading Market was a regular shopping spot for me when I lived in Philly.  The food is amazing and the feel of the market is so nice.  People bustling around and trying to buy the freshest veggies.
I'm in love with this Market, they have many unique and cool vendors. Many different options for ready to eat foods, fresh produce, cheeses, and sweets! Can't wait to return!
How can you not love it?  So much fun food from Italian to Pennsylvania Dutch.   Great for people watching too.

Worst Chick-fil-A ever. The drive through is always a 45 min ordeal. Food is cold and the employees are rude. I ordered a grilled chicken club and it was half off the bun, cheese was a thick slice thrown on as an afterthought, not melted at all. Kids nuggets had no breading and were dry. Looked as though they'd been heated in a microwave.
As far as touristy things go, eh it's okay. Great place to wander in and out of if you are close. VERY crowded most of the time, but many many options to choose from.
Dinics, Old City Coffee, Terminis in that order on rotation.... simply the best.
It's so great there and very unique. So many choices, so many good places to eat and buy fresh fruits, vegetables, etc. A real experience to see.

Philadelphia staple. If you go in the morning you can avoid some crowds, but it's almost always jam packed. Great vendors for food, produce, groceries, and gifts. Most of the places are very inexpensive so you can save lots of money if you brave the crowds.
you have to go if you ever visit philly. they have every type of food vendor you can think of. cheap and just....great.

I don't particularly love Potbellys sandwiches (though I know a lot of people think they're delicious), but I do love their insanely huge cookies/brownie bars and potato chips. That being said, Potbellys is a good addition to the other restaurants in this little strip-mall-ish type place on City Ave.

The employees are friendly and the prices are okay. I personally prefer CPK or Chipotle when I'm in the area, but if you're looking for a quick sandwich Potbellys isn't a bad option.

A foodie's paradise. A foodie photographer's paradise. A person who has a hard time making decisions would drown in this place. And I consider that a fantastic thing.

Even if you're not a foodie, go at least once when you have a bit of time so you can peruse through all the shops. The experience is unlike any other restaurant market place in Philly.

I ordered house fried noodles from Sang Kee, but I would recommend getting something a little more novel since you can get the full Sang Kee experience at their main restaurant a couple of blocks down. I'm looking to go back enough times to pick out my favorites from each shop. Don't worry, I'll be sharing it on my yelp reviews!
Good Kati rolls with good spice sand flavor. Reasonable prices and nice, fast, and friendly service!

How can you hate this place? It's a foodie's heaven that's open all season! Cheap good eats from ice cream, to doughnuts, to chinese, to soul food. You can't go wrong in this place if you want to try an array of dishes from different cultures. It' a market so don't expect it be fancy.

Cool place to go especially if you are new to or visiting Philly. Can be very overstimulating. Beilers Douts is a must try. Herschel's is good for a breakfast sandwich with pastrami. You can get fresh seafood.. not sure how great it is. Many other new places I have yet to try. Fun just to walk around and take it all in.

I love the market!!! So much food excellent experiences! I wish I lived closer! I love having so many different things to do! And traveling to the places are to far away! Excellent  I definitely recommend anyone to go here!

How could anyone not love this place!  It is a food heaven filled with anything your heart could desire.  I'm pretty sure I stopped by twice a day each time in Philly since it was conveniently located right across from my hotel.  There are vendors offering a wide variety of foods such as oysters, doughnuts, duck, pork and steak sandwiches, candies, produce, really anything and it was all amazing.  I really could spend all of my time and money and time in here and not care one single bit!  I only wish it was open late at night to satisfy my post bar hunger!
Love this place! So much selection, and it's a Philly staple. I recommend the fresh produce and seafood.
I know a lot of people love the Reading Terminal Market but when I went I thought it was to crowded and crazy!
One of must-go-to place in Philly. There're many interesting shops here, including one of the best ice cream places in town. It's great even just for sightseeing.

Everything yiu might be interested to eat and more, it can provide many people  will  a god healthy choice for a down right moan fest of delight.  From Asain  to Amish,  seafood to pizza.  Also you can pu c k up an old fashioned and good book to read while you dine. There are many fin place's to eat and drink as well.

The food was good but the dinner was ruined after a person from the street came in and aggressively demanded my attention ("hey, YOU, yeah YOU").  Ultimately, he forcefully took some of my money. The restaurant staff did not try to intervene (they just watched) even though he was also sexually harassing one of the employees.  The guy was continually fishing in his pants pocket screaming so one has to assume it was some sort of weapon...which did not positively add to my dining experience.

 As you can imagine, this experience was terrifying.  I spoke with the staff after the man left and they said that these things happen.  No, they don't.  But it seemed like this might have not been the first time the staff has experienced this.

They really needed to tell him to leave and call the cops.  I certainly feel that they do not care about the physical well-being of their customers.  The restaurant also made zero effort to make things right, too.

I will not go back because it is not safe to eat here.

A huge city block sized indoor market place with dozens of vendors.  
A must stop while in Philly, but you'll find that you keep coming back, we did. So much to see and several choices for breakfast and lunch.  Opens at 8:00 am with lines forming at the doors and closes at six pm so don't get there too late.  For breakfast we liked the Dutch Eatery, the Creperie,  the Old town coffee and brasserie donuts.    We also liked the honey shop and the olive oil shop.  You can find some great local (not touristy) gift ideas here.  We didn't get to try and fresh baked breads but they looked and smelled fabulous.  If you are lucky to be staying nearby you'll be able to visit frequently.   But Just the sights and smells make it a great stop on your trip to Philly.

I love coming here. There are so many different food options and stands to get gourmet, meats, cheese, etc. I could get lost in here for hours just walking around and checking out the different things each stand has. If you're with a group of people that's not sure what they want to eat, this is a great place to bring them. There are so many options, that everyone is bound to find something. Even if you're not hungry, this is just a place worth coming to for the experience. It's almost always crowded, but even when it's not it'll feel tight because there are so many stands. Even with that, I love Reading Terminal and I can't wait to come back!

BEWARE OF PARKING SCAMS IN THIS AREA........I pulled into a lot across the street that advertised parking for  $17, little did I know it was $17 per 10 MINUTES!!!!  Even though I immediately pulled out I had to pay the $17 and that set the mood for most of the day.  We ended up parking several blocks away at a meter that had an hour limit; by the time we walked the distance to the market we could only stay about 15 minutes before we had to leave for the long walk back to the meter.  From what we saw of the market it is a place we'd love to further explore although the crowd was overwhelming.   I truly believe if you cannot safely maneuver a stroller you shouldn't be in an area with such a concentrated crowd. 

 Come hungry!  We left in a mouthwatering state from the array of food smells but too long of lines to actually order anything.  If anyone has any suggestions for parking on a budget and manageable distance I'd love to hear about it!

This market rivals any market in the country. If you come to Philadelphia to visit the historic sites, you will get hungry this is the historic market in Philly.

You can eat here. You sit at their counter or at the seating area in the middle which means you can each eat what you want; hoagies, Chinese Soup, Thai, Middle Eastern, Soul Food and Amish food. 

It is really a market in the international sense. Fishmongers, butchers, produce stands, spices, pastries... and smells. This is food aroma heaven.
So many reasons to shop here. I don't even know where to start. Hell, there's even like 3 or 4 places that just sell cheese. You're bound to find what you came for.

Who doesn't love fried food? 
But don't expect your typical Taiwanese popcorn chicken, Cheers presents a unique concept of an XL flattened chicken you can eat like a pizza -- which is pretty much what the rave is about with this new spot in Chinatown. 

So what's the best deep fried dish option? From all fried dishes my friends and I tried, here's how we'd rank them: 
1. Fried Deep Beef (chunks)- This is a winner! Surprisingly better than their chicken! Lightly battered, crispy, yet retaining the juicy and tenderness of the steak. Definitely their #1 to get.
2. Ninja Crispy Chicken (XL) - different concept and also juicy, but not much to distinguish their fried chicken from other places 
3. Fried Giant Squid & Sauteed Calamari - Both good, not too oily or heavy, and fresh. But honestly, I couldn't tell the difference in taste or texture between the two... can you?!

Would I come again & Overall thoughts: Decent food but for the quantity you get and the price you pay, I would only stop by here for a snack with friends vs a sit-down meal (very small space inside, not recommended for large parties) 

Recommendations: Their specialty drinks that come in a chubby large cup is worth a try! If you've been to NYC or LA, it reminds me of the Half and Half cups. 
1. Grapefruit Green Tea - welcome a half cut grapefruit floating in your cup, juice and freshness guaranteed. Sugar level can be adjusted.
Ditto on all the other reviews! Great fun and interesting activity. If you can't find something here to try, well, I just don't know what to tell you.

Here I again.  Broad Street is interesting in this area because of gentrification going on in the area so I'm going to be nice but honest.

There were about ten people behind the counter and it appeared as though I was being ignored for almost minute.  Then Gasselle approached me I guess trying to smile to no avail.  Maybe because I asked if they were still serving breakfast.

I ordered the COMBO Son of Baconator, which has a small drink and drink.  I asked about the bathroom and she said she would buzz me in.  I went back and accidentally went right instead of left and when I looked back for Gasselle she was gone.  Another employee bussed me in, I guess there is a 15 or 30 second delay on the lock.

I came back for my drink and meal and it was setup for 'to go.'  I was not asked if I were eating in or out. I was eating in that day.

The meal was a typical Wendy's meal and could have enjoyed it better with if the workers did not treat you as though it is you who worked for them.
Amazing variety of high-quality, fresh, delicious food. I always bring my out of town friends here.

Reading Terminal Market is a nice spot in Philadelphia to take your family when you just want to get away. I live in Trenton NJ and there is no place like Reading Terminal Market anywhere near here. I love the Terminal but I wish they would expand their walking space because Saturday traffic in the Terminal is bumper to bumper.
There's a lot to choose from at the Market, but to guarantee a 5-star experience, have a Beiler's apple or blueberry fritter.
Sooo many options!!! Not enough seating but would definitely take guests visiting the city here. I'll be back (maybe not on a Saturday)

Food lovers paradise.  We ate at probably 10 stands and everything was great.  You can't miss the caramel pecan cookies and the amish doughnuts in the morning.  Don't come here if you're on a diet, but if you do, the grocery store area has some delicious pressed juices.  All of the vendors seem to love being here, and that fun vibe bounces onto the customers.

I don't usually write reviews on Fast Food restaurants because you've eaten at one...you know the saying!  But it isn't true. I usually eat at this location when I travel down to Philly. The first time I was introduced to ChicFilA. I thought the excellent  service was the norm at all the locations. Well, I was wrong! I traveled to Atlanta and the food AND service was horrible. Eating here today, made me appreciate the wonderful service from the manager to the workers! And the food is very good! Kudos to them!

Reading terminal market is a fun time for philly locals and tourists alike! The prepared food is great and they have a market for locals! They have everything from poultry marts, to world wide cuisine to bakeries!

This was my first time there and I came here with my husband. It is truly a wonderful place for foodies. Hands-down they have everything you could ever dream of. We started off at:

-Tommy diNic's - pulled pork sub with Sharp provolone and broccoli Rabe. One sub sandwich feeds two people. Trust me!

-Beilers Bakery - apple fritters hot out of the oven and made with love. A little too sweet for me. Wasn't our favorite. 

-Termini Brothers - cheese cake - imho, too heavy. Don't waste your $ on this one. 

-Beck's Cajun Cafe - their gumbo was peppery spicy and it's not due to the sausage or anything. Disappointed. 

-Flying Monkey Bakery - Whoopie Pie. This was truly worth the wait! They use real cream.

-Old City Coffee - now that's good to the last drop! Needed a coffee fix and refused to have my coffee anywhere else thanks to my many fellow yelpers advice. 

Will definitely return. I want to try Millers Twist, Molly Malloy's, Famous 4th Street Cookie Co., & my coffee place: Old City Coffee.

WOW! Where to start? First, I've been coming here my whole life and it never lets me down. You want it, they have it. Bakeries, dairies, butchers, specialty grocers, seafood, restaurants...it goes on. You need to just go. There's nothing anyone can say here that will truly prepare you if you've never been. I never go without hitting DiNic's for THE best pork sammie in the world. Bassetts ice cream is always worth a stop. And I'm always sure to get a little something at Termini's bakery. A must see during the holidays. Be sure to take advantage of the $4 parking (with $10 purchase) if you drive.

Super fun place to go just because of all the culture--definitely a Philly thing to do. 

I walk around the whole place about 3-4 times deciding what I finally want to eat because everything looks so good! There's mediterranan, sushi, Chinese, sandwiches, and cheesesteaks, and more! 

It's also a kinda interactive date place..but definitely not a first date!

Cheap, yummy eats!

Amazing place!!! Almost as good as Seattle's pike marketplace. I love all the food I've tried at the market. The place is very clean for a farmers market and smells fantastic! If only I had a bigger stomach, would love to try everything! My favorite was actually the freshly made donuts which came in tons of interesting flavors (including matcha cream and bacon).
