This is the Mecca of good food.  You can find any and everything you want to eat here.  I fell in love with the doughnut shop and the grilled cheese boothes.  Glad they had other craft items like specialty olive oils and beef jerky.

fun atmosphere at this market

can be quite expensive, but it is part of the experience

a must visit in the city of brotherly love

Awesome selection of delicious foods. One of my faves is the chocolate dipped cookie at the Famous 4th Street Cookie Company! And there's farm fresh produce at Iovine Brothers (they give student discounts on select days too).

Super pleased with my first time at The Industry. Ambience is great for intimate tables or group setting. The bar has tvs. There's something for everyone! 

Came on a Friday night and we got a table easily. Their specials all looked incredible. The menu was diverse. 

Mussels: if you like them, get them. Nice flavors and they pair well with the great beer selection. 

I got the fish blt. They fish itself changes based on catch of the day. I had a whitefish (can't remember which) that was tasty. The bread holds up well and it's a huge serving. Fries are perfectly cooked. 

My boyfriend got the wings and he seemed very happy. I didn't taste them but he's picky and didn't complain.

This place has great food, service and clean. I will have to go back and rerate all of my other fast-food joints. All hands down to this location. Real chicken in my book is way better then those other places. lol. Love the number 4.

The staff here brings you - your food after your order has been taken. World class service. Love-it.

Went to the movies and searched for a spot nearby since i was famished.  the place has great simple ambiance.  the food came out quick.  i ordered the veggie dish of day (brussel sprouts) & their cliffs of insanity cocktail (its a gin cocktail--i dont like gin but it sounded great so i decided id give it a try).  loved the cocktail.  its refreshing w a citrusy finish.  sprouts were good although they left me with a desire for balsamic vinegar...??  i followed the sprouts w an order of the quinoa salad. yum.  and i had the mac n cheese croqs...just because.  everything came out fast and it was all delish.
Yum. So much food here, I cried a little on the inside. Some things worth getting. The Rotisserie chicken wings and the donuts. You will definitely leave happy after eating here.

This was a fantastic place to start our morning touring Philly. It was great since we were in a group and there something for everybody. Excellent food, cheeses, spices and an eclectic of people and products.

This is a food MECCA. Just go. Go lots of times! Try the butter cake at the Flying Monkey! Beck's Creole Cafe gives samples of their deliciousness, and don't miss Beiler's - the Deli and the donuts are a must.

This is another one of Man v Food's spots so while visiting a friend up in Philly, we made it a point to come here to try DiNic's famous roast pork sandwich.  Unfortunately, the line was so dang long that we skipped it and figured that we'd save DiNic's for another visit.

Other than our failed attempt at getting a roast pork sandwich, Reading Terminal is great, although very overwhelming with the amount of people, businesses and food choices.  

Here are some of the spots that I stopped and purchased food at:

L. Halteman Family - great jams especially the blackberry and strawberry flavors; the wildflower honey went especially quick upon bringing it home

AJ Pickle and Patch Salad - they have the biggest pickles I have ever seen; 1 for $1

Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe - I could have gone crazy in this store, what with my sweet tooth but just bought dark chocolate covered espresso beans.

Fat Fish Sandwiches - With such inventive names such as "Fat Cajun, Fat Buffalo, Fat Pig, Fat Boy, and Fat Dan" I just ordered the soft shell crab sandwich.  I love soft shell crab, however, it was just tasted too fishy for me.

Lancaster County Dairy and Juices - Great fresh Strawberry Lemonade

Miller's Twist Pretzels and More - Get a fresh pretzel once it comes out of the oven...so soft and buttery

Old City Coffee - They roast their beans on-site.  Pretty good ice coffee.

Kauffman's Lancaster County Produce: sold interesting dehydrated vegetables such as okra and beets (recommended by MacRae O.)  I did buy it because I love both of those vegetable but in dehydration form, is a another story.  I ended up sending it to my dad who enjoyed it more than I ever would.  

Before I left, I ended my food gorging with a cookie to go along with my ice coffee.  I don't remember the name of the shop but you can't miss it as it's near one of the entrances.

Oh Holy hell, I was SO excited to find this place! more reviews of what's inside to come, but just the variety of what's available inside is enough to keep going back! Plenty of seating, great food and other stuff to peruse/buy, and bathrooms close at hand if you happen to be there for too long, as we were. If I were a local, I'd be there every day for breakfast. As we're only here for three days, it will just have to be three days in a row.

Is this foodie heaven?  So many choices here, that it is an indecisive persons nightmare.  Comparable to an amusement park where you line up to wait to get on the ride, the ride here being the food.  I had to try 2 spots in here on my first visit, and that was Beiler's donuts and DiNic's pork sandwich.  

Can't wait to come back and try more things.
everything there is amazing . its the heart of south phillys melting pot.
I'm not sure how I can sum up Reading Terminal in a review, but to keep it simple here you go: reading Terminal is Philly in a nutshell. Really. There is something for everyone
Consistently good food, but very crowded around peak meal times. Discounted parking in the garage next door with a ticket validated at the market.

I saw their advertised XL taiwanese chicken cutlet inside their window and I had to try it. 

Came in and learned that this place is a famous chain in asia and other parts of the world.

Food:
Their taiwanese chicken is crispy, juicy , and very well seasoned. Very similar to what I've had in taiwanese places in Asia which brings me back so thats a +. You also have an option to get sides with it like their rice & minced meat which is very hard to find for this kind of food. My group also tried their fried giant squid which was also really good. If you want fried food that has Taiwanese influence then try this place.

If variety is the spice of life, Reading Terminal has got to be the Mecca, at least in Philadelphia. Delicious eats from tons of places. In this humble reviewer's opinion it starts and ends with DiNic's delicious Roast Pork - worth the wait!

Fun, vibrant energy. It is just that people are so pushy and rude walking right through out in the crowded walkways between the vendors. I wish it was a little more spread out. Feels crammed but the food options are diverse and delicious.

I live three blocks from Industry.  It's become a go-to for grabbing a bite and beers al fresco.  I'm a vegetarian, and their whole grain salad is one of the best things I've had in ages.  They DID have a root vegetable dish that was similarly killer, but it unfortunately disappeared from the menu.  Hopefully that was a seasonal move, and it'll return in the fall.  A girl can dream.

The service is fine, but like a few others have mentioned, a bit chilly.  And my only negative experience at Industry was unfortunately a memorable one: 

A friend and I ordered s'mores as dessert.  Now I'm not a foodie, so I can't describe this well, but you know how marshmallows are held to the flame?  The propane or whatever had obviously overly penetrated the marshmallows, which tasted like I was swallowing gas.  Don't get me wrong: I "get" the taste they were after.  This wasn't it. 

When we mentioned this to the waiter (who'd been great to this point), he insisted it was the taste the kitchen was after.  We were like, "Please, if you dare, feel free to taste it if you don't believe us.  It's not right."  He declined our offer...but when he returned later, said he'd tasted it in the kitchen, and thought we were "crazy."

My dining partner is a psychologist.  "Crazy" didn't sit well with her, to say the least.

However, it was an isolated incident, and I like Industry's ambiance, beer list, and menu to let it deter me from returning.  That said, I wouldn't mind a friendlier staff.

Good food and lots of selections.

This is where you want to be if you can't decide on what to eat. There is an impressive variety of food sold here and it is almost impossible to not find something you want. The only minor problem with this market is its popularity and the lack of tables during meal time. Parking near here can also get very expensive ($30+). Everything we tried here was good to excellent. Highly recommend!

The market is a great place for a quick bite to eat, purchase groceries, or shop for specialty items ranging from soaps to baked goods to cookbooks.  There is a lot of variety, so it's pretty easy to find something for everyone.  Just be mindful about the days and times you want to go.  The market can be overwhelmingly crowded on the weekend.  So unless you want to fight the crowds, I would try to go during the week.
Fresh produce.  Fresh fish.  Coffee.  Desserts.  Steak sandwiches.  Teas.  Knick-nacks.  A diner.  Under one roof.

Lots of great vendors to grab food or shop around from. Try the pastrami sandwiches.

Good enough for me to come back again and sometimes crave.

This is a great place to go if you are with a group that is hungry, but everyone wants something different. Tons of tasty food options to pick from and a few boutique shops to peruse. Great people watching too!
Loved the location and the staff was very nice! Great brunch menu and prices are very reasonable.  I'll be back for the blueberry pancakes!
Great time,  food was good,  lots of beer choices,  a/c wasn't working the best was hot inside.  The buffalo chicken meatballs are awesome !
Awesome place, ive only been here once but i must say i loved it! Great food, nice people and lots of things to try....the only thing that sucks is how crowded it is!

This place is way too crowded. The food is good but not great, I don't get why it's so crowded all the time. There are many other places in Philly that have better food than places in Reading.    Come here if you have nothing else to do but this place is not worth is if you are on a busy agenda.

You should eat the dumplings fresh when it's hot.
It's full of flavor but I kinda wished that look different where you can differentiate them if you buy the combo. I brought one of each of all the fried dumpling balls that they had.

I only like the Asian pork and the spinach one.

When I think of Philadelphia I instantly think two things. Philly Cheesesteaks, of course, and Reading Terminal Market.

This Market really has some wonderful food merchants. And it was absolutely fantastic how close it was to our hotel!!! It was actually creepy how close it was...like not even 1/10 of a mile!


Though I didn't make it to every spot I had on my list to try, I did try out quite a few.
I first had a mixed single cup of cinnamon and dark chocolate ice cream from Bassetts. Creamy!
We then went to Chocolate by Mueller for chocolate peanut butter pretzels. Yum.
Next, I bought an anise biscotti and a chocolate chip cannoli from Termini Bros. Insane.
And our last stop was The Famous 4th St Cookie Company where we got their chocolate macadamia nut, double chocolate chip, and oatmeal raisin cookies. OMG.


Next on my list for Reading Terminal is a roast pork sandwich from Tommy DiNic's. I'm also hoping to go there between a Tuesday-Saturday, so that I can experience some of the Pennsylvania Dutch Vendors (amish...) like the Dutch Eating Place, Miller's Twist...

LOVE Reading Terminal!!!
love this market great food vendors love the donuts there best ever from the mennonites from lancaster county rocks, the new orleans restraunt rocks too love this place clean too

This is a staple place to bring out of towners for lunch or simply grab something when you can't make up your mind and need a lot of choices. Best days to go are when the Amish are there for more variety. It's really a unique place where everyone can find something, whether it's indulging in a cheesesteak, some Asian food or finding healthy choices like salads and sushi. My personal favorite is Diener's chicken wings. Rotisserie, flavored goodness that is not greasy and never disappoints.
The best spot to go in Philly for any number of cuisines, desserts, and groceries. I'd be lost without this place.
GO. Eat. Repeat. Buy stuff to take home. Eat. Repeat. Food the way it was when this world was young; fresh, vibrant & diverse.
We love the Reading Terminal!!  We had a great experience shopping and a super lunch at Molly Molloy's.  Always fresh and yummy
Fun to visit, tons of food, some of it not as cheap as I expected, but still very affordable. Not always easy to get a table. Great to just walk around and see everything.

Theres such a large variety inside. You have more than enough options for food, beverage, and miscellaneous. I normally go for food and/or beverage and have not been disappointed yet. This is a must go to.
So many selections! So much yummy food to try. Always a good choice if you wanna pick up a sandwich or a snack or something exotic.

There's a reason the paper guide for the market marks the seating areas with an icon of a pig. You will not leave here without eating like one.  You will not leave here without feeling like one.  Carnivores and vegetarians alike.  

You don't eat meat, you come to Philly and you want to experience the classic Cheesesteak? No problem! Head over to Carmen's Famous Cheesesteaks and get in line! Vegetarian cheesesteak is on the menu and seitan is the steak! I got mine with provolone, sweet peppers and onions and if that's what a Philly Cheesesteak is close to tasting like - then no wonder it's such a "thing" here.  It was pretty damn tasty.  

The bf had a pastrami from Hershel's East Side Deli and simultaneously wished he had room for the pulled pork from DiNic's right next door.  Next time.

I've also eaten at the Dutch Eating Place and loved the whole Pennsylvania Dutch vibe that I missed from when I visited Lancaster a few years back.  Just note: not much to choose from if you're a vegetarian.  Also, their famous apple dumplings were sold out on my last visit.  Boo!

Four Seasons Juice and Smoothies Bar is AMAZING.  The ladies are so clean about everything and the menu changes somewhat seasonally.  They have the best looking wheatgrass, too!  A must after indulging too much, leaving and walking around, then coming back for a nice tall fresh squeezed juice or smoothie.

Don't leave here without having a donut (or 3) from Beiler's Donuts....my personal favorites are the fritters.  Apple or blueberry.  Blueberry fritters, people! But the plain, sour cream or glazed are also good.  Everything else is too cloying with the goopy creams all over them.   Long line? No worries.  It moves really fast.

This was my third time here and I have ruined all my other plans for eating in the city by coming here first.  So.... Vedge, Blackbird Pizza, Dottie's Donuts, V Street, Mama's Vegetarian....please wait for me next time I'm in Philly.  I swear I won't go to the Reading so that I have room to visit all of you :)

Sometimes food takes me to a happy place and their food did just that. I went for a quick lunch at work and will definitely be going back. I ordered the veggie kati roll and added egg.  This place is close to Jefferson but just a bit further than some of the other restaurants so I somehow hadn't made it there until now. Trust me, it is worth the walk!

I feel bad, I really do, giving an average rating just because of how crowded it is. It means it must be popular! Still, it was crowded to the point of frustration.

The lines seemed to stretch forever. And even when you got food (or if), there was barely any room to sit down and eat. The place overall felt dirty and shabby. I expected something like I saw at Chelsea Market in New York, but this was disappointing.

I did find a nice lotion/soap stall that sold me a chai spiced chapstick though :)

Absolutely love reading terminal! It's one of the greatest spots in Philly! The meat vendors are great, as are the cheese vendors. Check out flying monkey for a delicious woopie pie. This place is a must see if you're visiting.

Reading Terminal Market is an amazing destination in Philly.  There are tons of vendors, something for everyone.

Be prepared for crowds.  

A place to return again, and again, and again.  Definitely a must-see location if visiting the convention center, or Center City Philadelphia.

It's best to go on off days/times, but this place is great. They have pretty much anything you could want and can provide a day's entertainment when you don't know what else to do.  We tend to go once every week or two to pick up produce and to wander around the stalls to see if anything catches our eye (honey?  fresh juice in interesting combinations? any type of food imaginable? spices? really, everything).  Just be ready to push your way through crowds and you'll be fine :)

Such a great place to visit!

Like the Ferry Building in San Francisco and North Market in Columbus, OH, this is a place where you can get everything from fresh fruits and vegetables, to varieties of prepared foods and baked goods.  I really have a huge respect for places like these since they showcase some great options that are usually from local farmers and vendors.  One thing that's really unique is that this place is so big...there's so much to see that it really does make for an awesome visiting experience.

Some of the best items at Reading Terminal are Beiler's Bakery and Bassett's Ice Cream.  There are a ton of other prepared foods I'd love to try, but didn't get to...I guess that's just another reason to come back!

Beck's Cajun Café: 
* Bourbon St. Breakfast is red beans & rice, fried egg, cheese, and grilled corn bread. This is a working man's breakfast providing you with the carbs and protein to get you through the morning until lunch. The sausage and eggs were just the perfect breakfast and the rest just reminded me of New Orleans. Rating: 5/5
* Breakfast Po Boy is a French baguette with choice of fried eggs, melted cheese, andouille sausage, turkey sausage, or ham. These were the perfect sandwiches with just the right amount of bread to fillings. The turkey sausage had a light texture but flavorful. The Andouille sausage reminded me of a Hawaiian Portuguese sausage and eggs breakfast. I was in heaven! Rating: 5/5
* Beignets (served on Sundays and Wednesdays) are French doughnuts/fritters served hot and topped with confectioners' sugar. Beck's makes the most authentic beignets outside of Louisiana. They have a beautiful golden brown crust and just the right consistency inside, not too dense and not too fluffy. If you've eaten beignets at Café du Monde in New Orleans, you will absolutely love these! Rating: 5/5
* Chicken and Andouille Gumbo is something my mom had to try. She loves gumbo and is certain this gumbo was made with love. The color is dark with the vegetables cooked down to their essence to flavor the gumbo base. The chicken and sausage add the meaty texture and flavor to the mix. Rating: 4.5/5
* The Alligator Sausage Po Boy is topped with caramelized onion, peppers, and creole mustard. The alligator sausage is mild and lends itself well to the sweet flavor of the peppers and onions and the robust creole mustard. Rating: 4.5/5
* Fried Oyster Platter is served with corn bread and choice of red beans & rice, white rice, or Cajun fries. The oysters were meaty and fried to a perfect golden brown with crispy outside and slightly briny and creamy on the inside. The red beans & rice was fantastic with nice pieces of sausage. Rating: 5/5
* Muffaletta is salami, ham, mortadella, sharp provolone, and olive salad served on Italian bread. My husband and I used to make this sandwich every day at Café Orleans in Disneyland. Beck's version was much better as there is more meat and cheese and they sandwich the olive salad between the meats which keeps the bread from getting soggy. We took these with us to the airport to enjoy before our return flight. The flavors of the different meats is just amazing and the olive salad had just the right amount of acidity to bring the sandwich together. The bread was very rustic with crunchy outside and tender yet chewy inside. Rating: 5/5

Beiler's Bakery: 
* Apple Snitz Fry Pie is reminiscent of the Hostess handheld pies but tastes more homemade with a buttery crust and slow-cooked apple pie filling. They only make them on certain days so if you see them, buy a bunch. We missed our chance to load up before we headed back home. Rating: 5/5
* Chocolate Whoopie Pie looks like a mini flying saucer with chocolate cake on the outside with frosting in the middle. The chocolate cake was marvelous with rich chocolate flavor and soft, spongy texture. The frosting in the middle was fluffy, creamy, and not overly sweet. They were so good, we brought a dozen home with us. Rating: 5/5

Salumeria: They had beautiful French pates, cheeses, and meats. We picked up some imported prosciutto, capicola, Swiss, and provolone to make picnic sandwiches in the hotel room for lunch. The prosciutto had a grassy essence blended with the aroma of aged cheese. The closest taste and texture comparison upon eating some is that it's like butter with a salty porkiness and almost obscene. Unfortunately, my work day had not yet ended or I would have enjoyed a glass of Rosé to complete the food experience. Rating: 5/5

Dutch Eating Place is a diner of sorts serving breakfast and lunch next to Beiler's Bakery. Since seeing Andrew Zimmern making and tasting scrapple, I had to have some. Dutch Eating Place served a Scrapple and Egg breakfast. I was so excited to finally try it and it was wonderful! If you like pork and liver, you'll love this. It is pork scraps mixed with cornmeal, wheat flour, and spices, like a savory pork cake. It fries up really well with a crispy outside and almost pate-like texture inside. Every meat vendor in Reading Terminal Market sold variations with pork, beef, and even turkey. Again, I wish I had a refrigerator in my room so I could have brought some back with us. Rating: 5/5

Miller's Twist serves up hand-rolled Amish-style hot buttered pretzels. Man vs. Food's Adam Richman stopped by during his visit of Reading Terminal Market. You can watch as they roll and artfully twist pretzels. They also wind these beautiful pretzels around full size and mini hot dogs. The pretzel is golden brown with a beautiful glaze on the outside. The interior is chewy and works well with the hot dog. The mini dogs are two-biter and perfect to share as a snack. Rating: 5/5

READING TERMINAL MARKET IS A MUST!!! My first time in philly I was eager to go to the market. When I finally arrived I was pleasantly overwhelmed. They have every kind of food you could imagine. As well as other products. In the two days we were there we went four times. So much good food!!
I love this place.  We came bye after lunch and hit up the bakery counters.  Bought way to much and ate it all. Look forward to coming back.

Just looking at the take-away menu for this shop made me want to try it. When I finally had the chance to stop in, unfortunately i wasn't very hungry so i didn't try a sandwich. I did however get a salad which was very tasty and quite large. As other reviewers noted, the location is tricky. It's not easily noticed just driving around, in fact we had to call to ask where they were. A sign closer to the main shopping center directing people would be likely to draw more business to them. The inside is large and comfy, definitely better then subway or quiznos. staff was friendly. oh and they have 'my little ponies' behind the counter :-) Another yea for smaller businesses!

Love this place ! Great food shopping and restaurant ! Its right in the middle of Philly. Theres certain things in philly that are musts to do. The zoo , the museums , Penn's landing, and the Reading terminal market ! Weve always had great food there. The cheesesteaks are so delicious. Awesome !
Amazing place. The people are kind and the food is amazing. Their mint lemonade is amazing as well, had a great time here with my sister after a day or work.

The fried squid is really good for a decent price. Their lime black tea is also really good and the size of their drinks for the price can't be beat. They also have a grapefruit green tea which is also great and it has half of an actual grapefruit inside! The workers are very friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend this place if you're looking to try Taiwanese inspired foods such as their fried chicken, fried squid or just for a drink!

Love love love this place. I'm totally obsessed with their kathi rolls. Reasonable prices and fast service. Their lamb roll is a must have. They're open very late on Friday and Saturday nights so it's the perfect post bar meal. Their chutneys are very nice too and perfectly compliment the rolls.
Definitely a place I want to avoid around any holiday or on the weekend BUT it serves a purpose and I'll always go back for the donuts and falafel!

Wow. Wow. Wow. I am not from the area but I would sooooooo love to have this in my hometown. I would probably visit everyday and be the size of a house. Talk about variety - it is here. If you are from out of town you must visit. Choose from candy, crepes, pretzels, seafood, fresh produce, meat sandwiches and aoooooo much more. There were so many places to choice from. I would definitely return!!

I was in Philly for a wedding. I went to Chinatown, and it was...Chinatown.  The food sucked.  Why would any Asian want to go there?  I thought I would be stuck without anywhere to go or do.   Then the recommendation for the Reading Terminal started coming in.  Boy am I glad they did.  This place was awesome.  Food everywhere!!  After going to Pat's several years ago, I swore that I would never buy another one.  I kept to my word.  I had the leftovers of what my wife couldn't finish.  It was so good!  I got into the longest line that I could find, and later found out that I was standing in the line at DiNic's.  I got their famous pork sandwich, and it was good.  The wife also gave me some of her leftover shrimp Po boy sandwich.  Awesome place.  Too bad, I will probably never go to Philly again.

Love this place, my only complaint is that I wish they had more maps because it's easy to get lost .. also I find myself buying produce then walking around and finding a better place 10 minutes later! Still what a great space though.. if you can find parking!

I swear, if I lived in Philadelphia, I could eat here every day and never get bored.  I wish Washington, DC had something similar to this place.  It's location, in proximity to the hotel we were staying at, was perfect!  

Tip:  The Down Home diner was very good later in the evening, once the Terminal closed.
A conglomerate of all foods from all cultures. If you are a foodie, you can't visit Philly and not come to Reading Terminal.

This place is a little too overwhelming for me. I'm like an ADHD kid in 3rd grade when I come in here. I can't make an actual choice on what or where to eat. I just can't. 

You need to either have a solid plan on what you want to eat or plan on being here for a couple hours to really check the entire place out. 

We found street parking right down the block.
Really fun place to stroll around, grab a great lunch and some nice produce.
Awesome food! Hayride! Vodka cocktail. Great time!! Came back with lots of bags lol!!
I love going to The Reading Terminal anytime I go to Philly. You have so many food and produce options that it's worth it. Highly recommend

Fun stop for lunch. Hop off the bus here. We, two people, ate at 4 different places consuming a Philly cheese steak (we got the wrong order but somehow it was still OK), a savory crepe, fresh squeezed juice and ice cream. Lunch was great! I think that even locals like choosing this place for the lunch but do be aware that there's nowhere without a 15 minutes line. I mean the lines move but still you're going to be in the line for a while. It's a great place to sample some real Philadelphia food.

The market is amazing and jam packed with diverse offerings of food and goods of all kinds. I loved it and the only reason I didn't mark it a 5 star was that it was hot as Hades in there!!! I imagine it would be a difficult to cool, but I found it difficult to remain in there long enough to do much shopping. It was like being in hell, but with nice people and cool stuff.
I absolutely adore Reading Terminal Market!
umm what more can you say but WOW!! TOTAL food heaven. Fresh foods, cooked foods from all type of cuisines, a bar, several deli's and cheese shops, bakeries etc. go. just go.

Great spot to go for food! There are many different options for food, along with small shops. Definitely one of the top places to stop by if you're visiting the city. There are also a variety of bars close. Chinatown is also within walking distance.

I really hate giving tourist traps five stars. But I can't resist with Reading Terminal Market. There are just too many good things here that I enjoyed.
 
- I had a delicious beef brisket sandwich with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone at Tommy Dinic's. Damn, that was good.
- Picked up some blue corn popcorn at the Amish store to bring back to my nieces and nephew. They loved it. The instant oatmeal was pretty good, too.
- I'm a sucker for soda, and getting imported Mexican Fanta at Flying Monkey was a treat.
- We also enjoyed a cheesesteak from Spataro's (I'm sure there are a ton of better cheesesteak options in Philly, we just didn't have the time to check 'em out).

People were friendly. The food was good. And the food wasn't too expensive.  Just being in the crowd at lunchtime was a memorable experience.

The Reading Terminal is continuing to disappoint me but for their tasty Gyros, fresh fruits, flowers and more I will continue to give them four hard earned stars.

Minus the annoyance of tourists and gatherings of people on jury duty the terminal can be a fund place to go. The open area seating surrounded by the old man playing the piano is enough to brighten anyone's day..that is until you get to the lines of minions gorging themselves on one of Rick's disgusting steaks topped with a thousand calorie ice cream delight. It's no wonder Americans are so unhealthy.

I for one like to keep to certain sections of the market myself. For those extra hungry days the Amish diner always hits the spot with their home grown, home cooked meals and for those lighter appetite visits there are two smoothie/juice bars [one being at the Middle Eastern market and the other just around the bend which is always run by two very sweet Asian girls]. 

There are several places to get those veggie-vitamins, but the organic market is the best place to find local and pesticide-free fruits and veggies as well as meats and some really great cheeses; Blue Mountain vineyards has a store where you can bring your lunch and enjoy a by-the-glass wine; and there are even some florists and artisans selling merchandise at small carts and inside little stores. There really is something for everyone...just don't expect to be able to actually sit and enjoy it because you might just be disappointed.

Before I even get to the food I must say that this is a very interesting place to visit. Not only is there a smorgasbord of places to eat, but there are groceries and markets. You can get burgers, German food, Chinese food, Amish donuts and more. If you want variety in your food shopping this is a fun place to go.

I will say that this market can get uncomfortably crowded-especially on weekends. the hallways barely have enough space for all of the people trying to buy items and people shove into you. I would recommend going on a weekday or making your way over early.

I have yet to try all that they offer since it is much! The Amish donuts are excellent. Sometimes they come out tasting a bit like old fryer oil, but they are usually quite good. They offer an interesting and fun variety of flavors like creme brulee. 

The burger place in the main seating area is quite good as well. The fries are cooked and seasoned well. They make a thinner style burger patty that is juicy and also seasoned well. My husband and I din't have to wait long!

There is a large bakery area with excellent and reasonably priced bread. I decided to give their cupcakes a go. My husband and I shared basic vanilla and chocolate cupcakes. They were not very good and I wouldn't recommend them. They mainly tasted like shortening with a vague flavor of anything else, but were very dry. The bread items and chocolate are quite good however.

The groceries and the meat markets are good quality and local. The prices are decent and they serve the throngs of customers fairly quickly.

Next time I have to try a BBQ duck or a roast beef sandwich! There are so many new things to try in that one space.
Great food, great variety. Don't go during rush times, and there are so many good vendors, I've never found it was worth standing in those with the longest lines. s

Cool decor, good beer. Porchetta sandwich was not terrible, but pretty dry. The burger went over well, as did the BBQ duck sandwich. The french fries were good and crispy. Only complaint was the service, which was pretty slow. At times it seemed like we'd been completely forgotten, which was especially irritating considering we were one of perhaps three tables in the whole place for the entire time we were in there.

I love the "Ok Produce" market here at reading terminal. I make the trip every single weekend just to go there. I can spend $10-$15 there and come back with enough produce, Fresh fruits and vegetables to last me for WEEKS. It would cost me 3X that much at the grocery store. Plus the people are super friendly. 

The other places in the terminal are great too. Awesome bakery shops and candy shops, excellent ice cream shops plus the Amish are there on certain days and they have the BEST goods and products. Overall, i love coming here with any out of towers and they also leave feeling satisfied.

How can you not give this place 5 stars?! This a MUST place to visit and walk around in when visiting Philly. They have a ton of food venders, deli's and little markets. When I first walked in, I felt a little overwhelmed with everything there is to see. I could not get over all of the fresh meats, cheeses, and seafood there was to buy. Wowza! I would come here to do my shopping for sure...my time would be spent at the deli with the many amounts and flavors of just the bacon and sausages alone. It's a meat and cheese heaven. 
The food venders have everything fresh including your sweets. There is a bar/restaurant towards the back to grab a refreshing beverage. Your only problem in this place will be which shop to stop at for lunch.
One should see this market. It has lots of options for tasty eats. Be prepared for crowded space. Other shops besides food, but mostly a food oriented place.

Masala kitchen popped up out of nowhere! My friend and I were in search of a quick but healthy meal after catching Don Juan by the Philadelphia ballet at the Academy of Music. This place had fresh new Lassi's - try the lavender, it's delish. Their lamb kebab roll was great and we got a trial of the chicken masala roll which is their specialty- a must order if you go. Bon appetite!

Resurrection of the ghost of Pizzeria Beddia.  Guys who run it are super friendly and accommodating (we screwed up the order process online and they said no problem, we'll fix you a pie) and the pizza is top notch, essentially an homage if not the replica of Beddia's masterpiece pizza.  So happy that it is here.  Soon to be my go to take out pie.

Hands down my FAVORITE PLACE IN PHILLY!!!!! Had the chance to experience the market during the AACC Clinical Lab Expo and I'm OBSESSED. Returned severally times over 2 days and it was worth every visit. DeNics is a MUST for the roast pork sandwich with broc rabe and provolone. I'm bringing some sandwiches back to Jersey tonight!

I spent many saturdays walking here with my folks to shop and eat breakfast...  I still go every time I'm in Philthy to gets my grub on.

Harry Ochs - Best Butcher in the world

Amish Breakfasts - Ummm scrapple and pancakes

Amish sticky buns - No raisins please, get these at the Amish bakery or at the breakfast stand.  Hands down best baked good in the world - Tartine's morning buns are a distant second

DeNic's - My favorite sammie in the galaxy is the roast pork, all garlicy and nice - with aged provolone and peppers

Birch Beer - Homebrew from the Amish, sweet!

Just about anything at Delilahs...

Down Home Diner and Jack McDavid - Because you made fun of Bobby Flay years before it became fashionable!  

And all the rest of youse there....
Grilled cheese stand and diniks pork is awesome. Also go to where they sell the donuts, the ones with the m and m's are the best

This was right across from our hotel which I thought was cool. It is fairly large compared to most markets in the south. It is definitely a hipster and tourist filled blob. I'm guessing it's almost always busy? Lot of cool vendors/food stalls. I would probably go back if it wasn't super crazy-maybe during a weekday? Definitely a place to visit and buy some cutesy little things.

This is a really neat place. I'd heard about it before coming to Philadelphia for a conference so I was excited to check it out. It can be a little overwhelming as there's A LOT of options and people. I recommend doing a lap around all of it before deciding what you want.

There's several little eateries to get juices, sandwiches, a hot and cold food bar, a coffee shop, bakeries, fresh meat and seafood, a philly cheesesteak spot, a diner, an oyster bar, a cajun spot, a greek one and several others!

Definitely check it out if you're nearby! Didn't have a lot of spots open to sit and eat so we brought our food back to the hotel.

With 799 reviews already, does the Yelp world really need an 800th review of Reading Terminal Market? Sorry, but I couldn't resist.

There's so much going on in here, so block out a couple of hours of your day to explore up and down the numerous aisles of assorted goods. Word of advice: if you don't want to eat here, don't show up hungry. Not one bit! You'll never make it. There are too many vendors selling everything from fruits and vegetables, to chocolate and cookies, to meat and beer. Notice how it just gets better and better? And that doesn't even include the actual, sit-down sandwich and food places.

If you work your way through the entire market maze and found you haven't purchased a thing, even to take home, then you're a liar. That's also impossible. So just accept it, have fun, people watch and leave with a lighter wallet. Don't worry, everybody's doing it.
Cute market in the heart of Philadelphia, but didn't see anything special there that I haven't found in other cities.

LOVE PEARLS OYSTER BAR. I've had breakfast and the seafood dishes and what a delight. This counter spot on the 12th Street side of the terminal is putting out dishes that not only look like fine dining but taste just as delicious! If there is such a thing as fine dining breakfast, it's here too!

Love this market! Definitely check out the RAW milk!!! And also the grilled cheese place :) 
I do wish there were more organic options, but it's a really fun place to look around, and great food!

Whoa, had no idea this place was here and randomly stumbled upon it today. So glad I did! One of the employees came over and was just crazy positive and upbeat. Walked me through how it works and got me started. They had a ton of staff so there were plenty of people to help along the way. Each person who got my tray at each individual station greeted me by name and seemed genuinely happy to be helping me. That's really refreshing and not the norm on this campus. My build your own bowl was delicious and I'll definitely be back!

The only problem with this place is that you can never make a legitimate choice on where to eat in a decent time frame. Too many places! It's too much to take in at one time! Also the place is rather small and get's crowded easily. I wouldn't go there during any event at the Convention Center because that's where everyone goes to eat.

Definitely a must when in Center City!! The food is amazing!  Atmosphere is one if a kind!  A few of our favorites are: Bassett's Ice Cream, the Tubby Olive, Spataro's-Cheesesteaks, Olympia Gryo, & Beiler's Bakery. Go there hungry...you will not be disappointed!!

What a zoo!  But I loved it!  Mostly... I wish we had had a chance to spend more time there because we came around lunchtime and there were hordes of people everywhere.  It would have been nice to check it out when it wasn't so crazy.  Similar to the Chicago French Market (on claustrophobia-inducing steroids), there were a variety of stalls with miscellaneous tantalizing food options.

We of course had to try the cheesesteaks, which I have to admit were subpar.  Maybe I just don't understand the Philly way, but I have had significantly better sandwiches called a cheesesteak outside of Philadelphia.  And the workers at the stall were about as friendly as robots... who hate you.  But that's okay, it's just a sandwich.  

Because it was lunchtime it was almost impossible to find a seat, but we finally found a table squashed uncomfortably between two other tables.  The whole place also could use a good scrubbing.

My biggest regret is not indulging in the drool worthy desserts at the Flying Monkey Bakery, but at least now I have a good reason to go back!

I heart Reading Terminal, it's my home away from home. It's hands down my favorite place in Philly! I'm here pretty much once a week to get my produce. Just walking around & people watching makes me happy!
I'm partial to the produce but they also have great food! (Thai, Deli, Veggie options etc) When I'm in the mood for some really good bread I go right to Metropolitan Bakery. Pretty much everything you need is right here.

Great place to grab a bite to eat late at night. They are open until like 3 on weekends. They have various kati rolls and rice platters. I have tried the chicken and rice, chicken biryani (very good), chicken tikka roll, chicken masala roll, aloo roll, and chicken kheema roll. I like the aloo roll (potato filled kati roll) and chicken kheema roll (ground chicken in spices) the best. You can help yourself to the white sauce and hot sauce dispensers. I have also tried a sample of the rose lassi. I liked it as it tasted kind of like go-gurt. I will be back.
One of the best historical food market on earth . You will find most amazing shops, every type of food. They have shops like 150 years old ..

In short, this market is incredible! There are dozens, many dozens in fact, of independently owned stalls which feature organic produce, baked goods, artisan cheesees, freshly cut meat, handmade onsite ice cream (Bassetts), gourmet chocolates (Chocolates by Mueller- superb!), even used books and candle/home decor items, but primarily it is a food based market. Come for breakfast or lunch and partake of the many purveyors of prepared foods scattered throughout the market, then plop down at a central seating area and enjoy the bounty of a truly extraordinary market!
it's a fun place. we have this type of market in nyc so only 3 stars.

Jose Andres is a culinary legend and this is a great idea!! However, I would've liked to see more cooked items on the menu to showcase the talents of a Jose Andres trained Chef...the salads are fresh and delicious hence the 4 stars but the chicken sausage is one of the few items that is actually cooked. I was thinking maybe they could add a meatless stir fry, caponata or even some veggie meatballs to the menu to show off a Jose Andres trained Chef...the price is good too because my huge salad was only 8.49 and the customer service was excellent
Had the Asian Chicken Salad which was very yummy. Everyone else at our table enjoyed their meals too. Good beer selection. Nice atmosphere. Would recommend for a casual lunch or dinner.

This place is amazing!! So many different food options! Everything I have tried here was delicious I love all the little different stands they had and a very cool place as it used to be an old train terminal
An amazing place to explore! Super yummy food and fresh produce :) Kinda expensive, but worth it.

We got the Longanisa dog, lumpia and calamansi juice. As American born Filipina, I felt LALO did a great job at creating dishes that were true to the Philippines, but also mindful of those who are less familiar with Philippine food. I felt like I was brought back to one of my big family parties with the lumpia and back home to moms kitchen with the longanisa, garlic rice, and egg. Truly tasted like a slice of home. Thank you so much
Great place. Lots of interesting vendors and food. A bit tough to find seating place, so grab one when you can.

No Big surprise here. I love it as much as others. I strolled in after having lunch in Chinatown. That didn't stop me from eating so much more here. I had the roast pork sandwhich from dinics with sharp provolone. It's was good. A little dry for my taste but it was good. I think I'm going back to try the pulled pork tomorrow. I then had bassets vanilla ice cream. The best vanilla I have ever had. I then had an all beef pretzel wrapped dog and took a salted pretzel to go. Delicious. I bough a couple of gifts at the Pennsylvania General Store. Decent prices and the chocolate converted prezels will be a pretty neat gift for family. 

I went on a Friday afternoon. Crowded but moving. Vendors are fast. People are nice. A lot to see. Give yourself time to walk through the entire place. This can definitely be a stop for breakfast, lunch and snacking.
Very cool place to go for a variety of food and drinks. Love these types of markets. It gets packed so be sure to expect a lot of people on weekends and better to on a weekday.

this place is heaven on earth , you can literally find everything you need here.
if you love food , you should make it a point to go there.

I love the RTM.  The place is always bustling with buyers, tourists, and vendors.  I particularly like the seafood at Jonny Yi, the sausages and deli meats at the Wurst Haus, and the confections of the Flying Monkey.  Every visit should include excellent coffee, espresso drinks, tea or chai from Olde City Coffee as well.   It's a great place for breakfast at the Down Home Diner, lunch at La Cantina a bowl of noodles from Sangkee Duck House, or of course Breyers Ice Cream.  Go, see, shop, and eat--you'll love it too.

I was surprised to see this place was open late but I was very happy to find it so.  

The menu is simple and inexpensive.  The rolls aren't so large as to be compared to burritos but they don't have to be.  I'd argue they're more flavorful and worthwhile than most burritos I've had.  

I had a chicken tikka and beef masala roll and they're both very different flavors but both were enjoyable nevertheless.  A platter may be better suited if you're looking for a filling meal but I think having two different kinds of rolls gives you the opportunity to experience different tastes.

They happen to have a 10% discount when you check-in on Yelp and they did honor it so that's a little perk to save you a dollar here and there.

There's plenty of seating inside and there's plenty of white sauce to go around if you choose to eat in.

FYI, your clothes may smell of food when you leave, not that it will smell bad though.

Recommendation: Beef masala roll

One of the most magical places I have ever been. Fresh fish counter, meats, sausages etc. as far as your eyes can see. A ton of different food choices from Mexican tacos to ice cream to Indian to donuts and chew steaks. Definitely something for everyone and an awesome experience. Super crowded during the lunch rush but hey that's part of the philly experience!

I'm a HUGE fan- I just don't make it there often because it's in CC and always crowded and I usually cart two small children around with me. 

We stopped by for Dutch Fest 8/9/13 and there was a small petting zoo and pony and buggy rides on Arch and it was a TON of fun for my little guys. There's always great food inside and various wares both Amish and local. 
 
They have some of the best cookies in the area at 4th street bakery and tons of butchers and even a beer garden. 

Since people stop and browse (read: block the foot path) I wouldn't be upset if they took out a row of vendors and made the aisles wider though...;-)

Reading Terminal has some of my favorite places to eat (4th St. Cookies, the turkey sandwhich place, Bassets, Flying Monkey, the Middle Eastern place, etc.) and is something I always recommend to people visiting the city. Definitely worth the visit!

A great market, anything you can think of to eat fresh and tasty. 
 Tom M. In the reviews is a dumb ass just because you turned idiot, I mean vegan sorry I get the two confused you shouldn't 3 star a place because of your stupid thinking.

I like to get my vegetables from Fair Food Farmstand when I have money (they have the freshest tastiest veggie selections and carry specialty vegan items) and when I don't have money I go to Iovine Bros. If you know you're going to use the veggies right away you can go to OK Produce, but ... just be weary and make sure to inspect every inch. I love Flying Monkey bakery, they make some delicious treats when you are feeling bad. Also don't go here on weekends unless it is very early. The tourists will drive you insane. Think; flea market but with food.

Not exactly sure what to add in this 228th review for a Philly foodie mecca, so I'll just add my favorite finds from last week's journey... "Dollar Hollar" at 4th Street Cookies, as they sell the last cookies of the day for $1 each (we scored the last 2 snickerdoodles!); my favorite espresso blend at Old City Coffee; canollis at Termini; choosing between the fresh fish and local poultry.  And $4 parking at the garage across the street if you spend at least $10... and if you can manage to make it through the market without spending $10, you might be the first!
best fired chicken and squids I got. Also huge drink very good and has cheap price . I will be back with my friend and higher recommend everyone for fired stuff.

This Place is in a word... Amazing. Point to a place on a globe and there is probably food from that country. This place is good for grocery shopping, wine/cheese/olive shopping, international gourmet foods, specialty butchers (lamb.turkey, beef, pork, and chicken) and many many restaurants. Its better to come very early on a weekday, it gets PACKED. Most of the places are cash only, there are a couple of ATM's inside. You can park in the parking garage right above the market for 4 hours. A must visit if you come to philly.

An action packed venue with so much to choose from. The pretzels were delicious. Lots of fresh produce, cheeses, meats, seafood to take home and cook. Also a great variety of cuisines to try and explore. Share dishes w others to get the most exposure to the different offerings.
Fun place to go, eat  and shop. Can purchase all kinds of food and treats. They  really cleaned it up from years ago. More bathrooms would be nice.
Remodeled state-of-the-art looking always have good food fresh food good place to go for your lunch good place to go for a late night snack

I've been going to reading terminal since i was a kid. After i moved into the city i found myself going grocery shopping here and meeting with people for coffee and bumble dates! There's so much variety which allows me and my friends to try different things every time. My go to favorite is the metropolitan bakery or the Amish market

Got a delivery done for lunch today. as mentioned in other reviews, this place is the haven for people looking for a healthy and quick bite in philly region. the moment i saw quinoa and gluten free options, i knew i had stumbled upon a place which would have something of my interest. it would be a bit pricey but there is hardly any competition so there is no choice in the matter.

I ordered a bison quinoa hash, caveman quickies - omega 3 blend, breakfast protein pack, devily eggs and curried chicken. 

now it might be just me, but somehow everything was lacking or ridiculously low on salt! the bison quinoa hash had a little salt, decent amount of ground bison, very little quinoa and beans. the devily eggs had no salt.. didn't taste good at all. caveman quickies was good - the kind of snack i would appreciate on a nice hike. curried chicken had no salt too... at first making it difficult to accept the curry flavor with maple syrup amd cranberries, but gradually the tastebuds got used to it. haven't had the breakfast pack yet so nothing on that.

overall this place aligned with my expectation that taste needs to be compromised for healthy eats, and i am fine with that. so will i order from this place again? yes, sure! one of the few places offering healthy food options in Philly, why not?

Food, smells, hustle, bustle,  people and choices.  The terminal market is a home run for the hungry person. From breakfast to dessert it's all here. If you can't find what you want then look for  the ingredients and go home and make it. The Market is popular lunch spot for tourists, shoppers and workings in the city.  It can get very crowded and timing is everything.

A historic treasure! I love that it provides food variety and even fresh groceries you won't get at a supermarket. It's very different from any other place to get food in Philly. Every time I have a visitor, Reading Terminal Market is a must. Try pearls oyster bar breakfast special! Amazing!

Very good plain chicken sandwich. Good coffee.  Breakfast biscuit with egg, sausage and cheese was sorry.  Not sure where the quality control is on these products.  Sandwich was luke warm and the sausage was tough and barely had taste.  Not sure if it was sanitary regarding the holding temperature. I will return for the chicken sandwich.

Reading Terminal Market MIGHT, just might, be as good as it gets. 

On a recent trip to Philadelphia I walked in and spent a good two hours walking around. I had to get a refreshment. The sheer variety of everything--bakeries, flowers, fresh meat, seafood, restaurants, Pennsylvania Dutch merchants, coffee shops, dry goods, groceries, etc etc etc--is pretty mind-blowing. 

I ate at Tommy DiNic's (delicious). I got a slice of marbled cheesecake from Termini Brothers Bakery. I sampled some delicious cheese. There was a delightful old woman playing piano in the center of all the hustle, and I bought a hand-knitted hat from Anastasia, who was from Siberia. Hershels East Side Deli, I'll be back for you. 

If you're a tourist in Philadelphia and especially if you're a foodie tourist in Philadelphia, Reading Terminal Market is a must-visit. Come hungry!

It's like the Italian market on the north side... but better! (sorry south philly)

pros!
1. very good selection of fruit and veggies never a bad apple in the bunch, literally. 
2. cheap, well depends on what you're going for. but even if it's expensive its good quality so worth the price!
3. food is good, quick service. ive eaten at several places and the staff is always friendly and helpful. theyre never impatient if you dont know what you want and always have a smile on their faces.
4. it doesnt feel like Philadelphia in here... its like ive died and gone to polite heaven where it smells like sweet sweet baked goods, organic chocolate milk, fresh cheeses and the floors have been swept!
5. tables outside! i love outdoor seating... 
6. theres a wine and spirits near by... can we say wine and cheese date?

cons...
1. during the weekends its always packed with tourists so if u know where you have to go, get there fast and dodge the little children as safely as possible!
2. during lunch time the tables indoors are always packed! you have to hunt them down and wait patiently, get warm food at your caution.. be prepare to have warm soup.
3. during conventions at the hotel right across the street this can be a hard place to get into.. with everyone standing on the sidewalk with nothing to do... i cant stand people who do this in the city. 
4. their hours.. sometimes i wish they were open later but thats why this place is so wonderful i have to plan to get there on time. and even though its not around the corner from me, i love making the trip down there.
Healthy and much tastier than I expected! Veggies, sandwiches, salads, fruit, and priced not badly for an airport.

It is a fun place to go as a tourist.  But, when I do I cannot help but wonder if the city had a rating system what kind of rating it would get.  It really is pretty damn filthy in there.  The food I have had was only ok.  The best was the pizza.

I'm only giving a 4 just for how crazy busy it is and how hard it is to find a place to sit and eat during the busy times - agree with others that weekday mornings are your best bet if you can make it then. What else can I say? It has everything and in both quantity and quality.

What a delightful gem!!!  My father often took me to Reading Terminal when I was a child. Bassetts ice cream was always a special treat when I was a child - and still is!  The market has morphed from a real "working man's" market to a culinary delight for today's obsession and interest in food with local and fresh ingredients.   We always take visitors to Philly to the market and they always want to go back for more.  Many times we've had visitors say that the Reading Terminal market was the best part of their trip to Philly.  Such an abundance of really great food, fresh flowers, spices, meat, seafood, cheese and a really great cookbook stall.  We are so lucky to have such a great place in Philly.  The atmosphere is exciting, especially when there is a conference in town and the Market is buzzing with people who are in awe of one of our best Philadelphia assets.
Don't forget that market businesses will validate your parking ticket for a drastically reduced cost at specific parking lots.

Let me start off by saying, if you have grown up in the tri state area, or more specifically in south jersey and other philly suburbs and you havent been to the reading terminal market, i must tell you that you are missing out on one of the most classic philly staples that has been or will ever be.   I could go on for days listing the stalls and vendors that need go be hit from fresh fruit and veg to the best bacon and meats in this whole area, but i won't.  I will simply tell you about the one sandwich that actually changed the way in approach my weekends.   

Dinic's stand at the terminal market is one of those spots that you need to know when to hit it.  If you hi at the wrong time, you could be waiting for a bit and your hunger will grow exponentially as you see the roast pork with gravy and beatiful garlicky greens being slathered between the best bread in town.  If you were me, you would be getting there around 10 AM to avoid the craziest traffic and you would be getting the non Roast Pork Sandwich, The Brisket of Beef with long hots which i can say, hands down the best sandwich in this market and prpbly in the top 3 in the entire city including Johns Roast Pork and Paesanos.    

Just go to the reading terminal market, be nice to the vendors and someone will definately validate your parking taking it from 20 to a measly 4 dollars.  Go, explore, and go again, you could never taste and see it all.  I beseech you, go. Its worth the trip.

Recently renovated. This chick fil a is what you would expect from a standard chick fil a. It's got more seating and a modern atmosphere. Food is pretty much straight from the cookbook and taste is just like every other chick fil a. Parking was easy as it's in a popular shopping area.

A must for any foodie visiting Philadelphia or for anyone in general. The market is full of culinary delights, local favorites, every possible grocery ingredient and international bites. It's often very busy and crowded and it's easy to get turned around, but just let go and enjoy. I go town for lunch since I work close by. Or I stop by on my way home to pick up ingredients for dinner.
There's definitely no other place than this! Best balaclava, philly cheese steaks and ice cream around. Easy to get lost in but definitely worth it to experience!!
the best place to shop in philly. the food is fresh i love it

This place is awesome! It has pretty much any kind of food you want. I've been here several times and have come away happy and full each time. Fresh cooked salmon with spinach and rice, pork spareribs with roasted potatoes, delicious baked goods....the list goes on and on. It also has Bassett's ice cream, which I haven't yet had but have been told it's the best ice cream around. I'd definitely make it a point to visit this place if you are ever in Philly.

Great place to take in the Philly culture. Tons of vendors and all sorts of food from which to choose, whether you want to have breakfast, lunch or dinner or take things home for either of those meals.  I have a sweet tooth so am loyal to the Amish bakery for cakes and donuts.  Donuts are made fresh everyday and people line up first thing in the morning.  Also a great Amish luncheonette in that same area which serves hearty/very generous portions for breakfast and lunch at reasonable prices. Another favorite would be Hershel's East Side deli which is in the middle of the marketer.  Very hearty jewish deli classics like matzo ball and chicken noodle soup, latkes, kugel, hot dogs, potato knishes, bagels with lox, New York-style cheesecake, and, of course, hot deli sandwiches stuffed with homemade corned beef, pastrami, or brisket.  My favorite is the reuben!!

I can't seem to get past Beiler's Donuts every time I go to Reading Terminal!!!  A vanilla creme donut is my all time favorite just in general.. but I have to get that and the apple fritter every time I pass Beiler's.  Everyone must try this apple fritter.  Trust me...
Yes.. Reading Terminal is usually crowded with people and could be daunting to those that don't know where they are going.  It seems that everyone around you does!  But have no fear, once you get used to the rush and the 'panic' of people rushing around you to get to where they want to go.. you start to fit right into the traffic patterns like the 'regulars'.
Go to the Dutch Eating Place (line is always is long, but wait isn't that bad), Sweet as Fudge Candy Shop, Hatville Deli for lunch meats and fresh bacon, scrapple, Dienner's BBQ chicken for great rotisserie chicken, 4 seasons Juice Bar  and of course Beiler's. DUH.
I'll get to the rest of Reading terminal at some point! (I've walked it many times.. but always return to that corner of the world for some odd reason!) Will definitely come back to Reading Terminal...

So this was a culinary adventure I wish we could have enjoyed more of. Unfortunately my wife couldn't get out of bed early enough, so we went here on the last day of our venture into Philadelphia.

I was overwhelmed by all the options available, all the different stands, the food, the options. It was overwhelming.

We ended up buying some liquor from a vendor, eating at this Crêpe place, and buying some amazing cookies. I really wish we had spent more time here. This was a most enjoyable stop.

Only complaint really was the parking. Then again we came here on our last day (Sunday morning I believe) so of course it was a little difficult.
if you've never been here, make time! Iconic Philly attraction.

RTM as a whole is a great place and a Philadelphia landmark. If you visit Philly, DEFINITELY stop in here, even if you don't buy anything, it's worth a visit. Be warned though, on weekends it can get extremely crowded. My personal favorites:

- Boneless Rib Sandwich with cheese from The Rib Stand
- Apple fritter (or any donut) from Beiler's (the line moves quickly)
- Cheesesteak Italian style (with sharp provolone, long hots, and broccoli rabe) from Carmen's
- Chicken shawarma from Kamal's

In my opinion, DiNic's is extremely overrated. If you want a better roast pork, try Paesanos, Chick's, John's Roast Pork, or Tony Lukes.

I came here on my latest trip to Philadelphia for breakfast. I did not know what I was getting myself into! I thought that as a market, it was going to be like an indoor farmer's market. I was so happily wrong! While there is an area where fresh produce is sold, there are an assortment of different vendors and restaurants selling just about any type of food product imaginable. While I did select a spot to eat breakfast and get a coffee, it was a very difficult decision to make! I honestly am looking forward to coming back to Philadelphia solely to spend a day in the market and eat. If you are in the city, do not miss this spot!

A must go! A great place to just walk around or get a good meal. We went the first time on a Friday and it was very easy to walk around. We went back on a Sunday and it was very packed but still fun to walk around. We ended up buying some fresh meats to take home with us.

Love this market. I've been to the market in DC and another in Boston but I think Philly has the best variety and down home flava.

The Amish walking around doing their thing is a riot to watch. You just have to wonder what these people are really like.

Secret: Skip the uber-trendy and annoying brunch spots all around philly and go this market. In the back corner is a great Amish diner that has the best hot cakes around! Let me know if you agree!!

As a tourist, I like. It's just the right size without being overwhelming (no, actually, it was overwhelming due to all the meal and dessert choices; definitely arrive on an empty stomach!). Everything is kept clean with accessible, regularly-emptied disposal bins. There is a good mix of vendors providing ready-to-consume food or ingredients to make your own meals at home. Definitely stop by for lunch if you are visiting town!

Show me anywhere else in the US that hosts an annual scrapple fest. Show me a market that has space to spread out tables, build a stage, and host an eclectic crowd of Amish scrapple men, family-owned scrapplers, and a few oddball scrapple enthusiasts wearing scrapple-themed t-shirts.

I'm from New England. We don't eat scrapple there.  On April 21st, I was schooled in scrapple by this crowd of pork-and-cornmeal mush-loving mid-Atlanticals. I watched in wonder as a table of judges assessed the entries in various categories. I tried the turkey scrapple, which I found quite delicious. I did not find the 'wedding cake' made from turkey scrapple to be as appealing.

RTM offers more than just scrapple, of course. For an out-of-towner wanting to eat as many Philly classics in as brief a time as possible, there is no better stop than the market. Don't forget to stop at the Amish pretzel joint - brushed with butter and fresh from the oven, they are a must-eat.

How things change! I remember the Reading Terminal Market in the 1970s, when it was dying a slow death. So very far from the vibrant place it is today, one of the most dynamic urban markets you'll find anywhere.

There's something here for everyone: prepared food that will please vegans and porketarians alike; prime ingredients for the most exacting cook; cookbooks; breads; sit-down meals; a food court on steroids with nary a fast food stand or mass-market vendor in sight. There's even a beer garden.

In short, a great place to browse, to visit, and to hang out in.

人山人海，包括中国炒面在内的世界各地美食汇总在一起。周末的时候一家老小都会来此饕餮聚餐，实在是瘦身族人伤心地。
可惜吃饱了墨西哥玉米饼过来的...从独立宫步行也就五分钟到了这里...尽量选择非餐点过来，否则座位实在难找咯

It would be worth the trip to Phillie just to see this place.  And if you can't find something here to suit your fancy something is wrong with you.  I only regret we didn't have more time to spend here so we could taste everything!

A nice market with Philly cheese steak, Amish apple sauce, Italian food items, and deli. Can be overwhelming if it's your first time. Certain stands are really busy. But you'll catch on. I always stop by the Amish stand, it is the most peculiar and unique part of the market.

Go for the sassy cookie girls at The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company, stay for the claustrophobia and panic attacks (they're character building, don't let anyone ever tell you differently.)

If you're really trying to impress someone, and you are, treat them to the hot wings at Frank's. Anyone willing to navigate those gigantic meat monsters in front of you is a keeper. 

Oh, and Olde City Coffee once let a frazzled, cash-strapped friend pay them on I.O.U. which was really nice. My friend paid the next day, but she remained frazzled. That's neither here nor there.

If you're not into slow-walkers, avoid. Unless you get an hour-long lunch. In which case, where you work, boo?

This is one of the best places in Philly to eat if you're not exactly sure what you want. With a large variety of foods from different regions and cultures, you could pick any shop to eat at and you won't be disappointed. There's also a couple delis and a market if you need to do some grocery shopping.  If you name it, it's probably there (Except the sushi place that is no longer here.) 

It is a tourist spot so some of the places can be a little pricey, but overall it's a good place to get a quick bite to eat. Because it's a tourist spot it can also get very crowded and loud when it's busy. 

Whenever I'm here I usually get a roast pork sandwich from Dinic's.

I looked this place up before traveling up to Philly. It was everything I expected it to be. If you are ever visiting Philadelphia this a must-go! So many delicious eateries and my boyfriend and I pretty much went around getting small meals from the places we were most interested in and made sure to stop and get donuts and cake from the bakery spots. I want to go back to try more restaurants and if I was from here I would definitely take advantage of all the fresh produce, meats, and fish that was being sold.

As an actual Philadelphian, I try to avoid Reading Terminal because it is SO crowded and touristy.  However, whenever I have a conference at the convention center or jury duty or am just in Center City, I'm drawn to this mecca of amazing local food.  My personal favorite is the creperie and Greek food.  I was on a 13 day jury trial, and I alternated between those two each day.  I also love the Iovine Produce place.  During my first six months in Philly, I didn't have a car.  I lived near Whole Foods and would often go there with a backpack and two reusable grocery bags, but it was expensive.  I started going once a week on the subway to pick up my fresh produce.  The quality was evident and the price was great.  The market also has a great bar with a good beer selection.  I used to really dig the winery but now find the wines too sweet.  There are also some great speciality shops, including one next to the wine tasting shop that sells Philly/PA gifts.  My parents beeline there every time they visit.  If this place keeps drawing in a local, clearly it is worth a tourist seeing!

Setting aside the incompetents serving, I got fried chicken feathers. Disgusting. Terrible. Worse. I know appreciate Popeye's chicken is more than a franchise recipe. To make up for it they gave me tenders which were about as tender as splintered wood. I asked for rice and beans three times and pointed. I got disgusting inedible greasy fries. Never again.

This market compares favorably to market places we've visited around the world - Tokyo, Budapest, Seattle, Vienna (Nachtmarket) and it is right in your back yard. Take public transportation to get there and a large appetite.

You know that you're in a real city when you can pop into a place like the Reading Terminal Market. Centrally located near our hotel, it was a great option for lunch on our arrival day into Philly. There are almost too many choices to choose from at this place. The wife and I opted for the German place with the curry wurst and the potato pancakes and both were great and filling. 
The curry wurst alone could have fed a small family of 4. It was loaded with German sausage, fries and a curry flavored ketchup. It was kind of the German version of poutine, but either way it was tasty. The potato pancakes were fluffy and not really greasy, which was nice.
The place was packed with us being there at lunch hour, but service was quick. Plenty of sandwich places, an oyster bar and many other ethnic food options, as well as butchers, cheese mongers, fish mongers and grocery.
I suspect a return visit before we leave Philly.

I can't come to Philadelphia without coming to the market. I don't think there is anything you could not find here. From fresh produce to all kinds of ethnic foods and amazing bakeries and confections. This is the place to shop and eat.

Holy. Crizap.

And I thought Portland had badass farmer's markets.

There's not much to say that hasn't already been said. Enormous and full of goodness. Really, really busy. But probably worth it, especially if the notion of a space bubble is foreign to you.

I had the chicken masala & paneer tikka roll.  I preferred the paneer. The bread was a nice texture, and held the fillings well. The sauces, or marinades that coat the proteins were tasty.The paneer and chicken breast on their own are pretty bland. The white & red sauces on the side help give flavor. Lassis are premade I think, so I passed.

Just like Spice End, if you buy 2 rolls you get $1 off. The platters I saw people eating looked good. I don't think they could be much better than a good Halal food stand on the street, which would cost about 1/2 the price.In reference I can get a chicken tikka roll @ one of my fave carts in W. Philly which costs $3 and is bigger.

The place is nice, clean, and open late. Food comes out fast, and the staff are very pleasant.I could see myself possibly returning if I was in the area late @ night and had the munchies.

Eating and cultural Mecca.  If you can't find satisfaction here you are in trouble. They have every nationality and the best donuts!  We travel from place to place and sat at a common seating area with all of our choices.  This is a must.

We will be back!

This is a pretty good shopping place in Center City.
Its got variety and its busy.
I think it has gotten pretty pricey ($$$) if you plan to sit and eat, but if you want to shop produce, the prices are very reasonable ($$) and the quality is good.

A good ol' fashion market. and its indoors. so, its going to smell like an outdoor market, but inside. 
Great selection of meat, cheese, bread, coffee, candy, more meat, cookies, and a whole lot of shit you only find in markets. Try the sausage place. I picked up some chicken sausage that was absolutely decadent (did I use that word right?). Mmmm....

Not just because of proximity, as there are a number of good bars around me, this place is one of my favorites. Food is great, beer selection is better and they have some nice cocktails too. Nice atmosphere and the jukebox usually has some good music playing (anywhere between Joy Division to Snoop Dogg). Staff is cool, bartenders are always friendly, and when you're in the mood, there's outdoor seating, replete with heaters in the awnings for those brisk days.

There is little I can add to 1400+ reviews. This place is a top destination for Philly. It reminds me distinctly of Pike Place Market in Seattle. It's a fine place to check out. Sometimes it has super good deals on produce. Otherwise, it's just never been my kind of thing. I prefer less crowded farmers' markets.

Fantastic market to satisfy everyone's likes!!!
I found myself acting like a kid in a candy store..  Food and more food that looks and smells better than the one I just drooled over..  My personal two favorite merchants were the dinic's; gosh their sandwiches are out of this world and the Salumeria, another great hoagies or sandwich whatever place...  
Find some time to explore this place.  Not only there are restaurants in here but also bakeries, flower shop, specialty produce, seafood, etc you get the point..  At one point kinda reminded me of the market in Seattle, WA.  You won't be disappointed to drop by gain a few pounds in here.

This place has great deals and really big portions. I liked the Asian pork dumpling a lot and the buffalo chicken was good but the others we ordered were pretty terrible (Cauliflower, honey chipotle, and cheesesteak). It might just be my preference but the textures were really unappealing and the flavors were not good. 

The watermelon and arugula salads was really tasty and the buffalo chicken noodles were huge. 

The dumplings are definitely not made fresh so it might be a good idea to listen to Philly mag and just stop by for a bag of frozen ones to keep at home for late night snacks.

What an awesome market.

The Reading Terminal Market is an indoor farmer's market with many shops, most focusing on food.  Butchers, fishmongers, florists, grocers, and specialty food stores are plenty, as well as restaurants, deli, and food vendors.  The famous Tommy DiNic's is in the market and their pork sandwiches are must haves.  I'm also a huge fan of Beth's Cajun since Reading Terminal Market was the last place I'd expect to have some bomb cajun food.  Chinese, Japanese, Greek, and Italian, cheesesteaks, and everything can be found here!

There are also plenty of bakeries in there and there's a bakery that'd probably fit your kind of diet.  There's even a Vegan baker here.  As soon as you walk in, the aroma of all sorts of baked goods just punches you in face, in a good way!  Beiler's is a good spot to indulge yourself in the world of buttery goodness.

Old City Cafe has got some bomb coffee and there's even a vendor selling fresh squeezed juices to quench your thirst!

It can get really crowded during lunch, since the convention center is right next door so be prepared to fight through some crowds or stand around to wait for a table.

Definitely take sometime to walk through the whole market.  I was lucky enough to go there for lunch for 3 days during my stay in Philly, but definitely wish that I had an afternoon to explore everything in there!

Seems so fun but actually BLOWS. Lots of unique vendors who sell the same food you can get anywhere else in the city, with only 10 times the wait. There are Amish there though (or Mennonites or whatever the hell) if that gets you off.

A fantastic place to visit whether you're a local or a tourist. Fresh foods from the farmer's market stands, eclectic gourmet baked goods from local vendors, and some of the best regional food you can find in the city. If you like roast pork sandwiches, or cheesesteaks, or Amish food, this is a great one-stop shop

The major benefit of working from home isnt the free time to come and go as I please, walk around the house in boxers, or sleeping late.  I get to go to the Reading Terminal during OFF hours and not have to deal with flower show freaks or the weekend tourists.  Yeah, that sounds rude but frankly, I dont give a shit.
