This place is dirt cheap for produce, either Iovine or the other little place in the center, great fish spots, two great cookie spots, great ice cream, the spice spot is cheap as hell, great thai and Indian spot, and in my opinion some of the best brick oven pizza at George's. Hell, you can even get your shoes shined here which I have done several times. I spent $40 there today and have more than enough food until the next week

You can't miss here...something for everyone and even some cute amish tail running around,  something about those bonnets they wear.  Just kidding.

Do not go here if you are vegetarian. 

Good drinks and snacks, apparently everyone else enjoyed their meal. Only two vegetarian options, falafel which I had a previous time and is dense and not good. I ordered a seitan dish which was honestly inedible, hopefully they take it off the menu. I am not a picky eater, this was just awful. The server didn't notice until he was clearing everyone's plates and aggressively asked me what was wrong with it in front of the whole table. He had otherwise been friendly and did comp it though which I appreciate.

This place is a must-visit for any out-of-town visitors to Philadelphia.  But if you can, try to avoid it during the weekends.  It gets pretty crazy and packed in there.

But for Philadelphians, I would recommend that you check this place out as an actual market.  There is great produce and meats/poultry/seafood to be found within the stalls in the market.  The prices are actually pretty good, and I prefer coming here to shop for cuts of meat and seafood that you can't get at a place like Trader Joe's and are of higher quality than some other grocery stores in the area.

One of my favorite places for a semi special dinner. Services are friendly and there are a variety of choices like seafood (mussels, oysters) and regular pulled pork, steak, and burgers. Their fries are really crispy, comparable to McDonald's thin fries.  

I have had the mussels and the portions are big with several large pieces of toasted bread. The sauce it is boiled in is absolutely delicious. I have also tried their beer and the prices are very reasonable to get specialized beer. My most recent favorite is the grape fruit mix beer, definitely one of a kind and if you are a girl you will enjoy it.

Their oysters are really good but I do not think there are specials like a buck a shuck here. It's fresh but $3 each so unless you got the cash don't order it or you will want more

Will come back again!

A permanent farmer's market, except additionally with delicious variety of every kind of cuisine you can imagine. Highly recommend you come here on a Saturday afternoon, and browse the huge selections of cheeses, meat, seafood, vegetables, trinkets, and dairy products...and then also make a meal out of the New Orleans, southern, chinese, mexican, indian, european....etc...fare. A heaven for foodies who love grocery shopping!

Came to philly this weekend and heard so many amazing things about the reading terminal market. There were so many choices to choose for food, desserts and goodies. Me and my boyfriend ate at Dinicos pulled pork. But they ran out of pulled pork so we opted for roast beef. SUPER YUMMY. 

For DESSERT we got Bassetts. We got the two scoop, cookies and cream with coffee. I'm not gonna lie but the scoops were hugeeeeee. They were so creamy and delicious.

This is my second visit to this great city and I can't believe I missed the Reading Terminal Market on my first visit. This is a must visit - right after the liberty bell.  OK - for get the bell come here first.  This place is crammed with food venders serving some of the best food ever. I stopped at Hershel's East Side for a pastrami Rubin  -  there must have been a pound of meat on this baby.  So good, I should have a stopped but I didn't.  Next stop will be Di Niks for the Italian pork sandwich.  I'll be back for that.  My wife said and I quote "we should move here".  Are you  kidding me, I'm a New Yorker by birth ... That would be sacrilege ... But I'll be back for the food.

While the Terminal Market doesn't boast the best food or the best prices in the city, it does have the best selection, and many of the options are good. My favorite part of going here is walking in and being hit by the incredible combination of wonderful smells. This is a truly special place.

Such an awesome market.  I currently live in Seattle but am contemplating a move to Philadelphia and am so happy I checked Reading Terminal out on a recent visit.  We are so spoiled to have Pike Place Market here, but knowing that Philly has such a great market - which is easily on par with Pike Place - is reassuring.  The farmer's produce section is sort of small, but the staggering variety of hot food/meal vendors more than makes up for it.  The wife and I will certainly enjoy Reading Terminal as much as we enjoy Pike Place now.

Not the best I had. The xl deep fried chicken is made from chicken breast with bones inside. It was a little dry and pricy for one flatten out chicken breast. The fried squad is also small and not worth 8dollar. 
Ps, They had scratch card in the first week and I happen to won a ninja chicken nugget. But when I went to redeem it , the cashier says I have to purchase something first in order to redeem the chicken nugget. That is unacceptable. I need to buy something in order to get a chance to play the scratch card and when I won I need to purchase something else in order to redeem it? Will not be back again

This place has it all everything from fine cheeses, meats, seafoods, fresh veggies, cookies you name it! I love the variety and most of the quality of the foods all under one roof! They have some of the best fast sandwiches (D'nicks) and other quality fast food in the city. However be prepared most of the time this place is PACKED!!! and when there is a food tour around my love for reading terminal becomes a love hate relationship especially when they take the last black and white cookie from 4th street cookie!! which is why I rate reading terminal 4 stars instead of 5!

A food lovers dream paradise! Get here early to avoid the lines and come hungry. Have your mind made up as you will find yourself in a wanderlust if you are not careful. Although that is an awesome way to kill a day.

What's not to love?

It doesn't matter what you eat, they have it.

Carnivore, omnivore, vegetarian, vegan. They have something for you.

Indian, Mexican, Middle Eastern, Chinese. You are covered.

It almost feels like you are in another country. Or several other countries at once.

And there's more there than just lunch. Used books. Spices. Crafts. 

But it's mostly about the food. Mmmmm.

By far the best kati rolls I've had in this country! The chicken is so tender, flavorful, and well marinated. For vegetarians, the aloo paneer roll is an amazing option, id say it's as good if not better than the nonveg options! At $5.50 a roll, Im definitely going to be a regular customer.

When I was visiting Philly in September, I fell in love with the Dutch pretzels and the Vegetarian Philly cheesesteak place. It reminded me of the Farmers Market at the Grove in Los Angeles, but with different foods. 
I wish I could have tried all the vendors here... guess I'll have to come back for more!
We had the rib place which was pretty solid. Donut place was pretty good,lots of options.  Some other spots looked appetizing as well
The only thing bad about this place is there are too many places to eat. I gain 10 pounds because of this place. I will defiantly stop back in when I am in Philly.

Having lived in Philly and then moved many times for work, I appreciate this market more than you know.   Lots of choices for breakfast, lunch and dinner.  You can walk aimlessly around with a cup of fresh made coffee and take in the multi-cultural possibilities.  Looking to cook?  You can pick from any beef, pork, poultry, or lamb cut you can imagine.  Need produce, bread, and desserts?  No problem, because this market has it all.  Wish I could transport this gem to Nashville!  They even have a bar inside.
So much to choose from. I really enjoy the variety that is offered. Super busy at times and hard to find a place to sit and eat.

It's overrated but it has some good eats. The fruit and veggies in the back are ok I've had much better. Plus it's too expensive. I don't take time out to go but if I'm in Center City Philadelphia and I happen to drive by I'm willing to stop in. But I don't make special effort to go to Reading Terminal

Love the variety here.... there is everything you could ever want. Restaurants and meat/fish markets. But closes pretty early, 6 I believe. 

I've been to one of the 
- Little restaurant for Gyros which were tasty. 
- Little Thai restaurant in the back right was also very tasty.  (If looking at the complex from the front) 
- Pakistani food was delicious and your able to get free samples. 
- Beef Jerky store makes me laugh and reminds me of home, but is incredibly expensive. 
- Ice Cream is tasty in the front. Something that starts with a B. 
- Donuts on the far left front are also delicious but incredibly expensive. $11/dozen. (If looking at the complex from the front) 

We plan on coming back every week just to try something for lunch. 

It's just fun to walk around and look at everything that they have to offer.
If you dont mind doing your grocery shopping in an extremely crowded place but with tremendous fresh and amaaazing options - this is the place to be!

My first time there and at first it was very overwhelming but don't despair!!!  I suggest walking the market before purchasing anything.  This place has almost everything your belly would ever want.  The Roasted veggie focaccia at Metropolitan Bakery was perfect with my bbq chicken skewer from Little Thai Market (the Thai BBQ sauce is pure crack.  I wish they sold a bottle of it).  Desert was cookies from The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company.  Those cookies are slap your mama good!!! Try the cinnamon oatmeal raisin cookie it's just so good.

Came here for the first time last night and enjoyed some brews as well as $4 oak cast... whiskey-ish drinks. Service was friendly and attentive and the atmosphere was nice and relaxed. I was also fortunate enough to enjoy (from a friends recommendation) a delicious "Lamb Neck Gravy". #SAVORY-LICIOUS

This place is a mad house, a million stalls, a million smells and food all over the place. Some of it looks like run down food court options, but some of them look amazing. I saw a butcher that was selling different types of sausages that sounded so good I wished I was a local and could buy them and grill them up.

Its a little frantic and hectic in here but finding a table for 5 to sit and eat didn't seem very difficult which was really nice. Over all clean place thats great to dive in for a random selection of eats.

Can you say WOW! A Foodies paradise! Made me want to move to Philly with all the fresh seafood vendors and meat markets all in one spot! It has offers of wonderful smelling foods and so much to see and take in. Jammed pack both times we visited. Experience it if you're in the area.

My Eden with cherry tomatoes and diced cucumbers was absolutely delicious. The people there suggested I try both the garlic mayo and cilantro sauces on my rice and they were spot on. Numerous people have seen what I was eating and commented that everything smelled delicious. I'm definitely a fan! 

I ordered the Eden again and the Frida Kale on a third visit. Both bowls were amazing!

9/20/16 update: The Beefsteak Burger was very good, but it's not that filling. It's mostly a big bun (an olive brioche bun) with a slice of tomato (mine wasn't that thick like everyone's pictures), sprouts on top, and some kind of sauce that makes everything taste good. I think adding lettuce and some nuts on it would make it a little heartier.

9/21/16 update: I tried the Beefsteak Burger again and this time I got a really nice, thick slice of beefsteak tomato (it was almost an inch thick so I don't know what happened to yesterday's). However, the bun was different. It didn't have the shiny glaze that yesterday's bun had and didn't taste the same. I added lettuce and sesame seeds to it for more crunch. It needs a little more sauce to make it better.

9/22/16 update: I ordered the Beefsteak Burger again and this time I added chickpeas and lettuce. My sandwich looked humongous (check out the picture). Check out the nice shiny glaze on the bun. Did I mention my burger was really big? Everything that is good about the quick serve industry (since this isn't fast food like a nationwide chain) is right here in this burger. They should call this the Yoga Burger! (although I'd prefer they name it after me ;) ) I'm raising Beefsteak to my coveted 5 star rating!

I love this pizza. I cannot get enough. The ingredients and method are amazing. I think this is the best pizza is the United States. In fact it may be better than the pizza in Italy due to the amazing ingredients and care that goes into each pizza. Go. Trust me. Don't wait.

Came in around 2am after a night out on the town. Packed (as usual I guess), but the cashiers were all super quick and friendly.

What we ordered:
1. Chicken n Rice- Halal guys copy cat, but doesn't live up to the standards. 
2. Paneer Kati Roll- Our favorite. paneer covered in the creamy tomato sauce- delicious 
3. Chicken Masala Kati Roll- 2nd favorite. Tasted like the paneer one- but with grilled chicken.
4. Lamb Kabob Kati Roll- not that remarkable but I remember the spices were strong.

Great for anyone that wants that quick and casual Indian restaurant experience. Also, makes really good drunk food in my opinion. Would love to come back if I'm ever in the area but definitely recommend the kati rolls over the platters.
Tied for best Indian we've had in Philly. Delivery was a mess (containers broken open, some food cold) but that may not be the restaurant's fault. Tough to say. Solid 3-star for now.

This is a great old school market. It's not full of those hipster type stalls many markets have these days, but it does not need to be.  I was walking around here with my wife and I kept saying how if I lived here I would come here all the time to try all the delicious looking food from the wide variety of stalls.  The choices seem endless and that makes it very hard to choose. I ultimately chose a cheesesteak from By Georges, but I could have easily have been swayed in a number of different directions. Next time in Philly I will definitely be back to try something else.

I love the concept of this place! It's a huge market with tons of vendors, both restaurant type vendors and produce and meat vendors. 

We went on a Sunday when we were traveling for work and a lot of vendors were still there but there were definitely some places that we closed. We also tried to go the last time we were in the area, but it was Labor Day and the market was closed. 

We tried to get small amounts of food from several vendors and almost all of it was really good. 

As an added bonus, they validate parking for the garage across the street. You just take your ticket to one of the vendors you purchase something from and they'll validate it for you. It doesn't cover the entire cost, but it's significantly cheaper. 

If I lived in the area, I would definitely frequent this place.

This place was just so amazing, diverse, and fun. This was my first time here but now I know that every time I visit the city I would like to visit the market because there are so many things to try! It's a little overwhelming but it just makes you want to come back and try a little bit of everything.

Stopped in here on Saturday afternoon to score the seasonal cult favorite - the Shamrock Shake. Best Shamrock Shake I've ever tasted, and it was the perfect shade of Shamrock Shake green and made my sunny Saturday afternoon that much happier. 

This McDonald's was clean, bright, busy - and the Shake was served quickly and with a smile. Almost made me want to order a Big Mac and some fries too....but I restrained mysefl. But if I ever get a random craving for chicken mcnuggets, I know where to go...

There isn't anything I could say about the Terminal that hasn't been said already. This place is like Six Flags for foodies.

I scanned the reviews and couldn't help but be flabbergasted by the 1 star reviews. To each their own I guess, but it did my soul good to peruse some of the 1 starers other reviews only to find out how bad their tastes are across the board.

Please don't come to Philly without visiting and eating your way through the terminal! Admission is free, but you're gonna need to wear  your comfy pants.

Best place ever.  From the pretzel stands to the diner, everything is just amazing, fresh, delicious.  If you're a tourist, it's a must for lunch!  Skip those overpriced restaurants and get a bite to go and sit at the park or in the terminal's own indoor seating area.  You can also get lots of local goodies, pastries, cheeses, meats, dairy, etc.  It's the bomb.  Great for the family as well, fun for everyone since there is someting for everybody!

Anything you could possibly want under one roof. They have some cheap and amazing produce, the best chocolate chip cookies I've ever had, delicious coffee (vanilla-almond!) and, um VEGETARIAN CHEESE STEAK that won't make you miss meat. The only fault I find is that this is not in my hometown.
Amazing selection of food, groceries, and desserts. Brokers, Bassets, and Terminis were excellent.

A must see when coming to Philadelphia! There are so many places to choose from to eat that it can be overwhelming. They have a lot of stores that sell fresh foods and meats. It can be busy and a bit crowded on the weekends. The food is reasonably priced. You won't go wrong by visiting this place. I'll be back on my next trip.

Reading Terminal Market = Disney World for foodies

If anyone asks me the question "I'm coming to Philly, what is there to see and do?" My number one answer would be Reading Terminal Market!

It is the perfect place for families, friends, couples, etc because you will be able to find something for everyone - even the pickiest eaters.

There are tons of places and kinds of foods to eat, in addition to a beer garden that allows takeout for those who are interested.

My favorite place to eat here is Meltkraft. I love the Melter Skelter, a grilled cheese with BBQ chips as one of its delicious ingredients. 

You can go here countless times and try something completely new and different each time. I also do groceries here as you can find fresh produce, meats, and more. 

The best part is, this is all indoors so as the weather turns cold, its the perfect place to spend a day eating and people-watching.

I consider this the Wal-mart of farmers markets. Everything you want under one roof for a reasonable price. The Amish section of the market is where some of the best food is found. I can't resist the pretzels and cinnamon buns.

Plain and simple. Do you like amazing food? You'll love it here.
You can get practically any food item your heart could desire here. There are so many amazing places it would be silly to try and list them all. Hershel's though is probably my favorite for a real great corned beef sandwich outside of NYC.

Out of all the reviews I have given, This takes the cake! 

This is seriously my favorite place! I've been to markets all over the world(Quincy,St. Lawrence, Mercado San Miguel, ect) and they have nothing on the reading terminal. Nottthing!  

First off, you have to understand almost all of the best food in Philadelphia is located here. practically everything you order is perfect. This includes candy, Ice cream, fruit smoothies, all kinds of food, flowers, and so much more... 

The Amish shops are what really puts this market over the edge. You know those Anne Ann's pretzels you can get anywhere? Get the Amish version here and you'll never look back! Ribs? Whole chickens? Purple veggies?!?! Yep got them too! 

I could go on all day, but I'd rather you just go and experience it for yourself!

Looked like fun eating there... many great places for people who ate meat. I'm a vegan and I didn't find anything I could eat on my first time there. My daughter goes to college nearby and she recommends this place but during off-peak hours to get seats.

It's lunchtime on a Sunday. I'm craving Chick-Fil-A. This is the only day I ever crave Chick-Fil-A. 

Why do I only want food from here when it's closed? Is it some unusual marketing tactic? No. It's just that so many of their stores are located near malls and shopping centers and people tend to do their shopping on Sundays. 

You head down to Ikea, Best Buy, or one of the malls and, boom, you're staring a closed Chick-Fil-A dead in the eye at lunch time. You could apply Leo Getz's philosophy on drive-thrus from Lethal Weapon 2 to this scenario.

I get that the owner is a devout Christian and he wants to be closed on Sunday because it is the "Lord's day" but people still need to eat. The J man handed out loaves of bread and fishes to his peeps. He didn't leave them starving, right?
There is something for everyone here.  Mexican, vegetarian, chinese, bakeries, greek...anything your heart desires all in one place!

If you're at Reading Terminal and looking for food, just head straight to DiNic's for a Roast Pork Sandwich with Greens & Provolone.  It's a SUBstantial sized hoogie so unless you're a big eater, do share with a friend and save room for some dessert and treats at the Dutch Eating Place.

Loved it.  I walked over from the sheraton four points which was super close. Inexpensive food options galore.  Had breakfast at dutch eating place and got super full so I didn't have room for the great looking donuts at one of the other stores. I walked around the marketplace and bought a natural beeswax candle for $6. I wish there was more space to sit and eat. The freshly baked bread looked yummy.

This is s great market to get lost in especially on a rainy day. There is a melange of different eateries: fresh meat, fish and wonderful produce.
It's best to come with a hearty appetite to sample all the great food.
The highlight was the produce department which displayed a fresh assortment of eggplants, sweet peppers, corn etc
This really puts NY Chelsea Market to shame
Highly recommend visiting when you visit Philly

I can't add much to what's already been reviewed, but RTM is one of my favorite places in Philly. If I had the time and energy I'd grocery shop here. There is everything from Thai to Cajun food, fresh produce, breads, cheeses, desserts, ice cream, coffee, smoothies, flowers, spices, cookbooks... the list goes on. Go and do not be disappointed.

This was my favorite place in all of Philly! I'm so glad the concierge at my hotel recommended I stop by to grab something for lunch. There are tons of food counters with anything you can imagine to eat. The lines for the Thai food were really long so I wish I had time to try that... I had a cupcake from Flying Monkey Bakery and a Cheesesteak from Carmen's while I was there and bought some candy from the Amish. I spent a good hour wandering around and wishing I had a kitchen so I could get some of the fresh food and cook!

An affordable, well-made salad is a rare thing in Center City (Market-East). There's plenty of the Pay by the Weight options, but I tend to go over board at such places. 

The Quest: find a place that within a short walk that makes a decent salad but doesn't whack you over the head with a big price tag. As a point of reference, I consider Salad Works to be over priced and not very appealing.

The closest place that I could find that met my criteria is Honeygrow. While searching on Google for a menu, I saw an ad for their mobile app - you get $5.00 off your first order!!! That's an IMMEDIATE win. 

I went with the Cobb Salad - overall, the ingredients were okay at best, but not terrible. In comparison, I would sit them in the same world as a Wawa pre-packaged salad. Saving grace comes in the form of a very good White Balsamic dressing. Normal pricing for this salad is $11.00. If I ABSOLUTELY had to eat a salad, I would probably go there again - for the sake of pure convenience. Otherwise, I'm not sure that their salads would do it for me.

However, they offer a menu of customized Noodle dishes... Boxes appeared to be a pint or half pint of food... Might check those out before deleting the app from my phone.
awesome place!  Got the best grilled cheese I ever had at the little cheese shop in the back of the market...same one that sells awesome olives!

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE the Reading Terminal Market. If we are picking up fresh food & vegggies for dinner or almost EVERY THING Beidlers makes ...... Its great!  Beidlers ( Amish near the front of RTM .... )  Has incredible puddings & fresh donuts.  MMMmmmmmm The best!  & Worth every penny!
During lunch hour, it's too crowded and hard to navigate.  But around 5pm...amazing!!
simply the best cannoli you'll ever have! i never bother with a box either because i always end up eating it immediately. delicious!

Lots of great food!, fun shops! great place for lunch, and for taking people from out of town to show them around Philly!

They have a food court style area with tons of delis and restaurants. Options range from Indian to Italian and everything in between.

They have candy stores, cookie stores and smoothies.

The shopping consists of book stores, soap, jewelry, some aprons and shawls,  wine and kitchen ware.

There is a candy shop that sells a novelty chocolate covered onion and has pictures of this guy eatting it. Its pretty funny.

Also they have this great fresh juicing places where it is all fresh! and no sugar added.

I like bringing out of town guests here to show them a little slice of Philly living.

I have personally eaten at "Hershels" see my review for details.

I went here tonight. My friends are from out of the country and they said they couldn't accept their ID's which is such bullshit. This is the only place it's ever happened to them, everyone else accepts their ID's. So then we said well we'll just stay for one drink then leave but they kicked all of us out because my 2 friends didn't have "valid" ID's. So bogus. If you're anything but all American don't think about going here

This place is amazing!  After heading home from Vintage Wine Bar where we had some wine and appetizers, my fiance and I stopped here for kati rolls.  Everyone there was so friendly and they even let us sample some of their lassis (all which were delicious!).  We loved the food so much we ordered kati rolls for delivery a few days later and although it was Saturday night, they were very prompt with delivery and they didn't charge us a delivery fee.  The food came hot and fresh.  Highly recommend!

I'm not a huge fan of Indian food, but was pleasantly surprised at the sandwich rolls they had here. This is more a fast food joint than a restaurant so be prepared if seating is lacking. I had both the chicken tikka roll and lamb roll and they were both good but I definitely liked the chicken tikka roll more because it was less spicy. Try the mango lassi, it is authentic and not fake like some other places that I have been. To finish off your meal you need to have some masala chai which is a good mix of spices and flavor. The prices here are extremely reasonable so definitely check it out.

Reading terminal has a lotta great options. It really depends on what you want. The wait can be really long depending on the time that you are going. Reading terminal has everything from cheese steak to cheese cake.
Great place for all kinds of food; produce is especially fresh

If you can't find something you absolutely love here ... well that's impossible so never mind. This place is big, filled with amazing vendors of all kinds, and stuffed with people. 

Why so crowded? 

Because everyone there knows the Reading Terminal Market is a landmark that's worth visiting anytime you're in the city of brotherly love. It would take me a year or two to get through all the vendors in the place, not to say that would stop me from trying!
Best place to shop.Has everything you need in one spot.And the Amish women are beautiful.

Great open air market with a multitude of shops and places to eat. If you are looking to buy food or food related items, this is a fun place in town. Can get crowded try to go during an off time. Sunday's the Amish places are closed (roughly 1/4 of the market)

Try- Dinic's pork sandwich. Get a chocolate organ (you can choose a heart, liver, etc.). Coffee place has so many options. Bieler's donuts are a must!

I have been here once and had a very positive experience. The vastness of the market and the sheer number of vendors is fairly overwhelming. However, that is also part of the fun. There are sweets, baked goods, dairy, jams, jellies, seafood, meat, prepared foods like sandwiches etc. If you can name it, it is at reading terminal. I ended up getting a Italian sub, several spicy pickles, chocolate covered bacon, and hot pepper jelly. Obviously service and quality varies vendor to vendor, but overall my experience was fun and delicious. This iconic Philly spot deserves a visit.

I love this place... and you will too.  It is fat kid heaven.  You can have whatever you like... so "treat yo self" to a day in a food utopia.  The only thing I can say they are missing that I need in my life... is korean food.  They are lucky everything else is so good... that I am gonna leave that extra star.

It's hard to vote for an entire food market, but I'm going to anyways. Fabulous place to go to if you're in the city, visiting or living here. You can find a meal for all budgets. I highly suggest Beiler's Donuts but get there early if you are going on a weekend! Termini Bros is also a local favorite for fresh cannolis.

They do need more seating options, which is why I'm marking this down.

Almost everything here is top notch.  I love the atmosphere and the free music.  The only vender that was disappointing was the Thai restaurant.  I love Thai food but thought they just "slopped" it together.  
The hardest part is deciding what to eat.

Awesome indoor farmer's market with tons of food to go and interesting international stands.  A must visit for anyone coming to Philly....
The best of the best is all under this roof!
If you have never been you need to experience RTM. Great place to get some great food, meet some locals, and enjoy the environment of the market!

There is everything in here: good food, grocery, butchers, coffee, snacks, pastry, kitchen utensil, local veggies, and even beer. I lived in Center City years ago, and I was here almost on a daily basis. When we moved away from the city, we missed it dearly and thank goodness, we are now close enough to come here almost every month. We'd come here to get lunch (if not too crowded), afterward buy a pound of chocolate covered pretzels from Chocolate by Mueller, turn around and get a slice or two of cakes from Termini Bros, then head over to a butcher to get steaks or fish vendor to get seafood, and on the way out to the train station, pick up some veggies and a cup of joe. This reminds me of the street markets in Hong Kong, except this is indoors, smells much better and is a lot cleaner. I am so glad they expanded recently to accommodation more vendors and added more sitting areas. I've lived in many different cities, and Philly is my favorite (yes, even better than SF and Los Angeles, take that California) and Reading Terminal Market contributes to Philly's unique character.

I am not going to recommend any specific place, because everyone has his favorite places. The only thing I don't like in here is cheesesteak. We were at the Terminal this morning and were just talking how none of the cheesesteak places measures up. If you want good cheesesteak, you'd have to walk or cab it to 4th and Market to Sonny's. Most people rate Sonny's secondary, but we've eaten around town and like the balance of greasy cheese, bread, and meat there the best. Personal preference.
The only place I can get hard to find spices and a variety of coffee flavors ice cream hot donuts Bassett ice cream platter sandwiches and the list goes on my favorite place to shop

In all seriousness, Reading Terminal makes me very proud to be Philadelphian!  I feel so fortunate to have such a unique place the proverbial hop, skip, and jump away.  I wish I could go there every single day.  

Any food you buy here is amazing - from the produce, to the imported cheeses and meats, to the counter restaurants, anyone can get something from Reading Terminal.  

There's Italian, Chinese, turkey, fresh-made smoothies, baked goods, top-of-the-line produce, cheesesteaks (from people who actually know how to make them - and that would be withOUT that ghastly Cheese Whiz!), and you can even pick up a cookbook or two at the Cook Book Stall.  There' s also a little sports bar tucked inside the Terminal that's pretty cool along with a diner.   

The best part about the Terminal is sitting down to eat in the table area where the people watching is priceless.

Wandering through the labryrinth of the Terminal, as well as the hoardes of people that are there at any given time on any day, is a treat for me.  As someone who was born and raised in the city, I appreciate this treasure trove of food and history and I continue to be amazed at the stuff this place offers every time I go there.

Reading Terminal is a well-run machine that has been going for over a century - and may it continue for another century and beyond!

You can get any and every kind of food here, ranging from Philly cheese-steaks (3 different stalls, all amazing!) to stalls with authentic Indian and Chinese food.  The place has a very "farmer's market" feel to it on the inside, as there are fresh vegetables, meat and fish being sold.  There are great desert places as well.  This is a great place to take the family for a fun meal, especially if your tastes differ.

The drawback:  CASH ONLY.

This is where suburbanites come to eat when they visit Philly so they can avoid those scary hipsters. Basically a glorified mall food court. Bland overpriced food everywhere, crowded, welcome to Disneyland.

Food was great, I loved the healthy sprout kathi roll and all of the depth of flavors in the sauces and the crunch with the veggies! Nice spice and flavor! 
The service was just really slow and the girl at the counter was meh.
Amazing place for food and groceries.  I love the Amish farmers who sell their goods.

This place is amazing. It's the large scale version of my favorite Cincy market. If I lived in Philly, I'd go here all the time. It does get crowded around lunch times and I'm sure weekends, though I was not there on a weekend. 

The market has everything you can imagine- it's foodie heaven! There are even gluten free options (my sister in law really appreciated that). Cookies, donuts, sandwiches, produce, cheese, cookbooks, flowers...  just go. I'd be there to try a new stand a day if I could!
Great place to spend an afternoon.  The produce stands are my favorite -- easy to spend a day here picking up little presents for yourself and other people.
Great place to eat. I went on a weekday and there was a lot of locals, which is always a good sign.

When I go to Philadelphia I always visit this place at least 3 times per visit. The choices for food are a wide variety. I am more impressed with the people watching you can do. From the fish fish to the aroma therapy you can purchase I could literally spend hours in this place. The cookie place at the front make awesome black and white cookies. Good tip at 5:00 when they get ready to close all cookies go on sales for $1 each. Get there early as they go fast.  This is also a great place for breakfast. Long lines start early but it goes fast and is worth the trip. Looking forward to my next trip in a month. I will definitely be there wandering the aisles. Go ahead and give it a visit you will not be disappointed!!!!
food everywhere for big eaters.  fresh produce on the go. pastries are very filling, plus enough options to keep you walking around for hours.

Ordered from here again because despite them fucking up our order a few days prior, I was DESPERATE for a place that had hummus AND fries however ultimately decided against order fries for thighs and waist reasons.

We ordered this yogurt dip they have as well as regular AND spicy hummus because the dips are SO CHEAP HERE! 

All of them were pretty good. The regular hummus is kinda boring tbh but the spicy hummus has little pieces of FRESH jalapeno in it. It's actually not spicy at all but that adds something delicious to the spread. DEFINITELY order the spicy one, trust me on this. 

The yogurt was also really creamy, delicious, and smooth. I'd recommend this as well.

Anyways cool bye

Crazy fun place to go again and again while you are in Philadelphia. Great breakfast, lunch and dinner options. Go where the lines are-that's where the best stuff is! Fresh baked goods, cheese, chocolate and flowers...it's all there. Oh, and ice cream.

What a great bar to have as our "local"! 

Always top notch craft beer on tap. Plenty of great bottles too. And Elexcellently mixed cocktails to boot. 

Then there is the killer grub! I haven't had anything on the menu that wasn't fresh, well cooked, and delicious! they've got some exotic/unusual stuff, and they seem to be known for that, but I usually stay away from that (pigs ear lettuce wraps)

Great ambience and staff as well.

Hands down, one of the best places I've ever had Indian food. I had a few favorites in San Francisco and Los Angeles, but this place tops it. Their aloo paneer wrap is to die for. And make sure to try the MK chicken dish. Disappointed we don't have this place at our hometown!
Loved the apple pie and cheesesteak dumplings. The artwork around the restaurant also made it a great experience.
The diner - the egg creams and grilled cheese sandwiches are not for the faint of heart ( or those with cholesterol issues) but O M G are they YUMMY :-)
I love everything about the reading terminal, but I love the diversity of the food the most, This market is a must for tourist!
Great food. Not enough seating at times. Tough with kids because of crowds.

The Industry, or as my mate accidentally called it, The Infirmary, is growing on me.  People make all the difference in business, and this maxim is no less true at a corner bar.  The staff at The Industry are mainly a damn decent sort of folk. One can talk beer  or whiskey with any one of the bartenders (or servers).  I still have a few serious critiques of the food...and I have my own peculiar draught preferences...but I was able to get up to the three star mark due to good old fashioned personal interaction.  If the chef's hand grows a bit more deft, we may even close in on four stars...

Very happy to have another healthy meal option in a central location. It's great to grab a quick from here (although I would recommend going at an off peak time to avoid the lunch rush). 

I love this place because I love vegetables but others have complained about the veggie centric idea. It can be difficult to come up with an optimal vegetable combination sometimes. Take a look at the menu before going! I like the warm bowls.

Certain add ons are extra money so be sure to ask beforehand if that is a concern.

You can also get multiple sauces!

Really fun market with a variety of food! Range of seafood to Asian food and lots of baked goods as well... my friend and I ran out of time to try the Peking duck but we managed to take beilers donuts to go and they are some of the tastiest donuts I've had!

Awesome place for every type of food for every type of palate. Very crowded on weekends. Expect long lines at some of the more popular food booths. Not a lot of room to eat, however, unless you can get a spot in one of the stools at the bar or go to the sit down diner. Great to go place.
This place is great! For all the fantastic tastes, sights and sounds Philly has to offer, do this!

I can't say enough about RTM. I made my way here last year while on vacation and my eyes nearly popped out of my head drooling at all the goodies. I had to return this year. Where do I begin? I grabbed a dozen donuts from Beiler's, fudge, butter mints, fresh made fruit juices, a Brielle grilled cheese sandwich from Meltkraft, and the icing on top was the Tikka chicken, rice and chick pea and spinach samosa. It's authentic Indian food and its to die for. I will definitely be back again next year. I haven't tried anything at RTM that I didn't like. There is an old man that sits close to one of the entrances(near the 4th St cookie company. He's old, crass and downright rude. Don't ask him to tell you where something is located. He'll belittle you for asking. I didn't take any points away for that because people are just people-some nice some not. I ignored him and went about my business and found everything I was looking for.

Very conveniently located right above the Broad Street line. The employees really make it. Their turnover seems much lower than average and the older women who work here are competent and friendly--no dead-eyed monotones. The *worst* part of this McDonalds is the other customers. It's within one block of a high school, a drug rehab, and a senior home, so it gets the worst of all worlds in terms of your fellow diners. In the morning the joint is full of  old folks gossiping at 70dB and at night it's crammed with cackling adolescents trying to look cool by bragging about their delinquency. Still, if you want fast food served to you by people who treat you like a human being, it's one of your best options.

IN SUMMARY
Food freshness: average to good. Food sometimes sits in the warmer too long. 
Order accuracy: excellent
Overall staff attitude: excellent
Cleanliness of dining area: above average
Cleanliness of bathrooms: average for fast food
Refills on drinks: no
Condiments, napkins, utensils: behind the counter, even napkins and straws
Kid's play area: yes, but it is almost never open
Drive-through: no

Who doesn't give Reading Terminal 5 stars?  Really?  This is Philadelphia's farmer's market and examples of some of the best food we have to offer.  If you are a tourist, you can stop here to get some of everything.  I've also been to 2 Gala events here which were great.

You know that scene where Belle walks into the library in Beauty and the Beast and it's the most awe inspiring moment ever?  That's this place, but with food.  Go.  You will never be the same again.  

This place is perfect for a Sun-date, to snag your weekly groceries and produce, and to get a fantastic lunch.  We like to get there, get some lunch, then grab some groceries and walk around before settling for a mid-shop beer at the bar.  My favorite spots are the numerous seafood places, all of the cheeses, the Tubby Olive - you can do some shots of delicious and fancy balsamic and olive oil fo free! - and the general bustling atmosphere.

This place is great! So much variety! The only bad thing is that the tables aren't cleaned after every use. Some places offer seating but many don't. Hershel's was a big hit for us. The pastrami panini was meat filled, moist and delicious! Doughnuts at the terminal are so fresh and scrumptious. Forget the name of the place but it's right by one of the entrances and directly across from a bbq spot, which we've tried too and it was good. Only bad place I've tried there out of the 50 they have was sung kee's duck lo mien. The guy didn't use gloves when serving and cutting up my duck with his hands. The duck was cold too and lo mien warm so it wasn't great. I'm pretty sure I got sick from it too

Though i have only ever imbibed and had the occaional fry i will say i am on board with what is happening south of washingtion..... well at least this place.

Ive been here "bird atching watching" a few times and have always had pretty good service. On my last visit i found out there was HH every day of the week from 3-5. i also tried the mummers punch which is basically two street in a bucket with ice.

Service has always been good not sure if this is because of the company I keep or if these south Philly servers just know how to earn their tips.


Their brunch menu looks like it might be my first actual meal. Paired along side their version of a Bloody Mary is right up my alley

Lots of great food available here. I ate the ribs from The Rib Stand (Pennsylvania Dutch), which were so tasty and tender. I had 5 baby back ribs, nac and cheese, and a container of bbq sauce for about $13. We also had a roast beef sandwich from Dinic's, which was very good.

It is a charming marketplace, I would have come here again during my trip if I had more time. All the stores are neatly laid out and easy to find with the maps provided. Overall a good experience. There is paid street parking nearby and a parking garage that validates your parking ticket for 2 hours if you spend a certain amount in the market.

If you don't mind fighting the crowds, this place is a gem! You can find just about any cuisine you could want. A must see if you're visiting Philly. If you're gluten free, be sure to check out Fox and Sons- they are a completely gluten free stand serving delicious corndogs, funnel cakes, and fries!
I just got the pork and honey chipotle dumplings for take out. You can't get them fried or steamed.  I went fried.  They were delicious. Both the flavor and texture were very satisfying.

My favorite spot in Philly for indulgent Indian street food. Open pretty late Favs:
-Achari Chicken/Paneer (if you're vegetarian) Rolls
-Chicken Biryani Platter: Perfectly cooked moist chicken/flavorful rice and salad+ pita on the side. I prefer this much more over their standard chicken and rice
-Mango Lassis: Thick and Creamy. Aannddd its mango lassi. Whats not to love?!
Bottom Line: If you are in the Philly area and are looking for solid late night eats or are craving desi street food, do not miss Masala Kitchen!

A quintessential Philly landmark. Although perpetually busy and overrun with tourists, this is still a place you must experience, especially if you're not from the area. This cavernous space is packed with produce, provisions, and prepared foods from all over the globe... theres literally something for everyone. I would try to avoid the lunch rush and weekends if possible, especially Saturday mornings, only because it can be nearly impossible to move around or get a seat. I would also not recommend coming here for a cheesesteak - much better can be had elsewhere. Parking can be insane - $6 for 30 min "special" in the attached garage. TRUST ME, it will take more than 30 min to do anything there.

The service was prompt and efficient not necessary engaging or friendly! I ordered The Stomachectomy  the idea is great, after each pancake a different breakfast meat; scrapple, bacon and sausage topped with an sunny side up egg. However the pancakes crumbled and fell apart as if the were made from grits or polenta. YIKES! I didn't eat it or send it back, I should have. The prices are fair, if you like the food?? I didn't!!!!
The kati rolls are amazing and the service is super fast. Chicken biryani isn't the best but definitely a great place to grab lunch if you're ever hungry!

Reading Terminal Market has a ton of different choices from breakfast to desserts, so if you're unsure of what's in the area or if you want something quick, try any of the little shops here. Have a good look around before deciding on anything. 

Most places take credit cards. 

Definitely stop at the donut shop in the morning. Warm just-made donuts!!!!! WHAT!

There's a great spice shop that carries every spice under the sun - amazing to peruse.

This place was a foodie's paradise. Each stall was better than the next. From spices to deserts to corned beef, butchers, fish mongers etc etc. For me the best find of the day was the Pennsylvania Dutch stand selling juices and milk. Best juice I've ever had barring those I've pressed myself. Every stall I visited the employees were happy, knowledgeable and friendly and it really made walking through the bustling lunch crowd worth it. Bought as much as I could carry..and left planning my next trip.  4 stars..would have been 5 if my parking wasn't 29$. I got validated.. But I stayed 15 minutes passed 3 hours. So instead of 16$ parking I got banged for 29$. I'll know better next time..and now so will you!;) ( parked in the garage across from the convention center. ) Also I visited on a Thursday early afternoon. If the lunch crowd was an indicator of how it would be on a weekend.. I'd stay away Saturday and Sunday. Other than that..its worth the trip.

One of my favorite places in Philadelphia.  I am here almost every weekend. Great place to buy fresh produce and meat or have lunch at one of the many food options. Also, the 4th Street Cookie Company is addictive!
Everything you can imagine. Best to go in the off season and better tues-sat when the omish are there.

Nice place to go to if you're visiting Philly! You can get the best food and desserts all in one place. If you live in Philly, even better; try out the grocery stores and all the booths for your everyday culinary needs.

You can be a tourist in your own city if you stop by RTM. What a fun place to go with your family, friends, or a cute city date!! There are so many fun and unique vendors to check out. For lunch, I love the corned beef special at the Hatville Deli. I get that with some cold apple cider. It's one of my favorite sandwiches. It has cole slaw, russian dressing, and a nice portion of corned beef  on rye (you can also get it with pastrami). 

They have chocolates, wine, kitchen stuff, farmer's and locally farmed foods. Check out the fair food farmstand vendor! They have lots of cool veggies and cheeses. 

There is a vendor that sells bee products-honey, candles made from bees wax, and lip balms. The Tubby Olive is a fun place to go and try different olive oils and vinegars on tap. It's pricey but you don't have to buy anything to get some samples :)

You can't live in Philly and not have been to this place. It has something for everyone. Saturday is the worst day to go because it gets super crowded. Once, I got out of jury duty early on a weekday and it was ghost town. The court also gave me some vouchers and coupons to use at RTM since it was only a block away. 

This establishment is right by Chinatown. I recommend taking a day to explore the area, there's that much to see!

Great spot to take out of town guests - give them a taste of everything Philly.
We took our kids to the Creperie inside the market and it was a huge hit!  How can you go wrong with banana, nutella and powdered sugar.  Sugar High.  Cheesteak line was huge and from what I hear so so cheesesteaks.

This place is great. Its a strictly in door market that houses a LOT of restaurants and small shops a little bit of everything is available to you including some of the absolute best in Philadelphia like Carmens and Tommy Dinics.

If you don't know where to eat in philly, this is the place for you!
This place is super cool. You can literally get everything and anything here. From desserts to produce to breakfast! 
It is overwhelming if you don't know what you want. I just searched for the most popular thing to get here which was Tommy Dinic's! My boyfriend and I shared a roast pork sandwich. While it was good, it wasn't amazing IMO but this place sure is.
If i'm ever in philly again, this is the first place that I would stop by!

I love coming to the reading terminal. It's like a fat boy dream. You have all types of food and desserts. When I get there I usually go for Dini's roast pork it's so good. Also melt Kraft is pretty good.they have Beilers donuts omg it's go good I bought a dozen one time and thought I was going to share with co- workers but ended up eating the whole thing. They also have termini and Basset ice cream there. I swear if I worked around there I would probably be 1000 pound and have a show on TLC.
Amazed at the selection and high quality throughout..  I have travelled to other areas that claim to have great market food courts but none is better than here in Philadelphia's Terminal Market

If you're into great food and want to buy great local, farm-fresh produce, meat, and eggs, this is the place. 

It's literally the best place to buy food in the city. 

There are great places to eat (bakery, amish bakery, chocolate shops, sandwhich places, italian places, middle eastern, sushi, etc)

Fair Trade Food Stand sells fresh off the farm produce, meat, etc. 

If you live near the terminal and shop at the supermarket, shame on you.

This place is awesome! Only found out about it just last year (even though I made several trips out to Philly beforehand). 

The selection of food here is insane in a good way. Though, I must admit, I only go to a few spots here: Beiler's, Flying Monkey and Wursthaus.

Not fittting with typical McDonald's standards. 

1/2 the seats were busted. no ice in the machines, no straws or napkins in the machine. Service stunk.

But they had the occasional Diet Coke on the stroll back to the hotel- I'll take that.

I could not survive without this wonderful establishment in my city.

EVERYONE and I mean everyone can find something they like here. There is everything from mexican and chinese to those wonderful PA dutch folks cranking out some delish soft pretzels and all are available within a few feet of each other under one roof. 

One of my favorite merchants is Kamal's Middle Eastern food stand. The chicken kebob is loaded with lettuce, tomato, cucumber, chunks of tender & spicy chicken with a delish sauce (I have no idea what it is) all wrapped up in a fresh pita. They also have an array of desserts, hummus and pastries for purchase.

To top it all off stop at Bassett's for some Gadzooks ice cream (shout-out to Preston & Steve).

There are also plenty of stalls to purchase cook books, spices and anything else food related. I have also noticed they hold some cooking classes here but have yet to find someone who has participated in them. Anyone!?!

The only thing that really is a downer is if you go at lunch time (which is when I usually end up finding myself there) it can be superrrr crowded.

I stumbled on this cute little place across Philly AIDS Thrift one Wed evening and decided to give it a try. I'm a senior on a fixed income so their $1 Wed special was a definite enticement for me. I was a bit confused, I was thinking of dumplings of old that my mother made as "chicken and..." but I decided to try the mixed root veggies and the apple dumplings dusted with cinnamon. Both were very tasty and I will definitely return. The staff was courteous and patient with me. The place is clean and has an eclectic vibe.

A wonderful timeless Philadelphia tradition.  I have been going her for more than 45 years.  It has evolved and changed over the years, but always a great place to eat, and people watch.  Wonderful food options be sure you don't choose the first one you see or you will be frustrated.  A sampling of the finest foods from all over the Philadelphia area and surrounding counties.
good variety. easy access.

Dinic's pork sandwich is good.  Bassette cookies and cream is good too.  We got plain noodle soup at Peking Duck for our son for $3 and it was alot of food, I end up eating most of it.  I really want to try Cajun Jambalaya, but too full.  Overall, great experiences and very diverse in term of food.  There are grocery, spices, live seafood as well.  Great place to visit.
Just finished my 2nd visit to this place. Consistently good food and great service. Perfect for a quick lunch. The food can be a bit spicy but it isn't extreme. I really like the Chicken rolls.

This place is awesome! Every kind of food to tempt you, nice little stalls, very diverse and fun. The only down side was how busy the place is. But I would definitely come back here every time I go to Philadelphia. Definitely try the Amish doughnuts, they are amazing. I was only able to eat a few things, but I want to come back and try more.

Great market!!! Would definitely visit again. We stopped by dinics and got amazing pork sandwiches with provolone make sure to get brocolli with it. I also stopped by a candy shop and got dark chocolate covered candied ginger that was amazing.
Come here. The plain and specialty pizza were both very good and the tomato pie was the best I have ever had. The crust was perfectly crunchy and the slices are large. The staff is friendly, too.

Awesome place to kill a few hours and stuff your face full!

My faves were denics (?) and the handmade fresh donuts. Everything was awesome though.

I love strolling through these markets.

A really cool touch were the multiple posters of other international market locations.

One of them was a poster for Vancouver, where I went not too long ago, but they also had places all over the world there :)

Reading Terminal is a great place to spend a few hours. Whether you're a Philly native or visitor, there's something for anything you'd want to do, see, or learn. While it does have tourist trap prices, it's just one of those magical things that's part of Philly.

I can say that this place is cheap in regards to produce, has great random products throughout, and has really delicious food items available for purchase. This is the perfect tourist place to take any visitor from outside the city. I once even saw Patti LaBelle there!!! 

My only negative is that it becomes so ridiculously crowded that it is almost impossible to walk around. In those situations I become claustrophobic and can't breath, let alone enjoy my stroll through the market. 

However, with all that aside I would highly recommend going here and I would also highly recommend going during an off time like during business hours during the week.

This place is something else!! I've been passing by it for at least 3 days without investigating. I finally pop up in here today and what do I find?? I find a city within a building that has international as well as domestic restaurants at my disposal. It's a flea market for food basically and is basically humongous!! 

I even found a cajun stand with nothing but Louisiana foods prepared from gator gumbo to sausage and chicken gumbo. They gave me a sample of the jambalaya, the chicken and sausage gumbo and I was heavily enthused!! Being from Louisiana myself, I had no complaints as to the taste because it had everything that was needed. 

You can find fresh fish, oysters, gyros, chinese, or anything you have your heart set upon in this place. Some places in here cook your seafood, lobsters, or what you want while you wait. Some of them are to go only as it pertains to Seafood or fish. What one place don't do, the other will for you!!! THIS IS ONE HELL OF A PLACE TO VISIT!! As I have 2 more full days here, I will be spending some time in this place.
One of my favorite spots in Philly. Always bring out of town friends here. Amazing variety and quality. Can't beat the environment.
I love eating here always fast with my food and always treats you well. The staff is always helpful and great set of people.

It doesn't get much better than Reading Terminal.  You name it (food wise), they've got it.  From fresh produce, to meats and cheeses, to desserts, to fresh made sandwiches... this place has pretty much everything.

Of course with those sort of options, this place can be busy... especially on weekends or holidays.

In addition, parking is a little sparse so your best bet is to park in the garage across street and walk over.  You can even get that parking validated if you spend some money at the market.

This is why Fast food at Chick-f-let is different. It is consistently great!    You walk in, your in a hurry, and the place is spotless, the employees smile and are pleasant. They want to serve you.  I'll pass 5 Bk's or McDonalds to come to a CFA.   The wraps are great and so is the carrot raisin salad.   Thanks to the founder, Truett Cathy, this is a great company!  And the service reflects the loving, caring attitude that they share.

Awesome place to get something to eat. So many great choices; allows everyone to get something different. Horribly crowded during the holiday season, but a place you MUST go if you live in the Philly area.

Very fun place, especially for visitors.  If you like crowds, come on the weekend.  All the shops are open and there are some great options for food.  If you don't like crowds, try another day of the week.  I know some of the shops are closed on certain days, so be sure to check ahead of time.
Love the Reading Terminal. They have something for everyone. Great Food of all kinds. Can be a little bit pricey and a little too crowded

Very fun. There's a lot going on here - lots of options, lots of people, lots of temptations. We came here for a stroll and then for lunch, and ended up enjoying both greatly. One of the hardest things was just deciding what to eat among so many delicious-looking options.

Great location in the center of the city.

Wish there were a little more seating and water fountains, and a little less crowding.
So many different options with incredible food. Definitely worth visiting while you're in Philly.
Everyone should enjoy all the different types of food this place has to offer. Even if your out of state or the country stop by for a visit

A must when in philly. This place is always extremely crowded, which can be a pain...but well worth the visit. We come here to pick up coffee, veggies, and chicken for the week. I don't eat here often because I can't stand the lines (especially the donut lines), but there's clearly a reason why the lines are so long.... the food is delicious!!
This place has good food but even better service! The most thoughtful, polite and hard working people are at this location. They are fast, kind, friendly, and provide excellent service!!
One of my favorite places to eat in the city. If you are a foodie this is a must!! Great place to get fresh produce, seafood and meats as well
This place is busy most of the time, but whether you're window shopping, looking to graze a bit, or just picking up some steaks for dinner, this is always a treat to go to!

I LOVE THIS PLACE!!! A must-see/visit when in Philly!! Countless options for food, shopping and drinks. I could have stayed in here for hours just looking at all the different stands, seeing the people and deciding what to eat next.

My friend and I stopped at a Greek place, and got the gyro. Such a classic and they did not disappoint, the staff was very authentic and friendly. The food came out fast and you could see & taste how fresh it was.

I could come back here everyday and try something new!!
Love this place.  They have something for everyone and a great atmosphere.  Get some overpriced fudge dipped cookies (definitely worth it) and  a pork sandwich from  Dinic's.

On a recent trip to Philly we visited Reading Market and I immediately feel in love with this place! This is a must for anyone interested in trying out different cuisines as well as a great market place for picking up fresh cuts of meats/fish, veggies/fruits, cheeses, sweets, and well I could go on and on! Reading Market is definitely a must do!

The best food, the best place to get lunch, snacks, cheese, flowers, bread, fresh fish and meats, Amish and other ethnic specialties.  RTM is a treasure no visitor to Philadelphia should skip.
Cheap parking at the garage on Filbert St. - just make sure to have your parking stub validated at one of the market businesses.
-Little known fact - the RTM sells gift certificates - great for your Philly friends and relatives.
Underwhelming. Honestly this is somewhere you visit once. I've been to bigger, better organized markets. We won't even get into the whole parking situation.

Every shop in the RTM is great. Each place has their own specialties. Buying some cooking products can be pricey, but the quality is unmatchable in Philadelphia. If you're in a rush get there early in the morning as to not get caught up in the lunch rush.

Wow... that's unfortunate that some had a neutral experience, because I have nothing but good things to say!!  I've gone for drinks before, but last night was the first chance at dinner.

Everything we got was tasty -- here are the highlights in the order it was received:

- Weyerbacher Autumn Fest.  Get some before I finish it all.
- Lamb Gravy - I could have eaten another bowl of that!
- Wedge Salad - the toasted nuts was a nice departure from the standard
- Double Burger with almost ridiculous amount of fries - they must have known my 3:1 ratio of fries to burger :)
- Striped Bass Special: my bf had to bat everyone away from it to finish
- Apple Cider Donuts - seriously?  And I don't even have a sweet tooth..

The best part: it IS a neighborhood bar.  The staff are laid back and convivial, giving out candy to the trick or treaters coming in.

To all the naysayers.. give the fall menu a shot.  I was not disappointed and can't wait to head back:)
Very busy food place. A lot of choices. But as a real Chinese food lover, will go to Chinatown for better Chinese food. But the place is worth to try out.

I enjoy going here because of the many varieties of items they have here esp if you are going with a large crowd of people who don't know what they want. I also come here to grab some cheeses or meats that I can't get anywhere else. However, the place is beyond cramped. Its tough to try and navigate during the weekends, so I highly recommend going during the non lunch hours.

For all the tourist, I do recommend coming here as a spot. Yes, its crowded, but there isn't many places like this in the states.

The variety of food here didn't fail to amaze me; it reminded me a lot of my motherland, Thailand where they have fresh food markets, and not a second goes by without it being jammed pack. I LOVE that kind of shock and energy that it brings you.  Right when I walked in, the smell of fresh fish and meat hit me at a special spot.  Of course it naturally invited me to buy groceries, but considering that I was on a trip and Philly is not my hometown, I settled for the hundreds of restaurants that were there. There were different types of cuisines to accomondate any ethnic group which was impressive.  However, the food was just okay. I went with four people and we all got our foods from different stations, but none of them really wowwed me. I think that mine was the best. I got my dish from a Chinese place that had hanging Peking duck. Though tasty, I most definitely had better. The prices here aren't bad at all though.  Fairly reasonable and won't break your wallet.

No Philly food experience is complete without the Reading Terminal. Whether you're foraging ingredients to make a great meal or you're grabbing some eats, the Terminal will set you right. 
All of the meat stands are great particularly La Divisa. Great raw fish is available as well. The produce from Iovine's is fresh, varied and affordable. 
Termini brothers, Bassets Ice cream, Beiler's donuts and the apple dumpling from the Amish counter will all satisfy your sweet tooth. 
For savory eats I love the oysters and soups from Pearl's, the roast pork from Dinic's (as much a Philly sandwich as a cheese steak) Sang Kee's duck/ wonton noodle soup, Cajun food from Beck's, ribs and wings from Diener's. Really, you can't go wrong and there are a ton of options. Amazing place. A must see and feel if you're visiting.

Best in Philly. If you're ever shopping in center City you must go there for a bite to eat. Enjoyable time.

John H

This location is awesome. The only one that serves breakfast and Wendy's breakfasts are superb. Everything was delicious and not slopped together. Bathrooms are for customers only but that's to be expected. Myesha made me feel special and like I was getting a special treat. This is definitely a great location.
So many varieties of food from all over the world!! All of them made within a homemade touch and simply amazing! A tour of the world's finest cuisines without leaving center city!
So many great food options. Every place I've eaten at there has been delicious. Especially Dinicks.
A must visit, don't miss Dinic's!! Best pork sandwich ever! The entire market rocks! Free parking across the street!
Very busy. Some food choices are a disappointment after waiting in line for extended periods of times. Everything is fresh however.

Tourists-must-go-to place. A lot of different kind of foods, fruits, meats and souvenirs. You can get good crepes, cookies, candies and also sometimes catch a live performance by unknown singer. Them food can be very pricey. If you're a local, just go in and buy stuffs only if other places (like your favorite stores) do not sell it. If you're a tourist, you'll have a good time here. There's always something interesting going on inside. 

It is not that easy to find parking. And if you do find one, it is not that cheap either.

The place I return to time after time. Since childhood when you could order snapper soup and get a bottle of sherry with it to today where pretty much everything is available. It is a little sad though that it has become more and more like a food court and less farmer and ingredient type places. I like going here to be inspired to cook at home but most places have prepared foods these days and they are not all of great quality. Still gotta love the place!

Whether you're a local or visiting Philly for the first time, Reading Terminal is a must! With a vast variety of spots to eat, a fresh produce market, meats, and dessert spots, this place has it all. Most vendors are from Lancaster and have the ability to share with you the exact source of what you're purchasing. Homemade jams, soaps, and trinkets can be found around the market as well. The best doughnuts can be found in Beilers! I recommend harvest apple. This spot is nice due to being indoors and getting a typical "packed market/city vibe" experience. With so many choices of places to eat, you can find something for anyone to eat here.

The selection of food here is absolutely amazing.  It is always a fun time even if you just walk around to soak in the sight, sounds, and smells of all the different food stands.  Also has fresh produce which is a plus.  It may not all be healthfood but you will certainly find something delicious to eat.

I've had an out-of-towner describe it as "food Disney".  For me, it's a great selection of oretty much whatever you'd want from incredible bakery items to cheese made on site.  It seems to bee one of the few places both tourists and locals enjoy.

Honestly chic fil a has the best customer service I even seen in a fast food restaurants 
!!!!!! Boston market starting to fet better !! U go in mcdonalds  service no good Burger King KFC noone compares to there service 
And the food is also good and clean place

I love this place! The environment is sooooo warm, friendly, authentic and classic. Offers tons of delicious food places and gourmets. I have tried the Dinic's beef brisket sandwich, which tastes soooo gooooood!! I adore reading terminal market because to a foodie person like me, it's heaven!!
I actually live in Philly, but every time I go there to the reading terminal market, I feek like I am a tourist because there are always lots of different foodstuff from different parts of the world to try!!
Reading terminal market has a character; it's an ancient Market in the heart of Philly which is worthy to spend at least a day in it while visiting this city!!

The industry is a pretty cool neighborhood bar. Loved the rustic decor, dim lights and high chairs. Has a decent beer list if you are into that. Our waitress was a mess. Every time she took a plate away something had to fall, whether it was food we didn't finish or utensils, just very rough around the edges. Food was okay. The falafel was nasty, the fries and dessert (chocolate mousse) were to die for.
Very cool I visited with friends while interviewing in Philly, now that I live here need to go back...

Went (more like stumbled) here after a night out. Someone in my group mentioned he went there for lunch THAT DAY and still recommended this place to us for post party munchies. That's some food love right there. And he was definitely on point with his recommendation. 

I had the chicken tikka roll and a mango lassi. The tikka roll came out piping hot, full of flavor, and well made. The mango lassi was also creamy and delicious, and cooled things down. 

I was too busy scarfing down my food to see how the other people were doing with theirs, but overall I think we all left happy and full. I also give mega props to the staff for staying open and being calm with dealing with the drunk crowds- the patience it takes to deal with those shenanigans without losing your shit is a pretty big feat in customer service. 

I wish I lived in philly so I could come back more often, but I'll make sure to visit the next time I'm in town!
So many great little restaurants all in one place. Authentic food from tons of different cultures and styles. Highly recommend.

One of my all time favorite spots in Philadelphia! Check out the Head Nut to get small amounts of spices while you're cooking on vacation. Miller's twist has the best soft pretzels I've ever had... and go back for breakfast to get egg, cheese, and bacon stuffed in a pretzel. Beiler's donuts are also a must try (and take 2 dozen home with you)
Awesome!  A disastrous place for an Overeaters Anonymous outing, though.

Cash only. Long wait (30 Minutes for 1 person). The Chicken isn't like the plastic example in the window.

I ordered a ninja chicken combo + upgrade to the grapefruit tea. The combo comes with your choice of fries, minced meat (ruo ro) rice, or white rice and a soda or soup, but you can upgrade it for $1.50 for tea. The tea was good and came in a huge quart or something size, enough for two people. For the food, I waited at least 30 minutes for a single order and when it came it, it was entirely underwhelming.

I expected the chicken to be a huge ass thinly sliced piece of chicken like the taiwanese night markets and the window display. Nope. It was just a regular chicken with somewhat decent salt & pepper seasoning. The rice was alright, but they were stingy with the minced meat sauce. It also came with some shredded cabbage that came with like a soy sauce vinaigrette and two bites of sea weed salad. 

The chicken was cooked well, but the breading came off rather quickly. It was normal sized. I mean I guess it was a good value for $10 and change, but I would definitely not wait 30+ minutes for this.

Favorite place of all time!! Crazy chaotic but FULL of amazing variety!! Literally every type of cuisine you can think of, including an all natural beeswax stand AND a whole flower shop, grocery store and several breweries. By far the most memorable spot in Philly!

If you need a touristy activity to take friends to, especially if it's a cold or rainy day, this place works great. Without being as stuffy and expensive as NYC's Eately, it's a fun experience with lots of great food options. There are some Amish shops that are fun to look through, and they do a great job around the holidays.

Variety in foods all over this place is great. Bakery bread good. I do like this place and have only found one place inside i dont like which is one of the chinese places which gave me the crappiest duck meat i have ever seen.
Everything and anything. Satisfy your every craving but be ready to sacrifice your time, sanity and life to this place. Worse than time square on a hot summer day kinda crowded!
what an amazing place.  Just be aware of parking hardships and crowds on weekends

I love The Industry! It's one of my favorite date places, because they always have tables available and it's spacious, but cozy. They have a great selection of beers on tap, and the servers are always super friendly. Brunch is my favorite meal there, but I've also had the fish and chips, which were delish! I'd highly recommend checking this place out if you're looking for a new bar to try in South Philly!

As good as advertised. I've always wanted to check out Reading Terminal Market, and now that I have this would be the only reason I would return to Philly. This is one of my favorite food halls slash marketplaces, just for the sheer variety of vendors.

I spent about 3 hours just eating my way through breakfast and lunch, and purchased a variety of food to take back home. I'm sure coming on a weekday during the earlier hours before lunch helped improve my experience as well, because if the place was packed with crowds on a hot day it would be pretty miserable.
Amazing place! There's a cacophony of sights, scents and sounds, cool merch, great atmosphere and some of the best food you can find in the city.

I salivate just thinking about this place! Some of the finest take out cuisine all in one place!
Will review individual businesses as I endulge.

Definitely a must stop for all visitors! It's filled with amazingness! All kinds of food vendors and small craft stores. Just so much to explore each time. There's a big public dining area. You kinda have to fight for seats. It's close to public transportation but parking is a nightmare especially there's events at the convention center. I love the diversity Reading is able to bring together.

Super fun to walk around. Definitely a landmark in the Philadelphia center city area. The food is EXPENSIVE and the couple of times I bought seafood from different stands at the market, it wasn't that fresh. I do love the vibes and just walking around and always seeing something new. They have all sorts of vendors and conveniently right next to the convention center.
Always fresh food I love their coffees as well. Been there to eat with my fiancé and is a lovely setting and very clean.
Lots of good places to buy from with very fresh produce, meats and fish from.
Whoa. This place is full of choices. I certainly don't think you can make a wrong one. If you're in town traveling stop by each day and try something new.

This market is a must if you're in Philly! There are so many good shops and places to eat at in here like Beilers Bakery, (Best donuts in the world.), Riehl's Cheese Shop, (Best cheeses in the world.), Meltkraft, (Best grilled cheese sandwiches in the world.), Mueller's Chocolate Co., DiNic's, Keven Parker's Soul Food and so many others I forgot the names of. They also have fresh fruits, meat, seafood, vegetables and juices. I got this really good fresh berry juice for $2.99 but I don't even remember where I got it from. If there's anything that's related to food you can get it here. If you want to eat good food come eat lunch here because there are so many choices: Indian food, cheesesteaks, gyros, pizza, crepes, beef jerky, sandwiches, fried chicken I felt so overwhelmed! I finally decided on a grilled cheese from Meltkraft and it was the best decision I made all day. If you love food and you love to eat this is the place to be! TIP: If you're visiting COME DURING THE WEEK IF YOU CAN. THE WEEKENDS ARE TOO PACKED and you can't even take your time and look at anything in peace.

This is what shopping for food should be like:  Good fresh produce, cheese shops, hoagies and cheesesteaks.  This is the kind of place where you come hungry and expect to spend a few hours cramming in twice as many meals as you should.
