It's not big, but when you see the variety of lunch counters, you will know what I mean.  Not a bad place to be a tourist.  It is reminiscent of Eastern Market in Washington DC if you've ever visited there, but more full featured.  It even has it's own beer garden(which I would only give about two stars on it's own merit - how depressing!).  Why people were so solemn in there I don't know.  They have so much to be happy about.  The Phillies are in the playoffs for the first time in, what, like, fifty years?!  Drink up!
Best lunch spot in Philly! There is something for everyone and a great fresh seafood market.
This place has everything you could never imagine in your wildest dreams. There is no point in trying to describe this wondrous marvel. It must be experienced
An incredible sensory experience. Dinics pork and rabe was simple, delicious, and worth the trip. The crepes and doughnuts were equally perfect.
A wide variety of food that will literally cure any and every craving!

I was in town for an event at the convention center and ate at Reading Terminal Market for almost every meal. The two meals I had elsewhere were mediocre and just reminded me how much I enjoy the food at the market. You have just about any type of cuisine you can imagine available to you in a very compact space. If I have any complaint at all, it is that the crowds make the place almost unmanageable at meal times. Still, though, it is worth it. Try Spataro's for a cheesesteak, Dinic's for the roast pork, or Bieler's for a donut. Even the hot-dogs at Miller's Twist were amazing. The only place I had that was below my every-rising expectations was Nanee's Indian Palace. The naan there had been sitting around in the hot box all day and was delivered to me stiff as a brick. I even saw the owner check it for softness before he gave it to me, so he knows it is a problem and he gave it to me anyway. But, I digress. Go to the market and pick a place at random. You will probably get a great meal.

Beefsteak is a terrible company. Their food is food truck quality but double the price. We come here often but after they keep raising their prices for miscellaneous charges from the sides to extra vegetables, we have decided never ever ever coming back. This company is on par with Subway, but at least subway has $5 foot longs! Notice even the setting, they vegetable crates as light modifiers, come on! Even Subway has a better, more friendly setting!

PEOPLE BE WARY! Save your wallet some trouble and go to a cheaper, more friendly place like Sweet Green or chipotle instead!

I have the pleasure of living a 3 minute walk from this undisputed gem of the Philadelphia food scene. Anyone visiting the city for a couple of days owes it to them self to give themselves an hour or so to explore here and get something to eat. The dining options run the gamut from the beyond-five-star Di Nic's roast pork sandwich to some fantastic Indian and Latin American food to hands down the best donuts in the city. 

For residents, there's the added mega-bonus of two great, cheap produce  shops, a couple of great seafood vendors, and two or three each of great lunch meat, coffee, and sausage/fresh meat shops. There's really something for everyone here and the bustle of the city's diverse population strolling and chatting their way through various culinary missions just makes it a wonderful place to get lost for a while.

If you visiting Philly, go here. If you are a native of Philly go back. If you are stuck in jury duty, walk a few blocks and use your jury duty discount here. There are too many favorites to list, but I would not miss 1) Miller's soft pretzels. Watch them being made, get one hot, dab it with a little mustard. Nothing anywhere else compares, nothing even close. You will never buy a street pretzel or go to a chain pretzel place again. 2) Dinic's pork sandwich with greens. Beats a cheesesteak any day. 3) A chicken pot pie at the Dutch Eating Place. You won't have to travel to Lancaster County to get your Amish dining experience. If you are local shopping for a dinner party, I like Godshall's poultry, Downtown Cheese, and John Yi's fish market. This is a don't miss destination, one of the great urban markets in the U.S.
My fav place to shop or eat. Some folks just be in the way, taking pics or just stopping and having a whole convo, like keep it moving or get walked on sheeeeesh..........

THE iconic food market of Philadelphia, you simply can't go wrong if you choose to eat here! A foodie haven, you can find everything from ice cream, chocolates, cookies, meats & cheeses, fresh seafood, vegan & veggie food and plenty more. There is a vast array of options to choose from.

If you have a strong aversion towards crowds, going here during the weekends maybe be frustrating as the lines are long and finding a place to sit maybe be difficult. But these are just small inconveniences in my opinion! 

Tip: Carry cash with you as some places are cash only!
This was our first stop in Philadelphia, and it did not disappoint!  I'm just sad we didn't get to try more things.  That just means we have to keep coming back until we've tried them all.

You enter the place and the aroma of Indian spices teases you. The setting is modern and small, giving it a cosy feel.

Ordered Achari Paneer as I was in the mood to eat something chatpatta. Was ready in 5-7mins. I I also got Chaas (Buttermilk) because you know...it is Chaas!!
They start off on the right foot by using whole wheat rotis for Kati rolls.
They have some chutneys on the side for you to take. The red chutney is really spicy...not for me!
I take the first bite and it doesn't disappoint. It has the chatpatta taste with the soft paneer to balance things, exactly what I was expecting. 
Chaas was amazing and provided the coolness to all the spices melting in my mouth! 

The only thing missing were Indian songs! That would have made it the complete package. 
But as they say-
Kisi ko mukamal jahan nahi milta!!
(Nobody gets a perfect world!)

P.S. - Go with a nice company. I sure had one and it made it a whole lot better experience
We ordered sprouted Kati roll, chicken masala and unda kati roll which was so oily no salt at all. I found it very disgusting.

Rarely do places live up to reviews like this place did.   I visited Philly this past weekend and knew I had to hit up the Market.  It ended up being a block from the hotel and it was AMAZING.  Seriously if you eat (which should be everyone) then this place is for you.  I was thinking about moving to Philly, renting out one of the vendor stalls ,and just living there.  Truly one of the greatest places I have ever been to and I will go back to Philly just because of this Market.
Do not miss the opportunity to visit the Reading Terminal Market!

This market was awesome. I came in here looking for a good, authentic Philly Cheesesteak and found just the thing i was looking for. Carmens inside the Reading Terminal market was awesome. Friendly staff and an amzing cheesesteak! Highly recommended.
Dude this McDonald's is trash I went their 3 days ago to get a 6 mcnugget and only got 5. I will not go here again ill go to BURGUR king next time
Excellent shopping but you have to be ready to fight tourists who laze about and get in the way for fun.

I love this place! There are SO many options for food of any variety -- you will not leave hungry. You can also get produce and meats/seafood here too. I loved Sweet as Fudge (the Amish candy store, with lots of homemade chocolate candies), Beiler's Donuts (fresh hand-made donuts daily!), Dinic's (awesome roast pork sandwich). There's Mediterranean food, burgers, seafood, dessert stands, Asian cuisine, New Orleans cuisine, cheesesteaks, smoothies, and so much more. I thought the prices were also fairly reasonable! Plan to spend some time here at least during your initial visit just taking in all the sights and delicious smells! It can get crowded though, and sometimes there are big tour groups or school groups. I would recommend coming here earlier in the morning or later in the afternoon when it's not as busy.
This was a great spot in the middle of downtown Philly that is just a variety of different foods, vendors, different cultures are put together I had breakfast and lunch here everyday I was here.
I walk there almost daily. I enjoy quality products at reasonable prices

We stopped by here last night after a movie at the United Artist Theater (it's just a short walk).  Although it was busy, we were able to grab two bar seats.  Our bartender, Bob, gave us a rundown of the draft menu, which had roughly a dozen beers listed.  They also have a decent-sized cocktail list and dinner menu.

The main complaint that seems to be coming from people is that this place is pricey (and that their beloved bar that was previously housed here closed).  I honestly didn't think I was overcharged in any way.  I watched the guys behind the bar make dozens of cocktails for over two hours and they worked their tail off on each one.  They used fresh fruits, they didn't use crappy liquor, and there were no pre-made mixes.  I wouldn't knock back a lot of these given that their $10 a piece, but I think you get exactly what you pay for here: a drink that's made well with a decent amount of alcohol and no artificial puckers.

We got hungry about an hour in, so we ordered the wings and the whipped tofu.  The whipped tofu came with a bunch of homemade potato chips that had just the right amount of salt.  Tofu may not be your thing, but they somehow made it taste more like hummus than anything else.  I thought the wings had a nice, subtle spice to them and the glaze was addicting.  They are $12 a plate and you only get 9 or 10, but I've been to places that only give you 5 of them for this same price.  It was actually the perfect amount to split with someone, as well.  

All in all, our bill was $30 after drinking there for close to 3 hours.  I didn't feel like I was getting ripped off by any means and I left The Industry full and happy.  I enjoyed my time here last night and I'm definitely looking forward to coming back to try more of their food.

P.S. In the off-chance that anyone who works here reads this: the underside of your bar has some unfinished wood paneling that actually gave me two splinters last night.  I'm a klutz, but please consider sanding this down at some point.  Thanks.

I love Reading Terminal Market.  There are always numerous vendors each housing their own specialty good.  There are soaps shaped like seashells and halal chicken curry and produce and samples of Dutch country handmade candies and herbs for wholistic healing.  Almost every kind of store is there and it's a great place to go on a big day or when your friends or family are visiting from out of town.  The only thing is that it can get a bit crowded, so maybe go when you're in the mood for a bit of hustle and bustle.

Absolutely love this place! The pies are HUGE and the slices too! We got their special roasted corn with other poblano cream, pepperoni, and cheese and loved them all! If you order a whole pie, it takes about 30min to make. Definitely coming back for our next Pizza night!

I do love this place. It is definitely a "food park" as my daughters are fond of saying. I still for the life of me can't figure out the parking. We always take the train in, but always want to know where the parking is, and how much it is. This is a Philly Icon-- and for all you visitors saying it was "ok" on Sunday, are right. But note that the Amish stalls are closed on Sundays- this is their normal business practice. Beiler's Donuts, the Amish breakfast place, all of these are wonderful.

Food! Food! And More Fun!!! Seriously, its a place you must visit while in Philly! You name it they have it cooked and raw LOL! There are also lots of deserts (cheesecakes, cookies, banana pudding, etc.)

We came to reading terminal market for lunch. There are many options for eating and I got pretty overwhelmed! But, since it was Sunday, a good portion of the market was closed. Carmens was really crowded so we opted out. My parents got the sang kee roasted pork and duck rice special. They loved it! I got a savory turkey breast crepe with veggies and cheese. It was pretty good, a bit too salty though. My favorite part however, was the BASSETTS ICE CREAM! It's amazing. I got vanilla and even the most simple flavor was perfect. I hope to be back!

Awesome experience. Everything going is here. Good food. Good produce. Good beer. Good desert. This is a must experience. Parked right across from the Reading Terminal. I suggest you get your parking validated there when you purchase something. Suggest you try the Roast Pork sandwich with Broccoli Rabe at DINICS. A competitor to the Philly cheese steak.

This is my kind of place. Local foods, great choices, and fantastic taste. Dinic's roast pork is some of the most tender meat I've eaten. The melter skelter at meltkraft's was a phenomenal grilled cheese sandwich. Also ate a pretzel from mueller's. The best pretzel I've ever eaten. Must try the apple dumpling from the Dutch eating place and the donuts at beiler's. Banana creme was amazing! Check this place out if you like good, local food
My go to Pizza joint in Fishtown. Really tasty Pizza. Wish they delivered but glad they sick with quality then quantity.
Always love coming to the market! It's an experience! Everything offered at the market is DELISH! Be ready to stand in line but it's worth the wait!
I grocery shop at the Terminal all of the time!! I buy my meats from the Amish people, they have the best babyback ribs ever! I'm very selective about my lunch meats, the Terminal is the place to go!

I love the variety of foods here. They even have indian food in here! I haven't tried everything yet but there is so much food here and something for everyone. A place where you can try everything from different places. Not to mention they have that grocery right in there where you can pick up fresh fruits and veggies! Also a place to chill and sit and eat there too somewhere towards the mid and back of this complex. Public restroom in the back and if I'm not mistaken: a shoeshiner in the back somewhere?! oh and fresh juices and this Cajun and kabob place also looked great! I keep finding new things to wanna come back to try. I really didn't know what to try first sometimes! Oh did I also mention a buffet in there too?! lol.

Wandered through this amazing place very late in their day after arriving by train from DC. Purposely stayed in a hotel close by so we could scope this very famous market that opened originally in 1893. 

What a place. If you want anything food related they have it. We walked every aisle, pleased that it was near closing and we had plenty of room to roam. Bought a Tropical smoothly for $5.25 which took the edge off our hunger gathered up in the nearly two hour trip from DC. 

We will be checking it out again during the busy time and look forward to seeing the place humming with people.
This place is legendary and one of a kind. For those of you visiting Philadelphia, I highly recommend visiting this Philly landmark, which is walking distance from our beautiful city hall building.
What can I say? I'm a pizza connoisseur. This pizza was great. The crust nice and crispy. The sauce was so good. Pizza was hot and fresh. The customer service was excellent.

Any visitor to this fair city absolutely must visit Reading Terminal Market. I have my own little routine, places to go, delicacies to enjoy and I suggest you establish your own if you plan on going regularly. Generally I start with dumpling soup, work my way over to roasted chicken wings, lots in-between before rounding it out with a cannoli. Go forth and enjoy.

Great place. All kinds of good food. Amish market and sea food, all kinds of other varieties. Downfall it's crowded and expensive. Amish make great food. Definitely worth the trip down there. I go once a month at least.

This is a must for tourists. So many great places to check out. I love the Greek place with the blue and white bar(it's the best gyro in the city). DiNicks is awesome, I get the pork sammy with sharp provolone and broccoli rabe. Try the trainwreck sandwich.. you may have a heart attack after but it's worth  a try.
I challenge you to find a better local place with more selection of food and fresh groceries. The prices are fair, too.

This place is just too much fun! Flowers, fresh veggies and meat, candy and more places to eat with different types of food than you can shake a stick at.  They don't stay open late (the diner does I think) and they are best to visit for breakfast and lunch.  It can and does get crowded in there.

Can't recall the name of the place but we had breakfast sandwiches on a pretzel that was just too tasty.  And the Amish pastries - OH M GEE!!!!  If you are in Philly you have to go visit this place and enjoy yourself.

This is the second time I've been forced to fly united and consequently, come to green leaf's. Both times the staff have been complete and total pros. Relaxed, chatty, smiling... And the rarest Philadelphia retail animal...happy. Seriously, id pay more any day just for human beings like these to wait on me in a restaurant. Kudos to management for creating what must be a pleasant work environment...or maybe they're just naturally pleasant! Plus my smoothies were good too.

Yummy Filipino food. For 35$ we were able to try a little bit of everything family style. I took one star off because the chicken adobo was on the dry side. Overall, I would recommend this place to those to come here who never had Filipino food.

This is my absolute favorite place in the whole of Philadelphia!!!

I'm the Queen of Fruits & Vegetables and this is my favorite place to do produce shopping. There are two stores selling that and the produce are aplenty, varied, fresh and cheap! And if you show your Student ID, you get a 10% discount - i love student discounts and merchants who offer that! =D

And soooo many kinds of food sold here - lump crab cakes and shrimp pad thai from the Thai store are good. Everything I've had here are good, quality for the money. And I think Reading Terminal Market does such a terrific job at maintaining the market clean and customer-friendly. The bathrooms are clean too. And there are plenty of seats available for people to eat and share their food. Great place to bring your family to. And I really like its location, right in the center of the city and so near Chinatown.

I LOVE Reading Terminal Market!
Love the hustle and bustle of the Market.  Good food and great atmosphere.

If you haven't been in a while , 2 new things to try!  Beiler Donuts.  They are worth every single calorie.  After these no other donut will be worth the effort!!!!   Valley Shepherd for all things cheese and things that go with cheese. Grilled cheese then donut for dessert.  You can't go wrong.
Amazing food. Great for a Quick bite. Price inexpensive. Will come back over and over agin

Such a great market to check out.  Everything you need is there under one roof.    Even if you don't buy a thing, just the atmosphere and all the different places with all the choices  is just insane.  Check it out and you won't be disappointed. 

All the best,
Tod

not sure why you would ever go to  whole foods in philadelphia. you really can't beat iovines prices for produce, and between giunta's prime shop and godshall's you have a mountain of high quality and reasonably priced meats and poultry to choose from. did I mention martin's? another great butcher with a huge selection of freshly made sausage including legit english style bangers, usual italian varieties, and more. Salumeria is your stop for cheeses and cured meats like pancetta, or a mouthwatering hoagie. Fair Food Farmstand is generally pretty overpriced (13.99 a lb for garlic? I don't care if its organic that is outrageous) but I don't know where else to get raw milk and I refuse to drink pasteurized if I can help it. Head Nut is pretty awesome, a small fairly new bulk spice and nut shop that has quite a bit of variety. Love that you can buy very small amounts of spices (whole or preground) here as they have quantity/price stages, and the best part is that it's CHEAP. Don't be suckered into buying one of those tiny 8 dollar spice grinders from Jonathan Best; go to Head Nut. Thai Kitchen has a lot of asian ingredients for sale like holy basil and fish sauce, and their cheap thai curries aren't too bad either.

There are of course many food stands, which range from okay to good, but those can be a bit tourist trappy and expensive. Places definitely not to miss: DiNic's (overpriced but still a damn great roast pork sandwich, go early though they have a tendency to run out of broccoli rabe), the Rib Stand, Smucker's Grill (absolute best breakfast sandwiches right here, get the scrapple egg and cheese, you'll thank me later. Or walk to the other side of the counter and buy some scrapple to take home, seriously, it's the best scrapple I've ever had.), Miller's Twist (sorry philly pretzels, you just got your ass kicked), Beck's for delicious po'boys, get the fried oyster, Herschel's for an awesome (but expensive) reuben or pastrami special on challah.

I would not reccomend down home diner, not sure why people seem to love it, the couple times ive eaten there the food was just sloppy and in one case I got regular (frozen) fries instead of the sweet potato fries that were supposed to come with my sandwich. Seriously just go to midtown II on 11th and sansom if you want a diner experience that badly. The Dutch Eating Place does a pretty tasty burger, but the fries were really disappointing. Fresh cut but soggy and oily, not crispy at all. 

Personally I don't go to many of the restaurants any more, I'm reviewing RTM as a place to get your grocery shopping done, and on those terms you really can't beat it for the price and quality in center city.

One side note and why i knock off a star, the fishmongers don't appear that great to me in terms of freshness and price. Maybe their fish is fresher in the mornings, but I'd rather go down to Ippolito's for cheaper seafood that I KNOW is fresh. this just an observation based on sight I have not bought any fish from RTM so maybe I am wrong.

Overall it's a great place to do grocery shopping or grab a bite to eat if you don't mind the overpriced-ness of the food stands, stop going to Whole Paycheck, go to the Reading Terminal Market.

I loveeeeeeeeee this place!

When I get there, I never want to leave.  It makes me sad that I can't buy certain things because I am just visiting, but all the meat, produce and seafood look so fresh and delicious.

There is such a variety of food in there.. it is hard to choose what you want to eat.  But it's great to know you have so many choices to choose from.  Definite go-to spot is Tommy's Dinic's.  Roast pork, broccoli rabe, and sharp provolone.  Better than a Philly cheesesteak!

Was here on a Monday night around 5 and a lot of shops were already closed.  Including DiNic's. - insert sad face here-

This place is awesome - hands down! Can't to visit the market again when I am in town! The "Old City" coffee was reasonably priced and the taste was great! Also visit the doughnut  please and ate the best doughnut I ever tasted and DeNik's - just excellent!!!

This place is great!  All kinds of food choices for everybody.  Parking can be tough and it can get a little crowded. If you're walking around the area it's an excellent place to stop and have a quick bite to eat with a huge selection.  But every time I go there I end up walking around looking at all the awesomeness.  Parking sucks

I don't have enough proper adjectives to describe my deep and unabashed love for all that is Reading Terminal Market. 

It holds some of my favorite booths and most delicious eats. Whenever we are within a five mile radius my husband suddenly gets hungry and has an urge to "just pop in and look around". 

Basically, if you have not had breakfast from the Dutch Eating Place, you are not really living your best life. Now get to it!
Bustling atmosphere, great place to shop whole fish, fudge, honey, and tons of places to eat!

I love Reading Terminal Market. I like that you can get all sorts of great food, prepared and raw. I love that there is a piano. I love that there are tourists and locals alike all enjoying the atmosphere. I love that there are cannolis next to shrimp.

The only real problem with Reading Terminal is totally unavoidable. On a day/weekend with the convention center is in use it can be very difficult to get anything. So much of the fun of Reading Terminal is wandering around, and on a day when its overly crowded, it ruins probably my favorite part of the experience. On an Empty day 5 stars.

Great for a quick, relatively large and tasty Kati roll. Got the chicken masala and lamb rolls, both of which were good and came with a wickedly spice sauce (on the side) which I also liked. Mango lassi was smooth and creamy, wish there were a bit more. Very friendly service and no lines to wait in usually. Will hopefully take advantage of the late hours soon!

Preface: I went to Reading Terminal Market on a Saturday at noon during the weekend of the international flower show (which was down the road) AND St. Patrick's day. It goes without saying that this triple whammy made for a very crowded and chaotic experience. There was barely room to move and navigating between stalls may have involved the tactful use of elbows. 

Now, aside from the crowds, Reading Terminal is AMAZING. Craving something? Reading Terminal probably has it. There's an incredible selection and most things are very well priced so come hungry! We were only able to hit three places before getting full. 

12th Street Cantina- Veggie Quesadilla with chips and guacamole. The veggie quesadilla was great and the guacamole was sublime. You can tell that it is made fresh. Don't forget the napkins because eating this can get messy! Overall, I was very happy with my selection. 

Indian place that starts with an N (totally forgot the name)- only grabbed a potato samosa here but they have many of your typical Indian food options. The samosa was bland and disappointing. It was also wrapped in puff pastry vs the usual samosa shell which would've been okay had the filling been more flavorful. 

Meltkraft- I love grilled cheese. Meltkraft has sooo many options from the filling to what fat to grill your sandwich in (duck fat? Truffle oil? Garlic rub?) We decided to get the basic grilled cheese with added jalapeños. The cheese itself was very very good but after grilling the sandwich was a bit oily. I also would've liked more jalapeños in the grilled cheese. Almost an entire half of my sandwich was jalapeño-less. But the cheese was on fleek
Hit and miss. Stay away from some dodgy Asian food dealers. Great fruit and veg. Very touristy. Watch out for pickpockets. -- Hotspur
It's a nice place to visit during the week, but on weekends can be a bit crowded. The food is always fresh.

The Terminal Market is a fascinating place offering virtually every type of food and beverage one can imagine pus many other items.  It is only open until 6:00 p. m. each day, which is a drawback.  Many of the items are expensive, but they are generally top notch.  The problem is the atmosphere: it is extremely busy, loud, and it is frequented by panhandlers who operate within the facility despite signs prohibiting the conduct.  It is no wonder that there seems to always be a large police presence in the market and not only for the officers to dine. Seating for diners is not comfortable and one is likely to be seated very close to others.  There are few sit-down restaurants; the diner generally orders at the counter and waits for their food to be served.  At By George, a fine Italian restaurant at the market, I was not permitted to buy a pizza that was on display.  I had to wait for a new one to be prepared.

Seriously laim Airport food...

Make sure to ask for a receipt... They will not openly offer one.
I love the variety at Reading Terminal Market! They have everything you could ever want to eat there!

Great place! Just went there for the first time on Friday after visiting someone in CHOP, location is great and the food is great comfort food. Bread is great, warm and sandwich is loaded. Not a long wait, service is polite and helpful....I guess my only complaint was that the menu was a little confusing, but the staff was willing and able to help. Liked the way the place was decorated, clean and warm.

GO! I dream about the pretzels and donuts
I ate here while in the city visiting my sister. What I would give for one of those pretzels right now!!

Also, we saw Usher walking around the market while we were there! Such a Fun spot.

If I could give this place ten stars, I would. This is a foodie's heaven - I would honestly consider moving to Philly just for this place!

My friend and I only budgeted two and a half hours for this place, and since having nine stomachs is not a reality for human beings, we decided to hit up only a few, select places (yes, this was a strategic operation).

Brunch at Dinic's- got the Italian pulled pork sub, which was great (not too salty), but heard the roast pork was even better, so maybe next time I'll try that.

We snagged a taste of some deli meats at the stand next to Carmen's, and I was half-tempted to pretend being a hobbit and have a second lunch...

Bassett's icecream is a must-have dessert. Amish icecream - can't pass up the creaminess that's actually not heavy but quite refreshing. :)

We also had pretzels from Miller's. Do yourself a favor and get one when it's piping hot...I feel like the Amish have the hand of Midas, figuratively-speaking. Everything they touch tastes so much more amazing than your average food items!

There are two cookie stands. Both are good, but I personally go against the grain and say the ones from Famous 4th Street's are better than Hope's. At least, if you're going for less decadent and less butter. If you like the sweet, heavy, buttery goodness, go with Hope's. (Or do what I did and get both and compare).

You can get fun souvenirs at Chocollate by Mueller - anatomically correct hearts, lungs, pancreas, etc. and chocolate-covered...onions. I was too weirded out to get that, but it would make a great passive aggressive gift. ;)

Finally, swing back in the late afternoon - all the produce prices drop to ONE DOLLAR. I got an entire cantaloupe for $1, and strawberries by the pound for $1. Such a steal...and don't forget the fresh milk and yoghurt - these are as local as you can get!

Dinner: Carmen's Philly cheese, hands down. No whiz though - whiz looks narsty (and I know I'll likely get crucified for saying that, but go for the provolone). President Obama came here! I can trust that recommendation haha.
Love this place and a must visit in Philly. We visited DiNic for their sandwiches: Italian pull pork and brisket. The place was crowded but it is such a great environment with courteous folks.
Gets crowded but the food in here during lunch is awesome.  There are so many choices in and you can get pretty much anything you want!  Very cool place if your downtown philly and in a  hurry
Everything but rutabega exists here.  That means it has everything you would need for a full shopping trip or a quick bite.  Beware of crowds -- it being packed is a good sign though.

We got extra awesome food at extra low prices, but I could only put up with the crowded chaos for so long before I needed some fresh air.  Luckily, residents of Philly seem to be much better in crowds than Bostonians - people actually apologized as they ran into you!  

At any rate, I loved coming here as a tourist, but didn't want to spend too terribly long here once I had my groceries in tow.
WOW! There is a lot going on here.  If you're in Philly be sure to check this place out.  They have just about something for everyone's taste here.....

Service is take it or leave it , not very warm or welcoming . All that attitude and the   pizza is super average. This pizza is the best if you're 5 feet away from this place. Crust has a nice crispy crew , light airy bread taste , but dry dry dry , absolutely no hint of sauce  . This is  what you call an unbalanced pizza slice  .

During my busy season at work, I usually get Humpty's delivery every Wednesday when they do the dollar dumpling deal for Hump-day. I've only ever gotten the fried dumplings and they are packed to the brim and very filling. Prefer their savory options over the dessert dumplings, since those can be hit or miss (although they just put carrot cake in the rotation and that one is solid). Asian pork and broccoli cheddar are my favorites.
Really fun place to visit. Lots to see. Food! Food! Food! Great place to get gifts for any holiday or special occasion. Lots to try. Seating can be a bit of a search but worth the effort.

I went to Honey Grow for the first time around two months ago and quickly became addicted.  I love stir fry and I started making it a weekly tradition.  By and large I've had good experiences here and the food has been delicious.  

Last night I went by and ordered my normal wheat noodles and chicken stir fry to go and later when I was eating it at home I noticed a large number of small white hairs in my food.  I have a beard so I thought maybe it was me, but no, these small white hairs were consistent from top to bottom in my to go bowl.  I'm not sure where these hairs came from, although I'm certain it didn't come from the staff that prepared my food.  

It might have come from the actual chicken, like sometimes you find on a chicken wing, but there was a lot of them littered throughout my stir fry to the point where I couldn't eat it.  I'm not trying to exaggerate, I picked out at least a dozens before I gave up and dumped the food.  This has never happened to me before at Honey Grow, but now it's got me wondering if I'd ever be willing to go back.
How can you not like a place that from door to door the smell is yummy.  General Store, Steaks and fresh food ... they are the best
It's worth it just to get the Basset's ice cream.  Go early on a Saturday and you will have the place to yourself (almost).

This place is AWESOME. My friend (who lives in Philly) suggested I go check it out my first night in town visiting for a work trip, so I figured I'd learn about using public transportation and get myself there. I went inside and it was about 3 p.m. - and just about everybody was getting ready for the post-work rush (read: not much was happening). So I walked outside and through the streets out to see Independence Square and some of the historic buildings, which were just a few blocks up the road from it. I returned closer to 5 p.m. and it was hustling and bustling. Whether you are grabbing fresh produce or a few staples for dinner, or planning to sit down and eat dinner, Terminal Market offers an extremely impressive selection of foods, both locally and from around the world. I stopped at the German place and had a schnitzel sammie for dinner, plus bought some genuine German cookies to bring back home. There is a bar on site and plenty of places to grab food and a seat. Very cool experience that I'm glad I did!
I haven't tried the rolls. The platter was just ok. Nothing really special about it but it was pretty good. The staff was very nice and the price is worth coming back :)

I love this place! On both of my trips to NYC from the west coast, I had to take the 2-hour bus ride to Philly to visit Reading Terminal Market. There is so much to eat, buy, and see here.

During the winter, there's not much to do outdoors. After visiting Love Park, my friends and I spent a couple hours at the market. It's warm inside and there is so much to explore. During the fall, there's much more to do and see outdoors, but I still spent at least 2 hours here. It's a great place to find things to take home with you - everything in one place.

I highly recommend trying the hand-rolled donuts!!! I should have bought 5 dozens when I was there...no joke. Sang Kee Duck House is also delicious.

Tried the special today. "Tabaching" consisted of garlic fried rice, 3 fried egg rolls, bbq chicken, bbq pork, lumpiang sariwa for $15. Overall, it tasted fine. 
The bbq lacked the traditional flavor of pork or chicken Philippine bbq. Maybe it need to be marinated longer. It was a little dry too. The egg roll was good but needs a different tasting dipping sauce. The sariwa has different vegetables than the traditional sariwa so expect something different so you're not comparing. The garlic rice was flavorful but kind of dry . It seemed some rice grains were hard or not fully cooked. Also, $4.50 is steep for canned juices and $4 bottled soda. 

PS . The Filipino barrel man should be glued to the base. Filipinos will get it but could be very offensive to other cultures and tourists once the whimsical of it is discovered.
I like reading terminal for great fruits and veggies and fresh spices, but I'm not a fan of the crowds. Go during the week or when there isn't a convention in town.

This place is amazing!!! Its a foodie heaven. It combines a flea Market like experience with a food court and farmers market feel. So many choices for things to eat. Seafood, deli meats, asian cuisine, pastries.  Take your pick and come hungry.
Best place in town to get food! Especially if your with other people that want to eat something different than you!! For travelers and tourists this is a Philly must do!!

OMG. Have I died and gone to food heaven???

Jessica White states it perfectly in her article "Best of Reading Terminal Market":

"History junkies have the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall, art enthusiasts have the Philadelphia Museum of Art and animal lovers have America's first zoo. Food connoisseurs, who eat as a pastime and not just for sustenance, have Reading Terminal Market, Philadelphia's historic and iconic food hall. Boasting over 80 merchants selling Amish specialties, fresh produce, charcuterie, cheese, confections, etc. (the list is endless), this bustling market overwhelms even the most adept food shopper. Street scoped out the extensive offerings, feasting on the best grub -- from the gourmet to the greasy. Whether you have 30 minutes or three hours, check out the best of Reading Terminal Market."

I ordered the longsilong (sausage over rice) and it was delicious! Who knew rice could be soooo amazing - it was wonderfully flavored with garlic and I couldn't get enough of it. Also got the lumpias, which my daughter and I loved! Toddler and mom approved!

We absolutely LOVE coming here every time we are visiting Philadelphia. They have soooo many delicious food and dessert options! Yum Yum Yum!
They also have excellent produce, meat and seafood options. A lot of local vendors selling merchandise as well. A definite spot to visit for sure!
My favorite place to by foodstuffs in Philly. Go during off hours (weekdays not during lunch) for the best experience.

Choices.  Thousands of choices to delight any foodie.  We love shopping here and eating here.  Parking in the garage across the street is the way to go.  Get your parking ticket validated and it's only $4.00.  The Mennonite/Amish places have different hours than the rest of the RTM, so check before you rush down to get a Beiler's doughnut on a Monday.  This is one of my favorite places in the city and it's constantly evolving and changing for the better.

What cant you say about this place. They have everything!!!! Cookies, Cakes, Coffees, Honey, Cheesesteaks, gifts, fresh fish, raw meats, veggies, etc. They have it all in one location. We love getting items from here. Try to avoid lunch time as they are really busy.

This is a great place for a goodie, lots of food stuffed into a small space. If you are in Philly you will definitely want to stop by and check it out. Every type of food and produce market. This place is always busy so there is no special time that would be best, just go when you are hungry
The Reading Terminal Market is like a Mecca for food. If you are a bipedal omnivore you must visit this place, and consume.
You can find anything you want here! Love getting fresh chicken breast from the Amish vendors, you won't regret it.  Fresh mozzarella cheese is a must also!

I got the Paneer Masala & Beef Tikka for take out the other day. I added an egg to both rolls and while both were delicious, the Paneer Masala was AMAZING. I will definitely be going back for it - it's one of those foods that you can't stop thinking about. The beef in the Beef Tikka was slightly chewy and it had a good spicy kick to it without being overbearing. I highly recommend this place to anyone that likes Indian food. I will definitely be trying out other items on the menu in the near future.

WHAT-A-MESS!!!! This location is fairly new. You'd think the staff would care about its upkeep. Clearly that's not the case. I went in this evening to grab some grub. Worst burrito I've ever had by the way.. Mainly because it wasn't properly made. All the meat was at one end of the burrito, while the rice and sour cream were at the other end. But that was the least of my worries. The floor by the drink machine had a HUGE spill which sat there the entire time of my visit. I dined in so I was there for at least 25 minutes. Every single eating surface (tables and counters) were covered in food people left behind. Again, not cleaned once in the time I was there. The trash can was over flowing. Full beyond its limit, spilled onto the floor, matter of fact, we had no choice but to leave our tray on the tray return with our trash still on it because there was no where else to put it!! The most annoying part of this was, two employees were on breaks, sitting and eating. I personally have never worked in the food industry, but if that were my place of employment, I would take the 5 minute cut into my break, to quick clean and sanitize the table tops and wipe up a puddle. Otherwise, you're pretty much asking for a slip and fall lawsuit.
Hope management isn't surprised when the time comes. This establishment needs to get their act together.
Being from Boston this indoor market is nothing new. I have been to a few in my life but this was the best. Massive with the best shops I have ever seen. The smell of food will make you very hungry.

I have to admit, at first I was skeptical because of some previous reviews...
This place totally blew me out of the water.

First off, this neighborhood NEEDED a place like this!!!! The food was A-MA-ZING.
We had the general tso's wings and chichironne to start. The wings were crispy, meaty and full of flavor. The chichironne...I mean, what else can I say...I love pork.
I had the tartar and he had a double industry burger...tartar was full of pickley, capers goodness with home made chips and the burger came out perfectly cooked.
I am not a huge dessert person, BUT I went out on a limb and got the doughnuts...YOU MUST TRY THEM!!!! They texture was perfect...light and fluffy on the inside, they smelled like funnel cake and that marmalade that comes with it was this perfect mix of red berry and citrus. I will definitely be back!

Update!

This location did reach out to me and ended up providing me a free meal. The difference was extremely noticeable and pleasant! As you can see from the picture, the sandwich is much larger as what I've always been used to in the past. The service and speed was still great as well. Love a company that can might things right with their customers. 

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Let me start by saying Chick-Fil-A if one of my favorite fast food restaurants. 

This is my first time trying this location and I was greatly disappointed with the quality of the sandwich. The chicken itself was extremely thin and fairly dry. There were a few bites where I only got the breading/skin. See picture below. 

The order did come fast, 30 seconds tops but may have been pre-made and sitting there. I've been the many other Chick-fil-A's which always delivered sizeable and juicy sandwiches which was why I was hooked. 

The fries however, was a good portion and the staff was OK. Maybe this was just an off day?

A great experience and highly recommended when visiting Philadelphia. Make sure you bring your appetite too. There are great breakfast & lunch spots here! The Crepe place is excellent and Di-Nico's makes a fantastic rendition of the Philly cheese steak but uses pork. I thought it was better than both Pat's & Gino's cheese steaks by far!

A perfect way to spend a weekends day. You may loose track of time walking from booth to booth but it's certainly time well spent. The vendors goods are everything and anything you could ever imagine, from handmade soaps to absolutely delicious lunch. There is something for everybody when spending your time at the market.

Love shopping for groceries here. I can always find the veggies I want. 
Nice fish and seafood and meat too!
Like the deli counters

I'm going against the group here. 3 stars for Reading Terminal Market. This used to be an old railroad station. Reading Railroad(bonus points for Monopoly nostalgia). If you're not hungry, at least go in to check it out for historical purposes.

After closing the train service, what better thing to replace it with than food? All of the food! I think you should at least visit this place once, but other than that... don't waste your time with multiple visits. 

When you walk in, it can be overwhelming. Tons of people. If there's one thing that's dangerous.. it's hungry people all in one place around dozens of food options. Options include: Asian, ribs, desserts, tacos, oyster bar, a buffet, burgers, sandwiches, produce, seafood, and that's barely touching the surface of all you can order here. 

I ended up ordering a beef brisket sandwich(with green peppers and provolone). I also had a tamale. The tamale was delicious. The brisket sandwich was mediocre. It was tasty, but overall the brisket was dry. It did help that they put sweet or hot sauce on it(your choice), but even with that it was still too dry. Don't try to cover up your dry meat with sauce and then be conservative with the sauce. 

This was one of the first places we visited. As we explored Philly over the coming weekend, every new place we went I became more annoyed that we went to Reading Terminal. With tons of places in Philly to eat, the Reading Terminal is mediocre.
Don't wanna go there anymore!   I'd rather go to China town.  Cheesesteak was so so. Don't really like it. Fried chicken,  not good.  Crepe,  no!

How could you give this place less than five stars. This is one of the best markets I have been to aside from my beloved Eastern Market. Of course it is going to be crowded and full of tourists, but there's nothing you can do about it except have some good eats!

If you haven't visited the Reading Terminal Market, your trip to Philadelphia is not complete. Food for every taste from cheese steaks to corned beef sandwiches worthy of a good NYC deli. Famous Chocolate Chip cookies! Bassets ice cream! Fresh fish, produce, meat, veggies, etc.
Best in the Nation if not the world.  And you can there which helps you avoid over shopping.
I looove the Terminal!!! I buy my lunch meats, seafood, poultry and variety of meats from the Amish people. I'm always there, I'll never shop no other place for my meats
We went here for breakfast!! YUMMY! Oh boy! It was a bit of a wait, but those pancakes and eggs were well worth it!

The Reading Terminal Market is quintessential Philly.  If you are a tourist, don't miss it.  If you are local, don't miss out!! My first year I avoided RTM because I felt so overwhelmed by the crowds, but then I happened to wander in on an off time & discovered the magic of feeling like the place is all yours for the taking! My favorite shops include Iovine's Produce, 12th St Cantina, La Divisa Meats, DiNIc's, & Beiler's Donuts [do not miss out on these, whatever you do!].  Philadelphia is lucky to have a gem like RTM; I always look forward to the weekend events they put on, for example, today is Bacon Fest if I remember correctly!

Example: You guys are goood. Let's take some food service Philly Steak, deep fry it like it's an egg roll and then call it a dumpling. THEN, let's make Chinese Pork Alfredo, slap it all in a box only Chris Tucker would love and then send this mess to someone you should'nt have. Long live the trust fund hipster turned yupster fund on this crap.
I love reading terminal market! I always bring guests here when they visit Philly! I just wish they were open later.
Cheesesteak dumplings?? I was thrilled to learn that this exists and so excited to try them. They lived up to the hype for me.
I could spend a day here just walking around -- the hustle bustle of Christmas is amazing and the smells and sights are worth all the crowds you encounter.
As far as fast food goes it was pretty good. Good sandwich, fast service. Nearby neighborhood is a little sketchy looking but it's not bad
Food delicious always crowded but well worth it. Love the meat market section and the soup food is to die for. The bakery is my fav as well

Local eats and fantastic quality all around. The RTM is very community-oriented and tons of shops and boutiques to select from. Dozens of favorites from DiNics to The Herbiary to Old City Coffee! Tons of history and within walking distance to most things

My all time place to go when I'm in center city . Reading Terminal have a variety of foods to choose from and also they have fresh fruits, vegetables, flowers and other scrumptious things you can't help to buy when you are at the Terminal !

This place is great! You can pretty much get anything you want! There are pastries, meats, sea food, produce, Mexican food, sandwiches, wine, candy, grilled cheese, coffee, etc - you name it, they most likely have it! It's a melting pot in the middle of the city. Beware: it gets VERY crowded at lunch time!!! Also, they validate parking for 2 local parking garages, making it only $4 to park! Check it out :)
Yummy! The Kati rolls here are incredible - packed with flavor. I love the masala pepperwala (lol) roll and the masala chicken roll. They have vegetarian options as well. Excellent for a quick bite.

So if you know me, you know I'm always bitching about food in America, specifically groceries in America. I think our grocery stores are depressing at best. I want to cry when I walk into certain grocery stores (*cough* SuperFresh) and pay way too much for limp "veggies" I wouldn't feed my llama and grey "meat" I wouldn't feed my dog, or that over processed crap that looks and tastes like a sawdust/toilet paper hybrid. I also don't enjoy paying $6 for an apple, WHOLE FOODS. UGH.

This is why I love Reading Terminal. In most other countries in the world, you buy FRESH, LOCAL food from MARKETS. And you don't spend your whole paycheck on it!!! This place is our answer to that. 

Reading Terminal is a brilliant indoor market in a really cool, historic building, just blocks from Chinatown, Old City, the Convention Center, and Center City. It's my go-to place to buy veggies (from Iovine's), lunch meat (from Reihl's Deli), and various meat and fish from the butchers scattered throughout. 

The prices are cheap. The produce is  fresh. What's not to love?! 

OH!!!!! And did I mention, it's like a giant food court, with plenty of vendors selling everything from sushi, Thai, and Chinese, to Middle Eastern pastries, Cajun, and Italian (that pizza place across from Iovine's makes the best meat balls and mediterranean pizza! HUGE lunch for $6.)?? There are several bakeries, including an Amish bakery and Le Bus. I worked 2 blocks away for a year, and I would almost always get lunch or breakfast in Reading Terminal. Whatever you're in the mood for, you can find it here!! 

A lot of the places in there are Amish owned and operated so you get some great, homecooked food and local produce without driving down to Lancaster. There are also cool little shops like the honey store and the wine shop that sell various trinkets.
Love it!  Never leave there hungry but the choices are way too many-I end up spending too much and bringing it home.

Reading Terminal Market is an amazing indoor marketplace chock full of grocers, bakeries, delis, and other ready-to-eat restaurants. I came on a Saturday and the place was packed. It's a bit gritty - not very polished or cozy - but I suppose that's part of the charm. There are countless options for a little snack, a sweet treat, or an entire meal, so you're sure to find something to satisfy. Definitely give it a visit if you're in the neighborhood and have the hangries - or just want to check out a very cool Philly institution.

The atmosphere is terrific and the prices are competitive towards what you might find in a regular market.  Depending on the time that you go though I am a little concerned about the increased presence of the homeless constantly begging as my wife has been there along with our daughter several times and they have gotten a little too close to her for my taste when we go as a family though we do enjoy the experience

We were visiting Philly for the weekend and we wanted to get something we normally do not eat. We heard of Humpty's and checked Yelp and we had to come. This restaurant is a must whether you are visiting or live in Philly. The restaurant has a very modern but homey feel.
We ordered a good mix of dumplings. We ordered 5 different ones. My favorite was Cheesesteak,  the spinach and cheese, and the edamame. 
They are the perfect size to eat as a snack which is what we did or have as a meal. They also have vegan options, I believe.
They also have a dessert option as well. It was pumpkin pie, but I was so full that I couldn't get another one . 
I highly suggest going to the restaurant and just getting at least one of each.

My favorite place to go to market! I absolutely love the crepes, Beiler's doughnuts, the flying monkey and old city coffee! I love the atmosphere of the market and the variety of things they have to choose from! I bought squid ink noodles from one of the vendors and they were excellent! Absolutely love this place and is a must go every time I go to Philadelphia!

Owner was cool. He let me order early since I came before the store opened. The ambiance is cozy and simple.

The starberry cheesecake dumpling, as weird as it sounds, was surprisingly good. Definitely coming back for it again.

The savory dumplings were OK. The flavors were very Philly. I had cheesesteak, edamami, and Asian pork. Interesting to try but it pales in comparison to traditional Chinese dumplings.

5  service
4  food
4  environment

Love this place! You have a range of food options as well as grocery items to choose from. 

No words to describe how much I love Reading Terminal Market.

This is my second visit to Philadelphia, and my second visit to the Reading Terminal Market. Decided to branch out from cheesesteaks and try MeltKraft grilled cheese -- so glad I did! The sandwiches are delish, and the staff were incredibly friendly. They even pointed me to various other foodie places around town. Five stars in general for the market, and especially for MeltKraft!

So this place is awesome.  It's right next to the convention center.  I was looking for a vegetarian option and there were enough options for me to choose from.

They have a donut place here that people are raving about.  I will come back to try that another time!
Great market place always busy if you're in that. I am not, which is why I gave four stars. Enjoy!
Very overwhelming but a great place to find anything you are craving! Loved the gluten free options and anything from dessert to breakfast to dinner, all day!

A Philadelphia tourist trap for many years and counting.   The Amish Markets and stands are good but the other locations are subpar at best.   Many of the customers are from out of town as there are convention centers nearby,  therefore most of the stands don't really care about customer service.   I recommend the Dutch Eatery for breakfast,  they are very good and Amish run so they do care about things like customer service.
Check out helpful tips, reviews, recipes and events in Philadelphia at website www.healthyPHILLY.com

Good options are good, I will give them 8 out of a 10 scale.  The food quality varies so you might need to see what others are ordering before you start. Overall it is a good place to get a sense of Philly foods.

My first trip to The Reading Terminal Market was back in 1952 when I was four. My mother took me there for my first Bassett's ice cream cone, and from then on, there was no turning back. I've had a long term love affair with the Reading Terminal ever since. 
Naturally, I also have hundreds of wonderful things to say about the Market, but I hardly know where to begin. Well, let's try this... The Amish part of the Market is always a real treat! Talk about some good old fashion cookin'! Wowee!  And then there's... Scrapple sandwiches, maple bacon donuts, FAB Philly pretzels, and at DiNic's, there's their famous Roast Beef and Pork sandwich, the winner of best sandwich in America!!!  
Seriously, if the angels made sandwiches, they would taste like this one at DiNic's.
So... if you come into the city for a visit, or you work in Center City, take the time to make The Reading Terminal Market a part of your day in Philly.  
It's more than just an indoor market and eatery - it's an Experience! 
Ya gotta go.

This place has everything anyone could ask for. Great selection of food and drinks from many different vendors. I have came here for a quick lunch and also to buy my weekly meats and vegetables. Highly recommend the cheese shop in the back and the gumbo in the food court area!

I only tried the Lumpia Shanghai (egg roll with pork) and the mango nectar. The mango nectar in a can is what it should taste. The Lumpia on the other hand was a little different for me with the sweet chili sauce. I'm originally from Jersey City, NJ / NYC and the Filipino food around that area is exceptionally delicious and not as expensive as this restaurant. I could give LALO another go another time when I head to Old City again.

Every time I come here I get so overwhelmed. There is so much to choose from. This really is a unique place in Philadelphia that I recommend any tourist or local visit.  I have eaten at several locations inside and my favorite is Pearls Oyster House. They have the best chowder and fried flounder. I would frequent this place if it were in walking distance.

I'm not sure what there is to say that hasn't already been said.  If you are visiting from out of town, this experience is a Philadelphia must.  Aside from weathering crowds, there is nothing not to like.

There are 2 reasons why I fly to Philadelphia International Airport versus Newark Airport when going back East.

1. Cost: Savings of up to $100-200 per ticket 
2. Reading Terminal Market:

Definitely not one of the largest markets in the nation, but sometimes less is more. There are some "hot spots" that were featured on Man vs Food and the Travel Channel's named DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef "Best Sandwich in America" and Beiler's Bakery are my absolute favorite to dine at.

I can see why DiNic's sandwiches was honored that award. I had the roast beef with peppers, provolone, and broccoli rabe that was an excellent sandwich. This sandwich used simple ingredients with the right balance of flavor and the freshness that you can taste and see.

This market definitely made my criteria as one of my all time favorite markets to visit. Don't let the size fool you. It may be small but the cultural diversity of merchants, activities offered (check their calendar), and location in downtown Philadelphia puts this on top of my list. Chinatown is ONLY a walking distance away!

TIP: $4 parking fee for 2 hrs with $10 purchase and validation for a quick bite.

I don't even want to give them 1 star. I have been to a lot quick airport restaurants but this is the worst. First off the location of where the order line starts is confusing. When u do place an simple order the staff seems confused. As u watch and wait there seems to be a lot of chaos. Employees shouting out completed orders. Past customers coming back to get their orders corrected. When I got my ham, egg croissant sand which it was missing the Ham. They included cheese which I ordered no cheese. Management seriously need to a hard look at this place and reorganize it.

Wonderful place! The atmosphere is very enthralling. 
Foods and smells are everywhere. I love the Dutch corner place, it's really good. They have some sandwiches and desserts you should try. I tried the pretzel shop and it was awesome as well.

This is a quirky "food court" with lots and lots of places to choose from.  In fact, it's too popular, as the crowds descend on the place at 1130 and it's PACKED from that point on.  It's hard to find seating, though some places have carved out little areas of their own.  There are many, many wonderful choices, including Philly Cheese steak (Sabatoro's) which was average -- double provolone with fried onions and jalapeños.  Melt Kraft, where my daughter got a really good grilled cheese and bacon - the bacon was crispy and the bread was big - so that the Gruyere and Cheddar didn't overwhelm.  Again seating is problematic, and it gets a bit wearisome, otherwise I'd have rated it a 5, as I love the quirky and nooks and crannies.

From fresh ingredients to fully cooked food, this is the place you get it all. You have all the options in the world to pick from. Be advised that the popular joints have a line and its going to be a wait, but so totally worth it.
Great variety of food which tastes good just a little pricey and it stays pretty crowded.

Overwhelming and packed with people.  Yet, the huge variety of great fresh made food make up for it.  We had food from the pretzel place, the dutch market, and the crepe place.  The cheesesteak pretzel was amazing.
Fun but very crowded and it can be hard to find a seat.  The large number of vendors is great since it has something for everyone and there are some excellent food choices (Beiler's, DiNic's).

An absolute must for anyone (foodie) who loves to eat! An institution in Center City Philadelphia it has an absurd variety of merchants with a wonderful ambiance. You will not be disappointed really - there is something for everyone! I have many favorite vendors there! I no longer work near there and I miss it terribly; however, I try to get there at least once a month.

what is there not to love about delicious, authentic, diversified food at your finger tips?  I will say if you are going to go - try going after lunch instead so there is more wiggle room to gawk at all the food your belly will be aching to sample!

If you are in the mood for a pork sammy - please go to Dinicks! Best sammy I have ever had in my life! Either wait for an open bar stool to order from the waitress or get in the To GO line. It usually moves pretty fast. 

Oh and the Donut shop---hand rolled donuts. I wanted one but ended up getting a half dozen b/c they were oh so good!

But really what can't you get here? It is a def MUST do for visitors.
I looooooove this place , will miss it once I move but till then I'm just going to enjoy it every day
This place has everything and I mean everything foods and vegetables from all over the world, if u can't find it here it can't b found !!so get on over there u won't b sorry

Beyond obsessed with this place. Whatever taste or kind of food you're looking for, you can definitely find it here. It is not only all affordable but also all incredibly delicious. I've never had a bad meal here ever and I've been eating and shopping here for years!
Good pizza, very small place. Doesn't seem their oven has the capacity to keep up with too much business. There was a wait for slices and they were turning away whole pie orders.

Grew up in Philly, and nothing compares! As a little girl I frequented this place if we were around that part of town for a cheaper, and more diverse range of foods. Anyone can find something here!!! Well... maybe, it might be harder if you're vegan or allergy sensitive. Otherwise, I've gone into this place with groups of 15, to groups of 2, to only me! It's an adventure for the larger groups, and sometimes a hassle to find seating, but it's worth it. 

If you're on a date, both of you can decide whatever you want to eat. Finding a seat will be easier. Plus, it adds a little adventure into the date. Perfect for showing off the town, if you're into that sort of thing. It's a great pit stop for after ice skating at City Hall, or shopping.

If you're going solo then it's the time to explore. You can easily spend 30mins-1hour in there and not get bored. I usually do grocery shopping in here because their produce isn't outrageously priced, and they have a wide range because the vendors are from all over. I love getting "exotic" fruits. ("Exotic" meaning, not exotic to me but to the average American). On occasions they have dragonfruit, starfruit, lychee, rambutan, and even Asian mangos which I think are much better than the species common to the Americas. 

I love being in an atmosphere where there's a food craze! This is a great spot for shopping, gifts, flowers, honey, and lunch.

My family and I go to Reading Terminal Market just about every week. Sure it's about 50 miles away from where we live, but it's that good! The Market is the absolute must-go-to destination for foodies in town and there is a never-ending array of things to try. Do make sure you visit the Market between Wednesday and Friday when the Amish merchants are there, and if you're going on a Saturday, try to get there early, especially if there is a big convention across the street like the Auto Show or the Flower Show because it does tend to get crowded. And don't show up at 4 PM because a lot of merchants will be shutting down soon and may be out of what you want. 

My favorites at the Market include the pancakes at the Dutch Eating Place, the roast pork sandwich with greens and provolone at DiNic's, peanut butter chocolate covered pretzels at Mueller's, soft pretzels at Miller's Twist, cinnamon buns, fritters, and muffins from Beiler's, and peanut butter or mint chocolate chip ice cream from Bassett's. And a big-assed turkey leg from the Original Turkey during the festivals that RTM has.

A must stop when in Philly. Crepes, beef jerky, tea, ice cream, donuts, Indian, fresh meats & produce and these were just the places we tried. Great atmosphere and all the vendors were very nice and helpful too.

Been wanting to try this place ever since the bourse opened but was unfortunately very hungover the first time I went and opted for something more nausea friendly instead.

Finally came back and made it a point to get some food from LALO. I got the bas-ka-bob over rice with a soft boiled egg and lumpia add ons. Also got the calamansi drink and the leche flan.

I have to give them props for the cute and different plating. The leche flan came on a wooden looking paper plate with a banana leaf underneath, bringing even more of the culture into the dish.

I really enjoyed the bas-is-bob dish. Being Vietnamese, I really appreciate a solid meat and rice dish with pickled veggies on the side. The chicken was very flavorful and nothing I had was too greasy, including the lumpia. The lumpia were pretty small but tasty. Wish they were a bit longer. Then the leche flan tasted good but was a pretty thick consistency which I'm not used to with other flans so that comes down to a personal preference.

I think LALO has a lot to offer, especially since filipino food is not very common amongst the restaurant scene. For what it is and how much you get though, I think it's a bit overpriced. This might be a general trend in the bourse (maybe rent is high?) but that would be my only qualm. Otherwise it's a great joint and I will surely try it again when I find myself there.

I don't know what to add to hundreds of Reading Terminal Reviews other than it's a must for any Philly trip. The blend of both market and food service businesses combined with the size of the space and the people makes for a high quality, uniquely Philadelphia experience. There is a lot going on so bring an appetite and energy. I've had some really good crepes, tacos and backed goods at Reading (pronounced Redding) Terminal.  Every trip to Philly includes a stop in, so I think it's definitely worth a visit.

I have a like dislike relationship with RTM. 
The like part all the vendors under one roof. It's a one stop shop for most of your food needs. The diversity is great. The friendly service.
My dislikes the messiness of the place, it's a major turn off for me to stay & eat there.  I usually take my food to go.  It's a major tourist trap especially on weekends. I avoid it then too many crowds & it looks like a tornado hit the place.
I do think you should go at least once and experience the place.  If cleanliness is a problem for you too just take your stuff to go. I go about once a year and that's enough for me, usually it's b/c we have company that wants to check it out.
Real nice the last time I was their I was working up there the crowd was cool ,but if you looking for food this the place to go too.

If this is not the best of Philly, I don't know what is. 
love to drop by here whenever possible, to try the cheesecake, the ice cream, the beer, everything , like farmer's market, plus the food.  Will try cheesesteak next time.
Love it...period! Prepared and raw foods, meats, veggies, desserts, juices, nuts, cheeses, sauces, condiments,fruits, candies, crafts...if you can't find here QUIT LOOKING!

I love Reading Terminal!
There is a small wine shop where I like to get wine.
There is an Amish restaurant called Smuckers where you should DEFINITELY get their Roast pork sandwich OMNOMNOM
There are also many places to get produce!

One of the stops that I really wanted to check out was the Reading Terminal Market because how can I say no to food?? We came here on a saturday because I read on the yelp reviews that the Amish People don't work on sat and I won't be able to try some of their foods. The place was big and you can compare this market to Quincy Market in Boston, Ferry Building in SF, LA Farmer Market, Essex in NYC(I still need to check this one out). The place was selling anything and everything of foods that you think of....One of thing that i wanted was their seafood but I didn't have anywhere to cook plus driving 2 hrs up to NYC, how fresh will it be so I skip out on that part. It was very crowed and people eating and buying food items. The reasons why I am only giving it a 3 star because honestly the foods is only average. It look nice and fun to be around but i just wish there is more things that stand out. I waited in lines for a roasted pork sandwhich and the line was long as hell but to my disappointed the taste was bland. The only reason I could finish it was the help of their marinated chili they have but the taste was bland!!!
The amish preztel was ok but nothing to brag about, i was going try a few other things but realize after giving them 2 try already, the 3rd will be my bad lol

I love eating at the Reading Terminal Market. I usually go here on Sundays when friends come to visit. Worth noting that it does close pretty early on Sundays, around 5PM, so don't plan on dinner here. It's open later most other days. It's a good lunch spot.

Great mix of vendors, amazing breakfast where I had an accidental egg yolk break last second in my omelet (it was the greatest delicious I have ever tasted) at Molly Malloy's; goat cheese, spinach and tomato omelet BTW...  Other than the grilled cheese place, bread spot, cheese spot, and MM's, I find the produce (especially mushrooms at some fancy place that I don't know) completely overpriced.... Molly's is worth it on it's own

This place is bomb! Sooo good. The chicken kheema Kati was delicious--full flavors. MK special chicken platter reminds me of halal guys. Will definitely have to come back when I'm sober for an unbiased opinion. Also, thanks for staying open late.

Very interesting. Various food, fresh made donuts and cake. The donuts place is not open on Sunday. The phili cheese steak is ok. Tommy dinic's brisket beef is pretty good and special because they use a whole skinny pepper for spice not regular green pepper you would think.  The fresh make donut is a must have!

This place was great! it had so much personality! so much food so little time! I was just a bit annoyed because my bf and I were getting so confused in here! we were running around in circles trying to get away from the booths we've already passed by. But this place was great! next time i'll make sure to bring more money =P

Decided to stop by and grab a quick bite and I was pleasantly surprised... The fried dumplings (Philly Cheese Steak and Asian Pork) where amazing and the price made it even better lol... I will be going back to sample the rest of the menu. Not a huge menu but Quality!

The good: pretty good food along the whole spectrum of ethnicities as well.  Definitely check it out if you're in the neighborhood and need food served to you quickly (as opposed to fast food restaurants). See the official site for food options.

The bad: it gets really really crowded! Be careful on the weekends and extended hours days due to events in the convention center because that's when the big crowds roll through. Two people I know lost their wallets here, so like I said, just mind your belongings in the crowds.

A great place to go and eat lunch, and then shop for meat / seafood / produce / cheese / pasta for dinner!  Some of the prepared food vendors are better than others, so be sure to do your research.  But they have awesome, very well-priced seafood, meat, and produce.

Wife and I went here because we were just to exhausted to find somewhere more suitable. BIG mistake we ordered the 2 for $5. We both got the fish. Each fish sandwich had 1/4 of a slice of cheese and each little piece of cheese was stick more to the box than to the fish. The fries were extremely cold. But the server was nice if that helps.

I love the addition of the Kennett Square Mushroom Company. Great spot for vegetarians and shroom-lovers! They always have a varied selection of fresh farmed mushrooms and seasonal foraged shrooms like chicken of the woods, chanterelles, morels. 
Great place for those interested in the abundant variety of mushrooms!

Just like the rating would imply, "Yay! I'm a fan." The Industry looks a little grungy on the outside, but don't judge the book by its cover. Upon your arrival, you'll notice the doorknobs are giant cleavers which might send a Sweeney Todd message to your brain, not to worry. It's more of a novelty welcome to a place that has food and drinks for anyone who likes to eat and drink.

Picky people, put your minds to rest. This is the place for you. Their dinner/lunch/brunch menu goes from simple to "That looks gross. I'll have that." (in a good way). 

I enjoyed the Breakfast Burger here and was pleasantly surprised with a complimentary coffee cake after putting in my order. I initially thought, "Look at this, eh? They know how to treat an Elite." I was quickly brought down to earth and put in my place when I scanned the dining room to find everyone had received the coffee cake. 

The Breakfast Burger comes at a fine price and is equipped with eggs (your choice of style), a sausage patty and cheese sandwiched between two French Toast buns (I know, right?), accompanied by a generous side of breakfast potatoes. The perfect amount of food, just enough to fill you.

The only couple of drawbacks separating The Industry from receiving 5 stars are the lack of parking. Don't get me wrong, it was simple to find parking on a Saturday morning, but I could see it becoming difficult with it being in such a residential area. It was also a tad dark for my taste. 

I really like the personality of The Industry. They don't try to be fancy even though their food is very high quality. The place clearly doesn't take itself too seriously (see: Staff T-shirts with "I don't work here" on the back). Everyone is very friendly and on top of their tables, and the artwork on the wall is a great touch and conversation starter.

I'd put this at the top of my hot breakfast/brunch places in the city. It's also one I feel might be a little under the radar, which I know people love to go to places other people don't know about. So, if you're trying to impress your friends for brunch, tae them here.

The reading terminal market is fantastic.The market itself has a variety of things and food for purchase. You can find some of the more obscure items at the market. As far as food there are many options with most of them being really good. My only complaint would be it can get crowded which makes it hard to move around in some areas.
There's no place like it! It's an incredible way to get all of Philly's most iconic foods in one place! Great crowd of foodies!
So many options to choose from, between fruit and vegetables, meat, fish, baked goods.  Perhaps not the prettiest place, but everything I've ever bought has been great and reasonably priced.
Oh my goodness, who doesn't love Reading Terminal Market? This place is fantastic. All the food vendors you could possibly ever ask for.

I love this place. We found it was within walking distance of our hotel and didn't know what to expect until we ventured into it. It really feels like an old historic city inside complete with street names.

You won't have any trouble finding food here for just about every taste.

There are a lot of great reviews which led us here and I gotta say I am not sure where they are coming from. For a place named Industry you would expect more. A lot more. We ordered 5 dishes and 3 different drinks and nothing besides the wine was decent. All of the food was bland, appeared old, and there was mystery food in one the dishes. We did not complain to them but they noticed dishes weren't touched and came back to ask. So, on plus side the service was decent and they handled our untouched dishes nicely.

Neat stuff here! Every imaginable cuisine, all kinds of quirky shops, inexpensive parking. Super crowded on a Saturday afternoon, so there was a little stress and a lot of bumping elbows. A unique experience that no visit to Philly should be without.

Was really excited to see this place open in the Bourse! The decor was fresh and colorful, the staff were helpful and friendly, and the little toys they gave out with your order number on them were fun and unique. I was surprised by their prices, which I guess may seem fine for tourists but are high for locals who are in the surrounding areas.

I got the shrimp roll and my friend got the grilled chicken over rice. Both portions were tiny for the price - not really enough food for a filling lunch unless you're a bird. The chicken was two small skewers over a small serving of rice, and the shrimp roll was also very small, with a few chips. The shrimp roll was very good, served cold - light and well-marinated. The chicken skewers and rice were fairly bland. 

All in all, we enjoyed the food but probably would not return at this point unless the prices and portions shift.
