Still leaving a 4-star review within the Bourse because if you're set on eating lunch there, this is a great place to go and the lunch prices at the Bourse are generally higher than average for the area for what you get.
My new favorite place to shop for fresh produce and hang out for lunch!So many choices to eat and for some sweet treats.

This place is a must-see if you're visiting Philadelphia. Reading Terminal Market is a huge indoor market with every kind of food stand imaginable, as well as produce, and even a restaurant. From Amish to New Orleans, to Indian, to Chinese, to Philly Cheesesteaks, you will be able to find something here. Reasonably priced small food stands with seating areas. Make sure you tour the whole place before settling on one. Or else get a little something from a few! 

You could spend a couple of hours walking around here and exploring. I wouldn't say this is better than Pike's Place in Seattle; it's different. Pike's Place has tons of fresh fish, beautiful flower displays, and is lined by small specialty shops on the outside. Reading Terminal Market has a stand or two for flowers, and has little food places nestled inside. Anyway, bottom line: great stop in Philadelphia...

Something tells me that I don't have a lot to add here.I have come here for years.It is one of the best markets out there ,not necessarily my favorite but a good one.You can buy all kinds of food , prepared and raw.You can buy books , goods , knickknacks.When it's not too crowded , it is fun just to walk around.Although it is often very crowded.If you haven't gone , you should.

Good place to chill . lots of palaces you choose to eat . good environment for all age's. What make it nice is in the city . a place after a long time walking and site seen in the city you come and cool of after a hot day out side and eat .

The food here is EXCELLENT.. However the delivery person was Awful!!!

So I ordered food from my work, when he arrived he called and said he was here, so I went on my 30 minute lunch and went to meet him. I told him exactly where I was at, and to make it easier walked to the corner of my building. He in return yelled at me and argued with me and was extremely rude. It took over 15 minutes and a phone call to the store to get him to show up to the right spot and he was still rude to me and expected a tip. I had less the 10 minutes to eat my food and the aggravation was un called for.

I love this place! I get groceries weekly and they are fresher and less expensive than supermarkets. Also, I go for lunch sometimes. They have everything from seafood, soul food, Italian, Vietnamese, chinese, Greek, Indian.. cookies, cakes, cupcakes, chocolates!! Everything!! They even have a bar, you can get a drink and walk around the whole Terminal with it but you can't take it outside. The only downside is it's always crowded and the isles aren't big enough, but keep in mind this place is old so.. I love this place and recommend it to residents of the city and tourists alike.

This place is a food lover's paradise!  I go mainly for Beiler's Bakery and their amazing donuts and baked goods.  You can get a smoothie, beef sandwich, dessert, and a beer all in one spot!  The lines move pretty quickly in most places, and most places also take credit card. There is always someone at the netrance to direct you to what you're looking for.

You spin my head right round, right round, when you go down, when you go downtown. Yes, I did change the lyrics. How does one justify America's oldest Farmer's Market, the Reading Terminal Market, when writing a review... You don't. 

Your head literally does spin around when you enter for your first time. Once you know the market well and where your favorite purveyors are, I'm sure it's a walk through the park. I had to see it all. 

A portion of the market does have Amish vendors, but you will only find them here Wednesdays through Saturdays, even though the rest of the market is open seven days per week. 

There are over eighty vendors and covers over 1.7 acres. Two descendants of original shops are still there. This market has also been in numerous movies, including Trading Places. 

I walked into aromas of freshly baked chocolate chip cookies and convinced myself, it was too early plus it was only vendor one, even though ten minutes later I was eating some of the best and hot pepperoni pizza I have had. 

There are six bakeries, two of which I purchased baked goods from and one that I have reviewed so far. I was not thrilled with Le Bus http://www.yelp.com/biz/le-bus-bakery-philadelphia-2, but I was very happy with Termini Brothers Bakery, which I will review eventually. 

They have a nice wine shop and beer garden where I noticed a few drinking beer at ten in the morning, a tea shop, coffee, dairy shops and a juice bar, where you can get blended and frozen concoctions. 

A homemade ice cream parlor http://www.yelp.com/biz/bassetts-ice-cream-philadelphia, cheese shops, fresh flowers, organic produce and raw milk. One place that I really loved was Salumeria, what an awesome market filled with Italian groceries, hoagies, salads and international cheese. 

Local produce stands are huge and if you love variety this is your place. All locally grown and talk about a variety of mushrooms! Shops galore for cookbooks, used books, linens, pottery, crafts, handbags, a general store and Amy's Place filled with unique gifts, especially for a house warming gift or a new bride. 

There are a good dozen or more meat, poultry and seafood shops and some will cook it right there for you. I did notice that on each cash counter, they do have posted whether or not they accept credit cards and if they do the minimum amount to charge. 

Now I'm getting hungry, amazing pulled pork and beef brisket http://www.yelp.com/biz/tommy-dinics-philadelphia#hrid:kJ9LwByjlxBcrf_cNZyJUA/src:search/query:Tommy%20DeNic's, pizza, pasta to go or eat there, sandwiches, cheesesteaks http://www.yelp.com/biz/by-george-philadelphia, perogies or crab cakes at Coastal Cave, mac & cheese or fried chicken at Delilah's http://www.yelp.com/biz/delilahs-at-the-terminal-philadelphia-2 

You can sit down in one restaurant and have a wonderful breakfast, which gets packed, there is sushi, a spice shop http://www.yelp.com/biz/spice-terminal-philadelphia, a little Thai market and chocolates galore. 

Originally named the Jersey Market, since most farmers, fisherman and hunters were carrying their goods from the neighboring state to be sold here. After many complaints from the town folks of this non refrigerated outdoor market, it was dismantled and two new markets evolved from this, the Farmer's Market and the Franklin Market. 

This site has been in use as a Farmer's Market since 1860 on High Street, it soon was renamed Market Street and moved indoors in 1892, because of health risks, traffic nuisances and it needed to be controlled. The Reading Railroad built the Reading Terminal Market as part of their use for downtown passengers. 

The hustle and bustles, aromas and excitement fill the air and whenever I have out of town friends or family, who want to tour historic Philadelphia, I am bringing them here. 

The market is closed on certain holidays and they do not keep long evening hours. Parking at several local garages can be validated inside the Terminal and will reduce your $10.00 cost to $4.00, if you are there for two hours or less. 

Many places offer a seven dollar meal deal and have them well posted. From what I noticed they seemed like a good deal.  I am not sure what the story of Philbert is, I do know that he is a pig that was created by Eric Berg and he is surrounded by money. Anyway, he is pretty cool and located at the end of the central cafeteria style dining area. 

I do hope that I did the Terminal some kind of justice, it is too awesome for words! There are out door cafe tables for two & bongos playing outside..

So, as I am walking through the market, everyone was staring at me and I do mean everyone. Finally two police officers approach me and say "you can not wear that t-shirt in here"! As I am looking down to see what in the world I had put on that morning, my daughter said " Oh yes she can, six time Super Bowl champions"! The officers laughed and said, "yeah, I guess she can"!  What was I thinking?!
Love the Reading Terminal Market. So much to choose from and what a variety. I can spend hours in here and love it. It's a mecca of melting pot

This place is a must visit if you come to Philly.  I could have spent hours in here if I had the time just walking around checking out shops- its huge!  They have clusters of tables in the middle where you can sit and eat.  Where we sat a little old lady was playing the keyboard and she was so cute!  I bet there is a place you can get any type of food you want- but you must go to the Amish bakery towards the front.  Their baked goods are incredible!
Such a cool experience. Put this on your list whenever you visit Philadelphia. So many places to eat it will overwhelm you.

Pizza Shackamaxon is in the house of Beddia which recently closed/moved. We stopped in Wednesday before heading to the shore. The girl working the counter and the pizza guy were super friendly. We ordered 3 slices for the road and 2 diet cokes. 

The slices themselves were pretty darn good. The cheese to sauce ratio was spot on and flavorful. It's a thin crust pizza and it's so light and crispy. The crust was a bit too well done for my liking. There is a fine line between color, flavor and burnt. At $4.00 a slice it's a bit much but it's a quality slice. There is limited seating in the place and they offer very limited drinks. We will stop back in though, solid 4 stars.
Always a fun time to go to reading terminal. They have great food and you can find decently priced fruit at some of the various stands.

This place is a foodie's paradise.
Rows of incredible top notch food choices and food product.. You need more than one (and a hearty appetite ) to fully appreciate it
Reading terminal is a place where there is something for everyone...  Overall it's a nice place and atmosphere most times of the day. I believe their prices are a bit high, but the location is prime.

This place is great!!! There is everything for everyone. The market is filled from bbq to cajun to philly cheesesteaks to seafood to donuts to candy to flowers and housewares!!! The food is delicious and the staff is super friendly. I've had the chance to try Spataro's cheesesteaks, Beck's Cajun Cafe, Beiler's bakery, and Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe. All great places and delicious food. The portions are great and the market is huge. Definitely come with an appetite.

Well in Seattle we have a Pike Place Public Market - which is comparable in size and scope.  However we have hippies selling tyedye clothes and really crappy"hipster" art.  OMG, not another Beaded POS. 

Reading TM, has Pennsylvania Dutch (PD) who seem polite, and while plain, they seem to have a knack for good food to eat.  I haven't tried the Scapple though.  This sounds gross yet so tempting!   

I know that i kept slamming Philly for not having a good coffee - but honestly, i go to starbucks in seattle more than anything, so what should i expect??  I should have just gone to starbucks in philly too.  Old Town coffee, nothing special.

Anyways, go to Reading TM, it's nice, there's places to sit and eat your "whatever"  Not horribly crowded.

I really don't think I'm gonna write anything you couldn't have read in the past 1,000+ reviews. I'll explain what I ate though.
Apple Dumplings.....Buy the 3 for $7 instead of 1 for $3.50. For a apple pie lover this is probably the best thing I've ever had in the realm of apple pie.
I do not remember what stand I got my Beef Jerky from but for $27 a pound I was kinda on edge....till I tasted it. I got Sweet and Spicy and it was exactly that. AMAZING JERKY!
Rocky Road Fudge - BOOM!
Split a Cheesesteak from some unknown stand before I realized there was a really popular place with a line around it. It was good, but I'm still yet to have a Philly steak in Philly that's better then my go-to spot in NJ
Pork sandwich from The Rib Stand - Pretty good size for the price with REALY good sauce they give you on the side. (Sweet OR Spicy) 
My girlfriend got Ice Cream from the really popular place and said it was good but I was stuffed at that point.

I know I know....I didn't try DiNics. By the time we got there EVERYTHING was sold out. I don't like Broccoli Raab anyway.

I did bring home some Habanero Cheese that rocks, and a more mild Chipotle cheese that I put out for guests.

I would have loved to come home with some of those $20/lbs Lobster tails the size of Popeye's Forearm, but I had a full night in Philly ahead of me and no way to keep them cool. 

I will return.

I definitely should come here more often especially because I live so close by.  I really enjoyed Iovine Brothers Produce, very affordable and fresh!  I've also eaten at a few of the restaurants here and for the most part, the food is flavorful, tasty and affordable.  I enjoy browsing the food vendors, I've had good ice cream by Bassets and good sandwiches at Hatfield Deli.  I also enjoyed Godshall's Poultry, very affordable, fresh and tasty chicken.  I've browsed John Yi's fish market too and things looked good there but I'm still not the biggest fan of fish, so I passed on it.  I think the catch with this market is to check the prices.  I thought that by going here everything would be cheaper, not necessarily, sometimes things are more expensive than one would think, so buyer beware.  For the most part though, I'm glad that Reading Terminal Market is around and I'd love to check them out again.  They remind me of Pike Place Market in Seattle, in a way except for the fish throwing, lol!

sorry I know this place is a Philly icon
It's so dirty- walk by at night and it's like Templeton after the fair in Charlotte's Web
GROSS

Always a winner for a quick bite to eat we're sit down at the bar and have a good beer never a bad moment of any terminal. This trip around all I had was a smoothie but it was well worth the wait in line excellent quality excellent service. I will be returning to the wedding party tomorrow Market whenever I am downtown Philadelphia

Absolutely delicious brunch today. Sat at the bar and the barman was very energetic and accommodating. Definitely a highlight of the experience. But the absolutely best part of the meal was the Philly Hillbilly. How can you go wrong with one dish that basically contains buffalo fried chicken AND sausage biscuits and gravy? They had me at gravy!!! Delicious!!!!! I'll definitely be back.

The food was unacceptable, given that I have visited plenty of Potbellys in Northern Virginia and DC and know how their sandwiches should taste. We visited on a saturday lunchtime, after I had already talked up how great our Potbelly's sandwiches would be with my friends. Usually the sandwiches are fairly consistent, regardless of the location, especially during lunch when everything is (or should be) fresh. 

However, everyone's sandwiches were made with old and stale bread. Even though I got a big sandwich to share they skimped a lot on the fillings. They had run out of the soup that was listed on the board. I have a hard time believing that they could run out of soup at 1pm on a warm day, I think that the employees were either too lazy to heat it up or too lazy to change the sign. Either way, disappointing. To top off our unexpectedly mediocre lunch, the oatmeal cookies we bought, which are usually really delicious were also stale! 

My suspicions are that the store just saved the old bread and cookies from the previous day and used them on saturday. Like I said before, unacceptable. For those of you who have visited and were disappointed - I urge you to try a Potbelly in the DC area so you can taste a fresh sandwich and cookies. They are typically great go-to lunch spots.

Cool place to look around and worth a visit but not many good food options. The only thing that looked worth buying were local products like honey, and flowers or the Thai food place (which had a super long line). There was also a store in the back with lots of seasonings to buy in bulk and lots of options for hot sauce. I had a great juice at a juice stand but the whole place only had 1 vegetarian/vegan food store, and it didn't sell any hot foods- only cold refrigerated soup. 
Disappointing, found another place nearby to eat.

Ah, the market. You're like a long-term, committed relationship. In the way of Scrubs' Dr. Cox. 

On the outside, you seem a tad rough around the edges. And by rough, I mean ragged. During your peak times, you are most certainly a violation of fire codes and human rights, with we consumers packed into the avenues as cattle being led-not to the slaughter but the feeding trough. I've been touched in ways I haven't been since grad school-er, I mean, my last visit to NYC. 

But, when I get a tad closer, unravel the mystery behind your crazy busy-ness, I see the soft, delicious, sentimental center. I love finding your produce bargains, munching on burritos or brisket, pasta or pancakes, chowder or chicken, you-name-it-they've-got-it. I love finding lavender oil for my home fountain, a Flying Monkey cupcake on those hard-to-function workdays, and just maybe SUPER rib-sticking grilled cheese sammie during those delightful winter months. 

So, continue on in your wonderful ways, Reading Terminal. I'll come back week, after week, after week. Just find an Arrested-Development-Style prison guard that can yell "NO TOUCHING" ironically from time to time, and you'll be the perfect Dr. Cox, the gruff mentor with a heart of gold.

To me this place was way too overhyped.. especially being somewhere near college students. I really like how they get their ingredients locally and such but it was way way too overpriced when faced with the amount you get and the way it tasted. 
My order had no had no flavor yet my friends was too salty and overwhelming. I ordered some kind of seasoned turkey, it was neither seasoned nor did it taste like turkey. Some kind of weird white meatball  kind of taste and look..
I mean people very friendly but otherwise, I'm just overall disappointed given how much people talk about this place. Will not be going back.

A heaven on earth for foodies like me.

Reading Terminal has something for everyone. Salads, sandwiches, wraps, pizzas, gyros, and crepes are just a handful of the many types of food offered here. I go to the Termini Bakery and Meltkraft Grilled Cheese when I want to indulge, and to Tootsie's when I am feeling healthy.

I love this place. Definitely more pros than cons. It truly represents the culture of Philadelphia. They have a version of any good food sold in Philly, cooked or fresh. They're open nice and early so you can visit before work. The hot and fresh donuts are to die for. Very diverse. It's just a great place to visit. Because of that, there are a few things for which you must pack your patience. There's just not enough dining space. It's definitely not a relaxing atmosphere. There's so much to see that you're bound to get stuck walking behind someone who behaves like a tourist although they probably live here in the city. You want to go to the terminal when you're in the MOOD for open market shopping. It's a great experience.

This place has ANY type of food you could want. After attending a conference in Philly for several days, I had no desire to venture too far from the area. I purchased a grilled cheese sandwich with chicken, roasted tomato and three different cheeses from a place that makes their own cheese. It was the best food I've had in a while. I also purchased the best Carmel chocolate chip cookie from one of the places. I will be going back to try something different today. This place is heaven on earth.

Pricey, Good, but not great.  A must try as an institution.  Solid food, Try DiNic's.  Its good, but not the best.  As an institution you must try it.  Def check out the wine store in there, and all the sweets shops.  There is motorcycle parking nearby, but if you park on the sidewalk near a bike rack, they won't ticket you.

I love this place, Old City Coffee (one of the best), the juice bar, the chocolate, the options for fresh vegetables and meats and prepared foods. The bakeries, the amish, the cheese, lol. I could go on and on but its girl's dream, the reading terminal market.
Staple...Try Valley Shepard Creamery, Tommy DiNics and Oysters

Excellent. Have been a patron of Reading Terminal for years. Have visited most stands. Poultry, meats, vegetables, cheese, candy and most especially Beilers and restaurants. Anything you want is here and I personally have not encountered a problem. Love it.

Fun, food, full of energy! I went crazy could not make up my mind where to eat!  Philly Steaks, Pork Sanwhiches, peking Ducks, cajun cuisine, best juices and smoothies!! Have mercy! I would come back each day for lunch for a month!! Try just about anything at Beck's Cajun Cafe. Amazing Creole and Canjun comfort food! The pork sandwich with provolone at Dinic's. Juices at Four Seasons juice bar! Hard to find a spot to sit but i am good walking and eating..helps getvready for next tasting!
Because of the Amish this place is amazing. Great job hard workers! Great food wonderful

quality products to be found everywhere...from produce to hot food and products they have everything.  The added historical nature if the building also gives it a kind of energy that is felt the first moment you walk in. This place is a must for anyone visiting Philly, and even though I am local I still love to go there for lunch every now and then.
Fun place to visit. It's like a huge food court. It was very crowded and no where to sit. We took a lap around and left but enjoyed the atmosphere.
Pretty cool market with lots of different food options. Would definitely come back here. So much to see and try!

I love this place! I am not sure what else to say...

They have everything that you can imagine as far as food goes. Well almost everything, and even some things that are really not great as far as nutrition goes (chocolate covered cookie? Win! cheesecake brownie? Hell to the yes!) The only gripe I have about the place is that quite a few of the little stores inside have a fear of credit cards, or they set some high amount as the spending limit when using a credit card. Which is fine if you are planning on buying quite a bit of food, but it can suck when you're just trying to buy some sandwich meat. Have you ever bought $10.00 worth of sandwich meat? It goes a long way. I used to love oven roasted turkey at one point. 

I always find something new when I'm in there. Probably because every time I go in there, it's incredibly busy, so I kind of make my movements through the aisles based on the general mill of the crowd (yes, I am that lazy). I don't mind it though. Part of the joy of walking through RT is just seeing what else I can find; effectively I'm a tourist, which I'm quite fine with.
Food came fast (that's what she said) but was not very good dumplings at all I had the broccoli and cheddar, philly cheese steaks, and last but not the best the buffalo chicken

I absolutely fell in love with this place! Wish other cities would have something similar. I stopped by during my business trip. I was unable to get through the whole market. But I plan to return!
I did stop to get hot green tea at Old City Coffee one morning and for lunch, I had duck with rice and veggies at Sang Kee Peking Duck. It was yummy. The next day, I went with a colleague to the Oyster Bar. He had fish tacos with salad (very good, and a good size serving, he said) and I had a bowl of oyster stew. That was very good. The market was clean, vibrant, just bustling with energy. I highly recommend this place.
Awesome place to grab lunch over the weekends and grocery shop. There are so many different kinds of food options, you really can't go wrong. It's like the best of Philly all in one place.

Best place in Philly for local's and tourist alike. Great experience, amazing, unique atmosphere and some of the best food in the city. Roast Pork at Dinic's with provolone, broccoli raab and long hots is the best sandwich in Philly and is more Philadelphia then the cheese steak, yeah I said it. If you haven't been its a must and when I have friends or family from out of town this is my first stop and I love it every time.

OK I'm a fan of markets, I'm used to the open air market of good ole Rochester NY, but if you want to shop come here and if you want to eat come here. I tried to "check in" to too many spots on yelp while I was there that they like blocked me---fie! Yelp I'm so good to you and you deny me! Bastards! Anyway we were supposed to get to the Italian market but came here instead, tomorrow Viva Italia! Very busy but friendly crowd. We were on a sandwich quest. This is a lie I was on a sandwich quest, I'm just lucky to travel with people who will go on the adventures I like to go on, that or the  I'll probably fork you under the table look gets it done. Either way I am lucky that they participate. The variety of items to eat is very good, if you can't find anything you are a block from China town. Our three sandwiches, apple fritter and fruity beverage are all rated in other posts, keep reading and visit the markets! Ground cherries, one stall had them, Montreal had them last week, is this a new phenom? Pretty tasty I'd recommend giving them a try kind of a fig texture, no pit, honey tones.

I am a true lover of this chain, however, this has been the worst experience I've had with them thus far. Service is chaotic with no rhyme or reason and the staff was not warm or friendly. I actually felt as if I was bothering them whem trying to place my order. The young man who took my order clearly didnt want to be here and at this point neither did I. However, after shopping woth my granddaughter, I promised her Chuk fila for dinner , so I endured. Three people receives their order while I waited for an ETA on our food. Finally , I asked why was the order taking so long and was advised they're waiting for cheese for my Spicy Chicken Sandwich. This should've been communicated prior to my asking and waiting frustrated as people marched in and out with their order! Had to return my very cold fries. This is not the Chik fila I love and this is a scar on their reputation

I don't get it, how is this the biggest tourist attraction in Philly? Reading Terminal Market reminded me of the Farmer's Market at The Grove upon entering, only completely indoors and much more cramped. While I found the various Amish vendors complete with workers who looked and dressed the part to be quite interesting and a novel sight, none of the food actually looked very appealing. 

Not sure if I'm just not appreciative of the culture or what, but I honestly don't get the draw of this marketplace.

Where can you go to feel the energy and vibrancy of Philly?  Reading Terminal of course.  So many different variety of food to choose from.  Then there's the fresh produce that are pretty cheap in comparison to some other places.  There are also events like cooking classes, ice scream festival, etc. to look forward to.

What can I say about Reading that everyone else hasn't said already. There are so many different options for food here that I just laugh when I see my friends drooling over the different options.

Dinic's is one of my favorite spots here for their famous roast pork sandwich. So juicy and succulent that I debate everyday whether to move to Philly just for this sandwich.

If you're around during the weekday, I would highly recommend trying out the Amish market food in here as well!

When you're ready to relax, have a beer or eight at the Beer garden in the middle.
I call another Pizza Hut in the said the same thing we closed what is going on with Pizza Hut need to go out off business ASAP

Good places all around.  I personally go to Hershel's East Side Deli for the corn beef sandwich.  Absolutely a must have if you're ever in the area.  Only problem is it's very crowded due to being a big food hot spot.

Jealous this doesn't exist in Chicago!  Such a cool place to visit for food & people watching. Pretty sure you can find any type of food you desire at this Market (including yummy Philly Cheesesteaks). There are also a few different places to buy fresh fruits & veggies as well as meat & cheese (indoor farmers markets). The market is huge and was such a fun place to explore while we were in Philly.

Absolutely LOVE this place! If you come on the weekend mid-day, be prepared to battle the masses, as so many others apparently love this place as well. Excellent variety of food choices and markets (meats, produce, sweets, condiments). My favorite two places are Dinics for roast pork sandwiches (Amazing!) and Iovines produce (grab an apple, wash In their customer sink, and enjoy on your walk. A must stop when in the city.

Although the Reading Terminal Market had been described to me, I was in no way prepared for what actually awaited me.

Options. Millions of options, as far as the eye could see. In my two visits here I saw an oyster bar, Indian food, sushi, Greek food, an Amish baker.... I could go on.

The first time I went, I chose a New Orleans's themed booth and had what I thought was the best sandwich EVER. That is, until I went back the next day to Meltkraft where I definitely had the BEST. SANDWICH. EVER!

It gets crazy packed in here, and waiting for your order often means standing right in the middle of a crowded walkway. Not good for the agoraphobic or claustrophobic, but so worth it if you can get past the insanity.
A Philly landmark and spectacular place to find delicious things of pretty much any kind.

Wow this place has a lot going on. There are so many shops to choose from and tons of options if you're hungry! Everything looked & smelled delicious. I tried the roast pork from dinic's and it was amazing! Grabbed some produce from Iovine's and it was all a great price. Also, I definitely recommend the cheesecake brownie from The Flying Monkey. It was so moist and yummy! The possibilities are endless here & there's something to please everyone. The center has the most traffic and can get a bit chaotic but the outside aisles were pretty easy to move through. You can't go wrong at Reading Terminal Market.

The kind of food oasis the concrete desert wanderer dreams about. Just about every kind of fresh food you probably crave in the middle of a workday, and some you didn't know you wanted.

The "street signs" along the aisles are clutch, so pay attention - it's easy to forget where you saw the fresh red snapper or those mozzarella balls, since the sheer visual overload produced by so many juicy vittles is enough to scramble your guidance system.

Decent produce - there's better in the city, but not with the convenience afforded by shopping for your faves and eating them both in the same spot. The variety of cuisine collected in one place is the Terminal Market's main draw; perogies or crepes, you'll likely find some way to get your filling.

One of my favorite places in all of Philadelphia. It's best to avoid it during lunch hours and weekends unless you like crowds. The produce stands are very affordable and most of the shops are delicious. My favorite places are Hershel's (Jewish deli), Dinics (must get the roast pork, broccoli rabe and sharp provolone) and Beilers (donuts). Whenever I'm downtown, I always stop in

DISCLAIMER: I visited the Market around noon (on a Thursday).  Being there during the busy lunch hour likely impacted my experience.  That stated - I didn't like the place at all.  My biggest issue: I couldn't find a seat!

Yelp reviews inspired me to buy a pretzel (and a drink) from Miller's Twist.  With hands full I walked around the Market for twenty minutes looking for a place where I could sit down and eat.  I never found that spot in the general seating areas (inside or out) so I snuck into the seating section of some vendor I can't remember.  By then my pretzel was cold.  It didn't taste very good anyway.
Fun place for a tourist to visit for lunch or a snack.  My kids loved the donuts at Beiler's bakery.
Love Lalo. Everything is delicious and fresh. The portion sizes are good, not too big, not too small. The service is always friendly. Highly recommend!

Pandemonium.  You should be able to find any food that you want here.  But, the place is bedlam.  Crowded, jockeying for seats, and billions of people.  The epitome of urban cacophony.  Go if you like character, activity, and bustling.  Stay away if you are looking for a relaxing place to eat.

This is the Chelsea Market of Philly. So many random food stalls and markets that were cool! They even had Amish choices, which isn't something we get a lot around me. It was definitely more old school, but was really nice. I found a great coffee company here and bought the most delicious coffee (besides my top favorite Jamaican Blue Mountain coffee). There are really great vendors and good products, so definitely check this place out!
Loved it!! Be prepare for the crowd! Loved the food! Tons of choices and one place thats a must visit.

Me and wife had a great time exploring the market. We had oysters as clams opened at one the fish mongers and ate it at the seating areas as appetizers. Can't get any fresher than that. For lunch we had corned beef sandwich and Chinese food from the Peking Duck stall. Lots of food, had to wrap up half of the food. 
After eating, went grocery shopping, produce, fish and meat. We live in NY, packed the grocery in ice.

What a vibrant fun place for a morning coffee or lunch. Philadelphia was wise to save this city jewel and check out the convention center above the Hard Rock Cafe - it was formerly the reading railroad terminal. Another great save by the community.

Dirtiest McDonald's ever seen. Pan handlers all over, floor and walls dirty. He ac vent over the cashier had about 3 inches of dirt on it. How does McDonald's allow this franchisee to still have this business. 
Disgusting

If I can give it no star I would! This was my FIRST time ordering from them and it will be my LAST! I read some reviews that they have bad customer service, but good foods. I wanted to give them a chance so I placed an order for 5 dumplings and Cheesesteak noodles and within a minute the employee call me saying they don't have the noodles. They didn't fix the menu before I placed the order. So he offer $10 worth of dumplings or refund. I said I want a refund. So within a few minutes he gave me partial of my refund. I call back and said I want a full refund and I thought the order was cancel. He said the order went out already and he can't do anything about it. So he said they can give me a refund on the 5 dumplings that was sent out and I can keep it because I don't think that it is right that I should pay more than double the price on it because of delivery and fee added. He recommend that I call Grubhub for refund of the fee and delivery because they can't refund that. I got my order quick and the foods was horrible to! Dumplings is an Asian appetizer. I should of known to just order from an Asian restaurant instead of American. 

I waited for the rest of my refund, but it took awhile so I called Humpty's Dumplings again and they won't pick up my call. I decided to call Grubhub and report them. Judy answered my call and try her best to fight for me, but fail because Humpty's Dumplings is unethical. She said she will try again and said she was able to refund me through Grubhub and not them. Judy recommend next time I should report the incident first if it happened again. Humpty's Dumplings has the WORSE customer service and HORRIBLE foods! Grubhub has the BEST customer service! BAD experience!

I got a phone call from the owner because I accidentally post this review at the wrong location. Well what can I say I was upset. I might call him back or just call it a lost because what's the point I don't like the food anyways.

This is a must see in Philadelphia.  So many great foodie options that have individual reviews on Yelp.  Reading Terminal Market is a destination not only for tourists but also for locals as well.  Always busy and always a good time, and gives a one stop shop for not only food, but also many other Farmers Market like items (i.e., crafts).

I love Reading Terminal Market!  You can find a little of everything here!  The food is delicious and you can get all kinds of yummy eats there.  They even have a couple of awesome fruit stands where you can get really inexpensive fruit.  I  love this place! I would have given a 5 star but it gets crazy packed and that is a con for me.
Mom and I had the Kasha and bowties the other day......best I've had since Coney Island in the early nineties !!   Will definitely go back for these !

Tons of options to pick the food anything you can think of if you can even go grocery shopping inside get out of the weather horrible parking good seating just in case you want to sit down and eat your food I enjoy people watching here

This Chick-fil-A location never fails at customer service . The line is always super long during any time of day . There's nothing but cleanliness all aroun and condiments area very neatly and organized . Compared to any other fast food chain you'll never see a manager walking around asking if you're okay or if you need anything as if you're eating at a restaurant. Hands down by far the best fast food chain around . Food always good except a few times where my fries tasted soggy or undercooked that's where that one star was taken off for . That's why I'm a frequent here . Whether it's for a chicken sandwich or a salad . Always excellent service.

Great variety, great food, and a "local" atmosphere in the middle of downtown district.  A must visit place for lunch.  

I usually go for the Philly Cheese Steak place and they were wonderful...  I once loaded up 8 of them (at about $10 a piece) and took it back home for the family and extended family members... man, I was a popular guy for a brief min.   Everyone loved it.

Solid, although strange (in a good way), dumplings. There are a number of fried (or steamed upon request) dumplings, mainly savory, to choose from. What is strange, or takes some getting used to, are options like cheesesteak and buffalo chicken dumplings. Both were good, as well as the asian pork, roast pork and shrimp n grits. 

The korean style noodles were pretty good and a little on the spicier side. It's a replica of a korean dish that includes noodles, spam, tofu, mushrooms, etc.

Service was friendly. The location itself has about seven tables to sit down and eat and those working there were very helpful. Definitely worth a try.

This is one of my favorite places ever. My favs are Carmen's, Dincks, Hershel's, Beilers and Franks A lot. Little story, I taught my friend Riley how to order a cheesesteak (American witout) she got all excited to try one. When given the opportunity she chose wawa. WAWA. I got really mad. Then when I was talking about the reading terminal market she laughed. This place is really important to me and she can't see that. Ughh whatever while I enjoy my cheesesteak, pork sandwich, deli, donuts and wings she can get her craft table out to cut her shirts. This place is great don't be like my friend and go here.
Love the diversity and all of the options! So far all the foods I've tried are great. I also love the chocolate covered pretzels from Mueller Chocolate. A must go to if you're in the city.

There is definitely something for everyone and for every meal here. It is busy and some of the lines are long, but that just tells you how great all of the food is. Two of my favorite staples are DiNic's, Miller's Twist pretzels, and Termini Brothers Bakery. All delicious and reasonably priced! I love coming here whenever I come into Philly and it's a great place to explore and try out different foods!

I want some food in bed with a little bit of everything....I went there when i was visiting Philly and had a great time.... we took the car around town...... Anyway we found food right when we step inside... had soft pretzels from the Amish stand...had a Philly cheese steak...bought some sub sandwiches...and had some ice cream.... it was fun walking around and seeing the little areas inside and having some snacks here and there...sadly there's no parking....and the area is really hard to find parking...place is really over crowed... Be aware every food stand has a line! waited about 45 minutes each time! which was pretty aggravating..

AWESOME spot. So many food places along with a few alcohol spots.
Only complaint was the amount of people. This place was a zoo and was almost near impossible to walk. However, once you made your way through, it was fine. I had Tommy DiNic's and it's safe to say it was one of the best sandwiches from 2018.
It was Italian Style pulled pork, long hots, and provolone. The sandwich had so much flavor. I would absolutely get again and if I head back to the market, I would probably STILL order Tommy DiNic's!

Lots of good eats, all in one place. There's a place there where President Obama had a meal. It's a nice hidden gem, where everyone in your family or group can have a meal of their choice, and still eat together as a group.

I was in Philly only for a night, and chose Reading Terminal Market (RTM) to spend my precious hours in philly and it did not disappoint. It is akin to an Anaheim Packing place, Grand Central Market, or any other kind of space with lots of food items inside.
RTM hits all the points: Philly Cheesesteak (of course!), organic market, deli, bakery, dessert options, and veggie/vegan stands. 

1) Spatros Cheesesteak- apparently it is traditional to have yours with cheese whiz, and I got mine with mushrooms and sweet peppers as well. It was very flavorful, and it was a solid cheesesteak. Nothing too spectacular, but i you're looking to check of trying a cheesesteak at its namesake, it'll have you crossing it off your list

2) Beilers Bakery- I had such a hard time choosing what to get from this place, as everything looked sooooooo good. I ended up with the blueberry bread, which was divine. It had fresh blueberries and it took lots of mindpower to stop myself each time I got started

Altogether, this is a bang for your buck while you're in Philly and should come here for some ambience and food if you're in town!

If a giant space filled with food can make a foodie have eating anxiety, this place is unbelievable.  My brother toured us around to his favorite spots, and I noted a trip to Bassett's at the end was required, regardless of the 20 degree snowy weather outside.

He pointed out some of his favorite spots, and then Eric R. grabbed a table and sent us off to eat.  I wandered and wandered and could not figure out what I wanted, though I noted a seafood vendor had soft shell crab sandwiches.  I swapped with Eric and he went off to get something while I held the table.  My brother came back with a sandwich from Salumeria and Eric R. returned with schwarma.  Then I went around again and found a Tea shop and got jasmine iced tea, but waiting in line at a few places I got shoved around and remembered why I don't live in the East Coast.

I sat down again and by then, the guys were almost done eating.  They insisted I try to find something and I set off again.  I decided my brother's sandwich had looked pretty good so I finally went to the Salumeria and got a small (but it is really huge!) turkey with the works.  It was pretty darn amazing.  We did end up at Bassett's for ice cream and then set off into the cold.  This place is wild.

This was my 1st visit to this location. Pretty standard... nothing outstanding to Yelp about. I actually came in just for snacks Barnana chocolate & peanut butter bites180 calories per package gives you about 5-6 yummy bites. Also ended up purchasing a veggie lasagna as well. Veggie lasagna = no traditional noodles eggplant, red pepper squash & zucchini other dried veggies some mushrooms with marinara. Fat free ricotta, I cooked mines in the oven as per the directions on the label & added mozzarella on top. This dish is 280 calories before my enhancements, it was gratifying. Grabbed 2 nut mixes as well. Visited on 10/20, cashier was nice enough showed me where the snacks were wrung me out that's it. Love that SNAP kitchen concept everything is well labeled so you can grab and go. Colorized for vegetarians, meat eaters, vegans and so on. Give it a whirl they have various locations an app & they deliver! Awesome for busy people on the go!!!

Food markets are like heart beat of a city and if you want to understand the pulse of a city, visit to food markets should be a must. This was one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. Only only complain is that is closed at 6 in the vending which is too early. MArket has its roots from 1800s and there are few merchants whose 3rd or 4th generation is running the place. That only happens when you are passionate about what you do. There are about 80 vendors and each and every vendor has something different to offer. One gets so much variety under one roof. There are about 11 Amish eating places which should definitely not be missed. Few vendors are cash only, so come prepared.

Simply one of the best pizza places in Fishtown. Slices are slightly pricier but huge. Excellent sauce, crust, the whole deal. Shackamaxon is definitely worth the wait--and be prepared to wait during their dinner rush.

Cheap good pizzas by the slice? Yes please! Also authentic cola in the glass is a classy way to wash down pepperoni. My kids gave it two thumbs up. The bites I stole from them were definitely worth the attitude I got
Running way from a coldest place to touch the local fresh popularity...everything is fresh to me!

Vibrant city market with delectable items at every turn. I'm originally from Buffalo, and this is what I wish the Broadway Market could be. We loved the breakfast at Down Home Diner and brought home cookies from Famous 4th Street  Cookies. Do not miss if you are in Philly! 

PS. If you give this place anything less than 5 stars because it's "crowded " and you had to "wait in line" , I feel sorry for your heart of stone.

My last meal before dying would have to be red curry from the Thai place, freshly blended juice from the juice place, and a piece of cake from the Amish.  If I could figure out when this place isn't packed, that would be my favorite time to go.  However, such a time does not seem to exist.  The crowds of slow-moving cattle make me somewhat homicidal, but Reading is a carnival for the senses, and it's unique charm makes it a gem for natives and tourists alike.  

**Seek out the piano in the back right in front of the shoe shiners.  Local players come on a regular schedule to play for whoever is around.  All of them are talented, of course, but my favorite is a teenaged prodigy who comes with his family on Saturdays.  Damn, can he play.  Brings me to tears.

The Reading Terminal has everything one could need for shopping from fresh fruits and veggies, meats/seafood, desserts, and everything else in between.  If you go during peak lunch time 12-2pm, it will be very crowded do be prepared to wait in lines.  It's a good tourist spot and natives to the city love it as well.  Breakfast, lunch, or dinner, one can't go wrong eating there!!!

Great place. 

1) Tons of options. 
2) Atmosphere is amazing. 
3) Foodie heaven.
4) Must visit.

If you want everything in one place when it comes to food I suggest going to Reading Terminal. It's very touristy so if you're into that sort of thing plan out a couple of hours so you can look at everything they have. There is a greasy atmostphere to the place but it gives it character. They have everything from their famous pulled pork, donuts, chocolates, indian food, burgers, hoagies, drinks, and tons more. My cousin bought some candles. I had some Indian food which was really good.
Unusual place.  Anything you want to eat is here.  Parking is impossible. Have to take public transportation or an expensive cab.  It is very loud, but worthwhile visiting just to experience.

I came to the Reading Terminal Market due to a recommendation from a friend, as he told me to check out DiNics for their famous Roast Pork, & Roast Beef sandwiches.
Upon seeing DiNics on a T.V. food channel, I made it a point to check out the Reading Terminal Market over the weekend. 

What can I say about the Reading Terminal Market?

Well, the best way to describe this place is - it's like a GIANT mega food court & store!!! 
You name it, they probably have it here...........all kinds of ethnic foods can be found here, as well as fresh farm produce, meats & poultry, finest seafood items, baked goods & confections.

My mission when I had visited the Reading Terminal Market was to try the sandwich from DiNics (which I accomplished), as I ended up eating both the roast pork, & roast beef sandwiches.............I really enjoyed both sandwiches, but between the two...........I gave the thumbs up to the roast pork!

While walking around the mall, I ran into another sandwich shop called - Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagie & Cheesesteaks. 
The time when I was there, I saw our island son - Barack Obama come to Carmen's to eat a cheese steak, so I figured if it was good enough for President Obama, it was a must for this island son to also give it a try too! Lol!

There is a very long history about the Reading Terminal Market, as I read a brochure about this place.............let me share a little of what I read.

Apparently back in 1892 the Reading Railroad opened the Reading Terminal Market below the tracks of their massive new train shed. The 78,000 sq. foot market held nearly 800 spaces for vendors & was touted as the "greatest food market" in the world!
By 1971, the Reading Railroad went bankrupt & the Reading Terminal Market started to decline & be in disrepair. 
Beginning in the 1980's, the Reading Company renewed attention to the market & began a turnaround of the facilities, and by 1984 trains stopped running to the station above the market and the city's commuter rail system was re-routed to bypass the old Reading Terminal. 
By 1990 the historic building was sold to the Pennsylvania Convention Center Authority, who rebuilt the market to strict historic preservation standards, and also set up a non-profit management company to run the market and maintain the historical integrity of this place.

I must say, if you're ever in Philadelphia, take sometime to check out the  Reading Terminal Market, as you should put it in your "must" list of things to do! 
Visiting the market has a lot of very cool historical value, as well coming here to try the various types of food...........it's basically a foodie lovers paradise!!!
I love the market and all of the wonders it has to offer. I forget how much is there!

Great local spot for tourists and people who live here. Bunch of mom and pop spots clustered in one tight space. There are so many different spots to eat. You could literally go restaurant hopping to each one. The place is packeD all the time and I only wish the place was bigger and opened for longer hours!

ALWAYS something to get here. Great place to take someone when you can't decide on what to eat in Philly because of everything they offer. Usually pretty crowded and difficult to find somewhere to sit and eat, but everything is worth it.

After all the hype I finally decided and gave this particular location a try. After 30-40 minutes of wait it was no where near worthy. The food was alright, just some general stuff. The group of staff were unprofessional. All you see were a bunch of useless staffs talking and not working. I wouldn't waste my time going here unless your craving is really kicking in.
Portions were smaller than expected but great food! The paneer masala roll was a favorite and the mango lassi was very thick and sweet. Great place to stop by!

Reading Terminal is your one-stop shop! It has EVERYTHING. Your first trip here will be overwhelming so allow me to guide you.

FOOD: Hershel's, They have the best pastrami, corned beef, and brisket, all hand cut right in front of you. Served on homemade rye bread. (get mustard and onions and you're set!)

Salumeria: On my top list for Italians. They're great because their products are fresh, delicious, and most of their add's such as Cheese, Roasted red peppers, and hot relish are included in the price. 

SWEETS: 4th St. Cookies. Delicious and affordable, especially if you luck out and get them right out of the oven! 

AMISH: If you want Amish food or goods, be sure to come Wed.-Sat. otherwise you will be sorely diappointed. (Miller's Twist pretzel's are like Auntie Anne's on steroids, yum!). 

PRODUCE: Super fresh, super cheap, mostly locally bought produce. Great selection and really friendly staff. 

COFFEE: Go to Old City Coffee and get an iced coffee. Really good here.

These are listed in a carefully thought out chronological order. Eat 'til you explode, get fresh produce at the end so you don't have to lug it around all day with you, then fight off the food coma with a refreshing iced coffee. Have fun!

P.S. You will get a chance to check out the whole market on your scavenger hunt. Good luck and god speed :)

I love this place. It has a good "industrial" vibe with the wood everywhere and iron look. There are typically around 10 -15 beers on tap, most are lighter styles (the IPA world is against me). Their food is very tasty but it is small portions. 

I've had the brunch ham and cheese hushpuppies with syrup. Tasty.
I've had the lamb skewers. Tasty.
The breakfast quesadillas were okay. 

I'd recommend this spot for anyone wanting something light to eat with a good beer in a really cool joint. I'm a fan.

I absolutely love Reading Terminal. It's a foodie's heaven and you can literally satisfy any craving you're having. Great prices and selection for produce and other goods like fish and cheese. A plethora of stands selling pre-made foods that you can eat there or take to go.  They have a fabulous selection of Amish foods that I grew up with back home. It's always pretty crowded and therefore hard to find a seat to actually eat your meal there which is a bummer. You must go to Beiler's Bakery (best sticky buns, pie, donuts and whoopie pies, oh my!) and Famous 4th St Cookies if you enjoy sweets!!! Prepare for long lines during lunch and weekends--especially at the most popular stands (DiNics, thai place, etc). Stands will validate your parking ticket for the garage across the street if you spend over $10 (i think it's $10) so you pay less for parking. All in all this place is a gem in the city and somewhere locals and tourists must go.

A great local market with tons of options across the board. I wondered upon DiNic's and am glad I did! I thought it was a little pricey, but that's probably just my mentality coming from the Midwest to the East Coast. The roast pork sandwich with cheese had great flavor, but was super sloppy and rendered the 2 small napkins they gave me useless. I also tried out the wings and mac and cheese from Keven Parker's Soul Food stand. Again-- solid choice! The wings were great, the mac was fair. I've definitely had better. I was surprised to learn after visiting that these two stands are two of the highest-rated there. I was impressed by both but would love to try some other places out next time.

Any trip to the city of brotherly love can't be considered complete without a trip to the market. Whether your a foodie, organic lover, craft queen, etc there is definitely something for you. All of the vendors are super nice and more than willing to answer questions you have about their products. If you are a foodie and are in reasonable driving distance bring a cooler for the leftovers/fresh meats and seafood.

When I have an afternoon free and i'm HUNGRY (or if friends are in town and I want to take them someplace cool) we head to RTM. I always get onse of those pretzel hotdog from the Amish stand. Then i walk around and graze on whatever is looking good. Oh, grab a treat from Flying Monkey Bakery - you wont regret it!

I love Reading Terminal, it's obviously a Philly classic and everyone needs to go at least once. (Just make sure you're able to handle tight spaces and crowds!) There is so much to look at and eat, you almost don't know where to start. I also think it's kind of charming how easy it is to get lost, it adds to the character, that's for sure! I definitely want the tradition to be preserved, but it would be great to strike a balance between the historic authenticity and more contemporary innovative food options. You're surrounded by animal products there, and I think it could be awesome to update some more for the growing plant-based population. I think there might be one vegan stand occasionally but that's all I've seen so far. You can find vegan options, but it's not as easy as it could be with a few alterations or new vendors. That said, there are terrific whole food options for good prices at Iovine's and OK Produce!
Great place to try a little bit of everything! We had pretzels at Miller's Twist and donuts at Beilers and everything was delicious!

This is one of my favorite spots in Philly! The huge variety of foods to be found are amazing. And there are just lots of fun places tucked away here. Definitely need to take the time to explore this little treasure if you have not done so already!

I ordered from here for the first time a few days back because of a friend's recommendation. I usually get kati rolls from another place in the city. I ordered Achari Paneer, Paneer Masala, Chicken Masala and Buttermilk. 

I have always like Paneer based rolls bette than the meat ones, even at the other place in Philly, and this time it was no different. The chicken roll was a little hard and tasted less marinated (chicken for sure is not as juicy and tender as the Kati Roll Company in NYC). I am also not a fan of the Masala rolls but that's just me. 

The Achari Paneer was delicious though but the highlight of the entire meal was the Buttermilk - I will order again just for that. It is just so tasty and every ingredient in perfect proportion. 5 stars just for that and the Achari Paneer. Also, love the fact that they have air tight bottles to deliver the drinks instead of the to-go cups which can be messy.
Reading Terminal market is the best place in Philly to buy produce. Their prices are a little high, but you can find ANYTHING you can think of there.Would have given 5 stars if not for the prices

Had dinner on Friday evening. Nice night to sit outside. I've always been a fan since Diving Horse opened years ago but it seems as though the portions have gotten smaller and prices have gotten higher. It's lost a little of its uniqueness over the past two years. I love the atmosphere but was hungry about an hour later. For the prices they charge I shouldn't be hungry till breakfast the next morning.

The only way to get out of here alive is if you go early in the day. It's otherwise crowded and full of tourists and chaos. Be prepared to be elbow to elbow with everyone and to fight off complete strangers to get anywhere.

There's nothing bad to say about Reading. Try the salmon platter from the thai place. It's a lot of food for $7 plus you get shirmp, don't skip the curry/crack sauce, it's poppin. The cookies at the cookie stand are also bomb as fuck but I wish they had gluten free options.

Originally from the area and had to try out the revamped Reading Terminal Market. It's a must go to for lunch, a fun afternoon of trying new foods or just being a straight out foodie for a day. The assorted venues offer a wide range of food options and fun trinkets.  We walked away stuffed from burgers and shakes from Hungry Burger, delicious coffee and a cute tote from the coffee shop, a great assortment of jams from the Amish shop, and the most amazing fudge and dark chocolate peanut butter cups from Meiler chocolates.   My older kids loved citing all the movies they could think of that were filmed here, I wish I'd googled that prior to heading there.  Took the train in to the city and  had a blast!
This place is so much fun with so much variety of food!!!!!!!!!! Lot go the stuff and homemade, freshly made. My old high school reunion from C. High was thrown here. Oh boy did we have a blast

Like other reviewers have said, this place is delicious!  My eyes were greedier than my stomach and I was only able to eat 1.5 of the 4 rolls that we purchased.  The beef tikka was by far my favorite, followed by lamb kebab and aloo paneer.  I also tried the chicken masala which was also delicious.  Honestly, there isn't anything I did not like.  I would highly recommend sharing with someone so you can try all the delicious flavors.  We were visiting the city at the time and really wish we had something similar where I am from.

Love this place. Give yourself and empty stomach and
Some time to get through it. Bet you can't go without getting a beer, pretzel, doughnut or your favorite Philly Cheese steak or Italian sub.

Lots of terrific eateries and gift shops.  We had excellent Chinese food during our visit.  On the flip side of the coin, AVOID this place on the weekends, as it gets so jam packed you can't even move.  The entire place was one huge mosh pit, and we had to leave as soon as we finished eating to avoid getting crushed to death.  We'll make sure to come back during the week when it'll be hopefully less busy.

First time ordering food online and after i paid for the delivery i was missing a meal. I called and guess what sure come by with your receipt and we will give you the meal. First of all i ask for a delivery cause my car is getting fix, ps i paid for the delivery meaning i can't go over there ill share my soggy ass taco with my daughters.

This place is unbelievably good! Honestly I would eat here every day if I could. The buffalo chicken noodle bowl is outstanding and they are constantly changing up the dumpling selections. It's a no frills, order at the counter atmosphere, and the quality is always consistent. I really can't say enough positive things. It's a must try.

Cozy ambiance, dimly lit and comfortable interior. I'm a sucker for the opportunity to try unusual appetizers, and Industry's dinner menu offers up crispy pig ears and sweet pea-truffle dumplings.

Their oysters are excellent! Fresh and tasty, and they serve them with a spicy, savory house hot sauce which is AMAZING! Think Tabasco with a savory twist. I could put this stuff on everything. On the downside, the shellfish weren't shucked properly and most of them ended up with tiny shell fragments that needed to be picked out.

Staff was friendly but mostly stayed out of our hair while we were there. Industry also boasts an impressive drink menu with several unique cocktails -- I'll be back to try!
Awesome, and you can't beat the parking deal $4 in the garage across the street with validation.

As a multi-cultural experience, it definitely earns high marks. I've been to nYC so I get the crowds and the bumping/pushing to get around. That said, it would be tough to get around with Kids during peak times or impossible with a wheelchair. 

It makes up for it with the unique  food vendors (Thai, Dutch, Chinese, ice cream, etc) as well as shops (delis, soaps, jewelry, etc).

DONT LET THE LINE OF LEMMINGS FOOL YOU. Bacon, Egg. & Cheese Platter With Potato: Scrambled Eggs here are bland and not fresh. Potatoes are disgusting, hollow little squares of grease, puffy with very little real potato on the inside. Highly processed everything for breakfast. Almost the worst breakfast ever. Do not recommend this place. Maybe they would not kill a bagel with cheese.

Such a cool idea/place. On my second visit to Philly, my friend took me here for breakfast/Lunch it was great because one person wanted a smoothie, and we wanted sandwiches. I got a sandwhich and motza ball soup from Hershels East Side Deli. Check the website for a map if you like. Both ended up being fantastic.
We went back the next day for a late lunch and had cajun @ Beck's Cajun Cafe, which was some of the best Gumbo I have had outside New orleans. They had Abita rootbeer, sooo refreshing. 
This is a great place to shop for fresh produce, meats, flowers and candy! I would recommend a trip here for a tourist or a long time resident. Great for foodies!
The terminal is a good spot, De Nic's is a favorite, and the Amish donut place is amazing. One of the go to spots for food in Philadelphia!

What an incredible market. So many places to choose from. The New Orleans eatery is authentic with red beans and rice etc. Amish food delicious. Go there often because soooo much to choose from. Diet before you go!

This place is awesome and definitely should be the first place you should go to in Philadelphia. There's so many different foods you can try out and so many small markets inside, you can easily waste a lot of time wondering what you want to eat.

I went to Frank's to get their BBQ Chicken Sandwich and fries. While the sandwich was a bit bland, the amount of fries we got was humongous. I mean, we got a big bucket full of them. I couldn't finish it all and had to give some to my friends. A friend of mine tried out a Thai place there and thought it was okay.  I would try out more places next time since it was only a stop for us in Philly.

Reading Terminal Market gathers a variety food and people together. Big restaurants and bakeries have their small shops inside. You can find all sorts of things from ethnic foods to books and flowers. The diversity is great. One of my issues is the crowded-ness and navigating the area. It does remind me of places in Asia, packed and noisy. But it is a neat place that adds to the uniqueness of Philadelphia.

Reading terminal is definitely not just a place, it's an Experience! If you ever visit Philly, it's a must. Reading terminal market satisfies any taste buds: Chinese, Japanese, Turkish, you name it! From my personal experience, if you are a sweet lover you must try the Beilers Donuts shop. It's truly delicious. 

Thank you for reading this and I hope you find it helpful.

Had a few communication/scheduling issues with sales team but overall I am very satisfied with the work that was done by Jason, Zachary, John, and Brady. There was a lot of work to be done and they did it flawlessly, efficiently, and neatly. Reviewed the system and answered all of my questions.

I am confident in the work done and am ready to remodel my basement.

Even thought Iived right around the corner, it took me almost a year to check out this spot. Went for brunch on a whim and did not regret it one bit. I got the Hillbilly Philly and the New Orleans Mule to drink. Couldn't tell you what anyone else at the table got because I was in a food trance. The Hillbilly Philly was insanely good, for the 15 minutes it took me to scarf it down, time stood still. Could of been because I was starving to death, but I'm going to assume it was how damn good it was.

What's all the hoopla about?  Yeah, it has some decent places to eat, but I do not believe that just because you group several decent places under one roof, their rating should go up.    One of the other reviews mentions that it is a good place for tourists because it has a sample of local flavor, and I agree.  But, if you are here for an extended period of time, or live in Philly, I don't see a need to plan a trip to Reading Terminal.  Take your guests here and let them sample a little bit of everything, take yourself to a specific restaurant outside the terminal's borders.

The market  is  an experience. Small stands  offer  unique foods. If you like baked goods try Amish bread and sticky buns the best we have ever had.Unfortunately the crowds can be a little overwhelming

Fantastic public market featuring cuisines from all around the world. Plenty of local and fresh options available too.  I got a great pretzel wrapped hoagie from Millers and picked up some local chocolate from another store. 

It's a little cramped and crowded, but to me, that's part of the charm. Definitely a must-see if you're visiting the area.

I absolutely love coming to Reading Terminal. Every time anyone comes to visit me in Philly I make sure to take them to this gem. It's not even as if we come planning to eat here, but every time we make sure to get some sort of tiny dessert or coffee just because there are so many delicious scents in the air. Would recommend for just walking around or for a nice meal :)

Noisy. Crowded. Busy. It's great! All kinds of fresh ethnic and local foods, cooked or uncooked. If you want to shop or eat in a bustling, casual atmosphere, this is it. Even if you are not planning to buy anything, it is just a great place to walk through as a tourist. It is close to the historic area of Philadelphia and to Chinatown (great eating and shops there also). If you have the time, definitely go there and "Don't forget the Cannoli" at Termini's Bakery in the market or down on 9th St. in South Philly. I'll have a Ricotta filled one. No powdered sugar on top; makes them soggy.

FIND A DIFFERENT LOCATION, NOT WORTH YOUR TIME!!!!! 
Super rude staff and unhelpful. Why do you guys make it so hard for me to give you my money? I've never seen such terrible problem solving. It's not the situation it's the principal, I'm not familiar with every specific name for everything they have, I asked for the fruit punch not knowing the specific name was "pomegranate cherry" the cashier stood staring blankly at me for an extended not providing any alternative help or solution to my problem, until I had to point at the fruit punch colored juice. Is it really that hard to problem solve ??? I don't work there I don't have the products memorized. Then after I had paid for my meal. The cashier stood there expecting me to lean all the way over(to his side) of the very wide counter to collect my meal, which being pregnant, makes laying on a table pretty difficult. NEVER coming back to this location EVER.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this place. So much food, so many options. It has EVERYTHING. Beiler's donuts, Bassett's ice cream, Dutch Eating Place's hot apple dumpling, Metropolitan Bakery's cookies, and many many more... Amish food here is amazingggg, so rich, decadent, sweet, and pure. Two words: food orgasm. 

I don't really come here for entrees. I'm not interested in real food -- I want desserts and other sweets!! I had tried Tommy DiNic's roasted pork and pulled pork sandwiches; they were great but didn't really stand out to me. I also had a hoagie at one shop (forgot the name), and it didn't stand out to me either. I think while the entrees here are good, there are plenty of other (and less crowded) places that have similar, and equally delicious, entrees. Plus, there are tons of food trucks in Philly that specialize in hoagies and sandwiches, and they're equally delicious and far cheaper! So, I mainly come to Reading Terminal Market for Amish sweets and non-Amish sweets. 

The place is always packed full of people, so that's one con, but it's also full of delicious food. A must-go for everyone, tourist and local. I would go everyday if I could.
Something for everyone! Whether you're looking for fresh fruits & veggies, or a greasy spoon lunch, you will not be disappointed with a trip thru the market.

This place is the best! All sorts of food from all walks of life. When can find snacks, meals, gifts, groceries. The biggest problem is that it can be quite crowded and noisy. It is a convenient walk from most Center City locations. Don't expect to find a seat to eat your lunch. If you find one it will be crowded and probably dirty.  It deserves five stars however because you can find anything and it's all wonderful.

First time I came here, it was love at first sight. The amount of food available is truly staggering. For sweets lovers, it's paradise. For someone in Philly at lunch time, it's the best place to go. The PA Dutch girls are an integral part of the atmosphere. They show you a part of Pennsylvania culture which cannot be found anywhere else in the world. The hardest part about the Market is choosing what you want because everything looks delicious.

I really enjoyed the atmosphere at this market. I can see why so many people rave about it. I think the range of food items here is good, but I've been to better markets in New York and Seattle that have outstanding food diversity. I went to this market hoping to be tantalized, but that wasn't the case. Some of the food options looked super dodgy, some some overpriced, and some just seemed so-so. I ended up leaving the market with some bananas and carrots. Maybe it was me, but given how much I love, love, love to eat food I surprised myself with my final food purchase. My one piece of advice for people going to the market for the first time would be to walk through the entire market first before selecting your food. Prices range wildly in there as does the quality. For example, my carrots and bananas would have cost over $3 at the vendor right next to the entryway, while another vendor only charged me $1.50. It pays to shop around in this market. Regardless of whether you love markets or not I would recommend entering the gauntlet and enjoying the experience. :)
Very good donuts and very good sandwich,I could say top 10 in United States, the liberty donuts and the slow cook sandwich with lots of meat
Lots of fun. Plenty of places to shop and eat including a winery. Biggest problem is the parking which is scarce and expensive
I would definitely go to philly for just this. I can't wait to visit again. So much food. Reminds me of Asia.
Great venue. Worth the trip.Tremendous number of food choices. ALL are good! Worthwhile!
Crazy crowded all the time but I love the energy and fresh produce, breads, seafood, pastries, and pub to get a drink and snack.

Really a solid food experience in Philadelphia.  A good number of butchers and fishmongers that provide enough competition to raise the product quality to a high standard.  Certainly one of the best places in town to shop for meats and fish.  There isn't enough enough competition on the produce front though.  The prepared-food vendors are a bit kitschy, but can satisfy an urge or two if needed.

In the former site of pizzeria Beddia, this place makes , arguably, the best slice in Philadelphia (I think Pizza Brain/ Pizza Dad's also is in the same league), better tasting crust and pie than the new Beddia  Pizza in the same nabe as all three. Admittedly, it is easier to get good crunch when re-heating and selling by the slice, but to me pizza quality is about two things: the crust (crunch) and the sauce. The rest is like ketchup and mustard on a frankfurter; it doesn't make the underlying frank good or bad. This place scores on both the sauce and the crunch, with a dough that is both airy and crunchy and tastes like Italian bread (much like the terrific Roman-style pizza at Alice in Center City).

Small place; very limited menu; not cheap for whole pies or slices. But, well worth the premium cost for the great result. Nice to see Philadelphia (well, Fishtown area) becoming a slice mecca like Greenwich Village. And, this place is doing its part. The guys making and selling it obviously care, too.  Wish they were closer to where I live. Bravo!
Fun place to be, all the commotion gives you a nice philly feel and the food options here are amazing. It is hard to pick from just one place
This place is excellent. The guys work hard to bring you great Pizza.Thanks Josh & Cello for making awesome ass Za.
I love that they have sooo many vegan and botanical options including but not limited to-- A VeGAN Deli - Called LUHV!! and herbiary - just to name a few

Awsome place to go when you dont know what your in the mood for. Many vendors to choose from. Went here during Jury duty and i got a nice discount. They have some stands where there are lines wrapped around the place. Everything from Pizza, Chinese, Thai, American, Italian, Sushi, Desserts, Candy and Specialty Coffees. I dont get to come here often but i would definitly like to go try this Thai Food stand that everyone tells me about.

Great selection of local foods... No matter what you're looking for, you'll find it here--reasonably priced, too!

Plus, all-around cool atmosphere.
OK place.  Not that great.  Fairly clean for a city that is not. Tourists drawn there.  Some locals seem to frequent it.  You can find plenty to eat but no where to sit.

This is a really nice market.  Lots of places to get yummy food (raw and cooked food). I like the many options, but it was so crowded you can barely move.  I doubt I would return if I visited the city again though.

Verdict: I could go here every day.

I went for Tommy Dinc's Roast Pork and Beef on my first sandwich. Philly knows how to do a good roast pork and Tommy Dinc's didn't let me down. I suppose that's why the line wrapped around their stand. Carmen's cheese steaks had quite the line and fan base too. Like other places here, they have their system down and food comes out fast.

The real star of the show was The Original Turkey. Go here for the Turkey Steak and be amazed. My family and I were deciding where to go. They offered a sample of their turkey and it was an instant decision. The meat was more tender and juicy than possibly any turkey I'd had before. I've had some good ones too.

Bassets Ice Cream small is actually rather large. Be warned and be prepared for some good eating if you go here. Don't miss Beiler's Donuts for another favorite. Their apple fritter is fantastic.

Great neighborhood place for Sunday brunch. The food and service are always top-notch. The interior is really cool and when the weather is nice they have outdoor seating. If you're a fan of Bloody Marys be sure to try the Ghost of Mary, it delicious!

This is quite possibly the most amazing place I have ever been. It was almost overwhelming at first. We must have walked around it about 5x before deciding on what we wanted to eat.

It is just an awesome, interesting place to walk around and explore. I wish we had been in Philly longer so that I had more time to eat at more places in the market!

Saturday gets extremely packed but it is still interesting. Sunday was kind of a bummer because many places weren't open.

Stunning. I mean, it is a flea market on steroids. 

Reading Terminal is located right where the old Reading Railroad Station used to be, and the market was moved indoors for sanitation concerns. Now it is a huge convenience for people who want to buy produce and goods in the area. I mean when you walk in, the first thing you notice is the diverse smells. I mean, it just smells of Central Pennsylvania (largely because most of the businesses are based out of that area).

One of the best things I like about this is the awesomely nice people, not to mention you can really get what you want here. Just be warned that the lines can get long at some of the more popular joints (especially Beiler's - their baked goods (notably the donuts) are awesome). 

It helps that the hotel I am staying at is adjacent to the Terminal. That way I can beat the crowds with much more ease than others.

On an advisory note, a lot of the Pennsylvania Dutch markets are closed on Sunday, so if you want to get your sweet tooth on, get there before then.

If you plan on coming to Philadelphia, this is a must.
