What a pleasant surprise.  This Old Steel Mill decor bar was very inviting.  The atmosphere really pulls you into their world.  I can imagine drinking here with friends for hours.  We had a couple of drinks and some sandwiches.  The fries were very well done and very shareable.  The food presentation was way more upscale than I expected for a bar.  Wait staff was friendly.  This place was not too busy but I don't think this will stay this way for long.

Pulsating and vivid market, one of the most iconic places in Philadelphia.
Great market to buy fresh food and produce, great place to eat.

Best pizza in the city, hands down!Pie is cooked perfectly with gooey cheese deliciousness. The pizza is simply special, I only wish there was an easier way to order it, instead of visiting the shop and waiting or coming back in an hour. Don't get me wrong though, it's definitely worth the wait. Or I just order 5 slices!

Love this place, plus the cheap validated parking across the street or the ride in from Septa make it easy to go! DiNics, Termini Bros, Carmens Cheese Steaks, Dutch Eating place and oh so much more, the hardest thing is deciding where to go and what to get. No matter your choice or preference there is a very good chance it will be very good if not amazing, But you must choose wisely!

Great place to spend an afternoon! 
The donuts are a must try, even though the line is long, it's worth it!

There is literally everything under the sun all collected into one place here. The aisles are labeled by numbers which is a god saver but its extremely crowded no matter the DAY or TIME. I highly suggest doing some research before you go if you dont like crowds or just wing it if youre about that life

How can you go wrong with like 100 places to eat from? Ice cream, fresh doughnuts, Philly cheesesteak sandwiches, gyros, it's all here. Only bad thing is that they close at like 6pm. Must run here after work! This is a definite must-do while in town. You could spend a few hours shopping for soaps and flowers, or bellying up to a variety of food counters. Love this place.
This is the coolest place! Basically an indoor farmers market. We had an amazing Philly cheesesteak with a pretzel bun. So good!
This is a great place to browse and eat lunch!  We loved The Tubby Olive for the balsamic vinegars.  We had lunch at the Middle Eastern stall with a bar, and loved the falafel and dolmas.

Great place to go. Have an idea of what you are in the mood for because making a decision on what to eat can be very over whelming. Have a solid game plan when entering. But always stop for a cookie from 4th st famous cookies.
Have had many delicious meals and key ingredients from here.  A great fresh market. Flowers, food, veggies, and desserts.

Great food and love the environment! It was my first one and I got the M.K chicken and rice. It was a little spicy so next I'll just get he regular chicken and rice. But still one of the best places in philly

It's extremely crowded but a fun experience.  You can find almost anything here.  I recommend breakfast at the Dutch Eatery and a cookie from the 4th street cookie co.  You can also get fresh produce, meat, cheese, spices, etc.
It's not in the best area of South Philly but they seem to do everything possible to deliver a similar experience to suburban Wendys locations and the food is just as good.

In this case the hype is all true.
This market is as indescribable as it is awesome. Wifey and I spent only 3 hours eating and exploring but I think several all day visits are required to do justice to the Market. If you hate crowds you had better go elsewhere. But if you love fresh meat/seafood/candy/beer/vegetables/ice cream/cookies, etc. all served by friendly, helpful folks of all backgrounds and ethnic persuasions, you will be pleasantly overwhelmed. Wifey and I can't wait to go back. Only this time we won't eat for two days in advance but I fear we still won't have enough room for all we want to consume!

If you're looking for traditional dumplings, this is not the place for you. If you've ever wondered hmm, what would it taste like if I jammed a fried dumpling wrapper with some unusual fillings? then come here. 

The variety of sauces on the table were great, and I appreciate what they're trying to do here. 

Winners: Asian pork, Buffalo chicken 
Pass: Honey chipotle chicken (when compared with the others, the flavor seemed mild!) and Spinach, Mozzarella, and Ricotta (appreciate the vegetarian option but the filling is woefully bland)

How did I never know about this place?! We could have spent our entire vacation here! It has a very fast paced vintage vibe during the busier times (breakfast, lunch, and after 4:00). The history itself is pretty unique since it's 150 years old. 
There's something for everyone. An eclectic mix of divergent shoppes and all with a flare for the extraordinary. You can't just buy lotion, it needs fresh goats milk and ingredients direct from the farm. You want donuts? They're made by the Amish right in front of you. Smoothies made with fruit from the farmers market. The people watching alone is worth the trip!

The food is decent, as in I've had better but it's close to my office & tastes good enough that I don't feel the need to walk any farther. The space itself is quite nice; very clean and open. It is over priced though, in my opinion. Paying nearly $3.50 for a lassi just seems a bit much to be. That being said it was a yummy lassi & I will probably go back

Lots of options to eat here and everything we tried was good, especially the ice cream. 

Super busy at lunch. Elbow to elbow.

I'm in love with Reading Terminal! I had seen in numerous times on various TV shows and I was finally able to go! Amazing food! Anything you want they have it and more! 

Tip: Make sure to take a lap before settling into a certain vendor when it comes to getting food so you see all the amazing options.

This Market is a must when you are in Philly. Come hungry- you will want to try everything. I suggest sharing with friends- that way you can try more of the amazing food offerings. This place is often very crowded- be ready for crowds. Come early. Many places run out of their most popular items. 
I always head to the melt craft sandwich shop in the back. My friend and I shared the special Fig-goat about it- fresh goat cheese, Granny Smith apples, and fig jam. As well as the Brielle- made with Brie, cranberry chutney, caramelized onions, and pine nuts. Sandwiches are served with homemade potato chips. 
We also filled up on yummy donuts and fresh, strong coffee. 
We were staying in the hotel across the street- so not sure how parking is. So convenient for us- as soon as we were the least bit hungry again- we could run across the street to eat more yummy food. 
We will be back. 
Loved the live Christmas  music while we shopped and dined.
love this place! there is so much food variety here. It is my go-to spot on Fridays after class. I highly recommend going to beilers and east-hershel (order the pastrami)

Love Reading Terminal!  Always something new to try, meats and ingredients are fresh.  Always have that hard to find item or spice.  

Old City Coffee.....best bar none!!!!

Great place for food. Good people everywhere.  Homeless do come in and beg but not as bad as other places in the area.  Will be very crowded during peak times (lunch). A lot of people familiar with the area use it

This place is awesome. Such great food selection. Dinic's is a must. Parking can be expensive even with validation. I used a parking app and was able to park for 6hrs and only pay $11 on a Saturday! Definitely check this place out and come hungry.

It's always a joy to shop at RTM. Great choices, lot's of incredible cheeses, wonderful sandwiches, but my most favorite thing is the merchants themselves.
My wife and I have been shopping here for years, and it's nice to have a smile, a hello, a thank you for coming back, stop again.
Just go. Get a beeswax candle, some greek food. Theres 80 vendors, eldest and largest farmers market of anywhere in the area. Be aware they close at 5, but it is the best spot for lunch. Just go

Walking into this humble abode, I call this foodie haven! Literally, it's just wall-to-wall of savory goodness from every diverse part of the world. As the City of Brotherly Love should continue to pride its rich and diverse offerings, Reading Terminal Market does that! Today I had Tommy Dominics for their roast pork sandwich (f**kin DELISH) followed by Beller's Donuts for a couple incredible donuts (Maple Bacon and Elvis's Delight - both had bacon!). I'm gonna have to come back again if I want to savor more of its fine offerings!

Love coming here, but it makes me feel like a tourist. But other than that, there's so much of a variety. and there's also a mini farmers market to get fresh veggies and fruit. there's always something new to try but the con is there rarely anywhere to sit and don't go on a weekend. you'll get too annoyed with how crowded it is, where you barely have room to walk
This place has amazing Indian fast food. Clean, fresh and delicious. And their Lassi is the real thing. So good. Definitely going back!

Worst McDonald's I have ever been to. Order the #2 just the sandwiches, get charged for one, and only got one also. The #2 is 2 cheeseburgers. That is why the price is $2.18. But I get charged $1.17 for one but it is supposed to be 2 sandwiches. Every other McDonalds gives 2 cheeseburgers for the $2.18 listed. Cheapskates.

What could be bad? No matter what you like you WILL find something that you like here. My favorite places are Miller's twist (cinnamon sugar is my favorite), 12th street cantina (great mexican food), down home diner (for breakfast), Sang Kee (try the pork), and Bassets (best ice cream in Philadelphia). The reason for the 4 star review is that the market gets extremely crowded.

Went to this place on our way out of Phili and felt excited that they had so many vegetarian options .. we ordered the mixed veggie roll , healthy roll and the paneer achari roll .. my mom felt the first roll had a lot of masala , I liked the second one although I wouldn't say it was super yummy .. my husband liked the third one also he felt it was high on paneer but less on the achar .  The mango lassi was very good though.. I might not go back here again ..

I'm surprised to see any negative comments. Green Leafs was the BEST place I've dined in so far at the Philly airport. The topping were plentiful, the staff was uber helpful and friendly, and EVERYTHING was fresh. I was VERY pleased!!! This was one of the best salads I have ever had ... even beyond the airport!
Love Reading Terminal.  Great food options, especially Iovine, Thai Food and Molly Malloys!

I love Reading Term. I've been going since I was a little girl. One of the best historical places, especially food places to go in Philadelphia. Try Tootsies, George's, the soul food place, Carmen's steaks, and the Amish bakery!

I got two different paneer rolls and I unfortunately found it to be a little too dry for my taste. The serving portion was worth the price though. But in general the price is a little more expensive than what I've seen at other places in other cities and in Philadelphia. However they do have this really spicy red hot sauce that you can add for some softness to the dryness of the roll. Service was fast the location is great there's outlets there if you wanna do work as well as free Wi-Fi. I think having some more sauces available would be a nice addition to the restaurant because it's really limited right now. There should be multiple hot sauce options and that would be a really great addition to have.
My favorite place since I was a kid for a foodie it's a dream . My favorites are always the Cantina, Hershel's Corn beef, and Godsells.

So cute and rustic! It was very crowded and hot but I enjoyed it nonetheless! Such great food and shops, we spent almost 3 hours there but it felt like 10 min! So much to see and do, definitely one of my favorite things to visit around Philadelphia.

Pretty good place. The clientele is all over the place. Sports fans, neighborhood folks, old people, young people, people in suits, people in crazy cat sweaters. Everyone

The food is great and their happy hour is on point. Pretty sure it includes wines too. There is tons of seating inside and out, but the place is absurdly noisy. Their brunch can be hit or miss. Chorizo and eggs is on point, but steak and eggs is a plate of disappointment. I dig their version of the bloody mary, which uses tomato water instead of tomato juice. Great for me, cause I hate tomato juice. Sucks for my wife, who loves traditional a bloody mary.

Service is really great though. It's not all condescending or chit chatty. They get you your order and bring stuff that you ask. That's it. Like I said, pretty good place. It's not a dive, but not a five-star kitchen. It's just, idk, comfortable, ya know?

Reading Terminal is walking distance from my house and I love that it is. Its such a great place to go to when you're cooking dinner for someone and you need adventurous supplies or when you're hungry, but not for anything specific. Their produce stands are priced well and they have every type of food that you could think of that you can take out or eat in. Definitely worth a walk around to check out its many offerings.

3.5 stars and I'm rounding up.

The Industry is THE place to go in Pennsport. Sadly there isn't too much going on elsewhere. Their burger is affordable ($8) and delicious, and their buck-a-shuck happy hour oysters are great too. Salads ($10) are of good portion size. The wings ($12) not so much. 

Adding to the oysters, they offer $3 "local" drafts from 4-7pm during the week and 3-5pm on weekends. This usually means Kenzinger, unfortunately. 

The menu is also heavy on weird meats and animal parts. If that's your thing, you'll totally dig it! It's not mine.

The first couple times we were here, the service was great. On Sunday it was abysmal. *shrugs*

The greatest part of philly! you have to go there once to try all the great food vendors. I recommend the amish diner and herschels pastrami. I've been there dozens of times and still have not tried all the different offerings, this place is awesome! wish there was one in every major city!

This is how you do an urban market! In Baltimore we have Lexington Market, which is like the Capitol building for Heroin City, U.S.A. While that can be a sight to see, I'd gladly give up Lexington's junkies hocking pills for Reading's sprawling venue filled with vendors who have been perfecting their crafts for years. Must stop on a Philly visit!

This is a great place to eat just about anything you can imagine. My favorite store is The Tubby Olive. The lady let us buy a baguette from the bakery and go around tasting all of the oils and vinegars. Amazing!

Is it possible to dislike this place, aside from the occasional crowds and long lines during peak hours? Everything you could possibly want is waiting for you, and the bright neon signs will guide you to exactly where you need to go. Coffee, ice cream, chicken, donuts, cheese steaks, fresh juices... 

If there's something you're in the mood for, you'll find it at Reading Terminal! Dinic's for pork sandwiches, Beiler's for donuts, Old City coffee, flower shops... the list goes on! And the workers are almost always cordial and friendly. It's a must visit in Philadelphia! I've only lived here for 3 weeks, and I know it has already become a favorite spot!

"If you love it so much, why don't you marry it" Got married in it, close enough!

One of my favorite places in the world. 

Favorites to take home: sausages from Martin', burgers from Haltemann's, cleaned whole fish from Golden Fish market, fresh pasta from By George, Amish jerky, Victory Thirst Quencher from Lancaster Dairy

Favorites to eat: DiNic's sandwiches, Hershel's sandwiches, Dutch Eating Place apple dumplings, Rib Stands boneless rib sandwich,
Great stuff everywhere!!! The only issue is you can easily get lost looking for a place inside of it
Wonderful place to explore and try new foods. The market is filled with shops and you can smell all the fresh food!

I am a huge fan of the Reading Terminal Market and frequent this spot whenever I am in the area. I always bring guests visiting from out of town for a meal and to gander at all the local goods. It's a great spot for people who are in the mood for different foods, since there are so many amazing options. I would definitely recommend this spot to anyone who hasn't been before!

I don't know if I've ever left a restaurant and just kept saying, "I can't believe that was so bad. I can't believe that place is still in business." I'm all for trying new combinations of foods and flavors, even hipsterndoofhi food like this. But this goes way beyond just hipster garbage. The dumpling was still cold in the middle after being fried. The "asian" noodle bowl had nothing Asian about it. It came out covered in parmesan cheese, was so salty it was barely edible (and I like lots of salt), and and was covered in some sauce that was as thick as glue. On top of that, the woman running the place looked like she had been babysitting a sick infant in the back - exhausted, bedraggled, and covered in stains. I NEVER leave reviews, good or bad.  THAT is how bad this meal was. I felt sick the rest of the day. What a waste of $20. Never again.
Love coming here. It's always a happening and all the different foods are delicious and stalls are unique. This is truly a treasure in Philadelphia.

This is an example of an phenomenal market! There are so many different things offered here from fresh vegetables and fruits meats seafood at the highest quality. This market has some of the best variety of prepared foods I love Peking duck all of their food there is phenomenal such a great place to eat duck is crispy in all of the best ways. There a great seafood places desserts galore shout out to the Fourseason fresh fruit and vegetable juice place is the best juice bar on the planet

One of Philly's best attractions. Super crowded on the weekend and closes a bit too early on week nights are my only two complaints. They have so many amazing food options, you really can't go wrong. Get a roast pork from DiNics. Really worth checking out if you are in the area.
Tried the beef tikka kati roll. Very reminiscent of the kati rolls I used to enjoy in Calcutta. Other than a kati roll shop in Soho, London, this is the best kati roll I have had outside India.

No trip to Philly would be complete without stopping in Reading Terminal Market at least once while you are there. This historic indoor market is home to so many different merchants offering up everything from cheesesteaks, ice cream, jerky, Cajun cuisine, pastries and all sorts of fresh food and produce (just to name a few).

In past visits I've had the chance to try the famous roast pork sandwich at DiNic's, sampled some delicious locally made cheeses from Valley Shepherd Creamery and picked up a tasty set of homemade chocolate truffles from Mueller Chocolate Co. Not to mention I've also been really impressed with the amount of fresh fruits, veggies, seafood and meats that are available for purchase throughout the market.

The only downsides I can think of when it comes to this place are that when it's really busy there can be good size lines that build up when ordering food (Carmen's, DiNic's, Beilers, etc..) and the market closes relatively early (I believe 6pm) each day so definitely try to get there earlier in the day if possible. Reading Market is a Philly icon / tourist destination that should be on your list of places to visit when you are in the city.

Sent my kids to get a full size Apple pecan chicken salad. They get back home and my salad has fu$!?ing BACON...I DON'T eat PORK and let's not forget to mention that they didn't even bother to put my damn pecans in the bag‍. My children are here at least once a week and it's always a issue I guess it's time to move on cuz I'm over this place.

This is an amazing place- definitely a must-go-to when visiting Philly! It's basically one huge market with everything and anything you can think of. From their freshly baked donuts to seafood, this place is a foodie's dream come true at a reasonable cost too! 

Theres also street side parking available right next to the market, usually free if not then one or two blocks down... super convenient!

Like going to the circus? Well imagine if the circus was all food, that's the best way I can describe RTM.. I loved it at RTM and hope one day my city will become cultured enough to appreciate a market like this too..

There are tons of things to do in Philly. Philly is known for having some of the best sandwiches in the country. So great that we are imitated all over the world.

The best place to get some of the best food and sandwiches is in the Reading  Terminal Market. There is literally nothing that you can't find in this place. They have hoagies, baked goods, Chinese Food, sea food, burgers, buffets, and a diner. They also have butcher shops and produce stands to get great fresh meats and produce from. This is one of my favorite places to go due to the variety of product selection that is available.

It does get kind of busy but that just ads to the atmosphere.

It is a place that everyone needs to visit when they are in Philadelphia.

If you park, park at the garage across the street. Most places in the market will validate your parking and it will only cost $4.00.

Busy, prepared food and meals. A grocery store, meat markets, and bakeries round out this must go if you're in Philadelphia. Careful where you walk outside as it is close to the convention center, you could step on the many homeless who camp out on the sidewalks unfortunately in the middle of the day.

I appreciate the risk of trying new flavors, which were not bad, but the choices were very limited and the food was too oily. Just an option to have the dumplings steamed would have improved the food so much...

A nice selection of IPAs. The mac & cheese croquettes were satisfying, an interesting take on mac & cheese  but the truffle dumplings were like little flavor bombs.  6 sidewalk tables available. Warm atmosphere inside.

I finally tried this place. It's fine for a small to go meal when you want some Indian flavors, but don't want to pig out at a buffet or eat large portions. The chicken masala roll that the reviewers rave about was okay, not bad, not great. You won't get the rich flavors here that you would get from an Indian restaurant, but they provide a good amount of chicken in their decently sized roll. The service is friendly, super quick, and the store is very clean.

The Reading Terminal Market is classic Philadelphia. Featuring some of the city's best food, from DiNic's sumptuous roast pork and roast beef, to Termini's incredible Italian pastries, the market offers a dizzying array of foods to eat or take home.

Come for the food, stay for the experience. It's like stepping back in time.

But the pork juice on your fingers will remind you why you're here.

Big fan of Chick-fil-A. Fresh and original ingredients.

I highly recommend their deluxe original or spicy Chick-fil-A sandwich over the plain since it adds a more full flavor, chicken tenders over the bites since has a little more meat for similar price, crispy delicious waffle fries, and a nice cold cup of Philly water. Don't forget to ask for any dipping sauces such as Chick-fil-A and Polynesian sauce since they don't always ask you.  Recently tried their honey roasted bbq sauce which tastes like a spin off version of the Chick Fil A sauce but has smoky flavor infused, recommend to give it a try! 

Great customer service compared to other fast food restaurants and great food, period.

I had a vegetable crepe that was excellent, but it was hard to enjoy because of the noise and the difficulty I had in finding a table. I would recommend this only if you would enjoy a hectic and crowded market.

This is my go -to spot for yummy AND filling drunk food... A better alternative to drunk pizza... which by the way now that Mama Angelina's closed down, there is always a massive line outside of Pizzeria Cappelli.

 I've met the chef of Masala Kitchen (from a previous Yelp event) and he is a charming fellow who is ready to accommodate anyone's taste buds, even at 2am. 

Tip 1: You HAVE to try the mint lemonade!! 
Tip 2: Don't forget to check in on Yelp to get 10% off your order!! 
Tip 3: Don't forget to get an extra ramekin of white sauce!!

You can really never go wrong with Reading Terminal.  A particularly favorable option if you have a group of people with different palettes - there's something for everyone! My most recent try was Becks Cajun kitchen, which was pretty good (a little overpriced) - but other favorites include Keven Parker's Soul Food Cafe and Beilers Doughnuts. I'm not sure of what healthy/vegetarian/vegan food options are available - there seems to be a lot of fast/gluttonous food. To me, produce is overpriced too, but a convenient offering of fresh fruits & veggies for those living in the city. 

It can be overwhelming, especially if you're a bit indecisive and on an empty stomach. For that reason, if possible, I would avoid peak lunch hours because of the heavy crowds. 

It seems like they're constantly under construction here. The building is historic, but it's nice to see some updating  taking place where necessary and improvement of the facilities (bathrooms, ect...) Park at the garage across the street next to Panera and get your ticket validated!
So cool! Couldn't make up my mind what I wanted! It was great just walking around and seeing all of the different restaurants and stores.

I've been to The Industry a few times now, and initially I had it in my mind as a 3 star place.  My complaints were that the portions were small and overpriced. 

I went again recently and found that the food had improved, the service had improved, and the portions were a little better. 

The cheese plate was delicious.  We tore that thing apart in minutes. 

My wife and I both got specials as our main courses.  I don't know what our two friends got across the table but they seemed very pleased and cleaned their plates very quickly between sips of rum and Grand Marnier (yes, seriously). 

I tried a center-cut pork with polenta and escarole special.  Inspiring!  Very well balanced and flavorful. 

My wife had some kind of pasta that I forgot the name of -- it looks like giant maggots, and I'm sorry that's the only comparison that comes to mind because it was d-lish and the textures all hit the mark really well. 

For dessert we had some of gelatinous mini-pie-shaped tort or something, and I would advise staying away from it because it is BORING.  The cider donuts, however, are fabulous, and whatever dipping sauce comes with them gets the whole thing just right. 

Great addition to an otherwise mummer-fied neighborhood (corner bars on 2 street that have questionable menus and make you feel a little unwanted).  

Hopefully before I get dragged to the burbs, Moyamensing will start to get a few more of these destinations.

This place has it all.  What ever you want to eat, they probably have it.  If you are in a group of people who are all picky on where they want to eat, these are the kind of places to stop.  They even have the Amish making up tasty treats.  Can advise anyone on where to go here because there are so many choices, it is over a hundred vendors packed in one huge building.

The best pizza. The thin crust is perfectly crunchy. The tomato pie is out of this world. They never fail to make a banging speciality pie. Go to spot. I eat here almost weekly. if you love pizza GO HERE.

Too crowded. Dirty. Meh vendors (tried four of them.. Terminis was the best of the lot) Everything is ridculously overpriced. Two burgers, two drinks.. $33. Only to take the greasy, mediocre burgers to filthy tables you have to wlak in circles to find empty. Pass.

One of the things I had intention of seeing when moving to the area was the Reading Terminal Market. Think indoor farmers market, amazing looking food vendors, flowers, chocolate, freshly made everything you can think of - cheeses, jam, pickled something, sauces, breads, baked goods, Dutch Pennsylvania invasion - sweet mother of jesus why do I only have one stomach... all under the same roof.

One of the things that thoroughly impressed me was the large amount of vendors of the Pennsylvania Dutch variety. They were legit, down to the garb and beards. Lots of respect there and I definitely plan on patronizing them regularly. There were these amazing looking pies in one booth that had me salivating. I had already had lunch so I skipped on it but next time I know... I am going to have pie, FOR LUNCH. 

It was unfortunately packed and full of tourists (me included) which made navigating a little frustrating and difficult from time to time. Which led to the misfortune of getting my wallet jacked by some pick-pocketing asshats who double teamed by pushing me around in a busy corridor. Beware of crowds near the exits, keep your bags in front of you or stuff your wallet in your underwear, do not take out money at the ATM there cause they will case you... it happened to me. Apparently it is a problem there and I didn't know any better. 

But overall? WOW. It was a cornucopia of culinary eye porn that was a game of "just the tip". I want more. I plan on going back to the crime scene despite my apprehension. No one, not even a wallet stealing prick is gonna keep me from such a killer resource. And next time I am going more prepared: empty belly and an extra sharp eye... more food porn to come.
Lots of tiny shops to explore.  Every nook and cranny smells wonderful from the food establishments to the herbiary.  A must see place in Philadelphia.
Wonderful food and selection, but if you are not one for crowds, I would avoid this place on the weekends.
This is an absolute must for visitors and Indigenous folks. Lots of wonderful food, Wonderful Coffee, wonderful produce, beautiful women , and a mixture of multiple cultures .

This place was quite interesting; I'm giving 4 stars only bc it's pizza from philly and compared to any other pizza in the area the pizza was decent. The experience within the restaurant is where we experienced a range of characters. Upon arrival the guy at the front counter wasn't really the friendliest. He was in the weeds with about three tickets; and made it known to myself and other patrons. We wanted to order two pies for our group but they informed us they only had one pizza dough left so we decided to order that and a few of the slices they had on display when the counter guy says to us "If you get those we won't have any more pizza so my husband and I look at him like okay.... so I say well we wanted to order two pies so we'll just take these four and then he says "You huya already ordered a pie". I'm a bit taken a back like did we not walk into a pizzeria where the goal is to sell your pizza?  So I proceed to say to the counter guy that we're ordering for a group of us with kids and what does it matter if you sell these to us or to someone else? They agreed to sell us two slices with our pie (yes it's a pizza pie!) we paid for our pie and the two slices and They told us it would take about 25 minutes so we leave for a drink while we waited. Once we arrive back to pick up our order the same counter guy then tells us he sold our slices! Like wtf! The other guy that was making the pizza (who happened to be the more hospitable of the two) offers to make us two slices or we could come in the next day and get two slices. That's what we decided to do and they honored their word they didn't forget we paid already and gave us the slices. Overall just an odd experience for "ZA" as they called it but if you're into that kinda stuff I would say the pizza was decent and i guess worth the wait.

We come here very often and it's a must see for people visiting the city. All of the food options are so great and the lines aren't usually too bad. We get vegetables here quite often and have always been satisfied with the food. Would recommend.

Some of the best pizza I've had! 
Good ingredients, finished with a drizzle of oil and fresh grated cheese to top it off. Good crisp crust. I'll stop anytime I'm in the area!

Tasty Kati rolls for those looking for a quick bite for something healthy and tasty, and a nice neighborhood Chipolte replacement in a similar price point. Don't overlook the Chicken Keema roll for a bite that is more juicy and spicy, the Rose Lassi for something a bit exotic and raves to the quality of the freshly made Naan. Service was efficient, timely and friendly. An excellent food addition to the Washington Square neighborhood!

How did it take me so long to try Snap Kitchen? Between all the dinners/ parties and traveling around the holidays, I haven't had much time to meal prep and needed something quick. I also wanted something healthy so ordering pizza or takeout wasn't an option. The grab and go meals here were exactly what I was looking for- quick and healthy. I stopped in after work so a few items were already sold out for the day. I ended up getting the chicken teriyaki and crispy chicken. Both were filling meals and the chicken teriyaki was my favorite of the two. I'll definitely keep Snap Kitchen in mind the next time I'm in need of a healthy alternative to takeout.

Coming to Philly for the first time, tons of my friends suggested me to check out Reading Terminal Market. It literally is a one stop market that has literally everything from groceries, desserts, and different food stalls. Walking into the Market was so overwhelming. It was a Sunday afternoon and it was so packed. However, the AC was on high and there was still a lot of tables available for seating.

If you are looking to try different things, this is the place for you.

The food ordered:
1. Beck's Cajun 
-Mac and cheese balls with BACON. Yes, with bacon.
-Chicken gumbo
The seasoning was so rich in this gumbo. I couldn't put my spoon down.

2. Carmen's Philly cheesesteak and Hoagies
I waited 20 minutes on line to order 2 cheese steaks. Yes, it's a long wait but it was totally worth it
-Classic cheesesteak
-Kamikaze cheesesteak (side note: it wasn't really spicy at all unfortunately

3. Hershel's East Side Deli
-3 meats platter
You are in for a real treat, 3 treats actually.

4. Flying Monkey
-Krispi Treat

Apple Dumplings!!! (Thurs-Sat) Filbert St Entrance
Amish rotisserie chicken (Thurs-Sat)  Filbert St Entrance
Fresh fruits
Fresh veggies
Fresh Flowers
Fresh Fish/Meats
Awesome! Everything.

The Reading market is fine and certainly a place for tourists to visit if they've never been in town before. But, its a racket. it isn't the best food in the city and its not as fabulous as it used to be in the 80s and 90s but there 's a good selection of prepared foods. The Meninite stands are one of the best.

I love RTM! I new before we came here it was gonna be a crazy and insane, but idc! My eye's went from cinnamon buns, to cookies, fudge, cheese breads, oyster bar, pizza and fried chicken. Like what do I do? Where do I go? Ahhhhh.... I need to taste every thing, so I started for the oyster bar and did that. Then walked over to try the pork and broccoli rabe and then I saved the best for last. A hot apple dumplings with heavy cream. OMG!!! For real, omg!  
I now can die happy. LOL!

Hard to rate the entire market, but in general, anything you need is here. Lunch, dinner, groceries, pickles, cheese, snacks, desserts, body soaps, honey, it's like a year round farmers market with diners and ice cream! While the amount of people is overwhelming at times, it's just something you come to expect from the crowds of tourists stopping in every aisle and in the middle of the walkway. Stay aware of your surroundings, mind the people around you, and take a few laps before you choose, there are so many good options!

Always a staple for when friends or relatives from out of town come for a visit. Good cheesesteaks, coffee, flowers, meats and cheeses. Can't stay too long, or my claustrophobia-introvert freaks out a little (i.e. it gets really crowded on weekends).

Go there. It's great tourist spot there. A variety of good 
Would suggest the following. 
Produce- Ivoine brothers
Breakfast- Amish 
Ice cream - Bassetts
I loved this place. There are so many options and everything was delicious. Make sure you are hungry when you go because you will want to try everything.
It's a foodie paradise for Philly, a lot like Pike Street Market in Seattle except food focused. Excellent lunch spot

Our driver dropped us off here after we checked into our hotel. After grabbing some cheesesteaks we strolled around this market.

There are so many great eating establishments for every type of craving. There's even a nice craft beer bar that serves pretty good beers.

Recommend visiting this place.

I love this place, but unfortunately I wasn't really hungry and didn't get to try anything spectacular except the Cinnamon ice cream from Basset.

But this place reminds of me Chelsea Market in New York but 5x better.
I guess because they have a lot of things I don't see here in NY.

I would want to come back here again since they were CLOSED for labor day!

*SAD*

The breakfast counter served some of the most delicious original recipes ever. The staff was attentive and made excellent recommendations based on our needs. Spotless.. one of the cleanest establishments I have ever had the pleasure of dining at and I can't wait to go back!
Never disappointed !! Absolutely love love love coming here for my produce and whatever else I happen to bump into!! It's obviously a tourist attraction but even that crowd makes it worth the visit.

This is one of my new favorite spots in Philly! It has been around forever, but I never gave it a fair shot. I went there with a grocery bag, and an empty stomach, and wow was I impressed! There are so many options, and it wasn't too over crowded for  Sunday early afternoon. It so unique and having a market indoors is awesome, as I can head and hang there day or night!
The worst McD I have ever been in.  The crew was like zombies and service was slow.  Ray Kroc would have closed this place down!

One of my favorite parts of Philly! 

Reading Terminal Market has something for everyone! There are so many speciality vendors there and local shops that produces goods. I will admit that sometimes I get overwhelmed coming here, but in a good way! 

I haven't had the chance to try as many food places in here, but the ones I've had are nothing short of delicious. They have every type of food here. Craving something? You can probably find it here. I have nothing but good things to say about this place. A definite must when in Philly!

This is a great experience for anyone who likes markets and is a foodie. There is a market for fruits, veggies, meats, deli, and sweets. It's a great first date activity, or just a nice way to spend the afternoon. Be prepared to spend lots of money on food and have a good time stuffing your face after you make a serious decision on what to eat!

Fun but crowded ,especially on the weekends , very overrated and overpriced priced. Could by items cheaper in other parts of the city. Really liked Beiler's Donuts. And the variety of meats at the butcher counter.  Other than that ,nothing special,it's  a loud overcrowded ,overpriced supermarket.

The best place to go if you want to eat anything and everything in Philly. Personal favorites: DiNic's Roast Pork, Termini Bro's Cannolis, Beck's Jumbalaya with Chicken Andouille Gumbo, and anything from Beiler's Donuts. Goooood luck finding a seat at lunch on a weekday!

Let me preface my review by saying that I went to Reading Terminal Market on a Sunday, which I suspect is not the best day to do a fair evaluation of the place.  I think only maybe 1/2 of the stores were even open so I'm guessing this place is much more happening during the week.

From what I did see -- nice variety of food stands, bakeries, pastry shops, butchers, markets and random knick knack shops.  If I lived in Philly, I would probably frequent the place to pick up some meat and seafood, all of which seemed fairly fresh and reasonably priced.  I heard that the Amish don't open their shops on Sundays so I'm a little bummed I missed out on the Amish pretzels that everyone seems to rave about. The food that my gf and I was ok (cheese steaks from Rick's and mac n' cheese from Delilah's) and on par with what I'd expect from essentially a glorified food court.

All in all, I found everything about Reading Terminal Market to be ok.  I would definitely be curious to see what the place is like at lunch on a Thursday.
Reading terminal is a great one stop shop for fresh goods and locally sourced fruit and vegetables. Take a look at the massive market.

Oh how I love this place. If you want it you will find it here.  My favorite place is Tootsies.  Great southern or soul food.  Turkey wings in excellent sauce/gravy, collards done to perfection, best fried chicken.  This is a buffet style. Price is good.  People so friendly and helpful.

MUST VISIT this market. I am not from Philly but was visiting a friend and their family. The dad works in one of the offices nearby and insisted that I try baked goods from the Amish bakery and Dinic's infamous sandwiches- didn't disappoint at all! From Dinic's, I tried a roast beef sandwich and a pork sandwich, both with provolone and broccoli rabe- heavenly to say the least!

A big girl's paradise. Food galore.  Weekend adventure. Sweet tooth island.  Everything you've read about how awesome this place is- its true!

Tip for parents- leave the bulky strollers at home. It can get very crowded and a headache to maneuver a big stroller or jogger

This is definitely one of my favorite spots in the whole city! It's a concentration of all the yummiest restaurants and food stands in the city in one place. I have tried Beilers Donuts (ask for a fresh made hot donut!) and the Dutch Food Place (bang for your buck and delicious!) the Creperie and the little farmers market in the back to get cheap and fresh produce. I bring people here when they're visiting from out of town and they always leave happy. 

Think of it as Philly's version of Grand Central Market in LA or Pike Place in Seattle with an east coast twist. Definitely a go to spot if you're a local wanting to grab a bite or a tourist wanting a taste of Philly.
I have lived in Philadelphia for 6 years and this is my favorite place to go. Dinic's roast pork sandwich with provi and broccoli rabe is a must have.

It's fun to walk around Reading Terminal Market to view all the restaurants and food markets.  If you work in the area it's a fun diversion to go over at lunch-time to walk around and choose lunch from one of the many vendors.  I also enjoy taking visitors to Philly here.

There is absolutely nothing in this place that won't blow your mind. RTM was founded in the 1890's, and has never closed since. About a third of the shops and eateries, bakeries, etc are owned and operated by Amish people. 

Three of the businesses at Reading Terminal Market have been run by the same families since the 1890's when the market originally opened. 

The Market used to be closed on Sundays (I assume) because of the Amish people, but a few years ago they decided to keep it open. So, you can go on Sundays, just expect about 1/3 of the businesses to be closed. 

Reading Terminal Market is where you go when you want to have a food experience that you can't have anywhere else other than Philly. As a local I can tell you this is where I take people just about every time if they have never been to my city. I take them to Cosmi's or John's Roast Pork later, once their RTM induced food coma has worn off.

I won't make any specific recommendations because EVERYTHING you can eat here is worthy of 5 stars. That's why it's great. You can walk around and sample all of this amazing food from all over the world and at the same time experience the TRUE definition of what it means to enjoy Philly's best. Locals come here daily to experience what they know to be one of the best spots on earth for amazing food (yes, earth).

Enjoy!

This place was PACKED on a Saturday afternoon. I will never return with that many people coming and going. I was unable to take my time and check everything out because I couldn't stand being around that many people. Not all places take credit you must have cash to make some purchases. I have been here many years ago and it was very cool. Just a little too populated for me. Maybe it would be better to go during the week.
I don't think there is another spot in Philly that makes me more proud to be a Philadelphia. This place has everything delicious you'd ever want and a charming crowded market feel.
A classic place to find any type of food you're looking for!  I highly recommend the Old City Coffee as well! Oh and don't forget about Beilers Donuts.  Ah now I need to go get some!

Perfect spot for a quick and inexpensive spot. Came visiting to philly and staying in a hotel nearby so this was perfect balance of yummy options and inexpensive prices. Wished there were more samples but probably a good thing there aren't for my waistline's sake
I just love the crazy crowds and circling the market trying to decide on what to eat.

This place is cool, I don't think we have this at New York or New Jersey. So many choices to eat around here, it took my family a long time to decide. It's a busy place, I noticed alot of FiveO's around here, I counted at least 12, when we were there. I don't know if its a good thing that they have so much security in there or a bad thing that they need so much security in there. It's my first time here so I may be over thinking the situation, maybe all those FiveO's were just there for lunch or something. Anyways, this place was very interesting, people need to come here when they visit Philly, I recommend it.

I love this place. If you not sure where to go to grab a quick bit. For breakfast, lunch or dinner. Reading terminal is the place to be. They have varieties of place in this one big building. Every time I go. I try something different & I never get disappointed
What can you say about the Reading Terminal? Whatever your heart desires is at the Reading Terminal, meats, deserts, spices, breads. You name it, they have it.

I love coming to the Reading Market. Yes, it's hustle and bustle and a fight sometimes for the food you want. Come early to avoid the crowds...before noon on the weekends. If you want the  breakfast at Amish Eating Place, come when it opens. Don't expect gourmet food here, but expect good, hearty local fare and great fresh produce that is discounted when the market is about to close.

Some notes:

Bassetts--it's not the creamiest artisanal ice cream around,  but hey, it's part of the Philly experience. I had the pomengranate berry chocolate chunk and it satisfied my ice cream craving for the day.

Amish bakery counter-for some reason, the men seem to ignore me when I go to pay. The women are much more customer service oriented. I have tasted many of the pastries--they are cheap and taste it. Too much sugar and too little butter. I usually only get the  breads with glazed toppings. The other goods are nondescript. And what's with all the unhappy children forced to work so early? Child labor??? During Amish week in PA(in July), don't miss the fried doughnuts. They are divine.

Le Bus-this place got some bad reviews from other Yelpers. I've never had a bad bread or bagel here. I love the cherry apple bagels and the olive bread. The day I waas there, they had a low turnout and too much inventory so they were discounting their bread at the end of the day. Whoohooo....

Flying Monkey-the cupcakes are good but just okay for the price.

Metropolitan Bakery-prices are higher;  everything they sell is delectable.

Termini Bros.-how can you sell sweets and be so snotty and rude? Someone should send all the servers to customer service class. Are their pastries good? Sure? But I've walked away from this place at least 3 times when I was ignored. And if you're selling biscotti at $20 a lb, you need to smile.

The chocolatiers Muellers etc....-if you are in to high end gourmet chocolate, take a pass. If you just want  a piece of Philly traditional chocolate, go for it.

Eating area--needs more cleaning people!

Bathrooms-try to find someone else to go. I do!

Oh, and if the crowds dismay you, Chinatown is just around the corner.

Really busy, but also really fun with great food. The Cajun food place was amazing, maybe a little salty, and Beiler's donuts was also incredible. 

It's fun to just walk through the whole building too, if it's not too busy.

I adore this place. It is like a HUGE farmer's market. I like the fact that I can get fresh organic produce while sipping Old City Coffee (my addiction). In addition, the food stands have something for EVERYONE.  I don't recommend going on the weekend unless you go about two huors before closing.

Had my first date with my now husband here! SO MANY great foods to choose from! The market is always bustling with great energy. It can get a bit crowded so beware but the food makes it worth it! There's a little something for everyone's tastes from carved sandwiches to ice cream to crepes and falafel to cupcakes and fresh fruit! 

We even did our engagement photos here and they were awesome!

The selection of local cheese, fish, meat, sweet, and vegetable shops is astounding!  Everything you find there is of quality and Prices are fair.  I wish I lived closer so I could shop here everyday.

ok I must say I was warned about this place!! A must stop market in Philly that has everything from cheesesteaks to fresh produce. After browsing for 30  minutes I wanted To try one of the pulled pork sandwiches. The line was so long that I settled on eating at one of the food counters that served New Orleans inspired cuisine. My shrimp poboy wrap was tasty and inexpensive.
Picked up some fresh fruit and nuts and few caramel cookies that were divine. I will be back today.... And probably tomorrow!!

Wow I wish my stomach had more space for food! There's so many great vendors to try! 

I came on a Saturday afternoon and it was packed! I got to try 2 different vendors, but wasn't my first picks, because of the lines. Our tactic was to try 1 thing at as many vendors as we could. Sadly, we tapped out at 2 + coffee. 

A lot of the places don't have a seating area so that was a little hassle. Still a great place to visit. If I had time, I would go back and try a few more places there! Probably need to go back at least 5 times using the same tactic to make some damage. Have fun!

This place was better than expected! Definitely the best pizza place to buy a slice. The slices are huge and every bite was better than the next! The slices are very thin but it still had the right amount of crunch. You can't go wrong with the pepperoni or cheese slice. 

The place is very small so don't expect to eat inside. There's some tables outside though.

Lesson learned. 
Never go on a Sunday.
Many stands were closed. 
The crowds were over the top and the baby stroller crews were rude. 
I may update at a later time when I've visited without the raging hordes. 

Having said that, we did find several stands open without the above mentioned issues. A nice Cheese stand, a bakery and Condiment where the clerk was actually helpful and not preoccupied with his Saturday night date recap (cheese place) or too busy to make any suggestions (bakery) - maybe she thought we were to fat already. 

Im leaving a separate review for the diner we tried. 

I get that people working there are probably over worked & under paid but IF I was a tourist instead of a new local I'd not be inclined to return. 

We are planning to go on a weekday soon & hope we have better results.

This place is awesome. This is equivalent to Seattle's Pike Place, SF's Ferry building, Boston's Quincy Market LA's Grand Central Market, etc. It's a place of culture and food and history. There's butchers, bakeries, candy, fruit, oysters, ice cream, beer, samosas, cheesesteaks, cookies, sausages, crepes, fried chicken, peking duck...... 70+ vendors of food and gift items. You might as well prepare yourself to stay for breakfast, lunch and dinner (an early dinner because it closes at 6 PM). Many of the vendors appear to be family owned and operated, so you feel good supporting these small businesses.

I had it bookmarked before I got to Philly, but it was right across the street from the convention center where I had my conference, so I would've bumped into it anyway. When I walked in, 10 different wonderful smells pulled me in different directions. I merged into the flow of traffic and began to survey my options. Over the course of a few days of meals I tried the roast pork from Tommy DiNics, apple dumpling from Dutch eating place, corned beef from Hershel's, and ice cream from Bassett's (America's oldest ice cream company!). Nothing disappointed! The biggest problem? Deciding what to eat.

The most important thing to know is DON'T COME ON SUNDAYS! Many of the vendors are closed on Sundays and you will not get the full experience and miss out on some of the best reading terminal has to offer.
Great restaurant, great menus, friendly employees, clean restaurant, neat appearance of all employees with team works

Tons of great stores. This place is a bit touristy but also fun to stop by as a local. Whether you're stopping by for breakfast, lunch, or just to walk around, you won't be disappointed. Caution: it does get very crowded around lunch and on the weekends so it may be hard to find a seat. Make sure to stop by beilers doughnuts before you leave.

Love this place. Can find all sorts of fantastic food here. It's all kinda expensive, but definitely worth checking out. I forget the names now, but there is some amazing ice cream, bbq ribs, fried chicken, and Dutch apple pies and such here. Definitely miss coming here with friends on weekends.
Omg what fun.  Had falafel, tabouli, hummus, pita and juice. Perfect lunch. Was going to try another place for dinner but they were closed. Darn!  Will be back for lunch tomorrow

I come here often, especially for the Beilers Donuts! They're made fresh daily, have endless amounts of flavor, and will leave you wanting to come back.

Pro tip - buy a 6 or more and they'll cost $1 per donut! That's less than Dunkin for much higher quality!

Busy busy busy. But clean well staffed and managed well. After watching the manager defuse an irate unreasonable LOUD angry woman, he politely delivered our food and spent time in the dining room at different tables.
Thank god for RTM! I can find almost anything here- good produce, great spices, tasty treats, honey, such a variety of spreads and jams, dried fruits and chocolate. I love this place.

This is a must do stop, if in Philly.
You can find anything to eat- especially in a group. No one can say they can't find anything to eat (although my son did try to Eeyore himself here)... he did find a bagel sandwich which surpassed his expectations.

Plenty of spots to sit and eat. Breakfast items abound for morning (or all day, if choose)
Three restaurants to sit and eat.

Loved the produce- sometimes hard to get while traveling.

Highly recommend- great people watching... great food, great experience.

Love love love it here ! 

Cheesesteaks were amazing here but you gotta make sure you go to the right one.  BY GEORGE ! We got way overpriced but delicious chocolate covered strawberries and breakfast at a cute sit down place across from the cheese place. 

For all my foodies, you will love it too!

This is a must-visit for anyone traveling to Philly. It's packed full of interesting, fun food options. I went here with my wife to grab lunch and the atmosphere is exciting. There are rows and rows of markets, restaurants, bars, shops. I would be shocked if you could not find something you liked here.

My wife got a chicken schnitzel sandwich and an apple soda. I got a grilled cheese with chips. Afterwards, we grabbed some nice fresh produce at a market. We both enjoyed our meals and had a great time wandering around taking it all in. 5 stars for sure
Unbelievable! The food, the atmosphere, the selection.  I have nothing but great things to say about this Market which I stumbled across completely by accident while in Philly for a day.

Best Spots & Menu Item: Millers Twist for a salted pretzel (see my review), DiNic's for a roast pork hoagie with sharp provolone and long hots, Bieler's Donuts for a maple bacon donut. 

A must see and eat in Philadelphia. This is one reason why I am happy to be a resident of this great city. Although I have listed my favorites, you can't go wrong here. Prices are fair and everyone accepts cards. The ambiance feels vibrant, local, family run, fresh, clean, and just fun. Come here just to walk around, but my recommendation is to arrive hungry!

Hot tip: Let your friend order for you while you look for a seat. It is a daunting task to find a seat with all your delicious goodies in tote.

Aside from the fact that this is an awesome place to take out-of-town visitors, don't forget to take advantage of the awesome market. The vegetables are always fresh and you can't beat the deal on meat and seafood. If you live in the city The prices are lower and the quality is better than most supermarket. 

In terms of where to eat:
Hershel's - brisket Reuben and matzoh ball soup
Beilers donuts - worth the wait; get a variety
Beilers bakery - 1/2 cina buns & pie slices
Becks Cajun - sausage chicken gumbo
Olympia gyro - gyro combo
4th street cookies - black & white, snicker doodles 
Termini bros - cannoli 

Tip1: since DiNic's is famous (overrated in my opinion), The line is always very long. However that line does not include the wait for the seat at the bar surrounding the booth. Wait for a seat to open up and skip the line- they will serve you directly & chances are you're going to end up anyways 

Tip2: The Pennsylvania Dutch booths are not open every day so make sure you check the website before getting your hopes up for some awesome food
Tiny bit small, horribly crowded, and not the cleanest. But it's a real, living market, not some showcase. Philly, this is your gem. Keep loving it to death.

The best thing about this place isn't the food; it's the sense of hominess you feel when you walk in. The diversity of the stands is amazing, and you feel welcome in any corner of the marketplace. Unlike other food courts I've been to, the Reading Terminal community actually feels unique. Each stand is a treasure; it feels personal and welcoming, unlike the Panda Expresses and Subways or the snobby "upscale" food courts with celebrity chefs in NYC.

That being said, I don't want to play down the food, which was really delicious. Beck's Cajun Cafe was my favorite. DiNic's was good too. The variety can be overwhelming though and I did stand around for a good 5-10 minutes figuring out what to get. If I ever find myself in Philly again, I will definitely be back.

where does one start when talking about reading terminal? if you're visiting or if you live here, the terminal is a staple in philadelphia. go for lunch, and take 20 minutes to make up your mind what to get. it's huge, is always busy, and fun to just putz around. fresh veggies, meat, fish, and cheese abound!

also the best little candy nook EVER, with candy you haven't seen since you were a kid, and another candy booth where i got the huge swirly lollipops for our wedding. 

also, i still daydream about the whopper flavored ice cream i had here years ago.

Honeygrow is one of my favorite spots right now and this particular visit -- I was very disappointed. The noodles to my favorite meal was changed and it just did not taste the same.

I always order the red coconut curry with: roasted shrimp, rice noodles (the noodles were different and the employee stated HG should have posted that the noodles are different), jalapeños, scallions, pineapples, cilantro, with extra red coconut curry. I did not know the change in the noodles (which were thinner) would have changed my favorite meal. It wasn't the same. At least the Mexican cola was good. The bread would be better if it was warm.

I order at this particular HG often and something is always wrong lol. I cannot even deny it. R.I.P to my favorite red coconut curry meal (if they do not bring  the original rice noodles back)!
Wide variety of food to choose from! Got some gumbo at the cajun place to die for. Pies from the Dutch, olives from the creamery, duck, gyros excellent.

Stop in hungry, everything you'd want in one place. It is a little overwhelming when you first walk in but take it all in and order from as many places as possible. We scored a table, then took turns choosing different items to try within our group. This was a great decision and completely suggest you try as well. It allowed us to eat a variety of items and none were a disappointment.

The Reading Terminal Market is kind of one of those things about Philly that appeals to both tourists and locals. If you're a foodie, you'll love it here. Just beware, the crowds can get pretty intense, especially on the weekends and especially around lunch.

So the market is kind of half actual market where you can buy meat, seafood, cheese, produce, canned and packaged goods, etc., and take it home, and then the rest of the stands in the market are all kinds of varieties of lunch counters, basically. There's sushi. There's Greek. There's Thai. There's cheesesteaks (well, duh... but if you really want a great steak, go to Pat's in South Philly or at least Jim's on South Street). Some places actually have counters where you can sit. Otherwise, there are communal seating areas with tables and such for people who want to sit and eat. It's a great place to taste and explore but bring some patience and a kind attitude with you.

Two cautions:
1. Many of the lunch places especially are cash only. There is an ATM in the building but you'd be better off to come packing with some cash.
2. The parking rates around the market are atrocious and the parking meter people are Nazis. If you are lucky enough to snag a street spot, make SURE you are parked in a spot that is for cars (some are for motorcycles only) and that you note how much time you have. Some of the spots are really tricky and are only like 15 minute spaces. You can also try nearby Chinatown -- it's only about a three block walk -- but parking there can be dicey, too. If you cannot find street parking, there are two nearby decks that have a deal with the market. Park in the deck, spend $10+ with a market merchant, have them validate your receipt, and your parking will only be $4. 2 hour limit, but that's plenty of time to get in, look around and get out. Info here: http://www.readingterminalmarket.org/about/parking/

Tourist trap for sure, but wonderful all the same. Reading Terminal Market is the go-to place if either you're not sure what you want to eat or if your party members all want something different. This is basically an open-air market, just inside. The bulk of the vendors are street-food style, fast-casual restaurants. So many sandwich options!

There are a couple neat gems amid the sandwiches, such as the used book store. It had great hard-covers, many of which were vintage printings. I thought about buying a new book to enjoy on the train or airplane, but like everything else they were overpriced. 

Don't come in expecting immaculate resort amenities or to be waited on, hand and food. The Market is all about its gritty, Old-Town Philly charm. One piece of advice: don't look up.

Having been to Philly a few times, I was excited to visit Bourse Market. It's a renovated food hall, very bright and clean. There are plenty of options to choose from, with food ranging from grilled cheese, to dumplings, to cheesesteaks. We walked around the entire market before deciding on La Lo. 

La Lo serves Filipino food. I was familiar with all the items and was excited to try some dishes. We ordered lumpia to share and each got an order of longsilog. Lumpia are fried Filipino egg rolls and they were delicious. The dipping sauce was light and flavorful. The longsilog is Filipino sausage; their version is served with garlic rice, vegetables, and a soft boiled egg. The longsilog was awesome, with the egg and rice, it was a fantastic combination. 

The staff was very friendly and helpful. Philly is lucky to have a great spot to try Filipino food!

New-age take on classic dumplings. They offer both savory and sweet dumplings such as cheesecake & pumpkin pie. Something for carnivores and veg-heads alike. I for one certainly appreciate the vegan options they have! 

Theses tasty balls are filled pretty well and although they are fried, they're never too doughy or overly greasy. Freshly fried and hot is obviously when they're the best!

The variety of choices make doing a mix and match order for our family with different diets simple. Edamame are definitely a fave with the kids. Hubs favors the buffalo and bacon mac and a go to for me is the cauliflower lime. Yum! 

These dumplings are one of my favorite items to eat at Night Market and other outdoor festivals. Pop 'em on the go! Not sure if I would go out of my way to eat them in store, but definitely check them out if you see them on the go!
Ordered from Termini Bakery. Excellent if South South Philly location. Stale dried up pastries in Reading Terminal with mark up price.

I made a mistake coming here. I walked in to a nearly empty restaurant and excitedly ordered my chicken and Lamb Platter to eat on the subway ride back to my dorm. Only to open my bag and pull out an order that didn't belong to me. 
My deepest apologies to the lady who's wraps I got, but whatever you ordered wasn't great. So enjoy the meal.

I was just looking for a good sandwich for lunch when I stumbled into this market hall. Immediately it hit me and I was in love with this place. The stands, the variety ... the everything! Seriously, if I ever was left in this place alone over night I would die from overeating. Everything here looks as I want to try it. If you're hungry and in the area: go here!

We decided to come here because the Mr. just had to try the roast pork sandwhich from dinic's he saw on the food channel man vs. Food. One word.... heavenly!! The roast pork with provolone and broccoli rabe had my taste buds doing a dance!! A 100% must try wheb you are there. There is so much different places to eat with many varieties for any kinda food lover. From coffee to an oyster bar to halal food and steaks! Beer and ice creams! Chocolate and cannolis. Seriously a foodie heaven!! Plus the different types of mini shops you can find some cool and quirky finds. For our first time there we loved it. Dont be alarmed if you have to walk a bit to find a ppace to sit. But trust me ypu will find a place and many more cool thibhs in literally every corner! And there is a parking garage across the street. I do recommend taking your ticket and getting it validated! You will save about $20 on parking if you eat somewhere there and spend $10+. Other than that I highly recommend this is a must when visiting Philadelphia!!

Stopped in on my travels South.  Excellent service, fast and accurate.  The food was hot and the folks were friendly and polite.  This place is clean and appears to be fairly new.  The owner /operator was very involved and made sure everything went smoothly.  Great meal!

Been waiting years for a Pilipino food joint to pop up  near Center City. It's a hip version of the mom and pops restaurants I grew up with in Manila and Southern California, but still keeping comfort and soul of the food without all the frills. This is what Pinoy food should be, down to earth, accessible and made from the heart.

What an experience!  Came her on Saturday afternoon of Memorial day weekend and the place was packed!  There are a lot of aisles of food vendors, lots of different kinds and they all look so good!  We got a Mediterranean platter from one of the vendors, I only waited about 5 minutes for the food to come out!  My friend tried to order a sandwich from a fancy cheese shop, but just as her order was being placed their panini press broke.  We picked up some drinks from some deli type stores, and then found a seat in a food court type seating area.  Some of the restaurants have their own seating, but since we were meeting in the middle we had to sit in the busier food court area (which only took about 5 minutes to find a seat for 2).  Then on the way out we grabbed a donut from this place where Amish women were baking them fresh in front of you (the line wrapped around the corner but went SO FAST, and was totally worth it!).  And it was $1.50!  This is not a place for a nice relaxing sit down meal, but is definitely a great experience if you're ready to deal with the crowds!

Always fun to browse this market. Brought home to NYC wonderful pastrami and corned beef sandwiches. Highly recommend this market.
Wanted to buy some meat but the buther I stopped at had no ice for my 3 hour trip home.
This is the coolest part of Philly, especially when it's really cold out and you want to see a bunch of things indoors...i dont like being outside when the wind hurts my face.
What a fun place full of choices.  You can go everyday and not have the same thing twice.  The people there are friendly and fast.  Great place for lunch and shopping for dinner and gifts.

My wife and I went there for lunch and enjoyed the food and the great drinks. I had a bloody which is their version of a Bloody Mary. It was a great choice and my wife had the special rye cocktail that she loved. My wife's' burger was great and my Thai salad was delicious.Our server Anna was very attentive and checked on us frequently.

There are so many great dining options here. My personal favorites:

The Train Wreck Po Boy at Beck's Cajun Cafe

The apple filled doughnuts at Beiler's Bakery

The Valley Thunder grilled cheese sandwich at Meltkraft

The apple dumplings at Dutch Eating Place

I LOVE THIS PLACE. It's one of the best markets I've been to. You can't really go wrong with anything you get here although you could look on Yelp for recommendations. In LA, we have the Grand Central Market which is similar but smaller. The food and variety here is much better though. It can get pretty crowded especially during lunch hour. As for parking, there's parking structures that has validation but you still pay about $5 for 2-hour parking (validation comes with minimum $10 purchase).

I love this place. Every time I visit I have to go and try a different spot to eat, I want to try them all!  The diversity and culture is incredible. I try to eat at different places each time and haven't had any complaints. The Amish donuts are incredible. The crepes, chicken, icecream. I feel like I'm walking back in history.

Since my last review, I stopped in again and had a great experience! I was able to order from the kiosk (next to it was hand sanitizer), easily placed my order, customer service was great, and the place was very clean!

Came back and ate there. Ordered my usual: red coconut curry, roasted shrimp, jalapeños, pineapple, scallions, cilantro, with the original rice noodles! They brought them back y'all! I was so happy! 

Also, reached out to Michelle, Guest Experience Specialist who reimbursed me for my unsatisfied past experience (which I was not looking for or expecting a refund). It's a great feeling when a business values their customers and go out their way to make them happy!

honeygrow is still one of my favorite spots in Philly!

Can be tough to find seating if you're grabbing a bite to eat while you're there, but the eclectic mix of food and goods makes it worth the trip. Also, I'm obsessed with the chapstick from Bee Natural. Better than Burt's Bees.

Still a top destination for me, but definitely something to check out if you are an out-of-town visitor.  Sometimes you're able to catch some live music while chowing down.  I particularly love the Herbiary for loose teas and other healthy gifts during the holiday seasons (or whenever, really) and the Thai kitchen is still the best for curry salmon with broccoli and rice (this is a cash only joint).  If you aren't shy, ask the people working the cheese counters for samples of the most expensive stuff they've got.  They can't say no.  Don't forget the dollar bags of produce at Iovines before you leave for home.

Definitely a cool place to stop if you are in the area. Its an indoor building where you can walk around and choose from many places to eat. I chose crepes and really enjoyed it. They also have a variety of shops inside too. I bought some candles.
Its a cool place to walk around. There is a main area to sit down and eat as well.

So let me start by saying that I used to love this place! The food was delicious, the people were nice, the ambiance was welcoming. But in the last couple months, the quality of all these things just went downhill and I find that very upsetting. I am vegetarian and I ordered a paneer roll. Instead I got Chicken. The same thing happened to my friend. The tomato gravy lost its balanced flavor, the paneer tastes stale and the people have become very unwelcoming. I don't think I'll be going back again...
My favorite location! Fast and efficient ordering process and excellent customer service.
Fantastic magical place. Love it!  The creperie is the bomb!

Loud, crowded, vibrant and full of personality! We thoroughly enjoyed walking around and looking at all the food choices at the market. There was something for everyone there. From American, Chinese, Thai, Indian, etc. meals to donuts, cookies, ice cream and fudge; there are many choices. We didn't stop at the pour house but it was busy and looked inviting.
This place is huge, but it doesn't seem very sanitary.  If you're looking to eat lunch here, skip it.  The food places are all tourist traps selling pricey horrible food.
When I first moved to the city this was one of my first spots to eat. So many cool places to get a bite and the cookies at famous 4th street are the bestttttt!!!

Went there with friends and the food was great enough to have lured me back again alone although the place is about an hour from where I live. Their rolls are very good. My favorite is the Achari Paneer roll. The aaloo paneer roll is quite filling although can be made a little more flavourful.  My non vegetarian friends loved their rolls too. Their lassi selection is wonderful too. The only thing I didn't like a lot was their Kala khatta drink. 

Will definitely recommend!

What can you say about Reading Terminal Market? It's the #1 spot for me in terms of taking friends from out of town. You can spend 1.5-2 hours in here easily, eating a nice meal, doing a little shopping (food or otherwise), and it's right near the Convention Center & Chinatown so it really is a great jumping off spot for a touristy weekend day. You can't leave without eating some Beiler's. The hype is real!
Great place...too many choices. Seating is the challenge but absolute must if visiting Philly.

This place gets really crowded around noon time and its crazy hard to move around. In some ways its part of the experience of being there. I prefer to go when it is less crowded and I can take my time and see all the sellers. There is pretty much something for everyone here. I personally love the cookies sold by Metropolitan Bakery.  I've also found the produce sold at Iovine Bros to be fresh and delicious. RTM will certainly not disappoint if you don't mind the crowds.

I like this place despite it being a tourist trap, it's always crazy busy, but the food is worth it. There is a ton of variety when you come here, Indian, Greek, Thai, Italian and of course Amish. The Amish are the best bakers in the world and their cakes and pastries are the best, they're fresh and fairly cheap. If you're a cook, there is a ton of food you can find here for your recipes, fresh produce, fish, meats and hard to find ingredients and cheeses. The sights, sounds and smells are enough to visit here even if you're just passing through and the bathrooms here are very clean and big enough to handle the crowds you'll see here.

A Philly Best!! The Reading Market is my jam!! Always packed, but damn that food and shopping is amazing!! The The roasted pork broccoli sandwich was more tender and enjoyable than the beef brisket one.

If you are looking for a variety of tasty local and unique treats, bring an empty belly and prepare for a great day.  This place get super crowded in the weekends but it's part of the appeal.  You can dine in or shop and make a fresh meal at home. If you are in philly, it's a must visit.

We Love Reading Terminal Market Especially The Omnish Everything Be So Fresh And Good They Cooked Food Is Very Good To We Love Their Fruit And Vegetables We Rather Spend Our Money There Then The Super Markets Cause Nothing At Reading Terminal Never Got Any Of Us Sick Love It There And Will Definitely Be Going Back Real Soon......

I love RTM! So many great things to eat, all served with a side of great people watching. My favorite spots include the Fair Food Farmstand, Valley Shepherd Creamery, the Cookbook Stall and Beiler's but there are so many other fantastic spots. You can usually find exactly what you're in the mood to eat. 

Reading Terminal Market is a wonderful Philly tradition.

Had oyster po boy at Pearl oyster house for lunch. What a ripoff, a measly 3 over fried, over salted oysters on a huge doughy hoagy roll with lettuce & tomato - for $8.50 plus tax. Not eating here again.

Every one should visit Reading Terminal Market when they come to Philly. It's so cool! It's basically a giant building with many food vendors. In addition you can buy produce and meats, and other things made by the locals. Some of my favorites here include the Dutch eating place (must try the scrapple and apple dumpling), Kevin Parker fried chicken, fresh squeeze juice and smoothies, the beef jerky, and the hand rolled donuts. Google a list of things you must eat here and try them all if you have the time and belly for it. You won't be disappointed! 

Reading terminal market is one of the places in Philly I miss so you! I was a tourist here and my husband and I ate here almost every single day. We even bought gifts here for our family. Delicious gifts! It's such a cool place and we loved coming here and finding a new surprise each time. We even bought fresh organic fruits here for our toddler to eat when we were in town. The bananas are so good and so sweet! Very cheap as well! I hope to be able to visit again someday.
Great atmosphere coupled with delicious food - something that you can't miss if you're a foodie in Philly.

This is by far the largest most overcrowded market I have been to thus far. I love places like this but on a Saturday morning/early afternoon, it was hard to get through the blobs of people and the endlessly long lines. We had already eaten before coming here-do not make that same mistake! There is something for every taste here and plenty of dessert options too so my advice would be to come hungry! If I was local I would definitely come here to buy all my vegetables, meats, and cheeses!
