The grilled cheese booth looked particularly interesting as did the number of Pennsylvania Dutch booths in the market. I also noticed a single spot that serves as a bar, which is nice to have so your whole group can get drinks and then choose separately where you want to dine. The only purchase we made here was at Old City Coffee for my husband. They forgot his order so not a great experience. I would definitely return the next time I'm in Philly but I would change one thing: I'd come hungry so I can eat my way through the market as one should!

I love Reading for their fresh local produce! But it's also a must anytime I have friends from out of town visiting. So many options to choose from and so much fun energy. It's always a little crazy, especially on the weekends but it's worth it and adds to the experience. I'm a huge fan of the crepes, ribs, smoothies, spice shop, cheese shop, and fresh baked cookies!

I try to control my fat kid tendencies in public, so walking into the Reading Terminal Market was quite an exercise in self control. I think I started hyperventilating as I walked in. I was also kind of ashamed that I was so giddy just being in a place with so many different kinds of food. I didn't even get to really look around as I was there with co-workers, but I spied those apple dumplings on the way out and I'm definitely going back for one. 

I had a sandwich from DeNic's and a lemonade from the Amish Dairy. The sharp provolone was great, I must say. Co-workers got some ribs from Delilah's which also looked really good. Got to go back.

Love this place. So many great eateries to choose from. Seating can be rough at peak times, but you can't go wrong with the food. Love the candy shop- I am forgetting the name- they are so kind and the candy is amazing!

This is the best market in town. The place offers cheapest items, fresh and baked goods. I come here quite often, the place is close and offers variety. The meat over here is always fresh.
It can be really crowded at times, however the wait is worth the quality. The breakfast over here is another plus. Good location, excellent variety.

This is a fantastic restaurant. There are not many in this area, and love to have good places to eat close to home. The food and people are wonderful, food is priced right. Beverages however are the more expensive side. I would order a cocktail or two but it's too pricy. This is a must try for the food, pulled duck sandwich is the best!!

No matter what your heart desires, you're sure to find it at the terminal. I go for Carmine's and eat while browsing. The Amish section is closed Sundays, so if you crave their pretzels or ice cream (or both!) don't come on Sunday. ALSO, not many people know this, but the terminal validates parking! Park in any nearby garage and bring your ticket so it can be stamped. You can get a stamp at virtually any place where a good or food can be purchased. You need to purchase something for a validation. You can stay in the terminal all day or just 10 mins and it will only cost you $4.00 to park with a validated ticket. Sometimes I park, run errands, hop in the terminal for some grub, validate my ticket and then go get my car. It's a cheap way to park in the city most of the day in a garage.

Where do I begin? This was my first stop in Philadelphia, fresh off the plane and having just had the chance to drop off luggage at my friend's house. All we knew was that we were hungry and also wanted to take in some sights. So we walked down the street and headed straight for the market. And this place was PACKED! I was not prepared for the onslaught of sights and sounds and choices. I had researched some things to try - such as the pretzels, donuts, and pork sandwich - but that barely scratched the surface of what this market has to offer. I mean, c'mon, chocolate noses! 

The first day, we tried the pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and sweet pepper and it was quite tasty. Also loved the pretzel. The donuts were unique although not my favorite, but there are definitely so many to choose from you are bound to find something you enjoy - we tried the key lime, oreo creme, and sugar. 

The next day we needed a quick breakfast and had to stop by for famous scrapple and the hot apple dumpling. When it came down to a choice of adding heavy or whipped cream, I decided to be daring and go with some heavy cream and I have never been happier with my decision! That hot apple dumpling was one of my favorite things. And scrapple was unique. I ended up adding some syrup and enjoyed it. Definitely not something I get back home!

This place is a must for both tourists and locals. Good food, good prices.
Amazing.  Anything you can think of is there. Its a bit overwhelming, but once you decide what you want, its worth the wait.
Best pizza of my life, it's truly magical. Go eat it. Also, they were super polite and kind.

One of the most amazing place in Philadelphia. The globally inspired food -- available for breakfast, lunch, dinner and dessert as well as for snacking -- is the main draw, while butchers, bakers, chocolatiers, cheesemongers and produce vendors offer food, ingredients and goods for sale.

From scrapple and samosas to soul food and smoothies, Reading Terminal Market is such a fantastic place to eat that it can be tough to choose what to get. So here are 10 of our favorite things to eat at Reading Terminal Market, the nation's oldest continuously operating farmers' market.

Awesome place! Great food & great beer/cocktails. Lots of cheap but high quality food and very different kinds of dishes too (lamb neck gravy/ pork ear lettuce wraps are what I got..sooo good) definitely recommend this place for any occasion.

This place is amazing. I lived in Philly for 1 month and ate here more than 5 times. Right across from the convention center. Always busy and full of tourists. Ive eaten the pot roast sandwich at the Amish stand which is awesome. The gyro stand is good. The mexican burrito spot is alright, though I'd try something different. The Asian noodle bowl spot isn't worth it, theres better places. There was a smoothy spot that was delicious. Its not too expensive in any of these places. On one side theres fresh fruits and stuff to buy grocery too. Definitely a worthwhile trip for anyone visiting Philly.

1 star to me is to generous they need zero as option!!

Before writing Review what I noticed:
I'm really not surprised at this Chain/Franchise's low reviews for more than just this 1 location after my experience. I can tell that the higher ups in their chain of command has little to NO concern about the lack of quality service that the faces of their Company offers when coming in to work. I don't fault the Product (the horrible staff) I blame the hire ups who allow them to operate in this manor. Smh

MY HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE:
I want to start by saying that I used to love Chipotle and used to go all the time about a year or two ago so I was definitely excited to go back to an old fav, but my order today is def the last time I'll waste any money at this place especially at this Cottman Ave/ Roosevelt Mall location!! 
I ordered my food via Doordash which I normally use UberEats but for some reason
Uber Eats don't pick up from Chipotle (which I def should of took that as a warning shot lol) but I wasn't to upset because I actually receive a 15% DoorDash when paying with my Cashapp card so that outweighed the UberEats dilemma.
I was busy doing a few things at home so time gets away from me and I haven't even noticed an hour has gone by with no updates from either DoorDash or Chipotle. So I go to the Doordash app and found no way no reach out to DoorDash or Chipotle in ways of providing contact numbers or DM options other than the call or message option for the Driver which makes no sense to me because all do us drive how can they tell me why my food is still not ready. As soon as I placed my order I immediately was able to track my driver's location In addition to seeing my orders prep time and eta pick up to delivery time which started off as showing about 30-40min which is reasonable given that I ordered close to 6pm-ish. Again I lose track of time and my daughter who I also ordered for asked me the status. At this point about 30 more  min. has gone by!! I'm annoyed to see no messages from DoorDash or Chipotle. 
I tried calling their number thats all over the internet including their own website and to no surprise the phone number was no longer in service!!! How can a place as well known as Chipotle not pay their phone bill??? 
 phone number for the restaurant 215.695.2083NUMBER DISCONNECTED!! It's so hard for me wrap my head around the notion that not only have I've been waiting close to 2hrs for food from a place considered Fast Food and already made!!! It  took over 2hrs for my food to be delivered when I live 10min away. 
Each time I tried to cancel DoorDash kept saying it's coming and offering credit which annoyed me as well because they weren't responding as quickly as I needed to them as well!! 
I ordered my food close to 6pm and received my delivery at 7:50ish. 
I ordered 2 burritos, 1 order of chips & 2 beverages and included a $5 tip for the driver which brought my total close to $40. The chips was greased soaked and disgusting I immediately through it all away.  I will NEVER ORDER FROM CHIPOTLE AGAIN. 

MY SUGGESTION: 
Invest in your Company again when Chipotle first popped up everywhere, I suggest hiring a Chick-Filet Staff Member who clearly train their staff members in the Marines or something  (doesn't even matter from which department you take a staff member from at chick-filet,   it can be the person who comes out to ensure the tables are clean or maybe their window cleaners  all of the are on point ALWAYS) to train your staff. This place has RE-written the book on 
*Customer Service,
*Customer Satisfaction
*Customer Appreciation
*Employee satisfaction/Appreciation 
And sooooooo much more!!
They take service serious!!!  Not one staff member strays from this Companies mission. I def don't see Chipotle being around within the next year or so if additional measures are not made to change things.

Crowded market full of different food sellers and little shops. We have a couple places like this in California. As long as you know you'll have to wait in a line, you can probably find whatever your heart desires.
Great place, A ton of things to do. Love going on rainy days.

walked a mile just to get a donut
and It was worth it

By far one of the coolest places in all of Philly! It was so good I went there twice in my few day visit! I wish I had gotten the names of the two places I went to as they were fabulous! I got a bagel sandwich that was a BLT with cream cheese on an everything bagel and I'm still craving another one ever since. 

The second meal was at the classic looking diner. We sat at the bar and I had a sausage egg and cheese sandwich that hit the spot perfectly!

This market is like sense overload. Being from Seattle and used to Pike's Place I was so happy to find this place. There's rows and rows of various vendors where you can find any food you may be craving! There's also fresh produce and a ton of fresh desserts that will for sure make your mouth water. I definitely recommend  walking all the rows before making a decision of where you may want to eat!
Omg! Heaven on Earth! So many vendors! The jerky shop is amazing, the pretzels are tasty, the gyros are good, and the shops are fun to shop in! What a dream. I can't wait to return in the future.

This place is okay.  Its great to have another late night option in the neighborhood.  I've been here twice and I'm already bored of their menu.  Granted I haven't tried half the stuff on there... but I kinda don't want to.  Either it seems a tad overpriced ($15 for a seafood blt, or arepas?  really?) or just not interesting to me.  

-pork nuggets:  okay.  pretty much what you'd expect
-chicharrones:  bleh.  good thing they were only $3.  even a touch more salt would have made them more palatable.  would not get again.  
-pulled bbq duck sandwich: good, but the duck is lost in the sauce of the sandwich.  why bother using duck when you can barely tell that its duck?  also the choice of bread (ciabatta) makes it difficult to eat with such a soft filling
-industry burger:  good.  pretty standard, but not good enough for me to make a specific trip here.
-arancini:  good.  this was a special menu item.  a touch underseasoned, but nice.
-pig ear lettuce wraps:  meh.  disappointing.  the pig was chewy, not crispy.  maybe because it was due to being doused in franks.  i love franks as much as the next gal, but that's all i could taste, chewy ribbons of franks.
-lamb neck gravy:  oh my yes.  so good.  would get this again and again.  and the dollop of ricotta is a nice touch.

Beer selection is nice.  Tried a couple brews i'd never heard of (and when it comes to beers i DO get around...).  It wasn't very full either time i'd been (weekday nights).  there are tvs playing the game, and a snazy electronic jukebox that accepts credit cards.  bathrooms (and cigarette machine) downstairs.
Huge variety...fresh food choices....produce, seafood, vegetarian/vegan, "ethnic" options

Kati rolls are like little gyros or burritos in case you didnt know. This place makes really tasty ones and the protein/rice plates are lit. Great sauces, open super late on weekends. What could be better?

Needed a quick dinner option in Center City and wandered into Masala Kitchen based on the Yelp reviews and was not let down --- we can't wait to come back and try more of the Kati rolls!

There are somewhere around a dozen options for kati rolls, ranging around $5 each. For a full meal, I'd recommend around 2 rolls per person, perhaps a third depending on appetite. I ordered the chicken masala (chicken bordered on rubbery, but the incredible flavor made up for the texture) and the Aloo Paneer (potato and cheese with mint-coriander chutney, which was amazing). BF also ordered the chicken masala along with the beef tikka roll, which I felt was salty, but he loved. On the side, they offer white yogurt sauce, which helps to offset the spice level and add a pop of flavor, or red chili sauce if you need an extra kick. 

They offer counter service with plenty of seating, though they do a lot of take-out business as well. Staff was courteous; food took maybe 5-10 minutes to be prepared. They advertise late hours on Friday and Saturday --- I can imagine their kati rolls are delicious after a night out.
Amazing place. Adore Iovine's for fresh fruits and veggies. The Head Nut is fantastic for spices, flour, sugar, etc.

If you are particular about your food and knowing where it comes from, or that it's of good quality, I can't imagine you will like this place.  It's basically an indoor market with purveyors of produce, meat and fish (I saw no evidence of anything being organic, free-range, antibiotic-free etc.) with the majority of places there selling what is essentially fast food (even though the names of the prepared food vendors are not readily recognizable like Pizza Hut, Wendy's etc., it still has that fast-food feel.  Blech.)

If you ever knew Haymarket in Boston back in the 80s/90s, or if you know Essex Street Market in Manhattan today, that's essentially what this place is like.   I was not about to buy anything at this place.  It felt depressed, gross and dirty.

The open-seating dining area felt like something you might find at an old baseball stadium....mainly people just stuffing their faces with food, but not SAVORING the food like people who appreciate find cuisine would do.  All in all, not a nice environment for foodies.  If you like going to street carnivals, sporting events, and eating the cotton candy, hot dogs, fried dough etc., I'm sure you'll like this place just fine.  ;-)

Hershel's pastrami on rye is better than katz's in NYC. 9 dollars cheaper too. Born and raised in philly and have had both in the past week. Hershel's is far superior. Could not taste the mustard on Katz's. Also noticed that Hershel's cuts pastrami portion then cuts it into thirds and stacks it so that you get a little bit of end fat with the leaner middle of the slice in every bite. Hershel's also throws it on the panini grill which gives it some texture and keeps it from falling apart on you, which happened to me on the flimsy katz's bread.
The Terminal is a bit of heaven for Foodies, the atmosphere is lively and extremely friendly and helpful, you could spend a day wandering from stall to stall sampling out of this world foods.

The Industry is 2 blocks away from  my house and I couldn't wait for it to open. I fully planned for this to by my new stomping grounds and am truly disappointed.

First time I went was in June during a heat wave. It had to be 85 degrees inside. The hostess told me it was because of the open kitchen 40 feet away- what? I ordered the pulled duck sammie. If I hadn't read it on the menu, don't think I would have guessed it was duck. It was swimming in BBQ sauce which made the ciabatta bun a soggy mess.

Next visit, I steered away from prepared food, figuring they couldn't mess up a cheese plate- wrong! $12 for 3 thin slices of cheese and both the bread and cheese were dried out. Maybe kitchen staff should visit Tria or Stateside to figure out how to serve cheese. 

In desperate need of decent food. I like Good Dog, so don't know what the issue is. 

I have worked in a number of restaurants and agree that the comments aimed at "ignorant" customers are rude.
Green tea grapefruit is AMAZING (whole half grapefruit ) and their beef teriyaki was banging . Seating is limited and min for credit/debit card is 15 dollars. However, they do use Wechat checkout

love love love!!!  How could you not enjoy this smorgasbord of amazing vendors and foods all under one roof.  Bring your appetite and your wallet (it's not cheap)....oh and wear those comfy jeans one size too big.  You will thank me later.
Tourist trap. Don't see what is so great about it.  Go spend your time at the Mutter Museum or the Art Museum.
It's an entire square block closed off to different markets, music and food.  If you're a foodie and love to try different things I highly recommend spotting here and enjoying some different foods.

This place is awesome! Such a classic building that used to be the train station and now houses all these great food vendors of Philadelphia. Such an amazing selection of so many ethnic foods. I love this place, every time I come to the city I must eat lunch here. Not open late, though.

This is one of my favorites in Philly. I've been here many times (take out and eat in) and love most of the rolls on the menu. My favorites are probably the masala chicken and achari chicken rolls. And the white sauce is amazing. Amazing. Take extra, buy a bottle, be happy. And they are open late, so it's perfect after night on the town.

Best Happy hour ever!! buck a shuck and beer specials are what sucked me into this place but there regular menu is really great.  I do hate how small their cheese plate is but other than that have no issues with the place.  One of the best parts is that you also get a discount if you show a paystub from a restaurant which is super great.

Reading Terminal is one of those places that you go into thinking it's going to be the best thing ever, and then inevitably leave mildly disappointed.  The entire market is eye-candy and it can be an adventure just choosing what you want to eat.  However, for the most part, the restaurants in the market are overpriced and not that good.  If you go during the lunch hour, good luck being able to move around at all.  Save your money and go to chinatown.  This all being said, going into Reading Terminal is a cool experience, and there are some gems, such as Herschel's (though again, overpriced).  Where you can make at well is on the non-prepared foods like produce and the fish and meat markets - these are all more reasonably priced and of generally high quality.

Best. Pizza. In. Philly. Bar none. But please do me a favor and don't go there. I hate waiting in line. Seriously, this is better than most NY pizza I have had. I should have given one star so people stay away and I can have all the awesome pizza to myself. It is a step up from the last place in the location for sure. Plus the owner had a personality. I think he has both business sense and and an amazing ability to craft pizza. Just save a slice for me if you go there.

Extremely dirty, some areas smelled terrible. Ate at the wing spot behind Molly molloy's and the raw chicken was left out at room temperature, unseasoned and terrible. I did love the grilled cheese shop and the mushroom company's products were great. I just couldn't stomach being there for more than an hour, the smell and dirtiness really turned us off.

Best Pizza I ever had? Philly, Jersey NYC, Maybe- big statement but accurate... really unique and after first bite both my wife and I said "wow!"The sauce and cheese, was delicious. Crust was incredible. As the cook took it out of the oven he sprinkled some spices and then a bit of olive oil. He seemed proud of his work!
I had a slice fresh out of the oven which I expected to be good and it was great. But then took two pies home, reheated and we all loved it. 
Note- they only have like 4 or 5 types of pies. I guess they specialize and do it well.
Dear Philadelphia, you can keep your Liberty Bell.  Just give me your Reading Terminal Market and I'll leave quietly.

The Industry is one of my favorite restaurants in the city. I have been for both brunch and dinner, and loved everything I've ordered. For brunch, they offer bottomless Fair Trade coffee and also serve complimentary coffee cake while you're waiting for your food. My favorite dish is the fried green tomato salad, which I've had both for brunch and dinner. I also love their fried mac and cheese bites. Service is always very friendly and attentive, and I really enjoy their drink menu.

I first want to say that I love food markets.  We stayed at the hotel that is right next to the Reading Terminal,so it was great.  We went on a Sunday, so a lot of the stores were not opened. 

Our first stop (before we started our day) I got a cup of coffee from Old City Coffee and tried the crepes at Profi's Creperie.  We also got a philly cheese steak from Carmen's.  The food was good and we were hungry.

Our second stop (on the way back to the hotel) we stopped and got a pulled pork sandwich from DiNic's, wings from Franks A Lot, and cupcakes from Flying Monkey.  

All in all I really enjoyed walking around in this food market.  It reminds me of Pike Place in Seattle and Borough Market in London.

Split decision...

We had one good sandwich (pork belly) and one bad sandwich (seafood blt) that had no sauce or toppings. It was pretty much a crab cake on bread. Restaurant was cool though, we will give it another try. I am pretty sure they just forgot the toppings on the seafood sandwich. Pork Belly sandwich was pretty darn good though.
Just one word.: yum! Go to the Amish spot for breakfast! You won't regret it.
Seemed like a standard tourist market in a city that people claim to be better than they are.

Place is amazeballs!!!   You can get anything under the sun--all well prepared.  Be sure to hit the cookie stores around closing time for discounted cookies!  

Must visit if in center city!

Amazing.  You can probably eat here every day and never  get bored. 

They have everything.  Literally everything, from flowers to brisket to Minnesota wild rice, all there. 

First time there was a little overwhelming, and I didnt need to buy groceries, so we got some beef jerky (25 per pound) but it was the most amazing beef jerky Ive had in my life.  We also got some Amish pretzels and baked goods, which were delish. 

I also want to note that the place was quite clean, in comparison to Bostons Quincy Market, this place is spotless. 

The place is huge and I would assume that residents of Philadelphia can do their major grocery shopping there.  I will definitely be back.

Variety is the spice of life here at Reading terminal.  Live Pianist serenaded us at breakfast.  Loads of good choices.  DiNics pork, broccoli rabe with hot peppers on perfect crusty rolls.  Large and generous for the heartiest appetites.  You'll need extra napkins for this savory juicy treat.  Several shops have long lines that move fast.  Service is warm and efficient.  Try several stalls to get the produce, meats, fish, bakery specials and ice cream.  Even a pickle shop.  Cajun, Mexican, huge Salad bar, burger, Hoagies and donuts.  Something for everyone.  Bee wax shop, gifts and all kinds of fun shops to explore while you are at Reading terminal.  Early Dinner is perfect for a quick Greek, Italian or Chinese meal too.  Take family and friends to Reading.
Amazing place and amazing food.  Really cool environment that the entire family can enjoy.  I would highly recommend!!!

Holy cow this place is amazing.  SO MANY RESTAURANTS - incredible food!  Every kind of food you can imagine is here within the area of one city block.  And when you are done, head over to Beiler's Bakery at the front corner for the best doughnuts you have ever had :-p

Definitely a solid 4 on the yelp scale son! 

Really great place if you're in the mood for Indian food and need it quick! I had the Paneer Kati roll and the chicken and rice! 

Blew my friggin mind! The white sauce is boss! 

Stop in or order takeout!

This place is amazing! I am very skeptical about eating Indian food as I always get disappointed with what I believe it should taste like. BUT, not this place! I tried it, and I loved it! I had the Chicken Masala roll (definitely, add the egg) and the Chicken Keema and both were excellent.  They also give you a dollar off if you buy two. A great lunch option if you work in Center City! Can't wait to go back and try everything else on the menu! Keep up the good work Masala Kitchen!!

OK we will admit it.....we would drive from NY to have this pizza again for the 3rd time . We know pizza and this is one of the top 10 we have had. Just the right "chew" which is very tough to get consistently right ......they do it every time. Cheese and sauce are balanced to make this the top contender

Reading Terminal Market is a Philly phenomenon that should be experienced by all at least once. 

I first went there in the dead of a miserably cold winter, and it was such a relief to see people smiling instead of wincing at the chill. Where people had been shuffling through the windy streets with their heads down, here was all chatty brightness. 

Unfortunately for me, this is a place best taken in with a couple pals. And if you're by yourself the first time you come, somehow all of that high spirited conversation and bustle makes you feel the pain of loneliness all the more. 

I had a great hot turnover of some sort from one of the vendors and then a chocolate covered pretzel from another. I wanted to get a slice of pizza too, but there was no place to sit. They have absolutely everything on sale here, it's a great farmer's market. A bit tight through the aisles but a fabulous place.
This place is a hoot. Gets a little too crowded for my taste but I've found amazing cheeses and out of the world pickles (check out the amish pickle stand)
Five f-ing stars all day long!   Have breakfast at molly mallorys... you won't be disappointed!

My favorite place to go grab a good sandwich before I walk around the city. Always a huge crowd but I love going there. I'm a Philadelphian now so it's even better to go for a walk and go there as well.

Way too crowded for my tastes.  There's nothing worse than fighting your way through the crowds to find some interesting, unusual, good food, but then having no where to eat it!  Avoid this place at lunch time.

Amazing 
$1 Hotdogs
$10 Pork Sandwiches at Dinic's
Can't leave without the Vanilla Cannoli from Termini Bros. , Yes 3. 

I said it. I only ate 2 because I had to give my wife 1. 
Thanks again from an original Philly born and raised but now living in Maryland.
One of the best places to visit in Philly if you love food. Some places only take cash. The Dutch eating place is phenomenal. Fresh food and great service. Best pancakes I've eaten in my life.

Had the Pad Thai with chicken from the Thai food place.  Was pretty good.  Note that the Reading Terminal Market tends to close a little early (about 6pm).

The Reading Terminal Market has a great selection of food and is in a great location relative to many convention area hotels.  The hard part is to figure out which type of food you want out of all the choices!

The sandwich taste was fine. It was about 2/3 the size of the other sandwiches on display in the cooler. The service was terrible!! I stood there more than 60 seconds while the clerk stocked cookies while facing me and not once said, I will be with you or even make eye contact. Finally when she was ready to take the order she stood and looked at me and then said "do you want to order something?" She had real who gives "a" demeanor. I was kinda surprised there was not more training before putting her on the front line. No time to ask for a manager, had to catch a flight.

If you are going to Philly, DON'T SKIP THIS! Try the Philly cheesecake, whoa! They have different eateries, diff cuisines, seafoods, fresh veggies, oysters.... muah muah muah, my eyes are getting full just walking around1... cookies, coffee....

This regular Saturday morning stop for our family is truly one of the best things about this city. Fruit and Veg, organic meat, dumpling soup, chicken wings, hoagies, cannoli...this place seriously has everything you want and don't want.

The crowds do get a bit crazy, especially around lunchtimes so try early.
Love this place... crowded but so cool. And the smells and food are to die for! A must stop when in the city.
iko8i8i o9ikooo989oii o.o9888o99i908 initiooo9 0o. 8oooo9 oii0oooout u polloi Kim u8i9in9o oop09i

I could easily spend a whole day here. 

Throughout my food tour of Philadelphia, this was a must-stop for me. I spent about 4 hours here, stopping everywhere from Delilah's for her famous mac n' cheese (or so says Oprah and as seen on Throwdown), the Amish stands, the Jewish deli, bakeries, spice shops, etc. 

I only stopped to eat at a few places, the most notable being Herschel's East Side Deli. Honestly, best hot pastrami I've ever had. Hands down. I live in an area that's laden with Jewish delis, and none of them can surpass Herschel's hot pastrami. I even asked the guy at the counter for the scraps he was cutting off so I can walk around and eat them, they were like candy in meat form.

Of course we stopped at Delilah's for her mac n' cheese. Honestly ---- GREASY. Really greasy. There was nothing creamy and decadent about it. I really wish I liked it, but considering I paid $5 for a small cup, that was a major disappointment. I had a bite, my mom had a bite and into the trash it went. Delilah did, however, lose to Bobby Flay on the Throwdown episode, so go figure... Because Bobby always loses to good competitors. 

Out of all the bakeries I stopped at, I'd have to say I like Flying Monkey the best. I had their red velvet whoopie pie which was DELICIOUS. Try that. They also had some "extreme" cake that was like 72398173981273 layers that looked like a total cake monstrosity, but I guess I'll save trying that for next time I visit, and so long as I bring a small army of people, too. 

I also went through two huge cups of hot cider at Old City Coffee. First when I walked in and I got one before I left. They actually used real unfiltered cider, versus most of the coffee shops these days that use filtered apple cider, which is just a slightly darker apple juice. There's no difference at all. So, of course this made me happy. 

Next time I come to Philly I will definitely be coming back. The one stand I wanted to go was closed, which was one of the Amish stands. I heard their honey is the best  which is what I wanted to take home. Next time.
I can always find anything from fresh meat to fresh produce here. Great meals at the various food vendors. Please check out Blue Mountain Winery. Awesome vino!

I love this place... They have just about anything you can think of to eat here. It a perfect place to grab a snack or some lunch.... It's also a good place to people watch. They have lots of seats inside and outside.

It's clean. The prices are reasonable. Service is good from almost all of the vendors. 

Definitely worth a trip to Reading Terminal Market.

It's like a foodie wonderland!  I love places that always surprise me, and that is just what Reading Terminal does.  One of my favorite stops is always the Fair Food Farmstand to pick up some raw milk or feta or some local, seasonable veggies.  The staff are great and you can pay with level up.

I also still love Tootsie's salad bar which always offers a light snack option.  If I am in need of coffee, there are plenty of shops selling brewed drinks or the beans to take home.  And cheese!  Fabulous cheese offerings towards the middle of the space. The newer additions include a spices and candies store, back by the restroom area.  And an oil and vinegar shop.  There is also another cheese store near these, so it is an easy walk down the line for all your artisanal goods.  I 

Definitely take a look at the maps on the wall when you visit.  It can be crowded at peak meal times and it is easy to lose your orientation with plentiful distractions around.  Some seating is available throughout if you wish to sit, when it is not as busy. I recommend making this a stop on your itinerary if you are in Philly and leaving yourself time to explore if you can.  One of my fav parts of center city!
Favorite eats in no particular order: Dinic's, Beilers, Old City Coffee, Termini Bros.
Best part of reading terminal market?  The food.  The worst part?  The people.  It's also the cheapest place for produce.

If you are dieting, not the place for you!!! Love the specialty donuts, great places for dining for breakfast, lunch or dinner. The Amish sells their wares and baked/cooked foods. Great place to purchase meats, fresh seafood, deli meats and fresh produce.

Hungry?

One must head here if in the area.  We walked over from The Walnut for lunch.  There's something for every taste.  Oh, how I wish this is something that was more readily available to us!
Cannot be overstated. If you do one thing in Philly, make it a visit to Reading. Food, culture, history; all are concentrated here.  A wow on every level.
One of my favorite places to eat and grocery shop in the city. So much variety. Sometimes after work, I'll pick up a quick bite before heading home.

The best grocery shopping in the city.  Iovine Brothers for Produce, Martins for meat, the place across from martins for seafood, the creamery for cheese.   And Reidels for lunch meat.  Love love love!

What a melting pot of cultures and influences under one roof! Amish selling wares (except on Sundays), halal middle eastern cuisine, fresh juices, soul food, burgers ... The list goes on :)

What I was really looking for was the raw milk ... But having gone in a Sunday the Lancaster Foods stall was closed :(
A huge place for different restaurants. Great for people that can't make up their mind on what cusine to eat. They have alot of different cusines and alot of outlets to satisfy your sweet tooth also.

Honestly a little bit overrated. The food is pretty decent, except for Sang Kee which has incredible duck dishes and char siu as well. Most things are a little bit overpriced, but I guess you are paying for the experience. If you want the foodie walkthrough, here's the must hits:

Beiler's has good donuts, but lines are long. 
Bassetts has good ice cream with lots of creamy flavors. 
Dutch eating place for apple dumplings. 
DiNics for a pork sandwich (personally not a fan but others like it). 
Kamal's Middle Eastern for a mint lemonade or some other fun and unique drink. 
Sang Kee for a duck fried rice. 
Mueller for a fresh soft pretzel. 

Other people have things they like also, but these are the ones I commonly hear about- I've tried them all and they're all solid. 

Pro tip: if you are driving, you can park in the garage next door for the hotel and then get your ticket validated for free 2 hour parking by a vendor if you spend 10 dollars at their stand.

Tryed Popeye's all over America  and in general pretty consistent not the of
Phil's airport food may be fresh, and hot one trip and cold  mediocre the next.. the manager is as rude and uncaring as they come and probably deserves to be sued over treatment I have witnessed to some of female employees. Employees run typical range you see in Philadelphia Airport from FU to average. I have noticed a newer employee  young female recently who is polite , friendly and a breath of fresh air.. maybe change is in the air. Let's hope as I am frequently trapped in PHL and have to eat somewhere.

best cheesesteak I've ever had was from here!
great cookies, too!
really fun to walk around and check out all the vendors.
only downfall was it was very crowded and HOT.

Philly icon - a must stop if visiting. We go often to get some difficult to find veggies and of course sticky buns that taste like nana's. Always come home with cheese and bread and a few other snacks. Never disappoints. Always look forward to their seasonal activities

Just point me in the direction of the food. And I mean ALL OF THE FOOD. Reading Terminal Market was destination number one for me on my first trip to Philly. I love public market houses and this had a little bit of everything. Reminiscent of Granville Island in Vancouver, you can explore plenty of fresh produce, much of which is locally produced by farmers in PA! Be sure to check our Fair Food's stall. Gorgeous, locally grown produce and value added products made with love. Not to mention, you can use Philly Food Bucks and double up dollars if you're on SNAP! Whoo! 

There were multiple large produce stands, Amish cheese makers, fresh fish and poultry stands, and all the prepared foods of your dreams. If I hadn't been financially fit an eaten breakfast at home I could've had more than a delicious iced chai from Old City Coffee. I circled the building a couple of times and I believe this was the only coffee station. (Thumbs down) but my drink was tasty!

The market is a great place to go if you're with a group and everybody is wanting something different. Go international or keep it strictly American, you're sure to find something to satisfy those taste buds. Next time i'a in town, I'll have to hit up the oyster bar and try some cheese and sweet treats! Put this place on your list!
The dumplings are good, not a big fans of their Chicken Pot Pie Noodle, service was awesome!!

This place has the rudest staff I have ever encountered in a fast food chain. Run by a bunch of wannabe gansters. I haven't gone to a KFC for over 10 years, so I drove over to this location while I was at IKEA, thinking I'd check out what's good. Big mistake! My first question "how does your meal box combo work?" was met with a middle aged woman giving attitude, saying I was wasting her time (???). Being the non-confrontational person I am, I just left. With a bad taste in my mouth. I drove over to the Burger King nearby and had a completely different experience - friendly staff and clean interior. If you're in the area, I recommend you go to a different place to get food.

This place is outstanding!!! Our hotel (home2suite by Hilton) is right across the street. We walked around a bit but we were starving so we chose Pearl's Oyster bar. I left a review for it. Anyhow, you can find such a variety of food -- fresh seafood if you want to cook yourself, desserts and little shops. I'd love to have this back home. Our hotel has a refrigerator so this would be great if we had the inclination to cook but we're doing too much sightseeing for that. This is definitely a place to check out!!!
Cheesesteaks. Over priced. Bland. Junk. Don't waste your time and money

I *love* healthy things and vegetables, so I really love Beafsteak's flash-steaming concept for their vegetables. That's exactly how I'd cook something if I could pick any way in the world to eat vegetables for the rest of my life, because steaming for *just* a couple of minutes is exactly how to get a lot of vegetables at their peak levels of nutrition and flavor for eating! 

However, I don't think the salad is hefty enough or mind-blowingly flavorful enough to be worth the price you pay. It's definitely a great place to go to eat dinner if you want something that will satisfy and keep your insides happy, but it's a lot to pay for just vegetables and grains.
Love the atmosphere and the awesome food this place reminds me of the marketplace my grandfather and I visited so often in Puerto Rico
It has amazing ice cream! Definitely worth try if u love ice cream as well as chocolate. Ez to buy seafood in large size(literally), too.

I didn't try EVERYTHING inside, but I definitely ate as much as I could. I stopped by Dinic's Roast Beef and Pork. Asked the waitress what was most popular and had at it! Finished off with some desert at Basset's, had some Banana flavored ice cream which I absolutely loved, but the heat outside made it impossible to eat all of that heavy cream. I'm sure Philly natives would say they're bored with this place as I would say of Times Square, but it was/is new to me and I can't wait to go back!
This is such a unique place to grab a meal and get a feel for a true Philadelphia icon.  There are very few places in the country as diverse and is a must visit if you are in Philly.

Stopped here for lunching to tour during a recent visit to the city.  Plenty of food options, but it does get pretty crowded at lunch time....expect some long lines during peak hours.  We had our Hearst set on a DiNics roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and it did not dissapoint.  Try to grab a small table away from the major establishments.
What's not to love about Reading Terminal? Basset's ice cream, DiNic's roast pork, Termini Brothers cannolis, heaven.

I stumbled on this wonderful market.  I was just trying to find the Dutch Eating Place for breakfast and didn't know it was part of the Reading Terminal Market.  What an extraordinarily wonderful market.  The pork sandwich at DeNics is the best I've ever had and the Cannoli at Termini's Bakery is to die for.
This is a very well run establishment. Was highly impressed with the food, service, cleanliness and courtesy of the employees. Well played chic fil a. Cheers !!!

What. A. Market!

There are cuisines from all over the U.S. and the world.

Fresh, delicious desserts and baked goods.

Vegan and gluten-free options.

So many vendors packed into a fairly small space, yet despite the crowds it doesn't feel overly packed.  Yes, some places will get a line, but it moves along quickly enough.

Not only are their cuisines-a-plenty to be had at the various restaurants, there are also places to buy fresh meat, seafood, produce and groceries.

Restrooms are pretty clean and don't get obnoxiously crowded.

Plenty of nearby lots for parking, and yes, it's above a train terminal, so it's easily reached by public transportation.

One thing to note:  The Amish take their Sundays seriously.  Hence the booths run by Amish will be closed on Sunday.

This is a place you simply must hit when you visit Philly.

Literally never have enjoyed slices so much. The guys behind the counter was putting everything into these pies and it shows. Had the 'classic white', a pepperoni, and tomato pie and it was all a divine experience. I am from a few hours away and am trying to actively come up with excuses to visit the city again (in part just to go here).

This place has a magical place within my heart, it has all the amazing options, if not more, of Chelsea Market in NYC but with spirit and old age feeling. 

Cheese sandwich to die for, yep! Authentic Indian with a twist, you bet! Cajun food that will leave you bewildered and grabbing for water, definitely! This place has it all and with a group of people that can't agree, it's better than the UN at bringing you together. 

When my group of 12 ran off, we all ended up at the same three tables, sharing, laughing, and drinking a few good beers and mixes.

If you haven't been, go! If you have, revisit! You'll create a few good memories and have a fantastic and delicious time.
I absolutely love Reading Terminal. They have everything for your needs whether it's grocery shopping, a bite to eat, having dessert or looking for something unique.
Great market...good place to stroll through on a Saturday to buy some choice items

All State Van LInes moved us from Pennsylvania to Massachusetts.  It went very well, our belongings were delivered in good condition within the guaranteed time frame.  I will use them if I ever move again. They contract out the jobs to other companies and contractors.
Nice place to visit when in Philly. There is a little bit of everything. Shout out to the businesses which are closed on Sunday's ! I suggest parking in the street lots for $10 all day.

I like that I have many choices, so I generally get entrée & dessert from different places. I enjoy the Amish food when they're open, very filling. Great for a quick bite, a relaxed lunch or even to get some fresh meats & veggies.
One of the best places to eat in Philadelphia. There are so many different places to eat inside the terminal. There is nothing that they do not have. So this is definitely a Philadelphia treasure !

I always bring family and friends to this place when they visit!! So many delicious food options, including local favorites like Beiler's donuts. A fun experience to get a taste of Philadelphia food and culture!

Gonna miss this place now that I'm leaving for MD. Great seafood sellers! DiNic's roast pork is an institution! The Amish diner in the back is great for breakfast/brunch! It's usually crowded, so be ready to deal with that.

I went here on a weekend. The place was slammed, but the selection was lovely. At first it looked like an Amish market, but there were other things that set it apart. It wasn't a strictly Amish market type of place. I noticed Chinese and Middle Eastern offerings as well. The line for the ladies room was ridiculously long and the crowd at the market acts like they just sucked on a bag on rotten lemons, but I digress....the food made all of the hassle worth it.

I feel like this place sums up the Philly food scene pretty well, for me at least.

Due to the fact that I made the trek to Philly, I made sure that I was going to stuff my tummy to new levels of discomfort. I started at Dinic's. The line was long, but went by pretty quick. I settled for a pork sandwich with provolone and broccoli rabe. It was pretty decent, I wouldn't cry to the sky over it, but I liked it. It set me back a little over $9...not the cheapest fast eat sandwich.

There is something about pretzels and Philly that really makes for a happy combo. I picked up a pretzel on my way out of the market...I'll review the pretzel place on its own....along with the Flying Monkey bakery.

Those three spots are some favorites in the market. I could stay there all day and stuff my fact with yummies.
I wish they hadn't built a convention center around it. But still a gem. Maybe Philly's greatest attraction.

This might honestly be the BEST market I have been to in a very long time.  I've gone to the West End Market in Cleveland.  The Lexington Market in Baltimore, and really, none of these compare.  This had everything you could possibly hope for and need.  Very crowded but why wouldn't it be?  It's the best.  

From bars, donuts, flowers, groceries, and Philly Loving souvenirs, I wish this was in every city I visited.  It made everything so easy food wise, entertainment wise, and it was clean and comfortable to be in.
Been for dinner and brunch and want to come back for a slumber party. The cocktails are so fantastic and house made sausage is to DIE for.

I'm not generally interested in tourist spots, but Reading is an exception. I'm a huge fan of the produce market and the beef jerky stall. If possible, steer clear on the weekends, as the market has a sardine tin feel (packed to the gills, that is). Be advised, many of the pastry shops intentionally employ Amish women in an attempt to lead customers to believe that the shop is selling authentic Amish pastries, despite this not being the case. This fact does not diminish the quality or tastiness of their food stuffs, but it is, at best, disingenuous.
Definite "must-do" in philly.  I love it and go back all the time.  There are so many things.  Saturdays are better than Sundays.

There is so much crammed into this space it is a bit overwhelming. You can find any time of food you could want. Space and tables are somewhat limited, but even as busy as they were, we were able to find a clean table.

Clean, efficient, inexpensive, and delicious - Masala Kitchen far exceeded my expectations! We ordered the chicken masala kati roll and the paneer platter. Both had the "creamy tomato sauce" which was to die for!! I'm a huge fan of Indian cuisine and can be picky at times, but I must say Masala Kitchen does a good job. I will definitely be returning regularly!

Update Sept 2016: I go to this place every time I crave Indian food - I'm obsessed.

In a city that has delusions of being "world class" ( if you've ventured out into the world you know what I mean) Reading Terminal IS world class. Not as big as the indoor market in Warsaw, Poland or as quaint as the one in Oxford, England - I always feel proud  no matter where I am that Philadelphia's Reading Terminal is one of the greatest markets of its kind anywhere. Besides the wonderful Amish presence, the variety of foods and crafts, the friendly pub - no matter how crowded it is I always manage to find a seat.
Great place to eat and shop.  Just beware of busy times.  It totaly sucks when its overcrowded.  Check that local activitys befor making the trip.

So hard to come here and not want to eat everything!!! Should probably come with a friend or two, so you can try every stall and split everything. Absolutely insanity with the line-ups to the popular spots (ie. Dinic's) during Saturday lunch hour...or maybe even all day? 

If you have an entire day to eat, you should probably come here.
i love everything. it's like one big supermarket of food.  flying monkey is the best with the cookies.

Holy macaroni and everything else they sell there. Fresh scratch food it's like parking in front of 100 food trucks and having your choice of every type of Philadelphia fare you could imagine. Breakfast lunch and dinner every day if I could...

This is probably my favorite place in the world. Everything you could want under one roof. It's a foodies dream. You can get a delicious pork sandwich, walk around the corner and get the best Pennsylvania Dutch pretzel you will ever eat. I would live here if I could, like a rat

Ah, Pizza Shackamaxon- you play so hard to get, but it just makes me love you more! Wait in line for 15 minutes, half of it outdoors? Sure. Be told that a plain pie will be a 45-minute wait even though it's only like 4pm? I'd wait longer. Stand in the tiny cramped space along the wall awkwardly while listening to a random dude in a baseball cap say "are you serious, an hour?!" to the pizza man? This is the way. 

The pizza is thin and heavenly and the crust tastes like bomb sourdough. The end.

"DiNicks is a must"  "It won national awards for the pork sandwich"

In all honesty, yes they are good sandwiches but they are not "knock your socks off and send them down the street" good.  

A place called Riddle Ale House in media, or Nicks roastbeef in Springfield definitely have better roast beef, and pork sandwiches.

Again, good but not great or worth the drive, finding parking, waiting in line.

Right off the bat a good tip is to go at an off time (and avoid Saturday all together if possible).  RTM is much more pleasant when you can browse through your options without constantly being in someone's way!

Though it may be a popular tourist attraction, it is also a favorite of people like myself that live here in Philly.  The following are some of my favorite spots at RTM:

- Dinic's (of course) 
- Hope's cookies (some very inventive flavors and every single one I have tried has been soft and chewy.  In my opinion, MUCH better than Famous 4th St. cookies which are also sold at RTM.  I recommend the english toffee bar cookie)
- Amish juice and milk stand by one of the exits (not sure of the name).  They sell delicious fruit juices and my all time favorite is the starberry orange lemonade.  There is even a huge jug at the stand where you can sample the lemonade.  I make sure to stop here every time.

LOVE LOVE LOVE the reading terminal market.   The sights, sounds, food and people make it a wonderful way to spend a few hours.   Met a group of friends which adds to the fun as we all ordered something different and then sat together sharing everything: duck wonton soup, cheesesteak, muffuletta, jambalaya and more.  So many wonderful flavors and spices.     The unique shops, the cooked food, desserts, produce and  they even have a corner with samples of liquor.   Unfortunately I didn't take pictures today but I'll be back again and again.  So next time for the pictures.

Though I've heard a lot about this place and this one is the closest to my office. I would still say, they are not worth the money.

Not good options for veggies and the place is too crowded.

Absolutely incredible food. I, admittedly, have not had a lot of Filipino dishes in the past.  However my wife and I have developer quite a taste for the deliciousness out of this kitchen.  The pork BBQ over rice with pickeled veggies is incredible.  Perfectly cooked with amazing flavors.  Crispy pork belly is mouth watering.  Add an egg for an even more greatness.  Longanisa is fantastic...a sausage with so many flavors.  The rice is perfectly prepared and for a simple but great side, the spring rolls hit the spot.  Definitely worth a trip to the Bourse to check out. You will not be disappointed.

Most overlooked place in philly for locals and tourists alike. Do not get a Philly cheesesteak here too many better option here and for cheesesteaks elsewhere. If you come with someone else or a group, go 'halvsies' as we call it so you sample as much as possible. Get stuff cut in quarters, lots of spoons/forks etc.  Get a donut. And walk here bc you best be hungry when you show up, and avoid lunch hour.

I was MORE than EXCITED to visit let alone chow down on Denics. I saw an episode of Man v. Food and applied myself to what he was praising and backing up with his and his mothers life claiming that Denic's Roast Pork Sandwich is like no other. Instantaneously, my mouth began to water at the meticulous placement of the sharp provolone and the boiling concoction from which the roast pork was being pulled out from. So, I decided to turn off my TV, send the dvd back to netflix, and go purchase two tickets from LA to philly just to try this god sent meat sandwich!

When I got there, the butterflies in my stomach churned quicker and quicker by every mile; my excitement was no exaggeration. As I stepped foot in the heaven bazaar I wasted no time searching for this legendary Denic's! I skim past the array of markets and hustle my way to Denic's. As my cousin and I wait in the never-ending line, we talk amongst ourselves and take pictures to take back home because we definitely cannot take the roast pork with us! As the line pulled us in closer to the cashier, we looked and saw a COCKROACH climbing up the glistening Denic's sign; the sight of that disease ridden insect dismayed my presence. Never-the-less, we order our food; we didn't spend $500 and cover all this road to get stalled by a god damn cockroach! Before I took my first passionate bite, I accustomed myself and made a pledge on the plane ride to not cry at the overload of deliciousness. Again, to my dismay, I bit and was about to GAG! WTF was Adam thinking?! I got exactly what he said! Roast pork sandwich, with sharp provolone and broccoli rabe! Sheer disgust and disappointment is all that rained down my face. Bitter, like biting into handful of Arugula! The only pro about the sandwich would be the barely noticeable presence of the sharp provolone.

All-in-all, it was a very interesting trip. I also visited a few other places that I saw on Man v. Food, however, those did not fail me. Denic's might be a delicious place to eat, but, I guess, my Californian tongue cannot handle the extreme flavors of the east. Judge it for yourself.
Best location for meat in Philadelphia = Giunta's. Ask for Brazilian-style steak and you will be happy. Super trust-worthy.

My chicken tikka roll was delicious, but was definitely small for a "dinner" portion. The roti was absolutely heavenly and I could have eaten many of those! My boyfriend enjoyed his chicken and lamb "masala style" platter. I wish they offered sides, because a roll plus a side would make a substantial dinner, but for now I will stick with this place for lunch.

Crowded all times of day. If I lived in downtown Philly, I'd shop here all the time. Great for tourists to get ice cream, desert or a full meal on the way to or from hotels in the downtown area. At the end of the day, bakery items were half price.  Workers are friendly and patient.

This is my favorite quick lunch to bring back to my office. So flavorful, quick, friendly service, and filling rolls. One fills me on a day when I'm not too hungry, and two almost put me to sleep. My favorite is the aloo paneer roll, highly recommend! And in the summertime, their mint lemonade is worth a try. I much prefer their rolls over their rice dishes (biryani is just meh) so stick to the Kati rolls and you won't regret it!

I want in to this place and seen a list of 1 2 and 3 dollar items so i ordered a 3 dollar item the totsl came to 5.60 i said it is only 3 dollsrs they told me that doesn't start till after the first of the year..

Why would you put a sign up for customers to see with no dates on it so people would no it doesn't start till January....
The owner of this business realky needs to talk to his manager's....if i was doing a secret shop they would have failed ....
I don't understand what all the fuss is about. It's a tourist trap.  They have decent options but I live here. It's a mall of food.

We love the wide variety of places to eat and bakeries to choose from.  It is very crowded here, but worth it.  This is our second visit to the Reading Terminal Market (RTM) and the only surprising experience we had was someone approached us asking for money.  My husband gave him some money, but then before leaving RTM, we were approached again by the same guy.  My husband reminded him that he had all ready asked us for money.  Otherwise, we enjoy eating and buying from the many markets that are at RTM.

It is a beautiful place to hang out and grab something to eat. Unfortunately it was very dirty, smelled really bad. I believe it us a place that you must visit in Philadelphia. But still not more than 3 stars because of the ambience.

Best place in the entire world, not up for debate. I have been to other cities with similar style markets but nothing comes remotely close to reading terminal. Everything is delicious. You literally can't go wrong.
Best pizza in Philadelphia by far. The staff that work there (&owner) are also awesome. The product is consistent - fresh, flavorful, high quality.

Fantastic Service. Even when they're busy, they take the time to be friendly and polite. 
Great location

Best place to go to in Philly. Come on an empty stomach. They have everything from every desert you can dream of, various cuisines for lunch and dinner, cute little trinkets, and deli and produce section. My favorite and what I always go to is Beiler's donuts - the most delicious thing I've ever eaten ever.
A lot of good places to check out. I also like to do my grocery shopping here. I try to avoid weekends because lines can get crazy and hard to move navigate around.

Reading Terminal Market, you are just like my own North Market is Columbus, Ohio. What an absolute treat when being away from home!

With my hotel being right next door it was a blast taking fresh produce back to my room for a yummy and healthy snack after walking all day. 

This is a nice gem, but man does this place getting insane-crazy come noon and after. 

Come early--especially if you've never been and want to get a look around at all of the vendors, because once the clock strikes noon, the herds of human cattle come shuffling in, which can make waiting in lines and acrobatic and annoying experience. I recommend coming around 11, because most of the Vendors will have their delicious smells wafting through the air, and chances are, there won't be a major wait to get food. 

Our stop was the infamous Dinic's. You know, Man vs. Food? Yeah, I know we're total Posers, but it was wonderful and we are still craving one of his signature sandwiches. We also stopped at a produce stand ran by some Asian ladies, and at an Amish place in the far corner serving up cobblers, and bread puddings. YUM!

All senses are inspired here; the smells, the sights, the sounds, but most importantly the tastes. 

Happy adventures and happy eating!
Best bacon ever!!!!! Great food everywhere! Great place to go on a Sunday morning.  I love this place!!!

Among the new eateries in the revamped Bourse food court is this Filipino spot.  La Lo is a play on words in Tagalog for Grandma and Granddad - both of whom have inspired the owner of this eatery.  The menu is not very long and indeed a few familiar Filipino dishes that I think could lend themselves easily to fast food status (e.g. Pancit) are not included.  In fact there are only five items currently on the menu.  Fortunately the one I tried - Lumpia Sariwa - was very good....(though I wasn't quite sure if I was to use the crepe underneath to roll up food in it and then eat it.)  To me Lumpia are kinda like spring rolls so this def looked different.  But it tasted good and had a very nice flavor mixture.  A Gina calamansi juice was the perfect beverage to go with my dish.  If you've never tasted refreshing Calamansi Juice, this is your opportunity.

All in all, it's nice to have something different in a food court and this Filipino café is indeed just that!

Amazing selection of vendors, food being made and eaten every square foot. The smell and the atmosphere alone makes it worth it to take a peek inside. I will probably be coming back here next chance I'm free in Philadelphia.

Love the Terminal Market. Whenever I come to Philly on the weekend, I make sure to stop buy for a sandwich or some sweets. Great options for food- read to eat or buy to prepare at home. It is a must do in Philly.

This place gets crowded, but this place is awesome. I love the fact that even during a large conference across the street I was able to get something fairly quickly because all the great options. I enjoyed a turkey stand that had this amazing fresh turkey sandwiches! Forgive me as I don't remember the name as I was so busy with work I just when in and out, but I REMEMBER THAT TURKEY!! :)

I have no tolerance for folks who hate on Reading Terminal Market.

Okay, so you won't have the best meal of your life here. The diner sucks. It's typically crowded. And there's a few pigeons kicking it with you, plus yeah... a rat or ten.

Still, this place truly resonates with the Philly experience. It's so diverse, both in terms of food and in people. I love the Amish juice and the seafood bisque. Around the holidays is my favorite time of year to peruse the aisles with a loved one, and just waste time. Actually, this is my favorite place to kill time, read a book, people watch. I have faith in Philly when I hang here.

In the summer, there's pretty sweet flea markets caddy-cornered on the outside too, Saturdays. If this place wasn't here, I might just pack up and dip for Baltimore or Brooklyn.

A really solid Chick-fil-A with excellent food. The lines can be very long, but there's a reason for it... it's because of the food! I've eaten several chicken sandwiches from here and Shake Shack and can tell you quite honestly that Shake Shack's overpriced chicken sandwich (it's twice the price of Chick-fil-A's) is no better than the chicken sandwich here. In fact, on one of the Shake Shack visits, the chicken sandwich ended up tasting far worse than any chicken sandwich from Chick-fil-A and that's a crying shame because so many people adore Shake Shack. The waffle fries and chicken strips are usually very good, the Oreo shakes are great, and the table service (if lines are long, you can seat yourself and a server will bring your order out to your table for you) is a plus. I hope they never, ever change. Kudos to the management and the great team working here. Oh, and one reason to come to Chick-fil-A rather than a place like Popeye's... they don't charge you 30 cents for an extra sauce pack!

So today I was recommended by several friends of mine to try their stir fry. So I got the "make my own" stir fry which came down to 15.34$. For the portion, I say it's a bit overpriced, but that was not my only issue. They also burnt my egg, forgot my pork, and the flavor wasn't even that good. I got a 'regular' amount of sauce and I can vouch that there was very little and I do not want to pay extra for just a little more flavor. I'm very disappointed with my first experience. This will most likely my last time as well. I had a nice conversation with the cashier; however, when I called to tell them they forgot my pork (which was three dollars more than the veggie option, which is what I was provided) , I was sent straight to voicemail.  Thank you for your shitty food.
Nice Variety of Food!!!
Who doesn't love Reading Terminal Market!  So many things under one roof, and you need a whole day to just explore.  Have breakfast, lunch, and an early dinner here.  It's worth the visit!

busy busy busy!

lots of stuff and vendors to look at and purchase

you have to stop by just to experience it.

Almost like the Ferry Building in SF, Chelsea Market in NYC but way way way more packed and busy than both

Finally got back to the Industry and I'm happy to report that they have earned another star.

Visited this past weekend for an early and quick Saturday dinner with my husband, his parents and his sister.  Our general rule of thumb when picking a place for an "L" family dinner is to choose a place with a decent burger, a few salad/lighter options, parking options nearby, and a place where we'll be seated promptly.  The Industry fit the bill for us in every way, so I suggested we meet here for dinner.

Since we had talked up the burger, everyone except my husband and I got one.  We wanted to try some of the other offerings since we've already tried their great burger- I went with the whole grain salad.

The whole grain salad was delicious- comprised of farro, peas, fava beans, and ricotta salata.  My only wish is that it had a TAD bit more of dressing on it- it was a little dry.  However, I still really liked the dish.  And at $10, it's a good value.

Luckily my in-laws all loved their burgers (and the great beer list), so yay for daughter-in-law brownie points.  So if you are planning a gathering for people that want a great meal with some safe options (such as the burger) or interesting options (pig ear lettuce wraps? buffalo sweetbreads?) at a very reasonable price, check out the Industry.

This place was pretty good. There isn't anything too special about the interior. It's pretty simple and like any regular old restaurant you go to.

The food, on the other hand, is far from regular. They have a variety of Kati rolls and you get a dollar off for getting two. The beef takki roll was well seasoned and tender. It was pretty good. The lamb kabob roll kind of threw me for a loop. It seemed almost minced or ground up lamb and a bit dried up. However, the flavors were there and it was decently seasoned. I was doubtful at first as to if it'll fill me up, but it does. 

Defiantly want to come back and try some other Kati rolls and see which one I like the most. Defiantly one of the better Indian food spots in the city.

They have almost any food you could want at a fair price. Especialy the Amish / PA dutch food.

The only part that sucks is the cafeteria space is kinda dirty/dumpy, and all the tourists every time there's a convention - can of sardines.

This place has an amazing selection of food.  You could literally eat there every day for a month and try something different each time.  It must be great for people that work close by.  If I did, I'd be eating there every day.

Really gives a true taste of Philly. Great variety here, and many great places. Some can be a hit or miss but most are great. I always come here when I am downtown, but it is always so damn crowded. Almost impossible to find anywhere to sit and almost impossible to move around without bumping into someone. If you get here and there is a huge crowd, it still is probably worth it. If I could give more stars. I definitely would.

This is foodie heaven!  Was amazed at the vast food variety and aroma - every corner is just brimming with something new and delicious.  Its arranged like a grid - but if you are a foodie, you can easily spend lots of time in here.  Has every type of food / cuisine you can imagine.  Wish they had more of these places in each state - really gives you a good taste of the city of Philadelphia under one roof.

Pros - too much to list : lots of variety, every type of cuisine, aroma, decor, seating : just amazing!

Cons - parking ( you have to pay for parking : park in deck because street parking is near impossible )

Overall - MUST see / thing to do when you come to Philly ( especially if you are a foodie )

Tip - park in the parking deck ( located near by ), street parking is extremely difficult as it is in the heart of downtown Philly.  Lots of things to see & do around the area ( lots of stores, chinatown, etc.)
Always a must when visiting Philly. Went on a Friday afternoon. It actually wasn't too crowded considering it was a Friday at lunch. Lots of food choices to choose from.
Love coming here just to try the different cuisines.  Especially love to come on the weekends sometimes for brunch and eat the Amish diner. Their pancakes are great!

Without a doubt my favorite spot in all of Philly (parking is meh, tho). But, the Dutch Eating Place (the apple dumpling is super cheap & tasty), coffee, oldie ice cream, and the old school oyster counter were my top spots. The next time I am in Philly, I will be making my way straight to this place!

I love the Market! Every kind of food you can want, all in one place - from prepared meals and sandwiches. to fresh fruit and veggies. I just moved to Philly, and have been told that many locals do in fact shop here for their groceries. Great people watching at lunch, and definitely not touristy like you might expect from such a popular place :)

We stopped by for a quick eat. Got a chicken roll and an aachari chicken roll. Both the rolls were good. I always thought katti rolls company rolls in NY were good but I don't think I will go back to the one in NY now. The food came out really fast and was hot and fresh and tasty.
Overall,
Rolls- 4.5/5
Price- 4/5
Service- 4/5

Personally, this place is both an irresistible draw and a great source of confusion. The latter due largely to it's sheer size and the incredible level of variety available here. 

Upon arriving, I always find myself doing laps just taking in all the visuals and aromas of the wealth of foods around me. I have to admit, I've been here numerous times and I can still get lost inside. I walk, stare at stuff, dodge people, read menus, walk some more, dodge a few more people, stare at more stuff. 

I've barely scratched the surface in terms of how many vendors within the RTM I've patronized. I've bought treats from the Amish and I've been to Pearl's & DiNic's - all were good experiences.

I can see why some might call it a tourist trap, but I personally would not characterize it as such. I think aside from it's practicality and usefulness, it's part of the rich history of the city and a throw back to markets of old. It's certainly a great asset to have here.

When it's time to leave I just walk straight until I find an exterior wall which will ultimately lead to an exit. Depending on what street I'm facing and my intended course, I adjust as necessary. 

There's nothing quite like it. Worth a visit.

This probably the best place in philly. You can get a plethora of food choices and do your grocery shopping at the same time. My favorite place to shop is OK produce if you want vegetables or fruit that you can eat and cook NOW!  Hershel is the best place to grab a sandwich. This place by far is the best place on Philly!

This is one of the best market I have been to in the US. Great stuffs at reasonable price. Choice is what impresses me. For every item there are more than a couple of stalls to choose from. Of course there are a few one of a kind items also. Had the fresh pasta from By George last night. It was good.

I love this place. I always make it a point to eat lunch at the Market whenever I'm in the neighborhood. There are so many delicious choices from cheesesteaks to deli sandwiches to gumbo to oysters....  just so many choices!

Besides the prepared food vendors, there are also many shops selling produce, meats, fish, and specialty goods. If I lived closer, I would definitely do some of my grocery shopping here. 

Some of the highlights for me are DiNic's Roast Pork, Beck's Cajun Cafe, and of course, Termini Bros. Bakery, where I absolutely must get a fresh canolli whenever I'm in the Market. 

Leave whatever you wish, but take the canolli. Trust me!
Great place for good food, there's great cheesesteaks, burgers, penn dutch, among others. highly recommended.

I absolutely love this place and every city should "try" to imitate Reading Terminal, if they could.  We went there all three days of our trip, ate at several restaurants, bought food any many of the vendors.  Bread from the dutch bakery, sausage from one of the meat vendors.  The place is great, crowded and full of things to see, try and do.  Nice having validated parking if you spend $10, that helps.  this is a must see for anyone that likes food and is visiting Philly.
Very good Asian/Philly inspired dumplings. Definitely recommend. $7.50 for 5 dumplings is a great deal for a small meal or snack! Will be back for sure.

This place has some of the best pizza in the city and also some of the nicest people who work there! The thin crust and perfectly browned underside are just a few things about this pizza that make it stand out. The fresh produce, meat and cheese all perfectly combine to give you a flavor explosion in your mouth. The cheese pizza is perfectly classic and the pepperoni only takes it another notch up!

Can't wait to order here again and again!

Great variety and the place is huge so you can try so many things! They have enough places to sit when you order food. Tried Carmen's cheesesteak which was pretty good and the apple dumpling from the Dutch eating place which was also good. Would not get the pumpple (pie baked in cake) again though.

Great Local place to come to on the weekend. There is so much to offer here; between the different types of food to the many ethnic backgrounds that walk around. It's really enjoyable to come here with friends or family and the experience makes for a wonderful adventure!

These rolls are quite delicious. My wife and I visited Philly last weekend, and went here twice in two days. They were so good. The Chicken Masala is my favorite, the Paneer Masala was also extremely good. The Aloo and Chicken Kheema are OK. Ask for the sauces and get the white sauce, its really good and delicious. Nice, quaint little place on Walnut with all the good spices for the right Kati Rolls.

Foodie heaven.  This is my crews go to after a fun night out on the town.  Sometimes the hours seem to be a little funky but it's worth the wait.  My fav is all the dessert spots.  4 stars because it's so damn crowded though.
I love the Reading Terminal because of its variety but it can be very crowded on weekends.  Try to hit it on a weekday and get some of the Amish goods.

Ugh.  
Kids these days and their very expensive,small portion, fancy named food.  Don't get me wrong I love fancy named small portions if the price tag matches the ingredients or portion a little bit.  This is Hipster highway robbery (coming from a cheapo hipster).
I had a super delicious and very interesting arepa dish with the best mole I've ever had.  Flavor gets 5 stars.

I also had a seven dollar beer served in like an eight ounce glass... delicious but... give me a break!  I need to guzzle beer!  I have a problem... I switched to PBR.

Let's break down the value:
Sweet Corn Arepas blistered tomatoes, creminis, poblanos, crème fraiche - $15
so let's see, 3 small cornbread, tomatoes, mushrooms, peppers and a dairy product.  This all amounts to about 10 oz. of product on the plate (being generous).

Value SUCKS!

8 oz delicious beer - $7 x 2 = one pint = $14!!!

Value SUCKS!

The food was really good, the beer was really good, but this is my personal review and I just can't imagine ever returning there.

Awesome place to visit for a while while walking around downtown Philadelphia. Many options to choose from and a food lovers delight. It was a fun experience walking around each food stand and smelling the aroma of fresh cooked food. Beware of limited parking and seating tables for groups and single individuals even throughout the week lunch rushes because there is many people during the summer.

A must-see for visitors to Philadelphia. Lots of great restaurants including award-winners and Philly classics like Dinic's, Bassett's Ice Cream, and Termini Bros, as well as year-round farm stands featuring local produce.

I love going to the Reading Terminal market during my lunch break. The food for the most part is good, interesting crowds. The only thing I hate is how rude the cleaning staff in the green shirts are. Other than them, the place is awesome.

Reading Terminal Market, made this foodie's heart extremely happy! What can I say, as someone mentioned in the Tips, this place is truly Disney World for foodies . Every kind of food you can imagine, you find it here and everyone seemed so helpful. The best part is, it is just across the street from our hotel. 

Having seen DiNic's Roast Pork topped with Broccoli Rabe over and over on Travel Channel, I had always wanted to try it, that was one of my foodie goals so that was one of my main reasons for coming here. We are so glad we did because we loved it. I know I will be visiting this lovely gem every day of our visit here
Just an awesome place to walk around and check out all the yummy food and treats.  We were visit for only a few days and so sad there isn't more time to explore and try all the food here

It all depends on what you're looking for.  There is a LOT of variety here, but it can get very crowded, especially during lunch time.  It's still a good place to go, though.
