Want middle eastern food?  Check!  BBQ?  Check!  Seafood?  Check!  Wanna pick up some veggies and fruit?  Check!  Got a sweet tooth?  Check!  Want to take home some baked goods?  Check!  It can be a little overwhelming, especially if you don't know the layout.  I've only been here a few times, and keep making a mental note to go when it's not as busy.  Also, it can be a little pricey, but not much more than other places in the area.  Again, it all depends...

I wish there was  seven stars like in the luxury hotels system!! This place is magical, I have been may times and it never a seises to amaze me. This time was particularly memorable because of the visit of my dad. He loves food and groceries stores!! I have never seen him so happy and I'm awe like today. This place not only made us happy but it gave us such beautiful memories together that wi will cherish for life and will share with my family.  

There is absolutely nothing wrong with this place except for that fact that you want to come every day I I will only get fatter!! I absolutely love LOVE the terminal and every tourist and local should come as often as possible to enjoy it and but good quality everything. :)
Wow- what a great place for food from everywhere. Awesome selection and a unique experience in the heart of the city
Beck seafood and gumbo, AMAZING. Busy place, but a lot to see. If you find a seat, I suggest you take it.

So excited that this cute Filipino food spot has opened in The Bourse!

My belly screamed for Inihaw (grilled pork with atchara over garlic rice) and Lumpia Shanghai, but I took a risk with the seasonal Shrimp Roll ... and didnt regret it! Omg those lovely chips are perfectly salty.

They have short hours (11A-4P, M-Sat) for now, but they expect to stay open later (7P) in the next few weeks.

Any chance of mega bags of honest to goodness chicharon with suka? Please?!

Prices are reasonable, location is accessible, staff super friendly, and food is delicious. I'm a fan!
It's the closest thing to Seattle's Pike Place Market.
Great place to eat lunch and fill the fridge with great food!
Great variety of food and other items to purchase.  Enough places to sit. A fun place to go and browse, or just to grab a bite from many food venues.

So many delicious options, it's hard to decide what to get. I decided on the Baby back ribs in the corner of the market in the Amish section. The ribs meat literally fell of the bone and the rub was just right.

Tonight after a seminar in the city I walked to the market. I was disappointed that Dinic's was closed because their roast pork sandwich w/provolone and long hots is one of the best things i have ever eaten. I got some jerky at the store i cant remember the name of that is awesome.  I got dinner to bring home for the fam from a place that i havent tried before. Glick's rib shack is AMAZING!!! The baby back ribs and the spicy sauce are delish!!! Surprisingly, the green beans are so so good!! Highly recommend Glick's!
Every tourist should visit the Reading Terminal Market!
So crowded and smelled like trash. But a cool place and I get the idea. On our way out we picked up pastries at Termini Bros. The lady was super nice and it was quick considering the crowd.

Ten months after my first visit, and I'm still obsessed. 

-The quality of their food has definitely improved since their opening. During my first visit (months ago) the chicken in my Kati roll was a little dry -- recently, the chicken has been perfect and moist. 

-Masala Kitchen is my go to for a post-bar snack, but I've also visited for a quick and cheap lunch. They also can put an egg into your roll (for an additional 50 cents), which makes it a lot more filling. 

-The Paneer Masala Roll is still my favorite, but I've now tried basically all of their rolls and can safely say that they're all pretty good. I'm not the biggest fan of the basic egg one though since it's a lot smaller than the rest. 

-I've gotten them to cater a lunch, and they're professional, easy to work with, and reasonably priced (free delivery!)

One con: the interior of MK has gotten a little smokey lately, so be prepared to leave smelling like indian spices and grill.
Very eclectic market, arrive early for best selection and to avoid the crowds.

Oh my goodness! I went to Philidlphia two weekends in a row, one for a bachelorette party and the other with a friend and we most certainly went here both times. If you visit Philly this is a MUST SEE! There are over 50 different vendors here that offer some extremely delicious and high quality products. I absolutely loved everything I got from here. Between the breakfast we ate at Down Home Diner to the doughnuts we got from Beiler's Donuts, it was all exquisite!

In terms of the ambiance, it is SUCH FUN! There is a ton to see and experience, as well as sample if you go at the right time where some places are offering samples of their products. It was a great place to also go with children, as there is something to appeal even to the pickiest eaters. Really and truly have a crush on Reading Terminal Market, it is such an amazing spot!
Shop. Market. Eat. The best! It's NOT just for tourists. Hotspur

Nothing like Reading Terminal to give you a unique experience of the Amish markets, fresh  farm grown produce, squeezed juice, and a plethora of cultural cuisines. My favorites are the crepe place, Olympia Gyro, 4th street famous cookies (woww), Termini Bros Bakery (Cheesecake!!), DiNic's roast pork, Bassetts Ice Cream. It's a struggle to find seats and maneuver through the crowds, so be prepared !

Many different places to eat, from all sorts of cultures. My family decided at the end to eat some Mexican food and it was just wonderful and the portions were huge too. We went twice, once Saturday around 2-3pm just to look around and we could barely move around because there were tons of people, and again Sunday around the same time and there was a lot less people. Just be mindful of when you want to visit.
One of the best places to go for fresh cuts and random food adventures! Too bad I only get to visit about once a month or so ... :)

Something for everyone!  Fantastic place to eat and buy food to take away.  From home style goods to food for all tastes.  We stayed close by during our visit to Philly and ended up at the market multiple times for food and snacks.  Loved this place!

Reading Terminal Market is awesome. You have a wide variety selection of anything to get to eat while there, to-go or grocery shopping for later. There are endless top notch food places here. It's great for people watching as well. A nice place for "tourists" to check out or anyone who works in the area for a good lunch. Could even have a super cute date night here. But, be prepared for crowds, lines and be comfortable with being uncomfortably close to people lol - many tourists flock to this place and do not know their way around, just a warning. The crowds/lines are well worth it though!

I freaking love this place. I'm big on variety and there is a little of everything here. I've eaten a multiple stations in here and no one has disappointed me yet. My fav is Hershals deli corn beef sandwich and the famous something (forgot exact name) cookies. Their chocolate chip with walnuts is huge and really yummy. I usually get one to share during the day and keep other one for late night need something after going out in my belly to soak up some of the fun from that night:)

This place is especially good if you have picky eaters with you. Something for everyone.

Destination numeral uno in Philadelphia.  Eclectic nirvana.  Sensory overload!  Definitely a must see place if you're in Philadelphia. Luckily a friend of a friend told us about this place and we took the opportunity to visit.  Fun evening!  Way too much to see or eat in one evening.   Hope to have a chance to come back to Philly again!
Great food and great value! Lots of option! Specially brisket ! That is really good ! And they have few fruit store with great value! I bought strawberry box for a dollar ! Fresh!

This was one of the first places I ever went in Philly and its still one of my favorite places in America. You can try food from all over the world and America in one convenient place at affordable prices and then buy very reasonably priced groceries to bring home.

We actually did a food tour that is offered on Wednesdays and Saturdays and it was a blast. The tour took us through the market with various food samples such as Apple cake, ice cream, snapping turtle soup, scrapple, and chocolate. We also went outside of the building to have a look at what used to be the Reading Terminal, which is now part of the convention center. It was a great way to get a history of the place and well as be introduced to some foods that I never knew about (scrapple!) and get pointed in the direction of all the best places to try and learn the proper way of ordering a cheesesteak. 

We also went all around and tried various samples that were put out on the stalls. They have the best cheese I've had, anywhere. MOST of the cheese I tried were absolutely wonderful and some of the cheese spreads were also amazing and super affordable.

Last but not least, I also did some grocery shopping. Got some sausages from Martin's, and some fish and mussels from the shop across from Martins. The fish was great, but the mussels were a bit funky even when I bought them. I made the mistake of trying to cook them the next day and they really started to reek at that point, so I just threw them out. The one sausage that I have tried so far, the merguez, has been excellent.

Amazing authentic Philipino food. Very friendly owner and service.

Lumpia: is very crispy not too greasy filled with meat. Definitely get this.

Flan: delicious with perfect sweetness and density. Highly recommend.

Container except for the porridge is environmentally friendly.

Chicken rice porridge: special menu. It's a chicken congee with ginger. Really refreshing. Perfect for cold winter day.

We took the chicken and rice platter and Achari chicken roll. The serving portion was huge for the platter  and  had amazing  flavors.  The roll was just ok, or maybe I took the wrong option.  For a place to be named kathi roll, you needed to up your game more.
A great historical market with tons of good food! Loved visiting it and enjoyed everything we had there!

First time at The Bourse and was excited to see this, especially as I saw a list online saying that this was the best offering at the Bourse. Overall, I think this place is probably the most interesting and unique vendor that I saw. 

Anyway onto La Lo experience, I ordered the Longanisa dog (sweet garlic pork sausage) for $10 and the mango juice for $3.50. The person working at the counter was pleasant and kind. However, they worked at a snail's pace to get my food. It was a bit past the peak dinner hour, and I was the only customer waiting. I really was not sure what they were doing, and I was seriously considering reminding them that I had ordered some food. However, I don't mind lackluster service if the food is good.

Onto the food. The longanisa dog was quite pleasant. Certainly quite a departure from the traditional kielbasas, sausage, and hot dogs with the longanisa dog having more of a sweet more gentle flavor with notes of savory meat. While it is not the same thing, it kind of reminded me of Chinese roasted pork (Char siu). The bun was sweet with a bit of a chewiness that worked well. The entire sausage was seasoned with a creamy sauce and garnished with some scallion. The sauce added a much needed savoriness to the sausage and the scallion contributed a nice refreshing crunch. 

The order came with a bit of chips that had a nice satisfactory crunch but was a bit under-seasoned. They did have spicy chili vinegar and fish sauce as condiments; the chips were improved with the addition of the former. 

The mango juice ($3.5) was just from a can. It was good, but wow, was the markup steep. You could get it for a fraction of that cost from Amazon or from Chinatown.

My biggest complaint about this was the price. The entire $10 meal with the sausage+bun with the chips was contained in a paper container that would normally be used to store a small order of fries. Was the food good? Sure. Was it phenomenal? No-- it was okay. If the price point was lower, this would have easily been a 3 star review. I get that this is in a touristy part of town, but so is Chelsea Market in NYC. At least the food there is generally at least really good even for the price.
Bad on every level.   They don't care.   Simple as that.  FU is the vibe from start to finish.   Management non existent.    Lots of love otherwise.   cheers.

DAM DAM DAM, and more DAMS!
This is a foodies dream! Yes it was featured on a number of foodie travel shows but to visit really is the telling tale. Walking in the Reading Terminal overall is an overwhelming experience but once you get your bearings right and focus, off you go! My gosh the food looked, smelled and taste amazing! From hoagies to Italian to Chinese to cheesesteaks to halal to Mexican; all is represented! The fresh meat, cheese, produce, seafood; amazing 

So what did I walk out with???

Sour candy of multiple types
Pistachios: chili lime and chipotle 
Sriracha Peas
Salami
Beef Prosciutto 
Pickled veggies
Lemon curd 
Beef sticks with jalapeños and cheese
Jam
Hot Sauce
And VODKA!!! 

Yes folks I had lost my foodie mind! No clue how I'm getting all this home to Cali but I will! Thanks to all the local folks, this was amazing!
One of my favorite things about Philly. Open everyday get any everything you need to cook to eat

Definitely a staple of philly. In prime location and has a little bit of everything to try. It's really busy and you're going to be bumping into people but that just comes with the territory. A must go if you're visiting philly.

My all time favorite market and must see in Philadelphia. So many delicious options for food and treats. Any food you can imagine under one roof. 

Perfect if everyone in your party likes different foods there are tables and chairs to sit and eat after picking which vendor you will be dining with.

While roaming on the streets of the phili downtown, following map, we came across reading terminal market. Intrigued by the number of people going in and out, we chucked our lunch plans and entered the world of this market. Flooded with variety of food options, fresh as they can get, we were tempted to try everything. The air was filled with the aroma coming from the food vendors, restaurants, bakeries, coffee, ice cream. I wanted to try everything I can eat. Constrained by the time, we tried French and Italian bakeries, and Mediterranean. The fresh baguette, focaccia, bagels, pastries, cannolis, and hummus-carrots were meddling with our taste buds. The coffee here is the best you can get anywhere. We left tempted as we hurried towards the next destination. However, later in the day while crossing this again, we came here for a quick pick up of cheese-tomato baguette to satiate us while we explored the endless options in this market. It is like inside farmers market which has everything, fun, food and fresh produce. It is part of Philadelphia culture and highly recommended on your visit/ stay.

This place is THE ultimate foodie paradise. I can (and have) easily spent hours here, browsing the endless rows of food stands. I come here from NYC because unfortunately there is nothing in the city that even remotely compares to this place (admittedly, it has crossed my mind to move to Philadelphia just to have this place near me). 

A few of my favorite things: jerky, San Kee duck noodle soup and Amish donuts. 

Pure amazingness indeed!

The best food options in one place ever. Best farmers market. I honestly love the market. Find something new every time I go inside and I'm there often. Great atmosphere. Definitely a hot spot and always busy.

I cannot lie, I am not sad to see Marabella Meatball company gone from this location- and I think Masala Kitchen has a great idea that's a good fit for the area- Indian food that's quick and good on the go. 

There's a lot of seating, so I'd imagine this'd be a good spot late night with a group. I got the chicken masala roll. I liked the sauce, I'd imagine a chicken tikka masala made in it would be delicious. However, I don't think the chicken had a chance to cook long enough in it- the meat itself was tender, but a bit bland. I liked that the naan it was wrapped in wasn't too thick, and how the roll was pressed in a panini press to make it more compact/easier to travel with.
The most overrated place in Philadelphia.  WAAAAAY too crowded.  I hope you don't like moving.
Place is awesome. Something for everyone. Dinic's Roast pork sandwich is my favorite!

Reading Terminal Market is a great place to shop and EAT!!! They have tons of different foods and baked goods.  My favorite spots are Ms. Tootsies Soul Food and The Amish BBQ chicken from Diner's BBQ chicken.  Even though I am born and raised in Philly I have yet to discover all that Reading Terminal has to offer, because there are so many different things inside.  All very reasonable prices.  A good place to stop and look around on a day off or even just to stop by just to grab a bite to eat for lunch.

I always drop in whenever I'm near there.

This place is always busy.  Great variety great food must visit.. Gotta visit Dinics the sandwhichs are great. If your lucky ull get a seat .  Make sure you know what you want or they get pissed. And no they dont have lettuce or tomato lol
The one place that looks a proper market. The city needs more of this kind.
The best for all things Philly regular visitor. See Kabal and his boys for a juice and love Dinics and of course the fresh produce

It was not the best butternut squash soup I've ever had, HOWEVER; it IS the best grilled cheese I've ever had!!! The grilled cheese, the draft beer selection, the service and the location are enough to overcome the average, but still good soup for a rare five star rating from uppity me!!

Interesting assortment of stores, food, and merchandise.  Some good food places in there.  The place is old but seems a bit on the grungy side.  Way too crowded to really enjoy.  You can almost forget about getting a quick bite to eat, as it's usually a long wait in lines to purchase food.

Essentially the Chelsea Market of Philadelphia. Such a great place to come to for all foodies. It gets super crowded through as it is the most touristy spot in the city.

Wished this place would be more friendly for people coming in later in the afternoon/evening as they close around 6pm. Some of the stands even close earlier around 3pm which is a letdown to me.

This bustling market is a must see for anyone visiting Philadelphia! Lots of amazing food, desserts, and shops, ranging from Mexican food to cheesesteaks to incredible bakeries. Not much inside seating, it can get quite crowded, and it closes before dinner time. But it is worth the trip - so may great options!

Often too crowded and has trouble-making crazy people inside.  I become impatient with things there like: this place made a tasty hamburger but they put salt on it plus the order taker talked crude.  Food would have tasted better without salt.

The best places to eat. Food from all different cultures and experience down folk real philly types of local die heart philly fans.  Lots of philly locals like myself have being coming to Reading Terminal for two generations. People sitting around hanging out meeting family, friends and co- workers plus cool  tourist from all over the world on vacation in our great Philadelphia town. And yes you can find vegan and vegetarian food there while listening to some nice jazz and panio sounds.
Great for grabbing stuff to make for dinner, also fun to show your tourists. I love Dinic's and tried the Flying Monkey this past weekend. Big fan!

This place is Amazing!!! Such good food and super nice people!  I could walk around and eat my way through this place. There is lots of fun things to try from Oysters to cheesesteaks to pickles to donuts to tea to James and jelly's. I've tried some of the best donuts at a place that starts with a "B" sorry can't remember the name and the best cheesesteak at Carmen's. Will be back to try more food and some fresh produce!

Masala Kitchen has become a favorite amongst many of the center city locals with dozens of kati rolls, multiple levels of flavors, employee discounts, and hot off the grill meat for the rice bowls. Having ordered almost every single roll (ranging from about $4-6), my favorite is still the masala chicken and the aloo (potato) rolls, and you have to get them extra spicy. The pepper/veggie versions tend to a bit too salty for my taste and rob flavor from the meat. In addition to the classic rolls and bowls, Masala kitchen also offers lassi and eclectic sodas, but it's prepackaged and would prefer freshly made versions instead.

Overall, this is a great spot if you're hungering for 2-3 rolls and it should only set you back for about $15, which is a great price for Center City.

Food: 4 stars
Price: 4 stars
Ambiance: 3 stars
Service: 3-4 stars

We ordered from here for delivery last night because we've been eating absolute shit lately and I wanted something on the healthier side. 

One eyeball perusal of the menu reveals many enticing menu options including a pastry stuffed with HALLOUMI and oregano and CHEESE ROLLS. 

In other news, this place is a mediterranean-chipotle-esque in the sense that you choose a style (bowl, wrap, salad) and then choose a protein and toppings and sauces and all that good shit. I ordered a salad with falafel (shawarma, lamb, and another veggie selection-cauliflower are other choices) with a bunch of toppings and sauces. The selection is DOPE, there is literally a million things to choose from and they don't charge you if you go over a certain number! I actually omitted the hummus because we also ordered a side and I didn't think it was necessary. 

My little falafel ball ordered a bowl with freeka grain because what the fuck is that. 

We also ordered lentil soup because our original order with all things stated above was literally only $35. This COULDN'T be real. There MUST be something wrong with an order so cheap. We had to rectify this situation by ordering a large portion of the lentil soup. 

The food came in reasonable amount of time. We actually let it sit for a while because we cracked open the vodka and poured ourselves an after-a-long-day-of-work vodka soda with a splash of cran. More than a splash for me. 

When we did finally bust that bag open I came to an immediate realization that THERE WAS NO HUMMUS. This is literally the main reason I ordered mediterranean food. I said to be healthy but I'm full of shit. Devastation ensued. I called the place and they surprisingly answered the phone after closing and referred me to caviar to make a complaint. There were a bunch of apologies and promise that it would never happen again. The response was nice but I would have preferred if they actually gave us everything we ordered from the start. This is the main reason for the three stars because the food was amazing.

The falafel was honestly one of the best falafel I've ever had and I've been to israel. It was DELICIOUS. The ingredients were fresh, based on what I could tell from my low-lighting ambiance living room. The sauces were amazing. I ate the SHIT out of this in two seconds I felt mildly sick afterwards. The cheese rolls were really good as well and I would order them again. The lentil soup has spinach and potatoes in it as well but had a slightly lower ingredients:liquid ratio than I'm used to with this variety of soup. My GF's freeka or whatever tf that is was DELICIOUS. She was so full she ate like half of it and I helped her out with about a quarter. 

I would definitely order from this place again if I wasn't worried that they would miss something in our order which is pretty irritating.
Crazy place like something out of Harry Potter but you're gonna find something good to eat

dkhfgkldshjfgkldsjhfg
dfglkdjfjjff fjfjfjflskdfjgh sdflkgjhdsfg  ghgjflkjdsfg dkfgjhd fgjj
this place is too crowded makes me feel icky sticky. and so expensive! i got some icecream for almost $5. what the HECK! i would rather stay home

Overall I love reading. They have great groceries, amazing desserts, and random little stalls that offer everything from earrings to honey chapstick. I'll break this down more

Groceries: I go to reading terminal for groceries as much as I can. I've been able to find everything, and for cheaper/fresher, except for milk and pasta. I always get my fruits and vegetables from "ok produce." They generally sell berries for $.99 to $1.99, and small bags of eggplant, apples, mushrooms, cauliflower, etc. for the same price ($1-$2). I'll get two full bags of fruits and vegetables and spend less than $10. Produce is always a good buy as well. Whether I need mussels, oxtail, or chicken I'm always guaranteed to get a good buy (and with multiple fish and meat markets you can take your pick). 
There's also a spice/dry goods store that I LOVE. I buy loose leaf tea, spices, and lentils/other grains all the time. Again, super cheap and very varied.

Food: The food is just ok. It's cool that they have pretty much any type of food you might want, but it's definitely not the best quality. The Indian food is underwhelming and the flavors are never on point, Japanese food is American Japanese and again not that great, but the soul food is pretty good. I wouldn't go to reading for the soul food alone, but if I have to eat there that's usually what I'll get. I'd recommend getting groceries and snacks in reading, and then eating in chinatown. 

Snacks/dessert: Beilers donuts are fresh rolled and amazing, reading terminal has addictive cannolis, and any of the bakeries has great croissants and other baked goods. I come to reading purely for the cannolis when i get cravings

Reading Terminal Market was the last place my parents and I checked out before heading back to NYC.

We walked in here for some breakfast without really knowing what we were getting ourselves into!! 

Walked out with a tummy filled with a nice sausage egg and cheese sandwich, a nice cup of joe, a bag filled with sticky buns, pumpkin roll with cream cheese frosting, bags and bags of candy and a donut. 

My parents and I were set as far as "snacks for the trip back" was concerned.

This place is really cool. There are a bunch of sandwich shops, an Amish corner that has breakfast, lunch, and dinner foods, a bakery, and a sweet shop, a large fresh produce section, olive oil & vinegar shop, several coffee shops/bakeries, as well as some cultural food like Indian, creole, Thai, and Chinese.

It's fun just to walk around and in general, things are very reasonably priced. Yelp reviews say this is $$, but I'd actually say at a lot of places you can get a sandwich and drink for just about $10. 

Even though it may seem overwhelming at first (& somewhat easy to get lost in), I'd suggest walking around first to get an idea of your options before choosing a spot to eat. Dicnic's roast pork sandwich is really good. I am not from Philly, so I wanted to try the traditional roast pork w/provolone & broccoli rabe, but I was not a huge fan. Next time, I'd get the roast pork w/provolone & roasted peppers. The broccoli rabe is more bitter than I expected and did not taste like broccoli at all. 

Tip - try to walk here or take the train & walk because parking is only street parking & it's difficult to find

When want good brunch in Philly, we go here. The beer taps usually offer a good variety of quality craft beers. The menu is good a changes regularly. The pancakes are tasty in either iteration they offer. And the coffee is fantastic. I know most people aren't coming here for coffee, but it is definitely worth drinking.
 The staff has always been friendly to us. They give us enough time to enjoy our meal and beverages without being interrupted every 3 minutes but not so much our glasses have ever gone empty without offering a refill.
 Thanks for having a great place to eat in this part of town...

Been to a lot of markets that carry many different produce and I must admit, reading terminal is a total rip off. Pricing is extremely high, and while some of the produce is very good, you can get the same quality at Whole Foods cheaper. I would say this is more tourist trap than anything. Had my first roast pork sandwich with  broccoli rabe at Dinic and it was eeh. Wasn't my thing, it was juicy but the pork was bland and the broccoli rabe was off putting in the sandwich. I prefer Chelsea market in ny or central market in L.A.. Those places are a lot cleaner and the you can get more exotic stuff!

Literally has every cuisine your heart could possibly desire.  I highly recommend stopping by the Louisiana creole stand if you're roaming and trying their chicken and sausage etouffee- although fair warning, if you do, you'll probably end up eating there (it IS a bit spicy). Aside from that, you'll also find fresh produce, meats, chocolates, cookies... everything!

One of my favorite places to go when i visited Philadelphia.  This market had so many different types of food to try...aisles and aisles of restaurants.  I wanted to try every place and every food...but i simply didnt have enough time.  This place is a foodie's heaven!  During lunch hours...this place gets packed!  especially the more popular restaurants (long lines)...all the empty seats they have pretty much get filled during peak hours.  Everyone that works there is nice and friendly.  This market is huge!  it will take you a while to look at all the restaurants and food.

Next time i'm in Philadelphia, i'm definitely coming back to place and trying all the places i missed the first time!!  I wished they have this type of place where i live. =(
The Chicken Keema roll was great. Staff is polite and service is quick. Also, the place is open till late so it's perfect for a mid night snack.

This place has everything! Sandwiches. Pizza. The best Philly Cheesesteaks. Homemade desserts galore. Local products and crafts for sale. Farmers market. Butcher. Ice cream. If you're touristing around, this is a definite go to for your group. Everyone can find something they love.

What can I say about this place that hasn't already been said?! This is the go to spot for all things delicious! Had some roasted pork, ate a giant Amish pickle and potato salad and killed some doughnuts. This place is top notch and i'd highly recommend.
One of the nicest McDonalds I've ever been to. Staff is polite and efficient. Despite the location, nobody seemed even particularly sketch.

Wow! You could eat three meals a day here for weeks and still likely not try everything! I stride walking the place twice to find the best option and still missed some stuff. Had a cheesesteak and one of the many options there and it was excellent. The ice cream was great too and I'm sure all the other options are tasty too! Truly a must see if you're visiting the area!

This is a simple, clean counter service restaurant with some or the best Indian food I've had.  The white sauce they offer is truly flavorful and balances the spice really well. Kati rolls, platters, etc. all delicious. Affordable as well.

Tried Karen Parker for the first time and the fish was outstanding!!! But lawd the Mac & cheese was thee absolute worse I've ever tasted!! No taste, bland, salt & pepper did no justice. I would come back but for the fish only.
The workers customer service was fantastic!!

By far, one of the Top 10 places in Philadelphia you must visit. My favorite places are: Iovine Brothers (produce), Hershel's (for sandwiches), Flying Monkey(for sweets), Little Thai Market (for Thai food) and for breakfast Dutch Eating Place. 

Whatever you are looking for: the market has it. For first time visitors, grab a map, cause the places are side by side and lunch time and after work "4-6PM" It crazy packed. Especially Saturdays. Have a game plan before heading in.
A nice place to surf or walk around. Find music art and mostly food. Nice bunch of people around from painter to piano players.I have fun every time I come and go somewhere different.

The perfect market for center city Philly.  A good balance of fresh ingredients and prepared foods to fit every cools needs and budget.  Saturday is usually the day of full isles with locals and tons of visitors.  Great place for lunch, shopping and people watching.

This is an indoor heaven market....

Once u step inside is like a whole different world !!!
There's a raw oyster bar ! 
Pecking ducks 
Middle Eastern food
Greek food
Soul food
Of course PHILLY CHEESE STEAKS!!!
There's also skin care products! 
Organic honey !
Varieties of desserts like a brownie stand  but be careful is weight by the pound and u will easily spend $40 getting brownies---  but what is that keeps me coming here !!!
The freshly baked donuts made by the Amish people - the line by far is the longest line in the market -  I just had to try it and I don't even like donuts like that ....

All I have to say is if Beilers donuts were in NJ- Dunkin Donuts would be out of business! I honestly drove one afternoon to Philly just for the donuts I kid u not !!!

I can't even describe it -it's so good u will never buy donuts from any other place!!!

Now what I don't like is that there are not many seating areas but I guess u could eat standing up ?
A must see and experience when in Philadelphia. Hustling and bustling food frenzy.  Something for everyone but good luck finding a table to sit while enjoying your epicurean delights.

RTM is a destination that has something for everyone. From comfort food at the Dutch Eating Place, bakery goods at Terminis, Lamb Tacos, Chinese soups at Sang Kee, and fresh produce and meats galore Reading terminal is an eating and shopping mecca that gives a Center City resident an alternative to the supermarket.  Always remember the Amish merchants are not there every day. Sundays and Mondays they are usually closed, though some may not be there on Tuesdays either. Lately there has been a lot of movement in the market, and new merchants have moved in, so its worth revisiting if you have not been there in a while.

This place is great!  
Here you can find the BEST donuts (Beiler's), some delicious PA Dutch foods of other kinds, plus about any kind of ethnic food you might want, and lots of knick knacks and gift items, as well as fresh fish (sushi grade, if you're into that kind of thing, which I am), fresh veggies (not really your typical farmer's market options though -- I think they're mostly shipped in from Mexico/California/wherever most grocery store veggies come from) and lots of other local mainstays.  
HOWEVER, this place is often mobbed by people from conventions, and things can be overpriced.  
If you are a guest from out of town, you will find few better places for fun, tasty foods and some local flavor, and if you live within walking distance, it's worth coming here for certain things, but it doesn't rank in my top 10 places for food in the city, not even close!
How can you not love this place.  There is something for everyone, I always try to make a visit and bring home food for my friends/family.  Delicious
This spot has great eateries. However seating was already limited. So the solurion was to remove more seats and make sitting even more limited. What a stupid idea.

I enjoyed my 1st time here. Lots of delicious food to try out and experience my highlight was turtle soup which was very good. It's a market with dress fruit and veggies. Just have to stop pass and see for your self

If you are a foodie, you've got to go to The Reading Terminal!  It is awesome.  It's basically an indoor farmers market that takes up an entire block in Center City.  My favorite thing at this market is the food products and food stations operated by the Amish.  Consistently delicious!  They also have lots of fresh produce, great butchers, fresh fish, fresh baked goods, and some artisans with various products ranging from jewelry to cooking gadgets to candles.  They also offer cooking classes, but I haven't taken advantage of that yet.

This place reminded me of the grand central market in L.A. so it's most def a must stop here either for shopping, drinking and definitely eating! Or take some food so you can take a stroll down to Love park which is only a few blocks away. This place was hella crowded but I see why. For sure a busy place not only for tourists  for locals as well.

Foodie heaven. If your ever in Philly you must go to this place. You can spend the whole day walking around stuffing your face with delicious, freshly prepared food. Some establishments are  pricey so don't get fooled.

I am half Filipino and grew up in California with the surplus of pancit. I am GF and was really happy to find this cute little food court area and LALO had something for me! The food is not your authentic Filipino cuisine so please keep that in mind. However, it is a great place to eat something wholesome and I mean who doesn't love okra? I was being a tourist and came about this after a long day of walking around for lunch.

Love this place. Go here with an appetite. You can have breakfast, brunch, lunch, snacks and more meals here. It has a mixture from candy to donuts to seafood and greek food. Every cuisine is there. 

It gets pretty warm in there. On the weekend it is crowded. The place closes at 5pm so get there before then.

There are certain places where the lines are insane but they go by fast.

What don't they have here?! Food galore, cooked and uncooked. I came here on a Saturday and we got parking for $4 at the Hilton Garden Inn parking deck, you have to spend at least $10 total at the Reading Terminal and one of the cashiers will validate your parking ticket... otherwise expect to pay at least $6 every 30 min..  There's a doughnut place here they make the doughnuts by hand daily.. line can get rather long on the weekend... I had one of the doughnuts it was okay... We also went to this Grilled cheese place they make the cheese by hand and some they store in a cave for a year! (Off site, of course) Enjoy, this place was epic!

I love markets so of course I had to put this on my list of things to do. No matter how big of a group you have everyone can find a spot to satisfy their craving. They have clothing, sweets, foods and many other items.
Amazing... always fun to walk around and get a bite to eat. And if you have family from out of town, obviously a go to spot.

A true taste of what Philly is all about (pun intended).  It is best to go during non-peak hours; I recommend mid-afternoon.  While there are a ton of vendors, DiNic's is definitely the crown jewl of the market.  Also be sure to try the Amish vendors who sell desserts; you can't get the quality anywhere else.  A full tour of China Town's delights (Dim Sum Garden) + Reading Terminal Market is a true treat for the tongue.

Where else can you buy fruits and vegetables, prepared foods, baked goods, and grab a brewski at the beer garden ? very cool place, always bustling with activity, very fresh seafood, very friendly people. Look if you have never been you gotta try it. Awesome lil gem in the city with something for everyone, however if your a " I hate crowds" kinda miserable person, well this is probably not for you. Happy exploring!

Imagine one of the best food courts you've ever been to and you got the Reading Terminal. We came here in search of a sandwich we saw on the Food Network and tried not to get carried away with all of the mouth watering foods. 

I saw some of the biggest prawns I've ever seen, great looking "salads and sides" had some amazing desserts and of course we ate the sandwich we were looking for (review to come). We also stopped at Molly Malone's for a pint with our sandwich. 

My question is if you had the opportunity to come here every day, what would you choose? It all looks fantastic. 

The one thing we really missed out on was the Pennsylvania Dutch (Amish) vendors since we came here on a Monday and they were closed. We even tried back on Tuesday to no avail, so if you are headed to Reading - make sure to come Wednesday thru Saturday to make sure you get to try it all.

This place is amazing! So many yummmy places to try. From good cheesesteaks, to chocolate, juices, bars. It's a place to spend a few hours roaming around trying out different foods. I tried the philly from Carmens and it was really good. This Irish pub is awesome too. Lots of seating and good food.

I love everything about this place except the prices and business hours. go alone or meet up with friends, either way you'll find something delicious to eat or something interesting to see. one of Philadelphia's great jewels!

My only complaint about Reading Terminal Market is that I can never decide where to eat, particularly when I'm really hungry (which, let's be real, is all the time). 

Is it a tourist trap? Maybe. Is it a fat kid's heaven? Yep. 

I've probably only sampled about a quarter of the total merchants within RTM, but I'm never disappointed. Not gonna lie though, some places are just average food-wise, but the charm of this place really makes up for average food in my mind. My personal recommendations are:

Profi's Creperie
12th St Cantina
Dutch Eating Place 
The Original Turkey
Bassets Ice Cream

Also, the fresh produce/meats/cheeses/bakery products/flowers available for purchase here are all incredible. Definitely leave yourself enough time to wander the place after you've stuffed your face to full capacity.

My sister was nice enough to bring me dinner from Masala Kitchen this evening.... #blessed. It was literally the best meal I've had all week.

Unfortunately I can't comment on the actual restaurant but boy, does the food speak for itself. I tried the chicken masala kati roll. It was so good! Extremely flavorful and the chicken tasted fresh. The best part? The white, yogurt based dipping sauce it came with. I've had my fair share of Indian food before but I've never had anything like this. It is literally out of this world! Do yourself a favor and ask for an extra container of it. You can thank me later! :)

Awesome farmers market type area. You're able to get any kind of prepared food you want, ingredients, flowers, etc... I had an amazing ice cream cone what was so large I had to get a bowl as well cause I would not have been able to eat all of it before it fell over. Really great place - a must stop.

Reading Terminal compared to other city indoor farmer markets, this one is much smaller but at least some or most of the vendors open on Sundays.  Food sell out fast for certain famous places on weekends so better grab the food first (even you were not hungry) then eat them later; they generally still tasted very good :)  Most of the food I tried, none disappointed me except the apple dumpling. It was too sweet, too saggy; the crust was soaked, I ate it when it was still warm.  It was the only one thing I didn't save it for later.

Sooo many choices. I can't even remember where we ate. I do remember the delicious pastrami sandwich though. And the very delicious crepes! You can find all kinds of yummines! Chocolate-honey-nuts-cakes and pies. If only parking in the area was easier, but it is downtown after all... Will go back, but this time I'll take the subway.

Amazing selection of meat, fish, cheese, honey, and crafts. I'd suggest going on weekdays instead of weekends due to high foot traffic. Also, try going earlier rather than later for the freshest foods and less crowds.

Fun place to walk around and see all the fresh meats, fish and produce. 
We ate breakfast at the Dutch Eating Place. I had mushroom omelette which was very good. Really creamy American cheese. Then had side of blueberry pancake. It was unfortunate that it was luke warm,  but still tasty. A little floury taste was evident. 
Husband had eggs over easy with bacon, which was plentiful and quite salty. 
We ended up speaking to both couples on either side of us, which was really nice. They said chipped beef good as was the apple dumpling dessert. 
Always find it fascinating the people that come across your path. 
This is a must go to place when in Philly!!  
Within walking distance to ALoft downtown where we were staying. See my review...
Amazing time at the market, awesome experience but it was packed. Enjoyed my time!! Great place to go if you are with a large group of people and they are not all sure what they want to eat.

Whenever friends visit from out of town, I take them here. If you live in Philly and haven't been, you're a fool. There are so many options for food and much more. Reading Terminal is great for eating and for shopping and wandering. Some standouts are the Dutch Eating Place and Hershel's Deli, though you really can't go wrong.

Amazing.  Philly's finest.  Everything here is good.  Donuts, Cajun, all amazing!!!  Definitely stop here for some food if you're hunan.  This place is huge, has great variety, and some amazing, fresh food.

The choices are endless. Every time I go inside I am overwhelmed about where to look and what to eat. My favorite choice is Beck's Cajun Cafe. I love their cajun chicken poboy and cajun fries. I also love Bassett's Ice Cream. They have so many delicious flavors, it's the best way to end a trip to Reading Terminal Market.

Love this place. A true Philadelphia original. I've been going to this market since I was a child in the sixties, and it still has that wonderful charm. How many places can say that today? From the best in baked goods and confections, to the freshest meat, fish, and produce, you can hardly go wrong shopping here. Also a great lunch spot!

Best pizza I've had in Philly. Owner Josh and Cello are freaking awesome people. Had a slice of pepperoni and Mexican Coke to buy some time today and we chatted the entire time. Great people and f'ing amazing pizza. Almost worth the trip from Oklahoma alone! Holy crap! Go here. Now.

Amazing location with options for days!

DiNic's is my personal favorite, always providing freshly made food!

Been eating and shopping here 25+ years! Still the best place in Philadelphia for day feasting and shopping. So much culture, so much history, so much Food! Eat all the classics from roast pork to Amish burgers. Shop for top quality meat and produce along with exceptional cheese and dairy. Support local farms and local Philadelphians!

Endless array of awesome food to choose from. You can get cooked, made to order, fresh from the seafood or butcher counter, and produce. Tons of great sweets and desserts. Also great Amish stores for goods and foods.

We had such a fun time here. We were visiting from out of town and wanted cheesesteaks. Of course we were on a time crunch so the traditional Pat/Gino's weren't an option so we decided on Reading. It was perfect! I had been here a few years ago and went again on this trip. They have everything from cheesesteaks to fresh fish to butchers to Amish baked goods. Something for everyone!
A Philly landmark. RIDICULOUSLY AMAZING! What's not to like. You can find anything & everything here.

I come here often, especially for the Beilers Donuts! They're made fresh daily, have endless amounts of flavor, and will leave you wanting to come back.

Pro tip - buy a 6 or more and they'll cost $1 per donut! That's less than Dunkin for much higher quality.
Great place to get a bite of all types of food , hustle bustle , great prices awesome food

Ordered here several times. The chicken masala Kati rolls are banging. They may seem a little pricey for their size but are loaded with meat. Their rice platters are pretty good too. The white sauce needs some work. Overall a great place for a quick Indian fix

When we first moved to Philadelphia, Reading Terminal Market was one of our first stops in the city. It is now a place we regularly visit when in the city. 

You can find anything from around the world here at Reading Terminal Market. From Indian cuisine to seafood, from fresh flowers to homemade accessories. 

It is fairly priced but it's all dependent on the place you decide to eat from. It is always packed and busy with all kinds of people. Definitely a must when visiting Philadelphia!

Absolutely no visit to Philadelphia is complete without a visit to the Reading Terminal.  You will have wasted your entire trip if you do not visit this place. It's a Philly Landmark;  A Philly Institution.  It would be like going to Italy, and never eat a slice of authentic pizza.  Anything your "foodie" mind want to eat, you will find it here.  Yes, the crowds can be massive, especially during lunch hour and on the weekend, but that's the beauty of it. I've mastered how to get around in here, but the smells of the different flavors of food, will certainly pull you in all directions, so indulge yourself and go where the aroma takes you. Bring a shopping bag too!
Amazing place.  Can be very overwhelming if it is your first time here but there is always someoen around to direct you to the best food spots.

Every time we go to Philly we check out the market.  Dinic's cheese steaks in the middle is the best cheese steak we've ever had! 

Everything is fresh; seafood, produce, baked treats!   

Every shop gives out samples so you can try before you buy!

Love love love coming over here.  I have my go-to spots, which I will specifically write about, but this place as a whole: food extravaganza!  Oysters, burgers, chocolate, bread, fried scrapple, halel food, Greek food......everything.  

It is a little clausterphobic and crowded in here, seating is atrocious, and it is a little tiny bit touristy (that's being generous), but that won't stop me from meandering over here to catch a bite for lunch.  Come early though.....some of the best spots close at 3.

Came here after the Broad Street Race for brunch. We went to the bar while our table was getting turned over. Not sure what the bartenders name was but he was extremely rude. He said he didn't have time to make any recommendations and that we should just order. After he made our drinks he gave them to us for free (which was nice) but acknowledged how out of line he was. We both got the breakfast tacos and home fries. Underwhelmed completely, not a ton of food and lack of savory flavors I was hoping for. The vibe was cool but other than that our experience was not great, starting with the bartender.

Fucking awesome!!! *drops mic* 
Best place to get everything under the sun and they never disappoint!!

I have been going to the Terminal since I was young and am now in my 50s. I have always loved this place especially during Thanksgiving and Christmas. I just love Spataro's, 12 Street Cantina and Bassetts Ice Cream. I am also disappointed that the Spice Terminal is gone. I also think that the Famous 4th Street Cookie Company is a little expensive and always has been. It's a great place, but can be really crowded especially during the lunch hour and holidays.

For dinner, we decided to go casual and try somewhere new! We found our spot- The Bourse! Inside the beautiful and historic building, you will find a variety of restaurants. You can find everything from pancakes to Filipino food!

My husband and I chose the Filipino cuisine at Lalo! I chose the Long Si Log which is pork sausage, garlic rice, and a soft egg. This dish was touched on all taste buds and textures! I thoroughly enjoyed the dish. Greg ordered the Lechon Kawali which is crispy pork belly with garlic rice. I tried a bite of Greg's dish and the pork belly was nicely rendered and actually crispy. Delicious!

Lots of great stuff here. If you have claustrophobia, panic disorder, any type of anxiety, etc. etc. avoid from 12pm-2pm. Avoid if there is a convention going on. There are literal swarms of human beings during this time and seating can be difficult to find.

Tips:
Iovine is the greatest, cheapest spot for produce and weird fruits.
Termini Bros has the best italian cookies. 
By George has banginnn pizza. Big slices.

Sure, this place is fun to walk through.  But the tourists who think this is a key food place to visit in Philly are seriously missing out.  Philly is a foodie paradise with INCREDIBLE restaurants!  Venture to 13th Street to try Lolita, Barbuzzo, or Jamonera, and to see all the gorgeous little shops on the street, including the artisanal chocolates made fresh at Verde; or go to Bareburger, Bluestone Lane, PS & Co, Buena Onda Tacos, V Street, Dizengoff, etc., for casual but DELICIOUS fresh food. Go to Cafe Karma (four locations) and sit in the beautiful gardens at their locations on 22nd/Pine or 10th/Pine.  Go to Whole Foods Center City and check out the delicious food hall!  For high-end restaurants, go to Talula's Garden, Zahav, Vedge, Res Ipsa, Suraya, and more!  To explore food heaven in West Philly, go to Kilimandjaro or Manakeesh restaurants, or try Chez Yasmine food truck.  For Vietnamese, go to Nam Phong or Vietnam Restaurant on Washington.  For pizza, go to Mama Palma's, Stella's, or Giorgio's on Pine.  Go to the fabulous Saturday Farmer's Market at Rittenhouse Square or the equally fabulous Sunday Farmer's Market at Headhouse Square. In South Philly, go to any of the treasures on Passyunk Avenue or to Stargazy for British pies. You get the idea...
Great variety and local foods and veggies. The ice cream and coffee are also very good. One icon place in philly that no one should miss when they are in town.

This market is great all except for the tacky food art hanging in center court. I'm guessing its some type of children's project? I really have no idea. All I know is I wanted to hold an event there and was told they could not be removed. 

Seriously? Good luck selling any parties in the near future with that eye sore..

10 Stars!!  Oh my gosh, I believe I just ate one of the best pizza's ever...Really, EVER. Whatever Pizzeria Beddia was doing, the new crew at Shackamaxon killing it just the same!!  Was back in town visiting family and been waiting for a good opportunity to drive over there. Being National Pi Day today...perfect reason...although when I walked in and said Happy National Pi Day, the guy looked at me quizingly. But the two guys were extremely nice and I enjoyed chatting with them. Seemed like a great staff!!

Ate slice of cheese, slice of pepperoni and pickled jalapeños, and 2 slices of the red tomato pie. All exceptional...but the tomato pie with great charred edges - all I can say is holy moly!!! it's un-f@#king-believable!!!...will make any bad day a good day!! I need to go back tomorrow before leaving City of Brotherly Love.
Great Kati rolls! Loved the beef roll and the chicken pepperwala! Definitely coming back for more!

It's been awhile since I was in downtown Philadelphia and you should always make time to stop at the Reading Terminal Market! This is the spot if you have any craving for great food and beverages. From OMG awesome donuts to classic Philly cheesesteaks, great sandwiches, seafood, soups, Middle East Food, BBQ, pastries, pizza and snacks I am sure I only scratched the surface so stop what you are doing and make sure you make the time to be here for lunch. There is an area for sitting down and enjoying your meals so no need to run out with it. Truly a must go to for your lunch cravings! Miss it already!!

Went to The Industry last night for dinner with my husband. We live in South Philly and are always looking for good restaurants close to home to put in our rotation. 
 
The Industry did not disappoint! The new interior is cool. The bar looked great. And our server was excellent. 

The food was very good. My husband had the pork nuggets, tartare and a swiss roll. I had the baby head lettuces, the veggie fritters and the wild berry short cake. We enjoyed everything. Well, except the swiss roll. My husband said it was kind of dry and not chocolatey enough. But our gracious server brought him the doughnuts instead which were amazing!

My husband was also happy that they have regular beer (Miller Lite) and not just craft beers. So many places we go who just have crafts beers do not offer a suitable pilsner and don't offer the regular mass market beers. He also had a glass of house cabernet that was very nice for a house wine. 

To the folks who think to is too expensive, it's not. Really, where are you eating??? To those who complained about the food, we need places like this in South Philly to push things a little! We need to add food options beyond the corner take-out and fast food. 

Overall, the is a nice addition to the neighborhood. I hope they flourish and add outdoor seating soon. Can't wait to try it for brunch.
Love reading terminal. So many different places to choose from and you can even grocery shop!

Great place to grab food, snacks and gifts. If you're here a few times, you learn the pattern when crowd starts getting larger and when it dies down. Wish that they would open later, although I find that most places in Philly closes early. 

If you're here for some Amish specialties, they are only at the market from Wednesday to Saturday. The other days, they are just moping at home wondering why they still need to drive to the city with their buggy.
A staple in Philadelphia food culture. You must eat here when visiting. If you don't you never really visited Philadelphia.

New place that has opened near city hall to cater for center city business district. I had a lot of expectations given it's global presence. Ordered lunch here through Grubhub for pickup. Food was ready by the time I reached. I ordered a falafel bowl with hummus and vegetables. It was good but nothing to write home about. There are plenty of middle eastern quick bite places in center city now so this place has a lot of competition and doesn't stand up to it. I would rate Naf Naf Grill better than Naya. 

Try it if you're in the neighborhood and want a quick bite. Not work it to travel to specially come here for food.
Everything about the market is great.  It's truly something you have to experience on your own to understand.

Who can imagine a Philadelphia without Reading Terminal.  I can't, and I don't want to.

Of course, the crowds are a problem, made up as they are of an uncomfortable mix of locals and tourists/conventioneers.  But such is the price one must expect to pay for having such an indispensable institution... everyone wants to go there, and for good reason.

Some pointers for the uninitiated:

- If driving, park at the garage across 12th Street.  Save your parking ticket, spend $10 or more at any vendor and they will validate, and the parking fee will be a mere $4 instead of the rack rate $26 as long as you check out of the garage within 2 hours of arriving.

- If you find yourself on Philly Jury Duty, walk here for lunch (1 block) and almost every food vendor will grant you a 10% discount.

- Amish and Mennonite-run stands are not open on Sundays.  It used to be the whole market wasn't open on Sundays, but thankfully that changed some years ago.

- The produce vendor Iovine Bros. on the south side of the market (bordering Filbert Street) is awesome.  Huge selection, great prices, and a nice mix of conventional and organically grown stuff.

I have been to many markets and this place takes first place. They have a farmers market and many places to eat different cuisine's. Prices were pretty fair. One thing that was surprising is the market closing at 6 PM. All of the staff encountered were incredibly friendly. With that being said, this is a very busy place! The space is tight and it could be overwhelming to make decisions of where to eat and the close proximity of vendors... Pretty typical of markets in large cities. I would not bring children here because of the limited space. They offer breakfast, lunch and dinner. Very fair competitive prices between vendors and generally kept quite clean. I'm going back again and again. Thank you!
Simply awesome. We got a half plain half pepperoni and it was on point. Staff was friendly and service was good. All around an easy 5 stars.

First off, I think yelping about fast food is a little silly - but a few weekends ago I had such a wonderful experience here, I feel like I HAD to tell the world. 

First off, it's probably one of the cleanest fast-food joints I've ever stepped foot in. The condiments area was absolutely pristine; there wasn't even a napkin out of place. I got my food about 30 seconds after I ordered it (which is a little creepy but awesome). There were fresh flowers on every table. 

And just when my friend and I were wow-ing at how impressive everything was, the manager came walking through checking to see how everyone was doing and if the food had met everyone's expectations. I mean WOW.

The only downfall of Chick-Fil-A is that they're not open every day.
WOW!  Tons to see buy and eat.  Really nice to get a feel for the past.  The worn out marble tables etc.

If I had to live in Philly I would do most of my shopping here probably as they do have some great selections for meats, cheeses, pickles, deli items, seasonings, specialty items.  I enjoyed the Amish selections on sweets and would have eaten here too but needed to move along.  The crowd is off-putting to me but that is what it is there.  parking cost a ton so we walked from our hotel.  I made a poor selection on a philly cheesesteak stand and it wasn't anything special and there was no place to actually sit and eat.  I won't ever go back but it was worth a look-see.
Huge selection of high quality food! Love each place in here. Very fresh food that's the best philly can offer. Also a tourist attraction in itself

I can never say enough about this place! Wish we had something this great in Memphis. From fresh seafood and meats to Amish pretzels and deli sandwiches you can find everything here. The pastrami at the deli is fantastic!

I tried the $5 deals today. Boneless hot buffalo wings and boneless teriyaki wings and bread sticks. The bread sticks were good. I see why the wings were $5 u get what u pay for. They tasted cheap. Like ribbed meat not white meat. Breading was over cooked. Borderline burnt taste. Nothing to write home about just average

It's a really nice find in the city. Lots of Philly- style food here. Great for tourists. Hard to find seats anytime of the market hours. Located in the heart of Philadelphia. Would like to come here again.

Holy shit.  Best tomato pie I've ever had.  I'm still in shock, it was so insanely good.

I just started working in the neighborhood and saw their tomato pie on instagram.  I walked over and luckily they weren't sold out! The guys behind the counter were awesome-Josh and Colin were both friendly and welcoming and just a delight.  I got two slices and ate one within 30 seconds almost, it was so delicious! Saving the other for dinner and already looking forward to it.

Go here! I'll be back! Thank you for the amazing tomato pie!

This is a late review from when visited but this place is on point in every good way possible. I've visited a few times for various meals but where they stood out was customer service on my catering order. I ordered some trays for a party I was having and the communication between them and myself just confirming the order and letting me know it was ready etc etc. the manager even came out to make sure all was great. When they say MY PLEASURE you actually believe that they care and enjoy helping. Which is rare in food...fast food...the world. So A++++ for this place

The only fired food I have been thinking about after almost a month. My boss brought fired chicken to me on the first day opening. It was surprised me especially I hadn't eaten for 8 hours! Plan to come to the store again this weekend.

Potbelly is solid and dependable food. Ordered the T-K-Y sandwich, which was plain, but good. The tomato soup has a nice little kick to it. My friend ordered the Oreo milkshake and wow, it tasted like a huge Oreo. There were also random mini Oreos served on the actual cup, too. There is a huge line around lunchtime, so I'd suggest coming before noon on any given weekday!

I got the achari paneer roll. Good spice level and the paneer tasted great. I do wish there was more to the roll? Maybe some cabbage, peppers? idk I am a bit new to the kati roll. 

The food prices are very reasonable but my can of coke was $2.25 which seems like a ridiculous ripoff and annoyed me just thinking about it.
Amish Doughnuts. Get the Amish Doughnuts. They're life-changing. They're the best I've ever had.
This place is unbelievable.  They have everything.  Whether you actually buy anything or not, it's worth spending some time here.
WOW! Very overwhelming!  So many sights, sounds, people!  What a crazy and exciting place.  It was nice that there were ambassadors available to help the lost and confused!

Nice neighborhood bar. Very spacious inside with lots of seating and some seats outside. Menu was a bit limited. The burger was tiny and mac & cheese croquettes were just ok. Service was ok, no complaints. I would come back to drink, but not eat.

I love the fact that this place has a lot of food choices and is generally inexpensive. There's always something to eat for whatever I'm feeling like. I especially appreciate the Amish foods on Thursdays. My only reservation is the crowd at lunchtime - be prepared to be bumped and possibly shoved and occasionally miss out on a table...it's all worth it though. Everyone who visits Philly has to stop by here... :)
Great experience, Great food. Four of us went for lunch we all ordered something different, from different shops and enjoyed all of it. I wish I had more time to spend there!

Home of the Best Sandwich in America. Somewhat touristy but it's a must-see for out of towners and definitely a place that locals should make a point to stop into every once in a while.

10% off any restaurant inside when you have Jury duty.

If you can't find it here, you ain't looking! From fresh foods to baked to ready to eat. And let's not forget the spirit tastings!!! Lemon cello is everything...even the beet vodka is interesting. I have been told the best Philly Cheesesteaks live here. If I lived here... Where I would shop

I wish I had more time to explore this place! There was SO much going on, but it seemed to have everything you could ever want. It's a foodie playground, and I can see why people love it so much. I had my eyes set on the produce area, which was slammed, so maybe I'll come back another time to get some goodies.  

It's only a four for me. I did love the concept and everything they had. It was exciting, but personally, it was almost impossible to move around (which is why I'm rarely in the city). 

I suggest coming here when you aren't pressed for time! There's to much to see to rush through it!

I am a no frills, beers and (veggie) burgers kind of gal.  I don't want to be impressed with fancy ingredients or downtown restaurant pomp, I just want to eat.

This place hits the mark.  Cozy, neat atmosphere.  I am sure it will be great in the fall!

We brunched here with a large group and found our service attentive, food yummy, and portions appropriate.

Prices are comparable to other similar joints in the neighborhoods.  If you are offended by the prices, I think you need to get out more.

Who doesn't love going to the Reading Terminal. The options are endless. You can get anything from soul food, to fresh meats and veggies, amazing sandwiches, food from different parts of the world like Thailand and Mexico. Sometimes it can be overwhelming because there is so much to choose from but whatever that may be you won't be disappointed. Some of my favorite places are Beilers, Little Thai Market, Metropolitan Bakery, The Dutch Market just to name a few. It's a tourist's dream.

This is one of the many places you HAVE to visit if you are touring Philadelphia. Old world charm in a high tempo retail/food service environment. Delicious prepared foods, fruits and veggies, baked goods, and Dutch-Amish staple products.

There is literally everything one could want here.

I really liked this place! Besides the lack of seating available - it gets pretty packed and it's hard to find a seat - there's really nothing to complain about!

There's a wide range of food and goods available to buy. I was able to buy a lot of things for my friends' birthdays who are coming up. They sell many different things - clothes, bags, candles/bees wax products, cooking utensils, books - and have food from different global cultures. I tried a vegan chocolate chip cookie from the Flying Monkey (I think?) and it was pretty good! This is a good place to come on a cold or rainy day.
Everything you could ever want! Local veggies, great variety of food, and a bar!

My favorite market I've been to thus far ever, even including markets in Europe! This is a must visit spot when you are in Philly and it's pretty much about killing all your food spots in one hit...if your stomach has space for it!

Come hungry and come alert. If you can, tag team with someone to try multiple vendors and also have someone to save seats if possible!
Maybe the best market in the universe. A must go to in Philly!
Best cannolis! Awesome flowers for good prices! Fresh meat! And if you have time, eat a grilled cheese!

Whatever you're in the mood for, from Chinese to a simple smoothie or nice breakfast, this place has it all! I'm a huge fan or Pearl's and Down Home Diner for a morning pick me up! The bacon stuffed french toast at Pearl's is to die for, be prepared to roll out of that place not walk.

I grew up coming here, so I never remember to review it. Seeing as I was just there on Saturday, I feel like I should throw in my 2 cents.

This is a MUST SEE in Philadelphia. You are experiencing a melting pot of culture, history, and of course, food, when you come to Reading Terminal. It is an experience that will transport you.

Like previous reviewers explained, it is CROWDED on the weekends. Check your anxiety at the door and just go with it. It is fun to get lost in all of the aisles and discover new things. 

My favorite places: DiNics, Terminis (incredibly authentic Italian desserts), Iovine brothers (for fresh, cheap produce), Beilers donuts, Beiler's bakery (very underrated pies!), Pearl's oyster bar (for clam chowder), Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties (I have fallen for their falafel), Martins for delicious sausages, Salumeria, and The Original Turkey, for when I need to recreate Thanksgiving in March.

There are so many amazing places here, you cant go wrong no matter what. Start a tradition with your family to come every now and then, they will never forget it.
Great place to go for lunch or breakfast and get a flair for Philly Foods. Best Grilled Cheese sandwiches. Also if a local and need to shop, some good choices for poultry, fish, meats, cheeses, etc.

I walked in and was wow'ed. Not my first time at a food court but somehow Reading Terminal is better and is a bit more than your typical food court. There are a lot of homemade goods and freshly made food. I loved all the Amish stalls. The prices for the most part are pretty decent. My favorite stall is the fresh donut stall from Beiller's. if you are visiting Philly, this is a must see place.
Like most Philadelphians, we love this spot for weekend lunch. I just wish more of the vendors stayed open on Sunday.

Reading Terminal Market is a collection of stalls, mostly restaurants, selling every food related thing you could possible imagine.

Whether you want awesome donuts, an authentic Philly Chessesteak, European pastries, Cajun gumbo, Italian subs, Chinese takeout, Indian Curries, Vietnamese soups, breakfast to go, a casual sit-down experience or anything else, you are going to find it here.

Raw fish and meat to take home?  Sure!
Cooked right here and served to  you on a bun? Absolutely!
Sauces, spices, jerkys?  Of course!

Really, if you are in the area for lunch YOU WANT TO GO HERE!  

Popular with tourists and locals, people who are not comfortable in crowds might want to stay away on the weekends but in the middle of the week you cannot go wrong.

If you hit the donuts shop, you want to try the fritters (apple and blueberry are both great),
The Cajun place has an alligator sausage sub that is divine (though their claim to fame is a sub called the "trainwreck!")
And if you go to the Ducth Eating Place, the dumplings are to die for.

You can get a cheese-steak at several places and I don't think you can go wrong.

You could eat here every day for a month and not hit the same place twice.

Why are you still reading this? Just go. Wander. And try whatever suits your fancy.

My family is from the Philippines, so I'm admittedly a little biased toward Filipino cuisine. Especially being from NJ, where Filipino food is quite ubiquitous, I'm very happy to see it making strides in the Philly area scene.

Putting that aside, though, I wouldn't rate this place highly if the food wasn't up to snuff! They did a nice job with putting a new spin on a traditional Filipino dish, so I'm a fan and would like to try more food here in the future.

We decided to have lunch at the Bourse, and I'd been wanting to try Lalo. My wife is GF, so I wanted to get something that she could try some of. They don't have a huge menu, and only one of them is truly GF (one doesn't have gluten in it but uses a shared fryer) - the longsilog. I appreciated that they were knowledgeable about the sensitivity and cooked the sausage in a separate pan as to avoid contamination on the grill.

The longsilog was very tasty, albeit on the small end (not bad for the price, though). The longanisa sausage wasn't the typical one I'm used to that's bright red and super sweet and fatty, but it was tasty - a little more meaty and smoky, yet still with that sweet taste. The garlic fried rice was yummy, and the soft egg was awesome (I think I saw a sous-vide back there). What made it all even better, though, was the sour vegetable slaw. Even though it's a side, it provides perfect contrast with the rest of the dish. I really enjoyed the dish!

I'd love to try more of their food on future visits. It's great that the leche flan is GF, and I hope they add more options!

I am half Filipino and grew up in California with the surplus of Filipino food. I am GF and was really happy to find this cute little food court area and LALO had something for me! The food is not your authentic Filipino cuisine so please keep that in mind. However, it is a great place to eat something wholesome and I mean who doesn't love okra? I was being a tourist and came about this after a long day of walking around for lunch. I got the Bicol Express and it was filling and the veggies were not overcooked which I loved.

Love this wonderful conglomerate of eateries and shops! Quite literally, there's something for everyone here-lunch, dinner, dessert, coffee, shopping and socializing-you simply cannot ask for more in a market such as this. In all my travels, by far, the best indoor market  anywhere.

Decent spot for a quick and healthy lunch. You only order through their computers so good luck if you need to actually talk to someone about your order. Clean and welcoming place on Temple's crowded campus.

By far, this was the most overwhelming indoor market I've been to - the choices were literally endless. So if you're REALLY ambitious, have time to walk around, and are with a group, you could each get food from a different vendor and share, Smorgasburg style. But warning: lines are LONG. 

After walking around the entire market (and getting lost) for 30-45 minutes, I finally settled on Dinic's Roast Pork and Beef - I got the Roast Pork ($8.75). Tbh I wasn't a huge fan.. the meat was tender and moist, but it didn't have much flavor, so I thought it was pretty mediocre for something so highly raved. 

The market, while stimulating way too many senses at once, is still pretty incredible and a must-visit!

The bad reviews are a little concerning to me because I've been here twice and have enjoyed it both times.  I live around the corner and am ecstatic that there is some place I can grab a beer and some decent food.  Don't get me wrong, the Brew House is great but The Industry is within stumbling distance, especially on a weeknight after a long day of work.  The beer selection is well rounded and the space is really nice.  I have not had any problems with excess noise, but  I realize I'm in a bar!  There is still much on the menu to try but I have had a few appetizers, salads, and sides and have not been disappointed.  Hopefully, the reviews start to change a bit and The Industry can flourish here.

If you go early on a Saturday, it's nice, as soon as it gets crowded it's ridiculous trying to move around. Some of the stands serve slop that is no better than a cafeteria, but they have added some nice food-retail options the last few years. I can't quite understand the huge line for the Amish Eating Place or whatever it's called, the food is sub-par - must be the tourists. Of course, it's ALL tourists. Personally, I have my own places I like to go, so just taking a spin around the aisles is enough. I'm not hugely enthusiastic about it, but I do enjoy going there sometimes.

If you're hungry in Center City and no one can agree on what to eat, the RTM is perfect, they've got cuisines A-Z for everyone.

This is definitely South Philly's newest best kept secret!  They have a touch of everything when it comes to entrees. Even greens for you vegans and veggie lovers.

The seating arrangement is ideal. High tops, low tops, bar and even outdoor seating. Our waiter Luis, was very funny and great with suggestions. All of the waitstaff follows behind each other so you are not left unattended. They even fold your napkin while you're away from your table. Just classy and impeccable.
My friend and I had pork nuggets for our appetizer which were prepared like a mini croquette with a sweet mustard dipping sauce. For my entree I chose the Seafood BLT with buttermilk shrimp and extra bacon. Spicy enough and oh so good! It was a very filling sandwich. Dessert consisted of homemade donuts with a sweet berry raisin like topping. This meal was out of this world and I can't wait to go back for another meal!  I had a very enjoyable dinner.
Favorite place for filipino food when I can't eat home cooking. Long time fan of their inihaw. Just tried their aroz caldo and leche flan, can't wait to order again!
Good pizza! Fresh and the ingredients are tasty! Try the special! Love there pizza! Order online and picked up was easy!
The best place to eat in Philly!!! Reading Terminal Market has something for everyone.

As a Filipino who grew up in dense Filipino community in LA, my ancestors would have been mad if I rated this place with more than a 3/5.

3/5 Food = The food is OK. I am probably the biggest critique on Filipino food since I grew up eating it all my life here in America and when I visit the Philippines. Their Lechon Kawali is probably the most disappointing one I have ever tried since their sauce wasn't even close to lechon sauce and the portion was so small for $12. However, their Lumpia Shanghai was good! I would recommend trying them. I didn't really enjoy drinking their Blueberry Kalamansi Iced Tea since I expected the Kalamansi taste to be more predominant. The Leche Flan was OK, not the best, but still worth a try.
