5/5 Service = People working at the cash register are very nice! Didn't have a problem with them whatsoever, and they even gave me kiwi and mango flavoured gummies! 

Overall, I would define this place as a hipster Filipino joint. I know they are trying to target millennials to eat here, but no way would my parents would agree to eat here. If you want to try OG Filipino Food, I would recommend making trek across the bridge to South Jersey where there are a few Filipino restaurant gems there!

Reading Terminal Market is the place to go in Philadelphia for one stop eats. You will find everything from cheesesteaks to different desserts. It's so many food places inside of the market for customers. It's probably best to make more than one trip to check out everything at Reading Terminal Market. The atmosphere was very lively. Some lines were wrapped around the corner. Hours at Reading Terminal Market is odd, so be sure to check the website. I definitely will stop by Reading Terminal Market every time I'm visiting Philadelphia.

No matter where you're from, what you eat, how old you are, etc. You are bound to find something you would like here. This is one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. 
You can find fresh oysters, delicious crepes, cajun food, nuts, kitchen gadgets, etc. You name it! I like trying different things at once so this is the perfect place for me. 
I can get an appetizer at one place, then go to multiple other places to share a dish, and then have ice cream, cookies, or any dessert I'd like. They also have a fresh produce section, deli meats, seafood, and other stores that sells raw material for cooking. 
I have been to markets all over the world, and I would say this is one of the best ones in America and will tie with markets in Barcelona and Venice. It has Philadelphia culture and paints a perfect picture of America's melting pot.  
I would recommend you to not go at the busy hours because it will be hustle, bustling. Some stores close at a certain day and time of the week. So be aware.

This is my go-to place for a quick, cheap, late night bite. However, they definitely need to work on their delivery times. 

My favorite is the chicken tikka roll with egg. The chicken is juicy and tender cooked unlike other kathi roll places in the area. The chicken biryani is also great.

The best place ro go for lunch when you're not sure what  you want to eat. Something will surely capture attention and stimulate your appetite.  While you are there you can grab some ingredients for dinner. The food there is all good because they are all competing for your return visit. This place is great for tourists and locals alike. !
This market is amazing. I have a good morning breakfast here with my bf. There are plenty of vendors with variety of food.

Ooh Chick-Fil-a.  Your delicious, juicy, tender chicken fried to crispy fast-food perfection.  I know you are bigoted about gays.  But I can't stop myself from the cravings that make me go against my principles and rush into your doors and stuff my mouth in self-loathing.

This particular location has excellent service.  They are super quick and they are super friendly.  

The milkshakes are excellent.  The chicken is great.  I love waffle fries.  Thank you Chick-fil-a for making me feel like I would snort your chicken if necessary.

Great place to stop for quick shop and very close to the Jefferson station for those who use public transportation! The fresh produce are pretty nice and prices are very good! There is a good variety of products for everyone! It could be a little too busy in rush hours in the afternoon so try to avoid being there by then! A tip for students! they have about 20% discount for students on Wednesdays! Have your school ID with you
They literally have everything! Little tip: all the Amish run shops are closed on Sunday. Best donuts I've had in a while. Get the peanut butter creme! Banana honey walnut crepe was amazing too!
Too crowded. The food at Tootsis was alright I guess. There was nowhere to sit! And a bunch of kids playing hooky were bothering me and my friend while we were having lunch
My favorite place to lunch in the city. Its just so hard to decide what to eat! I always take people from out of town, its always a big hit. I always get a warm soft pretzel brushed with butter!

I feel fortunate to live a few blocks away! Unbelievable variety; you can literally eat anything you want in this very building. Would even be good for a group of indecisve diners for lunch. 
Oh, but the shopping! Meat, poultry, seafood, cheese, olive oil, bakery, and the best goddamn produce market in the city.  A necessity for anyone that loves to browse and food shop as much as I do.

Foodie heaven!!! If you live nearby or just visiting the Philly area... definitely a great place to check out! Give yourself a few hours so you can walk around and check out all the vendors. Definitely come hungry, as you will have soooo many options for food. They have lots of produce, meats and dairy to do your grocery shopping too. I always try to shop local to support the small local businesses!

Be prepared to be elbow to elbow with people if you go during the weekend hours. But other than that, be patient because it's worth it! 

With the food placard, they have a select number of seats either at the counter or a few tables and chairs. But if you walk in more towards the back middle of the market, there is open seating like a cafeteria style place to sit! 

Have fun and try lots of foods!

Really cool place that exhibits both a touristy and local feel. If you're looking for any kind of unusual or exotic meats or produce that your local grocery store doesn't carry, you're sure to find it here. Went during Presidents' weekend, and this place was packed. It was very difficult to find seating. And for the most part, you are walking shoulder-to-shoulder with other people. A great location to find artisan-made, locally grown, family recipe goods. The terminal also has a rich history that you can learn more about by reading the walls. Personally, we came for ice cream, and it did not disappoint. You could easily spend hours walking around and looking at all the shops. From exquisite chocolate and desserts to chicken hearts, you'll find whatever you're looking for here. As long as you don't mind being part of a massive crowd, you'll enjoy your visit because there is something for everyone.

I hadn't had chick fil a in a few years.  I'm happy I ordered. The chicken sandwich was so good.  I'm picky about eating certain Pickles and forgot to order it without.  After I opened the Polynesian sauce I didn't care what was on sandwich.  I've never had the sauce before but it was really good. I might start taking shots of Polynesian sauce to start my day off right.  I missed the waffle fries which were tasty as well.

So much to see here you can't even see it all in one day. If you eat it they have it here. All kinds of specialty foods of every variety. This is a true market where you can buy all your ingredients as well as prepared ready to eat food and full on restaurants.

Probably my favorite place in all of Philly despite the fact it's almost always crowded to some extent. I work right down the street and Beck's and Keven Parker are two spots I frequently visit while there. A definite must for anyone in Philadelphia.

Must go if you are in the area!

Many different types of food places to choose from if you are with a large group and can't decide what to eat. They have many local spots to choose from. I couldn't make a decision. 

They also have tiny shops if you wanted to buy some local things like honey or souvenirs.

Reading Terminal is everything!!!! I loved the Crepes,  Kamal's Juice bar,  the gin tasting., The olive oil and balsamic vinegar shop and miller's Pretzels all stood out.  This is a must do when visiting Philly, it's a no frills culinary experience.  I was in town 2 days and went 3 times,  truly a foodies dream!!!
Love this market.  Lots of delicious food options for breakfast and lunch.  And great place to get all the cooking ingredients you need.  Wonderful place.  Wish NYC had a market like this.

Giving a review of Reading Terminal Market is absurd. People aren't going there because of yelp reviews, they are there because they are at the convention center, they are local, or they want a highly specific ingredient. 

Regardless of which one applies to you, you will get what you're looking for. Great place with many options (truly close to everything) for lunch; cheap place to pick up groceries with a short shelf life; place that has every ingredient I've ever looked for (and I like to cook). 

This feels like reviewing the liberty bell. Does my onion matter? Does it sway you? You're either coming here anyway, a regular already, or this opinion is meaningless.
Finally got some time to check this place out. It was so delicious! I will definitely be coming back!

It's hard to give Reading Terminal Market a solid review because of all of the variety. Variety is the best word to describe everything about the market. There is all kinds of things, all kinds of quality, all kinds of people. You can get Chinese food, cookies, cheese, BBQ, salad, bagels, produce, and basically anything else you want there.

Sometimes on the weekends the crowd is a lot to handle. It is sometimes shoulder to shoulder, violating fire codes kind of crowded. Other times it isn't quite as bad. There is one cookie place - I forget what it is called - it always has a line that goes all the way through the market on the weekends. If your intention is to go to a famous cookie place, that's probably it. You should get there early.  

The crowd is as diverse as the food. The destination is one of the biggest tourist attractions in Philadelphia. You see people from all over the world coming to try the food. I think the diversity is one element of it that makes it really special. 

The best part of the market is the quality of food. Some of it is just really really good. I definitely recommend coming hungry and trying a few different places. My favorite is downtown cheese. They have great cheeses and let you try before you buy.
Great times here and a very broad assortment of cuisines. Definitely a must see if you've never been. Beware it's always packed so don't take it personally if you get bumped into.

Being a foodie this place is like walking in food heaven! Lots of different cuisines under one roof. What more could I ask for?! I have tried the crepe place (there is only one so you'll know)--it was good but I've had better, Dinics roast pork sandwich would have to be my top go to place here though (about $10). Just try it and thank me later. If you are craving for something sweet, there is this amish place that sells donuts (the only one there too!). It was so yummy, not too sweet but melts in your mouth! You can't go wrong with reading terminal market.

Love Reading Market. Lots of different foods to choose from but DiNics is one of the best sandwiches in the city. Make a stop for dessert as well with lots of different choices. Great to visit on a Saturday if you can avoid the lines and busyness.

Wow- must see if visiting Philly. Large farmers market, lots of variety with food vendors. Something for everyone from breakfast, snack, lunch or dinner. If you leave hungry, that is your own doing. Eclectic shops as well.

This place is a foodie  mega pick it has from Peking duck 2 beef and cheese just some of the best cheesesteaks you can ask for has a farmers market inside and a meat market tomahawk steaks are humongoustook half a day just to see all the stuff I gained 15 pounds every time I visit

Unbelievable good food. Virtually anything you could want to eat.  Hershel's has THE BEST PASTRAMI IN PHILLY.  Probably a line up but that's why. It's sooo good.  Really great alternatives to chose from even if your not a pastrami lover like me!
OMG! Choices galore. If you don't find something you like, shame on you. I enjoyed the Indian restaurant Nanees Kitchen - Salmon and Curried cabbage.
the best market around:  has everything you could want to eat from veggies to dinner

It reminds me of the Ferry Building in SF, where there's many food stalls for eating and strolling through a marketplace. 

Nice center addition to the city. 

Pleasant stroll and drop by for an out of towner and a local! 

Enjoy!

This place is so much fun!

So many food vendors and markets that you could literally spend all day and not try everything there is to offer! It can definitely get crowded, especially on the weekends so highly recommend going early.

Love Miller's Pretzels, Dinic's Roast Pork, and Beiler's Doughnuts, just to name a few.

Parking is available across the street at the parking garage. Take your ticket - not credit card - to get it validated for a discount parking price when you purchase something within the market. Ask the vendor to validate your ticket.

Enjoy!

Love this Chick-Fil-A!

I swear it's just like being at a regular restaurant, like with waiter service.  The food is always fresh, the prices are right and they let you eat in peace.  We are never rushed, our drinks are refilled whether we ask the cashier or if an employee comes around.  The manager even comes around to check to see if your food/visit was okay.

My go to meal are the chicken nuggets with Chick-fil-a sauce! Yummy! I also love the side salad.  The Chicken Sandwich Deluxe is a second favorite.  The chicken salad sandwich isn't that good to me, but it's not bad and sure not the worse I've ever had.

You must get some of those Chocolate Chunk cookies.  I usually get a half dozen to take home, pop those babies in the microwave and yes it's like they melt in my mouth.

Reading terminal is a must for both tourists and locals alike. It's one of my favorite places in the city. So many awesome food vendors, led by the Amish merchants you won't find anywhere else. Let me list the vendors that make Reading Terminal so awesome:
1. Beiler's Bakery - Best Bakery in the city
2. Beiler's Donuts - Best donuts in the city
3. Smuckers - Best Roast beef sandwich in the city
4. Dutch Eating Place - Best diner in the city, featuring the apple dumpling
5. Dienner's BBQ chicken - Best Rotisserie & BBQ chicken in the city
6. Bassets Ice Cream - Best ice cream in the city
7. Beck's Cajun - One of the best places for New Orleans food in the city
8. The Rib Stand - One of the best places for ribs in the city
9. Kevin Parker's Soul Food Café - One of the best places for soul food in the city
10. Carmen's - One of the best places for cheesesteaks &  hoagies in the city
11. Pearl's Oyster Bar - One of the best old school seafood spots in the city

I also get my meats, fish and cheeses from Reading Terminal. High quality at some of the lowest prices in the city. My favorites are:
1. Riehl Deli & Cheese shop
2. L. Halteman Family Country Foods
3. Martin's Quality Meats & Sausages
4. Iovine Brothers Produce

I can go on and on. There are candy shops, pretzels, wine, and more... It does get extremely crowded at times, but wading through the crowd is always worth it. No matter what you have a taste for you can find it at Reading Terminal.

Lots of variety but way too crowded and a bit overpriced for what the vendors are selling. The best time to come here is during the weekdays around mid-morning. I'm not really into touristy things so if you enjoy going off the beaten path it is best to skip this place. I only come here when my work takes me downtown.....Lunchtime is insane and the weekends are even worse.
I love this place! It's an indoor farmers market with access to many vendors. Come hungry if you're looking for a quick bite, or sit down to eat at the diner. They also have lots of shopping.

A must do if you're in the Philadelphia area. Every food you can imagine in one place and it's made fresh. We tried a cheesesteak and ice cream. Park at the Hilton and bring your ticket to be validated for cheap parking. My only wish is that they had more shops instead of just food.

Love this place, especially the Amish restaurant.
It can get overcrowded on weekends.

If I could give 0 stars, I would! RUDE. I stopped at 4:30 prior to my 6 am flight. Lights all on, food out and ready, and a young lady standing at the register texting away. I walked up and said good morning. Her response: no. No? I giggled and said I'd like a smoothie. Her response: I said no, we are closed until 5.... I said oh, I didn't realize with you standing here at the register. Her response, I'm just texting, not working. CLEARLY. No hospitality at this place! It could have gone a much different, more polite way. Dunkin' next door was clearly a better option. Seems this is a common experience here based on the reviews so hoping they get closed next for a better, friendlier option. Never again.
Lots of food - everything you could want. Check to make sure there is nothing happening at the Convention Center though. It can get SO crowded.  I would bring anyone visiting Philly here.

I am not a tourist.... I grew up in Philly so Reading Terminal is apart of everything I love about this City.  It is one of the few places that has kept a good chunk of its traditions and maintained an artisan feel.

It is loud and ALWAYS busy!  There are so many delicious food smells that even if you just ate, it makes you hungry.  You can walk every aisle, then immediately walk it again and realize you missed something.  You cannot walk through without accidentally browsing. So this is definitely a multi-visit sort of place.  

And you do not and should not worry about parking.  No matter where you are staying in the city, there is a public transportation route that will get you to the Terminal for a minimal cost.  Trust that SEPTA (in this instance) is your friend... don't drive your gas guzzling SUV to buy Artisan breads made by the Amish.... that's just wrong on multiple levels.

Enjoy, enjoy , enjoy!

Great collection of restaurants and produce stands. My favorites are Iovine Brothers produce and Hershel's East Side Deli. Can't beat Iovine's prices and variety. You can't go wrong with a corn beef sandwich.

I walked to this establishment on a rainy Sunday evening and ordered the Paneer Masala roll. It was very tasty and will definitely go back to try some other items. The Paneer salad and rice looked good so maybe I will try that next time.

Lunch time and found a Filipino food place at The Boarse food court. My son ordered the Pork Laing- pork with kale stewed in coconut milk. I ordered the grilled pork- marinated sweet pork over rice and pickled veggies.  The food were ok. What would you expect from a food court right?  They were not the Filipino dishes that I expected. The portion were kinda small compared to other Filipino restaurant. However, the San Miguel beer was good though!!!! Lol!!!

Dependable, hot, delicious sandwiches.  I wouldn't say there's anything special about this location, but they do serve up a quick, loaded sandwich.  While the lines can back up to the door during lunch hours, they are efficient and will take your order in line to expedite the service.  Standard toppings - mayo, mustard, hot peppers, lettuce, onion, tomato, pickle, oil and Italian seasoning  (they are always happy to give you extra if you ask) and usual drinks and chip selection.  Milkshakes come short and stout - thick, full flavor with fresh ice cream - but oh so bad for you...The cookies are also a great sweet treat to add on to your meal and they are always baked fresh.  

Maybe just don't get both :)

Enjoy!

I love this place.  If you can't find it at the Terminal Market you can't find it!
Food is delicious and varied. Candy shop is the best, kitchen store has a bunch of "what did I ever do w/out this".  Great for out of guest of the city and locals.

Amazing historic philly staple
A must see if in Philadelphia amazing veggies fish beef poultry artisan cheeses any food to satisfy u
My daughter and I had the Masala rolls and the chicken biryani w/ white sauce. And I was pleasantly surprised at how good everything was. I'll definitely be eating here quite often.
Pretty much everything you could want in one place. Tons of energy, awesome food, gift shops, restaurants, produce; it has it all. Must stop when in Philly.

I adore RTM. I shop here every single weekend for the local produce and for meat from the butchers. Really, anything you can think of, they have it. Local honey, cook books, cookies, sweets, herbs, etc. 

It does get REALLY crowded later in the day so I recommend going first thing in the morning. Not all of the shops are open on Sundays, so if you want to see everything, make it a Saturday!

I love the reading terminal market, especially during the week when it isn't as busy!  Its a great place to buy little things, oils and balsamic, groceries, and a great place for breakfast and lunch!  All around a great market in Philadelphia and one of the best overall.
What's to say that hasn't already been said. This is truly an American treasure.

First time going and it was a pleasant surprise. The sheer amount of choices should be enough to keep anyone happy. My group had Chicken Curry, Pickles, Pretzels, and Gyro as well as farm fresh honey in the comb and everything was delicious. Excellent taxi coverage in the area too.

Love Reading Terminal Market!
So much to choose from.
A great spot for folks visiting Philadelphia or Philadelphia residents.

TEN stars if I could!!! GREAT food of ALL kinds! Gets crowded-- are you surprised? Little shops abound within this crowded huge place -- walking into them is like being in another world. Not enough lifetimes to sample all the goodies, but you can try!! Prices are reasonable -- food is GREAT-- ambience is more than enough to revive a tired person. And their "themed" days are also alot of fun.

Everyone told me this was a must-see place during my visit to Philadelphia. I went there twice during the lunch hour, once on a weekday and once on Sunday. I found it to be extremely chaotic, noisy, barbaric, and disgusting. If you like being crammed alongside wall to wall aggressive people who like to queue up to the trough to wolf down food, this is the place for you. Not my idea of dining. On my first visit, I was so overwhelmed that I left within five minutes. On Sunday I sat at a counter. It was 10 minutes before anyone offered to take my order. When I said I'd like it to go, I was told I had to go to the other side and stand in line. I ended up going to a different vendor to get a sandwich. It was acceptable, nothing outstanding.
Food is great. Was craving Filipino food really badly and loved how convenient it was to just come here and get vegan Kare-Kare.

Lunch time! I was starvingggg and decided to come in here with friends for a nice lunch. The interior surprised me a lot, there's not much space as I thought it would have and it is so cramped! I ordered sautéed calamari with soup for $9.18 including tax. I would say that it was very much worth the money for this fairly portioned meal. The sauce that accompanied my sautéed calamari was probably not the greatest choice but I dumped it into my shredded veggies just to get rid of it. The squid was chewy but still tender and the taste is great! Not too salty and a hint of sweetness. The soup had gotten my hopes up as I thought it would be filled to the brim but alas, it was halfway full. Nonetheless, great food and prices.

Probably the worst customer services ive ever seen.   The employees treated every customer like the were annoying.  A togo order took over 20 min to get and they didnt even call out the order.  They even told one customer oh well i called out your number and someone else took it.  The employee then rolled her eyes and walked away.  There were roaches running around on the front counter.  Only one employee was really working, the cook.   The rest were to busy giving attitude.  The worst ive seen in a long time.

Really really good lunch and shopping place if you are wanting to grab some things to make dinner.  Very good selections of produce, butchers and seafood.  I would suggest going with a crew so you can try a few different things. I try not to eat sweets much anymore but damn this place. Termini's best cannoli, sfogliatelle and the banana thing...Criminal!!!  So try not to eat sweets was appropriate to say this day .... The f'ing donuts are another problem.  The prices here are also very reasonable 

As far as food is concerned the Thai place was very crowded but gets good reviews and the gyro and Dinics were both very very good.  

The only problem is Philly is a little seedy, other than that hurry here if you haven't been.

A must see if you're visiting Philly, and a vibrant place for anyone else. My favorites are the Market Bakery, whose cookies, breads and sandwiches beat Metropolitan Bakery by a mile; Beck's Cajun Cafe, whose po-boy sandwiches you'll be craving until the next time you visit. The Amish stands are best for ripe tomatoes. The market has live music during the lunch hours and vendors are pretty friendly, if a little expensive at times. Go in with a plan; otherwise it can be a little overwhelming.

An incredible selection of food available! The workers kept everything very clean so me and my friends had many clean options to eat on. Would recommend this place to anyone who loves to have a wide variety of food options!

Not a bad spot.  Nice atmosphere, decent selection of beers, and a nice staff.   The food seemed a bit pricey (so I abstained) but the beers were about average.  I'd definitely go again.  I'd describe it as a nicer, trendier neighborhood bar.
It's on the list of things to do in Philadelphia for a reason. Worth going if you're a local or a tourist. From deserts, seafood to deli foods.  It has it all.

It was very crowded when I was there because it was pouring out so everyone was looking for shelter. I enjoyed it a lot, and there were so many foods to choose from so I got overwhelmed. Will definitely come back here next time.
This is the new improved Reading Terminal, part of Philadelphia's renaissance. Very impressive
A little bit of everything to cook but.....not much of anything "healthy" to eat, fast !
Great place to visit for both residents and tourists.  This is an important part of Philadelphia's culture; delicious food, great variety, vibrant atmosphere, and a great pace to pass time.
Love the variety of food sources under one roof. You just can't go wrong. And be ready no matter what you're craving you are guaranteed to find it there!

The Reading Terminal Market is a favorite among locals and tourists with over 80 food vendors offering delicious eats that is perfect for lunch or dinner and even dessert. A foodie's paradise. 

The Reading Terminal Market is similar to the Grand Central Market in Los Angeles and The Pike Market Place in Seattle. But a little different in which all food vendors are inside, in an air conditioned place (which is a nice way to stay cool during the summer months). 

Although there are tables and chairs, I feel that there just isn't enough, especially if you come during peak time. My husband and I came on a Thursday, right before noon and as the time progressed, it was getting busier and busier. 

One major negative that I would have to say about this food market is that they close early, at 6 pm every day. If only they stayed open later so that you could grab a later dinner. But now that you know this, just make sure to plan your visit accordingly so that you don't miss out if you are visiting Philly for the first time. 

Please note that a lot of the vendors here do take credit card and there are clean restrooms available.
Great atmosphere but a bit crowded at times. Great selection of fresh seafood, meats, poultry, vegetables, breads and divine chicken wings to die for.
amazing food, and a huge craft beer selection. service is always great, and everyone is extremely personable. an added perk: 20% off your bill if you work in the industry.
This market is always an overload of sites, sounds, smells, and delicious food.  Love the discount parking at the indoor lot next door.  However, could use a better local artisan bread bakery;)

A must see & experience in Philly. Numerous food vendors and unique stands including candy shops, Amish bakeries, organic fresh foods, cheese & meat counters, & more under one busy roof! If you can't find something you love here, you have issues ;)

I've decided to stop by here since it was the only place I saw by City Hall and glimpsed "McDonald's" in the distance. The restaurant looks extremely outdated, like it's stuck in the 1960's. It needs a major renovation and revamp. It didn't look very clean either, as some tables still had food left, napkins, etc. There were a lot of homeless and sketchy people here, hogging up the soda fountain. The best part was the cashier, she was extremely sweet and had a smile on. The burgers were made right, everything was good. Wifi worked fine as well.

Ordered on mobile. An employee called to say that they're not taking pickup orders and that I would not be getting a pizza and I won't get my money back for 2-3 business days because I paid with credit card. I was already in my car and about 7 minutes away from the store. Wrote to Pizza Hut via their website. Not really expecting a response. Support a local pizza shop that cares about their customers instead.

So many wonderful choices! Ended up eating at a place recommendation by a friend.  Dinics sandwiches! It was fabulous. We each ordered a different sandwich to we could trade halves. I got the Italian sausage and my friend got the recommended pork. They were both awesome. Flavorful and juicy and the bread was amazing. After we searched for desert and we couldn't decide. So many choices. Cookies, pastries, ice cream....  I also purchased some handmade leather crafts from a local Amish family.

One Friday, and without prior plans, Nando F took me to the Industry, to chill out & cheer up, since my flight got delayed by 6-hours. The yummy food, welcoming atmosphere and friendly service (kinda!) worked magic, that of-course before my flight got canceled, and I got all sad again. (Even a magic wand wouldn't have helped me then.)
 
The food:
Nando and I shared few small plates and split a burger. 
- Sweet pea & truffle dumpling: Stunningly delicious, just get them.
- Kimchee tater tots. Wonderful Korean style tater tots.
- Reuben pierogies with sauerkraut and thousand island. Enough Said!
- The Industry Burger with a fried egg: Less than average. Even with the added egg. 

The atmosphere:
Laid-back and welcoming ambiance. Love, love, L.O.V.E the rustic décor with the black and white photos of local chefs, brewers and other industry Pros on a formidable maroon wall.
Pro Tip: Don't forget to check out the vintage cigarette machine in the basement. And it's NOT a toy vending machine. If you actually insert your money (exact $12; cash only), you'll be served cigarettes as if you were in a '50s or '60s bar.

The service:
Thanks to Nando, our waitress became friendlyER. 
She just wasn't very attentive. Also, she wasn't listening carefully to our order. While we were still indecisive, we were naming out loud our choices to discuss. Generously, she brought out everything we were debating on getting, and it wasn't on the house if you were wondering. 
Otherwise, The food came out quick and warm. 

Three and Three Quarters Yelps.

Love this place. Best times to go are off times. Had one of the best breakfasts at the Dutch Eating Place last week around 10:30 (on break from jury duty a block away). Today, had a cheesesteak at Carmen's -- still a wait for the food, but there was seating and time for banter with the staff.

This pizza is literally one of the best I have eaten. The slices are big but super delicate in the crust. Omg... They mastered the dough to sauce to cheese combination perfectly. Each bite that I took had perfect consistency and flavor. 

I got cheese and pepperoni; both just fantastic options. The pepperoni on the pizza are tiny. When you bite into it, there is a slight addition of salt from the pepperoni but it doesn't ruin the balance. 

The shop is small and there are two big tables you can stand and eat at. Staff of super chill and they just seem like your friendly Philly neighborhood people who just want you to have good pizza. 

If I had to choice of just eating this pizza over all pizzas for the rest of my life, I would.... It's that good people!
Always a fun spot to get ANY food craving. Dessert selections are great, and lots of unique gift ideas at the Herbiary or Amish/farm shops.

I do love this place.  I'm sure most will find it to be an expensive tourist trap but that's why I go.   The selection of food offered is insane.  No matter what you're in the mood for, you'll probably find it.  Everything from Mediterranean to Cajun to Italian to your classic Philly Cheesesteak.  
Lots of Amish food items, jams, jellies, honey etc.  not sure how authentic it is though.  I'm no expert on the Amish but the guy who sold me honey was in traditional Amish garb but was listening to music via iPhone with Bluetooth headphones.  You be the judge on that.  
Crowds can be overwhelming sometimes so be prepared for that.
Alot of different food choices. From Hamburgers to chines to even a bar inside to get your favorite beer.

They have pretty much any food here that you could imagine, and with a fun and energetic atmosphere. Great place to get groceries for home, a dine in meal, or delicious dessert! Plus some cool other shops selling some non-food items. Would highly recommend for both tourists and locals.

Love it, you can find anything you want in here , my favorite corners are the chocolate stores , yummy 
Good for raining days , some places are over charging so keep your eyes open ;-)

Am I there only person from Philly who just started coming here about 2 years ago?
Everything looks and smells amazing. The lines are very long around lunch time (which is to be expected).
I really want to give RTM a solid try! When I worked in the area I went to Kevin Parkers for lunch a few times and it was good. Ive had Bassetts Ice cream and that was YUM! I've yet to give the Amish Bakery donuts a try. I have to come back with plenty of time and a pair of Yoga pants.

We had a wonderful time coming here and enjoying shopping and lunch. Specifically, we fell in love with Fox and sons fancy corn dogs. We eat gluten free and we were able to eat a corndog as well as a funnel cake! Oh, and fried cookies! That never happens for us! It was incredible and you could not tell that it was gluten-free at all! I can't say enough good things about this vendor! 
It is a little crowded in the market and there is a lot of vendors packed in there, I would recommend going down each row one at a time otherwise, you may miss a lot and you get turned around.

Excellent selection and quality! You can find a ton of different cuisines alongside classic American fare. A lot of high quality meats, cheeses, and other ingredients. Pretty reasonable prices too! Was really impressed, wish we had something like this near where I live.
I really like this place when I go into philly... there are so many different vendors to choose from and all the food is great! I do wish there were more places to sit down! it gets very crowded!

I really enjoyed this new Filipino joint at the bourse. We got the lumpia Shanghai which is lemongrass egg rolls that were bite sized and enhanced by the chili dipping sauce. I also enjoyed the chicken baskabob sandwhich which was sweet and a touch spicy. The staff recommended I mix the two juices - the mango and calamansi juices - great idea. Highly recommend if you want to give Filipino food a try!

I visited Industry after the were featured as one of the best places to get fried chicken in Philly.  The atmosphere was nice, our server was a bit rude.  I didn't think we were going to stay for dinner since service is very important to me.  I asked if we could sample a 'punch' type drink they were featuring and we were told 'no' its made to order and they cant make a sample.  Well, he didn't realize that he was talking to 2 ex bartenders and we know that a good bartender will gladly make a sample for a customer.  None the less we were hungry and had traveled there for a specific purpose.  We started with the house sausage and the 'ear' lettuce wraps both were quite tasty, the deep fried pig ear reminded us of bacon!  We then had the fried chicken and pulled bbq duck sandwich, both were delicious.
The food made up for the not so great service.
These dumpling are always so flavorful. The honey chipotle chicken were amazing. The cashiers was very friendly and our food came out quickly. Great to dine in or take out.

NOT SAFE FOR PERSONS ON THE SPECTRUM 
Sensory OVERLOAD no place to be quiet 
THIS PLACE WILL CAUSE MELTDOWNS!!!!!

As a professional chef I seek places to acquire the necessary ingredients.
This place would be great IF THE TOURISTS were not there. OVER CROWDED 
Reading terminal was the central hub for decades NOW Meh.
I only go If I can not find my ingredients elsewhere
Did I mention all the TOURISTS!!!!!
my god! they are there wandering like lost sheep stopping midway gawking and pointing.
Heres a thought GET THE HELL OUTTA OUR WAY WERE SHOPPING HERE!!!
It needs more space for people to actually walk
claustrophobia warning!!!!
Not a place for young children or NEURO Sensitive persons IT IS A SENSORY NIGHTMARE

Reading Terminal Market is one of those places I've never bothered to review because I assume everyone already knows it's awesome.

My favorite time to go is during the week when it's not as crowded.  But us suburbanites normally have to pack in here on the weekends.  It's crowded, loud and confusing.  However, the food is delicious.  So many choices.  When the weather is nice, find a bench or curb outside to escape the crowds while you eat.  Just be prepared to fend off the homeless people asking for change.  That guy isn't stranded and trying to get together money for a train ticket- I assure you.

This is a foodie's paradise.  I highly recommend this for a full meal or even just a snack.  So many different varieties of food and sweets to choose from.  My advice, go hungry!

There are two reasons to visit. One is the history of the building. Two is the FOOD. You can enjoy both at the same time! The only downside is that you're not going to be able to try everything you want to try in one visit. Here's my suggestion, if you have an Amish Market near your home, pass over the Amish food for other traditional Philly favorites. I found I liked the goods my Amish Market sells better than what I found here. BUT Dinic's roasted pork sandwich was something I'll never forget! (I'd also pass on Basset's for Franklin's Fountain or Scoop Devilles.) My next visit, I want to try the grilled cheese place and maybe get some oysters!

I visited the reading terminal market first on my trip to philly. THIS IS A MUST GO TO SPOT! Such a huge variety of different smells, foods and experiences! Definitely recommend grabbing yourself a map (look closely on the walls around the terminal). Downside is its PACKED! so many people! But there is open seating and bathrooms! (also little gift shops and lots of pamphlets around for the touristy types). Did notice some people playing live music outside!

Pure Bliss for the little fat person inside of you ... my little fat girl inside were dancing like a ballerina on crack from pure ecstasy. I simply wanted to hug every ounce of bacon that gallantly paraded behind the shelves simply teasing me. The notes of baritone, falsetto and soprano glided rose higher and higher as I fancied all the beautiful cheeses propped next to salamis and olives and all the beautiful things that makes one kick ass brunch or a sandwich or Hors d'oeuvre or just simply a beautiful.life.dammit. You can make it rain here! Rain chocolates that is! It 's so full of delicious goodness, it is uh-mazing!! 

and oh, Andrew Zimmerman was here and if you are anyone who loves food, you should definitely stop by here :D

Pizza is solid. I wish I remembered the guy working the counter but he was so incredibly friendly, down to earth made me want to hang out for awhile. I take that back, pizza was more than solid. I've had tacconellis, beddia, vetri, and this place is still special and stands out. If they partnered with weckerlys ice cream they could take over the world (or at least fishtown)

Get a slice of everything - and probably a whole pie for later.

I love chicken and this place will definitely be my go to spot for lunch! 
the chicken are huge and crispy!

Everything was very clean, and the visitors were reasonably spaced out. It was a breath of fresh air to be in a market like this after all this time spent in quarantine! I love the vibe of this place - reminds me a lot of a smaller version of Pike Place. My absolute favorite stand was the Caribbean food stand - their jerk chicken was some of the best food I've ever tasted. I'll definitely be going back to explore again, soon!!!

I'm not sure why I hadn't gone here before in my year-long (and counting) stay of Philadelphia, especially when its less than 5 minutes by car from work.  I LOVED this place.  Polite workers, bustling "market" feel, fresh produce, bakery, eateries, shops, etc.  Didn't spend a lot of time here, but I will be certain to go back.  I don't think that the 2 mini-tubs of specialty cream cheese (jalapeno and vegetable) in my fridge will do anything for my figure, but honestly, it is really that good.  

My one minor complaint is that the "oyster bar" at the front end (?) of the place only served fried ones!  :(

Everything about this place is awesome. Good food and diversity amongst the people. A nice place for tourists and for people who want to grab a good bite to eat if working in the downtown center city area.

Great urban market, I was impressed by the variety, selection and quality of the stalls. Great eat-in places, lively and appetizing. A must see in Philly.

Warning: the Dutch/Amish place is not open on Sundays.
This place is nasty. Need to take care of their bathrooms, especially if they strictly check if you have a receipt before they let you in. Horrible. Never again.
The food there was great! Just make sure you get a receipt, sometimes you don't get correct change!

I almost hesitated to write a review about the Reading Terminal Market because there are just so many written already, and what else can be said.  But when I have told people in my area of New Jersey about it, most don't know how good it is.  So, I feel it is my duty, in a way, to get the word out.

The selection of food items is really one of the very best of any market in our country.  They have so many things that you just can't get outside of PA, such as Amish cheeses made from unpasteurized dairy.

The two negatives are that there really isn't a convenient parking lot because it is located right in the middle of Center City.  That makes it harder to buy a lot of products because you can't just wheel your cart out to your car.  The crowds can also be intimidating.

Still, this market deserves 5 stars because the selection and the overall experience are rare and hard to find anywhere else.

I love this place! It gets pretty crowded and it is often hard to find seats but it is all worth it.  This is my favorite part of living in Philly(I am such a fat girl).  My favorite spots are:

L. Haltemen- I get all of my meats here. Always fresh and taste great.
Beilers Bakery- Everything here is good! Stay away if you are on a diet.
Franks A Lot- The best baked chicken wings with a bbq glaze. You must try them! The cornbread is also good.
Coastal Cave Trading Co.- Great seafood sandwiches!
Salumeria- Best Italian Hoagies!
Hatville Deli- Best cold cuts.

There are so many other great places to try here other than the places I have listed, I get so stuck on these places that I don't get a chance to try something new.

Was here summer 2016 and it was great. Came back June 2017 with same friend who accompanied me last time and we were both disappointed. Maybe we just had the bad luck to order all the worst stuff on the menu...? 

Couldn't resist ordering the short rib "pierogis" which sounded tasty and enticing but they weren't pierogis at all, more like 3 baked calzones with a thick bland crust and very bland stuffing. Maybe they'd pass as Russian "piroshki" but definitely not Polish pierogis which are soft dumplings and are very tasty.

My friend ordered tuna tartar. It came in a small plastic cup about the size of one of those plastic containers of mandarin oranges that come in 4-packs at the supermarket, a bunch of small tuna slivers, again not very tasty, and served with some kind of fried triangular chips. Made me long for the big tasty tuna tartar at Standard Tap (not sure if they still serve it, but it dwarfed the version served here and tasted much better).

Fish and chips - the fish bits were very tasty but portions were small while "chips" were a heap of thin french fries like you might get at a fast food restaurant except cut to two inches long.

Having worked in several restaurants I hate to be negative but with so many excellent restaurants in Philly, this one has jumped off my list. Sorry.

Best thing about the place is the location with easy street parking and outdoor seating.

Decided to go for a healthy option after the Temple basketball game. The salads were very good at this location. I normally get one of the noodle bowls from HG, but opted for a salad this time. The Golden Curry salad had a very nice flavor, was fresh and unique considering its main green was kale. I enjoyed the blend of curry and cauliflower that helped offset the bland taste of kale. I added chicken for the protein which helped. My wife ended up enjoying the Cobb Salad. We tried all their organic drink options and the best one was the tea. The service took a little long since the salads are made to order and most people get the stir fry bowls so it was expected. I never have a bad experience eating at any HG and would recommend you check it out for a healthy and delicious option. One interesting tidbit about this location is the company's founder is a fellow Temple U alumni and they happen to mention it in the decore. It's great knowing a fellow alum is responsible for a successful chain.

I love eating at every booth in here! Haven't been to all of them yet, but it feels like it's on my bucket list now. My favorite's include: the grilled cheese place,"Meltkraft" and "Molly Malloy's" Brussels sprouts (and I usually despise Brussels sprouts.) They also have Philly's signature "Black & White" cookies  and cute little décor vendors who sell all the touristy stuff. How cute :)
If you come here and can't find anything you obviously don't like food. They have everything from.fresh produce, meats, cheeses, spices. My favorite spot is the original turkey shop.
Great Food definitely a must. A lot of options, pretty much everything your stomach needs.

Everything looks nice and is nice, but to sum it up it is a tourist trap. I found this place a little over rated for what it is. After my friends talking it up who are local -- I found it unfortunate to not be somewhere I might myself to usually roam. Essentially what it is a huge market inside a terminal with lot of different specialty shops and eateries. 

In Washington DC where I reside in one of the suburbs -- there is a place on a smaller scale that is similar to this that sort of has spoiled it for me to no really enjoy these kinds of places and has saturated it for me. I like Reading Terminal for what it is, but I don't know if I'd consider it a 'must see' in Philly unless you're into this sort of thing. I like it for its historical significance, but the food choices were a little less than exciting.

I will probably give it a second shot at my next return simply to say that I did get the grand experience, but like I said -- it is a huge food and flea market gathered in one confined space. Don't expect to find parking around this very easily unless you get lucky like I managed to do.

Loved the ambience of the food market. There were plenty of food stalls but I did find that it lacked some foreign / ethnic foods. Great cheesecakes from Beiler, cajun fare from Becky's. It isnt easy to hrab a table n chair so try to beat the crowd at peak hours.

Awesome huge market with a lot of food options. Don't come here looking for healthy choices, though. It's comfort food. The Amish fare is extra tasty and fresh. Whoopi pies and soft buttery pretzels were my favorite. Locals, tourists and conventioneers all converge here.

Every city should have a reading terminal... but it will never be as good as Philly's. 

GO -- get lost in Reading Terminal... Graze on bites from this stand or that. I love that you can get Amish beef jerky, delectable Thai or Shawarma, sweet treats by the piece or by the pound... and one of a kind goods. 

Don't forget about the shoe shine by the restrooms... best shine for the price I've ever had. And fast.
One of my favorite places in the city. Not overly expensive and the food is out of this world! I highly recommend the Industry Burger and the Korean BBQ Pork Sandwich.

RTM (if you're from Philly, you call it RTM) is a city staple.  It's hard to rate any one place because it's so eclectic.  I really love the Dutch diners for breakfast, Original Turkey for lunch (or Dinic's if you wanna fall asleep in 20 minutes), and any of the bakeries will make a killer cookie. Beware because it's not a place fora private meeting or large groups but great place to catch up on your bestie and talk about your favorite jawns.

Absolutely loved this market! Everything from cajun food, to bagels, ice cream, fresh produce and retail shops. All of the stand employees were extremely friendly and helpful. This place makes me wish I lived in Philly :)

This review has nothing to do with the food there and is solely about a WONDERFUL employee, Cheron Henson. It was my parents first time visiting here and it was quite crowded. We finally found a high table to stand at while we ate our lunch. Cheron was sitting nearby and we struck up a conversation with her and it lead to the most fun personal tour ever! She brought us around to all the stations of a free alcohol tasting with vodkas, ciders, limoncellos, and more, which we never would have found tucked in the corner of the market if it wasn't for her. While she couldn't drink herself as she was on the job, she took the time to make sure we were all having fun! And it lead to my dad buying a delicious chocolate caramel beverage from the limoncello place. Cheron even made sure we were entered into the free raffle giveaway. She was so sweet and when we were about to leave we had a group hug!
The something for everyone! Prices are reasonable. Recommend Herschel's pastrami sandwiches and builer donuts
I love it here so much that I could spend my paycheck AND your paycheck here in a matter of one hour!!!  GO!!  Experience the wonder!!!!  Just bring cash and be ready to spend!
Very busy place and hard to get a table but if you love food it is a great place to visit. Love dinics roast pork sandwiches. The line is usually long but moves fast. We

Calling this place a market is a tad of an exaggeration.
While produce, butcher and shop stalls exist. Reading market really is just a giant indoor food court.  I've been to many of these so call markets and many of them do have tons of shopping. However, here, it's primarily the sale of cooked food for immediate consumption.

That being said, WHAT an indoor food court this is!  With rows and rows of food stalls, you can spend hours easily looking around and trying out different types of food. From Chinese food to the Pennsylvanian Dutch, there is something for everyone! If you look closely, you could find some neat stuff too like draft birch beer. mmmm. The stalls were also a visual treat. I enjoyed watching the cooks stuff meat into the cheesesteaks/roast pork sandwiches. Overall, i felt like the market was a stimuli overload!

I came during the auto show. bad idea. it was insanly crowded. You know that black friday or a full rush hour tokyo/nyc subway form of croweded.

Love the market.  Clean.  Has parking and restroom!  Great selection of shoppes and eateries - bring back memories of my time at la boqueria in Spain and Borough Market in London.  Has one of a kind shop that sell artisanal items such as beeswax candles, hand painted ceramics, fresh baked pastries, abundant selections of meats and charcuteries.  I find the locals to be friendly and ready to help.  Highly recommend this for anyone visiting Philly to add this on their itinerary.

Nothing to say that hasn't already been said about the famous Reading Terminal Market. The vibe is awesome - its like a food flea market. Theres so many great food choices, no matter what you pick you'll love it. My faves are the Dutch Eating Place foe breakfast and DiNic's for the roast pork and broccoli rabe sandwich.  If you've never been, make plans to go. If you've already been, go again. This is an absolute must for any visit the Philly.
Outstanding pizza and service. Fresh ingredients and their weekly specials always deliver.
This is the best thing to happen to lunch in Philadelphia! Fast, afforable, indian food. Absolute jem! Will be coming here often! I had the Aloo Paneer roll, the paneer was very light and flavorful.

As much as I would love to give this location five stars for the amazing variety of high-quality food, the one thing that always irks me is that there isn't more seating.  Seating can be hard to come by during busy periods like the weekend.  If you're looking to take stuff home with you, you can't beat this place.

This is great place to visit when you're a tourist in Philadelphia. If you're a local and haven't been there - get moving! 
There are great places to eat and terrific little shops. The Amish places are always great and some of Philly's finest can be found there. Check out Termini's for cannoli and the farmers market produce stalls.

Benefit for the Market: this is an annual event to benefit this wonderful Philadelphia tradition. Although pricey, the food is amazing (don't eat for like 3 days before) and the drinks plentiful. As this has progressed, they have gotten wiser to having more water and seltzer on hand - smart. So the evening; the libations: good with a superior assortment of beers, sad assortment of wind and even a coffee roaster....noice!

Music: jazz and cool not too loud
Dancing: till late and amazing
Food: wonderful

Bottom line: maybe not an every year thing but certainly worth a 'go'
Great selection, amazing vendors, and amazing food. Always a great place to take friends or family.

Great place to go and check out if you are visiting Philly downtown.
Many places to eat but I felt it was geared toward tourists (even though some are not).
Very convenient to go eat if you are attending conference at convention center or nearby hotels.  But I find that other really good restaurants that locals would eat are not in here. 
(I''m just visiting here first time but saw some youtube that introduced good philly cheesesteaks elsewhere).
Best place to eat!!! Try the Amish fried and smoked chicken wings, they are sooo delicious!!! Also across from it is a freshly squeezed juice place!!!! Yum!!!
All there food is great. I like there seafood and the amish food .
The drinks, the food, the social media is perfect... I went here because of their facebook... good times!!

Masala Kitchen is my favorite late night food spot in Philly. The staff here is so incredibly friendly, especially to the rowdy 2am-3am crowd. I am so thankful they are open late and the deliver as well (hallelujah!) The prices are already super cheap, but they offer $1 off two rolls. They have the best kati rolls in the city in my opinion because the flavor is better and not as dry i.e. it doesn't require a container of white sauce to make it yummy. One roll usually fills me up, but some of my friends prefer 2. I like the paneer tikka and the aloo paneer rolls the best. They also have lassi that's pretty good. I have yet to try their other entree options, but I've never really needed to!
Something for everyone! Check out the maps and reviews in advance so you don't get overwhelmed. You can easily walk by some amazing food and vendors!

I love it here! All fresh fruit, veggies, freshly packed meat in one place. You can also grab food from here which they have a variety of options from uniquely decorated donuts to rotisserie glazed wings, cornbread & Mac & cheese. If you have EBT, debut, credit or cash it always works here.

A plus on top of all of this is they have a parking garage & you can get it validated for up to 3 hours i believe just for $3!
Worst McDonald's I have been to. Service attitude environment everything. Too bad there is so limited McDonald's locations near center city.

Absolutely love it there! I'd get my mail there if I could. My fave spots are the Four Seasons Juice Bar, Glick's Rib Shack, The Dutch Eating Place and Miller's Meats. But I go to many other spots depending on the day and my mood. Treasure of Philly
Very good customer service. Impressed for a chik-fil-a.

Ate at OG turkey. They had like thanksgiving dinners but I couldn't get behind that on a Wednesday in March so I got the Texas griller. The turkey here's top notch and I feel like probably anything u get here's decent. Quick and easy lunch

The crowds, the crush, the noise .. it's all worth it to visit Reading Terminal Market, an indoor nirvana for both blue and white collar food lovers, with many of Philadelphia's Best under one roof. There's more than one (or two or three) incredible bakeries, multiple seafood vendors, a couple of butchers, a poulterer, three produce/grocery meccas (well, one mecca and two side chapels). The quality of food at all of them is terrific, and the prices are reasonable considering the quality. There's a honey place, a tea store and an herb vendor. Pennsylvania Dutch farmer's sell homemade pies, donuts, sandwiches, meats, cheese, etc. I get my Thanksgiving feast food here -- the poulterer is tremendous.

And the restaurants! Coffee, donuts, ice cream, several vendors for delectable cold cuts and spreads, sandwich places up the yahoo, two Asian places, one German, one Greek, a creperie, and more. There's a large community eating section in the middle of the Market and individual vendors have seating as well. Restrooms are available that are clean and well maintained.

Non-food vendors include a cookbook niche and a Philly-themed gift shop.

RTM appeared in the movie Trading Places, and it dresses up for the holidays with a huge miniature train set up, which is appropriate since this building is the former Reading RR (as in Monopoly) train shed.

The Market is open seven days a week but the Pennsylvania Dutch vendors are not there on Sundays or Mondays (and maybe Tuesdays?).

On 12th Street between Arch and Filbert, this fascinating indoor public market is near the convention center, not far from City Hall, and on Chinatown's doorstep, convenient to Market St. and many bus routes, and very close to the Chinatown bus depot.

Founded in 1892, it's a great place to bring visitors. Go there for the history, then stay for lunch! It's not nearly as crowded in the mornings before 11 and in late afternoon, even on weekends. Other times it is crushingly crowded with lines everywhere. Still worthwhile, but not as pleasant! The vendors are almost universally cheery and helpful.

There are multiple entrances. At the 12th and Filbert door you'll find maps of the Market and there are sometimes walking tours.
Awesome place!  I am from Boston and this is even better than Faneuil Hall!!!
If you are in Philly, you have to go to Reading Terminal Market. I visit this place at least twice a week. Lunch time can get crazy busy, but it's every second worth spend.

Love it. A real taste of Philly. Termini Bros for Italian pastry, Basset's chocolate Ice cream, those gross Philly cheese steaks, deli, wine, New Orleans food, Miller's pretzels, Amish baked goods, fresh produce, etc. A must for any foodie who visits Philly. It's an indoor food flea market. The Marriott is right next door as a landmark

We walked a whole 9 blocks to get to this place! :) Being in Center City, I'm not drowning in fast casual Indian food options. After having tried Spice End and Philadelphia Chutney Company, I was quite excited about another option. Stepping in I tried to follow my own advice of "Don't build it up, don't build it up."

The menu is nice and simple and you stand in line to order at the counter. There are various kati rolls (Indian wraps) and rice platters. 

We ordered:
   Chicken Kheema Roll
   Paneer Masala Roll
   Chicken Biriyani Platter
   Cost: $20.33

We were gently urged to try the Paneer Masala Roll by the nice lady at the counter and I sure am glad we did. There are two HUGE pieces of paneer (cheese) which were not dried out and covered in a nice creamy sauce. I didn't want to share with my husband. The Chicken Kheema Roll was bursting with flavorful minced chicken but it was a tad too salty IMHO. They do not skimp out on the filling size of kati rolls here.

The Chicken Biriyani Platter was presented as what you'd get at chicken and rice  food cart stalls. Half the plate was biriyani and the other half iceberg lettuce. There was also pita, a white sauce, and red sauce. The biriyani flavors were great! It met my requirements of the right aromatics, spices, and being not too oily. The spice level would slowly build up and the white sauce helped cool the palate so you could repeat the process. However the chicken was a little dry (not a deal breaker though). 

In the end I enjoyed eating at this affordable place and look forward to trying more items.

Been shopping at Reading Terminal since I was a kid.  Great for high-qualify, affordable groceries, meat, fish, as well as a panoply of prepared foods, gifts, etc.  As soon as I cross the threshold I feel happy!  I love to go early on the weekends to beat the crowds, as it can get very busy.  Plenty of seating so you can pause for a snack and some people watching.

Soooooo I do not write many reviews but I thought I would share. I do not want to be negative and the pizza served was ok, but nothing compared to the reviews. I guess I am a little confused with all these types of places popping up where it is almost a privilege to eat their pizza. We place our order in the morning and we were told it would be ready at 425. And they were 100% accurate which is nice. But for $49 dollars for a plain and a white is out of bounds. No way was it worth that price. It's was good but I named 10 places off the top of my head that were better. Again I do not want to put the place down but I think people either do not know pizza or are just wrapped up in the hype of these types of places.

Bottom line it was good not great. The reviews do not reflect the product. And the prices are stupid high. Pizza has one of the highest profits in the food industry. So again $49 dollars is actually higher then the shore.

LOVE this place! 

The achari paneer, paneer masala and chicken pepperwala are flavorful and tasty! 

Don't forget the two sauces- spicy red sauce and yogurt based white sauce.

My wife and I ate at the Reading Terminal Market twice. The first time, we ate at aand Amish spot run by a Mr. Smucker. The pot roast sandwich was delicious.

The second time we ate at Pearl's Oyster Bar. My wife had a crab cake sandwich and I had an oyster po' boy. Both were good, but not great.

We also shared an ice cream cone from Basset's: quite good.

When people review books they sometimes employ a simple system of "buy, borrow, bypass". For a place like Reading, which can feel like it houses just about everything under its roof, we might think in similar terms... let's try "frequent, few and forego"

now, despite having gone to Reading at least once a week for nearly a year now, I have to admit I haven't given a thorough tour of every shop represented, so the following are just selected from what I have been able to consider:

Frequent:

Dutch Eating Place - I would use any excuse whatever to stop here. 

Godshall's Poutry - I've never been disappointed by the meat I get here. Of course if you drop into Asian markets down the road, you'll notice the price difference. 

Iovine's Brothers and OK Lee tend to have competitive prices on most of their staples, but their grab bags generally cover different territory. If you're fishing for inspiration, it never hurts to swing by both shops

John Yi Fish Market - I've never actually stopped by Golden Fish, I guess it simply happened out of chance. I've had cooked and raw food from Wan's and I was never impressed. John Yi does the job for me.

Few

12th St Cantina - they sell guacamole, salsas, and a variety of tortillas to go, which is convenient since they are generally freshly made and great quality. They also have pre-made foods that are kept cold that would make for a convenient meal at home. 

Bassett's Ice Cream - Few if you can restrain yourself! The WHYY is fantastic, and not only because I love Terry Gross. 

Bee Natural - Love the raw honey. Candles are not my thing so I've never shopped for more than honey.

By George! Pizza - love the pizzas I've tried, and they have a variety of pre-made side dishes that will kick up the variety to dinner without the added time investment. 

L. Halteman - I've had bought their meat before and was satisfied with the freshness and quality. What I primarily come here for, however, is their smoked dog bone, which my dog is absolutely addicted to. I haven't really seen this offered anywhere else and my dog doesn't really go for rawhide so this helps me control her plaque and spoil her rotten.

Martin's Quality Meats and Sausages - They have 20+ varieties freshly made sausages that they have out everyday. Decent selection of meats otherwise. The reason why I don't come here for all my meats is because they don't cut their pieces for you. Meaning, the last two times I've come here for a pound of something, I walked away with anywhere from a quarter to nearly half a pound extra. This makes it harder to portion for meals, so I tend to only drop it when I know I wouldn't mind the difference.

Metropolitan Bakery - I don't eat bread much but I've enjoyed the few I've picked up from here. They also sell their bread for 50% off if you stop in late enough, though the selection dwindles the later the day as is expected.
 
Forego

Blue Mountain Vineyards Cellars - sells a lot of things that have nothing to do with wine. Wines are overpriced. 

The Down Home Diner - Food was pretty disgusting.

Giunta's Prime Shop - nothing wrong with their meats, just a $10 card minimum that bugs. As someone who doesn't like to carry cash and does buy groceries as needed each day, I tend to skop Giunta's altogether.

Jonathan's Best - GENERALLY forego, use in emergencies. 

The Tubby Olive - a bit gimmicky in my opinion. I like to go with a good olive oil and simply infuse on the shelf or on the stove. I can't really see the necessity for treated "gourmet" oils. 

For whatever else residing in Reading, I haven't experienced quite enough of them to merit a review. The rest will have to wait for a review update!

This place is not to be believed. It is like 100 (more?) small restaurants got together in one building offering food from all over the world. Beyond the awesome choices of what to eat there or take with you, there is this great energy. Many of the stands have their own places for you to sit and eat but there is also a central area with lots of tables. We could always find a seat. It's literally right across from the convention center and is definitely worth the 100' walk to check it out, even if you aren't hungry.
I love Reading Terminal . The food is fresh and delicious. Just hate the parking lots.

My first time here and Ismael made my visit very enjoyable! He patiently explained everything to me and helped me make informed choices about my meal! He even offered to make me fresh chicken if I waited seven minutes. My dish was delicious and had a lot of healthy toppings. I look forward to going back. They also did a good job of making the expereince very covid friendly.

Me and my wife went thru Philly for vacation and This is a GREAT PLACE for lunch near the liberty bell! Has everything from cookies, to fruits and veggies,to soap and spices, to restaurants that are mouthwatering great! We had a cheesesteak and a turkey sandwich and both were great! Did I mention cookies? 
The only part that disappointed us was that some stuff wasnt open on tuesdays but its still great.

This is the best tourist spot in Philadelphia! You will have plenty of options for food, delicacies, and other merchandise. The products are a little pricey likely from the rent of the stores but rest assured, they have quality products. They have a wide variety of food ranging from Thai, Greek, American, Chinese, Italian, etc. The list goes on and on. I recommend you come early as it gets very crowded during lunch time. They close also early at 6pm. Tables and chairs may be difficult during lunch time so better get your food to go. Restrooms are also clean at the corner of the market. Read through the history of the place near the restrooms - pretty interesting.

--- Short Synopsis ---
 
This place seems like a food haven and a foodie's (aka Yelper's) dream! There are so many delicious smells, tastes, and sights here at the Reading Terminal Market. I also like how it's simply organized into "streets" and blocks. It feels like there is something here to cater to many tastes!

Tommy DiNic's (or just DiNic's) and Beiler's Donuts were divine!
 
--- Detailed Review ---
 
Seeing how this place had the 2nd most Yelp reviews in Philly (2nd only to Pats Steaks) AND 4.5 stars, I had to come here to check this place out when I flew to Philly en route to a place a few hours south. I am glad I did!
 
Driving and parking here was a tad hectic, but I eventually found my way. The parking garage next door is $4 for two hours if you make a purchase of $10 or more from a Reading Terminal Market vendor. Just make sure to get your parking ticket validated. I would suggest walking and/or public transportation. I am going to do that next time.

As for the actual market, I was initially a little lost where I was, so I began wandering around. I eventually stumbled across a map near the restroom. This help me orient myself and explore the market. There are so many vendors, but they all relate to food, which is awesome!! Most of the vendors sell ready to eat foods like sandwiches, burgers, and pastries, but they are others that sell raw food like produce and seafood! 

From exploring, I noticed Beiler's Donut/Bakery corner had a long line and previous Yelp research led me to Tommy DiNic's. I had both and instantly fell in love with both! They were amazing!

For Tommy DiNic's, the roast pork sandwich with provolone and their broccoli rabe was such an amazing combination. The strong, but not overpowering, cheese complemented the succulent pork. The broccoli rabe provided that nice chewy texture. The bread's texture and taste was excellent along with containing all the extra juices of its delicious interior items. I also enjoyed putting the peppers they provided along the counters. It adds another depth of flavor along with a crunchy texture.

Just a heads up, Tommy DiNic's is also referred as just DiNic's on the map.

For Beiler's Donuts, I tried the harvest apple and blueberry fritter. They were both amazing, but I liked the blueberry fritter more. Each bite was like a blueberry muffin that had been perfectly deep fried with that amazing crisp edge to it, along with being coated in a sweet, succulent glaze!!

For any Yelper, even those just using Yelp to find places, this is a must stop destination in Philly! There are just so many options in this market!!

Delicious and fresh Mediterranean food. I tried chicken shawarma naya bowl, the protein and rice  was nice and warm, the salads we're fresh and crunch, the humus and tahini was delicious and to my surprise it came with a side of a small, soft and warm pita bread. Perfect lunch after wandering around Philly center city!

This place is fantastic! Not sure how we would have survived the winter without their delivery service. Unlike most Indian restaurants, their food is not greasy or heavy. It always arrives hot and fresh. I typically get the aloo rolls (since I mostly eat vegetarian), but my husband enjoys the chicken and egg rolls. It makes for the perfect light meal or late night snack when you're craving something flavorful but not too heavy.

Super cute market! 

Tip: Come super early or later in the afternoon to beat the lunch rush.

Metered street parking available- we were able to snag a spot around 2p Sunday. Parking spots seemed to turn over quickly. 

This place is poppin' and lovely for a weekend stroll. Your biggest challenge is probably navigating the crowds and finding a table to eat at, depending on your lunch choice.  

Our stops:
Termini Brothers Bakery: delish ameretti and horseshoe cookies. Always a pleasure to see fresh cannolis that are filled right in front of you once upon order. Love the idea- keeps that cannoli crust from getting soggy :)

Tommy Dinic's Roast Pork and Beef: Our fav lunch spot. Come early before they sell out of the beef brisket. Since we arrived later in the afternoon, we had to "settle" for their pulled pork which was still phenomenal!! We ordered one sandwich to share (they're ginormous). Each sandwich comes with the option to add toppings- we chose broccoli w/ cheese and it was perfect. We were content and satiated after inhaling our half sandwiches. TIP: If you "eat in" at the bar, you can skip the entire line! And their service is super nice and friendly. We left happy with our experience. 

There are also a lot of healthier options too (we are just total pigs)...and ultimately decided to leave with a smoothie/green drink from the juice bar to feel better about ourselves. lol 

Service was all around really friendly. You'll see a nice mix of college students and families here on a nice weekend. I'd definitely be back! :)
The ML special meal was delicious!!! The lassi and Chaas was excellent and so were the paneer rolls. Gentle on the pocket too. Highly recommended.
Great place to check out if you're new to the city. Also a good place to bring visitors. Lots of food options and a bar inside.

If you're hungry and feeling adventurous and exploring new palettes, then give RTM a try. They've got German, Chinese, AMerican, Cajun, specialties of the region, plus more. I've been here a few times. Have tried the roast pork sandwich from Dinic's. I've bought chocolate from the specialty chocolate vendor. It's a cool place to walk around and try and shop for new and different delicacies.

Solid pizza by the slice establishment but from what I hear, If you walk in during certain times of the days, you can order whole pies. 

The pizza itself has a thin but a not too crispy consistency, cooked well, with a good sauce. The guys behind the counter are very pleasant as well!
So much to do! Place is awesome, but super crowded everytime I go. Not easy to find seating if you are in a group of more than 4 people.

I've been to the NY location and this is my first time at the Philly one. If you know CAVA, it's a similar concept but I think it's better because it's not as overwhelming in food quantity and choice, but NAYA has better quality in my opinion.

I got the bowl with freeka and the cauliflower as my protein. Highly recommend this combo - too good. I think they have better flavors than most Mediterranean fast food places I've gone to and I absolutely love the garlic whip and the baba ghannouj. My favorite thing is just eating the garlic whip with the pita they give. Absolutely bomb.

I got the cucumber, diced tomatoes, pickled turnips, onion and tahini sauce. So amazing and good. The plus is always the warm soft and fresh pita to top it off.

Great place and great location right by city hall :)

They have it all.  You can find literally anything here.  Good location to meet friends, everyone gets to order their favorite items from the various vendors, grab a seat and take in the atmosphere of the history of bygone days.   Fun, crowded, noisy, but always satisfying.
So many choices it was hard to settle on what to get.  Chorizo fries are a must!fresh deli sandwich was like thanksgiving leftovers.  Plus ice cream and pastries for dessert.
A must see!!! We went multiple times just to eat various foods!!!  Finding a place to sit is difficult and tables were dirty so bring your own wet wipes to clean. The crepes place was to die for!!!

I use to go to NY for platters at the halal guys cart, it was good but so greasy and killed my stomach. I was in the area for and craving a platter, to my surprise it wasnt greasy the rice was light, soft and nicely seasoned.  Doesn't even make you feel bad later. I got the chicken and lamb platter. The meat & rice was flavorful and I liked that there was little salad but more of everything else. This is my favorite platter!!  The red sauce isnt really spicy like ny but very good.

I got the mango lassi, it was very good refreshing and thick and had a strong mango taste

I got the chicken tikka and paneer roll, through small it was very filling. Chicken tikka was a little dry but dipping it in yogurt took care of it. 

They packed the food very well and delivery came before the estimated time! Even my friends loved it better than other places we tried it philly!

Good place to eat; shop for produce, fish , sweets and meat. They have a large number of shops and it's get crowded. I have eaten the cheese steak ,  ice cream and pretzels here. All of them were very good and reasonably priced.  

It is across the street from the Jefferson train station.  

It's a fun place to visit and they have live entertainment outside the station.

Tourist trap with some good stuff for locals. City coffee roasts their own coffee right there and they have the best prices in the city. Good produce and seafood. Large variety of foods to choose from.

This is your average Potbelly sandwich shop, which is a good thing for me. I miss this place and I wish we had them in California since most of the sandwich chains here suck!
I usually get the Wreck with lettuce, tomato, mustard, and spicy peppers. Oh man the peppers are so delicious I regret not buying a bottle of them to bring back with me. 
Good, friendly, folks who work at this location also!
Hope it never leaves! All kinds of goodies! I love the fresh meats and the fact that it was actually a train terminal in the eighteenth century
Wide array of food! Can't go wrong with a dinics roast pork or an Amish breakfast. The wait in line is worth it so don't get frustrated.

Sooo much to experience here! For me, it's like the taste of Philly! I found a variety of local foods that were all amazing! We had dinner at Molly Murray's and enjoyed some fantastic beers, chili fries, beet salad and empanadas! The service was fast, friendly and professional! They had a very interesting menu with something special for everyone!

We also enjoyed some delicious coffee at Old City Coffee!
