Reading Terminal Market some of the world's greatest food wrapped into one lively and happy place.
There is a wide array of comida in the Market -- fried chicken, fish, dessert, and of course Philly cheesesteaks.
The seating is clumped together in the middle and it may seem hard to find a table, but it's really not. Trust me.
Great spot that anybody can vibe with.
Nice place, nice people, good food, drink and atmosphere. Many things to do inside and in the adjacent areas

If your definition of good food is one that looks like puke after you ate a lot of hulk theme green dye cake and tastes worse than it looks, then yea Masala Kitchen is amazing. The awful quality and taste of the food is only preceded by the stench and oh what a stench! It takes me back, to the worst smelling streets of Kolkata, me with my nose clutched, trying to make my way unscathed. I was in philly for 2 nights and the first one was magical till butchered by the food from this place. Would not recommend.
Loved it! Every type of food you can imagine. One seen this place on the Food Network and I was in Philadelphia on business. I got the oxtails at one of the many cool places to eat. Great experience.

This is one of my favorite places to buy produce and watch people.  The proximity to the convention center promises that the Reading Terminal Market will always be filled with interesting people and great food.

As a resident of Pennsport who wants the neighborhood to thrive and a food addict who is dying for a short-walk-away place to grab a good meal, I really REALLY wanted this place to be great. 

Don't get me wrong, it still has potential to be great, but for that to happen, the food needs to get so much better. Everything I've eaten there (arepas, fried green tomatoes, wings, sausage, burger, even the fries!) has been...meh. There's no better way to say it. Nothing's terrible, but nothing is particularly good either. For the prices they're charging and their supposed commitment to the industry, the food should really be the centerpiece.

On the other hand, it's a nice place to come for a happy hour or a late night drink. The ambiance is good, although it gets quite loud and the music choices can be...awkward. The drinks are good and quite strong, which helps justify the $10 price tag. 

So I'll keep going in the hopes that it'll stick around long enough for the owners to wise up and turn things around. In the meantime, stick to the drinks.

Sometimes when I am running errands I will go through the drive thru.  No matter who is working they always seem to be patient, kind, and efficient. 

Food quality as is expected.  Good price with the $5 fill ups.

So much food!! From all types of cuisines! If you're looking for a place to get a little bit of everything from Philly, this is the place. From candles to desserts to oysters to burgers to cheesesteaks, Reading Terminal has a little of everything. 

I came on a Monday evening around 5pm. The market closes around 6pm and I found it odd that roughly 10% of the stores were already shutting down. Regardless, I was able to have a cheesesteak from Carmen's, a cupcake from the Flying Monkey and even bought some candles. The concept is great, I just wished their hours were a bit more flexible. I saw tons of breakfast foodie places but Reading Terminal doesn't open until 11am. It seems more like a lunchtime venue than breakfast and dinner. 

If you're in town, it's definitely a gem to visit.

The guy making pizza is in the worst mood at all Times and it shows in the quality of the pizza. Extremely light with a thick layer of grease for $4 per slice. Expect to hear about how much of a bad mood the guy making pizza is. Will not go there again. Horrible experience.

Fantastic Pizza!
Friendly Staff!

Their specials are consistently some of the best slices I've ever had!
This place is amazing!!! If you have several members of the family that are picky, this is the place for you! It's got such a wide variety of foods, and deserts! Everyone was very nice!

Reading (pronounced "redding") Terminal is fantastic, lots of wonderful yummy things. However, there's also a bunch of people, so if you're not into crowds, do your research and figure out what time might be best to go (early morning? not weekends?). I particularly like getting the fresh squeezed/blended juices and smoothies. There are places to get produce, cheese, meats/fish, chocolates, gifts, coffee, pastries, and so much more! The prices are not particularly cheap, but it's not exorbitantly priced either. If nothing else, it's a great place to people watch. 

It's also ideally located for me, since it's right next to Chinatown, where I do my weekly grocery shopping.

Think of how bad a fast food restaurant needs to be for me to actually bother writing a review about it 

This place is awful. I've been here multiple times and each time They never have anything. Once they didn't have nuggets. if you place a mobile order it charges you anyway. So in addition to wasting your time going there only to be turned away, you also need to worry about calling McDonald's support to get a refund 

The people are also crazy rude there, and weirdos are constantly going in the store. Some guy was jacking off while ordering fries and when the lady behind me yelled about it, the guy behind the counter was just like "okay what do you want me to do about it." Like?!?!? At least be partially concerned? Idk
Love this place, although if you don't like crowds don't go here on the weekend. Great lunch spot when on Jury Duty or if you want to try some Philly staples. Great place to find fresh meats.

Very crappy service at this place. I was just standing there for over 5 minutes with three people doing a drive thru order. I guess these GED dopes can't handle anything on their own. Get actual employees and not idiots who probably barley tie their shoes.
One of the highlights of my trip to visit to Philly. So much to eat and see at Reading terminal market. You just want to try everything.

What a unique place with some truly great places to eat. Every time we go we find something new and interesting from the local counties peddling their products to the staple restaurants representing themselves. This place is definitely a hustle and Bustle place we you have to be patient when its busy as there are lines but always worth the wait. I have never had a bad or negative experience at the terminal.

A wonderful place to spend a few hours. (And if you love food, you'll definitely be spending a few hours.) Beware though, as it tends to get extremely crowded. There is such a great variety of food here and so much of it is so delicious! From a variety of ice creams to Indian food to classic gumbo to fancy corndogs with toppings to Puerto Rican food to banana pudding with special flavors... the list just goes on and on. You can even get fresh, smoked bones and pig ears for your dog here. This is a definite must-visit if you're anywhere within a 20 mile radius of Philadelphia. You'll find yourself coming back quite often, as I do. The only bad thing is that it's often incredibly crowded, and because you're in such a crowded place, the seating area where you can eat food at the tables is usually extremely dirty from people leaving behind trash and crumbs and messes constantly.
I wish this place was in Texas.  If you love great food of all types this is the place to go.  This is on the top of my revisit list next time in PA.
Dinics is the only reason I come here and it's the only reason I need to give the place 5 stars

An easy walk, busy, but navigable. A nice place that felt like a pavilion in county fairs. All indoors and all contained to a single building, lots of Quakers selling different goods. There is a restroom toward the middle edge  of the building.

This is the best pizza by the slice in Philadelphia and I'm willing to stake my professional and personal reputation on it. Strong words to express my strong feelings about Pizza Shackamaxon. 

As anybody in my family will tell you, my ideal pizza is thick (I abhor thin crusted pizza...), chewy and ample dough, with sweet tomato sauce and pepperoni toppings. Another thing they'll tell you is that I love eating standing up (I hate sitting in general). 

At Pizza Shackamaxon, I get the best of both worlds: to eat doughy and thick crusted pizza standing up with a lovely view of Girard Ave right outside. I've eaten here in a snowstorm and on a sunny spring day. I love the interior atmosphere of the restaurant and how it's always at a comfortable temperature to combat the bipolar east coast weather outside. 

As a picky eater, I gravitate towards the pepperoni slice and the cheese slice, but they have delightful weekly specials which they post on their instagram account. Even the plain cheese slice is teeming with flavor (lots of basil!) in each bite. Maybe one day I'll be adventurous enough to try one of the special flavor of the weeks.

Also, the employees always call me "miss" which makes my day :D

Finally... got a chance to dine at the Industry.  It's been on my restaurant list for months.  We had the risotto and veggie tofu dip with chips for appetizers.  The veggie tofu dip was served cold and on the sweet side.  The risotto was deep fried and served with a tomato based sauce.  It was ok.  We ordered it for the kids, but were expecting the traditional risotto (of course, should have known better that there would be a twist).  

The kids had the veggie alphabet soup for their entree.  It was light and healthy, and they enjoyed spelling words with the pasta.  For entrees, we had the bbq duck burger and flank steak; both were served with home-made fries.  The bbq sauce was sweet, wish it was spicy, should have asked for tabasco.  The steak was tender.

I had the mixed drink with egg white.  Had to try it.  It sounds weird, but the drink was very good.  I couldn't taste the egg white at all.  My husband tried various specialty beers.  The Industry has a decent selection of craft beers.

The best part of our meal was the outstanding service.  Our waitress was friendly, helpful and checked in on us frequently.
Do not miss Reading Terminal if you're in the city. It's foodie heaven! They have everything your tastebuds could want and more.

I have lived in the Philadelphia area for six years now and this is still one of my favorite places to visit. The variety of food you can get in here is ridiculous. You have to visit the usuals....like Dinics who has the best roast pork sandwiches. Also grab a dozen (or two) donuts from Beilers. I promise you it'll be the best donuts you've ever had. If they have any available....get the blueberry ones!! Come hungry so you can leave happy because you will want to try everything! !

Great Indian "fast food" with quality ingredients! The food is ready within minutes of ordering and you can easily take it out or eat it there. I got the chicken pepperwalla- it had the perfect amount of flavor and spice. If you like peppers, try this!!

I've only been here once, but definitely plan on trying the rest of the menu. The inside was impeccably clean and the servers were friendly.

This establishment is always quiet now I know why. Upon going up the drive thru, the cashier and employees were too busy yapping & texting on their phone. I guess there is no policy or Management on site to enforce it. Anyways, my ordered was mess up because the employees didn't bother to check it before handling it to me or lack of concern. This is why minimal wages shouldn't increase because of dumb### like these who refuse to do their job. Next time, I'll dine at Popeyes  instead to save me the headaches.

So if you are undecided on what to eat... just go to the Reading Terminal Market by the Conventional Center.
We had already ate so we got an Amish Donut that was highly recommend by several people.
We could walk around for hours.
The Sample of Chicken and Shrimp Gumbo from Becks Cajun Cafe was amazing.  I am gonna see if they ship.
The amount of Amish products was amazing.  If we weren't traveling with limited suitcase space I would of bought everything!!!
We settled on some Amish Donuts from Beilers.  Very good and rich!!!!
This is a must when in Philly!!!

Do you ever just walk into a place and in every direction you look in, you see food?  I'm not talking like a basic grocery store, but like gourmet food that you can smell just by looking in its direction.  If you are a foodie, this place has everything.  EVERYTHING!!!  It is especially convenient if you are staying at a nearby hotel like the Marriott Downtown since the market is not even a block away.  

So this market is a giant warehouse, and there are vendors literally everywhere.  It has many entrances, one of them being for a diner that is the only thing open 24/7... everything else closes at 6:00.  The food isn't just limited to grocery shopping - aside from the diner, there are plenty of sit-in restaurants too (and some have happy hour!).  There are bakeries and ice cream parlors too.  This place isn't just limited to food, either - there were a few vendors for gifts and for African wear and decor as well.  

The only food I got to try was from a taco place.  It was a chicken taco with very generous portions of everything.... the sauces, the meat, the guacamole, all of it.  How did it taste?  INCREDIBLE.  If I really had money to spend, I would sample various things to take home.  It is a great market and absolutely must be checked out if you are in town.

Great place for breakfast, lunch, dinner or anything in between! I got a bagel and iced coffee which were delicious but I wish I could try more. They had beautiful display cases with a huge variety of shops to pick from. I recommend walking around and trying some samples as it can be overwhelming with so many options. Also fun to people watch while enjoying your food at the tables provided

Love Reading Terminal! Best food stands. If you haven't been you must go. Favs are Guintas meats, diNicks, cheese shops, fresh honey, fantastic produce, pizza, great diners, fantastic breads and baked goods, restaurants, bar, diners. The best stuff!

I love reading terminal! I go there for a quick stroll around the market, lunch, an my weekly grocery shopping! I love to go past luhv deli for my vegan burgers an "cold cuts" an swing past ok produce for a good deal on some much needed weekly fruits an veggies! There's also a place ran by the Dutch who has these delicious pickled eggs an beets that my husband hates but I absolutely love them an every time I'm there I have to stop there or it's not gonna be a good trip!

Great slices! Better than Pizzeria Beddia. I am glad that Beddia moved onto its bigger place so that folks like me who just want a high quality slice of pizza can enjoy this spot. It's probably as close to the Jumbo Slice experience as you can get in philly (along with Pizza Dad's) so any DC transplants should enjoy this spot.
When in Philly, you HAVE to stop at this amazing and historic market. Located in the middle of downtown, the market has food vendors, unique grocery, and amazing treats and sweets of all kinds.

Kati roll is mediocre.
Missing the essential paratha.
Over prices for one roll, should get two for the price.
Avoid the platter.

I first came across this pizza place in philly critic review mentioning they were trying to be good pizza without the exclusive attitude of the original Pizzeria Beddia. I thought I would try it out since I love pizza. I arrived with friends and purchased a pie. During the transaction the manager or person that seemed to be in charge awkwardly emphasized how lucky we were to receive our pie. Ok I thought, maybe I got the last one. When we all finished, we noticed they brought out another pie to serve as slices. We each had one slice with the first pie and wanted more. As we walked up to buy more, other customers walked in. We were quickly told that we needed to let the other customers have a chance to get a slice first for "ethical reasons." Once we figured out that the other guests were given their allotted slices we asked if we could have the remaining 3 slices. We were then told that they were open for another hour and that the remaining slices were for other guests. When we asked for further explanation the staff mocked us claiming they only sold single slices to customers....despite their menu board pricing out whole pies. The conversation went on and the staff continued to be rude, asking our names and telling us to have a nice evening in a sarcastic way. Seriously, all we wanted was to buy some pizza. I'm sorry but it wasn't good enough to put up with this behavior. There are so many other great options and this place is awkwardly trying too hard to be exclusive

From the smell of fresh breads and cakes, to a nice hot Philadelphia cheesesteak, Reading Terminal Market is one of the best lunch spots and local markets in Central Philadelphia. 10/10 will come back again!

This is an amazing pizza in a famous location. It might even be better than the predecessor since the dough is stretched a bit thinner. Plus you can get slices to go. Great pizza! One of the best I've ever had.

At the end of my order it seemed like My cashier "Emily" Had a slight attitude I ordered a spicy chicken Sandwich with pepper jack cheese and my order came up to $8 and some change I told her that I had a coupon for the sandwich (minus the cheese added in the sandwich) and the coupon didn't scan correctly and she said that the coupon scanned correctly and told me that I told her that I wanted a spicy chicken-deluxe-sandwich and that the coupon did scan. I said "no I only wanted a spicy chicken sandwich with pepper jack cheese and a small strawberry milkshake" and I had a coupon for the sandwich and that it still shouldn't be $8 and some change. She said "well what kind of sandwich is the coupon for?" ..I said "it's for a regular or spicy chicken sandwich"..she then asked a manager for the card and he scanned his card and took off the milkshake instead of sandwich..after that was corrected to him taking off the sandwich instead of the milkshake she seemed a little flustered...and didn't offer me a sauce for my chicken sandwich. The sandwich was served fast tho' and the person who served me my sandwich was polite and did get me the sauce that I wanted. 

I was disappointed that my spicy chicken sandwich did not have any pickles on it as I was anticipating and my milkshake did not have a cherry on top. The bathrooms and outside area was clean and i noticed as i ate my sandwich in my car that they did tackle down their long drive thru line very swiftly. I usually have a much better experience at this chick fil a. 

I

It's just a tourist trap. I can never find a good place to eat. Food is mediocre at best. Ive tried burgers, burritos, pretzels, breakfast. But the desserts are excellent. Oh and the grilled cheese place is .  But the building is always insanely packed. I'd rather go to the Bourse food court. A little bougier

i made a haiku about this pizza: 

crunch like an earthquake
slurpable cheese (tang and grease)
the only pizza

I can't stop thinking about this pizza and it's coming out in weird ways, clearly. I am literally obsessed with this pizza. The only reason i go on instagram is to check the account for this place to see their posts/stories. Then this leads me to think about the pizza throughout the day. At least once a week, my willpower to resist the magic pizza caves, and I end up stopping in for two (huge) slices. 

Some people complain that 4 dollars for pizza is too much. First of all, these pizzas are cut into six slices so they are significantly larger than your average slice. Second, I'm not coming in here because I have a desire for just some pizza. It's because this is now the ONLY pizza i want, the only pizza that satisfies my stomach (soul). It is THE pizza and I'd pay 5 dollars a slice and i'm not ashamed to admit it. 

Thank you to these supreme pizza magicians. I love you a lot.

Philadelphia's own Kati Roll gem. One of those rare restaurants that's open late, easy on the pocket l(5.50 per roll) and is sure to tantalize your tastebuds - a combination that's hard to beat! And it's a lighter alternative to late night pizza. 

There are over a dozen different options including variations of chicken, beef and Paneer(cottage cheese). If you are looking for food after a drunk night with your friends, or if you are just scouring the city for good, cheap late night eats, this should be on your list!

We were excited to try this Pizza location when visiting Philly, but we were not very impressed. We decided to take the scenic route and walk a decent distance to try this location, but we were greeted by short tempered staff and cold pizza. I guess Pizza Shackamaxon caters more to the local individual as I'm hoping other people had a better experience than myself.

One of my absolute favorite places to go in the city! When my family comes to town for the holidays we always go there for lunch. The terminal holds a special place in my heart because my uncle and his father owned and worked at a butcher in the terminal, most of my older cousins worked in the terminal in the summers whether at the butcher shop, or another stall. My uncle died when I was very young, and soon after that the butcher closed. 

Another great place at the terminal is termini's bros bakery. The turkey place is a family fav. And there is a beer garden in there now and in front of the bar stools are name plates w the original merchants family names on them. Highly recommend
I will agree with most yelpers this is a must visit place in philly.  The taste, smell and people are all part of the experience.  If you love to eat then, you need to be here.

The Reading Terminal Market is one of America's largest and oldest public markets, housed since 1893 in a National Historic Landmark building.  The RTM offers the widest variety of restaurants under one roof, which includes a diverse variety of locally grown & exotic produce, locally sourced meats and poultry, plus some of the best seafood, cheeses, baked goods, ice cream and confections to be had on the East Coast!

If you are a foodie, then you can't miss a visit to the infamous Reading Terminal Market. I've been here numerous times over the years and I have yet to be disappointed. Don't miss the Amish Bakery, Beiler's, where at least the very least, you will experience some of the best PA Dutch home-style food in all of Pennsylvania!  I never visit Philly without taking advantage of an opportunity to snag a few Harvest Apple donuts from Beiler's! Best donut I've ever tasted!

My second favorite spot at RTM's has to be "The Original Turkey". It's like having Thanksgiving dinner every day! There are so many choices, you won't go home hungry! 

If you get a chance to buy a ticket to "Taste of Philly", you'll get your fill of cheese-steak, donuts, crepes, ethnic foods from all over the world, as well as some of the best desserts and confections to be found in the massive state of Pennsylvania!

Need produce? RTM gotchu. Need meats/seafood? RTM gotchu. Need artisan cheeses? RTM gotchu. Need baked goods? RTM gotchu. Need to eat? RTM gotchu. An indoor market with a variety of merchants to check out for your grocery needs, grabbing a bite/drink, or specialty gifts. A Philly staple!

My family is from the Philly area and I always have to make a stop here during my visits. For me, it's more for people watching and picking up sweet treats, although Glasers Black and white cookies aren't sold here any more (the store closed in NYC). 

Pros:
1). Lots of food options, even for the pickiest eaters. 
2).  Historically interesting
3).  Grocery shopping and specialty foods
4).  Close to Jefferson Septa stop
5).  Restrooms

Cons:
1).  Although there are tons of food options here, it's not the best available in Philly. They have mediocre cheesesteaks and Asian foods that you can get better in one of the cheesesteak places (Jim's, Genos, Sonny's, etc) or in Chinatown. 
2).  Super crowded!  If you can avoid bringing a stroller, do it!  Wait times for food can be almost an hour during peak times. 
3).  Not a lot of places to sit and eat. You have to stalk the tables and wait for someone to leave. 
4).  You're paying for the touristy aspect, so prices are higher for everything. 
5).  The fish markets can ruin your appetite with the stench of fish. 

Go ahead and fall for this tourist trap at least once. It's definitely worth visiting and probably my favorite market.

Such a neat indoor farmer's market setup! Unfortunately, the Dutch Eating Place was closed both times I went, and DiNic's was sold out of the pulled pork sandwiches...but I was successfully able to buy some artisan truffle boxes at Chocolates by Mueller, a Philly soft pretzel and other goodies at the PA General Store, a few scoops of Bassetts Ice Cream, and wished I could still have room for Flying Monkey Bakery or Old City Coffee. Pearl's Oyster Bar looked pretty enticing as well. I could've spent all day here if I didn't have business to do. Very impressed by the array of fresh meats, seafood, cheeses, nuts, produce, baked goods, even olive oil! They even already had t-shirts commemorating the Papal Visit as of early August 2015. Surprisingly, I didn't try any of the cheesesteak places here (By George, Spataro's), just didn't have enough time to explore all of it. Too bad the Wednesday and Saturday morning Taste of Philadelphia Market Tours fell during times I wasn't in the area!

The pizza was burnt, and looking at the pictures thats their pizza style.  Was a bit tough to eat and even the flavor wasn't impressive.  I came here because of the barstool review that compares it to Brooklyn's Di Fara.  Ive had Di Fara and it doesnt come close at all sorry to say.

Meh. We went at 1pm on a Sunday. It was so crowded it was hard to walk anywhere without losing each other. People were lined up 15+ people deep at each cash register to order food. If you love shiny objects, over crowding, and under performing this is the place for you. If you like out of the way, hidden gems, then walk past and go to ANY of the empty restaurants in the adjacent blocks.
One the nation's oldest farmer's markets is a "must see" in Philadelphia.  Be sure to try the Amish bakery's cinnamon rolls!

OMG!!!!! i love this place. There is so much that goes on & for you to try & sample that if you are on a lunch break or you go before you get to work prepare yourself to arrive or return late. There is no way unless you actually what you are looking for & want to get. Every time I go I am always late to work. This is one of Philly's best place for tourist to go visit while they are here.

Call me Kung Fu Panda but who doesn't like dumplings?!
I completely forgot that I bought a Groupon good for $7 toward dumplings.  I wandered in on a weekday afternoon.  The location was easy to find & very clean inside. Even found good short-term parking.
Didn't care about the menu. This stop was about the dumplings. I ordered cheesesteak dumplings to go. 
The first bite, brilliant!  Perfectly fried & loaded with the perfect amount of cheesesteak.  Nothing short of excellent. The second bite confirmed the first. After the third and final dumpling bite, the universe offered secrets!!  Humpty's dumplings are legit!  BRAVO!

Update: 
I tried the Buffalo and Honey Chipotle Chicken, Asian pork, Broccoli Cheddar, Sausage & Pepper, and the Cheesesteak.  Cheesesteak wins by far with S&P a distant second. The quality of every flavor rocks so run some past your taste buds.

Excellent food market with a wide diversity of quality offerings. Home of Dinic's, awarded "best sandwich in America". Baked goods are excellent here. At the produce corner you can find fresh squeezed orange juice for half the price of what you would pay in the burbs. This place truly has something for everyone.

I came here for a quick meal since we were at the convention center and we had to rush back for another panel.

The food was what I came to expect. Meh. It's McDonald's - it's fast and cheap, what do you expect? 

However, it took forever for them to get the food. I stood there for a good while waiting for it here. They had a group of us just standing there waiting to hear our numbers called.

Also, some tables were missing chairs. While other tables were still dirty, obviously not wiped down.

If it weren't so close to the convention center, definitely find elsewhere. 

One perk though is it's got a pretty view of some of the buildings.

This is the best pizza in Philly, no contest. Kind of like an artisan NY slice, but a little airier, fancified, cooked well-done. 

Killer tomatoes, cheese blend, and crust. White pies are always interesting, too. Guys running the shop are awesome.

I'm honored to be the Duke of Masala! I can honestly say every visit I'm 100% satisfied my partner and I eat here often and I always order the Chicken and rice platter which is layered on a bed of rice , lettuce, chicken , sliced tomatoes accompanied by naan (flat bread). Delicious food and open until 3am !

Pros: The Reading Terminal Market, literally, has something for EVERYONE! RTM is like Cleveland's West Side Market on steroids. What I like the most about RTM is that, if you only have limited time in Philadelphia, you can get pretty much whatever you're looking for here. I very much enjoyed the concept that you can walk in any direction and find a dozen different fresh and prepared food options, chatchkes to buy, fresh fruit and vegetable vendors, and just a huge variety of general stuff to ogle. And, in case you don't have enough cash, there's plenty of ATMs around.

Cons: The low ceilings and over-abundance of hanging signs (with few way-finding signs) can make it difficult to navigate. I visited on a weekend day during the holiday season, so it was pretty chaotic anyway. This place can be packed - I mean body-to-body. You may have to wait in line no matter what you choose; and, you'll definitely have to stand around and wait for somewhere to sit and eat.

I look forward to visiting the RTM again, during the week and not during the holiday season!
wow, wow, and wow...donuts, hoagies everywhere, falafel, chocolate, cookies, meats, smoothies, produce, seafood, flowers...JEEZ, you will not leave hungry...

Lunch Buffet was good. Not spicy like as I would like. Two sections of food and a good place to take your visiting elders from India if you in Philadelphia for a tour. It's quick to get in. Too heavy on curries. Road side parking is a bit tough if you are here on a busy day with lot of traffic.
Very culturally diverse food from all over! Great way to get a taste of local PA eats. Incredibly crowded all the time, very few places to actually sit, and definitely not suited for COVID times.

What can you write or say about the RTM that hasn't been said or written? Once you visit our historical treasures head over to RTM. Fresh produce and food from all over the globe. Take your high blood pressure and/or your diabetes medicine and ENJOY!!

Such a hidden gem! This place is delicious, inexpensive, and best of all - open all night :) Best kati roll I've tried is the mixed veggie. Service used to be a bit slower but they've picked up the pace considerably. Now you can get your food in less than 5 minutes.
The amount of choices there is incredible. If you go to Philadelphia, stopping here is a must. It has everything you can think of.

Brand new to Philly, I hadn't a clue where I was nor what I was to do while the Mr. was at a conference?  Our hotel was RIGHT ACROSS the street from the Reading Market so we wandered over for lunch - and never left  I was there every day, sometimes for every meal! Read the Yelp reviews for the major stars like Pearl's Diner for fresh yummy seafood, DiNic's roasted pork sandwich rated BEST SANDWICH IN THE US by Food Network, Little Thai Markets curried salmon ($8 people -crazy!?) Carmen's Philly cheese steak, the Crepes - oh my, HUGE and delightful!! Bassett's ice cream - same location since the 1800s and DELICIOUS!! I could go on & on - fresh meats & seafood, produce, SO.MANY. Bakeries  Stop by - it will be a highlight of your trip!! AMAZING!!!!

This place is awesome! There are so many places to eat, it will take you about an hour just to figure out what you want. You can get anything from a famous philly cheesteak to mazto ball soup!! There is an amish bakery towards the back that has the best chocolate raspberry cake! The prices are pretty fair too.  It is pretty hectic around lunch time, but if you can find a place to sit, it's fun to watch all that's going on around you.

A great place to go for much after the car show at the convention Center across the street! It was amazing to see all the incredible food choices here. It was absolutely PACKED at lunch time on a weekday. Very hard to decide what to pick there's so many choices...and difficult to find something for a vegetarian. I ended up getting a veggie stack on a bagel which tasted excellent and was a great value. A bottle of mango pineapple juice to go with it...then ended up going back inside for a fresh warm black and white cookie after I saw someone else with one. A big 5 stars. Philadelphia has the best food in the entire world.

Awesome Place

Where to begin?  This marketplace has a myriad of stands inside what kind of looks like Quincy Market in Boston, but let me tell you 100 times better.  You literally could eat at every stand for lunch and eat something different for 2 months, it's that large and diverse.  

All fresh food stands, you can do some food shopping as well.  The smells that reviberate inside this place are intoxicating.  I can see why anyone would eat at a crappy fast food place nearby, with this gem sitting in front of them.  

Whatever cuisine your in the mood for, they are bound to have it.  If your in Philly this is a must stop.  You could take an hour just to walk through and check out the entire place.

Check out the website:
http://www.readingterminalmarket.org/merchants

I will never miss it again when I visit Philly, awesome!

Thanks
I buy all my meat, seafood and poultry here!  Everything is great.  It's my Saturday hangout.

Super busy place even on a Monday when I went. But what an assortment of different foods and homemade goods! I went to the Candy store and got a huge pack of Blue Raspberry Gummy Bears for less than $3, went to the small buffet in the market which had a great selection and it was all tasty for about $10 including a can of soda. I would love to go back here and explore more. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to stay long but it was great looking around and finally seeing this place.
A great place to go for any taste of food or to shop. I take the kids here when we're out and about and it's minutes away from Independence Mall.

Terrible service, 3 times in a row at this location. Never had issues prior to this and mistakes do happen, however it's the stank a** attitude of the workers in the a.m. On this final incident, my order was incorrect 3 times! LOL idk if they're trying to be smart or if the comprehension level is that low! I'll eat at my regular location going forward.

This is a fun place if you are a foodie and need to buy supplies, at the same time its full of shops and Kiosks where you can eat and drink while you shop. If you are visiting Philly its a must, perfect day to spend an afternoon.

This place is never open.  I haven't had a chance to try the pizza because they seem to be closed every afternoon.  I am standing there now at 1:25 pm on a Tuesday afternoon.  According to their sign, this place should have been open at noon.

Reading Terminal Market is an absolute must whenever you're in the city of brotherly love. Being from Florida, we don't have anything close to this. When I'm in town I always make it a point to stay at a hotel that is right across the street from here lol. 

It's a large market and there is plenty of space to move around even when it's crowded. They literally have anything and everything that you could want here. 

There are butchers, restaurants, produce stores, a chocolate store and so much more. Not to mention this is where Bassett's the oldest ice cream shop in the country is located. You have to stop there and get an ice cream, no excuses lol.

There are two places here that I hit up religiously. The first one being Dinic's for a roast pork sandwich. Omg it is so fucking good. There is nothing else like it. Their other sammies look great as well, but I never deviate from the roast pork.

The second spot that is a must is Beiler's bakery located in the corner. It's a Pennsylvania Dutch bakery and it's fucking unreal. You can watch them make everything from scratch throughout the day. There is always a long line, but it moves quick. I'd say their bagels are better than the ones that you get in New Yuck. The star of the show here though are their Amish pies and their doughnuts. My favorite doughnut they have is the Apple fritter. If you're lucky enough to get one fresh out of the oven, you'll never be able to eat another fritter from anywhere else lol. 

All in all, Reading Terminal Market is a great spot that has anything that you, or your group would want to eat. That's the beauty here, there isn't a reason to argue over where to eat. Everyone can do their own thing and be happy. You don't have to be like me when I'm in town and come in on the daily, but you have to come at least once and experience it.

THIS PLACE IS A MUST GO, MUST SEE, MUST EXPERIENCE . . . 

I have moved to Denver, CO, but I am back in Philly visiting family and enjoying the Philadelphia Flower Show. An experience downtown is not complete without a trip to Reading Terminal Market. I would love to find a market like this in Colorado, no luck yet. If any Yelpers have any recommendations I am totally up for the suggestion. 

The Reading Terminal Market has everything you could every want, meat counters, fish counters (shrimp the size of your head - no joke), book stores, gift shops, mexican, thai, chinese, ice cream (yummo), crepes, grocery type stores for fresh produce (prices to die for - so low), chocolate, gourmet little treats and everything else you can imagine. 

This place can be very crowded so if your not into crowds this is not the place for you. If your like me and could spend hours just looking around and finding anything unique or new to try then this is the place to go. 

Take a trip downtown and experience the Market!

Reading Terminal Market was fantastic! Tons of food options. Just a visitor of Philly and I really enjoyed this place. I wish I had more time to visit. We got some cookies from the general store in the back and they were great!

Brunch was a pleasant surprise and treat. The service was good and staff was knowledgeable of the menu. However, I must say I was disappointed. I ordered the pancakes and found them to be quite lacking. The pancakes were kind of dry and reminded me more of flat cornbread that wasn't very sweet. I love pancakes and was quite disappointed. The hype of industry did not live up to the buzzing I have heard.....

It should be said that this is the 3rd iteration of a Middle Eastern restaurant in this location. This 3rd seems to have similar offerings to that of the last 2, but I hope this one finds success where the other 2 didn't.

I have been here 4 times. A couple of times I came during their opening week where the $3 special had this place filled to capacity. A nice-sized line outside the door attracted quite a bit of curiosity for a high-traffic area, so I am sure they capitalized in a major way. I enjoyed the bowl option more that week than the roll I got. The roll was so thin and scant on meat that I didn't feel full. 

My returns the last 2 times have been pretty good. I had the bowl last week and today ordered another roll. At first I was expecting another skinny pita roll, but I have to say they were more generous than they were the day of their special. I can only imagine now that they don't have to ration to hundreds of people, they can fill up regular customers a bit better. 
You can still get a decent chicken and rice bowl (minus the multiple toppings and sauce options) right from the cart adjacent to Naya, but this place is on par with the pricing for the area, so if you're OK with spending roughly $10 minimum, then go for it.
Hands down, the best spot to go while in Philly! The food is incredible and the shops are fun!

Awesome place, so much variety!! Reminds me of the markets in Italy
I buy all my groceries from here but also bring my family and friends for brunch when they're visiting from out of town.
The only con I have about the place is that it's super crowded sometimes, especially on Sundays.

A must stop if you are visiting Philly!  Food galore.  A wide variety of smells that can lead you to taste testing across this huge space.  So many choices you must visit over several days.  The crepe station is delicious with fruity, sweet, and savory choices.  I tried the lemon grand marnier.  I had a Hawaiian passion juice from Seasons Juice Bar.  Many in expensive choices.  I spent less than $11 on 2 things.  Stop by the old school candy vendor.  I did this in the 1st visit.  My 2nd day I stopped by the Soul Food restaurant.  I'm from
New Orleans so I know food and this was good.  Greens and fried chicken were amazing! Market closes daily at 6pm.

What a fun place and a must-go for anyone coming through Philly! I had a conference near the convention center and my hotel was around there so I was luckily able to get to Reading Market every day very easily! Would definitely recommend- but very crowded over the weekday lunch hour- I could barely walk through the aisles. I had gone back on Thursday and Friday around 4 pm and this was a much better time for me to go and wander the stalls and have a look at everything without feeling rushed. There is definitely something for everyone here- vegan, Chinese, thai, your typical Philly Cheesesteak, great desserts and wonderful cookies and baked goods!  Everything was pretty affordable as well.

New lunch spot alert! Naya has opened quite conveniently near many office buildings in center city! It's similar to Cava if you've been there- fast casual, build your own bowl of Mediterranean goodness. You pick a base (greens or rice), a protein (options for vegetarians and meat eaters alike) and then toppings (diced tomatoes, pickled radishes, red onion, hummus, babaganoush, garlic whip, the list goes on). They also have other items like sandwiches if you don't want to build a bowl. 

I wandered by Naya on their grand opening and they were promoting with $3 bowls! The line was long but worth waiting for. I had a bowl with a mixed green base and roasted cauliflower. It was seasoned with turmeric, and was really delicious. I also really enjoyed the toppings I added, specifically the pickled vegetables. Next time, I would definitely opt to try the falafel! Only complaint is that they did not have whole wheat pita! 

While they do have some seating, this place seems like it will draw a big takeout lunch crowd, so you may want to leave some time to wait in line during your lunch break! Also, they do have some premade items you can grab to go!

This place is awesome!  As a former area resident, it is one of the best places to get your Philly fix.  I won't list every favorite shop, because I don't have that long, but I'm a huge fan.  Just go - eat there and buy some goodies to take home.  I did, and I had to get on a plane to go home.  Frankly, I think TSA is used to it and probably jealous.

Yo Philly - the Terminal is the best!

I wish I could just take a larger shopping cart into this place and wheel everything home!  There is something for everyone here, all fresh made!  I have such a hard time deciding what to get every time we go!
I only wish there was a place like this closer to home!
Obviously a staple to Philadelphia. A must go and also a locals gem. The juice stand is the best! Can't go wrong eating anything here. Also great for fresh shopping

My favorite place to go to eat in Philadelphia. Individual vendors sell every style of food and I spend half my time exploring what interests me that day.
Furthermore, you can find local flavors to taste or give to others. A one stop shop and historic.

I can't believe I've never reviewed Reading terminal market. It's one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. One stop shop for all your food needs. Now every city should have a food market like this where you can eat local food from local vendors. I've been going here for years. They have plenty of fun eat in or carry out places. Most of the restaurants do not have their dedicated seating area. There's a common area which can get packed over the weekends. There's plenty of food options like Greek, Mediterranean, Cajun, Italian or even Philly local roast pork sandwich. Eat at the Amish places to discover local food culture. You can even buy fresh produce, meat and seafood, bread and cheese here. 

If you live in Philly, I'm sure you've been here. If you're visiting, make sure you add this as a must visit spot during your time here.
Had the Thai salmon curry bec it has a lot of great reviews - was not impressed. My friend had the Shrimp poboy; it was delicious. Spicy beef jerky is amazing, ended up buying a half pound jerky.

In my opinion, Reading Terminal Market lives up to the hype. It's worth checking out if you are visiting Philly. It's pretty overwhelming (but in a good way). There is so much to check out. The indoor market has a wide variety of vendors and food stations. 

In terms of food stations, my favorite one is the Cajun Po'Boy one. Also, whenever I go to Reading Terminal Market, I always visit the Amish vendors and check out their jellies and honeys. 

You can also eat inside the market. There are a number of tables, but seating can be hard to find during busy times of the day. 

I highly recommend Reading Terminal Market! Go check it out when you are in Philly.

I love this place!! A food lovers paradise. Hungry??  Want to eat?? You will hurt yourself trying to figure out which of the dozens of places here to try. Of course, there are plenty of places to buy food to cook at home as well. Seafood, fruits, vegetables, meats, cheese, it's all here in one giant madhouse!!  
       Of course, it's always good to come at times that aren't as busy.  Craving dessert?? Termini's, Beilers, Bassets Ice Cream. For the love of God, if you weren't diabetic when you came in, you will be by the time you leave!!!  Keep in mind that while Sundays seem a little quieter, that's because all the Amish vendors aren't here!!  I wouldn't recommend missing Beilers and their amazing baked goods!!  
      If there is one downside, it's the parking. As in most of Philly, parking is an abomination!! your best bet may be to find the closest lot and park there. This way you can take your time inside without worrying about rushing out for the time limit on the street parking.

So many choices, so many choices! Where do I even begin?!? Came here for the first time ever during Jury duty (even though I've been living here for ages!!! lol) and was completely overwhelmed. They have everything that you can think of...asian, italian, sweets, american, etc etc etc. You have to go here if you ever visit Philly. If you are a huge fan of food like myself, you would want to purchase everything! You probably have to go back everyday you're in town (and even if you did, you wouldn't have been able to still try everything)

Going back this weekend for the festival (yes..they always have stuff going on here)

My boyfriend and I were out and about and decided we wanted to get a pizza for dinner. Sure enough, Pizza Shackamaxon was right across the street, so it seemed like the perfect opportunity to give it a try. 

If you're just walking into the shop, you can only buy pizza by the slice, otherwise you have to reserve ahead of time. However, the gentleman working behind the counter was kind enough to make an exception of us and allowed us to order a whole pie for take out. Within 30 minutes, we got a fresh pie. 

The pizza itself is some of the best I've ever had in Philly. One aspect we love about this place is the fact all of the ingredients are very fresh. They use freshly grated cheese instead of the processed stuff that comes in industrial size (there was literally a guy behind the counter grating a huge block of cheese). You can also taste fresh tomato chunks in the sauce. The crust has a nice crispy outer layer with a thick, chewy center. The center had the consistency of freshly baked bread. 

If you're looking for a pizzeria that prioritizes the use of fresh ingredients, this is definitely worth checking out!
Everything you could ever want! Local veggies, good food, fresh cheese, and much more

This. Place. Rules. They have literally everything you could think of. The best and most unique food options. Philly in general probably has the best food of anywhere I have lived... and I have really moved around a bunch! I seriously think of moving back sometimes just because I miss this place, and Ralphs Italian! :'(

I love the fresh foods and fresh desserts .
I went to the Reading Terminal just to get some desserts.

Redding Terminal has everything! Its usually very crowded but worth the trip! They also have lots of homemade items that are great for gifts! The fudge booth is amazing! And they have lots of fresh fruit and veggies!

Loved this place! So glad we found it on our vacation. So nice that we went both days. This place was fun to explore and had everything you could want as a tourist. If I'm ever back in Philly you can rest assured that I'll be here again. The lines go fast so don't let that deter you from trying whatever you want. The lines mean the food is worth it!

They definitely need more seating here but Reading Terminal Market is a must-see (or must-eat) when you visit Philly.

There's so many different things to see/try/taste and Reading has it all. We ended up getting a pulled pork sandwich here and it was sooo good. While I wish there were more options for seating (we ended up eating standing up) I'd definitely come back here. 

Considering it's relatively easy to get in and out of on foot, you can stop by here for breakfast or lunch on your way to and from the landmarks that you may be visiting. There's also a designated Lyft/Uber pickup spot too.

As a college kid, it's hard to find healthier places to eat with decently affordable food. As a student on Temple's campus, I find that Honeygrow is a delicious option. I go on a pretty regular basis and took a few friends this time. 
We all used the mobile app, and I gave my friends a referral code through the app. I ordered a stir fry with egg white noodles, tofu, sesame garlic sauce, bean sprouts, broccoli, peppers, and some garnish. For around 8-11 dollars, I think Honeygrow is a decent bang for my buck. The stir fry boxes are packed with noodles, and they generally keep me full for hours. I also like that the mobile app makes it easy to order ahead and pick up. My friend who was pretty new to Honeygrow also enjoyed her food. She ordered a stir fry with egg white noodles, beef, sweet soy five spice sauce, a ton of veggies, and some various garnished. 
Overall, I'm pretty satisfied with the Temple University Honeygrow. I've had a few order errors before, but for the most part, the taste, quality, and price of my food keep me coming back. It's a delicious, healthy, mid-range price option on Temple's campus.

A must for anyone visiting Philadelphia.  Something for everyone. Carmen's has a vegan cheesesteak which is really good and you can load it up with all kinds of toppings which makes it even better.  Love the mint lemonade from the middle eastern deli, the Amish bakeries are amazing and it's so cool watching their old world traditions. Also the pickle stand (also Amish) is so good!  Duck noodle soup at Sang Key with their homemade chili oil is BOMB. The salads at the Greek deli (next to Carmen's) are delish. Seriously it is all so good.

Honestly there are too many places to call out as favs so just go and see for yourself. You won't be disappointed!! I've been here 50+ times and I always try and hit up RTM when I'm philly. So many choices it never gets old and never disappoints!

Very overwhelming lol. This place had literally everything you could ever want. All kinds of different cuisines in one place. Never take a woman here! Lol. I was so confused as to what to get. I wandered around the same places a good 3 times before i decided on the roast pork  sandwich from dinic's. I saw this sandwich on the food network and decided to try it out. I got it with broccoli rabe, sweet and spicy peppers and Swiss cheese. My first bite was like ehhh.. it was a huge sandwich first, second it just tasted like it needed more seasoning on the meat. But after a couple bites, you get the full sandwich and it was pretty good. I finished half because it was a huge sandwich! But i would come back here foR sure. They're a couple placees i wanteD to try. But, you can only do so much when you're full lol. Check pics below

The market is an experience that anyone traveling to philadelphia should try. The lines for more popular places can get a bit long so be prepared to wait. But the market has everything you can think of, it's a great place to try new things or try traditional Philadelphia staples.

I got 6 meals for $15 because I used my friends code to get $45 off of a meal plan. My coupon code/ discount code is AWHI-JR9, if you want $15 off of a meal and $45 off of a meal plan when you order on the app. Please note the code doesn't work in store. 

Now about the bbq chicken. 

The corn was good. The chicken was just ok. The bbq didn't taste like anything. And the veggies were basic. I won't be ordering it again. 

The shrimp scampi is still the best thing I've ever had from them. And I suggest everyone get it. I'll be getting that at least once/week. There food is normally very flavorful but his was incredibly bland.

I just ate at Naya for the first time today, and I was blown away. The quality of the food cannot be beat. It seemed really fresh, it tasted great, and the beef is grass fed! The line moves pretty quick, and the staff provides good customer service. The restaurant is spacious, and seems to have a lot of seating (especially in the summer, when there is still outdoor seating). It is a little expensive for lunch, but the amount of food (and the deliciousness) is worth it. Another plus is that you can add as many toppings as you want at no extra cost. Definitely a place that I will return to for lunch!
Lots to of places to eat.  The place just does not seem too clean to me.  It is very popular.  Anything you feel like eating is here.

One of the touristy place to visit in Philadelphia. I still haven't been able to thoroughly explore this place, which shows that this place has much to offer. They have variety of stores ranging from souvenir gift shops to chocolatiers to food. It's fun just to walk around.
When visiting Philly, Reading Terminal is a must see. Arrive earlier in day to beat some crowds however, various shops, eateries and attractions for every one to enjoy!
Lot of options and great local flavors. Avoid 12 to 1 that being busiest time of the day. My favorite is fresh local produce at decent prices.
My in-laws are Filipino and this taste just like their cooking! Food game out hot and delicious. Such a great place to visit if you're in Philly.
Unique food market.  Packed with all different types of eats!  Great variety and good quality.  The area was a little congested and it could have been a little cleaner.  Worth visiting!

I came here because I had a friend who was a huge fan of this place and wouldn't stop raving about it. The pizza itself was excellent. I got a white slice and a slice of tomato pie, and both were really good. The crust was pretty thin on the regular slice (which I like). The tomato pie was warm and delicious, and I'm not usually a huge tomato pie fan. 

The actual process of getting the pizza was a little bit odd...the white slice was ready to go, but the tomato pie was just going in the oven (last pie of the night around 7:30pm), so we ate the other slices while waiting for the tomato pie to come out. We ended up basically like pre-paying and "reserving" our slices from the last pie of the night, and we came back into the store once they were ready. 

I didn't mind the scenario per se because I was with a group of friends, and it was nice enough weather to sit outside while we were waiting for the pizza. There isn't any indoor seating though, so I can imagine this being a difficult process in poor weather. I would definitely come here again, but I would call to pre-order if that's possible.
All I have to say is this place is FOOD HEAVEN. It's probably one of the top 5 tourists "hot spots" in Philly. I can't point out any specific vendor and food stand because it's all DA BOMB!!

What a place, the ultimate food court! Actually food court is such a backhanded compliment, Reading Terminal is so much more than that. It's a conglomoration of cultures and foods that have been blended together to create a high energy atmosphere! I really enjoyed the different sites and sounds you'd see around every corner. From cajun, to chinese, delis, BBQ, or Amish markets, Reading has got it all!

Just a sampling of the places I went included:

Dutch Eating Place
Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe
Golden Bowl
Sang Kee Peking Duck
Beck's Cajun Cafe
Hunger Burger

I'd recommend all of these, however don't get the chicken pot pie at Dutch Eating Place becuase it's not chicken pot pie and really some weird Amish concoction that's posing as it. Otherwise, this place has so much to offer!

Rude, disorganized, no accommodation to sit and enjoy your food bites. It's a shame because the foods are definitely the best of the area,  just can't get near them without being molested. I  won't go back.

This review is because of the lack luster customer service being provided today. 6/24/19. They are busy doing stuff that isn't needed at the moment when they have customers waiting to order.. Super slow service, but the salad was fine.

This place was so cool. We were first recommended to go here by our Uber driver, and as we have never been to Philadelphia before, we didn't realize what this was. But it so happens that it was directly across the street from my hotel, so we went to check it out. So cool. It reminded me a bit of Eataly in New York City and other places where you can see several vendors and get various foods all in one, cool, eclectic place. I definitely suggest a visit.

This could be one of my favorite places so far since moving here. Their kati rolls are amazing. The bread is light and fluffy but not too doughy and filling. I've tried the masala paneer and chicken rolls. The thin sliced red onion adds a nice sweetness and texture. The masala is a perfect balance of sweet, savory, and spicy. The white sauce really compliments the roll. I have to resist the temptation from coming here everyday.

Yesss. All the foods.
So many choices that you can't show up here and not find something you want to eat. 
Not at all as pricey as all the high end food malls like we have in NYC.
Definitely a must visit while in town!

The signs of a great market are as follows: local produce (and flavorful), good bazaar (and fun), and really (really) delicious food (and famous!). When there's more than 250 food dealers and countless of tempting (not so calorie-conscious), as well as few healthy choices under one roof, from Hershel's reuben, Beck's mac n' cheese fried balls, to Beiler's maple bacon doughnut, I bet you can't stop eating at just one stall. Luckily, you can always come back for more.  P.S: Don't forget your Tums

What a tourist might pick:
- DiNic's: Roast Beef and Pork. ( Winner of best sandwich in America'12)
- The Original Turkey: The Stuffin' Cranberry. ( All-year-round Thanksgiving)
- Beck's Cajun Café: Train Wreck.

What a local might pick:
- Flying Monkey Bakery: Pumpple. (2 pies in 1: a pumpkin pie and an apple pie)
- Dutch Eating Place: Scrapple breakfast sandwich.
- The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company. ( $1 cookie holler before closing )

What I might pick:
- Meltkraft:  Valley Thunder Grilled Cheese.
- Beck's Cajun Café: Shrimp & Chicken Gumbo. 
- Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties: Chicken Shawarma. 
- Iovine Brothers Produce: Local fruits & vegetables. (10% discount on Wed. and Sun. for all students and Jefferson ID employees) 


Pro tips:
1/ Take your kids, they'll love Philbert the pig: Reading Terminal Market's mascot. 
2/ Get $4 parking validation with a purchase of $10: Two hours limit, and valid only for two assigned garages: 11th & Arch Streets (Expert Parking), 12th & Filbert Streets (Parkway Garage). 
3/ Amish vendors aren't at RTM on Sundays.
4/ Free WiFi access.

Five Yelps.
This place has an overwhelming selection of products. Lots of fresh cheeses and desserts. I recommend a visit if you like markets. Definitely a cool place to visit if you're in Philly.

A friend recommended this place and we stopped by for quick snack kinda meal. Not a very huge selection in the menu but whatever they got is really good. It's got a very indie feel to it with limited seating. Even the drinks were exactly how they should be. Not too sweet and viscosity was right on point. Achari Paneer roll was the best with perfect combination of tanginess and spice. Mix veg Kati roll was little on a sweeter side because of carrots and peas but wasn't bad either. Their yogurt sauce on the side makes the flavor pop and is perfect with any Kati roll. Red chilli sauce is very hot but still good. Overall, a quick stop n go place but if you are in this area, it's a must visit. Ratings
Achari Paneer - 5/5
Mix Veg - 4/5
Mango lassi - 5/5
Chaas - 5/5

Well, with over 1000 reviews and still carrying a 4.5 star rating, (a tough feat to accomplish on Yelp) there isn't anything I can say differently that would convince you to visit this market. 

This is the ultimate foodies' paradise in the Philly area and deserves all the accolades.

Just go and enjoy!

For my 400th review, I'm dedicating all of this little white space to the Reading Terminal Market.

Go to Philly.

Find your niche.

Raw, pure honey. Check.

Quality, local wines.  Check.

Home-style wings.  Check.

Donuts.  Doughnuts.  Check.

Pulled pork.  Check.

This place will appeal to any and every sense.

Global cuisines.  American eats.  Local crafts.  Wild herbs.  Fresh. Fresh. Fresh.

I am a Libra.  I cannot choose.  Variety anxiety.  That's a new one I just made up.

Self-diagnosis.

Sigh.

I'll be back in a few months.
Can get a little touristy so best to go on the weekdays if dealing with crowds is not your thing. Great produce section and love the new resturant Fox and Son...amazing corndogs and funnel cakes!
Love the variety! A bit overcrowded on the weekends, be prepared!

Yummm. This place is amazing ! I got an order of lumpia and pork sausage with rice/egg and veggies. I waited for a bit to get my food but it looked so delicious once it came out :) the lumpia is crispy and perfectly fried. The pork sausage was delicious and filling. The garlic rice was garlic goodness. The soft-boiled egg was perfection. The whole dish was great and super filling. Im glad I chose this place out of all the options at the food hall. Prob one of the best meals I've had in awhile :) can't wait to come back and try more food items !

Please forgive me I am a Philadelphian not overly fond of the Reading Terminal Market. We stopped there last week to have a quick bite and maybe it's the sound of the people, or crowds whatever but my turkey sandwhich wasnt worth the headache or price...
The bathrooms are clean..good thing

I wish I could go there everyday so many things to choose from fresh meats and the chicken is so fresh you can see the difference the it looks. I love the Jamaican restaurant there food is delicious and the produce place is so cheap

Took a visiting friend who is a gardener as well as a foodie here for lunch, and his eyes fell out of their sockets for the second time. A real operating market is a rarity; only a few dozen cities in the country boast one that is authentic and not full of contrived or chain enterprises. A feast for the senses including the eyes. We were able to have a tasty seafood lunch at Pearl's and shop fresh for an equally delicious dinner that night at home.

Love Love Love This Place!!! I love try all kinds of foods.This Place has it all from soul to junk food.Want to try different cheese or excellent pastries Try out Termini Bros now That's a piece of heaven!

Lots of fun to walk around and sip coffee and enjoy all the colors and smells and sounds. A good place to look and taste. I walked around in the morning and got breakfast and then got my coffee to go and went to all the little shops around looking for treats for the family.

A great place with a lot of great food. And with a great price. You can get coffee, bakeries, Chinese food, American, Italy, etc. Try the ice cream on the winter, And donuts with coffee. Buy some snacks or vegetables, You can do a lot of things inside. Only its hard to find parking lots on weekend and the place gonna be too crowded. Better go on weekdays

Always popping with energy and full of diverse options and delicious food.  Oh how much I appreciate the delicious fresh juice and veggie drinks, produce, and myriads of options.

This place exemplifies Philly and I would argue is the heart of Philly.

Great place for the whole family. Closes a bit early so it's more of a day trip. Take the bus it's significantly easier than finding parking. There's a grocery store inside, some clothes, and plenty of specialty foods to ensure everyone gets what they want.
I love everything Reading Market has to offer. The food, the people, the energy, the fresh herbs.

HOW TO VISIT RTM RIGHT/HOW TO TAKE OUT OF TOWNERS TO RTM in 11 easy steps

1. Do you/your friends hate crowds? Forget it. Just don't even try. I brought extended family here and they got so overwhelmed we left and they decided it would be a good idea to go to Field House for cheesesteaks. A part of me died that day.

2. Is it Sunday or Monday? Go home. That's where the Amish are, and you don't want to miss them.

3. Now that you/your normal friends are psyched for the experience, enter, be amazed, and maybe take a lap or two around to work up an appetite. 

4. Stop at DiNic's for the Best Sandwich in America talk about how this was on Man vs Food. (Roast pork, broccoli rabe, sharp provolone.) It's worth the line. Split it between at least two people. You're gonna need to save room. (Maybe let other friends get what they spotted/are in the mood for, too, if they're being good. I hear the Rib place, Meltkraft is great fancy grilled cheeses, and Hershel's is always good for some giant deli brisket/pastrami/corned beef sandwiches.)

5. Go to Termini Brothers. Get a cannoli. Look across the aisle at the other chocolate place. Talk about how weird chocolate covered onions are and how awesome chocolate cheesesteaks are (once you realize there's no cheese or steak in there).

6. Go to Bassett's. Get ice cream from oldest ice cream company in America.

7. Hit up 4th Street Cookie Company. Get cookies.

8. Go to Amish guy. Try juice samples. Buy some juice.

9. Go to Tubby Olive, try lots and lots of olive oils and vinegars. Buy a little bottle for whoever is the unlucky person who did not take this trip to Philadelphia with your friends.

10. Get some cheese from some cheese counters for later. Ask them what type of cheese to get.

11. Get some produce from Iovine's for later. If it's Wednesday (or Sunday, but it shouldn't be: See #2), use your student ID for a discount.

ENJOY PHILLY!
I love it one of the best places u can go to In Philly n still see some of the old culture n the food is amazing n it one of my favorite place in Philly

love love love The Reading Terminal!!!! So many vendors to choose from Fresh everything!!! The Amish vendors are my favorite besides Martin's. The sit down and eat vendors have some great food also. Pack your patience it can get very crowded in the Reading Terminal but the wait is worth it!!! Enjoy!!

If you only have time to see one place in Philly, this is it. Almost everything here is absolutely delicious. Ice cream, donuts, pretzels, chocolate body parts, cheesesteaks, all of the Philly classics and then some. 

Everything here is fabulous - I only wish it stayed open later. Make sure to get there early if you're planning to go for dinner since they usually close at 6:00 pm. If you are on a limited timeline, I would highly recommend stopping by for breakfast to get crepes, donuts, and coffee. The lunch and snack options are really good too, but the donuts are just a must try. I even prefer them over Federal Donuts. They stuff and ice them fresh on an assembly line for you to watch while you wait to order. 

The best approach to managing the chaos of this place is to just get something from everywhere and split it with other people. Every vendor is there for a reason - because people love them! You truly can't go wrong with anything you pick.

I read about this place couple of months ago when I moved to PA, and since then wanted to try it out. Wanted to know if it good as the Kati Roll Company in NYC! Please go and have food! It is AMAZING! I had the chicken pepperwala for lunch and the flavors are on point! Not less not more! It was perfect amount of everything inside! I came back after work to get take out, hopefully rest of the food is just as amazing! Definitely give this place a try, you will not be disappointed!

Man 
I can't say enough about the Reading Terminal Market!
I have lived in Philadelphia all my life..except like most, if I may vacation at the JERSEY Shore..Wildwood..
I have to insist that if you are around Center City Philadelphia...you most definitely bring your appetite and any extra money for food , that you might want to whip into a sensational meal, like Lasagna with handmade Sausage and 
Country fresh from the Amish, a beautiful salad and flower arrangement of such beauty that you steal the show .
And almost like Disney world, you might not be able to get everything done in a day..
So if fortunate enough to have at least lunch with a friend and a homemade smoothie kale and all.. homemade one at a time veggie burgers and the line can get long as it's well worth the wait! 
Hit the Reading Terminal cheese shop.
Turn around and grab some cannoli ! 
Or a butter slathered homemade Amish pretzel, served to you by the real Pa Amish country , originals who drive and commute towards the end of THE week...
And hustle from the break off day, till the sun hides away for yet another day...
Do not be left out! 
Don't leave Philadelphia, and say, oh GOD we didn't have a chance to see"the Philadelphia Mayor eating a pulled pork, or even a 50yr+ recipe for a crab cake to die for! 
The Reading Terminal Market is not a landmark to be missed! 
Philly girl "Maggie Razzi"
Love the Reading Terminal! Whether shopping for fish heads or just picking up a hoagie, a Philly must.

I love this place so much. They have all sorts of food options and I love just walking around and browsing. It can get crowded at times but it's such a fun experience. I definitely recommend it for people as a fun to-do in philly. I spent a good 1-2 hours just walking around and browsing. My favorite place is the ice cream by the exit/entrance right now but there's just so much good stuff to try in there!

I can see why RTM was rated the best market in the country.  With what feels like a 100 different food options each vendor could be hit or miss but after tasting many different foods it felt like more vendors were 5 star than "not worth the calories".

Public bathroom was clean, there are even RTM employees to help you find your way as you'll inevitably become lost in the various rows of food vendors, seating areas and flows of people walking here and there.

I love this place so much. If I lived or worked in center city I doubt if I'd eat anywhere else. The selection is just awesome. There are cold and hot sandwich places, buffet style, Cajun, Asian, Indian , Mediterranean, soul food, Italian, pastas, bakeries, seafood and market, coffee shops and butcher shops.

Can't say enough...you just have to go and see for yourself.

This place is a great "neighborhood" bar.  The drinks are well made and pretty strong.  Great beer selection.  Small enough that you can see a TV from wherever you are.  Bartenders are nice.  Crowdis eclectic and mostly friendly.  I'm a fan.  My girlfriend lives around the corner, so I could get used to this place.

I've had a few of the appetizers, but never any real food.  Chips and fries, both of which were very tasty.  I really want to taste the "staff meal" ... really neat idea.

I plan to update this review once I have some food.
I love the Reading Terminal for pretty much everything. I get most of my veggies from here. The $1 Grab bags are the best.

I love Reading Terminal. My husband and I live in Philadelphia, and have many options for food shopping. Reading Terminal feels special. We get our favorite foods and get to see the people that grow, butcher, curate, etc. with so much pride for what they do. When we move to the burbs, we will certainly be back for trips to Reading Terminal Market.

I loved this place bc I love variety and food. I ate from DiNic's [Italian pulled pork sandwich - I think it was $9/11?] and Bassetts Ice Cream [$5 for 2 scoops of featured ice cream in a cup] -- I recommend!

There were stores for food, kitchen tools, soap, tea, books, flowers, etc. So many things to see and feel and smell.

You can find cuisines from all over the world in this covered market. If you have dietary restrictions you can easily find some gluten free, vegan or dairy free options. The place was really packed when we visited on a Saturday in the middle of October at around 1:30 PM, but it was mostly people waiting in line for their food, not people walking around the market. It is a nice place to buy souvenirs from your visit in Philly, and these sections are by far not as crowded. Definitely worth a visit especially if it is cold outside or a rainy day.

Love coming here :) so many goodies. It is very bustling so if you're one who doesn't like waiting in lines, you'll have to suck it up! It's definitely worth it! All the baked goods, cute crafts, food, snacks, fresh produce, and service are great! Definitely an awesome market to bring the family to and enjoy your time together. The choices here are endless! Definitely need to go back and try them all.

Reading Terminal Market is a fabulous place to ramble around shopping and sampling so many types of ethnic foods, drinks, spices and confections.  The market is large and bustling.  It always seems to be crowded but lines move fast and it is worth the wait in my experience.  Come hungry and with a pal so you can split portions and sample more delicious dishes.  You will find everything from fresh fruits and vegetables to fish, shrimp and oysters.
First time at the terminal.  Been living in Philadelphia for 14 yrs and never been inside.. Has great vendors that offers so many things! Can't wait to go back!

Great place to try authentic Philadelphia street foods! Prices vary by vendors and must try their Philly cheesesteak and pretzel ! Gets super busy at noon time for lunch but best time would be when they open@10am! Park near the convention center for easy access walking distance to RTM!

Big market place! It has many vendors from aged meat, seafood, fresh bread, coffee, asian fast food, sandwiches and much more.

It was really crowded and I'm talking about shoulder to shoulder crowded. If you decide to get something to eat the seats are very limited and there is definitely not enough seating. You might as well stand and eat.

One of our favorite places to visit in Philadelphia.  So many great food options. We are at many of the vendors over the course of several visits.  And everything was great.  Definitely try the donuts.  They are fabulous.

This place is interesting... when you walk in it looks really nice then you realize half of the people sitting down are junkies... while I was getting my drink one of them grabbed my hair and sniffed it. The staff refused to do anything about it. If you dare try to sit and eat you will be approached and asked for money, don't try to offer them food either because they will scream at you that they asked for money. Once again the staff did nothing. Real family environment for the family!!

Came to reading terminal on my visit to Philly. This place was really big and I liked how much food options they had, but it was way too over crowded. You could barely find seats here. There were options from asian to southern to indian. My girlfriend and I got the gumbo, the gumbo was actually really good. We only got one to share to try it at first and we wanted to go get it for the second time but the line grew to about 45 minutes. We ended up trying this indian food spot, but it wasn't as good. Apparently they have really good donuts here but never got a chance to try it.

I don't understand what the big draw here is!  I guess if you live IN the city, it's has many merchants in one place.  However, it's very crowded of course because it's in center city. 
 It is filthy.  The tables and chairs where you eat were disgusting.  The bathroom wasn't very clean either.  And these were only the areas you can SEE!  It's so busy and congested taht it makes me wonder about everything behind the counters.  Yikes!  The prices are extremely high.  If you live in an outlying county, there is absolutely no reason to go here.  There wasn't one thing in this place that I couldn't get in normal errands in Chester Co. and the places I would go would be clean.

**Five Stars**

I literally died and gone to food heaven once I stepped in here!  A definite place to put on your list if you are in the area.

If you don't know what to eat, come here - whether you have dietary restrictions, on a budget or just plain picky - there is something for everyone! From your typical Philly Cheese Steak, hoagie, Soul Food, Greek, Amish foods and breads, seafood, various fresh fruits, hot and fresh cookies, specialty donuts, homemade ice cream...the list goes on...literally something for everyone.

While some can compare the Reading Terminal to "The Grove" in Southern Cali, I would somewhat agree.  The Terminal however, seems to have such a historical significance and different feel once you step in.  

My only gripe is that it would be great if they were open longer. Busy peak times are during lunch, some vendors start cleaning up and closing shop at around 3:30ish and the entire market closes at 6pm.

Overall, highly recommended, you will not be disappointed.

I live in the Suburbs of Philadelphia and make it my business to frequent the Reading Terminal for Five reasons. The variety of Amish Fresh Meat, Bassett's Ice Cream, DiNic's, Hope's Cookies and Le Bus Bakery. If you love lots of choices in Flowers, Food, Candy, Produce, Fresh Meats and Fish, Some of the best Amish Baked Goods and a reason to visit the terminal then these are just a few "Great but Valid" Reasons.
