You cannot visit the city without stopping at the Reading Terminal for both the experience and what it has to offer (Which is A LOT!!!) 
Bon Appetite & Enjoy!!!

For those of you looking for the incredibly well done and tasty dishes like kaldereta, pork belly and lechon kawali you read about in early reviews, be warned. They're not there any more. When LaLo first opened, I just loved it. It was the only place in the Bourse I ate at. Now, they've scrapped their interesting, varied  street food menu for the generic protein + rice platters you get in bad Cantonese shopping mall restaurants. I was so disappointed. I guess they are trying to appeal to a wider clientele, but damn, LaLo, you lost this customer.
Best Chick-fil-A in the area. Consistent service, never have any issues there, friendly workers even when there's a million customers to tend to.

I love this place. It's often very crowded but that's probably the reason the food is always fresh. The fried chicken people are miserable so I never get their food. Shame though- I love fried chicken.
Best place to get what ever u want, you don't need any other store besides this place, food, groceries, did I say food !!!

I've got mixed feelings on RTM.  It's a great place to buy fresh produce for cheeps, plus I love the variety of cheeses, bread, handmade chocolates, and other goodies.   But when it's crowded -- which is basically all weekend --  it's a special piece of hell right here in Philadelphia.  I'll gladly pay the extra couple of $$ at Whole Foods to avoid that mess!

The takeout food is hit or miss.  Basic 4 Vegetarian has pissed me off more times than I can count by being closed during mealtime hours or simply out of whatever menu item I want.  The crepe place is okay, nothing special.  The Indian/ Pakistani place is excellent.  The juice bar is a refreshing treat.  Oh, and in case you are curious and/or drunk:  do not eat the sushi!!

This is a fun place to get some philly culture in a concentrated area! We tried Tommy DeNics and Termini Bros which both were excellent. They also have some nice handcrafted goods as well as groceries! It was raining when we came, making it a nice and convenient tourist attraction! Definitely worth a visit!

The devil is in the details. The Chick-fil-A deserves an outstanding review. I ordered the market salad
And my cheese was in a little container on the side. 
I am slightly lactose intolerant so I appreciate this very much.
My chocolate chip cookie was warm without me having to ask.

It brings me with quite disappointment that this Pizza place isn't quite what others have raved about. I was expecting an above 8 pizza. I'm from NYC and now living in Philly and finding a good Pizza place has been a mission. First off the place is very small as others stated so do plan to go. It's priced too high in my opinion. The smell was amazing and it looked very good, and I was hoping the taste would be equally as good. The crust wasn't crispy instead it was soft and flappy. The ends had way to much dough for my liking. The sauce wasn't that great, however their was a good portion of cheese. Overall the taste wasn't as good as I thought it would be. I recently went to Tacconelli's in port Richmond and was very impressed, and had the bar too high up thinking this place would be about the same or better. 
I definitely recommend Tacconelli's pizza first and it's cheaper too. I wouldn't come back here personally. Hope this helps

I'm very new to Indian food and really enjoyed it!! The spices are abundant and work super well together as I learned the chicken masala roll is a classic. 

The service was super quick and they were so patient with all of my questions since I don't know my way around an Indian menu. 

The kati roll was soft and similar to a tortilla wrap but a little thicker and possibly better. The chicken was pretty moist even after sitting in the fridge for a couple hours and having to be reheated. Also you get a GOOD amount of meat for $5.75. I will definitely be going back to explore more items!

We have to visit Reading Terminal Market each time we are in Philly. There is something for everyone to eat at this place. Our recommendation is to split a hot / homemade pretzel first and then make your decision on the other places to visit while at RTM. We also will split numerous orders so we can try a larger variety of the vendors. This place is a lot of fun.

This place was crazy on New Year's Eve. I highly recommend you not bringing your stroller here. Use a baby/toddler carrier if you can. 

I don't remember the name of the place but the beef jerky spot is hands down my favorite place to stop by.

Probably the best indoor market in the country.  You'll find every culinary group in SE PA represented here: Amish, German, Italian, Vietnamese.  Seating can be almost impossible, especially during lunch hour, if you're hoping to eat here.
Love it. A must for visitors from out of town . Right across from Jefferson Station go out the Western end.
I love this place! You can find a wide selection of great food and produce here. Everything is fresh and conveniently in the same place. I especially love the brisket sandwich here.
New location is nicer, staff is friendly but it literally took more than 10 minutes to get my iced coffee and there were very few people here.

It's the mother of all farmer's markets (opened in 1892).

Yes, it's true -- the selection is daunting and the aisles jam-packed with patrons. It's practically a stampede during lunch hour. It feeds the downtown crowd, the convention center, and bus loads of tourists. Everyone's coming because there's too much freaking good stuff! I tried to eat at every stand during my stay in Philly, but couldn't pull it off (got addicted to The Original Turkey). Get a map of the place and plan strategically. Definitely try something new like the Amish breakfast... unless you're Amish yourself... and somehow gotten on yelp.com...

Tips: Explore the market before or after lunch. Save room for Bassetts ice cream. Bring a tote bag if you plan to buy random knick-knacks or produce.

I was recently in Philadelphia and was staying not far from here. This is what an urban market is all about. There are numerous stalls with foods of all different types. Worth spending the time walking around to take it all in - some places have counter seating and there are also tables in key places throughout the market. You can also take a number of items to go. It will get crowded during lunch hours, so plan accordingly. I was grateful for having something this close by with a good variety of food since I was eating in between meetings. I will review a couple of the stalls I ate from as well - but this is definitely a place not to be missed in Philadelphia!
Beware of attacks by panhandlers.  I was here on business.  Why would anyone go here by choice?  Stay away for your own safety!

This place is amazing! There are so many different food selections to choose from and everything looks delicious. We stopped by for breakfast and had some crepes, croissants, smoothies and coffee and everything was amazing! The prices are great too. This is a stop that must be made if visiting Philadelphia. I wish they had a market like this one in Orlando, FL!

Awesome place to visit when in Philly!! There is a huge variety of vendors here serving all types of things from gyros, to cheesesteaks, to burgers to Chinese food. Fresh made donuts and chocolates are here to satisfy any sweet tooth. While each place has reasonably priced items, you can find yourself running up quite a tab because you will want to sample everything there is to offer here!

Stopped here while out for the day in Philadelphia as per the suggestion of a friend who is a Philadelphia local. I had the Italian pulled pork sandwich and it was exceptional. There really is something for everyone in here, the perfect spot to stop with all of your indecisive friends and at an affordable price too!

I can't even begin to explain to you how completely EPIC this place is.
It's a foodie's DREAM and if I lived in Philly, I would be there every. single. day.

Some of The workers didn't cover their nose with the mask, one (who looked in charge) did not even cover their mouth. There were no enforcement of the social distancing even though the stickers were on the floor. If you waited for previous customer to walk before ordering, they would rush you to take your order which pressured me to get too close. I come here often and service is usually great. But in these COVID 19 times, they have to do better. I understand it's a lot but if your going to be open, do it right.

It is literally a 45 minute process every time I go here. Then after standing in line for that lengthy period of time they try to be stingey with the food so you can ask for a normal amount and get charged for it. Drive the extra 10 minutes, and go to willow grove. You will save yourself a lot of aggravation.

It's definitely one of the best tourist attractions in Philly. Everyone who has visited Philly before recommended me to visit this amazing market.

We were here on a Saturday morning around 10am. I had a couple of restaurants in my list : one for Scrapple and the other for roast pork sandwich. I was lucky to try them both. Scrapple is a local Philly food made of all the scraps of a pig. It does not sound enticing but when cooked right it's extremely delicious. I had scrapple from Down Home Diner. This place is pretty crowded. I waited in line for 15 mins to get seated. I finally got my scrapple after 30 mins wait. Although people like it with maple syrup I personally prefer the ketchup. Roast pork sandwich at Dinic's sandwich place was really good too. 

Reading market is insanely huge. Walking around all these local restaurants can be overwhelming. They have almost every cuisine that you can imagine. I also found something that I actually wasn't looking for. Egg puffs at the Indian restaurant made my day. It's our local Indian savory food and it had been over 3 years since I had a egg puff. I was over the moon when I found it here. 

I definitely recommend you to go through the list of restaurants that are at this market because it's just a lot to go there and decide where you want to dine. 

For the unlucky ones who planned to visit this place on a Easter Sunday, I feel bad for them as the market was closed.

I really wish more cities had something similar to Reading Terminal Market. You can go in there and find just about any type of food you could want, and just about all of it is amazing!

Aside from great restaurants, there is a humongous selection of fresh produce, meats, seafood, cheeses, which could easily lead to hours of walking around in awe of your surroundings.

Definitely a must-visit when in Philly!
Larry Alvin is very accommodating and awesome! This honey grow is for sure the place to get amazing, delicious tasting food with wonderful customer service.

One of the best places and markets that I've been to a while. I've traveled across the world and food markets are always my top pick, and I have to say THIS ONE is probably the best. Yes, there're a lot of lines, but they go fast. It's an experience you won't forget!

Yelp keeps telling me I need to review.... okkkkk here it is. Short and sweet.

* Its crowed except after 4
* Locals are irked by tourist who just stop in the middle of the isle when we are trying to get our lunch and you are on vacation.
* You will get lost (Local and Tourist)
* Have cash, many places don't take cards, there are numerous ATM located around. 
* Its delicious you can get a cake, smoothie, ham hocks, chitterlings, flowers, fish, cannolis, oils, Thai, spaghetti, ice cream , Shea butter, preservatives, donuts and a book under one roof.

Enjoy!

Ahhhh one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. 

Whenever I need to escape the office and explore - this is the place I go. Whether I'm in search of food, cooking ingredients, or just something to make me laugh... this is the best place to start. 

I think the most refreshing part about this market is that it reminds me of the traditional shopping experience. The farmers markets! The various vendors each with their own specialty. 

Some of my favorite establishments include:

 - Fair Food Farmstand (organic, local produce)
 - Salumeria (greaaatt italian hoagies. you can also buy gourmet meats and cheeses)
 - 4th Street  Cookies (best cookies in the city! the chocolate chips are usually still melty!)
 - 12th Street Cantina (Mexican - pick up a frequent buyer card... i'm almost at a free meal!)
 - Old City Coffee (so many choices! roasted on premises.)
 - DiNic's (roast beef! brisket!)
 - Down Home Diner (order the bbq burger or the scramblers)

 ... I'm sure I'll have to update this....

The crowds can be overwhelming... but I don't mind. This place reminds me of Europe and I could care less about being swept up in the commotion. It's therapeutic to me.

Besides the wide range of vendors that they have here, they also hold cooking classes in their audience style kitchen. I came here during a free class and learned how to make cheesesteak spring rolls. This kitchen can also be rented out for private events! 

The Reading Terminal... Anything you want you can find it here.
Wow. Some of the best pizza I have ever had. We arrived on a Saturday night and ordered our slices just before they sold out for the night. So glad we got to try it! Would highly recommend.

600th review!

I have experienced food markets before in Baltimore and DC, but boy is Reading Terminal Market is on a whole other level.  I would describe it as a cross between a food court, a carnival, and Grand Central Station. Given the many options and people watching opportunities, I can see why it's an iconic Philly attraction that everybody talks about. Come for the food, brave the crowds, and have fun exploring!
Love it Here! The food is great and the Little shops have something for everyone! a Must if visiting Philly downtown!

The quality of the food was good but the portion size was definitely too small for comfort. The amount of protein given was extremely small and since the bowls themselves are small it is hard to mix everything together which I didn't like. 

I was really disappointed because I should have just stuck to cava. Cava has more options which i actually like although the proteins here seemed better if I were to receive more.

One of my favorite places in Philly! This Farmer's market provides a wide range of options inside, and is a place where locals can get groceries, meat and seafood, but also where everyone can have a meal. There are lots of choices of restaurants and cuisines, including Philly cheesesteaks, Chinese food, burgers, ice cream, smoothies, Middle Eastern food, and many others. This is a great place to visit when in Philly's centre.

Absolute perfection, this place makes pizza better than 99 percent of pizzerias in New York. The tomato slice is divine and the regular plain cheese is artistic, it looked beautiful and tasted just as good. The pizza was so amazing that I had more than two slices and wound up having no room for a cheesesteak.

An authentic Philadelphia experience. Some of the city's best food is located in this big indoor market. The environment is very casual in here, but you can find a mix of markers, diners, bars and specialty food and product shops.

One of the best parts of living in Philadelphia. Local, fresh, handmade- It's all here. RTM is a genuine marketplace, vibrant and alive. Get to see your city first hand bumping into each other and jostling your way around a buzzing market. Turn shopping into an adventure, support your local vendors and try something new. Reading Terminal is amazing.
Best place in the city for a meal, produce or dessert.

This past weekend my boyfriend and I went to the Bourse on Saturday around 2 pm. I ordered the Filipino beef stew (Kaldereta) which came with garlic rice. It was really flavorful and delicious. Plenty of chunks of beef but the overall dish was a bit on the small side. 

A while back I also tried the longanisa dog at a festival. It was also very delicious and I would like to try it again at the bourse to see what the actual portion size is like. 

The bourse is a really nice place to grab food and I'm glad to see places like La Lo here!

How can anyone give this place less than 5 stars.  You can buy some vegetables, have a beer, pick up spice to make dinner,grab some candy, and get some take out.  This place is always a stop you need to make if you are visiting Philadelphia.
Absolutely amazing. I've eaten at the Thai place and a sandwich shop and highly recommend both. Such a fun place to walk around and explore! Everyone should walk through if you get a chance!

For a taste of Philly, visit Reading Terminal Market. From the small value and premium grocers to butchers, restaurants, and craft stores there isn't a lot to go wrong with here. The sheer scale of options here makes it easy for everybody... the potential lines can make it a bit more difficult, so get there early.

Naya is a create spot for lunch or a quick bit. It's also healthy! It's similar to an assembly type food experience where you choose your carb base like rice. Then choose your choice of protein and veggies. I personally enjoyed the Naya bowl with chicken along with all of the different veggies.

The service was fairly quick and helpful when I had questions of what the items were. The atmosphere was really open and easy to understand the menu and options. The price was around $10 for a bowl and a bit cheaper for the burrito/wrap option. 

I plan to come again!

This is foodie heaven. 

An overwhelming amount of food vendors, ranging in all kinda of cuisines!!

Explore, bring your appetites, and enjoy!

The Industry is a great addition to the neighborhood. We went last week with a large party and enjoyed ourself for hours at Aaron's bar. Everything from the atmosphere, service, drinks, food & even the bouncer made it an rockin evening. Keep up the good work Industry peeps!

I tried the $5 deals today. Boneless hot buffalo wings and boneless teriyaki wings and bread sticks. The bread sticks were good. I see why the wings were $5 u get what u pay for. They tasted cheap. Like ribbed meat not white meat. Breading was over cooked. Borderline burnt taste. Nothing to right home about just average.

I love this place.  it's my grocery store, and my favorite lunch spot.  People of every race and social class go there to do their shopping.  It's Philadelphia at its best. Just don't go on Saturday or, if you can help it, when a convention is in town.  It is a tourist destination, and i'm ok with that.  I just have to plan ahead to avoid the worst times when people have to move single file through the aisles.  Monday morning is the best for grocery shopping, unless you want to go to the Amish stands.  They are open only later in the week and never on Sunday.  This may disappoint tourists, but they have to understand why the Amish stands are closed -- they have a life, and it's not all commerce, all the time.

We went here thinking it was Pizzeria Beddia but were told he closed and they took over. Pizza looked good so we tried it. And it was super duper tasty! We got a slice of each of their pies. They only make certain kinds certain days but unlike Beddia, they don't close when they run out of dough.. they just make more... Thank the pizza gods! Every slice was great. And the guys behind the counter were very nice and informative. Wish I was there now actually.
Yummy eatery excellent customer service. I even got a side of garlic rice. The customer service is also great!

I didn't actually get a chance to eat anything here because I was busy stuffing myself with pizza and Philly cheesesteak elsewhere, BUT I loved this place and would absolutely want to return. There are so many different places to eat here and it's both overwhelming and invigorating. Really an emotional rollercoaster as I wandered through the aisles - I was simply bewildered at how many delicious places there were to eat. The whole atmosphere is warm and lively, and this would be a really fun place to go with a group of people and try as much stuff as you can. They have literally every food type here and even a grocery store with extremely fresh looking meat and produce. Truly a foodie heaven and I really want to go back.
The best place in Philly to sample a wide variety of some of the city's best food! My go to place for lunch whenever I'm in the city.
I have nothing bad to say about this place all the food in this place is bangin and the customer service is good. I love the Reading Terminal

Addicting and delicious Filipino food. My favorite is the Bicol express which has a coconut base with ginger, tofu and veggies; another favorite is the lechon kawali. The lechon kawali is crispy and delicious with a side of dipping sauce. Other lechon kawali I have had in the past from other Filipino places just wasn't up to par to the crispiness. The garlic rice with all the meals pairs well with all the proteins.

We didn't feel like going out to eat and we ordered delivery. Food was very good, warm and flavorful!!! We also got extra sauce which was a plus. We ordered the chicken masala roll, chicken and lamb platter and the beef tikka roll. The chicken masala roll was the best. Perfect sauce to meat ratio.

A must visit when in Philly!!! So many food options to choose from...suggest you eat a little bit of everything and take a meal and dessert home. 
We started with the Peking Duck Rolls at Sang Kee, then Corned Beef Reuben Sandwiches. We took the 2 Roast Pork Sandwiches with Broccoli Rabe and Termini Brothers Bakery treats for home. 
Cannoli, Pizelles and Amaretti cookies...Yummy!
We are already planning our next visit to the Market in the Spring.

Probably the best on-the-go Indian food you'll find, which is great when you're craving Indian but don't want the hassle of: (a) an intense food coma, (b) having lots of leftovers, and (c) dawdling and dallying over a lengthy meal.

That was us yesterday, and so kati rolls were the ultimate solution. These babies delivered the goods in a vehicle made of naan. Create delicious food that I can pick up with my hands and I'm sold. Griddled naans gingerly swaddled tender seasoned chicken, paneer cheese, and potatoes. I chose the chicken masala for my first bite and followed it up with the paneer tikka. Both were bangin' and the naan was damn near flawless. The usually unwelcome red onion was welcomed with open arms. Because it totally worked here, gently accenting and amping the already-nuanced flavors with yet another awesome layer.

Realizing that we couldn't manage a third roll on our own, we split the aloo paneer, and it was tasty, but it was my least favorite. This could've been because my first and second were so amazing. Maybe I just don't love aloo that way.

I'll be back for sure. If I can divert my attention from the kati options, I might give the biryani a go, but I don't see that happening.

I do, however, see myself drinking their white sauce, a homage to ranch dressing, out of a plastic cup, though. Yikes!

The SO spent a week up in Philly a few months ago and when she asked her host for a place closeby to get some food she suggested the Reading Terminal Market.

You should really prepare before you hit this place.  Bring some money, perhaps a shopping bag, and be sure to wear stretchy pants.  Sweat pants are probably best!

The variety here is really just stunning, especially as we had no idea what this place was other than "a place to get something to eat" before we arrived.

This building is huge and is a wall-to-wall patchwork of different food vendors, and I'm not talking about the same old fast food franchises you're used to seeing.  I mean row after row of independent vendors selling any exotic food you can imagine.  It was really amazing.  I defy you to show up to this place and NOT find any kind of food you're looking for.

Yes, it's crowded.  Yes, it's full of tourists.  Yes, you're going to have to wait.  And oh my god is the food good!

I have recently given up meat, but was almost in tears as I saw the incredible pastrami sandwiches and gyros they were serving.  I ended up having an amazing vegetarian Indian dish from one of the stalls.  We also picked up some freshly made and freshly sliced sour dough bread from one of the bakeries.

This place is definitely worth a visit.  You should probably starve yourself before you go.

If you're a foodie, you will absolutely fall in love with this place.  Come here for a stroll - as quick as 15 minutes or as long as a couple hours.  This place is food heaven with a little bit of every cuisine (American, Thai, Greek, Mexican, etc.), butchers, cheeses, seafood, Dutch Goods, homemade goods, and much more!

We came here on a Saturday morning and loved the hustle and bustle of it all (tourists and locals).  A good amount of the prepared food stands were still not open and prepping for the day.  I didn't check out the pricing for a lot of the food stands, but I'm going to say its not going to be the complete cheapest place to buy stuff, but it also won't be the most expensive.  

*Restrooms, ATMs & seating available.
*If you have little ones, the stroller will be ok, but a tight squeeze in some areas.

Customer service is awesome! They never fail to impress me with their service here EVERRRYYY TIME I come! They're also quick to serve you and if they see you walking towards the trash can, they'd proceed to help you throw it out. Awesome fast food (:

At the time of writing this review, Reading Terminal Market (pronounced "Redding"), has over 5,100 Yelp reviews. That's a lot. It's easily one of the most-reviewed places I've visited. It's one of those popular "public" markets with a food hall and a bevy of vendors selling everything from fresh produce and flowers to handmade crafts and jewelry. A lot of big cities have them. Comparable markets include Chelsea Market in New York, the Ferry Building in San Francisco, and Pike Place Market in Seattle. In Atlanta, where I'm from, Reading Terminal Market ("RTM") reminds me most of Sweet Auburn Curb Market. New developments have popped up around the country in recent years that try to emulate a sort of old-school municipal market feel.

RTM is different because, unlike its newer counterparts, its atmosphere is genuine and not manufactured. The market opened in 1893, making it one of the country's oldest. Some of the market's vendors have been around since the very beginning, over 100 years, like Bassetts Ice Cream. You can find them just inside one of the 12th Street entrances on the west side of the market. This is where we entered.

This is a Philadelphia hot spot and one of the most recommended places for out-of-towners to go. We visited over the weekend and the market was crowded with tourists and locals alike. It should definitely be high on any foodie's Philly to-do list. There are so many food stalls here and the selection is eclectic, from Amish-style rotisserie chicken, sourced regionally, from Dienner's Bar-B-Q Chicken to Peking duck from Sang Kee Peking Duck (an RTM outpost of a Philly Chinatown favorite).

In all, there are over 80 vendors packed onto one floor. They're classified into the following categories: bakeries, beverages, dairy & cheese; housewares, books, crafts, etc; meats & poultry, Pennsylvania Dutch (note the PA Dutch vendors are closed every Sunday), produce, restaurants, seafood, and specialty foods. The market is laid out in a grid with four large aisles going north-south, and 11 smaller aisles going east-west. There are a handful of communal seating areas (almost all seats were taken during our visit), restrooms (clean enough), and an attended welcome booth if you'd like to pick up a map and/or ask for recommendations. Some of the vendors also have their own dedicated seating.

A few recommendations:

1. Roast pork sandwich at Tommy DiNic's Pork & Beef. Perhaps the most popular vendor here. They offer wraparound counter service.

2. Pretzel from Miller's Twist. These are fresh-made, Amish-style pretzels. They're also known for their cheddar-jalapeno pretzel dog and breakfast foods. (Note: Miller's Twist is a PA Dutch vendor and is closed on Sundays.)

3. Scrapple from Down Home Diner. Also known as Pannhaas by the PA Dutch, this is basically pork scraps made into a savory pate. Reminds me of the Neese's liver pudding (livermush) I ate growing up in North Carolina.

Surprisingly, there's not really a well-known or recommended vendor for cheesesteaks here though there are some who sell them (e.g. Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagies & Cheesesteaks). Bring cash because some vendors, like Carmen's, are cash-only. A couple places that caught our eye that we didn't get to try were Pearl's Oyster Bar and Mueller Chocolate Co. (featured on Food Network).

There are two parking garages, one at 12th and Filbert (Parkway Garage) and the other at 11th and Arch (Hilton Garage). Signs posted at each entrance to the market advertised 2-hour discount parking with $10 market purchase and validation at the vendor.

If you're pressed for time in Philly, Reading Terminal Market is a great place to visit since there are so many vendors all in one place. If you're from out of town, be sure to visit the northwest corner of the market where all the PA Dutch vendors are located. They're unique.

This is my favorite goto place when it comes to Kati rolls. For those who don't know what Kati Rolls are, these are wraps (like burritos ) and have Indian filling inside. I recommend adding an egg to your kati roll as we get it in India. We ordered Achari chicken, spicy chicken,  lamb masala, Paneer masala and chicken biryani . Everything tasted delicious. The place is open late, I think till 2 or 3 am and the prices are very reasonable.  They have a selfserve Chutney counter. Must advise that the red chutney is very spicy. Be careful. White sauce had good flavors. Thei Mnlango lassi was also good, but I found a bit too sweet. The wraps are decent in size. I felt that the size has reduced since last time. But its still very inexpensive for the location. Perfect food after some drinks to get your hangover in Check.
Overall, I recommend this place.

I stopped into The Bourse last night and my girlfriend and I made our first visit here. As a number of other reviews mention, this has the advantage of being one of a pretty small amount of Filipino offerings in Philly, and I was excited to check it out. I used to date a Pinay and was in the Philippines a could of times, so I have built-in appreciation for their cuisine, and have always wondered if a time would come where their food got the wave of popularity here that Vietnamese and soup dumplings have in recent years. 

I ordered the lechon dish, my girlfriend got the lumpia, only wanting a snack. I was very happy with my lechon - it came nice and crispy on the outside, had an appropriate amount of melt-in-the-mouth flavorful fat in the middle of the porkbelly, and nice, tender meat; the way it's supposed to. The dish was simple and complimentary - the garlic rice was good on its own and way better still with the dipping sauce poured on top of the whole dish. The halved cherry tomatoes and pickled onions (?) on the side were minor additions, but I'd rather it have them than not. 

The lumpia, which I tried, didn't hit the spot quite as much, but they were still pretty good. It might just be as simple as them tasting a bit different from the ones I use to have, which tended to be thicker than these and include diced potatoes and/or carrots. But with that said, these still tasted satisfying dipped lightly in the sweet sauce they came with. 

I thought the place was a bit pricey for the value, but I expect that will be common in the Bourse. I'll be back even knowing that - they have a strong combination of quality, rarity, and easy accessibility for me.

This is the best place ever. If you come here you will be amazed by what you see and taste. 
Mitchell Thomas Wesby
8 years old 
P.S. Best place ever!

Literally something for everyone. If you can't find something here... then I don't even know who you are. 

I was attending an event at the convention center, located adjacent to the Reading Terminal Market, and found myself visiting RTM multiple times per day. And why wouldn't you? You can get hot food, cold food, sandwiches, pizza slices, stromboli, produce, fresh meat, dried fruit and nuts, grilled cheese, baked goods, coffee, smoothies -- the list goes on and on and on. Before coming to Philadelphia, someone told me, "The Market is what lots of cities think they have -- but in reality is 10x better." I didn't know what he meant then but totally get it now.

The only downside is the limited amount of seating. Not that you should compromise the variety and assortment of vendors just for seating -- but it seems easier to grab takeout than to try and find a table here, especially if you're with a group. 

So far my favorite items/spots have been the grilled cheese at Valley Shepherd Creamery & Meltkraft and the chocolate chip walnut cookies at Famous 4th St Cookie Company. I'm planning to go back for a Beiler's donut before I leave.

Pro tip: Some vendors are cash only, so plan accordingly!

I love this place.  This was my second visit.  I thought the first visit in the summer of 2018 was really crowded because it was summer and there was an ice cream festival.  Nope, apparently it's like this all the time.  Nevertheless, it was an enjoyable visit.  I highly recommend to anyone who's in the area.  There are all types of edibles and beverages.  I stocked up on adult beverages and chocolate and had a wonderful lunch.

Everything you can possibly want is here.  Amish food awaits you.  Great food and friendly service and staff. One can easily spend breakfast, lunch, dinner and desert at this one location.  Plus happy hour.

This market has a wonderful variety of prepared food items, produce, meats, specialty foods, places to eat and a few non-food shops. I love the atmosphere,

Some of the best was, i had roast beef and roast pork sandwiches from DiNic's, one of my favorites. This is a counter service place in the center of the Market, with delicious sandwiches with moist meats on crusty rolls that you can customize, with choices of sauteed spinach or broccoli rabe, roasted or hot peppers, sharp provolone, etc. Pepperoncini peppers and horseradish are on the counters. Don't worry if there are no seats, wait and ones will open soon. Take out counter is to the right.

Tips - 
Parking in the garage across the street is reduced cost if validated with a purchase.
Come hungry or you'll be sorry!

Variety! Be it bake goods with espresso to start the day, or curry empanada for quick snack you will find it here. Always a bit packed, but if the whole gang wants to meet up for lunch- each person will find something pleasing here and likely pick up a few things to go ;)

Lots of options lots of diverse and fusion style food vendors and restaurants which have things to eat in and to go. LoTs of cute shops as well, but sometimes the amount of people and lack oF traffic management makes me uncomfortable.
Great place to grab cheap and fresh veggies! Love how long the vegetables last! The stands are also amazing! I wish a majority of the stands didn't only take cash.

As someone who grew up in DE and who has traveled through Philly to visit the fam for the past six years, I can't fathom why I wasn't aware of RTM until less than a year ago, and why I never visited until the day before yesterday!  Although there is a public market in PGH, where I live now, it pales in comparison to RTM--a more appropriate comparison would be to the entire neighborhood that the public market is located in (the Strip District).  What I'd like to know is, how does Philly manage to fit most of the offerings of the Strip into one building?!?

Anyway, I wanted to make the most of my first visit to RTM, so I did my research, and hit the following places for the following goods, all of which cost me about $25:

DiNic's: Roast pork sandwich w/ sharp provolone and broccoli rabe
Miller's Twist: Pretzel w/ honey mustard sauce
Lancaster County Dairy: Orange strawberry lemonade
Bassett's Ice Cream: Peanut butter swirl sugar cone
Beiler's Bakery: Half dozen donuts

Because I came here directly off the train from Pittsburgh, which was running late and hadn't made the usual stop in Harrisburg for lunch, all I'd eaten all day was a bagel at 7am and an apple at 1pm.  So, needless to say, when I arrived here around 3:30pm, I was ravenously hungry, and ate everything listed above with the exception of the donuts, which I brought home for my family.  I was surprised at how many vendors were open when I visited, but one of them explained that they were open later than usual due to the proximity to Thanksgiving.  How lucky for me, since I wasn't expecting to be able to patronize Miller's or Beiler's, given that they're not usually open at this time!

I'll leave the details of each foodstuff I tried to reviews of the individual vendors (forthcoming), but suffice it to say that everything, with one exception, was supremely delicious!  I left RTM stuffed and happy--a good thing, since I had an hour-long ride on SEPTA to DE to look forward to.  I walked out of there wondering why I'd never been to RTM before, and thinking that I need to get back here ASAP to sample more of the offerings.  In fact, I'm planning to talk the fam into taking me back here for brunch at Dutch Eating Place on Sat. before my train back to PGH leaves on Sat.

Long story short, this place is awesome!!!  If you're a visitor to Philly, you need to see this place before you leave.  If you're a local and you haven't visited, crawl out from under that rock you're living under and get here ASAP!
This is my favorite place for fruits vegetables an hot roast beef and pork sandwiches

Best pizza in Philly!!! If you love thin crust, look no more. This place does it right! Best part is that they do pizza by the slice. The cheese, pepperoni and tomato pie were all excellent! The dough was nice and airy with an amazing crunch. I will only go here to get my pizza fix from now on.

Love this place. When I lived in the Fairmount area we shopped here every Saturday. Now that I am back in the city I go often. Fox & Sons is ALL GF!  The grilled cheese place in the rear makes some delicious GF grilled cheese.

Very healthy vegetable Pennsylvania does very well according to the overall organic consumer in the USA ! Place to try! 

You can find Chinese as Greek as many others choices aren't missing!

Incredible mix of cultures and food.  We loved the fresh produce, flowers, eating places, and the atmosphere.  It was amazing everything that we got to see the food was delicious the Greek stand was amazing the selection of cheeses was incredible

This place is ridiculous!  I've been wanting to check out Reading Terminal Market for a long time since seeing it featured on an episode of Man v. Food.  So much good stuff in there that it's way too much to cover in one visit.  A lot of the best stuff that Philadelphia has to offer can be found here:  Scrapple, BBQ, Grilled Cheese Sandwiches, Roast Pork, Seafood, and yes, even Cheesesteaks.  It was a sure treat to spend time over here.

Definite must stops are DiNic's and Dutch Eating Place.  But then again those were pretty much all I was able to visit due to my limited stomach capacity.  I'll have to come back again to try everything else.  I will definitely return!!
OMG, so many amazing places to eat.  The donuts, cakes, sandwiches, omelets are amazing anywhere you choose to eat.  If you are in Downtown Philly, this place is worth visiting.
Ordered two dinners for a late night meal at 9pm online. We waited about a half hour and we get there and they aren't ready but they said it would be 10 minutes. Waited 15 and we left. Ghetto!

Really nice place to stop by for a quick lunch. I like the option of customizing your entire order and trying new combinations. I had gotten the stir fry with chicken, a mix of veggies and regular amount of sauce mixed in. (I forgot what sauce it was!) I would recommend getting less sauce or on the side because everything gets really soggy. 
      Location is pretty convenient to the campus area. Service is really quick and friendly, which is a great plus! I would say the price for the serving size might be a bit overpriced, but it's tolerable if you really enjoy the food.
Food was excellent. Had a salad and my friend had the stir fry. It was a little hard to find the restaurant, but worth looking for. Thought it was a good portion and worth the price. I will be back.

Fun place to visit in Philadelphia anytime of year. Feast your eyes on Peking duck, Amish baked goods, Middle Eastern delights and then some. This place is a stones throw from Phillys Chinatown. Your stomach will be happy to oblige

A melting pot of flavors and different cuisines.
It is impossible to eat your way here in a day..more like a week. Places worth a visit are:
FOUR SEASONS JUICE SHOP; incredible edible fruits all processed into amazing vitamin packed juices. Anytime juice good as a meal or as a liquid snack.
MARKET BAKERY; artisanal breads, muffins, and coffee.
SWEET AS FUDGE CANDY SHOP; gotta a sweet tooth?
Best gummy bears i always get the green apple, blue rasberry,  pinneapple and coca cola..
Dont forget the lemom drops..get it all by the pound...LOL. if you worry about sugar they have sugar free items as well.
BASSETS ICE CREAM; home made creamy ice cream in very delicus flavors. I like coffee and chocolate bit the flavors can really get complicated.  
FAMOUS 4TH STREET COOKIE COMPANY; the best cookie in town, no questions asked just get in line brinf some cash and wait for the cookies to come out the oven.  My favorite are the chocolate, ginger snaps and snicker doodle. Yum..exponentially!
THE RIB STAND; come hungry and be ready to eat with your eyes. Ribs to die for with great bbq sauce. They too have pulled pork and other items but the ribs are awesome tender and well seasoned.
LOBINE BROTHERS PRODUCE; you can pick up fruit and veggies directly from local producers around the area.
KEVIN PARKERS SOUL CAFE; great mac and cheese and fried chicken with collar greens 
This market is amazing, you can live in this place.
I think i have been coming to this market since 2010 and every year it gets better!

Reading Terminal Market is a cool place to walk around in, but that's it, you're much better off just walking and looking rather than trying any of the food that is offered there. The restauranteurs do a good job of presenting some of the food items, but that is where the buck stops. The food just doesn't taste as good as it looks. Basically, Reading Terminal is a huge TOURIST TRAP. Go there, try something if you really have to, and then leave and never look back. There are many, more cleanly,less crowed, better quality, though albeit less well known places to dine in the city of brotherly love.

After living in Philadelphia for over 6 years how on God's green earth is this the first time I've ever been to Reading Terminal Market? My only regret is that I didn't find out about this place sooner. Oh how I wish I had known about the wondrous treasures tucked inside this well disguised market full of fabulousness when I worked just 5 blocks away. My taste buds would love me but my backside (and perhaps my husband) might not have enjoyed the consequences of my overindulgence. 

Believe them when they say this place is packed on the weekends.  The little old lady I almost ran over with my stroller can atest to this.  IN true Philly fashion she shot me a dirty look, mouthed some expletives and kept it moving.  Other than that , how could you not love this place? For starters, there are approximately 75 vendors in this locale so even the pickiest of people should be able to find SOMETHING they enjoy (Unless they're from NYC, then all bets are off because you know NYC has thee best of everything *insert eye roll*). The place is cramped, let's just put that out there. They say 100,000 people come through the market per week but honestly it feels more like 100k per day. You're sure to trip over tourists stopping and gawking in the aisles as local people trying to pass by get annoyed (sorry Grandma). Grab yourself a Tenant Directory (from either a bathroom or the market information booth) and it will help guide you to wherever your interests may take you. The directory divides businesses into the following categories: 

*Bakeries 
*Beverages 
*Dairy & Cheese 
*Flowers & Plants (one vendor) 
*Housewares, Books, Crafts, etc. 
*Meats & Poultry 
*Seafood 
*Pennsylvania Dutch 
*Produce 
*Restaurants 
*Specialty Foods 

Be advised that 30% of the tenants are closed on Sunday, this includes ALL of the Dutch Merchants (they only work Wed-Sat).   The market itself is open 8 to 6 from Mon-Sat and 9 to 5 on Sun.  

Treat yourself to a delicious pretzel (and fresh lemonade) at Miller's Twist. 
Get the famous apple dumpling at Dutch Eating Place. 
If you're into the Oprah hype, stop by Delilah's for the "best ever mac & cheese" (I can't attest to that and hell, Oprah looks like she'll eat anything to me so I don't know if she's exactly a qualified food source) 

You'll find Asian cuisine, Soul Food, Ice Cream, baked teats, cheesteaks, and everything you need to get the complete Philadelphia experience. 

Park anywhere in the Parkway Garage at 12th & Filbert Streets and park for $4. 
Bring your parking ticket to the market with you and after making a purchase of $10 or more ANY merchant will validate your ticket (upon request). 
You automatically receive flat rate of $4 for UP TO 2 hours of parking (anything over that and you're subject to the astronomical garage rates). 

If you're not in for a drive just take the train. You can exit either rail line at 13th street, head east towards 12th street and make a left onto 12th. You can't miss the signs and you won't want to miss the food!

This is a foodie dream. I've never been anywhere like it before (the closest I could say is Pike Place Market in Seattle), and I was in awe the entire time. We started at one corner and weaved our way up and down every aisle, stopping for roast pork sandwiches at Tommy Dinic's, whoopie pies at Flying Monkey, and donuts at Beiler's. I can't wait to go back (we're VA residents) and try more vendors!

This is pretty much the best place in the world, & I don't know what else I can say about it that 2,000 other reviewers haven't already said. It's magical, bustling, full of every kind of food you could possible imagine, from ready-to-eat to grocery. What do you want for lunch? Reading Terminal Market has it. 

Highlights, for me, are the large Pennsylvania dutch offerings, Meltkraft Grilled Cheese, the old-fashioned candy shop (homemade fudge!), & the pierogi place that I can never remember the name of - but seriously, probably anything you get here is going to be delicious.Other bonuses: Reading Terminal Market is committed to supporting purveyors of local & regional produce, & though it's easily accessible by public transportation, parking is only $4.

Planning to eat in? You may have trouble finding seating, as there's certainly not enough of it within the market. On nice days, find seating outdoors & people watch as you consume whatever delicacy you've just acquired inside.

I just returned from Seattle and their mighty Pike Market, therefore I couldn't help but compare. Bottom line, this market has nothing on Pike. It's a place for locals and probably tourists. But when I return to Philly, this will not need a revisit. 

Soap Lady is the coolest spot. Everything else can easily be obtained from other locations.

Ooops. Apparently I attached this review for the incorrect reading terminal market link.
-----------------------------------------------

I absolutely loved this clusterfxck of food vendors jampacked into these tight quarters. I may even have been more excited about coming here than my visit downtown.  There are tons of people, super noisy which I think just adds to the appeal of this Philly staple.

This is a foodie's paradise. No joke. There are vendors everywhere selling every palatable whoozits and whatzitz imaginable.  cheesesteaks, pizza, pastries, cheese, meats, seafood, they have everything here. There's a lot of scattered tables for sitting and you can literally eat your way through the market if your belly and wallet allowed. 

Some shops are cash only, but most take credit cards.  Parking can be found in the neighboring areas for a small fee. 

In my one hour here, we managed to get a half dozen donuts, a cheesesteak, and pizza.  That didn't include much browsing time though.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to truly enjoy walking around and soaking up the atmosphere.

So being from Ohio, I used to think the West Side Market in Cleveland was it...the end all be all. Then I moved to Philly and checked out Reading Terminal. Wow...I was definitely mistaken. This place was ridiculously large that I kept getting lost. So many different restaurants and stands of all ethnicities and cultures. I live close by so it's nice to get my produce and meats from this place. It smells amazing every time I'm here. I have only been on the weekdays so far, but from what I hear, the weekends are pretty packed so be prepared.

I love the Reading Terminal. I loved it as a child and it still fascinates me every time I go.  There are a very few things you couldn't find here. If you look someone has it on a Thursday or Friday. Sometimes Sunday is a bit sparse as the Amish aren't there, but you can still enjoy the rest.

There is NOTHING better than this market for foodies in the tri state area. Its a huge market warehouse filled with restaurants, food stands, produce, bakeries, fresh butcher stands, fish markets, bbq, fresh juice stands, even retail stores selling food related products!!
Theres no shortage of places to eat, or variety!! You can have Amish, Greek, Italian, Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai... theres even a bar restaurant towards the back for sports.
My favorite is Becks (creole/cajun), Dinics roast pork w broccoli rabe and sharp provolone sandwich (amazing!!) The fresh squeezed juice guy in the side corner, and the Amish stands with their incredible bbq ribs and their fresh bakery. Amazing dinner yeast rolls.
When my husband and I come we park right across the street, gather a few items at different vendors, then sit and eat lunch. After that? I grocery shop and bring alot of the food home. Bags and bags, hence the close parking spot lol
They have several dining areas and some of the restaurants have their own seating but do not come at lunchtime or during conventions or events ( convention center right next door) you will be standing or eating very closely w patrons!!
Great place, I will never stop coming here, I love it!!

This pizza is tasty, thin, and sliced large.  Of course at over $4 a slice with no additional toppings added, it better be!  There were four different options for slices on the given night I visited and at first glance, they all certainly looked great.  There didn't seem to be options to customize further.  I asked for an original to go, it was heated up quickly and I was on my way.

First impression, this slice is very, very thin.  While I appreciated the crusty-ness of the slice, there was no body or chew to the dough, which is not what I like.  The ratio of cheese and sauce was good, and there was a sprinkle of fresh parm on top.  

I'll be back to try other slices.
Place is the best. So many different spots, great food options. Produce, meats, pastries, coffee. It has it all. Long live Reading Terminal
Such a cool place to eat. So many quality choices. I wish that I lived nearby. Tons of fresh baked goods along with great ethnic options.

I'm writing this review as a student who lives nearby. I feel so lucky to live so close to a place that fulfills (almost) all of my foodie needs! 

I come here 2-4 times a week for groceries. My go-to places are Godshall's for poultry and Iovine Bros for produce. I also love the fish shop near the seating area in the middle (I can't remember the name!) because it's always fresh and the prices are ok for the area. The cheese shops are a bit overpriced, but there's nowhere else nearby to get good cheese for cheaper. 

I also frequently stop by to grab a bite to eat. I've eaten at almost every place here and I've yet to be disappointed! There's a great variety of different cuisines to choose from, but if you're looking for anything Asian, walk the couple blocks over to Chinatown. 

If you can, avoid coming on Friday afternoons or Saturdays because it gets so crowded that it's hard to move. Unless that's the environment you're looking for, in which case it's exciting and bustling with people, both local and tourists. 

A lot of places are closed on Sundays and the Amish places are closed on wednesdays too, so keep that in mind. 

RTM is going to be one of the things I miss the most when I move out of Philly!

Amazing quality, quick service, great persons working there! A wide selection of items but not so overwhelming that you can't grasp it all. Tasty food that is made with care and is of sufficient, but not overboard, portion. The Lassi are tasty. Open late, which is a benefit.

The epic metropolitan market for social, and edible satisfaction in Philadelphia. As crowded as the terminal can be, everyone is there to get what they want.  I knew I wanted a delicious home cooked meal. For me, it was The Original Turkey. I get the Original sandwich. It has succulent, savory turkey, crisp sweet lettuce, and lustful, crimson tomato. It fits. It makes my stomach howl. During the summer, I got to sit outside of the terminal with the rush of the city around me and this delicious treat in my hands. You see places like Sang Kee Peking Duck, Spataro's Cheese steaks, and Dutch Eating Place, you find your taste, you always want to return, and might find a solid conversation.

I love the market! There are so many different shops/restaurants to browse around and find exactly what you are searching for. Expect crowds when visiting the terminal as it is the place to be. Come hungry and eat you way around the market! Once you have eaten all the savory meats leave the market with a desert in hand. You won't be disappointed!

BANGIN'! 

Got there at 4:45pm and had to wait a spell for them to reopen with fresh pies. Worth it! Bought a pepperoni and (the last) tomato pie slices. Started with the 'roni and started to sweat midway through - wasn't sure how I'd make it through both (don't worry, I did). 

The place is on the same level as Beddia, but totally different atmospheres. Place is very tiny and standing room only inside - all ok. 

Would definitely come back here time and time again.
I love smuckers food counters. The pot roast on a roll is soooo good. So is the chicken sandwich. Im glad theyre open now.

Hermoso este mercado en pleno centro de la ciudad de Philadelphia, ya sean para comer o tomar algo, hacer compras o simplemente pasear por un espacio súper pintoresco.

Lo mejor del Reading Terminal Market es que tiene bocha de lugares para comer y tomar algo, todo súper variado, rico y genial.

Es un mercado con mucha onda, todo es súper lindo y recorriendo el lugar te podrás encontrar con locales geniales. Todo es súper fotografiable y es todo un placer darse una vuelta por acá. Un must de Philadelphia.

A really cool place full of culture. So many options. You can really take your time and browse or run in and grab what you like. Some of the restaurants have small seating areas and there is a few other sections you can stand or sit and eat.

I've visited this Philly icon a handful of times over the years.  This time around, I broke the most essential cardinal rule:  'Come hungry.'  Indeed.  You see, a couple hours before, I'd stopped with hubby and kid at John's Roast Pork.  A meal I'd ultimately regret, but that's for another review.  Point is, I was still so f***ing full, the mere sight of all the food here made me feel a wee bit queasy.  I tried to power through, though. I really did:

Miller's Twist:  I've eaten Pretzels from an Amish Market before, but not this particular one.  Happily, the classic Pretzel we chose did not disappoint. I have a secret (well, maybe not so much now) thing for Auntie Ann's Pretzels and this was an elevated, buttery, soft, warm version of that.  Even in my semi-nauseous state, that was clear.  We'd ordered some cheese sauce for dipping and both hubby and kid declared, "This tastes just like butter and not in a good way!" I'll concede they were right.  It was more fatty tasting than cheesy. I'd go with Mustard next time.

Smucker's Grill:  Since I knew from previous disappointment that the Amish stands tend to close earlier than many of the others here, I'd made a point of looking up the hours.  According to the official Reading Terminal site, on Thursdays, this stand closes at 5pm.  So imagine my chagrin when we were told at 4:30 ish that they were no longer serving.  After explaining that the stated hours indicated otherwise, they were very accommodating about whipping up a Pot Roast Sandwich for us.  I asked them to add horseradish cheese, sauteed onion, and horseradish.  We wound up eating this after our two hour drive back home to Brooklyn and were shocked at how delicious it was!  I can only imagine how good this is freshly made and warm.  

This was all we could um... stomach on this visit...  But fwiw, have tried the famed donuts from Beiler's and while they're fun to experience once, I'd say there are way better ways to spend your dessert calories in Philly.  DiNic's on the other hand...  That Roast Pork Sandwich is worth everything.

Random Thoughts:  At 3pm, this place was bordering on annoyingly crowded, but by 4pm, it was downright pleasant.  This also happens to be when three hour street parking kicks in v. one hour. We were able to find a spot on N. 12th. Street, right near the entrance.   I believe there are also a couple nearby lots, including at the Hilton Garden Hotel, that with a validated minimum purchase, only charge a few bucks for two hours.

Bottom line:  If you don't like this Market, which is the soul of Philly in so many ways, then you're just not doing it right.  Go at a less crowded off time.  And since all the various options can feel overwhelming, read through some reviews to help narrow down your picks.  In this particular case, at least, Yelp is your friend.:)
There are so many things to choose from here! But make sure you get some of Sweet Ninas banana pudding. You won't regret it!
No words can do justice to the kati rolls served at masala kitchen. Absolutely love their chicken tikka masala roll and their sauces! Big fan

Masala Kitchen shits on Spice End.

Do yourself a favor and order the Chicken Masala Roll and eat it there on those cute stools. Oh and don't forget to pour some of that white and red sauce on it before every bite! I guarantee your eyes will roll back every time :-P

Reading Terminal Market is a must visit when in Philly. It's a market with tons of options ranging from diner food to groceries to sweets! Inside is where Beiler's donuts and Tommy DiNic's is located but there's definitely more things you can go and try out as well like the Cajun food! There's also a honey shop that has cheap honey sticks. It's definitely crowded inside but there are also tables inside.

Tip: find a table before you find food. 
Quite a bit of fun downtown with a ton of people. A variety of food places. Very quirky. Reminds me of the main market in Saigon

Market was not as big as I originally thought. There is a good variety of food, including 2 Peking duck places, as wells as several cheesesteak ones (you know which ones are popular by the lines that snake around the stall). Tommy DiNic's looked good too, but the queue was too long for me.

The Reading Terminal Market is the first spot I went to on my first Philly trip. It was a short walk from my hotel and really gave you a sense of what to expect from Philly. The amazing smelling coffee from Old City Coffee and the delicious looking baked goods as far as the eye can see. Plenty of options for food from burgers, to cheese steaks to fish. There's also a fresh produce section as well a a few gift shops. I came here twice during my stay and it definitely has a little something for everyone.

This Location has always been my favorite, for many years! Sooooo... many " stops " with red n' green, with many selections and varieties all around!!!! 
I just simply love the Reading Terminal Market. 
They have all that you expect!

Eat experience I've ever had a chain. The gentleman taking the order was super helpful really funny and the cashier they took the money was also very professional and I very witty. Awesome crew will definitely eat here again

The food itself was just ok. The portion size was pretty good but I didn't find anything special about the food itself- I got a few rolls and ate one and a half.

I ordered delivery to my hotel room- it took over 45 minutes to arrive. They didn't give me any utensils. The yogurt sauce was forgettable. I wouldn't order food from here again.

Was ordering food at the drive through at around 5:20pm on the 2nd of January. The girl was terrible, she didn't want to take our order for some odd reason. Like didn't answer us besides "hi"...a guy came on and took our order. He was nice. Then when we pulled up they gave us less chicken than ordered and the wrong sides. But the same gangsta girl handed us...I mean...threw the order at us and shut the window. What great customer service. They do chicken wrong!

This place is awesome. Celebrating its 125th anniversary, the market is home to over 100 venders of meat, fish, poultry, cheese, baked goods by local artesans, as well as Amish bakers and prepared to take out. There are fresh produce vendors, Famous Deli cookies, Termini's Italian bakery with canoli stuffed to order, pizzelles, as well as cakes for a party or individual celebrations. Thete are many eateries: Pennsylvania Dutch, Asian, Middle Eastern, vegan, as well as the ubiquitous pizza and famous Philly cheesestake stsnds. Several homemade candy stores including Mueller's home of the anatomically correct body parts. Fresh herbs as well as essential oils and other specialties at the Herbiary shop, fresh brewed coffee, Bassett's ice cream, and eateries too numerous to list. There is seating throughout the market, as well as seating at individual stands. Try it, you won't regret it.

Came here all the way from MD per friends' recommendation. I love the fast food idea of home cooked meal, and it's Filipino food! My boyfriend and I shared the vegan kare-kare, caldereta, lumpia, and of course the San Miguel beer! The vegan Kare-kare was tender! I'm not vegan so I cannot eat kare-kare without the bagoong (fried shrimp paste) it doesn't taste right without it. Caldereta was good too! And I loved the lumpia. Growing up in a Filipino household, and obviously having Filipino food cooked for me all the time, I just don't see the reason to pay too much for it. But either way, I enjoyed Lalo. The workers there were very nice as well.

wish I would have taken a photo but I was so frustrated that a cheese quesadilla is made on a huge shell n only uses a half a hand full of cheese‍ also the wrap it in foil n then throw it on a grill for 30 seconds so when I go n open it it looked Lucile a wet tortilla shell‍ my husband n son use to love it here but I rather take the trip elsewhere if they want this food the girl tonight making the food is miserable and what's the point of wearing a hat when ur hair I hanging out of it I'll be having my husband n son also leave this ridiculous place 1star review bc theirs no way this place should have 2.5 stars also how do they never have coke cola ‍

New to the area this is quite a find.   Shopping for everything and I'm not in a supermarket?    This is all new to me.    I ate lunch and bought my veggies and chicken too.    I'm coming back next week.

Any trip to Philadelphia without visiting Reading Terminal Market is an incomplete one. The market itself is a sort of cultural epicenter of Philadelphia with its robust mix of locals and tourists alike. After an all too brief (two hour) sojourn here early in the morning I can reliably conclude that it is virtually impossible to top Reading Terminal Market if you enjoy food markets and consider yourself at least somewhat of a "foodie."

Upon entering, one can be forgiven for feeling a bit disconcerted by the sheer number of pungent aromas that greet you as you open the door. The market has an almost overwhelming amount of vendors packed into a relatively small space, which I feel only adds to the vibrant, bustling energy of the establishment. I don't think you can go wrong with any single vendor, but my favorites would have to be Hershel's East Side for serving one of the tastiest sandwiches I've ever eaten (Pastrami Special) and Beiler's Bakery for indulging my serious sweet tooth with their celestial baked cakes/brownies and rightfully well-renowned donuts.

This place is great! Lots of great Philly food vendors, seafood, Greek, chocolatiers, coffee and other great vendors located in an old Philly building reused for the permanent market. Tons of great food choices for those looking for Philly food or not. Been there a couple of times and keep finding new places to eat. Parking is tough in the immediate area but near downtown makes a great stop passing through Philly.

This place was confusing and delicious. You have to go at least twice- the first time you point and things and sauces and have no idea what your doing and what hot mess of a platter you have put together (if you make your own) and the second time you make much more informed decisions! Now don't get me wrong, both times were great but the second time I had better direction and knew which flavors I wanted. The chicken sausage (crumbled) is amazing. The black been and yogurt sauce are delish as well. Play around with all the ingredients and have fun! They also have fresh juice via fountain drink and they are all good. A great addition for healthy, simple food on campus.

Very crowded and vibrant market very similar to Chelsea market if you know New York City I love this place they have tons of vendors and places to see it and have a drink or food also shopping, things like candles essential oil soaps etc. etc. this is a very nice place to spend couple of hours and it's close to China town which is another great place to visit.  I would love to come back again!

Love this place; this market has every food you can think of. Fresh food, prepared food & restaurants inside the market. It's very busy on Saturdays & Sunday so just be prepared. It does seem a little pricey but worth it.
Late night saving grace--our go to late night food spot! So delicious!!!! Make sure to add an egg to your kati roll of choice!

Located in downtown Philly this is more than a farmers market.  Yes there are fruit and vegetables but so much more.  There is a wide variety of food choices from cajun to crepes to sandwiches to oysters. Almost any food you could desire can be found here.  So many choices it requires more than one visit.  It can get crowded and seating can become an issue but still well worth it.
An incredible food market. Don't miss Beiler's Doughnuts, they are delicious!

Wow. The other reviews were right. This McDonalds is gross - like it closed 10 years ago and someone forgot to tell the employees. 

The cashier complained that customers had come in and "bothered her" while she was scratching her huge mop of hair and another employee was washing the fry area down with the same gloves he packed our food with.

I'm really creeped out how this McDonalds has remained open.
A fun place to check out when visiting Philly! Lots of fresh food, varied prices. I spent about $10 on a pulled pork sandwich for lunch. It is very crowded and seating is limited so.
Excellent place to eat and buy some local produce. Too many options and always busy if u are there during lunch time. But they close early.
One of my favorite places - the cheesesteaks, crepes, ice cream, Amish pies!! Quite a unique and delicious experience
I love the vegetables and fruit stands and also the Amish pastries everything is old school in there including good customer service
Awesome place! There is a reason that this also a Tourist Attraction. The quality food places speak for themselves! 5 Stars.

What is there not to love about this magical place?!?! It is one of the best places in philly to grocery shop, so many incredible vendors. Everything is extremely well priced. I am always amazed at how much I save shopping there verses Whole Foods. Also, they have some of the best prepared food stands anywhere!! Whatever you want, you can have. From Peking duck to creole, to brisket sandwiches piled 8 inches high. I love love love it there.

I love pizza Shackamaxon! I've had their slices quite a few times as I used to live right down the street. I'm lactose intolerant and sometimes order tomato pie, and theirs is hearty/chunky/juicy. Overall, awesome go-to pizza spot. Only downside is that they sometimes sell out early.

Love the Reading Terminal Market! A must stop for all tourist. I always want something from the Pennsylvania Dutch countertop restaurant. Also, the soft pretzels, freshly made with butter brushed on top! Add some cheese ,....wow! Absolutely delicious!
This place is amazing. Really glad I checked it out while in the city. I recommend it to anyone and everyone!

We love this place we really like picking out what foods we enjoy knowing they are all good. I had turkey dinner had to share it was so big 
 We go back there every six months when we visit philly always fun great food experience

Reminds me of home. In Milwaukee we have the Milwaukee Public Market. They are very similar. Here in Philly I got a taste of what its like to eat, drink and shop like a Philidelphian. Which was cool.

I found out what scrapple is... not that i'd eat it but at least I can say that I know.

I like to support the local business and economy. The Terminal Market was a cool trip.

This place is ridiculous!  At the awesome level :-)

Such fantastic energy with the myriad of businesses and people all clustered inside.  A plethora of food choices (think Austin's food truck lots but inside) with a main sitting area in the center to enjoy.  Rather quickly moving lines for the number of people, and the cost at is the regular work-lunch level (~$7).

It is precisely what it sets out to be, and that's fantastic.

Great place to eat and shop. They have produce at affordable prices and so many food options. I was able to find quite a few vegetarian options. Try Kamal's falafels! Old City coffee is great. And the cookies at 4th street famous cookies are such a nice treat.  loved this market!

Reading Terminal is always my favorite place to head to when I'm in Chinatown or at work. Great vendors and stands with wonderful food! Also love the groceries you can buy at OK Produce and Iovine Produce. The weekends can be very crowded, especially during the holidays! But during the morning on weekdays, it's not so bad. I do recommend getting a roast pork sandwich at Dinic's and a few donuts at Beiler's! Great ice cream at Miller's Twist, as well as their pretzels.

This place is crazy! I mean there's restaurants and stations of practically anything you want. From meats to desserts to diners to knick knacks, there's literally anything you're looking for. It's such a huge space that we barely made our way through it all. There's people everywhere so make sure you can tolerate crowds. Have patience since it's very cluttered and congested. It's a really cool concept for a market though.
We absolutely love this place. There is all kids of fun things to do, all kids of shopping and fun things to do. We wanted to go every day.

The Industry did a great job hosting us for a casual company get together this past friday, kudos especially since a snow storm was headed our way! We had reservations for 5pm but luckily they were able to move it up to 4:30 since the weather was predicted to come sooner than anticipated.
We had the front section of the restaurant to mingle, eat and drink. They had open tabs going. They gave us a wings bar (buffalo, general tso) and continued to serve us unlimited appetizers: mac&cheese croquettes, dumplings, kimchi tater tots, buffalo chicken meatballs...basically a lot of fried food lol.
the wings were the star of the show for me -- I absolutely loved the sweet wings, I think they're the general tso ones. The buffalo wings were decent, considering I don't really like buffalo sauce. That said, the buffalo chicken meatballs are like a kick in the face so if you don't like buffalo, avoid. The mac &cheese croquettes made my dream come true. If i was a kid or had no self control, I would tear the place up eating these babies.
The kimchi tater tots were meh in my opinion. They were kind of hard and you couldn't taste the kimchi...and I know kimchi.
Last but not least, the dumplings were phenomenal. I'm not sure what's inside...some kind of green paste but it tastes infinitely better than how I described it. The soy sauce that is served with it completes the taste, yum. It was probably the healthiest thing we had on the tables.
Our servers were excellent, continuously coming over to fill water, add more food to the tables and take our orders. I hope to come again to try more of the food, because it's good, but I'm not blown away yet, hence the 4 stars.

Fresh meats all the meat department is excellent but some of the people working there have a bad attitude at the others concession stands ,, young woman said I have a cocky southphilly accent because I use the word cuz it all started because I said yo cuz how ya doing threw the lockdown ,, I was totally offended
Very packed every time I've been there and that wasn't just weekend days. I'd recommend coming during the week and at times where people don't have to work.

What a fun place for a traveler like me just in downtown Philly for an overnight. I had a classic and well chopped cheesesteak at Carmen's and then at Peking Duck I picked up some of the best fried rice I've ever had. So much fun to look, smell the great food and listen to all the accents.

Reading Terminal Market far exceeded my expectations! You can find anything you could ever need- from baked goods to fresh produce to tasty meats. I went to Reading Terminal in search of kabobs to grill for dinner. After walking around the entire market, I was unable to find them on display. I inquired with the staff at Giunta's Prime Shop. They offered to make them fresh-specifically for me! The staff truly went above and beyond! The kabobs included chicken, red onion, green peppers, red peppers, and mushrooms. They were absolutely delicious and made for the perfect weekday meal. I will definitely make a meal from Reading Terminal Market again!
Awesome!!!!  Everything you could want in one place.  So many markets and food!!!   Dinic's is awesome and there are some great dessert/ice cream places.

Oh my yum. We had never tried a roll before and were a little hesitant on how to order. We both had the masala roll and it was perfect - the meat was tender, the sauce was proportionate and it had a lot of flavor. I like heat, but the medium was a little spicy for me. We wish we had ordered an extra to share :). Will be ordering again and trying additional rolls!
So many good places to eat.  So many places to shop.  It's not just for tourists.  I worked near there and ate there at least once a week for many years. I always stop by when I'm in the area.
I got here 2 hours before close on a Saturday & they are out of pizza. I hear it's really good but c'mon figure out a system.

A friend and I were very excited to try this place out. both had a mix order of dumplings primarily cheesesteak and our cheesesteak dumplings both were freezing cold on the inside. Totally turnr our stomachs. Blahh. Never again.

This place was overall an A+++. The service was better then an actually restaurant service. There was an employee going around every single table asking if everything was ok and refilling soda and etc. the place was very clean and organized, even the sauces. Every sauce was lined up one by one. I have never seen anywhere done that before. The manager of was always on top off his employees and seem to be very nice to them. Great management comes with great employees. Definitely #1 fast food chain!!
Great food at every turn. My favorite was the Soul Food! Macncheese with fried chicken. Green beans looked so good too but I was kind of out of money to get them:(

We love this place, every time we end up in Philadelphia this is one of the places we go to. The diversity of food, unbelievable, I found even products from my homeland. Now that's for me something to be excited about. But can anybody explain to me what is so Dutch about the Pennsylvania Dutch? 

Last time we visited Philly, we were standing with Al Roker in line for a sandwich and another cool thing to know is that Reading Terminal Market is also highlighted in National Treasure, when Abigail Chase (Diane Kruger) is being chased by a bad guy. 

First thing to do when at 'RTM' is just to stroll around and observe and make note of all the good stuff they sell here. After making a decision what to order, the next objective is to find a area to sit and enjoy the food. (during lunch it is packed!) After finishing the meal, one more round through all the different booths, and maybe a desert to go.
I am recently employed in the terminal. Everything is amazing but sometimes it is hard to walk because it gets so insanely crowded.
Such a great atmosphere, so many goodies! From ice cream and cookies to the best Dinic's Roast Pork Sandwich, Reading Terminal is an experience you want if you are in Philadelphia.
Good variety of food and shops.  Parking is a bear most of the time but great place to head while in philly

As a local, Reading Terminal is one of my favorite places to go in the city. I love doing my grocery shopping here cause I can get a lot for almost nothing. 

When you come here park in the parking lot that is on 12th street right across from the 12th St market entrance. If you park here you get 2 hrs of parking for $4 with a $10 purchase at the market. Just make sure to get it validated inside - you'll definitely spend $10.

OK Produce, located right in the center of RTM (next to DiNics) is a great place for a college student on a budget to grab produce. They mostly sell dollar bags of produce that you then can slap the 10% student discount on. This place might not have the most quality produce but you get a bang for your buck. Iovine Brothers has nicer produce but you definitely pay for it. 

The Amish are not usually there Sunday-Tuesday so if you go then you are playing your luck to get some of their tasty treats. They run a lot of shops with Reading Terminal and you are honestly missing out if you don't get something from Beiler's Bakery. Some of the best donuts in town. I also like their Mac n Cheese from the Rib Shack. Definitely worth trying! Also, I recommend going early the day before Thanksgiving and grabbing a pie from the Amish.
