All the way in the back is the Nut Shop *or something along those lines* that sells coffee, rice, snacks, and tea in bulk. You pick out what you want and drag the bin to the front and ask the nice people behind the counter to weigh it out for you. It's definitely a good deal on a bunch of staple things. Plus they have some snacks that I used to get in my Naturebox *which I have now unsubscribed to*. It's definitely a good place to check out. 

The final place I want to mention is Meltkraft. If you are a lover of Grilled Cheese, you gotta check it out. This is one of the most satisfying meals in the market and they are always have a specialty sandwich. Plus, each order comes with homemade chips. yum. 

All and all, I am a huge Reading Terminal fan. I recommend going in the morning during the week cause the place is empty.

Visited for the first time over the weekend. The crowds are crazy and it feels really claustrophobic. We waited in line to eat breakfast at the Dutch Eating Place and grabbed cookies at the 4th Street Bakery. We will definitely be back to try the sandwiches, ice cream, bbq and donuts.
I was really hungry and the service is real good and it's lit. I really like the decor and the deals are amazing . The cheeseburgers are lit. Awesome families

Love the Reading Terminal Market! Lots of choices, something for everyone! Whether you're visiting for breakfast, lunch or dinner, you will find something yummy to eat.  Also many great fresh produce and meats to take home. Shop, eat and snacks all in one place.  Every trip includes a stop to bring home cannolis from Termini Bros! Yum!

I remember visiting Reading Market over 2 decades ago.

Busy, hopping place wafting with aromas of the different cuisines being prepared and served at the market.

I have been to many good halls and markets in the US, Canada and elsewhere.

As a produce, fresh meat and seafood market,  Reading Terminal Market is average.

As a food hall,  Reading Terminal Market ranks among the best of the best.

A must visit when in the City of Brotherly Love.

When I lived in Phillie, this was my go-to spot for fresh, homegrown veggies, local poultry, meats and fish.  In 30 years, the farmers market movement has caught up!  Now, its my go-to meeting spot for friends visiting the city, or lunch stop when I am working downtown.
The best way, bar none, to sample the tastes of the Philadelphia region and Pennsylvania, and be sure you are supporting local farmers and cooks.

If you're looking for something different, I would try La Lo.  There aren't many Filipino establishments in the area, so this might be your one chance.  

I went with some co-workers during lunch at the Bourse. There was no line, they make your food to order, so everything comes out fresh.  I ordered the Loginisa dog and Lumpia.  The dog was served on a bed of rice with pickled relish and poached egg, you get that nice runny egg yolk over the rice.  The flavors complemented each other well, the arrangement is similar to Vietnamese rice dishes, without the fish sauce.    

Solid food, a little pricey, but everything at the Bourse is, assuming that is due to the rent prices that needs to be covered.  It's something that you should try if you've never tasted Filipino food before.

The food is delicious, however, I'm giving a low rating due to the fact you have poor customer service. Whenever I order take out and specifically ask for the sauces on the side to be included and packed with my order, they never are and am told to pour them myself. This is difficult and frustrating because there is no parking available right outside and wastes time when I'm trying to just pick up and go with my order.

This place is okay.
If you want cheap, fast, non-authentic Indian food, then this is definitely an option.
The chicken Marsala roll was okay. Honestly, it's just an oily naan like shell with 3-4 chunks of chicken, sauce, and like 2 raw red onion rings.
It's fast. It's relatively cheap. But it's nothing to wow over.
The mango lassi was okay. Thick and tangy.
Service is nice and the place is clean.
Overall, this is sort of a last resort quick lunch. Not dying to go back, but I would if I was a pinch.

ALL THE HEART DESIRES IN ONE PLACE. The Reading Terminal Market is a staple for citizens and tourists in Philly. You can go grocery shopping for some fresh produce- then go around the whole place to try everything that stands out- donuts, seafood, burgers, wraps, fries, grilled cheese! There are multiple food courts spread around for people to sit down and enjoy their food!

I love the Terminal. I've been going there since i was a kid. The only draw backs are the large crowds in such a crammed place; But you can find fresh garden veggies at inexpensive prices & it's a great place to go for lunch or an early dinner.

A few weeks back, I enjoyed a beautifully nourishing vegan meal from LALO for the first time, courtesy of GH delivery. I'd been eating like garbage and was trying to do my body right. So I wanted a plant-based meal that wouldn't bore me to tears *and* fill me up post-workout. 

I ordered the Bicol Express -- a melange of tofu, veggies, coconut milk, ginger, and garlic rice, plus a cup of their atchara. It was heaven.

My sister and I stopped at the Bourse Food Court yesterday, and we were both famished from biking and walking around Independence Mall and Old City. I decided it was prime time for Bicol Express #2, and I was right. This dish was even better straight from LALO's little kitchen and right into my belly. I added on a side of lumpia, too, and these little spring rolls were divine crispy parcels of goodness, served with a sweet chili sauce that had me quadruple dipping. 

Sis went for the bas-ka-bob over garlic rice and devoured it. I snuck a bite of her chicken and it was bomb af. So about that garlic rice, which is dynamite... You really get a pop of garlic flavor in each bite. I love that!

The owner, Jill, is such a lovely person. Beautiful inside and out, and passionate about Filipino food and culture and sharing it with Philly. We're lucky to have LALO, which served as our grand introduction to Filipino cuisine. The prices are reasonable for what you get. We'll both be going back!

Really not impressed. 
Being new to the city, I had heard this was a place to see. I've lived near and frequented many places like this: SF Ferry Terminal, Pike's Place in Seattle, Cleveland's West Side Market, Denver's The Source. This is like any of those, but with less diversity, dirtier, and with lower quality offerings. 

We came on a Friday morning so the crowds were not terrible. The Lancaster vendors looked to have the tastiest things in the whole place, and they weren't so concerned with everything looking absolutely perfect, like so many other booths. To me, perfection is not appetizing, it just looks like cardboard. As other reviewers have said, the feel of the place as a whole was not clean. We saw a mouse run in front of us while browsing in the bulk/spice store. Sadly I do not think this is rare in the Philadelphia area, but I will not help normalize that poorly managed behavior by patronizing a dirty business. Needless to say we skedaddled.

Last up, we went looking for produce. I had heard that this was one of the best "farmers markets" in the country. I think people who say that are confused. There were two produce vendors, one much larger than the other. One of them was offering disgusting, old, very VERY wilted leaf lettuces, a clue that they either don't understand their offerings or that they just don't care. The other had a much larger selection, but nothing unique. Bell peppers, citrus fruits, etc. Nothing you wouldn't find at a regular grocery store.

I came to this place hoping for new and interesting. I left disappointed and thoroughly disgusted.

You gotta love this place.  The unique selection, the Amish, VietNamese, Asian, Italian and American stands all crammed in together.  Sure it's a bit grimey and can get mobbed at lunchtime, but give me Iovine's Produce, Och's Chicken Breasts, Some Tom Kha Gai from Little Thai Market and a hot fresh macadamia nut cookie from 4th St and I am good to go.

It is a blessing to live nearby.

This is definitely the place to be if you're visiting Philadelphia.  It is pretty similar to the Grand Central Market in LA, but there are a lot more stores/vendors/restaurants.  There is a pretty large seating area and plenty of stuff to try.  I specifically tried Beiler's donuts because that was one of the donut place I wanted to try the most.  I think no matter what you're craving for, Reading Terminal Market will have it.  Stop by and check it out when you're in philly!
Best kati rolls i have had... especially their masala paneer rolls! I love this place, it's a must try!
a little of everything, in a truly philly way. a must-stop to eat place... too many options to choose from. my only caution is to be careful around closing time. shops will close up to an hour early
The best place for lunch and groceries in Philadelphia.  Great people, great food, great variety.  I must-see for any tourist.  I local staple.

Pretty Cool place! We have one of these in our city but not nearly as large. This market was primarily food and produce based but there were some other stalls as well. 

We stopped to get a cheesesteak at By George, which had a very large and good looking array of food. I would like to be able to stop in here on the regular but sadly my time in Philly is limited. 

Definitely stop in here if you are looking for some lunch, meat, produce the selection looked amazing.

Fast and always delicious. Excellent quick meal for taking on the go or a quick lunch break. I'm from a city where good Indian food is few and far in between, so I definitely visit this place anytime I make it to Philly.

Absolutely essential to experiencing Philadelphia. You need to check Beiler's donuts off your list and at least a bit of the PA Dutch homestyle food before you leave. Dinics is worth the wait - but off-hours makes it pretty easy. Both locals and tourists visit - I get the dollar bags of fruit & veg at Iovine's and the student discount on Wednesdays. It's amazing for people watching. Highly recommended for finding food for groups who can't decide upon a restaurant. Seating is limited, but that's what your easy-going friend who trusts you to order for them is for - designated squatter!! Not for the claustrophobic when busy!!
Always fun to bring friends here - can be really crowded sometimes but that is part of the experience!  From raw honey to donuts to grilled cheeses you can find everything here!

Excellent Lebanese food ... As good as Cava, if not better!  This NYC based chain won a Best of Philly award for a reason! This location uses Soumaya and Sons pita which is always a win in my book. I ordered the Kafta pita, which is made of half lamb and half beef meatballs. Surprisingly good for a fast casual chain ... Can't wait to check it out more items. The place was almost empty on a Friday at 12pm.
Diverse, tasty and a little bit of peace in a crazy city!

This is the perfect place to take visiting friends and family members for a lively meal/activity and a taste of Philadelphia's unique foodie cuisine. It's chaotic and introverts need to take deep breaths.  But it's worth it.

There are deep fried cheese curds for sale at one of the vendors; I don't remember the name, but they're a central PA-based company. It is one of the most delicious things I've ever eaten.

Great for a family where each member wants something different. They have tables to eat. You can get Prepared food or even fresh meat and produce. It's overwhelming at first, but make sure you get a map of all the kiosks. Top choices: By George (pizza and cheesesteaks), Beiler's (donuts), and Famous 4th Street cookie company (cookies). Great location. Parking is convenient but you have to pay in the garage.

Plenty of places to eat inside reading terminal. They also offer multiple produce stands. However they just purely need more space. More space to walk, more space to sit. It is so crowded inside it's like a battle just to walk. The food options are good however I do wish they would offer more seafood restaraunts.

This place is the bomb. I didn't even come hungry - just looking for a midnight snack - and I gobbled down the Chicken Pepperwala kati roll and Chicken Kheema roll like there was no tomorrow.

The white sauce and red sauce complemented the kati rolls well. The wrap was delicious and chicken was beautifully marinated. The rolls were not too oily and just the right amount of flavor.

Fast service. Great food. Best kati rolls I've ever had. Would come back again.

Dutch eating for breakfast.  Blueberry pancakes were huge definitely enough for 2ppl.  Overall food was okay, can't go too wrong with breakfast food.  Prolly better than other food alternatives in the area!

Super cute place right in the middle of uptown. They have so many different choices for good and drinks here. They have a huge chocolate shop which makes anything and everything. They also have an Indian cuisine spot which is what we tried and that was great. Their curry was perfect. We also got a smoothie from a smoothie place that they have there. It was fresh and delicious. It was also vegan so you know that is was all fresh fruits. Loved this place

First time at the Reading Terminal Market. It was soooo crowded yesterday afternoon! Not sure if Sunday afternoons are always like that or if it was just because there was an event at the convention center across the street. Lots of stores seemed to be closed and it was partially under construction. The market is basically Pittsburgh's entire Strip District compiled in one room in the same building. Upside: don't have to walk far to get everything you want. Downside: limited space, crowds, long lines, slightly hard to navigate.

I had pre-picked a few options to try. Unfortunately, most of them had such long lines, it would have taken 20 minutes just to order. I ended up going to Beck's Cajun and The Thai Market. Both had relatively short lines and were very tasty. After ordering, finding a table proved to be the most difficult part. There is limited seating and it seemed most were being occupied by people who weren't even eating (irritating). We tried to eat at a small vacant counter near a bakery and they asked us to move for sanitation reasons. We eventually found a seat, but it was not an easy task.

It's a really cool market. I've been to some similar set-ups that aren't as crowded and really love them. I definitely want to come back at a time when it's less crowded to get the full Reading Terminal Market experience.

This place is great. There's lot of yummy foods to choose from here. There's a grab and go bar for beer and wine and all sorts of foods and sweets. There's also a fresh produce and meats section.
Something for everyone.

No way is this the Reading Terminal of yesteryear. I used to regularly go in from the suburbs.  It seems many of the old favorites like Spice Terminal have been bumped out and replaced with Food Court style vendors. Prices are becoming exorbitant, geared towards the tourist types. It's hard to negotiate in the afternoon with all the beige types gawking but not buying. Avoid at all costs during anything like the Flower Show. The fact that many of the Amish vendors take a day off on Mondays makes a great deal of the market dark on that day.  I have a perfectly well stocked Wegmans and Trader Joe's in my vicinity which makes a trip to Reading Terminal lame at best.
Heaven on earth for foodies. Period. I love this place!!!!

Reading Terminal Market is like a massive Pennsylvania food court with something local for any Yelper to try ... and 2-3 things for me. 

Coming here has been a Philadelphia tradition since 1893 and it still ranks as an obligatory tourist attraction for city visitors. We came a couple times (over a week) to try different foods and shop a little in the other stalls. 

Recommendations include:
 * Beiler's Doughnuts (underrated donuts)
 * Miller's Twist (Warm Amish pretzels!)
 * Sang Kee Peking Duck (Beijing-style duck)
 * DiNic's Sandwiches (ok, yet overrated)
 * Spataro's Cheesesteaks (average, but historic)
 * Downtown Cheese (say Cheese!!)
 * Valley Shepherd Creamery (Grilled cheese please)
 * Bee Natural (Local honey)
 * Fox & Son ("If" you like corndogs)
 * Dutch Eating Place (Apple dumplings)
 * Flying Monkey Bakery (Red velvet whoopie pies)

Note that the Reading Terminal Market is open 7 days a week from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm (except major holidays), so, plan accordingly with your meal schedule.
This place was way to crowded to be enjoyable. The massive crowd made walking cumbersome. If your looking for something with your family, I would skip this stop.

Love Love Love this place. I saw on Time Out magazine that Reading Terminal Market is one of the best places to visit ones in Philadelphia. Happy to say I wasn't disappointed.

Food of all kind, Cajun, Seafood, Phillys, Japanese, coffee and best of all CHOCOLATE. 

They have little markets to buy some grocery's like vegetables, fermented food, honey, spices meat... ugh just an orgasmic place to be.

I especially loved the pastries the Amish made. Delicious everything in their amazing, check it out of your ever in the area!
I love the Reading Terminal they have really good food. They have so many stores where you can sit down and eat and talk. They also have cakes and pies all kinds of goodies.

Wow, this is probably the best food market I've been to. Not only are there myriad food outlets but the prices are quite reasonable. If I lived in Philadelphia anywhere near this place, here is where you'd find me.

The grocery store is as good as many stand-alone stores you find. Tubby's olive oil place is great for gifts. LeBus bakery sells divine biscuits and croissants. Gourmet and specialty food items available, too. The breakfast place has to be good because half of Philadelphia was either sitting there or queued up. And many others.

I'm sure the market gets crowded but at 8 AM on a Saturday it wasn't at all. We spent about an hour and the aisles were still navigable when we left.
Good location. Very friendly staff. Horrible wifi. Kicks you off every 5 minutes.
Excellent breakfast spot. Had the 3 egg scramble first time. Second visit had it with fried oysters. Delicious.

What's not to love about the Reading Terminal? They have a wide array of foods to choose from along with my favorite roast pork sandwich from Tommy DiNic's. I can't forget Hershel's, they have the best corn beef special. I could go on and on about all of the great places to eat in the terminal but check it out and judge for yourself.
amazing counter service and fresh food... one market is greater than the next
So many options that it is going to take weeks to try all of them. Only tried Dutch eating place so far and that was delicious!
Its alright, way too packed for me though. My office is nearby so i go for lunch every now and then. Don't come around then or the weekends unless you want to feel cramped in. Leave the room for me
Great food options and many different vendors to look at. Donut line gets crowded though!

Glad we stumbled into this place. After a long day doing tourist things, my family and I decided to go  inside this building called 'Bourse.' Little did we know we will find this gem of a place! The girl that greeted us was very welcoming...and cute. We weren't even hungry but she sold us on a couple of entrees. We weren't complaining tho because once we received our orders, they were was delish!! It was just what we needed! The lechon kawali was cooked to perfection and the lumpia was just perfect to share. We also ordered a couple of beverages. Too bad we have to go back to L.A. and can't visit this place anymore. But if you're in town, make sure you visit this place. You will not regret it.

I've been to other honeygrow locations and always enjoyed my food. Just picked up some food from this location, get home and opened it up. There was a tiny worm right there on my cilantro. I called the store and they said they'd give me a refund which I appreciate but now I'm grossed out and still hungry

Tried this place a few years ago and was disappointed, but thought I'd give it another try. Sat at the bar for happy hour, was served the most pathetic oysters I've ever seen. Also, they were difficult to stomach when the bartender kept snorting and spitting into the trash can repeatedly. The food was not good, fries tasted like they had been frozen. Recently moved to the neighborhood so was hoping for a good go-to happy hour spot. This is not it. Philly offers too many amazing restaurants to go to this one.

It brings me with quite disappointment that this Pizza place isn't quite what others have raved about. I was expecting an above 8 pizza. I'm from NYC and now living in Philly and finding a good Pizza place has been a mission. First off the place is very small as others stated so do plan to go. It's priced too high in my opinion. The smell was amazing and it looked very good, and I was hoping the taste would be equally as good. The crust wasn't crispy instead it was soft and flappy. The ends had way to much dough for my liking. The sauce wasn't that great, however their was a good portion of cheese. Overall the taste wasn't as good as I thought it would be. I recently went to Tacconelli's in port Richmond and was very impressed, and had the bar too high up thinking this place would be about the same or better. 
I definitely recommend Tacconelli's pizza first and it's cheaper too. I wouldn't come back here personally. Hope this helps

This is an update on a previous review.  I had a bad experience with a to-go order and posted a review about it commenting on how I was surprised since every other experience I'd had with Honeygrow was positive.  Management reached out, listened to my concerns, and assured me it wouldn't happen again, which I really appreciated.  I've been back several times since then and have only had positive experiences.  The food is always delicious and I the costumer support I received was outstanding.  If I'm being extremely picky, I wish the portions were a bit larger because the food is so good I'm always left wanting more.  Overall I'd definitely recommend Honeygrow to anyone looking for something tasty and healthy to eat.

I was in from out of town, and once I saw the reviews on yelp, I knew I had to check this place out. Reading Terminal Market did not disappoint! There is something here for everyone. We were able to try multiple restaurants within the market. I was a little upset that the line for the donut shop was going around the whole market, but that just goes to tell you how good it must be! I was able to try the ice cream, which was amazing! Overall, i would say checking this place out is a must!

Here you can- Eat in breakfast, lunch and dinner in food court style, and a few restaurant counter styles, shop for groceries, shop for produce,  shop food speciality( meat, dairy, gourmet chocolates, candies, baked goods), gift shop candles, home scents, local craft jewelry, honey and specialty teas, even grab some flowers and EXPLORE some Philly's best local goods, all housed under one roof, all 4 seasons!  

Reading Terminal is a historic and hallmark merchant house in Philly.  
A MUST for anyone visiting the city of Brotherly Love! 
Loads of restaurants, takeout, and restaurant counters to choose from.  Take out or share communal eating areas, sit in at 2 of the sit in restaurant/ dinners or pull up to one of restaurant counters. 
Enjoy the Amish farm fresh dairy and wickedly good bake goods. The Italian meat butcher counters are a treat. The Arab food fair, Creaole counter, many Asian varieties or Soul food are always a win. Tea counter for tea lovers and fresh juicing for those seeking healthy raw, vegan eating options!
Family friendly and culturally enriching environment for sure. Be it for self, something to share amongst friends or family,  or gift shopping for a unique gift ideas, Reading Terminal has something for EVERYONE!!!
I understand the healthy concept but sorry, not a big fan of this retail. I also think the price is a little bit high when It comes to a fast food retail.
Most rude staff at an airport I've ever encountered. It says on their menu they can make smoothies non diary. Not one staff knew that "non-dairy" meant. Ridiculous. Do not go here

I always come here when I have a layover. They've got something for everyone! This is a great place for eating with a group since you can grab whatever you feel like from one of the many many eateries.

Some of my faves:

Flying Monkey Bakery- Whoopie pies. Especially the pumpkin chai in the fall.

Dutch Eating Place- Apple dumplings!

Iovine Bros. Produce- Cheap produce and some random finds. I have a recipe that calls for Spanish onions, and I get them here because I can't find them back home. Might not mean a lot to some people but it's a treat when I get to bring home produce from the east coast.

Fair Food Farmstand- Yummy finds like honey infused with asian pear or blueberry. My favorite find was the Trinidad Scorpion peppers.

Tommy Dinic's- Roasted pork sammich. Get it!

Beilers Bakery- Apple fritters and blueberry fritters!! Delish!

So, basically, you're gonna leave here 10lbs heavier.

I just love this place. I live close by in Center City and its a prime place for lunch. There are so many options for everyone. Whether you are in town for business, a tourist or a local there is something for you.

It is exceptionally busy during lunch and some vendors may run out of specific items or meals. But getting your meal is quick and pretty hassle free despite the rush. Except the coffee shop's usually have a bit of a line.

I also love the produce section. Fresh and undamaged and basically no line ever. They even have flowers which I just adore.

Great, no line food was ok & one whineie baby.Nice staff &kid play area(witch I did'nt use) .Overall it was awesome!
By:Mitchell

Reading Terminal is a Foodie Mecca. The market hosts vendors selling everything from seafood and meat, to fresh produce, to sit-down meals. It can definitely be overwhelming, but worth taking your time and wandering around. You could spend hours visiting every stall and trying samples. While the Market is very busy and loud, it's a great place to grab some food and people-watch. Reading Terminal Market is a must stop when in Philly.

Pro-tip: Visit on an empty stomach!
I visited from California. We don't many good market here. It was so nice to be able to taste the flavors of the city all in one place b

We got 5 of each - Asian pork, buffalo chicken, chipotle chicken, Philly cheesesteak. All in all very interesting twist on dumplings. I really liked it. It's a small hidden gem not many hear of it. The cheesesteak could have had more cheese but my friend said they usually put a lot so must have been a different  day.

Can't really say much that hasn't already been covered by close to 5000+ reviews other than I wish I had two or three extra stomachs just to be able to try everything. Just keep an eye on the hours since a lot of the places started shutting down when we came here in the late afternoon and maybe try not to come on the weekends if you can't stand large crowds. 

Things we tried:
1. Blueberry and apple fritters from Beiler's. Donuts usually rank a little lower than cookies for me if I'm in the mood for something carb-y and sweet but this really knocked all of our socks off. The Boston creme was way too sugary. 

2. Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. Incandescent. I took a bite and levitated a few feet off the ground. I think this even beats Levain for me. It was so unbelievable. I went back the next day for another (original chocolate chip no walnuts - and yes, they do have a version with walnuts).

3. A ginger shot from the stand selling ginger drinks. 

4. Smucker's jerky. We went there on consecutive days to pick up some more. 

Didn't get to try some of the other famous options, like DeNic's sandwich and the apple dumplings. There was also a little tea stand that looked very promising and Pearl's oyster bar. Next time!

Update: I just want you to know that I haven't been back here or any Pizza Hut since you disappointed me. I'm still mad at the company as a whole, but more specifically this location - at your apathy and inaction regarding my personal dissatisfaction. I hope that one day, I'll somehow get the chance to serve you, so I can refuse to do so like you did to me when I placed my order on March 20, 2019. #StuffedCrustGate2019
Excellent pizza!!! I was worried there wouldn't be anywhere decent to get a slice nearby coming from New York. Can't recommend enough.

Philadelphia staple. Enough to choose from to please everyone.  Good to eat-in or shop for - well, pretty much anything food related. Try to avoid the lunchtime rush, its easier to wander around and take it all in during off-peak hours.

If you haven't tried a Train Wreck sandwich OR an apple fritter from that corner doughnut spot OR the salmon red curry from that other spot you're missing out! I'm just sad I don't live next door to eat there everyday...
I really enjoyed this place lots of great eats within the same building. It's not overtly large which makes it overwhelming. There is a wide variety of places to eat here.
Tried French Cannolis there. They were sooooooo good!!! So regretful that I didn't get more. Definitely will miss it.
Amazing. Anything you could want in terms of food. What a great experience. Especially enjoyed the distillery samples.

An awesome surprise to find right across from the Liberty Bell. We are full blooded Filipino's who love to cook and eat together as a family activity. We met up with family from VA and Hawaii at this place and ordered the meal for 4 x 2 since there are 8 adults and 2 kids in our group. The garlic rice was good, the lechon kawali was as it should be crispy and melts in your mouth, the lumpiang shanghai was okay, the atchara (pickled papaya) was a little bit to crunchy and cut too big, the longanisa tasted more like a sweet Italian sausage instead of the Filipino sweet and I mean sweet and garlicky sausage. The downer for me was the "bicol express". It's Vegan they said. But it is no where close to a Bicol Express in taste and look. I don't mind Vegan food but calling it Bicol Express is so misleading. Please change the name. Great counter people! They carry the hospitality, warm smile and welcome of a Filipino.

When you first enter, you are so disoriented and have no idea where to start. There are so many different vendors and stalls that I wanted to try everything. My recommendation start from one corner and work your way around. It is a little difficult to find seats and a table so do that before getting food.
Food is good, they give you the option to literally get every topping available. Down side, it's very crowded during lunch hours.
The best sandwiches and ribs in the city. It's worth the trip downtown the Amish really know how to cook. All your shopping needs in one location

All I can say is Reading Terminal is just A1 as far as in anything regarding what you have a taste for. You want sweets like desserts it's a lot of shops that a satisfy your sweet tooth. You want food it's too many places for me to name. Just know you won't be disappointed.

Coming from Boston I was BLOWN away as to how large this place was.  The smell from the various restaurants is absolutely intoxicating.  You can easily spend an hour or more just exploring the different restaurants and/or looking at the various produce on offer here. 

If you're visiting Philadelphia then this place is a no brainer to stop by and explore! (unless you hate crowds...then stay clear)

What a gem of a place to be lost in, there are so many choices and finds here and I tried walking the entire block to find one good eats and realized there are too many places I want to try but with so little time. I ended up with fried chicken and snacks along the way put of the terminal. 

There are over 50 unique eats here and the best place to be stranded while missing a train. There were not too many tables to sit at, you have to be lucky and grab a seat. I would recommend this place to everyone who can't decide what you want to eat but have time on your hand to find a gem.

Service was good here. Food was uninspiring at best. I got a chicken plate that really lacked much flavor. You can dump a ton of the white sauce and hot sauce, but then you might as well just drink the sauce. I would skip the chicken plate. 

The kati rolls were pretty good. I think that is the better choice to eat at this spot. Other than that, not terrible food, but not great. I would pass and go find something else to eat.

Pretty good for airport food. At least you can feel healthy eating a salad or some yogurt. I've had a couple salads here and they have been alright. The people are very friendly but the last time I was there it was incrediibly slow. That would have concerned me if I didn't have plenty of time for my flight. I think there may have been some new people training or something because they were all over the map on who was supposed to be doing what behind the counter.

I ordered 2 of thier rolls. the price was excellent and I just assumes they would be the size of eggrolls (which is why I ordered 2). The first had mint and coriander, chicken and forget other ingredients nice and spicy and it was gigantic. so large that for me I could not even consider eating the second one I bought. It was also chicken but forget now what else but the rolls were the first 2 on the roll side of the menu. I did take a bite out of the second one (I was staying at a  hotel and was having surgery the next day so i wasnt allowed to eat and couldnt take it with me to the hospital so I ended up throwing it out) That was also very good. I would go back to this restaurant anytime

Wow! The Reading Market is amazing! Here you will find the finest cuisine of Philadelphia, all in one place. Whatever you desire... It is here.  I would give it ten stars if yelp would let me. This is a foodie paradise. If you do nothing else while in philly, visit Reading market. If you are on a diet, save up your carbs and calories and spend them here. What the heck, its so worth it.  Double xtra super highly recommend!

Went here for breakfast 

WHY DID I NOT READ THE REVIEWS FIRST 

Before I could even go inside I was approached by 3 beggars asking for change. 

I step inside and felt like this place was a homeless shelter over night with a few still waking up.

Will never be back. 

When I get out side they are arguing about who was there first asking customers for change.

Kafta Lamb Kebab over salad was great, Chicken Shwarma was too dry for me - but that said I did not load it down with sauces and tahini.  I did try the (very good) baba gahannouj and (not as good) garlic whip - on the side.  The Yogurt-Cucumber was very nice also.  Tomatoes and cukes were fresh.

I got in and out for $10.50 (including tax) and had a BIG whompin' bowl of Lebanese-inspired goodness.

I shall return.  The Qdoba of Middle Eastern.

This is hands down the best kathi roll place in Philadelphia. Masala Paneer roll, lamb kebab roll and even the masala aloo roll are damn good. Their lamb and chicken platter is delicious too - similar concept as the halal guys but with their own twist. The decor inside is casual and clean. They have a couple of long high top tables for groups and also tables for a couple or smaller groups. Their front desk folks are the best people I have ever met in any Indian restaurant. Kudos to that. I have been here 5 times and have met 3 different people at the front desk. Everyone of them is very very humble, cordial, polite and nice.

The industry is literally blocks from my house. They offer good selections of beer. Burgers are pretty good here. If you love meat, go for double or even triple burger. I think my waitress was impressed that I finished my triple burger within 10 minutes! It was good. Avoid the seafood BLT though. I had the other day. It was deep fried and way too salty. It will be one of my regular stops.

Holy cow the place was empty!! Thst should of gave us a clue!! I was expecting Anna psencik Chinese dumpling house but what I found was a young white male at the counter I was looking at the menu and it was mixed with American and Chinese dishes. I saw lo mein and then he said snotty have u ever had lo mein!! I said are u being a smart ass and my husband and I left. I have to give a star which doez not deserve one

Okay so I recently went on a little weekend trip to Philly. First of all Philly is amazing and historical an awesome. Okay back to Reading Terminal Market. This place is so crazy delicious. Like I could walk through here like Pac-Man and Chomp everything! There is everything from Gourmet Meats cheeses and seafood and produce to ready to eat treats as well. There's communal sitting areas where you can all get your favorite things to eat from the different stands and eat together in the same spot. For sure this is a foodie spot. They even have live music. Checkout Kamal' for their delicious Rose mint lemonade. Sang Lee Peking duck house is the spot for some tasty and cheap Peking Duck and roast pork.. then hit dinic's for a roast pork sandwich but hold the greens. Carmen cheesesteak is Juicy and amazing. I mean there's a line. Stand on it and wait. There's also a place called meltkraft the most amazing cheese ever. I mean there's so many different combinations of grilled cheese is crazy. Unfortunately I wasn't able to shove everything in my mouth in that whole Market but fortunately I did have some friends with me but I was able to buy a bunch of stuff and we all shared it which is the way to go. I'll be back for sure because there's too many things I did not get to eat.

This place is super cool. So many choices in one convenient area and safe from the real weather outside. Closest thing in California is the Anaheim Packing District but there's a special charm that I like here. Maybe it's the efficiency and gruff customer service or that the food isn't frilly hipster food but authentic. Prices are more reasonable too.

Anyway, I kept going back during my stay in Philadelphia and didn't eat anywhere else really.

You can't go wrong in this beautiful foodie place! Visiting from LA and I love this market! Friendly atmosphere and enjoyed many of the food stands available. This place is a must when in downtown Philly!

This is one of my favorite places to visit in Philly. For the past five years, I have brought a high school Model UN team to a conference in Old City, and I walk to this market at least once each day we are here. The food options are amazing: I always visit Bieler's stalls (doughnuts and baked goods), and I get breakfast most mornings at Miller's Twists (pretzel-wrapped egg sandwiches). There are bakeries, delis, gift shops, chocolatiers, ethnic food kiosks, and coffee stands--and more. Even the pickiest eater will find something here to enjoy.
So many choices, it makes it fun just to walk around and people watch! Love Iovine's!

The donuts are good (not quite the same as the ones you get when going apple picking), they are sweet and thin. The oreo donut was really good. The frosting taste like oreo's. 

Had a brisket sandwich from the market, it was okay.

Great place to shop for food that is fresh, delicious and quick service. Desserts of all kinds from baklava to home made chocolates, wonderful, wonderful, wonderful. 
Parking is a problem. Wish they were open till 9 pm.

The packaging of my chips were very dirty. Like something had spilled on it some time ago. However the food was so fresh and yummy. There's always a huge line in drive thru but it goes by surprisingly fast.

Visited here while in Philly and was instantly overwhelmed by the sheer size of the offerings of this market. There were so many places to visit yet so little time! My strategy was to walk through the entire market first and then decide on what I wanted to eat. 

I gaped at desserts that were strategically placed at eye level to entice customers, lobsters chilling in their tanks, trinkets and colorful jewelry, and pickled pickles and meats. And these were all in addition to the fresh fruits, vegetables, and meats that were on sale. 

Not realizing all of the available food options here, I had made dinner plans so I opted for some ice cream. I will say though that the Philly cheese steak (with bacon) that was prepared for my colleague looked fantastic! Should I visit again, I'll be sure to grab one. 

I wished there were more samples but settled for some delicious banana pudding. I found a map of the market in the middle of the market and found it to be useful so I'm sharing in here.

Quite a lovely spot to visit when in the area. I'll be sure to pop in again for that cheese steak....

Avoid. This place is very dirty. People loitering inside who clearly are not paying customers. The vendors in our opinion are not serving the best quality food nor provide a great customer experience. Worth mentioning again this place is filthy.

Reading Terminal Market is very uniquely Philadelphia.

A market 97% entirely devoted to food from Amish pretzels, sweets, cheese steaks, ice cream, chocolates, fresh produce to Thai, Indian, huge jumbo shrimp, etc.  The size is huge as one needs a huge stomach to intake all the food with all reasonable prices.  The aromatic smell and flavor will entice patrons for a food crawl and continuous grub for more.
Very nice market!  Of course it is crowded but they have a good guide/map. Everything looks and smells good! I sat to eat at the Dutch Dinner and got delicious cookies! Everything was GREAT!

One of my favorite spots for quick, cheap, and delicious take out! I've had the chicken rolls and the paneer rolls and love all of them. They are always super flavorful. Love the white creamy sauce that comes on the side, and I would recommend getting an extra side of the green chutney. The red chutney is not my favorite, but good if you want to add some extra spice. One roll is usually enough for one person, although I have split 3 rolls among two people if I am super hungry.

Just as great as everyone else says! Despite the crowds on weekends and the children running around unleashed, this place is worth it!

Definitely recommend Miller's Twists, my all time favorite pretzel place. Also, Molly Malloy's is a safe haven in the middle of all the chaos with seating and delicious food to share. From Molly Malloy's I recommend the brussel sprout satay, butternut squash croquettes, and goatcheese flatbread. Perfection.
Reading terminal market is so much fun! I picked up cannoli sat termini and then had lunch with a friend over in the Amish diner area.

Very crowded locations with all types of business and stores. Did not visit the restrooms so could not tell if they are clean and maintained. The quality and service of the stores in this market is very good. The fruits are very fresh and the price is just right, not as pricey as other marketplace.

Wall-to-wall five star ratings don't intimidate me. Philadelphia's Reading Terminal Market is a logistical nightmare. Sure, the food selections are global in scope and generally delicious but seating is at a premium and movement through the clogged labyrinth of stalls and tributaries is downright dystopian. 

I have no idea who's writing these hosannas to the RTM but all I saw was a bunch of grim faced fun seekers choking on their pulled pork and cannolis while balancing on one leg in the maelstrom. 

I know that I'm in the minority here but this contrarian is absolutely not passing Go, not collecting $200 and definitely not taking another ride on the Reading Railroad.

Love this place. It is all about the food: fresh produce, seafood, meats, and tons of places to eat. There are all cuisine to dine at in the Reading Terminal Market. It was really busy during the lunch time, so seating may be difficult.
Fun exactly what u'd expect.. had fun wondering around. Some interesting leathers for sale, got a delicious cannoli, there also a lovely oil place.  Worth checking during lunch time..

We stopped in after the Fishtown FestivALE around 5pm and were lucky enough to grab the last two slices of pizza (they make a certain number of pies a day and close once they are sold out). The pizza here is thin, fresh out of the oven and was really really good. I will have to give it another try before I call it the best I've had in Philly but it's definitely up there. Store is small but turnover at the tables were quick so we were able to eat there.
Love RTM.  Went here with my family while doing sight seeing in Philly.  Forgot how great it was.  We all had something great to eat and just loved it.

This place is a madness. We had tickets for the taste of Philly. We spent 20 minutes walking and fighting through crowd and could not find any food. Every vendor we visited, they were out of food. The only thing that we could get was liquor, but we wanted something to eat, not liquor. So, we left there to find a restaurant so we could eat.

This place is freaking awesome. I only wish there is something like this in New  York. The lines move quickly. It is crowed. But how convenient to have good food all in one location. Many, many options to choose from. My favorite was the pork and broccoli rabe sandwich from danic's. and Bassett's ice cream. There are many booths for grocery shopping aside from cooked food.
Decent service but the "healthy" smoothie was disgusting. Way too sweet. I believe it's made with soft serve ice cream. Not a healthy smoothie at all.

Large indoor market in downtown philly. You can find ANY kind of food here: tacos, BBQ, burgers, cheesesteaks, desserts. You name it they have it. Some of the best food philly has to offer. Excellent place for diverse eaters, and so many options to try out. Negatives about this place is that it can get crowded with longer lines and limited seating. It's also not the most clean area due to the amount of people that will pass through here everyday, but it's good enough. 
I've been going here since I was a kid and I love the food that is offered here. 
Must go to eating spot for locals and tourists!

Who doesn't love this place from the fresh meats to the sweet treats this is a go to if you visit ivon brothers for your fresh fruits and veggies ...Carmen's famous steaks is the BEST cheesesteak place I say in all of Philadelphia,  for sweets Beilers for the best doughnuts and the best stop for all your meats Giunta's hands down and for alll the vegan lovers you have to stop at Luhv friendly staff good eats worth it that vegan tuna is Life
Nothing to say but I go once a month. It is fun, delicious and, reasonable don't deny yourself the experience if you are close to it.

The experience was good in my opinion and the staff seems pretty laid back, but they treated me with respect and like a customer. I had to wait a few for fries as they didn't have any read after converting from breakfast to lunch.

My chicken was good, the fries were delicious, but the biscuit was slightly overcooked as the exterior had a crunch and the interior was a bit on the dense side, but the flavor was good.
Whatever you want. Meat, seafood, vedge, sweet, savory. Breakfast lunch dinner. Greek, Indian, Italian...ahhh I could go on....
Reading Terminal Market is a great place! So many varieties of food and cute little kiosk shops to browse.

Pretty much used to live here and got to explore every vendor there. 
Mullers=best chocolate ever.
Bassetts=excellent turkey sandwiches. Try the #2 with sourdough.
Kang Se duck. Try their soup. The best; wonton noodle soup with sliced pork!!
Thai place...(the name of the establishment eludes me at this time) has the best basil chicken and bamboo shrimp!
I could spend days in the RTM.....great spot!

The place looked dirty. I convinced my friends to come here instead of their competition, unnamed. I frequent the chains in NY and NJ and I was so embarrassed. The trays for attendant's were bare, not replenished well. The attendants were not pleasant, no forks or napkins available at station, tables weren't wiped, i was embarrassed. I even thought their food was not as tasty. An epic fail. I gave it a two cause the nachos were good, the guac was also missing something. Just an embassed outcome.

One of the top destinations to hit when in Philly! Too much to see too much to eat. Was pleasantly surprised to see an eatery that lives up to the hype. When you first walk in you can pick up a map, that's right a map! Lots to eat and see. Hustle and bustle crowd. It's everything I like in an eatery. Long lines, no problem! We were recommended to come here and glad we did as our second stop on our food tour in Philly.

Went to Beiler's for donuts, best was the apple fritter but the Oreo donut was awesome too. Then dropped by Sang Kee Duck for some roast pork and duck. Both were pretty good, not the best I've ever had but hits the spot. After that we walked around to see which place had the best hot pastrami sandwich because well we just wanted one! So we stopped by Hershel's and ordered it. Short line, toasted up and prepared to perfection! Delicious pastrami but alas we could not finish the sandwich. Box it and doggy bag it for later! After being stuffed with enough food for 3 meals we decided it was time to finally leave. We still had some other places to eat like the Cajun spot and cheesesteak (line was long) but just couldn't fit any more food in our bellies!

****THE GOOD****
- Atmosphere. Nothing like it in Philly where you get everything under one roof. Market style so it's busy but that adds to the charm IMO.
- Beiler's for donuts but the star here are the fritters. We had apple but I'm sure blueberry is good too.
- Hershel's for good deli sandwich. We had only the hot pastrami which rivals any NY deli. I believe the owner is from NYC.
- Sang Kee Duck was decent. Not the best and not bad. Come here if you need a Chinese food fix and roast pork and duck are pretty good.

****THE BAD****
- The lines can get long during lunch but it's worth the wait if you have the time.

****THE UGLY***
- Must have a bigger tummy for food!

Pretty darn good. I had to remember to take a photo of my slice before I finished crushing it... I got today's special (mozz, jalapeños, onion) and it's amazing. You can tell by the quality of the crust and the cheese that these guys know how to make a good pizza. I'm almost tempted to get a second slice but the first one was so gigantic I don't think o can eat two. Nice work, Pizza Shakamazing.

The first time I came in I ordered the Tikka Roll and the guy at the register could tell I had never been there before and suggested I try the Paneer Masala Roll. It is seriously one of the BEST things I have ever eaten. I have been back a few times since then. Nice people (with good suggestions) and quick service. Not a lot of "atmosphere," but for fast food, do you really care?

A place for tourists and locals. Filled with whimsical products like chocolates in the shape of organs and  everyday necessities like fresh meat, cheese, and vegetables at very reasonable prices. 

Tourist highlights and some of my favorite places to take visitors:
Beiler's Bakery - blueberry fritters and apple fritters are out of this world
Termini Brothers - cannoli are freshly filled and delicious 
Kitchen supplies store (I forgot the name) but there are cute and useful supplies inside 
Herbiary - beautiful herb products that smell great and organic soaps/lotions 

I love buying produce from OK produce (.99$ blueberries?! $1 pepper grab bags). You really have to pick and choose, but you can't beat the price. Iovine Brothers has a larger selection of provide and is great as well. 

For meats, I like Godshall's for poultry and Martin's for other meats.

This gem is perfect for healthy on the go or even a quick retreat within the city!

The food is healthy, fresh, and eventful. Concept is similar to a chipotle where you pick and assemble, but these guys do it better than other variations.

The portion is  generous so you're not leaving this place hungry! It's also well packed so it's easy to take on the go. 

The inside is fresh with  plants and a enviromental sustainable theme. 


Everything about this place made me feel good about eating here. Even the employees are courteous and on rope of their game.

This place is by far the pride of Philadelphia when it comes to food. You can find just about everything here and it is all fresh. We went there twice in the last few weeks and each time it was a new adventure.

Awesome place to visit. Lots of great things to eat. I love the Cajun place, Becks. 

This "Terminal" gets bee crowded on Saturday.

This place is overwhelming with so many places to eat, so there are so many smells. Some of my favorites there are Beiler's (amazing donuts!!) and Meltkraft (delicious grilled cheese!!). It's a cool experience to check out, but not my favorite place to go for a bite. I like showing people around as it is a staple for Philly. Definitely worth it to check it out once and see if it's for you! It has food to eat from all different cuisines, something for everyone.
This was an awesome place to visit while in Philadelphia we were here for a convention and it was easy to get to from the hotel and provided lots of different types of food

Very cool spot, reminds me of any other open market I've been to similar in New York & Chicago. Everything you can buy you didn't think you'd need, haha. From sushi, to barbecue, vegan places and candy shoppes galore. Don't forget the cheesesteaks- this is Philly after all! Expect to pay between $15-17 for a fully loaded sandwich.

I honestly loved everything about The Industry.

The food was awesome (more on that shortly), the beer selection was great, and the restaurant itself had this awesome cross breeze going on a warm summer-ish night between the open doors on each end of the restaurant and the ceiling fans. 

So the food:
Buffalo cheese curds (exactly what you'd expect) but super delicious.
Short Rib Pierogies, these were the only thing that was a bit of a miss for me. The short rib wasn't' very tender and the pierogis were kind of dry but the flavor was actually still pretty good.
Fried Chicken Sandwich - AMAZING. It has bacon jam. 
Steak Frites - also a winner according to my dining companions. 

The Industry has a very trendy/cool/clean vibe that I love. I would recommend this place for fun with a friends, a casual date night, or a as a great place to watch a sports game.

I went in for a kids quesadilla meal to go and they forgot to give me my quesadilla !!! No big deal mistakes happen , what is really wrong here is that when I called to see what could they do for me considering that I wasn't gonna go back for my quesadilla after driving 20 minutes ... they pick up the phone and hang up right away !!!!!!! So angry now and not because they didn't give me my order but because they don't want to pick up the phone ! This is ridiculous !!! Called three times and all three times they did the same thing ! People check your order when you're taking out

Great place to go and visit (especially if it's your first time in Philly)! They have a variety of meal options and some other cool stands. I expect it'll be a lot better as things start to re open. My favorite place is the Amish stand with all their various jams, jelly, and popcorn.
Doesn't get better than this people. If you go to philly, you must go here. Haven't hit a spot here yet that isn't amazing!
Good pizza! Fresh and the ingredients are tasty! Try the special! Closed from 4-5 pm!

Reading terminal market is a foodies home away from home. So many choices with so little time. 

I could live there. It's so busy and so big. Love this place because of the variety of delicious options you have. theres everything you can think of. But be ready to fight for a table to sit down and eat. I guess that adds to the reading experience. 

I can't get enough of it. I will probably be having lunch there for the next few days I'm in philly. The good thing is the people working and providing the service there are so nice and polite. 

We will meet again reading we will!

My favorite spot to shop and graze my way around!  From the gyro to the beer and everything in between from Condiments to ice cream to flowers to donuts to Amish food to seafood to Molly Malloy's. Family oriented and creating the next foodie generation.

This is one of my favorite places to eat at after a long night out! The chicken masala and aloo paneer rolls are my absolute favorite! They're big and so flavorful - 2 definitely fills me up. 

It's also one of the few spots open late night so get ready for it to be crowded and have a line. No worries though because it goes by pretty quickly.

Solid 3.5 stars! Chicken was a little dry. I ordered the shish taok with hummus, baba ganoush, and yogurt cucumber sauce with picked radishes. The yogurt cucumber sauce and picked radishes were both put on top of the baba ganoush and hummus instead of on the chicken or rice. So it just like one heap of sauces. Vermicelli rice were a nice change though! I don't live in this area so I usually frequent another middle eastern place on spring garden.

OMG! Been waiting forever for a Kati roll place to come to center city Philly. Good Indian fast food is definitely lacking around here. Was so excited a month ago when I got a flyer saying this place was open. Sorry to Marabella meatballs. 
Went in here for lunch today. Alot of the decor was leftover from the previous restaurant but it was really nice and clean inside. Service was also friendly and quick. I got the chicken briyani rice platter with white and hot sauce on the side. They didn't make my dish on the spot but that's ok because it was still really good. Flavor was spot on. Maybe a tad oversalted. They're very generous with their portions. Lots of meat and rice.  My co-worker got the chicken and lamb over rice which he said he enjoyed. Oh and prices were really decent too. Comparable to NJ and I'm pretty sure rental isn't cheap around here. Will be coming back time and time again if they keep up the good work! Please stay open!
Iconic Philadelphia shopping.  Felt very safe with the COVID-19 procedures in place.  One stop grocery shopping in center city

Great choice of food and products from all around many states and countries and all in one place. Nice vibe with the produce market with excellent quality produce with great price. I will have to get back to this place in the future. There are many things I want to try and I can't just do it in one day visit only. The other thing that I would like to get next time is the pastries. There are donuts, pretzels, cakes but I didn't have enough room in my stomach for all of them. What a great place in the middle of the busy downtown area. This place is packed during the week specially during the lunch time. Sometimes it takes time to get a table to eat the food that is eager to be eaten.
A smashing of different shops and vendors, Reading Terminal Market is a hustle of smells, flavours, and people.

Go Go Go... Fresh Seafood, Cuts of Meats, Delicatessen Cheeses.. plus numerous restaurants to grab a bite at and delicious deserts to choose from.. you can spend hours in this Market.. Worth the trip!!!
Have never seen SO many choices of foods in my life. You could spend weeks trying different things at one vendor. And there were SO many vendors!
Numerous options here it's a little pricy but you can get almost anything you want. Go before lunch hour in order to avoid the crowds and lines.
This place is great but doesn't hold a candle to the Lexington Market in Baltimore, Maryland. That is the only reason it's getting 4 stars.

Good neighborhood pizza, not great, it's better than Pizzeria Beddia in my opinion. It's a small place. Don't expect to go there and sit down to eat. Standing room only. Not worth going out of your way to eat.

My best friend and i have been non-stop raving about the pizza for a week. We split a slice each of: tomato pie, white special pie and pepperoni and they were all fantastic. There are very few slice shops like this in the city and it met all of our expectations. I'd go back again and again...and again. Do not miss a chance to get a slice from Pizza Shackamaxon if you're in Fishtown/NoLibs.

Foodie heaven. Walking into the market is highly overwhelming, as any foodie market tends to be. However, as a tourist this is an ideal place to go and explore.

No matter what food stand we went to, the lines were crazy long but they moved fairly quickly. We went to George's where they offered a variety of options for cheese steak lovers. One order of the sandwich with some additional toppings was about $11, not bad.

As we continued to explore I came across an all gluten free Indian/Pakistani Stand. I am not allergic to gluten but lately I've started to do some research and inform myself of what it means to become gluten free. So when I saw this stand I was so excited! It was so cool to see a such a unique option available. I went for the chicken wrap with mild sauce (sauce is not gluten free, but they were nice enough to notify me when I requested it). The wrap was about $8 and so delicious! It did not leave me extremely full but at the same time I wasn't left hungry, it was the perfect portion. 

Lastly, I had to have some dessert and went to Bassette's Ice Cream. I chose their cookies and cream shake which was yum! Other people had ordered shakes before me and had extravagant orders (with whipped cream, chocolate syrup etc), whereas mine was a simple shake. Nevertheless it was delicious. If you are ever in Philly make sure to stop here! There are so many options to choose from and you will not be disappointed.

Reading Terminal Market is a must visit destination! It's very busy any day of the week, but very worth it. There are stations from produce, to meats, to ice cream, to cheesesteaks, and so much more! There ARE restrooms too, so unexpected!

I was craving something sweet to enjoy with my friends later in the day. Considered the fudge place, famous cookies, hand rolled doughnuts, but opted for a Banana Nut Loaf from Beiler's Doughnuts. Don't regret it! It was just under $7, and easy to carry on my walk and subway ride home. The loaf was SO fresh! Perfect level of sweet, but not overpowering as banana usually is.

Can't wait to come back to the market to try another item!

Great indoor market. Very similar to the markets in Los Angeles and Seattle. A large variety of different cuisines and shops! Everything I've eaten during my many visits have been perfect experiences!

We stopped in to have lunch on the recommendation of a few people.  There were a lot of food options, so many that it was difficult to decide what to eat.  There were 2 of us together and we each chose a different place to get our lunch.  Neither of us was disappointed with our choices.  That said, I don't know that this place would come to mind if people asked me for a recommendation on what to do in Philadelphia.  It was crowded and out of the way for us.  While our lunch was good, I'm sure we could have found a good lunch that was more convenient for us.  So I guess my recommendation would be to stop in if you're in the area, but don't go out of your way.

Reading terminal is a huge space with a plethora of choices to the point of being slightly overwhelmed. Coming here on a weekend might not have been the best decision, due to the large crowds. You can find pretty much anything you want to eat in this place, along with great items that would make a great present or souvenir. There are things to suit every taste and diet. I will definitely be going back before I return home. But it will definitely be on a week day.
So many things to try, so much good food. I highly recommend a visit there no matter where you are in the city!

One of the coolest places I've ever been!  Online, this place looks like somewhere you can order a variety of food from.  In person, this place is sensory overload!

The variety of retail options boggled my mind!  I still can't fathom the food options.  I could have eaten cheesesteaks, Mexican food, Cajun food, bbq, steak sandwiches, crepes, classic American comfort food, and even multiple types of ice cream. Besides a meal, you can buy candy, fresh fish, fresh meat, and just about any souvenir you want.  

I'd almost consider moving to Philadelphia purely to shop here over and over again.  "SHUT UP AND TAKE MY MONEY!"
Friendly staff, brand new slick interior decor and furniture- a new wendys!  Food still not as hot as i prefer, but this location is 10times better than any of center city's.

I could stay a whole weekend in just this market!! WHOA. How cool of a place, with so many little amazing shops to walk around in, I can't tell you how much time I wish I had! Ended up stopping by a few shops to get some yummy treats, but I wish I hadn't have eaten for a week so I could eat everything in sight!! I do wish there was a little bit of an organization of where places were inside and that was coordinated a little better; for example: meat places in one corner, bakery in another, etc. but overall I had a wonderful time here and I wish I never would have left. 

Honestly told my best friend that I am coming back to Philly just to eat here again... among other things, but yes it was AMAZING.

So cute.  I thoroughly enjoy coming here and boyfriend was right when he said we would probably be here every weekend if we lived in this place.  It can be very crowded and slow paced (probably partly due to tourists like us) but is a great experience.

Don't exactly remember all the specific names, but here are some great places to try out:

-Shwarma place: amazing shwarma and they also have delicious berry smoothies here that are so refreshing!

-Nut/Olive Oil places:  these are right by each other near the back and have great products.  The olive oil place, Tubby Olive, offers samples of a bunch of its oils/viniagrettes and the majority of them are just spectacular.  Too bad they are expensive.. very difficult to select which to buy because they are all so good.  My recommendation is to try the White Cranberry and the Mushroom&Sage.

-Fish!  There are several places with fresh fish, including sashimi grade fish, giant shrimps as big as your head, crab legs and some really fresh looking other things.  Very attractive displays.

-Beef Jerky!  Cheese!  These stores are near each other too and have great unique selections and also offer up free samples.  The beef jerky place is especially interesting.

There are tons of other things in here: fresh produce, Japanese restaurant, Italian restaurant, several places offering deli meats, coffees, teas, kitchen supplies, hippie products, candy!  Amish people.  You can spend a good two hours just winding around here looking at things and the time just flies.

I find myself back here every time I am in Philadelphia and just burst with excitement every time I see those Christmas lights and the cow sign.  Such a fun place and I love it!

5 Stars, but due to the overwhelming crowdedness it needs to drop to 4. This place is a foodies freakin' dream! I didn't know what to expect really. Upon entering my eyes shifted all over, food stands galore, long lines and lots and lots of people. Everything looked so good. I wish I could have tried a bunch of different stands, but ended up at The Rib Stand. I wouldn't recommend this place because the Mac and Cheese wasn't good and neither were the Green Beans. The Meat was good though. They also sell random items throughout the market like groceries, soap, books, etc.

Crowded and busy, full of people slowly walking, obstructing your ability to get to food. Seating is less than ideal. 

Otherwise, multitude of wonderful options. All the food I've had is great. You mostly can't go wrong. You may get some decision fatigue because of all the options.

I would love to get back to the Reading Terminal Market more, though I will advise that Sunday isn't the best day to go. I recently visited on a Sunday and discovered that a number of the vendors were closed for the day - and for what it's worth, Wikipedia notes "The Pennsylvania Dutch merchants (a small but significant minority) generally do not operate Sunday through Tuesday". I say this because my cousin and her husband had heard from friends about the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants, so they were a bit bummed that the timing didn't work out to visit their location during our time at the market. 

All told though, this enclosed market offers a nice variety of coffee, dessert, and food options (if I lived in the area, I'd be going here all the time to buy fresh produce). There are also a variety of florist-type places and the like that add a great brightness to the market. I grabbed a coffee early in our stop at the market and enjoyed the experience of wandering through the place and taking in all the smells and sights around me. 

Prices with most vendors are reasonable, though also know that some portions of the market can get very congested (and very quickly) as the day goes on. This last time, I think we all arrived around 11am (and we managed to grab parking on the street right outside the market), but we were there about 20 minutes and the market really started to fill up. The place serving crepes, for example, had SO MANY people around it. 

TL;DR  Would certainly visit again, but I'd pick a different day of the week (Wednesday or Thursday, maybe?) and get there earlier in the day. Enjoyable experience though.

This is one of the must stops when in Philly.  It has everything one could wish in a market: vendors selling fresh produce, meats, seafood, poultry, coffee shops, bakeries including several Amish and numerous dining establishments.  It can be a wee bit overwhelming when you first walk in.   We  brought a map of the market and it assisted us in getting around.  It is next door to the Convention Center and close to the historical district so we were by a few times.  As I was at a conference at the Convention Center with thousands of attendees, there were often line ups over the lunch hour with many of the dining establishments.

Loved the variety of vendors and the smell of the baked good and food cooking.

Happy to recommend Reading Terminal Market when in Philly.
We love this place we really like picking out what foods we enjoy knowing they are all good. I had turkey dinner had to share it was so big !!

The place has some staples that you cant get anywhere else in philly... but its a mad house in there.  with that being said there are only a few places in the market worth the hassle.  but you're going to have to figure that out on your own... that's really the fun of this place though.  the discovery.  but after you've discovered what's good you basically don't go back until you've succumbed to your urges lest you wait in those unforgiving lines.

I had this once before and enjoyed it. I couldn't remember why it's taken me so long to go back. After I got my meal today I finally remembered why. I am basically spending $10 on just rice.

I got stir fry with ground turkey and green beans. I really like the flavors but could probably replicate it for a quarter of the price. What irks me is that I got about a spoon full of ground turkey and five small green beans. The rest of my container is brown rice. And they didn't even fill up my container to the top! I know $10 is not much but when rice is 3/4 of the meal then I feel I did not get my monies worth. I probably won't go back.
We are from Baltimore and our own Lexington Market just doesn't compare.  Fantastic variety, service, cleanliness.

This wonderful indoor farmers market is in the original Reading Railroad Terminal, a historic landmark. 

With purveyors of every possible food, it's fun to wander around gathering ingredients for whatever feast to come. I also enjoy having lunch or taking prepared food out from a number of restaurant stalls. 

Among my favorites are: 

Diener's chicken. The Amish do chicken right. I love their classic whole chicken and wings. They've recently added a few nice varieties of chicken, and 
roasted vegetables. 

Dinics for roasted pork with sharp provolone, onions and peppers. 

Hershel's - pastrami is worth dying for. I like the Reuben with Cole slaw. A half is enough for me for months.  

Sang Kee - duck noodle soup. 

Pearl's - snapper soup, breakfast burrito. 

Old city coffee

Famous 4th Street cookies

The best in philly and it's not close, the white (special usually) is the best white I've ever had and the red is very close behind. The only prob for me is the pieces are so big I can't do both so I have to always choose between the 2, white (special) usually wins

A must see if you are in this part of Philadelphia.    Right across the street from the convention center has what seems like hundreds of different vendors of every kind of food you can think of.  I could eat in there every day for a year and still not try everything.  I only wish it was open for dinner.

This place is crazy crowded on the weekends. But I love it anyway.

You can get everything from duck eggs, to fresh honey, fresh meat, corn tortillas ... anything!  I like to come here for a quick meal (though I can never choose!)  Molly Malloy's is also pretty legit.

I love the Amish Bakery. Pro Tip: Saturday afternoons everything is half off at their baking counter!

What is up with all the glowing reviews?! I guess some people will rave about any cheap food...

For starters, this food is not 'Indian.' It's plentiful, spiced and seemingly fresh but where are the delicious, fragrant spices that are the hallmark of good Indian food? Where the hell is the naan?

My vegetarian friend and I visited here yesterday. She will eat just about anything provided it has no animal flesh, so I can't really trust her opinion. The place is clean and the folks behind the counter seem genuinely welcoming, helpful and pleasant. They play dreadful American music that seems geared at getting patrons out as soon as possible, but they were all kind, helpful and gracious to us and other customers who came and went as my friend P. and I dined.

We both decided on the platters with rice, lettuce and pita (!) bread. I got the MK chicken, P. got a paneer dish. My dish came with 'white sauce' and I have no idea what it was. It did not have much of a taste; no yogurt tang, some discernible bits of stuff that could have been spices but had no taste. There is also a big pump dispenser of it, along with an equally big pump dispenser of a red hot sauce. That one just tastes hot, but in a flat, sort of chemical way. 

The food was served in a deep, round aluminum dish which would make a good container if you ordered take out. There was a lot of lightly orange colored rice and it did not taste like basmati. On top of the rice was chopped iceberg lettuce. No dressing. It was limp from the heat of the rice. I got a large amount of mostly shredded boneless white meat chicken that had that same generic hot spice and red sauce on it and over that was drizzled the mystery white sauce. To one side was 4 triangles of spongy, moist, limp and very bland pita bread. The dish was not visually appealing. The rice was bland, the pita bread was pathetic, the limp, warm chopped lettuce was atrocious and the chicken could have been any kind of warm, one note spiced protein. It was not juicy or dry-it just was. The shining part of the meal was the mango lassi. These are premade and sitting in a refrigerated cooler. Not too sweet, very thick and full of flavor. 

At different times in our meal, a server came over to check on us to see if we needed anything. Again, I was impressed by the genuine hospitality of the people working there, though it did not make up for the lackluster food. 

P., who eats very fast and tends to over eat as a result, said she felt 'great' after her meal. I just felt sad.

I just can't say enough about how much I loved this market. My husband and I visited Philadelphia for a week in May and stayed about a block from Reading Terminal. This made it easy for us to visit during the week days, when the market is much less crowded. I think we had some sort of food from nearly every stall. 

Some of the best food in Philadelphia (and probably the country) lurks behind the colorful and brightly lit counters that line the aisles of the market. Not only is the food incredible, but every time we went there (every day, sometimes twice a day), I was pleasantly surprised by the kindness and pride that the vendors exuded. You can tell the people here take their food seriously. This place was my spirit animal, if locations can be spirit animals.

Best things we ate while there: the salted caramel doughnut from Beiler's; the corned beef rueben from Hershel's Deli; ANY grilled cheese from MeltKraft (we tried three); cannoli from Termini Bros; roast pork w/broccoli rabe from Tony DiNic's; gator gumbo from Beck's Cajun Cafe; shrimp & grits Benedict from Pearl's Oyster Bar. Plus, you can grab an adult beverage from Molly Malloy's and walk around the market with it - because what doesn't taste even better after a few cold ones?

Reading Terminal Market deserves every 5 star review it gets as it has everything you need. It has a large selection of restaurants, cafes and delis and some of the best food you can get in the area, including DiNic's Roast Pork.

If you need good coffee, you'll find a place in the market. If you need a quality breakfast sandwich, you'll easily find a bakery or cafe that has one. Deli sandwich. Thai food. Pretzels. Donuts. So many good options in Reading Terminal Market.

Overall: This is a must visit place in Philadelphia and it never disappoints. Just be prepared for busy lines, especially during the weekends.

Pizza is so thin, the crust is so crispy. They sell by the slice. It is heated up for your order. You can buy tomato pie too in slice or as a whole. The tomato pie has thicker dough. You will be asked with crust or no crust. With crust means you get the corners. Definitely get this, so crispy. Tomato sauce is very fresh. 

Service is great and friendly.
The best and cheapest and most fun plaCe!!! Their produce is best, lovely flowers, and best food! So much fun and have everything

I'm in this airport all the time. Every time I come here, this place never has string beans ! Why?? Maybe they can't afford them??? I don't know but, it's really bothering me...and I've never been at a Popeyes where you can't get a string bean! Not everybody eats Fries! I definitely have a problem with several restaurants in the Philadelphia Airport. The customer service is bad here all around! Keep your money & don't patronage this Popeyes! 
The "Flight Attendant"

Miss the more local appeal of being a place for residents....It has become more of a place for tourists and lost some of the rawness which was both good and bad.  Sort of lost its magic and now is like a food court at a mall.

5 stars, ya!

so what cant you find in this place? its a cornucopia of eatable delights for sure!

my family of five was able to find five different things for lunch, all were at least above average and pretty cheap in context.
