i mean, the place is a zoo (not the real philadelphia zoo, thats another yelp) so we couldnt find ANYWHERE to sit as a family and even when we found a high table with no chairs we struggled, but we made it work.

they also had some cool cooking expo going on in the back, my kids weren't as interested as we hoped, call us surprised. 

thems the eats

This really deserves high praise.  I would not normally say this but anything below 3 stars is insulting.  I loved Philadelphia, I prefer it to NYC, and it's up there w Chicago.  This market is one of those places that make Philly truly great.  You want the best baked goods, fish, coffee, meat, lunch, dinner, etc, etc. this is the place.  We went each day and it was great, a must visit.
Super dirty inside. We went to a bar for wings(they weren't good) and drinks and there were flies all around. Probably won't go back.

Love come here every time I visit my brother. 

You can find any type of food you like, sweet or savory. Even buy your grocery from here. Some stalls are cash only, while others takes card. 

It is street parking.

There is a cheese shop that I love to get my cheese at and the famous 4th street cookie was delicious! I want to try the gumbo at this cajun stall and another that sells duck.

Longanisa hotdog was so dry and flavorless that I had to add sand to moisten and add flavor.  The dry doggie toy-like sausage was so far removed from actual good traditional longanisa, that I fear that if someone tries Filipino food for the first time at this outpost, they would be put off from ever eating Filipino food ever again.  Sayang naman.
Got cannolis for my sons birthday and they were outstanding.  They don't skimp on the filling and the shells were baked fresh that morning.  Highly recommend.

Amazing fine vendors. My favorites are the Fair Trade stand, Iovine produce, the local-product meat stand, Schmidt's German deli, a couple of cheese stands, Metropolitan Bakery, Old City Coffee...but all are worth checking out. 
Besides the cheese steak vendors ( I hate them all), the most popular lunch stand is the Asian vendor in the south-central section. You can tell by the long lines.

Tolle Markthalle! Auf jeden Fall ein MUSS, wenn man in Philadelphia ist. Egal ob frisches Fleisch, Gemüse, Obst usw. alles ist da. Sehr ansprechend präsentiert in großer Vielfalt und Auswahl.
Jede nur erdenkliche Nationalität auch bei den warmen Speisen. Die alte Halle hat ihren ganz eigenen Charme. Dadurch, dass viele Stände von Armish People betrieben werden, hat man auch ein bisschen das Gefühl einer Zeitreise. Spannende Mischung in dieser Halle. 
Man kann gar nicht soviel Essen, wie man probieren möchte. Die Preise finde ich normal. Die Speisen sind sehr leckern. 
Ich kann sie als Punkt auf der Sightseeing List für Philadelphia absolut empfehlen. Werde dort auf jeden Fall immer wieder hin gehen, wenn ich wieder in Philli bin.
great market...usually a bit crowded.

Don't know where to start, I'm in love with this market. I'm personally a big fan of markets with all the new and old school vendors and this market is ddefinitely one of my best places in Philly.

During our recent visit to Philly, we came here multiple and tried out a couple of different vendors. We liked how there are so many options to choose from and there is something for everybody. We loved the Cajun Spot(Beck Cajun) and the cookie spot. Overall definitely a must visit spot, and I'll be back very soon.

This place has a great, authentic market feel. It is a must do experience once in Philly. You can find all kinds of street food under one, historic, roof. It is definitely an must-have experience while in Philly.

I don't think I've ever written a review so soon after visiting.  I love dumplings in every form and filling. I also love everything thanksgiving related.  So I was over the moon excited that they have thanksgiving stuffed dumplings!!! And the slightly spicy cranberry sauce was amazing! The French onion soup dumpling is a must try as well. I only intended on eating one dumpling as I walked home but that one was so good I ate all five as I walked!! I forgot to ask for them steamed as it's on request only but fried were excellent. I'll definitely be back!!
The overall ambience and bustle of this place gave me hope for a return to normalcy. At every turn there was a new unique find, and this is a must stop for ever visitor

A must see if you're in Philadelphia. Though this is probably more of a tourist destination, it's a great way to check out a lot of local vendors and popular places in Philadelphia. My favorite grab here was the broccoli and beef rabe sandwich but there are cheesesteaks, desserts including apple dumplings, and stores selling both food and other homegoods. Very much recommend checking out this gem in the center of Philadelphia.
The Reading Terminal Market is one of my absolute favorite places!! My go to spot is definitely Hunger Burger, and my sweet treat spot is Beiler's of course!
This place is awesome! Everything you could possibly want in one place. It's so many different foods to try and beautiful merchandise to purchase. I will definitely be visiting again.
Love the vibe here. It's far, far away from me but if I need a place to duck in for a few before I go to watch a movie at the sticky movie theater 3 blocks away then this is my spot!

I love going to the Reading Terminal Market. Lots to see, do and taste. There is not much I don't like about this place. Maybe when it's very crowded. The fresh foods are awesome. The Amish foods are great. The cheese places are great and love the different flavors they have to offer.

Amazing! So many options!
No matter what you are in the mood for, Reading Terminal has it!
Desserts, lunches, snacks!
Great for a group who have very different tastes.

Your standard biryani and kati rolls - nothing out of the ordinary. Tastes pretty good - mostly popular because its open late. But not good enough for me to say I HAVE TO GO BACK for those kati rolls or chicken and rice.

LALO caught my eye when I visited the Bourse my first time. As I was placing my order at the counter for the Filipino beef stew, I saw the daily special for blood sausage silog, which  is like a garlic fried rice with blood sausage. I've had silog before and thought it would be nice to have it again today. I immediately asked if I could change my order even though the guy at the counter had already rang me up for a beef stew and I was about to pay. He was super cool about it and changed my order for me. He also advised that I pour this vinegar over my silog because it goes with the dish and I would enjoy it more. At $8, this was a sweet deal. The silog was served with a side of egg salad, and some pickled veggies, and topped with a fried egg. It was a tasty, well balanced lunch and I hope they would add this to their regular menu!
Love all the stores. Great to see the staff wearing masks. Great to take the family or grab lunch. Love it here!

Reading Railroad was always my favorite Monopoly property. I liked all of the railroads, but especially that one. Unfortunately, most of my family members knew this so they'd force me to mortgage it all to claim it. Reading Terminal? Just as cool.
 
This is a place where you can shop, eat, explore, indulge, pamper, and lose yourself for an afternoon in the aisles of restaurants and shops. 

Among the highlights:
1. Vegetarian cheesesteak sandwiches.
2. Beeswax candles and lotions, with live bees you can watch behind glass.
3. Purple roses.
4. Live piano music while you eat your lunch.
5. Fruit fry-pies. It's fried pie with fresh fruit fillings, enough said.
6. Donut vendor making donuts right in front of you. Giant vats of custard. *Cue Homer Simpson voice: Mmmm, donuts!*
7. Pig statue in the middle of it all, to remind you to pig out.
8. Handmade paper mâché food garland decorations.
9. Dutch cafe making apple puffs with fresh whipped cream.
10. Vintage bookstore. 
11. Cinnamon ice cream on top of Guatemalan chocolate coffee ice cream.
12. Fresh homegrown vegetables.
13. Cutesy culinary decorations/appliances: aprons, teapots.
14. Philadelphia tourist stuff: magnets, travel books.
15. Chocolate covered onions. Didn't try this. That just sounds gross.
16. Pay by the lb vintage candy store, run by an Amish guy in costume. Suspenders and all.
17. Free samples at many food vendors.
18. Fresh pretzels being rolled and twisted on the countertop.
19. Herbal remedies store. Awesome hand lotions.
20. Sights. Sounds. Tastes. Smells. Aisles and aisles of it. 

Skip the board games, go to the Reading Terminal.

My girlfriend and I visited for dinner at around 5 PM. 
We ordered a lamb and chicken platter and a chicken tikka masala kati roll. 
The platter had generous portions and was perfect for sharing with another person. The pita bread was warm and soft and the meat was nicely seasoned. 
The kati roll had a strong and rich flavor. When we ate it, it was missing the Chutney but it was tasty nonetheless. 
They also have Lassi and we had the Mango and Rose flavored ones. They were thicker than normal and had a thickness similar to that of yogurt.
There was no line and overall the restaurant is definitely worth going to with friendly prices and excellent food.
Great pizza, but the guys would not make a whole pizza for us? Forced to buy slices, Richard move, given it was not busy. Go for a slice I guess?

I'm pretty sure it's just the Philly locations here but today everything was screwed up from the beginning...they hung up the phone on me twice when I tried calling,when they did pick up the girl sounded like she was asleep and wasn't even able to understand a simple question. They quoted me 80 minutes which I've never heard of,it wasn't even a busy night. They didn't build the pizza the way I ordered on the internet...how do you screw that up when it's right in front of you? The pretzel crust was nothing more than regular crust with some salt on it,and they mistyped the amount I owed on the credit card so I ended up owing cash. Only in Philly^

RTM definitely is a foodie paradise with dozens of stalls that are crowded at each instance I went. I could easily see New York's Chelsea Market and Essex Street Market or LA's Grand Central Market compared to this because of the vast array of food items. Because of its central location near Chinatown, the bus station, several SEPTA stations, the convention center, and many downtown attractions, it's very highly trafficked. But its vast size and sheer amount of options is dizzying. 

I definitely like the organization that it has. The market is divided by "avenues" and "streets," much like a New York street grid. It definitely helps to locate something if you know where to go. But for someone like me who has "food court dilemma," I could easily spend a half hour trying to navigate the market's different roads backed up by crowds and unsure what to get.

There's anything you can imagine. You can get fresh and raw honey, cheesesteaks, Chinese, Middle Eastern, bread, Pennsylvanian Dutch, deli meats, Mexican, etc. It's a true gem for dining around the world. Allow yourself some time to navigate and get acquainted with the market's layout.

There's also a live band that plays occasionally. Pretty cool!

Our first stop on Philly was not for Pat's or Geno's or any other cheesesteak place. It was DiNic's for their roast pork, broccoli rabe and cheese sandwich. I've been craving this for years after catching a couple of glimpses from the Food Network. The line was pretty much wrapped around the place. 

Verdict? It was pretty awesome. Not as what I expected or hoped for, but it was still pretty damn good. For some reason or another the roast beef was much more juicy and flavorful than the famous pork. But hey, why not get them both and try for yourselves. 

Reading Terminal market is basically where both the locals and tourists go. Chocolate dipped bacon, chocolate dipped pretzel with bacon, a great donut shop which offers a variety of donuts including maple bacon, triple chocolate, coconut cream, mocha cream, etc...

You can probably spend a good 2 hours here before your clothes stink like seafood, fried batter and cheesesteaks. 

Really enjoyed the visit. Thanks Philly.

This place is one of my favorite foodie spots! I've been here numerous times and this place is still one of favorite places to go while in Philly!  The variety of shops and food options are so vast that you could spend hours there. Shops ranging from homemade goods, souvenirs, candy, bakeries, donuts, cookies, fresh vegetable and fruits, cheeses, meats...I could go on forever. And also a variety of food places so everyone's tastes buds will be fulfilled even the pickiest of eaters. The only unfortunate thing is that a lot of the Amish owned shops aren't open on Sundays. So a lot of those sections are blocked off since they are closed. We had gotten there a little later in the day so the cookie shop had a sale on their cookies for $1 each! It was def a steal. Also stopped by Termini Bros. and got some freshly filled cannolis! 

Reading Terminal is def a great stop if you're going to Philly! Though we didn't get to eat there--there is a seated food court section for everyone to enjoy your meal. This place is also perfect one stop grocery shopping!

good thing i don't live in philly...otherwise i'd be stuck in reading terminal all the time and spending whatever cash i have in my wallet on the variety of cuisines or really just eat until i need to readjust my waistline.

but then again, with all the greatness and tasty goodness that is crammed into the market, maybe i do want to live in philly :)

can't wait for my next visit...since i already got the liberty bell and rocky steps all taken care of, i can spend all my time in reading terminal eating to my stomach's content.

I love the terminal. The food. The cookies. The coffee. Everything about it is great. Tons of unique businesses and lots of great smells when you walk in you can smell an aroma of different scents. I love old city coffee in there and I also love the cookie. They have a great cook book place that I would recommend going to.

If you like "varieties" of food.... this is the MUST GO place!! So many different vendors selling food, beverage, dessert, etc. One of the popular place in town for sure~

This place reminds me of Grand Central Market in Los Angeles!! 

There are different bus lines pass by this market. Also, if you are taking the hop-on hop-off tour bus, there is a stop at this location as well.

I love markets and this one has to be one of my favorites!  It has some great fruit and veggie options that remind me of Granville Island in my city of Vancouver, but with way more cooked food options!  Your head is almost spinning as you see the famous Tommy DiNics, baked goods, Indian food, crepes, smoked meat sandwiches, cheese, pretzels, and more!  Definitely budget a few hours here.  Bring your cash, an empty stomach, and have fun!

Conveniently located near transit and the convention center.

I tried this place for the first time right after Beddia left the building. Back then, it was nothing to write home about. No point in coming back here, I thought. Not with a pizza shop on every other corner.

But recently, when I was craving a slice (because that's what happens when you're from the East Coast) while walking back home up Girard, I stopped in and grabbed one (plain/cheese) from Shackamaxon and was like: "WOW! That was a good ass freakin' slice!"

So now, Shackamaxon will be my go-to neighborhood spot for a slice. In fact, it might be the best "to go" slice I've had in Philly. I'm glad it's down the street!

Plain Cheese Slice: 5/5
VERY RUDE! Manager Would not let me use a fully functioning bathroom. stating its for employee use only.....

Holy jamoly! This place is local food chaos like I've never seen before.

My advice to you- if you're looking to experience it without having to come up for air every few minutes, try to avoid showing up at 12:30 on a Saturday afternoon like we did. I love a good food shit show but I also wanted to explore all of the booths without being pushed along by the masses. It's super-exciting to see the locals and tourists get behind this historical institution. 

When you do decide to visit (because you can't miss it!!), make a beeline for Miller's Twist and order a traditional pretzel. It will blow your mind. Trust me, wouldya? Plus it will only cost $3 at most.

Next up? Well, that's up to you- there's cheese, fresh juice, hot pork roast, Szechwan, fresh flowers, baked goods, hot apple dumplings and plenty of food  souvineers. My only regret is that we didn't have more room in our stomachs for the Yelp-adored apple dumplings. What a fun mix of people, sights and smells under one roof.

This is a must see/stop by to experience! I adore the Reading Terminal Market. They have so many different things to offer thanks to all of their amazing vendors. If able to stop by, make sure to try a freshly made grilled cheese with farm fresh cheese, as well as some freshly baked donuts and whoopie pies from the local Amish people. The flying money has great cookies, and there is also a local honey/bee stand that sells great candles! There are so many other things to eat and try but those are my favorites. You will even find their infamous chocolate covered onion which is made at their local chocolate shop, Mueller Chocolate Co. This is a gag gift which visitors get a real kick out of!

Was really looking forward to eating at this place because of what I've been hearing from my family in New Jersey and because I'm a west coast guy. Overall the food was quite good but my issue is definitely with the service. The problem started when I picked up my order and I saw that the carrots were missing in my bowl. I took it back to the front and let them know that they had missed the carrots, no apology was even given. Furthermore the lady went back, got me raw carrots, and brought them back to put in my bowl. I looked at her and asked if she could stir fry them. She unhappily went and stir fried them for a couple of seconds and then brought them back to me. In most situations they would have made a new bowl for me or at least offered to do so. Would not recommend this location.

Delicious finger foods and meals from all around. It was such a great atmosphere and there was music which made it even more fun. We ate mini corn dogs, bacon on a stick, ribs falling off the bone, philly cheese steak sandwiches and then there was a full market of foods, cheeses, hummus, soaps, raw meat and seafood fresh vegetables it was such an experience
I'm born and raised in Philly and Reading Terminal is by far the best place to experience all the taste in Pennsylvania  and food from all over the world...

Sigh...ordered four 4 for 4's. I requested NO ICE. Ice was in all of my drinks. Okay...also ordered BBQ & honey mustard. I received NO SAUCE for 16 nuggets. This happens way too often. The cashier was super nice, but the service was not.

So here's the skinny.  I wanted to eat something in Philly that I couldn't eat in D.C. and I didn't have time to try Pizza Brain and another café was not in my cards.  Yeah, all that was going on and I decided to turn to Yelp to see what was in walking distance.  That's how I found Masala Kitchen.

I like the progressive idea to do Indian food or any other cuisine with a fast casual twist.  In D.C., Rasa does this well but D.C. is inundated with restaurants copying, interpreting, modeling themselves after Chipotle.  Masala Kitchen had me hype because they aren't doing that.  Kudos to the Philly restaurant scene for doing it's own thang.

Restaurants seem to have one of two things.  Have a front line staff that are engaging, whether that restaurant is empty or packed.  Other restaurants seem to just be.  I am not one to enter an establishment and then turn around but I should have just done that this time.

I ordered a Paneer Platter along with a Lassi to wash it down.  The Paneer was ok.  Nothing special at all.  The naan was way too soft for my liking.  Not fluffy soft, soft like it could have been cooked a tad longer soft.  So that was that.  The only thing saving the meal in my eyes was the Makhani, a tomato based sauce served along with my meal.  That made the meal for me.  That and my bottle of Lassi.  The actual bottle, the beverage, not so much.*  

Three Stars only on the account of the Makhani and I bet some people will read that and be like, you must not have had good Makhani and you my friends are correct.


*I should have taken a picture of the bottle.  It was cute.  But I can't get into the habit of taking pictures of every cute thing I see.  I'll save some for memories.

This place is foodie heaven, if that's what you're looking for. So many different stalls offering a wide array of cuisines are available, but stay away or have a flexible schedule if you want to avoid crowds. I've never tried as soon as they open, but I know that midday is not too terrible, but I've only been on the weekend. I suspect it's not as bad during the week. If you're trying to get something specific though I would probably avoid going closer to closing (5 or 6PM) because they could run out of whatever you're going for. This place is just jam packed with people and for good reason! Most people have already done their research of places to hit up while visiting so if you haven't you'll know what you have to get by looking at the lines near these places.
The places that I have tried are Beiler's, Bassetts, Sang Kee, Shanghai Gourmet and Dinic's (of course). Haven't regretted anything here, so far! 

It can get a little stressful trying to navigate through the aisles with hoards of people walking every which way.
They have a great selection of foods ranging from savory to sweet and from chinese food to Amish. I would probably just take cash here to be safe seeing as a lot of the stalls could be cash only or have a card minimum. There also isn't that much seating compared to the amount of people there are. If it's nice outside, looking for a park bench or eating outside somewhere isn't a bad idea, but for the colder or rainy times hovering around the tables looking for parties that are almost done may be your best option. Just keep in mind that there may be 3-5 other groups of people doing the same thing.

All in all, this is a great place to check out if you're in Philly either for the first time or revisting. There are so many options of great food in one hub. Just be prepared to wait, a lot of crowds and limited seating.

This place is a Philadelphia staple. You can find everything you're looking for here, from vegan cupcakes to hand made jewelry. As a local, navigating all the tourists isn't my favorite thing but I still stop in to pick up inexpensive produce regularly.
The reading terminal market is really cool. This place has something for everyone. It is definitely one of the main attraction of our great city! I suggest you come take a look for yourself.

Sssooooo busy!!! But so
Many different food vendors. The line for the donuts was long but went fast.( BEILERS). They had pickles on the other side too!!! Now those were great. We chose the kosher ones and they were prefect in taste and crunch!! The line for sandwiches @ DiNiCi's wrapped around the corner, so we had to see what the hype was about. We ordered roast beef it was ok, but guy in front of me swore by the brisket sandwich. He had ordered 3 of them. Our sandwich was just ok. Flavor wasn't fantastic. But the line went fast. Lastly we visited HATVILLE deli shop for meat and that was great. Got roasted turkey, apple smoked bacon and chipped beef( taste almost like pastrami, but leaner in my opinion)

Hands down best donuts in Philadelphia. Glad I don't live close to this place, I would probably get fat because I can't stop eating them. Also tons of other great food here for good prices. Deff a must see in Philadelphia

I like the hustle and bustle, I only went to a crepe restaurant inside the market, and did some veggie shopping. I might not go back to get the veggies but I definitely have to go there for more crepes, and try out other restaurants there. It looks like a nice food court, but not like the fast food foodcourt.. they actually seem to have some pretty good place to eat there.. I will go back and try something else soon!

I went here before.The layout is quite messy. This place is full of people most of the days, so it makes me even impatient trying to find out the food I really want to eat. The place should be more organized based on the types of cuisines.
As for the food, I tried smoothie, burgers, chocolates from the gift shop, they didn't leave me much stunning impression instead of higher price points than their competitors outside.

Excellent! Had a few of their slices the other week, & just tried their tomato pie for the first time. The tomato pie is unbelievably good. Seriously- this spot stands on its own as just an EXTREMEly good pizza spot!!!

1love

We loved this place. We visited two days in a row. 
We had coffees, breakfast and a lunch. 

Everything is set up so well, clean and everyone was very friendly. 

One of, maybe the best food market I've been to in the world that has plentiful of seating, food and easy to walk around, especially with a pram. 

A must visit when in Phili.
The food selections are very diverse. There is something there for everyone. Even a place to get hard to acquire seasonings.
Great place to go for any visitor to the city. Lots of food options and very nice shops. You can find anything here! A great mix of the culture Philadelphia has to offer.

THIS is a place where literally everyone is at. The choices of places to eat in here is endless and theres so many things to look at. Just to name a few, you've huge cuts of BBQ meats, sausages, sandwiches, flowers... ice cream, a grocery store, candy shop and much more. Everything related to food and drink can be found in here. Literally any ethnicity, from asian food to mediterranean food, they got it. From coffee to candy, they got it. 

This place is a foodie's paradise. I was in town for a convention and Reading Terminal was within walking distance. Unfortunately, the big downside of this place is that its entirely too crowded during the rush. Shoulder to shoulder and human body traffic on the grid layout of the shops reminds me of downtown traffic. 

Will comeback next time I'm around. Really cool place.

I absolutely loved this clusterfxck of food vendors jampacked into these tight quarters. I may even have been more excited about coming here than my visit downtown.  There are tons of people, super noisy which I think just adds to the appeal of this Philly staple.

This is a foodie's paradise. No joke. There are vendors everywhere selling every palatable whoozits and whatzitz imaginable.  cheesesteaks, pizza, pastries, cheese, meats, seafood, they have everything here. There's a lot of scattered tables for sitting and you can literally eat your way through the market if your belly and wallet allowed. 

Some shops are cash only, but most take credit cards.  Parking can be found in the neighboring areas for a small fee. 

In my one hour here, we managed to get a half dozen donuts, a cheesesteak, and pizza.  That didn't include much browsing time though.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to truly enjoy walking around and soaking up the atmosphere.

Service is ridiculously slow compared to other chipotle flagships. I waited 30 minutes to order when there were only 2 people in front of me. It wasn't even rush hour. I don't understand why it was so slow. I've been to other chipotles at rush hour and the line still moved pretty fast considering all the people. This time around, the wait is ridiculously long. 

Also there was this employee who complained and constantly rolled her eyes after every customer. A customer wanted beans on the side and she made a face and was very unpleasant. I asked for a tortilla on the side and complained that she "burnt" her finger to the customers behind me. She made it seem like it was my fault that she "burnt" her fingers because I ordered it. If she was attentive enough then the speed of the line would have increased and she wouldn't have accidentally touched the inside of hot press. I rather travel all the way up to cheltenham for better, friendlier, and quicker service.
Extremely busy but a nice place to play tourist in. Lost of good options and I'm really big on organic food so I'm glad they have a few options here like that.

Always a solid spot if you are a tourist or a local bringing out of town friends. Lots to choose from. A fun 30 minute walk through the 10 or so aisle of the market is super fun and also include a stop anywhere that peaks your interest for breakfast or lunch!

I'm a New Yorker so I know good pizza.  The pizza here is really good with a delicious crust that is unique BUT this establishment looses 3 stars because they are not sanitary and pose a health risk to all those that eat here.  The cashier in the front (pink hair) handles your pizza with his bare hands AND in the same swoop he collects your dirty money.  You read it correct, he's both the server and the cashier.  GROSSSSS!!!  When I told him "you know you're wrong for handling the money and the food", he took a long pause and said "well what do you want, them to hire a separate person just to handle the money?".  I said Yes! or use gloves....DUH!!!!
Great food try Herschel's or Dinics both terrific sandwiches in their own right. So much food!!!

Basically like the Pike market in Seattle but enclosed to stay warm in Philly. Met a really cool lady selling mushrooms and she was originally from France. I'll probably always remember her thinking about this place. The cinnamon rolls are famous and you shouldn't leave without one! If you're at a conference at the convention center like I was, head here for lunch. It's an easy peasy walk! Also easy access from SEPTA public transit system.

Pizza by the slice in the humble ghost kitchen of Beddia's. This reincarnated pizza shop is located in the holy space vacated by the Pizza King himself. And yet they manage to fill those behemoth shoes! These Pizza Shackamaxon guys have done an amazing job. Honestly, the pizza is phenomenal. Here's why it's better than its predecessor:
1) Accessibility. It's open wed-sat from 12-8 on W/Th and 12-10 on Fri/Sat. You can buy by the slice and there's no obnoxious line.
2) They're super friendly and they Let You Use Credit Cards, like every other sane business owner out there! 
3) The crust is to die for. Crisp, not oily, not too salty, slightly charred.
4) The tomato sauce is not sweet. It's a perfect medley of crushed, not-too-tart tomatoes. 
5) Their "special" slices are ridiculously good. They make the best caramelized onions I've ever had on a pizza. 

In short, this place is a blessing to the neighborhood. It's mostly take-out, they only sell slices (no drinks, but there is free water) and you don't have to wait three hours and buy a whole pie. Regular slices $4, special $5. Go now!!!

Tried for delivery one night at the hospital. 

Wings were below average. More grease than buffalo sauce and the quality of wing itself was nothing to write home about. 

Short rib platter was adequate but not very tender and would not order it again. 

Chicken tenders and fries were soggy, but that was probably due more to the takeout containers. 

Buffalo chicken salad came with cold cut chicken/turkey which was a letdown (not spicy at all) and there were no peppers (the menu stated there would be). 

Delivery took an hour+. Overall not a great experience. Wouldn't try this place again, especially with such great Indian in the neighborhood.
If your going to be in Philadelphia you have to check this place out, every vendor that I tried has amazing food and a great attitude towards there customers. I can't recommend this place enough.

This is one great food mall. I saw about 2 vendors selling trinkets but this place is really just a great food market with Cajun, Pakistani, Indian, Italian, and of course Philly cuisine. Yes, hoagies and steaks are a cuisine lol So if you want diversity in your lunch, dinner or dessert, then this inexpensive food market is the place to visit.
Fantastic!!! Anything you order here is delish, really enjoyed the food and wish we had something in VA like this!

Love love love this market! Being from Hawaii I was just in foody awe at what this place had to offer on a REGULAR basis to the Philly population. Lucky dogs! I think I walked a mile in this bustling mecca of delights and wanted to buy everything! 

Right after I gorged myself on the wonderful pretzels at Miller's Twist, we walk around the corner and it's cookies, bakery heaven! Id' really have to exhibit          
self-control if I lived here. Good thing we were just visting LOL!  I bought a lot and definitely ate everything my little pig heart desired! I can't wait to come back!

What CAN'T you get here??  Well, you CAN get top-notch cheesesteaks, roast pork sandwiches, whoopie pies.  Park in deck across the street.  Pay your $10 for an hour or whatever it is.  Go to the market and feast!!

Such a fun place to go and experience culinary wonders and Philadelphia at its best. We do our regular grocery shopping here. Everything is local and always the freshest. Best prices. Best people serving their customers of all walks of life equally, with respect and individualized care.

This place is amazing.  It reminds me of a similar place we have in LA called "The Farmers Market".  It is an indoor, covered collection of mostly eateries and some stalls that sell gifts and other items.  I think you can pretty much find anything you want to eat here, from every type of cuisine, to dessert, to a smoothie, etc.  They also have a market where you can buy fresh produce and some groceries, as well as several meat markets, delis, and more.  I was honestly overwhelmed with the selection here.  Since I came here after eating lunch, I only grabbed a juice to sip on, but they also have many vendors that provide samples of their dishes.  I would highly recommend checking this place out if you are a foodie!
This is a must stop! So much selection to choose from. Dutch Eating Place has the longest line, and great service. Great coffee, juice & food. How does anyone decide with so much here?
Love it there!  Food heaven.  But stay away if you don't like crowds.
Always my choice , haven't branched out and tried anything else . Oh and the queso & Chips . Maybe I'll try something else one day

Came here twice and couldn't believe the sizes of the slices both times! Never thought I'd be obsessed with pizza but their pepperoni slices are really good! I personally would recommend it over the tomato pie. Will be back to try their specials sometime!
Don't eat here at noon the cops all eat here and they gonna find ya stash stay away at all costs
Order weekly from them! Love the food and they are pretty quick. Love the MK Special on lettuce no rice.

I go to this McDonald's simply for convenience and sometimes desperation. I actually hate going in here because the customers are...sketchy. 

The McDonald's is definitely dated and in need of a dire renovation. 

What I will say is, this is probably one of the best customer service oriented McDonald's i've been to. The workers here have a perfect system down because they are all fast and there is no attitude (every time i'm served). They are actually kinda friendly and make me seem stand off-ish since i just wanna get my stuff and leave as fast as possible! 

The managers are also very hard working and i'm sure that is another reason they execute so well. I rarely order food, but when i did, the food was prepared well and not too sloppy. I mainly go for coffee. 

other cons: 
- no "unsweetened" drink at the soda fountain. its all soda and sugary stuff. 
- there is no line system...which gets confusing when it is busy..who's up next?

Reading Terminal is such a staple place to visit while in the city of Philadelphia.  They have tons of shops inside, mostly food.  Some of the shops inside are great!!!!  It is slightly pricey.   Parking is a nightmare if your driving. I wish they had discount parking or something.   Not enough seating to eat your food. But I know it's a lot of people who visit so I understand. It's definitely worth visiting and trying out some food.  I recommend catching a uber there!

Pardon th
Called about an order being messed up and was hung up on. The manger has a horrible attitude; if you get food the food will be cold don't eat here'
Simply put, it's food heaven. I would gain 50 pounds if I lived in Philadelphia!
It's an interesting place, lots to eat. If we didn't have similar at home, it would have been 5 stars :)

I was not so sure what I wanted to eat that day and so I was looking for a place with a wide variety of food to choose from. Walking into rtm I felt like I was emerging myself into a dark whole of culture, every stand offering a unique experience and great quality! Seafood, cheese, marmalades, sandwiches, donuts, etc. Great food and ambiance.

Ridiculous Kati roll. Great portion for the price. Spices perfect. We actually ordered 3 to go and the girl at the counter was nice enough to bring the order out to our table. Def will be a must stop on our trips into the city.

So excited!!! I now have a Kati Roll NYC substitute in Philadelphia.  I just happen to walk by here today and of course had to try it.  I'm so glad I did.  The service and food are excellent. Prices are extremely reasonable.  This is definitely going to be a regular spot.

If you live near it, there are some great produce and fish market stalls that you can visit at times it is not jammed with people.  If you are going as a tourist, be prepared for crowds, particularly during lunchtime when finding seating can be a challenge.  It has a wide variety of food stalls (the cheesestak places will have long lines during lunch and tourist seasons) except for the Thai place which was sub-par.  Nice to visit but if you hate crowds, be prepared.....
There are too many good places inside to name.  Just go, sample a bunch, and be satisfied!  You won't be disapointed.

If you're in Philadelphia and you love food, then you must make a trip here.  It's a food lover's paradise.  Whether you're looking for meats, seafood and produce to take home or sample some of the local cuisine, there's something for everyone who loves to eat.  Even if you don't love to eat, then you should go (but why are you reading Yelp reviews if you don't love to eat?).

They have donuts, a vegan deli, cheese steaks, mushrooms, distilled spirits, pretzels, more donuts, pies, cakes, pies baked inside cakes, Asian, pork sandwiches, pizza, hot dogs, gyros, deli counters, oysters, ribs, and even a buffet!  What???

Some places have counters to sit and eat at and some do not, so you may or may not find a place to sit and eat.  It can get crowded so be aware.  

There's not much else you can say other than go here.  I would definitely go back next time I'm in town.

This was my first visit, and let me say, WOW! There is something for everyone, and the quality is outstanding.  This place can be packed and overwhelming, but don't let that get you.  Staff handles the crowds well, so there is no need to worry about long waits. We went to Dinic's (pork sandwich), The Original Turkey (thanksgiving sandwich), and Sweet Nina's (nutter butter banana pudding).  Everything waa flavorful and tasty.  Hope to come back soon!
This place is great, a little crowded but well worth it.  Lots of good food choices , fresh produce and more.

Indecisive?  Then you'll absolutely hate this place.

Hungry?  Then the Reading Terminal Market will be your seventh heaven.

With a hundred-some-odd businesses and dining destinations in a football field-sized space under a single roof, the RTM is a farmer's market on steroids and the gastronomic heart of Philly.  Housed in a former train shed, the RTM is an amazing slice of Philly culture.

Here's just a sampling of what you can find here:

*cheese shops
*delis
*produce stands
*Chinese food
*Greek food
*Middle Eastern food
*Italian food
*cheesesteaks
*hoagies
*coffee shops
*exotic teas
*ice cream parlors
*Amish food
*diners
*butchers
*bakeries
*fishmongers
*pastry shops
*handmade jewelry
*arts and crafts
*live music

And you know what?  Everything single one is fantastic.  There isn't a single bad apple in the bunch.

(Speaking of which, the apples at the fruit stand near the front-right entrance are superb.)

I brought a dozen-or-so conventioneers here for lunch last weekend.  Everyone went somewhere different, and everyone spent under $10.  And you know what?  Everyone was blown away.  

W I N.

Some people bemoan the RTM as too crowded, too touristy, too claustrophobic.  I think these people are missing the point.  The only thing that the Reading Terminal Market has too much of is charm.
Everything in here is good. It's a must. I don't know where to start. Just read the other reviews.
This place is amazing. It was VERY crowded the day I went, but that's because the shops were so great! I would definitely recommend this staple shopping center to new and old Philadelphians alike.

Such a cute little market area! Super clean and the vendors are great. 

Would highly recommend coming on an empty stomach as there are unlimited options
So many options and so much good food! I love that there is a large produce market as well as fresh seafood too.
The omish breakfast spot is awsome big portions and great tasting! If u need meat the venders have fresh meat amd seafood and the seasoning store is the best! Have to try it if in center city philly!

Reading Terminal is in an former Train Terminal - with gorgeous architecture not to mention some of the best local fare Philly has to offer. 12th street cantina mole burritos and homemade guacamole are a favorite, as are the myriad of spice, chocolate, amish and other stores.

I wanted to like this place but it was so ridiculously crowded, with barely any space to move, and most stores having lines that were way to long. Siting is very very limited. Unless you're going during less busy times, I'm not sure it's worth it.

Iconic tourist location for all food that represents Philly. There are many vendors and a wide variety of food to choose from. Quantity sometime does not equal quality. Seating space is another drawback. It's ok if there one or two but when you are with bigger group it can get difficult to seating.

With 25 minutes left before boarding we ordered the frozen yogurt - mine with 1 topping (granola) - my daughter opted out of tipping because she felt the $1.10 PER TOPPING too much to pay. I was eager to have a topping though I regretted it quickly once I saw the attendant sprinkle about a half a teaspoon full of granola whilst spilling quite a bit of the precious over-priced  kernels over & into the trash can where he held it. What  waste of money!   The frozen yogurt, itself, was ok but certainly not the best I've had. For the $5 or $6 price per small yogurt.   I don't think it worth it especially given the rushed service.   Learned lesson reinforced here... don't buy at the airport unless you are really really really hungry & the onboard peanuts & drink won't do.

If it's food you want, they'll have it.  Seriously, whatever it is, it will be here.  Fresh raw seafood, fresh raw meat, produce, cheesesteaks, bratwursts, greek food, thai food, a pub, an oyster bar, Amish goods, etc etc.  They have one of the best(and oldest) ice cream spots that I have ever been to in Bassett's.  Hell my ladyfriend even found a cart selling vegan tuna salad.  Don't get me started on what exactly that is but she loved it.  I've eaten in here 3 times and everything I ate was great, but.....

...It is always super crowded.  It's hard to find a place to sit and eat your meal.  If you do find a place to sit inside and eat, the table is usually pretty dirty.  You can't sit outside because the large homeless population in Philly hangs out just outside the building so it's hard to enjoy eating while being asked for money with every bite.  Maybe during the weekdays, it's less busy and easier to navigate through the market.  

I have I lived near here, I'd definitely drop in for meals to go or to pick up ingredients to cook at home.  As a tourist, it's definitely worht checking out but try coming during an off period not Saturday at noon.
I love this place. Can be kinda cluttered inside but such a variety of stores and friendly atmosphere

A must visit when in Philly. You can essentially get any food you're craving. I go pretty often, and the place is almost always jam-packed. Can definitely be overwhelming, but totally worth it. Beiler's donuts is my favorite spot!
Been coming here since I was a child and love it very much there's different stores to either eat or purchase items at and such a good environment

fun+food=great mix!
you can really choose any type of cuisine and enjoy in a casual atmosphere
nice to bring any visitors first time in philly and eat ur heart out!
also they have a nice some market for fruits and veggies at the corner that are not overpriced.

Kind of an average place to get Taiwanese chicken. When I think of this type of food, I want those bold Taiwanese flavors and this place kind of misses the mark by a little. The assortment of meats I ordered were decent in terms of portion but really lacked that punch I was expecting. I will comment that their grapefruit green tea is really worthy of coming for, if just for that. I've definitely had the drink way more often than I've had the food. On a hot day, there are few things as refreshing as that grapefruit tea so if you come, def get that.
Great selection of different foods. If your in the Philadelpia area you most check out the Reading Termianl Market. My favorite there is Tony Dinics!

Although some of the places were closed, the market was crowded, obviously (it was July 5th). I really wanted to try some of the cheeses and cold meats with bread, as well as the freshly cut fruits and juices but did not get a chance. I'd really like to come back with more time in order to try some of the food there. That would be my advice: come with time, preferably during the week and think in advance about what you would like to try in order not to be overwhelmed by too much choice.

This Wendy's is clean inside and out. I went inside because the drive through as always is crowded and slow. It. Ay not be Wendy's fault but the parking lot entrance is dark and the drive through somewhat dangerous and difficult to navigate. 

The young lady at the counter was very nice and she moved quickly. I need that because I really, really wanted a Frosty. Not to mention Frosty's were on 'sale' for .50!!
Great place... but when you're here you feel like you're gonna buy everything here, its so tempting lol
Horrible service for my first time ordering online. my order was screwed up and I got the wrong things and my food was very cold. Staff was very rude as well. I'm not eating here again!
Use to be a gritty urban market with great places to eat and drink. Unfortunately it has become very gentrified. Miss the Beer Garden. The place has become very bourgeoisie

Holiday coffee beans are currently on sale, so my boyfriend and I decided to pop in and see what this location had in stock. Both of the baristas that were there were very helpful. One offered to check in the back because he had a feeling that what was on display was not everything that they had, and he was right! We ended up getting 2 bags of whole bean coffee and are looking forward to enjoying the Christmas and Holiday blends well into the new year. I would definitely return to this location when in the area!
Perfect spot for a my lunch break. Ever since I discovered Naya I've been coming twice a week! Convenient, fresh, and delicious! I recommend :)

Reading Terminal is home to a diverse and delicious set of Philadelphia eateries, butchers, bakers, produce growers, and speciality shops where you can find anything your heart could possibly desire. 

I'll reserve my shop-specific reviews for their individual yelp pages but I highly recommend taking an afternoon to shop at reading terminal market for your normal groceries. You'll be so impressed at the quality and price difference in things like meats and produce. 

Also - take a minute and grab lunch at one of the delicious restaruants. 

Note: The market can get crazy on weekend afternoons so be prepared to take your time.

One of the city's highlights!   Great wide variety of everything on can think of.   Lots of food places to eat, vendors to choose from for retail products as well. 

Highly recommend:

Carmens cheesesteak 
The cookie place (forgot name) but so darn delicious 
The Dutch sweet shop 
By George (great pizza and sandwiches) 


Honestly it just really depends on what you're in the mood for.  Warning! You will be overwhelmed your first visit here.

Reading Terminal Market is a huge indoor food market in downtown Philadelphia.  There are hundreds of stalls that offer all kinds of foods from meats to fruits, vegetables and pastries.  If you are hungry this is the place for you.  There are also vendors that offer vegan and vegetarian options as well.  Tons of food to choose from.  Beware, it's crowded.  Parking is difficult as well.  There is very little street parking, however there is a city parking garage which fills up quickly.  Also don't forget to get your ticket validated at the market, otherwise parking is very expensive.  With validation 3 hrs. max for $5, otherwise your looking at about $10 an hour.  It's definitely worth going if you are hungry!

I am at awe how large this market is. The pure excess amount of vendors and options overwhelmed me a bit. And it's all in a good way. The place is clean overall, lots of food stalls, and lots of people. Everyone was friendly and ready to serve. We ate at Sang Kee for their duck and it was wonderful.

DISAPPOINTED! I would compare the customer service of this place to the service the soup nazi provides. It would make sense if the the pizza was world class or even the best in philly, but it is unfortunately a notch or two above mediocre. We came in with a few people, all wanting different things, and the guys working there gave us a terrible attitude about us ordering individual slices, trying to force us to order food we didnt want. We tried calling in advance, but they don't have a phone number. It sucks because i heard great things about this place, we only wish the service matched the hype.

This place is a foodie heaven. So far we ate an Amish made open faced turkey sandwich with mashed potatoes and gravy, bought some Amish pepper jelly, ate cheese steaks, donuts, icecream, roast pork and broccoli rabe sandwiches, & chocolate chip cookies. All in a days work.

I am from pittsburgh and this reminds me of a sampling of our strip district. you have to walk around it a few times to take it all in.  

The Ice cream is magical is all i can say and the baked goods are great too. Not a big fan of the coffee though...
this chipotle sucks never order from online they never put my exact order. when i ordered this time they had a pile of salt on my food it was honestly disgusting.

Every time I have been here I have ordered the tandoori seitan dish and pink temptation drink, because both are reliable and good. There is a decent cocktail selection and large list of beers. Not much in the way of vegetarian/vegan offerings.

Chipotle forgot to add meat to our tacos when we ordered . We called to put a complaint and the lady said we're lying that she checked the cameras and the workers put meat . Why would we lie and pick out meat from tacos when we're hungry to eat . Makes no sense horrible customer service
Such a wide variety of food choices, I'd go more often if I could. It's definitely a must see if you are ever in Philadelphia.
Everyone who visits Philadelphia should have a stroll through the market and grab a bite, it has something for everyone.

A bustling market in the midst of a historical city is exactly what this is. My jaw was on the floor with alll the smells and options from hot sauces, breakfast options, BBQ, coffee, bake shops etc. I'm
From New York so it's hard to get me to like anything that isn't from here. But it's a must go to especially for the Dutch breakfast (which we missed) to the sandwiches and local delicacies that tingle the sense and boggle your tastebuds. I would go to philly again just to visit the reading market and try the Dutch breakfast which has a line you would not believe
Loved this place!  Wish we had time to try every single vendor. Loved the atmosphere and the variety of foods!

Visit. Eat All The Things...

Go to DiNic´s.

ON day two - Drive to south philly and eat at John´s Roast Pork.

You want BOTH.

Then go to Paesano´s on Girard.

Try at least two sandwiches at each place.

Thank Philadelphia Jesus (Rick Oyola) that you are eating in one of the best food towns in the world. Salute the flag and try to ring the liberty bell. Run up the Rocky Steps...Shed a single teardrop.
Amazing Indian street food! Flavors were nice roti was pretty good on the rolls.  I wish they had paratha wraps for the Kati rolls also.
Peeking duck rolls from Sang Kee, ice cream, pork roast sandwich from Dinic's and enjoy the atmosphere and scents from all the stalls and the market!
A little over hyped place. It's a regular market in a closed fitting with a couple good eating options!

Loud, crowded, and chaotic -- just wonderful!  DiNic's roast pork broccoli rabe is beyond delicious.  I'm serious -- buy it, try it, and you'll be a fan for life.   Then roam around for desserts and sweets of all kinds, shapes, and sizes.  Just love the place!

European market - lite. Has a similar style and feel to some of the great European markets, in the sense that there's a good mixture of grocery and prepared food stands. However, it's smaller than some of those markets. For instance when I comes to either meat, fish, poultry, vegetables etc. there aren't a ton of a options per category.

There aren't many Filipino fast-food restaurants in Philadelphia, and I want this one to stay. Great if you're missing home and crave some quick comfort food. Most of all, I'm happy that I don't have to spend hours prepping lumpia or going back home to get my fix. Thank you, LALO!

My go to lunch place in Philly when I am in a dilemma as to what to eat for lunch! They have a variety of options from house made bread to Philly famous cheesesteaks to mouth watering vegetable lomein. It also allows you to buy groceries while you are waiting for you lunch to be prepared !

How could you don't give something so all encompassing 5 stars? Everything under one roof. And everything I've had here over the years has been excellent. 
You can get produce here too ya know?!?

RTM covers it all.

Best sandwich spot (dinic's)-check
Great ice cream spot (bassets)-check
Great Coffee spot (Old City Coffee)-check
Great pastry spot (Termini Bros)-Check
Great Cupcake spot (Flying Monkey Bakery)-check

And these are all just in view when you enter from 12th st.

Remember that you can park in the garage across the street.  Now, to save some cash, and by some, I mean a lot, spend $10 anywhere in the market and get your parking ticket punched.  Up to 2hrs will then only cost you $4 instead of the usual $20.

If you are in the area and have the time, go at least once. There is always a large selection of high quality food of all types. If it was 25 years ago, I would also say that the prices were low, but that is not the case now. The market has been discovered by high income people, who live nearby in the city. They are willing to pay high prices for the convenience and selection. I was there a few days ago, buying cannolis at Termini's. I passed by one of the butcher stalls, where the meats cost twice the price I have paid elsewhere.

When the two fancier places that I wanted to try while in town for business didn't even have seats at the bar, I opted for takeout. This was close by and highly rated, and sounded like comfort food on a cold evening. 

The descriptions had my mouth watering, so I opted for what I thought would be classics: a chicken masala roll and a veggie roll (fresh peas, carrots, green beans mixture mint-coriander chutney and crispy onions) to go.  With the open kitchen you can see the staff making your rolls.  Though it was a quiet night, with only one or two other groups in the restaurant, there were several delivery service people coming and going.  I also perused the cold case where they had homemade mango lassi, rose lassi, chai, and other beverages, but didn't try any.

My rolls were packaged in an insulated pouch, so that they were still warm after the few-block walk back to my hotel.  The flavors were great, and the pouch kept them warm enough.  The chicken was tender, and the sauce was enough to keep the meat moist but not make a mess. The veggie one was a tad on the dry side, as in my husband who needs sauce would've gotten the hiccups, but I really enjoyed the flavor profile.

Got my order wrong completely. Had to drive back 2 miles just for them to correct it. These cashiers need to get fired ASAP, this is happening way too much for it to be acceptable. Honestly, I'm about to never go back to this certain KFC. Get your shit in order please, then I'll return.

I stopped today to pick up 2 kid meals for my kids after school. The way the girl greeted us was whack. You could barely hear her but I put my order in and drove forward..? At the window, she told me the total. I asked her for sauce, she handed me my card and receipt-had her back turned to the window the time I waited for our food. She handed me the food and said "here you go" no..have a good day, nothing. Service is extremely well known at this franchise. So it's kind of surprising to find someone coming off like they don't like their position there?! I don't know what's going on here, the employees are like hit or miss.
Favorite pizza in the city. The only problem? It feels like they're never open! And if you want a whole pie, it's quite the commitment. Luckily I'm filled in a slice.

I want to eat all of the things here!!!  I would come here every weekend if I could.  It was a touch bit crowded for me, and if you know me I avoid crowds at all cost, but this place is worth braving the masses for.  And that's saying something coming from me.  I'd suggest grabbing lunch at one of the counters because it is tough to find a seat in the general seating area.  There are so many great little places to check out.  If you're into different olive oils and balsamic vinegars, you have to try out The Tubby Olive.  Awesome!  Can't wait for the next day trip to Philly.
Good options just dirty atmosphere. Its very dark and dreary and over crowded. I wish they would update it so it is more welcoming and cleaner.

I have enjoyed RTM in person for years. Once quarantine started, I tried ordering online for the first time. I have not been disappointed. They have always come through with the correct order and almost everything I requested. The fewer vendors you order from the more likely you are to be able to have a common delivery date, saving you in delivery fees.

Naya is a Mediterranean Chipotle, a fun fast casual restaurant where you build your own bowl chock full of tasty ingredients. Choose from a "base" such as lettuce or rice, add a main/protein such as chicken shawarma or falafel, then pile on vegetables, toppings, and sauces. The end result was a scrumptious and satisfying lunch. Prices were a bit high (over $10) relative to the competition, but the quality was good. Most patrons seemed to get lunch to-go, but the restaurant ambiance is nice (bright, spacious, and industrial-chic, also like Chipotle), if you want to dine in. Pay a visit if you want a hearty meal with Mediterranean flair.

Nice little pizzza stop! Ordered a slice of their tomato and their special. I liked their tomato slice better.

The crust of the corner piece (also dope they let you choose what you want, maybe this is normal and I need to get out more) is awesome! It's the right amount of crunch, flaky and taste. 

Thoroughly enjoyed

I'm not sure why Chipotle is getting such poor reviews. I'm a self proclaimed chipotle addict and I'm not ashamed. A little e.coli never hurt no one. Chipotle is in my estimation a great alternative for crappy fried fast food type things. Everything tastes fresh to me here and i can see it cooking, which is exciting. 
I love my burrito bowls...all the burrito deliciousness without any of the mess. It's huge and filling, which is good since it is a bit expensive. And as we are all well aware, the guac is extra. We get it chipotle. It's fine. 
I recently made a discovery here-the medium salsa. Try it! 
The people who work here are friendly, fast, and efficient. The food is delicious.  And this location actually delivers if you can believe that. They may be sprinkling crack into their burritos because I'm unreasonably hooked, but I'm ok with it.

What you're doing here is asking me to write a review about one of my favorite places in the country?

Look. Let me cut to the chase. 

Reading Terminal Market is a magical place. The type of institution you would brag to much younger people about visiting.

I frequently drive from Staten Island to Philly just to go here.

The selections are perfect, and there really is something for everyone. Come to think of it, there is something here for any mood you happen to be in.

If you haven't been here, then you haven't truly been to Philly.
Worst customer service ever, and the food is terrible. I'm surprised this pizza Hut hasn't shut down yet.
Love the whole experience!!! I could absolutely spend all day there. I think I love the fresh AMish pretzels the best!!!!

Alright, alright, Reading, you got me. I'm upgrading you to a fifth star. Fortunately, my last two visits over the weekend resulted in a much smoother shopping and exploring experience than my last visit. It probably didn't help that the last time I visited it was over a holiday weekend. 

This round I made a bee-line to Miller's Twist to snag the world's best pretzel and from there I toured from vendor to vendor to soak in the fudge, fresh juices, deli meats, doughnuts, you name it. What incredibly tasty and buzzing lineup! I also really appreciated the dedicated produce section that offers a farmers market vibe and reasonable produce prices for locals. This market is great to find something for all types of food interests and allergies but not so much to find a spot to eat and enjoy your purchases. Seating is a hot commodity. Fun note: they do have great free wifi.

The best place to grab high quality goods (such as chocolate, cookies, cakes, candy, fresh meat and produce). This market is HUGE. There were many options to choose from ranging from breakfast such as pancakes, waffles, sunny side up eggs, etc, to lunch/dinner such as hearty, meaty sandwiches like Philly cheese steak, soul food, roast pork and beef, etc. This place is packed with customers when it's near noon. The food taste absolutely amazing and it's very convenient to grab something and go from the terminal. The people here are really mindful and will tell you additional information if you tell them about allergies. One particular store told me the source of how/where their chocolate goods were made from. It was super helpful to know rather than giving me an assumption or a "I'm not sure."
Fabulous food!  Quite a variety.  The pastries are delicious.

I've been coming here for years and love it. From the fruits and vegetables. To the Amish beautiful tasteful pancakes and eggs. Coffee shop the maintenance people are great at keeping the place clean during this pandemic. Thank you

If you live in Philadelphia or are visiting, you have to check out Reading Terminal Market.  The market has literally everything you could possibly want.  DiNic's roast pork is my personal favorite.  The only thing keeping this from 5 stars is seating can be hard to come by.  If you visit during the week and are looking for seating from 12:15 - 1:30, good luck.  But the variety and uniqueness can't be beat.
Very interesting diversion, if you are in the convention hall area.  I would not make the trip just for this, but it is a nice add on to any other attractions in the area.
They have a little of everything. If they don't have it there guaranteed you probably didn't need it anyway!

Stopped into the Industry for a quick dinner before seeing a movie with some of the fam and immediately loved the atmosphere in this place. Casual and cozy. Our waitress was really sweet and speedy with getting us both drinks and our dinner orders. Definitely a safe bet if you haven't left yourself a ton of time to get somewhere else because they can turn it around. We actually gave ourselves a couple of hours before the movie and were in and out in under an hour! The reason I am not giving more stars is due to the food. I ordered the burger to split with my mom and she ordered the whole grain waldorf salad. These were the only two entrees I tried, although the fried chicken sandwich, the Korean BBQ pork belly and pasta all looked good and my dining companions all confirmed that they were. The burger was SUPER tiny for $9. Think like dollar menu size. It came with a large portion of fries which were yummy, but the burger was done really rare. We told the waitress our issue who graciously offered to replace it, but we declined. She took the burger off our bill anyway, which was nice of her. So again, great service. The whole grain waldorf salad unfortunately was also disappointing. The salty/savory dressing did nothing for the traditionally fruity salad and the faro added a weird chewy texture to the mix. We both didn't finish the salad, which was portioned much better than the burger and the pasta, which was also quite small for $15. Overall, I would come back for drinks and I'd be willing to try some appetizers. As I said before, the service was really nice here and I'd like to give the Industry another shot based on this.
If you can't find something to eat here... you are not hungry. Don't forget to tip the poor chap opening the door for you!

Always stop for lunch, my fav market. They have everything you need, its like a mini Philadelphia experience. If you are a food lover and visiting Philadelphia and don't have much time to go around the city, you have to visit reading terminal market. They have the best roast pork at the Dinics, philly cheese steaks across from Dinics, fresh bakeries, bailers donuts, fresh juices stalls, mini winery, and fresh farmers market, seafood and meats too. Foodie haven in the middle of the city.

Showed up here once absolutely blazzzed out of my mind. Literally riding a 9 or 10,,,, at LEAST!!! Anyways, that was NOT a mistake. This place is actually like High Wonderland (not in the sense that they sell bud-that would be tough tho, make it happen Tommy the Wolf!) they've got tons of stuff in here, flying Monkey is absolut a HIGHlight. those butter bars are Tea Leaf is a must see, truly a wide variety of strains for different drinking occasions, really nice Oolong. This is a HOT take i know but-- Beiler's is only good fresh! Now this is absolutely NOT to hate on them, those crullers are tough as hell fresh, but when even a couple hours old they don't old up, so eat em fresh! Overall some of the stuff here is overpriced, but thats a common knock on food markets like this. It's def a tourist trap, so make sure to go in off peak hours, like 9;30 am on a tuesday, but it def has charms.
Make sure to feed tha pig! 
Regards,
Rollin up a fatty J-ason Felton
Mid-State '06
Great prices on fresh vegetables n fruits.  Great place to find whatever you enjoy eating.

Oh yea I have NO IDEA what else to tell you guys that 1700+ already hasn't been said.  I can talk about the cluster , or a gathering of cultures under one roof that will overwhelm you. I can talk about the endless options of food to satisfy anyones cravings. I can mention also that there is a minature supermarket located inside.  I really don't know what else there is to mention other than this is a foodies paradise.  

Reading Terminal is by far the best option for anyone who wants a taste of everything , from the simple to the exotic. I know I just used the word exotic , but its true, when you step inside its like a whole different world. You don't know where to go to first pretty much, they have everything you could possibly imagine. 

A combination of cultures ready to hit you with an endless amounts of delights. If it isn't the Amish with their sinful donuts, pastries, cakes and pies, its their BBQ pit. Forget what you saw on TV about the Amish Mafia ,(If anyone ever saw it) these guys set up a "Front" in Reading where there is a line as  wrapping around the corner. All just to try their product, which by the way is on point. I do reccommend you go during the end of the week, these guys aren't set up on the weekends.(Sundays and Mondays)   I am still baffled by this.... the Amish, who knew they could attract so much attention. 

 A little side note~ To the Amish, I am now a loyal patron to your pastries, you made an offer I couldn't refuse.

Where else can you go for shopping, tasting, exploring, eating, all under one roof in the city. I am sure there is 1 or 2 spots, maybe , but do they have a bar inside? Yea I said it a bar, you can break away from the shuffling of on goers. All  trying to get that last slice of cheese or get that  fresh baked French bread. Slide on in at Mollys and take a breather, enjoy a few libations, recharge the system for rounds 2 or 3 maybe 4. I mean they do also have coffee stations along the way if you need a little pick me up , even they get blown out .  

Reading Terminal is pretty much the United Nations of cultures with American to European, to Asian, even Middle Eastern cultures trying to win you over.  This gives you  another reason why for you to return, endless options that can't be conquered in one day. 

 Plus they have cook books, a library basically of food preparations for every ethnic backgrounds  available. Reading even has a GINORMOUS section where you can buy key ingredients in spices and herbs,  where it would not be easy to find anywhere else.     

I am still trying here people to figure what to tell you that hasn't been said, so if I sound like I am repeating its not my fault.  I will tell you this though, the city did try to shut this spot down. In the mid to late '90s the city of Philadelphia came close to putting an end to Reading Terminal. I guess the power and the voice of the people pretty much told the city who their daddy was.  

Pretty much if I were to try to sum it up  Reading Terminal is a MUST. You'll definitely leave either with a full belly, or bags of goodies to peruse later. Now get in there and get a chocolate dipped onion to munch on as you enjoy the festivities of Reading Terminal.

This is the best piece of pizza you can get in Philadelphia. No-flop zone in full effect. Cello et. al absolutely destroying the game. The best pizza in the city was made in this exact location by Joe Beddia until spring of 2018. I had one of the last pies made by him. It was amazing but I was sad to see such phenomenal pizza disappear from the city. 

However, Jah provides

Pizza (Shackamaxon) easily carries the torch forward. A worthy successor to JB and the pizza is equally amazing. Pretty sure it's the same oven too. 

You guys rock. Thanks for consistently delivering the most fire pizza.

If I lived in Philadelphia...I mean Philly cause that's what I would call it if I lived there right? So if I did live in Philly, I would be at Reading Terminal Market every day. I would also be 100 lbs heavier because I would be eating a dozen Beiler's donuts, a couple of cannolis from Termini Brothers, Philly cheesesteaks galore, ice cream at Bassetts...

You can find everything here. Not just food but other goods as well. It does get super busy though so try to find non-peak times. But if you want to soak in all the food goodness that is Philadelphia, just go here. You'll find everything!
Even though I live in Denver now, I never miss an opportunity to visit RTM when I'm home in Philly. It's one of my favorite places in the city - if only there was one here!
Great variety of food for tourists! The flying monkey and hopes cookies are great dessert spots!!! I suggest for people to come visit here if ure from out of state!

This place is the best. I used to work Up the block from here. Good food. Good coffee. They would not be there if they did not scratch an itch. Also super cheep veg and fruits. Iavin brothers! And Kim's sea food. Old city coffee, and the whoppi pies!!
Great variety of vendors and product selection. A nice outing for any afternoon to grab lunch.

So much fun to frequent, especially during the holidays!!! It can get busy so be prepared. There are some great finds here and I love buying cooking gifts for my FIL here. Definitely a must if you're new to Philly or haven't been yet!
Stop in for a slice you won't be disappointed at all. Their tomato pie is wildly good.
Great place for fresh food but it gets very crowded, especially in the early afternoon.

Funny how this location was the only vendor who couldn't take meal vouchers from AA! They said their system was broken? They wait until you've stood in line and ordered before letting you know. Had to pay out my pocket for 3 cold breakfast sandwiches!

It's a tourist staple, but for good reason.  Reading Terminal Market seriously has some of the best food in the game.  If you're looking for a wide array of food (seriously, anything from vegan food to donuts to southern food, and of course, cheesesteaks), you've got to check it out.

My personal favorite spot in the market is Tootsie's, in the back of the building.  It's a build-your-own salad bar and build-your-own hot bar/soul food.  The staff is always super nice and the food options are plentiful, good quality, and a reasonable price (it's priced by weight, so you control how much it is).  

Just a fair warning, though, it's the Reading Terminal Market.  It's popular.  It gets PACKED on the weekends and during the peak of lunch time.
The food is YUMMMMMYY! Will be back soon. I had the pork dish and a side of kale and it was delicious.

Great place to buy groceries, especially fresh vegetables and fruit., best time to go is in the morning.
There are so many stores with a nice selection. I personally think that the place is a little bit overrated and overpriced excluding the iovine brothers store.
If you just visit it is a fun place to see. Great deserts and decent prepared food.
LOVE this place! Every time we come to Philly we go to the market. So much good food under one roof. A must if you're visiting Philly!!

Reading Terminal Market - with "Reading" pronounced as, "redding."

After walking inside, I totally wanted to grab some stuff for a picnic but I couldn't decide what to get. It was lunchtime and I was immediately jealous of everyone who worked nearby. You could easily spend half a year of lunches here without having to order the same thing twice.

My dearest lumberjack got major urges to cook with all the fresh ingredients and my eyes ate up way more than my stomach ever could. 

Come with a plan and come hungry.

We came here around 10am on Sunday morning and it was bustling but there were plenty of seats in the open areas as well as open stools at most of the vendors. 

Imagine all of the foods you could ever want to eat, you'll find them all here. There's a mix of (almost) everything, and enough to keep everyone in the group happy. From cheesesteaks to ice cream, to gyros and Thai food, each vendor adds to the delicious smells and excitement of the market. 

I bought a turkey & red roasted pepper panini from Market Bakery as well as a buttery chocolate chip cookie. Both the sandwich and the cookie cost under $10, I found this whole place to be pretty affordable for a tourist hotspot. The food was great overall, fresh bread and savory flavors. My partner got a meat lover's cheesesteak from Carmen's and was very happy with his purchase. I wish we had more time to wander around.

I would recommend this for anyone who's with a group that might be interested in eating different things and certainly for the exciting atmosphere of an indoor farmer's market with plenty of fun foods and people watching!
Love this place! Wide variety of food and little shops.   I had breakfast at Molly's and their avocado toast is just lovely.

If you are a foodie, you are absolutely going to love this market. There is row after row of nothing but different food stands. Good luck making a decision what to try.

After being overwhelmed for the majority of the time walking down each row, I settled on a deli style sandwich. And each sandwich was enough for two meals. I could not possibly have finished something this huge for lunch. 

I really enjoyed that the seating was all family style and open so everyone in our party could get something completely different. You will find no shortage of options here.

The hot apple dumpling from Dutch Eating Place. The best meal in Reading Market. That's it. Skip the mediocre cheesesteaks and the overhyped donuts and come straight here. 

Order at Dutch Eating Place's register and grab a table elsewhere to skip their line. The dough surrounding the smooth apple is the softest dough I've ever had, so buttery and thick and delicious, dipping in their divine, sweet applesauce. 

5 stars!!!!!!!

Who doesn't love this place? It should be pretty much a landmark in philly. Everyone knows and loves this place, inside you got foods ranging from bbq, cheesesteaks to sandwiches to ice cream to desserts. Then you got little shops that sell miscellaneous things. Gets jam packed during lu h time from the wave of people from the nearby area since it's pretty much near center city and Chinatown.

Went we got there, there was this lady and she said we couldn't be there due ring school hours and weren't there during school hours because we had a  half day and we went there to reLax and  enjoy our time because we just took two exams, but she was racists becaase she said that we had to get out and we just left because i didn't want tO get my friends in trouble. So we just left, but we are still mad because of that.
Great place for food, and groceries. There's so much variety and everything is hot and ready for you.  They got desserts, juices, all kinds of foods, meats, and small kitchen materials.

There are so many fantastic places to go to when you go to this market.  
1. Hershel's for the best Ruben pastrami on rye
2. Fox & Sins - dynamite cheese curds
3. Bielers- best darn peanut butter stuffed donut you will ever have and it was warm

Warning- 1/4 of the stands are closed on Sunday. 

I will dream of that donut until I go back the next time!
I loved being back in Philly for a conference and this was the perfect place to grab lunch. I wish I could have stayed longer to browse!

I have reviewed this location before after having a few bad experiences. I figured I would give them another chance to redeem themselves. Long story short, I shouldn't have. 

4:15pm - place online order for 4:45 pick up
4:45pm - arrive at location to pick up order and get told they will start it now.
