5:00pm - ask how much longer, and am told again they will start it now.
5:15pm - tell employee that people order online to avoid lines. How much longer do you think? Employee takes receipt  and slams it in front of the line cook who finally starts making food.
5:30pm - Finally eating stingy bowl prepared by cranky mc'hateshisjob. 

Go somewhere else.

What a great "food court" for the Convention Center!  I was here for WE16, and I ate at the RTM next door every chance I could get.  It's easy to find something delicious here, particularly with the information desk!  There's a map by the desk in case you're confused as to which door you came in and where the stall your searching for can be found.  There's a diverse mix of cuisines represented, so you're sure to find something for everyone.
Ordered for paneer roll, mix veggie and egg roll with some soda, classic 1am eat in India- have to say the rolls were flavorful and delicious!

It's the perfect place to bring out-of-towners. Try for a weekday so it's not so packed you can hardly move. Keeping track of a group on a weekend is really tough here, not to mention finding a place to eat together.

I suggest killing time during the prime lunch hour at Field House across the street. Delay your hunger with a beer and catch up with your friends, then forge a path through the diminished crowds to your favourite food destinations.

Highlights: Sang Kee Peking Duck (I always get the duck fried rice), Salumeria for killer hoagies, DiNics for roast pork, Miller's Twist for pretzels and milkshakes, Beiler's for doughnuts, Fair Food Farm Stand and Iovine's for dinner fixin's.

I really wish it was easier for me to get here during the week because I have major crowd-related claustrophobia issues and it's just too intense on the weekends.

Never ever use the Chipotle App, I waited forever for my online order while customer after customer was taking care of in the line. Finally a girl who I assume is some sort of manager told a kid to do the online orders which were hanging on the floor.  Neverrrrrr again!  Stay away!!
A wide, delicious variety of food. Not just restaurants, but shops too! I feel engulfed in culture whenever I'm there. Stop by if you can!

Pretty much must stop for all foodies visiting Philly. There is a big lunch rush and then a lot of places close down so plan accordingly. Absolutely hit the Amish booths, both for pastries and hearty breakfast sammiches in the AM. From there just wonder around and try whatever looks good.

We ordered 2 burritos and 1 quesadilla. We ended with 3 burrito bowls for pick up. None of which were made right and none of which had the extras we requested through the app. On top of all of this we had to wait 25 minutes after the pickup time only to receive cold food. Absolutely disgusting

What is the sense in having online ordering or Uber when you can't handle the traffic? If you can't handle the traffic close the store. There has to be someone coming outside handing off the Uber and the online orders is that too hard to figure out? Two orders got canceled by me today because I wasn't sitting in a line for 15 cars and going to make seven bucks for an hour and a half, would you? Damn you should be happy you have all this business instead you're just making people mad anyway. End it was barely 3 o'clock and the cars were all the way up the road and the line was not moving

Sadly the last time I had KFC I got food poisoning and never ate it again until today. KFC is just not my favorite, nor will be. They hold the lowest position as far a Chain-Fried Chicken, in my opinion. 

On a stroll through the neighborhood I was starving. The only reason I stopped was because I saw a Taco Bell sign. I decided to get both! Ha. As far as the wait in Drive-Thru....long. The chicken....not that great. I wont be going out of my way to come here; at the time it was nothing more than convenience.

I used to love KFC but their food has gone way down. I stopped eating their original recipe chicken a long time ago because it's way to greasy and was often undercooked. Today I tried the Kentucky grilled chicken. It had a good taste but the breast was the size of a small thigh and the leg looked like it came from a Cornish hen. Both pieces were either over cooked from the start or left under the warmer far too long because they were extremely dry. I also decided to try their spicy chicken. It was cooked well but the pieces were extra tiny. I had corn for one of my sides and it was over cooked to the point it looked shriveled and was scorched. My daughter's food wasn't any better. Colonel Sanders would be so disappointed to see the poor quality and lack of care put into the food offered by the once popular food chain. I'm sad to say I will no longer be able to satisfy my taste for good food from KFC.
So much good food!! Premium meats and cheeses and all the things... I get dizzy just thinking about all the delicious delectables!!!!

Tried the chicken and waffles was expecting 3 tenders and 2 pieces of waffles but got one piece of chicken patty and one waffle with the syrup in the waffle allready next time just put the syrup on the side not in the waffle allready.
This place is uh-mazing. I want to eat all the things.

Nice noodle dishes. A bit pricey in relation to the size but enjoyable.

Order was on time and tasty.

I love this place! I just want to spend the whole day going from one stand to another tasting everything. After I'm done doing that I want to buy one of everything I liked to bring home!
Local grown, home made, and just plain delicious. Cheese and sweets, snacks and drinks. You're sure to find something to enjoy. 
You just need to go. I was there for the Philly Marathon. I didn't get to spend as much time at the market as I wanted. I hope I will return some day. I'll take lots of pictures!

One of my favorites. I love to go there to get my cheeses for the holidays. The kids love that we can all go in different directions to get what we each want. Favorites are the pork sandwiches, two deli style cheese places and the bakery. Can't go wrong- awesome food and fun atmosphere!

I know that it can be a tourist trap but it is a great place for a meal. Over the years, they have really expanded the variety of food options here. If you want BBQ, Chinese, Indian, Italian, Cheesesteak, or Crepes then you can find it here. Metropolitan bakery has a branch here. Some of the best cookies in Philadelphia are sold here through the 4th Street Cookie Company. You can also do all of your grocery shopping here. They have butchers, fish mongers, and specialty cheese shops galore. There is a monthly cooking class that I'm still trying to attend.  You can also get baked goods from the Amish and Mennonites of Pennsylvania. They have a stall that makes fresh donuts and the line is rarely short. Have a great time.
So many great places to eat here. The family and I enjoyed trying different types of food.

If you aren't sure what to eat, then stop by Reading Terminal Market. They have a great selection of various foods all in one location. From burgers to sushi to donuts,  cupcakes,  etc.  Everyone will be able to find something they like. They have seating scattered throughout the market but you have to act fast as the seats get taken pretty quickly.

The only thing I would buy here is flowers.  
No way would I buy food or eat here.
Look around; you'll see why.
This is a must stop attraction for anyone visiting Philadelphia.  You will find some of the best food on earth here.

The Reading Terminal Market was originally opened in 1893 by the Reading Railroad Company.  There is  over 100 vendors selling baked goods,  produce, meat, poultry, fish, clothing, books, ice cream, subs - just to mention a few vendors. This is the home of Tommy DiNic's famous roasted pork sandwiches. It looked and smelled great, but I was won over by Hershel's East Side Deli for  hot pastrami on rye. No matter which vendor you choose, the food is going to be awesome!
So many choices! You can never go wrong. It's always hustle and bustle because it is such a staple in Philly.
Anybody who's visiting Philly needs to stop by here at least once. Good food everywhere you look. Absolute must see!!!

Absolutely beautiful little market in the heart of Center City. I loved the fact that's it's all indoors, yet there are so many small markets within that enclosed space (of about one city block).

There's a great variety of shops, from sweets/pastry/candy stores, to small coffee joints, to home decor, to stalls selling full meals and desserts, and even little stands where you can purchase produce. It feels almost surreal to see the huge variety of contrasting stalls and shops. There's also a large section in the middle where you can sit and eat food your purchase. 

It's a very quaint shopping destination, and a short walk from City Hall. Overall a nice place to visit in Philly!

It was my first time trying Filipino food and I would say I want to try more.
Among all the vendors at Bourse, I chose Lalo because it was so different from others. I asked for a recommendation from the owner, and chose to order Bas-ka-bob over rice.

The flavor was awesome! The smoky chicken was very well cooked without any parts that looked undercooked. The owner cautioned me that it would be spicy but I didn't feel anything. The sauce on the top is more sour and tangy than spicy.
The rice and vegetable salad was a good complement to the meat. And I loved the overall presentation of the dish with banana leaf! It really speaks to its origin.

Another thing I loved about this place was that the owner seemed to know his regular customers. In a market setting, they can really miss out on customer service but he was on top of it!!

I will come back to try other dishes for sure. The drinks also sounded really good :)

I moved 2 years ago out of philly and I am about to visit in a few days. I am so looking forward to coming back to this AMAZING establishment and getting the MK special. I've been salivating just thinking about it. Their food is so amazing and reasonably priced. Here I come!

SUPER busy inside always but a Philadelphia staple. A diverse array of food and desserts. I sometimes even go grocery shopping there to get produce, spices, and meats. My favorite place in reading terminal is definitely Beiler's Donuts. Their blueberry fritters are the bees knees! Always a long line but one of my favorite desserts in the city.
The only place I can get hard to find spices and a variety of coffee flavors ice cream hot donuts Bassett ice cream platter sandwiches and the list goes on my favorite place to shop

Can't really review single store front. I have been to most over past four years and I would say biggest suggestion is just go do a walk around and then let ur belly and nose decide for you. Everything is great and you will find something! Enjoy a true philly gem!

First off why is this listed as a sporting goods store?

I lived near Philly for ten formative childhood years. Reading Terminal was a fond but insubstantial memory - a blur of smells and associations more than any single event.

As an adult, it does not disappoint. In three days we came twice, feasting on cheesesteaks, buying cookies and coffee and generally seeing everything this food wonderland has to offer. 

What does Reading Terminal offer? Fresh produce, fresh seafood, cheese, meat, coffee, honey, jams, baked goods, chocolate galore, ice cream, pretzels, ethnic products, hippie dippie bath products, wine, clothes, and so much food ranging from Indian to Italian to Amish, scrapple to shawarma. 

Love it.
A must see if you are visiting Philly. Great selection of food and places to eat.
Love this place weather for eating, shopping, gift buying. Whether your a local or tourist definitely go. They have great food for lunch and I feel safe with the covid measures they have in place!

Cute market with a bunch of vendors selling a variety of stuff. There's also a bunch of restaurants too! So definitely check it out and see what each stall offers. I walked in and wandered around and it felt like Chelsea market in nyc. They also have bellers donuts here and cheese stands! I saw honey, beeswax candles, herbs, meat and cheese, cookies, pudding, cakes, and more!

You could go there a million times and always have something new to eat. Never disappoints and besides lunch time it's pretty relaxing to sit and enjoy your food. The donut place is my favorite and the roast beef place is my second. Really easy access from suburban station.

OMG OMG! How much do I loveeeee this place!!!! During the nice days I love walking over there. Soooo many selections, from handsome soaps, homemade liquor, all of which  not only looks good, but is amazing!!!! And the food court! There's something for everyone!!!

I love going to the butcher there. And the seafood monger!!!! A lot of things I cannot get at the regular supermarket and at reasonable prices. 

Crowded all the time though. So I usually go in the morning and off hours!

Al-Qaeda believes that heaven has the promise of 7 virgins.  I now know that they are wrong.... Heaven is located right here in the walls of this building!

I am currently updating my resume so I can move to Philly to frequent this place on a daily basis.  

My goal would be to start in the Dutch Bakeries and eventually eat and drink my way to the Italian Sausages.

Until then I still have the memories of that wonderful day at the Philly Farmers Market     

Philadelphians you are so lucky!
This place is magical. Sensory overload but such a cool collection of foodies. From grocers to restaurants, must stop here for the experience AND food

This is one of the nicer looking Chick-fil-A  restaurants. Service is slow and not very friendly. You are better off ordering inside if there is a long drive thru line. But I happily give this place 4 stars because the actual chicken they deliver here is as good as it gets for Chick-fil-A. Perfectly crispy and delicious. The breakfast chicken & egg biscuit is a particularly tasty breakfast.
This place is great and fast and has excellent food in a generous portion size for the price

As a Philly native, there's not a thing I don't like about this place, except for the crowds that seem to never disperse except at 4pm in the Amish section. Let me give you 2 of my favorite sweets places:

Beiler's is a conveniently located donut spot in the predominantly Amish section on the 12th street side closer to Arch street. My favorite donut(s) are the fritters, but particularly the blueberry one.

4th Street, the best cookie stop in the city IMO, is smack dab in front of the entrance at 12th and Filbert. These humongous cookies are sold by weight, but I pretty much always leave with at least 6 because getting to the counter is almost impossible some days. The peanut butter chocolate chip and regular chocolate chip are divine, but you can't really go wrong.

Obviously I could go on and on, but I'll let you take the adventure on your own.

Honeygrow is near and dear to my heart, a personal favorite of the surrounding Temple campus restaurants. It is literally PERFECT for those who are hungry on a budget and on a diet, but still want to have a good fulfilling meal. 

So many different combinations and this place is the epitome of innovation. With advancing technology, skip the ordering and head straight to the huge sleek touchscreens. With a couple taps, you get to fully customize your order, and if you're not sure what to try, they have the pre-made honey grow favorites but still super easy to swap out every little thing to pick and choose your faves. 

I've tried all the different flavors, bases, proteins, toppings - I've finally found the perfect combination (in my opinion). My new go-to order is the spicy garlic chicken combo BUT swap out the sauce for the sesame garlic. I love the combination of ingredients of the order, but the sesame garlic sauce is too good to pass up. 

Orders in the restaurant come with these cool bowls with a little duvet to put your chopsticks, so cute. To go orders come in Chinese take out boxes, even cuter. Hefty portion, everything is cooked to perfection with an amazing balance of saucy, savory, crunchy, soft, chewy, moist, you can have it all. Orders come out FAST so if you're short on time, this place is perfect. 

And to top all of this off, the place even comes with FREE WIFI.

I LOVE Reading Terminal. There's so much variety. Although things have changed since COVID they are slowly opening back up. I know its not good for their businesses, but I love that its not as packed as before. It can be suffocating when the market is packed. Some of my favorite stores are Giunta's, Thai Food Market, Mueller's Chocolate, Miller's Twist, By George, and Golden Fish Market. I'm down here almost every week w/my co-worker and then on my own. You can always find something new to eat.

Simply the best!

Foodies in Philly this place is for you. Anyone in Philly, this place is for you. Foodies all over the world, hop on a plane and get your (hungry) butts over here. 

Seriously though, show up hungry and come with a couple of friends so you can share and try lots of different things. 

I've been here countless times and still haven't even scratched the surface of all that there is to offer. You've got Vietnamese, BBQ, Amish/Pennsylvania Dutch, Cajun, and Middle Eastern just to name a few. Then there are fresh cheeses, meats produce, honey, and handmade goods. 

This is the top place I bring guests from out of town. Some of my favorite vendors are:
-Hershel's: get a corned beef sandwich, thank me later
-Miller's Twist: soft AF and better than any soft pretzel I've had in my 20+ years living in Philly
-Flying Monkey: get their whoopie pies (shhhh don't tell the Amish you're cheating on them)
-Bassets Ice Cream: I promise the long line is worth it. The flavors are super unique and it is always the best way to end the trip!

Reading Terminal Market is a cool place to visit once and it's not a place I would go back to. There are a ton of food offerings from sandwiches to burgers to middle eastern, fresh baked goods, bars, fresh (raw) seafood, fresh butchered meat and vegetable stands. Again nothing out of the ordinary but a cool place to visit once.
Love this market! They have everything, fresh meats, fruits, and vegetables. Bakeries are both excellent! Warm chocolate chip cookies at cookie place. There's a great variety of food here.
Always something wonderful here!  wish there was more opportunity for seating.  Love visiting when I'm in the city.  always bring home something great to eat!

Very traditional place, everyone advised me to visit it for food. It's not like as I expected. However, some places do have great good. I will advise to pass by but not like to drive and spent time trying to find the unlimited meal. Overpriced in general.

AMAZING. Perfect leopard pattern on the bottom, airy crust, tastes like it's been fermenting for days (just overnight). Great, high quality ingredients, too. Good service, fast-eating atmosphere (no seats makes it a slight drag). Feels classic and unpretentious. Five bucks for a pepperoni slice is worth it since it is the best pepperoni slice I've had in a long time. I'm definitely gonna keep coming back.

Went to the Dutch Counter. Not sure that is the actual name but it is an Amish place that makes fresh homemade foods. We had breakfast and they had the most amazing homemade strawberry jam. So delicious.

SOLID PIZZA! 

Be prepared...there will be a wait! Have the right mindset, and just wait - it's worth it.

Super tiny store front, which leaves every square inch of the shop smelling like the fresh ingredients and baked dough.

The 2 guys running the place are hustling the whole time. You can tell their passion pours into the pizza.

Limited options, which was appreciated, just makes it for a quick and direct decision making process. 

If you're lucky, you can order some different varieties, but if you can't, definitely try to get the tomato pie and a regular slice. 

There are some standing tables inside and small seating options outside. 

Music was on point inside, and crazy pizza-oriented art all over the walls. just really cool vibes. 

The pizza itself was really good! Crispy crust, coated with extra olive oil and cheese - so delicious. Those little details just make the whole thing. The sauce and cheese combination play really well together, and the the pie itself is cooked perfectly. Firm, but still enough give to bend in half if that's how you prefer to chow down. 

All in all, really solid spot in Fishtown that I think can be a staple for a long time.

If you are Lebanese and like grape leaves, leave these ones alone. Unlike any I've ever tasted, and not in a good way. 

Babaghannouj was decent, eggplant wasn't roasted so there isn't the signature smokey flavor I prefer. 

Wrap was decent, I guess. Was really hoping for decent casual Lebanese food in CC. This just ain't it.

The last time I visited Reading Terminal Market was over 10 years ago, when I was in middle school. Even at such a young age, I knew this place was special. The thing I remember most from that time was an ice cream cone that was bigger than my head at the time, but you better believe I polished off that entire thing! Now, coming back as an adult, I was able to appreciate Reading Terminal Market in all of its full glory. Over the past few years, fancy, often overpriced food halls have become more popular, but Reading Terminal Market embraced that concept years ago, and is quite reasonably priced. There are upwards of 30 vendors offering everything from meals to dessert to groceries and various Amish delicacies. It is always extremely crowded on weekends and at lunchtime on weekdays, so if you can go during off-peak times, you will have the best experience! Keep in mind that this is not a fancy restaurant, and not necessarily the cleanest, most modern interior, but the food is great and the prices can't be beat!
Been coming here all my life the atmosphere is wonderful and all the food is great.

This is a GREAT grab-and-go Indian cuisine spot! I forgot to take a pic of my Chicken Tikka Masala wrap but it was very delic. You can get pretty much anything on the menu in a wrap and go with it. Flavor profile seemed Gujarati influenced more so than South Indian or closer to the Nepal border. The cilantro chutney is worth the extra $0.50 too!

this was a fun place. claustrophobic nightmare. i had a reuben from Hershel's east side deli- tender over load of corned beef, oh so good
there were lots of choices of things to eat and drink. downside of this whole thing was the crowdedness.

What a nice place to get some Taiwanese comfort food! 

I ordered a combo fried giant squid (with an upgraded drink -- green tea grapefruit) and a samurai crispy chicken for takeout. My partner and I had such a satisfying cheat meal for $18.

The staff kept the box with crispy chicken open so it stayed crispy when I got home. The deep fried crispy chicken (both the chicken and the crust) is thinner than American-style fried chicken and very delicious with Taiwanese teriyaki sauce. The fried giant squid is also tasty, but more greasy than the chicken.

The green tea grapefruit drink is jumbo, almost like a big fountain drink in movie theaters. With a huge slice of grapefruit in it, it's visually pleasant! I asked for the low-sugar option, so it's a refreshing drink with the right sweetness level for me.

This place is mostly cash only (like many places in Chinatown). The minimum for credit cards is $15, but they accept Wechat Pay. However, the wait can be long.

Love, love, love Pizza Shackamaxon. Awesome place and the prices are reasonable. Pizza Shackamaxon has a wonderful Plain Slice, it was my choice today, and it was absolutely delightful. Bonus that their service is so good, they are so fast and helpful. Pizza Shackamaxon you make so happy.

Reading Terminal is one of my favorite areas in Philly to spend time wandering and getting food. I visit often on my lunch hour and have sampled a wide range of cuisine - from Cajun at Beck's Cajun Cafe to Burgers at Hunger Burger, and soul food at a Keven Parker's Soul Food Cafe to delicious fresh Amish food at the Dutch eating place and desserts like famous Beiler's donuts and Bassets ice cream. Such a wide range of amazing food!! There's also a fantastic produce market that has fresh fruits and vegetables and nuts which I've shopped in many times. They even have clean bathrooms for guests, and you'll need them if you spend an afternoon there like many people do. Love, love Reading terminal. Highly recommend during a visit to Philly!
I LOVE this place and the variety of wonderful foods, friendly merchants and festive environment.

Nice cute place in Pennsport. The inside had a very warm feeling with a lot of wood (floors, tables and bar). Looked like a great place for brunch, a first date or going out with family. It felt cozy despite being  a rather open space and without feeling too romantic. With that being said, we sat outside. Thankfully the tables were in the shade and you didn't feel like you were sitting in the street.  Definitely kid friendly during the day and according to my sister they are dog friendly too (outside of course). 

The menu was small but pretty diverse. My dad got a burger, I had an oyster po'bo, my BIL had a pulled pork sandwich and my sister had a grain based salad (quinoa?). We all loved our dishes and I kinda regretted not getting the salad my sister got because it just looked that good.  Oh and the beer menu was excellent!  Lots of craft brews!  

Our server was sweet and friendly.  She stopped back a few times to make sure we were all okay and to ask if we needed more drinks. 

We skipped dessert because Federal Donuts (doughnuts?) is just a short walk away!

I was walking by and came across this restaurant. I ordered the lamb and chicken Tikka Kati roll with egg and a mango lassi to drink. I must say that the food here tasted very delicious. I'm not big into Indian food although I'm Indian. But definitely worth a try if you want something quick and filling to eat.
Place is a foodies dream come true! Lots of variety and the people who work their are really nice... I LOVE THIS PLACE!!!!
The ultimate tourist trap.  But I love it though.  If you want to get a quick overview of Philly, especially food-wise, you have to stop here.
dont recommend if you have a social anxiety, panic disorder, or ptsd. food is good though. would recommend via grubhub.
Mexican food for gringos who don't know what real Mexican Food is. Their tacos and burritos are tasteless and will cause you to do nothing but fart for days.

Very good tomato pie and excellent pizza slice.

The menu is limited, but what they make, they make well, so really no need for much more. 

There is a bit of outside seating available as well.

The service was quite friendly and helpful, making it a great place to get some pizza in Philadelphia.

Lots to see and eat. There is a sit down diner, wine, and a produce market to boot. Many choices for cheesesteaks, Asian cuisine, and dessert. Ice cream at Bassets, Amish breakfast, and Dinic's are good choices.

Love RTM.  Great food vendors meat and fish markets and of course fresh produce.  You can find that unique item you can not find in the typical grocery store.  Let's support them...it's a Philly institution.

For some reason the employees at this location have the attitude of a McDonald's worker. I've always known chic fil a employees to be welcoming and nice but I have yet to experience this at this specific location. Also my food is never really hot. I think I will travel to a farther location to get the service that I deserve.

The food was good and the ingredients were fresh, but they commit highway robbery if you order online to go. I ordered extra chicken in my bowl which cost an additional $3.70. When I received my order it only consisted of one serving size of chicken (which is small to begin with). Normally I don't let something like this bother me, but if you're charging an arm and leg for extra chicken you better add it.

The staff employed here are also very lackluster. I was the only customer in the store and was not greeted nor helped despite clearly being confused about how to pickup my online order. 

I will not be returning to NAYA due to these reasons.

I've been here many times. Sometimes I grab a quick meal (Jury duty!), sometimes I sat, lingered, shopped....Really, it is a landmark and the longest running market of its kind in the US. Stuff you, Covid!

If you are a local, or not too far, consider stopping in.

LOVE this place - the food is so fresh and delicious. However I am only giving it 3 stars because the location is always CLOSED. I don't understand.  And what's equally as confusing is that when it is open, the hours are terrible. Closing at 4pm on a weekday and completely closed on the weekend? How do the owners expect to stay open/make any profit when the store is closed way more than it is open. It's disappointing as someone who enjoys the food and would like to order from the restaurant more often but am unable to. And for this reason, I foresee it closing down completely soon, which I hope doesn't happen but is nevertheless likely imminent based on the way in which it (barely) operates.

What's not to like. It the single place I always tell out of towners to visit in Philly. U can get what you want for reasonable pricing. I love browsing the book store, grabbing a beer in the tavern, and of course all the Food vendors from Spataros HUGE sandwiches to the Amish style baked goods. YUMM!

I came here to pickup a door dash delivery and it took them 20 minutes after I got there for them to have the food ready and half of their employees were wearing masks under their nose. Not just that but half the people waiting for pickup also wore their masks wrong and weren't told to correct it. This place is a public safety hazard.

This was A-day and an adventure I got to come to Philadelphia for 5 hours and I took did the most  I could in a short amount of time. The Reading Market  Is an adventure in itself there is so much to choose from every food group to choose from.  When you walk in it is an amazing treasure hunt if you want something sweet to eat something with fish something with philly cheese steak, chicken, soups, chocolate whoa did I say chocolate oh my goodness everything.  If you ever come to Philadelphia walk to the market street and 12Th and go visit this adventure you  Will not be disappointed eat to your heart's content.
they close early, but that can be expected from a market setting.  Love it
Amazing options. Creative and unique set up. Excellent food options. Plentiful parking options. Amazing location

I really wish I lived closer to the Industry. The food here is seriously fun, and delicious to boot.

On our first visit, my boyfriend and I just ordered food - mac & cheese croquettes, wild boar ragu, and the Korean BBQ pork belly sandwich. I can't pick a favorite dish, or even really rank them in - they were all unique and rich in flavor in their own ways.

The mac & cheese croquettes are creamy, rich, and cheesy fried balls sent from the gods. My boyfriend didn't love/need the kimchee puree, but I thought it added a great spicy/tangy flavor to the creamy ball of goodness. 

The wild boar ragu is rich, meaty, and warm - not a great dish for the end of August, more ideal for the depths of winter. Nonetheless, it was great. The boar is braised for hours and is falling apart in a rich tomato based sauce.

The Korean BBQ pork belly sandwich was sloppy, meaty, and full of BBQ/Asian flavors. I ate my half quickly and don't remember much else, aside from loving every bite of it. The fries were nice, too, but not the focus of any plate by any means.

Our server was really nice, attentive, and knowledgable about both the food/drink menu.
A GR8 place to get all kinds of food, meats and cheeses, eat-in or eat-out. Definitely stop in while downtown Philly. An experience.

The food tasted good for sure, but I wasn't blown away. The meal portion was a bit on the smaller side, which I guess is pretty typical when ethnic cuisines try and be trendy. The value for money wasn't so much the issue in this case but that I was hungry after the meal. The pork belly was tasty and the tomatoes worked really well with the dish. More sauce would have made the meal perfect and a little less dry. I have a feeling I would have been more satisfied with a hole-in-a-wall Filipino restaurant outside of Center City.
Good fast Indian casual takeout. Highly suggest as a lunch spot great flavor on the basmati rice and biriyani

Wonderful bazar of various food vendors. Nearly something for everyone. From a market fresh produce, vendors selling honey and cheeses, burgers and gyros, salad bar, to southern BBQ, wonderful pastries, and delicious chocolates. If you're hungry and looking for options right downtown, with a full compliment of visuals and smells, this place delivers.

Man, I really wanted to like this place. I'm not the biggest fan of fusion, but dumplings are kind of an even playing field for most cuisines so I was hopeful. To be super scientific, I got one of each of the regular, non-special dumplings fried. The consensus of all of them is that they don't really have enough flavor to be a dumpling, nor the food that they're paying homage to. The buffalo chicken was my favorite, but only after adding the house hot sauce. The honey chipotle chicken was completely unnoteworthy, the cheesesteak needed salt and cheese, and the other two were just okay. I feel like maybe the noodle dishes are a bit more satisfying in flavor, but the namesake of the restaurant really should be the home runner, shouldn't it?

Anything and everything you want to eat in one awesome place. Well maintained and very clean. This is an indoor cafeteria. I highly recommend Carmen's cheesesteaks. The donuts are made fresh everyday and melt in your mouth. I wasn't able to try everything but I look forward to visiting again in the future!
I forget where I got the salmon I had but it was here and it was AMAZING!!!!! I live in Germantown but I'll go all the way down to center city just have it again because it was sooooooo good!

Horrible. I can in with the intent to claim my free guac and chips. As soon as I walked in the young man at the beginning of the line was being very rude and smart toward me and made me feel very uncomfortable and disrespected just to mess around with his coworker and have a laugh. I was so upset. I walk to the front of the line to claim my free guac and chips and the young lady proceeded to tell me I needed to buy something to claim my FREE REWARD! You literally spend money in order to get this reward... that is the point of the reward it is a thank you for spending money at their restaurant. I never had this problem before. Obviously the managers need to be careful who they are hiring these days because the workers are rude and do not know what they are doing, also they just lost a faithful customer and I will proceed to tell my friends and family not to come to this chipotle ever again...

I like this place they have a famous donut place and ribs but oh my how dirty the whole building is. Super hard to find available tables and chairs. Especially clean once. Bathrooms, don't even ask. Wish they had more staff available at each designated area for Quick cleanups!
A must-visit at least once in your life...and will return because you didn't experience everything this amazing market has to offer.

Drive-thru
Spicy chicken deluxe sammich (hint: #4)

That's all I gotta say. 

BEST grubbin at a fast food joint..

Reading Terminal Market has everything anyone could ever want! Restaurants and shops of all different types of food. I've tried a handful of restaurants and all of them have been delicious. I also go here every week to get my produce because it's cheap and fresh! If you are in Philly, you must stop by here to grab a meal!

The new Bourse is already looking promising! I've been following LaLo since they announced they snagged a plot in the new food court so I was super excited to make it down for the soft opening. I got the inihaw and took a bite from my boyfriend's longanisa dog. Admittedly, I can't pick a favorite between the two! The bun on the dog was grilled and anything super garlicky is a winner in my book! The chicken skewers in the inihaw dish were cooked to PERFECTION and the sauce was unlike anything I've ever had. My only critique is the rice was a bit undercooked so it still had a mild chalky texture. The portions themselves are also more of a snack size than a meal, so I hope in the future there are sizes added for us hungry folk

Solid street Indian food. Chicken and rice tastes almost like the halal guys in NYC.  The Kati roll was decent. I had the chicken masala roll and the veggie roll.
The veggie roll was surprisingly better spice then the chicken roll. 
Great place for groups and enough seating to go around. 
Different lassi to try including rose and mango. Catering available with FREE delivery. I'm totally game for that!

I have mixed feelings about this place.  I want to support it because this place reminds me of the Essex St. Market.  As I quickly walked past all the local produce and shops, I wanted to support the Amish community.  I feel bad for them, no technology what kind of life is it worth living!?*
But then I saw a sushi place and there was an 8yr old girl sitting at a stool at the counter taking orders.  Isn't that child labor!?  I don't support that.

I think some order needs to be defined.  They should only allow local produce and local stores to resell here.  The Amish people shouldn't be shoved into tiny isles and corners, they should have nice booths setup to display their beautiful produce.  There was hours of hard labor put into growing that Napa cabbage.  It was gigantic and I wanted to buy it to bring home but I'd never finish eating it within a week.

I came in search of lunch and when I smelled the pork from Tony DaNic's, I quickly got into line.  This is not to be missed people.  If you come into this market, you'd better not leave without a hoagie.

*There should be an Amish country reality TV show.  They could bring in outsiders and see how long they survive.  Similar to Survivor, whoever can live w/o technology the longest wins.  If I were a contestant, I would totally corrupt them.  I'd be deemed evil and they'd kick me off the island..I mean the Amish land.

I've always experience great customer service at all Chick-fil-A restaurants.....however, this location is the only location i haven't seen good/great customer service.

The girl, Daytona, took our order at the register...looked she did not want to be at work or take our order.  Very straight faced.  She was also didn't speak much. Didn't hear the usual "it's my pleasure also."
(7/5/19 , 6:17pm, order # 6109275)

The food was okay.  The fries were only halfway filled.  The cheese and lettuce was not nicely packed within the sandwich.
Iconic Philadelphia food landmark. Something for everyone. Sang Kee Peking Duck is a personal favorite. Make sure to try the steamed dumplings.

Took a couple tries to catch this place open. First time we came they were randomly closed (it was during regular business hours and nothing was posted on the IG, but there was a sign on the door) so that was a wasted trek. 

Super thin crust that's also super crispy-charred. To me, it's the kind of slice I'd enjoy if it were cheaper. I think at the price point I was expecting a bit more so set myself up for disappointment. I wouldn't go out of my way to go back but would eat it again.

We came on a Sunday.   Parking on 12th in the garage horribly tight and scary driving up the ramp barely made it by the concrete side by and inch.  People so packed and shoving each other so very very bad place to bring young children.   Would have given less stars except for the historical aspect.  They really need to make it more family friendly.  Will not be back anytime soon .   Most other families looked harried.  Bottled juice 3.50 so twice price of regular items.

Everything Philly can be found at Reading Terminal.  Choosing a favorite food stand is like saying you have a favorite child.  There are plenty of choices and none are wrong.  Yes, there are long waits. It is always crowded especially on weekends.
A must see while in Philly.  Great place to grab some food.  Unique and several choices. Don't miss this!

Shackamaxon has great slices that you can walk in and grab most times very quickly.  The specials are always creative and very good.  Crust is crispy and pizza is very flavorful.  It is one of the better slices in Philadelphia.   These guys do it right!

All I can say is incredible! Recently went to Philadelphia for a few days for the Flower show, stopped in here to check it out and found our lunch and dinner place for the next 2 days! Anything you could possibly want to eat is here. Anything you could want to eat and bring home is here! lol Seriously though if you go, walk around it first and get a feel for all it has to offer. The choices are incredible, there can be lines, but they move quickly, and all the food places we stopped at served incredible food. I wish we had one here, since we don't I can look forward to revisiting on my next trip to Philadelphia. If you're hungry, this is an excellent resource!

The pizza here is probably the best in Philly. Better than Beddia, Angelos and Circles and Squares. Where this place loses a star is the attitude. I've been here 3 times and each and every time, no matter the time of day, if you try to order a whole pizza it's like the end of the world. They look at each other and say something along the lines of "oh god, should we just stop for the day?, can you do 1 more? Should I tell him no? Etc." The first time I went was shortly after the barstool review, so I figured they were just stressed. But the other 2 times were exactly the same. They'll say the wait is like 45min - 1hr, but when you come back in 45min your pizza is cold because it's been done for about 20min. I just don't understand why they make it seem like you're the bad guy for ordering a whole pizza. Just makes me not want to go back, which sucks because the pizza is amazing.
I love this place! The donuts are the best you gotta try it! Next up is the crepe place!
cool place.

It's a wonderful place to shop, stroll and meet people from EVERYWHERE. There are older markets in Europe but nothing more wonderful in the US of A.

Upon entering I had instant deja vu recalling that I last visited here when I came to Philadelphia in 2003.    It really hadn't changed that much (save possibly different vendors).    I arrived in Philly just around a quarter to one on Saturday.   After trekking it to La Reserve B&B to check in, I made my way back in search of a place called By George that had gotten rave reviews for their cheesesteaks.   Little did I know that they were located inside of Reading.

So I got there around 2:30 and it was quite the madhouse.   It took a long time to figure out where By George was but I eventually found it.   Of course there was a long line but it actually moved relatively fast.   The next challenge was finding an open spot in their food court area to devour the cheesesteak.    I eventually did find a place and as I finished I scanned the crowded area and saw Flying Monkey which looked to have some interesting desserts.

After my lunch I went to Flying Monkey.   I was checking out the desserts near the line.  The one dessert that caught my eye was their butter cake.   I was about to turn towards the line when I encountered a rude grandma who sternly told me to move out of the way so she can get in line.   I told her I was in line and she was ready to fight me.   When she realized I wasn't going to move, she bitched and moaned the whole time.  I looked away from her but could feel her steely eyes staring me down.    I eventually got my order of butter cake and left.   I imagine with the crowds there are probably a few fights that break out.

I found the cake so delicious I made a return trip to Reading the next morning on route to heading to the airport.    It was a lot less crazy and if I were living in Philly, I'd definitely opt for going in the morning to avoid the crazy grandmas and the large crowds.   With that said this is definitely a great place to visit while in town.

I don't even know where to begin. A wide variety of things (edible goodies) and places to eat. I could only imagine how much weight I would gain if I lived closer to here and ate here every day. Probably would make a dent with the number of vendors and options available after a year. I wouldn't say that this place is a tourist trap as locals also come here. This place does get crowded.

Great place to grab fresh food or prepared food.  Great location next to the Philadelphia Conference overwhelming number of places to choose from. Easy to get lost inside. Center. Lines can vary depending on spot and time of day but staff all do a great job of getting everyone taken care of quickly.  Everything from fresh fruit to deli meat or prepared cheesesteaks to Peking duck. Great sweets too fudge, cookies, and arrays opetite desserts. Yummy salmon bisque and fresh bread. Only open to 6 on Sundays and some of the stalls don't open (Amish and others). Some places that don't open on Sunday lease out their space other vendors.

We made the mistake of stopping here for food before we went to the Flower show.  We walked the entire building looking for something that caught our eye in the crowds.  They only thing we wanted (chicken and waffles) the vendor Keven Parker didn't have even though he had multiple signs saying he did, so we left and ate $8 philly pretzel dogs which really cost 2 for $5 when you aren't being ripped off.  Not an impressive food trip.
My wife buys our veggies, lunch meats and meats there every week. It is so affordable and she loves the atmosphere. There are a lot of shops to choose from and lots of  delicious bakeries too.
Love this place, there is something for everyone. This is a must stop for a foodie visiting Philly or for someone looking for something different for lunch.

One of my favorite places to bring my out of state friends--It's the home of a lot of historical eateries and shoppes. Philly is known for its locally aged meats, so definitely stop by Godshalls to grab some fresh cut turkey bacon, turkey chops and ground turkey sausage if you're a poultry lover. Also, you can find other things such as a variety of honey flavors, handmade ice cream and pretzels as well as the fresh and locally grown fruits and vegetables at the produce market. If you're visiting from out of town, put this place on your to-do list!

Please do yourself a favor and check this place out.  It has some out of this world food. Stop for lunch with some cooked food or grab yourself some fresh groceries for the house.  This place has a variety like no other.

This Honeygrow location has gone really downhill over the last two years since it's been open, both in terms of service and the food. As a law student pressed for time, I like the convenience of the HG+MG app when I'm at school, but when I order something ahead of time for pick-up, I expect the pick-up time to be more or less accurate by +/- 5 minutes. I've once waited 17 minutes past my pick-up time.

Also, this location has been putting wayyyyy too much sauce on the noodles. I've had to specify light sauce the last few times I went.

I've stopped visiting this location, which is such a shame because the location is so perfect.

The most fabulous pizza. Never thought I'd recover after Beddia left but these dudes are doing. pizza. right. Thank god you can walk in for a slice. No queuing for hours for the best pizza of your life. All hail PIZZA.

It's really hard to complain about Reading Terminal. There are so many options for us foodies. I say try and get there early as it gets crowded as the day goes on. The best spots are The Thai Kitchen and Terminy cookies (in my opinion). But I've heard the pork roast sandwich is yummy. Sometimes they have live music playing and I love the community feel of the eating areas. A must try for anyone visiting Philly.

Went here for lunch takeout with BF. We both work in the area. Being from India, we love our spicy flavors. This place is lacking. We ordered 2 chicken biriyanis, 1 aloo paneer roll and 1 chicken pepperwala roll. Pros: Yelp 10% discount; portions were good; rice and/or meat portion was adequate per order; roti soft; cool roti maker; food hot; kati rolls decent; good box for rolls; prices reasonable. Cons: biriyani is lacking all traditional flavors and spice- i hate having to recook any food. I had to with some indian spices. We Indians like our traditional Indian food.  Give spice choices to everyone but if you say the dish is spicy, taste it and make sure you are correct. Use traditional biriyani masala. Get rid of white 'mayonnaise sauce' and the red 'Tabasco like' sauce. Not indian. Replace with pickle or even raita.
This is a Philly landmark!!! Great restaurants and farmers market! Go and enjoy! You won't have any regrets

I find it amusing that in Chinatown there's at least two shops/restaurants that makes the exact same type of food. Cheers cut's direct competition would be Chi-Ken. Competition is usually a good thing because it promotes quality but that doesn't seem to be the case in this Chinatown. In fact, there are several restaurants in Chinatown that are mediocre at best with deceiving hip music & decor. Cheers cut is no exception to this. 

I order the fried chicken nuggets to-go and it came in a closed container with no holes. Needless to say my fried chicken nuggets were not crispy. Batter was bland - wish they added more black pepper and salt. I think adding some basil would help it as well. This place is by no means awful but it definitely doesn't do taiwanese fried chicken justice.
One of my favorite places in the whole world. Period!

It took me a really long time to get around to trying Naya because there are so many delicious middle eastern offerings in Center City--between Cava and Naf Naf and Dizengoff and Halal Guys and the ubiquitous food trucks--I thought they were crazy buying out a huge shiny glass space across from City Hall. But then I tried it and I totally get it!

What sets Naya apart: Juicy beef schwarma, freeka grain bowls, generous fluffy hummus and pita, cool creamy yogurt sauce, and unique condiments and snacks on the back shelves. And Naya just tastes fresher. As long as they keep their lunches hot and fresh, they'll keep bringing in the business as one of the best lunch places in Center City.

This is such a cool spot to come to. They literally have anything you could ever want to eat. My only complaint is a lot of the vendors are closed on Sundays, and I wish the place closed at 7/8 as opposed to 6. Overall though it's worth coming to. The Cajun restaurant had a wonderful staff, and the breakfast cheesesteak at Molly Malloys was delicious.

Have visited Reading Terminal a couple of times now and have always left satisfied although overwhelmed by all of the choices and options.  Multiple visits are required to experience all of it!

Usually arrive late morning before the lunch rush but this time we got here around 1 and they were busy/packed.  (Add re-opening and vacation time also). 

As mentioned, if you're looking for a dish chances are you'll find it here.  I was even surprised to see a Cajun spot & of course there is a cheesesteak stand.  Little shops with miscellaneous merchandise, Fishmonger, Butcher, Deli, bakeries, Ice Cream and an abundance of restaurant stands to name a few.  Favorite spots so far:  Beiler's Bakery (donuts, Sticky Buns), Dutch Eating Place (Apple Dumpling-award winning!), Mister Y's (Pretzels/Pretzel Dogs), Tommy Dinic's (famous Roast Pork) &  Flying Monkey Bakery (Chocolate Butter cake, mini flourless chocolate cake).

If you can find it, street parking is the cheapest option otherwise there are a few lots and garages close by.  

They've been around since 1892 and take up a full square block in Centre City.  A must stop when in Philly!  This place sets the bar for local food halls!

Tourist trap or not, this place is worth a visit.

+ Beiler's Donuts = HEAVEN.
+ Free food demo in the back left on the day we went (hello, turdurken!)
+ Lots of food choices from dumplings to pizza to cheesesteaks
+ Some specialty shops (shoutout to Bee Natural)
+ Public restrooms

The only downside is it gets very crowded and hard to find a seat. But be vigilant in your quest and be flexible with your experience... I enjoyed it all. :)

Ok, so if you are in Philly you have to stop here. Not only do they validate your parking pass for across the street (brings the price down to about $5), you have so many options to chose from it hurts. I can never make up my mind. They have the best donut place as soon as you walk in over to the left, there is always a line you can't miss it! There are various seating areas, but I suggest you take a quick (as quick as you can with so many options), scan what you think you may want and have someone or multiple people you are with wait at an empty table so you have somewhere to eat after you grab your food! A lot of the vendors are Amish therefore if you go on a Sunday most places are closed (and then those that are just closed on Sunday), but there is less of a crowd and still enough options to choose from:

I love the masala kitchen rolls. I usually get the panner tikka, paneer masala, aloo paneer or achari paneer roll. I've never been disappointed with their food quality. Masala Kitchen had modest pricing however be weary if you're using food deliver apps as I've noticed inconsistencies. I usually order from this place during the wee hours of the night as they deliver till 3am but some nights their deliver service takes awfully long. Almost always it's an hours wait however so worth it! Must try!

It was easy to spend a couple hours here perusing all the stalls and stopping to sample what the different vendors had to offer.

Beiler's Amish Doughnuts are apparently the thing to get here. I'm not usually a fan of doughnuts and found the apple fritter to be A-OK. Tasty, but nothing to write home about. I think I was hoping it would be a bit crustier.

I couldn't help but stop for a pastrami sandwich at Hershel's East Side Deli. The sandwiches are piled high, and you can order half a sandwich if you're concerned about filling up (which wouldn't be the worst thing in the world...)

Keven Parker's fried chicken boasts that it was named the Food Network's best fried chicken, and the wings didn't disappoint. We just ordered 3 wings for $7 to save room for other munchies, but the mac and cheese looked incredibly cheesy. The only downside was that the tip, wingette, and drumette were all still connected, which made it a little difficult to eat.

WOW! there is something to be said about a place that has been open since 1893! Incredible. So many vendors, so many delicious choices. Many classics are there. Many of these vendors have been featured on many travel and food networks. Not one vendor disappoints. beiler's bakery and donuts are both a must! Their donuts are delicious, we bought a half dozen and we devoured them (what diet, am i right?! Haha).  Spatro's who has been there for 72yrs, is delicious as well, i had a steak egg and cheese sandwich, it was like a breakfast version of a NY chopped cheese. There's just so much see and taste. Take your time, and arrive with empty stomachs!

THIS CHIPOTLE IS HORRIBLE! I order a VEGGIE BURRITO AND GET BEEF. I ate it and didn't swallow. Realized something was off. I'm vegan and haven't touched any meat  in over 8 years. They never get anything right over here.

I love this place. They have a bit of everything from Amish stores, to eaters, to Candy stores, to bakeries, to fish markets. Literally, you can find a bit of everything here. I recommend terminis bro bakery, the creperie, franks, and beilers bakery. The terminal also offers nice and fresh fruit and vegetable stands!! Definetly worth the visit!!

Everyone else has got the food experiences exactly right.  All I would add there is don't miss the pecan squares at the Flying Turtle.  They are to die for!  One more thing: some of the best people-watching in Philly, especially in winter around lunchtime.
Its ambience is really warm and alluring. You have many options to eat there or take away. It is too bad that market is closing at around 6pm.

This place is trash. The wrap I got was so soggy it was inedible. One more disappointing and disgusting thing about the Philly airport, not to mention the city itself. Save yourself the headache, and possibly an episode of digestive problems.

Disgusting staff... who are yall hiring nowadays kfc? A bunch of nasty attitude-no customer service skilled- rude people from around the corner? Please do better at selecting managers supervisors and employees. Yall gonna lose money big time! Worst kfc i ever been in...

I absolutely loved Reading Terminal! There were rows and rows of different ethnic foods and even more dessert options, how can you not fall in love with Reading. 

When you first enter the building, you'll be greeted with the sweet and savory aroma coming from all of the eateries. Your mind and stomach will be overwhelmed with all the goodness. 

Reading is a great place for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. If you are craving a snack during the day, you'll have more than enough options to select from. Reading offers Thai, Mexican, Greek, American, and Indian food, just to name a few. For someone who has a sweet tooth you'll get to choose from fresh made cannolis, doughnuts, cakes, chocolate, and cookies. 

Not only are there restaurants and stores in Reading, they also have stands that sell produce. I have also never seen any fresher poultry (chicken, lamb, beef) at a market. They even have a great selection of seafood (lobster tails, crawfish, clams, mussels, shrimps, crabs). There's even a stop for fresh cheeses and deli meats. 

During my short stay in Philly, I managed to come to Reading at least once every day. I came to either enjoy a meal or buy produce/poultry to cook a nice home cooked meal. 

I will definitely be paying Reading another visit whenever I come back to Philly. 

Tip: Some locations only accept CASH.
This was so amazing. The best of all Philadelphia has to offer food wise under one roof!

I usually review this place on a place by place basis, but Reading Terminal is an absolute institution in Philly, a must hit for any visitors, and a god-send when I'm trying to find fresh, local ingredients (particularly during the colder months).

This is a must-see if you're ever in Philly!
The market is huuuuge and has a ton of amazing food options - and such a variety! From the most delicious-looking sweets to the most savory-looking sandwiches, sides, and more. I truly wanted to try EVERYTHING.

It was really hard to choose what I wanted, but I ended up going with the lobster mac & cheese from one spot that I can't remember the name...but seriously you can't go wrong with whatever you end up choosing. But this lobster mac was fulllllll of cheese and lobster. So amazing.

100% recommend coming here!!

I love this place. A great place to come if you want options on food, drink, and grocery shopping. Multiple vendors for produce, meats, and cheeses. 
Great cafe with espresso, another spot for cheese curds, and just about any other thing you could imagine that would please the palate. 
A great date spot
Place to the family 
Or to just go and fully enjoy yourself.
Can't wait to visit again

Waited at the drive thru window for 5 minutes in silence, then ordered a grilled chicken sandwich and a frosty.  Paid, was given my frosty with no straw and was asked to pull into a parking spot to wait for my sandwich.  After 10 minutes of waiting in the car with a melting frosty, I had to get out of the car and stand outside to wait for someone to bring out my food because the door was locked at 9:30!  Really?  This is a fast food place, right?

I love this place, this is THE defining market of Philly. Always bustling with people, filled with all different kinds of amazing vendors, with a diverse variety of shops, from treats, to restaurants, to shops. This place is a very casual vibe, that makes you feel comfortable. Every time you come there, you will find a new place that you have never seen before. The bathrooms are relatively okay for a place that busy, but I am knocking off a star for the fact that there is never any room to sit down, due to the popularity of the place, but do not be dismayed by the 4 star rating, still go, as long as you don't plan on taking a seat.

Heard a lot of great reviews about this place! It was a 30min wait but was able to kill time by walking over to Weckerlys to enjoy some ice cream in the nice weather:) I got the tomato slices bc they didn't have a pie but the slices were big and the crust was thick! Tomato was delicious. Bc I'm dairy free, I couldn't try the pepperoni and specialty pie(basil cream base with Spanish onion and roasted garlic) but my friends loved it! Def would recommend for dairy free and non dairy free pizza lovers!! Come early and expect a wait cuz it picks up fast!
Awesome selection of all the Philadelphia hot spots. I would have given 5 stars but Everytime I have been there it is packed and hard to find a place to enjoy the food.

You want it? Reading Terminal probably has it. Beyond having amazing and sometimes hard to find foods, there are all kinds of fabulous restaurants that will make food for you. I wish I could pick a favorite, but I think it may be impossible. Make sure you take a day (and an appetite) and go explore!

Gem of Philly, a must for locals AND tourists! Filled with local produce, Amish farmers/Pennsylvania Dutch, freshly baked goods, hand churned ice creams, a small chocolate and candy factory showing their mold making techniques, artisan cheeses, fresh fish & meat, book vendors, spice shops, and soooooooo much more. Two of the merchants are even descendants of original vendors from the 1800's, how cool is that??!! Reading Terminal is great for grocery shopping, and lunch.. although it does get quite overwhelming with crowds at lunch. During the holidays they have a giant train display complete with tracks and train cars whistling and zooming around, RT also has lots of festivals and fun events for both adults and kids. I'm not going to list my fave food and market vendors because I love so much that is here and they would all be on the list. An awesome market, highly recommend!! Ah yes, I can't forget to tell you about Philbert! Philbert is the lovely 3' plump bronze piggy bank sculpture in the center of the terminal, he collects coins for charity. Eric Berg is a VERY special local Philadelphia sculptor, whose work is all over the city in major parks, the bear in Fitler Square, the dragon at Drexel, the vine covered cottage gate in Rittenhouse square, the sphere at Pennsylvania hospital and so much more. Reading Terminal is a gem, go!

This review is for the order placed for delivery. The hummus  is smooth and creamy, baba ganoush has perfect smoky flavor. Chicken  schawarma with grains has perfect flavor and seasoning. Tabouleh doesn't have much bulgur.

Baklava is a perfect dessert to end the meal. Nice flaky layers of phyllo.
No need to write a review, this place speaks for itself. Every option imaginable for food as well as some local artists and groceries available for purchase. Dope spot
Weather is a steak switch or chocolate this place has everything. I spend hours here looking and things and checking out and trying all the food. Also a funny ad tasty experience.

Gotta love open air markets that sell you incredibly fresh produce and has a list of endless, mouth watering vendors. Out of all the times I've been to Philly, I couldn't recall the details of Reading Terminal. Bf and I came here for weekend and we decided to come here for lunch on a Sunday. Sadly, Sunday means that the most notable vendor, Dutch Landing Co is closed (this is the Amish place every talks about). We talked by their booth and saw a delicious menu featuring chicken pot pie, blueberry pancakes, and that type of thing. 

We tried to eat as much as we could.  The famous sandwich shop here is the Pork place (sorry I don't know the actual name)- this is the one that serves the Italian bread hoagies with pulled pork, roast pork with broccoli rabe (which my bf got, with roasted sweet peppers), and beef..brisket? I don't really eat pork so I had a tiny bit. It seems watery and lean; the rabe was very crunchy and yummy. My bf loved it. It was some $11 with a drink. 

I went to Frank's chicken to get a side of homemade mac and cheese (yummy, very cheesy but not crunchy as I'd like) and 2 pieces of BBQ grilled chicken (not too sweet, but more like a rotisserie chicken- very yummy but nothing I hadn't had before- hot, with crispy skin and juicy), I wanted two homemade pierogis but they'd just ran out. Came to some $7. 

We walked around and sampled the jambalaya at the Cajun place, which was really spicy and yummy- I would have ordered from here again. Typical long lines included the pretzels and cheesesteaks. (We had pretzels from the same place that does chocolate covered stuff in the corner.. but sadly it was too stale. I'd get the famous pretzels off the street somewhere) 

 There is also that famous chocolate shop (another) that features pictures of Andrew Zimmerman (funnily) eating a chocolate covered onion (and not liking it). Instead, we sweet-ed it up with a big gooey chocolate chip cookie with walnuts from the 4th St Baking Company (cookie place near the entrance). 

While my travels have taken me to wonderful markets like Pike Place in Seattle and Granville in Vancouver..I've overlooked this wonderful little place close-by in Philly.

This is a great destination spot for starting a day trip to the Illa. Easy parking (keep in mind it's like 8$ for every 15 minutes. I'm only sort of kidding.) There's a bathroom. Inside this Market it's over- crowded and complete circuitry overload.  Lots of food and restaurant choices. Amish people, Jazz, Candy Apples, Various fruits, vegetables, meats an aroma of all things farmer market waft to your nose and if you're not hungry you wish you were. It all looks amazing. The only down side is that I left feeling like some rube tourist.
Obsessed. The cookie place has these amazing chocolate dipped lemon drop cookies. And my go-to is the falafel pita from the Greek stand. Really... All of it's good.

It's crazy crowded. 

The places in there are hit or miss.  It's worth checking out because there is something for everyone but be prepared it is crowded. 

Maybe it's because I'm not from the northeast, but it's too crowded for me. Hard to find a place to stand, much less sit, to eat.
Simply the best market in the region. Amazing vendors with long-standing staples for pizza, groceries and goods. Highly recommended from this local!

Love this place for fresh vegetables and food places to eat. Would not advise to buy seafood from the reading terminal market because the seafood is too expensive and not as fresh as other places. Everything else is great!

Foodies heaven. Must visit for all Yelpers.

This place was recommended by so many people including Uber drivers. It is unfortunate they close early. I wish they stay open for dinner.

Don't make the same mistake as I did and be sure to come hungry.

Amish soft pretzels looked really good. I know they are good as I had one in Lancaster earlier. I walked around, up and down and everywhere to check out each one of them.

This market alone is a destination and must visit in Philadelphia.

First stop in Philly. Right next to the Greyhound station.

Very old traditional American feel kind of market.
Deli shops, bakery, dinner etc.

Crowd looks older and I guess locals eat here too?

Quick stop for a quick bite, got an apple pie kind of thing from one of the Amish place.

The dish was ok, but guess it's good to try something traditional when in Philly.

Lots of variety & options in one place, but can become extremely crowded which is not really conducive to eating a nice and relaxing meal...often have to wait/hunt for a seat/table. Many of the places are over-priced, but it's one of those experiences when exploring Center City to do at least once. The produce markets do have good prices/deals and can find good deal at some of the seafood merchants. Parking offered at a discount or free at nearby garage...gotta check w them...I forget exact terms. At the end of the day the Dutch merchant puts many if the bakery items for sale. People literally wait in LONG lines for many if the merchants soooo something to be said for the demand...especially for the Amish Dutch food and Bieler's doughnuts.

The market is about 5 mins away from our hotel and it just makes everything so convenient. We tried the the roast pork sandwiches from DiNic's , it's good, but I'd enjoy it more if it's with roast beef. There's a long line there but moves pretty fast. We had juice at the Four Seasons Juice Bar, it's very delicious and the girls there are very friendly as well. We also got to try some donuts from Beiler'a Donuts, the price is so reasonable and the donut itself is very tasty. There are so much to try at the market, hopefully we will come back another time to try more food.
The best food market on the East coast. Jeep up the great food .. especially the Meat counters!
Great place to have a variety and tasty food! My wife and i love love this place...given it is so popular always crowded though
Wonderful place to go. Classic market lots of vendors and the best food in philly!! You have to go here or your not visiting good old Philadelphia pa!!

Now I understand what all the hype is lol.  I've never had Chick-fil-A before,  So I was pleasantly surprised by the great service and wonderful chicken sandwich I had. I had the spicy chicken and I have to say it had a good amount of spice on it. The fries were also good and the restaurant is clean. I'll definitely be back.

I will keep this super short and sweet.... 

Reading Terminal Market is one of the oldest and largest enclosed public markets in America. It is located directly across from the Philadelphia Convention Center (Corner of 12th & Arch Streets) in downtown Philadelphia.  This market offers everything from  handmade crafts--to fresh produce -- to fresh flowers-- to meats-- to seafood-- to fresh flowers-- and a plethora of dining options of every type of worldly cuisine. Make sure you bring your appetite and allow yourself plenty of time to wander through the enormous food bazaar. 

I ate at the 'DUTCH EATING PLACE' on my last visit.  I truly enjoyed their homestyle cooking. Everyone raves over their apple dumpling and breakfast fare. They can be found in the "Amish Corner" of the market and they're their perfect spot to sample classic Pennsylvania Dutch deliciousness. Again, there are plenty of options to choose from and you defiantly won't leave here empty handed or hungry.  

Final Verdict: This is a MUST VISIT if you're visiting Philadelphia.

The food is as excellent as always - less crowded than usual, but whether it's the duck at Godshall's, the baklava at Kamal's, Sang Kee's duck rolls, etc. etc., a wonderful experience. The produce, excellent cheeses, variety of chocolates, spices.. a feast for the senses!
Something  for everyone's  taste and very fresh food, wear your comfortable  shoes.  I love their meats a little pricey  but well worth it.  The only issue is parking that I  shop early.

A foodie's dream! So many different vendors, a melting pot of different cuisines. My favorites are DiNic's for sandwiches and Beiler's doughnuts. I will be back! 

Prices are very reasonable. They have a good amount of seating. Very casual. Make sure to get your parking validated.

This place is excellent. I had never had Filipino food so I wasn't sure what to expect. I was very happily surprised. I ordered the Bicol Express and loved it. I was impressed with how fresh and flavorful the veggies were and the addition of garlic rice made for a super combination. Delicious!  With terrific food and outstanding, friendly service, I highly recommend checking out this place.

I went with my S.O. so he could pick up a slice, and spotted the tomato pie coming out of the oven.  I couldn't resist.  Holy cow yelpers.. you were SO RIGHT about this slice of heaven. I should have taken the whole pie.

These guys have hit their stride and made this a great stop in for a slice, without the hype and wait of its previous occupant.  Highly recommend.

With the pandemic going on, it wasn't really crowded and there was plenty of parking too. But honestly, it's great to be in a place so full of culture and so full of choices. I definitely didn't have enough room in my stomach to try all the fan favorites.
Busy at peak times but often cheaper than the local Chinese grocery, and more exciting too
Lots of good food and a wide variety. It was pretty crowded when I went last week so if you don't like being close quarters with people during the pandemic I would recommend to wait.
Never disappoints...delicious baked goods, oysters, dinics, and bassetti's ice cream.  We always find something special to take home and the whole family loves it.

Man..  If I only lived closer, I'd shop here for all my meats and seafood needs..  This place has everything under the sun, from fruits and veggies, candy and cakes, coffee, Chinese Food, Indian, Sandwich shops, meats, seafood, beef jerky, ice cream, grilled cheese restaurant, etc....  You can really spend a day here and it's a MUST visit when you come to Philly...
This is a great place to get a "Taste of Philadelphia". Fresh food, plenty of choices and even a beer garden!

Very cool! Tons of sandwich shops, BBQ, Amish restaurants. All this while there are seafood markets, meat markets and a grocery store sprinkled about. Such a cool experience, if you want it, it's here.

No food courts (God, how I hate that term!) in the United States quite compare to Reading Terminal Market, IMHO. I mean it.

Not Pike Place in Seattle, nor even one of the many comparable markets in New York is quite the same.

The variety really makes it great, as does the quality of the average restaurant here.

For example, this Southern boy loves to grab a soul food meal, but my traveling buds often prefer to wander some distance away and grab bagels elsewhere, or seafood, or Creole, or a cheesesteak at Carmen's, or, well, you get the general picture here.

Prices are generally quite modest, as these eateries are serving masses of hungry people who demand good food at reasonable prices.

Not a good choice, though, if hustle and bustle freak you out.

In Philly? You really MUST stop here for an hour or two. (Take my word for this. It's a very important part of any good Philadelphia visit itinerary.)

I love chicken and lamb over rice Platters, I used to go to Spice End and I'm coming from 9th and Sansom, that's a long walk! Then I yelped and saw this! fairly new! And I'm glad I went in! the place is in a great location! Lunch hours it can be packed! so if you want to go in and out I suggest you call and place an order and decide if you want to eat in or take out. I've been here a lot of times and tried 90% of what's in the menu, I still can't find anything wrong with this place!!! Very tasty and great servings! They have great customer service as well! Highly recommended!

We've been having problems with places down that way going back years,although not that often,it's still common. Recently we ordered through GrubHub,but our items were still not completely what ordered. I don't know if the staff was distracted with talking like usual or what...
Great, nearly perfect pizza. Ordering it is a little annoying but it's very worth it.
Amazing place! Great food, and atmosphere.  We stayed across the street and went there every day.  So eclectic!

They have a wonderful variety of food and the prices are reasonable . The majority of places take credit/debit cards so thats a huge plus!

Bring your appetite because you'll want to try a little of everything

Where to start...head over to Down Home Diner for breakfast and a Banana-Pineapple-Orange smoothie at Kamal's and grab a box of donuts at Beilers.  Run around the block at least 10x to shed the calories.  Head back in for lunch - DiNic's for pulled pork or Spataro for a cheesesteak and fries, 12 St Cantina for loaded nachos, pearl's oyster bar for some shellfish and osyters ...grab a cannoli from Termini's and a bag of cookies at Famous 4th Street.. leave and go home and take a nap...and then go out and buy bigger clothes to fit in...worth it.

So many food places under one roof! Anything you have a taste for, it's probably here. A foodie's dream. There is also fresh fruits, fresh vegetables, baked goods, cheese, meat, ice cream and more. I came on a Saturday and it was very crowded. Some of the food places have their own seating areas while others do not. However there are general seating areas in various areas but it still may take you time to find a seat. I was lucky enough to find one in about 5 minutes. I would recommend to come with an empty stomach so you can try as much as you can. 

Best place to park
There is a public parking right across the street. If you spend $10 or more here, you can get a validation. 
Rates:
Up to 2 hours $5
Up to 2 1/2 hours $11
Up to 3 hours $17
*discount expires after 3 hours and fees are like $8 for 30 minutes alone 

There are restrooms here just in case you need one.

Word to the wise, avoid lunchtime hour! The drive thru is always at least 15 cars long. However, if you're a fan of Chik fil A, you'll probably just write another review whole waiting to pull up lol.. Food is always fresh, customer service is outstanding and the restaurant itself is always clean. I'm sure they get an award for best customer service practices every year. I've never had a complaint, just thankful there's one near me. Their milkshakes are divine..

Reading terminal market is amazing!! Good food, cheap food, exotic, local food, Amish food, Philly local food....... you can find anything you want here. Be careful, it's always crowded here. There isn't a day it's not busy. If you don't like people, this isn't your place. But if you want to explore different kinds of food Philly has to offer, this is it!!!! Can't express how much I love this place enough!
I have had some bad experiences there. It's good to see or to stop by during jury duty. Great for tourist to see.

This place is the BEST place to do grocery shopping, have lunch, and bring out of town guests to. I live only a block away and my grocery bills have gone down significantly because (most of) the shops at Reading Terminal are so much cheaper and fresher than a traditional grocery store. Iovine Brothers is great for produce, and they give student discounts of 10% on Wednesday and Sundays. Wan Seafood is great for fish supply. The spice shop right next to Flying Monkey has great spices, marinades, dressings, teas, etc. Not to mention the desserts are great at almost any of the chocolate shops.
