The beer garden and numerous lunch places (great cheesesteaks, falafels, crab cakes, anything you could want) make this great for groups also.

The Kati rolls are excellent! Got the chicken tikka and paneer tikka ones and both were great. Seasoned well and very tasty. Only wish they didn't charge $1.50 for extra sauce. That's too expensive. Other than that, loved the food.

This place is amazing! I would frequent Reading Terminal Market when I lived in Center City, Philadelphia. Whether it was for a delicious bite to eat, or to shop for ingredients, I found just what I was looking for & more! 

It's a interesting place to stroll, I would definitely recommend visiting!

Sooo jealous of the locals who are able to have lunch here or visit on the regular! Such a fresh VARIETY of food, with everything from gluten-free healthy to toothache diabetes sweet! Absolutely loved it! The smells walking through the aisles alone can stimulate your senses enough so that you'll be able to return to work with no problem. A straight uppercut to the beloved Pike Place of Seattle.

If you haven't been to the market yet, get there! It's got everything you could possibly need/want. Fish, meat, produce, wine, chocolate, sushi, smoothies, ice creams, salads, cheesesteaks, pizza, Amish stuff, honey store, kitchen store, Cajun, Chinese, turkey-centered, cookies, baked goods, whew- the list is truly endless. 

If you want to go to be seen and fight the crowds, go at lunch time. There's also a piano player in the center and group table seating open to all. 

If you want to save a few bucks, use your Level Up! Lots of the vendors participate in it within the market.

If you are going for the Amish baked goods, they're closed on Monday. Otherwise, go early and try their apple fritters- yum! The donuts are pretty good, too. The cakes and pies are just meh. 

Tootsie's Salad Express is pretty decent for a pay-by-weight salad bar with way more than just salads (think Chinese food). 

There is also a great little spice store in here that is great and also has a fantastic coffee bean selection. The people who work here are super helpful, too. 

There's also a bar in there, so if you're in mixed company and someone would rather have a beer than fight the crowd, well, there' truly is something for everyone!
Amazing- So may options and so much beautiful food. Best donuts i've ever had!

Wow, this is my new favorite place to go shopping.  Unfortunately, it's thousands of miles away from me since I live in California but my sister who lives here recommended that I visit and that I would love it; she was right.  I definitely have to come back for one more shopping trip before I fly back home.  Reading Terminal Market is an indoor market (perfect for a rainy day) and has many places to visit, eat and shop at.  The Market features bakeries (as pictured below), a mini meat and cheese market, a small scaled market that sells a variety of pastas, canned and dried fruits,  a whole produce section with fresh flowers, vegetables and fruits, a gigantic food court (I recommend getting the raspberry banana smoothie at the juice bar yum), and specialty stores too that are from around the world like the Holland shop (all items are designed and made in Holland) and feature some of the most beautiful ornaments and kitchen items I have ever seen!  And not to mention to satisfy your sweet tooth, there are many places to buy fudge, chocolate, cake slices and cupcakes too (oh my goodness)!  The Market can be a little crowded and a little overwhelming at times but this is a must see if you are ever in the area.

Stopped in here one morning while I was in Philly. If there's one thing I love it's food halls and markets like this. There's such a conglomeration of delicious food sights and smells and although it can be overwhelming to make a decision, you're almost never going to regret it. 

My theory still held true here when we stopped at The Fox & Son booth to order lamb fries. Not only were these visually appealing but the taste was beyond description. The best way to put it would be "explosion of flavor". They were just amazing. The lamb, the cucumber, tomatoes, feta, dressing - it all married perfectly. 

There were several other booths to stop at but we were short on time. 

My boyfriend and a friend of his went back a few weeks after and stopped at the donut place (when we were the line was incredibly long) and brought some back so I can attest that the long line is worth the wait. They were light, but dense and flavor packed. 

This place is an absolute must!
There are SO many options and if you can't find it at Reading Terminal, that's your problem! j/k But for real, it's awesome! So many options! Go! Go now!

Was an awesome place to wander around. So many stalls and interesting things - fresh produce and meat, handmade items and chocolate. Everywhere you turn there's something to see. I found an Indian food stall and had a tasty samosa. Easy to get turned around if you have no sense of direction like myself but it was fun.

There aren't many issues I have with the Philly food scene. It's a large reason why I've stayed in Philly vs. moving back to NY or Chicago. But if there's an area where the city could improve is in the availability of late night eats. I often dream of the "street meat" halal carts where you can stop by to get what you crave when it's past 2AM, all for a reasonable price. Thanks to Marilyn from Philly Grub, I've recently stumbled upon the solution - Masala Kitchen. 

Proprieter Vai Sonu and Chef Arjun have partnered up to bring flavor bombs in the form of Calcutta-style Indian street food. With most wraps and rolls, you've often stuck with a dry, tough flour tortilla that lacks flavor on its own. With Masala Kitchen, every bite is seasoned and will tantalize your taste buds without going overboard. It's also extremely portable, affordable, and almost everything made in-house.

Rose | Mango Lassi [$3.25]
Traditional yogurt-based drink
Kala Khatta [$2.25]
Sweet, tangy blackberry fruit
 
Pick up a couple of their lassi's to go. The traditional Indian yogurt-based drink is flavored with either mango or rose syrup and appear to be the perfect breakfast or workout smoothie. The Kala Khatta less viscous and is subtly sweet with a nice blackberry flavor. The mint lemonade was easy drinking as well, with the herbaceous sweetness offering up the perfect palate cleansing drink to end your meal. 

Chicken Biryani [$9]
Marinated chicken, basmati rice
 
MK's basmati rice is cooked perfectly, with juicy chunks of marinated chicken strewn throughout. And yes, they have the white and red sauces you often associate with street food. Balance each bite with the cooling white or amp up your spice level with the red!  

Paneer Masala Roll [$5.50]
Homemade cottage cheese, creamy tomato gravy "Makhani"
Chicken Kheema Roll [$5.25]
Ground chicken, lentil, Indian spices

But for me, the rolls are where it's at. The light and gluttonous paratha bread is lightly griddled on a large cast-iron tawa, which MK then fills with a number of delicious options. I'm usually not a big fan of paneer as it doesn't have much flavor on its own, but when coupled with their Makhani gravy, it's a blast of flavor that had me coming back for more. The chicken kheema offers a more savory spiced route, but nothing a douse of the white sauce can't balance out for the less intrepid eaters out there. 

MK also has a number of healthy rolls including a beet root and crispy cabbage roll. They just recently released a Pepperwala roll that marries juicy marinated chicken and their fresh-made paneer with crisp, fried green peppers. Just as delicious and definitely filling! 

So if you're looking for the perfect lunch or dinner option on the run - Masala Kitchen has you covered. And if you're out late on Friday or Saturday night and seeking a bit more flavor than your 24 hour Wawa, head over to MK. They're open until 3:30AM and you'll go to bed happy!

As a first time visitor to Philly, my sister had to take me to Reading Terminal Market because I'm a fan of these market/specialty shops places like Chelsea Market in New York City and the Ferry Building in San Francisco. This place is awesome. There is so much going on, and you can get so many types of food! They have Middle Eastern kabobs to Chinese to rubens and cheesesteaks. My sister and I had already gotten lunch, but she did suggest I try donuts from Beilers. I got a regular glazed one and a cinnamon sugar one. Yum, I inhaled them both within five minutes. No shame. They were awesome. I wish I got more to make me feel better about the Philly heat! Next time, I'm coming back here for a full meal and some grocery shopping! I eyed some really fresh seafood and meats and cold cuts.

The sign over the door reads "Reading Terminal Market".  However, as one perpetually fighting my waistline, it should read "Abandon hope, all ye who enter here".

Countless food vendors, all offering unique meals.  Roast pork, corned beef specials, kabobs, chicken, sausage...you name it, its all here.  I devoured a number of these infernal temptations and faced spiritual struggle as I realized that something so bad could be...so good.  There are also a number of dessert and pastry vendors, including the ninth level of the abyss, Termini Brothers.

You probably won't have Virgil with you on your descent into dieting hell, but once out there is salvation to be had in the Purgatorio of the gym.
Terrible food, terrible employees. Stay away unless you like getting sick. Would not recommend to anyone even if your in a rush.
An amazing experience from a to Z. I love this place. Always fun, great food, new experiences. Its a must.

Popped in when the line was short on a weekend in between grabbing a drink at a place nearby. This was the first time I've seen it open where they were still selling pizza, so I figured I had to try it while I could! Got the specialty pizza, coming with a slightly higher price but ingredients that made it all worth it. Amazing pizza crust (something I've not found much of in Philly) and really fun flavors.

This is a market and food hall in the heart of downtown Philadelphia. If you are in the neighborhood, be sure to come by and walk through the stalls and stop for breakfast, lunch, dinner and everything in between. Many of the stalls have diner-style seating or take away options. 

What I love about this place is coming early in the morning and seeing the locals eat here. Many of Philadelphia's finest officers begin their days here with a hearty breakfast. I also love that the restaurants have come up with creative ways to serve breakfast like a cheesesteak breakfast, an oyster scramble breakfast. Love, love, love!

I went to Molly Malloy's twice while visiting for breakfast. They have a wonderful avocado toast. Just when you think you had it with the boring same old avocado toast, Molly's will surprise you with their version topped with a fried egg over easy. The avocado is spiced wit pepper flakes and a dash of vinegar. Very very tasty and will keep you fulfilled for those long morning walks in the chilly weather. Service is great and attentive. 

I tried Pearl's oyster as well. Belly up to the diner and be greeted by the waitstaff. Did you say fried oysters for breakfast?  Yes, please!!! I had mine with egg white scramble. It was unusually delicious! 

Turnaround from Pearl's and you will see the Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. Get a cookie for the road. You will need it to top off this amazing experience!

It is really hard to not love Reading Terminal Market. It's a staple in Philly and definitely a place you should visit when you get the chance. My friend was visiting from out of town and she was overwhelmed by the entire place. The bright neon signs, people everywhere, and fantastic smells wafting into your nose are all part of what makes this place so unique. The place is a lot bigger than you would think which makes it all the more difficult to decide what you want. 

We couldn't decide what we wanted so we decided to do a lap around the place to see everything. As you weave through people you pass by coolers full of fresh meats, cheeses, basically anything you could think of. It's hard to not get distracted because everything looks so delicious. Once we made a lap we opted to stop for some Focaccia bread white pizza. I wish I remember the name of the place because it was delicious. Afterwards, we stopped by Beiler's donut which is one of the most popular stands in the whole place. The donuts are to die for and a must have!! (apple cider is amazing.)

Definitely stop by Reading Terminal if you get a chance while in the city because it really is amazing. Also, if you spend more than $10 at a shop, they will validate your parking ticket for the garage across and you only have to pay $5 for 2 hours!!
Stepping inside Reading Terminal is like stepping into another world. Its so cool, with such a variety of shops and restaurants, and everything is uniquely amazing. I cant get enough of this place!

Best Place to Visit in Philadelphia! So many vendors to explore and enjoy their offerings. Great for breakfast, brunch, lunch or happy hour! My favorite places are the Amish Market, Cookie Company and Gastropub for bites. Also, they do events on occasion so definitely check out their events calendar when you are in the area.

donuts, healthy foods, flowers, souvenirs, pretzels, every sandwich and food imaginable...they have it all!! and it's amazing how clean they keep it despite the traffic that goes through there every single day!! the praise goes to all the workers that work hard to keep it nice, clean and organized!   for the visitors it is a treat to come there and bring friends...for all the workers, it is hard work and we thank you!!

This place already has so many good reviews. Does it really need another one? Why yes of course, so I can add it to my list! 
Reading Terminal Market is one of my favorite places to visit when I'm in Philly. The market has a large selection of produce, meats, fresh flowers, seafood, fish and cheeses. I love the fresh Amish breads and jams that is sold here and it's a great place to have lunch. To really have a good experience, you need to come here on a weekday because it gets too crowded during the weekend.

Got moved to a different flight without much time to get food for a transcon flight. 

Ordered their caprese sandwich which was nice quantity and a good amount of quality mozzarella. Also very happy that the pesto sauce wasn't creamy/mayo-based.

Great stop if your traveling through Philly. I warn you be prepared for the hustle and bustke of the lunch hour and after work shop. Hut there are many jewels within the reading terminal market you can find everything from artisan wears from across the world to Amish pastries and Philly cheesesteaks.

If I had to pick one and only one place to take an out-of-town friend to experience Philly, it would be here. The Reading Terminal Market is a bustling indoor marketplace filled with an assortment of the best of what the city has to offer, from its Old City Coffee to Italian pastries and fluffy donuts to Amish breakfasts and cheap locally grown produce. 

It's a busy place so it can be easy to get disoriented. The whole place is laid out in a grid format, so when you enter, pause for a moment to get your bearings on what entrance you came from (or what the nearest shop is). Inside, hanging from the ceilings, you can see the signs for the different aisles/avenues, but they're not always visible. 

Tip: Bring cash! A lot of places take credit cards, but some places require cash only.

A Philadelphia staple that everyone must visit at least once. With that being said, I am a fairly devout foodie and still manage to get by without coming here very often. But every time I drop by, I'm pleasantly surprised by the selection, service, and art that is hand made food and fresh ingredients.

Have you been to Eataly in NYC? Have you been to Faniuel Hall in Boston? It has a very very similar vibe. Walking through the maze of the market is an experience itself, even if you don't stop to buy anything. It is a marvelous, glorious, hectic, loud, smelly, annoying experience. But it is so city and I loved it! It has hundreds of different food options, all classic Philly meals (donuts, pretzles and philly cheese steaks) as well as hundreds of other options. It is busy and crazy, but the food selection is like no other. THey also have a market, with hundreds of fruits/vegetables that looked so good! They had many butchers with meats and fish that also looked very fresh. This would be a great place to get fresh food if you live in this part o the city... or go to any of the hundreds of venues for pre-made food! I also loved that they had a corner of  "country store" type stuff with candles, jams, memorabilia, small candy stores.

It is genius, having it all together in the same building. Even if you aren't hungry, even if you don't like crowds or smells, it is a "tourist experience" to check this place out! It is magical, it is perfect... it is a necessity! 

I am OBSESSED!

I love this place there's so many different and unique shops, basically whatever your looking for you will find in here. My favorite was the one little flower shop because they had sunflowers which I couldn't find anywhere. I also got some cute jewelry from another little shop in there. I highly recommend going even if it's only once!

When my wife and I went to visit Philly we marked the Reading Terminal Market for a visit but didn't expect much since we thought this would be another version of a tourist distraction such as the South street seaport in New York, Fanueil Hall in Boston or Navy Pier in Chicago, etc...

Boy were we wrong and instead were treated to a really well run market with delicious food left and right and priced very reasonably.  You kind of realize that it's a serious market and not a tourist trap because there are tons of locals and even New Jerseyans from just across the bridge doing their everyday shopping.

There are great fresh baked goods, sandwich shops, seafood, butcher shops, restaurants, food stalls, artisans, dessert shops, wine stores and produce, etc.. A lot of the vendors there are Pennsylvania Dutch Quakers who also operate their shops in their traditional garb and really just produce excellent clean, fresh farm fresh food at great values.  Everything is affordably priced, fresh and delicious so you really can't go wrong.

La Lo.. YUMMMMM

I walked around the entire The Bourse looking for something vegetarian or vegan. Almost at the last stop I found La Lo. 

I ordered the Vegan Kare-Kare it is a 
peanut stew, smoked shiitake, grilled eggplant, green beans, & bok choy over garlic rice; this comfort will put you to sleep. So flavorful and you can tell this dish took some time to marinate.

I look forward to trying more items with hopes one day they will make veggie lumpia; if they did that I would probably be there everyday.

Love this place. Always look forward to getting their food. Food is always made at the perfect temperature and is always tasty. Only thing I can find wrong is the fact that it's probably unhealthy at times when it's that oily and tasty.

I love honey grow, but today I really wanted extra sauce on my stirfry and I paid an extra 50 cents (?? The charge seemed kinda dramatic for just an extra squirt of sauce) but when I brought it home im now seeing there's hardly any sauce on it.. less than I get when I don't pay the extra charge.... It might only be 50 cents but I still feel cheated and I'm very unsatisfied with my meal. $10 for an undersauced stirfry is gonna be a no from me. They didn't even cook the broccoli in the sauce. Dissapointed feel like I wasted my money

I visited this place in between a conference. I went to a cajun place and the food there was delicious!! Unfortunately, I totally forgot the name of it :( However, the market has sooo many options. It's a little overwhelming because of how many options there are, but if you have time and a few people, it's a great place to go through slowly and try/share multiple items. There were soo many desserts that looked amazing and my friend bought a box of 12 freshly made donuts and said they were delicious.

I travel to Philadelphia for work often and stay right in the downtown core. Being pretty busy and tired, Reading Terminal Market is a great spot for any meal or snack during the day. Super convenient, quick, full of variety and options and is reasonably priced. 

There is a fresh juice stand and they make me ginger and lemon shots for $1.50. Love it. 

The thing I love most about Reading Terminal Market is that my 73 year old father used to eat here with my grandfather when he was a kid. Makes me feel like the entire market is family.
A little overwhelming, a lot wonderful. Go on a weekday. Don't expect low prices, do expect extraordinarily food.

I've always enjoyed trips to Reading Terminal, since I was a little girl.  Before transitioning to a vegan diet, I would purchase rotisserie chicken from the Amish station along the north-most wall.  There is also a really tasty breakfast place inside and a cheesesteak spot I loved ( both run by Amish).  As you can see, I like the Amish :)... These days, I just order from the Mediterranean & Indian places. 

A lot of the shops are extremely cool as well! I usually visit the shops with homemade candles, natural health & beauty products, and African cultural items/accessories.  There is definitely something for everyone at Reading Terminal!

Good luck finding anywhere to sit in the main dining area, during lunch.  Also, parking down there throughout the day can be a major headache.  I'd suggest public transit or taxi service.

This place is amazing! There are so many different places you can grab some really great food at! It gets very crowded but if you are patient enough, you can usually always find a place to sit and enjoy your food. 
There is a great different variety and something for everyone!

Not only did my door dasher  have to wait over 30 mins but my food was super cold & full of cheese like really extra cheese it tasted weird. No one is going to feel comfortable ordering thru delivery if we receive our foods this way. We still pay extra of course for delivery and to receive food cold and not well done and late it sucks !!!!

I was looking for a quick take-out option nearby hotel and I found this place.
We ordered a bunch of Kati rolls, but none impressed us. I usually love Kati rolls and this was nothing like what we tasted before.
The only thing I liked getting from here is the Indian curry sauces in small cups. They are so cheap and are useful while staying with small kids.

One of my new favorite places to visit in Philly.  Good, cheap eats, more selection than Tyson's Corner Mall, but the quality is muchhhhhhh muchhhhhhh better.

I stopped by Dinic's for a roast pork sandwich (You can't miss this place because it has the longest line out of all the stores in the market)

Had a pretzel at Miller's Twist (very good)

Picked up a loaf of pumpkin bread from Beiler's Bakery (very good indeed).

Just walk around and be random.  Or do a quick Google/Yelp search through your smart phone to see if you can find something that peaks your interest.

Such a great spot, a must-visit when in the area. In the center of downtown, this underground-esque, culinary melting pot is full of bodegas, bakeries, delis, cafes, and much more. There's even a vegetarian cheesesteak. Will definitely return if I'm in Philly again, though I wish it was open later!
If you're looking for different stuff to eat or to shop for reading terminal is the place to go
Obsessed lol it was food heaven for me I was like a kid in a candy store lol can't wait to come back my friends are going to love all the food and dessert options

One of my favorite places to eat in Philadelphia. They have every & any type of food there so whatever you want they have! Getting a good parking spot is pretty hard but other than that it's one of the best spots in philly!

This place was packed when I went, I don't like crowed areas but why not give it a try, they had a lot of small restaurants, bakeries, groceries, and convinced stores u name it, we decided to try a philly cheesesteak because why not we are at philly and must give it a try. While my husband made the line I looked for seat u really have to wait for people to finish eating to be seated, if not you won find a sit, the Philly cheesesteak was delicious and mouth watering, there's other places to try but we really went with that. And left too crowed and I could not hold up a table while others are waiting, not very nice eat and leave. enjoy !

We went to this location today, ordered through drive thru. When we got home we realized we only got half order in one of our fries! This is so not acceptable! Not only that one of the sauce was half open. Seems like they just gave us someone's leftovers

We stumbled upon this place as we were walking down the streets of Philadelphia. Terminal Market is a true hidden gem! We were so impressed by the options and quality of food here! So much to see and pick from. We ended up trying a bit of everything from different vendors. I do have to say that the cookies were everything!! So glad to have found this place! Will be coming back next time I'm in town!

A food lovers paradise!  Walk around and take in the sights, sounds and smells.  There is something here to please every palate.  I've tried quite a few of the stands over the years and have never been the least bit disappointed.  Philadelphia is steeped in American history,  and if you're going to take in everything that the city has to offer, definitely try to make this market one of your stops.

A foodie's delight, for sure! I don't suppose there's ever a time when this market is not crowded. This was my second time and I had hoped it wouldn't be so crowded on a Tuesday afternoon but it was the week between Christmas and New Year's. I actually find this place a bit overwhelming, and I'm not sure if the fact that I'm a vegetarian and a fairly health-conscious person is a good thing or a bad thing. There are soooo many things to be tempted by. There's not a lot of vegetarian options but enough. There is actually a vegan "deli" but they were out of "mozzarella cheese" for the sandwich I wanted so I decided on a bowl of soup. Good, but like everything at this market, so overpriced. I also ate it standing up because trying to find a table is not easy.

pizza was tasteless full of grease, chicken alfredo pasta dish had no lid and was put into a small pizza box. the bread sticks were alright as well as the chocolate chip cookie pie but def not worth the 5.99 price. no way in hell would i do pizza hut again! 30 dollars wasted.
Amazing local city market. Best to go on weekdays, however, anytime but at lunch as it is very very popular.

I was overwhelmed with all the stores that were in here! But all was great! We tried Dinick's for their pork and broccoli sandwich - it was ok. Not the greatest, but it was juicy and the slight bitterness of the broccoli rah gave the sandwich a little more umph.
We also tried Salumeria, known for their hoagies. We got the Italian hoagie and I liked it a bit more than the pork/broccoli sandwich. Full of flavor and very filling.
Of course we had to get ice cream and Bassett's! Definitely a lot creamier than other ice cream we've tasted. Most definitely one of my favorites =)
I have to come here again to try all the other things in the market! So many things to do!

Do you have a full afternoon to do nothing? Are you hungry while doing that nothing? Whether you are with a group of friends or by yourself you could easily get lost for hours in the many treasures of Reading Terminal. There's so much to explore; food, produce, crafts, jewelry, cheese, chocolate, pastries. You want take out...or dine in? From Chinese to Dutch cuisine, they are ready to tap dance all over your taste buds(depending on where you go). Make sure you have nothing to do because you're only gonna kick yourself if you try coming on your cute little 30 minute lunch or right before something you need to be on time for...lol it's like a rabbit hole....you just keep falling to goodness. If you've never been be prepared for crowds and long lines. But the wait is worth. There's metered/street parking and the train, both regional and the MFL are across the street. So GO!! Discover for yourself. No sense in me telling you when you can experience this wonder for yourself!

You don't need to me to tell you that this place is great, but I can tell you my favorite spots from over the past 10+ years: DiNics, 4th Street Bakery, Thai (Salmon Curry - get their early), Gumbo-laya (combo at Beck$ but so good), Bellier's donuts and blueberry pancakes at the dinner; Sausage, egg and cheese roll-up at Millers. Can't really good wrong.
so many different cuisines! such a cool place to spend with your family on the weekends!

RUN! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN! this Chipotle is the worse thing that could happen to your Chipotle cravings and dreams. The place is filthy and the food is gross. I ordered a chicken bowl with brown rice, black beans, chicken, mild salsa, corn and lettuce. The chicken was so gross! It didn't taste right and it was mushy. The corn and salsa were bad, not as in taste but it went bad yet they were serving it. The utensils station was dirty and wet that I left without grabbing any. As for the food, I had a few bites and threw out my meal, not worth getting sick over it. Do yourself a favor and go elsewhere, this will taint you and make you never want chipotle again.

Excuse me for cursing, but one of the best goddamn chicken sandwiches ive ever eaten is one that I purchased here. The coating may not have been as crunchy as other KFC's but the chicken was still super tender and big!
For the price, the quality and variety of food is on point. The masala chicken kati rolls are so addicting. Highly recommend using the white sauce they sell as well!
Delicious fast food! We got the Chicken Kheema roll, the lamb roll, and the chicken korma rolls w rose and mango lassi - super tasty and friendly staff

Great variety of food and market options. I was in town for work and stopped here for most of my dinners. Bustling with people shopping and dining. Very cool spot. They do close at 6 and I found that even shortly after 5 some of the food stalls were already closed up. Just something to be aware of if you're planning to stop in for dinner.

Tried to call in a pick up order.  Hello? Hang up.  2nd attempt...hello? Hi I'm calling to see if you have some vegan options?  We have chicken and rice. OK that's not vegan.  After explaining to her what vegan was we decided on potato masala.  Pause...im sorry that's not vegan.  OK what is vegan?  Chicken and rice.  Are you f**ing kidding me? Beware vegans and vegetarians...They do not understand.

To be honest, this Wendy's is the most disgusting Wendy's ever. The people behind the counter are rude and disrespectful. They scream. They roll their eyes. They bang on the counter. They speak on the phone while taking orders. I REALLY DO NOT RECOMMEND YOU TO GO THERE AT ALL.

Went in with high expectations and were definitely met. Favorite pizza I've ever had. One slice is plenty! The crust was perfect and sauce was fresh. Tiny eating area with stand up room only. Would def go and highly recommend. 8.7 ;)

Staff and vibe are immaculate. Would like to thank Denise for making my mornings. 

Appreciate that they check on masking and ID people eating in the store for the vax cards.

Love you guys

This is one of my favorite places to eat.  It's a melting pot of culinary delights from every corner on the map. The Amish breakfast amongst their many other offerings is superbly fresh. This morning alone I hand fresh Apple cinnamon French toast, turkey bacon, and a freshly squeezed cup of Oj. There's no other place in Philadelphia that brings together so many delicacies under one roof. And that reason i give it five stars.
My girlfriend and I ate at becks Cajun cafe and Olympia gyro. Both delicious great service highly recommend.

The Industry is way overpriced for what it is.  I'd never been to Pennsport, so I never would have known about The Industry if it wasn't for Yelp.  The area is mostly residential and a street full of row homes.  My husband and I found street parking pretty easily in the middle of the street.  We headed over to the Industry and couldn't get anyone's attention when we walked in after standing there for five minutes, so we just found a couple of open seats at the bar instead.  

The cocktail menu is written on a chalkboard above the bar.  I ordered a tequila based cocktail.  It was tart from the citrus and similar to a margarita, minus the salt.   I can't recall the name, but that's probably because it wasn't a memorable drink. I thought maybe I just ordered wrong, so I ordered a cocktail with a peculiar name, "No balls, you won't", for my second drink. It was described as a strange combination of tequila, espresso, sherry, and hot peppers.   It tasted like creamy, boozy, espresso.  The heat from the pepper was very faint.  Nice creamy texture from the egg white, but I guess I was expecting a more interesting flavor from a cocktail with such a crazy name.  The cocktails were priced from $9 - $13.  The pricing seemed a little steep considering that there were no garnishes or amazing flavors, and the atmosphere in the bar was really casual.  I expect more when you're charging those kinds of prices.  The Industry is no Franklin Mortgage.  

As for the food, we ordered the cheese plate to snack on.  It wasn't bad, but again at $14, I guess I was expecting more.  I liked the idea of a cow's milk, a goat's milk, and a sheep's milk cheese combo.  Everything was ok, but nothing really stood out.  The sheep's milk cheese tasted exactly like one I'd bought at Trader Joe's the week before that I wasn't that impressed with.  The cows milk cheese was bland, and the goat's milk one wasn't my thing, but my husband liked it well enough.  The presentation was boring, and it came served with a spoonful of honey, jam, and a few slices of green apple.  The pieces of sliced baguette it came with were okay, but I like a crisper crust.  I could have made myself a much better cheese plate at home by randomly grabbing a couple blocks of cheese and a baguette from Whole Foods. 

The service here was fast once we were seated at the bar.  Overall, there are far better gastropubs in Philly and they don't come with this hefty of a price tag.

It's whackadoodle that I've never reviewed Reading Terminal Market, seeing as how it's one of those places I always encourage visitors to check out when they're in Philly. All kinds of yummy adventures await you inside those walls, the most awesome of which is Beiler's Whoopie Pie. Go early in the day because they sell out often - they're only $1 and are the closest approximation to earthly bliss I've ever experienced. 

Fresh produce, fish, meat, flowers, baked goods (make sure to stop by Flying Monkey Patisserie for some cupcakes to wash down your Whoopie Pie) and more...the choices are outrageous and there's something for everyone. I also love me some Delilah's for Southern food and the Amish food counter for some breakfast delights.  If you have the option of not visiting at lunchtime, I highly suggest you stay far away, as the experience just isn't the same when it's crowded; and trust me, the elbow to boob factor is crazy high during peak hours! If you've gotta be there between 11:30 and 1:30, might I suggest donning some full body armor?

Controversial: my anxiety does not do well here. It is cramped and insane. I go right when they open to avoid crowds. Personally it is not a good time for me. You can find amazing food and eat your weight in different types. The crowds, the slow pace of walking through it is too much for me.

Go early, grab food and leave.
Never go during peak hours or you will want to leave right away

I would like to preface this by expressing that I did not dine in here rather I saw this under a recommendation of philly pizza which I had shown my wife months back on yelp. I scrolled through many pictures and read reviews so I had to try it since pizza is my favorite food. However, I was highly disappointed. For the expensive $4.00 price tag for a plain slice of pizza, not only was the tomato sauce bland but the pizza was very much burned. A pie runs for about $24.00 so if you intend to test it out first I would recommend you buying a slice. I could not recommend this place to any one.

I just left this location. I pulled into the drive thru at 2:30 about 30 min before they close. When I stated my order to the girl on the incom she said they didn't have any fries. Or burgers. She went through a short list of what I could get. So after I decided on a value chicken sandwich. I pulled around to the window. I politely asked the girl if she could add on a drink for me. 

This is when things 
Took a turn for the worse. The girl said you people don't care about whether I have to get off of work. I get off at 3 AM and now you're ordering something else? I responded saying I didn't mean any disrespect I was just trying to add a soda to my order. She then began to go into a cussing rant about how she had three kids and told me what to do with myself.

I am so confused about this interaction. I was polite during the whole process; and for this girl in the drive-through to unleash Hateful tirade. Using I hate speech. This was unbelievable me and my friend were shocked and said To just cancel the food. Out of concern of our order being spat in. The manager came to the window and told me to 'drive the f-ck on f-gg-t'. I wouldn't believe this if it didn't happen to me. I wish I had time to get on my phone to record the interaction because not only did I apologize for inconveniencing her by adding a soda on at the window but I apologize for her stressful night. 

Whoever the manager was and this employee That worked October 28 at 2:30 AM was a disgrace to this company.

If I ever move to Philadelphia, I would buy a place near the Reading Terminal Market and never cook again.  I would also die early from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

Now, I haven't been to a lot of public markets like this, and more memorable ones for me have bee in Australia (such as the night market in Cairns and the Queen Victoria Market in Melbourne).  Some of the domestic ones, like Quincy Market and Boston Market, seems very touristy.  To be certain, Reading Terminal attracts its fair share of out-of-towners like us, but unlike Quincy Market there's still a sense that it's a place where locals come.  Maybe I'm wrong about that, but as compared to our subsequent experience in Boston just a week later, Reading Terminal was far less crowded, though still bustling with activity.

There are so many good things to eat here, and I wish I could remember all of the places we visited to get little bites here and there.  Cannoli, poutine, a big ol' freshly baked biscuit with jam, fresh fruit from the grocer, a pastry called a pig ear, and much more - all of it was good.  I wish we had more time to eat our way through the entire market.  There's so much variety, and overall prices were quite reasonable, at least when it comes to the little snacks that we were picking up at every other stall.

I just did a Google search for the best public markets in the US and this place consistently ranks at the top of any list.  Definitely a must-visit place in Philadelphia, and a lot of more interesting than lining up to look at the Liberty Bell.
4 stars cause tables are not clean and not a lot of tables in side, but there's a lot out side. In the weather

We were traveling and are big fans of Indian food and stumbled upon this place. Amazingly delicious! Inexpensive Indian street food with incredible flavors and cheap prices. I wish they were located in my city! It will be our go to place whenever we are in Philly.

I love this place!  It has a little bit of everything!  We walked around to see what it offers and it was a lot!!!  They even have a Filipino Restaurant called "Tambayan" (a place to hangout)!  We ate at Molly Malloy's for lunch. Chris and I both had the loaded Philly Cheesesteak which was phenomenal!  It was so good that I couldn't risk eating another Philly Cheesesteak while in PA for fear that it might not be better if not as good.  For dessert, I had to have ice cream from Bassett's - Butter Pecan, of course. It was heaven on a cone!
Food was good but seems overpriced compared to other similar places. Shorted me grilled nuggets. Does this look like 8 pieces to you? Nope
I got the Filipino sausage with lumpia and it was soooo good! It's great to see more diversity in old city! The Bourse is a great spot to try a bunch of different foods.

This place is so awesome! There are so many choices for food; including ready to eat and markets to pick up for home. It's great that everything is indoors and together under one building so you can experience all the flavors at once. Will definitely return! Loved it!
AWESOME! Literally anything you would ever want is at Reading Terminal. Stop what you're doing and go. Right meow.

Amazing food scene. Nothing like this in any other American city. Also, the vegetables are so cheap and organic too. It's a good place in a good part of town. 

Great place to get flowers, and cheese and pretty much anything a house-hold needs.

Reading Terminal is a smorgasbord of wonderful food stalls and eateries all compiled into one glorious Mecca. Beck's Cajun Cafe, Old City Coffee, Kevin Parker's Soul Food Cafe, and Beiler's donuts are just a few of the must visit spots inside. It's a must see if you're just touring around the City of Brotherly Love, and a great weekend shopping stop for locals.

This is a must see for visitors of Philadelphia.  It's like a MALL full of the cities BEST food's or shop for your own family.  Very poplar amongst locals,  good food, good people,  good place to visit and shop !

I ordered delivery from the Chipotle app. It was missing multiple items. I called Chipotle and the said that it wasn't their fault. They blamed DoorDash and said the driver must have taken it. I asked for the phone number for DoorDash. They gave me the number for Blue Cross Blue Shield.

The hustle and bustle here is definitely something you have to get used to but when you do you'll be in love.. There's food everywhere, sweets, fresh meat, fresh fruits and veggies, coffee beans, even aromatherapy shops. It's the perfect place to grab lunch and walk around to all the booths and meet some amazing people
A true and timeless classic. Absolutely love this place and all of the vendors. It does get crowded and there doesn't seem to be much social distancing in affect.

Reading Terminal Market is a hustling and bustling lively food hall with a large variety of food vendors, shops, and places to get groceries (produce, meat, whatever you can think of, you can probably find it here). Even if you come with a group of people, you'll be able to easily find something to suit everyone's needs. If you've never been before, I'd highly recommend visiting even if it's just to walk through. There are so many delicious-looking treats that I'd find it incredibly hard to leave without grabbing a single bite to eat!
Visiting Philly? A must-see on your tour list!
They make some interesting sandwiches, it was okay I would probably go there again.

This is heaven for any foodie.  Sandwiches, bakery,  coffee, spices, fresh meat and vegetables, seafood.  Whatever you crave is there.  When you enter, you will be overwhelmed by the wonderful aromas.

It became a must for us on our trip to philly that we went to reading terminal market and tried s cheese steak. Well it was such a great experience to go there, the food is amazing and the options are endless! The whole experience of the market itself is not one I'd seen and it was worth the trip outside of New York.
Plenty of options and great food. Sunday's are less packed but also have less vendors. Good location for tourist and local Philadelphians!

Really good pizza and tomato pie. Tiny corner joint with two standing tables to eat inside. We had 4 slices: plain, pepperoni (love the 'roni!), tomato pie, and the special. I liked the red pizzas more than the special, but it was still good. Crust is thin and crispy-- cooked through and not " floppy. " Served piping hot. We were here on an early Sunday afternoon, and didn't have to wait more than a couple minutes.

a crowded gem, local color, great food, crazy non-food items.
One of the places that makes Philly Philly. Don't miss Denic"s pork & provelone sandwich

Over and over again I try to order food to be delivered from them. And over and over my order is canceled an hour later for reasons like " restaurant has run out of an item you ordered" or "Restaurant has stopped taking orders". I have complained to the delivery service, Grubhub but they say it's the restaurant so here's my bad review for them.

Love this place! Super packed on Saturday's though. On sundays not everything is open though. Best to come on a weekday. So many varieties of foods and drinks and desserts. The Amish donuts are bomb. Great butcher shops and fish markets. Even a great produce market in the very back. Lots to see and try and enjoy.

I love the terminal. It's old school, crowded, and wonderful. So many types of stalls, stands,  restaurants and bakeries. My favorites are the Cajun restaurant, the mushroom stand, and the butchers. It's a wonder and I've never been unhappy. Don't even get me started on the baked goods or pickles.

So many good places to eat. DeNic's roast pork is my favorite but the lines can be crazy long around lunch time. The farmer's Markets are cool for fresh local produce. the Amish place is awesome for breakfast, they give you like a pound of butter. I wish the whole place was open later.

Cheap good eats here! I ordered the Chicken Masala Roll and Chicken Kheema Roll and both were delicious. Both rolls were spicy but the Kheema roll was spicier. I liked the Kheema roll more because it was ground chicken rather than cubed chicken pieces like in the Masala roll. The Indian spices were more well-distributed with the ground chicken so each bite was perfectly flavorful! Highly recommend coming here when you are craving Indian fast food. Workers were friendly and food was ready immediately.

Great in every way. Any produce, poultry, meats, sweets, meals and more there. I just got delicious BBQ wings there, it's at the same place they sell pierogies. I also get my cookies there..4th St Cookie Co. There is even a convenience store in the middle I can get milk for my cookies.
Very nice place to Visit. There are many nice shops here. We especially like the Amish market.

I'm fond of Chick-fil-A's customer experience more than -- sometimes the meal. It's disappointing when I frequent at this particular location and the employees do not want or choose to say their signature "my pleasure". I genuinely say thank you -- I would even appreciate "you're welcome". It's like the employees refuse to say it.

Of course, the food is good here.  This particular location makes it a bit disappointing because of the customers' experience. #ijs

There is something for anyone here. I had the pork sandwich at Dinics and w
It was amazing. Last time I was here I didn't enjoy because of the company but this time I had a blast. Bassett icecream is delicious and ..........  I can just keep on and on.

Who doesn't love this place? Such a huge building with plenty of food and shopping choices; perhaps too many choices? Here, You can get literally every type of cuisine you could possibly imagine. And it's all good! 
I've only been here a few times recently when in town and it's usually a cheesesteak, but last time it was Hershel's for corned beef and pastrami. (Separate
Review coming later). 
Parking can be a problem near here if driving, so finding a meter or affordable garage is difficult at lunchtime. We were lucky to find a mater spot after circling the block a few times. 
No indoor dining with Covid restrictions in place, but hopefully it'll get back to normal soon. 
If you've never been here, you must visit and enjoy the overwhelming vastness of the building and the plethora of cuisines. Definitely a must-visit while in Philly.

I can see why they got two stars and I know oh so well . I ordered through YELP and some how it directed me to this one after my order I was trying to get the one on Roosevelt. Why ...... because this one is NASTY . However I received my food and it was wrong I do not and cannot eat this I tried to call but guess what no one's answering.. I let it ring continuously and nothing they screw  your food up and probably know it and then don't even answer the phone to take responsibility. Don't go here please I'm gonna stay away from chipotle altogether after this crap.
Wonderful, i am a vegeterian, like the paneer rolls kati!! always like it..recommend to give some salad on side?! thanks

Rating: 3.5/5.

Food network's advertisements of "Tommy Dinic's" brought me there. The roasted pork broccoli sandwich was more tender and enjoyable than the beef brisket one. 

The highlight of the crowded and touristic Reading terminal market was the honey sampling at "Bee natural". Their raw honey was so delicious and came in so many unusual and interesting flavors! I ended buying a big container, which lasted me years.

The market had a miniature train track, which was a hit with children.

While it was a fine place to get your steps in, nothing was outstanding. I may have been spoiled by places such as the Boston Public Market or Eataly. Those luxuous markets offered more samples and surprising products.

If I were to have lunch there again, I would try the Carmen's shop selling cheese steack sandwiches.

I never want to leave this place. I visited it twice in two days. With tons of stores, markets, places to eat, souvenirs for days, and clean bathrooms, what more do you need. There's not many places to sit, but who cares?! 

Philly Cheesesteak-I went to Carmen's, it was okay, but next time I'll try somewhere better

First Ice cream shop in America, Basset's--a must go!

Don't be overwhelmed by the crowds, you'll get through it. Just enjoy it and have fun.

My wife and I visited Philly over the weekend and had a blast.  The one place we absolutely had to go to was the Reading Terminal Market.  We told our friends who we were visiting to take us there and give us the tour.  My friend is a mega foodie, so he knows exactly what to eat and when to go.  He made sure he told us it closed at 4pm, so that when I was inevitably running behind, he admitted it was actually closed at 6PM on Saturday...

There are a lot of people in this market, but its not so much where you cant comfortably move around.  There is action on every corner.  From restaurants, to bakeries, to candy stores...they have it all!  We made sure we had a delicious sandwich and we also had some famous donuts from a bakery who's line wrapped around multiple stores.

The only couple of things that bothered me, which are the reasons its not a 5 star is the prices are very high and it can be a battle to find a seat.  If you go alone or with another person your okay.  If you go as a group of 4, you may find it challenging.

I highly recommend coming here to anyone who goes to Philly!

I always saw this place on the travel channel and dreamed of going. I wish I lived in Philly mainly for this freaking market. I wish they had markets this great in LA (if they do PLEASE let me know)

Pros:
-SO MANY EATERIES. You could come here everyday for a month straight and try something new.
-Every place has decent pricing.
-The workers are all friendly

Cons:
-I guess the only thing I can point out is paying for parking. But it's only $4 if you park across the street and get it validated.

I love this place, and it's a definite go to if you visit Philly.

So many choices! Dinics, Hershel's, and Miller's Twist are among my regular go to's. Oh and Beilers! The best donuts known to man. Can never go wrong at Reading Terminal Market. Love the way they've added tables outside for eating. When we visited last the inside dining was all closed but I think it's opened now. We just ate outside and it was great. Pre pandemic, the market was always very busy!

I'd feel ridiculous for giving Reading Terminal Market less than five stars, considering the sheer variety and affordability of food offered here. Seafood, Cajun dishes, barbecue chicken, burgers, gyros, roast pork sandwiches, cheesesteaks, doughnuts and other Amish baked goods... you really can have it all.

Yes, weekend lines equal pandemonium. All the people there are clamoring for the same delicious eats all packed into one place, same as you. It gets especially crazy when there's an event happening at the Convention Center across the street. I'd try to go off-hours or visit on a weekday if possible. But otherwise, try braving the lines. Many of them actually go very quickly, especially Beiler's, and a lot of the restaurants are counter service places so there's a lot of in-and-out flow.

Wonderful place to experience all different purveyors of Philly and local areas around! It's crowded with tourists especially on the weekends but as a local who lives in the neighborhood I know when to go when when to avoid crowds (lunchtime for example)
There is something for everyone here and so long as you have a bit of patience you can make the most of this place. I will say that if you're from out of town give yourself plenty of time to explore and come with an empty stomach because there's a lot to enjoy!
This is on of our favorite places! We love the donuts , Hatfield deli and millers pretzels! Come hungry!

One of the places you must stop by when in Philly! I'd recommend this place for all of your brunch/lunch needs. There are so many choices in here and everyone is bound to find something to their liking.

Lines can be sort of long, but they move pretty fast!
Love Reading Terminal, to bad I no longer live down town, i would go several times a week.

This was my first time here and I had no idea what a Kati Roll was. Thankfully, they explain what it is on the back of their menu and also have a poster hung up in the restaurant explaining the layers of food and how it's made. It's basically like Indian fast-food!

This place is small, but conveniently located right on 12th and Walnut. They're open super late, until 3:30am most days, so great to stop by if you're out having a late night. 

I was impressed with how decently priced everything was. One Kati Roll is about $5.25 or so. I wasn't sure what the portion sizes would be like, so I ordered one Kati Roll and found it to be enough. My friend ordered two and she had some leftover to take home. 

I'm only giving them 4 stars because the service was not the greatest. They seemed scattered and disorganized and people were waiting in line for longer than necessary - and there were only a few people in there at the time! 

Overall, I liked the quality of the food and would come back in the future.

BEST biscuits and cole slaw ever of any fast food franchise i can make a meal just with large Cole slaw and 4 bsicuits 

it's an old KFC been there forever but if your smart get there 10 mins before closing and you get ooddells of chicken for $10 because they have to throw away whats left over by law.

This place is amazing. Looks small and unassuming from outside but inside is a whole mini village of shops and tiny restaurant counters. Shops have chocolates, pastry, meats, produce, alcohol, groceries and gifts. The restaurants represent almost every style of cooking you could be craving, Dutch, Soul, Diner, Gyros, Oyster Bar, Italian, cookies and smoothies and many more.

Really cool place to visit they have all kinds of food from breakfast, lunch . Anything you looking for . Sweets , chocolates.. u name it ... the also have a meat , fish market $ fresh produce. I tried the phillysteak

Fun place to shop and eat! Stumbled upon this place while walking around and wanted to get a quick bite. Unfortunately, it was difficult to walk around with my kid because he was so distracted with all the food and things for sale. A lot of vendors to shop and choose from. In some places, the line was really long. It was hard to choose where to eat because everything looked amazing!

As a law, when someone in Philadelphia is introducing themselves they have to say, "hi. my name is ____ and I live in Philadelphia - home of Reading Terminal Market". 
That should be a law. I come to Philadelphia fairly often for work (I'm a pro baseball player) and why is it that I'm just learning about this place. It's dizzyingly large. 
Crêpes
Cheese
Salami
Lox on a bialy 
Creole
Chocolates
Espresso 
Coffee
Oysters 
Coffee
Espresso
Pastrami
Peking duck
Baked goods
Produce
Seafood

God bless you.

A word of caution if you are thinking of getting lunch here... this place is popular and crowded at those hours! That said, the Reading Terminal Market is a must-visit if you are in Philadelphia. I have tried different food from a number of the restaurants within the Market, and have almost always had a positive experience. In general, I would recommend that you do some research and get your food to go, especially if you are in the area for a conference and are staying nearby. I recommend the croissants at Market Bakery, Beiler's donuts, and a visit to Mueller's chocolate store. The Market is also a good place to get groceries. Farmers from around the area have stores here and often sell good produce for good prices. You can also find all sorts of meats. Sit-down dining is also available.

Went tonight after hearing from everyone how great it is. The pizza was good but the staff was a joke. Rude and incompetent. They have no clue how to run a pizza shop. Do yourself a favor and take a drive up the road for circles and squares- better pizza and better staff

Similar to other line up and pile protein and toppers on a starch, but with a Mediterranean twist. Most folks take out - the line moves fast - so you can get back to class or a busy work schedule. But there are also some seats if you want to eat in. One communal table for 8, and a number of single counter seats around the place. 

The food - I got the Chicken Schwarma which Was good. There was also a grilled chicken that looked great. Others  in my group had the Cauliflower and the Falafel. Everyone was happy with their choice. 

Lots of interesting additions, and there is no limit!  There is Baba Ganoush, Hummus, Kalamata Olives, pickles, lettuce, tomatoes,  feta, yogurt, etc.  

Portions are big - several of us will be eating our leftovers for lunch tomorrow!

The Reading Terminal Market is by far my favorite place to go.  Yes, it get's busy....very busy with tourist that don't understand our "keep on moving" attitude.  There are almost always line at every vendor stall.  But I can't think of many places with a better cross section of not only locals but tourists.  

Start on the outside and you'll undoubtedly see some entertainment, some that is from a performer and some that is from just a normal person that keeps this city colorful!  The second you step inside your senses are immediately inundated with beautiful smells, sights of almost every type of food/cuisine imaginable and the sound of commerce and excitement.  

Some of my favorites are DiNic's, get a pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and provolone.  Swing by Martin's Sausages and grab some of the best chorizo I've ever had (my wife loves the chicken sausages).  Molly Malloy's is always available if you need some libation to take the edge off. 

No matter where you go you will love it!

Library of Congress ID description: An ode to this particularly compelling Chick-Fil-A location, in verse.

Deep in the wilds of Delaware Ave.
exists a closed-on-Sunday Valhalla of chicken you must grab.

Strips or sandwich, waffle fries and diet lemonade! 
You'll marvel at the low low price you just paid.

Only plump breasts will this corporation provide, 
along with two pickle slices your fluffy bun does hide. 

The coup de grace of this clucker franchise
are the workers whom to every occasion do rise.

With smiles and grace, they feed strangers like friends,
justifying every dollar their hungry customer spends.

We love the Reading Terminal Market! Tons of different food and store options. We have brought visiting family here as well and they loved it! It is such a cool thing to have offered to us right in the city of Philadelphia. Too many places to list but def. go check out the Reading Terminal Market and give yourself a few hours and some patience. Some of the Philly City Food Tours also give tours of the market which is pretty cool! Cheers!

What a fun place!! I wish we had something like this in ATL. Wasn't as expensive as I thought/had much more than the eye can see on the outside. Ponce City Market (something as close to this in ATL) should take notes. 

Inside there are restaurants where you can eat via bar space (utilized pretty well for space), buy produce, and buy random items. The restaurants are very diverse. We ate here once a day during our trip. The price tag to eat here is affordable. I really thought it'd be much more expensive since it's in the DT area. Awesome place to come for any reason: wanting a snack, a meal, coffee, desert, quick bite to eat, etc. Honestly think you can come here for everything, haha. If I was a permanent Philly gal, I'd come here daily or probably every weekend. 

Seating wise - not as bad as I thought. Space is available around the market AND some restaurants have bar areas to eat, so that helps with the craziness. 

But beware: if you come at rush time - you may have to wait some time to eat. There was a popular Philly Cheesesteak place that had a line at least 10-15 people deep during lunch. 

I high recommend people to come here... especially folks from out of town.

I can never get in line for the donuts at this place because this is my third time here and the line was beyond crazy! Are those donuts that good?!

We came here on a Saturday afternoon and as we were walking in through the entrance where the donut shop is the place was packed! Packed like sardines in a can! I don't really buy much when I come here because it seems like there's always a line. There are so many vendors so it's a good place to visit if you don't mind the crowd and the wait.

Awesome service ! Awesome happy hour with buck a shuck oysters *drools* and their fried mac and cheese croquettes were amazing!!!! My gym and hike workout for four hours totally went out the window after having one of these, I HAD to order a second one. So yummy.

My best advice that I could give anyone visiting the Reading Terminal Market would be to get there as early as possible, if not when the door are opening in order to truly be able to enjoy your experience here without feeling like a sardine in a can. 

I would say this is a must stop for anyone traveling to Philly and looking for some great food. There are so many pallet pleasing experiences here that even the pickiest eaters will be absolutely satisfied. 

I saw everything from freshly stuffed donuts, smoothie bars, crispy whole fried ducks (heads on), falafel stands, deli counters, grilled cheese storefronts, roast pork sandwiches, seafood stands, Mexican taco counter, chocolates and cakes made in every flavor imaginable you name it chances are the most likely have it. They also have an array of so many different ingredient stands from spices to meat and seafood stands they literally have everything.

My only complaint about the Reading Terminal Market is how cramped it gets in here so quickly and is almost chaotic not to mention the lack of seating to accommodate the hungry customer who I saw leaning over garbage cans at time for a surface to lean on and scarf down their food. They could use some more staff here in order to keep the eating areas tidy for the customers. I found myself wiping down my own table due to it being dirty from the previous people eating.

If you have never been to Reading Terminal Market, you have never really been to Philadelphia.
This is a must see.
This is a "must" for anyone visiting Philly!! It's filled with a variety of food & treats & some unique shops.

Overwhelming because there are so many options, but there is definitely something for everybody. Fun stalls and just a lively place to walk through even with COVID (though can get a little crowded which feels a bit strange). Had a really delicious smoothie here and had fun walking around. Can see why this is a recommended touristy place by city center.

So many good eats in one place!

It's super packed in here on weekends. There is a parking lot nearby the market. You can get your parking ticket validated for a discounted price if you eat somewhere inside the Reading Terminal. 

There are so many food options in here, so come hungry. They sell fresh fish, fruits, veggies, baked goods, meats, flowers, etc. Employees around the market are so friendly and helpful. Restrooms are in the back and clean. There is a lot of seating around the market but they all get taken during weekends. I'm sure if you come here on a weekday, you will have an easier time finding a seat. There is just so much to see in here, we had to walk around a bunch of times to make sure we didn't miss anything. Everywhere you look there is something yummy calling your name. 

A food lovers paradise.
Getting so touristy that it's difficult to function when walking through this place. Philly needs a food court for locals.

If dumplings are what you want then DUMPLINGS are what you're gonna get. They have some salad & sandwich options, but the stars of the show are obviously the dumplings. 

My roommate and I stopped by to get takeout as we were passing by one day. I got the Asian pork dumplings steamed, YUM. They're not very big and I inhaled them (not sure I even actually chewed them). There was no one else in the restaurant at the time so our order was done super quickly. 

If you're driving be prepared, parking is very limited. I jumped out and my roommate circled the block while I got our food. That area of South Philly can be challenging for parking.

Came in from out of town for a trade show. Found this little gem not more than five minutes from the BnB we were staying in. Walked in and my foodie heart melted. So far I've tried Ma's chicken and waffles, Hersal's deli, and one of the bakeries (I'll get the name and come back to edit this). All of it was amazing. You won't be disappointed!

This place has A little something for everyone. My fav places were : 

Amish markets, homemade hot jerky sticks, homemade chips, fresh jams... 

farm fresh meats, thick bacon, stuff pork chops, huge turkey wings

Philly cheese steaks@spataros

Amazing place for grocery shopping, a quick snack, or an interesting way to kill 20 minutes walking around or people watching. Every conceivable type of food, often farm fresh and prepared in front of you. For a tourist, definitely a stop you should make. This one helped rename "Market Street" in honor of the open air markets that crowded it, and Reading Terminal opened as a closed air market in the mid 19th century. Cool place. The Penn. Dutch usually aren't there every day, so don't be surprised.
I love this place. Lots of specialty stuff in the terminal. If you like cookies checkout Famous 4th Street Cookies.

Amazing spot to get a meal with a group of divergent eaters because I'm pretty sure they actually have every style of food here. I had Thai, Indian, Mexican and seafood on varying days during my week long conference stay. Prices are super reasonable. I would recommend going to at kindergarten lunch time or senior special dinner times because it gets absolutely packed at peak hours and it would be tough to navigate if you don't know where you're headed.

I hate to admit that I only just discovered the joy that is Reading Terminal within the last year, and on one hand I feel like I've missed out big time, on the other, my grad school wallet is grateful... 
There is SO much here, every time I stop in for lunch I end up leaving with something else as well from the to die for candy from the Amish stands (which also make good presents) to some fun infused oil, to fresh produce or cheese... You can't go wrong wondering around the Market filling your bags. 
The food itself is with out question a highlight of the city. My favorites include the obvious famous DiNic's, a the chicken cutlet sandwich, any of the cheesesteak places, Bassets Ice Cream, OK so EVERYTHING is good, and the Market is a Philly MUST. Just come, walk around, make your choices and enjoy!
The best of Philly in one place? Yes please! Within walking distance of many downtown Philadelphia attractions. A 'don't miss' when visiting.
Just the best. Great options. Great people. A true gem and working so hard to ensure safety in these tough times

This is the worst chick-fil-a I have ever been to. First off, there's only one line for the drive through. Second, the wait took for ever to go through it. And lastly, this was the first time I ever got a chick-fil-a sandwich where it was warm instead of hot. How disappointing.

This place has ranked high on my East Coast foodie bucket list. I wish I could have had time to try every vendor in there, but I was only in town for a short weekend, and you can only eat so much in the span of 48 hrs. 

We arrived at about 10:30 on a Sunday. Traffic wasn't bad at all and it was pretty easy to locate the parking lot, directly across from the market. Bring your ticket with you for validation from a market vendor. Parking is normally $29 for 2 hours, but if you spend $10, you can have your parking validated and it will only be $4 for 2 hours. Very reasonable.

I forgot the Amish area of the market was closed on Sunday's, they are only open Tuesday - Saturday. Shame we missed those shops, I hear they have some very yummy stuff. Oh well.

We made a couple rounds through the market, trying to decided what we wanted.

We first got a cheesesteak with whiz from Spataros. Not bad but not my favorite cheesesteak in the city. Pass.

We wanted to try Wursthaus Schmitz but they weren't open quite yet.

We got two cannolis from Termini Bros, very yummy!

And then tried the Ave. D from Milkcraft Grilled cheese. You can add bacon, tomatoes or have the sandwich grilled in duck fat. We chose the last option. It was dripping in grease, so I don't know if I would have gone with the duck fat, but it was still so decadent and amazing. Honestly I would go back for Milkcraft alone. Amazing stuff. 

I was worried we were going over our two hour parking window, but we got back to hour car with 30 mins to spare. 

Very cool place, highly recommend coming here. Just wish I had had more time to try everything!

We stayed in the hotel across the street and this was a very exciting surprise. We knew the city market was here, but we were still overwhelmed by the size and diversity of it. It had so many different things to eat and try -not as many places to sit.

We went at lunch time so the place was a buzz with life. We stopped by again later for dessert. Love this place. If you want to experience the culmination of a city, the city market is the place to go and Philly does it right.

Oh my, this is heaven on earth right here, I dont know if words can even describe. You to experience everything here personally, especially beck's Cajun, the gator gumbo is to die for. I'm starving for this place writing this oh my.
Very interesting vibes inside here, it's not very spacious and if you have a weak stomach don't recommend. I had a corn dog that was good.

I'm honored to be the Duke of Masala! I can honestly say every visit I'm 100% satisfied my partner and I eat here often and I always order the Chicken and rice platter which is layered on a bed of rice , lettuce, chicken , accompanied by pita (flat bread). Delicious food and open until 3am !

Interesting market that seems like a tourist-trap feat. the requisite higher than normal  prices - but that doesn't mean the food isn't still good! I've come back multiple times and each vendor I've visited has been a positive experience.
Excellent food, and at a reasonable price.  I love their achari paneer -- full of flavors, with generous amounts of paneer.  Their Rose Lassi is really good too.

I live nearby and have purchased flowers, caulk, paint,etc. They are always helpful and they sell mostly everything.
Recently I bought a replacement screen for my patio door and had  no way of getting it home. Tony offered to follow me home with the screen  in his van then as if that were not enough he volunteered to carry it upstairs to my deck!
This is hometown service!  I feel grateful to live close to this store!

Judy C

I love Reading Terminal Market. It has something for everyone and is a culinary delight. My only drawback is mostnof the items are over priced but that's to be expected in center city. I also don't like that police officers take up most of the parking around the buildings so it could be problematic on a busy day. However if you are new to Philly the Reading Terminal will be a good philly gem to visit and hang out with locals from all walks.

I swear the ppl who work here need to get retained! Most ignorant and miserable staff ever! They act like I was bothering them when I asked for the KFC sauce! I really don't know how this place stays open!???

I know why you are reading this section, you want to answer the foodie question to eat here or not to eat here. In short, yes, but keep this in mind:

DECOR:
Plaza/ food court style. Most places have their own energy and vibe some have seating. The main area for sitting is pretty spacious, and gets full pretty quickly so send a scout ahead of you eating or be prepared to have a mobile meal.

FOOD: 
The food is amazing at several vendors in this Market, but my fav all time food to grab is Beilers the doughnuts are melt in your mouth good, they are freshly made right in front of you annnnnnd you can grab on in a batch that you see being made.

WAITSTAFF: 
There really isn't much in the way of waitstaff. There is a team that prepares the various foods and then those that are selling it to you. I haven't had more than a diner experience to yo, but it is expected so I just roll with it.  

WHAT TO WEAR:
The crowd is pretty diverse and so are the clothing choices, or not. I have seen suits or blatant tourist gear in here. So I would say anything goes here.

CROWD: 
The crowd is massive from all walks of life it's like New York only indoors and less the constant yet surprising whiffs of pee every so often.

*TIPS*:
I would recommend that you not  drive to this location there really isn't a really viable place to park. Unless you want to park in a parking garage.

If you ever end up in Philly, you can't NOT check this place out!

It's a huge indoor market - they sell everything from candles, linens, & numerous gift items, to donuts, fresh cannollis, beef jerky, pizza, and pretty much any type of food you can think of or imagine!

The place is clean, cool looking, and if I lived in this area, I would be here oh-so-regularly.  You won't ever starve or run out of choices!

Some of the vendors there are:  

12th Street Cantina
Beck's Cajun Cafe
By George! Pizza, Pasta & Cheesesteaks
Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagies & Cheesesteaks
Dienner's Bar-B-Q Chicken
DiNic's
Down Home Diner
Dutch Eating Place
Franks A Lot
Golden Bowl
Hatville Deli
Hershel's East Side Deli
Hunger Burger
Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties
Keven Parker's Soul Food Cafe
Little Thai Market

That list isn't even half of what is there!

Our only fault was that we came at an odd brunch time, and already made reservations to eat lunch elsewhere, so we ended up getting beef jerky and donuts to go (& ate a couple of them while we were there.) If we didn't already have plans, we would have definitely tried Dinic's - "Home of the famous roast pork and broccoli rabe sandwich, crowned the best sandwich in America by the Travel Channel." Their line was crazy long each time we walked by, so you know they sell some GOOD stuff! 

I already know that we will definitely return the next time we're in town. Don't miss out; this place is foodie heaven!
Classic! Doesn't matter what you get! It's always awesome! So much to choose from. Good luck making a decision! Guarantee you'll be back! Only knock is parking.

I loooove love love Reading Terminal 
Literally that is all, except certain times are busier so be mindful! Enjoy
Been here on occasion.. Pizza is good.. Slices are overpriced, simply because ther crust is so big. Seems like half the slice was dough.. Guess Location is Important
This place is a food lovers paradise. I am going to make a trip to Philly once again just to eat here and i'm not kidding :)

The best spot in the Bourse in my opinion! The lumpia is fantastic, probably the best I've ever had. I also tried the long si log which was delicious as well. As other reviews have mentioned, it's quite pricey for the portion size, but as someone who doesn't eat a lot of Filipino food, it was definitely a treat here!

Damn. Not an option to try. Few things management should consider. First is aloo kathi roll is literally aloo curry and roti where are flavors of chutney??? Second, I tried kala khatta and it's bull$hit please remove it from the menu.

If heaven existed on Earth, it would be inside this building. The market is my absolute first stop to go to every time I come into Philly. It's where I want to be buried when I finally have to kick the bucket. 
     Hours and hours of my day can be spent here tasting all the delicious meats, pastries, cheeses, sandwiches, and beers.  My favorite sandwich EVER is inside this market. I wish they could pick up and move to Atlanta. I would be here every single weekend if I could. 
      Do yourself a favor, if you are a foodie and visiting or local, go here. It gets packed on the weekends, so if you can make it in here during the weekday, shoot for that. Was in there by 8:30am this morning and had a fantastic Amish breakfast. 

5 stars isn't enough, where are 10 when you want to give them?

This is the worst KFC that I've ever been to. They are rude and ignorant, the drive thru was unavailable.  When the lady over the loud speaker informed me of that she was very rude and disrespectful.  I came in to order my food, she greeted me with rolling her eyes and sucking her teeth.  Hire new help

If you love to eat, you will love it here. Come hungry, but not hangry. You could probably spend days here and still not finish all the stuff that you want to try. 

The best strategy is to come as a team. These are the roles of each teammate. Without them, you will not have the best experience that you possibly can have:

1. The hunter of seats - must be strong and able to hold their ground. You may have multiple members on this team. Their main lines are, "You can't sit with us" or "Sorry, this seat is taken, and that one too" 
2. The hunter of food - must be a wise decision maker and have great rationing skills as you will be the ones gathering and feeding the troops. Again, you may have multiple members in this team if you want to take down all targets of food in the building.
