3. The hunter of dessert - must be fast, but not too fast (you gotta make it back to the fort before everyone finishes their food because you can't get full on dessert only. Bonus if you can get everything back unmelted. 
4. The time manager - if you drove here, more than likely, you're parked at a paid meter. Your job is to make sure all teams complete their tasks in a timely manner and you return to your vehicle before the time runs out.
*This role may be combined with any roles above. 

If you master all these roles, you will have a successful meal. May the odds be ever in your favor, tributes. Let the games begin!

Everything you need is there.  Don't forget your Bassett's and OK Produce! Termini is there too... Even has gluten free corn dogs.  Amazing, historic, and oh so Philadelphian, support every shop there.

Dirtiest McDonald's - dirtier than I could ever imagine. Not sure how it is still in business. Even after double checking our order they got it wrong. There was a panhandler outside screaming at people who didn't give her money. A women came in yelling to the manager that she had to move the panhandler away because she was pulling down her pants when people wouldn't give her money. The manager was reluctant to do anything. 
This all occurred on Easter Sunday morning.  The food was fine -we ate it all but couldn't wait to leave.

What a gem in Philadelphia! And what a treat to discover it was right across the street from my hotel, Loews Philadelphia. 

Over and over again, we heard from locals: you must visit Reading Terminal Market. I need to read more into the history, but what I gleaned is that it's an old, historic building (old train station?) and one of America's oldest and largest food halls. 

There is EVERYTHING here. Prepared to be overwhelmed. There are so many vendors to choose from - cookies, ice cream, diners, cheesesteaks, Amish vendors, etc. Come hungry but with a game plan of what you'd like to eat. Lines can get long during lunch and dinner and congest the aisles. 

I wish I had more time here to explore and had done more research on where to go. I kind of just wandered around haphazardly, but I enjoyed every minute.

Great place!
Everything you could want or need in one place 

Amazing food 
Lots of sights and sounds 

We will return

Perfect after a late night at bars. There seems to be a lack of late night food options around this area, and masala kitchen definitely helps fill in that emptiness. Their specialty is the Kati roll, which is a paratha wrapped around meat or paneer. Here are a couple of my favorites from MK:

Paneer Masala roll -- although I'm not vegetarian, I prefer paneer over chicken because it has a softer texture, making it easier to bite into the roll without pulling half of the fillings out. It's pretty flavorful, and one roll is filling enough for a late night snack. The rolls come with a yogurty white sauce (perfect for balancing out the heat in the roll) and a spicy red sauce. 

Mango lassi: where else are you going to find a cool mango drink in the middle of the night? This is definitely a must have if you're already in the restaurant. 

Basically, masala kitchen is quickly becoming my favorite place for late-night eats. Make sure to stop by if you're bar hopping in the area!

I really love many of the vendors in Reading Terminal Market, but RTM itself doesn't impress me. Having said that, I understand why it's a great destination for tourists and locals alike. 

Pros:
- Easily accessible by transportation and close to many hotels and the convention center
- Very diverse food and merchant stalls that will appeal every taste. Even picky eaters will be able to find something they enjoy

Cons:
- There's not enough seating available. There are tons of food vendors and stalls, but only pockets of tables. Often times, the tables are dirty and not cleaned. For this reason alone, I always make sure to carry wipes when I visit.
- The walkways are too narrow to allow flowing food traffic and also sustain lines that build up for many of the stalls. You'll find yourself bumping into people on a busy day quite often.
- Can be a little difficult to navigate

Even though RTM has its pros and cons, I always find myself stopping in for a quick bite if I'm in the area. I do recommend stopping by if you're on vacation or here in the area for the first time.

WOW. Just wow. 
This pizza is perfect in so many ways. I've never had a slice there and not thought, "this is one heck of a slice." I love their tomato pie and the more complicated slices they do. I've never had a bad slice there and I honestly don't think they're capable of making a bad pie. Cello (sp?) is a pizza angel from above and I feel so lucky that we have Pizza Shackamaxon in the neighborhood!

I had a layover in Philly.  I hate this airport.  It's old, dirty, ginormous, and very busy.  The last time that I was here, I was not impressed with the dining options at all.  This time, I saw a Popeye's and figured that it would be a safer bet than other unknown eateries (horrible experience last time).  To my surprise, it was a pretty solid airport dining experience.  I got the chicken strips meal, which was surprisingly on par with non-airport Popeye's.  The price wasn't hiked up too high either.  The service was fast and the chicken was actually hot and crispy despite it being under the warmer light thing.  

My only beef with this place is that I didn't get a biscuit with my meal.  I love my carbs so I was looking forward to that greasy buttery goodness.  By the time I got to my gate and opened my box, I saw no biscuit.  It would have been too much of a hassle to go back, so I ate my chicken biscuit-less :-(.

So many choices it's overwhelming but in a good way. We got food from fourth street cookies, BECK's Cajun and two other places I wish I could remember. All was so good! Even though there are tons of vendors, everything is clean and organized. A must visit
Omg! I foodie's paradise. So many options and everting you could ever want to eat. Including a beef jerky bar.
Nice Saturday outing and good with social distancing.   The only problem I came across lately is expired food.  Besides that i totally recommend this place but always check expiration dates.

Love the Reading Terminal.

Quality food and houseware stalls in one location. Love it! What I don't love is the spacing. It's always crowded here which gives an indication of the popularity of the products but you can feel a bit overwhelmed by the crowds. Always disheartened when I see school-aged kids here during the week, DURING school time. Any truant officers in Phila. at all?

My favs are Flying Monkey, any and all of the Amish food stalls, Hershel's, Iovine's (freshest fruit and veg) and so many more.

This is a good people spot and I've always met nice folks here...workers and patrons like me.

4 well deserved stars.

I'm gonna warn you, Holy mother of Jesus it's crowded. Beyond crowded, like fire department looks at this as a lost cause crowded. But if you can't come in there and find something delicious to cook at home, eat there, drink, or flowers for the spouse you got some damned issues. I don't want to know people like that! Don't go to philly and miss this.
Unsurpassed for atmosphere, selection and price.  There simply isn't another indoor market in the country that compares.

I LOVE a great food hall, and this was one. So many vendors and some much to choose from. I can't get enough of this place. There is a very large amishcommunity with fresh goods. I suggest you walk the whole things before deciding what to eat.

Was just in line and the person working the front drive through was constantly coughing in their hand and arm. They proceeded to prepare my food as if I'm not watching. I canceled my order and requested a refund. 
That will be my last experience at this location.
Amazing place to get lost in for a few hours! It's nearly impossible to decide where to look or what to eat which is an awesome problem to have in my book. Definitely worth a stop!

God, this place is overwhelming. Also, probably don't come here hungover, it's going to REALLY overwhelm you. Most places take only cash. They literally have EVERYTHING here but it's just too much. Also, why is it only indoors? Let's take this party outside. After walking around for 15 minutes unclear what to do, I finally just closed my eyes and picked a Rueben place. Sloppy Rueben with a side of potato salad. My bf closed his eyes and picked a cheesesteak place. Subpar cheesesteak with a bag of chips. It is what it is. Don't come here with expectations. Don't come here trying to find a SPECIFIC place either. People are everywhere, bumping into you, stepping on the back of your feet, crowding you. Just close your eyes, pick a place, and get the hell out of there.

A market place full of all types of excellent goodies... definitely a place to visit if you're in center city or visiting Philly for the first time. Ribs, cheesesteaks, fruits, fresh meats, ice cream, cookies, handmade jewelry, etc... 

Must go......won't disappoint

This weekend we tried their Mikes Hot Honey, Burrata, Blistered Grape Tomato, Tomato/Cream Base

Trying to really capture that sweet and savory vibe with a slice would be everything. 

Well, they have DELIVERED!  I'm from Brooklyn, NY, so when I say pizza is good I'm giving you high quality ppl!
They delivered with a crunchy crust, delicious cheese, flavorful sauce, and that nice subtle hint of honey. 
There's zero doubt that they knocked it right out of the park; damn right delicious! 

@breeeeezy_sbd
Ahhhh I love this place! All kinda of food and desserts:) I forgot the name but there's a good BBQ place near one of the entrance.

Being new to Philly, I've been in search of a slice that reminded of the pizza back home in NY. I must say, this place  is it!! OMG, it was so good. Nice crispy crust, cheese to sauce ratio was spot on! My new favorite pizza spot for sure!!

Naya is a delicious healthy take out spot for lunch. I have been to the NY locations many times, and it was great to that there is a location in Chicago. 
The ordering process is similar to ordering at Chipotle, but with a healthier twist. First you pick your base- rice, or salad, or a roll. Then you pick your meat- they have meat like chicken shawarma, lamb kebab and falafel. Then you get to pick your toppings- there are unlimited toppings which is my favorite thing. I love picking feta cheese and hummus. 
The portion sizes are good, you will be full but since its not too heavy, you won't fall asleep after this meal.

Old City Coffee is where it's at. Got the coffee of the day because I like to change it up. It was a Kaldi blend. I'm not sure exactly what that is, but it was amazing. Even better when paired with some fresh made doughnuts from Beiler's

I went with the reviews and  had it on my "must see list"...the first night I was in there a gray baby rat ran across the floor I screamed and left. It took me 2 days to go back. 

Basic 4 Vegetarian Snack Bar is great! Their vegetarian cheese steak is as close as you can get and don't forget to add on the sweet potato fries.
Tried to go to Delilahs but during the lines are insane!
Went to the Crepe spot across from Delilahs but I wasn't impressed with the service. The lady taking the orders left us standing there for 2 minutes. Another customer came and she was quick to ask them for their order, they asked if we ordered already, and she had the audacity to say we already ordered!!! WE NEVER EVEN SPOKE TO HER!!!

In all, its a def a foodies dream come true...def a big variety of foods. Oh and not all places take credit cards.

Excellent service consistently - even with the crazy crowds. The friendly "my pleasure" whenever you request something, no matter how trivial, brings a smile to everyone's face. The food is solid Chick-fil-A fare and since this location is often busy, the food is always fresh, hot, and delicious. Low key Christian tunes serenade you in the bathroom as well so make sure you don't fall asleep in there.

Enjoy!
I love so many of the vendors here. Was in town for 4 days and we ate here at least once a day. Great variety of restaurants. Just wish it was open a bit later!

The must go to when in Philadelphia. I live in Wisconsin and have cannolis from the Reading Terminal sent to us for Christmas. I would move back to philly just to go there every week.
Amazing place,  a must see. The amish section is closed on Sundays.

For fellow New Yorkers visiting Philadelphia, this is your Chelsea Market meets ubiquitous farmers market.  Inside this huge expanse, you'll find aisles and aisles of prepared foods/meals mixed in with local produce, pastries, meats, and seafood you can bring back and prep yourself.  Prices are extremely fair and you'd be hard-pressed to walk through without finding something to buy and/or eat while you're here!

Been coming here since I was born. Enourmous place with so many eateries to choose from. Very creative foods too. Even just browsing offers so much to look at. Great place to hang out when sheltering yourself from the outside weather. Definitely the best place of this kind I've ever seen.
I'd give this place five stars but the only problem with this place is it often gets so crowded you can barely walk or find a place to sit. It literally gets almost impossible to think and function it's so crowded. So take into account when you come here.

Very cool place. Went at not a great time (2pm) so it was pretty packed. Not many places to sit and felt like I was always in the way. But loved the assortment of places, would definitely like it more at a less busy time.

So we were lucky to stay nearby this place that had so many choices for food.  Their Philly Cheesesteak spot was not good and they charge you for lettuce/tomatoes if you don't want a dry sandwich.  On the weekend they have musical guests by the area where all of the tables are at which was really cool.  Yes, it was crowded on a weekend but we still found seats and pleasant people to sit around and chat/eat with.  The Ice cream place was also awesome,.

This place is sick. Just sick. I am a seriously deranged foodie bent on eating the world and this place is my savior and kryptonite all in one. It soothes the savage food beast within but in time would bankrupt me, leaving me unable to feed myself. 

I'm not bothering to go into all the stuff they sell because every other Yelp review can tell you that. I'll just give you an idea of the kind of manic mindset you'll have as a foodie after visiting RTM.

It has everything you could ever want. And it's all so fresh, so delicious, so goddam beautiful to behold. I want to transplant this market right next to my apartment, vacate my apartment and live in a little tent in Beiler's with a summer timeshare at the fudge candy store and a little cottage by the gourmet grocer where the kids can drink blueberry lemonade when they're too hot. And when I die, I want to be buried with 4th St cookies and whoopie pies.

This place is a treasure trove. Unmissable if  you're visiting Philly. Come hungry. There's a Dutch diner, the best donuts ever, best Thai food in the city, veggies, artisanal cheese, coffee, atmosphere, vibes. Pure Philly.

New Yorkers: Think "Chelsea Market", but about 7,634,699,734,876,921 more raucous. 

Hot DAMN. 

This amazing conglomeration of foods and gifts is delightfully overwhelming. Pick up homemade fudge, market fresh veggies, Amish-made pretzels, and sinfully greasy cheesesteaks all within a 20 foot radius. 

A suggestion, for the tourists: it gets packed like a can of sardines in there. If you are carrying bags or luggage, drop it all off at your hotel first or be prepared to be "that person" that drags their loaded stuff through the tight crowds. (Ummmmm...sorry, folks. Ha!)

OoOohh Reading Terminal Market=)

One of my favorite places to go to Philly.  I've made it a habit to stop by here after I've mentally prepared myself from that long ride on the horrible Chinatown Bus around the corner and this place always seems to make the trip worthwhile when visiting my best friend in Philly.

I love walking around seeing the different selections of food...fruit, vegetable, fish, cheese, and bread markets..sooo much more...alll fresshhh all great=) 

I ate cheesesteaks and GREAT THAI food there.  I regret that I have yet to eat at the famous ice cream stand and try the crepes but maybe next time=P

Here in  Philly visiting fAmily and we checked out Reading Terminal Market.  What a fabulous place, where my Grandfather many, many years ago worked, making the visit quite nostalgic!  We stopped at Fox & Sons where we were able to eat safely as Celiacs!  My daughter for the first time in her life was able to try, eat and fall in love with Funnel Cakes!  The corn dogs were fab and so were the fries and gravy!  If you ever visit Philly, please go to the Reading Market and visit Fiox & Sons!  It's AWESOME and GLUTEN FREE !!!!!!

Horrible KFC... I love KFC/Popeyes but goodness it's as if they gave me chicken that they dropped on the floor it was disgusting !! And they drenched it in salt or something it didn't sit right in my palate. Idk what's wrong with these employees, they must hate their life because they project their sadness in life into the food

This is one place in Philly I'd come back to on every visit! There are a handful of small businesses located in the terminal. My friends and I got a variety of food to split with each other so we could experience multiple vendors without getting so full! During our morning visit, we started with coffee and made our way to grab a few things for a meal. Then we ended with a couple of different desserts. I wish there was more seating inside but I didn't have to wait too long for a table to get cleared. Highly recommended for a food hall experience!

Oh yes, Reading Terminal Market is just about as good as it gets. I'm actually sitting right in the middle of this establishment as I type this and I've been entertained for the last 15 minutes by a wonderful pianist going away at her piano. Even at 10 in the morning, there is a good crowd of people at the Reading Terminal Market and there's a nice sense of hustle and bustle. 

Onto the goods: There's tons and tons of vendors here. From bakery treats to good ol' mac and cheese, there's enough food to make you walk out the door 15 lbs heavier. On top of that, I think if you look hard enough, you could probably find nearly every kind of food here, or at least find damn near all the ingredients to make any kind of food you happen to be craving. 

I thoroughly enjoy their selection of meats, fish and produce but have no fear, candy lovers! Their sugary delights are also ridiculously fantastic. There's a candy vendor right across from my current seat and I can't help but to keep eying up their delectable display of chocolates and other sweet treats. 

All in all, it's reasonably packed on the weekends but definitely a place to walk through, if not shop through when in town!

We usually love this place but delivery took over an hour and our chicken biryani was too spicy to eat even though we indicated mild. And the sauce we were charged extra for had spilled all within the bag so we were really disappointed. The Kati rolls though were delicious as usual.  Chicken tikka and then I'm not too sure what the other one was.  I had ordered achari paneer but it looked like the same ingredients as the chicken tikka so I am pretty sure they messed up the order and gave us paneer Tika

This place could use a good clean. There's an underlying bad scent in the place. Been here many times for lunch and have seen roaches in the seating area.
Also lose the tough attitude  - it's really off putting.

OMG!  Terrific! Eclectic collection of freshly prepared food, venders, wares, groceries, seafood, meats, produce, local spirits, & non-alcoholic drinks!  Fabulous venue.  To go or indoor common seating.  Many places have their designated seating as well.  Don't miss this early in your trip cause you will want to go back. Check hours and be aware that some places aren't open on Sunday or Monday.  Closes around 6 pm.
Pretty overrated.  If you like sweets, you'll be in heaven.  It's crowded & uncomfortable seating.

Great Variety.... Crowded Weekends.

Wow what a selection of different foods!! Great place, great atmosphere. It can and is usually crowded, especially at lunchtime and on weekends, and with it being in the heart of center city definitely helps with this. All in all the crowds are well worth it.... Awesome place, Great, great foods!!!

One of the best thin crusts you're going to find! I'm normally not a fan of thin crust, but this one was just the right amount of dough. It has a really good crunch to it and mixed with the slightly sweet tomato sauce, you have a winner. I wouldn't go so far to say this is the best pizza you're going to have, but it's a very good one. I wasn't a fan of the outside crust, which was full of air and didn't taste like much. 

I tried an original slice and their special, which was calabrese salami, basil cream, jalapeño, and honey. Pizza was delicious - there wasn't too much honey if you don't want your slice to be too sweet. I liked the special, but I prefer the original slice. Not a bad sized slice for $4 either!

So living in Philly u try to avoid some of the more tourist filled areas but RTM is one of those places NOT to avoid. I swear there is magic in that building. It's almost like the entire energy of our amazing city culminates in this one place and I love that.
Whether it's the sites, the smells, the cultures, or the languages all around you, it's like a sensory overload in the best of ways.  It's the one place in the city where you can dive into the Indian culture with the best samosas and curries in town, or take a trip to Germany and taste some of their delectable sausages, or stay right in the USA and be smack in the middle of creole country with some Cajun crocodile on a plate...it's amazing all the culinary experiences you can have in one place. I guess that's why it is truly my favorite place in the city, it's always where I tell tourists to go should they ask, and it's always a place I take friends and family when they visit. 
I never leave without a Millers Twist salted pretzel and I always have to stop in the little Pennsylvania Dutch candy shop for some sweet treats, it's become a ritual that I enjoy more and more every time. 
Some days I just want to find a spot to sit in RTM and watch the city go by, it's a magical place.

One of the places that I worked inside before and have grown to love over the years. I mean face it. There are so many reason why you love and hate this place at the same time.

Why you hate it - it has a bad sushi display,it has a traditional diner that isn't open 24/7 (how does this exist), it's buffet section is kind of seedy, it has a horrible bar inside, Rick's Steaks moving out is going to kind of suck, there are 3 or 4 Chinese style stands and only one of them might be traditional.

Why You love it - incredible market atmosphere overall,The best Amish farmers section that's anywhere outside of Pennsylvania Dutch territory,  plenty of Authentic multicultural cuisines for inexpensive prices, piano music on the way to the bathroom, an incredible cooking book section, one of the best cheese stands ever, the fun events that take place, and the fact that Tony Luke's should be moving in could be amazing. 

No Matter what the good of it always outweighs the bad.
Love everything about Reading but I extra love Pearl's Oyster bar! Best variety of oysters on the half shell and their "oyster Sommelier" is the reason I keep going back.

You always know what you're getting so there were no disappointments but I'm here to write a review about the customer service I got today in the drive through. The man that was at the stand killed a lantern bug for me that was in my window side so I could put my window and get my food. Thank you so much! Lol

I first went to honeygrow because it was a new food option on my college campus. I downloaded the app which is great for pick-up when you're in a rush. Bonus: it comes with a $5 discount on your first order. I ordered the sesame garlic stir fry which was quite delicious. 

The beef was cooked but not tough. The seasoning was delectable, and it was great as a wholesome, healthy meal (new year, new me?). Honeygrow also offers a number of other healthy, filling options. I would recommend this place, especially to Temple students, and I'll definitely be going again!

This is a very cool place to check out if you're visiting and love food :)

There are all different types of food from pizza, the famous philly cheesesteak, salad, deli meats, indian food, halal food, amish food, bakeries etc and they sell jewelry and other random things. It's like a flea market food court with cool stuff.

VERY CROWDED during lunch, but a good place to check out when you're there :)

If you are visiting Philly, this place is a MUST GO for a meal! Come on an empty stomach though- there are TONS of options, Yelpers. While some lines may look long, don't be intimidated! They move fast.

Beautiful as a legendary food market and as art. My wife and I ended up a the the diner closest to the exit!

Delicious scrapple and breakfast spread! Thank you
I love Reading Terminal Market. It is a must stop destination when visiting Philadelphia.

A tourist classic in the City of Brotherly Love! Since the pandemic, more of the storefronts are back up running which is fantastic to see especially Mueller's! You can find almost whatever your heart desires here in terms of produce, meat, baked goods, etc. It is important to stay on your toes at the Market though. Most people will either run you over with their body or push you out of their way. I always recommend tourists who go to stay alert and if you want to look at something that makes you stand in the aisles, stand near solid structures like glass as you will reduce the risk of getting pushed around.

During my most recent visit to Reading Terminal Market, I heard a gentleman say "everything here smells so good" and that's when I realized that's just how I wanted to start this review - everything here really DOES smell so good. 

This market is a Philadelphia staple. Whether you're a local or a visitor, this is one of those places you just have to stop in to at least once. Whether you want to actually grab a meal, just take a walk around to see what all they have, or are looking to stock up on vegetables, fruits, meats, breads, or sweets, this is a great place to go to. Besides the delicious food, they also have some wonderful stands set up to buy great souvenirs and gifts. 

No matter what time of day you're visiting Reading Terminal, be prepared for a large crowd and lines. This is not the place to go to if you're crunched for time. I would recommend stopping in when you have time to spare. If this is your first time visiting, my other recommendation is to walk around the entire premise to see what all there is before you make any purchases. There are ample food options so it's nice to see what all they have to offer before making your decision. Just a few places that stand out to me include Meltkraft, Tommy DiNic's, Beiler's Bakery, Famous 4th Street Cookie Company, and Termini Bros Bakery. :)

If you're in or near Philadelphia, be sure to put Reading Terminal on your list of places to go to so you can take in just some of the greatness our city has to offer. Lastly, be sure to bring your camera/phone to take some photos and don't forget to bring along your appetite!
Love this place! Hatville is our go to for corned beef special.

I super duper love this place, you can find whatever you have the taste for here! Amazing cheese steaks, carved turkey, fresh meat and veggies, ice cream....you name it! This is my absolute favorite place to go to when I am downto

So happy I stumbled upon this place. The quality of food here surpasses all the other Mediterranean bowls & halal cart places that have been my previous go-tos. You can add as many toppings as you want at no extra cost, service is friendly, and the ambiance is perfect for a quick fast casual lunch! My favorite is the Naya rice bowl with half chicken shwarma and half kafta lamb kebob (yes, they let you split your protein!).

The Reading Terminal Market is by far the best spot for any food geek. Especially if you're a yelper this is spot to go. 

They have so much of the best and top quality food around. From, donuts to hoagies, cheesesteaks, coffee, seafood, name it they have it, 

If are a local or not. When you are down in the city. Take time to come hear. You will walk out with something for left overs and happy you came. Always try to leave with a cup of coffee from any coffee shop in the terminal is good and strong. And leave out with half dozen Donuts, you will never want to eat another donut esle where after you try them at the Reading Terminal. 

Tommy Dinic's for roast pork, Carmen's if you want alsome cheese steak. Hershels if you're looking to get a good pastrami sandwich,  Beiler's Bakery for the Donuts, Dutch eating place are you looking for some good breakfast, 

Just make sure when you come here you come with an empty stomach cuz you're going to need it!!! 

And the best of luck trying to find that one spot you want to eat at because it's tough to just choose one place!!

If you have never been here and you're from Philadelphia or visiting Philadelphia you need to go. Tons of different shops tons of different lunch options.  The kids will be entertained looking around and picking what they want to eat. Good place to bring a date if you're touring the city around lunchtime also. Vtrainers Personal Training

I've been to Philly a number of times and only now that I discover that this place existed.  I'm still pretty upset I've only discovered Reading Terminal this summer. It's pretty amazing! The closest thing I can compare it to is Pike Place Market in Seattle (without it being on the water).  If you've ever been to Pike Place, you'll know what I'm talking about.  

Located right in the middle of Philly, Reading Market has so many different stalls with a variety of merchants, ranging from small food stands. bakeries, ice cream shops, coffee shops, local crafts, fish market, butcher, salumeria, cheese shop, flower shop, fruits/vegetable stands, winestore, etc. OMG, my mouth is watering just thinking about it!

Word to the wise: come here on an empty stomach. There's so much to try and choose from, you will want to try everything.  Everything looks appetizing. Unfortunately, I only had enough space to try some ridiculously amazing Macadamia Nut cookies (drool) and a Kibbeh.  

Next time I come back to Philly, I'm coming back here gain, but hungry of course.
Everything your stomach could crave can be found in this market. From Chinese, to American, to sweets, flowers, souvenirs, etc. the reading terminal market is a must when visiting Philly!

1/13/20
Can't give an unclean place any more stars.  Trash all over the tables, a sea of trash on the floors, allows bums to sit in there and live at the booths all day. Cold /hardly warm food, no Ketchup machines or Ketchup anywhere. And a burger combo meal is $9.82 !!!!! I can find a million better spots to eat in Philly with cleaner, better environment and better food for $10 dollars.

It was a great and exciting visit! Tons of food vendors from meats to sweets. There are a few art vendors too. I wish there was more of that!

Definitely come hungry there is so much to try! I loved the Buckeyes I got. The Macaroons were ok but a little tough. I just wish there was a map or better signage inside.

Love it there.  So many food offerings and places to shop!  I went to have lunch with a good friend, and I ran right into a spice shop that had the spice that I had been looking for over a long period of time at a very good price.  I will definitely go back to shop as well as eat!

No customer service. Food's fine, but if I order from them again, I'll order online and pick up in store so I don't have to interact with their employees as much. Made it known that I was an inconvenience to them from the moment I walked in. Really wanted to like this place :(

This Chick-fil-a is so great! They helped me out so much i was in a rush to find something to take to a work potluck and they were so kind! They got me a platter ready in like 15 minutes! They are great!!!!
Always a great place to shop and now with Mercato delivery service, I can get food from the Market without actually having to go there.  Excellent!

This place is awesome in that there are so many places and spots to eat. 
However, the problem is that it's so packed that there is little seating areas to actually relax and dine. Also, feels a bit hectic inside. The tables also got a little gross because of all the other diners and not enough people cleaning or wiping them down. Each time, I ended up just eating at the restaurants inside because I didn't want to fight for food or wait on long lines at the different stalls.
This is one of my fav markets. Always filled with fresh produce and very nice restaurants along with very nice Amish people. I love their culture.

Good smoothie, but obnoxiously rude manager? 

Asked him about the large vs small smoothie, asked to see cut, tough to visualize numbers. He gave me dirty look and reply. After I paid, no thank you, nothing.

I guess when you are at the airport you can treat people like crap
ordered curbside pick up at the morning few days ago while there's already somewhat long line. I can get my food pretty good. Their mocha is very good but very high in sugar...
So cool - many options for fresh fruit, vegetables, meat and flowers. Lots of options to eat at too! Absolutely a must when in Philly!

Probably worst Chipotle i've been to. They're currently only doing online orders. I ordered the new chicken quesadilla and one if my sides were missing. I also ordered a steak bowl which came with 80% rice and probably half a portion of steak. I gave this location so many chances but the service is always lacking and the prepared food isn't up to par. Guac is always half mashed too.

UPDATE: just found a hair in the steak bowl

If you have a craving, chances are that Reading Terminal Market has what you want. With butchers, Amish stands, and candy shops to complement the coffee, seafood, and buffet options. My family's favorites include the gluten free cheese curds (they taste just like the real thing); avoid the mediocre cheesesteak
Classic Philly spot for a reason. Love Old City coffee and Olympia Gyros! Great little shop that sells honey and beeswax products near the back

This Chipotle is the worst one in the city.  Poor customer service, they act like they are doing us a favor.  Stingy with everything, giving half servings instead of the usual.  I'm Expecting and my baby hump only accepts chipotle so I'm a self proclaimed expert on serving sizes and acceptable customer service at a Chipotle.  I would rather pay toll and drive to New Jersey to the next closest one than eat food that has been around the unhappy people who work at the Roosevelt Mall Chipotle.  Please retrain your employees, and maybe clean the place a few times a day.

If in Philly this a must stop. If you a foodie this is a must stop. If you love cheese chocolate fresh pork sandwiches this is a must stop. I flew out here just to get my cheese for Christmas .... Great prices and amazing quality food choices. Come in the late afternoon less crowds

Great place to walk around, sample a bit, try new things here and there. Can't wait to come stroll around again once things go back to normal in the future. RTM is always a mandatory stop in my Philly trips!

There's something for everyone at Reading Terminal. Cheesesteaks, hoagies, gyros, cookies, pretzels, doughnuts, crepes, bakey items, teas, coffee, fresh cut flowers, Mexican, German, Indian, Halal, Asian, Mediterranean, a juice bar & smoothies, fresh cut meats, oysters, seafood, Amish cheeses & jerkey, hot dogs & corn dogs, fresh fruits and vegetables, wines, chocolate, fudge, ice cream, linens, mushrooms, cajun, pizza, ribs, fresh poultry, herbs, honey, olive oil, books, soap, skincare, and so much more that I know I'm missing. It seems e.n.d.l.e.s.s. 

If you need it, a map (in various languages) is available at one of the entrances to help you navigate your way around. 

I purposely booked my hotel for work near here so that I could easily walk here to get a few bites. My intent is to change it up with each visit and so that I'm always trying something different. 

Location: Its adjacent to Chinatown and about a 10 minute walk from Independence Hall & Liberty Bell 

The only con is that seating can be a challenge. Some food stalls have some seats available and there's some tables outside but my advice is to before the lunch rush (if you can) especially if you have a larger group.

LOVE LOVE LOVE READING TERMINAL! There's a spot that sadly I can't remember the name, but soon as you walk in it's adjacent to the homemade donut spot, there smoked wings are AMAZING!!!! The stand with the fresh fish, SOOOOOO GOOD when you get it home & fry it up! I just love the entire energy of Reading Terminal!

Has to be one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. Great combination of eateries and food stores. Can't be a better bakery than Beiler's, and I'm a devoted patron of DiNic's and Olympic Gyros. Termini's has a location there, and you can get an amazing array of meat, produce, and baked goods. One caution, if you go to eat lunch there at the normal hours, you will find pretty big crowds to contend with. Just goes to show you how popular it is.

There's no question that I love Reading Terminal Market.  So much that I actually went twice during my last visit to Philadelphia even though it wasn't planned.  In reality though, if you're visiting from out-of-town, you'll definitely need more than one day to try a good amount of the many food vendors it has to offer.

I covered a lot during those two days:  Beiler's Bakery, Dutch Eating Place, Tommy DiNic's, Keven Parker Soul Food Cafe, and Beck's Cajun Cafe.  All good eats and I highly recommend trying them all if you have a chance.  And even though that may seem a lot, there's still a multitude of over vendors I still have yet to try.  Maybe next time I'll try more of them, but it might be hard to sway from my favorites above, especially Dutch Eating Place and Tommy DiNic's, both which I already tried from my last Philly visit 4 years ago.

Like I stated in my previous review, Reading Terminal Market is truly a great sampling of what Philadelphia has to offer in terms of food.  And I don't think I can ever get tired of the place!

The Industry is a nice place.  Good atmosphere, great food at a decent price.

I came one night for the mac-and-cheese croquettes only to dream about them and return the next day.  They are good.  Absolutely not just you average "mac-n-cheez balls".  They are croquettes.  They use a light cheddar, the balls are huge (3-4 bites) and the breading is quite nice.  They are also complimented with a kimchee sauce that I wasn't a huge fan of.  The second time I got the mac-and-cheese croquettes I got a different sauce and it looked a little better.

I also returned for dinner.  I ordered the red snapper special and it was quite nice.  Everything was perfectly cooked and flavorized in all the right ways.

My only caveat was that the drinks are a little pricey.  So I didn't get anything to drink.
My boyfriend on the other hand ordered two cocktails which he could easy finish in about 4 sips.

Pretty good service though.
So fun and versatile, many wonderful people who are happy to point you toward the dinner/lunch of your dreams. The best part of Philly

300 conventioneers descended all at the same time. Surprisingly the lines moved quickly and everyone was able to be back in an hour. This is the best place for you and your group of friends to meet and everyone gets exactly what they want.  Everything is incredible. It's the best of Philly with the bonus
Omg this location is garbage,employees are so rude. They never have what's on the menu. You're better off asking what they actually have instead of looking at the menu.

This place is the masters of gluttony , it's like hitting the lottery with food.  Words can hardly explain the RTM, because it is so unique, and you feel like you've stepped back in time. One of my favorite go tos in Philly

Effing pieces of crap... it must be customary for them to screw customers this way because here we sit, an hour after placing an order through Uber and nothing. We called and were told our order was cancelled... no notification or anything. Not even sure how we get our money returned, and now no dinner. Philly csuckers.
What a great experience I had at the Terminal Market.  Anything you could possibly want is there.  What is really nice is that it is indoors on those cold winter days.

Seriously best indian food i've had in a long time. Ordered the paneer kati roll, and wow- to say the least. the woman at the counter was very helpful and patient with my questions. The mango lassi was also to DIE for. i will be going here for dinner soon!

Wide selection of healthy foods. Sometimes I worry, when ordering a healthy smoothie, if it's really going to be healthy. This green smoothie has spinach, banana, nonfat yogurt, and ice. It tastes amazing!!

This market is an iconic market in Philly. The location was convenient. The inside was quite big. I saw a lot of stores, restaurants, etc. I got cheesesteak and Dutch breakfast. I used a restroom. It was a relief downtown, Philly.
The market is located near SEPTA stations. You should stop by here as the first sightseeing spot in Philly!
Such a fun and interesting place! Lots of neat finds in this market. I bought a few souvenirs as well as some food. I highly recommend checking it out if you're in town!

I absolutely love the reading terminal market.
When I bring friends to visit Philadelphia I bring them here whether they have any interest or not.
I burn about 3 hours getting lost in this wonderland.  It's full of delicious food, my goal in life is to try food from each and every stand. Not a hard feat because so far everything I've tried is mouthwatering. I would recommend a certain stand to go to but it would just be unfair to pinpoint the "best" stand. All of them are exceptional in taste, quality, and service.
The prices here are a bit pricier, but you certainly get what you pay for.

I love this place!! It is very busy so I wouldn't suggest going to lunch exactly at noon! If you're enjoying a coffee or just wanting to walk around, this is a great place for people watching. Many great options and all of the food we had was delicious. If you have time to wait in line, definitely stop at DiNics!

The Industry has eased its way on to my short list of favorite bars in the city. I truly love this place. It's great for drinks, dinner, and brunch - sometimes all three if you hang out long enough (it happens). The service is always friendly and fantastic. 

In my humble opinion, the food has been getting better and better over time. There's always a great selection for dinner ranging from salads and sandwiches to entrees. For brunch, I always go savory but would highly recommend sharing something sweet. I once had a few bites of their baked pancake special and it was phenomenal.

Super solid spot.

Wow.... A little bit of everything, fresh produce, desserts & the food was amazing. Plenty of places to browse if your looking to grab something to eat. We waited in line for a half hour to get Frank's Chicken & Perogies It was good but I can't believe it took that long to get our food.  I Really couldn't believe how few tables there are to sit at, We had to put 3 of us at one table and 3 at a different table. I would recommend getting there either before Noon or after 1. There was a sea of people, even seen a lady flipping out yelling at a cop because some lady stole her seat. I really enjoyed walking around and checking out all the different markets, but My favorite part was the Pretzels the Amish made stuffed with cheese filled Weenies.

Man... it's not until you move away from a place when you ever regret taking it for granted.  I stopped in on my most recent pilgrimage back to Philly, and maybe I appreciated it more for what it is, but it was even more wonderful than I remember.  Although at the same time, it was exactly the same.

Fresh fruit and vegetables, termini brothers, denics, chocolatiers, books, linens, just everything you could want - and it's ALL good stuff.

I'm sorry Reading Terminal Market for taking you for granted when I lived in Philly and always going to Whole Foods.  You are the superior being.
Such a fun place to visit especially in the morning. They have anything you would want to eat plus drink at this place. It's a nice layout and offers a great atmosphere for shopping and dining.

I liked Reading Terminal Market, but if you don't know what you're looking for, it can be a bit overwhelming.  Case in point...all I wanted was a quick meal, but food is scattered through the market and I really couldn't tell what was good...I think I was too hungry to wander through and really decide what I wanted.  

I stopped for some crab cakes, which were good, but I wish I would have had more time to explore!

Definitely worth a walk through, but give yourself more than 30 min total (including eating!)

No words to describe how incredible this market is.  Truly my favorite place in Philadelphia.  The last time I went I got this incredible Thai food and cookies.  So many choices and goodies.  It is very affordable for the quality!  Highly recommend to anyone.

There is so much to eat here! Aside from the food vendors, there is also a grocery store and florist. If you want to eat in the designated dining area, you'll have to show your vaccination card which I appreciated. It can get pretty crowded in early so try to get there early on the weekends or go during the weekdays.

Native NY'er here. Date visited: 12/31/2021.

The Good:
-pizza by the slice available
-big big slices (props for this)
-fast and friendly service
-cute workers
-decent taste

The Bad:
-my crust was burnt (between toasted and charred. not toasted but burnt. 60 seconds too long in the oven
-slightly too little tomato sauce. just a bit more would have been perfect. the cheese-to-sauce ratio was a bit off (this could be because it was baked too long)
-pepperoni didn't have much flavor
-no Margherita available

Decent pizza. Could be amazing. Also try Cozette's in Queen Village for 5-star pizza.

If I was judging on looks alone this pie would be a 9.7! But, I have to be fair and rate it from first to last bite.

Saturday evening it was fairly slow with a 30 minute wait for our large pie. We came back 25 minutes later from a lovely walk around Fishtown and noticed the pizza was sitting. Meh.

Pizza in the car was the play. And yes, I originated it. 
This is a gorgeous pie no doubt about it. Cooked perfectly, golden cheese and grated parm to top it off.
The pizza is on the thicker side, I wouldn't necessarily say thick tho, and was very oily. You can tell the ingredients are fresh. Definitely some Fishtown flop.

I emotionally wanted this pizza to be better. I scored a 7.9 which I thought was fair and Jess went 7.5.not going out of our way to visit here but would have a drink and grab some slices. It was such a rollercoaster of emotions from a delicious bite to a mediocre one. Doesn't crack my top ten in Philly.

So much to pick from, I go on a weekly bases :) If you are going for the first time give yourself time to look around because they have almost every type of food to offer. One of the best places to eat in the city whether you are all by yourself or with friends or family. There is something for everyone there. And the food is always amazing!

Best thin crust New York style pizza!  We walked up to the window to place our order and got our piping hot slices in just a few minutes.  The slices were huge!   We went during lunch hour on a weekday and there was no line.  It was convenient not to have to order ahead of time.  Even if we had to wait in line, it would have been worth it.  Will definitely return.
Pizza Hut has really gone down on quality.  I used to love them.  I won't be back, I can spend way less on way better somewhere else

Holy sh*t this might be the best pizza in philly. Fairly thin crust but still some amaZing flavor and chew to it, not to mention the super creative and delicious special pies - like the bacon, date, mint cream etc. that puppy is to die for... low key makes me wanna drive back across the city for some more today

Yay, I get to join the long line of people who have written a review of the Reading Terminal Market.  My review will last 2 seconds at the top of the new reviews near you list and then get buried, never to be seen again.  Ah well, better make it count.

Here's my take on it as well as a few things I learned about how to survive.

1.  Come with an appetite.  I ate 3 separate lunches while I was here.  It came out to a meal every hour.  That's how I roll.
2.  Do not come here while there is another event going on...like say a Flower Show.  It's a little disconcerting when all the parking guys are telling you to enjoy the Flower Show.
3.  There are a bunch of pay lots to park in, just shop around for the best deal if you are going to drive in to the city.  If you're taking one of the buses from DC, you pretty much get dropped off right around the corner.
4.  You will get up close and personal with everyone at the market.  If you dress in layers, your body will be less accessible to other people's hands.  If you get claustrophobic, do not go here.
5.  People will think it's appropriate to bring luggage and strollers through the tiny aisles that make up the market.  Hurdle them or tip them over.  Then blame the person next to you.  This applies to old people and small children as well.  Do not be afraid to throw elbows.
6.  If you come alone, you can sneak into all the seating areas that much easier.  There's always that lone seat that no one wants to take.  While that couple is arguing about who should take the seat, you can swoop in and solve that dilemma for them.
7.  Bring cash.  Many of the stalls are cash only.
8.  This is just filler.  I wanted to make the list even.

This review is solely for the Gorgonzola cheese bought to me as a gift from my darling brother and his lovely gf.

Jesus, Joseph and Mary (in an Irish brogue)!!
This cheese transported me to an out of this world experience. After the initial bite, I left the planet, flew to the moon, danced and wined with aliens then landed back to Earth. Holy cow! It literally melted in my mouth, there's no chewing required whatsoever. I already had my crackers out to elevate the cheese, but after that bite, I put them away. It's so smooth, has the perfect texture (not too firm or too soft) and has the perfect amount of buttery creaminess, that it totally stands well on its own. The taste is so subtle but flavorful where nothing else is required besides a beautiful glass of wine to accentuate that wonderful aftertaste. I'm not a fan of blue cheese but this one, won me over.

If you're looking for a gift or souvenir, look no further, this is you're wining ticket.
Amazing!! I come here every time I'm in Philly. Termini bakery and of course an apple dumpling. Beef jerky too!!! Everything is so tasty!

It's Nirvana.  I'm Philly born and bred, so I have seen the evolution of the market over the years- opening on Sunday, all the wonderful cooked food vendors, make it a Mecca for visitors. Great offerings in a soulful spot. 
Proud of my city!

RTM is one of my favorite foodie places to go. You could seriously spend all day walking through, trying food and drinks of every kind. This is a must-do especially if you're from out of town. There is something to eat/drink for everyone.

I was craving some middle eastern food for lunch and wanted to skip the usual Cava or Honeygrow so I decided to give Naya a try. I'm so glad that I did. My order was about $30 (including all fees but tip) and it was a LOT of food for $30. The delivery fees kill you with UberEats but the food seemed very reasonably priced.

I ordered a Naya Salad with EXTRA Chicken Shwarma - you could barely call it salad. The extra protein made it more of a chicken bowl. It was very good and a great mix of ingredients.

I also got one Kibbe (deep fried beef ball) that was tiny but delicious. I opted for a side of Cucumber Yogurt dip and some house-made Baked Zaatar Pita Chips (that were very fresh despite their professional packaging). 

As I said, the meal was delicious and travelled really well. The packaging was great and generally I was blown away by this place that I had never even heard of before. If you live in Center City (or elsewhere - I live in Fairmount), definitely give this place a try. It was a nice change of place and the perfect delivery lunch bowl.

Went there for lunch today, Stood in line for over 5 minutes and then the girl started to take the order of the man behind me, which wasn't happening! I ordered an Extra Value Cheeseburger meal only to get back to my office and no fries. Horrible service, everyone needs to be re-trained there. Never again..

Unfortunately, my first-ever Reading Terminal trip really disappointed me: the food was "okay" at best, the space is very cramped and good luck to you on navigating throughout the market.

Paid visits to Carmen's Famous Cheesesteaks, Creperie & Flying Monkeys --- they're stuck in my mind, but not for any good reasons at all.  I'm very saddened to leave a 2-star review for this market!  Perhaps my expectations were too high.  

The Amish stands are closed on Sunday so if you are looking to get one of those delicious pretzels made by the Amish girls that everyone raves about, don't go on Sundays.

Chicken Masala Kati Roll (7.8/10) 5.7 

I really like this Kati roll! It's like eating chicken curry with roti, except that it's already wrapped up for you  The only thing I don't like is that some chicken cubes are too big. Those pieces don't get enough flavors in the middle and are very hard to bite . 

They have options to have red source ( spicy ) and white source ( curd, kind of like sour cream) on the side. I recommend getting both and mix them if you like spicy food!

At least one Saturday a month, my family comes into Center City to enjoy breakfast and shopping at the Reading Terminal.

The Dutch Eating Kitchen is the absolute BEST breakfast, and well worth the minimal cost. 

The Fair Food Farmstand has great organic vegetables, sauces and honeys. 

Amazulu has eclectic, authentic African jewelry, clothes, home goods, accessories and body treatments fro all over the globe! 

Monday-Friday, after 5pm, The PA general Store has happy hour where all the homeade cookies are $1 EACH!!!! There are nearly 30 varieties of cookies!

Hershel's East Side Deli has mouth watering Pastrami, cornbeef, egg salad and turkey sandwiches! Did I say MOUTH-WATERING???

Beck's Cajun has the best BREAD PUDDING with WHISKY SAUCE! YES...WHISKY! 

Finally, grilled cheese becomes an adult classic when you create one at Valley Shepherd Creamery & Meltkraft Grilled Cheese! Move over chil'rin...let the adults sit down!

This place has EXTREMELY CLEAN BATHROOMS! My only complaint is the cleanliness of the seating areas. People do NOT clean after themselves! Yes, the janitorial staff works HARD, but customers feel like they do NOT have to throw their trash out. Disgusting.

Listen here...They're only getting a 4 and not a 3 because the food is so good, but my goodness they did the ONE thing I can't stand...My ONE pet peeve when it comes to fast-ish food joints....
DON'T SHORT ME ON THE FRIES!! 

Hear me out people cause I know it shouldn't be a big deal, but when you pay for large size waffle fries, you don't expect the portions of a small one. Come on now ya'll. I know you working hard back there and maybe just maybe someone was rushing and didn't pour enough fries in...

But my favorite part of the fries experience was ruined!
Ya'll know what I'm talking about! When you think you're done all your fries and you reach into the bag and there's a few extra that must have fallen OUT of the fry container and its like french fry Christmas. 
All I'm sayin' is don't ruin French Fry Christmas for me! 

Anyway, the food is good as usual. l

Like the Liberty Bell, cheesesteaks, and that pesky city wage tax, the Reading Terminal Market is one of those things that makes Philadelphia uniquely Philadelphia.

Yes, it's a historical site, but more importantly, it's full of vendors selling delicious food. There's something for everyone: Amish sellers are there part of the week, and you can pick up groceries or get your grub on if you're in the mood for a cheesesteak, Thai, Indian, ice cream, oysters - you name it.

If the Market was open past 5 PM, I'd be the happiest camper. And poorer, but who's watching my wallet?

PRONOUNCIATION: Remember, it's "Redding", rhymes with sledding. Don't ask me why.

Oh what's not to love to the city version of a farmers market. You name it, they have it. So many cuisine's to chose from, you won't go hungry. From souls food, to Italian, and to vegan! So many options you won't go wrong. Bars, and sports, shops OH MY. If you are in philly; go try this food galore! I think everyone should visit here!
Really liked this place, very similar to the Pike Market in Seattle. Must visit if you are a tourist, and the cheesesteaks here are pretty good as well.

This is the most fabulous place!!! Food, food and more great food to choose from.  Fresh seafood, butcher meat, and vegetables !! Shopping, pastries, chocolate and Do Not Forget the beautiful and tasty doughnuts!!!

Really enjoyed it.
Good food everywhere.
Affordable price.

Visited on 3/23/19
-A late post (I was there before COVID-19)-

Food: Good
Price: Good
Service: Good
Parking: Street parking
Revisit plan: Yes if I have another opportunity to visit Philadelphia again

When going to Philly, my dad kept saying "Go to the Reading Terminal! I've seen it on tv!". I didn't know what he was talking about. Why did I want to go somewhere where people read? Then the hotel manager told us to go there for lunch. I then text my dad and told him where I was going and he said, "well, you don't listen to me". 

When we went inside, I was amazing. There was so much going on! There would food spots, markets, and little shops. It reminded me a flea market, BUT WITH FOOD. I had so many choices in where to get food. I ended up going to a sandwich spot that was well known that had "the best sandwich" in America from DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef. Thaaaaaat was okay, however the Reading Terminal was over all great and now I know where to go for a variety of food.

Reading Terminal Market is a must-see in Philly, though I found myself a bit overwhelmed by crowds and options on a weekend afternoon. I like that there are a lot of grocery vendors, like seafood, produce, and tea, and not just food stalls. The offerings lean classic and fast food-y rather than super millennial or artisanal.

Lines for Philly cheese steaks are long but move quick; I don't think this is the place to try it unless you're on a speed-tour like I was, as I thought it was pretty average and the experience getting it was stressful. The donut place is a cool stop to see them making different pastries, though I thought the one we had was meh. An unexpected highlight was the infused olive oil and vinegar spot-- you have to try everything.

I do appreciate that prices aren't overly inflated, but for me the crowds just made this too hectic. We really had to fight for seats, like looking around at multiple locations for over ten minutes. Try to hit it on a weekday if possible.

I love the place, everything for everyone, just because they said my review was a little short they should pay me more money and I would write more words....


I'm only fucking around, it wasn'Reading terminal that told me my review is too short it was the app. Lol

I saw this while Walking around Chinatown and figured I would give this place a shot.  I was enticed due to the picture of a whole fried squid and when I tried to figure out what this place was, I had a hard time figuring out the name of the spot.  I am not sure who thought the name through as it is completely stupid.  Best I can think is that it sounded good in Taiwanese and directly translated into English gets you this juxtaposed use of the English language.

The place is small and so you may not find a spot sit and eat.  I ordered the teriyaki beef dish and upgraded my drink to a green tea grapefruit drink for $1.55.  This place is cash only - this irks me as they charge you sales tax.  Nonetheless, I was enticed by the image of the dish and I was not disappointed when it came out.  There was plenty of beef and it was delicately cooked.  The meat was tender and easy to eat through and there was a good bit of rice with it.  The drink itself was enormous and was satisfying itself.  I was not sure what to expect but it is great quality for the money.  

This place wins the takeout spot of the year award based solely on its packaging.  Everything is segmented inside and the lid is airtight.  No spills of anything in your car.  

I will definitely be coming back to sample the menu.  However, I have to take a star off due to the fact that you can visit several other spots in the area and get a dish of comparable size, quality, and composition for the same price (or less) and they accept charge cards.  Also, while the prices are good, the extra dollar they charge compared to other spots for the same dish means another star off.  Combined with the lack of charge cards acceptance, this makes a difference since there is also tax charged.  I want to give more stars but there are other spots in the block that can give you the same for a tad bit less - and they have much more seating room.

Great place for a group to eat something for everyone Karen Parker's soul food was great ( Collard greens are awesome).  Dinic's roast pork sandwiches are everything you have ever heard about. Hershels corned beef and pastrami are great. Of course you can't forget the desserts are amazing with Basset's ice cream and Termini's cannolis.  The whole atmosphere is fun, it's like a throwback in time. People bustling around some people site seeing, some people grocery shopping, some people just grabbing a bite to eat and people watch.

While spending 4 days in Philly we had to stop in here on two of them.  This place is fantastic!!!  I loved strolling through all the different aisles of goodies.  There's a grocery area surrounded by different chocolatiers, bakerys, deli cases and food stands.  We went on a Monday morning and while it wasn't total chaos it was definitely busy and crowded but that didn't deter us from taking our time and trying as much as we could.  
We started with a pork sandwich from Tommy DiNics that was delicious, sat at Hershel's counter and split a pastrami sandwich that was equally great.  On our way out I nabbed a tasty mint chocolate ice cream cone from Bassett's.  On our second visit we got cheesesteaks from Spataros, another gem.  My only regret is not having had more sweets, there are some crazy looking doughnuts that I must try next time!
Check out the Thai place and get curry salmon & add shrimp. Thank me later. Other great options as well but this is my go to

Aside from fabulous places for produce, fish, meat and counter food the atmosphere is wonderful.  People of all colors, sizes, and gender gathered together in a peaceful manner - the way the world should be.  You can get basically any food of any nationality you can think of and don't forget the donuts and ice cream stands!

Really neat market.  You can literally find everything from fresh produce, to seafood, to tea, to homemade donuts.  There are probably close to 100 (if not more) vendors there and, if you have an appetite, you'll definitely find something you like.

We were a bit overwhelmed by the crowds as we went during lunch hours.  Judging by the large amount of folks wearing hospital scrubs, it's clearly a spot the locals go to.

We saw BBQ food, Mexican fare, a weird place that had burgers, hot dogs, BBQ chicken and pierogi's (that's one vendor... LOL).  There was a turkey sandwich eatery (good food there!) as well as cheese steak vendors.

A really good spot was also the fresh cookie place which has $1 cookies during the last hour they are open for whatever cookies they have left.  Get the macadamia chocolate chip cookie!

I absolutely adore Reading Terminal Market! I've been coming for over 20 years now, when I was just a little girl my family would visit the city during the holidays every year for the Macy's light show and the Charles Dickens; A Christmas Carol walk through. Afterward we never, ever skipped the opportunity to stop in for dinner and a Termini bros famous cannoli for dessert! Be aware that it gets SUPER crowded and seating is very scarce and hard to find. There is never an open table so you have to wait for one to open up and run as fast as you can to "secure the bag" before someone else beats you to it  most of the the time the result is just having to share a table with other people, or in some cases you may just have to unluckily stand and eat. I think the crowds, the noise, excitement all around and the race for a table is half the fun of this place that I really enjoyed as a kid. I would recommend to everyone that they MUST stop in at least once in their life for the atmosphere, shopping and good eats all around! I've actually never had a bad meal from any of the places once! I'll be back to update with a pic soon! :)
Found this place through a deal on Grubhub. Chicken shawarma bowl is great! Very fresh ingredients and a very nice portion size. would definitely recommend for a relatively healthier meal!

What a wonderful place and people. I went there last Saturday just to take a look and I was delighted by the smell of freshly baked pastries. What an aroma delight it was, I went home with nearly 6 dozen boxes of pasties for all my friends and family, it even tasted better then it smelled. Would definitely recommend 5 stars!

Very, very good! So much flavor packed in a small package! The combination of Indian spices provided different tones and aromas in every bite. Very satisfying. Must warn you, one Kati Roll will not be enough, so get 2, plus you'll get $1 off if you do. Paired with a fresh and tasty Mango Lassi, I'm very good now. Very, very good.

Staff is young, super friendly and engaging. My photos will not do the food justice, the magic is hidden inside the rolls.

I have to give this place five stars. Not only is it uniquely Philadelphian, it is also yummy 99% of the time! As much as I enjoy the sloppy Joes at the Amish diner, I still recommend that you skip the Amish fare (they use saturated fats and favor unhealthy shortenings over butter - for shelf life) and go for the uniqely Philadelphian and international cuisines. I love every stand. The Thai place has a salmon dish that is amazing and every stand there has a speciality, just ask the people in line for which items are the stand's signature dish(es).

Very fun. There's a lot going on here - lots of options, lots of people, lots of temptations. We came here for a stroll and then for lunch, and ended up enjoying both greatly. One of the hardest things was just deciding what to eat among so many delicious-looking options.  Great location in the center of the city.

Wish there were a little more seating and water fountains, and a little less crowding.

Stop by the  Thai place and get salmon with curry on rice.  Stop by Hershels and get some tasty matzo ball soup with potato knishes.  Everyone likes the donuts at Beihler's .  There is a plethora of different foods here.  It's a great place to shop and eat.

Every food vendor is opened and they're so many to choose from, definitely overwhelming if you're there hungry and on the hunt. 

They have seating but you have to wait online, your food will be cold by time you sit.

So yea, go here!

The Reading Terminal Market (Pronounced as 'red', not 'reed') is a collection of restaurants, shops and stores that really could soak up an entire day here if you wanted it to.  Sadly we didn't have all day, and just a few hours, but I think we sampled a fair amount of what the Redding Terminal had to offer.  

Rather than list every store that's found at the market, i'll just list the locations we visited.  Those places were we visited were:

DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef
Flying Monkey
Old City Coffee inc
Termini Brother's Bakery
Beiler's pickle patch
Glick's rib shack

Again, by no way is my very small sample of the market a real representation of the market, but my tastebuds were happy and if/when I return to Philadelphia, i'll be back to the Reading Terminal Market to sample more of what this place has to offer.  

100% pay this place a visit, and bring your appetite!!

Don't let the name fool you, BeefSteak is all about the veggies!!!

Tldr: Beefsteak offers a delicious arrangement of fresh veggies at less than $10 with a refreshingly pleasant staff as a bonus! =)

Food! Cause its the most important: I went in without any idea of choice I would make. Luckily, the staff was happy to walk me through the menu and eventually recommend starting with the build your own bowl. There were three different stations for adding food. The first section allows you to pick your veggies that will be placed in a cooker and added to the bowl later. Next, you can choose your carb( rice or quinoa) or protein option(chicken sausage). The last section allows you to add a variety of toppings and sauces before you're done. The build your own starts at $8.49 and goes up with added protein and some veggies. 

Staff: Beefsteaks staff did a phenomenal job. From the beginning to end of my order, they were courteous and focused on answering any questions I had. I also appreciated the opportunity to try the different sauces before I decided on one for my meal

Critiques: Beefsteak does a wonderful job at bring there customers fast food vegetable heavy food; however, that is at the expense of protein and matt options. Although there are a few, it is definitely short of adequate for a meat lover. Lastly, it sucks that they are only open 11 - 5 making it mostly a lunch option.

The best indoor market I have ever been to! I have been to Quincys Market in Boston, The market in Charleston SC and a few in Ohio this is the best !!! 
I enjoyed walked around the Market, highly recommend it to anyone and everyone living or visiting.
Bakery, seafood, meat market, food stands, produce and a flower shop. Anything and everything !!

We ordered delivery from here and were very pleasantly surprised! My boyfriend and I love Indian food but were at bit doubtful about their "Kati rolls"- although I love naan I usually prefer rice with my Indian food. However, the rolls are amazing! Our favorite was the Masala roll- it is juicy, a touch spicy, and full of flavor. We also tried the tikka roll, which was great but a little dry. Luckily, they delivered a tasty yogurt sauce with every roll which was delicious and made up for any dryness. We also ordered a mango Lassi which we both really enjoyed.

Not only was the food a hit, but they delivered within 20min for free! Very impressed and will be ordering again soon.

Still catching up on reviews and thought about this place while on a business trip in Philadelphia last year.
Reading Terminal Market was directly across the street from the hotel we were staying at (Home2 Suites). This place has everything!! I even tried out a Chinese restaurant here (the name in question is Golden Bowl). It was the best Chinese food I've ever had besides PF Changs, but that's still good too. :)
My dad tried out a Greek restaurant called Olympic Gyro. It was packed but we managed to find a place to sit to enjoy the food.
It's worth coming back!

Where do I start? Reading Terminal is a philly classic.  The food, the atmosphere, the people, and the location.  All unbeatable.  I've easily tried half of the different vendors food, and am yet to have an unpleasant experience from any of them.  Going here is a must for anyone who comes to visit me in philly, and I recommend it to everyone!
The Terminal is like a melting pot, they have every form of food from soup to nuts. I Love Buehler donuts they remind me of my mother inlaw famous donuts.

I always find time to visit here when I'm in town. I enjoy the history, the variety of shoppes, and the whole atmosphere of this marketplace. I can see why Reading Terminal Market has been in business for so long. Some of my favourite spots here are the tea shoppe, the beeswax candle shoppe, the General Store, the Mushroom shoppe, and Flying Monkey for their gluten free options. As a New Yorker I come here to stock up on items I cannot find near me, and it's also significantly more affordable. 

My only advice is to not visit during the Philadelphia Flower Show, because that's when the Market gets mobbed with tourists! This is especially true about the Donut Shoppe-my first visit to the Flower Show back in 2015, and my first trip to Philly. All I wanted to do was explore the Market, but there was a long line, a good kilometer (0.6 mile), wrapped around the outside of the building! Why? 'Cuz tourists wanted those famous donuts, that's why! XD:   But that's good for business so I'm not complaining 'bout that!

My only complaint is that (like many places in Center City Philadelphia) it closes too early (at 18:00 or 6pm) most days of the week (based on memory).  Otherwise I enjoy visiting and shopping in what feels like my eccentric Amish grandmother's farm stand.

The Holy Grail of food in Philadelphia.  If you can't find it here, you ain't looking hard enough. 
I have been coming here for far longer than I care to admit.  My mother used to drag me around the market back when it was the old Reading Terminal,  complete with the leaky roof and the floor was coated with sawdust.  There were carcasses hanging on hooks of every edible animal imaginable, some animals wtere still alive,  waiting for the axe.
It was unbelievable!  My mom made me sit with her and drink buttermilk at Spataro's, we ate with the Amish and had ice cream at Bassett's. 
Later in life,  I worked near the RTM and if I didn't visit there everyday,  I got a bad case of the shakes. I was there so much,  some of the vendors thought I had an apartment upstairs. They called me KYW because I was there two, three, four times a day. 
The RTM is different now, it's a kinder,  gentler market, shinier,  brighter and much more diverse. I still love the RTM very much,  and watching it grow has been like watching a family member mature over the years.

Visited from out of town. This place is magical even if parking is expensive or hard to find if you're not willing to pay. You can find just about anything you need for a meal. I picked up fish, spices, butter, coffee, wine, fudge, and even Jamaican chicken patties which were oh so good!

I've had a lot of "platters" in my life from: NY, NJ, and now PA. Masala's is probably a 6 out of 10. I got a combo (lamb and chicken) platter. the rice wasn't flavored and the meat seemed quite dry. I know the white and red sauce is supposed to be the star, but the red sauce had an over powering taste of paprika(?) i think. 

this is obviously not a meal you'd get for lunch or dinner... it's definitely an after hours/after drinking/hanging spot. But i don't know. I've had platters from carts around the city that were better than this. sorry!

Let me tell you, Reading Terminal Market was actually remarkable. This is a casual and friendly little place. These guys got a magnificent menu also. I became very good friends with the staff, who are all fantastic and super courteous. Incredible.

I've heard a lot of great things about this market and that it's basically a Foodie Central. Reading Terminal Market reminds me of Chelsea Market very much, except with more variety of shops and food. It's quite busy here and busy with customers and tourists

So many shops condensed into one block and there's different foods to choose from.From fresh produce to seafood to meats to sandwiches to sushi to sweets and a lot more.  You have choices of Chinese, Mexican, Japanese, Cajun and a lot more. Everything here is fresh and the foods are cooked on the spot. The food is cooked right on the spot.

They have seating areas around the market. There seems to be a lot of locals that come here and tourists. If you come to Philadelphia, Reading Terminal Market has to be one of the places you visit on your list.  I highly recommend all foodies to check out the Reading Terminal Market because there is tons of food and places!

Note: A couple of the shops are closed on Sundays, so your best bet is to go on other days.

Pizza here was alright but the reason they get a one star is because the customer service sucks. We asked them if there's a fresh pie coming out twice and they said no. A minute later, When the guys friend came the pulled out a fresh tray.

The only thing that keeps this from a 5 star rating is the fact that it closes by 6PM. Great food, wonderful variety. Especially like the pretzels from the Amish stand, but there's load  of good stuff. It gets very crowded, and finding a place to sit can be a challenge, but still a favorite place in Center City.
It's an awesome place with a ton of great shops and eateries. Would reccomend to anyone visiting the area. If you live there. You should get there as often as possible

The amount of love we have for this place is hard to express! A life goal is to spend 2-3 days here and just Sample and eat all that is available!

We came in on a weekend and found that some of the places were closed, but the vast majority were still open for our dining pleasure.

The place is literally rows upon rows of eateries and specialty shops. A small sampling of the places we checked out included a Mediterranean spot for drinks, a cookie shop for... You guessed it cookies, a place that specialized in Fair food that probably had the best cheese curds I've ever tasted, a spot where we grabbed a Philly cheesesteak, and a spot that made one of the best pastrami sandwiches we've ever had. Obviously, you're sensing a theme but this place is legit! If you didn't know that before you got here, we may need to get you the Internet.

Whether you come in here with a plan or just to Peru's, you'll find something that you need and probably five or six other places that you want to try. Going here on multiple days is advised!
Great place to get one of a kind items from the shops. Food stalls a varied and delish.
So many yummy options! I couldn't pick just one, so o got a bit of everything. Made myself sick stuffing my face, but it was soooooo worth it!

I'm honored to be the Duke of Masala! I can honestly say every visit I'm 100% satisfied my partner and I eat here often and I always order the Chicken and rice platter which is layered on a bed of rice , lettuce, chicken ,  accompanied by naan (flat bread). Delicious food and open until 3am !
