Always enjoy spending time here. Between the arts and crafts to all the wonderful eateries to shopping for dinner this place serves up a little of everything!

Fun!

So many beautiful and delicious foods packed under one roof. I definitely recommend the grilled cheese stand but do a lap around the market before you make any decisions because there's so much good stuff and you can prioritize after you see all of the choices.
Fun indoor market with lots of food options. We enjoyed the sights and smells. Meat and seafood counters left us saying, "Ah, if only we had a kitchen."

This gets 5 stars for the crazy loud fun place.  My husband I split something at about 5 different food places so we could  try more... ribs,  pastrami sandwich, philly cheese steak.   Oh the doughnuts.... and all the beer.  Fun fun fun.  It was Oktoberfest which made it even  more crowded and loud.  A must go in Philly for the atmosphere alone.

Very diverse and interesting place, every time I visit Philly I discover something new here. My favorite stand is Meuller Chocolate Co, which has a variety of fine chocolates, including different body parts and organs packaged with clever little sayings!
Over 59 plus vendors under one roof!  Very good selection of places to eat.  Surprisingly very clean, even the bathrooms!  Highly recommend that you visit this place!!

One of the most wonderful places in Philly, no matter what you're craving it's going to be there. Stall after stall of unique and interesting food. And tons of vendors selling other things too! If you want to sit down to eat, it's always a challenge to find seating, but that's half the fun.
Absolutely everything under one roof! One of my favorite parts of visiting Philly.

Wonderful superb from beginning to end. Wednesday is dollar dumplings day! and combined w the Groupon we were in our glory. Ryan the manager was a lovely dumpling-engineer teaching us the best ways to indulge. Loved the aloha pork noodle bowl and the roast pork noodle bowl- so flavorful! Seasonal Vegan options available! And we loved the taco dumplings and the cheesesteak (winner!) we weren't a fan of honey chipotle. END THE NIGHT with fried seasonal blueberry cheesecake dumpling! You won't be sorry! Ps- byob- but the beer store just a minute walk away (Beer Love) was superb to supplement our satiety.

What a lovely place to get lost in. I admit, I first heard of Reading Terminal Market from National Treasure. Stop laughing. I'm a huge Diane Kruger fan.

Ate so many good things. Bought some cookies to-go. Drank some coffee. Perused some shops. Amaze.

If the McDonald's franchise executives had any brains, they will shut it down. Maybe they are just not paying attention. There is no saving this McDonald's restaurant. Everything about it is terrible: The entire staff just doesn't give a hoot and don't understand what customer service is all about. They got my order wrong, which isn't bad enough. They also ignored me when I told them I did not receive my coffee as I stood there for three minutes.  So I walked away frustrated, sat down and attempted to eat at a filthy table.  After I took two bites of my breakfast sandwich I threw it in the garbage. It was horrible. And I wasn't going to waste my time waiting for someone else to ignore me complain. Better I forfeit my money than remain another minute in this embarrassment of a restaurant. As far as the seedy location, I'm grateful there's a security guard that works in there for the benefit of the patrons. This is a rogue McDonalds that has escaped the oversight of the parent corporation. So if you're feeling hungry and you see this McDonalds when in downtown Philly, don't walk - run away! Better you stay hungry for a a few more hours than eat here.
Love bringing friends and family here to show them all of the cool shops, it is very packed tho I wish it was a little bigger.
If you are heading to Philly, you have to check out Reading Terminal Market. Really cool experience!

A-Ok Pizza! I tried the plain slice which has a nice, crispy charred crust. The tomato sauce was flavorful but not outstanding. On a Philly Pizza scale, this is a solid 4-stars. Benefits are the slice was ordered through the to-go window and arrived promptly, piping hot!

Ordered the chicken tikka kati roll! Pretty decent size and fair price, but the chicken was definitely a bit dry. There are some sauces you can get more of that definitely helped it out a bit. Overall, it wasn't the best kati roll but an easy grab and go if I'm hungry and looking for a small bite to eat.
Excellent choices available of all types of foods!! Problem is that it's very crowded and not enough seating
A ton of things to go and see! So many great places to eat. Market Pantry has incredible sandwiches to go, smoothie place is amazing!
Must try if you're here visiting or lived in the city forever! Absolutely delicious and amazing venues, friendly staff and great shopping!

The Reading Terminal Market (RTM) is a foodie haven! It's one of the most well-known indoor markets in the country, so stopping by is a must if you're in Philadelphia.

PROS:
- Multiple dining options! From Cajun dishes to homey soul food and delicious breakfast and brunch items, there is a little bit of everything for everyone.
- Moreover, there is always something new during your next visit! With all of the vendors inside, it is difficult to eat everything you see in one visit.
- $4 parking at 2 different garages for 2 hours! All you need to do is take your parking ticket, spend $10 at ONE vendor and have that place validate it for you before you return to your vehicle and pay.
- The vendors are all friendly. Smiles were abound and enticing dishes were everywhere to be found!

CONS:
- Crowded and touristy. I accidentally "shouldered" a high schooler (or middle schooler?) from out of town because of how crowded this place gets (and because he was hogging the aisle).
- The open seating area is limited. You have two options: Wait for a table to open up OR you could join one. Some vendors, like Molly Malloys, have their own seating area. My family and I were fortunate enough to grab a table after a few minutes of waiting and, seconds later, two people joined us at the table. I'm totally fine with this, but hopefully part of the ongoing construction includes additional seating areas.
- Lines, lines, lines! Everyone wants a taste of the delicious doughnuts at Beiler's or the famous Roast Pork Sandwich from DiNic's, so expect to wait awhile at the popular vendors/stalls.

All things considered, RTM is a great place to grab a bite or even shop for a few groceries! I love the idea of indoor markets and food halls, so visiting this place was a great experience. I'm looking forward to my next visit.

Liked this place. I liked the Thai place, the produce section, ice creams, coffee. There are so many choices to make as to what and where to eat that is overwhelming. It was packed with people and finding seating was not easy. July 2019.

Perfect snapshot of Philly, the foods, produce, flowers, gifts, coffee and teas. It's all here. Beats the heck out of Pike's Place Market in Seattle (yes I've been along with markets from Perth to Hong Kong to Honolulu). It's a unique jewel in an otherwise bland, humorless glass and steel Center City Philly.
Great place, lots of different foods all yummy and fresh produce, it's just overcrowded making it hard to experience it all.

Great indoor market with a little of everything available. They have fresh seafood and meats, cooked food, clothing, ice cream, fresh juices and smoothies. Etc etc you can easily spend hours in there shopping, browsing, and eating. Don't forget to stop for ice cream at Bassetts, it's a must!!

10/10 highly recommend! Great places to eat all around! Spartos and By George is great for cheesesteaks. Beiler's donuts is amazing. Carmens has great customer service. You cannot go wrong with Dutch eating place and their specials(hot roast beef sandwich)! Dinics for the win on the pulled pork sandwich and last but not least Miller's twist for pretzels was my first love and the reason I repeatedly started going to the market in the first place. All in all, great food, fun, and more!
Very cute, lots of fresh produce and meats, unfortunately many places inside appeared closed due to COVID

We loved our time at Reading Terminal Market! So many unique shops and several offering samples.  We settled on some banana pudding from Sweet Nina's and a fruit smoothie from a place that has been in the market since 1987. Both delicious. Will gladly return any time we are in the area!

I love market places such as this one, as there aren't many in the states. Definitely worth checking out but be aware that this place is always packed and busy. We went Saturday morning and you're basically shoulder to shoulder with people the entire time. There is very limited seating so expect to order food and eat later or eat while you walk around. Many long lines for all restaurants, so settle on the one you think is worth it. I love that there is produce and other grocery items here as well. 

There's an Amish pickle stand located near the center. They let you sample items and sell pickles individually or by quart (I think). There's also a cute candy store and I was able to buy just watermelon gummy bears. They "don't take card for less than $5," which in fact violates their credit card agreement but WHATEVER. 

This place is located across from the convenient center and it was quite easy to Uber there, since we didn't have to worry about parking. Although this place is pronounced "Redding" and not "reading" so that might be a distinction needed if you cab it.

I absolutely will not stay anywhere in Philly that isn't walking distance to Reading Terminal Market!!

My family and I have enjoyed Sweets, Soulfood, Nawlins Cuisine, Philly Cheesesteaks, Corn Dogs, Beverages, etc from this awesome establishment over the years. 

My absolute favorite is Hershel's East Side Deli!! I always get ToGo from there to savor for days. Their Pastrami and Corned Beef Sandwiches are fannntastic!!

Just read from another Yelper that they have a Vegan Spot so I need to venture up to try them asap!! 

Reading Terminal Market continues to be a community staple constantly reinventing themselves and providing Philly w quality food vendors in a safe space. 

See you soon RTM !!

I normally don't write reviews, but after going to this McDonald's I felt a need. I was the only customer when I entered the store. All i wanted was a large fry, I nicely asked the cashier if I could have hot fries-the look he gave me , then said it will be 3 minutes I nicely said ok. Well several other customers came in so he decided to help them before he dropped my fries. Now I'm waiting for him to help other customers. As I was waiting along with several other customers someone said in a loud voice "get the heck out of here I'm not eating here a roach just ran across the counter! Well that was enough for me. I'm sorry how could I forget to mention there was a manager and 2 other workers just sitting around in the back laughing and talking instead of going to the front to help out! Last but not least, I don't mind if music is being played thru the speakers, but please oh please tell me why they had very offensive RAP music playing--clearly you could hear the "f" and b" words in the song. NEVER and I mean NEVER will I go to this place again. Once i get a free minute I'm going to find out who owns this McD's a write a another letter to them! This was horrible...

I'm a sucker for kati rolls! I love this place. Hidden Gem. Great Service. Amazing, flavorful food. 

The Paneer Masala, Aloo, Mixed Veggie, and Achari Paneer rolls are all must haves! 

I've also had the Paneer Platter, and enjoyed that. The sauces are all really good, as well.
Great selection, friendly people.  Fresh food at a good price!
Lots of options for lunch.  I will bring a cooler next time for meat and seafood to bring home.
A Philly classic,everything and anything you would want, too many choices and all the best of their categories, busy noisy crowded but worth navagating the crowds

After seeing the Barstool Pizza Guy come here a year or so ago, I've wanted to try this place. Today I took off from work early to finally drive out and try this "amazing" pizza. I wanted to call ahead to have the pie ready for me by the time I got there, but I was surprised to find out that Pizza Shackamaxon doesn't have a phone number. Better yet, they don't even have a online ordering service. When I finally got to the establishment, I saw there was a small "Sold Out" sign on the window. I was baffled how a pizza place (that has one job {to sell pizza}) could be sold out. The man in front of me was rudely turned away. When he tried to order a pizza, one of the workers pointed to the sign and said "we've been sold out for 2 hours" in a very snarky tone. I was disturbed by the workers attitude to the potential patron. While me pledging not to be a future customer won't affect the revenue of Pizza Shackamaxon (as it is extremely popular), just know that they left a potential customer extremely disappointed..... in more ways than one.
Amazing biriyani - best in whole town. My new favorite indian go to place for lunch and dinner. Service is very quick and friendly. My new regular go to food spot.

We ate at the Reading Terminal Market twice while we were in Philly. There's definitely something for everyone, but I'm not a huge fan of crowds and it was packed in there. They have all kinds of food, deli, pastries, chocolates, flowers and good people watching.
Chicken shawarma bowl and Kafka lamb kebab bowl was great! Just hit the spot.  I was very full and couldn't finish it all. My lunch tomorrow. Great choice. Highly recommend them!

All Different selections of food. We tried Bassetts Ice cream and it was delicious. But three kids cones for $15! Wow! But they gave you a lot of ice cream and it was great. We also went to Kamals spot that had a refreshing drink the lemonana for $5. We had scallops from UMI a 1/2 pound for $13. Amazing. It was a cool spot overall with a variety of food, but make sure you have your money ready! It was our first time, and we will be back.

This place is a must when visiting Philly.  While it can be overwhelming at peak hours, there is always something you can find to eat here.  Whether you are craving some italian food, indian food, deli sandwich or a traditional Philly cheesesteak, this place has it all!

My recommendation would be to avoid this place during lunch on the weekends - go before or after typical lunch hours!

One of Center City jewels . There are plenty of shops, restaurants many cuisines to choose from under one roof. Grab your favorite things to eat then meet up at a table to eat your amazing food finds. This is a winner for the entire family. This is also a awesome place to find souvenirs. Enjoy

Always hits the spot. My favorite is the chicken kheema roll. The chicken tawa is good too, but I would probably choose to have a second kheema roll over a tawa (I usually get 2). I haven't tried the chicken masala yet, and I'm curious about the vegetarian ones too. I did try the chicken and rice platter once and was not impressed. I'll just stick with the kati rolls, which are stellar!

Overall Score: 4.75 Stars (Always Cool)

This review just states the obvious: Reading Terminal Market is an amazing place. Where to start? It has pretty much everything. For a tourist, there are plenty of places to eat and shop. Oysters, turtle soup, Mexican, Asian, etc. What I like is that my daughter and her husband live in Philly, so we can also take advantage of the numerous options to purchase meat, cheese, and seafood. This type of market is very common in Europe, but not so much in the US. It is very well located, equidistant from Independence Hall and Rittenhouse. Unlike some reviewers, I have not really found Reading Market to be oppressively crowded...rather, it is vibrant and lively, but there is plenty of opportunity to eat what you want and to buy what you want. An amazing place.

Thanks

Good spot...
Bring cash...
Tough parking
Overall decent

I love the Reading Terminal Market. Fresh fruits and veggies meat is always fresh and the pastries are delicious. Prices are great along with the service. It has  become a staple in my home and will always be my favorite place to
shop

There's so much variety, if you can't find something, it's just due to your own indecisiveness or because it all looks pretty good. It's a market, so expect what you would at Chelsea Market or another big vendor emporium. The middle eastern and greek food spots are my favorite here, and the ice cream/chocolate vendors are a great way to finish off the lunch stop!

If you don't like crowds or pushing around like you're in Manhattan, you probably won't want to spend much time in here. It's worth a couple laps to decide what you want to get, so if you can handle it, I recommend you take your time and get adventurous.

I am a huge fan of markets like this one. I love the variety of food (and from different cultures). Unfortunately, that one Sunday I went (during COVID times too), a lot of the stores are closed. There was one particular smoothie/juice shop that I like so I got a mango juice. It was refreshing and tasted divine. I would like to come back and actually eat more! Love the ambiance and set up.

Reading Terminal Market reminds me of Chelsea Market in NYC, only it's way bigger, has a much larger selection of food stalls, produce, and shops. I found it bustling, but low key, with plenty of seating, not that much waiting around and I liked the layout a lot better because it takes up a whole square block and there are multiples to come in and out of the building.

Tried Di'nics roast pork sandwich with extra sharp provolone and roasted sweet peppers. I highly recommend it - the roast pork is so succulent and juicy, and the combination of the roasted peppers with the sharp provolone kept the sandwich interesting, so you kept waiting to eat more and more of it. On top of it, the soft italian roll would soak in the juices with each bite, and it just got more delicious at the end.

Really, really good.

Amazing Amish dinner pancakes bigger than the plate omelets and the candy and cakes out of this world
Don't forget the ice cream just trust me

CALLING ALL FOODIES!!!! This place is HEAVEN on Earth for food lovers!! I can't believe this past weekend was my first time here after being to Philly a few times!! Anything you could possibly want to eat in one place!! I did my homework beforehand since our time was limited and I wanted to make sure I tried nothing but the best!!

-Beck's Cajun Cafe: Hands down my favorite!! They were serving bright and early...couldn't pass up on trying the award winning Trainwreck sandwich...WOW!! My mouth is salivating as I type! I also tried their fried mac & cheese balls which were delish!! Staff was friendly and helpful!! 
- By George!: BEST Stromboli I've ever had!! We shared the Italian, phenomenal! 
-Valley Shepard Creamery & Meltkraft: shared the Somerset Grilled cheese which was good. Awesome for cheese and olive lovers!
-Old City Coffee: much needed booster after feasting!! 
-Flying Monkey Bakery: AMAZING SERVICE!! So friendly and sweet!! We actually came here Saturday and Sunday! Not a dessert person but my daughter loved their whoopies! 

Sadly, I could've done without :
-Sang Kee Peking Duck's shrimp dumplings...sauce was great, but wasn't a fan! 
-Fox and Son Fancy Corn dogs was terrible!! I went with the cheese and jalapeno corn dog...really wish I hadn't...sauce was gross and jalapenos were dried up and tasteless. 

But hey you live and you learn!   

TIPS:
-COME EARLY!! Some places don't start serving their heavier foods till 10:30-11am...I still recommend you get here as early as possible to avoid the lines. I got to the terminal at 8:30am and was able to grab some food, eat at a table with no wait, digest, and repeat once the the other places started serving. 
-Crowd starts coming in around by 11am, making the table seating limited.
-Come with a friend(s)!! It's so much more fun when you can try out a bunch of spots and just split it with friends. 
-A lot of the merchants are closed on Sundays (Amish thing) so if you're coming on the weekend, Saturdays is your day!

Reading terminal,  until we meet again!

I live walking distance from the Reading Terminal and often frequent it. I enjoy the unique small shops that offer quality cheeses, spices and fresh butchered meats. The owners are always friendly and inviting. The challenge with the Reading Terminal is the extremely overcrowded walkways which make it very difficult to maneuver through the market place or enjoy the experience. I highly recommend going to RT before 9am if you want to feel and see all that it has to offer.
Food was absolutely delicious and perfect for a light lunch ! Flavors were bold and delicious.Absolutely delicious? Yes, absolutely delicious! I had Chicken Kheema and Paneer Masala.

Perfect late-night spot with awesome kati rolls. Extremely quick service. Went around 11 PM on a Friday, and there were a few folks dining, but no line to order at all. The place is very small, with only a few tables, so I can imagine that it can get quite packed. Really appreciate the multiple paneer options vs. the one paneer option that the Kati Roll Co. in NYC has. I got the paneer peperwalla roll which was great. I have had some kati rolls which are too dry and others which are overly oily or very messy to eat, but this one was perfect - good portion size, each bite was packed with flavor, and it wasn't too spicy. I didn't even need to get any additional chutney on the side. Extremely affordable price as well for the quality. Will definitely be back!

An institution for visitors and locals alike, come here for lunch or to get your groceries or to do some shopping. If you're here for groceries, don't miss OK produce for bargains, and I found that coming in the morning or right before closing, i.e. 5:00 p.m., is a good bet for things to be less crowded.

Good place to get fresh food at a fairly reasonable price. The "Salmon Spot" as us locals affectionately call it is very popular and usually identified by the lines wrapped around the corner. It goes fast though because everyone typically orders the same thing so they make them really fast. They also have produce stores there (Iovine) that sell fruits and veg for good prices, plenty of specialty stores and culture specific boutiques and markets to keep you busy. Great place to walk around too.

Reading Terminal Market is one of my favorite places in Philadelphia. The Market has an incredibly diverse selection of food stands housed inside an old warehouse. For people that haven't been to Reading Terminal Market before I describe it as a small city of food stands. In addition, there's also a nice fresh grocery area if you're local and need to do some grocery shopping, and some other shops with things like soap and candles.

However be warned, Reading Terminal Market is always very crowded. 
Consult the map to find what you want, otherwise you may spend a long time wandering, gawking at the choices, and standing in a traffic jam of people who are doing the same thing. Seating is also unfortunately very limited because of volume of people. But this place is worth it!
Philly finest, never disappoint Fresh food, great service, upbeat vibe and always have what I need! My Friday vibe

I call this place flavor town, so good. Normally I wouldn't be wild and try this but it's awesome. 

Zero idea if it's healthy but it's gotta be better than a burger and fries.

Definitely a must see when you visit Philly. Very busy and something for everyone. From places with seating to takeout to vendors with merchandise. Will take awhile to snake through and see everything!

Unique in it's age and building, which is pretty cool. If you are a local a place to frequent and be proud of. As a visitor it was worthwhile and I'd stop again, but the variety and prices aren't much different from similar markets in DC, Lancaster, Chelsea in Nee York, etc.
Amazing selection, and personable staff as I experienced. Must try for a visit to Philadelphia.

Fun place to shop and eat! Stumbled upon this place while walking around and wanted to get a quick bite. Unfortunately, it was difficult to walk around with my kid because he was so distracted with everything. A lot of vendors to shop and get anything. Some places the line was really long so I didn't get to try everything there.

I love this place! It opens at 8am on saturdays and has an amish section, great food (new orleans, dinics, and etc), chocolates and desserts, stuff for your kitchen, chinese food and a whole slew of other things. I def recommend hanging out where on the weekend and just trying new food and walking around. Its so close to downtown and old town that when walking from one to the other ther eis no reason not to stop here!

It's 2019 and the same thing is going on that has been going on at this Wendy's it's horrible to see a business go down the way this place did i was there recently and purchased 4 meals so you know i needed a cup holder no they don't have one so i said ok, but they acted like i was wrong for asking and then got upset cause they forgot to give me my frostys really! My fries was cold and hard and my strawberry lemonade tasted like lemon water im over it....

Walked in to get a coffee..
Waited 5 mins.  Everyone was Soo busy doing other things...I walked out
I've been coming here since I was a little kid. You can find the best of everything in one conveniently located market. Nostalgia galore.

Every time we come to Philly the Terminal Market is a must stop for us. The entire family looks forward to the amazing Pork sandwich from Tommy Dinic's. They are delicious. There is always a line but it moves fast. There are so many food options on the market. There is definitely something for everyone
I'm been going to the Reading Terminal since 8th Grade. I'm there 2-3 times a week. It's my food playground. Live it there!

This has to be a must see on any trip to Philly.  I've been to Philly a lot in the past 3 years and I normally get there at around lunch time. There is no better place to start than reading Market. They have everything you can imagine all under one roof.  Want to try a cheese steak, there's  Spataro's Cheesesteaks.  Want what's is becoming Philly's signature sandwich, go to  DiNic's for one of their Slow cooked Italian roast pork, broccoli rabe sandwichs, with thick chunks of Sharpe provolone. You have a sweet tooth there are 7 bakeries and 4 candy booths. There is a clam bar and for those that like there lunches wet, there's Molly Malloy's. Now I'm not saying that this is all that Philly has to offer, far from it but it is worth spending at least an hour in.

This is for sure and experience you must do when in Philly ! 

I kept hearing about it from friends and didn't really know what to expect, was thinking this was going to be similar to Ponce City Market in Atlanta but it wasn't , it was WAY BIGGER scale. 
There was just about everything you can thinking of food wise: gyros , ice cream, jerk chicken , Chinese , I mean the list could seriously go on. 
I had already eaten lunch so I was looking at the many shipping areas of food : produce , fresh meat of any and all kind, fish, etc. it really was all incredible !!

I would recommend doing your research on places to eat prior to going here. There are so many options that it is overwhelming. I would avoid going here on the weekends and during the holidays. Lines are long and people are constantly pushing each other. Been here 3 times and never had a good experience and the foods we tried so far (Filipino and Mediterranean) were ehhh. But I haven't completely given up hope for this place since there's still many food stalls I haven't tried yet. Old city coffee is good tho but nothing special.

All I can say is wow wow wow 
Our first time in Philadelphia and we wasted no time running in here !!
Best Middle Eastern restaurant in town. Ismael always takes good care of his customers.

The drive-thru line is always SUPER long no matter what day or time of day. The time that I went, I walked in the store to order inside instead, and they were only allowing mobile app orders, but no one was allowed to walk in and order there. Despite this, the drive thru line was still super slow and took almost 40 minutes to get to the window. The food is usually fine here, but it is pretty disorganized and really slow for fast food.

I stayed in Philly for a weekend and was told that Reading Terminal Market was the place to go for a quick delicious breakfast. I sooo wish there was a place like this in Rochester, NY. As soon as I walked in my heart soared with delight. 

Reading Market provides a warm environment (literally and figuratively). There are countless mini markets in this indoor market. I was curious to see what I could find that I walked through the entire place before ordering anything. There's bakeries, meat/fish markets, souvenir shops, cafe's, and bread companies to name a few. The prices are low and competitive, which made my breakfast experience a little more challenging than I had hoped for.

I purchased a baguette breakfast sandwich at a New Orleans style market. The sandwich only cost $4.75 and it could easily feed 2 people. I was shocked at the portion size when they handed it to me. 

I bought whoopie pies for my family at a cute little vegan bakeshop as well. When I returned home with them, they gave rave reviews. 

It wasn't very busy for a Sunday, which made the experience even better. I would like to check it out on a Saturday when more stores are open.
Love the RTM. A true slice of Philadelphia and something for everyone.

The worst chipotle in Philadelphia. Every time I order from door dash some ingredients are always missing. I spend too much money for this to keep happening. I wish I could give 0 stars. This is highly unacceptable. Where are you guys finding these employees?? I can see this happening maybe once or twice. But it happens every time I order. Please contact them to fix this issue 
Thanks in advance

So excited to have a Filipino place so close by! The shop is cute within the newly renovated Bourse. Staff was friendly and they give you a cute toy with your order number on it. The wait was 5-10 minutes for my order of the hot dog and lumpia. The lumpia was really good! The hot dog was pretty small and for the price I expected a lot more. I shared this with a friend thinking an order each would be enough but we were both pretty hungry after. Worth a try, especially with the lack of Filipino places around but a bit on the pricey side for the quantity.
Seriously, if you can't find something amazing to eat here, your tastebuds are broken. And the apple dumplings at the Amish place? Get out of town.

At the Terminal, there's something for everyone! Quite the experience. Whenever we venture into the city, we visit the Terminal. Because it's such a popular destination, the city needs to help out by cleaning up the smells of pee and removing the homeless living outside.

Really, really happy about this place. In town for a convention, and I've been eating here every day. Pretty sure I could be here for a month and still eat new stuff every day. Every place I've been so far has been solid, which is impressive. Definitely worth a look!

Plenty of options for everyone! It's truly a combination of all sorts of things and no matter what the variety, everyone will be able to find something that suits their taste. Right now due to the pandemic, the place isn't very crowded. However, it's usually extremely crowded and it quickly fills up. 

This is definitely a more touristy attraction which higher price points for the food and potential gifts, but definitely should not be overlooked.

Recently went to Reading Terminal Market and all of the staff were friendly and following COVID guidelines. My boyfriend and I split the chorizo fries at Fox & Son, the black forest pastry from Termini Bros, and a slice of focaccia pizza from Market Bakery. Everything tasted phenomenal, the atmosphere was lively, and we will definitely be returning. Great casual date spot for anyone in Philly!

Food & price point: 3.25 Out of 5
Ordering the lechon kawali meal, al la carte lumpia shanghai, and a water bottle cost us $23.22 out the door. As my family would say más mahal (that's expensive)! I don't mind supporting local businesses, but for the amount of food we received relative to price we paid it's difficult for me to recommend this place to other people. If the reason the price is higher because of breaking even to pay rent at the Bourse I would recommend some other location.

Service: 5 Out of 5
The two people that served me were friendly, swift, & professional. Great service

Environment: 5 Out of 5
The Bourse is a great meeting location, right off the L. Inside the Bourse Lalo is has a family style bench our group sat at.

Overall: 3.75 Out of 5
As a fellow Filipino-American raised on home cooking I was disappointed by the portion to price point ratio second to the food being more Americanized. If I were the owner I'd focus more creatively about delivering Filipino cuisine to the unfamiliar folks, moving to another location for cheaper rent, and or owning a food truck to get more exposure. A fantastic Filipino American food truck blazing trails in San Francisco-Bay Area is Senor Sisig!

I loved there achar chicken roll, chicken masala roll and mango lassi. AMAZING!! I always got it delivered never went there to eat but they truly have the best Kati rolls I have had in a very long time. The food quantity is good too. One person can eat one whole roll, nothing goes to waste.
I shop here every Monday morning for my weekly produce & meats. I avoid it at all costs during tourist trap Saturdays

I go too RTM to buy bread from Metropolitan Bakery (like most of their breads) and pick up groceries from Iovine Brothers where you can get reasonably priced fresh produce. Bring visitors to try Beiler's donuts (apple fitter the best if you don't want too sweet) and Bassett's ice cream, a Philly original. Amish stores are interesting too.

Reading Terminal is the perfect place to meet friends & hang out, while grabbing a great bite to eat, or do some food shopping.

There is a vast array of food selection of eateries: seafood, Rotisserie, sandwhich shops, burger places, Thai cuisine, soul food, cajun. food, & a myriad of bakeries where you can get: pastries, cakes, fresh baked bread,  cookies, ice cream and other authentic desserts. 

Reading Terminal is located in the heart of center city Philadelphia. Don't fear trying to find parking, for there is a park lot across the street which provides discount parking to Reading Terminal patrons. This is a  place  you must visit if you are in the Philadelphia vicinity.
AMAZING SERVICE. Loved how polite and cute the staff were. My food was nicely put together. The seats and tables were clean.

If you are in Philadelphia and you are a foodie, this is the place to be. I was fortunate to stay at a hotel around the corner so was able to visit this markel multiple days in a row. I kept finding a new vendor that I wanted to experiment next.

They have food from multiple parts of the world. From bakeries, seafood, meat, soul food, cajun food, fresh produce, you name it, they have it. Make sure you look up their hours before you head over and enjoy the options.

What can't you get at 'Reading Terminal Market'? 

This was my work lunch spot for a couple years. It never fails to deliver. This place can be overwhelming with the selections and sometimes it can be difficult to find seating but it's definitely a great place to go if your group can't all decide on what you want for lunch.

Love this place! This may be the best food court ever!  Tons of choices, the sheer variety is a little overwhelming at first. From pizza, hoagies and bbq to falafel, Indian and fresh meat and produce. To quote the immortal Jake Blues: "This place had got everything!" They do a good job making sure everyone is wearing a mask during this pandemic and I felt like the shops kept their areas clean! For as much traffic is in there, that's no small task. If you're unsure what to try, find the spot with the longest line and give it a try, the locals know their food!! Enjoy!

I love this place! Great atmosphere and great places to eat. I always try new things when I am down town. But some how I always make my way to the Terminal! I recommend anyone who hasn't been? To make a trip here!

If your a foodie, this place wouldn't be new to you.  Definitely one of the places to stop by if your in Philadelphia.  This market houses some of the best food and food related items.  Bassett's Ice Cream, Beiler's bakery, Old City Coffee, Pearls Oyster Bar, MeltCraft and so much more.  These are just the places I frequent.  You can easily spend a whole day here as a destination spot.

Enough cannot be said about reading terminal. It's a one stop shop for fresh produce, seafood, meats, breads, desserts, spices and already cooked meals.  What I just named is only the tip of the iceberg, you have to go and experience this market to really understand. It embodies all of the flavors and foods of the city and it's different backgrounds in one place. Among some of my faves are The salmon platter from the Thai place, Kevin Parker's soul food spot and beiler's doughnuts (but trust me there are so many more goodies). 

Because it is a pretty well known tourist attraction it is extremely busy on the weekends but it also gets busy on weekdays during lunch hours from 11:30am-2pm but everything moves at a good pace and worth any wait. True gem in the city!

The first thing you have to learn about Reading Terminal is No1: Its the best place in Philly to go for high quality specialty food. You literally can get anything you want like a one-stop shop. HOWEVER do not go around lunch time or right after work and NOT expect to stand in line for a long while at any place you go.  
No2: Take a day and just explore the darn place, you'll always miss a cool store, wine shop to new business if you don't take your time at least once.
No#: I demand you to get dessert from the farmers market there or have breakfast brunch at the amish diner thats there. Period. Good luck.

There isn't much to say here, I mean it's McDonald's but a few key takeaways.

1. For a fast food place, my sandwich and coffee took way longer than expected. They only had one or two employees working the grill and one on register. It was morning and the line was pretty long.

2. Coffee was a little too sweet. My egg white McMuffin was on par.

3. Employees weren't super friendly. I'm always friendly with staff and the woman at the counter didn't bother to return the gesture or really acknowledge my existence.
Great variety and a lot of fun.  You can pretty much find anything you are looking for here.
Center city best of everything under one roof. Huge variety of homemade food made from I e and so delicious that you will be back as a regular. Go try it out I guarantee you will be satisfied

This is must when you visit philly so many market vendors from sit on restaurant s & deli's to merchants selling all sorts of items with delicious food from the good pennslyvania amish community it's the center attraction of downtown philly

This place is food heaven!  So many choices to choose from...chicken, fish, beef, pork, veggies, etc. 

They also have other shopping available..clothes, accessories, jewelry, etc!   

If you have a hard time making up your mind...this may not be the place for you! 

Great place to grab lunch or hangout with friends and not have to get the same thing.
Great customer service here.  Also love the fact that they foster relationships with their customers.  This sets them apart from other locations.
Just . . Don't go here. . Especially if you don't wanna get ripped off . . They skimp on the meat like a lot :/

A visual spectacle that offers a variety of food options to satisfy all palates. While the crowds can be overwhelming to some, its a rite of passage to enjoy some of the best treasures that Philly has to offer. Beiler's has become a staple for fresh doughnuts. DiNic's keeps accumulating awards for their excellent roast pork sandwiches. The one caveat would be to avoid the Chinese food options since you can go a couple of blocks away to Chinatown to get better (and cheaper) fare.

Enjoy!

Just grazed my way through the Reading Market if you are from out of town it is a must stop for your time in Philly.  We had breakfast in the Dutch Eating Place again and if you don't know what scrapple is have some with an egg or the Apple Dumpling the place is the best.  If you miss breakfast try a roast pork sandwich from De nici's another city favorite plus the hundred of other food and merchants spellings their wears at the market.  I am gladI live here in Philly.

I am very partial to Pike's Market, which, of all the markets I have been to, is the most colossal and impressive of its kind. For perspective, I have also been to the French Market in New Orleans, Findlay Market in Cincinnati, City Market in Charleston, and Faneuil Hall Marketplace in Boston, among other notable markets. 

Reading (pronounced "redding") Terminal Market is definitely unique to Philadelphia and worth a visit. It's like Pike's Market, but on a smaller scale. It's a very large warehouse space has offers aisles upon aisles of specialty foods vendors. They also have a farmer's market section in one corner of the market. They also house a fresh seafood market and several delis. There's 1 florist shop in Reading Market and 2 sit down restaurants inside the market. Most other food vendors either do not offer seats or just have limited bar seating. 

Some things I like about Reading Terminal Market include the large sitting area in near the middle of the market. Furthermore, they have complimentary cell phone charging lockers. That's right lockers. You can lock your mobile devices up and shop around while it charges.
Very good! I got the chicken masala roll, mango lassi, and masala chai. The food was spiced and full of bursting flavor. I highly recommend mixing the white and red sauces together!
Good chicken

I have to say I'm jealous that I don't live in Philadelphia so I can visit this place more often. Or maybe that's good for my wallet. From groceries, to restaurants, snacks to crafts you can find it here. It's a little confusing to navigate if you're new to the place. It's almost like a maze and it can be overwhelming. I got some really delicious cookies from the 4th street cookie company. I'll definitely come back here when I'm in town again.

I had bookmarked Humpty's Dumplings such a long time ago that I had honestly forgotten it even existed until I walking past it on a Wednesday afternoon. I'm not in Queen Village too often so I figured this was the perfect opportunity for me to check it out. 

The establishment is pretty small so just a few steps in the door and I was at the counter. It was then that I noticed a sign for "$1 dumplings on Wednesdays" - woo! Am I glad I stopped in or what!

The guy behind the counter was super friendly. I asked him for recommendations on which dumplings to get and he was quick to respond with simple and helpful feedback. 

I ended up bringing four different dumplings home with me - Buffalo chicken, cheesesteak, honey chipotle chicken and pizza. The first three are on their favorites menu while the last one is one of their current specials. After selecting your dumplings, you are given a choice of fried or steamed. 

I thought all of the dumplings were delicious, but the cheesesteak was definitely my favorite! Philly, represent! :D The buffalo chicken and honey chipotle chicken were close seconds, while the pizza was just okay. In my opinion, it tasted more just like a cheese dumpling than a pizza dumpling. 

All in all, I'm very content with my experience at Humpty's Dumplings. I probably won't be rushing back here anytime soon simply because I'd like to avoid the fried food temptations. However, for those days that I'm not counting cals, I'll return for some cheesesteak dumplings!

My review for this place is LONG overdue, and I know it is only going to be a drop in the sea of the 3,240 reviews this place already has. *Note that this place is called the READING terminal market, yet it is pronounce REDDING. 

This Market is nestled between 11th & 12th Ave and Arch Street. There are several entry and exit points, one being right by the Hilton. 

This place is a foodie lovers paradise and overload!!! There is virtually something for EVERY palate. Want something fresh, hot, sweet, creamy, chocolate ears, something loaded with carbs to indulge your senses...they've got you covered here!!!

They have a LARGE produce section filled with an array of healthy options, I didn't spend much time in this section but everything appeared to be in peak freshness/ripeness. 

There is a LARGE selection of fresh meats (steaks, roasts, ribs etc) and what seems to be an even larger selection of mouth watering deli meats to choose from. We are talking stacks of piled high meats ready to be consumed in between two slices of bread, topped on a cracker with a cheese spread (that they have plenty of) or to just snack on a lone. 

If you do not want to make your own sandwich, they got you covered as well. You can walk over to another vendor that sells gut busting sandwiches such as: chicken Caesar, fresh mozzarella, chicken caprese, Pompeii etc. The sandwiches can either be purchase on loaves (better have a big appetite) or a more hand held option like ciabatta. A few steps over and you can purchase one of their ridiculously HUUUUUUUGE philly cheesesteaks, where they prepare the food in front of you. They also put on a show while they make it, which is kind of cool. Don't feel limited to just a traditional cheesesteak, you can get a chicken cheesesteak, pizza cheesesteak, broccoli rabe, BLT cheesesteak and on. You can also choose the cheese, be it provolone, American, or the east coats favorite cheese sauce. 

Next to the philly cheesesteak counter, they have pasta sheets that they will cut to your preference, while you wait for your food. You can pay at the same register. The pasta we purchased was seasonal, Pumpkin Pasta and it was terrific. 

If you meander to the left of the cheesesteak counter, they have a variety of comfort foods ranging from lasagna, spaghetti, Stromboli's, chicken parmigiana, and meatballs. 

Once you have quelled your hunger pangs, head over to their bakery section. There you can load up with cannoli's (filled to order), cheesecakes, torts, individual sliced cakes. Ever wonder what a chocolate shaped foot with almond toes, or Van Gogh's ear tasted like??? The also have a variety of caramel apples, plain, dipped in chocolate AND caramel or overloaded with chocolate chunks, marshmallows and drizzled in peanut butter. 

There are plenty of other delectable delights in this jam packed market, too many to list. Come hungry and with plenty of ambition. You could easily spend hours, if not a whole day here. Lines can be long at times, and some counters require you to take a number. It is worth the wait and weight ;)
A must when in Philadelphia!!  Trust me you will not be disappointed. The assortment of food is unbelievable.  The food at DiNic's, speechless.  Best pulled pork sandwich I've ever had
Has everything you want in food. All varieties, quick, and the price is not expensive.
Something for everyone here. Southern fried chicken, breakfast bagels, crepes, smoothies, Italian pastries, so much to choose from. Fantastic experience.

A little uncomfortable during COVID-19: usually crowded, about 50-50 on masks (both the visitors and the businesses), and there's a large central dining court where no one wears a mask while they eat.

Other than that, some good selections and a good place to visit for souvenirs. I would definitely go back when it's a bit safer

This is a must stop every time you are either passing through or staying in Philly for any amount of time.

No matter what your mood, there is always something here for you, with endless options for sweet and savory foods.

For the best savory bite, you should head over to Tommy DiNic's for the Roast Pork Sandwich with broccoli rabe and provolone. Featured on Man vs. Food as well as his show on the Best Sandwiches in America, it really is an amazing sandwich and worth the sometimes huge line in this chaotic market.

My favorite sweet things include The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company right by the entrance, serving hot, freshly baked excellent cookies, and the Apple Dumpling from Dutch Eating Place, which is so sweet it will make you shake. Don't forget to try Hope's Cookies also though - located all the way in the back, they have some really amazing cookies and tons of other chocolates and sweets.

Whether you want some authentic Philly eats, or you are one of those Chinese families that must eat Chinese food no matter where you are, or you want an overload of excellent dessert options, Reading Market's got you covered.

My flight was delayed and it was pretty late so many restaurants were closed. I noticed this place had put up most of their food and began cleaning. However, I walked over and asked were they selling some of their food that was out and they stated yes.
Customer service was awesome considering they were about to close and trying to get home I'm sure. I ordered a wrap and yogurt and they both were great.

Overall this place is perfect if you're with a few people who all have a taste for different things. You can also go for rare grocery items and higher quality meats and cheeses. There are lots of vendors and it smells amazing in there!

When I come to Philadelphia, for some strange reason I have a hard time finding places to eat. One place I can always rely on is Good Ole Wendy's. During my recent visit I ordered a 10 pc chicken nugget combo. The nuggets were dry, spongey, and lukewarm. The fries were soggy. When I ordered the nuggets the employee asked "what's yo sauce!" I was caught off guard and confused for a moment and I said what?, "what's yo sauce !!" she demanded.  then it clicked. I said my sauce is Sweet and sour!, and then she stated "what's yo soda!!"   My soda is Coke!! I replied. 

Btw I think this is near where Will smith grew up.
One of my favorite markets in the city! Such a fun place to take friends from out of town on the weekend. All the vendors are great and there's such a good variety of food

Almost every big city has a market like Reading Terminal. It's great because as a visitor to the city, you can explore a variety of cuisines in one location.

The market is located very close to the convention center, which makes it very convenient for breakfast, lunch or a quick snack. Although it is extremely crowded at lunchtime, The vendors seem to know how to get people through the line and moving. There is a decent sized seating area, but during the lunch hour it may be challenging to find a seat for more than one person.

All sorts of food can be found here from Dutch to Italian, Chinese, Korean and Mediterranean. There are cheesesteak vendors, along with stands offering fresh produce, baked goods, and meat. The famous roast pork sandwich at DiNic's and Bassett's delicious ice cream are both located here as well.

This market is great for groups as the variety of offerings will surely appease even the pickiest eaters and the price points are rather reasonable.

Good and dense-packed market in a central location. Similar to Seattle's Pike's Place or St Lawerence Market in Toronto but I have heard that it is on par with LA's Grand Central Market.

We sampled food from a few food stalls and I enjoyed walking through the market. Definitely, a must-try place to check out and get several bites to eat.

This place was heaven. So many variety of food in such a compact area. The only problem is that there are so many people here during lunch hours. That and the fact that it closes early than I'm used to. There is such a diverse range of food that I'm pretty sure you can find what you want just by walking around for 15 minutes. Chinese, cajun, soul food, BBQ, dessert, breakfast, candy, groceries, there is just so much to this little terminal. There is also a seating area that had a piano and live music. It was very cute.

Tends to be crowded, be forwarned. It is great for all sorts of things. Highly recommend the Grilled cheese place. Nice people and excellent food. Get you meats and veggies here. Fresher and a better deal than the grocery store.
Crowded but so awesome! Prepare to pay for parking as well. There isn't a food that you couldn't find in this place! Yup, you may leave a few pounds heavier! But damn everything is delicious!
A great taste of everything that's good about food in Philadelphia.From soul food to fresh meats to sweets to vegan to the best Jewish deli I never get bored I discover something new every day

This place is insane. So crowded and hectic so be prepared. I would advise to go on off-peak hours so you can enjoy walking around and looking at things. I went an hour before they closed on a Saturday and it was still crazy. 

However, they do have some great looking food. I wish I could of tried it all! Getting our food took so long and we only had about 15-20 minutes before closing (6pm) and vendors were already closing up shop.

You can park in the parking structure for 2 hours for $4 if you spend $10 and get it validated!

Overall a fun place to browse for food, drink, and local products. We ate roast pork at Tommy Dinic's, got some flavored banana puddings, and a cheesesteak stuffed pretzel from Miller's Twist. There's everything from baked goods, seafood, beeswax products, chocolates, cheesesteaks, meats and produce..
The list goes on. I've been here twice (weekends) and it's always packed. Even on the off hours (3pm). If you want to make a trip here make sure you do it before 6pm as they close early!
If you are in Philadelphia this is a must see market. Could not stop taking pictures and sampling all the different foods.

My to go spot here in Philly. I'm new here and haven't had the best of luck food wise. I'm from the south and love foods with lots of flavor and good quality. Honeygrow hasn't disappointed me yet. I love their CYO stir fry options and am looking forward to trying one of their salads in the near future. I would recommend their Sweet Soy Five Spice with your favorite proteins and noodle selection. I usually choose ground Turkey, chicken, mushrooms, red onion, kale, and cilantro tossed with their egg white noodles. The only thing is their green beans can be a little too fresh for my liking and not cooked enough. So I wouldn't try that option again.

Slowest Wendy's I've ever been to. There always a long slow line here. The only time I've never seen a line is when this Wendy's is closed. Avoid this Wendy's unless you like waiting 20-30 minutes plus for your order.

Love this place! It's good for breakfast, lunch and even to pick up something for dinner. I am giving it 4 stars rather than 5 because I wish they would open up a little earlier than 8. Not all people start work at 9, so it makes getting breakfast there a little tough since I start work early.
Love this place in downtown Philly! You can find fresh fruits and vegetables and homemade goodies. There are restaurants and stands.

Who doesn't love the Reading Terminal Market?  It's big, crowded, noisy, and full of variety.  It could do with more seating and I'm sure that not every vendor is perfect, but this place is an amazing resource for the city and for anyone working next door at the convention center.
My favorite place in USA. If youre a foodie, you need to visit here asap. I travel philly few times per year just to indulge here few things, Pretzels, Doughnuts, crepes, hoggies etc etc.
So many choices. It little ThaiMarket is still my favorite place. Curry salmon bowl. BBQ chicken skewers and chicken spring rolls are so good.

Pretty awesome, especially in the middle of the city.  You can find anything you want.  Candles, fresh produce, fresh seafood, hoagies, wine,  beer, Italian food...the list goes on & on.  

There are several cheesesteak places....of course this is Philly.  

There are pictures of the Philly skyline & hand made stationary available.   Most of the fresh seafood shops/stalls offer to cook your purchases for you.  There are several cheese shops & Mediterranean shops. 

Everything looks very appetizing.   The Italian shops smelled wonderful.   Some things had reasonable prices (produce) while others seemed a little high (the seafood).

The decor of this place is wonderful and a fantastic upscale-casual place that is well-priced. Really loved the macaroni croquette and the house wines are not bad. Only issue was the Korean BBQ Pork Belly burger - I felt it was a bit dry and was lacking in sauce and was overall disappointing. However, the service was good and my friend's burger came out well. Definitely stop by if you're in town but ask for extra sauce with the pork belly burger.

Nice spot to visit if you are ever in Philly. Close to other shops. There are places to sit inside of the market. There are various shops that sell everything from chocolate to cheesesteaks. Well worth visiting.

Convenient location, awesome food and great price! I definitely recommend any of the Kati rolls. I've tried the chicken platter and chicken biryani platter, both delicious. You can choose to add sauce to the top of both platters.

I thought of giving 5 star for this, but poor customer service we always come here for the food, the food is really great and I asked for the extra sauce for panner the cash register was rude to me and telling me it's gonna be extra charge, even if you guys charge me that's fine, but please be nice to the customer. Sat 09/21/2019

Thanks!

Bright Now Dental in Newtown PA scams you if you sign up for financing.  I've been scammed.  They damaged a tooth so I stopped using their services and they continued to take money out of my account after the services were paid in full.

If you come to Philly you gotta visit the Reading Terminal Market. For a large selection of great food, amazing coffee and some really nice boutique local shops. I visit here with my wife at least twice a month just to hang out and have a blast!

So busy. So many choices. But it's a must experience when visiting Philly! I only had time to try one place - I don't remember the name but it was BBQ chicken. The chicken was pretty good and mac and cheese was even better! Entree + 2 sides was $9.75 comparable to most meals at Reading Terminal. 

Reading Terminal Market also has groceries, fresh fruits and veggies, deli meats, fish, cheese, etc. It gets super crowded during prime lunch time ~noon. The first time I ate lunch here was around 2-3 PM so it wasn't that crowded. I went the following day (Friday) around noon and the lines were soooo long. Didn't have time to wait so I couldn't try another booth :(

The place is have breakfast before going sightseeing in Philly.
You can spend the day here.
We ordered breakfast from the Dutch place. Blueberries pancakes ( large stack) the serving is large enough for two. We also ordered a western omelet it came with some buttery rye bread. Our bill was less than $20.
You must visit this market when you come to Philadelphia.

RTM is a philadelphia staple. You can find all types of cuisine, bakeries/coffee shops, grocery, small shops, and even a diner. Whatever you are in the mood for you can find it here. If you are lost go to their 12th and Filbert entrance and speak to the front desk staff. There are also copies of the RTM map. Take the map and explore the whole place. You can easily spend all day here just eating your way through Philadelphia. 

Keep in mind lunch hours here are insane. You have people coming here during their work lunch and then the hundreds of thousands of tourists who are in town as well. It is busy busy BUSY. Plan accordingly. 

The entire front left side of the market (the side along 12th and Arch) is closed on Mondays. Welcome to the city!
So many diverse and delicious options for food, groceries, and dessert. Definitely walk around and see what's all available before making a choice even though you really can't go wrong with much!

Reading Terminal Market is a great place to eat and see, the only cons were, it is always very very packed, and another is, people, (not the employees), are very rude!! 


    Besides that it is a great place to eat and see!

Hello everyone. As you may know, I often find myself patronizing the restaurants of the Philadelphia area when I go to visit my lovely granddaughter. Another place that was her idea. I am well over 60 so you may call me old fashioned however the atmosphere of the establishment put a sour taste in my mouth before my meal had reached my taste buds. To accommodate the anti-social millennial we order on big screens and dont talk to a single REAL person. Very confusing if you are not up to date with latest technology and forgot bifocals in the car. I will say that there was a good amount of options even though I did not understand. So after I placed my order through the possibly sentient computer system, I went to pay with cash so that this machine of higher intelligence could not steal my identity . Call me a geezer but I just don't trust like that. I will say that this was on WEDNESDAY at 2 OCLOCK PM so definitely not a "lunch rush" but for some reason the staff was sweating into my food. Seemed like they were understaffed. The girl at the register was patient at first as she explained everything to the old woman (me) who was very confused. However as her stress grew her politeness declined and she grew very impatient. I was ready to be disappointed yet again by my granddaughters lapse in judgement however when I received my food I was pleasantly surprised. The portions were very large and all in all it seems like a good way to eat relatively healthy. However, as I mentioned previously my granddaughter who has very poor judgment (god bless her heart) ordered a VERY spicy meal that she was NOT AWARE would be so spicy. Not the brightest she was in tears vetween each bite. A worker came up and asked her if she was okay I am not kidding. Wow. All in all this place is a decent eatery only losing 2 stars for the atmosphere and the fact that I was straining myself on the toilet for hours the next morning. I called my granddaughter to tell her I love her because I thought I might be dying. 


God Bless Everyone
-Marg :-)
Love this place I try to always visit the cookie company!

I absolutely love the Reading Terminal! It has so many great places to eat, pick up sweets, fresh produce, fresh meat and seafood! I love walking around each time to discover new shops. I always find something new to bring home. I love all the bakeries!
One must go here if you are visiting Philadelphia for a weekend. The Food court is an endless variety of food  and drink. Id say start at Reading  and game plan what you will do for the weekend.

I absolutely love takeout from this restaurant. The food is delicious and there's plenty of it. You could really split some of their meals with someone else. It's a great quick meal if you don't feel like heading out for dinner!

I had a whole Saturday afternoon in Philly alone for my first time and Reading Terminal Market was on my list!

I carefully planned out my visit, and after a bit of a struggle finding parking, I made it inside! I was here the first weekend after Philly had begun to reopen so things were a little weird, lots of random open space but this is the set up they deemed necessary for the Covid world. 

My biggest disappointment was the fact that I was only in town for a short while and staying at a hotel so I couldn't buy any of the amazing meats and veggies that I passed as I strolled through. I did pick up a few donuts from Beiler's to split with my boyfriend and a really good pretzel-wrapped hot dog from Miller's Twist. Everything was delicious! 

I wish I would have ordered a sandwich from one of the vendors but I felt like I'd already eaten enough. I was slightly overwhelmed and everywhere I turned there something that looked or smelled utterly delicious. This spot will forever be on my list of places to visit when I'm in the area!

If you're a foodie, YOU HAVE TO VISIT Reading Terminal Market! Options, upon options, upon more options! I loved visiting Reading Terminal Market for the first time on my trip to Philly. I wish my stomach was big enough to visit every place, maybe one day right? This is for sure a staple in Philly. I will be back very soon to try more FOOD!
Great place to sample a variety of food AND drink.

I just moved to Philly a month ago and I have tried a lot of bad pizza.  There is a pizza place on every block.  So, I drove to Fishtown to try "5 star pizza.
Congratulations, I give it 5 stars too.  The place is worth the trip.
I am always craving this pizza. It is so so good and the people are very friendly. Great spot if you are in the area (or even worth the drive to try it out). Best tomato pie!!

Border Springs Farms Lamb is a new spot at Reading Terminal Market or at least I have never seen it before. I was so excited when I passed by and saw they have lamb burgers. I had to take a double take and never moved beyond the cashier until I ordered.

I have been searching for a mouthwatering lamb burger for sometime. The few places that I had ordered the lamb burgers from in southern Jersey & Philly left me disappointed. They were often overcooked, bland or the toppings did not adequately compliment the burger. Well, I need look no further because this place has won over my tastebuds. So much so that I came here 2 days in a row just to order the lamb burger.

I know you asking so Michelle what makes their burgers so good. Why, THANK YOU for asking.. I think I will let these adjectives do the talking: moist, juicy, succulent, flavorful, hearty, lip smacking & finger licking good. I think that sums it up. It wasn't just the burger but the wheat roll/bun, arugula and the sauce that worked harmoniously to make such a powerful impact in taste.

So, my recommendation is if you want a good lamb burger try this place, you will not be disappointed.

Food - 4 (good for the price, got Chicken Briyani)  
Service - 3 (had to ask for food, long wait)
Price - 5 (cheapest around the neighborhood, except Chipotle)

So average is 4

I tried Beilers, Millers pretzel place, and DiNics. There are lot of different vendors, plenty of variety. The market does need some renovation. It is a bit gritty looking compared to the food halls in Boston and Chicago. Some of the vendors were not open. Dining was outdoor only. Overall, a solid stop.
Great place to stop and have lunch, when entertaining out of town guests.

Great place to visit when in Philly! Anything you have a taste for, they have it. Miss tootsies now has a spot in there which I'm happy about. They have sweets like delicious cookies, Cajun food, soul food, cheesesteaks, basically anything you can think of. The atmosphere is great and lively. I'd highly recommend!

this was one of highlights during my trip to philly. it's a market with such a huge variety of food. i tried dinics, the amish donuts, and a pastrimi place and all of them were super yummy. a must-see-eat-visit place when in philly
Great place to find almost any cuisine you cN think of or any meal breakfast, lunch, or dinner. It's been said you could eat several meals a day there for a month and still not hit every eTing place

The different option on the menu are amazing. This food is so unique and every bite is more delicious than the one before. The strawberry cheesecake dumplings are like nothing I've ever had before! 10/10 recommend

Reading Terminal Market is wonderland of food, smells and traditions that reflect the diverse population of Philly. 

You want a cheesesteak? No problem - there's at least 3 places to have one (but maybe consider roast park with broccoli rave and sharp provolone instead). Traditional east coast deli? They've got it. Authentic eats from all comers of the globe including Peking Duck, Thai, Indian, Greek, Puerto Rican and so many more? Most definitely. 

And of course don't forget poles of produce, fresh meats, whole fish, freshly ground spices and to-die-for cheese counters. Add in freshly pressed juices, local coffee and even a tea stand. It's honestly overwhelming and if I had the proverbial three wishes one of them would be to eat here on demand. 

One of the highlights for many people (myself included) are the Amish vendors who serve up the BEST baked goods, home cooked meals and delicious farm fresh offerings. I couldn't resist donuts from Beilers and you shouldn't either! 

I found the vendors to be friendly without exception and happy to suggest what's best from their offering. Take their recommends and try things you can't get at home. 

I've been to a lot of markets both in the US and abroad and Reading ranks up with the very best. It's well worth a visit. My only regret has to do with being a visitor and not being able to take many things home with me!

This place is so cool. I love the variety and all the options. I got an iced mocha from Old City Coffee. I wish I had studied the menu just a bit longer before ordering because while they were making my drink I noticed a Hot Apple Cider on the menu. I also got a black and white cookie from Famous 4th Street Cookie Co. The ladies working there couldn't have been nicer. And that cookie was one of the best black and white cookies I've ever had. There is also plenty of seating if you get a meal. I grabbed a tuna sandwich from Hershel's East Side Deli. It was packed with tuna! O.K. Produce had plenty to offer, however I found it kind of funny that they were selling Driscoll berries (Californian berries aren't exactly local, but still pretty delicious). Blue Mountain Vineyard and Cellars provides wines for pretty much everyone's taste buds. They even offered me a couple sips of different wines before I made my choice and took a bottle home.
So much fun to explore.  Go with a good appetite and at least twenty bucks to get the most out of the experience.

What's not to like about this place?

As usual, I skipped the scrapple and headed for Rick's and for desert, the Apple Dumplings (with heavy cream) in the Amish corner.  It's fun to walk around, take in the energy and watch all the people.  And each repeat visit is a whole new experience!

This location is fast, friendly, and clean. The service is excellent even during peak hours. It can be very busy during these times but everything was well prepared. 

*Corporate fast food is scientifically proven to be detrimental to your health, but if you're going to eat toxic garbage, chick fil a is one of the best options.

Great place to find a thing your tastebuds are craving for.. had the fried chicken from kevens, ribs from
Another spot and some corn bread and chili cheese dogs.. seating is first come first serve basis, but turn over of people eating are pretty quick.

We came here as tourists on TWO separate occasions- a great spot to eat and try different foods! Our favorites: we got a pastrami and sauerkraut sandwich (AMAZING) from a deli, biscuits with jam and honey butter, a spicy pickle, and chorizo fries! Highly recommend and you should try something from a few different stalls and share with whoever you come with.

The pizza's ok, but it's now three times I've gone during posted hours to order a pie (since they don't take orders over the phone or online) to find the shop closed for some reason or other.  Very disappointing: they need to get their act together.  A business should always be open during posted hours.

This place is awesome!! There are so many cool shops, ranging from flowers to donuts to BBQ to coffee to crepes to fish markets! I absolutely loved walking around in here. We got the crepes and they were great. I'd definitely recommend making a stop! There are a lot of people in tighter spaces so if that's not your thing maybe skip. I loved it!
Always have been satisfied with shopping here you definitely will find meat,poultry,fish ,herbs fruits, veggies and plenty of desserts and restaurants, smoothies ,just go you will be satisfied
Hands down one of the best and most authentic shawarma sandwiches in the city. And I've tried them all. Their spinach pies are also delicious.

I used to hate coming here, even when I would order ahead for curbside because it was just a mess with all the cars. 

Well not this time. There seems to be order now and I love the order ahead. I park in the spot and turn on my flashers and wait less than 15mins. Thee best way to order from Chick Fila is order ahead so you're not waiting long.

I love it here. I love the diversity of people, food, and coffees. It gets a bit too packed and so it's that weird "new kid in the cafeteria" feeling of staring folks down for a table. I hate that feeling - so I never eat in the terminal. That said, every time I go - I enjoy my experience. The last time, I had a veggie gyro (pretty good), snagged a delicious blue mountain coffee, a few beaded bracelets,  and got a little bag of handpicked assorted chocolates and candies as a sweet finish. I really like taking my son here - we love munching on our bag of goodies as we look at all the cool foods. I just make sure that I hold him SUPER tightly - the crazy crowds give it a kid losing Lifetime movie affect.
Great place with a great history. Many different stores offering variety of goods. Quality and price have a good balance. Good people, friendly and polite, respectful to their customers. Thank you.
A hopping place on Saturdays as I finally got to see the wares of the Amish that come here on the weekend.  Rum Raisin ice cream from the Amish stand, is pretty good stuff.

We were driving north and decided to stop in Philadelphia. This is a must-see when you're in the area. They have so many food and dessert options to please even the pickiest eaters.  We weren't starving, so we got some pretzels. The pretzels were super fresh. We went on a Wednesday, and the place was packed. There are a lot of parking options around the area. If you spend $10, you can get your parking validated (it didn't validate the whole thing but took off a couple of dollars).

So many great places in reading terminal it's definitely a one stop shop to grab things to make a meal or even just stopping in to try the great food places inside! Love the rib place by the doughnut shop, dinics roast pork is a must and hersals deli for a great sandwich

Holy cow! This place is massive! 
I honestly wished they had like a map or something to know where everything was. There was a ton of places that were closed or non-existent. Prices were a little higher than expected but there were a lot of goodies! I kinda disliked the fact that some places smelt really bad when walking past and having raw cold fish right across yummy cooked Caribbean food or something was not appealing! But what can we do. I would come back here, but it gets packed fast & very confusing.

4.7/5

So many awesome stores, and great atmosphere/vibe! I love walking around here and checking out all of the different stalls, from different types of honey to different jams to spices (check out The Head Nut) and cooked food. I always end by doing groceries in the back, which are surprisingly decently priced -- and they offer a student discount!

Reading Terminal also has a lot of really cool special events throughout the year to keep a look out for. For example, there was an Ice Cream day recently where many of the stalls served some form of Ice Cream. My favorite was the Filipino food festival. Do be warned that lines tend to be long during these special events, and it gets quite crowded!
This is an awesome place to explore, especially for foodies. Seems like a simple place but you'll spend a minimum of an hour to navigate through.

I love Lalo so so much and bringing me back to food from my childhood is soul healing in more ways than I can articulate. I've had them cater parties, brought out of towners, and introduced all my non Filinpx friends to some new cuisine. I've surely missed eating this delicious and authentic food all lockdown and I'm so excited to come back.

Simply Magical...

This indoor market is remarkable. There are endless aisles lined with everything from baked goods, confections, restaurants and shops. There is truly something for everyone here.

Been to Philly several times and never visited this gem. Most certainly worthy of a day trip. Be sure to visit on a very empty stomach. Do note that the market is mainly comprised of foods. 

Don't make the mistake we made and pay major for parking. Find the lot just across the street and pay for four to five bucks with ten dollar purchase.

Still thinking about this pizza I ate the other night. Perfect spot to grab a slice in fishtown. I came here at around 5:30-6 on a Wednesday. We had to wait a little because they didn't have slices of the special and they cooked one fresh. I walked over to palmer park to sit and they were still hot! Perfect crust, thin but not floppy. The slices were huge, definitely one slice is enough for a normal person, two if you're really hungry. I ended up getting the special white. It had globs of ricotta and garlic with a basil crema. The flavor was magical and the crust was thin and crispy. I highly recommend this pizza to anyone around!

An. Absolute. Must.

MUUUUUST!!! An absolute must visit when in Philly, baby! This public market has everything that your little heart could ever damn desire! Fresh local and exotic produce, high quality meat and seafood, artisan cheeses, fresh baked goods, and an amazing array of different cultural cuisines! Food, food, and more food! So many damn choices that it'll make your head spin. 

All of the stands are from locally owned and family run businesses, making this market even that much more special. Seating is cafeteria style, so you can peruse the market, pick up several food items, and then enjoy some grub right there in the food hall. Aside from food, this market also features several stands with handcrafted jewelry, clothing, souvenir, and more.

Of course, lil' ol' me couldn't purchase something from ever vendor (I damn sure wish I could have though). So, I ended up getting some bbq from Frank's bbq. Ordered a bbq chicken wing plate with mixed veggies, mac n' cheese, and a roll, and it was scrumptious! The chicken wings were super juicy and the mac n' cheese was so lovably cheesy. Can't forget about their yummy banana cornbread! I got one of these for dessert and it was sooo friggin' moist and delicious! I'm dreaming about it now. Frank's is an awesome option if you're looking for a spot to eat at in the market. 

You have to... HAAAAVE to stop by here during your visit to Philly. It's an iconic 125+ year city staple that has so much to offer.

Shacka was a definitely a Yelp find. 
I was in the area and was in the mood for a slice of pizza for lunch so decided to give them a try.
