A small and cozy place with a high top tables where you order and get your food at the counter.  Very simple menu with a pizza of the day and 4 other varieties.  I would say this is one of the reason's  why the slices are so good-focus!

The daily special was a Soppressata (having a moment as a pizza topping) honey & pickled jalapeño-amazing!  Only shame is that it won't be a regular on the menu.  Also, got the cheese and Tomato Pie slices for later which were both excellent.  They were out of Pepperoni.  Gentlemen behind the counter were friendly & service minded.

Semi busy around 1 on a Wed.  My new must stop for pizza when in Philly!

A staple of Philly - amazing indoor food hall/groceries/clothes. It's an eclectic mix of everything but the food you'll find in here is super good. There's food from all over the world so everyone can find something you like. Don't go on Sundays because a lot of the vendors are Amish and don't come in that day so you'll be missing out!

I love reading terminal. I was recently in the neighborhood and stopped in and got pastries from flying monkey (so delicious!), a vegan Reuben which was AMAZING and a chicken sandwich for a friend which he loved. I also often buy produce here at really great prices. The atmosphere and people watching here is the best. This is a true Philly gem.

Heard about this spot a few years ago and finally got to try it.......... I'm from Long Island and this ain't no NY style pizza don't get the two confused this not it period... I sent my homie a pic of this and he replied "I hope u not about to eat that" this place is another one of Philly hyped up spots. if u want Ny style pizza go to NY or Giovanni's on chestnut st Best pizza I've tried in Philly

Love this place! Great market with lots of stores and vendors -- you can buy almost anything here: cookies, pastries, desserts, sandwiches, meats, deli meat, candles, mugs, coffee, etc. 

I love the candles from the Bee Natural candle shop -- they're reasonably priced hand poured candles in a variety of amazing scents. 

Only reason for the four stars is that it's always packeddd, which isn't really a knock on the market itself, but I just had to throw that in there. Would definitely stop by if you're visiting the Philly area!
The best local market in the city with both local fresh food grocers and great food restaurants.

Best place for Indian fusion food ever! Drive all the way from jersey most weekends just to pick up. They maintain the taste and the quality to the max!! Must visit if you around. Also open very late.

Five stars for the amazing stands it has, the great produce, and how fun it can be to go there. Not every stand is five stars (or even close, really), but in the end, it is one of the best in-door markets in any city in the entire United States. It's not just a tourist attraction, if you ask me. My favorite stand is DeNic's.

If you are planning to visit Philly,  please stop by here! This is definitely a stop you want to make. The wide variety of restaurants will cater to multiple tastebuds.  

This market is one of America's largest and has been running since the 1890's. You can dine in and shop for your next meal for locally sourced meats and seafood. You can find produce, cheeses, chocolate,  and arts and crafts all under one roof. 

I recommend you take your time and walk through the whole place before deciding on a meal, because everything looks so delicious it will be hard to decide.

Okay this place is a MUST visit if you are a tourist! You really don't even suspect that this place even exists from looking outside on the street, but the second that you walk in, there is a huge labyrinth of food stalls and vendors. Every kind of food that you can think of is offered in this little market! From breakfast, to desserts, from Dutch to Thai, to fresh pressed juices, cajun, to seafood, this place is a foodie's PARADISE. We spent hours wandering around the market trying a little bit of everything! We got fantastic breakfast poboys at the cajun place. Full baguette, 3 eggs, and choice of meat for less than $5. It served as my breakfast and lunch! I knew that black and white cookies were a big thing in the area, and I got a fantastic one at Famous 4th street Cookie Company. (Pro tip: they have a touch screen where you can sign up for emails and get your first cookie free!). We got a huge jug of fresh pressed mango and raspberry lemonade from Lancaster Country Dairy for less than $4! So fresh and refreshing! We basically just went around picking up a little of this and that and trying out all the great things they had to offer, to the point that we were absolutely stuffed. They also have lots of stalls with great gift options as well! Do not pass up on this place!

I've got a real soft spot in my heart for Chick-Fil-A.
As a fast food establishment, it really stands out in terms of quality.  The standard chicken sandwich, garnished with the two pickles, will definitely satisfy your craving for a chicken sandwich that has been disciplined in the fires of a fryer and the intense demographic surveys they must have done to come up with such a fulfilling flavor.  Don't get me wrong - This is not high class, healthy cuisine...but it beats the heck out of Taco Bell, McDonald's, etc.

Chick-Fil-A's shakes are really great.  I am a sucker for the cookies n' cream.

Hell, even breakfast at Chick-Fil-A is good.  Fried chicken on a biscuit with hash browns and OJ?  Sounds horrifically unhealthy but it is damned good.

The cons- they aren't open on Sunday.  This is problematic because it seems that I start to crave Chick-Fil-A whenever I pass by one on a Sunday...must be that "you want what you can't have" thing acting up.
Not the best quality but has variety of food.

Possibly, maybe, heaven?  I've been to a lot of public markets. Quite simply, none of them compare to this place. All the good stuff you normally get, without the preciousness of the SF Ferry Building and or the contrived grittiness of Pike Place. Then, add in the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants and restaurants, which are simply incomparable. If you visit Philly, don't miss it. Hell, if you visit the east coast, don't miss it.
Proud to support the vendors the make RTM possible. Glad to hear it's now opened on Sundays too.
Ordered 4 stripes of chicken tenders combo and only got 3. So mad... Do not deserve a one star!!

Know this: it'll be slammed full of people & busy when you visit. Once you get over that, prepare to be wowed by the selection of freshly prepared food - everything from sweet treats, Asian-inspired dishes, fresh seafood, Japanese, BBQ, etc. A must-stop in Philly.
A historic site with many options to choose from. This place could keep you trying new places for months!

Worst nightmare as delivery driver came here to pick up thru drive thru and was rudely told by a teenage girl employee to wait for 2 walk-ins customers in front of me at drive thru! Almost hit them that's really dangerous for doing business for drive thru only. And by the time they finished and still blocking the pick up windows and later I was told the order for customer was cancelled after 15 min wait!

Honeygrow has been my go to for lunch and dinner the past few months.  I'm a fan of the red coconut curry with shrimp.  I've never really explored other than that menu item, but I'm sure the other stir fry options are great as well.  The rice noodles are usually tasty and good with the exception of 1/5 occurrences where they were trying a new noodle supplier.  I was glad to see they went back to the original supplier.  There was also an instance where they were out of noodles and rice which I had to unfortunately had to leave without ordering anything.  These situations were not the norm from my experience but they have happened in the past 2 months.

I do recommend checking your order before you leave though because I have missing or wrong items.

Overall, the food is fresh, tasty, and very cleanly!  So this place is a thumbs up.

I had the fruit cup and the fruit so fresh and flavorful.  Special recognition needs to go to the staff. Every single person was friendly, helpful and efficient. This little place makes PHL a much nicer experience for any tired traveler.

If you need the best Amish bacon and deli meats and cheeses and pickles and salads and all that go to the hat like deli next to brokers donuts which are the best yeastie donuts in the city. iovine bros for produce 
And the juice ladies and the crepes and the ice cream and the oysters and the Cajun gator and turtle gumbo and seriously it's all good just go!!!!

Everything looks nice....in a nice location.....food is subpar.  To sum it up?  A nice tourist trap.

This place has tons and tons of different types of restaurants inside (Indian, Middle Eastern, Philly Cheesesteak, gelato, etc).

If you sample anything from here your illusion will disappear...and you'll walk out wondering why you bothered coming.

4.25* for the visual aspects and entertainment.
2* for the food.

A wild variety of options for a wild variety of people. Beware of Sundays though, as some of the best shops are closed. I was almost overwhelmed by the mirage of options around me. Everything smelled like spices and olives and meat. I can't wait to be back!

This place is fantastic! While the various meat counters are pretty gross and off-putting, I was very happy to see so many fresh produce vendors, many of which were specializing in locally-grown and organic produce. I really enjoyed the pianist in the center area and listened to him play while I ate, which was a real treat.

There's only 1 all-veg restaurant, but most restaurants offer at least one or two veg options, so when you combine all the options together, it's a sizeable vegetarian menu. I was particularly impressed that one cheesesteak place had a big photo sign advertising their "100% vegan cheesesteaks", which appeared to be the only vegan item on the menu aside from the fries. Unfortunately, they don't have vegan cheese....yet!

The Chinese places had various fried rice and noodle dishes and the sushi place had several vegan sushi options. While I wasn't particularly impressed with Basic 4, it's nice to have an all-veg restaurant there.
Great food, drinks and friendly staff who is knowledgeable and passionate about their product.

The employees here were extremely polite and the service was great compared to other fast food restaurants. The manager and staffs came by to ask "How's everything?" several times by the guests table. For me this is rarity in fast food chain restaurants.

Love the decor and feel of this place. Came for brunch and it was okay.
Pulled BBQ duck sandwich was decent. Couldn't tell it was suck because the BBQ/sloppy joe sauce was so powerful.i like the soft brioche bun. Fries were nothing special but you get a lot. $13.50 is not really wort it.
Huevos rancheros was good, not very big. Shredded pork was delicious. Salsa and toppings were simpler than other huevos I've had. Crispy chips.
Service was okay. I wonder why many tables got complimentary sticky buns around us, but our big table didn't. I should have asked.
Overall, I'd come back to drink, but maybe not brunch.

I love chipotle, but unfortunately when I visited this location (which will be my last) I ordered just a bowl of chicken and rice. I checked my order before I left luckily, and I was horrified at what I saw. THE ENTIRE ORDER WAS COLD, there was barely any chicken and the chicken that was there was scraps from the bottom of the pan and then they just covered the rest of the bowl with rice. I asked the lady who was working that day if there was any way I could get extra chicken or refund the order and she said "I can get you the number to call for a refund but I don't know it". I asked to speak to a manager and he also said he would grab me the number because he didn't know it off the top of his head . After about 20 minutes there was no return from either one of them with the number I should call. They offered no solution to solving my complaint. Customer service and food quality are horrible at this location and I highly recommend against going here. None of the employees know what they are doing and they have no idea how to problem solve or to help a customer in need. I would give 0 stars if I could.

Amazing!!! Just moved to philly and came to this place randomly. I got the tikka masala and the paneer masala. Delicious. It is definitely comparable to that famous Kati roll place in NYC. I will definitely be coming back.

This chipotle is terrible, they never have food ready and can't order in person. What kind of restaurant won't let you order in person. I want to see it being made like all the other chipotles. Hope everyone here gets fire

What a fantastic market for lunch or dinner and to shop for great meats, poultry, fresh bacon, fruits and vegetables. It's very similar to the ones in Columbus, Seattle and Milwaukee. I love all the choices of fast but delicious offerings from appetizers to desserts and beverages. There are many areas to sit indoors and today they had the Chinese New Year celebration with 2 lion dancing and a very long dragon to ward off evil spirits  and bring in a prosperous happy and healthy new year of the rat 2020. 

There were stores selling trinkets, kitchen ware, essential oils and fresh homemade soaps. You can definitely spend a good 2 hours browsing around.

There was only one store that was not in business and it was a soul food snack shop. 

Restrooms and places to just sit and browse were available too. It's difficult to navigate a wheelchair or a buggy but you can.

Why in the world does Vegas not have a market like this!? 

When visiting Philly a trip to the Reading Terminal Market is an absolute necessity. Perusing all the aisles will make you hungry so be sure to bring your appetite. 

There are too many great food stalls to name but just know that whichever ones you choose will leave you feeling happy. I tried a number of different spots and each one was better than the one before it. 

It gets crowded on weekends, so plan accordingly.

This place is a hidden gem in Philadelphia. I am surprised that more people are not talking about it. The real reason why we came is because of the review by barstool. I popped in at 4:30 on a Saturday in December. Here is my review:

Service: 
- excellent service. Answered all of my questions before placing an order
- I came before the start of dinner, however it was still a 45 minute wait. I did not mind as that gave me time to explore the area. 
- no phone number to call. Just walk up to the window and place your order. Found this slightly inconvenient as I wanted to call to make sure they were open before making the trip. 
- very nice individual. All of them complied with COVID protocols. 
- when I went to pick up my order, they saw me waiting in line and asked me to come to the front to pick it up. I did not think they would remember me, but they did and saved me 10-15 minutes of waiting.

Food: 
The pizza is a solid 9.3. My crust was a little burnt but I know some people prefer that. Very thin and very good ingredients used to make it.
- fair price for a pizza pie. I think it was $24 for a pie
- wish they had more varieties or toppings, but oh well.

Ambience:
- N/A
Always love reading terminal. There's an endless amount of options. My only suggestion is to get more than 1 working ATM but very nice most places accept cards now due to the pandemic.

Have had continuously good experience ls at the reading terminal market.  All the food stands have excellent food, I've particularly enjoyed picking up fresh ingredients for recipes at home.  My only wish is that it would be easier to navigate and that there was more seating!

Was in Philly for the weekend and we happened to stop by the first day. Loved it so much we had to come back the second day. The only thing is that I wish they were open longer! From Philly Cheesesteaks, pretzels, coffee, they got it all! Would 100% come back here if I was in the city.

I've ordered twice now in 2 weeks. The first time I ordered via yelp and walked down to pick it up. I did have a hard time finding this place but it's just around the corner on 16th not directly on Market. My food wasn't ready yet so I kind of hung out and waited, which was perfectly fine. Servers were very friendly while I waited and I noticed the dining room and open kitchen were very clean. When I got back to the office I was shocked to see how much food it actually is, no way could I finish the whole thing. I thought the chicken was moist, the hummus was great and the vermicelli rice was excellent. Such a variety of toppings I felt like I chose them all!
Now on to today, I ordered again because I loved it so much the first time. I will admit I got it delivered because it was FAR too hot to walk outside today. This time I was a little disappointed with the food. I got it the exact same as last time but the chicken was dry, the rice was all clumpy and the sauces were lacking. So I'm pretty 50/50 on this place, I'll probably go back but it will not be soon..

This is one of my favorite things about living in Center City! The market has fresh produce (at ridiculously low prices), Metropolitan Bakery has amazing bread, and Farm Fresh Produce (I think that's what it's called) has fabulous local/organic/yummy/unusual stuff. I try to do as much of my grocery shopping here as I can--usually go weekly after work. There are also a couple of great places to get fresh (local) meat and good fish. Love this place!

This place is amazing.  Busy indoor marketplace located right in the center of the city that has every type of cuisine and all types of little shops.  Most of the places offer fast service since it's a hot spot for people to go on their lunch break.  

Reminds me a lot of Pike Place market in Seattle and puts grand central market in NYC to shame. Definitely put this on your list of places to checkout if you're visiting from out of town.

POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE

Good food. Service is a little confusing. They announced my order but no one heard it. On enquiring about it, the lady had nothing to say. 

Visited the place again, ordered the "vegetable biriyani" for takeout. The server confirmed there will be gravy and paneer(cheese blocks) inside. On opening the food, the rice was very dry with no paneer at all. We called the restaurant to complain. They denied our observation. Didn't even offer any sort of apology or refund. Very disappointed with their service & feedback. 

I've been receiving this sort of experience multiple times. The food is usually good but their hospitality totally brings their overall review down.

We've been ordering every week since mid-March through Mercato and love it.  Although I do still miss wandering around and personally shopping, Mercato is efficient and there are a wide range of choices from the merchants.  So, until it is safe for us to come back into center city, the delivery method is a life saver.  Thank you Godshall's, Downtown Cheese, Hatville Deli, Pennsylvania Store, Famous Fourth Street Cookie Company, O.K. Produce, Iovines, and John Yi Fish Market.

I love the tomato pie here. The times I've gone, I've managed to not encounter long lines. It was incredibly convenient to grab a reasonably-priced slice of ridiculously well-made pizza ($3 for tomato pie) that somehow holds up to its made-to-order whole-pie counterparts. After walking around all day, it was really satisfying to bite into one - rich, tomato sauce with the perfect ratio of ingredients, a pillowy focaccia-like base, and charred crust that in some parts almost tastes lightly caramelized. Sometimes simple is better.

There's really a niche for this really fantastic quality grab & go, when sometimes I want instant gratification and don't want to deal with the time and expense of a sit-down restaurant, commit to a whole pizza/the wait, etc. I generally have an aversion to pizza that's been sitting out and reheated, but the narrow opening hours and good oven seem to be part of the trick to avoiding the issue. Make no mistake though - there are tons of whole-pizza orders. It's best to come earlier if you plan to order multiple pizzas, since they make a fixed number and are also considerate of how many people are in queue.

I'm just going to be echoing what MANY other Yelpers have already said about this place, but I think it's worth a walk through if you happen to find yourself in Philadelphia. It's right in the heart of the city and there are so many food options here, you're bound to find something to please everybody here.

So far, I've tried doughnuts, ice cream, a sandwich, coffee, chocolate, and pretzels from here, and I've barely scratched the surface with that. I've never been to Pike Place Market out in Seattle, but I imagine this is like that (and both markets remind me of Chelsea Market Place in NYC).

The reading terminal market is one of my go-to spots in philly. It is perfect for lunch with friends because you can all get something different. They have everything from desserts to cheesesteaks to gyros- you can even do your grocery shopping here!
 
Every time I go, I try to go somewhere different. There are too many great options to choose from. 

The only downside is there is limited/crowded seating, but that is expected at such a busy place. Big plus for the restaurants that offer their own seating. 

Definitely a great spot for visitors and locals!
One stop shop for all the best that Philly has to offer. Go on weekdays to avoid the crowds
This spot is great for thin and crispy pizza. My favorite little hole in the wall place to stop for pizza when I'm near fish town!

What's not to love about Reading Terminal!? All the major food groups in one place: cheesesteaks/hoagies/all other sandwiches, rotisserie chicken, pizza, salads, Asian, baked goods, beer, candy and ice cream! Of course it's ridiculously crowded, what of the greatest eateries in the country isn't? RT is a mainstay of locals, and an absolute necessity for visitors.
The staff was nice and gracious but the salad was really bad and overpriced. I also ordered an express pineapple smoothy and it was bad too. I wouldn't repeat this place.

The Liberty Bell is great and all but this is by far my favorite place in Philadelphia. There is so much good food it's unreal. Standouts include The Dutch Eating Place, for made from scratch Breakfast and Beiler's Donuts for anytime! Honorable mention goes to DiNics with their amazing brisket  cheesesteaks, stuffed with peppers and broccolli rabe. Everything is very reasonably priced and service is friendly especially at the Amish stands. Location is very central so you can't miss it. Luckily our hotel was nearby so whenever we were at a loss for what to eat we came here and all was well.

This place has a nice look and feel to it and the service is friendly but oh my god is the food bad. 
Anyone who has had a kati roll before knows that the bread is an Indian style grilled bread which wraps the meat/veggies. Their bread is basically a raw tasting tortilla. Also the meat seems extremely stale and ill tasting, it gave me a stomach ache.

In addition to the the other kati rolls I tried, the lamb kati roll I ordered was basically some kind of minced meat which tasted horrible instead of actual bits of lamb.
Tons of great places to eat authentic food!

Seriously, what's not to love about RTM? There is something here for absolutely everyone!

If any friends or family members come to visit Philadelphia, this is one of the first places I'll take them. I think it does a tremendous job of showcasing the diversity of people found in this wonderful city.

Some of my favorite spots include:
--Miller's Twist
--The Rib Stand
--12th Street Cantina
--Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties
--Terralyn: Bath, Body, Spirit

The prices can be a little bit expensive, but it is nearly always worth it for the quality of ingredients and customer service. This is a place you definitely cannot miss if you're staying in the area! It's tradition.

The Reading Terminal Market is a great place to just eat and eat and eat some more and then shop for food and more food. Sadly they now close at 6 PM so get there before 4 really. They start to close down shops around that time. You can also go on the weekend but get there early. The place gets super crowded.

They have all types of food. If you want the best ice cream go to Bassets. I think you can still have them ship you pints, so think about that. It is really great ice cream. Also note that nothing here is inexpensive. It is all pricey. 

The best donuts in town are at Beiler's. If you love donuts it is a must stop for you. For Breakfast try the Dutch Eating Place. Everything there is great and made to order fresh. You will love it. You also have to stop in some time to have a pork dipped sandwich at Dinic's. 

You will love this place. Have a great time.

The Reading Terminal Market is a great place to visit while in Philly.  The variety and quality of vendors was fantastic.  I had never been to the market, so my plan of action was to wander through aisle by aisle and check things out, then make my decision about what I wanted to purchase and eat.  We arrived at the market a little after 11:00 on a Saturday.  It was busy but not overwhelming.  We saw delis, cheese shops, a dairy and restaurants/food stands that sold everything from oysters to sushi and even french crepes.  And, of course, a huge amount of vendors offering cheese steaks.  

By shortly after noon, it was unbearably crowded.  You could not move unless you were pushing yourself through.  Do yourself a favor and go early in the morning or later in the day after the lunch rush.  

Highlights for me were the orange strawberry lemonade from Lancaster County Dairy (a bonus, they offer free samples), an ice cream cone from Bassett's ice cream, and jerky from Smucker's Quality Meats & Grill.  I wanted a sandwich from DiNic's, but the line was waaaaaay too long.  

It was an overall fantastic experience.  I know it isn't feasible, but I wish the walkways were wider and that there were more areas for seating.

It can be very overwhelming visiting the RTM so I recommend checking out there website to make a plan of action. I have eaten here and there but not familiar enough to name drop just yet. It is a really great market where you can purchase breakfast/lunch, grab fresh produce, and grab a drink. The only down side is how crowded it can get. I read reviews about avoiding this place with a stroller and should have listened but we were at the car show and holding a toddler the entire time would have been back breaking. We tried getting a seat at Molly Malloy and when that proved impossible we drove back on our side of the bridge and hit up PJ's. 

Also can someone tell me what is in those donuts! The line was wrapped around the entire market. 

We haven't given up on you yet RTM. I will be back!

I'm so disappointed. I stopped by this location while running errands on Christmas Eve. I ordered on the app and there was a wait but when is there not a wait. Now I've had the Mac and cheese in Georgia and it was surprisingly good, I didn't have the same experience here. The Mac and cheese here is like you'd get from any fast food restaurant very Kraft and Velveeta like. The Mac and cheese I had in Georgia was like someone's Auntie or my mom had possibly stopped by and gifted them with a few gems, NOT ALL. Just that they were in the neighborhood of good mac and cheese with their recipe, not so for this location. The nuggets were hard and just not what I'm accustomed to from a Chik fila. I'm confused because I thought they are a chain and it should be the same? This was not like any Chik fila I'd ever been to. I hate it here
Them Wings from Frankies go crazyy! And the produce and juice bars are all really fresh. Unlimited options, perfect place to bring someone picky lol. New gem every time

Super cool - but very busy - food court and market atmosphere.  The aisles are a bit too narrow, so be prepared for crowds and some lines.  Many different types of places to eat, although some were not open at the time. I'm not sure what the scheduling is for all of them, but there's plenty of other options if your favorite appears to be closed.  Would love to see more areas for sitting; be prepared to do some hunting for a table.  Overall, a neat experience in downtown Philadelphia.

So many selections it will make your head spin!!! There's nothing I have tried that I didn't love. Fair warning - everything is pricey so if you have a large group or kids this might not be the best option for meals.

Oh Reading what would have I done without you! I came to Philly on business and RTM was my savior. I got a chance to visit 3 times and each time I tried different foods and goodies.

Reading is similar to Pikes Market in Seattle but everything is indoor and is on one floor. Lots to look at and the Market get super packed on weekends. There are tours that come through so be mindful that some of the food items or goodies may have a long line or may have sold out. 

Check the hours also because some of the shops are closed on certain days, or they may close early due to them selling out of their products. Also, some of the shops offer deals at the end of the day (e.g. 2 for 1). 

Cool place to hang out for an hour or so and only a block walking distance from my hotel, Lowes.

I love to hang out here. There are countless choices for food and coffee. Sometimes it gets a little noisy/crowded, but that's part of the charm, and a few minutes spend on looking for a seat is part of the experience.

This is an absolute must. I will skip a few of the usual obligatory superlatives and say...

1. Skip the hotel or fast food breakfast and come here. There are places to buy a cup of coffee, a pastry, or have a sit down breakfast in the market.
2. Bring cash. Most places take credit, but there are some small treats (like Beiler's donuts) that work best with cash.
3. There is a good balance here of local and tourist feel. On one hand, there's plenty of fresh fish, sausage, and produce, while on the other, sweets, specialty items from local vendors, and restaurants.
4. Be mindful of Sunday. Many vendors are not open on Sunday.
5. There are loads of lunch choices. You can eat sushi, Mexican, or bratwurst here, as well as plenty of other choices.
A very cool place to visit and a must smell/see for a tourist! Get everything you need in one place to satisfy your group! From middle eastern food to classic diner with everything in between!

It was my first time at La Lo (and at Bourse food hall) and my first time eating Filipino food.  I was with a friend, and we didn't know what to order.  We went with the Tabaching combo option which consisted of garlic fried rice, 3 fried spring rolls, bbq chicken, and lumpiang sariwa for $15.  We wanted to get a taste of everything, and this was the perfect dish to share for both of our first experiences.  

So I cannot speak to the authenticity in form or taste of La Lo's food, but I really enjoyed my first Filipino food experience there! The chicken skewers and fried spring rolls were really good.  I really didn't know what to expect with the lumpiang sariwa, but it was similar to a crepe filled with sauteed vegetables and overall, pretty good! 

I'd definitely be back to try some of the other things they offer!

Take your largest grocery bags, tuck a bunch of cash in your pocket (forget the purse, it'll just get in your way), and go mildly hungry, at about 10 am.

I always aim for the Lancaster County bakers and butchers and greengrocers (sticky buns; gorgeous chicken, pork sausages, and scrapple; fabulous celery or tomatoes depending upon the season), AND The Spice Corner (which may no longer be its name, but,. hey, they're the BEST whatever their name is).

For mid-morning snack, shop carefully, because you'll want to sample goodies from the multitude of ethnic delicacies available.  Do not expect to need lunch.

An iconic stop in Center City Philadelphia. Get everything from a delicious Amish breakfast, to locally sourced honey and fresh produce and other local artisan goods all in one stop. The Reading Terminal is a must visit one stop shop for city dwellers and visitors alike.

There's so many choices here! The aroma of the desserts and coffee is everywhere in this place. The grilled cheese is great and definitely need to come back again to try the other installments. Only down side is not enough seating

This particular store on Roosevelt Blvd has the absolute worse service of any I have ever gone visited.  We waited 50 minutes in a drive through where I could see 4 employees sitting in the booths on phones and eating.  They always have tremendously slow service and have made mistakes on our orders.  I will drive an extra 30 minutes or choose a different food option instead of eating here.

To echo the words of Jason C., "a nice tourist trap".  But there are a lot of locals that eat here too so what gives?  It seems like the regulars use the tables for lunches brought from home and maybe a dessert purchased within the market?

The only items worth purchasing will be made by anyone that looks like they're Amish.  The best items will come from those that are actually Amish.  You should probably check out my list aptly titled "Philadelphia" for more information.

Buyer beware...
Godshalls is a great butcher shop if you are looking for poultry (chicken or turkey).  They have good customer service and great tasting food

I LOVE the Reading terminal and it's a must that I get there every year before Christmas, but after Thanksgiving. There's such an old world feel with the open markets, great restaurants and one of a kind gifts. A must do if you're in the Philly area.

One of the best places in Philly! So much to choose from, so much to see. I love the fact that you can buy a beer and walk around. 
Weekdays are obviously less crowded than weekends, but any day is a good day. Choose from an array of different cuisines (I recommend the burgers and tacos) or if head over to the bakery for some awesome sweet treats. 
I love the fact that there are fresh fruits and veggies at a VERY favorable price. Also, a sweet german lady sells some beautiful artwork of Philly landmarks. I got some beautiful coasters of the area. 
AMAZING PLACE! 10/10 recommend.

What a place. The variety of food stuffs is unbelievable. 

If your hungry and want it, they probably have it!

Just be ready for crowds. The amount of people was crazy.

If you like the amish items , go later in the week, they aren't there on certain days.

As a Philly resident for 12+ years I never get sick of this place. Lots of vendors, mainly food and food related items. Molly's is a bar and restaurant in the middle of the market with classic irish bar food. My favorite place is Hershels.

It might be easier to ponder what the Reading Terminal Market is missing rather than highlighting the many, many great things about it.

1) Does it lack a great selection of vendors... no, it certainly has that covered
2) So are they all just crap... no, not only is there quantity but quality as well
3) Does it smell like, eh, Philly... nope, the fresh smells of deliciousness is a pleasant change from the streets of Fhiladelphia.
4) Well then how about celebrates, there is no way it has those... does Adam Richman (Man vs. Food) count? He marked his second trip there today!
5) Ok well, does it have a coat check...

Damn, I managed to find something the Reading Terminal is missing, coat check!  

So unless coat check is a deal breaker, I recommend you manage to carve out some time to check out the market.  Bring a date and explore or just go on an empty stomach...

What a shame.  This place has so much potential for a healthy, hearty meal, but WOW, the staff just RUINS it.  Not only are they unprofessional, but they're spreading disease!  I ordered a salad in a wrap, and although the woman behind the counter did put on gloves to start the process, she then proceeded to wipe her sniffling nose on her gloves about 4 times during my salad making process.  She put the salad in the wrap with those nasty sick gloves.  I wasn't even sure I was seeing what I was seeing, and I had already paid for it by the time she got to the wrapping.  I wish I'd had enough sense to ask for my $13.55 back!  I ended up tossing the whole thing in the trash.  (Better to waste $13 then to be sick for 2 weeks!)  I watched her continue to make food for people and continue to touch her face and nose through the entire process.  I wonder how many people she made sick.  I looked for a manager to discuss the situation, but NO one behind the counter was taking their job seriously enough for me to think there was a manager onsite.  (This was 30-Dec-2019 at 6:31PM ET, if Green Leaf's wants to check who was working that night.)  It's such a shame because they have the BEST options in the airport for healthy food.  Too bad it gives you a cold or flu!
Love the terminal..tons of varieties of fresh food, and plenty to eat. 5 stars

Outstanding, authentic, high quality Lebanese food ! 
Great addition to the culinary scene in Philly !
If you are visiting Philly you should check this place out. Reading terminal market is a foodie's dream.

I went here first as a part of the Philadelphia gourmet food tour. The donuts here are the best I've ever had. It's such a unique place where you can walk around and try different food. My favorite savory food was these cheese curds I had. This place is not something you would expect in the city. This is must go place for any tourist or Philadelphia residents

Exactly like CAVA. A chipotle/sweetgreens for Mediterranean food. A little on the pricier side ($11 for a bowl). But there was a lot of food in the bowl. I went at 11:15am during the week and it was practically empty but I've seen this place have lines out the door. 

Might come back but I'd rather try a new restaurant instead.
What's not to love about Reading Terminal, a staple downtown. At this time I'd probably go on off peak times, non weekend, non lunch hour on weekdays bc it's a crowded place.

I love this place.  So much better now than when I was a kid.  I remember it smelling very raunchy back then, but there probably wasn't any air conditioning in the Middle Ages!  

There's always something fascinating about the Farmers' Market, and I love to see the colorful fruits and veggies set out.  It's never quiet or empty - a lot of hustle and bustle is part of the experience, but the lines move quickly and the service is efficient.  The vendors know a lot of us snuck out of work to pick up groceries or grab lunch, so they don't waste time, but you can chat with them if you have time.

One of the coolest places I went to in Philly. I love food and options, so this was my heaven. I wanted to experience a lot of the different cuisines this city has to offer and this was the perfect place to do so. I absolutely loved the chaos of the little stores, markets, food stands, and counters, but be wary if you are claustrophobic. I forgot the name of the donut shop, but highly recommend. Also the little wine store which I thought was neat! And a metaphysical shop. Just such a cool place. Highly recommend!
A variety of foods for whatever you're looking for. From seafood to Jamaican. Can't go wrong with the terminal. You also can get your protein from the butcher and veggies from the produce as well.

TLDR: Reading Terminal Market is probably the best food hall I've ever been to and the selection of food here is amazing.

Food halls are quickly becoming a thing in bigger cities and Philly has their own with Reading Terminal Market. After visiting here for the first time not too long ago, I would have to agree with many other people are saying, and that is Reading Terminal Market is as much as a Philly staple as the Philly cheesesteak itself.

Reading has a pretty rich history and it's been around since the late 1800s. It has had its shares of ups and downs, but it seems to be going on stronger than ever now. It's not just all restaurants here either, you could skip out on going to a grocery store and get all of your produce, meat, poultry, flowers, alcohol, and much more all here.

Obviously with it being a market, you need to come in here absolutely starving to make the most of the selections at Reading. There are foods of all types and you will get stuffed by the time you leave. 

If you do end up driving to Reading, there are two main garages that you can park at, and make sure you bring your ticket with you. If you spend ten or more dollars at one place, a merchant can validate your ticket for a discount on parking.

While there are so many options here, I can recommend:

- Miller's Twist for pretzels (Seriously the best pretzel ever)
- Tommy DeNic's for a roast pork sandwich 
- Beiler's for just about any donut you can think of
- Little Thai Market for chicken red curry
- 4th Street Cookie Company for what else, cookies

I suppose the only downside to this place is that it's only open until 6 pm. If it was open late, I don't think I could eat anywhere else. 

If you've never been here, do yourself a favor and go here now.

Fantastic grocery and take-away selection. Definitely recommend heading here for meals if you're attending a conference at the convention center across the street. You can easily get a huge lunch to split with a friend for under 10$.

While a cheesesteak from By George! is the obvious choice, try out the schnitzel sandwich at Wursthaus, a pork sandwich with hot peppers from DiNic's, or a handmade kinish from Hershel's. 

Head's up that this place is CROWDED, so try to go a bit before the lunch rush if you want to get in and out quickly. Otherwise plan a 20 minute wait on line for the more popular restaurants.

I tried this on a whim when walking through the Bourse. The vegan Laing is dooooooooope. And gluten free!!! I haven't tried anything else on the menu but I've had the Laing a few times. If you're not vegan, add an egg!! It's so good.

Stopped here for lunch. Tons of healthy options. Make your own salads from fresh ingredients. I had the clam chowder and tuna wrap.  Food was really fresh and good, refreshing for an airport.  
They are located at the end of Terminal D.  
Service was amazing.  Fast and friendly.

Reading Terminal market has the best value for quick food in Philly.  There are so many options from grilled cheeses and cheese steaks, to ice cream and smoothies.  It is the perfect location for a large group that cannot decide on what they are in the mood for. 

The deli's make fantastic sandwiches, Meltkraft has the best grilled cheeses around, and there a handful of ice cream and fruit smoothie joints to choose from.  Not only do they have classic American food, but they have restaurants providing dishes from around the world.  Indian, German, Greek, and several Asian cuisines are all represented; just to name a few.  

The only thing that's a little tricky and can be a pain is the limited amount of seating. It is set up in a fashion with vendors down a line and winding all over the area, with the tables all clustered in the middle.  Usually there is a wait for seating, so I would advise standing if it is at all possible.  Besides this I love the variety and the option to chow down on whatever I'm in the mood for!
Seriously good pizza in fishtown ! The white specials are a must and the tomato pie is great . Service is always friendly too !5 Star Pizza

This place is a foodie + Farmer's Market haven!! It has delicious baked goods, sandwiches, BBQ, cheeses, hobby shops, souvenirs, books, and more! My BF and I came here on a Saturday and were immediately overwhelmed. We picked up a map because we already knew which stores we wanted to try.

Top 3 businesses worth stopping by:

1. Tommy DiNic's-- delicious roast pork sub w/ sharp provolone and broccoli rabe
2. Basset's Ice Cream-- creamy texture plus delicious ice cream with so many different flavors to choose from!
3. Beiler's Bakery-- so many cheap, freshly baked goodies!!.. I picked up so many it was hard to narrow down!

We also stopped by Flying Monkey Bakery for their infamous "pumple" (apple pie in a vanilla cake atop a pumpkin pie in a chocolate cake) and the Dutch bakery for their apple dumplings, yum! 
Definitely want to try the Wursthaus Schmitz deli and check out other spots next time when we have more time.
This is my favorite place on earth. It's perfect, it's heaven, it's like being in a movie. I could (and have) spend HOURS here.

so glad this place opened again!!! absolutely unique and delicious kati rolls. one might not be enough but two is more than enough! so affordable, so quick. can't wait to get lunch here all the time! the mayo sauce is also amazing :)

One of my favorite places in Philly.  Atmosphere, variety & quality are fantastic at every store I have visited.  Some of my favorites: Pearl's, Amish Eatery, Taste of Spain, the Family Meat store, the Deli meats near by, Iovine Bros for produce, the Deli sandwich shop in the middle and each dessert store!

Incredible food in a crammed location.

I am so torn about this review.  This market is iconic.  A part of me feels like everyone should go.  Another part of me feels like it was just too packed and you may be able to eat these foods with a well-curated Yelp list.  Thus my conflicted rating. 

We walked to Reading Terminal from our hotel near Independence Hall.  It was about a 20 minute walk.  We went on a Friday and arrived about 11.  The market had narrow aisles.  You regularly have to stand in line.  There are also many shops you will want to go and try their delicious foods.  You will be jostled around as you walk around.  The food goes from good to great.  

If you aren't in to huge crowds, this may not be the place for you.  If you are in to huge food markets and have a huge appetite, then belly on up.  You'll be in heaven.  We were both glad we went but aren't going to rush back.  It was just a little too much for us.
Always a great selection of produce. Their delivery through mercato saved me throughout the pandemic

A FOODIE'S HEAVEN! This is the market of all markets! I love bringing guests here from out of town picky people? This market will defeat them! From naked goods, to soul foods to fresh groceries and home goods, you CANNOT go wrong here! I come here after the the gym to have breakfast and once a week grab fresh flowers.

Butterfly in the sky, I can go twice as high. Take a look it's in a book, it's a Reading Rainbow?!?....No No No you're uterrly confused my friends, this is the Reading Terminal not Reading Rainbow you won't find Levar Burton here either :(

Reading Terminal was the one of the many highlights of my trip to Philly. We ended up having a hotel nearby so we were about 5 mins within walking distance of the terminal.  The Reading Terminal is an indoor public market and a historic landmark building for Philly.  There's tons of merchants and vendors inside the terminal to choose from, too many I can't even count so I will list my favorites:

Beiler's Donuts - OMGOODNESS, the east coast knows how to make dounuts and this place is no different.  Make sure you stock up on Saturday because they are closed on Sundays.

Valley Shepherd Creamery - this cheeseshop is known for it's grilled cheese sandwiches.  The Somerset is a must!

Four Seasons - if you're looking for a health kick this is the spot for you.  An assortment of fruit smoothies to choose from.

Keven Parker's Soul Food Cafe - Food Network Rated Best Fried Chicken, this is a must stop at the terminal.

The Reading Terminal has it all, a wide variety of food to choose from, sit down restaurants, you can even do a little produce shopping for the house.  If visiting Philly try to get a hotel near the terminal as it will be your one stop for a quick and delicious bite.

Reading Terminal is crowded for a reason. The food is good! Beer, donuts, Greek, Chinese, cheesesteak, honey, fruit, candles,  olives?? It's all here. Under one roof. Seating sucks. Bathrooms are clean. Never had a bad meal here. John Yi seafood is best in city. Beiler Donuts are best in the world. The place is sea to see dull of people on Saturday. It's just a must see place to visit when in Philadelphia. You will walk in But you will roll out.

First time we set foot on Reading terminal market, we were overwhelmed. We came at lunch time, 1pm. We were starving from our 2hr nonstop drive to Philly from NYC.

It seems as tho you can easily get lost in this place. It looked huge at first glance but once you get your footing steady, it isn't as big as I initially thought it was. Just one run around and we knew where everything was.

This place was a huge disappointment. We drove 45 minutes to try this pizza based off of a pic and review we saw on social media, and after doing a bit of research. We arrived at 630p on a Friday, today to find that business is dark and closed. Has a CLOSED sign on a pizza spatula in the window. Unbelievable. Not to mention that they have no working phone number to follow up And confirm if they are just on a break of some sort. Never again... DISAPPOINTED TO THE FULLEST!!!

Amazing staff and store! I love visiting this Starbucks location! My drink is always made perfectly and several times the staff has gone above and beyond to make my Starbucks trip great!:) The Pumpkin Cream Cold Brew is my go to seasonal fall drink! The perfect blend of creaminess and pumpkin spice!

When in Philly you need to stop by and take a look around. They have tons and tons of different types of foods. The donut shop inside isn't bad at all with tons of different toppings. The cheesesteak shop inside is also very good.
Will never , and I mean ever, be a place as special to me in philly as Reading Terminal Market. So many amazing memories growing up and now. Will forever support

Without any doubt the "Reading Terminal Market" presents all different variety of traditional Philadelphia Food and a reminder of old Philadelphia's "food market place".

Although this is not the first and only food market place in Philadelphia but it is very popular.

I am a fan of this place and I like it especially the food is great!

This is my personal experience.

Please share your personal experience that you had with every business at reading terminal market, especially if the person who was serving you or the business owner was not very respectful or was very kind or even the food's quality so they can correct and improve their services.

Reading terminal market is a great place to find all kinds of great things from unique gifts to specialty ingredients for tonight's dinner, this weekends party or whatever you need. The restrooms are always clean and stocked and the vendors do their best to provide great service. It's conveniently located near the Market Frankford Line and the Fashion District Mall. So why  only three stars?  NO MASK ENFORCEMENT by the many security and staff walking around and no table cleaning between guests. That's unacceptable with COVID19!

Best place in the city for fresh seafood, meat, and produce! They have a plethora of baked goods, different ethnic cuisines, and ready-made meals. I always bring friends here who are visiting the city. It's a great place to come as a tourist but yet all the locals love this place too and shop here regularly. I know, because I do!

My favorite places: 

Produce: Iovine Brothers 
Donuts: Beiler's Donuts
Cookies: Metropolitan Bakery
Honey: Bee Natural 
Ice cream: Bassetts Ice Cream 
Fresh bread: Market Bakery
Health smoothies: Four Seasons Juice Bar

One of the greatest indoor markets in the USA. It's truly hard to find a place that could even come close to the reading terminal market. The food is delicious and the store owners are friendly and knowledgeable on their products. I recommend you try everything you can't go wrong on anything here.
I love it here and any time I visit Philly we have to come by...they literally have any and every thing you can think of food wise.
Great market! It has everything you can imagine. Great food market. I recommend the fresh made doughnuts they were absolutely amazing.
The food is all very heavy. Not the best Philly cheesesteak I've had. Cool place to walk around though.

I'm so in love with Reading Terminal Market! It reminds me of Marche Jean-Talon in Montreal, but with way more food and less groceries/farmer's market (both are indoor structures, by the way). Vendors are separated by stalls/sections and there is even a map so you don't get lost. You just have to see it. So amazing. I wanted to try everything but I only have one stomach so I opted for the ones that had the highest Yelp reviews. Best decision ever.

Reading Terminal Market is now on my list of favorite places in Philly and dare I say it, overall, in my travel adventures (but theme parks - you'll always be #1). Don't miss out! You won't be disappointed with anything inside.

Reasonably decent wraps at reasonable airport prices. However the service was challenging. I got the "choose 2" tomato basil soup and quinoa wrap (vegetarian friendly). I also got the super fruit smoothie. At $8 for the meal and $4 for the smoothie, you can't beat the price at the airport. However the worker was trying to push pre-made sandwiches on me that weren't vegetarian which wasn't too cool.
If you're in terminal D, it's a decent cheap option, but I wouldn't venture across the airport for this.

Countless spots in Reading Terminal guaranteed to please your palate! I love coming here when I am in the city, and always look forward to trying new things! You can find incredible pizza, sandwiches, desserts, breakfast, and more! The people who work the booths are so friendly and helpful! Not sure what it is like in there since COVID, but you used to be able to sit down and eat and people watch--which is something I always loved doing! One of my favorite spots is the crêperie, located not far from the entrance(s). Sweet and savory crepes made fresh to order, and you can watch them make it yourself!
Parking can be an issue, but there is a garage down the street which is where I typically go when I am in that area. So much to do in the city, so coming here for a break and some lunch is quite adequate!
If you are in Philadelphia you MUST stop here!

Drive through line was forever long like always because they're food is delicious, however this location allows you to walk in which was awesome because service was so fast that I was walking out food in hand by the time the car that was in front of me at the drive through was just 2 away from ordering. Only downfall is with fast service corners get cut and this one was cold cheese on my sandwich which does throw off the taste for the spicy chicken.

OMG!!!! 
Absolutely, hands down best Indian food on the run.

While I was trying to pick a place to eat for dinner, I realized I haven't tried Masala Kitchen yet. I had to give it a try, and all I know, is that I'm kicking myself in the butt for not trying it earlier.

Confession time: I'm Middle Eastern, and rice is part of my life, and I LOVE good Biryani. 
I'm not a Biryani connoisseur, but if you've read any of my other reviews, you know I'm always on the hunt for a good Biryani. 
So, naturally, I ordered the Chicken Biryani platter "$9.00", which came with pita bread and lettuce. I was pleased with the generous portion- got me two meals out of one platter. The Biryani was spicy, and it was incredibly delicious.
 
Now, you gotta try a roll, and you'll fall in love at first bite! 
I'm telling you folks, Kati Rolls are like the new wraps! There is something about that thin, fresh, and handcrafted wrap-like bread named paratha. 
Your choice of protein (grilled Chicken, Beef tikka cubes, tender Lamb kebab, homemade Cottage Cheese and more) will be wrapped in paratha bread. I've tried Chicken Masala"$5.50" & Chicken Tikka"$5.25", and I'm absolutely hooked. The rolls had fresh green chutney, sliced red onion, and you may add a beaten egg to any roll for $0.50. 

Whether you are a starving early bird, a night owl with a midnight craving, or maybe just having a serious case of the drunchies, Masala Kitchen will sure be open way late to serve you. On weeknights, food will be served till midnight, Friday and Saturday until 3:30am, and Sunday till 11:00pm.

Tips: You'll get $1.00 off, when you buy two rolls- except Aloo & Unda rolls (not valid for delivery). Or use the 10% off your entire order, when you check-in on Yelp.

Great spot.
Four solid Yelps.

Pros: Outstanding New York style pizza sold by the slice or whole pie. The crust is crispy and expertly charred with a good chew. The cheese is high quality and supplied in generous amounts. The tomato sauce on the plain and pepperoni pizza is very tasty, on the thicker side, and not sweet at all. While the basil cream sauce on the white pizza is out of this world delicious. Finally, the artisanal toppings are fresh and also high quality (eg. fantastic pepperoni). On taste alone, Shackamaxon is the best slice shop in Philly and among the top four best pizzas overall in the region. 

Cons: No working number, no pre-orders available, No delivery, virtually no seating, shop routinely closed during normal business hours due to unforeseen circumstances, finding nearby parking is difficult, and inventory is extremely limited with pizza usually sold out by 7-7:30PM.

Bottom Line: The best slice shop in Philly and among the top four best pizzas overall in the region. An absolute must try if you live in the area or within a short commute. However, not worth an extended commute or going out of your way given the shop may be unexpectedly closed, the pizza may be sold out, you likely won't have a place to sit, and you will have difficulty finding parking . 

Pro Tip: Go early on a weekday because they open at 1PM and are usually sold out by 7-7:30PM on weekends.

This is my personal Disneyland. I have been going here for years and I'm now lucky enough to work in the area a few times a month. I can't get enough of the amazing verity of food and goods. I have also never had a bad meal from any of the dozens of restaurants. I won't very go into my favorite picks because I have always enjoyed whatever I have tired.

Just a heads up it's super crowded on weekends and lunch time and parking can cost an arm and a cheese steak. 

This place is a must visit for any foodie.

Was so excited to visit this spot when me and Eric went to Philly this weekend. We got there around 4pm and almost every single vendor was already closed. It said 6pm on the website and we were highly disappointed.. I wanted a roast pork sandwich from Dinics and a pretzel from Millers Twist and both were closed down. The only things that were open were the bar and The Flying Monkey Bakery. We got a Pumple cake which is pumpkin pie inside of a chocolate cake inside an apple pie inside a yellow cake. It was ok. Kinda stale but the cashier was so nice and friendly. It reminded me of the old Farmers Market in Bethpage that i used to hit up as a child. We looked around a bit and was just so let down that i couldn't buy anything i came for. We were leaving Philly that night so never had the chance to go back. Sad.

This place is the best thing about going to a convention!!!

I wish that every convention center in the world had a market place like this.  What a great place to escape too and have some lunch!!!  The Amish Bakery near Arch Street was making some fantastic smells today.

My favorite place in here is Tommy DiNic's...I had the most amazing sandwich here...go for the Roast Pork...trust me...I did it for 3 days!!!  It was like heaven on Italian Bread!!!

There is also discounted parking across the street on 12th Street...I think you have to spend $20 from a merchant and then they will validate.

Only issue is that during a convention it is always crowded on it...so plan according because there may be a little wait for your food...so schedule your booth time and meetings accordingly!!!

This market is by far the best that I have been to. There are so many different options to choose from. I had oysters and lobster bisque at Pearl's Oyster bar. Very good customer service! I also tried Spataros Cheesesteaks. It was a delicious Philly Cheesesteak.

Fun to come on a day when the weather sucks and you need some excitement. Food is everywhere in this place, which would make anyone happy. Fresh fish, fresh meat, and many gift shops in between. This place is like a mini indoor flea market. You'd enjoy it!

Warning... foodies should not enter unless you have strong self control or a fat wallet. Similar to Chelsea market in NYC, I walk around thinking to myself "I want to try that. Oh wait, I want to try that. No, I want to try this"... over and over again.
I bought rectum ripper hot sauce. It truly lives up to its name. I tried to use to spice things up in the bedroom but it's a little too hot and got sent to the ER.

This is the first visit we make since last year.  With the new health ordinance from the city of Philadelphia, ALL seating inside the Reading Terminal has been removed so the overall feeling of the terminal is of wider space. Masks are required, around the perimeter of the terminal you have security and they have set high boy tables for people to buy food and consume the food standing up with a place to at least eat your food standing.  I an cool with that. Me traveling for the day, i was ready with a picnic basket cause thats how we New Yorkers do...(plates, paper towels and plastic utensil) as i was craving soul food. We visited a few places hadvid deli, dutch place, four seasons juice bar, kevin Parker soul food.  The bathrooms were extremely clean and well attended throughout the day.  Tables out of the building were also kept clean, as you finish your meal and your group clears the table, they sanitize the table tops quickly.  They have enough security outside that i felt comfortable to not be hassled by the homeless population.

No frills pizza joint currently taking walk-ups only. Ordered the plain pie, was told it would be 30 mins, and it was ready on time. Thin crust, tasty sauce, cheese, and EVOO with an upper crust that was a bit charred. A tad pricey for $4/slice and $22/pie but overall, it's a solid choice if you're in the neighborhood.

There aren't many Filipino places in Philly, so when I saw that there was one in The Bourse, I knew I had to try it out. I knew coming in that this was not a typical Filipino spot- it's modernized, showing the innovation that the younger generations of Filipinos can bring to the table but probably also a way to appeal to the non-Filipino crowds. It's like there are two types of Filipino restaurants- the no-frills comfort food places attached to small Filipino markets that make you feel like your mom cooked the meal, and modernized/fusion Filipino places that make you feel like you're living in 22nd-century Manila. Lalo is the latter.

I came here on a Sunday morning after finishing up a photoshoot at Photo Pop, so I opted for their Sunday special spamsilog (spam, garlic fried rice and egg), blueberry calamansi iced tea, and leche flan. There was only one person in front of me, so my food came out quickly.

Blueberry calamansi iced tea- refreshing, but I was struggling to pick out the hints of calamansi (Philippine citrus fruit) in the drink. It may have been a bit dilute. Nevertheless, refreshing, and it lasted for the entirety of my meal.

Spamsilog- The menu said it was a pineapple-glazed spam which really enticed me, but I didn't really taste any pineapple glaze in the spam, whether it was a super light coating that the spam absorbed or if it was cooked into the spam. It simply tasted like a charred spam, but I really enjoyed the suka (vinegar) that came with it- it had a spicy kick that helped add another level of flavor to the spam. The soft egg was NICE, the runny yolk flowed out so smoothly (warranting an instagram-worthy boomerang). The garlic fried rice was great as well, the garlic wasn't overpowering (I actually don't like garlic too much, so this was perfect for me). The overall portion was just right because I left with no leftovers and no feelings of an oncoming food coma.

Leche flan- the leche flan came out looking like the FLAN EMOJI and with a lot of extra sugar syrup down the sides. The texture of the flan was perfect, but my only complaint was that with my particular flan at least, the caramelized sugar syrup (my favorite part) tasted slightly burnt and too bitter for my taste. Again, the consistency was on point, jiggly yet firm.

As some of the other reviewers have mentioned, this is a rather hipster Filipino spot that may be targeted at the younger foodies (like me) more so than the older generations. I think I would have some hesitation bringing my parents here, who are used to the milder, less complex flavors of traditional cooking. Because I grew up going to the Filipino markets, I'm generally cautious of modernized places (which have seemed to be popping up a lot recently) and how well they present tradition to non-Filipino audiences. However, I really, really appreciate Lalo's own approach to these traditional dishes! If it's making Filipino food more accessible to the general crowd, then by all means- as long as the Philippine roots are there by the end of the meal, I think that's what matters.

Point is, if you're looking for pure, traditional Filipino food, this place may not be wholly representative of it. Turo-turo style stores over in South Jersey will be as close to home-cooked meals as you can get, but you won't find many non-Pinoys eating there. You can thank places like Lalo, located among pizza and burger and sandwich vendors, for helping bring more recognition to Filipino culture and cuisine, which we have lacked for years as an "invisible" minority.

I follow Lalo on Instagram and am kept up to date with all of the new drinks and dishes they create and add to their menu. They certainly aren't afraid of experimentation and that's what I like about them! Will definitely be back to try something new!

Just next to our hotel we did a walking tour then loaded up with a salad and some cheeses for our room.  Clearly a well earned reputation for a most-see spot in city center.  Lots of local color and foods with a mix of locally grown produce and fruits, plenty of places to eat diner style with counter and stool and a remarkable set of gourmet speciality shops with experts to help you with selections.  Fantastic place to checkout just as all the other reviews said.  Amazing!

About a year or 2 ago they were pretty good but just yesterday I ordered through the phone application a steak bowl for 13$ nothing too crazy but they gave me my order with no meat I'm not much of a complainer so I ate it, it didn't taste bad but if I paid for something I would like to get it & on top of that there were small pieces of plastic in my bowl, I'm tired of this business letting me down last time before that I went it wasn't a great experience either my food was cold still tasted good but a long time ago it use to be really good I miss the old chipotle .

This used to be one of my favorite restaurants to grab takeout or delivery. However, as time goes on they are putting less and less meat in the container. Today I ordered extra meat and got less than I have ever received. Not happy for the price.

This place is really great. I would have to say it's one of the best markets I've ever been to because of two reasons: Variety and Quality. There is basically any food you can think of, some of the choices include French Crepes, Gyros, Deli style sandwiches, Chicken, Cookies, Baked goods, Chocolates, and so much more. The place is usually very crowded because of it's popularity but the prices are fair with some more expensive things (like $10 for a sandwich). I got a cornbeef sandwich at one of the Deli's and it was delicious, very fresh and good quality. It's fun to just walk around and look at all the things they have there. There is also an amazingly cheap produce area. I got a pack of white grapes for 90 cents! It's the cheapest produce I've found in the city. Near the produce section there is also a variety of dried fruits and trail mixes. The Chocolate peanut butter trail mix is so good. I would recommend this place to anyone who wants to bypass the typical sit down restaurant and spend an afternoon exploring all the different stands this market has to offer. Also to anyone who doesn't mind a big crowd (especially on the weekend).

I hardly ever give a five star rating but this is The Reading terminal Market so how could I not. This is my favorite place to visit in Center city Philadelphia. I usually park in The garage across the street if you're in and out within two hours and get your ticket stamped from a vendor at the Market it is only five dollars to park. 
The Market is clean enough of course it isn't perfect with all of the hustle and bustle of all of the eateries. 
There are so many places to choose from to eat with all kinds of fare. It might be a little overwhelming but after many visits I have a game plan. I have eaten at maybe a quarter of the places in the Market, so i have not even begun to scratch the surface. I would like to eat at every place in there but I probably will not live long enough. 
The staff at most of the venues are professionals and very nice. I have run into some snobbery but I just avoid those places. 
The atmosphere is almost Carnival like to me. I feel that same feeling of excitement when I am here like I did as a kid at an Amusement park. I have many many favorites here...so far and I hope to find more. I like bringing my family here because everyone can get what they want and meet up and eat together. 
I always recommend the Market to anyone visiting Philly if they are looking for real Philadelphia eateries because of the convenience and many places to eat. If you have never been to the Market, I suggest you put it on your bucket list.
