WHAT.

If you only go to one place in Philly, go here, and get these items:

What to get: Hot Pretzel, Lemonade, Shake from Miller's Twist.
What else: Pot Roast Sandwich from Smucker's.
And what else: Roast Pork Sandwich w/ Broccoli Rabe from Tommy DiNic's.
Any more: Beiler's Donuts and anything from Dutch Eating Place.
What not to get: Caught at Reading reading Penthouse by an Amish security guard.

But: While you're in Philly, you must also try John's Roast Pork, Nick's Roast Beef, and a bubble tea at Mr. Wish.

This is the quintessential Market for the East Coast. Every other City along the Eastern Seaboard wishes it had a market as lavish and spectacular. Basically it is food Paradise with all kinds of deliciousness inside. A lot of it is overpriced and touristy, but there are also some amazing hidden gems lurking within the walls, particularly those which are owned and operated by the Amish, who have a very large presence within this Market.

Speaking of very large presents... (pulls down pants)... happy Amishmas.

The number one highlight is Miller's Twist which is where you will get the best hot gooey pretzel you've ever had , which will make you never want to eat a pretzel from anywhere else, and will make you speak in very long sentences, and I mean very very long sentences. 

Also try their lemonade and chocolate milkshakes which are amazing. Make sure you get the plain pretzel. Or if it's a flying pretzel, the plane pretzel. The only other pretzel that I've had which compares is down at Sadie Anne's at the Dutch Village Market in Upper Marlboro Maryland. 

Next on the agenda you have to go to Smuckers Grill and get a Pot Roast Sandwich. The breakfast there is ok but the pot roast is otherworldly and sensational. Truly one of the best sandwiches in the world. You do not come to Philadelphia for cheesesteak sandwiches. You come here for other sandwiches such as John's Roast Pork and Nick's Roast Beef and this gem here in the Market at Smuckers.

The Dutch eating place is also very good as are many of the other stands in here like Beiler's donuts. But the next top highlight belongs to Tommy Dinic's. Roast pork is the sandwich that Philly should be famous for, and the only place that makes it better than Tommy is John's which is the ultimate pork destination. Tommy does a wonderful if overpriced roast pork with broccoli rabe. And I highly recommend asking for extra broccoli rabe. Once again skip the cheesesteak. If you must get one, try one when you go to John's, or grab one at Joe's Steaks & Soda Shop, along with some shakes.

Parking here is an absolute nightmare and they give tickets out the way molesters give candy out to children while hanging out of dark unmarked vans. I highly recommend using the parking deck and just paying the lofty prices to avoid the drama. Alternatively, park somewhere cheap far away, and walk into the center so that you aren't paying for every minute you're here. The parking meters and garages here are almost as much of a rip off as your Aunt was last night.

And if your friend Adel is hungry, I'll take him to the market, and will duly Fill Adel For Ya.

Oh, why can't this market be in NYC too?

It's all around wonderful.  For produce you have to look around a bit for the best prices.  

The number of food vendors was actually a bit overwhelming at first.  If you're a foodie, plan to spend a while here.  
A bit too overwhelming in my tired mind to detail much but highly rate it as a MUST GO!

This place has terrible customer service. All I wanted was to switch out one side for another for a $20 fill up. I was told repeatedly that can't do it and kept insisting I order another meal. Then the end result was to not serve me at all and told me to have a nice day. Who does that?! These trashy ass people that work for KFC. I see why that put these people in those types of position because they can't function in a real customer service job. Just know your order has to stay the same when purchasing this item. Reason so called promotional deal .. please it's been up there for long enough to not be promotional

What's the first thing a yelper does when in a new city?  Well, besides check into my hotel and jump on the bed (my usually ritual when traveling), the answer is -- EAT and DRINK!  And what better place to start such glutenous behavior then at the Reading Terminal Market.

Reading as in the Reading Railroad - monopoly comes to life in the city of Philly!

With over 61 vendors, this place is a virtual yelper's haven. This market was established in 1893 and have everything you want-- booze, cheese-steak from the famous "ricks", fresh farmer's market veggies, honey and honey products, cooking classes, flowers, candles, chocolates, wine tasting, Italian, Greek, bakeries... each place I ate often has locations in other parts of Philly.  So, I will review them individually.  But, collectively, this place is a dream!  (And it was walking distance from my hotel and conference at the Hilton).
There is no place like Reading Terminal Market! It's where you can go to find anything you could possibly want to eat. Not to mention delicious doughnuts!
Basically Philly's version of Chelsea Market. I came here on a very crowded day (Thursday around 12-1) worth trying out for good food, but we had to find a place to sit outside.

If you're feeling some spicy, tasty, greasy food, look no further than Masala Kitchen for their Indian street food! My friends (who had been there a few times before) brought me here and omg did I love it!

After skimming over the menu, I asked my friends for recommendations and they suggested I go with one of the masala rolls. I took their advice and got the Chicken Masala Roll. Honestly, I couldn't have been any happier with my decision. It was loaded with masala making it full of flavor with a definite kick (beware if you're not accustomed to Indian spices). The roll came out piping hot which I really appreciated! It was filling and made for a great late-night bite. 

My boyfriend got the Chicken-n-Lamb Platter which I tried. Although another winning dish, the Masala Roll won me over. It isn't very often that you get delicious authentic Indian street food in Philadelphia so why would you pass up on it?!

The establishment is nothing fancy. Very causal, with a "fast food joint" type of feel to it. Prices are reasonable making this a great spot to make a quick run to for either lunch, dinner, or even just a snack! **PRO TIP: 10% of your entire purchase with Yelp check in!**

I can't wait to return here for another Masala Roll! If you're looking for a beverage to get, I recommend the Mango Lassi! This cold, fruity, "smoothie" like beverage is a fantastic way to wash down the spicy food!

One of the worlds greatest markets! This is the kind of space that alters your home purchases because you don't want to be too far away. If I lived closer it would be a daily stop. If you have never been, you can't even imagine the level of awesome you are missing.
Fries were old, dark brown and lukewarm. She didn't even say anything as if they knew already. My asiago ranch chicken sandwich only has a half piece of bacon on it.
Grabbed some donuts from here and they were delicious! My favorite was the Blueberry Fritter! Bustling place that is still clean and well kept!

Are you hungry? Are you indecisive about what to eat? Do you also want to do some shopping all without leaving the building? Look no further than Reading Terminal Market! 

There are so many different shops and food stalls that there is something for everyone. Come hungry and follow your nose to delicious food. I'm sure you can't go wrong with whichever eatery you choose!

The Reading Terminal Market reminded me of a grungier, darker Saint John City Market in New Brunswick whose motto is "an original experience every time." I can see that being true of RTM as well! The first time I came I was overwhelmed in the best way possible: there was so much to look at, smell, and taste that I didn't know where to start. It's an enormous, chaotic, loud, very busy maze that's easy to get lost in... which I did repeatedly in my attempt to visit every single stall.

Not sure about something? Ask for a sample! I can't believe how generous and friendly just about every vendor was. From wine to cheeses to potato salads (yes, plural) to chocolates, I got to engage with local purveyors who were very passionate about their goods. 

There really is so much going on that I imagine the next time I come, I'll see, smell, and taste things I didn't even realize were there previously. If I lived in Philly, I'd absolutely make shopping here a regular event... and if you're visiting the city, I encourage checking it out for a quick dose of local flavor (literally and metaphorically), but be sure to give yourself plenty of time to explore every nook and cranny!

Pros
- it's chick-fil-a...still love their sweet tea
- can order through their app so it's fast and convenient when picking up

Cons
- long line in drive thru no matter what time of day 
- ordered grilled nuggets and they were way over seasoned
- they forgot the fries in our order (!!!!) so we drove back and asked for them and the guy was super skeptical. Instead of apologizing for causing an inconvenience he was so rude and hesitant about giving us the fries
Great vendors and so much fun to walk around and explore. Definitely stop by for some ice cream and donuts!

Honestly did not understand the hype. Seems like a perfect place for munchies, but the amount of praise I've heard from Desi people in the City just isn't justified. Not to mention the very limited vegetarian selection. Like how tf are you an Indian restaurant without a lot of veggie options. It just doesn't add up tbh!

After eating breakfast at Pearl's we walked around RTM. OMG food to the left...food to the right! This place is massive. It's like an indoor food flea market. I did visit the restroom and they were very well kept. There were a few restaurants that weren't open but the place was crowded with restaurant goers, sweet tooth satisfiers, and vendor shoppers.

SO sad to say this because I had such high hopes for this place, but it is by far one of my least favorite pizza places in Philly. It's a very small place, so I'd plan on doing take out, not eating there. They also don't have a phone so you can only order there which is a little annoying. The guys working there were FANTASTIC. Such personalities and so genuine.

I know people who LOVE this place but the taste just wasn't for me. Even though I personally didn't like the pizza, I recommend trying this place for yourself!

Such a cool place to go explore the various cultures of Philadelphia. Everything from butchers to candy shops to grocers to regular Philly cheesesteaks can be found at this market, and locals and tourists both get to explore a huge attraction to the downtown PHL area!

Wonderful space to grab groceries, lunch, or something sweet! This was recommended by a friend and it definitely did not disappoint. You can spend quite a bit of time wandering around so be sure to enjoy the space. During the food rushes seating is pretty tough and with a large group we had to scour a couple rounds to be able to grab two tables near each other. 

We ended up trying a couple cheesesteak shops, pretzels, and pork sandwiches across various shops in the space and they were delicious. There seemed to be a long line for a cookie shop as well but we didn't get to try it this time around.

Reading Terminal Market is a FOODIES HEAVEN LOL!!!

Hands down one of my favorite spots in Philly.  Literally every type of food you can think of is at this place.
Greek, Caribbean, seafood, diner, deserts, Chinese, Indian, fried EVERYTHING, subs and sandwiches galore, Italian, middle eastern, etc... I mean, the list goes on and on!!! 

We opted for the infamous Tommy DiNic's for their award winning roasted pork sandwich. It was really good. Get it the traditional way with the broccoli rabe, smoked provolone, and the pork dipped in au jus... it's sooo moist and juicy! 

We also had to stop at Fox & Son and get poutine fries (perfect pair with DiNic's roasted pork sub), and fried Oreos.

Then before heading back to the hotel, we made one more stop to the Flying Monkey. You have to try their award winning Whoopie Pies! 

All in all, Reading Terminal Market is a MANDATORY stop when visiting Philly!!! I can't wait to go again and try out new restaurants there.

This is a foodie's dream. So many vendors and food options. From cheesesteaks to bakeries, there are options for everyone. The prices at most of the vendors are super affordable considering its a hot location/tourist attraction. Try to visit during the week as the weekends can get mobbed and it's hard to check out the vendors without being pushed. Seating is not ample so make sure to scope out a table in the center before getting food!
Love making this one of my stops when I'm in center city.

Literally the worst location ever. The food SUCKS, the people are rude and no one wears masks. Like this place just needs to shut down, never had a good experience here and it's completely put me off chipotle entirely. U can never get ur refund for the nasty food they give you either. Just don't go, it's a waste.

I LOVE this place! It's so fun to visit during a stroll in the city. This place is the best because it's like a giant food court. There's such a variety of foods you can choose from, and they're all delicious! I could truly spend a whole day here sampling from every kiosk!

The best part is, a lot of the food is affordable and reasonably priced!

An additional perk is that it's next to the convention center, city hall, love park, etc! If you're ever in Philly, this is a must-go!

What an amazing place.  I moved here 2 years ago and go there 4 times a week.   Great food great variety.   Meat and fish shops, never a bad experience.  I highly recommend.   Amazing ribs in the far back west corner.

I've been to the dope-ass markets in Madrid, Barcelona, Venice, Portugal...and this is the only American venue that comes close to the variety of deliciousness of those world-renowned markets.

My homegirl attended college in Philly so when I would visit her, we would frequent this savory/sweet/uber-yummy market, often.

It has the following, and more:  sweets stands (chocolates, cookies, macarons, cupcakes, cakes, ice cream), Asian food stands (Japanese, Thai, Chinese), meat stands, cheese stands, fresh fruits and vegetable stands, diners, pizza stands, cheese steak stands...and...Tommy DiNic's (you gotta hit this stand up).
 
This spot kicks ass...I need to return, ASAFP.

I used to love coming to this chick fil a let alone had my girlfriend working there for a while. But recently the staff has become worse, very rude and not caring. Not the "chic fil a way" if you ask me. not to mention once the bald manager grew that horrible go-tee he's become an a hole. Will not be coming back unless I'm forced to.

A nice place for lunch or to buy some local groceries. It reminded me of the Pikes Peak Market in Seattle. My W bought a Termini Bros. cannoli at the market. The woman took the custard right from the refrigerator and filled it in front of us. I have never seen anything like it. Very impressive! 

If visiting Philadelphia, I wouldn't miss a stop at the Reading Terminal Market. Be sure and check the market hours as they close early.
I love it I played with my friends 24 hours and the food is bussin bussin you should try this

i love reading terminal market so much. i could spend an entire morning here just browsing through all of the different stalls. it's like a playground for adults who love food and the amish. it's heaven for people who get a thrill out of buying what is likely the best produce in the city and checking out 30 different types of honey and fruit butter.
Wow, so many options for food and dessert. I ordered me some BBQ and it was great. Only bad part is that it was tough to find a table to eat. I'd definitely return and try other foods and beer.

Covid be damned!! The Terminal was bustling with people this Friday afternoon. Social distancing??? Where??? Not here but at least everyone was wearing their masks. But I can say it's way more manageable to browse around and actually get to the stalls you want. Prior to Covid i would avoid this place like the plague that's how jammed packed this market can be. With a lot less tourists in the area now is the perfect time to enjoy all that the Terminal has to offer especially if your craving sweets, Bassets is not to be missed.

My coworkers and I would go nearly every day because of the variety of vendors - if one wanted Chinese another Italian, it had it!  

They were very fast with service since they knew most people had to go back to work - now stuffed and probably want to nap.  :)

i will NOT be coming to this KFC anymore. Their service was horrible and they messed up my order 3 times!! Very disappointed and they had an attitude because they had to redo my order. On top of that my sierra mist  tasted like straight up seltzer water. Very dissapointed with the management there. Would not reccommend this place to anyone.

Reading Terminal Market is a staple in Philadelphia with a 126 year history to boot. It's the nation's oldest outdoor market, though I'd consider it an indoor/outdoor market since it's enclosed in the infrastructure of the Philadelphia Convention Center. However when Reading Terminal opened in 1893 it most likely was outdoors, very much like local Farmers Markets which are set up throughout the Philly area, between April and September yearly.

What makes Reading Terminal special is it's  eclectic feel. There is something for everyone's taste, diet, preference. 

My fondest memories of Reading Terminal was of my 80 year old grandmother ( she lived to be 91!) catching the train from Media into Center City regularly to get her fresh fish. She only bought it from Reading Terminal.
This area has cute little shops and restaurants that are very good and the vendors are pretty friendly.

I go to Philly just so I can spend everyday eating at The Redding Terminal Market.  The place is huge and offers everything your stomach may fancy.  From succulent duck to ribs to the best pork sandwich ever, the (must get the)cheese sandwich to fresh fruits and veggies to desserts.  You want Italian? You got it! You want to gorge on fresh just made doughnuts? absolutely!  You're craving Indian or how about some turkey for lunch? Gobble Gobble, Nom Nom! Having a dinner party and you need some fresh seafood and quality meats?  Don't fret.  Want to have the fluffiest pancakes and omelettes? The Dutch Eating is a must!  Green juices galore! Thai noodle heaven! Deli delights! Desserts! Candy! Even skincare.  It's awesome and cheap!  Did I mention AWESOME and CHEAP?

I was so excited to find a restaurant dedicated to Kati Rolls, and this place did not disappoint! I opted for a vegetarian option and got the paneer masala, which was super flavorful. The worker at the counter was extremely friendly, and guided me through the different spice levels so that I didn't completely burn my mouth off.

The menu has a large variety of options but isn't too overwhelming. I would recommend one roll if you're looking for a snack and two if you're looking for a meal.

If my days of staying out late weren't behind me, this would be my go to spot for late night eats given its late hours and proximity to bars/night life.
Really disappointed in the lack of healthy breakfast options. Who doesn't offer oatmeal these days? How about soy or almond milk? Even Dunkin Donuts has almond milk.

Love Reading Terminal.  So many restaurants from so many countries to try.  Friendly staff at each establishment.  Following COVID rules and regulations.  Many cute shops to visit and souvenirs to buy.  A must visit when you are in Philly.
This place is incredibly unique! So many options for food, drinks, groceries, sweets, meat, etc. It was sensory overload in the best way!

Maybe I hyped this place up in my mind, but this place was a definite let down. I absolutely love markets, indoor, outdoor, I love them all; but this one had no special spark or experience. I love markets because they are full of the hustle and bustle of locals going about their regular day; however, this one was just okay. We tried pork hoagies here that were downright awful. I couldn't finish mine even though we had been travelling all day without lunch. The seating areas could use a good cleaning. The bathrooms had some not so friendly people outside "guarding" them. I really wanted to like this place but I don't have much else to say about it.

RTM defines the city - never the same, always exciting, always offering something new and delicious ... and yet, reliably familiar and always feels like home. Picked up favorite products from Really Reel Ginger and bought bundles of fresh flowers. This is our happy place!
Hands down my favorite part of Philly!! So so many yummy spots- my favorites are Downtown Cheese, Iovine's Brothers Produce & Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialities.

This is probably one of the best tourist spots in Philadelphia. There is such a huge variety of vendors offering different foods including sandwiches, salads, coffee, desserts, and even a butcher section to buy fresh cut meat. It was honestly so hard to choose what food I wanted to eat because there was so much I wanted to try!! Additionally, the prices are all very reasonable for the portions too so it was so worth it!! I tried the philly cheesesteaks on one day and the second day I went back and got a coffee and a breakfast bagel sandwich that I still think about all the time. 

Yes, it can get quite crowded with all the towards and the narrow hallways, but the experience is all so worth it. All the staff is incredibly friendly and patient even with the high capacity of people waiting to eat the yummy foods.

Hands down my favorite place to take coworkers or out of town family members. My wife and I go there at least once a month. To have a restaurant in there you need to be able to always be on point which they are. If your in the mood for Dutch, Cajun, Sweets or my personal favorite cheesesteak spot ( Steaks by George ) you will always be satisfied. Besides the great restaurants there have great shops in there as well. Every year I pickup fresh turkey and merguez sausage for my thanksgiving dinner from Godshalls. It can be crowded and a little touristy but being born and raised in Phila it's a must go.

I love this market and visited almost a year ago. My rating still remains five stars due to its wonderful epicurean nature. This market is huge: 78000 square feet with 800 spaces for different vendors.
There is an eclectic variety to choose from: bakeries, dairy and cheese, seafood(lobster!), produce and specialty foods.
There are also House ware and book vendors who sell wonderful cookbooks. There are 24 restaurants that can satisfy every craving from the classic Philly cheese steaks to New Orleans Cajun style fare.
Here are a few of my favorites:
Meltkraft: delicious  artisanal cheese sandwiches that do melt in your mouth.
The Flying Monkey Bakery: cupcakes from Spinoni to red velvet and my fave lemon. The buttercream frosting is so rich and delicious. When you fellow Yelpers check in you get a free truffle, we got a chocolate mint. The clerk was so nice and let me keep my check in redeem offer for next visit!
TerraLynn Soaps: where else are you going to find a Shalom soap bar( citronella and lemon). Also coconut oil toothpaste!
La Divisa Meats: allowed my friend to sample the pastrami( she loved it 2 big slices to sample!)
I love the vibe of this place. There are seating interspersed throughout where you sit and mingle: we met someone from Ottawa who recommended a Cuban restaurant to eat at.
The Reading Terminal Market is a virtual feast for eyes, ears and definitely palate!

If you're a foodie, this is the place to go.  All different kinds of food are available from chicken to Cajun.  There's fresh fruit and veggies, bakeries, seafood and meats.  My fave place to eat is Dinics roast pork.  They have the best pork and beef sandwiches in Philly!  There's parking for $4 at 12th & Arch with validation from a vendor.  The General store has cute Philadelphia souvenirs as well as local candy and cookies.  This place is fun for locals and tourists!

Excellent variety of all things food. However, I always find myself at the Greek booth which always has seats available at their counter. This time I went for the edamame fritters (similar to falafel). Bright presentation that was quite flavorful. Give this booth a try the next time you're meandering your way through the market!

If you just like good food, this is a great place for lunch. I was so impressed by the first time I ate, I went back again two days later to try something else. 

I forgot to take pictures, but the wrap and the bowel are delicious. If I had one complaint it would be not enough garlic whip, because I can put that on anything. But good news is you can order extra which makes me happy. 

I also ordered the side dish with cheese inside (both)...next time I am ordering more then one. It was like a tease. 

This might be my go to spot, especially since I can order online and just pick it up without a hassle.

This place doesn't really need any more 5 star reviews but I love the place so here goes another one.  If you're visiting Philadelphia and you love to eat food then you have to visit.  Huge place filled with every type of food imaginable with a large amount of Amish restaurants and shops featuring the best that PA has to offer!  Tons of amazing cheese shops, fresh produce, bakeries everywhere, fresh pretzels, Philly cheesesteaks, fresh meats, the list goes on and on!  Open 7 days but Sundays the Amish businesses are closed so about 30% of the place isn't open that day.  Give yourself amble time to browse as the amount of places to choose from is staggering.  A must stop on any trip to Philadelphia.  Enjoy!!
Best market in the entire USA! There's food for every appetite, I eat there almost everyday

What an awesome location in the heart of Philadelphia for awesome food! Reading Terminal Market has a variety of vendors - from home and garden to sandwiches to ice creams to Chinese food to Philly Cheesesteaks to desserts, and MORE! However, there is an extreme lack of seating areas to actually sit down and eat!

P.S. The Flying Monkey has the best desserts!

What I ordered: 

General Tso's (2)
Cheesesteak (2)
Buffalo Chicken (2)
Broccoli (2)
Spinach (1)
Mushroom Risotto (1) 
Chicken Pot Pie Noodles

What I got:

Spinach (3)
Cheesesteak (3)
Asian Pork (3)
Mushroom Risotto (1)
Chicken Pot Pie Noodles 

The noodles were awesome. The person taking my order was pleasant. 

What I got otherwise was just okay. I could have done without the Spinach altogether (3 of the worst thing of the order - boo). Not 1 chicken dumpling to be found in the lot. 

Definitely could have been a 100 times better.

I read about this place randomly on someone's top 100 pizza places in the U.S. and no lies were told. 

Great pizza. Specialty pizza is always going to be a winner. Always. I have not one slice of specialty pizza from here that I didn't like.  The specials change every week. You can also get your regular cheese only or pepperoni. The cheese pizza is pretty good. (I do not know what the pepperoni pizza is like). 

The crust is literally perfect; the crisp, the thinness. Although the menu is extremely limited, what they do, they do well. Four to Five napkins for sure.

Mixed results. Ordered the chicken and lamb platter as well as the beef tikka roll.

The chicken and lamb was fine flavor wise. The rice was terribly cooked. I was very surprised by an Indian variant restaurant having poor rice, crunchy sandy rice is not a pleasant texture. I would not order again.

Beef tikka, amazing. This is what I was looking for when I came into this restaurant. Flavorful, the roll had grilled flavor, everything you could want. 

If I ever came here again, I would only order from the Kati roll side of the menu.

This place never disappoints. I always get their paneer masala kati roll and one roll really fills me up. It's quick, delicious, easy to eat on the go and won't break your wallet! I also love their mint lemonade

OH BOY!  Foodie fun!   I enjoyed the place a lot and I purposely stayed in a hotel right nearby so I could breeze over there morning noon and before closing. I cant say night as they aren't open at night. 

    You can find all sorts of food!  Plenty to eat!  Would be great to have a place like this next door!    

    Helpful hint at one door on Race Street they have a holder of maps. GET ONE. I had some coupons for some of the businesses and it was hard to find them!  Its crowded and you have a hard time seeing signs through the crowds. That map was certainly helpful.  I'll post a pic of the map too!

    I cant give the place 5 stars though because of one major drawback. Crowds.  They need more space. I don't know whats upstairs but someone sometime back should have found a way to make another floor up there. They have maybe 100? 150? seats in central areas but those are only a small fraction of the demand. If you go with a family or group and you want to sit and eat together you have to go off hour or you can forget that idea!  Mid day Sat is a madhouse.  Individual vendors often have seats at their counters too but often just 5,6 or 7 chairs. Again if theres many of you you can forget that!

   Prices are not low either, but you can hunt for bargains. You will find some marking down items in the last hour or two. Especially bakeries that bag it all for a flat price, and put it on top of the counter. They want the counter bare when they go home.

   The actual fruit and vegetable vendors left are only a few, so not much there or major interest.  Lots of sweets, candy, honey, meats, cold cuts, sandwiches, turkey, ice cream etc. 
  
    Bassetts is the oldest ice cream in the USA. I had a coupon there but no way was I going to try and carry it and eat with such a crowd.

     Its fun though to walk through and maybe grab a few things to go and then find yourself a place where you can sit and enjoy it later.

Came here for a quick bite and split an achaari paneer Kati roll with a friend. Loved the spicy flavor and the texture of the paneer was done perfectly. Good combo of foods in there. 

We also ordered chai for 5 and had to wait quite a while to get them. We waited 10 minutes for our Kati roll and then another 15 for the masala chai. I guess a fresh batch needed to be made but I would recommend not ordering chai if you're in a hurry or can order ahead. It was cool that we could see the chai being made in the back in a big pot. And the staff was apologetic about the long wait time. The chai itself was good, It's not made with sugar so you'll have to add your own but it's delicious!
A Philadelphia treasure. You can get just about anything there. If you're a sweets person I highly recommend Termini's cannoli, and Beiler's donuts are arguably the best in the city.
Ummmm. Seating is tricky here and it is not friendly for the kiddos. It's hard to find something healthy to eat and it is always crowded.

I absolutely LOVED this place! I'm only in Philly for a few weeks so I wanted the full tourist experience so went to RTM and I truly enjoyed it. I will admit it was a bit overwhelming because we went there on a weekend and the place was so crowded we could barely move haha but it's all part of the experience I suppose. 

We got food from a few restaurants. We got Philly cheesesteaks from Spataro's (delicious!) and banana pies from this other dessert place (also delicious!!). 

There's also a relatively big produce market at the back of RTM. It looked great but we didn't get anything from there.

Overall, I would definitely go again if I have time. The place was a little bit dirty I thought in terms of trash on the floors but that is to be expected of any crowded public place I guess. Great eating joints and a fun place to go if you're a tourist ;)

What can I say about Reading Market Terminal that's not already been said before. It is centrally located at the heart of Philly in front of the Philadelphia Convention Center. Awesome Philly vibe, lots of cool shops and stores surrounded by ton of people. This place is a Philadelphia staple and definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.

For foodie tourists (like me) a stroll through Reading Terminal Market is basically baptism by fire. In other words, food porn to the max. Everything you could possibly crave in one (huge) place. I left, silent and stunned, with blood oranges, a block of chocolate shaped like a cheesesteak, herbs, spices, Amish goods, honey, looseleaf tea, I don't even know what else. The sheer number of food vendors, markets, specialty goods-- absolutely blew me away. 

Next time I'm going to be first in line at DiNic's for a pork sandwich. And if anyone beats me to it, I'll trample them.

Wow. There's so much food here. My husband and I only walked around munching on snacks here and there and even those blew us away. We tried ube pandan which was super soft. We've had the best sweet potato pie we've ever had!!!! There's so many venues, but they are organized well in neat rows so that you can't get lost. It was the neatest market maze I've ever seen. They close early though so I recommend breakfast and lunch here. Philly is pretty easy to get around on foot and using the bus transit. I do not recommend driving in - the streets are incredibly narrow.

I love this place! I always take the train and get off at Jefferson station right next to it. So many different types of foods to try. Whether you want a cheesesteak at Carmen's or a cannoli at Termini. The donuts at Beilers and pretzels at Millers are amazing too. You can't go wrong here! It's always packed inside even when I went early but it's always worth it!

This little piggy went to market,
This little piggy definitely didn't stay home,
This little piggy had roast beef and a bunch of other crap to,
This little piggy had none (what an idiot),
And this little piggy cried wee wee wee all the way home because they were full as shit after eating non-stop for over an hour.

This place is seriously dope.  It reminds me of faneuil hall marketplace in Boston except it is a legit market with local vendors where you can get everything from produce to baked goods as opposed to just being a giant food court. I mean they have that too but at least they can legitimately call themselves a market.

My biggest advice is buy stuff from anyone who looks remotely amish.  Their baked goods are incredible.  Sticky buns and pecan pie that I had there has me salivating right now thinking about it.

Also 2 hour parking for $4 with validation from a vendor here.  Go to the website for specifics.  But how awesome is that?

Downside?  Crowded as all hell.  Be prepared to throw elbows, shoulders, and dropkicks or be really quick on your feet in order to get a table to sit at.

There's was a bug in my salad and I didn't realize it until I was halfway done. I'm giving two stars because I think the hot foods may be okay and less likely to be infested. I do feel sick after eating

Love this place. We don't often get here but when I'm town love to meander, look at all the unique vendors, eat, and of course take some things home!

Parking easy to find in a few block radius. Expect to pay a lot!

Horrible location. Get people bothering you soliciting inside store so you can't even eat in peace. Also wasn't impressed to order chicken strips to get what looked to me like they were run over before placing them in my box. I'm wondering where the rest of my meat went and can I get it back.

Reading Terminal Market is an amazing place to come to and walk around.  It will be crowded, especially on the weekends, but it's worth it to come by.  They have about 20 places to eat lunch or dinner at, from cheesesteaks, to pizza, to seafood, to gyros, to Chinese food and more.

My wife loves the bakeries above all, there are fresh cookies, breads doughnuts cannoli and more.  You can also get fresh jams to put on your bread.  They have several Dutch bakeries within the market.

Definitely come stop by, it's worth it!
I love the Reading Terminal!!  Best parking dedal in the city!!  $5 for 2 hours!!

I once dreamt that I entered a food paradise, where I was surrounded by a palatial assortment of yummy eats and sweet delights.  That in this same place I could get a steaming order of Shanghai soup dumplings, and just as easily turn around and get an Amish-made hand-rolled pretzel, or even some Mediterranean food.  Perhaps instead of the pretzel, I could go for some luxury chocolates or world famous cookies or ice cream.  I dreamt that I'd be in the same place that once found Bizarre Foods host, Andrew Zimmern eating a whole chocolate-dipped, yellow onion.  

In this dreamland of food, I would enjoy the most incredible key lime pudding while sitting in a comfortable little cafeteria, all the while taking in the lovely sounds of a live pianist playing the tune to "Memories" from the Broadway show, Cats.  

All was well with this place.  One wound find produce galore, from jumbo, tiger shrimp at least 4 inches long, to all types of sweet delicacies (Turkish delight, and an exotic pastry called "Burma"), to savory local favorites (Philly cheesesteaks, pulled pork sandwiches), and even some household goods, flowers and jewelry.  

The New Yorker in me wished that this glorious place would be a perfect hybrid cross between Essex Market and Chelsea Markets, boasting of high quality offerings at affordable prices.  How amazing would this be, how glorious would this look.  How swell then, that when I came to my senses, I discovered this was no dream at all, only all this wishful thinking led me to discover Philly's Reading Terminal Market.  

Yes, this food paradise does exist.  And in this magical place, I only had to pay $1.50 for THE most amazing chocolate whoopie pie the size of my outstretched palm (BEILER'S BAKERY, FOR THE WIN).  Just, wow.  

If you're planning a trip to Philly, don't miss out on RTM.  It's a straight forward, down-to-earth food-lovers oasis.

Everybody is so excited about a food hall now, and Reading Terminal Market is doing it old school cool. There was an impressive row of just ice cream, and I was so excited even though I don't eat ice cream. All of the flavors that make Philadelphia delicious are represented. And it's a great place to people watch.

This place is easily one of the wonder's of the east coast.

From food to goods, to skin and hair care, the market yields natural care inside and out of all kinds. My personal favorite of the market, is food of course, but the legendary roast pork sandwich, to the rib sandwich I swear my father and law drove down for. We even had our fair share of garlic bacon we had the opportunity to taste many times before walking away with a whole pound of it and an amish butter.

This place overall is amazing, and we need more places like it EVERYWHERE!

I just moved to the area and I'm SO happy Masala Kitchen is close by. Their Kati rolls are incredible! They're just the right size for a small to medium meal. Very filling but if you're super super hungry, order a side. Then read is delicious, as are the fillings. I'll definitely be making this a frequent stop.
A busy place with a lot options but food in general are just ok.  Not worth stopping by.

Reading terminal is always crowded with long lives but good food don't forget to try the D-
nicks

Better than the best lunch truck festival. Anything you could possibly want to eat cooked fresh and authentic. I was there during a big convention time so it was pretty crowded. That made getting around a challenge but the wait times were not long and there was plenty of room to sit and enjoy. I'll go back on a less crowded day to spend more time sampling.

Another great Cfa in philly.... Was at Ikea. Choose to stop for lunch... Was packed with lines almost at the door. But moved fast... Got my food pretty quickly. Always get the spicy chicken deluxe meal. So good...

It's nice and clean inside. Bathroom always clean as well. The drive thru is always a line going around. But i assume when the food is more healthier then other fast food places... You are always going to have lines.

Would definitely come back to this location again.

This place is completely disorganized! After ordering our salads we got into line to pay. People are standing everywhere ordering salads and sandwiches and it's a totally mess. My sister wanted to order a smoothie and asked what was in it and the girl had no idea. She finally got an answer from 3 confused people who worked there and ended up getting the wrong smoothie (she ordered strawberry and got piña colada). When we went to pay they said which salads are yours? Looking at them they all looked the same and no one knew who's salads were whose. The salads were mediocre. I wouldn't recommend!

A lifetime of poor choices has taught me to appreciate the small things in life. I tend to set the bar pretty low and go for the lowest hanging fruit because I usually don't see the point in trying. 

Today was different. A burst of inspiration motivated me to leave the house. Where to go with no destination in mind? I thought for a second and then the lightbulb went off: McDonalds.

McDonalds is a American restaurant that tastes so good. If you have not been to one you have probably at least seen one maybe. I like the tasty fries which go right in my mouth I cannot gobble them fast enough.

On my way home I found a large tooth on the sidewalk outside. It was a really good day.

You can't come here and have the traditional complaints of "not enough seating" or "too long of a wait" because that is all part of the charm here. I love that every time I visit though, I go in thinking I want X for lunch but end up wandering around for half an hour before I actually settle on X. Too many amazing options.

Highlights for me:

1) Cheesesteak sandwiches (I down one every year during jury duty)
2) Amish pies (got two for Thanksgiving this year and felt blessed)
3) Produce market (well priced)
4) Nice place to get fudge
This place is the bomb!!!! The paneer Kati rolls are my fav. Cute. Clean. Quick. Good service. I definitely recommend.

Oh my goodness. I know this can be a late night drunk spot (open until 3am on weekends), but let me tell you as someone who found this diamond in the rough open after a long day at work yesterday, I was so ecstatic. I got two Kati rolls for about $12, and they were absolutely delicious. This place even sticks to my golden rule and put egg in the Kati rolls (egg makes everything better, don't @ me). Will definitely be back

We had our wedding 3 weeks ago here at the market and it could not have gone better. We worked with the team at All About Events, who were not only professional, competent, efficient, and organized - but their care for us as bride and groom was evident every step of the way. We felt they were as invested in our wedding being amazing as we were. Everything they orchestrated in the months leading up to our wedding went off without a hitch. 

We wanted a wedding where we could have different kinds of food (instead of just your typical wedding food) - and we got exactly what we wanted, with Philadelphia charm and style to spare! The atmosphere at Reading Terminal Market is energetic, but classy. We sprung for the market string lights and with the vendor signs and decor already in the market, it provided the perfect ambiance. There was plenty of space for a dance floor and Molly Malloy's did a fantastic job with the drink service. We were so in love with the whole evening. Would DEFINITELY recommend this as a unique and flexible wedding spot (we had 250 guests and they can accommodate even more than that!)

We would absolutely recommend events at Reading Terminal Market!

SIDE NOTE: Coming here for lunch, produce, meat, sweets and other food is absolutely recommended TOO!! It is a Philly institution and one of the best places to experience the food the city has to offer in an energetic, affordable and fun setting.

5 stars for their pizzas. Thin crispy delicious slices of heaven. One star reduction for customer service mainly due to their random closing of the restaurant. Three times in the past few months we went with note "closed for the day" taped to the window. They also randomly close early or open late. They don't have working phone number so no phone-in-orders and you never know if they're open or not.  Go at your own risk!   But if you go and they're open OMG their pizzas are fantastic.

We have been coming to the Reading Terminal Market for as long as we can remember. Place is always packed with workers nearby grabbing a bite to eat and tourists. I warn you, it is really crowded here all the time. Here are some of the food stalls worth stopping for:

Bassetts Ice Cream -
The first merchant to sign a lease at the Reading Terminal Market in 1892. This place is still owned and run by the same family. With more than 40 flavors, you can have your pick. The cone comes with a generous scoop(s).

Beiler's Bakery -
One of the best donuts. If this is your first time here, don't be deterred by the long line. You often hear people giving up when they see how long the line is. It moves pretty fast  and the best part, you get to see first hand how they make it in front of you. By the time you're midway through, grab a menu, choose your donuts so you don't hold up the line. My son who doesn't like sweets love Beilers'. Note: Not open on Sundays.

Flying Monkey -
The owner with the love of the movie, "The Wizard of Oz", named her bakery Flying Monkey. When I first discovered this place, they were famous for their amazing cupcakes but nowadays, it's more on their award winning Whoopie pies. The Whoopie pies were named the best in the world and it comes in many flavors. Another must try is their Elvis cake. We usually buy a huge slice home. Every item is made from scratch.

Dutch Eating Place -
The only item we have tried here is their amazing warm apple dumpling with cinnamon which is served with a dollop of cool heavy cream. It is to die for.

The Original Turkey -
I don't like eating turkey and the only turkey I will eat from is "The Original Turkey". You can see how juicy it is when they carve it right in front of you! Served with all your typical Thanksgiving fixings, you can have this all year round. You can also order it sandwich style. Don't forget to ask for extra gravy. 

Bee Natural -
I love to make my famous French toast at home. Instead of using syrup I prefer to use honey. I'm always pleased with the quality of their honey here. When I run low, I make sure to grab a bottle or two.

These are just a handful of stalls we frequent. The list goes on. There are also lots of counter lunch spots, food stalls and fresh produce. A must visit in the heart of Philly. 

If you park at the Reading Terminal, you can get a discounted parking for $4 if you buy $10 and over at any one of the merchants at the Reading Terminal. Just have them validate your parking ticket. Remember, it is only good for 2 hours. Otherwise it will be $10 for 2 1/2 hours.

Reading Terminal Market is AMAZING! I have been over and over again yet it always feels impossible to try all of the delicious food. They have done an excellent job with COVID safety procedures and have allowed us to continue enjoying all our favorites from there! So happy to continue supporting this community fixture.

I love that there are many different options available at Reading Terminal Market, to suit every craving. Being Filipino, I appreciate that they hosted a Filipino Heritage Food fest that featured cultural foods. The ambiance is ideal for any foodie, and there is something for everyone to try. Come hungry! And save room for dessert!

I could spend hours in here! It is so easy to find and you're in for a treat that will appeal to all of your senses. Inside you'll find endless cuisine options, handmade goods, cheese shops, butchers, local spirit tasting, a sports bar, and sweets. 

My suggested plan of attack is to start at Molly Malloy's where you can grab a local brew then sip, shop, and eat your way through it all! I loved our my meal at Pearl's. My boo and I shared a seafood platter and it was one of the best meals I've had this year. All of the seafood was perfectly cooked and tender, not too salty and super fresh. We also did some major damage at Downtown Cheese Shop.  And yes you can sample anything you want to buy. We even sampled some truffle cheeses before purchasing. They were very generous and attentive. 

Plan on spending a good bit of time here if you've never been. You will not be disappointed. Everyone I dealt with was incredibly friendly and helpful! It was the highlight of my visit!

Wow. Just wow. This is a foodies dream come true. A market with fresh amazing food within steps of each other. We tried 6-7 places and we could not get enough. Also we were on a three day trip and went all three days. We had Philly cheese steaks, pretzels, donuts- do not forget the donuts and pretzels!, chicken and waffles, roast beef, corned beef, cheeses, and cannolis. It was the best place for us to sample and split. We like to visit places and try out their food scene and this have such an amazing sampling of the area. I highly recommend. 
Note- it is busy! If you ca. grab you food and eat on the way. Do that or don't go at lunch rush. It was crazyyyy
My family love it here. I love all of amazing foods and goodies they have. Every December when my kids were younger we always went to see the trains.

Reading Terminal Market is my favorite public market in the world!!!  Whenever we visit Philly, this is the first place I want to visit!  This indoor public market houses so many of my favorite places!  It is simply amazing that to have them all in one location.

"Today the Reading Terminal Market is one of the nation's most successful public markets with more than 75 independent small businesses that offer an array of fresh and prepared foods, lunch counters, and places to eat and shop."

These are my "Must Go To" spots at Reading Terminal Market:

1)  DiNic's  (for the best sandwich ever!!!)

2)  Bassetts Ice Cream  (the oldest ice cream company in the U.S.)

3)  Famous 4th Street Cookie Company  

4)  Flying Monkey Bakery

These four places are my absolute favorite "5 Star" places that I have visited here so far!  

I can't wait to go back to Philadelphia and Reading Terminal Market!

There are still many other places that I have yet to try here!  

Reading Terminal Market......you are a dream come true to me!!!  ;)
From the outside it doesnt scream to you but onve you walk in its like a childs dream from deli food to sweets and snack, to seafood just about anything you can think of they have it

Came here with my wife and some friends recently, and I really enjoyed it! First, parking was pretty expensive but also not too hard to find, so it could have been worse :) Inside, there were many, many different restaurants serving high quality food! I ended up eating some donuts, a corn dog, and half of a pastrami sandwich, and all were super tasty. It's definitely crowded and can take a few minutes to order, but honestly, I was expecting a longer wait. Getting a seat in the dining area can be a little challenging since you basically have to hover around like vultures and swoop in when people are gathering their trash, but it never took us too long (we sat down two separate times) and the staff were actually very helpful in helping us locate an extra chair when we needed one. Oh, and there was a bar inside, so that was a plus for us :)

Anyway, I definitely recommend you come check this place out!

I absolutely love going to Reading Terminal Market. It's foodie paradise! The pretzels at Miller's Twist are just out of this world. There's some great little produce markets in there as well as Amish baked goods and donuts. If you're looking for good cookies and fried chicken, you can definitely find it here! You can also get so many different sausage varieties to cook at home. I like to get the kind with lemon juice, garlic, white wine, and parsley. There's something for everyone here!

Yo the barista's in Philly are built different, nyc native here visiting Philly and they are really risking it all for the brand. Starbucks, give this Man a RAISE! We were sitting in the cafe when the SB employee came over to a couple (seemingly homeless) and gave them a fair warning to leave, since they had been sleeping on the benches and were repeatedly asked not to. The exchange became hostile after the couple refused to leave along with their suitcases and bags of stuff. (Meanwhile bops were playing from Donna Summer and Lana Del Rey) the man of the couple had started to threaten the employee saying "You got the wrong one!" And "I'll show you what time it is big boy!" The employee did not back down for a second and insisted on maintaining a safe space for us. I appreciate a barista who can make a mean mocha and bring the hands when necessary.
Great place to shop, eat, browse, or hang out. Competitive prices and varied merchandise. The Reading Terminal is a long standing fixture of Philadelphia, and we'll worth a visit.

The terminal is a staple in Philadelphia. It's a wonderful way to shop and eat from multiple restaurants as shops. One of my favorites is sang key, a must try is the roast pork wonton noodle soup  with a side of additional pork, simply amazing. 
Hershel Jewish deli is also a favorite, home made corned beef and other goodies!
There is something for everyone at reading terminal
It's worth your time. We went During Xmas rush. And had a blast. Tons of people, endless food. Great time if you're ever near Philly. There's something for everyone here

This place has something for everyone. If you don't have a lot of time, But you want to take a little bit of everything in, this is the place to come too. Seafood, honey, Philly cheesesteaks, lunch buffet, everything you could possibly want.

This place is always a great site to stop at especially if you're visiting downtown and you've never been there. Great lunch spot with tons of variety and neat shops. Chris Vtrainers Personal Training

I really just loved coming here when I came down to Philly for the weekend. I'm a big fan of food halls in general, but the experience here was awesome. We had looked at the vendors ahead of time, but really the best thing to do is just walk around and find what you like. 

We started off with smoothies from Kamal's, which were delicious. They tasted so fresh and had no added sugar which made me feel better and it was a light start. We then had beef patties from Careda's - so good and exactly what I was looking for. 

Next we had corn dogs from Fox and Son, which I was actually the most excited about. They dip every one to order so you know it's fresh! It was super crispy and the sausage was delicious as well. I wish I had tried one of the specialty ones though! We finished off with take home from Sang Kee Peking Duck, mostly because I love duck and I wanted some lo mein. Also delicious and even better as a late night bite!

The other amazing thing is all the produce and meat stands they have here. There were so many local products from Lancaster and everything looked beautiful and fresh. We had planned on buying fresh to bring home to Jersey on Sunday- however, a good portion of the stands are closed on Sundays, including most of the fresh meat stands and local products so keep that in mind if you drop in on a weekend!
I love everything about this place, the variety of foods, but most importantly the QUALITY of foods. It makes me jealous of Philadelphians - I wish I lived nearer.

Always alive.  Some favorites are the New York style deli, the veggies at the food market and the little shops.  I could go on and on, but if you are not familiar with it, just put it onto your agenda.  It's a slice of Phila like nothing else...anywhere.

I remember when this was a railroad terminal.  Hard to tell now.
Pretty good, a little crowded and some stores were sold out of things, but good food and fun overall. There was nice music outside and it was a cool atmosphere. I'd go again.
DiNic's roast pork and beef is fantastic.  Asian places are all good.  The fresh fruit, veggies and butcher shops are incrediblel.  Must go!!

Who does not love this place? Every corner is filled with food and things to drool over. I've been here a couple of times and each time you end up trying something new. Sometimes I wish I lived nearby so that I could take advantage of all their fresh produce. 

I highly recommend Bassetts. DiNic's was pretty good too. The Spice/tea/coffee shop near the bookstore is really of great value!

You get anything from breakfast to lunch at this place.  It offers so many choices and they are all good!! A must if you are in a group with everyone wants something else.  Or you are like me want to taste everything! Great location and good pit stop or a starting point.  Love this place.

Some friends and I had a pretty awesome Sunday Funday at The Industry yesterday. I was quite happy to be reunited with the Ghost of Mary, one of my favorite spin-offs of a Bloody Mary that I had long missed since the closing of Swift Half. After several of those, our table decided it was time to share the Mummer's Punch. The serving suggestion is for 4-6 people, and we had three with two latecomers. There was more than enough for everyone. 

Two people at our table were at The Industry long enough for brunch and dinner. I heard good things about brunch but can only report on dinner. The burger with bacon was good, not great. I'm not going out of my way for it, but it is a decent option. The pickle mayo (which I asked for on the side) provided a nice dipper for the fries. A lot of the menu consists of items for the more adventurous palate (sweetbreads, pig ears, bone marrow, lamb neck, etc.). I am most definitely not in that category but there were still plenty of things to choose from. I'm interested in trying the porchetta sandwich and the fried green tomatoes.

Our servers were great and very attentive throughout our long stay. The music selection was awesome (although the Internet jukebox provided for some say in the matter - not complaining at all, just an observation). I'm looking forward to my next visit.

The best place in Philly to eat lunch. All of food places are top notch. The prices are not cheap but you get your money's worth. The soul food place is second to none but a long line for a good reason. It's worth the wait! The Down Home Diner is good for breakfast. Old City Coffee has the best smells and the best iced tea I have ever had. Almost anything in food you can find here.
This place... I'm not sure there's anything negative to say. There SOO many options that it's kind of hard to choose from.
Being from San Francisco and having the once proud Ferry building for foodies, the Reading Terminal was a dream place to enjoy. Spent a lot of time and money and look forward to returning.

Humpty's first had me at Dumplings. And whether you go with steamed or fried you end up with succulent balls of perfection that are the best that you won't find in Chinatown or dim sum spots.

Humpty's puts a bit of an Americanized twist on the dim sum classic, which actually kind of works since it gives you options like broccoli & cheddar and honey chipotle chicken. And since its in South Philly you'd best believe that they have a cheesesteak dumpling! My favorite though is definitely the Asian pork with perfectly cooked pork shoulder highlighted by classic ginger, soy, and scallions. 

No matter what you choose, grabbing 5 for $7 makes for the perfect mix and match meal. Especially when they have seasonal dumplings that include a dessert option. But non-dumpling lovers will also find solace in their noodle and salad options.

Room temperature Fries this Wendy's disappoints yet again. Yep will not allow me to leave this as a review at it unless I use more characters it suggests I post as a tip again. Also, Apparently buying  Large Fries to go gets you zero ketchup in bag

Pizza itself was fantastic. No question it's some of the best pie around. But it's another spot following this trend of having great pizza but punishing their customers with arbitrary business operation you wouldn't tolerate from Little Caesars much less a place that charges $24 for a pizza. It's the pizza equivalent of making people wait in a line to get into a club that's half full just to make it seem more exclusive.  No phone, no delivery, erratic hours, they can simply run out at any given time. Customers are literally bargaining at the cashier to battle for upcoming slices coming out of the oven rather than being able to simply order what they want. The wait could be as little as 20 minutes or as long as an hour. The employees themselves were very courteous in trying to keep everyone happy inside of a ridiculous business model.

Please someone invent a good pizza place that doesn't treat their customers like it's 2009 and you're trying to buy the iPhone on opening day.

THE spot to take visitors to in Philadelphia. No, not the Independence Hall, or the Museum of Art, or even to get a cheese steak. If you really want to celebrate freedom, give yourself the freedom to do a Rocky Run through the aisles of RTM, picking out and putting in your stomach any and everything delicious that comes to mind. Tons of choices, from amish baked goods to chinese food to soul food to crepes to gyros to amish baked goods to actual groceries. Did I mention amish baked goods? It may seem chaotic when you visit. Good. Embrace it. It is the Pennsylvania Madhouse Farmer's Market from Hell, and you'll enjoy your visit. Here are some Go-To Spots.

Beiler's Bakery: Amish Donuts. Get a dozen of them. Regret Nothing
Hatville Deli: Corned Beef Special Sandwich
Termini Bros. Bakery: Cannolis

Next to chinatown, so you can get your fill of fantastic food from both sectors and then take a nap by Independence Hall, like the Sons of Liberty did. At least...I'm pretty sure that's what they did.
Everything here is fantastic. Spices, PA Dutch foods, fresh produce, chocolate, honey, and snazzy lunchies everywhere. Also great place for dates

This particular Chipotle is the worst in Philadelphia,I've been here multiple times already the tables are filthy always and at 630pm when closing at 10 pm don't have rice and steak !Always something with this location it's def my last time coming here !Management def has to step and do something about this business,obviously I'm not the only one with the same complaints! It's not worth the one star

With a few rainy days coming in I knew this foodie had to stock up on delectable provisions and the market was the best place for that! I first encountered the market on a lunch break on the only sunny day during a business trip two years ago and knew I had to come back and explore. I brought two bags with me and left with fresh produce, fresh baked bread, the best looking Amish deli meats and cheese I had ever seen, spanakopita, lasagna, pretzel dogs, and cookies. A second trip a few days later with a friend we enjoyed sharing a burger and a cheesesteak at the diner...something for everyone and a must do experience visiting Philly!

Service was fast, my friend put an order while walking from the dog park on South St. Walked over to pick up the food and it was already ready. The food was good, I got the paneer roll and he got the chicken masala. Oh also, get the red sauce if you love spice. I love spice.

I haven't been there in a while, but it was always bustling and crowded with people looking for a delicious (but not cheap) lunch.  At the south end near the middle is a great mushrooms stand that sells Hen of the Woods.  Sautee these tiny mushroom clusters and add them to spaghetti sauce for a real treat.  The selection of cheeses in the market is enormous (most are made with animal rennet).  I'm a fan of Malone's restaurant, which is one of the few places in the market with comfortable seating.  There was a tv documentary made about the market in which they interviewed the owner, and he seemed like a good-hearted and hard working person.  Another treat in the market is chocolates, mostly on the west side.  It's a great place to spend a lively afternoon.  Go a little early or late to avoid the peak of the lunch hour.

If you come to Philly you must stop here. Easy parking in the garage across the street and public transportation accessible. 

Amazing vendors and the food is crazy diverse and good.

I think an update is in order because the market has changed a lot and I don't think for the better.My perspective may  be skewed by the fact that the place was incredibly crowded on that wonderful semi holiday Black Friday but what I noticed is the market is much less a market and much more a food court.I used to buy things here and look at things.Now there isn't as  much to buy or look at.You can eat but then again you always could .So I think it's beginning to get a bit boring.

Eating some thanksgiving dinner dumplings as I type this! Humpty's has a good product and I think my favorite is either the cauliflower or spinach ricotta. Don't forget that you can mix and match dumplings in one order and you can also get them steamed instead of fried which is a nice treat once in a while.

After the renovations, this particular Chick-fil-A looks marginally better, but is too open. Now you can see everyone from everywhere across the room rather than have your own private spot with a partition. The food seemed the same at first, but last night I had a violent stomach reaction to the food I ate, which was the spicy chicken strips meal. I also felt terrible this morning, too, as my body forced the rest of it out. I typically LOVE Chick-fil-A and praise this company to no end, but not anymore after last night. The only thing I can think of is someone didn't wash their hands.

Starbucks never ceases to amaze me with their policy on allowing the crumb bums and vagrants to take naps, store their belongings and stink the place up.  Beautiful new location. Lots of space to stretch out and nap. Friendly staff. Get rid of the crumb bums and smelly vagrants.

food was good,hard to find a late nice place that sells real food and not fast food.i like the extra white sauces included.meal just isnt complete without the sauce on it.will be calling again.i work late nights so this is perfect

Omg Pizza Shackamaxon tomato  pie is the best I've ever had!! It all started with a simple message "can I order 2 tomato pies for the ER and they fondly responded with a yes and on top of that they donated them to the front line. I love pizza and I had another favorite tomato pie for years however, this tomato pie is  unbelievably good! I had a slice driving into work and I can't wait to share it with my co-workers. Thank you!!!  You are my new favorite tomato pie.
good place to eat kati roll it is also open late .

The Reading Terminal Market is one of Philadelphia's gems. If you're indecisive (like me) it can be both a dream come true and a nightmare. I found myself in Philly today and thought I stop by to brainstorm on dinner. I found some good cuts of meats, walked around and came up with some side items to go with the entree. There are so many choices that it took me entirely too long to decide but having too many options is hardly a problem (or it is a quintessential first world problem). I grabbed some coffee and lunch while I was there, browsed around a bit more and left satisfied. You can count on finding high quality goods here with prices that rival any supermarket and restaurant, bakery, etc. 

When I left this morning I thought I don't take advantage of the fact that this amazing place is so close to me often enough. It was then that I made a promise to myself to come back soon (and often).

If you are looking to buy a MINI, whether you live in the Washington D.C. area or not, I recommend that you contact BLAKE DACOSTA of Passport MINI in Alexandria, VA.  I live in Delaware but I worked with Blake online to find the perfect car as a birthday present for my wife.  Blake was responsive, informative, courteous and always helpful.  When it came time to pick up the MINI, Blake had all of the paperwork ready, provided me with some additional advice and made the entire process smooth and transparent.  If you want to buy a MINI from an honest and knowledgeable sales associate, in my opinion, you won't find a better choice than BLAKE DACOSTA.

Lots of options to choose from, whether it's to catch a bite to eat, purchase some groceries or meats for a meal at home, satisfy your sweet tooth or other. Depending, there are also special attractions like a moving train exhibit for certain holidays. Both private and street parking available. The only downside is that it gets really crowded and finding a place to sit and eat can be challenging.

Whether you live in Philly or are visiting from out of town this is always a great place to visit!  The food and awesome variety of local vendors just adds to the ambiance.  A true melting pot of cultural experiences!  I've been a customer for over 20 years and love every time I go!  I've even made friends with some of the long time vendors there.  You get treated like family!
LOVE. Get the Di Nic's Roast Pork "Italian Style" which is chopped fine with seasoning. No cheese. Amazing.
Some good places to eat, some not, I'd say it's overstated, the down home diner really kills it for me, really bad food.

Love it here!!!! Drove from NY to get some cheesesteaks and decided to walk around here amd open our appetite.  WTH were we thinking.  We left full lol...We sampled everything and it's a must to try the FRIED MAC & CHEESE BALLS FROM THE CAJUN SPOT. (I forgot the name, sorry) just walk around you'll find it. Head to 2nd ave (every aisle has an ave name) and try the cookies from FAMOUS  4TH ST COOKIES, its AMAZING. SOFT,WARM ,DELICIOUS & FAMOUS ;)

Reading Terminal Market is one of the largest and oldest public markets in the country, so when a friend and I were visiting Philadelphia last weekend, we knew we had to visit! The market is jam-packed full of different stands and vendors: baked goods, butchers, produce stands, fishmongers, cheese shops, etc. It's tight, crowded, hot, and full of delicious looking goods. Definitely worth visiting, but be aware that it's crowded during busy hours!
The BEST lunch. So much food for a reasonable price. It's flavorful and delicious. I order ahead on the website and pick it up from their shelves. I can usually get two meals out of a bowl.

Brought a group of 23 high school students here for lunch one day and dinner the next. What an amazing place. There is literally something for everyone. Ethnic food galore and something for any food allergy. Tons of food and drink options and so many privately owned restaurants with specialty homemade food items.  During busier times, seating gets very limited and lines can get pretty long but it's worth the wait. Some of the prices are inflated but it's what you'd expect for a prime tourist attraction, staple of Philly history and so many (not all) homemade food items.  Perfect place to bring a large group or a solo meal. I will definately be back!!

So so fun. Must see if you are in the city! Grab yourself a cheesesteak or some amazing Italian food at Pizza by George and don't leave without some fresh juice from the market in the back and a doughnut from Beiler's! Or stop by their bakery! So delicious!

This place is crowded as hell. I got some expensive shrimp raw shrimps but they were jumbo and 2lbs ribs cooked. All in all the food was good just the crowd is a lot this is not a place for one who doesn't do well with crowds.

I always enjoy stopping by Reading Terminal Market. Whether you're in the mood for ice cream, authentic chinese, donuts, diner food, and more. You'll find it here.

I love getting the peking duck rolls. It's my Go-To whenever I'm here. I also love the little kitchen shop they have towards the back. I have yet to try the donuts because there's always a long line, but I really want to!

The ice cream is absoutely delicious as well. As unfortunate as it sounds, I kind of prefer visiting now during the pandemic because it's not as crazy packed as it usually is. Prior to the pandemic, you'd basically be shoulder to shoulder with guests. Nowadays you actually have some room to walk. Definitely stop by but wear your mask & bring hand sanitizer!

We stopped into the Market on a Saturday for lunch. At first it can be a little overwhelming because of all of the food and drink options. Everywhere you turn there is another store. Highly recommend going and try it out. 

There was limited seating options because of how busy it was, but the turnover at the tables was decent and a very nice lady that worked for the market cleaned the tables immediately after someone got up. We will definitely be back when we head back to Philly.

The READING TERMINAL MARKET is one-of-a-kind, Philly-food-centric, always embracing the new, while respecting and lovingly maintaining the old traditions and ways. The Market is always clean.  There are food options for EVERYONE.  Vegan. Non vegan. Gluten free. Pub fare. Sit-down diner comfort fare. Good coffee in several locations. Excellent Philly-based, sourced and processed by hand,  small-batch, proprietary liquors and wines for sale in an industrial-looking, but artful little section on the west side of the market. They offer taste testings and have some very well-curated offerings that one will not find at the average chain liquor store.  There are bakeries, and hand-made donuts made before the eyes of the (often lengthy) line of customers marveling at the process, and, the incredible glass bakery case filled to capacity with donuts of any and all varieties and flavors. If you are in Philly, if you love food, treat yourself and those you love to a visit to READING TERMINAL MARKET. Bring your appetite and your camera and your family and friends. Its a great place!

Amazinggggg. If you've never been here then you're seriously missing out on amazing food. I've only had their Marsala rolls and Omg PHENOMENAL. I love the idea of chicken Marsala wrapped up like a burrito. Everything is nicely compacted into a easy to eat roti roll. It does come with white and red sauce but Remember to add a side of their tomato sauce for dipping.

One thing hard about critiquing other people culture food is that they make it for their own liking. The kati Roll chicken appetizer was a tad bit to salty. The main dish veg biryani was okay. It had tofu in it which through me off! One good thing about this restaurant is that they pick up and deliver fast!

The pizza was good and the crust had a great yeasty flavor with a really good chew. They didn't skimp on the toppings like so many pizza joints. We have the White pizza and Pepperoni Slices. Great flavor and taste so wonderful. The service was outstanding!

This place is AWESOME!  

I highly recommend coming on a Saturday because all the Amish stores (some of the best) are closed on Sunday. 

Some of my favorites are Beiler's Donuts, Dinic's and Downtown Cheese. 

It can get very crowded at lunch time so if you don't like crowds, this isn't for you but navigating through the market is what makes it so much fun. 

There are tons of different types of foods, produce and some stores in here and it's a great experience for anyone coming to Philly!

Herschel's - pastrami sandwich.
4th st. Cookie Co. - chocolate dipped chocolate chip cookie.
Dutch Eating Place - hangover breakfast(but get there early to avoid the lines).
John Yi Fish Market - Get sushi grade salmon for that tartare that you're going to make later.
Jonathan Best - For groceries and spices such as pink peppercorns.
This could go on forever but I really don't feel like overdoing this review. The Reading Terminal is so, so great.

This was great for breakfast, lunch, or dinner! Hugh market for food items or groceries. You could get just about anything here and there is a lot of things to try! We had a great breakfast as you can see. Also beef side of bacon Delish!

This Starbucks is awesome !  
Personally, it's becoming a favorite!

I believe this is a newer location with a newish design, they even have cool plants, curtains, shades and a modern interior which is cozy and inviting.  The bathroom facilities are newish too.

What I personally like of this Starbucks vs other Starbucks in the area is they play music that's at a good volume, not too high and it's a smaller cafe so it doesn't get overly noisy like some busier cafes which can become a bit overwhelming.  

I find that the baristas are friendly and welcoming, positive and in a good mood!  

This is a nice cafe to relax and grab a quick bite.  
Warm, friendly atmosphere.  I enjoy it!  
Wish it was closer to me!

I've come here many many times and every time it has been a 4 or 5 star experience. I've never had oysters so chalked full of grit and grime, they were inedible. Terribly made cocktail, and egg white cocktail that was clearly not dry shaked, and inn-attentive wait staff. I used to be a regular here but I don't think I'll be going back. I asked the server about took the oysters away and basically said well it happens, he could've at least mustered an apology. And then not honoring the service industry discount put the cherry on top.
Fun to go through when you don't know what you want to eat.  The pastries are always good, the cheeses are great..... I love having this option in town.

Took 21 minutes to even place order - we were maybe fifth in line? No ice at the drink machine. All ALL sodas in one machine were empty, and several in the other. No ketchup packets at the bar. Dirty tables. Full trash can. Full staff, zero smiles, seemed very inconvenienced at having customers. Guy on the register couldn't count out change even with the amount right there on the screen. Didn't give entire order to us and had to go back and ask for the rest. Fries were cold. Took an additional 15 minutes to get food after ordering. Mostly cold burger. Just a circus of ineptitude. Would give negative stars if possible.

I was a bit hesitant on giving Masala more than 3 stars, but the more I visit, the more I fall in love with the place. If you're into halal truck food, you'll feel at home with their Chicken n Rice combo, as well as the MK Special, which is almost the same only with some marinated chicken in some spicy sauce. I feel like the highlight of Masala is the kati rolls. I am on a mission to try every kati roll sold in pretty much every and any variation possible. Chicken Masala is a friendly introduction as most people who eat Indian cuisine in America have had Chicken Tikka Masala before, and that rolled up in the warm, soft and crispy tawa roti makes a perfect lunch. I love that the service is pretty quick, and ordering through Eat24 proves to be the best option if you want your food by the time you get there. Not to mention it's probably one of few quality establishments still open after 9pm in the area, so that's a huge plus!
