Great variety, awesome food. There are many amazing places to choose from, I always leave with multiple items from all different types of places here. They have everything from soul food down to Asian cuisine. I love it here!!

Bottom Line:  A clean market that offeres a variety of foods and a great experience. 

If you've played Monopoly you've probably heard of the Reading Railroad.  In the late 1890s the Reading Terminal was built and used as a passenger train station and train depot.  But by the 1980s the building was no longer effective as a train terminal so the site was eventually repurposed, in part for the well-liked foodie market.  

Reading Terminal Market has over 100 vendors.  Some vendors are selling prepared foods while other are selling groceries, specialty items and gifts.  Meat, seafood, cheese, vegetables, chocolate and other goodies are plentiful here.  This place is a cacophony of sights, sounds and smells.  As a first timer I enjoyed methodically weaving my way through the market checking out all of the stalls.  Unfortunately I was there on a Sunday, a day that the Amish vendors do not participate in the market.  Other than grabbing some lunch I didn't buy anything but I would love to come back to try Bassett's Ice Cream, DiNic's and Molly Malloy's.
Was hoping to hit up Beilars but the line was really long in the early AM. Went to this diner ouster bar area for some breakfast. Very cool space and lots of diverse places to eat, drink and shop in.

This place has been on my bookmarked list for a while. I said if I ever made it to Philly, this was a go to. So this wave of food is quite interesting to navigate.

If you not a native and it's your first time USE THE MAP! This way you not walking in circles. There were some places that were not open. On a positive note, there were more places open than closed. I was able to eat at about 4 places....hey, I'm one person and I can only do so much damage lol! Reviews for the 4 places will be up soon. 

Masks are required. There is security walking around and checking. I'm sure I looked like the ultimate tourist taking it all in, photos, stoping and saying "Oooh and ahhh". All that was missing was a Fanny pack! Ha! 

This place was busy! There were cooked items, raw items, pickles, desserts, jerky, groceries, trinkets and everything else in between! If anyone lives close to this place or works nearby I'm trying to figure out why you would go anywhere else? 

I selected this place because if you can't get the full Philadelphia experience when it comes to food, this pretty much sums it up. Everything you want and more in one location. Every major city needs one or these. I'm sure it showcases what the city has to offer and local vendors are on display and they business will come to them. This was amazing. 

I ate and walked. 
I repeated x3
I came, I saw and devoured. 
Philly it's been real. 
I did not go hungry. 
For that I am grateful.

I go here to buy food products, not for the restaurant scene, which is lively, varied and packed - nice to see as I hit my choices for produce, meat and cheese. 

Downtown Cheese has to be the best cheese shop in Philly, with rich choices and rational pricing. The place is staffed by people who actually know cheese, and can work with you to assemble a tasting menu or address whatever other "cheese issues" you might have.

I vary my produce purchases by checking the freshness and pricing.... always find what I need... and the various "farm to market" stands provide ease of access to fresh stuff.

Only challenge is the shopping on the weekends can become gridlock, especially during car show and flower show events, at which point, I make a determined effort to arrive as early as possible.  Will never forget being spied by two librarians from Ohio attending a conference.. who noted to each other that "the natives really shop here..."....

Tasty fast food!

House made sausage wasn't as fatty as I thought it would be, was quite lean, layered on top of a slightly al dente fried rice with crunchy Lumpia on the side.  The soft runny egg served well to eggslime the rice adding a rich flavor.  The veggie-slaw on the plate were a bit too sour for me and I might ask to forgo them in the future.  

At 8:30pm and most other places in the food hall shuttered for the evening, save for a bar and a dessert venue, LALO being open until 9pm is a welcome sight.

The decor of the food hall was quite interesting and definitely a nice place to sit and eat quickly for lunch or dinner.

How can delicious pizza leave a bad taste in your mouth? So bad that I will never give this place my business again? Read on and I will explain.

Several months ago I saw a video of a place called Pizza Shackamaxon posted on Facebook. The person in the video gave it a pretty decent review so I decided to give it a try. It's far from me. About 40 minutes away, but I will travel for delicious food.

First time I tried it I was a little put off by the prices. $4 for a regular slice. $4.50 for a pepperoni, and $5 for a speciality slice. Expensive, but I tried it anyway. The pizza was good. I liked it. But it was still overpriced in my opinion. Doesn't matter. I ended up coming back to this place several times a week over the next few months. I usually order 3 slices at a time, a few days a week. Yeah I spend a lot here. Several hundred dollars a month on pizza slices lol.

I've read reviews on Yelp from people saying the owners were rude. I always saw them as being slightly pushy, but never to a point that it bothered me... until today.

I went in and ordered 2 slices of pepperoni and one specialty slice. In the past I've always just let them give me any slice they choose, even if it had a ton of burnt crust or air bubbles on it. I've never said anything about it. Well today one of the slices he cut off for me was really burnt on the crust. I hate pizza like that, so for the first time since going there I asked if I could have a different slice. 

And here was his response:

"Look, man. We're not going to do this every time for you", with an angry look on his face.

I had to take a step back and think about what just happened. I'm from Philly and I'm ok with Philly attitude, but what the F just happened here? 

I told him that I spend $50+ here a week and I have never asked for a different slice before. I asked him what the problem was. He told me that he "wanted to be fair to the other customers and I can't just pick the larger slices and get them." I told him that I didn't like burnt crust and wanted a piece without it and he said, "oh I thought you just wanted bigger pieces." He didn't apologize. He didn't care. I was completely shocked.

First off, for $5 a slice I should be able to pick any damn slice I want. You see me in there multiple times every week spending lots of money and I'm always kind and cheerful. Never rude. Never needy. I order my slices, take what they give me even if they are bad looking slices or smaller, and I leave with a smile and say thank you.

No "sorry". No "my bad". Just attitude. That's how they appreciate me.

Well I'm going to miss the slices I got here. I will not be giving them any more of my money. I will do my best to spread the word about what kind of d-bag this guy was to me. I guess they don't care, though. Heck, they even have a sign inside on the wall that says "SORRY WE'RE MEAN".

Maybe it should say "Sorry, we are unappreciative a$$holes.

RIP Pizza Shackamaxon. That attitude won't get you very far in the world we live in today.

- A must-go whenever you're in Philly
- Conveniently near most bus stops
- You can find anything you can think of!
- Ice cream, wine, olive oil, cheesesteaks, balsamic vinegar, candy, linen...
- Good place to get gifts
- Enough seating, although you'll need to wait around if it's lunch hour
- We wondered if only tourists stopped by but there seemed to be a good amount of locals grocery shopping for fresh produce and meats

Dear Mr. Grow, 3 stars. why? mediocrity. how? i wasn't sure if i was eating noodles or spaghetti. regardless, alright meal, fair amount of proteins in my stir fry, not enough vegetables however. how does that make sense? thanks for the food tho pretty covid safe for those concerned.
Always a great brunch plan! Never disappoints, go to Molly Malloys in the back for a walking Prosecco to start off your search for delicious bites

Awesome place before and after COVID!!!!
There are so many different places to eat and so many cool little shops. Great for breakfast lunch and dinner and outings with family, friends or on a date!

This is a great place. I live in NNJ, about 2 1/2 hours away and try to get here 3 or 4 times a year. My excuse is the Franklin Institute or Please Touch Museum for the kids, but the Terminal Market is my favorite lunch spot. Great burgers, chicken, Chinese Food and oysters, so much left to try. Great produce, coffee and fish to take home. Be sure to visit their website and check out the subsidized 2 hour parking for $4; otherwise it's $12 for 2 hours. Enjoy.
It is an amazing place with a collection of restaurants and foods from around the world! It is a must go to if you are in Center City

It's the jackpot of food and drink!

Juices, fresh made Philly pretzels, pizzas, ice cream, smoothies, cupcakes, whoopie pies, cookies, bread, candy, beef jerky, a Garden of Eden of fruits and vegetables, pasta, fresh fish and shell fish,Philly cheese steaks, gyros, Mexican food, any ethnic food you can think of, teas, coffees, grocery staples, cheese, gourmet foods, a soul food cafeteria, Amish food, it just goes on and on.    

The building used to be the Reading Train terminal.  It's close to 80,000 square feet jam packed with hundreds of vendors.

We were there on Saturday, it was overflowing with customers. 

What a cool place.

We liked the ambience, the server was friendly and knowledgeable, and the steak frites TASTE was good but the meat was pretty cold....

the biggest mistake was that a nice bottle of Malbec came COLD - really COLD!  even a novice should know not to serve red wine cold......we should have sent it back but she had already opened it.....

I don't get down to The Industry as often as I'd like. This is one of the most laid-back, chill places to drink or grab a bite in the city. Worth a special mention is the service, which is always very friendly and accommodating. I really believe servers at The Industry stand out from the pack when compared with other restaurants of similar style. The environment is fun and the music is always varied and awesome.

The drinks are where it's at. The Ghost of Mary is one of my favorite cocktails ever and I will sing its praises to anyone interested in listening. The Mummer's Punch is a good time, and the beer list is great. Happy hour specials are on point.

I'm not as enthusiastic about the food as I am the drinks but there is still a lot left for me to try. I did really enjoy the wedge salad on my recent visit. I was dying to try the banana pound cake but there wasn't room for dessert. Instead, I went with a double espresso and it was so smooth and well-flavored that I ordered another. Often, I order espressos to get my caffeine fix. I got that, plus I actually really enjoyed the espresso itself. Looking forward to my next visit sooner rather than later.
I really liked the ease of signing up and the information you requested is not to intrusive, however, I still like the idea of getting background on your patients is a great way to get to know them.
This was an amazing place to visit, different cuisines to select from.  We had breakfast at Molly Malloy's...the biscuits are huge food is tasty too.

I love everything about this place. What's not to love. 
Greek food yep. italian yep. Seafood yep. Chocolate yep ice cream yep. Amish pastries and whoopie pies? Yas! Fresh fruits and veggies? Yep. 
This place.is awesome!

mask compliance was on par! it was still v crowded and hot though. but we went to the omish restaurant, i forget the name but the cheeseburger and fries were soo good. some of the lines were long & it was so hot in there. but i guess that's to b expected in the reading terminal market. i just wish there some clearer pathways. but the staff is nice and the products are good including the prices.
So so so good! Got the OG pepperoni, did not disappoint. Can't wait to come back and try out all the other menu items.

I'm still making my way through to eat from every food stand in the Market (each visit makes me wish I could eat more!), but nothing has disappointed. 

There are more than enough reviews here, so I'm keeping this short.  Try everything, or if you're a tourist and not here often, don't be afraid to try something that's not hyped--you might still find something amazing.  Let yourself wander.   It's really about the experience.

Some favorite items:
-Blueberry/apple fritters, maple bacon donuts from Beiler's-- doughy, warm, fresh, sugary goodness.
-FRESH mozzarella from Meltkraft.   I literally eat it plain with fork and knife.
-Flying Monkey's woopie pies.
-$1 closeout cookies around 5pm from Famous 4th Street [on a slow day]
-Peking duck, easily accessible without going to Chinatown.
-Apple dumplingw/ heayv cream from the amish diner (foodies--this was featured on Food Network)
Got everything foodwise there.  Just not so good on the Cheesesteaks.  DiNic's is a plus....

Reading Terminal Market is one of the original markets in the US.  I've lived in  Baltimore and worked in Baltimore for most of my adult life and have been to similar markets in the Baltimore MD region (Lexington, North East, Cross Street, Fells Point, etc)  The Reading Terminal Market is comparable and larger to most of the ones I've listed.  I go to Philly at least twice a year and this is a must stop for me.  The boy likes to go to Di'Nick's to get his beef and pork sandwiches, I love to go to Sang Kee to get the duck wonton noodle soup.  The coffee shop has 2 different stalls (once in the front across from Sang Kee and the second one by the Philadelphia General store in the back).  We typically go on Sundays and the Dutch/Amish Market area is almost always closed sadly.  The general store makes awesome cookies and their chocolate chip oatmeal cookie is one of my must buys when we come here.  The ice cream is also a frequent stop and the Guatemalan Fudge ripple is one of my favorites.  They also have seasonal flavors such as pumpkin and eggnog.  

During covid, they have closed most of the indoor eating areas and they did have some tables set up outside for eating.  They do require face coverings but I did find that when we went I felt that there was more people than what I was comfortable hanging out with as we were wandering about.

I'm going to give five stars because the salad was good and the guy who made it was great. Awesome personality and made me feel welcome. Girl working the register was the complete opposite and looked like she smiles when someone slips on the ice. 

It can get expensive, but still a good deal for an airport. I can't stop at four ingredients so I loaded it up but felt I still received great value for what I paid. You also get one free drink refill which they absolutely do NOT have to offer, especially at PHL. 

Everything was fresh and well prepared! I also get the impression that if you weren't happy with your purchase the gentleman would make it right.

I really like this market. There's a little of everything here. I come here with anyone who isn't a Philadelphia resident and they can always find something to eat. Seating is sometimes hard to find during noon but that is to be expected. I am a vegetarian and I can always find something  by new to eat. Highly recommend if you have a group of people and have different food tastes.
Love this place! It's always crowded thou. So many different types of foods in this one place.
Love spending time here and seeing what the myriad of vendors have to offer.  Sundays the Amish area is closed so go a different day unless you don't care about some delicious baked goods

Definitely a must if you're going to philly! My boyfriend and I came through when we were visiting and there are soooooo many great options here! There's any type of food you can imagine and so many great spots to try!

This place is a dream! I wish we had one of these back home! Reading Terminal is basically a building with small restaurants inside. There are some shops for groceries and knick knacks but it's mostly restaurants. It was super busy on the day we came but the lines moved pretty quickly. 

We had eaten before coming here (don't make the same mistake I did! Come here hungry!), but I still made room in my stomach for extra food. What we got: 

1.) Roast pork sandwich at DiNic's
2.) Apple dumplings at Dutch Eating Place
3.) Mint lemon rose water lemonade at Kamal's Middle Eastern Specialties 

All were delicious and I was definitely sad I couldn't eat anymore. If I didn't have anything else planned for the rest of the day, I could seriously stay here all day and just graze my way around. Put this on your To-Do list especially if you're a visitor!

Popped into Good 2 Go looking for a heathy, low cal meal and was so surprised to find it. Veggie humus on multi grain bread with shredded carrots, thinly sliced cukes, apples, romaine lettuce and cheese. Bread was fresh & soft. Veggies were raw and also fresh. 

Grabbed some barbecue Pop Chips! Perfect! Quick, satisfying healthy lunch!

Ate 1/2 of sandwich and carried rest on board. Checked into hotel and the bread is still fresh. Stowed in fridge for later snacking.

What is there to say about the Reading Terminal Market?  They have everything.  It is a true gem in Philly.  Our favorites include Beiler's for donuts, Olympia Gyro, The Tubby Olive and the Hatville Deli.  Singling out merchants here is tough though.  There are so many great places.  The market is a great for breakfast and lunch.  Highly recommend visiting when you're in town!

A giant, gourmet food court is basically every foodie's dream and that is essentially what you'll find at Reading Terminal Market. Right across the street from the convention center, it certainly gets packed when there is an event going on but most of the lines move quick. I guess the only issue would be finding seating to eat your food. Some of the restaurants have their own seating and waiter service, some just have a bar area, and some have nothing at all.

I ended up trying a cheesesteak from By George followed by waiting 45 minutes in line for Amish donuts at Beiler's. Aside from that, they have pretty much any cuisine you'd like as well as fresh groceries (fruits/veggies, meat, fish, seafood, etc). I would definitely like to come back one day when it isn't as crazy to try out more things!

Have a hankering for BBQ? Check. Need a butcher? Take your pick! Fresh produce? There are at least three markets to choose from. Want any cheese you can imagine? Start perusing! Cheesesteak/cheesecake craving? You could get both!! Not to mention there's representation from most ethnic foods - Chinese, Indian, middle eastern, Mexican, Greek. On any given day, there are so many smells wafting toward you once you walk in that it can be very overwhelming. Reading Terminal Market is a Philadelphia tradition where you can satisfy almost any gastronomical craving you might have. 

I personally don't think that the stalls in the Terminal are necessarily the best representatives of the individual cuisines, but it's rare to find one place that can satisfy the palate of everyone in your group. And some items are more expensive here than if you had gone elsewhere. But it's a Philadelphia tradition - no trip to Philadelphia would be complete without a stop here.

Oh man where do I even start on this magical fucking place ...this is hands down in my top 5 best pizzas ever eaten this pizza was so fucking good I ate the entire thing standing above a garbage can like a homeless person this pizza is so good I'd gladly be homeless if it meant I could pitch a tent next to the building and live off the shit they throw away the crust alone is worth the trip I had a suspicion that it was a sourdough crust but one of the workers went over the technical side with me and explained how the crust gets its magical texture and chew, which might I add is cool as fuck of him to take his time to do especially as wild as I looked smashing a whole fucking pie outside by myself next to a garbage can, all in all if you're in the area find them if you're not in the area go get in the area!!!

So this one time I was at Reading Terminal Market and as I was salivating at all the amazing food options, this hobo-esque woman asked if I could spare any food. I decided to give her my just-made-that-morning ham and egg sandwich. She turned me down and said she did not eat pork and asked for money instead. WOW WELCOME TO PHILLY. 

Despite that odd experience, RTM has more than enough cheesy, meaty, savory, melt-in-your-mouth, cheat day goodness to warrant a re-visit (if I ever return to Philly).

The timeliness of online orders has definitely improved (yay!!!), but the excessive sauce issue hasn't. I always specify "light sauce" when I come to this location because they really overdo it on the sauce, but my order today was LOADED with sauce despite requesting light sauce. I think the solution for next time is to just get sauce on the side...

A fabulous place with a lot of personality.  I have been to similar markets in major cities around the world.  Although I would not regard Reading Terminal as the BEST of these markets, it is still fabulous in its' own right.

This is a must-visit on any trip to Center City. When we have friends from out of town, we definitely take them here. (And before we were residents we definitely went here too!) There's some famous stalls, and some yet to be discovered, but one thing is for sure - this is an ace food hall and there is something for everyone.

Be warned, parking is a hassle, so come mentally prepared to patiently drive around for a spot or pay for garage parking.
This is food heaven!  Variety, spice and life!  Fast service, nice people, and plenty of good food.  This is a must for locals and visitors, and the worker bees!
Love Reading Terminal, to bad I no longer live down town, i would go several times a week.

The Bourse is a recent-ish food court right next the liberty/bell independence hall area. Inside this food court there's a variety of local, hip restaurants with Lalo being one of the stronger contenders. Filipino restaurants are pretty sparse in Philadelphia (with Perla being a pricey exception), so I was excited to try this out. I ordered the bbq pork and was BLOWN AWAY. 

The pork platter comes with garlicky rice, pickled tomatoes and radish, and this beautiful, crispy fried pork that shatters in your mouth. The platter also comes with a soy sauce with a vinegar kick that makes the rice so good I could eat it alone. The flan is creamy, dense, and full of rich custard/caramel flavor--the perfect end to any meal. 

I can't vouch for the authenticity (although I asked my Philippine co-worker, who says it is pretty authentic), but I can vouch for its deliciousness. The only gripe I have is I wish there was more pork! Although I will say it is a comfortable portion that will make you full but not stuffed.
Sampled the Pork Adobo Siopao- CAN I GET AN AMEN. This was decadent! The sweet sauce was a delight to my palate coupled with the amazing texture of the soft bao. Staff was friendly! Place was clean!

The food is good however 8/10 times I go to the Cottman location I feel like they are very sloppy with their bowl and burrito making. I also heard one of the employees say that when the online orders ask for extra anything he doesn't make them extra anything because we were too lazy to come in store. The employees every time you come into the Cottman Ave location are always so rude, unpleasant. They act as if they are being inconvenienced by us being there. I always feel like I'm bothering them when I ask for anything.  The store is always a mess. The employees have poor customer service training however the manager at this location is the reason I keep going.

I fell in love with this market place immediately!  Since I recently visited Seattle, it reminds me of Pike Place Market.  

When you walk in, you'll become overwhelmed by the amount of people congregated around different vendors combined with the scents of amazing food sold here.  There are many varieties of food to choose from.  Not to mention the assortment of desserts appealing to anyone's taste buds.  

There are many vendors selling cute crafts to Philly souvenirs.  You'll notice the strong Amish presence at many of the sites.  Fresh baked breads and delicious fudge are ready to purchase and devour.  Yum.  

I would highly suggest stopping here whether you are just visiting or a local.

Horrible service. The old lady working the register was very miserable; huffing and puffing. She was very rude and did not want to service me. She also spoke in a very soft tone that I could not hear her, so I asked her again and she gave me a nasty look. I have not been to KFC for a very long time, and this was probably one of the reasons I would never want to come back. This KFC needs to hire more competent workers and not hood rats.

(I'm finally posting this draft from before the pandemic) Now this is what a market should be!  It has a little bit of everything for everyone. All of the staff were friendly and the choices weee abundant.  I will review each of the stall separately, but just coming here is an amazing food experience.  I actually liked the little gift shop they had next to the bathrooms for touristy gifts. Also, I would reccomend not trying to park to get here - it's really difficult even on the worst rather days!

Just no. I was in the area taking my family to some tourist attractions and we stepped into the Bourse for a quick bite. I'm usually a fan of food halls, especially the ones in NYC. Usually a group of unique restaurants where I can get a bite from different places and create a smorgasbord. I grew up in an area with a lot of Filipino's so I love the food and was excited to have easy access in this moment. Well, I ordered the Adobo chicken and this was the DRIEST chicken that I've had in a long time and it also was flavorless. It was a large portion and I just tossed it and went on with my life. What a waste.

This place is a horror show and the WORST McDonalds I have ever been to in the world. 

The McDonalds had construction going on the outside. When you walk in, it reeks like a high school gym. The tables and floor were very dirty. I have never seen armed security at McDonalds but this one has it and they need it because there were several sketchy looking people inside. Once you get past all these things, you notice that there are only 2 people manning the kitchen and taking orders during peak dinner hours. Food took about 20 minutes to arrive. Once you get it, it is cold... Once you survive this disaster and need to use the bathroom you are greeted by a bathroom that reeks, has a broken door handle and is wet everywhere like someone has showered inside.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. IT IS BETTER TO GO HUNGRY.

This place is a must for visitors.   The perfect Philly spot.

You can get everything you can imagine (except furniture..lol).   Ice cream, jams, honey, jelly, cheesecakes, gazillion bakery items, pastrami, donuts, chocolate...list goes on and on.

There is no way you can say you are hungry if you're in this place.  So many choices.

Prepared foods and fresh food is all over this market.

It gets packed on a Saturday and hard to walk.... They are open on Sundays but many of the vendors are not.  

I love coming here.  The only draw back is seating is at a premium and the restrooms are blah.

Will I be back?   Definitely.

Been having a bad run lately with fast food places around here, not opening on time, not caring etc.
I was planning on just going to the BK, but I saw lights on here and wondered if they had breakfast too( places like here and Taco Bell advertise breakfast but the locations I've seen aren't open then)...so I figured I'd try here since I never actually had Wendy's for breakfast. 
I pull up to the speaker... wait... no answer. So I go ahead and drive around and sho 'nuf they were prepping the machines etc. This was 6:40... their hours say 6:30, they looked surprised i was there. Get with it people.

If I could give this no stars I would. This is the worst Chipotle in the whole city, disorganized, the staff look like a bunch of kids that don't know what their doing. Covid has been going on a for a whole year snd this restaurant doesn't even know how to run the takeout orders let alone prepare the food correctly without being sloppily. Like the food is nasty like the staff aren't better trained.
I love the atomesphere and the food. I go here often for the sights and eating assortment.

I came to this location after leaving the airport, the manager asked us what we wanted and then after asking us she called another young lady over to take our order(please don't ask why) so I had to repeat myself! While I was waiting for my food a young man came to fill the lemonade up not having any gloves on(BACTERIA!!!!). Then once I got my food my fries were not filled up and some sticky stuff on the box. Asking the young lady for another fry she took it to the manager and the manger dumped the fries with the rest of the fries and scooped up the same fries! I'm not sure what the trainings like for this location, however it needs to be revisited!!

Fun place to meet up with friends and eat till you pass out! I've been here a handful of times before and generally don't get disappointed with the food. 
Since it is a tourist trap expect to pay more then you generally would for the same food elsewhere. 
My friends and I were there for harvest fest where they close down filbert street for some fall activities and vendors. We got some food there and some food inside the market. Overall what we got was pretty good!
Got some seafood paella which has more rice and not that much seafood but still pretty good. Got some pizza that was great!
My husband and our friend split a cheese steak form one place and then a roast pork sandwich from another. Both were great! I got a fruity pebbles donut which was amazeballs. My favorite ice cream place is there and I got a salted caramel pretzel ice cream  delicious !! Def. Want to come back and try other things.
The food is delicious,  the waitress was friendly and also gave suggestions love the place
very fun and a lot of selections to choose from.  a must go when visiting philly!

This location is always busy! Going in seems a lot quicker than the drive-thru. The employees and they run like a well-oiled machine especially on Saturdays. Only once was my order incomplete and it was fixed right away! Love the salads!

I can't believe this place.  This is foodie HEAVEN.

So basically, this is a huge terminal filled with different food vendors.  It ranges in everything from Thai food to Amish food to donuts to a bar to Cajun food to a candy shop to a butcher to a winery to ice cream to...well, you get the point.

If you are a food lover (and I suspect you are if you are on Yelp) and you are in the PA area this is a must do.  Yes, it was extremely crowded, but it was worth it.  There are so many delicacies to try and there is something for everyone here.

This market is reminiscent of Pike's Place Market in Seattle, only better because it's indoors (so in case of rain) and has more food versus flowers and other local stuff like candles. I love all the food stalls - I just want to try them all (so many choices!)! They must be good because as I was searching yelp reviews, most of the individual places are rated four stars. 

I am not sure what the parking situation is like, since I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn around the corner. It seemed street parking is VERY limited, so parking in a garage is probably best. I don't know the hourly cost ($33/day), but the same parking garage I used for the hotel can be used for the market (entrance is off of 11th or Arch streets). Apparently there is a deal right now that you can now park up to two hours nearby in a garage (not sure which one) for $4 with vendor validation. Perhaps this is a way to gain more business, but it seemed people were in full force either buying food at the grocery stalls or sitting down to eat. 

I noticed there are some places only open in the morning versus not open in the afternoon for lunch, so be forewarned! Your best bet is to use the Yelp app as a tool to figure out the operation hours of the different places. Good luck!

I really don't know how people decide on just one thing at terminal market.  There are so many great food options.  My first experience my friends brought me here and I didn't know what to expect, didn't know much about Reading Terminal Market but quickly learned.

Note that I've had some experience I would say be prepared for tons of walking and tight spaces due to the crowds in each isle.  Also it can be a bit difficult to find a spot to sit and eat again because it is generally crowded.

Selecting the right meal can be assisted because most venues are really good about giving samples to try.  I usually have one meal and another meal to go for future meals.

The market is in the middle of the city, therefore driving to terminal market and finding parking is not for the faint of heart.  I usually Uber there and have no issues.
Im dying of hunger.  This guy is like yo want so food?  so i went inside and got some food.  i didnt pay tho because im a hobo.

I love the Reading Terminal and visit almost once a week for food, groceries, or gifts. If you are looking for a place to eat or simply something to do, I highly recommend going to the market. To paraphrase another review - no matter what your taste or mood, there is something here for you to eat or buy. That said, below are some recommendations of items that are widely considered surefire favorites.
 
* pastrami rachel - Herschel's East Side Deli 
* roast pork sandwich - Tommy DiNic's
* apple dumpling - Dutch Eating Place
* cannoli - Termini Brothers
* apple / blueberry fritter - Beiler's Doughnuts
* half sour pickles - Beiler's Salads / Pickle Patch 
* regular soft pretzel - Miller's Twist
* sweet potato battered corn dog - Fox & Son 
* salmon curry  - Little Thai Market
* peking duck - Sang Kee Peking Duck
* whoopie pie - Flying Monkey Bakery 
* rotisserie / smoked chicken wings - Dienner's BBQ
* ice cream - Bassetts Ice Cream
I love George's steaks and they also have a burger spot thats on the other side thats pretty good and four seasons smoothies are awesome too

What can you say about a place where you can get just about anything your heart desires (ok, except World Peace, but I'm sure this place comes close to it).

Come here for lunch.  Come here for dinner.  Pop in for some eggs before heading back home on SEPTA.  This place has everything.

Not my first time here, but finally got a review in.  Have had lunch.  Have had dinner.  Have eaten in as well as taken carry out.  It has my farm fresh cage free eggs as well as donuts.

Need I say more?

WE go here when me and my friends go to the philly car show. This place is always packed. There are so many choices when it comes to food, from cold sandwiches, cheesesteaks, BBQ to tons of desserts. The market always seems to be pretty clean despite how many people are walking around. Seating is a huge issue, there is definitely not enough seating although some places inside do have private seating areas. I've had meals from a few different places in there which honestly I can't remember, the one place Dinic's stands out to me. They have a nice beef brisket, we get that a lot however, if you get there before 11am they will not serve you the brisket. We got their at 10:50 one day and they refused to take any orders for the brisket lol. All in all always enjoy going to there and trying something different, but not guaranteed to be able to sit and enjoy it lol.

As soon as I walked in, I said it reminded me of Essex St. Market in NYC...but as I kept walking, I realized it was just bigger and better (and I love the Essex market). This place blew me away. If you can't find something to eat here, you are going to have to turn in your digestive system. You don't deserve it. 

The smells, the colors, it's completely overwhelming. I saw amazing prices on everything from fish to fruit to beautiful NY strips ($10.99/lb). If I wasn't hopping on a train for an hour back to NYC, I would've stocked up for sure. 

Somehow I got talked into eating an enormous roast pork hero from Dinic's with delicious spicy peppers all over it. For breakfast. And it was phenomenal.
Very pleasant atmosphere, friendly people....they have the best ribs and salmon over rice at the LIL THAI MARKET  the Amish chicken wings melt in your mouth

Do NOT come to Masala Kitchen. I came here on a Saturday night for some late night food and while I was in the bathroom, the staff unlocked the door in the middle of me using the bathroom to let some drunk guy in. I was not even in there for a full minute before this happened - it was closer to 30 seconds. 

This was extremely violating and I will never give Masala Kitchen my business. I do not encourage anyone to frequent an establishment where they think this is OK.

It is a fun place , so many different food from different countries ( Chinese, Indian , Italian. .. )
Also you can buy fresh fruits, vegetables , meats ...)
I love this place

Probably the worst experience I've had at Chipotle. 

The chips were at least a day or two old 

The guacamole was brown. 

The burrito was cold as ice, and tasted like a wet Baby diaper. 

I wound up just throwing it all away.

I just heard that RTM might be closing their doors forever. This is a tragedy. One of the best places in the city of Philadelphia. A destination. We need to do whatever it takes to keep the the Market open.

This place is the BOOM.COM... I love  farmers markets & the one is a rare gem... There is no two stands a like & prices are super fair... I love you can buy books, china & then sushi all in the same building. It has been feature many times on different travel programs..

It's a must go to in the Philly area...
Extra GROSS. Absolutely hate this place. I've ordered more than 7x, each time trying to forgive and forget, but they relentlessly f*#¥ things up every time. Don't do it.

Reading Terminal Market has so many food options that it's impressive. I could literally spend all day walking around, just looking at everything there is to see. Whenever I have friends visiting from out of town, I always bring them here because it's such a great experience.

Reading Terminal has everything you could ever need. I love to buy fresh produce, fruits, and meat from here and the prices are generally reasonable. But the variety of options makes shopping here so great. Plus, although there is often a large group of people, it never feels crowded and most of the lines move really fast.

If you are looking for something fun to do or want to try some interesting choices of food, you should definitely go to Reading Terminal!
Very cool place! Has every kind of food you can imagine! Lots of good food!! I will for sure be back!

I love coming here to eat. If you want to navigate the market in an efficient manner, there are maps available when you enter. This place closes at 5pm, so make sure you get here early. Reading Terminal Market has everything - fresh produce, seafood, meat, cookies, coffee, omelettes, grilled cheese etc.  
There are also lots of Amish owned business here if you want to eat some Pennsylvanian Dutch food!

Here are some of my favorite spots:

Miller's Twist: get your hands on a breakfast pretzel log. I got one that was filled with bacon, cheese and egg and it was amazing. The pretzel was buttery, and the filling was warm and cheesy. I was there in the morning and there was definitely a line for these amazing breakfast logs. This spot is Amish owned too!

Sweet as Fudge Candy Shoppe: Another Amish owned business with lots of candy, and home made fudge. You can ask for samples of the fudge, which are made with real cream and butter!

Old City Coffee: Great place to grab coffee, they can also make your coffee fancy as they have a variety of syrups! They do sell coffee beans which you can take home.

Bassetts Ice Cream: This place has such amazing ice cream- I tried the strawberry which tasted like real fruit. The salted caramel pretzel was the bomb - vanilla ice with chocolate covered pretzels and caramel drizzle. This was soooo amazing.

Can't wait to come back!

The reading terminal is a must go to in Philadelphia.  The food at the little booths are always fun and adventurous.  If you can get a seat at the diner inside you are lucky but you must try.  A good place to grocery shop of you live I. The city near buy all the food is very fresh.  The bakery items are specially good a must have it the Pa. Dutch stand which only opens on certain days.
Every time I am in the city over night I HAVE to stop by the Reading Terminal to pick up something delicious! Whatever you want, they have it here!

Tried the Humpty Dumpling food truck at Made in America, so can't give a full out review of the actual shop, but the dumplings, oh the dumplings! The broccoli cheddar and Philly cheesesteak dumplings are must tries! I'd also highly recommend trying the Oreo cheesecake dessert dumpling. It's yummy and a sort of Oreo cheesecake filling as opposed to having an actual Oreo stuffed in it. Such a cool concept, and really tasty food.

I love this place!!!!! They have so much variety and different types of stores. I always go to grab some produce, meats, and jerky. It's also a fun place to bring friends who want to explore the city.

You cannot miss in the RTM. If you like donuts, I highly recommend Beiler's - it's definitely our favorite. But you really cannot go wrong with eating anywhere in here. I've tried a ton of places and have never been disappointed.

Also, there's plenty of affordable, fresh produce! If you spend at least $10 in any one of the places in RTM, you can get a stamp for cheaper parking (if in one of the designated garages).

One of the best slices in the City of Philadelphia for pizza enthusiasts and casual pizza fans alike. Slices  have a crispy thin crust with a slight char, perfectly balanced red sauce, gooey cheese and fresh toppings. As a rule, everytime I go (as should you) I ORDER THE SPECIAL! You won't be disappointed, they might switch up meats from time to time or not have any at all, but THE SPECIAL is a white pizza with a mouth watering buttery crust, melty mozzarella and ricotta cheese. Seasoned to perfection, so no need to ask for any. All in all, pizza at it's finestsee u there.......

A friend visited me from New Hampshire wanting you see landmarks in Philadelphia. I took her to the Reading terminal and it did not disappoint. We bought cookies and cheese steaks. I showed her where I regularly buy vegetables and meats. These are always well priced and fresh. The variety of foods and merchandise bring me back again and again

Yup, came as a tourist and loved it. I love markets like this. My only gripe is that it's tight and you can get lost....lol I would have loved a map of all of the stalls and restaurants. But in any case, the food is fresh and the selection of eateries is pretty astonishing. I'm sure their is some historical significance mumbojumbo, but really it's just a large market with great food and also some random gifts/goods too.

So many shops so little time! This market is located right next to the convention center which was a plus because that's where we were for an event. 

There are so many delicious shops within the market that we saw. It was crowded because the event plus locals and tourist. I'd like to go back and see if it's less busy without a major even happening at the convention center. 

Shops we tried:
Beck's Cajun - Beignets were yummy. Fried Mac and Cheese was good.
Pricey $$$$$

Dienner's Bar-B-Q Chick - Delicious crispy fried wings! We got regular and Parmesan flavor. They were great.
Price $$$

Spataro's - The Philly cheese steak was alright. I wasn't sure if all spots would have good Philly's or if Geno's or somewhere else would. The breakfast Philly was pretty good though. I liked it. 

Indian Spot (sorry I can't remember the name) 
Located near the front right in front of the ice cream joint. Adjacent from the Greek spot. 
- The Shawarma was amazing! I got the lamb and it was yummy delicious. We also got smoothies from the Juice Bar at the shop. They were all natural and not sweet. Both were pretty good. 

Beiler's Donuts - Uh .. the line was ridiculous! We didn't get to try these and I'm not sure if that line was worth it. I'm wondering if there's gold in the donuts!

Cookies & Co - The cookies were pretty good. Any cookie is good to me though. 

Coffee Spot (Right next to the cookie spot) - Mocha latte was pretty good. Strong and tasty.
So many choices, so little time!

So delicious! I ordered the chicken platter and loved it--the chicken was flavorful, the sauces lent a great blend of spicy and creamy, and the naan was perfectly soft. The platter reminded me of Halal Guys--in a few ways, it's quite similar! Ordering online was super convenient as well. I'll definitely be returning!
Love the cheese shop-great selections. Love I one brothers grocery and their juices. The ice cream is the best I've ever had at Bassett's too

It's a good thing I don't live in Philly. The intense Mets fandom might not help, but what I'm really talking about is the Reading Terminal Market. If I lived within a reasonable distance there's no telling how much I might weigh. Basically, what I'm trying to say is go to the Reading Terminal and try not to eat yourself silly.

It's right there in the middle of the city and has been for quite some time. Last Sunday showed some construction being done to the exterior so the classic blue and red lit up sign was a little covered. No worries, the food is still flowing inside.

Now don't get me wrong, I'm from New York and we have our own food-filled market in Chelsea. And when thinking of markets, Quincy up in Boston deserves a mention as well. There's plenty all over that do. But the variety of edible amazingness at RTM is almost unparalleled. 

Enter and pick a direction to go. Some might stumble upon original and old school spots like Bassett's Ice Cream and Godshall's Poultry, or perhaps DiNic's (personal favorite) and Spataro's which have your beefy Philly staples ready to go. I seriously can't dive into everything in this market, but here's a quick food-type list of what you'll find just by walking around: Delis, coffee, BBQ, ethnic food, cheeses, condiments, chocolate, bakeries, seafood, wine, donuts, burgers, salads, teas, a buffet, plenty of fresh produce, and dodo bird eggs (okay maybe not that last one). Don't forget to stop in the PA general store or one of the book spots for something to remember your experience (besides your food baby). 

Once you make your mostly edible purchases, if you'll be eating them immediately, there's plenty of seating areas scattered throughout. It's easy to stay and explore, but leave within two hours and you can get your parking ticket validated (as long as you spend 10 bucks in RTM, an easy feat). You'll then pay a great price of only $4. They want your business, and you should give it to them!

Overall, the Reading Terminal Market is worthy of a visit in Philly just as much if not more than the Liberty Bell. Yep, I went there. So go forth and eat something! You won't be disappointed, because the Terminal will grab hold of your senses and you'll see, hear, smell, touch, and definitely taste exactly what I'm talking about. Thanks for the food, Philly.
Lots of different stores sometimes the line is always too crazy but it's worth it.My favorite is the Beilers Donut!

A Philadelphia-must-visit. It may be crowded here, but you can enjoy EVERYTHING here! Philly cheesesteaks, fresh doughnuts, asian cuisine, greek cuisine, amish breads and fudge, an abundance of ripe produce and flowers, smoothies, pizza, and so much more!
Decent salad for airport food. One of the healthier options for sure! I'd stop again if I was in terminal D.
Amazing collection of good purveyors. A must on any visit to Philadelphia. The creperie and the coffee and spice store are my favorite

An amazing selection of cooked food and grocery delights , fresh meats , cheeses,pastas and seafood for any palate. Well worth the trip for a great breakfast , lunch or dinner or the finest foods to create a wonderful meal.
The food was awful. I ordered a chicken sandwich, sweet potatoes, and macaroni and cheese. The sandwich was terrible, and the lettuce was wilted

Unfortunately I rarely travel south of south street, but I came here because a friend recommended it and boy was I glad I listened! 
First thing that impressed me was the door handle, it's a knife! The place had a super laid-back, chill vibe with dim lighting... Perfect for a late night dinner. Waitstaff was attentive and friendly. 
Mac and cheese croquettes: fabulous, fried, crunchy balls sent from heaven with a side of kimchi purée. I could have had this alone for dinner. 
Buffalo chicken meatballs: soft chicken meatballs covered in intense buffalo flavor... Simply scrumptious
Generals wings: unfortunately these were a huge miss. They were covered in sauce, but the sauce didn't have enough flavor that the wings had a bland chicken wing taste to it. We tried our best to enjoy them by drowning them in ranch 
Seitan tandoori: being Indian, I may be a harsh critic. But this was well done seitan sitting in a broth of just garam masala and lime. It tasted nothing like tandoori dishes should. Whomp whomp
Salted Carmel bread pudding: it was a huge portion for two people. Decent bread pudding with a tasty icing. But the entire middle was still cold. But our waitress was awesome and didn't charge us for it cuz we couldn't eat it. 
The appetizers were definitely the highlight of the meal.. I would come back for happy hour for a beer and just apps for sure. Unfortunately they dropped the ball with the other dishes.

A philly must see! Fantastic farmers market with fresh food brought in daily! Head in towards the end of the night for cookies for $1! Fresh bread at various stores and fresh gourmet oil at the tubby olive! With so many restaurants, everyone can find something to eat!

This is a Philly institution, and for good reason.  The variety of foods, the busy atmosphere, the history--definitely worth a visit.  My favorites include the Amish pretzels and cheesecake, sweet Lebanon bologna sandwiches, and the cinnamon ice cream at Bassett's!
I have been enjoying this place for a few years now. One of my favorite places to find Indian cuisine in Philly. Kati rolls with the white sauce is to die for definitely a must try.

Welp...
I made it home sweet home for the weekend and I am neva, eva, eva disappointed by the magnificent Reading Terminal. Did I mention never? You walk in and you still get that quaint, old fashion charm of the Terminal with new and trendy foods to satisfy the pickiest of eaters and those with food restrictions. I can't even begin to tell you, but I will, how elated I was to find an All vegan foodery in the Terminal!!!!! LUVH Vegan Deli was e.ver.y.tang!!!!!!! Oh my gosh!!!! I was able to have an Italian Hoagie that made my taste buds sing, and then the vegan Rueben....what?!!!!! The Pineapple Bundt Cake....smh....you all need to stop....the delicousness...well...I'm here for it alllllll!!!!! If you make it to Philly and you want a plethora of choices take yourself to the Reading Terminal and enjoy a little bit of evrything.

In terms of honeygrow experiences, this one was just okay. The ordering process was straightforward and easy as always, and there was a lot of seating in this particular location. I was in the mood for something different from my usual salad order. I had tried the red coconut curry before at an event so decided to go with that. 

It took a while for the order to come up but since I was getting something hot instead of a salad, that was fine. When my name was called, I had to ask for a cup and the extra slice of bread that I ordered. I feel like this happens a lot at honeygrow; something often tends to be missing from the final order (occasionally, it's the salad dressing, which is super annoying when you get it all the way home!). 

My noodles were so lightly dressed there was barely any flavor. I was glad I added on crunchy onions at the last minute, otherwise there woudn't have been much taste at all. 

I really like honeygrow overall and especially their mission to use high-quality ingredients, but the experiences can be hit or miss.

Working in philly allows me to stop into reading several times a week, which I happily do.
Everything from produce, butchers, cheesesteaks and dessert is offered. Not to mention a florist, organic skin care and even clothing. Seriously, there's so much offered here.

One I first started to come to reading I was overwhelmed with all the food options, what to eat, what do drink, who offers a better special, who makes a better sandwich, ugh, so many options.
But I mean, who can really complain about having to many options?! NO ONE! 
All the spots I have tried here are great! Food is good and staff is good.

Seating is limited but what do you expect? This place is always packed and has hundreds of people at any given time. They always have piano player during the lunch hours which is really cute. 

Come on an empty stomach, be open to trying something new and walk around the whole place! Look at all your options! Enjoy!!!

Clearly this is the #1 go to spot in Philly. This is a big market in the city. They have everything your heart desires from donuts to pancakes to chocolate and cheese steaks. You must come here if you are visiting. Expect it to be extra crowded on weekends. Come hungry, leave full and happy. Wish I had something like this closer to home.

I recently moved to Philadelphia and have been trying a ton of new restaurants. NAYA is one that I have continued to order from week after week and I have yet to be disappointed. I'm a huuuuuuge falafel fan and I've tried a few in the area but no one beats NAYA. Highly recommend this place (and try the rekakat and spicy green sauce)!!!

On 2 different occasions (because I gave them a second chance) they had prepared my orders incorrectly. 
1st time: I requested milk with my coffee. Received my order with cream - in which I am unable to have because it makes me nauseous it's why I requested milk! Then my bowl of food had no utensils or napkins, was I supposed to eat my food in the bowl with the coffee stirrer that was included along with the creams I didn't ask for? 
2nd chance: there was a staff taking order with her iPad. I carefully asked if you guys had milk because I cannot drink cream, she said yes. I said ok. Proceeded to the next station where another staff gave me my receipt. What did it say?! Coffee w/ sugar ‍. Proceeded to the pickup window, got my order, checked the bag, what was in it?! JUST SUGAR! Luckily I checked before leaving trusting that my order was correct! I told the staff what I ordered and that your co-worker reassured me that I will get what I asked for. This was when I found out from them that they DON'T HAVE MILK! This isn't a problem for me if I was told at first instead of just misleading me. I am a customer! Do you not want business?! Just do your job! Don't mislead a customer especially when you're in the food industry! Often times having a meal is what everyone look forward to the most after a bad day and to have their order incorrectly not once but twice, it isn't a pleasant experience unless of course, you don't care about the voice of your paying customers.

They have two tablets as soon as you walk in where you can order. Food was prepared quickly. They have some tables on the sidewalk for you to chow down.

Kati rolls were OK. I only recommend the Paneer Masala out of the 3 we tried. Both the chicken roll and aloo roll were too salty for my liking.

The Reading Terminal Market is phenomenal! They have a little of everything from fancy corn dogs to classic American baked goods, soul food, and Louisiana classics like gumbo. They are more than just food stalls; they sell cheeses, bread, meats, and a range of fresh seafood. They are friendly for almost every diet including veganism. 100% recommend this place, perfect for exploring new flavors and any meal with friends with different taste.
I live in Philadelphia and when my friends come in from out of town I take them here an they all love it. Pastrami sandwich's, Amish food, cheesesteaks, cookies, and much more

Great local market in center city of philadelphia near municipal building, a lot options to get with varieties special when big events happening at convention center philadelphia or holidays events every years

Like every other blog, article, and Yelp review says, Reading Terminal Market is a must visit if you're travelling to Philly. It has every kind of food imaginable, and there are so many great spots for dessert that even I was sugared out by the time I left (that literally never happens). We arrived at 9 am which was perfect because it wasn't as busy and we were able to beat most of the lines that got much longer by the time we left at noon. We ate at least 10 stands, and while there were some items that were just ok (Beiler's donuts, 4th street cookie, Bassett's ice cream), everything was worth trying.

Honestly I give this food market 5/5. One of the better food markets I've been to with so many different types of foods, produce, and fresh meats! I love love love the apple dumplings, the tiramisu pastry at termini is so good, pretzel is so soft, my list of foods to get from here are endless!

My go to healthy fast food options are Honeygrow and Sweetgreen. Now Sweetgreen takes the cake (ironic I know) for salads in my opinion however Honeygrow wins for stir fry! I try to get something different every time I go. I've gotten Spicy Garlic, Walnut Basil Pesto, Red Coconut Curry, and i've created my own. Red Coconut Curry is however my absolute favorite of the bunch. If you're a Thai food fanatic this is your dish. 

Also a huge plus in my opinion, you can customize (types of noodles, protein, veggies, sauces, etc) each dish at a kiosk so they don't have to deal with undeceive people..aka me.

Tip: Make sure for protein you UNSELECT the default option before choosing another protein option. lol I wanted tofu so I selected it but didn't realize the shrimp was still selected...so I ended up getting both in my stir fry. It was interesting and in my defense, I was starving so I wasn't paying attention lol May the odds be in your favor y'all!

My favorite place in Philadelphia - really.  This is the place I've taken out of town guests for years.  You can get pretty much anything foodwise here, whether fresh or cooked by the many small and diverse restaurants within the market.  This is the real deal - it's been around for over a 100 years without a chain place in sight and not a fake mall-type food court.  It's also right smack in the center of the city.  Don't miss the Amish pretzels - freshly made in front of you.  The pretzels don't travel so just stuff your face while you're at the market.

I ordered two vegan pizzas here on Tuesday 1/12/21.  It was suppose to be beyond meat sausage and the girl told me it was vegan cheese I took a bite when I got home and yes it was delicious but I felt like something wasn't right.   I went to pizza hut in warminster and ordered the same pizza.  I was told they don't have vegan cheese yet so I just ordered the beyond meat sausage pizza.   The sausage was lighter in color and rounder than the sausage from 4501 castor ave.  The manager name Ross sold me two pizza's that was not vegan.  I don't know if this is the African american girls fault with the braids or the managers.  VEGANS BEWARE GO TO WARMINSTER FOR YOUR VEGAN PIZZA.  I CAN'T BELIEVE I ATE ANIMAL PRODUCTS ON TUESDAY.  DO THEY REALLY NEED MONEY THAT BAD???  I EVEN GAVE THE BLACK GIRL A FIVE DOLLAR TIP AND SHE TOTALLY PLAYED ME.  SHE KNEW I ASKED FOR VEGAN EVERYTHING!!!!   NEVER AGAIN!!!

I absolutely love Chick-fil-A! The staff and food are always spot on. No complaints about that. The line is always long but what chick-Fil-a isn't?! 
I wish this business was closer to my home.

I love this place! I can stay in this market for hours. I came here for to peruse and came across Keren Parker Soul Food Cafe.
Now, this IS the BEST soul food I've had in my days on this earth. I ordered the chicken wings with mac n cheese and another order of candied yams. The entrees come with one side. Also the tropical ice tea with the slice of watermelon was icing on the cake.
It was so good, I ate there everyday during my visit to Philly. I also visited the Amish bakery which is to die for. Tip: They close on Sundays.
Another Tip: Go with an empty stomach, this isn't for the faint of heart/stomach.

A great spot in center city that used to be a go to when I was in the office! My top 3 falafel fast casual placed in the city and the staff has always been so lovely to me and my inability to make a decision when ordering. Definitely stop in!

Our stop here was my favorite of the day! My friend and I loved walking around and checking out all of the beautiful and delicious piles of food, and the cool little stalls.  So glad my drIver recommended we stop here. Ate donuts in the morning and lunch too, and tried to get as many restaurants in at a time! 

Bfast: get a donut and coffee!!
Lunch: bye George--get a Stromboli or try the local pizza (forget what they call a slice) where they slather a square of dough w loads of tomato sauce. Greek salad was good too! Also, stop by the pickle stand and get a Kosher dill--YUMMMMMM!!

Missing 1 star for a lack of contact info so you can't even call to get any info like what their slice of the day is. Maybe there's a website that gives that kind of info in which case I'd give them 5 raving stars. Now I recall you're supposed to go to their insta.

Anyway, the name alone made me want to eat there. I think it's simply the name of the street it's on but for an out of towner like me it's intriguing. I met an employee when I got there a 1/2 hour before they opened for lunch and he was so nice. 

We ended up not waiting for lunch but rather going back for dinner. We got that day's special pie which happened to be vegetarian which is perfect for me. I don't remember what was on it other than pear but it was an amazing combo of flavors, it's a white pie, btw. It was also HUGE! Cooked perfectly.

I love food markets and this one didn't disappoint. The minute you walk in you are in food heaven. The aroma in this place is unbelievable, all of your senses will be working overtime. If you are foodie like myself then you must come here. I got to try some Cajun food, roast pork sandwich, cookies, candy apple and olive oils. I was pretty full by the time I saw the Amish place and the fresh donuts so I couldn't try them but I will next time I'm in town.

This is a great marketplace. There is a great variety of restaurants and shops. I spent a lot of money here. Watch out for the crowds. Lines can get very long at peak hours, it can be difficult and frustrating to navigate. I was with someone who gets anxiety in crowds and we had to leave, so take note of that. Come outside of peak lunch times if crowds are an issue for you. Some of us returned later to eat and I went back later to do some shopping. I found great gifts for my family, instead of the usual souvenir shops. I wish there was more seating and it would be nice if some of the food stalls stayed open a little later at night to accommodate people coming from the Convention Center later in the evening. That said, if I'm back in Philly, I will return.

Wow just wow! When I first walked into this place I nearly had a breakdown. I love food so much and they literally have any and everything that I could possibly want. 

My first thought was to not pick the first place I saw and to do a complete walk through of the entire space. What a bad idea because I wanted everything that I saw! I decided to go with Becks Cajun cafe for my lunch and I couldn't have been any happier. (The blackened catfish is delicious!)

There are also many places where you can buy fresh seafood, meat, produce, etc. If I lived closer I would definitely shop there for all of those things! The only negative thing I will say is that grocery prices are jacked up slightly. Everything else is very decently priced. 

I will definitely be back when I'm in the Philly area again!
Amazing and fresh food. The staff is very friendly and considerate. I ordered the 2 bowls and 1 wrap. Everything was delicious. Will sure be back again.

Hello hello! I stopped here while visiting a close friend of mine in Philli, and I must say that I was in for a treat.

I ordered chicken briyani as my meal, and I got a mint lemonade on the side (handcrafted by the restaurant). The food came out very quick, and it was absolutely so delicious! By all means authentic Indian food, I grabbed white sauce and hot and spicy red sauce to dress my food in. The chicken was extremely flavorful, you could taste the notes of each and every spice that the chicken was seasoned with. The Naan bread complimented the dish perfectly, and I made sure to dip with each and every single bite of food.  The mint lemonade was so fresh and it seemed to compliment the food perfectly. It added a special zest to my taste buds. 

I was in paradise, and I recommend that you give this place a go! Cheers to good eats!

Came here for the first time and it's a very clean restaurant. I was a typical newbie and forgot my drink at the counter, but the person who brought us our food was kind enough to get it. The rest of the staff are very friendly and everyone is neatly dressed. I'll be coming back again.
What's not to love?! One stop shop ftw! Do yourself a favor and pass by the Metropolitan Bakery. Thank me later

If you are visiting Philadelphia, you should definitely stop by this market. It's not a "luxury" place, but it has a lot of different food stands and dining options...very "philadelphia". Sometimes there is also live music. To eat your food, there is a communal dining area, or you can get it to go. Most of the stands are very good... but can be a bit on the pricey side.

I work in Philly during the weekdays - this is a solid quick lunch or dinner spot. Most of my friends prefer Naya over Cava. I think I'd go to Cava for a bowl, and Naya for a wrap. Overall, Cava does have more options - just don't go too crazy with all your toppings or it'll taste funny.

Last time I went to Naya, I arrived a little before 8PM (closing) and they still managed to accommodate me and fry my falafel on the spot! I got a whole wheat wrap, babaganoush (eggplant spread), lettuce, pickled turnips, cucumbers, tomatoes, and the mild tomato base "spicy red" sauce on the side. They also heat up and toast your wrap for you which is great - like a Lebanese burrito! For $9, I was pretty full from my whole wheat pita wrap. 

I'd definitely recommend to come again!
My favorite place in Philadelphia. the freshest produce and some great places to eat. my favorite place in Hershels

Pizza was good but the staff was very rude to us. They made us feel uncomfortable and it was a really weird situation. I wouldn't recommend coming here and I definitely won't be back. FYI, they have prices listed for whole pies but the staff says "one slice per person."

The Reading Terminal has most of the best foods Philly has to offer under one roof. Looking for a REAL Philly cheesesteak? You can get one here. Looking for some fruits and vegetables fresh from a farmer in Lancaster? Right here. Looking for a quick lunch that's healthy and fun to eat? Right here. Termini's, one of the best bakeries in Philly? Get their to die for cannoli right here! You can't go wrong at the Reading Terminal.

What do you say about an amazing place that already has over 600 reviews?  I know; put the ten (10) most important things you need to know all in one place.  So, especially if you are a 1st timer, read on.

1. Be prepared to embrace the crowds.  It's part of the Reading Terminal experience.  Think about it.  All those folks are there because the place is so amazing!

2. Don't visit on Sunday, Monday, or Tuesday.  Why you ask?  There are over a dozen Pennsylvania Dutch (Amish) vendors that are definitely worth visiting.  They have special hours and don't open on these days.  It would be a mistake not to see them.

3. If you want the very best deals make sure you end your visit during the last hour of each day.  That would be between 5:00 and 6:00 PM Monday -Saturday and 4:00 to 5:00 PM on Sunday.

4. If you are a foodie be prepared to be overwhelmed, stunned, amazed, and generally blown away.  You won't be able to do it justice in two (2) hours.  Think three (3) or more.

5. Speaking of two (2) hours, it will cost you $4 for that amount of time at the 12th & Filbert garage.  All you need to do is spend $10 and any vendor will validate your ticket.  Even better is to not park at all and take public transportation.  

6. Check the website for cool events especially to see the live music schedule.  http://www.readingterminalmarket.org/events/

7. Some folks say the place is touristy and they are partially correct.  That's true of some of the vendors but anyone with half a brain can spot them in a second.  If that's not your thing just walk on by.

8. If you want to stay in the market and have an adult libation, check out Molly Malloy's.  It's a great place for a beer.

9. If you are thinking about lunch at prime time (11:30-1:00), please think again.  And then think again and again.  Trust me; it's complete and utter craziness.  Eat early or eat late.

10. Last but not least let's talk Tommy DiNic's as this legendary emporium deserves special mention.  I know, I know, you saw Man vs. Food and you want "The Sandwich."  Is it worth it?  Yeah, it is.  Stroll the market and stop back occasionally to check on the length of the line.  If you see it below twenty five (25) folks, go for it.  It really is an amazing sandwich.

As just about everyone says this place is a must for a Philly visitor.

This place a must visit when in Philly! It's an indoor food market and has anything and everything you could want! Cajun, Chinese, American, Indian, Thai, bake shops - everything!!!! 

Some of my favorite places - Beiler's donuts (coconut custard donut is to die for), Becks Cajun (gumbo is great), Miller's Twist (jumbo pretzel dog with cheese), Sangkee (roasted duck with lo mein), crepes (forgot the name of the place.

What an amazing selection at this market! Food and goods from local businesses all in one spot. Perfect place to eat with picky friends or family because there is something for everyone. Avoid the chaos of prime lunch hour or if eating there, take turns grabbing food while someone snags a table in the seating area. 

Check out the map or website ahead of time to look at reviews and items you want, otherwise you could end up with a dud or annoyed locals if you don't know what you want. :-) The only bathrooms are way in the back by the seating area. Please note that they lock doors at 6 PM, so don't plan on spending time here after your 9-5 job or after a day of tourist exploration. 

Variety and some really unique and/or homemade food or products make this place a winner!
Haven't been here in awhile but I know it's a Philadelphia staple. Must try if you're visiting the city.
Reading Terminal Market is a wonderful place! There are so many delicious food options to enjoy. It is crowded on the weekends so it might take a little longer to find a place to sit.

This is one of the best places in Philadelphia 
All the venders serve really good food . Love every inch fresh meats , poultry , fish cold cuts ,spices and a great vegetable market . The Duck Lomein is delicious

Always make it a tradition to stop by Reading whenever I visit Philly! This morning we came by for breakfast and decided to get bagel sandwiches at the Market Bakery. The service here was fast and efficient, so the line goes by fast! We enjoyed our sandwiches very much. One thing that stood out to me was how soft and fluffy the bagels were! Very delicious and worth our time.

favorite place to go play and bring out of town guests.  Something for everyone.  High dollar to low dollar; useful to flightful fancy love this place.  Prefer to drive in but the train experience is great for the grandkids they love it.

I love Reading Terminal Market!  It literally has anything and everything you are looking for.  I sometimes go just to look around, and I probably go there every weekend.  I love the falafel place and Bee Natural , which has honey chapstick, candles, soap, and regular honey.  So many surprises like really cheap produce and a used bookstore.
I love coming into this place everytime I am in Philadelphia. The wide selections of food, snacks, supplies etc has me constantly coming back.

This place is top 5 one of the best places to visit and eat from in Philly. Born and raised in Philly and I still get excited when I go and spend more money than I intend to. It's hard to resist all of the delicious treats and food in this place. It's a foodies dream!

Must stop spot in Philly.  You will always find something you can eat.  Come here hungry and try a little something at each of the stands.  Very busy business lunch so be prepared to wait and be cramped for seating.

reading terminal market is bustling with locals and tourists all trying to get a bite or two of philadelphia's best grub. from soul food to gyros, an oyster bar to cheesesteaks, doughnuts, roast beef, falafel, gourmet cookies, crepes, etc. etc. etc.... 

lots of choices. you'll want to bring some tasty local treats home, so make reading terminal market one of your last stops if you're visiting. trust me, you'll want to come hungry. and bring friends so you can share lots of dishes from all over the indoor market.

the prices are great, and there's something for everyone's tastes. also, it's not all food (well, it's mostly food)... there's a great florist and various little shops for locally made goods and crafts, too!

seriously though, you'll eat til you're stuffed and then eat some more.

tip: if you have the choice, don't come on a Sunday. many of the stands are closed on sundays (including beiler's doughnuts, which are incredibly delish). boo.

I haven't been to a chick-fil-a in years after there controversy against the gay community. This particular restaurant happens to be the closest of my niece favorite place.  Going inside was probably the first mistake because the first thing that catches my eye is everyone behind the counter, kitchen and floor had long hair. I only seen two workers wearing any type of head gear and one was  a male. I was flabbergasted that I was even seeing this but she wanted something from this place. I joked to her don't be upset if you find hair in your food. I just got a salad because you can't mess up a salad right? Boy was I so ever wrong! This was just bad karma at me because I told my wife this place looks like a hair fashion show or contest for the longest hair. How can you even give this place any stars. I'm sure there better spots out there but this will never be frequented by my family again. 
Stay away if you don't want long hair in your veggies or go to attend the hair show. My votes on the girl with the blond braids down to her calves.
Very nice place! I would recomment the pulled pork sandwich at Dinic's.

i love reading terminal market, it has a wide variety of food and wares and definitely a fun place to visit if your in philly. it's also right near chinatown if you want to make a day out of going to the two
Love this place. Be sure to check out the spice shop in the back. The doughnuts are to die for.
Wonderful place to get shop through for different stores try different foods. Korean hotdogs!

There's no bad thing to say. For 100 years and variety, the doors are still open and always busy tells the story. If anyone says anything bad about Hershel's, look for a fight, with a little fat on it.

Did not eat here today but there was a shrimp on the floor right by the door. PLEASE clean this please! I almost steped on him and could have sliped! I have ate here before I found the shrimp and I like it but it makes me want to have more food. It's good and tasty but please Fran needs some more food! Here is the picture proof of the shrimp.

Hi Reading Terminal Market, this place is awesome and I would say this is Philly's food heaven!  Parking may be an issue if you come here during peak eating hours, but you may be lucky with some street parking, or just suck it up and park at a deck!

Anyways, this market does have some fresh food stands, similar to a farmer's market style if you have some grocery shopping to do, but I feel the best part of this place are the massive amount of food stands inside.  Beware if you come here on an empty stomach, you will want to try so many things that I am sure you will get full quick... and buy too much!

Over the years Reading Terminal Market has allowed people to try many various types of food.  Whether you are looking for a good sandwich, cheesesteak, Asian food, soul food, pastries, ice cream, donuts... it is all here!   

NOTE: The general hours of Reading Terminal do not apply to ALL the food stands.  Some close earlier on specific days and a few (the Amish establishments) are not even open are Sundays.  Take a look at the operating hours of specific food stands you want to check out before you come here or else you may be disappointed that it is closed!

Some of my favorite stands:

Bassetts Ice Cream - Ice Cream!
Beck's Cajun Cafe - Gumbo!
Beiler's Bakery - Doughnuts!
Carmen's Famous - Cheesesteaks!
Flying Monkey Bakery - Whoopie Pies!
Hershel's - Brisket, Corned Beef, and/or Pastrami Sandwich! 
Meltkraft - Grilled Cheese Sandwich!
Sang Kee Peking Duck - Duck noodle soup!
Tommy DiNiC's - Roast Pork Sandwich!

There are still other stands I have yet to try.  So yes, I HAVE to come back again!  It is just so hard to try new things when many of these dishes are already very satisfying :)

Place is small with limited seating.
Had the MK Special. It was tasty. Was surprised to find the$2.25 coke I ordered was only 8.5 oz...

Very nice indoor market, converted from what used to be a train station, and it is a local landmark. Here you can find a lot of interesting things from Philly Cheesesteak or Hoagie shops and other kinds of little eateries to coffee shops to meat shops to bakeries to shops that sell little international crafts to produce, etc. I included one of my personal favorite eateries and coffee shops in my photos. The only problem is that it often gets too overcrowded sometimes. Otherwise, this place is very interesting and a must-see on your to-do-list during your visit to Philly! I always stop here when I visit the Philadelphia Area...
