I absolutely love it here. My husband and I always stop here when in town. The market offers such a vast variety of different shops and food venues. It's always busy, so try and get here on "off" times if you want to avoid the crowds. Plenty of parking nearby if you're traveling in.

Okay, I don't have that much to say about Green leafs and Bananas but I will say that their food and smoothies are absolutely out of this world; amazingly delicious.  Green Leafs and Bananas is located at the airport in Philly right next to Delta Airlines departing gate.  After a very long flight plus a layover in St Paul, Minnesota, my husband and I only had a small bowl of cereal that morning plus some complimentary snacks on the plane which consisted of a tiny bag of almonds and some ice water, we were absolutely starving!  Green Leafs and Bananas was right in front of us and we wanted to eat anything at that point; I am extremely happy we decided to eat here.  I got a tomato and mozzarella panini sandwich and a strawberry smoothie and my husband got a turkey and cheese panini sandwich and a soft drink.  The panini bread was grilled and the cheese was melted perfectly and gooey (yum)!  My strawberry smoothie was super delicious and one of the best smoothies I have ever tasted.  My husband loved his panini as well and the price of our meals were not expensive either.  Other items on the menu included smeared bagels, soft served frozen yogurts with toppings and make your own salads too.  This was the perfect place to satisfy our hunger pains and quite delicious too.
Great selection, fresh produce, vegan options. Cookie spot is delicious & has great coffee
One of the best assets Philadelphia has. I would shop for all of my groceries here if I had the pecuniary means.

I like this place. Not sure how I'm supposed to write a review for this place there's lots of places to eat here. I guess if it's the entire market I'll say that that front left area is nice, feels more authentic. The back seating area has too many neon I feel. It's not so crowded like you see in the movies and it doesn't feel really like a market-market either because its not really a bunch of open shops. It's a food joint as far as I'm concerned and they've got a good selection. The Rib Stand is pretty good. I tried the the Spataro Cheesesteak too which isn't bad. I tried going here late but they close way too early as far as I'm concerned. Looks like a lot of places close down early here in Philly. But I like this place, like I said. Plenty of food to pick from.
What's not to love!  Crowded, sure, but great food, drinks, coffee, everything.  A must see and enjoy place when in Philly.

I am a loyal of the other -not to be mentioned other kati roll place in center city west-. 

I was returning to Philly and my bestie Anupma S. suggested we try this place for our drunk cravings. 

It's full of drunk young American Indians after 2am. 

I got the masala paneer roll and didn't like it. Too much fake curry it was so liquidy. And none of the crunchy onions like I like and fresh cilantro. And the white sauce didn't hit the spot. The curry was just that standard gross stuff you get like in the box at Trader Joes *exotic indian curry in 2 min*. 

Leaving at 3 stars cause service was nice, and fast, and maybe it was just my roll.

We liked it ....but it was crowded and noisy and difficult to maneuver.  If you like that then think of a higher rating as I took a star off because of it.  Very difficult to find what you were looking for.  Some businesses more friendly than others.  seapite the variety, did not find everything we were looking for.
Love this place! I come every year around the holidays!! my favorite. I recommend to go to the Juice Bar!! so refreshing!

This is the best food hall I've ever been to (granted I haven't been to many, but this one is a must do in Philly). Was very crowded on a Saturday at 4:30pm. 

The building is right downtown - an old train terminal converted to a huge, open area absolutely packed with local purveyors. It seemed like there were close to 100 sellers, offering meats, fresh veggies, baked goods, ice cream, coffee,  flowers, tons of international cuisine, and more. There are atms, a small seating area and bathrooms. 

I only had the time and appetite for the ice cream from Bassetts (which was great) but I definitely want to go back to try others. If long lines are any fair judgment of how good a place is, then I need to try the donuts from Beiler's - the line wrapped around half the market. 

I could totally spend a couple hours here at least. Check it out if you're in town.

Reading Terminal Market is a Mecca for foodies and shoppers alike.

This place has everything, from butchers to bakeries, to olive oil emporiums, to bars, to gifts and cookbooks, to prepared foods and farmers markets....you cannot go wrong when coming here.  There is something for everyone!  

When I come to Reading Terminal, I usually need a game plan, otherwise I will spend hours walking around and exploring everything they have.  I certainly have my favorite spots, but I like to try something new or something different every time I come as well.

If you haven't had a Sandwich from DiNic's, make sure you stop by.  I also love a good corndog from Fox and Son's Fancy Corn Dogs.  My favorite butcher is Giunta's Prime Shop, and I can never go without grabbing some ice cream or a Beiler's Donut. 

I would also highly suggest checking out the cheese vendors and chocolate/candy vendors!  

Honestly, you cannot go wrong here, I could easily go on and on about each vendor I have tried, but frankly, this review would be way too long if I did that!

I personally like to come at off times to avoid the lunch rush, it can get very crowded and overwhelming.  But coming on an off time during the week helps with that.

The best thing to do if you have never come before is make sure you have lots of time to spare.  I suggest walking around and trying a bunch of different things.  I also suggest coming with an idea of what you need and then trying something new each time you come.  The possibilities  are practically endless!  A Philadelphia staple, make sure to check our Reading Terminal Market if you can!

What a great place. All 7 of us went for lunch and everyone got what they wanted. For me it was lobsta mac n cheese OMG. best i have ever had. Then we got ice cream, some olive oil to bring home and fresh flowers to enjoy.
Thin and crispy, great tang on the sauce, perfect amount of grease. Had a plain slice but will be back to try their specials. No frills, standing room only. Awesome guys running the shop.

If you are a tourist or a local go early. It gets so packed that you can't move without being an inch from someone else despite my need for personal space, I still love this place (especially the vegan desserts at Flying Monkey). You can literally find something for everyone: fresh product; homemade items such as confections, candy, and pickles; candles; wine; limoncello; books; etc. with so many places under one roof. I especially love taking my nephews here for to watch them make donuts at the mini donut factory.
Amazing place to grab lunch during the lunch rush. So many options and so much delicious food! I always stop by this place when I'm in Philly!

1 star is way more than I would give them. Ordered from DoorDash tonight, a 60 dollar order for my family, we did not receive ONE thing that we ordered. They gave us a bunch of old chicken strips, popcorn nuggets & chicken littles. Probably not even half the worth of what we ordered. Everything was cold & gross. I don't understand how you can possibly get every single thing wrong. I work in food service, that's almost HARD to do.

Love love love this place!  It is amazing and anyone who visit Philly must come visit this Market on an empty stomach!  And I mean it!  Once you walk in, you'll feel like you will get lost with so much going on under one roof.  One corner you see people showing for produce and the next corner you see a meat market.  Throughout the entire market there are different eateries, bakeries, desserts, ice cream and a bunch of goodies that you're wishing you had a third stomach just so you can try everything!  

Take some times to look around!  My friend and I have already decided the next time we visit, it will be on an empty stomach and trying a little bit of everything at each station.
Been shopping here for so long, great deals at OK Lee Produce, and the pound deals for cheese at Downtown Cheese are amazing!

I ordered online. When I went to pick up, I actually had an order to pick up. This was my third chipotle today. The only one that had sofritias. I was also pleasantly surprised to see out of all the locations I've entered today, this one was doing in person orders as well.  Guest and workers wearing mask properly. Only downfall was no silverware in the bag or out to grab.

It is very unfortunately if you have a bad bladder and have to use the restroom there is no where to use the restroom here in the city because most of the restaurants like this are not allowing the general public to use the restrooms
There is literally something for everyone here. Huge variety of foods and drinks. It is pretty crowded and like most of these types of markets not much seating to really enjoy what you get to eat.

Love this place! It's like the Mediterranean version of chipotle. The staff are so friendly and the food was so good! The chicken in my bowl was perfectly cooked and the toppings were all delicious. I loved my bowl and would definitely order from here again!
Reading Terminal market has the best selection of food in the inter city hands down I don't got to the supermarkets  like Shoprite any more

Reading Terminal Market is the most magical place on Earth, not Disney.  I don't think words can express how much I love this market.   It is one of the oldest public markets in the USA.  It's been around for 126 years.  You can find anything here.  The market has a wide variety of ethic products, Pennsylvania dutch products, homemade soaps, local spirits, locally sourced produce and meats, international and domestic cheeses, exquisite chocolates, and much much more.  

I am obsessed with Downtown Cheese, a shop offering an overwhelming selection of cheeses and cold cuts from all over the globe.  Mueller Chocolate Co. was my second favorite shop.  They have a chocolate covered onion and other unique chocolate offerings.  I personally enjoy the truffles.  

This place is also foodie heaven with all the little quirky restaurants offering from American, Mediterranean, Italian, Vegan, Caribbean, I think you get the picture; they have whatever you fancy.

5 stars! My new favorite spot in Philly.

Did not live up to expectations.  They are rationing tap water at the front and do not include raita for biryanis.  Platters are expensive compared to what you get in nyc for the same portion of food and taste is middling or average.  I got the chicken and rice platter and there were no grilled onions or peppers.  Just minced spicy chicken and rice with a weak salad.  Vegetable Biryani is very run of the mill.  And what is with the water rationing.  Excuse was only one jug of water and it's filled less than halfway.  They would've gotten three but just lost a star for this cheapness

I feel sooo lucky that such a service exists. Since I'm moving, between laundry back up and time, Got Laundry saved the day! I had the pleasure of meeting Ray, what a nice and professional guy. I actually ENJOY the the fact of having done business and supported a family business instead of Big Box business. It just proves there are still caring businesses and people around. I'm just sorry I'll only be a 1 time customer since I'm moving out of state. Got Laundry? sets the bar high for other businesses to follow. Thank you sooooooo much Ray/family. Money can always be replaced some how, but time is something you'll never get back. Got Laundry? has saved that precious time. I would recommend this business over and over.

weirdos, children working in booths, cool vendors and awesome produce. i honestly thought the market would be much bigger... however, once you're inside the actual building- it's kind of underwhelming. even with that fact... i still enjoyed coming here!

many booths were closed and i wasn't able to tour everything here. from Italian sandwiches, Gumbo, Gyros, Fish & Chips, Ice Cream, etc... this is a great way to get your chow on!

I am never disappointed at chick fila. This location was no different. Excellent service with a smile! Food was fresh and delicious. A step above all other fast food establishments. Keep up the great work!

Great place to get a bite to eat, but many heath code violations. Definitely recommend tho great food, who cares about violations and i right Seriously great place to get in and out of quick with great food!!!

Delicious place for slices! Hard to beat the former pizza shop here, but pretty close. The special was awesome--purple cauliflower on pizza with a basil cream base and bell peppers--so so good! Plus, they let me draw on the walls!  will definitely be back next time I'm in my former neighborhood!

I'd like to give 4 stars for the ambience and variety of food offerings they have, but I was left feeling pretty underwhelmed by the food I and my boyfriend ended up ordering. I would say 3 stars for the food. After getting my bearings and dodging long lines, I settled on getting a falafel pita from a middle eastern stall. The pita was fairly dry and underwhelming. I also got a "spinach samosa" from an Indian food stall and it was not good. The samosa was essentially a turnover with no flavor and it was almost $5. My boyfriend got food from Franks a lot which was also pretty underwhelming with a really slow moving line. He got a hot dog that took an obscenely amount of time to get and was the least complicated thing on the menu and onion rings. All in all, reading terminal is a huge tourist trap, so be prepared to wait in long lines for underwhelming food depending on whichever stall you find yourself at. I would suggest it for a snack and to see it, but perhaps not for a satisfying meal.

We walked around Philly for a few hours and were hungry. Reading Terminal Market better have been worth it, dammit. When we walked into the place, it was kind of cool and perplexing: think an indoor street fair, but well-regulated. In a terminal, go figure.

Unfortunately, the day we came was the day before Memorial Day and a couple of places were closed. Fortunately, it was the day before Memorial Day and the place wasn't engulfed in crows and long lines.

As we circled around the different food vendors, I kept passing by the nondescript Basic 4 Vegetarian Snack stand. It looked so unassuming, kind of sparse, and the nice ladies were walking back and forth albeit not taking orders because there weren't many customers to serve. 

My sister settled for some Cajun food and I grabbed a veggie chili cheeseburger.

Oh my.

I stuffed my face. Because this is the best fake-burger I ever had!!! It was a little steep for a "chili burger," (around $6-$7), but it was huge. And delicious. Two co-occurring adjectives that supersede price. Okay -- that can be read incorrectly if your mind is in the gutter. But that was some good fake-meat.
i love this place so much. I don't even know where to begin. Everybody is friendly and it's been SO clean & easy during the pandemic. Please go, as these small businesses need us!

Love both locations. Aloo paneer is my favorite. You can't beat the price for a great vegetarian meal!!!
I also get extra tomato sauce and I use it when I grill chicken at home

Food was incredibly good! The service was quick and friendly. Easy to walk up, get your delicious indian street food and they even have limited outdoor dining spots to sit and eat in the age of COVID. The rolls are like little burritos of your favorite Indian dishes...... amazing. Make sure you try the sauces too! They were priced so that you can buy a few as one won't fill up an adult with a hearty appetite. I will be back whenever I am in the area.

Overwhelming-- it's jam packed with food and treasures galore. I'm sure anything your heart desires can be found here. If only my stomach was as big as my eyes. Definitely a must do when in Philly. I'm from WA (state) and live in SD, and Reading terminal feels like a combo of a public market and Liberty Station (on like a macro scale or what Liberty Station wants to be).

Pizza Shackamaxon is my new standard in Philadelphia.  The perfectly browned undercarriage carries the weight of the delicious combination of sauce, cheese, and pepperoni. The perfect acid from the sauce mellows the cheese and spice kick from the crispy pepperoni. The crust is crunchy and chewy and the flavors blend together perfectly. The wait times aren't too bad (yet) and you can even order slices. Still no phone, but it truly reminds me of the good ol' days of the glorious previous tenant. Will be going back soon!

Enjoy!

Love this place! I visited Philadelphia with my sister and we ended up coming here everyday we were in town. 

There are many vendors and the Amish are there to sell their products on Saturdays. If you go on a Sunday, only about half the vendors are opened.

You can find everything from all sorts of food, bakery, dessert items to gift shops, beauty supply, etc. They're all local vendors and everything tastes amazing. We definitely enjoyed the soft pretzels, especially the stuffed breakfast pretzels.

Would highly recommend visiting here to try a variety of foods while in PA. I flew in from San Fran and loved this place. So many different places to try! Will definitely be coming back to try some more delicious food and drinks!
Best place to stop for breakfast / lunch in the city, regardless of if you are a tourist or local.
I come here a few times a week, great place to get any kind of food you want and do your grocery shopping as well.

This chipotle overcharged me twice. I compared the prices between this chipotle and the other chipotle in The Northeast Shopping Center and they just overcharged people. The employees just goof around in the back without masks on and they give you dirty looks. They look like they don't want to work there at all. When I walked in, one of the girls gave me a dirty look as if they didn't want ti serve me. The security guard is useless, he stays on the phone and comes in and out of the store.

Such a fun place to shop around downtown. We got fresh shucked oysters, seafood for my pup that was in the hotel for only $2.87 (we got six shrimps and a big sardine). I also bought some amazing shampoo bars (yes!! Ditch the bottles) as well as local raw honey! Our final spot was the four seasons juice bar. Simply amazing, super fast, and so refreshing. It was so well priced too. We got a medium (20 oz.) carrot cucumber ginger juice for only $4.95! You can find almost anything in this fun, busy, historical market. I am only giving 4 stars instead of 5 due to their lack of recycle bins and their use of styrofoams in some of their vendors stands. C'mon people, save the earth! Still would go back though.

So much stuff!  There's gooseberries in the produce section. The thing about the produce section is that it is so expensive.  for example, I just got starfruit at Trader Joes for $0.99 each, but was $1.99 and also about half the size here.  

Somewhere in Reading Terminal there's a stand with rose lassi and pomegranate lassi!  It's unhelpful that I forgot to make note of the name.  

I never go to Reading Terminal without getting gator gumbo at Beck's.

This place is not how I remember it. 

You can't pause for a half of a second without someone banging into you or being irritated with your presence being in their way. I felt like I was completely surrounded by people at all times without being able to take a breath. 

There were lines everywhere. People everywhere. *Questionable* people everywhere. 

I didn't even want to eat anything because the sheer volume of people made me feel like it can't possibly be clean. 

They have produce stands, bakeries, hot and cold food stands, people selling soap, jewelry, etc. You have to really pay attention because some things seem like great deals and others seem like total ripoffs. 

We did return at the very end of the day to get some cookies and it was much calmer and tolerable at that time. If I were to return here, it would definitely be towards the end of the day when the experience is better. If you like the hustle and bustle of crowds up your @$$ you will enjoy it no matter what. If you are not in the mood for crowds or aren't a crowd person at all, you can come in for the experience but you probably won't last long. 

if you've never been here at all and you are visiting Philly, go for the experience at least once. I personally will have to weigh the options before deciding if I want to go in again and I would never make a special trip to go there, that's for sure.
My favorite place in Philadelphia. I go here at least twice a week. Heaven. No matter what you're in the mood for, RTM has it.

I've been going to the Reading Terminal Market for years now and I love it. I love that I can get just about any kind of fresh meats, seafood and cheeses you could ever want. There are things I'd never thought I'd try but after going for so long you start to get an idea of what's good and decide to try it. I love the people and going on a rainy Saturday is the best. To have lunch and get all of your fresh foods and produce for dinner. And the candy, that is just indescribable as it's freshly made and so good. I would highly recommend that if you've never been, it's worth a visit whether you are local or visiting from another place. It's just as much a landmark as the Liberty Bell in my opinion. Totally worth the trip. If you plan on spending the day, I do suggest bringing a cooler so you can get your food to bring home since I believe it closes rather early.
Love this market, it was my first time,  a lot of great food and even candles and honey. The famous dinics is here, the best roast pork sandwich. My friends and I brought a lot of stuff.
Highly recommend if visiting the city! So many food choices and booths. However, there is no seating and it's very crowded.

This has always been my first stop on every trip to Philly.  You definitely have to come on a Saturday since the Amish vendors are not here on Sundays since they have to rest and go to church.  I usually get:

(1) Tommy DiNic's - roast pork, broccoli rabe, provolone cheese sandwich
(2) Miller's Twist - garlic pretzel
(3) Beiler's Bakery - maple bacon doughnut

There's probably a lot of other things I might get - shoo fly pie or apple dumpling from The Dutch Eating Place, cookies and cream ice cream cone from Bassetts Ice Cream, Train Wreck Po' Boy from Beck's Cajun Cafe, Pumpple Cake (vanilla cake/apple pie/chocolate cake/pumpkin pie) from Flying Monkey, or roast duck rice platter from Sang Kee.  Sadly, I only have one stomach and not many friends willing to go to Philly.  I came during COVID-19 times and there's a dine-in area in the back where you have to wait to be seated.  There's booths (max 4 people) and they clean each table after every seating.  I'll definitely be back when I come to visit Philly.

A great place to go when you want to eat a lot of different foods! A lot of tourists go to the Reading Terminal Market, but I know a lot of locals go there too. There are so many different foods to try that it is hard not to enjoy your experience. Whether you want delicious sandwiches, Spanish food or South American food you are bound to find something for the whole family! You can eat your way throughout the world all in one place in Philly! And definitely done forget to get desserts such as, cannolis or donuts!

Hmmmm.... How do you fairly rate a place with some of the neatest eateries in town but so crowded its like you're in a giant group hug as you navigate the place?  I had one of the best french crepes there outside of Paris.  Not the same but still very good.  I've purchased fine european linens there as well. There were lots of food stalls I'd love to try, but you HAVE to get there as soon as it opens.  Use the train if you can, parking is not handy.

Haven't you figured it out by now?  

Any place that has over 800 reviews, and is able to maintain 4 1/2 stars with all of those reviewers, is worth going to.  In fact, I'm shocked that anyone in their right mind would give this place only 4 stars.  

No, seriously, stop reading these reviews and just get your ass over there.  You'll thank us later!  

Because if you can't find something you want to eat at Reading Terminal Market, then you just don't like food.  Really, give it up and just go on a liquid diet or something.

Oh my gosh, so many good things to say about Reading Terminal Market.  Their variety of food is top notch and you always can find something new when you are there!  We are obsessed with 4th Street cookies.  They also do private events at this place, which I had no idea.  Would be really cool for a wedding - wish we had known about it!

The breakfast sandwich chicken egg and cheese on a biscuit is so good at this location! And the chicken is actually crispy and seasoned compared to other locations I have been to. 

The food was on point here, but it was lacking the smiling and friendly service I am used to at other locations. It's definitely a different environment at this location compared to other locations I've been to. I thought all the restaurants were the same but this one is way different when it comes to customer service.  I would return just because the chicken tasted so good, but I won't expect service with a smile or staff saying my pleasure- because the service here is lacking.

The sort of market I wished I had closer to home.

It's indoors with lots of food options: hot cooked to order, pre-made, baked goods, juice places, bakery items, fresh made baked goods, confectioners, smoothies, etc, etc. Some of the small restaurants have seats (from a couple of bar stools up to 15-20 seats). There's also common food court seating, although it was mostly full when I was there.

It could be chaos, but it's actually laid out pretty well, with a number of entrances, and enough division between establishments that it doesn't feel like a street market.

I sampled from 4-5 places (that's all my stomach could take). ALL were decent, and honestly surprisingly well-priced for the city center of a major metropolis. If I lived or worked nearby, I'd be in here regularly.

There's also one or more places offering a butcher, fishmonger, florists, produce, and a variety of knicknacks and home goods. It's a complete market, and that's though I probably missed a quarter of what was on offer.

At this point (June 2021) the majority of the market was open but masks were required inside. A handful of empty or vacated spots implied places that didn't make it... but the vast majority of the place was not just operating, but bustling.

There's one sour spot-- closing time is 6pm (when I was there), which is awfully early for the dinner or commuter crowd. I don't know if that's normal here, or a covid effect.

All of that deliciousness is housed in a historic structure with easy access from the city and tourist destinations. Small local businesses, a variety of good eats, a sense of community. Check it out!

My absolute favorite market in America.

This is because of the cheeses sold by the Mennonites, who are so nice that they provide samples of everything. And the prices...let's not forget how cheap they are!

You can find a steak and onion cheese, which is to die for! YUMMMMM!

And everything else in that market is too good for words. Even the butchers, who sell prime cuts that are ready to cook.

The mennonites sure know how to make hearty delicious food so go have anything they are selling.

Even the baked good are so cheap! I once got a red velvet cake here for $8.

I LOVE THIS MARKET SO MUCH! Go on a Saturday or Friday and not a Sunday when the Mennonites are not there. You need them.

My wife recently had some furniture reupholstered at  Ms Bak's Upholstery.
The work is done on premises.  She found the workmanship to be excellent.
It was completed when they said it would. They have material to choose from or you could purchase your own. They have pick up and delivery .She is so glad she
found this business.

A quintessential part of Philadelphia! There is something for everybody here! It's the ideal one stop shop and a must see if you're visiting from out of town! A few of my favorites are bielers for the donuts and by George for the eggplant parm and vegetable lasagna!

This is the market to which all other public markets should be judged. Whether you're shopping for food or looking for a meal this is the spot. It's a total mix of cultures from South Philly guys selling cheesesteaks, to the Asian seafood market, to the Southern Soul Food, to the Amish vendors, and everything in between. The oldest business in the market (and one of the oldest in all of Philly) is Bassett's Ice Cream (in Philly since 1861) they make some of the creamiest ice cream around. Two of my favorite treats here are the Amish pretzels at Miller's Twists and the Apple Dumplings at Dutch Eating Place (just to name a couple). The Terminal Market is a huge clean place and there's always a seat or two to sit and relax or eat, one seating area even has a piano player playing throughout the day. If food isn't your thing there are also a couple shops selling spices, wines, and gifts. If I had to narrow it down I would have to say Reading Terminal is one of the top 3 things to do while in Philly (next to the Art Museum and Eastern State Penn).

In the age of Covid 19 the scene at the market is pretty pathetic. Empty booths and no-show vendors make the place feel dead. Parking is stupid expensive. To get into the market you have to run a gauntlet of street beggars, winos and homeless. We definitely will not be back.

WOW, you must experience this cornucopia of food at least once during a trip to Philly. Its impossible to truly take it In during one visit. We made three separate trips and found something new each time. Desserts, meats, fish, Amish all sandwiched together and all seem to make money here. Dinics roast beef w/provolone was good but a bit dry, Martins Sausage stand we bought home ribs, ground beef and stew meat which were a good prices. Even got an insulated bag from them to get the meats home in good condition.Bassetts Ice cream had good ice cream and Flying Monkey bakery had good cupcakes. Overall great experience well worth a visit.
It is very busy during lunch time hours 11am-2pm so be prepared or come later in the day. Some stall close earlier Tuesday and Wednesdays (Amish mostly) You cant walk out of here empty handed.

POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE

Good food. Service is a little confusing. They announced my order but no one heard it. On enquiring about it, the lady had nothing to say. 

Visited the place again, ordered the "vegetable biriyani" for takeout. The server confirmed there will be gravy and paneer(cheese blocks) inside. On opening the food, the rice was very dry with no paneer at all. We called the restaurant to complain. They denied our observation. Didn't even offer any sort of apology or refund. Very disappointed with their service & feedback. 

I've been feeling this sort of experience multiple times. The food is usually good but their hospitality totally brings their overall review down.

This is THE WORST chick-fil-A I've EVER been to. When they first opened up, I was very excited because I usually travel a good distance to get Chick-fil-A. This one is closer to where I live. I'd rather drive the distance than to ever come back to this one (Northeast Tower). There are a few staff in there that are nice, but most of them are young kids that are just rude and careless. The food is almost never fresh! It's like they have old orders laying around and just give them to whoever orders the same thing. I called the manager to complain and he completely disregarded what I said. Let's just say, I won't ever be back there again. (& that's a shame because Chick-fil-A is known for their amazing service).

Very cool place to visit! Lots going on and SO many places to choose from to eat. I loved the wide variety of food they had from Chinese to Indian to a Jewish deli, there's a place for everyone to eat. Some stores sprinkled in between all the eateries. Parking was a little bit of a hassle but we were lucky to find something right in front on. Sunday afternoon. Would definitely recommend to come eat here for lunch!

Got lunch with a coworker and was happy to find that there was no line for NAYA. We both ordered grains/greens bowls -- I got cauliflower and chicken shawarma, and she got falafel and lamb kafta. Everything was delicious and the portions are very generous. I also loved the warm, pillowy pita bread that came with the bowl -- super great for dipping into the baba ganoush topping!
So many great places to choose from, its tough to choose what to eat! Haven't been here in a few years, so some new vendors to try.
You cannot leave Philly without making a stop here! There are so many great vendors serving amazing food!

Great food market ! Mix of everything ....

Few things that they need: 

1) more tables - please 
2) a limit to how long one stays at the table 
3) security to regulate crowds 
4) renovation upgrade
Absolutely worst chipotle I've ever been to avoid at all costs rude employees, dirty, it's the worst do not go

I love coming to this market. The options for food are endless! There's also produce markets here with fresh fruits and vegetables. You can get anything,  cheesesteaks, sandwiches, fresh juice, Thai food , Indian food, bbq, etc!!

The last time I visited Reading Terminal was when I was in town for a wedding and that was many years ago.  While it was sad to see some vendors that were shutdown, it was good to see majority of them were still operating and even though it was 9:30am, there were lot of folks visiting.

If I lived in the city, this would be my go to place for all my needs.  If you are not sure what you want to eat, no worries, they have lot of variety of vendors  - from Chinese food to donuts, it's a matter to determining what you want to eat, a never ending battle!

Overrated to say the least, they won't serve you a pie, but will serve you 8 separate slices. Sold out my ass, you have one job, serve me fucking pizza you ding-dong. The guys that work here are such assholes, selling over price slices of shit, who do you think you are. They treat their customers like absolute anus, I can spend my hard earned money else where, I hope the shop burns down.

A have-to-go place in Philadelphia. They have all kinds of food and I personally really love the Dutch breakfast and donuts . It is always crowded and you may need to wait in line for a long time sometimes.

Definitely a must see when you visit Philly. Very busy and something for everyone. From places with seating to takeout to vendors with merchandise. Will take awhile to snake through and see everything!

Unique in it's age and building, which is pretty cool. If you are a local a place to frequent and be proud of. As a visitor it was worthwhile and I'd stop again, but the variety and prices aren't much different from similar markets in DC, Lancaster, Chelsea in Nee York, etc.

This place needs to be shut down!!!
Place looks nasty as hell and food looks like it was 200 years old and smell so bad. The never gave us utensils for our mashed potatoes what they expected us to eat it with our foots? Smh never again I rather die of hunger !! Shut this place downnnnnn

Solid spot for a quick lunch during work. The portion size for the bowl is pretty generous, and it comes with pita (relatively standard now). The falafel here is probably my second favorite out of the surrounding restaurants (current falafel rank: 1. Mamas vegetarian, 2. Naya, 3. Naf Naf, 4. Cava). In terms of all of the rest of the toppings and bases, I think overall I still prefer Cava for its variety.

Wow, Philadelphia's Reading Terminal Market is like Seattle's Pike Place or Los Angeles' Grand Central Market. Not only is it filled with tons of vendors with delicious food, it's a treat for your eyes!

Definitely come hungry so you can try out all the different foods. So many varieties - Chinese, hamburgers, meats, beers, and more. Since we ate already, we were only able to get some donuts and try some ice cream. Definitely get some donuts from Beiler's Bakery as that is one of the most popular vendors... as proven by the long line!

How the HECK had I lived in Philly for 19 years and on a visit 11 years later, I make my first trip to Reading Terminal Market? I am very upset at myself for not venturing out here sooner and soaking up all the amazing food, gifts, energy, flowers, clothes etc etc etc.

Now, going on the weekend... prob not the smartest idea as it was PACKED. However, maybe that is part of the experience?

We actually just stopped in for lunch and had a specific destination, DiNics, and it was worth the wait! We also stopped by a cheese shop to take some goodies home. 

There was soooo much more I wanted to check out, I can't wait to go back!!

What can I say that hasn't already been said? This is a wonderful market with so many independent retailers and shops that is any small-business-shopper's dream. There are vendors who sell sandwiches and pastries, meats and seafood, jewelry and watches, fine chocolate and exquisite cordials, fresh donuts and baked goods, and lots, lots more!

It was very busy when we visited, on a Tuesday morning, so I don't even want to imagine what it is like during the weekends! We mostly window-shopped and ultimately bought a maple donut for about a buck and which tasted phenomenal. I really love places like these that could be overpriced but choose not to.

Absolutely a must-visit place when visiting Philadelphia!
Strong mix of diverse tenants with something for everyone. A market in the true sense and reminds me of the great markets is used to go to in London like Camden and Billingsgate.
Not going back. Used to be our regular spot. Recently while chewing my Aloo kati roll, a metallic wire came out while biting into it. This was a scary experience.

I found this place by just searching what's near my job to eat and OMG these are SOOOOO good. 

I got three Buffalo Chicken and two spinach. This place is truly a hidden gem. The customer service is great too which is really important to me. They have a new retuning customer.

PROS - Good crowd, good beer selection, good service. 
CONS - South Philly parking, average food.
Overall a good place to have a beer with friends!

This place is crowded as hell. I got some expensive shrimp raw shrimps but they were jumbo and 2lbs ribs cooked. All in all the food was good just the crowd is a lot this is not a place for one who doesn't do well with crowds.

I love it here! There's always something to see or take in and it's great for people watching. The best time to visit is during the week, as it's less crowded and you have more of a chance of getting a table. Some of my favorite counters are Old City Coffee, Beilers donuts, and Four Seasons juice bar. If you park in any of the garages that offer discounted parking near by, bring your ticket in to be validated for a parking discount.  

The only downside is that it gets so crowded on the weekends you can barely move around and it closes at 6 pm. Also, many of the Amish counters are not open on Sunday.

In the age of COVID and restricted indoor spaces, staff was very helpful and attentive in cleaning and disinfecting eating surfaces/tables for each new customer.  Checked quickly each stall and what they had to offer, and at the end got myself a Yellow Thai Curry for $7 + tax.  Great place.

Really cute place to sit with friends over my most favorite of finger foods- Dumplings.  
Oh Yeah Baby, Dumplings !!!

Three of us were impressed with the fillings offered in the dumplings. So many choices. 
I got the combo for $13.50 which included five big stuffed dumplings, A very nice salad with pretty greens, crumbled cheese and raisins and a bottled high end drink from their cold case. A bargain for what turned out to be a filling meal. 
For my five I choose 3 cheese steak and 2 chipotle chicken. With the wonderful salad and drink I was stuffed like it was dinner. Speaking for myself I absolutely love the dumplings. We never felt rushed out of this place and it was nice to sit and enjoy each other's company over good food for a little bit in really cute pleasant surroundings. 
And if the others were here they would agree with me.
I'll be back for sure

Don't ever buy to this shit resturant you make a order and it's says ready to pick then when u go in there you have to wait another 30 min because they don't do their job that's it the worst food ever
Love it here! I do my usual run for my grocers and for lunch stop my di nics for a corn beef excellent!! Fantastic atmosphere and people are quick with their service pricing is the best!!

Ordered a chicken lifestyle meal. The chicken is dry and Unflavorful. The avacoda isn't clumped together, the peppers are overcooked. Probably will not be ordering from this location again. It is bad representation of Chipotle Brand.

A little bit of everything. Here they have lots of little shops and its like an open market. There is very limited seating and it didn't feel really clean. I got a dutch western omlette at a shop but it just tasted like a very buttery omlette. It was jusy okay. I didn't like the limited seating here.

Never had a problem ordering food from here. Love their chicken deluxe sandwiches and waffle fries! Just remember to order your sauces when doing pick up as they can get very busy and it's hard to get in contact with them again. Other than that no issues.

I popped into this Snap Kitchen location yesterday to stock up on meals for the week. The layout is exactly like the one in Old City, and there were friendly employees ready to answer any questions I had. 

From this round of goods I've so far tried the curried chicken salad (very flavorful and perfect for a healthy, high-protein snack), the goat cheese and tomato tart, which was excellent, and the chimichurri beef. After trying several of the medium-sized entrees, the beef was easily the heartiest and most filling. 

Snap might seem pricey, but when I compare it to the amount of ordering out I generally do during the week, it all evens out. I definitely feel like my meals are way healthier when I buy in advance for the week, instead of waiting until 2pm day-of and making terrible choices because I'm too hungry to think straight.

Snap, I am picking up what you're putting down.
It's got everything you are looking for in food and assortment of other items... if you can't find the taste of Philly here... then I'm not sure what to tell you.  An experience for the tourist 100%

I liked it to be honest but do not for the love of God bring your car into this city. The parking for 1 hour was like $30 almost. Like I understand the location but for the love of everything holy in this universe take uber. Any ways the terminal is great there is a lot of people and shops to go to its amazing but for the most part half of the crap there is mediocre and nothing to special. I like the fudge place that is run by those Amish people. I gained like 20 pounds just by walking into their shop but it is worth it because it tastes great. Although all the tourists are crap and some of the employees can also be rude. Other than that ... mehh 7/10

One of THE BEST lunches I have ever eaten! Order the chicken and rice, it was delicious. The chicken is so packed with flavor, the rice so authentic and pillowy and the white sauce just helped bring everything together beautifully! I'm only giving it a 4 star because they forgot to tell me I had to pick up my drink from the fridge - so I walked out without my beverage! But otherwise, absolutely delicious! Will come back again!!

The place has everything you want under one roof. What more can you ask for? Most of the time I come here it's to pick up Produce from Iovine Brothers, Lapsang Souchong at Tea Leaf or a Smoothie from Four Seasons. It's hard to only hit one merchant while you're here. Even your pockets want to keep spending. 

I will admit I try to find any excuse to just be in the heart of this hustle and bustle. Some people just using the Terminal as a walk through, while others doing there Daily or Weekly grocery shopping. From the vibes to the smells, the Terminal has got it going on.

I absolutely love the Reading Terminal Market. My particular favorites are Bassets Turkey (for the best sandwich on earth) Termini Brothers Bakery (for Canolli to die for) and it is a true foodies dream.

Chipotle has awesome food, so if you're feeling Chipotle go grab some! Just not from here, the service is terrible. They are awfully rude, and every time I've gone so far they've messed up my order AND forgot to give me drinks that I paid for. 

After politely asking for my drinks they forgot (not even mentioning my messed up order) I was given a terrible attitude for no good reason. No matter what the situation is, customers shouldn't be treated this way. I won't be going to this location again.

Nothing I can say about this place that hasn't been said before in the 5000+ reviews. We had a pretzel cheese dog from Miller's Twist and loaded chorizo fries from Fox and Son. Both excellent choices. That hot dog was killer, perfect cheese to dog ratio and the pretzel was SO good - soft and buttery. 

Chorizo fries. super salty and delicious!!! See indulgent pictures.

Haven't been since I was a kid and it was better than I could have ever imagined. I brought my European friend and we walked every aisle overstimulated like kids in a candy store. Food was very rich but we walked it off.

If you come to Philly and skip this place and are a foodie, your trip was not complete. 
I hate to say it but you messed up. This place has so much going on and so much variety and culture it almost over whelms you. 

There is a reason why this place has such a great review from our fellow yelpers. They have a little bit of everything, I recommend if you come in a group everyone go to a different spot and grab something and meet back up and split so you can try a little of everything. 

It can be tough to find a place to sit but just be patient. This place is worth a visit for Tommy DiNic's (which is why I came) but it had so much more than I expected. Seriously don't sleep on this place. If you are looking for a cold one hit the bar that is in the back by the restrooms. CHEERS!!!
It's crowded of course... but that's the experience! If you don't mind rubbing up against people I'd say go!
Great food and service, always a fun-filled experience! The food is authentic and always made with love!
Excellent food market that has maintained its authenticity.

This is foodie haven. I came here the day before the my Rock N Roll half marathon so my sister and I could "carb up". We started with Chinese food and ended with french crepes. Its foodie heaven, but often packed to the nines. Its best to come with a very small group and just accept the fact that you will probably have to share tables with someone. 

Overall, if you are looking to eat soul food, go there. Or if you just can't decide if you want ice cream or whoopie pies.

MUST SEE!  You are a fool to come to Philadelphia and not stop here.   Seriously!  
Nuff said. That is all. Trust me. I have great taste.

As a Filipino I am hesitant to go out and eat Filipino food (why buy it when we can make it at home). My girlfriend loves Filipino food so Lalo was one of the vendors we decided to try out during our visit to The Bourse. 

This menu has many of the popular Filipino dishes and comfort foods that I grew up loving. We ordered the long si log, which is Filipino sausage that came with sunny side up egg, garlic rice, and pickled vegetables; this is a very traditional brunch dish that they sell in the Philippines and what my mom cooks on the weekends. They do a pretty good rendition of it. It's hard finding good longanisa, but they either imported some good stuff or made it quite well in house. The garlic fried rice was also done well, it had really strong tastes of garlic which I love. We also ordered lumpia shanghai which is Filipino eggrolls. Each order contains a good amount, but they are tiny. It was crispy and tasty but expensive for the quantity. 

They also had in stock a lot of popular Filipino beverages. We got calamansi juice (Filipino lemonade), and I got to try the most popular beer in the Philippines for the first time, San Miguel. 

Overall it was a good, nostalgic experience for me. My girlfriend really enjoyed all the food and drinks we ordered. We would definitely come in again and try other dishes. Nothing can beat my mom's cooking though!
Many vendors! Many tastes! How can any foodie resist wandering this market for inspiration and gluttony? It speaks for itself. But MOST DEFINITELY stop here if you're in Philly.

So many options that I can never decide what to eat.  Both times I've walked around completely overwhelmed, and left empty handed.  I'll try again someday, but I will research particular places so I know exactly where to go, and what to get.

Great selection of vendors and lots to buy!  It a place that you can visit multiple times and always find something fabulous and new!!
Take your time and explore what this wonderful market has to offer!
Has so many different food options. It's incredible. Pretty busy even during Covid. Great Philly cheesesteak options. And can get fresh produce. No where to sit and eat currently.

This spot is a foodie's haven. They seriously have every type of food imaginable to man (almost everything). I've only been to Philadelphia twice, but I believe this is a go to spot for food. The atmosphere is so lively and full of life, and as a people watcher, I thrive on feeling people's energy, so this is just a good place to feel alive and eat some good food! They also sell fresh produce in addition to grab and go, plus sit down foods. I've only eaten ice-cream from here and had brunch at one of the breakfast restaurants, but all the food around me looks so good! I'll have to dedicate some time when I visit again to sample more of their options.

I just tried this place for the first time, and I am loving it. Masala Kitchen opened yesterday, in the former location of Marabella Meatball Company (which had been a favorite of mine.) 

Their specialty is "kati rolls," which are meats, paneer cheese, veggies, or eggs, wrapped in a thin flatbread. I ordered the chicken masala roll and achari paneer roll (paneer "with a hint of pickle.") When you order two rolls ($3.75-6.00 each), you get $1.00 off. 

The chicken masala roll is awesome. It has huge chunks of tender, white meat chicken in a masala sauce, with sliced onions, in the wonderful kati. The kati is thin enough to not be overly filling, but dense enough to hold all the goodies inside without ripping. 

The paneer roll is also great. Lots of cheese and a delicious, mildly spicy green chutney. None of the food is spicy, for those who are hesitant to eat Indian because of its reputation for hotness. You can add hot sauce upon receiving your order if you want to heat things up. Despite the lack of chili-pepper-hotness, the food is full of flavor and punch from other spices and fresh ingredients.

The yogurt sauce that came on the side is so good, sweet and savory at the same time, and very flavorful, a lot like tzatziki.

The staff in the restaurant was very friendly and helpful, making recommendations, and offering us samples of rose lassi (yogurt with rose syrup.) The lassi was really unique, and anyone who enjoys the flowery taste of rose or jasmine will love it.

If you live in the city (and don't just work there like I do), you will also be pleased that the restaurant is open very late every day. 

Monday-Thursday: 11:00am to 12am
Friday: 11:00am to 3:30am
Saturday: 12:00pm to 3:30am
Sunday: 12:00pm to 11:00pm

That's good eating in the middle of the night!

A little or a lot of just about everything food here. We ate a hot cheesesteak and I do mean hot meat and  pepper sandwich here at one stand and had to hightail it over to the ice cream stand to tame the flames. Great spot to people watch, shop and get your eats and drinks on. 

Highly recommend this stop on your downtown Philly tour.

FOOD! Any place that has a variety of foods to eat is 5 stars for me. This was the last stop for us on our mini road trip. Shout out to the lovely gentleman that gave me his parking ticket with 25 mins left on it. Since we weren't sure what to expect we just walked around and looked at all the delicious food. There is something for everyone with so many different types of foods and goods to buy. We weren't really hungry so we just got smoothies at the juice bar and they were delicious. I could see us driving 2 hours on a Saturday to come back and get some. I can't wait to come back with an appetite and try some other things.

Wow is all i can say!  This place is awesome!  This place is a HUGE station that has tons and tons of small stations set up for food and groceries and more food!  There's a small area to sit and eat and people watch.  Just walk around, pick a direction and go and smell the food!  

Really - it's really awesome.

I had been hearing many good things about Humpty's Dumplings, so when we were shopping nearby and needed a recharge, I happily crossed the street!    The building is easy to find - it's the one on the block with one of those funky cool and beautiful mosaic fronts.

We were greeted nicely by the young man behind the counter, who told us which dumplings were most popular - cheesesteak, asian pork, buffalo chicken and the gobbler turkey & stuffing dumpling. We ordered a variety - basically everything but the turkey one as we are currently turkey-d out.  We sat and admired the very funky (and a little creepy at times) art in the dining area.

The young man brought our dumplings out, piping hot, a few minutes later.  We are glad he wrote which was which on the paper linings because, well, they all look exactly the same on the outside.  The only other clue was the sauces provided - ketchup for the cheeseteak, buffalo sauce for the chicken and soy sauce for the asian pork. I have no idea what people do if they order a variety mixed together.  That would be challenging.

Everything was delicious, truly, the cheesesteak bites were delightful, the asian pork probably the most like any other dumpling you'd get and the buffalo chicken zingy and savory.  

I worry about this place, though.  They're making the jump from food truck- where the menu of dumplings and salads are perfect - to a restaurant. It's a tough jump, and I think in this case because the menu is so limited - just dumplings and salads - it feels like all you're eating are appetizers and sides.  Yes, 5 golf ball sized dumplings are a lot of food, equal to a meal, but it feels like you're snacking.  

I would LOVE to see them succeed because I think what they're doing is clever, cool and beyond all delicious.  What it may take is expanding their restaurant menu to offer things that people associate more with a 'meal' and less with a 'snack'.  

Also, make sure the workers in local businesses around you know your product and can recommend it.  Offer them a free dumpling or something, because when their customers ask "where's a good place to grab a bite around here?" in a sea of chains and restaurants, you want them to say - aw, man, go to Humpty's, they have really great food and it's cool tool.  Just a thought.

I'm glad I don't live or work near Reading Terminal Market.  I would gain so much weight.  There are tons of tasty and quick options for breakfast and lunch.  The prices are a little high, it's what you'd expect from a touristy spot like this.  

There are sandwich shops, breakfast joints, cupcake stands, gifts and candles, beeswax stuff, honey, candy and fudge, fish markets, meat markets, greek diners, chocolate, chocolate, chocolate, raw bar, book shop, and (most importantly) one of those penny smooshing machines.

Long lines in an extremely congested environment.  Yes there's a variety of choices.  But no I don't think any of them are super great.  I will commend the market for having lots of vegetarian and vegan options.  But I don't think it's the kind of place that you can gracefully explore - you really have to go in with an agenda.  

If you are considering taking your child here for trick-or-treating I would suggest against it.  While the vendors who did participate in the trick-or-treating were very helpful, generous and accommodating, there were not many of them that participated.

Based on selection and quality of food alone, I'd rate this place as close to a 5 as it can get without jumping in front of me during the climactic gun fight with Lo Pan and the Decepticons.

In terms of actual experience going there, I'd rate it a 3.5, if I'm being generous.

This all averages out to a solid 4.

The only reason the experience can be kind of stressful is that it's always packed. Like, Asian night market packed. Like, gambling den on 4 v 4 cockfight night packed. You get the picture. Whether you just want a container of takeaway, or some quality meats, cheese, or artisan whatever, you will be waiting in line, likely for 15-20 minutes. I've yet to come here at a time of day when it wasn't filled up like 25 cent drink night at Paddy McRegretfuls.

That said, you have to go here, and you have to try everything. They have what you like, I guarantee it - except Vietnamese cuisine, I haven't seen that there.

For 5 straight Sunday nights in a row I've visited between 7:45 - 8:05 PM and every time they've shut down early with a sign that reads "sold out." Also every time, multiple people were standing outside also to be disappointed by being misled with a website that posts a 9 PM closing time.  In all of my life I've never encountered a pizza place that continually runs out of supplies or closes early?!   Seems like mis management or maybe what is seemingly more likely a simple lack of regard for setting regular and loyal customer's expectations.  How about keeping your hours until 8 PM so you can manage inventory better?  Or better yet, why not post closing hours at 8 PM?  Also, honestly opening at 1 PM on Saturday and Sunday? Who is that convenient for?  Like every other pizza shop within miles is open at 11 or 12 on the weekends (for many lunch is over by 1!)  Guys, your pizza is good, but not great (see Barstools review for example). You're not Beddia.  Convenience to your loyal customers is more important than opening and closing when you feel like it.  I have been a loyal customer and pay homage to small businesses in the neighborhood that keep their word to customers. If you can't handle keeping your hours or keeping enough supplies to last the day, change them.  On the other hand, I've discovered Slice Pizza as a fantastic alternative with the same prices.  I've also now frequented Peace of Pizza, thicker slices but conveniently and always open.  Like many in the neighborhood would agree, I would also say Pizza Brain has much better pizza as well in general with much better customer service, and convenience.  I've made the permanent switch. Best of luck!

It's pretty dirty inside and it smells funny to me. However, in thanksgiving of 2020, I really needed to find meat for my collard greens and the butcher shop had exactly what I needed! I give it 3 stars for that shop.

I wish I lived in Philly just to go to Reading Terminal Market regularly! Baltimore has 6 public markets and though I've only been to 3 of them, I'm going to overgeneralize and say this one is better than them ALL (debate is welcome lol)! There's so much to taste and see you need at least a couple weeks daily visits to try it all. I love that there's ample seating to enjoy the goodies you buy.

This was my first visit! I got breakfast from the Dutch Eating Place and baked goods from the adjacent bakery. Everything was delicious from the fresh churned butter on my french toast to the thick cut turkey bacon. I took home wheat and oatmeal bagels, cinnamon rolls, sticky buns, and crumb cake for less than $10! I love the Amish!

I'm with my fellow yelpers, if you're in Philly and don't stop here you're totally missing out. I CANNOT wait to go back!

Honeygrow is a really great option if you're looking for healthy "fast food". As a student on a budget, it's very conveniently located on campus and the pricing is fair. Each time I've ordered from here I really felt like I was getting enough food and good quality as well. 

I used the app to create a custom order and got a code from a friend and we both got a discount from our orders. I think this is a great option for students, when saving a little goes a long way. The app was easy to navigate and the food was ready on time and was very satisfying. There is a large variety of options to choose from if you're making a custom order or you can just pick a preset meal - I've tried both and they are both equally as good. 

Overall, really good option if you're looking for something quick and healthy. And with the app, you can order and just pick it up and go which makes it very convenient.

I was born and raised in Philly. The glowing reviews for this place never fail to make me shake my head in bewilderment. As far as I'm concerned, this place is the Pennsylvania version of the Pennsauken Mart and my private version of a house of horrors. 

When I was a pre-schooler, my grandmother would drag me here to shop. The place smelled bad, like a combination of rotting meat and decaying vegetables. As soon as we'd arrive, I'd start to cry and squirm. No amount of my Nan threatening me with the leather belt she always carried in her purse to mete out instant punishment would reset my behavior to quiet and compliant. I wasn't a horrible, temperamental boy in general but going to RTM pushed every one of my buttons. As a shy, nervous kid, being in a big, moving crowd of people frightened me, but I was too young to express my feelings and fears, and even if I'd been able to do so, my grandparents were no nonsense immigrants who did not tolerate or pander to childish folderol. After many dreadful shopping trips with me crying, screaming, trying to run away and generally creating a scene, my grandmother began to go here on her own and leave me at home-in peace.

When I was a high schooler, sometimes friends would want to go here on a Saturday to just walk around, people watch and then get something to eat. By then, I was too big to cry and make a fuss, so I'd simply go off on my own and meet them elsewhere. Years later, I was a loner in art college and the few people I did hang out with were not the types to find RTM a 'fun' place to spend free time.

Flipping the calendar pages forward to when I moved back to Philadelphia a bit more than half a decade ago, I was simply awed by all the changes in the city, the new skyline and what was suddenly a vast wonderland of places to eat. I'd heard about Melt Kraft (RIP), which was THE place for grilled cheese sandwiches. Unfortunately the stumbling block for me was its location-Reading Terminal Market. My late friend Dee offered to go with me to help me work through my childhood associations with the market. I readily accepted because-anything for a good grilled cheese sandwich, y'know? 

We went on a Sunday. The insidious smell of rot and vegetal decay hit me as soon as I walked in, but it was not as intense as I'd remembered. The press of the crowd was, though. Dee got directions to Melt Kraft, we pushed and shoved through slow moving bodies in winter clothing and found the vendor. And a very long line of people who also shared my love of gooey, hot cheese. I said I would skip the sandwich but if she was up for it, we'd walk around. 

Since I don't like donuts, roast pork sandwiches, cheesesteaks, hoagies or looking at meat and dead fish, I don't drink coffee nor do I care for pancakes or iterations of waffles, that left a lot of places for us to just pass by and skip. I am acutely aware that I am a neurotic person, so I asked Dee if RTM was as dirty and unpleasant as I perceived it to be. She said she honestly felt it was fairly clean for a market of this kind, but she understood my feelings. We made it to Iovine's produce which oddly calmed and soothed me, but not enough for me to spend any more time there. 

Even if I was forced to entertain out of towners that I absolutely loathed, I wouldn't torture them by taking them here.

My travels have taken me to the Casbah in Morocco, public markets in Africa, butcher shops and green grocers all over Europe. I adore Chinatown and the whole Italian Market area. I can spend hours in either place walking around, eating, drinking and shopping. To me, Reading Terminal Market is nothing but a huge, smelly, crowded tourist attraction, a so-so sub par food circus and a place for me to avoid. This is, of course, simply my opinion and your mileage may vary. More power to you if it does. 

If you are a visitor to Philadelphia, please keep in mind that we are much much much more than RTM, the Phillies baseball team, soft pretzels, cheesesteaks, the Liberty Bell and the "Rocky Steps" (which are merely part of the building and lead to one of the entrances to the Philadelphia Museum of Art).

I love their roti rolls and for $6, it's a good deal.  I usually get the chicken masala as the aloo roll with paneer in it.  Try it with white sauce in the side.  You can order online or at the kiosk there and they afe fast and open late.

This is a pretty fun market, especially if it is your first or second time coming. There are a lot of different vendors all under one roof, with lots of gourmet options. Some of the produce is the same and a little more expensive than some Chinese supermarkets just down the street in Chinatown. However, the convenience of one stop shopping under the guise of being "down town at the markets" is very fun. Be sure to bring plenty of money and an empty stomach to snack as you shop!

Cool historic place to grab some lunch.  Was excited to know that this used to be a terminal for the Reading Railroad (I couldn't help but immediately think of all the good times I had playing Monopoly and picking the card that said "Take a ride on the Reading Railroad"..... now I wanna go play Monopoly).Fun spot to check out if you're visiting Philly. Be sure to bring cash- not all places within the market take cards.

One of the best food markets I've been to. Love the variety, and seems like you can't go wrong with whatever you decide to eat here.

Tommy DiNic's: Roast Pork w/ Broccoli Rabe & Provolone Cheese. Super delicious meat, but cheese too strong for me. Very large sammich cannot fit into little girl's stomach.

Bassetts Ice Cream:  Salted Caramel Pretzel (vanilla ice cream with salted caramel swirls &  chocolate covered pretzel nibs). Loved the flavor and the way the pretzels and caramel were incorporated. Very American ice cream. Creamy, heavy, and sweet.

Molly Malloy's: Golden Monkey. Very tasty beer. Found myself tasting something different with each sip. Crisp, sweet, bitter- idk there's a lot going on here.

This place is awesome. It is crowded however with a lot of people, but if you are a foodie then this is the place to go. They have almost every kind of food possible to man kind except for Japanese and Korean.  You go here to also get ice cream, honey some fresh meat like fish and meat.  They gave awesome donuts as well. This place has hard places to get seating as well. If you are lucky there are some restaurants that have seating.  Overall a great place to go.

Reading Terminal reminded me of the outdoor markets and bazaars you'd see on a travel documentary, although we lacked the voiceover narration of Rick Steves, Andrew Zimmern, or Anthony Bourdain. still, it's a lot of fun.

jam-packed with stalls filled with trinkets, donuts, books, sandwiches, coffee, spices, incense, and more, there's something for everyone. seating is haphazardly strewn about; consider yourself lucky to find a seat anywhere.

the best plan is to grab something and keep walking. or, run into your friends - completely unplanned, since they live in Connecticut these days - and find out that they have a big table with their family. the donuts they got were superb - I don't know which vendor, but I had a super-dense chocolate donut that was as big as a car tire. okay, I exaggerate, but it was epic and delicious, unlike what you'd get at Dunkin (or, perish the thought, Starbucks).

worth a stop if you're in Philly.

Yum! This massive food market is located conveniently near the Greyhound station, so it was quite easy to visit during my weekend trip to Philly. Tons of food, both prepared and not, there's something here for everyone - you just have to be willing to find (and wait) for it.

Seems like almost everything is solid, but I had to do some research anyways and ended up getting:
- Snickerdoodle cookie from 4th Street Cookie Company: So huge! I didn't like the rather crisp edges on the outside (prefer a nice, gooey cookie myself), but the middle was delicious.
- Smoked chicken wing from Dienner's: Love that they let me order just one, even though the guy looked at me weirdly. The wing was piping hot, and the meat juicy and tender with some delicious smokiness. Skin, as always, was the best part.
- Roast pork sandwich from DiNic's: After seeing all the hype over this sandwich, I have to say I was let down. Not that it wasn't good, just that it wasn't revelatory, which I'd expected. Definitely get the greens and provolone, lest you end up with just a pile of meat on bread (not that there's anything wrong with that...)
- Cannoli from Termini Bros: Oh my. I used to work in an Italian bakery that I'd thought had the best cannolis until I tasted this. Fresh to order so the shell stays crisp, and the filling is not too sweet.

Tips:
- Some vendors are cash only.
- A lot of places aren't open on Sundays (Dutch Eating Place, Beiler's, and Dienner's, to name a few). Definitely want to try the chicken pot pie and a Beiler's donut next time around.
- Place is super crowded, but we still had no problem getting a table at lunchtime on a weekend.
- Take a picture of the map located next to every entrance!

Did anyone realize that whomever added this restaurant to Yelp spelled it wrong!?ChiCk-Fil-A!!!! There's a C in the name. 

Anyway, I do love chicken, and this chain does it well. The only thing that sucks is that they are closed Sundays and for some reason, it's like the only day my wife always brings them up. Grrrrr! But, on the other days that they are open, my go to items are:

Spicy chicken sandwich - very nice kick! One of the only fast food places that makes spicy chicken have a slight spice to it.

Grilled market salad - it has a ton of fruit (berries & apples) and nuts in it. It's my staple for when I need something on the healthier side

Waffle fries - You can't go here without getting the fries.

Overall: I'll definately be back. Place is clean and run pretty well.

During my three day stint in Philly, I came here twice. I love this market. The food is a little pricey, but I was on my vacation budget, so I was okay spending a few more dollars per meal than usual. They've got everything you want here, including meats, seafood, produce, ice cream, and various desserts. It's also a great place to people watch. I came in during lunch rush and shared a table with random people attending a nearby convention. I even got some tips from local cops on what to order!

Friendly people, and tasty food. What more could you ask for?

This place is a must, when visiting Philadelphia.

My family and I love it here. It never disappoints, and you get to shop through many different stores and try different foods.. The vibe is always great.

We love the Thai Salmon dish, the cannoli's and the farmers market for fresh meats/produce. 

I live in NJ so I normally travel to Center City by train, so it becomes quite the adventurous day for us.

Reading Terminal Market walks a fine line between being a top 5 tourist destination in Philadelphia, but also still serving as a utility for local Philadelphians looking to grab a bite to eat or maybe even groceries on the way home. With so many specialty food vendors selling everything from specialty meats to donuts to fresh produce, there is something for everyone. 

Reading Terminal Market is an absolute must-have on any "to-do" list for anyone visiting the city. Every time I have had a guest in town, I have made a point to make a stop at RTM.

Great place, but if you're in a hurry to get lunch avoid getting there sometime between 11 and 1. I love the atmosphere and almost everything I've tried there, but I especially love the ice cream and doughnuts.

The indoor market is always busy with stalls that line every inch of the place. You can find bakeries, donut shops, butcheries, flower shops, and small restaurants all around you. Come ready with cash and be ready to Wade through crowds of people.

A Philly must! Want a cheesesteak? How about a fresh juice? Oh, you'd rather have breakfast? You can get everything right here! A plethora of Philly cuisine awaits you at this beautiful market. It's busy all the time, but worth multiple trips to experience everything. Lines can be annoying if you go at peak times, but it's worth it. I highly recommend picking up some fresh flowers from the flower market and a make your own juice!

I would recommend this place to a friend! I am under 25 years old with not so good credit but  the salesman "Sean" was really helpful and I was able to drive off the lot for just a dollar down and a one year warranty. He was really patient and friendly with me. He even helped me get auto insurance which is mandatory to drive off the lot. The one critique I would add is that it was a all day process mainly because they don't tell you the prices of the car upfront because they have to go by your income so every time you pick a car your interested in they have to submit the information to the financial counselor who is off site and that's takes up to 30 mins each time. I only took me two days to find something that was in my price range and that was reliable and convenient.

I dont get to go to Starbucks often, largely because it's not within my route to work. 

I had a mocha latte and it was delicious. I wanted something warm and soothing. 

The barista was pleasant and made my drink carefully. The atmosphere of this Starbucks was quiet. There were a few groups of people and they were not too loud.

I will return to this location.

Reading Terminal Market (or 'RTM' for short) is famous among tourists. A potentially better spot is the newly renovated Bourse, but RTM has some things going for it. On my recent visit, I grabbed a buttery Miller's Twist warm pretzel, Hope's cookies from the Pennsylvania General Store and a cookie from 4th Street cookie company, and a tiramisu cake and biscotti from Termini Brother's bakery. All of these were good. My taste test (albeit of different types of cookies) leads me to give a slight nod to 4th Street's macadamia chocolate chip cookie (the healthier looking Harvest cookie - cranberries, oats, cinnamon - at Hope's was actually kind of greasy). That said I like the selection at Hope's as well as their signature peanut butter chocolate dipped cookies. 
My one disappointing experience with RTM was the Dutch Eating Place's open face turkey sandwich. Not sure how this got positive reviews - the plain white bread was drowned in gravy that coated excessive turkey - so much unappetizing food! I've had their delicious apple dumplings in the past (so I know they offer some good items); Stick with their breakfast/desserts. Another limitation with RTM is the lack of healthier options (try Tootsie's market for a fresh salad bar).

I pretend like I'm not a crier, but let's face it - I very much am. I cried when I found sashimi grade salmon in a Cincinnati seafood market. I cried when my boss told me that about how her dog trots and meets new dogs. Hell, I cried when Jordan Staal was traded from the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2012. I have never met Jordan Staal. I have absolutely no ties to his life.

Why am I telling you this? If I tell you this, you will know exactly what my reaction was when I walked into Reading Terminal Market.

I cried. I bawled like a baby right next to Bassett's Ice Cream.

They were joyous tears, of course, but that doesn't take away from the fact that my over emotional self doused the baked goods at Beiler's with my waterworks. I may have been so overwhelmed that Valley Shepard may now be selling a variety of pickles featuring my tears. The waterfall of emotion perfectly showcased reason #3162 why I can't have children - I certainly wouldn't make it through nine months of this kind of overreaction.

But, guys. Everything was just so damn beautiful.

By the end of my time in Philadelphia, I had eaten at 3/4 of the entire market. The stalls are plentiful but the aisles are cramped because I am clearly not the only person that appreciates the perfection that is Reading Terminal. I ate my weight in ice cream, I stood in line waiting for a subpar Philly cheesesteak whilst complaining in a faux New Jersey accent, I ... I may have even scarfed down a 4th street cookie while hiding in Jonathan Best's grocery so that when I emerged from the abyss I could pretend to be famished and hit up another stall. (If you ever ask me again whether or not this is true I will look you in the eye and swear on my grave it is not. I'd rather go die harboring a secret large enough to make me a Hogwarts ghost than shamefully admit on multiple occasions that I am enough of a fatass to eat two meals in the same hour in the same place.)

This is, by far, the best indoor food market I've ever visited. I still dream about Carmen's Franklin cheesesteak (they add cream cheese to it! Smart people) and I've recklessly attempted to recreate DiNic's iconic roast pork sandwiches at home. (Broccoli rabe is difficult to cook y'all.) I am currently attempting every which way into visiting Philadelphia again so I can skip and dance my way through this amazing food mecca. In the meantime, I will cry - because apparently I do that for everything.
The family loves this spot! A little bit of everything and a lot of Philly flavor! Something for everyone!

I've been enjoying the Reading Terminal since I was 17.  So I've been going there for great food for 31 years.  

Stopped in this past Saturday afternoon to get some lunch.  My boyfriend mentioned a Thai restaurant that he used to go to when he worked in the city.  He recommended the salmon dish which was soooo good!  

I stopped in a Moroccan shop and everything was so beautiful and made in Morocco.  Took me right back to being there when I was 19 and in the outdoor markets!

I grabbed some cookies too....and they were only $1 each because it was National Cookie Day!

The terminal has everything you want and some things you didn't even know you needed!
